Source: The King of Worms is known to us. He and the necromancers who follow him are our greatest foes.\n\nTake the unclean thing to the statue of Arkay outside and burn it. Perhaps, with Arkay's blessing, we can put an end to this blasphemous graverobbing.
Honest Pierric?  Consorting with Cults?  Surprising. I know a thing or two of the cults near Crosswych.\n\nBring me ten hag's toes and perhaps I'll be in the mood to share my knowledge.
I know what you're thinking.  Quit staring at my feet and get moving.  You can find a clutch of Hags southwest of town.
My Pierric?  What am I to do?  The doctor bids me not to leave my house, but has yet to diagnose my illness... I feel so weak...
What do you want?  I have a long, grueling trial ahead of me, I cannot afford distraction.
Yes, of course, you're right... I must return.  I don't know what came over me before...
They intend to... raze Crosswych?  What about my Gwen?  This was not what they told me...
Could you speak to Doctor Severain on my behalf?  Whatever is plaguing me, I need to know if I am to help Pierric!
A bear once killed my sister.

Ah, Guen.  I am not "holding something back," but due to the circumstances surrounding her condition I need to be certain of the diagnosis before I make a pronouncement.  If you could collect a reagent for me I could complete the necessary testing.
Ah yes... Begging your pardon, but I fear I need to test you to see if you are all that you - LOOK OUT!
Ah!  The final ingredient.  The wyrd will soon regret my exile. Now, on to young Pierric.
He wasn't the carefree hero his companions thought.  He may have been lured into joining the Cult of Ulorion - they can be very persuasive when needs warrant.

They meet in a cave to the north.  Ancient magic makes quick work of the likes of you, so use caution.  I have a copy of their plans you may take - they don't bode well for Crosswych, I'm afraid.\n\nYou'll find the plans near the mantle.

Indeed he was - but no longer.  He disappeared just two nights ago during his watch. He didn't raise an alarm, which is odd - Pierric is as vigilant a man as any I've known.  \n\nI can't help but fear the worst.
Who are you?  Why have you slain my personal guard?  What do you want?
I have no time for interruptions, soldier, speak quickly.
I hid during the attack. I saw the cultists smash into a shrine behind the cave wall, then seal it.
Bold yet reasonable.  It appears I have no choice in the exchange... Here.  Take them.
Guards!
What!  My messenger will burn if he failed to deliver my orders!  Here, take this to your Captain.  Hurry!
It is unfortunate you must die.  The Throne has use for such sly agents.  Guards!
I'm part of the Fighter's Guild... I do odd jobs outside the mines. There were far too many cultists for me to face, though. Sometimes the best plan is to live and fight another day.

If we destroy the webbing, we can use the ram to bash our way into the shrine and stop them.\n\nWhen you're ready, hit that webbing with all you've got! They'll probably try to stop us, so prepare for anything.
They used a battering ram to get inside the shrine. They disabled it after opening the wall, but if you can protect me, I think I can get it working again.

Alaric? Aye, I know him. Poor lad. His parents vanished a month ago. I'd knew he'd run away, but not where.

I'll keep Alaric safe. This camp... disturbs me. 

Can you go west and see if you can find the camp? Find out what you can about the place.
If I don't leave Grayborne I'll be killed?\n\nRoche is a hateful fool! I'm no threat to anyone; ask around the village if you don't believe me.
Please! Don't turn me in. I'm just doing what I need to survive - you don't know what it's like at camp. Let me go - I'll be good from now on, promise!
You... you're a real jerk, you know that?
My parents? I... I have none. I live at our camp, with the other children. Mother Murk gives us everything we need. Wanna see?
Oh good! I'll put these to use at once. If I could impose upon you once again, please deliver these potions I've just finished to Inquisitor Bieller of the Lion Guard.

Then you've wasted your journey. I know Tristan worries for us, but I'm not leaving this swamp until I find my daughter. In case you haven't noticed, I can take care of myself. If you want to help us, help me find Isabelle, first.

Our soldiers here are dying. We have to send them on their journey without worry that the horrors of undeath will prevent them from reaching their rest. Please, go find symbols of Ar'kay so that he may watch over them.
If i'm to join any Watch, I'll accept no position less than Captain of a Watchtower. I was Captain of the Guard in my homeland, and in a real city to boot - not some speck on the map.
Immutably. I righteously defend Crosswych from what invaders may come from the northeast...
Only for a bit!  We've never been attacked on this front before...  Perhaps I would be better suited to a post within the city.
I heard the hermit in the forest was out trying to talk to the ghosts. I don't know what he's up to, but it can't be good. Who talks to spirits, you know?
Rumor has it a foreign mage of some kind has come to try and help. A Redguard, even! We don't see many of them around here.
A hermit? Can't say that I do. Although... if he comes into town at all, one of the town criers has probably seen him.
A Redguard? Here? That's something you don't see every day. Haven't heard of anyone like that, though, sorry. The blacksmith might have, though.
You must mean Claude. He's out there, day and night, trying to tell the spirits something about his grandfather or something. If you ask me, he's not quite all there.
Oh, the mage, Irama? Lovely girl. She's trying to bring the spirits away with her, in crystals. I hope she's up to the task.
Who are you to tell us where I can't live? You big doofus! You should go away now!
We don't have much to give, but will part with what we can. Take one of the boxes along the back wall. It should provide basic first aid capabilities.
I am sorry, child. I am no priest of Arkay-- I know little about the undead.
Averos, that rabid cur, murdered King Ranser.  Sure as steel.\n\nThe fool!  His folly will bring war down upon us all, mark my words.
Well, that's the difficult bit.  I need a powder made from ground Wolf's Teeth.  Five should do it... I don't need to tell you how dangerous those beasts are.
Ranser's ghost is accusing her through the mouths of our citizens.  Use this to expell his shade from the possessed.\n\nDo this and you'll understand why I suspect Virolynn.
Дякую.  Дайте-но мені хвилинку.
It is as I suspected.  Guendeline is with child.  Given her circumstances, I don't know that she'll take well to the news.
Me? With child? But Pierric and I aren't even wed!  Please, you must find him... give him this note - wherever he is, whatever he is doing, he must know that we are to be parents!

Pierric is not much like other men. He spent - spends - lots of time by himself, far away from town. I admit I saw him returning late in the evening from the direction of the Wrothgar Mountains on more than one occasion...

Do I look like I read? If it's parchment you're on about, you'd do better with a priest. They have the leisure for that sort of tripe.\n\nLast I heard, a sect devoted to Arkay set up in my old chapel. I'd say you should poke one of them about it.
While you were away my Watchers brought me news of the murder weapon.

gra-Muzgob? During my time at the chapel, I ran her off a time or two. Orc witch, if I remember. Had a thing for dead bodies.\n\nThought she was dead. Probably wouldn't stop her. Her old house is south of here. Maybe you'll find something there.

Weeping witch? I'd bet my bones she means the statue of Mara, behind the chapel. \n\nBad business, this. In my time, we kept the fallen safe. Still should. You want to end this, I'll back you. Meet me at Cath Bedraud. I've got a favor to call in.
Perhaps. My name is Claude. Who are you, and why are you asking me this?

Poor Seth.  Still trying to sell snakeskins to the snakes. He really should move on, but knowing him he'll stick with it 'till he's in the ground. In any case, here's the package - not that anyone in Crosswych will be able to afford anything in it.
Raising the dead? That may have been what riled the spirits here to begin with.\nI may know where these instigators are. There is a camp to the north of here... I'll show you where it is on your map.
I am fine, thank you. While I appreciate your timely intervention, might I inquire as to what brings you so far off the beaten path?

<Curate Marcel's face darkens.>\nThis blight will not be tolerated. I will help you in this task, but we must act quickly. I will need water blessed by Arkay-- you can find it in a tomb near here, where others of my faith are interred.
Once you have the holy water, light the brazier at the southernmost graveyard. I will meet you there, and we can set about this business.\nNow go! Quickly!
We arrested the courier, but he must have hidden the weapon before we caught him on the road.
Elsie cured my son of chills once.

Missing corpses. Pah. How can I ask souls to die for Northmoor if we can't even bury them?\n\nA few years back I hung some bandits for graverobbing. They set up southwest of Camp Mercy. Go there and kick over some rocks. Maybe a snake will crawl out.
No matter what you know, there's nothing you can do, now. The ritual won't be stopped!
Roche and the wyrd; there's a story there.\n\nAll I know is Roche's son was in Westtry, some months ago.  He came home wounded, and neither Elsie nor the wyrd could save him.
Graverobbing? Is that why you beat me within an inch of my life? Look, it's like this. So maybe a few times we maybe dug up some bodies and maybe sold them to an orc. Don't murder me over it!
Some female orc - Jha gra-Muzgob. Don't know what she did with them and don't care. We're just trying to make a living. You want to murder someone, murder her!

Hmm. Was a gravedigger awhile back at Cath Bedraud, looting graves. Palo. Couldn't prove it, but I put the fear of Akatosh into him. Thefts stopped.\n\nIf anyone's connected to this Muzgob, it's Palo. Go shake him up a bit, see what falls out.

Barnard sent you? I'd never! I've not touched a grave save to bury the dead. Man's a lunatic! Said he'd break both my thumbs!\n\nI tell you, friend, I'm just an honest man trying to make a living. I certainly haven't been selling no bodies to no orc.

That wasn't me, swear on my mother's soul! It must have been gra-Muzgob! She knows I gave her up!\n\nLook, I'm just trying to make an honest living. I met her behind the chapel when I had a sale, all right? That's all I know! Please don't kill me!
The Lion Guard won't abide any witch.\n\nBut the wyrd and Roche? That story's more personal. They took his son, you see. No man can forgive that.
You can always trust the same snake to slither the same way. Good work.  I'll gather a few men. Meet us behind the chapel in the graveyard. You and I, we're putting a stop to this.
<The acolyte laughs, madly.>\nThe Mistress is going to destroy Camlorn with a monster the likes no one here has ever seen! You have no hope! The Colossus will crush you!
It is hidden in the forest! You'll never find it! Mistress Jha has hidden it well.\n<The acolyte spits.>

Now that's good ale …

Roche's boy went to fight in Westry; when he came back he wasn't right. Badly hurt, but more than that. The wyrd couldn't cure him.

Then he disappeared.  Roche blames them.
My cow wouldn't give milk.  Elsie gave me some herbs for it, and now we have all the milk we could want.
Lord Ranser was murdered here in Camlorn on an official visit.
So.... you're the Glenumbra hero? I can't do much with this missive. I can tell you that there has already been a murder. You should report to Oron. He's Faharajad's representative here.
Lord Ranser was murdered here in Camlorn on an official visit from Shornhelm.
Lord Ranser was a "diplomat" from Shornhelm. Between you and me, he was a right bastard. Back in the war, he gutted old Ulorion of the Magis Order.
Oron is leading the investigation from Fahara'jad. He's a man serious about his business.
Fahara'jad? Where're you from again? He's the Lord of the Nine Crowns. Brought together the nine kingdoms. Married off all his daughters to do it.
Oron? He's back with Lord Sebastien in the castle.
"LORD" Sebastien is the Lord of Northmoor. He's married to Parvani of the Nine Crowns.
The Magis Order is my outfit and the army of Northmoor. We report to Lord Sebastien. The army was started by Ulorion, but is currently ruled by Lord Averos.
I gave the weapon to a second courier.  Her name is Katarin.  She took it to Aldcroft in Urvaius...\n\nI just wanted to return to my home in Glenumbra...

I can help with that-- I owe my brother one. I'm worried about getting there safely, though. With both bandits and aggressive wolves in the area, I'll need protection. Lord Jes at the Hands of Northmoor holdings in Camlorn could provide it.

Oh Isabelle, you look just a mess... and yes, friend, I will return with you, now that we've found my daughter. Just be warned. I did not have my sword before. I have it now. If I see that Lurker, I'm going to cut it apart, piece by bloody piece.
Oh praise the Divines, at last someone's come! This swamp is horrid, horrid! There are flies and snakes and leeches and... oh, it's just dreadful. Please, good knight, escort me back to my family!
Julien wants to give me gems? That is so sweet! \n\nI wasn't sure if he understood what I was hinting at the other night, but does this mean … does he feel the same way about me as I do about him?

Oh. I see. He didn't get the hint, after all.\n\nIf he's in love with Guendeline though, then it's for the best. In fact … here. Take the piece I was crafting for the Dorells. I was tempted to keep it, but maybe it will bring Julien happiness.

Gods! Such exquisite work! It's … it's beautiful! I had no idea Julien had such good taste. And I guess this means he has some coin, too!\n\nTell Julien that my feelings for him have grown. Tell him I love him and I will wait for him.
I've lived in this village my entire life.  I'm not going anywhere.
I froze up. I knew what I had to do, but I froze up. Divines protect me. I've never seen anything so awful.
But sir... it's all I've ever wanted to do. You may be right, but... I'm not giving up. Next time I see a zombie, I'm hacking it to bits! Sir.
You're right. I believe you. I promise you sir, I will do better.

By Akatosh, I've never been so scared. Those things... they're monsters. What if I die, end up like them? I'm not cut out for this. Just tell Capel... something. Tell him I died. Either way, just let me leave.
Divines forgive me for being such a coward.
I... I'll try, sir. I guess if you learned to fight those things... maybe I can too. Thank you.
You have a good and kind nature.  I thank you for your mercy.
Oron is an official from the Nine Crowns.  King Fahara'jad sent him to find Ranser's killer before there's another full scale war between Shornhelm and Northmoor.\n\nHe is just inside the manor.

Shornhelm's military is invading ours.  Well, part of it.  Their military split after the last war.  Part didn't want to accept the peace with Northmoor.\n\nRanser was in Camlorn to prove he had nothing to do with the rebels.
A Reachmage in Glenumbra!  I heard of the Goblin invasion, but a Reachmage that far south!  These are sinister times indeed.\n\nOron will want to see this.

That man was a devil.  He led every charge in the last war.  Stories claimed he couldn't die...  sure as steel, he's dead though.  I saw his body with my own eyes - run through with a blade of some kind.
The Kingdom of Nine Crowns is the alliance that High Rock joined years ago.  We are united with Hammerfell and the Orc nations of the Wrothgar Mountains.

The necromancer lashed out at me, with some kind of force. It hurts, but I have an idea of where she is now. There is some kind of ritual going on-- you must stop it! I'm afraid I will be of little help to you like this.
Averos? What's that overzealous fool want with me?
Does he, now...

You want the sword too? Cursed thing! I don't have it anymore - it was bound for Aldcroft up north, so I gave it over to Katarin, a courier bound that way. Gods, I hope the Magis aren't after her too! Can you find her? \n\nBack to Glenumbra for me!
I suppose so.
More than I'd like. Everyone here has a shady past of some sort or another. Crosswych attracts exiles from all across Northmoor, and they don't come here for the sights!
Well, for one, I wouldn't call it a 'town'.  It's a village, no matter what that fool Godwin says.  I won't be staying any longer than I must. I may relocate to Wayrest - now *there's* a city!
Certainly.
They're an odd lot, that much is certain. Crosswych attracts a diverse element. Makes for interesting days, if you don't mind the rather puerile drama.

Crosswych used to be home to the miners up at Khuras, but there isn't much work to be had there now.  Most of the villagers left for greener pastures, but I like it here.  It's quiet and safe - not counting the Werewolves, of course.
Certainly.

I know it's a town by the will of Godwin alone. I doubt the Magis Order even knows we exist - a blessing and a curse. Granted, we don't have to deal with their iron-handed rule, but we also can't get the protection we need from the Werewolf threat..

Most of the townsfolk are eccentric but harmless - with one exception: Vireche. Rumor has it she was thrown out of her conclave of witches because she violated one of their rules - she killed someone! \n\nI'd be careful around her.
Can't you see them? Werewolves... just lying in wait for a chance to pounce.\n\nThis much I promise - they won't catch me unaware. I'm ready for whatever they throw my way, cursed beasts.
So Veraul's cranking that brain of his again, eh? Very good. Here's what I've observed of Shornhelm movements from my vantage above the pass.
My scouts have delivered me what they can about Shornhelm movements on the ground. Take this parchment to Veraul and we'll see what he can do.

Reports? I'm a bit busy keeping the wounded alive, here. \n\nLook, if it will get you out of my tent, here's everything related to Shornhelm that my patients have rambled about in their fevers. Perhaps it will help Eagle's Watch stop this carnage.

I should have guessed. Tarrant thinks I'm poisoning his crops.  Known the man twenty years and he suspects me of such a thing! \n\nNo, it isn't me you should be questioning - it's whoever took up residence at the Biren farm after *their* crops failed.
They packed up and left after their ground went sour, but someone's living there still - I've seen the lights myself!
It *was*. I don't know what you think you're doing here, but unless you have business with the Lion Guard you'd best leave.
That isn't your concern. Keep to your own affairs, stranger - you do *not* want to raise the ire of the Lion Guard.
That's a ridiculous accusation, and the only one authorized to make ridiculous accusations around here is me. You'd do well to remember that.

Fine! My life is forfeit anyway.

<The acolyte pulls a scrawled map out of his robe and sets it on the cart.>

I hope, for both of our sakes, that you're confident in your ability to stop her.

That's perfect! Completely unique and totally romantic! If Guendeline doesn't fall in love with me after receiving this, then there's no hope for us at all.\n\nWhat did Khalisah think? Was she glad that I took her up on her offer?
Feelings? For me? You can't be serious. \n\nI've known Khalisah since we were toddlers. She's like a sister to me. I mean, I love her dearly, but not like that … at least, I don't think I do.
All right. That's probably for the best. Otherwise, I'd always wonder what would have happened.\n\nTruth is, if Guendeline turns me down, I can always approach Khalisah.

All right. Maybe … maybe you're right. Maybe I've just been a fool this whole time, chasing Guendeline because she teased me when true love was right under my nose.\n\nWill you take the necklace back to Khalisah and tell her I was wrong?
Mother always said I was hopeless when it comes to this sort of thing. I never really thought about Khalisah in that way before.\n\nWhat do you think? Have I just been blind this whole time?

He … he does? You mean, he feels about me the way I feel about him?\n\nI don't know what to say. I thought my dreams were dead, and now you tell me that they have come true. Tell Julien to come to me. I must hear this from him.
That old sop prattling on about it again, is he? Man's got no spine. The spirits, they don't bother no one. Just weep and shriek some nights. Breaks up the monotony of duty, as I see it.

Last man to look into it - he jumped off a cliff. Still, maybe you'll do better. Heh.\n\nGo inside, then. Talk to Bhogoth. Big orc. Nutty as a squirrel. Oh, the asylum guards are all on the line now, so the inmates are running things. Watch yourself.
That'll go well for you. Digging into spirit matters, that's best left for the priests.
From what I've heard those spirits weeping about at night, what happened here years ago is best left buried. Buried deep, deep down, if you get me. You'd be better off leaving it alone.
Tell me things, you say. Crush your head, they say. So many voices. Orders. Questions. Stop crying. Stop crying. Hate crying. Crying doesn't help.

You're the same? No. Still in one piece. Not in pieces. So many pieces.\n\nI throw it away, but the key comes back. Other took it, but jumped. You take it now. Make them stop talking. Key's to the west tower. Voices are there. They're asking for you..
I'm not cut out for this!  This is supposed to be the quiet tower... get away, you'll bring them to me!

I went first, after the lock. 

I gave the child his first taste.

Going my way leads to lies, 

While the wolf's fangs close with haste.
The others can't help you. The others can't give you what I can.
Thank you.
I killed many. So, so many. Find the blood I spilled in the pass below Eagle's watch, west of our lines. We'll see their curse undone.

I was last to offer blood,

A hearty aperitif. 

Follow me where darkness dwells

And I'll tell the tale of grief.
Thank you.
The others can't help you. The others can't show you what I can.
To save his blood, I sacrificed my own. Look for me there, at the lone house west of Camp Mercy. See then how they hate me.

Guardians of noble blood,

Offered the child all we had.

I can offer only sword,

And the fight for good turned bad.
Thank you.
The others can't help you. The others can't teach you what I can.
They were so many, we, so few. The child had to be protected. Look for me in the ruins southwest of Eagle's Watch. We'll find our answers.
Just because my assignment has been quiet for some months doesn't mean that we are immune from assault, and when that time comes, I will avail myself admirably!
If you would be so kind, please tell the Warden I'll resign my post here and take whatever he has on offer.
I do!
There is much you do not understand.  This is larger than the murder of one man...
It took an evil blade to kill a beast like Ranser.  Here.  Take this back to the investigator in Camlorn.
Too much.  You must alert Fahara'jad!

Those of us among the wyrd knew of a cure for the disease which now consumes her.\n\nYou will need to collect Wolfsbane and Belladonna Berries which grow on the Spriggans to the south of here. Please, you must be swift!
Come with me, quickly!  I can track him.
Thank you.  While I prepare the cure, you should speak with Virolynn while she has the strength to respond. She is in her bedchamber. Please, do not over tax her with questions.
Oh, yes. Pierric. He left me, disappeared without a trace... is it any wonder I found comfort in the arms of another?

I have to be honest, I'm trying to put that behind me. I haven't been feeling well, and Doctor Sevarain doesn't seem inclined to tell me what might be wrong with me. Could you speak with him on my behalf?
Me? With child? What will Julien think...

Pierric is not much like other men. He spent - spends - lots of time by himself, far away from town. I admit I saw him returning late in the evening from the direction of the Wrothgar Mountains on more than one occasion...
I must break it off with Julien. I am going to be a mother. If Pierric returns, I will be forever his wife.
I should slap you for implying it could  belong to anybody else.
What do you want?  I have a long, grueling trial ahead of me, I cannot afford distraction.
Yes, of course, you're right... I must return.  I don't know what came over me before...
Guen? Do you speak the truth - I am to be a father?
What do you want?  I have a long, grueling trial ahead of me, I cannot afford distraction.
Oh, is she? I find it interesting that the person bringing me this information is the same one who fouled our sacred union...
I find that highly unlikely...
A wise choice.  Go to Thetis the Poisoner, near Grayborne.\n\nThe poison is his, and he will know the cure.

Good.  Very good.  

Take my tabard to Sergeant Gallmau on the way to Camlorn, tell him how I died and that Frey was brought to justice.

Be careful; Frey had a gang who may be looking for you.

She was courageous and determined, that one.  \n\nHere, take her tabard.  Tell Sergeant Gallmau that you took care of Frey and that Barre has passed on.  He should be somewhere on the road between here and Camlorn.
At least her death wasn't in -\n\nLook out!

Foul wolves besiege us - unnatural beasts, risen from their graves! The undead things refuse to die, and their bite spreads a wasting disease. Too many of my men are afflicted or dead already. Without help, we're doomed for sure!
I believe you have unfinished business in Aldcroft...

Wayle and I were on patrol and tried to quiet down one of the damned "Hands of Northmoor" rabble-rousers, when the man, smelling like liquor, pulled a knife on us! He said he'd be a martyr for the cause and stabbed Wayle!
I'd appreciate it. I managed to stop Wayle here's bleeding, but I'm no healer.

Well, I was worried about ol' Wayle, and tried to stop that rebel as fast as I could... used a bit o' magic to do it, just a bit of fire to scare him so's we could get away. Next thing, a crowd of people is throwin' stuff at us and so we hid here.
I don't rightly know. I cast a bit of fire-- to scare him, y'see, and then tried to get away with Waylan. I heard a bunch of shouts that we'd killed him, but I didn't use that much fire, I know it!
She is in the belly of the beast.
That is completely a pop culture reference. FIRED!

When she visited, she brought sweet things and... ugh. They were bugs. She made us eat bugs. How could she be so evil? What she did to Alaric...\n\nWhen she left, she always went north. She went into the lake. Maybe... you could start looking there?

The Chamberlain was obviously an agent of the Shrouded Throne.  I expect you will find other agents in Aldcroft as well.\n\nReturn to Aldcroft and speak to Warden Godwin, perhaps he has news of Gargast's associates.

The Chamberlain was obviously an agent of the Shrouded Throne.  I expect he will has contacted his associates by now.\n\nReturn to Aldcroft and speak to Warden Godwin.  Perhaps he has spotted the Chamberlain.

Isaac... yes. I recall the boy. Never fails to deliver my powders dry and without delay. It would be a shame to lose him.\n\nShornhelm poison is primitive - not like mine. My standard curative should work. Take this. Apply it to his wound to cure him.
Follow me! Try and keep up!

I must now return to the High King.  Fahara'jad will pardon Sebastien - his valiant defiance of the Shrouded Throne will not soon be forgotten.\n\nYou should travel to Crosswych and dispose of Gargast's allies there.

The Chamberlain was obviously an agent of the Shrouded Throne.  I expect you will find other agents in Crosswych as well.\n\nWhen you reach Crosswych, speak again to Warden Godwin. Perhaps he will have news of Gargast's associates.

The Chamberlain was obviously an agent of the Shrouded Throne.  I expect he has contacted his associates in Crosswych by now.\n\nJourney to Crosswych and speak to Warden Godwin. He may have found news of the Chamberlain in your absence.

High Rock should have fallen centuries ago.  Our borders would shift with the seasons.  Books will claim High Rock persevered due to the steadfastness of its populace.  The truth was, until recently, viciously defended.

The Shrouded Throne are commanding rebels from Shornhelm and crushing our forces at Eagles Watch in Kingsguard to the north.  If they break through...  they must not.\n\nHurry to Eagles Watch and speak to Averos.
I can't even begin to express my thanks: you clearly need no test, because even if you were a werewolf, you'd be the kind I liked. I'll send word to the Warden that you are welcome in Crosswych.

I have placed a sound box of my own design to the south of Aldcroft. When activated, they attract Bog Lurchers. My intent is to allow wardens to wind the boxes and cull any Bog Lurchers who appear. I need you to enter the bogs and test my box.
Take this to the victim, administer it as soon as you can.  My poisons are not to be trifled with!
You fool!  You had my instructions... all that matters is Morgan Frey's death!  \n\nI'll take the antidote, and only hope I can find him again and repair both our failures.
I feel stronger already... I'll deal with Frey.\n\nGo and see if you can locate his henchmen.  They camp in the forest to the west, deep in the trees.  Keep them out of my way.
Frey's band of brigands have been terrorizing the roads here for months.  His contacts in Camlorn were selling the goods; I shut them down.\n\nHe murdered my brother and father in retaliation.

My mother's alive! Not that disgusting bog witch... my real mother! She told me all about the brave knight who saved her. \n\nMother said we're going to go to the caravan to stay. We're never going to be apart again. It's all thanks to you. Thank you!

Your warning's too late, I fear. Sebastian's hall is awash with royal blood! King Ranser of Shornhelm is slain. The Redguard emissary hunts the assassin, but I fear in vain. The Adamant Crown has cracked, and war will come of it, mark my words!

Hah! Don't blame me. Blame Guillie. He's a filthy human being, and that's why his house is infested with rats... RATS. And what do they do when they can't find any food left in his house? They wander next door into mine!  I won't tolerate it.
Well, you'll have to take that up with Al'kari. She keeps roosters in her house... ROOSTERS! Guess what they do first thing every morning? You try sleeping through that!
With you and Mother, I know everything will be okay. Lead the way!
Thank you!
You'll regret this.
Fantastic! Thank you, friend. Now if you'll excuse me, I need to go gather more rats.
Who are you? Who wants to know?
I'm ready! Just let me know when it's time to go!

Indeed, you have found him. I am Oron Nassir, vizier to the Golden Court of High King Fahara'jad. My king sent me to foster friendship between two worthy kings, but now one of them is dead. Now I am hunting a murderer and a coward. Can you assist me

We must cast our net wide, before this traitor runs far. No deed this dire can be done without leaving ripples. Inquisitor Danain is well positioned to hear of intrigues. Ask him if he heard any whisperings, before or after.
He commands from Magis Order Headquarters - the barracks directly west of this Manor House.

They call Danain an inquisitor: of an order devoted to fighting evil and dark sorcery. His struggle against darkness doubtless gives him some insight into who may have done this evil deed. It would be worth knowing who he might suspect, yes?
I know a Hand well - name of Barnard. Did a right fine job cleaning up the bandits here, before he moved out to Eagle's Watch. If you're thinking of joining them, you could do worse.
The Hands of Northmoor? I honestly don't know much about them, but the ones I've met have treated me far better than those Lion Guard ruffians. They seem like stand up folk.

Bah, those layabouts are nothing more than too-rich nobles playing a game of soldiers. They'd crumble under real attack. The Lion Guard has kept us safe for as long as I remember, and they will still. You should join the Lion Guard, not some farce.

I know what I'd *like* to do, except she knew I did it - a big black cat lives behind the barracks. If you could lure it to her house, it'd scare the roosters. Cats love rabbit, if you can find one it'll follow you anywhere!

I've been thinking about this for a while... a big black cat lives behind the barracks. If you could lure it into his house, it'd likely eat the rats. Cats love rabbit, if you can find one it'll follow you anywhere!
Няв.
Няв?
Odette's gonna get you for this!
Really? Great work. Now please pardon me, I need to go to the market to purchase more roosters. The louder, the better!
Yes, praise the Divines that you've come! Let's get out of here...
Yes, please!  Let's get out of here as soon as possible...
You've done all this? Oh, you're in for it now! Come to us, bog queen! Come destroy the infidel!
But... you don't understand. She doesn't allow us to leave. The wolves will tear us to bits.
You'll really...? Oh no. It's Mother. Mother's coming!
Aye, although I may not be for much longer if these bandits hear you yammering away.  Keep your voice down!

*I* did, but my possessions did not! They looted the chest from my shop upstairs. When they realized they couldn't open it, they just took the entire thing... luckily, I keep the key on me at all times.
I'm sure they'll find a way to do so eventually. Tell you what - i'll give you the key. Bring its contents back to me and I'll reward you handsomely.

Vandica's my friend who came from the fountain! She's a little girl, just like me, but not everyone can see her. Only special people!\n\nMommy says she's not real. Vandica gets real mad when she says that, and turns all purple. Hee...

She's not! I know she's not! She flips coins and we have tea parties and she shows me... oh, I thought you were a special person, too.\n\nI know. I can prove it! I'll show you where we play. Then you'll see she's real, just like I say she is!
Try and keep up this time!
Excellent. I'm encouraged by your success; now onto bigger things.\n\nThe source of the wyrd's power is their tree. To strike against it, there are some spell components you will need.

Collect three hearts of the spriggans that guard the wyrd camp, and also some of the local Worm's Head Mushrooms.

Take this catalyst, and put them in it.

Then use the resulting potion on their tree.

Oh, the Inquisitor sent you? Right then, you'll want to start up by the temple-- you can see it up on the hill there, to the east. There's usually a priest out front, just let him know you're patrolling for us so's he doesn't get worried.
Finally, after checking on the crafters, head on by the front gates. It's always busy there, and I generally keep an eye on the tavern-- far too much drink in some people there of late.

After the temple, you want to check on the crafters in the southeast part of the city. It's usually pretty quiet there, but occasionally some fool will try to break in somewhere and do a runner out of town.
What?! We're utterly defenseless... what am I to do?
Mommy!
Oh, excellent! Thank you-- I was getting worried that we wouldn't have our usual watchful eyes keeping the peace around here. Good to see the trouble hasn't hindered the Lion Guard overmuch.

You were wise to come to me. The Hands and the Order despise each other. Neither is poised to look into this graverobbing.\n\nI know the ex-chapel keeper of Cath Bedraud well. His name is Gui. I say, investigate things with him. Keep matters neutral.

My advice? Way I see it, you crack a graverobbing ring using its hired help. They're the most like to talk with a sword under their chin.\n\nI say we shake down every bandit and mercenary in King's Guard. One's bound to turn us on whoever hired them.

Obviously, a spy within Eagle's Watch is sending tips to Shornhelm. How else could they find our dead?\n\nI believe a Shornhelm spy hides among the refugees. I say we round them up. Interrogate them. With the right persuasion, the spy will surely talk
Yeah? Or what?
Wha? What're you... talkin' about?\n\n<Braen is having difficulty focusing on you.>
Wait... Jaine is actually mad? I thought we was jes' playin'! I'm so sorry Jaine, I didn't really mean it, I jes' thought...\n\n<Braen begins mumbling to himself.>
Ol' Braen -is- in his cups just a bit, isn't he. You're right, I'll lay off. Sorry for the trouble, sir.
Blessed mercies! Where is it?
I'm right behind you!
Ні…
I'll believe this when I see it.
It mentioned reaching Annalynne? I do believe that's Warden Godwin's fiancee. Perhaps you had best warn him, they may be aiming to hold her for ransom...
I didn't... oh, Bal take you! I'm just trying... what? Ah!

The vampire… he sent us ahead, just as you. You're walking into a trap <<1>>. It's he… who wishes to control the power of the Lightless Remnant.\n\nWe must stop him before he manages to destroy all of Rivenspire. Help me… we'll fight him as one.
The Coldharbour Glyph behind you… activate it. I have already destroyed the Dark Council member who held dominion over this part of the Doomcrag. \n\nHurry… before it's too late.
Bless you, stranger!  Let's go south to the forest - I can reach my home in Glenumbra from there.
Namira's blight!  I should burn the forest down - it would end all of my troubles.

I anticipated the courier's demise.  I will send a group of Magis Order Watchers to transport his body to Westtry.  There they will prepare a ritual which will allow you to communicate with his spirit.
Questioning? Questioning about what?
What is it? What's this about?

As I said, these are hard, desperate scum. They've thus far professed their innocence, but I can see the guilt in their eyes. \n\nHave no worries, friend. We'll have a confession soon enough. For now, go gather a few more refugees - just to be sure.

No surprise. These scum are like starving dogs - they'll snap at any moment.\n\nI've good news. A refugee admitted to helping a necromancer steal bodies. My aide, Heaton, took him to Cath Bedraud to reveal his master. Go meet him behind the chapel.
You're sure, then? We'll clean up after. You'll need to tell Lady Kallath that we found the ones who killed Dalomar.
Good. Let's be done with this, then.
You're sure about this? I don't want to drag you into something this ugly. If we live, you'll need to tell the Sergeant while I keep Wayle safe.
My thanks. I could not have stood against the two of them by myself, much less three if you had sided against me.

Heaton, a spy? I'd not believe it if not for his absence. To think, he was hiding under our very noses. It's too bad you could not bring him back to be put to the question.\n\nStill... the threat is ended, for now. Tell Captain Blayne of our success.

According to my Watchers, Countess Virolynn hired a courier to deliver the weapon to a town in Daenia called Grayborne.  I sent word to Inquisitor Roche of Grayborne - if you want the weapon and the courier, he'll have intercepted both.
Countess Virolynn governs the town of Aldcroft in Urvaius to the east.  Her family was slain by King Ranser.
Watchers are the lowest ranking members of the Magis Order.  We Inquisitors command them, but ourselves answer to the noble High Inquisitor Averos, the leader of the Order.

Gerard is in the Shornhelm camp below. Enter the camp, find his tent, and steal his plans.\n\nYou could fight your way in, but I'd suggest a sneakier approach. Slay a soldier and don his uniform. Just avoid the werewolves - they won't be fooled.
This ritual will summon nearby spirits, the courier's among them.  Everything should be in place by the time you arrive in Westtry, you will simply need to make contact with his bones.

In the last war against Shornhelm, Ranser killed Ulorion the grand battlemage, High Inquisitor and founder of the Magis Order. Averos was Ulorion's ablest student, and Ulorion's successor. Averos swore vengeance upon Ranser years ago, and now he has

Averos leads the Magis Order, he's their High Inquisitor. He's dangerous: he and his Magis Order lackeys will be the doom of all Northmoor, if left alone. But there are some in Northmoor who will not leave them alone...
No...  however, you should eavesdrop on the Magis Order.  Those thugs are always crowding the Inn.  I am sure you will find Watchers boasting of Averos' deed.

I knew it! Why flee Camlorn and hide his sword if Averos were not the killer? If he can be proved guilty, the entire Lion Guard could fall. Their abuse of Northmoor would end. You must find that blade - it may be the key.
If the blade is bound for Grayborne, seek out my friend Brennoc there. I shall send word ahead , so he will stop the courier and end Averos' game before it's begun.

Now I make the poison. Simply use it on at least five rabbits near my garden. The Goblins that kill them for food will sicken and die.\n\nI sincerely hope they don't die right on my noxious herbs and crush them. This is very stressful for me.
Oh, thank you! I've been trying to find my way back to camp for hours now.
I am. Thank you for finding me and showing me the right direction!
Ah ha! Thank you.

Sadly, the size of the lake makes a search impractical. The minty smell, however, is common among Greenfoot Roots. A large colony of such grows beside the lake.\n\nBring me a sample of water from the area. I shall test it for traces of the bog witch.

I was ambushed by angry spirits as I tried to pass by the ruins! I had to leave my cart behind and just run for the city. I thought they were going to tear me apart! As if that weren't bad enough, well...
I saw bandits sneaking up as the ghosts gave up the chase. I think they've been robbing carts! It's especially bad because I was bringing weapons to one of the lords in town!

I was just 14 when my parents disappeared. I came looking here for them and then I... forgot.

Mother Murk visited often... she brought sweet things. Oh. They were bugs. Ugh, she made us eat bugs!

When she left, she went north. Into the lake.

I remember... one day, my parents just left. Then one night I heard them calling to me, from the swamp. I went into the swamp to find them, and then... she took me.\n\nWhenever she came to us, she smelled... minty. Like she'd been rolling in mint.

She said... our parents? Mother had... but she said... my mommy's alive?\n\nOoooh, that witch! She tricked us! She made us think everyone was dead! Oh, brave knight, I'm so sorry I doubted you! Please! Will you help us find our parents?
Oh, thank you! I've been trying to find my way back to camp for hours now.

I can't help you. We're under siege. Those zealous Lion Guard think I'm some sort of spy.\n\nI'd give myself up if I thought it would stop them, but the Countess won't allow it. But if you help me run the Lion Guard off, I'll ensure you can see her.

We'll release her docks as soon as she gives us the spy, Gargast. We have indisputable proof he's working for Shornhelm, and I won't have him escaping by sea.\n\nYou want to see Virolynn? Help us reveal Ghargast. Do that, Virolynn gets her docks back.

I'd not expected to need such a rare elixir out here - but I can certainly mix it for you. I would ask a favor in return.\n\nBog lurkers are a constant nuisance to the caravan. Go slay them while I mix your elixir. I'll have it by the time you return.

Indeed I have. It has been some time since I was able to work with such rare ingredients. The elixir shall be, I believe, sufficient to your needs. I wish you luck in your quest to root out the unnatural elements that threaten the innocent.

Elsie Dolban?

I'd stay away from her.  She's in league with those wyrd women up on the hill, almost a certainty.

Woman living alone like that, potions and poisons… up to no good!
At last! Those zealous fools came to their senses!
Don't splash me with elixir...
I didn't expect the Redoubt Camp to be in such good shape. Blarae's last report was much less positive. You must have done an excellent job there. I do in fact have something you can help with.

I really appreciate it. Take them to the innkeeper, Nathaniel Varle. Inquistor Roche in town is quite busy, and probably doesn't need the interruption. Varle is also a good man, and will be able to direct you to anything Grayborne needs.

I need someone to make a run to Grayborne, in Daenia. One of our inquisitors is there with several soldiers, and they're running low on magicka potions, as well as some others. I realize it's fairly mundane for someone like you.

Not a problem. Give me just a moment to inject it with one of my poisons... 

Ok, all done. Here you go.

You can find Scar's Den to the southwest.
You must intercept Gargast before he reaches his masters in Crosswych. May Gargast pay! I cannot leave Virolynn's side - I'll not fail her again!
Thank you, but wait a moment before you leave. There's more I must tell you.
Fine, help Eliana if you wish! I'll hire hunters to chase him down myself!
We must heal the Countess before she expires. I have managed to slow her bleeding and delay her death - but I cannot leave her side or she'll expire! I need your help!
Thank you! I must ease her bleeding, first. In the meantime, speak with Caldrun. There is more that you must know.
How can you say that? Virolynn's life is more important than revenge!
Of course, my friend. I will summon her.

Now that you mention it … yes.\n\nFor a most intrepid soul, a real challenge. The wyrd have stolen my staff. If you can find it and bring it back to me, I will tell you how to use it to your advantage against them.

Ah, excellent, you found my staff!\n\nThis bodes very well for you and I, very well indeed.  I will entrust you with this staff for your next task.  Take it with you back to the camp and kill the Wyress Jacinta.
Let us hurry. Arkay has favored us thus far-- let us not waste his blessings.
Let us be done with this. I worry about the forces behind these undead, that they can send assassins against us.
I'm glad to hear your opinion, and equally glad of my capacity to disregard it. Elsie *will* leave, my men shall see to it. Good day.
Clearly you require instruction in your methods of persuasion. Meet me at her house and I will demonstrate how the Order deals with situations such as these...
That's no surprise.
There is a ravine, an ancient alcove, cut into the earth, in the forest northeast of here. The ritual is taking place there. I will mark your map with its location.
Out of my way.
Good luck!

Can't say for sure... but it feels like eyes are on these farms, watching us. 

Father must have crossed someone before he went all mad in the head.  

Why would someone go through the trouble of unleashing scamps and letting our cows out? Who knows?

What do you have there? \n\nGrut-Nak's blade? You managed to defeat him? I'm impressed, but why bother? He plagues the nearby lands for days and before Alcaire can stop him, some stranger with no reason slays him. Are you after my position as a guard?

You bring me a broken piece of metal and ask me if I'm familiar with it? Is this a threat? Are you indicating that I too will soon be like that blade - broken and shattered in your hands? \n\nLet me ask you, are you familiar with my fist?
Please, I have no gold! Do not slit my throat! I did nothing, I swear it!

It looks like any other blade I've seen. You might want to head toward the keep though. Word has spread that one of the guards has her eye out for a very specific dagger. Couldn't tell you why though.

There is a curate of Arkay living in a house just to the northeast of here. His name is Marcel and he has been a good friend to my parents. He would be invaluable in our cause, but he has been cut off from Camlorn and us by bandits.

There was a ranger who knew all of the hiding places in this forest that passed through here a bit ago. He was headed past Camlorn, and some of the soldiers who came north said they saw his camp in the ruins near the city.
Watch and learn.
And you would know, I suppose?
I'd like to see him try.

You've diminished the Goblins' magic. Well done. That will go a long way towards pushing them away from Grayborne.\n\nTo truly dissuade them, we need a particular artifact: the legendary Howling Pipe.

Inquisitor Roche's men took the Howling Pipe from a sister of the wyrd they … apprehended.\n\nYou can get close to him. We cannot. Take this powder and throw it in his face. It should stun him long enough for you to get the pipe back.
What you lack in wisdom you make up for in nerve!\n\nYour meddling in the matter of Elsie Dolban made an enemy of me.  GUARDS!
What have you done?\n\nGUARDS!!
I know quite a few, but they're all terrible.
Say when you're ready.
Off to Camlorn you go!
A skeleton walks into a bar and asks for an ale...and a mop.
I could tell you about the well, but that's a dry joke.
Say when you're ready.
Off to Crosswych you go!
I named my pet salamander "Tiny" because he's my newt.
You're right, of course... *I* must return.  *You*, however, can stay here and rot, for all I care...\n\nNow give me back my robe!
I'm doing well, thank you. At least, for now.
Sadly, no. I just pay attention to the winds.
When the winds pick up, my eyes get watery and I can barely breathe. For now, though, I'm fine.
I am tired! M'lady doesn't have near enough hands for her holdings! Never a minute to m'self, that's what.
We live in interesting times, traveler. I wouldn't darken your sleep with some of the tales I've heard.
Best not. G'bye.
I'm with you, let's go!
Those thieving little Murklings are known to do more than just steal. They aren't above cutting your throat should they catch you unawares.
A cousin of mine has had several run-ins with them. And he bears the scars from their last meeting. Don't trust any Murkling. If one is close enough to speak with you, strike first!
My wife wouldn't leave the cottage lest our son return home and find it empty. Then she ran off, too. That leaves all the work to me...not that my son did much work to begin with.
Alert!  Alert!  Unbeliever in our midst!
I've had cows with more energy than he ever showed! At least my daughter will marry a good crofter to take over the farm work.

If you ask me, he's run off to join the Murklings, and good riddance to him. Always dawdling about his chores. We'll see how he likes having to steal his daily bread instead of doing honest work for it!
Just my thoughts, and I'd as soon forget them. Tell me something: what do you know of the Lion Guard?
As have I. You guard your words, which shows great wisdom. I have heard many things about the Lion Guard that trouble me, at least a little.
There may be some misinformation being spread about them. They have always been good to me. If only things were simpler, eh?
Some say their motives are not pure. Others say that only the doubters are impure. I no longer know what to believe, and that is why you find me lost in thought.
That's what THEY said...
Someone from the...Magis Order. I think. I'm not sure. It's hard to tell sometimes.
I...I can't remember. It's probably not important. Listen, please say nothing of this to anyone. I must be imagining things. Please!
Wouldn't you be? They come in, looking and touching and asking questions...sometimes more than once in a day! It's distracting me from my shop!
As a shopkeeper, I hear many things. My sources, however, depend upon my discretion. You'll hear no gossip from me.
I will speak to King Sebastian about Countess Virolynn. I need you, my friend, to speak with Baron Winoc.
You will find Baron Winoc in the northeastern corner of Camlorn.

Baron Winoc is a respected nobleman of Camlorn. I hear he is an honorable man, prominent in High Rock's militia. His defense of Northmoor doubtless alerts him to any threats to the kingdom: he may know much indeed.

The Magis are battlemages, defenders of Northmoor. They say they're our protectors, hunting hidden evils. They've become a legion of thugs, oppressing common folk at the slightest suspicion. Of course, to speak against them is proof of wrongdoing!

My sisters and I are against harming anyone, yet the truth remains: These Goblins are causing trouble. They will only cause more.\n\nFrighten them with the pipe. After that, perhaps killing their leader will finally convince them.

Not directly, not yet. The Hands of Northmoor are the original militia, who protected us of old. The Magis Order was founded to reinforce the Hands, but now eclipse them. But I've heard some among the Hands grow tired of their arrogance...

Well, I'd not want to burden you with troubles, but if you insist... Times are grim, the worst I've seen in a score of winters. Werewolves in Dwynnen, bandits on the road, and ravening ghouls here in Ykalon! All the while, strife ties our hands.

You've not heard of them? The Magis Order hunts witches and slays monsters. They were founded to defend Northmoor and they've done a fine job; I've never felt safer.  But some say they go too far. And now, I fear they have too many foes to face.

How you view them depends upon many things. Some say they bring hope to the simple folk who've struggled beneath the Magis Order's dictates. Others say they're little better than bandits. I've never had trouble with them, myself.

Look around you. The Magis Order, founded to protect us from evil, has grown so zealous that they can't tell enemies from friends. There are some calling themselves the Hands of Northmoor who've tired of them. Their feud may lead to civil war.

There were a group of Kings who ruled High Rock during a period of peace and great prosperity.  Recognizing their rule would someday conclude they sought to deny fate and extend their rule.  They became vampires.
Precisely.  I was commanded to withdraw Northmoor from the Adamant Crown.  When I refused soldiers appeared on Shornhelm's border and Ranser visited Camlorn to personally encourage my compliance.
One of them, yes.  Fear not, I walk openly beneath the sun.  \n\nHigh Rock continued to prosper under the shadow cabinet until High King Fahara'jad's sought to forge the Adamant Crown.
The good Baron told me to keep an eye out for the courier, and for you as well.

Adwyn his name is, and he's in trouble. The Magis dogs were waiting for him, and took him soon as he arrived. They've got him in a storehouse east of town, holding him tight: a brace of Watchers guard the place, threatening any who come near.
Inquisitor Roche ordered his arrest.  I am sure Roche wants to retrieve the sword before the Hands - to protect Averos from the murder charges.
You went to Daenia in pursuit of the murder weapon which was used to slay King Ranser. You were supposed to speak to either Roche or Brennoc, what did you discover?
I'd heard this through my contacts. So the second courier sent you to Countess Virolynn who was attacked by a werewolf.  Did you slay the fell beast?
I'd heard this through my contacts. So the second courier sent you to Countess Virolynn who was attacked by a werewolf.  Did you slay the fell beast?
I'd heard this through my contacts. So the second courier sent you to Countess Virolynn who was attacked by a werewolf.  Did you look after the Countess?
I'd heard this through my contacts. So the second courier sent you to Countess Virolynn who was attacked by a werewolf.  Did you look after the Countess?

These are ill times. There's enemies at the gates of Eagle's Watch, and now Crosswych is besieged by werewolves? It is time to put this new alliance to the test. Give this missive to Godwin. It will allow him to request help from Fahara'jad himself.

Murder! And a king, no less. Hospitality is broken, the king is disgraced, and who knows how it will end? This was to be an age of peace, but the old feuds still burn too hot. Now there will be war with Shornhelm. Blood from blood.

We Bretons have always fought. Daggerfall, Wayrest, Evermor-- we've shed all their blood, and them ours. Why, I can remember the last war agaisnt Shornhelm. Now we're sure to have another. May Stendarr's mercy be upon us all.

It's the Redguards-- the King in Sentinel married off four of his daughters to High Rock Kings. Northmoor, Shornhelm, Evermor, and Wayrest-- all the kings are brothers. Brothers-in-law, to be sure, but brothers all the same. And now that's ruined.

None can tell, that's the real horror. whoever the assassin is, they are long gone. There's an envoy from across the bay-- he's leading the hunt for the killer. If we can bring the killer to justice, maybe Shornhelm can be appeased.
Ranser is dead, slain under King Sebastien's own roof! The King of Shornhelm, dead. I saw his body, with these eyes I did. Poor man had been hacked near to pieces. So much blood...
They say no news is good news. Still, we have plenty of travelers passing through who tell us bits of news now and then. What interests you?
No, not really. Well, perhaps. I don't know who to turn to for advice.
Aldcroft's a good town. Small, but it has everything anyone needs. Traders pass through regularly, so our shops are usually well-stocked.
I've overheard things that I think certain people, if you catch my meaning, would pay handsomely to learn. And yet...
I have no time or patience for anyone who would give these wretches mercy.\n\nGo bother that fool Brennoc.
We're looked after here, unlike in some places. It's not perfect, but I'm happy. Of course, that could just be the ale speaking, eh?
Well, this is my hometown. Turning in strangers to the Order is one thing, but my neighbors and friends? Still...I could use the coin. I don't know what to do.
You're very perceptive. Why starve until the Countess turns in that traitor, or fend for myself in the wilderness? I'll give the Order what they want and take what I can!
Elsie! She practices witchcraft of a diabolical sort, probably taught to her by those evil wyrd.

The Beldama Wyrd … never mind that, just go meet her yourself. I'm sure once you speak to her your course will be obvious. She needs to leave town, immediately. Do this task for me and you will be rewarded ….
You are a true hero to Northmoor. I'm certain Averos will be glad of your service. Journey to Eagle's Watch as soon as you can and look for him in its west tower.
Given what you've done for Northmoor, I cannot command you. Very well. Return to me if you decide to travel to Eagle's Watch.
Before you leave, there is one other matter to discuss.
Very well. I trust your judgment. If after speaking with Sebastien you decide to investigate things in Crosswych, speak to me again.

Close one, that. If you'd not arrived to warn us when you did, we'd all have been caught with our pants down. Can't say I'd raise a mug to Averos, but his choice in spies and messengers is beyond reproach. Head back and let Averos know we won.
Westtry? That was our sister village. No one knows what happened to it, or those that do aren't talking. Iven of Westtry might know more. He's on the East side of town.
Coming right up!

Then I fear you are too late. Ranser is dead. But wait - you are the one who saved King Drugo, yes? I hear rumors - they already call you the Hero of Glenumbra. Your arrival is a blessing from the Divines. Will you help me find Ranser's murderer?

King Sebastien would never risk war by slaying King Ranser, but someone wished it to appear he did. As emissary to High King Fahara'jad, it is up to me - and you, my friend - to prove Sebastien's innocence. If not, the Adamant Crown will break.

As you wish. Once you have concluded your business, I urge you to return to me. If we cannot find Ranser's true killer, I fear Shornhelm and Northmoor will plunge into war, and our entire alliance may crumble.

Murdered in the night by an assassin. They found Ranser in his chamber, hacked to pieces. In the resulting chaos, Shornhelm's and Northmoor's delegations fled. There are many who know much, I fear, that are beyond our reach... at least for now.

First, speak to High Priest Canning - he has Ranser's body in the temple near the manse. Canning works to call forth Ranser's spirit, so that we may learn the murderer's identity from the King himself. So far he has had no success. We must learn why.
The Chalice? That beacon of darkness is a foul thing we pried from the dead hands of a daedra-worshiping witch. The world is better off without it. What use does a holy priest have for it?

I shed no tears for Ranser - the dog murdered Ulorion, our Order's founder. Yet I serve the King, and cannot let any accusation against him stand. I'm loathe to trust you numinous gravewalkers, but you may have your beacon - if you prove your worth.

You understand why we are so wary of you demi-mortal numinous. Your very existence conjures thoughts of daedra, or worse. Even so, Oron trusts you, and I see no other way out of our predicament. Take the Chalice to Canning. Clear Sebastien's name.
Oh, you seek the Soulstone of Brall? You, and so many others. You'd shudder to learn what I had to pay to acquire such a rare prize. Why should I give such a valuable treasure to you?

War with Shornhelm would raise the price of steel, but clearing the King's name will keep more of my customers alive. Very well, you may take the stone, on two conditions: first, bring it back. Second, you must earn the right. A favor for a favor.

Of course I will lend you the stone - a bargain is a bargain. A Shornhelm invasion would destroy commerce all over High Rock. For the good of our people, and of our King, I give up to you my dearest treasure. Just be sure I get it back.
Tell him fear not - I'm quite safe here. The Order is all bluster. They'd not dare threaten us, not in front of all these people. Still, I appreciate your concern. Take care.

Did he? Just between you and me, I've had my share of troubles with the Order. Nothing too bad, mind you, but trouble all the same. During the day, in the crowd, we're safe. Alone, at night... who knows? Tread carefully, friend.

I know Dalomar well - he's down here every day filling our ears with his lies about the Order. Now that you mention it, though, I've not heard any bellyaching recently. Maybe he grew tired of sedition.

You're looking for Dalomar? Well I didn't tell you, but a few days ago there was a Lion Guard bloke down here asking all sorts of questions about him. Funny type. Don't know what came of it, but best you stay clear of whole matter, I think.

I've not seen Dalomar of late - but I did hear something odd. Couple of Lion Guard patrollers were down here yesterday, talking about the fish - how they'd die choking on all their own talk. Had a good laugh about it. Odd, if you ask me.
Yes. With the artifacts you've gathered, I do believe we have a chance to contact Ranser despite the disturbances beyond the Mundus.

Yes... but we must be cautious. These artifacts glow brightly beyond the Mundus. They will attract more than Ranser's spirit. Any distraction could summon something... unexpected. When you are ready, light the Holy Incense Burner on the left wall.
Yes. We need both artifacts before we can proceed. I'll leave that task to you.
We Bretons don't live as fancy as some folks. Queen Maraya  lets me run the house as I see fit and I keep things simple. I didn't expect that, Her Grace being from across the water and all.
One of the eldest daughters of High King Fahara'jad and as practical as they come. Her Grace keeps to herself mostly, but she's open-handed with gifts come feast days.

I've been the housekeeper since before their wedding, all those years  ago.  Her Grace is pious and pure.  King Sebastien couldn't have brought us a better wife and Queen. Unless he'd married a Breton, that is.
His Grace is strong-minded, like Bretons. Some say His Grace shouldn't have married one of the High King's daughters just to make an easy peace. I say peace isn't always easy, marriage or not.
King Sebastien can be rash... he's always had that regal air. Born to it, you might say.  I will allow that His Grace throws supper across the room less frequently,  now that Queen Maraya's here.

An odd guest. Hardly ate, and drank not a drop of wine. Never wanted any of us in his rooms after he retired, not even his own manservant. If His Departed Highness had let one of us near him, maybe he wouldn't have been sliced to ribbons.
His Grace had odd Shornhelm customs...that is to say...I don't gossip about the dead. It's bad luck!
Murder, that's what! His Highness, King Ranser of Shornhelm. Dead! Benwick ran out of the guest quarters screaming, he did. I daren't go in there.
His Highness's ghost, that's who. He didn't die natural...'twas murder!
Well, I'm sure not touching it! Not alone, anyways. I know they'll make me go in there to scrub up, but I won't go alone. I'm afraid of ghosts!
So much bad news... News enough to turn your stomach. Like cheese will. Do you know what goes into making cheese? Disgusting! I'll never touch the stuff again!

Arkay preserve us! Thrandor Direnni was an Aldmer sorcerer ages ago. Legend has it his sanctum lies somewhere north of here. I will free the possessed - go immediately to the Redoubt north of Camlorn and find Commander Blarae. Recover Ranser's body!
Follow meeee!
Mother Murk is gonna get you for this!
Troubled times...you know nothing of the werewolves?

The way I heard it, the north is crawling with werewolves! The entire village of Westtry in Dwynnen has been lost to the beasts, and Crosswych is sore beset.  Can't tell friend from foe in them places.
Lets walk.
Hooray! Follow me!
Ah, Thank you. These will work just fine. If you'll just give me a moment, I will grant you your reward.

He said what? That's nonsense! The only reason Vorgo the Red Rook even knows my name is because he's robbed my shipments so many times. \n\nThe man's a lunatic, and an outlaw besides. Would you take his word over mine?
Yes! Did Geves sent you? I thought I was surely lost!
Thank you. Your efforts today have helped us all.
This is not the imposter you are looking for.
I'm not missing, I'm perfectly fine! Just need to open this chest of drawers and they won't budge. Can you give me a hand?

He was?

I see.

Would you do a bereaved wife a last favor and... retrieve his purse for me?

You will need to speak with the Princess - a lowly servant such as myself cannot offer you a blessing, even in death. Princess Aurais is just inside the castle. Nothing can touch you while you walk in the spirit world. Be safe.
I am. You do not belong here - you are not one of the Dead. What do you seek?
I have something to show you, then. Please come with me.
This way...
If only I had done something in life to deserve such chivalry. You have my blessing, Hero, for what it is worth.
I will return you to your living body, Hero. Good luck.
Excellent! Not many could defeat such a dark foe. I worry, though, that my blessed chains have broken.
What?! That is... very troubling. I must mediate for guidance. In the meantime, ask Ranger Lord Merin if anything needs to be done.
Yes take me!
Yes take me!
Yes take me!
