Teleport me out!

Wraiths in the ruins east of Camlorn attacked a merchant named Jael. Now you'll see how we turn evil against evil.\n\nWe took this Soul Cage from a necromancer. Go to the ruins.Fight the wraiths until they are weak, then use the Soul Cage to trap them.

It's the Chalice of Gwedrun you want? No one in Camlorn can be trusted, and I'll not part with it easily. Prove yourself to me by helping the Lion Guard with their patrols or by clearing the ruins of some troublesome wraiths, and I'll consider it.
Indeed you have. Very well, the Chalice of Gwedrun is yours.
Indeed you have. Very well, the Chalice of Gwedrun is yours.

Coty! So loyal. Always at my side. 

How many battles have we seen, you and I? How often have we survived, when others fell? 

Divines willing, today we'll see the destruction of the Alessian Order. Slay them all, my friend! For king and kingdom!

Daggerfall  nobles claim the deer for themselves.  There's plenty of other game, most of the time.\n\nThese days, though, a trapper might take whatever he can get, with the forests as dangerous as they are.  A man might need to poach just to get by.

I seek Dwemer relics from the distant past... relics integral to deciphering the Deep Folk.

Once I uncover them, the Mages Guild will have no choice but to invite me into their order!

If they want access to them, they'll have no choice.
So you've dispensed with Corbeau, have you? If only that were the end of our troubles with the Rooks. They're a plague on Camlorn, and a plague on my name.
This... this is my family ring. It belongs to my brother. He will be elated to receive it. Please, take this to him. He is right over there guarding the camp. You have my thanks!
All these refugees. I feel for them, and I know they need a home, but it can't be here. There isn't any room and the place smells of waste.
It's horrible what's happened there. I'm glad the Lion Guard is here to help take Camlorn back.
Werewolves took over the city is what I hear . Some say there's a big werewolf leader, uglier than most. He's what turned most of the people into werewolves.
I want to go home. Here, I'm living in my own filth. This harbor cannot support the number of people here. Duke Sebastien needs to do something to get us home.
We've all lost family in the worst way possible. I saw my own husband, he...he killed my mother when he turned into that - that damned thing.
Yes. A werewolf. That's how they do it. Take us one at a time and turn us into wolves. They make us fight for them...and do worse.
Duke Sebastien called for help from High King Geriant and His Majesty's sent Averos and his Lion Guard. I hope Averos can take our homes back from those werewolves.
They sent us here to take her back. That's as plain a mission as you could want. What they didn't tell us before we came over the Iliac Bay is that she's been taken by werewolves.
Overrun by werewolves, or overrun by men, we'll take her back. The only difference between fur and skin is they smell different when they burn.
Sibellec? I hear that her precious moors aren't hers anymore. Whatever has been happening to High Rock hasn't left her alone either.
Sibellec is the 'queen of the moors'. We've pretty much left her alone and she's left us alone.
Some people claim she came here from the Reach. I won't speak of her anymore here - her ears are everywhere!
If you ask me, Sibellec is the cause of all these troubles. That witch wants one thing: for us to be gone.
Sibellec means us no harm. She's an odd one to be sure, but she just wants to be left alone.
I don't know anything about her. Sorry.
I don't know anything about her. Sorry.
Sibellec, I don't know for sure, but supposedly Duke Sebastien is trying to get her aid in dealing with the problems in the moor so we don't have to fight a battle on two fronts.
If you tell this to anyone else I'll call you a liar, but Sibellec once cured a disease I'd gotten from a...very friendly barmaid. Sibellec is strange, but you can trust her.
Just some local witch, right? I can't say I know much about her.
Duke Sebastien and Lord Averos have cooked up some plan to use her to keep the creatures off of us while we kill wolves.
No, I've not heard that name.
Angof... yes. I think I overheard a guard mention it. They lay the troubles of the land at his feet. They say he is from the Reach.
Angof. I hear he's an agent of the Aldmeri Dominion. They call him the Master of Thorns.
Angof, no. I don't know the name.
Angof... no. The only name I know or care about is that wolf... Faolchu. I won't get a good night's rest until he is burned and his ashes scattered over the Iliac Bay.
Angof, the Master of Thorns. Yes, he's taken up in old Cath Bedraud. At least, that's what I hear.
Angof is our next stop after we liberate Camlorn. We've already got a camp near his hold out in Cath Bedraud.
They say he's got a hold on some big cemetery in the North.
I've never heard the name.
One of the refugees claims it's him what leads the wolves.
The pack leader. He's responsible for the death of Camlorn. The spit dries in my mouth just saying his name.
Damned, he is. The talk is he's a foul legend come back to life. Not like any other werewolf I've heard of, and his pack isn't afraid of the sun.
Aye, that name I know well enough. He's foul, that one is. Stinks of the grave and smells of mange. I've an arrow I'd like to test on him.
He's the pack leader. Made all the other werewolves around. Kill him and we've got a chance.
He's the pack leader. Made all the other wolves around. Kill him, and we've got a chance.
He's working for Angof. Apparently Angof raised him from the grave. Our job is to put him back there.

The sheets! The confounded sheets!

Yes, there's a band of miscreant looters down at the docks. Pirates, or their allies, I expect.

No doubt they're hiding the sheets there somewhere, hoping to sell them later. Astrid's Lot, they're called.
As you wish. Divines protect you.
Very well. Faolchu started this nightmare.\n\nDivines willing, you'll end it.

That buffon Chancellor Weller certainly has been complaining about this or that. You might try to see what has been causing the clouds to swallow his sunshine. He's in the fancy blue tents in the northeast part of the port.
Warden Rielle over at the guard tower in the southern part of the port seems to be worried about her volunteers. She's working with a bunch of raw kids trying to play at soldiering.
Lord Averos has been trying to take the war to the werewolves ever since he arrived from Wayrest. I know he's at the port's Northwestern gate looking for help on how best to take back Camlorn.
Ahnarra grieves for Camlorn. Overrun by werewolves, its citizens forced to live in filth here in Aldcroft. Once Duke Sebastien cleanses Camlorn, Ahnarra will be glad to return there.
That is a difficult name for Ahnarra. Sib...Sib...how do you say it? All Ahnarra knows is that this person lives in the swamps.
That is a name Ahnarra does not speak aloud. It is too dangerous.
Ahnarra heard that Faolchu's bite is worse than his bark.
Let's go, then.  Beware of lights over the water!

This is sad. I can't condone his actions, but he has risked his life for this community more than once. I leave this up to you. If you wish to turn him in, speak to Captain Rielle near the little house to the North.

I just combine the Wolfsbane with this potion of Liquid Silver....and there you go!\n\nMy grandmother taught me these remedies, though they've fallen from favor lately. Would you mind administering this to one of the soldiers in the tent for me?
Farewell, Coty.
Oh, you stay clear of Astrid's Nords, youngster.  They're nothing but trouble, came here about the same time as the Camlorn refugees and been trouble ever since.
Yes?  Is there something I can do for you?

Yes, yes. This will do nicely. 

I should be able to discover what's causing the poor people dying in the mine to fall under Angof's influence...

...but first, I have something for you.

What a terrible tragedy.

S'Raverr and his daughter had just moved here. The mine collapsed. Many died.  

And now?  Now it's worse.

It was Dwynarth, you know, an ancient Alyeid city.  Scholars come from time to time, to study them; I think there's some up there now.  They say you could go there sometimes and speak to those who have passed on, but it's probably just stories.
Those children... now that's a strange thing.  Running into the woods at all hours, acting strangely, even aggressively!  Each parent swears it's not their own child, but who knows...
I don't know about them running off, but one of those wee miscreants broke into my forge and stole tools and wrecked the place.  The children in this town act like none should, I tell you.
Here have another.
The tone of the crystal and the hum of the pillar combine to create a resonance that sends calm through out your body.

That cave-in... so many lives lost....

Now few will go there, out of fear. They say the mines are haunted.  

Crosswych needs that mine, though. We have few other sources of income here.
The Ironstone Mines are cursed! Everyone here knows that. \n\nThey say it's because of something the miners found there, just before the attack of the risen dead.

First, there was the cave-in. Now the mines are filled with undead. 

Without the Ironstone Mines, there would be no Crosswych, but it's been a curse as much as it's been a blessing.

Actually, it's been more of a curse lately.

The ruins? Dwynnarth was an ancient Alyeid city.

Scholars show up from time to time to study them. I think there's a few up there now.

Some say you can go there and talk to the shades of the departed. That's probably just a story.

Those old ruins? No one goes there anymore.

We have enough trouble with the mines without looking for more of it.

It's not worth looking at a pile of haunted old stones.

I think there's a scholar up there now, probably studying the stones. Most of us Crosswych folk stay away. \n\nThey say there's some sort of magical power source there, but like everything else around here, it's wretched haunted.

Something's responsible for all this.

They're running into the woods at all hours, acting strangely, and lashing out like little beasts! 

Each mother swears her child is fine. The fathers just get angry. No one wants to take responsibility.

Children in Crosswych are a menace! I've never seen anything like it. 

Simple child's mischief is one thing, but those wicked little scamps cause more trouble than you could possibly imagine.

It's disgraceful!

My own children are well-behaved, but some of the others here... well, their behavior would shock you!\n\n Aggressive, mean, and reckless. You know what? I want to know who their parents are! I blame them.

It's the high cemetery for all the Bretons... or it was, at least.

Now it's just the unholy pit these foul undead crawl from.  

The Lion Guard soldiers are doing all they can there. Can you imagine fighting the risen bones of your own kin?

Cath Bedraud? Bretons have been buried there for centuries. Even their kings and queens are interred there.

Once, it was a beautiful place, but now you can't go anywhere near it. It's too dangerous. 

If I were you, I wouldn't go there.

Once it was a beautiful landmark, something Bretons could be proud of.

Now it's just like everything else here: ruined and overrun with undead horrors.

It's the high cemetery, you know! Very impressive.

He's blighted Glenumbra.

If the Magis Order could ever defeat that vile dog, perhaps we could go back to a life without undead horrors.

I doubt that would ever happen. We'll never be rid of him.

Don't even speak that name! 

We've suffered enough because of him. For all I know, that evil wizard is watching us right now!

He's poisoning Glenumbra. No one knows what he has planned fo us.

Only this: he must be stopped.

I don't know whether it's going to take a few brave souls or an entire army.

Either way, we can't endure his evil any longer.

That place was once the home of my distant ancestors. 

You'll see Ayleid stones there. They're superior to any other magic you'll find.

Oh, and a scholar named Lael  was here a few days ago. She was headed in that direction. I sold her some paper.

I met a scholar who was headed out to the ruins.

She bought a pony from me. She needed it to carry all her books.

That's a dangerous place to study!

S'Raverr knows very little about them.

Perhaps Theldyn Andalor would know?

Yes. Ask her! This one does not know much.
I've only seen them once. They're not very impressive.  \n\nFolks only care about them because they're haunted.

Ah, the ancient Ayleid site! 

That scholar, what was her name? Lael! That's her.

She wanted us to fend off the undead while she did her research. Imagine that!

We have orders. We defend the town. As it is, we have our hands full! She's on her own.

We used to play among the stones there when I was a little girl!

We can't now, though. It's too dangerous, even if you travel in numbers.

It's never safe there, even if you're armed. You should stay away from that place.
We used to play among the stones when I was a little girl.  Not now, though - it's dangerous even if you're in numbers and armed.
The mines? Rabinna would never go there. It's much too dangerous.\n\nThis one fears for the safety of the miners.

My wife was in the mines when they collapsed last year. She was lucky to get out alive! 

Now she works in the village with me.

That place is cursed. I won't let her go back.

My sister will be working there soon.

I fear for her safety, what with all the undead and the cave-ins. Still, it's a good living, if you can survive it.  

We'll ask the Eight for their blessing and hope for the best.

My brother doesn't want me to go in the mines.

First, there was the collapse. Now they say it's haunted. 

You know what? I'm not afraid. They don't scare me.

I was one of the lucky ones. That's all I'll say.  

It's folly to go in there again, but a man has to feed his family somehow.

 We do what we must.

These Bretons are fearful of the mines, but how bad can it be? 

I spent seven years cutting rock in the Alik'r Desert! I had scorpions in my boots and sand sharks breathing down my neck.

If there's good money to be made here, I'll take my chances.

There was a cave-in there last year, during the Second Seed.  

Many miners perished. Now the place is thick with undead.

I don't want to see their faces again.

I don't know much about that mine, except there are plenty of undead to fight.  

The people here say it's cursed. I don't know if that's true.

The place is full of walking dead. That's bad enough for me.

Children. What a delight! 

S'Raverr has seven of his own. This one's daughter, Rabinna, helps S'Raverr here. 

Be careful of these Crosswych children, my friend. They're not... quite... right.
Rabinna would like to have children someday, but not if they resemble those Crosswych terrors. \n\nThey're wicked little things!

The children in this village are a menace!

I think it was Panoit's boy who broke into my forge and stole my tools.

He says it wasn't, of course, but they're lying little thieves!

One of the girls here was trying to herd all of our goats.

Turns out, she was trying to send them off into the marshes. 

It's strange how the children around here act, sometimes....
I caught one of those little wretches sneaking into our supplies the other night.\n\nHe ran away before I could get my hands on him! He has no idea how lucky he was....
Everyone complains about the children.\n\nWhat can we do?  We're soldiers, not nannies.
I've seen children run through these gates and out into the forest at all hours of the night.  \n\nCan you believe it? What kind of parent lets their children do that?

The great cemetery?

S'Raverr has never been there, but this one knows that's where the Bretons keep their dead.

There must be hundreds of thousands of Bretons in that cemetery. Even the most exalted kings are buried there!

Remarkable, isn't it?
Rabinna doesn't know much about the cemetary, only that it's of great importance to the Bretons here.\n\nThis one is not an archaeologist. This one does not understand.

Cath Bedraud! Now that's a cursed place, if ever I knew one.

Our order needs all the help it can get there. I took a wagonload of weapons to them a fortnight ago.

I sincerely hope they're not all dead by now. One would hope.
If there's an evil heart hidden in this land, it beats somewhere in there.

Angof. Yes. Of course. 

They say... they say he is the cause of so much trouble here.

They say horrible, evil things about him!

Forget about that for now. Have some wine.

He has brought great misery to many.

Someone should cause him some misery!

That would be justice. Someone should make him miserable.

My uncle is a forester. He works in the southern woods. 

Have you seen what Angof has wrought there?  Do you know of the evil that came to those woods?

He's twisted the land. He's poisoned it. Now his legion of bones threatens everything we have.

There are those here who won't even speak his name out loud.

They're afraid he'll hear them.

I'll say no more about the matter.

They say he listens through the briars.

They say his evil seeps under every rock and into every shadow. His curse is spreading, reaching to the farthest corners of Glenumbra!

Something must be done before it's... too late!

That's what they say.

Our troops marched through Wrothgar on our way here. I saw his handiwork as we passed Cath Bedraud.

He has no tactics or strategy. He wants to poison everything here, scheming until all of Glenumbra has been corrupted.

That seems to be working.

Angof? That's the one villain I'd like to kill more than any of my other enemies. 

Cut off the head, and shortly thereafter, the head will die.

They should let me at him. I'd solve all this with one swift stroke.

Skorvild the Smithy says my boy Etienne broke into his forge. 

He claims my boy stole his tools and wrecked the place. I know it wasn't him. He's a good boy!

I saw the footprints, though. It was someone's child... but whose?
Vartisans are skilled practitioners of the art of maintaining the Varlines passing through Tamvir, Varlines which keep the Altmer magic flowing strong.

Very astute. As a rule, Intricants maintain Imago Serries spread across Varyllis, but the Imagerie is Langdruun's crown jewel. He would not trust it to any but me, and I am still close enough to the Kinhouse to respond quickly if the need arises.
Do I look like a wyress? All I know is I asked Alene what she needed, and she said spriggan limbs. She knows her stuff.\n\nYou still wondering? Go ask Alene.
This appears to be what is left of an Enchanter's Staff.\n\nFrom the markings, it cannot suggest anything other than the Maormer were trying to control The Serpent.

What is this? It's... magnificent! Where did you find this? No, it matters not.

Normally I'd charge a fine bit of gold for this, but since I'm so low on supplies....

Let's see what we can do. Please, abide for a moment.
Foul undead assault our lands from the south, and the thrice-cursed Maormer continue their onslaught unabated. I advise you to seek sanctuary at the Kinshouse.
I have been blessed with the task of supervising the maintenance of the Imago Serries and the Imagerie. The Imagerie is the crowning achievement of the Felballin Kinshouse.

Who would dare to challenge us?  Who would dare to threaten our very Mother, whose magic is older than even these temples that have risen and fallen again all around us?  Who dares to poison the Great Tree against her loving daughters?  Who?

Once, none would dare come close enough to we sisters to ask these questions. Once, we sisters would not answer. But now there is a darker and greater magic than our own, and I tell you this: we must be rid of it before it destroys us all.

There is a witch in the bog who styles herself a queen.  We sisters do not like her.  Her magic is that of the Reach, and she is greedy for power.  Yet it was not her magic that took our home from us.

The trees whisper of ships on the western shore.  What fools men are, who wage their wars while the Mother languishes and the land rots under their feet!  When the battle is done and bodies bleached to bone on grass, we and our Tree will remain.
To the west on the shore, a fool and his servant brave the harpies to catch fish.  Fish!  He should hope someone saves him, before the hunter becomes the prey, and well deserved!
Have you seen the fishermen on the western shore?  Those harpies will eat them alive if they're not careful.
When I first came to the Great Tree, I thought nothing could ever threaten Her magic.  I was wrong.  Now we will be more vigilant.  This will not happen again.
Before the corrupting spirit came, the spriggans were friendly and peaceful creatures.  Now they must either be purified or destroyed.
I'll try not to slow you down.
Tell Vestrial I tried my best.
Optimate Telenger was dispatched to rid the shores of the undead, but I wonder if his force is enough to destroy them. Such a concerted attack must be the orchestration of some greater threat.
Though I have studied the Varlines, those rivers of Magicka that flow across our land, I have much yet to learn. For instance, can a damaged Varla Lens truly be repaired?

I believe so! A tome, Varlines and Vartisans, describes the process in detail - but alas, it was taken by Hainen the Deranged.\n\nSeek the book in Hainen's mountain retreat, up the path northeast of here. And tread lightly!

You tell me! I've seen stranger things in my lifetime.

My eyes may grow weaker with each passing day, but I know a mudcrab when I'm speaking to one!

Where is your shell?

Why do you want to know? Are you here to steal my shells? I know you're up to no good! You're just like that crazy woman to the north of here.

These shells sell for a good bit of coin; you won't take them from me! 

Leave me and my shells be.
To the north of here, along the beach. Crazed lady trying to plunder riches of the dead. She's wild as can be.\n\nI'd stay away from her if I were you. Something is not... right with her.
From here that horn appears to be of Nord craftsmanship. May I have a closer look?

Eccentricity is tolerated, but I fear Hainen has quite lost his wits. He is said to be attempting to create an Imago Serry by turning living people to stone. What madness! To think my wise teacher could fall so far....
The Maormer are formidable enemies. Their knowledge of engineering and the sea allowed them to design a massive ship with the ability to churn through earth as easily as water.

If you travel due east, you will come upon the Tower of Verdant Grove, which sits perched on the edge of the Stonewake. \n\nThe Stonewake was created by the magics of Landbreaker. Follow the wake north, and there you shall find the shattered ship.
They wished to destroy our blessed Crystal Tower. However the arrogant Maormer underestimated the power of the mages there, who were able to destroy the ship just short of its intended target.
Quest NPC always told me to steer clear of that puppy.  I just wanted to pet him and he ate me!  I'm going to go back to him... he is probably sad without me next to him.

The Maormer have managed to sweep up the southern shores of Sunhold Island and only the Oyinaam keep them from advancing.  \n\nThe music created by the Oyinaam repels them. Obviously their taste in the arts is as muddled as they are.

Greetings Advuenturer, I am the great and all powerful Important Mage. I see you have managed to find the magical tome.  That tome would increase my powers and allow me to become the most powerful mage in the land...
Fantastic! HAHAH!  Quickly, dig out the tome and give it to me!
What?!  I MUST have that tome.  You shall regret that decision... I shall return when you least expect it!
I want that tome.  If you give it to me, I will reward you handsomely.  What is your decision?
I am an Exemplar, the embodiment of the power and glory of the constellations. However, I am but one piece in the grand orchestra.

Because the Beacon drove the Discarnates Rogue, which makes it permissible to slay them and harvest their Daedric Soul Gems. Why else?
You found one of Commander Lafavre's soldiers. He did not make it.
Five thousand lamentations! All is over - but Altmer dignity requires making an appropriate end.
I am under no obligation to answer. I have provided aid, as Rolantae wished me to.
It would not be wise to speak of it here. Open it when beset by enemies, and not a moment before.\n\nThis is not hyperbole, but a sincere warning.
No. Rolantae and I never required more than one.\n\nAnd thank the Firmament for such meager graces as that.
We were collegues. Classmates at the Psijic Academy on the Isle of Artaeum. We even shared lodging for the last decade of our schooling.\n\nMore than that I do not care to discuss with strangers.
A Kirin? I don't believe such a creature exists!

Hmm... a Kirin? Are those the lovely quadrupeds I always see lying under the Bonfom Benla Trees? Those trees have the strangest appearance - with those yellow leaves and white bark. I never understood why we even cultivated such plants.
K Bye

It was horrible. When Orgnavar replaced Auri-El, the Skyharkers bound to Auri-El wailed hideously and tore at their eyes... they became the Starblind.\n\nThen Prime Skyharker Suuniqwe disappeared! Skyharker Vilmo is the new Prime Skyharker.
Our ancestors built these defenses several centuries ago. The lines of stone channel the power of the Varlines to enhance our protective magics.

It is without a doubt the most definitive text on the Vartisans' craft. Hainen stole it from the Kinhouse several days ago, for reasons I cannot fathom. What could he stand to gain from a Vartisan's knowledge?
hullo thar

The Isquer Kinship has long been protectors of Mara's Shrine, The Fane of Breath. \n\nI am honored to be among those protectors, but our focus has shifted to repelling the Pallid Devils in the south.

Today I roam the land
I'll always lend the weak a hand
I am a soldier know me by my arms
I trust I will be kept from harm

A title of respect precedes my name
I'd rather die than have to suffer shame
In stories and a game I live today

What am I?
Wow.... You really are an idiot
Your such a wait.... You actually got it right?  Umm... Still get out of my face!
Hahaha.... Wow.... No....
You must be the biggest idiot in the world.  I was right about you!!!

Who are you to deliver this to me?

Matters in the keep must be worse than I feared. Now Lakana entrusts her letters to strangers.

Wait... this letter speaks of a threat to her life. Apparently, she doesn't believe Duke Nathaniel can protect her....
I knew it! Go get him!

That's disturbing news, but not unexpected. Lord Montclair will wait for someone to release the captives.\n\nThis could be the first major move against our interests, especially if these people are infected with blood fever. We must strike first.

Have you lost faith in House Tamrith so quickly?  

If the affliction spreads through the city, we'll be as good as dead. We cannot let the infected escape alive.

If you want to help, then tell me: who did she send you to rescue?
Uhn... the altar's true name? It's... jakay-jhe. Speak that to banish the altar and its spell.\n\nThat's all I know. Please, don't hurt me anymore.

All Daedra have both a true name. These are words of power to banish it back to Oblivion.\n\nThe altar holding Vanne is a Daedra - though not intelligent. It resists traditional magic. But if a coven member reveals its true name, we can banish it.

It's tricky, but I've learned a thing or two about manipulating Daedric essence. Simply put, we need more Daedric essence than powers the altar - hence why you'll collect the hearts.  I'll extract their energy and use it to break the altar's power.
I know what this looks like, but I'm not responsible. \n\nRemember the letter you delivered to me from Lakana? It exonerates me... and it incriminates someone else.
Not so fast. I can't resist leveraging a business opportunity....\n\nSome brigands have taken a foothold in one of my storehouses. Take out their leader, and I'll give you the letter.
Good. My storehouse is the southernmost building on the east side of the creek. \n\nI'm sure that ruffian will be no trouble for you.
That may be, but I still do what I can to make my way in this world.\n\nIf you won't help me, I have more pressing matters to attend to. Good day.

By Ruptga! You are a good friend to have, <<1>>.

I'll bring these lists to Captain Rodrick. I'll expose these Bretons for what they really are. 

I can't wait to see the look on his face! Now I'm certain to get a license.
Of late I noticed how Sir Hughes would eye my wife. She was a most rare beauty - the type of beauty a man would kill to possess.
I trusted Sir Hughes with our lives. I never thought would betray us! I fear he killed that which he could not have...\n\nHe will pay. By the Divines, he will pay with his life.
What else would you like to know?

One of my spies said that Ra'ud at-Mara contacted him. He's trying to sell information about a threat to Alcaire.\n\nRa'ud is a slippery fish. I don't like dealing with him, but he's our only lead. He's at the Mule and Bull. See what he knows.
Who spoke those words to you? Who sent you?\n\nYou tread on rocky ground.
There's a short list of people who know those words are important to me. I'll have to pay each of them a visit. \n\nSo, you have my attention. What do you want?
Tailas and I will have a conversation about the virtue of silence. \n\nDoubtless he sent you with good reason. Tell me why you're here... and what you want to know.

Have a care. Attentive ears are everywhere.

No, the Brotherhood didn't act against her. However, I do know the party responsible for this indiscretion. 

I can tell you... after you fulfill a contract for me. One bloodstained hand washes the other.
Then our business here has concluded.\n\nOn the topic of our conversation, know this: Discretion is best for your health. You will be silent... or you will be silenced.
Be careful of the guards. Sometimes, they are displeased to discover the murder of upstanding citizens.\n\nIf anything goes wrong, you do not know me.

A merchant whose name I can't disclose has requested the elimination of his competition.

You'll remove that target before he ever gets here. 

Here's the plan: you'll follow a Alcaire merchant to a secluded location and then dispatch him undetected.

Master Ahtah's Book of Circles is an ancient copy of Frandar Hrunding's venerated Redguard tome. It predates the reign of Reman III. When he took power, he altered passages in the book.\n\nUnaltered versions are rare. They cannot easily be replaced.

Rin and Makana are sister and brother. They came from Al'akir to study with Master Ahtah. Christophe is a young Breton, one of Master's most promising students.\n\nChristophe and Rin met here and fell in love. I doubt Makana ever got used to that.

Excellent, I have something for you. \n\nFor recruitment purposes the Brotherhood keeps track of all those who kill in cold blood. This particular list contains the name Lakana. Next to her name is that of her killer's. You may have it.
That is fine; all other murderer's names have been redacted. \n\nDo not think to use this list to incriminate me. I have another list, upon which your name is written.

Nonsense! Speak with my head councilor, Juillen. He can vouch that I've been in court all day. 

If my court is spreading whispers about me, I will certainly do something about it.

Thank you for bringing this to my attention.
Not much of a rumor, but they've got a witch over in the stocks. She killed her husband, they say. Some Lion Guard soldier named Derelle is taking her side. If you ask me Derelle is a witch too.

Names don't matter in these dark times. What does matter is what the group I work with fight for. We are known as the Ravenwatch and if not for us, this town would of been overrun weeks ago. \n\nOur leader sent me to assist you against the Bloodsworn.

The battle of Shornhelm is just a glimpse of what is to come from the west - the Doomcrag. \n\nYou should investigate it youself. Come to your own conclusions. When you return... seek us out in the under city. We'll have the answers you search for.

He thinks you to have a special ability that could aid us. The Bloodsworn you slew was just one of many who wait in the shadows, eager to strike. You defeating him was a test to prove yourself to us - in which you succeeded.
There's still sounds coming from the east. Are you and Jerwinna going to do something about this?
Good luck!

I know about Dabienne, but I've had no luck freeing her. The townspeople are agitated. If you know some way to free her, I'd welcome your help.\n\nConstable Sal's at the center of town. Convince him to release her, and I'll make sure she's protected.
Back again, I see. Are you interested in taking up my offer? I will give you the evidence you seek, if you take care of a contract for me.
Be careful of the guards, they sometimes frown upon the murder of upstanding citizens. If anything goes wrong, you do not know me.
Then our business is done. On the topic of our conversation, discretion is best for your health.

A merchant, whose name I cannot disclose, has requested that we eliminate some competition before he moves in to the region. All you must do is follow an Alcaire merchant to a secluded location and dispatch him undetected.

Not so fast. I never pass up a chance to leverage a business opportunity....

Thanks to Lakana, I can no longer do business in the shadows. I require a license to operate in Alcaire. 

Help me get one, and I'll share what I know of Lakana's murder.

The duke only allows a small number of licensed vendors in his lands. 

However, if the duke found out about the local merchants fixing prices, he'd revoke their licenses.

Get me the price lists from three corrupt merchants. I'll expose them all.
Good. And here's a friendly warning: Alcaire's guards react strongly to any threats to the local merchants. \n\nIf you're going to do anything illegal, you'd best do it out of their sight.
I don't care. Bribe them. Intimidate them. Rob them. Kill them.\n\nDo whatever you feel must be done. Just don't fail me. I want those lists.
The blood of an innocent - indeed, this will please our Prince greatly. Be a lamb and place it on the altar, dear. We'll step from the shadows once you've placed the sacrifice.

Honestly, it worries me. Long ago Sotha Sil made a pact with the Daedric Princes, forbidding casual summoners from unleashing them.\n\nHowever, the Glenmoril Coven have ancient ties with Hircine - if they asked, I don't know that he would refuse.

From what Inwold said, the coven member who was to sacrifice him was named Sister Agnes. The other coven members may not know she's dead.\n\nI'll stay here for a bit. If you bring me the robe of a coven member, I can spell it to disguise you as Agnes.

Daedric Princes are fickle, and Hircine prizes only mortal sacrifices. Sacrificing one of his prized Hernes may enrage him.\n\nIf you gather a fresh Herne heart and place it on the coven's altar during their ritual, I bet *bad* things would happen.

Excellent. This will do nicely. Give me just a moment... there.\n\nDon't put the robe on until you're going to use it. The enchantment will only last a short time. And don't get too close to the coven - they know magic, and they may see through mine.

It's coming back to me. It was late, and everyone was asleep.

I heard shouts from inside Ahtah's study. I entered to find Christophe crossing blades with Rin. He had Ahtah's Book of Circles clutched in his free arm.

Naturally, I helped. He fled.

Rin protected Christophe, even when he refused to take the Dreamless Potion. She didn't want him exiled. When I found out, what was I to do? Turn in my own sister?\n\nChristophe did this. He thinks he can summon a Shehai. We had to try and stop him.
Ask anything you wish.

A madness afflicting Menevia. We believe it comes from the dreams of its people.\n\nThose with the fervor think of nothing but the wants of the day, with no care for future or past. Immediate gratification is more important than their own lives.

We do not speak openly of her, for many in Stormhaven would frown on our beliefs. She cares not for empty worship. She values the defense of the people over credit for her grace.\n\nShe is dusk and dawn, mistress of twilight. I say no more than this.

Long ago, our benefactor gave me a recipe - a Dreamless Potion. All Spirit Wardens imbibe it nightly. We cannot permit ourselves to dream, you see, or we could fall into nightmare. We live only in the waking world, as our benefactor has charged us.

We are protectors. We do not dream. To do so exposes oneself to threats beyond those most can see. These are what we stand against - the smoky black tendrils of the nightmare.\n\nYou may have seen the fervor throughout Menevia. We work to stop it.

You have been a great friend to us. Now, I need your help.

My initiate, Fahjiri, went to the shrine to the east to complete her rite of passage as a Spirit Warden. She has not returned.

Search the shrine for her. Bring me news of what you find.
Dusk and dawn watch over you.
I understand. If you change your mind, please speak to me again.

A Shehai is a mighty spirit sword, created by a master Sword Singer by weaving magic, artistry and the powers of one's own mind. It is a deadly weapon, unseen since the days of Frandar Hunding, who wrote the Book of Circles.
I...I've been drinking for so long now, everything in my past is a blur. Some days, I don't even remember my own name.

A Shehai is a mighty spirit sword, created by a master Sword Singer by weaving magic, artistry and the powers of one's own mind. It is a deadly weapon, unseen since the days of Frandar Hunding, who wrote the Book of Circles.

We were Ahtah's apprentices at Pariah Abbey. My sister Rin protected Christophe. She did not want him exiled by the Spirit Wardens, despite his odd behavior.\n\nChristophe stole Ahtah's Book of Circles and summon the Shehai He must be stopped!

Several nights ago, I heard two Knights of the Flame talking.

They claimed Lakana was raising a revolt against them. They said Sir Hughes should "take care of it."

I tried telling James Tailas, but he paid me no heed. He should have listened to me!

You mustn't be from around here. Everyone knows how King Ranser declared war on Wayrest. Tried to show High King Emeric what for!\n\nTruth be told, it didn't go so well. After about a year, Ranser was defeated. Happened right up there on Traitor's Tor.

Fahjiri was trapped by dro-m'Athra. You slew it. This one is grateful to be free.

Yet Fahjiri worries. The evil used this one roughly. It learned things about Durak. It hungers for him. 

There is danger. Go warn Durak, now! This one will follow!
What would you ask of Fahjiri?

This one came to complete the ritual. All Spirit Wardens do. This one drank the potion, and the dro-m'Athra came - a nightmare! The potion was to stop dreaming, not summon it!\n\nThis one was bewitched, held, hurt. Fahjiri wishes never to dream again.

It is a Khajiit word. Nightmares. dro-m'Athra have haunted Fahjiri since this one was but a kitten.\n\nFahjiri fled Elsweyr to be free of them, and lived many years in Stormhaven without nightmares. Months ago, they came again. Durak offered help.

Fahjiri's mother was once trapped in a nightmare by the dro-m'Athra when Fahjiri was still in her womb. Mother escaped, but was forever scarred.\n\nFrom birth, Fahjiri has been tormented in dreams. Only leaving Elsweyr allowed Fahjiri to escape.

For many years, the dro-m'Athra let Fahjiri be. Fahjiri heard rumors of Pariah Abbey, of those who do not dream.\n\nWhen the dro-m'Athra came to Stormhaven, Fahjiri came to Durak for help! Fahjiri fears Durak's help left him open to the dreams.

Poor souls in Elsweyr have been trapped like Durak, asleep without waking. The dro-m'Athra come and trap them in nightmares. \n\nDurak searched Fahjiri's soul to try and sever the link to the dro-m'Athra. This one fears they found him through the link.

Could it be? Could the dream world have taken Durak, even while he was awake?\n\nThere is only one way to find out. If Durak is indeed trapped in the dream world, I must go there. I must free him, even if costs me my life.

You would risk yourself, for us?

Sep's skin. If you weren't right, I would try and talk you out of it. With Durak gone, I must lead the Spirit Wardens.

If you really wish to do this, you'll find a potion in our shrine to Azura beneath Pariah Abbey.
You have done all you could. If I live to see another day, we will speak again. I must prepare.

The Dreamless Potion is not all we have learned. We have a potion of dreaming as well - endless dreaming.\n\nAt any other time, I would not think of using it. There's a good chance anyone who drinks it will never wake. Even so, I must try.
What would you know?

I had a dream when I was born. I was to found an order and lead it against a great evil.\n\nIt was only after growing in Orsinium that I realized I was not destined to lead orcs. I came here, to Stormhaven, and it is here the Moonbird came to me.

The Moonbird taught me of the Dreamless Potion, and of the nightmare that lurks in the dream world. It showed me where to build Pariah Abbey, and I carved it from rock with my magic. It told me one day, Azura would call on what I had made for her.

Like Azura herself, it is a wonder to behold. Its crystal feathers glitter like cut diamonds, and its center glows with light. It is wet and slick to the touch, like glass in rain. It speaks inside my mind, and in the minds of those who serve me.

Like all Daedric Princes, her motives are unknowable. I like to think that Azura cares for all her children, and foresaw the madness Vaermina would unleash upon them. Whatever her reasons, we serve her with all our heart and soul.
S'Rashi will not forget your generosity.

S'rashi is known throughout Wayrest. Ask anyone where they would go to find out something. They say, "S'rashi knows! Go to S'rashi."\n\nIf you can't trust S'rashi, this one has no desire to do business with you. Trust S'rashi.
Let me see. Ah, this is a platinum-level invite. The count says you get to come and go as you please.\n\nThat's more leeway than he usually gives his guests these days.
He's in the manor with his betrothed, <<1>>.\n\nTonight's festivities have already resulted in four deaths. Better hurry.

They've begun fusing my soul to the Book of Circles. We're already merging as one.\n\nThe book's power can save or destroy entire villages, but it can only be activated when it's joined with a spirit warden.
If you want the Moonbird, then make me a good offer!

Oh ho ho! What a grand tale you weave. The fate of Stormhaven rests on you acquiring my Moonbird? If only I'd known!\n\nI applaud your bravado. However, the fate of Stormhaven doesn't reimburse me for my time. Make me another offer!

My menagerie lacks one creature: the rare and angry Wyvern. They are vexatious to capture and impossible to tame. However, if you gather an egg from cliffs to the north, I could raise one as my own.\n\nSo, shall we trade? The Moonbird for a Wyvern Egg?

While I am sorry we could not do business, I welcome you to think on my offer as long as you wish.  Please feel free to come and go from my estate at your leisure. You have done great service to my friends, and will always be welcome here.

Now that is an offer! It just so happens I need a warrior of your prowess.\n\nI would not be loathe to part with the Moonbird for a creature of equal value. I am wary of Daedra. The clever creatures can turn on one at any time.  I propose a trade.

<It would be difficult to escape were I in my true form. I will transform into an egg. Place me in your satchel.\n\nOnce transformed, I will be helpless - but should any guards search you, they will have no way of knowing I am inside such a small egg.>
Excellent
<Very well. Return to me when you can... but hurry. Every moment that passes, The Fervor consumes more of Menevia.>

Oh ho ho! Well done, hero, well done.

This wyvern will be raised by me, loyal to no one else. Imagine, being the only noble in all of Wayrest with a tame wyvern!

My men brought the Moonbird out to the pool. Per our agreement, you are welcome to it.

<It is dangerous to cross Menevia in my true form. I will transform into an egg. Place me in your satchel.\n\nOnce transformed, I will be helpless - but should any search you, they will have no way of knowing I am inside such a small egg.>
Excellent
<Very well. Return to me when you can... but hurry. Every moment that passes, The Fervor consumes more of Menevia.>

Sir Hughes claims he was under a spell. Ensorcellment drove him to murder my beloved Lakana. 

Without her, my nights are too long and my days too numerous. 

I can't think clearly. You saw Hughes. What do you think I should do?
I trust your conscience. \n\nIf you feel Sir Hughes must pay for his transgression, then I'll prepare for his execution.
I trust your conscience. \n\nIf you feel Sir Hughes wasn't responsible for his actions, I'll prepare for his immediate release.
I'll tell you everything that I can, but we must hurry. They stole Ahtah's Book of Circles, and now they are stealing my soul.

The basecamp is through the door over there. Keep going up the stairs. I'm holding the creatures off as best I can.\n\nThey left me behind, and I wasn't fast enough. One of the bloodfiends grabbed me. I feel cold. I feel ... hungry.

Azura is a Daedric Prince and ruler of Moonshadow, a twilight country of shades and half-thoughts. While the Divines remain distant and aloof, Azura touches our lives every day.\n\nWe believe, unlike her Daedric kin, she wants what is best for us.

Yes. Sabotage. Daedric Princes like Hircine value mortal sacrifices only. Sacrificing one of his prized Hernes may enrage him.\n\nCollect a Herne heart, and place it on their altar during the ritual. If Hircine reacts, it may distract Nissa's guards.

You'll need a disguise to get close to the altar. Take a robe from a Glenmoril Coven Initiate. Put it on before you place the Herne heart on the altar.\n\nThe disguise should keep the coven off you until it's too late. Then, it's just you and Nissa.

When I came in this morning, I saw signs of a struggle. Master Ahtah's study was in disarray, his Book of Circles gone. Dried ink covered the floor.\n\nI saw three sets of inky footprints leading to the window: two sets chasing one, as if in pursuit.

I think Makana fought Christophe, and Rin tried to stop them.

Makana hated Rin's romance with Christophe, especially since Rin's first husband died in a duel defending her honor.

I bet one of them took the book. Maybe a Spirit Guard saw something?

I saw a scuffle on the road: two chasing another. I thought they were bandits!
 
A mob took one to Hammerdeath Arena. They took the other to Baelbrone, a den of drunkenness and debauchery. 

Where will you start looking?
I wish I'd done something to help them, if I'd but known who they were.\n\nI wish you luck tracking them down, my friend.
I wish I'd done something to help them. If only I had known who they were!\n\nI wish you luck tracking them down, my friend.

Can't say as I know any of those, but as far as Redguards go, Moric Nirine has this beast of a woman in his stable. She fights like no woman I've ever seen!\n\nWhen she's not drawing blood, I hear he keeps in the slave pits beneath the arena.
Haven't heard of any of those. Couldn't hurt to keep asking around, though!
They say that their grazing land has been flooded. They don't understand the nature of progress; the river must be dammed to irrigate our crops. Many people live in Stormhaven, they must be fed.
Who knows why ogres do anything? Perhaps it is just because they don't like anything that is bigger than they are. All I know is that they must be stopped.

Save me? They need us both! Without my soul or the Book of Circles, the ritual will fail.

Ahtah can use the book to restore all of Menevia, but I am just one man.

You can save me or the book. Breaking our bond will destroy one of us.

Then Ahtah's Book of Circles will be destroyed, and they can never use it to destroy Menevia.

Act swiftly! Release me from this spell before their ritual is complete.

I can get out of here by myself. I'll meet you at the cave exit.
Then I go to the home of my ancestors, knowing that the Supernal Dreamers cult has been defeated.\n\nAct swiftly! They have nearly completed the ritual! The book is over there....
You step through the portal.
You step through the portal.

The creatures must have infected them while they were held captive. 

Why did my visions not show me this? The power of Montclair's magic must be clouding my sight!

Yes! That has to be it. We still have time to stop them.
I think … I think Hinault's son is right. I think I did attack his father.

The prisoners we freed!

Several of them went back into the city against our warning, insisting they were fine. My visions did not say otherwise. 

We'll need to find them and see if they are infected! I know of three. They could endanger us all.
What else would you call it, when one's prey lies prone and helpless before him?
A tempting proposition, but this one must decline your offer. Perhaps another time.
Ugly, is it? And smelly? Why...!\n\nStep forward, you hideous wretch. You're going to pay for those insults.
Yes. I know.\n\nWhat is your point?

Sorcassil hired Shadowhiskers for this job, yes. Normally this one does not take assassination contracts... but the Canonreeve made an impressive offer.\n\nSuch treachery! The Canonreeve must be exposed, no? Go then. Tell your people.
I'll go away. Far away. I'll find a place to hide, someplace where I can't hurt anyone.\n\nI don't trust myself. Stendarr help me! I'm so hungry!

From Hotspur? It's been a while since I've seen him. He's not someone you'd soon forget, if you know what I mean!

Yes, I have some nice grain. For the Horsemen, it's free of charge. You can take it.

Oh, and... tell Hotspur that Nathalie said hello.

I'm not surprised! Though my clan has tended its herds in <<1>> for hundreds of years, we keep to ourselves.\n\nThey say we're descended from the giants of <<2>> because of our courage and strength. We're like our horses: proud and enduring.
It's Jenny! Whenever someone touches Jenny, she hurts me! That's why I put her in my toy box. \n\nPlease, make the bad things go away so we can go home again. I want to go home!
Yes...thank you. Can we go home now?
Only Godrun has the key. You will likely have to take it from him by force. You will not stand a chance with his men around; you will have to wait for them to go on patrol.

I am in your debt, but I still need your help. Godrun may be insane but he is right, the dam must be defended. Perhaps he will see the light if we take care of the ogres.\n\nMeet me at Camp Gavaudon, to the north, and together we will deal with them.
Thank you.

Hah.  Well.  Nathalie.

She's a fine woman.  A good friend.  

... why, what did she say?

Hrm.

So... all right, then.  Other topics.

Too bad about the weather.  And the corpses.

Nathalie?  Well.

I suppose.  Yes.  Somewhat.  She's charming, you know.  

Maybe once, some time ago.  I seem to remember.  Possibly.

Once I was the pack mother of the wolves your kind call the Cinderfen. I left this world many moons ago, but my spirit was compelled to return.\n\nI cannot rest until I know my children are no longer corrupted.
Choose...but choose wisely!
What would you like to know?

The Claw serves as an anchor to Molag Bal's domain of Cold Harbor. It allows the planemeld to manifest so strongly here.\n\nI would not even think of taking it if I were you. The power of the Claw cannot be controlled by one such as yourself.

I know a powerful daedra guards the Claw, roaming the temple interior. More over, my lord Molag Bal long ago placed certain enchantments on his Claw, spells that would alert him to any malign actions directed at the artifact.
Not far from here.\n\nThe Claw rests upon an altar in the deepest recess of our Temple.
I've reset it
Ready....go!
Did the witch send you?
Yes, I should. Thank you for your help.

We've been trying to get a look at the lower city. The massive statue platform in the middle of town is more than just a display - we believe it is some kind of elevator. We've read reports on the upper city, but no one seems to have ever gone below.

Look for machine buildings, spread out around the upper city. The notes we have suggest that repairing the machines in those buildings will re-activate the elevator, and maybe some other things as well.

We had split up to fix various machines. I was watching the lift in the center when I heard some kind of loud gong, and then the constructs activated. I ran back here to try and get help, but I'm cut off from my team.

When the constructs activated, Hurgen tried to fight them. He yelled at me to get in a building, because the constructs wouldn't go in them. So far, he's been right. I'm hoping my team has taken cover in the buildings, and I'd look there first.

Despite everything, if we can get the elevator fixed I still want to see what's down below. We came all the way out here and we knew what we were getting into. My team knows how to fix the machinery up here, so if they can be found we can go deeper.
My lovely Gurz, I do so miss her. I do not regret my duty's here but I so long to see her again.
Let me see. Ah, this is a platinum-level invite. The count says you get to come and go as you please.\n\nThat's more leeway than he usually gives his guests these days.
He's in the manor with his betrothed, <<1>>.\n\nTonight's festivities have already resulted in four deaths. Better hurry.
So you are the reason the bombardment has ceased, thank you stranger. I shall leave for Orsinium at once. Please tell Borkul gro-Shatur, my second in command, that he will take over my duties here.
My Gurz lies ill? Malak, what should I do? The dam remains under attack from the ogre scum but I feel I must be by my wife's side.
Those letters are my only joy here in Stormhaven. If only the dam did not lie under siege from the ogres. Were it not for those curs I would go to here immediately.
I have taken the countess away, but it was with no animosity.\n\nThe countess you see before you is the reflection. The true countess is in the mirror and that is where she will stay.

I will not. The mirror is the gift to her, but she is the gift to me. \n\nIf you wish to release her, you'll have to pass through to the other side into my domain. You shall find a warm welcome there.
Balcone? That bastard led us here.\n\nDon't believe anything he says. He's the cause of all of this!
There are old ruins on the hillside to the west. They're guarded by restless spirits.\n\nI wouldn't go near the place for love or gold, but I hear folks still find ancient artifacts up there.
Greetings!  I'm the QA Talker, I like to converse about a great many things.
Not a word. And every day we sit here is more gold I won't be earning. And all because some noble or another decided he wanted to be king.
No, I'm their bard, but I lost my lute so I thought I'd improvise with a hammer and an axe.\n\nOf course I'm their blacksmith! Now go bother someone who likes to talk.

Yes, I am a priest of Arkay in service to the Shornhelm Guard. I've been tasked with giving the final blessing to the soldiers that died in today's battle.\n\nWithout Arkay's blessing, they could become enthralled by a necromancer.
Haven't you heard? Baron Montclair has taken control of Shornhelm's upper city and his forces are on the march. It's like Ranser's War all over again!
I'm not grumpy. I have a wonderfully sunny disposition.\n\nNow get lost before I accidentally hit you with my hammer. Twice.

Thank you, but this task is mine to perform. I trained many years in Wayrest to become a priest. If I can't get through such a task on my own, I'm not suited for this calling.\n\nArkay tests me. I must prevail.
Arkay is the Divine of Birth and Death. He is the caretaker of the Divine Cycle all mortals must traverse—change and rebirth. Only through him can we fathom the meanings of these heady concepts.
More questions? I haven't done anything wrong!\n\nI don't care about Shornhelm's problems. I'm on my way to Fell's Run to meet my cousin. These soldiers have no right to stop me!

Because these soldiers are a bunch of empty-headed, magic-snorting imbeciles! I've half a mind to crush their heads together and just leave.\n\nI won't, though, because I don't want any trouble. I just want to be on my way.
My cousin said there would be work there for me. I think he owns a farm now. It's hard to imagine him farming!\n\nHonest work's getting hard to come by, so I'll take whatever I can get.

"Know?" I do not "know." Sapiarch Lilia did mention a distillation of Nimbleberries known to remedy magical paralysis.\n\nNimbleberries grow under the dome at the north end of the Imagerie. Gather some in this flask, and apply the result to Ameralee.

Oh.  Yes.  

Well, you could kill carrion harpies or the helhests or... well.  It's probable some of the corpses out on the battlefield will be tainted.  You could... harvest some of that flesh.

Sorry.

Good to hear
Sorry to hear that
How are you?
No. Please, no. I knew I shouldn't have let her talk me into leaving. But she was the mayor of <<1>>. She said she needed to stay behind.\n\nPlease, tell me what happened to her. I must know!

Well, now! You're interested in Old Stenric's stories? \n\nI've seen more wars than most, but I've never seen anything like <<1>>. Grown men screaming in the streets, slaughtered like cattle …. I hope my boy died well.
I used to study in the Mages Guild in Shornhelm, but I came with Jerwinna's regiment to investigate Crestshade. \n\nI tried to save as many lives as I could. I only wish I'd been more successful.

Yes! Oh, Mara's blessing on the little things but they're constantly underfoot. 

Would you like one? It's the least I can do after all you've done for me! 

Graymalkin is an excellent mouser. I'm sure her kittens will grow up to be the same.
All right, just let me know if you change your mind!
Oh, wonderful.  \n\nHere, <<1>>, take this one in the basket.
I am King Ranser's general, the commander of the elite forces of Shornhelm.\n\nAt least, I was. Now I command naught but dust, while Ranser himself leads his undead legion.

Has it been so long that Ranser's War was forgotten? Know that King Ranser was proud and his army strong. He attacked Wayrest.\n\nBut this action united all of High Rock against him. After a year of conflict, he met the Orcs here in final battle.
I don't know. Mother always said I was hopeless when it comes to this sort of thing.\n\nWhat do you think? Is it a mistake to chase Guendeline? Is Khalisah the better woman?
It was full of water just a few days ago. Now, nothing but mud and dust!\n\nIt must be a curse! My father says it's the vampires, that they've brought a curse down on the entire kingdom!

You know. The blood-sucking, evil, somewhat romantic kind. Surely you've heard of them? They've always been around, but lately there are more than ever.\n\nDon't tell my father, but I actually think they're kind of exciting.

You mean you would actually trade me that for this unworthy beast? If you are willing to do that, you are as dumb as the damn horse!\n\nWhat will you do with him? He's only good for hauling heavy loads, and he's not even much good for that!

Ha! You're as crazy as that dog-loving boy Handre! This horse does not want to be free. He would not even know what to do. \n\nI will trade with you, but no taking it back. You will feel like a fool when the stupid thing just stands there.
Do you think I'd rather beg than work? But work for a dust-sweep isn't as common as it used to be. And a man's got to do what he can. I have a family to feed, after all.
Bless you and bless this glinting gift. Tonight I will turn this clanking metal into bread and turnips for my family's supper. A feat greater than the most talented alchemist can conjure, eh?
Who can say? What with this civil war and all, maybe people don't care as much about cleanliness as they used to.\n\nI'm just trying to make ends meet, and economics was never my strong point.

They come in the night! Clawing! Biting! They have the faces of friends and lovers, but they're monsters! Monsters!\n\nI tried to run, but I was trapped! In my own house! That's when my own husband turned on me! I had to kill him. I had no choice.

Monsters! Who cares what the technical term for them is? The kind of monsters that used to be our friends and loved ones. Until the blood cravings take them. And the madness. And the rage.\n\nSoon all of Rivenspire will be filled with these creatures!

No! He wasn't my husband. Not any more. He was a monster! He came back from Northpoint, and the next morning he … changed. There was rage in his eyes. Madness.\n\nHe was an animal and I had to put him down. May the Divines forgive me!

Once, I was the master of a vast enterprise, brokering deals, trading goods. Now I'm nothing but another destitute drunk—thanks to those vampires. \n\nAnd do you know who suffers? My daughter, that's who.
Belle? She's outside, fetching water. She's such a smart young woman, and I've brought her down with me and all my talk of vampires. What kind of father am I?\n\nPardon me, but I need another drink.

They have everything to do with it! Oh, they may have looked like Montclair ruffians when they trashed my cart and took everything I had. But make no mistake! There were vampires among their ranks!\n\nNow my daughter and I have nothing. Nothing!
If you're looking for my lazy husband, he's out somewhere, doing who knows what.\n\nI work two jobs to keep us fed, but they call him the dust-sweep. It breaks my heart.

Well, things might be worse elsewhere. We at least have a house here, such as it is. I don't want to end up living in some raggedy tent, worrying about wild animals—or worse—attacking. \n\nShornhelm is my home. That's where I'll stay.
He was, but there isn't much call for his services of late. Me? I take care of the miller's children every morning and then clean noble manors all afternoon.\n\nI'm wiped out!

I know your kind. You befriend me and then you take everything I've collected for your own! Well, I see right through your plan and I'm having no part of it! \n\nNow get away before I scratch your eyes out! I have sharp nails, you know!
I will be. The pain will pass. My son carried me home after the … incident. He's been taking care of me since.

I was outside, watching Countess Tamrith walk by, and I commented about how beautiful she was. Next thing I know, one of Montclair's ruffians struck me and knocked me down.\n\nIf not for my son, I'd probably still be lying out there.
He's a good son, but I fear he might try to avenge me for the insult of the … incident.

No, no. She isn't blood-cursed, or anything like that. She just mentioned how lovely the Countess was, and one of those Montclair thugs punched her.\n\nMy mother has protected me my whole life. Now it's my turn to watch over her.

Because our constantly bickering nobles are the reason Montclair decided to strike out on his own.\n\nI admire the High King immensely, but why he thought setting up a triumvirate instead of just selecting a local ruler, I'll never know.
okay i will

I've lived in Fell's Run all my life, and I'm as stubborn as any Breton here. 

Still, I'll never understand why so many folks throw up their hands at the Orcs coming here.

Money is money! Their coins are as good as any others!

There's always been a few here and there, mostly working as mercenaries. After the sack of Shornhelm, some of the Orcs came north to settle.\n\nThe first few years were hard, but I think people are getting used to seeing them around now.

Oh, Grok's harmless. He just can't hold his liquor. 

I let him stay here because he entertains the customers with his war stories. Plus, he tips well.

Always remember: tip well.
They might mention something important in front of you if you eavesdrop on their conversations. Likewise, they might have some important parchment or something in their belongings.
If you didn't already pick one up when you were looking for the cure, you will probably have to kill one of the Rooks.
Thank you for collecting the QAT Catnip.  Now I can make stew for Tiny.

I'm a cattle wrangler. I ride around these parts, watching people's herds. I've been working for the Edralds for most of the last few years. \n\nI just came up here to track down a few bulls that had managed to wander off.

Not much to tell. Rumors, mostly. I heard that everyone in Moira's Hope was turned into bloodfiends. And House Montclair attacked the Rivenspire troops over at Hinault Farm.\n\nPlus, there's the bandits. So I'm leaving, and I suggest you do the same.
Of course I'm upset! Rivenspire's going to Oblivion in an ox cart, and there's not a damn thing I can do about it!
It's certainly better than the question! But why should I expect you to understand? You're not even from around here.\n\nGo bother someone else. I've got more drinking to do.
By the Divines! First an attack on Camlorn, and now an invasion here? <<1>>, you have my thanks.

I know that bandits take over old encampments, sometimes even abandoned villages, and make themselves at home.\n\nThose leaders divide up and defend their territories like the dogs that they are. They're all over Bangkorai.

You killed her! My love! My betrothed! 

We grew up together, fought together. Something turned her, but I know she still loved me.  

She's never harmed me, never. I... fed her things. Remains. I... we.... 

We would have been fine by ourselves.

By Mara, you're right. I should have seen it. I suppose it was easier to blame Irne rather than see the true cause.\n\nStill, this doesn't mean Irne's not out to get me! I'll watch him close. Even so... let him know I don't blame him for my boat.

That claw does fit the hole, almost exactly. If you hadn't put it right in front of my face, I wouldn't believe it.\n\nStill, that doesn't mean Valentin isn't plotting something else! I'll keep an eye out. Can you let him know I'm sorry?
Maybe you're right. Her hunger was growing. It was endless, boundless. Who knows where that might have led?\n\nI'll go back. Just let me have a few last moments with her.
Irne Guylitte's been raising all sorts of fuss about someone sabotaging boats, down on our docks. Wouldn't surprise me, with all the undesirables around.
Of course I am. Are you not?\n\nIt is however simply another challenge we are thrown up against and must overcome. It's that simple.

When isn't it? Even when the farmers task the lone adventurer with saving their crops, it always involves the slaying of some poor creature that simply lived its life.\n\nEither bend the creature to your will to live by your standards, or be rid of it.

Have you not figured it out? \n\nYou are trapped within her grasp, just as I was. I faltered in my journey. Words of warning fell upon my deaf ears. So many lives were lost because of my ignorance! You cannot let this be your fate. You must go!

This plane you stand in is simply a spell of deception being weaved before you. We can shatter this illusion sending you both back to Doomcrag. This will throw her off guard when this happens. You must strike quickly or your soul will be hers.

According to his orders, Pirate Captain Ra'Dara was behind the destruction of the lighthouse and our missing villagers.

Perhaps I was wrong about Captain Leon.

Take this key. Free Captain Leon. Then get him out of my town.

Have you not noticed Veraya's lust for the kill? With every battle fought within this realm the balance tips in her favor. I am already gone; a mindless fool lost on what I thought was love. Do not make that mistake. You must defeat the Dark Council.
Where would we be without our fishing boats? Irne Guylitte down at the docks says someone's been destroying them. Maybe he's doing the destruction himself...
Irne Guylitte says someone's been destroying Koeglin's fishing boats. I say, if Irne's at the docks all day, he knows more about what's going on than he says.
I'm ready! Thank you!

Well, there was this crazy Khajiit just come through here, rambling and raving about his plans to sneak into the Imperial Palisade.\n\nWild-eyed fellow... called himself Tor I believe. Looked like a skooma eater if ever I saw one. Smelled like one too!

You refer to the rumors about my ward, Tor? It is no secret that one has an appetite for trouble, but Ra'Vardo fears his wild nature has led Tor into true danger.\n\nA brave <<1>> might search for the wayward Tor inside the Imperial Palisade.

Since the lighthouse went out, many ships have run aground and lost cargo in Alcaire Cove. One Captain's loss is another Captain's gain!\n\nI'm paying well for any valuable salvage you find. Just bring it to me and I'll give you a fair price.
We've always had pirates along the coast, but no one knows what happened to our lighthouse after this last crew arrived.\n\nEven the soldiers who went out there have never come back!
They say pirates killed the lighthouse keeper to keep the light from ever being relit. Who knows what horrors go on in the dark now?
And you need to mind your own business. Get out of here before I lose my patience with you.
Ha! Let's see if you can make me stop, <<1>>.

The good stuff! There's plenty to be had with the lighthouse out, and ships running aground.\n\nCaptain Lash is out right now with some crewers on an island to the south. If you find any decent salvage, you should see her! She'll give you a good deal.

The Ashlanders are blessed by Meridia.

Long ago our ancestors shielded her from her father when he cast her from the heavens to the mortal plane.

She blessed our bloodline, and so we remain untouched by blight.  It is her will.

He's in the keep somewhere, but I suspect he's not taking part in the battle preparations. \n\nWhen he returned just now, he did reiterate the order to attack the Redguards, but he was not well. He seemed sick somehow.
I don't know. Help us retake the keep, and then we can sweep the grounds.\n\nThough he remains the head of our order, I imagine he must eventually answer for his crimes.
You're right. This doesn't make any sense at all.  My duty is to do what's right, not to blindly follow orders.\n\nI'm with you.
You would have me disobey direct orders and turn against Sir Croix? You sound like that coward Sir Edmund.\n\nYou are an enemy to the order, and I will see you slain.

I've done what I could, but I failed to find Sir Croix. Now I fear he would best me quite easily.\n\nI need you to do this. I believe the other knights will stand down if we can defeat Sir Croix. Will you face him for me?
Enough blood has been shed this day.\n\nBlow the siege horn atop the garrison and I will call for an end to the fighting.

Prices are higher than normal on food. Most farmers moved closer to Alcaire Keep for safety.\n\nThere might be one or two farmers out there, but I can only guess at the horrors they have to face every day.
Oh, I dunno, umm... you know... stuff.  Did you want something?
My family used to live out on one of those farms beyond the Keep.\n\nI pity those farmers who stayed out there when evil times befell us.

I don't leave Alcaire Keep after dark. Some say that the Balarel Ruins not far southeast of here are infested with undead creatures!\n\nThere's enough gone wrong with Alcaire, I don't need the dead to tell me about that!

Down the road, just before you reach Firebrand Keep, there's a cave. Windridge Cave.

Full of brigands. Thieves. Cutthroats.

My neighbor's one of them.
We used to store cheese at Windridge Cave, between Balarel Ruins and Firebrand Keep.\n\nLately, it's full of brigands and the like. They probably ate all our cheese.
When I was a child, I played in a place called Windridge Cave, a bit northwest of Firebrand Keep. I used to feel safe there.\n\nNow it's full of trash, filth, and brigands.

That s'wit thinks he controls all the shipping around here, but he doesn't! We could do just fine without his meddling.\n\nI used to run a legitimate business, and thanks to Orvona, I have to struggle to make my books look innocent!
What, you think he actually deals with his shipping "enterprises?" I'm his cover, and he needs me if he's going to stay in business. Why, I think he should be paying me for my services!
All right! You've made your point. Here's Sugar's protection. And if you repeat anything I've said to you, I'll make sure you pay dearly.
Wonderful. Let me take them off your hands. Sugar will speak with you now. Please be polite.
Valenwood was never a friendly place, but there are things in the woods to the east... Large, shambling things that I've only glimpsed before running back to town.

That demon! How coy of him to send someone in his place.

I was going to let him hide in the bushes a bit longer. I supposed it's childish, but I can't help teasing him.

As for his pants, I'll return them. All I ask is that you dance for us.

Giles, Idah, Luc, and Diane are my dearest friends. All of them crave novelty.

You must dance for us. Entertain us! Let the music take you!

Please, find my friends around the springs and dance for them. When you're done, dancing fool, return to me.

All ruined! Orvona will not be pleased. But, you have done as he asked, so his ire will not be directed at you.\n\nThe slaves were blighted when they arrived. Orvona tries to avoid dealing with them, but the early stages of Blight are hard to detect.

We sent a caravan to Omaynia a few days ago, and Orvona believes it carried more of these blighted slaves.\n\nI have no doubt they succumbed to the Blight soon after. They couldn't have made it much farther than Marshmine, if you wish to find them.
How wonderful! Dominique and I do not often see eye to eye, but she does have excellent taste in entertainment.\n\nDance as you will.

How thoughtful of her! Dominique certainly knows how to entertain us. 

We knew those dreugh could never appreciate the hot springs as much as we do.

Well, then, dance away!

Wonderful! Marvelous!

Dominique has such great ideas for entertainment, eh? 

Well, don't keep me waiting. Dance!

This is terrific, my dear!

Dominique told us removing those dreugh eggs would make the hot springs more exciting. She was right!

Dance away!

I appreciate that, my dear, but what of me?

Am I to be the only one in this venture who lacks for entertainment?

Come, dance for me as you danced for my friends. Dance for me!

I imagine dear Mazhe is getting a bit chilly without them. He could have had them sooner ... if he knew how to dance.

Open the chest beside the pool. The pants are inside it.

Oh, and do let Mazhe know that I'm thinking of him, my dear.
