I wish to tell you that my death was noble and that it meant something. Sadly, I was betrayed by my brother and sister Knights. They were the ones who sealed the cave trapping me with the Four. Still, I should have fullfilled my vow.

The Band of Four in my time, now they are the Fallen Four. When alive, they raided the countryside taking what they wanted and murdering those who stood in their way. How they and I are back as spirits is unknown to me.

Yes. After I pursued the Four into this cave, my fellow knights must have decided that it was better to trap us in this cave versus risk the Four's possible escape or the lives of more knights. A cowardly decision...

I vowed to bring the Four to justice. Regardless of circumstance, it was my duty to fulfill my vow. But it was the four who killed me. They fell upon me, and while I struck one a mortal blow, they triumphed in the end. I am shamed even in death.
No. The cave has been opened recently by graverobbers seeking the wealth of the Four. They meet an untimely end I am afraid, and end up serving the Four...
I'm afraid I'll only be able to answer questions relating to our... task we've asked you to complete. You are a stranger here. I'm sure you understand.

Mandran Veloth and Orvona are shipping partners. But now with the Ordinators keeping their eyes on the shores, he thinks to cut Orvona off.\n\nHe is an important contact for us, but we cannot let this insult go without recompense.

Delte Sedrane came to strike a deal with Sera Orvona, and in his generosity, he did not realize the value of the contract he sold.\n\nSera Orvona does not take well to the fact that she swindled him, and simply wants his property back.

Ah, please keep your voice down when asking about that. Sera Orvona had a bad turn of luck at cards a fortnight ago.\n\nA Dunmer named Alam Sernsi took advantage of this, and won the very cufflinks off of his coat. Get them back any way you can.

We obtained a potion from Durak, a wise orc who leads the Spirit Wardens of Pariah Abbey to the north. The potion prevents us from dreaming.\n\nDurak believes The Fervor affects those who dream, and I have no reason to doubt him.
Where did you find that? Was it you? Did you kill my Pasqal? Give it to me!
Oh my. Oh yes. I haven't seen that in years. I had thought it lost foresver. May I have it?

You'll find lovely windflowers to the northeast, but there are other flowers nearby.\n\nDisgusting acanthe grow to the southeast. Go northwest, and you'll be among the putrid lunarias. Celsia infest the fields to the northwest.

They're as pale as the moon. Some say the lunaria flower speaks of a night with one's true love beneath the stars.\n\nI say they're not worth the trouble. After the blossoms are plucked, they die as quickly as a man's interest.

Windflowers are like love's first kiss. 

Their delicate blossoms of pink look so fragile. A breeze could carry them away!

Treat them with love and tenderness and they flourish, like a marvelous romance!
Some say celsia's pale yellow beauty matches the dazzling flowers in the gardens of the Divines.\n\nTo me, they're smelly, messy things that should be fed to pigs.

The acanthe's numerous blossoms are a beautiful shade of pink.

I've heard it said they stretch to the sun as if reaching for Aetherius.

I don't think so. To me, they grow like weeds. They should be killed on sight before they ruin a garden.

I hate lunaria above all else.

See how the blossoms are already turning brown? They don't last. It's a waste to pick them.  

How could Ra'ud ignore my wishes? Tell Ra'ud I'll never speak to him again.

Ah! My favorite!

Does Ra'ud think I'm fragile enough to require constant, tender care? I would not squander a chance to receive such lavish attentions!

I'm pleased by his gift. Tell Ra'ud to come to me as soon as he can.

I hate celsia. They may be beautiful, but when I touch their sap, my skin bursts into an uncomfortable and unattractive rash.\n\nHow could Ra'ud ignore my wishes? Tell Ra'ud I'll never speak to him again.

How interesting that Ra'ud would present me with a bouquet of acanthe.

I hate acanthe. Its scent is like rotting flesh.

How could Ra'ud ignore my wishes? Tell Ra'ud I'll never speak to him again.

Many methods exist to make them, but Breton fireworks are the best!\n\nMages lock magical power inside granular sand, then, imbed those vials inside flying sticks of wood. After launching, they explode in midair, creating a marvel of color and sound!
How did you get this? Took it off some corpse I'll wager. Yes, it is mine, and I'd like to have it back.
My mother's hairpin. Yes. Yes. It is mine. I don't know how you found it and I don't care. Please, may I have it?
Fixed...game continuing though

Help me? You have to stop me!

Stop me from killing Lakana again and again!

 I see Lakana... I see myself... the blade... the blood... I can't look away!

Lakana! What have I done? Will I ever find absolution for this unforgivable crime?
Very well.
My dreams sometimes frighten me. I heard that they created a potion up at Pariah Abbey the keeps one from dreaming!
What do I look like? A gossip monger?\n\nAs it happens, I do know that many of those in Pariah Abbey never come to Reywell. They sleep dreamlessly all the time, thanks to some potion they made.
Not long ago,  the leader of Pariah Abbey...I forget his name...created a potion that prevents him from dreaming.
I've seen several matches at Hammerdeath Arena. If you have not seen the gladiators fighting for their lives, you should do so.\n\nVery entertaining, especially the pathetic pleas for freedom.
Have you been to Hammerdeath Arena to watch the games? It's quite a spectacle with all that fighting in the pits.\n\nI won quite a lot betting on their last champion.
If you're looking for a good fight, go to Hammerdeath Arena. Many of their best fighters are former slaves up against some professional fighters.\n\nThe events are exhilarating!
Yes, I'm all right … but not absolved. I ordered the Knights of the Flame to rebellion. I murdered the duchess. I betrayed the duke. \n\nThese stains on my honor cannot be washed away.
Windridge caves? Found it? Unlikely. Let me take a look...
Philippe's old sword. Yes, I recognize it. I made this for a knight in training, a long time ago.

That axe? I see that axe every night. The axe that slaughtered my family. The axe that took my parents and brought me here as a child. Is that why you are here? To strike the final blow and end my servitude?
This axe haunts me. I know it from my childhood. This was the axe that was used to slaughter my family and bring me to this cursed place as a servant. I should like to have it... and destroy it.
Ah, yes, I have those here.  Take some.  Good for the Blighted Outlanders or small children to play with... not much use for anything else.
We accept this in payment for Solon the slave. He is free to go, as are you.\n\nNow get out of here.
What is this?  This little rock will help me?\n\nI need a cure, not baubles!
If... you're certain.  Maybe it will work.\n\nYes, all right.  I'll go.
Leave?  When they hold the secret to healing me somewhere in the Conclave?\n\nI refuse!
Is this how you aid the blighted?  I may be stricken but I can still kill you!
I won't leave until I'm cured!  Tell them to give me the cure that keeps them unblighted!
Without the cure I have nothing to lose!  Do your worst!

It is unclear to all involved exactly what transpired, but suffice it to say the Haven we knew is no more.\n\nA dark magic now pervades the town. Peering south one can see a massive, unearthly device towering over the walls. Its purpose is... unknown.

Set down next to me, enjoy the weather, and wave to Mister Mandibles when the old Thunderbug shows his head on that hill across the way. I've got some ooze-eel jerky here, and later maybe I could find us some Sun-Dusk Ale.\n\nOr are you more ambitious?
This is... very disturbing. Thank you for bringing it to me. Our incanabulists will need to look at this before we take action.
If you're looking for information about the kickbacks, I might be able to help you.  Meet me in the tavern alley after you talk to the Harbormaster.  Come alone.

A cave the east of the Refuge. The Bosmer bury people in it.\n\nBetween you and me, I seen Imperials taking bones out of there and carrying them south into Haven town. I can't figure what they want with them.
You should take it to Warden Brehat in Deleyn's Mill as soon as possible.
I'm not telling you anything.  Stop interfering, I'm warning you!

All right, all right!  I work for "Sugar" Orvona.  She's paying me to help get smuggled shipments through for her.\n\nIf you want any more information, you'll have to go to Sugar Cove and talk to her yourself.

You've jogged my memory... I work for "Sugar" Orvona.  She's paying me to help get smuggled shipments through for her.\n\nIf you want any more information, you'll have to go to Sugar Cove and talk to her yourself.
You know nothing, and you'll find out nothing!

This Ordinator attacked me before I could even explain my predicament! What else could I do? I was forced to defend myself!\n\nPlease, I just want to leave these shores and get as far away as possible!

I was piloting my vessel along the shallows, when this Ordinator started shouting at me to land and surrender my goods! When I complied, he attacked me!\n\nHe's out for my blood now - there's no way I'm getting out of here while he's still alive!

I am an Ordinator, empowered by the Tribunal itself! Think not to question my right to be here.\n\nThis man thought to sneak away without surrendering his goods, and I will see that he pays the price for his hubris!

Imports and exports are strictly forbidden until we have controlled this Blight. No one is above the word of law, but he thought to circumvent it by taking his goods along the shoreline!\n\nHe deserves nothing more than death for his crimes!

You'll say I'm biased because of my allegiance to House Redoran.  But there's something sinister going on.  They've benefited too much from the misfortune of the blight.  Personally I don't think they're interested in seeing it it end.

Oh my, yes.  They're my best customers! \n\nI've had a run of very expensive work for them, all fine silks and gems, and I'm happy to serve them!  They've protected us from the Blight, with that Blightfence they built.  House Dres protects us all!
Indeed.  It's magnificent, is it not?  We have spared no expense here, and why should we, for the glory of our house?\n\n... well, and the protection of the people, of course.

Go to the house itself, then.  Speak to the Lawman Adrusu - she's my cousin.  Tell her I sent you and if you're fortunate, you might be able to aid us in our endeavors.\n\nOh, and beware the blighted souls trapped in the fence.  They sometimes escape.
Hike!
Reset
The lawless Dres have already dug up countless graves.  Take some of those bones they scattered around the tombs here in Necris, and leave my remains be.

I saw the legions of Akaviri on our shores.

They came to destroy us and take the survivors as slaves to their far-off shores.

The flood came soon after. I did not survive, but I must know: were the Akaviri successful?
We craft wood. Weapons and armor, enchanted gearbindings.\n\nForest magics, incarnate.

Then I need not lurk here any longer.

I wish I could tell my comrades of this, but they have gone mad with the passage of time.

Do not hate them for their madness, stranger.
Leather from beasts. Pliable armor. Restoration potions, go down easy. \n\nWell? Join up?

Heroic remains!  The remains of heroes; now that's a feat.  You're a force to be reckoned with.  You should meet House Father Teranos.  He's here inspecting the fence.\n\nIt's a great honor, you know.
You're a force to be reckoned with.  You should meet House Father Teranos.  He's here inspecting the fence.\n\nIt's a great honor, you know.

The Dres Ordinator came... they took my betrothed!  All of the papers and evidence she had built against House Dres... everything!\n\nPlease, you must help.  Find out where they took her.  I know you were helping her; promise me you'll do something!

Adrusu, that snake.  Yes, talk to her.  Maybe you can make her tell you where they took my poor Llameni.\n\nOr... since the Blight, the Gatekeeper keeps a log of all shipments in and out.  He might have logged when the Ordinator's caravan went through.

What injustice there is in this world! Why should I suffer the same fate as the Akaviri invaders?

How am I to rest, knowing I did not die defending my countrymen!

I was a nameless casualty in a senseless natural disaster.

Must I find comfort in that fact, stranger?

Is that the only thread to which I have to cling?

I tire of suffering on this plane. Perhaps it is time to find peace far away from here.

Ah, my poor Toves, his heart broken so young! Separated by death, yet forever faithful he is! But I cannot bear to see him and not hold him... \n\nI long for him to leave, yet I cannot stand the thought of him gone!
You... you are wise, mortal. Despite our love, we cannot be together. I must move on if he is to know peace.\n\nFarewell, sweet Toves! Please, do not mourn long for me!
Happier times, friend. We were betrothed, and thought to be married in Mournhold. But misfortune stole us apart, and here I lie, as a ghost, and he a mortal.
Do not speak as if I do not care! You do not know the sorrows we endure, stranger! My murder hangs heavy upon his countenance. I cannot rest while he is so sorrowful...

Would you not turn the very earth upside-down to find your desire? I care for nothing more in this world than Arynia, yet she was... stolen from me! Taken by the cruel clutches of death!\n\nBut I will not let this be so! I have come to find her.

I admit, I came here with just such an intention, but I... was afraid. Your words ring true, friend. What else is there left in my life if she is gone?\n\nArynia, I come for you. Death need not keep us apart!
What? Why would you say such a thing? Do you think that death changes one so much as to fracture our love?
In truth, I had not figured that part of my plan out quite yet. But I must find her first, don't you agree?\n\nI fear she hides from me, believing I will do something drastic...

Arynia and I were engaged, and a fortnight before our wedding, she was murdered in the streets of Mournhold.\n\nHer father brought her here to rest in the family's tomb. I came to Stonefalls to find a way for us to be together.

It's quite hard to see the initial signs of infection. This is why we isolate any newcomers to see if they develop any symptoms.\n\nHowever, any strong exposure, such as being caught in a Blightstorm, will show symptoms immediately.

I can use for someone with your talents.

We've captured an Ashlander who's immune. I suspect his kind have been spreading the Blight.

Get a confession of guilt from him. Once you bring it to me, you'll have an ally in House Dres.
You can't make me go back out there! You don't understand... the Akaviri, I've never seen their ilk...
Kwama.
I... I don't know. I've lost track of time...

He settled this area long ago - was the first Razorvine Bosmer. They called him Toad-Eye... something to do with one of his eye sockets containing a living toad. \n\nThe Spinners are known for entertaining their audience, not imparting the truth.
They are, admittedly, an acquired taste. So what became of the Akaviri?
Blight? Then we are truly doomed. I wouldn't be surprised if the Akaviri were behind it. I think I'll stay right where I am, thank you.
Spectacular! So... it is safe for me to leave?

We spoke out against the Conclave's Wise Woman.

The Conclave is without mercy to the Blighted, and gives them false talismans.  We objected to this practice.

And so we are here, where the Dunmer have perished, and left us as good a place as any.
Who are you to ask?  If you have questions, take them to Adusamsi.  She will decide if you are worthy of an answer.

Let this one see, yes... yes. \n\nAs I thought! This one knows the unnatural taint of dark magika. These storms... they will get worse. That one must warn others of this discovery. Make haste to Fort Thendr and warn the guards there of this discovery!

Does he now?

I'd be curious to know how this... mage... came to this conclusion. We have investigated this matter thoroughly and have proven otherwise. 

Who is this mage?
Excellent. \n\nWe will send our guards to the mage at once. We cannot have the scaled ones spreading lies amongst our people.

Of course he did. 

He knows the price he'd pay for speading hysterical rumors. We will have our guard keep watch of the area for signs of his return. 

House Dres thanks you for this news.

An Argonian? 

Curse his false claims of dark practices! The scaled ones spread lies and speak nothing but of ill omens. This mage wishes to spread panic amongst the citizens of Ebonheart.

We will need to handle this. Where is the Argonian?

Ahh, come to learn? Runecrafting is an ancient and noble art. We manipulate magicka, imbuing it into runes, jewels, and staves. \n\nWe can also change a common shirt or robe and make it a source of power for mages!

Let's see … we scribe scrolls that any man or mer can cast. We prepare soul gems, trapping the essence of mystical creatures. They can be used to enhance powerful magical gear!\n\nThe Runecrafter's life is a fulfilling one. What say you?

The leather armors of an outfitter are what you want if you don't want to clank when you move.\n\nThe magics of petrified bones allow our maces to strike harder than any created by a smith. Use a mace you want to stand tall against all attackers.

These ancient bones can also be carved into enchantments that transfer their magics directly to a weapon or breastplate. Casters purchase these by the dozen.\n\nWe also make salves, that envigorate the body, in ways that are prized by fighters all.

Of course! Welcome to the forge! As a smith you'd use pressure and fire to reshape the world to your will. \n\nPlate armors and well sharpened swords are our stock in trade, for everyone from the lowly footman to the greatest warrior.

We combine minerals and magic to create restoratives for mages. We forge enchanted trinkets that rogues can clip to their gear, granting them enhanced abilities. \n\nWe're flame and metal and magic combined! So! What do you say?
The Ordinator left for Heimlyn Keep not long ago.  You can follow him there, if you're interested in talking to him.
Be careful, Blightbane.  You can only push the goodwill of House Dres so far.  Do not threaten me.\n\nThe Ordinator left for Heimlyn Keep not long ago.

Oh, cursed existence! What have I done to deserve such scorn! And I was blind to the thought that she may be gone... forever!\n\nOr perhaps she despises me, even blames me for her death! I cannot bear to think of it... I must leave!

Because the Infernal Device, augmented by Sload Necromancy, has drawn Netherhaven into the Oblivion plane of Cold Harbor. \n\nThese Sload, you see, worship the Daedric Prince of Cold Harbor: the dread Molag Bal.

The Cold Harbor effect will spread, inexorably, until all of southeastern Valenwood is drawn into the clutches of the God of Schemes. 

Life will become unlife, and the domain of Molag Bal will interpenetrate with Tamriel. 

It is a woe beyond woes.
Keep your voice down, imbecile!\n\nWell? What does he have to say for himself?

Well, that's not news here in Kragenmoor.\n\nI'll have to ask you to file a report with the clerk in the judicial district, and make sure to refernce the right case number and file, else it'll just get thrown away...

What?! I've already paid him twice this week!

I mean, uh, he's joking of course. Paying a guard would be... illegal!

But now that you mention it, I've brought him a present from my travels. Could you bring this to him... discreetly?

That's a strong claim to make, accusing my own men! I have been wondering where he's been getting all that extra leisure pay, and some of my other men have been talking... I'll look into it, I assure you.
That's a strong claim to make, accusing my own men! I have been wondering where he's been getting all that extra leisure pay, and some of my other men have been talking...
If he wants another favor, it's going to cost him.\n\nGo back there and tell him I want my normal fee, up front. Then maybe I'll see about getting his cargo out of harm's way.
About time! Ah, I went through the last batch so fast I thought I was going to find another seller!\n\nGoing to be a pleasant evening tonight!
Who gave you permission to snoop around my private locker?!\n\nLook, I don't want any trouble. I'll let Melves through, no charge.

I'm not quite sure but I know the main force here is working on preventing the Lion Guard from sending reinforcements to Camlorn.\n\nThese bandits are working for someone, I just don't know who. I wish I could help more.
Thank you! I swear, I won't work for the Red Rooks anymore. They'll never be able to find me again.\n\nI'll leave as soon as it's clear. I'm sure a distraction from you would help.

The wardens? Yes, perhaps that's best.

They'll be fair with me. I'll provide them with any information they could want.

I'll leave as soon as it's clear. I'm sure a distraction from you would help.

That explains the silence these few days.

We feared the worst. Thank you for the information.

Now get him out of here and into the quarantine pens.

The Lion Guard?

They'll torture me for sure. At least it's better than staying here. Perhaps my imprisonment won't be too long.

I'll leave as soon as it's clear. I'm sure a distraction from you would help.

He commands the siege camp at the base of Leaftower. Some snooty Altmer, come over from the Summersets. Prince Aeradan agreed to let him command under the terms of the Aldmeri Dominion. But we don't need their help!

Taken by Imperials. Unbelievable, isn't it? They came out of the east, along the old Reman Road that runs north of Gil-Var-Delle.\n\nThey advanced far enough south to destroy the village of Karthdar before the Altmer arrived.

That's what I'd like to know!

We're both part of the Dominion now - us Bosmer, the Altmer, plus the Khajiit. Prince Aeradan, the Camoran heir, thinks the Altmer know siegecraft better than Bosmer.

That may be true, but Bosmer have other skills.

I think it's a great excuse for Altmer to run around Valenwood acting superior.\n\nI don't see what it gets us. The Valenwood is what it is. They want to change things. My people don't need change. We want the blessed peace we enjoyed before the war.

Ye gods! What blasphemy is this?

Friend, let me enlighten you. Almsivi is the holy name of the Three: the lords Almalexia, Sotha Sil, and Vivec. 

The Three were raised to godhood for their great and pious deeds!

I have been accused of Daedric worship. Perhaps you can help alleviate this situation?\n\nThe only evidence they have is in the basement of a house at the far end of the Blighted District. If you destroy it, my name will be cleared.
What? Why would she ask you to do that...?\n\nOh. Oh, no. Not my sweet Ferema. Friend, though my heart breaks, I thank you for telling me this.
I'm sure they do, but times are hard, with the Blight.  I look for the best price - and quality, of course - that I can.

What?

What are you saying?  

No, never mind, I know what you're saying.  I get your message.  I'll... I'll deal with House Dres alone.  I don't need trouble.  Be on your way.
Hmm... you have a point, about the House Dres label.  I hadn't considered that.  \n\nWith status comes a markup.  I'll just charge more.  Very well, tell House Dres I'll deal solely with them.

They do, do they?

I should have seen this coming.  I have no wish to make an enemy of House Dres - particularly given their popularity here - but my loyalty is to my customers.

I buy the best goods at the best price.  That won't change.

You dare threaten me?

Did you forget the part where I told you I was a soldier before I became an inkeeper?

Do your worst.  I don't bend to threats.
My good name comes from clean rooms, good food, strong ale and fair prices.  \n\nI know what you're doing, and it won't work.  I'll buy from the traders I choose, not just House Dres.
House Dres?  I suppose that I could... but why can't I use other sources?  I don't understand.  It doesn't make good business sense!

Oh dear.

Are you saying someone will... you are saying they will, aren't you?  Oh, my.  

Well, if you put it that way, I suppose I have no choice.  How unfortuante.  All right.  All right.

Oh... I like that idea!  Do you think that's true?  I get a lot of their business already but I can always use more.  \n\nExclusively, you say?  All right, that's enough incentive.  I'll use only House Dres goods from here on.

The Corprusarium?  But that's where they send the blighted.  I don't want to go there.  \n\nI have my treasure to guard.  Are you sure you didn't bring me anything?  I have so many nice things, but I could always use more.  Anything in your pockets?
Don't threaten me, flat-head!  I will thrash some politeness into you!
They might have treasure?  For me?\n\nI could take some.  Just a little.  I'll go and see, that's what I'll do.  Yes, I'll go there now.
Divines be praised. The cultists trapped me with these focus crystals. \n\nI'm a bit of a mage myself, but I'm powerless inside this ward.

I could use a seasoned warrior. There's no point relying on the local watch. They're simply not up to the job. \n\nThe Duke's in the lighthouse, guarded by Bloodthorns. I was waiting for reinforcements to arrive before making a move.

You're a bold one. Very well, when the reinforcements get here we'll make sure none of the cultists slip away. \n\nAnd if your plan doesn't work, we'll drink a toast to your memory later in the tavern.

We were sent to provide more security for the Duke and to keep something like this from happening.\n\nIt's too bad we didn't arrive sooner. The local watch just wasn't prepared to deal with the Bloodthorns.
Defiler!  I will not tolerate this insult!
The spirit of an old warrior thanks you for letting me rest undisturbed.\n\nThe Divines go with you.

If I were to, say, get "captured" by the officals in Aldcroft, then the Red Rooks would have no reason to threaten my family. I would be in prison.\n\nI'm sure the officials would be swarming around my house in no time. My family would be safe.
Yes, and if you set me free I might let you live!\n\nOr... I'll tell you where my treasure is.
Wicked <<1>>!  You have provoked the ire of the Great Scamp Xzzil!\n\nTaste my awful wrath!
It's deep under the bridge on the road to Othrenis.  \n\nXzzil the Scamp is magnanimous.  For your help, he will not kill you.  Goodbye!

I'm afraid not. 

I'm simply a treasure hunter in search of a more illustrious future. 

Until I discover something the guild finds valuable, it's all I'll ever be!
How's it going.
And... bam! We're in conversation 2! You didn't even notice.
Done!
Now what would you like to do?
Sounds good to me!
And here we are! *I* am not attached to the NPC speaking! Weird!
Sounds exciting!

My beloved died of his wounds from the attack on Camlorn. He wanted his ashes scattered at this bridge. 

I was attacked by wolves. I can't make it.

Please, help me honor my beloved's last request. Take Andre's ashes to the bridge and scatter them.

I smuggle slaves from Stonefalls back to their families. Last night I met with Taluro, my contact, but he attacked and left me for dead.\n\nHe has extinguished the lighthouse, probably to stop any runaway slaves from leaving port. You must stop him!

Well, it's nice to see someone finally taking an interest in my important work here.\n\nThis is the site of the final great battle between the Akaviri and the Dunmer.  The fighting was cut short when the volcano you see over there erupted.

We all know that it was part of their agreement in the Ebonheart pact.  But there has been no real proof, since all the Argonians died in the eruption.\n\nThis battle site holds the key.  Soon, I will be famous!  Er, we.  We will all be famous, I mean.
I am.  I may have Blight, who knows.  I don't want to report but it's the right thing to do.  I'll go.
I don't have Blight!  Are you mad?  It's just a cold, or a chill of some sort.  I'll do no such thing!
Now you threaten me?  Go!  Harass someone else!
I'm fine.  I'm just fine.  Leave me be and I'll sleep it off and will be right as rain tomorrow.
I won't go!  I have a family to care for, and my business to maintain.  You can't make me go!
I know I seem unwell, but it's not the Blight.  I took some of the remedies they sold me, and I feel better already.
I know.  I know you're right.  I don't think the remedies worked at all, and I'm only getting sicker.  I should protect the others.\n\nI'll report to the Quarantine Master.

What's this?

Oh, whyever would he want me to look at this? How... where did he find it? Not that I know anything about it.

In fact, I bet it was you who sold Orvona out! That's it! Who is he going to believe - me, or some stranger?!

As I said, best to mind your own business. Unless you want to pay off her debts?\n\nIf Hleri can't afford her vices, that's not my problem. Ravnos has offered to take her under his wing, be one of his nightingales, but she's awfully reluctant. Shame.

The Ashlanders have been receiving information from a traitor among the guards of Fort Virak! If I find out who...  I will tear that Guar Licker apart! You must get me out of here. I must return to warn the captain.
Lead the way!

The Ordinator Vusara fdevised the ritual to mitigate Akaviri's curse on these lands. 

If the ritual isn't performed, thousands of Akaviri undead will arise.

They'll march across the lands of the living again.

Ordinator Vusara was one of our greatest heroes!

Sadly, she vanished with her research a few months after devising the ritual to deal with the troubles here.

Since her work was not complete, this ritual only forestalls the curse.

The war ended about a decade ago.

The battle here was instrumental in our victory.

Supposedly the Argonians used their Hist magic to reawaken a dormant volcano. The resulting eruption killed thousands of Akaviri.

You're kidding, right? No, I can tell you're not.

Hmm. I was hoping to get out of this cell.

If he's putting out a contract on my life, I might be safer here... though I don't think I'll eat the food anytime soon.
What? Oh, my tea... of course, I'd forgotten what time it was.\n\nI suppose hiring my servant to kill me would be far too obvious. Well, it looks like I've survived another day!

The Temple has every right! We protect the people of these lands from every atrocity we face including those who would spread the word of false gods! \n\nDo not stand in our way thinking you are righteous or you too shall pay.
Stand in our way then, hero. See where that gets you.

And why must we? Do we offend you with our offerings?  Are you sickened by our worship to the Daedric Prince? \n\nYou will find we will not simply roll away by a simple budge of a stranger. Do not force our hand or you will regret it, I assure you.

The Ordinators are fools if they choose this course of action. We are not a band of weaklings who will simply lie down and die for them. If they dare set foot upon our sacred grounds, their blood will soak the ground on which we stand.
Living champions? Well, you're just in time. They're about to come through that portal!
For what purpose have you summoned me?
The sun breaks through the canopy and shines upon you, Silvenar. No better words can reach my ears this day. \n\nIt will be done.

Someone called us, summoned us.  All I know is I felt the call of a descendant and was roused from my slumber.\n\nSee, all the nephews and nieces are angry now.  They must have driven the descendant away before she told us what she wanted.
The Ordinators have shut down the docks for fear of The Blight. Nothing but scavengers and blighted creatures there now.
The spirits of the Solir Nath Ancestral Tomb have been disturbed by something. That place has stood silent for many years but now the spirits cry out in torment.
I've heard that Fort Virak is isolated and left to fend for itself against an overwhelming Ashlander force. Word has it they are hiring mercenaries and sell-swords.
It is said that those who pray at the Shrine of Meridia are granted immunity to the blight.
It is said there are still great treasures to be found in the Dwemer Ruins to the southeast. I've even heard that there is a huge chest hidden somewhere within the ruins.

The beautiful Spirit made Josaja sleepy. Josaja is no fool, but felt comfortable with lying down in this dangerous swamp. When Josaja awoke she felt weak and disoriented. The Spirit was gone.\n\nThe Spirit took some of Josaja's energy.
Elder Knonk is not forgetting the deeds of the <class> before him. The <class> will be taking this small gift and learning that the story of the Elder's rescue will be long remembered.

We managed to close two of the portals, but these blasted shadow creatures cut us off from the main force. I need to make sure none of them can slip into the house, but someone needs to assist Commander Viskel.

If you could destroy some of those shadows and stop their leader, a creature called Veddergen, we could clear up the rest. Thin out their numbers, then speak to Commander Viskel, just beyond the gardens. He could use the help.
My love! My life! I live for you! Why do you wound me with your words?\n\nYou must be tired. Let us retire for the day, shall we?

Is this a jest of some kind? 

It's been so long. I have not laughed in a long time, my dear. There's so little to laugh at during the war.

Tell me another joke, so I may thrill to your lilting voice!
I'm already restful when I'm gazing into your eyes, my sweet. \n\nI could die happy knowing you are near me.
One of the witches has gone missing. Some are saying those cultists hauled her into a cave.
What would you like to know?

Though these ruins are Ayelid, they were not the last inhabitants. During the First Age, the Aldmeri did much research here into Reach magic.\n\nAt the time, they still hoped to keep the western Reach as a bulwark against further Nordic invasion.

The Mages Guild has decided that Angof, a powerful Reachmage who also dabbles in necromancy, is the primary threat to High Rock.\n\nIt is my hope that the murals in these ruins will have some clue how to counter his power, and thus defeat him.
Do not think for too long. Time is short. Simply place the crystals into the brazier on the dais.\n\nThey bound me here long ago. I can almost taste freedom's sweetness. Release me, mortal!

My greatest desire is to be free of these uncomfortable shackles. They chafe my skin and make it difficult for me to breathe.\n\nI only ask for this one small kindness. You have the power to grant my freedom. Please?

Wait! Please reconsider. I have done nothing to harm you. I only wish to be free of these bindings. Look at how they've bruised my skin. No one deserves to suffer this way.\n\nThe barrier will collapse and kill me. I beg you, mortal. Help me.
Yes! Turn away from this foolhardy path. Release me, save me, help me! Whatever words you need to hear, I will say them!\n\nDestroy the crystals in the brazier. Your decison will be amply rewarded.

Stay out of the woods to the east. The Imperials to the west will just kill you, but from what I hear, there are things in those woods which will do much worse. Dangerous walking trees, strange noises - the stuff of nightmares.
Tome the first, hidden underground. A tomb for a tome, a home among bones.

Not yet, but it will. We will charge the enemies' ranks and they will see what true determination means. \n\nI've sent orders for Captain Taern and the King's Guard to charge the breach in the north wall. Tell the general to prepare his troops as well.
Tome the second, not hidden, but lost. Salty leather jaws made knowledge a meal.
Tome the third, once hidden, now exposed. Taken to the heights, to a tower, in the light.
The knowledge held here is too great for some. A mind unprepared will lose control, flee from its place, expand beyond bounds. And then, another moves in.

Why, his Grace is the Duke of Camlorn! What else is there to say? He loves his people and they love him. \n\nHe was driven out of Camlorn by Faolchu and his werewolves. Now he reigns in exile from Aldcroft. Well, at least he did before the kidnapping.
Whitestone was its name. Lost to time, swallowed by the earth. Its creators fought the forest, forces of nature, beyond their control. Eternal unrest is their fate.
Not who, but what. A vision, in mind, through eye, unalive. Through magic alone, I bestow what I know.
The body remains, but the mind is fled. On an island of stone, she finds no refuge.

Have you met anyone touched by the blood fever? Have you met one too far gone to be seen as a man?\n\nThe scourge is outside these walls, and if I am correct, Lord Montclair has something to do with it. Anyone Montclair captures is now a threat.

You are a brave one, aren't you?

You betray my house to side with a child, and then you expect to be welcomed back so easily?

I give you this warning. At this wars end, you had best left the city gates or you will find yourself locked away, fool.

If you're dark minded, there's coin to be gotten in the Man-Grove Swamp, northwest of Southpoint.\n\nSpirits there entrance people and pull them under the swamp. The swamp will spit out their bones and belongings once the Spirits are done.
Ah... yes, of course. It's the least I can do, considering you saved me from becoming bug food.\n\nStill, I don't think I'm long for this world. Ask your questions. I'll help you best I can.

Because they pay me to be in Valenwood. I don't care why. Never asked. It's nothing personal - I'm just trying to make a living.\n\nBesides, the Empire has been colonizing the rest of this continent for centuries. Why should Valenwood be any different?

Myself, I was born in Skingrad, near the Imperial City. This army comes from Cyrodiil too, by the will - and coin - of the Tharn dynasty. My fellow soldiers and I traveled many long roads to get here.

Oh, gods. This hurts. Ah....

Sorry. Strongholds? There's the Palisade of course, west of here. And our Rangers are set up in a small compound outside Haven town, to the east.

There's more activity up north too, but I don't know much about that.

Seeing Elder Brump to the south, near Stumptown. 

Watching him scout the town with Cliffvoot sentries.

Realizing that only the sentries returned.

They're turning these ruins into their home camp. They have been summoning all sorts of dark creatures, building an army.\n\nThere's something else, too, some artifact they're guarding. It's on the bottom floor - along with a massive Daedra.
It's driftwood, outlander. Exempt from the Green Pact. It's not forbidden to build fires, it's forbidden to cut wood for them.

That I do not know. \n\nI am a traveling man of faith who walked into a most devious trap. Perhaps Montclair wishes to see the extent in which he can bend a man's faith before he breaks. He will be terribly disappointed.

You wish to help one that you would call a stranger?\n\nYou show a kindness I have not seen in many of days. The guards have spoken of a hidden latch to this cage. If you can find it and unclasp it, I would be able to make an attempt to dash away.
Spare me a copper and I might have something to tell you.
Yes! Whatever you do, do not lay hands upon the <<1>>s which litter these ruins. You will surely be possessed by a maddened spirit, such as that which you have just vanquished from my person.

Soldier Hill's in the mountains north of Cath Bedraud, We used to go there to honor our fallen. Since the undead appeared, no one can get there.\n\nBut, folks report seeing a campfire lit there at night. Looks like someone's living up there now.
Talking does not suit me, yet I find myself compelled to speak to you.\n\nI am weary with loneliness.

I think I have always been able to talk. I cannot remember when I was born. Did I spring into being, fully formed?\n\nI remember a cave, and strangely, I recall moving about it. How is it that a tree can move?
Am I not a tree? My leaves nourish me, and my roots embrace the soil, but something is not right.\n\nWhy do I think? Why do I contemplate these things when others do not? What makes me different?

Except for the torches, which frighten me with their flames, I am comfortable here. I am happy.\n\nHowever, I cannot stand not knowing what I am! Please, help me. I may go mad wondering what is wrong with me. There must be answers within this cave!
Ah, what luck! Tell me, friend, what have you found?
Oh, if only I could read! What, pray tell, does it say?

Truly? Will I be as free as my comrades of the soil?

Though I ache at the thought of losing what few memories I have, I long for the sweet embrace of nothingness, living without conscious thought.

Will you use this potion upon me?
How horrible! Even the thought of fire makes my leaves quiver!\n\nAre you quite sure this is the only way? Perhaps it would be best if you simply left me instead.
I see.\n\nHave you found anything else that may help me?

Yes! The artifact had to be activated with blood. We searched for so long, only to learn this at the last moment.\n\nI killed her for her blood, since only one of us could use the artifact. This was my reward! A mockery of immortality as a tree!
I can feel the liquid engulfing my roots. It is good to know that I will have peace for eternity.
Arkay bless you! Tell Marthe Yvienne how many of us you saved when you leave the Mine.
Arkay bless you! Tell Marthe Yvienne how many of us you saved when you leave the Mine.
Before you may cross, you you must answer me these questions three.\n\nWhat is your name?
Wrong.
Wrong
Correct.\n\nWhat is your quest?
Wrong.
Wrong.
Wrong.
What? I don't know that.
Wrong.
Correct\n\nWhat is the average flight velocity of a sparrow?

You know nothing. I know he still honors my wishes.

I am with child, <<1>>. I know that's nothing unusual, but the father is not a Breton.

The child's father is an Orc named Magharz.

I am glad you see it that way; most would not.

I've only overheard them whispering. They want to use my child as a sacrifice!

You must help me! I know how to stop them!

That's why I chose to flee with my child. Well, I tried to, at least. 

Please, I know I am no one to you, but you must help me. 

I know how you can break the shield holding me. Break it, so we can both be free.

We attacked Northpoint and made off with her treasures. Then one of my sailors ran us onto this sandbar. 

My crew turned on me to make off with the gold, the cowardly dogs! Then they betrayed each other.

The treasure's around here... somewhere....

We caught the Red Cohort by surprise and swept them out of Southpoint Town, but we can't afford to give them time to regroup, or they may counterattack. \n\nWe need you to take the battle to them. Hit the Imperials hard, and keep them off balance.

Our ancestors, the giants, used the mammoths as mounts long ago. Their spirits look after our people, just as we looked after them.\n\nMammoths still roam the area near Breagha-Fin. They're docile creatures, but don't think about taming them.

I've often thought we should try and ride the mammoths as our forefatehrs did. It would certainly make plowing easier.\n\nAncestry aside, mammoth wrangling involves a bit of risk. I'm sure it's just a matter of time before I get it right.

Isn't it obvious? Many of the people of Northpoint are descendants, although few outsiders believe it.\n\nThe Nevin family can trace back its lineage to the people of Breagha-Fin, and they claim giant heritage as well. Makes sense to me!

I have travelled far, stranger. I could tell you tales of adventure, intrigue, and even betrayal. \n\nHowever, I've put my past behind me, and speaking of such matters … well, I'm not prepared to do so.

Does the sparrow question the tree she nests in? Does the hawk ask the sky ….

Excuse me. I should answer your question.

I read. I write. I grow what sustains me. Above all else, I contemplate what brought me here … what brought all of us here.

All ogres have nasty teeth. Collecting them proves they're dead.

Our loyalty to the clan pays for our families' freedom and safety. I'll do anything to protect my family. 

I've already turned in 653. Only 124 more to go!
Hurgh … ulp … wha-\n\nWhat is this? Oh, gods. Oh, blessed Arkay, what am I doing?
Uh, well... people got to eat, don't they?
We were supposed to get help for Marcel. The priestess begged us, but Balcone wanted to stop here first.\n\nHe wanted to break into the ruin. We tried, but there were undead inside.
Nothing! He was behind us. He ran when the monsters came. He … I can't breathe …\n\nDon't … don't listen to him ….

I've always been fascinated by the great river lizards. I've always wanted to bring them closer to me, so I developed a ritual.\n\nFor a lure that's powerful enough, I needed the heart of a great crocodile. Of course, I'll still mourn <<1>>.

We were just standing here talking. He said you went in to talk to the countess, so we were waiting ….\n\nThen all of the sudden an arrow flew out of nowhere right into his chest. He was dead before he hit the ground.

Nah. They might want to stay, but I just can't deal with all that. We made a good go of it here, but I need to move on now. Spend some time alone.\n\nIt's a shame because we made quite the team back in our younger days.
Long enough
Excellent! We need all the help we can get. \n\nThe ogre attacks have been relentless. Get ready for battle. We can expect an attack any minute now.
Excellent! For the honor of Clan Murtag!
When you're ready to fight, I'll be here.
We need to free the sick captives. If you've heard any rumors about missing people or kidnappings, I've learned they are all true. They have several up there. Free them and then return to me.
A bunch of zombies have risen up, and are attacking anyone who comes near.  The patrol's been too busy to send anyone out to take care of them.  Perhaps you could help out and deal with them?

Great.  You'll need to kill at least one of them, and make your way to the crypt, and then back to me.  If you can do that, it's probably safe enough.  I'll keep watch from outside.  Feel free to take care of all of them.

Are you feverish? You are one of the only Redguards willing to resist Potentate Versidue-Shaie.

My father King Aphren has surrendered. We will not. We will retake the keep and mount Imperial heads on its walls.

Let Versidue-Shaie look on that!

Are you blind? Even now the Imperials camp within the walls of Aphren's Keep. Their hubris will be the death of them.\n\nHoonDing with us, the walls will run with Imperial blood. My father has abandoned the Redguards, but I will not. Stand with me!

You know as well as I King Aphren rules Stormhaven … or did, until he surrendered to the Potentate.

Yet my father has lost his spine. He should be forgotten.

Versidue-Shaie seeks an empire, but he will find only ruins.
It's not? Are you sure? I don't want to go back to a world where I'm reviled. \n\nWhere is Mathias? Why hasn't anyone come to help me?
Whoever you are, I'm going to make sure you're well-rewarded for this.
He did? How do you know Mathias?\n\nNever mind. Can you take me to him? Can we leave this terrible place?

She led us against Potentate Versidue-Shaie. He demanded we disband our army and join his empire. King Aphren, Princess Mira's father, agreed. He claimed it would spare us a long, brutal battle.\n\nHe was a fool. Redguards bow to no one!

It does. And by Maouloch, we need you! The ogres are about to make another big push, and I can only spare so many soldiers.\n\nWill you join Murtag clan in battle? We need you out on the battlefield right away.

What went wrong? I'll tell you what went wrong—I was trained to fight ogres, not rocks! \n\nWe can't even get to the ogres! It's those damn boulders they're throwing. Every time we try to charge across, another one of my soldiers gets smushed!

There's no one left to help—just me, and I'm spent.\n\nGet through the ogres, and you can do it alone though. A pickaxe to the support beams down there will bring the whole place down. Smash 'em … and then run for your life.
Considering I'm an hour late and knowing Dirdren Marvo's impatience, I probably am.

I was on my way to deliver a message to the Stranded Lurk when I was ambushed by hostile Ashlanders. They took my  weapons, and the message. Please try and retrieve it. For all I know it was vital information that's now in enemy hands.
I'm going to stay here and appear as though I'm still tied to this post so I won't arouse suspicion. The Vereansu have taken my weapons, so I am no use in freeing the sick.

To protect the Covenant! Orsinium sent our captain, <<1>>, to the Covenant as a military leader with backbone. Ogres followed us from Wrothgar, and we have to deal with them now. We'll keep Wind Keep safe against all her enemies.
I've heard about the killings, but we're here to protect the Covenant's citizens. We aren't here to protect mongrels that sneak through the cracks. Just the protection of the citizens.

<<1>> was sent here to fulfill our duty as members of the Covenant and take the fight to our enemies. We were ambushed on our way to Wayrest, and it is our duty to make the attackers pay. I don't know why we are worrying with the ogres.

I am concerned with our duty to hunt down those who ambushed us. The killing of mongrel races doesn't interest me, unless it is my duty to kill them. Then it does interest me. <<1>> gave us orders to watch Wind Keep, so I will fulfill that duty.

Why would you ask such a question? We are here to find spies and we will. Spies attacked our Captain, <<1>>, as we were coming from Orsinium to Wayrest. Now we are stuck fighting the Ogres. Ogres may be dumb brutes, but they aren't spies.

Murders? Spies murder only true citizens of the Daggerfall Covenant. If the spies fall on themselves, I wouldn't call that murder anymore than when a wolf kills a rabbit, or I kill an ogre. Now move along.

Those fire vials you have pack a powerful punch.

Smash one at the base of a rock. See if it's enough to launch a boulder down into those Daedra. 

We need to take out as many as we can, as fast as we can!

As soon as you launch one of these things, things are gonna get a little crazy.

I'll try to hold off anything that heads up the pass to you. If anything gets past me, you'll need to stop it before it puts you down. 

Got it? Good! Let's go!
Ah, I'm glad you asked! I am a treasurer of history, Northpoint's foremost expert in the chronicles of our people.\n\nAlas, I fear I have too much on my mind to tell you tales now, my friend.

All right. Take it. 

If you come back and I'm dead though, I still want it back. I want to be buried with it.

It's always brought me luck. Hope it does the same for you, for all of us.
He was with you wasn't he? Tell me what happened! \n\nTell me!
It... it can't be. Not Verandis. He's too strong. I can't believe you. I won't. \n\nHe still lives. I... I can feel it. I won't give up.

He stayed within the Merge to save us all? Perhaps he will finally forgive himself for all of this.\n\nHe will be back. I'm sure of it, <<1>>. Until then, the Ravenwatch will be under my command. This I do in his memory.

As was the case with all of us.

He'll be back. I'm sure of it. 

I just know it.

I let the Dreamers capture me so I could discover their plan.

I used magic to eavesdrop when they thought I was asleep. I know where the artifacts are.

I can slip my bonds at any time, but I can't collect the artifacts. Too many cultists!

Every night I dream the same dream. I try to eat, but when I bring food to my mouth, it turns to dust and blows away in a storm.\n \nBut I keep trying. Eventually, I begin to turn to dust. My hands, my arms, all begin to blow away in the wind...

Every night I dream I am in the desert dying of thirst. A storm breaks, but it brings no rain. It brings only thunder, lightning and wind.\n\nSand blows in my mouth. I can no longer scream as the thirst and sand stifles my voice and my life.

I dream every night that I am to attend the ball of <<1>>. When I arrive, I am covered in dirt and dung from my daily chores. \n\nGuards lock me in the stockades for my royal insult. People throw mud at me, and only my tears reveal any cleanliness.

In my dreams, I can almost put them together. The clues are all there. I almost have it solved. 

There's more than one murder! There's a bigger picture. 

Every time I wake up, I forget what I found in my dreams, but the clues are here.
Hmm. How to explain.\n\nImagine every kind of animal in Valenwood mashed together. A furious, skittering, barking, slathering fit of claws and teeth - fur and feather.

That wasn't entirely my idea, to be honest.

One of my friends from the gambling dens suggested it first, and here I am now!

Of course, the dreugh keep trying to come back, poor things, but this is our place now.

Why, up near Wayrest, of  course.

It's obvious the gods made these hot springs for the nobility's recreation.

The Divines favor those who possess divine right.

One of my friends from the gambling dens suggested it.

He's with a certain local guild, providing certain ... services, as needed.

He's keeping an eye on my summer home, if you'd like to meet him. I must name no names. It's a secret.
Oh, sure! Sure! I'm a topnosh … I'm a good wine seller. I'm Drothan. The Winemaster! I sell from Fort Virak to Davon's Watch and ever'where in between.\n\nAre you real? Your ears look funny.

What do you think, dolt? I've been kidnapped! 

They sent a flag of truce and a ransom note to my husband, but he hasn't paid yet. 

Why am I not surprised? Serge has been useless since the day I married him.
Maybe we can work together to restore the land.
Oh you are spying on me for the witch.

A Tale-Spinner. A sage, though there's little that's sage about them. Mostly they lie around and make up stories while other people work.\n\nThey can talk to plants, though. These razorvine walls are their doing.
The cost is 1 gold piece!
Here is your ticket. You may enter the arena!
Get out of here you bum!

Rumors about House Indoril? Only what is true. They are leaving us wide open to attack by pouring all of their resources into the war in <<1>>. When we're attacked by vicious creatures of nightmare, it will be too late!
I heard it on good authority from Endal Relendas. He works near the Council and is always picking up on conversations they don't want us to know!
Here are the challenges that are available:
Good Luck!
Which event would you like to end?
The Portals are closing
I was afraid of this. Someone must have spotted us moving the eggs. \n\nBaron Sorick said to do it, so we did it. We're not paid to question a noble's order.
Hmm. Scruples. Not a luxury I can afford.\n \nThat egg you have looks ready to hatch. You want Sorick to pay for his crimes? Toss that egg in his pool, then watch. Me, I'll find a new boss.
Of course. Baron Sorick appreciates your discretion.

And I have more terrible news. Those damned outlaws cast a sleeping spell on Abbot Durak. I can't wake him.\n\nHe came down here for this Scroll of Summoning, said it would stop the biggest fire. I just hope it's worth what it cost.

Azura praise his foresight! This will get us back to the abbey.\n\nDurak said this Scroll of Summoning should be read near the largest fire in the field. Please take it and use it there. I'll meet you at the abbey when you're done.
Back from seeing the Goblin?
I see. I do not tolerate being lied to. Our business here is finished.
I am willing
Hmm, well we will take the high road and make a peace offering.
What did he say?

Ra'ud? Oh, yes! He's a poet. He's so sensitive. I might enjoy spending time with him.

I love windflowers. They awaken my desires. They're delicate, like a butterfly's kiss. 

No one brings me windflowers, alas, since they know I hate other flowers.

Windflowers grow northeast of Reywell.

There are so many flowers nearby, though. I wonder what Ra'ud would choose on his own ....

A poet's gift is what he says and how he says it. A lover's gift answers his beloved's requests.
I hope Ra'ud gets it right this time.
I hope Ra'ud gets it right this time.
I hope Ra'ud gets it right this time.
What?  I love windflowers. I hope Ra'ud's sending me a bigger bouquet of them.
I see. He thinks so poorly of me that he can't be bothered to pick the flowers himself.\n\nTell him to take his bouquet and choke on it. I'll never speak to him again or suffer his advances.

Tell him that I'm quivering in anticipation of the delights to come.

Perhaps he will sing to me. I hear poets have the gift of song. Maybe we'll drink the finest of wines together.

I cannot wait!
The dreugh came clattering into Dreughside, attacking people. It was terrifying! \n\nMy husband, Arcady, tried to rally folks to fight back.

Sergeant Stegine brought a few guards. He's a good man, but it was four of them against all those dreugh.\n\nBaron Sorick owns this land. We begged for more guards, but he says the dreugh will leave on their own. Doesn't he care?

Their hatching pools are nearby—but they've never bothered us before. \n\nFor some reason, the dreugh came into town, looking for trouble, and the people fought back. Some were killed, but others were dragged away. It's awful!

The Dream Shard is a priceless relic, a literal piece of Azura's realm of Moonshadow.\n\nWith it, we can distill water from the Cave of Dreams into Dreamless Potions. Without that shard, we can't make any more of them.
It won't be easy. The spell enthralling the Abbot traps him in sleep and forces him to dream.\n\nIt's a clever spell, since the Spirit Wardens can't enter his dream. In fact, we can't dream at all.

We have another potion we rarely use: a Dreamstride Potion. It'll put you into a dreaming sleep. Then I can merge your mind with Abbot Durak's.\n\nYou must find him in his dream, figure out what holds him there, and awaken him.

We drink Dreamless Potions nightly. That's why we're immune to dream attacks from our enemies, the Supernal Dreamers.\n\nAs of now, you're the only person in Pariah Abbey who can dream: the only one who can save Durak.
Good. Once I've removed these chains, we'll awaken.\n\nSpeak with me again in the waking world.

I've heard them refer to themselves as the Midnight Union. From what I can tell, they're a gang of thieving scoundrels.\n\nThe two I've seen the most are Albert and Alison Lanier. I bet one of them has the key to my cage.
The last I heard, Serge was headed out to the Reywell Hot Springs northwest of here. He's probably stinking drunk and sitting in a spring somewhere.
Oh, his lordship would never permit that. \n\nHe knew what was going to happen, but he doesn't want his involvement known. He planned it that way. But that's his business, not ours.

It's your funeral, stranger. \n\nBut listen, he pays me keep these things quiet. Seems to me you have a choice: you can stick your nose in an get into trouble, or you earn a little bonus by staying out of it.

They went to The Thrambles - a patch of primeval forest north of Razorvine Refuge.\n\nIt's dark and full of things that'll eat you. Everything from blood-sucking hoarvor to a giant Senche-Tiger. So they say, anyway. I'm not going to find out.

I am a tale in children's minds. I keep their secrets and share them inside. I blur their thoughts into fantasies, kept like a canvas of art or a submarine depth. Though an illusion, it occurs every night; I give them a fantasy, I give them a fright.
You do look like trouble and I suspect it would be a nightmare to know you.  Move along.

You are more intelligent than you appear.  A few days ago the guards brought a man and a woman in.  The man was bloodied and beaten.  The woman they took over to the Inn.  I hear she is getting quite the attention. She goes by the name Valoria.
You certainly are living in one.  The reality is that you're not as smart as you would like to be.  Get lost.

Yes you have a very active imagination.  I bet you're imagining me giving you information right now!  That is not going to happen though.  Go away or I imagine that my blade will find its way into your throat.
I offer a variety of services here.
We offer comfortable beds and lucky for you we still have a few available.  It's 5 gold for the night.
We have fresh killed meat and an endless keg of ale.  The bartender will fetch what ever you want.
We have the finest women in Tamriel.  They are eagerly waiting to comfort you.  Which would you like to lay with?
Valoria will not dissapoint you.  You will find her upstairs in the first room on the right.
My family was attacked by the guards.  They killed my parents and brought my brother and me here.  My brother is being held in the cells in the guard house.  Can you free him?
Be careful of the guards.  You must sneak in and not alert them.
My dad is still alive? That is wonderful news!  We must free my brother and return to him.

My dad and sister are still alive!  I'm afraid the same wont be true for me soon.  The guards have assured that my life will come to an end.\n\nPromise me that you will return to my sister with a message for me?
Thank you!  Tell them I love them and to forget about me.\n\nYou must get out of here before the guards return.
Bah! They're like locusts. Every once in a while they just swarm. \n\nBut this is worse than usual. It's the first time they've breached the gates.
He hates Goblins. I mean we all hate Goblins, but he really hates them. I've asked why, but he won't say. \n\nShould've listened to my instincts and sent him to another post.
So he's alive? Did you free him?
Take my ring and necklace from the dresser.\n\nYou can trade them at the armorsmith and weaponsmith to help in the arena.
We can't get him past the guards, but there's another way.\n\nOne of the guys who frequents this place can secure his freedom, but you must fight in the arena for him. Speak with Morgen Shadehands.
You want a favor from me?  Do you know who I am? \n\nWhere would you get the idea that I'm in the buisness of handing out favors?
Valoria, Valoria, Valoria …  yes a man will agree to anything in the arms of such a woman.\n\nI know her brother's life is rotting away. I can arrange for his freedom, but you must fight for it.
I own some of the greatest gladiators to ever fight in this arena.  \n\nI want you to enter the arena and becomes its champion. If you can conquerer the arena, I will get her brother's freedom.
Don't dissapoint me. If you lose, I'll make sure that Valoria and her brother die with you.\n\nSpeak with the Master of Events inside the arena.
You want to challenge the Arena Champion?  Head to the center of the arena and prepare for your death!
There's lot of work to be done.  leave me be for now.
We'll be right behind you
Yes, it must have slipped from your pack. Luckily for you, I found it. \n\nI thought you might come back to look for it. Try not to lose it next time!

I can't pay him. I bet my last coin on a fight at Hammerdeath Arena and won, but the Orc who bet against me refuses to pay up.\n\nYou want money? Go beat it out of Ugurz. He's working with a gang of Orcs down by the southern docks.

Sorry. I'm flat broke. And it was actually one of S'rashi's friends who convinced me to sell the estate and invest in pig saddles for children! \n\nBig surprise—they didn't sell very well. I lost everything.

Oh? So you're going to kill me? Because … I don't have the money. Nothing to be done for it. I'm not going to run though. I'm a man of integrity, at least in this case. \n\nYou don't think S'rashi could give me a few more weeks?
Yes, it must have slipped from your pack. Luckily for you, I found it. \n\nI thought you might come back to look for it. Try not to lose it next time!
Ahtah's Book of Circles is imbued with ancient powers. Even Ahtah will not invoke them.\n\nLegends say this tome has the power to affect entire villages. Its magic is truly incredible.

<<1>> is Count Hosni's cousin. He's been visiting here quite some time now. I can't tell if he's trapped here like the rest of us or if he's just enjoying the power he holds while he's here.\n\nHe keeps the chest on the second floor of the manor.
He's just north of us, sitting near a tree. I rarely let him out of my sight, but I think he prefers to keep an eye on me as well after he found out about the winding key.
All I know is that the trap is an enchantment. The lock can't be picked, nor the trap disabled, so you must either have a key or know the order to play the harps.
As long as they're quick. I'm looking forward to taking in Barnabe's reaction.\n\nI have no doubt there will be bloodshed.

Tomes that survive for centuries are inherently powerful. 

Ahtah's Book of Circles isn't just revered for the magical knowledge within it. We value this book for the blood encrusted on it.

This rare tome is stained with the blood of Makela!

Makela Leki! 

She was a swordsinger, one of the legendary few who could summon a swordsinger's sacred weapon: the shehai.

I don't know who saved her blood, or how it came to be on Master Ahtah's Book of Circles. That would be another tale.
A swordsinger forges a shehai through training, meditation, and devotion.\n\nShehai are rare. Even Master Ahtah has not created one.

Hosni just wants more sport for the Aaena. Keep in mind, not only is he demanding an item he knows I don't have, but he's also sent you to get it.\n\nYou should be wondering why he's chosen you for such a futile task.
Hmm. Not sure. Don't know. \n\nBut after this, we should finish them for good. Wipe out the whole tribe. That's what I say.
Sadir stole Ahtah's Book of Circles. The book is powerful, but no one intended it to be used as a weapon.\n\nHe needs both the book and a spirit warden's soul to distill its magic.

Sadir leads this circle of the Supernal Dreamers cult.

They worship Vaermina, the Daedric Prince of dreams and nightmares.

" … from grain-slave to hoplite and loved well, took death from an arrowhead made from the beak of Celethelel the Singer, the Whitestrake went on his first Madness. He wrought destruction from Narlemae to Celediil, and erased those lands from … "

" … the growing armies of the Paravania and his bull nephew. Pelinal called out Haromir of Copper and Tea into a duel at the Tor and ate his neck-veins while screaming praise to Reman, a name that no one knew yet."

"Gordhaur the Shaper's head was smashed upon the goat-faced altar of Ninendava. In his wisdom, Pelinal said a small plague spell to keep that evil from reforming by welkynd magic. Later that season, Pelinal slew Hadhuul on the granite steps of … "

" … Ceya-Tar, the Fire King's spears knowing their first refute. No weapon of the Ayleids could pierce his armor, which Pelinal admitted was unlike any crafted by men, but would say no more even when pressed. When Huna, whom Pelinal raised … "

" … the maps of Elves and Men, and all things in them, and Perrif was forced to sacrifice to the Gods to keep them from leaving the earth in their disgust. And then came the storming of White-Gold, where the Ayleids had made pact with … "
" … for Umaril had the blood of the 'ada and would never know death."

" … the Aurorans of Meridia and summoned them. They appointed the terrible and golden-hued "Half-Elf" Umaril the Unfeathered as their champion. For the first time since his coming, it was Pelinal who was called out to battle by another … "
Miranda's the heir to the Farangel estate. Technically, this all belongs to her.\n\nWhen Miranda and I met, it was love at first sight. I knew we were made for each other.
Thank you, whoever you are. You've saved my life.
No. If I leave this gate to Quagmire, the spirit will take me. \n\nUnless—I suppose I could force the spirit out of me and into a dreaming cultist. It's not as certain, but it could work.

There's a vial of poison over there, next to the candles. I can recognize its foul stench from here. Bring it to me.\n\nAnd thank you. I couldn't really ask Gerard to do this, no matter how necessary.

Word is the Midnight Union just pulled off a jewel heist. We can use their stolen gems to pay the ransom. \n\nCheck inside a couple of the nearby houses. I've heard they hide their loot by dispersing it that way.
I can use puffball caps to make a sleep potion.\n\nAlchemy's a hobby of mine. That's why I have a crate of exotic fungus waiting for me on the dock.

Puffball caps? Oh, you fool—that's not a sleep potion, it's poison! \n\nNow no one's guarding Miranda. Lord Serge will probably poison her, too. You'll need an antidote … and so will I, since I drank from the kegs. This vervain should do it ….
I order the lord's alchemy supplies for him. A crate of dried vervain was just unloaded on the east beach. \n\nLady Miranda's in the manor house. Use this key to get inside—and please, hurry!
You're right. Take the antidote. Maybe I can find vervain for myself in the lord's alchemy chamber.\n\nLady Miranda is in the manor house. Use this key to get inside—and please, hurry!
