Testing, testing.
You're telling me! It was a slaughter, on both sides. \n\nThe sergeant said there were dreugh eggs among the houses, and the dreugh must have come after them. I don't know.
Pfui. I'll just say you wrote it yourself. \n\nIt's my word against yours, and I'm a Breton nobleman. Don't waste my time.

I admit that might be enough to be … inconvenient.\n\nBoth Dreughside and the hatching pools are in my fief. Both are infested with pests. I just came up with a brilliant way to have them exterminate each other. What of it, lowborn?
But of course. You're quite reasonable, for a commoner. \n\nHere, this ought to be enough. No paltry amount! As for Charnis, I'll deal with him.
You, kill me? A Lord of Wayrest?\n\nPerhaps you would. You have that look about you. Very well. I'll have my men remove the eggs. Satisfied?
Please, don't leave me here! Have mercy!
Check on Adiel Charnis. Her house is just north of here. She told me dreugh took her husband.\n\nI need to stay here to keep an eye on the defense, but I'd appreciate it if you could help her out.

Everyone's always excited to receive an invitation from Count Hosni. He's always thrown the best parties. \n\nBut this one is different. Something's going on. Guests have disappeared. And now the guards won't let me leave.

The guards stopped me when I tried to go out the gate. They were quite rude. One of them said, "It's not your time to leave yet, my lord. And when you leave, you'll be carried out."\n\nI didn't like the sound of that. Not at all.
What? I don't know what you're talking about.\n\nTake a walk.
I've seen Hosni worship at a shrine to Vaermina and then take a sleeping brew. So check the shrine.\n\nThe rest is on you.

Those worthless curs kidnapped me with a shipment of fine art from <<1)>>. They took my art and were going to ransom me back to my family in Wayrest, but I managed to escape. \n\nOn top of it all, they... soiled... some of the paintings.

That sounds like the Guild is asking for a favor. I have a favor to ask of them. 

When I was kidnapped, I paid an Orc sellsword named Lokk for his services and he never reported for duty. He won't return my payment.

Could you get it back for me?
There's no need for hostility... I apologize if I've wasted any of your time.\n\nThey've taken over a burnt-out farmstead between Aphren's Hold and Wayrest.
He surrounds himself with his band of Orc thugs. He probably won't give up the payment through polite conversation.
There's no need for hostility... I apologize if I've wasted any of your time.\n\nThey've taken over a burnt-out farmstead between Aphren's Hold and Wayrest.
Excellent. I hope no one was hurt. Too badly, that is.\n\nThe Vermeir Cutthroat bastards are in a burned out farm between Aphren's Hold and Wayrest. You can't miss them.

It's the Supernal Dreamers. They've opened a portal to Oblivion in Maw Cave—that's where those Scamps came from—and we came here to close it. \n\nIt was a trap. The Dreamers wanted Master Muzgu for some reason. And now they've got him!

They're trying to open more portals here and there. We need to stop that—but I have to go try to save Master Muzgu.\n\nCan you kill some Scamps and hurl their heads into the nascent portals? The magical feedback should shut them down.
It's simple transliminal metaphysics. The Scamps just came here through another portal from Quagmire, Vaermina's realm, so they're still charged with positive creatia. Got that?
Yes. Barnabe and Geon hate each other. They're the only guaranteed form of entertainment I've found here on a daily basis.\n\nLosing them would be a shame.

Very well. I'll contain the Daedra as long as I can.\n\nTake a Scroll of Dream Trapping from the rock over there and use it on a sleeping cultist to bind him to your will. Then you can lead him back here.

You can't assault me in the middle of the street! Can you?

Look, I can give you this. It's my wedding ring. My wife left me a year ago, and it's worth a good amount of coin.

Just take it, all right? Take it and leave me be.
What are you going to do about it? Threaten me? \n\nHa! I'll stomp your face in. Turn and go now, unless you want to die.
S'rashi? I don't want trouble with the Midnight Union. \n\nTake the money. Tell S'rashi I-I didn't know. I'm sorry for the confusion.

You're a scrappy little <<1>>. You amuse me.

Take your debt. This is nothing to me.

Now get off my docks before I change my mind.
Wait a minute. That's not fair! I didn't ….\n\nLook. My reputation's already bad enough. Last thing I need is more rumors. I do have some money. Just take this and go.

Tsk tsk! S'Rashi cannot give out such information without compensation.

However, this one sympathizes with your plight.

Finish S'Rashi's favor. Then we will talk more about this.
We're questioning these cultists about what they're doing here without our permission. Count Hosni won't let us perform a formal investigation, so we're running our own.

Thank you. When I drink this, I'll die and disappear. The ritual circle will send the Daedric spirit back into the realm of dreams.\n\nPromise me you'll go through the portal to Quagmire and slay the spirit.
So be it. Take care, friend.

It's true—I've seen it. Lady Adima designates a guest who's offended her in some way, and the guards take him away.\n\nThe rumor is they're made to fight to the death. Just like in Hammerdeath Arena. I'm serious!
Just between you and me—I'm sure of it.\n\nWhen a guest is taken away, Lady Adima follows. And the last time she came back, she had blood on her shoes.
"It was the year two-hundred and twenty-two, in the First Era of recollection. The Ayleidoons held Cyrodiil under sway, a pressed sheaf of bickering kingdoms and baronies and lordships."
Ah, the hero of the day—or so I expect! How lovely to see you here. Isn't this divine?\n\nSmile, you fool. Nod your head and laugh a little. Act like you're enjoying yourself.
"For the Ayleidoons were callous masters, devious and prone to perverse desires. As were their Daedric overlords, the wanton whims of whom are still well-known in our times."

"And it was in this day that the Slave-Queen did arise, she who we name Saint Alessia, also called Al-Esh, also known as Perrif.\n\nFrom thralldom was she born into a life of subjugation, surrounded by a world of abject misery."

"With the magics of the dread Daedra, demi-gods and dark princes from the realms beyond, did the elven lords keep their slaves at bay. For the Nedic tribes were un-united in those days, having neither leadership nor civilization to bind them."
Don't take too long. It's not easy keeping this up. \n\nWell, give him my regards, won't you? Now I'm going to get another drink. Stay happy!
How amusing! She says the same thing about you!\n\nBecause I don't want to be taken downstairs and killed. And I assume the same goes for you. Any ideas on how we can get out of here?
Let me see. Ah, this is a platinum-level invite. The count says you get to come and go as you please.\n\nThat's more leeway than he usually gives his guests these days.
He's in the manor with his betrothed, <<1>>.\n\nTonight's festivities have already resulted in four deaths. Better hurry.

" … into a great Empire, and claim her seat at its head, the First Empress. And bloody was the war, and long, but the Slave-Queen was indomitable in her will - that the elves be crushed beneath the feet of those who were made to build … "

"For it is only so long that such injustice can survive, in a land of thinking men. And so it was that, with an army of slaves before her, and the champions of Light and Life beside her, did Alessia endeavor to transform the lands of elves … "

" … the woman-child Alessia, and there make with her that pact which would break the armies of Elf and Daedra for all time. From that day forth it was destined that Alessia should sit in judgment of the Ayleid kingdoms, and see them destroyed."

"Seeing the blood-pacts made by the Ayleidoons with the Daedra, the Aedra having left the races of Cyrod to their own machinations, descended unto the plane of mortality and, seeking that virtue most akin to their own nature, did appear to … "
" … and later suffered under, their kingdom of vice. And long was her reign, and fruitful, for the Empress and her northern allies made good upon their union, and prosperity flowered in abundance."

We'll expel the Daedra. Draw the cultist into ritual circle. After the Daedric spirit consumes its victim, it will return to Quagmire.\n\nFollow the spirit through the portal to Quagmire, kill the Daedra there, then return. Ready?
Sadly, no. The prophecy was quite clear. "Crown restored to king before the keystone bring."\n\nWe realize it should be "brought" instead of "bring," but you know. Prophecies.
Why, the kingdom of Zuuk! And now that you're here, the king of you.\n\nIt is a responsibility we do not take lightly.

The slums are on Lord Sorick's land, but he refuses to send more soldiers. He acts like he's enjoying the slaughter!\n\nWe must stop this before all the peasants get themselves killed. You can help by taking eggs from the slums back to the pools.
The robes of a dead prisoner? I'm not sure I'd want to be in this tower with a dead and naked Supernal Dreamer. Even moreso, I don't think the Captain would like it much either.
Excellent point! All right, here you go. \n\nUse them wisely. Anything that might be a thorn in the side of the Supernal Dreamers is a good plan to me.
Nice doing business with you!
Suit yourself. No loss on my end. Besides, I think even the cultists here would be glad he gets to keep his clothes on.
Now you're speaking my language! I'm sure I could let you have them for say, 50 silver.
"Named for its connection to the great Ayleid Towers, the staff contains eight autonomous segments.\n\n"Each one independently channels the energies of an associated tower."

"The master enchanter Aurelia of Dramgadoon submitted this first hypothesis."\n\n"This was easily proven through sublimation of the god-spark enthralled in the staff's spur during the uninhibited period which followed the caesurae of Loreth's reign."

"The perpetrator of this act remains a historical mystery, though some assert that the staff was thereafter incomplete.\n\n"The spur was alternately lost or stolen. (However, I should articulate that it was never actually destroyed.)"

"We can assume from the historical record that the victors of Blue Road never made it to their ultimate destination, but were instead overrun by the Alessian Order forces stationed at the nearby fortress of Lake Kheydin."

"The staff itself was recovered in the fifth century during the Alessian rebellions and briefly employed against those rulers of the Empire, as described in Tedrimur's account of the battle at Blue Road.\n\n"Subsequently, it vanished."
"One may then muse: If the Alessians possessed such a weapon, why did they not employ it to their advantage?"
"This places the Staff of Towers squarely in the hands of the Alessian Empire during the tumultuous years of rebellion in which they were ultimately driven to defeat."

<You've reached the final page.>

"This brings us to the Dragon Break, which will be fully examined in my next manuscript, entitled Time, Towers, and the Staff of Chaos.

-- Reginnus Vertantian, Historian of Hillborne"

"This historian can only conclude that the staff never made it to the hands of the Emperors, that instead a faction within the Alessian Order concealed the staff's existence with the intent of using it to an even larger purpose."
"Maruhk preached for ninety days and ninety nights, stopping only one hour in every twelve to relieve himself and quench his gullet."
"The Maruhkites uphold that as he preached, Maruhk was in fact in the grip of an epic and all-encompassing vision, a visitation from the spirit of St. Alessia herself."
"Maruhk's words were uttered as one not in possession of one's self, as if the sermon was merely being translated through him by another being."

"Detractors maintain the monkey-prophet was merely deluded by an excess consumption of skooma, jagga, hop-caps, or in some instances, Daedra blood. Concrete evidence to support these allegations is surprisingly lacking."

I went to Wayrest to buy Miranda a gift. While I was away, the Midnight Union overran the estate and took her captive. \n\nI can't pay a ransom—my wife's family has money, not me! I must bargain from a position of strength or they'll kill her.

I need a carrot to tempt them and a stick to threaten them. You seem fearless—see if you can collect jewels hidden in the houses, and puffball caps from a crate on the docks.\n\nOnce you've got all that, meet me near the boathouse.

Again? These guys just don't get it. We'll turn a blind eye to some things, but not robbing people in the streets.\n\nWe had an understanding with the Midnight Union, but ever since their presence started weakening here, we get these upstarts.

They're known as the Backstreet Gang—your basic thugs, but there's nothing basic about their leader.

Name's Ondre. They call him 'the Grinder' because he grinds up his victims. Wanted for dozens of murders.

Say, you want to do another good deed?
Look for a large gate to the west. You'll have to go through and leave the safe grounds of the estate.\n\nThe barracks are at the end of the path before it curves down toward the shore.

Only because those items belong to the Supernal Dreamers. Since Count Hosni's engagement to <<1>>,  he's treated them like nobles. You'd think he'd forgotten about us completely.\n\nIt's created a lot of tension between the two factions.
Now that sounds like a fine spectacle, and one truly worth paying for. \n\nTread carefully. Those who find themselves indebted to Hosni only find freedom in death. Fortunately, we have a plan.
I wish I knew, although I have a feeling it has something to do with <<1>>. \n\nSince she arrived, he only cares about entertaining himself with his sordid games.

We're doing that already. We got a hold of some of them and took to questioning them up in the tower. The count would never know. \n\nLuckily, you can't tell their screams from the screams of his own guests!
Impressive, isn't it? But I suppose it's to be expected from the Midnight Union. I can't imagine the things I could find in there!
That's not what I've heard. The rumor is, he keeps his most valuable items locked up in a chest inside the manor.\n\nNot just any chest, though. This one's been enchanted.
The lock can't be picked. The only way to open it is to dispell the enchantment on the lock. I've heard it has something to do with music.
Count Hosni recently handed over our barracks to those Supernal Dreamers. \n\nI can't risk getting caught. It would be too tempting to kill them all should even one of them dare speak to me.
To Quagmire, realm of the Daedric Prince Vaermina, Queen of Nightmares. \n\nBelieve me, she means the mortals of this plane nothing but ill.

Only how weak their bodies are. It's obvious they're here for a reason. It's just a matter of time before one of them cracks.\n\nThink of the lives they might save if they only told the truth, namely their own.
It's good to know that we agree on something. Feel free to admire all you like.\n\nI prefer to think of it as a collection.
I'm amazed someone of your caliber would have an eye for such a thing. I accept your compliment.\n\nNow, once again, I am busy.

Of that, have no doubt. 

Prizes such as those are too valuable to be kept under a simple lock and key. Protecting them requires more than the watchful eyes of mere mortals.

Let's just say I'm more than confident when it comes to their security.

Nonsense! My estate is heavily guarded, and my guests have learned the consequences of stealing. 

They know them well … perhaps too well.

In some kingdoms, they cut off a thief's hand for stealing. Here, I prefer to cut out a thief's heart.
Such rabble wouldn't dare lay a finger on my personal effects!\n\nBesides, Count Hosni allows me to leave my instruments in a more private treasury.
Enough questions. As I said before, I am busy.

I gave you a chance... a chance to join me and save this forest from all who would harm it. Do not think that your "friends" in the so-called Dominion won't destroy the forest just as the Imperials have.

This is not a matter for debate. If you do not accept that all invaders in the Valenwood must be eradicated, then count yourself among their number.\n\nI have no need to parley with enemies. I will do what must be done myself.
Deception? I merely helped you see things the way I see them, so that you could ascertain your true enemies.

Allies? I see you've made your choice.

If you can't see that these invaders you call allies are just as vile as the Imperials, then you will be removed along with them.

I will complete the cleansing of this forest myself, with or without your help.

Ha! S'rashi's brother's so kind! Abandons and asks a stranger to take his place. He's soon chasing sweetmeat in Senchal. No one cares for S'rashi.\n\nBrothers should be loyal. You owe S'rashi nothing, but S'rashi will pay for help, yes?

You've got more stones than I gave you credit for. I like that. \n\nTell you what. If you can get what I owe Louis out of the lockbox over there, you can keep it. All you have to do is take it. Easy as that.
Well … there is one. This gem. It summons a protective Scamp.\n\nWe're not supposed to use it, but as long as you bring it back, I suppose it can be our secret.
I hate to part with it, but I do have this amulet. I hope it will aid in the cause.
Really? Did he tell you why he wants it?\n\nThe signet proves ownership of our estate. Once he has the ring, my wife and I can be disposed of. So what did he buy you with?

So the story is true, then. Well, I hope you succeed—but not at the cost of our lives. \n\nHosni only spares me because I've hidden the ring. If he kills me, he'll never find it. But I fear his next step will be to threaten my wife, Sirali.

Hosni has separated us—he's put Sirali in the summer house, above the beach. Go there, make sure she's safe. \n\nAnd tell her about the Dream Shard. She and Hosni were quite close. If anyone would know where he'd keep such a relic, it's Sirali.
Turn right outside my door and go to the west gate. Then just follow the path along the bluff to the summer house.

You'll just have to trust your instincts. I think you know the difference between an honest man and one who's … gone mad.\n\nYou want the Dream Shard. I want to know that my wife is safe. Maybe we can help each other.

You'll just have to trust your instincts. I think you know the difference between an honest man and one who's … gone mad.\n\nYou want the Dream Shard. I want to know my wife is safe. Let's help each other.

It's coming to an end.

With the Huntress gone, her magic fades. We... we are part of that magic.

Existing in this world is not something we can do without her.
Stay with me... until the end.\n\nYou've been a great friend, <<1>>. Soon... I'll be with my father and mother again. Part of Valenwood. And we'll watch over you. I promise.

Your mission was hard enough.

You've done so much for me. For everyone. Enerist left to be with his family. I wish I could be with my brother. I... miss him.

But your here... that's enough.
Thank the Eight. I've been so worried since Hosni separated us. \n\nAnd now those Supernal Dreamers outside are threatening me. Though it could be that Hosni just sent them to intimidate me.
I do—and I think that so-called Lady Adima is to blame. \n\nI'm certain she's why he's threatening Rihad and me. And I'd wager she's putting him up to even worse.
He did that? Then he's taken High Rock's main defense against Vaermina's cultists. \n\nOh, Adima's behind it, all right. If only we could prove it.
Bah! He got me, but it's not bad. Just need to get my bearings and I'll be fine.\n\nGo after Elvira. I couldn't live with myself if that monster Ma'jhad Kha killed her.
Oh he did? Here you go. Now get going and tell that swindler I want my cut this time.

A disease of the blood, one that ends in dementia and vampirism. I thought it legend, but I have seen strong men weep as it ravaged mind and body.\n\nJust as they find release in death, it wrenches them back to the living world as a soulless creature.

I believe he is building an army of mindless beasts from our own people, all of them sickened with blood fever.\n\nWhen you enter the <<1>>, you will see my suspicions confirmed. I pray you have the fortitude to do what you must.
He often plays in the courtyard garden. \n\nDestane's a maggot, but he's close with Hosni. He's smart, and he's no coward, so watch yourself.

You need to first collect 5 pieces of Green Maple from the stumps outside of the gates. 

Then you need to open up your recipe book and follow the instructions there. 

Do you understand?
As I had foreseen. \n\nIt is gratifying to have one's foresights proven true. Well done.
You should have the honor of returning the Dream Shard to its place on Azura's Statue. Please see that it is properly returned. \n\nThen we can talk about what comes after.

You need to harvest 5 pieces of Green Maple, from the stumps outside of the gates.

Next open your recipe book and follow the instructions to refine those pieces and make 1 piece of Planed Maple. 

Do you understand?
Green maple. Logs on the ground, north gate. \n\nOpen yer recipe book. Pick the recipe. Follow instructions.

A cursed creature from another realm. A Daedra. It must be slain.\n\nAn enchantment hides its foul form, but this scroll of sight will reveal it. Follow the sound of falling water and use the scroll to find it.

My remains were poured into a box centuries ago along with countless others. \n\nThe box was used against its purpose. My spirit was brought here to see this wrong put right. What was summoned must be destroyed.
Good. Can't learn by yourself. Tree grows alone, dies alone. Ready for some recipes now. Novice.

I was, and still am. I just allowed myself to be captured so I could listen to what the Supernal Dreamers were planning here.\n\nI've learned this much—it's far more serious than just a few stolen relics.

There were some extremely powerful relics here—ancient conjuration boxes.\n\nIt seems the Supernal Dreamers have learned how to activate these devices, and they plan to use them to summon terrible fiends.
We're not savages, novice. We learn by collaboration, by studying the techniques of others. You'll need to research the work of others, find inspiration from what they've done.

Haha. No. I promise. After being tied up recently in Alcaire, I decided to study the art of escaping these kinds of binds.\n \nThe crude ones used by the Supernal Dreamers are especially easy.  I'll be free any minute.
Open your pack. Read it. Hhmph.
Buy some pitch. Elodie, inside, sells it. Wood from earlier. Still have it, yes?\n\nGo to crafting bench. Open yer recipe book. Follow instructions. Make something.
I don't mean anything by it.\n\nIt's just, the count is different since he met that woman. But I don't ask questions. I suggest you don't either.
I don't mean anything by it.\n\nIt's just, the count is different since he met that woman. But I don't ask questions. I suggest you don't either.
I don't mean anything by it.\n\nIt's just, the count is different since he met that woman. But I don't ask questions. I suggest you don't either.

You've already gathered the ore. That's the hard part.\n\nTo smelt the ore into an ingot, open your recipe book and select the copper ingot recipe. Follow that recipe, fire and steel, and you'll have an ingot in no time.

Open your crafting notebook, and go to the research section. It's a separate tab at the bottom. Then take the sword and drop it into the slot right there in the notebook. \n\nYou need to really study the sword. Test the edge. Break it down!

Mortal, you waste precious time!

Forgive me. I must apologize. I'm just so wretched.

Take the crystals you've gathered and throw them into the brazier on the dais. That will disrupt the barrier so that I may finally leave. Then I'll reward you.
Take the Apprentice Sword scroll out of your backpack and read it.\n\nIf you lost the scroll I am sure Gard, my apprentice, has one for sale.

Orcs loyal to the High King had Ranser and his legion surrounded. Story goes that Ranser had some grand strategy to win the war, but General Dathieu betrayed him. They say the cursed legion still guards the tor waiting for the chance to strike again.
"This is my confession.\n\n"As a novice of the Maruhkati Selective, I watched helplessly as the glory of my order was crushed under the heel of Imperial interests."

"Our forces were disbanded, a standing army of the faithful dissolved down into a few scattered companies.\n\n"I heard all this, rather than saw. We initiates were relegated to the sanctuary, the last bastion of Maruhkati supremecy."

"What I know came through a torrent of rumors, words which quickly flooded the close confines of our stronghold. The Alessians had turned on us. They allied themselves with the elves. Our soldiers were ordered to stand down."
"The masters refused to speak of it. But there were whisperings throughout the refuge. After the rite, the staff would be brought here. In the archives, it would be secure."
"Then there was talk of the staff. The ancient power. It would be our salvation, to break us from the elven yoke for good. A rite would be performed, and we would be free."
"Finally the day came. The staff was brought to us. In the depths of our fortress we hid it, where the faithless and the unbelievers could not reach it."
"What was already the final refuge of the Maruhkites became the final resting place of the staff."
Skygazer peonies grow far to the north, near the waterfall. They prefer the higher ledges of the mountain ridge.\n\nBreloth loved their fragrant blossoms. They always looked wonderful in her hair.
Finding the wine is simple. Talk to <<1>> at the Wayside Inn. He'll sell it to you.\n\nYou know how the Bosmer like their drink. I'd like to bury the bottle with her.

You'll find plenty of mudcrabs at the base of the waterfall to the north. Stragglers are sometimes found in the passing stream.\n\nTheir succulent claw meat is the most important part. My wife never cared for the rest.

Open your crafting journal and go to the Research section. \n\nSelect the jack and start taking it apart. Note how the jack is constructed. Learn the subtleties that aren't captured in the written word. Got it?

You've found a recipe of mine? Oh! I thought I had lost it in the flight from Crestshade. \n\nIf you were to find enough spider ichor for me, I could use it to save a lot of lives. You would be compensated for your time, of course.

Really?

Well, that's what I need to find out. Yes?\n\nCould be anything, really. Stagnant water. An ill-favored star. Blonde women, especially the ones with ribbons in their hair. Corpses. Corpses are a good prospect. All sorts of things leak out of them.

Of course. Mathias is such a sweet boy, and he's served me well. It's a pity that I no longer have need of his service. \n\nI've been so false. So empty. I have no right to be a countess. I can see that now in my reflection.

Oh! Well then, I suppose you're an old friend of the countess's… I don't want to pry of course.\n\nBut, well, I am curious. What exactly is your relationship with her?

You mean if I were the count? I hoped for something like that, but my days of courting the countess have come to an end.\n\nI've no gold left for gifts. Haven't been able to give her anything for weeks. She's already forgotten me.

A mirror? No. She probably already has ten of those. No, the miniature pony—that's the thing.\n\nI'd bet Sir Brice gave her the mirror. Or I guess you could ask little old Alainne Babiloine. In fact…. oh, never mind. What do I know anyways?

I suspect the mirror was a gift from Raolin Munier. Ask him, or ask young Alainne Babiloine if she knows.

Of course… no, I promised to keep that secret. Never mind.

The mirror? Mathias could've told you… oh, but he was killed, wasn't he?\n\nWell, I don't mind telling you. It was actually a new suitor, but a strong contender. Tall, dark, handsome. Very dignified. I heard his footman call him 'Sirion'.
Well, I mean, I was curious, so, yes, I followed him. He hiked up into the woods north of town.\n\nKind of peculiar, honestly. So, can you tell me what this is all about? I'm dying to know.
Are you asking me to indulge in idle gossip? I assure you that I am above such shameful talk.\n\nI will keep my opinions of Raolin Munier to myself.

Maybe so. I was just thinking that Alainne seems to really idolize the countess. Talks about her all the time. Even hides in the bushes and watches the manse sometimes. \n\nI'd just speak with her. She knows who that mirror came from.

I suppose he's an honorable sort. He certainly carries himself that way. \n\nIf I was to choose the suitor to whom I had lost the countess's hand, it would be him. I could at least understand her wanting to marry a knight.
I know of him, but I don't consort with members of the working class.\n\nI certainly hope he wasn't the one to win the countess's hand. I would be humiliated to be upstaged by someone of low birth.

I suppose I'd be a fool to turn down such an opportunity. \n\nVery well. There's a young woman named Alainne who's … obsessed with the countess, what some might call a 'stalker'. She'll know who presented the mirror. She's the one to ask.
Where did you get those? Those are mine!\n\nNone may touch those save for me. That blade, that hilt, that pommel … to hold them again. Please, give them to me.

If you can break the ogres' charge, I'll move the command post up to the tower and you can meet me there.

That I am not an Argonian. I am a crocodile. \n\nThis lifetime, I have borrowed the form of another, but my true form is calling me home. I must return to the river.

Begin? I don't know. Days ago? Weeks? No … I was scratched.\n\nDuring the battle with the Montclairs … I remember a snarl … something touched my arm. I forgot about it until I noticed the deep scratch while I was tending to the wounded soldiers.

I knew that scoundrel couldn't have done this on his own! He has no mind for warfare, that's for sure.\n\nWe will need to mount a counterattack immediately. I will not let another usurp Shornhelm from me!

Not only have you defeated Lord Montclair, you have assassinated his master. If you were of Rivenspire blood, I would have you knighted immediately!\n\nAn Altmer was asking about you not moments before you arrived. Let him know we accept his deal.
Since then, I've been dreaming while I'm awake. I dream about teeth and blood. So much blood!\n\nI can smell it all around me. And I'm hungry … so hungry.

Rites so horrible, the details would blast your mind! Suffice to say the necromancers draw energy from their captives' torment so as to rend the barrier between worlds and summon more of their nefarious ilk.\n\nWhat I mean is, they're sacrificing them.

I'd sooner eat sand than do business with these Dunmer swine!

No. She just said it was for my own good, then something about a dream and my dad ….\n\nI don't understand. Who was that man and why did my mother tie me up?

Anything and everything. With Constable Pascal acting strange, Deputy Luric and I took the initiative. \n\nI may not have heard where their base of operations is, but there are plans for some other attack floating around the camp.

The Princess? She is all right then … that is good. King Fahara'jad sent me to protect her, but there is little I can do from out here. \n\nI do not wish to start a war, but I will if my king orders it. I await new orders even now.
Ah yes, indeed. The poison-maker was quite stubborn, but he spoke a name with his dying breath.\n\nIt means nothing to me though. He said "Falhut."

After the attempt on her life, that makes sense, but why go to her father? The Knights of the Flame are here to protect her. \n\nThat makes no sense. Why would he send an army here? The assassin's poison came from Alik'r—the duchess said so herself.

Dame Falhut? Are you … are you certain? That's a grave accusation. Of course, she was opposed to the marriage. \n\nWe'll have to question her, but sending a Knight of the Flame to apprehend her might not be wise.

Whew! They stink! Take these sacks. Put the talons on ... there! And the feathers go ... like so.\n\nThose look pretty good. Well, they look like harpies, at least. Anyway, can you put the four of these around our village?

I made bases for the scarecrows on the village outskirts before the elders made me come back.\n\nThey're at the lake, the east cliffs, the west cliffs, and right here. That should protect the whole village.
I can't imagine who would do such a thing.\n\nIf that is the case though, someone needs to send word to the Knights of the Flame at Alcaire Castle.

Technically, I work for the Fighters Guild, but Lanbaar contracted with us for a bodyguard.\n\nHe heard about the trouble in Shornhelm and figured to turn a quick profit. A good thought—until we found out the fighting spilled into the countryside.

Looks that way. At least until the Shornhelm Guard gives the all clear. From what I gather, the guard allowed themselves to get ambushed up at Hinault's Farm.\n\nYou never hear about the Guild getting ambushed, I can attest to that.

Hey, nothing's been stolen from Lanbaar yet! I protect the cart, I get paid. It's not my problem if the Khajiit can't get his goods to market.\n\nAnd I did stop a thief the other day. Not that anyone thanked me, mind you.
I wish I could tell you that I died in valiant battle, but I cannot.\n\nLike the very bandits I came to slay, I starved to death here in the dark after my fellow knights collapsed the cave.

I vowed to slay The Three after they killed my aunt and uncle in a robbery. 

I fear my failure to satisfy that vow is what drew my spirit back here along with theirs.

If you can destroy their spirits with my blade, my vow will be fulfilled.

In my time, they were the Band of The Three, robbers and bandits who achieved considerable wealth. They hired men to do their dirty work.\n\nReally, they were nothing special, just murderers and thugs who operated long enough to get a reputation.
Because you speak to me as if I were here and alive. \n\nI am an echo in these caves, the scream of a time long past. I don't know quite what you are, but I need your help.

Their spirits have returned as the Fallen Three, and they are worse than before.

Now The Three and their followers venture forth from this cave to steal people's souls rather than their money.

You must stop them.

Yes, my fellow knights did what had to be done.\n\nI can only imagine how difficult it must've been, but I had failed to fulfill my vow, and it was the only way to ensure The Three would terrorize this land no more.

No, these caves were too complex and the bandits too numerous. \n\nAfter the collapse, I crept down to find The Three eating their minions to survive. I was too hungry, too horrified to face them, and I knew they were only putting off the inevitable.

For better or worse, the Duke defers to me on the matter for now. Nathaniel shares King Emeric's bloodline but not his talent for calm under pressure.\n\nOf course, the Duke's wife being King Faraha'jad's daughter doesn't make matters easier.

I cannot defy the Duke's orders—not with an army at the gates. You can.

You didn't hear it from me.

I can only tell you what Darima told me. My father insisted Darima have a larger-than-usual armed escort. It's not the invasion everyone makes it out to be.\n\nI can almost understand their paranoia. Perhaps it is partly my fault.

I've tried to protect myself, but that's only raised suspicions within these walls.\n\nI … cannot speak more of this. Know that the rumors are not true. My father's soldiers do not seek dominion or conquest, only my safety.

Because it has greater potential for destroying the Daggerfall Covenant. \n\nMy choice to go to my father for help rather than the Knights of the Flame only made matters worse. I'm sorry for that now.

The Knights of the Flame are sworn to defend Stormhaven from any who would do harm to the Bretons. \n\nBut our primary duty is to protect the royal Family—High King Emeric of course, and his brother, Duke Nathaniel at Alcaire Castle to the north.

Clan Murtag offered us a choice. They left well-trained soldiers in our village to guard the Bretons. If we don't help them against the ogres, our families will pay.\n\nWe fight for the Orcs here to keep our children safe there.
How can she say that? How could she leave without him?\n\nShe can give up if she wants to, but I won't. Not until I know for sure. I still haven't searched everywhere. Will you help me?

I don't just believe—I know. My mother is just not thinking clearly. We haven't even checked all the buildings.\n\nI've actually been putting off the northern barn. It creeps me out. I'll go talk some sense into my mother, but could you check it?
"I was sleeping soundly in this cave when a gang of uncouth ogres stumbled upon my camp.\n\n"Obviously I managed to escape their meaty grasp, but I was forced to abandon my famous suit of armor!"
"Should anyone happen to find this note, I beg of you to liberate my armor from the uncivilized creatures within this cave and return it to me post-haste."

My duty is to ensure the safety of this village, and my gut's telling me that she's part of the threat. Too many coincidences. If we can get the village secure, we can revisit the matter.\n\nRight now, I need to deal with this ship.

He's not, but even if he was, it wouldn't be my problem. My duty is to the village—not his ship.

Bottom line—he needs to turn his ship around and head back out to sea. If not, we'll just sink it right here. 

That'll solve his slaver problem.

The slavers are on board! The captain claims he's not with them, but I know the truth.

He's asking me to send the town guard to help him clear the slavers from belowdecks.

Envoy Darima marches up with an army, claiming she's on a diplomatic mission from King Fahara'jad of Alik'r. She says her message is for Duke Nathaniel alone and demands entry.\n\nAll I have to say is, 'over my dead body'.

My mission is clear. No one from the Redguard camp allowed in the castle. I'm a Knight of the Flame and I will enforce that directive to my dying breath.\n\nSir Hughes is the head of our order. If you have concerns, speak to him inside the castle.

You did? Incredible! One hero comes to the aid of another, selflessly helping a stranger in need. Cheers to you!\n\nI suppose you're wondering how that skeleton came to be here. I will tell you my tale, if you like.

I immediately set out to find the rogue, that's what! Utilizing my superior tracking skills, I quickly discovered his trail. But it seemed my quarry had caught wind of my pursuit, for the trail led off into the Great Forest!

This knight is not so easily daunted - so I pressed forward through the wood, trying to overtake the fleeing criminal. It was soon after that the thunderstorm struck, and I was forced to seek shelter inside this cave.

Indeed it was, my fellow. The beasts caught me unawares as I slumbered by my fire, and I was forced to retreat deeper into the cave.\n\nBut fate is not entirely cruel, for it was during that headlong retreat that I stumbled upon the very man I sought!

Yes, and what a fight it was! The wretch had only a rusty dirk to defend himself with, but he fought like a caged senche!\n\nI soon defeated him, but before I could retrieve my sword the ogres were upon me again, and I was forced to abandon that too.

Yes, quite true. I've spent my time since then hiding here in the shadows, scavenging what scraps I can just to stay alive.\n\nBut at last, those days are behind me! Once you return my armor to me, I shall easily charge past these brutes to freedom.

I came here on a sacred mission—to slay the notorious bandits known as The Three. 

I ventured into these depths leaving my fellow knights behind with orders to collapse the cave if I did not return.

This cave became my tomb.

Perhaps, but by sealing the cave, my fellow knights succeeded where I did not. The Three starved here in darkness.

But now the cave is reopened and their spirits again threaten the land.

You must put their spirits to rest.
He did? That fobbing cheat! He always does this to me. He promised I could kill the slavers.\n\nWell go ahead then. I won't try to stop you.

Of course! She's smart, our mayor! She knows we can focus our energy through personal items.\n\nLook for my staff at the small bridge nearby. We mounted a defense there. Bought the mayor's husband the time he needed to get the refugees away.

I can teleport you there ... for a small fee.

Forgive me for asking for coin. The reagents for our spells are costly.

Let me know when you're ready, and I'll begin the spell.

Bad luck. Could've just blown by Koeglin, but thought to stop for extra supplies. 

Who would guess the lighthouse was out? Hit a rock—didn't sink me, but hurt the hull.

Now I gotta wait for repairs.
We have to kill it. You have to kill it. \n\nMy sword! In the dream, I left it in the throne room. The Omen is drawn to it. Find the sword and find the Omen.
Follow the river's path once you cross the bridge south of here. The way may not be easy, but if you stay close to the water, you will soon see the valley below, where the villagers take refuge.
Logs have heartwood, makes shields, bows. Look in groves. Mushrooms make potions.\n\nLeather makes armor. Skin beasts, take skins.

Ores for armors and weapons are found in the mountains, or on rocky outcroppings. Mystical metals can be found near ancient ruins, used in enchantment. \n\nMinerals are found on rocky outcroppings, and are used to form the base of powerful concoctions.

Hides can be gathered from the wild creatures of the land, to make armor.

Salves can be made from the viscera your prey.

Petrified bones can be found along water courses and cliff sides. Carve these to make magical enchantments or weapons.

Mystical components can channel magicka through items. They're usually found near rocky outcroppings. So are semi-precious stones, which can be ground up to make inks for scrolls.\n\nAnd, of course, spirits can always be captured to make soul gems.

A cult? What cult? You don't mean …? Oh no! My dad! She said something about him and a sacrifice he had to make …. \n\nThe man said they were going up the hill to the west. Please! You have to go after them!

Akatosh was the first of the Eight Divines. Some refer to him as the Dragon God of Time. He embodies the qualities of endurance, invincibility, and everlasting legitimacy.\n\nHe is, perhaps, the most widely worshiped deity throughout Tamriel.

Kynareth, the Goddess of Air? She rules over the heavens themselves, and her power touches us all. The wind, the air, and the very elements all fall within her domain.\n\nMany turn to Kynareth when in need of good fortune.

Those who travel by land or sea often pray for good weather and safe journeys. Others look to her to bless a child's birth with favorable stars.\n\nShe's the most powerful of the sky spirits, and many benefit from her favor.

I'm astounded you don't know. Julianos is our great god of wisdom and logic. To worship him is to devote yourself to ever-increasing knowledge. \n\nHistory, law, and philosophy are merely a few of the subjects he shepherds.

Indeed it may be. Our temples are more akin to academies than what you see here. We better ourselves and our faith through the knowledge we gain.\n\nThose who fully devote themselves to Julianos are some of the wisest in all of Tamriel.

Dibella is the goddess of beauty. Her cults vary wildly due to the range in which beauty may be expressed and worshiped. One may contain painters and sculptors, while another contains those who choose to explore beauty in a more sensual way.
Perhaps to some outsiders, but we uphold both external and internal beauty. Our wish is to spread this beauty across all of Nirn, so everyone may learn to value both.
Arkay keeps the balance of life and death. He is there when we're born and will be there again when we die.\n\nBecause of this, he is both loved and feared.
Oh! You came back. You … you have to help me! \n\nSome creepy guy was here … and then my mother tied me up, locked the door, and they left! Can you get me out?

Not only death itself, but the cause as well. Arkay may be many things, including famine or plague or natural disasters. He must maintain the balance.\n\nThis also explains his disdain for necromancy. To undo his work is the greatest form of blasphemy.

Zenithar, out of all the Eight, is probably closest to our day-to-day lives.\n\nHe presides over work and commerce, valuing honesty. He believes earnest labor begets peace and prosperity, and he has no interest in the destructiveness of war.

If you've ever felt love or compassion, you've known Mara yourself. She is the mother-goddess of Tamriel who watches over us. \n\nAs her followers, we strive to mimic her benevolence. Our only enemies are those who advocate hatred and intolerance.

Stendarr is the god of mercy. Any who undertake a life of war or adventure should be familiar with him and what he stands for.\n\nMercy is not an act of weakness. Rather, it is an act of strength to rise above our greatest inner turmoils.
Many do. They'll never realize the power that mercy has. They'll never gain the respect and admiration of their peers.\n\nThose who don't believe in mercy must believe in fear.
The blade may have rusted to the point where it is useless in battle, but its magic remains.\n\nDefeating the spirits below with the sword in your possession will bind their souls to its steel.

Quietly, stranger! Kir and I were separated when the sabre cats ambushed us. I can handle them one at a time, but outside these ruins, they attack in pairs.\n\nDoes the blood of giants flow through your veins? Can you force the cats back?

He's right to be concerned. When we were ambushed, I fled.

Rolan hungers for battle more than I do. He's probably somewhere fighting fifty cats at once. Even our sister Jehanna is stronger than I am.

Can you help me out of here?
Yes, of course I am. I'm not a yearling, like my brother Kir.\n\nHave you seen him? He and I were separated by sabre cats.

Ha! They're as nervous as mares, startling over the littlest thing.\n\nTell Father that I'm fine. These ruins have sheltered me for more than a day, and I've fended off several cats myself. Soon, they'll all be gone.
You know me? Have you seen Rolan? Is he still alive?

Father always worries about us. Rolan and Jehanna are very strong. I'm the youngest, but I don't want to be coddled like a newborn foal. I'll be fine.\n\nTell my father that the Herd Mother guides and protects me.

Don't return to this camp - I won't be here. Meet me farther within the ruins.\n\nOur base camp for the final assault on the <<1>> will be on the mountain itself. Look for the door to the east of the spider nests. Good luck.
Don't know. Hear it's been out for a while, though.\n\nCould be the lighthouse keeper's been killed. Don't really care. Just want to get back to sea.
Don't come back down to the docks.\n\nI'll be fighting my way up the mountain at the same time you are. Our plan is to establish a camp just outside the entrance to the Doomcrag. Meet me there.

You are brave, perhaps even a little foolhardy, but I like you.\n\nThough I fear for your safety down there, I will not stand in your way. If you return with the ledger, I will be forever in your debt.

Indeed, but perhaps it would have been better if Sir Hughes had uncovered that truth …. No time for regrets though. \n\nWe will do this properly now. Let Sir Hughes handle it. It is what's best for the Covenant.
Help? I feel cold. I feel ... hungry.\n\nBy the Divines! Please. I'm so hungry. You've got to get away.

Oh yes. Lived here all our lives. Our daughter Ingride took over the farm a few years ago. Between you and me, she does a better job.\n\nThen our granddaughter Rozenn lives here, and our other grandchildren Phinis and Marlene are visiting.

Yes, of course. I would gladly give my ledger over, but unfortunately, it is belowdecks.

This is why I have asked the constable to assist us in eliminating these Dunmer dogs, but he has refused.

I'm afraid we are at a stalemate in this respect.

The sergeant on duty won't let me through. Please take me there. Ask him to let me pass.\n\nMy beloved served honorably at Eagle's Gate, but she died during an assault. I want to remember her where she served.
His Excellency the Count wants to talk to you about your performance. You know, killing.\n\nHe awaits you on the viewing dais above the main arena.

I've never seen Arnoit Sidrey or his wife, but you're not the first to speak of him. It's an old tale. Him finding travelers, begging them to help.\n\nYou know what? No one even remembers his wife's name. She supposedly died here, in Ranser's war.
Good guess. Take this Midnight Union sigil with you. The guards will see it and let you pass unharmed.

An armed escort is customary in Alik'r. We mean no insult, and certainly no threat. They say we bring an army. An army would be hundreds. This is merely one regiment. \n\nIf you might convince the Knights to listen to reason, I would be obliged.

The prisoners have already been released. You may find they've been roughed up a bit. We are … enthusiastic.\n\nThere's one rather stubborn fellow who refuses to go until he's spoken to you. He insists on knowing if you're safe.
The General is very busy with the business of commanding his troops. I cannot trouble him with random visitors. \n\nMove along now, stranger.
You don't. The only way I would admit you is if I receive orders from the General himself.

Dame Falhut? By Ruptga's beard! I knew that wench was capable of dark deeds the moment I laid eyes on her!\n\nShe will pay for her crimes. I only pray there aren't more traitors involved in this conspiracy.
I came out here to be alone. Rivenspire is falling to pieces and I want no part of it.\n\nIf I were you, I'd find a hole to climb in and I wouldn't come out until all this passes.
Oh, he's a tough one, all right. Chews through challengers like a scythe through wheat. \n\nYou know, we're both from the same stronghold? He wasn't always so invincible.

He almost never gets hit, is what. I think it must be his armor. He's never brought it to me for repairs, not once.\n\nThe only time I've ever seen him take a blow is from behind. He's real careful about protecting his back.
Patience is the key, runtling.\n\nJust wait. He'll charge you. If you get out of his way, he'll throw himself off when he misses. That's when you attack: while he's regaining his footing.
It's a pity, but I can't trust anyone under his sway. They must die.\n\nGo to the mews and ensure they do not escape alive. I will have <<1>> meet you there.

The Fervor. They suffer bloodthirst, like the miners who converted this mine into an unspeakable arena.\n\nThe minions of the Midnight Union were drawn by the senseless slaughter in the miner's arena. Then they moved in and made it their own.

Yes. They know nothing but blood now. Their lust for it blinds them.\n\nI still can't believe my bad luck. My husband is a Spirit Warden, so we escaped the Fervor's madness. Now he's about to become its victim. You must do something!
This is just the beginning. After the fighting breaks out here, you can just kiss the Covenant goodbye.\n\nWe'll be at war with Alik'r within a month.
Are you kidding me? Bretons and Redguards have never gotten along. \n\nThey're just not like us. It is what it is.
Hammerdeath? It used to be the foremost gladiatorial arena in High Rock. The Midnight Union ran the gambling, taking a cut off the top.\n\nThen their leader, Count Hosni, changed the rules.

Instead of fighting to yield or first blood, all combats now go to the death. The legitimate fighters avoid the place now, and only scum compete. \n\nAnd the audience is even worse. Bloodthirsty swine.

Nor will I ever be, after they took this place from me and my brothers. But I can't leave it. Not Hammerdeath. I've put too much into her to leave her behind.\n\nThat and my love for the arena, the blood and death …. I won't ever leave this place.

Dead. Both of them. By the venom of the Spider Queen, one of Hammerdeath's prized champions.\n\nAs much as I'd like to tear that spider limb from limb, theirs was a glorious death after a great battle. I can only hope for that when my time comes.
It's the blacksmith skills. The Midnight Union isn't fond of anything besides their penchant for blood. Hard labor isn't one of their priorities.

I'm not much in the ways of giving advice. I'm merely an announcer. There are those who are familiar with the champions that still remain here at Hammerdeath. <<1>> for one. You can find her up by the refreshments.
For a small fee, I can teleport you to the Mages Guild Hall in Wayrest. Just let me know.
I was … hoping you might volunteer. That would help … avoid a scene. \n\nFalhut's home is north of the inn. If you'll go there first, I'll get some of my men and come as back up.

I sent a messenger to Alcaire Castle asking for Sir Hughes to explain the situation, but I haven't heard back. I suspect he may be preoccupied with whatever chaos transpires at the castle.\n\nIf only Sir Croix would just wait.

If you ask me, it's because Sir Croix is a bloodthirsty brute. He's never believed in the Covenant.\n\nCroix himself simply maintains that we should follow Sir Hughes's orders whether they make sense or not.
You're not here to … oh, merciful Stendarr. Lakana!
That would be best. His complaints try my patience.\n\nHe's at the rear of the dais.
Sure. She's one of the hillmen. They're a big folk: taller than you and me by a long shot.\n\nSome say the hillmen are the great-great-great grandchildren of giants. I'm not sure if I believe that.

We were sent to Shornhelm to assist House Tamrith against House Montclair. House Montclair must have known we were on the way. \n\nThey set up the perfect trap for us. They blocked our advance while using a pincer maneuver to cut off our retreat.
Survive? I'm not sure that we did. I was able to rally a small force and punch a hole in their line to get back to Oldgate. Only a handful of my troops made it back.
Yes, I can see that. \n\nI underestimated you. Glad I wasn't betting, 'cause I'd have bet against you on the last two bouts. And I'd have lost.
Yes, I can see that. \n\nI underestimated you. Glad I wasn't betting, 'cause I'd have bet against you on the last two bouts. And I'd have lost.
Invisible Step

The north arena is her playground. She's been alerted, so just enter it, and she'll come out to play.\n\nRemember to stay in the middle of the arena. You want to be where the spectators can see all the action.

Well, if you had a really big boot, you could crush her under its heel. Ha ha …!\n\nAll right, not funny. I suppose you could talk to <<1>>. He said he thought he could take out Her Creepiness, if he had to. Maybe he's got a secret plan.
Invisible Step
This is his arena. Just step into the ring, and he'll do you the honor to come out and dance.
You know, I'll tell you, because I've come to think you deserve it. \n\nGo talk to <<1>>. That surly old Orc is mean as a viper, and he's got a grudge against our Scourge. I wager he'll help you.

<This Ayleid gem pulses with the light of many trapped souls. They were taken from soldiers who died recently in the Shrouded Pass.>\n\n<A layer of dust covers the altar, but the gem is spotlessly clean. Obviously, it was placed here very recently.>
<This man has deep knife wounds on his back and sides. A viscous green ichor cakes the edges of the wounds.>
<The man's valuables have been taken, but a scrap of parchment remains. It appears to be a note.>
Oh. That's … that's a pity. Well, now this is a mess.

I'm taking a chance here. Sometimes I hear strange things. Like what's on that note: black roses with thorns. \n\nI've heard whispers of dark nature magic. That's just the kind of thing Roy—your dead man—would be interested in.

I don't know. I told Roy what I heard. Then things would happen. \n\nTry Captain Aresin. He and Roy talked a lot. The Captain plants himself at the base of the castle stairs. Remember, the base of the stairs, not the top.
Look, I don't want any trouble. That's a phrase used by the King's intelligence network. It means someone's going to get killed. \n\nI don't want to know anything more. Just leave me out of this.
I said leave me alone!\n\nTake your questions and go. I'm not involved in this. This sounds like something that Roy would want to know about.
Well, not to me. Talk to someone official, like <<1>>. He's over at the bottom of the castle steps. \n\nI don't know what else is on that list, but this feels like treacherous business.
I'm afraid those aren't for sale.\n\nThe crescent moon is the heraldry of the Casimir family, the rulers of Daggerfall.

If a crime has been committed, talk to Captain Aresin. It's his job to keep the city safe, so he's as good a choice as any.  \n\nHe's usually by the great stairs behind the Mages Guild. He likes to keep an eye on the approach to the castle.
Roy? Where is he? Why did he send a stranger in his place?
Dead? Mara's Hands! Let me look at that note. It's our code, all right. Someone who uses dark nature magic is planning to assassinate King Casimir! \n\nBut who's behind this? I need to know more.
The rest of our soldiers went ahead to establish a camp at the <<1>>. I'll hobble my way there while you take care of the signal.\n\nMeet me there. May Kynareth exalt you over your enemies.

Just don't try to play me for a fool. But with Roy dead, I don't seem to have much of a choice.\n\nTalk to Grenna gra-Kush at the Rosy Lion Inn. If Roy was onto something, she'll know what to do. Betray us and … well, she'll still know what to do.
And? Why are we talking?

Eager. Reminds me of Roy. Go upstairs. Find Leveque and rattle his teeth, but don't kill him. We may need him later. \n\nJust don't mention me. I'm not an agent of the crown. I'm just an Orc enjoying her ale.
By Malacath! Roy stepped on a nest of snakes this time. One of the vipers is upstairs.\n\nHe might know something. I'd confront him, but he knows me. Maybe a stranger like you can get him to talk.
I'm from Wayrest. I'm visiting for my cousin's wedding, if it's important. And you?
What? Ridiculous.\n\nSomeone! Anyone! There's a ruffian threatening me!

Agreed. I'll tell you everything I know. Martine Lerineaux hired me. He lives next door to the inn. In the large manor house. \n\nI'm a mason, you see. Martine wanted me to make him a map of the tunnels beneath Daggerfall.
The secret ones that lead to the castle. But I don't know what he's planning. I swear! \n\nI just needed the gold. I've got my own troubles back in Wayrest.
I thought I heard some noise upstairs. But you don't look any worse for the wear. Did you let that snake Leveque live?
Roy's contact in the city guard was Captain Aresin. You can find him on the approach to the castle.\n\nBe careful. I imagine that whoever killed Roy won't want you to pass along this information.

"Martine,\n\n"Your ships are more than adequate to transport our agents. All you need to do is deliver the cargo. Once night falls, we'll emerge from the crates and use Leveque's maps to get close to King Casimir."

"Angof will be pleased with the chaos caused by Casimir's death! The kingdom's leaderless ranks will offer the Bloodthorn little resistance. Rest assured that you will be compensated very well for your loyalty to the Bloodthorn's cause."

"See that those crates are not disturbed. The agents inside must stay hidden until the time is right. If they are discovered, I will perform the deed myself and then come back for you. Do not fail us.\n\n— Verrik"

It doesn't make any sense, does it? It's like a cow building a house out of steak.\n\nI asked Verandis, and he said something about killing wolves, the size of deer herds, and starvation. That sounded like a bunch of Altmer nonsense to me.
You've earned my trust. Take this ward with my blessing.
Here, take the ward. We're counting on you, <<1>>.

The assassins are in my port? Find these snakes and kill them, but do it quietly. I don't want to start a panic.\n\nI'll alert the guards. If any of these conspirators get past you, we'll cut them down.
Merciful Ruptga, my prayers are answered! Help me!\n\nPlease, get me out before that spider monstrosity comes back! I've been trapped in this cocoon for days!

I overheard the cultists talking. They have a prisoner who's a threat to the werewolf leader, Faolchu. They plan to execute her.\n\nIf she really is a threat, then it seems crucial that we rescue her.

The forest is enraged. Filled with hatred. We tried to calm it as we always have before, but our magic falters.\n\nNever have the elemental spirits refused to answer our calls. The grass, the trees, the very earth itself—they're dying.
For now, our purpose is to defend the villagers from these creatures. I can construct a simple ward to protect the mill, but we are far from the Wyrd Tree. I shall require a focus.
Fantastic!\n\nI have to put this on display. Wait here a moment.
Splendid. Cut me loose. We'll kill these Bloodthorn dogs and then go after Faolchu and his werewolves.
Sebastien? We don't have time for … oh, very well. We'll talk to the Duke. \n\nLet's go, then. No time to waste.

Ranser, the former king of <<1>>, once marched against <<2>>. Even though he's dead and <<3>> is under my control, it's in my best interest to keep an eye on the situation there.\n\nAn unseen eye notices things meant to be hidden.
Did he say I stole his damn hog again? I didn't. Not this time, not last time, not ever! Do you see a pig on a spit in here? \n\nMost likely Glutton broke out and started rooting in the alleys again.

Every time the pig escapes, Wickton accuses me of thievery. Every time! What a nuisance.\n\nLook, check the alleys in the northeast section of the city. The sooner that pig's found, the sooner Wickton will shut up and leave me in peace.
<The pig squints up at you before returning to its feast. It devours the tender roots with surprising gusto.>
<This grain sack bears the mark of a Daggerfall merchant. Clearly, the Red Rooks stole it.>

I'm no expert, but Hircine is the Daedric Prince of manbeasts. The amulet bears the Call of Hircine. \n\nWerewolves can't resist its call—it forces them to reveal their true nature. Pretty useful, right?
What of it? Don't you have some werewolves to go find?

Dead? Rugged fellow, had a dog? That's Roy. Well, that was Roy. I'm sorry he's dead, but I'm not surprised. \n\nIf you figure out what Roy knew and who killed him, I'm sure someone will reward you. It's also a good way to get yourself killed.

Fair enough. All right, here's the dark truth. I'm related to Faolchu. He's my ancestor. Every day, my family and I live with the shame of the horrors he inflicted on the world. And now he's back.\n\nSo I hunt werewolves—and I kill them.

In taking her life, I lost my own. Now I understand why I am able to speak and think ... and dream.\n\nImmortality's price is too high for me. I don't want to think or live this way. I beseech you to help me!
I know that it's not a very large cave  Actually, I'm not entirely sure how I know that.\n\nStill, you haven't been gone very long. Could there be someplace within it you missed?
I'll be waiting for you right here.\n\nOf course, you knew that already. I can't move. I'm a tree.

Ah, right. That's not what I expected to hear. We did capture a werewolf at Camlorn. For a little while, anyway. My battlemage, Lexi, did it. She should be able to help you.\n\nLexi! Front and center, if you please!

Come though. This is an historic day. We have strengthened the seals on the Impervious Vault. Your friends and many others have gathered to witness the return of the Ansei Wards to their rightful place.\n\nTake them. The honor is yours.
The Wyrd Tree sustains us. From its roots, we draw strength. From its leaves, we find comfort.\n\nIts roots stretch through all of Nirn and thus its power touches everything.
And my thanks to you. But there's someone else who'd like to thank you. \n\nHis Majesty wants to speak to you. Go on.
It was a monster! It tore out Guillaume's throat and disappeared into the river. It was hideous!
I'll create a link between the three of us. We'll be able to see into the werewolf's past. And, hopefully, into Faolchu's past as well. The connection between offspring and sire is strong.

My sister was always headstrong. She chose <<1>>, and she wouldn't take no for an answer. They were on a state visit when we met the king and the duke.\n\nMy wedding was first, followed shortly by hers. Now Lakana is dead, and the Covenant is shaken.

Faolchu died a long, long time ago. He was summoned back from the dead. I want to find out who to blame for that. You can read the history of a werewolf's sire from the blood of his offspring. \n\nThat's why we need to capture a werewolf.

My husband and I must travel to Alik'r to speak to <<1>>, my father. We will return my sister to her birthplace: Sentinel.\n\nWe'll keep the Daggerfall Covenant strong. Lakana wouldn't want her death to imperil all we've worked for.
You saw what I saw. In order to stop Faolchu for good, we need to put an end to Angof. A tall order, but it's not impossible. \n\nWait … the werewolf apparently has something to say.
Faolchu has been ahead of me every step of the way. This failure falls on my head. But we can resolve this here and now. \n\nI need to die and you need to take my blood.
This poison will kill me quickly without contaminating my blood. Swear to me you'll finish what we started. Save the Duke and restore my family's honor.\n\nAnd may the Eight watch over you.
Damn it! I hope your noble attitude doesn't get everyone else killed!\n\nAll right. I guess I'll stay alive long enough to see this through. Let's go before it's too late. I'll meet you in Aldcroft.

We're wasting time! I need to die so you can take my blood. \n\nIf administered in time, the blood of the master can cure his spawn. You know I'm Faolchu's descendent. If the Duke drinks my blood, he'll be cured of the curse.
Is this blood? You want me to drink this? Oh, very well.\n\nAh! The pain fades … and the madness clears! I can see now how close I was to losing all control. How shameful.

She went out to bring the townsfolk here for safety, but I'm not prepared to receive and protect that many people. Could you perhaps retrieve some food and materials for barricades?\n\nWhile you do that, I'll see if I can't find the Captain.
Leon? I loved him once. Perhaps I still do.\n\nBut there's the matter of Molag Bal to deal with first. Leon made a deal with the Daedric Prince. Despite your actions, that deal remains in place.

He wasn't praying to Stendarr. At least it wasn't like any Stendarr prayer I ever heard. \n\nAnd I heard another voice in the house. It was alien, Captain. Evil. I don't mind admitting that what I heard has me more than a little frightened.

For the moment. I haven't forgotten how to swing a sword and the inn's walls are stout.\n\nApothecary Muriel's helping the wounded, but she needs more hawthorn berries. She can't make more healing poultices without them.

My shade was only one aspect of the curse. There are also the innocent spirits of Westtry and the angry spirits of the invaders.\n\nUse my sword to make the town safe for mortals or use this gem to set the innocent spirits free. The choice is yours.
Yes, the needs of the living outweigh the needs of the dead. Go, then. Subdue the angry wraiths and make Westtry safe. \n\nWhen you're done, return to Leon.

This gem represents Westtry's torment. You'd use it to save us, even if Westtry remains a danger to the living? That such mercy still exists makes my heart glad. Take the gem and free the innocent spirits. \n\nWhen the deed is done, return to Leon.

This picture... it's of my husband and I. He fought alongside Rosalind, and is now one of these wraiths. My lucky hammer, too, and... this sword. It was the pinnacle of my craft, and the last thing I made before dying.\n\nI believe you now.
Very good. I'll return to Aldcroft.\n\nMeet me there after you rescue this mysterious woman.
With the note? I don't know. That's just what Roy did. He would find out things. \n\nDaggerfall has many eyes and ears. After all, information is cheaper than war.

I sell the best fruits and vegetables in Daggerfall. Lots of people come by. I talk and I listen. Then I talk to my friends, like Roy.\n\nAs for other people? Maybe they should decide what they're going to do, now that they know so much.
Damned persistent, aren't you? Roy's a friend. I trust him.\n\nPeople I don't know, I don't trust. And I don't know you.
Roy was a good man. Loyal to Daggerfall. People trusted him. Even that old dog loved him.

I guess. I liked Roy. He watched out for the merchants around here. And, in exchange, we helped Roy.\n\nI listened and let Roy know what people were saying. If we ever told him something important, Roy made sure the right people were informed.

Martine the merchant? We need to know everything! Get inside Lerineaux's manor. Look for anything that can shed light on what they're planning.\n\nI'll stay here and keep an eye on Leveque, so take anything you find straight to Captain Aresin.
By Mara, you always did have good timing. Here, let me prepare some poultices for you. \n\nIf you can apply these to any wounded guards, they should be able to get back into the fight.
I... I'm sure I don't know what you're talking about. Please, this is not the time. I need to find Rosalind! I need to find my wife!

Rosalind is dead, like all of us. The warriors of our town became the wraiths that you see here, and Captain Rosalind was first among them.\n\nIf Leon is looking for her, he may not know he's dead. Take him this sword. It was for Rosalind.
<<1>> said he'd pay good silver for them!\n\nUnfortunately, I don't have any eggs, and I've driven the harpies mad, stirring up their nests like this.

It's a monster, I tell you! A monster! Prowls the alleys. Shreds its victims with claws and fangs. It'll kill anyone that crosses its path!\n\nThere's a dead man in the south alley, but he's no beggar. He's one of those Bloodthorn cultists.

The beast prowls along the river's edge and hunts in the alleys. It doesn't eat what it kills. It just slaughters and leaves the corpses for the rats. \n\nIt's the curse of Camlorn! I want no part of this evil.
With you? Yes, of course. But, please, keep your voice down.\n\nNo need to alarm anyone unnecessarily.
Fight a werewolf? Never had the opportunity and I hope it stays that way.\n\nA werewolf's bite carries the creature's curse. It can turn you into one of them. Or so I've heard it said.

I'd say it were a lot of superstitious nonsense, except the rumors keep coming. They say that werewolves have overrun Camlorn, north of here.\n\nWith the way the Lion Guard has been acting, there's certainly something going on up that way.
I'll tell you whatever I know.

The watch found Old Gianne last night. The night before, it was Ragged Ron.\n\nWhen one of us dies, they blame the cold or the plague, but Gianne and Ron were cut up something horrible. Now they say it's a wolf.

We're everywhere. We're easy prey. Some folks just don't like us. Take your pick.\n\nThis killer isn't stopping. It's brutal. Sooner or later, it's going to start killing a better class of citizen. Then the watch will take action.
You're a life saver!
I did not believe ….\n\nI prayed and prayed, but felt nothing. I was convinced the gods had deserted me, but you … you are their sign to me.

Ah, the focus objects! These will do very nicely. Let me just, uhh … hmm. I don't think that was supposed to come off.\n\nWell, these swords are pretty beat up. I'm sure we'll still have plenty of material for the ritual, though.
Of course. We'll be using the amalgamated essence of the past, focused with these ancient weapons, to open a sort of window into history. \n\nFollow me.
Oh, really? Do you know how much gold I get for a crate of harpy eggs?

Yes. We should've stayed in Camlorn. At least my sister would still be with me. We thought we'd go to Aldcroft, but ran into trouble here in the fens before we got there.\n\nBloodthorn Cultists swarmed in and grabbed all the women and took them away.

The grub-sniffer will instinctively make a threating display when it smells the musk, to avoid being eaten by the beetle it smells.\n\nAll you have to do is lead him around the camp. Walk by the workers. The lizard will show you who is guilty.

Of course! Did you know lizards smell with their tongues? They are quite adept at detecting even the faintest trace of a scent.\n\nI have a fine tracking lizard, if you're interested in purchasing one. I'll even train him to the scent of your choice!

My daughter is lost to her grief. How can she send you here, to a haunt of vile cultists, to retrieve a pipe? Sheer folly. \n\nShe should have something of real value, something that will allow her to move on.
Then go back to your Lady and pray for salvation. We will defend Shornhelm from all threats, whether they come from Lord Montclair or from its own.\n\nWe have no more to say to each other.
The cystals are powering this magic globe. If you destroy them, it should dissolve the damned thing.\n\nThen we have to get out of here. It won't be long before she returns!
May the essence of Aetherius protect us all.\n\nNow, please, stand back. I must perform the ritual of warding.
Stop talking nonsense! The raiders are lying in wait just outside of our town, we need to prepare our defenses!\n\nMe? A spirit? What folly!
Our village was attacked by Nord raiders. I prayed to Stendarr for aid, but my wife, the captain of the guard, was more practical. She went to rally the town's defenses.
No, not even a whisper. But I did hear the shouts of the Nords and the cries of my people. I feared for my dear Rosalind.\n\nAnd then I made a terrible mistake.

I offered my soul to anyone who would preserve us. Molag Bal accepted. \n\nHe let the Nords kill us all. Then he preserved the town by binding our spirits here. We relive our final moments over and over, experiencing our slaughter for all eternity.
Delicious. Thank you.
Ask. I will answer what I can. \n\nProbably.
Mother Murk opposes the wyresses. She's your enemy, not mine.\n\nI can see how her darkness twists and harms the world around her, though. Such terrible things she does.

This talisman contains the blood of my ancestors. It's the essence of all the stablemasters before me.\n\nIn times of great trouble, we've used it to summon those ancestors back to us, so they can fight to defend our home.
The Wyrd Tree, the spirit that gives life to this land. My sisters and I are Beldama Wyrd. We serve the Wyrd Tree.\n\nWe came here to discover why anger infests this part of the forest.
No, and that worries me.\n\nThe forest no longer speaks to us. We sensed that something was wrong and that's why we came here. But beyond that, we are at a loss as to how to make things right.
Let this torchbug fly where it will. Let it guide you to the essence of Aetherius. It will find the soil that is most pure and draw out what I need for my focus.

We are the witches of the Wyrd. We serve the Wyrd Tree and the forest is our home. If this was Breton against Breton, we would not get involved. \n\nBut something unnatural caused this. The forest has been wounded and that concerns the Beldama Wyrd.
We stand apart, but we aren't heartless. No one deserves to die for something they haven't done.
For years, I've been hiding gold under a tree southwest of the lighthouse. Dig it up and give it to my daughter. \n\nThen she needs to go to my brother in Crosswych. There she can start anew.
I am called by many names. Mire-Witch. Old Bog Crone. The Swamp-Seer. \n\nYou may simply call me Sibellec.

No, I come from the Reach. Just like Mother Murk. And Angof. \n\nNot everyone who comes from the Reach seeks to do evil. The wyrd are hospitable, so I reside with them. Yet I don't begrudge Mother Murk her wickedness. It was her path to choose.

Mother Murk uses dark magic. She will drain your life to restore her own vitality. \n\nThe charm, once empowered, will reflect her magic back upon her. But you must use it at the correct time or it won't be of much help.

The spell worked better than I anticipated. We didn't just create a window into the past—we opened a door. The very air ripples with temporal disturbance. \n\nSomewhere nearby, a door into history stands open. All we need to do is step through it.

Someone brave and rash enough has to actually step through the door we opened. \n\nI'm too valuable to get lost in the past. And Bhagrun would probably change history with all his usual bumbling about. Ask Grahla what she thinks we should do.
They were supposed to cast a simple divination spell, nothing more. \n\nSarvith wasn't supposed to open any doorways.
Examine the ripples. See if there really is a doorway of some kind out there.\n\nAnd keep an eye out for anything else out of the ordinary. Who knows what they may have pulled out of the past.
I don't like this. Time magic shouldn't be meddled with. \n\nBut what's done is done. Maybe one of those ripples has the answers we seek.
That would help a lot. Bring them to Muriel at her shop as soon as you can. \n\nAnd Captain? Be careful out there.

That's fine. Giant's toes could make a bigger gap in the seal, but they're probably hard to find here anyways.\n\nThese should do the trick … I think. Hmm. Worm's Head on top of the Flame Stalk or Flame Stalk inside the Worm's Head?

Sure. I just need a minute to think about exactly how to word this … hmm. 

Gada, Gada, Tobr'a … Tobr'a Tobr'a Gada …?

Go on. I'll be right up.

Oh. Absolutely. It's only one person going in anyways. Without the giant's toes, I can only open the seals so far.\n\nOf course, Fahara'jad thinks that one person should be you. He wants to talk to you first though. Go on up.

The struggle between wyrd and hag is as old as the swamp itself. Both sides have sought my help, but this is not my battle.\n\nYou, however, have picked a side. I help you and indirectly become involved. Just as it should be.

Your hope is contagious, wayfarer. I am pleased that your road has led you here. General Thoda is not a man of faith, but even he agrees your coming seems more than a coincidence. \n\nIf only one of us can enter the vault, I think it should be you.

I cannot adequately express my gratitude. You must be careful, though. Azah believes the Withered Hand is far more powerful than we realized—Uwafa and Alasan in particular. \n\nIf you see either of them, I suggest you exercise extreme caution.
What's that? You mean you haven't heard of the great <<1>>?\n\nYou don't know about my valiant campaign against the harpies of Shrieking Scar? Those beasts are a menace to Daggerfall!
Of course. Be off, then!

Well, I wouldn't ask too much of an untested fighter such as yourself, but a few of my less experienced fighters have been away from camp for some time. They might be in trouble.\n\nHere are their names. If you're interested, you can track them down.
Thank the Divines! I've been trapped here for two days!
Good. Now craft the ring.
Did that blow to your head rattle your senses? \n\nWe're on the verge of turning the tide and we'll launch the strike against Faolchu's headquarters soon. Come, my love. We have work to do.
