The Alessian orders, of course. They're crucial. We captured the messenger but not before he handed the orders off. We need to search enemy soldiers until we can retrieve them. We can't have the Alessians surprise us when we're this close to victory.

Excellent. You're a credit to the Direnni Guard.\n\nNow we can prepare a proper counterattack to the upcoming Alessian assault. They won't know what hit them! You should show these to the Ayleid King. He just arrived and is eager to get involved.

What? Nonsense! Alana can handle it. If these orders are any indication, I need you to lead our defenses.\n\nBut speak to Alana before she goes, if you like. Just make it quick. And don't forget to talk to the King.
I appreciate your concern, my love, but orders are orders. If either of us fails, this entire battle could be lost.\n\nBut have no fear. I'll make sure we never have to worry about Faolchu again.
Later, my love. I'll tell you all about it after the battle. No need to distract you right now. It's nothing but good news, though, I promise.\n\nI love you, you know. Now go.
Yes, Captain. \n\nThey dragged Alana up the path behind me. Good luck. We'll get Faolchu for you.
Very well, Captain. I'll send one of our soldiers with you. She'll meet you inside.

You sent them to be slaughtered! I was wrong. Faolchu isn't an ordinary man. I drove my sword right into his heart and he didn't even feel it. Our weapons won't be able to stop him.\n\nThe soldiers won't stand a chance.
Someone needs to get this information back to our camp. If Faolchu eludes you, our remaining forces need to know how to kill him.\n\nGo, my love. Go make history.
Why, yes, of course. Are you sure you're all right? \n\nIt doesn't matter. What happened?
Fire! Can it really be that simple? \n\nAlana's said that all along, but now we know for certain. Now we can take the fight to Faolchu. And we can win.

Where else would she be? She's the one who approved your mission. Don't you remember? \n\nI'm sure it'll all come back to you. Time travel can be very stressful. Anyway, Alana's in camp. Go tell her what you learned.

What's wrong with you? Why are you looking at me like that? You know I'm the descendant of the spirit who appeared before you. \n\nGet your head on straight and tell me how Faolchu was originally defeated.

This was Farmin's amulet. I know it well. It is as I feared: he fell to the undead horde.\n\nThe Withered Hand is raising an army of dead here. Without the Ash'abah to stop them, this unholy ground would pose a threat to Alik'r.
Lead the way.
The ancient armor, it drew you into the past. \n\nBut we knew it was temporary. You belong here, my friend.
Fire! Of course! That makes all kinds of sense.\n\nQuickly, report your findings to Grahla. She needs to hear what you learned.
According to the legends, when the Nameless Soldier killed Faolchu the armor shattered. The Nameless Soldier died. I was afraid history would repeat itself.
Rub the talisman to summon an ancestor to aid you. He can remain on this plane of existence for only a brief time.\n\nUse it sparingly.
Very good. Now craft me the ring.
Very good. Now, use all your skill to craft that ring. \n\nAnd whatever you do, do not imbue your soul into it. If I had a copper for every apprentice that's done that …
To control our ancient kings, just as they try to control us!\n\nWe were at peace, stranger, silent in watchful slumber. Then the screaming began. Not just in our minds, but in our souls.
No, not us. At least not at first. They were loud, insistent voices. Crying in our minds. Screaming. Submit! Submit! They broke our will and shattered our defenses. \n\nThey want us to join them.
He was a mighty ruler of ancient Camlorn. His powerful blade of skyfallen iron forged a mighty dynasty. \n\nIn war and peace, he ruled by the sword.
He was a ruler of great wealth and renown. He brought trade and prosperity to High Rock. \n\nThe Prince's power was in his vast reserves of gold, the balm that soothes all tempers.
My lord was a hunter. He stalked dangerous game from Skyrim to Valenwood. No beast could elude him, no target could evade his arrow.\n\nIt took many assassins to lay him low.
She was our beloved ruler, a queen with martial skills and unsurpassed beauty. \n\nHer shield, the Green Aegis, protected her in battle. It was the symbol of our undying loyalty to her.
We knew you could defeat the Bloodthorn cultists! And now, the time has come.\n\nPlease remain and bear witness.
Your confidence is inspiring. Thanks for that.\n\nNow prepare yourself. The vine's protectors will be on us as soon as I cast my spell.

Take this flask of funerary oils. Use it on the undead and dispatch them while they're burning. By using fire, we can guarantee they will never be raised again.\n\nReturn to me after you've destroyed them.
The foulest criminals are executed and disposed of here.\n\nFor many generations, it's been the duty of the Ash'abah to maintain the Tear's defenses. We protect unconsecrated bodies from necromancy.
I agree. They've been imprisoned for much too long.\n\nBeldama! Sisters! Focus your power on the stranger! It's time to break Angof's hold on the guardians.

Let me see … the Lady goes before the Warrior and after the Steed. The Shadow chases "closely behind" the Steed, which means it immediately follows. \n\nThere is only one order where all that can be true: Steed, Shadow, Lady, Warrior.

They came disguised as pilgrims. Their chants were unfamiliar. Some thought it was because they were from a foreign temple.\n\nWhen the dead swarmed out of the necropolis, the priests realized the betrayal, but they died before they could stop it.
I wish I had your confidence. I mean, I know what to do, and now you're here, right?\n\nOh, what am I so worried about? Consider those damn vines destroyed!
Then keep me safe while I destroy this damned thing!
You know, when you say it like that I almost believe it. Let's do this thing!
Good. Now for our battle plan. \n\nWe need to take and hold the city courtyard, just inside the main gate. And we could use your help.

Well, if you haven't noticed, we're under attack. By werewolves. Giant, stinking, dishonorable werewolves. Faolchu's werewolves, to be specific.\n\nAnd I have too many injured to get them out of here safely. Until the camp is cleared, we're trapped.

This amulet will summon The Guardians, ancient elemental spirits. You are now attuned to them. \n\nBefore you call them, however, you must prepare the ritual site. Capture a Lurcher, take it to the sacred site and destroy it to cleanse the ritual area.

I was with Wizard Benele at the nearby Merovec's Folly, looking for an important relic. \n\nWhen the undead attacked us, we were forced to retreat. But the mage swore she was close to finding something. She did some magic thing and vanished.
Once we've cleared a path into the courtyard, we need the inner gate locked to keep more wolves from coming through. \n\nThe lock is in the northwest tower.
Let's go. Cut your way through the wolves to that tower, and lock that inner gate.

She said that a nearby crypt contained a relic we needed to defeat Angof. I would have remained by her side, but she just disappeared!\n\nI told Commander Ales what happened and he said I should find you and let you know.

A patroller sent you? Then listen carefully, because I always have a plan.\n\nThe Red Rooks use trained wolves to guard their camp. Increases their confidence, but also makes them careless. We can exploit that to save the hostages.

I need someone who can get in quietly, grab some wolf's woe, and take it to the hostages. With that plant, the hostages can walk out without attracting the attention of the wolves.\n\nThe hostages are locked in a house, so you also need to find a key.
I think you should finish the task <<1>> gave you before you start another patrol.
Before I call the battlemage out to capture a werewolf with you, you should finish the patrol <<1>> asked you to complete.
Commander Ales? A good man and a good soldier.\n\nBut how did you find me?

I did? I knew I left my journal somewhere.\n\nBut I haven't told you the most exciting news! I found the Midnight Talisman. With it, we can punch a hole in Angof's barrier at Cath Bedraud. We just need to recharge the beautiful little relic.

Do you like the name? I thought it up myself. Sounds simply ominous, doesn't it? Anyhow, it's a Daedric relic used to manipulate Oblivion portals. If you know how, you can use the talisman to get past arcane barriers.\n\nAnd I know how.

No, I'm the queen of the Nords. Of course I'm from Camlorn! Did my brother Guy send you?\n\nI gave the cultists a hard time, so they tied me up. They took the other women away, though. I think they traded them to the bog hags.
We can't hold the courtyard unless someone locks the inner gate. That'll keep werewolf reinforcements from reaching us. \n\nI need you to get into the northwest tower and lock that gate.

Well, don't get bitten. Not that I care, mind you, but Faolchu doesn't need anymore of our soldiers turning into his werewolves.\n\nSecure the camp and then I can get these wounded soldiers to some healers.
I'll do my best to answer, friend. It's our good luck you happened by when you did.

The wyresses are witches of a sort, devoted to nature and the Wyrd Tree. They helped us after the attack and said we could stay at their camp until we were ready to move on. \n\nIt's nearby, to the southeast. What remains of my group is there now.
The Lion Guard? They can't even defend Camlorn!\n\nThat must sound bitter. Well, you're talking to someone who lost everything. We had nice homes, shops, comfortable lives. Now look at us!
You must act with the honors, of course. Replace the relics on their respective altars.
Here. I hope you have better luck this time.

Open your recipe notebook to the research page. It's a separate tab at the bottom of the book. You'll need to unravel the mystical bindings on the rune. Just place it right there on the page, and follow the instructions there.\n\nThen enjoy the sizzle!
Sack, there at the stall. Scroll not important. Just ingredients. Directions. \n\nResearch and inspiration. Master the craft.
Didn't think you'd make it. Hhmph. Well done. \n\nMastered recipes. Refined lumber. Now: become an apprentice.
Make a shield. Buy pitch from apprentice. Elodie.\n\nGo to crafting bench. Open yer crafting journal. Find the recipe. Follow instructions. Come back and show me.
Well done. Remember, you never learn anything by studying your own work. You only learn by studying the work of others.\n\nI think you're ready to master your first recipe.

On the table there in the corner. The scroll itself is unimportant. It's just a list of ingredients and steps. \n\nIt's the knowledge that you gained through your research, combined with the recipe, that allows you to fully master a rune.
And all without rending your very soul from your body! Well done novice! Very well done.\n\nYou've made some things, learned some things … I say you're almost an apprentice.

Let's have you … make me a rune. Buy some sandstone from Timmon. Then head to the recipe table. Use the sandstone and gems to create the rune you just learned about.\n\nThen come show me your work. Almost-apprentice!
Hmmph. Don't learn by repeating. Learn from others. Look at work.  Learn the techniques. Learn the craft.\n\nInspiration, artistry, carving, craft. Pull apart the shield, novice.
Open yer recipe book. Go to Research. Tab at the bottom. Drop the shield in. Pull it apart.\n\nPry the rim off, note the rivets. Learn.

The Bloodthorns have an arrangement with the hags. Something about exchanging us for their help against the wyrd. They even have a contract. I saw them arguing over it earlier. It should be around here somewhere.
Casnar? That's a … sore subject. Believe it or not, he's actually getting married today. \n\nShould be at the wedding right now. I know. I know. I should be there, but I'm not.

I don't know. Maybe because there are armed thugs out there, with orders to break my kneecaps if I try to leave?\n\nIf I thought I could get past them, I'd make a run for it, but they'd catch me. It would be pointless.

Ask Tiela's father. He's the one who hired them. Paid Uncle Thakh to make sure I don't get to the wedding.\n\nJagnas has been against our marriage from the beginning. I don't know why I thought he would come around.

Of course! He wants Tiela to think I stood her up. She'll hate me for the rest of her life and think he was right all along.\n\nThe bastard. If my father were alive, he'd beat the Oblivion out of Jagnas. Of course, that would only make things worse.

That's the first good news I've heard today. \n\nBut if you're here to take me to my father, you can get that thought right out of your head. There are beautiful women in Camlorn that still need to be rescued.

The inn's locked up tight and the innkeeper was killed trying to reach us. \n\nGet the key from the body and enter the inn, then shine a signal light. I'll rally the civilians and get them to safety. We'll talk about my key after that.

In all seriousness, I'm not doing anything before we find a safe refuge for the civilians hiding in the surrounding buildings. \n\nThe inn nearby should be defensible enough and it's full of supplies. There's just one catch.
Casnar? Why doesn't Casnar come talk to me himself? Oh yes, I remember. He prefers the indoors.\n\nProbably better that way. Yes. Casnar needs to stay at home … or do you take issue with that?

Slow down now. No need to be rude. Like I said, I'm a businessman. Truth is, I didn't much like the deal I had with Jagnas anyways. \n\nYou'll owe me a favor, but I'll give him a refund, and your boy can get married whenever he likes.
My people wouldn't have really hurt the kid anyways. Casnar and Tiela make a nice couple.\n\nIn fact, if you'll do me that favor we discussed, I'll have my men escort Casnar right up to the altar.
I'll answer what I can. \n\nToo bad you aren't asking about a nice place to eat in Camlorn. That I know. History of this bog and information about hags? I only know what the wyresses told me.

Sibellec is a Reach witch staying with the wyresses. Wyress Emilie says she can look right into you and see things about your past and future. \n\nThe wyresses say she isn't evil, but I'd still be careful around her.
They say she's got a taste for flesh. Thinks the bog belongs to her and the hags. \n\nThe wyresses have been fighting with her for generations.

Fate has led you here, just as I have foreseen it. You wish to resolve the conflict between the wyrd and the coven.\n\nMother Murk's anger and darkness run deep, even for a Hagraven. She's powerful and leads the coven through fear and pain.

I don't know where he is. He was in the village before the attack and I fear the worst. \n\nMy father and I, we didn't always get along. That's why I joined the Red Rooks in the first place. I just hope he's still alive.

You'll need this charm to defeat her, for she can siphon vitality from even the strongest foe. Kill the lesser hags and drain their power into this charm.  \n\nBut use the charm only when Murk tries to siphon your life force. Don't waste its power.

Then drink from the cup behind you. It holds a potent concoction to put you into a deep slumber.\n\nIf you are worthy, Leki will reveal a vision to you. Retrieve <<1>>, <<2>>, and <<3>> from this vision, if you can.
<<1>> summoned me.\n\nFor matters of honor, many turn to an arbitrator for counsel. And, when the situation necessitates, I am willing and able to execute justice.

Stone and steel! Well done. Remember, you'll never learn anything by studying your own work. You can only learn new techniques by studying the work of others.\n\nI think you're ready to master your first recipe.

There's a recipe on the table just over there. The scroll itself is unimportant. It's just a list of ingredients and steps. \n\nIt is the knowledge that you gain through research, combined with the recipe, that allows you to fully master a crafting.

If you must know, the guardians are the Ehlnofey. They've been a part of the land since the dawn of Tamriel.\n\nThe guardians have been with us since we first found the Wyrd Tree. They protect the land and guide us in our duties.
Yes, it's true, but only because resisting would have been to no avail.\n\nThey sought to use my manor as their command center. They would have slain me if I had not complied!
Good question. But how should I know? I'm just a former Lion Guard who decided to join the wyrd. \n\nThe tree keeps me safe. That's good enough for me.
Good. I cannot harm this corruption of the earth, but I can protect you from its attacks. \n\nListen to my warnings and you will prevail.
The Wyrd Tree must continue to reach for the sky. You must destroy the <<1>>.\n\nHeed my warnings and you will survive the vile creature's onslaught.
Destroy the corrupting spirit and then we can cleanse this place. Listen to my words. I shall offer what aid I can.
They're servants of Molag Bal. They seek to conquer Glenumbra. \n\nPlease stop them. We won't be able to resist the Bloodthorn much longer.

Because of Angof! He seemed like the strong leader that Glenumbra so desperately needs. He can be very persuasive. \n\nI never thought about the harm we were doing until the ghost of my own ancestor confronted me.

That's not hard to guess. It took everything we had to liberate Camlorn. That means two things.\n\nFirst, the enemy lost their base in Camlorn. Second, Aldcroft is vulnerable. I imagine the enemy will strike soon, before we can regroup.
Of course I am. I'm so scared I can't think straight! That's why I'm begging for your mercy and your aid. \n\nWhen this is all over, I'm going to run—north, east, anywhere my feet will take me.

I could guess. With most of our force besieging Camlorn, we're stretched thin. And frankly, the local watch isn't much use. \n\nWith the Duke gone, the enemy can take Aldcroft. Then they hit our troops at Camlorn from the rear. But I'm just guessing.
I can see that. So he's afraid to face his former comrades? He should fear the wrath of the angry dead more!\n\nStill, he has made an effort. Of a sort.
Return to Harald. Tell him to renounce the cult and continue to make amends or he'll suffer the vengeance of the dead. \n\nNow go. I wish to return to my rest.
Though Camlorn's safe now, werewolves and the Bloodthorn cult still threaten Aldcroft. \n\nWe knew they were planning something. We just didn't know it would involve taking the Duke captive.
Splendid! Cut me loose! You may think you defeated Faolchu, but his influence spreads like wildfire.\n\nSomething's not right in Aldcroft.
Sebastien? I have no time for …. oh, very well. We'll talk to the Duke. But every moment we delay allows the threat to grow stronger.
Remember, you never learn anything by studying your own work. You only learn by studying the work of others.\n\nI think  you're ready to master your first recipe.

On my table over there.

The scroll itself is unimportant. It is just a list of ingredients and steps. 

It is the knowledge that you gained through your research, combined with the recipie that allows you to fully master it.

Well done. You have demonstrated to me that you can master the basics. And you learned enough recipes to attempt to become an apprentice. \n\nThe question is, are you ready to put your skills to the test?

Make me a jack. First go to my apprentice Torvald and purchase some horn studs.

Next go to the crafting table and open your recipe book. Use the horn studs and the cured thin hide  to craft the jack.

Then return and show me your work.
If that was a joke, I don't think it was very funny.\n\nGo capture me a werewolf. I've got things to do.

Sir Granden was a great hero of High Rock. Standing alone in the pass to Stormhaven, he turned back the raging Nord invaders. \n\nAs the first spirit to fall to the Bloodthorns, he will be a fearsome opponent.

You're... helping us? I didn't think anyone would.\n\nThey're bringing bodies in via boat, and turning them into undead. If you can burn the bodies and destroy what zombies have already been created, we can stop them from massing an army.
Now don't ask me to guarantee that this antidote will work. Faolchu's spawn are unusually resilient.
In a church? Certainly not. But I could do it at the inn. That's Darien's plan. To get us to the inn. \n\nThen we'll see about crafting an antidote for this terrible affliction.
I heard the screams, and can feel the weight lifting from my mind.\n\nWe have another problem, though. The traitor Red Rooks gave information to the Bloodthorn.
Thank you! Thank you so much!
I … I don't feel so well.
Lord Velian, the Bloodthorn leader here, knows about the safe house. We saw him breaking through the wards.\n\nTamien ran ahead, but he stands no chance against Velian. You must help him!
Why, you heartless … I'll never see my family again!
Yes, I quite understand. I ask but one favor. Let me say farewell to my wife and daughter. They're just inside. It will only take a moment. \n\nThen you can do what you must.
Gautier's retaken the camp? You must have led quite a charge. \n\nTell him I have almost a full company of soldiers in here. And we're ready to fight.

We're nomads who follow the ways of the Ansei. Redguard society shuns us because we do what they won't do: we strike down the undead. To them, we're honorless animals.\n\nThat doesn't matter. They need us, and they know it.

Though he bears it well, "leader" is a title he'd refuse.\n\nMarimah brought our tribe into the light twenty years ago. A necromancer named Suturah ravaged the Alik'r with an army of the undead. None but the Ash'abah would stand against him.

We're an ancient sect, though we only returned to modern Redguard society twenty years ago. A dark necromancer named Suturah attacked the Alik'r. \n\nHe knew Redguards honor the dead and that we wouldn't stand against their assault. It was a slaughter.

Legend says three brave Ansei imbued a set of swords with their soul energy. The swords became necromantic wards of immense power. Because of this, undead cannot be raised within the bounds of Alik'r. \n\nNow the swords are safely kept in Sentinel.

Marimah is a legend among the Ash'abah. He led us against a terrible necromancer named Suturah who nearly conquered Alik'r with an undead army.\n\nMarimah's blade was the tool that finally ended Suturah's assult. Stories say his skill rivaled Leki's!

The Ash'abah broke Suturah's storm. I rallied my tribe, led them into battle, and personally took Suturah's life. \n\nI kept his corpse in sight at all times, until it was consecrated by the priests of Sentinel.

King Fahara'jad supported us, but quietly. He couldn't do so openly, as tradition says it's dishonorable to harm the dead, even when they're at your gates.\n\nWe defeated the army, and Marimah killed Suturah. I used to think the story ended there.
What? No, not at all! We're given coin to get eggs and feathers. It's a pittance, but it's better than nothing.\n\n We haven't quelled the harpies, though. We've just stirred them up!

Have mortals so soon forgotten the old ways? Surely the wyresses remember the standing stones. \n\nFirst, the stones must be cleansed of Angof's dark influence. Protect the wyrd while they destroy the corruption binding the stones.

No, but cleansing the stones should loosen Angof's grip. Tell <<1>> about the corruption. She will know what must be done.\n\nOur time grows short, mortal. Free us before Angof's corruption takes hold.

It's called Merien's White Mask. My father loves to name his spells after himself. \n\nWhen cast on a building, the spell cloaks everyone inside in a shroud of misdirection. Makes anyone who looks see something other than what's really there.
I was hoping you would say that!

Yes. I believe Angof is using the nature of Cath Bedraud, along with his powerful magic, to hide himself outside Nirn.\n\nThe talisman is said to have the ability to open tears into Oblivion, which we can use to bypass Angof's boundary.
I was confident I could return before the wards wore off.\n\nIt was a risk I had to take, and I knew Commander Marone would not approve of my side venture.
Wouldn't you be? I mean, it's a dangerous affair we're all mixed up in, but the sheer possibilities of the talisman are staggering!\n\nJust think of what it means for Glenumbra and the Mages Guild!
Faolchu wasn't called the Invincible General for nothing. You can cut him, bash him, fill him full of arrows—he just keeps coming.\n\nWe must discover how they stopped him and ended this ancient war.
That worthless thug? Gods only know how he got appointed. He brought his own "guard" along with him.\n\nIt's not safe to be asking about him, especially in the open. I've got to go.

I found an inscription in the crypt. It described the relic in remarkable detail. Apparently, the talisman can draw energy from the land itself.\n\nAncient magic saturates this site. It's the perfect place to perform the ritual of recharging!
I perform the ritual. You stand there and look heroic. Simple?\n\nAre you ready?
I could tell you the basic story, but if you want a deeper understanding you need to ask our loremaster, Dhalana.\n\nShe's up on the tower, observing the movement of the spirits.
Of course. What would you like to know?
This is where Clan Direnni fought to defend High Rock against the invading Alessian Order. \n\nThe Alessians outnumbered them three to one, but this was Direnni land and the clan prevailed.

The Alessians were a fundamentalistic sect that wanted to purge Elven influence from Tamriel's religions. \n\nWe think Faolchu was one of their generals. They called him the Changeling. And the Invincible One.
Legends tell us that the Nameless Soldier killed Faolchu. It's said the Nameless Soldier prevailed by making a great sacrifice.

Nothing could stop Faolchu. The soldiers he bit became werewolves and turned against their own. This land should have fallen to his lycanthropic plague. \n\nBut someone or something killed him that day.
The Direnni settled in High Rock long ago. \n\nThey were ancient High Elves who stood with the local Bretons against the Alessian invaders.
Seems likely. We don't know how the Nameless Soldier defeated Faolchu yet, but we're determined to figure it out.

Did she? Well, now that you've found me, perhaps you can help. \n\nThe guardians no longer speak to us. There's an old rite to contact them that might work, but it's too dangerous for us to attempt. After all, we aren't warriors.

I don't know. You're not one of us. But we have to try something, I suppose.\n\nSee the lurchers out there? Gather their limbs. That's the dangerous part. Then burn the limbs at the altar atop the nearby ruins. If it works, a guardian should appear.
Yes. I can see that now. A wise man passed through here not long ago.\n\nHe foresaw all of this, and he warned me, the desert is the kingdom of death by divine right. We cannot change that.
The ritual worked, but something … well, something awful looked at me while I was channeling energy into the relic. \n\nI think there's something trapped inside the talisman.
Just getting down here tired me out more than it should have. I know you can handle whatever's inside the talisman. \n\nI'm pretty sure it's just a banekin or a lesser Scamp.

Whatever's inside the relic, it's certainly not friendly. \n\nWe can try to dispel it using the wyrd revelation stone in the circle just up the beach. Put the talisman on the stone and kill whatever emerges. That will do the trick.
Dremora? Oh, those are bad. Sorry. At least it's gone and we can use the talisman now.\n\nI have enough energy to open a portal for both of us to use. Are you ready to return to the redoubt?
She was killed. But her sacrifice was worth it—both in the past and in the present.\n\nIf you discovered Faolchu's weakness, then Alana's death wasn't in vain.
The land's turned against us! Spriggans and imps have overrun the mill. \n\nMy family and I escaped, but the rest of the villagers weren't so lucky.

I don't know. There might be a way to help the other villagers. A group of women showed up as we fled. Called themselves the wyrd sisters as they threw around spells.\n\nThey helped us escape. Maybe they know what's going on out there.
Why do strangers always ask me that?\n\nNever mind. What did you want to know? With bandits and harpies in the wilderness, there's no shortage of troubles.

North of Daggerfall proper there are rocky cliffs known as the Shrieking Scar.\n\nLocals who venture there tend to go missing. They probably end up in the bellies of harpies that roost in the nooks and crannies of the stone.

Red Rooks, they call themselves.\n\nIt's a shame, really. Most of them used to be good and regular folk from all across Glenumbra. These trying times have turned them to banditry. Watch your step around them, stranger.

Get them a gift. Some Hag's Breath! It's an aphrodisiac. They might not be able to walk for a few days, but it'll make the wedding night unforgettable!\n\nThere's an old hag in the desert—Viyaneh. Kill her and bring her Hag's Breath to the wedding.
I bet Lafont was hiding him there until he could turn poor Glutton into ribs and chops. But now I've got my prized pig back.

Lafont's guilty of something, I'm sure of it.\n\nBut what do I care about strange vines? Talk to Zhagush over by the Mages Guild if you're so interested. He knows his plants. Sold me some herbs one time when Glutton ate something that upset his tummy.
Well, don't dawdle. Ask your questions. I don't have all day.
They're death mages led by the cursed Reachman, Angof the Gravesinger. \n\nI heard they were causing trouble north of Glenumbra. They must be getting bolder if they're operating in Daggerfall.

Angof and the Bloodthorn cult use them for some foul purpose. If you see the vines, that usually means the cult is active in the area. \n\nThe vines spread an evil poison through the soil. It's a hateful substance that kills everything it touches.

Angof's a Reachman, one of those magic-cursed savages from the border of Bangkorai. \n\nBut he's more than that. He's a necromancer. They call him Gravesinger because he made a deal with the Daedric Prince, Molag Bal.
Are we all right? Soldiers have invaded our farm and you're asking if we're all right?\n\nWhat is this? Some kind of trick so you can take our house, too?

And I should just believe you and open this door? I don't think so.\n\nIf you really want to help, bring me weapons to arm my family with. Once we can properly defend ourselves, I'll happily open this door.

Not just any weapons, you hear me? I need a two-handed sword. And one-handed swords for my wife and oldest son. My youngest son needs a bow. And my daughter, she insists on having a pair of daggers.\n\nBring the weapons back here when you have them.

We are the echoes of old voices, remnants of a time long ago. Still, a few of us remain.\n\nWe were the Y'ffre. Then we became the Ehlnofey, the Earth Bones. We nurture the land and guide the wyrd. They call us guardians.

They are a pestilence. They serve the corruption that binds us, the one called Angof the Gravesinger.\n\nThe cult spreads his decay, planting his blighted seeds to pollute the natural world. They prepare a path for Angof's true master—Molag Bal.

He is a tremor in the land, a poison in the water. He is a whisper, a shadow, a chill wind. He is Gravesinger and Reachmage, necromancer and corrupter.\n\nDeath and decay are his domains. Angof binds us and seeks to make us part of him.
Ah! Excellent. My other assistant has been … well, I suppose the technical term is consumed. I told her not to get so close to that giant lizard.\n\nAnyway, I could use your help.

Ah, you do understand! Four keys open the vault: the Keys of Flames, Blades, Strife, and Crowns. Three of the keys are hidden in this tomb.\n\nI have the fourth key. It's an heirloom. Been in my family for generations. Take it and get the other keys.

I'm going to recover the legendary Jeweled Crown of Anton. Well, as soon as we can get into the locked vault. I understand the place is filthy with traps and undead creatures.\n\nYou see where I'm going with this, don't you?

In life, I was the royal seneschal of King Anton of Daggerfall. I died in this tomb, along with my king.\n\nHis Majesty's bones have turned to dust, but I remain. Perhaps we can help each other? One favor for another?
A noble with delusions of treasure hunting entered the tomb earlier. \n\nI can help you find the vault she seeks. In return, you shall help me.
They are abominations of the Bloodthorns! The lurchers were spriggans once, until the cultists twisted and corrupted them. \n\nThat's what the Bloodthorns do. We must stop them!
You can handle this on your own. There's fresh blood inside the farmhouse. Can't you smell it?\n\nI need to collect my healing supplies from the tower so I can help Gennove and his family.
Right. Good. Whatever.\n\nThe sooner we get this done, the sooner I can get something to eat. Suddenly I'm starving.

We were attacked by the Bloodthorn cultists and their lurchers. They descended on the Wyrd Tree like locusts, overwhelming us before we knew they were there.\n\nMany sisters died defending the Tree. Those of us who survived built this camp.

We seek the aid of the Guardians. We need their help to retake the Wyrd Tree and drive out the cultists and the lurchers.\n\nEach of us seeks the Guardians in her own way, but none of us have had any success yet.
Of course. Go on.

Our lordship defends Daggerfall. He will not let our proud history be forgotten. \n\nWe may be part of the Covenant, but it was he who insisted the Knights of the Dragon be maintained as a separate entity.
Every kingdom has troubles and every monarch has challenges in times like these. We shall endure.\n\nOur enemies—the Dominion and the Pact—will not.
Daggerfall is the jewel of Breton cities. It's the home of House Deleyn. Each son is a more worthy king than the last. \n\nWhy do you think they call our alliance the Daggerfall Covenant, after all?
We need to summon the guardians. With their power, we can cleanse this place of Angof's foul influence.

Angof's cursed vines prevent the guardians from getting anywhere near the Wyrd Tree. \n\nFind the vines that grow within the circles of Wyrd blossoms and destroy them. That should allow the guardians to appear before you.

What do you think I've been doing here? Making soup? \n\nHere it is. Go beat up on some werewolves until they're weakened, then douse them with this. If the cure works, they'll revert to human form. Then send them back here.
You're brave to cross blades with these heroes yourself.\n\nDon't worry though. This man will ensure you do not fall.
Very smart. I've rarely seen her equal with a blade. \n\nLet her keep the heroes occupied and perhaps you can use magic to send them back to the sand.
<The door is unlocked.>

I can't enter the vault, so listen well. There are two crowns inside, but you may take only one. One is King Anton's jeweled crown. The other bears the curse that binds me here. \n\nI want you to take the cursed crown.
No. Your soul is already trapped elsewhere.\n\nBut if anyone else touches it, they will be bound here. They will take my place. And I will be free.
Now, don't be modest. You've more than proven yourself. Destiny beckons and you must answer its call. \n\nSay, that sounded rather good. I should write this stuff down.
<This ancient tome has the power to activate the pillars in Salas En and to close the portal beneath the ruins.>

We train the ways of the ready sword and the sharp mind. Our martial tradition dates to the time of the Ra Gada, by Leki's blessed blade.\n\nEven if you never plan to wield a sword, you'll face one in battle. Here, you'll learn to survive.
Leki, the divine daughter of Tall Papa, is the Sword-Saint who taught new ways of wielding the blade.\n\nThis school is named for her, on the very place of one of her many miracles.

Only the ancestors know for certain, but legend says Rada arrived to find Leki, as a warrior of sand wielding a blade of the hardest rock.\n\nRada bowed to it. When it bowed back, he found an opponent worthy of his skills. They dueled.

You need only look to where we stand for the answer. The blade broke in two, and a great sandstorm split the horizon.\n\nWhen it cleared, Leki had erected a shrine from the sands, and its oasis held the purest water in all Alik'r.

They crossed blades for three days and three nights. Rada's strikes parted the sand but briefly, and he tired as the days wore on.\n\nAt last, Rada put all of his strength into one final strike: the weakest point of his opponent's rocky blade.

A tyrant threatens your people. If you submit to him and become his willing thrall, your people will be shown mercy. If you attack, you and your people will be driven from your homeland and exiled to the sea. \n\nWhat do you do?

I too chose to attack—but all choices bear a cost, wayfarer. When the last sword was sheathed in the shadow of Mt Hattu, the dead were beyond counting. Many more were lost at sea during the exodus. \n\nWas the price of honor too high?

Submission would have brought peace, yes. But at what cost? All that Yokuda was and is finds its source in the blade. We could not waver. Even so, there is always cost. I chose the sword—many and many were lost. \n\nWas this the greater good?

You are a scout for a great army, perched on a mountainside. In the pass below, a band of enemy soldiers slowly approach the position of your dearest friend.\n\nDo you abandon your post to help your friend, or do you remain hidden to report the attack?

Yes, your friend may die if you do not render aid. But if you fail to report the assault, is not the entire army put at risk? How many men could lose their lives for this one soldier? \n\nOne's loyalties are truly put to the test.

So, you place duty above personal concerns. Your superiors would be pleased, certainly … but could you bear the guilt? Could you walk all the long trails of your life knowing that your inaction led to the death of your closest friend?

Giant Goblins, beasts thought conquered by Divad, have returned. The fight goes poorly. You know the location of powerful magicked blades, but they are dangerous. They were hidden for a reason.\n\nDo you seek out the blades or fight on without them?

You would have met a glorious end.\n\nWe chose the blades and destroyed the beasts. But as a result, the Shehai—our spirit swords—were forever destroyed. Centuries of wondrous tradition was snuffed out. I must bear this weight always.

I acted as you would.\n\nWe chose the blades and destroyed the beasts. But as a result, the Shehai—our spirit swords—were forever destroyed. Centuries of wondrous tradition was snuffed out. I must bear that weight always.

You have won a great battle and covered yourself in glory—but you are gravely wounded. A magical memory stone will allow you to record your last thoughts.\n\nDo you think of the battle, recording history? Or do you immortalize your beloved family?

The battle was important, yes. But is love not also worthy of rememberance? I thought of my training and the details of the battle. But as I turned my thoughts to family, death silenced me. \n\nNow they are forgotten—lost for all time.

Family is paramount, yes. But are not all Redguards bound by blood? In immortalizing your own family, you may have robbed a civilization of one of its greatest glories. \n\nThe price of legend is high. The battle is celebrated, but my family is lost.

When the stone is fully activated, it's going to generate a magical aura that's going to be hard to ignore, especially for a creature that's probably filled up to the eyes with the stuff.\n\nHe'll, mmf, notice, don't worry about that.
Ha! Only Tu'whacca has such knowledge, my friend. I could barely hear you from here. Luckily, Tu'whacca has shared some of his wisdom with me.

Tu'whacca tells me that you are bound to the greatest of Redguard virtues: honor and loyalty. You are drawn to great summits and glorious ends. Hold fast to that courageous spirit, but know that sometimes we must make sacrifices for the greater good.

You walk the narrow path that cuts between glory and sacrifice—valor and patience. You measure your pusuit of honor with reason and foresight. To see all ends is a gift only Tu'whacca possesses. But to walk in his footsteps is wise indeed!

You show great wisdom with your choices, my friend. You pursue the deepest honor—that which is found in sacrifice. Your pursuit of the Withered Hand is proof of this, is it not so? Only know that caution is sometimes the enemy of progress.

Students prove themselves through the art of battle. Any fool can win a duel, but a master knows who will challenge her, and where it will occur.\n\nYou must think as the masters did. Learn not just how they fought, but when, and why.

Listen! This is a tale of <<1>>, blademaster of <<2>>. While on walkabout, <<1>> encountered a wagon.\n\nThe wagon's owner was an uninjured woman, facing an unmasked man. He held a battered axe; she, a pristine blade.
The woman said the man was a bandit who had already attacked her once. She begged <<1>> to intervene.\n\n<<1>> walked away, yet the woman lived to tell her tale. Why did she live?
If this was true, why beg <<1>> for aid? If she and the bandit fought, she'd have seen his measure. She would have known she could beat him.\n\nYou must look deeper.

You see as <<1>> did. The woman claimed she fought the bandit, yet she had no wounds. Had she parried his axe, her pristine blade would be notched.\n\nHad <<1>> faced the "bandit," the woman would have stabbed her in the back.

If that was true, why would he not kill her afterwards?\n\nHe challenged her without a mask. She would know his face, and could have pointed him out to the authorities. Why would he have let her live? Look deeper.

Then hear the story of <<1>>. Long ago, a foreign mage came to challenge us. He claimed his power a match for our blades. One by one, he dueled our students.\n\nThis master of alteration could turn steel to mist at will. Every student lost.

You see as <<1>> did.\n\nThe foreign mage claimed his power a match for our blades. Indeed, any steel that threatened him turned to mist as fast as one could blink, but a training sword is wood, and wood is nothing like steel.

Think of what you suggest. Would a student of <<1>> strike before the opponent was ready? This would sully his honor for the sake of temporary gain.\n\nNever. No Redguard would resort to such a dishonorable tactic. Look deeper.

A valid strategy, one that has certainly felled even the most powerful mage. Yet what would it have proven?\n\nThe mage made no claim he could defeat any bow. He said only that his power was a match for the sword. Look deeper.

<<1>> was an initiate, yet he faced the mage and won. So handily, in fact, that his opponent made apologies and left, forever shamed.\n\nOf all the students who faced the mage, <<1>> was far from the best warrior. How did <<1>> win the duel?

I tell you now the story of <<1>>'s end.\n\nLong ago, <<2>> was the blademaster here. In his last days, he called his favorite student to him. If she could give him what he wanted most, she would become the next blademaster of <<3>>.

That is what you must discover. <<1>>'s legend is known by all, even the serving folk. Direct your questions to them—<<2>>, <<3>>, and <<4>>.\n\nOnce you know what they know, return to me and give your answer.
Like many here, I came to <<1>> to become a great warrior. Despite my training, I lacked talent with a blade.\n\nI returned to my family, ashamed. And then, I remembered one of <<2>>'s lessons.

"We do not choose when we rest. To give up the hard road is to bring suffering to the next traveler." Basically, never give up.\n\nTen years I've trained since that day. I'm no master, but if my family needs me, I can defend them.
Anyone who knows of our school has heard of him. He was the master who brought the teachings to so many, tireless in his quest for perfecting the blade.
In truth, no one knows! Many tales were told about his last battle with a group of bandits.\n\nSome say he survived, and went on to roam the sands beyond Leki's Blade. I can't imagine that myself.
Forgive me. These students mock my temper. You'd think I'm the old master's reincarnation, the way they bellyache!\n\nIn any case, I know only the stories, such as the one about the enchanted knives.

He forbade Redguard trainees to dabble in magic. When a traveling merchant brought enchanted knives, <<1>> upturned the cart and chased the poor man into a sand dune!\n\nHe wouldn't even use the metal! He threw the knives out after the merchant!
Excellent! Then tell me, what did <<1>> want at the end of his life?\n\nWhat did his student give him?
If such a thing existed, <<1>> would never have used it. No true Redguard warrior in his day would stoop to magic, no matter how dire his cause.\n\nNo Redguard would be so weak. Look deeper.

<<1>>'s sickness was great, and a Redguard who cannot fight is as weak as a toothless snake. But Redguards do not throw their lives away, no matter the hardship they face.\n\nRedguards fight. They fight even when there is no hope. Look deeper.

You see as the young student did, so long ago.\n\nBy that time, <<1>> was old and weak. No Redguard wishes to die in bed, but it's shameful to take one's own life to avoid hardship. <<1>> left, not to die, but to face one last battle.

Then we'll see the make of your steel in battle.\n\nMy students have trained for seasons, but you have the experience of true battle. If you can defeat them all, then I will count you as an equal to them. If not, then I have no time for you.
Too little, too late, stranger.\n\nIf you had come to us before that monster knocked on our door, maybe things would be different. Instead, my father is dead and my family is scattered.

A sword? Just like my father requested? I wish he had just let you in. You could have saved him.\n\nI'll run to the Shornhelm Guard. Please, find the rest of my family. We got separated in the confusion.

She knocked on the door. She sounded concerned, said … she was there to help. When my father opened the door, he was attacked. He yelled for us to run.\n\nI heard my father's screams. They followed me as I ran.
Why would he issue such a command?

I see. Adrien was always a brave boy. Though obviously his head was full of nothing but stones. This cannot be allowed to continue.\n\nI offer myself in his place. My skills as a healer do not appear to have diminished in my death.

The Queen would be a powerful ally. Her skills has a healer were legendary. But I cannot work against <<1>>'s wishes.\n\nHe gave explicit instructions. However, you are not under any such order. The choice will be yours.
Very well. I will allow you to bind me to yourself. In that way, I will be able to come when you need my aid against the Imperials.\n\nThe necklace you used to summon me should suffice.

Very well. We have everything we need for the ritual. <<1>> is currently a shell. Using the power from the souls you gathered, we will draw his soul into the body we created earlier.\n\nWhen you're ready, use his talisman to start the ritual.
When Faolchu dies the armor will eject you from the past. You'll return, unharmed, to the here and now. \n\nYes. That's what will happen. I'm sure of it.
You … you were the one who came to the door? Who my father sent off to get weapons for us? He should have trusted you.
I feel better with these in my hands. I just wish you would have made it back sooner. Then maybe my father would still be alive.

I wasn't close enough to hear, but someone knocked on the door and convinced my father to open it.\n\nThat's when the screaming started. And the blood! I panicked. Probably would have died myself if not for Jowan.

I'm afraid it is. I'm sorry for the deception, but we needed your aid and couldn't take the risk that you'd refuse.\n\nPrince Adrien commanded us to raise him as a weapon against the Imperials. However distasteful, we need his aid.
No you don't, and I don't mean to let you.\n\nOnly crew and special guests down there. Anyone else goes down, they'll get cut.
Go ahead then. Take it. Go down there and get yourself killed. It's no skin off my back.
I care about two things: my crew and my gold. Seeing as you threaten neither, you haven't got a leg to stand on.\n\nLeave while you still have the rest of your limbs.

Yes, and every thought we think. Our lives are the shadows fate casts on the sand. Do not fear this truth.\n\nThink of fate as your constant companion. To glimpse upon fate is to see what unites us all.
Now listen carefully. There will be a lot to remember.

The Heralds are three engraved statues that each offer a riddle. You must place an offering before each Herald.\n\nThe statues are the Herald of Thirst, the Herald of Memory, and the Herald of Illumination.
Yes, the bastards! I tried to sneak past them, but … well, you see how well that turned out.\n\nBeing a ghost has put a bit of a damper on my adventuring career.
The histories I read never specified, but it's said that the greatest treasure of the Breton kingdoms was stored here.

There are a number of possible offerings in my bag.\n\nTake my backpack and see if you can match the offerings to the correct Heralds. Engravings on the statues provide clues about which offerings they will accept.

The Goblins? Certainly not! I've been studying the local gargoyles—I believe they're the key to certain Yokudan myths and legends.\n\nThe Goblins are irrelevant. Their interference has been most inconvenient. Do be a dear and show them no mercy.
That is not a matter for you to worry about.\n\nThe owner won't come looking for it, if that's what you're wondering.
<This backpack contains three items that seem appropriate: an old cup, a glass bottle full of water, and a wooden ladle.>
<You find three possible offerings in Dusant's backpack: a blank scroll, a chronicle of the Deleyn dynasty, and a copy of "The Lusty Argonian Maid.">
<Dusant's backpack contains three possible offerings: a torch, a candle, and a chip from a welkynd stone.>
Yes, most satisfactory. Stibbons would have dusted them off as well, but one mustn't be choosy, must one?\n\nNow, off to our first camp at the dig site, where we'll find my man Stibbons. Shall we?

I am the High Librarian of Dresan Keep. I was charged with protecting our greatest treasure—the combined histories of the earliest days of High Rock.\n\nDo be careful with these books. They are in pristine condition.

Indeed. Our patron is Hermaeus Mora, the scryer of the heavens and he who determines the Tides of Fate. \n\nThese treasures have been sealed away for too long. Hoarding knowledge is worse than hoarding gold. Or so our patron has decreed.
Take this index. It contains the names of all the volumes and scrolls the keep contains.\n\nYou must give the Dresan Index to someone who can make use of it, such as a scholar of magic.

I suppose you should know the truth. Ancient inscriptions here described some unique alchemical processes, which I tried to duplicate. \n\nI fear I succeeded all too well, and Stibbons' unfortunate condition is the result.
Praise the Divines! You're a lifesaver, Stibbons. Er, I mean … whatever your name is.\n\nAt any rate, give me a moment to read these over, and I'll know what I need next.

You're right. It's the only safe path. I knew that all along. That's why … well, a good healer can craft a poison as well as a poultice. When I dropped my kit, I held on to it. I knew this was how it had to end.\n\nTell Fairfax I'm sorry.
Ah, ah, ah. Not quite yet. We need weapons and armor to help protect these civilians.\n\nThere are caches of Camlorn Guard supplies hidden around the city. Gather some and we can arm more people.
Oh, we can give you fire. \n\nAt least we can once the Lion Guard archers arrive. Keep Faolchu busy long enough, and you'll get all the fire you need.
What do you mean? We just spoke over Gennove's corpse. I asked you to look for the Hinaults.

I can't sneeze without him asking if I'm all right these days. I don't know what his problem is!\n\nI'll talk to him when I get a chance. If you've accounted for all the Hinaults, I'll make a final check on the farmhands and then meet you at the tower.
What? No, that's not right. You just left a minute ago!\n\nYou must be wrong. If you're in the field for too long, Akatosh can play tricks on you. He can make a moment last an hour or vice-versa.

I need to develop an antidote for the Yokudan stoneflesh potion. And to be safe, I'll need to test it on other research subjects before applying it to Stibbons. \n\nSo I need the original reagents back so I can make more of the stoneflesh potion.

You sought to protect the Wards? Praise Tu'whacca. That means there are still living those who oppose the menace of necromancy in the Alik'r.\n\nHearken closely then, for my spirit cannot abide here long.

We sacrificed ourselves to create the Wards, and through them we have protected the consecrated dead.\n\nBut the Wards have fallen into corrupted hands now, and we are powerless to stop them. You must recover the Wards ….

My father sent me because he feared the Withered Hand might target our navy.\n\nI don't think that's why the necromancers came, though. Many centuries ago, this was the home of one of the Ansei. One who sacrificed themselves to create the wards.
Very good. Now craft me that ring.
Like a civilized person, you may leave through the door on the far side of the vault. No need to use the well again.\n\nThe ward on the gate has been broken and the door will open now.
Yes, my friend, but you turned the tide. \n\nWe had all but lost the war before you came and showed us the way to victory.

Indeed it is. It's up to you to administer it, of course. You should probably pour it into whatever noisome slumgullion they're brewing up in those cookpots.\n\nWhile you're attending to that, I'll consult with our hireling guide.

We can't just sit out here. The Lion Guard would just be as quickly overrun again if Faolchu sent another wave at us.\n\nThe position of power is in our hands now. We go on the offensive and catch the beast off guard.

Gautier sent several of his troops to start the assault already, but Faolchu keeps funneling his wolves through the central gate.\n\nGet to the courtyard and into the rear tower. There's a lock for the gate there. Lock it up for us to stop his charge.
You're looking at them. We're all that's left.\n\nWe can hold this position, but we don't have enough troops remaining to make a full assault on the city.
General Gautier is already working on getting a scouting party out to Aldcroft for more units. We can't give up our offensive.

The wolf's woe grows all around here, so it should be easy to acquire.\n\nAs for the key, grab a Red Rook uniform and look around. The disguise should fool the bandits, but watch out for the wolves. Otherwise, shake a few bandits until a key falls out.

The General has sent a batch of troops forward to keep the werewolves off guard, but they're swarming out of the main gate.\n\nIf we can lock that gate, we can slow them down enough to overtake the courtyard.
There's a tower in the central courtyard that holds the lock. If you can fight your way back to it and throw the switch, we can start to take my city back once and for all!
I'm unsure. The General has some ideas and has already sent for reinforcements. We can't just stand here though. We can't.
What any ruler should do. I'll serve my people. \n\nI failed to defend Camlorn once. That won't happen again.
That's a problem for another day. Let's enjoy this victory. \n\nYou won here. Savor that while you can.

Ah. This is for Gabrielle, isn't it? She's a regular. In a city like Sentinel, we Bretons have to stick together.\n\nI have some in stock. You're welcome to them. Don't worry about payment. I know Gabrielle's good for it.
I'm sorry, but I'm out of stock … because I'm out of stalks. Hehe. \n\nSeriously though, some Lion Guard mages came through and bought my last batch. Neeneban, the lizard trainer, might have some.
Worm stalk caps? No, I don't. Lizards enjoy worm stalks, but they're also poisonous to them.\n\nDead lizards don't sell, except in times of famine. There isn't a famine right now.

Flame stalks! Tasty treats. They help with indigestion … for a lizard at least.

You're not a lizard. What do you need them for? For some spell with Gabrielle I bet, and she doesn't even like lizards ….

Oh well. Just take them, but she owes me!
Oh, you must mean Monkey! Yes, he is adorably large, isn't he? I'm afraid I spoil him—only the best bugs are good enough for my Monkey.\n\nHe's quite smart, aren't you, Monkey? Quite a little smarty.

One has to start somewhere! Monkeys are terrific—everyone loves monkeys. And if I can't have a monkey, a lizard's the next best thing.\n\nYou know, sometimes I wonder how my life would be different if my father had only given me a monkey.

Yes! It may seem odd, but it makes sense to me.\n\nFrom the time I could walk, I wanted a pet monkey. I pleaded and begged, but my father always refused. "Monkeys are arboreal," he said. I still don't know what that means.
I'm sorry. I forgot I wasn't speaking to one of my fellow intellectuals.\n\nWhere shall I begin? Long ago, there was a maiden ….
Please. I am an academic. We can speak in more modulated tones, can't we?\n\nAll right. I am ready. I was waiting for you, remember? We should continue our quest for Azei.
I will have to be. I cannot risk the consequences of leaving <<1>> up to his own whims in such a site as this.
It's a long story, one that's hardly worth the breath to tell. Hmm. How should I explain this?\n\nIn another life, I owed the queen a debt. When her daughter needed aid, I had to help.
Oh! They were terrible! Ravening madmen. And madwomen. I think we should fall back to Evermore.\n\nIs that enough? Because this wound really hurts, and I'd like to get some rest.
It doesn't matter. I have the information I came here for.
Are you mad? Sellan wants the people to rise up and fight. That would be suicide! \n\nStill, the Red Rooks harass me every day, demanding more and more gold. Oh, no! I think I hear them now.

Far from here, where the earth and sky grow cold, lies the chill of the Reach. \n\nDaedra worshipers live there, mocking the Aedra, the Ehlnofey. They call themselves Reachmen and their mages pollute the land with dark magic.

My fellow guards and I were fools to think we could contain the Ra-Netu. We needed someone like you to simply cut them down.\n\nI will go, but would you check on the dockmaster in the east warehouse? I promised I would not leave without him.
Give me a moment to finish what I'm doing here.\n\nGo on outside. I'll meet you there.

Weren't you listening? They killed him! First, they ran the watch out of town. Then they took over our businesses. Now they murdered the mayor!\n\nThey extort, threaten, and murder to their heart's content! And no one can stop them!

Oh? Well why didn't you say so? The Red Rooks took over my mine. They're forcing the miners to work until they drop.\n\nYou want to stop the Red Rooks? How about running them through with a sword. That'd be damned useful.
Very good. Now craft me that ring.

So many people … they died when the Bloodthorn cult devastated Eagle's Brook.\n\nIn return for my cooperation, the Red Rooks promised to protect my father and the people of Eagle's Brook from the Bloodthorns. They lied.

I know it is wrong for me to strike them, but we cannot stand by and let the Ra-Netu overrun Sentinel!\n\nI was prepared to dishonor myself, but now that you are here, I would rather flee and avoid this conflict if I can.
This Ra-Netu caught me! He was trying to bite me, to eat me! I tried to fend him off, but he jerked and his head ran against my blade—it wasn't my fault! \n\nWhat am I going to do now?

Lord Velian is the leader of the Bloodthorn cult. He killed me and bound my soul to power his rituals. That's how he raised all those undead!\n\nWith the ritual disrupted, he needs another soul. That's why he's taken my son.

He's no ordinary criminal. He's a Reachman from the north.\n\nWe can't have him in a normal cell. He may kill his fellow prisoners, or ensorcel the jailer. Of course, out here he may just turn into a bird and fly away.
They're a tribe of people from the frozen north, known to command strange magic, and harbor no semblance of humanity.\n\nI've fought them before. They bleed just like any other man.

That's what I told my mother, but she swore it would let me fit in with the other children in Evermore. It didn't.\n\nBut she was a stubborn one. Had to be, to adopt an Orc child. I turned out well enough.
That's what we plan to find out. We know they've already burned two of our outlying farms.\n\nWhy they've decided to mount an offensive now ... I've no clue.

An invasion, or just short of it. The Reachmen kill what they can eat, and burn what they can't.\n\nSo many farms and livelihoods are destroyed, thanks to those monsters. And when will we see recompense?
<<1>> has always looked after her subjects. Why should she not aid us now?\n\nIf the Evermore army were not manning the garrison down south, we would have an armed answer to those mad Reachmen.
I don't pretend to know the reasoning of madmen. They howl for blood like rabid wolves. I've heard them.\n\nIt's clear they want nothing but our lives. Evermore must protect us!

He has taken the duties of our king in the queen's absence. We in the court are all thankful for his compassion and wisdom.\n\nNevertheless, the court is closed to commoners for the foreseeable future.

His Majesty had gone to our garrison to the south in order to perform inspections and provide morale.\n\nThe garrison was attacked from the south. His Majesty was slain, and Sir Renchant was one of the few to survive.
She is in seclusion in her chambers, mourning the loss of her husband, the king.\n\nHer daughter and son have both fallen to misfortune as well. We pray for our queen in these hard times.

It's both a blessing and a binding of service. Once a soldier has given his life to the royal service, he is forever bound to serve.\n\nQueen Arzhela, Stendarr watch over her, will always be protected by her loyal soldiers.
They couldn't have gotten too far into the graveyard. The poison mist acts fast. \n\nHopefully, they stayed together. Once you get them out of there, we can plan our attack against Angof.
Arkay blind me if I know. When the King mentioned your name, the dog perked up and stuck with us all the way from Daggerfall. \n\nLooks like he's happy to see you.

A reckless noble named Darien led a handful of soldiers into Cath Bedraud. He seemed intent on saving the Dragons, but he was also extremely interested in getting closer to Angof.\n\nHe kept going on about werewolves.

I wish I knew. I didn't think. I just rushed in to help the Dragon Knights. My guards started gasping and falling to the ground, just like the knights. But not me.\n\nThese are the only survivors, but I don't think they'll last much longer.

The mist is thicker toward the gate. They won't survive passing through it again. \n\nBut the mist doesn't seem to affect the necromancers. Those amulets must protect them. Kill a few, take their amulets, and give them to the knights.

This man is very dangerous. He is the leader of these Withered Hand dogs. He offered me the chance to leave peacefully ….\n\nI wanted to protect my fellow priests, but we could not surrender Tu'whacca's sacred ground without a fight.
So it begins again. Satak was the First Serpent.\n\nSatakal eats himself, and the spirits move to the Far Shores to wait for their next skin.

Hearken, wayfarer! They were here before the walls rose, and they are here after! And yet some mock these lowly creatures for worshiping them. What folly!\n\nThe flying stones hold the secret you seek. In their unyielding flesh that is not flesh.

That's why I had you dose the Goblins' stew! Do pay attention. Several of them must have been petrified by now. \n\nI've prepared several versions of the antidote. I'll need you to apply it to the petrified Goblins and record the results.

Ruptga became the Tall Papa, and he made the Great Map with the stars in his hand.\n\nWhen Sep tricked the spirits, he put a star in his pocket. This was the Pearl that fell out when Tall Papa squashed Sep with his staff.

Sand covered the Pearl. Thus, it came to Zeht, who works the land.\n\nWhen the Pearl is uncovered, the time of Sep's Hunger will be over. Water from the Pearl will run over the skins, and the Hungry Stomach will at last be full.
Know this: the Pearl is the Way and the Guide.\n\nIt is the light to the Far Shores and back again, as they are placed by Tall Papa's hand.

The only real world is Satakal. You cannot eat the stars.\n\nOne Sound will open the Way, and One Sound will close it. This is the sound of the worlds, calling to something to save them. What answers the call is the Hunger.

We could use the help. These damned Red Rooks! They destroyed my town and now they're trying to take over Crosswych.\n\nI made a vow. I will have my revenge. I'm going to rally the people of Crosswych to take back their town.

The townsfolk are scared. If they stick their necks out, they end up as slaves in the mines. Or worse.\n\nWe need the support of the town council. The few that haven't been dragged off to the mines need to show the people how to stand up to these curs.
I'll tell you what I can.

Wizard Benele is here on behalf of the Mages Guild. She claims there's a relic in the ruins that will help us defeat Angof, but magic is so unpredictable.\n\nAnd, truth be told, Wizard Benele can be easily distracted.
In hindsight, I may have spread the patrols too thin.\n\nI sent them to patrol the grounds around the redoubt, to protect the Gaudet Farm, and to guard the western ruins at Merovec's Folly.
Derp!
Schturfen!
Of course. I'll answer what I can.

If you can fight, and you know the difference between a man's head and a wolf's arse, we can use you. \n\nWe need to cut through the werewolves and link up with our troops in the western end of the camp.
Link up with Shaza and get our troops to the western gate. It might be enough to turn the tide. For now at least.\n\nYou clear us a path and get to my general. We have to take Camlorn back.

Am I sure I heard her voice outside our door, asking us to open it? Am I sure she leaped at my father and sank her teeth into his neck? Am I sure he told us to run with his dying breath?\n\nYes! It was her!

Then maybe she's insane. Would that make everything better? Maybe my father wasn't killed by an undead abomination, but by an ordinary madwoman.\n\nLook. You're right. She doesn't look like a bloodfiend. But she was definitely the one who attacked us.

Please, this isn't right! I've done … terrible things. But I'm still me—most of the time, anyway. I think it's only when the hunger takes me that my mind goes … somewhere else.\n\nPlease. I … I don't want to die.

Lieutenant Fairfax. Sometimes I thought he had a … fondness for me. I hope he didn't. I really hope he hated me. I can't think about what might have been.\n\nTell him not to look for me. I want him to hate me with all his heart.

I can do this. I can control it. It's only when I get hungry that I lose control.\n\nI'll live in the wilderness, far from people. I'll survive on animals. Never people! Never! I'm sure I can control it.

The Withered Hand has already sacked Lainlyn and risen its dead. Now they're looking for living, breathing allies.\n\nThey plan to contract with the Saltwalker Company mercenaries to protect their physically weak spellcasters.

The Saltwalkers are motivated by gold, but also honor. If you can convince them that contracting with the Hand would not only be financially risky, but dishonorable, they might see reason.\n\nWe've sent <<1>> ahead. Make contact with her first.
Perfect. Thank you. I'll put them on the wounded knights and Darien can lead them to safety. \n\nDo you have any more? I might be able to use them to clear the mist.

If I merge them and cast an amplification spell, I can increase the size of my protection ward. If I can get to a central point and hold the spell long enough, our troops will be able to get in.\n\nYou just need to defend me while I do it.

Good. Meet me at the center of the graveyard. \n\nWhen Angof notices what I'm doing, he's bound to send someone to stop me. If they interrupt me while I'm casting, the spell will fail. And that won't be good.
Follow me and stay close. It's not that far.
Stay close. You need to keep them off me until I finish.

The Nedic peoples were the ancient ancestors of our human kin here in Tamriel. Those who dwelled on the isle of Herne had long struggled to resist the Elves prior to the Ra Gada's arrival. Upon seeing the Yokudan sails, they took up the sword again.

Such things are difficult to imagine, yes. In those times Goblins were mighty beasts, and their cruelty was not tempered by cowardice as it is now. Their filthy strongholds littered the sands of Hammerfell like a pox when the Ra Gada arrived.
Well, Tu'whacca tells me that you must do battle with the spirits of the long-dead giant Goblinkin. To what end? I do not know. But only fools doubt Tu'whacca's wisdom.

The Song of Divad tells us that he and his band of Sword Singers worked their sacred forges and consulted eldritch tomes for many long years to create five great swords. With these blessed blades, the Ra Gada forever vanquished the giant Goblins.

It is the heart of Orcdom in Tamriel, settled at the foot of the Wrothgarian Mountains. It is a city of simple things—towering and cold. It has been razed and rebuilt countless times. The Orcs are a tenacious people.
You must face the ancient Orcish spectres in battle, and then summon and defeat their leader, General Theshaga. \n\nTu'whacca says there is great wisdom to be gleaned from this.

So I'll be the eyes and you'll be the … uh, everything else, I guess. I'm not used to having anyone else patrol with me, but this arm won't be able to hold a sword for a while.\n\nHave you ever done a scouting patrol before?

I know a few points where we can get a good look at what's going on inside the garrison. Lead me to them, and I'll tell you what I see.\n\nGuide me safely through the Imperial patrols, and protect me if we're spotted. Simple, eh? After you, then.
Velian killed me in a ritual circle in the fields east of town. That must be where he's taken Tamien. \n\nThe circle is surrounded by towering vines. Go quickly. Save my son.

The winds gather even now. The storm will appear here any moment—when it does, you must race. Follow the trail of the blue flames and reach the final flame before the storm does. \n\nAre you ready to test your fate, my friend?
You suggest I would do otherwise? I am honorable, even if you outlanders are not.\n\nIf <<1>> violates the terms of the duel, I will ... even the balance.
Good, because the commander will no longer talk to me. <<1>> called me an honorless mongrel for refusing to participate in their dispute duels.\n\nI didn't come here to play in their little arena.

See what you can do to drive a wedge between them. The chief is <<1>>. She's a sellsword, but values rules and honor.\n\nThe necromancer's name is <<2>>. He is doing his best innocent-mage-need-strong-warrior routine. Talk to them both.

I told the girl from the Guild what needs to happen. We've been speaking with the Hand for days now. If you want to interrupt these negotiations, you'll have to follow our custom: a duel of dispute.\n\nThis isn't just a brawl, though. We have rules.

The duel is one-on-one, with any spells or blades you have when the fight begins. No outside interference. Your guildmate can't help you, nor can Qabeh's undead or acolytes.\n\nThe drum in the center of camp begins the duel.

Ahh, pup. You just don't understand. The Withered Hand will soon rule all of Alik'r! The chief here? She understands that. She wants to be on the winning side of this war.\n\nYou've already lost, fool. You just don't know it yet.

Sep take them both! I don't trust <<1>> in the least. Who could trust a necromancer?\n\nYou know ... we could end this right now. If you keep him occupied, I can get the drop on him. Fair fight or decisive strike? You make the call.
Hmm. <<1>> wouldn't react well to treachery. You make a good point.\n\nYou'd better sound the drum and get this started. We don't want to give them any more time to finalize the contract.

When the stakes are this high, honor is a small price to pay. Go to the red carpet in the tent corner. Stand there and talk to <<1>>. He won't see me coming if you have his attention.\n\nI imagine <<2>> will be ... displeased. We should escape quickly.
I do not know. Is it? Is there even another wind storm to race?\n\nI am not sure what to believe. What do you believe?

Yes. Sir Lanis and his knights volunteered to come with me, but I only see Dame Alexine. \n\nThere must have been too many of us for the binding stone. This isn't good. The other knights could have been scattered throughout the crypts.

Good. But listen—there's only one way to get out of these crypts. You have to kill Angof.\n\nI don't have any other way to deal with his various protections and defenses now that I'm down here. He dies or we never leave. Those are our choices.

After you, then. You have good shoes, right? That's something knights never remember. After a couple hours walking in metal boots, even the toughest soldier will be crying with every step.\n\nTravel light. That's my creed.
They shouldn't be hard to find. They probably haven't bathed in weeks.\n\nIf we're downwind, we'll smell them. If we're upwind … well, we'll hear the flies around them. Lead on.

We met Wizard Benele outside. She said you'd use a binding stone to call us. \n\nThen suddenly we were down here, in the dark and surrounded by a horde of undead. The rest of the contingent must be somewhere nearby.

My best guess? They're deeper inside this maze of catacombs. \n\nIf you find the knights, send them this way. I'll hold the passage with this overconfident fool. He can't stop talking, but at least Darien's a decent enough fighter.

My best guess? Deeper inside the catacombs. \n\nIf you find any knights, send them this way. I'll hold the passage with this overconfident fool and his crazy friend. When they aren't flirting, they both fight like a whole platoon of Orcs.
It means we need another source of information, one who's been inside their camp.\n\nWe need to capture one of the Imperial pickets patrolling between <<1>> and the <<2>>.
You're the mad fool who went into the catacombs ahead of us, aren't you? \n\nBy the way, did the other knights make it? That binding spell seemed to throw me a bit short of the mark.

I'll head out as soon as I see a clear path.\n\nA word of warning, though. The lurcher in the chamber ahead is extremely tough. I'd keep it away from the totems surrounding it if you plan to challenge it.
Honestly? We beat the stuffing out of one of them, bash him on the head, and then tie him up before he recovers.\n\nTake this cudgel. Use it on an Imperial picket that you've beaten up a bit.

You speak truly. By raising the dead, Qabeh brought outside interference into the duel. He has no honor.\n\nYou've shown me what filth I was about to ally with. And to see the dead rise, the horrors of undeath firsthand ... my eyes are open.

My blades have already slaughtered the Withered Hand acolytes in camp. Their bodies burned quite well. We will do the same to any members of the Hand we see in the future.\n\nWhich just leaves you, <<1>>.
If I knew, don't you think I would've escaped by now?  \n\nAll I know is the tiles must be used in the right order, and the order was determined by time, whatever that means!
I am a Wizard of the Mages Guild - a difficult rank to achieve, if I may dispense with false modesty.\n\nNormally I'd be sequestered in the Mages Tower at Evermore, performing research.

I went to <<1>> with King Eamond because he asked me to. We often debated matters of strategic or political import. He valued my advice.\n\nI … regret my skills were unable to protect him. Eamond was an uncommon mind. I will miss him.

The King's Guard lost their leaders in the fall of the Garrison.

I am very intelligent, but I'm no military leader. I know that. They knew that. They asked me to lead them because Eamond trusted me, and they trusted him.

How could I refuse them?

They're Eamond's - I mean, the sovereign of Evermore's household troops.\n\nThey're bodyguards, if you wish - trained, equipped and paid for by the Mournoth family. Only the finest and most loyal soldiers are invited to join.
There were two dozen knights before the battle at the Garrison. Now there are only eleven - and me.\n\nAnd I'm not technically a member of the Guard.
But you ran against the storm … you won! You saw it just as I did.\n\nWait a minute. I think I know what this is about. Did Hadoon send you?
After each trap fires, there's a brief moment when you can disarm it. \n\nDuring this moment you have to defeat its guardian. It's the only way.
So I'm not the only one left? That's good to hear.\n\nI'm pretty exhausted, but I'll see if I can find them after I rest up for a few moments.

Indeed I am! I know you may not have much experience taking risks like this, but sometimes you just have to follow your instincts!\n\nRegardless, I owe you my thanks. Why, if Stibbons were stuck as a statue forever, I don't know what I'd do!

He is a good friend, but he thought this fate business was all nonsense.\n\nThe woman had prescribed his fate as well, but he did not believe it. Nonetheless, I believe he did go into the desert to see. Perhaps you should seek him out.
Yes, please. Some healing is just what I needed.
I've already agreed to duel you. We have nothing more to discuss, pup. \n\nEither way, you should watch your back. These mercenaries will soon be an extension of the Hand.
Ah, you must be one of Vargos' new recruits. We could certainly use the help, if you're willing to throw in with us for a while.

We've got a literal undead uprising on our hands! Our patrols meet them in the wilds while our primary mage, Gabrielle Benele, searches for a magical relic that will turn the tide.\n\nBut I'm concerned. A few of the patrols haven't returned.

The Lion Guard doesn't usually look for outside help, but desperate times call for desperate measures. Do what you can to help any patrols you come across.\n\nAnd if you run into Mage Benele, maybe you can help her out, as well.

I'd love to, but there's some kind of barrier protecting the crypts at Cath Bedraud. \n\nUnless Wizard Benele can get us through that barrier, we can't get to Angof. And the undead will just keep coming.
Yes, I am. Sir Etienne brought us out here, and when he was wounded, I took command.\n\nI've secured a fallback perimeter, such that it is. The Reachmen are leaving us alone for the moment.
You can't understand. How could you?

You are clever, my friend. If I prove fate does not control us, it does not matter that fate led me to this truth. \n\nIf a goat introduces itself to a hungry coyote, it will be consumed. Fate may play a hand, but only to a point.

Could one prove or disprove an illusion? Such proof could be an illusion itself. Our debate will soon chase its own tail.\n\nMy good friend Anjan would tell you that fate pulls our strings. You can hear his musings firsthand near Rain Catcher Fields.
