A riddle? No! The riddle. The one these ruins whisper every night! The one that hums through the walls when the sun beats upon them!\n\nYou know whereof I speak. You've read the three inscriptions. If you haven't, what are you waiting for?
We have boats to and from <<1>> daily.\n\nFor a modest fee, you should have no trouble finding a crew to sail you across Iliac Bay.
I believe that much is all I am allowed, to relive it over and over. To torment myself. Hermaeus Mora loves that I am sure.
They're here? That's great news. I'll go find them in a moment.\n\nBe careful around this spirit. I think he's cursed me already. My mind is blue and cold.

Yes. The picket must be sufficiently wounded for it to work. Don't kill him.\n\nThe cudgel will merely stun him. Once he's down, you can tie him up. You'll need to work fast before he regains his senses. Then we'll march him back to camp.
I don't regret resisting those bandits. If Sellan's organizing a revolt, I'm in. \n\nI'll see you outside.
Sellan, eh? I heard he ran with the Red Rooks at one point. \n\nHe must have seen the light when they sacked Eagle's Brook. All right, I'll join him.
I was on my way to tell Sellan I'd join him when the Red Rooks captured me. I've been down here ever since. It's time to finish what I started. \n\nThank you.
It's his own sword. I shouldn't have left him alone.\n\nPlease, look around to see if there are any traces of his killer!

Yes, but she wasn't here when I arrived. She may have gone out to find a poultice, or herbs, or whatever she needed to treat his pain.\n\nI hope she's all right, though she should've waited for me to get here before leaving Sir Etienne alone.
I'll find Sellan and join his resistance. But first, you have to promise me something. Foreman Blaise has got to die. He's the cruelest Red Rook in the mine. \n\nPromise me you'll kill him.

Sellan's got a good plan. I'll go help him. But you need to do something for me, too.\n\nForeman Blaise has got to die. We'll never break the rest of the Red Rooks while he's still in charge down here. Promise me you'll kill him.

Consider me a member of the resistance. I'll go find Sellan immediately. But you need to do something for me. You need to kill Foreman Blaise.\n\nThat cruel Red Rook keeps the mines in constant fear. Kill him and we can take back what's ours.
I came here as an envoy to plead the case against the Withered Hand. I don't care how much <<1>> protests of honor. \n\nI won't be ripped apart by ghouls to satisfy her ego.

Oh really? Fine, I'll do as the chief requests. I agree to duel a Fighters Guild representative. Sound the drum. Let's end this farce. The Hand shall be triumphant.\n\nIn the end, it doesn't matter. I will have their swords one way or another.
I don't know exactly, but the Bloodthorn cultist told me about the guardians.\n\nWatch out for a summoned creature, an impassable trap, and a warrior spirit bound to Angof's service.
All I know is that Angof drew on the collected power of his cultists to summon the creature. I hear that it's more plant than beast.\n\nAnd, of course, it's terrible to behold.
Actually, I couldn't get anything out of the cultist about the trap. Sorry. You're on your own with that one.

It seems that when Angof first came to power, a certain knight took offense and tried to kill him. \n\nAngof captured the knight's spirit and bound it to serve him. I understand he's extremely powerful and not at all happy about the situation.
Good. This should buy us enough time to act.
The shard-key is bound to my spirit, as surely as I am bound to guard it. \n\nBut I wonder, will you listen to a riddle? A useful riddle?

What cannot be said directly may be hinted at. Listen, then. "Rot and death are Angof's guise; living flesh holds his demise." \n\nI must release the shard to the one who brings me what the living flesh beyond this crypt holds.
I cannot say directly, only through riddle. \n\nSeek what differs in the next room. Take what the living flesh holds. Then unbind me with it.
Yes, but take care what you say. The words must be repeated exactly as written.
No, you fool! The stone! Look at the … ahh!
No, fool! The stone! Read the … ahh!
Ah, it's done. Thank Stendarr. \n\nHere, take the shard-key. I am free to ascend at last. Destroy Angof. Avenge me and the others that have fallen victim to his crimes.
That seems unlikely, unless they are in truly dire straits.\n\nYou've piqued my curiosity. Where did you get this information?
Ah. That's what the noise was? I confess, this baffles me.\n\nWhat spy would risk handing secrets over to his enemies by bringing a journal full of valuable intelligence along on a mission?

"We?" You aren't part of our army. "I" need to halt this raid, and "I" will redouble the guard on the depot as soon as its practical.\n\nIf you wish to help the guards in the meantime, speak to <<1>> at the supply depot to the southeast.

Amateur spies don't get sent to infiltrate enemy camps. That's a task for someone with experience.\n\nIf the Imperials would send such fools among us, they must be desperately short of veteran soldiers.

What? Don't joke with me. This is the most boring job in the camp, next to doing the laundry.

We're facing an attack? Damn! They'll probably want me to warn the camp or something. I'll miss everything!

Wait! Do you hear something?
Argh! I'll go sound the alarm. You stop them from carrying off any of the crates!\n\nAnd save some of those thieves for me, or I'll kill you!
Hmph. Got my hopes up for nothing. If you want to sit here and be bored with me, help yourself.\n\nI'd kill for a jug of ungorth right now.
No ... Gall and pox! They took it! I got here as they were leaving and they struck me down as I tried to stop them.\n\nPlease, get Bonerender back!
I'll be fine. Just ... just get the weapon and kill the leader of the Reachmen. I'm sure that he will amass a huge army behind him now that he wields that power.

She's the head of the Pellingare smugglers. She runs the whole operation with the help of her brother, <<1>>.\n\nI'm positive she's holed up somewhere in these sewers. Be careful if you go after her, though - she didn't rise this far on wits alone.
The Imperial commander, <<1>>, tortured me. He broke something in my hand and wrist, and I told him where to find the others.\n\nI put my comfort over theirs. <<2>> heard me, and she'll never forget.
He commands this group. I don't know their affiliation. They're here for the mines, and that's all he cares about. He'll keep it running no matter how many conscripts he kills.

Onsi's Breath is the most lucrative mine in the whole of Bangkorai.\n\nThis is why the name it carries comes from great Onsi, as it yields much and more for the making of weapons and armor. That's why <<1>> took this place by force.
Morwha's blessed bosom! Loath as I am to send you from one danger to the next ….\n\nThe Seventh Legion's captives in the mine need your deft aid too, if you're willing to go on.
The others have all collapsed in their tents. They're exhausted! But I wanted to welcome you back. \n\nAnd Sir Lanis wants to talk to you. He's telling the Lion Guard commander what happened.
Who knows? Maybe he wants to give you a medal or something.\n\nWell, go on. We'll be fine. I promise.

<<1>> in Sentinel sells good lizards. And <<2>> near Bergama has sold a few good racers.\n\nUnfortunately, I only carry one lizard suited for racing—<<a:3>>. He's not fast enough to be a winner, but you never know!
Excellent! Remember, he's not the fastest of the bunch. But maybe in the right hands he'll do well.
I do want this track to succeed, but <<1>> has to admit I know what I'm doing, too.
A lizard needs to be light, but muscular. Their shape can affect their speed, as can their diet.\n\nI've got something for the latter, if you're interested.

No. Only my skull was crushed, and this by the tip of my partner's pickaxe.\n\nWe finally found something of value down here—gems. But in that very moment, I saw the price of my life's blood in her beautiful eyes.

Yes, and keenly do I feel the need for revenge. In death, I have been granted this opportunity. I have poured my hatred into the gems we found.\n\nGive them to her. Give them to Samsi, and she will be repaid for her treachery.
We're pretty isolated out here. The Red Rooks came in and took over without any interference from the Lion Guard. Our local watch was no match for them.

The Yokudan inscriptions are mysterious. Frankly, I'm baffled by them. But Mareh has dropped hints that he knows what they mean. \n\nI'm sure he could tell me what I want to know, if I could only figure out how to give him what he wants.

They contain the key to the antidote for my stoneflesh potion.\n\nSomehow, the gargoyles inspired the early Redguards to experiment with their own flesh and bone. If I could only understand their cryptic inscriptions, I could master their alchemy.

No. Well, yes. Kind of?\n\nI'm not a knight or a man-at-arms, if that's what you're asking. None of us in the militia are. We're levied from Evermore's citizens when there's an emergency. When there aren't enough real warriors.

I didn't mean to be. I'm just a butcher. I don't know anything about fighting!\n\nOur real leader was Felix Sergond, the tavern keeper. He at least knew how to beat up drunken orcs. He died at the Garrison, trampled by one of the Gallants' horses.

Well, you've got good armor. I have a shirt.\n\nYou've got swords, and axes, or whatever it is you've got. I've never even seen some of these new-fangled weapons before. I've got a grain scythe that would be ruined if I actually used it on someone.

You know what is here?\n\nThree noblewomen that are smarter than me, stronger than me, and angrier than me. They expect me to contribute advice, then ignore it. I wish they'd let me go back to the miltia camp ….

You have to understand. The militia, we're just … crow fodder. We're not expected to do anything more than get in the way of the enemy.\n\nLady Alimah led a charge into the Imperials' flank. Some of us got in her way. She just … went through us.

There's no reason you should be. If you don't mind my saying - what are we to you? You pass by dozens of folk like me every day without giving us a thought.\n\nSorry. I guess it's decent of you to say, whether or not you mean it.

Well, you've got all that enchanted jewelry, fancy … I don't even know what that's called … and whatnot. I have a shirt.\n\nYou've got magic. I've a grain scythe that would be ruined if I actually had to use it on someone.

You know what is here?\n\nThree noblewomen that are smarter than me, stronger than me, and angrier than me. They expect me to contribute advice, then ignore it. I wish they'd let me go back to the miltia camp ….
My leg still hurts, but at least the swelling's gone down.\n\nDid you learn anything about … what we spoke of earlier?

You did all you could. <<1>> was truly mad. I don't think anyone could have stopped him once his paranoia took root.\n\nIt's important that her death did not end the Daggerfall Covenant. She could never find rest if her father's legacy was destroyed.

So that's where all the food was coming from! No wonder they wanted to keep things quiet.\n\nI'd better keep this information to myself, or there'll be an uproar. I just hope they know what they're doing.
I'll be fine now. Here. Take my lucky thingamabob.\n\nThose guys kept talking about Bonerender. Why would I know anything about rending bones? I'm a farmer!
Yes, but I'll be fine now. Here. Take my lucky thingamabob.\n\nThose guys kept talking about Bonerender.
Yah. I'll be fine. Here. Take my lucky thingamabob.\n\nThose guys kept talking about Bonerender.
By Mauloch's sulfurous hatred! And here I thought that traitor and bandit was our only hope … where's <<1>>, that bastard?\n\nLeft me here to rot. I'll rot him!
He did, did he? Wait till I get my hands around his throat!\n\nThe key to these shackles is kept in their surveyor's tent on the hillside across from us. Free me, so I can kill <<1>>!
You want me to fight with you instead of leaving to warn the rest of the camp? That would be irresponsible! There's no way I could possibly agree to ….\n\nYeah, sure. Let's do it.

I'm going through my first change soon. It'll be my first time as a werewolf.\n\nEveryone's experience is different. It's a kindness to keep me away from everyone, really, until they know how this will affect me.
Yes, well … we have a need for it. If Kerbol hasn't told you, then it's not my place to say more than that.\n\nI need to get back to work.

Good for you. I don't. You know what I want? I want to go home. 

I want to meet my wife at the door, yell at the kids for knocking things over, and sit down to a warm dinner with a cold ale.

Think you could arrange that, you Covenant turd?

That would be great, if I wasn't tied to a pole! I can't exactly hold a spoon like this.\n\nIt's been a long time since I had a hot meal with real meat: not salted, but with blood in it. Camp meals keep me on my feet, but leave me longing for home.

Warm ale? Pah! Only savages drink warm ale! I hate campaigning outside of Cyrodiil. Why did we even come here?\n\nAnyway, how am I supposed to drink that with my hands tied behind my back? You expect me to lap it up like a dog? Would that amuse you?
Ha! Easy to talk tough when your enemy is tied up, eh?\n\nGo to Oblivion, Convenant dog. I have nothing to say to you or any of your barbarian friends.
By the Divines! Ah, Stendarr, help me endure this!\n\nCovenant pig! I'll never be able to hold a sword again!
I'll kill you! I'll kill you!\n\nI'll break every bone in your body! I'll carve you into mincemeat!

Empty words. We both know I'm not leaving here alive, not after all the murders on both sides.\n\nThis is no sporting war, no contest over honor. This is survival. The winner is the one left standing. Just admit my next meal is my last meal.
Oh? I'm not as easily bribed as you expected, am I?\n\nSo it's to be torture now, isn't it? The older soldiers say your kind is like that.

Stew would be great, if I wasn't tied to a pole! I can't exactly hold a spoon like this.\n\nIt's been a long time since I had a hot meal with real meat: not salted, but with blood in it. Camp meals keep me on my feet, but leave me longing for home.
And there's an old Imperial tradition of poisoning your enemy's food and drink. It's long been considered the "civilized" way for nobles to kill each other. I'm sure you've heard of that.

Warm ale? Pah! Only savages drink warm ale! I hate campaigning outside of Cyrodiil. Why did we even come here?\n\nAnyway, how am I supposed to drink that with my hands tied behind my back. You expect me to lap it up like a dog? Would that amuse you?

The only way you can get your information is by torturing me?

Ha! Imperials are spit on here. Your people say we're cruel … evil ….

You know what's cruel? Hurting someone because you're too stupid to think of another way to get what you want!
By the Divines! Ah, Stendarr, help me endure this!\n\nCovenant pig! I'll never be able to hold a sword again!
I'll kill you! I'll kill you!\n\nI'll break every bone in your body! I'll carve you into mincemeat!

I'm here because I was ordered to be here. I'm here because my comrades are here.

The nobles tell me I don't have to know their reasons. Torture me all day. That's all I can tell you.

Heh. I'll probably make something up if you hurt me enough.
"Start over"? Are you … are you joking? After what you just did to me?

No. You would do worse to my comrades.

I know what you want, Covenant scum. You want a golden road to retake <<1>>. If I tell you anything, my friends will bleed and burn.

I'd rather die than kill them.

You … you'd deny me even the mercy of death?

When we fall, the nobles raise us to keep fighting. Our oaths of fealty bind beyond the grave. It wasn't always like this. When the Empire died, parts of us died too.

What do you want to know?
You … can you promise that? If I tell you what I know, you'll make the attack quick and clean? No execution of prisoners? No burning them out?\n\nI know our nobles would see them die for no reason.

Orcs, too? Ha! What does it matter? Go ahead. Call them in. It doesn't matter anymore.

Do whatever you want to me. I'm not going to turn on my fellows. I'm not saying anything else to you.

You've failed. We're done.
We're low on supplies, low on soldiers, and a long way from home.\n\nI can't tell you what the commanders are planning. The nobles don't share their plans with us common soldiers.
We're a private people. Our history is our own and no business of yours.
<Inside the knapsack is a rough map with directions from Sentinel to the mines. The pack also includes some old clothes, half-eaten rations, and a journal.>
Too boring. Rules. Threats. Watch duty. Feh! You know what would be fun? A party! \n\nAnd I didn't even bring a hat.
The fight for Balfiera is more than just capturing the Fort at the center! There are many other aspects to war on this small slab of rock.
Battle Tasks are always running because the fight is always changing! Be on the lookout for flags that mark key locations to capture every fifteen to twenty minutes!
Fort Balfiera is fueled by support structures we call Resources.  There are three of these per keep: a Farm, Mine and Lumbermill.  Capture these to cripple the keep!
The Fort is the primary objective on this island.  Capture Fort Balfiera, and our entire Covenant reaps the rewards both here on the island and abroad.
Speak to the Commander and Skirmisher to get proper orders for tasks here in Balfiera. Be warry though as the enemy may have the same orders!

I don't know, but it can't be good. They're up there calling on Vaermina, the Daedric Prince of Nightmares… putting me to sleep and talking about summoning… something.\n\nIf it's what I saw in my dreams, it's something terrible.

Without a doubt. I even heard King Emeric's name…. We need to warn him. We need to warn everyone.\n\nI told the village constable, but he's more worried about these slavers. He doesn't understand. These people worship Vaermina.

Hadir had to recruit a mercenary? Not a good sign. Let me see those messages.\n\nBy the Eight! The Dominion's planning a full-scale assault! These messages, they're waiting for orders to attack. We have to stop the commander from issuing that order.
No more than most men. She's the Daedric Prince of nightmares and evil dreams.\n\nShe's … horrible, but some people actually worship her.

For a whole army? Through the desert? There's no baggage train in Mundus long enough for that!

The nobles insisted we could forage off the land like we do in other campaigns. Anyone who doubted was … silenced.

They planned a one-way journey.

We had a few hundred, mostly raw recruits. There aren't many veterans, but it's not the living you have to worry about.\n\nThe nobles had us gather corpses. At this point, half our army is dead … and the dead don't need to eat.

I don't know. I told you: they don't explain their strategies to people like me.\n\nThey made sure we captured wells along our advance west from Colovia. We had some water, but we're spreading out our rations by making soup.

No, its a recent change. Necromancy was no more tolerated in Cyrodiil than it was anywhere else.\n\nWhen the Empire fell four years ago, many of the nobles started openly practicing necromancy. It's spread since then. It's almost a mark of culture.

How should I know? Why don't you tell me about your supplies and troop size? Then I could guess.\n\nWhen we drove the defenders out of your fortress, they were in a panic. They were leaderless, but it looks like they've reorganized.

We never had many to begin with. The rest died in battle or from the heat.\n\nBefore we left Colovia, the nobles drafted thousands of people into the army. They didn't get much training. They were just there to fill out our numbers.
Divines, yes! These Bretons will be the death of us all.\n\nJust look at their armor! That tells you all you need know.

There's so much of it! Layers of metal plates that weigh as much as the warriors who bear it. You can't feel the wind on your skin or in your hair.\n\nThat's how they think. Heavy, ponderous, obsessed with defense. That is not how warriors fight!

On the balls of my feet, on the tips of my horse's hooves!\n\nAn army must be like sand on the wind, light and swift. It should seek the cracks in the enemy's defenses and blow through them, wearing away the edges so more can follow.

Mine and no one else's! The Gallantry of Hallin's Stand, the finest horsemen east of the Abecean Sea!\n\nWe came to aid the Garrison. But defending walls is not our way of fighting. I lost many of my fine stallions - and a few horses, too.

It is a town southwest of here. To our shame, it was occupied by the Imperials - dogs and sons of dogs!\n\nBut they do not hold it happily. Our cities are roses - fair to behold, but if you clutch them you taste only their thorns.

Gallants. Horse-warriors. The Breton call us knights, but we don't fight like their knights. We wear leathers, turn quickly, fire our bows from the saddle. The wear steel and wield steel. Their horses can only move quickly in a straight line.
Greed and cowardice have a price. She craves this tomb's treasures, but she wants you to take the risks. \n\nI would consider this justice.

There's a tower at each of the cardinal points. Each tower is the focus for a powerful mystical shield.\n\nThe four shields overlap to create an area free of necromantic energy. You'll have to speak to <<1>> if you want to know more.
Ge epea veyn! Eve as gravia lambe ye lael.
Ne goria! Heca! Delia ye metana Gandra Lambe, sino.
Yes, I can make it. I even have information to pass on to my commander, so the scouting mission won't be a complete failure.

I told you my father was a bastard, but what he did happened many years ago. I had no part in that! Why should I have to suffer for what he did?\n\nIt doesn't matter. Listen, you need to convince the ghost to move on.

Please. Convince this spirit that we suffered enough.\n\nMy mother ordered the hired guards to reclaim this place no matter the cost. It's out of my hands. These men will kill anyone who gets in their way.
Yes, I think so. \n\nBut what about Cecile? She was ahead of us and I saw her get captured. They took her toward their camp on the beach. We can't leave without her.
Not too badly. Luckily, you got here ahead of their interrogator. \n\nThanks for freeing me. Now we have to look for the others.

It will, but to prevent you from freeing every miner within, I suggest that you seek out one captive in particular.\n\nHe used to run this mine, before they took it from him. They still allow him freedom of the camp unlike the others, however!
That's … just what I was counting on! Right, now I know how to adjust the concoction to make a working antidote.\n\nSoon Stibbons will be right as rain, thanks to my brains and your brawn!

I know you mean no insult with your questions. I just thought I'd be rid of my past by now.\n\nWhen we first met, she was Lady Arzhela of Wayrest: a firebrand married to King Eamond some twenty years back. That seems so long ago now.
I could help you figure out what happened here, if you tell me what you've found. \n\nI might not have your eye for detail, but I knew Sir Etienne well.

For peace, if only for a generation. Lady Arzhela's marriage bound <<1>> and <<2>> in kinship.\n\nBlood's a hard bond to break, even in the most trying times. That was reason enough for the marriage. I think in time, she even came to love him.
Me? I was a simple gardener for the castle in Evermore. Lady Arzhela sat out there when she was homesick.\n\nSometimes, she'd talk to me about Wayrest and her old life. We became … quite close.

Oh, I knew the gossips would've wagged their wild tongues and ruined the queen's reputation. I cared for her too much to let that happen, so I left.\n\nNow fate's given me a second chance to help my Lady Arzhela … and I will.
He-he did …? I-I do not know what you speak of. \n\nI would never kill Haidar! He was my partner, my friend, my mentor …. Please … I must be going.
A lesson …? Yes. Fine. Maybe. A lesson that this life was never meant for me.\n\nPlease, just forget we met here … forget all this. I-I'm just going to leave.
Is this another test? I'm not trying to escape, I told you!\n\nI am not leaving this mine. Nobody else knows how to reinforce versus structural collapse!

Oh, you can believe that I will. If this is part of some scheme, it's not a very good one. \n\nOnly one thing would turn this mine over more quickly than just striking the chains from these miners, after what's been done to them.

It is, and we're on high alert right now. A Baandari smuggler named Ildani escaped from the Guard, and we suspect she might try to reclaim her contraband.\n\nIf you see anything suspicious, let me know.

You met her? She asked you to come and steal back her goods, didn't she? Perfect. This time we can catch her and her buyers.\n\nIf you'll help, according to statute twenty-two, I can offer you a reward.

Downstairs? Just now? Damn it! That has to be Ildani! I could catch her right now, but according to regulation twelve, I can't leave my post ….\n\nI've … I've just got to make an exception. Will you watch this area for a few minutes?

Fantastic. You'll be acting as a deputized, non-uniformed city guard—as permitted by regulation eleven. \n\nYou'll take Ildani's goods and offer to deliver them to her buyers. We'll be watching, and once we have all the buyers, we'll close in.
Ah! You do spotless work, walker. Now the goods must be delivered though.\n\nIldani worries that the guards might be looking for her, but risks can sometimes be fun, yes?
We use a code. Just say, "Alik'r is so hot. I'd rather be elsewhere."\n\nAfter you've delivered the goods, meet me on the bridge in the center of the city.

Ah, you are so kind! You think Ildani is sleek, yes? \n\nSorry. No sweetmeat for you, but Ildani will reward if you deliver wares to buyers: a servant at the inn, an apprentice at the smithy, and an alchemist at the market.
At last! My patrons were getting anxious. I take it you have a package for me?
I understand. I also hate the heat, my friend.\n\nShould I assume you have something for me?
Yes, it's unseasonably warm from here to Bergama. The coastal winds blow in a southerly direction, and Lainlyn has the best restaurant in the desert.\n\nYou have the package?
You made it just in time. Those serpents are looking at me and sticking out their tongues. I think they were licking their lips!\n\nLet's go!
Go to the back of the mine, near the exit shaft. If you don't see him, just start ringing the cave-in warning bell.\n\nWhen he shows up to see what's going on, finish him off!

He's at the back of the mine, near the exit shaft. If you don't see him there, just start ringing the cave-in warning bell.\n\nWhen Blaise shows up to see what's happening, you can finish the bootlicker right there and then!
He's at the back of the mine, near the exit shaft. If you don't see him there, just start ringing the cave-in warning bell.\n\nHe'll come running to investigate and you can ambush him!
<<<1>> begins to stir.>

They say I spent too much time with solutions and mixtures, that they dulled my senses. Nonsense! I can see and hear better than ever!\n\nThat skull over your shoulder is grinning at you, by the way. I think he's plotting against you. Yes, he is.

She's a thrall of the Nereid, the one who stole a valuable artifact from these ruins. We believe it served as the keystone to this Ayleid conduit.\n\nI wanted to speak to the Nereid directly. You're a stranger. What is your part in this?

Quite dangerous, my mortal friend. Though the Ayleid people are long dead, their traps and weapons remain.\n\nTime has worn away the safeguards, however. The backlash from tampering with these traps without taking precautions could be deadly.

She's manipulating them into destroying centuries of knowledge with their water worship. They endanger their own lives in the process!\n\nWe have asked them to return the Water Stone and leave these ruins. We will not ask again.

Feh! The peasants and beggars can worship the Nereid elsewhere. We have come to study, and possibly prevent, a disaster far beyond anything your people have seen.\n\nYou are not beholden to this worship-crazed Nereid. Would you help us be rid of her?

It's refreshing to hear you say that. None know the depth of secrets hidden within the archives. To see this Ayleid marvel, to understand its purpose ….\n\nYou are not in thrall to this crazed Nereid. Would you help us be rid of her?

With the city liberated from Faolchu, some of the Camlorn Guard came up this way looking for a fight. A noble named Darien was acting as their leader.\n\nHe seemed very angry with Angof—something about werewolves.

A wise choice, and one you will not regret. This artifact will allow you to speak with the corpses of the Nereid's victims. They lie unburied within her realm. \n\nLearn more about her Water Stone and anything else we can use against her.
Do not speak to <<1>>. She speaks lies.

That's an odd question. I've known the duchess since we were children. We grew up together.

Now she's dead. Nothing will ever fill the hole in my heart.

I'll take some comfort in seeing her here at home with her family. It's where she needs to be.
At the moment I am. My partner stepped away to go moisten the sand.\n\nBut if you're planning to pull a fast one, know I am authorized by statute six to use deadly force if necessary.

Farwatch is a lightly defended position in a remote corner of Covenant territory.\n\nIf they could establish a base here, they could strike where they pleased, taking their pick of vulnerable targets.
How fortunate for you. But no one ever considers the wants and desires of a ghost.\n\nOh, very well. Let's get this over with.
Wonderful. It's just the thing to take the edge off this heat. <<1>> likes to take credit for the success of the inn. \n\nI'm guessing my little service is what really keeps them coming back!

Thank the gods. Better late than never, I suppose. I swear that <<1>> works on a totally different schedule than the rest of us. I was getting desperate!\n\nBelieve me, an apprenticeship doesn't really pay off my debts.
Of course. There's just the matter of our fee and you're on your way.

Scouting. Good eyes, like an eagle, or a magpie. \n\nMadame's coin purse sparkled. It sparkled to me. Then came lashings. Then sitting, doing nothing. Then Madame Lurue and the dancers. Like a party … only not fun.
What a presumptuous question! Such temerity!\n\nYou are very rude, just like my brothers. They bound me here. They were jealous of my powers, my stature!
Excellent. I was starting to wonder if <<1>> finally got her tail caught in a trap.\n\nThings would be … complicated between us if the guards caught up with her.
Yes! I intended to aid the Direnni against the Alessians. I hoped to get land from King Ralethiel as a reward.\n\nMy brothers bound me here so I could not participate. They never returned for me!
<The reliquary contains a pendant shaped like a golden tongue. It hangs from a slender golden chain.>
<The slightest touch causes the pendant to disintegrate. You hear a rising chorus of whispers, like a sudden wind. Then the whispers fall silent.>
In truth, I do not know. My people are long gone. \n\nI could move on to Aetherius or I could remain in Tamriel. See what became of the land after the Alessians were defeated.
Your words ring true. I should move on.
Indeed, it might!\n\nI must admit, the very idea fills me with a feeling I have almost forgotten. I feel … excitement!

To kill everyone in the city … it is unthinkable. There would be no political gain from such a thing … no, the people responsible for such a thing would only be motivated to murder.\n\nThat is why we will show them no mercy.

Know then the burden of my dishonor!\n\nSayeedeh never loved me, but I was blind. When she and <<1>> announced their betrothal, I believed he had forced her. I slew him, an innocent man, and realized my mistake only upon hearing her cries.
I'm disappointed in you. Citizen volunteers don't grow on trees, you know. \n\nNow wait a moment while I find someone else to help you.

Sentinel would be vulnerable without water. The nobles would dry up without a full pitcher at hand.\n\nStill, cultists tampering with the rain catchers ... too terrible to consider! If they can strike here, are any of us safe?

I thought my death would cleanse it, but as you can see, the blade now draws only more blood.\n\nThere will be no peace to any who claim it. And so, I put it away from my tomb, that there might be distance between it and me.

Too long. Sometimes allies, mostly rivals. To the Imperials, we are all the enemy, regardless of what we were before.\n\nLikewise, they are now our enemy, above any other! Hopefully, <<1>> hates them more than she hates me at this point.
The Withered Hand attacked and corrupted the temple. They raised the honored ancestors from <<1>> to attack the city. \n\nMany died. Many more fled. A few may remain inside in need of help.

The High Temple of Satakalaam was built to serve the Motalion Necropolis. The honored dead's journey to the necropolis begins here. \n\nThat is an important part of the ceremony. Corrupting the High Temple weakens the consecration of the necropolis.
Friends? Friends? He's a liar, a thief, and a cheat! What kind of friend is that?\n\nI may be a bandit, but I've got standards, unlike that desert low-life!

They did? Well, I'm glad to hear that, at least. Forgive me. I have been languishing alone for a long time. Can you release me?\n\nYou would need to destroy the relics that bind me—the Seal of Anchoring, the Animus Needle, and the Soul Prison.
And I pray to Stendarr that you put a blade through his heart. \n\nGive Angof what you gave Faolchu. Then maybe we can put this nightmare behind us and rebuild our lives.

Darien? Know him? Not really. Well ….\n\nOh, all right! I know him. Darien and I were once … that is … I've spent some time with him. Before. In the past. Way, way past. If you see him … oh, never mind. What's that look for?

When the werewolves attacked, the damn Bloodthorns appeared inside the city. It was as if they'd been here all along. I think they even opened the gates for the werewolves. \n\nThey had a plan and they executed it perfectly.
Prepare to defend me for 30 seconds.

This widget sets me to be your follower. I will despawn if you get too far away from me, or logout.\n\nYou should make your own actionlist for this, but you can reuse the action lists attached to each of these prompts.

The Seventh Legion soldiers here have been ordered to find and loot the Dwarven city of Volenfell for an ancient device their Chancellor seeks. \n\nI've forged new orders that will send them back to Cyrodiil instead, but they lack an official seal.

You saved my people from their zealots. They will not stop until all that I am is destroyed in the name of their insatiable thirst for knowledge.\n\nYet all is not lost. You have diverted the tides in our favor. Come, and you shall be rewarded.

Lorelia. She is a Nereid. She is the water spirit of Lake Halcyon. \n\nLorelia says the Primeval Seekers have misled you. She is an element of nature, seeking only to foster life. She told me to explain her purposes here.

The landscape of Tamriel is ever-changing. The desert south of here is expanding and will someday overtake this area too. Lake Halcyon has already begun to slowly dry up. \n\nLorelia only seeks to prevent that, to keep the lake and the forest alive.

These ruins hold ancient secrets and relics of power. With them, Lorelia can create a Water Stone—an everlasting source of water that can keep Lake Halcyon alive for all eternity.\n\nMyself, the Rain Disciples, and the wisps aid her in this mission.
Excellent! I knew you would come through for me! \n\nThis is good. Very good. Now there's really nothing the Primeval Seekers can do to stop us.

Yes. We have everything we need, but you must be the one to create it. I cannot touch the Water Stone without risk of losing myself. Our natures are too similar. \n\nYou will do this for me, though, won't you?

Lorelia … she told me to wait for you to bring the Water Stone, but one of the Primeval Seekers—a Dremora—snuck up and attacked me!\n\nShe made me tell her where Lorelia's sanctum is, and she said she was going … she was going to kill her!
In the western cavern … take the back passage up. That leads to Lorelia's private sanctum.\n\nPlease, hurry! If that fiend kills her, I'll never forgive myself.
Would you like a child or a follower?
What kind?
What kind?

It did. We were buried here in Cath Bedraud together. We were at peace—all of us. Until this dark reach magic arrived and began to corrupt the spirits of the dead.\n\nNow look around you. They wander at this sorcerer's command. Even my husband.

Bring the ring with you. There might still be a link from the living to the dead.\n\nIf you can use it on the undead in the area, I'll attempt to create a link and draw their spirit out. You'll need to finish them quickly once it happens though.

The magic has already taken its toll. I just wish to have my husband back with me. Please, you have to help me.\n\nI can show you a way to find him. In the process we might be able to free some others from this torment as well.

I wish I knew. I followed the knights in here without thinking. My guards started gasping and falling to the ground, just like the knights. But not me.\n\nThese are the only survivors, but I don't think they'll last much longer.
Better grab a couple of extras, just in case anyone else shows up while you're gone.\n\nI'll wait here and protect the knights from the Bloodthorns.

The mist is thicker toward the gate. They won't survive passing through it again. \n\nBut the mist doesn't seem to affect the necromancers. Those amulets must protect them. Kill a few, take their amulets, and give them to the knights.

I was so scared! He changed then, and explained what would happen to me. He told me about <<1>>. \n\nI didn't believe it at first, so I waited. People who heard about my attack made it clear I wasn't welcome. By then, it was too late. So here I am.
It was an accident. While hunting rabbits, I stumbled onto a feeding werewolf. He instinctively attacked, but stopped before he caused me serious harm.\n\nUnfortunately, he'd already bitten me.

Well, not you exactly. But certainly someone like you. Brave, capable, strong. Carries a well-worn weapon.\n\nThe Lion Guard needs you! Go to our fortified camp up on the hill. Look for Commander Ales and tell him Vargos sent you.
The Lion Guard goes where it needs to go. And we need to be here. We're barely keeping Angof's undead forces from flowing out of Cath Bedraud.\n\nThe rotting bastards are damn tough, that's for sure.
But I haven't seen anyone …

Yes. I'll stay out here and keep watch. \n\nTake whatever relics you can find and look for some sign as to where the Nereid herself might be hiding. Even without a Water Stone, she's too dangerous to be left alive.
<The remnants of smashed relics litter the altar.>

Liar! It's not the relics you want! You want to steal my memory essences, don't you?\n\nToo late. I've already infused them … into myself! I am the Water Stone! Once I activate the shrine, I'll flood the ruins and rid myself of all you vermin.

She's turned herself into a Water Stone? That mad creature. I never would've even guessed that was possible … fascinating.\n\nNonetheless, then our only recourse is to kill her, and we were going to do that anyhow. Is she still in there?

Flood the ruins? That would kill everyone!\n\nWhich I guess would suit her just fine …. Damn it! She's gone to the shrine on the east side of the ruins then. Quickly, we need to get there as fast as we can!
Hhmph. You sure? Carving: challenging. Forest: dark and cruel.\n\nAnd I don't talk much.
Good, novice.\n\nStart small. Climb the tree slowly.
Hhmph. I guess. Look stalwart enough.\n\nStart with the basics. Climb the tree. Start at the bottom.

Another one? So the king made you an outfitter and now he wants me to train you. \n\nWell if you want I will teach you some basic gathering techniques, and keep the royal guard out of my hair. Are you ready?

I just knew that the King would forgive me! After what happened to my last novice .. it wasn't my fault anyway.\n\nAnyway! I'm happy to take you on as a novice runecrafter. Are you ready to begin with the basics?

The King decides who I should take into my service then, eh? Mauloch's teeth, I would have … but no matter.\n\nYour first lesson is to work some copper ore. Gather some, and then smelt it into a copper ingot.
The undead don't have money and what they like to eat, <<1>> does not sell.
For the moment, the Baandari will stay put.  We're safe enough for now, tucked back here.
Traveling is what the Baandari do. Unless the Hollow Wastes is in upheaval. In that case, we lose two horses to a bad sandstorm and shelter here from roaming undead.
You have a gift for understatement, friend.  You are welcome to shelter here. The shipyards are no place for a Baandari right now, nor for you, if you want my advice.
I ask you again, because this is an important decision to make: will you explore the mystic pathways between this world and the next?\n\nWill you join the Runecrafter's guild?
Excellent! Welcome to the guild, novice! \n\nI can almost guarantee no one will steal your soul and use it to fuel a mystic rite. Almost.
Keep your head, and you may become a legend. Let your attention wander and you can lose an hand!\n\nYou're ready to commit to the guild?
All right, novice. If you're going to make it in the Smith's guild, you're going to have to start with the simple stuff. \n\nDon't worry. We all started with the simple stuff. Hah.
Clearly the only way for either of us to be safe is … to merge ….\n\nGive me the stone, and then … stand back. I don't know what will happen.

Great another lackwit who thinks that can find treasures in the mangy fur of a dead wolf.\n\nWell if you must …  Do you swear to follow the guidance and strictures of the honorable guild of outfitters?
Very well. You arre now a Novice. Let's see how you fair.\n\nTalk to me if you wish futher instruction.
Excellent! Another set of willing hands working for the good of the Daggerfall Covenant. What guild name should I write on this Writ? \n\nWould you like to be a Smith, a Forester, or a Runecrafter?
A wise choice, friend. Runes and scrollls, enchantments and soul gems! You'll make a fine runecrafter.
A wise choice, friend. Steel and flame, blades and armor. You'll make a fine smith!
A wise choice, friend. Staves and cloth, shields and bows! You'll make a fine forester.

Just behind the cathedral here in town is an old entrance to the Snakebite Mine. It's mostly tapped out these days, and rumors say brigands use it for a hideout.\n\nStill, there should be some ore left behind in there. Gather some, and return to me.
Baandari scouts see vultures and jackals. Strange scents and frightening sounds on the winds. No workers come out to the camp. In better times, they trade with us, drink and dice with us.
The Baandari often camp here when trading. In better times, the workers from the shipyards come by to trade or dice. But no one comes now.
<<1>> makes fine weapons, to be used, not just for show.  The Baandari can defend themselves.

<<1>> is not helping them, he helps the miners! Without his knowledgeable eye, the central chamber would collapse on top of the conscripts while they work!\n\nThis was his mine, and the Legion took it from him. I assure you, he's no Imperial puppet.

The captain? Yes, the captain. Ran him through. Tainted-Heart just laughed.

He took off southwest toward the river, and she chased after him.

I … I can still hear them screaming!

Part of me wishes them pain for their role in our deaths, but they are blameless. <<1>> chose to betray us, but they were just an excuse.\n\nSave them. Do not burden us with more pain from the world of the living. <<1>> lived in a house to the west.
First you have to promise to help me. I didn't stumble into a Lion Guard camp by accident. I came here for help, not to be taken prisoner!\n\nI had no choice! They're holding my family!
You wouldn't! You wouldn't harm an unarmed man who's simply trying to save his family.\n\nWould you?

Not much for strategy, huh? If you're dressed as a Red Rook when you slit Envoy Caoiss's throat, imagine the amount of distrust that will cause! \n\nYou need to find a Red Rook uniform, though. Dig around in their packs until you find one that fits.

All right, all right! But if my family is harmed ….\n\nA Bloodthorn envoy plans to meet with the Red Rooks to finalize their alliance. The meeting's going to take place in the Dwynnarth Ruins. If you disrupt the meeting, it should break their truce.

Yes, yes! I'll tell you everything I know. But only after they're safe.\n\nThey're holding my family in an abandoned house to the south of this camp. If you get them back here safely, I'll tell you everything you want to know.

The Red Rooks! I'm a tracker. I know this area like the back of my hand. The Red Rooks tried to convince me to join them, but I said no. So they captured my family and threatened to kill them.\n\nI want those bastards dead just as much as anyone.
Kip is safe? Oh, thank you! Thank you so much!\n\nCome, Darcielle. We need to get out of here and find your father.
Captain Gilame. She's scouting the Farwatch perimeter. \n\nIf you intercept any messages meet her up on the cliffs, at the ravine bridge.
The Dominion has a camp nearby. It's across the ravine from Farwatch Tower.\n\nYou can reach it by crossing the wooden suspension bridge.

Ahh! One of Curio's, eh? Welcome to the forge! As a smith you'd use pressure and fire to reshape the world to your will. \n\nPlate armors and well sharpened swords are our stock in trade, for everyone from the lowly footman to the greatest warrior.

Ahh, come to learn? Runecrafting is an ancient and noble art. We manipulate magicka, imbuing it into runes, jewels, and staves. \n\nWe can also change a common shirt or robe and make it a source of power for mages!
We craft wood. Weapons and armor, enchanted gearbindings.\n\nForest magics, incarnate.
By Mauloch's hammer! I could smell the smelted steel when you walked into the room.\n\nI'm sure you'll make a fine addition to the guild.

Of course, of course. Like the ore on the mountainside, the Smith's guild endures. We'll still be here if you decide to come back this way.\n\nPerhaps you're more a Runecrafter, eh? Head north from here, and speak with <<1>>. Mauloch guide you!

We combine minerals and magic to create restoratives for mages. We forge enchanted trinkets that rogues can clip to their gear, granting them enhanced abilities. \n\nWe're flame and metal and magic combined! So! What do you say?

You'll love it, friend. The first time you set ink to scroll, the first time you etch a rune … you'll never be able to go back. Julianos smiles on you today, truly.\n\nWelcome to the Runecrafter's guild.

Wisely said, friend. No need to rush into a decision like this. Go, contemplate the runes. Return when you are sure.\n\nIn the meantime, perhaps the Forestry guild would be a better fit? Speak with <<1>>. He is just to the south. Go well.

Let's see … we scribe scrolls that any man or mer can cast. We prepare soul gems, trapping the essence of mystical creatures. They can be used to enhance powerful magical gear!\n\nThe Runecrafter's life is a fulfilling one. What say you?
Nice. The wood speaks. You listen. Talking, not required.\n\nWelcome to the guild.
Fine. Remember, the wood speaks. Listen to it. Come back, decide later.\n\nGo well.
Leather from beasts. Pliable armor. Restoration potions, go down easy. \n\nWell? Join up?
The Dominion has a camp nearby. It's across the ravine from Farwatch Tower.\n\nYou can reach it by crossing the wooden suspension bridge.

The Bloodthorns and Red Rooks plan to finalize their alliance. They're meeting in secret right in the ruins behind you! But the relationship has been rocky at best, from what I was able to see.\n\nI don't think it will be very hard to force them apart.

Just wiping out the ones at this meeting won't be enough. That might even bring the two groups closer together, since you'd be giving them a common enemy.\n\nNo, you need to turn them against one another.

Of course! It's a great idea! Take my clothes and go to the ruins. Find Envoy Caoiss and attack him while wearing a Red Rook uniform. That should shatter the alliance!\n\nIf you lose the disguise, dig around in Red Rook packs for another one.
We were sent to gather information on the Dominion presence at Farwatch. \n\nI can confirm that they're here in full force. And they certainly know how to fight!

Ah, how refreshing! I only have one piece of a focus element. Now it's yours.\n\nI'd been looking for a way to use it to get <<1>> back under control. It's been so difficult. I can't imagine what's happened.

Nothing stays dead here long, as you'll soon see. The Imperials meant for <<1>> to be their most powerful weapon. \n\nNot long after their first attempt, something broke the spell and caused them to lose control.

It's out of the way and makes a great base of operations. They can signal their ships from the tower.\n\nUnless our luck changes quickly, they can use the tower to launch a full-scale invasion of Glenumbra!
There is wisdom in that. I … perhaps I can attend a meeting. Just to see what your group has planned.\n\nWait! I think that guard heard us talking!
No! Of course I don't want to watch others die!\n\nI just don't see what I can do about it. There are so many Imperials. What can one person accomplish?
Of course! I can't deny that valuables have been stolen and Orcs have disappeared. Everyone is up in arms, and it doesn't help that those two loudmouths keep arguing all the time.

Leonce commands the militia, and Ghak speaks for the Orcs.\n\nLeonce took control of the inn. Claims the Fell's Brigade needs a stronghold in case the trouble to the west gets any closer. And Ghak wants to know where the missing Orcs have gotten to.
Fine! I will go and listen to your group … if they have anything to say worth hearing.\n\nDamn it. That guard is looking at us. Now look what you've gotten me into!

You arrogant dog! You strut around with your fine equipment, doing whatever you please.\n\nDo you know who enables your lifestyle? People like me: builders, growers, and teachers. And you dare to question my honor?
Quickly then. Allow me to combine the heartwood shards into a poultice.\n\nShe's fought so hard to resist the poison and deserves rest. I hope this works.
I hope so. Here. Take the poultice and apply it to the poor little thing. I must be prepared to do … whatever is necessary.\n\nPray to your gods that it works.

How could that possibly be any of your business, outsider?\n\nBut if you must know, treasured possessions have been stolen from our homes. No Breton would ever perform such a dastardly deed, therefore the Orcs must be guilty!

My side? My side of the story is the truth! These dogs accuse us of robbing them while our brothers have gone missing. We didn't do anything!\n\nAll I know is, someone has to answer for abducting innocent Orcs.
Quiet! The bad one will taste your words on the air.\n\nHe's coming closer. Bloodfiends accompany him … so many bloodfiends …. They want our blood!

I saw Reezal-Jul in a dream. It was the night Crestshade was attacked. I could feel his presence. Now I always sense him. He watches. He waits. He's … he's … he's coming for us.\n\nMother's worried sick about all this.
Perhaps I'll see you there. Or maybe I'm just playing along, an-\n\nOh, Tu'whacca's breath! I think that guard just overheard us.
So be it. The dagger has been tossed. Let us see which end strikes the earth.\n\nAnd so it begins! Even now, there is a guard watching us. Are you prepared to defend yourself?

Thank Stendarr! That will buy us precious time. \n\nWe need to douse their signal fires before they can send the command. Take this storm rune and use it to put out the fires. Then meet me on the shore.
A moment, friend. I think one of the guards has been eavesdropping on us.\n\nAre you ready for a fight? Let us begin our glorious rebellion!
I know the place. I've never been there myself. There are stories about the owner, Ufa.\n\nHmm. One moment. I think I may have spoken too loudly. One of the guards is looking at us.

If I knew an easy way past them, we'd have liberated <<1>> by now.\n\nThere are paths to avoid most Imperial patrols. If those can't take you where you need to go, use a disguise. That should let you walk right past them without attracting attention.
No so fast, stranger! One the guards is watching us. I think he may have overheard.\n\nIf you can keep him from killing me … well, I'd take it as a kindness.

The Fell's Brigade has turned against us? That makes a certain amount of sense, but the news is still distressing.\n\nI'll talk to the mayor about this. In the meantime, I have something else I need you to do.

The best method to get around is by rooftop. Keep a lookout for pathways between walls and buildings. Some call those paths the "Thieves' Highway."\n\nLook behind the Mages Guild where <<1>> is. You can traverse almost all of <<2>> using the Highway.

You can't buy one, if that's what you're asking.\n\nThe best place to find one is on an Imperial. Sometimes we're lucky enough to kill one without getting obvious rips or bloodstains on their uniforms.
That's where the governor's mansion is. There are no easy paths around the grounds. The Imperials patrol there constantly.

No, they're not, but it's the best advice I can give you. \n\nAlso, the Imperials desecrated our town with their skeletal soldiers. If you pass too close to one, they'll attack you. The dead show no mercy to the living.

No! No, no. That would be bad. I scared the others. They didn't like me. Besides, I don't want to draw Reezal-Jul to the camp.\n\nTell the Captain I'm sorry. I'll stay here. Maybe he'll leave the camp alone if I hide here with Mother.

Reezal-Jul likes to take parts from different bodies and make entirely new creatures. That's probably what he'll do to the Captain. Or turn her into a bloodfiend.\n\nThe cave is full of vampires. Maybe you should use the secret tunnel.

Please! Please don't hurt me! I need to take care of Mother. I'll tell you what you want to know.\n\nThe tunnel is over there. It's small. Hard to spot. Secret. I saw Reezal-Jul come in and out of there.
Let's get moving.

I have my word as a warrior. \n\nIt's the Fell's Brigade! It has to be! Why else would they ban me and my brothers from serving in the militia? They're up to no good! That's the only explanation for locking up the inn.
You can call me <<1>>, as Ufa does.\n\nAs my father was the grandeya of Hallin's Stand before me, it's my duty to be grandeya. I don't want to discuss more than that at this time.
Hhmph. You sure? Wood's hard. Forest is mean.\n\nAnd I don't talk much.
Good, novice.\n\nStart small. Climb the tree slowly.
I ask you again, because this is an important decision to make: will you explore the mystic pathways between this world and the next?\n\nWill you join the Runecrafter's guild?
Excellent! Welcome to the guild, novice! \n\nI can almost guarantee no one will steal your soul and use it to fuel a mystic rite. Almost.

Great another lackwit who thinks that can find treasures in the mangy fur of a dead wolf.\n\nWell if you must …  Do you swear to follow the guidance and strictures of the honorable guild of outfitters?
Very well. You arre now a Novice. Let's see how you fair.\n\nTalk to me if you wish futher instruction.
If our Lady has been captured by those fiends in the ruins, she won't be able to provide us with the rain we need to survive.\n\nLeaving fate to the whims of the weather is a dead man's gamble.

A hero? I never thought of myself that way. I led my soldiers into battle, doing my duty. Their corpses littered the hillside.\n\nWe protected … I do not remember now. What we protected remained safe, escaping while we held our ground.

I was a general of a small army. A larger force was marching towards our city. I led my soldiers to meet them away from the city allowing our people time to seek shelter elsewhere.\n\nI don't remember if we won, which probably means we didn't.
I am now. The harbor master said that since I was always up on the platform, they might as well give me the job.
I used to be a fisherman, but after my wife and daughter were taken, I just felt like I needed to keep an eye on the horizon. I guess I hoped to keep it from happening to anyone else.
Ebonheart slavers. Sent in a boat and took them right off the shore. So now … I watch.

Lately, mostly harpies. They live in the crags along the coast, but something has stirred them up. They've been attacking travelers—even within sight of Daggerfall's walls. Be careful if you head that way. And leave your family somewhere safe.
Last week in the dawn mists I thought I saw Aldmeri swan ships heading up the coast toward Farwatch. But then the mists thickened and they were gone. Probably just my eyes playing tricks on me.
My Breton neighbors! Just because my father was a Reachman, they think I'm a cursed follower of Angof.
Yes, yes! Stendarr bless you!
Angof the Gravesinger! He's a Reachmage, and part of this damned Bloodthorn cult. \n\nYou're not blind. You've seen the vines, right?

You don't trust me either? Look, I'm loyal to the Covenant. My father came from the Reach thirty years ago with Durcorach's Horde.\n\nHe was wounded at Daggerfall and left behind, and my mother … well, she took him in.

I never met him, if that's what you're asking. My father told me tales of Angof. He was a terror, even back then, and now he's here in Glenumbra. \n\nEvery Breton bully has joined his Bloodthorn cult, but I get the blame!

I was going to hide here until this blew over, but now Angof's cultists have invaded the woods. \n\nIf Angof isn't killed or driven out, I've got no choice but to leave Glenumbra. Maybe a ship captain in Aldcroft will take me as far as Wayrest.

<This chest is inscribed with several unknown scripts. However, one is recognizable. It reads:>\n\n"Three Guardians hold sway over the Serpent: the shadow-keeper on his left, the light-wielder on his right, and his great weapon cleaving the sky."
<The inset is empty.>
Kill me? Ha! To kill Uela, you must find her first. \n\nI can reach you, but you cannot reach me!
Hmmph! Where I am is a secret only a crow can know. And the crows call for your death, not mine. \n\nCome after me and the last sight you will see will be a black beak … pecking out your eyeballs!

Evidence? Our belongings disappeared just as the Orcs started to leave town! What more evidence do we need?\n\nGhak claims his brethren have been abducted, but we know better. Orcs are thieves and liars—every last one of them!

Things began to go missing. Valuables, mostly, and all from Breton homes. Then Orcs began to disappear, vanishing without a trace.\n\nAccusations were made and tempers flared. The constable had her hands full, so I called out the Fell's Brigade.

The abominations are created just across the water. A witchman has built a transformation altar there to perform his foul work. \n\nI am not equipped for this task. Will you go destroy the altar and kill the witchman for me? For the spriggans who died?

<This raven's body bears signs of capture by a wild animal, although its lacerations are larger than any animal near the area could make.>\n\n<A trail of black feathers leads into the nearby cave entrance.>
I don't know! I came back and found that the door was open. Gennove must have sacrificed himself so the rest of the family could escape. But blessed Arkay, why did they open the door?

The weapons? Of course. It's just the enormity of it all. It's frazzled my nerves. But the rest of the Hinault family—you have to find them!\n\nBefore you go, I have to tell you something. The dead … they sometimes return as bloodfiends.

I'm not sure, but the lieutenant thinks the Montclairs are responsible.\n\nIf any of the Hinaults were killed, you have to burn their bodies. Take this torch and start with Gennove. Then collect his ashes so his family can give him a proper burial.

Just behind the cathedral here in town is an old entrance to the Snakebite Mine. It's mostly tapped out these days, and rumors say brigands use it for a hideout.\n\nStill, there should be some gems left behind. Gather some, and return to me.
<The mammoth doesn't respond, but you can hear the nearby growl of a stalking tiger. Soon, it will attack.>
I'll answer as I can.

Is the tree invincible against the many cuts of an axe? A giant can stand against five men, but not thirty.\n\nThe mammoths are mighty, but without the hillmen to protect them, they're outnumbered. The tigers will prevail.

Ha! Iif you ever see him fighting, you'll see what they fear.\n\nOur patriarch has punished most of the tigers around here at least once. He's given them scars to remember him by! Still, he's old now, and he's tired, and the tigers are many.
We were betrayed. An army doesn't simply sneak in and overtake a Redguard city like <<1>> without inside help.\n\nSomeone ensured their journey's secrecy and opened our gates for them while we slept.
Money, perhaps. Power. Our scouts are watching the most likely suspects.\n\nTwo nobles in particular appear fairly untouched by the attack. I have no doubt at least one of them is behind this.
I was afraid that was going to be the case. I'll … I'll try to be strong. For my sister.\n\nI just wish I could bury them in the family graveyard. I won't sleep easy until that's done.
And darkness lights our way. Welcome to the resistance.\n\nI've been watching <<1>>. Ufa was right to suspect him. He's been to Governor Seius' mansion twice now.

And darkness lights our way. I see Ufa has found more help. Believe me, we need it.\n\nTell Ufa I have reason to believe <<1>> isn't involved. She's been arguing incessantly with Adham since <<2>> fell.
And darkness lights our way. Thank the gods! Ufa's finally sent someone.\n\nI have news of grave importance. In fact, we can't delay any longer. You have to act now.
Adham has never held public favor, but he truly is wise.\n\nThat makes him dangerous. He could easily negotiate a deal with the Imperials.

<<1>> is Adham's betrothed, and an unwilling one, I might add. She's too young and beautiful for a man like him.\n\nWe've been watching her to see if she can give us any leads, but there's nothing to show she's involved in any schemes.
<<1>> just became completely enraged. He went on and on about the warehouse. Some Imperial soldiers restrained him.\n\nI'm certain something's in there, something he's very worried about.

Find out what's hidden inside the warehouse. It's the largest building in the southeastern section of the city. This could be the key to finding out the traitor's identity.\n\nI'll take the news to Ufa personally.
Fool! This key belongs to me now.\n\nOnce <<1>> has had his fill of this place, I will control this town!
<<1>>? She's still alive? No matter.\n\nMy bodyguard and I will finish you off. Then I'll take her life as I did her pathetic father's!

I'll ascend the tower and shout the call to arms. That will signal the beginning of the rebellion. \n\nDefend this tower. If any Imperials get by this door, we won't have a chance of succeeding. Are you ready for this?
Here. Take this key and use it to enter Governor Seius' mansion.\n\nI want to stay among my people, so I can remain as an inspiration for them. I wish you the best of luck.

Our grandeya's advisor, Adham. He's a worthless Forebear who somehow wormed his way into a position of power in a city governed by Crowns.\n\nGrandeya Ubaid was killed during the invasion. He was stabbed in the back! We must right these wrongs.

We have two. The first is our own Captain of the Guard, Dhakir.\n\nI refuse to accept that no one saw these Imperials. No alarms were sounded. The gates were left unattended. The failure is obvious. We just need evidence to prove it.
There are people all around us! Particular ones? This one cannot say. Not without some convincing.
There's still no sign of hard evidence against him, but I still think he's the one.\n\nEvery bone in my body says so.
Yes. She lost her brothers in the invasion. It weighs on her.\n\nI can see she blames their deaths on Adham.
Right. We use lumber. Basic material. \n\nSouth gate. Stand of trees. Green maple. Head out, gather, come back. Talk then.
That's not far. I can get you there, free of charge. We'll have to take the smaller vessel. No spare coin to pay for their ridiculous docking fees.\n\nWhat do you say? Ready to go?

Nothin' untoward, I'd say! We're paid well for his simple deliveries. What's easier than leaving a box of gold on an island?\n\nI don't like the way those Reach keep watching us, though. He may have to pay extra next time. My boys are getting spooked.
I can't guarantee the efficacy of the antidote I would make. Faolchu's get are of a very different breed than the average werewolf.

Unless you can coax a werewolf to drink this, the best you can hope for is to weaken one by fighting it and then splash this concoction on its wounds. That may be enough.\n\nSend anyone who transforms back here.
Luckily with the blood you've gathered and the ingredients around the inn, we should be able to put something together.\n\nLet's see … yes … here we are. Smells of rot. Should be just right then.
I hope you mean, how can you get one!\n\nIf you can find an <<1>>, that will serve the purpose. They're carried by legion officers, of which there are two, <<2>> and <<3>>, at this camp.

Weather? You call this weather? It's misery! It's a curse from Akatosh to keep us in eternal gloom!\n\nWhy, the gods must be having an epic piss-up right now and laughing at us as we suffer in this chill!
Yes, let me return to being cold and doing hard labor at the same time.\n\nYou hear me, Julianos? Surely you must, you divine bastard!

I can teleport you there for a small fee.

Forgive me for asking for coin. The reagents for our spells are costly.

Let me know when you're ready, and I'll begin the spell.
Burying them in mounds of muck. They'll hack you up with those claws or knock you out with bile. Then they'll bury you in mud.\n\nI don't know why they do it, and I don't care. I want it stopped.

Long ago, a magical artifact imprisoned Sadal, the Brother of Strife. That artifact's become the heart of the coral.\n\nThat's what the Covenant is after. Alexandra Conele wants it, and she is without mercy.
We were escorts for Ahknara and her band. She's going to infiltrate Fort Arand.\n\nPlease, don't hurt us. She never told us her plans!
You've never heard of Ahknara? They call her the Poison of Alik'r. She's an infamous assassin. They say she cut down an entire Dominion army in one night.\n\nWhatever she's planning, it's big.

Thank the Three! I thought I was going to die in here.\n\nThere's a powerful mage named Alexandra Conele leading these soldiers. She knows how to enter the heart chamber. She ripped the knowledge right out of my head!
You'll find the manor along the north city wall.\n\nI'll be there with Tanval.
Excellent. Let's get going.
This port's the key to Stonefalls. That's why these Covenant bastards are attacking.\n\nThey're keen to take the city, but we aren't going to let them. The Nords are here to defend the Pact.
They made it? And so close all along. Yes, I'll go. I just need a moment to clear my head.\n\nBut be careful down here. You don't want to end up like that spirit.
I was ambushed. Warm-blood assassins do that. \n\nThey hoped I wouldn't reach these tunnels and discover the roots of Ahknara's plan. They died with that hope unfulfilled.
Enslaving the dead is evil. Furon does not understand this. As for Giron, I think he does not care.\n\nThere is a better way.
It was. Spirits are not meant to be trapped. Furon wants to enslave them through magic, but that's torture to the dead.\n\nFreeing these spirits is the right path.

Ah, greetings. Yes, I was just thinking about the situation here. These spirits make up an ancient army of Chimer warriors. Blademasters from the time before Red Mountain.\n\nIt's fascinating to observe ancestors so … closely.
Just so. It proves we can force these spirits to guard Davon's Watch! A potent defense from any future siege. \n\nGiron has a plan for repeating this ritual on a larger scale.
You are very kind. Strangely kind, for a place like the Ashlands. I stand here, tasting the air, and do you know what I've learned?
I can't thank you enough!
That scale-back? I kept my tongue when times were good, but now when the town is weakened, he's suddenly helpful? \n\nThis is just a trick.
Nonsense. We've lived in the shadow of Ash Mountain all our lives. We know its dangers.\n\nIt was those Argonian savages. Find <<1>>. Then ask that scale-back where my daughter is.
Because his people have taken my daughter, <<1>>! She was doing chores for me, and now she's disappeared.\n\nOne of the farmsteaders saw that Argonian <<2>> watching her. Who else could it be?
Return <<1>> to me. Then maybe I'll see what Soft-Scale wants.\n\nLook for <<2>> in the ruins. The Three only know what she's doing.

More akin to friendly rivals, I would say. We've jointly dealt with maintaining Shornhelm ever since King Ranser died.\n\nIt was only a matter of time before one of us wanted full stake in the city. I only wish I was the one to strike first.
Yes, I am. Look at this. This is no natural run of lava. These are footprints. A spirit of wrath came through here.\n\nStubborn Girvas will not hear my warning. He thinks the eruption caused this.
Good. I'll activate this last one. Once I do, the other barriers on all five will harden like a shell.\n\nWhile I do this, you must slay Ahknara before she slithers away again.

Baem chased after Ahknara. He'll need your help more than I do. Look for him. I'm sure he's wounded, if not dead.\n\nOnce this is done, use the trapdoor atop the bluff. It leads to the command post below.
As you can see, his daughter is not here.\n\nI did see <<1>> earlier. The flow of her life takes her to the base of Ash Mountain regularly.
I don't know for certain, just that I saw her walking west out of town. Find her. Then perhaps Girvas will listen to me. \n\nIf you succeed, use this.
Very well. I must commune with the coral. Protect me, no matter what happens.
Bad blood. I thought everyone knew that.\n\nBack before the Ebonheart Pact was formed, Dark Elves enslaved Argonians. They raided the Black Marsh and brought the captives up here to work.
Ha! Spoken like a courtier. You know, just saying everyone is friends doesn't make it so. \n\nForming the Pact was a battle, and there are still many sides to it.
Sure, but the bigger problem is the Dunmer. They used to be lords and masters until the Pact was formed.\n\nNow all of a sudden, the Argonians are free and everyone is equal.
Denthis was just showing me how the spell works. Then the Shadowsilk tribe jumped us. They carried me off as a tribute for Grimmstal. \n\nEnough talk. Get me out of here!
I offer my gratitude.\n\nPlease wait. I'll make a poultice to soothe the burns of the injured. I'll need you to use it on them.
The Dunmer don't trust Argonians, especially me and my egg sister, <<1>>. They fear we'll harm them.\n\nYou are a stranger, so they may let you heal their wounds.

My heart is at ease. I've decided how to contact the coral. \n\nThis won't be easy. The Coral Heart could unleash a Brother of Strife, but simply taking the heart would kill it. Ill winds are blowing, friend.
The coral summoned the dreugh. If I can show the coral we're friendly, it may aid us by turning the dreugh against the Covenant.\n\nTime is precious. If I'm to succeed, I'll need your help.

I'll rally my soldiers and lead them to the Coral Heart chamber. She must be inside.\n\nHave you seen my aide, Sings-With-Reed? She knows more about the coral than anyone. She must have some kind of plan.
We'll draw her out and fight her face to face. We'll rip the Heart from her bloody fingers.\n\nI don't know if you've ever faced a Breton mage lord. It won't be easy.
Truth falls like a cool rain, carving many channels in the mud. \n\nMy truth is different from the Dunmer's, yet both are still true.

I have no love for them. Do you hate fire for burning down your hut? The fire acts as it must.  \n\nThey saw our huts, and their nature required them to act. I trust a Dark Elf to act as a Dark Elf must.
A signal. It's colorful, but harmless.\n\nIf you find Lady <<1>>, use it, and I will come to you.
Are you mocking me? Yes, of course I am.\n\nI'm trapped by lava flows and flaming shalks, and I can't walk. If I ever get home, I'm going to drink a whole jar of sujamma.
Of course he is, the overprotective guar. Since we lost Mother he's tried to run my life for me. \n\nI think I'll need two bottles of sujamma when I get home. Forget what Father says.

This was a shrine to the Three. I come out here to pray for Mother. She was taken from us a few years ago. She was the sweetest woman I've ever known. Some days I swear I can still hear her voice … anyway. I was out here when the eruption began.
We train troops and store provisions here.\n\nWhy the Dark Elves built a fort against the mountains, I'll never know. What's it protecting? The mountains? Dunmer! I'll never understand them.

I agree it is rather obscure, but I can only interpret it as a threat. The writer wants me to determine the secret of these lampposts, or the missing priests will remain missing permanently.\n\nWe can't let that happen!

These are my eggs, the fruit of my tree. My roots must join with the coral for us to be truly of one mind.\n\nPlace my eggs at the three large clusters of coral around the antlers. Then meet me in the heart chamber.
Once my people were their slaves. They were not kind masters, and now they are not masters at all.\n\nBlood was spilled. Words and promises between our leaders is not enough to cleanse the stream.

You do not justify when you can just act. We had no armies, no roads, no crop fields … none of the accomplishments Dunmer call "civilized."\n\nWe were beasts in the swamp, but now, they must share power with us.
Yes. Perhaps your elders didn't teach you these things. \n\nThey stole us from Black Marsh so we could pick their saltrice, tend their kwama, and scrub their floors.
Well, it's all beyond me. I'm just another sword-swinger. What should we do?

Fort Arand was built a long time ago atop a set of Daedric ruins. I think the ruins were a prison for some fetching Daedra.\n\nB'vek! Who can keep track of all that ancient lore? The fort is out of the way, so we use it to train troops.

A few years back, a fetching big Aldmeri army invaded Hammerfell. They sacked a town and established some fortifications.\n\nThey sent messages home, and the Elves sent a shipload of reinforcements. The Redguards were quaking in their boots.
Those two are smart, and they're tough as trail bread. I'm sure their idea is sound.\n\nTalk to Giron. Best get on with it.
Well, maybe enslaving the dead's not the best idea. That Scaleback sees the world differently, but she's seldom wrong.\n\nLet Reesa know. She'll tell you the rest.

That's what they say, f'lah. Over the next few days, a bunch of Aldmeri troops in the fort disappeared. \n\nA Redguard army rolled up to the fort, but didn't attack. It just sat there, stopping the Aldmeri from escaping Ahknara's venom.

Not as such, f'lah. The Dominion made a mistake, y'see. They took captives from a Redguard ship they managed to get offshore from their new holdings. \n\nThat night, one of the Redguards broke free and murdered every last Elf aboard.

The fort was built on top of the ruins shortly after they were found. Reports of Daedra worshipers led General Arand to investigate the mountains above the fort.\n\nThe general claims that when he found this place, a Daedric gate stood open down here.

A few years back, the barriers were dropped and the gate was gone. No evidence proved it ever existed. \n\nWas Arand mad, believing he saw a gate that wasn't there? Did a Daedra emerge, leaving an open gate behind it? The land may know. You should ask.
No, but they set up the barrier stones and built the fort.\n\nThey did it to protect Stonefalls from anything that might crawl up from below.
The Argonian helped you find her? Pah. Self-interest and cunning, I'm sure.\n\nI'm … grateful just the same. Morvani means the world to me. Ever since her mother was taken from us.

They have beastly, baser urges. It makes them hard to trust. When the swamp calls to them, they rise up against their neighbors and strike them down. \n\nEven the kindest, the most gentle, are not spared from their wrath.
The Covenant closes on us like nix-hounds on a kill. They think they've already won the city.\n\nThey're entirely wrong. They are doomed to the last man.

You are the plan. There's a relic beneath the city guarded by spirits of my ancestors. For me to fight them would be blasphemy, but you aren't of House Indoril. \n\nThe entrance is through the tombs across the square. Bring the relic here.

The Akaviri were invaders from across the sea: fierce snake men and all manner of monsters. We faced them here on these plains, but they overwhelmed us.\n\nYet we fought and died and held until Vivec himself came and put an end to it.

Vivec brought water to cleanse the land. His children breathed the holy water while the Akaviri drowned. It was a great victory for Morrowind.\n\nRumors say the Akaviri came here looking for an ancient relic. What it is, I do not know.

One who does not know the Tribunal lives in a dark world.

Three living gods—Vivec, Almalexia, and Sotha Sil—bless Morrowind and guide us in these troubling times.

Vivec is the wisest of living gods. We are scarcely worthy to look upon him.
It's where you get kwama eggs.\n\nYou can also get kwama cuttle, the waxy substance that grows on their beaks.
I don't know. Potions, I think, or something to fight poison or cleanse water.\n\nI never asked. I just harvest it.
Well, it's a hole in the ground where kwama live. That's a mine. \n\nYou didn't think we dug it up like those Nords dig iron, did you?
I'm angry at myself for getting caught by these milk-drinkers and I hate that. \n\nI owe them a debt. Want to help me thwart their little invasion of Morrowind?

In fact, I do. \n\nThe Orcs are carrying kindlepitch—I could smell it. Probably to burn Elven houses. Kill some of these snowbacks, collect their kindlepitch, and throw it at their torches in the supply shacks. It'll be fun.
Oh, I tied myself up for fun. What does it look like? I've been captured by Orcs!\n\nCut me free. I've got an idea for getting back at these stinking snowbacks.

Both have practiced the arts of necromantic magic under Karnosis for as long as I can remember. They are both powerful in their own right.\n\nBe on your guard when you confront them. They will use both the living and the dead against you.
Then we should go.
Follow me.
Do? Burn those ballistae. Same for the ladders. Burn them to ash.\n\nI'll be leading a sortie from the gate. Meet us when you're done. It'll be glorious!
