It was before the signing of the Pact. The Argonians of Senie still served my neighbors as slaves. Several of them made a break for freedom, and … my Rainisi … she was just out for a stroll.\n\nAhem. But today Morvani lives. Thanks to you.
Only that you need to bring it. I tried to reason with my ancestors, but they do not understand our peril.\n\nYou must succeed where I cannot.

Last Will and Testament of Frodibert Fontbonne\n\n"In death as in life, I would dedicate all my resources to supporting my dear son Donel and specifically to expanding his intellect and furthering his education."

"In that same spirit, I would like to pose a challenge of wits for Donel to claim his inheritance. The clue to begin the challenge is this: 

'After day turns to night, you must follow the light.'

Good luck my son. I am proud of you."
Yes, and I am grateful. When we meet in the next world, tell me how beautiful the land became.
I'm not paid to think about this. That's a luxury for someone of higher rank than me.\n\nI'll admit something seems off-kilter. If only the House councilors would see it that way.
Yes, outsider. \n\nOther than Khralek, you're the first person I've spoken to since … the beheading.
I am—was—a priestess of the Tribunal. I came here with a group of six other priests to seek the source of a terrible spiritual disturbance.\n\nWhat we found was horror.
Khralek is cunning, for an Orc. The spell can't be broken as simply as that.\n\nKilling him is the only sure way.
Khralek gro-Vortag is practicing terrible necromancy in this land. He studies a new art to bind the souls of the dead to morbid fetishes.\n\nWe became his latest experiment.

Just that easy, eh? Fort Arand is a training ground. Other than the handful of veteran instructors, we've got nothing but wet-behind-the-ears recruits here. \n\nThey'd be eaten alive by those Covenant troops.
Me? No, not yet. I wait for the plague to find me. That's all we can do, isn't it?\n\nThe House leaders debate how to keep the plague out of Narsis. How to protect us. Why do they even bother?
Skeever calls himself Gruznak the Impatient. I guess these Orcs consider recklessness a virtue. \n\nCan't say I think they're wrong. Just be careful. I hear Gruznak is one tough horker.

They try, but the solution eludes them. We'll slowly fade away, one by one, as the plague takes us all. Gates can't stop it. We can't lock it out.\n\nEnjoy your last days, outsider, for the plague takes us all in the end.
I'm not sure. I saw the captain approaching, then felt a sharp pain in my head. I think I heard a footfall behind me before I went down.\n\nWhen I came to, he was dead and our attacker was gone.

Assassins! Captain Llaari should see this. She's in the command post, the largest building in the fort. \n\nReport to her, and I'll spread the word to the other troops in the fort. We need everyone on guard and watching their backs.

Damn! We need to find out what they're planning!\n\nIf I had a handful of able soldiers, I'd send them into the camp to search for plans. Unfortunately, Fort Arand is a training ground filled with milk-drinking recruits.
I overheard that the Vereansu ashkhan, Ginasa Solas, plans to leave. If the Vereansu escape, it is only a matter of time before they return and attack us again.
Shor's bones, you're a brave one! Put steel or spell to the commanders in the encampment. They're the ones most likely to have a copy of their orders.\n\nThen head for the gates of the fort.

If only it were that easy. I just learned that our village elder, Tennus Andalen, was captured, tied up, and tossed into his home. Then the Vereansu set the place on fire. He won't survive much longer.

If we can prevent another massacre, then the elder's death won't be in vain. Enter the Vereansu camp, destroy their supplies, and kill the ashkhan.\n\nWe will wait for you along the road to Narsis. Vivec guide you!
The elder must be saved! Under his leadership, we will rebuild our village.\n\nWe will wait for you along the road to Narsis. Vivec guide you!

Tribunal protect me, but I can't make this decision. You must decide. Will you stop the Vereansu and let the elder die to protect us from future reprisals, or will you save the elder and let the Vereansu escape to continue raiding?

Victory? Sometimes the living can't see that the costs are too high. The giant destroyed us as well as our enemies, and what use is our domain if it is but charred earth?\n\nIn death, the only thing I want is to be alive.
Do the guards search for our missing people? No, because the House councilors don't tell them to.\n\nI'm not going to become a victim. That's why I'm leaving.

No one does anything in Narsis if the kinhouse doesn't command it. It's that large building over there. You can't miss it.\n\nBe careful, outsider. They might decide you're sick. Plague this, plague that! It's their only concern lately.

"Let these words embody the agreement between King Kurog, sovereign and mighty ruler of Orsinium, and the Oathbound warchief, Gruznak gro-Volkar.\n\n"Herein lie the terms set forth between the Oathbound and the Daggerfall Covenant.

"The deaths of the wicked and deceitful Dark Elves are prized above all other deeds in this venture.\n\n"For each Dark Elf skull claimed by the Oathbound, King Kurog shall bestow control of the lands at Malak's Maw for one year.

"Furthermore, fulfillment of this agreement shall pardon Gruznak gro-Volkar and his Oathbound for crimes committed against the Daggerfall Covenant.\n\n"These crimes include murder, banditry, and impersonation of agents of King Kurog of Orsinium."

Look around. Narsis is practically deserted. The plague, the curse, whatever you want to call it. It's driving everyone away.\n\nOr maybe that crazy story the villagers chatter on about is true. I guess anything's possible.

I think the people are scared. And they should be. The Llodos plague rushes onward, and Narsis is directly in its path.\n\nIf there's any truth to the other rumors, then I'm sure the House councilors will deal with it.
<You've taken the inheritance, storing it carefully to give to Donel when you find him.>
Of course not. Let me guess. You met my drunken fool of a husband, Norgred?\n\nI'm sure he was remorseful, hungover, and making up stories.

I'd be grateful if you found it, too. Norgred probably dropped it near that house by the water where the plague husks have gathered. It's not that far. Just down the hill.\n\nMaybe you'll find his pants there, while you're at it.

He lost the <<1>>? And tried to blame a witch?\n\nWhat he did was drink too much last night. He was bellowing about witches and plague husks when I came back with my herbs. Then he ran off half-dressed, waving the axe and yelling incoherently.

Donel June? Let me see.

Donel June, Breton from Wayrest. His unit was sent to Cyrodiil.

Donel June died in glorious battle in service to his king. There is no death more honorable.
I will not touch it … yet. Please take a piece to each of my students. They understand what must be done, and they are ready.\n\nAfter that, meet me at the southern mustering camp.
Yes. My body will perish, but my soul will become one with the trees of this place. The land will bloom again.\n\nPlease, give me the cap.

The guards here apparently don't like cheaters. They grabbed me after I threw that potion into the Arena, said they were going to feed me to the beasts of the Frozen Arena. We're free now though, but I don't think we can go back the way we came.
You'll notice many Covenant troops about. I'd bet my birth-mud she's opened the reinforced cap that sealed these tunnels.\n\nClearly, she plans to lead an army into the fort from below.
No, there's an exit to the surface behind the final plate.\n\nI activated the first one. Activate three more on the way to the last chamber. Then meet me by the final plate.

Long ago, this place was built to imprison Daedra.\n\nSee that floor plate below the door you came through? There are five of those. When they're all active, a barrier will rise and imprison those within.

We fell back, retreating from fort to stronghold. Whole companies were lost defending our people. The Nedes besieged our cities and burned our farms. \n\nOur sorcerers made a plan and we lured the humans here.

All my life I fought for the Chimer. I skirmished with Dwemer and drove beasts from the Ashlands, until a greater threat loomed.\n\nThe Nedes struck Stonefalls with a lust for territory and slaughter. They were men of the north, violent and cruel.

General Balreth and Legate Sadal. My calculations were correct, not that I expected any less.\n\nBy talking to them you're now attuned to the final clash between Chimer and Nede. Now all you have to do is step into the past.
You'd think the entire town had disappeared, the way everyone carries on.\n\nPeople are missing, but Giron has guards looking into the matter. For all we know, they fled to avoid the Llodos plague.
Very little. No one has actually seen any of these people leave Narsis.\n\nAnd we don't have enough guards to follow up on every lead.
I usually don't hire mercenaries, but these are desperate times.\n\nIf you can prove these claims aren't just fearful delusions, report back to me immediately. You'll be rewarded.

Giron believes we must seal Narsis to protect it from the plague.\n\nNarsis is a center of trade, and such drastic measures aren't called for. Though I admit visitors have been few due to recent events.
I haven't decided. They say I'm not aggressive enough. That my indecision hurts Narsis.\n\nPerhaps Giron is right. I just don't know.

Ah, Narsis, my beloved city.\n\nAt its peak, Narsis was a vibrant center of trade. Merchants would come from far and wide to hawk their wares. Profits grew, and House Hlaalu reinvested it in the city. That seems like so long ago.
Most are back east, dealing with corruption inside Mournhold. Few want to enter a region ravaged by plague.\n\nBut I won't give up. I'll weather this storm and lead Narsis back to prominence.
I'll make a run for it. \n\nPlease, find my brother Mevis. He may be a pain, but I don't want him ending up spitted on some Orc's sword.
I'm sure going to try.\n\nPlease, find my brother Dedras. The Covenant soldiers were hot on his heels.

We got split up. The last I saw Drathyra, she and Mother were just ahead of the invaders.\n\nThere's a cave at the edge of the pools. Drathy, Mevis, and I used to play there. I'll bet that's where they went.
Yes, now that those soldiers are gone.\n\nI'm going to make a run for it. Wish me luck.

No, I haven't seen them since the attack. I did hear Drathyra—that's my sister—telling mother she knew a cave they could hide in.\n\nThere's only one cave that could be. It's on the western edge of the sulfur pools.
Please, find my family.\n\nI'm going to make a run for it. Wish me luck.
You're sure? I might summon a Daedra that could take my head off with a single claw-swipe.\n\nYou are ready for this, right?
Kill the Daedra at the nearby ruins. Take what we need from them.

We have only a few moments. The Nedes are about to break the line. But Sadal and I will save our people and be remembered forever!\n\nHelp the sorceress complete the ritual. Pray at the brazier, soldier. Pray for the destruction of our enemies.
Good. Kill wounded soldiers to gather the Spirits of Strife and slay fire atronachs to gather the Spirits of Fire.\n\nThen return to me, and we will end this war.
I think so. Please, give me the bottle.
The Three bless you.\n\nMother? Everything's going to be fine now.
He stabbed her. Merciful Three, he stabbed her!\n\nWhy did he do that? We did nothing to threaten them.
He said he had an herbal antidote. He actually waved the bottle in my face. He said I could have it if I, well, entertained him and all his men.\n\nI spat in his face.
He went south to our guar barns. Said he wanted to hear the beasts scream.\n\nWe keep greef brandy in the storage shed there. Light some on fire. I bet that would get his attention.

Khajiiti pirates! They're raiding our village—taking slaves and supplies. We couldn't stop them. They're merciless. Just a few of us made it to the gate.\n\nIt's not safe for my people here, but I won't leave without Leel-Vata.
My mate and our spiritual leader. She was in the village when the pirates attacked.\n\nI'm just an old saltrice farmer, outsider. I beg you! Find her and bring her back.

Oh, my head … I thought you were my egg-brother, Seeks-the-Night.\n\nHe led them to us. He hated that my mate was the village elder. He even gave the invaders our sacred relics. Such treachery in our own clutch!

You are not Saxhleel. Why would you help us? Still, I should not refuse such an offer.\n\nThe Khajiit stole our sacred stones and their sorceress took our Hist branch. We brought it all the way back from Black Marsh when we settled here.

Your desire to help our people gladdens my heart. I wish my egg-brother had your spirit.\n\nThe Khajiit stole our sacred stones and their sorceress took the Hist branch we brought back from Black Marsh when we settled here.
Yes. You got here in time. She's resting now.\n\nI'll help Mother make her way to the stead. We'll see you there. And … thank you.
If I come back without that axe, Evigna will never forgive me.\n\nAnd her mother—she'll give me that look.
Bala? Bala … ah, yes, the Ashlander! You remember her, don't you dear?\n\nMy performance must have been quite convincing.
There's no challenge in terrorizing servants. I wanted to crush someone's dreams.\n\nI convinced her I was desperately in love. I said I would leave my wife. It's a shame, though.
That I died! Please, tell her you found me. Say that I'm still passionate for her.\n\nGodyna and I will have a delightful time watching her heart shatter.
Where is he? What did he say?\n\nI'm shaking. I miss him so much.
The one that says her daughter married a fool. Well, Norgred Hardhelm is no fool!\n\nA witch cast a spell. That's the only explanation for why that axe left my hands.
Mining sulfur, of course. We get it from the pools.\n\nAlchemists pay a premium for it. They use it in potions, but they don't want to gather it themselves.
Take a deep breath! It smells like rotten eggs here, night and day. It gets in your clothes and your hair. \n\nMost alchemists are just too proper to put up with the smell. Can't blame them.
My wife! What about the witch? Oh gods, I need to get that axe back.
I think I remember fighting those husks. \n\nBut thanks for finding the <<1>>. I don't like it when <<2>> gets upset. She gets very loud.
You doubt my skill? If it's any consolation, what's left of you won't take much effort to clean up.\n\nMe, I'm a ghost already, so it hardly matters.
Good for you. Prepare yourself.

This is all their fault—the hauntings, the destroyed crops, the ruin of a beautiful home. They're foul-smelling animals. I told Tiril that Cat-Men make poor slaves.\n\nAnd then there's that monster. They brought it here.

Ra-shadda summoned it. He's some kind of shaman. My husband broke up a ritual that Cat-Man was performing a few nights ago. We punished everyone there and confiscated a totem from their makeshift altar.\n\nThe creature's afraid of that totem.

Once free, they will hide in the marsh until the Khajiit are done looting our village.\n\nThey're lazy creatures, easily distracted. They will grow bored and depart long before they can capture us again.
Only the sacred stones and the Hist branch matter. Anything else they take is just a thing, unimportant and easily replaced. \n\nBut the villagers, they cannot be replaced. Please, save them.
And you're an outsider fumbling around in events you don't understand.\n\nLeave this place before you do something you'll regret.

You've spent too much time with miserable Dark Elves and stupid Nords. I'll not be baited by your taunts. \n\nI'm long gone from this place, fool. You're speaking to an echo. You cannot harm me any more than you can hurt your own shadow.

And I will enjoy watching you fumble and fail!\n\nGo back to my sister and tell her of her thin-scaled mate's failure. Vara-Zeen was never worthy to lead the village. He couldn't stop me and he was never worthy of my sister!
I'll answer what I can—but ask quickly!

The Goblins have slaughtered many of my men. Even my eldest son has been sent to his funeral pyre. Now my youngest son, Bjorick, has gone missing.\n\nTroll's blood, traveler! These little vermin are a plague on us.

You want to help? Get out there and kill some of those stinking Gobs.\n\nBjorick is nearby. I heard him call my name. If you can distract the Gobs, I think I can get to him. Meet me here when you're done.

They set up a tent for her along the shore. I'm sure you'll find her there, gloating over the treasures she stole from our village.\n\nAnd Seeks-the-Night gave her the Hist branch as a gift! That's the most profane disrespect a Saxhleel can show.

Yes, as much as it pains me to admit it. My egg-sac of a brother always believed he would be the next village elder, but Vara-Zeen was chosen instead.\n\nSeeks-the-Night always hated Vara-Zeen, but to doom us to slavery? I spit on my own egg-brother!
My middle son, <<1>>, is leading the search for Bjorick west of the hall. Go help him find his missing brother and end the nightmare that has befallen my household.

He fears vengeance for all he's done, and he's right to be afraid. But he forgets the power of the Hist. I believe we can use the Hist to force him to return. \n\nPerhaps that is why he took the branch and gave it to the Khajiit in the first place.
It's said a Saxhleel can sometimes be called home by the Hist. I'll give you the branch. Use it to mark the door to my brother's home. \n\nIf it summons him, kill Seeks-the-Night. Kill my brother.

Fire! It's the Vereansu's answer to everything. To them, it purifies plague victims and blasphemers alike.\n\nThose kwama droppings! I tried to circle around a pack of plague husks and ran right into an Ashlander patrol.
Warriors! To me!\n\nProtect the hall and safeguard the innocents. Defend the hold!
We can't go. Not yet! The Vereansu believe we defiled the Tear of Saint Veloth. They plan to destroy it.\n\nWe have to get to the monastery and save the Tear. If they destroy it, we're all lost.
Crush the eggs. Crush them! That will draw out the ugly spider queen and her Goblin ally.\n\nSovngarde awaits. We'll kill these beasts and send the Goblin horde to the pits. Ysgramor!
It's time. Honor Mavos at this brazier in the center of Othrenis. \n\nBy the way, the dead may want your blood for daring to disturb a highborn. I'll just wait over here until you're done.
Yes, I could, if I remembered. There's not much use for remembering once you're dead.\n\nDon't pester me with questions, worm! I'm beginning to forget why I should care about the living.
He's important, so he gets the important-looking tomb. It's the largest crypt in the necropolis.\n\nI'll … uh … be gathering my notes. Don't wait for me.

Very brave, acolyte. Now, listen. Mavos can't last much longer. He gained control of two powerful guardian atronachs. \n\nThey should be able to hold even Balreth. Ragebinder and Blaze. Go to the braziers. Summon them, and let this day be done.
Interesting lot. They aren't nomads like most Ashlanders. They've been in this vale for as long as anyone can remember. But, since they don't welcome visitors, they're a mystery to most.

The snakes that dwell in the vale have unique and valuable skins. Some even say they're infused with Magicka, but people say a lot of things. \n\nThe point is, those snake skins are worth a small fortune to the tribe.
Touch the altar! Balreth's power flows into the guardians. He should be bound … or he might explode.\n\nAnyway, be prepared for anything, apprentice!
Gifts from merchants often have strings attached.

What does House Hlaalu know of good will? Their kind is only interested in profit. \n\nI'll take his bauble, but I won't be his puppet. The Farseer has no time for traders. Tell him he's wasting his time.

There is a hidden passage near here, which will take you to the northern part of the city.\n\nLord Montclair won't suffer from the loss of a few soldiers. There's no need to slaughter your way through his front line when you can go through the back.
Only a fool risks his life for no gain. But, I will not stand in your way to get yourself killed.\n\nThe passage is through a well at the center of the city, if you ever tire of warming your blade.
Yes, thanks to your swift action! The serpentbounds' behavior concerns me, though.
Perhaps. But our faith teaches us that there is no such thing as coincidence. \n\nThis omen should not be taken lightly, You need to speak to Farseer Bodani right away.

I know why you're here. I was going to ignore your petitioning, just as we've ignored the merchant these many days. \n\nBut your quick defense of Iru-Ahan shows me you are honorable and willing to help others.
Signs and portents are everywhere, if we choose to see them. \n\nSomething is causing a disturbance here in the vale. It could be your arrival, or the presence of the Hlaalu merchant.

I had a vision. You walked the Coiled Path and braved the Trial of the Ghost Snake. Your fate was unclear to me.\n\nGhost Snake calls to you, and you must answer. The outcome of your trial will determine how we deal with the merchant.

"The spell is something the Dark Elf savages use to speak with their 'honored dead.' I can adapt it to enslave the souls of Pact troops. If I can perfect it, the living dead will be the perfect weapon for this siege."
My spies are telling me <<1>> sent most of his forces to <<2>>. He shouldn't have the strength to hold <<3>>, but he's repelling our attacks.\n\nI think I know how he's doing this. I hope I'm wrong.
Speak quickly, I feel my life falling away from me.

I'm already dead, but my body has not yet realized it. I've forced the Reachmen to pay quite a toll for my end, but I must pay my share as well.\n\nDon't worry about me; as long as <<1>> dies, I die well.

Sadly, I have the heart of a young warrior in an old man's body. My passions aren't quiet, and seeing <<1>> again banished all thoughts but duty and vengeance from my mind.\n\nIf only my soldiers didn't need to pay the price for my sins ….
Desert Evermore? I would never do such a a thing.\n\nDesert that rat Renchent who thinks himself regent but leaves his people to die on Reach-made swords? Him I'd desert in a heartbeat.
Luckly you. A less fortunate brother … lost his nearby.\n\nTry not to loose it again.
Azura bless you! I spoke with a wise woman. She told me to gather Graven Caps near the tombs.\n\nI'd collect some, but the wardens would stop me. I wouldn't even be here if it wasn't for Eanen!

I wouldn't worry about it. I whipped him for messing up our shipments and he's probably off sulking.\n\nThe boy claims it wasn't his fault that we received the wrong crates. Like I believe that! He needs to pay better attention.
They're stacked on the other side of the shed. Damned kids broke into them during the night. Took whatever was in them and ran.\n\nIf you want to pick through the broken crates, be my guest.
You're a little like Eanen. He was always gentle and kind with me.\n\nNow to find him. I'll search the tombs to the southeast. Would you search to the west?

My grandsire was a powerful shaman. He passed down an ancient formula for an elixir that allows a traveler to walk in the "otherworld" between the living and the dead. \n\nIt works on those who've become attuned to the realms beyond.
But … but he swore he would wait for me, no matter what!
Oh, thank you! \n\nQuickly, where is his tomb?
No! I don't believe it.\n\nYou must have found the wrong tomb.
Nothing at all. Don't mind me. I'm just a servant here.\n\nWhat's it to you, anyway? Why are you in my master's house?
He's an important person in Narsis. A writer. Writes all day. Writes all night.\n\nBut don't touch his journal. He can get frightfully angry.
How would I know? I sweep! I dust! I don't read!\n\nThe master would never let me look in his journal. His room upstairs is off limits. I stay down here, cleaning. Just as my master tells me.

Day 26\n\nThe plague is slowly spreading from Quarantine Serk, covering Deshaan like a black rain. Vox will be pleased. Many have left Narsis for Mournhold. They think they'll be safe there, but they can't escape the coming reckoning.

Day 42 \n\nWe figured out how to spread the plague. By injecting the substance into a corpse's blood and letting it fester, the plague's potency increases tenfold! It must be the dead blood. We need more bodies.

Day 32 \n\nThe substance isn't strong enough when added to water. The solution becomes diluted, and most of the effective properties fade. Until we can formulate a stronger version, we need to look for other ways to spread the plague.

Everyone knows my husband. Evis! If he hasn't borrowed something from you or finished off your ash-slake ale, then you're not trying very hard.\n\nHe was supposed to be back hours ago. That lazy lout is late.
That would be a big help. I'm sure he's sleeping it off in one of the nearby houses.\n\nIf you find an Elf that smells of piss and ale, that's Evis. Tell him to hurry up or he's walking to Mournhold.
He ships our goods. He mentioned something about a botched delivery that he had to deal with.\n\nYou know what he's probably dealing with? His thirst for ale!
You're interrupting my interrogation, that's what. And just as I was about to get to my favorite part.\n\nI have no quarrel with you. Not yet. So go away.

That doesn't matter. We've linked strange shipments to this courier. He refuses to talk, but I've never met a man I couldn't break.\n\nTake this letter to Councilor Ralden. It explains how vials of the plague were shipped into Narsis.
Listen to me closely. You and I are on the same side here. I've been hired to track down the origins of the Llodos plague.
Never mind. I'll do this another way.\n\nKnow this, however. We've tracked shipments of the Llodos plague into Narsis, but we don't know what happened after they got here. Narsis is in danger.

Why is everyone in this town so damned stubborn? I'm armed to the teeth and dangerous as all get out. And you're not scared? Not even a little?\n\nFine. You're lucky I don't feel like killing you today. Do what you will.
The warm-blood was sent by those who honor and protect this Vale. Most curious.
Ssssss! Let me show you!
Every path leads in two directions: into light and into darkness. \n\nLight and dark. Good and evil. Sunlight and shadow. Two sides to all things, little warm-blood.
Beyond "no one will work together"?\n\nEach faction has a different reason. Which would you like to know about?
I wish I knew their complaint. They refuse to talk to us. I even went to speak with their quarter's leader, <<1>>.\n\nShe accused me of plotting to kill a tree. As if I cared about such things!

The Nords in town are lumber traders from the Rift. You might have noticed a lack of trees.\n\nWhen we asked <<1>> to help defend the town, he accused us of being "fancy." I assume that's an insult in Skyrim. Also, I think he was drunk.

Our people love fighting. It's our nature. We fight the land just to survive. Only the Dunmer's natural superiority allows us to flourish in this wasteland.\n\nLately, our people have been demoralized. Even <<1>> at the Tribunal Temple expects defeat.

We received intelligence this was a military training ground for mages. Clearly … clearly we were wrong. My commanding officer was so certain. She was the one that began smashing relics. She was the one that unleashed the curse.
I'll try. But I'll never forgive the Covenant for my son's death.

Ahh, good! Sotha Sil has smiled on us, finally. All we needed was another pair of hands. Take those components and mix them in this Daedric urn. They'll coalesce into a potent Etheric Totem. \n\nThat will be much better than the potion we were using.
Vox? Never heard of her. Why would I be afraid of a Vox?\n\nNow will you let me go, so I can take my wife to Mournhold?
No more torture! I've had enough for one day. I'll tell you the same thing I told the crazy lady.\n\nThe shipment contained something for the Maulborn camped outside town. That's all I know!
Ha! That's hilarious. Let me go?\n\nYou can tell the house officials to go lick a guar. They don't know what's coming. None of you do.

And I messed up! I delivered the shipment to the wrong location.\n\nBut I fixed it. I fixed everything. Just you wait. Those missing villagers? It's no coincidence. You'll see. Vox will destroy you all!
Some of our people heard a Dark Elf talking to others of his kind. He asked if they'd seen the Dres rowing out to our Hist Tree. He saw jars of poison in the boat.\n\nThat's not hard to believe.

Rhavil Urano. My people overheard him at the inn. He was drunk and talking too loud.\n\nNo one spoke to him directly. It's never been wise for an Argonian to confront a Dark Elf, especially lately. We're far from Black Marsh.

The Dres have always regarded Argonians as little more than savage children.\n\nWe needed to be "civilized," so they "uplifted" us by putting us to work as slaves on plantations and in mines. No more. Now we speak beside them in the council.
No, but it's not difficult to believe, is it?\n\nThe Dres think we're little more than animals. But the Pact freed us. What they can't enslave, they destroy.

The Mabrigash must make their own choices. Connect with the world outside or remain isolated. It is never only light or shadow.  \n\nAs long as they honor my kin and I, they are free to do as they please.

I am the Ghost Snake. I am both constant and ever-changing. One thing to you. Another, perhaps, to the Mabrigash. \n\nAid the Mabrigash as you will. The choice is yours to make. I can send you back to the Farseer. She waits for you at her tent.

While you were gathering mudcrab meat and reeds, the guards caught him trying to harm our Hist. We can't get anything out of him but his name and House.\n\nSeems the rumors were true. House Dres is trying to murder our Hist.
You may do as you wish, but his mind is boiling. His words skitter like a mudcrab in a pan.\n\nYou will gather no moisture from this one.
He was scratching at the bark, licking our tree! When the guards shouted at him, he dropped an empty bottle. \n\nNow he's very ill. The truth is as plain as the face of Masser.

Ghost Snake is wise but inscrutable. I had hoped he would demand that we bring the merchant to him.\n\nIt's no coincidence that you arrived at the same time as the merchant. You are bound up in this. You must help us decide.
I crafted a Snake Totem representing the entwined fates of the Mabrigash and the merchant. Get it from my tent. \n\nI will have the merchant brought here.
Very well, I'll do it.
Now you must choose. If the Mabrigash are to remain isolated, place the totem in the fire. If we are to change our ways and trade with the Hlaalu, give the totem to the merchant.
Seek guidance where you would. Speak to my people, the merchant, or even the merchant's assistant, if you wish.\n\nBut then you must choose.
He will remain in the Vale, serving the Ghost Snake.

We know where the missing villagers are, but we need your help. Due to the lockdown, no one can leave Narsis. No one, that is, except you.\n\nDon't look to the sky. Follow the Star. She provides the key. She will guide your way.
So they treat me like some sort of criminal? I've been nothing but respectful!\n\nAnd trade would help them.
Of course I benefit! I'm a merchant. Trading is what I do! \n\nHow about this? Propose a limited trade agreement, on their terms, and I'll agree to keep other traders away from the Vale.

I understand your confusion, my friend. The Herd Mother has long given us a unique ritual, a way to mount our horses that has nothing to do with reins or saddles.\n\nWe become one with the beasts, and run together as one body, one mind.

This is the first time they've used the ritual. It can be overwhelming, at first, and the foals fled before we could restrain them. \n\nNow, though they are merged with their beasts, they act only as riders. They have no control.
The Star? What are you talking about? Has the plague rattled your senses?\n\nLeave me alone. I have plants to tend to.
Help? Is that what you're doing?\n\nListen. You didn't hear it from me. Star is a cat. She runs around in front of the kinhouse. Now go away and leave me be.
Then I welcome you, Telvanni-chosen. \n\nThe spellplague emanates from the hidden chamber. Normally a portal provides access, but the curse has disrupted it.
Ok I'll help.
When the portal is open, enter the hidden chamber. Dispel the remnant of the ancient magics. Confront whatever powers the curse.\n\nEven I don't know what you must face within.
Where did you hear about Star? I'm sorry. I can't help you.\n\nSpeak to Halyen. I have nothing else to say to you.
I like the color of your gold! I know Star. She's a stray cat. Very smart. Runs around like she's the house councilor, she does.\n\nIf you want to know more, talk to Halyen.
So those damned fools are at it again? Don't get involved. Just get out of here before the plague gets you.

A damned smart cat!\n\nThe group meets in secret. They're trying to find their missing friends and family. They don't trust House Hlaalu or the guards, but they aren't soldiers. They're going to get themselves killed.
Star the Cat. That's how they contact each other. Find her by the kinhouse. Follow her. She reveals the location of today's secret meeting. They constantly change locations.
We're tired of waiting for House Hlaalu to act. We know where our people are being held. But because of the lockdown, we can't go get them.
I watched the Maulborn abduct my egg-sister. I saw where they took her.\n\nI saw Councilor Ralden and Advisor Giron go to the same place. You have to help us!
So that's it. Hlaalu's leader disappears, and they finally decide to take action?\n\nI don't give a damn about Councilor Ralden. I just want our people back.
Act! We'll get weapons, ignore the lockdown, and rescue our people. If anyone tries to stop us, we'll cut them down.\n\nAre you going to help us or not?
We need weapons. We can't fight the Maulborn with our bare hands.
We're going to rescue our families or die trying. I don't trust you, outsider. We'll deal with this ourselves.\n\nLeave us. Run back to your house masters and stay out of our way.
I've been passing information to him. My mother vanished, but I have my orders. So, I've been hoping Madras and his people would find something I could take to the house leaders.
Those people just want to see their friends and families again. But I don't want them to get hurt. Calling the guards will just make the situation worse.
What did I do? What did it do to me? I see. I feel. I'm awake. \n\nI touched it. It smelled like flowers and black earth. It tasted like rain and summer wind and the deepest green.
Keep your voice down. Say that name too loudly, and they'll slap you in chains. Now what do you want?
Then the time has come. Take this whistle. When you're near the kinhouse, blow it. The sound will be our signal to create a distraction.
Use the key downstairs to open as many weapon crates as you can. With them, we can arm the villagers.\n\nNow hurry. And don't screw up.
Use the distraction to enter the kinhouse. Head upstairs and search for a set of keys to the armory.\n\nBut don't dawdle. The guards won't leave their posts for long.
I hope so. We only have so many people willing to sacrifice themselves for our cause.\n\nTake the whistle. Same plan as before. Blow it, grab the weapons, get out.
I never saw him before. I asked him for coin to get more skooma.\n\nHe was a Dunmer. Someone called him … Bravil? Weevil? Wabbajack? Rhavil! That's it.
He said the tree's sap would be better than skooma. He was right.\n\nHe said the Argonians might be angry. Do you think they're angry? To me they always look angry. It's the teeth.

<<1>>, that Argonian who's advising <<2>>, thinks the coral summoned the dreugh to defend itself.\n\nFact is, we were losing when the dreugh showed up and altered the battle. Now we need to preserve the few troops we have.

The coral summoned dreugh to defend itself. The coral thinks and reasons. We must ally ourselves with it. If we show it we're peaceful, it will turn the dreugh against our enemies.\n\nI'm still working on how to do that.

Just so. The Brothers of Strife are destruction incarnate: flaming fury, crushing all in their path. They cannot be controlled or channeled, only imprisoned.\n\nEbonheart is near, and Conele would like it burned to the ground. We have to stop her.

The waters of his mind are boiling. In his current state, he could harm others. We will keep him here with us until he calms down.\n\nI have never seen a Dark Elf drink from a Hist. He may never recover.

The Hist are for the Saxhleel—or the Argonians, if you prefer that name. What passes between us and the trees is beyond the ken of other races. It is sacred.\n\nAs for what happened to him, I do not know. What happens when a fish swims in ale?
Of course he did. Ralden hasn't been able to make a decision on his own in years. At least he's finally doing the right thing.\n\nAs for you, I have something you can do.
I suggest you slice a path through their camps by the lake. Look for anything that will tell us the location of the Llodos plague.\n\nReturn when you find something.
The Maulborn are obviously involved. Any fool can see that.\n\nWith the city sealed, all of the guards will be busy. However, you don't have those responsibilities.
He has done what is never done. Normally, he would be killed for this blasphemy, but he's just a poor dupe. \n\nRhavil tricked him. It is Rhavil who should swallow the razor-eel.

Of course he did. Sending an overconfident outsider into camps full of Maulborn certainly sounds like a day at the fair.\n\nAnd if they killed you, you'd never find out that he brought the plague to Narsis, would you?
This doesn't look good. There must be a reason why Giron wanted Narsis sealed and why he wanted you dead. Get back there and find out.

I've been watching Narsis for weeks. We even have an agent inside the kinhouse. Anything that enters or leaves Narsis is tracked, and those broken crates had Giron's name written all over them.\n\nThe question is, why? What have you discovered?
The organization I belong to does two things: finds targets and eliminates targets. My target happens to be connected to the Llodos plague.\n\nOur goals overlap. Let's leave it at that.
Not your concern. Just remember what I told you. We're on the same side.\n\nAnd don't get yourself killed, hero. Narsis needs you.

Let's just say I'm well informed. I've suspected the connection for a while and his abduction of the councilor confirms it.\n\nMy associate and I tend to avoid situations not covered by our contracts. Still, we might be able to assist one another.
A group of townfolk meets in secret. They're trying to find the missing people. Talk to them. You may be able to help each other.
A door leads to the ruins, west of Narsis. That's where they've been hiding our people.\n\nIt doesn't matter, though. Madras and the townfolk aren't trained to fight.
An advisor from Mournhold sent to assist Narsis. That's all you need to know.\n\nNow please, unless you have something useful that I must know about, leave me be.
Madras gave me this key to give to you. Now please hurry. It was scary watching my friends try to figure out which end of a sword to hold.

We were ambushed in the ruins. During the fighting, I slipped past the others and found the key to this building.\n\nOur missing people are here. Many are alive, but by the Three! What were they doing to the dead? It's horrifying!
They were mixing the Llodos substance with the corpses. The plague festered in them. They were bled into our water supply!\n\nThat's why Giron didn't want us to leave! He wanted to infect us all!
Of course. I barely arrived in time. They were about to kill Ralden. At least I was able to save one life today.\n\nPlease, hurry. These people need healers immediately.
You actually succeeded? Well done.\n\nI gathered the guards and came as quickly as possible. A contingent has gone into the ruins to deal with the remaining Maulborn. What happened in there?
So that's why he wanted Narsis sealed. He wanted easy access to more plague carriers.\n\nHouse Hlaalu will make sure no one drinks the water until the lake is cleansed.
Ruins beneath Narsis. You can find the entrance to the west. Old door, looks out of place against the rocks. Door's locked to keep people out of the ruins.\n\nGuess that didn't work out.
Don't thank me. You're the one rushing into the fire. I should be thanking you.\n\nJust be careful down there. If what Madras said is true, you're going to run into a lot of opposition.
It's too late for me, but you must listen. Don't let anyone drink the water. The lake must be cleansed.\n\nAnd I need to tell you about Vox.
She's their leader. Narsis is only the beginning. They're making Llodos plague in the Gorge. They're going to spread it to … to Mour ….
I see. Ralden was a good man who cared for his people. He should be remembered that way.\n\nThe guards are dealing with the Maulborn in the ruins. What happened in there?
So that's why he wanted Narsis locked down. He wanted a ready supply of plague carriers.\n\nHouse Hlaalu will make sure no one drinks from the lake until it's cleansed.
We fight drunk! We've got a keg of fine, strong mead from Riften right here. Pour yourself a mug and get to it.\n\nUnless you're too fancy, of course.
Ha ha ha! You could only beat me if I was blind, stinking sober … and I'm not!
What? Well, this is unexpected! \n\nWhen they bound me up like a criminal and dragged me over here, I thought I was done for!
Har har! You're clever, you are. Let's see how well you take a blow.
Are you asking for a challenge? Shor's bones! I thought today was going to be dull.
I said I would. And I don't go back on my word.\n\nI hope the rest of the Pact fights like you, not that milk-drinking Urano.

<<1>>, that Dark Elf here before you. He kept asking to buy our lumber so we'd leave town. I told him no, we had a contract to keep, but he offered to double it.\n\nNo one pays that much for wood, even good Rift spruce. What a skeever.

Don't know, and didn't ask. His story smelled like last week's fish. Whole time we were talking, he kept looking around for a crack to ooze through. Sweatin' like.\n\nThe boys ran him off with a few light cuffs to the head. He hasn't come back since.
There's some kind of fumes leaking into the mine. They're making the kwama go crazy and become violent. It's a disaster!

Giant domesticated insects. Deepcrag is a kwama mine. We raise them and harvest their eggs.\n\nThey're usually as docile as cows, but those gas fumes have them so riled up they're downright bloodthirsty. I'm not going back in there!
Use the anvil across the hall. Make sure you have the ingredients with you, and then just make use of the recipe in your book. \n\nMay Kynareth guide your hammer!
A recruit, eh? Welcome to the forge! As a smith you'd use pressure and fire to reshape the world to your will. \n\nPlate armor and well sharpened swords are our stock in trade.

Ore for armors and weapons are found in the mountains and near rocky outcroppings. Magical metals for enchantments are found near ancient ruins.\n\nMinerals are found by rocky outcroppings and are used to form the base of powerful concoctions.

We combine minerals and magic to create restoratives for mages. We forge enchanted trinkets that rogues can clip to their gear, granting them enhanced abilities. \n\nWe're flame and metal and magic combined! So! What do you say?

Use the anvil across the hall. Make sure you have the ingredients: a copper ingot, and the pine charcoal you bought from my apprentice. \n\nThen just open your recipe book, and follow the instructions.
Gather five pieces of copper ore from the old mine south of the docks.\n\nThen open your recipe book and select the oxidized copper ingot recipe. Follow that recipe to make the ingot.
What happened, my new recruit? A troll steal it from you? Hah!\n\nMy apprentice might have another for sale. Check with him.
I knew the forge was in your soul, recruit. You've learned enough to attempt the apprentice's trial.\n\nThe question is, are you ready to put your skills to the test?

Make me a sword, a blade fit for a warrior. Go to my apprentice and purchase some pine characoal. Use the charcoal and a copper ingot at the crafting table to make that sword.\n\nWhen you're done, return and show me your work.

Gather five pieces of copper ore from the tailings dumped in that old mine I told you about. Then open your recipe book and select the copper ingot recipe. \n\nFollow that recipe to make the ingot. Easy as bleeding out a skeever!
Kynareth guide your hammer blows, my new recruit. I'm always glad to welcome someone to the forge. \n\nLet's begin with the basics of shaping metal.

Head out to the old copper mine south of the docks. It's mostly tapped out these days, and rumors say brigands use it for smuggling.\n\nThere should be some low grade ore left behind. Gather some, and return to me.

Open your recipe book and go to the Research section. Make an entry about the sword there. \n\nYou'll need to truly study the sword. Test the edge. See how the tang and hilt are attached. Bend it till it snaps. Break it down. Know how it was made.

Good. It's not inside you. Listen to me: there's some … horror … making copies of people. It kills you, then makes a copy of your body for its own.\n\nBut it's not a perfect copy. It can't mimic speech.

I had to do it. They were changing. \n\nYou think I'm mad? See for yourself. I was in the cellar of that stable. It leapt into one of my troops, and I trapped it down there. Go in and introduce yourself.
Burn the flowers at each shrine. They're a rare variety of gold kanet called "Roland's Tears" and are sacred to the Three.\n\nI pray they hear you.
The Tribunal does not abandon their people. Just as a parent shelters children from dangers they cannot comprehend, the Three shelter the Dunmer from threats beyond their ken.

Tell him that My Lady is mindful of his doubt and fear. There is no shame in either, so long as he helps others bear their burdens.\n\nBy helping others, his fears will be allayed, but if he spreads his despair, My Lady will chastise him.
Ah. You are the child whose soul was stolen. My Lady is concerned for you.\n\nAlmalexia is the Merciful Healing Mother of the Dunmer. She is the most beloved of the Tribunal.
I am merely a servant and messenger of my Lady, not a teacher or priest.\n\nSeek the temples and libraries to learn more. Perhaps, in time, you may speak to Almalexia herself.
All prayers are heard. Not all are acknowledged.

Every small cog drives a greater gear. Each is necessary; otherwise, the whole collapses.\n\nWhen any cog shivers from the stresses on it, the Master feels it, but the load he assigns it is no more than he knows it can bear.
Wizard. Mystic. Master of the Clockwork City. An architect of time and a binder of Oblivion. One who masters the tools that mastered others.\n\nDoes this answer satisfy?
Good.\n\nSeek. Learn. When you are prepared, find the Master. He will be interested to hear your conclusions.

Actions carry conviction better than words. A skilled Poet arranges for others to be where they should be, when they should be, to fulfill his needs and desires.\n\nYet the question Sildras asked was not the one in his heart.

A man of poisoned words put doubt in Sildras' heart. He said the Poet is less than He once was.\n\nTell the disciple that Vivec's Words and Wit and Way of War are as keen as always. What is Vivec beyond these?
Did Telvanni send you? Thank you, stranger! \n\nI'm going to make a run for it.
The spirits are bursting from the dying. I'll remember that day until the day I die.\n\nBut that day won't be today. Tribunal bless you.
Three walk by your side, traveler.\n\nAnd may they curse the Covenant for all they've done here!

I was wounded in battle during the Akaviri invasion of Stonefalls years ago. A sweet soul named <<1>> nursed me back to health. \n\nThough her family disowned her, we were married a few years later. She has given much for our love.

Many of these milk-drinkers consider it heresy for a Dark Elf to marry one of another race. As if the Three care who we love and live for!\n\nDespite the hatred, Edwina and I have stood strong. Our love and land has endured … until now.
Look somewhere else. These are the General's private quarters. He doesn't allow visitors.
He hasn't been himself lately, that's true. \n\nAll right. Here's the key to his locked furniture. But remember, I'm watching you.
My family back in Mournhold needs the gold.\n\nAll right. Here's the key to his locked furniture. Just hurry it up before we both get caught.

I was a battlefield healer supporting the warriors at the Akaviri front. <<1>> took a grievous wound from one of the Akaviris' monstrous beasts.\n\nAs I cared for him, I fell in love with him. We've been together ever since.

Vivec is a Warrior Poet, the ruthless and elegant soul of his people. He guides and protects all. Sharp of eye and tongue is he. Long is his reach. Longer is his spear.\n\nHow can this question be on the lips of anyone in Morrowind?

The sniveling Dark Elf? He needed the fresh air. His words were addled. Telling everyone how I should run my town.\n\nAs for his concerns, the Dominion deals with the Khajiit, not us. And for the moment, she is protected.
You have it? Daril? Yes, I smell it on your fingers. Fresh and sweet, nice like rain. You didn't open it, did you? Maybe take some for yourself?\n\nPlease, I need it. Can I have it? I know things.

<The first scroll reads as follows.>\n\n"Disciplinary action against Captain Valec Doronil is necessary for insubordination and deflating the morale of Tal'Deic Fortress with unnecessary adherence to foolish protocol. His punishment: Execution."

Oh. It's words you want. Yes, the Khajiit, she has a name: <<1>>. There's a meeting. One of her kits and … and a foreigner. Soon, very soon! They meet in the warehouse south of here.\n\nYou get there first. Spy on them! Good, yes? Now, give me daril.

"Notice: My personal aide from Mournhold shall be appointed as retainer and stationed in the mess tent. He shall be accorded respect and asked no questions. Failure to adhere to this decree shall result in harsh disciplinary action."

The sermons of Vivec are beside every bed. Vivec's psalms are sighed from every maiden's lips. His wisdom makes his people as hard, capable, and enduring as the Poet himself. \n\nAll know Vivec, for Vivec would have it so.

No matter how often I punish them, some of these soldiers must adhere to rules and regulations. Where's the fun in that, I ask you?\n\nSince you're here, I think we have a Nord spy in the fort. Expose this spy and I'll make you a captain.

That's what makes this spy so dangerous! And never question my orders again. Never! Go expose Ragna Stormcrag for the spy she is. I command it!\n\nNow get out of here, both of you. I have things to do.
Well, that's a new one. \n\nI've been the General's bodyguard for nearly a decade. If I was plotting against him, I think I'd have made my move by now.
I've devoted my life to protecting the General and helping the Pact. That's why I need to find out what's wrong with him. \n\nMaybe you can help me.

I'm risking my neck telling you this, but I don't know what else to do. \n\nI think the General's gone mad. One moment he sees traitors everywhere, the next he's canceling security patrols. There's no telling what crazy whim will spur him on next.
It's the primary trading route between Mournhold and the west. It's also home to a trader's camp. Every caravan that comes through this part of Deshaan depends on that camp.

I … I see. I hadn't considered there might be threats more grave than the Covenant invasion. You would think, given all we know of the treachery of Coldharbour, that I would see that.\n\nWhat of Sotha Sil?
That's an excellent question. Harrassing caravans seems to go against their usual method of operations, doesn't it?
A moment is all I can spare, I'm afraid. The General is already greatly displeased with me.
I am ashamed. The Three have shown more faith in me than I have in them.\n\nI dread asking this, but what of Lord Vivec?

I am a soldier, loyal to my house and the Ebonheart Pact. I am sworn to obey my superiors without question. I don't have the luxury of questioning orders, no matter how suspect.\n\nIf I'm to be executed, so be it. Until then, leave me to my duty.

I wish I knew. I've always served dutifully, followed the will of the Tribunal, and defended the fortress with honor.\n\nI've even been enforcing the General's nonsensical orders, usually against my better judgment.
Only indirectly. We see the Three less every year. They no longer make their annual pilgrimage to Red Mountain on Vvardenfell, and no one knows why.\n\nIt all seemed so convincing when he said it.
Ha! Yes, I should have known. Vivec is the most subtle of the Three.\n\nIt's true. I've been counseling a Dunmer who questions his faith. He told me the Tribunal are losing their powers.
His name is <<1>>. He hasn't come to pray for days now.\n\nHe was in such despair. I think he'd even stopped bathing. The last time I saw him he smelled terrible, like fresh offal.

The alchemist who created the Llodos plague. Merdyndril. He's making it stronger. More potent. \n\nThe Maulborn plan to smuggle it into Mournhold. Infect the whole city. There's no time. You need to stop them!
The Maulborn can't bring cargo through the city gates without official papers. They're carrying forged shipping manifests.

"When you're able to slip away unnoticed, find the others in the ruins by the river. I ordered the soldiers to avoid the area, so you should have no trouble. Destroy this note after you read it, Durel Gilveni, or I will burn you to cinders."
So, the old scoundrel sent you over here to get something from me? Well no one gets something for nothing. All you have to do is simply convince me to give it to you.
Maybe. It's worth a try.\n\nTake out some of the Maulborn down in the traders' camp. Get those forged papers!
I don't have a brok.. I see. Yes well, good point. Here is my key. Simply open the chest and take what you would like. I mourn for the loss of good manners, today.
My. You are a charmer. Very well. Here is the key. When you finish with that oath, perhaps you will come back and visit. Here is my key. Use it to get what you need from the box behind me.
Ahhh.. yes. Nothing lubricates the cogs of understanding, like a little grease on fingers holding coins.  How wonderful. Take this key and use it on the chest behind me to open the box.
That's a great relief. Well done.\n\nThe Covenant troops haven't left their encampment to the west, but it's only a matter of time before our inactivity encourages them.

I don't know this mer. Why would he cause so much trouble?\n\nPerhaps he's an agent of Sheogorath. That's an unpleasant thought. The Daedra of Chaos is worse than any mere Covenant army. Can you aid me further?
And which do you think I should have, the Foozle or the Woozle?
Rhavil must have a house in town. I'd like you to find it and watch him.\n\nI'd like to see myself, but I'm sure he'll recognize me, so I'll need to cast a spell on you.
Search for Rhavil's home. I expect it's on the west side of town.
Commoners would call it a scrying spell, but I'm beyond such crude hedge magic. It will enable me to see and hear what you do. Furthermore, I'll be able to "speak" to you.
The foozle it is. Here please give me the foozle.
The woozle. Interesting. Yes, please. Hand it over.
Well, a Foozle is very foozley you know, I mean you just can't help but look at the curves and say, "Wow! Now that really hoops my fooz!"
Dare. Dare! The Woozle. We-heh-hell the WOOZLE is so hard and solid. I mean, you know where you stand with people when you have a Woozle!
So that silly fool sent you for my Woozle? You can have my Woozle when you defeat me in one-on-one personal combat. Think you can do that?
Let's see what you have then, meat.
Maybe you should go speak with Donkey then. I am sure he could sell you a used Woozle. Hah!
A sleezle. Yes, my long lost brother liked sleezles. That's the one for me.
A Sleezle is, well, it is just so desirable. I mean, I'm putting my faith in you that you won't tell anyone of my rampant naughtiness in seeking it. But, EVERYONE wants one, we just don't admit it.
Let me guess. You've been talking to Fervyn. Decent cook, but doesn't have the sense Azura gave a sheep. He should learn to leave well enough alone.\n\nJust walk away. This isn't your concern.

It's not up to me! General Gavryn made them enforcers. That gives them the authority to do whatever they want. If I so much as mention it, I'm as good as dead.\n\nSorry, but I'm not sticking my head through that particular noose.
Another fool with a death wish. But for the sport of it, why don't you make the first strike? If it doesn't kill me, I'll finish you off quick.

Your next trial is that of the Heart, where unnecessary distraction and digression lead to failure. Follow the well-traveled path marked by statuary. Speed is of utmost importance.\n\n<<1>> awaits you at the finish. Are you ready?
Good question. Before we strike back, we need to gather our swords. \n\nI wish I knew how many of the others survived.
Mavos is ancient, so he knew ancient secrets. How else?\n\nHe helped bind this dangerous weapon, but he died a long, long time ago.

Alexandra Conele's army outnumbers us five to one. If the dreugh hadn't attacked us, we'd have been wiped out.\n\nNow the dreugh are burying my men in mud. Unless that stops, we can't keep Conele from getting the Coral Heart.

<<1>> thinks Conele wants to use it to command a Brother of Strife. Sings-With-Reed knows more about that.\n\nI need you to look for survivors in the mud mounds. Oh, and the Daggers caught Galyn. You need to rescue her.

During the First Era, the Chimer created the Brothers of Strife in a desperate bid to defeat their enemies.\n\nLook what it did in a single day! My scales shrivel thinking about that heat. Who would let it roam free?
Well …. You've proven yourself a friend of our village. As a friend, we'll entrust you with our secret. \n\nIt's simpler to show than explain. Please, do not be alarmed.

Tanval Indoril and his Vanguard stopped here on their way to the Tormented Spire.\n\nAt first, the grandmaster refused Tanval access to the mountain. Then Tanval snapped. He ordered his Vanguard to take the grandmaster's son hostage.

Captain, I'm counting on you to keep the Vanguard in line. The grandmaster's son is not to be harmed. \n\nSome of your best men are guarding him in the tomb west of Kragenmoor. Make sure he stays there until the rituals are complete.
No. We'll need to take the information from the Vanguard. As I see it, you have two options: you could sneak into their barracks here in town, or you could assault their camp.
Perhaps. Can't remember. Kaasha is a loyal servant, and doesn't wish harm to come to House Dres.
Together, we've begun the liberation of Kragenmoor. \n\nLet's get to my father. We'll run these Indoril out of town.

I did. Look, I don't know how this thing works. All I know is it climbs inside people. It kills them and then creates a double. When you kill the double, it sheds the body and runs.\n\nIf it needs a new place to hide, these burned corpses won't be it.
Thank the Three. Look, I know just how to get out of here. I used to play in these tombs as a child. \n\nFollow me quickly back to the city. We must speak to Father.
<<1>> did her best to scare the leggings off you, did she?\n\nDid she say whoever catches the murdering snowback is in for a nice pile of shiny gold coin?

I saw the creature slip into one of our guards. He attacked me, so I panicked and hit him with the totem. He wailed and ran off.\n\nI should have kept that totem with me. In all the chaos, I left it in our bedroom.
No! I don't believe you.\n\nI know that's him. There's just something wrong with him.
About time the vicecanons do their jobs. Arilen's body lies captive in the mortuary. I can't even see him, let alone bury him!\n\nWhy all these ridiculous delays? Dumac take this accursed town!

Finally looking into my brother's death, eh? I get it. I'm sure you and your vicecanon pals had better things to do than your jobs.\n\nNaldyn wasn't the brightest star in the sky, but he didn't deserve this.

Eroni and I always believed in the Pact. We came here to build a better life with Argonians and Nords alike.\n\nSome of my people blame the Shadowscales, but what would they gain from her death? We treat everyone the same. It makes no sense!

Shadowscales, who else? He spoke out against the Argonians, and rightly so! He was targeted for having the courage to say what we all think about them.\n\nI'm no bigot, but if you ask me, the world would be a better place without those scaly fetchers.
Most of Stormhold. Naldyn ran up a lot of debts. He also picked a lot of fights with the lizardskins.\n\nIf the Shadowscales didn't get him, it's because someone else moved faster.

Thank the gods! She's in the … mortuary, which they keep locked. But Eroni made those locks, so I have the master key. \n\nHere, take it. Please, find out who did this. Don't allow her to become a symbol against the Pact.
<A quick examination reveals Arilen's throat was slit.>\n\n<The shaman's notes might provide more insight.>
<Naldyn Indalor's body looks relatively unharmed, but the shaman's notes may reveal more.>
<Eroni's body and clothes seem charred.>\n\n<The shaman's notes may reveal what happened.>
Yes, if it isn't too late already. When Clavicus Vile cursed us with this hollow existence, he placed our spirits in the <<z:1>>. It must be recovered.

Stone and steel! Well done. Remember, you'll never learn anything by studying your own work. You can only learn new techniques by studying the work of others.\n\nI think you're ready to master your first recipe.

There's a recipe on the table just over there. The scroll itself is unimportant. It's just a list of ingredients and steps. \n\nIt's the knowledge that you gain through research, combined with the recipe, that allows you to fully master a crafting.
So embarrassing. I twisted my ankle during my Trial.\n\nWould you walk me back to Hissmir? I can't make it alone. So many beasts in this marsh!
Take this totem. <<1>> can let you inside the Daedric Prince's temple. Once inside, place the totem upon the <<z:2>> as an offering to Clavicus Vile.

Decades ago, the Knahaten flu swept through the land. The children were first. By Z'en, I can still see the bodies ….\n\nBut Z'en couldn't save us. So at <<1>>'s behest, I prayed to Clavicus Vile. He bestowed this mockery of salvation upon us.
Gethis saw Eroni … alive! He watched her enter their home, on the other side of Stormhold. He asked you to meet him there as soon as you can.

Eroni … my Eroni … she's gone, I know that. But when I saw her enter our home, I had to find out how she'd returned. That's when she stabbed me.\n\nIf that Argonian hadn't leapt between us, she'd have finished me off.

You call this survival? To never again taste guar-flesh, nor feel a lover's touch? We are but shadows in the water.\n\nSome feel the curse is a Daedra's cruel jest, yet I thank Clavicus Vile for a vital lesson. Immortality is the true curse, you see?

Fah, of course she'd sell them weapons. But protection? That's my business. Nobody but me offers protection here.\n\nSeems like your Dark Elf friend was correct. Some of the lads are aiding the Dominion, and they're doing it without my say-so.

With the <<z:1>> in the hands of the Worm Cult, they can influence us through our curse. They could force us to surrender, attack one another … any number of awful things.\n\nBut they don't possess your soul. They hold no power over you.
Ha! Sure, this one will tell you all about the secret hideout. And then, this one will invite One-Eye to tea.\n\nStupid shaveskin! Get out of this one's whiskers before he claws your muzzle off.

No, no. Your sincerity is obvious. This one likes his pelt unbloodied. \n\nThe Lady, yes! She dens in an abandoned mine. Awful, damp place, not like clear sky. Finding it is your challenge. There is no more help here.
You did, but that was not the true test. Was achieving your goal worth leaving behind someone in need?
Time is meaningless, for the true test lies within your own heart. You willingly failed a task to help someone in need. This was a necessary distraction.
Your time doesn't matter, for all advance. Reflect upon the failure within your own heart. This was the true test.
Well, now she's a popular one. Word's out that she's got money, hrr?  \n\nWhat makes you think you'll take a piece of the cut?
You think that comes for free? Ha! By your looks, you couldn't pay me enough to tell you what color her tail-fur is.\n\nGet out of my territory. You waste my time.
Good point. I prize my pelt.\n\nYou'll need this key to get into her hideout. Now you've got nothing to complain about, right?

That makes an unpleasant point. Well, it was only one Bosmer. No need for a bloodfeud.\n\nThere's a trapdoor in the small warehouse on the docks. That's where you need to go. Not that you'll get out alive.

I don't know, but he tried to save my life. They were still fighting when I crawled out the door. They both moved so fast.\n\nPlease, help him remove that imposter from my home. Don't worry about me. I'll soon see my true Eroni.
<The Argonian's body is still warm. It's covered in numerous cuts and scorchmarks.>\n\n<A careful search of his clothing discovers a hidden pocket containing a small journal.>
"Entry 442: Just watched <<1>> enter her home. This isn't right. Her body remains at the mortuary.\n\n"Going to see what this creature wants, and why it wears <<1>>'s face."
That soothes like a soft rain in the night. Her death will remind these mammal-lickers who's in charge here.\n\nThen we will talk about your Dominion problem.
Tanval has lost control. He must be stopped, but first, the grandmaster needs help.\n\n<<1>>, upstairs, will know more. Go. And good luck.
They're deeply personal ritual items. I slaved for two weeks making that kwama-grease candle. And the skull belonged to my favorite apprentice.\n\nWhy? Because I said so.
So you did. The trial forced you to choose between mercy and ambition. Your heart was big enough to achieve both.

That fool thinks Worm Cultists can sway the proud warriors of <<1>>, does he? I'd say the man lacked a spine, if I couldn't see it for myself.\n\nWe have no hearts to fill with fear, or blood to run cold. No blow is mortal. We're unstoppable.

We can't die, but we can fall for a time. It's how the cultists overpowered one of <<1>>'s acolytes and stole the <<z:2>>.\n\nHere's the temple key. When you're done, bring it to <<3>>. And tell her not to lose this one too, would you?
That's the spirit. Bring one for me.
I do! It's quite simple. Defeat any of these warriors in single combat to pass the Trial of the Fang.\n\nOh, and you must drink poison. Nothing permanent, just something to dull your senses.
<The Argonian in this hut was only recently killed. His body is still warm.>\n\n<The flesh of his body looks charred, just like <<1>>'s body. There's no mistaking the similarity in the wounds.>

We need no sleep or food. There's no sickness and no pain. If I fall in battle, I recover.\n\nI don't care if I can't see, taste, or feel the same way I used to. Clavicus Vile's blessing makes us perfect warriors.

You have come to challenge for leadership, yes? That is why <<1>> is dead, and you are not. You will be the new gang boss, if you … uh, decide not to kill us.\n\nLet me show you our usefulness! You desire the riches offered by the Dominion, yes?
<<1>> couldn't tell his coccyx from a hole in the ground.\n\nAs for <<2>>, well …. She needs to stop regretting who we once were and consider what we can become.
Sure, the ones with marrow where it counts. The rest listen to <<1>> whine about a "curse." But they'll come around.
I'll do what I've always done: protect my people. From themselves, if necessary.
Your sickly pallor comes from <<1>>. Excellent! I accept your challenge, and I offer you the honor of first strike.
If you desire to fight me as part of your Trial of the Fang, you must first swallow a mouthful of <<1>>.

Yes, but I've been here less than a day. Some of Stormhold's citizens were here longer, held in the alcoves nearby.\n\nI'll distract these Dominion snowbacks. Should buy you time to free the prisoners. Meet me on the surface!

Argonians! Always the unexpected. If I know Reed, she's already lurking near the Covenant camp. Look for her nearby.\n\nIf you can find her, bring her to the Coral Heart chamber. Then we can finish this.
I was thinking the same thing about your teeth.

Yes. Ra-shadda's beautiful wife, his most precious Jazadi … their lashes stripped her fur to the bone. She died from their torture. That is why this one called the dro-m'Athra.\n\nRa-shadda regrets this. Trading hate only brings more suffering.

Use the idol on the dark spirits, then kill them to charge it. While you hold the idol, anything that possesses you will cease to be. This is how we stop the monster.\n\nThis one must apologize to Ruvali. Meet us in her home when the idol is charged.

If Ra-shadda had many nights, he could explain. We integrate the gods of Tamriel with our own, so we can coexist. We also do it to amuse ourselves. \n\nBut there are Khajiiti spirits outside Tamriel's pantheon. Dark spirits. They are dro-m'Athra.

He spoke of his dead wife and his tortured people. He's mimicking sorrow, but Khajiit are incapable of normal emotions. Right?\n\nLook at my sweet Tiril. Ra-shadda must pay for Tiril's death. You agree with me, right?

That is your right. I have watched your progress, <<1>>. You have done well. This other has also passed the trials. You will both commune with the Hist today. When you are ready, drink the Hist Sap.\n\nThe effects can be disorienting, so be prepared.
I … I saw what you did to my fellow Maulborn. I don't want to end up like the others out in the great hall.
We're the Maulborn! You can't order us around! We control your general. We control your fortress.\n\nYou're too late to stop us this time.

All right, don't kill me! I'll tell you what I know.\n\nThe real general is dead. Sacrificed in the name of our great mistress, Magistrix Vox. We called forth a Daedric entity to replace him. The simulacrum wears his shape.
It's a Dremora. It's here, in one of the chambers below. It visits the general's corpse there every few hours to maintain his form. \n\nPlease, I've told you everything I know! Spare me!
Ithis Omalor of House Dres hired us to attack the caravan.\n\nHe had something to make the machines from the ruins fight alongside us.
I don't want to die. Can't you say I cooperated?\n\nDres raiders are going to the entrance of Mzithumz to ambush the Hlaalu guards. If you move fast, you can save them.
I don't know! It was like a magic wand, only metal. But the cursed thing blew up and the machines went berserk, attacking everybody.\n\nYou aren't going to kill me, are you?
Dead? Shor's bones, what happened? What's going on down there?\n\nI can't believe I failed him ….
Come to learn, recruit? Runecrafting is an ancient and serious art. We manipulate magicka, imbuing it into runes, jewels, and staves. \n\nWe can even transform a common robe into a source of power.

We scribe scrolls that any man or mer can cast. We prepare soul gems, trapping the essence of mystical creatures. They're used to enhance powerful magical gear.\n\nThe Runecrafter's life is one of power and contemplation. What say you?

Mystical components channel magicka through crafted items. They're usually found near rocky outcroppings. As are semi-precious stones, which can be crushed to make inks for scrolls.\n\nAnd, of course, spirits can always be captured to make soul gems.
I ask you again, because this is an important decision. Once you've joined with us … let's just say I take guild membership very seriously.\n\nDo you agree to join the Runecrafter's guild?
Very well. Welcome to the guild, recruit.\n\nI can almost guarantee no one will steal your soul and use it to fuel a mystic rite. Almost.
I ask you again, because this is an important decision to make: will you explore the mystic pathways between this world and the next?\n\nWill you join the Runecrafter's guild?
Excellent! Welcome to the guild, novice! \n\nI can almost guarantee no one will steal your soul and use it to fuel a mystic rite. Almost.
That explains why the General wanted us to avoid the ruins. This is terrible news. General Gavryn was stern and demanding, but he was a good leader.

Ha! That explains why the constructs turned on the raiders.\n\nI saw someone in Dres livery enter the ruins. He was fiddling with some kind of relic. I'd wager he's Ithis Omalor, the leader of this raiding party.
I'm not above giving the Dres some payback for the damage they caused.\n\nI need to clean up out here—but I want that Omalor fetcher who ran inside. Feel like doing some hunting?
We're not savages, novice. We learn by collaboration, by studying the techniques of others. You'll need to research the work of others, find inspiration from what they've done.
Open your recipe notebook to the research page. It's a seperate tab at the bottom of the book. You'll need to unravel the mystical bindings on the rune.\n\nThen enjoy the sizzle!

Oh, novice novice novice. Lucky for you that <<1>>  has some extras for sale. Do be more careful in the future. Leaving those things lying around could - I've heard - lead to horrible, horrible magickal accidents.\n\nI've heard.
Well done. Remember, you never learn anything by studying your own work. You only learn by studying the work of others.\n\nI think you're ready to master your first recipe.

On the table over there. The scroll itself is unimportant. It's just a list of ingredients and steps. \n\nIt's the knowledge that you gained through your research, combined with the recipe, that allows you to fully master a rune.
And all without rending your very soul from your body. Well done novice. \n\nYou've made some things, learned some things … I say you're almost an apprentice.
Let's have you … make me a rune. Buy some sandstone from <<1>>. Then head to the recipe table. Use the sandstone and gems to create the rune you just learned about.\n\nThen come show me your work.
Really? After what happened to my last novice .. it wasn't my fault anyway.\n\nAnyway. I have no problem taking you on as a novice runecrafter. Are you ready to begin with the basics?

To the south of the docks is the entrance to an abandoned mine. It's mostly tapped out these days, and rumors say brigands use it for smuggling.\n\nStill, there should be some gems left behind. Gather a few, and return to me.
Open your recipe notebook, novice. As I said, I've already laid out the recipe in there for you. Just follow the recipe, and you should have polished hrotanda in no time!

Go to the workbench across the hall. Make sure you have the ingredients: the polished hrotanda, and the sandstone you bought from  <<1>>. \n\nThen just open your recipe book to the page on apprentice runes, and follow the instructions.
I ask you again, because this is an important decision to make: will you explore the mystic pathways between this world and the next?\n\nWill you join the Runecrafter's guild?
Welcome to the guild, novice.\n\nI can almost guarantee no one will steal your soul and use it to fuel a mystic rite. Almost.

If Ra-shadda had many nights, he could explain. We integrate Tamriel's gods with our own, so we can blend in. We also do this to amuse ourselves. \n\nBut there are Khajiiti spirits outside Tamriel's pantheon. Dark spirits. They are dro-m'Athra.
I guess it's now or never.
Then it will "twin" you.\n\nYour body will appear dead, but your soul will suffer unending torment. It's worse than you can imagine. Ra-shadda will speak no more of this.

You're the only one I trust to do this. Go to the front lines. This sounds gruesome, but I need you to inspect the bodies of Covenant troops after they fall.\n\nLook for anything … well, unusual. And be discreet. I don't want the troops to panic.
You should be the one. You communed with the Hist, refined the amber … placing the Zaht stones was enough for me.
Hrrr! This makes my fur stand on end, but I will take you there safely and return you safely.\n\nAre you ready?
Then come aboard, and I shall ferry you there.

A High Elf has come visiting, demanding a supply line through <<1>>. She's willing to pay handsomely for the privilege.\n\nClearly she is a Dominion commander. If she dies, there is no one to execute their plans here … and I will have her gold.
She's in a cabin on the lower deck, waiting for me to return. If someone else arrived instead of me, I'm sure they could take care of this problem.\n\nI, of course, would never strike down a guest.
They're on the upper deck. Follow me.
One-Eye don't take social visits with nobodies like you. Get lost, before I make you disappear.
That's a relief. Now get me out and give me the book. I need to report in to Sergeant Maril.\n\nMaybe you could put in a good word for me? Tell him how brave I was?

Go to the crafting station across the hall. Make sure you have the ingredients: the polished hortanda and the sandstone. \n\nOpen your recipe book to the page on apprentice runes and just follow the instructions.
Thanks, friend! I'll figure out a way to reward you back at the fortress.
What? After all we've been through?\n\nFine, fine. I'll deal with Sergeant Maril myself. If you can't say something helpful, just don't say anything at all.
Ahh. Solicitations. We shape wood to our will. Carve weapons and armor, and create enchanted gearbindings. Forestry magic incarnate.
We use the skins of beasts to create leathers for pliable armor. We use secret alchemical mixtures to stir restoration potions.\n\nWhat do you say? How does the wind blow?
Ahh. Solicitations. We shape wood to our will. Carve weapons and armor, and create enchanted gearbindings. Forestry magic incarnate.
Excellent. May your scales stay wet and your time in the forest be fruitful. Welcome to the guild.
As you say, traveler. It is wise not to fight the river's course. I will still be here if your path returns this way.
We use the skins of beasts to create leathers for pliable armor. We use secret alchemical mixtures to stir restoration potions.\n\nWhat do you say? How does the wind blow?
<<1>> worries too much. I never ran from a battle in my life and I ain't about to start now.
That's the spirit! If it's quiet to the east, run west, I always say. Just watch out for the plague husks and rescue who you can.\n\nI'll take this poor soul and deliver her to Healer Senar.
Uninvited and unannounced guests have no place here. Be aware that I'm entertaining important people today.

Nonsense. The Vanguard is my priority right now. I'm sure one of your abilities can find ample employment elsewhere. \n\nIf you have further questions—and I'm sure you do—speak to my seneschal, Denu Faren.
Green maple. Logs on the ground, north gate. \n\nOpen yer recipe book. Pick the recipe. Follow instructions.
You are certain? Carving can be challenging, and the forest is dark and cruel.\n\nThe river offers many dangers. Dare you brave it?
