Welcome aboard, novice. We'll start you on the ground, and let you slowly climb the tree.
You are certain? Carving can be challenging, and the forest is dark and cruel.\n\nThe river offers many dangers. Dare you brave it?
Welcome aboard, novice. We'll start you on the ground, and let you slowly climb the tree.
I surrender! She's on the upper deck in the captain's quarters. The guards won't give you trouble if you don't make any.\n\nHope your business is worth the pain you're headed for.
My father, Last-to-Water. The Daedra still has him.\n\nHe tried to stop Fatestealer.
His stone is in the main campsite.\n\nI'm sure Fatestealer will not give up her prize willingly.

Senil insults me with his fancy words and sense of superiority. Still, I could look the other way.\n\nWhat's this Khajiit getting out of her deals with the Dominion? Find out where and what. Then we will talk more about Senil's freedom.

A pretender, that's all. She skulks in the shadows, afraid to challenge me, but she pays her spies well.\n\nI'd like to see that mangy cat as a new rug on my deck. I want her paychest in my hold! That would solve your problem, would it not?

Everyone knows I'll pay well to know this Khajiit's plans. Plenty of bites, but no meat.\n\nRight now, there's another wharf rat waiting outside. See what that squealer has to say. If it sounds useful, give him this reward.

What? Yes, of course I'm … wait. Blast it! You're with the caravan, aren't you?\n\nLook, I know when I'm backed into a corner. I'll tell you whatever you want to know. Just help me get out of here alive.

Of course! The General's madness, the strange sounds coming from the ruins—it all makes sense now. We were so blinded by protocol, we couldn't see it.\n\nI'll assume command immediately and send troops to deal with the Maulborn. Thank you.
Give me a moment to write this down.\n\nHere. Take this summary to Captain Valec. It explains everything in the manner he prefers: nice and orderly.
It happened last night. That's all I know.

I did what I was told. \n\nMagistrix Vox gives orders, not reasons. She supplied the rod to control the constructs, but it malfunctioned during the ambush. After that, the spiders attacked everything!
Wait, no! I told you everything!\n\nPlease, can't you …? All right. I'm going. I'm going!
Fine by me. Better them than these walking buzzsaws.\n\nLead the way.
I ran for it and hid down here. From the sound of it, my raiders got caught between the Hlaalu and the spiders.\n\nYou're going to get me out of here, right?
I heard a strange noise by her cart. I saw one of my people, wearing a red jerkin and … and that's all I know.
I had nothing to do with it! Whoever it was ran to the east. That's all I know!
I saw nobody, but during the later watches last night I woke when I heard someone running to the east. Perhaps it was the thief?
Who knows how these places get their names?\n\nOne scholar claims the Mabrigash have ties to Sithis. If you ask me, that's nonsense.

Well, according to the tales, the spirit of the Ghost Snake watches over them and speaks to them. \n\nYou want my opinion, it's all a carefully concocted story they use to keep visitors away, and frighten misbehaving children.
That's why it's called commerce, not charity.  \n\nI can keep other traders from bothering them, and the Mabrigash can improve their situation. Everyone benefits.
I know nothing about stolen relics. Now, get out of my house!
We have to proceed cautiously. I don't want any more of my soldiers getting infected.\n\nBut the Maulborn have to be dealt with. For good.

Always. A cliff overlooks their loaded wagons. And I've got archers up there. \n\nGet to Naryu Virian. Tell her to have the archers shatter the crates from above. We'll see how the Maulborn like being exposed to their own plague.
Ah, that changes things. \n\nWe've spotted the plague shipment they planned for Mournhold. I want those crates destroyed, but I need my troops at a safe distance when it happens.
They're the lost souls of those who failed the Trial of the Ghost Snake.\n\nThey weren't able to kneel before the great Fang Spires and commune with the Spirit of the Vale.
They serve the Ghost Snake and protect the vale from poachers and predators. The snakes that dwell in the vale are special.
Hrrr, how very persuasive. No need for such threats, friend. Yes?\n\nThe Lady has her nest den underground. An abandoned mine, I believe. Good luck—or not—finding it.
Hmm, you're that sure? Well, that sounds like a pirate's deal. You do all the work. I take half the money.\n\nThere's a trapdoor in the small warehouse on the shore. That'll get you to her.
I know only that it will change us. Whether for good or ill, only time will tell.

By your next action, our fate will be sealed.\n\nIf the Mabrigash are to grant access to the Vale, give the totem to the merchant. If we are to remain isolated, tending the Vale without outside interference, burn the totem in the fire.
He sees opportunity here. The snakes shed their skins, which can be used to make a rare and valuable leather.
Typical Ashlander outlook, I think.
Destroy it, so Clavicus Vile's grip upon us ends. Our bones may collapse, but our spirits will finally be free.

Then you know the shape of the problem. Our Ashkhan has laid siege to the Tribunal Temple.\n\nHe knows I disapprove. He rallied the hot-headed warriors of our tribe while I was meditating. He snuck out while my back was turned.
Clavicus Vile provided the means on the day he cursed us. Deep in the Daedric ruins burn two braziers: one of ice, the other of fire.\n\nPlacing the <<z:1>> into the <<2>> will destroy it.
Preserve the <<z:1>> forever. Clavicus Vile's gift has its drawbacks, but it's the only life we have. Don't let the weak-willed take it away from the rest of us.

There's a room deep in the Daedric ruins with two braziers that always burn. I'll give <<1>> some credit. He figured out what they did.\n\nPlacing the <<z:2>> into the <<3>> will preserve it, and us, forever.

The monks must understand we are not their enemy. Take an offering of herbs and potions. The Ashkhan took our store to his camp. His renegades are protecting them.\n\nFight through them. Take the medicine. Deliver it to the Temple. Can you do this?

He acts against my wishes, but he is still our Ashkhan: the patriarch of our tribe.\n\nI keep the Kagesh tribe moral and wise. He keeps them safe and strong. He is our right arm and sharpened steel. All his followers are my children.

I would have him give up this folly and rejoin us. We should live in peace, far from the housemen. If he won't listen to me, I'll have to step away from his side.\n\nSo understand me, outlander. If I must order Ziddak's death, I've failed.
My brother's plan, actually. Giron believes we can control the dead, harness them in a powerful defense for the Watch. His method must be tested before we attempt a larger ritual.
Just so. Take this talisman. Use it and learn how to free a spirit.\n\nThey will cling to this world, so first, you must weaken them. When you have done this, speak to me again.

We do not have it, not yet. <<1>> hasn't met with the High Elf to get our cut. But if you could take it, like you took the life of <<1>> ….\n\nLet us talk above ground, where it's safer. The others may not see you as their leader yet.
My hut has everything you need—a calcinator, an alembic, a mortar, and all the essentials.\n\nMy alchemy journal should also be there. Just follow the instructions and you'll be good to go.

Don't worry. My journal contains all the details. I wrote everything down. \n\nEver since that accident, with the fire salts and ectoplasm, my memory has been a bit shaky. Or was it fire salts and fly amanita? I can never remember exactly.
<You have six gizzards to grind up with troll fat and wisplight powder.>
You're a real pain, you know that? Here I am, trying to make sure Narsis doesn't become a breeding ground for mindless husks, but you want to play the hero, don't you?\n\nIt's so aggravating!
Very good. Now craft me the ring.
Bah! Raston claims things won't change, but I don't trust him. If you ask me, the Hlaalu are just one step above thieves.
If it were up to me, Raston would have quietly disappeared the first night he arrived here. But you're the one making the decision, not me.
At first, I just wanted the merchant to go away. But I've been thinking.\n\nPerhaps it wouldn't be so bad to deal with the outside world.
No. Many are set in their ways and fear change. But if we're cautious, we may benefit in the long run.

Most are shades of those who failed the Trial of the Ghost Snake. Others are wanderers who accidently stumbled upon the Coiled Path, and fell victim to the snakes or shades. \n\nThe vale is a dangerous place for the unwary.
They are bound as servants of the Ghost Snake, to protect the vale from poachers and predators. The snakes that dwell here are special.
Very good. Now, use all your skill to craft that ring. \n\nAnd whatever you do, do not imbue your soul into it. If I had a copper for every apprentice that's done that …
We are … we were part of the Renrijra Maor.\n\nWhat does it matter, the past? We follow your orders now. Once this is all over, we can go back to doing what we do best: making money.

Our wise woman sent you? By Azura! You couldn't have come at a better time. Let me see what you have.\n\nI'll take the herbs to <<1>>. As for you, there are many injured soldiers here. Take the draughts and use them on the dying.

Meet me in the main temple complex. It's up the stairs to the southwest. I'll be speaking with Curate Brethis.\n\nBrethis is supposed to be wise, for a houseman. Surely I can get him to see reason, even if this guar-brained Ordinator won't.
Excellent! Another set of willing hands working for the good of the Daggerfall Covenant. What guild name should I write on this Writ? \n\nWould you like to be a Smith, a Forester, or a Runecrafter?
A wise choice, friend. Potions and leathers, shields and bows! You'll make a fine forester.
A wise choice, friend. Steel and flame, blades and armor. You'll make a fine smith!
A wise choice, friend. Runes and robes, enchantments and soul gems! You'll make a fine runecrafter.
A recruit, eh? Welcome to my world. As a smith you'd use pressure and fire to reshape the world to your will. \n\nPlate armor and well sharpened swords are our stock in trade.
Shor's bones! I could smell the smelted steel when you walked into the room. You'll make a fine addition to the guild.
Of course, friend. Like the ore on the mountainside, the Smith's guild endures. \n\nPerhaps you're more a Runecrafter, eh? Head west from here, and speak with <<1>>.

We combine minerals and magic to create restoratives for mages. We forge enchanted trinkets that rogues can clip to their gear, granting them enhanced abilities. \n\nWe're flame and metal and magic combined! So! What do you say?
Come to learn, recruit? Runecrafting is an ancient and serious art. We manipulate magicka, imbuing it into runes, jewels, and staves. \n\nWe can even transform a common robe into a source of power.
Honor to you. The first time you set ink to scroll, the first time you etch a rune … you'll never be able to go back. \n\nWelcome to the Runecrafter's guild.

Wisely said, friend. No need to rush into a decision like this. Go, contemplate the runes. Return when you are sure.\n\nIn the meantime, perhaps the Forestry guild would be a better fit? Speak with <<1>>. Vivec guide your steps.

We scribe scrolls that any man or mer can cast. We prepare soul gems, trapping the essence of mystical creatures. They're used to enhance powerful magical gear.\n\nThe Runecrafter's life is one of power and contemplation. What say you?
Communing with the Hist teaches who we were before makes us what we are now. To remember our ancestors' deeds is to know ourselves.\n\nLearn of our past and act with what you gain.
The little s'wits are quick. If you get too close, they'll run away from you.\n\nTo grab them, stand as far back as you can. That way, you'll catch them by surprise.
He finished his trials before you arrived, and is currently in communion with the Hist. He must not be disturbed.
I've been here for weeks, playing the political games common to all Dark Elf kinhouses. I've decided I hate such games.\n\nBut you'd be surprised what you can learn if you just stand back and listen.
Giron isn't our target. We're after the one who created the Llodos plague.\n\nI decided to reach out to you and provide a modicum of aid. Your actions may lead me to the one I seek.
Raiders attacked our caravan. They had Dwarven machines with them. Like spiders!\n\nThey ambushed us—we should have been slaughtered. But then the attack broke off.

One of our Dunmer Great Houses. There's rivalry between the houses, but not open conflict.\n\nYou're an outsider. Maybe the prisoner will talk to you. We're holding her up the road, in the ruined tower.
Something went wrong. The spiders suddenly attacked everybody and everything.\n\nWe captured one of the raiders in the chaos. She's wearing the insignia of House Dres.
The Trial of the Fang remains before you. You must fight while at great disadvantage. <<1>> will assist you in your preparations.
Here's a list of the victims' families. They may know if their kin had enemies. If you can prove whoever's behind this, come find me for your reward.
The Hist cares not for kingdoms or politics. It shares what we have forgotten. How we use its gifts is our doing.
I doubt the guards will try to restrain you. You can come and go as you please.\n\nSpeak to Madras. Let him tell you our plan. You must help us. I need my egg-sister back.

"Subject died from a precise cut to the throat. The cut runs just deep enough to sever a vein and vocal cords. The body shows no sign of struggle.\n\n"A small, precise cut upon the chest was made after subject's death."

"Subject died from a single stab wound to the heart. The strike is clean and precise. There are no visible signs of struggle.\n\n"I noticed a small, separate cut quite near the mortal wound. I estimate this cut was made after the subject's death."
Good. This one's revenge has come at too high a cost. Ra-shadda should have tempered his fury. By Jone and Jode, he regrets what happened, \n\nHave I convinced you of this? Will you set me free?

"Initial review suggested the subject died from heat or flames, but the burns do not extend beyond the surface of the skin. Whatever caused these burns was no natural flame.\n\n"Subject bears a wound in her chest—a clean, precise cut."
"Upon consultation, this combination of wounds is unknown to the local Mages Guild."
The Worm Cult necromancers encamped nearby raided our village last night. We trapped three of their lieutenants inside our huts, but they refuse to surrender.

"Entry 441: Three Dark Elves killed in Stormhold, and rumors call it our work. Preposterous—the Night Mother gifted none of them with her call.\n\n"I'll return to the Enclave when I discover who's behind this."

Our scouts call them <<1>>, <<2>>, and <<3>>. We tricked them into the cellars below our huts and bolted the doors.\n\nPerhaps you can convince them to surrender. If you confront them, <<4>> would call you a friend.

<You've found a sketch of a fair Altmer woman on the marked page. It's signed "Valrendil." There's writing below the picture in much shakier handwriting.>\n\n"Such scrawls do your beauty no justice, my love. I will see you again, and soon."
Our history. Carvings, keystones, and bits of Hissmir itself. All of it rough, old stone.\n\nEvery season, we take them to our pilgrimage sites. They have no value to anyone but us.
"WANTED: <<1>>, for dereliction of duty. Proof of his death will be rewarded by your assigned Dominion paymaster.\n\n"Subject is delusional and prone to sympathize with enemy Argonians."
<You see several ancient Argonian relics. They've been carefully wrapped and stored.>\n\n<One of the more intricate and ancient jars is broken, despite its careful packaging.>
Wait! Some High Elf pilgrim offered my tail's weight in gold for those things. But after he saw them, he said they were useless!\n\nTake the relics. I want nothing to do with any of this.

Of course, I should have expected this. \n\nTell the generous <<1>> not to fear. My work does not threaten Argonians. It is personal—the work of decades—and now I may finally have succeeded, though I must betray the legacy of the ancestors.
Of course I am! Don't I look like a beautiful High Elf noble?\n\nAre you with the Dominion? Did they send you to arrest my husband for desertion? Begone! He must not be bothered.
I am Valrendil's wife! I am the one he loves, the one he cares for, the one he has sought all these years. I will make him happy. Forever.\n\nI have no more business with you.

Wife? He came with no wife. How could ….\n\nAh. How foolish of me. Our wispmother has assumed the form of <<1>>'s dead wife. She is strong. Far greater than the simple spirit I thought her to be. This is dangerous.

I always make plans. Ssaa. We must seal her in something ancient and powerful. \n\nSee the far xanmeers? Each holds fragments I need to make a prison. I'll prepare the ritual site. Gather the pieces and meet me where the newly dead are buried.

Yes. We grew up together in Senchal. J'kur looked after Vahara. He fought the slavers to protect her.\n\nThey put Vahara in the mines and J'kur down here. Word came to Vahara that J'kur would start a riot. He did it to be with Vahara again.
Bah, lies! She told me you'd say such things. \n\nWhy you, a stranger, could possibly hate her, I don't understand.
I'm taking orders from a milk-drinking pup and a cat? \n\nHa ha! This should be amusing. I'll be there.
Fine. I don't care what happens now. I'll meet you there.

All are as one within the Hist. To be as one requires discipline. The trials prove your commitment. \n\nThey also test your body and mind. We must see if you're capable of surviving the process without dying or going mad.

My wife lives! She's blessed by an Argonian reincarnation, thank the Hist! Though I wanted this, I was still amazed at how quickly she awoke in this place.\n\nThe Dominion will execute me for desertion, so I remain here, in the home my beloved created.
My appearance? You cast aspersions on my beauty? My husband will throw you out!\n\nAnd he shall, for he loves me and he will stay with me forever. You, however, will not.
I didn't see him when I arrived, but he must have been here. Ra-shadda was already bound. Ulov must hav-\n\nWait. Ulov?
Let me see that. By the Three! My poor, darling Risa. I miss her so much.

Before the sickness, our miners uncovered an old temple to Clavicus Vile. When we were dying, I sought the Daedric Prince of Bargains to save our village, at any cost.\n\nI begged the Daedra for immunity to the sickness. You can see the cost.
I've seen these symbols before. The Wood Elves sometimes write this way. Hmm.\n\nThis is a treasure map. I cannot read these notes, but I know someone who can.
It may take time. Assuming he's not passed-out drunk somewhere, I'll send word to for my crewman to meet you . \n\nA treasure hunter now, are you?
Oh, yes. Your esteemed friend asked me to translate, but I couldn't resist coming along.\n\n<<1>> is a fine tracker, I assure you. We'll find this treasure with no snags.
A while back, Argonians in Stormhold were slaves to the local Dark Elves. The two other vicecanons work to mend the bad blood, but it's slow to get anything done when nobody trusts the guard.

They're a pain in the fundament. An armed group of Argonians lurking in the swamps, killing enemies of their people. If you want to twist a Dark Elf's ears any more, you may as well burn an effigy of Almalexia.

Recently some Argonians went missing. We heard a nasty rumor about Dark Elf slavers in the city. False, of course.\n\nThen the bodies showed up—all Dark Elves. The new rumor says Shadowscales are targeting Dunmer. Nearly started a riot.
Outrageous! That oafish Nord has the audacity to send an <<1>> to me?\n\nA sick joke, this is. Arilen's body rots in the mortuary while the vicecanons do nothing but play politics!
Look in the mirror, scaleskin. He spoke out against you people, and rightly so!\n\nYour Shadowscales are to blame. We bring civilization to you cretins and you thank us with knives in the dark!

If I bet like Naldyn did, I'd put all my money on one of your kind. He had a habit of pushing around … uh, Argonians.\n\nIf it wasn't a Shadowscale who got him, I'll bet they were next in line. But I'm sure you know all about those guys.

The vicecanons represent each of the Pact's territories: Skyrim, Morrowind, and Black Marsh. Each were forged in the Akaviri War, and are competent in both strategy and diplomacy.\n\nTogether, they oversee the safety and prosperity of <<1>>.

<<1>> hails from Skyrim, and is the most vocal of the three. <<2>> came from Morrowind after the Pact's unification.\n\n<<3>> is also a relative newcomer to Black Marsh. Her history may be in question, but her aptitude certainly is not.
I was only gone for a second.
My wizard uses it to add energy to his arcane experiments. The Supernal Dreamers, however, have figured out how to use the crystal for their own nefarious purposes.
Well, first and foremost, they belong to me! But more importantly, they hold vast power! Power, do you hear?!
The crystal appeared to me in a dream, held aloft by a Daedric lord. He claimed it was a gift and that it was a part of my destiny. When I awoke I found the thing in my lap!
They want to imbue themselves with nobility. I think they've got a ceremony that'll make them lords of this land.
I had no idea it could be used for such nefarious purposes.The small coffer it came in was etched with odd symbols.\n\nI thought is was just a pretty crystal.  I used it for a paperweight.
Very good. Now craft me the ring.
Very good. Now craft me the ring.
Such beauty. Why, look at the molding!\n\nAlas, a king who cannot protect his subjects is no king at all. This crown only serves to remind us that our people suffer.
I stole them from some cultists, way back in my adventuring days.
The power of true love!
I showed the coffer to my wizard and he said they were Daedric symbols, though he did not understand their meaning.
My fool of a son took it and lost it in a card game. Clearly it was a set-up with these cultists.
Some sort of nightmare scenario, I'm sure. They'll probably take over the dreams of this very land. Or some nonsense like that.
They must've figured that each shard would transform one of them into a noble. More shards equals more royalty. It's basic mathematics.
For security reasons, I can't go into specific detail. I'm sure you understand. Suffice it to say that we're helping to defend the Covenant from the forces that threaten us.
The Dreamers believe they found a way to alter reality with the power provided by the shattered crystal. I don't know if they're right, but I don't really want to find out. Just stop them!
Fine, I needed to use the bathroom.  There.  I said it.
The Supernal Dreamers.  The Crystal holds the power to summon creatures of great power with the correct ritual.
The invaders hold our citizens in the lowlands. <<1>>, <<2>>, and <<3>> are their names.\n\nWe overheard the mages who bound them speak of a <<4>>. Acquire this scroll and free our bound subjects.
I pay so little attention to religion. I do not know for sure. He claimed that he was "Lord of dreams, drinks, and doxies" and was dressed like a jester. Not much of a god if you ask me.

He did in fact. He claimed that this gemstone would belong to a great hero who will cleanse the land of corruption. Naturally I can't allow this cult to steal such an important item from its rightful owner.
Yes, this is just another option.
The General accused me of being a spy. If I'm caught snooping around, he'll arrest me. \n\nI can't very well protect the fort while I'm locked in a cell, can I?
I'm asking for your help. Not for me, but for the General and everyone stationed here.  \n\nSomething's seriously wrong and we need to get to the bottom of it.
I'm not entirely sure. Some ghost of the past. Heimlyn Keep sits atop a reliquary. We tend an archive of ancient magics, weapons, and relics. Even we, her stewards, don't know all that lies below.
My poor brother. He's a good elder, but he has many responsibilities. He cannot hunt insects like his sister. I will return to him soon. \n\nYou offered to help my brother. Will you help me, as well?
It's like a disease that weakens and saps your life force. It's fast, and it's deadly. \n\nAnd you don't just die. Your soul comes back as a dire apparition. That's foul, ancient magic.
I'm tracking the Covenant leader. He ran from my blade before it could feed on his flesh.\n\nBut another danger looms over our town.
I'm positive. <<1>> and I studied the curse for decades. This is Clavicus Vile's way of being playful, I suppose … though I don't presume to know the intentions of any Daedric Prince.

Lucky for us, I think ahead. Years ago I fastened one of my toe knuckles to the <<z:1>>. I can sense it's still in their nearby camp.\n\nAfter you give those moss-gargling cultists a good pounding, bring it straight to <<2>>.
Your words smell fair, but tasting is proof. Let me see what you have there.

Yes. I erect the spine of apology. While you were away, we caught a Dark Elf defiling our Hist.\n\nPlease, apply the fertilizer you've gathered to the base of our Hist. As long as I am with you, the guards will let you through.
One of our guards is escorting him to my lodge. \n\nHe seems half-mad. He was doing something to the tree. And apparently, he is of House Dres.
Oh, don't get upset! Just a few others. <<1>> will expect a cut. And <<2>> and his boys will need their share.\n\nBut there is plenty to go around!
Go—be on your way and I shall be on mine. We'll see who's the victor in this battle soon enough.

An illusion? Ha! Illusions can't create these feelings or the devotion I see in her eyes. I believe in my <<1>>.\n\nThis is preposterous. If you persist with this madness, I'll stop you. I don't know how, but I will.
I … what? Very well. Sometimes I think what I see isn't quite right. Sometimes from the corner of my eye, or when she thinks I'm not looking.\n\nAnuiel's clarity, have I lost the Fixed Center?
She … may have forgotten a few details.\n\nBah! You know nothing of death's toll. It makes no sense! Though I may not be able to stop you now, I shan't give up.
Ah! You've not seen him, then.\n\nYou should know a powerful mage fights at his side. Her spells make him incredibly powerful.
Indeed. You could have chosen not to come to the Temple. Many choose paths that are unwise.\n\nNow hear my words and perhaps you will choose to help me.
Pure moisture. This will only take a moment.\n\nThere. Done.

That's the irony. We are researchers, scholars in pursuit of knowledge. We used our spellcasting might to hold our own against the Daggers. But if they had not released the curse, odds are we would all be dead.

The last few people in the Keep are still cowering in their quarters. Adras, Ramalii, Neron, and Hadrill. Some of my assistants are working to hold back the curse, but I don't know how much longer they'll hold out.
It's a dark legacy from the time of the Chimer. The … things … put in the reliquary were locked away for a reason.\n\nWhatever the Daggers did accidentally released this spellplague.

The reliquary is an ancient quarantine vault. The Telvanni used it to imprison things that should never have been free.\n\nI imagine most things in the cache were destroyed by the Covenant's attack. But not the plague.

A clever question. It never occurred to me that a totem might work, not until I saw victims of the plague's final stages.\n\nWhat I saw gave me horrible but useful insights into the nature of the curse.
They're brave souls, but I'm worried about them.\n\nWithout their help, we'd have lost the fight before you even arrived. They bought us time.
I'm lying still on the ground. Don't worry. I just tried to eat an eel that's too large.\n\nI must remain here a moment until I can stand again, but I fear the Covenant's leader may escape.
House Telvanni hasn't joined the Ebonheart Pact, but we still have responsibilities in central Morrowind. \n\nWe've kept watch over the reliquary under Heimlyn Keep for generations.
I'm a soldier. I came here under orders to take out military assets. Not threaten scholars and harass teachers.\n\nPlease, if you let me go, I won't make trouble. I just want to live.

Indeed. Long ago, when our people were still Chimer, this land was known as Veloth. \n\nThe Chimer revered the Daedra, but they despised the agnostic clans of Elves called Dwemer. The Chimer and Dwemer clashed again and again.
This curse was terrible, and worse, uncontrollable. The Chimer lords bound the curse in a hidden vault, then slew <<1>> and <<2>> and imprisoned them with their wicked creation.
Terrible weapons were made and used. The spellplague was one such weapon. It was created by two mendicant mages who worshiped the Daedric Prince Namira.
The captain of the Covenant soldiers. His blade was poisoned. I can already see the edges of mother's wound blackening.\n\nI must be calm. I can't lose my wits like some rattlebrained Altmer.
We must force the dead mages who created this curse to help us. \n\nCrack open the spell cages holding <<1>> and <<2>>. Summon them, fight them, bind them. Then find me.
Because when a god asks questions, people say what they think the god wants to hear. \n\nAnd my known agents fare no better.

Thank you, my child. A loyal servant, Magister Navisdyn, has been murdered. Somehow, my blessing failed to protect him.\n\nGo to the Mages Guild. Speak to Wizard Bothisii. Remember, though, to only invoke my name if absolutely necessary.
A favored servant has been murdered. I would know who has done this evil deed.\n\nThe Great Houses often quarrel, but blood is rarely shed. And never the blood of one favored by the Tribunal.
Very good. Now craft me the ring.
text
Sure I know <<1>>. That bum owes me money.\n\nLast I heard he was upstairs.
Sure I know <<1>>. That bum owes me money.\n\nLast I heard he was upstairs.
Watch out for <<1>>. He always keeps close to his body guard.\n\nIf you want to get to him, you should time it so his body guard isn't around.
Watch out for <<1>>. He always keeps close to his body guard.\n\nIf you want to get to him, you should time it so his body guard isn't around.
The curse has been broken. No more will the spellplague corrupt the heart of Stonefalls. \n\n<<1>> must be told.
You haven't heard? Princess Elara is missing, and Prince Adrien's been wounded fighting outside the city.
You'd think, right? But Gharzu's thugs are always hanging around, driving decent customers away.
Gharzu's the new captain of the guard. He was appointed by the knight regent after the king died. They aren't proper guards, though. They're nothing but common thugs!

The Imperials happened. We could see them on the march from Craglorn, rank upon rank advancing towards the walls. I ran. I'm ashamed to admit it, but …\n\nHallin's Stand fallen. What hope do we have now?

In the north, the Reach claw at us from every side. By the First Forge, friend, we can barely send a caravan without having it attacked by those animals. \n\nWorse, the Bretons are blaming us for the Reach's attacks! Trying times.

I'm getting all this inventoried, packed, and loaded for shipment south. Arms and armor - all fresh from the forge here in Evermore!\n\nHm. Is "fresh" the right word for armor? I guess it doesn't matter ….

To a mustering camp just north of Bangkorai Garrison.\n\nOur combined armies were pushed out of the fortress by Imperial invaders. We're trying to reoragnize for a counterattack. They need all the weapons and armor we can get them.

To Bangkorai Garrison. Our armies retook it from the Imperials, but the enemy had looted the armories. We need to restock them so we can continue to push them south and east.\n\nWe can't stop until the bastards are back in Cryodiil!
I'm on my way to Farwatch Tower to conduct research on the flow of magical energies in abandoned locations, and behold! There are two damn armies in my way!\n\nThis is just my luck.
Yes, armies! Aldmeri Dominion advance troops have latched onto Farwatch Tower like a tick on a deer, and it'd take a Daedric prince to dislodge them.\n\nIrritations! Fools! I have work to do!
Not on your life. I was about to pull out of here altogether.\n\nJust waiting on the Lord General's permission, and for that damn mage to finish whatever he's doing downstairs.
"There are few sites in High Rock more majestic than the pale gray stones of Farwatch, whose tower has stood as a sentinel over the western shore since the dawn of the Second Era."

"For all of its majesty, however, Farwatch gained a reputation for infamy by would-be conquerors. Renegade knights from the city of <<1>>, displeased with the bounties granted unto them by their liege, sacked Farwatch not long after it was built."

"Seeking to establish their own fiefdom with unsuspecting free-men of the region as their subjects, the knights turned the tower's dungeon into a maze of torment for those who refused to bend their knees."
"Farwatch may be a beauty from afar, but those versed in local legends rightfully avoid the tower undercroft for fear of disturbing the bones of those knights."

"An uprising amongst the local foresters started a brief seven-day war that broke the knights' hold on the region. They were condemned to die in the very dungeons in which they tortured their unruly subjects."
You think I was born yesterday? I'm not falling for that one.\n\nYou're not going to help me. You'll just bring the voice back. Please … just let me sleep in peace.
Sir Edgard said that? I always thought he hated me.\n\nYou … have an honest face. Perhaps you're right. I'm getting out of here!
You have to. She'll eat my soul if I try to leave!\n\nNo … it's coming!
Yes. I see now. It was guarding the totem, wasn't it?\n\nYou have my thanks, stranger. I'm getting out of here.

No. I have to stay here. This is my punishment. I shouldn't have touched the totem. I thought … it doesn't matter what I thought. I was wrong!\n\nAnd the voice says I have to stay. It's not so bad. I can sleep. And dream.

I don't take orders from you, whoreson dog! You … you're absolutely right. I can't stay here. What was I thinking?\n\nI'm leaving and any Daedra that gets in my way goes straight to Oblivion! Because I'll kill them!
By the King's Shaft! You've made it mad. Run!
Who … who are you?
Yes I can. I have to! I have to hide until the voice stops! I can't take it anymore!
Come with you? No, the voice says I shouldn't.\n\nIt says … oh no! She's here!
Right. Of course. Anything to get away from those whispers ….

Ha! Everyone knows your name these days. Ever since you got rid of <<1>> and that bastard Gharzu.\n\nWhen the Queen stands up and praises you in front of the palace, that tends to get noticed, friend.

Oh, they're still here. For the moment, anyway. But they're a lot quieter now that their leader's gone. They've even stopped trying to grab Rosette while she's waiting tables.\n\nBetween you and me? I don't think they have any place to go.

Give me a break, okay?

Look. I signed up with the Lion Guard to impress a girl, not to die alone in the dark. Who cares if the Goblins overrun the Bonesnap Ruins? 

Ogres? Did I mention they have ogres?
You have no right to judge me! My father left when I was five. I never had a positive male role model.\n\nLook. Just go away. I'm begging you.
I think the necromancers called it an "animus geode." Fancy name for an ugly purple stone used to steal someone's soul. Blessed Arkay, I watched them murder all four of my guards!

Sacrifices must be made, soldier. And the Chimer have sacrificed enough. Kill Nedes until the river runs red with their blood. Take their hearts as trophies.\n\nAnd once you've decimated the front lines, their leader must pay.
Praise Vivec! I need to get these potions to the workers as soon as possible. \n\nI'm sure it will help. It has to.

I don't know! How would I know? I don't go into the mine! Why are you asking me?\n\nI'm sorry. This is so stressful. I'm worried about my husband, Boril. He went back inside. And I have no idea what happened to my idiot cousin, Renvis.

He's concerned about the workers. Thinks they're still in the mine. I'm so worried. Boril hasn't raised a sword in years and the kwama aren't acting normal. \n\nWill you go after him? Take him these potions? And drink one yourself before you go.
No, I suppose not. My family's been involved in things I'm not proud of.\n\nThat's part of the reason I returned to Mournhold.
Her voice commands the lost souls, so that's a likely reason. I weep for the other travelers who fell prey to her traps.\n\nYou should leave our cursed gravesite while you still can.
No one has asked about the sacred performance in a long while, n'wah. You dare brave the wrath of the Mirthless Order? Would you risk death to learn my secret knowledge?
If you wish to brave the Mirthless Order, that is your choice. Here's the second part of the performance: \n\n"In response, the morag of Koal Canton released their kwama …. "
The Mirthless Order will track you, no doubt, but that is your choice. The third part of the performance goes like this:\n\n"Only when the mehra was burned in a sujamma molag …."
That is old news. I have a greater worry.
Pash-Riha. My crazy sister.\n\nWe repelled a Covenant attack. Afterwards, Pash-Riha chased their leader to the northwest. Could you find her? If she is dead, could you drag her corpse back to town?
The Kothringi settled around an Ayleid ruin. \n\nWe heard all the villagers were killed by the Knahaten flu, but there's one survivor.
Some say they were descended from the Nedic humans. They lived in Black Marsh as far back as records go.\n\nThe Knahaten flu destroyed their culture. We thought they were all dead.
Then we conscript you into our service. We are King <<1>>, your liege lord.\n\nWe will entertain your petitions, should you have any.

When our kingdom is secure and our dignity restored, the keystone will reveal itself. So says the prophecy!\n\nThe first order of business is to create a new crown. We sense your reluctance, but nothing can be done without our crown.

Nerys, Liam, Wilhem, and Gerren are still imprisoned in those animus geodes. But I overheard the necromancers say the geodes are fragile with spirits inside.\n\nI'll make a break for it. You smash the geodes. Please, don't let them suffer such a fate!
Those beasts and their bugs lair in the mountains north of here. They scuttle along the coast, catching fish and squatting in caves. \n\nThen the Covenant soldiers came to Stonefalls.

I think most of them were captured. I saw some of them dragged off toward that cave to the north. \n\nI'll report to Diiril and let him know what's happening here. You go to the cave and see if you can find the others.

They used the caves along the coasts as supply drops for landing troops. They drove the Goblins from their caves and killed their spider queens.\n\nNow the animals are searching for new lands. They're trying to take our home.

If you find Borolg clad in his magical armor, use the totem on him. The armor will sink back into his flesh.\n\nNow go kill him. Tell Elder Seven-Bellies when Borolg is dead. I'm sure he'll want to know.

My husband … Hrogar's eldest son, Hroding. I had to stand by his funeral pyre. These vermin, these Goblins and their spiders. They only wish to take and kill and destroy … they don't care about wives, hopes, or dreams.\n\nPlease, leave me be.
Yes. You will be more likely than I to discover the truth. But if the need arises, invoke my name to clear any obstacles from your path.
Good idea. Exactly what we need.\n\nOn your way, then. That tunnel will take you to the top of the cliff.

My Lady has many responsibilities to her children.\n\nIs Iliath more important than the Covenant invasion? Than Molag Bal's schemes? Than a mother struggling to give birth in Mournhold, or a father praying for his sick child's life in Seyda Neen?
Balreth is one of two ancient magical juggernauts, the Brothers of Strife. Their story is too long to tell now. It is enough that Balreth is a powerful weapon at our command.
The Magister was my mentor. I don't wish to talk about it right now. \n\nBut why do you care? What's the death of a guild mage to you?

And leave the wee scribbles? They weren't really affected by those nasty fumes. Most burrowed away, clever and cute as can be. But these little beauties are safe here with me.\n\nNice and safe, aren't you my little friends? Yes you are!

Ah! Now that is a wiser question.\n\nAlmalexia bids me to say this: Go to the chapel below this temple. Take ashes from the urns of Nerathren and Faryon. Scatter them in the eternal flames beneath the northern and southern towers.

Even if they do attack, everyone here will still die some day. Even you, child. One night, you will close your eyes and never return to Tamriel.\n\nThe Tribunal does not offer immortality, nor does it shield the reverent from the trials of life.

The Ordinators will appear before you. You must earn their respect.\n\nLong ago, Nerathren and Faryon were guard captains who gave their lives to defend Iliath. Defeat them in combat, and they'll aid in your defense of Iliath.
We're just fine, aren't we little ones? Yes, we are! \n\nCareful of the big old warriors and workers though. The fumes made them very grumpy. They might even be mean to the scribbles!

Suppose a mer asked you for aid against an enemy he could not defeat alone.\n\nIf you can defeat him in battle, he's weak, and he wants you to solve problems for him. If he can defeat you, he's strong, and his need is genuine.
Well, let's see what's left of the old place.
I see. You're in on it. I suppose there's no way around it, then.
Ambush me?
Ah, Sar-Keer and Tastes-the-Breeze. \n\nThey want to kill me, as they killed my mother and father.

Kaoc! You come at an opportune time, stranger. The Hist must have guided you.\n\nDaedric energies permeate the swamp, overwhelming the power of the Hist. I tried to commune with the spirits, but you can see from the state of my hut how well that went.
I appreciate the offer.\n\nIt's time to deal with the past. It's a shame the lizards suffered under my parents, but they've no right to take my life.
Thanks for the warning, but I'm sick of running. It's time to face the past.\n\nIt's a shame the lizards suffered under my parents, but they've had their revenge. They've no right to take my life.
We'll consider it a blessing of the Tribunal for now, and leave it at that.\n\nThe Maulborn who haven't fallen to the plague are in retreat. We've just one final matter to attend to.
It's time to face the past. \n\nIt's a shame the lizards suffered under my parents, but they've had their revenge. They've no right to take my life.
It is my pleasure to uphold my family's honor.\n\nWith my father leading the defense, victory is certain.
I'm here to reclaim my family home. It's been sealed since my father died, when we fled the city for Vvardenfell.\n\nI was so little then, but I promised I would return.

My family kept Argonian slaves. They worked our saltrice plantation and were the source of our wealth. And the cause of our doom.\n\nWhen the Pact freed our slaves, they rose up and murdered my father. My mother and I fled.
Frankly, I'd welcome your company. \n\nThe family townhouse is nearby. I'll meet you there.

A shadow hangs over my family. My mother returned last year to claim our property. I never saw her again. She was murdered, I'm sure of it.\n\nNow I think someone is following me. I can handle myself, but I'm still worried.
Ah, Sar-Keer and Tastes-the-Breeze. They want to kill me, as they killed my mother and father.\n\nThe house is nearby—meet me there. It's time for me to face my past.
By Veloth's hammer, that's the best news I've heard all day.\n\nListen, the Vereansu are never going to leave us be. Not while their leader's still alive. I know that sounds terrible, but it's true.
Yes. <<1>> leads these Ashlanders. Go to the Vereansu camp and kill him.\n\nCut off the head of the snake and the body dies. Then they won't threaten the <<2>> ever again.

Veloth shed the Tear after he led the Chimer from Summerset to Morrowind. The artifact has the power to heal sicknesses.\n\nWe haven't been able to cure the Llodos plague, but the Tear can slow the speed at which the plague ravages the afflicted.
Can you think of a better way to safeguard it?
No, not unless you find a way to use its power. \n\nThat's not something I can help you with.

It's an Ayleid temple built on even older Argonian ruins. I've only been inside it once.\n\nThe Ayleids were … unkind to its earlier inhabitants. They were also fiercely protective of their treasures.
<Of the many piercing cuts covering the body, the most significant wound punctured the center of the magister's chest.>
<This wound was made by a triangular-shaped blade. It's a smooth, clean wound. The blade must have slid through Navisdyn's defenses and killed him instantly.>
That's a Fighters Guild tunic! Why would the Fighters Guild be involved in a murder?\n\nAnd how did the murderer circumvent Lady Almalexia's blessing?
A strangler's barb hit <<1>>, and she dropped her bow in the muck. She's a bit shy about asking you directly.\n\nPlease look for it. It must be in one of the <<mz:2>>.

Absorbed? I don't know … I entered the temple and saw the keystone. And then, nothing.\n\nNow that you've said it, I feel something. That must've been what kept me alive when the rest of my village died.

You can't accuse the Fighters Guild of a crime like this without solid evidence.\n\nListen, go talk to Viiron. He's the Quartermaster at the Fighters Guild. He and I are … very good friends. Tell him I sent you and he should cooperate.

They tied him up and threw him into a burning building. And they continue to fan the flames! They consider our work to be blasphemous, and fire is their solution to everything. \n\nPlease, you must save Dolril!

These violent statues depict the horrors of the past, when the Elven Chimer fought the invading human Nedes.\n\nThis was the birthplace of the mightiest magic the Chimer ever conceived. As a Telvanni, I must know everything.
These are the Brothers of Strife, immortalized in stone. It was here our ancestors, the Chimer, made their final stand against the Nedes. \n\nAnd it was here they created the Brothers of Strife.
In that case, don't just stand there! Release me! I must report to <<1>> before any more soldiers get here.\n\nIs the rendezvous the same?
Nice to know some of us weren't captured. I'm sure I'll never hear the end of this.\n\nNow if you could untie me, I'll be on my way.
Just the words I want to hear. Cut me loose!\n\nI've got plans for these low-life dryskins. I'm sure <<1>> would approve.
Good. That's on the hill over there.\n\nI could use you in my future plans. See you soon.
Then the plan hasn't changed. Hopefully, I'll see you there.\n\nAt least you made it this far without getting caught.
Excellent. Then we haven't been discovered yet. I'll see you there.
A triangular …? \n\nI heard what happened to Magister Navisdyn, but it has nothing to do with the Fighters Guild. Get out of here, s'wit.
They attack because they don't know Hedranna disapproves. I'd hoped to avoid this, but there's no choice.\n\nI would like to give you a … an artifact. Hedranna gave it to me as a last resort.
I don't know. The wise woman spoke into it. When you activate it, her image appears and repeats what she said.\n\nIf you use it near Ziddak's Ashlanders, they should let you pass.

She didn't say. I've seen similar devices in collections of Dwarven relics.\n\nI don't know why the wise woman would have such a thing. The Dwarves were sinful people who wallowed in selfish curiosity.
Our Ashkhan acts against the wishes of our wise woman. If his duplicity was known to our people, they'd never trust him again.\n\nIt would destroy him.

He does what he thinks is best for us. It's difficult to explain to outsiders.\n\nThe Ashkhan is the father of our tribe. Would you want to learn that your father is a liar? That he puts his desire for revenge above your family's safety?
I admire your strength. If I couldn't trust my father's wisdom, I'd feel lost. Where would I turn for counsel?\n\nI'm sorry. This isn't your concern.
I'm glad you do. It's not easy for me to explain.\n\nIt's a terrible thing to lose faith in those you love.

We've repelled the Ashlanders' first assault. It's only a matter of time before they launch another one.\n\nI have to give them credit. Breaching the tunnel was a creative approach. Fortunately for us, the Ashlanders are lousy engineers.
The support beams holding open the breach … I can hear them cracking from here.\n\nIt would be easy to knock them down, if you had the tools to do it.
The temple monks do a good deal of manual labor here, gardening and suchlike. Look in their quarters: those outbuildings back behind the temple. A pickaxe would work.

You're right, it's not the safest plan. That's why we'd like you to weaken the supports, not knock them down outright.\n\nIf you can use a bit of finesse, they won't collapse before you hit the last one.
I think that's obvious. You'll need to get out as fast as you can.
That's the spirit! We're right behind you.\n\nRemember, we have to find out how the plague was made. Then we can get to work on making a cure. Let's go.
We've got Merdyndril, the alchemist who created the Llodos Plague, cornered in these ruins. We need to capture him and find out how he did it.\n\nWith you at our side, we can't fail.
He died valiantly, then.\n\nDid you learn anything in there that would help us?
Praise Vivec! With the notes, we can finally craft a cure. \n\nThe Maulborn have fallen to their own plague. The merchants are already returning to their camp.
The stuff in the crates was extremely potent, but also very short-lived. It came and went fast, and we haven't seen any more afflictions.\n\nBut if this had reached Mournhold ….
Out back. In the training yard. Feel free to take a look, if you want.\n\nBut be discreet. And don't alarm the guards out there.

Bothisii? Well, then. Where are my manners?\n\nOnly a total idiot would leave their tunic behind, and the weapon you describe is unusual. If someone wanted to blame us for this, they'd probably hide it in our weapon crates.
I've never seen a weapon like this. It's crafted from rare Daedric steel.\n\nSee the crafter's mark on the pommel? This dagger was forged by the Steel Mask.

My brother and I were the greatest generals of the Chimer. Yet even we couldn't stem the tide of Nedic muscle and iron.\n\nWe were desperate. The sorcerers' plan to create the Brothers of Strife offered us a way out.

I'd start in the crafters' circle here in the city. Someone there might know how to contact him. \n\nI hope you can prove we had nothing to do with this crime. And next time you see Bothisii, tell her I said hello.

The Steel Mask is a weaponsmith. Probably the best in Morrowind. He works with materials no one else will touch, like this Daedric steel.\n\nThe smith is reclusive, though. Expensive and hard to get a hold of. Prefers to keep his identity a secret.

We drew a line in the ash. At this temple, we declared we would go no further. \n\nMy troops held the line in the riverbed below while Sadal and I made the sacrifice. We became the Brothers of Strife, and as brothers ended this war.
History lessons?\n\nVery well, if you insist.

I must perform a ritual of clear sight, but I can't do it alone. I have a potion that must be placed in the ceremonial jars at the base of the stele surrounding the xanmeer.\n\nI'd ask my hunters, but most of them are wounded or fighting the beasts.
I have no idea what you're talking about.\n\nNow, if you don't mind? I'm very busy today.

Early in the First Era, when the Chimer were still new to Morrowind, the Nedes invaded. The battle that brought Sadal and Balreth here was the climax of that war. \n\nThe Chimer were forced to desperate measures to prevail.

A more obscure topic, certainly.\n\nIn ancient days, the Nedic tribes marched and plundered across the land. We call their descendants Nords. Even then, they were fearsome warriors who lusted for conquest.

Do they teach nothing these days? Long ago we were the Chimer, with light skin and fair eyes. We worshiped the Good Daedra. \n\nTo mark the ascent of the Three, we were gifted with this more sober complexion—and the realm of Morrowind forever.
The Steel Mask doesn't accept commissions from just anyone. Why should I recommend you?

Legends say you cannot destroy wispmothers, just as you cannot destroy the moon or stars. No, her essence must be sealed, or else she will rise from the swamps again.\n\nShe's taken a fancy to her new lover. This we can use against her.
Why did the kwama go crazy? The smoke vials were a joke. She said nobody'd get hurt. She promised! \n\nI didn't do anything wrong, I swear. It wasn't even my idea!

It was all Edrasa's idea! \n\nI knew it was wrong. I promise that if I don't get eaten by kwama, I'll go to the temple in Mournhold and pray to the gods with all my might. I'll even give gold to poor people … when I get some gold.

We have to get out of here. I know a shortcut! But there's a big kwama in the way.\n\nIt went into that tunnel over there. If you poke its eggs, I bet it'll come out. Then we can run up the tunnel and escape!
Our home taught us to survive.\n\nEverything in Black Marsh tries to eat us. When something bites us, we bite back harder.

A monstrous Orc and a treacherous storm mage. We slaughtered their troops, but they were too powerful to take down.\n\nMeejapa is tracking them to the east. Look for him if you think you can defeat these champions.
Xuth! I should have known. The stench of Oblivion permeates this bog.\n\nYou placed the potions, though—I can tell. The miasma around each stele has cleared up, at least temporarily.

We were set upon by the Vereansu, a tribe of heathen Ashlanders. They attacked Muth Gnaar, this place of healing and refuge, killing monks and afflicted alike.\n\nWe're a simple order. We use the <<1>> to help those afflicted by the Llodos plague.

I gathered as many survivors as I could, but the Vereansu have taken captives. They toss them into burning buildings!\n\nOur leader, <<1>>, is still in there searching for survivors and trying to protect the <<2>>.

Our retreat here was no accident, soldier. Only at this place of Daedric power can we complete the ritual of calling.\n\nWe'll wrench the Daedra from their dark plane, split them open, and use their power and Nede blood to save our people.
I don't know. They revere Veloth. Call him the Prophet. They hate this plague and probably want the relic for themselves. \n\nBut they disrupted our work and now the plague husks are everywhere!

Yes, with the power of the ancients behind me, I can discover the exact nature of our enemy. Perhaps then we can discover how to cleanse the swamp of this foulness.\n\nStand back. This may be dangerous. Talk to me when I'm done.

The Daedric corruption is strong. I was nearly overwhelmed, but at last I've pinpointed the source.\n\nThey attack our heart, our soul, our memories—they're attacking our Hist tree. We must free it at once.
I must conduct the rite. Your duty is simple: do not let any souls enter this circle, or they will become trapped as well.\n\nLet me know when you are ready.
A keystone? I don't know what you're talking about. \n\nI can't think of anything while my kingdom is in ruins, not while trussed up like a boar awaiting a feast. Free me!
We understand you would not recognize royalty when tied to a pillar. Therefore, we request you untie us.
Then you know what I did. I can hear it in your voice. It was foolish and dangerous. I'm so ashamed.\n\nI've been trying to make up for all this by helping the injured workers.

It was a gift from Boril. If he sees it, he'll know I was involved. Please, I deserve to be punished, but I don't want to lose Boril.\n\nIf you don't reveal my part in this, I promise I'll find a way to make up for it.
Almalexia bless you!\n\nYou won't regret this. I'll help Boril and the miners. I'll even stop complaining about the kwama. And I'll certainly never do anything so foolish ever again.
Let me see that! \n\nThis is my wife's amulet. She told Renvis to poison the mine? Why would she do such a thing?
Foolish, selfish woman! Workers were hurt. Livestock was killed.\n\nI won't tell the others what she did, but I don't know if I'll ever be able to trust her again.
You are kind, One-Who-Stands-Over-Me.\n\nCould you stab his corpse with my dagger, the Mota Fang? I feel bad that my failure has denied Mota her chance to feast on his flesh.
Maybe, but I've seen it all. I don't think anything could surprise me anymore. \n\nLet me take a look.
You! You're the reason the guards are on alert.\n\nWhat do you want from me?
Oh. My.\n\nDo you know what this is? It's an original edition of "The Art of Love and Swordplay" of the Nord poet Fjokki.

I knew Vanus Sathram would cause us no end of trouble. It's because of Magistrix Vox. His loyalty to her is … unhealthy.\n\nHe lives in the house next door. Please, don't let him drag all of House Dres into a mess of his making.

It details, in epic balladry, the carnal exploits and adventurous deeds of the warrior poet Fjokki.\n\nThe author claims the work is a true history, but many of the exploits it recounts are, well, highly unlikely.
Fjokki was a bard of exceptional imagination but decidedly limited skill. \n\nAccording to his epic stanzas, he never met a creature he couldn't make love to or kill. Or both.
Don't judge House Dres by the actions of Vox's Maulborn cult. They broke off on their own, I swear it!
Dozens of works describe individual aspects, but nothing really encompasses that vast and labyrinthine subject.\n\nTry this one. "The Dapper Dunmer." It's all yours.
It's an axiom that there's no such thing as a Dunmeri joke book, but this is close: "The Dunmer Dunce." \n\nTake it. Please.
No, it's lurid trash, and common as guar. \n\nBut I admit I've had a weakness for Fjokki since my youth. What do you want for it?

You're only a soldier, so I'll spare you details. We're infusing the blood of our enemies and the Daedric essences you collect into our chosen vessels.\n\nThe general and his brother have volunteered themselves for this … sacrifice.

The general and his brother will die—the power they receive will consume them. But they will be reborn, more fearsome than even the mightiest horde of Nede warriors. \n\nWe, the Chimer, will win this day.
Excellent. My house believes in deeds, not words.

We're in trouble. Your diversion worked, and Gar went looking for his younger brother. That's the good news.\n\nThe bad news is the Goblins are gathering for a final attack on the hold. Quickly, get to Hrogar and warn him.

Be quiet, unless you want to join me. \n\nThese pirates are smuggling supplies and weapons to the Dominion troops in Shadowfen. If we don't shut down their operation, the Dominion's skirmishes will turn into a full-blown battlefront.

Greed. I foolishly thought that since most of the pirates are Argonians, they'd hate the Dominion.\n\nBut coin and old hatreds speak louder than words in this town, as you can guess. Little more than animals, they are.

Because he's a spy. Why else would he be here? He was blathering about our duty to Shadowfen. He was spying. It's obvious.\n\nNever trust a Dark Elf, especially my mates. They're proven pirates, ain't they?

For the crime of believing pirates cared about the welfare of the Pact.\n\nRumors say the Dominion is smuggling in supplies through this miserable landing. My questions were not welcome. Their so-called leader seized me and put me out here to rot.

Or maybe you could join me here. No?\n\nIf you insist, you'll have to get her attention. A few well-placed punches should get you an audience. You might try going to the beached ship and knocking heads with one of the drunken rowdies there.
I will follow. The map will show the way.\n\nThese symbols are two landmarks. Find them, and we will know where the treasure lies.

No, I'm the last of the Kothringi. I should rejoin my people. There's a ritual to pass the keystone on to you, although it would mean my death.\n\nLet me give you the keystone. At least my survival will have meaning.
I am prepared for this.\n\nMy village and my family all died without purpose. I've lived long enough alone. I am ready to join them.
When you absorb the keystone, a part of the Kothringi will live on as well.
Let me pass the keystone to you. Your need is greater than mine. \n\nI have no fear of death, only death without purpose.
Each of the Voleks has been dealt with … one way or another. Betina is the last of her line.
Tastes-the-Breeze and I had an egg-daughter. Eyes-that-Glint.\n\nThe Voleks worked her to death. Their own daughter must pay for that crime!
Ha! Good joke! Rigurt can't wait to use it on the Dark Elf ambassador. \n\nNow, which glorious item can I tell you about?
Did she, now? I suppose I can spare one of my scouts.\n\nTell me what you need. Do you prefer someone good with a bow or good with a blade?
A rogue it is. Watch his back. I'd like to see him return in one piece.
One of my archers will suffice. She'll take good care of you.
They're relics that tap into <<1>>'s power. Anyone who controls all the keystones and <<1>> itself would become nearly unstoppable.\n\nObviously, it would be disastrous if the Dominion got them.
Thanks! And remember to speak loudly—you're a Deputy Envoy of Nord Culture now!

Dark Elf dress is so fancy! I heard of tailor in Mournhold's crafting district named Iirila Maleran.\n\nGive her our gift of Nord traditional garb. She'll be so impressed, she'll give us nice Dunmer clothes in return.
That is a top-notch cultural relic—a Heart of the Wild! \n\nTake it to the monastery called Muth Gnaar. Give it to monks as offering, but make sure to get a good Dark Elf relic in return.

The little gray-skins mentioned a place with a great library. Shad Astula. \n\nThey're sure to appreciate our book. Maybe trade for a book on Dark Elf culture and customs. That would be most excellent!
Splendid! When you recover enough materials around our kingdom, use the anvil to shape it.\n\nHere's a smithing hammer, loyal subject. We are, after all, a benevolent monarch.

Riddles! Yes, I enjoy riddles. It has been a long time since anyone has challenged me. For a long time, I have protected the vessel from covetous eyes.\n\nA riddle game, mortal? Let us play, for I grow bored.
Foolish words will be your downfall, mortal.\n\nI await your next answer. Pray it is more informed than the last.
You have played my game fairly. Or perhaps luck guides you through it. Either way, your answer is true.\n\nThe vessel is yours, until it returns to my watch again.
Over the ages, you will curse your haste. Mortals are too rash. \n\nBe sure of your next answer. My patience with folly is not endless.

A serpent swims with silver lungs,
And soon will drink the vessel dry,
A bird of gold danced on its tongue,
Both flutter, fade away, and die.

What am I?
Why, they're our people! \n\nEven if they weren't, we wouldn't suffer anyone to be treated that way. Not in our kingdom.
It spoke? By Sithis, I don't know how you could carry this. It reeks of Oblivion.\n\nLet me begin the … wait, something's happening! Xuth!
Hmm. I prefer gold. But what have you got?
Baby mammoth fur! The Great House nobility will go mad for this.\n\nHere. Take these display pieces. They were made with my experimental dyes. Makes the colors nice and vibrant.

Oh, don't worry. A mere triviality. Certainly nothing that should stand in the way of a cultural exchange.\n\nHere. Take these display pieces. They were made with my experimental dyes. Makes the colors nice and vibrant.

What's that odor? Have these ever been washed? Wait. This is baby mammoth fur. It's illegal to export it. \n\nYou know, in the name of cultural exchange with our allies, I might have something to trade.
I don't know what to tell you, stranger. Have you seen what's happening here?\n\nDid you bring arms and armor, or maybe some kindlepitch? We could use some Nord war supplies right about now.

The Three have taught us, "Fulfill your rights and duties." \n\nHere, take this loaf of stale bread. Tell them it's the Holy Loaf of … oh, I don't know. Make something up. Exaggerate. Nords like that.
That's an animal heart! Like, from an ox! What am I supposed to do with a dried ox heart?\n\nPatience. Patience. I suppose you want something in exchange for this?
He'll be mourned. He was the father of us all … in spirit, I mean.\n\nI wish he could have let go of his anger. I hated seeing him like that.

When we go to market, they spit on us and call us heretics. When we pass, they draw their children inside.\n\nIf our men are beaten or our women assaulted, the first question the Ordinators ask is, "What did you do to provoke this?"
To you, what passes between Ashlanders and House Dunmer is distant news. They oppress us. We retaliate.\n\nFor you, it's all rather abstract, but we have to live with it every day.
Last year the Ashkhan's daughter was murdered. The attackers were known, but the Ordinators did nothing.\n\nWhen her brother complained, they slit his throat.
I spotted <<1>> tied up over there. And I heard Nuwisha's voice coming from the cave nearby.\n\nAs for <<2>>, he must be deeper in the Dominion's camp.
Vox's son grew distant, more radical. He broke his mother's heart.\n\nWatch, listen. This is how Vox's dark journey begins.
Then return to the eve of the Chimer's defeat. Return to the moment when the Brothers were born!
She's upstairs crying over her husband's corpse.\n\nGo on up there. If her husband starts to move, kill him with fire.
Meram was caught and punished. \n\nMagistrix Vox witnessed her son's torment. She was powerless to intervene.
Sure. What do you want to know?

The soldiers have their hands full with the Withered Hand and couldn't spare anyone to handle this business. So they hired us.\n\nTimes are hard, but if you're a mercenary with a bit of skill you can earn decent coin.
Never seen a lamia before? They're vile snake-women, scales from the waist down and the neck up. They can control serpents and other poisonous creatures.

They've created a spell to fill us with raw elemental power, greater than our enemies can stand—if it works.\n\nWhat they can't say is what happens to us. Will my brother and I still remain or will we be nothing but beasts of destruction?
Sep teaches us to be patient, and so I am.

Zeht's tears are blessed, and the waters of this place were once pure. Pilgrims would come to pray at the shrine near the wellspring's heart, receiving blessings from all the gods.\n\nWith Ssethreka's brood present, the prayers have ceased.

Her very presence is a sickness. She is an abomination, with scales that drip poison and fangs that crave blood. Sep and all the gods of the sands curse her name!\n\nHer reign over these caves must end.
A spirit? Selfora is overrun with spirits. So many people died! And now they remain, angry and vengeful.

As a trusted servant of the Tribunal, Vox had access to their inner chambers and their most prized treasures.\n\nAlmalexia believed Vox's devotion was strong, her faith unshakeable. Almalexia was wrong.
I think so, but probably not too far. I need to get to the inn. That's where the survivors were gathering.
Oh, you're not here for the job? A thousand pardons!\n\nI hired Ragara and her mercenaries to investigate the Zehtswater Cave. It's south and east of here, by the Goat's Head Oasis.
Clean water is rarer than diamonds in the desert. It's in everyone's interest to see the cave secure.\n\nOf course, it helps that my business is making sure water is accessible. For a price.

The oasis is a source of water for many travelers, and the cave itself is a sacred site for those who worship Zeht and Sep.\n\nSomething has poisoned the waters. And the native creatures are in a frenzy.

Fair point, fair point. All right, I won't deny it. Friends and I came looking for Daedric tidbits to sell to mages.\n\nThen those Dominion soldiers came. They were thick on the ground until today. I was about to make a break for it when I saw you.
Caught, one by one. I'm the only one alive. Well, alive and wearing my own skin.\n\nHey, let's help each other escape. You draw their attention and I'll slip past them. What do you say?

You what, now? Look, some Dominion mogul came through here, a while back. "<<1>>," they called him.\n\nHe's the one who bound a Dremora and forced her to steal faces off the dead. You want to stop him? You must've been the only egg in your clutch.

Used a captive Dremora to pull their souls from their body and seal them in magic rocks. Then … well, you've seen how these Dominion wear faces.\n\nI still hear their voices, calling from those rocks. They're dead, but still in pain. What a scam.
Rage consumes me! The Maulborn invade my home. They attack my children. They attack me! \n\nYou have proven yourself loyal and capable. I call upon you to serve me once more.
The old protective wards have been restored. We swim against a current that is too strong.
Xuth! You're the sun on my scales. The first ward is beneath the ruins just ahead.
Other wards are in other ruins, along the approach to the spire.\n\nGo swiftly. And may the wind be at your back.
Daedra, down in the caldera. We tried to push past them. \n\nWe failed. I'm lucky to be alive.
I know that now. Sadal summoned the Daedra the moment we arrived.\n\nEven with the artifact, I can't control him.

One final ward remains. Your key won't work. To disable the ward, you'll need to slay an ancient gatekeeper lurking in the caldera. Summon her at the ritual bowl below us. \n\nAnd listen: I'm sorry, my friend.
An unfortunate, but not unexpected, turn of events.\n\nHopefully, this <<1>> has taken her last victim for a few generations.

I was blind … a desperate Mer, tricked by his loneliness.\n\nYou know, she must have loved me. She saved my life so many times … from Dominion spies, from things in these swamps. She … it must have really cared.
Farewell, curious creature.

What business is that of yours, outsider? \n\nNo, forgive me. That's the pain speaking. <<1>> sent us out to collect <<z:2>> blood sacs and <<z:3>> venom. But something has driven the creatures mad. They attacked us!

We don't know. Nexith is planning a divination to reveal the power corrupting the swamp's creatures. He needs those components, but we failed to collect them.\n\nCan you help us? He's waiting south of here at the xanmeer, our stone temple.
The Maulborn penetrated the Temple and opened a portal into Oblivion. Even now, Daedra swarm within its hallowed halls.\n\nSuch sacrilege must not stand!
Appearances are everything! They feed opinion and belief, and such matters are important to me. \n\nBut enough questions! Save the Temple and you will be renowned among mortals and favored by gods.

You shall hear, though you shall never speak of it. \n\nThis enemy uses guile and subterfuge. I need time to understand the threat they pose. My divine defenses have been breached and the Temple has been invaded. I cannot be seen to fail!
Magistrix Vox used Daedric magic to split the seams of the wards around the High Chapel. Then she opened an Oblivion gate to fill the Temple with Daedra.
We're Shadowscales, born under the sign of the Shadow and trained as assassins from birth. \n\nWe're called upon to sway the balance of power, or right wrongs, in and around Black Marsh.

Vox seeks to desecrate the Temple, steal our holy artifacts, and then loose Daedra upon Mournhold. \n\nIf she succeeds, a great many of my children will die. And my people may lose confidence in the Tribunal. That would be catastrophic.
You need to get into the High Chapel. Vox managed to bypass the defenses, but its wards are still in place, drawing on the full power of the Tribunal. \n\nWe must get you past those wards.
Go to the cloisters of Vivec and Sotha Sil. My companion gods are absent, but they left trials I can activate to grant their blessings. \n\nPass the trials and you will be blessed.
Without the blessing of each of the Three, no mortal may pass through the wards and enter the High Chapel.\n\nYou have more than proven yourself to me. You have my blessing already.
Vivec's teachings often take the form of allegories and tales. His lessons are learned by listening and then acting.\n\nHis challenge exemplifies that approach. You must listen, then act.

A temple worker named Vamen dueled Belronen Telvanni, slaying him before witnesses. But Vamen was a loyal spy. To incite such discord was against his nature.\n\nAs Vivec did, speak with Vamen. Determine who truly slew the Telvanni.
Kill you? I could have done that long ago.\n\nYou are strong. You overcame obstacles that blocked even the false goddess. Why kill you? You'd make a fine ally.
Some can stay isolated in the Vale or some may choose the outside world. Two sides of the same path. \n\nThe merchant's presence has already changed the Vale. What happens next is inevitable.

We've lived in the vale since before the first fireside story was told, and we honor the Ghost Snake. We care for its serpent kin and live in harmony with them. \n\nFor this, Ghost Snake watches over us and protects us.

The Coiled Path tests us, proving our worth to the tribe and the Ghost Snake. Those who survive the journey become stronger and wiser. Those who fall become ghosts, protecting the vale.\n\nMay Ghost Snake guide you, outsider.
<<1>> and I think you should be the one invested with the power of the Relleis Lor keystone. The only way to acquire it is by absorbing the stone.\n\n<<1>> knows the ritual.
Because the Shadowscales know you're someone we can count on, someone who sees things through to the end. You deserve to possess its power.\n\nAre you ready to begin the ritual?
You intrude where you have no place. You weaken the rites it took dozens of mages to craft. Are you insane, mortal?
Perhaps, but spellcasting of this magnitude requires planning, patience, and perfect execution.
Trial and error is the essence of spellcasting. Many attempts are necessary before a spell succeeds.\n\nSome never succeed. We shall see. Submit to the trials.
I'll teleport you to the top of caldera. Simply retrieve the Focus Stone at the back of the nearby cave. \n\nYou'll need to follow the spells we took to contain Sadal. Are you ready?
Do you indeed? Perhaps you aren't as short-sighted as that arrogant Indoril grandmaster.
I find myself almost impressed, but before the way to Sadal's prison opens, there is another test.\n\nMy colleague guards the final Focus Stone. Are you ready?
Again I find myself talking to you. Very well. \n\nAs you've already seen, completing a complex spell requires precision. Controlling the ebb and flow of Magicka is the heart of spellcraft.
The cave behind you holds the final Focus Stone. To reach it, you must understand the ebb and flow of magic.\n\nYou represent all living mortals here. Try not to embarrass yourself.
So you do. Unlike the grandmaster, you've proven you can act with planning, patience, and courage.\n\nNow with our aid, you can reforge Sadal's bindings.
We'll return to the caldera. Place the foci around the caldera platform. The other mages and I will take it from there.
My mother? I have a mother? I don't remember much besides my name. This is my world, my everything. I've never known anything but this place. \n\nAnd you don't belong here. Why are you here?

The keystone is a relic that can tap into the power of Loriasel, an Ayleid ruin here in Shadowfen.\n\nIf someone obtained all the keystones they'd have control over Loriasel, and that would grant them immense power.
Our ancestors created them. We did not always live as we do now.\n\nEvery xanmeer contains echoes of our earliest magic. Using my connection to the swamp, I'll reveal the corruption's source.

Namira is the Lady of Decay, the Daedric Prince of spirits and shadows. She's the patron of vermin and squalor.\n\nShe wants to extend her influence over Xal Ithix. The relic is the key to open that door. But you can use it against her minions.
The Keeper bound these two, but it said I was too precious for bonds. Its master wanted me to decide for myself when my memories return.\n\nWhat does that mean? Memories of what?
A fanatic? Daedric Princes? I … your words ring true.\n\nWhat … what did I do?
A power struggle? I don't remember any of that. I don't remember who I was.\n\nThere must be something I did … before …  that would help me remember.
<This skeleton is covered in Hist sap, and strange runes are carved into its bones.>

<This journal's pages are written with a burned piece of wood. There's name is on its cover: <<1>>.>\n\n"… no demands or hints about what they want. Tried to look at their leader, a Nord. His face is always covered."

The Dominion captured their souls in strange rocks. They're on platforms, and they glow like rutting wamasu.\n\n<<1>> complained the rocks were very fragile. I bet smashing them would release my friends.
Just so. The general leading the Nede troops is called Ornskar. Kill her and cut out her heart. \n\nWhen you have these sacrifices in hand, meet me at the ritual altar in the center of the temple.
Yes, that is true. \n\nMy suffering follows a different path. I'm cursed to only observe.
My thoughts, my memories … they're a jumble. \n\nI think there may be a way to save the town. It's so hard to remember.
I can't. It's as if a fog covers my past. I know I am cursed and little more. This is my home and I must watch this suffering.\n\nIf the veil lifts from my mind, I'll tell you what I can.
Be wary, stranger. My heart tells me spirits aren't the only things left in the wake of Selfora's destruction.
There was a decanter, somewhere in the temple below. Its water was holy. \n\nYou have seen the strange fires throughout town? I remember that much. Maybe this liquid can quench those flames.

Violent, unthinking monsters!\n\nWithout our constant prayers to direct the power of the Tear, many of the afflicted were suddenly overwhelmed by the plague, and they transformed into those … creatures!
Don't ask questions. Just listen. We know where our people are being held, including Councilor Ralden.\n\nFollow the clues in the pack. I'll see you at the meeting place.
Lesser supplicants who petition the bride of Sithis for aid. When I deign to answer, my Shadowscales prune the garden of Mer and Men.
A small blessing, my supplicant. You could smell their lies.\n\nNow, take my blade. See the world as it truly is.
Gaze upon the true enclave around you—the domain of Sithis! There, you shall find the traitor's soul and destroy it!

I'll get these to Madras. No one will question why I have the weapons, since I'm a smith and all.\n\nGet back to the kinhouse and wait for us there. I'll be sure Madras sends someone to find you when we're ready.
Take it to the dais and place it with the reliquary pieces.\n\nVox believed that when she shattered my reliquary, she removed me from this battle. Your deeds have foiled her scheme.

She wants to return to a simpler time, when our people worshiped the Good Daedra. But that time is passed.\n\nNonetheless, she wields my hammer, Veloth's Judgment. I used it to defend our people. She uses it for revenge.
