The fog begins to clear, but so many memories rush in!\n\nWhat you fought was an echo of Magistrix Vox. She left it here to bind the spirits to this place. Part of her punishment of Selfora.
I got the information from my contact in the group. \n\nReport back to the kinhouse. I'll meet you there. I'm going to retrieve a key that you'll need. And keep this quiet, all right?

They've always had a mean streak. Don't get me wrong, they're great warriors, but ever since the General made them the camp enforcers, well … let's just say they've become overly enthusiastic.\n\nI probably shouldn't say any more.
I've already said too much. I don't want any more trouble than I've already got.\n\nIf you want to know more, talk to Commander Taldyn. Just watch yourself. The Sentinels can be fearsome enemies.

You could try. The Sentinels are all about power through intimidation. The only way to stop them is to beat them at their own game. \n\nChallenge their fiercest warriors to face you in combat. Defeat them and you break their hold on the camp.
We're trying to restrain Balreth but Daedric portals keep opening. Those of us who've survived Balreth are being pulled down by cursed Scamps.
Take what's in this pouch, throw it in the portals. I was supposed to but my coming death prevents me. \n\nFind Magister Enuse when you're done. She should be north of here.

The vicecanons expect our help? Where were the vicecanons when the Imperials left us to rot? \n\nWe've been trapped here for years. Half the prisoners lost their minds and started eating the rest of us.
You don't have to tell me twice!
It's close by. Now that the fire's out, I should be able to make it.

I was carrying orders when they captured me. Should've been more careful, but we've never seen Imperial activity this deep in the desert.\n\nI didn't even have time to destroy the orders. They've got everything I was carrying.

They contained every patrol route the Covenant uses in the area. We need to make sure we recover those orders, and eliminate everyone who's seen them. Luckily, I know exactly who to hit.\n\nIf you're willing.

You'll want to find <<1>> and <<2>>. They interrogated me, and they're the only ones high ranking enough to bother reading the orders.\n\nSo eliminate them and recover my orders. And then we maybe can get out of here.
<<1>> is a good woman. May I live long enough to tell her so.\n\nIf you're looking for the Bellael keystone, does that mean you're going to free us?
It's pretty clear that we're in over our heads. They took out four of my companions. What chance do I have against those monsters?\n\nDon't worry. I'll make it worth your time in the end.
You utter fool. Stop me? Not even the Tribunal can stop me.\n\nThe power of Veloth's Judgment courses through my body. You shall feel its power as I take your life and absorb your soul.
Innocent? Innocent? You saw what your goddess did to my son!\n\nWhy do you choose to be a willing slave of those imposters? Think for yourself. Stand with me.

The Tribunal is a lie. They were born as mortals, no more divine than we are. Who are they to sit in judgment on us?\n\nThey just found a way to gain and wield great power. As I have. And as you shall, if you join me.

Let me absorb your strength, combine it with my own. Have no fear. You won't die, but you will become part of something greater than yourself. \n\nHold still while I strike you with the Judgment. Strike you—and make you immortal!
Free? I don't understand.\n\nMy companions often speak of freedom, as if there's something more somewhere else. But they say we're trapped, that the Keeper holds us in this realm.
Up there, on the western altar. We can't touch it.\n\nYou could talk to my companions. About freedom. I'll listen.
I am. I was. What's the proper way to say that when you're dead?
Don't be. You saved my family. And you can do something more. You can save Selfora.
There's some kind of link between the Bellael keystone and prisoners going feral.\n\nIf you don't use it to free us, if you just take the keystone away, the results will be disastrous.
Vox possesses my hammer, the Judgment. Like any such artifact, it can be used for good or turned to darker purposes.\n\nBut all is not lost. I can protect you from the hammer's powers.
When Judgment falls, Vox kills her target and traps its soul. The trapped souls feed her power, making her stronger than other mortals.\n\nFew can survive the hammer's strike. But you shall.

I shall bestow upon you my blessing. Imbued with the power of my holy favor, the hammer cannot kill you. \n\nBut it will send you to where the other souls are trapped. You shall free Vox's prisoners and thus break her power.
The Keeper imprisons us. It binds us to this realm.\n\nIt mocks us. We can't touch it. We can't touch anything. But you?

The Keeper feeds upon the orbs of ruin around the altar. I've seen it. The Keeper's linked to those orbs. \n\nIf you attack it, it will turn to the orbs for power. But if you were to shatter the orbs while the Keeper feeds ….
Perhaps. The Keeper says it holds our souls—that's how we're bound. \n\nIf the Keeper is defeated, perhaps I would be free.
The Keeper's tricks hold me here. It's locked my soul away and it taunts me with it, holding it in its crazy game of puzzles.\n\nIt's so close, but it might as well be a million leagues away.
I can't touch it. I can't touch anything.\n\nBut, you? Can you? If you could strike the keys, slow them down so they reach the locks at the same time …. Oh, please. You must try it.
On the eastern dais, two keys rotate in a pattern around two locks on the flagstones.\n\nTo free my trapped spirit, both keys must be in place on both locks at the same time. Or so the Keeper says.
I killed? Yes. I killed. I remember. I thought they deserved it.\n\nMother! The Three! Who did this? Tell me?
Murder. Yes. And it isn't over, is it? Because now my mother murders in my place.\n\nCome. I'll open the portal to her domain. Together we'll stop her. This has gone on long enough.
The way you say that, I know I did something horribly wrong. I must have. \n\nBut who made me like this? Who put me here?

Then here I shall remain. If I hurt others before, I must be here to protect others from me. Yes, that must be so.\n\nI can do one thing. I'll open the way to the Reservoir of Souls for you, the way back to the mortal realm.
Sure I know <<1>>. That bum owes me money.\n\nLast I heard he was upstairs.
Watch out for <<1>>. He always keeps close to his body guard.\n\nIf you want to get to him, you should time it so his body guard isn't around.

Aside from the fact that she is utterly mad? She came to receive the blessing of Saint Veloth himself. The Saint told her she was doing evil, not good. \n\nShe flew into a rage, smashed the reliquary and opened the Daedric portals.
<The keystone glows with a pale light.>
Indeed he is.\n\nI believe Vox was afraid he would try to stop her mad plans. By smashing the reliquary, she drained the Saint of his power.
The Velothi tradition is not all meditation and contemplation. Veloth was a warrior as well.  \n\nSadly, some lost their lives to Vox's madness.

"A master creates the Perfect. That which sparks numbers the Houses which built this temple. That which spins numbers my closest companions and myself.\n\n"A master destroys the Imperfect. That which threatens is rendered to its base components."

I'm heading east, to Eidolon's Hollow. I suspect you'll be going there eventually.  \n\nLook for me in the camp there. They're going to need my skills as a healer and an alchemist for the final push against Magistrix Vox.
These are but a few of the innocents Vox imprisoned in her Reservoir of Souls.\n\nBut her power is broken now and they're free to pass on. That was your doing.
Sotha Sil has devised a test that allows him to learn more about you each time you complete it.\n\nYou are to repair one of his clockwork toys—and then break it.
All gears turn like the Hurling Disk. All artifice is ephemeral. And at times, parts are of more use than the whole. \n\nThere. Divine wisdom. Does that satisfy you?
Both Malvari and Da'ravis have been dead for a long time. They cannot return to life, but they can be set free.

"I've cast a barrier on the gate to the keep. Now I can complete my ritual unhindered. Without a <<1>> and a <<2>>, no one can cross the barrier.\n\n"And if the ritual is successful, Stonefall will be ours within days!"
Eldri fusses too much. \n\nI'm needed here. My contributions may be less flamboyant than those with a more militaristic approach, but I help in my own small way.

Fort Virak sent a small group of troops to help Lukiul Uxith. They are good neighbors.\n\nThe Covenant insects swarmed them before they reached town. We came across them while hunting for the Lieutenant.
Ah, so much to explain.\n\nUnderstand this: the echo of Vox that you fought earlier isn't gone. It's my jailer and tormenter. I'm chained to it, but it's also chained to me.
With the decanter. It can do much more than put out magical fires. It's a vessel for spiritual energy.

Now you want to tell stories! Very well, I will tell you one of my own.\n\nThe Dominion came. They coveted our Hist tree. When we would not allow them to tap it, they slaughtered everyone and drained the tree of its sap.

You know nothing of my village. Argonians are bound to their Hist tree. My staff came from ours. Long ago, it was a gift from the Hist tree to us.\n\nMy people will feel and know the connection, but in madness they will resist.
They did not tell us their plans!\n\nNow the Hist tree has been drained and my people have nowhere to go when they die. They linger, trapped in madness.
Go to the crater in the middle of town. When you get there, I'll summon Vox's echo. Defeat the echo again, but this time draw it into the decanter.

Father … may have been overconfident. We broke the wards and, as you learned, dispelled the guardians when we summoned Balreth to Davon's Watch.\n\nFather was sure I'd be able to replace them. I don't want to let him down.

I showed you Magistrix Vox's arrival and how she demanded we join her. Treason! We would not do it.\n\nWhen we refused, she decided to make an example of us. She used Saint Veloth's Judgment to tear a hole in Selfora.
Yes. We called in several favors to do it, but we've cracked her code.\n\n<<1>> was after something hidden in a Dwarven ruin. A place known as <<2>>.
I'm not sure, just yet. <<1>> is far from here. From Doshia's notes I've prepared a portal that will carry us across Tamriel. \n\nWhat do you say, comrade? Will you venture with me into the unknown?
Take the crystal and the tome. Give them to Merric, and he can begin learning what it will take to forge the weapon.
I have something I must attend to, comrade. The knowledge we have gained here has flooded my mind … I must mind the river's course. \n\nI'm sure we'll speak again soon.

Our meeting at Othrenis left me curious and frustratingly conscious. Can you really imprison Balreth?\n\nDeath has given me a certain … perspective. And, of course, I have time to indulge my curiosity.
Balreth's attacks have cost him power. You should defeat him while he's weak.\n\nRight now, I feel him moving in the caldera of the volcano, gathering strength from the lava flows there.
Yes, though I doubt it will be easy. If he reaches a lava pool, Balreth will regain strength.\n\nThere was something else. Ah! Don't let him light you on fire. Yes, that's something you should avoid.

As you've seen, Scamps love the fire and magical energy Balreth exudes. Be ready to deal with more of them below.\n\nOnce we've destroyed his fiery shell, we'll be able to bind him again. This time, it will be for all eternity.

My staff can only hold so much. It's only a small branch of the Hist tree.\n\nIf they are not too mad, these spirits may have enough energy to restore the Hist tree. Then we can return to its warm embrace. Give me the staff.
The Hist tree screams! It suffers, and spreads its torment to us! Can't you hear it?\n\nThose screams … they'll drive us mad!
It's more than sap, it is the Hist tree's soul.\n\nWhen an Argonian is created, it is said the sap becomes the Argonian's blood … its essence … its spirit.

… are made from the essence of this Hist tree. As long as the spirits remain outside the tree, its essence is fragmented.\n\nWhen the Dominion boils this essence to create their foul brew, the torment to the tree and the spirits will be unbearable.

They're boiling, distilling, and destroying what's left of our Hist tree's sap!\n\nQuickly, take my staff again. The Dominion's camps are near. Find them, and use what power is left. Destroy their vats, and the staff can call the Hist sap back to us.
The Night Mother sees the absolute truth of one's soul. She speaks with our leader, but a walker in shadow and in light is … like, a borrowed coat in a thunderstorm, yes?
Praise the Three! Oh sweet, sweet Alto Wine. This makes me feel like singing!
It's the Fish Stink, down by the docks. A brute named Hectur runs it. He's unreasonable about his precious bottle. \n\nYou can't just smooth talk it away from him.

Good, it's quieter now as the madness fades. With the aid of my egg-kin, I can restore the Hist tree, but it must be done quickly. \n\nWe're fading. I don't know why, but our essence, our very being, drifts away on the breeze.

Yesterday, I thought I'd spend my remaining years trying to keep these people alive. Now I have options, and that's a good feeling. Thank you.\n\nYou'll want to find the gerent and let him know about the keystone.

If they interfere, our essence will fade before the Hist tree is restored.\n\nDon't expect help from my fellow spirits. I will draw on what little power they have left to strengthen my prayers. The rest of the burden is on you.
I don't think the Dominion will give up so easily. My guess is that they'll come back. If they do, you'll have to protect the ritual.\n\nSee to your needs. Then let me know when I should begin.
Very well. Last time, the Dominion came from the north, driving toward the Hist Tree. They are not the most cunning creatures, so I would expect the same this time.\n\nYou must protect the spirits!

Undead aren't part of the proper world. \n\nWe normally return to our Hist tree when we die, but if that's prevented or if our tree is suffering, we remain. Then we go mad. Is that considered natural?
With Vox's echo gone, I am free.
Tell my family I love them. Tell them to carry on.
Prepare yourself. The Echo of Vox approaches!

And then? In an instant, the souls of half the townsfolk were ripped from their bodies. They flew into the hammer. \n\nShe left nothing but twisted remnants of those souls behind as guardians of sorts.
Undo, no. Soothe, maybe. But first you must defeat the Echo of Vox. It holds the corruption here. It's the poison in Selfora's wound.
He's a blowhard, and he hates bad singing.\n\nWhen Valen gets soused on Alto Wine and starts belting out verses, look out!

The Maulborn put events into motion you can't comprehend, let alone stop. Your general is dead and his body lies in the caves below! Let me go and perhaps I'll convince my mistress to kill you quickly.

Well, all right. But you didn't hear this from me.\n\nSince the General made them camp enforcers, the Sentinels have become brazen criminals. They're even forcing people to pay for protection. Nund refused to pay. Now he's got three broken fingers.
I've already said too much. I don't want any more trouble than I've already got.\n\nIf you want to know more, talk to Commander Taldyn. Just watch yourself. The Sentinels can be fearsome enemies.
Best I can do on short notice. Sorry.
Hmm. Well, I do know that the guard watching the General's quarters, Defender Furen, hasn't been paid lately. Maybe you can use that, hmm?
I feel sick. Too many fumes.
Thanks. I did a stupid thing.\n\nEdrasa gave me this necklace so I'd do it. She said it was a present from Cousin Boril, when they got married. It's worth more than I earn in a month!
Here, take Edrasa's necklace. I don't want it any more. \n\nI can get out through the tunnel, now that it's clear. I'm really sorry. Really, really sorry.

She said Cousin Boril only cares about the kwama. She thought that if the mine got closed for a few days, he might take her to Mournhold. She wanted to dance and shop and have fun.\n\nShe never thought the kwama would go crazy!

You've seen it yourself. Balreth, the Brother of Strife, is forever imprisoned. He's shackled to Ash Mountain.\n\nYou did this. You did what took countless mages many attempts and failures. For a mortal, you're quite an impressive sort.
Yes! You should thank me! You couldn't have done it without me. And you are welcome.\n\nNow go. Get out of here. This is no place for the living.
She used to serve in the Morrowind army as a war wizard. I think the explosions were too much for her. \n\nAfter she retired from service, she opened the Ebony Flask with <<1>>.
Not exactly, but then again, that's your side of this business, isn't it?\n\nMy only advice is to talk to the nightflowers at the inn. In their line of work, they learn all the best secrets.
Lady Fedrasa? I don't care for her, actually, but the money here at the Ebony Flask is good. \n\nIf it wasn't, Amil and I would have cleared out long ago.
I don't hate her, but there's no love lost between the nightflowers and Fedrasa.\n\nShe regards us a necessary evil. She doesn't even partake of our talents! Pah! Plus, she's incredibly jumpy.

My guess is she's caught one too many fireball blasts in the war. She still hates loud noises.\n\nThere's an alchemist next door who's constantly testing flash powder and sulfurs. If she hears so much as a "pop," she jumps right out of her skin.
Yes! I'm sure a wealthy traveler and hero such as yourself could spare a few gold for a worthy cause!\n\nWon't you think of my poor children wasting away?
Thank you! Thank you!
I'm afraid I'm not at liberty to say.\n\nAll I can tell you is I swore to guard those chests with my life. That ought to give you some idea of their importance.
Ha! Let me guess. Orona convinced you to harvest kwama cuttle and bring it back to her?\n\nShe probably gave you some line about not being wasteful and putting the stuff to good use?
The only person she plans on helping is herself. She'll sell the stuff in Mournhold and make a tidy profit.
What does it matter? The kwama had to be killed. Is it better that the cuttle go to waste? Why pass up the opportunity to make some gold?\n\nOr are you thinking of selling the cuttle yourself?
My idea, my profit. Alchemists can't get enough of it, and it's not commonly available. That makes this the perfect situation.\n\nI won't apologize for being pragmatic.
Ah, yes! This will help my egg-brothers and egg-sisters rest in peace!
Follow me. You'll see.
Did he? I bet he got hurt fooling around with the spider constructs.
The cultists forced their undead thralls to carry it away. Such will be the future of <<1>> if you don't recover the <<z:2>>.
What brings a war hero of the Ebonheart Pact to distant Kragenmoor? I would be more welcoming, but today important matters distract me.
Apologies, but the Vanguard demands my attention at the moment. If you have further questions—and I'm sure you do—speak to my seneschal.
How typical! Listen, this ruin is a two-person job. I need someone to cause a diversion so I can sneak into the next chamber.\n\nCould you test that control rod on the spiders inside?
No reason to get all gruff and grumpy! We'll take care of you.\n\nThere's bound to be valuable stuff in here. Raynor and I will split anything we find with you.
That's the spirit! Now go create a diversion.

How should I know? Raynor built it. \n\nHe calls it a control rod. I bet it controls the constructs! Use it to capture one of those spider things. It might take a few attempts, though. Raynor's devices don't always work exactly as he designed them.
The first is Varnag, a feral nix-hound. The next is worse: Bleiger, a vicious and territorial bull netch.\n\nWorst of all is a clannfear named Gurlisk.
We drove our guar here to trade. \n\nThe ashlands give our tribe many things, such as food and shelter. They aren't as generous with medicinal potions or steel.
Ha! Even if we would have the housemen, they wouldn't have us.\n\nThey won't even let us within their walls to trade. We must stay outside, bedding with their animals.
They believe the three elders of their "Tribunal" are gods.\n\nWe know the truth. The so-called Three are murderers and necromancers.
Because they're heretics … or because we are. Whichever you prefer.\n\nWe hold true to the faith of our ancestors: the worship of Azura, Boethiah, and Mephala.

You'll need a disguise to appear as one of the Vanguard. The sentry at the door is turning everyone else away. Once inside, try to stay out of sight.\n\nSpeak to <<1>>. I hear she might have what you're looking for.
Now? Here?\n\nNo, I've already said too much. I have no love for the housemen, but my people need their wares. Ask someone else.
A kind gift removes suspicion. You come for a package for the great House Dres, yes? Here it is.
Threats and menace, threats and menace. Here, take the uniform, and leave poor Kaasha to her bondage.
He's the least vicious of the three, but look what he did to my leg!\n\nWe met him on the road southeast of Ebonheart. Our best guess is he escaped from a Goblin tribe … or ate them.
He floats along the shore west of here. \n\nDo not ask me the origin of his name. I assume it stems from the way netches float through the air.
Strange story, that. Summoned by an old conjurer who lived in the hills east of Kragenmoor. The conjurer died, but it stayed. No one knows why, and no hunter's ever tracked it to its lair.
Truly? How did you … no, the Night Mother's blessings are not for me to know.
Everyone who wants to ascend the Tormented Spire must speak to the grandmaster of Kragenmoor. House Dres controls access to the peak. It's an ancient site of magic and blood.

Families were always separated. Though kept apart, we sometimes managed to meet. When I despaired the most, thoughts of them kept me sane.\n\nIn the end, they died deep within this place, alone and afraid. Look in the cells.
Dres holds the magical pattern for a key: a mystical focus that allows you to pass the veil protecting the spire. Only with the key can one make the climb to the summit.
My memory fades, thank S'rendarr.\n\nI remember fear, rage, and pain … and then relief.
Very little. The Imperials built it in the First Era. When they were pushed out of <<1>>, they abandoned it.\n\nI'm not sure why the prisoners remained. Some say they're cursed.
He had the reputation of being honorable, at least for an Imperial.\n\nI don't know what he did to get left here, but it must've been bad. The Empire abandoned a skilled general.
Don't you think we've tried? My Imperial brethren used the power of your precious keystone to bind us to this prison. If we leave, we die.\n\nNo one bound to the keystone can even touch it.
Argonian artifacts of great power. Legend ties them to various ruins throughout <<1>>. The vicecanons can't let them fall into the wrong hands.
Of course. I'll tell you anything I can.
I refused to slaughter a village of Argonians. It wasn't a fair fight. They had no soldiers.\n \nI don't believe in pointless slaughter. My superiors thought otherwise.
It hasn't been easy. Argonian traders stop by sometimes, and we've been able to forage enough old Imperial supplies to muddle through.

Each Great House has its sphere of influence. Would you begrudge the Hlaalu their merchant contracts?\n\nHouse Dres has done much to help civilize the less fortunate races. And besides, we are now forbidden to enslave our Pact allies.
Tanval Indoril left them behind after his talk with Grandmaster Dres.\n\nOur grandmaster is the only one who can grant access to Tormented Spire. He must have agreed. Tanval went that way.

It's an ancient site of blood, magic, and power. Sadal, the Brother of Strife, is held prisoner there.\n\nWe think Tanval wants to use the Coral Heart to free Sadal. He would unleash the monster on the Daggerfall Covenant.
It's probably in the prison warden's office. It'll be a long walk. The shorter paths up to it crumbled or collapsed long ago.\n\nThere will be a lot of ferals to deal with on the way up.
That's the beast that attacked our caravan. He savaged my leg and took one of our guar.\n\nI'm glad someone brought the thing down.
Ha! No. Lately, some savage creatures have been terrifying the wastelands. They've proven more than a match for our hunters.
I've heard of him. He's territorial and very powerful.\n\nMy people are better off with him gone. Thanks, stranger.
Ha! No. Lately, more savage creatures have been roaming the wastelands. Some even outmatch our hunters.
My tribe knows it well. An old conjurer summoned it before he died. Don't know why it didn't return to Oblivion, but it didn't. No hunter's lived long enough to track it back to its lair.
Ha! No. Lately, many savage creatures have been roaming the wastelands. Some are more than a match for our hunters.
You … monster! I'm just trying to earn an honest living!\n\nHere, take everything! Just don't hurt me. Please, just let me go!
You're a lifesaver! Thank you!
You have my eternal thanks.\n\nI owe my life to you.

I came back to look for my wife's cousin Renvis and the rest of our missing workers, but I haven't had much luck.  \n\nI've been stumbling around in the dark, trying to avoid getting eaten by kwama. But I did discover something quite disturbing.

Treachery! The mine is filled with open vials spewing noxious fumes. This was no accident.\n\nI sealed several of the vials and cleared this chamber, but I can't get down to the lower levels without getting swarmed by kwama.
My story? My wife returned from the war, but she brought the fight back with her.\n\nVivec knows, I tried to help her get over it, but I couldn't live with what she'd become. I left.
Might as well be dead. Or maybe I should be drunk. That's close enough.
Well hello there.  This is the QA conversation, are you able to read this?
I know, right!?
Good, good.  If you can read this as well, then this is a pass.
What do you mean, "no"?  How did you answer this question then?  Eh, what's that?  Explain yourself!!
Said good day, sir!
That's what I thought.  Good day, sir!
Hello!  I'm a talking pot!  A cauldron, to be exact!
Well then what are you bothering me for?  Now bugger off!
Yes, I believe I just said that. Now what can I do for you?
I know, amazing right?  Now get lost!
Don't you touch my stew!  It's not for you.  This stew is not for you and my favorite color is blue.  Boo hoo.
Just need a moment to recover. If you hadn't come along … I'll be fine, Stendarr willing.
Hello.  I guess the talking totem pole sent you?  Yes, I know why.  If you can read this, it must be working.
Yes, I'm sure.  Consider this part a pass.  Now you can move on to the next part.
Yes, really.
Have you eaten yet? The large, foul-tempered rats on the docks taste really good. \n\nIt's a pity the barkeep doesn't care for them. I don't know why.
He's a crank. He hates drunks singing in his bar. Apparently, he only likes "beautiful voices."
All my fault. The stinking Covenant boarded my ship while I was drunk in the crow's nest.\n\nWe lost everyone. Now I'm just a lookout on a barstool, sailing in a bottle.
Hectur? He's a crusty one. That makes it even funnier when you get under his skin.\n\nFor a good prank, grab a wharf rat and toss it in here. Then watch him go!
Nah. I buy him a drink once in a while, just to take his mind off things.\n\nThen he starts singing and Hectur wallops him. It's hilarious.
I see you know your wines, friend.\n\nTo get that bottle, I had to cut through a dozen Bretons and send their captain to Sovngarde.
What? I turned back an entire fleet of those dirtbags while I was swimming.\n\nWhy do you think they call me "The Fish"?
Well enough to know he's all talk.\n\nOnly one person should worry about Hectur: Valen when he's had too much Alto Wine.
I can't, at least not here. Hectur won't even sell Alto anymore because of Valen.\n\nOf course, you might find a loose bottle on the docks.
Hello.  You must be trying to pass the Talking Quest.
Yes.  Now be on your way.
Because I wrote it.  Anyway, consider thie a PASS
You mean my brother's invention actually worked?

If you do, you'll be the hero of Deepcrag! Seal the vials in the middle and lower chambers. If you run into any miners, give them one of Edrasa's potions. \n\nAnd keep an eye out for Cousin Renvis. He's not the sharpest arrow in the quiver.
I'm not sure. Its emitter … thing … is broken. I could fix it if I had some spare parts.\n\nHmm. Maybe we can get your sparky little friend to help us.
I have no idea! It might open that big door over there, or it might unleash a giant walking teapot with razors for arms. \n\nThere's only one way to find out, right?
Probably not. Just a legend. I'm almost positive.\n\nAnyway, there's something important here. I can feel it. Something the Arch-Mage won't be able to ignore.
Oh, don't be such a baby. You sound like my brother. Anyway, its emitter … thing … is broken. If I had some spare parts ….\n\nHmm. Maybe we can get your sparky little friend to help us.

No, not you—your spider. You'd just ruin the parts prying them out.\n\nGo beat some spiders into submission, then have your sparky friend collect their parts. I'll wait for you by the emitter at the other end of the chamber.
Dwarven constructs scavenge parts to repair themselves. They're designed to remove delicate mechanisms from disabled constructs to reuse elsewhere.
Watch yourself in there. Ayleid ruins are no place for the unwary.\n\nI must remain here to encode a report for the vicecanons. They'll be very interested in what you've uncovered so far.

The archives will reveal Vox's past, letting you witness the events that brought us to this moment. \n\nStart with the western anima archive and touch the anima crystal. Then speak to me and watch and learn.
I heard her communing with the Lord of Lies. Molag Bal is harvesting souls for some dark plot. He's especially interested in the souls of the faithful.

Comrade, grab that book and her notes on the table. I saw her scribbling after speaking to her master. We may be able to learn more about this plot, learn what this "Mortuum Vivicus" is. \n\nGrab them. Then let's get out of here.
Molag Bal! May he burn in the glare of a thousand suns!\n\nIt's just like him to send an assassin to kill a noble warrior. That's a coward's weapon.
Xuth! The Mortuum … what? And I can't make tails or scales of these scribblings. No matter.\n\nIt's going to take time to decipher this scrawl, but we'll put our best scribe on it.

There are certain things in my past that I cannot remember. Things that simply go black when I try to picture them.\n\nThis voice is the one constant. The one thing that is always there for me. Perhaps it is connected?
The Brothers of Strife are imprisoned. The storm has passed. The spire is silent again. It is over, at least for now.

Then I know that the memories that are no longer mine are meant to be forgotten. Perhaps I will find comfort in that. Perhaps I will start a different journey to seek out my past.\n\nBut at least I will have the voice to comfort and guide me.

He returned to wisdom at the end. Holgunn will grumble, but he will lead, at least until the Great Houses choose another.\n\nAs for me, I must return to my tribe. I will bask in the sun and try not to think of storms. Stay moist, my friend.
I had to say farewell. The honor of my House has been restored, Stonefalls is safe, and soon, Garyn and I will be side by side.\n\nMay the Three watch over you.

Inside Vox's cave. Whatever she is doing there, an extremely strong spiritual force is radiating out. Strong enough to drown out the voice that speaks to me.\n\nFind a way inside, get to a safe area, and contact me again. I'll know more then.
Kyle pretends to be a merchant, but what merchant outfits his crew in uniforms? They kick off anyone they don't recognize.\n\nHis sailors - and their uniforms - frequent a bar on the docks.
Of course I do. But that's a topic for another time. Heh.\n\nKyle keeps his things under close guard. You'll need a distraction if you want to get to them.

That milk-drinker? Ha! He's probably locked in his ship, pointing his sword at anyone not in one of his precious fancy uniforms.\n\nGo to the bar near the docks. His men'll likely be there, getting stanky Elf-drink all over their uniforms.
Never proposition a Dark Elf noblewoman.\n\nOh, about Kyle? His ship has a rat problem. They carry poison to control them. It works just as well on people, if you take my meaning.
He knows he is marked, and rings himself with men in colored garb.\n\nBut his men are weak to drink. Were I seeking to board his ship, I would visit the bar at the docks.
His ship has many rats beyond her captain.\n\nRelease a rat aboard the ship, and watch the lesser creatures scurry to catch it.

<<1>> fears for his life. He's surrounded himself with guards and hides behind lock and key.\n\nYou'll find him in the basement of his house, but you'll need a key to enter. I'd search his house for the key.
<<1>> likes to poison kittens. It would be poetic justice to use his own poisons on him.

<<1>> knows there's a contract on him. He's locked himself in his house and filled it with guards.\n\nYou'll find him hiding in the basement, but you'll need a key to enter. I'd search his house for the key.
<<1>> likes to poison kittens. It would be poetic justice to use his own poisons on him.
<<1>> values his life. He's surrounded himself with guards and hides behind lock and key.\n\nYou'll need a key to enter the basement of his house. I'd search his house for the key.

If you want to get <<1>> by himself you may need to create a distraction.\n\nExtinguishing a torch will draw a guard from his path and releasing a rat or throwing flashpowder into a fire will distract multiple guards.
Sure I know <<1>>. That bum owes me money.\n\nLast I heard he was on a scouting mission in the countryside.
Watch out for <<1>>. He always keeps close to his wolves.
Sure I know <<1>>. That bum owes me money.\n\nLast I heard he was on a scouting mission in the countryside.
Watch out for <<1>>. He always keeps close to her wolves.
Sure I know <<1>>. That bum owes me money.\n\nLast I heard he was on a scouting mission in the countryside.
Watch out for <<1>>. Ke keeps his wolves close at hand.
Sure, if you got some Alto Wine. I need to get my nerve up.
A canny one. We dare not question your honor when it fills you to the brim!\n\nIt's true, we need no crown to be king. But how can we rule with our subjects in perilous danger?
<<1>> is an Ayleid ruin. \n\nWe knew it protected a well of great magical power, but we never knew how to unlock it, not until the Dominion started poking around for the keystones.
That'll do. Urp!
These are the last of the Maulborn—the dregs of Daedric cultists called in from across Morrowind. Vox won't find any more reinforcements.\n\nSo, yes, it matters. Take out as many as you can.
You'll have to do something about the chieftain first. He won't let me out of his sight!
<The staff was organically formed, not carved.>\n\n<It was evidently shaped by magic, nature, or some other unnamed force.>
They're large, overgrown plants. When threatened, their spiny tentacles grab at you and pull you in.\n\nEven experienced scavengers can get caught by them if they aren't careful.

I am Jofnir Iceblade. Former master of the Fighters Guild. Don't interrupt, I cannot speak long. Doshia has taken Merric beneath the island, into the vault. She drains his soul for her master's dark plans.

Ayleids. They left the river's path a long, long time ago. They trucked with Daedric Princes all the time, unlike the godless Dwarves.\n\nDry scales, comrade. Say what you will about them. Ayleids recognized true power.

<Most of these pages are too charred to read, but the rest reveal day-to-day snippets of a peaceful hamlet untouched by war or tragedy.>\n\n<Though diverse hands penned this book, the most recent entries were written by <<1>>.>
<This key obviously unlocks something large, judging from its size.>\n\n<Several of the Argonian huts scattered throughout the village have heavy doors. This key probably works with one of them.>
You wish to atone for your looting? Good.\n\nThis existence is unnatural for us. Our spirits must return to the Hist. Take what you've pilfered to my hut. I'll meet you there.
With cleverness! Swap that bottle out when he's not looking. \n\nHe probably can't tell the difference between good wine and swill.
We're dungeon delvers—intrepid explorers, just like you.\n\nKireth handles the manual labor, while I … well, I'm the genius. Together, we make a good team.

We may be young, but we have a great many talents at our disposal.\n\nIf you must know, this is our first real expedition. We need to find something to prove our worth to the Academy. Then the Arch-Mage will have to accept our applications!

The Academy of Shad Astula, of course. \n\nMy sister and I, we don't come from a wealthy family. We need to find something of magical or historical significance to impress the Arch-Mage so he'll let us study there.

Something old, something powerful. Something that will impress even the jaded Arch-Mage of the Academy.\n\nAll of the greatest Dunmer leaders attended the Academy, and it would be unfair to the world to deny me my place among them.
Yes, you heard right. Screaming. In the crypts below.\n\nListen—I have somewhere to be—don't think I'll see you there. But perhaps later.
They killed us! How else? They demanded the Hist tree's sap, as though it was ours to give.\n\nThis existence is an abomination. We must do something. More specifically, I need you to do something.
I have a little power left. You have the staff piece. Together they become a tool.\n\nSubdue spirits by force. Then use the staff to absorb their energy. We'll meet at the tree for the next step.
Xuth, I don't know! Some kind of Dominion sorcery.\n\nOur enemies look like us. They've killed a lot of innocents with this scheme.
I'm glad you're here, since you were instrumental in bringing their actions in <<1>> to light.

A scout reported a large Dominion force in the area, so we moved down here to counter it. Then we started hearing rumors: people who weren't themselves, fathers attacking sons.\n\nIt didn't make any sense … at least, not until you showed up.
A giant spider? I knew it!\n\nCan I see what else you found?
I'm wounded, curse it, but I'll try to answer any questions you have.

Sadal is the second, greater Brother of Strife. We put Balreth back into his cage at Ash Mountain, but his ancient fiery brother still lurks in the heart of the Tormented Spire.\n\nWe can't allow Tanval to let that monster out.

Garyn is why. He was Tanval's only child. For all the medals and honors he received during the war, I think raising Garyn gave him the most pride.\n\nLosing Garyn to the Covenant broke Tanval … I think he's snapped.
Another one of these cursed Morrowind volcanos. Like Ash Mountain, they made the spire into a mystic prison to hold a Brother of Strife. \n\nIt's south of Virak, just beyond the town of Kragenmoor.
This could be just what we need. \n\nI bet this gets me and Raynor into the Academy.

It's a bastion of House Dres, and their grandmaster is the only one with access to the mountain. The spire has a mystic veil that stops anyone from wandering to the top.\n\nTo get to the spire, we'll have to deal with the Dres.

Some kind of elaborate Dwarven device. Obviously.\n\nSee the crystal prisms set up around the chamber? This emitter fires a beam that reflects off the prisms and then does … something! Oh, this is so exciting!
Me? Why I'm … an amateur archaeologist. Yes. Yes, I'm an archaeologist!\n\nI came here looking for artifacts and such.
No, I'll be fine. You go do whatever it is you do. And do it somewhere else.\n\nI'll just keep looking for artifacts. They're for my collection.
Oh, something small. Something shapely. Something I can take back to town with me. I'll keep it next to my be ….\n\nI'll keep it in my collection.
On the slope of the volcano to the southeast.
I couldn't even begin to guess.\n\nTribunal priests like to think they're wise. Why not ask one? There's an acolyte serving the housemen in Kragenmoor, southwest of here.
My people find them in the wastes from time to time. Sometimes, a gullible outlander or houseman will assume they're art. No offense.\n\nThey might even give us gold for one.

Saints bless you! But we have an even bigger problem. \n\nIn all the chaos, we just discovered that the Saint's holy skull is missing. One of my priests saw a daedroth carry it off. We must recover it!
Acolyte Hlen's on the trail of the daedroth that took it. I saw him follow the thing toward the western crypts. \n\nNow please hurry before that beast damages our holy relic!

Um, yeah. Fact is, I kind of lied to you.  \n\nThose merchants owed me weeks of back pay, and now they're dead. My family will starve without that money. Those trinkets you recovered may not seem like much, but they'll feed my family for a year.
I couldn't risk it. I'm sorry I misled you, but I can't let my children go hungry.
Return them to the spoiled children of wealthy merchants? Why should I? They won't miss a few trinkets!
An ally. For now. My goal is to find the source of this so-called Llodos plague.\n\nAnd that's all I can tell you.
Woof!
Woof!
Woof!
I'd be honored to help in any way I can, friend. What do you need?
We have so little after the destruction. Nothing that could match the uniqueness of this object.
That's a dried animal heart! Is that from a goat? I don't ….\n\nI'm … um … humbled by your gift, friend. We shall put it in a place of honor and reverence once the temple is rebuilt.
I did as you said. And the families were so grateful! They even offered me a job as a caravan guard. \n\nMy family won't go hungry again.
I made some gold off that loot you salvaged. My family is eating right for the first time in a long time. Really, I can't thank you enough.
Well, here. Take this loaf of bread. \n\nIt isn't much, but it's the only Muth Gnaar loaf to survive our flight from the temple.

About time he found someone to help. I'm glad you're here!\n\nWe've traveled all over Black Marsh searching for ancient Argonian relics. We finally get a solid lead, only to find pirates ahead of us with a treasure map.

Good! <<1>> and I need help. The pirates found three Argonian puzzle stones. Together, those stones can unlock the entrance to these ruins.\n\nWe think a priceless piece of Argonian history lies inside. We want it.
Ugh! Ghastly-looking thing. Where did you find this?
Why does that sound familiar? Ah! Of course. This must be one of the artifacts Haldyn described.\n\nIt's more hideous than I expected.
He came through town not long ago, gathering supplies. He was going to search the ruins on the plateau to the north. \n\nI warned him those ruins were ill-fated, but he ignored me.
Yes, he was definitely looking for it … or something like it. I gather he knows something about its past. \n\nThe fellow's name was Haldyn Omavel.
It's her! I mean … you found one! Amazing!
That can wait. Give me that! \n\nThank you! I have to try it now. I'll get your payment out of my pack as soon as we're done here.
Oh. Don't you know? No, you wouldn't know.\n\nThank you, friend. You've earned a substantial reward for this.

Many died fighting the Daedra who now defile the shrine. Those who remain seek to gather the pieces of my reliquary.\n\nSpeak to Priest Dilyne, who is best favored of my servants. I know she still lives.
Once, a thousand seasons ago. Less? More? I have lost track of time.\n\nHow I long to sink into the soil, unremembered and unremembering.
Yes. I remember. My only hatchling ….\n\nI died atop a tower, thinking only of him. But I will never join him, not now.

With the portals closed, we'll be able to get rid of the remaining Daedra. Most will vanish when their conjuration runs out, anyway.\n\nDon't worry about us. Go to Eidolon's Hollow and deal with Vox once and for all.
East of here. Just follow the lake shore. And watch out for any remaining Daedra.
I would if I could! \n\nThe relics here date from before my people stopped building xanmeers and started living in mud huts. We know they're an important link to my people's past.

I don't know as much as <<1>>, but just look at these ruins! Xanmeers, the Argonians call them. \n\nThe lizards' ruins go way back, and this one's old, real old. Anything from that time must be valuable … I mean, significant.

Maybe not. This "map" is a stone puzzle in three pieces. When you find one piece, it finds the next. The pirates don't know what they've got, but my partner, <<1>>, does.\n\nGet those pieces to us at the xanmeer, and we're in. And you'll get a cut.

Maybe not. The pirates don't know how to assemble the puzzle, but I do. Find one piece, and its magic will find the next.\n\nGet the puzzle stones from the pirates and bring them to us at the xanmeer. We'll unlock their mysteries together.
If the Divines will it. The worms caught us off guard, but we made them pay in blood. Did Colors brief you on our contract? What we seek?
As you say. There won't be an anchor here anytime soon, thanks to the two of us. I should be moving. We had word of another cell north of here, near Aldcroft.
The Hist led us here. Maybe the stones sought me out because I know how to use them.\n\nGive them to me. I can make them work, I know it. The relics must be nearby.
I found you ransacking my camp and insulting my wife. Now you talk to me about trust?\n\nYou mock me, and I will not have it.

A blight upon the land. In the hands of my ancestors, the Fangs could be used to destroy whole villages. They turned crops to ash and created undead horrors out of my peoples' enemies.\n\nBut that's not the worst of it.

Just as I thought. Combined, the stones become a single object: a Hist key! \n\n<<1>> found what looks like an entrance into the ruins below, but it's magically sealed. I think this will open the door.

I think so, at least for the moment. But we're worried there are other survivors still outside. \n\nThere's a temple on the hill overlooking the town. We're hoping that others have found sanctuary there.
Yes. I saw how you handle yourself. I know you can make it.
We're no match for ghosts. I barely survived skirting the edge of town. None of us would make it there.
Sure I know <<1>>. That bum owes me money.\n\nLast I heard she was near the well in town.
Sure I know <<1>>. That bum owes me money.\n\nLast I heard she was near the well in town.
Sure I know <<1>>. That bum owes me money.\n\nLast I heard she was near the well in town.
Watch out for <<1>>. She always keeps close to her body guard, <<2>>. You'll need to deal with both of them.
Watch out for <<1>>. She always keeps close to her body guard, <<2>>. You'll need to deal with both of them.
Watch out for <<1>>. She always keeps close to her body guard, <<2>>. You'll need to deal with both of them.
I won't go without a fight!
Perfect! You go hide. I'll count to 10, then come looking for you!

I asked Nelvan and Marolos to gather plants. They might have some, but it wouldn't surprise me if they just ignored me. The workers don't like me very much.\n\nOtherwise, check the area. Redweed grows near the rocks. Aloe should be out in the open.
But no! The books! Lost … knowledge lost. The Golden Eye … displeased. I must ….\n\nI must go. You're right. Knowledge can be rediscovered.
So not every spirit in Selfora is filled with hate? Then I am thankful to it that my mother and brother are still alive.
Maybe he went to the town hall. It's usually locked. Here, take this key. \n\nPlease, he might be hiding there. He might be injured!
My father, Tidyn Arthalen. No one has seen him since the catastrophe struck. Was he at the temple?
But the screaming fire! In their eyes, in their mouths, everywhere!\n\nThe Master of the Oghma opened my eyes to their souls … showed me how they burn inside.
Think so? Come on. No one's that eager to get humiliated.\n\nDo you have any idea who you're dealing with?
All right, loudmouth. Let's see what you're made of.
What? You're joking, right? That's a joke!
Hold on! Wait!\n\nTake the damned thing. It's not worth fighting over. I'll … I'll enroll again next season.
You're trying to goad me into a fight? Me?\n\nThat's hilarious! Do you know how many of my father's advisors I've sent to the healers after they dared to question me?
Fun? For me, yes. For you, not so much.\n\nGet ready to lose, loser.
You know what, why don't I just give you my invitation? No sense fighting over this silly thing.\n\nI'll just have my family get me another one.
I killed something once, but it was an accident.\n\nWait, why are you bringing this up? Academy students just spar. They never fight to the death.
Going to attend some fancy Academy of Magic.\n\nMy family's never had any magicka, but I … I have the gift. I never wanted it. I never asked for it.

You're right. I would just fail horribly at this spellcasting stuff, and I miss my friends already.\n\nI'll tell my father I figured out how to control it, and I'll never use magic again. Here, you can have my invitation.

Father wasn't sure what to do with me. When the invitation arrived, he seemed eager to send me on my way.\n\nI've never been this far from Lower Yorgrim before. I don't know if I really want to go to Shad Astula.
I've been better, my friend. Tanval and I have been shield brothers since the war, but Kyne save me, I might have to kill him to stop him.\n\nI don't want to think about it.
It's on the other side of the bridge. There's a staircase to the south of here, but I can't tell you if the path is safe or not.
You know why, my friend. The death of my son, Garyn. I couldn't bear it.\n\nVivec knows, when I was younger, I had trouble with my anger. It still plagues me.
Yes, I should have known. The destruction near Davon's Watch, my dishonorable orders to the Vanguard, my shame at Fort Virak … I will never be able to atone. \n\nI'm sorry, my friend.

Beat him to the Fangs! But it won't be easy. The ruins are full of traps and guardians, and Barvyn has a tremendous advantage. The Hist key will let him bypass most of these dangers.\n\nI'm afraid I can't go with you. I'm not strong enough.
I think so, but it's magically sealed. My tools are useless.\n\nWhatever's in there must be really valuable. It must be significant.
"A cult"? I'm no cultist, blind one. I'm a scholar. I follow the path of Hermaeus Mora. \n\nThese foul invaders are the cultists: servants of the Dark One, Mehrunes Dagon.
I see the truth, but your eyes are closed to the light. \n\nThe Golden Eye looks out through my own. I see things as they really are.
Interesting, interesting. Ragnthar is a Dwarven ruin. Why would he …? We must travel there, comrade. See if we can uncover more.

Sure, of course. Had me set out some supplies for him a few times. He said he was going out to Ragnthar, that weird old Dwemer ruin. I kept telling him the Mages had already emptied it out, but he kept telling me he needed to go.

Oh, studying it and such. Ragnthar is … weird. Unique, I guess you'd say. See, nobody really knows where it is. Physically, that is. It has an entrance near here, right? But the Mages say stepping through the door is some kind of … uhh.

He said he was meeting someone. That he had to meet with them somewhere safe. That what they were talking about was very important. Guess that's why Jofnir went to the trouble of going to that weird old place.
<Little of the body remains. It's clear from the size that this was once a Nord. Settled within the rib cage, you catch a glimpse of a guild insignia.>
You have seen the spirit of Jofnir, but always just for a moment. This one believes we can summon him. Speak to him. \n\nLearn who murdered him.
Aelif told you, she has power. Magical gifts, connections to the lands beyond. She will use them to draw the spirit to this place.\n\nThen we shall see, yes? We begin.
Perhaps for you. This one has suspected all along. \n\nThe lizard was the one to become Guildmaster. The lizard was the one who set us on this crusade. Aelif smelled something foul on the wind.
You persist! Very well. We used three Focus Stones in our binding ritual. Obtain the Focus Stone of Flame from the southern rim of the caldera.\n\nMind the lava. You look quite flammable.
For that, you should talk to Noyei-Heem. It was his misfortune to be a slave here. \n\nHe went into the village.

All of us waiting for the boat have invitations, but I doubt you'll find anyone willing to hand one over to you. \n\nIt's a big honor to be invited. Anyone willing to toss that away isn't really Academy material.
Seek out the spirit of Levissii Gilvayn. She was with us during the binding of Sadal.\n\nShe waits for you now on the stairs above the caldera.

I fear I don't know for certain. So many things I don't know.\n\nYou'll have to test it. See if the water will work on the magic fire within the Chamber of the Tree. Look for a brazier of unnatural flame.
There's something you must see.
It's not that simple. Candidates are carefully selected after months of observation. \n\nUnless, of course, they pre-qualify by wealth or birth.
There, you see? You've pre-qualified by wealth. This invitation has your name on it.\n\nOr it will, once you add it.
Yes, yes, you're something special. Come aboard and prepare yourself to enter a realm of wondrous magic and magical wonders.\n\nNow sit down and hold on, Your Majesty.
You got it, Your Majesty.
<<1>>? His brothers put you up to this? Well, he's not here. He's in the mine with more valuable, productive employees. \n\nNow excuse me, I've got a labor problem to deal with.
The Ordinators are still conducting their own investigation. Feel free to examine the area yourself.\n\nNow, please. Leave me to my grief.
Woof
Ruh-roh!
Roh-kay!
Ruh-roh!
Woof!!!
Woof! Bark! Woof!
Whine ,,, whine … woof!

More of the same, Plenty of drinking, Valen singing his song, Hectur bashing him for it, Suron picking fights with just any Nord who comes here. I don't know what it is about those guys and Nords, but when they get smashed, they really get smashed!

It seems nice enough, but certainly is rough. Most of these people are nice, come here to have fun, but the stinky drunks, like Suron or Valen, the ones stinking of Alto Wine, seem to like getting into trouble.

I don't know much, but I've heard they're up to some nasty business. You can't even get on their boat without a uniform, so who can tell what's really going on? The Pact is desperate for people, so I guess they've lowered their standards.

It was a gift from our master, Hermaeus Mora. Placed upon the brow of one dead or dying, it drains memories.\n\nWe use it to record the lore of the faithful. You will use it to take knowledge from the mind of the enemy.
Only to the ignorant, the crude, and the stupid.\n\nAnd you are none of these, are you? Then you have nothing to fear.
He is known by many names. The Dark Elves know him as the Golden Eye.\n\nTo him, knowledge and memory are the only treasures of value. He gathers all words and all thoughts in the realm of Apocrypha.
None, in fact. The hatching has begun.\n\nYou must defend our Hist from these invaders. I've done nothing but rebuff you, but those hatchlings deserve a chance at life.
It's not up to me. The eggs call, and we attend. It's the worst possible time, but we can't stop it.\n\nWhen the ritual is over, I'll send my assistants to help. That's all I can do.
My notes … that key. I figured out what's buried under the xanmeer, and it must stay buried.\n\n<<1>> went in? We have to warn him.
Oh, no. We need to leave them sealed in the xanmeer, for all our sakes.\n\nWe have to stop <<1>> before he gets to the Fangs of Sithis.
Ah, yes. The Arch-Mage asked me to expect you. He's been waiting for you to arrive.
No need to be worried. The Arch-Mage has visions about people all the time. It's one of his many, many gifts.\n\nPlease, report to Arch-Mage Valeyn right away.

My pleasure! The Academy trains promising magic-users to become great scholars, charismatic leaders, and mighty heroes.\n\nIt's sponsored by the Great Houses, and this is the first season that we're accepting candidates from all Pact nations.
What a silly question. Of course not!\n\nThe Mages Guild has too many ties to the enemy alliances. The Academy is strictly a training ground for future leaders of the Ebonheart Pact.
Some days I wish I'd never crawled out of my egg. I came to Stonefalls to be a guar herder. Shalks ate them.\n\nWent to Davon's Watch to be a bartender. Bunch of Nords kicked me down the street.
That's not even the worst of it. Came west to try my hand at mining. It started off well enough. Got some equipment, even talked a few of the locals into helping.\n\nThen the volcano erupts.

Yeah. It turns out my planned dig site was a Daedric ruin. Complete with screaming and chanting. Frothing monsters inside.\n\nThis pales in comparison to that time I spilled some brandy on a Hist root.
Huh? Oh, right, right. Mind where the river carries you, traveler. Can't trust the Daedra.

Then there was the time I bought a cheap dagger from this pawn broker in Ebonheart. I wore it on my belt and these cultists started chasing me, yelling, "The Razor! The Razor!"\n\nI threw it in the river and kept running.
Do not doubt what was meant to be. Powers beyond our comprehension set things in motion and all we can do is take the ride. I saw you in my visions. You have come to protect the Academy.
Touch the vision orb behind me. Watch the pattern play out.\n\nSimply repeat the order by touching each of the spheres. If you make a mistake, you may start over.
I thought so. And here we stand like stupid milk drinkers, waiting for them. \n\nNothing for it. We'll just have to kill them all. You ready?
You did? Is she okay? We got into an argument and she stormed out. She said she was 'leaving forever', which has happened before.
They're tied closely to the history of my people, for good or ill. The mountains of the Ashlands are rife with old Daedric ruins.\n\nSome are not as forgotten as we might like.
Perhaps having it back will calm her down. I threw it out into the fields to the south - you might be able to find it there.\n\nIt's possible a kagouti ate it, they do enjoy sparkly things.
Oh, yes. Orana can be a little melodramatic sometimes, but I worry I might have gone a bit too far.\n\nI was angry, you see, and I threw her amulet out into the night.
I've learned not to dismiss rumor and legend out of hand.\n\nWhether there's an actual library or just a fiery pit of screaming Daedra, I couldn't say.
They dot the slopes of Ash Mountain. Legends tell of a secret Daedric library there, devoted to the Daedric Prince Hermaeus Mora.
Excellent. Let's begin.
Obviously. Your deductive powers are incredible.
They killed Jazadi. It fills this one with rage.\n\nRuvali will not forgive Ra-shadda, but she may yet understand him. That is the first step to peace.

He went to the stables. Tell Ulov to meet us there.\n\nRa-shadda wanted you to use the totem on some godless altar east of the pumpkin patch. Once you've found Ulov and used the totem, meet us at the stables.
Yes, he must. We agree, then. It's settled.

The cat went to the stables; tell Ulov to meet us there.\n\nRa-shadda wanted you to use the totem on some godless altar east of the pumpkin patch. Once you've found Ulov and used the totem, meet us at the stables.
You believe that? But, my Tiril ….\n\nEnough. Enough death.

Ah yes, the Dark Elf. He was a diligent student, if somewhat crass. Talented, to be sure, but there was something off-putting about him.\n\nMy suspicions were confirmed when he locked Crow Mother in the tower. Of course, she got her way in the end.

You've seen it. War and disease ravage our lands. We're surrounded by enemies, yet still we tear at each other's throats.\n\nOur students will help change that. And you will keep them safe so they can fulfill their destiny.

Crow Mother is lonely. She doesn't get many visitors, and we, her children, aren't the best company. Hard to believe, but true.\n\nWe agreed that if we'd teach Rulantaril the secrets of magic, he would return to her side.

Yes. The bargain's power brought him to her side and locked him in the tower. It's just as well, really.\n\nYou want to talk to them? Rulantaril left his tower key in a ruined structure nearby. It's in a cursed chest with a fiery guardian.
Oh! You know I'd never burn anything, right? Just a figure of speech. \n\nI can't fail my initiation test. I couldn't face being sent home.
An instructor said one of these shadow clucks has a magic amulet. Ate it, probably.\n\nI'm supposed to use this wand to focus my magic on the clucks and find the amulet.
Actually, I'm afraid to find out. \n\nYou don't seem at all timid. Would you do it? Please find the amulet. I can't fail this test!

Like many born away from the Hist, <<1>> is withdrawn, but never entirely silent.\n\nShe thinks I blame her, but <<2>> has done nothing to harm him or this village. No, it's <<1>> they wanted … and together, we can find him.
It cries out through the horrors. Can you hear them, too?
I must do what I can for our future. The hatchlings struggle. Someone must care for them and teach  them the ways of the Saxhleel.\n\nThis will be my task.
You dare to threaten me from your narrow concept of right and wrong? \n\nI see. Then I'll go, no doubt to the peril of all who remain. I won't let you spill more blood under the Hist.
I am not a murderer, like them. Or like you.\n\nIt's not yours to judge. You aren't one of us. You don't know what we must sacrifice, what we must teach.
You're right. My assistant believes we can cleanse the eggs that were exposed to bloodshed. I pray she is correct.\n\nThank you. My work beckons.
My assistants and I have much to do before the next full moons.\n\nThe hatchlings have taken their first breaths through cracked shells. We must protect their emergence.
I am part of the Hist, a part you can perceive and help.\n\n<<1>> of the Dominion steals my memories and weakens my fibers, using <<2>>'s fragile new connection to reach me.
Restore our clarity. Eject Carethil from my dream.
Thank you. The Hist are in your debt.
Mercy! Please …
Don't worry about it. It was hilarious!\n\nI'll take the amulet to the instructor right away. I owe you one.
Well, if you had any ideas about getting into the storeroom or the pantry, forget it.The keys are in the <<1>>'s strongbox, and he never leaves its side.
Sure!
You'll never kill me!
This is a day of reckoning. We will bring down one of the biggest leaders in all of Stonefalls, and using <<1>> will announce our presence to the world!
I'm not helpless, you know. I can do this. \n\nArgh! Never mind. I give up. I'm not getting sent home over some stupid fish that doesn't exist. You want to help? Fine.

Well, you can either fill this pond with fish so I can actually catch one, or figure out what these orbs do.\n\nThey gave me a book, but it just contained some stupid riddle. I threw it on that table over there.
What am I, a child? I'm going to be a commander in a House army, or maybe an advisor to the Pact leaders! They should have just given me a spell I could cast.

My spell went wrong. The instructor said to round up the little ones, bring them back safe, and we'll get them fixed. \n\nBut, well, one got away and climbed on top of that big rock. Oh, Hadmar is so ashamed!
Hadmar is scared of heights! Oh, why did little rat climb so high?\n\nI crafted a totem. Makes a helper fly up to get rat. But no one wants to be Hadmar's helper.
You would be helper? Thank you!\n\nFace big rock in front of Hadmar, activate totem, then climb and grab nice little rat. But be careful. If you point the wrong way, you'll fly someplace wrong.
Oh, little rat is safe! Now Hadmar won't get beaten with rakes, like at home.\n\nGood, good, good. I'll take little friends back to get fixed up right away.
Who? You mean <<1>>? Yeah, he's a pitiful fool, he's sure to be in the gutter again soon.

Certainly he does. He was a fair wine trader, but he drinks his stock more than moving it. His family deserted him then he lost all his wares in a fire, so into the bottle he goes. He must be dealing in unsavory goods since he drinks all his wine.
I've heard <<1>>'s been trading with the Blacksails. I've even heard he's been trading in various poisons lately.

Yeah, that's him. He's been acting weird lately. Drinking lots and very jumpy around open flames. Of course, if you've seen flash powder in action, you'd know why. Once, flash powder caused a fire that burned half his wares.
The duties of the keeper fall to me. There are many sleepless nights ahead.\n\nI learned much from Uxith-Ei, but I am not like him.
<This chest remains empty.>
Truly? What happened? Were the ruins infested with undead? Stendarr's wrath would have served you in good stead.
<This chest remains empty.>
<This chest remains empty.>
I shall work the anvil. Form the core. You will keep the fire at the proper temperature. Many and many times must the fire be stoked, to keep an even flame and flow.
Well, this is the only place to get a drink near my ship, but that Suron guy gets under my skin. If he tells one more Nord joke, I'm doing to stomp his face.
I'll need to blindfold you before we leave. We trust you to go, but … \n\nWell, we need to have some secrets. Otherwise what's the point in being a ranking member? Heh.
<This chest contains <<1>>.>
<This chest contains a <<1>>.>
Shad Astula's been overrun. The last of the Maulborn, from the looks of it—they must need more soldiers. \n\nAnd they're getting them. They cast some kind of spell to enslave the students.
That's what it looks like. \n\nThat spell didn't work on us—don't know why. We carried out the Arch-Mage's orders, but then the Maulborn caught us and threw us in here with you.
I'd smile wider than a slaughterfish at your success, but I suspect <<1>>'s plans involve using <<A:2>> for an unspeakable horror.\n\nGo on, then. Speak it.
When the trouble started, he gave us some arcane items and told us to find places to hide them. Then he went off on some mission of his own. \n\nI'm glad you're awake. Can you get us out of here?
The Maulborn general himself. \n\nOne of the senior students recognized him. Said he was Darvasen—used to be the Arch-Mage's assistant!
<This chest contains a <<1>>.>
<This chest contains a <<1>>.>
<This chest contains a <<1>>.>
<This chest contains <<1>>.>
I was afraid to. There're guards out there!\n\nMaybe you could check it. Discreetly.
I have been! Every chance I get! But praying is thirsty work.\n\nI even volunteered to help the priests. I'm making up for what I did at Deepcrag, I promise!

<The sticky substance looks like a mixture of tree sap and blood. It oozes slowly from a mortal wound on his chest. His body is lukewarm.>\n\n<Scrawled inside his shirt collar are the words "Subject 17.">
I open portal and we go find big Nord. Name Hatmeer! Or Hadmead? I forget. Mortals have dumb names.\n\nNo matter. Come, come. We go now. Big Nord hides in building next to where we appear.

Hadmar isn't sure. One moment I was walking to instruction hall, next moment—boom! Hadmar knocked on backside.\n\nWoke up in here, with Arch-Mage standing over me. He said wait for you to show up. I waited, and you showed up!
Yes! He told me to set up my totem near big rock outside. Lena hid her lockbox high up on top of rock. \n\nLockbox is very important. We must find lockbox and bring it to Lena!
Just outside!\n\nYou use totem to reach the lockbox, while Hadmar stays on ground. Then we'll find Lena!

The lockbox. Right. The Arch-Mage tinkered with my wand and told me to hide it up here. \n\nThat was just before Darvasen tossed me in that cell. I still can't believe the Arch-Mage's old assistant is the Maulborn general.

You can use my wand to scorch the Scamps. And illusion dust is the residue of illusory monsters. With enough of each, we can prepare a spell to get us through to Darvasen.\n\nWe'll need Tedras, though. That spell is his specialty.

He said we'd need the wand, but he didn't say why.\n\nWait, I know! The Maulborn have occupied the library vaults and sealed the door. And what makes the best spell of unlocking? Burnt Scamp hide and illusion dust, of course!
You heard correctly. If I had the right ingredients, that is. But getting them will be tricky, considering the Maulborn occupy the Academy.

Illusion dust and burnt Scamp hide. Perfect! Just give me a moment and … there we go! \n\nI'll wait up here. You know, to keep your escape route clear. Now go find the Arch-Mage and put an end to that Darvasen.
Last I heard he <<1>> was on his ship in Davon's Watch but you'll need to disguise yourself to get on the boat.\n\nPerhaps one of the sailors at the bar has an outfit you can steal.

I've heard word that <<1>> docked his ship in Davon's Watch a few days ago.\n\nYou'll need to disguise yourself to get on the boat. If you can cause a commotion, you can steal an outfit from one of the sailors at the bar on the docks.
You'll find <<1>> aboard his ship in Davon's Watch, but you won't be able to board the boat without a disguise.\n\nPerhaps one of the sailors at the bar on the docks has an outfit you can steal.
I've heard that they carry poison on the ship to keep the rats under control. You could add some poison to the captain's food.
Watch out for <<1>>. He always keeps close to his bodyguard.\n\nIf you want to get to him, you should time it so his bodyguard isn't around.
The ship has a rat problem. If you release a rat aboard the ship you can use it to cause a distraction.
Here we go. Try to keep up, yes?
She's just too jumpy. They say the Akaviri War made her twitchy. She's easily startled by the strangest things. \n\nLike lizards. Those lizards infesting the Argonian quarter drive her crazy.

Ragnthar is twisted out of space. This entrance here will allow us in. But it is not really here. If that makes sense? Lucky for us, Aelif came prepared. She can bring the door into focus. Let us inside.
The Dominion retreated into the ruins after the lamias tore them apart. If we strike while they're bloody, we can pay them back for <<1>>!

Then we must learn where the crocodile rests its head so we can crush it in one blow. \n\nI shouldn't ask, but after <<1>> I must. If we knew <<2>>'s movements, we could end this abruptly. Would you do us the honor of finding the crocodile's lair?
Then let's get going, comrade!
Excellent. Any questions before we go?

Then … when Doshia took me prisoner, she was to harvest my soul for this abomination? By all the Eight! \n\nWe should be moving. Aelif will await us here, keep watch for any unfriendly faces. Come, follow me. And try to keep up.
Comrade … did you say try? The Vivicus is not some long-destroyed legend?
This equipment is very old and very delicate. Stendarr willing, we must try to get it right the first time.\n\nHere are the fire salts. Let's begin.
Use the bellows, here, to stoke the flame just a bit. Use the valve to my other side to stoke it yet more. And for a truly fearsome blaze, pour fire salts on the coals.
The lever, just next to the valve, releases pressure from the forge. But do not worry, I'm certain you'll do fine. Are you ready to begin?
We are well on our way. I can feel it. We'll have to tinker with it to see wha-\n\nStendarr's grace, what's that noise?

You shattered the Jagged Lens and broke the spell. The few Maulborn who were left were totally outnumbered, and they ran for it.\n\nThe Arch-Mage had us bring you up here. I've been watching over you. You know, as a friend.

Safe as gorapple pie. Thanks to you.\n\nAnd you—you weren't even supposed to be here. I heard how you got your invitation. And now we're all alive because you broke the rules. I'll have to think about that.
Don't give me that look! I was worried about you, that's all.\n\nOh, and before I forget, the Arch-Mage wants to speak to you. He's right outside.

Yes, though we lost a few students and instructors in the fight. \n\nThe fact that the lens was buried below the library vaults was one of our greatest secrets. Darvasen used that knowledge to aid the Maulborn.

Quite so. They're running out of loyal troops. When Darvasen told them about the lens, they saw it as the solution to all their problems. \n\nIf Darvasen could turn our students into soldier-slaves, the Maulborn would be back in business.
For you, here, yes. But I don't need a vision to know that you still have unfinished business out there.\n\nAnyway, I'd like to thank you. And there's one more thing.

Too many voices. All of them very important, used to being heard. They want this mystery solved and they want it solved now. They are used to combat, direct action. All this thinking hurts their heads.

Questions, not blades? Yes! Merciful Pact-soldier takes pity on Kazdi!\n\n<<1>> took his big glowing egg behind that door and sealed it up. He's like a spider wearing a sash: "Treat with respect, salute often!" But Kazdi knows … still a spider.

Heh, Aelif would have hoped you'd notice by now. This one loves to fight. Loves the thrill of combat. But a thorny puzzle, a tricky lock, a track to follow in the woods? Just as much fun as a blade in a brawl.
You may attempt again. Remember, unnecessary distraction leads to failure.
I see. Try to do better. Remember, distraction can lead to failure.
I wonder if it would work on the big spiders.
Look around! I had a quick peek at the machinery in here while I was waiting for you. \n\nI think this entire chamber is some sort of complex Dwarven device.

The Dominion clearly targeted <<1>>. As his spirit reunited with the Hist, it was open to suggestion. Weak. And now, it's lost.\n\nI need freshly picked <<2>> to track his spirit. It grows within our mushroom cave.
Then quiet them. Slay them.
That was Molag Bal himself. Did you hear his voice? Made my blood run cold. That such an evil thing could be right here, in our midst ….
Really? Sorry about that. I'm still refining the design. \n\nI hope the other one I made holds up. That f'lah from House Dres paid a lot of gold for it.
I'm sorry, comrade. I knew Jofnir a long time. You're right, we need to report in. So much has happened.
Well, how else could I get it tested? Be reasonable.

He was born to slaves in Vvardenfell. And yes, he's Argonian, but he's different. Distant. Haunted. Listens to words more than meaning. But he's my husband, and I love him.\n\nThe tree-minder lured him here.
Yes, though I didn't catch all of it. Crystal shackles? Buckles? I'm not sure.

The tree-minder says Argonians born away from the Hist are damaged, but they can be healed by some sort of ritual to join them with a Hist.\n\nI don't know. I don't want them to change <<1>>. And why does the Dominion want him … or the others?
I think … I'll let Aelif lead the way this time. Come.
What has happened, comrade? I do not like the look on your face. Or the scowl Merric bears.
Hsssk! The God of Schemes himself has taken notice of our quest. We're all in murky water now, comrade. And the current grows swift.
That's about what I figured. Run along, pup. Go hide.\n\nI'll handle this. If the monster catches you … well, I'll have to kill a copy of your corpse.

Yes. He actually visited a few times in the months before he died. Always came into town dirty and smelling like boots after a hard march. Never asked why. Didn't seem like a thing he was likely to tell me.

Sure, I remember him here! But not his business. I think he spoke with Akhita a few times. Wish he was still around. Be interested to hear what he thinks of this contract. Knowing the council's all torn up about it ….

Oh, you know. The Guild has always been about our short, simple contracts. "One and done" was the mantra a lot of the lads used. Now this long-term thing, with the anchors? The coin's good, but it's a big change. Not everyone likes it. That's all.
In her travels, Aelif has learned little tricks and techniques. She has fought mages, Daedra, the undead. Even werewolves. You don't hunt monsters as long as she has without learning a thing or two.
Why recoil so? Am I truly so hideous? Would you spurn me, as Rulantaril did years ago?
Thank you. He's raging in the corridors below us, trying to blast his way out with magic … the magic we taught him.\n\nPlease, don't kill him. I don't want to be alone.
Then you're as cruel as Rulantaril. Shadow take you, mortal. \n\nOr perhaps you'd like to take his place at my side? Find me below … if you dare.
No! I won't let you hurt him. I'll protect him.\n\nRulantaril, my love! They come for us.
Do you, now? Very well, intruder. Tell me.
How would Aelif know? She was behind you.
Oh yes, Colors, the heroic Guildmaster. Pff. We don't need to wait for Colors. You and Aelif are more than smart enough to figure this out. Here, give those items you found on the cultists.
Dourstone Vault. An old Imperial tower, on an island off the coast. Go, seek Merric there. Aelif will find our heroic Guildmaster and get additional blades.

You didn't recognize the Dremora from her projection? I think her name is Doshia. Quite full of herself, actually. \n\nHmm. This note mentions an "island tower." Aelif wonders if it speaks of Dourstone.

Are you asking if we're comfortable? None of us are comfortable outside Black Marsh. Too dry, too open, too bright.\n\nStill, at the moment we are treated well, and the Hist Tree will soon be cleansed.
Before I was here, I cared about the rain only when it fell on my tribe. Now I must worry about Stonefalls and this Pact.\n\nThe reeds can bend to the wind, but I must not.

I spent much of my childhood here, living with my mother's family. \n\nSome of my fondest memories are of playing with my father on the shore of the bay. I learned to fight with the troops in the square.
In the wake of Balreth's rampage? It goes well. Senie will be rebuilt, and ash from the volcano will actually help the farms, at least in the long run.\n\nIt's been hard, but Daen Seeth will prosper.
We're holding them. In some places, we're barely holding on, but we're holding them.\n\nBut I wish I hadn't invoked the Brother of Strife.
I do. I wish I hadn't been needed here. I should have aided the effort at Ash Mountain. \n\nThe Brothers depend on old magic from another time. They have no place in Stonefalls today.
Kyne blessed us with a victory at Ash Mountain, but we're still fighting those milk-drinking Covenant bastards. West of us, they've locked horns with Vivec's Antlers.\n\nAnd I've heard rumors.

A scout from the northwest border made it to the city, bloody and bruised. He said a force was marching on Fort Virak. If they take Virak, they're on the doorstep of Riften, up in Skyrim.\n\nThose Dagger bastards! To Sovngarde with the lot of them.
I am, though I wish I wasn't. What a monster!\n\nBut it's got the Sacred Cranium, I'm sure of it. It stalked off this way and I sneaked after it.
It went into the crypt. You can probably follow it just by its odor—it smells like a hot forge.\n\nAre you going after it? Because I'm not. That thing breathes fire.
It's not operational without miners, if you catch my meaning.\n\nWhat do you really want?
Thank you. Your efforts have lifted the morale of the priests and acolytes, giving us all hope. We are in your debt.
<The pilgrims' bodies are still warm. They died very recently.>
