<You find another dead pilgrim. Her throat was cleanly cut with a blade, and from the damage to her body she clearly fell from the nearby cliff. Like the others, her body is still warm.>
I don't need an all-out war, not until the vicecanons send help. The fewer dead, the fewer angry Goblins. \n\nAnd with that totem, I'll have some bargaining power.

Their camp's above the mine. We employed a few of them, but otherwise we left each other alone. I don't know why they'd be upset at us. \n\nMaybe they decided we looked funny. Or maybe they wanted my favorite dress. Either way, it has to stop.
Take some more. It's not like slop is expensive.
Fine, have some more, but don't waste them. We've only got so much to throw around.
I am not a traditional Argonian. My egg-sister says that my part of the nest was kept too dry. \n\nPerhaps that is why I yearn to immerse myself in the River of Humor.

Rumors say the performance required precision. Performing it incorrectly was punishable by death. A mysterious order protected the rite, murdering anyone who performed it without care.\n\nOf course, I'm sure those are just rumors.
Yes sir!
Very well. The first part of the performance goes like this: \n\n"One day, in full view of the n'wah, the mehra of Koal Canton …."
Yes sir!
Performance of the sacred rite requires exact preparation. True humor must be taken seriously, so an improper performance demands death. \n\nThose who fail find themselves facedown in the hackle-lo.
Well, have a snifter of greef then, muthsera s'wit. Just know that Kragenmoor is the ancient home of the Mirthless Order.\n\nIf your friend performs the rite improperly, he will be slain.
Arf! Arf!
Woof!
Woof!
arf arf
Well, if you had any ideas about getting into the storeroom or the pantry, forget it.The keys are in the <<1>>'s strongbox, and he never leaves its side.
This is a day of reckoning. We will bring down one of the biggest leaders in all of Stonefalls, and using <<1>> will announce our presence to the world!
My damn laundry. Not that it's any of your business. My captain likes to see clean uniforms on deck.
Tense? Tense? You hear that drunk elf prattling on? Nords this. Nords that. I'm two pints away from cramming my fist down his throat.
I was. Now I am but a remnant of my former glory. \n\nMagistrix Vox shattered my reliquary and reduced me to my current state. You need my blessing to defeat her, but as I am now I cannot bestow it.

Many of my priests died fighting the Daedra who now defile the shrine. Those who remain seek to gather the pieces of my reliquary.\n\nSpeak to Priest Dilyne, who is best favored of my servants. I know she still lives.
Restore my reliquary. \n\nFind the pieces, scattered about the shrine, and bring them to Master Aron at the central dais. When I am made whole, I can help you prevail against Vox.
Interesting. Why was my father here? And who is this witch he mentioned?
I stabilized the portal, but it's not going to stay that way. I need to attend to it.\n\nWould you go to the court my father mentioned? Maybe someone there knows of his fate.
There are two tolls you can pay: the toll of flesh or the toll of silver. Choose!
The toll of flesh commits you to fight our enemies, the wretched bats of this wood.\n\nEach time you kill a bat, we'll descend to feast upon the bat's tender bits.

The toll of silver! Search the dark caves and the farthest corners of the woods. Collect trinkets of shiny silver left by those who fell to the wolves. \n\nGlitter and glister! Such trinkets please us with their luster.
Speak then, featherless one!
Then we shall feast on our foes. When you have killed four and four of the flying rats, find the Seneschal of Carrion.
Then go to the caves and bring us trinkets.\n\nThe Seneschal of Carrion awaits at the Blackfeather Court far up the road to accept your shiny, shiny tribute.

The Tribunal has long held it in their care. Mad and reckless, Vox stole it from their Temple.\n\nNow I am fading and my connection to this plane becomes more tenuous. If you would restore my reliquary, delay no longer.

The General ordered me to stay out of his quarters on the lower level. He's never done that before and I want to know what he's hiding. \n\nHe's posted a guard, but if you can get past him and search the room, maybe you can find out what's going on.
Quickly, tell me of the sacred performance. Moisten my scales.

The court is fat and happy. The bats are dead, and we have fed. Eyes and wings and skin and ears. Such tender bits!\n\nWe are pleased with your tribute, featherless. The duke wishes to speak with you.

Such glitter and gleam! Such twinkle and shine! We thank you for your tribute, featherless.\n\nOur duke will want to speak with you. Go! Present yourself to the duke for your reward while I add these glitteries to our hoard.
Just take out those watchers near the portals. If you don't kill them close to the portals they guard, another one of the creatures pops up to take its place. Blasted Vox.
Questions? We charge you a toll, yet you want to talk instead of pecking us?\n\nMiraculous! Speak!

I thank you, as should all Argonians. It would have been better had the Fangs been left buried, but now they've been unearthed, we must keep them safe.\n\nSo far, you're the only person unaffected by them.

What? What? We are crows. Do crows not hold court where you come from? Do they not cluster, conspiring and plotting and politicking?\n\nWatch them more closely, more carefully. Pay attention next time!
A crow must leave the nest and fly. Crow Mother has left us dominion over the wood, and our war with bats and wolves keeps us busy.\n\nEnough talk, fledgling. The wood is yours to explore. Go!

Crow Mother hatched us, taught us to talk. She made me the duke, for I am the smartest and biggest and loudest.\n\nBut then she forgot us. I think she was tired of our cawing and wanting. Want, want, want. We want.
I'm not sure. It worries me, but not as much as the Fangs in the wrong hands.\n\nHere, take the first Fang while I consider what we should do with them.
What I hope to accomplish is difficult. Perhaps impossible. It will require great strength of spirit! \n\nI sense this strength in you. That is what drew us together in the ruins.
A storm rages towards us, Adept. War has come to Tamriel, and the Mages of this great guild must have quarter.\n\nI intend to offer them a safe haven. A sanctuary where they may study in peace.

I created that sanctuary, centuries ago! It was stolen from me by an agent of chaos, and magically transported to the Shivering Isles. \n\nTo recover the island we must locate four hidden tomes. This is the task of which I speak.
What are you going to do?\n\nIt's gnawing at my mind. If I give it to you, I'll go mad. I'll die!
Spellbooks? How pedestrian. \n\nAs it happens, I'm feeling particularly charitable at present. I'll allow you to enter. After.
Here, take it! There's only one, I swear. I don't know where the other Fang is.\n\nThat thing burrowed into my mind. I never want to see it again. Never.
After a test of your resolve. This isn't a lending library. If you want the spellbooks, you'll have to earn them.\n\nA portal has been opened, just behind you. Close it, and I'll grant you passage.
Shalidor! That pompous Nord and I go way back! \n\nI know what he wants, indeed I do. His island. He wants to steal it back. Oh, how I love a challenge.

Where's the sport in that? Tell you what. I'll give you one book in exchange for your heart or lungs. Your choice.\n\nNo, wait. I have a better idea! Let's have a contest. A contest, wrapped in a mystery, with an enigma glaze! Oh, what fun we'll have!
Excellent! Cheese and cabbage for everyone!\n\nBut wait! We should inform Shally-dorable of our deal. With any luck, he'll die of embarassment all over again!

A few tasks, the odd deathtrap. Nothing so difficult as, say, reassembling the Staff of Chaos or rebuilding the Numidium.\n\nTake the first book. Puppy-killer. And I'll give you an additional book for each test you pass. Are you game?
We are in words and treaties. The moot might meet in peace, but we remember what the Argonians were like when we dragged them out of the muck.\n\nWe know what they really are.
That's the calm man's choice, stranger.\n\nWithout my daughter at my side, I don't give a damn whether some scalebacks are bleeding out in the ash!
Last I saw him is he was running for the old Argonian quarters. If he's alive he's probably trapped in there.
I'll mix this. And this.\n\nThere. Now to test it. Would you take this to my assistant?
Oh, no! He's much too afraid of me. He's hiding behind the large mushrooms to the south.\n\nWe call him Not-So-Quick. Just tell him I don't want him to drink it.

He'll get better. Here, smell this. Does it smell dangerous? No, of course not! It smells great!\n\nYour turn. You'll want to be out in the open, preferably in the exact center of town. Enjoy the experience.

Really? She said that? Then my first reaction is to drink it. But she knows that's what I'll think, so I shouldn't. But I should do the opposite of that, so ….\n\nDry scales, I think I've figured her out. Give it to me.
Not sure. \n\nWhy don't you fiddle with the prisms while I think this through? Maybe you'll get lucky.
Maybe. \n\nThe prisms might be out of alignment. I think we need to direct the beam of light to a specific point. Adjust the prisms until something happens while I work on the emitter some more.
Ssk! The Reach vermin hide behind their magical shield. We must bring it down, for the Pact and glory.
Hssk. Imbue the effigies with the corrupt magicka. That should clear the way into the mine.

We're in a pocket of Oblivion. Everything you see is crafted from illusion and metaphor. \n\nEven the grass beneath your feet is just a memory of grass. Your mind is struggling to make sense of the chaos around us.

Of course, Mistress. As you know, we bards call it Skald's Retreat. The greatest talespinners in Skyrim gather here. And, of course, we have loremaster Brugar as well. Keeps a library of ancient stories and artifacts.
Nightmares. What are you talking about? I'm hiding from the Dominion army. Don't you see them encamped just ahead?
I've … I've got a performance tomorrow. The Song of Sinmur. In front of everyone. Have to be ready!
Yes, you did! You don't believe in me. I can be a great skald. Walk Skyrim and learn the songs. Just name a tune and I'll belt out a lyric.
I've spent most of my life studying Oblivion and the various methods of fighting Daedric threats. \n\nThe Tribunal is wary of Daedra, and with good reason. Nothing good ever comes from Oblivion.
Technically, the Crow's Wood is part of Evergloam, one of the realms of Oblivion. It is the realm of perpetual twilight, ruled by the Daedric Prince Nocturnal.

Huh. The general doesn't get many visitors. Or any, really. You'll find him in a shack to the southwest.\n\nA word of advice: Don't stray into the western side of the prison. Not unless you want to get eaten.
Help from Maraamur, that's a laugh. Slept through Engling's performance, dribbles mead from his mouth like a pup. How can I help you?

Because the Academy couldn't find a living person who could tolerate rowing spoiled mages-in-training back and forth all day long.\n\nPlus, I owe the Academy a debt I won't be able to repay in a hundred lifetimes. So here I am.
You stand before a Nether-Niece of the Mistress of Shadows.\n\nI am the Crow Mother, the Daedra Lord of this region of Evergloam.
That's right. Some of the prisoners went feral. Animals, that's what they've turned into!\n\nGood hunting, though.

Even kin of the Night Mistress grow lonely. The crows I created from my feathers were pleasant enough company for a while, but I tired of them.\n\nRulantaril was my first visitor. He was so kind to me.
Some think it's the keystone's influence. Using it to trap us must've had some effect.\n\nOthers think the feral were weak-minded, and broke under the strain of our situation. Who knows?
That's it, then. Now we can … wait, no. We need one more thing. We need Engling's lute. Have to have her lute.
I suppose I can give you a little more.\n\nThere! This should last nearly twice as long.
Sounds good. Watch my back, right? Keep the bad mead demons from getting me.
Thanks, stranger. I got separated from <<1>> and <<2>>. They ran to the Argonian huts, and I hid here.\n\nI hope they're all right!
I think one of those things is getting closer!
I can't stand this much longer!
I've got to get out of here. Got to find my brother!
These vines, they're so tight.
We'll sing songs of you yet, my friend! Now you just need to convince the only other person awake on the island. His name is <<1>>. And he's an idiot.
Sorry, that's not fair. He's actually a drunk. He's upstairs. Keeps squealing like a stuck skeever when I try to talk to him. I'm sure you'll be able to convince him.
I did not "lose them," fangless. They were stolen from me by Supernal Dreamers. Slay them. And keep slaying them until you find my bongos.
I am a knight, my featherless friend. "The" knight, I suppose, as I am the only one in this realm.\n\nYou will address me as "sir."
Do not doubt it! I am the Knight of Marrow, noble guardian of the Blackfeather Court.\n\nI am on a quest to recover bones full of delicious marrow for the duke to eat.
No, I'm afraid I can't. I must be about my own quest. You have delayed me long enough. These bones won't collect themselves.
He is my liege lord, the master of the Crow's Wood in the absence of the Crow Mother.\n\nAs a visitor to the wood, you will be asked to complete a quest of your own.
I'm talented. My skill pours from the sky. I never even picked up a book, but look how naturally I brewed this potion!\n\nAnd look how colorful it is! That's talent.
For the change of pace! Court gets so noisy. Here, I'm the only one squawking. \n\nAnd I get the choice bits from the fish that wash up on the shore.
You're in Oblivion! Nothing is ever quite what it seems, and you shouldn't let your eyes betray you.\n\nIf they do, pluck them out and give them to me. Eyes are so delicious!
As close to fish as you can get in this place. Memories of fish, I guess. Remember that nothing here is real.\n\nI guess that means you're talking to yourself, featherless one.
<<1>> drew power from three Ayleid crystals to seal the door. If you activate the crystals, they take back their power from the door. Then, you open the door and wallop <<1>>.\n\nSimple, yes?

The first one is near the sealed door. The others are in the same room, but held up high in claws.\n\nFear not, merciful friend! Passages lead to the claws, through hordes of angry-dead and countless snake-ladies. But <<1>> keeps light on her feet!
The Supernal Dreamers. They must be stopped or the world will end. Recover the crystals.
They're antiques, of course! Highly collectible! Also, magic.
Cultists! You know. Do bad stuff, summon the unspeakable, destroy the world. Call themselves Supernal Dreamers. I wonder what Supernal means?
The shattered crystals can be used to control the orbit of the moons. Those who control space control the world.
The Supernal Dreamers are a group of daedra cultists who manipulate dreams.
They are really bad dudes.

They're Daedric cultists of some stripe or another. To be honest, I can't be bothered to distinguish them. \n\nBut they're going to use the shards of the Crystal of Power for a Daedric summoning ritual, and that's all you need to worry about right now.
I don't believe you.
Along the cliffs, past the docks. Just follow the smell of brimstone.\n\nThe locals avoid the place because of the stench, but a man came down not too long ago and walked right in.
My house is on fire!
Jinkies, not again. That's the kind of thing that happens to Goblins all the time. Story of our lives. I could tell you all about that, but I know you don't care, so why waste my breath? Kill me now.

I am Geoffroi Stictal, the Lord of this realm. I govern the properties you see here, from the largest house to the smallest campfire.\n\nI am also the keeper of the Crystal of Power, which prevents this place from being removed from existence.
The Crystal of Power has been in my family for generations. We were entrusted with keeping it safe a thousand years ago.
It's a faux-shanty shack. I wouldn't expect a commoner like you to understand.
Why? Because I can. Plus I'm just a demonstration.
Heck if I know.
Of course, he occasionally stands-in as my jester.
It was only a rhetorical question.
Ah, I see. I shall have him tested immediately.
Because they're Daedric cultists, and everyone needs a hobby.
I will be dead soon <cough>. You must hurry.
Don't be silly! All magic are crystals.
Oh, I don't know. Important stuff.
Ahem! So, a Goblin-fancier, are we?
The Sky?
Because of the Dragon tears.
Dark Elf. Mage, by the look of him. "Telba-something," I think he said. He asked for directions. Said he was looking for his father.\n\nSorry, I've got to get back to work.
I am what remains. I was lost in this wood, trapped here and chased by wolves until they caught me.\n\nI grieve for you. There is no escape from this wood.
There is no salvation for me now. Flee this place of shadows if you can!
Such cruel fate! Where was he when I still lived?\n\nBeware the high moor from which the tower rises. Ghosts who have wandered far longer than I lurk at its summit, hungry and hateful.
You'll forgive me for not thanking one of <<1>>'s murderers for turning her coat. \n\nBut the Khajiit is your prisoner. What would you do with her?

Then as a duly-appointed vicecanon, I authorize summary judgment upon a spy within our borders. Guard, prepare the Khajiit for execution.\n\nOnce this business is finished, I'll join you in the Inner Bailey. <<1>> will suffer a crueler fate.
You can't be serious. The Dominion stole our soldiers' skins, murdered a vicecanon, and destroyed Argonian eggs at the hour of their birth.\n\nBeheading would be leniency.
Vile thing. A bit of magicka focused … and there.
A powerful benefactor. She hates that monsters can ruin the lives of everyday folk.\n\nOur benefactor has put gold behind her principles. And so, we put our strength behind her cause.
I can feel my flesh decay. But I'm not dead. Please, kill me. I'll tell you anything if you promise to kill me.

<<1>> fled further into the mine, but <<2>> ran into that hut. I'm not sure if he's still alive. Frankly, I don't care. That lazy scaleskin left me to die.\n\nMany thanks, my friend. When we meet again, the mead will be on me.
That's true, though without my help, it will take Valaste considerably longer to translate it. \n\nI'd like you to return and let her know the bad news.
Tests. Well, that's a start. I suppose.\n\nWhat of Shalidor? He was drawn away from here in a burst of light.
Yes, Rulantaril is here. We made a bargain, but he thought to renege by binding me in this tower.\n\nHe still fights me. He doesn't want to stay. Make him see reason. Make him honor our agreement.

Sweet Rulantaril came to me, the nether-niece of Nocturnal, to learn the secrets of the forgotten magic. \n\nIn exchange, when the time came, he was to return to keep me company. That was our bargain, sealed in blood and arcane runes.

He tried to avoid his responsibilities, but the magic wouldn't allow it. He made a … tiny miscalculation. \n\nWhen he left, that hurt me deeply. He used me, but I forgive him. He must stop fighting and stay with me.
I don't know. Desperation, I suppose?\n\nI knew I'd made a terrible bargain, and I didn't want to live with it. But I do, don't I?
Of course he did. He's my son. He's intelligent and resourceful. I left him all the clues he would need.\n\nI was hoping for a rescue, not rebuke from a stranger. Are we done?
That's not something I care to talk about with an outsider.\n\nWhy don't you ask <<1>> about it?
That topic is off-limits for me.\n\n<<1>> might tell you about it.
They don't pay me to worry about that sort of thing.\n\nWhy don't you ask the ferals? They might even answer … in between bites.
Very well. Get the <<z:1>> to <<2>>. She's holding the tower southwest of the camp against the ferals.\n\nAnd remember: I'll hold you to our bargain. All of it.
That's all?\n\nThen we must stop him, and quickly. Search the remains of this camp for any indication of <<1>>'s whereabouts. I'll rally the soldiers and prepare to assault the ruins.
They stay here. Master says he doesn't want them to be dead yet.\n\nI get them when time comes. No worry!
The students you helped want to speak to you. They're waiting at the docks.\n\nI think they want to say goodbye.

Well, Geirvarda doesn't seem very thrilled about going to the Academy. And Renus and Guronii will wager on anything. \n\nI even heard some students buy their way onto the boat, but I'm not sure I believe it.
I know. You have things to do. Important things. We just heard about everything you did before you arrived here.\n\nBut we didn't want you to forget us.
We wanted to give you something. It's not much, but maybe it will help you remember the Academy.\n\nNow where did I put it?
No. I want to, but I'd better not. My family would be angry. \n\nAnd studying at the Academy has got to be better than herding goats.
I want to love her of course! She is my sweet, my cuddles, my etherial netch.
Not good. Not good. \n\nI'll start translating this right away, but I hope Shalidor returns to help.
Xarxes' backside! Then this is going to take a while.\n\nCheck in at a guild hall from time to time. I'll leave word for you when I've finished.
I'll send you back to Tamriel, then. Are you ready?

They must think me thick-shelled … and they'd be right. I came to help. No one, not even a Goblin, deserves to be a slave. <<1>> used their totem to control them.\n\nSo I stole the totem. I thought if I returned it to the Goblins, they'd leave.
And they even chose a war chief and settled in. They'll keep attacking the village until the vicecanons wipe them out.\n\nHelp me clear the blood from my name.

So she can enslave the Goblins again. That would bring peace … of sorts. I can't bear that. If I had the totem, perhaps I could solve this.\n\nGo out the mine's back exit to the Goblin camp above us. The war chief must have the totem.
Of course! People come for miles around to hear me play. Do you have any requests?
Perhaps. But you haven't been sponsored and we haven't checked your background. \n\nNow, please go away. I'm too busy to chat with over-ambitious bumpkins.

You do, eh? It'd better be important. You'll find him in one of the ruined buildings north of here.\n\nA word of advice: don't stray into the western side of the prison. Not unless you want to be eaten.
For dinner. Some of the prisoners have gone feral.\n\nCaptivity with no hope of escape will do that to the weak-minded.
I'll tell you what I can. I'm no expert on Goblins.

Goblins always chase after their totems. Surii knew that.\n\nShe paid someone to steal it from the Goblins. She lured them here and then hired a mage to enchant the thing. Apparently, Goblins are easy to charm.

After I gave it to them, the biggest beat the others into submission and took it. So now he is the warchief.\n\nHe's probably close to the center of their camp. They circle around their totems like flies on a carcass.

I don't think it would be good. \n\nI heard a story once about an Argonian who destroyed a Goblin totem. He wanted to save his village. The Goblins went on a rampage for weeks. They shredded tree, hut, and nest alike.
Was there medicine to ease my pain?
Excellent! You've done my people a great service.
Is he dead?
If she lives, why do you stand before me?

He's known as the Daedric Prince of Madness: the Mad God. \n\nMy distant cousins, the Dunmer, call him one of their Four Corners of the House of Troubles. He's a threat to the bloodline and their Tribunal.
Is the boss dead?
Aieee!
It's an honor to know you.
Well, spit it out.
I see! Tell me, is Remelie dead now?
Well? Is the vile boss murdered?
Splendid!
What?!
Madness comes in many forms. Sheogorath encompasses them all.\n\nHe rules the Shivering Isles, but often takes an active interest in our world. That usually leads to someone's sorrow.

Shalidor was the most famous arch-mage of the First Era. His dedication to spellcraft and his commitment to research were unmatched by any before or since.\n\nMost mages revere him, though he does have his critics.
You're not going anywhere in life with that attitude. Jerk.
Nah, I'm kidding. Violence is funny.
Oh no! I've had a sudden revelation that killing sentient beings is immoral!
Great work!
You did what!?
Shalidor felt that one should earn the right to be called "mage." He created many trials to test the spellcasting mettle of men and mer.\n\nHis loudest detractors were those who failed those tests.
Well I die without pain.
Well I die with pain, but I die knowing I sacved the world.
The documents you found in the Maulborn camp contained several names. A few appeared over and over.\n\nAfter a little bit of digging, I connected one of them to our target.
Now you've got it. Varon and I will join you shortly. We need to send our report and wait for our next orders.\n\nStay safe. I'll see you soon, my friend.

Because I also learned that Hlaalu troops have been ambushed by superior Maulborn forces at the Obsidian Gorge. Our target leads those forces.\n\nWe want the alchemist. Saving Hlaalu troops isn't part of our mandate. But maybe together ….
Oh, just one of the many shrines to my lord. The common rabble know it as Cheesemonger's Hollow. \n\nSheogorath is fond of it, but rarely graces it with his presence.

For a number of reasons we have to operate in secret. If word got out about my true identity, my life wouldn't be worth a one-legged kwama.\n\nBut know that I adhere to very strict guidelines. That means I can't just stab anyone who ticks me off.
Are you lost? Do you know nothing of the place you've come to?\n\nThe Shivering Isles are Lord Sheogorath's realm in Oblivion. To tell you more would, as my lord puts it, spoil all the fun.
I am Lord Sheogorath's chamberlain. I handle his affairs and look after the Shivering Isles while his lordship is away.
They slit my throat and call it a day. Puts me under a bit of pressure, you understand.\n\nSo don't get me angry. That never ends well.

He's my contract, yes. Not his Maulborn troops, however.\n\nWe have to walk a careful line. Let's just say my organization isn't in the highest standing right now, but some house leaders still place their trust in us to get things done.
The Song? Of Sinmur? Look, mead demon. I'd love to help you, but I don't know the lyrics. Or the melody, to that particular tune.

<<1>> swore to fight the Dominion's enemies. You saw the horrors <<2>> brought to these lands: skin-stealing, egg-killing … nothing the Dominion should be. <<1>> upholds the Dominion by helping Pact-soldiers stop <<2>>, yes?

Return to Dominion army with news of <<1>>'s fate. Emphasize how stupid tactics, awful plans, and crimes of war were his ruin. <<2>> may leave out her part in <<3>>.\n\nAfter that, continue defending the Dominion from all foes. <<2>> swore an oath.

Yes, on battlefield where fighting should be. Not against Pact families in their houses. Not in swamp-lizard nurseries.\n\nPlease, Pact-soldier, give <<1>> the chance to fight Dominion foes under the sun, not from the shadows.
Complex indeed. Much of this is beyond my understanding, but … here. This one is an attunement spell.\n\nWe can summon <<1>> himself! We'll need some ritual orbs ….
This Khajiit came with the Dominion soldiers who committed terrible crimes on <<1>>'s behalf. If not responsible, she is complicit. Is this truly your decision?
Set one of these Dominion criminals free after the terror they brought to Shadowfen? <<1>> plans to end the Argonians as a species!\n\nYou earned my trust at <<2>>, but this is too much to stomach.

Guard, take charge of the Khajiit. Prepare her for interrogation. If she gives you any trouble, shave off her whiskers. \n\nOnce our soldiers push back the lamias, I'll join you in the hunt for <<1>>. The Hist guide you, friend.
You wish her execution? I admit the thought pleases me, but vengeance often clouds reason. Are you certain she must die?

Clever. They'll consider <<1>>'s experiments an extravagant waste of resources and focus their attention elsewhere.\n\nI'll escort the Khajiit from the ruins and meet you inside the Inner Bailey. <<1>> won't see another sunrise.

Then we'll take charge of the Khajiit. Guard, treat her as my personal ward. I'll allow no reprisals against her.\n\nOnce our soldiers take the entrance, we'll join you in the Inner Bailey. <<1>> can count his lifespan in minutes.
Even now, <<1>> works to separate my people from the Hist. If you must consider what to do with the Khajiit, I urge you to do so quickly.
<<1>> brought me in to keep the Goblins in line. That trinket of theirs only does so much.\n\nAll these years of experience breaking slaves to be properly obedient, and then a damn Goblin stabs me.
Sinmur. The giant led the Reachmen from Shor's Stone. Arrived just in time to see the Watch Captain throw herself into the fray. I need to restore order here. Can we press you into service again?

That soft-hearted Argonian stole the totem, breaking its spells. I'll wear his hide for boots! Goblins are animals. We were teaching them a trade.\n\nWith you here, there's still hope to salvage this mess.
I'll … I'll survive. I can't say the same for all of my men. Wait. Who in Oblivion are you?
We believe Magistrix Vox is holed up in the caves here. \n\nBut we don't have enough troops to go in after her. Or stop her, if she tries to fight her way out.

Our Lady Almalexia suggested that perhaps Saint Veloth, whose hammer Vox wields, might be able to provide assistance.\n\nBut his shrine to the west has reportedly been overrun. And we don't have enough troops to do a thing about it.
You're going to perform a play. My play, actually. Wrote it meself.\n\nI call it "The Folly of Isolation." It's a tragedy and a comedy, both at once. A tromedy!

Beat on some Goblins for a bit, then slam that totem down in front of them. They'll cower at the sight.\n\nWhile you do that, I'll climb down. Meet me inside the mine at the slave quarters. We'll retake the place … if you've got the totem.
We need to learn more about these things. The ghasts keep repeating the name Calix Thorntongue. Go kill him, take his heart, and bring it back to me.
Not long. A few days. Perhaps a week, or a bit over that.\n\nMy house still stands, but if we dally much longer, they and my beloved will turn to ash!
Before we get to your motivation, we need to set the scene! The scene: Tamriel. \n\nThe three alliances are at war, and the wee little Mages Guild wants none of it. They want to stand alone.

Oh, everyone! Right up to the high muckity-mucks themselves. Just remember: you wait for your cues. You kill nobody unless it's in the script.\n\nNow, let's get going! I can't wait to see it performed. Here, Maleel will even light the way for you.
Pity. The tomes you seek are beyond the door at the top of the stair. Once you're outside, follow the path.
Indeed. As you do, collect their hearts. I feel powerful magicka radiating from this one. With more like it, we may be able to put an end to Stral himself.\n\nI will be back at camp, researching.

What madness! I, bereft of weapons and arms, and a slave dares speak? Be you a dream-spirit sent by the <<1>> to test my resolve?\n\nVery well, foul wind. We away to my liege! I'll waver not from duty, despite the <<1>>'s ploy!
Though the <<1>> overthrew my liege lord with trickery, my oath binds me true. I must obey him as my new liege lord.\n\nYou awaken a truth long since dead. Leave me to my misery, slave.
Our opening act features the Ebonheart Pact. Hah, that rhymes, doesn't it? I'm a poet, and until now I didn't realize it.

I swore a sacred pact to bulwark my liege lord from every menace. Yet the <<1>> twisted our oath. When he commanded, a profane compulsion forced us against our liege lord.\n\nI wept freely as I struck her down.
Still your tongue, lowborn! Think not to abscond with the <<1>>'s <<z:2>>, nor any other treasure within these walls!\n\nOr so my oath compels me to say.

Don't be presumptuous, mortal, or I'll banish you to the Isle of Lusty Bards.\n\nAhem. Like I was saying: as the curtain rises, our Ebonheart friends are at peace. Allies. Historically, though, they've been at each others' throats.
No time for witty banter, eh? Fine, fine.\n\nThis act features the Aldmeri Dominion. Cats and Elves! I never had a taste for either, honestly. Too much fur and fancy.
Let's play it by ear. The scene: Queen Ayrenn is addressing some of your peers.\n\nAs a master thespian, you should respond to her heartfelt pronouncements as you see fit. And … action!
Because it means the play is almost over. I'm enjoying this so much I don't want it to end! And the sideshows! Have you enjoyed my little illusionary performances? Very … illuminating, I think.
Well, it isn't. This is a professional production! And you are the star.\n\nI'll set the scene. We can just improvise from there. Remember: show, don't tell.
I won't tell ya, I'll show ya! That's the essence of storytelling. Show, don't tell.\n\nWhat do you think this is, community theater?
Hmmph. I don't know. Your performance was a bit uninspired at points. And you refused to eat cheese with me!
The book will take you back, it knows the way. Just remember, little actor. You still have one book left. And if you thought my play was rough, just think of what's ahead. Hah!
Yes, yes. You did make me laugh. And cry. And kick Maleel in the head. I suppose that's all I could ask.\n\nTake your book. Just don't eat it all at once!
I'll catch up as soon as I can. Kyne watch over you.
She's in the cave just south of here. It leads through the hill to the giant camp.\n\nI heard fighting, but I don't know what happened to <<1>>. Please, find her!
You … you're not a cultist. What are you doing back here?
Absolutely. I think. You're much less alive than you were a few minutes ago, anyway.\n\nThat should get you through the shroud.

It's rather embarrassing. I went out to meet my ah … lady friend, down by the west gate. Next thing I knew, someone dropped a sack over my head and knocked me out, cold. When I woke up, I was a prisoner.

According to the tablet, The Eyes of Yokuda are here in the city. Legend has it that these three gemstones open the door to the Yokudan Archive.\n\nIf I'm correct, the Archive might hold the fabled Cartulary of the Tamed Dunes!

It's a legendary tome that contains knowledge carried over from the land of my ancestors.\n\nYou think Redguards are survival experts? The Yokudans forgot more about steel-craft and desert survival than the Redguards ever learned.

The tablet mentions three areas: "The Gauntlet," "The Lair," and "The Ruin." I don't know what those are, but they don't sound very inviting.\n\nWatch for monsters and traps. You'll probably find both. When you've got The Eyes, meet me by the Archive.

Stop <<1>>! He enters the Hist through <<2>>'s mind to take my memories. <<1>>'s treachery will kill me, and my children will suffer.\n\nI will send you down to the Hist's roots. Kill <<1>>, and save <<2>>.
Good. The <<1>> will put you in a dream-like state.\n\nYou will feel as if you're <<2>> himself, and you will know what his spirit needs to reunite with his body. Follow your instincts.
Harassing? I'm collecting on a debt! I gave this woman's husband enough coin to outfit his expedition in return for a number of valuable artifacts. Now he's run off with my money!
Splendid! Then this won't be a total loss. Hand them over and I'll consider Tavo's debt paid in full.
Easy now, friend. No need for violence!\n\nYes, I see your point. Forgive me, Nahrina. Consider Tavo's debt forgiven. I'll leave you to your grief.
I don't, but I have to try. If we enslave them, what does that say about us?\n\nIt isn't about the Goblins, really, it's about what we want the Pact to be. And I want it to be better.
May the rains be ever on your back, friend. \n\nThis nightmare will be over shortly. Let my brothers know I'll see them soon.

It's the natural way of things. We're smarter and stronger, so they should obey us. \n\nThat's better for them and better for the Pact. We all win. Don't let that pit-bait scaleskin tell you otherwise.
That's a good choice, both for yourself and these little brutes.\n\nI'm sure the boss will have your money topside.
It will burrow into your mind, the way it did mine. I only have one Fang, and look what it's done to me. Look what it's done!\n\nI can't live this way. Kill me. I beg you! Kill me now!

Now you can see why I had you investigate. I didn't want to panic my troops. \n\nAfter each day of fighting, we've allowed the enemy to collect their dead, out of respect. Serien is raising them at night to face us again the next day.
I don't profess to know the <<1>>'s ways. But my oath compels me to protect <<Ac:2>> above all. Of this, I doubt not.

That old lizard, Walks, came to me with a plan to infiltrate the fort. I told her it was too risky. Now we're fighting a losing battle.\n\nIt's time to take a risk. <<1>> and an elite squad are in the ruins under the fort. She'll explain the rest.

Then why do the <<1>> and <<Ac:2>> seem one and the same to me? I cannot serve two masters. It goes against my oath!\n\nWere you not beneath my station I'd embrace you, slave! You've revealed the falsity underpinning my oath.
He showed up after the Imperials marched through. <<1>>. He's summoning more and more Daedra.\n\nHe gathered those who survived the first Daedric attacks, but I don't know what he may do to them!

Yes, drink it. Then you'll be able to go where we cannot. \n\nOf course, not all in the otherworld will welcome you. Contact with the beyond could be unpleasant, so avoid any creatures you see there. Good luck.

You're different. You must know that. Not all of you is with us, yes? That makes you the perfect candidate for the elixir. \n\nUsing the elixir, you can pass through the catacombs beneath <<1>>. Find the door, open the way, and end this siege.
He's gone. That milk-drinker was experimenting on us. Turning us into fodder for his undead legion! He turned them!\n\nTurned me, too. It's just a matter of time.

Too late for me … dying …. then I'll reanimate. Serien's planning something … some necromantic ritual. Got to stop him.\n\nLook, you've got to end us. Take a candle to the journals. Fire will do the rest. Go!

Such wisdom in a slave. My oath was to forever bear arms and armor in the name of my liege lord. Your plunderous ways freed me from mystification!\n\nI swore to my liege lord, not the <<1>>! This travesty ends now.

If Meridia favors me, <<1>> shall perish with the source of his power. Your thievery must be held account, but leniency is in order. Perhaps a finger of your choice?\n\nSlave, tell me true. Do I seem vigorous and lively? The world seems … indistinct.
Yes. My thanks.\n\nNow that I can hear the Hist, <<1>> wants to teach me to be a healer. Feyne wants us to return to Narsis. I don't know what to do.
You're right. Marriage means sacrifice, and Feyne deserves consideration after all we've been through here.\n\nI can always learn a trade. Thank you.
Your counsel follows my heart. I'll make it up to Feyne later.\n\nMaybe we'll even return to Narsis after I'm trained. Thank you.
There's more to it, isn't there? \n\nThe Dominion used crystals on our people. Pulling at them from inside their heads, they said. But some don't remember it at all. Why?

Ah, that clears it up.\n\n<<1>> has developed a strong connection to the Hist through this experience, something he lacked since his birth. He must become a healer. Please convince him of his destiny.

The game is a foot. Or a leg. In fact, all manner of severed limbs.\n\nBut don't worry about that! I've brought you here because I've been watching you. You work too hard! You need a nice little vacation.
Of course! This is my chateau! It's me family's estate. Gets handed down from me to myself, and so on, and so on.\n\nI think you'll love it here. Or hate it. Or one of the two, certainly.

Catch? Such an untrusting soul. If there were a catch, I'd say it's that two of my guests are murderous cannibals.\n\nMy advice? Don't let anyone eat you. If anyone tries to kill you, kill them right back!
Well, let's see. Now that you're settled in, you should tour the grounds. We have this lovely maze at the chateau.\n\nYou simply must see it.

Jolly good, you're getting it! I knew if we spent enough time together, you'd start to think like me. I have that effect on people.\n\nIt's a bit too dark, actually. Why don't you light a few braziers as you go? Improve the ambiance.

Is it that obvious? Yes, we were in love.\n\nI don't even remember what we fought about. What if I died and she never knew I'd cross a desert for her? When she gets this, if she wants to reach me, she'll know how.
Of course. I don't like being trapped.\n\nWe fled the recent invasion. We thought these ruins were abandoned and secure. We were wrong. They're here, consorting with the dead.
Their badges bear a black worm. They've bound my people to their soul collector crystals.\n\nFree whomever you can, and kill those Worm cultists! Come meet me afterwards in the southern chamber.
Well done! You're already proving your worth to the guild. \n\nSorry, did you say strange? What happened?

I am the Master of Incunabula, the keeper of tomes. \n\nI've come here to inspect the local Arcanaeum, the guild's library. I've dedicated my life to expanding our guild's knowledge. Standards must be kept.
They'll focus your Magicka, attune your life energies, and draw him to this place.\n\nThe ritual will apparently also link your mind with his.
It means that the arch-mage will be able to guide you, and speak to you whenever he chooses. \n\nAre you ready to begin?

<<1>> brought the bodies to me, but they're mauled. Broken apart!\n\nWhat was stolen must be returned, or their angry spirits will haunt <<2>> until the void takes us all. <<AC:3>> did this, I'm sure of it!
I saw her flaunting them as trophies. Slay her. Slay her, and bring what you find to me.\n\n<<1>> and I return to the antechamber with the bodies. I'll wait for you there.
They say lamias can talk, if they wish it. From what I've seen, they're little more than beasts.\n\nPlease restore what's missing to the bodies. I'll guide their spirits back to the Hist.
Once the fighting dies down, <<1>> and I will reunite them with the swamp, as a fallen leaf returns to soil.
Yes, actually. It's very pleasant. Some odd things, here and there, but overall … look, are you room service or not?
What? Well, no throwing me out. Throw me out and I'll have my advocate drag you before the Alinor courts.\n\nWe'll strip you of every coin you've ever earned. And every coin your sons will ever earn!
Such confidence! Braggadocio! Gumption! I like that! \n\nThe last place I'd like you to visit is our humble little manse. Just behind me.

Aye! We have an old rhyme about them. Ahem: "Four lights in a row, poke one to make it glow." \n\nNo, that's wrong. Maybe it was "Four lights in a trough, poke one to turn it off?" Hmm. Something like that!

They are the tendrils of Coldharbour, reaching into Nirn. The minions of Molag Bal erect dark shrines in his honor, landing sites for these horrors.\n\nThe coin this contract brings is good. And in this time of trouble, we need a focus.

Yes, I am new to my role as guildmaster. The death of my mentor, Jofnir Iceblade, has been hard on the Guild. He was well-liked among the rank and file.\n\nI hope the river has carried his soul where it wanted to go.
Now just hold on there. Haven't you been wondering why it's called the Chateau of the Ravenous Rodent?

Well, you should! And before I give you the last tome—before I reward you and Shally for all your hard work—you need to meet one more member of my family.\n\nLet me tell you the story of old Uncle Leo ….
Ehh … too much, I'm afraid. To be honest, it's become an embarrassment to the family. \n\nSo … as the final act of a courteous guest. Go kill Uncle Leo, will you?
<The skeleton tilts its head slightly.>
I should make you fight Narwhals on the open ocean. I should make you run a gauntlet of angry Argonian concubines! \n\nBut I won't. Book's yours.

Yes, yes. Well, I'm sure you and Shalidor will be very happy with your new book.\n\nOf course, Valaste has been the one doing all the reading, right? Send her my best. And tell her to read real close on this last one.
Not unless you've spent your life poring over obscure Daedric tomes. The Chateau is in the darkest part of Dementia, the shadow land of the Shivering Isles. I'm worried that ….
I'm … I'm fine adept. I'm just tired. It's become very draining to translate these tomes. Don't worry about me. I can open the portal to the Isles for you straight away. If you'll allow me?
They're after me. Once they breach my tomb's defenses, their magic can bind me to their will.\n\nIf you're the best this time has to offer, I see why they're looking to the past for heroes.
Exactly. Now you cut off the head of the worm. See the chamber below? Their leader's down there: a lich named Lord Vantir.
Good. I'll make my way back to entrance. I'll wait for you there.\n\nArkay guide you, my friend.
I've never faced a lich before, but I've always had reasonable success with violence. \n\nThat soul collector's trouble of a different kind.

Aside from the lich guarding it? One of the cultists called it a focus for the other collectors, channeling the energies to trigger something with unimaginable power.\n\nSounds to me like a good reason to destroy it.
They don't look like much. Little Argonian carvings. I have no idea why they're so important. \n\nYou'll find them inside four reliquaries, near the stone altars in the swamp.
You've seen combat, and I need all the help I can get today.\n\nVillagers are scattered across the island. We need to warn them.
Yes! Wait, no! Is the Master playing his games again? \n\nWait, I mean scenarios. I do enjoy his scenarios. They taste so yellow.
Yes, yes! Evict me! Open the door right now, or I'll peel off your face and wear it like a mask! I'll claw through this wood and tear out your succulent throat with my teeth!
No, not at all! There are things skittering around in here.

Hmm? Oh, don't evict me. As long as I ignore the noise, it's … it's quite nice in here.\n\nYou can't see the poetry of my soul from behind a door. You can't look into my eyes, and know that my mind is my own. You can't see the intensity of my truth!
Can you comprehend the power I once had? Why should I help you with anything?
My friends and I were out hunting in the woods when a mad mage ran up and began throwing spells at us. I think he only nicked me.\n\nHe dropped that wand in the snow as he left.
Bleakrock Island. I was in command for years until Captain Rana took over.\n\nNow we sit on our hands while she dithers and frets.
I repelled an Aldmeri Dominion scouting party once, and we've had bandits and raiders aplenty. \n\nI handled every emergency, but Captain Rana won't listen to a word I say.
You did take a hit to the head.\n\nTen years back, when the Akaviri invaded from across the eastern sea, the Nords, Dark Elves, and Argonians united to throw them back! Now, we're the Ebonheart Pact.

Lighting the watchtower. When we spot a ship, we're supposed to send a signal. \n\nWe spotted one, but Rana's delaying. She wants proof it's not a merchant, so she sent our only boat after the ship. It's loaded with the garrison's troops. Foolish girl.
We feel our brother's rage, but do not understand. He says the Dark Elf vicecanon tried to destroy the eggs at <<A:1>>. What does this mean?
Our brother's thoughts roil like thunderheads, yet we do not understand. He says the vicecanons shed their skins like water snakes to hide their intentions! Where is the truth in that?
Our brother's fear spreads through the roots. He claims the flesh-walkers boil our blood in vats of iron, all at a Daedra's command! Where is the truth in that?
They cleared away a cave-in from the north passage and there was the city. Of course, the first few that entered were skewered by traps or eaten by scarabs and gargoyles.\n\nServes them right.
Hmm? Oh, I'm more concerned with the state of the Hist than our safety.\n\nDon't you see? If we heal the damage to the Hist from within, perhaps the <<A:1>> will recover from <<2>>'s blasphemies.
The barrow has been here for as long as anyone can remember. \n\nLegends say a cult of Dragon worshipers built it, as well as the shrines like it on the mainland.
Ha! Once we smashed those Snakes, they didn't come back.\n\nNowadays we've got other problems—the Daggerfall Covenant and the Aldmeri Dominion.
He drinks too much, fights too much, and doesn't have the sense Kyne gave a horker. He's the best cook on the island, though.\n\nSince Father died fighting the Akaviri, we've only had each other.

About ten years ago, there was a collapse somewhere inside. After that, people started disappearing.\n\nAs long as I can remember, the cave's been forbidden. Captain Rana lectures us every time someone goes in to prove how brave they are.
<The skeleton remains motionless for a moment, then slowly raises its hand. It clutches feebly to a single sheet of paper, clearly torn from the same journal.>
Daughter? What are you talking about?\n\nWait … me?
What? Let me see that!\n\nNo. He only wanted immortality? We trusted him!
I don't know, and I figure I'm better off that way. \n\nThink about it.
Of course. The Dark Elves and Nords turn up their noses. That just leaves more for me.\n\nI'm no good running on wet decks anyway. It's the lost toes.
No, but I let the Elves think so.\n\nWhen I was younger I sailed on a "legitimate trading ship" run by Khajiit. When the Dark Elves caught us, they took my toes for thieving.
What, this? It's good Skyrim weather. Not even squalling.\n\nCome back in the dead of winter. Cold enough to freeze the hairs in your nose.
Traps. The restless dead. All manner of horrors.\n\nWe've got to get these people through.
Aye, me and Tillrani. Built that house ourselves, board by board.\n\nWhen I got here I never dreamed my commander would bed me. Even less that she'd like me enough to take Mara's vows.
You washed up on the shore. \n\nStrangest thing—your clothes weren't wet when we found you.
Ha! Do I look like one? I'm glad you have to ask.\n\nI'm just Maesa's apprentice … so far, anyway. She's been teaching me for about a year now.
Have you seen the size of Maesa's arms? Holsgar says she once punched out a mammoth.\n\nSmithing is a great way to let out frustration, especially after Otroggar comes over.

Oh, yes. We start with a lump of metal and end with something useful. Horseshoes and nails and swords and whatnot.\n\nI hear there are other kinds of crafters on the mainland, but I'd never be anything but a smith.
He's a fisherman. Fisher-lad. He stops by every day to see me.\n\nHe's always making dirty comments. Someday, my da's going to hurt him.
You what? No, my comrade. My friend. You have been deceived.
I … I did. Comrade, I serve the Daedric Prince Meridia. She blessed me with a sacred mission. I mobilized the Fighters Guild to defy Molag Bal. Jofnir … would not listen to me.
It's not the pigs. I love these pigs. They're like messy kids.\n\nIt's all the other work I have to do around here. And for what? Look at this place! Nothing grows here!
Ask myself that every night as I lie in the loft. Life's got to be better in Windhelm or Riften.\n\nJust a couple more seasons, and I'm leaving. Father can hire some help.
They got me in the forest. We were gathering firewood. Dedring, my brother, tried to fight. They split his skull with an axe.\n\nI thought I was a dead man until you arrived.
I am the vestige of a king chosen to serve on the first council. We came to Volenfell long ago, and thought it our duty to tame this wild land.\n\nWhy are you here, wanderer?

The warrior wave of our fleet, the great Ra Gada, sailed to this land in ages past. We are a people of strong and noble heritage. \n\nTo earn our respect, you must succeed at a trial of combat, of kingship, or of bloodlines. Choose now.
What makes you worthy of such a relic? Any common thief could make it this far.\n\nOnly someone truly worthy may take the Cartulary from its resting place.

The Ra Gada brought fear to Volenfell's shores. Breton, Orc, Nord, and Elf alike trembled at our battlecries and the prowess of our sword saints.\n\nTo prove yourself worthy, you must best this challenge.
Do you, now? You are either confident or arrogant. It matters little. Great kings are often both.\n\nTell me, wanderer. How would you use the secrets of the Cartulary?

You speak truth. Yokudan blood flows through your veins. I can sense it. \n\nThe Cartulary is yours, by right of blood. Use it as you will, but know that to abuse its secrets will bring you and your children great dishonor and misfortune.
This trial is not for you. You are not a descendant of the Ra Gada.
A true king knows that strength is often found in humility. We foster our people because they, in turn, make us stronger. A king is nothing if he is not beloved.\n\nYour answer satisfies me.
Was it this Paldeen who overcame the dangers? Who battled the guardians? Who risked life and limb to stand before me? No.\n\nYou are the focus of these trials, not Paldeen.

You're a plunderer, then! Many of the Ra Gada kings were corsairs. We raided the coastal cities and merchant vessels of the Bretons. We were both wealthy and feared because of our ferocity.\n\nYour answer satisfies me.
Your soul is missing. Want mine? It's black and gooey.
No. We're having old friends for supper. Drink some roots. Stay with us! You'll be safe here.
The stones! The shiny ones. They're pretty until you turn your back, and then … whoosh! Skulls implode. Bones shatter.
Want, want, want. Greedy squirrels. We wanted to leave here, but then? Shiny stones.\n\nI ate them after. They were cold. They hurt my teeth.
This is my safest place. My friends are here. Don't take them!
People don't die. They change shape, like Arawe. She's a candlestick. She's bright as the stars. And Tarak? He's never been happier.
It gives me headaches! And it tastes like sawdust. Go on, you eat it.
The shiny stones did that. The roots, the water, Oriell's three toes. \n\nI tried to save him, but his head wouldn't stop leaking. Now he's a milk jug.
І що?
That's … that's the first thing you've said that makes any sense.\n\nFine, take Eiman. Just leave my friends alone. And don't blame me if the shiny stones get you.
What? Who in Oblivion are you?\n\nGet out of here before I gut you like a trout.
Quick, come inside! We've almost made it past the Scamps. I heard them say the portal is just beyond.
This is most refreshing! Thank you.
For all the good it does. Bleakrock is snowed over six months of the year. When it isn't, the soil's poor.\n\nWe eat a lot of dairy. Aurochs can graze and eat hay from the mainland.
The Pact offered a bounty for settlers. They wanted the garrison at the tower to have access to "civilization."\n\nBet you didn't know civilization smells like auroch dung, eh?
We mainly live on fish. And that crazy Argonian likes mudcrabs.\n\nYou know what I miss? Apples. Used to get them when I was a boy in Falkreath. No more.

She spends all day with the blacksmith. She wants to move to the mainland and spend her life at a forge.\n\nThat nice fisherman Otroggar has been trying to woo her for months. She won't even listen to him.
You were unconscious at the time. I found you by the shore and brought you back to town. Mathor's been clucking over you since.\n\nSo. What happened to you? Shipwreck?
Lousy luck. Could be worse, though. You did wash up before you froze to death in the sea.\n\nWe have a sailing caravel, maybe you can take work on it. If it comes back.

I've been drinking stout all day. If you told me you were Akatosh come to grant my wishes, I might just believe it.\n\nWe have a sailing caravel. If it comes back, you can take it back to the mainland.
You seem spry for a soulless corpse. What does that mean? We don't need our souls?\n\nAw, stout always gets me philosophical. I should stick to mead.

I'm the miller. The big windmill yonder? Mine. Not that I often have work. Nothing much grows here.\n\nEvery month or so we load our caravel with fish and trade them for grain in Solitude. It's not efficient to mill it here, but it is cheap.
Some hours ago the garrison spotted a ship sailing east. That young Dark Elf, Captain Rana, loaded up most of the troops in the caravel and sent them to take a look.
Ha! I should know? Follow your heart and keep off the skooma, I suppose.\n\nSeriously, I'd get your soul back. I bet it's important. Our caravel can take you to the mainland, if it comes back.
That ship's a wallowing merchantman, not a warship. Like as not they're all in the teeth of the ocean now.\n\nWhich leaves this a fort without a garrison. No good comes of that, I says.
They need a leader, but they're stuck with me.
I need you to unlock a door deeper inside the tomb. That door will have stones with flower symbols upon it.\n\nHead through the door behind me. I'll see you soon.
He took the others up the hill, behind that rock outcropping. Please, save them!\n\nI'll try to make it on my own. There's no reason to stay here any longer.
I saw a group of them exploring the cave. They laughed at me, hanging in the ice.\n\nThen the Frozen Man got them.
Our home. From here, we reach throughout Shadowfen and beyond, as is our calling.\n\nShadowscales don't normally welcome outsiders, but the normal order of things … was disturbed.
You're unaware? We're chosen at birth to serve the will of Sithis.\n\nTo many beyond our enclave, we are simple assassins. But that is ignorance of our true role.
I'll do my best. I'd been hiding, but the fires finally forced me out of my home! I thought I'd be safe here, but it doesn't look as though any place is safe now.
They're being held in a place known as … Cheesemonger's Hollow. It is a realm of the Mad God, <<1>>. Stand by my side, and I will open a portal.
I'm a traveling merchant, and was away when the Daedra attacked.\n\nWhen <<1>> sent word of the first attack, I returned as fast as I could and found everything ablaze.
My first thought was the Imperials did this, but these fires were set too recently. The Imperials left before I set out.\n\nLooters, maybe? Or whoever summoned the Daedra?
My neighbor <<1>> sent word of the attack. He was certainly alive then.\n\nI hope the others survived, most of all my precious <<2>>. Please, look for them while you deal with the fires.

Yes. He's a good man. He's engaged to my daughter, <<1>>. He was away when the Daedra appeared, and I sent a lad to find him along his usual route.\n\nIf you know his name, then he's alive, it seems. We are truly blessed.

Not much. He's an Imperial. But he arrived after a different group attacked us, then left.\n\nI'm sure he will kill his prisoners, maybe feed them to his Daedra pets. I heard screams from atop the hill. He's there. I know he's there.
I fear the Covenant would intercept us if we went straight for Davon's Watch.\n\nSo we're going to make for Dhalmora, a small town down the coast. Are you ready to go?
We sighted a ship offshore. I've sent my troops to investigate. If it's the vanguard of an invasion … well, we'll need to evacuate.

You'll find the people of Bleakrock all across the island.\n\nDarj, the hunter, went to Skyshroud Barrow. Eiman's out at Orkey's Hollow with his sister, Rolunda. Seyne, my sergeant, is out at Hozzin's Folly.
I've been her second-in-command since we arrived on the island. She really is a skilled commander. \n\nThis just isn't her finest day … or mine.

<<1>> fears for his life. He's surrounded himself with guards and hides behind lock and key.\n\nYou'll find him in the basement of his house, but you'll need a key to enter. I'd search his house for the key.
<<1>> keeps close to his guards but they all wear the same uniform.\n\nMost of his guards won't look twice at you if you're wearing a uniform but he and his dogs won't be fooled.

<<1>> knows there's a contract on him. He's locked himself in his house and filled it with guards.\n\nYou'll find him hiding in the basement, but you'll need a key to enter. I'd search his house for the key.
Most of his guards won't look twice at you if you're wearing a uniform but <<1>> and his dogs won't be fooled.\n\nYou could use a uniform to avoid detection and get to him when he's alone.
<<1>> values his life. He's surrounded himself with guards and hides behind lock and key.\n\nYou'll need a key to enter the basement of his house. I'd search his house for the key.

If you want to get <<1>> by himself you may need to create a distraction.\n\nExtinguishing a torch will draw a guard from his path and releasing a rat or throwing flashpowder into a fire will distract multiple guards.

I can make it. Thank you!
What do I mean? Look at this place! The island is overrun with Daedra. Sheogorath has given us the apple, but it's riddled with worms.

You know, funny thing about deals. They're really the sorts of things you should get in writing. I said if you completed the trials, you could find the island.\n\nThe portals to deepest Oblivion scattered here and there? A sort of bonus.
I've been hunting beasts in the wild of Skyrim all my life. Deathclaw ravaged a couple of herds near Kynesgrove. I took on a contract to end him.\n\nI always fulfill my contracts.
I'll bet she's there now. I'll see her there. Thank you!
Yes, my family. I should go to them. Here I go!
Kyne protect me! Thank you. I'll go.

I don't know how spells work! I tried picking up the wand, but it wouldn't let me. I think it does the spell … or undoes it.\n\nLook, my friends are Faltha, Brend, and Runs-in-Wild. They're skeevers now. Please find them and use the wand to fix them.
Proof? What are you talking about?

There's a smuggler's landing on the far side of Last Rest, the old tomb. They berth ships there sometimes. Even if it's empty, we can hide.\n\nI don't want to leave without our people, but we may not have a choice. I don't know what to do.
If that's true, then that ship … my troops … curse it! Tillrani was right. We must evacuate. \n\nFirst thing's first, though. We have to signal the mainland.
If that's true, then that ship … my troops … curse it! Tillrani was right. We must evacuate. \n\nFirst thing's first, though. We have to signal the mainland.
If that's true, then that ship … my troops … curse it! Tillrani was right. We must evacuate. \n\nFirst thing's first, though. We have to signal the mainland.
Are you sure about this? Anyone we haven't found will be left behind.
Thank you. Be careful out there.
It's an old Dragon shrine. It's a relic of the Dragon Wars. \n\nSome of the villagers claim they saw undead out there. I sent Darj out to get proof.
Thank you, friend. \n\nAfter you find Darj, keep looking. The more people you can send back here, the better off we'll be.
Locals claim it's haunted. They dare each other to spend a night inside. It's a silly custom, but a harmless one.
<<1>> adopted Eiman and Rolunda after their parents died. She won't leave without them.\n\nSend them back here. Then see who else you can find.
It's an abandoned mine. A family came out from Stonefalls to work the place. Rumor has it they're Daedra worshipers.\n\nNow some bandits are hunting through the place, and we need to know why.
Thank you, friend. \n\nOnce you've dealt with the bandits and sent Seyne back here, see who else you can find.
The Covenant is here. They set fire to the village.\n\nNarrald and I tried to protect the Earth-Turner family and the rest of the farmers.
Yes, I can sense them. Some worm defiled this place.\n\nYou are now my will incarnate, mortal. Enter the barrow and kill this worm.
They're vermin. Crazy about some feathered pole.\n\nWhy do you ask? You're not a Goblin-lover? You're not going to set them free or anything rash, are you?
No doubt <<1>>'s doing. May his corpse dry to a husk!\n\nWe must wake the vicecanon before <<A:2>> tears her mind apart!
Bluntly put, but yes. Without slaves, this mine can't turn a profit, and the Pact loses iron needed for the war effort.\n\nBesides, Goblins are animals. This is an improvement for them.
No hitting! Okay, Surii figured out their totem was the key. She stole it and had a mage enchant the thing.\n\nWhoever holds it controls the Goblins. Someone took it from her and let the Goblins go.
Wait, adept … you're not making sense. What do you mean? Sheogorath put that curse on those books to slow us down, make the task more time-consuming.

I suspect we find and remove whatever afflicts the Hist. I'm embarrassed to say I have no idea how.\n\nBefore your arrival, I found myself wracked with pain. Now, all is calm. The Hist's subtle way of indicating you should lead, yes?
Holsgar the Miller found you along the shore. \n\nHe was certain you were going to die, but he dragged you back to town, just the same.
They don't appear to be part of the Hist. Perhaps a vestige of <<1>>'s experiments? If so, we should remove them, yes?

The Dark Elf vicecanon returns to the old ways, when egg-clutches hatched as slaves. She destroyed a hatching to remind the Hist of her power.\n\nIf our brother speaks lies, we must feed him to the mire. Which is the truth of it, flesh-walker?
I'm not entirely sure. It was named after a prospector who came out here with his family. They said they were mining for iron, but folks saw them wearing dark robes.
That's the story. One day there was a fire, and the whole camp burned. Locals said they heard monsters roaring.\n\nThe place has been boarded up ever since.
You quickened our dream, small one. Yet our memories wither and fade. We must soon follow.\n\nWe could not stunt the vicecanon's greater purpose, so we sent her beyond the dream.

We rejoin the void, where all roots lead.  But the vicecanon carries our thoughts through seasons to come. In time, perhaps she can grow a new Hist, a different Hist from us.\n\nIt is not for you to follow us to the void. Go now, and be blessed.
There's a grand hall in the center of the island. We'll be able to survey the situation better from that vantage point. You and Valaste make your way up this path. I'll meet you there.

If you want to see it that way, sure! It's another trial. I'm sure you and Valaste - oh, hello dearie! I'm sure you'll have no problems closing the portals.\n\nHonestly, I'm surprised the Mistress of Incunabula didn't see this coming.
Oh, I'm sure you'll figure it out. You outwitted daffy old Sheogorath, right?\n\nAnyway, pull the crystals to close the portals. Have fun, see you soon!

No reason at all! What are you implying? That my choice to curse the books was a calculated move?\n\nThat crazy old Sheogorath knew there were only a handful of people in the guild that could do the work she did? Madness!
Good. This one opens the way. The lizard won't escape her claws this time!

Our brother claims his blood was stolen from him by flesh-walkers and boiled in vats to sate a Daedra's gluttony. But if his fear overtakes him, we must sever his roots from the rest of us. Which truth is true, flesh-walker?
Sheogorath left a powerful ward on this building. I'll need a few moments to crack it open. Go! I should be done here by the time you return.

These memories are … recent tragedies? The Hist-brothers don't understand the anguish, and fear the Hist must be full of rot.\n\nPerhaps if you help the Hist-brothers understand the Hist's anguish, they won't need to cut it away.
This pit of a mining village? It's a terrible place run by a horrible person.
Before the Pact, Argonians were enslaved here.\n\nWhen our chains were finally broken, most of us left. Too much blood and pain in this place.
Xuth! <<1>>. I can say nothing good about her. She was a master when we were slaves, and she remains a master now.\n\nShe was fond of the lash. I doubt that's changed.
Our family worked in the mine, back when Argonian slaves did all the work. I don't know why, but a few days ago, our brother returned.\n\nWe've come to take him away from this place.
Our family worked in the mine, back when Argonian slaves did all the work. I don't know why, but a few days ago, our brother returned.\n\nWe've come to take him away from this place.
Fate speaks in riddles. Your fate was written in the Scrolls, long ago. It is entwined with the fate of the Five Companions. \n\nI have finally located Lyris Titanborn in Coldharbour.
She works a terrible forge, under the lash of the great deceiver, Molag Bal. Her soul is in great danger. You must go to her. \n\nI can manifest a gate to that dark realm, but you must go quickly.
My apologies. It's been a rough few days with little sleep for anyone.\n\nWe've just had a little problem with Goblin … um … sympathizers. The Goblins were just workers until someone stirred them up.

Yes, precisely! Groveling creatures like mindless scaleskins and filthy Goblins need guidance. Can't do anything on their own. We had to do something. The Pact made it impossible here, freeing th-\n\nWait. I shouldn't have said that, should I?

Great power ripped open a way to Oblivion here, and that can never fully be shut. Scamps are the skeevers of those realms, wriggling through the gaps. \n\nIll-smelling, fire-spewing skeevers who killed my assistants and drove me from the ruins.
I've put a crack in his ward, but no more. The Mad God's power is formidable, even here. You and Valaste may enter. I may not. Just make sure to watch after her. I can see the state she's in.
I fear the Mad God may have gotten the better of us. But perhaps something can be done. Go inside, deal with Sheogorath. We've come too far to be put off by his tricks now.
Some folks have, mostly youngsters. Until recently, this place was haunted by dust and the occasional frostbite spider.\n\nNow skeletons rise from their graves. Something has changed.
You don't get it. If you take the Fang, I'll still be its thrall. It's stronger than me. It will make me do things—awful things!\n\nPlease, have mercy. Take the Fang, but kill me, quickly!
Bleakrock Island. Off the coast of Skyrim. <<1>> found you washed up on the shore.\n\nCaptain Rana will want to know you're awake.

You need to ask? Bah! Once, everyone knew the ritual. \n\nThree runestones unlock the door. They're placed in prominent positions around the shrine. Find them and put them on their pedestals around the door. Then you'll gain entrance. Now go!
The people of Bleakrock owe you.\n\nI owe you.
And she will need time to recover. One does not leave such a place unscarred.

For now, you must leave me to my meditation. I must set my mind to the task of locating Sai Sahan.\n\nUntil then, embrace the unknowable. The drops of water cannot know themselves to be a river, yet the river flows on.

As you saw in my visions, the Amulet's misuse ripped a hole in the barrier that protects Tamriel from the forces of Oblivion. That damage must be undone, and the Amulet is the key. \n\nBut, to find the Amulet, we must first locate Sai Sahan.

It's a wretched place. A haunt of cowards, traitors, and lost souls. \n\nAnd Daedra. Their vile spells violated my mind. Forced me to doubt myself. To disobey my own will. They'll pay for that, and pay dearly.
I'm no mage, I'm a warrior. I have no knowledge of such things. \n\nMy skill is with a blade, as Mannimarco will discover when I remove his head from his narrow shoulders.

After the Soulburst, one of the five, Sai Sahan, fled with the Amulet of Kings. According to the Prophet, it's the only object in the world that can repair the tear in the veil between Tamriel and Oblivion.
Who is Ysgramor? Just the greatest hero of the Nords, the man who led us to Skyrim! He was our first king. \n\nFounder of Windhelm! Leader of the Five Hundred Companions! That was Ysgramor.

We spotted a ship offshore. I think it's the Daggerfall Covenant. They've claimed lands to the northwest across the High Rock and Hammerfell.\n\nIt might be a scout, but I still think we're in for a fight.
I'll answer what I can.\n\nCaptain Tillrani's got the villagers thinking I'm an addled netch, but I'm actually a bit smarter than that.
Posted to this backwater, you mean? I made a hasty decision, a bad call. Soldiers died.\n\nI learned my lesson. Now I don't act without proof.
I took her job. You might have heard her yelling about that in the square.\n\nIt's petty, but what can I do? Every time I've reached out to her, she's slapped my hand.
A Nord asking me about Nords. Clever … for a Nord.\n\nHonestly? Your people impress me. Most I've met are stout and adventurous. Strong of arm and heart. Good folk.
I like Nords. Most Nords I've met are strong of arm and heart. I call them the proud spine of the Pact.\n\nI'm also more comfortable behind their swords than in front of them.
I'm not a scholar, but I'll tell you what I know.

Other than our beauty, brains, and rapier wit? We proudly work to enact the will of the Tribunal, our living gods.\n\nIf the Nords are the heart of the Pact, and the Argonians are the soul, the Dark Elves are the brains.

You're asking me about Argonians? That's cute. I know you like your mud, and you rarely get upset. Most Argonians I've met mostly keep to themselves.\n\nAlso, we once held you as slaves. So there's that. Sorry.
I'm not a scholar, but I'll tell you what I know.

I won't speak for you, friend, but I live to enact the will of the Tribunal, our living gods. With their help, we can meet any challenge.\n\nIf the Nords are the arm of the Pact, and if the Argonians are the heart, we're the brains.

The Argonians are a mystery to me. The ones I've met keep to themselves. Good scouts, I'll give them that. \n\nNot long ago, the Dunmer held them as slaves. That ended with the founding of the Pact. Now we're all best friends.
I'm not a scholar, but I'll tell you what I know.
I won't go without a fight!
I won't go without a fight!
I won't go without a fight!
I won't go without a fight!
I won't go without a fight!

When you quickened our dream, we knew her great purpose and sent her beyond the dream. But you … we could not send you just yet.\n\nYou healed the wounds inflicted by the flesh-walker <<1>>, small one. The Hist shall dream of you, always.
In seasons to come, we'll grow and blossom. Our roots will mingle with the withered roots of our brothers. They will heal as we do.\n\nYou've made our future whole. Go now, and be blessed.
Still with us, is he? That man is luckier than a Khajiit in an abandoned fishery.\n\nWhat does Hrondar want? If it's for me to say he was right about sticking together, he can drown himself in a bog.
We don't need rescuing, we need Hrondar to recognize we're bait in another Dominion trap! Tell him I won't allow such wasteful theatrics on our behalf.
If you find <<1>>'s regiment, you'll find him. Tell him to call off his attack before the Dominion picks him apart. He shouldn't throw away his soldiers for what little remains of our forces.
What do you want to know? The longer we talk, the longer my people are in danger.

The vicecanons lead the flesh-walkers, but our brother says they lead the skin-walkers as well. If our brother speaks lies, we'll cut the rot of his thoughts away. Which is the truth of it, flesh-walker?
I'm using the Conversational mood.
I'm mood curious, inquisitive. Isn't that great?
I'm mood hopeful yearning. Isn't that great?
My mood is pleading, ingratiating. Isn't that great?
My mood is grateful, thankful. Isn't that great?
My mood is proud, confident. Isn't that great?
My mood is commanding, ordering. Isn't that great?
My mood is aloof, haughty. Isn't that great?
My mood is triumphant, victorious. Isn't that great?
My mood is empathic, pitying. Isn't that great?
My mood is affectionate, loving. Isn't that great?
My mood is suprised, awestruck. Isn't that great?
My mood is excited, urgent. Isn't that great?
My mood is happy, pleased. Isn't that great?
My mood is busy, distracted. Isn't that great?
My mood is apathetic, bored. Isn't that great?
My mood is sardonic, ironic. Isn't that great?
My mood is grim, determined. Isn't that great?
My mood is exhausted, breathless. Isn't that great?
My mood is tired, weary. Isn't that great?
My mood is sick, weak. Isn't that great?
My mood is wounded, suffering. Isn't that great?
My mood is nervous, worried. Isn't that great?
My mood is fearful, scared. Isn't that great?
My mood is terrified, horrified. Isn't that great?
My mood is disappointed, remorseful. Isn't that great?
My mood is embarrassed, ashamed. Isn't that great?
My mood is unhappy, depressed. Isn't that great?
My mood is suspicious, skeptical. Isn't that great?
My mood is annoyed, frustrated. Isn't that great?
My mood is indignant, offended. Isn't that great?
My mood is contemptuous, disgusted. Isn't that great?
My mood is taunting, mocking. Isn't that great?
My mood is evil, sinister. Isn't that great?
My mood is angry, perturbed. Isn't that great?
My mood is enraged, hateful. Isn't that great?
My mood is whispering. Isn't that great?
My mood is conspiratorial, confiding. Isn't that great?
I see. Dear Eiraki, always trying to help her big brother.\n\nWell, while we formulate our plans to retake Lower Yorgrim, I suppose there is something you can do.
I think so.\n\nThank you. I'll see you down the river.
I'll dance on the water—thank you.
With your aid, moist one. My thanks.
A few years now. Got him when I was in the Pact army. Right off the battlefield, in fact, after the victory over the Imperials at Fort Farragut.
They were Nord lands at the time. And they will be again.\n\nHe was all fur and bone, trying to eat a dead Imperial. No dog deserves that. I did name him after an Imperial, though.
Ha! That Rexus defended the fort armory. Everyone else is dead, he's surrounded by Nords, and he's still swearing to defend the stash.\n\nA loyal man, that. But stupid. We gutted him.
We're used to taking contracts as they come. We pick our own jobs.\n\nThe guildmaster, though … she wanted us to go hunt Daedra. If only we had followed orders ….
The choice must have been tough. \n\nMay Kyne watch over Rana and the warriors on the docks.
I won't go without a fight!
We are at war with the upstarts from Daggerfall and our old enemies from Aldmeri. We need fresh arms!
Good luck soldier!
Come back when you're ready to aid the Pact.
I'll meet you back in Dhalmora. My thanks.

Our brigade came to the shrine to pray. That's when they fell upon us. Daedric witches!\n\nThey bewitched most of my soldiers. We four are all that remains, and Droi is burning with an unnatural fever. I fear he won't last much longer.

It's likely the witches killed or cursed them.\n\nOf course, they could be barricaded away, just like we are, waiting for help to arrive. Droi mentioned something about them before the fever took him, but we've had other things to deal with.
He was cursed by the witches. The fever burns away all that he is. Soon he'll be a mindless slave, just like the others. \n\nThe Keepers could heal him, but we haven't seen a Keeper since we arrived.

I don't expect to see those troops again. We're headed for a beach on the far side of the island. \n\nThey don't think I know about it, but smugglers sometimes anchor in that cove. I just hope we catch a break.
I won't go without a fight!
Charming question. The war with the imperials. The few of us that could fight enlisted with the King's army. Those that were left were ill fit to defend our homes when the enemy found us.
