Most went to build camp in the ruins of Silaseli to the East. It's been abandoned for centuries, but you couldn't drag me there. Mark my words: there's never been a good turn in an Ayleid ruin.
Appearances are decieving. The bags of gold I paid the King's healers guaranteed I was found riddled full of dibilitating diseases and injuries, dooming me to this life away from the front lines.
No, I'm alone in my highly refined survival instinct. The majority of the dispossessed are of the normal skill-less-peasant or wounded-veteran variety.
You search in vain, then, for the Keepers are lost.\n\nKyne no longer lights their way. Why should the Keepers maintain the shrine of a god who ignores their prayers?

Think about it. You'll figure it out soon enough.\n\nNow leave this place and take everyone barricaded in that building with you. The Keepers don't need to be rescued. And this grove belongs to us now. Go.

Kyne blesses the Nords before battle, but Nords die every day. We lose sons and daughters in these stupid wars. And what does mighty Kyne do? Absolutely nothing!\n\nWe refuse to worship a god who ignores us and lets our children die.
You can't. Don't come back for me. Just get Aera, Denskar, Littrek, and Trynhild. I didn't see where they went.\n\nRana's at the old tomb. Tell her … tell her I forgive her.

Denskar headed to the bunkhouse. Aera tried to take shelter in my home. Then the soldiers set fires, laughing.\n\nPlease, you have to get water. Save our people! I came to warn you, but the troops … they caught up to me.
Thank you! This has been difficult, but I'm grateful.\n\nRoruld muttered something about honey and giants. If you're up to it, I'm sure he could use your help to get his first batch of mead started.
<This dresser is locked. Perhaps one of the bewitched soldiers has a key.>
As soon as we're up and running, you can have all the mead you can drink! \n\nOh, by the way. Have you met my twin brother, Yraldar, yet?
You're new to Stonefalls? One of the Bleakrock refugees? Then you'll need supplies, yes?\n\nDavon's Watch is the closest town to this village. It's a hub for traders from across the Pact.

Those Stormfist ruffians chased a giant across the road, right into my beehives. It's scaring the bees! And frightened bees make bitter honey. \n\nYou need to get rid of that giant before anything else goes wrong.

Wait, it's coming. Another one of my brilliant ideas—there! And that is why Haraldar made me the master mead maker!\n\nUse the bees against the giant! Just kick a beehive. The bees will go after the biggest target out there, the giant!
I know your decision will be just. What have you decided?
Once a month. I trade our guar hides and meat for smithed goods, fine tools, and luxuries.\n\nI used to bring back news from abroad, but people here aren't interested in much beyond their fields.
I hope you're joking.\n\nThey're the three members of the Tribunal: the living gods of Morrowind. Almalexia the Mother, Sotha Sil the Wizard, and Vivec the Poet.
I was sent by the Tribunal Temple in the town of Ebonheart. Disciple Sildras ordered me to bring the true religion to these heathen barbarians.

I can't make this decision. Colors and I have fought side-by-side in some of the worst places on Nirn. Whatever caused her to act this way … if she'd just spoken to me … made me understand. Stendarr's blade!
You're no fool. We have fought together, side by side. The council has decreed her death!\n\nDo what must be done, lest Aelif do it herself.

The lizard is here, in Coldharbour! This thing, this construct. It must be the Mortuum Vivicus, comrade! We have caught her in her obvious lies!\n\nThough, it is true, Meridia is the prince of fools and weaklings. Perfect for that scaled traitor.
Truly? A Daedric Prince. But then, Colors has lead our charge against the Daedric anchors. She lead the hunt for the Mortuum Vivicus. She can't be all bad, then. Right?

The Three are Elven in form. They feel the pleasures and pains of mortal flesh.\n\nYet they are immortal, all-knowing, and immensely powerful. In the Akaviri War, Vivec flooded the battlefield and drowned the enemy. No mere mortal could do that.
I am here to keep you safe, comrade. And to help you see this task done. You must destroy this abomination, this Mortuum Vivicus.
The Argonians, of course. Look around. Mud huts, spears, cave paintings—this is the pinnacle of their culture.\n\nOur people wasted centuries trying to civilize them. They're as stubborn as guar.
They listen politely, ask questions, and go back to worshiping trees.\n\nI blame the shaman, Veth Veidal. They all call her "Mother." She poisons their minds with her pagan heresies.
I'm going to do what I do best and return to the Earth Forge. We fought the priestess of a Daedric Prince! The guild will need sharp blades, and I plan to supply them.

I never wanted to command the guild, but it seems I have no choice. I may have to crack a few heads, but I don't see any other way to hold the guild together after this fiasco. Of course, without your help it could have been worse.
Captain Rana spoke of you when she passed through town.\n\nTell me, what did you think of the Covenant forces? Could they burn our village like they burned Bleakrock?
There's never been a need for more guards. Most days, I help Nebaxireet hunt for game, or I help Hixeeh-Raj herd our guar. The worst we've faced is a few drunken sailors.
Yes, this is a small village, but so was Bleakrock. And like Bleakrock, we maintain a signal fire outside of town.\n\nThey wouldn't come for us, but we might be caught in the current.
I know your decision will be just. What have you decided?
Perhaps not so much. But our possessions would burn, yes? The wood and fabric.\n\nNo matter. If they come, we'll run away. Things can be replaced.
I would make more elsewhere, especially in Ebonheart or Kragenmoor, but I've chosen to stay in Dhalmora.\n\nIf one is patient, one can gain great treasure. So I hope, anyway.
It's to the west, just through the mountain pass. You can walk there in less than a day.\n\nThough with the Covenant's problems, I might just postpone this month's trip.
Family. Why would I leave my clutch-mates? They love the mud's musk in Bal Foyen.

I know this book. Many Nords carry similar hymns written to our goddess. It's strange that a Daedric witch would take this from a Keeper.\n\nPerhaps it's part of their spell. Maybe they use a victim's property to maintain control.
A hymn book, a journal, and now a witch?\n\nI have my suspicions, but there must be more to it. This can't be what I think it is.
It sounds like the witches attacked before we arrived.\n\nI wonder if the Keepers were already cursed when this was written. That would explain why they were acting strangely.
A few. We scattered. Some locked themselves inside their houses, but the Daggers set those houses on fire.\n\nIf it wasn't for that crazed Dunmer, I'd be feeding crows.

Just that. Know that once you touch the lanceata pholiota, it will only work on you. Bring it here, and I'll guide you to a place <<1>>'s spirit could be.\n\nBe careful of the cave's wamasu. They're a necessary but dangerous part of our cultivation.
Well, it was just an idea. And a rather good one, too. Oh, I know! Let me splash you with this. It smells like smoke and ashes. The bees hate it. Now you shouldn't have any bee problems.
I'm fresh out. \n\nBit of an accident in the storeroom with a lantern, I'm afraid. Suddenly, no more kindlepitch.
Raiders? In Bal Foyen? Take the kindlepitch. Warn the Watch.\n\nYou are sun-blessed for telling me. Have you spoken with Urona at the fort already?

Sithis blessed us with a clutch of eggs. Master offered to send them back to Black Marsh, but we chose to keep you all with us. If we had listened to him, none of you would have been born slaves.\n\nCan you forgive me?
Is that how you address your master?\n\nYou're a slave! If you look at Feyne again, I'll put your eyes out. Do you understand?
Different isn't wrong. I love you the way you are.
Then I will die knowing whatever my mistakes—and they were many—I will be at peace with my son. Thank you.
Why, you scaly little piece of ….\n\nYou'll suffer for this!
Do you mean it? I can come with you?\n\nI know it won't be easy for us. <<1>>, we're stronger together than apart.

And you brought me its toe. I was only joking about that, but thank you.\n\nI started organizing things here. I don't suppose you ran into my brother Bjoruld, did you? He looks like me, but he's not as smart.

I sent Bjoruld to get a barrel of appleblossom honey from the barn. He probably got lost, but I need that honey to make more mead.  \n\nCould you get the honey? And if you see Bjoruld, send him this way. He needs to deliver these casks to Windhelm.
Belowdecks. Follow me.
We're preparing a meal. Restless-Tail and I usually do the cooking. We all eat together here—everyone in Dhalmora, I mean.
Yes. Our names are Tamrielic, but most of the villagers have Jel names.\n\nThat's because we spent so much time among the Dark Elves.
I'm sorry. Saxhleel. That's what we call ourselves. It was the Elves who named us Argonians.\n\nI don't even know what "Argonian" means, honestly.
Jel is the language of the Argonians … um, I mean the Saxhleel. Our people.\n\nRestless-Tail, Fetches-Glitter, and I were raised speaking Tamrielic. We don't know much Jel.
What? Why, because we were slaves, of course.\n\nRestless-Tail and I worked the fields at a saltrice plantation from the day we were born.
They've used our people as labor for centuries. We were all freed when the Pact was signed, of course. \n\nOfficially, anyway. They say some Elves still trade in our flesh.
Both. And neither. Nords might call me a shaman. Ladrasa, the Tribunal missionary, calls me a heretic.\n\nI am one with the Hist. Their sap is in my blood.
No, you couldn't understand. Only those who have communed with the Hist understand.\n\nSo I will tell you this: In your travels, seek out Shadowfen. Our people there can help you understand.

Truly, you do not know? You have been among the Dark Elves and Nords too long.\n\nThe Hist are the sacred trees of Black Marsh. We come from them. We return to them. We are of them, but ever apart. They sing in our blood.
They are trees. They grow only in the depths of Black Marsh, our ancestral lands.\n\nWe hold them sacred. Those who would harm them meet our wrath. You do not need to know more.

Because I do not worship her false gods. As this village respects my wisdom, her words hiss away like drops of water on sun-baked stone.\n\nLadrasa has no respect for wisdom. She heeds only her vain and preening false-gods.
We sometimes hear about attacks against lone travelers, but the giants mostly keep to themselves.\n\nI've never heard of them attacking a settlement before.

These are troubled times for Eastmarch. We hear that the Orcs grow more and more aggressive, and there are rumors that disenfranchised Nord clans plan to start a civil war.\n\nAnything could have provoked the giants.

Rations. Made from an old family recipe. An army fights best on a full stomach, or so they say.\n\nIn truth, my warriors have a tradition. They always eat these specific rations before going into battle and I'm loath to break our routine.

Before we charge out to deal with the wolves and giants, we need someone to rescue any other villagers still trapped out there.\n\nIf you could get the civilians out of the way, that will be one less thing for me and my warriors to worry about.

Meet us at the manor house to the south when you've completed these tasks. The armory there contains the weapons and armor we need to make our first strike against the giants.\n\nGood luck out there, stranger.

What? No. That can't be right. Even though I suspected ….\n\nNo. No, there must be some mistake. To go against everything they believe in, everything they were taught. Why would the Keepers do such a thing?

Are you sure you're up to this? <<1>> is one of our best assassins and he's lying unconscious in a bed.\n\nIt took more magic than I thought I had to get him back to sanctuary. I doubt I could do it twice.

This isn't our first dream killing, but it's the first that's gone so bad. I can't imagine what went wrong.\n\nWhen <<1>> didn't return I opened the portal again and went through. I found him lying next to the General's spellbook holding a singed hair.

That's the spirit. I've opened a portal to Fort Virak. Head on through when you're ready.\n\nYou'll need to collect one of the General's hairs and spike his drink with a sleeping potion before you can enter his dreams.
Why yes! But now I'm going to stand up and wave.\n\nSo, how does the camera view work when you're talking to me?
I'm sworn to secrecy by my order, but rest assured, our cause is just.\n\nClear our path into the caverns, and you'll be rewarded. That's all you need to know, and all that I'm permitted to discuss.
If you don't think the reward is worth the risk, perhaps you should leave.

We follow the ways of the Chimer, not the false gods of the Tribunal. We're servants of the Webspinner, who Vivec usurped. Dunmer, Goblin, or dreugh, we're all caught in the strands of the spider's web.
It says, "I am reading this note I found on a dead body. What does it look like I'm doing?"
<<1>> fears for his life. He's surrounded himself with guards and hides behind lock and key.\n\nYou'll find him in an ancient crypt, but you'll need a key to enter. I'd search outside for the key.
<<1>> keeps close to his guards but they all wear the same uniform.\n\nMost of his guards won't look twice at you if you're wearing a uniform but he and his dogs won't be fooled.
<<1>> knows there's a contract on him. He's locked himself away in an ancient crypt.\n\nYou'll find him hiding in the ruins, but you'll need a key to enter. I am sure the guards will have one.
Most of his guards won't look twice at you if you're wearing a uniform but <<1>> and his dogs won't be fooled.\n\nYou could use a uniform to avoid detection and get to him when he's alone.
<<1>> values his life. He's surrounded himself with guards and hides behind lock and key.\n\nYou'll need a key to enter ancient ruins. I'd search outside for the key.

If you want to get <<1>> by himself you may need to create a distraction.\n\nExtinguishing a torch will draw a guard from his path and releasing a rat or throwing flashpowder into a fire will distract multiple guards.

Yraldar's outside somewhere. He hates losing, and I know he wants a crack at the Orc bastard that killed my Inga. If you see Yraldar, make sure he isn't in over his head.\n\nFens should be along shortly. I just wish I knew where Bjoruld was.
That sounds like Yraldar, all right. He hates losing. He's kind of the warrior of the family.\n\nFens will be along shortly. I just wish I knew where Bjoruld was.

What do you think mead is? It's fermented honey! The flavor changes depending on the honey, spices, and herbs used in the process. It's a delicate balance to get it just right. \n\nYou can try some when you come back.
In a moment. I don't feel so good.\n\nToo much honey. So sticky! So yummy! So full.
Wonderful! I'm sure it will make a delightful mead.\n\nAnd another batch is ready. I would be honored if you would be the first to taste it.
A touch of this, a bit of that. Just take a good long swallow.\n\nSee if you can taste the subtle notes of Alik'r spice, wildflower honey, and late summer herbs.

What? Were you raised by an ignorant Dark Elf?\n\nShe's our goddess! Widow of Shor and Goddess of Storm! Kyne gave us life. She protects us in battle. She blesses our weapons and armor. And when we fall, Kyne leads us to Sovngarde.
Kyne is the warrior goddess, the mother of the Nord people. She watches over us and protects us. She blesses our weapons and armor before we enter battle.\n\nI wouldn't expect you to understand.
Haven't you heard? There's a war brewing in Eastmarch. Most Nords capable of wielding a weapon are already on the battlefield.\n\nIf we had the numbers, we'd march right in and take back the shrine.

Haven't you heard? The seeds of war have been planted in Eastmarch. Most of our fellow Nords are already on the battlefield.\n\nIf we had the numbers, we'd march right in and take back the shrine. But as you can see, it's just Yllolda and me.

Soldiers often visit the shrine before going into battle. How else would we receive Kyne's blessing?\n\nThe Keepers provide shelter, allowing pilgrims to pray for a day and a night. But Alhana and the others have been gone longer than that.

I don't think so. Captain Alhana is a stickler for schedules and protocols. But ever since that traveling merchant told us tales of witches and corruption at the shrine, we've been too—well—too frightened to go and check on them.

Well, he said that evil witches sacrificed the Keepers at the shrine. Used some unholy ritual to turn them inside out!\n\nDamn them for cursing our shrine and our goddess! We won't stand for it! But we don't want our insides on the outside, either.
Oh, don't get so high and mighty with me! We're just simple soldiers. If these evil witches could corrupt Kyne and her shrine, what chance would we have against them?\n\nAbsolutely none, that's what.
Go away, witch! You won't curse any more of my soldiers. If you don't leave, you'll taste my blade!
That's the most rational thing I've heard all day.\n\nHold on. I'll unlock the door. Don't let any of the witches follow you in.

You want to prove you're not a witch?\n\nMy soldiers had their souls ripped out and their minds turned to jelly. Release them from that dark existence and bring me their amulets. Nothing as evil as a Daedric witch can touch amulets blessed by Kyne.
Kralald? Really? How do I know you didn't bewitch him, just like the others?
You again? Perhaps you weren't lying after all.\n\nIf you actually gathered my soldiers' amulets, please slip them under the door.
These … these belonged to my soldiers. I never thought I'd lose my troops at a shrine of all places. We never even made it to a proper battlefield.\n\nPlease, come in. The door's unlocked.
Explore the shrine. The witches there might have a clue.\n\nThere's also a locked dresser by the bed. One of the bewitched soldiers might have a key. I'd love to know what they've locked in there.

I'm a farmer, not a fighter, and the place is still crawling with Stormfists. Could you go to the meadery and make sure it's safe? \n\nOnce inside, grab the recipe book and some fragrant herbs and rare spices. Then Roruld can start making mead again.
Before the fever took Droi, he mentioned a witch by the lake. He said she didn't attack him.\n\nFind this witch. If she's really willing to talk to you, she might have something useful to say.

No, it's just … Tavo hasn't been back from the desert like he promised he would. \n\nHe set out to find a cache of Yokudan relics from a ruin east of here. We had hoped to sell them to get out of this crushing debt.

There is a lost city beneath the sands somewhere in the rocky expanse east of the Alik'r Desert, or so Tavo thought. We've been mixed up with so many awful people lately that I'm beginning to doubt the information he got was genuine.
Excellent. Yraldar hates losing. He's loyal to King Jorunn and what Fildgor Orcthane is doing just makes him angry.\n\nFens will be along shortly. I just wish I knew where Bjoruld was.
You'll be able to reach <<1>>'s spirit, wherever it wanders.\n\nClose your eyes. Chew carefully. Concentrate on <<1>> and the Hist will guide you to him.

You picked a bad time to visit Voljar's Meadery, friend. It used to make the sweetest mead you ever tasted. But that was before the Orcthane's thugs showed up demanding free mead.\n\nTheir leader got angry and lost control. He killed the Voljar family.

I'm a farmer, not a fighter, and the place is still crawling with Fildgor's thugs. Maybe you could get into the meadery and make sure it's safe. \n\nOnce inside, grab the recipe book and some fragrant herbs and rare spices. We'll follow behind you.

More than you know. They killed my wife, Inga. She was Old Man Voljar's daughter. I plan to reopen the meadery. My brothers came to help.\n\nWe need to get rid of the Stormfists and gather the ingredients Roruld needs to start fermenting mead again.
Giants attacked our village. Many villagers died in Lower Yorgrim because of these mindless savages!\n\nI gathered the few survivors I could find and fled to this fishing camp.

I don't know. This is the first time the giants have ventured this close to the village … and the first time they've attacked us.\n\nMy brother Skorvild is assembling a force of warriors to drive off the giants. You should talk to my brother.
Investigate the building where the head Keeper worked. Last time I checked it was locked.\n\nIf you can enter the house, you might find something that will make sense of this situation.

Yes, and keep an eye out for my warrior, Burj. I sent him to retrieve supplies but he hasn't returned.\n\nIf you could also collect those supplies, it would improve our chances against the giants immensely.
Oh, yes! This is more than enough. The flower is very potent. Thank you!\n\nWith these, I should be able to reduce Droi's fever.
I put a knife in the big oaf's neck, but not before he unlocked the door. The witches swarmed inside. I had to leave Droi there so I could warn you. \n\nWhere's the Captain?
Then it's over. I'm the only one left.\n\nIt's kind of funny. We came for a blessing, but we were defeated before we got to the war. Why did the Keepers turn against us?
Wait, Keeper Ormi? By Kyne, she thinks her sons are dead? I knew her sons! I served with them. \n\nSahun survived. She doesn't know? No one told her?
You're right. Ormi and her witches destroyed my brigade.\n\nThere's something going on at Kyne's shrine, up on the hill. My guess is you'll find Ormi there. Make her pay. For all of us.

She killed and cursed my brigade and you want to save her? Fine. I'm in no shape to argue with you.\n\nSahun spends time drinking in Windhelm at the Cold Moon Inn. Helps him forget, he says. Go drag him back here if you think it will help.

I did, with a little help from these two. They found me dragging myself through the grass, making too much noise for my own good.\n\nBut I did get to gut one of the witches on my way out. Made me feel a little better.
Who wants to know?
I'd rather have her think that than know the truth.\n\nI'm a disgrace to my people and to Kyne. My brother, my ship, my entire fleet—they died right in front of me! And what did I do? Nothing!
No. My mother is the head Keeper at Kynesgrove. She'd never turn against Kyne and her people. She should honor my brother's memory, not disgrace it.
No, I can't. If what you say is true, then it's already too late for my mother.\n\nDo what you must to save those people, but I can't face what she's become.

No. I won't give up on her or Kyne.\n\nI lost faith in myself the day I lost my brother, but I never lost faith in my god. Kyne teaches us to fight for what we believe in, and that's exactly what I'm doing. I'm fighting for my mother.
Pray for forgiveness.

I won't. Kyne has shown me the way again.\n\nWithout your intervention, I would have continued to rain horror upon my people. Thanks to you, I can make amends. These soldiers will be cared for until they are fully healed.
No. The soldiers still live.\n\nThey were to become members of our Daedric coven, but I won't let that happen. Not now. Your friends are back at the Keeper's house, safe and well cared for.
The guild has accepted an unusual contract. We've agreed to eradicate Daedric Anchors when they drop from the sky. Wherever they appear, Molag Bal's minions soon follow.
As we speak, two of my guardians investigate rumored anchor sites. Merric and Aelif are the best the guild has to offer. Meet up with them outside of Daggerfall. You can proceed from there.
I want Feyne by my side wherever we live. Clearly, she's not happy in the mire, and I wasn't happy in Narsis.\n\nYou've traveled. I trust you. What would you do?
Life won't be easy for me as a former slave. Even with Feyne's help, the best I could hope for is work as a laborer.\n\nBut her family's there, and she misses them. I value her happiness.
She wouldn't leave, and she'd be unhappy.\n\nBut once my training's complete, we could move elsewhere. Maybe a city like Stormhold would suit both of us.
All I'm saying is that where I'm from, the only things that walked on two legs were Men and Elves.\n\nThis place? Half the beasts are mouths with feet.
We're far southeast of Bleakrock. It's a coastal region of Morrowind called Bal Foyen. \n\nBehind you is the Inner Sea, and across that is the island of Vvardenfell.
An Orc head on a pike will be great for business!\n\nIt shows that this meadery is safe and that the Snowpeaks are as tough as nails!

My wife loved this place. It's been in her family for generations. I want to keep the tradition going to honor her memory.\n\nMy four brothers came to help. I'm grateful, but they aren't always as useful as I'd like them to be.

In Davon's Watch? Since the Covenant invasion, it's gotten better. We've got to boil a lot of guar hides to make armor for Pact soldiers.\n\nDon't ruin our profits by driving off the invaders too soon.
I would never complain, serjo. The Pact has … done so much for us.
Because we're free now. But so many Dark Elves still see a slave when they look at one of us.\n\nThey weren't so particular about who picked their food when our hands were shackled.

It's just … it's not fair, serjo. Look at my cart. It has the finest fruits and vegetables in this land, but I must sell them for next to nothing. \n\nOnly the poorest Elves will eat food picked by Argonians.
Nothing burns like kindlepitch.\n\nWhen Davon's Watch sees the fires go up the way they do with kindlepitch, they know it's not a drill: it's the real thing.
Check the dockyards. Lineem just offloaded a fresh supply.\n\nWhen you see her, warn her about the attack. She's such a fragile lizard. Don't want her going to pieces.
Xuth, she's a crafty one! Very well. Consider the docks on alert. \n\nIf you're going to light the fires, I can help you get there. Follow me, sun on my scales.
I don't know. Maybe I can help you talk it out. \n\nWhat do you want to know?
I want to think so. I really do. But the Bretons are known for their magic. If they could find a way through or around the walls ….
I trust you. You've already saved us once. If you decide to go to Rana's aid, I know it will be the right call.\n\nI know Darj will win the day.
Captain Rana knows her business. And she has capable people with her, including my daughter.\n\nBut the docks have no walls, no defensive positions.
I did. Trynhild is proud and stubborn, like her mother used to be.
As well as you'd expect. Honestly I was surprised by some of their ferocity.\n\nThey forge us tough in the north, eh?
I need you to get me the test widget.
Thanks!
Hurry back.
Because they are! They haul our goods. They eat our trash. Guar are magnificent.\n\nAnd I have heard rumors about the Covenant. If they attack, who but the guar will carry our belongings to safety?

Control the Chimer commanders. Where they go, their men will follow. Cracks in the earth have uncovered ancient burial mounds. Search for the bones of the Chimer general and his captains. Then we can wrest control of these spirits.

By freeing their commanders. Where they go, their men will follow. The cracks in the earth have uncovered relics of the past. Search for relics belonging to the Chimer general and his captains. Then we can wrest their attention from the past.
War has wounded this land. Now it is our turn to sacrifice, so the plain can heal. \n\nMy students understand this and are willing.
Thank Kyne! I thought the Captain forgot about me.
I'm on my way.
Just try and stop me!
There is more. When you are done, go to <<1>>. Let him know we made this salve to help.\n\nPerhaps he will see we are not his enemy.
He went to the keep. Said something about a "master portal" opening at its heart. \n\nA Covenant general is coming through.
Finally! Hurry up and untie me! I want to get out there and crack some heads!
All right. I won't crack any heads until the Lieutenant says so. I'll meet you at the barracks.
I thought you'd never ask!

It's an Argonian town, full of canals, mud houses, and mosquitos. \n\nBal Foyen was just a swamp before the Great Houses donated it to their former slaves. Believe it or not, Fort Zeren used to be an entry point for the slaves brought from Black Marsh.
I must have worried her terribly.\n\nPlease, the hound that attacked me it's … sick. It's rabid.
Further up the path. If it wanders down to the docks ….\n\nMy wound might be infected. If you can take care of the hound, I'll limp back to Bishalus.
It's the biggest port in Stonefalls and one of the largest cities. Most of the trade on the Inner Sea passes through here at some point.\n\nIt'll be the first place the Covenant hits. I just know it.
Captain Hamar and Lieutenant Koruni finally sent someone to get me out of this? It's about time.
Have you come to kill me? Do your worst. I won't bow to Fildgor.
Thanks. I'll see you there.
Of course. I'm with you.
Thanks. I'm on my way.
You know me so well.

We're ready to take back the barracks. I need you to deal with the invaders' commander, the Nord called Halskar. \n\nFind his orders. We need to know what's going on. They should be someplace safe, not far from wherever you find the lout.
I had a feeling about you! Glad to see that I was right.\n\nNow follow us!
Sometimes, Gena's a strange girl. She's a master crafter. In fact, she thinks she's one of the best woodcarvers on the coast.\n\nI think she wanted to show off for me. Silly girl.
No. No other name would fit.\n\nMugs of Voljar's mead have been raised to seal bargains, toast brave Nords, and end challenges for hundreds of years. We plan to continue that tradition.
Open your inventory and right click on "Skull-Cracker's Head."\n\nThat will start the quest from an item in your inventory bag.
No idea. Perhaps their generals don't see a mud-brick village as a threat.\n\nI wish they'd felt the same way about Bleakrock.
That's why Father sent him with me.\n\nNormally, Father brings the crops to town himself, but there's trouble at home. Father didn't want anyone to bother me.
The Covenant is here. They'll strike at any moment.\n\nPut yourself between the Covenant attackers and the refugees.
Don't let her die alone.\n\nFight well. Kill that bastard.
There was one Dark Elf—a priest, I think. He stood too close. He looked up at me and started breathing funny.\n\nI let Horker take a bite out of him and I haven't seen him since.
Goblins and spiders are everywhere. I'm worried.\n\nMy father's a strong man, but … well, it's been a mammoth's age since his last raid on the Summerset Isles.
The relics you took from that strongbox were stolen from the royal tombs beneath Fort Morvunskar.
You have the heart of Ysgramor! I knew it. Go out into the courtyard and back up the Pact soldiers.\n\nYou have more experience than most of these milk drinkers, friend. Show them what you know.
Hrogar's Hold. It's far to the west of here. Beyond Ebonheart, even.\n\nIf you go, don't tell him I sent you. Just … help him. He's a proud man.
There were too many. The Daggers came off their ships in waves. Rana, Seyne, and the others held their ground.\n\nCaptain Rana got the Breton who led the sack of Bleakrock.

Let me guess. He wants to reassure me of his commitment to the Pact. \n\nWhat do the Nords call a conniver or a coward? A milk-drinker? Does he think we can idly sip that vile mead and find a strategy to win this war at the bottom of our cups?

They're still under the spell of Daedric influence. I'll work on freeing them, but it will take some time.\n\nDo not fear. I'll make sure you receive safe passage through the grove. I am their leader, after all.
Unfortunately, Captain Rana and Sergeant Seyne were both … casualties. \n\nThey'll be buried with highest military honors. And they will be remembered.

Talk means nothing. A blood contract, on the other hand, is binding. \n\nTake my dagger, Viper's Strike. Use it on any Stormfists you slay. It absorbs the blood of enemies to power its enchantment. Return it to me when it is fully charged.

Legend claims it was a gift from Boethiah to one of my ancestors—a reward for some bloody deed or another. Who can say what's true or not? \n\nBut it is a unique weapon, and one of my most prized possessions!
I see. Thane Mera is playing her political games again? \n\nNo matter. As the last racer to arrive, you get to light the starting flare. Get ready. The race begins as soon as you ignite the flare.
It's my pleasure to swim downstream with the Ebonheart Pact. This shellback lives to serve.\n\nBlood for the Pact.
Not long, as the river flows. But then, not long ago, Argonians came to Fort Zeren as slaves.\n\nNow a shellback runs a fort built on the trade of his flesh. Delicious, yes?
Captain Darj. Field promotions are the sweetest of all the river weeds.\n\nThat Nord knows what we're up against. I don't. Simple as that.
Does the river care when rocks disturb its flow? Argonians have endured worse than Dark Elves for allies. \n\nWe stand with our Pact brethren against the northern monsters and the southern Mer.
Yes. In wartime we decry the hated enemy. We call men monsters to steel ourselves for battle.\n\nIt dries my scales to hear that they would act as monsters, as well.
So did I. The last thing I remember was a terrible pain.\n\nI woke up in here, next to Droi. One of the witches was tending to my wounds. I'm still not sure what's going on.
What do I care about the village? I would leave here if I could, but my egg-kin make me stay to help fight. \n\nIt's as they say: there is no escaping the wamasu's jaws.
That's wonderful news! And we're still all alive?\n\nThis isn't how I expected this to end, but I can't argue with the results.
I follow a different stream—not my tribe's, not the Dark Elves and their false Tribunal. Some of us are still true to the old way.\n\nMy mistress calls and I must answer.

War approaches like a storm on the wind and the Prince needs our help. Why should I trust him or his champion? Perhaps some discourse will show me the measure of Irnskar's advocate. \n\nDoes war make a person stronger?

So impatient! I won't waste any more of your precious time. Actions speak louder than words, anyway.\n\nChallenge Hald Bitterblade. He's the Stormfist commander. Find him on the east hill and bring me his head as proof of your victory.

Even the strongest soldier breaks at the first sign of trouble if his will is weak. Strength serves no purpose without the conviction to back it up. One more question.\n\nWhy should I trust Prince Irnskar now?
An obvious answer. Another question.\n\nWhich serves best in time of war—a strong will or a strong body?
No, you are not of us.\n\nAs a stream finds its way to the ocean, so I will find a way to my mistress.
Thane Mera just left. She wants to speak with you as soon as possible. You can find her in her usual place, standing in front of the palace.
Another murder? In broad daylight? Thane Mera just left and she wants to speak to you. And she needs to hear about this, anyway. Hurry and meet her in front of the palace!
If you do not know, then you are not meant to know.\n\nAnd if you did, you'd be dead.

Well done, Champion! You ran like a Khajiit that was being chased by a banekin!\n\nThane Mera just left. She wants to speak to you as soon as possible. Meet her in her usual place, out in front of the palace.
Treachery. An Orcish arrow. Poisoned. I drank a potion, but it didn't help.\n\nI'm finished.
It's too late for me. You need to listen! I saw where the assassin fled. To the south, away from the city. They must be hiding nearby.\n\nAvenge me, Champion. Avenge ….
Good. Here he comes.
This is House Hlaalu's Treasury, Davon's Watch branch.\n\nWe securely store any items or money you wish to entrust to us.
By Vivec, no! What a bother that would be.\n\nNo, you can recover your stored items or gold at any treasury in the Ebonheart Pact. There's a branch in the largest city of every province.
You can buy additional storage space, but we don't charge to store your possessions.\n\nMaybe they'd try that sort of racket in the Covenant. The Tribunal Temple won't allow it in our lands.

Actions speak louder than words and the Argonians need reassurance.\n\nIf the Stormfist Commander, Hald Bitterblade, were to, say, lose his head, that would send a useful message to the Orcthane's troops.
We operate under the protection of the living gods: Almalexia, Vivec, and Sotha Sil.\n\nNo one takes anything from our care without permission.
You truly don't know?\n\nYou must know about House Indoril. They're one of the most powerful noble families in all Morrowind. Tanval is the grandmaster of the House, the leader of the entire clan.

The Konunleikar, the great games to honor the reign of King Jorunn, fills the city with mirth and good cheer. When a new king survives to his tenth year on the throne, we celebrate.\n\nBut not everyone who has come to Windhelm is in a festive mood.

The Stormfist clan hasn't been seen in a decade, but they returned for these games. Since then, there have been numerous injuries and a few deaths. And, I fear, worse things are to come.\n\nThe clan stays at the Cold Moon Inn. See what you can learn.
<The cup seems at home on the simple altar.>
You've never heard the songs of Bofinn Thin-Fingers? Ah, me. I guess they don't reach beyond old Skyrim.\n\nDa's a bard, one so good that the Solitude bards came begging. He turned them down.
Oh, aye. I'm handy with a lute and a harp, enough for this crowd anyway. Except for that Lady Aeyne. Bit of a snob, that one.
Sounds come out of my mouth, but only the stray cats like them.\n\nSometimes the highborn mages try to get me drunk. Then I sing, and … well, they find that pretty damn funny.

I'm taking the gauntlets off and granting you the authority to do whatever is necessary to deal with these assassins.\n\nI name you as Justice Carl of Windhelm. Dispense your authority as needed and deal with this as quickly as you can.

Well done! I'll mobilize the guard to prevent any more Stormfists from getting into the city.\n\nGo south and find the assassins. Bring me back something I can show to King Jorunn to let him know we've taken care of this problem.

Excellent. I will mobilize the guard and patrol the city. King Jorunn must be protected.\n\nWhen you find the assassins, destroy them. Bring me back something to prove to the King that the situation has been dealt with.
<This pedestal appears to be a good resting place for the Truth of the North book. I should find the missing page and place the book here.>
<The book fits on the pedestal perfectly.>
It's not exactly a secret, is it? The hills are now littered with survivors from Silaseli, all pulling in my alms from sympathetic travellers, leaving me with scraps.

Yes! It used to just be me and ill-fit for service act. Now I've got to contend with all of these Silaseli survivors who, in addition to being downtrodden war refugees, have the survivor-of-a-necromantic-plot pity going for them.

Well, some of the locals can be friendly and attentive. Idesa is always ready for a good time. I think she may be a bit more serious about our relationship than I am, however.\n\nNo matter. She's good for a bit more entertainment before I move on.
I just don't know. It's so hard to remember.

Generosity always clears away the fog. I saw one of those Stormfist clan ruffians with a bow flee south, out of the city. I thought it was strange that he ran just as the racer fell.\n\nHe threatened a few people, but not me. No one ever sees me.

Running errands for the princeling, are you? And I'm not your first. My aides tell me you went to see the lizard before coming to me.\n\nI suppose Irnskar wants to affirm his commitment to the Pact. Wants to drink vile mead and discuss strategy.

Talk means nothing. A blood contract, on the other hand, is binding.\n\nUse my dagger, Viper's Strike, on any Stormfists you slay. The blood it absorbs powers its enchantment. Bring it back when the dagger is fully charged.

So you have. I'd applaud, but killing a few Stormfists isn't really that significant of an accomplishment.\n\nHowever, your efforts on behalf of the princeling prove that he does wish to make amends for his idiotic behavior at Fort Amol.
Yes, true, but that's not as much fun. \n\nOh, very well! I shall work with Prince Irnskar. He shall benefit from my considerable knowledge and expertise.

And I see that you brought me his head. Bitterblade was a worthy foe and your efforts on behalf of Prince Irnskar have improved my opinion of him considerably. \n\nI shall confer with the Prince and offer my counsel as needed.
My body. The Crown of Freydis. They should both be here, but they're gone.
I'm a soldier of the Pact. I have a duty to stay in peak condition.\n\nLet the High Elves recline on couches and nibble grapes. Indulgence weakens them.
No one else needs to.\n\nThey can behave indecently, consorting with low-borns and barbarians. I'm held to a higher standard.
Who are you to ask?
What's that saying about curiosity and Khajiit?\n\nYou interrupted my exercises, and now you bore me. If you aren't here to train, then leave.
Nothing. It means nothing.\n\nI have no more breath to waste on words. If you're not here to train, leave me to my exercises.
If they're too weak to save themselves, they don't deserve to breathe.\n\nDon't soil yourself dallying with lessers. If you don't pay the price for that, your children will.
That's your misfortune, not mine.
Bala was there?\n\nExplain, dog. Quickly. Before my hand betrays my will and puts my blade into you.
What?\n\nHow do you know this? And why would you throw their disgrace in my face?

By Vivec! Bala was an Ashlander. Lowborn. A heretic. But she was lovely. Wild. Her eyes could kindle a fire in any man's heart.\n\nThe thought that my father could abuse such a spirit … that my mother could be a party to her humiliation ….
Then his affections were a lie? He brought shame on our family for amusement? \n\nWhat did my mother say to this?

They're an odd pair, aren't they? The grandmaster is so cool and cerebral, and Holgunn is so … Nord.\n\nMost know only that they served together in the Akaviri War, but our guild collects secrets. You'd like to know more, wouldn't you?

The grandmaster's unit was ambushed by those Akavir Snakes, cut off from the rest of our forces. Holgunn's scouting party came on the scene and rushed in to rescue them.\n\nHe and the grandmaster were the only survivors. They fought back to back.

Oh, by Vivec, no!

A lot of people are in both guilds. I just like to tease the finger-wagglers. Ever spoken to that stuck-up crone, Aeyne? She says, "Oh, we have such deep secrets. We are to you as you are to mudcrabs."

Pfft.
While you were in the tomb, Koruni launched a strike against the invaders from the barracks.\n\nA detachment of soldiers arrived from Windhelm just in time to help us take back the fort.
Another new recruit. At least it looks like they've sent me an able body this time. \n\nIf you're going to be useful, you first need to learn about the tools available to you.

A wise lizard. A large Covenant force has landed west of Ebonheart. Their leader, <<1>>, is known to be ruthless. She reports directly to General Serien.\n\nIf <<2>>  doesn't stand together, the Covenant is sure to sack the city.

Because we who rule Ebonheart are of House Dres. We are not well loved, even by other Dunmer.\n\nI need you to visit the Argonians, Nords, and Dunmer of <<1>>. Convince them to work together before the Covenant attacks.

First, you need to learn how to use the transit portals. These portals connect keeps under our control.\n\nUse the transit portal here to travel to the Northern Morrowind Gate. Once you get there, speak with <<1>>. He'll teach you about siege weapons.
What? Who are you?\n\nGet out of here before I raise the alarm.
Right, right. Come on in.
Sister and I came down from Dhalmora, our village just up the path. Misei, my brother Fetches-Glitter, and I run trade in Bal Foyen.\n\nNow, as I was saying. Hungry?
Ah, new blood! I'll teach you about siege weaponry. We use catapults, ballistae, trebuchets and rams.

It keeps the Stormfists from advancing, and the lack of shadows hinders their spies and assassins. So, yes, the fires help.\n\nWhile you deal with that, I need to check on a troubling report I just received.

A mere scratch, nothing more. The Stormfist clan's assassins are dead, and that's good enough for me.\n\nI guess I've become too complacent, while Fildgor's hatred has obviously deepened and festered.

When I won the throne, I was forced to exile Fildgor. He never forgave me for that. So I assume he returned to take the throne. I wonder what he promised his Stormfist and Orc allies?\n\nI need to think about this. Please tell Thane Mera that I'm fine.

After dear Nurnhilde fell in battle, my brother and I threw back the invaders. Afterward, we disagreed on who should succeed our sister. I believed in diplomacy and wisdom. Fildgor believed in rule by force.\n\nI couldn't let him take the throne.
Meet me behind this building, at the entrance to the tombs. I shall wait for you there.
Return the relics to their rightful places in the tombs below, of course. What else would you do with them?\n\nAccomplish this task and I shall forever be in your debt.
Then the same fate that befell the traitorous Nord shall befall you. Do you really wish to play this game with me, mortal?

We were near the center of the hot springs when we were attacked. I … I pushed Imhey down. It was the only thing I could do to get away.\n\nI wasn't thinking. I never meant to hurt her. Please find Imhey! I need to go!

For keep attacks, we have trebuchets and rams. \n\nTrebuchets wreak havoc on keep walls. Rams, obviously, will get you through a keep door. Keep in mind that you won't be able to push a ram into position on your own.
Offense is the best defense, right? If enemy siege is giving you trouble, attack it with a ballista. Their siege weapons will crumble in no time.
If you're looking to take out enemy soldiers directly, your best bet is to use a catapult. They have the largest damage area. Nice for hitting a moving target.
In the ruins atop that bluff. Follow this gorge to the east to reach him.\n\nIf you're able to defeat the monster, I'll name you One-Who-Breaks-Mountains.
The General's hair and his spellbook will form a link into the General's dream. Enter his dream, find him, and kill him.\n\nIf you can find <<1>> lost somewhere in the dream. Help him.

Well done! While you were gone, another task has presented itself. A task more suited to your talents.\n\nI learned that the Orcthane's troops are establishing a camp in the woods to the south. They need to be discouraged.

Fildgor's spymaster, Ramorgol, leads the effort. I want him stopped. And I want whatever orders he carries.\n\nI'll send my scout to help you. After you deal with the spymaster, my scout has information on a second target I want you to take care of.
This isn't my nightmare? This is the General's dream? I had thought that world to be the dream and this reality.\n\nYou have my gratitude. Give me a few minutes to collect myself and I'll join you.
Our home was destroyed in the Covenant bombardment. My baby daughter … the house collapsed on top of her. We couldn't reach her.\n\nNow my poor Melila just cries and sleeps … cries and sleeps.

It's an Argonian town west of Ebonheart. The name means something like "place of assimilated lizards."\n\nThe name is a slur, or it used to be. Today, my people are proud to stand with the Dark Elves. Hrm.
I understand. When I had gold and a home, I wouldn't help someone who looked like us, either.\n\nVivec smile upon you anyway, stranger.
Your generosity shames me, stranger. May Vivec smile upon you.
I wish I didn't have to beg, but I don't have any other way to care for my wife now. In her grief, Melila can't help herself.\n\nPlease, could you spare some gold?
Only what the legends say. It happened long ago, when we were … different. \n\nYou see, before we had the Tribunal to guide and protect us, we were Chimer. We were just another group of Elves.

Vivec! How many lifetimes of lament must we travel? I pledge myself on the rubble of broken hearths and houses.\n\nThe fire in my heart is fierce. Let it consume me. I say the words in your name, Vivec.
We were at war with people from the north. They wanted our lands and our gold. We called them Nedes, and their war on Stonefalls was particularly brutal. \n\nWe were defeated.

It's said that two brothers, powerful warriors, sacrificed themselves. They gave their lives to gain great weapons of power.\n\nThe Brothers of Strife defeated the Nedes, and Stonefalls remained in Elven hands.

Quiet fool! What kind of people are we recruiting?!\n\nListen to me, I am here to see if you are worthy. I don't have much hope for you myself, but such is my task. I'll lend you some of my knowledge. Are you ready to do as I ask without question?

Good, maybe there's hope for you.

Out in the street is Armando and the Dark Mother has called his name. First, assess your mark, look around him, talk to the people nearby, see if they know anything useful.

Return to me if you have any questions.
Oh, yes. The lizard and the Nord with the stump … we shall stand in front of the wave and break it with our blades.\n\nActually, I just hope we both survive. I've grown used to the dumb lumberjack.
Aye. Boots and I get along very well.\n\nThat comes from a deep, fervent love … a love of headshots at a hundred paces. Swip! Thunk.
Not sure. I think we'll hold.\n\nThe biggest surprise today is the smallest Earth-Turner.
Why are you back here already? Didn't you talk to anyone or even look around like I told you? What have I done to have to suffer this way?\n\nGet out of my face and get started already!
Three keep us, yes. She's on the other side of the bridge. The sergeant here assigned one of his swordmasters to train her.\n\nShe's got the fire of a Dark Elf and the strong back of a Nord.
Three keep us, yes. She's on the other side of the bridge. Rolunda's sparring with her even now.\n\nTryn's got the fire of a Dark Elf and the strong back of a Nord.
Perfect! You know that you have to poison him, so what better way than putting the poison into his drink!

First you must find a suitable poison, given he's a merchant there may be something among his wares that would work. Be careful not to be seen, we don't want to scare him.\n\nOnce you have a suitable poison, then place it in his drink.

Interesting….but you could use it to your advantage. Often there are things around that make your job that much easier. There are many rats nearby. Find one, catch it, then release it neaby. Dogs and wolves have a hard time not running after them.

How? What do you mean how? Find a rat, catch it, with your hands. Then open up your backpack and let it go somewhere where an animal will see it. It's not complicated. Please, keep questions like that on the inside or else I may get upset.
Very good…setting fire to his cart could be a good way to lure him away from his wine.

Given the chaotic times in which we live, merchants often trade in <<1>>, which is very useful when you want to make a big fire out of a little one. Here take some, but try not to burn yourself. And don't waste it, this stuff is not cheap.
Perhaps. Just tread carefully. This place is sacred to us, and there is only so much I can discuss.
I'm Reggr Dark-Dawn, hammer to Mistress Theran. Cross her, and you will answer to me.
Ask Mistress Theran. If she chooses to share our purpose, so be it, but I won't betray her trust.
An old story. Goblins and dreugh fighting for territory. They seem to have reached a stalemate.\n\nUntil that's broken, it's not safe in there.
The Webspinner. Mephala, princess of secrets; the Anticipation of Vivec; she who weaves the sordid web of mortal affairs. Do you know nothing of the world you live in?
That's not a question I'm permitted to answer.\n\nThe Webspinner has led us here. That is all you need to know.
Records of the time before the Tribunal are poor. The Elves were different then. We called them Chimer.
We were also different. Before we became the Nord, we were Nedes.\n\nWe marched south, seeking to free Stonefalls from the hateful Elves.

Two Elf brothers cheated. They sacrificed themselves to gain great power. They became the Brothers of Strife.\n\nThe Nedes were defeated. Thus, Stonefalls remained in Elven hands and does to this day.
Holgunn? He's as Nord as they come. A raging blizzard in the middle of summer, Holgunn is.\n\nHe served in the Akaviri War, fighting alongside Tanval, the grandmaster of House Indoril.
Would he now? And I suppose I should just jump at his command? Why should I do that?\n\nHe's demonstrated nothing but hard-headedness and brashness since before his father was poisoned.
I suppose for the sake of my friendship with Jorunn, I should give the Prince a second chance. I'll meet with him.\n\nHave you talked to the other thanes yet?

I'm not convinced he's acting in the kingdom's best interest. I trust King Jorunn. He's a man who listens and plans. \n\nBut he allowed his son to run wild and independent for too long. And look at the trouble it's brought us!
You're as pushy as the Prince. Very well. Take this dispatch to King Jorunn. \n\nHe's in the Dark Elf tent, being tended to by their healers. I want to hear what he has to say on the matter.
There were too many. The Daggers opened magical portals and came right through the walls.\n\nThe hunter, Darj, led a mighty defense. Those Earth-Turners were fierce.
Yes. The only one to survive was the wife, Aera. Her husband apparently sacrificed himself to hide her in one of the fort's towers.\n\nFear not. Darj and the others will be remembered.

Well, I expressed my concerns. I suppose, for the sake of my friendship with Jorunn, I should give Irnskar the benefit of the doubt. I'll meet with the little snot.\n\nHave you talked to the other thanes yet?

You should probably talk to Thane Oda Wolf-Sister next. Oda is a fine woman, if a bit odd. She's very fond of wolves. Very fond. \n\nShe's probably outside the fort, communing with her four-legged friends.

Holgunn's unit was ambushed by the Snakes, cut off. The grandmaster's mages were nearby and rushed to the rescue.\n\nHolgunn and Tanval were the only survivors. They fought back to back and took the Snakes down.
Don't seem very compatible, do they? A cool, cerebral Dark Elf and a loud, boisterous Nord. But they've become brothers in blood.\n\nThey'll do whatever it takes to save the Ebonheart Pact.

You didn't see it. His face … twisted and torn, as if a Daedra was trying to rip its way out of him. He charged in and tore these creatures apart!\n\nHe was about to do the same to me. Then you showed up.
Don't let his fancy looks fool you! He'll eat you, too. Mark my words!\n\nOuch! This damned bite burns.

These creatures are the twisted offspring of a vampire and their bite is just as dangerous.\n\nOnce bitten, the curse seeps into your body. It gets into your blood until the fever takes you. Then the craving comes over you—the craving for blood.

I don't know why Sildras thinks the Three would abandon us. We have observed all the proper rites. \n\nThese flowers, for one—"Roland's Tears", the rarest of the gold kanet and sacred to the Three. It is a powerful offering.

There may be a way. I need to get her back to my manor, though. If she stays out here too long, the sun will find her. Then she'll experience a pain like she has never felt before.\n\nRight now, she just needs to shut up and listen to me.

I'm just like the creatures that attacked her, except my mind is my own and I'm a little more sensitive to sunlight.\n\nNow before you do something we'll both regret, hear me out. If I'm going to save Scales, I'm going to need your help.
I don't have to open this. I know that Harvald is concerned about Irnskar. Assure him that I'm well enough to guide my son and my kingdom.\n\nTell Harvald that I will talk to him later.
I believe so. The old Nord cup symbolizes and honors the servants who performed the thankless duty of providing for the needs of each generation's royal family.
All I can tell you is that the cup holds the key. Examine it carefully and choose wisely.

Rules? Haven't you ever ran a race before? \n\nYou have to run along the outer walls of the city and must pass through each of the nine towers along the walls. One for each hold in Skyrim. The first racer to pass through the ninth tower wins the event.
Ha! My reputation precedes me!\n\nI may be half drunk most of the time, but my mind's still sharp. Prince Irnskar wants to meet with some of the thanes and the Pact delegates. Am I right?

Of course I am! But spare me your assurances. The Prince is a skeever. \n\nYou know what will convince me to attend a boring war council? Mead. Specifically, some of Voljar's Meadery's best vintages. Some crates recently arrived in camp.
"… And so he crushed some muckspunge pulp into a netch's tentacles."\n\nThere. Go, and bother me no longer.

I know who doesn't have it. Me!\n\nA crate was given to the Dark Elves, but they loathe the stuff. Ask their quartermaster. Bet they'll give it away. Or just look for bottles lying around. I don't care where it comes from, as long as it's mead.
"… bled all across the anmor and poured their shein upon the ground."
"… the mer was put to the dagon. The mora was safe to travel again!"\n\nThere, it is concluded.
You … are dulling my teeth. Please, does this go somewhere?

I need bloodfiend dust. You can get it from the creatures that bit her. Then maybe we can reverse the effects and save Scales here.\n\nI'll keep her safe in the meantime. If you can get that dust, bring it to my manor.

The book contains a collection of ancient Nord proverbs. As you can see, a page has been torn out.\n\nBut that was not the only book damaged when the Stormfists invaded this chamber. You need to find the correct page to restore that ancient book.
Read the book and any pages you find.\n\nMatching a torn page with the writing in the book should be simple enough for one of your experience and skills.
Ah, this is the stuff! Drink with me. To the Skull-King's health! I mean … the Skald-King! \n\nA Skull-King would not be a good thing.
That's the Nord spirit! Sort of.\n\nNext time though, try it like this: "I suppose one drink isn't enough!"
My brother … has all honor deserted him? Why would he do such a thing? Fildgor ….\n\nGo! Quickly! Perhaps you can catch him before he gets away. You must retrieve my mortal remains and my crown!
No. Layers of magical protection engulf the interred. Any Stormfist that tried to even touch my body would have been obliterated. Only those of royal blood could have—No!
It is indeed! And thank you for your help, my friend. As long as we hold Fort Morvunskar, you are welcome here.
Interesting….no wonder he's found himself targeted, and you can use it to your advantage. Search his goods, find the poison, I'm sure it'll be useful, as it always is.

How? You want to join the Dark Brotherhood and you don't know how to use poison? Look, take a poison, preferably lethal, then you find a way to get it into your victim. You could put it in something he eats, or something that might impale him.

Figured that out all by yourself did you? Why, your mom must be so proud.\n\nWe wear disguises to blend in. Having a disguise doesn't mean you can do anything you want. You'll find people don't like you messing around with their stuff disguise or not.

I mean if you are poking around where you shouldn't be, then you will get more than you bargained for. The disguise lets us walk among them, unmolested, but keep track of where people are and do what you need to when they aren't looking.

Ok, disguise or not, you're not getting in that strongbox with the First Mate around. So watch him, pay attention to his habits, and then pick your moment to sneak in and get the key from that strongbox. Just make sure to not get caught.

What is the matter with you? Did your parents drop you on your head? If you mess around with the strongbox with the first mate around, he'll get annoyed and may throw you in the river. If that happens, then I'll be annoyed, and you don't want that.
A spy, am I? But why? Oh, my!\n\nYou're a smart one. Whatever will I do with you?
Ahhh…so that's what the contract means…well, you know what to do, now go do it.

You are a meathead. and if you keep that up, we're going to have trouble. Try to listen this time, you get the poison, you sneak it into your mark by hook or by crook. In this case, Kyle seems like a chunky boy, sneak it into his food.

You really are simple, aren't you? Well, so how would one get on board a Blacksails ship? Oh, I don't know, maybe by being a Blacksail? Several are drunk in the bar. Think about that, if you can manage, and don't get into trouble or so help me…
That's no fun! Join me inside. We'll play a game of shells.\n\nWin, and you get Eiman. Lose, and you'll be my newest squirrel.

At least that's a start. Try to act normal, you're about to board a Blacksails ship and they don't take kindly to people poking around in their business. Our mark is here, <<1>> is pacing around. His contract requires he dies by his own devices.
That's no fun! Go on, look around!\n\nOh, and mind the bears. I never got around to changing them back.

That's for you to discover. First, find a way on the ship, then see what you can find. I'll be here if you have any questions, which I sure you will. Remeber watch the people, stay out of their way, and don't get caught as you collect what you need.

This job will be slightly different as you may need to deal with some hostile people. Iin house, guards are oblivious slouches. Unfortunately, they are also tough as nails. They'll stomp you if you rumage through their things. So, don't get caught.

What do you think? You have a brain, use it. Oh, all right, look around, talk to people, find out where Marcus is, then go from there. I know he's here, now it's your job to find out how to get at him and then how to take him out.

I haven't seen him much. I heard with all the Blacksails being killed that he fears for his life. So he's taken some of his friends and locked himself downstairs. I haven't been down there, not yet anyway.

Interesting … what a strange thing. How are we being obvious enough to stir suspicion? I'll have to talk to the Listener about this. \n\nNever mind that, we know where he is, now you have to figure out how to unlock that door.

Well, you're a smart one, here's a question even you can handle. How does someone normally unlock a locked door? \n\nDon't hurt youself trying to answer, I'll tell you: with a key. I suspect it'ss in the house somewhere. So find it.
Well, that's good news because the contract did indicate a bonus if poison was used to kill him. As before, find the poison, get it, then sneak it into something he will eat or drink.

I sometimes believe you feign stupidity just to get me angry and it makes me want to stomp you into Oblivion. How do you do that? Forget this, I'm not telling you, and futher more, I'm leaving before I do something you'll regret.

You have to be kidding me. I'd say you lay you face on my blade about thirty or forty times, maybe that'll jog your memory. Now get out there, talk to the people, look around, and don't get into trouble or so help me…
My point exactly! Like there are more rats in this place than people. The dogs love it well enough, but living with rats? Gross!

Oh! Many apologies. I'm the Ebonheart Pact envoy in Windhelm.\n\nI've lived here for some time now. I can honestly say that I know all of the city's movers and shakers. If you need anything, anything at all, I'm the one to ask.
Yes. Thank you for all you've done, but your skills are needed again.\n\nOur troops will begin the assault on Skuldafn, but we need a faster approach to reach Fildgor.
Yes. We have several of our best scouts searching the area.\n\nThane Mera found something in the hills, north of here. Those Dragonshrines are rife with passages and secret entrances.

My father is still weak from the poison, but he's recovering. I'm organizing things here while he gets his strength back.\n\nI need to regain the confidence of our Dark Elf and Argonian allies. My regrettable actions at Fort Amol have made them wary.
Speak to the highest-ranking Pact leaders in the camp—General Yeveth Noramil of the Dark Elves and the Argonian leader, Eyes-of-Steel.\n\nSee what we can do to demonstrate the strength of the Pact.

The Captain wants us to eliminate Shaman Moramat. She's powerful and she's responsible for many Pact deaths. The Captain also wants whatever orders Moramat carries.\n\nRemoving the shaman would be good for morale—especially mine.
Reports indicate that she's just east of here, setting up another camp.\n\nI think the Orcthane is really trying to box us in.
The Vanguard set up camp east of town. When Tanval went to the Spire, he took most of his troops with him. \n\nThose left behind won't like someone just wandering in. They're spoiling for a fight.

He gave me the bottle. Said it was for the tree. I thought it was skooma. I tasted it—it was bad. I fed it to a lizard. He didn't like it either. He died. \n\nThe bottle broke! How can I fill it with sap?
Excellent. What have you decided?
We'll meet in front of the healers' tent. I'm sure my father will feel well enough to join us.

We tell the story of the Silvenar and the Green Lady. Their union, and reunion, in their every incarnation.\n\n<<1>> begins and ends our stories, but she's changed things. Now the story is dark and wild, and we've no power to change it back.
Do I look like the quartermaster? Or a mead drinker? Or like I care?\n\nGo talk to Vala, if you must.
Mead? Disgustingly sweet stuff. Makes me long for shein or a flask of flin. Those are proper beverages!

Yes, that is my House, Three be praised. While the other Houses have entangled themselves in this Ebonheart Pact, our Wizard-Lords, in their wisdom, have kept us apart.\n\nPower comes through knowledge, ancient and modern.

Yes. No! I was trying to destroy the Silvenar in our story. Why in the two moons would I do that?\n\nThere's something else in the story. I feel it inside me, trying to get out. Trying to control me again!

Listen! Take the essence of the Silvenar. Guard it. Keep it safe. The Green Lady must unite with the Silvenar as always. Find the Green Lady, and save her as you saved the Silvenar.\n\nThe Hound calls me. I cannot resist!
I don't understand this powerful craving for mead. Where do the Nords put it? It doesn't seem to hinder their ability to swing their weapons, though. \n\nHere. I'm glad to get rid of these.
I enjoy a good benefit. You're offering gold for stuff my troops wouldn't touch if Vivec himself ordered them to drink it. That's a fair trade. \n\nTake these bottles. Good riddance to them, I say.

You've recovered the essence of both the Green Lady and the Silvenar. Grant that power to the <<1>>, and their story will once again be about their immortal union.\n\nThe other spinners await you below.

Of course we did. We were losing. Our homeland, everything we'd fought to build, was about to fall to these vile humans. \n\nThere could be no peace with the Nedes. I became one of the Brothers to serve my people.

Go slowly, and watch. You have your disguise, so most of these guys won't bother you. The dogs will, however, sniff you out, so you can't get close to any of them. If you need to take a rat with you and lead a dog away.
<<1>> is our retreat, our place of word and song. We protect <<Ac:2>>—a symbol of the Bosmer people. We tell tales of our past and our future.\n\nThrough our words, the Bosmer prosper.

When the Silvenar and the Green Lady unite, they forge a connection to the Bosmer and Valenwood, empowering <<Ac:1>>.\n\nSome say it was crafted by the first Silvenar. So our stories tell, which in turn makes it true!
Of course, I forgot. You did not conceive this plan.\n\nIn the base of the statue just north of here is a shrine dedicated to Boethiah. Go there and offer the heartstones to the Brothers.

The traitorous Nord from the Stormfist clan watches his troops from above. He's arrogant and vain, or so I hear. \n\nGo out the east gate, just up the path, but be careful. The area is thick with the Orcthane's soldiers.

Yes. I must be. \n\nI wonder what the lens of history will show when our people look back on this day? Will my brother and I be remembered as the saviors of our race? Or will we be known as monsters and horrors?
<The giant gestures to a nearby spot.>
Help me get free of these roots. Then I'll explain everything.
Self-preservation. Roots first, then answers.
The dead shalk over there. I killed it before these roots grabbed me. Cut out its fire gland, then use it to burn away these roots. Hurry!
Oh, good. She probably knew I got myself in trouble. I'm glad she sent you to save me.
Beneath the Night Mother are five elite members of the Brotherhood, known as the Black Hand. The Black Hand is made up of one Listener and four Speakers.

Yeah, this drunkard runs it for the Blacksails. I suspect he's in debt to them for something, I've heard that he not only runs Flash Powder, but also poisons, weapons, and even Skooma. I don't know whether to pity him or beat some sense into him.

What's it to you anyway? What would you do if the Blacksails took your family and forced you to trade vile stuff for them? I have to do what they say. The wine keeps me from thinking about what has happend to my wife and children. So leave me alone.

Other than it's a stinking Skooma pit? Or that it really irritates me that I have to be here waiting for you to do your job? Or that I hate these Skooma fiends and would rather gut them than smell them? Ok, can you please get started so I can leave?

Look around. It's dark down here, so if you put out some of the lights, then it may make it easier to move around undetected. But these guys won't leave the lights out for long, so if you  put out a torch, someone will eventualy relight it.
You've definitely got his attention. Now we need to take the fight to him. \n\nHere are the shalk glands I collected. We need to find a way to feed them to the Dremora, directly.

Nicolas lived? Traitorous, lying bastard. He was part of our circle. If he's alive, he made a deal with the Dremora. \n\nBut, you may be right. The altar may be the answer. We must get you back to the glen!
Might be. Maybe even other restricted items, like Skooma. But you didn't hear that from me.
That was no Harvest Festival. Those people are Daedra worshipers, and we're in terrible danger. We need to get out of these tunnels!
The same way you freed me. Use shalk glands to burn the roots in these caverns. That should weaken him.\n\nI'll work on planning our escape. Once you've burned the roots, come and find me.

We're directly beneath the tree. Except it's not a tree. It's a minor Daedric lord. \n\nThe tree's roots are the key. He channels dark energy through them, to keep this pocket of Oblivion from collapsing upon itself. Destroying the roots will hurt him.
You've got that right! We work hard and relax harder. You're welcome to join us.\n\nA bard wandered into camp right before you, so we'll have music as well as mead!

The cooks, Kalogar and Heggvir, are arguing over what to serve for the party. They're up near the main hall. Kalogar favors steaks. Heggvir wants to make goat stew.\n\nThey want me to choose, but I hate to pick favorites. You decide.

Oh, did he? I'm sure he'd want something extraordinary for the party. Not just a slab of meat that's burnt on the outside and raw in the middle. Something worthy of a chef of my caliber.\n\nA savory goat stew would do the trick.

Berj and the workers want meat! Seared, salted, and still bleeding! I ask you, what goes better with a cask of mead than a good bear steak? Nothing, that's what!\n\nHeggvir probably wants to make that fancy goat stew of hers. She uses herbs.

You simpering fool, try not to waste anymore of my time or my flash powder. Here take this. Don't waste it this time. Use it, do what you have to, and then get this job done. I grow tired of watching you bumble around.

Is there a reason why you need more? I gave you more than enough, so I'm sure you don't need anymore. I'm sure you can fulfill your contract without me having to give you more of what is mine. You couldn't possibly have bungled its use, could you?

Look at it! So adorable. So plump. And so delicious! I'll start cooking right away.\n\nOne more thing. Berj wants more mead. Would you talk to Ralduf Wolf-Kin? You'll find him by the storeroom where we keep the mead. He has the key.
Key? What key? \n\nOh, what's the use! It wasn't their fault. They didn't mean to take it! I won't say any more. I won't tattle on my friends.

The key is lost. But I know where it is. Sort of. One of my wolf friends snatched it off my belt. Swallowed it in one gulp.\n\nI refuse to kill them for a key. They are beautiful, noble creatures. A woman who once loved me treated them as kin.
Do what you must then. They ran to the north. They're probably not far.\n\nAh, my noble friends. I can't bear to watch this.
Thanks for all your help. Now relax and have some fun. The party's already started!\n\nYou know, we could use some music, though.

Well done, friend! I mean rare! Good and rare! I'll start searing these steaks right away. \n\nYou know what goes good with bear steak? Mead! And Berj needs a few more barrels. Go see Ralduf Wolf-Kin at the storehouse. Get his key and get the mead!
You can blame a woman for that. Love of my life. \n\nWhen I was a lad, I hunted wolves for sport and to keep them away from my family's farm. Then I met Oda. What a fine woman!

We spent a summer together. Too short a time in these northern climes.\n\nShe was from a noble family. Taught me to respect wolves. She claims them as kin. That's why I took the name. And why I won't kill them. Oh Oda, I miss you so much!
I suppose I have made them wait long enough. \n\nI like to build anticipation in my audience. Makes the reaction that much better.
Yes, yes. It's time. \n\nA bard must always gauge the audience. You want them relaxed, receptive. If they are too deep in their cups, they can't appreciate the wonderful tones of my lute.

For a story as important as the well-being of the Silvenar and the Green Lady, we spinners will tell the story together.\n\nBut <<1>> has gone on her own, so the story's not yet strong enough. She may want to use you to increase its power!
Oh, there is. He's the one not dressed like a royal worker. \n\nHe's upstairs, last I checked. Why don't you go up and ask him to play us a song?
She's let you into her story, and you aren't a spinner. That means you don't need to follow our rules.\n\nFollow the story with her, and set it right again. For all our sakes!

I have always been within this story. I am the Silvenar, the immortal spirit of the Bosmer. I protect and nurture the heart of our people.\n\nYou … have met one of my incarnations, I think. If that is true, then I would know you as friend.
Yes, even I have felt the change. The story seeks to destroy me. You must not allow this!\n\nI will summon my allies, but I cannot do this alone. Will you help?
Safe? None of us are safe. All the threads are breaking apart. The Worm Cult awakens the Oathbreakers! The necromancers enslave the spirits of Ouze!\n\nYou must stop this!

The Worm Cult wants to enslave the ancient spirits in this mire.\n\nThe Bosmer buried here spurned the Green Pact long ago. Shapeshifters, unwilling to submit to Y'ffre's will. They are eternally trapped and eternally protected.
It's not too bad. Just a scratch. A little bit of rest and I'll be fine.
Seyne and I will be reassigned, I imagine.\n\nTryn says she wants to continue training, despite her recent loss. I'll ensure she has a place with us, if I can.

Not sure. Never expected to be in the military, least of all as a commander. The lads want to keep up the fight. I expect we'll muster to the east with the rest of the troops. \n\nJust hope we can keep everyone safe.

How do these things always start? Impetuous youth!\n\n<<1>>'s son <<2>> wooed my daughter in secret. I told her no love would last. It was not long before the Drublog shaman uncovered their trysts. Then, the bloodshed began.
Mortal trappings are unimportant. I must see this place kept safe.\n\nHave you burned away the heartwood? Is it out of the Worm Cult's clutches?
Then you've thwarted the necromancers' plans to enslave the creatures of Ouze. They've one recourse left to them, but with your help, I can stop it.
No one knows who struck the first blow. It was a battle. Chaos. Blood. Anger.\n\nNow the Drublog swear they'll kill us all. If only they'd just leave! By Z'en, we will not give up our homes!

You will need the strength of a powerful Oathbreaker in order to overcome the necromancers.\n\n<<1>> was the strongest shapeshifter of those who refused the Green Pact. Ever since the Totem of Y'ffre bound him here, he has protected the other spirits.

You'll have to defeat him in battle to disperse his excess energy. The totem will absorb the wisps left from his exertion.\n\nHe's aided the spinners for centuries, but still, he's more likely to fight you than help willingly.

The warlord who leads these brigands, Lob the Cleaver. He's inside, along with the deadly Orcs that are always at his side. They're a nasty piece of work, the lot of them.\n\nEnter the arena and sound the horn. That will tell the giants it's time.

Lumber. Maera and I ran the lumber mill. She told me you saw it when you first met her. That was a nice little stead.\n\nBefore we went out to Bleakrock, we used to be traders, peddlers. I think it's time to pick up that life again.
I took a hard knock on the head. I don't remember much from earlier today. \n\nThere was drinking and singing. And pie. I think I remember pie.
Show them no mercy!  \n\nOh. I think I need to lay down for awhile.
To be honest, I wasn't seeing all that clearly before the attack. I admit I had a drink. Or seven.\n\nI remember there was singing. Then the screaming started. Or was it screaming and then singing?

No. Still waiting for orders to muster out. Shor's Bones. If you'd told me a year ago that I'd be Captain in the Pact miltary, I'd have called you a damned liar. Hope I can remember which end of the blade to hold.
No, I wish I could. That poor bard, I think I remember him yelling, too.

You saw those things out there. They're mindless monsters—as ugly as they are evil and only interested in killing and feasting.\n\nDo you really want Scales out there attacking people? No? That's why I put her in a cage.
I just hope they put us back in the fight! Having my rank returned is like a gift from the Three. \n\nNow they just need to tell command where to send us.
Not sure I'd phrase it that way, but yes. We've been through so much. I'd be mad as Sheogorath if I wanted to turn things out like this.\n\nBut it's good to be back.

Wherever the forces of evil prey upon the innocent, wherever souls are stolen and bodies shriven, wherever a people cry out for justice, there goest I! \n\nI mean, this whole eternal servitude business is rather nasty, don't you agree?
Very well. If it guarantees your assistance, I'll set her free. But what happens after that is on your head.
