I swear by the blood of my clan and my clan mates, I only want to help her. She's safe here. I'll protect her for as long as she remains with us.\n\nAnd if the cure fails, I'll teach her to control her urges.
There's a chance, but it's just that. A chance.\n\nThere's no guarantee she'll survive the process. I've seen it kill as often as it cures. It's a risk, but the alternative is far, far worse.
You made the right decision. I promise I'll do everything in my power to help her.\n\nWe'll watch over her. If she doesn't improve, we'll make sure she doesn't succumb to the bloodlust.

I see, I see. A rescue, is it? Well, that's a different kettle of fish, isn't it? Hmm.\n\nThere is a cistern that drains into the waterway. The door is locked, but that's not stopped me before. Why don't you meet me there and we'll see what's what?
Dibella's garters, why? Lovely grounds, no question. But it's positively brimming with angry cultists carrying rather large weapons!
Yes, it's a terrible state of affairs.\n\nIf only I could remember ….
A bloodbath! <<1>> killed them all! So much screaming, echoing through the entire valley!\n\nHow could this have happened? Is this the workings of the shaman?

I'm trying, really I am. I remember coming out here to get some fresh air. For a bard, he sang like a wolf with its paw in a trap. No, he wasn't that good. \n\nI got tired all of a sudden. Probably drank my mead too quickly.
I'm sorry. That's all I've got. Bad singing, falling asleep, and getting stabbed.\n\nBut other than that, it was a great party!
One pint of mead. Not even. Half a pint at best. My memory is all hazy.\n\nI sang along with the bard. His lute was just enchanting! Next thing I know, I wake up, covered in wounds. It's a mystery!

Such a blur. I might have seen … things … moving around. Not quite human, but too small to be trolls. Not ice wraiths, either. Those things leave ice all over the place.\n\nYes, that's it. We were attacked by small, not-quite human … things.
I don't think so. The guildmaster has everyone focused on this Daedra contract.\n\nI prefer to keep flexible. I'm open to whatever chance may bring.
Yep. Boots is the best kind of hunting partner: he's deadly and quick, and he keeps his mouth shut.\n\nWe're hoping to stalk some big game in Deshaan. Right, Boots?
I'm not really sure. Some kind of disease, as I hear it. The local troops are having a hard time dealing with the situation.\n\nCommand thinks a group of irregulars might be able to help.

Praise Y'ffre! This means a lot to me!\n\n<<1>> hasn't returned from her hunt. When she goes out, she normally returns the following morning with her kill, but we haven't seen or heard from her in days.
I'm still worried about Aera, but at least she has Rexus to keep her company.\n\nTryn will make a fine warrior. She's taken to army life like a fish to a stream.
They tested us out before giving us an assignment. Hoknir hit every impossible shot they threw at him. That really impressed command. \n\nI'm glad he's watching my back.
Deshaan's closer to Black Marsh, so I think he's looking forward to it. He keeps complaining about his dry scales.
I was worried at first, but with some training, she's proven deadly. \n\nAnd she's practically adopted Trynhild. Good woman.
The chief … she went mad. Ulagash and I … we tried to stop her.\n\nAnd <<1>> … he used <<2>>'s blood! The chief's son!
<<1>>'s husband, <<2>>, headed out with <<3>> and <<4>>.\n\nI've prayed more would help find <<1>>, but we've seen both werewolves and Houndsmen near.

<<1>> usually hunts near the southern falls. That's where <<2>> said they'd start the search.\n\nIf she encountered a foe, she might have loosed her entire quiver defending herself. I'd keep an eye out for arrows and follow any signs of struggle.
Of course I am! My lion form suffices to dispatch trespassers. Well, usually.\n\nNow I ask the questions. Who are you, and what do you want?
The Totem of Y'ffre? Indinael would never part with that, not while she lives!\n\nBut she doesn't live, does she? I would feel her presence if she did. You didn't steal it from her, did you?
They must have taken her! Wouldn't a father know if his daughter died?\n\nThe Drublog destroyed our entire village! Monsters, all of them—my daughter's actions never warranted this madness!

Hah! I know you can't; the totem is fully charged! You're not as much of a pushover as I first thought. Look for me again soon. Maybe I'll give you a hand.\n\nBut you still need to find <<1>>. I don't know what she's cooking up!
Well, why don't you ask her yourself, and stop bugging me?\n\nYou've drained most of my spiritual essence with it. That is as much of a contribution as I'm willing to make.
We're going to Deshaan. Command isn't sure what's happening exactly, but there's some kind of outbreak of disease.\n\nThey think a group of irregulars will be able to do some good there.

They're worried about Aera, but Rexus has adopted her. I'm sure she'll be fine\n\nDenskar and Littrek are able soldiers, even if they haven't had much training. A few more weeks in the field, and I'm sure they'll be hardened veterans.
She's the heart of the group.\n\nWithout Molla, we'd still be a ragtag group of refugees. She's an incrediblely capable woman.

I asked them if they wanted to leave, but they're trying to forge a new life on the road. Before they moved to Bleakrock, they were traders.\n\nNow they're champions of the coin, getting us new supplies for the journey! Who would have thought, eh?
He's a talented cook. He's been keeping us fed since we left Ebonheart. His sister kept him too sheltered on the island.\n\nNow that he's got to earn his keep, Eiman's doing just fine.
<The altar is empty. Someone must have taken <<1>>'s body.>
<A crude sword. Not the sort of finely forged weapon commonly carried by bandits or soldiers.>

We turn my father into dust and end his tyranny once and for all.\n\nThe hunters are merely a distraction. If we deny him their blood, he'll grow curious, perhaps even vulnerable. He'll want to know who interfered with his plans.
<A streak of blood stains the surface of the rock, as though someone was dragged across it and scraped an exposed patch of skin.>

Yes, yes, Jaruk always has a plan.\n\nThe bloodfiends hunt by scent. They have the hunters' scent and await the command to strike. If we mask the scent, the bloodfiends will lose interest and wander off. The hunters will be saved!
In a haze of memories, that bard and his music stand out like the sun on a clear winter's day.\n\nBut where is he? I don't see a bard among the living or the dead.

I agree. Search the area and see if you can find him. People remember music and the bard is missing. A coincidence? Maybe, but I don't like the sound of it.\n\nI'll stay here to help the wounded and keep watch over the camp.

Take this liquid. It is a gift from Jaruk's close friends, Cello and Harp. Don't ask what it is. You don't want to know.\n\nSplash it on the hunters. Make them smell like something the bloodfiends won't want to eat.
Yes… up the path… fearsome looking creatures. Not human, that's for sure.\n\nI tried to follow and help.

Oh, they'll hate it. They'll probably try to kill you!\n\nIt's best if you rough them up a bit first. Show them who's stronger. Then splash it in their faces. As long as they end up very smelly, the hunters should be safe.

If I were to guess, I'd say Falmer. I've never seen them before, but heard tales. Pale and wasted, but vicious. \n\nThey were dragging the bard up this path. There's a cave up a ways. My friend Vestrek was following them.

I'm one of the royal workers. I followed the creatures that dragged off the bard. Rieklings, unless I miss my guess. They haven't been seen around these parts in years.\n\nThere were too many of the foul creatures. I couldn't help him.
No, I'm not all right! These creatures dragged me here after slaughtering half the workers in Cragwallow.
I may have answers. Ask away.
I don't speak to giants. I know them.
I'm a friend of the giants. Let's leave it at that until we get to know each other a little better.

The same reason anyone fights with giants. They're stupid. \n\nFildgor Orcthane leads the Stormfists to war against his brother, the Skald-King. Along the way, they revel in malice and destruction. That's just one of the consequences of war.

Well. About that. I'm not actually a bard.\n\nI found the lute. It's enchanted. I play a few notes and my audience falls asleep. They wake up later, a little confused, a little groggy, and missing some gold or an item or two. Perfectly safe.
What? You wouldn't leave me in here? I had no idea the lute would attract the rieklings! It never did before! And I never wanted the workers to get hurt.\n\nI'm not a violent person.
What? He seemed so harmless. And kind of talented. What a shame.
I'm not a criminal! Well, not a dangerous criminal. \n\nAll right. I swear by the snow on my mother's grave, I'll turn myself in.

Thanks to you, their plan for an army of shapeshifters has failed. Now they must put all their energy into creating one powerful creature.\n\nYou must get what they need before they discover it. I've hidden it in a sack nearby. Go, quickly!
The farms. Ulrich led us here when the Reachmen attacked. No one enters the ruins, he said.\n\nHow I wish he'd been wrong!

When the woods were new and wild, we were shapeshifters. It was necessary back then, since the Valenwood had not settled on one form either.\n\nY'ffre gave all of the Valenwood a form and a purpose. But some Bosmer refused the gift. They remained wild.
They dragged us away. One by one. Laughing, they were. I curled up in a corner. So small, barely breathed. They didn't notice.\n\nPlease. Help the others. Like Ulrich would've, had he lived.

One of the farmers. Used to be in the Lion Guard. Men respected him, and women admired him. To see him fall … to know what they did.\n\nThey boiled him. I heard them say so. Boiled. Evil. So much evil.

I am the Green Lady, the immortal aspect of Bosmer strength. I take orders from no one.\n\nThe Hound told me the story, and it excites me. If he's a part of this, then so am I. The story shall include us both!
I don't know that name. Hmm. Yet, I feel something when you say it. As if this were all a dream ….\n\nNo! He said there would be temptations, charlatans, liars! The beasts will take care of you!

I am the herald of Z'en, keeper of the balance. I collect and assign the debts of the faithful. I am here to stop this cycle.\n\nThe Drublog paid many times over for the death of <<1>>'s people. His curse will only feed Mauloch's fury.
My, aren't we an inquisitive one!\n\nI'm not used to so many questions. But I have been spending a lot of time around giants lately, and they're not really big on conversation.

He offers his blood as sacrifice, calling upon the forest itself to mete out justice. But it is not justice he seeks. It is vengeance.\n\nZ'en will not have more blood shed this day, but one death is better than many. If you cannot stop him, I must.
What can you do? What you must.\n\nMathragor has put his trust in you before. You have the chance to guide him away from this path.

<<1>> has lost sight of Z'en in his grief. He sees no other recourse but more death.\n\nMy master grows impatient with this world. I will not hesitate to strike him down if he defies the will of Z'en.
The spoken word can shape the future in ways stronger than the tears and blood of thousands.\n\nIf your words ring true, perhaps <<1>> will see a new path.

Then all is lost! The stories tell of a dark creature, fueled by pure essence at its core. That is Spinner Indinael.\n\nShe will become a terrible undead being, a servant to command the legions of the Worm Cult. They make her their puppet!

Wait. You have it … the totem of Y'ffre! She must have known, must have seen her fate! She's sent you to save her!\n\nYou need to get inside, and quickly! The Worm Cult's already started their plans. You must use the totem to stop them!
Use it on the creature you find inside the caves.\n\nThe Worm Cult controls it now, but the totem may be able to break their power over it. Or even destroy it entirely.
Thank you! You can use a gland from the dead shalk over there to burn the roots. Then I'll answer any questions.
Ох.

I think not. Such a path fits neither my role nor my disposition. I am a friend, not a foe. Besides, this is your mission. I wouldn't want to steal your glory.\n\nBlow the horn and the big folk will come. They'll help you.
It was easy enough to slip inside thanks to all the chaos you caused. I decided to wait for you here.
No! You can't leave me with these creatures!\n\nIt's not my fault those people died! It was the lute! The lute!
But the rieklings grabbed him before he finished robbing us. \n\nSo where's the lying bard now? Did the rieklings kill him?

Oh, it's not just you. Others have tried to help Valeric. They either see how futile their task is or they fail.\n\nMy master wants to explain this to you. You don't have to make any decisions right now. Just hear him out.
He will meet with you in his manor, the one to my left.\n\nNo harm will come to you at this time. Majorn gives you his word.
You deny an invitation from my lord? You are foolish, just like the ones before you.\n\nMajorn shall know of this. You have made a terrible mistake this day.
Giants and wolves! I don't know why they attacked us, but now my home is gone.\n\nPlease, spare some gold?

The threads pulled in every direction. They threatened to snap. My death was the least of the evils possible.\n\nWith your help, I challenged the story. And with your strength, I was able to change my fate.
You're most kind, stranger. I appreciate your generosity.
May the Eight watch over you anyway, you miserly milk drinker.

A weapon is only as good as its wielder. Not one in a hundred could have used the totem to direct their will.\n\nThe totem is sacred among the spinners, so it must be returned. I've asked Gwilon to thank you personally for your aid.
Monsters! We tried to stop them! Strange hunched creatures. They had that bard fellow. He was still alive.\n\nThey carried him up the path.

Spriggans once guarded these burial grounds from those who would intrude or escape. The necromancers slaughtered them, and stole the heartwood from their corpses.\n\nYou must burn the heartwood before they can use it to control the spirits!

My father won't risk going outside. It's too dangerous. The sun is deadly to his ancient form.\n\nNo, he'll send his thrall, Tunus, to see what went wrong. We need to catch my father before he returns to the crypts and locks the doors behind him.
<Lothgar appears peaceful. His ancestors surely welcomed him to Sovngarde.>

Rala will sneak into my father's manor and wait for Tunus to return. She'll deal with him. I need you to enter the crypts.\n\nRala may be a vampire, but she's still young. She wouldn't stand a chance against an ancient.
Rala is quick. She can blend with the shadows. Slitting a thrall's throat is well within her capabilities.\n\nBut someone more powerful than her needs to confront my father.
I couldn't resist the urge. I had to feed. Valeric keeps us locked away. He doesn't let us feed, not naturally, not like this.\n\nI need blood to survive. Why deny me this pleasure?
You can't stop me. No one can stop me.\n\nI'll continue to feed. I'll grow strong. I'll defeat the ancients!
No … I … you're right. What am I doing? I've fallen, just as the ancients wanted us to.\n\nHere. This is the key to the crypts. Tunus had it. Go in there and end this. Please.

It's been so long. You just don't understand. How could you?\n\nI need this to live! Valeric starves us. We mostly feed on animals, finding criminals when we can. There's a reason we're not as strong as the ancients. We must grow stronger.

With Worm Cult blood and bone! Kill them all. They must pay for their transgressions, just as we have.\n\nThe Green Pact imprisons us, but we'd rather sleep in the tar forever than serve the Worm Cult for one day.
Monsters. Whatever they were, they weren't people. Short, scuttling creatures of some sort.\n\nOh, poor, dear Kalogar.
Yes, it all becomes clear. She chose you to set her mistake right. And that you must do, brave one.
You must defeat him. Only then will the Green Lady turn her gaze to the Silvenar.\n\nBe wary, for he is a formidable foe. <<1>> tells it in her story.

No. Kalogar told me to run, so I did. I ran behind the hall and hid until it was all over. I can't believe Kalogar tried to fight them.\n\nIt was all so confusing, I didn't see much. I wish I had more to tell you.
Y'ffre, confer your blessing upon this place, that we might behold the bravery of the Green Lady!

This is incredible! How'd you get these images in there? If I'm reading this correctly, this is beyond anything the Mages Guild can do!\n\nI wonder what other amazing things might be hidden in here? What do you think?
Thank you so much! I can't wait to show this to Raynor.
You're right. Those stuffed robes wouldn't last an hour down here, but we do it all the time.\n\nThey'll pay good money for what we find, and we can remain our own bosses!

This is incredible! There's a map of every Dwemer ruin I've ever heard of and a bunch I haven't! There's even mention of a massive underground city. I thought that was just a myth!\n\nI want to follow these leads, but the Mages Guild ….
You really think so? I love exploring old ruins, and there's enough in here to last for years and years.\n\nI wonder what Raynor would say?
Yeah, you're right. We shouldn't abandon our dreams just because of a new opportunity presents itself.\n\nThat's not very magely behavior.
Z'en has decreed the payment in kind must end. <<1>> defied his will.\n\nI took his life to restore the balance, but it was not without cost. Z'en tires of such mortal feuds.

You killed Majorn, not me. Don't take this the wrong way. We're grateful for what you've done, but you did it.\n\nYou destroyed a tyrant who could have built a formidable force, one strong enough to challenge the Skald-King. Now that won't happen.
Of course. It wasn't your fault. You did what was necessary.\n\nIt's just a shame to lose a friend. May she rest knowing that my father's tyranny has ended.

Valeric opposes me because I embrace my true nature. I take what is mine without thought or hesitation.\n\nValeric questions everything and tries to fix our people. He deprives them of what they need to survive while telling them there is a better way.
Not really, which is odd. I wasn't in my cups or anything. I don't think I'd even finished my first mug of mead.

When they finally taste fresh blood, the fever takes hold. They become wild, savage monsters more dangerous than anything I create.\n\nMany call me evil, but at least I do not feed indiscriminately. I feed to survive. I feed to increase my power.

Valeric must be stopped. My people may kill hundreds, but when his followers lose control they kill thousands more.\n\nI hide nothing from you. I am not a good man, nor a good father, but I shall not kill my only son. For that, I need your help.

Valeric will use the hunters in the area as he attempted to use you. They must be destroyed.\n\nTake this rune. Use it on one of my bloodfiends. It will follow your commands. Make it do your bidding. Take it and slaughter the hunters.

If that is your decision, so be it. After you leave here, know that I am your enemy. When next we meet I will tear out your heart and drink your blood.\n\nAnd that shall still be better than if one of Valeric's followers becomes crazed and attacks you.
Nasty, biting bugs are useful! Their insides spit and burn. Bring such parts, and I will clear the path.
Shield your eyes! If the acid splashes upon you, all would weep.\n\nBehold, your path is clear!
They've slaughtered my family and laid waste to my home! They will answer for their crimes!\n\nIf Z'en won't help me, I will find another that will give me justice!
I will not! They must all pay. Do you hear me? They must pay with their lives!\n\nI'll suffer no Drublog on these lands as long as I draw breath!

<<1>>! If I could see you once more, I would know what to do!

She would weep if she saw me now. She only knew kindness and love. Why did I survive while she died?

You're right. I must find the balance again.

Ah, but that is where you are wrong.\n\nValeric will continue to spend every moment of his existence attempting to end mine. I grow tired of it. I have shown you a small glimpse of the power I can give you. Help me and I will give you even more.

My son hides in the crypts beneath this manor. Use the trap door in the next room and go to him. Then end this.\n\nMake his death quick, if you would. He is my son, after all. I do not want him to suffer.
It is the power to steal life, the power to consume an enemy's energy and make it your own.\n\nThis blessing I give you. Do not waste it.
It isn't right for a father to thank the murderer of his son. Instead, I shall simply say that I appreciate what you've done.
Indeed! The soldiers call this place Jorunn's Stand, for King Jorunn is determined to stop the Orcthane and restore peace to Eastmarch from this very encampment.

There's still some tension. The Prince made accusations when the King was poisoned, and that certainly hasn't helped matters.\n\nTo his credit, though, Prince Irnskar seeks to make amends for the strained relations.
The assassination attempt hasn't hindered the Skald-King's ability to command, if that's what you're asking.\n\nThe Dark Elf healers tend to him and he grows stronger every day.
Yes, I'm sure you do.
Eveline. I was part of a circle of mages testing the boundaries of conjuration. I'd say we were wildly successful. Mortal terror notwithstanding.

An interesting outlook. Learn by losing.\n\nI think the Stormfist Commander, Hald Bitterblade, might learn by losing something, as well. His head, for example. At least his troops would learn a lesson—to fear the Ebonheart Pact.
A thoughtful response. I do worry that Prince Irnskar's insular thinking is dangerous and goes against the edicts that formed the Pact.
A minor Daedric lord. On this plane, it manifests itself as a giant tree at the center of the Hallows.
No, this wasn't the work of any Breton god. The being we're dealing with is a Dremora Lord. It adopted the guise of the Bad Man to lure the gullible into its trap.

We're not in Glenumbra anymore. The Hallows and these tunnels exist on another plane. A pocket realm. The more the tree grows, the larger this realm becomes. If left unchecked, it could destroy half of Glenumbra.
Deep beneath the roots of the tree.
I can only assume you were sacrificed. I don't know why you weren't immediately consumed. The souls of the living are like mead and bread to this thing.

The search for divine knowledge. Natural curiosity. Lots of reasons.\n\nLook, if we knew it would corrupt our circle, impersonate an old harvest god, and drain the souls of the living, we certainly would have reconsidered!
Like I said before, it's probably just superstition, but as my great-uncle Nichodemus used to say, "It couldn't hurt!"
We're a friendly folk here in The Hallows. We share our traditions with all who would respect them. And it's always nice to see a fresh face at the table!

The tale is well known in these parts. In his youth, High Kinlord Rilis was a hero, instrumental in bringing order to this region.\n\nHowever, Rilis' thirst for power, which drove him to perform great feats, was his undoing.
Our religion is ancient, but its followers are few. Most Nords call us cult and worse things.\n\nBy helping your king, perhaps we can show everyone what our faith truly stands for.

The necromancers bound and bled me. I sent the other spinners to get help, but it's too late to save me now. My tale comes to an end.\n\nBut that's not important. The Worm Cult's come to deny the shapeshifters their eternal slumber.
Why, the Harvest Festival, of course! Go on inside and see for yourself. Talk to <<1>> if you'd like to join in the festivities!

When he isn't asking inane questions, the Dreamwalker makes the same claim. So many questions! He actually believes we turn into bugs and fly! \n\nWith your king's life hanging in the balance, I hope you haven't put your trust in the wrong place.

As you say. Before your friend can enter the eternal slumber, we need to enhance the king's life force. Bring him back from the brink of death long enough for the Dreamwalker to slip inside. \n\nOtherwise, the journey will kill them both.

Horrible creatures, but their blood has its uses.\n\nI'll open the gate to our ritual grounds. Please don't disturb the monks who pray there. Your king sleeps on the center platform, where our High Priest administers to him.

And do you see her? She's not here. She's out there somewhere, communing with her beloved wolves. \n\nHow can I protect her when she runs off into the woods without so much as a by-your-leave? She's a maddening woman! Maddening!
The kind that'd be creeping around a dank cave and talking to hooded men. Mark my words, they're up to something.
Canis cap mushrooms tend to grow on logs. I think I saw some on the big log right outside this gate.

Last I saw, she was east of the camp. Communing. With wolves. But she does have a connection to the creatures. I've never seen one so much as growl at her.\n \nOf course, you won't be so lucky. But if you kill any wolves, she won't be happy with you.
Let me guess. He wants me to attend his very important war council with our very important allies from the Ebonheart Pact. Is that what you came here to tell me?

I'll think about it. I need to see what my wolf kin think of all this.\n\nOn the one hand, they don't like the Orcthane's troops invading their territory. On the other hand, they don't appreciate our presence here very much, either.
<The broken bottle is partially filled with fresh blood. Whoever did this must be nearby.>
<The cart is filled with putrid corpses. It has seen much use and seems ready to fall apart.>
<Amongst the papers is an old, torn map. There are bright bloodstains on it, as well as a fresh mark. It indicates a cave entrance along the ridge line.>
<This well now contains water, but some viscous slime was recently mixed with it, perhaps as part of a ritual.>
<<1>> meant to kill me, but <<2>> stopped him. He took the blow meant for me.\n\nPlease, you have to end this. Tell my father … no more blood!

I was a good soldier once. I was a faithful follower of Kyne, along with the rest of my family.\n\nAfter the disaster, I was disgraced, no longer fit to serve in the regular army. So for a time, I sold my blade to the highest bidder.
You ask more questions than my mother, and she's the Keeper of Kynesgrove!\n\nLeave me to my drink or I'll show you how good a warrior I used to be.
What does it look like? I sit here and I drink until I collapse. Then I get up and drink some more.\n\nIt's the only way I can endure the memories.

Simple. You get into the Shrike camp and find the key to their ship's hold. I've even got a "volunteer" to give you a disguise.\n\nMeet us at the edge of the dock. Sal's got another hare-brained plan to sneak us all aboard.
Don't forget your disguise! Get what you need from this one, and find that key. Look for the captain's tent, the biggest one in there.
This is a fort, not a roadside village.
Besides, strange things are happening at the logging camp next door. Something to do with spriggans and trolls, I hear.\n\nEven the Orcthane's troops refuse to go near the place.
Just give the word, and I'll follow.
If anyone can beat that damn Stormfist, it's you. And that would certainly boost the morale of our soldiers.\n\nBut be careful. Fildgor doesn't choose his leaders lightly.
So my monks tell me.\n\nWe don't usually deal with Daedric magic. We can keep King Jorunn alive, but we can't restore him. Your Dreamwalker is our best chance. I hope he's done this before.

You brought what we need. Now the Dreamwalker must enter the Dreamstride. From there, he's on his own. My magic can't help him.\n\nPray at the totems of the Three Old Gods. Perhaps they will show you the Dreamwalker's progress. Then we watch and wait.

Something has sparked the Dreamwalker's magic as well as our own.\n\nWhatever haunts King Jorunn begins to flow into this world as well. As the poison spreads through his body, he fights back harder. It's pushing the forces into our own plane.
The Dreamwalker was most likely injured by the blast of magic. He was the last chance we had. Your king can't do this on his own.

It's an Ayleid ruin. The stormwardens use it as a sanctuary for the Sphere of Storms.\n\nMight I say this isn't the best time to be chatting away? The Sea Vipers aren't going to wait on us before getting to the sphere.

Me, I'm just a soldier. I keep the area secure for the stormwardens. Usually. I left for a bit and came back to see the Sea Vipers tramping over the ruins.\n\nBeen a while since I've had some exercise. I arranged my warmest welcome for our invaders.

They're Bosmer who've sworn to protect the sphere. Some say they learned how to use the sphere from the Ayleids themselves.\n\nThey use the sphere to defend the coast, tend the forest, stuff like that. Sort of like monks who control lightning.

Some magic Ayleid device. The entire ruin was built around focusing its power. \n\nDoes a good number with controlling the weather, in the right hands. The stormwardens use it and protect the sphere, and have for centuries.
At least someone else had some luck. Take the key inside and find the stormwardens. With this last <<z:1>> in their possession, they'll be as safe as torchbugs in amber.
I'm as well as I can be. With my father slain and my family fled.\n\nPlease, will you help us?
My husband, Gjakil, and my two daughters, <<1>> and <<2>>, ran into the hills. The cultists were right on their heels.

A spinner is not without defenses. I am a storyteller—I simply changed the narrative.\n\nI hid the thread of its existence behind a tangle in Ouze's story. The Worm Cult, intent on their own plot, didn't unravel the knot.
Seems the Shrikes shoved them into random crates in the warehouse. <<1>> can sniff them all out.\n\nYou've met him. He's our monkey.

Easy! Give him a cue, and he'll do the rest! Just let him take the lead.\n\nWe'll hide ourselves on the ship, and leave the hold unlocked for you. You both meet us aboard later. This'll be easier than I thought!
I've got them all tucked away, waiting for my signal. \n\nYou got those supplies from the warehouse, right? I think I can use them right about now.
<Agnedir's wounds indicate the draugr killed her.>
<Kerthor was definitely killed by the draugr.>
My husband Selgaard? Is he all right? Why isn't he with you?
Shor's bones! Why did I offer shelter to those travelers? I should have known better!
Thank Y'ffre, he's alive then!\n\nWe could've beat the Drublog ambushers, but they brought in a creature. Huge. Ugly. Nothing we did hurt it.
I couldn't say. I fought back, but the Drublog warriors hit me over the head. Everything went blurry and I woke up here with Sariel.\n\nPerhaps she saw more.

Tridi, Nedrek, and the others work in the main chamber, down the east tunnel. That's where the ore is.\n\nAvoid the west tunnel, though. It's full of trolls, and they're worse than the Orcthane's thugs!

You must understand, we support King Jorunn. We're loyal to the Skald-King.\n\nWe refused to deal with Fildgor's agent. That didn't go over so well. He needs ore to craft more weapons, so his thugs barged in and seized the mine.
He did? You've seen the Silvenar? Praise Y'ffre!\n\nThey attacked us on the road. Raen fought the Drublog ambushers, but they knocked him out cold. I was no help, but I saw everything.

A Drublog shaman chanted words from a ritual book, and energy flowed from <<c:1>> into these giant crystals.\n\nThe shaman kept chanting as they carried <<c:1>> away, but we were separated from him. Please, we have to get that book and stop the ritual!

Ah, Stormhold! This was our home until the Dunmer … oppressed us. Now it is not a proper Argonian town, not like it once was. \n\nStill, it is a good place for Shadowfen's vicecanons. Here, they can deal with all kinds and still live in comfort.
Anything he can. He promised he would be careful. He's very clever, but I worry.\n\nHe's the foreman. He feels responsible for the miners.
They've spent blood in defense of their land. They have to finish what they've started.\n\nI … I'm going to challenge their chieftain. It's the only way.
Our magic allows us to call forth aspects of the Three Old Gods—the Fox, the Bear, and the Wolf. Spirit forms to help us perform tasks beyond the scope of mere mortals.
The Fox is crafty and quick. He enhances the speed at which we do things. Makes us faster, more agile than we are on our own.\n\nIf you are in need of speed, you may want to call upon this aspect.
The Bear is strong, mighty. A protector. He enhances our strength and shields us from harm.\n\nIf you're in need for protection against overwhelming odds, the Bear should be your ally.

The Wolf is sly and observant. Ferocious and deadly. She watches and waits for the best opportunity to strike. With her aid, our eyes see the hidden weaknesses of our foes.\n\nIf you seek the weakness in your enemy's armor, call upon the Wolf.

<The silver writing glows through the muck and blood covering most of the pages. The ancient runes are indecipherable, but there are pictures.\n\nOne prominent illustration shows the image of a glowing runestone. The image pulses as if alive.>
I'm Owen Pavelle. I'm part of an expedition that was sent to explore this barrow. My team was cataloging the ruins when the draugr attacked.

I am. Saw you helping some of the others. I've been sneaking around, sabotaging what I can. Sometimes I pretend to work. Sometimes I wear their armor and go where I want. They don't really pay that much attention.\n\nDid my wife, Eitaki, send you?
Excellent! We're strong and we're determined. With weapons, we can rout Fildgor's troops. \n\nTheir leader, Magister Osanne, has been investigating the deeper chambers. And that worries me.

We were in a rush, so we hid our notes in an urn on the scaffolding in the next chamber. We left an ore sample in there, too. But there's a chance Osanne found it.\n\nYou could disguise yourself and grab the notes.
It wasn't a Drublog; it stank of sulfur. Could've been an ogrim, though my experience with such creatures is thankfully limited.\n\nSomehow, it kept the Silvenar from using his power to escape.

I didn't see it clearly at the time, but I've had visions of it ever since. It's a Ritual of Unbinding.\n\nI could feel <<c:1>>'s energy slipping away, as if he were being drained of his very nature. I've never felt anything so cold or evil.

Crates of uniforms are scattered throughout the mine. There's a crate right there.\n\nJust be careful. They don't notice you if walk around like you own the place, but Osanne's guards might be more alert than the average Stormfist thug.
What of the others? Did you find my brother-in-law? My young cousin?
Don't worry about me. Save your concern for the next dead thing that walks through that door.
I pray that the others are safe. Tell Selgaard I'm alive and still fighting.
Kyne have mercy on my family.
They seemed friendly enough, and we never turn away those in need.\n\nBut they asked the oddest questions about Bonestrewn Barrow. They were much too interested in that old crypt!
They wanted to know how old it was, how big it was … if it was dangerous.\n\nPeople visit the barrow from time to time. I didn't think anything of it until ….
I helped one of them steady his pack. Owen was his name, if I recall.\n\nA helmet spilled out. A Covenant helmet. I should have done something then.
They said they were going to Windhelm, but I watched them go.\n\nThey headed toward the barrow.

Their leader, Valcent, he saw what happened. He thanked me and said it was time for them to depart.\n\nThey headed out without another word. I knew something was wrong, but I was just happy to see them leave.

The poison polluting his body. It makes him reimagine his fears and lets the nightmares tighten their grip.\n\nHe will continue to seek a way out as long as the dream continues. You must follow the King deeper still.

Continue to pray to the totems. You already set one of the fractured parts of his spirit free.\n\nYou need to be quick this time. If the King knows he's in danger, the dream will collapse behind him and strengthen the nightmare's power.

Three burial urns chain my spirit to this cavern. I cannot leave while they remain. Destroy them and I can escape before the cultists bind me.\n\nTwo urns rest in the lower reaches of the cave. Destroy those first.

Daedric rituals often come at such a cost. Obviously, I should be sacrificed. I'm the weakest of us.\n\nWhen the Drublog attacked, Raen fought back while I was captured straight off. I'm an advisor, not a warrior. The Silvenar needs warriors.

Heal me? Through my own mind? You would use Daedric magic to cure me? That's the very magic that harmed me.\n\nYou don't need to do this. I've fought an army that claimed to be invincible and emerged victorious. Fildgor's poison won't stop me.

If you think I'm a good advisor, listen: freeing the Silvenar won't be enough. His power's drained. The Drublog guarding him won't just let him walk out.\n\nRaen can help you. Use the runestone on me.
It's a hard choice, but a simple one. It's my duty to die protecting the Silvenar. I failed once, so badly I can't fight anymore.\n\nThe Silvenar needs advisors like Sariel.

It means I never saw the exit. How will I find it in my dreams? The fires—I remember the fires. They must be the key.\n\nIf I don't survive, you must get word to Almalexia and the other Pact leaders. The Pact must not fall!

No! Raen's good in a fight, but even his skill pales before yours. If you use the runestone on yourself, the Silvenar will be restored, but weak and in his enemies' hands.\n\nDon't throw your life away!
Try it, and the last thing you see will be me wresting it from your hands! Sariel and I can't get the Silvenar out of here. Only you can!\n\nLet one of us do what you can't. Don't fail the Silvenar!

I was so helpful till now. No, I've seen you fight. If anyone can get the Silvenar out of here, it's you. And Sariel. She's young, but wise.\n\nThe Silvenar needs such advisors, not near-dead warriors. Sacrifice me.
Valcent's some sort of necromancer. He turned poor Ophelia into a monster.\n\nHe plans to raise an army of the dead for his own foul purposes.

All right, I'll confess. This is all wrong. I joined the Lion Guard for a little adventure, but this isn't what I had in mind. \n\nValcent's mad! He intends to raise an undead army. He has no orders. He's totally gone rogue!
Pull the switch to my left. It will unlock the cage and open the door to the ceremonial chamber. That's where Valcent is doing gods-know-what. \n\nBut please, don't pull the switch to my right.
What? No! How can you say that?
It was terrible. I locked myself in here for my own protection. Valcent killed the rest of our expedition! He killed every last one of them!
When the Pact was formed, three heroes of the Akaviri War—Hrondar of Skyrim, Servyna of Morrowind, and Heita-Meen of Black Marsh—were chosen to keep the peace here.
I'll be a thrall, under his command. I can feel the pull of his will already.\n\nSoon I'll be your enemy. If you defeat me, I'll be free. If you fail, he'll take both our souls. Try not to fail.

Earlier, when we were running through the compound, I noticed four rays of light coming from the towers surrounding the main building. I think those are coming from the binding stones. We need to disrupt them to stop the ritual.

It's wet, swampy, and the damp makes me itch under my armor.\n\nThis was the Dunmer toehold in Black Marsh, back when they were enslaving Argonians. Now the town's trying to find a new line of trade, with the vicecanons based here and all.

The runestone. When Raen … was sacrificed, it changed into a rune key. If you invoke its power against the binding stones, you'll sever their connection to the ritual. Sever all four and the energy drain will cease. <<1>> will be free, but weak.

Sariel, when she spoke of the ritual, she mentioned binding stones. When we were moving about the compound, I saw rays of bright light streaming from the four towers surrounding the main building.\n\nPerhaps those are what she meant.

Ah, Stormhold, this was our home until the Dunmer … oppressed us. Now it is not a proper Argonian town like it once was. \n\nStill, it is a good place for Shadowfen's Vicecanons. Here they can deal with all kinds in comfort.

When you … did what you had to do, you turned the runestone into a key. Using it on the binding stones should break their connection to the ritual.\n\nOnce all four connections are broken, the energy drain should cease. <<1>> will be weak, but free.

How to say? They … oversee Shadowfen. Two were heroes in the Akaviri war: <<1>> from Morrowind and <<2>> from Black Marsh.\n\n<<3>>, from Skyrim, is new. He replaced <<4>>. He is new, so I cannot speak about him.

The Argonians have a history with the Dunmer, so somebody thought it would be smart to have three Pact vicecanons run the town: <<1>>, <<2>>, and <<3>>.\n\nMostly that means the Nord makes sure the other two get along.
What choice do I have? Even with Sovngarde's power to aid me, I lost. The Crown of Freydis rejects me. The thorn in my side became my undoing.\n\nYou've won. What will you do with me now?

Good to know! We've been doing what we can to confuse and delay them. Jomund has been sneaking around, passing along information. Sometimes he's even in disguise.\n\nThese thugs are easy to fool, but they're scary when they get angry.
<<1>> came from Morrowind after the Pact's unification. <<2>> is also a relative newcomer to Black Marsh. Her history may be in question, but her aptitude certainly is not.
Jorunn, my soft, cowardly brother. How did you find someone with such strength and honor to represent you?\n\nI accept your decision. I will face Jorunn's judgment.
And so it ends. At least I die in battle. A true Nord could ask for nothing more. Tell my brother how I died. Perhaps he'll learn something from me, after all.\n\nNow finish it!

How to say? They … oversee Shadowfen. Two of them were heroes in the Akaviri war—<<1>> is from Morrowind and <<2>> is from Black Marsh.\n\n<<3>> is from Skyrim. He replaced <<4>>. He is new, so I cannot tell you about him.

Best news I've heard since this started! \n\nYou need to find my sister's husband, Jomund. He's up ahead, sneaking around in disguise and causing all kinds of trouble for the Stormfists. He needs to know what's going on.

Nurnhilde is safe and my brother … dead? I am all that remains of our family. My brother was honorable, if misguided. Despite his crimes, he will receive a royal burial.\n\nI will mourn later. Now, there is business to attend to.
I almost wish Fildgor had not survived his encounter with you. Now I must deal with my own brother.\n\nAnd there's only one possible punishment for treason.
True. But I find no joy in ending my own brother's life.\n\nMove back and let me get this damnable duty over with.

Such a shrewd, calculating proposal. It's not the Nord way, but the idea has merit. If we could make him work with us, think of what we could accomplish.\n\nAnd, I confess, it would break my heart to put my brother to death. Thank you for your counsel.
What do you wish to know?

Proud, stubborn man. Jorunn's at his weakest points now. On the edge of life and death. You have only one more chance to enter the Dreamstride, one more chance to break the nightmare and set him free.\n\nIf you fail, you will both be lost.

Three of them oversee Shadowfen. Two were heroes of the Akaviri war: <<1>> from Morrowind and <<2>> from Black Marsh.\n\n<<3>> is new. He's from Skyrim. I don't know much about him. He replaced the late <<4>>.

That's good news. While you were doing that, my miners drove off most of the Orcthane's troops. Milk-drinkers, every last one of them! We'll clean out the stragglers.\n\nI have one more favor to ask of you.

That chamber, the one where we found the mysterious metal … we left some of the ore in there. But the trolls, they seem attracted to the stuff. They won't let us near it.\n\nDeal with the trolls and recover the rest of the ore. I'll meet you outside.

The King's dreams try to deceive him. You need to be on guard. Look through the shadows and observe.\n\nIf you fail to convince the King that what he sees is a lie, he will perish. And when he dies, his dream ends—and so do you.
At last, some good news! Z'en willing, <<1>>'ll pay for his treachery. But we have more pressing concerns at the moment.\n\nThe enemy is at our gate and knocking most vigorously.
I can try. What do you want to know?
I am the statue, what remains of it after the desecrations of time and vandals.

Give me time. The Drublog and the Houndsmen can't have missed your disruption of the binding stones. They'll be here soon, driven by <<1>>.\n\nKeep them back while I regain the energy they stole from me. Only then can we leave.

Once, we called him stormwarden. Now, he's nothing more than a petulant child.\n\nHe demanded we use the sphere for selfish purposes. He even spoke of turning against the Thalmor! We refused and cast him out, but before he gave away his <<z:1>>.

He believes the Sea Vipers are his allies, now that he's turned over his <<z:1>> to them. Ha!\n\n<<2>> will pay for his crimes, and the punishment will be swift and terrible. The storm is not a forgiving master.

We're the last scraps of an ancient order. Once these spheres were throughout the Ayleid realms, across all coasts this side of Cyrodiil.\n\nThe Ayleid are no more, but we've persevered. Time, like the storm, waits for neither man nor mer.

It is an ancient artifact created by the Ayleid. They used it to protect their shores, water their crops, and speed their ships.\n\nThere were once dozens of them, but we know only of one. We guard it with our lives.

The sphere is waning. If it isn't recharged soon, our defenses will fall.\n\nWe have a source of power available in the storm atronachs. Their thunderstones should be enough to maintain the sphere. We'd be in your debt if you could obtain some.

Through the door and down the hall. They gather throughout the ruins when the sphere is active.\n\nOnce you have the thunderstones, look for two receptacles in the great hall. That's where we drain power into the Sphere of Storms.

Run! We'll use the extra power to seal these ruins completely. If you don't get out quickly, you'll be stuck with us until the invasion is over.\n\nTell Mariel we'll send for her when the doors reopen.
Do I look like I'm getting on well? I bet you still have a house with a stout door to lock.
It's not enough the damned giant went stomping through. Now the undead stalk the streets!\n\nWe've complained to the soldiers, but they say their commander doesn't have time to deal with it.
No, no. <<1>>. He's on the south side of Riften, at the Fighters Guild.\n\nWe should have stayed out in the woods. Sabre cats I can deal with. Walking corpses? Just … no.

Reading and writing fascinate me. I helped <<1>> collect old journals, Drublog and Bosmer both. I kept a journal too.\n\nI hid it from my father. He's so angry at the Drublog. I don't think he'd understand.
Do I look like I'm getting on well? I bet you still have a house with a stout door to lock.

Of course I'm alive. The magic that allowed you to enter the Dreamstride would have disappeared if I died. Frightening thought, though. To die in another's dream.\n\nI'll consider this while you find the King.
This again? Look, the cult is gone. I was dispatched to aid the city with all of five soldiers. The rest marched off after the giant. I don't have the manpower to investigate rumors.
No, no. <<1>>. He's on the south side of Riften, at the Fighters Guild.\n\nWe should have stayed out in the woods. Sabre cats I can deal with. Walking corpses? Just … no.
It's not enough the damned giant went stomping through. Now the undead stalk the streets!\n\nWe've complained to the soldiers, but they say their commander doesn't have time to deal with it.

He followed a pretty young woman. She looked familiar, but I couldn't place her.\n\nShe ran up the steps and the King was right behind her. But something strange happened. Specters appeared. Very vicious.

Be careful. These spirits are more violent and powerful than the others in the dream. Drawn from the King's strongest memories.\n\nIf you fail, we all die horrible, horrible deaths. Probably very painful. Please try to avoid that.
If you want to waste your time, fine. I won't stop you from looking.
Of course! All of us have, not that the damned soldiers will listen to us. The smell's how you know they're coming. Death and rotten fish.

I've studied the Drublog! Z'en has so much in common with Mauloch, if you look past the surface.\n\n<<1>> will know what to do. Maybe his words will convince my people to live peacefully with the Drublog.
No, Shor take them. The soldiers won't do anything. They say we're making it up.\n\nWait. Do you smell something?
Of course! All of us have, not that the damned soldiers will listen to us. The smell's how you know they're coming. Death and rotten fish.
No, Shor take them. The soldiers won't do anything. They say we're making it up.\n\nWait. Do you smell something?

<<1>> told stories of these journals, and now you bring them to me. Hm.\n\nSince the earliest days, blood and toil have known no end in our hearts. Mauloch demands a blood price. Z'en's price is no different.

Such an impertinent question! I suppose there's nothing for it.\n\nI am master of Ilayas, and once, the stormwardens. Without me, this place is a shadow of its former glory. Invaders would have never crossed this threshold under my command!

One of the Falmer approached our tent. It was menacing, but kept a safe distance. Aronel lost his composure and ran. I heard him shouting as the Worm Cult captured him.\n\nHe should have listened to me!
Up the ramp behind me. The cultists will have taken him to their camp. Would you rescue my foolish friend? While you keep them busy, I'm going to slip out of the cave and head towards Ivarstead.
Help? If you're lucky, I won't kill them myself! \n\nThey've severely taxed the sphere so much, I was forced to wake. And now I am forced to defend what they cannot.
It's my fault. I brought our best blades to Shor's. The recruits I left behind never had a chance against the savagery of the Reachmen.
I agree. I've recovered sufficient magicka to create a portal out of Jathsogur.\n\nAre you ready to go?
Don't take too much time. I must leave now; if they somehow re-energize the binding stones, I'll be trapped again.\n\nUse the portal or not; it's up to you.
It was a trick. Conjured by that creature you killed. Nurnhilde is dead. Her beautiful soul is gone.\n\nI'm all that's left to lead my people. I cannot fail them!
I know. There's so much to do, and I cannot allow my brother Fildgor to complete his plan. Not while he has our sister's body and her crown. \n\nNothing good will come from his machinations.

Unusual? How unusual? Is it stone? Metal? Crystal? The suspense is killing me!\n\nActually, no. The suspense is rather mild, and I'm already bored. People always want me to examine this or study that. Like I don't have enough to do!
Glows? Attracts trolls? Well, let me see it, then. \n\nThis might be more interesting than I originally thought.
Yes. <<1>> and I have run this farm for almost forty years. Our children, and their children, do the work now. \n\nWe just … we used to enjoy the quiet life before all of this.

The Crown of Freydis, the symbol of our people, can only be worn by the true heir of the throne. It won't fit upon an unworthy head.\n\nFildgor believes that he can merge our sister's spirit with his own, making him worthy of the crown.

If the crown fits, it proclaims Fildgor as the true King. Not even I can oppose the one who wears the crown.\n\nThat's why Fildgor must be stopped. He can't be allowed to desecrate Nurnhilde's spirit.
According to the legend, "Just as our crops feed on the soil of the Hallows, so too will the Bad Man feed." \n\nAlso, it's a tradition. Humor us.
How dare you? I'll make your blood boil and hear your soul scream! I will torture you till eternity ends! I will—
Don't rush me. Better yet, make yourself useful.\n\nBring me the Varla Stone tincture from over there. And be careful with it! It is rare and rather unstable.
How dare you challenge me, mortal? I'll sear your flesh with molten iron! I'll—
Aye. Even in death the Companions yearn to fight for Skyrim. Would you enter battle with a warrior, a firemage, or one of our talented healers? Choose, and they will fight by your side.
Well chosen. This lass stood with the crew of the Kaal Kaaz in their final battle.
Aye. Wisely chosen. This lad stood against the might of Red Mountain, and sings the tale to this day in Sovngarde.
This lass tended the crew of the Krilot Lok. She met her end facing the Argonians of Black Marsh! Wisely chosen.

I told you it was unstable! I'm sure the feeling will return to your fingers … eventually. \n\nI need one more thing. Ovuld's Study of Metallurgic Anomalies. I was reading it by the river while I was getting some sun. I think I left it out there.

Analysis takes time! Proper procedure must be followed and careful study can't be rushed. And sometimes I perform random experiments just to see what happens. \n\nNow hurry! I need to check Ovuld's notes. I think he mentioned this ore.
Something gnawed on the cover. Ah, well! The uninitiated are always hungry for knowledge.\n\nLet me see what Ovuld has to say about this metal.
Nonsense. Careful attention to detail and advance preparation always results in stable, safe experiments.\n\nNow let's test this mysterious ore.
A zombie? Oh, aye. One tried to take a bite out of the horses. I put it down with a shovel. It's behind the barn.
I'll take that and burn it. We've had enough trouble with Fildgor and his followers to last a lifetime. \n\nThanks for intercepting this.
You live? Of course. His anger came after you were consumed in flame.

Of course! That may be the only way to defeat him!\n\nQuickly, now. Burn the shalk glands at his altar. He'll be forced to consume them, and they'll burn him from the inside out. You must hurry. It's our only chance!
Soon after you were sacrificed, the Bad Man became enraged. He turned on us. Rained death upon the grove. It was consumed in fire. \n\nAnd now you return. What did you do?
Of course. I always honor my promises.\n\nEnjoy the power!

You dare raise your voice, slave?

But you speak the truth. That is how history will remember me, if I do nothing. I can't lend my sword, but I'll shield you from others who've awoken.

May the storm see you unbroken.
I can still feel the touch of their knives. The pain. \n\nI feel the call of Sovngarde. But I will help you before I go.
Right behind you.

We've run afoul of him before. The Hound was behind the trouble in Dra'bul and my kidnapping and imprisonment in Jathsogur.\n\nHe wishes to supplant me as the Green Lady's rightful consort. We have to stop him, for the sake of the Bosmer people.

Desperate. We definitely need your help.\n\nThe Silvenar told us there's some sort of mystic barrier keeping him out of the city. I can't see it, but I do see the Houndsmen in the ravine below, carrying those damn silver shards.
Ha! I appreciate your confidence, but I'm just a scout.\n\nI'll help as I can. When the Silvenar says the barrier's down, I'll see you in the city.
I don't know much that you haven't been told. My guess is the Houndsmen carry them to somehow reinforce the mystic barrier, but I don't know for certain.\n\nI'm sorry I can't tell you more.

It's not an evil creature, but a bound spirit, tied to the wards that protect the city.\n\nDefeating it won't destroy it completely—in fact, it will probably re-form soon after—but it will temporarily sever its connection to the wards.

It'll give the Silvenar an opening to project his will into the city. The Silvenar, remember, is the spiritual essence of the Bosmer. If he can extend his essence inside the city, he can help unravel the wards.\n\nBut you'll still need the spinners.

No one wants to risk the hostages. They split up families and killed a few of us to show they mean business. \n\nI lost my best friend when she tried to get to Fort Amol. They killed her as she ran down the road.

The Stormfists are crafty. They put relatives on different work crews. They'll hold workers as hostages while their families rest, then switch and do it all over again. \n\nI don't want my family harmed. I need to be here when the shift changes.

Yes, but we didn't hurt them! Please, I'll tell you everything I know if you just let me go.\n\nI … I was there when the youngest of them, <<1>> was taken. I can tell you about her! Just promise you won't kill me.

We welcomed the Drublog! We shared a single cup in friendship, and this is what they return?\n\n<<1>> was honorable and just, but <<2>> changed that. And all the others followed his bloodlust! Nothing more than animals, they are!
<<1>> is the youngest of the three. She acted like she knew she was going to be taken.\n\nThey imprisoned her in her home, surrounded by all her nature totems and strange-smelling herbs.
We channel the touch of the Lord of Brutality. All across the wood, the Reachmen are being transformed. Stral himself undergoes the ceremony inside the central ruin. \n\nNow please kill me.
We made a deal with the Reachmen. They unleashed the giant, Sinmur. And we promised to bless them with the touch of our dark lord.
I think so. My memories, my being, rushed back with the <<1>>'s destruction.\n\nUntil you came, I'd thought my crew lost and our secrets revealed. They didn't get it, did they? The manifest?
Rotmeth! It takes years to make. Precious stuff used in ceremonies. Weddings and the like.\n\nThe mammoths seem to have gotten into it, though it's anyone's guess how. It's kept high up in the trees!
Bound up the soul that once pumped this organ. The Worm at your feet refused to answer my questions. So we'll need to try a different approach.
We make it from fermented meat, seasoned with thunderbug organs. I can't give you the exact recipe, naturally.
Of course. Would you have us drink wine made from fruit, as the Altmer do? That's disgusting.\n\nNot to mention a violation of the Green Pact. We could hardly serve such a thing at a wedding.
Yes, it symbolizes the muscle of the boar, the power of the forest, the strength of the Bosmer people. No wedding can take place without it!
Does my mind play tricks? You say <<1>> survived?

Your story is a dark one, my friend. But perhaps the light will shine brighter for it.\n\nHengorn was a dark soul with no bright tale to tell. Thanks for cutting his story short. What can I do for you? For the Silvenar?

Yes, very much! They're physical manifestations of the rebirth of the Green Lady and the Silvenar. With them, we can set the tale on the right path again.\n\nWhen I recover, I'll see if I can attune them. Thank you.
I'll do what I can, but we need to add a few more twists to the story. Spinner Caerllin is captive nearby. He hasn't broken, but something's amiss.\n\nFree him, and together we can do something.

It was the Hound! He forced us! I saw him capture <<1>>. The spinner's in his prime, and let the Hound know he'd fight him with all his strength.\n\nBut the Hound still bound the spinner, right in his home.
Shor's bones! What with the giant attack and all, I completely forgot about all that. \n\nMy sincerest apologies. Here you go.

The warrior-spinner focuses on the present. He sees a great battle with the Green Lady and the Hound to bring her to her true lord, the Silvenar. His bonds are tied to that sight.\n\nAnd the spinner already claims victory. He laughed as we bound him.
The spinners defied the Hound, so he bound them with elements of their own strengths.\n\nHe even bound <<1>>, the strongest of the three. She'll grow even older in her prison!
Sorry. We had some trouble and there hasn't been enough mead to fill the order. I'll get it on a cart as soon as possible.\n\nHere. Take this bottle. It's my way of apologizing for the delay.
She's in her home, and hardly noticed us.\n\nShe lives in the past, seeing patterns of ancient times replaying today.
Oh, such embarassment and folly!\n\nIt's a horror perpetrated against the dignity of Dunmer culture.
Excellent! And just in time, too.\n\nWe must welcome most important foreign dignitaries to Windhelm. Here. A set of cultural garb just for you. Please put these on.

What's it matter to you? Have business with the King, do you?\n\nThen stand in line with the rest of the peasants. Seems like every alley-rat decided to show up and whine about something when they heard the King was coming. But he's not here for that.
I just want this all to be over. We're not used to dealing with so many different groups all in one place.\n\nAll right. Find Thod and I might let some information slip. We'll leave it at that.

The King shows up with his honor guard and all the Pact officials, clearly up to something important, and you just expect me to tell you what that is?\n\nDid you always get milk when you whined for it as a baby? Be off, I need to find one of my guards.
I lead. I bear the blame. Tears and mead are for another day. Wish she was here, though. We need her right now.

The Reachmen are in the vault beneath the Hall. Our most treasured artifacts are down there. Reach shamans have placed one of those damned spellshields on the door. \n\nTirora would be able to … wait.
I must ensure the Hall is cleared. I need you to go into the vault. Kill any Reachmen you find and check on the relics we guard there.

You must mean that drunken idiot who tried to keep up with Jeggi. He wasn't even in the same league.\n\nWhatever he was drinking was pretty foul, though. Smelled more like wet kagouti than sweet mead. I think it might have been Argonian.
He wandered toward the river, carrying a few bottles of that vile Argonian beverage.\n\nHe's probably still down there. I'd wager he's either passed out or nursing a bad headache right about now!

She is? Yes. Yes. Her fire burned my future away; I couldn't see the story unfold.\n\nHmm … I still can't see. Her fire took my physical sight. But I still live, and my tale continues while hers is over. Can it be erased?

Yes, but she'll be difficult to rescue. Her tormentor is Ungolor Swordsnout, a Green Hunter who refuses to change out of his werewolf form. He's brutal.\n\nHer tree stands east of here. Free her, and we three spinners will help you.

Why? You've done a great thing. My inner sight clears. You rescued Einrel; her tale gains strength as we speak, and I can hear her.\n\nShe gave you good advice. All three spinners must be freed to help the Silvenar.
Don't want to. Want to sleep. Perfectly good dream … oh, Naryu … I love you, Naryu ….
Drinking? Why would you say that? \n\nNow put on the cultural garb! We must look dignified!

What? No! Of course not. Well, maybe a little. The mead you brought looked so good. I took a teeny swig to calm my nerves. I can't help it if the bottle was so small.\n\nBeing master of ceremonies is hard work. I bet King Jorunn drinks plenty!

I'm sure it was one of the other guards. There are a lot of us and we're known to relax with a bottle of mead or two. When we're off duty. And never to excess.\n\nSo really, I wouldn't worry about it.

Both the Commander and Thod headed toward the barracks on the west side of town. If you hurry, you should be able to catch up with them.\n\nThen you can go get a drink and relax. Seems like you could use it.
Yes, thanks to you. A few bites here and there, but I'll recover. The tale continues, though the storyteller has changed.\n\nDoes that surprise you?

Ha! Truth in narrative! Amusing.\n\nWell, I'll endeavor to speak plainly. Events can unfold in one of two ways: either the Lord Huntsman and the Green Lady continue to bond and plunge the Bosmer into feral darkness or ….
Sorry. A pause for dramatic effect.\n\nOr, you go to the throne room, defeat the Green Lady, kill the Huntsman, and restore the Silvenar. Plain enough for you?
I said "defeat," not kill. It's called nuance.\n\nThe Huntsman twists the tale of the Green Lady. Her power keeps the Silvenar at bay. Defeat her, and the Silvenar can reach her.

The Arch-Wizard, and a few others along the path ahead. With your help, we should dispatch them easily.\n\nThe wizard is channeling energy into a <<1>> attached to the captain. I heard them say something about memories.
Don't stray too far.
<The ornate door is locked shut, but shows signs of recent use.>
<From the other side you hear a quiet shuffling, a pause, and then a loud click as the door unlocks.>
<There are three items positioned along the frame of the door that look out of place. They move slightly when pressed.>
What are you talking about?\n\nPeople always mistake me for someone else. Now please, I must be going.
Thod? Oh yes. The burly one. Of course.\n\nMy apologies, I'm recovering from a sickness. And I forgot something in the barracks just now. Sorry, I must go.
<There's another click, then the sound of stone locks sliding open.>
<There is another click as the carved sword gives.>
<There is a small click as the shield is depressed.>
Have you been drinking with Thane Jeggi and the soldiers?

What? All of this in Marla's house? You have to understand how strange this sounds. You're telling me that the Commander I was just speaking to is actually dead?\n\nAnd there are others? Including two dead Marlas?
<A scattering of crudely made arrows, perhaps dropped during a struggle. It appears that whoever attacked Cragwallow used this path.>
Ask anything, friend!

Ah, pickled fish …. Sorry! You make Rigurt's mouth water.\n\nWe placed the order for stinky fish with fishermonger in Lower Yorgrim. Cross the bridge south of here and follow the shore east to the village.
Finest mead in all of Skyrim comes from Voljar's Meadery.\n\nGo out the gate and cross the bridge. Then follow the road west along the river to get there.

I sent my worthless assistant to retrieve fancy Dunmer garb from my vault at the bank. It's in the north part of city. You can't be too careful with your fancy pants, right?\n\nAnyway, he never came back. Go look there for tiny little Dark Elf man.
Haven't you heard? Giants attacked Lower Yorgrim!\n\nGo speak to Eiraki in the tavern over there if you want more information.
Maybe. Hopefully.\n\nLots of folks say the land is cursed now. Nords can be pretty superstitious, you know.

It's pickled fish! No one actually eats this stuff. It's more of a tradition than a food group.\n\nI've even seen a starving horker refuse to eat these stinky fish! It might be good for keeping the wolves away, though.
<This tankard matches the others from the mead hall. Maybe the bard used this one. It's a bit battered and dented now. It seems that someone was dragged up this path.>
You need to ask Haraldar about that. I just fill the orders. He's right outside if you haven't spoken to him already.
Not since you put that Orc's head on a pike. You'd be surprised how much business the Orc's head on a pike has brought to the meadery. Thanks again for taking care of that for us!

I'm talking about the clothes! These rags … they're a horrendous joke, and Rigurt plans to meet the ambassador wearing them! It's an incident in the making!\n\nI will not have it! I'm doing Rigurt a favor.
Oh, I suppose you wouldn't remember me.\n\nI was just a lowly registrar in Mournhold when you and your friend Rigurt visited my fair city.

They sent me here to work for Rigurt. They presented me as a gesture of goodwill because I offended the Nord cultural ambassador.\n\nThat man is a barbarian! I won't have him denigrate and belittle the Dunmer culture with any more of his shenanigans!

That's good. If you want <<Amz:1>>, you should go through the chasm between here and the city to collect them.\n\nCome back up this way when you have enough. I'll check with the Silvenar and see what you need to do next.
Those clothes are an abonimation! They're a diplomatic incident waiting to happen. I'm doing Rigurt a favor, really.\n\nYou can't have them!
Continue down the slope. The Houndsmen patrol the ravine, carrying those shards and looking for loyalists who escaped the city.\n\nAnyone on the Silvenar's side is their prey.

As I said, they are creations of Silvenar's three great spinners. I'm certain the Houndsmen are using them to turn the wards of the city to their master's evil purpose, to help him keep me from the Green Lady.\n\nOf course, there are other defenses.

In addition to the wards, there is the Guardian of Silvenar, an elemental creature that patrols the bridge. He will be compelled to act against us, by the same magic that turns the wards.\n\nYou must defeat him … after you recover the shards.

He is mad, that's why.  A few days ago, <<1>> was overcome with the desire to return here. Maybe it's a perverse homesickness … or maybe he just lusts for Dunmer gold.\n\nAnd now he's dragged me back here.
Damn those Argonians! They can't keep anything quiet. All right. It's Goblins. \n\nYou want <<1>>? Then rescue my workers. Just try not to kill the Goblins. Oh, and bring back their Goblin totem.

Well, I had the men gather table scraps from the mess. There's no food in that mine. The Goblins will be starving.\n\nThrow scraps at them, and they'll go mad for it. They might even fight over it. That's better than them eating my miners.
Don't be silly! Here come the dignitaries!\n\nNow look casual. And dignified!
Yes, he is! He's just returned from up north. Said there was an attack on the pass at Boulderfall.\n\nWhy, do you know him?
Then you know what a good man he is!\n\nFind him for me, my new friend.
I don't know. I heard … I heard some of them screaming for souls. They did something horrible to my father and some of the farm hands.\n\nThat was when Gjakil shouted for everyone to run.
It's just a family farm. My father got her started, back before I was born. The locals called it Treva's Farm. We mostly grow enough food to feed ourselves, and sell the extra in the Riften market.
They're from a camp up in the hills. We barely ever see them. They mostly keep to themselves, herding their mammoths between here and the rivers to the east.
Not really. Like I said, they keep to themselves.\n\nSeeing them angry like that was terrifying. Gjakil says they're territorial. I guess that's what set them off.
Yes, of course. I did promise. \n\nI don't suppose I could just promise to find a new line of work? Then we can just skip the part that requires me to surrender.
I'll be fine. I know a restoration spell to seal wounds. But I will need help getting into the ruins beneath Abamath.\n\nThey're down there. The Worm Cult. And we must stop them.
All right, all right. I'll go back to Cragwallow and tell the royal workers what happened.
He did. Ran right past me. \n\nHe yelled something about you, rieklings, and going to Cragwallow to repent his evil ways.
The truth! Mostly. Perhaps I included one or two omissions.\n\nI explained all about your most excellent rescue, though, I assure you. For a fake bard, I can tell a rousing tale.

Well, I saw no reason to tell them I knew the lute was enchanted before I started playing. \n\nI'm giving up my thieving ways. I shall return home to Solitude, eventually, and perhaps get some proper training at the Bards College.
A friend of Aera's? Well then, welcome to Nimalten.
Slow. My advisor Borodin is at the inn, questioning townfolk. My court mage, Golun, is at the Mages Guild, researching the Worm Cult. Would you help them?

Assistant. Not slave. I already broke a guard's hand for getting a little too friendly. Put a little fear in them and now everything's perfect.\n\nSo, what can I help you with? And if you say "staying warm" your hand is the least of your concerns.
Assistant. By the Three, no one listens around here.\n\nAnd let's just say I have ways to convince Gelds to go back to the table. That's all you need to know for now.
The King is a respectable man. He has more sense in his pinky than the Prince does in his whole body. It's hard to imagine they come from the same stock.\n\nSo sure, why not. I'll help you.
I think faithful old Rollie and I will just sit out here and enjoy the fresh air. \n\nI'm older than most of the team. I'm not in the mood to match drinks with the younger workers.
Well, here we are! We're all Worm Cultists. Hah! Everyone in Nimalten worships worms and dances with Daedra.
He's a fool. Has Golun uncovered anything interesting?
Oh? And what is that?
I don't know. I cut her, and she scampered like a skeever.
Aera. She tried to recruit me to the Worm Cult. They want Nimalten as a base in the Rift.
No, not long. I was a soldier. I retired last year and found a spot on Berj's team.\n\nI do the surveying and other odds and ends, not the heavy rock-breaking and hauling.

Eager. I like that. They've got the <<mz:1>> at their tents; their glow should help you find them. Once you've recovered the stones, head to the ruins' entrance.\n\nI'll meet you there, and we'll go in.

I don't know, but it wasn't long after they entered the barrow that the draugr shambled onto Bonestrewn Crest.\n\nGo see what those Covenant milk-drinkers are up to. Maybe then my brother and cousin can rest in peace. Now I need to see my wife.

I embody the physical strength of the Bosmer, but it proved useless against Hircine's magic.\n\nThe Hound was once my dearest friend Ulthorn. Despite everything, I thought I could make him change his destructive course. I was wrong.
Retrieve <<Ac:1>>. It was crafted in Valeguard and sent here for the wedding ceremony.\n\nFortunately, the spinners hid it away somewhere in the city, to keep it from the Hound … and me.

Excuse me, but who are you?\n\nAnd why is King Jorunn requesting any help from us? The Prince made it very clear that he thinks very little of my egg-kin and I. Why we even bothered coming here is beyond me.

It's too late to help Darkwater, but not to reclaim our honor.\n\nA deal then. If you remove the head of the large troll we call Death-In-Winter and bring it to me, I will consider returning to Irnskar's meeting. For the King.

The Prince cares nothing for us! He refused to send any help to my kin in Darkwater Crossing.\n\nThe trolls wander the town now and only the Hist knows what happened to my people. I offer the same thing to you as the Prince offered to me. Nothing!
Always begin at the beginning, my friend. That is the best place to start.
A monster! No doubt some vile beast from the darkest reaches of Oblivion!\n\nI can't imagine how it got here. And I have no idea why it would do such things to our soldiers.
Yes, of course. The spinners of Valeguard prepared the Handfast for the ceremony. We hid it from the Hound.\n\nI've sent word of your victory. It's on the way now.
Really? Why am I not surprised? Perhaps you know the messenger already.\n\nCome, follow me and I'll take you to him.
You must! We can't let this attack go unpunished.
You're looking at the Dancing Scrib, greatest acting troupe this side of Elsweyr!\n\nAt least, we were. Until we got a bit broken up.
Oh, you'll just have to help us to find out, won't you?
These two hold the present story, as it should be: the Silvenar joins with the Green Lady. I can use them to remove the barrier.
Wait. The last two <<mz:1>>. Give them to me. They embody the future we're fighting for, after all: the Green Lady and the Silvenar.\n\nWe've no shard for the Huntsman. He made his own.
Something feels wrong here, but I can't put my finger on it.
The Llodos plague. It's been ravaging our cities, turning our loved ones into walking corpses. We came here to escape it.
Garil was infected. He seemed fine at first, but the infection became obvious during one of our hunting expeditions. \n\nI had to abandon him in the crypts. I doubt he survived.

The spinners of Valeguard are nearly as well known as those of Silvenar. Every generation, it is they who prepare the Handfast for the wedding ceremony.\n\nOne of them brought it here. Follow me, and I'll take you to him.
They are building an army of Daedra! Their leader, that bastard, Thallik Wormfather, stole Ysgramor's axe, Wuuthrad. He has roused the ghost giant Sinmur!
Many have gone to Sovngarde today. Many more will follow unless we close the portals and stop Thallik Wormfather. \n\nNo ordinary soldier can deal with this. For this task, I need you.
Thank Kyne! Since you're here, will you help me? We have big problems outside.
I don't know. Head outside with me? If there are any more big feet out there, I'll need help.
Yes. The clan's blood is ablaze.\n\nI'm afraid if we give them time to regroup, they'll attack the farm. I saw the chieftain rallying the warriors and their mammoths.

Last night the cultists stole the <<z:1>>, the relic holding our spirits. In time, they'll use it to enslave us.\n\nWe musn't become thralls of the Worm Cult! <<2>> has a plan to stop them, but it will require your aid. Please, speak with him.
You would defend us? With your life? You remind me of Treva himself. The old farm-thane never backed down from a fight.\n\nHere, follow me. I'll show you the way.

Easier said than done. The energies protecting the relic kill living creatures who touch it.\n\nBut there's a way. Make an offering to Clavicus Vile and the <<z:1>> will think you one of us. Then you can recover it safely from the Worm Cult.
Nothing good. Please, don't touch the right switch.
Fine! Have it your way! It activates some sort of mechanism. This cage is some kind of sacrificial device.\n\nI beg you, whatever you do, leave the right switch alone!
While the handfast ceremony is complete, their bond is still forming.\n\nThey must unite the physical with the spiritual, a process that takes many days … and many nights.
The final two <<mz:1>> unlock the door to the sanctum inside these ruins. Don't lose them!\n\nBe ready for anything in there.
Clan bosses lead organized attacks. Cut off the head, and the ice wraith dies. You get me?
I don't see how that can possibly be any of your business.
I'm bored now. Run along.
Oh, sweetie. I'm not a soldier. I'm the morale officer. I'd be happy to raise your morale whenever you want. Come by anytime!
I've been watching the logging camp. Strange things are happening over there.\n\nApparently, they're having problems with … oh, what do they call them? Spriggans? Even the Stormfists avoid the area.
I didn't come all this way to fight walking trees. Plus, we don't have any orders regarding Spriggans or logging camps. \n\nIf you're so interested, feel free to look into it yourself.
We're at war! An attack is always possible.\n\nBut I have a dagger and I know how to use it.
Hey, we all want to help in our own way. I assist the cooks and healers. Help keep the camp on track. \n\nI wanted to be a part of all this. You got a problem with that?
Yes, yes! Your ship is ready, and a fine one it is. Very few rats, plenty of fruit.\n\nLet me know when you're ready to set sail.
Good, good! Follow me, please.
Despite the cold, harsh landscape, Eastmarch can be beautiful. \n\nBut when this war ends, I'll return to Black Marsh without a second thought. It is my home.
