<<1>>? Nothing should block her entry to the sacred grove. Perhaps this is all related ….\n\nNormally, the spriggans allow me to come and go freely. But now they rage, and won't let me through.
We need to do more than that. The matrons must be awakened.\n\nDisturbing Treehenge's roots should do the trick. They'll know what to do!
I hope so. Word around camp is that King Jorunn's healing nicely. \n\nBut decisions need to be made. Orcthane Fildgor's ambition and hatred must not be allowed to spread.
Many things. I play music for my friends. I listen and nod. I gather herbs for the cooks.\n\nPinooh watches and learns. Travel is interesting, even during wartime.
The Prince makes mistakes. The Argonians are skeptical, the Dark Elves are scornful. But opinions can change. They often do.\n\nThe Prince has a good heart and that will see him through. I think.
A council gathers. Hopefully decisions will be made. Perhaps action will be taken. \n\nThe soldiers are ready. Even a sharp sword loses its edge if it remains in its scabbard too long.
Pinooh hears about you. Your brave deeds may one day make a fine song. These Nords love singing songs about brave deeds. They don't sing well, but they do sing loud.

Talk freely. Thane Oda is as trustworthy as I.\n\nBut understand that I have enough trouble as it is and I don't need any more bad news. I have my hands full trying to figure out how to calm the Prince and get the Pact delegates back to the meeting.

I have no issues with King Jorunn, but his son is an imbecile! He believes that the Nords are superior to all! And he had the audacity to insult our Lady Almalexia!\n\nLet's see how well the Nords do against the Stormfists without our help.
Sure as Sheogorath's a madman. Back before the Pact was formed, Unnvald raided all along the Morrowind coast. His crew always came back laden with gold and honor.
Aye, but almost no one uses this pass anymore. Merchants ship cargo from Ebonheart to Windhelm, and then make the trip down to Riften.
It's not how he reacted to the Pact. It's how the Pact reacted to him. Suddenly it wasn't polite to venerate a Dark Elf-murderer. He's been out here ever since.
You mean you're not in league with that Sadri character? I find that hard to believe.
Ha! You think me a fool, child? Ysgramor's axe is safe in Fallowstone Hall.

Tervur Sadri is a murderer. He brought in these thugs to drive out our miners, then killed my father and stole the deed to our mine. \n\nI guess he didn't expect me to come after him. But you cut a swath through his protectors.

Fair are your words. And fair you may be. But I see the Jarls in the shadows behind you. It's not enough they exiled me here. Swept me under the rug. Now they plot to make me disappear! Dark Elf fanciers. All of them.
Yes. And by the corpses I saw on my way in, I'm sure you know how to deal with him. \n\nOh, and you can keep anything valuable you find down there. I guess it's only fair.
Well, I need to stay here and see about getting this mess cleaned up. \n\nAs for you—go down into that pit and catch up with your former accomplice, Tervur Sadri.
You must have met my twin brother, Thelm. \n\nLet him know I'm all right. He worries too much.

My people came to Fort Amol from the west, but the town wasn't big enough to absorb them. They settled at Darkwater Crossing. Then the trolls came ….\n\nYou have done what that arrogant Prince would not do. Thank you.

Perhaps. That is for them to decide. But at least they have that choice.\n\nLike King Jorunn, you demonstrate honor. I will return to the Prince's meeting and hear what he has to say. You have earned that much.
I'm fine. The trick is to look busy. The Stormfists don't really know what we do down here. \n\nI don't want them to hurt my sister, Garvilda, though, so I just keep moving so they think I'm working.

I knew I could count on you. Reliability is an admirable trait.\n\nThis will taste good. Probably make taking orders from that barking dog over there a bit more tolerable. And it should be enough to get the job done.

Of course. How did you think I was going to convince him?\n\nNow do me a favor and stay alert out there. I've seen enough shadows and sheepish grins to know that something isn't right in Fort Amol. But that's why I'm here now, isn't it?
So you say. My Thane's suspicions are just. You come to us with tales of a shattered legend. You offer no proof.

I've learned that the thane needs to settle down. Having a troubleshooter come all the way out here? Because Fjora had a fight with her housecarl? Shameful. It makes Nimalten look bad. I'm thinking we need a new thane.
None. Now, the undead may assault my Thane's keep again at any moment. This is his home and we will defend it. You have no such obligation. It would be best if you leave this manor, quick as you can.
Shut up and get out of here. Bleeding feels good. Reminds me I'm alive.
Through there. Be careful.

I've been tracking a Breton Illusionist by the name of Dhalen for a while now. The villain created quite a stir by assassinating a few nobles in Mournhold recently.\n\nI discovered that he took a contract with Fildgor and tracked him to this region.

I need to make sure our alliance friends are playing nice with each other, then I'll meet up with you.\n\nAfter I get out of this damn dress and into some proper clothing. How do women wear stuff like this all the time?

Not exactly, but I'd wager he's inside the keep.\n\nI'm not sure what we'll find in there, but you'll need to be quick. Dhalen's already a step ahead of us. The man bought Vurlop with the promise of gold. Who knows who else he's got on his side.
I, well, thanks. Maybe I could get used to wearing such finery when things aren't so dangerous. \n\nWhat am I saying? Get your arse in there and save King Jorunn!

Oh, no! I hoped Kerig made it to Fort Amol. \n\nOrcthane Fildgor's troops have taken over the mine. Half of us were sent to work in the mine and serve as hostages. The other half wait out here and worry. My family's in there right now!

We need weapons. Overpower some of the soldiers, grab their weapons, and give them to my husband, Jomund. He's somewhere in the mine.\n\nAlso, set a few miners free along the way. Look for my siblings, Tridi and Nedrek. I need to know they're safe.

He consorted with Oblivion to ascend to power. Those who stood in his way, he killed, though always under mysterious circumstances.\n\nEventually, those around him saw through his schemes and imprisoned him. Lifetimes have passed, but Rilis remains.
Rilis' pact with the Daedra keeps him chained to Nirn, though he is dead.\n\nWere it not for the Daedra who freed him, he would be serving his sentence still, until time immemorial.
If <<1>> sends for reinforcements, he'll gain enough soldiers to clear these Dominion muckworms from the ruins. We can manage until then. It's a good place to fight with our tails to the wall.
Windows are wonderful things, my darling. No one ever remembers to lock them!\n\nI'm sure you've crawled into or out of more than a few windows over the course of your adventures.

Grandfather always felt ill-treated by the Jarls. Lately he's become convinced they plot to kill him. Some poor man came with a message from Jarl Angjord. Grandfather accused him of being an assassin. He was beheaded.
I don't think you'll just find a key lying around, but you never know.\n\nI'll check down here. Take a look upstairs and see if you can find anything.
I could tell you where to find the only decent meal in town, but that's probably not what you mean.\n\nWhat do you want to know?

It's a Dunmer city, built on an Argonian village, built on an Ayleid ruin. Confused, like much of Shadowfen.\n\nConsider it a last bastion of civilization before Black Marsh. Everything south of Stormhold is lizards and mud.

War heroes from the Akaviri war. Strong leaders. Honorable to the last. A good thing too since Shadowfen's troubled by its past.\n\nMy people kept Argonian slaves within living memory, and that's not a wound to quickly heal.
Not much, sadly. It's mostly Argonians missing. Some think slavers are to blame.\n\nIf that's true, the Pact may not survive such discord.

For all intents and purposes, I am the real king now! Any who would challenge that are being dealt with. But I wanted to congratulate you.\n\nSo many lives lost because of you. I'm envious. That poor Guard Hloenor. Greedy Lord Vurlop. The mind reels!
I hate to say it, but. Thorulf has been grandfather's Housecarl since I was a girl. He always seemed cold. Aloof. Lately he's changed too.
Oh, her name? I overheard them. They shouted her name to each other. The brutes.

Well, yes. That's the entire point of why we're here.\n\nNow, I must apologize. I have matters to attend to. You'll find that my guards now control the manor. You can try to stop us, but I doubt you'll have very much luck.

Vurlop did say that he would take care of her, didn't he? My poor Vurlop was many things, but a liar wasn't one of them.\n\nThen there's that pretty little Dark Elf outside. The feisty one. She'll be a fun one to kill. And, of course, King Jorunn ….
Okay, I hired her to attack him. But she still stole my silk. Listen, forget about killing all those bandits. Would you just retrieve my silk?
You adventurers are so impatient.\n\nJomund said he would send me more samples. Then I can perform additional tests on the metal.
Lately he's been directing the household. Telling grandfather what to do. You saw it, didn't you? Grandfather didn't order you away. Thorulf did.

I want to search Thorulf's room, but he keeps it locked. His guard, Sirkidur, holds the key. They both suspect me already. You, maybe, have a chance.\n\nGet inside. If you find anything, meet me upstairs.
I … I had to! Turil steals my customers, bad-mouths my wares. Plus, I have a starving family in Stonefalls. Would you doom my poor family?
I don't think … they did start about the same time, actually. But, no. This pass saw thousands of skirmishes between Nords and Dark Elves. The dead have never risen before.

Yes. Yes, I did. And I'll tell you why. I've not told anyone this, but the money I make with this silk? It goes to suffering war refugees. If you give me my silk back, you save hungry familes torn apart by war.

Yes, exactly. Even before Red Mountain, the old Nedes invaded Chimer lands through this pass. Thousands have died here. Not all of them received Arkay's blessing. Though I'd expect—now that I think on it, that's odd.
It's just … I'd expect dead Nords and dead Elves to keep fighting each other. But the dead focus their attacks on Fullhelm. Sorry. What do I know about the undead, anyway?
They died when I was very young. A Dark Elf raid on Riften. They hit our farm as they went through. All they left was ash.

Aye. He had another stead nearby. Just luck we weren't killed as well. He took up raiding the next spring. Gran and I made projects while he was away. Quilts, paintings, for when he returned. She kept a candle burning in the window every night.
Yes, I—don't say it. Please. I know what you're thinking. I couldn't bear to hear it. He's had a hard life. We all have.
I don't think they do. What grandfather did was a long time ago now. Before the formation of the Pact, he raided Morrowind. He'd gather warriors and sail off once or twice a year.
After the Pact was signed, he was offered the Thanedom of Fullhelm. He didn't want it. It's too far from gran's grave, here. They said if he didn't go, he'd have to answer to the Tribunal Ordinators.
One of the best. Warriors came from across Skyrim to sail with him. One year the Bards College sent a skald to chronicle the trip. That was the year Davon's Watch went under the axe.
They don't need to kill him. No one sings the songs about him. The Ordinators banned them. The Jarls pulled down the statues in Riften and Windhelm. He's worse than dead. He's forgotten.
Ysmir's beard! "Arkay the Enemy?" A necromancer's tract! All these years, and Thorulf betrays us to the dead.

The illusionist fooled us all. His magic allowed the Stormfists to look like people we trusted. Something in the wine we shared, we think.\n\nOne of them took the form of the King's servant. He poisoned the King's dinner.

She never identified herself. When the Stormfists broke in, she just appeared out of nowhere and put two daggers in their backs. Then she told us help was coming and she ran off.\n\nShe wore a helmet, but I'm pretty sure she was a Dark Elf.

Fighting broke out as soon as King Jorunn fell ill. We dragged him away from the meeting and locked ourselves in here.\n\nWhen the Stormfist broke in, I thought we were finished. If that woman hadn't shown up, we'd probably be dead right now.
We should be fine. And we're not helpless. We can protect the King.\n\nBut please hurry just the same. I don't know how long he can resist the poison.

When you entered the safe room, I heard the ambassadors trying to be quiet upstairs. Next thing I know, Stormfist thugs are waving their axes around and attacking the manor.\n\nI was about to leave the same way I entered ….

I was talking about you, but I also figured more backup wouldn't hurt. Irnskar and his guards are downstairs. They rushed over as soon as the fighting started.\n\nBut King Jorunn … he didn't look so good. He's not going to make it, is he?

Fildgor plays dirty. I wish I could help more, but I've already overstepped the limits of my contract. I need to get back to Mournhold. A new matter involving a rival group has become an issue.\n\nBut these people still need your help, hero.
No. I don't. Wait. Grandfather's sword. Bonebane!\n\nWhen the dead first attacked, Thorulf led a group to retrieve it. Thorulf said the blade was destroyed, the men killed.
Yes. But who will believe us? My grandfather is wrapped around his little finger. The guards dare not stand against him, not if they want to keep their heads.
Always the hero, aren't you?\n\nI'm kidding. I'll find you again when I need your help. In fact, I'd like that. Now go. Save King Jorunn. He needs you more than I do at the moment.

The bastard. There's no way he could have destroyed it. It's been blessed by Arkay dozens of times.\n\nGet Bonebane. It's at a monument to grandfather south of the fort. Bring it back, and you can prove Thorulf's a liar!
Fildgor might have driven the blade, but the Dark Elves and Argonians did nothing to protect my father!\n\nNow where is he? Tell me!
Guards, go to the King at once!\n\nAs for you, what's your involvement in all this? Why are you here?

I must tell Vigrod. You infiltrate the mine. Heiress Alona has the only key to the mine door. I tried to steal it but could only get a key to her sanctum, just to the south. Get in there, find out what you can, and grab that mine door key.

Yes, they are. We've told them to leave. And just like you, they've ignored us.\n\nBut they would need the holy seed to harm <<1>>. The spriggan guardians will stop them, and <<1>> will enter our leaves and branches, safe forevermore.
Are you a living servant of the Green Lady? Can you keep her safe?\n\nHmph. I suppose she may have need of you, but I still don't like trusting outsiders.
My scouts report that the Stormfists are fortifying Cradlecrush, to the southwest. We can't let them establish a foothold or we'll never get rid of them.

If only we had the troops for such an action. We're in no condition for another battle right now, but I think we have time.\n\nSomething strange is going on over at Cradlecrush, but it doesn't appear that they're about to launch an attack or anything.
It's an old Orc fortress, but it hasn't been used by hostile forces in years.
Unusual sounds. We hear crashes and moans, toppling trees. We see smoke on the horizon. I have no idea what to make of it and I can't spare anyone else to investigate right now.
What are you doing here? Don't matter, the guards will deal with you.
What? No one tells me anything. Hold on while I unlock the door.
I have only this ward that I hid from the guards. It's all I have to save me from the Hagravens. Please don't take it from me.

Three preserve me, yes. I did … terrible things. But someone needed to do it. Molag Bal is pure destruction. Nothing can be built on a foundation of worms. \n\nNecromancy, though, is just a tool. And now I wield the weapon of the worm.
No. We did that. The bastards tunneled up from below, into an old cave we used for storage. While we were defending the walls, they went under us. The fire's keeping them down, but that won't last.
I was hoping the hero of Bal Foyen, Ash Mountain, and elsewhere might volunteer. If you smash enough of them, maybe the Worm behind this will appear. Good luck.
Give me a few minutes to catch my breath. I can make it back to <<1>> on my own.\n\nHave you seen <<2>>? Last I saw, he was heading toward a canyon West of here.
Not much. They're not very bright and they've always been unlucky, so anything could have happened to them.
Thank Kyne you're back! While everyone was fighting off the attack, Thorulf raised a skeleton in the manor. He told grandfather the undead had broken in, that we were all going to die.
More than that. He went mad, raving! I think he might kill himself! Then Sjarakki came in and said you were turning back the skeletons in the shed. When Thorulf heard, he got wild-eyed and bolted.
If we help grandpa, Thorulf will escape. But if we go after Thorulf, Unnvald will die!
Yes. His chamber is on the second floor, on the left side.
He fled down the southeast road. The one that goes past the old Dragon temple at Forelhost.
I don't know what they're looking for, but the bastards are all over the mine. They've slaughtered most of my miners. I think a few are still alive, held captive. Find them and free them, if you can!

Deep in the mine is an ancient Companion tomb. The Reachmen shamans went into the tomb, then the clansmen used two relics to seal the entrance. Their leaders are in the tomb, but you need those relics to get in.
The cultists poison our roots. Their blasphemous magic runs through our veins. We burn alive.\n\nWhy have you come, mortal? Will you end our suffering?
Then save Treehenge. If our roots collapse, the whole of this place will fall into ruin.\n\nSave us before the cult consumes all that we've grown!
She is correct. The Worm Cult interferes with the natural state of Treehenge.\n\nIf we could retrieve the holy seed, there'd be no trouble. Then, nothing could stop us!
That would be ideal, mortal. They threaten the stories of a hundred lifetimes.
Then we must take her back, quickly!\n\nThere is an altar not far from here. It's used to ready a soul before it takes root. Perhaps it can also be used to bring her back to us.
You must wash the shrine clean with the moon and stars. It will serve as a beacon to <<1>>.\n\nThough without a place to root, I don't know how long she'll be able to hold on.
Fallowstone Hall must be retaken! There are relics hidden beneath the Hall, including a mighty weapon that was used to kill Sinmur long ago.\n\nDo you want to follow me or meet me there?
Yes! I heard them whispering, felt their blackened magic!\n\nThey seek to turn me into an abomination! All of us!

We were all once the Green Lady. The bond between us is strong, but tenuous so long as I'm not yet rooted.\n\nIf they corrupted me, it could spread through us all. I need to take root in the seed before it's too late!
The cultists have all but destroyed us. They kill Treehenge from the roots.\n\n<<1>> must live if we are to heal.
The cavern you first entered holds Treehenge's roots. Within is the holy seed, cast off from the first sprout.\n\nFind it and bring it to <<1>>. It will allow her to root and flourish.
It will act as a vessel for <<1>>'s essence. Bring it to her and she will fill it.\n\nBe quick. <<1>>'s lifeforce scatters to the winds. Take the seed, and I will send you to her.
They came! <<1>>'s so weak, she couldn't fight back!\n\nOne of the cultists captured her, but they didn't get far. I'd know if she left Treehenge!
Up the path, near the great tree at the center. They're trying to rip her from Treehenge.\n\n<<1>>'s still fighting—you've got to save her! I don't know how long she'll last!
There's nothing holding her together. Any moment, she could just disappear.\n\nI couldn't stop them before, but now … I know what I must do.
There's no time. She's fading away as we speak!\n\nI must make this sacrifice for the good of the henge … for the good of the Bosmer.
She gave her own lifeforce to save me. I couldn't take it all, not after all she's done for us.\n\nFor now, she sleeps. We'll tend to her until she recovers from this ordeal.
Excellent. Do you know the way? I can lead you to the front.

No, please, get away! Who—it's you. Don't look at me. Don't touch me. The bastards, the Hagravens, they took my eyes! Sucked them out of my skull! I can't … what they did to me!\n\nMake them pay—kill them, rip their eyes out!
I've got a gut wound, and I'm losing blood. Aside from that, I'm doing just fine.
To protect us from the undead, and those who carry the plague.
There's the King's festival if that type of thing interests you. \n\nMe? I'm not a fan of large crowds. They bring in all kinds of trouble.
I've spotted several Maormer camps along the beach. The survivors were likely split up for interrogation amongst them.\n\nThat's what they do. Interrogate. Torture. And then, they kill you.
Garil? He's not with us anymore. If you want more than that, you'll have to talk to Danus.
Scavenging and hunting. Our leader, Danus, has had remarkable luck finding fresh meat.
I've no idea where he's getting it. Why don't you ask Danus?
I don't trust that Stormfist clan one bit. We haven't seen them in a decade, but they showed up for this year's Konunleikar. They're nothing but trouble, you mark my words.

Well, you saw what Fildgor's crew tried to get away with. I knew they were up to no good the moment they arrived in town.\n\nI'd suggest you stay vigilant. Might be more of them around. And they probably aren't too happy with you.

Not getting involved in Windhelm affairs, that's for sure. King this, jarl that. A bunch of people with too much power in their hands who don't give a damn about us small folk.\n\nEr, not that I mean that literally of course. Well, maybe.
He's not my king. We don't have kings. Treethanes sure, but not kings.\n\nNo, I'm only here to enjoy the party and make some gold. My talents are always in high demand.
Sometimes people need a hand and I offer mine. For a fee.\n\nIt's surprising how much trouble people can get into. Lucky for them, I happen to be around.
As long as it's not for my hand in marriage. I'm sure my husband wouldn't appreciate that.\n\nI'm teasing, dear.
Garil? I heard he vanished on the last hunting expedition. Danus would know more.
Well, you arrived just in time for the King's Konunleikar festival. Clans from all across Skyrim have come to compete in the games. It's all to honor King Jorunn's rise to power.

The Cold Moon Inn attracts all kinds. Especially the kinds that don't want to draw attention to themselves. But we welcome all paying customers. The food's hot, the mead's cold, and the place is clean. Mostly.

I hear lots of things, but most of it's kind of boring. This might interest you, though.\n\nI hear the King's brother, Fildgor, has returned to Eastmarch. King Jorunn defeated him in a challenge once, so who knows what he's up to.
Danus calls it meatloaf surprise. I'm surprised I'm able to keep it down.
You'll have to ask Danus.
What? But we saw his bow.
Getting warm.
What do you mean?
It's an old city.
I like music.
Very well.
That's preposterous! He was fine when we were separated! \n\nPlease, you must find him! Search the crypts. I'll keep questioning the others. Someone must know what Danus is playing at.
I hope a troll eats him.

The whimsical harps of the Altmer always bring a tear to my eye. Their fingers gently caressing the strings of the beautiful instruments, plucking and strumming songs that touch your soul.\n\nIt's like they can see right into my heart.
The Windhelm docks are busy most days. But with the Konunleikar festivities … let's just say I barely have time to have a pint of ale and a bite to eat.

Well, most people are having a good time. With Fildgor on the move, there is a bit of a sober undercurrent these days. \n\nStill, you can't keep the Nord spirit down for long, not when there's food and mead to be had.

Plenty. You can participate in the Konunleikar, perhaps. Or just watch the competitions.  \n\nWe have a couple of fine drinking establishments. I recommend the Cold Moon Inn, but others prefer the Sober Nord Tavern.
And normally the sun brings warmth, but not in these chilly climes. What can I do for you, land strider?
A boat. \n\nI'm a sailor. On a merchant ship. Our captain has family in Windhelm. And she kept going on and on about a festival of some sort. She was very excited.
<<1>>.\n\nThat woman is the definition of beauty and grace. Sure, many would call her a simple stable girl, but I know her to be so much more.
Why would I do that when I can sing her a beautiful song that describes my feelings?\n\nWhat a strange suggestion.
Well, she knows my name. At least, I'm pretty sure she knows my name. I'm working on more.\n\nHopefully, this song will convince her of my worth as a suitor.
It's what she wants. I don't feel up to it, but I guess I can't do a worse job than the last fellow. Sorry. I know it's too soon. I'm trying to keep Hallie's—to keep Thane Hallfrida's spirits up.
Thorulf left this behind in his haste. A shard. This would be the shard of Wuuthrad you sought?
Hah! I won't let a damn necromancer use me! I'll burn. Just like my daughter, all those years ago. I will not be raised!
What? No! Thorulf has been my Housecarl for—I would have known! Just a few weeks ago, he gave me a token of his faith.
Liar! Thorulf warned me you'd say such things. My soldiers are dead, my fort lost. I won't let you raise me as a puppet of your dark magic!
See for yourself! Part of a weapon. Said it came over with Ysgramor. Had been in his family for generations. No faithless Nord would give such a boon.

This is a shard of Wuuthrad? Thorulf gave this to him not long ago. He claimed it was a family relic. Now that I think on it, grandfather began to change not long after. I wonder. Could Thorulf have cursed this?
My mind … everything seems so much clearer, now. It had some sort of hold on me. Shor's Bones. \n\nWhat was I thinking? What have I done?
Aye. He muddled my wits worse than Riften Mead. \n\nYou said the undead were taken care of. And Thorulf? Where's that bastard?
Strange lights and sounds have been coming from the shrine. It's not normal. Ormi is probably there.\n\nWhatever she uses to channel these dark powers, it's corrupting the serenity of the grove.

You can't reason with Daedric witches! We've all suffered losses, but they take my soldiers and turn them into mindless slaves. I can't forgive her for that.\n\nThey need to die! Every last one of them. I … ugh … what's going on?
Oblivion take that girl! She sang a song to end us all. What you're seeing in the sky is Quagmire, Vaermina's Daedric realm. Skald's Retreat now straddles the wall between worlds.
Ha! You? You're as damp as stinking swamp moss.\n\nIf you want to scare this one, you'll have to do much more than that.

The Renrijra Maor. Some called us pirates, others privateers. It did not matter. We sailed under the papers of the Dominion, capturing enemy merchants for our profit and for the Dominion's pleasure.\n\nNo more talk. This is wasting precious time.
Go slowly. I'll try to follow, but I can't see or fight.
I hear your challenge, Mistress, and I heed your call. It was my honor to weave the song for you.
Yes, the song. The ancient song, the ancient tune. Your whispers in the night. They inspired me so. But I know you don't wish me to speak of it.
I'm ready to spar anytime.
Gonna walk around in a circle, man.
Of course! Who doesn't?
Like it? I don't like it at all! It's too damn hot!
What kind of Nord are you? Enough of this. I need to find some shade.
The matrons said she's withering. Too weak to take root. But I won't let it end this way!\n\nI can give my life energy to <<1>>. It will give her the strength she needs.

Fool! To destroy the Circle of Iron, you'd need a forge capable of melting iron! Or you'd need to hurl it into the crashing flood of a high waterfall.\n\nBy the time you find either, my minions will kill you!

My wife! I'm talking about my wife. She was … is … the joy of my life. Such grace as you see but once in a hundred years.\n\nThen death took her. I could not prevent it, but I cannot let go. She was caught between worlds … until now.
What?! No! That forge won't be powerful enough. Mere Wood Orcs couldn't possibly create a fire great enough to melt iron!
There are? I mean … the waterfalls in this area aren't powerful enough to destroy the Circle of Iron! They would have to be, well, very high waterfalls with lots of … water ….\n\nOh, no.

Only here. It must be the proximity to the Hist reclaiming its dead. To have her back with me—it's wonderful!\n\nYes, of course, you should meet her. She's within. It just looks like a cave, but inside, she's recreated our home.
That's a relief. There must be a power source nearby, another <<z:1>>, or something darker.\n\nLook! There! On the pedestal!

I speak through this object, not from it, mortal.\n\nThat troll-herder Mauloch must not invade this realm. The pathetic worms in the cave beyond must be destroyed. You must stop their foolish rituals.
Laugh while you can, mortal. I cannot fully manifest on your plane now, but I'll see you again. Remember the name Ibezai, for I will kill you.
And we will finish this, once I completely manifest on your plane! Sleep fitfully, never knowing when Ibezai will strike!
This is not about what you want, but what I need. This stone drinks souls, and its thirst is strong.\n\nTake the geode in your hand. Sacrifice her soul to clear your path.

Use the <<1>> to absorb her soul and it will dispel the barrier. The Worm Cult is of no interest to me for the moment, but Mauloch cannot be allowed to invade Nirn.\n\nWe have history, Mauloch and I. It would amuse me to see his plan destroyed.
These blasted thugs came in and ran them off.\n\nIf they smash the equipment or the eggs, we'll be ruined.
Oh, no, I'll make it worth your while. Old Selos' has got a pile of real gold down there somewhere—he's sold a lot of these eggs. You'll be paid, right enough.\n\nNow, let's go and save him.
They seem to think this is a gold mine, and we're hiding untold wealth somewhere down inside. \n\nIt's madness—I can't imagine where they got such an idea.
Boethiah? Why does she want my soul?
I'll answer truthfully, my new friend. Whatever you wish to ask.
I only know of the song, I don't know how to perform it. My apologies. There are many songs sung at the retreat. To know them all would take three lifetimes.
I think the Queen got to her. Engling pulled something from the lore vaults. Dusted it off, set it to a tune she heard in a dream. A nightmare, more like. Vaermina's hand at work in the world!
I don't know if you've seen them yet, friend, but nightmares stalk the island. The sky, the smells, the sounds … they scream out the name of the Queen of Nightmares.
The council has spoken. Sees-All-Colors never returned to the fold after your visit to Abagarlas. She has fled, she is guilty … she must be killed.

I have an idea, but we must confer with Merric. He's returned to the Earth Forge, to finish work on the Prismatic Core. Aelif is ready to open a portal, take us straight to his side. Are you prepared?
Yes, practice. Well, I remember the second line: "The story I have to tell."
I am you, Silvenar. Your ego, your superior strength of will and mind. I am what makes you greater than the rest!\n\nReject my gift and you will fall. You are nothing without me!

The true purpose of the Bosmer was revealed to me. With our unquenchable thirst and never-ending hunger, we become the devouring beast.\n\nWithout the Green Lady, the Silvenar will fall. She will return to the wilds, and the Bosmer shall follow.
Oh! The Jarl! I didn't recognize you. I remember only the first line: "Gather 'round all who'd hear."

This obviously wasn't the Prince's idea. That Nord is a whiny little s'wit who's had everything handed to him on a silver platter. He'd never stoop to ask for help from one of the "lesser" races.\n\nWhat is this really about?

Shh! No one needs to know that.\n\nVaron gave me my first solo contract. It's a special one. The target's around here somewhere, but I haven't pinpointed where just yet. So … I'm in disguise. Not my first choice of garb, but it works.

For a friend, anything. One of the guards hates cats. Earlier, I saw a cat run into the building. The guard chased it for an hour.\n\nBring a cat with you. It might prove useful. I saw a bunch of them following the Argonians around. Try over there.

Gelds is an idiot and the Prince is … well, he's a royal idiot. Bringing those two together might hurt more than help with any problems you have here.\n\nBut since you asked so nicely, I can help. Might even get me closer to my goal.

I can be rather convincing when I need to be. Especially in this attire.\n\nThe jarl keeps some of his best wine locked away in the barracks. Snag a couple of bottles for me. Just be careful in there. The guards don't like visitors.
Of course! Listen as I pick it out on the strings. One of my favorites, very tricky.
Hah, ya old crow. How about the third line: "About Ysgramor, greatest of us all." See? I know the songs!

My totem spirit will fight, but it is most useful in that it can heal your wounds. Just stay close to it and the energy it manifests will help you recover in battle.\n\nI wish I could do more to honor Raen's sacrifice.

It will fight alongside you and lend you some of its strength. Do not expect miracles; my strength is small and the totem spirit's energy parallels mine.\n\nI wish I could do more, in Sariel's memory.

Well, since you asked so nicely! One of the guards hates cats. Really detests the creatures. I saw the guard chase a cat that ran into the barracks for more than an hour.\n\nSo bring a cat along. I saw a lot of them hovering around the Argonians.
Oh! Well why didn't you say so? Here, teach me the melody on these harps. I never forget a tune once I've heard it. Rusty-trap-Maraamur, they call me!

After I teleport out, I'll leave the portal open as long as I can. We'll meet again outside, beyond the reach of the Drublog.\n\nDon't wait too long; the portal won't stay up forever. And I wouldn't be surprised if more Drublog show up down here soon.

Why fight through angry Drublog warriors and treacherous Houndsmen? You freed me and killed their leaders. They won't thank you for that.\n\nI must go now. I can't risk being trapped again. Use the portal or not; it's up to you.
If I'm going to perform this thing, I'll need to sober up a bit. Now get going, mead demon!

What do you mean why? It's a magic spell! We need the lute that cast the spell. Shor's bones. And I thought I was the drunk one! I'll meet you on the southern tip of the island once you have the lute.
Yes. We called in several favors to do it, but we've cracked her code.\n\nIn service to her dark master, <<1>> was after something hidden in a Dwarven ruin. A place known as <<2>>.
There are travelers everywhere, carrying the plague. Once the symptoms reveal themselves, it's too late. How could we be sure? When death comes knocking, you don't invite him in for tea.

We're not sure, but it seems to have something to do with that Mortuum Vivicus her notes mentioned. <<1>> is far from here, but I've prepared a portal that will carry us across Tamriel. \n\nWhat do you say, comrade? Venture with me into the unknown?
I haven't much choice, have I? You're here now, so I can only pray you're not infected.\n\nAnd even if I wanted to force you out, I doubt I'd have much luck. You're clearly a formidable opponent.

The quarantine will not hold. It's only a matter of time before the city's water supply is tainted, and Narsis is ravaged by the Llodos plague. My people are not infected, and I've vowed to keep them safe.
Away from the roads, away from the cities, away from the unclean throngs of infected. We've chosen to leave the outside world to the fate it deserves. Here, we will be safe.

The visions, my friend. The Ayleids fled from the forces of Molag Bal and hid away the remains of a powerful relic. Merric has taken the crystal and the tome to an ancient forge. There he's begun the work of crafting the weapon anew.

In time, comrade. First you and I must travel afield, to the ruined city Abagarlas. It was there the Ayleids went, to stop the Mortuum Vivicus. Together we will understand the threat to the present in the events of the past.
This one apologizes, comrade. She has been urging action for some time. Finally, to be able to … ahem. We have been tasked with investigating Jofnir's death, yes? We should begin.

Jofnir kept a room nearby. Aelif gave instructions no one was to be allowed inside until we arrived. I shall keep watch here. Enter Jofnir's quarters, and search for … something. Anything, to suggest a road to travel.
The thane is impatient. I almost have it. At first, it stumped me. Why would the cult come to this backwater? What could the cult find in Nimalten and nowhere else?
I think so. It happened so fast.\n\nWait. Why hasn't the smell gone away?
I think so. It happened so fast.\n\nWait. Why hasn't the smell gone away?
Still strong as a horker! Too stubborn for the Queen of Nightmares to get her claws in.
When I think of their filthy claws on my tomes. Yech! She's the jealous type, Vaermina is. Doesn't like anyone knowing too much about her. Wants to keep her little secrets. Ysgramor take her!

Sure enough there's plenty of stories about her. Queen of nightmares, dreams, sign of ill omens. Her followers are called the Supernal Dreamers, and they spend their days trying to bring nightmares to life.
Name's Bragur. I tend the books and artifacts here. You're tending to them yourself! Ask your help? There's a pint of mead in it for you.
Get the rest of my books back! Her nightmares crawled all over the shelves, pulled out anything that referenced herself or her Dreamers. Now they're out there in the cold, getting ratty.

My sister and I normally deal with Dwemer relics and ruins. We're old hands at running dig sites, though.\n\nThe Worms have destroyed artifacts and ruined everything here. And the Draugr are everywhere now.
We know precious little about their plans, other than we have to stop them. But I'll tell you what I know.
Now you're talking. A song cast this spell. Another song could undo it. My best bet: one of the old songs of the Companions. Say, the Song of Sinmur.
Aye. You'll have to learn the lyrics and tune from other bards on the island. Don't worry, you won't have to perform. Meet me at the manorhouse when you're ready.
We're asleep. What you see in front of you is my dream-self. As for why I'm unaffected … I don't know. I'm skeptical by nature. Perhaps what the Queen is selling just isn't enough to make me bite.
I'm eager to learn what he uncovers. In the meantime, would you investigate Betar-Nes's home? It's just south of the thane's hall. I trust you'll miss nothing.
In the library, with a pair of smashed skeletons. The Worm Cult, I'm sure of it. But how did they get past my guards?
To help you clear <<1>>, you'll need the battle prowess of a Nord warrior. Say the word and my best is yours!
I'll answer what I can. Be brief, though. There's still much to do.
Excellent. Good hunting!
Take your time.

Tribal clans from far to the west, up against the border with High Rock. Area's called the Reach, so Reachmen. They're nasty, been giving the Jarls trouble for generations. I've no idea what they're doing so far from their clan holdings.
Boneshaper. Worst kind of shaman, one step up from necromancer. They use corpses in their foul ceremonies.
No. I'm proud to ride with the Companions, Ysgramor's heirs! Fallowstone Hall is our lair, just north of town. Always happy to wield our blades in service of the Pact.

None whatsoever. And I wish the burrowers had never broken through. This is nothing but trouble.\n\nOh, I admit, it looks kind of pretty in there. But no miner's going to want to work in a pit that's infested by rolling buzzsaws.
The other mages and I have been trying to force our way inside. We've been preparing the effigies for a spell of our own. Hssk. Their shamans are powerful. Now, with your arrival, we can strike.

The Maormer grabbed <<1>> and <<2>> on the aft deck. I'm not sure, but I think they've also got the carpenter, and at least one of the strikers.\n\n<<3>> and <<4>> are somewhere too, but I haven't seen them.
Kwama eggs are treasure enough for me, thank you. That's what I know, and that's what we'll stick with.
Just doing what comes naturally. And now their warriors are defending the hive.
Words aren't easy to catch. We Bosmer don't force sounds into symbols. So, we'll make them write themselves.\n\nEnter the chamber in the great tree, and slather the blood on the skin hangings within.
The blood will pull the story from the animal skins and into Old Tusk's flesh!\n\nThen we'll seal them to the flesh with fire!
Look for the mine foreman, Gandis. He should know where the Reachmen are hiding, and if any workers survive. But first you must open the way into the mine.
Roasted meat? Smells like a Wood Elf delicacy. Is it lunch?\n\nStrange markings branded into it. Wait. Are these … did he write their story on a block of meat?
Hmm. You don't look like a Maormer spy. I'll need to trust my instincts about you.\n\nThe captain was taken by <<1>> for interrogation. I'm sure you know what that means.

Our ship ran aground not far from that old wreck. The manifest's disguised as a regular book, but it won't take long for them to discover its true meaning.\n\nOnce I'm armed, I'll meet you aboard ship. Go with purpose.
Outside town, dark shamans imbue bodies with corrupt magicka. Take this talisman. Use it to remove the corruption and return the bodies to rest. Then we will turn the Reach's evil against them.
The waters run deep and swift within <<1>>. Even a champion may get swept away if alone.\n\nI can offer a firemage to accompany you on your quest.
You are wise. The firemage I have chosen will not fail you.
If you wish, I can offer a healer to accompany you.
You will be honored with the presence of one of our finest healers. Do not let us down!
Important decisions must not be made hastily.
Do not take too long, Time is not on our side.
I was attacked by a zombie! It jumped right out of the damn lake.\n\nGet out of here! I'm sure it's still around.

Kyne's wings. No, I'm groaning like a stuck pig because it attracts fish.\n\nIt scratched me getting at the fish rack. I'm going to become one of those things! I'm getting hungry for brains. I can feel my hair and teeth falling out.
Oh, you're an expert? Some kind of necromancer, eh?\n\nJust go. The more you talk, the more I want to bite your head.
Bring the Captain to the cave for interrogation. If she is unwilling to speak, I will tear the knowledge from her mind.\n\n-Sameht
I didn't see him, but he must have been big. Huge!\n\nProbably an Orc.

As I thought. They've found their gold in a new employer. If you hadn't intercepted this, we would have been in a bloodbath.\n\nCome. This death will help us twofold. If you are willing to help as well, that is.

The Drublog overran the marketplace, but a few townsfolk took refuge in the Mages Guild and the Trade Hall. Concentrate your search in those buildings.\n\nClear the way and send them to us at the barracks. We'll regroup there.

I think it's worth a try. The Queen's counting on us, and with the captain dead or missing, her duty falls to me!\n\nI won't abandon Velyn Harbor without a fight, and I don't think its people will, either.
The Queen sent us to escort the Green Lady to the city of Silvenar, but the Redguard and Drublog clan got here first.\n\nThe captain knows more than I do, though. I hope she's still alive.

Damned if I know. We heard the screams and saw flames in the residential district. Then I saw the Drublog Wood Orcs and heard the clang of their steel.\n\nThe lieutenant almost ran across the bridge before I could stop him.

He'd have run right into the Drublogs' hands to save the captain, but I saw we had no chance.\n\nI don't know how the invaders entered town without an alarm, but I won't let the lieutenant die for it.
Not my call. But if it keeps the lieutenant from launching a two-prong assault with only one prong, I'll do my best to get them ready.\n\nMaybe we'll get lucky.
Ah, my friend. You misunderstand! You will be the courier.\n\nMy children stole the body as soon as you left. It lies upstairs. Let's see if his uniform fits you.
A simple switch, friend. The Gold Coast waits for orders, and we will give them.\n\nDeliver this altered letter to their captain. Let one enemy kill the other.

Nearby, a pack of werewolves stalks and waits. No doubt they would tear us apart if not for the mercenaries in their way.\n\nAs the Gold Coast and the werewolves fight, it would be best if few survivors live to tell the tale.
New courier? Good to see some fresh blood in the ranks. Now, let's see that letter.\n\nHm. Not what I was expecting. Curious ….
You're relieved, soldier. Unless you want to go werewolf hunting.\n\nWell, I'm not paid to question orders. Time to rouse these louts out of their cups.
Ah, but now they must consider a battle on two fronts. It will give them pause when the second courier arrives. We must close the net, and quickly.
<<1>>? I know she wasn't happy, but I didn't think ….\n\nThe brew! Is it safe?

The blood of a vampire gives strength and vitality, even to those on death's door. Whatever runs through their veins serves to enhance their life force.\n\nThe tiniest amount should suffice to get the King through the ritual.

The hot springs to the north. Rumors suggest the place is haunted by the undead. Wittestadr, they call it.\n\nLet's hope the rumors are true. Of course, you'll also need to get one of them to give you its blood.

The Argonians joked about one of their own during the feast. They called him the Dreamwalker. He watches over the dreams of the people of Darkwater Crossing.\n\nYes, the same place where the trolls now run rampant.

The spirits assure me that this Dreamwalker still lives. He is essential to saving King Jorunn.\n\nWhere he hides, that I don't know. Search Darkwater Crossing for some clue as to where the Argonians have gone.

I am connected to the spirits of this world. Specifically, I have a bond with the spirit of the wolf. This bond has existed my entire life, even when I was a small child.\n\nWhen the spirits called to me, I left my home to seek them out.

I was young and I missed my family. My responsibility to my bloodline finally called me back to Windhelm.\n\nI left the people I grew to love, in the middle of the night, and never looked back. Now we must go to them to save our King.

I found the Ternion monks. A cult, some would call them. But they heard the spirits, just as I did.\n\nThey took me in. Trained me to listen to the call of the wild. To hone my skills. To be one with nature.
He comes from the north, set to arrive at a small camp just outside these gates.\n\nWe must get the letter before anyone from the Gold Coast does.
Search the campsite. If the courier is not yet there, lie in wait for him.\n\nI put my faith in you. Please do not disappoint me.
Let's see. Saved the High King from poison, fought a horde of Orcs to a standstill. Stood with the Pact at a high moot and ensured the alliance didn't shatter. Nah, haven't heard of you at all.
They are mystics. The art of Mysticism allows a Mage to manipulate the flow of magicka. These dark shaman, they pull the corpses from the ground. They drain the remaining magicka from the body.
Mysticism responds strongly to sympathetic acts. Their spell here wards the cave. Symbolically, it's the same energy hulled from the dead. We will set one against the other. Hss.
That's right. To these Boneshapers, the body is just the rind of a fruit. They squeeze it with rituals. Drain the last of the river water from the dead.

No, but I don't want a good officer dying for one that might already be dead.\n\n<<1>> is young, but he's one of the best lieutenants we have. The captain? Let's just say we can always get more like her.

Sharp, aren't you? When the assignment came down for us to be an honor guard for the Green Lady, <<1>> pulled as many strings as she could to get command.\n\nRecognition is everything to her. Fighting isn't.
<<1>>'s atronach is starting to thaw. It's waking up!\n\n<<2>> said this might happen. Something about regular bindings? And now she's gone, no one knows how to bind it!
This land had been mined, burned over, flooded, and abandoned. It called out for rebirth and nurture.\n\nWe three sisters heard the call and came. We tended and restored it.
Not so loud! Laughs-at-Danger is an honest Argonian merchant.\n\nDaril is very powerful, very dangerous, and very expensive.
Quiet! Fine. Go. Don't look for Laughs-at-Danger again!

A ruin to you, but a cradle of life to the plants and creatures that have come to live here. \n\nYour kind consumes the land but never restores it. Fortunately, once you've got what you want, you leave. Then our work can begin.
<The shredded corpse of Nordahl. His injuries don't appear to be from sabre cat claws. If anything, they seem to have been made by human fingernails.>
She does? I'm surprised. The sergeant's one of the hardest fighters I know.\n\nWe can't let up. The captain either died fighting, or she needs our help. Either way, we have to push on.
And you should give it, if only to make amends!\n\nBut I know you mortals. So, listen: the lamias have brought with them treasures—cold, hard treasures. We have no use for them. Take them away.
Until I know for certain, it's my duty to attempt a rescue. <<1>> and her men were on the docks when the Ra Gada landed.\n\nShe might've gotten safely into the lighthouse, but I don't know.

The Drublog hold the landward gate out of Velyn Harbor. I need you to clear the way for the runner.\n\nWhen the road's clear, blow this signal horn, and one of our sprinters will take word to Deepwoods.

We need to alert the rest of the Broken Coast. I want to send a runner to Deepwoods, just in case we can't take back the harbor.\n\nI'll keep pushing forward, on the slim chance the captain's alive. But I've an idea that needs your help.
What are you trying to say?\n\nAt any rate, someone's got to go to the upper floor and check on the rotmeth. I'd go, but my head's pounding like crazy.
Then it could be anywhere! This is an insult. To me, my family! We've brewed rotmeth for centuries!

It's a rocky hill on the other side of the mammoths' corral. We sometimes take them there. The grass gives them a peppery flavor.\n\nI'd go with you, but I'm nothing in a fight. I'll stay here. Out of your way.
What? Can't a guy have a little peace and quiet for a while? Brigands, overbearing brothers, too much honey … I need more sleep.\n\nI was having the most wonderful dream about a bear ….
Oh, all right. I'll get back to work. \n\nI just need to rest my eyes for a few more moments.

Not at all. It's supposed to stand still and keep things cool. But now it's creaking around, taking a swing at anything warmer than an icicle.\n\nI can hunt well enough, but atronachs aren't my usual game.
I knew I could count on you!\n\nIf you don't come back, well … I don't know what I'll do, but I'll certainly do something!
Why should I … I led a Worm Cult cell here. We planned to loot the ruins. Dragon Priests wore powerful artifacts. Masks. And I wanted one.\n\nEyes of the King! You used a summoning spell on me!
We died … died to the Draugr. Maggots take your tongue! The unbound dead bested us. We never even saw a Dragon Priest.
Ah, that's why you're here! Want it for yourself, do you? \n\nToo bad. The Draugr took it from our corpses. And the temple is sealed once again.
My spirit is bound to your geode, yes. You can drag me from Aetherius whenever you wish. So do as you will. \n\nI'll laugh when you die.

You presume you can defeat the massed dead. And an ancient puzzle will just unlock for you? Amazing. \n\nScum, the gates of Forelhost are sealed. The cult might have succeeded, had the Draugr not murdered us. You are doomed.
It's a common puzzle in Nord crypts. There are three runestones. Totem animals on each face. Arrange them in the proper combination and the door is unsealed.
As I said, we were looking for clues when we were slain. Many of these tombs have hints or keyphrases in their ornamental runes.
<The crude figures carved in the rock wall are Nord runes, not the Dragon-speech elsewhere around the temple. The dialect is archaic, but you distinctly make out the words "center" and "snake.">

<The crude figures carved in the rock wall are Nord runes, not the Dragon-speech elsewhere around the temple. The dialect is archaic, but you distinctly make out the words "use three" and "different.">
I will be when we can get back in the meadery. \n\nIt's important to Haraldar that we get this place back in business as soon as we can. I don't want to let him down.

I apprenticed to a brewer when I was young. How different can it be from brewing ale?\n\nThe Voljar recipe books are extensive. I can just follow them. I do plan to add my own flair to the process, however.
No. Inga and I live near Solitude. She came to visit, to help her parents prepare orders for the Konunleikar.\n\nShe wrote to me and said there was trouble. By the time I got here, it was too late.
My clan has always been at one with the forest. We worship Kyne in her most primal form, taking only what we need and preaching to those that would work in the deep woods.

It will help me find my way through her dreams. I enter the Dreamstride and cure people from within.\n\nI've always had this gift. I try to use it for good, but … things don't always work out the way you hope. I try not to think about those times.

We followed lights. Shore lights, we thought, marking a safe route through a horrible black fog. It blotted out the very stars above! All we could see were the lights.\n\nTurns out the Maormer lit them, drawing us closer in till we ran aground.
Terrifying. If we hadn't already been on alert, I don't know what would have happened.
He was. The energy that swirled around him. The host of Worm Cultists, the moans of the dead. I hope never to see its like again.
Sinmur knocked down the wall before we could drive him away. Some of the Mages focused their fire on his head, and that seemed to … annoy him. I can't believe he didn't go down.

Sheogorath! He's made this process insufferable. I translated the last book you retrieved, but it doesn't make any sense.\n\nI can't find anything that might lead us to the next trial. I must be missing something.
By all means. "Circus of Cheerful Slaughter" is just there on the desk. \n\nBut be careful. The treachery of the Mad God knows no bounds.
Really? Hand them over then! Let's get this party started!
<The bones of Sinmur the Terrible are entombed here forever. The heroes Fireheart and Darkhammer sacrificed all to end Sinmur's reign of savagery. The Companions will forever remember their names.>

My wife was ill. This Dreamwalker. He promised he could cure her. By entering her dreams. She swore off practical medicines. Said there were other ways.\n\nThey were lies! I held her hand as her life slipped away. He killed her.

No, I'm … I'm just very tired. Thanks to Shalidor, we were able to decipher the deeper ritual hidden within the tomes as a set. \n\nHe's ready and waiting. Together, you'll perform the ritual that will … hah. Perform. Like a dancing midget!
Then I die. And the Dreamwalker's reagents are lost for all time.\n\nDo it! Take my life! My wife … she waits for me ….

I came here to make them suffer. All of them. To make them feel the pain as I did.\n\nI put blood around the village. Lured the trolls here. I watched them destroy the place. And now, it seems, I hold the life of another in my hands.

Just focus on the task at hand. I've prepared the ritual space, as you can see. Here are the books. Take them, and place them on the pillars of light around the Hall. \n\nThey'll focus the power of the books for the Archmage.

The Mad God is a deranged skeever, that's why it's proving so difficult. There's not so much actual text … the last two have had clues we could use to unravel his nonsense. This one is nothing but nonsense!
No time to talk about that now. I know exactly who you met. But please, I must try to save this one's life first.\n\nThe present now. Then we can discuss the past.
It's Valaste. She's been working day and night to understand these books. Sheogorath has a warped and twisted mind, and I worry that this work is taking a toll on her.

Honestly, Adept, no. Valaste has a singular mind. As long as those books are cursed such that I can't read them, she's our best and only chance. She's almost as smart as I am!\n\nJust don't tell her I said that.

Who says I don't care? Look, we have refugees from all over the Rift here. We've got wounded from the attack, and soldiers staging into the rest of the Smokefrosts. I don't have time to run down every crazy claim.

Of course! This is what we've worked for, all this time. Putting up with the mocking and insults, Sheogorath's poor attempts at humor. We'll recover the isle, and the Guild will have a safe haven from the war!
Maybe yes, maybe no. There's a big demand for daril right now. Nords really want the stuff.\n\nBut something isn't right. I might stop carrying the stuff.
Daril allows Argonians to see the layers of light and sound behind the world. But smooth-skins? \n\nSmall doses may work for smooth-skins, but I don't know. Very dangerous.
And here is your daril. A pleasure doing business. Now go away.
Daril is very dangerous and very hard to get. Demand is high, so price is high.

Then I suggest you seek out Oda Wolf-Sister next. She's a fine woman, if a bit odd. Very fond of wolves.  \n\nGood luck finding her, though. She's usually wandering around in the woods, communing with her beloved wolves.
One of many.\n\nBeautiful woman. Dark hair. Pretty eyes. Like the sea. Asmalah came to me and begged for my help. I knew her chances weren't good, but I decided to try to save her anyway.
Luckily none of my people were lost. But poor Asmalah. He acted out of grief. Out of love for the woman he lost.\n\nI forgive him.
Can't you see I'm busy? Many people to care for, including one who slowly slips away.\n\nI don't have time to deal with strangers until my own people are safe and secure.
Of course. A favor was promised, and a favor you shall receive.\n\nWhat do you ask of me?
Poison? Poison is more dangerous than physical wounds. Some of these vile substances cause dreams to collapse.\n\nNo matter. A promise is a promise. Where is the King?
The Ternion monks! I have heard many things about them! Many interesting abilities are attributed to these monks.\n\nNow I'm eager to visit the Ternions. I'll meet you there.
You've done a great thing, ridding this world of my father. Speak. Tell me your desire and I shall make it so.
They're bath salts! Next you'll tell me that mead is bad.\n\nYou sound just like Grida. Give me the salts!
Hey, she's nice and all, but she's clingy. She was starting to mess with my relaxed attitude.\n\nBut you brought the salts! Let's just enjoy them.
That's a good one! What a joker! A zombie ….\n\nCome on, hand them over.
You have earned my trust, friend. Therefore, I must believe you speak the truth.\n\nTake it. Save the King. But don't make me regret giving this to you.
My blood? Do you intend to turn the Skald-King into one of us?\n\nWhy would you help us stop my father just to create another vampire?
Just barely. Shall we try that again?
Then let's go. \n\nAnd this time, let's try not to take on so many at once. All right?
Some believe that to perform a task for another deserves a favor in return. I am not such a person.\n\nI'll listen to your request, but I make no promises.
Of course you are. Of course. That's your story and you're sticking to it.\n\nTake my blood. Turn your King. Let him become one of us. I look forward to seeing how this plays out!
My blood? You want to turn the King into one of us?\n\nHa! Perhaps I misjudged you. We think alike, you and I. Yes, take my blood. Soon this land will bow to the vampires!
Eh. Have you ever fought a starving bear with a scat rake? No? In comparison, zombies are like sweet rolls. Get on with ya.
Good.\n\nI've had a bit of luck myself. I sent our militia toward the dock. They're waiting for me so we can attack the invaders.

No, we need a distraction so I can get the militia into position. The invaders are unloading supplies … setting them on fire should be plenty distracting.\n\nThe supplies, I mean. Burning's too good for the invaders.

My team will hit them from behind. By the time you're done burning their supplies, they'll be split up and scattered. We'll hit them on the docks while you attack from the warehouse side.\n\nWe'll exterminate them like the vermin they are. You in?

I don't feel the same way about the captain as the lieutenant does … did.\n\n<<1>> was always a bit of a martinet, which isn't bad in and of itself, but I never thought she has what it takes to lead troops into battle.

Nothing … everything. I don't know. It's just a feeling I have. Despite what the lieutenant says … said … I think the Ra Gada landed very easily.\n\nWe should've had some warning. Anyway, nothing we can do about it now.
Sea Vipers, so get ready for some action. The stormwardens probably sealed themselves off by now.\n\nIt's going to be a real puzzle to get in there.
Anything to help explain Jofnir's death. Aelif is certain: it is no coincidence he came here just before he died. \n\nWe will find the connection somewhere in this warren of gears and pipes.
Let Aelif see … this is Jofnir's! His body, here? But why? He was to be interred near his home in Eastmarch.
Oh, you know. Spells, dark magic. Their leader's strategy was to wave his arms and shout. Often. He would hold up some metal thing, like it proved something.
A big Nord, all in black. Only Nord with them. He never came back down the path. Like as not he's still up there, frozen stiff.
Oh, yeah. They were panicked, cut up. The cats, they were on the wounded before they could flinch. I don't think any of those dark-robed bastards made it out of here.
They were terrified. Scared to death. The ruins here … they have a reputation. Folks who go up don't always come back. \n\nThose that do? They tend to be a lot less talkative.
I dragged myself behind this rock when I heard them coming. My fire had already burned out. My only good luck today.
They were the mortal hosts of the Green Lady, when they were alive. For their sacrifice, they're interred here.\n\nUsually, it's quite peaceful.

Not quite. The Green Lady is a Bosmer, and a force of nature. \n\nWhen one Green Lady dies, another one takes the Green Lady's power into herself. Power and soul unite, which creates what we know as the Green Lady.
Yes—normal ruins, with no Men or Mer to ravage its plants and animals. \n\nIt's a pact, mortal. We'll do this together.

I don't know for sure. I expect the souls of the matrons are steeped in the power of the Green Lady, even through death.\n\nI've heard the matrons know all the memories and experiences of prior vessels. One Green Lady, so many lifetimes.
You, help us? \n\nI suppose we have no choice. The serpent women are fearsome and bloodthirsty.
Thank the Stars for that old man. Cannie is hurt, and some of my team members have been taken. We need to get her back to camp. Now that you're here, we can make a break for it.
Perhaps. We were out there looking for runes. Combined, these runes form a key. We only need two more.\n\nTake a look and I'll meet you at the entrance of Ezduiin's undercroft.

The power of malice and fury. Snakes and log-striders lived here in peace, but the serpent women have driven them mad. They are a danger to all.\n\nFind my Sister of Waves, and together, we will stop the serpent women.
In this case, we do. Something in the outside world—your world—drove the lamias into these ruins. \n\nAnd here, they've found a perverse source of power.

I'll keep the militia fighting. We'll keep the rest of the Ra Gada off your back while you deal with their leader. Once he's dead, they'll break, I'm sure of it.\n\nWe've come so far. We'll win this yet!
That mer owes me five gold. You've done well.\n\nJust a moment and I'll assemble the key.

Truly? This is the last time I trust an order to that Bosmer. It fits, though. Ezduiin has been one disaster after another. First, the spirits. Now the supplies. And to top it off, my top scholar and her team are missing!
Stars, yes. Andewen and her team are somewhere in the ruins, looking for the Mallari-Mora. They're long overdue.\n\nIf you're not here with supplies, perhaps you'd go look for them?
Uricantar. He's here. He's trapped the others. He's using their souls to form the gate. You have to stop him.
The gate opens onto a shard of Aetherius. Without the soul binding rituals, the gate will close.
Take my amulet. It should let you see … touch Aetherius. You'll have to make a decision. Break the bindings or kill the students. \n\nJust beware the thirsters.
I can't see them. They must want to speak to you first.
Oh, thank the streams. \n\nDid one of my sisters send you? Do you know of our terrible troubles?

Alas, that seems the only answer. The lamias are led by a powerful queen, and only by defeating her can we bring peace to this place.\n\nLet me gather my strength and I'll meet you with my sisters at the queen's lair, deep within these ruins.

Yes, we did. The Drublog fled the town as soon as they learned you'd killed their leader. We defeated the remaining Ra Gada, other than a few holed up on their ship. We'll take care of them later.\n\nIn the meantime, we made an interesting discovery.
Remarkable. I'm not easily impressed, but you've done it.\n\nAnd Uricantar disappoints, to the bitter end. Such a waste.

From me! My exploding arrows can take out multiple rabbits with one shot. Very effective. But they'll cost you.\n\nSteady-Hand's confident. He won't mind. He encourages challengers to use whatever advantage they can think of to try and beat him.
I knew it. You have the look of a winner.\n\nJust watch where you shoot those arrows.
They mean to invade Vulkhel Guard. Their plan is to use the lighthouse at South Beacon to communicate with their fleet. \n\nWe need to stop them.

You have more important things to attend to? Don't answer, that was rhetorical.\n\nThree of my scouts are being held captive. Free them and have them meet me at Skylight Beach. I'll scout the lighthouse and find a way to gain entry.

Only kills made with the hunting bow count. Kills with any other weapon are disqualified.\n\nYou have exactly one minute to nab the appropriate number of rabbits or to snag Golden Jack. Do either of those and you win.
Your time starts … now!
Try all you want. You'll never beat my record.\n\nBut knock yourself out. Let me know when you're ready.
Your time starts … now!

Wait! I heard what the Worm Cult is after. They're searching the Rift for spirits of Ysgramor's legendary Five Hundred Companions. They intend to enslave those spirits and bind them to the giant Sinmur.
The Captain's wish is my obligation.
Never better! \n\nClever woman, our Captain. Skylight Beach is our old drinking spot. Few would know that. Naming it as the rendezvous point tells me that your message is genuine.
Skylight Beach? Ha! I know just where it is!
No. All I have is this page from my husband's journal. I can't leave this circle, but perhaps his words will lead you to my daughters.
Find my daughters and grant me peace. This separation has been horrible. I want my girls back. That's all.

The lighthouse is solid stone, but even stone can burn, with the right mixture of kindlepitch and fire salts. \n\n<<1>> can tell you where to find the necessary ingredients. Use this glass vial. One well-placed fireflask should be just the trick.
In a while.  \n\nIf we remain at Cragwallow, we'll need to post a guard in case the rieklings return.
<<1>> says the Maormer placed a magical ward on the lighthouse door. I need to figure a way through it. \n\nGo, quickly! I'll locate you when I've found a way to get you inside.

Don't remind me. This ceremony is supposed to show Auridon that I honor our people's culture and heritage. \n\nIt's supposed to show that our ancestors see me as the rightful heir. I guess our ancestors have ideas of their own.
This is what we know: Stral and his elite warriors were tracked to the wood. As soon as we hit the treeline, we saw the hoods and robes.
This magical dagger can cut out a cultist's heart that will magically continue beating. \n\nThe heart can reanimate a cultist corpse, for a bit, and it will tell us what it knew.

She's lying in wait, ready to pounce as soon as I lower my defenses!\n\nI can't complete the Queen's ceremony unless you banish her from this plane. Be careful. She'll tear your throat out if you give her half the chance!
I am Quaronaldil. Once a member of the proud Duure family, now lashed to the face of Nirn by shame. \n\nI had the misfortune to call Essanyon Duure my brother.

My Sister of Rain uses the power of water to heal the injured. My Sister of Waves can use the power of the breakers to crush our foe. \n\nFor this cause, I am willing to put myself at risk. When you ask, I will attack the vile queen directly.
Just this: the lamia queen has already defeated us once. We cannot stand before her power, and must retreat once we've assisted you. \n\nThe final battle is yours alone.
We must push forward or all is lost. Follow me!
Knowing the mage, I only have my best guess. The tiles represent the great constellations. \n\nHe held the guardian constellations in high regard—the Mage, the Thief, and the Warrior.

Ezduiin was home to many powerful mages when I walked beneath the sky. Within this vault lies a magical lattice, very similar in function to the crystal you now hold.\n\nOnly much, much more powerful.
I knew it! That lying skeever scum!\n\nCome, we must show grandfather. I'm certain he will … wait. Is that Sjarakki?
A bit. Not from hunting the Worm Cult. I miss Bleakrock, my family whole and happy. How easy it is to let the best times in your life slip by without noticing.
Nonsense! I feel their presence. We're still connected. Linked by blood. Linked by magic.\n\nThere's so much work to do. So much we still must accomplish. So much energy … to touch … to devour.
We gave them new life! But he stopped us. Because a little blood scared him!\n\nBut now I have my daughters back. We can start again. As a family.
My husband didn't appreciate our work. When he found the bodies, he was shocked. Disgusted. He never embraced the power as we did.\n\nNo. He had to stop us. The fool!
Nothing that concerns you. For the service you provided, you may live.\n\nBut don't follow us. I won't allow anyone to separate my family again!

Why, the ones your fellows are sealing, now that the sphere has sufficient power. Firras is dead, so they can close all escapes without worry.\n\nYou, on the other hand, should worry about your own escape.

If you go up the stairs, an army awaits. Dangerous, but it'd be entertaining to see you fight your way through the Sea Vipers.\n\nThere's another way, if you're interested. Only for a friend of the stormwardens.

There's a hidden sally port beneath a stone table, just around the corner. Give it a good shove, and you'll find yourself outside the lower level.\n\nIt's the last exit to seal, but don't dally. Or let those Maormer cretins see you.
How do you …? My wife is dead, stranger. Leave her in peace.
Tell me you didn't help her! Tell me you didn't bring her and my daughters back together!\n\nNo, of course you did. And now we'll all pay for your mistake.
My wife turned to Molag Bal. She worshiped him! Then she drew my innocent daughters into her cult.\n\nThey murdered people! But that doesn't matter now. Where is she? What's she planning?
They practiced their magic in a ruin south of here. That's probably where they've gone.\n\nShe planned to give my daughters to Molag Bal when I killed her. You have to stop her!

There are two priestesses elsewhere in the ruins, women I trust. If Norion has turned against me, I fear for their lives.\n\nStand with them as they perform their parts of the ceremony. Keep them safe.
I don't know. It mentioned Norion, my advisor. You met him in Vulkhel Guard, I believe.\n\nMy friend, something has gone wrong here. I hate to ask your aid again, but I must.
The Maormer made several camps along the beach. The survivors were split up for interrogation while the others search our ship.
Whatever they're doing, they're sure to have split the crew amongst their camps. That's how they work. Divide, then interrogate, then kill.\n\nThe Maormer show no mercy. They're savages.
I know the Maormer took <<1>> and <<2>>, and I'm fairly sure they captured the bosun and quartermaster too.\n\nThey also took <<3>> and <<4>>.

It was the fog. Thick as the forest, and black as ink. We couldn't see, so kept closer to shore than usual to follow the lights.\n\nMaormer lights, as it happened, not the shore markers we'd thought they were.

<<1>> and <<2>> must be somewhere, but I haven't seen them.\n\nLet's see, who else … our carpenter. Yes, and the bosun. Oh! The quartermaster! Never saw him so mad. One of the strikers, too. The Maormer killed almost everyone else.
This was a normal trip to Velyn Harbor, but there was this fog …. I've never seen such a vile black fog. Dark, thick. It caught us by surprise.\n\nWhen we neared the coast, the Maormer attacked.
As you wish, mortal. I will maintain the integrity of this realm as long as you need.
We will make ready to face the lamia queen, and meet you when our spells are prepared.

I wish I did! The Velyn Harbor militia's hungry for more than meat. They might have come from the forests around Deepwoods, or perhaps they were hiding out in Ilayas Ruins.\n\nTruth to tell, I don't know much about the area around Velyn Harbor.
Velyn Harbor's an important port all right, but if it's so damn important to the Dominion, where were the Green Hunters? Why is a place like  <<1>> allowed to survive just up the coast?

Falinesti has not been seen for generations, but there are many who travel to the Sites. They need food and other supplies while they wait. Very profitable!\n\nIf Walking City appears, well, Jarakh will be pleasantly surprised.
Now that I'm aware of the danger, I can protect myself and those around me.\n\nI won't be caught by the same trick twice.
The Drublog shamans and the traitorous Houndsmen conspired to drain my power, and sever my ties to the Bosmer.\n\nThey used an ancient Daedric ritual, catching me unprepared. It won't happen again.

A powerful Hircine-worshiper known as the Hound. He wants to usurp my place beside the Green Lady. He's a Bosmer; I sense his pain, and recognize his anger now.\n\nThis isn't the first time he's attacked. Stand with me and you'll run afoul of him too.
The town of Silvenar. There, I'll wed the Green Lady and join my spiritual essence with her physical power.\n\nIt's a ritual that happens once a generation, and it will happen again soon.
Excellent. The cultists use the mammoths' ivory for fetishes in their dark rituals.\n\nAnd what of <<1>>? Will she be along shortly?
Oh. I see. There'll be time enough to mourn her, after my work is complete.\n\nThe cultists carve the ivory at their camp. Acquire their ceremonial knife, and we can put a stop to this!
A Worm Cult ambush. Undead rose from the path ahead and behind. What few guards we had panicked and were killed by those monstrosities.\n\nOnly one of us managed to escape. <<1>>.
The Worm Cult ambushed us. It all happened so suddenly. They caught us totally off-guard.\n\nIf it weren't for <<1>>, I'd be in a cage somewhere, waiting for death.
Yes. Sinmur and the Worm Cult are crushed, but Ysgramor's warning concerns me. What could he mean?\n\nFind <<1>>. He should be outside. I must think on this.
A fellow prisoner. The name's Lyris.
Keep it, for the time being. You may need it. If any more of these stones turn up, I'll find you. In the meantime, I should inform the Queen of our progress.
Yes, yes. So you keep saying. I can say I'm a Dwemer King as many times as you want. Doesn't make it true.

To keep their new Dark Elf friends happy! They raided our lands for centuries. Murdered and raped and burned. But now they're our "friends." In my day, Nords repaid their debts. Whether that was gold, honor, or blood.

Yes. Haraldar and Roruld take care of producing mead and running the meadery. \n\nI just help out where I can. Sometimes tossing a rowdy patron out the door, sometimes working on the farm. I'm glad we came here.

You ask those soldiers outside if the war is over! Ask the men on those walls, the ones who grew up without a pa. Or the women who had to be released from some Dark Elf saltrice plantation. War doesn't end. It just stops.

Ha! Wuuthrad. Sinmur. And next Ysgramor himself returns from Sovngarde to lead us into Imperial City, aye? Maybe you're not an assassin. Dark Brotherhood members don't kill their targets with fairy stories.
If Wuuthrad had broken, we'd have heard of it—even out here. You tell me: why should I believe you?

Oh, I see. After ten years "protecting" this pass, no one remembers Unnvald Ironhand. You think I'm some feeble old man. When you were a twinkle in your da's breeches, I led warriors into the heart of Morrowind!
And I told you you won't find any such thing at Fullhelm. Assuming I believed that Wuuthrad has even been shattered: what would a shard be doing out here?
Well, you can rest easy. Nothing landed here, friend. And my Thane has reason to distrust strangers at this hour. It would be safer if you left. Now.
Did she now? Hallfrida is a lovely girl. Her charms will someday make m—make a man very happy. But she's been raised entirely by the Thane. She's naive, and she's headstrong.
I admire her as I admire all my Thane's possessions. She's merely acquired some bad habits in her isolation. I'm sure that with firm instruction, she will prove very companionable.

We need to hold our finest weapons in reserve. I already explained this to her. Well, what can be done? She's just a silly girl, after all. I'll try to make her understand again later, using smaller words.
Well, no. But to control these spirits so completely, he'd have to be close. \n\nThe crypt is a winding complex, with plenty of places for quiet spellcasting.
They're the Cult of the Black Worm, worshipers of Molag Bal. \n\nWhatever they are up to in Abamath, it can't be good.
Abamath's an Ayleid ruin, built on an even older Orc settlement. The Ayleids drove out the Orcs. Turned them into slaves, like as not.
She was traveling with us to Silvenar, a Bosmer city some distance from here. <<1>> managed to slip away in the confusion of the attack.\n\nLater on, she snuck back in and rescued us.
