Abamath was built by the Ayleids over an Orc settlement. Orcs say it's the birth place of the "Blood of Mauloch," their face-painting ritual.\n\nThe mud holds no real power, else their ancestors wouldn't have been cast from this place by the Ayleids.

The Worm Cult took us completely by surprise. Undead rose from the ground and came shambling out of the forest. They surrounded us.\n\nWe dropped what few weapons we had, and they separated us. <<1>> must have escaped in the confusion.

Yes. She said she was able to slip through an outcrop of rocks as our party panicked. Arithiel cut my bonds, then went to free the others.\n\nShe said to meet her here, but I haven't seen or heard from her since she freed me.

Their leader said oathbound avengers will bring an age of blood and doom to the Elves. I think the Worm Cult is plotting to destroy <<1>> and use the remains to sweep across all of Tamriel.\n\nI pray we stop them.
The forest provides its bounty and protects us. The Sigil is the symbol of our bond. Between blood and roots, heartwood and heart.\n\nWe've always kept it safe. Until today.
As usual, sowing discord. However, this sect is different. They spoke about an arcane ritual, and Mauloch.\n\nTheir leader's a powerful necromancer, <<1>>.
Good, for I fear they plot to summon Mauloch himself.

It's true. I once served the Worm Cult, and everyone I loved died by my hands.\n\nWith each death, pieces of myself cracked and shattered, until my hatred turned inside out and I finally saw the Cult for what they truly are.

Yes. Mauloch would sow destruction across Valenwood as an unwitting puppet of Molag Bal. The Worm Cult would follow in his wake, raising an army of undead from his slaughter.\n\nWe need to get past that barrier. Take my soul.

She betrayed her people and joined the Worm Cult. Only after she was forced to murder her own family did she question her choice. \n\nHer word is worthless, but her soul … feed it to this gem, and rid yourself of the traitor.
If you can stop the Cultists with my soul, do it. The stone requires a soul to dispel the barrier, and I am willing.\n\nA fitting, bloodthirsty safeguard for their ritual.

Captain Tendil of the First Auridon Marines. We were sent here at the behest of Her Royal Majesty, Queen Ayrenn.  \n\nWe walked into a trap. Agents of the Veiled Heritance stripped us of our uniforms and gear and left us here to burn.

When the Skald-King calls, the people answer! I should have dealt with the Worm Cult long ago. Before they grew in strength and numbers.\n\nWe must defeat them here. Then we can attack their base at Arcwind Point.
We have a stash at the farm near the edge of town. Return them to us. \n\nI'll personally see that every last imposter dies, screaming for mercy!
In the mountains to the west. It will not be easy to get there.\n\nBut first, we stop the Worm Cult here and retrieve Wuuthrad!
Did you now?

Shor's bones! You've never heard of the Five Hundred? The Companions are the brave warriors that rode with legendary Ysgramor in the battles to conquer Skyrim. We are their descendants, by blood and by bond.
Garil was weak. He didn't understand the need for … moral ambiguity. He threatened to turn the entire camp against me. That was unacceptable.
Spare me your judgments. We do what we must to survive. \n\nI've watched hundreds die from the plague. Horrible, painful deaths. My people are safe here, but they must eat. Something had to be done.
You would doom my people to starvation, or death by the plague? That's truly madness.
Sheogorath must have touched my mind. I could have sworn you just said the silk has been destroyed.
You … you what? Why would you do that?
There's not much time. What do you need to know?
Elenwen. I run an inn here in town, but if you don't hurry up, they'll have it burned to the ground!
Why would the Queen send men to attack her loyal subjects? It makes no sense. But it would be just the sort of ruse the Veiled Heritance would use to undermine her authority.

We were expecting an attachment from the First Auridon Marines to prepare for the Queen's visit. Then this lot arrived and started killing and burning. \n\nWe were readying for a celebration, not a slaughter.
My father, and the man standing beside me! Silly fool.
A group of Altmer isolationists who hate outsiders. They think the Queen has been corrupted by our alliance with the Bosmer and Khajiit and seek to overthrow her.
I hope I have the answers. Ask away.

My assistant Teldur and I were overseeing preparations for the Queen's visit. \n\nI thought it odd that the marines arrived so far ahead of schedule, but decided that fortune favored us. I've never been so wrong.
Canonreeve Valano, Silsailen's chief administrator. The town has prospered under my guidance. Well, until today.
You what? Do you have any idea what you've done?

You sound like Garil. \n\nPerhaps you're right. Perhaps we have lost our way. Those who wish to leave will be free to do so. I can never return. This is my world, now. This is where I will die. Farewell, outsider. May you never know hunger.
It's that simple, is it? Just leave? Return to the outside world and forget what we've done here?
You what? Do you have any idea what you've done?
You really have no idea, do you?
I'm sorry. It's the cinnamon-scented perfume I wear.
It was Garil's favorite. I may have overdone it today.
Yes, Holgunn and I have spent quite a lot of time together since the battle at Fort Virak. Our paths down the river are now one. And in some ways we have you to thank for that.
High in the mountains that separate Stonefalls and Skyrim, my friend. It's worse than we thought: the Planemeld has begun. You're the only one who can stop this fusion from spreading.
I would happily take the chance to gut a few Worms. But we can't. Our blades are worth nothing here, at this confluence of Nirn and Oblivion. You are on your own.
Help me. Please help me.
It burns. It burns from inside out!
Please. Make it stop.
Help me. I can't take this anymore.
You are a capable sort. Stars guard your steps! I'm going to get us out of here.\n\nPut a stop to this madness. Find Uricantar and end him.

What a curious question. But if you insist. I am Telenger the Artificer—renowned genius, author, and explorer.\n\nEzduiin is my latest endeavor. I will bring futher glory and honor to the Mages Guild!
I've come in search of the Mallari-Mora. I'll present it to the council and reap the rewards.
He is … was … one of us. One of Telenger's students. Telenger cast him out.\n\nUricantar is here. He's the cause behind all of this.
Go ahead.
Perhaps the Veiled Heritance offered him wealth or power. They may have even offered to make him Canonreeve of a larger city. Who can say?

The front door is heavily guarded and almost certainly locked, but one of the guards should have a key. \n\nI've also heard there's an underground entrance. An old smuggling tunnel that leads to the beach. That might be your best bet.

We'll … we'll rebuild. When you see the Queen again, tell her I'm going to take on the position of Canonreeve. For the time being. Just until we get things set right. \n\nI won't let my father's cruelty stain our town.
I can't imagine life without performing, my friend! It's too still, too stagnant. Thanks to you, we all get a second chance to make our fortunes!\n\nI mean it. Thank you.
I've been trying to convince Ela to head west. See what we find out there, in the deeps!\n\nBut maybe we should stick to something a bit safer, after all this excitement.
A mixture of kindlepitch and fire salts burns bright as the sun. Toss it into the heart of the beacon and the stone will melt like butter on a hearthstone.
No. Don't want to. So cold.
Don't! Don't hurt me! It was the dead thing, the dead thing in the water! It ate him. It took my father away and ate him. It's still out there. Keep it away from me!
Densorr used to make her this foul-smelling tea. Never had a taste for it, but Yiri loves it. She brewed the last of our leaves just the other day.
There might be someone. A Baandari peddler named J'darzi showed up just after the attack.
Ah, a customer of fine taste! But, alas. J'darzi is so sad. He has but one bundle left. He doesn't know if he could part with such a ….
Such a generous soul! You see, in the midst of this destruction you have made J'darzi's day. Enjoy the finest that Elsweyr has to offer.
White Moon? Father's tea. Pa always said it reminded him of the stories. The peddlers would tell tales around the campfires.

Look for Buzul and Dadazi, a pair of Khajiit; and Alanaire, an Altmer lute player. I don't know a lot about them. We were selected individually, but they're terrific musicians!\n\nI hope you find them. A band of one can't perform!
Discover why the guardians have become silent.\n\nThe Bloodthorn cult is involved somehow, I just know it. But we need more information.
They're gone? You're certain?\n\nI'll never forget those hands, those dead eyes. Thank you. For not letting my father die in vain.
Yes. When the Hound announced the Green Lady would marry him instead of the Silvenar, many Bosmer couldn't believe it. He seized control of the town and a few loyalists escaped, like us.
Nearby. In the ravine. We fled down here to escape the Houndsmen, with the other Silvenar loyalists.

When we arrived, the four of us set up a camp at the edge of the canyon and held a practice before entering Silvenar. Chased out, before they ever heard a note, too!\n\nAnyway, I'm sure everyone's trying to rendezvous there.
They're elemental spirits. They've been part of this land since time began. They nurture the forest and guide us in our work. \n\nBut now they're gone. It's as if they never existed.
She did? She hung back when the rest of us ran. I thought … no, I was wrong.\n\nHave you seen my mate, Dadazi? She was with me, but I fell and had to hide.
Yes. I am sure I can make it to the camp, especially if it means I'll see Dadazi again.\n\nBut, there is one more thing. I hate to ask, but ….
Please, you've got to find her! I twisted my ankle when I fell. I don't know what I'll do if the Houndsmen have her!
Thank Jone and Jode! I twisted my ankle, but I can keep moving since Dadazi's safe.

Our instruments! When the Houndsmen attacked us, they stole our instruments!\n\nIf you search their camps, you'll find them … or perhaps the shape-shifting bastards are still carrying them around. Please say you will find our instruments!
You've heard of me? No, I can see it on your face. It was Laen, wasn't it? She sent you to find me.\n\nHave you seen my clumsy husband, Buzul? The fool panicked and fell as we came down the canyon.
Damn. Buzul doesn't deserve any of this. He's a good mate, even if he just wants to play the drums all day.\n\nHelp him get to the camp, please?
Certainly. I haven't had much trouble avoiding the Houndsmen when I'm alone, if you get my meaning.\n\nOh, and as long as you're going to fight the Houndsmen anyway ….
Thank the gods for small favors. That's a relief! Replacing a good drummer is hard.\n\nHusbands, well, those I can find in any crowd.
The Silvenar gave us each instruments, and they're valuable. If you could get them back, I'd very much appreciate it.

She's all right? She's all right? What do I care? I've been chased by Houndsmen! I've had harsh critics before, but really.\n\nWell, I wouldn't say "harsh." Or even unfavorable. No, the critics have always liked me. What were you saying?
Oh, she does? Well, she can just go ….\n\nNo, wait. You aren't a Houndsman. Why would she send you to capture me? Isn't that what the Houndsmen are for?
If you're a friend of the Silvenar, Laen didn't betray us! She's a jealous harpy, but she didn't throw us to the Houndsmen after all.\n\nWell, now, that's a song of a different key.
Laen's jealous of my singing ability, which she lacks, and wanted to get rid of me.\n\nApparently, I'm mistaken.

Of course! I'm nearly there now.\n\nBut I need to ask a favor. Can you retrieve my instrument? It was a gift from the Silvenar and is precious to me. And if you get the rest of the instruments back, that'd be nice, too.
You saw the same thing I did. We stopped the ritual and you killed Thallik, but Wuuthrad shattered. Thallik used the remaining power of the axe to fuse with Sinmur.

Gravesingers are necromancers that seek power over life and death. They seek to control the realms we would nurture and protect. They call upon the the Daedra who hide in darkness to aid them in their efforts.
You are truly amazing! Hopefully, this will convince the others I didn't betray them.
They think because I'm a Bosmer, I sided with the Hound.\n\nWhen the Houndsmen came, they attacked all of us. As a Bosmer, it was easier for me to get away, but that's it.
They aren't music lovers? And I really think that's it.\n\nWe started playing and a big werewolf, Grimclaw, I think he called himself, went crazy! We can't get to Silvenar with him on the loose.
All right! Follow me. If we leave the camp, the rest of the band should be safe.

Probably! Werewolves have great hearing. I'll prove I'm no traitor to the Silvenar or the other minstrels! You kill their leader and that will be that!\n\nIf you want, I'll play my lute. Grimclaw will come.
Let me know when you're ready.
My soldiers are stretched thin, and they can only keep the Daedra contained until you close the portals. \n\nIf you can cut off the reinforcements, I will give the command to engage.
Aye. Ysgramor's axe is a powerful relic, imbued with the core of his strength. In the hands of a powerful mage like Thallik, Shor only knows what he can do.
This is it, my friend. The Worms are tired of waiting. If we don't stop them, the Planemeld occurs, thanks to the combination of Thallik's power, the might of Wuuthrad, and the essence of Sinmur.
Not until the last of the stones has been destroyed. Only one remains, as far as I can tell.
I'm prepared for anything. If he's sided with this Veiled Queen, he's a traitor. That means we end him, here and now. \n\nAre you with me?
You have to ask, I have nothing to tell you. When you know what you want, come talk to Rejmina.
Perhaps, but the axe shards have vanished. If they can be found, Wuuthrad might be made whole again. The axe's haft still remains though. Grab it and let's get out of here.
No. Yes! Let me be, stranger. Soon I will be able to sleep in peace. Soon.
I will lead the Pact forces to Trolhetta, on the Skyrim border. It is a place of great magic.

Mmm, the dreams keep me awake. Why do they keep coming? Same face, same eyes. Fazaddu tries to stay awake but it's too much. Too much to take alone.\n\nSweet mead is company for Fazaddu. Yes, the sweets will chase the dreams away ….
Because I'm worried, my friend. If not for our success this day, the Planemeld may have spread to all of Tamriel.\n\nSo, I will travel to Trolhetta and see what the Pact mages can tell me.
I must answer your question with a question.\n\nWhere's the Hound? Does he still intend to marry the Green Lady?
The Hound's bond with the Green Lady was based on his presumptions and his reliance on the power of Hircine. Both have proven false.\n\nBut where's the Silvenar?
A brutal end to a horrific tale.\n\nThe Hound thought his childhood bond with the Green Lady was enough to keep her, but the tale of the Bosmer is greater. The city is safe, but where's the Silvenar?
Here, take it with the blessing of Y'ffre.\n\nIn Valeguard, we always know when a new <<1>> is needed. When a new Silvenar and Green Lady are called, so are we.
I couldn't agree more.
I'm in no position to object. Much.
Do you really hate me that much?

Freezing to death. You? \n\nJorunn dispatched me to follow a group of cultists. The damned cats didn't know about my mission. Cut me up bad. I felt like I was going to be fine … until I ran out of wood. It's right over there. Taunting me.
Hurry. You need fire to stay alive up here. And watch out for the cats, too. I'd hate for us both to die up here.
Strike? My friend, you have learned little from me.\n\nNow we must gather our greatest resource—gold.
We'll buy the loyalty of the rest. Jainda, one of the traders, has already pledged to aid our venture.\n\nIf the other merchants contribute, we'll have enough for a tasty bribe.
Moon. Something? White Moon. That's what it's called. Just know, it won't be cheap. He's been gouging anyone looking for a little luxury.

Eraral is mad if he thinks I'll pay for his mistakes! But this now involves all of us.\n\nTake my promise. I'll offer my aid when he wishes. It won't be gold, but it will be of some value, nonetheless.
Don't you think I know that? I hear them practicing day and night!\n\nThis is about Eraral's scheme, isn't it?
Well, I can't offer much, but whatever Eraral wants, he can have. I'd like to get out of this mess with my life and my goods, if at all possible.
Don't repeat yourself. I know what's at stake.\n\nYou'll have support. But make sure Eraral remembers us after he's out of this mess.
He was taken. Taken by the cold eyes in the water. Drowned men. He pushed me away. Biting like animals, vicious. Hungry. Screaming. Oh, Papa. Why won't you stop screaming?
Not what I imagined, but if you insist.
The ballroom? Music? How dreadfully inspiring.
Brilliant! That's the role I was born to play!

The Gold Coast captain was very angry. She and her men and took Eraral-dro captive.\n\nShe said I could go free if I brought this message to you. I didn't want to leave my master, but you can help him more than I can.
At the captain's tent on the hill.\n\nI'll make arrangements with the traders while you are gone. Please, help my master!

We've been under their employ for a short while. I had questions about recent events affecting me and my men. He wouldn't cooperate, so I was forced to take him prisoner.\n\nI won't release him until I get answers.
As you please. But if you make any effort to free him, I'll take action. Swift, bloody action.
<The crude figures carved in the rock wall are Nord runes, not the Dragon-speech elsewhere around the temple. The dialect is archaic, but you distinctly make out the word "plumage" and "right.">
To charge its enchantment, yes. If that makes you or the princeling squeamish, however, I perfectly understand.
As if I had a choice in the matter.
The ballroom? I think I can be of use there.
When I escape, I plan to haunt you and all your friends.
If that's what you want. But what's the point? I'm dead, you know.
I knew you had good taste. I could think of a worse place to spend eternity.
Drama? Really? I already miss my music.
I don't know. Normally people wait to hear the musicians before they set out to hurt them.\n\nDo you want to argue, or do you want to help? I want to rescue the other minstrels, but I'm no fighter.
I've heard rumors of a ritual altar higher on the peak. Maybe you should find a way to the peak.\n\nYou know, before the Draugr kill you.
It … thrives in the cold. Yes. Look for fires around the altar. Light them before you summon it. \n\nTry to fight it in the cold, you'll end up like me. Then we'd have some fun.
The traitor, Firras. He must die.\n\nI will not suffer betrayal in my order. Insubordination deserves death. Letting the enemy into our fortress has called the fury of the storm!
Even if that yarn were truth, what makes you think I have such a thing? Eh? Planning to blame me and slit my throat?

Scum! You act so callously with my very soul! \n\nVery well. Before a warrior ate her face, Madrasa told me the center stone was the snake. And she said the right stone had "plumage." I don't know what that means.
Hss! Not so loud!\n\nTo save us all, continue with the plan. If the mercenaries are bought off, the captain will have no support. She will be easy to take out then, but not before.
No doubt Tabil has already gathered them together, but he's no good at negotiation, I fear. Ensure they get what they desire.
I was expecting gold, but instead they brought entertainers. The mercenaries are less partial to riches and more to pleasure.\n\nI'm no good with such things. Entertainers. Talking to them, I mean!

You are a true friend to the Baandari! I'll tell you what I know.\n\nEach entertainer has a specialty, of sorts, that hopefully matches the tastes of the mercenaries. You'll just have to figure it out, I suppose.
Enough for me and mine to sleep well tonight. The mercenaries have no reason to attack if they gain nothing.\n\nThey are a people without honor. I am glad for it.
Hah. First time the soldiers have mustered out since the end of the Akaviri war. We provided support for Riften's troops, and tended some of the wounded from Virak.
The Cult of the Black Worm …. Worshipers of Molag Bal and all he stands for. They create discord and bring death across Nirn in his name.\n\nWhatever they are up to in Abamath, it can't be good.
My egg-brothers and sisters were terrible. Bigger and stronger. They pulled me out of the pools just to watch me dry out.
The plants, they mean so much to me. Like family along the river's edge, yes?
Children? Their last assault was just weeks ago. The plants, they console me. I lie in their green vines, twine my fingers through the cool leaves ….
She used to be one of my prized students. Very accomplished. \n\nShe's now a high ranking member of the Mages Guild—the Master of Incunabula. She oversees the Arcanaeum in Skywatch.
Assisting me, of course. Andewen is a true seeker of knowledge. She may care for her books, but research in the field is her first love.
Incunabula. She oversees research and training. A coveted position. One that most of my students aspire to, but few will obtain.
Quite attentive. Yes, the Mallari-Mora is an ancient relic. A talisman. Its power took the lives of everyone here. Cursed their immortal souls.
When you put it that way, why not? Here you go.
I bet you don't win very much, either. But suit yourself.
And I will, trust me. I'll do everything in my power to support you.\n\nSince I can't fight beside you, I'll summon a flame atronach to help you stop the Cultists' ritual.
No, actually! They weren't here when we arrived. Though it's merely conjecture, I believe someone has rediscovered the Mora.\n\nThe disturbance of the talisman has caused the bound dead to stir.
Once you're in the sanctum, I'll do what I can to block this entrance, should anything try to join the battle from this side.

Ambitious to a fault. In trying to show Telenger just how much he didn't need the Artificer's guidance, he accidentally destroyed our first weeks findings.\n\nTelenger was furious. He wasted no time in discharging Uri.
To tell the truth, I feared we wouldn't win this fight. The Rift is finally back under Pact control.

The overlay with Aetherius has allowed powerful spirits into the undercroft. They're what brought us down here in the first place. \n\nBe careful. If one gets hold of you, you could get pulled in yourself.
Of course you have! He can't possibly let me go. Can't possibly let me succeed. \n\nIt no longer matters. After you're dead and gone, I'll find new vessels. Draw forth the power I need from them.
I wouldn't have it any other way. Come. Let's see which of us lives to tell this tale.

And I hadn't planned to be here! I planned to take over from the old mer and perform the life-binding with Andewen. \n\nInstead, look at me. This is my last chance for a legacy. To own and control a shard of the Aether!
Only the Stars know for sure. The dig was going well enough—until the spirits appeared.
Such a shame. Ezduiin was once an elegant Ayleid town. A testament to the greatness of the ancients.\n\nTrade and travelers flowed through Ezduiin, right up until the end.
Yes, proudly. I'm just a Student, though. Not that it matters. After I gain the Artificer's favor, I'll be setting my sights on bigger and better things. Like Master-Wizard.

Telenger's assistants have a reputation. Prone to accidents, you know? I told my parents I wasn't interested, but they insisted. \n\nHalf-wits. I am perfectly capable of climbing the ranks of the Mages Guild on my own merit.
No. This one is here to learn. These others seek only advancement in rank. Ejukki seeks true knowledge. \n\nThe Artificer accepted this one based on true skill. Not a bloated recommendation letter.

I'm not sure how much I should say. Uricantar was close to Andewen. And like a son to Telenger. Then things changed. He was cast out. \n\nNow I don't even think Uricantar is allowed into the Guildhalls.

I'm not sure. Some sort of artifact, certainly. It was used by an overzealous cult leader to end his life—and the lives of dozens of others.\n\nThe spirits we struggle against today are theirs, no doubt.
Oh, no. I can only assume our poking around roused them. They must be working to protect the Mallari-Mora.

A mer named Essanyon Duure chose this town as his last stand. He spoke to the gods. And eventually began to claim they spoke to him in return. He began to preach in secret, and his cult came together at the heart of Ezduiin.

Of course! He recommended a cousin of mine during her early days with the Guild. She's now a Wizard. Training to become a Master of Incunabula, like Andewen. I've even heard Archmagister Astrinque was once his assistant.
Me? I'm quite capable. I'm just not stupid enough to risk my life for fools.

Well, no one wants to let the Artificer down. But oftentimes apprentices arrive in Telenger's service on the wings of recommendations they don't deserve.\n\nIf he knew their true skill, he'd know how incompetent they truly are.
Telenger is brilliant, but naive. His knowledge of archeology is vast. His knowledge of the mind and its motivations lacks.

The Maormer carry a magical rune that dispels the ward long enough to gain entry. Steal a rune from one of their patrols near the lighthouse, use it to dispel the ward, and you're in.\n\nYou need to hurry! They're nearly ready to signal their fleet.

No … it is not that simple. We call them the Oathbreakers, but they are not evil.\n \nTheir spirits rest in Ouze until the time of renewal. They must rejoin the Bosmer so our race can be whole once again. The Worm Cult would put an end to that hope.
The Maormer use fire salts to warm their food on long voyages. They should have a supply in the hold of the ship moored in the harbor.
I have stores stashed in a cave on the backside of this island. You'll find a bag of kindlepitch among them. More than enough to reduce the lighthouse to slag.
Did she? How do I know you're not one of the imposters?
Ah! I thought you had the look of a champion about you. To earn the title and represent Geirmund's Hall, you must pass three tests.\n\nA test of might, a test of wit, and a test of spirit.
Daljari holds the test of might. Iroda holds the test of wit, I think. And, yes, Widulf holds the test of spirit.\n\nGood luck!
He's in the town square, just over the bridge. You must hurry! He's hopelessly outnumbered!
The shame Essanyon brought to my line grounds me to Nirn. I have hoped, for centuries, to somehow undo his folly.

No. I saw the growing madness within my brother, and had to act. I spoke with the guard of Skywatch, but not in time to save the targets of his zealotry.\n\nAnd not in time to stop the slaughter of every soul in Ezduiin.
You don't understand. I stood beside my brother for months as the cult grew here. I could have ended his madness at any time.\n\nInstead, like a coward, I stayed my hand. Behold the cost.
Well, I'm a sellsword, so that's not a problem.\n\nNot in the market for gold, though. My boss can smell it a mile away. She'd know I'd two-timed her, and then I'm right back where I started.
She the tough looking one? Ugh, not in the mood for this.\n\nWhatever. I'll see if it's worth it.

Hmm … really? I heard some of the others talk about his technique. Never thought I'd get kneaded on by a Khajiit, but I'll try anything to get rid of this knot.\n\nYeah, sounds better the more I think about it. Good choice.
I've been training all day, and I just want to relax.\n\nGot anything that'd help me with that, huh?
I'm not sure about those Khajiit instruments. I might just fall asleep.\n\nWell, I guess a little sleep wouldn't hurt. Eh, I'll try it.
Ah, I dunno. I'm bored. Restless, like.\n\nI want to punch something. Or someone.
Ah, that fancy one? I think I could break her in half without trying.\n\nThat's the best you can do?
I'm not one for dallying with those pointy-eared Elves, but I noticed a few interesting scars. Heard he has a few interesting tales to go along with them.\n\nThis could be interesting.
Oh, is she the Dark Elf? I liked her moxie. And her biceps.\n\nI bet she could give me a run for my money. Heh, this'll be fun!
Hm. Not a fan of those fancy ones you had prancing in here. I need excitement, not pretty faces!
Yeah, yeah, I know. Sweet-tongued Khajiit told me all about it. Lots of promises, not much to show for it.\n\nSo, when does the show start?
That little one? She did smell nice—like well-roasted venison.\n\nNot that'd I'd eat her, ha! But anyone who can cook like that, I'd be glad to meet.
Ha ha! I saw that one come in.\n\nMaybe I'll have him do a little dance for me. I'll have to scrounge up some grub beforehand. No sense in a show without a snack!
Hrm. I'm not sure about that. Eh, I'll try anything once.
Aren't you supposed to figure that out?\n\nHurry it up, too. I'm hungry, and when I get hungry, I get angry.
Refuse to answer an outsider's pointless questions, for one. I'll catch up with you at the barn later. Now go!
Fine. Grab that bucket from the well and put out the fires. If you find any villagers, tell them they need to evacuate until it's safe. \n\nWhat are you waiting for? Move like you have a purpose!

Like there was nothing for me but blood, and the kill. If you hadn't arrived, I'd be a Houndsman, hunting innocent Bosmer. But stronger, with my power as the Green Lady encouraging others to turn feral.\n\nWe must complete the handfast quickly.
No good, no good. Well, go back in and I will try and patch things up.
No, thank you. I'd rather not drink anything in a Daedric temple.
Damn right!
Yes! Here we go.
No need to get violent. I'll drink it. See? Good to the last drop!
Estre has sealed the castle within a powerful barrier. It's powered by wards and guarded by Dremora. \n\nDestroy the wards and we drop the barrier.
One of the guild mages, Sinien, has a plan. We retook the hall here to gain access to a source of magical power.\n\nHead inside. She'll tell you what to do.
Ah, well. Don't suppose you have about a hundred blades behind you, no?\n\nAll right, then. Time you saw more of town.

No, but my parents were, and I brought them back to the Hist when they died. Though I am not from Hissmir, I plan to remain.\n\nI did not pass the trials my first time, but studied hard and eventually made it through.

Yes, though some disagree with this.\n\nFew non-Argonians bother to come all this way for the trials, so I see no problem with it. If they wish to learn from the Hist, and they pass the trials through diligent effort, why shouldn't they participate?

Two wards power the barrier around the castle. Here in the hall, we focus our will. Shape the tip of a spear.\n\nAlone, we'd be no match for a Daedric Prince. Together, Estre's magics don't stand a chance.
Your first priority: get pressure off the troops. Get out there and put steel or spell to those Reachmen bastards. We need to push them back and regroup.
Locate <<1>>. The troops might have an idea where she's gotten to. We can't lose another capable officer.
A pass cuts through the hills here, yeah? Straight into the Smokefrost Peaks. Normally comes out just north of Riften. But not after that damned giant Sinmur collapsed the hillside.
Aye. No easy way to get through now, to send word to Riften. With what's happened over at Fort Greenwall, we're almost cut off here. Hmm. We'll have to get the fires lit.
Bandits, sounds like. I'm not sure. Only a few of our runners are getting through, yeah? I don't know if they're caught up in combat or what.
Aye. There's a tower on the hill near here. Great big horker of a bonfire set up, with wood treated all special. Light that fire and the whole Rift will see the smoke. Put everyone on alert.
A pass cuts through the hills here, straight into the Smokefrost Peaks. Normally comes out just north of Riften. When a giant hasn't collapsed the hillside.
Aye. No easy way to get through here or send word to Riften. With what's happened over at Fort Greenwall, we're on our own. Hmm. We'll have to get the fires lit.
Aye. There's a tower on the hill near here. Great big horker of a bonfire set up, with wood treated all special. Light that fire and the whole Rift will see the smoke. Put everyone on alert.
Bandits, it sounds like. I'm not sure. Only a few of our runners are getting through. I don't know if they're caught up in combat, or ….
You're welcome to try, Ebonheart dog.
Please, I don't want to drink that!

That is beyond me. If I have to guess, I'd say this isn't some minor piracy, but the spearhead of an invasion. But I'm no officer—I fight for a living.\n\nAnyway, burn the supplies and that'll get their attention. Ready?
I'll order the militia to strike when we see enough smoke. If we can catch them by surprise, we'll drive the invaders toward the lighthouse.\n\nIf not … well, it was an honor.

Fist of Thalmor

He fought when others fled.
He died while others lived.
He rests in peace while we await judgment.

In his memory, we stand on guard.
He and Sinien are already inside. We have one more portal to close.\n\nThe High Kinlady Estre clutches to Dagon's robes. Hides within the Deadlands.

When I came to Velyn Harbor, I wasn't certain how I'd be received. I brought along a guardian to protect my trade goods, but when the Redguard attacked, I didn't want him killed needlessly.\n\nI think it's time he joins the fight.
Terrible. I trusted Estre. I allowed her to use me, and my people have paid the price.
Okay. If you change your mind, come see me.
I'll whistle him up. He'll follow you faithfully, as long as you stay in Velyn Harbor.\n\nOnce the fighting's done, he'll come back to me.
The Thane's fest doesn't attract just drunken brawlers. Some real champions come to spar as well. \n\nYou want another challenge? Seek one out. Then we'll see what you're made of.
That's all I need to know. Look, I need to get these men to safety. You, I need back in the field.
Up the hill here is a bloody great signal fire. Specially treated wood. When it burns, the smoke it sends up will be visible all the way in Windhelm. Get out there and warn the Rift. Go!
You found one!
I'm ready when you are.
Another five minutes and I would have been an undead. Thanks for being prompt.\n\nHelp me with these bindings? You've got work ahead of you, if you're here to help.

Simple, until the lighthouse begins to burn. You won't be able to come out the way you went in, and you can't sprout wings and fly away. \n\nTake this teleport scroll. It will transport you back to the rendezvous point at Skylight Beach.
Garron isn't leading this whoreson lot. It's a pair of nobles, siblings by the name of  Varaine and Allene Pellingare.\n\nThey're not going to give up without a fight.

They've raised an army—plenty for you and me to handle, but they've gotten it in their heads that they'll storm the royal district and take over the city with it.\n\nWho knows what kind of power Garron promised them.

You have my thanks. With your help, we may have the situation contained before the public catches wind.\n\nI'll head back to the city, find the Pellingare head and let him know what's happening. Maybe get you some armed assistance.
He's clever, I'll give him that. He's making too much money not to be doing something shady. I think we can help open the authorities' eyes.

Thank you for that. I'm not really fond of these kinds of events, but the thanes insisted. It's good for the people and good for the alliance, they said.\n\nIf only we had been able to get the palace ready in time for all this.
I support the Nords. Let's leave it at that.
Clans from all over Skyrim, dignitaries from the other Pact nations. I'd be a fool not to expect trouble.\n\nBut I trust Thane Mera and the Windhelm Guard have matters well in hand.
We come to celebrate alongside King Jorunn and our Pact allies before business commences.
Pact business. We support each other, but there is still so much to resolve.
You really need to visit the Sober Nord Tavern. The bard that performs there is phenomenal. And easy on the eyes, too, if you catch my meaning.
I'm here to work and earn gold. The idea that I could be a Covenant spy is simply ludicrous. Ridiculous, even.
You didn't, did you? Then how did that even enter the conversation? Forget I said anything.
My cousin, Lupandinus, accompanied me here. We heard that Windhelm didn't have any true alchemists, so we decided to set up shop here and make our fortune.
Make sure you stay out of the back alleys. I heard that poor Kwelen was roughed up and robbed behind the bank. Such a terrible thing.
Not as much as I could be. We need more forest-related events. There isn't even a proper log chopping contest!\n\nAnd I really don't like those Stormfists ruffians. They can be so pushy and mean.

My whole family loves trees. My little sister, Agnedir, for example. She's apprenticing with our cousins at Bonestrewn Crest. Good trees out that way.\n\nI just wish she'd write to me more often. I haven't heard from anyone out there in weeks.
If you need a weapon, nobody sells a sharper blade than Meling Snow-Bourne. Her family really knows how to make metal hold its edge.
That's what they claim, but my Nord friends also like to … what's the saying? Pull my braids?

That's the strange part. Logging Chief Jafelma has never sent me on a wild netch chase before. And her letter sounds serious. Even got Thulvald himself  to go check on the logging camp, and he never leaves the city.
I was really hoping to get assigned to the wilderness. I tried to get a spot at Thulvald's logging camp, but he had more loggers than he could use. Oh well. Maybe next season.
South of here. Past the royal work camp at Cragwallow. They say that part of the forest is haunted!
Doors. Lots and lots of doors. With some old runes above them, the kind you see at these mounds. We tried lots of them, but they never seemed to lead anywhere.
Leave that to my giant friend. He knows just how to get you inside the fort.
One of the documents you recovered indicated that the mammoths are difficult to control.\n\nIf you free a few of them, that should distract some of the Stormfist soldiers while we assault the walls.
Stories are told here, and by some ancient magic, made to come to pass. Strange people, strange customs.\n\nI came to find inspiration in the spinners and their lives. They are a curious lot.

Perhaps you should ask why my packages are so valuable. Some of them are somewhat … less than legal.\n\nNords and Dunmer think my face is forgottable, but I'd still prefer to do business with no name.

The fortress has a north gate and a south gate. One of the notes you took off the scouts says that two locks secure each gate.\n\nFlip the switches atop the towers to unlock the gates. The giants will rush in and we'll split their forces!
As spiritual leader of the Bosmer, he symbolizes the Green Pact between the Bosmer and Valenwood.\n\nTreethanes, kings, and warlords bow to him, yet the Silvenar's power is intangible. Curious, no?
Never bow to authority, especially when they want to cut off your head. Now go find that giant!

I'm not surprised you ask. Few worship Z'en these days, though his shrines once spanned the whole of the Valenwood.\n\nHe is the god of toil, and payment in kind. Fitting we make the Wood Orcs pay for their actions!

The Knahaten flu decimated his faithful. They say Argonian Shadowscales infiltrated our worshipers and spread the flu, curse them!\n\nWe are the last of Z'en's followers. If we fall to the Drublog, none will be left to keep the old ways.
You don't get to know everything, mortal. \n\nDoes that frustrate you? Just know that some grudges are ancient and some answers are beyond your understanding.

Don't you know where you are? This is a sacred place to the Orcs. The ritual arena of Malacath. When you blow the horn, you'll signal the giants and challenge Lob at the same time. He'll have no choice but to follow the rules of the arena.

Almost certainly not. In addition to the Stormfist legion that Fildgor Orcthane put into his command, Lob travels with a dozen of the fiercest, most savage Orcs you will ever have the pleasure of fighting. They're really quite impressive.
You would abandon this cause that you have worked so hard to advance?\n\nIf that's what you wish, go. I won't stop you. But I think you'll be back. We all have a desire to see what happens next.
Queen Ayrenn has arrived. She is just outside, with her retinue. This one is certain she'll want to hear your report.\n\nGo. We will speak again soon.
Wonderful. I'll have Amuur make up another batch of aloe straight away. I hope it wasn't any trouble for you?
Sorry, sorry. This is about my fourth day without sleep. Are you feeling well? Can I help you?
Does it matter? No matter which way you go, the world is a dangerous place.\n\nThen again, anywhere is better than here.
Why do you think I'm standing alone in the middle of nowhere?\n\nWell … I'm not exactly alone. You're here. Lucky you.
Boredom and ennui here are better than terror and fear anywhere else.\n\nI've accepted my lot in life. It's a crushingly hopeless empty life, but it's mine. All mine.
If I knew how to get that damn rabbit, don't you think I would have caught him by now?
Place this flask of Altmer ale in Bar-Neeus's supply chest and then notify Guard Bronorr at the Fighters Guild. You'll be rewarded well when it's all over.
Bah. Rumors spread by jealous rivals. My goods are all on display; I sell no illicit merchandise.

I erect the spine of warning. My wares are all on display. All customers receive courteous service and fair prices. No one gets special treatment or secretive deals. Perhaps others would better meet your needs.

Yes, yes. Well done, well done. Let's move on, then. Here's the second riddle.

I float in the sky, I cover the land. 
I can carry your weight or slip through your hand.
Hah! You're doing better than most. Now for the final riddle:\n\nWhere are the oceans dry, the mountains flat, and the sky can never be seen?
Good. That's good. Now that you've cleared a path, I'll try to get out.\n\nShor! Not dead yet.
Let me guess. The Prince wants me to attend his war council.\n\nWait! What's that smell? You! You dare approach me covered in the blood of my kin?

You invaded their territory! I'll consider your request, but for now take this salve. Its odor calms the wolves. It should last long enough for you to return to camp without going on another murderous rampage.\n\nTalk to Thane Jeggi. He likes meetings.
Shor's bones, I was ready to murder you. Some bastard just tried to kill my niece. That's him. Gutted like a fish.
Not a surprising plot from a Dunmer, especially that one. Sarisa would rather lie and steal than accept charity.\n\nAllow me to express my gratitude in coin.
Go ahead. But avoid the entrails. No telling what he's been eating.
He's a damned skeever, coming after a young girl with a knife. Yiri just lost her father, and now this man tries to kill her? What would the Worms want with Yiri?
Then do it quickly. We're running out of time.
The spine of welcome is more effective than that of threat. Deliver this package to Sarisa. I choose to extend friendship when others express hatred.
They took us off-guard. Came in quietly, in row boats. Snuck right past the Auridon fleet without so much as a "by your leave." We never saw them coming.
South Beacon's on the west coast. There's little more than a strait between here and the Summerset Isles. Historically, it's been easy to defend.\n\nI wish I knew how they made it past our fleet.

Most were thieves and highwaymen before they joined up. I offered them a fresh start. Now they're some of the best scouts and assassins in the Dominion.\n\nUnfortunately, those skills don't help much in a standup fight.
Ask anything you'd like. You've done more than enough for us already.
Ask away.
<<1>> is a mentor to us all. She's one of the finest scouts in Tamriel. She personally created all of the most commonly used maps across the continent.
My father was a sailor. And my grandfather, before him. My ancestral home was full of Maormer war trophies. \n\nLet's just say my family has had their fair share of run-ins with the Sea Elves.
Heh heh. Truth? I get terribly seasick. So much for tradition, eh?
Damned unusual. Auridon has one of the finest fleets in all of Tamriel, but they slipped through our patrols without raising an eyebrow. It's like they knew our precise movements in advance.
Not among this troop. I'd trust any one of them with my life. But they're getting their information somewhere.
Fleet movements, navigating the bay, the layout of Auridon—it has to be someone pretty high in rank. Damned peculiar.
I'm not going anywhere. Go ahead.
He's too quick. You can't line up a shot. Vurila almost got him, but it wasn't on purpose. Those exploding arrows of hers. She fired at something else and almost caught Golden Jack in the blast.
We were practicing stealth techniques on the beach. They came out of nowhere. Rushed us. They cut down half the troop before we could blink.
By the skin of our teeth. <<1>> and I were both wounded. We obviously didn't make it very far. I think <<2>> may have gotten out alive, though.
That Argonian? Aye. Never trusted him. Too friendly. Heard the rumors surrounding him, but there's never been any evidence to justify kicking him back into the river.
I … found proof. Canonreeve Valano … member of the Veiled Heritance. Didn't want to believe. \n\nI confronted him. He … tried to escape. Captured him … brought him here. His men were waiting.
I hired the Colovians beyond our gates to protect us. But now, they're more of a threat than anything else.\n\nSoon, they'll tire of our excuses.
The young ones' eyes shine at the thought, but I won't let their blood be shed for my actions.\n\nAnd to act, I must know the Colovians' plans. Perhaps you'd be willing to help?
I'm glad we understand each other. Take Sela and go. And make sure she never returns to this place. \n\nShe is obviously a woman of taste. Cinnamon, to be specific. And we all get so very hungry.
Troll's blood! Now we've got him. I'm gonna enjoy this!
Now we celebrate.\n\nFollow me to the balcony.
No! Too late for me. Must go! Stop Valano … before he escapes.
Yes, yes! Just him. Please, hurry!
Searching for his money, is what he meant. He's convinced Father had a cache of gold somewhere in the bottom of the mine.\n\nBut if Father had such a cache, he took the secret to his grave.
What haven't they been doing? Kidnapping, murder, necromancy—you name it, they've done it. Captain Viveka hoped to stop them, but we failed.
For many years now. I've been waiting for him to save me.

And from something worse. It chose me. Forced me to infect Indaenir, as he was once called. The Silvenar now, one who should be pure.\n\nIt's a spirit. Malevolent, terrible. I left my memories to guide Indaenir toward healing.
I sense him, like a prey senses its predator. That's why I thought you were he.\n\nHe must trust you very much, to allow you into his secret.

Since my fellow Green Hunters killed me, I've been prey for Hircine's huntsmen. They stalk, kill, and devour me. When I awake, the hunt begins anew.\n\nAnd meanwhile, Indaenir became the Silvenar. One with a dark past.
Extinguish the spirit I infected Indaenir with, and I can rest at last.\n\nHe must confront it, and drive the impurity out before he truly becomes the Silvenar.
Well enough. It's good to have a reason to get up in the morning. Without my family the way it was … it's easy to wallow in thoughts of Bleakrock. Of the good days.
The hunt for this Clan Matron. That's what I do, now. Denskar used to say I latched onto things like a momma bear. Wouldn't let anything go. Now I use that instinct for the Pact.
Thank you. When I was raising kids on Bleakrock, I never thought I'd be here, doing what I do now. But I'm good at it.
After my breakdown … some of the others pulled strings for me with Pact command. As I was training, we talked about what I would do. This seemed the perfect fit.
After Bal Foyen … I had a hard time. Losing family is never easy. I couldn't handle it. Even the others from Bleakrock just reminded me of everything I'd lost.
Well enough. It's good to have a reason to get up in the morning. Without my family the way it was … it's easy to wallow in thoughts of Bleakrock. Of the good days.
This investigation. That's what I do, now. Denskar used to say I latched onto things like a momma bear. Wouldn't let anything go. Now I use that instinct for the Pact.
After my breakdown … some of the others pulled strings for me with Pact command. As I was training, we talked about what I would do. This seemed the perfect fit.
Aye, my dear old friend. I had no idea when I passed into the Rift that we'd be seeing so much of each other.
This trouble. This is what I do now. I've been sent to investigate the attack on the thane.

There's not much to tell. Bastard asked me for a private conference, said he had something sensitive to tell me. When we were alone, he pulled a knife. I had to crush his scaly neck with my bare hands.
Not a thing. To think of all the days I let that scaleback drink my mead. Live in my hall. Bah!
Keep that to yourself. I won't have Nimalten fall into chaos. We're on his trail. My advisor and the court mage search for any hint of the cult as we speak.
I need to do more research. I need to consult a book in the thane's library to be certain. I'll meet you there as soon as I can.
Don't touch me! I'll kill you, you hear me? I'll kill you!

Everywhere is dangerous in wartime, my friend.\n\nThe Mages Guild doesn't take sides. Our scholars travel across Tamriel, so we have guild halls in every big city. We welcome scholars from every alliance.

"Dealing with Daedra is no trifling matter. Fortunately, we have a way to ensure our safety, if not victory. Assembling the shards will cause the Daedra to gain influence within Tamriel, but destroying the completed item throws her back to Oblivion."
Ah … yes. I did it. I turned them to stone. But for a good reason!\n\nIt was the only way to protect them from the savage beasts.

My advisors are my confidantes, my bodyguards—they fill multiple roles. We were en route to my wedding with the Green Lady. When the Drublog attacked, they were slain or taken.\n\nTwo survived: Raen and Sariel.
The Drublog used a foul spell to trap me; I've never encountered it before.\n\nThat same energy prevents anything beyond this Psijic contact. I can't escape without your help.

A warrior. He's my military advisor and a bodyguard.\n\nHe fought hard during the ambush, but was overwhelmed. If you free him, he can advise you how to battle the Drublog, but I fear he was severely wounded and may not be able to fight.

As <<c:1>>, I'm the manifestation of the spiritual strength within every Bosmer. But I must join with the Green Lady before my role can be fulfilled.\n\nThe Drublog attacked my retinue on our way to this ritual. We had no time to ask them why.
The youngest of my advisors, Ambassador Sariel's visions give guidance when those twice her age see no clear path.\n\nShe could help you find out how to free me.
Woof!

Cities are cosmopolitan, or should be. City folks tend to be more tolerant, and most guards prefer to avoid battles in the streets.\n\nInside a Nord drinking hall, all bets are off. For some reason, Nords have grudges against the Altmer. Imagine that!
Stranger! You stand in the presence of greatness!\n\nAre you here to buy me a drink, or would you rather tell me how amazing I am?
Uh, not long. My son was its first victim, bless his heart. I'm not really a healer, just the town alchemist. \n\nBut I couldn't just sit by and watch people suffer.
Actually, we just ran out of salloweed. A big patch grows just outside of town. Will you gather some?\n\nAmuur's already got the next batch of salve prepped. Just need the sap to get back to work.
Salloweed aloe. It seems to hold back the illness for a time. I apply it to my patients as soon as they show symptoms. \n\nIf their condition worsens, though, we put them in quarantine.

The Colovians drink our wine and eat our food. They are waiting. For what, we must find out.\n\nI've heard of a courier's arrival within the hour. I need his message before it gets into Colovian hands.
A matter of gold, and a matter of pride. They've demanded more than agreed upon. Suspicious, yes?\n\nI believe they weigh two contracts—ours and another's. They wait on news from Colovia, by courier.
The one and only! My words are sung in drinking halls from Windhelm down to Daggerfall.\n\nI've written enough epic poems to fill a library of the Mages Guild!

You're a grim sort. You're not here to drink, are you? \n\nLet me guess. You're one of those boring literary types. I'm plagued by critics! And I've never earned the recognition I deserved from scholars.

I knew it! Just a matter of time until they came to me. \n\nA cute Khajiit asked me for one earlier, but she ran off. Something about a drunken fool. Her loss! She left her book on that table. It's yours!

As I said, I am not sure, which is why I must see that missive before it reaches the mercenaries' hands.\n\nPerhaps it is nothing. Perhaps it simply says to leave. But I cannot hold my family to "perhaps."
Oh. They did? That's unfortunate. Very unfortunate.
Yes, actually. If you could pass out the aloe to some of the villagers, I'll be able to send Amuur to treat those farmhands straight away.\n\nNew patients popping up every day.

Hmm? I'm sorry. My mind is drifting. Very tired.\n\nSome of the local farmworkers must have been touched by the plague. I'll send Amuur and some of the mercenaries to treat them. Thank you for telling me.
You're not afraid, are you? Stay strong, my friend. We'll find the heart of this corruption.
Not terribly fast. But I can make it. Just lead the way.\n\nI'll be right behind you, bolstering our spirits with song!
I'm sick? Stars. I suppose it was only a matter of time. It is my barn, after all.
It's about time! My family helped to found this Stars-forsaken town. You'd think I'd be one of the first to get treated.
Salve? What? Does that mean I've got the plague? Stars above. Mother won't be able to bear this.
Thank you! Here I thought my biggest problem was keeping the farm. Now I'm worried about catching the plague.\n\nThe Stars move, I suppose.
The High Kinlord didn't know of her treachery. He let her into the city and … that was it.\n\nWe lost touch with Rilis after the gates to the Deadlands opened. I hope he's still alive.
You've done what you came to do. Get out. And don't dawdle. \n\nBad enough I have to deal with these dirt farmers. Now I'm dealing with their diseases, too.
Hendil's done so much for this town, all I can do is trust him. Wish this wasn't happening to me, though.
He's here. He piled in right behind the Battlereeve. Said something about supporting the Marines and the guilds.\n\nYou know how he is.
I am as you made me, Master. A magicka memory matrix. A place to hold safe your dearest memories.

Research entry. As I suspected, the Worm Cult plans to use bound Companion spirits to empower Sinmur. I've found evidence they're gathering in the crypt beneath Nimalten. The footprints lead from this fireplace, here …. What? No!
Yes, Master Drendruf. Your notes on the Companions indicate they once bound powerful heroes as eternal guardians. I cannot recall any other information on this subject.

Estre dropped a barrier around the inner castle. We'll need a way past it, to get at the portals. I think the Battlereeve and the guild leader plan to crack that thing like an egg. The frontal approach.

Yeah, I heard her. You'll need to beat the last Nord's time. Drink ten mugs from the keg. \n\nYou might want to take a bite of food every few drinks. That'll soak up the mead, so you don't get sick. You ready?
Didn't recognize the face, but the armor. That was my old armor from my campaigning days.\n\nI had no idea. All this rage, this hatred, must have been bubbling within me for years.
Behind you is a stage. Beside the stage is a keg. The brew inside the keg could drop a mammoth.\n\nYou think you're tough? Drink the brew, then recite Geirmund's Oath. That would be impressive.

Lord Geirmund, great battlemage,
saved the Rift in Harald's age.

He slew the wicked Gauldur three,
and set their father's spirit free.
<The audience cheers.>
You're a smart one! We'll need to stay here to power the ritual. You act as our focus, our agent in the world.

I rode with Ysgramor and the Five Hundred. I stood with the greatest of us all against the giant Sinmur. I gave my life to bind and watch over Skyrim. Until the rise of Alduin the World-Eater, my blade guards this land.
Tucked away, for now. I thought it fitting I kill you both together.\n\nDon't think you'll get out of here alive. Our contract with the Khajiit is now null and void.
What? More Khajiit trickery?\n\nI tire of this banter. See if your words are so sharp when I cut that Khajiit's throat!
He's dead then. I think I knew it, deep down. Vikonn kept my locket on him always. After Sinmur attacked, Vikonn was gone. At least now I know. Thank you.
Yes, it's mine, I'm afraid. That's how Flavia always referred to me. She was a dear cousin as well as my acolyte. Flavia vanished when Sinmur attacked Riften. May Mara grant her soul peace.
Yes. My wife, Pria, had it on her when Sinmur attacked Riften. I'd hoped she was still alive and would come back to me someday. But she never will now.
Ah, but I have an army at my back. I don't walk into a fight unarmed, unlike your Khajiit allies.\n\nAll the easier for us to cut them down, I say.
Ha! Not on your life.\n\nMaybe if we feel charitable, we'll round the Khajiit up and sell them to slavers, instead of killing them outright. I'm not averse to profiting from this debacle.
Take this talisman, find the wards. One's in the east wing of the city, the other in the west.\n\nJust point, focus, and we'll do the rest.
It's got to be colder. Out there. Than it is in here.\n\nPlease, build us a fire. Warm us up, and we can go.
I've spent some time studying these monoliths. I've managed to create a little magical fob that imitates their energy.\n\nEssentially, it will make one of the ursines your furry friend. For a time.

Back in the bad old days, before the Pact, Fort Virak sent necromancers up into the Rift. They thought to overwhelm us with undead.\n\nGrandfather stood against them with Bonebane, and crushed the assault. His troops called it the Battle of the Bones.

Grandfather would tell you it was to honor everyone who died. But that's not true. You can't see it from Fullhelm, but you can certainly see it from Fort Virak.\n\nThat's no mistake. It's a big waggling finger in the enemy's eye.

He said he found the sword at the bottom of an ancient barrow. When he was younger, he was quite the adventurer.\n\nHe claims it was held by one of the Five Hundred, and that a beautiful ghost gave it to him.
Sort of? Grandfather likes to tell his stories. After the Battle of the Bones, he laid the sword in a chest and swore he'd never raise it again.
My Thane, look! This stranger wields Bonebane! \n\nThis stranger must have stolen it! What more proof do you need that they plot against you?
It would be Razum-dar's pleasure to fight by your side. \n\nFollow. He shall lead the way.

Very good. The Gold Coast mercenaries are nothing if not skilled at fighting. The werewolves will be no match for them.\n\nHonorable Eraral-dro spoke highly of your skill. We'd hoped you'd follow through with our little deception.

Kill the commanders in the mercenaries' ranks. Make it look as if they fell to werewolves. You'll need a paw from a werewolf for the right marks. \n\nThat should distract them for a bit. Eraral-dro will be at the gates when you return. Be safe, friend.

<The audience boos.>
Yes. Yes, I am. Thank you. I just couldn't take that first step. I felt safer freezing to death than I did trying to leave the cave.\n\nDamned but the mind is a strange thing.
I see your point. Well, here's to "deep cover."

Yes, it was. I refused to believe the rumors about Estre. I allowed her within these walls against the will of my advisors.\n\nI'll make it my life's goal to make amends.
For Ysgramor! The Hall will be ours once again!
See you back at the Hall!
To the Hall!

Thanks for coming with me.

His tomb was built upon this lake,
and in his name this oath I make.

Should evil come, should night descend,
I swear the Rift I will defend.
The alchemist is paying us good coin to keep things locked down. He doesn't like folk sniffing about.\n\nBut, uh. Maybe you have some good coins, too?
Are you crazy? Look, there's no way anyone without a pass can get in there. One of these expensive, irreplaceable passes.
Be quiet, touch nothing. Don't worry, this'll just be between the two of us.\n\nCode of honor. You understand.
Well then you're not going in there! Get lost.
No! She's the love of my life. Nothing you can say will change that.\n\nI just wish this cave wasn't so dangerous. The poor thing gets scared around these strange mushrooms.
Marry it? That's ridiculous. I'm already married!\n\nAnd I'm always careful. I never bring up marriage with another woman. That's just asking for trouble.
It's a damned shame I lost my pass. I'll have to get a new one. In a few hours. If I remember.
Then they care about you even less than I do. Get out of here.
Beneath this island lies the tomb of Lord Geirmund. He was a hero, long ago.\n\nAre you familiar with Geirmund's Oath?
Beneath this island lies the tomb of Lord Geirmund. He was a hero of long ago. \n\nAre you familiar with Geirmund's Oath?
Beneath this island lies the tomb of Lord Geirmund. He was a hero of long ago. \n\nAre you familiar with Geirmund's Oath?

She? Of course. Beautiful women love my poetry, especially the bookish ones.\n\nI have something … darker … she may enjoy. They love the dark stuff, especially my sonnets. Makes them feel … vulnerable.

I have a book of sonnets she might like, but I would prefer to deliver it to her personally. Feel free to peruse it.\n\nIf this maiden wants a … private reading, I'd love to meet with her. Somewhere romantic. Perhaps a graveyard at midnight.

Agreed, but … my injuries are worse than I thought. I'm useless as a fighter, so I'll keep to the shadows until you've cleared a path ahead.\n\nPlace the remaining <<mz:1>>. I'll meet you at the sanctum's entrance deep within the ruins.
Merormo leaves me here to die. And he doesn't even mention me?\n\nStars take him! I'll kill that traitor twice.
A mage. He teleported us all here and started casting some spells, and. Oh, that really is a nice pair of boots you're wearing. Could I just see—
Oh they're somewhere back there. I couldn't get <<1>> or <<2>> to give up their shirts. And I really wanted <<3>>'s pants, but he refused. Misers. \n\nYou're sure you don't have anything to trade?
Imbecile. The planners wouldn't. The builders would. Their slaves were too stupid to remember the rune combination. Haven't you seen something like this before?

All we know is my grandfather died because he listened to that skeever's lies.\n\nI am Thane now. I will lead as my grandfather showed me long ago, before he left his senses. With a strong hand and sharp mind. I'll keep his legacy alive.
<words words words. I had good intentions. Please don't tell on me>

I want him remembered as he was, before <<1>> poisoned his mind. We'll burn him on a pyre at the memorial to the Battle of the Bones, his greatest victory. \n\nHe will be remembered, no matter how inconvenient the Jarls find it now. I'll see to it.
What's he hiding? \n\nI'm not sure I understand all of this, but I was right! This plague, or whatever you want to call it, is all his fault.
No idea. But it's clear—whatever's going on has to be stopped. \n\nPlease. I know you barely know me. But my sons are all I have. I don't know if I could go on. If they were to ….
The quarantine? But everyone's sick down here. Am I going to die?
So tired. You have to find Hendil. Don't want to die.
Tancano, my son. He's sick. I've been trying to hide it. But everything's gone wrong.
I just want my son back! Not this monster. \n\nPlease, don't hurt him. I can still make this right. I can still—

My son. He feeds off of them. Then he bends them to his will. They become his thralls. \n\nI've been bringing people down here since he first got sick. Once I find the cure, I can set everything right!
I don't know. They were under Tancano—the monster's—control.\n\nI don't know what will happen now that he's gone. All we can do is hope.
I understand. I don't … I don't deserve freedom. Report me to Netanwe. She can take me in. \n\nI can't face all those families. Can I wait here?

<<1>> was insane. Tearing out people's souls with the shard, using that dark energy to transform into a lich. Disgusting. She got what she deserved.\n\nI must gather my surviving troops. Grab the shard and meet me outside.
What? He's a monster! Who could do such a thing?\n\nNelulin. Did you find him?
Thank the Stars. \n\nWait, what about Iwelien? He's been in there so long!

Yrna Stormcrag carries decent wares. She learned her craft from the best there is—me! \n\nAll of the traders on Merchants Row sell quality merchandise, although you do get what you pay for. Just tell them I sent you.
It can get a little crazy, especially when we have a festival. I can't wait to see the eating contest. It's always exciting! And now I'm hungry.
Have you seen the handsome Dark Elf hanging around the forge? He's so exotic! And he's a noble! We're going out tonight and I can't wait! I just know he has something amazing planned.
I wholeheartedly agree! But it also makes me a bit sad. It reminds me how much I miss Queen Nurnhilde.
Ah, beautiful. Look at this handwriting—
Oh, aye. But these are the only songs the Thane wants to hear. Reminds him of his reaving days. No skin off my back, long as he's paying gold.

Do I look like a Nord? Ha! I'm a traveler like you, friend. I play where the money's good, though Thorulf's been a bit stingy in that regard.\n\nLast time I mentioned what I'm owed, he threatened to slit my throat.
Lovely! One day, I'll be singing songs about you.\n\nAs for me, I'll soon be slipping off to find a friendlier tavern to play. <<1>> may not be entirely pleased when she notices the missing key.
Why, from the nightstand of the lovely <<1>>. I don't think she's noticed it's missing yet. It was a busy night, and she's an … energetic lass.

Well! How interesting. I'd planned to slip in myself, collect my fee and be off. But if you're willing to risk your head in place of mine, I'll not stop you!\n\nSettle my debts and the key to his room is yours, friend.
You little skeever. All a ploy to cheat me out of my hard-earned wages, eh? \n\nFine. Take they key. I know when I've been outplayed. It's time to cut my losses and be on my way.
How did you know that? My older sister, Ragna, serves as the Nord envoy there. She was hoping to make it home for the Konunleikar, but she couldn't get away.\n\nI hope she's well.
It's the celebration. You know how it is … cheap bunks for cheap drunks.\n\nPa had to hire extra help, and he never does that.
<<1>>. He has such interesting scales, the nicest eyes … and his tail is rather dazzling.\n\nMaybe Pa will keep him on after the celebration.
Help my grandfather make things right. What Thorulf tried to destroy, we'll make stronger than ever!\n\nAs for that thieving, lying skeever … we'll see to him in due time.
Most likely on the platform in front of the palace, looking out over the city. She loves this city so!
I wish I had those skills! No, I just sell this stuff. What I really want to do is write! Like that Fjokki guy. His poems are so romantic!
What doesn't she do? Windhelm would fall apart without her constant diligence. Between the Konunleikar, Pact business, giants, and the King, it's a wonder she has time to do anything at all!
I know Daedra-worship isn't fashionable these days. But really, who's Sanguine ever hurt? I mean, maliciously.
It's just Sanguine! Everyone in the swamp has visited the temple at least once. \n\nYou should go. It's in a cave east of here. You'll have a great time!
The animals here are normally very tame. Energies in the wood. Now they're vile and bloodthirsty. I believe they've been possessed by Daedra.
I don't know? I don't know. \n\nThe beasts are insidious. And we Altmer never bargain with Daedra.
To even consider summoning one of those monsters. It'd be inviting a death sentence.\n\nThe atronachs, at least. They're more constructs than … no, a death sentence.
Even a shard of the mighty Wuuthrad is a potent artifact. My ancient axe still has power left. Use it, hero!
Hmph. Think I pulled a muscle, and it aches real bad.\n\nDon't go spreading this around, but someone to knead it loose would really hit the spot.
Ah, no. Not exactly. Was hoping for some refreshments beforehand, but I don't know what's decent around here.\n\nIf you have anyone who can make a good sweetroll, that'd be great.
Aw, I didn't mean it like that! I'm just looking for a little friendly competition, you know?\n\nGot anyone that could go toe to toe with me, you think?
The captain will have no one to support her should you attack. If there ever were a time to rescue Eraral-dro, this is it.\n\nPlease go quickly, and make sure he hasn't been harmed!
I wish I could! That pig of a Centurion doesn't trust the people here, or Riften's guard. Tells me not to listen to rumors. If something's going on, you need to shove the proof in his face.
This debacle is all Merormo's fault! These beasts, controlled by Daedra? All his idea. \n\nHe was trying to create animal soldiers. Fanged shocktroops with the ability to reason.
My nephew. Yandir. Went off to join the fighting and—damn it! I just wanted to stop spending our blood. My sister will never be the same!
He did what? Why would he do that?
What? Do you have any idea of the seriousness of this accusation?
Perhaps. To us, it is simply our home. The Mabrigash have protected this valley for many years. \n\nSometimes life here can be harsh, but serving the Ghost Snake gives me peace and purpose.
A long ago war in our homeland led to famine. But the legendary farseer Hareth heard the Ghost Snake whisper in her dreams. She led our ancestors here, and here we've remained.
No. Some leave us. If it's in their nature to wander, they go. \n\nWe honor our vows to the Ghost Snake. The outside world only occasionally intrudes upon our peaceful existence.
Hhmph. Mages. Fine, fine. Thank you for speaking with me.
Then follow me.
I sent <<1>> to a local dragonshrine. More Worm Cultists were seen around the shrine.\n\nWould you see if she needs any help?
Nurara! The Dark Elf noble's daughter. Isn't she the elk's antlers?
Maybe she'll come watch when I win the bragging contest. I'm an avalanche! I bury the competition!
Well, that's an opening Innbild would have jumped on. Lucky for you, I'm not my sister.
Sorry. It's just that whatever I do, Innbild gets all the attention. Even the stupid bard is in love with her! And I get to serve the horkers upstairs.
What? Never seen a Khajiit that wasn't trying to kill you? The day is still young. Who knows what it will bring?
We're always on the lookout for important and rare manuscripts. Books of a magical nature are especially in high demand.
Dremora? Why do you ask? Have you encountered a Dremora? You must tell me all about it.
Well, it is called Vale of the Ghost Snake. You aren't wandering around the Vale of the Nix-Hound, you know.

Of course. Don't be an idiot. We hunt them for food. Their fangs make great tools and adornments, and their skin has all kinds of uses. \n\nWe honor them and protect them. We only kill for what we need.
Indeed. We found a defensible position and have held them back, thus far. We have no idea what's going on. Why are the Reachmen here? How did they get mixed up with the cult?
We've tried everything. Even some things I'm not proud of. \n\nAn undercover agent named Belron, who joined us in Shadowfen, has narrowed it down to two options. One cruel, one not so much.
I know, I know. The very idea disgusts me. To stain the river with your own hands. But I see no other way. The cultists have sworn dark rites to Molag Bal. They cannot be broken.
The sooner I'm clear of this place, the better I'll feel. Speak with you soon, soldier.
Necromantic energies gather in the heart. It's the seat of life and unlife. Everything I need to know about a person, I can learn from his heart. Hmm, I suppose I am a little obsessed.
Oh? The recipe's in my pack, I'm sure. Don't know where my pack's gotten to. Why would you need—\n\nYes, my sweet? What was that, you said?
Ah, very nice. From <<1>>, right? Rather fetching! Even if she is high strung.\n\nThank you, my new friend!
Your kindness shall be remembered. Until we speak again.
At the bottom of the ruin there should be a totem powering the death shroud. Destroy it, the shroud goes away, and the living can enter the ruin.
We offer the same goods. By eliminating him, we claim a prime location and remove a direct competitor.
Let's just say Bronorr has been looking for a reason to boot that Argonian out of Riften. You don't need to know more than that.

Death, Reachmen, now the Worms. I need to check on my family. We have a little farm down south. My wife's father started it, actually. \n\nStop by and say hello, if you get the chance. Tell her I sent you. Woman makes the most amazing sweet rolls.
Canonreeve Valano, an agent of The Veiled Heritance? That's a serious accusation. I hope you have proof!
Look down. I've made room for a new heart in our friend here. Put your new trophy in its chest. Then stand back.

Oh, I'm testing them. Much like I did to <<1>>. Each now resides in a small world of their own making. I'm fascinated by emotion, the power it holds. \n\nI'm afraid to say, but … they're not doing very well.
Oh! What a splendid idea. External stimulus in the mix. Here, I'll open portals to their little worlds.\n\nSucceed or fail, this should be simply fascinating.
Yeah? Perhaps I'll be having answers for you.
Not for one who's hoping to supply the drinks for the handfasting!\n\nI know the Bosmer have their own brewers in Vulkwasten, but perhaps I can put a new twist on their tastes!

It's east of here, past Deepwoods, near the center of the continent.\n\nI've been thinking of going there, to study Bosmer brewing tricks, but with the attack on Velyn Harbor, I'm worried the road is not safe.

Truth to tell, I don't know a lot about it. It's a combination wedding/coronation. I guess it only happens every couple of decades, and the next one is coming up! Should be a huge party, and a great chance for me to make some money!

Velyn Harbor's the main shipping port for Malabal Tor! It's the only trading port open to the Dominion not rife with piracy and corruption.\n\nIf we don't get organized, smugglers'll start going to places like Bloodgutter and we'll lose our profits!

Just northeast of here. It's always been a haven for pirates and smugglers. I don't know for sure, but I think they came under attack the same time Velyn Harbor did.\n\nHmm … could be an opportunity, there. Oh, wait—never mind! No smuggling here!

Maybe to you, but it's no joke to us! It's hard enough getting Altmer, Bosmer, and Khajiit to all fight together against the other alliances. Getting them to trade with each other is a nightmare!\n\nStill, with the trouble come the profits.

As my crew and I sailed up the coast one night, we were accosted by a sea hag and a pack of ensorceled sea dogs. We resisted her charms, but before I could give her the boot, she cast a spell and cursed my eyes to blindness.
Aye, my ill-gotten gains from conquests untold. To be honest, I was surprised my crew left me with as much of the treasure as they did. Feels good to know there is honor among thieves.
Aye, and as the pirate's life has no place for blind Captains, my crew marooned me here with boxes of booty from my quarters.
Not until he hands over his treasure. Unless you think you can handle me and my friends, don't bother me.
Why do you ask?
Whoa, whoa, let's not do anything drastic. I'm sure we can work something out.\n\nTell you what, if the old man splits his treasure with us, we'll get him to Anvil. Deal? Deal!
What's it to you? The great <<1>> terrorized these waters for years! It's a pleasure to deal him the same hand he dealt others.\n\nI'll take all the treasure, with or without his permission.

They're up on a plateau west of Velyn Harbor. You can see them when the weather's clear.\n\nAs I undertand it, the place used to be a seat of power for someone called a "stormwarden." I don't know more than that.

It's an area north of Velyn Harbor and the Bosmer tell me it's where the current Green Lady was born.\n\nShe is, or will be, or was, one of the Bosmer rulers. Something to do with a wedding or a coronation. I really don't know more about it than that.

You should talk to Thane Jeggi, as well. If he isn't drunk, he should attend the council.\n\nMeanwhile, let me rub this salve on you. It has a scent that will keep the wolves from attacking you. It won't last long, so I suggest you go back to camp.

I've never been to  <<1>>, but I hear it's a haven for smugglers, pirates, and thieves.\n\nIf I were the Ra Gada, I'd go there to recruit some of the less-savory types. And then the Green Hunters could just wipe them all out.

The Green Hunters are agents of the Green Lady, who represents Bosmer physicality. They're her scouts, her warriors, and her enforcers.\n\nThey'd clean out <<1>> if they had a chance. Fiercer warriors never lived!
Firsthold is where High Kinlord Rilis XIII rules over Auridon. While Skywatch is the capital, he's chosen to stay here due to the close proximity of his ancestral family home, Castle Rilis.
It's where High Kinlord Rilis' father ruled and most of the family is now buried.
High Kinlord Rilis XIII is the current ruler of Auridon. He's a great leader. As all leaders, he has his share of enemies, but overall, he's very tolerant and listens to his people.

Only that her point is valid in the eyes of the Altmer. He wishes to remain neutral. High Kinlord Rilis strives to maintain peace amongst his people. The last thing he'd want is to be in the middle of a war between Estre and Ayrenn.

The High Kinlord greatly respects and revers her. He's extremely close to duty and believes in the order of things. While he agrees with her cause, he's reluctant to take an official stance on the views of High Kinlady Estre.
While I appreciate the Queen coming to Auridon, all this talk of the Veiled Heritance has me worried. I don't want to be caught in the middle of their own personal war.

Yes. What if the Ebonheart Pact or the Daggerfall Covenant attacked, just to find us fighting amongst ourselves? It's foolish really. I heard the Maormer invaded South Beacon, too! It's just one more thing to worry about.
Certainly more than the Veiled Heritance. While I sympathize with their cause, it seems foolish to wage an almost civil war here in Aurdion while there are greater issues at hand.
Only that I hope she rots in Coldharbour. She brought this Daedric curse upon us. Worshiping Mehrunes Dagon! It's unthinkable!
