I pray you jest. Daedra worship is strictly forbidden. Only the insane would even consider it. Hence, High Kinlady Estre and her madness.
Nothing good can come of that Daedric Prince. Out of all of them, he'd be the most feared. Some govern over realms that may be viewed as neutral, but his is everything evil.

In a word: destruction. He also governs over change, revolution and ambition. You could say those are more neutral, but look at Estre and what she's done. Her ambition's brought nothing but destruction.

I wouldn't say I fully support them, I just understand what they are working toward. Altmer are certainly at a higher level of existance than Bosmer and Khajiit. It's only natural that we'd like to separate ourselves.
Of course, and why not? We are more directly decended from the Aldmeri. We're far more civilized and intellectually advanced. We're not cannibals and don't look like animals.
I sure hope Ayrenn wins! Not that I know much of either, but if the Queen is fighting for the Dominion, this Bosmer is on her side.
My guess is I'd be on the first ship outta here! I don't want to stick around anywhere I'm not wanted. I only came to Firsthold to make a profit, but this attack sure has set me back.
I tried to focus the spell from here. The wards are too strong. It took immense concentration, and the effort drained both my magicka and strength.
Indeed. The magicka surged, and I couldn't control it. Auri-El knows I wish I could be of more use. \n\nCouldn't take on a Scamp, the way I'm feeling.
Good. <<1>> and I are done with Horseshoe Island for now.\n\nThis place used to seem so far away from everything, but it's as busy as Sentinel these days. Time to move on.
No. <<1>> says the island's thick with Maormer. Guess I need to trust her vision now since I lack my own.\n\nThe chests are buried in the caves. I trust you know how to use a shovel?
This Konunleikar is very unusual. Clans have come from far and wide to compete, including some we haven't seen in many years. It makes it difficult to predict what will happen.
Meling is my sister. Most of my family deals in trade of one sort or another. We all know our business.
Of course! But you need to guess. What do you think my event is?
What? We've been putting on this charade for a pile of bones? Is that all he has?
Hmm, this barely covers our expenses, but I suppose it'll keep my comrades' knives out of my back.\n\nBest not walk away from this mess empty-handed.

After hearing bloody tales of the great <<1>>, I'm not surprised his crew dumped him here with nothing but memories.\n\nNo deal. A worthless bag of bones won't pay his passage. Only a fool would take that payment.
Terms have changed. No treasure, no transport.\n\nUnless you have something to sweeten the deal, I'll find a better mark.
Aye? What did he say?

Aye, but at least I have what we came here for. I suppose I'll collect some water and mudcrabs for a Crustacean Stout while <<1>> seeks transport.\n\nAssuming the Maormer don't kill me, I know this island well enough to survive.
<Searching carefully through the books, you spot a small, folded note among the pages of one tome.>
<You take the note from between the pages.>

Yes. And to do that you'll need to get past the mercenaries. The unsmiling thugs at the door won't give me the time of day. Maybe one of the others could be convinced to help you? \n\nOr maybe a disguise? I don't know.
Because of you Silsailen survives to rebuild and the Veiled Heritance's plot to undermine my rule has failed.
No! My boy. My Iwel.\n\nHendil. Where is he? Where is that bottle-sniffer?
<A stab wound to the chest was the cause of death. Blood and hair can be seen under the fingernails, signs of a struggle.>
<The face of this corpse has been slashed. Numerous knife wounds are scattered around the torso and hands.>
If we don't try, then we have lost already. We shall try. And if the Hist favors us, we shall win.
What a ridiculous question! How can we not? The alternative is unimaginable.
If you're going to drink in Windhelm, you better drink mead! Voljar's Meadery makes the best mead, and the Cold Moon and the Sober Nord both serve the stuff.
Oh. Of course, sorry. My younger sister is in there, has been for almost a week. I just hope my letters cheer her up a bit.
Thanks. Me too. \n\nI'm off to collect more letters. Stars protect you, friend.

Don't know. Only Hendil and Amuur go down there, really. The guards go inside sometimes to leave food and my letters, but they don't go much past the entrance.\n\nThey won't let anyone else go in there.
My letter? How did you ….\n\nOh, what does it matter? Please, just find Rilyn. I need him here.
There's a cave, to the southwest. We were supposed to meet there tonight. Bring him back to me, I beg you.
Those jerks over there took it. See if you can get it back, why don't you?

I noticed peculiar standing stones. They weren't here last year. I'll bet they've got something to do with whatever's happening.\n\nIf more of the faithful come to the Summer Site, they could walk into a trap.

It's one of four sites visited by Falinesti. The Walking City moves, or moved, with the seasons, traveling between its Fall, Winter, Spring, and, of course, Summer Sites.\n\nThis valley was once the Summer Site.
Those of us who seek the Walking City. We believe Falinesti will return someday, so we travel the same route the city once took.\n\nWe won't abandon our search for Falinesti, or its people.
You don't understand. She was a prisoner there! I freed her, and now we can finally be together!

Should I let them starve? The Falinesti faithful dream of finding a great city to take them in. They bring few supplies, sit in the forest, and hope the Walking City will appear.\n\nMercenary? Perhaps. Jarakh disagrees.
Velyn Harbor. I find markets and report to my fellow traders. The Summer Site does not look promising, however.\n\nStill, if you find out what's wrong, perhaps the market will improve.

So the legends say, but there are many legends. Some say Falinesti travels other worlds. Others believe it misstepped and fell into the ocean. Darker tales say it was taken into Oblivion.\n\nBut Jarakh is not an expert. Barothlas may know more.
I think so. The lighting, or whatever it was, burned me, but Jarakh has put some salve on my wounds. I should be up and around in a few days.\n\nPerhaps the Walking City will arrive by then.
Don't come back to me without it!

Of course! I understand why people might think it's never coming back; it's been gone for years. But the Walking City traveled Tamriel for centuries, perhaps even millennia, before it vanished.\n\nIt'll come back. It has to.
I went up to the standing stones at the edge of the valley and there was a big flash.\n\nNext thing I knew, I'm on my back with burns all over my chest. Still, this beats having a city drop on you!

Don't you see? The Walking City doesn't just walk, it arrives! If a city appears out of nowhere, it could kill those waiting for it!\n\nI think the lightning-magicka is a warning. Falinesti's on its way!
He better or Harnald's going to get an earful from me. Get him to the dragonshrine.

Me? No. He's the spiritual heart of Valenwood. The power of the forest courses through his veins like blood.\n\nFrom what I hear, you can tell that from looking at him. The Green Lady's lucky, if you ask me.
Nilara's only treethane because her aunt, and now her cousin, were the Green Ladies.\n\nTreethanes are supposed to be servants to the village, but Nilara acts like she's in charge.
She lords it over everyone else! Wouldn't hurt to see her cleaning up the area.\n\nDoes she think this village maintains itself?
I should help Jorald clean up. Then I'll go to Riften. My aunt and uncle work at the Withered Tree. They're the only family I have left.
So what are we waiting for?
Escort the scout to the ritual site and stop those cultists! She's ready when you are.
You've done enough. You saved my life and avenged my parents. I have nothing to reward you with, but if you stop by the Withered Tree in Riften, my uncle Wilrek might.
There's no time! Once the magicka fades ….\n\nOh, never mind! Meet me in the small cave past the menhir, across the planks. Quickly!
Junk? I gave you more credit than that! Those are my treasures.

They're priceless treasures! The flagons are from the finest inns throughout Nirn. The bones came from a giant fish that once swallowed my ship.\n\nAnd the meat's from an ancient white mammoth I caught and killed, barehanded. Priceless, I say!
That skeever won't get any more from me. A deal's a deal.\n\nHe never asked what the treasure was, did he? It's not my fault he might've expected gold, is it? Hah!

Aye, and don't get any ideas about snagging a piece for yourself. It's tasty and fermented, but it's all mine.\n\nThe Elves can have the bones. I hate to part with them, but I suppose I'll have to let them go.

Yes. There are many theories about what happened to the Walking City. I believe it was drawn into Oblivion and trapped there, with all its population.\n\nAt last, I've found a way to open a portal large enough to rescue it.
My husband was one of the thousands in Falinesti when it disappeared. I love him, and won't stop working at it until I've rescued him.\n\nAnd I'm not alone. You can help me now.

Near each of the standing stones in the valley is a nearly imperceptible Oblivion tear. Leftovers from my earlier experiments, but they're letting Daedra in.\n\nA mortal's touch will close them. Once one is closed, the other three must be shut quickly.
First, I must time my ritual with each closure.\n\nThis area is unstable, and the tears would open up again in a few minutes. I can't both close the tears and perform the ritual. I need your help.

The second reason is the Daedra will open a portal in the valley and summon more of their kind.\n\nYou must fight your way to each tear, then meet me at my laboratory within the northern cave. Are you ready?
Good. I want you to speak with two members of the Queen's court, <<1>> and <<2>>. They await assistance from the guard, hands I can't spare just now.\n\nWho do you want to speak to first?
Does it? Then they must be blocking the city, too! We're too close to give in now.\n\nYou must stop them! Clear a path for the city.
Taken below, all of them. Tovisa tried to escape, but they took her too. They'll be mutilated and murdered, like all the others. You must save them.
It's about time! Steel and stone, you've got to get me out of here. I've got to reach my Moroth.
He's there. Trapped with the rest of the Talon troops. Has to be. \n\nLook, I'm not the one the Daggers are after. They're after my Moroth.
That can't be true! All these years … all my research. They all point to one thing: my husband is trapped in Oblivion!\n\nDon't you see? We must try again!
Have you no heart? I want to save my husband, yes, but also the entire city! I've tried for so many years. I can't give up! I won't!\n\nI'm going after them now!
You can't be … you're not ….\n\nNo, you're right. But I'm convinced my theory's right, too. Falinesti's in Oblivion. I must find it. I will try again.
I see you prioritize well. You'll find him at a warehouse west of here. Be sure to tell him that I sent you. \n\nOnce you've finished with both of them, report back to me on the town's upper level.
You'll find the steward at a warehouse east of here. Be sure to tell her that I sent you. \n\nOnce you've finished with both of them, report back to me on the town's upper level.
They'll have set up to bombard the lighthouse. Standard tactics. So, we take out the artillery first.
Ah. Ahh. In that case, you'll do nicely.\n\nMy servant followed a burglar to this warehouse. The ignorant knave stole a set of marine deployment plans for the Queen's upcoming speech.
Well, I'm sure I wouldn't know. I'm no burglar. In any case, we can't let those plans escape.\n\nThey could be used to bypass the Queen's security. And we wouldn't want that.
We're all about Dwemer relics and ruins. But the Worms have ruined everything, destroyed lots of artifacts. And the Draugr are everywhere now!
It'll take more than a Dunmer's rusty blade to send me to Sovngarde! \n\nJust give me a moment and I'll be back on my feet.
She has family at the Withered Tree in Riften. Snow-Shod clan. Good folk. I'll make sure she gets there safely.\n\nAs for the long term, well, all wounds heal in time.
Not very long ago. Raerana's still recovering. They're upstairs, if you want to see them.
I've taken a liking to Raerana. I'm going to stay and help her through this. May even give the Snow-Shods a hand.\n\nWho knows? Maybe one day she might just fall in love with me.
The poor man. He always had the worst luck, but he never let that stop him. I think that's what I loved about him most. I'm sure he was trying to get back to me.
She was a sweet girl. But she had a knack for being in the wrong place at the wrong time. I'd hoped to keep her safe in a temple of Mara, but Sinmur's attack put an end to that dream.
She was the light of my life. I thought of her all day at the forge. I don't know what I'll do now. There's nothing left for me here. I don't want to talk about it anymore.
We were as close as brother and sister could be. Svein was always there for me, the best big brother ever. And now he's gone. Excuse me, I need to go kill something.

Oh! All right, then. What was it? Right, the supplies. \n\nTwo of my cooks took deathly ill, right in the middle of preparing the Queen's feast! I suspect sabotage. I want to be sure all of our food supplies are safe.
I'm not upset. Not at all!\n\nI'll examine the supplies in here. You, go to the warehouse next door. Make sure everything is fresh, and there's nothing out of place.
Oh? A pity. \n\nKeep the plans. You can give them to the captain next time you see her. In the meantime, I must attend to the queen.
Thank the Stars! You found the problem.\n\nHold on to that. The captain will want to see it.
Feh. Some kind of criminal feud, I'm sure. \n\nNow then. If you have some other task, you should be about it.
The advisor? Yes, yes. Far end of the docks, to the west. Can't miss him. \n\nFair day!
I wasn't here. I went into Riften to visit the market. When I returned … please, let it not be true!
Ah, help from the captain. Excellent. Inside, we've cornered a dangerous mer. \n\nHe's wanted by the crown, has valuable information, and threatens to kill himself every time we approach the door.
I need him alive. Just get in there and get him talking. Don't listen to what he says, he's half-crazed.\n\nYou get him talking, we move in behind you. Got it?
They're coming. I know you're just a distraction. Listen closely.\n\nCaptain Astanya is corrupt. She's a member of a group called the Veiled Heritance.

Veiled Heritance. They're planning an assassination attempt on the Queen, at the temple.\n\nThey bribed members of her staff to get the speech moved here, where they can have the captain in their pocket.
No. Prison will interfere with my research, so I will not be going.
Oh? A pity. \n\nKeep the plans. You can give them to the captain the next time you see her. In the meantime, I must attend to the Queen.
Thank the Stars! You found the problem.\n\nHold on to that. The captain will want to see it.
Don't worry. He'll receive a fair trial. The captain is always very even-handed in her pronouncements.
Stop right there. On my authority as captain, you're under arrest—under suspicion of conspiracy to regicide!
I've seen him around. Seemed a little odd, not especially dangerous. But he may know something. See if you can track him down.
Mere luck. To my neighbors who suffered, I extend the claw of succor. They have but to ask to receive aid. My success enables me to be generous to those in need.
Riften is a challenging place to do business. Success breeds jealousy, especially when one is an outsider.
It is as this one said. Razum-dar is your new friend. But then, this one's friends call him Raz.\n\nYou may have noticed your last new friend, Fasion. He lies dead on the ground behind you.

You must get past the captain's men. Seek out another of our lady's agents, Eshaba. She stands watch in the marketplace, peddling her wares.\n\nAsk her for a souvenir of the First Marines and she will set you on your path.
The captain happened. Fasion and Raz worked together as agents of the Queen. Fasion was not willing to give up secrets. And so now Fasion is dead.

We're talking about justice here, for my family and all of Riften! Don't you think it odd that Sinmur spared Bar-Neeus's stall and demolished ours? Rumor has it he's in league with the Worm Cult. Are you with them or us?

What's that in your pack? Deployment plans for the marines at the temple. And do I smell the taint of poison on the air? These are the tools of an assassin!\n\nIt's no use arguing, scum. Not another word out of you.
Razum-dar. Yes, I know the name. You haven't answered my question, though.
The guard captain? Absurd!
Hmm. We've taken every precaution. The whole area is locked down. Watch Captain Astanya assured me.
I suppose now you think you're morally superior to us. Tell me, how hungry have you ever been?
Your point being?
Interesting. Raz knows Mathiisen's Canonreeve. Malanie. Would not have suspected her. If she's donned the Veil, she's probably running the show here.\n\nExplains something, too.
Astanya? I can't believe it. No doubt Urcelmo will triple his watch.\n\nShe truly was an agent of the Veiled Heritance?
Betrayal? She turns against her people after years of service? And she spoke of my betrayal? \n\nShe obviously could not be trusted. But you have proven your worth.
The marines are blunt instruments. A queen must have a lighter touch. You've met Razum-dar, first in the Eyes of the Queen.\n\nWould you join him? Become an elite agent for the good of the Dominion?
Ah, ah. No need to get all dry-scaled on me. The answer she seeks is a mirror. \n\nThere are several around, but I know there's one inside the storage building by the water.
Feh! No honor among thieves. The answer she seeks is water.\n\nGo to the lake, so she can see you figured it out. Be careful not to drown. That would be a shame.
Ach! It's a map. She wants you to find a map. There's one on the wall of the drinking barn.\n\nMay your scales dry and bugs nest in your loins!
Oh, this is just the first riddle. My price is quite reasonable.
Pleasure doing business with you. The answer she seeks is a mirror. \n\nThere are several hand mirrors around, but I know there's one inside the storage building by the water.
Oh, the second riddle? A modest fee. Very modest.
Ah, good to do business with a smart competitor. The answer she seeks is water.\n\nDip that bag into the lake and return it to her.
Oh, for the last riddle? I would expect you to be down a number of coins, yes?
Ah, such wisdom in your deeds. She wants you to find a map. There's one hanging on the wall in the pub.\n\nThank you for doing business with me, Guardian.
It's a Dragon mound. The old Dragon cult used to do horrible things here. So goes the legends, anyway. The dusty old bastards still walk around down there, too. Protect their old secrets.

I'm not entirely sure. That pretty delver, Kireth. She translated some of the old runes and we got to talking. I wonder if she's all right?\n\nAnyway, she said the runes talked about a guardian. Something or someone powerful.

Yes. Good. Right before the attack, Kireth translated the runes, but we couldn't make sense of them. It's like ancient poetry.\n\nI only know it has something to do with opening the doors. I pray you can decipher it.
It's some kind of puzzle. Kireth and I were close to cracking it when the Worm Cult attacked. I think they're after the body of the Companion buried in the vault!
Heard them talking. They thought I was dying. I did too.\n\nSpirit of one of Five Hundred Companions is here. They want to soulbind it to Sinmur, increase his strength.
It's true, then. Malanie leads the Heritance here. This town is corrupt, down to the roots. \n\nDamn it! The Queen will not be pleased.
Mother disappeared a few days ago, and we don't know if she's dead or alive.\n\nNow all Father does is sit outside and drink.
My sister tries. She's in the town guard, but there's only so much she can do without permission.\n\nI need to get back to work now.

My shield-sister Hakra and I were bound to the Rift as caretakers. We were put in place to guard against threats like the Worm Cult and the return of Sinmur.\n\nWe gave our lives that our future kinsmen would know peace.
Heh. You don't say?\n\n All right, hero, go on in.
Really? Plague? Kidnappings? Hostile cultists? Boring!\n\nJust ask my father, the House Councilor. He says there's nothing to the rumors.

She guides us to live in peace and simplicity. She is the sun and rain that nourishes our small group. \n\nWe came here to follow her teachings, to escape the violence of the world and live uncomplicated lives.
No one ever wants to talk to me!\n\nFine. He's probably in the kinhouse.
Make it quick. Don't want to be off my guard.

We try to follow the pure stream, but that path isn't always easy. Instinct tells us to form a fist and strike, especially when the enemy is upon us.\n\nBut we are not warriors. We have no weapons or armor. And we are afraid.
The Redguard, the Bretons—they only let my people into the Covenant to use us as slaves. \n\nWe take the field first. We haul their heavy loads. And all the while they laugh at us behind our backs.
Some of the men looked past my skin and tusks. Saw me as a person. \n\nMost, though, just gave me grief because I was an Orc, a woman, and their superior.
In my youth, I raided Breton settlements. A Redguard killed my clan matron. Slaughtered her over some imagined offense.\n\nI have no love for these people or this Covenant they keep.
Moroth was the one who convinced me to leave.
Treason? You'd accuse me of treason? Here? Are you mad?
I told you, he was an advisor to the Orc king. He's seen the injustice against our people at the highest levels. I trust him with all my soul.
Mauloch's fang. Yes. I don't like to think about it.\n\nHad to cut down this kid, a Redguard blade I'd trained since … I don't want to talk about it.
There was a Redguard here a bit ago. Friendly enough, but I didn't catch his name.\n\nYou're not looking to cause trouble are you? We like things peaceful in Ivarstead.
Just as we'd hoped. You did very well for new blood.

That part of the vision remains clouded. Nonetheless, here you are and we must get ready.\n\nI need to confirm your sensitivity to magic. The lights in the next chamber form a … test of sorts. Only the most sensitive individuals can see them.
I … I just want all this to end. Please.\n\nI can't tell you any more, yet. Talk to the Chieftain, or Shaman Chirah. They can tell you more.
I cannot speak of this to outsiders. If the rest of the world knew …\n\nNo, you must speak to Chieftain Suhlak. She'll decide whether we can trust you or not.

The rest of the village feels the same way! We simply want to rest!\n\nAll right, Helushk's crazed warriors seem to enjoy this horrible state, but they're mad! You can't doom the rest of us for their sakes!
Helushk's soldiers? Can't you see them? They're guarding the entrance to the Daedric shrine!
Of course! That's where—\n\nLook, you really need to talk to Chieftain Suhlak about all this. Let me get back to my work.
He's the village war-chief. He was in charge of Stillrise's defense before ….\n\nWait. If you haven't talked to Chieftain Suhlak, I shouldn't talk to you any more.
Well, they haven't tried to catch me yet, but Helushk's soldiers are crazy! They're up there, guarding the shrine and practicing, night and day. They think being undead is great. They're insane!
I don't know if he's your friend or not, but I saw him speak with Akvid Gray-Sky over there.
I'm not finding you very pleasant. The Redguard spoke with Akvid Gray-Sky for a while. He might be able to tell you more.\n\nAnd don't run off Akvid. He's one of my regulars.

Because they actually like being undead! They think it makes them invincible.\n\nLook, the rest of the village just wants to rest … to die, to put it frankly. Helushk and his fanatics want to stay undead forever. If that isn't crazy, well ….

He's the war-chief, so they're practicing fighting, of course!\n\nLook, in the old days, Helushk was a great protector of the village. But since the curse, he's been going more and more crazy. He thinks his men can be an unstoppable army.
Who, wait, who are you? \n\nLeave me alone. I don't know any Varnedo.
Of course she does. This one can read the skies as well as the captain. But Anala will be staying right here. \n\nFor now, at least.
There are rumors of Maormer about. Anala will have none of it. This one stays in the safety of the Guard, until the coast is clear.
Who? I don't know any Captain Fairies. And I sure don't know anything about a goat. \n\nLeave me be, all four of you.
Say, something seems to be coming back to me. Last I heard, he was setting up camp to the northeast, near the river. \n\nJust don't say I told you, all right?
Whoa, no need to get violent! Look down by the river to the northeast. Varnedo said he was going to set up camp there.\n\nJust go away and leave me out of this.
Oh! The Captain! Scourge of the Sun! Destroyer of happiness and joy! Fine, fine! I'll be on my way. \n\nWould you tell Degail for me, though? She said she'd meet me here. When she gets back.
Ah, yes. Yes. No. No, I don't think so. Once was enough for me. \n\nThese legs were made for the land, and that's where they'll stay.
Ask War Chief Helushk. He's the only leader with vision in Stillrise. \n\nWell, I suppose the Chieftain's okay, but Shaman Chirah and his whiners are driving the rest of us all crazy!
Sea sickness. My guts are over there in the corner, if you want to examine the aftermath. \n\nOh, I wish I'd listened to Degail. Such a smart girl.
We'll see, we'll see. The War Chief has plans. I think you'll be surprised.
Ha! That's something we don't have to worry about. Stillrise Warriors may fall, but we always come back! The War Chief will turn us into Tamriel's most feared army. Nothing can defeat us.

Are you crazy, or have you been talking to Chirah's Followers?\n\nThose miserable fanatics would rather die than live forever. Yes, we're undead, but we're also immortal! We can fight and fall a thousand times and never die.

Anyone the War Chief says! Oh, we're not going to just go out and slaughter people. We'll fight for the causes Helushk says are right, and just.\n\nAnd we'll get paid for it, too. We'll be the wealthiest mercenary company in the world!
I'm told survivors retreated to our shrines. Find them and rally them to the Hall. \n\nI'm going to hold the main doors. I'll wait for you there.
I am <<1>>. I rode with the Five Hundred at Ysgramor's side. But now, my very essence is wracked by magic.
Much hangs on your actions, my friend. The Worm Cult are seeking to use me in some way, to enslave my spirit and then bind it somehow. You must stop them!
Should have known. Look, she's already taken everything.
You'd … you'd do that? Such generosity!
Damn you. And that Bosmer witch!
Follow him to the ritual site and stop those Worms! He's ready when you are.
Stars take you both! Fine. Here's the coin. Just go.
Yeah? Let's see what you've got. Today's the day someone finally stands up to Malareth!

Let's see if you have the stomach for this one. Inside is <<1>>. Take this poison, slip it into his drink without being seen. Try to act normal, he's not a complete fool, but he goes a little too heavy on the drink and the women.

That's for you to discover. Of course, you have the poison, so now you'll have to find a way to get him away from his drink. I'll be here if you have any questions, which I sure you will, or if your nerves fail you.
Ahh…this could be your chance. Talk to her, see if you can get her to lure him away.
What do I mean? What do you think I mean? He's a man who wants a woman. If she plays her cards right, she could have him following her all over Riften. It's not that complicated.

Degail didn't believe the rumors. She went for a walk along the southwest shore and never returned.\n\nYou are so much braver than Anala. You should look for Degail! Yes, look for Degail. Anala will remain here.

Ha! Her and Anala got into a fight. About? About Maormer scouts. Yes! That was it. Rumors of Maormer scouts near the Guard.\n\nDegail went down the shore to prove Anala wrong. I'm sure she's just sitting out there with a bottle.

Last I heard, she went down the shore. I didn't want to get involved, but she and Anala got into it over some rumors. \n\nAnala claimed that Maormer scouts were spotted nearby. And Degail didn't believe her at all.
There are rumors of Maormer about. Anala will have none of it. This one stays in the safety of the Guard, until the coast is clear.\n\nEspecially after what happened to Degail.
Oh! The Captain! The Scourge of the Sun! Destroyer of happiness and joy! Fine, fine! I'll be on my way. \n\nAfter one more spiced wine, of course.
I'm the Sergeant-at-Arms here. I'm in charge of the furnaces up the hill there. I practically run this town. Don't be sniffing around here too much. I have everything in here nice and orderly.
Sea sickness. My guts are over there in the corner, if you want to examine the aftermath. \n\nMe, I'll be huddled here on this bed for a good long time.
I've got my eye on you. Don't touch a thing.
A guard now stands before the door. Seems an odd place for a guard, yes? Want you to investigate. This one has another lead to run down.
I didn't see them until I was almost on top of them. Their ships are all along the western shore! I'm sorry!
Fivefold venerations be upon you! I knew … I knew the moment we met that you were sent by the Divines.\n\nAnd, truly, the Divines have more to say to you.
You'll report nothing! Odendil! Condalin! Now!

You little idiot. Ayrenn, that traitorous cow! She's the one who should be brought up on treason charges.\n\nShe's betrayed the Altmer—her own people! The Veiled Queen will soon be crowned and you can't stop us!
Near Fistalle's house. Bastard.\n\nMeet up with Raz near the forge when you are done. He'll know where Malanie is then.
What do you think Raz did while you searched the town? He watched, observed, calculated.\n\nRaz has very good eyes, you see.
Ok, you could use this to your advantage. Talk to her and maybe there's a way to convince her to be more socialiable with our friend.
What is the matter with you? Did your parents drop you on your head? A mother would do anything to protect her children, believe me I know this firsthand. Do I have to draw everything out for you?

Ahhh…interesting. Well, you know, a little gold could grease the wheels in this case. And actually, if she helps us out this time, then I may talk to her myself. She could prove to be useful beyond this little job.
You are a meathead. and if you keep that up, you and I, we're going to have trouble. Try to listen this time, offer her gold, treasures, whatever, and see if she is willing to help then.

You really are simple, aren't you? Well, so how would one get on board a Blacksails ship? Oh, I don't know, maybe by being a Blacksail? Several are drunk in the bar. Think about that, if you can manage, and don't get into trouble or so help me…

No surprise to me, both women and men are taken by her. Yeah I know her, I'm here everyday aren't I? Well, maybe you wouldn't know that, anyway. I know everyone here, take <<1>> over there why don't you? I'm serious. Take him. What did you ask?

She's smart, beautiful and her daughter is sharp as a tack. That don't mean she's got it easy. She struggles to make ends meet. Once I gave her a coin or two to help me home when I was a bit sloppy. Don't remember if it were one or two to be honest.
No, only what I've seen and heard. Please, you must warn the Queen. She's in grave danger, and the guards here—oh no.

Let's see, have my list here.\n\nNelulin, who should be out fixing the sheds about now. Eryeril, no doubt hiding in his home. And Aninwe. She owns this farm, probably just outside the barn here. Those are the next victims on the list.
The Companions are friends of yours, are they? Well, we'll see. Mother thinks there are some very valuable items in their vault.
Ever hear of the Blades of the Sons of Ysgramor? They're very special weapons of the Companions, worth quite a bit to the right people.
Sure, what do you need to know?

The <<1>> is an item of last resort. You shouldn't have to use it if you're careful, but things happen. If someone tries to get rough with you, throw this in their face and it'll take the fight out of them giving some time for you to get away.
Well, good for you. You're learning. Get back to the lodge; Mother will be waiting.
Easy, eh? Mother always has bigger plans; maybe you'll fit into those somehow.\n\nSpeaking of Mother, you'd better report back to her.
Aye! Sinmur and Thallik lurk at Trolhetta. I can feel them, like rotted teeth that must be pulled. Use the shard's power to end them!
That was a struggle for the ages! Long did we battle, a titanic fray. Weariness finally made him stumble and I sank Wuuthrad into his ugly face. How we drank my victory that night!
He's your problem now, hero. I hope you're up to the task!
Because it was my weapon, forged from my bitter tears after our defeat by the wretched Elves! I slew legions of mighty foes with it; Wuuthrad's legend and power grew with my own.
Yes, as you have seen here. Even that worm Gullveig, forever may her soul roast, could use a small piece of Wuuthrad to suck the souls from innocents. Imagine what Wuuthrad whole again could do!

The Vereansu, bah! They fear the Llodos Plague. Their solution is to capture our monks and the afflicted alike and toss 'em in the fire. \n\nI won't stand for it! I traded my sword for a monk's robe, but I'm no coward!
Safety sounds good. Is there mead?
It's not a party without the Jofarr!
Probably faster than looking on my own.

Yes, this is it! I'll just chew it up and then I can apply it immediately. \n\nWe should see results within moments. Please, go tell Odvild. She's on the balcony. This will mend her suffering as well.
Wasn't he terrifying though? Such big teeth and such sharp claws! I shudder to think of what he might have done to a helpless Bosmer like me. He's really dead?
I prayed nightly for a champion to deliver me from these beasts. And now you're here, my savior!
Oh, mercy! I'm just a Bosmer, what chance do I have against such fierce beasts? I can only pray my death is swift and not too painful.
Are all heroes so modest? But danger still lurks. A deadly beast called Greatclaw lives nearby. Last night I saw it kill a man by dropping a tree on him!
Well, but it was a great big bird, wasn't it? Huge! With a cruel beak and massive claws?
The foul beast fled, knowing you'd slay it, my champion! I fear him no longer. What would I do without you?\n\nI beg you to help me one last time!
Oh, please. Don't fail me now, when the danger is greatest!\n\nSave me from the evil Goblin. I promise you'll be well rewarded.

Cracktooth! A terrifying Goblin. I could never defeat him, small and helpless as I am. But I know a brave, powerful champion like you can slay him easily!\n\nHis camp is to the east, across the river.
He's … wait, what? You found an actual Goblin?
Oh, her. Little Bosmer lass with a sob story about great beasts and how helpless she is?
She lures people in, tricks them into fighting nearby giants. The giants kill them, she takes their valuables. Then on to the next sucker.
Yes, the dark-robed mages. Deep in the ruin. They're breaking the binding that holds me here. They're pulling me apart!
Navigate the puzzle. Get past the doors. Stop them!
Had a run-in with her, eh? At least you're still alive. Not many folks who meet her live to tell about it. Most end up floating in the river.
She goes after travelers, folks no one will miss. She plays with them a bit then somehow gets them to attack the local giants.\n\nThe travelers die and she takes their stuff. Quite a scam.
You did? Well, that'll make our roads safer for a while. That's good news, friend!
She's long gone by now. No fool, that one. Moves on once locals are wise to her.
I just realized. Sage Tirora still may be able to help us. This pouch of ashes. We use it to commune with the ancient spirits of the Hall. \n\nShe's newly dead. And if I know Tirora, angry.
At each of the memorials near the Hall is a small brazier. Burn the ashes at each altar, and see if you can locate Tirora's spirit.\n\nI'll rally the men here and inside the Hall.
The Shor-cursed son of a skeever named Stral Blackthroat. He leads the Rageclaw clan and is said to now lead all the tribes assaulting the Rift.
Aye. We've the honor to safeguard the legendary axe, Wuuthrad. It rests in the vault, secure in the arms of Ysgramor's statue. Please ensure that it's safe.

My cruel and callow binder. "The greatest Mage of our time," his students call him. \n\nIn my time, we could have consumed his power in but a trice. Snapped him up as an appetizer, and nibbled on slow-roasted turtle stew as a main course.
Ha ha! For the love of Kyne. You don't know who Ysgramor is? Or the tale of Wuuthrad?
See, you're not so slow. Let me give you a few things first.\n\nThis is a <<1>>. Sneak up behind someone, then use it to rattle them and sneak by.

We have ways to peacefully deal with people who stand in our way. A quick rap on the head of your target with the Blackjack should give you time you need. When the person recovers, other than a headache, they'll be fine.
Well, what do you think? They'll try to thump you! So if you'd rather not slaughter a bunch of your friends, then don't get caught.
You have any other questions?
Good, good. Look, I hate to rush you, but I have another task for you. \n\nOne of my men, Heldil, has cornered a thug nearby. We need to talk to this lowborn scum.
We've no time for this. He's involved in a plot against the Queen, that's all I can say. \n\nWe need someone like you to get to him. He refuses to speak with a member of the guard.
Get back! One step closer, and I'll cut my throat.
Why should I trust you?
Fine. Fine. Just don't try anything. Get in here.
A gang of mining thugs from the mountains who call themselves the Pit Rats. \n\nThey're bandits, really—scum who raid mines and take whatever they can loot.
How should I know?\n\nThough I did overhear something about how they think there's gold down there. Idiots.
Of course it's true! It's a Nord legend, isn't it?

From Ysgramor's ebony tears as the Elves burned Saarthal, the great weaponsmith Yngol forged the axe Wuuthrad. Ysgramor wielded Wuuthrad ever after, wiping the traitorous Elves from the Rift.\n\nWuuthrad is held to be the greatest of all Nord weapons.

He was the greatest of all Nord heroes, the harbinger of us all! He brought humans to Tamriel, leading a fleet from Atmora. They had some trouble with the Elves that then ruled the Rift, but Ysgramor and his Companions dealt with them! Ha!

Ysgramor led the Companions on a campaign of vengeance against the elves. Wielding his axe Wuuthrad, the harbinger of us all led his warriors in a rampage across Skyrim. The cowardly Elves fled before the Nords' wrath and Skyrim was ours.
I already told the Mages Guild we tracked her to the house and she disappeared. Are you from the damn guild or are you just looking to die?
This map shows her house. We can't find her, but there's something set up in there. Go see for yourself.

This is a good batch. We'll have quite a haul with these. Run these over to my son, Ulfslod. He should be out fishing behind the house. \n\nHe'll have some coin for you. Honest work gets honest pay. Don't want anyone saying I'm a piker.
Depends. Why are you looking for him?
Go through the door behind me.
On second thought, here you go.\n\nThis map shows Malsia's house. We can't find her, but there's something set up in there. Go see for yourself.
"The guild's sent assassins after me. Now that I have the skystones, I must begin right away."
"The skystones may not be able to hold the portal open. Should they fail, I'll be trapped. But I'll take the risk. I must find where the portal leads."

Necromancers who lust for immortality can transform themselves into liches. Vile spells and sacrifices are involved. They gain tremendous power but lose their souls. More than this, I don't care to know.

The situation unfolding upon the battlefield is telling enough. These orders only confirm my suspicions.\n\nThe Alessians plan to slip past your defenses to, how do they put it, catch the Direnni with their trousers down? What a curious phrase.
<<1>> took the portal to the Smokefrost Peaks. We had reports of Worm Cultists infesting the area.\n\nMind looking in on her, just to see how she's doing?
She went through this portal to the Ragged Hills, to investigate rumors of Worm Cultists there.\n\nAmitra's my youngest sister, maybe too young. Would you go check on her?
I'll just write that down. By order of the First Auridon Marines, your presence in Vulkhel Guard has been registered.\n\nDo your best to stay out of trouble and out of the way. Fare you well.
I see you prioritize well. You'll find him at a warehouse west of here. Be sure to tell him that I sent you. \n\nOnce you've finished with both of them, report back to me on the town's upper level.
You'll find the steward at a warehouse east of here. Be sure to tell her that I sent you. \n\nOnce you've finished with both of them, report back to me on the town's upper level.
Good. I want you to speak with two members of the Queen's court, <<1>> and <<2>>. They await assistance from the guard, hands I can't spare just now.\n\nWho do you want to speak to first?
Help? No. I don't think so. \n\nActually. My guardsmen are all tied up right now. If you're up to it, perhaps you could look into some things for me?

You hit your head recently? The Queen leads the Aldmeri Dominion. \n\nShe had some kind of wild time away from court a few years back. But now she's returned to reclaim her birthright. Lead the alliance.
Off gallavanting across Tamriel? Who knows? Who cares? \n\nI wish I could just quit my job, then come back to it when I get bored. Pah.
Probably talking up the "unity of the Dominion." Not all of us are fans of being united with our feral little cousins and furry friends.
Probably talking up the "unity of the Dominion." Not all the Altmer are fans of the alliance yet. \n\nNo offense.
Queen Ayrenn's personal guard. They're led by Battlereeve Urcelmo, one of the most decorated warriors in the Dominion.
No. I'm captain of the city guards here. The marines are the right arm of the Queen. My duty is to the city.
That's like asking why my father Maurice was such a bastard. There are things we aren't meant to know.\n\nWhen the voice whispered to me, it said that the land was no longer mine.

According to my father's journal, this property has belonged to my family for centuries.\n\nBut Maurice was also a lying bastard whose death was long overdue. He was known for only telling half the story.

Search the ruins. See if you can find a ghost wandering around, or wailing or rattling chains, or doing whatever ghosts do.\n\nDo you think I should hire a priest to perform some kind of ritual? Owning a haunted estate is all rather new to me.
Damn ghost won't let them in! Why else would I be standing out here?

It must be nearby. I can feel its dark energy.\n\nThe undead manifestation of Lodorr's lieutenant, Ulfnir Ice-Blood, guards the antechamber to this room. Perhaps the crown lies with him. Defeat him, and search his body. I'll keep searching here.
<<<1>>'s corpse bears marks of torture. A symbol is carved into his forehead: the symbol of Mauloch.>
Sure, I guess, depends on what you're asking, but I'll do what I can.
I'm not exactly sure what you're asking, but listen, I'm busy. Catch me when I'm outside,
Now here's some <<1>>. If you're in trouble and escape is your best chance, throw this in their eyes and run.
Finally, wear this uniform. It'll show you're a member of the Black-Briars; might open some doors for you.\n\nBe careful, these guys won't be happy if they find you in the vault.

She told me she didn't mind his advances. That she actually … liked him. I forbade her from seeing him, but she didn't listen.\n\nI knew their dalliances would anger the Drublog. I've prayed to Z'en for guidance, but've gotten no answer.
Don't you know? It's illegal to sell goods from the Dominion or Covenant here. And black marketeers are dealt with harshly, in Riften at least.

As you say. The murders brought the Skywatch guard down upon Ezduiin. The cult held off their blades, but just barely.\n\nIn an act of desperation, Essanyon used a magical relic called the Mallari-Mora. Killed every soul here. Bound them forever.
Duure began to claim Magnus himself called for the blood of a Skywatch noble. He sent his cult to act as daggers in the night. A manor house full of royalty was slaughtered.
"If I reach the Aetherius, my soul may be torn from my flesh. The soul gem should protect me."

Yes, now that you mention it. Sirinque, one of my students, said something about freeing the spirits. She's nowhere near as analytical as Andewen. \n\nI think she's down at our forward camp. I'm sure she's fine.
I hope so! If they're not ….\n\nNot worth thinking about right now.
Some of the spirits appeared, grabbed my researchers, and then vanished.\n\nWe need to get into the undercroft. It's the only place I can think they'd be.
Of course, but speak quickly.
How long do you have? I'm sorry. This is just not the place for a protracted metaphysical conversation. \n\nIt may be enough to say that Aetherius is the spirit realm. The land of the dead.
It's a name we're all trying to forget. Uricantar is very close—was very close—to me. \n\nTelenger cast him out of the guild and forebade him to use magic again.

I can't begin to guess. Not without more information. But the use of the Mallari-Mora. It may have twisted, broken off a part of the spirit world. \n\nIf a mage were to gain access to such a place—the power. That sounds like Uricantar.
He couldn't understand that power has to have limits. That some costs are too high.\n\nYou can see here what he's willing to do for a taste of power.
My brother's story is a sad one. Suffice it to say, he is responsible for the trapped souls you see in these ruins. His zealotry doomed these souls to eternal torment.
Just so. There is one obstacle to overcome. A puzzle that defends the ancient mage's spellwork. \n\nThirteen tiles surround a chest within. The correct four must be activated to access the lattice.
You have the pleasure of speaking with High Kinlady Estre of Errinome, scion of royal Aldmeri blood and ruler of Skywatch.\n\nI'm lucky enough to be married to Prince Naemon, Queen Ayrenn's brother.
I'm Prince Naemon. Ayrenn's brother, husband to Kinlady Estre.

Why, I have the pleasure of being the High Kinlord of Firsthold! The name's Rilis. The Thirteenth.\n\nMy family has ruled the northern tip of Auridon almost as long as Altmer have lived on the island.
Dead? Dark Moon and dull claws. Damn these fanatics.

She mentions a rat with a blade. Condalin is the forgemaster here, controls the smithy on the far end of town.\n\nGo, see what you can find. And be careful. Meet Razum-dar around the other side of the forge when you are done.
Let Raz see that. \n\nEven in death, she laughs at this one. Clever girl. It is a code, telling us who she suspected.
She wants every coin! How much blood can she wring from this stone?
Fine, fine. Take it. No wonder the pockets are always dry.
Absolution! Absolution from the gods. Thank you! Stars above, thank you.
Pah. Guards do nothing! Malareth's scum, every day. Stars take you!
Malareth always twists the truth. She'll get nothing today!
To Oblivion with Malareth. She already has all the coin!
Malareth. She won't have another week's pay!
Stars! Fine. Here's the payment. And tell Malareth that's the last gold she'll ever see from me!
Bah! Time to take a stand. You're not the only one knows how to fight.
Words fail! Malareth will never see this face ever again!
Just another of Malareth's mercenaries. Always with the same message. This time you get nothing!
And it's not wise to harass strangers!
Fine, fine. The blade's not a familiar friend. Sadly, coin doesn't seem to be either. Here.
Yes? Yes! Thank you, thank you! You don't know what this means.
Malareth's mercs. So high and mighty. All you'll get today is a fight!
Is that so? Don't be shy. What do you need?
Aye. Come, my friend. For Fistalle. For the Queen!
A wise purchase, then. Very beneficial. \n\nPlease take it from the chest, here. Just behind me. If you see our mutual friend again, be sure to give him this one's best.
Ahh. Yes. Eshaba has that. The perfect thing to suit your needs!\n\nBut are you certain? This souvenir comes with certain expectations.
I … can't say. I won't!\n\nEverything's gone wrong, but we did it to save Tanglehaven. That's all that mattered.
Injured? I should be so lucky.\n\nI don't know if I can face the consequences on my own. The village. My mother! If you would come with me, I'd be grateful.

They don't think we need the Dominion to survive. They think the Queen is making a mistake, "elevating" the Bosmer and Khajiit to be equals with the High Elves. Racists. Isolationists. And general idiots.
Yes. As did Fasion. He told you true. We are the Eyes of the Queen. We are few, and we stick to the shadows. But we have the honor of being the Queen's most-trusted agents.
The battlereeve is fiercely loyal. He believes his marines are immune to manipulation. Like newly forged steel blades. But Razum-dar knows, better than most, how quickly stains can set in.
Blood from a heart. His heart. My sire. My father, the one who gave me this … gift. It's his heartblood I need.\n\nBut my mother's in the village, safe. How could she be in danger?
No! Please tell my mother I died. I don't want her to see the monster I've become.\n\nMaybe I can stop my father. Maybe … no, not again!
<<1>>'s father <<2>> came back, after all this time. But he wasn't the same. Something … changed him.\n\nHe attacked me! I asked him where he'd taken <<1>> and he bit me.

First, I must take care of the dead. I know getting their remains wasn't easy. Thank you.\n\nIf I can't see my daughter again, I'll at least make her proud. I've a few hours left before the change. I'll make the best of them.

Much of magic is in the detail. These spirits should not be here. Their presence is inherently fragile. \n\nWith manipulations of the magicka-field around you, your will can carry the punch of a warhammer.

Yes. As the Drublog gathered their forces, he promised me a way to defend the village.\n\nWhen the fighting started outside Tanglehaven, I couldn't control myself. Hot blood covered everything. I tore into friend and foe alike. I couldn't stop!

It's why I couldn't go back. What if I'd lost control inside the village? All of this would mean nothing if I killed everyone.\n\nBut I won't let my mother pay for my weakness. The heartblood must come from my father. Please, help me stop this.
My father? Thank the Stars! I'm tired of being a bargaining chip.
Ugh. My sister. It's her fault we're in this mess. \n\nThe Heritance just wanted some information. No problem! But they insisted on taking Palith as insurance, to make sure I'd behave.
They captured me to manipulate my brother, Eranamo. They had him do a job and then shoved him into a room in the ruins to the north.\n\nBastards.
That's my father! Always thinking. \n\nBut I can't … I can't leave without Eranamo.
Uncertain. Aronel might know, but he's not very coherent right now. I gather it contains a fragment of Hakra's soul. Jabbing a corpse with it should enable Hakra's spirit to re-animate that body.

Oh, hush. I didn't know they were in league with the Pact. And now you're here meddling too. Fine.\n\nMy escape won't be enough. I gave them some detailed military intelligence. Will you help me retrieve it?
As well ask the tree how long the wind will blow. I do not know. But I suggest you hurry.
Many mortals call me Boethiah.\n\nSate the geode's thirst with Arithiel's soul, and I will grant you a boon, for a time, to aid in your battle with the Worm Cult.
Hah, no. She still worships me. Appreciates me. Not like my old man. \n\nIf father were here, he'd lash my hide.
Troll's blood, you are eager! Every year, members of my household proctor the tests. Seek them out, and they'll set you on the path.

No. The voice, it could have lied about everything. But if I don't try, we'll both be cursed.\n\nI guess it's a blessing my mother's in such a daze. I'd hate for her to know what was really happening right now.

Another comes for my blessing? Drink deep, and let the beast behind your eyes take hold.\n\nAh, but is that fear I smell? The young Bosmer fears what the future holds. Her flesh is weak, but not for long.
The Elf child must take the heartblood from her sire. If her mother drinks of it, she may yet be saved.\n\nBut there is no redemption for the child. She is mine.
What? He … my son is a traitor? He gave deployment plans to the Heritance? And the Pact?

How ungrateful the little Elf is! She took the gift willingly, and now she wishes to turn away.\n\nHer flesh and blood are mine, but I am not without mercy. Perhaps she can save someone … her mother … from the same fate.
Did he tell you my wife—his mother—was murdered by the Veiled Heritance? That he's put all of Auridon in danger? More wives and mothers and daughters, just so he can feel important? Like a big man?
Green bless you, then! I have everything I need from this hut. Was just about to take my leave. Would you do me a favor and clean up? I want to make my report.

No one will be truly safe until these Spider Cultists are defeated. I don't understand the method behind it, but they're bringing innocents here to enslave them with their magic.\n\nI'm fearful of asking, but were there other survivors?
Thank Ysmir. I'll head there as soon as I recover my strength. I thank you again. \n\nIf my fellow Guildmates live, they'll be up ahead.
Take these fire salts. The empty crates over there are the perfect kindling.\n\nHead to the camp on the bluff when you're done here. I'm sure Arfanel would wish to thank you.
I'll be fine. I'm fortunate you got here when you did. They were preparing to turn me.

Two-Blades is alive? Then perhaps the Divines will us to fight on. Good.\n\nThose Cult members told me they would grant me a blessing, that it would turn me to their cause. They've been enslaving people in the same way.
Hah! Enough with that Thane business. I don't even deserve the title.\n\nBut yes, ask what you will!

Thanes are masters of mighty cities! I'm just an old military man. Won too many battles, and they ran out of little medals to pin on me. \n\nSo they dubbed me a Thane and gave me dominion over all you see before you! Hah!
I'm sure the skalds are eager to tell you that particular tale. An old Nord hero bore the name. And his legacy lives on today.

You've arrived at a fortuitous time of the year! The mead is at its best and to celebrate I invite all my kith and kin to the hall.\n\nGet this many warriors together, and they just have to compete. So we host the challenge and have some fun!
I have to. This is justice. He's a traitor to the crown. To his family.
Stars, yes. Let's get that bastard. Merormo needs to pay for what he's done here.
No, I have to. I must—my son. My own son! How can I kill my own flesh and blood?
I never thought I'd live to see the day. I've failed. I've failed as a father and as a soldier.
He's a traitor to the crown. He's committed treason, murder, and theft. How do I justify that? Even as his father?\n\nIt's my duty.
I'll live.\n\nThank you for your help, but as someone who usually plays the role of the mercenary rescuer, I just want you to know that I can't afford to pay you.

Bless that man's bald head!\n\nThose Cultists captured me and boasted that they would bless me with "the Obsidian Husk." They were going to take me to some shrine up ahead, said they would "make me clean." It sounded very unappealing.
Why it's a party, of course. I'm afraid we weren't expecting you, so there are no seats left, but make yourself comfortable anyway. I'm sure Vesta will be along soon with refreshments for all.
Stars, yes! The Festival of Defiance. An annual celebration of freedom and victory. Skywatch, retaken from the Sload, in the wake of the Thrassian gambit.
You know how the Khajiit are like mer, but cats? Imagine that, only with slug-toad things. They're a Betmer race, beast mer, and their empire once ruled the seas of southern Tamriel.
You seem tense. Agitated. Don't you like to see people having a good time?\n\nJust have a mead and forget your troubles for a while.
I'm glad you're here. I'm happy for the chance to honor Lady Estre.\n\nShe's my brother's wife, after all. But it all goes in the Font if the Heritance tries something.
No. Not I. We can't be seen discussing such matters. Razum-dar is very close by.\n\nAuri-El's scales protect you.

I sent Ranarwa and the others to look for survivors. They mentioned the Cultists spoke of this Obsidian Husk.\n\nThat it allowed them to turn flesh to shadow, and bestow a "blessing" to enslave innocents. May I see it?

I'll try to destroy this thing. The Spider Cult leader, Vila Theran, retreated to tend to other matters after she crushed our offensive. She will no doubt be alerted when I use my magic on the stone.\n\nI'll need you to defend me one last time.
Just follow.
Do I look like a steward's assistant? Do you take me for a commoner? No. But, yes, I happen to know where she is. \n\nEast warehouse, just north of the docks. You can go now.
Feh. Some kind of criminal feud, I'm sure. \n\nNow then. If you have some other task, you should be about it.
Just hold it for the moment. Heldil is just up the stairs here, house on the right. \n\nGet going. Remember—the Queen's service.
That feeling of dread, it just vanished. My guards felt it as well.\n\nWe walked right up here without any trouble. Even cleared out some imps along the way.

It's all true, I'm sure. If you shake my family tree, all kinds of wickedness will fall out.\n\nNot that I'm much better, mind you. But at least I don't hide my nature and I honor my deals. Unlike my father.
Skywatch is a dangerous town—today, of all days. You know of the festival? Estre's ceremony, yes?
Oh, truly? Consider yourself most welcome then. Apologies for my brusque greeting. It's been a trying few days.
Take the earring Raz used to disguise himself. We don't want anyone to recognize you.
Take the earring Raz used to disguise himself. You won't get far under the Veil looking like that.
The Heritance. Raz has word the Veil has fallen on Skywatch. They plan to attack the royalty, make a statement. We need someone to find the cell and snuff it out.\n\nAnd by someone, Raz means you.
Fine, then. On your guard!
Get out of here. Another word and I'll have to bring you to a magistrate.
Damn it, I tried to warn you. Remember that! I tried.\n\nI'm leaving before the ghost makes my head explode or something. I'd run if I were you.
Raz needs a partner, now. So yes, you will soon be free. For a price. \n\nYou must warn the Queen and her battlereeve. The captain will attempt to murder the Queen at the temple.
Ah! A patriot! Let me get a look at you.
You look about right. Stars, yes! You might be just the right type. We'll need to test you first.\n\nIf you've been around Skywatch at all today, you've seen the Royal Guard. Right?

These Bloodthorn cretins ambushed me! And while I was on a mission of incredible importance! There were dozens of them!\n\nBut I didn't go down without a fight. What will the Lion Guard do without me?
Recruit Gorak claims that you helped him defeat dozens of cultists and recover the dispatch from a foul necromancer. \n\nIs this true?
Hmm? Oh, I remember seeing you around.\n\nHere. Just take care of it.
I'm impressed. As I expected, you're not just recruit material. You could be an officer.\n\nLet's drink a toast to your health!

These caves were once a great burial mound, where all creatures of the Grahtwood came to die. But a thousand thousand moons have risen since then, and the roots have long overgrown it.\n\nWhat could you be doing here, Oraneth?
The Baelborne heir … he could have been my son, if Maurice had only stood up to his evil mother. Instead, he let her lock me in that tower.\n\nWhat happened? Only what was meant to be.

He ran head first off this cliff. The curse remains in place, just as Tachnim promised when he first appeared to me in the tower.\n\nYou know, I never asked what happened to my child. It's comfort enough that Tachnim continues to honor our bargain.
My master made the deal. I am merely the messenger that carried out his orders.

Evil? Such a mortal way of thinking. I exist to serve a purpose. Right now, that purpose is to ward this land from the Baelborne.\n\nWhen my master commands it, my purpose will change. That is not good or evil. It simply is.
He serves at my master's side.\n\nFor as long as the child remains useful, I shall honor the bargain that was struck.

You have this one's apologies. He was looking for Fasion. It is a happy accident, for us both, that you could be saved.\n\nYou escape the cell. And Razum-dar's new plan to warn the Queen moves forward.

It is somewhat embarrassing, but … this one's face is known to some of the royal court. If Razum-dar were to approach, they would know something is amiss. \n\nYou, a new face in a marine's uniform. They would suspect nothing.
Let's get going then!
Escort <<1>> to the ritual site and stop that ritual! Speak to them when you're ready to begin.

I didn't abandon them, if that's what you're asking. We were ambushed, and a dozen of us were killed in the opening moments of battle.\n\nI called for a fighting retreat, but not everyone made it back. I was the only one.

Spiders. Lots of spiders, and their handlers. They wield strange magics, blessings from Mephala, that enshroud them in darkness.\n\nTheir army consists of enthralled travellers as well, innocents made loyal to the Cult by the power of the same magic.
They're Daedra worshipers. Specifically of Mephala.\n\nThey've been enthralling travelers moving through the Grotto, and turning them into beings of darkness loyal to the Spider Cult.
Excellent! Let's do this thing.

The Orc that stands … er … sits … before you represents the future of the Lion Guard! I am Recruit Gorak, pride of New Orsinium!\n\nPlease untie me. We have work to do. We must recover the General's dispatch and return to Captain Vistra.
Ask anything, friend!
I can't believe they captured me again.
It's about time. I'm getting out of here.
This place used to be a model of discipline and decorum. Now we're being harassed by thugs dressed as soldiers! It's a disgrace!

Not many.\n\nIt wasn't so long ago that the alliance was forged between Orsinium and Wayrest. Orcs have spent more years fighting the Lion Guard than joining them. I intend to prove the worth of my people.
Thank you! You won't regret this, I swear!
Eight be praised! I can't wait to see my family again.

To prove myself! A messenger disappeared in these swamps several days ago with a dispatch from General Gautier. No one had the wits or the will to venture out here except me. Oh, and you, it would seem.

I grew up reading about the Lion Guard. My mother collected books about the Guard when I was a child. Books such as "The Lion's Roar," "Guardian of my Heart," and "For the Love of a Lion."\n\nI read them all. I knew that this is what I wanted to do.
Really? I'm a paragon of my people and a perfect example of the essence of true Orc.\n\nIn short, I'm exactly what the Lion Guard needs!

Gorak's eager. Maybe too eager. He wants to be in the Lion Guard so badly that he'll crawl over broken glass to impress us.\n\nHis attitude hasn't sat well with the other officers. I'm the fourth commander he's been assigned to.

Talk to any miners you can get close to without arousing suspicion. Let them know we're organizing.\n\nOr just kill the Red Rooks in the mine. The miners will try to escape if you clear a path for them.
Gorak has a fire and a passion. I respect that.\n\nI just need to find a way to temper his enthusiasm and harness it before he gets himself or his fellow Guards hurt.
Your actions will raise the town's morale, I'm sure of it. \n\nIf you see Marent Ergend, talk to him. He's been itching to go after the Red Rooks as well.
Your actions will raise the town's morale, I'm sure of it. \n\nI heard you spoke to Marent Ergend. That means we'll soon have more strong hands to help us oust these black-hearted rogues.

I thought Lord Diel was doing good work, studying the harpies to figure out why they've become so hostile recently. Plus, it was the big break that my brother's Daggers needed.\n\nBut now I'm not so sure.
Oh, I don't know! Maybe I'm just worried. Gelvin and his crew have been gone for a long time and I can't help but imagine the worst.\n\nAt least Bumnog made it back.

Well, I'm not going to leave while Gelvin's still out there, if that's what you're asking.\n\nBut I swear, if anything's happened to my brother and Lord Diel is to blame, well, then his lordship is going to regret it.
This one. This one does not believe you. You are a spy for Tanion, yes?
No. No, you are right. Nurad knows all the instructors. Have you come for food, or medicine?
Nonsense. Are we strict? Yes. Do we make our students work hard? Yes. \n\nCombat, tactics, etiquette—to join the Thalmor, there's a great deal to learn.
Fine. We have nothing to hide here. Visit the classrooms, spar with our instructors. You'll see our lessons are tough, but fair.

This is not a cafe in Skywatch. This is war! \n\nThe Pact, the Covenant. They look upon Auridon as a succulent fruit, ripe for harvest. We must prepare our students for the trials they'll face in the field.
I've just come from buying bandages and ointments from the Baandari. Those Khajiit are the only friends we have around here.
You didn't see the beatings? The mistreatment? You think they smack us around like that, then hand us a bandage?\n\nThey're not real careful about lunch and dinner, either.
Need to go talk to Ilara. She had it bad today, too. Her scars don't show on the outside, though. Get going.

I want you to see these people like they truly are. Nurad, another student, took the supplies back to his dorm. Go talk to him.\n\nGet the supplies, then bring them to Brinthir and Thalorel. They got it bad today.

I told you, I went to talk to Ilara? I stepped away for five minutes and Tanion's trained dog Malangwe jumped her.\n\nShe's taking Illie to the cave! She can't survive another night in Saltspray, not in the state she's in.
No. The instructors take back our training blades after class. \n\nWill you go talk to him? I'll grab some of the others and meet you at the Baandari camp.
I'll muster the students! We'll storm the caves! All we need are blades.\n\nZaban, the Baandari that gave me the bandages. He'll trade with us.
The whole time … I thought he turned our pain into money.\n\nHe was trying to help us.

This is it. Look … I … we're afraid of the cave. Saltspray. Too many memories. Go look for Ilara. She needs to get pulled out of there.\n\nWe'll grab weapons from the camp here. Then go deal with our teachers.
My people allied with the Dark Elves. Our slavemasters are now our friends.\n\nAnd yet, nothing has changed. I'm still treated like a slave. I should be free to flow as the river's course demands.
My magicka is bound. My superior, he holds a gem that constrains my power.\n\nYou destroy their supplies, yes? I gain my freedom.
Yes. The crystal may backfire if not properly attuned.
I see I've chosen another trustworthy ally. \n\nVery well. I'll try.
Good luck.
I can't. My magicka is bound. I could try, but if I exceed the power the stone allows me … pain.\n\nExcruciating pain.
I'm relieved she's finally come to her senses! A woman of royal blood, off doing who-knows-what in the wilds? Ridiculous.
As you wish. Draw!
Why would you need those?  \n\nNever mind, I'll tell you. They're in the houses in the west side of <<1>>.
All right, all right! I was going to steal them for myself …. \n\nI'll mark the three houses on your map. Just let me go, please!
I don't know, I swear!

My father used to scare me with the spell. He'd cast it on his workshop and make himself look like a hooded specter in a white mask. We argued about it. A lot. \n\nI never found it as funny as he did.

The guards caught me sneaking around. They don't believe I'm trying to save the village. \n\nThe Bloodthorn are gathering the villagers at the docks for sacrifice. They kill them and raise them as zombies! I don't want my friends to end up like that!

My father's a mage. His signature spell is a spell of hiding that I know can protect the villagers. If you can reach our house and prepare the spell, I can rescue the villagers and meet you there.\n\nYou just need to convince Dame Clarique to free me.
Where do you suppose I'd keep it? I'm a ghost—we don't have pockets. \n\nI'd insist you pay up on that wager, but I've got no use for your coins neither.
You talked to him, didn't you? Why exactly do you trust this bandit? I'm not even convinced there are any villagers left alive in there to save. We haven't seen anyone but the cultists.
No invitation, no boat ride. Those're the rules.\n\nGo talk to the new students. Maybe they can explain things so that even you can understand.

I suppose that's a good point. If what he's told us is correct, we wouldn't see the villagers, anyway. He says they're being kept down by the docks.\n\nVery well, I'll let the bandit go. I just hope I don't regret this.

That's not going to happen. If you want to help, go to the docks and see what's happening. I'd appreciate any information you can bring us.\n\nI wish I could send a force in there and clear the cultists out, but Camlorn might call us back at any time.
A is for apple.
B is for bread.
C is for cinammon.
On my mark, magical pillars will appear on a set path. Follow the markers and keep to your feet. \n\nOh, and 'ware the imps. Little bastards have sharp teeth. Ready?
<The ritual table vibrates with power, waiting for components to be placed upon it.>
<The order was incorrect! The spell fizzles and doesn't work.>
<The order was incorrect! The spell fizzles and doesn't work.>
<The salve hums with power as the scent of cherries wafts up from the table.>
<Success! The spell is complete!>

Alandare proctors your final trial—the trial of strength. Get going.
To the Ayleid ruin? About time. But there's a wrinkle. We can't go straight there.
It needs <<1>>s. The town had three of them as artifacts, but the Maormer are probably taking them. I'm fairly certain they took one to the dock.  The other two are in town.
Well, I can bombard the ships with my fire spells, but I don't have that kind of power. I need to use the ruins as a focus. But it's powered down.
A member of the First Auridon Marines. I serve under Battlereeve Urcelmo. I'm currently on leave.\n\nMy wife passed, just recently.
The Heritance—again. I was assigned to Queen Ayrenn's detail, so my wife went to stay with her sister in Silsailen. \n\nThe city was sacked and they were both murdered by these bastards.
I've lost enough to the Veiled Heritance. I won't lose my daughter. \n\nPlease. You have to find her.
Sorry, we don't know each other well enough to get that personal just yet. Trust me, though. We both want to stop the Maulborn.
Right now, I'm your very best friend. Work with me, and we'll make sure Narsis isn't destroyed by the Maulborn.
Oh, this should be good. What?

Sea sickness? The biggest swells we hit wouldn't have made my old mother queasy. And half the trip he spent in the cabins, swilling that awful meat brew Bosmer love. \n\nStars above! What about Anala?
Maormer? What kind of phantom fear is that? I expected better of Anala. The Maormer are no threat to Vulkhel Guard.
Well. Auri-El strike me blind. I'd best be getting out of here, then. If we don't move quickly, they'll lock down the port.
Very well. Are you ready?
The test is simple. I will give you a riddle. You choose from the items on these tables. One of them is the correct answer. Choose wrong? Face the consequences.
You know, I think you earned the truth. But this is a pretty big secret I'm about to share. Are you sure you're up to the responsibility?
I like the way you think! All right, we'll keep our secrets. For now.\n\nBut next time we meet, we're going to have a long, private conversation, you and I.
I know you won't. Come closer. This is for your ears only.\n\nVaron and I. We're part of the Morag Tong.
Keep your voice down! Just being associated with the Morag Tong can get me put to death. We're here on behalf of Mournhold, understand?\n\nNow get out of here. We'll meet again, I'm sure.

You're kind of an innocent, aren't you? The Morag Tong. Organized crime? A league of assassins? We used to be part of the establishment, but we're kind of on the outs these days. Some of the house leaders still employ us, though.

My life is measured in hours.
I serve by being devoured.
Thin, I am quick.
Fat, I am slow.
What am I?

Two bodies have I, two joined into one.
The more I stand still, the faster I run.
I flip on my head, some watch me with dread.
What am I?

I say much, but you cannot hear me.
I open, but you cannot walk through me.
I have a spine, but I have no bones.
I shouldn't be judged by my face.
What am I?
Oh, it'll work. But it's idiotic. As usual, my father only takes into account the big picture.
Who knows? He muttered something about looking for Hadmar and a familiar. \n\nWhat do you think the Maulborn want us for?
Saltspray Cave. It's just north of campus, towards the beach. They throw us in to correct our behavior.
I understand. This is my battle to fight.\n\nGo. Stop the Bloodthorn. I'll free my father and bring him back here. Meet me here after you destroy the Bloodthorn boats.

I owe you, friend. We'll find a way to deal with the cultists.\n\nThe Bloodthorn took control of a house in the center of the village. That's where we'll begin to search for my father. I'll get some things together and meet you there.
He's going to collapse his prison! I'm not an expert in pocket planes, but that doesn't sound healthy. He's going to kill himself to stop the ritual!\n\nI can't let that happen. I'm going after him.
Cruelty for the sake of cruelty, this one thinks. We don't get enough food. They mock us, beat us. \n\nWe're supposed to be training for the Thalmor, but they treat us like slaves.

When young, I'm sweet in the sun.
When middle-aged, I'm the life of the party.
When old, I'm worth my weight in gold.
When I'm gone, everyone laments my absence.
What am I?

We've been working to get recognized for years. Up until now, our discoveries have been curiosities, not important findings.\n\nInformation on how the Dwemer used soul gems in their constructs, though? No one could ignore that kind of a finding.

I used his spell, the one he always used to scare me with, to slip in unnoticed and rescue him.\n\nAs we made our escape, we were overrun by banekin. Father cast some kind of spell and I blacked out. When I woke up, I was here and he was … there.

He came to me and spoke to me about my crystal. When he told me you were retrieving the lattice, I found my courage and followed Quaron out here. \n\nYou still have the micro-etched crystal I gave you?

This lattice is an elegant extension of the principles the crystal uses. By enmeshing it within the lattice, it will amplify the power of the crystal. It will free these spirits of the Mallari-Mora's curse.
I failed him, but you didn't. You stopped the Bloodthorn cultists, just like he wanted.\n\nI want to bury my father. Could you speak to Dame Clarique for me? I need a moment alone.
Answer this correctly and our business is done.

I attend every battle.
I attend every duel.
My tooth is sharp.
My swing is cruel.
What am I?

Friend to soldiers, guardsmen, and mercs.
Scarred from battle, unbowed by hurt.
I always face forward, when battle is joined.
When on the march, I watch from behind.
What am I?

I'm always smiling, but I never laugh.
I once loved life, from cat to calf.
I'm always staring, but I cannot see.
I once held secrets, those given to me.
What am I?
Now you must prove your heart's endurance. Speak to Varustante and she will begin your trial.
They were going to kill Ilara. Just for being what she is. How … how can I be anything other than Khajiit?
Yes, yes. Thank you.\n\nThis one is sure Baham is worried.
You fight. Every officer under the Veil needs to know how to fight. Behind me is the combat ring. You'll go up against other officer candidates.
We'll see. Head up the stairs, join the melee. If you survive, you're in.\n\nPrepare yourself.
The supplies from the Baandari. Yes. Thalorel and Brinthir are in the other dorms, recovering. Today was a bad one. For all of us.
Oh, of course! If someone asked me to drink some kind of poisoned mead, I'd have questions too!
Why wouldn't I? I love going out to these fests, and Vofknir always puts out a good spread. Nothing in Kyne's teaching prohibits strong drink!
I'd have thought that was obvious. Without the heart-racing, vision-blurring effect of the mead, you wouldn't be able to see the fires.\n\nYou can't run the Trial if you can't see the fires!

Well, I'll tell you. I've heard some of the scholars say they're naturally occurring. Some kind of vapor rises up from the ground and the lake. Something like that?\n\nMe, I think they're gifts from Kyne herself!
Oh, no reason. Look, you seem very healthy. If you take too long I'm sure the mead will just wear off. And you'll have to come back and start again.\n\nPretty sure. Almost definitely sure. Yeah.
Our friends and neighbors. They were trapped by the imps. There was nothing we could do but run for our lives.
Thank you, my friend. You're certainly braver than I am, I'm sad to admit.
Let's just say, there are certain magical tomes in King Jorunn's library that mages in his employ are forbidden to read. My curiousity got the better of me, and it cost me my job.
Ridding Eastmarch of an undead malevolence bent on conquest and domination? I think that might do it.

A powerful mage from Era of Myths. Lodorr forged a crown of cruelty and domination. It channeled his will, and allowed him to enslave an army of followers. They say it took Ysgramor himself to finally defeat him.

My son said that? I'm sorry. I didn't mean to berate you. I can still collapse this plane. The Bloodthorn may escape, but we'll stop the necromantic ritual here and now. I'll follow you back to the portal.
Bloodthorn cultists followed you into the house. I got the drop on them and guarded the portal until you returned. They're upstairs. See for yourself.

Now that my father is safe, I want to get out of Glenumbra. I'm through with this place. And I don't want Dame Clarique to put me back in chains.\n\nYou should go speak to her. I need some time with my father.
Secret? <<1>> is a trader, nothing more. I sell things, you buy them! This is the way of things.\n\nAt least it should be. Some people think differently.
They say no one gets into Belarata, but <<1>> is better than anyone!\n\nWhy have a door that leads nowhere, yes? Want to keep someone out? Build a wall, not a door!
