Good luck. You will need it! The Mane himself could not get them to leave.\n\nNot the Mane. Not his armies. These ones do not understand or live the Riddle'Thar.
Ha! Even if I wanted to show you, I could not. These people, they harass me day and night! There is no end to their whining.\n\nGet them to leave me alone! Then, maybe, I might show you.

That cat over there sold me a staff he said was older than the ruin itself! Well it was old, all right! Fell apart in my hands not a mile out of Valenwood!\n\nAncient artifacts must be preserved before you sell them, everyone knows that!
I suppose that will have to do. Educate your friend in the proper treatment of his finds, will you?
Hmph. You're right. This isn't Summerset, after all. \n\nWhen all this war business is over, these savages should learn a thing or two about how things must be done!
<The Speaking Stone comes to life.>

<<1>> went blind. He asked me to bring him here for one last adventure.\n\nBetween the Maormer, these Wood Elves, and everything else, I'm ready to head back. But I will never abandon the captain. Never.
The captain can only see what's in his mind now. If he wants to relive his past and call it an adventure, so be it.\n\nI just wish he'd listen to me sometimes.
Ah, you sweet-tongued devil. That's what I like to hear. Follow me!
<The voice stone flashes brightly>
People are getting their lives back in order, mourning their dead. \n\nWe will recover, we always do.
It is a great pity that Heseph was killed. He was a good man and an able administrator.\n\nI think Lia wants to be mayor. Not sure how I feel about that.
Oh, I suppose someone has to be mayor.\n\nIf you ask me, she's too busy making doe-eyes at that Tamien Sellan to run the town.
I … I think so. The werewolves attacked as we followed this trail. One of the beasts knocked my blade out of my hand and nearly took off my head before I fled.\n\nI hope <<1>> got away.

It connects to an old path leading to Hircine's shrine, but I haven't been that way in ages. It makes sense the Houndsmen might set up camp there.\n\nI saw a few more arrows and corpses along the path, so maybe <<1>> held her own.
No need to thank me. We really must get moving though, eh?
Things will be difficult for a while. I'm not sure if people will want to rebuild. \n\nMy father stayed behind to help where he could.
Call it revenge. Or redemption. I should never have gotten involved with the Red Rooks. \n\nI want to try to stop them here. They have a strong leader who wants to make this his base of operations.
Things will be difficult for a while. I'm not sure if people will want to rebuild. \n\nWith my father gone, I had nothing more to hold me there.
I heard that one of the leaders of the Red Rooks had taken over the town. \n\nI wanted revenge for Eagle's Brook. Or redemption, maybe. I should never have gotten involved with the Red Rooks.
We were in transit. Ayrenn. Her Majesty, I mean. She's taking a tour of the realm, and her closest advisors travel with her.

No, she. Well, she's a faster traveler than the members of her entourage. \n\nMinantille has gotten a bit soft since leaving the military. Nuulehtel isn't very confident on a horse. And Merion won't keep his hands to himself. Makes travel difficult.
I'm not sure. His face seemed familiar, somehow? Maybe, a few years ago? During the signing ceremony?\n\nSorry. I'm terrible with names.

Yes. I'm an alchemist. Before I met this fine lady, I was worried about magical manipulation. For some reason. Hmm. Anyway, I was going to collect spores, create a potion to guard against …. \n\nDid I mention we're to be married?
I brought a few things in with me. Oil. Some flint and tinder. And I think I saw a pile of straw somewhere while I was wandering around.\n\nJust. Hurry.
Not a clue, but the Wizard Bothisii seems very upset about something.
She's hoping to purchase a portal. She wants to go shopping in Windhelm, but she wants to avoid the long boat trip.
As I said, he used to be a member of the Queen's inner circle. He knew Merion, Minantille, and the rest very well. Until he was expelled.

Yes! You've got it. That was it—he was casting spells to manipulate emotions in others. That kind of control over another persons mind. It was driving him insane, I think.\n\nYech. Glad you took care of that one.

I'm trying to remember. This was a bit ago, around the signing of the Aldmeri Dominion charter. If I recall correctly, his wife left him. \n\nThere was an investigation, something about the experiments he was conducting.
Why, an invitation to the Academy of Magic, of course!

You don't know about Shad Astula? That's where the Houses send their best and brightest to learn magic and become future leaders. Oh, and I guess the Academy has been opened to the other Pact nations, as well.

Despite many days of meditating and scrying, Sai Sahan's whereabouts still elude me. The projection that you witnessed in the Foundry of Woe showed him to be in great peril.\n\nIf we are to find him, I will need your help, Vestige.
The Academy of Magic is located on a remote stretch of land upriver.

When Saint Veloth came to Resdayn, what Morrowind is now, he planted the seeds of his homeland. Only the Tree of Summerset survived. This temple was built around it.\n\nStrange. Why do I remember this clearly when all else is fog?
A boat on the Mournhold dock ferries students back and forth to the Academy, but you need an invitation to get on the boat.
Good luck. May Y'ffre guide you.

Unfortunately, yes. That's how he knew about the Jagged Lens. \n\nIn fact, I found him experimenting on a student with the lens when I relieved him of his duties. He was furious when I expelled him from the Academy.
I thought she was a devoted servant of the Tribunal!\n\nBut the things they say about her now are very disturbing.
They say that Magistrix Vox controls the Maulborn and set the Llodos plague loose upon us.\n\nReally, how do rumors like this get started?

It was a relic from the migration from Summerset, still in its original site in the underground temple.\n\nTamper with it? Remove it? Unthinkable! Still, don't feel bad that you destroyed it. You did what had to be done.
Excellent. So now you see—this gem dampens my magicka.\n\nThe crystal I gave you, along with a bit of spellwork, should set me free.
I will start the spell. Once I have the crystal weakened, I will tell you to use the crystal I gave you. Using it will be the final boost I need. \n\nThen I shall be free. Ready?
Oh, she did, did she? And where were you when my crew was being killed by walking skeletons? \n\nNo matter. It's just you and me now. You, me, and this door. And the door is stuck.

Gladly, pilgrim. She is the greatest of Daedric Princes, mistress of dreams and nightmares. All come under her sway as they sleep. \n\nWe supernal dreamers are her worshipers, spreading word of her divinity across Tamriel.

They were—but Vox replenished her forces by calling on all the Daedric cults in Morrowind. \n\nThere are many who openly revere the Three but secretly worship their Anticipations. That's who opposes us.
Phaer used to be a mining town. The workings are still down there. \n\nAfter folks started to get sick, we wanted to keep the worst away from the uninfected. So we put them in quarantine down below.
No, not at all. Amuur and I go down regularly to care for them. We set up a contract with the mercenaries to keep everyone safe. \n\nThis'll all turn out fine in the end.
Calm yourself, friend. She's inside with the Queen. They're practicing for the Thalmor ceremony tomorrow. No need to worry.
Then we end this. Come with Razum-dar!
I know. That's why Raz asked you to investigate the Heritance.
They chased me. I was prowling around the canonreeve's place. Trying to figure … trying to figure out how to turn on that old device.\n\nYou need a set of stones … Aldmeri power stones.
You do that. I'm just going to sit here and rest … try not to get myself stabbed any more today.
Estre doesn't even know magic!\n\nEstre?
The Veiled … surely this is a jest?
Rela leads the Pact here. From some place called Mournhold. Sent by those freaky god-people on the Tribunal, or so I hear it.
One of the Heritance council's top men. I guess he got in good with the Veiled Queen somehow, to get this job.
It's a protection spell. Lodorr's soul is still bound to the crown. Quickly, there's no time. Give it to me!
Ask away.

I can do this. I can resist the mead. For my Gamirth. \n\nFather sent you? Good, I can use the help. The mead is enchanted. It muddles our minds and clouds our memories. But I may have found a way to purify the mead and stop the cravings it inspires.

My brother, Iwelien, was one of the first to fall to the plague. Hendil was so kind, talking to mother. Explaining things. Iwel's been in quarantine for days now with no word. \n\nShe's beside herself. Now with me having to take the salve. Damn it.
<There is no answer. The door is unlocked.>
Shh. Keep your voice down. \n\nIt's part of our indoctrination. We have to denounce the Green Pact every day, commit ourselves to the Dominion.
The instructors keep saying "there is nothing but the Dominion." We're supposed to give up our "old lives" and become one under the Thalmor.\n\nNow leave me be. You'll get me in trouble.

Only Auri-El knows. Dawnbreak's a supply stop between Firsthold and Skywatch, no different than any other town in Auridon. \n\nJust glad the High Kinlady wasn't here when they hit. She left an hour or two before we saw the first Daedra.
No clue. Dawnbreak's just a supply stop between Firsthold and Skywatch. Only notable thing about it: the High Kinlady was here just before they hit. Word came down she made it out, though.
Poor girl. Thank you, for what you could do.\n\nIn the meantime, I've sent out patrols to hunt down any remaining Daedra. They should report back soon.

The Mages Guild gathered a team of the best dungeon-delvers from across the three alliances, members of the Undaunted, just in case they ran into any ruins or relics. My brother went into the old library with a couple of other treasure-hunters.
Thank you. You've been ever so helpful. It's a shame I have to kill you.
What did you think?
You just don't understand. These people are raw, untrained, undisciplined. We must take extraordinary steps.
Thank you! You have a keen eye for quality. Especially rough, with the chattel we have for students here.
Nothing comes to mind. Just the student dorms, and I'd prefer you let the trainees study in peace. \n\nThank you for your interest in the college. I'm afraid I must be going now.

I wasn't sure any of the flowers survived the trip here. Coldharbour is a dead place and Kyne is concerned with living things. If you found the flowers, maybe she hasn't abandoned us.\n\nI'll make the purifying potion now.
Ні.
Так.
Don't you dare touch my spiders. They're my spiders! Mine! Get out of here. Go away and never come back.
<He stares at you.>

I know, I know. I can't explain it. But the last few days, it seems like people don't become sick until after Hendil gives them the salve.\n\nOr perhaps I'm just reading too much into this. Either way.
Hmph. Depends on what you want to know.
I'll tell you. You mentioned quarantine. To say the truth, my coin purse isn't feeling all that well.
Ha! That it is. Your best bet is to grab one of our uniforms from the cabinet in the bunkhouse. \n\nAnyone up there is sure to be sacked out. Won't notice a thing. Just don't tell 'em I sent you.
I wish that were possible. But I promise you, once we escape Coldharbour we will find a way to rescue her together, Vestige.
Get out there and look for our patrols. They'll need relief.\n\nI need to oversee the defense here. May Auri-El preserve us, all.

I am a dangerness … dangerous … woman. Even without my silver daggers, I could flay you. If you think you can threaten me, drink again! I mean, think again! \n\nIf you want my daggers, you'll have to duel me for them!
These relics are my life, traveler! If they become corrupted and stained my life will be over.\n\nI wish I could take this fancy spell with me. I'd go get them myself.

The instructors spout nonsense about civilized behavior whenever we ask that kind of thing. Meanwhile, they try to break us out of our racial customs and culture.\n\nIt's like being short or having a tail is an affront to the Dominion.
The High Elves insisted. They felt, ahem, that "without the proper training, our new allies would be unable to represent the Thalmor agenda."
Stop. Just walk away. I appreciate what you tried to do,  but ….\n\nJust walk away now.
How can you say that? How can you say he deserves—\n\nFine. Fine. I won't touch him. I'll let justice be done.

I'm too duel to drunk. Did I ever tell you I once had a pair of silver dueling daggers? Given to me by … who gave them to me? I should remember. He was such a nice man. \n\nI was brave and fast with my knives. You should have seen me duel.
I won't run. I'll—\n\nTie me up. I'll wait for her to come for me.
What? What do you mean behind everything? He helped! He passed out that salve to everyone and … oh.
Treasure? You won't find that here. But revenge? \n\n…Aye, revenge might just be possible.
That is what I have come to be called. My true name is lost—even to me. Years of torment have taken their toll.\n\nQuickly now, we must make haste to the Anchor!

The Anchors are Daedric machines of the darkest magic. Their chains bind our world and pull it towards Coldharbour. \n\nI can use one of these Anchors to return us to Tamriel, but you must lead me to it.

I despair that you haven't heard of the Direfrosts.\n\nOur family made its reputation as witch hunters. We were heroes to the commoners, and fond of inviting them to feasts within the castle, where they could fawn over us. It was … enjoyable.
One night, a witch seeking revenge for a Coven we raided made her way to our gathering with the locals.\n\nShe played the part of an elderly widow, and we opened our home to her.

She attacked viciously, freezing some, outright killing others with piercing ice.\n\nShe sought vengeance on the Direfrosts for killing her family, you see. Were she not a witch, I would pity her. As it is, I would end her where she stands, if I could.
Lichloving bloodfiend! Stars damn that alchemist. I'll drag him to Skywatch myself, see him clapped in irons.\n\nWhere is he?
I said I'm reading. Go bother someone with an intellect closer to your own level. I'm sure Lady Clarisse and that Altmer artificer would be happy to listen to your inane ramblings.

Really? Well, your timing is terrible. Couldn't you have shown up before we started killing each other?\n\nI'm … sorry. It's not your fault. I'm just frustrated in myself. And a little in pain. Can you believe Mim stabbed me?

Angof told me to plant the seeds in the corpses of the fallen. He seemed desperate, but there was also a kind of compassion in his eyes.\n\nHere. Take them. I don't want them. You can perform this task. Maybe that will help us.

Angof selected me. The bastard who tried to destroy Glenumbra picks the Breton. Of all the arrogance and gall!\n\nI guess it doesn't matter now. He gave me these strange seeds. Said they'd help if I planted them.

Help? You can't help. We're stuck here. Fighting to the death. No one gets out alive. That's just how the game works.\n\nMim will kill them all. Even the Observer. Then he'll have to let us out. He can't hold us here if he's dead!

He said it harnessed the power of the dead, whatever that means. Called it his death rune. It's dark magic and Mim wants no part of it!\n\nShow Mim you actually want to help and figure out what to do with the rune. Maybe we can use it against him.
Help? Just like this one's new master, Thallik, has helped? He tossed me in this pit, gave me this rune, and wished me luck.\n\nI don't even know what to do with the rune!
Help? No one can help us. We're already dead. Lost. Forgotten. More playthings for Molag Bal.\n\nWe can't win this dreadful game. No one can. Why even bother trying?
And he did. He showed me the Admiral's control isn't absolute. \n\nMeet me at the wreck of the Golden Era and we'll find his hidden journal.

The shadow … the one Lady Estre gave me. She said it would protect me.\n\nBut when I refused to fight, to aid the shadow, it claimed I was unworthy. It said I wasn't fit to own such a fine shadow. And then my only chance to survive walked away.

I couldn't even hold on to the one thing I needed to survive. It's useless. Either I fight for naught or I end it all here and now.\n\nI refuse to play this game. I refuse to fight against my friends and allies. It's better this way.
Hmm? Oh, sorry. This book is so engrossing. Could we talk later?
Whatever. Just go away so I can finish this interesting treatise on Dwemer displacement theories.

I don't know what … wait! You're right. This place radiates Daedric magic. I can feel it in the back of my skull. We need to free the others!\n\nFind Lady Clarisse. I remember. She realized something important before we were drawn into the spell.

It will purge the corrupt enchantment from the mead. \n\nThere are three casks. They never ever run out of the Special Blend. Pour some of the potion into each cask. Once the enchantment fades, the craving should go away.
Did you indeed? That be well. Let me see it.\n\nI have a plan, but it only includes me.
Go. Have to keep my eyes open.

Damned vipers came out of nowhere. The town was completely unprepared for the attack. \n\nWe were doing a training exercise nearby and a guardsman ran to grab us. Tried to hold them at the docks, but …. Well, you can see that didn't work out.

Not really sure. But I know what it does—burns up ships that pull into the harbor!\n\nIt's usually inactive, for obvious reasons. But the canonreeve should have been able to power it up long before the Maormer pulled into port.
Ahh. You're the one who destroyed the lighthouse at <<1>>. \n\nYou saved my sister's life. Mara's heart, it's good to meet you.

You're a curious one. I imagine the Thane is keeping his eye on you.\n\nYou want me to reveal a secret? Secrets are a bard's trade, after all. There should be a price. I know! A contest! A duel of words. If you win, amazing secrets will be told!

Oh, you're angry! How positively adorable!\n\nWhen last I saw my beloved lute … I played a song for the lovely Juvilda. I struck a pose, inspired by the statue outside her house. And I sang my heart out, let me tell you. She was suitably impressed.
I say something witty and clever about you … and then you respond in kind. I'll start.\n\nWhither goes that guar? Did it escape from Vvardenfell or is it your sister?

Oh, well played! Well played! \n\nIf I had my lute, I would sing of your prowess. It's gone, though. I last played it for Juvilda. I struck a heroic pose, like the statue of Ysgramor near her house. Sang my heart out. I used be quite good, you know.
Excellent retort!\n\nSpeaking of retort, your armor is so old, even an Akaviri wouldn't wear it.

Begone, you of sober face and dull wit!\n\nMaking me think of my poor, lost lute. How depressing. I last played a song while wooing Juvilda. I struck a heroic pose, like the statue outside her house. Sang my heart out. She was suitably impressed.
That makes no sense. Why would a guar need a lute? It has no fingers! Let us try again.\n\nWho cut your hair? A Falmer? Ha! Take that!
That's ridiculous! Why would the Covenant tie up their own spy?
I'll handle this. I know just what to do when Raynor gets too absorbed in his work. We developed a system for just this sort of situation.\n\nLet's go.
Why would he care? My tailor's a Khajiit, but that doesn't make me a Dominion spy! \n\nThere's no conspiracy. We were ambushed, simple as that.
I can't stand any more bureaucracy! I'm tired of standing in lines and filling out forms.\n\nLet the registrar do whatever paperwork he likes, but I'm done with it!
See? Finally someone with sense has entered the conversation. I'm not going to wait around here all day.
Well, when you put it that way, I guess I could wait a little longer.
What? That's insane! Their alchemist interrogated me three times. Tortured me! Why would he torture me if I was a traitor?

I'll return these to Hridi and Hautt. Ask them to help keep people's spirits up.\n\nDuring my confrontation with the Thane, he said he holds our souls. He laughed at me. Said how amusing it was to see me agonize over my friends as they waste away.
My cousin, Condalin, appointed me Chief of the Flame. I make sure the forges are always hot and running during working hours.
Why, he's the Forgemaster. Runs the whole operation. \n\nHe pulls all the strings around here. With the Canonreeve's approval, of course.
It is! So important, in fact, that I'm paid ten times what these workers get. Hah!
Good, good. I'm here to see what sort of wares Condalin has on offer today. \n\nWe have an arrangement. If you know what I mean.
Yes, yes. It's a sweetheart of a deal. I pass on the goods, and Condalin never has to deal with the unclean.
I have clients. Clients from all across Tamriel who prefer fine Mathiisen steel. The blades crafted here are far superior to the crude curved swords of Alik'r, and the pitted dirks of Skyrim.
Absolutely. We're a forge town, here. We supply blades to the First Auridon Marines, the Queen's royal guard. Even the famed Vinedusk Rangers!
Oh, I don't know. They try, sure. But they're not of the people. Why should they be paid the same as a skilled High Elf worker? Eh?
Well, Malanie's the Canonreeve and Condalin's the Forgemaster. We joke that she runs the front and he runs the back. Heh.
Oh, aye. Cheap labor immigrants. There are some in town that, ah, hate 'em. \n\nBut at least she doesn't have to pay 'em all that well, eh?
Fair enough. Work here is hard. But it's good, honest work. \n\nAt least, working the forge is honest. Don't know about running it.
No. Not at all. Good workers are good workers, doesn't matter if they've got fur or can't change a torch. \n\nThey deserve to be treated right. And I aim to do that, best I can.
I'm the foreman. I try to make sure the steel is forged on schedule and that the workers are cared for.\n\nAt least a little.
Look, I do my best. The Canonreeve, the Forgemaster—they don't care much for us grunts. \n\nAnd they've no love for the Wood Elves and Khajiit. Sometimes I think they see them as work animals.
Malanie and Condalin are business-minded. They see everything in the bottom line. \n\nI just try to make the work as bearable as possible.
Low wages. Grueling hours. Dangerous working conditions. Last week three Bosmer were mangled trying to load a boat. This one doesn't know how much longer he can take it.
Condalin and Malanie don't seem to give a damn, that's for sure.\n\nEnginaire argues with them, but they don't listen. Dark Moon take them.

Simple. This one is a Khajiit. If she were some High Elf hustler, she'd be getting the best deals and the best merchandise. \n\nBut because this one has fur, a tail? All she gets is silence. Dark Moon!
Pah. At this point, no. Zurka needs nothing. She's just trying to open up trade. \n\nThe Khajiit, the High Elves. We are allies now, yes? Auridon and Dune need each other.
Dull claws, busy. Zurka has been here a week. The only person who will talk to her is Aonus, and he's just an apprentice. \n\nThis one will give them one more day. One!
I know now that I made that  terrible bargain with a Daedric Prince in disguise. I was desperate. \n\nYou've saved our souls and I am grateful. Will you reveal my part, or let me try to make amends?
I cannot argue with you. The ones who fled, or who shriveled into the beings we see wandering about will never see Sovngarde, It weighs heavily on me. \n\nSpeak to Nelhilda. Tell her… tell her.

I will strive to make up for what I did in ignorance and selfishness so long ago. \n\nI will help the remaining villagers, as the effects of the long enchantment wear off. But I will grieve for the lost, those shriveled souless ones.
I can't. I promised Father I'd wait for him. I won't leave without him!
No, no! Her ring, it's all I have left. All that's left of my Fara. \n\nI've just … I've misplaced it.
Truly? Is it safe to go?
I … you're right.\n\nPlease, find him. His name is Almion. Tell him I've evacuated?
He went to check on Pirtar. I think we heard his house collapse! Poor man.\n\nPlease, find my father. His name is Almion.
Oh, thank you! Threefold blessings upon you. \n\nIt could be anywhere. This old place is so messy.
Damn it. Fine, fine. I'll go.\n\nMy Fara. Will I ever find you again?
Three-and-five-times blessed am I. Thank you.\n\nAnd blessings to you as well.
<You find a wooden pendant hanging from his neck. The pendant is engraved: "To my loving father. Your Ela.">
No! It can't be true. It can't. He … he was just here.\n\nFine. Fine, I'll go.
Thank you. Thank you so much. My Fara is grateful too, I know it.
His name is Pirtar. I reported him missing to the First Auridon Marines. The Daedra lit our house up like a torch. \n\nPirtar forced me out before the ceiling collapsed, and I haven't seen him since.
Yes, thanks to our son, Esaranir. We were lucky. We've only lived here a short time, but it seems to be one thing after another.
Eight bless and keep him. Our house is on the north end of town. Please, they won't let me back in to look for him!\n\nThis whole thing is my fault anyway.

Cloudrest. When my husband, Fain, told me were moving to Auridon, I was hoping for Firsthold or Skywatch. \n\nAnything to remind me of my mountain home. Dawnbreak is a poor substitute, but I've made do.
Damn it! She doesn't think I can handle myself. \n\nI'm a Rilis! The blood of Auridon's greatest warriors flows in my veins.
Fine. Fine. I'll even pay you for your time. Just remember, the helm will only work for a scion of house Rilis. It's no use to the likes of you.\n\nLet's go.
Ask away, mate, but be quick about it. We need to move out soon.
We was searching for the shipwrecks of the All-Flags Fleet. \n\nDo you know the legend? Scores of ships lost at sea, each one loaded with loot.

Many a year I've sailed the seas around Tamriel, but I've never seen its like. It was vast, larger than all Alten Corimont, and it spun up all sudden-like.\n\nNo wonder sailors call the waters around Thras the Cursed Sea.

Aye, that'd be a fine end to our adventure. We find the great Lost Fleet, and then we walk away from it. \n\nWe lost too many crewmates finding this place. We owe it to them to do at least a little plundering before we pack it in.

Treasure, of course. It's a legend in Alten Corimont that some of our swabs sailed in the fleet that sacked Thras. The ones who survived came home loaded with loot.\n\nIf my ancestors could do it, so can I.
Nothing I couldn't handle. Bigfoot Jak challenged my leadership. Now they call him Pegleg Jak.

I found the log of Admiral Olo's navigator. That told me how to find the Thras Archipelago—or where it used to be, before it mostly sank. \n\nOlo had himself a good navigator, all right. Her directions led me right into the maw of that whirlpool.
Do? What an odd question. I drink! Everyone knows that.\n\nI used to own a smithy once. At least … I think I did. Why do you care?

Well, you can't. There aren't any here. It's too dangerous, what with all these drunks around. The Thane said so.\n\nAnyway, I haven't lifted a hammer in a long, long time. Now go away and leave me to my mead.
Oh, aye—but it'll make a lot of noise. Likely to attract more of those bony swabs. \n\nTell you what. I'll work on the door if you'll keep the bone-boys off me. Deal?
Of course I do! What kind of a question is that?\n\nYou have to admit, though, things have gotten complicated since the Pact was formed.
I'm the Canonreeve of Dawnbreak. I run this town.\n\nI've made a lot of bad decisions, but siding with the Veiled Heritance and Lady Estre has been the worst by far.
I thought the Veiled Heritance was right. We're a small town, set in our ways. \n\nSo we welcomed Estre and ignored warnings from Skywatch. I never thought she'd use the town as a playground.
For her Daedric worship of Mehrunes Dagon. It's her fault the Daedra are here. I can no longer claim ignorance. \n\nI never would have thought she'd fall in league with a Daedric Prince!

Despite many days of meditating and scrying, Sai Sahan's whereabouts still elude me. The projection that you witnessed in the Foundry of Woe showed him to be in great peril.\n\nIf we are to find him, I will need your help, Vestige.
Raynor sent you? But why? I just found the most fascinating … wait, where am I?
I hid the final chapter of my journal in the hold of my ship, the Golden Era. It's docked at the skeleton village. \n\nMy journal holds the key to reaching the Admiral's sanctuary.

Find the Admiral and destroy him.\n\nHe's using the ruins of the fleet to build his Coral Tower. He wants to reach the portal in the sky. We're his slaves, working endlessly to make his mad desires come true.
What's this? Alten Corimont …?\n\nSithis take it! This is nought but the ravings of a madman. Where's the secret he promised?

I see. I suppose I should ask whether or not you're part of this elaborate trap, but I sense that you're not an illusion. \n\nI can feel the spell, however, crawling back, trying to slip into my mind. What an odd sensation!
I wouldn't know exactly, but I'm sure Telenger's around here somewhere. He's really quite clever. And dashing, to boot! He reminds me of my … my good friend, Stibbons.

Hmm … I remember that we discovered something or another, but the details elude me. Perhaps if I had more time to recover from the effects of the spell.\n\nWait a moment, Telenger said something important just before I became engrossed in this relic.
That there Crown of Bones—it's cursed, belike. You could destroy it. That might set the sailors free—or it might destroy them. \n\nI have another proposition for you. Give the crown to me.
Then the curse is broken at last.
First we goes up against Molag Bal. That's a swab what needs taking down a peg. And I'm just the lizard to do it.
I must ask you to reconsider, mate. I've got a quarrel with this here Molag Bal, and I intend to lead these sailors against him. \n\nAfterwards, I'll set them all free. Assuming we survive.

Aye, but Molag Bal made it for the Admiral, not for me. \n\nI know a trick or two I learned from an old shaman. I think I can use the crown on the sailors, one by one, to set their souls free. But first ….
Maybe you're right. Nelhilda struggled to find the enchantment, and she lost her beloved Gamirth.\n\nShe deserves my honesty. I hope she can forgive me.
Mother will stay here while we're down in the vault.\n\nWe will fulfill my destiny!
I can't. I promised Father I'd wait for him. I won't leave until he returns!
No! It can't be true. It can't! He—he was just here.\n\nFine, fine. I'll go.
That's asking a lot of me.\n\nMy father always seemed more … aware. I sometimes wondered if he knew more than he let on. But to have caused all of this suffering? My poor Gamirth!
I stopped keeping track yesterday. Now I'm just using this time to sit and think.
The many ways I'm going to make that registrar suffer … after he finishes processing my entry, of course.
This vault contains a portal, and the power emanating from it is overwhelming. Something on the other side seeks to pierce the veil of illusion that hangs over this ruined library.

I have my suspicions, but I hate to speculate. If you must know, I think it might be one of the fabled Lights of Meridia—the sources of power she used to hurl the Hollow City into Coldharbour.\n\nCome in and we shall investigate further.

Relmus would not fiddle, and my loyalty must be bought with both rhyme and riddle.\n\nThe Dark Elf is weak, and I refuse to be meek. So someone stronger I seek! Is it you, I must ask? For this one simple task—find my lovely lady's carnival mask!

Three pieces to find, each of a kind. \n\nThe first below the rock bridge, where the spiky vines live. The second one stays, near where the river meets my gaze. And the third piece sits, by the frozen giant's bits. So now we are intertwined!

When the job is done, we can resume the fun, with the Dark Elf safe and unspoken. But finding the mask is no easy task, for its pieces are scattered and broken.\n\nI know the locations. I know your motivations. So listen well with great expectations!

You must pick a side in the game. There is no other option. The rules are built into the very fabric of this domain. The only way to save your mages is to follow the rules and win the game.\n\nNow, choose a side or leave the mages to their fate.

Angof the Undying grows weaker. He doubts the choices he's made. Regret overwhelms him and pushes him to desperate measures.\n\nAre you sure you wish to side with one who carries such a debilitating burden?

Thallik, one-time servant of Mannimarco, sees nothing but death and desires nothing but power. There is more evil in his soul than you could find in a hundred mortals.\n\nAre you sure you wish to side with one whose soul is blacker than the night?

Kinlady Estre of the silver tongue. Quick-witted and capable of bargaining her soul over and over. How many Daedric lords have won and lost it, I do not know.\n\nAre you sure you want to side with one who is so deceptive?

So you believe. You must win the war first.\n\nNow who will you choose? Angof of the Reach? Thallik of the Wormcult? Or Kinlady Estre, the former Altmer Princess? You may speak to them once more before you make your decision.
Perhaps. She's a powerful woman, and some mage with a grudge could have set this up. Just missed the mark.\n\nWe'll look into it.
There are a pair of Dremora further up in the cave. They're preparing another mass summoning as we speak. \n\nIt's up to you. I can't leave Qoramir here like this.
Thanks. You were right, by the way. Estre's not just Veiled Heritance—she's a thrice-damned cultist as well!\n\nQor overheard the High Kinlady talking to these Daedra by magical sending.
Thrice-blessed are we. I couldn't have asked Urcelmo for a better Marine.\n\nWhat of Estre? Did you learn anything more?
I had a feeling things would get worse. We need to get word to Lord Rilis of Firsthold. And fast.
The Rilis Helm. It imbues the wearer with the strength of a mighty warrior. \n\nIt's the birthright of my family. Been in the Rilis line for generations—all the way back to Rilis the First.
No! I mean. You can't. It's in the vault below us. The vault is shut fast by a trio of wards. \n\nEach ward is guarded by one of Rilis's loyal captains. And only I know how to lower the wards.

Despite many days of meditating and scrying, Sai Sahan's whereabouts still elude me. The projection that you witnessed in the Foundry of Woe showed him to be in great peril.\n\nIf we are to find him, I will need your help, Vestige.
Danger presses in from every direction. The city doesn't know how to handle it.
Even in a crisis, the city must maintain its bureaucracy. If that means we all have to deal with a little inconvenience, so be it.\n\nI can wait.
We'll only be down there for a moment. And when I emerge with the helm, I'll be a powerful Rilis warrior.\n\nI'll be able to keep her safe for the rest of our lives!

Look around, you fool! Would you open the cage of one prison simply to release them into another? This whole realm is a prison!\n\nNo, there is no way to save your mages. We are all trapped here. Forever.

Thallik and Estre's champions must fall. Use my seeds. Plant them in the bodies of those you slay to gain new allies to aid you.\n\nIt won't be easy, and you probably won't win, but you're the best chance I've had to end this since I got here.

The magic that created this body resides in this land. If I can win this game and escape these Cliffs of Failure, I hope to find its source.\n\nHelp me win and you can take Juline with you. I simply seek a way to end this madness.
You and everyone else shoving their way into the city. What makes you so special?
My turn to see the registrar, so I can go about my business. \n\nThe Dark Elves have so many rules.

Gamirth believed it had something to do with a Daedric Prince and a bad bargain. If that's true, we never figured out who struck the deal.\n\nAll I'm certain of is that the mead is delicious and it never runs out. And drinking it has cost us our souls.

Not a one in the whole place. Some of us shrivel up and turn into the creatures outside. Others run off to die, like my Gamirth did. The rest of us drink.\n\nI abstain from the mead for a while, try to remember the old days. Then the craving returns.

Yes. We stay inside and drink. We have no souls. We were afraid to die in this godforsaken place. Nords without souls aren't welcome in Sovngarde, you know.\n\nThe Thane does what he can to keep us happy, usually by opening another cask of mead.
Really? I knew you could do it. Well, I mean, I didn't actually know you could do it, but I had a good feeling about you.\n\nDid you see the others? Relmus? Mim?
Oh. The reward. I'm pretty sure you don't want any part of whatever the Observer is offering.\n\nJust … be careful up there, you hear me? I have a bad feeling about this.
I have to find them! We got into this together and we're going to get out of here the same way.\n\nWhere were you rushing off to, by the way?
Fine. Just remember it this time.
Fine. Just remember it this time.

My life can be measured in hours,
I serve by being devoured.
Thin, I am quick,
Fat, I am slow,
Wind is my foe.
Two bodies have I, though both joined in one,\nThe more I stand still the faster I run.\nWhat am I?
I have lots to say but never speak,\nI open but you cannot walk through me,\nI have a spine but no bones.
When young, I am sweet in the sun.\nWhen middle-aged, I make you gay.\nWhen old, I am valued more than ever.

Keep me with you to survive
In the fields of death few keep alive
I am like a taller knife
deadly enough to end a life.
I'm by nature solitary, scarred by spear and wounded by sword, weary of battle.\nI frequently see the face of war, and fight hateful enemies.
Always smiling but cannot laugh\nAlways staring but cannot see\nOnce held secrets and dreams
Oh, I see! One of my cousins must have sent you.\n\nGrandfather promised it was for me. Now fetch off!
Oh. Well, trust me, it's really interesting. I wonder. If I were to cast Spell Absorption at a Flame Atronach, if the resulting pyrodynamic inversion would ….
What? Who are you to come into my home and badmouth the greatest mage the northlands have ever seen? Get out!
Hmm. Maybe you should talk to <<1>>.
Sure! I'll have some wine. Maybe a cheese plate, too.
You should probably walk away now.
And I think you need to get gone before I show you the back of my hand.
Gosh you're cute. But I have no idea what you're talking about.
I'm married. Remove yourself from my presence.

A mask of beauty and style, it gives my lady power of shadow and guile. It broke and fell, at a party so swell, and now neither of us knows where it does dwell.\n\nSo to this place I'm sent, to seek, to repent. And to find where that pesky mask went!
Welcome to the Veiled Isle. You're just off the coast of Skywatch. Our own private training ground. \n\nYou've been chosen to join. A cut above—an officer of the Veiled Heritance.

You can see the black soul gem here. Place your hand on it. Good. You can come and go all you want. But first—you take the oath. \n\nBe sure you want this. You commit your immortal soul with this pledge.
Repeat after me. I pledge my life and soul to the Heritance and the Veiled Queen.
I don't know what you're talking about. I've been here forever, enjoying the drinks and the fire pit dancing.
You don't miss much, do you, my friend?\n\nNow let a girl enjoy her sujamma in peace.
Gone? How? \n\nWhat happened down there?
My Sor. So determined to prove himself. Auri-El keep him safe.\n\nAt least someday, perhaps, he'll be happy again. Like the little boy I knew.
What? It was supposed to make him powerful. Like his father. \n\nI lost my boy for nothing?
I hope so. Dame Narine is not known for her patience.
Fantastic! It's been so long! Maybe now I can find some peace.
<The crystal feels warm in your hands and hums with energy.>
The god of secrets and hidden knowledge, dear. Would that he was speaking to me today, the paint would be flowing. Instead I'm standing here waiting for Silvermane to tell me what to do.

Oh, most days I am dearie. Most days. Couldn't find a more lovely place to ply my trade than home sweet home in Auridon. Just look at those trees. If you've never been, be sure to walk along the beaches to the east. Just gorgeous sunsets.
Am I all right? Oh, I'm perfect. But I am not who you seek. You won't release them from our spell! They belong to us now.\n\nBut you? You shall simply die!
How sweet, but I'm not who you think I am. Now, how should I kill you?
No, not even a little. You won't find your artificer. And you'll never leave here alive!

Confounding, isn't it? Such is the way of things in Coldharbour.\n\nThe game goes on, and so there must always be a game master. Still, I am amazed that you managed to win the game. That should have been impossible. So, choose your reward!

You won, fair and square. So you may select one companion to take with you when you leave. Only one. The others must stay and continue to play the game until they can win for themselves.\n\nNow, are you ready to make your decision?
Very well. The mages are yours. Angof will have the honor of continuing to play my game.\n\nFarewell, and thank you for such an excellent competition. You will not be allowed to participate again.
The vined one? You would abandon your comrades for one such as he? You continue to surprise me, mortal.\n\nNow, you and your prize must go. Do not return here, for you may not play the game again.
Of course you are. But you could have sided with the weepy, thorny bastard. Or the deceptive Lady Estre.\n\nBut, no. You selected me.

Watch your tone! To win, you'll need more power. Take my death rune. Use it when you wish.\n\nDon't try to deny that you've enjoyed the power. Freedom from one's flesh can be so … rejuvenating! No need to thank me. Just go out there and win.

Eager to serve. I like that. So much more backbone than what the cat demonstrates.\n\nWell, if you want to win, you must defeat Angof's and Estre's champions. That's all you have to do. Simple, when you think about it.
Ah, that explains it! No one has ever done such a thing before. The Observer said he would have to change the rules now. \n\nBut this one wonders, where are his friends?

Yes … that is what the Observer meant when he said he was changing the rules. Thallik was so angry. He stormed off. Muttered that if the Observer died, no one would be left to enforce the rules.\n\nI will find the others and meet you up there.
I must find them! We will band together and escape this place, one way or another.\n\nWhere were you rushing off to, by the way?

Confounding, isn't it? Such is the way of things in Coldharbour.\n\nThe game goes on, and so there must always be a game master. Still, I am amazed that you managed to win the game. That should have been impossible. So, choose your reward!

Very well. The members of the Mages Guild are yours. Thallik will have the honor of continuing to play my game.\n\nFarewell, and thank you for such an excellent competition. You will not be allowed to participate again.
The Wormtongue? You would abandon your comrades for one such as he? You continue to surprise me, mortal.\n\nNow, you and your prize must go. Do not return here, for you may not play the game again.

You won, fair and square. So you may select one companion to take with you when you leave. Only one. The others must stay and continue to play the game until they can win for themselves.\n\nAre you ready to decide than?
No, I suppose not. \n\nBut it looked the way they're described in "Magic from the Sky!" What else could it have been?

Oh, I understand. I really do. But do those things need to be mutually exclusive? I think not!\n\nYou saw me as the best path to victory, so you struck a bargain to join my side. As a connoisseur of bargains, I can assure you that you chose wisely.

Oh, yes! You have a quality I haven't seen in Coldharbour before. A gleam in your eyes. You can do this!\n\nNow, that nice shadow fellow you helped earlier is also sworn to my cause. Just use my mask when you need assistance and he'll come running.

So direct. How delicious! I could just eat you up. I really could!\n\nFor me to win, my champion must eliminate my opponents' champions. But the Observer, that clever gamemaster, always makes sure the champions are evenly matched.
I suppose it will have to do. I've been away from my studies far too long!
I suppose you're right … should have asked, at least.\n\nI'd hoped to get my money back. Ah, well. It could have been worse.

That's surprising. Oh, I had complete faith in you. I really did. But no one has ever survived long enough to defeat two champions. It's unprecedented!\n\nDid you see Juline and Mim? What happened to them?

I bought a magic stone. Slipped it into <<1>>'s pocket to get back at him for rubbing ivy on my bedroll.\n\nNot a minute later, he's struck by a bolt from the sky! Look at him! He's lucky to be alive!

If the Observer has changed the rules, I doubt it's a reward he plans to give you.\n\nMy guess? He's going to throw more opponents at you until you finally fall. It's what I would do. Well, good luck up there. I think you'll need it.
I guess I should go try to find them. They really are lost without me, you know.\n\nWhere were you rushing off to, by the way?

Confounding, isn't it? Such is the way of things in Coldharbour.\n\nThe game goes on, and so there must always be a gamemaster. Still, I am amazed that you managed to win the game. You accomplished the impossible. So, choose your reward!
Very well. The mages are yours. Estre will have the honor of continuing to play my game.\n\nFarewell, and thank you for such an excellent competition. You will not be allowed to participate again.

The conniving princess? You would abandon your comrades for one such as she? You continue to surprise me, mortal.\n\nNow, you and your prize must go. Do not return here, for you may not play the game again.

You won, fair and square. So you may select one companion to take with you when you leave. Only one. The others must stay and continue to play the game until they can win for themselves.\n\nNow decide. Who will go with you?
Sure, it's in my pack. I'll get it.
The foreman has me working all the time. Things were much better when my cousin was still alive.
That's fair, friend. The work here is rough and tiresome, but it's good, honest work. At least, working the forge is honest. Don't know about the people who run it.
No, not at all. Good workers are good workers, no matter where they're from. They deserve to be treated right. And I aim to do that, despite my employers' opinions.
I do my best. My employers don't care much for us low-level folk. They particularly hate the Bosmer and Khajiit who come here. Consider them work animals more than proper mer.
I'm the foreman. I make sure the work gets done properly and honestly. And to make sure the conditions are good for me workers.
Malanie and Condalin are business minded. They see everything in the bottom line. I just try to make the work as bearable as possible given what little resources I have.
Many soups, many different flavors.
Many soups, but not all at once. I have only one pot! If you are too greedy, you get no soup at all!
No choices. Today I make root vegetables in a silverskin broth.
I hear things. Rumors about the Skald-King. Talk of secret Pact meetings. Tales of people not acting like themselves.
I lost some of my apprentices to the beasts. So when I made it back to town, I cast a spell that would protect everyone. It was the only way.
It means the inn is full and profits are through the roof! That's what it means, friend. That's what it means.
Do you see the Skald-King? I'm here with me, myself, and mead. Lots of mead.

No! She's not safe! Hughes is going to kill her! He's crazy—something about his dreams. If you don't believe me, check his journal. He was writing all about it. \n\nFirst though, untie me. I have to get back to the castle and warn Lakana!
This house belongs to me and my husband, Benus.\n\nIf you have business with Benus, you can find him at the forge.
Oh, my. I think there's been a mistake.\n\nYou should leave my home. Now.
No song, huh? \n\nWell, know that this is the fabulous Everfull Flagon, purveyor of the finest mead in all of … wherever we are.

I do, I really do. Wait, was that some sort of insult? I should give you a proper thrashing for that! \n\nBut I can't stay angry at you! Have I told you about the time I performed in the Tribunal Temple? My voice made the Dark Elves weep.
I'm engaged in a long-term research project dealing with necromantic peculiarities.\n\nNow stand back. Death magic can be dangerous to the uninitiated.

The Everfull Flagon has the finest mead! \n\nDon't drink the mead. Gamirth is dead? He was my daughter, Nelhilda's, mate. Her true love. I suspect the contents of that letter will break her heart—if she's sober.

There are two trials, each designed to prove your worth to one of the factions here in Haj Uxith—the Trial of Spirit and the Trial of Body. One shall test your intangible qualities, the other your physical virtues.

You must try our Special Blend. Do you like to celebrate? Everyone here is always celebrating something!\n\nNelhilda and Gamirth were working to find a way to end this madness. Go upstairs and talk to Nelhilda. She has a plan.
Who cares? We don't need a reason to celebrate. It's time for mead! And the Special Blend is out of this world! Celebrate that!
It certainly is! Best party ever! And this place serves the best mead.\n\nBut you really ought to talk to Brent. I mean Berd. No, that's not right. Bernt! Talk to Bernt!
Unusual? For people to drink and enjoy themselves? I find it refreshing!\n\nRelax. Have a drink. I hear the Special Blend is very tasty.
Don't like Grubby. Won't listen to him. Go away.
No! I'm a Goblin. We're a tribe. A family.\n\nGah. Leave before I kill you.

As long as those creatures prowl the woods, we're in danger. I believe the monoliths in the woods have something to do with the Daedric influence. \n\nDispel their energies. Hopefully that will free the animals.
I'm the Thane of the Everfull Flagon. It's my duty to make sure everyone has a good time. I take my position very seriously.\n\nYou should either join us or leave this fine establishment.
They're ancient. I've studied them for years in my spare time. Not even really sure who put them up. But I'm certain they're why the local creatures are normally so docile.
Ah. Yes. I theorize that wherever the Daedra came from, they're somehow polluting the energy of these monoliths.\n\n Dispel that energy and—I hope—the Daedra will become powerless.

There are many who wish we could rebel, but the Admiral holds the Crown of Bones. Molag Bal himself gave him that terrible relic.\n\nWith it, the Admiral controls the cursed skeletons of the fleet. But you aren't cursed yet.
I need to—we need to—extract the Daedric energy from these beasts. To do that, we'll need a test subject.\n\nYou'll have to rough the furry fellow up a bit first. Weaken him for the spell to work.
Meet me at my tower with your friend. Just follow the road through the grove.
Hrmm. And maybe I will, at that. Alten Corimont, he said. That changes things. \n\nAll right, mate. You're in. But a ship has only one captain, and that's me.
No! It hasn't! Look, whatever's actually controlling these things, I think it's at the bottom of the cave.\n\nI'm. Very woozy. Blood loss. I'll stay here, try to stay conscious.

It's not just the Daedra. It's the monoliths. I've studied them for years. Worked out how the magics pacify the beasts. But that's all the magic does. It turns beasts into mewling pets. Not combat troops!
Yes! The Flame Atronachs are essentially just raw Daedric energy given form. I summoned some, hulled them down, and poured them into the monoliths.\n\nThat creature in the cave was not in the plan.
Unlikely. The whole town was in the grip of plague when I left.
What? That bastard. Pretending to help the sick. Thank you traveler. Whinnie and I will head back soon enough, then! Stars thank you for your kindness.
How—how did you know?

He wants to prove himself to his ancestors. He thinks there's some sort of treasure, deep in the vaults. Sor wants so badly to be a Rilis. \n\nI just want him to be safe. Please, will you look after him?
Cats? What cats?
Relax! I'm just fooling with you. Of course I see the cats. They're my babies. They keep me company in my old age, since my ungrateful relatives are too busy to come and visit.
Yes, we celebrate every year! A triumphant appreciation of the day Skywatch was retaken from the Sload.

Of course! Skywatch is a magnificent city. Telenger's Emporium is not to be missed. There's an ancient Ayleid ruin right in the middle of town! And our docks are visited by men and mer from across Tamriel.
They are, ahem, "slug people." A Betmer race like the Khajiit or Argonians. Their empire once ruled the seas of southern Tamriel. They struck out at other nations as despots and slavers.

What isn't? Ships pull into the harbor every day, bringing new smells, sights, and sounds to our fair city. Some of the dockworkers race frogs in between jobs, and the Barbed Hook always has a tasty brew on tap.
The race was boring. This city is boring. You're boring. Go bother someone who doesn't have important things to do.

The weak always resort to threats and violence. Oh very well!\n\nI saw one of those Stormfist thugs run away as soon as the racer fell. He fled out of the city, heading south. It was like Molag Bal himself was right behind him.
I'd prefer to find a hot meal and a strong drink. Now if you'll excuse me, I'd rather not talk to you any longer.
I'm fine. I need a drink and I miss Gamirth terribly, but otherwise I'm fine.

I made a bargain, but I was tricked. I realized too late that the mage who promised to help me was likely a Daedric Prince!  \n\nAfter that, the Flagon slipped into Coldharbour and we've been trapped here ever since.
One of the patrols returned—thanks to you—and mentioned a cave entrance to the northeast. Landare couldn't wait. She took some mer and they left for the caves.
She's always been this way. I'm worried she's in over her head. \n\nHelp her, please. Maybe you can strap her fool head to her shoulders.

Telenger the Artificer, greatest Mage of our time! He's in the field, even now, in the ruin just below Skywatch. \n\nSometimes I like to imagine I can see him down there, among the old buildings of Ezduiin.
Very! He and his assisant, Andewen, travel across the face of Tamriel in search of lost and forbidden lore.

That's because I drink mead! You should, too. Our Special Blend will put hair on your chest and make you strong.\n\nAnyway, have some mead or take a walk. We're having a party here and I'd hate to have you spoil the mood.
Can you have another mead? Of course you can!\n\nVery well, ask what you will. But be quick about it. We don't want to attract any undue attention.
Wrestling? That's for amateurs! But pig chasing? I'll win that one, for sure.

I'm trying not to arouse any suspicion. The Thane is always watching, listening. We must put on a good show.\n\nThe celebrating has been going on for a long, long time. Who would've thought that an endless supply of mead could become such a curse?

What would you have everyone do? Put their lives on hold until peace blooms across the land? Well, friend, that time is a long way off. Better to use the time we have than to wait for the time that may never come.
Aren't you the brave one! I'm kind of busy right now, but I might let you buy me a few meads later tonight. Just try to keep up with me.

Canst thou see? I am a joke, made real. A spirit, bound by the power-mad knave known as Telenger. I hath served my master faithfully, fulfilled my task.\n\nAnd so now he has me serving. The likes of you.

Master goes on ever so many travels. When he returns, he does so with objects and bric-a-brac. Baubles that even the basest mind would dismiss. But the living today. Idiots!\n\nAnd so I sell these cheap trinkets for … him.
All the time! It certainly makes the day go faster. This one is special, though. In honor of the Konunleikar.\n\nI just wish I won every now and then.
If you're talking about that stupid game my cousins always play, I guess so. Someone has to beat them, after all. It might as well be me.
Sales have been amazing since the visitors started to arrive. Not much call for my stock among the Nords, but you wouldn't believe how popular my wares are with the Dark Elves and Argonians.
Do not attempt to know my heart, mortal.\n\nJuline is pure. Unlike the rest of my army, she's not tainted by corruption. I need one such as her if I am to win this war.

I want to become whole again. That's why I play this ridiculous game.\n\nNow leave me. The seeds have increased my forces and given me the numbers I need to win this war. That's all I required of you.
Serve the Lord of Schemes? Never again, mortal!\n\nI fight this battle to live. To reverse what I've become. This magic that made me like this hides in this realm. As does the magic to restore me.

The rune you carry is more powerful than you can imagine. If the cat knew its true potential, he would never have given it up.\n\nThe power of the dead flows through the rune. Necromancy, some call it. But the rune serves another purpose, as well.

Use the rune within this circle and you will transform. Then the rune will absorb the essence of everything you slay.\n\nThe more you kill, the stronger the rune becomes. But don't linger. The death rune's transformative power lasts only so long.

The death rune transforms you. Every death you deal in this form fills the rune. I intend to use the fully charged rune to escape this plane. Not even the Observer will be able to stop me.\n\nAnd I'll remember anyone who assisted me, of course.
Perhaps. There's—

What? Can't you read my mind? I tease! I tease!\n\nI came to thank you for the service you provided me. A service I didn't even ask you to do. The Dark Elf here … such a poor fellow. The things he considered doing to himself. Very sad.

Because you need to decide soon. The Observer won't let you play the game much longer if you don't select a side.\n\nI invite you to join my team. We'd be perfect together. It makes perfect sense. That's why I'm so glad I thought of it!

Direct and to the point. I can appreciate that. We have so much in common, you and I!\n\nI wanted you to know that you're exceeding the Observer's expectations. He thought you'd be dead by now. He certainly didn't expect you to run and save everyone.
<Fresh water splashes in the fountain.>
<A few gold coins glitter on the mossy stonework, marking the wishes of passersby.>
Why? Because it's not safe.\n\nAs to what's in there … I can't really say.
Yes. It's … I suppose I can say this. It's as much to keep things in as to keep you out.\n\nThere, I've said everything I can.
Won't. I've been forbidden to speak of it by the Artificer himself. You want to know what's in there, take it up with him.\n\nIf you can get him to talk about it.
CH - CoF - Observer Optional C
As you wish. But don't take too long. I have a game to get back to!\n\nOnce you've made your decision, talk to me again.
Angof's power is far greater than our own. You'll need someone of his caliber at your side to defeat Molag Bal.\n\nIt just makes more sense to select Angof instead of us.
Please, that isn't all I need. I'm hurt. I won't make it out on my own.\n\n<<1>> is out there somewhere. If you catch her, bring her back to me. I'm doomed without her.

Think with your mind and not your heart. Angof gives you the best chance for victory. We both know that.\n\nI wish there was another way. I wish we could all walk out of this together. But Nirn is more important than a trio of mages.
Look at me! I'm a monster!\n\nI deserve my fate. The others … they did nothing wrong. You came here to save them, so finish what you started!
It doesn't matter. You did what I could not. You won the game.\n\nNow take the mages and get away from here before the Observer changes the rules again!
Take these berries. <<1>> loves them. Feed her a few and she'll follow you anywhere.

Because the balance of the game must be maintained. If you select Angof, then the mages take his place. If you choose the mages, Angof remains as a leader in the game.\n\nYou are lucky that I agreed to provide this reward at all.
Very well. The mages are yours. Angof will have the honor of continuing to play my game.\n\nFarewell, and thank you for such an excellent competition. You will not be allowed to participate again.
Thank you. I'll be here, waiting. Unless a crocodile gets me.
The vined one? You would abandon your comrades for one such as he? You continue to surprise me, mortal.\n\nNow, you and your prize must go. Do not return here, for you may not play the game again.
I … the unmitigated … how dare … fine!\n\nTake them all and do not return. My master will be angry, but not as enraged as he would be if the game was permanently disrupted. Now, be gone with you!
What? How dare you threaten me!\n\nYou are lucky that I even gave you a reward at all. The balance … the balance must be maintained!

Can't you smell the smoke? Silsailen is under attack! I barely got my father out alive! The Canonreeve, almost slain!\n\nThese brutes may wear the uniforms of the First Auridon Marines, but they're imposters.
They're agents of the Veiled Heritance. I'm sure of it! Teldur, my father's assistant, is trying to organize a defense. \n\nYou look capable. Will you help Silsailen?
<This guar is very dead, torn apart by crocodiles. If the creature ever wore a pack, it's long gone.>
As you wish. But don't take too long. I have a game to get back to!\n\nOnce you have made your decision, talk to me again.

Because the balance of the game must be maintained. If you select Thallik, then the mages take his place. If you choose the mages, Thallik remains as a leader in the game.\n\nYou are lucky that I agreed to provide this reward at all.
Very well. The mages are yours. Thallik will have the honor of continuing to play my game.\n\nFarewell, and thank you for such an excellent competition. You will not be allowed to participate again.

The one with the heart as black as night? You would abandon your comrades for one such as he? You continue to surprise me, mortal.\n\nNow, you and your prize must go. Do not return here, for you may not play the game again.
I … the unmitigated … how dare … fine!\n\nTake them all and do not return. My master will be angry, but not as enraged as he would be if the game was permanently disrupted. Now, be gone with you!
What? How dare you threaten me!\n\nYou are lucky that I even gave you a reward at all. The balance … the balance must be maintained!

Two fragments of my soul remain imprisoned. Free them, and I would … I would finally be able to move on.\n\nAnconath's cries have echoed through this chamber for years. The silence now is almost deafening.
Well, this one is trapped in a cage. Could be pointy sticks poking my tender paws, but otherwise ….\n\nWhat do I think? I think you should choose your Mages Guild allies and get us out of here!
How powerful could the lying one be? He's as trapped as we are!\n\nWe came to this dreadful realm to accomplish something great. Please, let us see this through alongside you.
Because you enjoy winning. Only I can provide the power you need to stand against Molag Bal!\n\nNow go tell the Observer that I'm the one and get me out of this blasted cage!

If that were true, why are you still talking to me? You know I am the right choice. I'm the only choice!\n\nIf you plan to march on Molag Bal, you need the most powerful allies at your side. This has already been decided. You just have to accept it.
<Crocodiles tore this guar apart, along with any bags it was carrying.>
<From the savage bite marks along this guar's back, anything it once carried is most likely in a crocodile's stomach.>

My research is vital to the study of spellcasting. This amulet may enable the safe and efficient harvesting of potent magicka, such as the wamasu's lightning. It's relatively safe, which makes Drulis's refusal so galling.

He tends to get hurt. If he'd just follow my instructions, all would go well.\n\nI told him to remove the codpiece last time. And not to touch the copper wire before that. He may be an old family friend, but he's not the swiftest boat in the river.
Your determination gives me hope. I resigned myself to the pain a long time ago.\n\nYou'll find the last fragment through the gate in the south-east.
As you wish. But don't take too long. I have a game to get back to!\n\nOnce you've made your decision, let's talk again.

Oh, come now! I've never encountered a rule I couldn't bend to my own advantage. You just have to figure out how.\n\nMaybe you can threaten the Observer and make him change his mind. I'd certainly enjoy watching you try!
Then we will drink a toast to your comrades and honor their memories. I can even provide a sympathetic shoulder if you need a good cry.\n\nNow, get on with it. I'm anxious to see what happens next.

I'll be much better once you get us out of here. I've never liked tight, confining spaces.\n\nYou are going to select us to set free, aren't you? That is the reason why you came to the Cliffs of Failure, after all.

Of course he does. And the High Lady batted her eyes and stuck out her bossom. She does have an effect on people, I'll give her that.\n\nBut she's here for a reason. Whatever she did, she deserved this fate. We didn't. Remember that.

Because the balance of the game must be maintained. If you select Estre, then the mages must take her place. If you choose the mages, then Estre continues to lead her side.\n\nYou are lucky I agreed to provide this award at all.
Very well. The mages are yours. Estre will have the honor of continuing to play my game.\n\nFarewell, and thank you for such an excellent competition. You will not be allowed to participate again.

The one with the silver tongue? Her words are more powerful than I expected to make you abandon your comrades for her. You continue to surprise me, mortal.\n\nNow, you and your prize must go. Do not return here, for you may not play the game again.
I … the unmitigated … how dare … fine!\n\nTake them all and do not return. My master will be angry, but not as enraged as he would be if the game was permanently disrupted. Now be gone with you!
What? How dare you threaten me!\n\nYou are lucky that I even gave you a reward at all. The balance … the balance must be maintained!
That's his problem. He must be crazy if he thinks I'll suffer through another of his experiments.\n\nDid he tell you about the magicka-storing belt? Nearly cut me in two.
Be my guest, but I warned you. All of <<1>>'s experiments result in blood loss.\n\nThat flat-head still blames me for the failure of his Wand of Satiation.
Perhaps you're right. He hasn't killed me yet.\n\nThough he might succeed this time. Let him know I'll test it shortly.

He's tried that too many times to count, and I have the scars to prove it.\n\nI've been bait for cave trolls and dug through dung piles, but getting myself shocked to death isn't research. It's torture.

My husband, Sinyon, is the Canonreeve of Dawnbreak. My parents thought us a good match. \n\nBut Dawnbreak is a sty, a place more fit for watering horses than raising a family. And Sinyon has turned out the fool.
Yes. I warned him about Estre and this Veiled Heritance. Queen Ayrenn is the rightful heir. It's our duty to follow her command. \n\nUntil Ayrenn fails us, my faith lies with her.
It's the Queen, Ayrenn. We were supposed to leave town, but word of Ayrenn's schedule reached us. I wanted to see our new Queen, the founder of the Dominion. If only I'd been less selfish.
Yes. Esaranir enjoys hunting. He barely made it back from Shattered Grove. It seems Daedric activity is everywhere these days.
Yes, but gods, did you see what those Daedra did to the manor house? Can you imagine how long it will take to clean and rebuild?
I've the honor to be Dawnbreak manor's chief servant. I live to serve!\n\nMara's Heart, give me strength in the days to come.

Far to the south. I travel all over Shadowfen, selling my goods in every town and city. I had a particularly good season this year, until the crocodiles attacked.\n\nStill, I can probably catch and train more pack guar on my way back.
Stormhold's the largest settlement, a good place for trade.\n\nMy main route takes me to Stillrise and Mud Tree Village. I used to travel down to Zuuk too, but not in the last few years.
I've been stopping there for the last, oh, five or six years. I usually stop there after Mud Tree Village. Stillrisers are crazy for tools and iron ore. They pay with old Kothringi coins sometimes.

Mud Tree was once an old Dunmer fort, but now it's a mining town.\n\nMy people used to be slaves to the Dunmer, but now they mine for a living. I heard rumblings about Goblins at the mines lately, though.

I haven't been to Zuuk in a long time. It was a Kothringi village, but the Knahaten flu took a heavy toll there.\n\nNow that I think about it, a merchant in Stillrise said something about a brother who lived in Zuuk, I think.
The amulet would be a catalyst for spells <<1>> has been researching. He hopes to use it to recharge staves more quickly.\n\nWell, I found a wamasu for him, but I won't be his test guar any longer.

I did not dare to hope you would make it this far, but your abilities have been astonishing.\n\nThe pieces of my soul are free, though my husband left two Daedric minions, Ilambris-Athor and Ilambris-Zavon, to prevent the shards from reuniting.

The Daedra maintain spells that will keep the shards from ever merging—my soul from reforming.\n\nMy husband meant for my pain to be the likes of torture in Oblivion. How better to ensure that than to bring denizens of Oblivion to me?

You have been very gracious. \n\nThis shard has been freed, but if you're willing to help me further, there are two other shards to free—and the crypt's caretakers in the south wing must be defeated before I can become whole again.
He's a liar and a cheat. We discovered he was courting all three of us at once.\n\nThis was his favorite wooing spot. Seems fitting that he die here.
Perhaps you're right, if the stains on his smallclothes are any indication. We'll let him go, but all of Cyrodiil will know of his shame.
I can't believe I trusted you. I let him trick me into yet another death trap!

The amulet didn't protect me against the lightning, and the beast's jaws nearly took my head off! It destroyed my favorite shirt. Gran made that shirt!\n\nNow leave me be. I don't want that thing finding me and finishing the job.
Of course he did, the skinny weakling! If it wasn't for him, we wouldn't be in this mess.\n\nA Dremora mage runs the place. Clouds minds, breaks wills. I can't get my soldiers organized!

The Daedra called it the Tower of Lies. I scouted around, looking for stairs or even some sort of secret entrance, but no such luck.\n\nThe water looks pretty deep, though. Should be as safe as a walk in the park.

Lord Geirmund, great battlemage,
saved the Rift in Harald's age.

He slew the wicked Gauldur three,
and set their father's spirit free.
How would Palith get out then? I'm a better alchemist than a fighter, as you can see here.\n\nLeast I know how to make a man talk.

His tomb was built upon this lake,
and in his name this oath I make.

Should evil come, should night descend,
I swear the Rift I will defend.

My master hates when his servants fail him. It breaks his heart. But he will forgive if they can prove they still have something to offer.\n\nTake these three. Failures, every one. But my master offers a chance. He allows them to compete in my game.

The rules are simple. These three cannot participate in the game directly. They must use pawns to fight for them. In this case, the mages.\n\nIf a chosen champion falls, so too falls the corresponding leader. And redemption slips from their grasp.

Do you want that information in the hands of the Pact? No? I didn't think so.\n\nI managed to hide one of their uniforms in my cot. Grab it. Then we can slip past the soldiers and retrieve the information. Simple!
Arrest me? That beef-witted bastard! To think, I even cooked that man breakfast!\n\nWhat in Oblivion's gotten into him? First he arrests a Knight of the Flame, and now me?
Of course you do. Just make it quick.

We tried, but … well, this place is strange. Most of us just gave up, lost our will to resist. It doesn't affect everyone the same way, but it does make it hard to organize.  \n\nMaybe if you shake things up a bit we can snap out of this. Maybe.
Oh my poor little Pascal. What a mess you've made ….\n\nOne thing's for sure—we need to put an end to all these wicked accusations he's been making.

What do I look like? The social committee?\n\nThere's a bunch of prisoners down here, from all over the place. There's even a Dremora. Probably pissed off Molag Bal. But I don't really know and I don't really care.
She's an interesting one. Not bad to look at, as far as evil creatures from Oblivion go, but she has a mean streak.\n\nI'd be careful around her, if I were you.

You get to compete as well. Join a team and lead it to victory! Do this and you can claim the prize that has thus far been unattainable—freedom from my game!\n\nAnd I'll even sweeten the deal. Win, and you can take one of the mages with you.
Father. Here? Oh. So he's waiting outside the cave, then?
Right. Right. On the road. Um, would you mind if I hang back a few after we get out of here? \n\nYou should go ahead. Tell him how helpful I was. Before I walk up.

That's my thought! I'll provide whatever help I can from in here. I can tell you this: one of the other scholars, she called this place the Library of Dusk. Couldn't wait to start exploring.\n\nPlease hurry. Whatever the Daedra want, it can't be good.
Then choose your side and stop boring me with your indecision.
I'm uncertain. <<1>> brought my unit to <<2>> as part of our final training. But when we arrived, the city was under pirate attack.\n\nWe worked with the fisher-folk to help the citizens escape.
The Jackdaws, a pirate band that raids throughout the Long Coast.\n\nBut how could one pirate ship do so much damage? They shouldn't have taken the city at all, let alone as quickly as they did.

The Speaker for the Mane. He brought my people into the Dominion.\n\nI'm lucky to serve in his private guard. He sought to introduce us to other lands and people of the Dominion. I do not think he meant our first journey to be this exciting.
The fisher-folk? They were away from the port during the attack. The rest are refugees from <<1>>, mostly guards and merchants who escaped the city.

The Speaker hoped to locate <<1>>, but we could find no sign of her garrison. He feels the city's defense is our responsibility.\n\nBut there are few of us. Please, find <<2>>. Help take <<3>> back from the pirates.

This one … I, I do not know, not exactly. I only know what I must protect.\n\nBut <<1>> spoke with some refugees before he left. The merchant <<2>>, and <<3>>, who leads the fisher-folk. Perhaps they would know.

Really? Most mortals look alike to me. Plus, there's that smell. The odor of warm blood and quiet desperation. Mildly unpleasant, if you don't mind me saying so.\n\nAh, wait a moment … I do remember you.
I assure you, contrary to the way this looks, imprisonment is not my usual situation.\n\nBut before you get any ideas in that mortal little head of yours, I do not need your help this time.

Indeed. All kinds of rumors. 

Spies at court. An attempt on the Duchess's life. An army of Redguards with orders to storm the castle. 

Sir Hughes, the head of the Knights of the Flame, sent me here to make sure the village remains secure.
He was wading through the swamp with a handful of soldiers. They looked greener than the water.\n\nBut good luck to the Cat Lord, I say.

To the other end of the marsh. I've only seen the place from the <<1>> docks. Never thought I'd wade through it.\n\nIf you're headed after the Cat Lord, cross the marsh and make for the walls. I'd wager he's by the gate.

Never seen it before this evening. I've sent apprentices there for alchemical supplies. Had I known it was crawling with hoarvor, I would've increased their stipends.\n\nBut not by much. You have to keep them in line.

One moment I was nearly asleep, and the next I heard yelling. I looked outside and saw raiders with torches, so I leapt out the window and ran.\n\nThat's right. Completely nude, all the way here. The fisher-folk loaned me some clothes. Good of them.

He passed through on the way to <<1>>. Seemed more concerned with retaking the city than rescuing its people.\n\nThat's unkind. Some of my fisher-folk tried to sneak back inside, to bring family and friends. Too few have returned.

He gave a big speech about throwing the pirates back into the sea. Almost believed he could do it, with his handful of soldiers.\n\nCross the marsh and head for <<1>>'s outer ward. You'll find signs of the Cat Lord, I'm sure of it.
Lots of nasty critters, but some good fishing on the sea-side. We usually head there in pairs. One to fish, one to watch for hoarvor.\n\nDon't let your guard down.
We were in our camp, bedding down for the night. Saw a big ship sail right up. No challenge from the dockmaster. \n\nI took a boat out, paddled carefully. Then I saw Jackdaws pouring onto the docks.
Curse? No, no. My bloodkin are loyal to the last, but at times they're thicker than troll dung.\n\nIt's clearly poison, though how it affected so many is indeed curious. Why do you ask?

Sharp clawed, that one. It's why I left her in charge.\n\nThis has been enlightening training cruise for my soldiers. I wanted to show them life outside of Elsweyr, for them to see what it means to be a Dominion citizen! I never expected this.

Then here, take this list. Everyone who fell ill had three similarities. They ate food cooked in the same pot, drank water from the same well, and wore clothes washed in the same stream.\n\nBring a sample from each. We'll find the source of the poison.
Be my guest. Just don't expect any help from the guard. \n\nThe slavers are like rats—quick to scurry back into a hole—but they fight nasty when they're cornered.
There's no time. I've already had years of my life stolen from me! Please, just give me my belongings.
Sheor's teeth, she's coming!\n\nKeep those blasted trinkets. I have to get out of here before she catches me!
A question for another time.\n\nRight now, we need to deal with these pirates—Jackdaws, they call themselves. We spotted a few giving orders to the others. These Jackdaw lieutenants are the key.

We must know why have the Jackdaws lingered in <<1>>. What do they plan for its citizens?\n\nTake my notebook and find the Jackdaw lieutenants. Make note of anything they say which gives us a clearer understanding.
Yes, they're her property. And so am I, according to Vvardenfell law. Why should I honor the laws of slavers?\n\nYou're working for her, aren't you? I can't believe I trusted you!
You're all the same! Savages, all of you! \n\nI should have known better than to trust a member of the Pact. I'll never make that mistake again!
