I meant it quite literally. She's my property, a slave fairly traded from High Rock. \n\nIs that my locket? Did she run off with that too?
What? But you're one of the Pact! I thought you were all the same!\n\nYou'll let me go free, then? What about <<1>>?
I'll try to retrace my steps. It's so easy to get turned around in this place!
Good. This should only take a few moments.
My mother's blade! I thought I'd never see it again. I owe you more than you know, stranger.\n\nCome along, <<1>>. Thank your gods I'm in a forgiving mood.
I don't have much to offer in the way of a reward. My family has suffered in recent years. What you see before you is everything I own.
She has a good life. She's well looked after. You know these Bretons, they're such children.\n\nSurely you have no objections. The Bretons are not our allies. I'm well within my rights.

There was a drought and my family's crops failed. There were too many mouths to feed. \n\nSome Dark Elf traders arrived in port. I didn't even know what was happening until I saw my father walk off the boat. I was only fifteen.
You do that. \n\nSoon as we can ensure the town's in no immediate danger, we can talk about releasing your friend from the stocks.
Really? What are the Jackdaws planning?
Good! If you can enter the fort and open the gate, I can bring reinforcements to you.\n\nWhere is <<1>>? I must tell him of this plan!
Then we both must hurry.\n\nKeep your wits about you, friend. We'll meet inside the fort and stop these pirates from whatever dark magics they plan.
Broken arm, it's nothing.\n\nStand with us. Drive these bandits into the mud!

Skordo? He could be one of Arakh's assassins! You could be one of her spies! Never trust an Orc. Or a spy! \n\nBlessed Leki … I just don't know who or what to believe anymore. This place is getting to me. To all of us.

That's what any competent spy would say. Wouldn't hurt to prove you're not an illusion. Or a spy. \n\nTell you what. My sword is back there, with the ogrims that attacked us. You get my sword for me and we'll talk. Meet me near Arakh's camp.

Actually, I'd prefer you didn't. 

I appreciated your objectivity at first, but I must admit, I am beginning to question your intentions.

I'd prefer if you simply left town.

Yes. Sabyssa the blacksmith too. And I don't care how it sounds. 

Defending the village is the highest priority, and we need weapons for that. Sabyssa is refusing to supply us. 

She's leaving me no option but to have her arrested!

Because we made a stupid deal a long, long time ago. We became the guardians of this forest in exchange for power and immortality. But look at the cost!\n\nNow the Shadow Walkers hunt anyone who dare sets foot in these woods.

You need to collect the bark of a spriggan. The bark's magic allows the creatures to—how should I put this—feel their way through the dark woods. \n\nInfuse the bark with the wisps of light and you should be able to spot the runners.

There might still be a way to save the other soldier, the Khajiit. But you need to trust me.\n\nI won't oppose my clan directly. They're my family. But I can help you find your friend. I just want to make sure no one else gets hurt.

The pirate leader intends to fill <<1>>'s streets with undead slaves, but there's still time to stop them.\n\nThey're coming from the Fighters Guild. I need someone I can trust to get inside and disrupt their foul rituals. Can I count on you once more?

We were friends for years, and then one night … well, I guess you don't need the details.

For a month or two, I thought we had something. Then he just broke it off—wouldn't even let me in his house to talk.

He acted like I had betrayed him.

Good idea. Perhaps there's some indication of why Pascal's behaving this way.\n\nHe's just … not himself. I'll talk to some of the other townspeople. I bet some of them have noticed his behavior as well.

He did? He was having trouble sleeping ….

You know I saw one of those weird cult members leaving his house. The Supernal Dreamers. 

You don't think that has anything to do with this?

Don't know much about them really. I think they're dedicated to some Daedric Prince? They're crazy people.

Someone saw a group of them in the hills to the north, and then there was that one who visited the constable.

That's really all I know.
By Alkosh's scaly nethers, I knew you'd come through!\n\nNow, the pirates are likely to have the Fighters Guild heavily guarded and locked down.

My soldiers are loyal, but if I'm not beside them they'll fight with half a heart.\n\nAnd this way, we keep the pirates' focus on the Speaker for the Mane's flashing weapons and luxurious hair. Meanwhile, you can gut them when they aren't looking.

Because I don't completely trust myself. While I have avoided the illusions that trapped the others, I can still feel the pull of the Daedric spell.\n\nFind the power source and meet me at our camp outside the ruins. And take this token, just in case.
Yes, he convinced me there was never a curse.\n\nKnow that while <<1>> remains ill, I speak on his behalf. I'm his hearth-wife, and I say the poisoner must be brought to justice.
Speak with the unafflicted. Find out where they were the night before the sickness began. Return to me with their tales, and we can find the lies within them.

Raz may have oversimplified. These Altmer, the ones who wear the veil. They do not see themselves as racists. They see themselves as members of a far superior race. The rest of us just need some … help.
This one is proud to work for Her Majesty. We are called the Eyes of the Queen. We are a select group, the best. \n\nWe are some of the few that Ayrenn can trust, these days.

Her Majesty trusts you. And you were of great help in Vulkhel Guard. Why would this one not trust a new, fresh face? \n\nRaz would never watch you with careful eyes, ready for the first sign of betrayal. Never!
"Auridon for the Altmer." Cats like this one out, shortie Elves out. Nothing but tall folk, fair skin, and pointy ears as far as the eye can see.\n\nBoring, yes?
Strange, isn't it? Well, first of all, we perform a lot of charitable works and otherwise keep a very low profile.

Second—and more important—we are here on the sufferance of the authorities in Wayrest because we're dedicated opponents of the Supernal Dreamers. \n\nVaermina's perverted cult has been a curse on High Rock for generations.
You mean the curse? Sure, I'll help any way I can. It's what I do.\n\nMost of our warriors are sick in their beds, or barely able to hold an axe. More bandits for me!
Wonderful. Good luck to you.\n\nOh, you want to question me? A bit pedantic, but I appreciate a thorough approach. Ask what you will.
Once the chief is back on his feet, I'll be the new forge-wife. Then we'll see who gives the orders.\n\nNot that you care. Go ahead. Ask me anything.
It's shameful for the raiders to do such a thing. They must have dropped the poison in the well during one of their attacks.
I wish we were back in the mines, even with all those spiders. At least <<1>> is safe in the longhouse.
Exactly. So you see how important it is to recover the Dream Shard. \n\nThe safety of the realm is at stake.

We use them to protect ourselves from nightmare attacks by our enemies, the Supernal Dreamers. Since we don't dream, we're not vulnerable to dream magic. \n\nWe also send them to the king and his counselors … another reason we're tolerated here.

Indeed. As I said, even the town guards knew something was amiss. I told them to be ready. I suppose Pascal will probably have to be restrained.\n\nOh, well, best thing for unpleasant work is just to get it over with. Let's go.
They won't tell me. That means it's bad, isn't it? I'm going to die.
Truly? Your words bring me hope.\n\n<<1>> isn't here, is he?
I see. Strange, I thought I would fear this moment, but instead I'm filled with pride that I could fight beside the Speaker for the Mane. And beside you.\n\n<<1>> isn't around, is he?
If I die from wounds justly earned, I'll greet my ancestors with honor. Tell the Speaker it was an honor to serve him.
No!\n\nHe rallies the people of <<1>> against the pirates. Please, do not distract him with my fate.
I can use <<1>>'s own belongings to buy my freedom. Freedom … I can hardly believe it!\n\nFarewell, my friend. I hope we see each other again.
How do I know you aren't just a distraction so Eilram can slip behind me and stab me in the back?\n\nWait. This is my helm. I'm so confused … but Eilram did kill my friend, Ifriz.

Do either of us have any other options?\n\nIfriz created the barrier that blocks the way out of this prison. Eliminate Ifriz and the barrier collapses. But you must find Ifriz if you are going to kill him.
Ah, little mortal. I have already provided more help than you deserve. The rest, as they say, is up to you.
I'll take those trinkets, if you please. You've robbed me enough for one day.\n\nI thank the Three my father didn't live to see this. You should thank them as well.
When the roots are fouled, there's only one thing left to do—rip them out of the ground.
Raz recruited her into the Eyes. Vouched for her to the Queen, and trained her as best he could. Now this one has to tell her parents. Another sad tale of the Queen's Eyes.
Just thought better of her. This one knows she and the Queen used to correspond regularly. To think she's fallen in with the Heritance.  \n\nShows even good people can do stupid things.

You have, perhaps, something better to do? Look, we are the Queen's Eyes. We do the tasks that must be done, even if it means getting hit on the head. Killing those who do not deserve it.\n\nRiding a guar naked through an Argonian temple.
Raz only shares that story with veteran field agents. Perhaps another day.
What? This one would never note that this is the second time he is saving you. From jail. In less than a month. \n\nNot out loud, anyway.
What do you think Raz did while you searched the town? He watched, observed, calculated.\n\nRaz has very good eyes, you see.
Razum-dar unlocks the door. You go find Condalin. This one finds Malanie. \n\nJust be careful.

Look, if I wanted to kill everyone, I'd have done it right the first time.\n\nThat's what troubles me. If the poison was meant to kill, there would have been more venom. Why would the poisoner show restraint?
Everything was quiet when we arrived, but bones and other refuse littered the halls. With the wards broken, it wouldn't surprise me if more than books are moving about.

The curse couldn't poison me. Nothing can! When I find a new bug or beast, I don't just kill it, I eat it to gain its strength!\n\nSometimes you, uh, pay for it, but you've never truly conquered something until you've buried it in the ground.
Nothing! I'm a horrible liar. Everybody knows it.\n\nLook, the chief got sick. We have a history, and I don't want <<1>> to think I poisoned him, all right? That'd be terrible.
Seems a week doesn't pass without a spider bite in the mines. Comes with the job. I suppose old bites and dizzy spells kept me safe from the poison.\n\nI don't know what else to say.

Is it that obvious? I mean, no! Nothing like that!\n\nThe chief and I disagreed over the mine's value, but we resolved things. We don't see eye-to-eye on trade matters, but I'm no traitor to the stronghold. And I'd never do anything to hurt <<1>>.
I apologize. I was just grateful for the short amount of silence I had while they were out gallivanting around the ruins.\n\nBut, on a more serious note, their bumbling may have uncovered something.

Well, it's not much to go on, but we were sent here to find a relic. Something called the Nephrite Glyph. It's written about in many texts, but its whereabouts have always been … vague.\n\nBut now we know - it was stolen.

If I'd wanted to sabotage the stronghold, I could have the walls topple, or make shoddy blades that crumble in our warriors' hands. Yet the walls stand fast and our weapons strike true.\n\nAny other insults you care to toss at me? I have metal to work.

Shored up defenses, repaired weapons and armor for the few warriors left standing. Haven't you heard the ring of my hammer? Used it on a few bandits, too.\n\nBandit helmets can't take three hits! Clang, clang, crunch. Shoddy workmanship.
Now that I think about it, I checked the weapons the day before. The day everyone got sick, I worked here, in the forge.
None of my bloodkin died from the poison. It only made people sick, just as <<1>> showed me.\n\nHis brother isn't fit to rule a privy, let alone our tribe.
Fine. I'm the one who poisoned the stronghold.\n\nBut what I did was for the good of my people.
I'm sure she does.\n\nDon't believe everything she's told you. <<1>> is no monster, and <<2>> would be nothing without his wives.
So? I needed some ore. Three spiders came from nowhere and I had to defend myself.\n\nI must have lost it in my rush to escape. It's a wonder I made it out of there alive.

Sorry to disappoint, but I don't plan to walk into my death. There is more to the brothers' story than you've been told. \n\nPlease, don't rush into anything. Seek out <<1>> and hear his side of the story before deciding what you believe.
Gargak is the rightful Chief of this stronghold! His brother is half the man and an utter fool. He won the trial by fighting dirty. I am simply trying to help set things right.
<The cat appears ready to run. She looks at you as if to insist that you follow her.>
Good, good! Time to pack! On my way, yes?\n\nWhat? You expect me to show you now?
Not exactly. <<1>> did say "maybe," yes? No?\n\nSuch misunderstanding over a little knick-knack. Just a rock! How could I know what it did? Most of what she gave me was harmless!
Would you believe … nobody?\n\nNo one with a body, anyway. And really, if you don't have a body, well, who is to say, yes?

In the ruins. Belarata. There is a ghost, yes? She thinks … aheh. She thinks I am her lover! So she gives me things. Clothing, trinkets, things that belonged to him.\n\nMost are harmless! Old, but dangerous? Never! Well, mostly.

Never drink from an unmarked bottle that's been locked away since the First Era with a Daedric guardian stewing in the contents.\n\n"But I'm <<1>>," he said, "and all my drinkings are mighty!" I tried to warn the man. I do hope his beard grew back.
Fine, fine. <<1>> will show you. Come, follow me.

Exactly what it looks like. Just because Narsis doesn't have giant stone walls doesn't mean we can't lock the place down.\n\nWe have orders to make sure no one gets in or out. Except you. Still not sure how you pulled that off.

Damn. That's what I was afraid of. The book mentions her specifically, some sort of "caretaker."\n\nHer specialty was … well, there's no easy way around it. She controlled the minds of others. It seems even the Ayleids feared her.
Hmm. I was hoping for more of a challenge. Since you don't look so tough, I'll let you have the first strike.

<That's it. I'm done. Haven's just too hot for me. If you want to try to keep up your back-alley trade, you'll have to do it alone …. and that includes creating the mixture.\n\nYou remember how to do it, right? If you don't, here's a clue.>

<It's all in the portions: Sweet, sticky moon sugar cane. Foul, noxious, bitter mangrove juice. Viscous hist sap. Hope that's descriptive enough. If it's not, you'll need all new ingredients!\n\nMake your mixture, then go to the beach.>
<The bookcase is protected by an ancient grate, yet there seem to be books missing from its shelves.>
<A faint series of clicks issues from within the bookcase.>

…Then you need to find the Midnight Union. True. But not yet.\n\nThe entire purpose of the attack on the abbey was to acquire the Dream Shard—and its purpose is as a defense against the Supernal Dreamers.

Do you know the Code of Mauloch? It's a simple code, but it's the one I live by.\n\n"Don't steal" … so I aim to conquer. "Don't kill your kin" … and none have died in my attacks. "Don't attack without cause" … but I have more than enough cause.

No. I'm sorry. We just can't take that risk. I dreamed about all of this, you see. \n\nThe slavers, the ship, the knight—they were all working together. Even the blacksmith, and I've known her for years.

When my father passed, I was to become chief by right.\n\nBut then my little brother challenged me for leadership of the stronghold. Two schemers put him up to it, as long as he'd make them hunt-wife and forge-wife. They knew I had no respect for them.

Not by my brother's skill. His future forge-wife insisted we use matched weapons.\n\nAs we fought, I grew light-headed. My palms burned and I could barely keep a grip. But I fought on and was about to strike my brother down … when my sword shattered.
They sent an assassin. You only know what lies they've told you. I should be the one to lead, not my suckling brother.

No other explanation. The hunt-wife poisoned the hilt, and the forge-wife delivered a blade that shattered in its first melee. My brother must have known.\n\nHeard they died last month, some sort of fire. A shame they won't see me take my revenge.

Well, they're certainly not the altruistic organization they pretend to be. It's definitely a militaristic cult, but who controls them is still unclear. I'm sure they're connected to this Vox mentioned in the notes you discovered.
No idea. We're still working on that.
I don't see how. It's my birthright to rule, and my brother stands in the way.

A played out Imperial mine, I'd heard. And it's infested with trolls. Clearing them out will be no easy task.\n\nHmm. I suppose if there's ore in the mine, I could leave my brother to rot in the stronghold. But I'd need proof.
Silen? She always lets her political worries get in the way. But very well. Ask your questions. Just don't take too long.
I'm not entirely sure. We received a retinue of penitents—led by none other than High Kinlady Estre herself. I was walking between the shrines, talking to Monastic Nenaron, when the screaming began.
I am an Aldarch. And an old one, at that. I may not be much good in a fight. But the touch of a Daedric lord? Pah.\n\nNo part of my soul wants to traffic with the likes of them.
Mine was a nightmare of betrayal, and they are among my betrayers. Count Hosni was betrothed to our Sister Safia before he met Lady Adima. \n\nAnd there is another reason.
It's an open secret that Count Hosni commands the Midnight Union. We thought him our friend.

Sometimes in pairs. They slam shut on your ear tips, then flutter off. It seems half the library has tormented us since we tripped the wards.\n\nI've been trying to settle things down, but it's slow going without my assistants.
She—she what? If she's capable of that, this corruption could be her doing. Mara's Heart!
I tried to help those I could, but the penitents went mad with fear. Daedra boiled up from the central shrine, burning and killing as they went. \n\nThe "Prince" behind this is a fiend.
I tried to help those I could, but the penitents went mad with fear. Daedra boiled up from the central shrine, burning and killing as they went. \n\nThe "Prince" behind this is a fiend.
Oh, and it speaks!\n\nI just finished a <<1>>. Some of my finest work, between you and me. Though you couldn't possibly appreciate the detail.
Why, you need to entertain me.\n\nThere are a variety of chests throughout the gardens. I placed your friend's soul in one of them. See if you find it before my posing retinue tears you to pieces!

The Steel Mask in trouble? I don't know if I should trust you, but I know trouble for the Mask could put us all in danger.\n\nFarona Telvanni. That's the Steel Mask's real name. She meets clients in the gardens outside the city.

Willing to prove your worth? That's different.\n\nHouse Dres stole a shipment of weapons sent to me by the Steel Mask. I'm sure they've armed their guards with my goods! Retrieve the weapons from their farm outside of the city and then we'll talk.
If I had to guess? The stench in the air. The pain of the afflicted. Dagon. Mehrunes Dagon. \n\nIt's his razor that cuts across my heart, I fear. May he drown in the Font of Harmony. Yech.

I'm ashamed to say I left Nenaron inside. I dropped a quick rune of protection on the ground for him. Mara knows if he's still alive.\n\nI tried to get him moving, but he kept raving about some relics. Silly, stupid mer.
Thank you. The way they treated these weapons is appalling. House Dres didn't deserve to wield them.\n\nThe Steel Mask is really Farona Telvanni. She meets clients in the gardens outside of town.
We are the Saxhleel. It's what we call ourselves in our native Jel tongue. Only the smoothskins call us Argonians.\n\nWe lived here peacefully, tending our fields. Until the pirates set upon us.
Stars yes, a ward. To keep the corrupted contained. It's taking a lot out of me, to be honest with you.\n\nBut Mara keeps and preserves me. As she always has. I'll be fine.
Oh! Hopper? No, no. I'm the only one that can race Hopper. He's my little amphibian baby.
Ah! Fine, fine! Just take care of him. \n\nI'll pick him up out of the lane after the race.
You? Hhmph. Snooks is above such base displays. He is a far superior creature.
A compelling argument. Very well. Run him against these reprobates. I'll take him from the lane when you're done.
Bloodthirster desires victory! She slakes her lust on glory! \n\nShe's like me, though. She only works for coin!
Good luck, Bloodthirster. Don't embarrass me!\n\nYou! I'll pick up my frog from the lane when you're done. Go!

I don't know for sure, but I overheard something about the slavers taking over a village up the beach. I'm betting they took the rest of the crew there.\n\nIf there's a silver lining to that cloud, it's that they're out of Captain Angarthal's reach.

Never met the man myself, but his name's well-known in these waters.\n\nAngarthal's notorious for terrorizing the Abecean Sea, enslaving the Altmer. Guess he joined up with this outfit after the Ebonheart Pact was formed.

I'm certain solutions will present themselves. There's no telling what this corruption has done to the holy sites. \n\nThe Divines will want you to re-sanctify their spaces, certainly. They're watching, always.
<This bag is full of a mixture of bugs and strange gel.>
<The frog looks hungry.>
<The frog looks full.>
<You let the frog nibble at some chow.>
Follow me, my young friend. And find out.
No, that was the Aldarch's doing. She didn't want me to die. Or become co-opted, like the others. Such a kind lady. \n\nHrm. If a little brusque with me.
Oh, no. No, no, no. These relics, they're sensitive. Like me. Even waiting for the corruption here to drain away could spoil them.\n\nCan't let the treasures of the Divines go to rot.
I told you we'd be right behind you. I'm truly beginning to understand what Naryu sees in you. You certainly know how to get things done.
Oh, she's out and about. Like you, she's out doing what she does best. Now, talk to the captain and let's get on with things.

The Dunmer crept up from the south and attacked in the dark. They killed the watch guard, but not before he sounded the alarm.\n\nWe reacted fast. I had … an uneasy feeling, so we were on alert. Lost a few good men, but the Dunmer lost more.

It's possible,  but we cornered most of the cowards and cut them down.

The last dozen or so barricaded themselves in the warehouse. Current plan is to just starve them out. 

If your messenger's alive though, they've got him in there.
I'm going to scout around and figure out our next move. Meet me at the huge gates after you've set the supply shacks on fire.
She—she what? If she's capable of that, this corruption is no doubt her doing. Mara's Heart! That we would live to see such things.
She what? No doubt she's behind this then. Some kind of ploy or distraction.\n\nMara's Heart! That we could live to see such times.
A traitor and a cultist both? She wasn't content to be one form of harpy, had to double up. Disgusting.\n\nNo doubt this is some kind of ploy on her part, then. Bah!
No! Truly? Thrice-be-damned is she.\n\nIf she's capable of that kind of treachery, perhaps she had a hand in what's happening here.
Damn. Then no doubt she's behind this assault! Sickening, that she had thrown her power around in this way.\n\nI damn her three and five times. Power-mad harpy.

Thanks for rubbing it in. So the plan wasn't going perfectly … but I was adapting.\n\nI didn't hear where their base of operations is, but I did see plans for some attack floating around the camp. I had hoped to take those back to Deputy Luric.

You did? Well, then I guess we can consider this operation a success!

If you haven't already, we just need to get those plans to Deputy Luric in the village.

I guess I should go reassure my mother.
Thanks. You were right, by the way. Qor overheard the High Kinlady talking to these Daedra by magical sending.\n\nShe's behind this whole thing.
Thanks. You were right, by the way. Qor overheard the Veiled Queen talking to these Daedra by magical sending.\n\nShe's behind this whole thing!

Good. When we get out of here … we have bigger troubles. Qor says the Veiled Queen is behind this whole thing!\n\nQor managed to overhear this Veiled Queen speaking magically with the Daedra. She's a thrice-damned cultist!
Just repeating what Qor said. We're pretty removed out here. Maybe this is news on every streetcorner in Skywatch and we just don't know about it.\n\nIf it's true, we're in trouble.

<The body has several obvious wounds. It's difficult to tell which caused the fatal blow, but it looks like there was more than a single assailant. Lying in the dirt is a badge bearing the name "Helonel.">
Karulae, their rapid action planner. Calanye, their woman on the inside of the Fighters Guild. \n\nHelonel, racial purity advisor. Behind several documented attacks on Bosmer and Khajiit.

Aranias. Strange one. Haven't heard her name linked to any particular crime. Rumor is that she's a personal friend of Estre's.\n\nMost likely a highly placed agent, but no idea about her area of expertise.
Good. Meantime, I'm going to get Qor here back to the manor. Meet us there.
Tanion found him praying. Shouted at him, and threw him in the cave. Something about making him "an example to his mongrel race." \n\nThese are the people teaching us here, damn it!
Saltspray Cave. Pretty little hole in the ground behind the college. They use it as a corrective measure when we step out of line.

The Thalmor's the ruling party in the Dominion. It's made up of High Elf canonreeves, Wood Elf treethanes, and a handful of Khajiiti chieftains.\n\nTake a wild guess what's the strongest flavor in that particular stewpot?

I'll tell you a little story. Friend of mine, Brinthir? \n\nA few weeks ago it was his birthday. Back in Grahtwood he and his parents used to do this little ceremony honoring the Green. Simple thing, just a few words.
Do I look like a Treethane? Maybe they don't know what goes on here, I don't know.
I'm thinking on that myself. The arrangement of this ritual altar is not one I am familiar with. \n\nBut there are not many benevolent spells one can cast using a necropolis like this, yes?
Bakkhara is thinking! Wait … do you feel that?

Thank the stars! You have to get me out of here!\n\nAhem. It seems I set off an ancient trap. But I think I've determined how those strange lights channel their energy, and how to turn it against them.

Once trapped, strange creatures covered in eyes and tentacles descended from above. They reinforced the sconces with foul magic from their largest eyes.\n\nThose eyes are key. Extract one and use it to refocus the lights! It should break the binding.

I was certain it was a good theory. All part of the scholarly process, my friend! \n\nBut never mind that, I should thank you for your timely rescue! I'll head back to our camp. I cannot wait to tell <<1>> what happened here.
<The bookcase shudders a bit as you push the book into place.>

Well, the last thing I want is for you to go running in there unprepared. Might end up getting jumped by Ma'jhad Kha and get locked up with everyone else.\n\nThe main thing is just to light the fires though. Is that what you wanted to ask about?
Improvise. Pull a burning log from their campfire.\n\nThen light 'em up—the tents, and all those stolen goods out there on the dock. Hopefully, that'll distract Ma'jhad Kha.

You're not thinking about taking him on, are you?

That's one crazy Khajiit. He was actually a slave himself but turned on his masters and took over. Killed his competition and became some kind of slaver king.

Trust me. Light the fire. Distract him.
<<1>> suggested <<2>> was under her control. A ruse, and one I should have seen!\n\nBut if <<3>> has <<Ac:4>>, she can use it to restore her spirit to her body. We have to get it back!

Through the door. We've never been able to open it, and I don't know where it leads.\n\nQuickly, after her! I'll attempt to restore the wards here, should you fail. We can't allow a Daedra to wreak havoc with <<Ac:1>>!
<<1>> keeps to itself. Because of this, they think we'd make perfect slaves.

So, you've met the Argonians of Silent Mire. Peaceful, meditative, calm, accepting. Well, not me!\n\nOur home was attacked, my friends killed. Of course I'm angry! Vengeance will make me feel better, so pile those cat corpses high!
The new gear from the Baandari, yes. She is kind, Baham. Always making sure we are taken care of.
Thalorel and Brinthir are recovering in their dorms. Today was a bad day, for all of us. Dark Moon, yes? \n\nGood luck.

Mature kwama are very sensitive to changes in their environment. They have especially developed sense of smell. Scribs haven't grown enough to be bothered by the fumes.  \n\nAnd fortunately, this section of the mine isn't too contaminated.
Yes. Please. And then go find my dad! I'll meet you outside!

I've dealt with sickness, broken bones, and plague. This is poison, I have no doubt. Symptoms are very similar to bites from the spiders in our tin mine.\n\nI'm thankful none have died, but it's damn inconvenient. The bandit attacks are relentless.

and in his name this oath I make.

Should evil come, should night descend,
I swear the Rift I will defend.

Lord Geirmund, great battlemage,
saved the Rift in Harald's age.

I won't know anything for certain until I get those samples.

My neighbor? Are you saying what I think you're saying? I mean, Ingride's nice, but she's ….\n\nWell, I always did think she was rather pretty, and she is a widow. I think maybe I'll just have to pay her a visit. Thanks for the suggestion.

Left the juices intact as well! You've the mind of an alchemist, I can tell.\n\nIt's the stomach juices! Brings out the properties of the fronds. Crocodiles aren't so different from wamasu, but wamasu eat these and crocodiles do not. Therefore ….
<Someone clearly ransacked this cart. Upon closer examination, you spot a small piece of ragged red cloth caught under a loose nail.>
<You notice a torn red shirt buried in the trash pile.>

Queen Ayrenn has come to our town, as part of her tour. While she's here, the rumor is that she's going to bestow a great honor upon Estre. \n\nEstre's already the Canonreeve of Skywatch. Be interesting to see what's next!

The Sload released a disease, the Thrassian plague, on an unsuspecting Tamriel. A catastrophe late in the First Era, if I remember my history correctly. They infected sea beasts and sent them to run ashore all along the coasts.
A few years. But we've never forgotten. It took the All Flags Navy to free us, with aid from a resistance in the streets.\n\nNever again!
After the Sload released the Thrassian plague, they capitalized on the chaos it caused. They moved in on cities along the coasts, sacked them for goods and enslaved the folk that lived there.

Not sure what else there is to say. Mass death, military gambits, and the poor Khajiit lost more than half of their people.\n\nWe showed them, though. The All Flags Navy took the fight to their homeland, and slaughtered them. Nasty.

The Abbey is home to the Spirit Wardens, devoted to Azura, Queen of Dawn and Dusk.\n\nYes, we are a cult, but King Emeric makes allowances because Azura is benevolent. Vaermina is not—as her intentions with Ingride Vanne make clear.

Vaermina is the most horrid of Daedric Princes. Dreams and nightmares are her dark domain. \n\nWhatever her agenda on our plane may be—you can trust it is not good. The Supernal Dreamers intentions with Ingride Vanne make that clear.

It will not be easy, and you will need to move quickly, but it can be done.\n\nYou will need to reverse the Daedric ritual, which will require gathering a few … somewhat grisly items. Then you must follow the directions exactly to break the spell.

The Supernal Dreamers have put her into an enchanted sleep, tied down in front of a portal—undoubtedly from Vaermina's dark domain. They will summon a Daedric spirit to inhabit Ingride's body.\n\nYou need to break the enchantment to free her.
To cement their relationship, the Queen plans to elevate Estre within the Thalmor. Everything must be perfect.

It is a pleasure working beside you, my friend. \n\nStart at the Barbed Hook tavern, down by the docks. Use the phrase, "The wine here is made with Alik'r grapes." Raz is certain that will get you somewhere.
You could ask my sister. She'd tell you. \n\nIf she wasn't dead.
The Midnight Union has taken some local folks captive. They hold their families hostage, then force the able-bodied to fight each other to the death in their arena. \n\nIt's just terrible.

I was taken captive. My friend Aara helped me escape. \n\nThey're holding my husband Thomin down in the old mine, to make him fight. But now that I'm free, he could be rescued. Please, you look like you can handle trouble. Could you …?
Hist amber? No, that's impossible! it must be a fake.\n\nGet that abomination away from me!
They're in the way. End the threat they represent to our cause.\n\nReturn with a blade and we'll move on to the next step.
I'm sure I don't know what you're talking about. I've been here forever, enjoying the drinks and the fire pit dancing.
You don't miss much do you, my friend? Now, go away and let a girl enjoy her sujamma in peace.
William a widower? I'm so sorry to hear that. Poor Rosalie. May the Eight bless her soul.\n\nAre you suggesting I … hmm. Maybe I will pay the Nurins a visit. I appreciate the suggestion.
Maybe. <<1>> hasn't been the same since he returned. He's normally so enthusiastic about his studies, but he's withdrawn into himself.\n\nIt's downright unsettling, watching him suffer like this.

I don't know. To tell you the truth, I'm not even that close to my aunt. My parents just sent us here to work the farm for a season.\n\nIf you want to search for my aunt, that would be great, but I just want to get my sister and go home.
I know. They're terrible, aren't they? That's another reason why I just want to go back to Camlorn. People are nicer there, I think.

Navisdyn was killed on the guild docks behind the hall. You may examine the scene of his death, but please respect his remains. \n\nMy mentor meant a lot to me. If you find anything pertinent, please bring it to me. He deserves justice.

I don't want to hear moaning. We've a long road to walk before we remove that heretic Ayrenn. \n\nThe Veiled Queen deserves only the best. So we only take the best.
You and everyone else in Morrowind! But I can't help you. Have a nice day.
Ah, I knew the old lizard was good for something!\n\nThe magic barrier, it's gone! And the hatch is unlocked! We can get inside. Hurry, before those pirates spot us.
He'll catch up. I'll leave the door open.\n\nCome on! Do you want to get caught?
Truly? You are certain? If you're mistaken, accusing her—

Oh, you're so young. You must not have children of your own. \n\nOlder parents eventually realize that you just can't afford to spend all your time worried about the kids and the grandkids. I have enough to worry about with Giraud.
They attacked a few merchants on the road. And they tried to murder the Thane!\n\nI'd sleep easier under the foot of a mammoth than in this town.
I live here and work at the inn. Until recently Nimalten was a quiet place. Seems like there aren't any quiet places left in the Rift.
Cowards, the lot of them. They ran south from the Reachmen, rather than holding their ground. Now they're robbing us!
<The statue bows, as if pleased.>
<The statue bows, as if pleased.>
<The statue bows, as if pleased.>
Not every day, no. But it's not unusual for us to zoom off to some distant location every few weeks or so.

It's a … sensitive matter. We've intercepted secret messages to King Fahara'jad from someone inside the castle who goes by the alias of "Almandine."\n\nMy hope is that a little research in the library might reveal where this term comes from.

Unfortunately, the duke requires that he personally approve all visitors to the library, and he can't know about this. \n\nThe library guard—Sir Gregory. Perhaps you can persuade him to look the other way, or failing that, to leave his post.

No … I couldn't ask her to work. She wouldn't like that. She might even leave me.\n\nNo. She spends most of her time in the market. Too much time if you ask me. I can't stand the way all those merchants look at her. The other knights too.
A protective barrier. With something inside? Aelif can sense a great power here.\n\nFormidable. But this one knows a spell to negate it.
Not without your assistance. Aelif will subdue the crystals. You must destroy them. \n\nYour window will be short. The spell is taxing, and Aelif can only maintain it for so long. Be quick.
Aelif will begin her spell. You run to each of the four crystals. The crystals empower the barrier.\n\nDestroy all four crystals, and the barrier will fall.
My friend, it's time to go. Quickly! Follow Speaks-With-Lights!\n\nShe can open the way out of this place.

Now you've got to return that totem to the Stonechewers. \n\nThe Goblin camp is to the the west, but I'm not sure where the totem belongs. If I were you I'd ask that crazy scholar who lives near the camp. Nellic Sterone—that's his name.
Of course. Aelif hopes you are ready this time. This is a difficult spell.
As Aelif begins to cast, move to a crystal. Destroy it. Move to the next crystal, destroy it. Move on. \n\nAvoid the barrier, and be fast on your feet.
I know, I know … you have a weapon and you're more powerful than a dozen House guards. I've met more than a few just like you since all this started.
Because Darima is the only one in the castle I can fully trust. \n\nI need her here, and I fear that if she leaves, they may not permit her to return.

Thank you. Things are truly desperate when a daughter of King Fahara'jad must rely on the generosity of a stranger, but I do believe in you.\n\nThe future of the Covenant—and my life—depends on you. Ruptga go with you, friend.
She is? Then she is in the castle? \n\nGo then—quickly! Tell Lakana so that she may be prepared for this wench-assassin! I cannot go in, so you must protect her!

She's thrice-blessed, she is. <<1>> commanded a unit in Glenumbra. Saw the hypocrisy of the Daggers firsthand.\n\nShe and her husband managed to flee to the wilds of Khefrem. Got us word through a Baandari peddler.
Think so. As far as you can trust any Orc. \n\nShe's loyal enough. Refused to leave her husband behind. No negotiation on that point.

Don't recognize my insignia, do you? We're with the Talons. The Queen has her Eyes, yes? The Battlereeve has his Talons.\n\nWe work with some of the other covert units. Provide strong arms where they're needed.

You've got it. Breath of Auri-El! A few times we were their only protection. Don't know if any of the Eyes are still up there with my squad.\n\nHope so. They're brave—when they're not hiding under a bush.
I'm just a line officer. Not worth a chase across the ocean. Morothmash, my husband, is who they're after. \n\nMoroth was an advisor to King Kurog gro-Orsinium. He wanted out, a real life.
I am gifted with a touch of the sight, child. I saw you coming. And I saw that I could provide for you a small gift.
It is fleeting, but precious: a new experience. For, after all, we are all new arrivals to the stage of history. \n\nTell me. What do you value most? Adventure? Knowledge? Or beauty?
Did Lakh tell you anything about my situation?
Kurog gro-Orsinium, trolls take him. Since the early days of the Covenant, I stood by his side. I was close as anyone outside of his clan could be.\n\nClose enough to see how tight the reins were.

High King Emeric, the trader king. The traitor king. Bastard's always hated the Orcs. Only offered us territory so our blades and strong backs would end their civil war.\n\nNow he sees Kurog as a favored dog sitting at the table, begging for scraps.

Simple choice. The Covenant sickens me and the Pact would never take me. Even in far-off Orsinium, we've heard of the Queen's bravery and strength of spirit. I can't wait to plead my case in front of her.

I, and a few other Eyes, were assigned to an expedition up north. We smuggled a pair of defectors out of Covenant lands, but the thrice-damned Daggers followed us.\n\nNow we're just trying to keep the body count to a minimum.
Can't say I'm much a fan of Argonians. I suppose I can't help but associate them with the Pact. \n\nThe Guild walks a neutral line, though, so it's not fair to hold that against her.
Not much to think about, I barely know her. \n\nYou can't imagine my shock when I heard she was chosen as acting master general. And I'm not the only one.

Suspicious. Jofnir's Master General for a reason. He can handle his own. He doesn't just disappear.\n\nI think something's happened to him. This just isn't right. What's even worse is Colors wants to focus on these Dark Anchors. What about Jofnir?
I can't say if she's the best, but I do like the direction she's going in. \n\nThese anchors. Something has to be done. The Fighters Guild is the right choice to undertake them.
Fair? Perhaps. I was a bit put off when I heard we're taking on these Dark Anchors as a Guild. But Colors hasn't said we can't take on other contracts on the side, so I suppose that's fair enough.
Of course. Jofnir's a great leader. He's fair, and allows the Guild to operate as it always has. \n\nSees-All-Colors seems to have her own agenda. But what that is? I can't be certain.
There's been speculation, but Colors should be heading up an investigation herself! How do you let something like this just fall to the wayside? \n\nIt makes no sense.
Times have been hard, but the Three will see me through. Can you help me today?
The blessings of Almalexia will be visited upon you thrice-fold for your generosity.
I hope you meet someone more generous if you find yourself in a similar situation. Praise Vivec, anyway.

I hand it to you. Found it on a pirate's corpse and recognized the markings. The luck of Rajhin was with me!\n\nI'm sure the Fighters Guild will approve of you smashing anything that doesn't belong. When you finish, inform <<1>> of your success!
Marauders. Attacked us on the road between here and the Gorge. They took everything we had. Everything!
What? Why would pirates do such a thing? We must get to the fort and stop them!\n\nBut if they hold the fort, they must have the gates locked. How could we get in?
Daggerfall Covenant, Maulborn, common thieves … they didn't exactly introduce themselves. I just hope one of those anchor things falls on their heads.
We were set upon by bandits on the road. But you don't want to hear about our problems. If you can spare a little gold, you can be on your way.
May your roots spread far and grow deep, kind friend.
I understand. And may all of your blue crawdads turn gray with scale-rot.
You must know of the glorious Nord Cultural Exchange! But our important work is delayed by … bureaucrats!
Your dumbness is charming, but while Rigurt waits by City Center, Axulfa has decided to see the sights of Dark Elf metropolis.
Shad Astula, the magic school. The boat to the Academy leaves from the dock here in Mournhold. It's a great honor to be accepted and I can't wait to begin.

Wonderful. When all the flying books fell, I knew it had left the ruins.\n\nI'll return it to the <<1>> Mages Guild, per our agreement with the king. We won't need to worry about Daedra finding it there.
The Red Rooks have taken over the town. Caught everyone by surprise. \n\nMe? I'm just minding my own business and hoping they just go away.
Yeah. And people still mostly leave me alone. Which is still fine by me.

I found this scrap of paper. Says there's one in the tavern … another in this old mage's house. They're both on the other side of town. \n\nThe third one … the Maormer's captain has the last one. It was in the canonreeve's manse.
Possibly. Looks like we must get to the heart of the matter and leave no corner unexplored to solve it.
There is an oasis near Bergama. Ogre's Bluff. Meet Aelif there, and we will journey to Ragnthar together.
I don't, but I'm willing to bet that someone in Bergama does. I'd ask around there if I were you.
I don't, but I'm willing to bet that someone in Bergama does. I'd ask around there if I were you.
I don't, but I'm willing to bet that someone in Bergama does. I'd ask around there if I were you.
Oh yes! They recently opened the Academy to all members of the Pact. As long as you have a talent for magic. And if they think you're leadership material.
Always two steps ahead, Herius is. That's what keeps us alive.
She's at the cordon on the other side of town. At the moment, our only goal is to hold the Maormer here. \n\nWithout reinforcements, we'll never throw these bastards off the coast.
What? The last I saw, she was carving her way through undead warriors. How bad is it?
Nonsense. I'll send for Mages Guild healers to treat her immediately.\n\nDon't you worry about <<1>>. She fought like she was born with six claws. There's no way she'll go without a fight.
Well, <<1>> has been working on a ward to use against them. He's just down the stairs, go ask him about it.
Splendid. Now, I just insert them into the rod like so. By the way, I hope you can destroy this mechanism if it attacks us.
Yes, I found a way to undo their twisted magics. Here, take these wards. Place one on the ground near a lurcher and it should unwind him. I have only five, so use them wisely.
Well, you just helped me avoid a vicious stabbing. We were a group of twenty this morning. No longer.\n\nI'll bet my dog of a husband set up this ambush.
That's ex-husband, actually. Bastard probably knew I was coming.\n\nWe were … developing competing studies on the Dwemer, and I found the location of this ruin, Volenfell, before he did.
Poisoned me, stole my journals and notes. Left me for dead.\n\nSo I came after him with a small army. Who knew he'd have one, too?
Only thing I can do is try to get my research back from him. This place houses the Guardian's Eye, an artifact I've hunted for months.\n\nWill you help me? It'll be worth your while.
I was, uh, preparing the bait. The beast won't come out of the water without this. At least that's what Mother said.
Now we lure out the monster and kill it. Easy, right? I sure hope this proves my courage to Mother.

Fantastic! A hall referenced as the "Guardian's Helm" should be your first stop, accessible through a side passage nearby.\n\nMy texts hint that you'll find a mechanism within, probably a lever, that will open the way for us to move deeper.
We have a ways to go, I'm afraid.\n\nYou'll face Dwemer mechanics within. Traps, automatons. Mind your surroundings.

This city was part of an early colonization attempt. The jungle was infamous for being untamable, but our best minds took that as a challenge. The story goes they built a sprawling metropolis. And then it vanished. Never to be seen.

Honestly? Who knows? Root Sunder has been a ghost story for centuries. There may have never been a real Root Sunder. But this certainly looks like a lost city. And if it will get my name in published papers, I'll swear it's Root Sunder all day.
I can't believe I lost my sword again. I don't know what to do.\n\nI want to be a warrior and make Mother proud, but I also love smithing. What do you think? Should I become a warrior? Or a smith?
You found my sword! Thank you. I want to be a warrior and make Mother proud, but I also love smithing.\n\nWhat do you think? Should I become a warrior? Or a smith?
I think she wrapped it up in a piece of bacon and fed it to one of those Scamps!\n\nThat's what it sounded like, at least ….
Take it, but please get rid of the Hagravens before I'm brought in there.
The barrier hums with energy, blocking the entrance to the crypt beneath the Bone Orchard.
The high family of Firsthold, House Rilis has ruled this part of Auridon for centuries. In the past, it was known as a proud line of warriors. \n\nUntil the last Rilis, that is.
I was. I think I loved him. But the tales of Daedric power he was given … even the power to control the minds of mer ….\n\nWhat if I never … what if I never really loved him?
Excellent. It's been fascinating to work with Shalidor. Even though he can't read the book, he's been an invaluable resource. I had to decipher layers-upon-layers of meaning hidden within the tome.

The Tomb of Dringoth was long forgotten … or so we hoped. Within lies the remains of the ancient Ehlnofey necromancer, Dringoth, who sought to obtain immortality with bloodshed. He slew hundreds and raised their corpses into an army of undead.
Spider venom. Enough to incapacitate, but not kill.\n\nOdd. Mingling with water in such a fashion would require a variety of alchemical compounds to dilute the venom.
Look for <<mz:1>>. Their venom sacs are potent, and durable enough not to pop when you smash the filthy creatures. They hate the light, so you'll need to search the deepest parts of the mine.
I'm saying it's odd, that's all.\n\nWhat's important now is the antidote. The venom is common to the spiders infesting our tin mine, but I'll need a concentrated amount.
We're having trouble opening a portal directly there. So we created this anchor to help us. Some trickery of Sheogorath's, no doubt.\n\nThe next time around, I'm sure this won't be an issue.
The greatest among the ancestors rose up and turned back the undead horde by laying a trap. A great pit was dug and the ancestors piled high the bodies of those who had fallen to Dringoth's minions.

Yes, but he had no idea that for seven days and nights the Spinners of Grahtwood prayed to Y'ffre and had channeled their energy into the ring of standing stones surrounding the pit. When Dringoth entered the ring to raise the dead, he was trapped.

When the flames faded from his corpse, the ring was filled and a stone crypt constructed. The doors were sealed and the elders agreed to safeguard this place with Y'ffre's Blessing to prevent anyone from ever raising our dead again.
Every man, woman, and child strong enough to string a bow emerged from the trees with fire in hand. In a single volley Dringoth was pierced and immolated by hundreds of flaming arrows.

Rilis the Thirteenth. The legitimate heir of the despot Rilis the Twelfth—Sorondil's half-brother and current High Kinsman of Firsthold. \n\nHe's a good man, I hear. Less scarred by the acts of his father than Sorondil.

Rilis the Twelfth. They called him a despot, a murderer. He communed with Daedra. Committed horrible acts in the depths of his palace. \n\nFor his crimes, he's trapped here. In the banished cells beneath the castle.
You want the next tome, right? Well, I need entertainment! I can only light Prince Maleel here on fire so many times before it gets boring.\n\nYou understand.
Sounds good. I've heard Skald Svari holds out at one of the shrines. You rally her to the Hall and I'll get the others.
This ornate globe will collect the memories of the cultists. You use it on them then kill them.\n\nBelron can peer into the stored memories and perhaps see Stral speaking to a cultist.
Here's the globe. Use it on living cultists, then kill them. Their last memories will rush into the globe. You'll need to do this a few times to make sure you get a memory of Stral.
This ornate globe will collect the memories of the cultists. You use it on them then kill them.\n\nBelron can peer into the stored memories and perhaps see Stral speaking to a cultist.
Here's the dagger. Cut out the heart of a cultist and give that beating heart to Belron. You'll find him just south of my tent.
This magical dagger can cut out a cultist's heart that will magically continue beating. \n\nThe heart can reanimate a cultist corpse, for a bit, and it will tell us what it knew.
Give me the crown! Now!
Then, you die!
Of course. You're the only hope I have of getting my wife back from <<1>>. I'll tell you everything I know about the Imperial death traps inside that cave.
All good investigators always have questions to ask. What did you want to know?
Well, I hate to give this up, but I guess you need it more than me. This key opens the door to a hidden tunnel. It might help you get behind those guys.
Suit yourself, friend. You might as well make yourself comfortable. You'll be here a while.

These caves were an uninhabited gully last I knew. Merchants sometimes used it as a waystation to dump illicit cargo before checkpoints, but no one ever laid claim to it.\n\nIt seems like the Goblins found a troubling new use for the place.

The easy answer for the Mer is to say, "None," but that goes beyond hubris—it is plain foolishness. Goblins are extremely difficult to root out.\n\nThis batch may be some escaped slaves from the mainland. It's not unheard of.
I mean exactly what I say. You'll be here a while. Everyone stays longer than they expect. Might as well sit and wait it out.
Depends. How long you got?
Me? Oh, simple. I'm supposed to sit here and not move from this spot. Simply sitting … sitting. \n\nSitting here. Just sitting. Sitting here … sitting.
Same here. We're all here to perform a task. For as long as he wants us to …
Better grab a couple of extras, just in case anyone shows up while you're gone.\n\nI'll stay here and defend the knights from any wandering undead.

Undead guardians. The Imperials must really want to keep people away from the treasure if they resorted to necromancy.\n\nOh, and watch the floors for traps. Fire, spike plates … one wrong step and you'll be mutton on a spit.
<<1>> thinks she can unravel the secrets of the treasure's guardians. He'll keep her alive until she's no longer useful.\n\nOr until he sees me. Said he'd kill her the moment I show my face. Bastard.

What hasn't happened here? There are Reachmen all around the town, attacking us every day. A bunch of them broke through our lines, swarmed into the mine, then sealed it behind them. Good riddance, I say.
Channel the touch of the Lord of Brutality into us. All across the wood, my Reachmen are being transformed. I will undergo the ceremony within the central ruin.
Anything to help with your mission, but be quick. I need to move out soon.
All right. You can access the cave through the old mine behind me.\n\nOh, and if you spot any of my crew, send them this way. We'll need more numbers to take out the mutineers.
Death all around isn't enough for you? It is for me. There's also shamans out there, corrupting corpses in our graveyards, floating them out of the ground. Who knows why? Not me.
How should I know? I'm not down there, am I? You wanna know, you go down there and see for yourself. If you do find out, don't tell me. I don't wanna know.
Good, good. And filled with memories, I see.\n\nNow, let's hope one of the cultists whose memories you stole spoke with Stral. If so, we can learn what's going on here.

Seriously? Not much. It holds very little military value. For the most part, the place was built over the royal crypts to protect them from vandals and thieves.\n\nThe kings and queens of Skyrim are buried here, including our beloved Queen Nurnhilde.

The Stormfist clan supported the traitor Fildgor when he tried to take the crown from Jorunn. We haven't seen them in almost a decade.\n\nAs for the how, well, one moment they weren't here and the next we were surrounded. I suspect foul magic.

My plan is to sneak into the barracks and kill the invaders' leader, Halskar. Meanwhile, Captain Hamar waits for soldiers to arrive from Windhelm.\n\nIf I can take out their leader, the reinforcements shouldn't have any trouble taking back the fort.
Anything to help with your mission, but we must be quick about it.

Fort Morvunskar's primary purpose is to protect the royal tombs beneath it. Most of our departed rulers are buried here, including our dearly missed Queen Nurnhilde.\n\nBeyond that, it doesn't really hold any military significance.

I received word that Lieutenant Koruni plans to try to infiltrate the central barracks and take out the leader of these invaders.\n\nMeanwhile, I need to wait here for Windhelm soldiers to arrive. Then we'll sweep in and join the Lieutenant.

The Stormfist clan hasn't been seen in these parts in almost ten years. Back then, they supported the traitor Fildgor.\n\nAs to how they took us by surprise, I'm not sure. They came out of nowhere! Still, it dishonors us that we failed to stop them.
Yes. Don't want to escape. Go away. Leave me alone.
Nobody can get me in here. Can't be bothered. Can't be hurt. I'm invincible. The way I want to be.
Forever. Be safe in here forever.
As long as it takes. To be safe. Safe from all the evils. Safe from all the things. The things who want to hurt me. Safe from everyone!
Yes, the Mane and his kidnappers passed through this area recently. Our scouts discovered that they traveled through the camp of Colovians that are currently attempting to take this fort.
Sorondil is scion of the last High Kinsman, Rilis the twelfth. \n\nI … I was Rilis's mistress. And now my son risks his life for some fool treasure.
I hope so. Sage Tirora has passed to Sovngarde. Fallowstone deserves a sage, someone to record the Companions' deeds. But first I must prove myself.
The sage-to-be and a companion must pray at Fallowstone's shrines. Visions of the Five Hundred in their prime should appear to them. Will you take these prayer beads and accompany me?
You can find <<1>> In the yard, training the troops.\n\n<<2>> can be found assisting in the infirmary below.

We have been able to hold off the enemy so far, but perhaps we can help each other. There is a good chance that the enemy knows where the Mane was taken to.\n\nHere at the fort are two Khajiit champions, twins, that can assist you.
Just a moment, mortal. Lord Sheogorath asks that you perform a task, first. To prove your competence.\n\nHe claims to have misplaced a pair of items. Items you must recover.
A fork and a staff. Please do try to be quick. My Lord enjoys making me wait, but he's not very patient himself.\n\nI've opened a portal for your convenience. It should lead you directly to the fork.
Despite the age of these ruins, I suspect the usual defenses are in place. As I am averse to danger, would you explore the ruins to locate any Dwemer generators inside?
This control rod will keep our new friend loyal to you.\n\nI suspect the generators have been damaged over the years. You'll need to escort the spider to each and bid it to repair them.

As you see, we are not the first to enter Bthzark. In truth, I accepted Bhosek's request to explore these ruins only because they contain something I want, something I believe others died trying to obtain.
Knowledge is the greatest treasure. The Dwemer guarded their secrets as a king protects his gold. In Bthzark, the Dwemer hid a set of schematics, mechanical drawings that I greatly desire to possess.
Yes, chief learn talk, then Byz learn talk from chief after much time with masters. Byz very wise.\n\nBut Byz will not talk if you say not to! Byz just clean shiny things, trophies of old masters!
Elf is Nelanya. She make deal with Toothmaul tribe, weapons and armor for help! She even give … what is word … contract! Yes!\n\nElf kings and lords have to accept deal!
Contract is in dens, down tunnel. Byz will wait by chief's den! You will see! Byz tell truth!
The King's Arrow! Well met, my friend. The town's under constant threat and a horde of Reachmen took over the mine and sealed themselves inside.
<<1>> is trying to break into the mine. We've got people trapped in there. And we need to understand what in Oblivion the Reach are up to!

They're an order of Breton knights, fiercely loyal to High King Emeric, and by extension the Daggerfall Covenant. I've never heard of them operating this far from High Rock. Only more reason to contain them now.
Woman? What woman? I saw you strike down Halskar, pull something from the lockbox, and then pause for a long moment.\n\nI thought you were catching your breath up there.

Well, they do say that the royal tombs are haunted. Soldiers tell stories of seeing and hearing strange things during night patrols.\n\nStill, if a spirit spoke to you, those relics must be special. Did the spirit happen to give you a name?
Queen Nurnhilde? Our beloved Queen was struck down in battle against the Akaviri ten years ago.\n\nI'd listen carefully to whatever Queen Nurnhilde said to you. You are truly blessed, my friend!

Let me see that.\n\nThis doesn't even make sense. I can't think of a court in the land that would take this seriously. The wording isn't even in the Goblins' favor. They think this is going to buy them some kind of status?
Make no mistake, they are still Goblins. Still, if we can break up the alliance here and now, it will save us much grief.

Magnanimous of you. I'll leave you to it then, and go to see if the signal fire brought in any backup.\n\nBreak up this alliance and find this Nelanya person. See if she likes being threatened with sharp objects.
Mehrunes Dagon's plane of Oblivion. It's a wasteland. Nothing but stone, lava, and Daedra. When the gates first opened, I had a good look. \n\nAnd smell. Mara's heart, that place has an odor!
The cart was full. They said they'd be back for me soon.
Of course not! Who harms their dinner before they feast?\n\nI'm sure they're going to be very good to me. At least until supper time.

This world is a deadly place when the sun glows bright in the sky. It's just too dangerous outside.\n\nEven the wounds I recently suffered require time and a great deal of blood to overcome. Imagine the cost of trying to deal with all those hunters.
Let me review my notes ….\n\n Ah, yes, my research says that we need to bypass the "Guardian's Skull." It, too, should have an unlocking lever that will allow us to pass deeper into these ruins.

I must say, you are a strange one. Others would have drawn weapons the moment they saw what I was.\n\nAnyway, I could attempt to scare them away. But they're hunters. I don't suspect they scare very easily.
Almost definitely. The transition from the "Guardian's Helm" to "Guardian's Skull" implies vulnerability, I think. We must be getting closer to the Eye.

Just because I'm not attempting to rip you open and feast on your blood doesn't mean that I'm not thinking about it.\n\nIt's our nature to lust for the life within you. Luckily for you, Valeric has taught us to control our hunger.
Valeric saved us. He has his reasons, I guess.\n\nHe even infiltrated a Dominion military camp to save Jaruk. The Khajiit was dying and Valeric turned him.

Valeric believes that this power is a curse, not a gift. The temptation of blood must be controlled at all costs, he tells us. We were not meant to feed upon one another.\n\nHe teaches us to survive, but not to lose control.
Koth is Koth. Pup tell Koth you want speak. Speak.
I was different once. A servant, given to the Nords as a gift when this alliance was formed.\n\nEventually, though, my masters grew tired of me and I was thrown out into the cold.
All Elves lie! Trick! Elf said there would be trick, but she lie, too. Why trust you?
Tired of Elf-speak! All lies! Not want any of you, just to be left alone.\n\nHere. Key to Elf cave. You kill or not kill her as you want. Koth is done with this mess.
I didn't. The cold overtook me. The next thing I remember, Valeric was watching over me. He gave me his gift to save me.\n\nIt's kind of funny. On the day I died, my life truly began.

His father belongs to the Volkihar clan. Tyrants known for their cruelty and lust for blood. They embrace their power and believe themselves to be greater than mere mortals.\n\nAs you can guess, Valeric opposes this line of thinking.

Valeric's father believes that a war is coming and he wants to take advantage of that. So he's building an army. You can see his spawn all around the hot springs.\n\nAnd he continues to try to convince Valeric to join him, of course.
Ah, yes! Many times. Each time, things have gone horribly wrong.\n\nIt usually ends up very messy. Lots of blood. But don't worry about it. Everything will be different this time.

I could crush you, yet I do not. You need to understand. \n\nThe two who follow my son are all that remain. The others lost control, slaughtered villages in their mindless rage. They had to be, how do I say it, put down? Such a waste.

Of course he didn't. Why would he tell his new ally that he was the cause of such rampant slaughter?\n\nI grow tired of these questions. I have told you what you have asked, now you must answer me. Will you assist me or shall we be enemies?

I don't care what Valeric taught us! This is who we are! This is what we are!\n\nIf we ever hope to defeat the ancients, we must embrace the power as they do. We can't keep feeding on skeevers and hope to grow strong. We must … we must feast.
In that case, I'll take any help I can get.\n\nWe tracked the Worms from Stony Basin. Got here just ahead of them. I guess that's why some of the delvers still live. And a few of my men.

The delvers found an ancient puzzle and gathered notes about it—clues. The Worms killed the delvers to get their notes. Whatever they're after, we can't let them get it.\n\nSave who you can, but we need those notes.
Yes, I think so. I believe the ruins contain the burial vault of Valdur, one of Ysgramor's Companions.\n\nThose pages you've collected? They're the clue to getting inside. If only I'd had more time!
I hope so.\n\nMy apprentice, Daneras, is down in the vault … if he's still alive. Find him. Together, the two of you must find a way into the tomb and stop the cult.
I'll survive, Mara willing. Who are you?
We'll be fine. We've held them off this long. We can hold a bit longer.\n\nYou just focus on what Sinien has to tell you.
Firsthold must not fall. We've unsheathed our sharpest blades. Curious about these folk?
My personal elite guard. We call them Talons. The queen has her Eyes. I have my Talons.\n\nBetween the Talons and the Marines, the finest blades in Auridon are arrayed against Oblivion.

Razum-dar's folk. Eyes of the Queen. I know you've worked with him before. Normally they'd never expose themselves like this. \n\nThe cat said, "We do not draw blades in the daylight." But here they are, making sure we live through this.
Sinien's spellslingers. Mages from the guild hall. Normally they'd be curled up with a good book or brewing some obscure potion.\n\nThey've done the guild proud, backing us up.

I received word just before the blade came down. You fought beside my Talons at North Beacon. I'm damned proud of these folk.\n\nBetween the Talons and the Marines, the finest soldiers in Auridon are arrayed against Oblivion.

Definitely! Didn't Urcelmo tell you? He's been trying to find weak points in the barrier for us. \n\nWhen that thing goes down, he's sure to move up. I'd look for him in the inner courtyard—after your victory!

If my research is correct, then you've unlocked the door to the Eye itself!\n\nAccording to my notes, the Eye is located in a chamber called the "Guardian's Orbit." Sounds … somewhat grisly. It's probably the structure up ahead.
Probably the most powerful constructs yet remain in this ruin. The Dwemer are so very fond of leaving their treasure with their traps and automatons.\n\nBe ready for anything.
You have questions? The waters of knowledge flow stronger through Aronel, but I will answer what I can.
Ha! Do I look like one? I'm glad you have to ask.\n\nI'm just Maesa's apprentice … so far, anyway. She's been teaching me for about a year now.
He's a fisherman. Fisher-lad. He stops by every day to see me.\n\nHe's always making dirty comments. Someday, my da's going to hurt him.

Oh, yes. We start with a lump of metal and end with something useful. Horseshoes and nails and swords and whatnot.\n\nI hear there are other kinds of crafters on the mainland, but I'd never be anything but a smith.
Have you seen the size of Maesa's arms? Holsgar says she once punched out a mammoth.\n\nSmithing is a great way to let out frustration, especially after Otroggar comes over.

Have you seen the size of Maesa's arms? Holsgar says she once punched out a mammoth.\n\nSmithing is a great way to let out frustration, especially after Otroggar comes over.
We were sent here by the Pact leadership. They believe the Worm Cult wants to enslave the spirits of ancient Companions. Something about strengthening the newly raised Sinmur. That is all I was told.
We found it embedded in a pillar inside the cavern. We suspected its existence from lore that Aronel had come across, so we searched for it once inside.
It contains a tiny portion of Hakra's essence, her soul. Stabbing a newly dead corpse with it should enable Hakra to take possession of the body, perhaps for only a limited time though.
As am I. Watch and see a true warrior in action!
Nothing would please me more.
You think so? Then let's find out!
Fight? I don't even know how to hold a weapon! What can I do?
The Fists of Thalmor? I thought they abandoned Velyn Harbor!\n\nIf they're still here, maybe there's a chance. All right, I'll help.
Alone? I can't fight them by myself! I saw what they did to the others. Haven't you seen the bodies?\n\nIf I hide here, maybe they'll take what they want and leave.
Ha! Do I look like one? I'm glad you have to ask.\n\nI'm just Maesa's apprentice … so far, anyway. She's been teaching me for about a year now.
He's a fisherman. Fisher-lad. He stops by every day to see me.\n\nHe's always making dirty comments. Someday, my da's going to hurt him.
