Have you seen the size of Maesa's arms? Holsgar says she once punched out a mammoth.\n\nSmithing is a great way to let out frustration, especially after Otroggar comes over.
Really? The Thalmor are still here? I heard their captain ran away, or was killed!\n\nMaybe we've got a chance with them on our side. Velyn Harbor's my home. I'll fight for it.
The Fists of Thalmor? I thought they ran off!\n\nBut how can they take back our entire town? There aren't enough of them. I heard the captain got killed in the first wave, along with her men.
Well, they've got me! Give me a weapon and I'll learn how to fight.\n\nThanks for finding me. I … I don't think I could've done anything on my own.
The Fists of Thalmor are still alive? And they've got weapons? Good.\n\nI'd rather smash skulls with a mace, not my bare hands.
Can't wait to give these Drublog what's coming to them.\n\nHope the lieutenant has a good morning star. I like weapons I can swing.
Oh yeah! I forgot to deliver the message to the constable in Koeglin Village as well. \n\nThat's actually kind of funny, isn't it? Unless … are you frustrated with me?

I know. You're right. I've never been a very good messenger. I always wanted to be a king or a duke, or something more important … but here I am.\n\nI'm doing my best. Please don't tell anyone about this. I'll do better next time—I promise.
Oh good. You had me worried there for a moment. \n\nThanks for understanding. I'll see you around the castle, I'm sure.
High Kinlord Rilis didn't know of her treachery when he let her into the city. And that was it.\n\nWe lost touch with Rilis after the gates to the Deadlands opened. I hope he's still alive.
Mehrunes Dagon's plane of Oblivion. It's a wasteland. Nothing but stone, lava, and Daedra. When the gates first opened, I had a good look. \n\nAnd smell. Mara's heart that place has an odor.

Not recently. Sir Hughes has been up at Alcaire Castle, advising Duke Nathaniel.\n\nI wish he'd come back too. All this controversy at Firebrand Keep. The Knights of the Flame need a strong leader and they need him around.
He's here. He piled in right behind the Battlereeve. Said something about supporting the Marines and the guilds.\n\nYou know how he is.

Estre dropped a barrier around the inner castle. We'll need a way past it, to get at the portals. I think the Battlereeve and the guild leader plan to crack that thing like an egg. The frontal approach.

Can this be? The Divines must have had a hand in this. Frostheart Blossom just might save him. I'll apply it immediately.\n\nPlease, go out on the balcony and tell his wife, Odvild. This news will mend her heart as well.

It's partly Sir Hughes' fault. 

He sent us orders to make preparations for a battle with the Redguards. Goes completely against the Covenant, and some of the knights are refusing to comply. 

Hughes needs to come clear things up.
Ha! I'd laugh harder, but it hurts. Sir Hughes is probably the most respectful knight our order's ever known.\n\nMurdered the duchess… ha! That'll be the day. No more jokes, okay? It hurts too much.

I'm sorry to say that Sir Hughes is in no condition to talk. I tried to help him, but this is simply beyond my ability to treat. \n\nIt seems to be some type of curse. He came in mumbling to himself, and soon he was just … gone.

Well, it was my ritual.\n\nThree Imperial mages hired me to turn condemned prisoners into an undead force—the Empire frowned on necromancy, you see. But when it came time to perform the ritual, they locked me in with the prisoners!
Now, for the staff. When last we spoke, my lord recalled the discomfort of desert sand.\n\nI believe it lies somewhere within Hammerfell, in the dry and decayed hands of Prince Maleel.

I do not think you could cause his condition to be any worse, so you are welcome to do what you like.\n\nI warn you though, curses like this are very unpredictable. If you start to feel dizzy, I would suggest stepping away.

Duchess Lakana? He said he had killed her, but I assumed he was hallucinating … he's very ill.\n\nSo you are here to place him under arrest? Even if he is guilty of such a thing, he cannot answer for it if he is catatonic. He must remain here.
This is the necropolis Asakala, the resting place of Prince Maleel. Also known as the Scythe of Yokuda. \n\nThe prince's underlings were clever. They crafted magical seals to guard his resting place.
Observe the Yokudan statues. Each bears a crystal in the helm and a seal at the base. \n\nThe essences you see swirling around in the air here? Their energy can be used to unlock those keystones.

Here, I can grant an aura that will allow you to capture the essences as they pass through you. Collect as many of the small ones as you can. They should unlock these scarab seals on the statues nearby.\n\nI'll need to consider the other two.

I will stay and mourn my son before I return to my clan.\n\nI knew in my heart that Valeric would never abandon the path he selected, but I never stopped trying to change his mind. At least I can find comfort in that fact.
<<1>>, <<2>>, and their small-minded Commander <<3>>. When their imperfect grasp of the ritual destroyed us, they locked our souls to the mortal realm.

Because they thought the principles of necromantic binding were the same as conjuration circles. Instead, the magic flowed through their very minds, turning their skulls into imbued foci.\n\nI can end this cascading effect if I possess their skulls.

Those small-minded fools were too concerned with politics. They thought if they could control the ritual itself, they'd have no need for me. The height of arrogance, to think they could begin to understand the complexity of my preservation ritual!
The undead don't eat, sleep, or breathe. They make perfect guardians for a place such as this. \n\nAnd I suppose a secret cache isn't very secret if you have to replace the troops every six months.

The rest of the militia and I will stop the Drublog from burning this area to the ground.\n\nI'll make one of the buildings atop the hill into a makeshift headquarters. When the runner clears the gate, meet us up there.
Activate the welkynd stones around the ruins. Speak to the spirits that watch each stone. If anyone knows how to get into the ruins, they do.
Others entered before you. They have released an ancient evil in the depths of our sanctuary. No more shall pass!

The countess was so sad about Mathias. She sent me to get flowers for his funeral, but on the way, one of these crazy cultists snuck up and just grabbed me.\n\nHe dragged me back here and they asked me all these questions.

This whole thing—the mirror—it wasn't the suitors. These cultists wanted to get rid of the countess so they can take over the town.\n\nThey forced me to talk. I think they're planning to kill the countess at the funeral. You have to go stop them!
In danger? Is it one of those pathetic suitors? Are they really that determined to have me out of the way?

I don't want to fight them. They have their orders, but they're wasting time. Every second that passes is another second our people remain in danger.\n\nSometimes you have to resort to drastic measures to save the ones we care about.
I know this isn't an easy decision. Especially for someone who has no stake in this.\n\nBut I have to know if you're going to help us. We could use someone with your skills.
It's an ancient Dwemer artifact of immense power.
Is what it?
Are you one of those who violated our sanctuary?
A terror unseen for millennia has been unleashed. Death and eternal torment await all in this land. What hope do you have of stopping forces you cannot understand?

Last time, <<1>> got out by the fur on his tail. The ghost wants her lover to stay forever.\n\nBut there is a barrier within. Beyond are the treasures of the Ayleids, locked up for centuries! Nothing like the trinkets I sold.
<This wardrobe holds finely tailored dress uniforms. A thin layer of dust covers the uniforms.>
<This nightstand contains a pristine comb, a silver container filled with a musky lotion, and neatly folded handkerchiefs. A fine coating of dust covers everything.>

That bastard sent the bandits on me! Their leader, Chanda, told me he hired her. I was lucky to escape alive.\n\nLook, how about I pay you to steal back the silk from Chanda? You'll find her camp to the east.
The poem on the sword opens the ruin, yes?\n\nMore scribbles are all around the ruins. Poetry! Spoken randomly they do nothing, but if we knew how they fit together ….
Good. Take the sword as a symbol of our pact. I, er, want it back later.\n\nI will keep her busy. You figure out the poems. And when we get out, we will both be very rich, yes?
Down into the cave. The same place they dragged the others. May the Three watch over their souls now.
Thank you. I really am trying to help. \n\nBoth plants will work in the potions, so anything you find will help.
As usual, Boril's wife wants someone else to do her work for her. She's a bit spoiled, if you ask me.
Here, take what I have. \n\nWouldn't want it said that I didn't do my part when the mine was in trouble.
Yes, I'm sure. Edrasa will have to do her own work this time.

Aheh. I admit, I do not do this only for you!\n\nUntil now, I have only been able to, shall we say, receive gifts from her. If even a handful are like the lightning stone, well! It could be fairly lucrative, yes?
She may not let you in, and there is still the barrier!\n\nNo. We do not hide our sugar in one boot. We go in separately.
It seems Edrasa has found someone new to do her work for her.
Did you say pay? Well, look at that. I happen to have a few redweed stems right here.
I'm sure. Running around digging up plants isn't going to help the headache I have from those fumes.
We could open the ruin and share in the plunder! We'll enter separately as paupers, but leave together, rich as kings!\n\nSo, you will help me?
Oh, do I? Thanks so very much for noticing.
Well, one can't be too careful. I might as well take the Maulborn cure. Just as a precaution, you understand.
No. Probably because I started to get ill just before I got here.
Not so bad … at least not yet. Maybe they'll let me join up after I get the cure.
I appreciate your help, but let's be clear. I'll pay you to recover my property, not to ask questions.

All right! You won't understand anyway.\n\nI lost a small potion bottle, my work clothes, some finely-ground mineral dust, and, well, a type of screw-driven tool I'd rather not elaborate on out in the open.
Ah … but curiosity kills the Khajiit. And it kills other people, too.\n\nBut, seriously, my tools aren't anything remarkable. I'm just a very private person. Can't you just trust me?

He's down below. He's got Wuuthrad down there too. I worry about what he might be planning.\n\nI cannot get through the door though. It is bound by some horrid necromantic ward.

It requires a living sacrifice. Someone has to touch that gem over there in the ritual circle. They will die, but then the door can be opened.\n\nOne of the cult members did it to open the door for Wormfather.
No. There is no time. The door must be opened and you must go after Wormfather. \n\nI'll make the sacrifice. It's the right thing to do. It'll ensure my place in Sovngarde at least.
Yes. That's it then, isn't it? Best get on with it.\n\nIt's a good end. Tell the others my story, would you? Tell them I died well. For the Pact and the Skald-King!

I was just following my chieftain! Wouldn't you? Thallik Wormfather promised us glory, everlasting life, and power. It was all lies and ash.\n\nI'm tired of war. Please, I just want to go home to my children.
I thought I'd die here and never see my girls again. I'm ashamed I was part of this foolish war.\n\nI'll return to the Reach and live a good life. I'll never go to war again. Thank you!
Thank you! You won't regret this. I'll return to the Reach and live a good life.
I understand. He may be a Reachman, but we're not monsters. I'm ashamed I considered it.\n\nGet him out of here. I'll open the door for you.
Very well then.\n\nI've instructions to have you return to the Isles. My lord would have a word with you.
Wonderful! I'll just take … Forky! Oh, I've missed you so much, Forky! Let's never, never be parted again.\n\nGives me goosebumps just to hold it in me hand again!
Still here after all this time … I had expected them to crumble with the ages.
From <<1>>s? Never would have thought of that. You know what? These will go right into the fire. Time we had a celebration! Thank you, traveler.

Careful of the mature kwama.The big fellows don't like this smell, no they don't. These little guys aren't as sensitive as their elders, so they aren't angry.\n\nOh, and be careful if you see the Kwama Queen. Not friendly. Not friendly at all.

<<1>>, Lady of the Weald! Surely they still sing of her? Her hair, bright as the sun! Her skin, pale as the moon. Nine years we were together, happy! \n\nThen the war … I'd gone north to fight the uprising and died there.
An old knight. <<1>> the Gold, they called me! I had lands, titles, slaves ….\n\nAll dust, now. Even my love has forgotten me!

An army of them. Side by side, they'd stretch from here to the Niben! But that was our downfall.\n\nSo many slaves. We could not bring them to heel. Not all of them. They killed her before slithering away.
She brought me here with words of light, but knew me not. When I went to her, she cast this barrier to keep me and all others away.\n\nI have been in this place ever since. Waiting.
Release from this nightmare, what else? <<1>> remembers only the sword! Its enchantment blinds her to everything else!\n\nIf I still had the sword, maybe ….
What? The sword? Give it to me!\n\nWere I alive, I could grant you such splendor! Alas, everything is dust. But I am forever in your debt.
Bring her with me. To Aetherius, to whatever lies beyond.
And, as promised: the book. Go ahead. Take it!

Hm. As dark as that may be, I can't say that I'd feel guilty. You know, back up near the portal, I think there was a Reachman in a cage. Perhaps he crossed the cult.\n\nI suppose you could bring him here and trick him into touching the gem …?
All right, but be quick. \n\nWhatever Thallik Wormfather is doing down there, we need to get in there and stop him, and fast!
All right. Thank you. I'm sorry again that I was part of this attack.\n\nIf you ever visit the Reach, maybe you can meet my girls.
Thank you. You're a kind soul. I'll tell my girls about you … the foreigner who saved my life.\n\nI'll raise my children right. We'll never trouble the Pact again.
Yes, the greatest party in all the worlds—the Five Finger Dance! Baan Dar's realm. You've done so well today, I know old Baan Dar will be glad to have you at his side.
Here, if you please. Aelif, stay with our new friend. You two search these bodies, see if you can find anything of note. A pleasure meeting you, O my comrade.
I can't … I can't say. My time grows short. Save Merric, stop the Daedra. Ware the followers of Molag Bal ….
I disobeyed him. There was a ritual. A … a child. She reminded me of my Bruca. I was supposed to sacrifice her for the cult.\n\nI couldn't do it. I set that girl free, and I don't regret it!
Oh no, is it about father? He's dead, isn't he? No! Tell me he's all right. Please!
He never abandoned his principles. My father was a stubborn but good man.
Oh father … he was the best man I've ever known.\n\nWhat will we do without him?
Our power is stretched to its limit. But … your need is great. Very well. We will raise one of the legendary Five Hundred to aid you in this time of great peril.
Ha! You have the spirit of Ysgramor, my friend. Yes. Two blades are more dangerous than one.\n\nSpeak to <<1>>, <<2>>, and <<3>>. Choose a companion and tear the Worms apart!

There are four portals in the ruins. There are many cultists and many Daedra guarding them, but if you can find the portals and close them, that will reduce their numbers.\n\nThe blessing of Ysgramor's Five Hundred Companions will be with you.
My lord is certain he lost his utensil somewhere in Skyrim. It was during a visit to his friend Korthor in Vuldngrav.\n\nThat was during the Merethic Era, I believe.
Prince Maleel al-Akir, the Scythe of Yokuda. A formidable warrior, in his day.\n\nThat was over a thousand years ago … but still.
What can I tell you, Adept?

What sort of Arch-Mage would I be if I didn't? \n\nI spent my mortal life seeking knowledge of all things, not just magic. Yokudan, or as you know them, Redguard, culture is no exception. If Valaste was here, I'm sure she could tell you the same.

You need only to be near them to collect them. My spell will keep the essence tied to you until you're ready to deposit it within the statue. \n\nJust remember, you'll only be able to collect four at a time.
Alik'r is under attack. A necromantic cult has disrupted the normal ebb and flow of life and death.\n\nThe dead that once served Maleel are now a way into his tomb.

Just so, Adept. The lesser essences you see before you will empower the statues with the orange and green crystals, the statues near the entrance to this complex.\n\nI need to consider how we'll empower those two rear statues.
Beneath the statues lie buried the dead of Prince Maleel's armies. Their essences have bubbled up from beneath the sands, released by the dangers threatening Alik'r today.
Yes, of course. Forget the gear, just save Charadin!
Of course! How could I have forgotten?\n\nHere, hold still.

Abamath was built over an ancient Orc settlement dedicated to the worship of Mauloch. It is said the "Blood of Mauloch" originated here, deep underground where the blood flows.\n\nIf there's a shrine or some ancient blood magic within the ruins ….

The entrance to the ruins is locked by <<mz:1>>. I saw a few Cultists guarding them as I was dragged to this cage.\n\nGet the <<mz:1>>. Two of them unlock the outer door. We'll use the rest inside the ruin.
I want you to find their shaman. I saw him heading to the beach a short while ago.\n\nThe chieftain is waiting for something, and I need to find out what. Find a good hiding place and listen in.

This object is called an <<1>>. The Cult imbued it with a curse. When attuned to a door, it can only be destroyed by the release of a soul.\n\nFeed the <<1>> a soul and it will shatter, clearing your path. Arithiel's soul will do nicely.
Once it's yours, it'll send you straight back to Tamriel. Funny how books have a way of transporting you ….\n\nSimply hold your breath, close your eyes. And count to … let's say a million?
Trust me. What I did is horrific, and I must atone for my crimes.
In this dream state, only you and I are real—and I'm only really certain of myself.
I do. Which means those cultists are planning something—something big.\n\nKing Emeric must be warned. That is the highest priority.

I have much to do here! Finding buyers, collecting gold! Aheh. This will be quite profitable, no small thanks to you!\n\nFeel free to visit from time to time! Now that those noisy rats have left, we may conduct business, yes?
Just over there, in the post on the beach. Forbid any of us from going in and all.\n\nHate to see that meat go to waste, but I'm not about to disobey the chieftain.
That's what the chieftain said. Some voice told him, or so he says.\n\nI don't questions my betters. Neither should you.
<<1>>? I thought she was just another person heading to the town of Silvenar. Now I'm not so sure.\n\nWhoever she is, she saved my life and deserves to be rescued.
They're the Cult of the Black Worm, Daedra followers. Molag Bal worshipers. They spread destruction and chaos wherever they go.\n\nThey're in Abamath for something evil.

<<1>> must be detained until my arrival. I've given the materials you need for her bindings. She is not to be harmed, else your tribe will pay in blood.\n\nVelyn Harbor is but the first gift. The conquest of a hundred cities await, if my will is done.
Then begone. I have many things to prepare in Silvenar before I can return to <<1>>. \n\nSee that no one interferes with the ritual. <<2>> must not escape.
Outsiders have no place here. The House Hlaalu hirelings should pack up and go. The trader is in Farseer Bodani's hands now.
She fell into the trap that Hound spoke of. Now my uncle, our clan's chief, waits for the Hound to take her away.\n\nThere may still be time to save her. Talk to my father, <<1>>.
Yes. He made the trap, at the chief's request.\n\nHe's in the lower arena. I've wasted enough breath trying to convince him. Maybe he'll listen to someone else.
The poor child is bound with borrowed magic, as my brother commanded.\n\nThe Hound comes for her. You can't stop it.
Don't take that tone! It's not as simple as you think.\n\nI'm old. Soon, I'll die. I can't make choices about the tribe's future. That's the chief's, my brother's, role.

That thought has also crossed my mind. You think like a wise woman. I like that.\n\nThe trader insulted the Farseer and her anger has blinded her to such consequences. Talk to wise woman Iru-Ahan. She may be able to help you.
His handiwork, but these Daedric symbols aren't Mauloch's.\n\nThere's no time to study it, though. If he gave you this, it must be used to free <<c:1>>.

The merchant isn't your concern. His fate is in the hands of the Farseer and the Ghost Snake.\n\nStill, something disturbs the Vale. I thought it was the merchant, but now the signs and portents point to you.
The signs and portents are all around us, influencing events. Can you not see them?\n\nIf you want my advice, you should—Wait! What's that?
Thank you. I'll follow when I see it's safe to move.\n\nLook for the sconces to either end of the ruins. That's usually where they are.

Ha! Everyone asks that.

King Aphren conquered Wind Keep and renamed it Aphren's Hold—just to the south. The town kept the old name. 

It's a small place, but we do a fair amount of trade. The countess is wealthier than most of her suitors.
I'm sorry. The things that they're doing to my friends ….\n\nWait. I remember something. I saw a cultist taking keys into the camp's central tent. That's where you'll find the cage key!

Yes. It'll take too long to explain, though. I must go after him. The Hound is my concern, and mine alone.\n\nYet, I can't just leave the Silvenar in danger. It's as if I must be in two places at once.

She must be up ahead. Looks like there's an entire legion of soldiers standing between this chamber and the end of the sewers.\n\nAnd my guards are waiting for them. We'll meet her army in battle—give you the opportunity to deal with her.

Yeah. The countess has at least five different men who've been courting her. Not common folk like you and me, either. \n\nWe're talking noblemen. People with lots of gold to throw around. They buy her some pretty fancy gifts.
I wouldn't go near that place if I were you. They say it's haunted.\n\nSome other people came by asking about it recently. Haven't seen them since—so like I said, I wouldn't go there.
I don't know. They were all wearing the same types of clothes. Looked like some kind of Daedric Cultists. \n\nAll the more reason to stay away from Aphren's Hold if you ask me.

Yes, of course. I have orders from the Tribunal Temple to register you and grant you access to the city immediately.\n\nThe Sacred Lady, Almalexia, requests that you attend her in the Temple at your earliest convenience.

Yes, yes. I already said that. Weren't you listening?\n\nIt's a rare honor to receive an audience with the Sacred Lady. You should go now and leave this lowly clerk to his duties. We can't all have appointments with the divine.

I can't think. They're ripping me apart!

Follow … symbols … above doors … Whale, Eagle, Snake.

Hurry!
I'll be theirs, corrupted by the cult. My spirit will ravage the Rift.\n\nStop them, please!

Now that you mention it, there's Treva's Mammoth Horn! It's old and one use might shatter it, but it'll stop a mammoth in its tracks!\n\nHere. Use it if you have to. I don't care if it breaks, so long as you come out alive.

No, I just enjoy hanging around the Temple. I love all the gnashing of teeth and hypocrisy.\n\nYes, I was waiting for you. Look, don't get too excited. There's trouble brewing and I don't have a contract, so I can't officially get involved.

The Maulborn are in the city. I saw what they did in Narsis and I don't want to see the same thing happen in Mournhold. I'm not supposed to care, but I guess I'm getting a little soft.\n\nYou've got the clout to find someone in power and investigate.

Wait, you got a date with the Sacred Lady? You really are something.\n\nLook, tell her about the Maulborn. Maybe she'll let you look into this. I normally wouldn't think of using her, but this is important. And I know Almalexia cares about the city.

If I knew the location of every Dwemer ruin? I could explore places no one has seen since the Dwemer were actually alive and kicking. That would be amazing!\n\nAnyone can be a scholar, but I could visit places no one alive has ever seen!

And I'll see if I can find out where the Maulborn are hiding. I'll meet you at the Flaming Nix, the cornerclub southeast of here.\n\nOh, and listen—don't breathe a word about me to Almalexia. Promise you'll do that and I'll help you save Mournhold.
Chief take all from homes of old masters, put here so we see trophies! Trophies of Elf-masters who wrong us!\n\nByz not forget beatings. Hit! Hit! Always hit in face!

From big island, yes. Byz told to muck out dung pits, clean floors, run when small Elf-masters throw rocks.\n\nChief take us away from all this, form Toothmaul tribe! Yes. Now we look on trophies to remind of us of hardships.
<<1>> was at the docks to meet the dignitaries. The Redguard arrived instead.\n\nShe probably went down fighting. If she's alive, though, we'll rescue her!

No, no tricks. You've clearly been able to sneak by or butcher every Goblin between the entrance and this room, so I don't fancy my chances in a straight-up fight.\n\nI'd rather talk this out. That is, if you can restrain yourself.
A gift? Oh! A <<1>>! I love these things! Bet you I can solve this in less than a minute!

You have helped my people. And through your actions, you have aided me. I sense that your accomplishments thus far are only the beginning. \n\nMy registrars have given you access to the city, but I would like to personally thank you for your deeds.

Courteous of you. My terms are simple.\n\nIn exchange for my life, I shall quit this cave and leave the Goblins to whatever fate you and your Dominion compatriot deem proper. You're even welcome to whatever spoils you find.

They were willing and able dupes. From the perspective of many in the Veiled Heritance, we're already losing. It was easy to agitate the Goblins against their former masters. We are willing to use whatever tools necessary to even the field.
What's the use in dying for this? I don't fancy my chances against you, and the Toothmaul aren't as useful as I expected them to be. No sense continuing the charade.

I sense that there is more to your story, but I won't pry. I trust your instincts and your judgment in these matters.\n\nConsider yourself blessed with my authority. You may investigate the Maulborn presence as you see fit.
They let the Colovians pass through the ward's protection. Before you ask, no you can't just use one to enter the camp. We've tried that.
Yes, they might be attuned to the holder's race. Regardless, they try to keep too many from the wards at the same time, so a handful of them should be enough to overload the wards.

Do not be so quick to offer your thanks. After all, you are doing all the work. Should you remove this Maulborn thorn from my side, I will have yet another reason to thank you.\n\nGo, speak to your secretive allies. We have similar goals. For now.

To protect my legacy. While this Guild was … after my time, I accomplished much in Tamriel. I founded schools of magic, oversaw the construction of the Great Maze, and bore my Spellmirror into battle.
Leaving. My superiors were none too happy with me for the whole Toothmaul business.\n\nYou were good enough to spare me. I'm waiting for a ship to come into harbor so I can leave Auridon for good.
After a fashion. I appreciate you giving me the chance. It's fairly obvious that my loyalties were in the wrong place. I'm not sure where I belong anymore, but it isn't here.
And do you know why I had to do it? Do you know what her father did to her? If you're truly Raerana's friend, you'll keep what you know to yourself. She needs me now. I'm all she has.

I know it. I laid powerful enchantments on my final resting place. When my legacy is threatened, I'm drawn back from Aetherius.\n\nMy presence here is proof enough: the Three Banners war is a threat to every Mage in Tamriel.

I won't waste my time recounting his antics. Suffice it to say, he got the better of me. Bets were made, wagers were lost. \n\nAnd my sanctuary, Eyevea, was pulled into his realm … my apprentices screaming all the while.
Probably. But she's still protected by the Midnight Union.
Too crowded. Only gots room for one group. Too many groups out here. You beat them, maybe you go in.
No, they're all equally shallow and untrustworthy.\n\nSir Brice and the Altmer Yarelion are the worst. It was probably one of those who gave me the mirror.
The Mane is, and has always been, our spiritual leader.\n\nKhajiit may travel far and live in distant places, but deep within, we are guided by the Mane, and Riddle'Thar.
Maybe you fight me!

Riddle'Thar sets us on our path, long before we know our milk-name, or take our first breath. The First Mane revealed the existence of Riddle'Thar to us, and we hold its revelations close to our hearts.
Just doing the Master's will. I will open the door for you.\n\nOh, and mind the Scamps. The little imps adore fresh flesh. Such children.

The House Dres farm outside the city is on high alert. I saw the guards get violent with people for just walking by.\n\nThey're using a courier named Thauravil to deliver bribes to House leaders and city officials. I think they're hiding something.
I hadn't considered that. You can really sniff out gems from a dung heap.\n\nAll right, I'll take Khammo to Anvil. He proves his worth on arrival, or he's fishbait.

Jilan-dar sells weapons. He gets snatched along the road and dragged here to be eaten, and he notices that the Goblins have shiny High Elf weapons and armor that could be resold to the Dominion.\n\nKhajiit needs to get back to his boat, though.

Sir Brice is a 'man of honor'. A Knight of the Flame with what he claims is a passion to match.\n\nThe poor man. Brice believes his own falsehoods. He says he loves me, but if I were clothed in rags, I'd be invisible to him.

He claims he was drawn across the leagues by my beauty, but the truth is that Yarelion is the disinherited son of some wealthy mage. \n\nRather than a talent for magic, though, Yarelion has a talent for spending. He would have me be his bank.

You find some of the weapons caches here in the gully, bring them to Jilan-dar outside by his boat. He will cut you in on profits. It is a bad time for the Dominion, and they will be eager to buy the weapons.\n\nDeal?
Terrifying isn't he? The will and attention of a child, with the power of a Daedric Prince.
I think you're trying to intimidate me. \n\nHere's a bardly riddle: if what's right is wrong, then what's left is right. And that's all you'll get from me.
Well, look on the bright side. You're still upright on two legs. You're not inside-out, or bright purple, or afflicted with new, angry limbs.\n\nIt could be worse.
I can't help her while I'm stuck in this cell, can I? Get me out and we'll talk.
Oh, I'm sure that several of my suitors will have already suggested they take custody of the estate.\n\nBoth Yarelion and Sir Brice are likely trying to rally support so they can petition the king.
Now, that hurts. I'm a scoundrel of my word. Trust me. Unlock the cage and I'm all yours.
Long ago, Ysgramor used Wuuthrad to slay Sinmur. That act imbued the axe with great power against the giant. Even Wuuthrad's shards can cause him tremendous harm.
Never thought I'd ferry the great Captain Khammo! Got to admire his moxie.\n\nI'll keep my end of the bargain. Now leave me to it before I change my mind.
I have Frirhild's ring. You could take it to Jorald and tell him you found it on some bandits. He'll believe you.\n\nThen Raerana and I can escape from here and be free at last!
Please, show mercy! Do you want Raerana to be completely alone? I can take care of her. This was all for her!\n\nShe knows me, she knows why I did this, why I had to do it!
You could help instead. Give Raerana some closure, and steer suspicion away from me. \n\nI have an idea, if you're open to it, if you truly care about Raerana.

The mirror? Is that what was wrong with her? Oh goodness! Mathias would've known. I don't really know the suitors ….\n\nMaybe it was Sir Brice … or that Altmer, Yarelion? Probably the Altmer. He's shady. I'd check him first.
I don't know. Maybe it has something to do with what happened to the countess? \n\nDid you talk to her? What did she say? Is she all right?

You know me so well! But we'll need to get the courier's key. He's been picking up wine here, then delivering bottles around town. He tends to keep a bottle or two as he goes along.\n\nWe might be able to use that to our advantage.

Don't get too cocky, hero. House Dres has fallen far and its agents are on edge. If the courier thinks he's being followed, he might get spooked. You want him relaxed enough to start drinking, got it?\n\nSo keep your distance.
You had to go and sweet talk me, didn't you?\n\nFine. Go downstairs and borrow a bottle of wine for me. I'll do the rest.
Poison! Don't give me that look. It's not lethal poison. It'll just put him into a nice, deep sleep.\n\nFollow him, and when he takes a sip from his bottle and falls over, you can grab his key.

This fool has pestered our hunters, importuned our wisewomen, and insulted me by demanding to speak to the man in charge of our tribe. \n\nI brook no challenges to my authority or disruptions to the Vale.

<<1>> discovered a way to harness the power in each shard and turn it against Sinmur. He'll place the shards you've collected in runic braziers.\n\nActivate those braziers to unleash the shards against Sinmur!

Perhaps, but not alone. If you plan to fight him without the shards, seek out other powerful warriors like yourself. You have little chance of besting the giant alone.\n\nRemember, Ysgramor fought alongside 500 Companions!
Our best bet is someone who saw a shard land. North of here is the refugee camp of Lost Prospect. I'd start there.
Thane Unnvald holds Fullhelm Fort to the northeast. If a shard landed nearby, someone there may know of it.

Once you kill the Drublog's leader, I hope those Orcs lose interest in the town.\n\nCurse it! <<1>> was a good leader, and dedicated to the Dominion, if a bit hot-tempered. I'll do my best to keep things together, but it'll be hard without him.
Rumors say a shooting star fell near Forelhost, a frozen peak to the northeast. It couldn't hurt to investigate. Just be sure to stay warm.

Then we'll fight until they leave, or help arrives. The Queen will send an army to protect the Silvenar and Green Lady once she hears what's happened in Velyn Harbor.\n\nSo I fight. And I'll keep fighting, no matter what.

Tired. Angry. Sad. I want to kill every Drublog and Redguard in <<1>>! <<2>> was ten times the leader the captain was! He didn't deserve to die.\n\nYou know, I bet the Drublog are only in this for pay. They'll quit when they see we aren't easy marks.

I was going to take him to the Ghost Snake, but all that changed when you arrived.\n\nI have seen a vision of you upon the Coiled Path. You have a role to play in deciding the fate of this man and our Vale.

Sir Brice is really respectable. I don't know why the countess isn't more receptive to him.\n\nHe's a Knight of the Flame and everything. I think he would make a good husband. Of course, he's never even noticed me.
I think he's from some rich family in the Aldmeri Dominion.  \n\nAll I've ever heard him talk about is gold. He even described the countess's hair as 'strings of gold.'
Like I said, the only ones I know at all are Yarelion, Sir Brice, and Raolin Munier. And I've only seen them in passing. \n\nI'll tell you what I know though, if you think it'll help.
Once we remove the barrier, the researchers can examine the relics before I sell them. <<1>> promises, no tricks.
I think he's from some rich family in the Aldmeri Dominion.  \n\nHe's really twisted. Something in his eyes. I always want to bathe after he looks at me. Don't really know any more than that.

Sir Brice is really respectable. I don't know why the countess isn't more receptive to him.\n\nHe's a Knight of the Flame and everything. I think he would make a good husband. Of course, he's never even noticed me.

Raolin seems cold to me. He breeds and sells livestock. He's wealthy—not as rich as the countess—but Raolin has gold. \n\nShe's out of his reach though. Gold isn't the only difference between the stable and the manse, if you know what I mean.

I think the Farseer runs the tribe, but Raston dismissed that idea. He doesn't believe a woman could have that kind of power. I hope he didn't insult her.\n\nAnyway, Raston went to talk to Gulakhan Harrinat. That was the last time I saw him.
Mathias is… dead? That's… That's terrible. Whoever did this… we have to make him pay. Please find out who it was.\n\nI'm going to need a few minutes to myself if you don't mind.

Who knows how these places get their names. Ithrini said that the Ghost Snake they worship is Sithis. Nonsense, if you ask me. \n\nAll I know is that big snakes slither near the swamps. They looked very real to me. Not ghostly at all.
I heard their mewling. Look, I'm in this business to make a living. If the old man splits his treasure with us, we'll get him to Anvil.
Good! Now we wait for the courier to come pick it up. We don't want to draw any attention to ourselves.\n\nStay close. There he is now. Closer, come closer!

I'm not sure. I've never been to this part of the Shivering Isles before. We're after the final tome, though, so we have to assume he has something truly perverse waiting in the wings. Certainly Valaste has suffered enough.

No, eyes front! Look at me. We're close friends. Closer. I said something funny. You're laughing. He just passed by. He's got the wine.\n\nLike what you see, hero? Of course you do. He's almost at the door. Keep watching me. All right, he's out. Go!
Irien? Altmer girl? Yeah, I promised her a way off this rock. But that won't ever happen if I die in here.
Is that really important right now?\n\nBhosek stole it from someone else. Can't steal from a thief. If you get me out of this, I'll owe you big.
Here then. I will begin the incantation. \n\nI would ask you to help me in this one last thing before I return to the river.

When I become a crocodile, I will forget this life. If I fight beside you, I can keep my focus, at least for a little while.\n\nI have made the preparations. Eating the heart is the last step. Fight with me, before I am gone forever. Are you ready?
Join me in vengeance. These bandits have destroyed what's left of my home.\n\nI would begin my next life by avenging my previous one, but I will need you to guide me. I wish to kill their leader.

My squad slashed through the front lines and made for water, hoping to cut off their supplies and reinforcements.\n\nThe vipers caught on and hemmed us in. Surrounded us and cut us down. I'm only alive because I ran.
This is a disaster. I should've just killed him and taken what we could scrounge from his corpse.\n\nTell the captain he can keep his bones and rot on this forsaken island.
That's my brother—always thinking of his family. Thank you, stranger.

No. I'm afraid not. I couldn't afford to give her a flower. 

So it was a mirror that finally won her over? Maybe Sir Brice or Raolin Munier was the lucky one. 

There is someone who would know for sure, but I am sworn to secrecy.

There is something unusual about you. I sense it and certainly the Ghost Snake knows of you.\n\nTalk to this man. Take his measure. Then speak to me when you're ready to face the trial of the Ghost Snake.
<<1>>, leader of Velyn Harbor's Fists of Thalmor, the honor guard for the Silvenar and the Green Lady, was found hiding beneath the docks! Without a scratch on her.
You should. You'll see what the lieutenant and I had to deal with.\n\nI'm heading back toward the center of town to make certain everything's secure. I'll meet you in the warehouse district.
Still in her hidey-hole. I put some guards on her, in case she tries to disappear … or the civilians try to lynch her. She has an interesting tale to tell. You should hear it.
Victory heals wounds as well as laughter does, and I've had a touch of both today.\n\nOf course, there's grim work ahead of us, cleaning up after the invaders. But at least the city's ours again.
We were inspecting ships when a sentry cried out "sail ho!" or something equally meaningless.\n\nIt didn't make any sense. After all, we expected a ship! I told the men to stay at attention.

And look like fools in front of the Green Lady? Of course I didn't sound the alarm!\n\nWhen the enemy attacked, I immediately saw we'd be overwhelmed. I organized a retreat and hid until reinforcements arrived.

How dare you? I did what I had to do to save my command! The lieutenant's sacrifice was … unfortunate. If he'd waited, I'm sure the raiders would have taken what they could and left Velyn Harbor more or less intact.\n\nHe died for nothing.

All the time, if you must know. Dolril is … unique.\n\nFor the leader of a pacifist order of healers, Dolril craves action. He can't help himself. He's attracted to trouble. And he always wants to do good. It's very confusing for the rest of us.
No, but I have an idea. Word in the hall is that there's a big contract, a huge contract. All hands on deck.\n\nShe probably wants you in the fight.

He calls himself "The Hound." I know little of who he is, or what his true purpose is.\n\nI do know he craves the attention of <<c:1>>. He would slaughter a whole village if only to ensure she remains unharmed.

We have lived alongside the Bosmer for generations. Some would say they look down upon us with disdain. And they would be right.\n\n<<1>> is wrong, but there are many who follow him. Many who would fight to see the Bosmer brought low.
How could I witness this monumental event if I was somewhere else?\n\nAs to who I am, well, at the moment, I am your friend. Let's leave it at that.
Aren't they fascinating? Ayleid civilization interests me. I'm documenting several ruins in the area.
My daughter. I trust her, yes.\n\nI'll tell you how to remove the binds, but that's the only help I'll give you. I can't work against my clan's chief.
<<1>>. She's young, but sees our struggles with clear eyes. My brother should listen to her.\n\nI can't help you. But I'll give you what you need.
Excellent! To be honest, I wasn't certain you could pull it off.\n\nGive them to me now.

No, I won't! I'd rather—oh, Baan Dar's ears, you've already seen them.\n\nI take care of … problems, much like you. I came to Velyn Harbor to eliminate a smuggler and a slaver and I did my job. Unfortunately, the invasion hindered my escape.
Actually, no. Killing just one of them would send the right message to the survivor.\n\nIt's not smart to eliminate potential employers, even when they're enemies.
Many thanks!\n\nIt might surprise you to know that the people who hired me aren't friends of Velyn Harbor. Even worse, they didn't pay me.

Yes, well, their leader didn't hire me. His lieutenants did.\n\n<<1>>, and <<2>> worked with my target and didn't want their boss to find out. They hired me to kill him, then they tried to have me killed. I'd kill them myself, but my wound ….

<<1>>, and <<2>> are lieutenants, leaders of the Ra Gada invasion force. They all worked with my target and didn't want their captain to find out. They hired me to kill him, then tried to have me killed.\n\nI'd kill them myself, but my wound ….
Some call them Heartland High Elves. They worshiped Daedra, kept slaves, and were notoriously violent people.\n\nIt's hard to reconcile that knowledge with their beautiful structures, isn't it?
An ancient place of power on Summerset Isle.\n\nIt's beautiful, especially at dawn. Or so I hear. I've never seen it with my own eyes.
I … can't talk about it. Telenger forbids students to discuss their work with anyone else but him.

I study with Telenger the Artificer. Have you heard of him? I went to Bangkorai with him once. It didn't end well for most of the students, but fortunately, I left unscathed.\n\nHe suggested I come to Belarata.
He's an instructor with the Mages Guild in Auridon. I'm lucky to work with him, I can tell you that!\n\nTelenger encourages direct study of the Ayleid ruins. I admire him.

Cursed? Mara's mercy! That's terrible! I guess you're going after Sirion then? 

Is the countess all right? Never mind. You have work to do. Go on. 

This is getting good. I can't wait to see what happens next.
Well I never… some nerve you have after I told you where to find Sirion.\n\nThat's fine though. You don't have to tell me. I'll find out on my own. I have my ways.

I understand. You're on the countess's business, so I'm sure it's important.

Besides, I can figure it out on my own. I have my ways, you know.

Goodbye for now then.

Wonderful. I didn't think you were such an amateur. But this must be your lucky day. The courier came back to get more wine. \n\nYou know the drill. Look into my eyes. Focus on me. Stay real close. Let the courier leave. And go!

Yes, I did. And I guess you've killed a few people in your time, too.\n\nYou may not approve of what I do, but we're on the same side right now. And I can help you do more damage to Velyn Harbor's invaders if you return my tools.

Have you ever lost a child or a spouse? Do you know what that pain is like?\n\nIt's unbearable. The Worm Cult said they could bring them back. We'd be reunited. All I had to do was pass them information.
Do you remember Denskar? Littrek? Do you remember how they died, bleeding from Covenant blades? \n\nI watched it all. I watched them die. You can't know how painful that is.

I barely see Tryn. She's off on her missions. And she'll be dead soon, too, in this pointless war.\n\nThe Worm Cult came when I was grieving. They said they could reunite me with my husband, my boy. All I had to do was pass information about the Pact.

Do you remember Trynhild? My daughter? She died on the docks of Bal Foyen, cut apart by Covenant blades. \n\nI don't blame you. I blame them, and myself. She's gone, and I'm alive. Do you know how painful that is?

Master Raston Vendil is missing. He went into the Mabrigash camp to make a trade deal. It seems he, ah, misread the mood of this tribe. Something went wrong.\n\nI wish we'd never come to the Vale of the Ghost Snake.

They're away, on "missions." I never see them, but it doesn't matter. They'll be dead soon, too.\n\nThe Worm Cult said they'd reunite me with Trynhild. All I had to do was pass information about the Pact.
The Pact. Of course. It's all about the Pact, isn't it? Everyone dies for the Pact. Well, why not add me to the tally? See if you're up for it!

Well, I want to go back to the graveyard and pay proper respects to my poor, sweet Mathias.

And I suppose I must say something to my suitors. 

Speaking of which, I'm sorry you had to talk to them before. I know that must've been painful.

Maybe. But I chose to believe. It wasn't just secrets. Soon the cult asked me to kill for them. Golun. Thane Fjora.\n\nMy family would despise what I've become. I'm done with the cult, but it's too late, isn't it?

Maybe. But I chose to believe. It wasn't just secrets. Soon the cult asked me to kill for them. Golun. Thane Fjora.\n\nTryn would despise what I've become. I'm done with the cult, but it's too late, isn't it?

Maybe. But I chose to believe. It wasn't just secrets. Soon the cult asked me to kill for them. Golun. Thane Fjora.\n\nDenskar would despise what I've become. I'm done with the cult, but it's too late, isn't it?
What justice can the Pact offer? To make up for all I've done by rotting in a cell?\n\nI'm going far away from the Pact and the cult. Come after me if you want, but be ready to fight.

I must hide from the cult, and they'll be after you too. \n\nBut, why spare me, after all I've done? Never mind. I'll go and I won't be back. My family will forgive me someday, I hope. I won't waste the chance at life.

Ashlanders, but even more isolated than most. Worship some snake spirit. Raston wants to trade for their unique snakeskin leather.\n\nThey won't tell me anything right now. Probably because I'm part of House Hlaalu. Maybe they will talk to you.
Yes. I betrayed you, even after all you did for me and my family. But you'll end my pain, won't you? That's good. It's fitting. But I won't just lie down and die.\n\nIf you want to kill me, earn it!

Face justice? Perhaps. But face my family? No. I've hurt too many. I can't do anything about that rotting in a prison.\n\nI'm leaving, going far away. Come after me if you want, but I won't just lie down and die.

I must hide from the cult, and they'll be after you too.\n\nBut, why spare me, after all I've done? Never mind. I'll go and I won't be back. My family will forgive me someday, I hope. I won't waste the chance at life.
I think it's probably best if I just stop pretending. \n\nI have no intention of marrying again, and I should stop playing these games. You helped me realize that.

You don't think so? Have I judged them too harshly? \n\nIt's hard being a woman of authority and being unmarried. I felt Mathias understood me, but that the suitors were all fools. Perhaps I should rethink that.

You wanted to know if we were lovers?

Yes. We were. No point in hiding it now. I think I loved him. It felt like it was just a game. Only now do I realize how wonderful he really was. 

Better than my suitors at least.
So it is not just the spirits of the soldiers that have been disturbed.\n\nDoes the king too wander these ruins in search of peace?
All right, all right. Why are you always so close? Stand back and let me work. \n\nI'll lure him upstairs. You wait a moment, then follow us. When I give the signal, go ahead and snatch the key.
What's there to say? She was my sun, my moon, my stars. I was never one to really appreciate nature until I met her.\n\nI guess that's one of the benefits of having a Bosmer wife.

Well, they're not just rumors of course. The Bosmer do eat people. She didn't have a taste for it, though. \n\nThat's part of how she ended up here. So I guess I'm grateful for that practice. We always joked about it, too.

Oh, that was a long time ago now, but they didn't much care for it. My mother never spoke to me again, and my father never let a day go by without expressing his disapproval.\n\nThe townsfolk were slow to accept her, but over the years, they did.
Natural causes. She just woke up one morning and she was dead. She always said, "We aren't young saplings anymore." She was right.\n\nI thought I'd go first, though, her being a Wood Elf and all.
Thank you! Here, here's the ring. Take it to Jorald and set us free!
Then I'll do it without you! Nothing can keep Raerana and I apart!
It's been so long since I felt this joy. It feels like … hope.
No, not in this one. This little cave's my haven. My refuge.\n\nSaving Falinesti is my pilgrimage, but everytime I move forward, something pushes back. And yet, I'm sure I can save the Walking City.
He's a proud Redguard warrior, one of our best, and a follower of Stendarr. Merric's full title is "Resolute War Horn." He's sworn to fight the spawn of Oblivion wherever they touch Tamriel.
Proof that the guild accepts all kinds. A Khajiit. She does as much damage with her wicked tongue as with her curved blade.\n\nTaciturn, rude sometimes. But a cunning fighter.

I've been on the receiving end of Raston's vaunted charms a time or two. I'm not surprised he managed to offend every woman in the Vale.\n\nI wonder if the Farseer would consider another option. I don't wish Raston ill, but I have an idea.
Everyone wins. \n\nRaston doesn't end up as snake food, I gain prestige among the Hlaalu, and the Mabrigash can limit the amount of influence the outside world places on the Vale.

They let Raston live, as long as he promises never to speak of the Vale or return here. \n\nThen they sign a trade agreement with me. They deal with me and I keep other Hlaalu traders away. It's a mutually beneficial arrangement.

The Ironhand ogres were making a drive to attack Wayrest. We fell in their path. They ate all our livestock and broke the levees.\n\nThen General Godrun and his Orcs drove the ogres back, but these looting bandits came in right after.

They're just a ragged group of looters and scavengers as far as I can tell, though I guess they are a little more organized than I would've expected.\n\nDro-Dara or one of my other companions may know more.

Well, they either drowned when the ogres broke the levees, or they fled, or the bandits have probably killed them now.\n\nI didn't see anyone left when I was sneaking away, except my companions, and the bandits have them tied up.
I guess our team does sound a bit quaint these days, doesn't it?\n\nDro-Dara first suggested we retire about twenty years ago, but it was ten years later before we actually settled down here.

This cave system. It links directly to the sewers beneath Mournhold. Well, to part of them. The sewers are more extensive than you'd think.\n\nThat's why I couldn't find the Maulborn! They can move through these tunnels without being noticed.
That's not relevant right now, hero. Stay focused! Find the Maulborn and figure out what they're up to. Then we can talk about my sordid yet extremely intriguing past.

Protections were placed down here to hide people. People with blood on their hands. People like … me.\n\nIf they found a way to activate the Daedric wards again, then the Maulborn have a virtual hidden highway to use against us.

Bet you're surprised I'm a Redguard. Well, I've been the lighthouse keeper for more than twenty years.\n\nThese invaders killed innocents. There's no honor in that. They soil the name "Ra Gada" when they use it this way. I spit on their bones!

I'll find someone to answer that question, once I've reclaimed my armor and blade.\n\nMeanwhile, I must beg a favor. Board our ship and destroy a document of greatest import. It cannot fall into Maormer hands.

A Thalmor fleet manifest. It details who, what, where, and when the entire Thalmor fleet moves. Its value to pirate scum such as these Maormer is self-evident.\n\nThe manifest must not fall into their hands. It must be burned.

Nonsense! I take pleasure in rewarding those who serve my will. May this lantern provide you light in even the darkest situations.\n\nBut I sense something troubles you. Tell me. Fear not to speak your mind in my divine presence.
She has shared those feelings many times over the years. \n\nAfter the events of the last few days, Dro-Dara thinks she might be right. Perhaps retirement is just a bad idea.

Dro-Dara is old, and working a farm is hard, especially if starting over. Like Janne, Dro-Dara also misses life of adventure.  \n\nIf you can convince Knarstygg and Murk-Watcher to leave, this is what Dro-Dara would prefer.
Of course. Janne will always be a good friend. Still has wildness in her blood though. Dro-Dara understands that she needs to roam some.\n\nPerhaps she will join us when her legs grow weary.

Yes. This one was a member of the Mages Guild in good standing for many years. Was tired of casting spells though.\n\nDro-Dara wanted to settle down and rest, but maybe that just wasn't the fate Riddle'Thar has seen for him.

Worm cult. Daedra-worshiping scum. They assemble anchor sites, assassinate leaders, corrupt the young. \n\nEnsorcelled by Molag Bal's dark words. A fate will befall them worse than death, I can tell you.
I hear and obey Stendarr's call. I crack heads for him in faith. I crack heads for the Guild on contracts.\n\nSometimes I do both at once, when a joyful chance presents itself.
Tevynni spoke with Iru-Ahan and made that same suggestion. A sly ploy. Clever. I admire that.\n\nI would be willing to deal with a smart woman who respects and understands our ways.
Yes. I fear the Arch-Wizard uses the <<1>> to strip victims of their memories.\n\nIf that's so, we must destroy the <<1>> before the captain succumbs to its effects.
My blades are at your disposal. Lead on.
Shazah will tell you what she can. This one and her sister arrived just a few days ago. We came to Grimwatch on news of the Colovian invasion from the north. A siege sat at the fort's front gate.

Indeed. We had just begun to push back against the invaders when a dark spot appeared in the sky. The Mane! Shazah and her sister have known Akkhuz-ri for years. He pulsed with dark energies and spoke in a profane voice.

They're alive. What a relief! I saw them dead. Broken. Everything undone. That wizard tormented me with such horrible visions!\n\nBut they're safe, thanks to you. Please, lead the way out of this place. I'll follow … albeit slowly.

There is a way. An incantation—the crocodile song. I was never taught it, but I have known it my whole life.\n\nOne song must end for another to begin. There is an old crocodile here. Ripplestrike. With his heart, I can sing the song.
The Wisewomen won't speak to you. They've had their fill of male outsiders for the moment. \n\nMaybe the Gulakhan will answer your questions. Maybe.
The Wisewomen may be willing to talk to a female outsider.\n\nBut the Gulakhan is probably the better choice to answer your questions.

Thank you. The river has truly guided you here for this purpose. \n\nTake this charm. Place it near Ripplestrike's nest. He will not be able to resist the call. He will come out, and then you can kill him.
Which do you mean? The gear? Or the relic?

Ancient. Dwemer. Worn in places, this piece was used in one of their constructs. Smells … fresh in some ways. Has been away from any ruins for a while. Shame. Might have been able to learn something more.
Crude construction, shaped by small fingers. Female Breton … perhaps Wood Elf. Colored from clay. This region, so more likely Breton. Smells burnt, of cinders. Shaped near a wood-fire stove or kiln.
Aelif makes her way as she can, helps the Guild as she can. Just a humble Khajiit. Originally from the city of Dune. \n\nThis one is of little importance.

How should I know? I'm an honest merchant! I just wanted to set up a little trade agreement with the tribe. They make some gold, we make some gold, everybody wins.\n\nNext thing I know, they tie me up and act like I committed some crime.

I was soaking up the local flavor, if you know what I mean. These Mabrigash ladies are lovely! But my flirting made that witch Bodani mad.\n\nBesides, they refuse to let me speak to the man in charge. Why are they being this way?
Well, I … I did ask the Farseer to summon her boss and get me a glass of shein. But I asked nicely and everything!\n\nDon't let them feed me to the snake! I didn't do anything wrong.
Take this to siphon away the energy trapping <<c:1>>. Only then will her bonds be broken.\n\n<<2>> will be at the main arena's entrance. Tell her I understand. Tell her, she was right.

The vision I had was strong. Your choices determine the fate of merchant and Mabrigash alike. But you must speak to the Ghost Snake.\n\nThe Coiled Path begins just outside the village. But know that the Serpentbound will block your way.
The three folks I need are Crafty Lerisa, Jakarn, and Neramo. Any or all of them would do.

She's an old friend, captain of the Maiden's Breath. She's also a master of disguise. We can use that.\n\nThe Sea Drakes used their lighthouse tricks to run her ship aground near Saintsport. Rescue her, and she might join us.
You won't spot her. She stays well hidden. Your best bet is to look for her monkey, Howler. They're never far apart. \n\nFind that monkey, and you'll find Lerisa.
He's a thief, but he's the best there is. He'd be a big help in the heist I have planned.\n\nProblem is, he robbed Bhosek. Nobody robs Bhosek. He's been tossed into the Grave, under Bhosek's palace.

There's an entrance off the river, under the palace. Watch out for traps and the other prisoners. They're all murderers down there, the worst scum on the island.\n\nThat's the Grave. You can leave any time you want, if you can get out alive.

Neramo's nice enough for an Altmer, if you get past his Dwemer fixation.\n\nThing is, the relics he finds in Dwemer ruins sometimes come in very handy. He just might have a device we can use for our heist.
There's a Dwemer ruin outside town—Bthzark. Neramo went there to dig up relics. Help him find some and he might just join us.
Bloody Bhosek, or Headman Bhosek, as he calls himself now. He took over the palace years ago. Killed the old ruler and took his place.
Captain Helane, but she's worse than Bhosek. Her Sea Drakes run <<1>> south of here. Biggest band of murderers on the seas.\n\nBhosek and Helane tolerate each other. Neither's ready for a war, yet.
The Screaming Mermaid's just up the road, and they've always got good rum. Just keep a grip on your coinpurse, or you'll be a beggar by day's end.

Bhosek's thugs, the Bloody Fists. Cross one, you cross them all, and Bhosek will have your head on a pike faster than you can say, "Please don't put my head on a pike!"\n\nAlso, the Sea Drakes will gut you if you enter Saintsport.

Deserted, the traitors. See, there's a fortune to be made from Breton galleons. Thing is, King Fahara'jad called for an end to it, now that we're all part of the Daggerfall Covenant.\n\nOf course, as a loyal Redguard, I obeyed.

If by "disagreed" you mean "tried to kill us" then yes. Bunch of bloody mutineers.\n\nLambur, myself, and a few others ran them off the ship, but word spread. No one here wants to sail with a captain who won't raid Bretons.
The size of the task. Our benefactor has asked we call in every guildmate, from the lowest associate on up. \n\nEvery member of the Fighters Guild has been tasked with ending this Daedric corruption.

I heard that the Farseer calls the shots, but Raston dismissed the notion. He wants an exclusive deal for the beautiful leathers the Mabrigash make and he may have overstepped.\n\nRaston was speaking to Gulakhan Harrinat the last time I saw him.

Who knows how these places get their names. Ithrini said she heard that the Ghost Snake was Sithis. Nonsense, if you ask me. \n\nAll I know is that I saw big snakes near the swamps. They looked very real to me, not ghostly.
I don't know anything but the name. I overheard it as they marched me through their camp, that's all. <<1>>, and Mauloch.

Simply put, war paint. There's a spring or something inside the ruin filled with red water and mud. The original inhabitants believed Mauloch gave it to them so they'd be strong.\n\nIt's a myth. A legend. But what if there's something to it after all?
Another male. And an outsider, as well. Wonderful.\n\nMaybe the Gulakhan will answer your questions. I certainly won't.
Be careful here, friend. Even though you are female, you don't understand our ways. \n\nI'd avoid the Wisewomen, if I were you. Try the Gulakhan. He may be willing to answer your questions.
Of course. After-action report, yes? Wise choice.

That thought also occurred to me. You think strategically, and I can appreciate that.\n\nThe trader insulted the Farseer and her anger may bring more unwanted attention to the Vale. Talk to wise woman Iru-Ahan. She might be willing to help you.
If you must.
We do not make up stories just to scare away outsiders. This Vale is an ancient place and not kind to those who do not dwell here. The Mabrigash have been here for many generations.

That ignorant outsider. He managed to insult our women and anger the Farseer. She will send him to serve the Ghost Snake for his insults.\n\nThe Mabrigash do not welcome outsiders, but we will treat them with courtesy if they respect our ways.
We don't make up stories just to frighten outsiders. This Vale is an ancient place, protected by an ancient entity. \n\nThe Mabrigash have served that entity for many generations.
If you must.

That ignorant outsider! Let's just say that he mocked us and made the Farseer very angry. He will serve the Ghost Snake. The Farseer will make sure of that.\n\nWe do not welcome outsiders, but we treat them with courtesy if they respect our ways.
Sneak up on you? It's what I do. Now, answer my question. What are you doing here?

How charming. The Maiden's wrecked on the sandy shore. As for Crafty Lerisa, you've found her. Just in time, too.\n\nCaptain Helane's Sea Drakes have my crew. I won't leave without them. Help me rescue them, and I'll owe you a favor.

We're going to disguise my crew as Sea Drakes. Take these clothes. Look for a portly Breton, a sour Redguard, and a big Orc. The Drakes are keeping them in the large buildings.\n\nOnce they're out, meet me by Helane's ship.
It all happened so quickly. I don't … <<1>> came at us in a rage. He screamed that we were unworthy to pray at Mauloch's shrine. Then he drew his weapon ….\n\n<<2>>, my love! You have to help him!
They were still in Mauloch's shrine when I ran away. I think <<1>> was stabbed by the shaman!\n\nHave mercy, Z'en! Don't let us be parted like this!
Jofnir? His passage down the river called me to this post. What did he say?
Not long. Aelif told me you found some trinkets with the cultists. Between those baubles and the notes you found, hopefully we'll have a start for the translation effort.
Interesting. I'll get in touch with some of our sisters in the Mages Guild, see if they can investigate this apparition. \n\nI try to avoid the walking dead, when I can.

The lure of revenge over petty slights and the demands of an arranged marriage, shaped the rage within my despair. The Cult's agents nurtured my anger and drew me in.\n\nI hate what I became. What I did.
Yes, yes. You sound like my mother, beloved though she is. I shall recover.\n\nRejoice, for some day soon you and I shall again take up arms together.

In the eyes of Z'en, all love is welcome. But worshipers of Mauloch, like <<1>>, feel Orcs should keep to themselves and not consort with other races.\n\nMy dear <<2>> must still be with <<1>>. I fear for his life. Please, help him!

They're rabid beasts who sing praises to the Blood of Mauloch. Legend says there is a cave somewhere in Malabal Tor where the blood flows like water.\n\n<<1>> claims to lead his people to that "promised land." He's nothing more than a tyrant.

Nothing in magic is certain, but necromancy, despite its bad reputation, is generally predictable. \n\nAt the same time, the dead of Aphren's Hold might have more solidarity. Use at your own risk, I suppose.
Thank the Eight! I thought I'd die in here!\n\nHelane came by not long ago. Told me to look forward to a public flaying. Then she beat me bloody, laughing the whole time. She's one cold witch.

Honestly, that was a surprise. I was told it was a quiet place.\n\nI presume it was the Supernal Dreamers who disturbed the dead. Perhaps because they sought the sword, or perhaps they were only trespassing. Either way, they're all dead.

There are no specific records of what occurred here, only vague references.\n\nKing Aphren allegedly spent all his time at war. While he was away, his enemies apparently attacked Aphren's Hold and killed everyone. The king himself died soon after.

King Aphren's Sword was sacred. He never let anyone else touch it. \n\nWe don't know how it was shattered or even if it really has magical properties. It certainly sounds like it's worth studying though.
I knew she wouldn't leave me to rot! Quick, untie me!\n\nThe Sea Drakes spent the past few hours breaking my fingers. I can't wield a sword, but I can still strangle a few on my way out.

My friends, gone. My daughter, missing. What is left for me? I've nothing left, except rage and grief. \n\n<<1>> must pay for this massacre. She must die. Blood for blood. Payment in kind. Such is Z'en's will.

It's the only path left to me. She must've taken my daughter. So, she must die.\n\n<<1>> will be in her longhouse above the shrine to Mauloch. When she is dead, find me in the Shrine of Z'en, across the stream. I must pray for guidance.
Ha. Another of Helane's tricks? Let me go, then chase me down and beat me within an inch of my life?\n\nI'll chance it and make a run for <<1>>. See how far I get.

A passing merchant told me she saw a Khajiit near the Dra'bul wayshrine. But <<1>> ran off from here. I don't want to go too far away in case he returns.\n\nIf he returns. He'd better return, or I'll kill him.
Almost done then. Everyone's out except my first mate, Deregor. They've got him in the belly of Helane's ship.\n\nYou'll find the keys below deck. Look for Deregor down in back.
I'll be visiting Helane in her cabin, to thank her for the hospitality she's extended my crew.\n\nCome on up after you release Deregor. You should really say hello.
Her cabin girl had a key. Poor little Bosmer lass, barely any meat on her bones. I think Helane was starving her.\n\nShe's on her way to <<1>> now and I'm one key richer.
Good trick that. Did I really disguise myself as a fern? Or did you see a fern because you weren't looking close enough?
We keep it out of their hands!\n\nAnd now we've got to find the runestone, too. The shaman used it and the book together.
Ah, yes, my precious sword. To wield it again would feel so good. I should never have shattered it. I must make it whole again. I must.\n\nWhy do you have these? What did you want with them?
You insolent, unworthy whelp … how dare you? \n\nTell me—what do you want? I'll give you anything, just to hold it for one moment. You need me. You need me to restore it.
The dead do not lie so easily as the living. Yes, you can trust me. Give it to me and I'll restore it.\n\nAnything, anything just to hold it again.
Oh … oh yes! Thank you! It's been so long. \n\nI never should have shattered the sword. It was a mistake.
Yes. Yes. Of course. I have haunted these halls for centuries, hoping I might wield this weapon once more.\n\nThere. The sword is whole again. It feels … it feels wrong though. All wrong.
It matters not. All that matters now is that I might restore it and hold it once again.\n\nThere. The sword is whole again. It feels … it feels wrong though. All wrong.

I did. Since the day I discovered what had happened, all I wanted was to beg her forgiveness … even more than I wanted this damn sword.\n\nPerhaps now, though … perhaps I can make amends. Perhaps I can show her how sorry I am.

Regret. The sword was my favorite possession, my best friend, and with it, I subjugated these lands.\n\nBut in the process, I left my family unprotected. My sweet little girl … was killed. I couldn't live with it. I shattered the blade in my grief.

Because … because it was my obsession with this weapon, and the war I waged with it, that ruined all that I loved. \n\nMy sweet … my sweet daughter. While I fought to subjugate my neighbors, I left her here. They killed her, but it was my fault.
Mira? You saw my … my Mira? My poor, sweet child. I wronged her so.\n\nI worried that her spirit would not rest. I wanted to seek her out. I have been unable to enter her tomb though.

Yeah? Ha! I knew she got away! Helane said she was being keelhauled and beaten, but I knew better. They don't call my captain crafty for nothing.\n\nGet me out of these ropes and let's get out of here!

I—I cannot force you. Perhaps I don't even deserve an opportunity to make amends. \n\nTake it. Whatever you do with it, just take it away from here. My daughter's tomb is just down the corridor. Just … please consider it.
Yes. Please do. Here, take it.\n\nPerhaps it will allow her to rest. Perhaps it will allow me to rest.
You can help me. You can show her. You can tell her how sorry I am.\n\nIf she sees the sword, she will …. maybe she will understand. Please. I beg you. Give my daughter the sword.

Sounds crazy, but Feluz is so full of life. We met in Daggerfall. He ran an exotic goods store. Our love for the unknown is what drew us together.\n\nHe promised to show me the world; I'd never been outside Glenumbra. And now … I hope we find him.

Its beautiful forests. And to visit the fabled Deepwoods. Have you been there? I've heard all its ladies are green!\n\nPlus, <<1>> has friends at the <<2>>. We'll set up a shop. Imports from Wayrest, or something.

There are two Daedric shrines within Jathsogur. We found the book at this one, so I bet the runestone is at the other.\n\nThe second shrine is on the other side of their fortress. They wouldn't want to make it easy for anyone to recover both items.
We can't stay out in the open, and the longhouse we were being held in is probably teeming with Drublog.\n\nThere was another longhouse south of that one. Maybe we could try going there?

Well, he has white fur and scares easily. I've known him to hide behind fallen trees, rocks, and even under mushrooms.\n\nHe also loves to jump and climb on things. He's pure cat, through and through.
Me? Did I do that? Her starving little cabin girl may have poisoned her drink. Who can say?\n\nDid Deregor get out?
I'll just be going then. I told my crew to gather on the beach. I'm going to make sure they all made it out.\n\nMeet me there and we'll square up.
Oh, it's jarrin root. A very nasty local poison. It won't kill her, not right away.\n\nIt starts by dissolving the stomach lining, then goes from there.
I'd love to stay and watch, but no time. You can stay if you like.\n\nIt's actually her poison. Kept for slaves who disobey. There's an antidote on the dresser, if your heart bleeds enough.
I'd feel mildly disappointed, but I leave it up to you. Meet me on the beach once you're done here and we'll settle up.\n\nJust watch your boots. She'll start vomiting soon.
<Her struggles ease as the antidote quickly takes effect. She will likely live.>
I figure, if you want something kept safe, give it to the Goblins.\n\nThey'll watch it for free, they're too stupid to trade it, and they'll kill anyone who tries to take it.
Here's the thing. You went through a lot of trouble to free me, right? There's no way you'll let me get eaten by Goblins. So you, my good friend, will follow me to their mine. Yeah?

I'll kill the Goblins in the scaffolding in the next room. You grab the gem. It's in a chest on the floor. \n\nThere's a passage on the far side. Take that and meet me outside. If something goes wrong, regroup at the inn in town.
The crystals around the door are activated by three welkynd stones in the ruins. I think I can handle one of them, but you'll need to deal with the other two.
No. If his spirit cannot rest without my forgiveness then all the better.\n\nLet him share my fate, and know true loneliness.

Thank you. This… his connection to the sword is so strong, I can sense his energy.\n\nI remember… there was a time when I was a little girl, and he made me feel safe. I could at least speak to him, I suppose.
Then why have you come here? To mock my pain?\n\nThe living have no concept of how the restless dead suffer. Begone then.

His sword? His most prized possession? His most sacred treasure? He never even let anyone touch it….\n\nIs this how he hopes to find redemption? Give it to me. I would like nothing more than to destroy it.
Hmm. It doesn't feel especially magical. \n\nNonetheless, this is what I was sent here to reclaim, and you have aided me in this cause. The Mages Guild thanks you.
Oh … so this is how the king has asked you to make his amends?\n\nYou can't be serious. The king deserves no such favors, and that sword belongs back in Wayrest. Please … you can't do this!

Ha! I presume she was among those killed when the king was out conquering his neighbors? \n\nFunny how a restless afterlife can change the hearts of the dead. Doubtless, he deserves no such redemption. May I have the sword now?

Go, then! There is nothing left for me. Nothing left but burning hatred. I can feel it in my veins!\n\nIf Z'en will not give me justice, then I offer my blood to Mauloch! I offer my body and soul to his bloody vengeance!

It is clear Z'en has abandoned us. For my piety, Z'en allowed my family and friends to be murdered! Tell me, how is that payment in kind?\n\nI curse the Drublog clan until the end of time. They will find no rest, no solace, no peace!
No! My flesh and blood, stolen from me by those twice-cursed fiends!\n\nZ'en, this is too much! I beg you, don't give me this burden to bear as well! Curse <<1>>! Curse them all!

My daughter only ever wanted peace. Perhaps the chief's son did, too. But their blood has forever stained these lands. There's no going back.\n\nIf I don't stop the Drublog, the suffering will continue. The curse is the only way to end this.

Don't speak to me of sacrifice! <<1>> was a Drublog, same as the rest! I told her no love could live between the Drublog and our people. And now, she has paid the price.\n\nThe Drublog know only blood, and blood they shall have!
Many a captain who sails these waters will be glad of that news! Now, let's talk favors. I owe you a big one.

Well, your choice. I hope the next crew she shipwrecks and murders appreciates your soft heart.\n\nThe important thing is she knows I had her. She won't cross me again. Now, about our debt. What do I owe you?
Many a captain who sails these waters will be glad of that news! Now, let's talk favors. I owe you a big one.

Well, your choice. I hope the next crew she shipwrecks and murders appreciates your soft heart.\n\nThe important thing is she knows I had her. She won't cross me again. Now, about our debt. What do I owe you?
Jakarn. He's a liar and a thief. He stole a gem from Headman Bhosek.\n\nNow, if the gem came back, Bhosek might let him live. Can you help me, or not?
I knew you were a smart one. Smarter than Jakarn. You just saved his life.\n\nIf you see him again, tell him to leave this island and never come back.
Now that's just too bad. If you do run into him again, tell him that if we catch him, he's dead.
Well that's a shame. Still, getting <<1>> off my trail is a good trade. She's relentless.\n\nI'll be honest. I'm just a little hurt. But since you saved my life, we'll call it even.
Well that's a shame. Still, getting <<1>> off my trail is a good trade. She's relentless.\n\nI'll be honest. I'm just a little hurt. But since you saved my life, we'll call it even.
Hey, now. The headman stole it first. And you brought it back to me, didn't you?\n\nThanks, good-looking.
Hey, now. The headman stole it first. And you brought it back to me, didn't you?\n\nThanks, good-looking.
I know you're only trying to help … I'll answer what I can, but please keep it short.
Well, sometimes. But I deserved it. I'd talk back to him or I'd be gone for hours with Rilyn. I was a bad daughter and now he's gone forever!
What? Where did you hear that? Certainly not - Eislef loved me!
Well, she did spend more money than she should. They would argue about it sometimes. But so what? Eislef drank too much. Does that mean the barkeep in Riften is a suspect?
I already said "no," didn't I? Rilyn loves me and would never hurt my parents!
No, of course not! How can you ask me that? Our family had problems - all families do - and Rilyn knew about them, but he'd never do anything like that!
