What are you saying, that if she did she deserved to die? How does that matter? How my parents spent their money is no business of yours!
No, of course not! How can you ask me that? Our family had problems—all families do—and Rilyn knew about them, but he'd never do anything like that!
What? Where did you hear that? He drank, sure. All of us do!
What are you saying, that if she did she deserved to die? How does that matter? How my parents spent their money is no business of yours!
Well, she did spend more money than she should. Can't say on what. They would argue about it sometimes. But so what? Eislef drank too much. Does that mean the barkeep in Riften is a suspect?
So what if he did? I deserved it. I'd talk back to him or I'd be gone for hours with Rilyn.\n\nWhy does it matter? I loved him and now he's gone forever!
This was a Breton island, hundreds of years ago. War Chief Yzzgol and the Seamount Orcs wiped them out.\n\nThe Seamounts were the fiercest raiders on the sea, until we settled here.
Steel and stone, how can you ask? High, defensible cliffs, a view of all approaches from the fortress, fertile land for crops—what's not to like? Yzzgol's wives insisted we settle here, so we did.
My orders are to watch them until they try to break out or until Chief Tazgol gets here and cuts off their heads. That's all.\n\nAn Orc follows orders, even if they're stupid.

We're not savages. We respect the enemy's dead.\n\nWhen an Orc dies, he gets a cairn to mark where he fell, weapons atop it. We don't stick our dead in the ground like Bretons. Even so, we won't desecrate their graves.
<Applying the grease did the job. The lever finally turns.>
Take the Staff of Arkay, a potent weapon against undead. You must first charge the staff, then use it to destroy the foul abominations summoned by these necromancers.
The blasphemers employ dark magic to raise the dead. Disrupt their rituals and release that energy. The Staff of Arkay will convert this into power to destroy their dark creations!
In life, I was a priestess of Arkay. I served King Renwic for many years. I was with him when the Seamount Orcs invaded. We died together at their hands.
<The lever still won't budge. You need to apply more alit grease.>
Many died under their blades. But that was long ago. The Bloodthorn Cultists desecrate our graves today. I beg you to stop them.

Even in death I watch over my people. Necromancy is a crime against Arkay. The aura of corruption builds as my countrymen's bodies are raised and desecrated by these minions of the Worm.\n\nI need your help to stop them.
The Bloodthorn Cult's necromancy corrupts nature. They're led by Reachmen of the worst sort, allies of Mannimarco.\n\nThey raise our dead to assault the Orcs. This desecration must end!

Bright moons be praised! The fire barrier into the temple! My sister Khali led some of the remaining soldiers down into the temple below the fort. She was cut off when a barrier of dark flame went up.

Tell the king to be on guard for any suspicious news coming from Gavaudon.

Perhaps he already has some idea of how Vaermina seeks to sow chaos in the region. 

It may even be that the Ironhand ogres' aggression is somehow related.

The staff will reveal circles of corruption among the crypts. There lurk the Bloodthorn Cult's abominations, hidden in pockets of Oblivion.\n\nPlant the staff in a circle to draw an abomination into our world. Then destroy it!

No, they can't be. Maybe a splinter group or something. I don't know what to think. Not all of us exactly see eye to eye on our current situation, but to join up with the Maulborn?\n\nThat's just idiotic.
Do what you do best. Rush in swinging weapons and tossing magic around like there's no tomorrow!\n\nIf you find whoever activated the wards, get them to tell you what's going on down here.
I suppose anyone with knowledge of the Daedric arts might be able to activate them. I'm not an expert on magic, you know.\n\nI need to warn somebody. Varon needs to know about this.

I know you will. That's why I ran into you on your way to the Temple. I'll drop the Ordinators an anonymous tip. Maybe even get word to your beloved goddess. Hopefully someone'll show up to give you a hand.\n\nJust don't die on me, hero. Got that?
And if I did? Are you going to drag me out of here and into some other old ruin where my talents will be forced once again?\n\nI'm getting really tired of this.
And if I did? Are you going to drag me out of here and into some other old ruin where my talents will be forced once again?\n\nI'm getting really tired of this.
And if I did? Are you going to drag me out of here and into some other old ruin where my talents will be forced once again?\n\nI'm getting really tired of this.

Just exploring the island. I came across these fine fellows disturbing the graves and decided to kill a few.\n\nI've collected some robes in this bag. Take one if you want the zombies to leave you alone.
I'll be hunting cultists while you're playing with your staff. If I find any more robes, I'll leave them for you. \n\nThese necromancers are disgusting, but they do dress well.

I overheard cultists talking about a portal. The relic that's causing all the trouble is in there.\n\nI lifted a uniform off a cultist who no longer needed it; it's waiting in the bag. Might help you get past some of the ones I left alive.
If we had a way to focus that energy, it might break the seal.
Helping you out, as always. Follow me; I know a shortcut.

It's a ritual focus. The Drublog used it against <<c:1>>.\n\nRemember I said they drained his energy into crystals? The runestone is the conduit. With it, we can reverse the ritual and give back the energy!
Good. Try it on the door.
<It appears that the stone slab here might be able to open, if you can find the switch that operates it.>
My wife? She isn't dead? Thank Riddle'Thar!\n\nOh … but she will never forgive me. Never. She said as much last time. How wretched is <<1>> now?

Khali … does not think so. The barrier here seems much stronger. And she senses—moons, that is strange. This one senses a dark energy powering the ward on this door. We'll have to open the door from the other side.
There's a ruined doorway on the south wall. This one bets we could slip through.\n\nIf my suspicions are right, whatever is beyond this door is powering the barriers.

Two things. First, once I've recovered my strength, I'm going to fight my way out of here. That should draw the attention of at least some of the Drublog.\n\nSecond, I can give you my totem spirit. It will aid you in battle.

I can use my visions to get out of Jathsogur, so you don't have to worry about me.\n\nI've also recovered enough energy to invoke my spirit totem. It will follow you until you leave Jathsogur, aiding you as it can.

The motivations of Daedric Princes are often a mystery. \n\nWhatever her ultimate plans may be, it's clear that in involves destablizing Stormhaven and perhaps destroying the Daggerfall Covenant as a whole.

I will go directly to Shinji's Scarp. That is the front line in the battle against the ogres. \n\nI hope there to learn more about what's befallen Azura's shrine in Gavaudon, and perhaps I can look for signs of Vaermina's Omen at work.

The Ironhand ogres have plagued southern Wrothgar for years, but lately, they've turned toward Stormhaven,\n\nThe ogres seem more organized than they've been before, but it is impossible to know if Vaermina is involved in any way.

Well. There we go then. That wasn't quite so bad as Abbot Durak made it sound. I'm sure he had his reasons though. \n\nWhat about the Daedra, the "Omen" that was behind all this? I trust it's dead, or gone?

Well that's good at least. You two are the experts, though I suppose that's a dubious honor.\n\nIf there is an Omen in Gavaudon, I'm guessing it's similarly disguised? Godrun didn't report anything suspicious but maybe it's worth asking Captain Ernele.

In Gavaudon? Why couldn't it be in Morrowind or somewhere else across the continent?\n\nGods. We already have enough trouble in Gavaudon. General Godrun says the Ironhand ogres are far from being fully defeated.

He's the best damn general in the Daggerfall Covenant, if you ask me, and he's a good friend.\n\nHis army came to our defense against the Ironhand ogres. They've fought hard, but the battle's not over. Godrun's headed back to Shinji's Scarp even now.

Yes. Ernele was fighting with Godrun, but he's just been reassigned to shore up our defenses here in Wayrest.\n\nIt may be a wild guar chase, but it's worth asking Ernele if he saw any signs of Daedric influence in Gavaudon.

No, no. Just … lots of rumors about the council investigation. The old guard thinks Sees-All-Colors would have had a lot to gain from Jofnir's death. And from what I've heard, she's not at the meeting.

Well, you know as well as anyone else. These Supernal Dreamers have been trying to recruit people all over Stormhaven.\n\nWe're hoping this will serve as a deterrent. If we catch a cultist, we'll execute him. Nothing more than that.

I came to Mournhold a few weeks ago. To visit some friends. I guess word got out that a Telvanni was in the city because I suddenly found myself tied up in the sewers.\n\nThe Maulborn. They kept badgering me about Daedric magic.

I only know what I heard. I think they were planning an attack of some sort. They sent off a large group just before you showed up.\n\nI told all of this to the Sacred Lady. She said you would visit me and I should tell you to find an Ordinator.

Members of House Telvanni are known for their knowledge of all types of magic. I guess they assumed I could make the old wards active again.\n\nI did what they wanted. Eventually. It was either that or … I don't want to think about it.
Indeed. The Sacred Lady wants you to know that she wasn't able to eliminate all of the pests you found in the sewers.

Not that I know of. General Godrun's been losing sleep, worried about the ogres, but other than that, everyone's been sleeping just fine … or at least as well as you can expect for a war camp.\n\nGeneral Godrun is acting a little strange though.
Really? I heard there was a woman who joined the cult in Alcaire and tried to murder her husband.\n\nWe don't look too kindly on that. You didn't come here to talk about politics though, did you?

Sure enough. I was acting liaison to General Godrun out at Shinji's Scarp, but he's worried that the ogres might break through and attack Wayrest. \n\nGodrun suggested to the king that I be assigned to organize defenses here, so here I am.
It sounds like <<1>> and the others have made it inside. Our task is not yet complete. <<2>> senses an even stronger source ahead.\n\nPlease, speak with <<1>>. She'll know what to do.
If I felt like fighting, I'd fight. But I feel like fishing today, if it's all the same to you.\n\nI'm sure there's plenty other Drublog that'll indulge you, if you want to fight.

Wood Orcs, of course! But you knew that.\n\nWe're the biggest tribe in Malabal Tor. Some, especially <<1>>, think we shoulda been asked to join the Aldmeri Dominion, but I'd just as soon be left alone. Still, it's caused trouble. There'll be fighting.
All Drublog like to fight! We do it to prove ourselves. The strongest must always show their strength!\n\nBut I've proven myself enough. I don't care what <<1>> wants us to do, I'm gonna fish today!
Between you and me, I really don't think so. \n\nGeneral Godrun has done a good job. The orcs have driven the ogres almost back into the mountains. Morale at Shinji's Scarp is quite high.
It's not my place to question the general, but he does seem to be blowing the ogre threat out of proportion.\n\nThat's just my two coppers, though. Good luck if you're headed out to Gavaudon.
I sense the source of this corruption is beyond the door up ahead. There's sure to be some kind of defense. Between the three of us, I'm sure we can see it done.
One of us should stay behind to hold the door. <<1>> suspects this silence is merely the calm before the storm. The 'mathra are gathering in the shadows. I can smell them.

You seen Elves runnin' around? The chief's been working with them for a few weeks, getting involved in politics or something. Only gonna end bad, if you ask me.\n\nAnd you did ask me. Now, go away so I can catch my dinner!

Quiet! You'll scare the fish.\n\nHe's the Drublog's chieftain, of course. But he wants more. I think he wants to rule all the Wood Orcs of Malabal Tor and he's not afraid of getting outside help. Not the Drublog way, I think, but I'm just a fisherman.

I remember … dancing with the pigs! And then … a long slide down the hill, past the gaping mouth, and splash! Water everywhere!\n\nThere … and there! Mouths in the vines! Clutching at me! <<1>> crying, so far away. I thought they killed her.
Such a kind traveler! <<1>> would not be so kind to <<2>>!\n\nAlso, I crave your help. If you happen to find my lucky pouch, fortune will smile upon you.
No! I can't face her. My bag of goods is gone! Without it, we can't set up shop. No shop, no gold. No home.\n\nI should stay in this tree stump. <<1>> would tell me so.
Moon-sugar candy. But don't worry! I've learned my lesson.\n\nThe candy will fetch a good price at <<1>>, trust me. I have friends there.
Our gods both demand payment in kind. Of course, that means each demand retribution against the other.\n\nIn the valley, it has always been paid in blood.
With the souls restored and crystals relit, the key crystal should now be visible.\n\nThis is the key to Prince Maleel's tomb. You must use it in order to gain entry.
Anything out of place, anything connected with a place or a person. We thought his death just the touch of chance, so we did not know to search. Anything might be a clue.
My wife can't disown me now! Look, my dear, our friend found our goods!\n\nAnd, um, you have my lucky pouch … yes?
Thanks for bringing me the bucket!

Camping. That's funny. Well, if you didn't know, there's trouble in Alcaire Castle—the Bretons and the Redguards aren't getting along.\n\nThe Fighters Guild can't be seen taking sides in their squabble.

It shows we're neutral. Stay inside at the inn and the Redguards will suspect we're helping the Duke. Stay at the Redguard camp and we look no better to the Bretons.\n\nAh, a few nights under the stars won't hurt. This will blow over in no time.
He's the chief's son. I told him of my father's worries, but he said he would talk sense into his mother.\n\nWe didn't foresee how far <<1>> would go to turn <<2>> against us.

I'd hoped we would be one day. But <<1>> saw us embracing by the lake a few nights ago. He must have told <<2>>. She flew into a rage.\n\nSince then, all arguments end in bloodshed. Peace has been torn asunder.
I thought the wasps could be useful. I had some success with the process, as you can see by my sweet Chezik here. \n\nBut they are skittish creatures, especially when they reach their full size.
I was saving these. They're rather tasty when roasted and seasoned properly. \n\nSince you're helping us, it would only be fair to give you what I have.
I don't, I'm afraid. But there are plenty of wasps in the field. \n\nI'm sure you'll have no trouble collecting what you need.

We found him in his quarters. The endless sleep. It was very sudden. But at the time, we thought nothing of it. Jofnir was getting old. Sooner or later one of the faster blades would have made him sit down.

Sal's a master escapist, with the proper theater. What's more theatrical than a little smoke and flame?\n\n<<1>> wants to smoke out any Shrikes barricaded in these buildings. Maybe he just wants to set the whole place ablaze. Either works.

No. But it's all I've got right now. And I think you can manage <<1>>'s enthusiasm.\n\nTake this oil. You'll need it to make the smoke. If Sal's nearby, he'll know we've come for him, and he can make a dramatic entrance.
Hush! <<1>> mustn't see. Give it to me, quickly now.\n\nYou've been so kind! Please visit us at <<2>> sometime. But first, speak to my wife. She believes she is the boss in this relationship.
No? I don't believe you. <<1>> saw a glint in your eye.\n\nYou can't trick a trickster. Give me my lucky pouch!
I guess we are content you found our goods. Thank you for that much.\n\nPlease, speak to my wife. She is, uh, not speaking to <<1>> at the moment.

The Mages Guild and the Trade Hall are beyond the forge in the courtyard.\n\nWatch out for the Drublog in the marketplace. They're fighting the Fists of Thalmor and we can't beat them without reinforcements.
None. And slow though he was, he never would have gone to … what was it? \n\nYes, Sovngarde. He never would have gone to Sovngarde without a fight.
<<1>> brought us here to meet the Silvenar and the Green Lady. We're their escorts.\n\nThe captain would know more. Ask her, if she's still alive.

That's the lieutenant's call. I'll do my duty, when I get patched up.\n\nI doubt <<1>> will abandon Velyn Harbor, though. He's serious about his duty. And any militia we can raise will follow him, I guarantee it.

<<1>> was at the docks early this morning to meet the Bosmer dignitaries.\n\nThere wasn't time to sound an alarm, and I don't know if she survived the first attack. Maybe the Fists of Thalmor can avenge her death. If she's dead.

Did he? You can't fly, can you? Sure would make it easier. Failing that, if you're willing to make a run for it, I'll cheer you on … from back here.\n\nOne tip: don't run in a straight line. Zig-zag. Hide behind the rocks and you just might make it.
<<1>> has no choice but to trust you. I guess the bag of goods was too heavy, hmm?\n\nTalk to my wife. I'm sure she'd like to thank you for your help. More than I would, yes?

Z'en, this is too much for one to bear! My daughter Dalaneth … my child! I couldn't find her before I was forced to flee.\n\nSome villagers went to hide amongst the forest. Please, can you find them? They may know where she's gone.
Clan Murtag has a score to settle. Again, it's not your fight. \n\nThe less you know, the better. You'll hear about it soon enough.

As far as King Emeric knows. That's what he requested—wanted his old friend to bring his clan down here to defend Stormhaven.\n\nIt's ironic considering what these people did to Orsinium in years past.
My head aches! To think of the trouble this causes!\n\nThe pigs cannot be too far away. They are on a hill overlooking the water. A pond? A lake?
It was, let me think, yes! A cave, with teeth made of vines.\n\nThe vines! Beware the small vines! Some will turn to teeth, to gnaw on you as they gnawed at <<1>>!
Nightmares? By Mauloch, of course not! I'm an Orc. We dream of blood, glory, conquest. \n\nThe things most people would consider nightmares are sweet dreams to me. No. My sleep is entirely pleasant.

The water begins to clear. Two cities, one worships Meridia. The other Molag Bal. Abagarlas, the city of the dead, creates a relic to strike at the Meridians. Delodiil, city of light, creates their own weapon. Forged around a heart of crystal.
I'm going to crush this pouch the first chance I get. \n\nIf you stop by <<1>>, please come and see us.
"Yes?" That's all you have to say?\n\nMoon-sugar candy got us into this mess in the first place! Even if I take the pouch away, he's probably already hidden a handful of it.
Lucky for him, we know where <<1>> is now. Seems all that smoke got his attention, and he started screaming his head off.\n\nWhat's less clear is how to reach him.

Take a look across the water. <<1>>'s up on that outcropping, about a stone's throw from here. Problem is, the whole place is crawling with Steel Shrikes.\n\nYou're the only one who stands a chance of getting him out of there.

Just so. These Ancient Ones steal into the heart of the enemy with this crystal weapon. They stop the ritual, and their king ends the dark rule of Abagarlas. But they are hunted. So they try to find a haven, a place to hide the crystal.
Sweet Ela! I knew she wouldn't forget about me!\n\nGet me out of these binds, quickly! If I know her, she'll be halfway to the next village before I catch up!
You're right. It's just … he can't control himself sometimes, and it scares me.\n\nI'm sorry. We'll be on our way shortly.
Feluz will eat half that pouch the first chance he gets!\n\nUgh. Just be on your way! Leave me to clean up after this cat.
You have the right of it. They sought to hide their prize … but the priestess of Meridia first gave her life. She relit the crystal heart so that the weapon could one day be forged anew.

We've got some preparations to make. Maybe we'll toss a few barrels of kindlepitch into the camp before we set off. A parting gift of sorts.\n\nI'm sure we'll run into each other again. Maybe even when we have a show to perform!
I searched through the rubble … was just about to give up. Glad I found you though.
After what you did, it was an honor! You shut them down. Our soldiers cleared out the stragglers. No more Ironhands.\n\nI know General Godrun will want to see you.
Oh, yes. Every year folk form up into groups to trick and prank each other. This year it's the Khajiit of "The Pariah's Hand" versus the Bosmer of "The Subtle Knife."

Yanabir-ja, leader of the Hand, preaches about the misadventures of Baan Dar most of the rest of the year. Dolirdor likes to make light of it, but she's a blade for hire when she's not planning practical jokes.

Bah. She's around here somewhere, sticking her nose into Drublog business. Put me in a foul mood, she did.\n\nGot no right to tell the Drublog what to do. Nosy Wood Elves need to be put in their place!
Watch your tone, whelp. Drublog don't answer to you.\n\nHere's your Elf friend now. Get out, before I lose my patience.
Good. Follow me—we want to be a little less … visible for this.

You hadn't heard? I've been so long in this backwater that I forget travelers like you don't know all the local gossip.\n\nStarted when that Redguard army marched up to the walls and pitched camp. Those tents across the river, that's them.

<<1>> may be praying at the Green Lady's shrine in the middle of the village.\n\nShe tried to convince people to search for <<2>>, but we're not strong enough to face a pack of werewolves or Houndsmen.
Are you completely feral? I'm not getting tortured for helping an intruder stranger! Leave me alone!

That's easy. All you've got to do is get captured, killed, and stuffed into a soul gem like yesterday's laundry!\n\nIf you're serious, Cadwell can probably get you in. Might be too late though. They just chased him into the guardhouse.

Maybe not a army, but that's what the Duke's men call it. They're all upset these Redguards are here to somehow capture the castle or something.\n\nPersonally, I don't get it. Redguards, Bretons, even us Orcs, we're all supposed to be allies.

Camping? Not ever! I'll leave the rugged stuff to the boys in the Fighters Guild. \n\nNo, fortunately the Bienena family is willing to put us up at their house. It's a little cramped, but its better than sleeping out here with the mosquitoes.
I'm with the Mages Guild. Pursuit of knowledge and standing ready against any Daedric threat—that's what we're about.\n\nSo Master Curmaland doesn't want us getting tangled up in local politics.
Go away or I'll call the guards! They'll … they'll ….\n\nThey'll probably take me, too. Just go! Leave me alone!

Feet first. That is the fastest way in. \n\nAsk Cadwell. That crazy bastard seems to know every corner of this place. You better hurry, though. I heard they just chased him into a building near the waterway.
You want to get into the castle? Are you feral? People who go into the castle never come out!
Why do you think I'd know? Because I'm an Imperial? We're all the same in this place. We're nothing but scum!\n\nLeave me alone!
They serve the Hound, a servant of Hircine.\n\nIf the rumors are true, and they kidnapped <<1>>, I don't know why. She's sister to our sacred Green Lady. Whatever their cause, it cannot be good.

It's mostly guesswork, but informed guesswork. \n\nI had an aunt who briefly joined the Supernal Dreamers, so I'd heard the rhetoric. When Adima showed up, her talk about "achieving one's dreams" immediately made me suspicious.

The first arena is called The Pit—an accurate, if unimaginative appellation.  \n\nThe Pit's current champions are The Pack. They can only move on by defeating all of the other challengers, yourself included.

Alchemy! She gives him potions that put him into dreaming sleep, then visits his dreams, seduces him….\n\nThe worst of it is, he'd been betrothed to a good woman, Sister Safia, a Spirit Warden. Adima made Hosni drop her. Poor girl.

Indeed I have. And that's put me in their debt. More than I can ever hope to repay.\n\nBut then, you can't be in debt to dead men, can you? That's where you come in. And I've a plan that might tip the odds in your favor.
Confidence. I like that. But these are seasoned fighters who know how to compete. I've certainly lost enough money betting against them.
Good thought! Perhaps some in the guildhall saw him there. This one suggests you question our comrades in Bergama. Aelif will meet you nearby, she has some preparations to make.
This room is filled with crystal stands. We just need to find the crystals that fit and replace them. It should then allow the beam to continue and open the door.

Search the caves. The totem needs to be restored to the Goblins' shrine. \n\nIf a shaman sees you, expect some kind of trouble. One of them knows a shape-changing spell—and he's got a wicked sense of humor.
My guess is the automatons have them. Kill them to find out.
The automatons. I think I saw you pick one up earlier? Try it in one of the stands. \n\nThe empty stand closes to the lit one is probably your best bet.
Now Aelif is truly surprised. The Guildmaster had the magical prowess of a particularly slow horse.\n\nWhat was he doing at that ruin?
Relics? Jofnir was no scribe. He was like most Nords this one has met: a warhammer diplomat. The Guild lost some contracts because of it, but the rank-and-file loved him.
He did? So he knows what happened here? \n\nIf all the Spirit Wardens in Pariah Abbey came, we could take the shrine back for good. Why haven't more Wardens come?
There are? As bad as what happened here?\n\nI guess I shouldn't complain then. I should just be grateful that Azura sent you to help recover the rest of the artifacts.

They're Bosmer corrupted by the Hound, a Hircine worshiper who wishes to usurp my place at the side of the Green Lady.\n\nHe's fed their desire for power by "gifting" them with lycanthropy. If he severs my ties to the Bosmer, they'll fall to his whims.

I appreciate your confidence. One last thing: these conjuration boxes are inhabited by spirits. I can't predict what will happen when you close them, but it must be done.\n\nAfterwards, meet me down where Tabakah's camped out. Good luck, friend.

You can. The Dreamers won't let us just waltz through their camp, and I'm not much use in a fight.\n\nLeave the other relics with me though. You just need to find the key to the boxes somewhere in the camp and then seal them closed.

Ah, good. Werewolves attacked us. I wounded a few of the beasts and got away, but not before they tore into <<1>>. I'd hoped these Houndsmen might hold clues, but nothing.\n\nHave you seen <<2>>? Is she safe?
This bow goes everywhere with <<1>>! She wouldn't give it up willingly. It was an engagement gift from her father.\n\nThere's only one cave nearby which might serve to hide her. It's not far.
She says she's all right. We should get moving.\n\n<<1>>'s been through enough battles to know her limits.
No. These shafts are <<1>>'s handiwork. Only she and the Green Lady could weave such sweet death with a bow.\n\nI've seen too many of her arrows. She might have used the last on these three fools.
There's a small alcove nearby. An old hermit's den. I'll wait for you there.\n\nBaan Dar be with you, friend.
The Houndsmen have come and gone from the campsite near the old shrine to Hircine.\n\nIf you'll search the camp, I'll do my best to track the patrols. One or the other will lead us to <<1>>.
Good. I hope <<1>> is unharmed.
<<1>> must die for what he's done. To kidnap the Green Lady's sister, my wife! The fool condemned himself by his actions.\n\nLet's go to the cave and end this!
Lead on. We'll be right behind you.

Why, yes! My moon-sugar candy keeps me in good spirits. Wonderful, glorious moon spirits dancing along the walls! Do you see them? They are so majestic. No more talk, they beckon this one to the dance!

Rama's holed up in that cave over there. You don't want to tangle with him—he's meaner than a nest of vipers.\n\nHe traded swords with me because his had lost its edge. If I were you I'd just take this sword back to <<1>> and say you killed him.
Yes, from Westtry. How I long to travel there with him. He described it as bright, beautiful, and full of life.
Keeping us out, yes. But perhaps. Perhaps also keeping him in? Aelif has tried to have Jofnir summoned from Aetherius. And it has never worked. Perhaps now …. Aelif has an idea.
Perhaps with the barrier down, we speak to him directly. This one knows how to reach out. Aelif can draw him to this place, so close to his body. What do you say? Are you ready to get some answers?
What kind of a question is that? My true love has been cast into a dark pit to die. If I thought I could get past the traps, I would go in after him. I can always buy another dress.
It's beneath the palace and anyone thrown in dies there. Jakarn said the guards are brutal and the other prisoners are worse.

Traps, guards, and other prisoners prevent that. Jakarn said there are rows and rows of traps. And everyone down there, except for Jakarn, is a vicious murderer. No one's ever gotten out. My poor Jakarn!

The warrior wave, child! The warrior wave! Our ancestors arrived from Yokuda, striking terror into the hearts of all who lived in the southern Iliac Bay.\n\nWhat do they teach children nowadays? Go away. Leave an old man in peace.

Her majesty set this one a task: investigate the leadership of the Veiled Heritance. The Veil's trail leads here, to the town of Mathiisen. \n\nWell known for their steel blades, yes? But also, apparently, weaponsmiths for anarchists.
You contact agent Fistalle on the east side of town. This one pads around her house. Then, we meet to discuss her report.\n\nToo bad Raz is so handsome, yes? He would get noticed.

You're in danger. Danger I can't fully comprehend, not even in death.
Chief Tazgol doesn't see the danger. The Bloodthorns are after an ancient Ayleid weapon that we know nothing about. We must catch up to Tazgol and stop him from rushing in!

I'm pleased he sent someone who respects my wolf kin. Maybe there's hope for the Prince yet. I'll attend the council. \n\nYou should talk to Thane Jeggi before you return to the Prince. If Jeggi's sober, he should be a part of the war council as well.

Enjoy your time among the wolves! They are such intelligent and fascinating creatures!\n\nBut enough with the pleasantries. You said the Prince sent you? What does that thick-headed hooligan want now?

I overheard him telling a Redguard girl he'd whisk her off to Sentinel. That he was a ship captain. She swooned like a fool. Like I did.\n\nI'd tell the Headman where he's hiding if I didn't hate the Headman more. I need off this island.
Without the Breton ritual Vardan used, only one without a soul can cross the portal. That means you.\n\nYou must activate the welkynd stone, enter the spirit realm, and kill Vardan.

Several reasons. One is that Headman Bhosek commissioned me to explore the ruins.\n\nA fascinating aspect of Dwemer ruins are the ancient mechanisms to be found inside. Bhosek thinks to use them in <<1>>. I need to get inside to investigate.

An excellent suggestion. I believe this automaton can unseal the door, if it can be reassembled and controlled. \n\nI have its control rod but two focusing crystals seem to be missing. Find them and I'll do the rest.

Indeed. Look how busy they are—carving femur flutes, skinning durzog puppies, disciplining their females. So misunderstood. Like us, yet unlike. The Goblins live in a world apart, one I may never enter.\n\nI can only dream.
Y'ffre, confer your blessings upon this place, that we might behold the skill of the Green Lady.
Angry? Not he! When he saw her skill, he forgot he'd meant to show off and instead gloated about her prowess as if he'd taught her himself!\n\nHe was always proud of her and loved her.
Ulthorn thought he'd show her. He'd been having lessons for a year or so before she and <<1>> came along.\n\nGwaering's first arrow split his in two. Her second, the same. She never missed. Ever.
To be the next Green Lady, of course! Her next feat all but confirmed it.

Yes, some say this is the grave of the first Green Lady, lost to time before the Green Pact. Others believe the tree is the first Green Lady herself.\n\nAll agree this place is sacred and a blessed site of Y'ffre.
You've got to stop them. I mean, "we." We've got to stop them.\n\nShe mentioned Balding Hill. We can only hope it's there!
She is …  was a mage of no small skill. She could do the most wondrous things with ice! You've never tasted ale so cold!\n\nBut now she's gone. And the brew with her.

I don't know, we had an argument. She asked me to run away with her. To meet her there.\n\nI thought it was a joke, but that's the last I saw her. She knew I would never leave! This is my legacy! My family's legacy!

I know where to find my father. He'll be waiting near the village. But if I fight him, I may well lose control again.\n\nI can't do this without help, and my mother's in no shape to face him. You're the only one I can trust right now. Will you help?

<<1>>'s assistant. Bit of a marvel when it came to the arcane. Whipped up this fellow like it was nothing! She was sweet on <<1>>, but he didn't see it.\n\nThat's all past us, though. Now that thing is up and about!

More often than I'd like to admit. Every now and again some idiot decides to share his fortune with a mammoth. A few broken fingers usually put an end to it.\n\nThis is unprecedented, though. Someone must have fed them half our stock!
No dearie, I think we've all earned a little reward. Baan Dar is well pleased with this year's Boast. The best we've seen in years, to hear the way it's told.

I may yet linger. There are always more books to catalog or cross-reference.\n\nOr perhaps our patron has another task for me. The flow of knowledge and the march of history never ends. And a good librarian's work is never done.

You don't need to know.
Shazah will tell you what she can. We only joined the fort's defense a few days ago.

Apparently there are very strict rules against cheating, here. When I threw that potion into the arena, the guards grabbed me. Said they were going to feed me to those beasts you slayed. \n\nWe're free, but I don't think we can go back the way we came.
Then he's still alive. Thank the gods! \n\nBut, you! You can't stay! You have to leave before they find you here!

That's my understanding, yes. \n\nThis is our only chance. Don't muck it up. And good luck!
It's hard to describe. My memories, my feelings, they've been fragmented. Ripped apart. And all the fragmented pieces have been locked away in different parts of the Foundry.

I've tried. The Daedra took everything. My willpower, my courage, my sense of self. I'm an empty shell. The fragments are reflections of my worst fears and most painful memories. I can't … I don't think I can face them.
Even without a head, sometimes the serpent takes a long time to die. The Maulborn cultists are still out there. Perhaps that's what's triggered my visions.
After we hit Bhosek's palace, we're done here. Are you sure you're ready to leave?
If we're going to do it right, we'll need Jakarn, Neramo, and Crafty Lerisa.
Time to fill you in on the plan. We're after Bhosek's sailing logs.

"Welcome! If you're reading this, something has gone horribly wrong with my most recent experiment! \n\n"I've created a potion that allows the imbiber to take control of thunderbugs. It should be right on the table. Go ahead, pick it up!"

Those records are worth a fortune to King Fahara'jad. They're written proof that Bhosek has violated the king's order to stop raiding Breton shipping. With those papers in hand, the king can threaten to destroy Bhosek if he doesn't stop.

Absolutely. His envoy is on the dock now, waiting. As soon as we turn over the sailing logs, he gives us a fortune in gold.\n\nThe trick will be getting into Bhosek's palace, stealing the logs, and getting out with them. That's your job.

Dibella's silky britches! Look at the books on this list! This is unprecedented!\n\nWhere did Richard find such a thing? What a remarkable discovery.

In life, I was Gjalder, father to Lyris. My spirit was torn from its rest and brought to this foul place. The Daedra force me to experience my own murder, again and again. I thought my torment would never end.

Yes. My ancestor had the box made to protect her valuables while she was at sea. \n\nThe box was tied to her blood so that only her or her descendants could open it. It's been passed down from mother to daughter ever since.
Deep within our sanctuary, others have unleashed a force beyond their control. Lead me to the door, if you dare to enter.

I can offer help with the guard, perhaps. You wish to deal with him quietly, correct?
I removed this device from Clanker. When pressed, it produces quite the incapacitating shock.\n\nIf you would test it for me, preferably on a living subject, I would be grateful.

After you entered the ruins without any trouble—and I'm not counting the imps, mind you—I assumed that the spirit had fallen asleep or something.\n\nAnyway, as we stepped inside we were hit with a wave of incredible force. It hurt. A lot.

Great. Just great. If you shake my family tree, my father wouldn't be the only bastard to fall out of it. But he might be the worst.\n\nWe have to reason with this spirit. Show her that I'm not the one who wronged her and I don't deserve her wrath.

What? Why would I do that? That's a foolish idea. A Baelborne never abandons his property.\n\nWe need to get rid of her. Explain our side. But I'm not really sure how to communicate with a spirit. Maybe you could summon her or something?
You just … well, you … damn! I don't know.\n\nHead back to Daggerfall. The Mages Guild there has a library. They must have a book or a scroll or something that has the information we need.
Now we're ready for the real challenge—the heist.\n\nThe target's Bhosek. That slimy bastard's finally gonna get what's coming to him. We're going to steal his sailing logs.

The cultists opened a portal with this welkynd stone. Vardan entered the spirit realm and commanded the relic to send forth spirits to slay Orcs. He and the relic were trapped over there when the portal closed.
Not at all. Vardan still commands the Ayleid Relic, and spirits still spew forth from their realm. He must be killed and the relic brought back. Activate the welkynd stone and end this!
I do hope you're not dabbling in necromancy. That magic always causes more harm than good.\n\nBut yes, we probably have what you seek. Check upstairs. That's where we keep books on the arcane arts.
No, I just love sodden hands and the smell of wet clothing.\n\nYes, I'm doing laundry, fool. Now leave me be.

Hoping to put one over on the headman, eh? Have you met the others who tried that? Their heads are up on pikes somewhere. We add about one a week.\n\nStill, if you've a deathwish, I could spare a uniform, for a price.
The Ghost Snake has a taste for bog rats. They make a proper offering. But only if you bring exactly eight of the plump creatures to the Fang Spires.
That's fair. At the rate fools keep trying to pass themselves off as servants, I'll soon have enough to buy my way off this rock.\n\nLook in the crate for your new rags. Try not to die!
Then you'll need to poke around the palace just as you are. I think the Fists will enjoy caving in your head.

Do not question the will of the Ghost Snake! Besides, that's exactly the number of rats that fit in the bag I gave you.\n\nMore than that, I cannot say. The mystery of the sacred number is not for the ears of an outsider.
Oh yes. Try these on. I'm sure they'll fit you just right. In the meantime, I'll just continue my sweep of the palace.
You want to follow ghost?
Use this by the fire!
Shouted at you too, did he? He just went out back to carouse with the latest slatterns from the mainland. Best hurry up and refill his drink.\n\nYou don't want him running out of drink.
By helping you accomplish what the Baelborne has requested.\n\nMy master sent me to help you summon the spirit. You need to see why the Baelborne curse must not be broken.

Ah, words are so much less effective than seeing the reality of a thing. Now think carefully before you answer my next question. I need to determine if you can truly summon this spirit of the dead.\n\nWhat is the spirit's name?

You can't remember one simple thing, but you seek to end a spell you don't understand.\n\nMy master retracts his offer. You must find a way to summon the spirit on your own. I suggest starting with the mine behind the Daggerfall cathedral.

Claudie Themond was a quiet woman. She never wanted power or riches. All she wanted was love. A family. A home to call her own.\n\nWhat token did the one she love give to her? What was the gift that would prove to be her undoing?

You can't remember one simple thing, but you seek to end a spell you don't understand.\n\nMy master retracts his offer. You must find a way to summon the spirit on your own. I suggest you start at the mine near the Daggerfall cathedral.

The kind that is crucial to the summoning! If you are to call her spirit to this realm, you must focus on who she truly was. Remember the visions you saw. She showed them to you for a reason.\n\nNow, what is the spirit's name?
Have we met?

I said I would think about it. \n\nIn the meantime, let me rub this salve on you. It has a scent that is pleasing to my wolf kin, so they will not attack you. It only lasts a short while, so I suggest you head back to camp.

Does he now? I'll think about it. \n\nI need to see what my kin think of all this. On the one hand, they don't like the Orcthane's invasion of their territory. On the other hand, they don't like our presence much, either.

You invaded their territory! I'm not sure I'll attend the council. I'll decide later.\n\nFor now, let me rub this salve on you. Its odor calms the wolves. It should last long enough for you to leave this area without going on another murderous rampage.
Wait! What's that smell?\n\nYou! You dare approach me covered in the blood of my kin?

I am pleased that he thought to send someone who respects my wolf kin. I'll attend the council. \n\nThe lingering effect of the mushroom will keep you safe, but it wears off quickly. You should find Thane Jeggi. If he's sober, he should attend.
You don't seem to be truly enjoying being one of the wolves. No accounting for taste, I suppose.\n\nIn any case, you said the Prince sent you? No doubt he wants me at his war council.
What is that delightful scent? Ah! Another admirer of wolfkind. \n\nYou've eaten a Canis Cap. You have that wonderful musky scent of fur and dirt and grass and old meat. Mmmmm.

The mine once belonged to the Themond family. Before it was shut down. They still own the land, and much of the family is buried just outside the mine.\n\nPlanting the spirit's belongings in her family's soil may awaken her.

I have a certain connection to this … situation. Neither your bad memory nor my master can change that.\n\nYou need to see why this curse was placed on the Baelborne family. I may not be allowed to help you directly, but I can guide you.
Something so ordinary as a piece of jewelry once promised an eternity of love. And yet it led to Claudie's untimely death.\n\nMy final question. What drove Claudie to act as she did?
Trying to catch a few winks, no thanks to you! First all that yelling, and then the smoke, and now this!\n\nDid Berthor send you? He's such a nosyknock!
Aw, they never hurt anyone who didn't hurt them first! Pitiful little creatures, they are ….\n\nI can't keep my eyes open anymore. Leave me, won't you?

Fear? I imagine she was scared. Not only for herself, but for the child within her. I suppose fear could drive her to make the deal she made.\n\nI'll take those items. Go to the gravesite, by the Daggerfall cathedral. My master will send Claudie there.

Love? I hadn't thought of that. Love could have driven her to make the deal she made. Love promised and love betrayed. An interesting theory.\n\nI'll take those items. Go on to the gravesite, by the Daggerfall cathedral. We will send Claudie there.

Yes, revenge. She hated the Baelbornes. Wanted to destroy them more than anything. Except saving her child. The deal she made … you'll see.\n\nI'll take those items. Go on to the gravesite, by the Daggerfall cathedral. We will send Claudie there.

My dear friend, Headman Bhosek, is sleeping off the attentions of these two lovely ladies. They are quite a handful. And an eyeful too!\n\nWhy don't you take the good headman's key inside for safekeeping?
Sleep? Ha! He hibernates, but only when he's not guarding Bhosek's things. Doesn't drink or smoke or carouse either. He's too dim for it, but he loves bashing heads.

Never. Well, I take that back. See the brazier behind the throne? We don't light it, ever. Helthar's terrified of it. His family burned up or something.\n\nLast time we lit it, he ran like a rat from a burning warehouse.

I fell in love with a coward. A Baelborne who couldn't disappoint his mother, even if it meant his beloved had to die.\n\nMy love turned to hatred in that tower. Before the end, I begged and prayed for someone to help my unborn child.

I made a bargain. Got my revenge. Saved my baby. The Baelbornes deserved to lose what they loved the most. Their wealth. Their lands.\n\nI felt my child leave me. I could smell the smoke from the tower. I heard the screams. The deal had been struck.

No! You can't. The master won't let you. My … my baby. What … what would become of him? The master would kill him.\n\nI don't believe you would do such a thing. You know the Baelbornes are evil. You know that my curse must stand.
The Baelbornes don't change! That family carries evil in its heart.\n\nLet them all rot. The ward in the waterfall will always keep the Baelbornes away. The master made it with his own blood.

Our only chance is to push on and win this thing. The guards are beholden to the holder of the Brimstone Crown, the Champion of the Blessed Crucible. The current champion is the Lava Queen. She's been champion for over 300 years.
There's a barrier in place, invisible to the naked eye, but one I feel resonating out from Silvenar. Its energy keeps me out of the city.
I can't believe it! This armor is who I am. It's what I am. \n\nA warrior without her armor is like a bear without claws.
The Silvenar sent scouts around the city. It's covered by a veil, and he can't get in.\n\nBy Y'ffre, what's happened? Why can't the Silvenar and the Green Lady be married peacefully?

There's nothing to be done from here. I told him I'd wait for orders, and so far, no one's sent me anything new.\n\nTalk to the Silvenar. He told us how you helped him in Jathsogur … perhaps you can help him again.
Just what my sphere needs! Just give me a minute, then throw that switch over there.

Of course you found Nanwen! What did you think you would find? An Ayleid warlord's body? Intact? I've looked for years and never found one! \n\nBut my museum collection needed a centerpiece, and Nanwen was crushed in a cave-in. So I … dressed him up.

Figured as much. It felt like the air shifted for a moment. When we tried to walk through the ruins, nothing stopped us this time.\n\nBut as soon as we walked in here, this man fell out of the sky. We thought it was an ambush!

He's the son of the ghost that tried to kill me? That's just great.\n\nI think he's hurt. But if he wants to pick up where his ghostly mother left off ….

If I took after my father, I'd put an end to the young man. It would be the prudent thing to do.\n\nBut I never liked my father. There's been enough hatred between our families. It's time things changed.
He has a mansion in Wayrest, but he spends most of his time in Dreughside, keeping an eye on his fief. \n\nHe often lords it over us from upstairs in Arbogasque's house. How I hate him.

She is correct. The city is protected by ancient wards, designed to keep forces hostile to the Bosmer from entering.\n\nBut the wards have been turned against me! I can't enter the city without destroying them, and that would be cataclysmic.

The city is an extension of the physical and spiritual power the Green Lady and I share. Breaking the wards would, at the very least, shatter that connection, making the handfast impossible.\n\nForcing myself inside would accomplish nothing good.

No one should be able to change the focus of the wards, not until after the handfast, unless ….\n\nThe spinners of Silvenar! Yes, it is possible that they could, together, change the wards. They wouldn't do so willingly, but they might be forced.
The Houndsmen patrol the ravine below the city, carrying <<mc:1>> to reinforce the wards.\n\nKill the Houndsmen in the ravine and collect their shards. I'm certain those will prove useful.

After Lyris took my place in the Wailing Prison so that we might escape, the Daedra moved her to the Foundry of Woe. \n\nIt is a place of torment and despair. She toils endlessly, making weapons for the enemy.

Then we leave for Betnikh, an Orc island that hasn't yet joined the Covenant. I hope to change that.\n\nLambur's happy to go home. She may try to thank you with ale. My advice? Make it to six mugs. You'll have a friend for life.
A guest of who? The Abridans? Malderbash? I don't remember. \n\nI was ill, or so they tell me. I came home to recuperate. My friends, some good shein, and I'll be right as rain in no time.

Rosalind fought to the end. When the Nords attacked, many of us cowered. But not Rosalind. She took action. \n\nOnce they were Nord invaders, but now they are animated corpses and wraiths. Fight them, as Rosalind did, and relive her final moments.

I don't know. While I prayed, she fought the invaders. I heard that she was going to light the signal fire at the lake to warn Eagle's Brook and perhaps compel them to aid us.\n\nFind something of hers. Some jewelry, perhaps. It may help.
A connoisseur then? Always happy to show off what this region has to offer. \n\nI hope you enjoy it.
I don't understand. We were looking for an Ayleid warlord—to put in Endarwe's historical collection—but we never found one.\n\nPlease, take me to Endarwe.

I was afraid of that.  \n\nThere was a cave-in, and the next thing I know, I'm on a slab with a necromancer chanting over me. She didn't seem to notice, so I laid still and hoped she'd go away. She stayed for quite a long time.

Once again, I'm out in the field with the great and powerful Telenger. And, once again, he's trying very hard to drive me mad. Would you be willing to lend that crazy old wizard a hand?

It's in the middle of the city, in the royal courtyard and gardens. No one is allowed inside, though. A Mages Guild spellcaster is posted outside and a magical barrier bars the way. \n\nVery mysterious!

Telenger the Artificer calls our fair city home! He runs a small shop and exhibition space for the Mages Guild on the west side of town. You can see relics from his travels, magical displays—all kinds of things!

I heard them say something about a hag coven in the north fens. My sister Bethany was fighting them as they dragged her off. \n\nI don't know what to do. I feel useless. I'm not used to this sort of life. I sent the others to the wyress camp nearby.

Not much. It's big and it smells. Bloodthorn cultists roam the southern fen and hags prowl the north.  \n\nI wish I had stayed in Camlorn. I thought we'd be safer out here, but look what happened. I hope Bethany's all right.
Please try to find my companions. These cultists are insane, but the hags … who knows what they're capable of. \n\nI'll go find my brother. The poor sod is useless without me.
There may be more constructs waiting on the other side of this door. You go first.
An easy task. Those earlier explorers likely retrieved them, only to find themselves sealed inside Bthzark through some treachery. Their misfortune is my—our—gain. We must find where they perished.
<The dust layering the bottom of this chest has been disturbed. Whatever the chest held, those contents are missing.>
The schematics are mine at last! Splendid.\n\nThis places me in your debt. What would you ask of me in return?
The schematics are mine at last! Splendid.\n\nThis places me in your debt. What would you ask of me in return?
They're somewhere inside the city. The Silvenar can't sense them with the wards intact, but once the guardian's defeated, he'll be able to extend his perceptions into the city, however briefly.
You've already done your part here, Hallowed. Let's just stand back and let her do her thing.

We're from Camlorn. There's been trouble there. We thought maybe things would be a bit more settled in Aldcroft. But no place is safe these days. it seems. \n\nIf something happened to my Elodie, I will never forgive myself.
More or less, he's usually a take-charge sort of fellow. \n\nIt was his idea to head to Aldcroft, so he feels responsible for all of this. His sister was among the women they grabbed.

That is a bit of bright news amid all this mayhem. \n\nI promised Elodie we would return to our nice little home in Camlorn when the troubles were over. If she is returned safely to me, I can keep that promise.

Do you always question a gift from a god? But I am in a generous mood. The lantern requires no fuel or flame to produce light. Simply activate the lantern and it will summon a ball of illumination to your side for a short time.

I sense they're being held in the trees within the city. The bonds of Hircine surround them, however, so you can't go directly to them.\n\nYou'll need to learn about the spinners and their prisons in order to free them.
Good, I was beginning to worry you got cold feet.

The wyresses are witches of a sort, devoted to nature and the Wyrd Tree. They helped us after the attack and said we could stay at their camp until we were ready to move on. \n\nIt's nearby, to the southeast. What remains of my group is there now.
I'll do my best to answer, friend. It's our good luck you happened by when you did.
The Lion Guard? They can't even defend Camlorn!\n\nThat must sound bitter. Well, you're talking to someone who lost everything. We had nice homes, shops, comfortable lives. Now look at us!

Not much. It's big and it smells. Bloodthorn cultists roam the southern fen and hags prowl the north.  \n\nI wish I had stayed in Camlorn. I thought we'd be safer out here, but look what happened. I hope Bethany's all right.

Sheor curse me, but I have no idea. Deleyn's Mill has always focused on our work. We don't get involved in politics or feud with our neighbors.\n\nOf course, chopping down trees could make a spriggan angry, I suppose.

All I know are their names: <<1>>, <<2>>, and <<3>>. This is my first visit to the city and until the handfast, my connection with the Bosmer is incomplete.\n\nI know how you can learn about the three spinners, but it will be dangerous.

Question the ones who bound them. The Houndsmen's witches worked with their master to craft special prisons for each spinner.\n\nForce the witches to tell you everything they know about the bindings and locations of the three spinners.

You'll see them soon enough. They're especially thick up north. You can't miss them. They're all twisted and diseased-looking.\n\nI'd suggest staying far away from those awful vines. They're nothing but trouble, of that I'm sure.
Not since I've lived in Deleyn's Mill.\n\nCome to think of it, those strange vines that recently sprung up are new. I couldn't cut them even with my finest axe.
Why wouldn't I be down here? It's perfectly safe. Are you worried about the Arbordawn? They're harmless! Of far greater concern are the Daedra. They're the real problem down here. Silly creatures.
Once you've learned about the three spinners, I'll contact you again.\n\nLook for my Psijic projection beneath the Great Tree at the center of the city.
Take this creature, born and bound to the essence of Aetherius, and let it guide you to what I need. Hopefully, it will find enough to establish the ward.
I'm not sure, but I've got a bad feeling about the Dres farm and I think it's all connected somehow.\n\nThe Dres and the Maulborn. Makes a certain amount of sense if you think about it, doesn't it?
I suppose that's so. The Rangers are spread thin across the Dominion and into Cyrodiil.\n\nDamned Colovians wouldn't have been able to take us at all if we were at full strength.
Now that I've had a moment to examine the ward, it will be a simple ritual to open the doors. However, it will take a few moments to complete. And I expect my efforts will not go unnoticed.

It's clear entering the temple was a poor choice. My enthusiasm for discovery has caused problems like this before. I imagine Andewen would be happy to provide you a list of past occurrences … but I digress. The temple must be resealed!
No. Now, I'll teleport us out of here.

Her essence focuses on the future of the Bosmer people as she sees it. Naturally, she believes in the love between the Green Lady and the Silvenar breaking through the shadow of the Hound.\n\nThe exact solution to the puzzles is a mystery even to us.
You should come inside. Let's talk.
Take out the corruption stones. They are inside the caves throughout the area.
Why else would I be cleaning her cabin? I want it to be perfect when she comes back. Spotless.\n\nThis whole mutiny was just a temporary setback. I'm sure of it. We'll sail again soon.
Kaleen did, with help from Lambur and Tumma-Shah, I mean. And Master Kasan.\n\nThey were amazing! So fast and strong. When it was over, Kaleen ordered the traitors off the ship, and good riddance!
Oh, Kyne yes! It was terrifying. Captain Kaleen told the crew we were to stop raiding Breton galleons, and that's when it started.\n\nThe crew went nuts. They tried to take over the ship!

<<1>> has lost sight of Z'en in his grief. He sees no other recourse but more death.\n\nMy master grows impatient with this world. I will not hesitate to strike him down if he defies the will of Z'en.
The spoken word can shape the future in ways stronger than the tears and blood of thousands.\n\nIf your words ring true, perhaps <<1>> will see a new path.

The Spearhead's the fastest galleon on the seas! Master Kasan gave her to Captain Kaleen when he retired. He taught her all she knows about the sea.\n\nOnce the captain gets a new crew, we'll be off again.
She's amazing! She's smart, tough, and a real fighter. She's incredible with a sword, even for a Redguard who grow up using them. I've never met anyone like her.

Well, it's kind of embarrassing. But funny!\n\nI was living on the Wayrest docks, picking a few pockets here and there to get by. Then Kaleen came walking by, with a huge bag of gold swinging from her belt.
She said it was a good lift—taking her purse, I mean—and offered me an apprenticeship.\n\nSailing the seas, drinking and fighting, finding treasure—I love it. Captain Kaleen's an incredible mentor.

I did steal it! She didn't even notice it was gone until I was halfway down the street, but boy, did she get after me. She can run!\n\nWhen she caught me, I thought I was dead, but she offered me a job. She was impressed.
Hmm, tempting … but you've got a job to do right now. Definitely some other time, hero. I'll see you at the farm.

The spinner acted as if he knew what was going on everywhere in Malabal Tor. He told the Hound that a hero was on his way and that the Silvenar wouldn't be locked out of the city much longer.\n\nCould he have meant … oh, no … he meant you.

Isn't it obvious? The people of the city of stone caused this. They have no regard for the natural world.\n\nNature only bends so far before it begins to suffer. Then it reasserts itself. Nature always prevails. That's why the vines appeared.

The vines! They started appearing weeks ago, bursting through the soil and spreading throughout Glenumbra. We've never seen such vines before, and even the Wyrd Tree was engulfed by the strange growths.\n\nWhatever's happening, no one is safe.
And go against my brother's command? I am not the chief, he is! His word is law!

With the Bosmer surviving … and the Hound dead. She spoke as if it had already happened. She also said that each spinner has the key to his or her own release, even if they can't affect it.\n\nPlease, let me go. I'll leave the city forever!
Irien's out there. Oh, and guards. I saw many, many guards.\n\nLook. Let's slip out a side exit. That way, we can both keep our heads.
Sai's a friend. Maybe my best friend. We need to find him and get him out of there!
Mutiny. We saved the ship and those that live fled ashore. This one hopes they have the sense to stay away.\n\nIf they return, Kasan's claws will taste blood once more.
Bless his heart. I knew the Captain would send me some help. Never seen you before.\n\nPerfect. You can do the dangerous—I mean, the exciting part of the operation!
We need to tell the Prophet about this. He'll know what to do. \n\nBut first, we need to find a way out of here. I don't care what else they throw at us, nothing's going to keep me from helping Sai.
They were not Kasan's crew. They belonged to Captain Kaleen, before they mutinied and tried to kill us all. Now they belong to no one.

Master Kasan is but a humble sailor, though others will tell you stories. Some whisper the name Kasan Five-Claw, Terror of the Seas.\n\nYet these are stories for children. We have better things to do with our time, yes?
Some call her the Duneripper's Daughter. Others the Forebear Witch. We, her loyal crew, call her Captain Kaleen.\n\nShe is a master sailor, though Kasan now wonders where her allegiance lies.
Kasan taught Kaleen much, though she is her own woman, strong and proud. Kasan is grateful to help her find her way.\n\nShe is a worthy successor. All that was once Kasan's is now hers.

There is a Forebear King in Sentinel now. Fahara'jad. He has allied himself with the Bretons and Orcs in this "Daggerfall Covenant."\n\nKasan fears his apprentice thinks much of Fahara'jad. Too much. A true sea-rover has no such loyalties.

"Thunderbugs are skittish creatures, so you'll need to be quick. Also! The potion only works on ones near the river.\n\n"If you wander too far from the currents, it's likely the bug will break free from your control. Good luck!"
Excellent. All right, this'll do wonderfully.\n\nYou go on ahead, and I'll see if I can get our <<1>> to show his face.

Agomar always delighted in inviting the locals into the Keep for a meal on cold nights. Drodda attacked us disguised as a peasant on one such night, launching her spells as soon as we let her in.\n\nHalf of us ended up frozen. The other half, dead.
I'm a warrior, not a shaman. I'd take too long trying to figure it out.\n\nIf my father didn't tell you, then maybe it's not important. Or he was ashamed.
Let's just say I've spent more than my share of time sneaking around beneath cities. If you've seen one sewer, you've seen them all.

I do? I do, don't I? 

I've been acting like some silly child. I don't know what came over me. I'm a grown woman and I have responsibilities to attend to. 
Can you get me out of here?

I thought everyone knew of The Blessed Crucible! The ancient arena where warriors are forged into champions? The no-holds-barred fight to the death, where the winner is crowned Champion of the Crucible and awarded the Brimstone Crown?

The mutineers? Some met Sithis. Others fled like the dryskin fools they are.\n\nCaptain Kaleen commands this ship. I honor my captain and stood by her during the mutiny. The ship is still ours, but her crew is gone.
Captain Kaleen told the crew we would no longer raid Breton galleons, by order of King Fahara'jad.\n\nBreton galleons have much treasure, thus the crew was displeased.
We are not alone. First Mate Lambur stood with us, as did Kasan Five-Claw. Even little Nicolene wielded a dagger for Kaleen.\n\nXuth! She is lucky to be alive. Besotted, sun-blessed little fool.

Captain Kaleen is ashore, looking for a crew who will not attempt to seize the ship. I would worry, but Lambur is with her.\n\nThose who trouble Kaleen when Lambur is near often get their heads twisted backward.

A relic from a lost age, forged in the planes of Oblivion. That's the tale, anyway.\n\nHonestly, I've no idea where it really came from, but I've seen countless deaths and gallons of blood spilled by warriors trying to win it.

Hm. I remember being upstairs, and I heard a voice at the door—a man's voice.

A few minutes later, Mathias brought up the mirror. When I looked, I recall feeling dizzy, and then I was here.

Mathias didn't do this, did he?
I sensed her departure. The shadows cast by her destructive anger will fade from these fens in time. Perhaps she will find peace in whatever lies beyond this plane.\n\nYou did well, I think.

She was a dark and dangerous creature, to be sure. I do not mourn her, but I wish her to be at peace.\n\nMother Murk's influence on the hags was strong. With her gone, the balance of the Fens will change.

The other Bosmer named us so because we refused the Green Pact. Why should we give up our shapeshifting abilities?\n\nWe wished to live our lives as we always had, and were sequestered in Ouze for eternity.
Of course. I'll pull my weight, unlike Jakarn.\n\nHe's not getting near another woman until I'm too old to stop him, and we Altmer live a very long time.
Following Jakarn, of course. Why else would I be along?\n\nI'm looking forward to working alongside him, sweating shirtless in the hot sun. You wouldn't understand.
I was quartermaster. I made sure we had the supplies and equipment to do whatever Lerisa wanted.
For now. But Captain Lerisa is hoping to get her own ship again. We'll see how things go in Betnikh.

One of the finest, my good friend! I used to own my very own tap cafe in Wayrest, before that thug <<1>> closed me down.\n\nI hope to open another one, once I collect enough coin. Maybe in Daggerfall. Hmm.
I'm sorry. I got scared. Did you see the size of that thing?\n\nWell, I think I can give it another try.

I'd been traveling with a few Dunmer botanists. I tired of their obsession with Bosmer horticulture, and struck out on my own.\n\nAs soon as I had a run-in with one of the native thunderbugs, I knew I had to stay. So much potential!

Thunderbugs congregate in packs to feed off of their fellows' elemental energy. The bug you brought absorbed the excess energy overwhelming me. \n\nI hypothesize the transferal of energy caused the thunderbug to disintegrate. A pity.
May the Mother Spirits guide us! I tried so hard, but I wasn't able to save more than this single villager.\n\nI'll make sure we both get back to the mill.

<<1>>. I'm a collector of sorts, one who travels to places others dare not go.\n\nI hoped to join Neramo's expedition to Bthzark. When I heard he had completed it and was sailing on, I just had to come along.
You're inquisitive. What I do, I do well. You'll be glad to have me on this voyage if we encounter slavers.\n\nAnd I make a wicked sliced ale.
If there's one thing Master Kasan taught me, it's that knowing your ship and crew keeps you alive.\n\nSeems like you'd make a fine captain, some day. But you'll have to find your own ship!
Injured? Injured? What does that matter? Everyone's dead! \n\nI think … I think I'm the only one left.
Survivors? I'm not all alone? Oh, thank the Eight! I have to get to the mill and see who else is still alive.

Every last one of the damned things that got too close. A Nord never gives up. And a Nord never backs down from a fight.\n\nI'll keep fighting and swinging my axe until my arm falls off. And then I'll find a way to fight some more!
I'm not afraid to die, stranger. But I might as well do it while defending the village.\n\nThanks for the help. I look forward to fighting at your side back at the mill.
The land remembers those who tread upon it, for good or ill. The totem taps into these memories and shows us the ghosts of the past.
Thormar. It's an Ayleid ruin, but most of it's collapsed beneath the bluff. The scholars never come here anymore, so it makes a perfect place for the Boast.
Oh, you know how it is, dearie. You get to be a certain age and it seems like you've seen everything.\n\nAt the Boast, there's always something to make me smile.
It used to be. But we haven't used these halls in a long, long time. Not since we fell out of favor.

That's just it. Their shouldn't be anything down here. Not anymore. Sure, in the past, when the wards were active, we used this place to come and go as we pleased. There wasn't a better hiding place for a group of dedicated assassins-for-hire.
The wards use Daedric magic to protect these tunnels from scrying magic. Even works against the Tribunal, from what I've been told. Anyone down here is practically invisible to the city above.

We have a two-pronged counterattack prepared. We're going to burn the Colovians out of the village, then take them by surprise in their camp. \n\nI'd like you to help one of my aides prep for our first attack.
Talk to Glooredel, our alchemical engineer. Her lab is at the base of the tree.\n\nShe'll fill you in on the plan. Meanwhile, I'll work with Herdor in preparation for our second assault.

When we grow the village, it expands out from a common root system. We can use those roots to burn the whole place at once.\n\nI've concocted an alchemical admixture with shalk guts and fire salts. Should do the trick.

Every home in the village has an urn, where sap from the root system comes up into the building. Pour the admixture into the urns and they should light.\n\nThen meet me at my workshop. We'll blast the roots and the whole village will go up!

Are you really so naive?\n\nHouse Telvanni rejected membership in the Ebonheart Pact. We remain isolated, pursuing our own interests along the Telvanni coast. That's just one of the reasons the other houses distrust us.
I don't care what you believe. But I'd never heard of the Maulborn before I came to this vile city. And I certainly had no intention of betraying the Tribunal before they threatened me.
People cower when they see me coming.
I won't take your insults sitting down!
You've found me out. Jurak is no priest. He stole this robe and wanted your help to steal the ring. But he had a very good reason for everything he did.
The ring of Rid-Thar is a sacred relic of my order! It cannot be taken from the temple grounds and sold in some market!
<<<1>>'s body appears to have been shredded by claws from behind. It looks like the search party was ambushed.>
Glad to have you. If we win the day, it's going to be glorious.\n\nIf we fall, it'll have been an honor to fight with you. Here they come. You ready?

I was once Sanarel the Great, Master of the Summerset Isles, Champion of Trinimac and the Slayer of Felhorn. \n\nThose days, alas, are over. More's the pity. Now, I am a humble servant to the Champion of the Blessed Crucible.

No, though it would have been a mercy. She was particularly cruel and wished to see me disgraced. I've been her slave ever since.\n\nNow, it seems, I have a new Champion to serve. May you wear the crown for a thousand years!
My story is the same as every wearer of the Brimstone Crown. I was Champion for nearly 200 years before I fell to the Lava Queen.

Banish the Daedra that defile our Temple. Defeat them and then make your way to my altar.\n\nWhile you slay their minions, I shall determine what the Maulborn are really up to. Now, go, and carry my divine rage with you!
You would compound the sacrilege that has already been wrought upon our Temple? No, that is unacceptable. If you will aid us, you will do it with our blessings—or not at all!
You've found me out, my friend. Jurak is no priest. He was your guide and companion in the ruins of Belarata. But, truly, he had a very good reason for everything he did.

Bosmer priests, of a sort. They interpret the Green Pact, and often serve as diplomats for the Bosmer.\n\nThey tell stories to each other as their prayers. And strangely enough, their stories come true.

A bard in the best of times, and a scavenger in the worst. I came to hear the stories of the Bosmer, and found them unintelligible.\n\nI've only just begun to understand the depths of the spinners' power. I doubt they know it themselves!

You've heard of the Silvenar and the Green Lady, yes? The spinners tell the story of their life together, guiding the Bosmer to prosperity.\n\nThat is how it usually goes. But it's changed, and I fear for the Bosmer people if it is not changed back.
Fermentation. Flowers. A number of other things you don't want to know about. Tastes like honey but kicks like a horse.\n\nIf he sold it, he'd be rich, but he just drinks it all.

Only <<1>> can start the story. But once it's started, it can be retold! You may be just what this story needs. A fresh idea added into the mix!\n\nLook closely at <<Ac:2>> to begin the tale. <<1>> won't be able to resist!
You took longer than I expected. Everything go all right?
Not in recent memory. Tanglehaven's not a large village by any reckoning, and the Drublog know we've very little worth taking.\n\nThey attacked without warning, and left as quickly as they came.
Yup! I'll even let you light it! Just use this torch. We should be safe in here. Mostly, anyway. \n\nOutside? It's going to be a fiery mess. It'll be glorious!

Very noble! I'll admit it, we're not good with civilians. They're our blood relatives, our children. But our real family is the Rangers. \n\nSometimes we forget that. I'll make sure to tell the Captain about your kindness.
Nice work. Fast. Good. We'll catch even more of them unawares.
Yup! I'll even let you light it! Just use this torch. We should be safe in here. Mostly, anyway. \n\nOutside? It's going to be a fiery mess. It'll be glorious!
They burnt the village, but did they actually take anything?\n\nJust lives. Nothing but lives.

If she knew what happened, she wouldn't call me her daughter anymore. We've … I've made a terrible mistake.\n\nThe spring. It's all from there. I must get to it, but I'm afraid of what might happen if I get scared again ….
This is my daughter's. I gave it to <<1>> before she left <<2>>. \n\nWhere did you find it? Have you spoken to her?

Yes, and I suppose that's answer enough.\n\nI wish I could pretend I don't know what'll happen, but it's obvious, isn't it? I'll change. Eventually become a minion to Hircine's will. Poor, poor <<1>>!
No, it can't be! My sweet daughter, dead? \n\nShe yearned for a new way of life. I begged her to stay. Now I'll never see her again.
<The bow is finely crafted and light to the touch, an elegant weapon. An inscription is carved just below the grip, "For Lanwaen, my moon and stars." <<1>> will want this.>
<<1>> and I need to rest now. Please, tell <<2>> we're home safely.\n\nStop by to see us before you leave town. And … thank you. Y'ffre bless you!
Of course. Do you want me to tell you about Elanduya, my eldest? Wirande? Or little Soraperil?
That's my shield all right! You must be one of those Ra Gada who jumped me!\n\nNow you don't have your buddies to back you up. Prepare for a pummeling!
Mendol. My youngest boy. He joined the military, fought on the front lines. And died in defense of his homeland.\n\nI wish I could have made him see. Made him realize it was a mistake to leave.
He was just like my brother Paaulen. So smart. He could sell a fur coat to a Khajiit. \n\nSoraperil wasn't a Mage, but he taught alchemy with them at the Hall here in Skywatch.
My fiery girl. She got tired of her mother's coddling. Took up with a musician, and sold lutes up north for years. \n\nEventually she grew to miss me, and we were close for decades before she passed.
I know, so old fashioned. I named him after my father. \n\nMy first boy. I knew what name he'd have. And he made me so proud.
Not Ra Gada? Ha! That's exactly what a Ra Gada would say!\n\nI'll leave your broken body as a warning to the rest of your friends. They will fear the name of <<1>>!
Hrm. True enough. But this could be some Ra Gada trick!\n\nTell you what. Hand over my shield and I'll let you off the hook. This time.
We found her backpack and a few personal items at the falls, but nothing more. And then, the werewolves ambushed us along the trail.
He ran further up the trail. When the werewolves attacked, they ripped <<1>> to shreds. He … he died screaming at us to run.\n\n<<2>> is an able fighter, like <<3>>. He must be alive.
Praise Y'ffre!\n\nI told her this search might prove dangerous, but she wouldn't hear me. She and <<1>> are cousins, and blood runs deep.

Well, let's see. Let's take their ideas and turn them into something worthy of Baan Dar's laughter. We'll need some things from the Wood Elf camp. One of their Rotmeth barrels and some poison from Dollie's pack.

The Khajiit are going to use alchemy. Transformation potions and the like? Well, there's a hardy breed of plant near the ruins called the strangler. It can process Dollie's poison, turn it into something non-lethal.
Ha, it already sounds hilarious when you say it out loud. Oh dearie, thank you. This is going to be the best Boast in years. You're going to love the Five Finger Dance!
Then kill the nasty things. Crack them open and harvest their core stems. Poisoned strangler stems create a powerful hallucinatory effect when thrown into a fire. The Khajiit will just love it!

<<1>> is a powerful fighter, but there are werewolves and Houndsmen out there. I asked him to wait for reinforcements, but he left immediately with his apprentice, <<2>>.\n\n<<3>> is <<4>>'s cousin, but she's no warrior herself.
Thank you. It would be a shame if we were to lose two of the Green Lady's relatives to the Houndsmen in one shot.\n\nY'ffre guide you in your search.
This village is a holy site, established after the shrine of the Green Lady was discovered.\n\nI'm sure someone will be willing to give a short tour, once <<1>> has been found.

We don't know. Everyone's so upset, they've gone a bit mad, seeing things that can't be true.\n\nOne of the villagers said she saw <<1>>, but he's dead. Lost to a pack of wolves when his parents were attacked. We never did find his body.
You mortals. Always such high aspirations. You dream of interfering with my plans, but it is a fantasy.
You can. There's nothing you can do now. The Omens were a distraction, a daydream. Now, the real nightmare begins!\n\nYou see … you protected your general … but you sacrificed your king!
Do you really think my manipulations would be so vulnerable? You are not even a hindrance.

The falls, where the current Green Lady, Gwaering, risked her life to save a friend. I can reveal a bit of the story with a blessing <<1>> taught me.\n\nIt's a little dangerous with the werewolves and Houndsmen about, but they're no match for you.

Gwaering and Ulthorn, her constant companion, often played here as children.\n\nOne day, a starved pack of senche-tigers came along and circled the pair. Ulthorn suffered with fear, but Gwaering stood fast.
