Gwaering picked up a bone and growled like a tiger herself. Then she gave them what-for until they surrendered! I came along just as they ran off.\n\nUlthorn was quite embarassed of his inaction, but remained proud of Gwaering.
Let's go to the archery range. It's just up the hill.\n\nWatch out for those werewolves! There are so many of them. I hope the Green Lady sends us help to disperse them.

He grew up and learned the hard way that one doesn't always get what one wants, or is promised.\n\nThey'd been betrothed, but when she was chosen as the Green Lady, Ulthorn was forced to step aside. The Green Lady always weds the Silvenar.

You've done well, mortal. You returned my Dream Shard, you vanquished Vaermina's Omens, and now you've cleansed my shrine as well.\n\nBut the Mistress of Nightmares has not yet released Stormhaven from her clutches, has she?
The Archmage, Telenger the Artificer. He owns the Emporium here in town, and leads the Mages Guild of Skywatch. \n\nHe's a crusty old crank when it comes to getting his way.
I found Leggy on a Guild expedition to Morrowind. He was huddled in a corner, shaking, and I coaxed him out. Tweaked a few of his gears back into shape, and … well, we've been together ever since!

No, no! Don't look at it that way. Look at it from your view down the river. \n\nIf you look back and see Leggy and I standing here, forlorn and forgotten, won't you regret that? More than you'd regret taking a few baubles those nobles won't miss?

Indeed, and King Emeric has been very tolerant toward my Spirit Wardens … a fact I have not failed to notice. \n\nFirst, Vaermina attacks my abbey, then she desecrates my shrine, and now this. If I didn't know better, I might think it was personal.

This time, she has unleashed her own consort, Galthis—the Night Terror. He consumes King Emeric's mind in the nightmare, blocking your entry.\n\nI will give you a Duskstone to penetrate the nightmare, but defeating Galthis will be another matter.

You've proven to be talented and resourceful so far. Let this be another test of your strength. I'm sure you'll succeed in serving me faithfully once again.\n\nGo now, mortal. Go save your king … and teach Vaermina to keep her hands off what's mine.

The warehouses contain Velyn Harbor's food supply. While I'd rather burn it than give it to the invaders, things aren't that desperate.\n\nLet's keep the destruction to a minimum. We still have a chance to take the town back.
Dream Shard? Yeah, I heard some of the Union lads talking about it in low voices.\n\nI gather they stole it from the Spirit Wardens and gave it to Count Hosni. They were pretty smug about it.

You've never heard of Queen Nurnhilde? Forgive me, but that's so hard to imagine.\n\nShe was the Skald-King's sister. She ruled our land during the Akaviri invasion. Our beloved queen … she died defending us from the hated invaders.
I'm impressed, mortal. You navigated my nightmares without losing your nerve, and yes, you have saved your little king … for now.

Of course you will. 

You have slain my consort as well. I'll get over my loss, but I think I'll keep you here for a while in his stead. 

Perhaps a century or two will teach you humility ….
I suppose those Ra Gada wouldn't dare approach me after what they've done. Especially to return my shield!\n\nGive it here, then.
Sweet, but totally unnecessary. I'm not interested in flattery or flirting. I just want to serve my drinks and get this day over with.
The King's festival. Enough eating, drinking, and sewage in the streets to let Jorunn know he's appreciated.\n\nAt least there are the contests. Maybe Pa's new hired help will win me a prize.
Brew? Yes. Where did you get it? That smell ….\n\nWait. Where am I? What am I wearing?
I … I remember now. Too much root pulp. Less kick, more crazy.\n\nGrubby was right! I'm out of my gourd. Things are starting to make sense again.
Tazia sent you? Or Zal-sa? For what purpose? What have those lazy attendants done?\n\nNothing has gone right since Rakhad … but never mind. What do you mean?
Our families knew the risk of living with us. I've warned them about this. But some soldiers still don't understand the cost of war.\n\nBut still. Thank you.

The clan knows <<1>> as a crotchety blind man, but really he's a sweet old cat. Rats now live in his well, he says. \n\nShuzura is very fond, truth be told, and she does not want him hunting rats in the dark.
<<1>> is always complaining about something. This week, he says someone is stealing his crops.\n\nShuzura thinks it is the local children playing jokes, but he is sure bandits stalk his fields.
Poor little <<1>>. Of late she's had bright moons and dark, both. Her uncle passed away, but left her his old house. She tried to move in … and now swears the place is haunted.

Not unless you're a fan of lectures about the etheric substrate of Nirn, or the building blocks of Oblivion realms. Telenger is a powerful mage, though. Probably the greatest of our time, if you don't count Guildmaster Vanus.
We actually went looking for them, if you can believe that. We'd heard they had a new king and that he was stirring up trouble. We figured we could handle them, but there were too many for us.

The people that normally live here, the people in the camp nearby, call themselves the Falinesti Faithful. They patiently await the return of the great city, hoping it will change their lives. The Arbordawn … have lost their patience.
Our families knew the risk of living with us. I've warned them about this. But some soldiers still don't understand the cost of war.

This is a resting site for the great walking city of the Falinesti. Every autumn the massive treebeast would creak and groan its way across the landscape. Set out roots in the Halls of Ichor, down there in the tunnels.

You know firsthand how adept the mercenaries are at killing. These people are merchants, but they know it too.\n\nJust ask nicely. Be persuasive. Cunning. Somehow, I think they will do as you say, no tricks necessary.
Indeed. The body on my floor proves that.\n\nWho was this man who came to kill me? What did he want?
Of course! Betting is just another form of battle. It requires intelligence, strategy, and tactics. I'm extremely good at it. And earning some extra gold never hurt anyone.
And go up against the reigning champion, Thane Jeggi? Not on my best day, friend! That man can drink a lake full of mead and still be thirsty.
Angof? I've heard this name whispered by my agents.\n\nThe royal spymaster reports of unrest across my kingdom stirred into a froth by this Angof, but that's all we know.
Creating chaos is a method, not a goal. It's a means, not an end.\n\nThere's more going on here than chaos for its own sake. We must get to the bottom of this.
Of course. Apologies, I'm a bit distracted at the moment. \n\nMy name is Endarwe. I'm a student of history, an avid collector, and the leader of the Merethic Society.

We're a loose group of adventurers who specialize in acquiring antiquities. We'll go anywhere, do almost anything, to collect history.\n\nSome governments are not so keen on the work we do, so we tend to operate as inconspicuously as possible.

This is one of the necromancers. He made two mistakes: he had roughly the same height and build as myself, and he turned his back to me.\n\nIf I can get the blood out, his clothes will make a fantastic disguise.

The crypt's got to be somewhere near the ruins of Merovec's Folly. She kept a journal that she was constantly writing in. I'm sure it contains the location of the crypt.\n\nOur camp is west of the redoubt. Her journal is probably still there.

The Green Lady personifies our feral nature, who consorts with the Silvenar to balance the Bosmer's emotional and physical sides.\n\n<<1>> is famous for several chosen from its citizens to receive the title, including the most recent one, Gwaering.
They're bondsmen of the Hound, mortal agent of the Daedric Prince Hircine.\n\nNormally, they keep to themselves, but they've recently flocked to Hircine's shrine not far from here.

On the hillside behind me, but you can't climb it. Head down the ravine, past the camp. Go a bit further to the stone steps leading up into another ravine.\n\nMake your way through the ravine to the bridge. And be careful. Our enemies are everywhere.
I've got this, uh, frog chow here. It'll get your critter out in front for sure. Just have to be careful. \n\nFeed it too much and it'll get slow. Don't feed it enough and it won't come in first.
I'm in a little bit of trouble and Malion over there has banned me from running any more racers. Only way I'm going to get out of debt is to bet on someone else's frog.
It's taken me some time to get my special chow right. I lost some races even though I had some sure bets. And now I'm in a little bit of debt.
A … a job? Ha! Oh, that's a good one. A job!
Bugs. And uh, some alchemical reagents. Don't worry, the little hopper will be fine. \n\nI may be a little desperate, but I wouldn't hurt a frog.

You've seen the fields here, on the stead? Well, crops keep disappearing in the night. Plants just don't up and walk away!\n\nShuzura keeps telling Ezzag it's just children playing pranks, but he has lost half his crop this week!
It's bandits, damn it! Thugs and hooligans are taking Ezzag's crop.\n\nHead down to the field! Find their hideout, kill their leader. Bring me his head!
Just dig into the bag of chow here and stuff the little critter full.\n\nJust be careful to keep an eye on the thing. You don't want to overdo it.
Well, if you don't feed the thing enough, it won't get the full benefit of my special formula.\n\nFeed them too much and they'll get a lead belly. We all know what that's like.

My son may know more than me on that matter.\n\nMy only guess is that they sought to break the Lion Guard. Divide our forces and destroy us. If not for your intervention, they very well may have succeeded.

Yes, throughout Glenumbra. The Lion Guard is spread thin, and without King Casimir's full support I'm not sure if we'll be able to deal with it all.\n\nOf course, if I had a few more like you, we might just have a chance.
<The frog looks so full it might burst.>

We rebuild. Of course, we still need to deal with Faolchu's master, but tomorrow is another day and we should relish this victory.\n\nWell, don't let me keep you. We both have things to do, and you should speak with my son.

I wanted to thank you. Personally.\n\nWe might have been able to retake Camlorn eventually, but it wouldn't have been quick and it certainly wouldn't have been pretty. You saved lives, and that's not something I'll soon forget.

I'm resigning from the Camlorn Guard. Never did like being stuck in one place for too long.\n\nOnce this Angof thing is finished, maybe I'll travel for awhile. See exotic lands, exotic women. Drink exotic wine. Oh, and cheese. I love cheese!

I'm resigning from the Camlorn Guard. They need builders now, not soldiers.\n\nBesides, that Angof thing is still out there. Someone has to go deal with that. Unless, of course, you'd care to tempt me with a drink before I start my heroic journey?

And what are you going to do? Anyway, my job here is done. My father will take good care of the city.\n\nI'm not one for building things and making repairs. I don't even own a hammer. I'm sure I can be of more use somewhere else.
A pity. I would have enjoyed sharing a drink with you. Ah, well.\n\nAnyway, I failed these people. The werewolves slipped in on my watch. I need to make sure that never happens again.

Well, then! All the more reason for me to get out there and deal with this Angof fellow once and for all!\n\nThe werewolves slipped in on my watch. I need to make amends for that. I need to make sure Camlorn isn't threatened again.

Ah, that's a long story. But I can sum it up in two words—the Akaviri. No, make that three words. The damn Akaviri.\n\nThe palace suffered extensive damage during the siege of the city ten years ago. I hear the repairs are almost finished. Almost.
The Palace of Ysgramor. They've been working on restoring the place for the past ten years and it still isn't ready for the Skald-King's use.

Dead? Truly? So … I can still be Emeric? I can still be High King? I don't know I deserve that at this point, but … I guess it's a good thing. \n\nYes. My binds are actually loosening, and that is very good. Does this mean …?
She wrote to me about that. Were you the stranger that helped her? Then I thank you for everything you did.

If all goes well, we'll be able to peer into the past. Hopefully see what happened to Faolchu. Find out how the Dirennis were able to defeat the Alessians so long ago.\n\nAnd if something goes wrong, well, then we shall see what we shall see.

We're collectors of lost relics. Some items we trade for on the black market, other we procure directly from ruins. We take our name from the Merethic Era, the legendary age between the creation of Nirn and the start of the First Era.

Every piece the Merethic Society admits into our compilation must have aesthetic or historic significance, and elevate the prestige of the collection as a whole.\n\nWe leave the archaeologists and the Mages Guild to fawn over potshards and jewelry.
A fragment from the past, I think. Something that was pulled forward with the spell.\n\nLet's hope that was all we pulled forward.
You, Gloo, and I are going to be running this thing. We'll be some of the first out of the tunnel.\n\nI've got the second line mustering down below now.
You and Gloo took out the Colovians in the village! Now we can concentrate our forces on the counterattack. \n\nWe're also itching to make sure Nendaer's all right.
I told her no, not this time. But now she's sent you after me. I give up.\n\nWe sacrifice so much to Zenithar, it's a wonder we have any left for ourselves. Very well, here is my share.
Oh, that offering. I clean forgot about it. Lots of other things on my mind. Busy hands, lots to do, people to see—you know how it is.\n\nHere, take it and go away. I hope Antias appreciates this.
She's the love of my life! I promised to take her away from Stros M'Kai. Then the Sea Drakes attacked and took her and Shamal.\n\nI'll never see her again!
Again? I haven't time to put together an offering. \n\nI must get back to my research. You collect four ears of corn from my fields, then I'll bundle it for Antias's pagan ritual.
Zenithar means nothing to me. He is but a shadow to Sithis, the Perfect Chaos.\n\nPerhaps if you do me a favor, I will make an offering.
We fought but there were too many of them. I protected Iriana as long as I could but I got knocked out. I saw them dragging her away as I fell.
He's a Khajiiti bard, a friend of ours. When I came to, he was gone. Maybe they've killed him already.
I can barely move. Those bastards left me for dead and took Iriana. I'd never get anywhere near her.
No good. Bhosek'll never believe it. He's a suspicious bastard and will think we're trying to trick him somehow. He'd have our heads on pikes. I'm too fond of my head to risk it.
Nonsense. Oh, fine! Pagan rituals are about all I haven't tried at this point.\n\nHere, this bundle of corn will make an appropriate offering.
I'll try to make it to town. I'm too injured to be any good to you, and if the Goblins catch me out here, I'm dead.

When you defeated the guardian, I projected more of my essence into the city.\n\nI've learned something about each spinner and their bonds. They're being contained by puzzles that tap into each spinner's essence.
You're not with Bhosek are you? No. You don't look dumb enough.\n\nSo tell me this: if I was planning something, why would I need you?
He may be annoying, but I bet he's got a nose for treasure!
Crafty Lerisa, eh? I won't lie, she'd be a big help getting what I want to steal.\n\nYou get me Lerisa, and I'll cut you both in on the take. Deal?
He's a charmer, that one. Damn good thief too, and I need one of those right now.\n\nGet me Jakarn and I'll cut you both in on our take. Deal?
He's an odd one, but I might have use of his particular skills. He could be just the thing for a heist I have planned.\n\nGet me Neramo and I'll cut you both in on our take. Deal?
<<1>> is the youngest. She is a master alchemist, and her purview is the future. She foretells many things with her prophesies.\n\nTry to assemble her history in the solution to her puzzle.

<<1>> was a powerful warrior before the spinner's path found him. He is blessed with a keen awareness of the present.\n\nHis perception of things happening here and now, particularly regarding the handfasting, should be the key to solving his puzzle.

She is the eldest and most powerful spinner. A wizard almost from birth, she sees the past more clearly than you and I see the present.\n\nShe draws parallels between then and now. Use that in solving her puzzle.

The Hound is using Ayleid stones to imprison each spinner. The key to each puzzle is tied to each spinner's essence, but their very spirits power the barrier keeping me out of the city.\n\nSolve the puzzles, free the spinners, and open the barrier.

Yes. If you fail to solve a puzzle, a manifestation of that spinner's spirit will appear. Kill it and the barriers will fall, but at the cost of a spinner's life.\n\nTry to solve the puzzles and free the spinners, not kill them.
I'm an Eye, same as you. The island's lousy with us right now. We need to get people talking, learn where the Heritance got their support.

The Heritance is massive. Arms and armor, food, logistics, supplies … Estre was going for the big win. Who supplied them? Who provided those weapons and armor? \n\nWe have a lot of hard questions to ask in the coming weeks.

Frankly, I wish your memory was as hazy as mine. What I do recall, I'm … rather ashamed of. \n\nI am the King of Stormhaven, the High King of the Daggerfall Covenant, but that damn Daedra reduced me to a pathetic child ….
<<1>>'s still breathing? Then I've still got a reason to go on.\n\nI have to get that plant's sap before it's too late!
<<1>>'s deal was a good one, but it's not worth Zurana's life. We stole the crops, collected the coin, but now ….\n\nPerhaps you can make her a better offer?
Great. For the right price, he's yours.
They kicked me out. They heard Bhosek threatened me and they don't want to risk his Fists storming in to arrest me.

Each has a home surrounding the Great Tree. Go up from here, then cross the tree-bridges and climb up further still to their homes.\n\nSearch the spinner's home for clues to solving each puzzle. Return here after you've broken their bonds.
Ah, I see. I'd forgotten. Well, here, let me bundle it nicely.\n\nThere you go, a lovely offering for Antias's ritual.
Perhaps you are right. Yes, yes. Zurana needs to find a new way to make coin. \n\nShe will leave, and Rakhad can find his moon-sugar some other way.
Now you are talking sense! Zurana and her men will leave and split your generous donation. Rakhad will have to find some other way of getting his moon-sugar.
Hmm … I don't think you understand.\n\nFollow me. Zurana will show you what is really going on.
That's what the headman claims. That's what got him thrown into the Grave.
You mocking me? \n\nThe headman makes the laws. It's my job to punish anyone who breaks them. Now beat it before I toss you in the Grave.
Treason. His actions would have destroyed the Daggerfall Covenant. \n\nHe has been found unworthy in every way. He deserves to die.
But I am King Emeric—the new King Emeric. The unworthy weakling will be gone, and I will take his place.
Nothing that concerns you. \n\nOur business right now, your business, is defeating the ogres.

What? Why would you risk your neck for us?\n\nI'm not in a position to argue. The plant should be near the Ayleid well. Be careful of the stranglers. They don't care whether their meat is dead or alive.
He said that? After all this, he wants to give up? <<1>> and I, what've we got besides each other?\n\nDoesn't matter what you say. I'll find a way to save him, with or without that plant.
Illusions. The blessing reveals a spiritual imprint left at this place.\n\nY'ffre has blessed us with this memory to show us the spirit of true courage and self-sacrifice.

Yes. As a child, Gwaering practiced archery here with her friend Ulthorn and sister <<1>>. She outstripped them from the very first day.\n\nThat's when her Aunt Finoriell, the previous Green Lady, saw her potential.

I still can't believe you came along. Me and my brother, we were orphaned. Haven't been able to rely on anyone but ourselves since.\n\nThis sap'll give <<1>> a fighting chance. Let's go while I'm still conscious.

Kalari is not even sure they are ghosts. She doesn't know what they are.\n\nI inherited this house from my uncle Enak-do. He passed away not too long ago. When my brother Mathal and I tried to move in … bah!

It's bad enough that these apparitions keep appearing and disappearing all over the house. But every busybody in S'ren-ja keeps trying to help Kalari! As if she was some kind of fragile flower. Dark moons!
Fine, fine. I'll loan you the monkey. Take him around the beach, see what he finds!\n\nJust get the little screecher away from me.
Y'ffre, confer your blessing upon this place that we might behold the glory of the Green Lady.

He or she is the incarnation of our history! A living symbol of our devotion to the Valenwood, and the voice of the Bosmer people!\n\nBut in the end, the Silvenar is a Bosmer, with a title passed from one Silvenar to the next.
<The monkey seems excited. It clearly wants you to follow it.>
You threaten? I erect the spine of warning. In my younger days, such words would have brought your death.\n\nNow I seek peace, even with my superstitious neighbors. Here is my offering.

Well, the Silvenar and the Green Lady need to be happy together. How that happens changes with every story.\n\nSo I think you must go through <<1>>'s story and make sure that happens. Everything else will work itself out.

I lent my favorite axe to Shagol. He says he left it somewhere in the woods but won't go find it. It is a matter of honor to me not to retrieve my own axe.\n\nIf you get it for me, I will make the offering to Antias's godling.
We need to know who's leading the outfit and where we can find them. We're going to kill them all, anyway. Right! Yeah!\n\nBut it'd be good to get their commanders before they escape.

Yes. Once her Silvenar died on <<1>>, <<2>> vanished. The priests and spinners searched for any sign.\n\nWhen they could not find her, they came to <<3>> to pray for guidance at the Green Lady's shrine.

As the priests and spinners prayed, Gwaering came to the shrine to join them.\n\nWhen she touched the shrine to offer her prayers, the tree began to glow and she rose into the air, revealed as the blessed Green Lady before the assembled faithful.
Indeed. Her glory was revealed, and all Gwaering's experiences and talents must have been ordained by Y'ffre to prepare her for this ascension.

The Green Lady represents our feral flesh, while the Silvenar is the spiritual. Both are chosen by Y'ffre for the common good of our people.\n\nTheir union is sacred, and we are all made stronger for it.
And here is my offering to the godling, as agreed. Of such compromises our days are made, here in Cropsford.

We must confront the Hound! But I have grim news.\n\nThe Hound has somehow enthralled the Green Lady's spirit. That's why the wards against my entry were so strong. She's in the audience hall, fighting to repair the damage you've done.
Sure, friend. I've lived here all my life. What are you interested in?

Give me the silver shards. They contain the essence of the three spinners' stories. I can use them to overcome the Hound's spell, but only if I can physically get to the Green Lady.\n\nGo to the audience hall and distract her.

Together, the Green Lady and the Hound will be formidable. Our only hope is for me to get to the audience hall quickly and help. If you're overcome, all Silvenar, all the Bosmer, may be lost.\n\nFight bravely, and well.

She's a warrior, first and foremost, and will abandon her repairs to confront you. Then I'll be able to break through the barrier.\n\nOf course, if the Hound gets to her before I can … best not to think of that.
Auridon's the place for that, my friend. Just head east out of town. The beaches along the coast are some of the most beautiful—and serene—places you'll find in all Tamriel.
Hmm. Lot of good places for that in Auridon. I wager you'd like Ezduiin, though. Ancient ruin in the middle of the island. \n\nI think I heard the Artificer himself is leading a research team there!
I have just the place. Mathiisen, just south of Skywatch. Sleepy little forge town, with the best steel in the Aldmeri Dominion. \n\nJust remember, pointy end towards the other guy.
You've never heard of Telenger? He's a national treasure. An Archmage, a living connection to the past. I hear he has quite the shop set up in Skywatch.
To love someone so strongly, only for them to be taken away is a hard thing for any mer to learn. He left Deepwoods, to seek his fortune elsewhere.\n\nIn any case, we should continue our tour.
Let's return to the village. That's where Gwaering's greatest moment took place.\n\nThere is an area near the shrine where our people gathered to watch.
As you wish. I'm not sure I know much more than you, at this point.
Oh thank Auri-El. Someone who's not too blinded by my crown to ask a real question. \n\nApologies. Of course, I'd be happy to chat. What would you like to know?
She's in Saintsport. The Sea Drakes lured her ship onto the rocks. Those bastards really know how to ruin your day.\n\nIt's south of <<1>>. Look for the big lighthouse.
An end to the Dominion. They want me to step down, to appoint their own regent, for everyone not of High Elven descent to leave the Summerset Isles. The list goes on and on.
I wish I could say yes. Astanya got closer than anyone else has. Subverting a watch captain. I can't believe they'd be so bold.

They're racists, High Elven supremacists with no understanding of the real world. Short-sighted misanthropes with delusions of grandeur! \n\nBastard throwbacks that should crawl back beneath their rock!

He was tossed in the Grave. It's the prison beneath Headman Bhosek's palace. He throws people in there to forget about 'em!\n\nYou can get in through the tunnel off the river. Just watch out for the traps. There's lots of traps.
Ha. Have you heard some of the rumors? My exploits have been greatly exaggerated, I can assure you. \n\nExcept the story about the bear. That one's true.

My father, King Hidellith of Alinor, passed on to Aetherius. He was a good man. As is my brother, Naemon.\n\nI returned to take my father's place, because my lifetime of experience has prepared me, honed me, to be the ruler we need.
To be blunt, the Altmer are too few. Together with the Wood Elves and Khajiit, we have the iron will, the strength of arms, and the depth of character to solve the problems facing Tamriel.
He's a brilliant Dwemer sage. Not that he's Dwemer himself, but he studies them. He's out at Bthzark, digging in the ruins there.

I do. I spent years traveling the face of Nirn. The alliance we've forged is the strongest in the world. \n\nI spent months working with the Mane and the Treethanes to create this Dominion of ours. I'm very proud of it.

Ha. No, Raz and I met while I was traveling, many years ago. We met in Wayrest. Or was it Whiterun? Something with a "W."\n\nThe story's a long one, and involves a drunken schoolmarm and a purple velvet dress. Ahem.
Thank you! While you're looking for them, I'm sure I can use any, er, distraction you provide to sneak back to our camp.
Very good. While you're slaughtering the Houndsmen, I can safely make my way to our camp.\n\nHope to see you there.
Good, and if you have to kill a few Houndsmen to get them, don't let that slow you down. Damn mer have no appreciation for music!\n\nI'll sneak back to camp during the commotion.
<Beneath a layer of grit, engravings mark the blade as Shazeem's.>
<Qawi looks at you expectantly as you pull the sword from the sand.>
Illusions? Kalari supposes that makes sense. Mathal was always learning little tricks, little … but where is he? Where is Mathal?
No! Damn it Mathal, you stupid stupid Khajiit. Why would he do this to himself? Why would he do this to me?
What? Why? Where has he gone? Kalari will drag him back here by his ears! Why would he do that to me?
Hmm. You're here about the rats. Good. I can hear them down in the well. \n\nThey must have found some way in, a back way. And lately some of the water has tasted funny. Bah!
I'd do it myself, but if <<1>> found out I'd gone down there she'd string me up. \n\nGet down there, roust out those rats, and make sure they can't get back in.
This one finds it hard to believe you've dealt with everyone already. You have helped gentle Milk Eyes with his rats?
Skooma dealers? In Shuzura's town? Dark moons! But then, surely, you couldn't have also helped cussed Ezzag with the children stealing his crops?
Shuzura is speechless. Did … was Rakhad there?
Yes … my family brewed this rum. And my father's ring. It's coming back to me!\n\nMy old blade … and my lucky dice. Now I remember! I'd even forgotten my dear companion Qawi.
Still fuzzy on that. I was bound for Daggerfall when pirates hit us. I think I was thrown overboard in the battle.

What kind of teacher would I be if you didn't learn something? You'll accompany me down into the temple and we can put an end to … whatever this is. It's through the vinewall on the far side of the main cavern. I'll meet you there!
Just so! I say, you are a learned assistant. Remind me to raise Andewen's guild stipend after this is over. She's truly a mage of great intelligence. Are you ready to begin?

Nothing! Just stand there, assistant. And observe. Using a novel application for hermetic harmonic resonance, I shall completely seal the temple. Airtight, this time, if you will. No allowing Mephala's influence to leak out.

Oh, they'll be quite all right. With the Daedric influence removed, they'll return to their old selves very soon. Actually, that's worth studying. I think I'll leave some students behind to observe their behavior.
For all we've learned here, the Falinesti Faithful may be a better resource to answer that question. Or, at least, a more entertaining one. Some of their stories are quite fanciful you know.
Ah, we've got another brave one here, do we? Well, if you're so tough, you should talk to the captain. She might be able to make use of someone who's so … courageous.
You'd better. I see a noble here surrounded by an angry mob of commoners. \n\nNow, just between you and me, I think I know what this is about. So what can you tell me that'll clear this up?
Take the ladder up from here. It's above us, high in the Great Tree.\n\nGood luck, my friend.
I didn't get a good look at them. They swept through the Fists of Thalmor like a storm of arrows.\n\nThere was nothing I could do but run.
I sense it still, for we swore to protect, even in death. There is a cottage to the south of the mounds, they may have taken it there.\n\nThe screaming in my mind, in my soul… it is agony…
The success of the Omens was never critical. This was a daydream. The nightmare begins now.\n\nYou fool. You protected your general … but you sacrificed your king!
Of course you don't.\n\nYou actually believed my manipulations would be so vulnerable? You are not even a hindrance.

Then the Dancing Scrib performers sail into the sunset aboard our ship! It wouldn't be the first time we've had to take an unscheduled bow.\n\nCome see us off at the docks after you burn down the town.
The survey team gets supplies from them every month. I tried to warn the Fists of Thalmor before they entered the forest.\n\nI was too late.

Until a few years back, Wilding Run was a village. Not a large one, but enough to be missed.\n\nThey all vanished. No one knows what happened, save that the Hound once set foot here. The Thalmor sent us to investigate.
They say he was once a Bosmer, and this was his home. With all the destruction he's brought upon us, it seemed reasonable that he may be the cause of the disappearances.\n\nNow I'm the only one left.
Dead, like those Fists of Thalmor. The creatures set upon us at night. If I hadn't been up late doing research ….\n\nI don't like to think about it. Can we talk about something else?
It was the most frightening thing! Spriggans burst from the soil and started attacking everyone. And then the fire imps started setting everything ablaze.\n\nWe barely escaped with our lives!

Just delivering supplies! A survey team works in the ruins. We keep them fed, carry correspondence, and make sure they're all right.\n\nThis is the first time anything bad's happened. Probably the last, too.

Ulthorn allowed me to think I could reach him, but his words were wrapped in Hircine's magic as the Hound.\n\nThey drew out my primal spirit, and I lusted for the hunt. I felt as the ancient Bosmer must have felt, before the Pact.
Scout Anglith, chief of the Silvenar's hunters, should know.\n\nConsidering how much you've helped us already, I can't think of anyone else who deserves the honor more than you.
Old bones and a bunch of rocks to me. If you'd asked anyone here, you'd think they'd discovered Falinesti.\n\nIf they found something, it's probably best forgotten.

Not if they got hit by the same creatures. I suppose there's no way to know for sure. Not without going in there.\n\nIf you find them, tell them to keep their heads down. Maybe whatever they woke up will go back to sleep.
Without Angof's magic, hopefully the vines will wither and die.\n\nIf not, I'm sure the Mages Guild can conjure up a spell to clear them away. I'm not too concerned about them.
<<1>>'s alive? If she made it, there's hope for the Captain, and all the rest!

The Lost Fleet, or the All Flags Fleet, was an armada sent by the Colovian Emperor, Bendu Olo, to eliminate the invading Sload. The Sload were defeated, but much of the fleet vanished without a trace.\n\nSave this compass.

Yes, but I can't put my finger on it. We've heard rumblings that things up north aren't looking any better.\n\nNot necessarily vines and such, but there are whispers of other things out there that we need to be concerned about.

I hear there's trouble in Koeglin Village. Something bad is happening up there.\n\nBut don't worry about that right now. We just saved the people of Glenumbra. We should be celebrating! Now where did I put it?
We scattered like chickens when the creatures attacked. All of our training, gone … fear is a funny thing, yes? Even the Captain panicked.
The sentiment is appreciated, but if you go in there, best take care of your own hide. Only Baan Dar knows what else is in there.
Possibly. He's a great bear of a man. If anyone survived, it'd be him.\n\nI sent a scout to search for survivors. She hasn't reported back.

Borgas was a High King of Skyrim during the First Era.\n\nHe died during the Wild Hunt of 369, in Valenwood and carried the Horn at the moment of his death. Though the Horn is in pristine condition, the Wild Hunt left no trace of Borgas's body.

Aiden Direnni was an Altmer folk-hero. According to history, he led the Direnni clan of High Rock against the Alessian Order of Cyrodiil.\n\nHe appears in myths as the last king of a heroic line, a champion in the fight of Mer against Men.
Mansel Sesnit ruled Yokuda centuries before the Redguard came to Tamriel. \n\nHis governance was brief, but eventful, laying much of the structural groundwork later Redguard rulers would utilize.
Так?
It was a violent, bloody time. The Alessians were on a holy crusade to purge every Mer who occupied this land and called it home. They destroyed anything with even the smallest connection to magic.
Wise, kind, courageous. Everything one could want from a constant companion.\n\nBut you'll see soon enough. I only hope that what you learn will help you in the present situation.

Would you stand by while those who didn't deserve to die were judged by religious zealots? Unless I strongly misjudged you, I think not.\n\nWe did what was right. And we would do it again. Which is why I'm here.

You must be insane! Guess I won't question my good fortune.\n\nThe ones I've found are dead, but I haven't seen a sign of <<1>> or the lieutenant anywhere. There's some tracks, but they don't make any sense.
Surveyor's camps. Hopefully some of them made it out. I'm not optimistic. After that, we should search the ruins.\n\nWe could try the overlook, but that's a far trek.
We came to mine, but got trapped by bears. Eventually we ran out of food, and my whole family perished.
The dead. You may have noticed, but they're a lot more lively here. Put one down and it just gets up again later … hmm.\n\nIf you see a corpse, signal me. I have some arrows that might do the trick.

Look for the tombs of the Winvale Patriarch, Matriarch, and the Scion. They were very important in their time.\n\nI'd suggest honoring the Winvale Founder's tomb last. He was really angry. Scared me witless when he just appeared out of nowhere.

I'm going to do whatever I can to make up for my mistakes. I'll get out of here and go home to Daggerfall. Find something useful to do. Maybe help my father at his tailor shop.\n\nI certainly won't be joining any other cults in the near future, not me!

It seemed like a good idea at the time. I was never let in on any big secrets or plans, though.\n\nAccording to the Founder, I joined because I'm a shiftless idiot and a lazy, good-for-nothing slob. He really ripped into me.

Yes, he surprised us all. We weren't expecting the last king of a dying people to show up on the field of battle. But he's a brilliant tactician and his advice can only help.\n\nMeanwhile, we'll send Alana's unit to put an end to Faolchu.
It's my disguise. Just a way to blend into their ranks before I make my escape.

The old Silvenar and Green Lady were diplomatic envoys for the Queen. Getting the Bosmer to work with the Dominion and so on, but they both died recently.\n\nTheir replacements somehow absorb their … spirits. I don't know how it actually works.

Bosmer tradition says the Silvenar is their spiritual side, while the Green Lady is their physical side. When both sides marry, the Bosmer are stable and balanced.\n\nThere's a new Silvenar and Green Lady at the moment, and they haven't married yet.

This one was doing a bit of clean-up in Vulkhel Guard after the Astanya incident. Heard about your problems here and thought we could lend a hand. \n\nGot here too late, of course. Your efficiency is impressive.
Ask quickly. We're in the canopy without our climbing hooks. Let's not waste time.
I should. Been a jaqspur for many years. Joined the Fists of Thalmor when the Dominion started recruiting.\n\nFigured they would need a guide. Turns out I was right.
No, but every few years this part of Valenwood gets restless. Lights in the forest, pebbles flying around … it's different every time.\n\nI've never heard of it getting this bad before.
Good. We don't have much time.

I served the Green Lady for years. Finoriell, the one before Gwaering.\n\nWhen the Dominion formed, some of us jaqspurs joined as a show of good faith. And, well, High Elves aren't exactly known for their forestry.
Strong. Taciturn. Figured actions spoke louder than words. A true Green Lady if there ever was one.\n\nWhen she passed … we all felt it. The jaqspur especially.
Nothing personal … but to my ears, you're like an old mammoth stumbling in the brush.\n\nI jest. Truly, Finoriell once said that about me. I do miss her.

Jaqspur arrows. Useful for hiding bodies when … well, sometimes you don't want them lying around.\n\nTips coated in a special oil. Nothing magical, just speeds things up a little. Hard to come by. I've only a few left.

My people, the Bosmer, believe they are two halves of our lives. The Green Lady is our physical aspect, while the Silvenar is our spiritual essence.\n\nWhen they are united, so are we. They're important to the Bosmer, and to the Dominion's stability.

He'll be as safe as his entourage can make him.\n\nDon't worry. I may embody the physical prowess of the Wood Elves, but <<c:1>> has all our spiritual strength. That's why our union is so important to my people.

My name is Gwaering, and I've only recently become the Green Lady.\n\nThe former Green Lady, my aunt Finoriell, died while traveling on behalf of the Dominion's Queen. At her death, my destiny was revealed, and I began the necessary rituals.

The Bosmer were once carefree, untroubled by things beyond Valenwood. With changing times, we also changed.\n\nThe Silvenar holds the spiritual essence of the Bosmer, and the Green Lady holds the physical aspects. Each generation, we renew our vows.

The Silvenar can be either a male or female Bosmer. No one knows who's chosen until the old Silvenar dies, and the new one awakens.\n\nI don't know much about this Silvenar yet. He's new to the role, like me, and we've many rituals to complete.

Too many, if you want to know the truth! Still, it's important for the Bosmer to see the Silvenar and Green Lady married. It keeps us stable.\n\nI'm proud of my heritage, and have renounced my worldly obligations in order to become the Green Lady.

The Silvenar senses the emotions of his people, and we sense his. Without the union between the Silvenar and the Green Lady, the Bosmer would be guided only by emotions.\n\nThe Green Lady balances that with instinct and action. The Bosmer need both.

Help the locals. They'll need all the help they can get. Raz hopes he can find some intel here, perhaps unearth some new leads.\n\nThis one has sent agents to every town in Auridon. If there are more like this Valano out there, we shall find them.
So far as Raz knows, yes. She left not long after you did for Tanzelwil. This one is sure she'll be happy to see you there.
Yes. Razum-dar works with the Queen as a member of a small group. A group he thinks you would be ideally suited for.\n\nWe are called the Eyes of the Queen.

We serve at the pleasure of the Queen. She often asks us to investigate issues she finds troubling. Sometimes, you understand, the jackboots of the Marines are a bit too noisy.\n\nSo she sends the Eyes. To … watch.
Raz looks around Silsailen, and he is impressed with your efficiency. You've done good work here against the Veil. We would be lucky to have someone such as you.
She has gone to a place called Tanzelwil, north of here. An ancient Altmer custom, where monarchs speak with those who have come before.\n\nAs a Khajiit, it is something Raz can respect.
We are trapped. We hold the door against the Colovians, but that is all the good news Raz has to report. Beyond the door here the ruin has collapsed. We cannot reach you and you cannot reach us.
We cannot risk it. The tales of the circlet make it a clear and present threat to the Queen and all of the Dominion. It must be destroyed … even though it may cost Raz his life.
Raz and his men came down here knowing what had to be done. You do not know me, but … Raz must trust you to do what we cannot. You must unlock the shrine behind you and destroy the circlet.

So to open their portals the Supernal mages are channeling negative dismay-waves from the dreaming cultists. Positive Scamp-head meets negative dismay, and poof! \n\nAnything else? I need to rescue Master Muzgu.

It's an Ayleid ruin. Years ago, Breton raiders attacked us. An outnumbered patrol held there for weeks until they were wiped out. Later, our army destroyed the raiders.\n\nIt's just a ruin, really. I don't know what the Bloodthorn want with it.

It's a graveyard. Not ours—Breton. When we conquered the islands hundreds of years ago, War Chief Yzzgol left it intact out of respect for our enemies.\n\nWe don't desecrate graves, but the Bloodthorn Cult will. Plenty of fresh bodies.
It's mostly wilderness. There are Ayleid ruins, but they were looted long ago.\n\nI don't know what the Bloodthorns want there, but Laganakh might know more.

Once the Worm Cult's hold weakened, we destroyed our prison. Though we spurned Y'ffre's will, we don't deserve servitude to necromancers!\n\nI am the <<1>>. When we were imprisoned, I chose to serve as envoy between Y'ffre's faithful and my kin.
She is my puppet, just like all the other creatures in this story. Her weaknesses allowed me to enter.\n\nYou can't thwart me. You know nothing of the spinners and the power they wield!
You may know me by my Daedric title, but for now, I play the part of the Hound. I created a wedge between the Silvenar and the Green Lady.\n\nThe Hound is a convenient scapegoat for my invention.
The Bloodthorn Cult assaulted the fortress. They were repulsed, but they stole a Breton scroll the Orcs found here long ago. Chief Tazgol thinks the attack failed but I'm not so sure.
The cultists retreated after the initial assault; they came here to steal that scroll, I'm sure of it. But why? Have they set a trap for us? We must know before the chief decides to attack.
The Oathbreakers. We spurned Y'ffre's will, and we paid the price. Our lives.\n\nY'ffre can be just as cruel as she is compassionate. Beware the wrath of gods, mortal.
Sure, I know <<1>>! His mother Iriel is just over there by the merchants tents.
That name is not familiar, no.\n\nThis one has been too busy not selling anything to learn the local's names.
Sure, I know <<1>>! Why, his mother is just over there by the targets!
Going to combine these and plant them and see what happens.

Yes. Time to get rid of the Red Rooks. Anyone who wants to help is welcome.\n\nDon't bring attention to yourself in town and they should leave you alone. Speak to Tamien Sellan. He's upstairs at the Inn.

Use the Direnni magic of your armor to spot the covert Shadow Scouts before they can do any significant damage, then dispatch them with extreme prejudice. Simple enough, really.\n\nBut I'm actually very curious about you.
I appreciate you saying that, but this isn't one I can just shake off. It's my burden though, and I must bear it.\n\nBut enough of this dreary talk. Come with me to the throne room.

Indeed. For the sake of Stormhaven and for the sake of the Daggerfall Covenant as a whole.\n\nEnough dreary talk though. The good news is that Vaermina and her Daedra are gone. Come with me to the throne room.

I am too, and I owe you for that. And more, really.\n\nYou were the one who acted nobly in there. Not me. You had enough courage for both of us. I was broken—you saw me. I can only hope this experience will make me a stronger, a better king.
Once the body expires, we bring the soul to rest here, in Treehenge. Forever, I suppose.\n\nThe spinners then begin the tale of the next Green Lady.
I can't pretend to know. But if the Worm Cult is here, they want the matrons' souls for some vile purpose.

These old Ayleid eyes see many things. Everyone in this yard, for example, radiates an aura of life force.\n\nBut not you. Your aura's missing. I can't tell if you're not truly alive or you just don't belong. I've never seen magic like this before.
Not really. The mammoths usually sleep it off, but this time they got out. And they really, really hate to be woken up.\n\nBut I'm sure you'll have no trouble! I mean, just stand back a bit!

Founder of the Rangers. Every time we regrow the village, we find him a new resting place. Rangers don't forget Rangers. Not now, not ever.\n\nFollow me. I'll take point, but you'll get to do the fun stuff.
I made a bet with my friend, <<1>>. We're both Adepts at the hall in Vulkhel Guard.\n\nI bet her that I could find more relics than she did in a two week span.
Simple. Set fire to those crates one by one until she talks. Either she talks or the tunnel explodes!\n\nMaybe rocks will crush her. Or she'll burn alive. It's all such a mystery!
Gloo tells me they've wisely filled those crates over there with kindlepitch. \n\nI think we'll use them to convince this dog to bark.
Would you? That's unbelievably kind. You'll be three-times blessed in Aetherius. \n\nI should warn you: Angrel's something of a terrible person. And, sincerely, thank you.
Someone who must remain secret. For now.\n\nBut time is wasting. You need to understand that this curse must not be broken.
You have to understand. Akatosh. Daedra. It didn't matter who heard me. I just wanted my baby to live.
Allow me to clear your eyes.\n\nThere. A bit more in … focus.

Perhaps. Perhaps not. But this is neither the time nor the place for this conversation. We shall meet again and then we shall see what we shall see.\n\nBut now we have a battle to win. I appreciate your report.
Honesty! A most redeeming quality. But we will have to speak of this later, when matters are less pressing.\n\nRight now we have a battle to win. I appreciate your report.

The moon kisses the rivers flowing through here in beams from the sky, The stars travel on gossamer wings, in torchbugs gracing frond and leaf.\n\nTake them to the altar, and they will guide her back. Go now. You must not delay.

How? He's just a man, my love. I'll stick my sword in him a few times until he drops. Then I'll stab him again!\n\nI'll be back in no time, carrying his head high as a trophy. I can't think of a better gift to celebrate our new family.

I like to see what the world has to offer. I have traveled to many places. The golden sands of Alik'r, the icy hills of Eastmarch, the murky swamps of Shadowfen. I have seen them all!\n\nMany places to see. Many things to learn. And many more to go!
My journey isn't planned. It just happens.\n\nThis town could be a good place to settle for a while, now that the troubles are over. Perhaps I will stay here until I move on.

I lost a game of cards, if you must know. A merchant needed protection and I foolishly used my usual fee to stake my bet.\n\nThis one really should not drink the meads and the ales or gamble before consumating a contract.

You're the hero of Malabal Tor! Turned back the Redguards at Velyn Harbor, fought the Drublog in Dra'bul and Jathsogur, and trounced the Hound in Silvenar!\n\nI've had many a toast in your name, friend,

I'll stay in Silvenar for the handfast celebration. I want to try this "rotmeth" I've heard so much about.\n\nAfter, I might go to Reaper's March. I hear they have fine drink up there. You can tell a lot about people from what they drink.
Hroggi the Landstrider, traveler of the world! A true Nord doesn't let the snow melt under his feet.\n\nNot many know my name yet. But now I can say I've met you!
A prison of the mind. Built for who I once was. Hircine gazed into my soul, turning memories into a torturous labyrinth.\n\nOne part of me escaped. And Hircine made it into a weapon.

Deep within the prison, where <<1>> cracks his mind like a nut. If she succeeds, she will hollow him out and make him into one of her servants.\n\nHis shell will roam Nirn, hunting and killing everyone he ever knew.

Simply pass this barrier. See the items on the table? Three memories, meant to steel a Hound's resolve.\n\nChoose correctly and the barrier falls. Choose poorly … and her servants will have fresh prey.
I couldn't leave the lieutenant behind. I dragged him back to camp before I came looking for you.
Continue to scout for the Fists of Thalmor. Someone needs to look out for these mammoths in the brush.\n\nIf we meet again, the drinks are on me!
Don't look so surprised! I can navigate the forest, especially since you kept the spirits' attention.\n\nThe hardest part was keeping his wounds closed.
I am as the Artificer named me. Mephala. Webspinner, debaser, and consumer. Have you enjoyed sparring with my newest Deathweavers?
Nothing like an empty mind, waiting, yearning for purpose. The lost city, the lost Faithful, the great Artificer, all tremble in the web of Mephala.
I have no answers for you, child. None that would satisfy you, anyway. Now, take your Artificer and go. The temple doors are open. You've done your part here today.
The Houndsmen. They wanted <<Ac:1>>. I wouldn't tell them where it was hidden.\n\nWhoever you are, you must make certain the Hound doesn't obtain it!
A weight off my mind! Thank you so much. Now I can rest.
I'm sorry … I haven't the strength to help you. I must rest ….

Who, not what. The Daggers. A mercenary group out of Daggerfall. They're highly trained and extremely deadly. Or so they tell me. They're also lost!\n\nBut they do work cheap, which makes them perfect for my purposes.

I am Gwilgoth, assistant to Treethane Thalrinel of Silvenar. I regret to say the treethane is currently indisposed.\n\nShe suffered greatly at the hands of the Houndsmen, and is in recovery. Is there anything else I can do for you?
They left hours ago and we haven't heard a word since. Only Bumnog returned, which is why he's available to help you.\n\nWhy are you still here? Get out there and find the missing Daggers!

How quaint. No, the Silvenar and the Green Lady are nobles among the Bosmer, but the treethane runs the city itself.\n\nCertainly, no request made by either would be ignored. But surely you can't see the Silvenar doing book-keeping?

I'm busy organizing the restoration of the city, as well as the celebration for the wedding. The Khajiit guests have been most … challenging.\n\nThough handfasting is complete, there must be revelry on this joyous occasion!

Torture of a most brutal kind. They began questioning immediately after they captured the city.\n\nBut their efforts led to naught. When you killed the Hound, they fled like beaten dogs. We are in your debt.
You've invaded my home. You've slaughtered my people. Why would I help you, Orc? You'll kill us all anyway.
Do you think me mad? I'll not betray my husband. You'll kill us both.\n\nNo, Orc. Renwic will finish his spell, and he will wipe you all out.
I know nothing about his plans.\n\nI thought Orcs had honor. Now you threaten unarmed prisoners? We have surrendered. Ransom us like civilized folk.
Savage Orc. Do what you will. I will not betray my king or the royal family.\n\nWhen the mainland hears of what you've done, they will crush you.

It's Baron Sorick, the lord of this district. There's all this trouble with the dreugh, but he just blithely watches from the top floor of Arbogasque's house, apparently enjoying it. \n\nI don't like it. The whole situation smells wrong.
The Orcs fooled us. The beach attack was a feint. Many others landed elsewhere. They waited until we were committed here. Then the rest headed for the keep. We have failed … I have failed.
The island is lost. Run to the keep and tell the royal family. Get them to the shore and sail them away.\n\nWe'll hold the beach as long as we can.
Treehenge is the resting place of the vessels of the Green Lady. When the Green Lady's mortal body dies, we bring their souls to this holy place.\n\nIt's as much a library of knowledge as a tomb.

Just hand you one of my famous dishes? Not a chance. Perhaps a trade though. I'm running low on sugar leaf, which grows wild hereabouts.\n\nYou collect three leaves for me and I'll give you some of my famous Goblin's Delight.

Much, comrade. And not enough. Aelif had Jofnir appear to the council, to Merric. They were reluctant to believe, but they could not deny Guildmaster Iceblade. His testimony is one of the reasons she did not release him to Sovngarde.

This "Mortuum Vivicus" Aelif has heard so much about? She does not know. Those visions of the past you saw in Ragnthar, at Abagarlas, made it sound like a potent threat. But … what if Colors was behind all of that? Aelif does not know.

Yes, she is. Very eager. Aelif has resented Colors since the day she took over. This obsession with the Daedra, with the anchors … together we will put an end to her foolish leadership and this unwinnable crusade.

A foolish war against the might of a Daedric Prince? Why would Aelif want to put an end to that? This one has the backing of the generals, comrade. You may be speaking with the new Guildmaster after today.

The Daggers were hired to help Lord Diel gather research about the harpies. We get him what he needs and we get paid. Simple as pie.\n\nBut now the rest of the Daggers are missing. We need to find them and make sure our first mission is a success.
Rrr! A skooma lab? In my well? Get me my blade! It's around here somewhere. \n\nWe'll go back down there together. You just point me in their direction and I'll cut them to giblets.

With my skooma-peddling rats dead, it should be nice and quiet out here.\n\nEzzag complains about trouble at his farm when we play cards, though. And I heard that little Kalari girl crying about her uncle's house. Might see if they need a hand.
Excellent! I have a little Goblin's Delight left from my last batch. Didn't want to part with it until I had enough sugar leaves to make another batch. \n\nHere you go—enjoy!
Stormhaven is safe, thanks to you. And I'd say the Daggerfall Covenant has more than a fighting chance. I'd put my money on it, at least.

Now to mix in my special ingredient … there! Zich sometimes sleeps under the bridge. Go put the food on his pallet and hide nearby. He won't come by while you're there.\n\nTime for that rodent to die!

I've kept my eyes and ears open. They've been forcing me to scout the area, but they haven't been paying all that much attention to me.\n\nThe envoy and the Red Rook leader, they kind of hate each other, from what I could see.
I am too, my friend. I am too. \n\nI heard the king was ill, and I understand we suffered from similar afflictions.

While you were talking to Milk Eyes, Tazia was patching some holes in the well, and … well. She fell in. \n\nIt looks like the old cat has bigger problems than rats! Do you smell that? They're running a skooma lab down here!

Tazia is going to hide right here. She's no smuggler-killer. As for what you should do, the chemicals they use are very flammable. You might be able to smash up the tables. Then just find a torch or a lamp. Burn the lab all at once!

Disgusting. Uncultured. Devious. His guards are criminals and his laws benefit only himself.\n\nI pray to Auri-El that the sea rises up and swallows this pit. But only after Jakarn and I are long gone.
Very smart. You are a wise counselor. \n\nAfter I speak with the king, I will make my apology. Thank you, my friend. For everything.
I am … a little distracted, but yes, I came to pay my respects.\n\nSeeing Sister Safia here has caught me off-guard. Do you think … do you think she could ever forgive me?
You don't know? We—the Bosmer, I mean—don't eat plants. We don't farm and we certainly don't cut down trees!\n\nIn exchange, the forest provides for us. You've seen our homes? They're grown that way!
Well, I only heard a little when Dabienne reported back. Something about crazy villagers locking her up and planning terrible things.\n\nHow about you tell me what happened?
I … I think so. I can feel again. My roots go deep into the earth. It … stings a bit.\n\nThe matrons want to thank you, but I fear their pride prevents them. So I will. Thank you.

So many people … they died when the Bloodthorn cult devastated Eagle's Brook.\n\nIn return for my cooperation, the Red Rooks promised to protect my father and the people of Eagle's Brook from the Bloodthorns. They lied. For that, they need to pay.

The cult focused all their power into their abominations. Now these are dust and ash. The threat to us is ended, but the threat to you remains.\n\n<<1>> wishes to repay our debt to you. Speak to him. Learn your true peril.

Sternis Gelves. He's the real threat. Without him, the Red Rooks are just disorganized thugs looking for pockets to pick and purses to snatch.\n\nIt was his idea to take over Crosswych. He's building an empire here.
Oh, didn't I say? Forgive me, my memory is often as insubstantial as I am these days.\n\nMy wife was the captain of the town guard. She was dedicated, and she never turned from her duty.

If you find one of Rosalind's keepsakes, it should help strengthen your connection and allow you to see her final moments as you follow her path.\n\nThe stronger your connection, the better chance you'll have of lifting this curse and setting us free.
We have an army of lamias to deal with. \n\nOur solution is decapitation—kill their leader, and they will abandon their objective. It's our only chance to gain a foothold on this island.

The Seamount Orcs attacked generations ago. They took our island. Under their rule, what we called Betony became Betnikh.\n\nMy failure to defend my people was unforgivable, but how I attempted to defeat the Orcs was worse.

I attempted necromancy. An ancient Ayleid Relic is buried on this island. The Bloodthorn seek its power.\n\nEnter the portal beside me. You will see my last day through the eyes of my enemies. Learn what you can.
This group waits on the beck and call of a powerful lamia matriarch who decimated our forces as we arrived. She has since retired to the caves above.\n\nWe need her dead.
This you must do alone. I have an invasion force to coordinate, and I need you as a spearhead.\n\nThe island caves are up ahead. Good luck.
This is going to be a bigger challenge than I thought.\n\nMaybe a comic tale. "How the Constable Got His Comeuppance." You'd be the hero, of course. I'm sure I can make a good story of it.
Oh. I suppose I can work with that.
Terrible things? Always a crowd-pleaser. What kind of terrible things?
Ooh, slavers! That's good. The crowd always loves slavers—as villains, that is. \n\nSo you fought a great battle against them, one against many and then defeated their captain in single combat?
Ah. Good point. Dabienne might not like that. It's a shame. \n\nA romance always generates good tips. Well, a heroic tale it will be! Thank you for your help.
Wonderful! Slavers, swordplay, and a romance—I can hear it all now. It's sure to be a crowd pleaser. \n\nIs there anything else?
Wonderful, a heroic fight scene for the finish. \n\nAnd then Dabienne swooned in your arms as you freed her from the stocks?

Yes. My family ruled Betony for nine generations. That came to an end this day.\n\nThe memory behind you is that of Drago Aubertin, one my bravest soldiers. Enter it, find Captain Seline, and learn our fate.

Please, but do hurry. I worry that the wolves will chew up my book of patterns.\n\nI've made dresses and suits for nobles. Very elegant garments. The patterns in the book are priceless. Without them, my business is finished.
No. I could not abandon Betony.\n\nOnce my family was safe, Drago and I led a small vanguard in search of a legend from the time of the Ayleids.

Orcs led by Warcaller Targoth pursued us. Drago and my vandguard died so I could escape. At last, I came to the doorway to an Ayleid ruin, lost for centuries.\n\nTargoth followed me. Enter his memories and witness my fate.
Whispers spoke of a relic hidden somewhere on the island—an ancient Ayleid weapon that could summon an invincible army.

Yes. Once I summoned the relic's power, I realized what it demanded of me. Souls. It craves souls.\n\nI would not pay that price, but the Bloodthorn will. They will raise this undead army and slaughter you all.
Tazia grabbed you, got you out of there. There was an explosion, like we hoped, and then smoke and fumes from the skooma. We won't have to worry about that lab anymore.

Much like the Green Lady, the Silvenar's chosen. He or she always represents Bosmer spirituality. The current Silvenar's Bosmer name is Indaenir.\n\nI don't understand how the choices are made. It's a blessing bestowed upon them.
The Silvenar is the Green Lady's consort. He's our spiritual leader. Their marriage balances the Bosmer's inner and outer senses.

The Silvenar is our spiritual leader, and can be either male or female.\n\nEach generation brings with it a new Silvenar and Green Lady. Once they marry, the Bosmer's feral and spiritual sides unite, bringing us balance.

The mysteries of Nirn span beyond the Dwemer. The Ayleids fascinate me in equal measure. I had to see this place for myself.\n\nThe more vexing mystery at present, however, lies with these Orc spirits.

What would you have me say? The Prince of Lies is everywhere. He undermines Meridia's efforts, places whispers in our ears. I tried to explain it to Jofnir in Ragnthar, but he wouldn't listen. He refused to hear my words.

No, no. With my skooma-peddling rats dead, it should be nice and quiet out here.\n\nThat fat bastard Ezzag complains about trouble at his farm when we play cards, though. Might see if he needs a hand.

With my skooma-peddling rats dead, it should be nice and quiet out here. But now that you mention it, I heard that little Kalari girl crying about her uncle's house yesterday. \n\nNice girl, reads to me sometimes. Might see if she needs a hand.
With my skooma-peddling rats dead, it should be nice and quiet out here.\n\nWhy don't you go back to that lecherous wreck of a Clan Mother and see if she has anything else for you to do, hmm?
A Daedric prince, like Molag Bal. But totally unlike that cruel monster. \n\nMeridia is the Sunfire, enemy of the undead, beacon to all that live.
Yes. Surely you have seen the darkness within Aelif. I didn't know, not for certain, but … I believe she serves the Lord of Lies, and consorts with his minions!

You see it before you. The Mortuum Vivicus. After our time in Abagarlas, I knew that stopping this monstrous creation must be my priority. The Lady sent me a vision, a dark path through Oblivion. It's taken me all this time ….
Even you must have noticed the ghostly figures in the field. This is no ordinary haunting. Something brought them back and binds them here. \n\nI suspect the answer is inside the catacombs.
Indeed you should. The ruin is sealed magically, but it is a minor challenge. I shall unseal the door for you and await your return. My research is best done in safety.

An end to the dark plots of necromancers. The culling of cultists, and the death of Daedra. In short, she's offended by the God of Schemes. She will stop this weapon, and crush his champions beneath her heel.
I know. I should have.\n\nBut Merric is a servant of Stendarr. I feared he would react badly to my love of the Lady. As if she were like that foul schemer Molag Bal.
Yes! Snatched from Tamriel just as the Ayleids were to destroy it. Lurking here all this time, like a caged beast, while Molag Bal fed it soul after soul … restoring it to unholy potency.
Hah! Ezzag knew it. That Shuzura, thinks she is so smart. Did you deal with them? Is their leader lying in a puddle of blood, somewhere?

Not for Ezzag … but over cards this one's friend Milk Eyes complains of rats down his well. The old fool is likely to try killing them himself, if no one takes care of the problem. That's what we need, a blind man down a well.

Not for Ezzag … but over cards this one's friend Milk Eyes complains of rats down his well. And his niece Kalari just inherited his brother's home. She has said there is something wrong with it … ghosts?\n\nPerhaps you help them, as you did Ezzag.
Not for Ezzag … but his niece Kalari just inherited his brother's home. She has said there is something wrong with it … ghosts?\n\nPerhaps you help her, as you did Ezzag.
No, Ezzag is happy now. You have saved him from the bandits. Perhaps you go back to the Clan Mother, tell her how nice Ezzag has been to you, yes?

They are the sea-cousins of the Altmer, and have been our sworn enemies for generations.\n\nWe suspected they were planning an attack against Malabal Tor, so we struck first. The size of their invasion force … surprised us.

Our agents on the mainland reported strange lights, ambient auras, and sudden lightning storms off the coast of this island, a known Maormer territory.\n\nI believe they are preparing powerful weather magic.
Well, I may have to fill in a few gaps—a chase or a mystical amulet or something.\n\nDon't worry, you'll be famous!

Nightmares? Dremora? No, that's just too much. You can't just throw anything into the tale. \n\nI think a jealous constable will work much better. And we don't mention the Daedra. That will be much better. You'll see.
Now? We wreck their camp. Burn and pillage everything that takes your fancy. Siege weapons, tents, cargo—you name it!
Listen well. I have located a safe harbor from which we might plan our course of action. You must meet me there.
Your instinct is dead on. After you've had a chance to frolic, head towards the other part of the ruin. Take out this Festius and his aides. \n\nDon't worry. I know Nendaer's smiling on us.
I awoke upon a sandy shore—a stretch of beach outside a bustling city of Elves. Vulkhel Guard. \n\nThe Harborage is in a seaside cave, outside the city. It is there that you will find me.
Listen well. I have located a safe harbor from which we might plan our course of action. You must meet me there.
I awoke in a city of Bretons, its air heavy with the smells of baked bread, horses, and intrigue. Daggerfall. \n\nThe Harborage is in an abandoned cave, outside the city.
Listen well. I have located a safe harbor from which we might plan our course of action. You must meet me there.
I awoke to choking ash in the air and the sounds of strife. I am in Morrowind, home of the Dark Elves, in a city called Davon's Watch. \n\nThe Harborage is a ruin in the cliffs, west of the city.
Why do I have to explain these things to you? Just talk to Bumnog. He knows what I hired the Daggers to do.\n\nNow stop pestering me and let me enjoy all this nature that my sons keep going on about.

Everyone has to start someplace. Even the Fighters Guild had a first mission, didn't they? Who are you to judge?\n\nNow let's get out there and do what we're getting paid for. Let's find the Daggers and bring back their research!
Harpies, eggs, whatever we can bring back so Lord Diel can figure out why these birds have become so violent lately.
Prepare yourself. The journey is difficult.
This one collects the means to return home. Will the kind stranger help?

We have to find the missing Daggers! Gelvin, our leader, and the Remly brothers. We find them and help them finish their jobs.\n\nAnd while we're at it, we look for the queen birdy, Foulwing. She's a vicious killer and she needs to be dealt with.
Exalted friend, I am grateful beyond words.
I am of the Green, of the dark and growing depths. My lifeblood pulses through the roots. My skin smells of loam.
For now. I sense a darkness, a growing corruption. If the grovetenders are kept away from their charge much longer … it may begin to … fade.
An echo of <<1>>, before he became the Hound. When he left this place, his hunt for the Green Lady consumed him. Exactly as Hircine intended.\n\nEverything else was left behind. I was left behind.

Then you would free the spirits of Westtry's innocent villagers, ending their bondage to this place.\n\nHowever, the danger to mortal travelers would remain, and the living will never find welcome or solace within Westtry's borders.

Then you must destroy the enraged wraiths and make Westtry safe for mortal travelers once again.\n\nBut that will leave the innocent spirits of Westtry's villagers trapped here forever, bound to the haunted town.
I … you're right. You're absolutely right.\n\nI've been acting like a Wood Elf. No more! Chief Ugorz goes where he wants, and the Taskmaster will like it! I'll meet you at the overlook.
Tempting. If I were an idiot. The Overseer stationed a Taskmaster here to keep me in line, and Suronii wants me to risk his wrath?\n\nShe should know better. She's seen the Taskmasters work.

You … killed her? Incredible! That's strength I can respect, friend.\n\nAll right, I'm in. With a warrior like you in our corner, maybe Suronii's scheme is more reasonable than I thought. I hope to see you at the overlook.
My house is a mess, filled with food, pots, pans, cookbooks, and so on. I gave up on cleaning it and just live out here now.
This one … wants to believe you.\n\nVery well. I will meet you at the Overseer's overlook. Just don't tell the Taskmaster.
This one cannot leave, on threat of endless death from Taskmaster upstairs.\n\nYou are mad to come here—they have not taken you. You should flee while you can.

Huh. That is … surprising.\n\nThis one always thought that any who would challenge Taskmaster would be five kinds of dead. This one … supposes she can stop working, now. Zirani will go to the overlook. You should come with us.
Of course. I have been Akkhuz-ri's Speaker for years. Our relationship is far older than this Dominion we struggle to keep together. Ask me what you will.

Let Kalari read that … so Rakhad threatens my life directly, and Mathal thinks to save me through fear. The typical thinking of a stupid, stupid brother.\n\nHe died for Kalari, that idiot. Such a waste ….
No, Kalari would like some time alone to think now. Perhaps you could help old Milk Eyes? \n\nKalari reads to him, sometimes, and as of late he has been complaining of rats in his well.

No, Kalari would just like some time alone to think now. Perhaps you could help old Milk Eyes? Kalari reads to him, sometimes, and as of late he's been complaining of rats in his well. Or Uncle Ezzag? He says someone has been stealing from his field.
No, Kalari would like some time alone to think now. Perhaps you could help Uncle Ezzag? He says someone has been stealing from his field. Uncle likes to tell stories, but he has been very insistent.
No, Kalari would like some time alone to think now. You have done so much for her. You should go speak to the Clan Mother.\n\nTell her of all you have done for S'ren-ja.

You interrupted the flow of that Conduit Stone, causing an overload. Maormer equipment can be delicate.\n\nIt is well that you did—Maormer use Conduit Stones to enhance their magic. It will be more difficult for them to maintain this storm, now.

Let Kalari read that … so Rakhad threatens my life directly, and Mathal thinks to save me through fear. The typical thinking of a stupid, stupid brother.\n\nHe may be a coward, but at least he is safe. Bright moons.
No, Kalari would like some time alone to think now. Perhaps you could help old Milk Eyes? \n\nKalari reads to him, sometimes, and as of late he has been complaining of rats in his well.

No, Kalari would like some time alone to think now. Perhaps you could help old Milk Eyes? Kalari reads to him, sometimes, and as of late he has been complaining of rats in his well. Or Uncle Ezzag? He says someone has been stealing from his field.
No, Kalari would like some time alone to think now. Perhaps you could help Uncle Ezzag? He says someone has been stealing from his field. Uncle likes to tell stories, but he has been very insistent.
No, Kalari would like some time alone to think now. You have done so much for her. You should go speak to the Clan Mother.\n\nTell her of all you have done for S'ren-ja.

The scouts report that there are two more Conduits Stones to deal with, one up ahead, and one at the summit of this mountain.\n\nMy soldiers and I must tend to the wounded, but we'll guard your rear as you advance. The lamias have all but fled.
Who knows? It may come to that. Haven is a long way away, but it was a warning to all of us. No stronghold is safe. I'm just glad you're here. There's no one I would trust more with such a task.

I don't … can't know for sure. He never even showed an interest in magic! He's always been a good leader. Quieter than usual these last years, but I just thought he was adjusting to our new Alliance. Dark Moons. Dark Moons.

His true name is Akkhuz-ri. We've been friends since we were children. He was brought up by the lunar clergy, as all Manes are. I was the son of Elsweyr nobility. We both knew we'd make our mark on the world. I never thought it would be like this.

When we were younger I had fears that Akkhuz-ri would be taken captive. The Mane would make for a tempting hostage, I thought. We had Mages enchant a ring he wears on his right hand. My prayer caught up to this ring, and told me where he'd gone.

Fha! This one spits in the face of death. Of course, that spit may contain a trickle of blood, but ….\n\nNo, I am all right. The healers have already patched me up. The moon shines upon your face, I see. Is there any way I can help you?

Lord Gharesh-ri knows more, but his vision may be colored by hope. Mine is not. The Mane has always been greedy and self-serving, but lately he has been cruel. His orders do not benefit the Khajiit as they once did.\n\nHe changed before we came here.

We're trying to capture a few of these creatures. Lord Diel wants to observe the harpies and see if they demonstrate any odd behavior that might explain the recent acts of aggression.\n\nBut we're still working on our traps, as you can see.

We've got some throwing snares. The only problem is the damn harpies are too strong. They need to be weakened before you hit them with the throwing snares.\n\nI may have a sword, but I'm not a fighter. That's too dangerous an approach for me.
I was raised by the knights you cut down. They taught me to be brave. I'll not beg.\n\nFather will cast all of you into Oblivion!
Now that we have a cure to Faolchu's strain of lycanthropy, General Mandin and I decided to search Glenumbra for remnants of the curse. \n\nWe're going to root it out!
Slowly and dangerously. I hope Mandin is having more success than I am. \n\nThe Red Rooks have certainly been an annoyance. The more of them you put in the ground, the better.
Lord Diel said a few. So four, I'd say. Yes, four harpies should do.\n\nIf this works, please tell his lordship that we gave you the traps, all right?
Famished! Haven't had anything to eat since they tied me up.\n\nThe Houndsmen will pay for this. Once I've gotten my strength back, that is.

The mantle of the Green Lady passes from generation to generation, but not usually from one family member to another.\n\nOur aunt was the previous Green Lady, so it's quite exciting Gwaering's been chosen this time.
I don't think they know Gwaering, the Green Lady, is my sister. They were looking for easy prey.\n\nHah, I put up quite a fight! Nothing was easy for them.
A temporary insanity, brought on by the Worm Cult. They will remain steadfast to their duties.\n\nOnce the spriggans have cleansed the cultists from Treehenge, she will be able to take root.
<This door is sealed by a force you cannot overcome.>
I thought the pass was a short cut, get me closer to Daggerfall. I'm not really good with maps, though. \n\nI'm not anywhere near Daggerfall, am I?

Yes, well … I'm a spontaneous sort. Yes. Spontaneous. Grab my tools and take to the road. Go where the moment takes me. \n\nI wanted a fresh start. Adventure! Excitement! I hadn't considered the wolves, though.
I am Targoth, Warcaller of the Stonewolves. Cultists have violated my tomb and those of my warriors. The vile priestess Drusilla leads the cult, dragging our spirits back to this realm.
In life, I wielded a magical war horn. My soldiers obeyed it, hearing its call across all barriers. Drusilla now uses it to call my warriors from beyond the grave, binding them to her will.
She is in the lower chambers. Kill her before she can send my soldiers against our descendants. That will free me from her bonds. Then the horn can return my warband to its honored rest.

Hey, and one more thing. I really appreciate what you did for the villagers. \n\nTake this whistle. Use it to call up some reinforcements when you're in the camp. It's the least I can do for a noble soul like yourself.
Good. Now let's finish this. \n\nFor the Rangers. For the villagers we lost today ….
Loss, death, pain. Sometimes Daedra are to blame. It's hard to say.
For now. <<1>> always got a little strange every few years. Spirits, strange lights. It's different every time.
