Why, we're a merry band of peacekeepers! We focus on diplomacy and matters of the soul.\n\nYeah, right. We're an elite band of soldiers. The forest's own shock troops.

In the old days, before the Dominion, our woods lore was the only advantage we had over the other races. Khajiit can see in the dark better than we can. High Elves have always been better spellslingers than we have.
Hrm. Not much like one. How do I know this isn't a trick?\n\nWell, if you give my shield back, I'll let you off the hook. This time.
You know, the eyes and ears of Daggerfall? That's how King Casimir keeps track of what's going on in the city.\n\nBut you didn't hear about it from me.
We've cut the legs out from under the Maormer.\n\nWe need only deliver the killing blow, and shutting down the last Conduit Stone should do it. It should be just ahead.

Ha! To hear him tell it, it was all his idea. Vanus Galerion, First Mage of Firsthold, was the real founder of the guild. Rilis just allowed him to do his work in the city. \n\nI heard rumors he even bargained with Galerion for access to Oblivion.

Oh.  I should have listened to ….\n\nWell, anyway, if you help me get my things, I'll stick to the main roads until I reach a safe settlement. Aldcroft sounds fine. I'm just anxious to get going. Fresh start and all that.

That sounds like my sweet Odei. Kindest man in the world but as helpless as a kitten. \n\nWe spent the night at the Lion Guard camp nearby and he must've wandered off. He sleepwalks sometimes. Odei's not used to rough living.

Oh, I do hope he isn't frightened. Even deer tend to startle poor Odei.\n\nI was taking him to my mother's home in Wayrest. She just loves Odei to pieces. I can better concentrate on my job if I know Odei's safe.
Yes. I remember him. Who could forget a name like that? \n\nFontbonne enlisted a few months ago and asked to be sent straight to the front lines. May be hard to find. What do you need with him?
You have his inheritance? That's certainly something he'll want to receive. \n\nI'll send word out to get his location, and then I'll send a special courier to ensure this gets to him.
Good luck. I'll see you back on the ship.
My pleasure.\n\nMeet me outside the palace. I'll pick out something special for you.
Get your disguise and meet me out back. Leave Bhosek to me.
I like your confidence. Let's see what you can do.
Let me know if there are any lingering effects. Twitching, mainly. I'm quite curious about the twitching.
Of course. I have no doubt you'll be up to the task.
The Great Tree, of course! You know … the massive tree we're standing under.\n\nIt easily towers over Daggerfall Castle. Simply magnificent!
Yes, exactly! You see, I'm an architect by trade. The structures in High Rock lack finesse.\n\nI came here for inspiration and found it!
I've seen the White-Gold Tower in Cyrodiil. My next stop is the Crystal Tower on Summerset, if the Thalmor allow my passage. \n\nWhat can I say? I love grand structures!

Help? The Daggers don't need any … oh, who am I kidding? I'm the leader of the Daggers and we don't have a clue as to what we're doing out here.\n\nIf you're willing, we'd appreciate any help you care to provide.
I was collecting unhatched harpy eggs to bring back to camp. One of the things Lord Diel needs to complete his research.\n\nI got one egg, but we need to collect a few more.

In the nests above. Be gentle with them. I don't want the hatchlings to come to any harm. I'm going to rest a moment and then head back to camp.\n\nWith the gold his lordship pays us, the Daggers can really make a go of this mercenary thing.

Yeah. I hear their leader, Hosni at-Tura's gone a little soft in the head. The Midnight Union's still here, mind you. Operation here's run by a Khajiit over at the Cloudy Dregs. \n\nI hear he's not in very good favor with his boss these days, though.

I got this tip on where to find the Grinder. His boys contact him by knocking on this drum down by the docks.\n\nNone of my guards have the guts to go after him. Frankly, neither do I. If you're willing, though, there's a reward in it.
I overheard them mention the ruin of Carzog's Demise. Whatever they are planning, it is to take place there. \n\nBut that is not my concern. Now that you have the horn, free my warriors.
How can rain fall from the sky? How can rivers flow to the sea?\n\nWe don't question the gift. We accept it, embrace it, and hopefully use it wisely to benefit our people.
Then you condemn my warriors to further degradation! Surely you have more honor than that.\n\nWe no longer belong in this realm. Our battle is over. Let us have peace.

Gelvin has a good head and a good heart. Always puts the Daggers first and keeps us on the right side of the law.\n\nOf course, that's part of the reason we're still struggling. Sometimes mercenaries can't be too choosey about the jobs they take.

You're not listening. I'm saying that it doesn't matter. He could be a saint or Molag Bal himself.\n\nWhat matters is that we get paid so the Daggers can stay together. Got that? Now let's get back to camp.

This Lord Diel, something's not right with him. Why does a noble care about harpies?\n\nBut whatever. It doesn't matter. The Daggers need to get paid. If not, our mercenary group collapses and we're all back to the streets. Again.
I believe we already covered that. Now let me have a look at these beauties.\n\nAh, so round and smooth. Well, oval, really. I'll begin studying these eggs right a … wait a moment.
Where's the other egg? I was promised five harpy eggs, not four. Didn't they teach you to count?\n\nThere will be no deal without five eggs! Five! No more, no less. Imbeciles!

Then I suggest you find that bootless lout and get it back. There will be consequences. These are my eggs!\n\nLet his sister know that if Gelvin doesn't return, I will have his right hand cut off for stealing from a noble!
He is the most decorated member of the Guild still living. The master Artificer, and creator of the Emporium you see around you.\n\nHe's also marvelously handsome!

A real Ayleid ruin! Right on our doorstep! The Guild and the Thalmor have strict rules about entering Ayleid structures. And anyone with common sense knows those things are trapped and crawling with beasties.\n\nBut Telenger's no commoner!

In my study, of course, absorbing the wisdom of the ages. Finally, the chance to learn and experiment at my own pace. Without slackwits hanging on my every word.\n\nAnd then he came bungling in, and shackled me to his will. Bastard!
They must never be together, from the beginning, now, or in the future. The story will change to keep them apart.\n\nAs they should always have been.

I wish I knew. The rest of the Daggers made it back, but there's been no sign of my brother. I had my doubts about getting involved with Lord Diel. I just wish I'd told Gelvin about them.\n\nBut who are you anyway? Why do you care about any of this?

Well, you helped my brother and his Daggers so far. I only hope we can continue to count on your support.\n\nSo, listen. I heard Diel's threats. His claim is ridiculous, but he has gold. Paying guards to support a false accusation is easy enough.
Well, at least you're honest. Still, you've helped the Daggers so far.\n\nSo I guess I'll be honest with you. Diel's claim of theft is ridiculous, but he has enough gold to make his lies stick.
I think I know where you can find my brother. Whether you agree with Gelvin, me, or the bastard Diel over there, we need to find Gelvin and that egg.\n\nI don't want to see my brother get hurt.

There's a house on an island directly west of this camp. That's where we first met with Lord Diel. I could see that Gelvin was very interested in the place.\n\nI'll give you a head start before I tell Diel about it. Now go, find my brother.

I know, I know. I was on my way back when I decided to investigate this place.\n\nWhen we first arrived, Diel and his sons came out of this building to greet us. I figured if there was any place to get any answers, it was right here.

Nothing yet. But this whole situation feels … off. I'm sure that his lordship hasn't told us the whole truth about the harpy frenzy.\n\nAnyway, I'm not leaving this house until I find something that sheds light on what Diel is up to.
Close your eyes.
Be swift. There is not much time.
Hircine, a tyrant from Oblivion. Hircine, who is Half the Conscience of Man.\n\nHe is the father of werebeasts, and thrills in the hunt, no matter the prey.

A forge. Instead of steel, it shapes flesh. Instead of fire, it stokes the soul. Here, Hircine crafted his Hound. A living weapon driven by passion.\n\n<<1>> is not so discriminating. They build a crude army of dead flesh.

To capture the Green Lady, I would think. The strongest of the Bosmer, greatest hunters of Nirn! How could Hircine resist such formidable prey?\n\nHe's sought her as a trophy for generations. And I was the key.

I was a hunter once. When the Green Lady rejected me, I searched for aid. I came to <<1>> and found Hircine, waiting for me.\n\nHe turned my love into an obsession. Twisted it to his infernal purposes. And I became his Hound.

Hircine did not abandon this prison. He gave it to <<1>>, and she created an army of husks from Hircine's conquests.\n\nShe seeks to overrun the Valenwood and slaughter its people. I cannot allow that.
A harvester of souls! Hircine used her to create this prison. She crafted the perfect madness from my memories.
Can you believe it? A wolf in the city? But that's what the watch thinks. Who am I to say any different?\n\nStill, it feels more like murder than the work of a wild animal to me.
The fools! Did they succeed?

Fanatics from the Reach. Rumors are that they're involved in dark nature magic—and worse! We try to stay clear of those fobbing maniacs.\n\nIf the monster decided to just kill Bloodthorns, that would be fine by me.
Haven't you heard? Everyone's talking about it. The town of Camlorn's been taken over by an army of werewolves!\n\nDon't look at me like that! I heard Damien and Fabien talking about it.
The Green Lady is the personification of the feral side of our people. Here you see part of the scene when Gwaering was revealed by Y'ffre.
Many different ones. It's such trouble to write them down.\n\n<<1>> usually talks only of the Silvenar. He's the one who noticed their story had changed.

As real as a summer roast or a cricket's song. I've yet to determine if they speak what they see, or if reality conforms to their desires.\n\nOne spinner told me how thirsty he was and suddenly, he held a mug of mead. Fascinating!

Corpses. Tough as iron. A shade followed them. We couldn't get a good look at it.\n\nI've heard stories about the undead, but I never thought I'd live one. We were trained to fight men, not what's left when they die!
Be asking your questions quickly. I must go after I search these bodies.
A magic device from the time of the Ayleids. Ilayas focuses power into it to control the weather.\n\nThe stormwardens have guarded it for centuries.
I was sent to scout the region and report on Ilayas. I found <<1>> on the road as she was returning to the ruins.\n\nWhen we arrived, Ilayas was overrun.
They are Bosmer who've guarded the sphere since the Ayleid left. They use it to defend the coast and keep the forest growing.
At least someone else had some luck. Take the key inside and find the stormwardens. With this last <<z:1>> in their possession, they'll be as safe as torchbugs in amber.
There's a cave, a place where tales from the beginning of our time live alongside random hoarvor.\n\nIn the cave lies Old Tusk, the first mammoth to walk Valenwood. Perfectly preserved, but dead.
It'll come apart in your hand, no knives needed!\n\nDid I say perfectly preserved? I meant, not rancid, just showing its age. After all, Old Tusk was the first mammoth.
Not much. Enough to make a tincture. I'm not going to turn the blood into ink. No, no, not exactly.\n\nWhat we'll do invokes an ancient rite to inscribe a spinner's story to flesh.
One who is eager to end the horrors of this place. I am a shadow of <<1>>, the one who is called the Hound. I seek to make amends.\n\nWe should make haste. He slips further away with every breath.

I've cast a spell within the chamber. The blood awakens the words spoken to the skins, refreshing them. They'll bond with the nearest flesh, the chunk you took from Old Tusk!\n\nMeet me by the fire pit at the bottom of the tree when you're done!
Let me see that. What in the name of …?\n\nLord Diel's been poisoning the harpies the entire time! He orchestrated their frenzy! And he claimed he's been trying to help. He's been using us!

It's tainted gold. The Daggers don't operate that way. We're not common thieves that break the law just to fill our own pockets.\n\nThis is a dangerous edge to walk, and it cuts both ways. I didn't want the Daggers to start out like this.

Well, we'd have to disband. We'd go our separate ways and hope we can find a way to feed our families.\n\nDamn it! This isn't an easy choice. I just can't accept that we'd get our start helping a noble do the wrong thing.
Of course. You're right. Diel has to be stopped. \n\nI think I know what to do. And if all else fails, I've always been good at improvisation.

But you don't understand! This is wrong! I pride myself on doing the right thing. I've never broken the law or asked the Daggers to do anything illegal.\n\nBut now everyone's depending on me. I don't know what to do.
What's wrong? What's wrong? Isn't it obvious?\n\nLady Javierre took the last sweet roll! I was looking forward to that all day!
What cult? Lies. More lies. That man was a dream interpreter! \n\nHe told me! I saw it myself—all these people are conspiring with the slavers!  You are too, you traitorous swine!
My little ones haven't had a hot meal in days and the magistrate is going to evict us from the shack we live in.\n\nIf you could spare a bit of gold, I'd be eternally grateful.
Of course you can't. You have more important things to do. I understand.\n\nI'll just tell the little ones that it's pebbles and dirt for dinner again tonight.
Oh, bless you, friend, bless you! The little ones will drink well tonight!\n\nUm, I mean eat. Yes. They will eat well. Um. Thanks.
The Houndsmen and the mer. When they attacked the city, I tried to fight them off, but there were too many.\n\nI'm lucky I escaped to this hut.
Thank you! May the stars always shine upon you.
I'm too good a fighter to let the wounds show. But they're here … on the inside.\n\nMaybe you could give me a little gold for medicine, though.
I, well, I did most of my work in the shadows … at night. I took two, maybe three … no, four! Four mer on before they hurt me too badly to continue.\n\nLook, can you help me or not?

Trebuchets, catapults, and ballistae are the tools of our trade. They cause tremendous damage to walls and foes. \n\nWe have a few of each here. Pick one that's not in use and fire at the targets on the range.
No. You'll see when you fire them. The trebuchet and ballista fire the farthest, while the catapult has a shorter range. Remembering this will come in handy during assaults on castles!

Trebuchets work well against castle walls, dealing massive damage. There are three types—firepots spread burning oil, stones smash walls and foes, and iceballs cause damage and ensnare soldiers in ice.

Ballistas fire fast and true; they excel at destroying enemy siege engines, including rams. Standard ballista bolts smash their targets, firebolts cause extensive burn damage, and lightning bolts shock and ensnare their victims.
Catapults are excellent weapons against enemy troops. Meatbag catapults spread debilitating disease, oil causes fire damage, and scatter-shot causes impact damage.
Each weapon—trebuchet, ballista, or catapult—has unique abilities and uses.

Take your time. The spinners work with the past, present, and future, and likely left clues to help solve the puzzle of their bindings.\n\nLook carefully at each stone, and read every book within their chambers. I'm sure you'll find the answers.

This dagger you've handed me has a very sharp edge. No, not you. The Daggers are of my own making.\n\nLet's find Lord Diel, give him his egg, and get our gold. Our families won't go hungry, but I may never sleep well again after this.
You've done enough. Just keep Lord Diel busy. It's not up to you to finish this. That's work for the Daggers.\n\nEven if it turns out to be our last job, we're going to do it right.
Ah, yes, yes! This one's shell shines even brighter than the others.\n\nMy, um, study of this specimen will surely guarantee our success in stopping the harpy frenzy.
If you think to try to slander me, worm, good luck with that. I put gold in the pockets of the highest-ranking guards in the city. No one will believe you.
You … what are you … oh, bother!\n\nVery well, tell me what you want.

I don't know. I don't trust him and I never will. \n\nBut it's odd. The blind hatred I felt when I saw him? I could have strangled him with my bare hands. But now … I think he was right. That hatred was poisoning me.
We're not done yet. We need to keep moving forward. \n\nThe passage is blocked by a rock slide, but now that I have my axe back I might be able to break through it.

Yes, yes! The Konunleikar. The Nords are very proud of their celebrations, and this is a big one. \n\nThey want to prove that even though the Akaviri damaged the city, Windhelm is still a beautiful and vibrant place.

The Akaviri hit Windhelm hard during the invasions. Most of the damage has been repaired, but work continues on the palace.\n\nKing Jorunn insisted that the rest of the city should come first, so the palace was the last thing worked on.

That's what the Nords call this celebration! The entire city is celebrating King Jorunn's tenth anniversary as the Skald-King.\n\nNord clans have come to Windhelm from across Skyrim to compete in various challenges to honor the King and his reign.
Those are Oathbreakers as well. Oathbreakers can shapeshift to many different forms at will, but some have recently become trapped in a single form by the Worm Cult's meddling.
Looking for you. Laganakh told me you were headed this way, chasing the creeps who attacked the fortress.

If you want my advice, and not that you asked, talk to Oda's housecarl, Jaema. She tries to keep track of her thane, which isn't an easy task. Last I saw, she was up at the front gates, searching for her master.\n\nNow go. I'll find Irnskar shortly.

Good. Very good. The tunnel is cleared then, yes? Akkhuz-ri is eternally grateful. He can make it back to Marbruk and send reinforcements to hold the tunnel.\n\nThe far greater concern is discovering what has prompted the undead to attack.

Yes. This one saw the prince with his own eyes. He is no longer Naemon though—he has been raised and possessed by some darkness. \n\nEven so, Akkhuz-ri does not understand. The prince ordered his forces to attack, and then he disappeared.

Of course not … and I am grateful for your assistance. It's true that I can't do this alone. I just think marching the entire army into the forest would be a mistake.\n\nCome though. We mustn't tarry. We must discover the Shade's true motivation.

Back to <<1>> where he'd be safe. I couldn't stop her from capturing him, but I can undo the damage she's done.\n\nHe won't remember much. I know the horrors <<2>> can wreak upon an unprotected mind. None should have to endure that agony.
Of course! You need only ask. After all you have done, this is the least I can do.
I cannot leave this place. It is bound to me, and I to it.\n\nI'll find a way to destroy it, even if it destroys me in the process.
You've saved countless souls. <<1>>'s army threatened to engulf all of the Valenwood. Its people can ill afford another threat in these troubled times.\n\nFarewell, friend.
This little gut wound? I've had worse. Once, an enraged hoarvor … but really, this isn't the time for stories.\n\nWe'll swap adventures when you come back, eh?

It's the first line of defense for the stormwardens.\n\nLook for the constellation tiles. Activate the Tower, Shadow, Lover, and Thief tiles in that order. If you forget, I'm sure you can figure it out by looking around the ruins.

I can't be sure, but I suspect <<1>> is behind this.\n\nHe was a stormwarden, but left in a huff about a week ago. I think he was upset about how the others were using the sphere. Rather, how they weren't using it.
Sorry, friend. He just headed back up to the Cloudy Dregs to speak with the money lender, S'rashi. \n\nIf I know the captain, he may be having a drink downstairs before he goes up.
If S'rashi had time, he would gladly give it to the captain, but S'rashi's own hide is on the line too.\n\nS'rashi has to have the money, one way or another.

S'rashi owes debts but is also owed debts. There are three in the city who have gold that should be S'rashi's. \n\nFirst is a gambler, next is a nobleman, and the last is a smuggler. You help S'rashi collect and S'rashi pays generous percentage.

Whatever business Midnight Union has in Wayrest, S'rashi handles it. Buying. Selling. Trading.\n\nS'rashi helps city dwellers too. Lends money to those in need. He's a good one. Glad you will be helping him.
You are helping S'rashi, yes? Then S'rashi will tell you anything … well, almost anything.\n\nYou would like to know about the gambler, the nobleman, or the smuggler? Just ask and S'rashi will tell.
Captain Marck. Very smart man. Smuggles weapons, skooma, whatever makes him gold, yes?\n\nMarck lost his ship though. Borrowed money for a new one. S'rashi needs money back now.
You know Captain Marck? Very good. Then you'll have an easier time convincing him to pay S'rashi back.

Ervine. Louis Ervine. He is a nice man, but a little dungy, and he has no sense. Keeps making bets even when he's lost everything. \n\nS'rashi feels sorry for Ervine, but forgives his debt for too long. S'rashi must collect now to save his own skin.

These upper class turn their noses up at S'rashi until they need S'rashi's help. Padier Nytte comes from old family, very rich, but not anymore.\n\nNytte says he has no money to pay S'rashi back, but S'rashi thinks Nytte is lying.
Ha! Orcs don't settle lands, we take them! The Seamount clan was the scourge of the seas. We took this island when Chief Yzzgol cleared out the Bretons.
If you're willing to pay the gold for him, S'rashi will not complain.\n\nConsider the captain's debt settled.

This is true, and S'rashi does not want the captain's blood on his hands.\n\nThis is all right though. You have collected most of S'rashi's money, and he is grateful. S'rashi can cover the rest, for now.
You must use my plant allies to defend me. Fire stands against fire, like against like.\n\nI feel them approach. Be ready!
Faolchu's a terrible brute! He leads the werewolves that invaded Camlorn and forced the rightful rulers to flee for their lives.
Sure. I tracked a few of them to their cave. Rather than poke around on my own, I decided to wait for you, my friend. And here you are!

Not that you asked, but if you want my advice, talk to Oda's housecarl. Jaema tries to keep track of her thane, which isn't an easy task. Last I saw, she was up at the front gates looking for her master.\n\nNow go. I'll meet with Irnskar shortly.
Let's just say I have some inside knowledge that can help us put an end to the mangy dog.\n\nNow get me out of these ropes.
With me? Fool. Let's get this over with.

I'm the Thane of Windhelm. My father was Captain of the Guard. I followed in his footsteps and climbed a bit higher.\n\nWe Stormcloaks helped build Windhelm centuries ago. We're an old family and we're proud of our heritage.

We don't like to talk about it, but Jorunn wasn't the unanimous choice to ascend the throne. The Stormfist clan backed his challenger, and they have been associated with ill omens ever since.\n\nDiscretion is called for. Hence an outsider, like you.

You're good at digging up information. Where better to keep an eye on things than right in the middle of the race? I can't post guards at every tower.\n\nAnd as an outsider that no one has ever heard of, your participation should confuse our enemies.
I see that now. His story is not mine.\n\nThe incarnation of the Green Lady must know you. I will entrust you with my essence. Complete the story as it should be told.

What do I do? What don't I do! Rules and regulations. Meetings with King Jorunn and other thanes. Now I'm hosting Pact delegates. A lot of political nonsense!\n\nMostly I delegate so that I can guard the city. People feel safer with the thane around.
Sure, I guess. I'd prefer if you went and helped them, though. But ask away.
Don't you know anything? Hircine! The creator and guardian of all were-creatures?\n\nHircine's Call … well, it calls to their true nature. Reveals them for the beasts they really are.
We shouldn't dawdle, so make it quick.

We're an odd bunch, that's for sure. Gelvin found each of us either drinking away our troubles or begging for gold on the streets of Daggerfall.\n\nWe were good for nothing and all but forgotten. Gelvin wanted to change that.

I vowed that I would always face my opponents as an equal. If an enemy came at me with a sword, I would meet his blade with one of my own.\n\nThe harpies fight with claws. How could I go up against them with anything more than the fists nature gave me?

A few of us tried to join the city guard or hook up with the Fighters Guild. Truth be told, they wouldn't have us. We weren't good enough for them.\n\nSo we formed the Daggers to show them that they're wrong.

Well, not really. We were talking about how we needed to find a job, and suddenly Lord Diel's men were making us an offer.\n\nWe took it as a sign that we were doing the right thing. The Daggers were going places!

Lord Diel's guards were in the city, looking to hire some muscle. They found us in the Rosy Lion, celebrating our newly formed partnership.\n\nWe needed a job, Lord Diel needed some help, and here we are.
Sharp and natural. They don't wield weapons, so neither will I.\n\nI will fight them head on, fists against claws. And I will do so with honor.
The relics you recovered are very important. When they were removed, it disturbed the draugr below.\n\nPlease return the relics to their proper resting places.

There is nothing simple about this matter. You must return the relics to the exact spot they were taken from. Inspect each chamber carefully, for there will be clues as to the proper placement.\n\nI can advise you, but I know little of these relics.

Nothing yet, but it needs to get stuck on one of these pikes. That's where it belongs.\n\nYou should do the honors. It's only fair, since you defeated him and all. That should put the fear of Shor in the rest of those Stormfist lackeys.

What did you say? How dare you! That's my property! You expect to get away with this?\n\nI knew I shouldn't have put my trust in a bunch of low-life scum. You'll be in the hands of the Daggerfall guard by the end of day!

You? Friends with the King? Oh, that's brilliant. Really, it is. You must dine with his family on a regular basis? Perhaps vacation together in the countryside?\n\nI'll give him your regards. It's a shame about your tragic accident and all. Guards!

You think the guard would believe you? Some street rats who lay a claim against a well-respected noble? You're dumber than you look. The guard will chuckle as they lead you to the dungeons. \n\nOr maybe we'll just end this right now.
What impertinence! You really do get under my skin. Enough of this. No one will miss you or those street rats.\n\nGuards! Deal with these thieves!
Yeah, I figured that out. His lordship was also behind the whole harpy menace thing, too, wasn't he?\n\nWell, it's a good thing I decided not to count on Gelvin to turn a profit.

Well, I trust you. Besides, I need to set these birdies free, and they're not going to be very happy when I do. You've dealt with enough Dagger business for one day. Leave this to me.\n\nGo on, go on. I'll catch up later.

I snatched this from the camp when no one was looking. It's not much, but a few gems are better than no gems at all.\n\nWhy don't you tell Gelvin that you found it on his lordship's body. We don't want him to think I stole it or anything.
What do you mean?
The pompous ass carried these around with him? That figures.\n\nTechnically, we did complete the job. Wait, what am I saying? This isn't right. These gems don't belong to us.
That sly dog! Well, his lordship does owe us for all the work we did. Doesn't he?\n\nIt's not like I can return it to him, and I certainly don't want to give these away.
I'm always ready for a fight, especially with outlanders.
A uniform? Hmm. Must've been a cutpurse. They're always hanging around the docks, waiting to steal away with some cargo.\n\nBe careful around here.
A uniform? Hmm. Must have been a cutpurse. They're always hanging around the docks, waiting to steal away with some cargo.\n\nBe careful around here.

If you find his banner, burn it. I'm certain he's an Altmer spy. He wants Vlastarus to declare openly for the Dominion, making us a target for everyone else. He and his Aldmeri banner are a danger to everyone here.
On that promise, I will help you to enter our catacombs. Precede me to the door.
You lack a soul. That loss may serve you in good stead inside. Lead the way to the door and I will help open it.
The stones connect this world to the spirit realm. For most, touching one tears the soul from the body. Without a soul, you are safe.
To us, who were here when all was new, it was our sanctuary. The three stones act in concert to open the doorway. This is the only way in.
That is our duty. In life, we were the guardians of this sanctuary, Death did not free us from our duty.

Why not? Good soil, stone, and ore, and plenty of it! And far from the mainland. Yzzgol wanted to raze it and move on, but his wives convinced him otherwise. Three blades make a strong counter-argument.
Let me think … wait a moment! The way he shrank back from our torches ….\n\nFire! That's the answer. It has to be! Tell the others. Help them. If Faolchu isn't killed, we all lose.

Though Sai remains hidden from my sight, Lyris brings news that an agent of the enemy lurks in Vulkhel Guard. Fear is on the lips of the people. Darkness walks among them. Even a blind man can sense it. \n\nIt is the hand of Mannimarco.

If it truly is an agent of Mannimarco's Worm Cult, it may provide us with a clue that will hasten our search. \n\nSeek this agent, but tread carefully. The Worm Cult is a cult of necromancy, and the undead are fearsome opponents.

Venture to Vulkhel Guard. Speak to the fisher, Mehdir, and the jongleur, Diranor. It was on their lips that Lyris first heard of the troubles lurking in the shadows.\n\nLocate this agent of evil. Return with any personal effects they carry with them.

Though Sai remains hidden from my sight, Lyris brings news that an agent of the enemy lurks in Daggerfall. Fear is on the lips of the people. Darkness walks among them. Even a blind man can sense it. \n\nIt is the hand of Mannimarco.

If it is truly an agent of Mannimarco's Worm Cult, it may provide us with a clue that will hasten our search. \n\nSeek this agent, but tread carefully. The Worm Cult is a cult of necromancy and the undead are fearsome opponents.

Venture to Daggerfall. Speak to old maid Maxelle and Husniya the mercenary. It was on their lips that Lyris first heard murmurs of trouble lurking in the shadows.\n\nLocate this agent of evil. Return with any personal effects they carry with them.

Though Sai remains hidden from my sight, Lyris brings news that an agent of the enemy lurks in Davon's Watch. Fear is on the lips of the people. Darkness walks among them. Even a blind man can sense it. \n\nIt is the hand of Mannimarco.

If it truly is an agent of Mannimarco's Worm Cult, it may provide us with a clue that will hasten our search. \n\nSeek this agent, but tread carefully. The Worm Cult is a cult of necromancy, and the undead are fearsome opponents.

Venture to Davon's Watch. Speak to Feduira Llaren at the market, or Okeeh the beggar. Lyris first heard murmurs of trouble lurking in the shadows from them. \n\nLocate this agent of evil. Return with any personal effects they carry with them.

I'd love to hear your theories, but it won't mean anything if we don't take this camp back first.\n\nWe need to be able to reach Faolchu to actually defeat him. Let's talk after the siege camp is once again under our control.

That's one of the problems. I know you can find these beasts all over Shadowfen, but I don't know where. And I'd get killed if I went roaming around the swamps!\n\nYou'll … you'll have to ask <<1>>. But don't let him know I sent you!
May Jode bless you with his tears, and keep you always at his breast. Why have you come to the aid of Kansur-jo? This one felt sure he would die here.
The Monastery swarms with the Stonefire cult! But, yes. The sacred Claw must be kept safe. This one will bestow upon you the cool light of Jode's grace.
How did you know to find us here? How did Jone lead you to this one's side?
Ah. So you are here for the Claw, in point of fact. Ahem, well. Mahazi will not turn away help. Untie me, if you would.
Yes, your report, you insipid twit. What, did you contact me by accident?
I've managed to learn a thing or two. Have you seen any of the other scouts?

Just appeal to his vanity. The old lizard's pride got me into this—I don't see why it shouldn't get me out, too!\n\nHe's probably just outside the city, hunting. That's what he does all the time. Thinks he's the greatest gamesman in Shadowfen.
How dare you speak to me in such a … wait, you're not one of ours, are you? Color me intrigued. \n\nYou speak to Abnur Tharn, overlord of Nibenay and Chancellor of the Elder Council.
Well, out with it. I don't have all day.\n\nYour disguise is terrible, by the way. You look like a character from a bad adventure novel.

Are they? I didn't think that Redguard has-been had a single friend left. Not in this world, at any rate. \n\nNever fear. Sai Sahan is safely locked away. Even if they were to discover his location, attempting a rescue would be suicidal.

Of course I do. But I'm not in the habit of revealing vital secrets to insipid lackeys.\n\nNow, be gone! And if you contact me again without good reason I shall contact your cell commander and have you properly thrashed for your ineptitude.
Correct me if I am wrong, but didn't you contact me? Fascinating. \n\nAre you merely a blundering local, I wonder, or something more?

Are you, indeed? I didn't think that Redguard has-been had a single friend left. Not in this world, at any rate. \n\nLet me give you some free advice. Forget about Sai Sahan. Even if I told you where he was, attempting a rescue would be suicidal.
Of course I do. But do you really think I'd tell you and risk incurring Mannimarco's wrath? I think not. \n\nAh the owner of this place returns, and he doesn't look pleased. Fare well!

Well, neither of them are very subtle. Keep your eyes open. I've discovered why the Colovians are here. We stand upon a vault of the Ancients. Within this ruin is a relic. Something the Ayleids wanted hidden.

She's a piece of work, isn't she? I've spoken to Razum-dar. He's led troops down into the ruin. But the Colovians … those bastards. They've collapsed the main entrance. And activated a ward on the rear.

He's too tall for real field work, but he's still a good soldier. I've spoken to Razum-dar. He's led troops down into the ruin. But the Colovians … those bastards. They've collapsed the main entrance and activated a ward on the rear.
Excellent work. I've managed to find where the stones are being held. They're stashed in a pair of chests here in the Colovian camp. They've set two of their most powerful mages to guard them.
Juluda-daro has only a small piece of the puzzle. Have you found any of her fellows?
<You slide bits of leaf into the phial and stopper it. As the leaves dissolve, the phial becomes warm to the touch.>
We stand upon a vault of the Ancients. Beneath this stone, the Ayleids stored away something they wished hidden for all time.

Damned fine soldier, <<1>>. Razum-dar told Juluda of the relic. He led a troop of the Queen's own into the ruin. But the Colovians, bastards. They collapsed the main entrance and activated a ward on the rear.

Pah, <<1>> is too tall for real field work. Razum-dar told Juluda of the relic. He led a troop of the Queen's own into the ruin. But the Colovians, bastards. They collapsed the main entrance and activated a ward on the rear.

Ahh, well done. Well done indeed! Then Juluda is happy to tell you where the stones are. She managed to beat it out of one of these dogs. They have stashed them in a pair of chests inside their camp. Set their most powerful mages to guard them.
This one sensed the danger here, the threat to the Claw. And the threat to you, Hallowed. The Mane, the Claw, the Hallowed, the moons … everything has its place on the path.

You have already encountered the cult, and their dark thralls. The cult, in their ignorance, tear at the temple walls. They want to enter the inner sanctum, overcome the wards and claim the Claw. Fools.

I don't like to gossip, but there's been an Imperial vagrant nosing around for the past few weeks. Suspicious looking fellow. I actually saw him picking through the trash outside the castle a few weeks ago.\n\nI've no idea where he is now.
<A quick draught from the phial numbs your tongue. After a few seconds, a warm, tingling sensation spreads through your limbs.>

Oh? Do the winds speak my name? Or the birds? Or is there, perhaps, someone else who told you to speak with me?\n\nMy adroitinosity is known throughout the fen, of course, but it whispers only to its creatures. And me, of course.
<You slide a petal into the phial and stopper it. As the petal dissolves, tiny bubbles foam to the liquid's surface.>
<A small sip from the phial burns your lips and tongue. After a few seconds, a sickly sensation seizes your stomach.>
Good. Here it is ….\n\nDripping crimson, it washes across battlefields. Both friend and foe fall in its wake. The few who defeat this undying enemy surrender to its cold embrace.
Everyone? The metropolinia hum with tales of my vigoritude. Well, who am I to deny them?\n\nGo ahead, ask your questions.

What? Ah, the rivers grow torentious stories of her perfitudinousness. Let me guess: She's asked you to hunt for her, fearing to brave the fen she so easily mocked while in her cups.\n\nGo ahead, ask your questions. I will deal with her later.

The fens speak to me readily about their bountinosity of beasts. Please, ask me about any of these and I will stupendify you with my knowledge.\n\nBut know that most beasts of the fens can be found anywhere … if you are wise enough to find them.

Larger and more deadly predators than the kagouti, alit hunt the Venomous Fens, along the southern edge of Shadowfen.\n\nBe careful. These beasts carry a disease called ataxia. You'll find yourself staggering and weak if you let them bite you.

They are two-legged predators, more aggressive than guar and similar in some way to alits. They eat anything they can fit in their large mouths.\n\nTo hunt them, search the central regions of Shadowfen, in Leafwater.

Interesting, but deadly insects. They can be found singly or in swarms. Beware the wasp queen! She has a mighty sting and is often protected by her lesser drones.\n\nWasps dwell mostly in the Venomous Fens, the southernmost region of Shadowfen.
Mudcrabs live all over the world, but the sweetest of the hard-backed beasts live here, in Reticulated Spine.\n\nThe foul-tempered creatures can be found all along the northern region of Shadowfen.
Ha! Perhaps that was too simple.\n\nAre you ready to hear the next riddle?
Wrong.\n\nCome back when you're feeling more clever.
Wrong.\n\nCome back when you're feeling more clever.

Prepare yourself.

It runs smoother than rhymes. It falls but cannot climb. It trembles at the lightest touch, yet can carry the heaviest of burdens. Its sweetness soothes the spine.

What is it?
I am like the river's mouth. Ask me of any creature in Shadowfen and I'll pour the knowledge into you. They live more progeniful lives in some areas than others, and I shall tell you where.

Larger and more deadly predators than the kagouti, alit hunt the Venomous Fens, along the southern edge of Shadowfen.\n\nBe careful. These beasts carry a disease called ataxia. You'll find yourself staggering and weak if you let them bite you.

Interesting, but deadly insects. They can be found singly or in swarms. Beware the wasp queen! She has a mighty sting and is often protected by her lesser drones.\n\nWasps dwell mostly in the Venomous Fens, the southernmost region of Shadowfen.

They are two-legged predators, more aggressive than guar and similar in some way to alits. They eat anything they can fit in their large mouths.\n\nTo hunt them, search the central regions of Shadowfen, in Leafwater.
Mudcrabs live all over the world, but the sweetest of the hard-backed beasts live here, in Reticulated Spine.\n\nThe foul-tempered creatures can be found all along the northern region of Shadowfen.

Present company excluded? Hmm. \n\nWell, there was a dodgy looking Imperial hanging out in a doorway near South Gate Alley this morning. He was eyeballing everyone who happened by. Seemed like a cutpurse looking for an easy mark, if you ask me.

Funny you should ask. There was an odd-looking Imperial fellow in town a few days ago. He was asking about local burial grounds, said he was trying to track down his great aunt's remains.\n\nYeah, right. And I'm Queen Ayrenn's chamberlain!
<You slide bits of leaf into the phial and stopper it. As the leaves dissolve, the phial becomes warm to the touch.>

Heh heh. This one thinks you're a bit strange!\n\nKidding! Kidding! Hmm. I am thinking I did see an Imperial man lurking around by the lighthouse, like skittish prey. He thinks I do not see him, but this one has a keen eye.
<You slide a petal into the phial and stopper it. As the petal dissolves, tiny bubbles foam to the liquid's surface.>

Let me think.\n\nAh, yes! Imperial fellow, tall, brusque, rather boorish. He pushed me while I was haggling at the market. Scurried off toward the east end of town when I tried to have words with him. Typical.
Come to think of it, there was some out-of-towner mucking about in the abandoned stable, last night. I didn't pry. None of my business. Also, he was armed. I'm no fool.
Wrong.\n\nCome back when you're feeling more clever.
Ha ha! Correct. You're good at this.\n\nOne riddle remains. I hope you're prepared for it.
Wrong.\n\nCome back when you're feeling more clever.
Hmm …. Ah, yes. This should get you thinking.\n\nDestroyer of kings and maker of merchants. It brings high men low and low men high. A wise man's vice. A fool's folly.
Wrong.\n\nCome back when you're feeling more clever.
Wrong.\n\nCome back when you're feeling more clever.

Excellent! That is the very riddle upon which <<1>> lost his lute. His greed cost him his most prized possession.\n\nAs promised, here is his lute. I hope this experience has taught him the price of greed.
Hmm. I do not return items lost on a bet. Did he tell you he lost it gambling?\n\nPerhaps you're a gambler as well. Would you like to win it back?
Very well. Spit it out. What's your theory on how to kill an unbeatable foe?\n\nPerhaps it will be better than the last half-dozen ideas I heard today.

Intriguing. At least that makes more sense than throwing salt on the despicable creature. Well, perhaps we'll get a chance to put your theory to the test.\n\nIn the meantime, can I count on your continued assistance?
Excellent! This will be fun.\n\nLet me know when you're ready to hear the first riddle.
An intriguing proposal. It has been long since anyone challenged me.\n\nYes. I will hear your riddle. If I cannot answer it, the lute is yours.
But that wouldn't be any fun. No fun at all.\n\nCome now. Play a game of riddles with old <<1>>. If you answer correctly, I will give you the lute.
I ask no gold, merely your time and effort.\n\nYou will play a game of riddles with old <<1>>. If you answer correctly, I will give you the lute.
Hmm. I have never heard the like.\n\nMay I have another clue?
Ah. I am honored you chose to share your riddle with me.\n\nHere, you may have the lute. I hope you share your wisdom with <<1>> so that he never again gambles away such a fine instrument.
Is … Is it love?
An intriguing proposal. It has been long since anyone challenged me.\n\nYes. I will hear your riddle. If I cannot answer it, the lute is yours.
Ah. I am honored you chose to share your riddle with me.\n\nHere, you may have the lute. I hope you share your wisdom with <<1>> so that he never again gambles away such a fine instrument.
Is … is it love?
Hmm. I have never heard the like.\n\nMay I have another clue?
It used to be a safe village, so close to the Imperial City. But with the empire in shambles, there was no one to protect us. Bandits attacked the village and we barely escaped with our lives.
I'm studying the Ayleid ruins that dot Cyrodiil's landscape. There is so much we don't know about those ancient Elves. If you want more details, you'll need to wait until I publish my papers.

Of course. No place in Cyrodiil is far from Ayleid ruins, it seems. There are ruins at Ceyatatar to the north and at Nornalhorst to the south. Both are dangerous places, however.\n\nIf you do visit them and find objects, please bring them to me!
She should be just up the road, by the hatching pools, waiting for another mark.\n\nShe's crafty. Don't let her trick you into large bets.
By the Three, you did it! You saved my life and returned my livelihood.\n\nI don't have much, but what little I have is yours. I'll earn it back, and more, when they hear me play in Stormhold.
Never again. I sought a shortcut to riches and nearly lost everything.\n\nA fool and his lute are soon parted, my father used to say. Had I listened to him, I would have avoided this folly.

Who doesn't, except for other Orcs, of course? The Orcs here stole this island from Bretons generations ago.\n\nAnd they're still not part of the Covenant. Can you believe that? Chief Tazgol refuses to join!
Give me the meat … quietly! <<1>> is here, and he's suspicious. But if he doesn't see you pass me the ingredients, he'll have to admit I won the bet!
Don't ask! What I have to do if I lose … it doesn't bear thinking upon.\n\nJust know that if I lose this bet, I'll have to stay drunk for the rest of my life to live down the shame!
Return to my clan's stronghold. Depose Gloorig and exact the blood price for my father's death!\n\nIf they'd marched with him, he'd still be alive! My people would still have a worthy chief!
Thank you! This'll show the old lizard!\n\nNow, pass me those ingredients and I'll whip something up quick!
Settling a bet with my friend, <<1>>. She disparulted my profession and I mean to see that she is properly punished.\n\nYou know something about our wager, I believe?

Gloorig told them a woman was not worth the effort, no matter her strength.\n\nAccording to my sister, Gloorig seized power when we left. She sent word he'd even taken my father's wives for his own! Coward. He dared only with my father gone!
If they didn't start out that way, that's certainly the case now.\n\nA marriage made in Oblivion, to be sure, but effective nevertheless.
Rest and gather my strength. When I have recovered, I will strike out on my own.\n\nThe lizards here have no backbone. Perhaps the daughter of <<1>> can beat one into them!
Ha! I knew it! You are a percepicous individual. Give me the meat. I'll be rubbing this in <<1>>'s face. \n\nWell, not literally. That would be disgusting.
<<1>>, daughter of <<2>>, whose blood is Mauloch's by honor and strength!\n\nThrough our shared blood, his strength is mine.
Trust no one but yourself. And maybe me. Once this gets out of your hands, you have no idea who'll get hold of it. You need to destroy it.
Distrust of Bretons and Redguards, apparently. He's still angry about the sackings of Orsinium by Daggerfall and Sentinel. Refuses all overtures from the Covenant, won't even listen.
An assassin attacked my father. I snapped his neck, but he grazed me with a poisoned dagger.\n\nMy father and I came alone to find a cure after the clan refused to march together.
I plan to! Code be damned, I am stronger than that coward! I'll see him pay the blood price, or die while cutting his throat!\n\nIf no one else in the hold will challenge him, I must!
<<1>>, chief of the greatest Orc hold in Skyrim! Dead now, but with honor.\n\nNow Gloorig rules the clan, a coward sitting in my father's seat.
This relic is too powerful. It'll corrupt anyone who has it. Destroy it, and let's get out of here.
My dear fellow, I'm not alone in my opinions. All Bretons dislike Orcs. But since we have to deal with them, my friends at court felt I was best qualified for this mission.

Abnur Tharn shows his face again. I get the sense that he might have a larger part to play in the coming events, but for good or ill I cannot say.\n\nLeave the orb with me. I shall be able to use it to locate Sai Sahan.
Didn't the Prophet tell you the story of the Five Companions?
I don't know where to start. There's so much to tell.
You only know him as the man who killed you and stole your soul, but back then he was Emperor Varen's most trusted advisor. It was Mannimarco who convinced Varen to search for the Amulet of Kings.

Varen wasn't a true Dragonborn Emperor. He didn't share Alessia's bloodline.\n\nMannimarco said the amulet could change all that. He said he could use it to perform a ritual that would turn Varen into a true Dragonborn.

It took us more than two years, but we finally recovered the amulet and returned to Cyrodiil to perform the ritual. \n\nMannimarco set us up. The ritual caused a violent explosion of magical energy. We lost Varen. Sai Sahan and I were declared outlaws.

Mannimarco convinced the Elder Council to recognize Abnur Tharn's daughter Clivia as Empress-Regent, but Mannimarco was the true power behind the throne.\n\nSai Sahan and I went into hiding. There was a bounty on our heads.
Abnur Tharn is Grand Chancellor of the Elder Council, and chief advisor to his daughter, the Empress-Regent. He's also Mannimarco's toady.

We were chosen by Emperor Varen to join him on a quest to recover a lost artifact called the Amulet Of Kings. \n\nThe five included Varen, myself, a Redguard named Sai Sahan, Abnur Tharn, and the traitor, Mannimarco.

Tharn's first loyalty is to his family and the Empire, and he's a ruthless bastard when it comes to defending them.\n\nThe Worm Cult obviously doesn't share those loyalties. Tharn would never trust them, but he's too much of a coward to betray them.
Maybe. But what could we offer him? He's already got more gold than the Gods themselves!
Why not? I'm the only one who might discover how it works. You can't hand it over to the fools who run the Covenant. Destroy it rather than that.
Give it to me or destroy it. Those are the only choices I will accept.

Let's make sure you actually have the skills I require before we discuss that. I want to see how you deal with the traps my former liege put in place.\n\nGo. Speak to the lady. We shall talk more later.
I don't often agree with Kaleen, but she's right. We must hand it over to the Covenant. King Fahara'jad will see that it's used responsibly.
Save the citizens
Trust Kaleen. She knows Fahara'jad and she's convinced the relic can save lives.
Keep the relic, please. My brothers are in the Covenant army. This could prevent war and save their lives!
What do you mean? Didn't you hear me? Don't you dare risk the lives of my brothers! If you destroy that relic, I never want to see your face again.
<The orb pulses with power, driven by the energy of thousands of stolen souls.>
<<1>> needs the husk of a giant wasp for some sort of container. I'm sure she'd be happy to tell you all about it. Just bring the husk back to our camp, so we can get on with this.
Have you not listened to Kaleen? Her words betray visions of power over her enemies.\n\nThis thing must be destroyed! We cannot allow this curse to fall upon anyone else.
There are no right hands to hold this evil! It must be destroyed.\n\nI cannot sail with one who would give this to those who lead the Covenant.
Priest of Arkay. Tried to stop them … Daedra caught me. <<1>> tortured me. Bragged that I would serve her master ….\n\nBlessing. Need blessing!
Of Arkay. Protect soul from Molag Bal. Stop it being perverted. Phial of water, in tunic. Reach it, please?
I … thank you.\n\nTake urn to <<1>>. <<2>>. Tell her … I am at peace.
Good. Take urn from this place. To <<1>> … in <<2>>. Safe with her.
Nearly dead, never make it. You are strong, better chance ….

Bright moons, you are talented. I have the soldiers hanging back. The temples here venerate Jone and Jode, and I do not think the lunar clergy would appreciate mass bloodshed here. In fact, the cult has befouled the shrines. Darkhearted bastards.
That poison wouldn't be here if not for Imperial incompetence. I'm here to make sure it can't harm any more people in this swamp.
My mother, Velatosse. She's at her home nearby, waiting for word about my brother. He's down in the cave, waiting for Hendil to come up with a cure.\n\nIt'll be all right. Thank you.

Imperial cities have thrown their trash into the rivers for years. The water takes it away from them, so what do they care?\n\nWell, I'm tired of us treating everywhere else like garbage. That's how this poison found its way to Shadowfen.
I've created an enchantment that will allow us to capture the gas. However, I need special containers to use the enchantment on. That's where the wasp husk comes in.

I shouldn't tell you this, but I don't care about rank. The gas is an experimental weapon deemed too dangerous for use on the battlefield. It was supposed to be locked away in the catacombs of the Imperial City, but that obviously didn't happen.
Excellent just give me a moment and … done.
About what you'd expect. It weighs on me.  \n\nThat's why I made my way to Crosswych. I think I can help the people here.
Once you've collected the poison, bring it to me. I ….\n\nIt's Marius, he wants to speak with you. Please, tell him nothing of what I said!

I've enchanted this container to draw poison within it. Place it in the path of the roaming poison. Once the container collects the poison, you can safely recover it. \n\nWe need to hurry; I hope no one else has been hurt.
Oh? I assumed you were part of the clean-up. What's Marius planning?\n\nI don't know you well enough to ask a favor, but I implore you to listen. I fear what Marius plans for the poison.
Rhea and I will take care of the poison in this region. You handle everything past Hissmir. \n\nOnce you've collected the poison, bring it to me at the disposal site near Zuuk.

Rhea would rather do what's right than what's necessary. I'm a soldier. I don't have that luxury.\n\nLook, I'm willing to pay handsomely for your help. If you decide you don't want the money, be on your way.
By Arkay's beard! Evil swirls about that urn, it is a cursed object. You were right to bring it here.\n\nWhat of Mallius?
That is the worst news I have received in a long time. I will take the urn to a holy place where its corruption can be cleansed.\n\nDid he die at peace, in Arkay's grace?
Your willingness to help shames me. \n\nYou're right. I must be strong if we are ever to feel safe again. I'll find a way to help you and Sellan. I can spread the word that we're going to fight back.
You probably think I'm just foolish, imagining Red Rooks around every corner. \n\nBut those nasty bandits are rude, greedy, and dangerous. I don't want to end up poor and destitute.
They are yours, my friend! May he look kindly on you throughout your days.
I will remain, for now. The people of Shadowfen will need Arkay in the times to come. I will do what I can to serve them.
Let Sellan know I'm with him. \n\nWe'll stick a hot poker in the backside of that pompous Sternis Gelves and the rest of his beef-witted Red Rooks!

Not sure I entirely trust that young fellow. But standing around doing nothing doesn't sit well with me, either.\n\nI'm not much use in a battle, but I can spread the word. We'll raise an army to deal with these Red Rooks!

Many were killed. Their undead corpses still roam these tunnels. \n\nThe rest were corrupted by the being we conjured. They're mindless followers now, doing its bidding. They created the Harvest Festival to trap and sacrifice unwary travelers.

Tradition! Whenever a new monarch takes the throne, there are endless rituals and ceremonies. \n\nI myself was more than halfway through the eighty-eight days of liturgical chanting required to take the throne. Then my dear sister returned.

Oh, you know how it is. In the waters off the island, there are great sea beasts. Smaller creatures cling to their sides, eating the scraps they leave behind.\n\nIt's just the same with nobility on land.

Oh yes. When our father King Hidellith, may he reign in glory, passed away she was slated to begin the ceremonies. But then she left. Just … poof. Gone, before she even entered the Sapiarch's Labyrinth.
Just so. And so it fell to me to spend the requisite three thousand five hundred and fifty-five days studying Altmeri custom and ceremoniarchy. \n\nAhem. But I digress.
Oh, nothing.\n\nIt's just hard to see how she'll ever gain the trust of the commonry now.
Yes. Some will say that the dead know something we do not. That she's unfit to be Queen.\n\nThere's nothing to that, as you well know. But it won't stop some from saying it.
Continue the rituals, of course. The priestesses are waiting on me. No unquiet dead will keep me from finishing what I began here.

I've no idea who the Veiled Queen might be. Perhaps the leader of that Veiled Heritance group?\n\nAnd in my estimation, Norion would sell his own mother if he thought he'd get a good price at the market.

Norion was a staunch supporter of my father. And after him, Naemon's bid for rule. He was very … vocal in his disappointment when I returned and took the crown. \n\nFor Norion, it's all a power game. And I wasn't playing his way.

Truly? I had hoped Astanya led some kind of small splinter group or gave a grandiose name to a group of thugs.\n\nIf they can strike at a whole town … get to me here, through Norion. Stars, they're a real threat!
Just so. I had hoped Astanya led some kind of small splinter group or gave a grandiose name to a group of thugs.\n\nIf they can strike at us here, through Norion, they're a viable threat.

It's as I said. The ceremonies are for the people. They've always been a part of crowning a new Altmeri monarch. \n\nThe people are already nervous about my extended absence. They need to know they can trust me.
It must be Norion. Thrice-damned skeever that he is, he's also an accomplished mage. \n\nTo control them so utterly, he must be nearby. I'm sure he'll show his face soon enough.

You didn't even know him … you ….\n\nNo, you're right. Heseph wasn't a soldier, but he was a strategist. He was trying to work around these bastards. The least I can do is continue what he started. I'll do whatever Sellan asks.
Are you mad? Everyone who tried is either dead or enslaved in the mines.\n\nWe can't win. The Red Rooks are too powerful. I just lost my best friend. I don't want to lose anyone else.
My band of warriors—the Stonewolves—fought and died here. To honor our sacrifice, our remains were left upon the bloodied fields.
No. I am shackled to this circle. Drusilla bound me here to gain access to my war horn. I will not be free until she is dead.
They seek to add my warriors to their numbers. But that is only part of their plan. Aid me, and I will tell you all I know.
The Ayleids—Wild Elves as some call them—have always fascinated me. They are long gone but their ruins remain on Betnikh. From these we glean how they lived and died, so many years ago.
We are not all warriors, and we are far from the savages outsiders assume. Some of us wield a quill as skillfully as others wield warhammers.
Go to Mages Guild.
Esan came as the Champion bade. He came to speak to the Guild. But the Magister … turned on Esan. They have killed me.
Of course, my friend. Our little adventure here has brought up a few questions of my own.

The Dunmer crept up from the south and attacked in the dark. They killed the watch guard, but not before he sounded the alarm.\n\nWe reacted fast. I had … an uneasy feeling, so we were on alert. Lost a few good men, but the Dunmer lost more.

It's possible, but we cornered most of the cowards and cut them down.

The last dozen or so barricaded themselves in the warehouse. Current plan is to just starve them out. 

If your messenger's alive though, they've got him in there.

Outright traitors like Norion, we end. No question. The problem is that traitors like Norion are only fanning the flame. \n\nIf I can't win over my people, the Heritance will be dealing with me instead of the other way round.

We have dozens of stops along the road, speaking at farms and holdfasts. My next big event is in Skywatch, I believe. They're throwing a festival, and I'm to make a public appearance with my sister-in-law Estre.\n\nAlways thrilling.
Worried about them turning like Norion? Hmm. I don't believe so.\n\nNorion was old guard, and never very fond of me. Most of the others awaiting us on the road honestly want change.
There's no love lost there, no. My brother took the news of my return fairly well, all things considered.\n\nI'm not sure his wife has it in her to be as forgiving. She wanted to be Queen.
Orc scouts sighted Bloodthorn Cultists in Carzog's Demise. Tazgol's mobilizing the army to go kill them all, but Lambur's worried. She thinks it might be a trap.\n\nDid you find out anything?
That's awful! I'll go find the captain.\n\nGet back to the fortress and let Lambur know. Maybe it's not too late!
Go to Temple District
It was crafted by my grandfather. Over the years, its sweet sound has brought joy to the hearts of sullen audiences and tears to the most stoic warriors. I've yet to find its equal!

I sought a shortcut to buying a home in Stormhold. I thought myself a match for that scaly trickster, but my mind blanked when confronted by her riddles.\n\nI should have stuck to musical competitions.
You don't know what you're talking about. Paranoid! If you saw what I saw .…\n\nI dreamed about this—every last detail. You think that was just a coincidence? No way.
It's something from Glenumbra and quite valuable, that is all I know. Magula sent me to fetch it, while trading goods. She needs it immediately, but I cannot yet leave.
No. Well, I don't know. This is my home. This devastation. It's almost too much to bear.
Yes, I'm fine. I separated from the others in order to rescue as many of these citizens as possible. The others seemed more focused on killing daedra. But that's their priority.
Me? Of course. It'll take more than that to hurt a Vinedusk Ranger. What're you doing here? Here to help?
<<1>>, on the island of Stros M'Kai. Have you struck your head?\n\nLong may you prosper, though perhaps elsewhere.

That's what my brother Gelvin calls his newly formed group of mercenaries. The Daggers. From Daggerfall. They're not really that bright, but their hearts are in the right place.\n\nLord Diel hired them to help him gather research about the harpies.
Oh, you know. A plan. To, uh, save Daggerfall from the harpies. Yeah, that's it.\n\nYou know what? You ask too many questions. Talk to his lordship if you want to get involved.
Return the horn to its rightful place atop my tomb in the next chamber. Then my warriors will rest once again.
Yes. I'm his mother. Why?

Right. But the worst part is, I think I'm stuck like this. I put a pile of gold on the wager and we sealed the bet with a spell. A binding contract spell. \n\nUntil I can win or lose the wager, I don't think I can move on.
Yes, I am. I'm sorry, have we met before? Your face is unfamiliar to me.
Dead? Hmm. \n\nWell, that's too bad for her. She just lost. Wait, you spoke to her before she died? Or after?
Hah! She's given up, hasn't she? I knew that little mouse couldn't keep up with me. \n\nI already know where I'm going to spend her coin. I'm going to buy this fantastic gown from the Aegis.
At last. I thought I was going to die here!
What? Our orders were to protect the reliquaries! Removing the relics is the worst thing you could do. This is a disaster!
I knew Hjorik wouldn't let us down. Thank you!
Thank you! I should be able to make it to the church now.
About time Hjorik sent someone. I've been freezing out here!

It's not that simple! There's a whole ritual to perform. The tree-minders must first calm the dreugh, and then return the relics to their containers.\n\nBut my father knows this. He knows the relics can't be disturbed. This is madness!
Removing the relics will enrage the dreugh! The tree-minders will lose control over them!

The Maormer have amassed a large force on Tempest Island. We think they've found a way to tap into the Island's inherent natural powers and they plan to unleash that power in the form of powerful storms. They have to be stopped.
Just board this ship behind me and we will take you to the assault on Tempest Island. We can use all the help we can get.
I came to make an offering to the Bright Moons. My brother Indal is off at the front in Cyrodiil, and I was to pray for his protection. That was when the screaming started.
Place the offering pouch at the nearby shrine to the waxing moons. Then my letter at the shrine to the bright, full moons. Finally, light a candle for Indal at the waning moon shrine on the hill.
Yes. They were everywhere. The dark spirits clawing at my throat. I tried to run … but I didn't … please. You have my letter, my offering. Finish what I could not.
Some say it is a tomb where the Fenlords encased themselves in ice to wait out the long ages! Others suggest a jewel-encrusted crown that reveals all places and possibilities at once!

Does it matter? It is old and very well guarded! If we gain it, we will be renowned! If it is powerful, we become powerful!\n\nWhatever happens, our names will be sung throughout the ages! Is this not a worthy goal?
If it is big, leave it and sell the location to any who would have it. If it is small, take it and find the highest bidder!\n\nIf it is powerful … well, some things are best kept to oneself, yes?
As you see. Zahra is Zahra. Joined the guild, but that wasn't for me. Too much sitting and waiting for orders—bah! Alkosh waits for no one, why should <<1>>?
Mages, to find things that are hidden. They have the most exquisite libraries in Dune—row after row of books. It's easy to see how things become lost!\n\nThen again, there is a guild for that too ….
Just as one finds things that are lost, another may lose things that are found. There is profit in both! Neither much tolerates the competition.
Studying the dead. Learning more about them. They have no minds, yes? Nothing to fill the space between the ears. Replaced with magic, old magic.\n\nFortunately, there are ways around that ….

Even in death, the Fenlords distrust their servants. To guard against rebellion, they inserted control icons into the heads of their arisen slaves.\n\n<<1>> found one. With it, I hoped to gain passage through this place, but its magic is stale.
We are the Order of the Claw, the keepers of Do'Krin. This one has protected the sacred Claw all her life. Prayed to the Bright Moons for guidance and the safety of the Khajiiti people.

Do'Krin Monastery. "The Warrior's Grin," in the Tamrielic tongue. A holy site to those of us in the lunar clergy, a stopover for pilgrims, and a training ground for those who practice the martial vows.

You're obviously the capable sort. And if you're willing to help us, I would be a fool to deny the mercy of Jone and Jode. The alternative is Javad Tharn with his hands on the Claw. That must not come to pass.
Of course. But that would mean abandoning my clan. I understand the importance of our traditions. I must be sure I'm doing the right thing.
He went into the keep. Sir Croix might be protecting him though. \n\nFinding Hughes may be difficult until we clear up all the confusion here. You should talk to Sir Edmund. He's just up the steps.

He went into the keep. With all the fighting that's been going on, it's hard to say where Hughes may be.\n\nAsk Sir Edmund. If everything's settled down, he'll want to help you. Edmund should be up in the courtyard, or just inside the main hall.
You met my daughter, then. She has spirit, I'll give her that. She'll make a worthy wife.
Only out of respect for the chief and for the good of the alliance, not for you. Are you ready to go?

I've heard all the talk about the Daggerfall Covenant. Captain Kaleen mentions it enough. Orcs, Redguards, and Bretons in a grand alliance.\n\nMy ancestors fought at Orsinium. Many died fighting the Orcs. I respect them, but I'll never trust them.

Does not work well. Magic has faded, yes? It is enough to stop one of these monsters in its tracks, but only for a time.\n\nZahra was barely able to overcome the one at our feet. This is why I need your help.
If you think it best, Zahra agrees. Your help is needed to supplement Zahra's cleverness.
With regret, no. <<1>> is very clever but not so strong. If the Moons do not smile on us, this stone may be Zahra's only escape.
Lerisa's choice, not mine. That said, Mekag's not bad, for an Orc.\n\nBut I'm not setting foot on an island full of them. Especially not a clan that's refused to join the Covenant!
Ha ha ha. The traps, dog. You'll never get past the traps. The Ancients were too good at their craft. You'll never … you'll never get to the circlet.
In life, I laughed. Some say I was mischievous. An impractical present for a practical woman seemed irresistibly witty.
The Spearhead is set to sail. Are you ready?
When my love left to become the Green Lady, she left something behind.\n\nI kept it to remind myself of our time together. Of what could have been.
In my darkest hour, I prayed to every god and creature on Nirn. I was desperate. I needed a way to change what was. Change the story of the Bosmer.\n\nI found it here.

Xuth, you speak as one new to the high seas. I have seen this island and countless others like it.\n\nThe captain and Chief Tazgol have an arrangement. We have visited Betnikh more times than I can count.
We came for the circlet. General Lavinia has great plans. We've … we've started with Arenthia. With the circlet, we'll take the Dominion apart piece … by … piece.
I'm staying here for a while, then moving on when the roads are safer. Until then, I just have to worry about running out of ale. Oh, and wolves.
She is the chief's only daughter. I would rather her be miserable and alive than dead on some fool adventure. But I don't expect an outsider to understand.
So. She sent you to argue for her? She knows her duty. It is our way. The alliance her marriage makes for our clan will enable us to survive in these dangerous times.

Our lives belong to the clan! Its survival depends on marriage alliances more than strong sword arms. Lokra must accept her part and perform her duty.\n\nIf you want to help, remind her of this. Maybe she'll listen to you.
A good Orc female doesn't spend her time on frivolous courting. When she wants you, she takes you. I've made my interest clear, so now it's up to her.\n\nI need another drink.
I sense Lokra found an ally in you. But your efforts are for naught. I cannot determine her path. Nor can her mother or my son, the chief.
Chief Tazgol pays us well, to acquire and deliver cargoes. I believe he pines for the days when his ancestors ruled the high seas, plundering and pillaging. Perhaps he sees some of himself in Kaleen.
As companion to famous Zahra, a share in my fame, of course! But you mean compensation, yes? <<1>> has a cache reserved for this very thing.\n\nDo not worry, you will be paid well!

Esan left to investigate the second portal near the Mages Guildhall. He may have sought out the advice of his peers in the Guild. They're over in the merchant district, my friend. I'd like you to see if you can find him.

Only Lokra can decide. Her sense of duty battles her desire to live her life. Many daughters have chosen exile over the years. I did once. While the decision is Lokra's alone, she seems to value your advice.
To follow her heart. Lokra knows what she wants, and she knows the cost. She wants to be free but fears exile from the clan. \n\nHer heart knows the path she should follow.
She wishes to be free of guilt. She knows what she wants but fears the consequences. Choices always come with a price. \n\nLokra must choose and accept the cost.

Koeglin Village smelled like a dock, and I don't appreciate the sort of riff-raff that comes off those boats. \n\nRowdy sailors knocking over my wood piles and stomping my flower beds every day … By Azura, I couldn't take it anymore!
So what's your opinion, after talking to everyone? I really want to know.

Fine. We have to get word to High King Emeric, so <<1>> has asked me to sail you there. Understand I only do this out of respect for the Chieftain and for the allaince, and not for you. So are you here because you're ready to go or what?

Bayya has a warding totem. Used it to seal the hall. Always … always said it was protection magic. But the Mages. They're trapped in the Hall. Kill Bayya, and destroy the totem. Save the Mages. And this city.
I don't know. I heard … I heard Bayya shout something about the Tharn. Javad Tharn must have corrupted the leaders of our hall. They ran for the inn. They must plan their escape … the totem.
Cultists attacked our fortress, Khazun Ghash. They thought their magic would be too much for the primitive Orcs.\n\nFunny that magic doesn't work when a mace caves in your skull.
Bloodthorn. Necromancers who think too much of themselves.\n\nAfter we stopped the attack, Chief Tazgol ordered us to burn the bodies. Don't want them raising each other, eh?

Even if <<1>> was called away, one of the other tree-minders should have stayed to tend the fire.\n\nMy father would sooner lose an arm than disobey orders. I smell treachery. I'll wager this is some twisted Dominion plot.

Fine. We have to get word to High King Emeric, so <<1>> has asked me to sail you there. \n\nUnderstand I only do this out of respect for the Chieftain and for the alliance, and not for you. So are you ready to go or what?
The dreugh may have taken them. They've been driven insane with blood lust. \n\nDreugh bury their captured prey alive, in piles of hardened mud. We must find them before they suffocate.

Give the relics to me. You've done enough damage for one day!\n\nForgive me. I've no right to blame you. You were only following my father's orders. You can trust me. The relics will be safe with me until we locate <<1>> and the others.

Great! Let's go. I'll stick close, if you don't mind. You look like you can handle that weapon you're carrying and I'd rather not get eaten by a construct.\n\nIf we get separated, I'll meet you back here.
I could always go into treasure-hunting. I hear there's some kind of valuable stone down in the Koeglin Mine.\n\nCourse, I could end up with something worse than splinters ….

Vile scum called the Bloodthorn Cult attacked. I got the name from one of the survivors before I split his skull. They're necromancers, defilers of the dead.\n\nWe taught them a lesson. They won't be back.
A few broke into my library, probably just to hide. Some old Breton scrolls are missing, likely destroyed in the attack.\n\nBreton scrawlings, bah! If they came for those, they wasted their lives.
Mauloch only knows. And I don't care. Whatever the reason, they died poorly and in great numbers.
There's a pack of Dremora just up the road. I'm sure they're heading into Bruma. We need to keep them out of town.

Not without getting that totem out of here. They can smell it or something. Even then, we'll need reinforcements to take back the Watch. \n\nI sent a request to Captain Ernard, but if he doesn't arrive soon, we'll just have to withdraw.
I suppose you're right. It's an honor to enable two clans to unite. I should hold the clan above myself and do my duty.
You're right. I value my family, but this is my life. I should live it as I choose. I'm going to follow my heart.
We should separate to cover more ground. If you find them, bring them back to this camp. \n\nMake haste! Every moment puts them closer to death!

Ayleid necromancer kings who once ruled Black Marsh. When their slaves rose against them, the Fenlords had them executed and revived as undead.\n\nPreserved against the ages, they toil even now, protecting the tombs of their long-dead masters.

Unknown. Some say they created the <<1>> and left Nirn forever. Others claim they were overwhelmed by Alessia's rebellion.\n\nWhat matters to Zahra is finding the <<1>>, obtaining it, and getting out of here alive. A fine goal, no?
Some ghost story about the old Pariah Catacombs—probably just rubbish. \n\nOf course, no one's been down there in years, so you never know. Anything could be down there.
Look at the blade. That's Saervild's weapon! What could drive a father to such madness that he would murder his own hatchling?
Just off the road to Wayrest. I'll mark it on your map.\n\nHey though, if you find something down there, don't forget the girl who gave you the tip.

I mean too late! He's been infected too long. I've seen it before. Soon he'll be one of them. A vampire.

I … I have to stop this. I have to stop him from coming back.

Don't I?
At the bottom of the hill the abbey sits upon. Here. I'll mark it on your map. \n\nI'd be careful if you go down there. It could be dangerous!
Then Saervild has betrayed us all. Perhaps he has been taken by some madness … or perhaps he is in league with our enemies.\n\nBalance must be restored. Where are the relics now?

Yet here is his body, and the relics are nowhere to be found. \n\nIf Saervild was an agent of the Dominion, the relics could already be in our enemy's hands. In time, they will discover how to use them to control the dreugh.

The Dominion camp, at bog's edge. I'm no warrior, but there is something I can do. A ritual that might serve as a diversion.\n\nI'll need something from their camp. Something laden with their scent. Can you do this?
When you have the item, bring it to the reliquary within these ruins. I'll prepare myself for the ritual and meet you there.

Yeah. Farangel's Delve—an old mine where the Midnight Union's hiding who-knows-what.\n\nBeen trying to work up the nerve to sneak in there and have a look, but now I'm too drunk. If you're interested … there. Marked it on your map.
You're not going to try to write a piece on this yourself, are you?
Just gathering my belongings. I had to leave so suddenly I … missed a couple of necessities.\n\nNow, get out of my house, won't you? I don't want you here.
Of course this is my house! I told you it was my house. Why would I be in here if it wasn't my house?\n\nAnd you're still standing there. Didn't I just tell you to leave?

That's just what he wants you to believe. And you're stupid enough to listen to his lies! It's a shame a troll didn't rip your heart out. It's what you and those killers deserve!\n\nNow get out of my way. I have what I came for.
