Figures you'd be working with the lizards. They always lure outsiders to their cause with false promises and sob stories.\n\nThose Argonians are killers. If you're working with them, you're no better than they are.

Oh! In that case, let me point it out on your map. It's straight ahead. Just up that hill there. You will tell me if you find anything of historic importance, won't you? I might even give you a byline for your trouble…
What am I talking about? That Dreamwalker! He uses dark magic, magic he doesn't understand.\n\nHow many innocents have to die because of his recklessness?
Hah! Thank the Eight. I'm glad that witch got the justice they deserved. They sold their souls to Javad Tharn, that coward. I can't believe they locked us in here. \n\nYou've saved our lives.
You are most welcome. Close the portals … and beware. If you have slain Bayya, you have earned Novundo's wrath. The Magister was a powerful summoner. And will no doubt be a deadly foe.
I was up at Bearclaw Mine thinking. Alone, by myself, I wasn't drinking! All of a sudden, I saw something moving inside the place.
It's just up the hill there. I'll mark it on your map. I'd go myself, but … uh … I can't abandon my company! You know how it is.

Hehe … I wish I had, but no.\n\nIf you really want to collect for S'rashi and don't mind getting your hands dirty, you could always dig up my grandfather's grave at the temple—he was buried with a valuable stone. Always seemed like a waste to me.
It's a terrible spot, actually. If only I could've made it to Alcaire Castle.\n\nIf the bandits see me here like this, I'll be lucky if the cart is the only thing I lose!

Wizard Benele is nice enough, but she's not very sensible. She barely looked up from her books and scrolls, even when the fighting got intense.\n\nOh, she'd pause long enough to zap a zombie that wandered too close, but otherwise she was oblivious.
Watch yourself. You are a guest here.
How did you get in here? Get out!
I don't know for sure, but I heard they were camped out up the road at Portdun Watch. \n\nHere, I'll mark it on your map, just in case you feel like getting them before they get me!
Goat stew is delicious, full of meat, potatoes, and not too many vegetables. \n\nHeggvir is a pretty good cook. She'll probably need your help getting some of the ingredients for her stew, though.
Of course I like steak. I'm Nord, aren't I?\n\nThat's all Kalogar really knows how to cook. Bear steaks, usually. He'll probably need your help getting the meat.
We just need to make sure we have plenty of good food and we're all set.\n\nFunny that two visitors wandered in today. You and that bard. At least the party will have proper music this time!
Place the bedding in the reliquary. My ritual will plant the seed of the Dominion's destruction in the minds of the dreugh.
Of course I like steak. I'm Nord, aren't I?\n\nThat's all Kalogar really knows how to make. Bear steaks, usually. He'll probably need your help getting the meat.
Goat stew is delicious, full of meat and potatoes. And not too many vegetables. \n\nHeggvir is a pretty good cook. She'll probably need your help getting some of the ingredients for her stew, though.
The Dominion must be stopped before they learn the secrets of the relics, and Saervild must pay for Njorlund's murder.\n\nLet us begin. Place the item on the reliquary.
The prey's scent is placed into a sacred vessel to attract the nearest predator. This ritual will turn the dreugh on the dryskin fools who seek to enslave them.

Wonderful! Here. If you feed this herb to a goat and pet it, it will follow you around like a lost puppy. Lead it back here and I'll take care of the rest.\n\nThe amazing aroma of the simmering stew will have mouths watering throughout Cragwallow.
One of the wild goats that wander around the area. They eat the flowers and sweet grasses during the spring and summer. It makes them so delicious.
Don't wait too long. I need to get the ingredients all simmering together. That way the flavors meld. You can't rush good cooking!
Yes, but the dream is Hosni's. Somewhere in this dream is the Omen of Blood, the demon from Quagmire that drives him to madness. \n\nYou must find the Omen, and slay it.

That old bear should be in his lair this time of the day. It's north and west from here. \n\nJust drop that old lunch on the rock in front of the cave. The smell should lure Old Ironclaw out and you can take care of him.
Well, don't take all day. There's a lot of steaks that need to be seared and lots of hungry people to feed. And they're hungry for real food!

That's where you come in. You look like you could carve up a bear.\n\nGo lure Old Ironclaw from his cave. Just toss these leftovers Heggvir made out front. It should attract the bear. Goodness knows no Nord will eat the stuff.

I do! If you had known Oda and seen her among the wolves … well, you would look at them differently, too.\n\nShe was blessed by Kyne and the wolves were always gentle around her. She taught me to respect them. Ah, my fair Oda.

Whoever the Dreamwalker is trying to save. He sent you for his reagents, didn't he? That's why you were in the house.\n\nThat's why I was there too. To make sure he never stepped into another dream again. Let me go and I'll tell you where to find them.

I put the reagents into a vase and threw it into the ruined building I ran by.\n\nTake them and get back to your Dreamwalker. Just know it won't work. She's dead, regardless of what you do. Just … just like my wife.
I tried to destroy this monster after what he did to my wife. But it's out of my hands now.\n\nLet me go and I'll tell you where I hid the reagents. Kill me and you'll never find them.
Mauloch's hand, no! If she were, we would not have these troubles. She is the daughter of Sholg, Tazgol's Hearth-Wife. That one's softness has made Lokra selfish and difficult.
I don't know about the others. They must've wandered off in search of shelter. They don't have the bravado of an elite Bosmer warrior. That includes the Moon-Hallowed, too.
Have you checked with that Urcelmo fellow? Real uptight High Elf with a stick up his arse? That Moon-Hallowed woman might be trying to save people before closing that portal.
Not with that goody goody Altmer marine? Perhaps she's with that Kazargi cat. Search me, though.
Aye. She was. But we got separated as soon as that Atronach followed me in here. She probably got sick of dallying and went straight for the portal. Check there.
I pay her no mind. I only wish I'd given Tazgol a daughter. My boys are strong, but the clan needs more daughters.
I do not.  She might be with that Odreth fellow. He looked dead-set on killing as many things as possible, and the Moon Hallowed might want to clear out daedra before closing the portal.
He might be with Lieutenant Kazargi, who said that she went to ensure her relatives were safe in town. Otherwise, I don't know.
She might be with that Odreth fellow. He looked dead-set on killing as many things as possible, and the Moon Hallowed might want to clear out daedra before closing the portal.
She was, but we split up recently. She said that she had had enough and was going after the portal once and for all. You can find her out there.

Rarely does a clan permit a daughter to leave, and never without cause. Lokra is the chief's only daughter. We need her to do her duty. If she leaves without permission, well, clanless life is never easy.
Most outsiders view Orcs as savage beasts. We have many enemies. We must be harsh to survive.

Shackles are not always made of iron. My destiny was decided when I was born a female. As the chief's only daughter, my duty is to marry into another clan, forging an alliance. It is our way and my fate.
Go ahead; it won't do any good. Orc clans survived this way for many generations. It's simply how things are. I understand that, as much as it angers me.
If only I had the courage! I want nothing more than to see the world before I marry, but I can't, not without the blessing of my mother and grandmother.

The clan chief is the only male who takes wives. The wives are crucial to the leadership and stability of the clan. Sons eventually try to take over the clan by strength, while daughters are married off to other clans.

My research suggests the three parts of the sword—the blade, the hilt, and the pommel—can be found in the three towers within the hold.\n\nOnly King Aphren's spirit can reforge the sword. You must take the pieces into the king's tomb.
It's not that. I would enjoy the honor and responsibility of being a chief's wife. I just want to see the world, to live my life, before I marry for the good of the clan.

The Hound … the Silvenar … the Green Lady. They fight with each other and who gets chewed up and swallowed? We do!\n\nI'm tired of worrying. Maybe I'll go to Velyn Harbor or Elden Root. The Altmer don't have these sorts of problems.

Well, you've traveled more than I have. Maybe you're right.\n\nStill, if we could go a week or so without the mer attacking, or someone killing our leaders, or spirits of the past trying to take over, I'll be grateful.
Travels? Leave Silvenar? Well, let's not go that far. The roads are dangerous!\n\nMaybe I'll have a drink and think about this. Elden Root's pretty far away.
Could you please elaborate a little? I've waited here for quite some time with the expectation that you would bring me the sword.\n\nI think you owe me at least some explanation.

S'rashi likes Captain Marck, but debt must be paid in gold, or in blood.\n\nHm. There is another walker in Wayrest who owes S'rashi a blood debt— the Redguard assassin Ramziq. If you kill Ramziq, S'rashi will forgive Marck.

Ramziq has been hiding, but S'rashi knows where. She's in a home just down the street in the market.\n\nBe careful though. Ramziq is a very dangerous warrior woman, and she knows S'rashi will send someone after her.

You what? I've been researching this for months. I hiked all the way out here—on my own, I should note, and now you tell me you gave my treasure to someone else!? \n\nNext time, if I want something, I'm not hiring someone I meet on the road!
And now you're just going to give up? \n\nFine. I'll find someone else to help me. Just be on your way then.

I'm the overseer for the royal work crews in this area. When I left for Windhelm a few days ago, my workers were hale and whole. \n\nNow I come back to find many of them cut down and the rest injured and confused. I need answers!
Yes, yes … but I've been waiting to hear the musicians! When they showed up in Silvenar, there was some trouble with the Hound.\n\nMaybe he doesn't like music?
They told you? You've talked to them? These are some of the most famous musicians in Malabal Tor and you know them?\n\nI … uh … I mean … can you introduce me? No, wait! I'd be too embarrassed.

Yes, yes … but I've been waiting to hear the musicians! They haven't shown up yet. I know they arrived in town, but there was some problem with the Houndsmen.\n\nI hear they fled into the ravine below the city.

I doubt it. Everyone was so caught up in staying away from the Houndsmen that no one cares about the band.\n\nI bet if you head across the bridge and into the ravine you might find some trace of them. Unless the mers got them.

That poor man. I once knew a Redguard. Good man. Had a loving wife. Very sad time, but that's another discussion.\n\nIs bad that we have no reagents. Will make the ritual more dangerous. Less likely to succeed.

No, and I've never been bitten by a thunderbug, either, but I know it hurts!\n\nLook, if you're interested in Dark Elves, you should just wander around outside the city. They'll find you, soon enough.
You and anyone else who survived whatever happened here.\n\nI need to report to Jarl. How did you end up in Cragwallow?

My gut tells me you aren't responsible. No injuries, but you seem to be recovering your wits well enough. \n\nHelp me investigate what happened. Talk to some of the survivors. Let's see if we can piece together recent events.
No. Look, they say you're a hero and everything, but I'm not interested in being your friend.\n\nOff you go now! Farewell!
We've had too much upheaval here. I just want things to get back to normal. The sooner we clear away this mess … and the bodies … the sooner Silvenar will feel safe again.

It's a grim time. We lost a Green Lady and a Silvenar, then came within a Khajiit's whiskers of losing the new ones before the handfast!\n\nLook, I know what you did for us, and I'm grateful, but we've had a lifetime's excitement in the past few days.

I thought you might. Your life is all about danger and adventure, isn't it? The rest of us are just trying to survive.\n\nI'm grateful for what you did, but I'd rather not need any heroes for the next few years.
Must try anyways. Do not have much time left. Still have chance of saving, even now, just much more dangerous.\n\nMany thanks to you for trying. Will remember that, whatever happens.

I wish I could remember something. I was relaxed, drinking a bit.\n\nI heard the bard start to play and I decided I was going to have another piece of pie. Next thing I knew, I woke up with this lump on my head and … and … they're all dead ….
No, it was just a normal pie. Apple, I think. Oh. Sorry, I'm still a bit fuzzy.\n\nI think there might have been a brawl outside. Maybe someone got into a fight?
I'll recover. Sometimes the magic goes wrong and bad things happen.\n\nI'd risk all of this and more if I had another chance to save her. But no, it was not to be.
Without my reagents, I couldn't protect myself from the horrors that roam the Dreamstride.\n\nBut I don't blame you. At least you tried to help when no one else cared. That means very much to me.

Not exactly. Sometimes even when everything goes right, something goes wrong. You can't save everyone, no matter how hard you try.\n\nThe Redguard hates me for what happened to his wife. I guess he got his revenge. He took one of our own this day.
That which lives in dreams, can be slain in dreams. \n\nIf you kill Vaermina's Omen in Hosni's dream, it will be ejected from our world forever. And my son will be free.
Will hate bring back Sister-of-Wind? Did it bring back Asmalah's wife?\n\nHe did what anyone would do. He sought revenge against the one he thought was responsible. He did what he thought was right.
I'll tell Blue-Bird about her egg-sister. Then I'll let the clan grieve for its loss.\n\nOnce I know the clan is safe, I will move on. Find a new purpose. That's the way of the Dreamwalker.

I think so. I was having a drink. We could even hear the bard playing from inside, though it was a bit muted.\n\nI don't remember much else until Kalogar pushed me out of the way of … something. To protect me. And look what happened.
It's all so confusing. But now that you mention it, perhaps it was more like shrieking. Like some kind of angry creature swooping in for the kill.
No, no. We were singing. The bard was playing. I think I saw you singing along, too.
I honestly can't recall. Did I fall asleep?\n\nI remember a sudden pain. Something or someone stabbed me. There were noises, but it all seems … foggy or something.
All right. Take it. If you come back and I'm dead though, I still want it back. I want to be buried with it.\n\nIt's always brought me luck. Hope it does the same for you, for all of us.

I remember the bard started to sing. A droning ballad of some sort. Come to think of it, he didn't seem to know the words. \n\nAnyway, and then I sort of woke up, covered in bruises, with my friends dead around me. Who would do this?
Not easily, but I promised them.\n \nSince I will fulfill the sentence, I think you should decide whether any of them should be released.
Into that cave. I never even knew there was a cave up here.\n\nHe was still alive when they dragged him in there. The Goblins seemed excited about something.

I'm a road worker, not a soldier. I'm not going to walk into a den of rieklings. That would be suicide!\n\nWhatever has the rieklings so riled up probably led to the attack on Cragwallow. I hope you can save the bard and figure out what's going on.
I'll be fine. That was some damned impressive work. Khali would, I'm sure, offer you some kind of critique on your technique. I'm just glad I have you here today. Especially for what must come next.

I know not, but I certainly aim to find out. First though, you must report what we've learned to Marbruk. We need to at least keep them informed.\n\nDon't worry, when the time is right, the forest will help me find you again. Until then, be safe.
I don't work with him. I serve him! As you should. The prince is your better, and serving him is serving the Dominion.\n\nThink about it.
I need to report to the Thalmor Council. The Queen and Speaker Gharesh-ri will want to know we've had some success here. This one trusts you to get the job done.

Bright moons, my friend. Go carefully. This invasion, it smacks of desperation. Until now Tharn has been content to pull the strings from the shadows. To openly attack a Dominion icon like Dune … he must have a plan.

I don't see a portal, but … I have to trust my instincts. Let's cleanse the shrines and let the bright moons shine down on this place. You see to the temples of Jone and Jode. The old shrine to Lorkhaj still stands. I'll take care of that one.

We have pushed back the Daedra. You heard the Tharn, he means to walk the Two-Moons Path himself. I can't … I can't put this off any longer. We must make for the Temple of the Dance. Follow me. I'll lead the way.
As often as we can! The Skald-King himself sends the mead to us on a regular basis. Likes to keep his workers happy. \n\nGood man, King Jorunn. Shor bless him.
Here and there. These camps are well built and well maintained. Great places to rest when the weather turns ugly.
His body is shutting down. This blood will work as a countering agent to the poison. It won't be enough to turn him. I don't think.\n\nBesides, we don't have many options available to us, do we?
The cursed blood of my family does indeed run through my veins.\n\nI'm not ashamed of it. What I'm ashamed of is what my people do with this power.
I believe that I can trust you. If you help me with something, I'll do whatever you ask as long as it doesn't involve hurting anyone.

A final defense bars our way into the reliquary proper. The Guardian Senche stands watch inside. Normally, you would have to be a high priest of the lunar clergy to cease its protection. With the blessings you carry, you will have no trouble.

Just so. In peaceful times, the Claw can sit in the darkness. At rest. This is not a peaceful time for the March. The Claw may yet be a weapon against the Tharn and his brood, and the priests will know how to use it.
This one … he senses a darkness moving towards us. The cult must have felt the change within the Monastery. We should move quickly.
Wherever the lunar winds take you next, know that you have done the Khajiiti people a service today. Keep the Claw safe that it may protect our tomorrows as well.
The most prominent of the remaining councilors are Councilors Virgile, Donella, and Theodore. Look for them around town and convince them to help us or we're finished before we even get started.
Whatever it was, it wasn't a miner. That place is abandoned. That's why I go there to uh … think.
Fascinating. It must be simply fascinating. It's something I've always dreamed of.\n\nIt's really not fair that this happened to you. You're no Goblin scholar. It should've been me.
My wife Jakild is a strong woman. She can handle herself, but I'm afraid that the draugr might be too much for her.
My brother Kerthor is strong and hard-headed. We don't always get along. But I wouldn't wish these shambling monsters on my worst enemy!
My cousin Agnedir is so young and so beautiful. We agreed to allow her to apprentice with us for the season. If something happens to her, what am I going to tell her mother?
Funny you should ask. My cousin Afren was just telling me about some Ayleid ruin some wizard was telling him about. Called the place Silumm.

That's exactly what I told Afren! He's all talk, though. His mouth starts running after he gets a few drinks in him and talks big. \n\nHe's probably sleeping it off somewhere nearby. He'll wake up tomorrow and forget all about Silumm.

Well, it has a name you can say, for one. That's highly unusal.\n\nAfren said the Dominion was interested in old Ayleid ruins, such as Silumm. He decided to go see what was there. He likes to think he's brave, but he's afraid of his own shadow.

The Dominion. They could have agents hiding anywhere around here.\n\nThe bastards are particularly interested in old ruins. And in case you haven't noticed, you can't take a dozen steps without running into an ancient structure out here.

They're probably looking for magical artifacts they can use against us. That's my guess.\n\nI wanted to check out a few places, like Enduum. But my superior said no. Told me to stay alert and obey orders. Bah.
No, not anymore. There's steady work and it's nice here. Not to mention that the walls are thick and strong.\n\nCity life can be dangerous, but it's nowhere near as deadly as life in the wilderness.

No, but it could have! I used to explore a lot, go on adventures. And then I discovered that old Ilessan Tower. The place gave me a really bad feeling.\n\nNow I know that adventuring isn't for me. I'm staying in the city from now on.

I can ask one of them to lead you to the remains of the cursed dead. If you can find the skulls or some such—bring them to the Stone Table. I will go ahead and prepare so we can commune with them. \n\nJust trust me on this. It'll work. You'll see.
Perhaps. This one is getting quite hungry.
This one likes that! Here are my fangs! Now off to find a warm room and a good meal.
This one does not see any profit in that. This one shall continue the hunt!

Really? I heard rumors of chaos at the Abbey, but I had hoped they weren't true. \n\nThe Midnight Union's never really been a problem. I mean sure, they engage in a little smuggling and gambling, but this … it just doesn't make sense.

Well. We need to go straight to the source. The Midnight Union does nothing without the approval of Count Hosni at-Tura. I can't imagine him being behind this, but one never knows.\n\nHosni has a walled estate on the shore to the west of here.

Strangely enough, the man has apparently chosen this same time to have a betrothal celebration, and I happen to have an invitation I won't be using.\n\nGo in my stead and talk to Hosni. Find out if he knows anything about the Dream Shard.
No. Despite what <<1>> would tell you, sheer force can pummel us into the ground. Without <<2>>'s magic, my bones would still be in the pile where the Worm Cult left me.\n\nLousy mushroom-nibblers.

Healing magic works. We often use magical fonts recovered from the temple, like the one next to me.\n\nThe cultists took one last night, but <<1>> has another. The rest are inside the temple. You're welcome to use them while you're still … underfed.
Perhaps if I rest a moment, I might be able to continue.
You're right. Continuing would be too dangerous. Here are the fangs I've found so far. Good luck!
To Oblivion with you! I'll find the strength to continue!
I'm in it to the end. I'll prove my worth to my clan, and reap the rewards!
Pah. With the Green stalking my steps, I'll have this bounty before anyone else!
Ah! I … you're right. It's very dangerous out here. Here … here are my fangs. I'm going home!
Last night, I saw lights up there—a lot of them. \n\nThe place is supposedly abandoned so no one believes me, but I know what I saw!
It's just up the hill there. I'll mark it on your map. I'd go myself, but General Godrun would have me hanged if I abandoned my post.

It was Serge. It was all Serge. \n\nIt was like he was two different people: generous, loving Serge, and greedy, hateful Serge. Only I think the hateful one was the real man. He didn't want me—he only wanted my family's wealth.
You don't have to tell me twice!
Oh, thank you. I'll go to the fishing village. That's where Eiraki always takes us during an emergency.
What the Colovians are looking for. Why they're here.

But it's … well, I suppose you're right. Go ahead and destroy it. Then we can get out of here.\n\nYou're going to have to get the key from the riekling chieftain to let me out of the cage. You are going to let me out, aren't you?
I had no idea it would attract rieklings. They placed it on that altar-thing over there. Their chief seems to like to look at it. He keeps coming in. Makes me nervous how he stares at me.
No! Leave me alone! I didn't look in the sacks!
A relic. The Ancients, they used this ruin as some kind of a vault. Something they wanted hidden away. Forever.

She's a good soldier. Very quiet. Like that cat, Razum-dar. Snuck a squad into the ruin looking for the relic. Damned Colovians, though. They collapsed the main entrance, activated a ward on the rear.

Good soldier. But bloodthirsty. The other cat … Razum-dar. Cool as ice. Led a squad into the ruin after the relic. Damned Colovians, though. They collapsed the main entrance, activated a ward on the rear.
I saw them, before I got hit. They've stashed them in a pair of chests in their camp. Set their most powerful mages to guard them.
Please don't kill me. He sent you to get his precious meat after I failed to return, didn't he?\n\nI don't want anything else to do with Skorvild or his cult. Just leave me alone.

You don't know? Skorvild has always been intense, but lately he's become obsessed with power. His militia treats him like he's some sort of god.\n\nI suggest you stay out of his way and leave Lower Yorgrim before it's too late.

Skorvild organized a militia. He wants to offer his services to the Skald-King. But something went wrong. He forced us to eat the disgusting rations he made. After that, the giants attacked Lower Yorgrim.\n\nI think Skorvild drew the giants to us.
I don't know exactly, but I think it has something to do with the rations. \n\nI … I looked in one of the sacks. His rations. He makes them from giant meat!

Skorvild discovered a ritual in a secret room beneath the manor house. He's become more and more belligerent ever since.\n\nYou need to tell Eiraki about this. Bring the giant meat to her as proof. She'll know what to do. Me? I'm heading to Windhelm.

So you'd think, but we've never caught any of the traitors. They may not actually be Bosmer at all. \n\nOur enemies are always one step ahead of us. Oromin doesn't want to believe it, but I think it's obvious there's a spy among the Thalmor.
Everyone who's too lazy to do his own—Ilwen, for example. I'm not a farmer, so I contribute to the common good in this way.

Not at all. What have armies ever done for peasants, aside from kill us, enslave us, and ruin or steal our crops? Dominion, Pact, and Covenant—they're just different names for the same mindless violence and evil.

The Ironhands come from our side of the mountains, from Wrothgar. They've plagued our efforts to rebuild Orsinium for years.\n\nMurtag clan has fought them more times than I can count. That's why King Emeric asked us to come to Gavaudon's aid.
A fair point. Raz … er, I will keep that in mind. \n\nYou have spoken with the treethane then? You understand my genius plan, yes?

Our shrine is dedicated to Zenithar, the patron god of those who earn their way in this world. Prefect Antias is very diligent in seeing that the proper offerings are made, ensuring Cropsford's prosperity.
Oh, there's part of me that misses that life. I spent much of my youth selling my sword to the highest bidder. It was exciting and took me across Tamriel. I loved it!

Because it was Bretons who destroyed Orsinium, and now Murtag clan must come to their rescue? Maybe.\n\nEmeric's my friend, and he's High King of the Daggerfall Covenant, but we won't forget Orsinium. 'Wait until next time'. We … that's what we say.

Both. I fought at Emeric's side in Ranser's war. We helped drive the Reachmen from Stormhaven, and in exchange, Emeric returned Orsinium to Orc hands. \n\nThat conflict was of mutual benefit. This one isn't.

Our chieftain is in Wrothgar, but I am proud to say I lead Murtag clan in battle. Centuries ago, Murtag clan was one of the strongest clans in Orsinium. \n\nWe were nearly destroyed along with the city, but we are resilient.

I also remember sleeping on the cold, hard ground, going hungry for days at a time, and the constant fear of a blade in the back.\n\nFarming may lack excitement, but it has its advantages. Good friends, good food, and a warm bed.

Some of us do, some don't. It will be decades before Orsinium regains its former glory.\n\nMany see the city as a reminder of past defeats. Nonetheless, Murtag clan works to rebuild it, and to defend it from the Ironhand Ogres.
What? How could my brother cause the giants to attack Lower Yorgrim? That makes no sense! What proof do you have?
Oh no. Skorvild has gone insane! Please, you must stop him. If he goes ahead with this ritual, he'll only make matters worse.

Troop movement in Cyrodiil, defensive measures to shore up the border with Colovia, payment schedules for soldiers housed at Dune—there are many important things in that case. Things even Zadala does not know about, to speak truly.

We must warn the tree-minders! Take the relics to <<1>>. Her camp is near the ruins. She'll know what to do.\n\nI'll go back to the camp and speak to my father. There must be a logical explanation for this.

If you can make the ridge, I bet fifty gold those ogres fall back.\n\nTake my warhorn. If you get across, climb the tower and blow the horn. That will signal us to move up and establish a forward command post. Guts and glory, friend!

Indeed, indeed. I am Molg the Music-maker. I am a craftsman. I make beautiful instruments.\n\nAh, I know what you are thinking. "An Orc? Making delicate instruments? Carrying a lute, instead of an axe?"
I'm actually not a very good musician. But I am a good craftsman.

For sale? For sale? Are you mad?\n\nThese instruments take me years to make. Each one lovingly crafted, I travel the world for the woods, the inlay materials. Sell them? It would be like selling my own children.
I understand. I will mourn for my brother later. Right now, we still have to do something about the giants.

First of all, he's a Breton. No self-respecting Dunmer would ever marry one of those people. But even if he were Dunmer, he is poor and will remain so. My daughter will not marry a lowly Breton farmer!

I don't know where the closest giant burial ground is, but perhaps if we burn the remains it will show them that we're sorry. That we want to be left in peace.\n\nUse the fire right outside, then meet me at the fishing camp when the task is done.
You don't know my father. He blames Bretons for all that's wrong in Cyrodiil. And he hates Remius.
Yes, actually! Sorry, but my brother's made off with it. Egolor fished it out himself. It was really beautiful … nice carving, dark wood. Looked expensive.

Perhaps my time among the dead has hardened my heart, but I don't mourn my brother. Jorunn is a good king, but he would have been soft on Fildgor. You did him a favor.\n\nNow you must leave this place. Go, speak to Jorunn and tell him what transpired.

Honorable, but perhaps misguided. You should have just killed him and been done with it. Forgive me, my detachment from life has given me a cold view of things.\n\nYou should speak with Jorunn and make sure that Fildgor pays for his crimes.

Green take him, he's running debts with some people down at Thizzrini Arena. He headed off to sell it and clear some of his accounts. He usually rents a room, a little house, when he's there. That's probably where you'll find him.

That's better than I expected. You have proven yourself worthy enough to join my militia and share in the strength that will soon be ours.\n\nOur strength will increase a thousandfold, more than enough to defeat the giants and all of Skyrim's enemies!

You see the spriggans and lurchers everywhere? They feel it. The coming invasion. Daedra.\n\nI am the last priest of the Wooded Eye. We were charged with protecting this grove, but the wards have failed. We have failed.

Ah, yes. Perhaps I wasn't exactly forthright. This grove exists to conceal the Cradle of Ilmyris, a library of … secret knowledge. The Wooded Eye are its guardians. We serve the Woodland Man. You might know him as Herma-Mora.

You impress me, stranger. I have one more task for you before I include you in the ritual.\n\nThe giant's leader prowls the hill above the village. Kill him, and the giants will submit to us. Then their power will truly be ours!
Bah, you are a fool. That is the only way to gain the power of the giants.\n\nIf you won't eat, then I have no use for you. Go!

I know a ritual that makes the meat in those sacks very special. It imbues the person that consumes it with the spirit of the animal it came from.\n\nBut to show your dedication to our cause, you must eat some of the meat before I unlock its power.

Interesting town, isn't it? It's the largest in Shadowfen, and one of the few places you'll find Dunmer architecture.\n\nLegend has it the Hist conquered the Ayleids who once lived here. Complete nonsense, but an amusing story nonetheless.
How'dya like the view?
You. I remember you. At least I think I do. Perhaps I just imagined it. That's all imagination is, you know. Memories of things that never happened.
Truly? I thought I dreamed my master offered me a place in his realm, in Apocrypha, when my service was done. But that may have been the caretaker before me.
Oh, you know how it is. A revered site, with a group of mystics and fanatics caring for a bunch of roots? We get some pretty strange types here. They're fervent, Green bless 'em. But strange.
Just the opposite! I care about the city. It's my sincere hope I live to see Falinesti return, one day. I just don't have a problem with bathing myself or wearing comfortable clothing.
And we do so with songs in our hearts. One day Falinesti will return, and we'll be rewarded for our stewardship.\n\nIt's a quiet life, normally. But we like it.
You will bind the Daedra, but you do not yet know what tendril of fate and fortune brought you into my grove, into this ruined reflection of my library.
A conundrum. The Bosmer soul escaped Ilmyris. We require a replacement. Saromir, my caretaker, satisfies all requirements.\n\nKill him and bring his soul to me.
<You remove the arrow.>
You mean, I must go to the shrine? How can I resist my master or question his wisdom? \n\nNo-no-no, I can't. I-I'm too afraid. Forgive me Woodland Man, but I can't stay here!
Madfolk, every one of them. They think … I don't know what they think. They're sure they can force Falinesti back here somehow.\n\nIndring, the leader of the cult? He's maddest of all.
Through communion with the spirit of the site. We tree-stewards have a few tricks up our sleeves. Get those samples for me, and I'll show you.
We've been friends for years. He's half-crazed, babbling about the tunnels ….\n\nI just hope they can be saved.
<Egolor's body has suffered multiple knife wounds. There is no sign of the scroll case.>
Raz will be fine. A few burns will not kill this one. But, uh, for the moment, he thinks you should press on alone. \n\nYou must catch Asteril and find out where Pelidil is hiding!
She … used some kind of magic to escape, but it was not a portal, so she cannot have gone far.\n\nShe must still be here … somewhere in these tunnels.

Negotiate? About what? Oh. I know. You want us to bow to your queen and swear allegiance to your—whats-its-called—"Aldmeri Dominion."\n\nHuh. Problem is that our allegiance is to the Wilderking, and he doesn't seem to care for your Dominion.

They're just upstairs. I know Abbot Durak will be relieved to see you. \n\nHe said to send you up right away when you returned. Whatever's going on, I hope you can help General Godrun. He's like a father to me.

Not in person, but I don't doubt the Wilderking exists. He speaks to me in the babbling brooks and the wind in the trees. \n\nOther Bosmer petition him for an audience, but I don't need to. He already tells me everything I need to know.

Tavo invested in a speculative prospecting expedition. They didn't even find enough gold to pay the diggers. We lost everything.\n\nThe Lost City was just a rumor, but we were desperate. Yombira loaned us the money, and … well, you know the rest.
Try to start over, I suppose. Life in the desert is harsh. One cannot grieve for long, or the sands will swallow them whole.\n\nI'll survive. It is the way of our people.

With these relics, I should be able to start a new life. It will be bittersweet without my beloved, but it is what he would want.\n\nLife in the desert is harsh. One cannot grieve for long, or the sands will swallow them whole.
You should not make such accusations.

Dark moons! If Asteril got away, we will have to track her down. \n\nAnd the Veiled Heritance is here …? That is troubling. Razum-dar suspected a few might have come, but he did not expect them to be here in any numbers.

Possibly. If they cannot rule the Dominion, perhaps they would destroy it by attacking Valenwood. But Raz would not have thought the Heritance could muster enough manpower …. \n\nLet us go. We must tell Treethane Fariel what we have learned.
Hm. Some of Razum-dar's contacts warned him that the Veiled Heritance was not putting all its hopes on Prince Naemon—that they had "backup plan."\n\nNaemon is dead. This must be "backup plan."
Njorlund. Boy couldn't find his own arse with a clairvoyance spell. Takes after his whoring mother. \n\nEnough talk. When you find the relics, bring them here.

My son and I were delayed on the road. A Pact scout should be here any minute to take the relics back to Stormhold. If I'm not here, he'll raise an alarm that would wake dead Ysgramor! \n\nI sent my boy to get them, but he's worthless.
I… I'm just hearing things.

A powerful enchantment forms a link between their bearer and the dreugh queen. When placed in the reliquaries and blessed, they have a calming effect upon her workers.\n\nThese relics are sacred to my people. Using them as weapons is blasphemy.
I will ignore the voices. I will ignore the voices. I will ignore the voices.

I went in and spoke with the Orc Chieftain. He agreed to give Andur and I free passage into the forest, but only after I told him about your scare tactics.\n\nI know the Orcs out here were getting spooked, but he'll order them to stay now.

Oh. Please don't say that. I really am sorry, but there's more to this, and I just didn't have a choice.\n\nLook, you can still satisfy the Treethane. You'll just have to go in and kill the Orc Chieftain—he'll attack you, so it will be self-defense.

She did? That's funny … because Andur and I offered to drive the Orcs away and she turned us down!\n\nI don't know. I'm beginning to suspect this is some elaborate Bosmer trick, and the whole village is laughing at us when we're not looking.

We'll just have to venture deeper into the forest on our own. We'll probably get lost and suffer a slow and painful death, but that's the risk we have to take.\n\nIf you're going after the Wood Orcs though, I know something that might make it easier.
He's a lying, cheating, good-for-nothing scoundrel. Worst of all, he waters down his drinks.\n\nHe and I go way back. And that's all I'll say on that matter.

The Ayleids built it on top of some ancient ruins. Then the Argonians moved in. After that, the Dunmer came, built their town on top of ours.\n\nWhen we're all dead and gone, I'm sure someone else'll build on top of all this too.

No. I used to live in Narsis, a Dunmer town north of here. We came here with a wagon full of sundries. First mistake.\n\nThe swamps aren't half as treacherous as the traders. Now we're just another pair of wanderers, looking for the next meal.
It's just business to most of them. In a place like this, you need to look out for your own tail first.\n\nIt's the friendly ones you've got to watch out for. Never trust a smile.

No, but I'm new to this branch. Seemed like a good idea at the time—living and working directly in your research area!\n\nI can't count the number of times I've tripped over some Ayleid junk on my way to my room. Annoying.

Mostly just new variations on varla stones. We think this was one of their older outposts, judging by the sheer number of underground chambers.\n\nThe unexplored ones we've sealed off, for the city's protection. But we'll get to them all, eventually.

I expect it's because it's one of the few structures here that isn't sinking into the swamp.\n\nThat and being in close proximity to an Ayleid ruin means we don't have to go far for research material.
Oh, they say it is distracting! That I can't keep close watch on our visitors if I'm running my mouth.\n\nThat's a load of rubbish! I should be questioning every person coming down these stairs.

Well, having both guilds in one place means we need to have enough security for both.\n\nPlus, last month some mage flooded the ruin with Scamps. Don't want to have that happen again. Took us weeks to get that smell out!

I take it you're not from Morrowind, then? The Pact's treaty forbids slave trade in either Nord or Argonian lots. Fine by me—slaving always left a bad taste in my mouth.\n\nMaybe one day there won't be a market for slaves at all!

There's always a market for free labor. Morrowind's slavers just have to range farther to get their goods. Bretons and Khajiit are always popular.\n\nIt's a bit barbaric, if you ask me. But, I don't question the laws of the Pact!

Uh, no. Well, it depends.\n\nI try to treat everyone fairly—a coin's a coin, after all! But some Dunmer still look down on Argonians, and plenty of Argonians don't trust us. For good reason, I suppose. It's a shame.

Well, I didn't follow the politics of it. The Akaviri were invading Morrowind, and we needed all the help we could get.\n\nSo the Argonians and Nords fought on our side, and we won. What better motivation than freedom?

I'll tell you what everyone knows. They come in the night and take newborns—any that are born under the sign of Sithis. Then the children are reared to love killing and obey orders.\n\nLittle more than another kind of slavery.

That's a tough question. Some say he's just another Daedric Prince. Others call him a force of nature, something inseparable from our world. The Void, Lord of Nothingness.\n\nMakes me shiver saying it out loud.

No one's sure. Anyone can petition for a contract, but it's up to the Shadowscales to fulfill it or not. How or who decides, no one knows.\n\nMakes me afraid to leave my house. I could step on someone's tail and be dead the next day!
Yes. The mistress asked me to clean. She promised me many treats if her home is spotless when she returns.\n\nMany, many treats.
What? Why? Did she … are you trying to gain the favor of my mistress?\n\nI see! This is a test. No, I must finish my work.

Of course. Why would I not be all right? My mistress returns soon, and she will be delighted. Then we will have many treats together, and all will be right again.\n\nAs soon as I get this last spot done.
This is the last spot. Last stubborn spot, and I will clean it.\n\nThe mistress wants it so. Then it will be so.
She is my mistress. A beautiful Dunmer woman, made with the grace of a hundred bowing reeds. Her voice is like warm rays of sun. Her touch like the wind's caress.\n\nYes. She is my mistress.
Perhaps we will. You have certainly proven resourceful in the past.\n\nEven if you escape Quagmire, mortal, you will not escape my vengeance. I can be patient, very patient. Goodbye … for now.
Whoa, whoa! They just pay me to look tough. Think I'd be dumb enough to tangle with you?\n\nBesides, this place was getting on my nerves. I'll never scrub the smell out of my armor.
How you going to do that from the bottom of the swamp?
It's not like that! The Argonians don't pay us a cut, is all.\n\nBut maybe the other side of town could use a patrol, right?
I don't bully innocent folk. Not for the pittance I'm paid.\n\nBut you're right. This isn't what I signed up for.
Are you serious? Well, you'd have to buy out my contract. You got that kind of coin on you?
How about that. My third fight of the day with a milk-drinking fool.
Looks like you can see the future.
Absolutely. Khali would make a far better Mane. Her strength and resolve would serve her well. Shazah is well acquainted with the darkness of the Dro-m'Athra. She knows what must be done.
Glad we speak the same language.\n\nDamn! Should've asked for more.

I can do this. This is my responsibility. Take Khali and leave this place. Hallowed, she should be the next Mane. I am just a scribe who was born on a particular day, at a particular time. I do not deserve to be Mane.
Yes, Hallowed. Shazah is brilliant and talented. But I do not think she can physically take the strain of holding this darkness within her. I have the strength and the will to take on this burden.

Yes! Shazah is much better suited to lead our people. She has studied so long and so hard. She knows much of the Bright Moons and is much better at dealing with people. She should lead. And I should stay.

We officially hold allegiance to no one. But we're Argonians, and if the Dominion steals treasures from our land to establish a seat of power, we must stop them.\n\nThough … we're somewhat out of our element here.
Slowly. I returned to Wayrest to request additional supplies and men from the King, but it appears things aren't entirely peaceful at home.
So I'm stuck until resources free up. That, or I go back to Aldcroft with my helmet in my hand.

Intruders! Greedy for power. Broke the wards and attacked my fellow priests. I can't defend against the coming Daedric invasion alone. \n\nI need your help restoring the wardstones while I complete the warding spell, or Daedra will overrun this place.

Indeed. The Dominion is searching for an Ayleid artifact, the Relleis Lor keystone.  <<1>> believes it's too powerful to fall into their hands.\n\nThe citizens of Murkwater that weren't killed in the invasion are being forced to excavate for it.
I would be lying if I told you I didn't have the occasional urge to howl at the moon, but nocturnal indescretions aside I feel quite good considering my former "affliction."
Take this whistle. Our first priority is to save Murkwater's people.\n\nWhen you locate them, use the whistle to signal my agents. They'll take care of the rest.
The Dominion took particular interest in a local scholar named <<1>>. She was spotted, accompanied by two guards, headed to the eastern Ayleid ruins.\n\nI believe <<1>> can lead us to the keystone.
We have come to request the aid of the High King. Camlorn is recovering slowly, but our forces are much depleted after the siege of the city. I don't have to tell you that, surely.

Yes. A Daedric Prince. But the only reason the Daedra are bound here is to keep this place hidden. Ordinarily, they pose no threat.\n\nThey broke their bonds when the intruders destroyed the wards, and now they threaten all of Greenshade!

We're waiting for King Jorunn and his troops to arrive, but Fildgor has his own agenda. He's moving fast and I don't think the army is going to show up in time.\n\nBut I've got a few ideas on how to slow him down.

Light the signal fire. That's the sign the King's troops are waiting for before they make their final push up the mountain.\n\nThat said, I still don't think they'll make it in time. You need to reach Fildgor and slow him down. Good luck.
I am Gordhaur the Shaper, the Fire King Hadhuul, Haromir of Copper and Tea, the Flower King Nilichi, Umaril the Unfeathered. Or I am just Saromir. It's becoming hard to know.
This one has seen nothing. But you might want to ask the Argonian, Many-Eyes. She works for the Fixer; she sees much and knows more.
I mind my own business, mouse. Perhaps you should as well.

Hah! Fine, you're no mouse! No need to show your teeth. I didn't see anyone leave the place, but Many-Eyes was hanging around there earlier. You might want to talk to her. She's usually near the arena.
I could tell you, but I have forgotten how. Or perhaps I never knew. \n\nListen: the Woodland Man calls you. In the pool. It's best if you do not look directly. It looks back, you know.
I don't know, stranger. It's been a long day. I might have seen something, but it's so hard to recall ….

You're going to stick your nose into this no matter what I say, aren't you? Fine.\n\nThod decided to have a drink with the Prince's entourage last night. Haven't seen him since. Probably passed out somewhere, but I can't be too careful right now.
You know, come to think of it, I do remember something. Many-Eyes, the Argonian that works for the Fixer? I saw her coming from down that way. You can find her by the arena, just behind me.
I don't believe I know you. Why should I tell you anything?
Why didn't you just say so? I saw Many-Eyes over near the Wood Elf hut. You should ask her. You can find her over by the arena. She's an Argonian. Can't miss her.
Thank you. Seeing a friendly face has renewed my strength.
Thank the gods they weren't overwhelmed. I'll go at once.
Others? You've no idea how thankful I am to hear that. I feared I'd be all that's left.
The Ayleids kept the keystones separated. One was hidden in Relleis Lor, the ruins you see around Murkwater.\n\nThe Dominion must have learned this and sent a force to recover it.
This name is familiar to me. I might know something, yes. But knowledge must be paid for. I'm going to need something from you before I tell you anything about his death.
You can't see the work we do from the shadows. However, this operation would be doomed if it weren't for you ….\n\nAsk <<1>> to lend you one of her agents.
It's simple enough. You go speak to the people that owe me money. You find them and … remind them that they owe me. Don't kill anyone. Dead men don't pay debts. Then I'll tell you what I know.

All right, all right. Don't be so hasty. I need my scales intact, thanks.\n\nI saw a Colovian woman leave Egolor's hut. She wiped her bloody knife on her tunic as she left. And she was carrying a scroll case.

She tried to sell me the case, but she wouldn't tell me what was inside. I didn't pay her what she wanted for it. She said she knew someone who'd offer a better price. Some zealots in camp near Dune. The Stonefire Cult, maybe?

That works, of course. Consider this your good deed for the day. Heh. I saw a Colovian woman leave Egolor's hut. She wiped her bloody knife on her tunic as she left, and she was carrying a scroll case.
<The dead soldier's unit markings match those of <<1>>. His skin is slightly charred, like other victims of the skin-stealers.>
<As you search his body, you find a small, cracked vial. It shatters, spilling its contents on your skin.>
I don't have the money. Do your worst, ruffian.
I'm young and have much to learn, but my connection to Black Marsh, to all Argonians, helps me.\n\nThe more I research, the more control I gain over my power.
The thought of the Dominion walking all over my people makes me sick.\n\nIf there is killing to be done, count me in.

We prepared to assault the cave when the soldier beside me stabbed me in the back. When I fell, I saw my own regiment attack itself.\n\nThose skin-stealers wore our friends' faces to betray us from within! Do you think that they have my face now?
I saw them take <<1>> alive. Knocked him out, dragged him away to that altar like a piece of meat.\n\nDon't let them steal his face!
Where Pale-Heart goes, I follow. She and I are clutch-mates, hatched at the same time, and trained together from our youth.\n\nWe share an unbreakable bond.
Though I'm an assassin, I care for the people of Black Marsh. Shadowscales are quite misunderstood.\n\nOur work is subtle, and always guided by faith.

We hunt the Dark Mane, who has taken root deep within Moonmont. His legions have boiled up from below, killed most of the monks.\n\nAnd the beacons that mark the site as holy ground are grown dark. They fuel a ward lock upon the temple door.

That crazy Elf! She tried to cut my chest, but I kicked her off the altar. Said she'd be back with a duller knife, so it would last longer.\n\nWait, I smell her. Cut me loose! Don't let her steal my face!
The beacons are marked by large pillars around the temple. We'll need to cleanse the beacons, and restore the site. \n\nOnly then will we be able to crack the ward and go below.
<<<1>>'s gaze continues to focus on something you can't quite see.>
I thought no one would come for us.\n\nI've searched many years for the keystone, and had a breakthrough before the Dominion arrived. I tried to mislead them, but they found my notes.
It should be in one of the chests we unearthed. Be careful as you open them. An ancient evil guards the keystone.
Find the keystone first, and worry about me second. Who knows when Dominion reinforcements will show up?

Listen, I saw them both just a moment ago. And unlike the Commander, I slept last night.\n\nNow it's not that I don't believe you found a drunk Nord by the river—it wouldn't be the first time—it's just that it can't be Thod. I can prove it.

Well, here I am. A troll tried to eat me and a spriggan chased after me. By Y'ffre, those things give me the creeps.\n\nI was looking for Jafelma, but instead I found a couple of woodcutters hiding in here. So I decided to join them.
Very good. <<1>> will be pleased.\n\nAre you ready to take back the town from those Dominion scum?

One of the woodcutters saw her helping a logger near the other cabin. I was thinking of going to look for her, but then I thought about those creepy walking bushes and decided to stay right here.\n\nI'm a clerk! I didn't volunteer for this!

We've learned that the Dominion brought a large shipment of crystallized fire salts. These salts are highly flammable. \n\nWe want you to assault their ship, collect the fire salts and then spread them around the river.
If that's not enough, why not kill their leaders? <<1>> and <<2>> command the Dominion forces from the ship.\n\nNow is our best chance to create confusion among their ranks.

My friends and I are monster hunters. We specialize in killing unnatural creatures. Werewolves, Daedra, and so on. We prefer operating in out-of-the way locations. Spindleclutch is close to Daggerfall, while offering us the privacy we need.

The Shadowscales are going to systematically kill every Dominion soldier we can get our hands on once the river is on fire. \n\nWe are currently studying their troop movements and getting our agents into position.
What's to say? He's a good leader, a good soldier, and a protective father. More than that, he'd have to tell you.
Ага.
You should have the honor of lighting the fire, after all you've done for us.\n\nI've stacked up a pile of wood, light the remaining fire salts and set everything ablaze.
Kill them first.
Don't tell me Lord Fancy-Pants actually left his cozy office in Windhelm. He hasn't been in a real forest in years!\n\nAt least he made the trip. That's more than most bosses would do.

I think that this part of the forest belongs to a spriggan matron. At least, she's certainly treating the place like it's hers. \n\nShe sent the forest trolls and lesser spriggans to harass us and drive us off.

Well, I think we offended the forest spirits. I know it sounds strange. But the forests of Skyrim are ancient and magical. And not everything likes to be disturbed.\n\nI think Thulvald bought land that … had a prior claim attached to it.
I've been travelling all over since. I hopped a boat to Stormhaven not too long after we parted ways.\n\nI heard they might have coin and need of a strong arm here. Sadly they are lacking the former.
I'm not entirely sure yet, but East I think.

I could, I suppose, but I am planning to move on soon, and I know you. Danger won't have root here long now that you've arrived, and as I mentioned, there isn't much treasure to go around on this one.
Hah! I've more or less given it up unless you count chasing after Darien when he goes on a tear.
That's right, you see. Darien needs a babysitter more than a wife. I have no desire to embrace him in either way. \n\nStill, every day is a new adventure.
What? No! No.\n\nWhat would give you that idea? Darien's about as faithful as a bred stud, only he doesn't have the looks.
I had heard the Knight of the Flame might be interested in new applicants, but there seems to be a bit of turmoil in their order currently.
I don't know, actually. I did read an interesting posting about an archaelogical expedition to Alik'r yesterday. \n\nIt sounds like it could be safe work.
Slavery, border raids, and in-fighting have them primed for chaos. They just need a little … push. \n\nI've written meself a part, a small but pivotal role. If you'll excuse me ….
I was a fool! I brought my wife and child to this tomb, looking for shelter from the storm. I lost everything. Everything!

I'm not just the best-looking scout in Shadowfen, I'm also the best tracker. I can pick up <<1>>'s scent and lead us right to him.\n\nI'll need someone to watch my back while I follow my nose. We should work in pairs with skin-stealers about, yes?
Portals have opened across Dune, allowed Daedra into the streets. I saved Esan here from being an ice sculpture, and in return he's proposed a bold plan. One I think may give us the upper hand.

The one you seek has gone to meet with a group of Stonefire Cultists at a camp near Dune. She's a Colovian named Elissa Belenus. I saw her leave Egelor's hut with a bloody knife in one hand and the case in the other.
Maybe. Hrondar sent me to this festering sewer to get Argonian relics. Something about turning the tide of the war.\n\nThe Dominion's likely here for the same reason.

<Though recently dragged here, the body is cold and decaying, as if dead for much longer than the others. His corpse is conspicuously absent of signs of battle.>\n\n<You notice a small hole on his chest, as well as a slight charring to his skin.>
You want to help? Bring me the relics! We can't let the Dominion get their hands on them.\n\nTake care of this for me, and you'll be rewarded from Vicecanon Hrondar's own purse.
Good. You'll find them in the small reliquaries scattered around the area.\n\nIf you see my lackwit son Njorlund in the bog, tell him to get back to camp. Once we have the relics, we'll be moving on.
If the vicecanon was dead this whole time … was it a … a skin-stealer who … who launched the attack on the cave? Or before that, when we lost the other vicecanons?

You have nothing to fear. Your smell will be sun-blessed to their senses, and the Dominion dryskins will smell like prey. The most delicious freshwater trout. \n\nGo quickly, before Saervild flees with the relics!

Jafelma comes from this part of the forest. Knows it like the back of her hand. I figured she'd be able to deal with the ghost stories.\n\nBut trolls! How does anyone deal with a herd of trolls? There's so many of them!
Know that great lightning feeds the wamasu well, but many reeds burn in its wake. Without reeds, the guar cannot feed. Without guar, the wamasu starve.\n\nBe careful what is seared by your lightning.
Eginir went to check on the logging cabin. He's a Wood Elf, so I figured he'd be able to deal with strange forest activity.\n\nBut he hasn't come back yet and now I'm concerned about him.

Jafelma's reports stopped arriving several days ago. So I left my office in Windhelm and came out to investigate.\n\nThe few woodcutters we did find said that the trolls began arriving in dribs and drabs, followed by the spriggans.
You could be of great help.\n\nThere may be a way to see into the recent past; watch those who performed the dark rituals as they creep about the island.

Of course he did. And did he tell you that my special Bosmer senses could figure out what's going on out here? Well, he lied about that, too!\n\nThe Nords claim there are forest spirits. Maybe one of the woodcutters chopped down the wrong tree.

There is a totem by the bridge to the south. Using this will show you a shimmering echo of where someone was. Like their ghost. Find and follow any apparition that appears.\n\nI pray you are successful in this hunt.

Laugh if you will, but these forests hold many secrets.\n\nThulvald probably got this land for a steal. Certainly, our presence here seems to have offended something. I'll try to lead my workers out of here, but that spriggan needs to die.
Here. When you feel the poison's fire in your veins, challenge any warrior to single combat. Go, prove yourself ready for the Hist!

You mean things happen beyond the walls of our wonderful city of Windhelm?\n\nAs it happens, I was just talking to a trader who stopped by for a drink. The traders always tell the most interesting stories.
The Commander is occupied by other matters at the moment. As one of the officials helping coordinate efforts at Fort Amol, perhaps I could be of service?

Oh, the usual. He was going on and on about an ice-bound cave called Chill Hollow, ill-fated treasure hunters, and lost love.\n\nAll the old caves and ruins have their stories, I suppose. Me, I prefer life here in the city.
My cousin and his family ran into a bit of trouble. Money trouble. He came up with a plan to earn some gold and clear his debts.

When the plan to save your family from debt involves sneaking through old ruins like Icehammer's Vault in hope of finding treasure, then yes. I have concerns. \n\nMy cousin is a clever sort, but old tombs are dangerous places.

I am a noble and an advisor to the Jarl of Fort Amol. I have been charged with making sure that all of our esteemed guests are well cared for.\n\nI assume you are part of King Jorunn's guard if you seek to speak with Commander Yjarnn.

Ah, yes, Thod. Of course. He was just here, as a matter of fact. You just missed him.\n\nYou weren't the one looking for him earlier by chance? Yjarnn mentioned someone looking into guard business. Not many folks care about Thod.
Just a bit here and there. I'm looking for two artifacts in Blackheart's collection. If, by your graces, I can have those, I'll leave everything else to you.

Have you ever seen the dead walk? I have. And I wish I hadn't. It's chilling. Gets in your head and doesn't let go.\n\nBut I thought the legends were nonsense. Thought I could walk right in and make a fortune. Damn Stormcrag family!
They are to me. But we're getting ahead of ourselves. We're not even inside, yet.
In the basket next to me is a uniform worn by Blackheart's minions. \n\nPut it on, and you'll be as hard to spot as a spriggan in a tree.

The Stormcrags! An old Nord family with a lot of old Nord gold. They built a fancy crypt to keep their dead relatives in.\n\nLegends say there's treasure inside. And I can certainly vouch for the dead that roam the chambers like they own the place.

Ha ha ha! Not hardly. There are so many that they can't tell each other apart. \n\nThe Sea Hounds, however, have noses keener than a man's eyes. They'll sniff you out and alert their masters, so avoid them if you can.

Well, how about I help you instead?\n\nYjarnn has been on edge of late. Perhaps the King's presence makes him nervous. Or it's all these foreigners. Who knows? But he has been acting strange. I'd keep an eye on him if I were you.
Yes. Well, no. There's also a brute named Iron-Heel who guards the inner haven. \n\nHe has a small army with him, and he'll step on your face if you're not careful. With his big feet.

I love your enthusiasm, but I have my own way in. \n\nOh, and be wary of the pirates in the caves above. They're Blackheart's elite, his most trusted crew, and you'll find that they have … a different disposition than the seadogs out here.

You seem eager to help, so I'm giving you something to do. If I toss around false accusations or involve the King's guards, it might seem like Fort Amol can't deal with its own problems.\n\nTrail the Commander. Determine if my fears are justified.

Yes, you marvelous fool. I allowed them to pull me from Oblivion, bind my essence, and siphon my power because I'm secretly behind their shabby little plans.\n\nOh, but you don't know about those, do you?
You've heard of <<1>>, the celebrated Dominion alchemist? It's all his doing, you know.\n\nI'll tell you his plans for your impending doom. For a small favor, of course.
Zaht stones …. The Hist may be showing you a way to defend Hissmir against some future threat, but I have not heard of Hist amber in an age.\n\nYou should speak with <<1>>. If anyone knows, he will.
Gone. Whatever the Hist showed him, he was in a hurry to act. Perhaps his people are threatened as well?

Necromancers, practitioners of the most vile magic, and the bane of the Alik'r Desert.\n\nIt has been many years since we faced such a threat. I hoped the rumors about this group—the Withered Hand—were untrue, but today's events prove otherwise.

Several years ago, a diabolical necromancer named Suturah led an army of undead against me.\n\nSuturah was defeated, but the rumors suggest his sons have returned for revenge. They are calling themselves the Withered Hand.

We each think the other vicecanons are incompetent. Ha! No, it's politics, plain and simple. The one who stays behind looks out of touch, so off we came to the muck. \n\nPolitics be damned. Next time we draw straws for staying dry in Stormhold.
When the Dominion ambushed us, they made a deliberate effort to split our forces. If Heita-Meen and Servyna have any sense on the battlefield, they'd recognize that and stay together.

Why does anyone invade anywhere? Those pristine towers of theirs must get boring. Maybe a good brawl in the mud beats chasing their cousins for kisses.\n\nTruth is, I don't care why. I care to get them out.
Fruit of the Hist. Its magic once powered the Zaht stones, protecting us from our enemies all those years ago … but the Hist haven't borne fruit in an age. Why do you ask?

Toward the western ruins. If you find any Hist amber, keep it from <<1>>'s hands and return it as swiftly as you can. Should the Dominion plan to capture <<2>> for themselves, I must prepare a defense.

Oh, no. <<1>> also asked about the Hist amber. Then he left here in great haste.\n\nIf he possesses any amber, he could use the Zaht stones upon the Root Stewards, the pilgrims … everyone in Hissmir! Why would the Hist show him this vision?

Let's make a deal. Ferals overran one of our camps. The survivors of that attack need patching up, but the <<z:1>> are still in the camp.\n\nIf you can recover those supplies, one of my people will tell you where the keystone is.
Oh, sorry. There's a lot going on. Did you happen to find him?
More than willing. It's been too long since I crushed an outsider's face.
I don't even like Garnikh, but I'll duel you just for fun.
My daggers are always willing to teach a lesson.

Damn. The poor bastard. I told them … I told the guards that they were going to have to fight back.  \n\nIt is one thing to be superstitious, but when the Ra-Netu are attacking the city? It's time to put the superstitions aside.

No. We're not all so hung up on our beliefs. Can't ignore the tradition though … not unless we want fruit thrown at us, or worse.\n\nRegardless, right now I'm just glad Tava's winds guided you here—someone to get the Ra-Netu off the damn docks!

I do. I overheard the necromancers. Their leader is calling the dead from the sea with some kind of dark ritual.\n\nIf you can disrupt the ritual, the dead should … well, they should drop dead, or at least stop crawling out of the water.

Ah, that is the challenge I now face. The people of the Alik'r Desert, even those in Sentinel, are superstitious. They believe that striking the dead carries a terrible curse. For them, it is an act of dishonor.\n\nThat is why I need you, wayfarer.

Then your visit is fortuitous indeed. My own son—Prince Azah—has been investigating the rumors about the Withered Hand. He is a bright young man, but he needs help. \n\nFirst though, I would ask you to inform General Thoda of what has befallen.

You have to look at this from my point of view.\n\nA stranger walks into town and makes outlandish claims about spies and imposters and murders. How do I know that you're not one of these Stormfist traitors trying to cause trouble?

It's quite a tale, and I cannot do it justice now, but the battle against Suturah was the most difficult of my life—both in military and political terms.\n\nIt was the Ash'abah who saved us. They had the thankless task of fighting the undead.

Like you, I am escaping this place. But, since I have been here for some time, the Tall One asked me to help the newer prisoners find their way. \n\nThose who are captured will be flayed. Sadly, that will not end their torment. Soul Shriven cannot die.
No need. The loss of your dignity will be my reward.

We are the vestiges of people whose souls were stolen by … the God of Schemes. I dare not utter his true name in this place.\n\nThe Soul Shriven are doomed to slavery in Coldharbour for eternity, or at least until we are no longer useful.

Oh yes. The lesser Daedra actually fear them. Ferals have no fear of pain or death, because that is all they know. That, and eternal hunger.\n\nThey will attack and eat anything they can get their claws on, even each other.

The longer we remain here, the less … whole we remain. Our bodies waste away, our skin shrivels, and eventually our minds twist and lose any notion of reality.\n\nThe oldest of the Soul Shriven are completely insane. We call them Ferals.

You certainly are insistent, I'll grant you that much.\n\nLook, I'll check the house as soon as I can. In the meantime, go talk to Lord Vurlop. Shor's Bones, if there really are spies in Fort Amol, His Lordship will know what to do.
And miss you embarrassing Garnikh and "his" hunters? Not a chance!
He's even more close-minded than most males. It's a wonder any of them live to adulthood.
What? No. I never imagined ….\n\nI think you better tell me what happened, friend. And start at the beginning.
I wouldn't. He's strong enough to challenge Tazgol for leadership of the clan. If he succeeds, you'll want to be on his good side.

I'll need to have a word with Hloenor. The implications for the Pact are horrifying. Dark Elves and Nords have died—finger-pointing will escalate into violence as soon as word gets out.\n\nEspecially with Prince Irnskar's temper.
Lower your voice!\n\nThis can't be. How could Fildgor's soldiers get into the fort without being noticed? Did you tell anyone else about this?

Go to the Nord camp and speak with Thane Harvald. He's honorable and intelligent. I'm sure he'll want to keep this quiet.\n\nHe also possesses common sense. If anyone knows how we should approach this problem, it's Thane Harvald.
I'll come with you, if it means our release. Just don't expect me to fight.\n\nFriendly advice? If you have to shut an iron gate, keep your fingers away from the bars.

Over time, all the prisoners bound to the keystone lose their minds. They become feral. Please, don't leave us to that fate.\n\nThe prison warden had a book about the keystones. They knew, and they still did this to us!

I've had worse. If we had more time, I'd show you some of my more interesting scars.\n\nAnyway, thanks for helping us. Thulvald isn't a bad man, but like a lot of Nords, he's lost touch with the land. It's kind of sad, if you think about it.

When we lose our connection to the land, we forget the spirits that live there. I'm not just talking about ruins full of ghosts and draugr.\n\nPeople forget that dark woods and ancient caves hold secrets. And forgetting such things can be dangerous.
How does anyone wind up anywhere? I wanted to see the world!\n\nEveryone thinks that Bosmer just want to hide in trees and shoot bows and giggle like children. Well, some of us want more than that.

Sorry, but I'm still a bit rattled by all this troll and spriggan business.\n\nAnyway, I have a way with numbers, so Thulvald hired me as his clerk. Believe me, the last thing I wanted to do was dodge trolls in the forests of Skyrim.
That … I'd rather not talk about.
Undoubtedly, but I suspect the attack at the docks is merely a feint. \n\nThough cleaning up that mess should remain our first priority, I suspect the Withered Hand is planning something even worse.
Yes. The greatest threat the Alik'r faced from the undead was in the First Era, when the Yokudan rulers were still establishing a foothold here.\n\nThat was when the Ansei Wards were created.

It is not an ancient Yokudan custom, but a tradition that developed in the desert. \n\nHuman remains decay slowly here, and our people came to believe their ancestors' corpses were sacred. To harm one would draw the ancestors' curse.

Zombies? Such a crude term! These Ra-Netu are the remains of sailors who shipwrecked off the coast! \n\nWe respect our dead here in the Alik'r desert! Even those who died at sea are honored ancestors. We do not fight them—we would be cursed!

No. You are an outsider. These are not your ancestors, and as such there is no dishonor in striking them down, no curse.\n\nBut the fact that the dead have risen at all … it is terrible. We have strict laws … this should not happen here!

I have not called on them. I have even disregarded their warnings. \n\nYou must understand—the common people despise them. To call on them again might cost me the crown. That is why I must rely on you, wayfarer.

The Ash'abah. Where do I begin? They walk among us, but only in shadows. People believe they are cursed.\n\nThey are dishonored warriors, bound by the sacred oath of their forefathers. They must fight the dead when called upon to do so.
Who else would I be, mortal? Recent events have called me back from Sovngarde, but I am still my people's beloved queen.\n\nNow don't you have some relics to put back in the tomb?

I can't keep secrets from my Prince, no matter how hot-headed he may be. I'll make him understand the seriousness of the situation.\n\nBut I doubt the Argonians and Dark Elves will listen. They were very angry when they marched back to their camps.
And that's not what I wanted to hear.\n\nThe Prince will have to be told about this, of course. And the Argonian and Dark Elf delegates. They need to be able to protect themselves.
I'll wait inside! I won't stick around to be captured by the Renrijra.\n\nIf you're smart, you'll follow me. Looks can catch up to us.

Perhaps, if you say that King Jorunn sent you. They might not forgive the Prince and return immediately, but they might listen to you.\n\nThey need to know that we value the Pact and their companionship. Do whatever it takes to make them happy.

What does he always do? He opened his mouth and let words fall out. He said many terrible things and drove them away.\n\nAnd all his father asked him to do was coordinate troop movements and battle plans while the council of war was in session.
No! You realize what this means? Not one moment of relaxation! Not one!\n\nAnd damn it, I thought this talk about the Withered Hand was just rumor. Are you sure this is true?
Well, you found me. Tell Grigerda I'm fine. But I'm not going to hide in the manor or church while these monsters roam our streets. I'm staying out here until they're gone … or I am.
The Sentinel Docks? The nerve! \n\nBut it sounds like something those motherless dogs would do. I tell you, Uwafa and Alasan might just be more dangerous than their father.
That's why I'm out here. I've had enough of her yelling to last me a lifetime. I'd rather face these monsters than spend ten more minutes listening to her.
I can walk if you get me free of these bonds.

Uwafa and Alasan are the sons of that old bastard Suturah. They're calling themselves the Withered Hand as a fear tactic.\n\nI knew them when they were boys. They're the same age as Prince Azah … speaking of whom, we should inform him as well.

Exactly. He knows more about this business than I do. That's for sure.\n\nIf you'll go round up the prince … I'll have to find some way to explain to my wife why I'm leaving again … then we can all meet at the palace.

We all do. Suturah was one of the king's viziers—kept his little hobby a secret.\n\nThen one day, the king came to meet his viziers and found them all dead. The real surprise was when Suturah ordered their corpses to attack. That's how it started.
Don't worry about Eiraki. My sweet little sister will always have a place in my heart. Or should I say, in my stomach!

I tried to train them in swordplay … Uwafa and Alasan, along with Prince Azah.\n\nThose two had no interest though. I would always catch them torturing insects and animals. The Prince—he hated them, and they hated him right back.
Only a little ways ahead. We will be waiting for you.

King Jorunn is guarded by a squad of soldiers he selected personally. I'm sure everything is fine. Still, we can't be too careful, but I don't want to embarrass the King needlessly. You and Lord Vurlop can handle this. I have faith in you.

Skorvild? Well, my brother is a respected leader in our community and a great supporter of the Skald-King.\n\nHe can be a little intense, though, and some people find that a bit disturbing. But he loves Lower Yorgrim and wants to set things right.
Perhaps.\n\nBut we can think of nothing while our kingdom lies in ruins. We slowly comprehend what a boar must feel while trussed up and awaiting a feast.

No. Yet another way in which I failed! I should have followed them out into the street … I'm such a fool!\n\nMaybe someone else out there saw them—maybe they can tell you which way those men took the prince ….

You are powerful, my friend. But Shazah has long experience dealing with the dark energies here. She must be the one to dispel them.\n\nBesides, the ritual will no doubt draw attention. You must protect Shazah as she works.
<This coffer is empty.>

That was my journal! You're a clever one, aren't you? Good, my partner <<1>> and I could use some help. I'm going to have to trust you, but you need to trust me, too.\n\nGive the puzzle stones to me. I can use them to find what we seek.

Just as I thought. Combined, the stones become a single object: a Hist key! \n\nMy partner, <<1>> found what looks like an entrance into the ruins below, but it's magically sealed. I think this will open the door.
Ancient relics, the creations of my ancestors.
Ancient relics, the creations of my ancestors.

King Jorunn is a good man. Strong and wise. I hear he hates cats. He gave shelter to my people when they fled from the Stormfists and their Orc allies. \n\nBut that doesn't change the current situation. And Prince Irnskar is still a guar-licker.
Even now, our subjects petition us for succor.\n\nThey wail day and night. We hear their pleas, and even now they call to us.

The invaders bind our subjects with foul magics. They hold <<1>>, <<2>>, and <<3>> in our lowlands.\n\nWhen mages bind the helpless, they keep a <<4>> at hand. Find one of these scrolls and free our bound subjects!
A good king listens to his people.\n\nWe hear their pleas, day and night. Even now, they speak to us. We find it curious you cannot also hear their cries.

Of course. If you were not raised here, you would not know. \n\nThe Ansei Wards were created centuries ago, the first time necromancers threatened the people of the Alik'r. They were created to protect us from the risen dead.

Or perhaps the protections are not so evident.\n\nThe Ansei Wards maintain our covenant with Tu'whacca. If we consecrate our dead, those dead cannot be raised. Thus, the Withered Hand can raise only unconsecrated corpses.
