It would be unthinkable. With the Ansei Wards, the Withered Hand could raise our most honored ancestors—legendary warriors who were heroes in life, but would be most terrible enemies in death.  \n\nThat is why they must be stopped.

Our priests perform the consecration ritual at funerals, but if the corpse is lost, this is not possible.\n\nAdditionally, Suturah was also fond of murdering people and raising them right away. I assume the Withered Hand is doing the same.
<This coffer contains nothing but dried mud.>

Let me think. No, nothing comes to mind.\n\nThe Dunmer are finished helping those who show no respect or gratitude. Now if you'll excuse me, I'm trying to stay warm. Feel free to talk to my servant Naryu if you need something more.

I can take guards to the Impervious Vault, but we're going to need help … from the Mages Guild.\n\nAs much as I hate to admit it, only they know how to unseal the vault. Will you go to the guild for me, wayfarer?
<There is nothing but a little slime in the bottom of this coffer.>
<The coffer is quite empty.>

I want a bottle of wine from the barracks. That's where they keep the jarl's personal stock. I'm tired of drinking this cheap piss they provided us with.\n\nJust watch out. The place is off limits and the guards tend to deal harshly with intruders.
This looks familiar. Looks drew something in one of his journals like this.\n\nWhat is it?

Of course! I remember some of that old lizard's notes. This key won't just let us inside the xanmeer, once we're inside, it'll protect us from the traps and the xanmeer's guardians.\n\nWe can't wait any longer!

It is said that wielding the Fangs gives you to Sithis, which casts all you are, and all you could be, into a great void.\n\nYou see, the Fangs consume the bearer's soul. They bestow you with great power, but strip away all that makes you a person.

Perhaps. My ancestors created the traps so that their descendents could bypass them. If you encounter a trap, the solution should be somewhere nearby.\n\nThere's no protection from the guardians beyond the Hist key, unfortunately.

Everything is a sign! The way a shadow falls, the taste of food, the smell of decay …. Signs, if one can decipher them.\n\nTake the ruins across the water. Once, they dominated the landscape, but now they're broken bits of rock. It's a sign.

Well, let's see … I make my business at the arena dealing in debts and wagers. There are several people at the arena that owe me coin. If you'd be willing to talk to them? Heh, or perhaps you'd just clear their debts outright. Then we could talk.

I've never been inside, but its energy flows through the rocks. It hums, like a wasp. To me, that's a sign I should stay out. To others, it could be a sign of welcome.\n\nThat's the thing with signs. Everyone is free to interpret them their own way.

To get Gelds nice and comfortable. Then I'll convince him that what he just drank was poisoned. Lucky for him, I have the antidote. Of course.\n\nHe'll do whatever I want to get it, and that should be very entertaining.
Spirits? Nonsense!\n\nCome, we'll show you. Our subjects await a royal declaration at the castle tower. It's not every day you'll have the honor of escorting a king through his dominion!
I found two doors in here, but they're both locked tight. I'm sure the King is behind one of those doors.\n\nWe just need to figure out how to open them.
And you shall have it, according to prophecy. "The king in his tower declaims the keystone's hour." Have no fear, your king shall be the vessel of your deliverance!
As certain as we can be when it comes to prophecy. But we will do all in our power to ensure it comes to pass.

Hah! That'd be a lifetime's work! More than a lifetime's!\n\nI used to travel the fens a lot before I settled in Hissmir. At least the Ayleids don't bother with this place, like they do other old stones.

So have you! I can smell them on you. Musty. Ancient. It clings to anyone who's seen them.\n\nGandranen, now, there's an evil place. The Ayleids, dead for so long, walk there. Or so its said. I'll stick to Hissmir, thank you very much.
Yes, of course! Please, help me!\n\nLook, I'm sure you don't mean it. There's no help for him. My brother, that is. I don't expect to see him again, and … why am I even telling you this?

Maybe. Well, there's no harm in telling you. He's dead in that stupid kwama mine off <<1>>. I told him they had no idea what they were doing!\n\nI won't discuss any details, but let's just say none of those miners will come back.

He's enjoying a gift from Fildgor. The King that saved his people from the Akaviri, killed by his own brother. Yet no one will ever know. No, they will find the body of poor Dhalen the Breton, defeated by their heroic king!\n\nOh, that would be me.
Well, I couldn't let you have all the fun!\n\nSeriously, you have to understand. My organization used to be respected. Now we're hunted for what we were. What we represented. That has to change.

Lob and his champions must fight you in the prescribed order. They can't attack you all at once. They have to play by the rules and challenge you in waves.\n\nYou'll be able to handle that. I have faith in you.
Then I'll shadow you, and alert you when I pick up <<1>>'s scent.\n\nReady when you're ready!
She tried to sell me the case. She wouldn't tell me what was inside, though, so I wasn't willing to hit the price she was after. Now then. If we're done …?
How do you think I make a living? I buy there, sell here. It's what I do. All legitimate, of course.\n\nPicked up a load of timber in Wayrest—it'll sell for a pile of coin here. It better.
<<1>> always smelled of mead. I didn't … I should have ….\n\nXuth! What secrets do the Dominion already know?

The Fangs are our birthright! They are dangerous, yes, but the Night Mother will shield us from the worst of their influence.\n\nAnd if they overwhelm me, the other Shadowscales won't hesitate to send me back to the Hist.
<<1>> of the Shadowscales. The Fangs of Sithis must not fall into the hands of the ignorant.\n\nHand them over or face the Night Mother's wrath!

You learn by doing, of course! Gather materals and start experimenting! As long as you pay for the use of my tools, feel free to use the anvil over there. The other craft masters will cut you the same deal to use their tools and benches.

All right, novice. If you're going to make it as a weaponsmith, you need to start with the simple stuff. Don't worry. We all started with the simple stuff.\n\nGather some iron ore and leathers and try to make a sword.
Steel and stone! Orcs don't give their secrets to outlanders. Try Daggerfall. I'm sure you can convince some poor sap there to teach you.

The Fangs are powerful relics from another age that would overwhelm your soul. I'm surprised they haven't already. They are only safe in our hands.\n\nAnd if that's not a good enough reason, we'll kill you if you keep them. Decide now.

The Fangs were gifts from the Dark Husband to the Night Mother. Sithis gave them to her and we model our weapons after them. If these are truly the original Fangs, they are both great and terrible artifacts.\n\nAnd they belong to the Shadowscales.

You don't know and yet you recovered the Fangs?\n\nThe Night Mother is the bride of Sithis, audience to the Black Sacrament. She holds the power of life and death. Do not defy us, for we act on her behalf.

I do not know … and I fear we have only made the situation worse.\n\nWe thought we could contain them … we built barricades and tried to herd them away but … it was to no avail. Now I fear, we are in even greater danger.

I do? I do! I know Raynor wants to get invited to join the Mages Guild, but we both love exploring old ruins. With this, we would be the foremost experts on Dwemer ruins! That's better than stuffy old mages.\n\n Can you talk to Raynor and convince him?

I do, don't I? Thank you, friend. Kireth and I will be able to force the Mages Guild to accept us. For that matter, we could even go back to Shad Astula if we wanted to!\n\nCould you talk to Kireth about this. I don't want to upset her.
You are wise. I see now why you were the one destined to recover the Fangs.\n\nGive them to me. I swear we will keep them safe.

I don't know. But even if they can, then what?\n\nThe Shadowscales undergo rigorous mental, physical, and spiritual training from an early age. Maybe they could hold the Fangs safely, but wouldn't that make them too powerful?

You must find the pair of altars binding me, further inside the complex.\n\nDo so and I pledge to share the Dominion's plans, and direct you to their most prized possession. Also, I pledge not to violate your corpse on your burial day. A true bargain!

You can never know that, dear mortal. But you're best able to help me dance upon my captors' innards, aren't you?\n\nFor but a small favor, I'll tell you the Dominion's plans, why they've come to Shadowfen, whose faces they've taken … everything.
All right. It's likely we'll both die here, but you've accomplished miracles already. Perhaps fending off a band of Shadowscales isn't beyond your power.\n\nGive me the Fangs.
Within each altar you'll find simple foci. A mortal's touch destroys them and removes my bonds. Then, all I offer is yours.

There is no other way, my sumptuous little morsel. Break my bonds and I'll give you what you desire … perhaps more. Or don't, and let your self-righteous pride doom the entirety of Shadowfen.\n\nMortals do love pretending they have a choice.
Strange. People don't usually come looking for the condemned. He's not far beyond these walls.\n\nA word of advice: don't stray into the western side of the prison. Not unless you want to be eaten.
For dinner. Some of the prisoners have gone feral.\n\nCaptivity with no hope of escape will do that to the weak-minded.

Ha! To try to put a name on me is to try and hold chaos in your hand, mortal!\n\nIf it helps you stay sane, think of me as a miniscule piece of Sithis … a jot of intellect and will, contained within this shadowed form.

Why? They are already champions of the Night Mother. No, leave them their own tools.\n\nYou awoke the Fangs, you may wield one while I keep the other. Your friend holds my gift. Take it, and use it as you will. I will see you again sometime, mortal.

Politeness without obsequiousness! A welcome change. You would make a good Shadowscale.\n\nMortal, you have done enough for me. The Fangs have lain dormant too long. They should be in the world again.

You can find the spriggan matron near the pool, just south of here. Be careful. Elder spriggans are ruthless and dangerous.\n\nBut if you can handle it, the elder spriggan really needs to die. It's the only way we'll all get out of this forest.

Smart idea, dealing with Daedra. Before the Dominion came, she promised my friend the night of his life for a drop of his blood. \n\nI guess being flayed alive counts as the night of his life. She wore his scales like a robe. Seems trustworthy, yes?

Maybe! I spent many cramped nights listening to <<1>>, the High Elf in charge of this place. I'm sure I could piece it together.\n\nBut my friends don't deserve to be trapped in glowing rocks. Free them and I'll help you. A good deal, yes?
Trust me, it's for the best. I'll make my way to the inner chamber, where <<1>> spent most of his time.\n\nTry not to attract the Dremora's attention while you're about. She's a vengeful creature.

The Dark Mane's residue has twisted the altars to Masser and Secunda. It crawls from between the bricks, stretching and clinging to any ray of light. \n\nThe darkness of the Dro-m'Athra reaches from where they dwell beyond, snuffing out all it touches.

Ah, yes. Each of the three altars is normally aligned to one of the lunar phases. Simply refocus their light. Throw back the darkness, and reclaim … ahem. \n\nThat should allow you to pass through the door.
The keystone was stolen, absorbed by a Kothringi named <<1>>.\n\nThe Knahaten flu killed the rest, but somehow he was immune. Did he send you here?
I shifted, which is strictly forbidden by the Green Pact. I was cocky, did it to prove that I could, that's all. It was a mistake, I understand that now.\n\nPlease, I've suffered enough.

My family was slaughtered by the Wood Orcs, and I burned down their village, every last structure, every last tree, for revenge.\n\nI shouldn't have harmed the forest. I should have rallied my people in a mourning war and feasted on my enemies.
The other races laugh at us. Why do we depend on them for wood we could easily take for ourselves?\n\nThe Green Pact is for the weak. We are not the servants of the forest. The Green should serve us!

All those people you just put down? They were my comrades—until we came here. This place … the whispers … it drove them all mad. The few of us that didn't lose our minds were captured and strung up.\n\nSpeaking of … can you help me down now?
Meridia protects me. I champion her cause against the Daedra, and she bestows her blessings upon me.
I don't think … I know. I can smell the thing.
I suppose there's one thing I could do for you. A little prayer our comrades used to say before battle.
Look what they've done to me! The people I knew are gone. There's naught left in them but madness. Madness, and the will of the whispers.\n\nI take it you're immune, too?
Fabulous. So fortunate for you. Now how about you get these webs off me?
The others aren't sworn to serve Meridia. She protects her followers from the curses of the Daedra and the undead.
Well. That was rude.\n\nTell you what. There's an old Fighters Guild secret that just might help. Here goes….
The Kothringi sent you to steal more Ayleid treasures! If only the flu had worked!\n\nDo not take me for a fool, thief. You shall not leave this tomb alive!
May Tall Papa bless you, friend! I thought I'd met my end.\n\nPlease, get me down?
Really? Then how did you break the ward on the temple? <<1>> was the one who sealed me in here!\n\nYou shall not leave this tomb alive!
I escaped the curse, by the blessing of the great Merid-nunda. The whispers … I hear them, yes. But it's like the buzzing of flies, not the madness of men.

I would … I want to … but I'm so weak. I've been trapped down here for so long, I can't even see straight.\n\nYou have to keep going. Find out what this is and stop it. But I'll give you something before you go—a blessing from the Fighters Guild.
This is our home, outsider. The Ternions prefer privacy, so we make it a habit of not letting everyone know where we live.\n\nI hope you can respect that.
We worship the old gods—gods that aren't recognized by most of the Nords. They call us zealots and fanatics. Worshipers of false gods.\n\nI think you can understand why we don't live in Windhelm.

I'm holding up well. Glad I saved my friend back in Darkwater. It took a lot out of me, but not enough to stop me.\n\nNever thought I'd get to save royalty. I'm nervous and excited. Like the first time I ate kanoba spike fruit from home.
I still hurt all over from the previous Dreamwalk. I will push through the pain, though. I won't let another life be lost today.\n\nI promise, I will save King Jorunn … or die trying.

It means your king's last moments of life are upon him. His spirit is strong, a fighter. I believe that's what has caused these projections. He won't give in to death.\n\nSadly, we can do nothing to help him from out here.
Kothringi … yes. I remember now! I am a Kothringi! A plague swept across the village. Sickness, death, corpses piled everywhere ….\n\nIs that why I entered the temple? To find the keystone?
There is nothing left for me here except for these statues. \n\nStatues I built to remember my people, so I could have someone to talk to. Yes, that's why I built them. Someone to talk to ….

When he saw the Daedra, Esan may have raided a vault at the temple. He stole a fang talisman, a magical relic. He's attuned it such that we can focus its power and seal the portals. I'm sure the priests wouldn't approve, but they're not here.
The Fang lay dusty on a shelf for many years, and its power has waned. Esan's attunement, though, has made it such that we can gather power from the Atronachs. We can revitalize the Fang.
Fighters Guild. We defended Firsthold from the Daedra. We defend Nirn from their Anchors.

Welcome to the guild, Associate. Right now, we're looking to reward members that kill Daedra out in the world. \n\nReturn after you've got a few kills under your belt. Some rewards, or even missions, might be waiting for you.
Enormous chains descend from the sky, and rip open a passage to Oblivion. Daedra appear, and lay waste to the countryside. I don't know who started calling them Daedric Anchors, but it fits.
Brave. When the last Guildmaster died, some of our old hands took off. We're still looking to replenish our numbers.\n\nWhat do you say then, do you want to join the Fighters Guild?
I don't answer to you. You are standing on hallowed ground, heathen!
An organization dedicated to the pursuit of knowledge. Docents of the guild seek out books, tomes, and ancient scrolls in their travels.
As you say! I hearby grant you the rank of Student in the Mages Guild, with all the responsibilities and privileges thereof. Good luck, docent!

Precisely. We seek out new information, capture it in our libraries, and make copies for distribution across Tamriel.\n\nEach book you find, we'll credit you in the guild ledger. The more books you find, the more credit you accrue.
Docents with good standing in the guild earn the opportunity to buy special items only available to members. \n\nWe may even have unique opportunities crop up for those with an adventuresome spirit.
Excellent! We'll credit you for your findings on the guild ledger. \n\nThe more books you find, the more credit you'll accrue.
We're preparing this encampment to receive the Skald-King and the Pact delegates.
Last I heard, he was still at Fort Amol. Or maybe he's on his way here? News isn't the most reliable these days.\n\nI hope I get to meet him when he arrives.

No doubt he'd be eager to join his father. He's not ready though. Even now rage takes him. One must be calm to even think about taking such a journey.\n\nSending him in there would only guarantee the death of both father and son.
You say it truly. She will remain here, a prisoner in darkness. Only through the strength of her heart, the wisdom of her mind, can the evil that is the Dark Mane be contained.

You have seen for yourself, Moon Hallowed. The devastation at Fort Grimwatch? That is what is possible for a Dark Mane fully in control of their host. When the host and the Darkness are one … the Darkness is terrifying.

The thought that Jorunn failed his soldiers—that they gave their lives for nothing—weighs heavily on his mind. He must see the truth that they laid down their lives because they loved their King. They believed in him.\n\nGood luck.
Do you even know where we are right now? This cave …. My sister and I fell down a hole while we were hunting. \n\nWe nearly froze to death. We barely got out alive. Wait ….

I would not have made it out from this cave if it wasn't for my sister.\n\nI blacked out from exhaustion and the cold. Nurnhilde carried me the rest of the way to safety. Damn it all. I don't know how we got out of this cave.
Nasty little Goblins. Disgusting creatures, in my opinion.

Hmm. Again, not what I expected. I think I've heard of this … "Aldmeri Dominion," but I don't see how inclusion in this group would appeal to me or to the people in my domain. \n\nAligning with you would only alienate us from others.

Interesting. You think we have common enemies? My only enemies are those who would seek to harm Valenwood. \n\nLet us test your theory though. Show me one of these enemies of whom you speak, so I might better understand.

The Veiled Heritance. Yes. I am familiar with this distinction as well. \n\nThere is one among this group who has come to Valenwood to see me, and I find her curious … very curious. I am not inclined to consider her an enemy.

The intruders who broke the wards above unwittingly loosed the bindings here below. Four of the souls broke free. In their confusion, they wander these halls seeking escape. Subdue them to restore the seal. I will reward your faithful service.

In due time.\n\nAs to the Daedra, their magicka powers the wards that protect my library, but binding them here is no small task. It requires a foundation of souls, each of different blood, from my servants in Tamriel.
A holdfast of the Dwemer, the Dwarves. We're somewhere in Hammerfell, I think, near the South Dragontail Mountains.\n\nOr so Doshia's notes say.
I've killed a lot of people. Everyone on Blackheart's crew has.\n\nBefore Blackheart brought us together, we were a desperate lot, and he knew it. Forced us to become monsters and savages.
It sounds like an excuse, but Blackheart has the means, and I want out.\n\nBut I'll need your help.

Because I'm no murderer. Not by choice. And I want someone to hear it.

I'll prove it. Sort of.

If you're happy to push on, I'll explain what we're doing.
There are two enchanted skulls that Blackheart looted from a Skyrim-bound vessel. \n\nAfterward, he soon … changed. He grew powerful. To defeat him, we need those skulls.
I'm going to seal this door and make sure you're not followed. \n\nI will meet you once you've dealt with Atarus. Good luck.
I know they are. One is kept in the Haven at all times, held by Atarus, one of Blackheart's monstrous pets, just up ahead.\n\nThe second is kept by the Captain himself.
If I did I'd be the wisest woman in Tamriel, comrade. No, no one knows what made the Dwarves disappear. \n\nOr at least, no one is saying.

Why does the river take us anywhere? The Dwemer built complexes all throughout northern Tamriel. My guess is that we're at this ruin for a treasure of some kind.\n\nIf just any Dwarven ruin would do, there are closer places than Mzeneldt.
One will die whether you refuse or not.\n\nPut the mad priest out of his misery or I will choose another. Be assured, you will find that choice … less than optimal.
Different. Strange. Like a part of me is missing. No guards, no castle walls, just the limits of my own mind.\n\nFabrications and illusions—perhaps that's all you are.
Your face is familiar … but I can't remember. You have my thanks, regardless. Both you and the Argonian.
A considered choice. Go tell Saromir his fate.
Your rebellion is noted and the consequences take shape. Orthenir is drawn to his death in Saromir's place.\n\nBind his spirit, unless you are willing to let Daedra overrun Greenshade.
We're a small town, right? We don't get a lot of visitors. But these people were walking around like they owned the place.\n\nAnd everybody has been looking at me all … strangely.

Your concern is appreciated, but in case you have forgotten, I am dead. You have already done more for me than I ever expected. I return to Sovngarde now. I will welcome my brother when he joins me.\n\nWith luck, I shall see you there one day as well.

I wouldn't talk like that in front of <<1>>. In my experience, prophecies like that have a way of fulfilling themselves. You brought this attention on yourself. Show a bit more subtlety and you might just live through this day.
Smartest thing you've said today. Yes, I'm taking you to <<1>>. Mind what you say to him, and keep your guard up. And don't trust him. I certainly don't.

It's hard to explain.You know how sometimes you think you see someone watching you out of the corner of their eye?\n\nEverybody in town has been looking at me like that since I got back. I swear to the Green!

Let me tell you about <<1>>. When he won, he collected. When he lost, he borrowed. When the well ran dry, he whined. He owes me a lot of gold. If I forgave the debts of every whiner with a sob story, I'd be out of business.
The Stormfist happened, the savages. They cut their way through our ranks, screaming about the Orcthane.
Why not? Come on, big shot. I'll take you to him myself.

Of course he's still alive. Dead men don't pay debts. We made a deal, him and me. He's working it off. Doing a little heavy lifting around the camp. And when he gets used up, I'm going to sell him.\n\nHe doesn't know about that part yet.
I've no idea. We're a peaceful group. We commune with Kyne as guardian of the deep woods.\n\nWe have no interest in who holds the throne in Windhelm.
I have a daughter. She left the clan, years ago, to find her fortune in the city. I told Awyn to get the Sigil to her.\n\nSo many dead. If anyone will continue our tradition, it will have to be her.
I needed a Bosmer soul. Orthenir was convenient. Now you know the price of disobeying a Prince of Oblivion.
Our clan is … was … isolated. We cared more for the turn of the seasons than the fashions of the big cities.\n\nMy Aerana wanted more than what Kyne could offer. So she left.
Yes? Something I can do for you?
What? My mother, my aunt? Dead?\n\nThey were such boring, simple people. They would never have hurt … why?
The Sigil! I have to go, I have to find it. It was so important to her ….
Stendarr's sweaty swordarm, I still have trouble understanding everything that's happened. Aelif dead, a minion of Molag Bal.\n\nAnd Sees-All-Colors … did we do the right thing?

Aye, she did. But they were both my friends, comrade. I'd known them both for … we used to joke, you know? About what we would do if we led the guild.\n\nWithout them, I don't know what I'm going to do.

Aye, you're right about that. But Aelif was my friend, comrade. I'd known her for … we used to joke, you know? About what we would do if we led the guild.\n\nWithout her, I don't know what I'm going to do.
Thank you. Now stand back, please.

It won't be easy. When I tried the simpler version of this ritual, the Daedric force nearly destroyed me. I can't imagine it will allow you to place the components easily.\n\nBe careful in the swamp, especially around the stele.

It's part of their skin-stealing magic. The real question is, where'd they get so much? Wait, I don't want to know.\n\nWhatever they did to the Hist sap turned it flammable. Once we enter the Vault, set those vats on fire to end this nightmare.

That's the easy part. I heard <<1>> mutter the words a hundred times.\n\nMaybe you can get something useful out of that Dremora before she realizes you double-crossed her. If you keep her busy, I'll open the door.

It hit the swamp like a wave. One day, our scavengers were picking through the trash as they always did, the next a Daedric miasma swept over Xal Ithix.\n\nThe creatures of the swamp became malevolent and powerful, threatening our village.

Xal Ithix is a small village in the Black Marsh, an Argonian settlement down-water from larger towns and cities of Shadowfen.\n\nWe've survived—thrived, really—by scavenging in the swamp, pulling treasure from others' trash.

No, not always. Beyond the mud huts of our village, you'll see the great ruins of the ancient Argonians—the xanmeers and the stele.\n\nThey were built generations ago by our ancestors. We live in their shadows, in more ways than one.
The swamp itself has turned against us! It's the hoarvor. They usually feed on small mammals. Clutches have been known to swarm sickly wamasu.\n\nBut nothing like this.

They're much larger than normal and more powerful. In days past, if a rotgorge did attack an unwary scavenger, all she'd have to do to break its hold was smack it on the shell with a stick.\n\nNow, the things cling until you kill them. They're mad.

What do you want to know?  <<1>> has been communing with the Hist longer than I've been out of my shell. He knows every inch of ground, every drop of water in Black Marsh.\n\nIf anyone can figure out what's wrong with Xal Ithix, he can.

The tree-minder is proud, but also wise. If he can't solve our problems himself, he'll ask for help.\n\nI've never known him to put his own desires above the needs of the village, and I can't believe he'd start now.

When you're done, meet me at the top of the xanmeer. I know a few tricks that will get me past the swamp creatures, especially with you distracting them.\n\nI'm sorry I can't help you with the potions, but it's just too much for one person.
A what now? Gonlas got trapped in a ritual? Why would he be doing a ritual in his house? He's not even a mage!
Check the other houses in town. Look for Tashpir in the next house on, Lothiel and Ganniel in the one across the square. My place is that last one on the row. Meet me there when you're done.

Unearth the relic. It's buried at the base of a nearby stele. Once you have it, you'll need to climb the winding road to a tall ritual site that overlooks Xal Ithix.\n\nThere, you should be able to use it to stop Namira's minions.
I must stay here to keep the Daedra back. Go to the Hist tree, near the center of Xal Ithix.\n\nDuring my trance, I saw what they did. Namira's minions placed a relic there. It poisons the swamp.

In my vision, I saw the Dremora react to the relic. They are terrified of it, of what it can do.\n\nThe same energies it uses to corrupt our Hist tree can be turned upon Namira's minions. Wield it, and you can destroy them.

Skordo knows everything and he's tough as nails! Captains Eilram and Arakh may be in charge, but Skordo keeps our unit running smoothly. I suggest you talk to him before you do anything else down there.

I assumed Molag Bal was trying to be funny. It's really just a deep pit, so the tower is a lie. Get it? A lie? No? \n\nNeither did I. But maybe there used to be a tower here once. That probably makes more sense.

I'm a Wood Elf. I'm not a front-line soldier, if that's what you're getting at. If I have to fight, I prefer to do it from a distance. \n\nAnyway, jump off here and you should be fine. I really appreciate the help.

The fat-bastard ogrims dragged away my friends. We joined the Guild together.  It ain't right, them getting tortured by ogrims.\n\nYou rescue Sinfray, Borgath, and Vikord. I'll find Overseer Aruz and then you and me can deal with him, permanently.

Who am I? You could not hope to comprehend my true nature, filth. Think of me as an aspect of the Lady of Decay and rightful ruler of all spirits.\n\nI claim this land and all within it. None may defy me!

Indeed. I'm sorry for the deception, but I wanted this nightmare to end. To be free from this torment.\n\nAll the pirates you'll encounter in these caves are like me. We're part of Blackheart's original crew, and share his curse.

Those cold-blooded primitives fell once; they can fall again! I will show them that their "spirits of the Hist" are pale shadows compared to me.\n\nNow, leave my Hand where it lies. Abandon your foolish quest.
There is nothing else, I swear. \n\nI beg you to finish this by killing Blackheart and taking his skull. Destroying it will end this torment for the entire crew.

The skull's dark power protects Blackheart from true death, and you will need me to destroy it if you can defeat him.\n\n I'll meet with you once you've bested him. I would face him with you, but I fear I would fall under his control again.

Some call them Dwarves—a race of brilliant artisans and metalworkers who possessed great ingenuity. They built vast underground cities filled with remarkable inventions. Now such works are all that remain of the Dwemer.

Wonderful! Now comes the best part—mixing ingredients to give the guardian its powers. \n\nLightning bellies and hive seeds make a fire guardian. Hive seeds and dew bugs make a wooden guardian. Lightning bellies and dew bugs, a water guardian.

Goblins. Cursed, cursed Goblins happened. They stole much of my herd in the middle of the night. Those remaining were lost to snakes that had taken to calling the oasis their home. There is no end to my troubles these days.

Yes. It'll be your guardian! Use this husk and build the one you want. Then we'll test it against the others.\n\nLead it over to challenge two other guardians. Tell you what—you can even use these healing roots to give your guardian an edge.
Good.\n\nOur task to eliminate the High Kinlord Rilis is the only one that remains. And Rilis will need a mortal host to enter Nirn.

Yes. This Shade that's assumed the form of the late Prince Naemon is behind this, but he's not here. And it's true, mysteries aside, we need to put the Blackroot clan back to rest, but the rangers are exhausted.\n\nAre you willing to help me?
A treasure of some kind? A potent weapon or an epic spell? Doshia respected only one thing: power.\n\nWhatever it is, we must get it away from here.

Doshia knew of this place, and so others do as well. If we don't retrieve … whatever it is … others will come. And it must have something to do with that Mortuum Vivicus. If Molag Bal plans to unleash that weapon again, we must stop it.
The last days of the Dwemer were endless war. Their mages raced to perfect ever more esoteric spells. Ever more powerful weapons. Perhaps the origins of the Vivicus stem from that long-gone era.

Doshia kidnapped our comrade, Merric. She intended to harvest his soul for Molag Bal, in service to a plan involving this "Mortuum Vivicus."\n\nAnd then, of course, you came to his rescue. Slew her, and stole her journal. Which is what led us here.

When the Captain spoke to the cursed skull, it claimed to be the Daedric Prince, Molag Bal. \n\nI thought it some trick, or jest, but then the skull growled an inhuman word and we came under its sway. I became the wretch you see before you.

His skull is the key. It protects him from true death. \n\nI can destroy it if you best him. Go through the Roost and face him if you're willing. I won't risk fighting him lest I fall under his control again.
Many things. The journal spoke of this place. But it also spoke of … terrible things. Things I wish I could unlearn. Prolonged contact with Molag Bal twisted her mind.

None can say for sure. Some believe they achieved divinity. Others claim they were consumed by some folly of their own. Perhaps both are true. But long ago they vanished, the entire race, leaving little but their marvelous treasures behind.
That's where the harpies are kept, tended to by hags. The harpies protect Blackheart's home when he's set anchor, and they are essential for his dominance on the open seas.

What help can you give them, mortal? I cannot strike you down, but my minions are more than enough for the likes of you.\n\nEven those foolish Hist-worshipers recognize that. They won't even approach this part of Xal Ithix.
What? How did he know—\n\nMortal, if you attempt this, my creatures will overwhelm you! Nothing will stop me from taking Xal Ithix.
Dim the gleam of avarice I see in your eyes. The treasure I seek is knowledge, worthless to any but a scholar. Those who help me acquire this can expect to be well-rewarded, however.

I got home and saw Bowenas talking to Ezreba. As soon as Ezreba saw me, she shouted. Two hooded men jumped me out of nowhere. One of the men slammed me up against the wall and they left, carrying Bowenas. She called for help, but ….

I don't know! I didn't see where they went. Maybe … try looking at Ezreba's house? She lives in one of the Khajiiti homes past the fields. I'll … I'll go look at the temple. If she managed to get away, it's the best place to hide.
Because the harpies' distraction alone is devastating. Few are left alive to tell the tale. I remember boarding ships after the flying beasts only to see them picking flesh off the bones of the crew.
Ships at sea are usually not worried about anything but another ship. Blackheart's harpy flocks attack ahead of his ship, eviscerating his target while he moves in.
A rare and exquisite thing, to be sure! My inn remains clear-headed so you don't have to.
You find me well, Stendarr be praised. Doshia's tender ministrations are the worst to befall me in some time.\n\nTender attention and the kindness of my comrades have restored me to health.
Now that is a loaded question! We carry some exotic Dark Elf and Argonian beverages, but our best-selling drink has got to be Voljar's spiced mead. My friend Betra loves the stuff!

Betra is the love of my life! She's so wonderful! If not for her, I'd probably still be working in that skeever trap, the Cold Moon.\n\nShe's away on business, at Fort Amol, but she promised she'd be home in time for my birthday.

Sees-All-Colors would be the one to ask about that, oh my comrade. I have seen the journal, but have little idea what it says.\n\nGive me a problem I can solve with a stout weapon. Those are the problems I enjoy.
Aelif is well, moons be bright for asking. She worries about the time and money spent on this … quest.\n\nWe destroy anchors, slaughter Daedra. But what is accomplished?
Ask our dear guildmaster, comrade. She spent many favors and much coin having it translated. And refuses to share the results with Aelif!\n\nIf Aelif cannot be trusted, who can?
I never gave it.
I'm here. Let's leave it at that.
Only if I give you time to use it!\n\nCome forth, my corruption! Be manifest and destroy this worm!
We build whatever needs building and fix whatever needs fixing. We serve at the pleasure of the Skald-King!
Yes. I'm going out with the road crew. We'll be repairing roads throughout Eastmarch, starting with the area around Cragwallow. But first, we drink!
Windhelm's most prestigious bank. Well, really, Windhelm's only bank. \n\nSafest place to store your valuables. Just talk to the banker over there.

Fire. Nothing causes more chaos than a raging fire. Scares even the most dim-witted, hard-headed Nords.\n\nThe carts the Stormfist brought are full of weapons, food, and other gear. Set them ablaze and start a panic. That should slow them down a bit.
Yes, but <<1>>'s death weighs heavily on Heita-Meen. She says she should've known. Poor thing, we were all fooled.\n\nBut enough of our troubles. Did you stop his imposter?
Once she's recovered, <<1>> will no doubt celebrate your accomplishment. But this artifact you mentioned, the <<A:2>>. Do you know anything of its whereabouts?

Ezreba's been talking to me for days about wanting to set up statues, art pieces, in the center of town. They're ugly and have these crystals. Anyway, when she came to talk to me today, she didn't come alone.

To reach me, you must first unlock the prison door. Molag Bal uses crystallized darkness to hold me and suppress my power.\n\nMove the crystals from their locations to the prison door and the way shall be opened for you.

She kept talking about the temple ruins. Something about the ruins being the source … she was beside herself. She kept saying "just don't hurt him." I don't know. I'm sorry, everything happened so fast.
I am the last Ayleid king.\n\nIn our ancient language, my name means Ruler in Dark Times. I can imagine no darker time than the end of the Ayleid people.

I am a servant of Meridia. Her master tactician and strategist.\n\nBetween my master's blessings and the time-distorting nature of this dread realm, I am still alive. Consider that your good fortune, for you will never defeat Molag Bal without my help.
Good. If you can get this mess sorted out we'll be back to business as usual and I won't have to listen to any more of <<1>>'s moaning.

He's a copper miner. Veins of copper ore were found in the mine a while back, but the stuff isn't worth much, so it just piles up.\n\n<<1>> somehow manages to scrape out a living selling it to a few buyers.
Yes, comrade. The journals also speak of a tome, instructions for creating the weapon. The crystal heart of the weapon and the means to construct it lie here somewhere in these ruins.
Very well, but please hear me out. The Pact should not resort to slavery.
You are welcome to stay in Xal Ithix, of course. We've still got some cleaning up to do.\n\nI recommend you avoid the high road, though. There are still Dremora lurking there.
I know some of the scavengers have had problems with the stranglers. You could go down into the swamp and see if you can help out.
You might explore outside Xal Ithix. I understand there are some ancient ruins nearby, between here and Hissmir.
Someone close to you has plans … plans for both of us. Plans to betray you. \n\nI am anchored, contained … pulled away … beware, comrade!
I was looking through the temple ruins and somebody jumped me. By the Green, my head hurts worse than the time I won the troll arena jackpot and we … erm. \n\nBowenas! Did you find her? Is she safe?
Yes! She ran past me just a moment ago. I called to her, but she just kept running. Heard her crying as she ran.
She might seem crass, but she has shown her worth. I would gladly follow her; she has a righteous will and the strength to back it up.
That I do not know. I heard them mention the warehouse at the west end of the docks. Maybe the ritual is there? Wherever it is, you have to stop it. Then tell Captain Zafira.\n\nTava be with you.

Unishi has just finished preparing two potions for other buyers in town. Deliver them and we have a deal. \n\nOne goes to a woman named Dariah, and the other to a man named Irwad. This one will mark their houses on your map—make it easy for you.

The plan is to get you to the second level so you can find out what's going on up there. I refuse to believe the captains just gave up on us. \n\nWe'll get some weapons, rally the troops, and follow you shortly.

It could be. There is no safer place in Coldharbour, for Molag Bal's reach cannot extend into the Hollow City. That is what was intended, and that is the way it is.\n\nPlease, walk with me. Let me show you why this city will serve your needs.
It's about time. Hand it over.\n\nShe promised me my hair would grow back and that I would have hundreds of children! This better work!
I'm not big on speculating, but I'm certain that blackheart Ifriz has something to do with it. Be careful around that one.\n\nOh, and one more thing. If you see Gwilir again, kill him for me.
Find Captain Eilram. I know him. He's a good man. This place must have him confused. Or something worse has happened to him. Either way, we need to know.

It's his damned fault we ended up down here! He blundered into a Dremora patrol during a scouting mission. Led them right to us! That imbecile couldn't scout his way out of an empty crate.\n\nBut we really need to find the captains now.
Yes. This is just what I need.\n\nNow leave me with my prize. Many days of pleasure ahead.
Don't tell me what to do, peon. You're just jealous.\n\nI already paid Unishi for it. Now hand it over.
Why look when you have found your new calling? Spikeball is the most exciting new sport in all of Tamriel! You will be hero to all!
Perhaps you do not understand. Bunul is running a business here. He must run a match. Perhaps, after the match, Bunul will be more willing to discuss this <<1>> person. But only after the match.
Ah! Laws in Alik'r are so strict. So many things are banned but should not be. The Baandari specialize in wares like this.\n\nNo cause to complain though. Can be very profitable for us, if you help.

No problem. You've heard of skooma, yes? Makes people happy, and harmless as long as it's made properly ….\n\nThe Baandari sell only the best skooma. Probably, that's why the guards have taken it—for themselves.

Baandari are very special tribe of Khajiit. We lost our homeland many generations ago, so now we travel, not just in Elsweyr, but all over Tamriel. \n\nWe sell exotic goods you cannot find anywhere else. Ildani brings Baandari wares to Sentinel.
Yes, yes! I heard him complain this ruin didn't hold everything he needed. He left to find a place of power where he could use his special egg.\n\nWhat did he call it again?

Yes, that's the one! Here, this portal leads beyond the ruins. I'll stay here and see about freeing any prisoners stuck inside.\n\nAnd if you're planning to inform the vicecanons of <<1>>, perhaps leave me out of your report, yes? Yes.

Oh, it thinks it can defeat me. You have no sense of your own futility, do you?\n\nMuch as I desire, I can't steal a walking tragedy from this realm. Go, look for <<1>> and <<A:2>>, as though your actions matter.
Somewhere beyond these ruins, I'm sure. This portal will take you from this place, I promise. And that is the last promise to you I will keep.
Where? I'll tell you where. Here, give me your map, wayfarer. There's an old mine on the cliffs overlooking Goat's Head Oasis. That's where you'll find the dirt eating creatures.
My attempts to use the Orb of Discourse to locate Sai Sahan did not meet with success, so I decided to try a more direct approach. \n\nI used it as it was intended, and contacted Abnur Tharn.
He admits that he knows Sai Sahan's location, but he will not reveal it. He demands to speak with you, directly.
Battlereeve Alduril, vanguard commander for the invasion fleet.\n\nAre you having second thoughts? We need those Lamias dispatched, post-haste.
Subtlety and stealth. Let's not bring the entire castle guard down on our heads.\n\nAnd didn't he say this was a town of soul shriven? Maybe we can find one who knows his way around.
Try to be inconspicuous. We just got free of this place. The last thing we need is to get recaptured.
I remember your <<1>>, yes. He was a fierce runner. Great speed. Very powerful.

You must understand—one doesn't become a Thalmor agent until their loyalty is proven beyond question. \n\nIf Asteril confesses or if we find substantial proof, I will admit I was wrong. Until then, I remain extremely skeptical.

Report the extent of this attack to <<1>>. I expect to return with reinforcements quite soon. We'll drive the Dominion from <<A:2>>.\n\nIf you see opportunities to aid the keepers, I urge you to do so.
This is Thalmor business, and I am going to the Thalmor residence to confront Asteril myself. \n\nYou are welcome to accompany me, if you choose.
The desert can be cruel and unrelenting. A wise traveler knows where he can find shade and cool during the heat of the day.
Haha! Ildani knows well how to slip out of metal bracelets. \n\nAmong the Baandari, the Ja'khajiits learn this before they learn to lace their boots!
Ah, but if you were in the open desert, it would not be so. When I cross the wastes, I always keep in mind the nearest refuge from the sun.
There's a mine I often use, because underground is even better than under canvas. Allow me to mark it on your map.
The Dominion tells us nothing. Those who left, they killed. Those who stayed, they let live.\n\nWe don't know why. We continue to prepare for the hatching. They haven't stopped us from that, yet.

Her death troubles me greatly, but the integrity of the Thalmor is of greater concern, and I am pleased to be proven right in that respect.\n\nWith that concern behind us, we can finally start searching for the true source of this treachery.
This one doesn't know, but it captivates Didakah's attention. Perhaps it is magical!

Then go, light the braziers in the Xanmeers of First Light and Setting Sun. As you walk amongst the Dominion, listen with care. We must know if they mean us harm.\n\nAnd look for <<1>>. If she … still lives, inform her I'll need her assistance.
Didakah knows. He was told by nice traveler. Traveler told this one that the shiny comes from ruins to the south. He showed Didakah on a map, now Didakah shows you on a map.
Ezreba just … she just wanted to save her husband. A week ago, dark pilgrims arrived in town. Members of the Stonefire cult. They came to this one's home in the night. They took him. Now … look.
This time, it's almost as though the runes themselves were mocking me. I translated the text relatively quickly.\n\nYou can see when you read it … the words themselves just make no sense.
If you'd told me years ago that I'd do spellwork with Shalidor, I'd have called you a liar.\n\nI'm happy to do the work. It's the chance of a lifetime. But I can't help but feel I'm in over my head.
Ezreba will turn herself in. You have nothing more to fear from this one. She is so sorry. So very, very sorry for what she's done.

How sweet of you to ask! Ifriz hides behind illusions. I have removed them.\n\nHe has something of mine. I want it back. Kill him, and both our problems are solved. But hurry. He will soon discover his defenses are down and hide himself again.
Oh, praise Zeht! \n\nI've waited so long. I asked Unishi to make me a potion that will make my husband kind and loyal. I hope it works.

Jorunn's brother, Fildgor. He desired the throne. Normally, succession is determined by the Crown of Freydis, but there were … complications. Anyway, the brothers fought, Jorunn won, and Fildgor was exiled.\n\nEnd of story. Or so we thought.

Yes, it's just that treethane. It's not my place to say, but I wonder if she isn't just a few leaves shy of a full tree. \n\nI mean … I came to speak to her in the spirit of scholarly study, but she treated me as a child! She said "run along now."
If the Dominion overhear us, we're both dead. We'll have to make this quick.\n\nI fear they plot to take the Mnemic Egg.

Very well. The Mnemic egg traps the essence of a Hist's memory. It holds the memories of those hatched in the pools.\n\nWithout it, our people would be doomed. With it, the dominion could train an army with the memories of our greatest warriors.
I'm sorry, but I cannot tell you more with so many Dominion around.
It is our most sacred relic and must be protected at all costs. Without it, our people would be doomed.\n\nThat is all I can say to one who is not a keeper of the egg.

Yes. They've come for the celebration, but also to meet with King Jorunn about Pact business. I try not to get too involved.\n\nIn fact, I'm not sure how Jorunn stands all the pomp and ceremony. It would drive me insane!
<This ledger contains various numbers and information dealing with taxes. The numbers vary little from year to year, although recently, <<1>> purchased several lots of fine ales and wines.>

This trial determines if your spirit can understand the spirit of my people.\n\nWe cherish courage, which helps us face this realm's horrors; endurance, which allows us to bear its hardships; and preservation, which keeps our traditions alive.
I am your advisor. We both wish to stop Molag Bal's machinations. I offer you what help I can.\n\nThe Hollow City awaits you and your allies. Use it wisely and it shall not fail you.
I have no idea. I've never done anything to offend her. I've never even met her!\n\nI should be going though. Someone's waiting on me, and he can get a little impatient.
Know that our arrangement with Molag Bal prohibits us from interfering with the Dremora who collect sap from the Hist.\n\nYou, however, are under no such obligation.

Demonstrate your strength and physical prowess. Destroy the vats and disrupt their operations. If you add more treated wood to the fires, the sap will burn and the vats will melt in the intense heat.\n\nComplete this task, and then return to me.
<<1>> can go count his scales. A Dominion dryskin cooked and ate one of our unhatched eggs! Though I'm sworn to the Shell, I will not allow him to harm another.
Make the egg he consumed his final meal! Spill his blood upon the ground, where it may feed the roots of future generations. Show we fight to protect our young.
I wasn't thinking of the others, I ….\n\nYour words humble me. I'll return to <<1>> shortly. He'll know how to stop this madness, I'm sure of it.
What good is the hatching ritual if these despicable fools eat our young? Tell me, what platitudes would <<1>> say to that? This dryskin must be stopped for good!

There must be more to it than massacre. What can they achieve by waiting before slaughter? They could kill us now and have done with this place.\n\nSomething sinister is at work, but we have no time. The hatching will soon begin.

Now is not the time for questions. Now is the time for betting! Place your bet on one of these fine lizards. Winners get fed, losers feed us. Right into the stewpot! After the race is finished we can discuss your friend.
Jolly good! You're paying attention. Now, this is a play in three acts.\n\nIn each act you'll isolate the guild from those bloodthirsty, political, warmongering sons of silkworms. By killing them.
Then there is hope.\n\nAs the hatching approaches, the Dominion will likely observe the ritual. Would you stand with us, despite the danger?
An educated choice! That one was trained by professional breeders! Keep this between us, but he is my favorite as well.
Ah, she's a lucky one! I've seen that little lady win a dozen races this very day! Don't spread it around, but if I were to bet, she would be my choice.
You are wise, my friend! This little beast was found in the wreckage of a Daedric Anchor. I confess, she is my favorite. Swifter than swift!
Suit yourself. The races will continue all day!
You question my skill at cooking? This one's stew is known for yards around! But, eh … maybe you have a suggestion? An exotic recipe?
Many thanks. Now, let's get our little friends to the starting line. The race is about to begin!
No! None of us are! The Ra-Netu are going to kill us all!\n\nIt is not fair! I am too young to die … I just want to run, to run away ….

Blood and honor! I have always had faith, but never have I … you are here to fight the Ra-Netu?\n\nPraise Ruptga! I was prepared to dishonor myself, but he sent you … I will go then. Gods be with you, my friend. Is the way clear?
I figured. We started sending people through the portal as soon as the barrier collapsed.\n\nThere's a city nearby. We saw it before we were captured. We're going to try to regroup there.

Use the other stone pillar. The one on the platform behind us. Touch that stone pillar and an apparition will appear. One of your enemies, as you say. \n\nFight this enemy so that I might see its true nature.

By the light of Jone and Jode, this is the craziest thing ever seen!\n\nEven Razum-dar would have lost his patience by now! If you think all this makes sense, then Hazazi is starting to wonder about you too!

She is one who has been blessed with fascinating gifts. Gifts I cannot afford to ignore.\n\nYou would know her identity though. I was able to capture one of her memories. Touch the Petitioning Stone again and I will share it with you.

The damned Akaviri! Their invasion a decade ago continues to haunt us! They caused extensive damage to the palace, but I made sure the rest of the city was repaired first.\n\nWork on the palace proceeds, but it goes exceedingly slowly.

Of course. You see, the culture of the Alik'r evolved around this ideal. \n\nMany of us today realize that exceptions must be made, but in my position, to ask my soldiers to strike down the dead would cause an outcry, and possibly lead to rebellion.

They are our greatest hope, for no matter how great a threat the Withered Hand may pose, they cannot even compare to the necromancers of the First Era. \n\nThe Wards contain the spirits of three Ansei heroes who sacrificed themselves to protect us.

They uphold the covenant with the Divines. As long as we consecrate the dead in the name of Tu'whacca, they cannot be raised by even the most powerful necromancy.\n\nThus the Withered Hand can only raise corpses that have not been consecrated.
Well done, outsider. That should give the Hist time to heal while the Dremora rebuild the refining vats.

Watch and listen. While I could explain things to you, it will be better to simply show you. The history of the city permeates these streets, and with a bit of magic I can reveal it to you.\n\nNow, come. Let us walk.
I cannot feel the Hist. This must be why the Dominion waited. To see if the hatching would fail.
Everything.\n\nNow leave me, I really must prepare the ritual.
Very well. When we die, our memories return to the Hist. When one of the Hist dies, it gives seed to a Mnemic Egg.\n\nEverything it witnessed—everything we witnessed—is contained within that Egg.
I'm sorry, but we do not have time. Ask me later, when this is over.
You must still perform the Trial of Spirit. Speak to Xohaneel when you're ready to begin.
Then the time has come to choose. \n\nDo you agree that life, no matter the hardships, is sacred? Or do you side with the scholars, who would rather end the suffering and let our Hist tree die?
I'll offer myself to Sithis, in exchange for holding back the void. It must be done. Save the unhatched eggs!
Without the Hist, the eggs can't hatch. Now there is only void! I feel it, forming around the tree.\n\nYou saw what it did to Ahaht-Ei. The same will happen to our unhatched eggs!
Keep the eggs from the void. Protect our future!
I pray that we are not too late to stop the Withered Hand, and with the same breath, I thank the gods for guiding you here.\n\nTu'whacca watch over you, wayfarer. Here comes Gabrielle. Are you ready?
I warned you once the price of refusal. You cannot undo what has been done. But If you wish to stop the Daedra from spreading death across Greenshade, you will bind the Bosmer soul.

No, a High Elf. But he does awful things to swamp-lizards through their special trees. Poisons them like a spider's bite, see?\n\n<<1>> uses his big glowing egg to destroy swamp-lizards. Behind a door, like a clawless coward. That is all Kazdi knows!
Open sealed door, squash <<1>> flat, wash foot.\n\n<<2>> can help open the seal! <<1>> bragged of defenses so often, <<2>> knows them like her own whiskers.

Simple. <<1>> wishes to stop the clawless High Elf who kills swamp-lizard babies and leaves Dominion-soldiers to die. And see Elsweyr again, maybe?\n\nIf <<1>> shows you how to remove seal on door, you splatter <<2>>. Deal?
Khaba has no interest in talking of troublemakers. All she speaks of are bets and trolls, winners and losers. Perhaps if you were to bet, she would remember a loser named Tand.
This is not fair. Ingredients cost money. Unishi cannot afford to give away free potions!\n\nHow about this? You want to help the monkey? You help Unishi, and she will do what you ask.

You can't hear the noise? Piercing, like fleshflies roosting in your ears? And the smell, like … moss and alit hide, set aflame.\n\nBut we must remove it from these ruins, before the Dominion returns.
Did <<1>> remove your hands, then?\n\nA joke, my friend. None shall touch <<A:2>> until I'm certain this isn't some kind of Dominion trap. Please, stand back.
Some, you say. They murdered our hatchlings, our children. Why?\n\nBut you saved some. That is … it's a good thing. It must be a good thing.
Then the danger is graver than I thought. The <<1>> bears the memories of the Hist. Severing our link is the least they could do with it.\n\nCome, we must leave this place!
We must restore our link to the Hist. Without it, <<A:1>> will never see our young rise from its cool waters.\n\nThe Dominion could only cause such a thing with a powerful artifact.
This one wants no trouble. What do you want to know?
Good! This will be a fight for the ages!
What's the matter? No stomach for blood? Do you weep at the sight of bones?
This one doesn't want to make an enemy of the Vinedusk Company. Ask your questions, quickly!
Excellent! Let the battle begin!
It was you who stopped the Colovians? Out of respect for what you did at Arenthia, you may ask your questions. But be quick, I have much to attend to.
Ah, yes! <<1>>! It is said he took down three Giants, single-handedly. Watch you don't fall into the pit. He would grab you by the ankles and beat his opponent to death with your corpse.

A fine choice! A fearsome opponent. Terrorized the back country for weeks before our trainer caught him. Don't get too close to the railing if you've been drinking. Trust Khaba when she says, you don't want to get between those two!
Those memories would be lost and the Hist would suffer. We would suffer.
As we speak, the eggs grow moist. Before we begin the hatching, I wish to know the Dominion's intentions. But endangering yourself on our behalf isn't something I can ask.
<Nothing happens.>
<The holder warms to your touch.>
Agreed. Allow me to create a portal to Meridia's city. We can speak there.
<Nothing happens.>
<The keystone leaps from your hand into the holder.>

The time of the great Argonian civilization was coming to an end, and our Hist tree feared what that would mean for its children.\n\nWhen Molag Bal offered a different solution, the Hist tree gladly accepted.
Take a look at the crystal we discovered. Eilram thinks it may be one of the Lights of Meridia the Mages Guild told us about. If it is, it could be invaluable to our efforts here.

Yes, provided you prove yourself worthy to both sides. Our two factions argue over the ultimate fate of the Hist tree.\n\nWhich is the better outcome? Eternal death or eternal suffering? And then, of course, there is your mission to this dread realm.
Khaba remembers him. He bet and bet until he lost all his gold, crawled into the bottle. <<1>> heard of his losses, and his drinking, and his debts. He might have even heard from Khaba.
You have proven yourself, as I knew you would. I shall answer what I can.
Of course the fights are close! They're trolls!
Come back soon. Maybe your luck won't leave you next time!
Started a few weeks ago now, when the mist … changed. Turned a sickly color.
I was? What happened?
<<1>> … <<1>> … ah yes! Dulan remembers him now. Yellow braids, younger? He was here. He lost many coins, then got into the moon-sugar rum. Sad state of affairs.

I have been tracking my prey for many nights. A heathen vampire who shall soon be cleansed from this world. I thought him alone, but now that I see this place I suspect a lair is hidden nearby. He shall regret leading me to his vile nest.
Some kind of commentary about Shalidor's goal, no doubt. He may be a child, but Sheogorath certainly knows how to make a point.
The more we deal with him, the more I'm convinced. The Mad God is a spoiled child. Pulling legs off bugs just to watch them twitch.\n\nWhat else happened?
Falinesti? It is gone, yes. I can sense its absence, like a hole in my heart. It still walks. Somewhere.\n\nThis land has greater worries.
Down deep. Beneath the soil. Something locked away in stone and metal. A dark voice, whispering.\n\nThey heard her. Heard her whispers.

Vampire scum. He barely put up a struggle before he fell to his knees, begging for what he calls a life. I did not expect such weakness.\n\nI will finish him now, if you'd be so kind as to step aside.
As you wish. In this moment or the next, his existence shall end either way.\n\nBut be wary. A vampire attempts to sway and beguile with its words. Do not listen, no matter what he says.
Kept to ourselves. Didn't prey on the living! The beasts, the hoarvor glutted themselves on the blood of hunters. We fed on them. We didn't kill anyone. It was a natural way. Until he came.

The skull rests in the back of this cavern. Its curse seeps into the mists all around us. Destroy the skull and the magic goes with it.\n\nI never wanted this. Spare me and I can bring others to my side. We can be of use to you!

The veiled one. Altmer, I think. Sought an alliance. Promised power. Told us we didn't need to hide anymore.\n\nOthers in my clan agreed. He taught them a ritual using an ancient vampire's skull. Said it would allow them to make countless thralls.

Did I not warn you of this? That his vile tongue would worm its way into your thoughts?\n\nThere's no such thing as a good vampire, just a vampire that has not yet been tempted. Our goals here are the same. Will you forget them for this scum?
Quick work, mate! \n\nNow pick up me skull, add it to the lot, and put the whole kit and kaboodle on the ground over there. I'll be doing the rest.
Much more, but there is no time. You must keep moving if you want to survive. Go, now!
Be swift. More lamias could boil from the ruins at any moment.

Of course, you have much to concern yourself with. When last we spoke, we had explored the Dwarven ruin of Mzeneldt.\n\nWe found an ancient crystal and tome, left behind by a squad of Ayleid soldiers fleeing undead abominations.

You have my apologies, comrade. When I heard the Ancients speaking of the Mortuum Vivicus, I knew the past might contain more clues to solve our present crisis. I wanted to begin my research immediately.

Simple. <<1>> wishes to stop the clawless High Elf who kills swamp-lizard babies and leaves Dominion-soldiers to die. And see Elsweyr again, maybe?\n\nIf <<1>> shows you how to remove seal on door, you splatter <<2>>. Deal?

<<1>> can show you how <<2>> sealed the door.\n\nHe blamed Dominion-soldiers for not finding keystones to seal the ruin, but refused to let us search. Too much time poking swamp-lizards in the chest with his knives. Coward.
Ah, Pact-soldier is clever indeed! Then this will be so very simple, yes?\n\nCome, we must activate a crystal. After, <<1>> will show merciful kind friend where the keystone fits!

Hrrm. Keystone makes it faster to get to <<1>>. <<2>> supposes Pact-soldier could fight through countless snake-ladies and angry-dead to avoid losing the keystone.\n\nIt may have uses elsewhere, but <<2>> does not know.

From what I gathered, one of Naemon's servants has stolen General Malgoth's bow and compels the Blackroot Clan to fight by the Right of Theft.\n\nWhat we need to do is steal the general's bow back, and then we can release him from his vows.
Then we should begin.

We call it the Earth Forge. Merric found it on a contract a few years ago. The maintenance constructs had long since shut down. The ruin contains the most unique blacksmithing setup … even the basest of metals sing in its embrace.

In Mzeneldt, we saw visions of Ancient soldiers. Survivors of a strategic attack on a city of darkness. Abagarlas is that city, an ancient stronghold of Molag Bal. I expect we will learn much from those old stones.
The stench of magic issues from that fissure. I can smell it. And I can feel it through my skin!
Thank you very much. \n\nFortunately, I can translate the ancient Ayleid, and that should tell us how to close the portal.

Just scrape a bit off the top and … there. An old trick I learned living so long in this dreadful place. My friends thought it was funny to hide from me, so I'd use this to see them.\n\nIt also has an interesting side effect.

Touch the bark to a wisp of light and then cross the bridge. The runners are searching for the remaining soldier. When you spot a runner, follow him. He should lead you right to your friend.\n\nAnd if the effect runs out, just touch another wisp!
Merric is a big boy. He doesn't need Aelif padding around behind him, watching his every step.\n\nI look forward to seeing what he's discovered.
Aelif must blind you to take you to the forge … and now you ask her where you are being taken?\n\nPerhaps you do not understand the meaning of the word secret?
No! This is my imagination!

We must rely on the scenes of the past. After being poisoned, General Malgoth went to the Nereid temple. It's likely he died within.\n\nI suggest you go in and search for the general's remains. I'll continue searching for clues out here in the forest.
It means there's something down there, something bad. And it's after me, I'm sure of it. It knows that I'm special and it wants me.
Why does everyone keep saying that? Yes, I can smell it. There's an evil, magical sort of smell to it.
The kagouti gore the Hist to drink its sap. In the Hamlet, a Tree dies screaming. In the Mire, a Tree goes mad.\n\nThe guar watch the kagouti, but do not understand.
He keeps thinking he smells magic, evil magic, coming from the fissure. And he thinks something's after him, because he's "special." I think he's crazy.
You have spent your gold very wisely, sandwalker. Give me the scent and the lizard will be yours!\n\nAnd just like that, it's done! Safe travels!

Jahi would never believe such lies! But, if it's for her, I will give you a lizard for your scenting.\n\nThere, now you have it. Your lizard will find whoever has that rotten odor clinging to you. Or perhaps it's simply your disposition I smell?
Oh, please! Don't encourage him. The earthquakes upset everyone. And that fissure's been here for years. The rest of us have adjusted; why can't he?
The fissure appeared four years ago. Four years! I'm sick of hearing about how he senses things others don't, that he should have been a mage. Either he stops this madness or I'm leaving!
The kagouti think the guar won't bite off the tusk that strikes it. Now the kagouti are brought down to the mud.
The guar seeks reeds to fill its belly. A gully in which to wallow. These are what the guar needs.\n\nLeave conquest for the kagouti.
How fortunate for you. I shall enjoy observing how you go about accomplishing that particular miracle.
The mortal continues to speak to me. What does it want, I wonder?\n\nPerhaps if I ignore it, it will just go away.
Yes, we should be going. We must find Sees-All-Colors and inform her what has happened here. Lead on, comrade.
You have the right of it. I'll speak with the Provost Generals, and post some guards. If undead can come boiling up out of the mountain at any time, there's no telling what might happen here.
I do not know! Perhaps he somehow can track the core itself? If the Prince of Lies is planning to use the Vivicus once again, the Prismatic Weapon is a threat to his plots.
No, not just yet. We came so close! Don't worry, though. I can complete the final steps on my own. This weapon will yet see the light of day, mark my words. The Mortuum Vivicus will yet be destroyed.

Me? Not much. No one pushes Skordo around.\n\nBut the others? They chip away at rocks until they drop and get tormented by ogrims. Some even have their souls yanked out. Turns them into empty husks. I wouldn't wish that fate on an Elf!
<You removed the Gem.>
<You removed the Gem.>
<Nothing happens.>
<The holder warms as the keystone clatters into it.>

War Chief Yzzgol's plan worked! After you drew their soldiers away to the beach, we struck from the woods. The keep fell to our might and cunning. \n\nThe king and his vanguard fled. We gave chase. Now, the last weak knights flee before us.
The weakling king has fled deeper into the ruins. His vanguard is dead. His wife and daughter are our captives.\n\nYzzgol has declared they will not be harmed—for now.
He cowers in a room sealed by powerful wards. Pah! Bretons and their magic.\n\nTargoth, you should interrogate our prisoners. Perhaps one of the fools will betray their king!
Ha! You dictate terms, pig child? Give me back my sword and I'll give you a clean end.\n\nAsk your questions. Amuse me.
I will die before I betray my king!\n\nRelish victory while you can. One day, we will return to reclaim what's rightfully ours. We are done talking.
Knights? You mean, that you Orcs haven't slaughtered?\n\nWhy am I even speaking to you? Monster! I'll say no more.
Why threaten me? Our island is yours now. Spare us, spare our king, and let me lead the survivors into exile.\n\nYou have my word as a Priest of Arkay.
I am not afraid of death. You, however, should be. What has bloodshed gained you but pain and death?\n\nPray for Arkay's forgiveness, child. All you will get from me is pity.

Then hear me. Arkay compels me to break my silence.\n\nKing Renwic is desperate. He seeks an ancient power hidden in the ruins. Scrolls as old as the island whisper of a terrible weapon, an Ayleid relic.
It summons an undead army, one I fear he cannot control. That army is a crime against Arkay, and it will slaughter more than Orcs.\n\nI love my king, but you must stop him.
We have ears everywhere, Adept. An intelligence report fell into my hands that mentioned these tomes.

I don't know. It's always a delicious mystery, cracking open a book for the first time.\n\nThey could be anything from ancient recipes for stew to high arcana. Even racy journals penned by Elven poets!
No! You'll just murder him before he can save us. \n\nI won't let that happen. Father knows a secret power, one left by the Ayleids.
I am pleased to be able to lend you strength to face this enemy from your past.
By Mauloch's right hand! My Warcaller triumphs again. We will end this assault and the efforts of this cowardly king.
Then I will cut him down. Stay your blade beyond this door, Targoth.\n\nLeave King Renwic to me.
There's no honor in the slaughter of a broken people and defeated knights. If King Renwic surrenders, he will join his people in exile.\n\nLet them spread word of our ferocity across the seas!
One of Xohaneel's necklaces, I assume. And which one do you think matches my pragmatic outlook on life?
No, that isn't for me. That amulet belongs to someone who bravely attempts to negotiate agreements both within and outside our community.

Thank you. I deal with the hardships of coaxing food from this foul land. Without my dedication, who knows what my people would be eating.\n\nPlease, take this Gem of Endurance. You'll need it when you go to the top of the pyramid.
No, I can't take that. That amulet is meant for someone who maintains our hallowed traditions.
Of course. And which amulet do you think best matches my venerable nature?
And which of Xohaneel's baubles do you think matches my daring nature?
No, thank you. That amulet belongs to someone who demonstrates bravery and conviction when faced with unknown situations.
Thank you, but no. That amulet is meant for someone who patiently bears the brunt of this harsh land.

Thank you. My role here is to preserve and pass on the traditions of my people so that each generation never forgets where we came from.\n\nTake this Gem of Preservation. You will need it when you go to the pyramid's upper level.

Thank you. I need to be brave and resolute to negotiate not only with my own people, but with the sad and dangerous creatures that roam this twisted plane.\n\nHere, take this Gem of Courage. You will need it when you reach the top of the pyramid.
Thank you, but no. That amulet belongs to someone who works through hardships.
No, thank you. That amulet should go to someone who maintains our ways and traditions.
Shalidor! Labyrinthian's father, the Spellmirror's forger. Are you speaking truly?\n\nAnd uh … this book's pages are blank. Why is it glowing?
Good. That means you understand the spirit of my people.
You must still complete the Trial of Body. Speak to An-Jeen-Sakka when you are ready to begin.
Very good, outsider. Now you must choose between eternal suffering or eternal death.

With you are two motes in the darkness. Khali and Shazah are the Lunar Champions, truly. One will go on to shine as brightly as Jone and Jode. The other will twist and rot and wither here in the corruption below Moonmont.

You are the Moon Hallowed. It's your destiny to make this choice. One will leave with you and walk the Two Moons Path. They will become the next Mane. The other will hold the Dark Mane in place here, and dwell forever in darkness.
He must pay for his crimes!

A wanderer much like yourself—a dour Dunmer fellow—passed through here. Bought supplies and headed straight into the moors, my warnings be damned. Seemed like he knew something.\n\nYou want to figure this out, I'd start by finding that Dunmer.

No, only the hunters. I manage clan affairs and the upkeep of the village. This was simpler before the forming of the Aldmeri Dominion. Valenwood is changing, and its people with it. I find my time occupied in dealing with the necessary adjustments.

All right. You're going to have to protect me though.\n\nThe chamber may be clear now, but as soon as I start the ritual, they'll realize it on the other side. They might try to charge through and stop us.
He's known as the Daedric Prince of Madness: the Mad God. \n\nThe Dunmer call him one of their Four Corners of the House of Troubles. And he's earned the title a thousand-fold.
You mean besides the obvious?\n\nWhen the dagger is fully charged, it drains life energy from its victim and transfers it to the wielder. That property has saved me on more than one occasion!
Yeah, well, this crisis transcends religious differences, don't you think? I want to secure the grove, you don't want Greenshade to be destroyed. Binding the Daedra is good for both of us.

The scholars believe that the Hist tree cannot continue as Molag Bal's slave. It withers away, but the crystal will not let it die.\n\nThis cruel existence, this terrible suffering—it must come to an end. Oblivion is preferable to eternal torment.
He was gone as quickly as he came. He was outfitted for battle, though that isn't strange for adventurers. But he walked as one who knows his goal, and will not be deterred.

The warriors believe that the Hist tree must survive, no matter the torments it is forced to suffer. The crystal must continue to sustain it, to keep the spark of life flickering despite the endless pain.\n\nLife is precious. The Hist must endure.

You disappoint me, outsider. Still, our tradition allows you to make your choice. It also allows me to challenge it.\n\nYou must defend your decision and prove the strength of your conviction by defeating our champion in combat.
The spirits of Daedra supply magicka to the wards. It's all very complicated.\n\nThe important thing is that you find Saromir and learn how to bind the Daedra permanently.
Then go to the challenge grounds and face our champion.\n\nBut know this. Our champion fights to end the Hist's pain and suffering. You cannot hope to overcome the strength of his conviction.
I knew you would understand. Tell An-Jeen-Sakka that the Hist tree's torment cannot continue. It is just too cruel to even contemplate.
Your conviction and certainty serve you well. So be it. The scholars will accept your decision.

I see. But our traditions allow a choice—any choice—to be challenged.\n\nYou must defend your decision by defeating our champion in combat. If you cannot uphold your conviction through battle, then how can you expect us to honor your decision?
Then go to the challenge grounds and face our champion.\n\nBut know this. Our champion fights to preserve a sacred life. You cannot hope to overcome the strength of his conviction.
A better decision. Tell the Treeminder that the Hist tree's life is sacred and it must be preserved.
Your conviction and certainty do you proud. Very well. The warriors will accept your decision.
Yes. They were very threatening. And when Halindor showed up, they attacked me. Dragged me down here. Ezreba apologized the entire time. She said she didn't want to be doing this.

Don't take him too lightly. Madness comes in many forms. Sheogorath encompasses them all.\n\nHe rules the Shivering Isles, but often takes an active interest in our world. That … usually doesn't end well.

Yes. An example of Sheogorath's "humor." There are those that find his madness amusing. I am not one of those people.\n\nThe Mad God would just as soon serve you an aged cheddar as he would flay the skin from your bones. Remember that.
I know only that the magic he summons will slaughter our army. Unless we stop him, every Orc here will die.
We must learn how to reach their cowardly king and the nature of his foul magic.\n\nMake these prisoners talk! We have confiscated their belongings. They may hold clues to what they know.

They must pay the blood price.

I took this charm off a Reachwitch. Hold it tight and order any guard to execute his prisoner. The charm will chain their soul and compel them to answer you.

You will have one question, Targoth. Ask wisely.
The Code of Mauloch is clear. So long as these Bretons aid their king in his foul magic, they remain our enemies.  \n\nIf you can coerce them through words alone, do so. If not ….
Don't steal. Don't attack without reason. Fight with honor. Protect your tribe.\n\nThese Bretons claim to have surrendered, but if they refuse to answer truthfully, they remain our mortal enemies.
