They aid their king in his foul plan to kill us all! Unless they tell us how to stop him, his magic will wipe us out.\n\nWe are at war, Targoth. Do what you must.
Perhaps. Come back here after you light the fires. I should have more information by then.
Alive? Good. That's good.\n\nWaves smashed me against the ship. Cracked a few ribs. Not the best feeling.
<Which gem will you place in the statue?>

All I know is what I saw with my own eyes. Hunters simply dropping their bows and wandering unarmed into the moors as if bewitched. Then their bodies turn up later, or what's left of them. Can't explain it.\n\nExcept ….

Strangely enough, several. They all reported an odd sensation that wasn't present before, as well as an apparent rise in hostile beasts in the area, but otherwise returned unscathed. \n\nIf this is some spell, maybe some are more resistant than others.
I can manage. Talking makes me cough up blood.\n\nSo I'll quit jabbering.
Tastes like sandals boiled in mint perfume.\n\nBut if it knits my ribs, I'll drink the whole bottle.
Good. I'll find <<1>>.\n\nGo. Get them back safe.
<<1>> pulled me ashore. Went to find shelter. Never came back.\n\nHeaded to a nearby cave. Find him. Tell him we're all safe.
<Which gem will you place in the statue?>
<Which gem will you place in the statue?>
Terrified, are you? Ha! You should be.\n\nOur king is a mighty sorcerer. Even now, he summons an undead army from the depths of these ruins. Flee while you can, Orc! Leave our island!
He told me to die valiantly and take as many of you with me as I could. See the bodies stacked around us? I have done my duty.\n\nMy king is beyond your reach. We are done talking.

Our ship's hold was packed full of an old Bosmer healing remedy. The labels say <<1>>, but marines call it glow juice.\n\nThe wreck scattered bottles across the beach, must be what brought out the alits.

No fear. Bravery, or foolish inexperience? I cannot trust one who could become enthralled at any moment. \n\nProve to me you have the will to resist this foul magic. Find me at the lair up the hill east of here. Then I shall consider it.

I have hunted them all my life, and yet I have never seen magic such as this. I do feel their touch upon it. I feel it testing my will with every step I take. \n\nBut I shall not falter. I shall face these creatures and leave nothing but ash behind.

Squat creatures made of teeth, claws, and endless hunger. I've heard their cries up and down the beach since I came to.\n\nTheir sweet-tooth is bigger than their walnut brains. I saw one of the stupid things swallow a whole bottle of glow juice.
She's alive? I suppose that's some luck amidst all this wreckage.\n\nCan't say the same for my leg. If I don't put too much weight on it I can manage a good hobble.
The gods give us pain to test us. Or amuse themselves. Either way, I'll deal with it.
Blessings upon you, stranger. I'll limp my way inland and find a safer place to wait for <<1>>. Just knowing she's out there gives me hope for the rest.

<<1>> dragged me out of the water. He'll want to know <<2>> and the rest of the squad are all right. Think he said something about looking for shelter in a nearby cave, but I was still coughing up sand.
Glow juice? By the gods, it just might! Soon as I can stand on my own, I'll head inland.
Oh, Renwic, forgive me.\n\nThere are crystals in braziers by the door. Turn them to lower the wards. Now please, spare our daughter.
Visanne? No. She's just a child! You cannot kill our child!
Ayleid crystals impart memories directly to the reader. Overuse leads to a problem of capacity for most mortals.
Yes, and since you have succeeded in stealing it, it falls on you to invoke the Right of Theft with the general.\n\nWhatever you ask him, he will be compelled to do.
I'll use the combined powers of the books and wrench the isle back to Tamriel. Sheogorath has lost, adept. We're almost there.
Willing or unwilling, all who strive to grow in skill and scope are my servants.
Why? So you can torture the incantation out of them? Kill me if you must, Orc, but I'll not betray my countrymen.\n\nPray Arkay forgives your violent ways. I will not.

I saw her swept overboard in that damned storm. Held onto the rigging long as I could, but it tore the skin off my palms. If I can't hold a weapon, I'm useless to my squad.\n\nDo you have any bandages? I lost my kit to the sea.
Hope they appreciate their good fortune when you find them.\n\nI can get inland, after I rest. Fight with purpose.
I can manage. I wasn't holding the rope with my feet. \n\nWhat about you? What's your plan?
You should let <<1>> know. He spit in fate's eye when he pulled me from the water. Said he saw a cave nearby and was going to look for shelter.
Glow juice? Used to think this stuff was only good for practical jokes on snowy days.\n\nOnce I can heft Spleen-shanker, I'll push through the beach and find <<1>>. How about you?
My memory is as unerring as my word. In the crystal behind you rests knowledge you did not know you sought. Others have killed for such wisdom.
What else? Power. They called it the Heart of Valenwood, but no matter what it's called, it means the same thing.
Hurt me? You'll hurt us all if Father doesn't stop you.\n\nI'm not afraid of you, Orc! I'm not.
You beast! Mother is a queen! You can't …. Please, don't hurt her!\n\nYou turn the crystals by the door. That is how you open it. Now please, don't kill my mother!
By your command, he will pay the blood price.

Try eating a canis cap mushroom. It's supposed to mask your scent or something. Wolves won't attack you. Or so I hear. I just stay away from wolves.\n\nOr you can kill wolves until you find Thane Oda. But that won't end well if you want her help.

No. This pathetic being is hardly even worthy of my blade. \n\nThe one I followed here is called Faenir; a much more formidable foe than this maggot, I assure you. We shall meet him soon enough. He and all of his coven shall die.
I cannot refuse. Make your question count, pig child.
What is he… planning? Ha! He is planning to kill you all!\n\nAll that trouble just to ask me something I would have told you when I was alive! See you in death, pig child.

No… I won't… There are two runestones by the door. Turn them both, and the ward will lower. King Renwic is inside. He raises an undead army to destroy you.\n\nThere. You've made a traitor of me. Now unbind me, cursed Orc!
Hiding? Ha. He hides through the door you'll never open, plotting a doom you cannot avoid.\n\nYou killed me for this? Fool. I look forward to seeing you die.

Yes, he was the loudest of the supporters along with Athraedal and Lathriel. I saw them speaking with the veiled one often. They'd never listen to me. You'll have to go through them if you want to reach the skull. \n\nNow please, just let me go.
Let me answer your question with one of my own. Do you know of Dementia and Mania?
"Uncle Robier's Vegetable Garden" was … surprisingly calming. But read into the subtext and things quickly become dark. It's the tale of a plantation.
Auri-El make me truthful, I think so. Sheogorath speaks madness and breaths insanity, but when a Daedric Prince strikes a deal they … tend to keep their word.
By your command. Let her pay the blood price.

The Shivering Isles, the Oblivion realm you've been exploring on Sheogorath's mad errands, is primarily divided into two spheres. \n\nIn Mania, the colors are brighter than bright. Beautiful flowers bloom, and creatures skitter through the underbrush.

Dementia has dark shadows, overcast skies, and snarling beasts. Dark stone and rattling chains. That's why I'm so tired, adept. Last night my dreams were of Dementia, and the Chateau of the Ravenous Rodent.
Even in death you torment me! Ask, and be done with it!
Just as I told you. My husband is casting a spell to wipe you out.\n\nYou murdered me for this? You'll reap what you sow. Oblivion take you!

There are two runestones by the door. Turn them both to lower the ward. My husband is inside. His ritual will raise an undead army to defeat you.\n\nWe didn't start this war. The death of your people is on your hands. But please, spare my husband.
In the center of the ruins, behind the door you cannot open. \n\nThere. I have told you what you asked! Now unbind me, cursed Orc!
Well, think about it. He didn't have to give you any of the books if he didn't want to. \n\nIf he's gone this far with his little game, why would he stop now?
The book describes a well-appointed guesthouse. A beautiful maze, where you can while away the afternoon. And a sprawling manse with rooms upon rooms.\n\nMake of that what you will.
It will be done. Let her pay the blood price.
You are damned in the eyes of Arkay. Ask your question and be done with it.
The king uses a weapon of ancient magic uncomprehended by Breton or Orc. All will die.\n\nNow, by Arkay, release me!

To open the chamber, turn both runestones by the door. The king is in the center of this ruin. He seeks an Ayleid Relic that will raise an undead army. It will destroy everyone.\n\nNow, unbind my spirit!
King Renwic is in the center of the ruins. He will put an end to you. Arkay will remember the death you've brought and repay you in kind.\n\nNow be gone!
Very well, Warcaller. The child will pay the blood price for her crime.

My father told me, "You will find your bow in an animal's bone. Before it's even carved, you will see it." Mammoth's tusk—extraordinarily difficult to make a good bow out of—but it was just like he said. I saw it and I knew.\n\nWhat do you want?
Heh. Death plays tricks. I thought you said "leave." But that's not possible. We don't deserve rest. Not after what happened here. The Ooze is the only fitting place for us.
My army is loyal even deep within death, deep within the Ooze. They would march against the sun if I commanded it. They will march against Naemon.
Cruel beast! Father will make you pay for what you've done.
He's going to defeat you! He'll avenge me, avenge everyone. He'll use the magic in this ruin to wipe you all out.\n\nYou'll die, too. You can't stop him.

The runestones. You must turn the runestones on either side of the door to open it. Father told me… oh Father. I'm so sorry.\n\nHe hopes to raise an army of undead Ayleids. He wanted to use it to defeat you. Now please. Let me go.
He is just beyond that door, but you'll never open it. It's warded, and you didn't ask how.\n\nI hope he destroys you all. I hope he sends you to Oblivion!

You don't really expect me to answer that, do you little mortal?\n\nNeedless to say, it amuses me to bide my time here and observe your plight. No need to concern yourself about my safety, though, for the lesser Daedra will not harm me.
Even if I cared to explain myself to you, I doubt that you would understand. The politics of Oblivion are much too convoluted for your primitive mortal mind to comprehend.

I will not hinder you, dear mortal. Consider that to be help enough for now.\n\nKnow this, however. The exit from this place is currently … unavailable. I suspect you will rectify that in the very near future.
Oh, yes! Watching them has been very entertaining. They struggle in a web they cannot see and it makes me laugh.\n\nYou mortals! So easy to manipulate and so much fun to play with.
<You press the thunderbug bellies and hive seeds into the husk. The thunderbug bellies burst into flame and ignite the hive seeds.>

<You squeeze the dew bugs and thunderbug bellies into the husk. The thunderbug bellies ignite. This causes the dew bugs to pop, releasing their collected water, which immediately extinguishes the thunderbug fires.>
<You push both the hive seeds and dew bugs into the husk. The dew bugs begin to eat the hive seeds. Soon after, the dew bugs expand and pop. The seeds flower and grow out of the exploded insects.>

Up the road behind me is our guest quarters. But, silly me! All three rooms are already occupied. Frankly, they've overstayed their welcome.\n\nOne of them, though. Hoo! Just not fitting in. Could you do me a favor? Could you tell them to shove off?
What do you mean?
Some kind of sacrifice? This is too big for my squad to handle. We need reinforcements.\n\n<<1>> spotted a beached ship nearby. It looks intact, and she spotted Dominion sailors aboard.
First a hurricane blows out of nowhere and destroys our fleet. Then an able-bodied Dominion marine is captured and tortured to death?\n\nWhat else was in that cave?

The Black Daggers are the local gang. They use Capstone Cave to the northeast as a base. They don't generally cause trouble, as long as I keep the food and drink coming.\n\nJust a few broken dishes here and there.
<The armor bears the insignia of an Aldmeri Dominion marine lieutenant. His corpse is soaked in blood as if from many shallow cuts. Greenish foam mingles with the smeared blood.>

We need to combine our forces and find who murdered <<1>>. My squad and I need to pull his body out of that damned cave.\n\nWould you warn the sailors on that beached ship? They need to know it's not safe to wander around.

Why do I need a reason for everything? Mortals, mortals, mortals! Always needing a reason to do things.\n\nFor example: people like to think light chases away the shadows! I prefer to think that without a few lights, there'd be no shadows to enjoy.
The hurricane killed hundreds of marines. Why does it matter if one of them died in a cave?
Unless they're sporting Dominion armor as a fashion statement, I'm afraid so.\n\nIf my assistant had half a brain, he would have let himself be captured rather than lead the Aldmeri troops back here.
Well, we are at war, and an enemy army this deep into our territory would be a very bad thing.\n\nI would hate to think I destroyed the Daggerfall Covenant … of course, it was really Stibbons' fault.

I suppose that's a reasonable question. As you might imagine, the Elves have locked the main entrance to the portal room.\n\nThere is a back way, however, through an old prison of some sort. The pillars unlock the door into the prison.

Stubbed their toes, eh? Never understand why they fight in sandals.\n\nUntil the leaks are patched, our hold will take on water. Oh, and our <<z:1>> cracked in the storm. Locate a replacement in the wreckage and I'll have a sailor pick it up.

And I'm sure they'll be as useful as they were in the hurricane.\n\nShould they care to prove otherwise, they're welcome to do actual work patching leaks in the Prowler's hold. Maybe they can locate a replacement <<z:1>> in all this wreckage.
This skull tethers Blackheart to the living world, and shields him from death. As long as it remains, so too, does he.
Those pirates are a stick in the High Elf eye! They capture our merchant ships and raid our settlements.\n\nIf I had any say, we'd negotiate with a sword at their throats!
Not as long as <<c:1>> confuses diplomacy with capitulation!\n\nHe's inside with the rest of them, pretending this won't end in bloodshed. Go, see this farce for yourself!

My researchers in High Rock gave me the essential background. Salas En was an Ayleid stronghold, built by human slaves in the Merethic Era. \n\nThe Elves eventually got what they deserved during the Yokudan colonization of Hammerfell in the First Era.
Sure, talking's easier than working.\n\nWell? Ask.
Good! I know where Blackheart Haven is. Saw it on my last trip out. Be damned tough to get in there I suspect but I think I could probably do it.
And I told him, the mere act of doing so would complicate matters with our long-time Maormer allies. They take great offense to the Dominion's claims upon our island.
By all rights, this is our island! <<1>>'s people occupy it with our blessing.\n\nIf she breaks the treaty, so breaks our truce. We'll take back our island, and the Khajiit will pay the price.
We keep our copy on an island far from here. I see no reason to send for it. I won't allow High Elf wharf-rats another chance to take our rightful lands!\n\nWhy don't you bother <<1>> for her copy?

Look around you. What great armies do you see? Our survival depends on knowing when to fight, and when to please.\n\nThe treaty brought us prosperity for generations. I will not be the one to break it.

Then there's little chance for compromise. I'll call a break in formal talks until everyone calms their nerves.\n\nYou understand the stakes, yes? It's why I ask you to take a more active role in locating the treaty. I don't do so lightly.

I can't allow the Dominion's first act on <<1>> to be one of conquest.\n\nI understand our mutual friend prefers the rum served at a nearby tavern. Perhaps he would have ideas on securing a copy of the treaty.
<<1>> certainly won't—his viper tongue is sharp. But <<2>> can't, because her copy was stolen.\n\nIt only takes three drinks to loosen the tongue of a Chancery clerk, if you were curious.

The pragmatist in this one says it's because you have no firm connection to the Dominion. The optimist says it's because you have proven yourself more than capable already. When you have the treaty, meet both of us at the bridge.
<<1>> is certainly being watched by the Maormer. You should inform him the treaty is safe. He will know what to do next.
<<1>> and <<Ac:2>> are being put up in the armorer's home.\n\nEr, this one recommends you knock before entering. Green Lady gets jumpy at silent approach.

Eh? You don't know about the haven? What kind of a sailor are you? It's the privateer city, the black heart of the sea, home to Captain Blackheart himself. People been looking for it as long as I can remember and I found it, by accident even.
Go ahead and use the boat behind me. I'll get you there.

I suppose so. Promise me you're not out to join that bunch of sea wretches though. They're a horrible lot and I won't be party to helping them. You got it? If you're going, you're going to rob them blind or put a dagger in them.
High Elves are known to cut off their ears to spite their face. Who would be a better example of such hubris than <<1>>, puffed up lackey to <<2>> himself!
I want you to meet the family! So many fond memories. There was that one time, with the scalpel? And all of our family dinners, hah!\n\nAnd of course, you'll get to play with the family heirlooms!

It's quite fascinating really. It would seem to prove that the Altmer and the Ayleids were still connected further into the Merethic Era than we believed.\n\nI actually wrote a book on the subject. Well, someone wrote it for me, but who's counting?

Because this slimy Maormer had a hand in <<Ac:1>>'s murder! We should march on their embassy and put it to the torch this very moment\n\nOh, never mind. It's like I'm speaking to a ship's mast. Do continue your "investigation," would you?

Look for hampers with clothes, or kill a Sea Drake and take theirs. Put on their clothes and you'll look just lovely.\n\nOh, do watch out for the Sea Drakes with torches. They're not drunk. If you get too close, they'll spot you and alert the others.
Yes. This one is pretty famous. Perhaps you have heard of Zur? But Zur must tell you. This soul-meld is killing us. Will you help us? Will you unmeld our souls?

Spoilsport. Suffice it to say that old Uncle Leo has quite the history with the ladies.\n\nEver since his last lady love, he's preferred the company of squeakers to speakers. And I turned him into a Flesh Atronach.

Ahh, a mortal after me own heart. Well, Uncle Leo was quite the ladies' man back in the day. He had a beauty in every town, from Windhelm to Stormhold. \n\nAs the years went by and his looks began to fade, it got harder and harder to … y'know.

Right. Well, not getting the attention of the ladies, the way he used to … it started to drive Leo a little bit batty. \n\nAnd that's when I stepped in. Can't have someone as well loved as Leo all lonely, right?

Cheese for the smart skeever! Leo couldn't resist her. Thought he'd have an out on our deal if they got married. Nope!\n\nHis flesh melted like wax on his wedding night. Became an Atronach of my very own. Now? All his girlfriends are rats.

Unmeld is so too a word!\n\nPardon. The Dwarven device that caused this is inside the laboratory, but rubble blocks the way. Collect Zur's notes and a bottle of pearl tincture. With those, this one can make a potion that will get you past the rubble.

That's what the Maormers called them as they brought them ashore. They're attracting the serpents to the island.\n\nWhen I saw the crew carrying the horns into the caves, I gave chase only to be captured.
I'm well enough to help you put a good bleeding to these Maormer bastards.\n\nJust destroy the horns. If more of those serpents come ashore, we won't hold long.
It's a lush place, gorgeous and vibrant. We have guild members poised across Tamriel, ready to join us there. It will be the perfect place for the guild to study in peace. It will be glorious.
I believe so. I'm sure you're as sick of the Mad God's games as I am. \n\nNow come. I will perform the ritual and open a portal to our new home.

I know you said you were sorry, but the question has been asked.\n\nOne of us is disorganized and enjoys experimenting with Dwarven machinery. The resulting explosion reduced the entryway to a pile of rubble and sent our supplies in all directions.
Safe enough. We'll make our way to the entryway. We can manage a simple illusion to mask our presence. I wish we weren't so weak, however. I never realized ….

A few of us arrived together, but only the alchemist and I survived the experiments. Zur's explosion had one desirable side effect—it destroyed our Dremora captors. We have information vital to the Mages Guild, should we escape this predicament.

I never realized how my ability to perform magic defined me. Now that I cannot do the things that once came so easily to me, I almost don't know who I am. Having a talking cat inside my head doesn't help much, either.
I'm whatever I wish to be. I change bodies like High Elves change clothes, though the corpses in this temple limit my wardrobe.\n\nWhat does it matter to you? Why do you trespass?
Set foot in this temple and see for yourself. Such commendable posture! I could definitely wear you in the autumn.\n\nAs for <<1>> … he's fit for display under full moons or new.

No—the quartermaster said missing, as in stolen.\n\nThese Maormer swarming all over the beach … Oblan thinks they got onto the Prowler somehow and stole the ship's sun-sighter. I think he believes they even had something to do with the shipwreck.

The Maormer are Sea Elves. They're pirates and raiders, and they've got no love for the Altmer.\n\nI've heard they have weather-shamans that can control storms, but that might just be legend. The quartermaster believes it, though.

He needs that sun-sighter. Without it, the Prowler can't do much more than hug the coast. I don't know much about navigation, but I believe Oblan. He and the rest of the Prowler's crew seem to know what they're doing.\n\nI'm glad we're helping them.

If the Maormer took it, you'll have to take it back. The Prowler's lookout says that most of the Maormer are clustered around one of the wrecked ships just off the coast. She thinks they took it there.\n\nGo to that ship and get the sun-sighter back.
The Maormer plan something, but what? Wait, the apothecary sold Daedra blood in these specific amounts? That would explain the strange liquid upon the …. Oh no. Bright moons, no.

This is a sample of the vile cloud from around <<c:1>>'s body. Bring it to <<Ac:2>>. Tell her it killed her beloved.\n\nAs for the rest, <<3>> will see what you found. We must move like Khenarthi herself is at our backs.
This isn't funny. I was all set to give you gold for helping us, but that's not going to happen now. Just go away and leave me alone.\n\nSpoil sport.
No poison in all of Tamriel could harm my beloved!\n\nBut … this scent was on his body. Why is it out here, as well? I can see it, leading away into the heart of this wretched city.
You're blind to it. Easily remedied.\n\nFollow, if you can.

I don't know a lot about it, but apparently it's something sailors use to navigate on the high seas. It uses the sun or the stars to show the ship's exact position. Without it, the Prowler can't sail out of sight of this island without getting lost.
I followed his orders. Daedric poison, for the Wood Elf and his mate. I followed his orders.
<<1>>. He said they could stop the tempest. Had to be removed.

The spirit of Rilis XII is imprisoned here. He was a madman, and the crimes he committed were such that, upon death, his son sealed his spirit here.\n\nRilis' magic was so powerful that the prince would not risk that death would stop his father.
To truly defeat him, we must slay him on Nirn. Otherwise, he will persist forever.\n\nAnd the fact that he has enthralled the Keepers has proven we can no longer risk his presence. In any form.

We are wardens of the Banished Cells, sworn to stand watch on Rilis XII. Our lives are tied to this place.\n\nEach Keeper was once a champion of Auridon, with titles, friends, and family. Now there is only our post. My friends have abandoned theirs.
My what?\n\nYou mean the apothecary? I assure you, he was never in my employ.

You're lying! She must be dead, or else she'd have come for me!\n\nShe's coming for me, isn't she? I … I'm a duly appointed ambassador of the Maormer people. The grounds of the embassy are sacrosanct, according to our treaty!
This does not excuse mindless slaughter! We are better than our enemies.\n\nYou must apprehend him. Don't let <<Ac:1>> cut him down like an animal! We must learn what the Maormer plan for <<2>>.
I trust you'll do what's best for my people.\n\nNow I must … apologize to <<1>>. Whatever the Dominion needs, we will provide.
Not long ago, Rilis attempted to escape. We fought him, and though we contained him, he nearly won.\n\nAfterwards, the Keepers turned to the same Daedric magic that Rilis used to match his strength.
I do! By all the gods, I do!
Praise the gods. Thank you! She was going to ….\n\nBind me, and I will leave for <<1>>'s judgment.
I'll keep him alive for a time. He won't starve. His limbs have so much flesh to sustain him.\n\nGo tell <<1>> the Maormer is dead. Leave me to my work.
Go. This is a private matter.

Another honored enemy we must send to <<Ac:1>>. Too many, today.\n\nNo matter. Before he fled to the embassy, <<2>> mentioned something about a "tempest." Did he say anything about this before he died?
I fear we'll learn soon enough.\n\nWhat a nightmare! I hope all dealings with our Dominion allies won't end this way.

<This damp bow has apparently been sitting beside the river for a while. The bow string is tied too tight and the shaft appears slightly warped, but it will have to do if you want to compete in the contest.>
Wait until I am in position. \n\nThen you must undo the final binding stone. He will emerge, and you will do battle. Fight well—you fight for all of Tamriel.
I will serve as Rilis' host. His spirit will take over my body. But he will be bound by my mortality. If I—we—are killed, Rilis will die. \n\nFrom there, it's straight to Oblivion for him.

So I offered him a little deal. I gave him back his looks, his youth. All he had to do was promise never to bed a maiden more than once! Simple, really, and he took the deal with gusto.\n\nHeh heh heh. Then, a few years later, he meets Mjoll.
I said I'd consider it. <<1>> is the only one who can make that call.

Barnacles on the arse. They're all Sea Elves—"Maormer," they call themselves. Nothing more than pirates, if you ask me.\n\nSome say they have a connection to the water itself, but it's a lie. Anyone can learn weather magic like they do.
<<1>> uses it to navigate. I could tell you how the sun and stars show the ship's exact position, but none of it matters while it's in the Sea Vipers' hands.
Do you think I take drinks from strangers?

What a ridiculous question! I am the Great Mage's essence of health. \n\nThe Daedra captured Vanus. They planned to use him to power the Great Shackle. To prevent this, Vanus divided his essence into three fragments.
What? Give it here!

No. We've gone to great pains to keep Razum-dar's plan secret. \n\nThe spy must believe that Ayrenn is really here. There've been rumors that the Maormer plan to raid us, so we've put word out that the queen has come to make sure the city's safe.

Yes. Mad as the cat may be, his plan might actually work. \n\nThe story is that the queen wants to "personally" investigate the old Imperial Underground. You'll escort her there to meet Asteril—a Thalmor officer we suspect may be a spy.

As soon as Sanodil gets the spell right and turns your friend into a queen. Assuming this works, you and Razum-dar should leave for the Imperial Underground straight away.\n\nOh. Here we go now. It's about time.

Ha! The cat didn't tell you, did he? No, we can't send any guards. We don't know who we can trust. \n\nHe thinks the two of you can handle it though. I don't know if I'd call that confidence or foolhardiness, but I hope Baan Dar is with you either way.
The pride of the Long Coast. We'll sail for the Dominion as long as they pay us to raid enemy shipping.
Jone and Jode, don't let the captain hear you say that.\n\nPirates steal and pillage for themselves. We're privateers, so we do it for whoever pays us. A crucial distinction!
Yes, I can sense its reinvigorating presence. Give it back to me and I shall free myself.\n\nFollow my light to the slave quarters. Then we can recover our essence of stamina.

<<1>> took over the Prowler a few years ago. She's smart, cunning, and deadly dangerous when provoked.\n\nShe's also luckier than anyone I served. Every ship in the fleet smashed to flinders on <<2>>. Every ship but the Prowler.
Good luck. Do me a favor? If you find them before I do, tell them the ocean hasn't killed me yet.

I suspected as much. As soon as the horns went quiet, the serpents fled back into the sea.\n\nOnce that happened, the rest of the Maormers broke, either surrendering or running wildly back into the sea.
I sell no poison. Check the ledger inside, I beg you!

Pick your champion, then watch their deathmatch from the comfort of the balcony. Why not enjoy the death and carnage with a cold ale in hand? What could be more pleasing?\n\nNow, who will you bet on? <<1>>? Or <<2>>?

I think so. I can still feel the spell tugging at my mind, though. Just in case, Kireth and I are going to our camp outside of the ruins.\n\nBut I'm worried about the others. Since the spell doesn't seem to affect you, can you look for Lady Laurent?
Who can say? She has tried to warn troublemakers off in times past, before <<1>> can get his claws on them.
Yes, adept. I recovered quickly after you left. I'm just … I'm feeling a little weary. This business with the books you've been collecting.  It's taken a lot out of me.

These books are like word labyrinths. There are layers of meaning upon meaning, endless research avenues. He's laden these things with oblique references that only someone with my mastery of lore would be able to understand.\n\nIt's very tiring.
This one does not know and she does not want to know. <<1>> makes troublemakers and debtors disappear. Khaba is not so curious about their fate that  she would risk sharing it.

Like I said, just a little weary. Don't worry adept. I'm up to the challenge. I'm one of only a handful of people in the whole of Tamriel that could have puzzled these out, in fact! \n\nWe'll see it done.

Normally we've got plenty of contracts and odd jobs. But right now our new guildmaster, Sees-All-Colors, has all of us working one job. One giant job.\n\nWe're out hunting Daedra and wrecking those damnable Anchors.

Once you go through the portal, the token will attune itself to the access point. If you get lost, use the token and it will return you to the portal.\n\nWhat was once a curiosity that won me fortune and acclaim is now a vital tool in our mission.

Ha!  I knew you had steel in your blood. Welcome to the guild, Associate. \n\nNow get out there and slay some Daedra.  If you do a good job, there'll be a fat reward and maybe even some special assignments for you when you return. Walk with Mauloch.

Ha! Are you joking?  I'm practically dragging in drifters off the street - anyone who can lift a sword. What we're up against is… well frankly it's unbelievable. We need strong, seasoned fighters like you.\n\nSo what do you say?  You in?

You haven't seen one yet?  Feels like they're everywhere these days.\n\nBasically a huge chain comes thundering straight out of Oblivion, hits the ground, and starts pouring out Daedra. Mauloch's teeth - I'd never seen the like till recently.

The Dominion relies on <<1>> for his sound judgment. He's taught countless students the ways of magicka, including some of the Queen's own advisors. His role in the invasion is paramount for our future success.\n\nIf anything were to happen to him ….
The Guild is an organization dedicated to the pursuit of knowledge. We travel the width and breadth of Tamriel, seeking out books, tomes, and ancient scrolls.

Excellent! I hearby grant you the rank of Student in the Mages Guild.  Welcome to the fold. From now on every book you find and every book collection you complete, will enhance your reputation with the guild. Walk with Julianos, my friend.

In a manner of speaking, yes. We seek out knowledge of every kind, store it in our libraries, and make copies for distribution across Tamriel.\n\nWe leave the business of wars and petty disputes to others. The pursuit of wisdom is our only concern.

Guild members in good standing earn the opportunity to buy special items only available to members of our circle. \n\nWe also have special tasks that crop up from time to time for those with a thirst for adventure.
Thank you. We should keep moving.

Excellent. I'm delighted that you've brought them to us.  You're well on your way to membership in the Mages Guild already! We reward collections like yours. In fact, knowledge and study are our primary pursuit!
Why, I am. I'm <<1>>! I see your "Dominion" teaches you nothing of my people.\n\nI shouldn't bemoan your ignorance. You fools ended centuries of captivity when you removed the Mourning Stone.

Yes! We tirelessly pursue all manner of books and scrolls.  The Guild doesn't care about wars, battlefields, or boundaries: just knowledge. Any you acquire will improve your reputation with the Mages Guild.

Excellent!  I hearby grant you membership in the Mages Guild, with all the responsibilities and privileges thereof. Every book you find, and every book collection you complete, will earn you reputation in the guild. Walk with Julianos, my friend.

We can teach you special spells and abilities only available to members. And from time to time projects crop up for guildmembers with ambition. Who knows? You might attract the attention of Mistress Valaste or Guildmaster Vanus.

Oh, I believe I'll keep him. At least until my summoning ritual wears him through.\n\nYou see, undead are all so … beige. But I'm willing to adorn myself with hundreds of tawdry outfits in order to collect the more colorful garb at <<1>>.
Who can say? Dulan never sees them again. Now, go. This one has races to run.

Oh, of this I am sure. But if <<1>> heard about this … well. The boss doesn't mind drinking, and he has a certain patience for owing … but drunks that owe a lot of coin tend to disappear. They are hard on the peace and bad for business.

Never mind that accursed blue rock. I'm about to restore my wardrobe to its full glory.\n\nBehold this <<1>> fellow. Such vibrancy! I could use more like him, but one must be willing to run through a bolt of silk for the finest coat.
Sweet and salty in a stew? Hmm. That is not a bad idea! Good luck finding this Tand. Dulan must try this new recipe!
Who can say? Dulan never sees them again. Now, this one has answered your questions. Tell him the secret of your recipe!
You have three fine reptiles to choose from. Pick one to win. First across the finish line gets the prize! Which do you choose?
Yes. There we will find out the truth about this Thalmor Officer, Asteril. She's quite the beauty, I'm told. But traitors are never what they seem, yes? \n\nThis one is … no, I am ready when you are.

Yes! Bunul likes your style. The game is simple. You must run the course and beat the other runners to the finish line. Each of you will carry three spikeballs. These you can use to throw at your opponents, to stun them and slow them down.
Fine, fine. Come back when you find some courage, yellow-tail.
Only my pride. But we have a more pressing matter.\n\nAs <<1>> sensed my thoughts, I could sense his. He plans to overwhelm and enslave <<2>> with an undead horde by the next dawn!
<<1>>'s men were chasing him. I have never seen such an athlete! This one thinks a spikeball or two would have served him well.
Spikeball? No. He was terrible at spikeball.
Ezreba is good friends with Gonlas! She was just dropping in on him. No harm done. \n\nAhem. Ezreba will be going now.
<<1>> was a powerful Maormer wizard who learned to separate his spirit from his body, even in death. He can "wear" hundreds of mindless forms at a time.\n\nThankfully, I know his weakness.

The Mourning Stone's endless water supply tied <<1>>'s spirit to his body. When <<2>> removed the Mourning Stone from the temple, he set <<1>> free.\n\nOnce again, <<2>>'s sloppy methods nearly cause the death of me.
These gems focus the Mourning Stone's power. <<1>> had me remove them from his tomb.\n\nI propose <<2>> recovers the Mourning Stone from <<3>>. Meanwhile, we restore <<1>>'s prison. Simple enough.
Yes. Speak with the Archmage. He's meditating on the challenges ahead. I'm still somewhat … drained from my efforts, so he'll open the portal to the Shivering Isles for you.
I'm so glad you asked! On the surface it's a simple book of nursery stories from the Dunmer land of Stonefalls. But that's just on the surface.

So much more! Each story has hidden meanings. Clever references to arcane lore, twisting and turning into the depths of history. It was fascinating to fully unlock the secrets of the book.\n\nSheogorath may be a madman, but he's also a genius!
Not much. We tried to scry into Oblivion, to get a sense of the place. \n\nI couldn't see anything, but I was swept up in a strong sense of homesickness.

I came of age where most High Elves do: the beautiful green shores of the Summerset Isles. I often think of the pink petals and soft breezes of my homeland.\n\nI'm not sure why those memories returned to me today, though.

Of course, adept. While investigating some ruins for me you caught the notice of Arch-Mage Shalidor, ancient patron of mages everywhere. We're working with him to complete the Mad God Sheogorath's trials and recover Shalidor's lost sanctuary.
Adept, what transpires between myself and the Archmagus is between us and no one else. I don't need to answer your questions or anyone else's.
<<1>> is too important for the Dominion to lose. Besides, we both saw how the summoning ritual weakened my master.
Thank you. I should prepare myself.
Then it's decided.
And he calls me stubborn.\n\nAll right.

That's madness. I've experienced so many summers. My greatest accomplishment was watching <<1>> blossom into someone who'll far surpass my own deeds.\n\nNo, she must recover the Mourning Stone. You and I should confront <<2>>.
Then we should waste no more time.
Then I'll respect her choice, no matter how much I disagree with it.
Please, help me convince <<1>>! I will gladly seal myself in the tomb to spare my master. <<2>> is a threat to all on this island.
It's an heirloom. My Lord is quite fond of it. Has a bit of magic around it, too, I think. \n\nI don't know. I don't question Lord Sheogorath.
We of the Mages Guild are dedicated to the pursuit of wisdom, of knowledge. Wars and petty disputes hold no interest for us outside of academic curiosity. Are you interested in becoming a Docent?

Congratulations! I hereby grant you the rank of Student in the Mages Guild, along with the responsibilities and privileges thereof. Every book you acquire, or collection of books you help to complete, will now earn you status among us.

Docents bring rare texts of all sorts to us, so that we may expand our libraries. In exchange we offer them access to buy items which are restricted to guild members, as well as the occasional special task for those who are willing.

Fascinating… we have been looking for this for some time!\n\nYou're well on your way to earning membership within the Mages Guild, just in bringing this to our attention. The Guild provides great rewards when a Docent acquires books for our library.
I do not know the mechanism myself. But Saromir—the caretaker of the Vault of Memories inside the Cradle of Ilmyris—he'd know. If he's still alive.

Congratulations! I hereby grant you the rank of Student in the Mages Guild, along with the responsibilities and privileges thereof. Every book you acquire, or collection of books you help to complete, will now earn you status among us.
Docents earn reputation by bringing in rare texts for our library, and as your reputation grows it comes with greater and greater rewards.\n\nAre you interested in joining the Mages Guild?
You'll have to excuse me. I make it a policy not to discuss what guests have come to the caravan or what they do here. We value the privacy of our clients, you know.

Ah. I understand. I'd like to help but … you know, perhaps some of the games-runners may have seen him. If you were to speak to them, maybe spend some coin, perhaps they may recall this kitten. It's what I'd do, if I were you.

I was afraid you'd say that. Then all we know for sure is that the stony bastards are coming from the ground. \n\nI was thinking of trying to collapse their holes, but I need someone to defend me while I do it. What you say? Are you up for it?
No idea. We took it from a temple near the coast. The place was full of artifact, if you're into that sort of thing.
And I need a new rigging and a serving wench. Too bad for us both.\n\nNow get off my deck before I throw you off.
Well, that's a serving wench.\n\nThree minutes. If my sailors see your hands where they shouldn't be, I'll keelhaul you myself.
Working. Our ship foundered, why don't you go help us out?

Oh. Well, the Prowler is like a hen in a wolf den until she's seaworthy again.\n\nMaybe your marines can prove they're more than two-legged cargo in shiny armor. If they pitch in, I'll consider reinforcements. They up for it, or are they all talk?

The fork excites and synergizes magicka around it. When held in the hand of someone more notable than yourself, it can produce dramatic results.\n\nIn your hand, it might be suitable for conveying roast beef to your mouth.
Ahem. My lord visited with Korthor a very, very, very long time ago.\n\nReally, what do they teach mortals these days?
We'll show that old sea-cat what Dominion marines can do.
We're a little banged up, but we can still defend a beached ship from pirates. We'll show that old cat what Dominion marines are made of.
Wait, take this. I found some glow juice while I was looking for my squad, but they're on the mend. You'll get used to the taste.\n\nWe'll be along shortly. Watch yourself.
Good. The squad's wounds are slowing them down, but we'll be along shortly.

We're sailing for Daggerfall Covenant lands now. There's been action as well. A few days ago, the Aldmeri Dominion launched a surprise assault on Glenumbra.\n\nThey took Farwatch Tower along the coast, then swept down to attack the city.
The relic. After you turned it over, High King Emeric had the best minds in the Mages Guild examine it. They figured out how to turn it on the Dominion forces assaulting Daggerfall. It crushed them.

You should see Nicolene before you leave. Her brothers were there during the assault on Daggerfall. The Ayleid army appeared just before they would have been wiped out.\n\nI think she wants to thank you herself.

Hundreds. The Dominion force was completely routed, and many soldiers were saved, not to mention the residents of the city.\n\nThe relic burned out after one use, but the Dominion doesn't know that. They won't hit Daggerfall again anytime soon.

We're sailing for the Daggerfall Covenant now. Privateering is as profitable as ever, except now we're splitting the skulls of Elves as well. Lambur and her lot have all left, probably for the better.
Hardly. She couldn't raise enough money to buy her own ship. I offered to help, but she took that as an insult. I guess eight years of sailing together doesn't mean so much.

Tell that to Nicolene. Her brothers died when the Elves assaulted Daggerfall. We repelled them, but hundreds died. The Elves and their mad queen are chewing us up everywhere you look.\n\nYou should probably leave before I hurt you.

I understand that the Aldmeri Dominion sacked Farwatch in Glenumbra, and we couldn't stop them. I understand they've sunk dozens of our ships in cowardly assaults.\n\nWith that relic, we could have stopped those attacks.
Haven't you heard? The Aldmeri Dominion launched an attack on Daggerfall. They took Farwatch Tower and made straight for the city.

It's ruined. One use was all it had, I think because of the tinkering by the king's mages. It was enough.\n\nMy brothers were on the beach. They were about to be overrun by the Elves when the relic saved them. Thanks to you, they lived.

High King Emeric used the relic you saved at Carzog's! His mages had been working on it since we delivered it, and they figured out how to activate it without feeding it souls.\n\nThe Aldmeri Dominion was crushed. It was a complete rout.
What's wrong? Both my brothers are dead. They died fighting the Dominion at Daggerfall, along with hundreds of others.

Don't try to confuse me. I've seen what the Elves are doing. Captain Kaleen and I have fought them across the seas. They are marauders and killers. They want all humans beneath their heel.\n\nGet out of here. Just go away.
The relic, you pox-blinded fool! If you hadn't destroyed it, the High King could have used it in our defense. We could have crushed the Elves and saved our soldiers. We could have saved my brothers.

Still without a ship, though sailing with Kaleen pays well enough. We're raiding for Fahara'jad now, even have a nice bonus for sinking those damned Elves.\n\nSoon I'll have enough to strike out on my own again.

Happy's a relative term, my dear. I'm no dog of the king, and I really don't care who wins this war, but so long as the covenant pays well, I see no harm in helping my countrymen.\n\nTelonil's working his magic. We won't be at this for long.
And why wouldn't I be? Captain Kaleen's new venture as a privateer for King Fahara'jad is making us all the gold we need. Who knew war could be so profitable?

Oh yes, and for reasons quite unfair to all parties involved. Best not to dig into it too deeply. Old memories.\n\nSuffice to say, Captain Kaleen does the killing and I do the counting. Of coins, I mean.
A reasonable question. If my fellows hadn't exiled me from the Summerset Isles, I suppose I might feel a bit conflicted.
Since Captain Kaleen took us to war against the Elves, life has been interesting. Thus far, none among us have fed the roots of the tree. Let's hope it will remain so.

We sailed on Daggerfall during the attack by the Elves, but we are not a warship. We carried supplies. There were a few close calls with High Elf mages.\n\nOne died from an arrow to the neck. Sithis smiled upon us both.
This one will not begrudge you that. Your heroism on Betnikh was impressive. Still, I can't say your choice was wise.

We disagree. This does not justify abandoning Kaleen. We have been through too much to split over such an issue.\n\nShe faces many enemies in this time of war. As her mentor, I will fight beside her until we both die.

Indeed. The Aldmeri assault on Daggerfall did nothing to ease her feelings. She still believes that relic could have been of use.\n\nEven if she is right, it needed to be destroyed. The power to consume souls should not exist.
There is no mystery. Kaleen is still my responsibility. She faces many enemies in this time of war.\n\nAs her mentor, I will fight beside her until we both die.
The war. I have no love for High Elves, but I hope to take a berth elsewhere soon. As soon as Lerisa has gathered enough money to repair the Maiden's Breath, we will do just that.

Jakarn? Ha. Once I had him, there really wasn't much else to discuss. He's not a man you hold on to too tight, and honestly, it wasn't what I thought it would be.\n\nJust don't tell him that. Or Elethien, for that matter.
Oh, him. He left us in Daggerfall. Said he was going to strike out and start a cafe. Haven't seen him sense.\n\nDidn't care much for the man's taste in cooking. I imagine he's failed by now.
Well enough. I can't say I'm proud of how things ended with Kaleen, but it had to happen. It was time to find my own path.

Oh, she's loyal enough, so long as you do exactly what she says. The moment she thinks you've turned on her she'll gut you like a snake.\n\nI'm not interested in talking about Kaleen. Captain Marck is a bit rough, but I'm sailing with him for now.
Just once. She offered to "help me buy a ship." Can you imagine that? She kicks me off the Spearhead after eight years together and then has the nerve to tell me I can't cut it on my own.
Fine. Sailing for a Captain who doesn't think devouring the souls of hundreds of my people is an "acceptable loss." You could learn a thing or two from Captain Marck.

I'm certain you did. That doesn't make it any less horrible.\n\nDon't worry. I gave Captain Marck my word I wouldn't stab anyone in their sleep. If we're going to sail together, though, you'd best stay out of my way.
This and that. One thing I'll say about wartime—there's never been a better chance to get rich. I've made more in the past few weeks than I made the year before we met.

Let's not use harsh language. I've liberated certain objects from people who really don't need them anymore. Where's the harm?\n\nA word of advice, though. If you see any contracts from a group called The Midnight Union, I'd stay away.

One never tells, my good looking friend. Let's just say I learned enough about them to know that it wasn't somewhere I wanted to be.\n\nCaptain Marck, by comparison, is my kind of scoundrel. We're going to work well together.

Their leader is mad. I'll liberate some poor sap's purse as quickly as the next man, but murder and bloodshed is not on my agenda.\n\nIf you get a contract with them, tear it up and walk away, unless you want blood on your hands.

I joined Kaleen just to make Jakarn miserable, but I found I rather like the sea. It's not a bad life.\n\nI won't fight against my countrymen, but Captain Marck isn't involved in the war against the Altmer. I'm happy here.
The Aldmeri Dominion launched a surprise assault, hoping to knock the Bretons out of the war. It went horribly, mind you. That relic you procured slaughtered quite a number of my countrymen.

I wanted to study it, not turn it over to blind apes who would burn it out at the first sign of trouble.\n\nStill, a grudge is beneath me. I'm a scholar of history, and history will judge your actions.
I thought you would like to know the results of your careless actions. The Bretons, of course, did something to the relic. It's quite inert now. The fools destroyed it for good.

Quite well. I've not yet secured enough capital to launch another expedition, but Captian Marck has been quite generous since he discovered my talents as a mage.\n\nI've even had the opportunity to set a slaver ship on fire. Exciting work.
I was taking a nap, worked in the field today. I woke up to find that damned crystal … I'm sorry, I don't remember anything else.
Oh, you have no idea. The cool breezes, the soft petals. And above all, to be among other Mages. To have you all understand. It's amazing, adept. Thank you.

Hah! Old Vanus has been around so long, he knows pretty well everyone. Ayrenn, Emeric, even crust old Jorunn owe him favors. I guess that's what comes from living the better part of six hundred years.

Hah hah hah! Adept, do you know what my people think of Mages? They think Mages are outsiders especially good at enslaving or killing my kin. Orcs that cast spells? Cheaters and outcasts. But not here ….
Shor's bones, no! I've met more non-Nords in my time here than in my whole life in the Holds. But that's how it should be. Spells and research, lore and learning binding the Guild together!

I know it, adept. Mages are respected and, yes, feared in the Ashlands. Our time here will bring us closer to the other races. And we'll bring that back home, to our sometimes more … close-minded brothers.

Pah. The Black Marsh has been raided and burned by every type of pointy-eared Elf. By Imperials, by Bretons … even the cat-men. No, I don't believe this dream of equality for a second. At least I can get soul gems at a discount.

This one is impressed. The island is fragrant, the other Mages have proven themselves friendly … more or less. And there is much learning we can do in this place. This one hopes Eyevea survives, and endures.
Look around you, adept. My people live in paradise. Would you leave the soft petals, the southern breezes, the beaches of the archipelago?

A Greenspeaker is a Mage who has dedicated her life to working in and alongside the Green itself. We use our spells to guide and enhance the growth of trees and plants. We create furniture, weapons … even housing for our people.
Ahh, the Wabbajack. Maleel held it down in that dusty tomb for so long ….\n\nSay, why don't you clear its throat? Take it in hand and use it on some of these holier-than-thou temple types?
Comrade, the council has faith in you. I have faith in you … as does Stendarr. What you did, you did for the good of the guild, and all of Tamriel. I know they will support your choice.
Bera told us of Aelif's plan to hunt Sees-All-Colors. I see that Merric and the spirit of Jofnir Iceblade accompany you. Tell us, for all and the Eight to hear. What happened?

No need to worry your pretty mortal head. The Wabbajack, it unleashes the potential in everyone. The unrecognized essence of artistic beauty that swells and beats within the—\n\nLook, you want the book? Whack some folks with the Wabbajack!
Carrying out our sentence, punishment for her foul deed. And yet I notice that she still stands, hale and whole. Why is this?
Carrying out our sentence, punishment for her foul deed. She is not here … her sentence was carried out, then?
Undoubtedly it was the same person that assumed her likeness and attempted to assassinate the queen … er, Razum-dar. \n\nSpeaking of the cat, it seems he may have found something.
<This book contains a list of names dating back several years. The majority of the names are Breton. There are no Orc or Redguard names on the list.>

You and everyone else in this forest, it seems. My clan has already declared your allies to be trespassers. You don't want to know what we do to trespassers.\n\nThe Shadow Walkers will catch them. They always do.

Have you noticed the swords left near these campfires? I think your companions are trying to tell us something.\n\nI'm going to keep looking for them. If I can reach them before the hunters, they might just get out of this forest alive.
Vampires feed upon this essence and weaken it.\n\nKill the vampires and collect the energy they siphoned from me. Restore that energy to me and I can easily break free of these flimsy bonds.

Heh. Funny you should ask. I was wondering the same thing. Then I realized he'd lured me here so his assassins could kill me.\n\nThis is my reward for my loyal service. A blade in my gut and a nice, cold tomb.
I believe so, oh my comrade. There's really only one way to find out: you will bear it into battle! The ultimate test will come against the Mortuum Vivicus itself.

Oh, he's moved well past planning. This is what we call the "execution" stage. The part where the Maormer, backed by the Veiled Heritance, storm the shores, and the Altmer reclaim their rightful place in the world.\n\nBest practice your bowing.

No doubt Aelif has already told you of the council's decision. The province generals have condemned Colors to death. She never returned to any of her quarters. She seems to be avoiding guild members … my friend, I don't know what to think.

She thinks Colors has turned on us. That she's gone over to the Prince of Lies. That if we can find her, we'll find the Vivicus … enough. My friend, before you speak to her I must ask of you a question.
Aelif has a plan. Everything about what she proposed sickens me … but we are desperate. She believes Jofnir can find Colors, track her somehow, that they are linked. She also thinks … bah.
Truly? Just? The murder of a brave and fair-handed leader was just? What words did she weave to convince you of this?

You do not need to worry about Merric. We have already reached our decision about him. However, Sees-All-Colors …. Comrade, normally we would never allow a Daedric worshiper to remain close to the guild leadership. But these are desperate times.
I see. I know Meridia as an enemy of death across Tamriel. A light in the darkness. But still ….\n\nVery well, we will deal with her in a moment. Where is the Khajiit, Aelif?
Indeed. Where is the Khajiit, Aelif?
You do not need to worry about Merric. We have already reached our decision about guild member at-Aswala.
Yet more betrayal! I've known for years that her tongue was forked. But the Lord of Lies!\n\nYou have cleansed an evil corruption from the guild, comrade. We owe you a debt of gratitude.

I won't question your judgment. Their fates are decided, but the fate of Valenwood is what concerns me. \n\nThese shadow rifts the skulls mentioned—we must close them quickly. That's where the Shade's realm is bleeding into ours.

Quiet, Gadris! This one knows what he's doing.\n\nThis is most fragrant work, my friend. Most fragrant! Zur shall draft the potion immediately. It should make you slightly smaller. Certainly small enough to squeeze through the rubble.
Long enough to slip into the laboratory. A few minutes, give or take. Now, let Zur think. Was it six or seven drops of tincture?

Not much really. I heard he just followed Prince Naemon around like a little lost puppy.\n\nNow he runs off with Naemon's body, steals the Staff of Magnus, and takes charge of the Veiled Heritance? It seems this puppy might have a bite after all.

Sure, but there may be other spells active down there. Take a look at the observation windows and remember the details of each holding cell.\n\nThe Daedra must be keeping those notes for some reason, and I believe in always being prepared.

The High Elves, Wood Elves, and Khajiit stand united under the Eagle banner. We secure our borders against invaders, from the Covenant and Pact, but it is no easy task. And <<1>> leads our Dominion, of course.

We heard voices in the woods. We thought it was other members of our expedition, calling to us for help. But Captain Alphaury figured it out. The voice comes from this tower.\n\nWhoever's locked in there needs our help. And he will help us in return.

A safe haven? In this place? Kamu looks forward to seeing such a thing! Let me rest for a moment before I head out.\n\nI wish I could go with you, but until my injuries heal I would only slow you down. Good luck, my friend.

We never asked to be dragged into Coldharbour. We never made a deal with the Daedric Prince.\n\nBut ever since we got here, the Wood Elves raid our nests and slaughter our children. This cycle of murder needs to end!

You are a hero! You stride through Coldharbour with confidence, and not even the Wood Elves can touch you!\n\nYou can win this battle for us, and we will be in your debt. We will show you how to enter the tower. Even help you in your mission.

You have to help me convince my clan to break this ages-old agreement! We've guarded these woods and that cursed tower, assuming that one day Molag Bal would reward us and let us return to Valenwood.\n\nBut that's never going to happen.

Like me, you've been outside this forest. You know about Molag Bal's plan. You know about the Planemeld.\n\nYou have to tell them that our agreement is worthless. How can we ever return to Nirn if Molag Bal destroys it?

The Colovians are being deceived, and the truth will set us free. Cariel has learned that this attack on the March was prompted by the Stonefire cult! Worm Cultists at the beck and call of Javad Tharn whisper in General Lavinia's ear.
I will find you near the Wood Elves' camp. I have ways of moving through the forest unseen. Can be dangerous, but worth the risk.\n\nI will do anything to get our children back.

The Colovians, for all their flaws, are a faithful people. If they find out that their General is in league with a Daedric cult, their resolve will break. But Lavinia herself will never crack. We need to wring a confession out of her second.

A Centurion named Gavo. He runs the tower district for Lavinia. Gavo keeps a leash on his troops, he follows orders to a fault … and he keeps a tight schedule. Search the district for his plans, and we'll know just where to find him.

Yes, Zur, I'll be sure to mention it.\n\nI am not a mixer of potions, and I don't want to debate the merits of alchemy with Zur again, but the cat knows what he's doing. Inside, look for my notebook. It lists what you need to craft the antipodal rods.
We were just sitting down to a meal when we heard someone at the door. I think … I'm sorry, I don't remember. There were people in hoods, robes. The next thing I remember, we were here.

Well, yes. I can't argue with that. I understand why you would want to side with these creatures. I also know you need to get their eggs back.\n\nBut my people don't need to die while you do it. Recover the eggs, but don't hurt my people.

The Shadow Walkers watch the forest, but they're too confident. They leave our camps practically undefended. You could sneak in, get the eggs, and get out. \n\nYou can do it. I know you can! Please, just consider what I'm asking.

Small port, serves as a trading hub for the moon-sugar plantations on <<1>>. Home to the tastiest double rum in the southern seas.\n\nLots of Maormer there. They even have an embassy. That means problems for the Dominion.

Oh … very well.\n\nZur reminds me that time is short, so I will try to be brief. The rods form two opposing forces that should create a negative energy vortex. In theory, the vortex will unlink the strands that bind our souls and set us free.

It shouldn't be a problem. The laboratory has a forge. Just follow the directions and apply the proper catalyst. The rods should be able to withstand the reversal process.\n\nAfter you forge the rods, meet me by the Overseer's atelier.
Find the metallurgy workshop. My notebook should be there, placed neatly on a workbench. It contains a list of what you need to create the antipodal rods. Gather the items and craft the rods.
I must return these eggs to our nest. But there is one more thing you must do before my people will feel truly safe.\n\nPlease, may I tell you about this final task?
The key is divided into two shards, each protected by a Shadow Walker guardian.\n\nAs soon as you acquire the two shards, go to the camp in the center of the forest. My people will meet you there.

Maormer are Sea Elves. The High Elves kicked them off their island, so they found a new island. But for some reason, even though nobody's around to remember any of this, they want the first island back.\n\nElven feuds. You know how it goes.
<The skeleton hasn't been here for more than a few days. There are hundreds of small cuts and nicks on the bones.>\n\n<The faint smell of blood permeates the area.>
How exceedingly arrogant you must be. I rather like that. But then, just because you have a high opinion of yourself doesn't necessarily mean that it's deserved. We shall see.

Unfortunately, I've no more credentials to give. If you want them, I suppose you'll have to spar with one of the other hopefuls and take theirs.\n\nThat shouldn't be a problem for someone so confident in their abilities, should it?
We found you floating in the water. I'd seen corpses with more life in them, but Captain Kaleen dove in and fished you out anyway.
The captain of this vessel. She's currently ashore, recruiting for our latest contract.\n\nYou might want to pay your respects, seeing as she saved your life.
You're on the Spearhead, Captain Kaleen's ship.
I am one of Captain Kaleen's few remaining loyal crewmembers. The rest … well, the less said of those bloody-minded mutineers, the better.
Every person here took an oath. They'd rather die than be captured. If you want to save some, you're welcome to it. \n\nBut every soul out there should know the cost of war.

Do you, now? That's adorable. Do you really think you have what it takes? And even if you get your credentials, are you prepared to fight to the death?  \n\nI'll give you a shot. Just take care you don't soil yourself.
Really, I just fished you out of the water. Master Kasan got you breathing again. The important thing is you're alive. \n\nBut if you're feeling grateful … I could use some help.

If only I could have someone like you around full time.  \n\nIf you'll get the switch, that will give me time to study up whatever words I need to speak to close the portal. Once you get it opened, I'll just go on in, so meet me in the portal room.
It's through this door right behind me. The problem is that it's locked, but … it appears that it's controlled by a switch deeper in the ruins. \n\nWould you be a dear and find the switch?

A job. Anyone who helps is going to get rich. Right now I need a fresh face, someone this island's butcher-in-charge, Headman Bhosek, doesn't know and won't stop.\n\nBasically, you recruit the folks I need, you get a cut of the take. Interested?
Don't blame you for being cautious. Just think it over. You change your mind or want a chance to get off this wretched island, you know where to find me.
What, this place? No. This isn't the first Vinedusk Village, my friend. Won't be the last.\n\nThat's the nice thing about growing your barracks. Always somewhere new to live.

I wish I had a troll for you. Sadly, I need to save them for the real challengers. \n\nPick one of my other combatants and ask them to spar. Maybe you can find a scrawny one. Defeat them in a fair fight, and you'll get your credentials.

But will your skill with a blade tickle my whiskers or raise my hackles, I wonder?\n\nYou are so very lovely, Zara wishes she could give you the credentials based on looks alone, but that witch Feluni capped the number of combatants in each division.

Whenever we grow a new Vinedusk Village, we make use of our surroundings. The Ayleid ruins nearby? They're currently playing host to the remains of our revered founder, Nendaer the Ironbark.\n\nDamned Collies are camped right on top of him.

We face the Vlastarus Cohort, supposedly the best troops in the Colovian army. They splintered off from the main attacking force at Arenthia specifically to take us out of commission.\n\nKind of flattering when you think of it.
Why, draw your steel and dance with one of the other lovelies in camp. Defeat them in a sparring match, you see? \n\nYou'll get your credentials then, lovely. Oh yes.
Did he? I'm surprised he could get that out through the whimpering and whining! \n\nLady Laurent already has someone to recover her tools, and you would recover them and give Stibbons the credit?

Just following orders. Even before this, Stibbons couldn't keep up, so Lady Laurent hired me.\n\nI was just getting a bird's eye view before getting to work. Say though, if you were going to save Stibbons the trouble, why not help me instead?
Well for one thing, I'm better-looking. For another, I'm actually getting paid. \n\nStibbons was always just a glorified slave. Help me get the tools and I'll cut you in.
At one point, yes. Over the years the Rangers have evolved. Now we take on tasks of all kinds. Assassination, espionage—you name it. \n\n"You may cut the stalk, but you can't kill a vine." That's us.

You should meet up to investigate a couple of hot spots in the area. Rumors are the curse army walks again at the abandoned town of Vullain. Packs of Bosmer who have gone Feral terrorize the area near the Verrant Morass. Where would you like to go?
That's what I've been wondering!\n\nHe spices his rum with moon-sugar, you know? I'm sure one of the servants brings it to him. If I catch him sleeping at his post again, I'll inform the ambassador!

So he's actually doing his job? Most of the time he's writing love letters to some pretty face in town. Zadi, or Zami something?\n\nHe's a fool in a crow's nest, searching the horizon for any sign of her love. Pah!
Sounds good. Once of the Vinedusk Rangers was sent out there to keep an eye on a camp of the Veiled, so look for him. <<1>> will meet you there after I ask him more about this Shade.

Be careful. Vullain is known as the Dread Vullain because rumors were that spirits wander there, and I never believed it. Now we get reports of the cursed army walking again, and given what's happened here…. Two Vinedusks were sent there to verify.
Yes. The foolish bird makes her nest on a ships's mast, thinking it a tree. I was just such a foolish bird.
Utter tragedy. When my kwama unearthed the Dwemer ruins in these caverns an illness afflicted my miners … and the kwama.

I suspect you've not been here long. \n\nThese Redguards have a foolish distrust of all things arcane. It's a superstition brought with them from that absurd archipelago of theirs. You know—the one that sank.
All right. It's time to get paid then. Give me the tools and I'll go ahead and give you half of what Lady Laurent promised.\n\nI think that's being pretty generous of me.
There's no trouble that magic cannot mend. But spells that efficacious are beyond our ken. For now.
Yes. They say it was a paradise. I often wonder what they'd say if a mage offered to return it to the surface.
There is a stigma—though nothing is said to my face. Only when I show them my back do they speak. \n\nBut I know that my work aids our people. I have only the Eight and my conscience to answer to.

You're not? Tell me you're not going to give them to that sniveling Stibbons.\n\nEven if Lady Laurent does decide to forgive him, it's just a matter of time before he makes another mess. I'm not going to stick around to see it.
Praise the Eight! You just saved my reputation, and my livelihood.\n\nCan I have the tools then?
You're not? You don't mean to give them to Tamien, do you?\n\nBecause I'll … I'll be really disappointed if you do.

The Veiled Heritance has sent me to negotiate the problem of the Wilderking, if he exists at all. My orders are plain: convince him to aid us, or remove him.\n\nThe Shadow Watch should be very helpful in this regard.
It could be worse. Lady Laurent pays well and she's got a pretty ambitious travel schedule, so I'm getting to see places I'd never dreamed of.\n\nCan't say this desert's one of the highlights though.
No. That expedition was quite a success, and I was the one who found you ….\n\nThere's simply no explanation for why she's treating me this way.
I was wondering if you were going to ask that. \n\nYeah, I snatched up a few toolbags earlier, but there's no reason for me to give them to you, is there?
I suppose if you want to lug around the extra weight, I won't complain. \n\nOnce you've got them all, though, just remember to bring them back to me, not Stibbons.

I was out gathering fungi when the mist suddenly took on a strange hue. The next thing I remember is waking up in a dark place, surrounded by strange Bosmer with glowing eyes. They told me I'd be one of them soon. It's true. I can feel it.

It's said her hovel appears and disappears at her whim, and that she could brew potions to cure any ailment. It's been a long time since I heard that story. And that's all it is. A story.\n\nI'm going now. Please don't look for me again.
A cure for this? Ha. You mean like the potions the Wild Witch brews in children's stories?

The false Nord will use those prisoners against you. He'll steal their skins, prolonging his life and ending theirs.\n\nBut I can capture their souls for myself. Such sweet suffering I'll deliver upon them …. And the false Nord, when you slay him.
So firm, so decisive! I could roast and devour you.\n\nBut now isn't the time to speak of the future. Stand back. I assure you, it will be quick for them … in this realm.

I suppose I could watch you die at his hands. Go on, prove you're a unique and special creature. I'll try not to chuckle when he cores your skull like an apple.\n\nOr accept my aid. I'll let you think it over, if thinking is something you do.

When you approach, that Nord skin-stealer will kill those prisoners and gain power from their deaths. Something the Daedra worshipers used to do in <<1>>.\n\nI'll run in and release their bonds. I've untangled worse knots, magical or otherwise.
Keep him busy, would you? I don't want to decorate his axe.\n\nAll right <<1>>, you can do this. Faster than a fleshfly, nimbler than Khajiit.

Then I'll stay here and avoid getting my tail lopped off by a skin-stealer. If you strike fast enough, maybe he won't have time to harm them.\n\nLet me know if you change your mind. Those prisoners don't deserve such a fate.
And here I am. The last sane one standing. Hurrah, I suppose. \n\nNo doubt you and my lord had a good laugh about that. Not that I've ever heard him laugh. Or would want to.
So it would seem! I must admit, I underestimated you. \n\nYou have your Summoner Division credentials.
You keep performing like that, we might just see you in the finals. \n\nI'll be keeping an eye on you. Don't disappoint me.
Replenish the warding ritual. Amuse myself by playing tricks on the babbling fools in Ilmyris. I suppose I'll have the time now.
I suppose I did agree to that. How inconvenient. I was expecting great things from that Khajiit.

You see, there's that arrogance again. Perhaps you'll do, after all. \n\nAt any rate, I'm the current champion, so at least I can look forward to embarrassing you before an audience. That will be entertaining.
The smell of victory is all over you! It makes my back arch, but in a good way.
What about them? Look, the forest is great. Don't get me wrong. And we try to honor the Green where we can.\n\nBut this is war, damn it. If a few trees are burned to make the enemy pay, they burn.
At the very least. Ooo. That kind of strength … the power in your sword arm, it makes me want to groom myself. \n\nKeep fighting like that lovely, and you'll get a lot more than credentials.
Just … head deeper into the ruins.\n\nFind a way to disable the Engine.

Well … you and I both know I'm not really Stibbons, but I think I'm doing a good job of playing the part. This Tamien fellow is just complicating things.\n\nI'll never forget what you did for me back at the tomb, by the way.

For you, anything. Beyond the sealed door is the Vault, and inside is the creature who wears your vicecanon's face.\n\nHis master <<1>> took the <<A:2>> away. A shame, truly. But I'll tell you how to cripple the skin-stealers in the Vault.

Their key is sap of the Hist, boiled in vats. Fused with my essence, the sap is how the skin-stealers steal the memories of their victims. No more sap, no more skin-stealers.\n\nFor my essence makes the sap flammable. So burn them. Burn them all.
Admirable. But there are rules regarding new entrants. Certain credentials are required.
You come prepared! Ambitious and resourceful. How refreshing!\n\nVery well. Have you a stage name?

That won't do! Stage names must evoke mystery and intrigue. They should have a dramatic flair! Hmm. How does this sound?\n\nFrom parts unknown, comes the enigmatic, the inscrutable, the dangerous … Mysterious Stranger! Yes, I like that. You're in.
These Bosmer hate their invented god! They insist that the Wilderking exists, only to hunt him fruitlessly, trying to destroy him.\n\nIt's remarkable the lengths they go.
Right as rain! A few of our mages are accomplished Greenspeakers. When we move to a new area, they plant the seeds and perform the rituals. Within a few days … new village!

You are paying attention. Nice! Most don't.\n\nYes, the trees all grow together. They take waste and such into the roots, to keep the village healthy. And they deliver the hot sap into every hut to keep them warm.
It's a Vinedusk thing. We risk our lives every day. We do the things others can't—or won't—do.\n\nCompared to some missions I've run, burning a few huts doesn't seem like much.
Captain Ethrel and the rest of our scouts are trapped on the other side of that portal!

It is about pride, for the Captain. We were attacked in our barracks. That is where we train. \n\nWe don't mind moving the village, but we don't like it. I think Odreth is just a little embarrassed. Colovians, taking us by surprise. Pah!

I don't know. I've seen my husband out here, calling for me. I keep myself hidden because I don't want him to see.\n\nI can't go home like this. When I turn …. Just leave me. I'll end it soon. I just want to watch the sea a bit longer.

Oh, the Green Pact? Yeah, we don't worry too much about that sort of thing out here—though I know a lot of my relatives down in Valenwood would weep to hear me say it.\n\nI've even had a salad. There, I said it! And I liked it!

You're asking me why we don't give a spit about plants—in a warzone? If the other alliances knew all they had to do was grow trees to defend their forts ….\n\nWe would already have lost Cyrodiil, I'm sure.
Once the tyranny of the Shadow Walkers has ended, you will have the help you need. But first, we must recover my children from the council.\n\nDid you acquire the portal shards from the guardians?
Good. Direct the shard key toward the portal at the center of the arches. The lamias will do the rest.
The Captain is no mortal man. Not any longer. \n\nHe wields otherworldly power, as you will see, and that skull you hold is one of two that grant him his abilities.

You will. You are a new arrival, yes? \n\nThe newly arrived have more free will, more fighting spirit. But that won't last. It never does. In time … uncounted years, perhaps … you will become Feral. It is the fate that awaits us all, eventually.

It's a name, a title, and our holy city. Quite an honor to carry around such an important word, and the occasional burden in its confusion of outsiders.\n\nNot even <<Ac:1>> calls me by my given name. "Edhelorn" doesn't roll off the tongue, I suppose.

A freshly grown fruit, still without blemish. On behalf of the Bosmer people, it's my goal to keep it that way.\n\nIf you speak with <<Ac:1>>, don't mistake her manner as distaste for the Dominion. She simply misses our home of Valenwood.

As Silvenar? Seems like it's been such a short while, but the wrinkles on my face tell me differently.\n\nOr did you mean as Dominion envoy? I've taken on diplomatic tasks for our fledgling alliance since its inception. So, not very long at all.

She sustains me, and I her. Together, we are the aspirations of the Bosmer people given form. Put simply, she is the love of my life.\n\nAlso, she grows ill-humored when I gush about her within earshot. I'd best say no more.
Merani … thinks she should stay. We are such a small community. I know Ezreba and her Hizurrdo well. We would be the worse for her absence.
Such a thing is not for us to decide. Tashpir's brush with darkness … he leaves this decision in the moonlight.
This is a difficult question but Kada thinks she should go free. Kada would do the same if her mate were taken.
