"Should she stay?" What kind of question is that? She's a cancer in our midst. I felt that darkness in my mind. She should be cut out! Now!
Stay? You're even considering letting her stay? The Green take you, get her out of our village!
I know Ganny is mad as a wet Khajiit. But I say let her stay. Everyone deserves a chance to make things right. And Ezreba's a good sort.

The main portal was unguarded when we got here. Captain Ethrel took four of our number through. That's when the Dremora swept in and captured us. Set up crystals to seal the portal.\n\nIt was a trap and we walked into it like yesterday's dinner.
Well, you've come to the right place. It's one of my favorite tales, though it's quite embellished these days. Better for frightening the children away from certain dangers.
That's the idea. But there are secondary portals all around the main one, protecting the crystals. Ready yourself for a fight.
<<1>>'s son. When his father succumbed to skooma, <<2>> swore vengeance upon the smugglers responsible. This one tried to stop him from going by himself, but <<2>> wouldn't listen.
Are you certain you've spoken to everyone you need to? I don't want to make this decision lightly.
How would I know what others call me? I am Galereth. And you are inside my home. Why have you come here?

Ever try piloting a ship through a hurricane while your entire cargo of kwama eggs hatch and go bug-nuts? Been there, can't recommend it.\n\nAfter we wrecked, they made a kwama-line toward this cave. I came after them, but they're a bit distracted.

They always get surly after hatching, but these kwama are downright unsociable. I tried to stop them from chewing on those huge roots. They objected.\n\nBumped into a fine-looking tree trunk on my way out. Thought I was done for, but it kept walking.

If they'd stop eating those giant roots, they might get better … but I don't blame you if you have to put down a few to save the rest.\n\nJust be careful. Nothing fiercer than a crazed kwama. Not even my sister-in-law.

Oh? Kwama didn't take to it, whatever it was. I heard them munching on it, same as those roots.\n\nThe little ones seemed scared of it. If you can help the pretty tree trunk do what it needs to do, I bet they'll head back this way.
The spirit is old and powerful. It seeks to move from root to root, aiding the Great Tree as it's able.\n\nBut it's a healing spirit, of singular purpose. It doesn't know how to defend itself.
The Great Tree shields <<1>> from the winter winds and keeps our settlement shaded from the heat of the summer. Its story entwines with ours.
I'm uncertain. If so, the spirit must be protected from harm while it heals the Great Tree's roots. It knows what it must do.

So she can't face her husband after what she's become. I … know what that feels like. \n\nVery well. Take this to her as soon as possible. She must drink it before her transformation is complete or it will be too late.
I'm running low on the blood I harvest from the hoarvor nearby. I dislike collecting it, but it is a necessity for me. If you will gather some, I will give you the potion when you return.
I might have something that will do the trick, assuming they haven't fully turned. But I expect you to do something for me in return first.
Good. Good. This will do for awhile.\n\nAnd in return, your potion, as requested. Get it to your friend quickly. It must be taken before the transformation is complete or it can have no effect.
It's simple. Three lizards to bet on. Either way, you get to taste the finest lizard stew in Reaper's March!\n\nSo which lizard will it be?
Thank you! The race is about to start!
Oh, that one was trained by professional breeders! An excellent choice!
She's a lucky one! I've seen that creature win half the races today. More than that!
Absolutely.
That one saw its mother get cooked in the pot and hasn't lost a race since. Guess it doesn't want to end up in my belly!

We are so close. You need to use the rods to activate the Dwarven device that performed the soul-meld. \n\nOh, and the crystal! I am getting as careless as Zur. Look for a glowing crystal. The Overseer placed it in the machine to power the device.
Believe me, the pleasure is all mine! I never thought I'd have a chance to work with the illustrious Tharn family. If my old mother could see me now ….

I'm already suffering enough without you making a mockery of me. I just started thinking about my childhood now that my life is over, that's all. I liked those stories. Even if that's all they were. Children's tales.
Ah, well, in a manner of speaking. Understand that Zur and I do not have two separate bodies to return to. But if this works, the soul-meld won't kill the both of us.
Very well so far! We're taking stock of what we've managed to recover from the city in terms of material. I just came from reviewing our progress on the docks.
Excellent, let me see … ha! This is an amazing find, my friend. With this, by the Green, we'll retake the city for sure! But first thing's first. We need to get the Centurion to Kazirra.
We need him alive, right? You talk, I get into position. Then I introduce him to the butt of my dagger. Pretty simple, as these things go.
You're going to love this. You're going to walk their commanding officer right past the damned Colovians. Straight out the front gate.

My superior, a Khajiit named Razum-dar, has this appreciation for disguise. I've got this earring of his, with a simple illusion spell woven into it. No good for long-term missions, but perfect for quick infiltration.
I'm going to gag him and dress him as your prisoner. Then, like I said. You simply walk him out the front gate. Easy as lying. This will take just a moment. You ready?
Absolutely! Want me to explain the rules again?

I was with Telenger when we discovered the ruin. The damn cultist attacked us, and nearly killed me. Thank the Eight that Telenger was there! I barely escaped with my life, but not before my beautiful hair burned off!
You know I am! Those Arbordawn idiots are all the proof anyone needs that the Wood Elves need to keep to their forests, and the High Elves need to stay in Summerset!
Of course I am! It is the greatest honor of my life to be in the presence of the great Mer, and to serve him in any way I can!

Well of course I am! When I got the chance to be part of an expedition led by none other than <<1>> himself, I had to take it. I joined the Mages Guild to explore Tamriel, and here I am, at long last!
What would you have us do? The Wood Elves slaughtered my people. They would not listen to reason. The only chance we had was to remove their leaders.\n\nNow we shall watch the Shadow Walkers crumble.

You have helped us. Now we shall help you. I instructed Tzik'nith to head to the ruined passage that leads to the tower. You shall find her there.\n\nKnow that the lamias are in your debt. Call upon us if you ever need our strength and cunning.

As I promised, this door leads to the tower. I do not know what the tower holds, but we have heard the cries for help from within.\n\nBe careful in there, outsider. This is Coldharbour. Even the most mundane things can hide terrible dangers.
The Khajiit told me of a city of safety to the east. I will take some of my people, for we would very much like to see this city. We will be there if you have need of us, my friend.

The magic will separate the intertwined strands of our souls, but only one of us will survive the process.\n\nDo not be dismayed. We rejoice at a chance for one of us to survive. Go on ahead. We will meet you inside momentarily.

Ah, Lyris. Girl's as mad as Sheogorath's jammies. Heart's in the right place, I suppose. Says she's got to rescue the Prophet to save us all from eternal torment. How an old blind man could do that is quite beyond me!

Originally, we were going to force him out into the street. Make him confess to his soldiers firsthand. You've found us a much more elegant way to see this done. We'll use their own illusions against them.
It's only right you have the honor of holding the crystal. I'll interrogate Gavo. And Cariel will be on hand to ensure he … cooperates. Just get the crystal pointed at him when you're ready to begin.

I hadn't actually given it much thought. Anything's possible, I suppose. \n\nTruth is, I've been here so long, this place feels like home. But a good uprising now and again is a pleasant diversion, so where's the harm, eh?

An Imperial gentleman. Apparently he was once a powerful mage, but the years haven't been kind. \n\nLyris says he knows of a path back to Tamriel. I rather think that if one existed, I'd have found it by now.
Enjoy the combat! Who will you bet on? <<1>>? Or <<2>>?
Excellent! Get ready for some carnage!
Good! This will be a fight for the ages!
Good choice! <<1>>'s a fighter with a terrifying history. It once terrorized <<2>>!\n\nI bet you're happy that you're safe up here than down there!
What's the matter? Scared of watching real fighting? Come back when you've got some courage in you!
The Colovian killer! <<1>> singlehandedly halted a Colovian attack!\n\nSomeone like you would flee in terror from such a beast!

The Radiant One knows many things. She knew that one day the city she plunged into Coldharbour would serve her purpose. At first, she thought I would fulfill that prophecy.\n\nBut I failed, and now I need your help.

Have no fear. I am as alive as you are. Molag Bal has preserved me so that I can endure his endless tortures. His cruelty knows no bounds.\n\nI can't slip free of this lightless oubliette, but I have managed to send my projection to meet you.
Exactly. And I'll have the blood that's due!\n\nWhat does this creature's life matter to you, anyway?
As if this day hadn't gone to Oblivion already … you feel the need to remind me of all my debt?\n\nYes, I still owe S'rashi. The Dawn Posset is a quality ship; it'll take time to pay her off.

Of course. Lost the ship at the Koeglin Lighthouse, and the crew moved on … I'm lucky Elvira stuck around.\n\nWe bought the Dawn Posset in Wayrest and took on a new crew. Good people; we're due for a streak of luck after this.
NYI - Dialogue
NYI - Dialogue

I understand. I am certain she'll find another way to mourn her husband.\n\nI asked <<1>> what he meant about the "tempest." After what <<Ac:2>> did to him it is difficult for him to focus, but what he did say isn't good at all.

The Maormer have some ships waiting offshore. <<1>>'s people signaled them before <<Ac:2>> arrived. Some sort of invasion force.\n\nWith the Dominion's help, perhaps we can fortify the town. That alone may save many lives.
More than interesting! Awe-inspiring! Thrilling!\n\nDon't you want to see another fight?

The dead are sacred. It is what the people of Alik'r have always believed and always will. \n\nJust as we respect our elders, so do we respect our ancestors. It would be dishonorable to strike them, and might even cause one to be cursed.

Acting commander of this regiment. My superior didn't survive the hurricane, so it falls to me to secure the Aldmeri Dominion's foothold on <<1>>.\n\nA change in command is never clean. But if everyone does their part, we'll recover quickly enough.
Yes, <<Ac:1>> is an old Khajiit ruin not far from here. We excavated <<Ac:2>> from one of the chambers. As you can see, its supply of water appears endless.
You must remember the alliance you're sworn to protect.\n\nPerhaps you should lie down until you recover your bearings, soldier.
Arrogant Sea Elf pirates. To my recollection, they aren't known to raid <<1>>. Oh, and they have a thing for snakes.\n\nBut I'm sure we both have more important matters to attend. If you'd excuse me?

<<1>>. Though <<2>> heard it was a beautiful island, this one thinks it would look better without all the wrecked ships.\n\nNot even the Dominion's greatest fleet can sail through hurricanes. We are fortunate to be alive.

A cook on the flagship. I used a cleaver to take guts out of animals.\n\nBut <<1>> needs help, and now I use needle and thread to put guts back into soldiers. Hard work, but I thank the two moons for every one I save.

The locals call this place <<1>>. I gather it was an Imperial fort destroyed long ago. We were lucky to find such a defensible position close to where we washed up.\n\nOr did you mean the island, <<2>>? The fleet's destination, as you surely recall.

It's no secret this island is of strategic importance. From here the Dominion fleet can reach many coastal targets where we could establish a beachhead.\n\nBut we'll need to rebuild the fleet, first. Hardly an auspicious start to our invasion.
Excellent. Let the battle begin!
Tall Papa willed it to be so!

To really make an impression, you need to hurt the lamias. Kill them, burn their eggs, and defeat their champion. Even our strongest warriors haven't been able to accomplish that!\n\nDo these things and that should be enough to get you an audience.

The Shadow Walkers are always watching. If they see you inflicting pain and suffering on the lamias, they'll take notice.\n\nCause enough chaos and defeat the lamia champion. That should make my clan invite you in with open arms!

Mother sent you? It is good she can't see me trussed up like a sheep. The bandits were more challenging than I expected.\n\nShe could have killed a few when she scouted the cave, but no, I must always be tested.

Most people here deem this to be sacred law, not superstition. Even King Fahara'jad must respect our customs.\n\nIf he were to ask his people to disrespect their ancestors, his rule would swiftly come to an end.

These dark arts are not practiced by our people, but yes, we have experienced the plague of necromancy in the past.\n\nFighting these plagues has always required great sacrifice. Those who have fought the dead have been dishonored, cast out.

Ha!  No - I will be honest.  You ask how I came to live here? A great deal of coin and the favor of our King, Ruptga's praises be upon him.  My family and I own a small merchant fleet that has become essential to the war effort.
Trade brings what Crowns fear most: progress. But I'm not concerned. Like a sand storm, the dissent will pass. Every time they bite into an imported Glenumbran apple, they prove me right.

Good, no.  Booming, yes.  Aside from the occasional Aldmeri corsair, we've been able to do business virtually unhindered.  Opening trade routes with Daggerfall is the best thing that's ever happened to our economy.

Take the crystal and head out to where Lavinia is spreading her message of tolerance and understanding. It should imprint the new illusion onto every stand in the city at once. Some kind of magical resonance, I think. I'm no mage.

The Colovians will break. Lavinia's forces will scatter. The perfect time to cut off the snake's head. According to Cariel, the General is using my favorite inn as her own personal manse. Kill her and we'll do the rest.
You thought her a poor mewling widow? Ha! Mother is not entirely what she seems.\n\nShe warned me to wait and watch before approaching <<1>>. I have much to learn.

Daedra happened. The Hollow is infested with them. Turns out that muskarse Oraneth was summoning them down here, to fight a war for her. Turned out well, no?\n\nMy Mages are slaughtered. And still, Kargand must find his sister, Bakkhara. Will you help?
Good. Now, untie my bonds so we can look for the key to <<1>>'s lair. Swish-slash-poke, done.
Defeat the Daedra. Your claws look sharp enough.\n\nThis one would search to the last plane of Oblivion before giving up on his sister. If Bakkhara lives, we will find her. Will you help?
Maybe. That's certainly more than any of my people have been able to do.\n\nIt won't be easy, though. She's a powerful old snake! Her cave is at the highest point in the lamia camp.
I think I'll be safe enough here. But you can hide under my counter if you wish. Just don't drink anything.

Next comes the exciting part! You test our theory!\n\nSee those two pillars? One represents Zur, the other Gadris. Insert the antipodal rods and turn on the device. If it works, you should be able to separate our melded souls.
Yes, as we have explained. One body, one soul. At least one of us will survive to help the Mages Guild. This one knows you will make the right decision.
For me, flight is not an option. What then would people say of my armor, if I did not trust it to protect me?
To avoid Ra-Netu? You are kind to warn me, but our honored dead dare not step into the forge. Onsi would not allow it.
I heard as much. In Daggerfall the city guard would have dealt with them already.\n\nThe people of Alik'r have proud traditions, but they take reverence for the dead too far.

Well, I told you that killing lamias would get their attention. You performed an honor deed. They respect that. Hopefully, that respect will last long enough for you to help me before they decide to kill you.

You stay here. I'll go see the council and give them the lamia's head. That should be all the incentive they need to agree to listen to you.\n\nIn the meantime, talk to the Wood Elves here. Any information you gain is just another arrow in your quiver.

I'm not sure I should help you, but you seem to be on Faraniel's good side. Maybe if I give you some advice, I'll get on her good side, too.\n\nI recommend you try a little humor when you talk to Erthor. He's a dry old leaf, but he does like to laugh.
You dare challenge me? You test my patience, fool. \n\nBegone before I forget my manners and gut you where you stand.

You don't honestly believe you can do that, do you?\n\nMy people made a vow to protect this citadel long before I was born. The elders are ancient and stuck in their ways. They'd never agree to break our oath.

I hope I don't live to regret this.\n\nInril is the oldest member of the council. She's also the most willing to listen. But you have to show her some respect. Let her speak. Respond only when spoken to. That's all I can think of. Hope it helps.
Spikeball is a footrace with a twist. You get a spikeball! Someone ahead of you? Spike them! That's pretty much it.
All right! Head to the starting line and wait for my countdown! It's right over there to my left, where the other racers are!
Come on, give it a try! Everyone loves spikeball!

Dealing with the council can be tricky. It's a collection of individuals, each with his or her own idiosyncrasies.\n\nThey are devoted to Molag Bal and our oath of servitude. It won't be easy to convince them to break those ancient promises.

You can't fail. You just can't. Were the Shadow Walkers down here helpful? Do you need to talk to them again?\n\nWhen you're ready, just use the portal behind me. Present a good argument and make it count.
The Guild is subject to certain restrictions that don't apply to lone warriors like you.
Of course! We can get started right away!

The essence before you has been used to feed the slaves and keep them working. Talk to the slaves and convince them to release my energy so that I can break free.\n\nIf the slaves refuse, there is another way.

The slaves' taskmaster used a device to rip away my energy. The device can recover the energy, but doing so will destroy the soul shriven you target.\n\nHowever, the device only works from a distance. Get too close and you can't target a slave.

The most frustrating of all—politics and religion. Our Guildhall is not a permanent fixture here in Sentinel. We operate at the pleasure of the king and his viziers. They could make things difficult for us if they wanted to.
Welcome to the world of Stewardship. I need a drink.

Let's take the case you brought up: if we began cutting down the Redguards' "honored dead," we'd face a public relations disaster. Recruitment would dry up, and we can't afford that. Fighting Daedra is something of a team sport.
Kazirra was right, then. She'll be relieved to hear it. The Colovians are on the run and I'd say we've done a damned good job here today.
You should talk to Kazirra. Tell her your account of what went on. I consider it an honor to have served with you here today. I'm going to make sure the Queen hears of your bravery.

Yes, we have sworn to protect the passage that leads to the tower known as the Lightless Oubliette. In exchange, we have been given the gift of shadow-walking.\n\nWhen our contract is fulfilled, the Daedric Prince shall send us back to Valenwood.
Respect is a luxury I cannot afford. I need proof that Molag Bal lies to us. Do you have such proof? Can you show it to me?

Heh, well, yes. We still await our day of release. Hundreds of years, however, do not mean much in a place where lives are measured in eternity.\n\nWhat makes you think Molag Bal will break our agreement?

That annoying Faraniel has convinced you of her fables, hasn't she? I tire of this old argument.\n\nBut you did perform an honor deed. I shall give you one chance to convince me that we are being duped. Go ahead.
You speak with confidence and conviction. Very well, I shall consider your words.\n\nA persistent fool may know more than an isolated genius. We shall see.

I do not give a damn about your respect. What does the opinion of an outsider matter to me? I just want the truth.\n\nI have listened to your words as the honor deed demanded. Now go away and leave me be.
Such terrible news! But how can I know that what you say is true? It makes no sense.\n\nWhy would Molag Bal destroy our beautiful and beloved Valenwood?
No singing or dancing will be necessary, thank you. As for trust, that has to be earned, not given.\n\nI shall consider what you and Faraniel have told us. Then the council shall decide.

Do not raise your voice to me, outsider! You came to ask for our help, not to harass us with your wild notions.\n\nI have heard your words and shall give them the consideration they deserve. Now move along.

You must understand. To simply accept the word of an outsider, to turn our backs on everything we believe. You ask much, stranger.\n\nStill, Faraniel has been insistent about the very same concern. Tell me something to sway my opinion.

Such disrespect! I have never allowed anyone to speak to me in this manner! Still … your words concern me.\n\nI shall consider what you have said. But I do not wish to speak with you anymore. Please, leave me.
This news … disturbs me.\n\nThank you for sharing this information with us. Speak to the other elders while I consider what you have said.

What isn't wrong there? An earthquake devastated the place four years ago. Now a fissure runs through the middle of town. Constant tremors set back efforts to rebuild. To top it off, monsters emerge from the fissure and attack the townsfolk!
Too stubborn. Chorrol is their home. They are determined to stay. It would not surprise me to see their descendants still there, hundreds of years from now.
Don't run so fast this time!

I haven't quite figured that out. I can feel them, though. They feel like wounds in the forest. \n\nI have some small ability to mend the Green, but it requires all of me. I'm going to need your protection.

While it allows you to see anyone hiding in the shadow realm, it also masks your presence from them. I've used this method to avoid patrols and sneak out of the forest. It really works!\n\nBut remember. The effect is temporary. It doesn't last long.
Not a chance, dunghead!\n\nIt was given to me. Go find your own!

The Wood Elves started hunting us almost as soon as we stepped into this dread forest. They killed Captain Alphaury in cold blood! I barely escaped. The snake thing found this one, lost and injured, and led me safely through the woods.
Well, in that case … Just make sure you shut down this damn forge.
Do what you must, but I'm keeping this energy! It gives me the strength to move my sorry bones.\n\nNow, leave me to my sorrow.
Why? You don't look like you need it. Without it, I'll grow weak and wither away.\n\nWait, that's what you want to happen! You want to hurt me!
And what will you give me in return? What do you have that will keep me whole and strong enough to do the work that is required of me?
Oh, so high and mighty! You think to take the place of the Taskmaster, do you?\n\nOh, very well, take it and get out of my sight. Some of us have to work for a living.
And how will that help me? No, this doesn't sound like any deal I want to be a part of.\n\nNow leave me to my work before I call the Taskmaster!
It … will? I don't know … oh, all right. Take it. Take it and leave me alone!
A great mage? A great mage is the reason I'm in this godsforsaken place! \n\nI knew you were out to hurt me. Well, the Taskmaster gave me this energy and I'm going to keep it!
And how will that help this one see the escape plan to fruition?\n\nThis one thinks you should bother someone else now.
Dear Alexis, why would I do such a thing? The energy makes me strong. I haven't felt this good in such a long time!
Always with the violence! Your kind. So predictable.\n\nVery well, take it. This one hopes you choke on it!
And this one is what? Chopped skeever?\n\nFind someone else to rob, you thief!
Oh, Alexis! You remembered how much I love bright and shiny things!\n\nI never could refuse your requests. Take the energy and use it well.
My dear Alexis, don't say such dreadful things! The Dark Lord will hear. Then what will become of you?\n\nNo, I'll keep the energy. It's for your own good.
You have seen, of course … the tribe is weak, and I am soon to return to the sand.\n\nAnother must fulfill the sacred duty of the Ash'abah … that other is you. It has been foreseen.

My guess is that he's with the girls at his seraglio by the north wall. \n\nI know what you're thinking, but it's not because the prince is some kind of ladies' man. The girls help him gather information. Perhaps he'll already know what's happened.

Mages Guild warlock and master conjurer, at your service. I'm an expert on the planes of Oblivion, so I was an obvious choice to undertake this mission.\n\nI was raised on the Shivering Isles, so I am intimately familiar with Oblivion.
An excellent suggestion! There's no time to waste. Let's get inside and free the others.

Then when you free me, I'll fight <<1>> alone and will likely die. <<1>> will poison more families with skooma. Another will swear revenge, be captured by bandits, and wait for death in this cave.\n\nOr we can kill <<1>>. Still simple, yes?
When I entered the room, the braziers were ablaze, and I … I think I stepped on a pressure tile. The brazier snuffed out, and this trap grabbed me. Maybe … if you relight the braziers?

I-I do not know. I never imagined this realm would be so … elaborate. How could he create this? Where does he get such power?\n\nWe have to stop this—whatever it takes. Perhaps we can find the source of it. Yes. We must.

I'll have to explain later. There's nothing we can do while we're trapped here. We need to find Naemon's Servant and destroy him.\n\nI suspect he's at the Stone Table. Once again, you will have to defeat him. Quickly! I will meet you there.

The Great Mage himself couldn't have done any better, but don't tell him I said that!\n\nAfter you return my energy, I will break free. The last fragment is trapped in the Foundry. Follow my light and I'll show you the way.
They're on the high ground surrounding the grove. There are three of them.\n\nPlease, hurry. We've not much time.
I'm a priest of the Wooded Eye. The last priest, from the look of things. Can't say I'm happy about it.

Get here? It's always been here. How to explain? It exists, but to most people it blends seamlessly into the forest. You can't see it, unless you are woven into the wards—or you figure out a way to break them.
It'll make this grove once again invisible to all except those who know where to look, or who are woven into the warding.
Oof, them. One of them looked like he'd seen … livelier days. The other just looked shifty. Both Altmer, I think.
Four seals contain the magic that binds me to this machine. While this essence is locked in place, they siphon my energy into the forge.

Days? Weeks? I cannot tell. The voyage between worlds disrupted all sense of time and space.\n\nI know only that you were deposited into the sea, and some charitable soul fished you out and brought you to dry land.

Legend has it that the Dwemer left Rkugamz centuries before they themselves vanished from Tamriel. They embarked on an exodus from the city when the Aedra supposedly cursed their masterwork, the Great Engine.\n\nIf I'm correct, this explains much.

Vanus divided himself to prevent them from using his considerable energy to power the Great Shackle. It didn't stop them from plugging this essence into the forge, however.\n\nUnlock the four seals and I'll be able to escape this damn machine.

I think the Engine is the cause of what we've witnessed here. I would like to study it in detail, but we'll have to deactivate it, perhaps destroy it.\n\nWe are fortunate to have avoided the miners' fate—so far. We should hurry.
No way, milk-drinker. This lodge is for members of the Ebonheart Pact only. Leave now, or you'll regret it.
Whoa, whoa! Easy now! Uh, I suddenly remembered … I have to go on patrol.\n\nSee, I'm just going to step away … no harm, no foul.
Enough talk. Leave, now, or I raise the alarm and we end your miserable life.
Yet more betrayal! I've known for years that her tongue was forked. But the Lord of Lies!\n\nYou have cleansed an evil corruption from the guild, comrade. We owe you a debt of gratitude.

I'm fine … I … look, I'm just tired of getting shuttled around on pointless diplomatic assignments like this.\n\nI always get stuck guarding these opulent lodgings. Never get to relax, never get to unwind.

Morwha's mercy! Maybe you took a head-bump, too! Did you forget about the battle? The Ra Gada will drive these evil Elves from our lands for good.\n\nI am to fight at your side today, brother. Tell me you still feel up to it!
No, no. I'll be fine. Now, that lanky High Elven sweetbread in the leisure tent? Nallore? He might be able to … never mind. \n\nLook, get going before anyone sees us talking.
Well, aren't you a sweetheart? Buying some time for your friends. \n\nI'd be happy to spend some time with him or her. For a small fee, of course.
Oh, I know her. Irvina, right? \n\nDon't worry about her. Here at Pa'alat, we specialize in memorable moments.
Ha! No, you're not. You're lying. Look, get out of here before I call down the lion's fury on your head.\n\nUnless … you're hiding a keg of ale somewhere in that fancy garb?
Ha! Forget this standing around. Shouldn't have told speedy Seyran!
Finally! I haven't had a drink in hours. Grab me a drink from one of the leisure stalls and you can do whatever you want.
Then these bindings can no longer hold me. This essence will join you and then we can find the physical form of the Great Mage.
It speaks. I suppose I should be impressed that one of your kind even dares to approach me.

Through the boiler tunnels waits the mighty guardian, <<1>>. Defeat the guardian and open the cage that holds our physical form.\n\nI can lead you to the Great Mage. Just stay close and follow my light.

Oh, little mortal, you amuse me so! \n\nSurely you have more important things to do than waste time with me? Aren't there rocks that need to be chipped or bugs to be swatted? Perhaps you need to mutter to yourself and wander around in circles?

Most of the guests here suffer from one or more such afflictions.\n\nIf you linger long enough, perhaps you will adopt one of these distinctive quirks. Or perhaps not. I will continue to watch with interest to see what develops.
Pity. To think they'd miss out on this fascinating conversation.

Very nicely done! Clear links … yes, links between Ren-dro and agents in Riften. Deep in the heart of the Pact. \n\nAnd correspondence with an operator in Sentinel. The Covenant's fingers are all over this place.

By the Green, I'm done with that. These bastards have relaxed enough. Get into the drinking tents and set some fires. Kill anyone that tries to stop you.\n\nCause enough commotion and Ren-dro's men will come running. Then make for the compound.
Our primary goal now should be to reclaim any documents Ren-dro has stolen from the Eyes.\n\nThere's only one place they'd be: inside his manse. Only problem is, the place is crawling with guards.
We are the image of our creator. We do not distinguish amongst ourselves because we are nothing apart from the Wilderking.
The curse upon each tome is designed to feed souls to Oblivion. But if you are able to resist their pull, you can collect the tomes and bring them to the shrine for their destruction.

On the shores of <<1>>, beyond the town of <<2>>. It is lit by an ever-burning flame.\n\nShould you collect all the tomes, bring them to the shrine without delay. No matter how strong you believe you are, I fear the tomes are stronger.

These … ruffians definitely have the relics, but I … I don't know where.\n\nSome of the bandits were talking about the "leader's stash," which is somewhere nearby. By an old, broken staircase, I think they said.
It's a secret lair! Ren-dro has a secret lair. He probably keeps his more important business down there. When I retire I'm going to get my own lair.
You look strong, Sameer. My heart is proud. I believe this will be a day of destiny for you and your brother.\n\nIf we wish to remain here, we must cleanse the land of these Elves' taint.
Oh! Yes. Yes, that's almost certainly where he is. What do you say, my friend? Ready to deal out the Queen's justice to a traitor?

Scattered. The Captain … it all happened so fast. She was struck and in the chaos, we lost sight of the others. I tried to save her, but….\n\nWe need to find the others, if they're still alive. And then we need to close that portal for good.

That's why I've come along. I've studied the Moonhenge.\n\nThis plane has its own Moonhenge. It's like a mirror of the one in Valenwood. We need to find the sigil stone that anchors the portal between this realm and Greenshade.
I will show you how to get into the tower. Full of shiny treasures, I'm sure!\n\nAnd we will become your allies against the Daedric Prince. Even fight at your side, if that is what you wish.

I'm not asking for anything you can't do. \n\nAnd I'll go with you when you're done! To help! I've been planning to leave anyway, so now's as good a time as any. You can use me. Just … don't kill any Shadow Walkers. Please.
Forgive me. <<1>> couldn't be allowed to roam free. Something had to be done, and you had the strength to see what I could not.
Well, just between us, I doubt it. But it's been here for a long time, so who really knows?
I'll ensure the Mourning Stone remains guarded at all times. I should make a full report so the Dominion understands the danger of <<1>>'s capabilities.
Yes, donations have dried up and the faithful lose faith. We desperately need that claw back!
Monks have to eat too, you know. And the faithful love to gaze upon it and offer donations for its continued upkeep.
I know how that seems, but I see no other way. The Black Daggers are truly horrific, more like beasts than decent people. You'll be saving many innocent lives!

Yes, we've sent several emissaries. Each was tortured, killed, and skinned, not necessarily in that order. They are impossible to reason with, and we lack the strength to defend ourselves from them. We need your help!
You speak truth, and yet the young should never die for the old. It is the singular travesty of war.
I need to record everything that happened here. <<1>>'s skill troubles me. Without further study, the Dominion will bear no defense against his strange capabilities.
Perhaps there is a gateway back to our realm, back to Valenwood … some place where life and death intersect ….\n\nThat's it! The Stone Table. I must go. I'll meet you there.
Ah, the name for my newest outfit.\n\nHis flesh sags a bit, though the power in his bones reminds me of my youth. And the robes … I'd forgotten the feel of silk upon newly won flesh.

My master and I had little to do after the shipwreck. When the locals mentioned a temple where the fountains never run dry, we leapt at the chance to investigate. <<1>> insisted on leading, of course.

A contemporary of my master. A rival, really.\n\n<<1>> found a strange relic inside the temple called a "Mourning Stone." He was barely able to remove it before the undead struck. I think he brought it to <<2>>.

Those monsters? We've been at war with them for ages. My people will never listen to you if you take their side.\n\nThe Shadow Walkers are powerful. We would be of great help to you. But only if you aid me and convince my people.
<<1>> thought it could be used to control the weather, perhaps prevent another hurricane. <<2>> disagreed, of course. He insisted on studying it further at <<3>>.
No, we must enter the tomb together. Though he can't "wear" you, he could quite easily obliterate you with his magic. Only by splitting his attention can we hope to defeat him.
No, which is why we must be the ones to enter the tomb. After he saw you through my eyes, he seemed convinced that to "wear" you would destroy him.\n\nFor some reason he feared you.
The centerpiece of this old Khajiit temple. After <<1>>'s reign of terror, the Sea Elves gave it to the Khajiit so it'd become the key to his prison.
Yes, mock me with your presence. My vengeance will be all the sweeter.

Usually we'd be out pursuing various contracts. By the Eight, there's more than enough to do out here in the desert. But these days, our new hall steward has us working one big job.\n\nWe've focused all our resources on destroying the Daedric anchors.

Ha! Sure Let me just pull him from my satchel! \n\nYou people don't understand. The Wilderking manages the entire forest! He doesn't have time for idle talk. Why do you think so many people doubt his existence?

Fair enough. Welcome to the guild, Associate.\n\nNow it's just a matter of slaying as many Daedra as you can find.  If you break some of those chains, there'll be a reward and maybe even some special assignments waiting for you when you return.
Is a croc's arse watertight?  Of course we're recruiting, provided you've got the skillset. From the looks of you I'd say you're an excellent candidate.\n\nSo what do you say? You in?

Yeah—huge chains falling out of the sky?  A seasoned adventurer like you, I'm sure you've seen one.\n\nFrom what I'm told, they're coming straight out of Oblivion, Wherever they hit, Daedra are sure to follow.

I like your confidence, outsider. You've got some bark on your hide!\n\nAnd that's exactly what you're going to need if you go up against Elder Gluin. Don't take no for an answer and keep pushing him. Do that and he eventually gives in.

We'd get to see bright skies and clear water? I've only heard stories about such things!\n\nListen, if you speak to Elder Elsaril, show some compassion. Life on the council can be harsh and unforgiving.
I know only the ones we see at the Lindai ruins. Those are necromancers, mages of the most evil sort. The undead serve them as guardians.

I fear so. Rumors tell of other Circles of the Shadowed Path, groups that infest areas across Cyrodiil. Nothing of these other circles is known to me; the group at Lindai is enough for me to worry about.

A lich is an undead creature, completely evil.\n\nNecromancers who lust for immortality can transform themselves into liches. Vile spells and sacrifices are involved. They gain tremendous power but lose their souls.

For some, the lust for power overwhelms all other desires. The thought of wielding that power forever becomes an all-consuming passion. And necromancers deal with the undead every day. Perhaps undeath loses its horror for them.

Of course it will, but what am I to do? Allow my public image to endanger the kingdom? Sometimes a king cannot save his face and his people at the same time.\n\nStill, I would prefer we not shout our plans from the rooftops.
The necromancer slew your father and then reanimated his corpse. It is the most terrible thing I have ever seen. \n\nHe is lost. There is nothing to be done for it.
This one does not know. Some kind of difference of opinion? \n\nTazia would suggest you speak with the Clan Mother if you'd like to know more.
Oh, you know. Small things for a small town. One of the older persons was complaining of rats. \n\nAnd Tazia thinks someone said children were stealing their crops.
It is quite a list. I have never heard of this antidote before, but my father assures me it is what we need.\n\n<<1>>, <<2>>, <<3>>, and <<4>>.

After Dread Vullain, I was sent to reinforce the outpost. You know how it goes. One moment you're sharpening your sword and the next you're entering a Daedric portal in the middle of a creepy Ayleid ruin.

I think they're some kind of magical devices used to call beasts from the sea, like that thing.\n\nIf we don't destroy them quickly, I don't want to think about what else might come crawling out of the waves.
I'll try. Might get distracted exacting some much-earned payback on these monsters.
Scout Paranarth. I … I'm sorry I abandoned the Captain. This is my first fight. When the Daedra attacked, I just. I lost my nerve. It won't happen again. I promise.
As you say.
Excellent. My three loudest kittens are <<1>>, <<2>>, and <<3>>.
Hmm. Perhaps. Lately a few of our clan mates have been on my doorstep day and night. If you were to investigate, Shuzura could get some real work done.
Bright moons light your path, little one. You will find his house east of here up the hill. Good luck with those rats.
You'll find his farm southeast of town. Shuzura is sure there's nothing to that fat old Khajiit's whining. Your kindness may quiet him down, though. And she thanks you for that.
<<1>>'s new home is at the very south end of town. Thank you for seeing to the girl. \n\nShe's sweet, and Shuzura hates the idea of her fretting.
And which of my sad little kittens will you lift from the sand?

Because it is clear that one of us must make this sacrifice. You are in line to become king now. If you strike our father, you would be throwing all of this away. \n\nFor me, there is not as much at stake. Just speak the command and I will go, brother.
Daedra, imprisonment, and crazy Bosmer—there is no end to Hazazi's suffering. At least you are here again to help me.
First, a question. Where did you come from?
Hazazi's tail swishes with joy.
Because you are no soldier, which is useful. You can speak with the locals, assure them we are not invaders or marauders.\n\nNow, come. Let us try to fit in.
Rescue? Azsu does not need rescue. His claws are sharp and his wounds are minor!\n\nBut …. perhaps it is better to have allies in a place like this, yes?
The Daedra are blind as bats when Azsu stalks his prey.
What? That isn't possible.\n\nNo matter. I'll rekindle the shrine's fire with my own essence, but you must promise to destroy them. You saw what happens to those who possess the tomes!
What does she not do? Shuzura is the Clan Mother of S'ren-ja. Arbiter of disputes, leader in rituals venerating the Two Moons Dance, eldest of the women in the village.
Pah! Rakhad was my assistant for many years. Made himself invaluable. Then Shuzura finds he has been in contact with the smugglers and skooma dealers from Pa'alat!

There is not much to tell, my new assistant. We are a sleepy town, yes? \n\nWe trade with Willowgrove, try to keep the men from going to Pa'alat or Hadran's Caravan, and the merchants make trips to Dune when we need supplies.

Yes. There can be no doubt. The Withered Hand … we have never faced such a threat, but it is our duty to stop them.\n\nYou … you must become one of us, you must become an Ash'abah. Then you must stop the Withered Hand.

There is a ritual. My daughter … I told her the ingredients were for an antidote, but she knows now, they are for your initiation.\n\nThere is not much time. You must decide … are you willing to join us, to become an Ash'abah?
A simple Khajiit, doing what she can to survive. \n\n<<1>> came to this shrine for guidance. It's said the flame gives visions to those who seek it.
Answers to unasked questions. Mysteries defined by the stars themselves. And if <<1>> makes some gold along the way, all the better.\n\nThis shrine is key to all of these things.
While searching for the shrine, a spirit appeared to me and warned me away.\n\nDon't you see? Hermaeus Mora rewards the pursuit of knowledge. The spirit is a test to keep lazy seekers away!
It's a shrine to Hermaeus Mora, Daedric Prince of knowledge. They say if you stare into the fire, all will be revealed.\n\nBut without the ever-burning flame, there's no way to find the lost books.

Tomes, lost to the ages. They're full of secrets from an earlier time, a connection to our past and a bridge to our future.\n\nIt doesn't matter what lies the spirit told. <<1>> will find those books!
No. You deserve to be honored for your actions, but the vizier says that by law, you must be exiled instead. \n\nI-I don't know what to do ….
Then that is a blessing. Once the books begin calling to you, there is little time before they ensnare you completely.\n\nBurn the books! Don't let their burden destroy you.
Don't listen to her! Remember the visions. Remember what happened to those who possessed the tomes!\n\nBurn them now, before it's too late!
I showed you an echo of what happened to the previous seekers, yes. But I did not conjure them from nothing. What you saw was the truth of it!\n\nI beg you … burn the books!
Of course! He's the Daedric Prince of forbidden knowledge. These tomes can only be destroyed by his energies.

He was. Sameer went on to start a family and a tribe in exile. They wandered the desert as nomads and became known as the Ash'abah.\n\nHaqmir became king and ruled peacefully until years later, when he again faced the threat of necromancers and undead.

This one knows the proper care and handling of old texts. Also, the importance of trade.\n\nTo you the books are useless things, but to me they have value. Hand <<1>> the books in return for value. Just think, no more spirit to natter at you!

You are full of surprises! And to rest any fears you may possess, <<1>> will bring them to the scholars at <<Ac:2>>. This one will do nothing with the books until they are certain no dangers lie within.\n\nNot that knowledge can ever be dangerous.
<You lift the books toward the fire, but your hand freezes in place. You feel a prickling shoot across your skin. A faint pain blossoms in the back of your head.>
<The books slip from your fingers. The flames roar. The pain fades.>
Shuzura confronted Rakhad about his dark dealings. He laughed, said she had become a "feeble old cat." She showed him. Had Rakhad run out of town. Now no one doubts who runs S'ren-ja.

I heard a pine thrush call, but those birds aren't native to Black Marsh. Then I saw my friend raise her mace and bring it down on my helmet.\n\nBut now I know their smell. Sweet with decay, like swampwater. A lingering taste of burnt leaves.

The deed is done, Sameer. Whatever that thing was, it was not our father. I know that in my heart.\n\nWe must respect the law though. I struck down our father; I desecrated his remains. I must be exiled.
It's quite literally your skin to risk. Hope you have better luck than my friend!\n\nMe, I'm getting out of here. Soon as you make a diversion, of course.

He was. Haqmir went on to start a family and a tribe in exile. They wandered the desert as nomads and became known as the Ash'abah.\n\nSameer became king and ruled peacefully until years later, when he again faced the threat of necromancers and undead.
Moons, yes. Very public, very angry. Some kind of difference of opinion? Zal-sa does not know.\n\nAsk the Clan Mother if you'd like to know more.

Yet I have no patience. Burn the vats, little plaything. Please me with your actions, and I'll please you with your life.\n\nOh, but don't fret. I honor my pledges. I even have a present to build your anticipation.
Small things, but they add up. An old man complaining of rats, someone said their home was haunted.\n\nAnd Zal-sa thinks someone said children were stealing their crops.
I'll bet she did, mangy old Khajiit. Bah.

Maybe a week? Yes, just over a week. Those nasty creatures have been fouling my water and scrabbling around down there that long.\n\nDisgusting. If Shuzura liked me as much as she claims, she'd have sent someone over sooner.

Let's just say Shuzura isn't blind like this old cat. She knows a good thing when she sees it. And she's been trying to see Milk Eyes … I mean, she's been trying to see me for years now. \n\nI don't need that in my life. Clan Mother is crazy.
Tazia. The Clan Mother's attendant, along with Zal-sa … who, now that she thinks about it, she hasn't seen in hours.\n\nThat's not important right now.
Tazia just did what anyone would have done, she thinks.\n\nAhem. Tazia will go tell the Clan Mother what has happened here. You go tell Milk Eyes his "rats" are gone, yes?
Hmmph. Nice work. \n\nI'll get <<1>> to have <<2>> seal up the cave, clean up my well, and such. She's good at such things.
Yes, please. I know Laudine and Varius would not want to exist as vampires, preying on the weak and innocent, living on blood. Burning them before they can rise as bloodfiends would be a mercy.
By now they're either dead or turned. Vampires are not especially patient creatures. I pray that they're only dead but fear they have been turned. I beg you to help end this nightmare for them.

Your reticence is infuriatingly enticing. Very well, <<1>> used Hist sap and my stolen essence to create his skin-stealers. The Hist sap is what steals the victims' memories.\n\nIt's all to acquire the <<CA:2>>. With it, he has all of Black Marsh.

My patience grows thinner than you'll be after I fit you with a scathing-girdle! Fail to uphold this bargain and I'll instruct you in pains of which you've never conceived, mortal.\n\nWait, what is that swamp-rat doing to the Vault door?

Well, I hate them and want them to writhe in Oblivion for all time. That enough for you? \n\nThey wiped out my gang. They hit us like a ton of manure. One minute, we'd never heard of them, the next they had their weapons sticking into most of us.
Who knows? I don't care much. I heard they're all over Cyrodiil. Once I rebuild the Quickstep Bandits, I'm going to wipe them out, wherever I find them.

What rock have you been living under? Everyone's heard of the Quickstep Bandits! It was the best bandit gang in all of Cyrodiil, led by yours truly. We stole from the rich and gave to ourselves. We were feared from Warden to Bloodmayne.

Lurchers. Take seeds from the Shimmering Tree in the village and plant them in the Orcs' camp. In a few minutes, they'll sprout out with a vengeance.\n\nThe Orc Chieftain won't surrender so easily though. Just kill him. Leave the rest to the lurchers.

Those cursed Black Daggers happened. Word of our success must have spread across Cyrodiil, and they came to take over. They jumped us and killed everyone but me. I just barely escaped with my life and have been hiding out here ever since.

I'm starting over. I need to gather some funds, and then I'll rebuild the Quickstep Bandits. I'll be more careful this time, keep things quieter. We'll jump the Black Daggers as soon as I've got enough folks with me. They're all going to die!
Because, my lovely, now you will fight in the main arena and Zara will have to slice your lovely face herself.
Oh yes, my lovely. We shall, indeed.

There seem to be a lot more rumors than any real facts.\n\nSome say he's a man. Others say he's a spirit, an embodiment of the forest. What I find most fascinating though is the rumor that he actually shapes the entire forest. That's just incredible!

Very well. Then here it is. Go to the makhadda in the back of the tent and drink.\n\nBe prepared, initiate. The potion will bring on a vision of the past. When the vision is over, you will know what it means to be Ash'abah.

Ha! Of course not. He's mainly here acting as my guardian. \n\nThey warned us that this place was dangerous, and if the Wilderking is really as unpredictable as people say … well, never hurts to be prepared.

Me? I was born and raised in the Summerset Isles, on a rather small island known as Silatar. It's a pretty secluded place. \n\nGrowing up there was what first sparked my interest in studying nature magic, but … well, it was very lonely.

He is the voice and spirit of the Wood Elves. They say he is, was, and will be their greatest leader … whatever that means. \n\nThis one knows him as an unrivaled diplomat. He is also the Dominion's best hope of resolving this matter peacefully.

Chieftess Niriel wasn't wrong about the Orc war captain. I did my best forest spirit impression and nothing fazed him!\n\nHe's pretty angry at the way the other Orcs reacted to the destruction of the totems, though.
Oh no. I'm not a fighter. The Wood Elves of Bramblebreach are pacifists, see. We usually have guardians do our fighting for us.\n\nMy advice? Don't let him hit you.
Our esteemed vicereeve represents the Aldmeri Dominion's interests in <<1>>. He is personal retainer to <<2>>.\n\nHad <<3>> not returned, he would advise a King. Pity.
Representatives of the Aldmeri Dominion. <<1>> carries the interests of Summerset and <<2>>. <<3>> and <<c:4>> represent the Valenwood.

It's perfectly situated for naval stagings against Cyrodiil. Furthermore, our holdings depend on our naval prowess. If this island were left to its own devices, our enemies would find a way to use it against us.\n\nBut such speculation isn't healthy.

Eh? What does it matter? Ezzag grows moon-sugar, of course. It's a common staple in Reaper's March. We trade it with other villages, and sell it in the markets of Dune.\n\nHave you ever had moon-sugar encrusted ham? Delicious!
None of your business.\n\nGo bother the clerk. He doesn't know when to shut up, either.
No, little mortal, I am neither your jailor nor your tormentor. I am merely a disinterested observer who finds some tiny enjoyment in your predicament.
Few come here by choice. Between the fumes from the fissure and the monsters crawling up out of it, Little Oak Place isn't the best market.
Find out why <<1>>'s senche-tigers roll on their backs instead of filling their bellies with rat.\n\nDoes one expect to keep his job if the inspectors find vermin in our fields?
At best? The inspectors will recommend our moon-sugar be confiscated.
Like that oak behind me, I believe that great things will come in time. That is why I stay.\n\nPlus, my cart broke down on the other side of town. I'm stuck here until I can afford another.
Ha ha! You have made Ezzag's day. No, his week! Ezzag shall name the next barn he raises in your honor.

Chorrol is far from Black Marsh. I hear the call of the Hist tree and long for its embrace. The soil of Cyrodiil is poor for Hist and Argonian. We cannot grow here.\n\nI wait only for the roads to be safer. Danger swirls everywhere during wartime.
When moon-sugar runs dry, people turn to smugglers. With smugglers comes skooma.\n\nBut the inspectors aren't from here. If we tell them, they will not listen!

When the wind goddess Khenarthi first traveled across the heavens, legends say she grew tired and rested in the branches of a small sapling before resuming her journey.\n\nThat sapling became the Great Tree, and gave <<1>> its name.
Yes, that's <<1>>! Please, you must find him!\n\nHe's all <<2>> has left.
<<1>> heard many things in <<2>>. <<3>> leads the skooma-peddlers within a nearby cove. Its entrance is on the beach across from <<4>>.

To the east, a plantation burns. Was it due to the inspectors' recommendations? Who can say?\n\nEither way, <<1>> will weep for our passing. With Laughing Moons gone, skooma will flow through the streets!

Ha! You pull this one's tail, yes? A white powder, very sweet, used as spice for food. \n\nSome of us believe it gives true insight into ja-Kha'jay, where all fates are bound. Others use it to brew skooma.
You know of moon-sugar, yes? The moon-sugar cane grows well on these isles. With my people's sweet tooth, there can never be enough to sprinkle on our meals.
It is not this one's place. The monks at Two-Moons Dance might instruct you, if you seek them out.
Poison.\n\nSkooma-peddlers claim a single drop lets you escape from the world. It's because drinking the stuff makes you want to drink more of it, until you want nothing else.
We must pay our debts. If our neighbors own more land, how do we match their crops at market? We must turn to alchemy to grow better crops, yes?
Yes, our crops came in much bigger this season. Not that it matters now.
Yes, <<1>> shares a temper with hurricanes. After a great quarrel with this one, he stormed off and left us short-clawed. Father had to cancel his trip to <<2>>, and now he's ….
"Do not eat the rats," this one says. Do they listen? No!\n\nStupid senche. Lazy senche!
It was not this one that did those things. He … he remembers. The screams, the anger, the blood … Akkhuz-ri remembers. He was ridden, controlled, by an ancient evil. We call it the Dark Mane.
This one remembers it talking to Javad Tharn … speaking of dark treachery. Visiting places throughout the March. But no, Akkhuz-ri does not know where it went. Please, we should leave this place.
<The order was incorrect! The spell fizzles and doesn't work.>

Uncle Enak and I were always close, I suppose? Kalari's father died when she was a cub, and after he treated me like a daughter.\n\nHis only other family in town is my other uncle, Ezzag. He already has a farm on the edge of town.
You are a guest of this council and you insult me? I will not abide such disrepect, outsider.\n\nNow tell me. Why do you believe that Molag Bal would renege on our agreement?

They began showing up almost immediately after uncle died. Very strange.\n\nKalari does not recognize any of their faces, and as far as she knows no one has died in the house. Uncle passed away while on a trip to Dune.

Oh, Mathal is probably off getting into trouble. Again. After our father passed away my uncles Enak-do and Ezzag tried to teach him right from wrong. He would never listen.\n\nKalari has barely seen him since we inherited this house.
I have heard your words and I shall think upon them. Please, speak to the other elders and tell them of your fears and concerns.
You have a wit about you and your words have given me much to consider. Have a care, though. Valenwood was once my home.\n\nSpeak to the other elders while I think about this.

So you say. But your words carry an insolence and a rudeness I must consider, as well.\n\nI shall think about what you have said. Talk to the other elders. Share your so-called wisdom with them and we shall see what comes of it.

I require neither your pity nor your condolences. I have listened to your words, wild and fanciful though they may be, and given you your due for your honor deed.\n\nNow away with you. I have other things to do.
I sought to avenge my father's memory, but was captured by bandits. Mother saw my capture and sent you here to assist. Next, you untie me and we kill <<1>> for his crimes.\n\nSimple, you see?
I … what? I hear your words but I do not understand what they mean.\n\nPlease, you have given me much to think about. I think. Share your news with the other elders and leave me to my thoughts.
The poor animals that roam the Valenwood … the people. I … shall consider what you have told me and pray for an end to the pain and suffering.\n\nThank you for sharing this news with me.

You might be laboring under the misapprehension that the entire arena is impressed with your prowess, but now they're going to see you for what you really are: an arrogant prat. \n\nBest of luck. You're going to need it.
This one has been trapped for what feels like an eternity. Let's leave here at once.
The door at the top of the tower has sealed with a warded barrier. I've seen the Worms use similar sorceries before. It will sear you to ash if you touch it.
Kargand? This one's brother? Why would he follow me to this place?\n\nIf he is trapped as I was, I will not leave him behind. This existence is one of nightmares.
This one is  grateful you came back. Please, let us escape this place.\n\nIt tears at my mind and soul.
This is really uncomfortable. Maybe you could just cut me out of here first?

Here's a thought. The flesh atronachs that patrol the castle halls are assembled in a laboratory very close to the warded door. \n\nIf you created your own atronach, it would be bound to obey you. You could force it to smash through the barrier.

It's a simple process. A child of five could do it. Unfortunately, we don't have a child of five, so I'll be forced to walk you through it.\n\nYou'll need some good-sized chunks of flesh. Take them to the laboratory, and I'll contact you there.

Oh, they've got the relics. \n\nFrom what I've overheard their leader, Accalia, divvied up the relics to his favorite lieutenants, but kept the chalice for himself. I think he's is selling it or something.
These tunnels just go on and on. And lots of them are trapped. \n\nYou can spot the triggers for the mechanical traps if you go slow and look closely. The trouble is, some of these traps are magical.

Ha! Who'd have thought, eh? I left Winterhold as a pup. All I remember was that cold. \n\nAnd I'm not talking about those balmy Skyrim winters. I'm talking about Hildrif, that cold-hearted daughter of the jarl. Brrr!
Because I got out of there as soon as I could! I traveled the world a bit. Took in the sights, y'know. But I knew I was home when we came ashore here in Sentinel.

To Sovngarde with that! Ship them off to the Pale! Let them pal around with the horkers for a while, then see what they say about the Alik'r. \n\nThis is paradise! Stiff salt breeze off the bay, sunshine the whole year round. Paradise, I say!

Stout folk. Stiff-backed, of course, but good-hearted. They weren't thrilled about me buying this place at first, but they got over it when they tasted my mead. \n\nThey don't laugh as much or as loud as Nords—but they don't fight as much, either.

If you're talking about the docks, not much. I've heard they walk funny. Sort of bow-legged, like an Elf just out of the saddle. Ha! \n\nWe shouldn't talk too loud, though. The locals don't take kindly to folk speaking ill of their dead grandpas.
Too late, sugar-thief. The fire destroyed every last calcinator.\n\nWait, I expected my sister to check on the tools herself. Why did she send a stranger?
You lie! My father left yesterday to trade in <<1>>. Didn't he?\n\nOh, no. I set the fires to destroy those damned tools, not to hurt anyone. Not to hurt my father!

We have to go out to the Binding Pool and channel the energy to rebind the serpent. I've read everything I can, but this is old, wild magic. I don't know if I can do this. \n\nAnd if the Maormer mage is out there … well, I certainly can't defeat him.

All right. If this works, and you are able to defeat the Maormer mage … I'll need you to do one more thing—when I say the word, use the blood rune to activate the final seal—that's it.\n\nAll right. We can do this. Yes. All right. Let's go!

We lost our last harvest to the thunderbugs. Despite the debt, <<1>> bought alchemical tools. To improve our crop, she said.\n\nBut last week I caught her brewing skooma. That vile drug destroys lives! When she refused to stop I knew what must be done.
Then you have done what I could not. My husband now rests with the ancestors, free of the skooma enslaving him.

My sister despises sand under her claws, but recently I saw her digging out on the beach. Why else would she be out there, if not to bury skooma?\n\nI should go to my father. Would you look for any skooma hidden on the beach?

I don't want my family imprisoned. The fire was to destroy any trace of skooma.\n\nRecently I saw my sister bury something on the beach. I was headed there next, but I should be with my father. Would you search for the skooma she hid on the beach?
Of course they are. That's what the council does. Sometimes I think that's all they ever do.\n\nBut do you think they're going to help you?
Of a certainty. King Fahara'jad, blessings of Ruptga be upon him, is King of Hammerfell, and rules over the Alik'r and many points beyond. This is his center of power—and the Forebears'.
Of course you did. I know you did. Now we just have to wait.\n\nAh, someone's stepping through the portal now. Here comes the council.
Really? You're not serious are you? Oh, may the spirits guide me through this dark hour.\n\nWell, we're about to find out what they thought. Here comes my father now.
Do not concern yourself. The King's rulership over these lands and its people is firm as stone—among Crown and Forebear alike.

Indeed. Our realm is … diverse. The Forebears are progressives who firmly support the Covenant. Their counterparts are the Crowns—traditionalists who cling to the ways of lost Yokuda and reject the practices of Tamriel.

King Fahara'jad, may Tava grant him eternal life, has made great contributions to the war effort. We Redguards are unparalleled in swordsmanship and grand strategy. Many of our most talented officers have already taken command of battalions overseas.
It is death in a bottle. Distill moon-sugar cane the right way and the crystals make you happy and stupid. Do it the wrong way and you get shaking fits, you foam at the mouth, and then you die.

When <<1>> embraced skooma with more affection than he did with me, I gave him every chance to claw his way back.\n\nBut skooma-peddlers are slavers of the mind itself. When <<1>> turned his addiction into enterprise, there was no return.

Poisoned arrows to stun, a blade to finish. I spoke to each as they lay frozen on the dock, before adding crescent moons to their throats.\n\nThese unclawed shaveskins had it coming for pulling <<1>>'s father into their fold.

The council can no longer ignore the truth happening around us. For too long we obeyed our vows and waited for a reward that will never be granted.\n\nShould we continue on our path, even after Valenwood is destroyed?

It means that your argument has convinced us. I sent runners to unlock the ruined passage that leads to the tower. My daughter said that you were interested in the place.\n\nI will also send a group of soldiers to aid you against Molag Bal.

No agreement was reached. Some sided with you, others were not swayed, but we remain divided on what to do.\n\nWithout a clear decision, we must continue on the course we currently follow. We remain in the service of Molag Bal.

It means that the time has come for you to depart the Moonless Walk. You are no longer welcome here. If any of our people aid you in any way, they will be exiled from the clan.\n\nWe appreciate the honor deed, but this conversation ends here.

Not for long. I always know it's month's end when debt collectors pound at our door, but last month they didn't show. When I asked why, <<1>> said not to worry.\n\nThis must have been her scheme. She's always had father wrapped around her tail.
Oh, and our <<z:1>>!\n\nIt must have fallen overboard when we beached. Our lookout saw those skink-fingered pirates make off with it. You'll have to get <<Az:1>> back, any way you can.
They already did. That's the problem! Moon-sugar makes you sleepy if you eat too much.\n\nRats eat moon-sugar, senche eat rats, and then? Lazy senche! Especially you, <<1>>.
Not with sugarbellies. These useless senche could only kill a rat if they fell upon it. From a great height.
Thunderbugs nest nearby. They defend their delicious eggs from anyone who'd make a meal of them, yes? If you grabbed an armload of eggs ….
Go inside, lock the doors, wait until they leave? No, let this one think. Without senche hunters, what could ….\n\nThunderbugs … heh. No, it would never work.

Undoubtedly! But they'd hesitate to harm the eggs, once you possess them. Smash an egg into each rat nest, and the thunderbug's electric frenzy kills the rats before the inspectors arrive.\n\nYou're sturdy, yes? A little shock won't stop you!
What? Let Kalari see that. Mathal and Enak were running skooma? \n\nAnd for Rakhad, of all people. Shuzura's old assistant. Dark moons and dull claws!

Kalari does not know … but wait. Right here in the letter, uncle says to "get Kalari out of the house." And he even says "make her think it is haunted, or something."\n\nMathal, moons bless him, is not very creative. Could he be behind the ghosts?

Rakhad's house. That's where he has to be. She kept seeing him near that well, wandering about. Kalari thought he was just being lazy, drinking water. \n\nTo do this magic, or whatever it is, he would need a private place. That must be it.
Yes! You did it. You really did it. I've tried for so long to convince them, and now we can finally leave this wretched place. I can look upon a real sky!\n\nWhat did my father tell you to do?

When the council finally makes a decision, they act with speed and certainty. I suggest you head for the door to the ruined passage as quickly as you can.\n\nI'm going to talk to my father. I want to be a part of the group we send to help you!
No! How could this happen? I can't believe they didn't listen to you. How could they be so foolish?\n\nBut I'm not giving up. I refuse to let it end like this!
Take this key and head northwest. Look for the ruined passage. It leads to the tower.\n\nDo what you need to do and maybe, despite themselves, my people will get the help they deserve.
Exile, death—anything is better than continuing like this!\n\nBut understand how grateful I am that you tried to help me. No one else has ever listened to me before. I appreciate it. Now go!
Something you'll want to hear. You just made the Prowler seaworthy, and <<1>> always pays her debts.\n\nGo, talk to her. She only bites if you give her good reason.

Our lookout watched the Sea Vipers drag a Dominion marine into a cave. Later, he saw your friends remove the marine's body.\n\nIf we weren't so short-handed I'd have ordered his rescue, but three of my own crew were missing.
Before we understood the danger, I sent my crew to scavenge among the shoals so we might repair the Prowler. We thought they'd disappeared, but one just returned—and she tells a harrowing tale.
The Sea Vipers happened. Now there's a new storm brewing, and I fear they're the cause of it.\n\n<<1>> recovers below. Hear what she has to say for yourself.
But the room still spins! Why did I board this accursed ship?
Of course. What do you need?
No, but she serves the Dominion. <<1>> gave me our letter of marque herself. We were asked to scout for the fleet.\n\nThe only thing we spotted was a hurricane.

I spent much of my youth in the Summerset Isles, amongst the Altmer. My parents were travelers who always had an ear to the ground. If you understand my meaning.\n\nAfter they died, I went to sea. It's how I ended up on the Prowler.

Originally, the lights were a gift from Meridia. Power that protected the city and made life easier for its inhabitants.\n\nWhen she pushed the city into Coldharbour, she filled the lights with even more of her divine power.

As you no doubt noticed, Molag Bal's realm has its own defenses. Things that teleport onto this plane tend to get scattered. As were your allies. As were the lights.\n\nThey could be anywhere, but most likely they are guarded by Molag Bal's forces.

Rumors, only, I'm afraid. \n\nI have heard tales of a strange prison to the northwest, a tower that is not a tower, that guards one of the lights. And others whisper of a vile laboratory to the southeast that distorts the purity of Meridia's light.
Please, I only have 200 gold.
Really? O, Wayfarer, you bring me unbelievably good news.
Then I've got a little surprise for you. In the next round, you get to dance with yours truly. And I never lose.\n\nNow we'll really see what you're made of. See you in the main arena!

It awakens feral instincts and ferocity. The result, as you've seen, was chaos.\n\nThe fighting that ensued unearthed a host of Dwemer constructs that gladly joined the fray, and the mine became a battlefield.

Return to the Hollow City when you are ready.\n\nKing Dynar has begun to form a council of war and wants to discuss plans and strategies. I believe the assault on Molag Bal's inner sanctum shall begin soon.

You got it. Look, my brother's the expert, but I think the Daedra are using the projection lenses to spy on the people trapped in the library. As long as the lenses are active, the doors won't open.\n\nI'm thinking sabotage is in order.

King Dynar and Vanus have begun to rally the troops. They have called for a council to meet here in the Hollow City.\n\nThere are decisions to be made. Plans to draw up. The time for war fast approaches, and we need to be ready.
Nothing would please Ishalga more. You are aware that it is her right as defending champion to set the rules?
First, you must bring Ishalga a gift of skooma. This is a banned substance produced from pure Elsweyrian moon-sugar.
The Grand Champion has spoken her terms. You are free to do as you wish.
Feluni's staff confiscated some recently. It's in her private quarters.
I've got eyes and ears everywhere, you know. And I can help you with your problem. You see, I have a key to Feluni's office.
Me? Oh, nothing. All I need is for you to win against Ishalga. Despite your popularity, Ishalga is still heavily favored. With your success in the arena, I'll make a fortune.
None whatsoever. Here's the key. You'll find the office around the corner. But remember: If you win, I win. If you lose, I lose, too. I don't like to lose. Good luck.
You got it? But how did you—? Never mind. Ishalga is just surprised you got it so fast.
How dare you accuse this one of such dishonor? \n\nYou will pay for such insolence! Ishalga will see you in the arena!
A pity. Someday you must show me your technique for egg acquisition, yes? It would be good to have alternatives the next time these lazy muskarses  go on a sugar binge.\n\nEven you, <<1>>!

The colony from Yath would have fallen, but Haqmir led his tribe against the necromancers and their army of risen dead. The Ash'abah accepted the dishonor of fighting the dead to save the kingdom. So it has been ever since.
Ask then. But be quick. If that serpent gets free, it'll destroy everything on the western shore of Valenwood, including Woodhearth.

The colony from Yath would have fallen, but Sameer led his tribe against the necromancers and their army of risen dead. The Ash'abah accepted the dishonor of fighting the dead to save the kingdom. So it has been ever since.

The seals are actually small pools of water. Elain, Ralos, and Valir—they're named after those who sacrificed their lives to bind the serpent. That's all I know.\n\nDon't know how the mage broke them or if the blood rune can really repair them.

I only know that he's very powerful. When our scouts approached him, he burnt them to cinders with the flick of his wrist. \n\nI suspect he also knew about this place beforehand, and he probably studied up on the seals … and on the serpent.

You mean did I just happen to be carrying one around? No. I found it with this text, and I'm proud to say I actually knew what it was!\n\nI've read a good bit about blood runes. Kind of a morbid fascination, I suppose.

You have now witnessed the first sacrifice, and you know that true honor need not be named.\n \nYou are one of us. You are Ash'abah.  We will recognize you as our brother and together, we will uphold the sacred duty of our tribe.

You have now witnessed the first sacrifice, and you know that true honor need not be named.\n \nYou are one of us. You are Ash'abah.  We will recognize you as our sister and together, we will uphold the sacred duty of our tribe.

Again, I'm only guessing here, but I read that the Maormer were once able to command such creatures.\n\nIt scares the Oblivion out of me to even consider it, but what if their mages have rediscovered such magic?

You have now witnessed the first sacrifice, and you know that true honor need not be named.\n \nYou are one of us. You are Ash'abah.  We will recognize you as our brother and together, we will uphold the sacred duty of our tribe.

You have now witnessed the first sacrifice, and you know that true honor need not be named.\n \nYou are one of us. You are Ash'abah.  We will recognize you as our sister and together, we will uphold the sacred duty of our tribe.

By successfully completing the trials, you shall show your worth and skills to our factions. Then you may participate in the great debate that has fractured our community for so long.\n\nAre you ready to undertake these trials?
The Trial of Spirit is a test to prove your worth to the scholars of Haj Uxith. It shall challenge your mind and determine your strength of spirit.
Yes. Spoiled from the sun and … well … I hate to speak ill of Ra-Netu, blessings upon them, but they did some minor damage as well. I had more reagents on a boat in the harbor. But it sunk.
I'm not sure if I will ever be all right, but I live.\n\nI'm ashamed that I thought Zur was silly and scatterbrained. My time melded to him taught me so much. Zur had … a good soul.
As you wish. Please speak to An-Jeen-Sakka to begin the Trial of Body.
As you wish. Speak to Treeminder Xohaneel and she will start your trial.

We're going where the holes are—there are a few big ones they're coming from. Collapsing them may not stop the Hollow completely, but hopefully it'll at least slow them down. \n\nIf not … well, at least we'll go down fighting! You lead the way.

I believe that the crystal powering the device is one of the fabled Lights of Meridia. Grab the crystal and meet me outside. You should be able to open the exit door.\n\nWith my strength returning, I can teleport myself to a safe place.
My arse it is! Look at those meats! Prime cuts! Just a little … you know … dry. Wait—no, this one is wet.
Excellent. Our gracious Inspector has been most patient with us. Perhaps witnessing your ingenuity will affect his findings.

From what I've read, it sounds like that might not be possible. \n\nThis is no ordinary sea serpent. The text refers to it as the "Great Serpent." I don't know what that means, but apparently binding it here was the only way to stop it.
I don't know what to say. She—well—she didn't make it home.
I thank you.\n\nI hear you were the one who drove off the Ra-Netu. I know it's blasphemy, but I wish you'd slain more of them. My Donya didn't deserve this.

I managed to make it deep into the caves before I was caught. The summoner was building an array of sorts with strange pillars similar to those holding the horns. It must be powered by magic.\n\nThat array should be destroyed as well.
Of course. Or do you wish to let them rest and take the other this time?

Our Hist cares for us, protects us. To preserve our culture, our Hist tree struck a bargain with Molag Bal.\n\nNow the crystal provided by the Lord of Brutality somehow keeps the Hist alive, but it cannot fully heal the poison in this soil.

I'll destroy it. With the money we spend to rebuild, it will be like the skooma never happened. I'd rather debt collectors pound at our door than skooma dealers.\n\nDamn my eyes. Father should've been in <<1>>!

Three statues at the top of the pyramid represent the challenges our values must contend with. Place the gems in the correct statues to symbolize overcoming these challenges.\n\nThen meet me at the base of the pyramid when you have finished the trial.
Take these amulets and speak to the people on the south pyramid. Give each amulet to the person that best represents its spiritual quality. For each correct match, you will receive a gem.
