Akatosh is the primary deity of the Eight Divines. He appears as a Dragon, to those blessed enough to see him. Thus he is sometimes known as the Dragon God of Time.\n\nHe is known as Auri-El to the Elves.

Indeed. The Hollow are all created from the same mold, and the Hollow Lords are the mold. Without them, there can be no new Hollow.\n\nIndanas has taken the Shadow Watch to defeat the last Hollow Lord. Exit the fort through the pit, and join her.

They are the greatest of the Aedra, the beings that created Mundus, our world. After Akatosh, they are the gods Dibella, Arkay, Zenithar, Stendarr, Mara, Kynareth, and Julianos. Akatosh is their chief, but all have their adherents.

Ah, the shipwreck? Worst hurricane I've seen in decades.\n\nIf you're headed through this plantation, watch your step. Last night some buildings caught fire. Usually the skeevers keep to themselves, but they're acting up something fierce.

In the hands of these necromancers, the strength of the Ansei Wards is much weakened. With some magics, they might even be able to pervert the Wards' power for terrible ends.\n\nIt is good that we will soon have them back.

Of course. All priests of Tu'whacca know such things. \n\nThe Wards were forged when three Ansei gave their lives to channel their spirits into their blades. They did this so that the Wards would protect the consecrated dead.
Saw him on the way in. We gave his daughter some medical supplies, but he looks bad.
Dominion government. I'm an officer, charged with keeping the peace. They sent us to <<1>> weeks ago.\n\n<<2>> commands us. He's at <<3>>, toward the center of the island.
The Prowler needed a cook, so I volunteered. First time to travel by sea. Thought all the water would be like the marshes back home.\n\nBut now, even the smell of food … oh, gods!
Grunda's a cheeky one, and she knows we're getting close. She's summoning reinforcements faster than Darien can kill them.\n\nYou'd best get to it!
Do not worry. This one is not afraid. The process can be reversed. Our research tells us this. Zur is optimistic. And if I die, then it is just on to another adventure, yes?

We are very different. Zur has learned much sharing a Dark Elf's mind. Few Khajiit experience such a wonder, yes? Gadris will do many great things, provided the unmelding works, and so will Zur. But this one would never choose himself over another.
Right! We control the rest of the Chasm now and the troops have matters well in hand.\n\nLet's go and have a sit down with Molag Grunda. She's always good for a laugh and a song.

Zur is Zur, but something is missing. This one's soul feels … emptier, somehow.\n\nBefore our meld, Zur thought Gadris was stiff and nasty. But I know better now. Gadris was brave and selfless. A true friend and a great mage. He will be missed.

We must leave this place. But first, the crystal that powers the device. It is one of the fabled Lights of Meridia, yes? You should take it. This one thinks it will be useful later on.\n\nZur will teleport outside and wait for you somewhere safe.

This is our home, our refuge from the chaos of Cyrodiil. Acolytes retreat inside for rest and meditation, reflecting on the world and Akatosh's plan for it. Having folk like you stare at us through the windows would be distracting.

Who knows? I sure don't. Anyone who does know isn't talking, not to me anyway. Abbess Shei-Chuna prays constantly for Akatosh's Word but has never received it, that I know of. Some say his plan is beyond mortal ability to understand.

In my youth on the plains of Deshaan, I was taught to worship the Tribunal—the false gods Almalexia, Vivec, and Sotha Sil. I would have been lost to their unholy idolatry if not for a chance encounter with a priest of Akatosh.

At great personal risk, he came to my village and preached the word of Akatosh. All around me, Dunmer jeered at him and threw rotten kwama eggs. But I felt a divine presence fill my heart with a light I had never before known.

Sadly no. He was tortured and killed. But before he died, he told me he came from Weynon Priory. That night, I ran away. Akatosh guided me here, protecting me from the dangers of the long road. I will serve him the rest of my days.
That farmer shook himself to death. You think I don't recognize a skooma overdose when I see one? That I don't know why skeevers are frothing at the mouth?\n\nI should arrest the lot of you.
I will need far more than luck—but I thank you all the same.
Indeed it did.

Yes, well, the city guard was taking some interest in my cargo just before the attack. Their suspicions, while totally unfounded, could have caused some delays. I've a very tight schedule, you see. \n\nNow, I shall start again. Unsuspected, this time.
That's a lot of skooma. I had my doubts, but I'm glad you came to your senses.\n\nNow, what should I do with you? What else are you hiding?
Last chance. If someone doesn't tell me where the skooma is, you'll all face the consequences.
Yes, well … it's my job to ask questions. Perhaps moon-sugar fumes can cause the skooma shakes. Maybe I see skooma where it isn't, sometimes.\n\nI'll leave them to their grief.
These Khajiit used you to cover up their crime? You did the right thing by giving this to me.
We've seen more and more <<m:1>> lurking around the island. They must have supplied the family with equipment needed to brew skooma.
Buying time to get your stories straight?\n\nGo ahead, I'll be right over here. One warning - my ears are as sharp as my dagger. I'll prove it to you if you even try to whisper.
Then <<1>> found nothing in the storehouses but suspicion. She's bluffing.\n\nWhat will you tell her?
What's right is allowing us to recover from tragedy, not suffer more of it.\n\nPlease. Make this right.
Then how am I having this conversation …? I mean, I-I feel different … I don't even think my heart's beating, but …. \n\nDo you think … I mean … am I undead?

Explains why <<m:1>> popped up all around the island. If they're running more and more skooma, they'll approach farmers to brew it directly. That kind of short-sighted greed is what leads to situations like this.
I'm not sure I believe you.\n\nYou're lucky <<1>> is busy with <<2>>. He doesn't have a lenient bone in his body.
I don't serve everyone for my health, scab. I've run this bar for years, and I'm not taking any guff from some shoreside soldier!\n\nNow that we've got that straight, what can I do for you?

And why shouldn't I be? I've lived here more than half my life, and I couldn't give a fig what any noble-born brat has to say about it!\n\nBesides, the longtails like my brews. Not a bad arrangement to do what you love and get paid for it too!

One of those comes in every month, seems like. These ruins aren't going anywhere. I just pack away the bar and wait for it to pass.\n\nEven if I lost everything, the Khajiit would get me back up and running. They're good folk.
From what I overheard, they split them up among the gang leaders, so they could be anywhere. \n\nYou'll have to search the whole place.

Please, adept. I'm going to be fine. As I said, translation of the books has taken a considerable toll. I'm exhausted. But it will be worth it. \n\nThe sanctuary will save so many lives, and give us all a chance to work in peace.
Yes. Some of them were talking about a broken bridge and a pit where they throw unwanted prisoners. They called it "the Croc Pit," so I guess there are crocodiles in it. Be careful where you step!
Thank you. I just need some time to steel myself and then I should be able to make it.
Only a little—stuck down here, I couldn't hear much. One relic is in an outside tower. And I know for sure the bandit leader has the Chalice of Mara. \n\nThat's it.

I … I know. She's very tired, even worse than before. But she's done masterful work in translating these books. And I'm sure she'll be an asset once we reach the island. She'll have plenty of time to rest soon enough!
I suppose she has been garbling her words a bit. I just assumed that it was due to mortal frailty … I sometimes forget how fragile you are. We will watch over her together, my friend.

We allow Molag Bal's minions to draw sap from the Hist tree. The only thing sustaining the Hist in this foul land is the crystal that Molag Bal gave us.\n\nBut over time, the crystal has poisoned the Hist. It is dying.

We believe that the crystal is one of Molag Bal's vampiric shards—foul relics that corrupt whatever they come in contact with.\n\nThe crystal only prolongs the suffering of the Hist. No matter the cost, that suffering needs to end.

If only it were that simple. Our Hist is weak, barely sustained by the crystal that feeds it. It hasn't spoken to us in a long, long time.\n\nBut I have had dreams. They revealed your imminent arrival and hinted at your involvement in our debate.
Then … the curse was meant to put the books in front of Valaste. She was meant to read them. Adept, this is very worrying. But we need to deal with this after the island is safe.
She'll be with you! She'll be fine for the moment. \n\nValaste, go with our friend here to close the portals. The adept will keep you safe.
My sister placed colorful seashells near whatever she buried. I bet there is a sack full of skooma vials next to them.\n\nI'll be with my father. If you find anything, bring it back to me.

He was tormented by the Daedra, worse than Bakkhara was. Perhaps for longer—time can work differently in the Daedric realms.\n\nA mage of Kargand's power could be a danger to Tamriel if he is driven to madness. He's always had a dark streak.
A vile skooma-peddler. <<1>> destroys families and brings great warriors low with his filth.

Skooma is distilled from moon-sugar, which is sacred to we who worship the moons and stars. But those who use skooma for pleasure quickly become slaves to its visions. Scum like <<1>> profit from this addiction.
He hurt his back in a terrible accident. He took skooma to relieve the pain, and it came to both sustain and enslave him. After years of its use, he withered to a shell of his former self.
<<1>> hasn't learned that fear and hatred cloud judgment. <<2>> said he would be foolish to seek revenge.\n\nBut he's a boy, and they have more important things to do than listen to their mothers.
I fear killing him may be the only solution, though Bakkhara would rather face the Daedra again than lose her brother.\n\nI can see on his face that he is fighting for his soul.

Kargand has never shown empathy towards anyone but Bakkhara. \n\nHe was always ready to advance at the expense of others. It is … touching he came back for this one, but he would not have done it for you, though you helped him.
This one … regrets it. But understands. Bakkhara will do it. Bakkhara owes him this much.\n\nAre you sure about this?
This one hopes you are right. Honestly, Bakkhara is glad.\n\nI will take Kargand with me to the Guild and we will do what we can for him. You're sure about this?

Yes, I do. You can keep the smirks and crude jokes to yourself, I've heard them all.\n\nFor your information, fertilizer is a booming field. Farmers can't get enough of it; animals can't stop making it. I just connect the two ends, so to speak.

Rhina was an Armiger in the Order of Diagna who died in the final days of the Siege of Orsinium. \n\nShe was born in the siege camp there and spent her entire twenty-six years fighting the Orcs. They say it was her sacrifice that brought us victory.

Hmm. That's inconsequential. Whatever it is, it may serve a purpose in our battle against the lord of Coldharbour. If we can acquire it, then this excursion will not have been a complete waste of time.
I told you. My fertilizer smells like roses. Everyone says so. With that sack on your shoulder, you'll smell better than ever.
We are doing our best to wrap and sanctify our honored dead. Many are hacked and cleaved and require dressing. What happened here was abhorrent.

Razul fought alongside Divad Hunding, leading the Ra Gada to conquer Alik'r. \n\nWhen the Na-Totambu and the Yokudan nobility came later, Razul made himself Yokeda to cement the power of the Ra Gada. Some call him the first Forebear.

Yes. She seized the throne the ancient way. \n\nLate in the first era, the King died with no heir and the nobles squabbled over the throne. Afsar solidified her rule by killing the opposition. Despite its bloody start, her reign was very peaceful.
We will attempt to rebury them with some modest dignity. Now, I mean no disrespect, but I must ask you to leave. The taint you bear may affect our rituals.
Lies are a coward's oasis, so I tell you the truth. During the attack, I committed a great sin. I am … hesitant to confess it, but I must if I am to retain my honor.
Don't play coy. The Captain's already paid an Emperor's mint to Ren-dro's madam.\n\nI'd try not to keep him waiting. Just prepare yourself for his … appetites.
Right, right. Just head inside and strum the harp when you're ready. The Captain's very particular about first impressions.
No! No, wayfarer. Had I attacked one of my ancestors, I would not be standing here among them.
I drew my sword.
No … no, of course you are right, wayfarer. The greatest shame is found in cowardice.  I made my choice. I will face the consequences. I thank you.

Do you think so? Forgiveness is a virtue we Redguards often struggle with, but surely our honored dead have learned it in the Far Dunes. I will show them my face and hope for the best. I thank you, wayfarer.
Thank you … farewell.
Is that not enough? We Redguards do not cast down our sheaths unless we aim to spill blood. \n\nI was cornered and I panicked. If the Ra-Netu had not stumbled ….

The Colovians are certain they hold Arenthia. They're getting sloppy. Most of them won't look past the uniform. The patrollers are a different story. Their one job is to be on the lookout for people like us. Stay clear of them.
Most of the patrollers are on their own, and generally carry torches even in broad daylight. Silly bastards. As long as you avoid them, you should be fine.

I appreciate your spirit, but save it for the game. \n\nI have been master of this game for thousands of years. Many have tried to defeat me. All have fallen. I confess that the game has begun to bore me. Where is the challenge?
Then <<1>> learns to stand with allies rather than on his own. He shows me he is ready. With time and training, he will honor his ancestors.
No, we killed a husk. My father died long ago.
Ahh, a taste of home! Look, do whatever you want. I'm out of here.
<<1>> brought dishonor and shame to our family. He turned his back upon us.\n\nI had no choice. Though he'd destroyed himself, I wouldn't allow him to destroy any others.

Father disappeared and plantation owners began to die. Mother knew he was proving himself to his new skooma-peddling masters. She searched, but found no trace.\n\nYears later, I heard of <<1>> the smuggler: a mean old Khajiit with a silver mane.

New recruit, eh? Then you need to know about our mission boards. The Bounty and Scouting boards are on either side of me.\n\nEvery so often, Sorcalin sends Vilya over with new missions. I post them to the boards for all to see.

Train at <<1>>. I'll honor the memory of who my father was, not what he became. Find me there, if you would.\n\nTravel by starlight, walker. May your footsteps fall silent and your blades strike true.
Bounty missions are simple: Kill enemy soldiers. If you kill enough of them, come back for a reward.
Information is vital to winning this war. Each Scouting mission sends you to a target deep in enemy territory. If you can get there and look around, report back as soon as possible.
About time. I almost gave this to someone else. Take it to Zan. You'll find him at the siege range, west of the Eastern Elsweyr gate. Just look for a Khajiit with singed fur.

How true! So you can understand my excitement!\n\nYou have come here of your own accord. You seek to defend the mages. So … unprecedented! Still, to participate, you must choose a side. There are no wild cards in this game.
I noted the ardor of the moons within you and sent you to aid <<1>>. That is help, yes?\n\nBut I would know, how did my son fare against <<2>>? Did he fight bravely, as he was taught?
They are in the game now, below us. They fight for their lives, doing all they can to survive.\n\nI'll be curious to see if they make it past the first trial. So few do, you know.

That portal will take you to the battleground. Find the mages there—if they haven't been eliminated yet.\n\nBe warned. Once you enter the portal, you are committed to the game. Remember that. I don't abide cheaters or quitters.
Oh yes! Unishi told me exactly what to expect, and I think it's going to be wonderful!
We need concrete evidence that Ren-dro is in bed with these bastards. \n\nGet inside their quarters, and search everywhere. Correspondence, letters, something … anything I can show to the Queen.
Of course there are! I trust you to get past them. Persuasion, bribery, intimidation … whatever it takes.\n\nI have some ideas on how you can approach them.

Sound theoretical extrapolations are what Gadris excels at. And this one's experiments support his research. We believe the device can be forced to unmeld our souls. In any event, we won't survive the soul-meld. At the very least, we must try.

What's that? Yes, Zur will pass that along. Now quiet, please.\n\nThe Overseer's in there. He put us into this Dwarven machine. He's dangerous. Many of the constructs that roam this place are under his control. Gadris recommends killing him quickly.

Mim talked about a plan to get us out of this … said we just needed to play along. But as soon as we got down here, the Dark Elf fled and the cat stabbed me. Said everything would be all right.\n\nNever trust a cat.
<Your hand shakes and your vision blurs, but your fingers do not release their grip on the books. The pain in your head is excruciating.>
Scared? Not at all. I'm terrified. He's arrogant, cruel, and vindictive. And those are his good qualities.\n\nTake my advice and stay very far away from Niro. It's healthier that way.
Imagine the flames are the waves of a vast ocean.

I used to be a bad person who did awful things for Niro. But I'm better now. Saw a chance to get out and I took it. Grabbed Marina and ran. Didn't stop running until we got here.\n\nMarina hates it here, but it's better than being back with Niro.
Cold waves on a clear blue ocean off the coast of Summerset.

Now picture an island. Trees around the island shimmer in the sunlight; each gently cresting ocean wave sparkles.\n\nMany stones, roots, and flowers on the island were shaped by magicka. Only two living Altmer possess such power.
One of those two Altmer stands outside the manor on this island. Her island.\n\nGo to her. Become her friend.

Indeed. A thousand pardons. I am preoccupied, to say the least.\n\nI must go and warn the guard about the threat to the Impervious Vault. If you would relay the news to my father, the king, though, I would be forever in your debt.

Octavimus, that's why. My fool of a husband had a good job, we had a nice house, lively friends—we had it all. He threw it away, for no good reason that I could see. And he dragged me here, to the butt end of Cyrodiil.

Oh, he babbled something about not feeling fulfilled, not liking who he was turning into, and other nonsense. Nothing that made sense. And he won't talk about it now. When I bring it up, he tells me to go sweep something.
Certainly. He used to be Octavimus's boss, back when my husband had a spine and ambitions. You want to have some fun, go mention Niro's name to Octavimus. Watch him soil his farmer pants.
You exposed the Maormer, and that was propitious, but it may also force the enemy's hand. This one does not know what they have in mind. Whatever it is, the Dominion must be well prepared.
A decision must be made. It may behoove us to take the fight to the Maormer immediately, or there may be other tasks you think more important to address first.

Possibly. They found an ancient relic there and absconded with it, as is their wont. Then the undead woke up. Hrrr.\n\nThey hold knowledge of this artifact - knowledge that could be of use in any upcoming hostilities. This one cannot say for sure.
It will doubtlessly save lives, and we need every loyal pair of hands we can get.\n\nIs it worth the time we will lose in the search? This one cannot say. That is for you to puzzle out.

It is hard to know the mind of an Altmer, much less a Sea Elf. They seemed content with the stalemate they had entered into with <<1>>, but now that the Dominion is in the picture they may resort to desperate, drastic measures.
A wise decision. The temple is on the eastern side of the island.To echo my good friend, <<1>>, move with haste!
Your compassion is well-placed. The ships foundered on the western side of the island. To echo my good friend, <<1>>, move with haste!
Then you will want to speak with <<1>> at the docks on the east side of <<2>>. She is champing at the bit much like you. Fear not, <<3>> will not be far behind.

He's a fine man. He was always giving me jewelry, perfume, all sorts of gifts. And he was hardly ever fresh.\n\nOctavimus should try to be more like him. All he gives me are dirty flowers he picks from the field. And ticks, mustn't forget the ticks.
Words, mostly. Plus some punctuation marks to make it easier to read. A little spit too, since I like to lick the tips of my pens.
I know what you meant. That was my polite way of saying it's none of your business. Let's just leave it at that.\n\nDon't you have a letter to deliver?

No one of any importance. Just a former employee of mine. I'm writing him a friendly note, to let him know that I still think of him from time to time. And that I know where he lives.\n\nAll that should matter to you is that he has some money for you.
Who wouldn't be happy to get a letter from me? You seem like a very suspicious sort, asking all these questions. I hope you don't bother poor Octavimus with questions like this.

A hurricane blew up out of nowhere just as we got within sight of Khenarthi's Roost. The seas went wild. We tried to make a safe landfall, but most of our ships foundered.\n\nI fear many of my men were lost, but I just don't know.

A lot of the survivors came ashore near Eagle's Strand. <<1>> suggested we move to high ground to survey the land. I think there might be more survivors along the western shore.\n\nWe can see a lot of wrecked hulls from here.
Good. We'll need every intact ship we can find if we're ever going to continue with our mission.\n\nOnce Khenarthi's Roost is secure, I'm certain we'll have more to do.
Honestly, I'm not certain. I've been told to focus on securing Khenarthi's Roost.\n\nIf you want to continue helping out, make certain the island's secure. Then we'll talk about what happens next.

We need to secure the Lane—the sea route between Elsweyr, Khenarthi's Roost, and Auridon. For that, the Dominion needs an uncontested presence on Khenarthi's Roost.\n\nMy marines will help provide that.

Ah … Samaea-do was picked to return to Khenarthi's Roost as part of the Dominion's military in the hopes that she can smooth the way for our forces to set up a more permanent base on the island.\n\nBut it is a bittersweet homecoming.

This one had hoped to sail into the main port of Mistral, far north of here, and perhaps take a few days leave to visit the nearby plantations. Her family still lives on the northern part of the island.\n\nStill, one still has hope.
Yes. This one was born here, last of her litter-mates, but first to leave for the mainland. She joined the military when war broke out and never imagined she'd be sent back home.
I was outside and I heard someone coming up behind me. Next thing I know, I am lying on the floor writhing in pain. I am sorry, friend. Wish I could tell you more.

This is Khenarthi's Roost, off the coast of Southern Elsweyr. We were supposed to make a more tactical landing, but that hurricane took us all by surprise.\n\nAt least we made it here alive. Not all of us were so lucky.
That's why I asked you to come early. I'm not sure what will happen either. Before they get back, I want to be carefree. We can visit some of our favorite places together.
You don't know what this means to me. Now, what will we do first? I know. Let's race to the lighthouse, like we did when we were little. Bet you still can't catch me!
Oh, you know. I say that the Green didn't give us all this to hold grudges. Give her another chance, you know? Besides, Bo would miss her if she wasn't here.
Bah. No business of mine. What am I, a Treethane? The only fate I decide is mine.

Glad to hear it! Good to know you weren't fooled by his promises. Or are you just saying that?\n\nMaybe he sent you to follow Mim. Maybe you're part of his game. This one doesn't know what to believe! And this stupid rune Thallik gave me. It's useless!

Thallik said to look for the runes on the ground. Some kind of circle. The moons take Mim if this one understood a word he said!\n\nYou figure it out. Just don't make Mim regret this. This one is trusting you because you haven't attacked Mim. Yet.
Bright moons light our path, then. Speak to Shazah, and she will describe the trial before us.
An ancient Ayleid ruin beneath us. The entrance is shut by magic, but we will get in eventually. The legends speak of treasure inside.
When I say "treasure," I expect junk and trash of no real value. You would not be interested.\n\nPerhaps another site would hold your interest more.
MmHmm. Hmm hmm Mmm mm.

It's that Sea Elf. Maormer, they call them. I think he's doing it just to annoy us.\n\nIf they'd just gag him, he couldn't cast his spells. But they need to question him, I suppose. I just hope he doesn't ruin my maps!

Me? I guess I am now. In Valenwood I was a cartographer. You know, a mapmaker! When they recruited me for this mission, I thought all I'd be doing is surveying land.\n\nTurns out, there's a lot more responsibilities. Oh well!

I know <<1>> will keep me alive. He far prefers a living form to the dead. Strange, how can I know this?\n\nI feel him stirring within me. Help <<2>> restore the Mourning Stone. Go, while you still can!
Those ruins draw evil to them. Sometimes it's undead, sometimes it's evil cultists, sometimes it's rabbits. Any place the Ayleids once lived, a vile aura seems to linger.
Don't let them pull the fur over your eyes. Rabbits are pure evil. You crawl into a rabbit den, see dozens of beady red eyes all around you, well, you're never coming out again. Mark my words.

All Elves are evil, of course. But Ayleids were the worst of them all. They tortured, killed, and ate anyone not of their tribe. Fortunately, they're all dead nowadays. Probably cannibalized themselves to death.

<<1>> will sustain me. Better a living form than a dusty old skeleton, I suppose. I'd hoped for more time to meditate, but this wasn't what I had in mind.\n\nGoodbye, my friend. You're what all in the Dominion should aspire to be.
There you go. Hurry, it won't remain open for long.
There you are. I'm afraid it won't remain open for long.
The Veiled Heritance tasked me to either destroy the Wilderking or convince convince him to join us - if he even exists.

Has she?\n\nI love Laniriel. But we swore an oath to leave a caretaker to protect the Fading Tree. That is the price the whole village must pay so that we can live in the paradise the Wilderking creates for us.

Mim needed to slow Juline down. She's hard-headed. Ready to rush into battle at the smallest provocation. It may not seem like it, but Mim saved her life.\n\nWhat does it matter if this one can't figure out what to do with Thallik's stupid rune?
She refused to step down from her position, so we killed her.\n\nHer guards actually tried to put up a fight. So entertaining.

Wait … you want to help the others? A shadow. That's what Lady Estre gave me. She said it would protect me as long as I did whatever it said. If I do a favor for it, it would do a favor for me.\n\nYou have to find the shadow.

I have my preparations to deal with, and you have yours.\n\nThe first step is to make sure the ritual targets the correct creatures. Marking the vampires' lairs with their own blood will guarantee this.
Then our journey continues for a while longer. Watching our steps from here on out, yes?\n\nIf you can still help my companions, Mim asks that you do so. We need to find a way out of this. Together.
The potion will work. You'll see. And know that I am grateful for your help. We both are.
You caught me. Sure, there's lots of folks around here who'd do it, but I like to ask newcomers to town to help out.

We're always looking for new folks to settle here. More people to share the workload means a better life for everyone.\n\nThen we've got undead in Culotte, and we see more Goblins every year. Settlers who can handle a sword are always welcome.
Sure have! Both Hisham and Octavimus were just passing through. I asked them to help gather produce, they saw the town, liked it, and decided to stay. It's a win for everyone.
Azartah is pleased with it. Trade is good, with much commerce between here, Alessia, and Drakelowe.\n\nAzartah was wise to find such a fragrant locale, yes?
Perhaps. The Goblins are a concern. I smell more of them nearby every year. We shall see how the village prospers.\n\nBut in business, the wise do not talk of their plans, no?

Why are you a member of the Dominion? Are all their causes noble? \n\nYou judge me, but how many Covenant or Pact loyalists have you murdered because you were following orders? Ever thought to reason with the Dominion's enemies?
I don't owe you an explanation of my choices. \n\nYou have Sangur's orders. Go kill your new enemy.
Truly? This one thinks you may have been led astray. The Moon Hallowed is a sacred and terrible burden, a role only for one soul in thousands.
Good. You can buy these weapons from siege merchants at our gates and castles, yes?

Driving off attackers is always the first step. Then repair kits can fix some of the damage, yes? Here is a practice repair kit for a siege weapon. Use it on a trebuchet, catapult, or ballista.\n\nWhen done, Taralin will speak with you.
And not a moment too soon. If I had to inspect one more bloody soul gem, I'd have thrown myself from the tower.

It was her older brother's fault—the dirty thief. He took advantage of her.\n\nHe came to Zariya, on the run from some dangerous people to whom he owed a great deal of money. He asked her to sell some items he and his friends had "acquired."

Have you heard of the temple of the Mourning Springs? Ancient, it is, but not visited by the people of the Roost. Avoid it, they do, with superstitious dread.\n\nBut someone must go there. Its waters are drying up, and the mourning springs must flow.

A fair question. I know things. Things that can help you. Here's a bit to whet your appetite.\n\nMannimarco isn't doing any of this to serve Molag Bal. His ultimate plan is to out-scheme the God of Schemes … and to replace him.
On the eastern side of the island. Go there, and your way will be revealed.\n\nLook for the moon-stones! They are the key.

But at a cost … this one saw. And this one would not envy you that choice, though she cannot fault your rationale.\n\nYou have prevented a great evil from gaining freedom and plaguing the Roost once again. Thank you.
The Amulet of Kings is the key to everything. Why do you think he kidnapped Sai Sahan? He's torturing him. Trying to get him to reveal the Amulet's hiding place.
I'd love to discuss this further, but this is hardly the place. Get me to a safe haven and I will tell you the rest. That was our agreement, was it not? Now, let's— \n\nWait. Did you feel that?
Precisely. With the Amulet at his command, Mannimarco believes he can trap Molag Bal's essence and absorb his power. He seeks to become a god himself!
This one and Bakkhara are very close. She has been there for me always and always will be. This one will stop at nothing to find her and will let no one stand in my way … friend or foe.

Judge Xiven has them on trial in the Hall of Judgment. From what I've been able to overhear, it isn't going well for them.\n\nTo get inside, we need to bring down that barrier. Then the mages and I can get back to the mission that brought us here.
The three elemental crystals, yes. But more than that. We also need a key to open the locked gate.\n\nI saw them place the gate key in a guarded coffer in the northern section of the ruins.

Defenders must be overcome and our banner must be raised on the flagpole. For castles, we must breach walls or sunder gates to reach the heart of the enemy stronghold.\n\nAll easier said than done, as you will see.

A trick I picked up. Made it easier to get around the Shivering Isles. I was using it to scout the area when I saw you approaching.\n\nSome consider my methods unorthodox, but the results speak for themselves. I certainly wasn't captured by the Daedra.
Do you think I haven't thought of this?\n\nBut I would be failing my oath to the Wilderking and the entire village if I didn't stay behind.

Indeed. The village can help raise my child, but I'm <<A:1>>'s only caretaker now.\n\nI'll stay behind to tend the tree, in accordance to my oath. The village must leave before its too late. Go. Tell Laniriel I—just go.

What? I didn't know. Why didn't she tell me? What kind of caretaker would I be if I didn't care for my own child? And yet, I have a responsibility to the entire village now. \n\nThis problem comes at a terrible time. I must decide quickly.

We are the only alliance fit to rule Cyrodiil. Taking the enemy's castles and resources is the way to prove this.\n\nYour participation in these actions enables you to acquire equipment and weapons from Dominion siege merchants.

Because Mannimarco has delusions of godhood. He cares nothing for the Empire, he seeks only power. \n\nI've never done battle with him before. He's far more powerful than I imagined. Ah, well. Too late for regrets. In for a bean, in for a beanstalk.
First things first. We need to get out of here alive.
We certainly can't go back the way you came in. I'd imagine they're swarming the grounds already. \n\nThere's a refuse chute further down the path. It's a bit of a drop, but we'll probably survive.

This one does not know what is memory—what is delirium. There was a great fire. Always there.\n\nThey pushed Bakkhara's soul against it, grated it against the heat, until Bakkhara was not there anymore. And the Daedra controlled what was left.
You stand at the Temple of Two-Moons Dance. Here, we learn and practice Riddle'Thar.
The way. The path. The road. Riddle'Thar is all of these, and none. For one, the road is a wall. For another, a wall the way.\n\nWe all seek our place in ja-Kha'jay. Riddle'Thar helps us find it.
In the way one follows a map through a maze, one follows Riddle'Thar through life.\n\nIt teaches us to avoid—and embrace—danger. To fight and to run away. To accept change and to stave it off.

A maze contains many things, not simply a way out. The best mazes hide many sweets behind traps and crevices.\n\nRiddle'Thar is not so much a way out of the maze as the way with the most sweets along the way!
Ja-Kha'jay. It is what we all hope to achieve.
The Lunar Lattice, where all fates are bound. Our place in the universe. For the Khajiit, anyway.
It is different for everyone. For some, it is to become King and rule over the little people, yes? Ha! We should all be so lucky!\n\nFor others, it is death. You have some experience with this, no?
Ha! One should hope not! If we are lucky, we reach ja-Kha'jay long before then! Otherwise, what is the point, yes?
Only that you have had your sugar stolen. A curious thing, that. <<1>> does not envy you.\n\nStill, keep your head about you and you will find the way.
<<1>> lets me perform small services for the temple. In exchange, I am fed. I can even watch them train, on occasion!
My family won't have me. I stowed away on a merchant ship and it brought me here.\n\nAfter months fighting with <<1>> for crab meat in <<2>>, I heard about the temple.
Of course! I'm quick! I can do half of what you see up there without even trying. Everything I can't, I'm learning!
Return to Deshaan and show my family how wrong they were! They'll have to take me back. If they won't, I'll make them!
Good. Then there is nothing more for us to discuss.\n\nLet us hope your brother learns to listen to my counsel and to make better decisions than you have.

In times of old, the carvings and adornments upon the walls would sing of the dance. Precious stones inlaid upon intricate plaques would speak to Masser and Secunda. \n\nTime has not been kind to these adornments … but still, they may speak to you.

Ah, so you've met him. My master calls him "Eel-Kill." Something about an experiment gone wrong, many years ago.\n\nThe Mourning Stone you saw came from this temple. <<1>> was barely able to remove it before the undead fell upon us.
Some. Some <<1>> picked off dead men in the sands of Alik'r. Others, straight from the palaces of Dune.

A great desert in northwest Tamriel, where lizards swim like fish in the sea. Where the dead lie rotting under a blazing sun and none will dare to bury them.\n\nWill they bury themselves? <<1>> wonders.
Home to the great libraries of Elsweyr, where secrets lie scattered like gems in the sand.
Easy salvage. The storms wrecked half a dozen ships just off the coast, and some of them have beached on the <<1>>.
Oh, we would be, but <<1>> finds half a keg of Aldmeri brandy and suddenly it's a New Moons gala!\n\nIf we don't get out there, someone else will.

The ritual the Elf plans to perform will drive my children mad. But there is a better solution, if you're willing to listen to reason.\n\nMolag Bal is the real enemy here. Let me help you free my children from the Dark Lord's thrall. Then we both win.

She's an elder vampire! Setting those monsters free will be like ringing the dinner bell in a Nord feast hall before the meal is ready! \n\nHer so-called children see us as food and nothing more. The only logical solution is to perform my ritual.

I can perform my own ritual. It will destroy the Harvest Heart and set my children free.\n\nHelp me accomplish this and my children will be in your debt. They will provide you with safe passage through the Orchard and aid you against Molag Bal.
Of course. I am Abnur Tharn. It will take more than a few brainless cultists to rattle these old bones.\n\nNow then, where were we?
Ah. Yes. Ahem.\n\nTruth be told, I don't know the precise location, but I do know that he is Mannimarco's prisoner, and that the King of Worms is trying to pry the location of the Amulet from him.

A village that appears only once every thousand years at the bidding of their invented god? It's amazing. The Fading Tree itself could make up a lifetime's study.\n\nI don't have that kind of time to waste, though. I'll be moving on soon.

Why do you ask such meaningless questions? We cannot hold together much longer. You need to finish this!\n\nChoose one of us and pull a lever. Please. And may the sand beneath your paws always be warm, my friend.

I understand your hesitation, but … whether you join us or not, defeating the Withered Hand is your destiny.\n\nBy becoming Ash'abah … you are simply fullfilling our duty by doing what you are already destined to do. Nothing further is expected.

I can, though your voice is distant, muted. Please, pull a lever and finish this process. This needs to end, one way or another.\n\nNo matter who you chose, you have my gratitude. Ancestors bless you, my friend.
The next contender is Mirten, a Breton with a keen blade and sharp eye. Are you ready to fight him?
The next contender is Thael the Impaler. All hail Thael! \n\nAre you ready to fight her?
The next contender is the Ravenous Rayfa. You'll know if she likes you when she knocks you down. But then she'll cut out of your heart, so the feeling might be moot.\n\nAre you ready to fight her?
The next contender is Ravius, an Imperial mage. You're best to watch your step around him. Are you ready to fight?
The next contender is Norirtil the Nomad. We don't know exactly where he's from, but we do know that he instills fear in the warriors he faces. Are you ready to fight him?
The next contender is Einnel, master sorceress and mistress of spirits. Are you ready to fight him?

She turned them in to the guard, but they had planted evidence on her suggesting she had stolen some valuable gems. \n\nIn the end, they were all executed … even my poor Zariya. So now I ask, would you be willing to consecrate her remains?

Yes, and Zariya knew that, but her brother promised to find legitimate work once he paid his debts, so she agreed to help.\n\nBut then he and his friends came back, asking her to fence more stolen items, and threatening violence if she refused.
Fix things. Make them better. Deal with pests who ask too many questions.
Depends on the type of pest. Vermin? Brush away like little flies. Some pests bigger than others. These, I introduce to Veri.
My first wife. She died at sea. No body. Nothing to bury. No use for her coffin.\n\nI carry it with me. Anyone makes trouble? They spend a night with Veri. Few make trouble after that.
Then we have understanding.
Sorry? Veri had the tongue of a six-headed serpent! Believe me, it is better this way!\n\nOnly ones she scolds now are those who make trouble.
I am actually the next contender. But I'm so rich that Feluni has allowed me to have a surrogate fight for me. A real beast, too. His name is Jawsnap. Are you ready to fight me? I mean, him?
Your next contender is Serit the Sentinel. She's an animal lover from the sands of Alik'r. Are you ready to fight her?
The next contender is Doradrin the Dark. He practices the darker arts of beastmastery. Are you ready to fight him?
Boots. Metal. Elves, it seems. <<1>> thought a mudcrab was on the hook, yes? He was lucky this one saw him before the line was cut.\n\nHe is alive, but only just.
Take him to the temple, yes? Priestesses of the Two Moons are skilled healers as well as mystics. They will know what to do.
Bandits are attacking merchants on the road. <<1>> got smart and hired mercenaries, but they can only do so much ….
The storm, it causes chaos, disrupts the regular patrols. This makes the bandits bolder.\n\nSoon, things will quiet down. Until then, <<1>>'s coin feeds a few mercenaries, yes?
Of course, child. Mara teaches that knowledge is the water used to grow a strong and healthy mind. What would you know?
All of the relics are sacred to the Goddess of Love, though the Chalice of Mara is the most holy. It's said the Lady sent it to be used at the Wedding of Saint Alessia!
Four of them. Eliana, Decanus, Veranus, and Talania. None of them have come back and I fear for their lives. If you can help them, in Mara's name, please do.
Very little, to be honest. This place was once an Imperial stronghold called Fort Sphinxmoth.

Aye. He's one of the chapel guardians Priestess Marcella sent into the ruins. Veranus is … not very clever, and I'm worried about him. He gets into the worst predicaments. Veranus is about as smart as these bandits.
We knew where to track them because they call themselves the Sphinxmoth Bandits. Heard them boasting as they rode off with the relics.
Hmm. I think I saw an old book among those old tents. I've got to stay on the move, but that book might be able to tell you more.

Have you observed the sand barriers on those passages in the canyon walls? I suspect the Prince's generals may be waiting within.\n\nTheir essences would no doubt be more than enough to activate the other two statues.
Very simple, adept. The seals at the bases of those statues show a scorpion and a spider. \n\nThose were the spirit totems claimed by Maleel's chief generals, Sahdina and Rashomta.

The black blood flowing from the Harvest Heart binds the vampires to Molag Bal. But it also gives us a connection we can take advantage of.\n\nWhile I provide the power to destroy the minds of the vampires, you must sever the connection to Molag Bal.

The black blood flowing from the Harvest Heart binds my children to Molag Bal. But it also gives us a connection we can take advantage of.\n\nWhile I provide the power to destroy the Harvest Heart, you must sever the connection to Molag Bal.

Some call me the Crimson Matron, others the Concubine of Coldharbour. I am an elder vampire, brought to this new life by Molag Bal.\n\nThese are my children, but they have been enthralled by the Lord of Brutality.
The ceremony begins with consumption of the moon-sugar elixir. This unique brew will make your mind more receptive to the touch of Jone and Jode.
Thank you, my muscles are really starting to cramp up.

I don't think of him as a pet. He's more of a companion, a cure for my loneliness. No one appreciates how cut off from civilization I feel out here. It's hard being a culinary genius in a village of peasants.

Don't tell me you're another Goblin-hater? Aemilia is bad enough, with her unreasoning prejudices. I don't want any more like her skulking around.\n\nGoblins are greatly misunderstood. They're actually kind, loving beings, when treated properly.

I was born and raised in High Rock, in the great city of Daggerfall. I was never lonely there, let me tell you. I had many friends and hordes of admirers who appreciated my genius. I never spent a lonely day—or night—in Daggerfall.
We entered the ruins to recover the stolen relics, but the bandits got the drop on us. Quick, break the lock on these chains. Get me out of here!
I … I think they got Talania. I saw her stabbed. Decanus and Veranus, though. I think they might still be alive, somewhere deeper in the complex.

But it's fact! My interactions with Zich prove it. When treated with kindness and respect, Goblins are friendly, loyal, and loving.\n\nIf only others were willing to give them a chance, there'd be a lot less unreasonable hatred of Goblins in Tamriel.

Unthinking prejudice isn't limited to remote villages. It taints big cities too. I believe all creatures are meant to live together in peace and harmony, a view widely despised. I left Daggerfall and eventually settled here. And here I'll stay.
Ha! I don't know how you think you've been operating, but you don't exactly keep a low profile. The Eyes of the Queen see everything, friend. We know all about you, and we like what we've seen.
I know you, but you don't know me. We have a mutual friend. Scrawny cat named Razum-dar?
I was being chased by the bandits when I lost my footing and tumbled into the pit. They laughed at me. Left me down here. I thought I was safe … until I heard the hissing.
I know. News travels fast in the intelligence game. Nice work up there.\n\nAnyway, Raz has nothing but good things to say about you. I'm glad to have you with me on this.
I know. News travels fast in the intelligence game up there. Ahem. Look, you did what you had to do. \n\nRaz had nothing but good things to say about you. I'm glad to have you with me on this.

He's well. I think he's working some kind of military deployment up in the north. A ruin … Senalana? I think that's it.\n\nAnyway, he has nothing but good things to say about you. I'm glad I'll have you with me on this.

There are some panels showing the constellations down this corridor. I think it's a mage-lock. If you touch the right ones you can open the door. The trick is figuring out the right order with all of those hungry crocs around.

Not … entirely, but they have certainly been blown out of proportion. Some people speak as if respectable citizens were disappearing left and right. \n\nIt's true that a few people have gone missing, but they were mostly beggars and vagrants.

I overheard you speaking to the Magistrate. You expressed an interest in assisting with the investigation?\n\nI know she believes we have the situation under control, but I'm afraid nothing could be further from the truth.

Oh, I haven't the foggiest notion what's in the prison. It's been centuries though—whatever was down there is surely dead.\n\nIf not, well, you seem capable enough, and it can't be any worse than the damned Elves.

How kind of you to ask. Let's see … I was in Wrothgar for a while, but Orcish history is such a bore, so l left there and visited some Dwemer ruins in Morrowind. Then I wound up coming here. \n\nStibbons has remained with me, of course, regrettably.

Who knows? Who cares? The blathering fool created such a mess here. He's become a liability, especially since the Tomb of Kings.\n\nI have a new man assisting me now. He's much more … efficient. Not as efficient as you, but you're not for hire.
I've been here for a few days already, so I know the guard rotations. \n\nYou would not believe what the Covenant's captain here is into, I've never … ahem.

Let's see, this time of day … Andwulf and Ivanya are on duty. Andwulf looks like a warrior, but raise your voice and he'll run for cover.\n\nIvanya … well, let's just say she enjoys the services of the "men of leisure" working the camp.
Then you may come and go as you see fit. Would you like me to get the door?

Chests full of gold. Owning a sound ship after a hurricane can be quite lucrative, even when the only cargo is Dominion luminaries seeking passage.\n\nDon't worry, I won't charge you. Without your help, the Prowler would be a mass of broken timber.
Aye, the Prowler is fully restored and ready for heavy seas. <<1>> even managed a few improvements using some Maormer … donations.\n\nHave no fear, she'll get you safely to Auridon.
Oh, sure, of course. Hrm, are the walls supposed to wobble like that? Never mind. Are you ready?
Yes. Just a little nervous. Damned moon-sugar roiling my stomach. Hmm. It's this ceremony. Just irritating formality. Dull claws, let's get this over with. Ready?
Because he's a brute and I need to be the one to give her the tools. \n\nIf I can't make her forgive me, she'll just leave me here, and then, what will I do? This is my only chance!

I suppose I'll mourn <<c:1>>. I must find oils for his body, and tools for the rites. I can almost feel his hand on mine, and hear him whisper "all things find their way."\n\nBut they won't. He's gone forever. And soon, I'm to follow.
That's the kind of confidence that we'll need. Let's do this.
The sooner we're done with this, the better. Let's go.

They wanted to use my energy to power the Shackle. That indicates to me that the Shackle utilizes some form of energy. \n\nDisrupting that flow of energy may be key to destroying the Great Shackle. I'll know more once we get inside.

Crocodiles! The terrifying beasts infest the riverbed near S'ren-ja, but the Clan Mother refuses to do anything about them. This one doesn't want to end up as crocodile food! People have been vanishing, and I just know it's the crocs!

What can I tell you that isn't obvious? The Great Shackle is the ultimate version of Molag Bal's Dark Anchors, a massive weapon capable of completing the Planemeld of its own accord.\n\nIt would be a fascinating device if it wasn't so terrifying.

Don't tell this one you haven't heard of our little crocodile problem. The Clan Mother refuses to send anyone to deal with them after <<1>> never returned. \n\nThis one really thought he had a shot at chasing the beasts away. Oh, well.
Where? Do you have a death wish, then? They're south of the bridge if you're anxious to die, friend.

I never met the mer myself, but he was a particularly arrogant High Elf from what I've heard. And that's saying something. \n\nNo one knows why he came here, but the Clan Mother gave him permission to "play" with the crocodiles.

The restless dead. And no mere skeletons, these. Long ago the Dragon priests commanded legions of thralls. Worshipers of the Dragons themselves.\n\nAs a reward for their service, they were cursed to defend these shrines … forever.
I wish it were so. But no. You and I are merely forming the core. Whatever weapon we decide to make, the runes and hilt and all of that must wait for another day.
We heard rumors that the Canonreeve was rallying her Thalmor guards for a venture into the Hollow.\n\nWe feared she would use the Hollow as a site to cast powerful magic. We were right.

She is dead.\n\nShe was a member of the Thalmor, displeased with the Dominion's performance in the war. The Mages Guild believed she came here to release a power that could turn the tide. All she has done is compromise this Hollow.
We do not know, and it is for her sake that this expedition was launched.\n\nBakkhara's brother is a fellow mage, and leader of this search party. If she can be found, Kargand intends to find her.

We of the Mages Guild came down here to stop her. We defeated her in battle, but failed to counter the spell she cast, and a great darkness burst forth.\n\nBakkhara, our leader, sacrificed herself so that I could escape.
Yes. He took many mages with him, and he would probably take you, if you asked. He will do anything to get his sister back.\n\nI caution you again—you court a dangerous beast by entering the Hollow.

They are called Aurorans. A strange type of Daedra, I think. Aelif has only faced them once before. \n\nIf she recalls correctly, they choose their allegiances carefully. Very curious that we would face them here.

Poor girl. With a companion like you, it's no wonder she's confused. She's lucky we arrived before you could stuff her head with any more silly nonsense.\n\nThere is a natural order to things. The Rock Witch, of all people, ought to understand.
What? Then why are we talking?
There's an island of motherless children near Daggerfall. A whole island.
There are so many people. And look, it's <<1>>! Why's she here?\n\nI bet my parents want me to show off my powers. I thought they were bringing me a teacher or something.

Blade's edge! A portal? They could've marched their entire army right into Alik'r without us even knowing it?\n\nDamned ancient magics. Always a liability. Always. Just tell me the portal's closed now.

Praise HoonDing for protecting us from the infidels, then. I'm sure you deserve some of the credit too.\n\nAlbeit, we should probably station some soldiers here just to keep watch on the place. Like we don't have enough to worry about already.
The Trial of Body is a test to prove your worth to An-Jeen-Sakka and his warrior faction. I'm sure it involves some kind of contest of strength and physical prowess.

You don't say? I presume he was kept alive by some Ayleid curse? \n\nFascinating! I knew there was more to discover in these ruins. I'll definitely have to study that. I don't suppose I can speak with this Orc?
Oh well. Just to study the cell in which he was imprisoned will be fascinating, I'm sure. I appreciate the tip.
I suppose after all these years, it would be hard to blame him.\n\nHow fascinating though? I can't wait to speak with him. You are an inexhaustible supply of assistance. Thank you!

It was too much to hope he would just wander off into the desert. \n\nIt's hard to let him go. After so many years, I want to reward his loyalty, but the truth is that he's absolutely useless, and can't seem to prove otherwise.

This one isn't sure. The little Elf appeared out of nowhere, but at least she didn't try to kill Kamu like the other Elves did.\n\nThey both claim to know how to get inside the tower, but Kamu doesn't trust either one of them.
This one doesn't know very much about this area, but this one always has opinions. Ask what you will and I will answer. It's the least I can do.
Stibbons recovered all my tools? Perhaps he's more resourceful than I gave him credit for.\n\nI'll have reconsider my decision to terminate his employment, at least until I have all my tools.

Without a doubt. He's also a lot more expensive, of course. \n\nBut you get what you pay for, and Stibbons was clearly a case of sovereigns wasted. I do hope he doesn't die out here in the desert though. The poor thing!

Kamu never saw her before. She stepped out of the shadows, but she didn't attack immediately.\n\nIt is apparent to this one that she is anxious about something. And she seems eager to help us. Perhaps too eager, if you know what Kamu means.

The little Elves are ruthless killers. They call themselves the Shadow Walkers. As far as this one can tell, they hunt and kill anything that enters these dark woods.\n\nThey never even gave us a chance to beg for our lives before they killed Alphaury.

When we were resting at one of the campfires, a group of snake things rushed toward us. But they didn't attack us. They charged the Elves sneaking around our camp.\n\nThe two groups don't seem to like each other. They may even be at war.

When we were searching the woods, we ran into a few snake things. They attacked us when we got too close. They never seemed to actively hunt us, though. And, of course, that snake thing over there helped Kamu.\n\nI did notice something else, however.

What a choice! Like deciding whether to roast slowly or leap right into the flames. There is no good answer.\n\nBut if we were seeking allies, Kamu would choose the Elves. They are strong and capable. They could be a great help against Molag Bal.

Well, the friendly snake thing did help me. We shouldn't dismiss them out of hand. They lack organization and fighting skills, but Kamu can't deny their ferocity.\n\nPerhaps they are worthy of consideration, as well.

They are monsters! They destroy our eggs and slaughter my people! If you aid the Wood Elves, we can never trust you.\n\nThe lamias are powerful. We would be of great help to you. But only if you help us end our war with the Wood Elves.

You've seen my people fight. We're trained to kill. It's what we do.\n\nMaybe … maybe if you can show them that Molag Bal has been using us, lying to us, maybe they'll see his treachery for what it is and join your cause.

The Magistrate says I impeded the investigation. Apparently, she went behind my back to conduct her own inquiries.\n\nI found evidence she has been meeting secretly with Fakimal, one of my bailiffs. When I asked her about it, she had me locked up.

Hautt and Hridi were admired in our village. If the enchantment is wearing off, they'll help me rally the others. It would help if Hautt had his lute and Hridi had her silver daggers.   \n\nWe can continue what Nelhilda has begun.

You are deep below the Temple of the Dance, Hallowed. Tradition dictates that the start of your journey should be rooted in what has come before. Here you will find that the past is very much alive in the moonlight.
A skilled healer, and sharper than <<1>>'s claws! It's good he survived the shipwreck.\n\nThis place, <<2>>? It is a beautiful place, thank the gods. Otherwise <<3>> would be completely overtaxed.
We know the name because a few island locals live in the towers up the beach. With their help, <<1>> set up camp for the castaways. The locals bring food, drink, and medical supplies.
Queen Ayrenn sent a missive detailing your arrival and orders. You are here to secure the Staff of Magnus.
Safe, in our vault below the city. We have guarded it day and night. When you are ready, I shall show you into the vault.
Of course. What would you like to know?

Yes. There is no other way. Do you understand the power of the Withered Hand? King Fahara'jad, the Ash'abah … they cannot stop them!\n\nEventually, the Hand would have come here and killed everyone. This deal is our only hope.

Yes, comrade. My meeting. I am the Countess Hakruba, daughter of Tigonus, flower of the sands, and Province General of High Rock.\n\nThis meeting was called at my request, as I have the honor of leading the council.
Flaminius Auctor, Province General of Cyrodiil, at your service. I've long had the privilege and honor of being the guild's arm at the heart of the Empire.\n\nHow I wish that was still the case.
This one is the province general of Elsweyr! She has earned the name Iron-Ear, and fights like a champion of Thizzrini Arena. You'd do well to watch your tongue, my friend.

Hah! Aren't you a milk-drinking simpleton?\n\nSkyrim is littered with relics from the time of the Dragons. Shrines, tombs … trust me, comrade. Many are the lies and stories told to children. Dragons do not number among them.
By the Green, I am uneasy. All this talk of death and magic. Give me something I can hit! \n\nI didn't become province general of Valenwood through quiet meditation. I got this post through action!

I'm sure you've seen some of the council as you've traveled across Tamriel. Each represents a former province of the Empire, managing business there for the Guildmaster. \n\nStendarr give us strength.
I didn't even want to let myself think it. When she disappeared after your visit to the Ayleid ruin …. What is your proof, my friend? The council will need solid evidence.
Father was sent to treat the Knahaten Flu outbreak in Orcrest seventeen years ago. The disease proved too potent, and … he and his team died. I was there, as a cub.
Aelif did what? Stendarr's breath, that's disgusting. I'll have to talk to her when she returns. But … I suppose it did answer our concerns. Oblivion take lizards and cats, both!
Basic tactics, soldier. I need to cover your back so the Daedra on the hill don't flank you.

That must have been quite a … grisly scene. The other bailiffs are already on their way over there. I will leave it to them to arrest the Magistrate as well.\n\nWhy though? Why did the Magistrate and Fakimal kill all these people?

Yes. The story is one from her own past, but she's convinced that she's living through these events for the first time.\n\nYou'll play the part of the close friend she never had. Someone she can trust, who can change the person Aranias becomes.
I'm … I'll be fine. Khali and I have known we would face darkness here since we were cubs. I just wonder … I want to know what he meant, earlier. Let's go, and find out.
Of course!\n\nNow, sit down by the fireplace. Imagine there's a nice, warm fire burning there, and I'll set the scene.
Ask nicely.
Those who honor the ancient Yokudan traditions are always welcome here. Come inside and enjoy our hospitality.
No need for your sympathy, Hallowed. This is what my father meant. This is what he spoke of, when he spoke of decisiveness. I need to move forward. No looking back.
Yes. Like Khali. I've spent so much of my life studying. So much spent examining texts, words. Action, though. Action is needed to be a true leader. Let's go, Hallowed.
Really? You need to consult with a monster before you agree to help the great and powerful Vanus Galerion?\n\nOh, very well. Do what you must. I'll wait here until you reach a decision.
Of course you will. No other decision makes any sense.\n\nI'll follow you into the ritual sites. Protect me while I cast my spells and we'll have the army on the move again in no time.
A most wise and honorable decision. I'll follow you to the ritual sites.\n\nProtect me while I perform the ritual, and we will break Molag Bal's hold on my children!

Of course. Take all the time you need. It's not like you're trying to save the world from Molag Bal or anything like that. Oh, wait. That's exactly what you're trying to do. \n\nI shall await your decision with bated breath.

Let's see, who's on duty now? Ah, Quinton. He's a dullard. He just opens the door for the parade of pretty faces. Tell him you're there to meet Captain Balrook's disgusting needs.\n\nJust know you'll probably have to deal with the Captain personally.

Seyran. That bitch. A drunkard. Want her to step aside? Just buy her some ale.\n\nBut … you know what? I owe her. Why don't you convince her to step away? Suggest you've got a keg waiting for her under the bridge behind the lodge.
The war isn't very old. But I've already seen enough action to hold plenty of grudges. Let's just say she cost me.\n\nAs for what I'll do … that's up to you. Get her to move however you like.
Once you have what we're looking for, head towards Krin's compound. We'll need to get inside if we want to grab back our intel.
Can't promise I won't lie. But I'll tell you what I can. Ask.

Ren-dro is very well-connected. Very. He has dozens of business ventures across the Dominion. And he's in tight with members of the military from his time as an Eye.\n\nErm. That is, from his time before the Queen was coronated ….
Ha! I don't know how you think you've been operating, but you don't exactly keep a low profile. The Eyes of the Queen see everything, friend. We know all about you, and we like what we've seen.

He's well. I think he's working some kind of military deployment up in the north. A ruin … Senalana? I think that's it.\n\nAnyway, he has nothing but good things to say about you. I'm glad I'll have you with me on this.
I know. News travels fast in the intelligence game. Nice work up there.\n\nAnyway, Raz has nothing but good things to say about you. I'm glad to have you with me on this.
I know. News travels fast in the intelligence game up there. Ahem. Look, you did what you had to do. \n\nRaz had nothing but good things to say about you. I'm glad to have you with me on this.
I know you, but you don't know me. We have a mutual friend. Scrawny cat named Razum-dar?

Ren-dro still has some friends in the Eyes. He knows I'm out here, and the guards know what I look like. Hence the disguise.\n\nYou … well, to be honest, he probably knows about you too. But they won't be expecting you.

Ahem … well. Officially the Eyes were formed when Her Majesty was crowned two years ago. \n\nLet's just say Her Majesty was preparing for her return long before she actually got back to Auridon. Ren-dro was a big part of that.

I hope he is not missing, but we must consider the possibility. Many people have disappeared, and the young man doesn't show up for his own wedding?\n\nFor his sake, I hope he simply changed his mind.
I do not know. I heard the killer was found dead, but that he was working for someone else. \n\nWho would instigate such evil?

We know that you have come to this realm with the Fighters Guild and the Mages Guild. We know that you seek to stop the Planemeld that Molag Bal has orchestrated.\n\nWe want to help you, but we can't while our people disagree.

The scholars, of which I am a part, believe that eternal death is better than the eternal suffering our Hist now endures. The warriors, led by An-Jeen-Sakka, feel quite the opposite. Existence, they feel, any existence, is better than oblivion.
I'll tell you all I can, Hallowed. I've read almost every tome in the Tales of the Two Moons Path series, and studied at the side of Moon-Bishop Hunal himself. When I could understand him, anyway.

This is the council of province generals. They run the guild under the direction of the Guildmaster. And they're very concerned. I've been speaking to them about our experiences with the ghost of Jofnir and the attack on the Earth Forge.

I'm almost certain it will be dangerous, yes. Tharn promised us he'd walk the Path, didn't he? He's powerful and capable of almost anything. If he has been able to warp and twist the shape of the Two Moons Path, there's no telling what we'll face.

According to the stories, the Path is a spiritual one. We're walking into the heart of my people, the very soul of the lunar faith. Each part of the Path represents something about the candidate, the Hallowed, and the Khajiit.

Yes, manifestations. In the past Manes have fought in climactic battles on the Path. They've loved and lost, seen distant shores and spoken to inhuman spirits. Whatever we face will represent the challenges of here and now.
Thank the Green! Yes, take them. They're in that chest over there. We were just finishing up. Take them and we'll get out of here as soon as we can.

We feel … the council feels that we need to further investigate Jofnir's death. You will be their eyes and ears, with Aelif assisting you. She's gone to get some air outside. She can explain in more detail.

Istah? This cannot be. He is a good Crown. He has always been a friend to our family, and an excellent Justice.\n\nI should like to see the evidence before I believe such a thing. Until then, I will assume the guilty party is still on the loose.

Magistrate Sulma? I-I cannot believe this, even of a Forebear. Her mind must have been twisted by some dark magic.\n\nI suppose though, if no one has told us that Casnar's corpse was found, then that is a good sign.

With a young man, the blood runs hot. He may have found another woman. \n\nOr it could be that he realized the foolishness of the idea. His family does not support the marriage either. His brother was not even planning to attend!
Simply call down the light of Jone and Jode. Each of these reflectors is misaligned. Attune them to the moonlight, and see what the Bright Moons wish you to see.

For a Crown to marry a Forebear? In Sentinel, this may happen, but in Bergama, it is unheard of. For generations, our families' allegiances have not changed.\n\nIf these two marry, whatever allegiance they choose, they will offend half the city.
Of course, of course! She probably knew exactly what to expect here. No moon-sugar-induced vision would scare the likes of her!
I'm ready. Shazah's done well, I'm sure. Time for my chance to prove my worth!
Of course, you're right. I always worry Khali gets worked up too easily. But then that's what pushes her to do amazing things.
Yes, yes. We must be serious now, focused. I am ready. I've studied most of my life for what we begin today. Let's go.

Ha! Oh yes! I'm sure King Fahara'jad would like that very much! \n\nFor Crowns and Forebears to settle our differences while he is in power, this would mean Fahara'jad's line would have everlasting legitimacy. I cannot support that.
By all the … fine. Then you'd best get on with it. We can only hope the Dominion doesn't find the keystone while you're doing errands for a mad Kothringi.

Haven't you ever seen the results of a Daedric bargain before?\n\nNow, please. Go upstairs and talk to my daughter, Nelhilda. She has a plan to save us all. And with your help, maybe this time it will even succeed.

The mead's in here, so no, not many. Besides, those creatures out there aren't very friendly. And some of them were once our friends and neighbors.\n\nOne day, though, Gamirth had had enough. Even his love for my daughter couldn't keep him here.
I need a rare magical flower, Kyne's Tear, to make a potion. Unfortunately, the flowers are invisible. You need a Kyne runestone to see them. There may be a runestone at the nearby abandoned shrine.
This whole bloody castle sits on top of an ocean of unstable Oblivion-whatsit. The Daedra use pipes to control the flow of it all and it comes out as steam.
<The body is not wearing a ring.>
Well, I can handle the tinkering, but you'll have to keep the beasties off me. It will be quite a romp!\n\nAre you game?
I need to secure the gateway that leads to this plane's Moonhenge. You and any others you find should meet me there.\n\nThen we can discuss how to destroy the sigil stone.

Just what it damned looks like. The Dawnmead took us in the night. I still can't believe I'm alive! Poor Galathril and Thanael … they were trying to save the relics while the mercenaries held back the assault. I … I just ran.
<The body is wearing a wooden ring with the inscription, "Zariya + Darius.">

A council of elders leads the Wood Elves. They live upon a large rock that floats above us. Queen Fah'jik's eggs were taken and hidden up there.\n\nYou will need a key to open the portal and gain access to the floating rock.

He's not? Well … I'll be a lizard's uncle. I guess our little talk may have convinced him after all!\n\nWe all went out drinking last night, and my cousin and I made one last attempt to talk him out of it. I guess it worked.

Damn. I don't know. I would have expected him to tell me if he had made such a decision. \n\nWith so many people missing lately, I prefer to make sure. He should be at my cousin's house—the last one before the west gate. Will you check?

It has everything to do with the trial! It is the trial!\n\nBeneath the north pyramid, Dremora gather sap from the Hist into great vats. They use treated wood to heat the sap and refine it, drawing forth its magical essence.
<You remove the ring from the body's finger and splash the corpse with funerary oils before lighting it ablaze.>
<You pull the ring off the decaying hand.>

You must understand. I love my little brother, but he's so naive. He shouldn't associate with a Crown girl, let alone marry her. \n\nOur father—Tu'whacca keep his soul—would never have approved, so I cannot approve either.

The Queen sent me to check on our Bosmer allies, and a good thing, too. This whole forest is rife with corruption. I offered my assistance to Captain Ethrel when the Daedra came through the Moonhenge.
Please, do not play the part of the fool. To strike our ancestors is a shameful and blasphemous act. You must know that.
Of course I do! But … I cannot disrespect our father's memory ….\n\nNone of this matters though. Right now, all that matters is Casnar's safety. I will approve the marriage before I see him harmed!

I've been fighting the craving, trying to find a way to break the spell. I want to save my father and the villagers, if I can. \n\nAs for my father—he was always a strong man. The mead never seemed to affect him the way it got to the rest of us.

The flowers grow around the trees near the lake, but they only reveal themselves to someone who carries a runestone of Kyne.\n\nThere's a deserted shrine to Kyne not far from here. You should be able to find a runestone there.
The same thing every mage wants. Knowledge. \n\nThe rumor has long been that an ancient forest spirit dwells here, one that is undocumented by the Guild. I would find it and learn what I can from it.

I wish I knew. Never developed a taste for the stuff, I guess.\n\nBut I see my daughter struggle against the craving. She remembers things. Grieves for her beloved Gamirth. Some of the others try to resist at times, but then they go back to the mead.

Nothing good, that's for sure. He covets the magical essence of the Hist sap and refines it into potions and elixirs whose purpose we can only guess at. It's a perversion, but it is one we must endure.
The Daedra scattered us soon after we got here. We need to find the others and close the portal before the Daedra organize.
What aspect of the wolves would you like to know more about?

If you settle the debate in the warriors' favor, then the Hist tree continues to live and our civilization shall endure, just as it always has in this harsh land.\n\nPlus, my warriors shall stand at your side in your final battle against Molag Bal.

I've been watching the Daedra closely. The commanders pass in and out of a gateway to the north, or what passes as north in this place.\n\nIf I had to guess, I'd say our Moonhenge has a twin on this plane.

Well, most of the doors in here are sealed with pressure from that steam. It's all rather complicated, but in a nutshell—if I can tamper with the pipes, we can open the doors to the inner keep and you can slip inside.

Good job! She's a brilliant woman. Studied alchemy before we wound up here. She's good at patching up patrons and dealing with sick villagers.\n\nHurry, now. Take the flowers to her before the mead draws her back in.
No. He's a strong one, the Thane.\n\nBut he loves to celebrate. Keeps the party going day and night. It never really ends.
Ha ha! Once again, you have your duty and I have mine. I'm going to clear the gateway entrance for you in the meantime. Send the others my way, if you find them.

He's a Crown, one of the discontented bucking Fahara'jad's rule. The Crowns are traditionalists, you see. They resent Fahara'jad's agenda. \n\nSo this one is rattling his sabres against progress and change. Much good may it do him.
The teeth are ten inches long and razor sharp!
Bigger than a man's head!
What? What does that matter?
Warlock Carindon? He is … obsessed with his work, some say almost to a fault.\n\nBut he is on the forefront of the art, ever-seeking new frontiers. An excellent quality in a Mage.
I don't know for sure, it's just a feeling. I'm sure it's nothing, don't worry about it.
This Khajiit is not one to speak out of turn. But the look on the faces of the Bosmer out there—it makes Ahainar's fur stand straight.
A thousand thanks, wayfarer. We guards don't talk much, but we see a great deal.

The Forebears can be just as bad. I find the entire conflict absurd. We are all Redguards—our differences are relatively minimal. We just crave conflict. \n\nI suppose that's to be expected in a warrior culture.
Not yet. But this one would prefer outward aggression to their dead stares, yes?

This outcome, while sad, is for the best. We shall give you a boon to help you in your struggle. Without the vampiric shard, the Hist will pass on naturally.\n\nBut first, you need to convince An-Jeen-Sakka to accept your decision.
Of course. I shall wait here for you to return.
Comparatively yes, but I've been studying magic as long as most people have been crafting swords.\n\nWe don't see many places like this near Alik'r. I'm glad I agreed to accompany Carindon.
Mother was a great warrior, a commander. She led a squad in the campaign to retake Orcrest and Riverhold from the damned Colovians. That was almost twenty years ago.

Why are you even asking? I'm fine. I've known I'd be facing something dark in here since I was a cub. The monks made it very clear. Here, wherever we have to go next … the Two Moons Path. This is not an easy journey.
I can't say I understand him completely, but a Mage as old and powerful as he is entitled to some oddity.\n\nThis expedition is dangerous, but I'll never make a name for myself by sitting in a tower.
You're asking a Dark Elf why he's so suspicious? You're not exactly the sharpest sword on the rack are you?
I cherish the study of magic as much as the next mage, but I enjoy it even more when I don't have to be stuck in some dusty tower.\n\nThere's work ahead of us, but I'm ready.
Honestly, probably not. We're in the deep wilderness out here, and forest spirit or no, that's dangerous.\n\nAlso … those Bosmer don't look particularly welcoming.
Don't bother. If he went to this much trouble, he won't change his mind. If you really want to help, there's only one way. \n\nYou'll have to talk to Uncle Thakh.

If not, then this will be a short trip. Not much a handful of mages can do against a forest full of Bosmer.\n\nCarindon is a brilliant mage, but I think his ambition may be getting the better of him here.
He has been very … insistent on this expedition. I suspect that a mere "forest spirit" would not be worth the time of an entire group of mages, but you didn't hear me say it.
A runner reached me in Rawl'kha. My foreman, the one I told you was out trying to find that last battle site. She found it. They're due west of the Falinesti Autumn site.
I know not! We have guarded the vault day and night. I placed the staff myself.
No. The vault is off limits to all but … wait. Vicereeve Pelidil recently toured the vault.
The queen's business, or so he stated. The staff was present before his visit, but I did not check after he left.
Unthinkable, yet … what other conclusion can we draw? Such illusionary magic is beyond the ken of a common thief.\n\nTo the surface. I must question the watch.
As soon as we're done talking, the fight begins.

I knew you had more sense than those scholars! You understand that life—even a bitter, harsh life—is better than nonexistence. My warriors will be at your side when you need them.\n\nBut first, you must tell Xohaneel of your decision.
If you must. I shall wait here for your return.
