Uncle Thakh and his gang run the streets here in Bergama. They're not above-the-law, but they can be dangerous.\n\nIf you can convince Uncle Thakh to let me out, I'll go to the wedding. Jagnas won't be able to say a thing.

The monks taught us that this cleansing would open old wounds, and I expected to feel triumph … victory. Like any day in the field. But here … he was just another threat to put down. I think I understand what my mother was telling me.

Who I fight is not the question I should ask. The question I should ask is: Why do I fight? I fight to protect those I care for. And, perhaps someday, those I lead. Thank you, Hallowed. I could not have done this without you.

He departed into the wilderness. He said he had orders from the queen to bring Naemon's body. He did not return.\n\nHe was always foolishly devoted to the prince. I pray nothing has happened to the prince's body, too.

The Staff of Magnus is an extremely powerful object. There's no telling what wickedness he could achieve, if he desired it.\n\nRest assured, he would not have accessed the vault if we'd had any suspicion of his loyalty. Someone must inform the queen.
Hah, Uncle Nethrin pulls through after all. I'm … I'm not all right, no. But I will be. They cut me pretty good, and I had to crawl underneath poor Emalin over there.
Let's discuss this matter like civilized people then ….\n\nActually, thump that!

The Moonhenges are connected. If we don't destroy this one, the Dremora will just replace the sigil stone.\n\nLike I said, I've done my research, and I have a scroll that will do the trick. There's just one, enormous, significant problem.
No. We all know what you've done in service to Queen Ayrenn. You're too valuable to spend the rest of your life trapped in Coldharbour.
Only the spell can destroy Moonhenge, and its destructive power is … considerable. It'd likely wipe Valenwood off of the map.
The spell uses the sigil stone's power. As the sigil stone is destroyed, the portal will collapse on itself. There won't be time for the caster to make an escape. They'll be trapped here.
Exactly. A permanent exile, and probably a horrible death as well. I can't handle the responsibility of that choice.
I … understand. I created the spell. I should be the one to cast it.

You're not soft on them, are you? Amadour's bad enough, the way he moons over them. Don't need more like him around here.\n\nThey're dirty, sneaky, traitorous, vile little beasts. I'll kill every one I see, especially around here.

Haven't you seen them all? Open your eyes! They're always lurking around the village, looking for things to steal or people to kill. And eat, probably.\n\nNo one here takes them seriously, but they're going to overrun this village someday.

Does a fuzzy newt-goat have seven toes? Don't look at me like that! It's a perfectly appropriate analogy.\n\nAnyway, I hope I reach them before the hunters do. Otherwise, your allies don't stand a chance.
Because I'm tired of seeing people get hurt. Things need to change around here.\n\nWe've already spent way too much time talking about fuzzy newt-goats. I really need to get moving.

I work for him, not with him. If we were co-workers, I'd have killed him by now. The only reason I'm still working here, and the only reason he's still alive, is that he's paying me to do all the hard work in his fields.

The Shadow Walkers use runners to search the forest. But you'll never see them. They become one with the shadows, all but invisible when the clan is on high alert.\n\nThere is a way to see the runners, though.

Of course. It will be dangerous, but committing to our craft is danger in itself. Any mage is prepared to give his or her life for the art.\n\nBe on your guard. I suspect the other Bosmer we encounter will have a similar demeanor.

Of that I have no doubt, but eliminating these Bosmer could enrage the forest spirit, if it is indeed here.\n\nTake Evoker Ahainar-jo with you. He may be able to connect with these natives where Patraud could not.

He stands there in the field, staring at corn. Then he moves to another field and then stares at that corn. Sometimes he pokes at the corn and mutters to himself.\n\nIt drives me crazy. His gold is the only thing keeping this shovel off his face.

I think he keeps the souls nearby. He always comes and goes as he pleases. If you could destroy the Thane, our souls might return to us. Then we could leave this place.\n\nI think his lair is in one of the nice houses near the old well.
I appreciate your help. I need to make this right. For Nelhilda. For Gamirth. For my friends.

Oh. That is very kind of you to offer, but my administration has a handle on the situation. I believe Justice Istah and his officers have some promising leads. \n\nYou are a guest here. It would not do for us to put you to work.

What negotiations? These dungy Elves don't want talk. They say they only answer to the "Wilderking." Who is this? Who knows? They'd rather pull Hazazi's tail than give him a straight answer!\n\nIt's not fair. Hazazi always gets the worst assignments!

Hazazi likes this idea. If you can just get the Bramblebreach to make sense, this one will be impressed. \n\nHazazi thinks it's a wild guar chase, but if you want to try, speak with their Treethane. May you have better luck than Hazazi!

A recent development. Felari thinks it's a good sign that you can see the world so. Things were not always this way. The Wood Elves of Valenwood and the Khajiit of Elsweyr fought often in the March. For land and for power.

We mostly find what we seek in mass graves, sad markers of ancient battlefields. Truth be told, most of what we uncover is worthless. But if it brings even small comfort, if it bridges the divide at all, it is worth it.
A Greenspeaker of Valenwood, from the Grahtwood. He has proven himself a thoughtful and sensitive mer, a good partner in this cultural exchange. He has taken this setback very hard.
You've made it through the first part of the Two Moons Path. The moons have given their blessing for you to continue. Now you must see what else awaits you in this plane.
Those were reflections of the Khajiit past. To show where we have come as a people. Now you must see what the future holds for the Khajiit people.\n\nAre you ready to continue along the path?

Just amazing to think of this as the full council. Skyrim, High Rock, Elsweyr, Valenwood, and Cyrodiil … hardly the whole of the Empire. We've lost a number of generals over the last few years, and a few even quit after Jofnir died.
I finished what I could on the weapon and we repaired the damage from the Daedric attack on the Earth Forge. The core remains unfinished, though, while we deal with these plots.
The Green bless that cat! Yes, the damned Dawnmead. Those skooma-peddling bastards will do anything for some coin. Even rob those who would right ancient wrongs. Did she tell you of the work?

For a small place, there are many stories. Prefect Antias rules here, though not all are happy with that. Goblins scurry about the outskirts like the vermin they are. And several here are from surprisingly far away.

That is what I had hoped. Of course, neither Forebears nor Crowns will open up to a stranger, and in fact, you can't even enter their respective fellowship houses. \n\nI have a plan though. You simply have to wear these dishdashas to disguise yourself.

I do. My bailiffs and I are Crowns. Duty requires we be impartial, but Forebears do not trust us, and now our fellow Crowns distrust us because we work for the Magistrate.\n\nNo one talks, so we have no leads on the disappearances. Will you help us?

Aelif reached out to members of the Mages Guild. They tried to summon his spirit, talk to him. They failed. Aelif says something is preventing him from talking to us. I don't know much of such things, but I'm sure she has the right of it.

I'm fine to stand, but my leg is fairly torn up. I'm not much use on the road right now. Meanwhile, I have researchers digging at sites all over the March. Uncovering bones and relics for the project, not knowing about the bandits.

Yes, if they haven't been already. We have diggers at sites near Thormar and Willowgrove, and a team out searching for a third. Both sites saw massive battles between our two peoples. We just wanted to see those bones home.

She has been prefect here for many years, leading the village. She is also a devotee of Zenithar. The god one follows is no one else's business, except with Antias. She insists on seasonal offerings to Zenithar from all villagers.
The Bloody Hand tribe has always been nearby; they are a known danger. Recent rumors tell of scouts from another Goblin tribe seen about the village. Their strength is unknown.

Most figure it is the cost of having Antias run the village, a job no one else wants. Some, like Shagol, run and hide when the offering is due. A few protest but eventually give in with mutterings. Ufgra gra-Gum does not give.

Being from far away does not make them strangers. They have all lived here for years and are part of Cropsford now. Their stories are their own and not mine to tell. Lulius, Hisham, Octavimus, and Amadour may tell, if you ask.

It is Ufgra who does the daily work of managing the village, seeing to the sowing and the harvest, keeping the Goblins at bay, and so on. Without Ufgra, the village would be lost.\n\nAlso, who argues with a sullen Orc?

Yes. People get quiet when my bailiffs and I are around. Explore the city and listen. In particular, wear the disguises and visit Ra Gada's Respite and A'tor's Oasis. \n\nFollow up on any leads, and report back when you have something solid.

What can the tree do about the wind? You survive that which you cannot change. We are a village of farmers, we cannot wipe out a Goblin tribe. Even if we hire heroes for this task, the Goblins would just come back. It is their nature.
I'm sure you heard of the unrest in Cyrodiil. Three banners set upon the other, the sacking of the Imperial City, the death of the Imperial line … my time with the guild has not been quiet.
The Dawnmead are terrifying. We're just researchers, we're not combat trained. They haven't tried to rush the mercenaries yet, but it's just a matter of time. Vicious animals.
No. They're still in the chest, right in camp. If you hurry you can still retrieve them. Take them and get out of here. That's what I'm going to do.

Well, there is the matter of this Moonhenge. It seems to be connected in some way to the Moonhenge in Greenshade.\n\nAs long as it's here, all the Dremora would have to do to re-open the portal is replace the sigil stone. So we need to destroy it.

I created a scroll for just that purpose. Unfortunately, it requires the power of the sigil stone. As the sigil stone is destroyed, the portal will close for good. The person who casts the spell will be trapped here.

Perceptive as ever. Frankly, you are the only one of us that we can't spare. For either of us to make the choice would only be self-serving.\n\nBut be quick. The portal began to collapse when we removed the stone. Soon, it will all be moot.
This spell, combined with the innate magical properties of the Moonhenge? This is Ayleid magic we're talking about. We might destroy the entire Valenwood.
Stop right there. You've got more experience at saving the world than us. We're not leaving you to rot in Coldharbour.
Understood. Sir. It's … probably best that I cast the spell anyway.
Excellent. Let us begin.
Every candidate that undergoes this ritual is met by a figure from their past. The trial path is meant to cleanse the candidate of doubt and regret. The guide aids in that process.

Every Mane walks three paths. The life path is spent growing and loving and learning. The ceremony, here today, begins their trial path. After the cleansing at the temple, each candidate faces a trial unique to the course of their life path.

Just watching Glu … hey, it's none of your business! Someone send you to spy on me?\n\nNothing to see here, not for a seasoned adventurer like you. But I know there is something interesting, not far from here.

A very scenic spot called Timberscar Hollow. There's a cave with a huge, Dragon-guarded door. Or so I've heard. Sounds like something you would like.\n\nGo south on the path behind me, bear left at the fork, you can't miss it.

A warrior, part of a raiding party from Windhelm. We attacked this island long ago.\n\nHey, when you knocked my skull off that Argonian's body, do you remember where it landed? No? All right, I'll keep looking.
Not me. Not interested in that sort of thing. More interested in the sights right here in Cropsford.\n\nMove along now. You're starting to bother me.

Three pieces to find, each of a kind. \n\nThe first below the rock bridge, where the spiky vines live. The second one stays, near where the river meets my gaze. And the third one sits by the frozen giant's bits. So now we are intertwined!
Nara is a good fighter. Perhaps she'll find a way out of this mess on her own.
Paranarth is green, but bold. She'll do her duty.
Understood. Hazazi won't like it, but that's never stopped him from doing his duty.
Azsu is fearless. A good choice, if there is any.
Right. Nara has never shirked her duty.
Understood. Paranarth is inexperienced, but loyal. She will do as she is told.
Hazazi acts like he hates it, but he loves nothing more than serving the Dominion.
Fearless Azsu. I don't wish this on anyone, but he'll give the Daedra a damn good fight.

Because I love him. In addition to being "Daddy's little girl," I'm also the maid, cook, and housekeeper at home. Father's gotten used to having me keep house and wait on him. He'll never let me go, to Remius or anyone else.
Then you must be of the living.\n\nMy eyes are veiled. My time here draws to a close.
What? I don't have time for games. I need to find the lieutenant … I must find her.
Damn. And it looks like you're short another.
At least she died for a good cause. And it looks like you're short another.
She always wanted to die in battle. And it looks like you're short another.
My people have turned on themselves. The Hunt, it's driven everyone …. I've tried to protect the Silvenar and the Green Lady … they're not safe.
You will soon see it for yourself.\n\nBut first, you should view another scene from Aranias' past. She was a bit younger, and excited about her newly-found skills. Are you ready?
Of course, my friend. I'll answer whatever I can.
I'm not sure. I've kept this secret for so long, watching my friends waste away and give up hope. They'd hate me for what I've done. And rightfully so.\n\nAnd Nelhilda. She would never forgive me.

I know. I keep thinking about how kind he could be. Always helping others. He did something terribly foolish, but I know he is not a bad man. \n\nI'll try to forgive him. But I do wish we could leave this place.

Yes, he can stay here in his precious tavern. Atone for his sins in solitude.  I don't think I can ever forgive him. \n\nI keep thinking of Gamirth. That note you gave me broke my heart. I … I want to leave this place.

So much "happened next," but I especially draw your attention to two particular events.\n\nOne scene is atop the lighthouse. The other, in the manor's great hall. They will help you understand more about our troubled Altmer, I hope.
Oh, don't worry, it was an entertaining twist, to be sure. But sadly, as real as it may seem, this is just a story.\n\nIn real life, you were not there to kill Andur.

He has had considerable time to grow in power. And his temper has not gotten any longer, if you understand me.\n\nIt seems the Veiled Heritance have sent him after Aranias, to ensure she kills the Wilderking, or dies if she fails.
In the garden. She's been commanded to kill the wife of this Bosmer. You should hurry to her. She faced this alone last time.

I met him. He wanted to get into this story, but he wouldn't ask nicely.\n\nBut there's nothing we can do about that right now. We have a story to finish. Aranias' big moment is about to arrive. You should go to her.

I've heard whispers of a nearby city. They say it's a safe haven. I'll try to convince everyone to travel there with me.\n\nEven if we can't return to our world, I would feel better knowing that Nelhilda and the others were safe.
What fool idea is that? A daughter marries who her father tells her to, when he tells her to. Anything else invites chaos and the perils of interbreeding.\n\nYour presence offends me. Go now.
What? How can this be true? Fakimal has been known to bend the law, but he always followed orders. I can't imagine him going on a killing spree.\n\nWhere is he? I would speak with him straight away.

Dead? The poor boy. I-I don't understand. You're saying he was killing people under orders? \n\nThe only people with the authority to issue orders to Fakimal are myself and … the Magistrate …. You think she's involved in this?

That … looks like Sulma's key, and this would explain why she put me in the stocks.\n\nMay I request one last favor then? The Magistrate's home is southwest of the Hall of Judgment. Would you investigate the place?
Why didn't you say so! You're a deputy of the guard? The same guard whose authority ends where my ship begins?\n\nOn the dock, or in the water. Your choice.

The Guildmaster sets the goals of the guild as a whole. The council interprets her wishes at the province level. \n\nAs head of the council I resolve disputes, and ensure we are working hand-in-gauntlet with the Guildmaster.
On your way.\n\nAnd don't bother my sailors. They know I'll turn their hides into sailcloth if I catch them shirking.
<<1>> is the best scrounger in the regiment. If you want, I can send him out to look for a <<z:2>>.
Not much to tell. Larus and I have lived in Cropsford all our lives, grew up with each other, and just sort of ended up together. It's a little sad when you think about it. I try not to.

Always something happening in Cropsford, though maybe not things outsiders would be interested in. The ongoing drama between Madria, Almerel, and Remius is always entertaining. Chef Amadour and Lulius are both oddballs but mostly harmless.
He's on his way. Anything else we can do?
Suit yourself. Anything else we can do?
She'll have those leaks fixed in no time. What else?
All right. What else?
<<1>> is as good with a mallet as she is with her sword. I can have her patch the Prowler's leaks.
<<1>> is our best tracker. He can recover <<Az:2>> in no time.
I almost pity the Sea Viper who's holding onto <<Az:1>>. <<2>> will recover it soon enough. What else needs doing?
King Dynar is trapped within a tower of darkness, bound by shadows and dark magic. Meridia's lights can unravel those bonds.\n\nWithout them, you won't be able to set the Ayleid King free.

Being somewhere else? There's always some crisis or another here. We see more Goblins every day. Sometimes they raid the warehouse and steal foodstuffs. Ufgra and Antias handle that sort of thing; go look up in town if you want to know more.

Depends. Ufgra handles all the day-to-day emergencies, while Prefect Antias deals with long-term issues. Just don't ask her about Zenithar!\n\nYou'll find them both in town. Antias is usually in her house, but Ufgra likes to be outdoors.

It is good that he did so, as the Battle and Warfront missions are under Atahba's care. Vilya brings Grand Warlord Sorcalin's orders. These Atahba posts for brave warriors to see and accept. You have questions?

Battle missions send groups of soldiers to capture valuable enemy resources, yes? The farm, lumbermill, and mine around each castle support its war efforts. If we capture those resources, that castle is greatly weakened.

Warfront missions are Atahba's favorites! These are major attacks to capture enemy castles; many brave warriors are needed. Taking castles from our enemies is the key to the Dominion controlling Cyrodiil.

Why does everyone ask me that? I'm Prefect Antias's eyes and ears out here, since she seldom stirs from her house. I keep everyone's spirits up, make sure they're all happy and productive, and so on. A lot safer than my last job.
Off by herself around the xanmeer. She's proud of that bow, and its loss affected her greatly.\n\nFor a scavenger, she's too attached to material things, if you ask me.

It was the only deal Alasan would accept. It seems terrible, but we're only killing vagrants, criminals …. To save the city, that's a sacrifice I'm willing to make.\n\nLet me finish this—it's only a few more corpses. Will you keep my secret?

If that's your choice, I will turn myself in. There's no point in trying to deny my crimes. \n\nMark my words though, wayfarer. You've doomed Bergama. The Withered Hand will kill us all. I hope I'm wrong, but in my heart, I know I'm not.

I can't tell you how relieved I am to hear that. \n\nWhen I saw you coming out of the basement, I thought all of this was going to have been in vain. You realize, of course, that this means Istah will have to remain in the stocks.
Have it your way. What else needs doing?

All right. I have witnessed many dark crimes in my time as Justice, but they pale in comparison to this.\n\nTo think our own Magistrate would make a deal with the Withered Hand. What could she possibly hope to gain from such a thing?

Unbeknownst to me, hordes of undead decided to suddenly haunt the ruins. I went trotting in, soiled my trousers when I saw what was there, and just barely escaped with my life. I'm never leaving this village again.

Treasure hunter. I used to comb the ruins of Culotte, an Ayleid ruin west of here, for artifacts to sell. But that place has gotten a lot more dangerous lately. I almost died last time I went in there.
Then it's time for that mangy privateer to make good on his promise.\n\nMaybe you should do the talking. I'd just rub it in.
All right. I appreciate what you've done for us. We'll keep the Prowler safe while you take care of the rest.

Perhaps this child shows the Wilderking is pleased by our service and won't let anything happen to <<A:1>>. He wouldn't let anything happen to it.\n\nMy family needs me. When the village returns to the Wilderking's paradise, I'll go with it.

Egg and youngling, my early years were spent in the rich swamps of Shadowfen, far to the East. Wanderlust took me from those waters and set my feet on a path westward. I followed that path here, where the land spoke to me and I remained.

It is a good place. There is plenty of water and good fishing. Some swamps would be nice, but I do not complain. The people here are worthy companions, except for Almerel. And sometimes Ilwen.\n\nSun-blessed Cropsford is my home now.

There are three villagers who died before I could learn their stories: Norvir, Fardel, and Thara. \n\nTheir vessels remain in this cellar, and it is my hope that their belongings do, as well. If I could hold their belongings I could hear their stories.

Selfishness, I think. Almerel claims to object to me because I'm Breton, but that's not the real reason. He's gotten used to having Madria wait on him hand and foot and he doesn't want to lose that. He doesn't care what she wants.
You are most gracious. I cannot risk the tunnels—I live for more than myself. \n\nI must trouble you to do this alone. I'll meet you above, at the docks.
Then thank you for freeing me. I will await one who can help me finish the story.

Who wouldn't be? I debase myself daily to beg him to release Madria and he refuses, insulting me to my face and likely behind my back. I'd like to stab his eyes out, but for Madria's sake, I just walk away and come back when I've calmed down.
Anything Antias thinks is beneath her. I get to do her laundry, clean her house, run her errands, and take her cat for walks. Any task that might sully our precious prefect's image, I have to do.

Why? You here to steal my job? You can't have it!

I get a few coins a month, plus all the leftovers I can eat. And I get to sleep on a mat on the floor. With the cat on my face.

At least I'm not moping around town like Ilwen, the loser.

Not me. It bothers Marina but I like having some space to ourselves. If I want to see people, it's a three-minute walk. You just can't put a price on privacy.\n\nMarina now, she likes staying indoors, says the trees give her the willies.
Fascinating ….\n\nCarindon is still speaking with our captive Bosmer but I will join you to investigate this. We should be careful. Too many have answered Aetherius' call today.

A big city. Not saying which, as there are people looking for me. But it was dirty, crowded, noisy, and dangerous. Out here, all I have to worry about are Goblins, and a sharp rap to the head with my hammer takes care of them.

Yes, our moon-sugar storehouses burnt in the night. My father ran inside to save our tools, but he barely made it out.\n\nDo you hear his wheezing? The sweet-smoke ruined his lungs. He needs powerful medicine, or he won't last until morning.
Father tried to save our alchemical tools. If any survive, we could trade them for medicine.\n\nPlease, this one begs you to salvage any tools from the wreckage! There's little time for my father.

And you are not. Hard work is how one shows Nirn that you deserve to walk its surface. Also, the sight of an axe flashing in the sun discourages Goblins from coming near.\n\nIf you are merely sight-seeing, go to Crown Point and feast your eyes.
Deeper into the forest.\n\nIf this Selene is here, that's where she'll be.
Do your legs quake at the thought? Yes, there are Goblins all around this village. At least two tribes of them. They skulk around the edges, not daring to attack openly. But someday, perhaps ….
It's the big tower you see to the South, on the hill. From its top, the world spreads beneath you. If you have nothing to do but stare at others, climb Crown Point for a view worth seeing.
She's … she must be related to the forest spirit Carindon is looking for.

Oh, I'm a merchant! I sell wares we make here in town over in Rawl'kha or down in Pa'alat. Or Willowgrove. Or Hadran's Caravan. That's why I'm drunk, see. \n\nI was buying drinks for my business partners. Just part of business, you know?
I know enough not to underestimate anything when it comes to this place.\n\nThis expedition has been tragic, but I won't let it end in vain.
We speak to her and hope that she can be reasoned with.\n\nToo many have fallen today for me to give up now. If the time comes for me to face death, then my soul will join my comrades' in the stars.
There's one, but the crew turned me away. Said they couldn't take on any useless cargo.\n\nAll they see is some shirker come to eat up their stores. Damn them, I'm a Dominion marine!
I … I was gambling, all right? After I sold off everything I could, I used the rest to gamble on spikeball races at Hadran's Caravan. \n\nPlease! Please don't tell my wife.
The last Ayleid king? Here? Then Captain Alphaury was right. The key to our victory is locked away in that tower!

Yup! She's the Treethane of our little village. The Colovians used to live here and then they left. So us and the Khajiit moved in our stuff and now it's ours! \n\nIt's nice, even if we didn't grow any of the buildings.
I sense your mockery but take no offense. All things that grow from our hard work are beloved by Zenithar. This pumpkin patch is a fitting site for his shrine.

Zenithar forbid! I'm not dumb enough to flood my fields all the time. The plant roots will rot. Any fool knows that. But it seems that Lulius doesn't; these are his fields. He'll learn, but it sure seems to be taking him long enough.

Can't you tell? He's from the Imperial City. Fled from the Tharns is what I heard. He won't talk about it though. He knows nothing about farming, but he seems to need to be studying something, so I guess corn is pretty harmless.
Were it that easy. The barrier ahead appears to be magically shielded. \n\nThe mages and I will attempt to bypass it. I need you to venture farther and see if there is another way.

He served his purpose. We were attacked as soon as the door was opened. By Bosmer, woodland creatures, Selene's entire army it seems.\n\nWe held out as long as we could, fought like trapped Nords. But she was too powerful.

I could not risk telling them the truth. Only a few at the Guild know of Selene's existence. \n\nMy superiors decreed that no mage interfere with her, for she is ancient, and her power is great. But how could I resist such a mythical creature?

I won't be judged. Not by you.\n\nThrough this barrier is the first changeling the Mages Guild has encountered in thousands of years. What mage could turn down the chance to study her, no matter the risk?
Maybe. You know I've always had a special connection to the land. Sometimes things happen, and I don't even think about it. It just happens.
<The cuts on the lieutenant's body form strange but repetitive patterns. His blood was smeared across the uncut portions of skin to create wave-like symbols. The exact cause of his death is unclear.>

Slow down now. No need to be rude. Like I said, I'm a businessman. Truth is, I didn't much like the deal I had with Jagnas anyways. \n\nYou'll owe me a favor, but I'll give him a refund, and your boy can get married whenever he likes.
The ritual has begun, and I am already bound to the Ansei Ward as it is bound to me.\n\nIf you strike me down, the blade will be shattered.
The god Zenithar has blessed Cropsford and watches over us, keeping us from harm and ensuring that we prosper. Everything we have, we owe to Him.

Zenithar is the patron god of hard work. The people of Cropsford personify everything Zenithar holds dear. We work long and hard in our fields, waste nothing, and help our neighbors. All this is glorious in Zenithar's eyes.

Your mockery deserves no response. I merely sense Zenithar's approval of our work in Cropsford. We have much still to do.  Goblins, undead, and other troubles surround us, but with Zenithar's guidance we will overcome these challenges.
This one? Injured? Nobody can injure Razum-dar. He is invincible … but he must ask that you talk quickly. He does not think he will be awake long.
This is a dark age we live in, where there is much work to be done. I hear rumblings that the undead and other vile creatures stir to the north. I shall go there first, and beyond.

No! Wait! Please do not!\n\nIt is sweet of Darius to try to do this for me, but I am not ready to go to the Far Shores. My body was dumped here for a crime I did not commit, and I would see myself exonerated before I rest.
We must walk our own paths now, wherever they lead, and woe to those who bring fear and dread to the world—for beneath our feet they shall become but ashes.

I do. The fiends who did this to me, my brother and his friends … their remains are here too.\n\nThey framed me for stealing valuable gems, but the truth was that they swallowed the gems. They died with the proof of my innocence in their guts!
Yes, as the corpses of the dirty dogs have decomposed, the gems have been … exposed. \n\nIf you would recover these gems, that would prove my innocence.
Heard he used to be a pirate. Got his ship by ambushing a captain and cutting his throat in cold blood. Then he claimed the title of captain for himself and made it stick.
Same thing again, is my guess. He gets his gang to infest the militia, gains our trust, then murders the captain and takes over. Why mess with success?

Ahh, people spreading rumors. You heard true enough. We hired an Altmer mage to clear the land above the village, to make room for our beehives. It's been days, now, and if he doesn't complete the contract soon ….
Well, if he doesn't complete the contract soon, he'll have to eat his wife. Alanya seems like a lovely girl, and I don't want that to happen.

Well, perhaps. The mage's tent has some papers and personal items inside. You could look to see if anything there might explain this delay? And, hmm. Perhaps Alanya may be able to suggest what to look for.
Ah, that'll be the key that gets us in to the Admiral. \n\nOr rather, you. I need you to get that Crown of Bones thing. I've got another task ahead of me.
Ah, that'll be the key that gets us in to the Admiral. \n\nOr rather, you. I need you to get that Crown of Bones thing. I've got another task ahead of me.

The key must open the Admiral's Coral Tower. Take it, enter the tower, and kill the Admiral. \n\nAs for me, it's my duty to look up me dead relatives and see what I can do to help them. Even if it's only to lay them to rest.

Oh, I do—and I've seen you in action, so I expect to get it. \n\nBut the dead skeleton had mates in his crew from my village. That makes them relatives, even ancestors, mayhap. I think I can use that connection to break their bondage. Worth a try.

Oh, I do—and I've seen you in action, so I expect to get it. \n\nBut the dead skeleton had mates in his crew from my village. That makes them relatives, even ancestors, mayhap. I think I can use that connection to break their bondage. Worth a try.
Ulmion, Meratille, and Bashshi-ra. All very influential, in their own way. \n\nWe need to ensure they're freed before we launch a full-scale attack.
Excellent! Many opportunities for heroism, adventure, and thrilling tales after the fact. So, my friend, what will it be? Will you tend to the hostages, or take out their commanders?
The soldiers. The ones who call themselves the Fighters Guild. They seem strong and capable, at least at first glance.\n\nI shall speak to their leader at once.
Raz does not mind getting dirty. It is safe to say, blood looks good on Raz.\n\nTake Larnil's armor if you don't think you can go unnoticed. It is not fashionable, but at least you will blend in.
Hah! Dirty hands for dirty work! Raz will see to our captive friends, then. Stay out of sight if you can. Or, grab Larnil's armor. It's not fashionable, but you will at least blend in.
They will give her to the witch. The Rock Witch.\n\nThe land will kill her. They said the land ….
Not this Goblin-faced meat-eater, his wife.\n\nWait a minute. You're not with the Heritance!
He's fine. He's just tired. We've been running for so long now. I don't know how much longer we can keep this up.
Hmm? Oh, that was Ezreba. She's a good friend of Bowenas, my wife. She was so nice, she was asking me how Bowenas is.

A crystal … Oblivion, no! I thought they were jewel peddlers. I've seen crystals all over town. If those crystals are what's causing the strangeness … I have to find my wife! Please, will you do me another favor?
Oh, yeah. Ezreba seems fine. Whatever's happening, she seems to be all right.
We did what we had to do. This isn't your fault. This is … this is Ayrenn's fault! That witch. She held the Dominion so tight that it suffocated. And now we have no more breath in our chests.

I think so. They're probably … about a week ago, pilgrims began passing through town every day. Some of them asked about the ruins. I didn't think much of it, honestly. I should have paid more attention.

I have no idea! It's a tumble-down, old temple to the Divines, left over from the Colovian days. Just a big empty shell and the old catacombs. A greenshaper came through town a few years ago and worked her magic on it. She found it depressing.

This one and his mate, we lost our way one night. We followed a light in the forest and wound up in this depressing place.\n\nWe took shelter in a cave to the northeast, but that didn't work out so well. Especially not for poor Ernabi.
I'll be fine. As soon as I stop bleeding out of my side, and can walk on my own accord. Actually, now that you mention it ….

Ha. "Business." Every few weeks Halindor volunteers for Rawl'kha's run. He goes off, sells our goods to the first peddler he sees, and heads to Hadran's with the coin. \n\nLet me guess, he was drunk when you got to town?
It's a sad tale. For twenty years I've raised all kinds of exotic beasties. From giant snakes to wolves and even, well, a few stranger things. Never had a problem, not once!

He's right about that. He mentioned it offhand before he left for Rawl'kha. I didn't think much of it, just figured he was drinking again.\n\nBut now … did you see that spirit thing? Are those things inside my neighbors?

It's so sad. I think one of the miners must have gotten a cut working out here. There was blood on the air, and Limbrender went mad with bloodlust. The other trolls followed him into the mine. And I'm just left out here, hoping they're all right.

Ahem. Well, I was on my way to Thizzrini Arena with my proudest accomplishment—a full brace of trained trolls. Or, at least, they were tame when it was just us. Just me, the trolls, and their alpha. I named him Limbrender!
Some rather nasty things lurk in these caves. You need to be careful.
I knew it. He came back to town sloshed, and it's only dumb luck these whatever-they-are didn't get him too. I love that man, but the Green knows he tests me.
Hmm. He keeps telling me he's trying to change. I guess he's finally gotten serious about his responsibilities. Good to hear, in the midst of all this.
Yes, they took him so that she … she had to help them place those crystals. They did not tell her at first, but as soon as Ezreba saw one she knew. They summon the Dro-m'Athra.
Thank you! Thank you, stranger. I'll go for the exit and see you outside. Good luck!
An old story, Ezreba thought. A tale the Clan Mothers tell to scare you, keep you from misbehaving. Ezreba only knows what she was told, as a cub.

The dark mages that you've been fighting. That is what they are called. They've come from the north, Ezreba thinks. From somewhere in Colovia, or Cyrodiil. How they knew to come here, how they knew of the Dro-m'Athra, she does not know.
He … he could not be turned. That is who these dead are. The dead of Greenhill, the strong. The ones who would not submit to the darkness of the Dro-m'Athra. They killed him because he was strong.

The Mages Guild hired Lady Laurent and a few other scholars and treasure hunters for some sort of mission. I was never really made privy to the finer details.\n\nAnyway, Lady Laurent had me gather her equipment and follow her through a portal.
I will. Just … be careful down there. The people in robes, the cultists—they're everywhere!

Ezreba does not know. But the ancient ruins of her people are everywhere in Reaper's March. It is said, long ago, her people locked away the darkness. They hid the darkness of the night beneath the ground. This must be one of those places.

Ahem. "The moons shine brightly at night. But where the bright pale light shines, the darkness is that much deeper. As the people, as the Khajiit live in the light, so things live in the dark. These are the Dro-m'Athra."
Yes. Badly. Swords can cut … cut pretty deep, it turns out. I feel the wounds in the Dominion much worse, though. Those wounds will be the death of me.
Very well. Take all the time you need to make this decision. I'll need your council.
The trip was not without its perils, but everyone watched out for each other.\n\nThe Groundskeeper told us we could settle here, in the Shining Star Inn. Rather nice place, don't you think?

No. I thought about it. I'm glad he was honest with me. The others would just get angry at him, and what purpose would that serve?\n\nEveryone just accepts that some strange curse befell us and that you came along and broke it.

Yes. He gets tired easily, but we keep an eye on him.\n\nI'm glad you told me to try to forgive him. He made a dreadful mistake. I can tell he grieves at the suffering he caused. At heart, he's a good man.

Indeed he did. A couple of others remained behind as well. They didn't want to risk the journey.\n\nI've tried to temper my anger at my father, for causing so much pain. But I can't find it in my heart to forgive him. Not yet.
I did. I felt they were owed an explanation for the lost years and lost lives. So Bernt would not really be welcome here, even if I do find it in my heart to forgive him.
Quickly? It's been weeks since the bandits attacked!

Really? Are you sure? You're teasing me, aren't you?\n\nCome on. We should change clothes. Mom wants me to look presentable for our guests. I'm sure you can find something that suits you inside the manor, in the guest room.
Hesitant? I hate this! And they've got something particular they want to see.\n\nWould you do me a favor and find out? Mingle among them. Eavesdrop. Find out what they've planned for me.
Always. Raz will see you at the lighthouse when our tasks are completed. Bright moons guide your steps.
No reason, really.\n\nI just like dancing. On tables.

No leader? That is an unacceptable situation. I shall take command of this Fighter Guild force. It is the only logical solution.\n\nTalk to those within this building. After I consult with the Groundskeeper, I shall join you inside.
If you're certain, I'll mark you down as having completed training.\n\nAre you certain?

A safe haven, eh? I didn't really expect to see cheerful flowers and clear water anywhere in this dark realm. I assumed we were walking into untimely and painful deaths.\n\nGlad to see I was wrong this one time.
Well, you can't just call him a bandit—he obviously has military experience, and he's smart, no doubt about that. He was someone of consequence before he sank to being a gang boss.

I couldn't let you go off and save the world all by yourself, could I? Not with just these Fighters Guild braggarts. \n\nBesides, there was a portal. How could I not step through and see what was on the other side?

An Ayleid? I thought they were all, you know, dead.\n\nOf course, this is a Daedric Prince's plane. I really need to stop being surprised by such revelations. I have a feeling that won't be the strangest thing I find out before this is all over.
That's a good question. I heard that Captain Alphaury was killed shortly after we were scattered. l was hoping to find another officer here, but no such luck.
They are somewhere in these burial grounds, though I know not where exactly.\n\nYou will know her corpse because she still wears the wooden ring I gave her when we were first married.
Who knows? Perhaps he made a mistake and was disgraced and discharged. Or maybe he just developed a taste for gold and blood.

I think there are a lot of good soldiers out there who need our help. I also know that if we just charge out there with no plan, we're as good as dead.\n\nI'm always eager to rescue a fair maiden or two, but not at the cost of everyone's life.

For now? I shall speak with each soldier here. Tell them what I think we should do and how we should do it. Perhaps listen to their opinions.\n\nTo rush into battle with no allegiance is to command a unit that is already defeated.

Continue to amass our forces until we have enough troops. Then we meet in council and plan our attack.\n\nThe Chasm to the north protects Molag Bal's inner sanctum. We must cross it and confront the Prince if we hope to save Nirn.

Small groups have trickled in since your departure. The warriors inside seem to be under the protection of the knight, Darien. An exceptional fellow. Brave to a fault and devoted to lost causes.\n\nCadwell found them in the wilds.
That's why I need your council, my new friend. Ezreba has been instrumental in Greenhill's success. The town would not be what it is today without her. I … do not know what to do.
I'll follow you. I'm … I'm not going anywhere by myself! Such a brave soul!

It was terrible! We knew the empire was falling apart, but we thought we were safe. Then bandits attacked one night. We ran from the village with nothing but the clothes on our backs. We got separated in the dark. I just hope she made it.

We'd heard it was safe, far from the battlefields. A friend of our mother's—Brittia Imbrex—lives there. She urged us to leave Pell's Gate months ago. She said we'd find work and a home in Vlastarus. I just hope she's still there.

You have no idea how grateful I am to hear you say that. I'll ensure Ezbeba buries every single person who fell today. And she will work with Halindor to seal the catacombs beneath the temple.\n\nBut we will ensure she has a future here.
I … I understand. I'll see her removed from the village. We'll bury our dead without her, and seal the catacombs beneath the temple. I want to put this behind us as quickly as possible.
Very well. What have you decided? What do you say we should do with Ezreba?

Every member of the Dominion should cherish the Elder Scrolls. Our sacred trust to protect them must be our primary focus.\n\nThe Elder Scrolls are prophecies, in essence. But they are much more than that.

Brittia Imbrex. We owe her our lives. She told us to come here months ago. We didn't listen, certain that Pell's Gate was safe. Vlastarus is everything Brittia told us. I only hope Eneriell makes it here.
A rescue, eh? That's all very flattering, but I'm never unprepared. Keep a dagger in my boot for just such an occasion.\n\nI can escape on my own just fine. Any word about Fariel? Is she okay?

The Grand Warlord orders these attacks. Access to each scroll is blocked by a gate. To unlock it, both castles protecting it must be taken away from the alliance that holds the scroll. Once the castles are captured, the way to the temple is open.

The scrolls contain records of all past and future events, but they cannot be read without a severe price—madness, blindness, even death.\n\nMany believe they were created by the Aedra, but why or when is unknown.
Every Elder Scroll we hold grants power to all the soldiers of our alliance. This is another reason our enemies cannot be allowed to keep any of them.

The Elder Scroll must be taken from its temple and brought to one of our six original castles. Once there, it must be placed upon a scroll pedestal. Needless to say, capturing an Elder Scroll requires the cooperation of many soldiers.

Books in this temple contain information about the scrolls, if you wish to know more.\n\nWhen you are done here, go speak with Grand Warlord Sorcalin. Anything else you need to know about the war, she can tell you.
Fine. Are we fighting our way out? I don't have a way to disguise myself.
It was terrible. I was having a nice glass of wine with Bashshi-ra when suddenly … wait, did he do this to me?

I'm more scared of him than those undead up there. He's going to be mad. He told me not to screw this up. It took him years to get Munya to agree to marry him, and now he's going to have to do it all over again.

There was a lot of yelling, fighting, movement. I'm smaller than a lot of the fighters, good at sticking to the shadows. So … I hid. \n\nI'm not proud of it, but at least I can still help them. Or, rather, I can get someone like you to help them.
A potion? I see. Thank you.\n\nDon't do anything too heroic, okay? I'd like to think I might see you again under different circumstances.
How awful. I overheard them talking about this only being a diversion. Do your allies know about that?

Shattering the blade was the only way, albeit there were … consequences.\n\nNecromantic energy was released, causing the dead of Tava's Blessing to rise. The necromancer himself is not a lich, but he has become … a powerful spirit.
You will not live to tell of it!

Ha! That would serve Angiente right, if she came back and ate his face off. No, only necromancers can raise the dead. I haven't seen any of them up there. Someone must have raised those dead to guard the ruins and then left, maybe long ago.
Between you and me, I think she's better off dead. Angiente's not a very nice man. I was amazed she ever agreed to marry him.

If what Cadwell says is true, our job isn't finished here. And I'm positive we got the Daedric Prince's attention at the Shackle. He won't be too happy about what we did to his toys.\n\nThat means we need to hit him before he hits us.

Let the mages inside know that I'll be joining them in a moment. I need to finish with Cadwell and the Groundskeeper first.\n\nI don't know about you, but I find them both to be more than a little … peculiar.
I need to consult with my colleagues in the Mages Guild. We need to gather whatever information we can on this planar vortex. I hate going into a situation blind.
Bright Moons keep you! Kanniz will come with you. May Jone and Jode keep us safe.

It's a prison pit. Ifriz the Unraveler runs the place. He loves to taunt us. \n\nThey split us up. Some of us are down here, but our captains, Eilram and Arakh, are upstairs. A locked passage separates us.
The four of us, yes. There were many more, but, well … you've seen it out there. Even our fabled leader was lost to the harsh plane of Coldharbour.\n\nWe're all that made it back.
What? You've got to be kidding. I saw him being torn away. There's no way they'd let him live. You must have him mixed up with someone … there just isn't any way.

Wasn't just me. A whole group of us got caught by the Daedra. We teleported into Coldharbour to take the fight to Molag Bal, but that didn't work out so good.\n\nWe're down here, our captains are upstairs, and we're all up to our necks in ogrim dung!
Nothing, except that he loves the sound of his own voice.\n\nThere's a Dremora hanging around. She might know more about him. Ask her.

Well, she isn't a guard. But if she's a prisoner, the ogrim certainly don't give her any grief.\n\nTell you the truth, I'm curious about her myself. I've noticed that she's been watching you since you dropped in on our little party.

Not so loud! I left because I couldn't take it anymore. Geneura made us hunt people for meat. I hated it—hated smelling their terror and hearing their screams. Finally, I couldn't take it anymore and ran away.

Laugh if you must, but it's true. I couldn't live with myself any longer, so I ran. Apparently not far enough. I expect they'll track me down now and I'll have to leave again. I'm never going back to Geneura!
Would you like my blood?

Oh! Tu'whacca bless your soul! This will be immensely satisfying!\n\nSearch the corpses of my brother Thadret, Hillid the Blade, and Islaif the Highwayman. I expect their spirits may come forth. I may show up as well … just to watch you smite them.
Of course you are! Those s'wits weren't smart enough to get these before they fled, and I knew that.\n\nI planned this perfectly. I stole the designs fairly and by rights, they should be mine.

Morrowind. I work for House Telvanni. You should know that the Ebonheart Pact is as much my enemy as it is yours.\n\nYou should also know, if I don't return with these ship designs, they won't just kill me, they'll kill my children as well.
I do, and as much as it shames me, I'm going to beg you to let me keep them. \n\nWhere I come from, when you're sent on a mission, you're expected to succeed. The price for failure is unthinkable.

House Telvanni does a great deal of … trade by sea. These designs, the reinforced hulls, would make our ships invincible. \n\nI cannot delay here any longer. I beseech you, for my children's sake, let me take the designs.

You're ruthless, you know that? I suspect I might do the same in your boots, though.\n\nTake the damn designs. My death and the deaths of my children will be on your hands. Watch your back. We may come and haunt you.
You are generous—more generous than I dared hope, and I am grateful.\n\nNext time I encounter one of your kind, perhaps I will stay my blade. Luck to your house, stranger.
Invisibility? Excellent. I'll make for the bridge. Drop a few of those briny barnacle-lovers for me.
<The coals are burning hot.>
The Silvenar and the Green Lady. They're being pursued by the Wild Hunt! Our own people … hunting us down. Please, go. Save them … save the heart of the forest ….
No time. Since the Khajiit fell away from the Dominion, things have been desperate. The Covenant, the Pact … pressing on every front. We had no choice, had to turn to the Wild Hunt.
Rescue me? Hah. From fine wine, salted pork and clean skooma before bed?
It … it doesn't matter. The others will find me. And with my Silvenar dead, I shall soon follow. The heart of the forest, dead, and the Wild Hunt rampant. This is the end ….

Go! There's no hope now … if the Khajiit hadn't left us. If those bastard cats and the witch-queen of the Altmer hadn't … go! Leave us, and remember that the heart of the forest once beat within the chest of an Elf.

You do not imprison Bashshi-ra. At best, you attempt to negotiate an appealing outcome. Yes, I was captured along with the others, but as soon as the sack was removed from my head, I bartered my way into a more comfortable situation.

Damn. Borgath was a good soldier. And a good friend. Thanks for helping the others, though.\n\nI've been watching for Overseer Aruz, but he hasn't come out of his chambers yet. We need to get his key.

The key opens the passage to the next level. That's where they took Captain Eilram and Captain Arakh. If there's a way out of this ogrim dung pit, it's up there. \n\nOnce you get the key, you need to head upstairs and find Captain Eilram.

My main concern is the Fighters Guild. We did try to talk to some of the others, but they've been here too long. Even some of our people haven't recovered from the effects of this place.\n\nBut the way out is open now, if they come to their senses.

So I had hoped, but it seems Vicereeve Pelidil has taken to sea even before we arrived.\n\nI suspect he may attempt to flee when he realizes his forces have lost the shore. That's why you must go after him. You must ensure Pelidil does not escape.

Captain Jimila and her crew have retaken the Prowler and she says the ship's fit for action. They're ready to set sail as soon as you get on board. \n\nMay the winds be at your back, my friend … and may Pelidil fall quickly to your strength!
Because they're rich, that's why! That big house has bags of gold and jewels, I've heard. We hit this place and we never have to work again. I can't believe Klovag isn't here.

That's not who we are! We're raiders, folks who find rich people and steal their stuff. "Building something" is for suckers, the types we raid. Our Mom would be so ashamed if she could hear Klovag speak like that.
We had an argument. For a few years. He wanted to stop raiding, to settle down and belong to someplace. He kept babbling about wanting to "build something," if you can believe that.

Your actions have caused beneficial reactions. Those you saved found others on their way to the city. And the mages have opened stable portals to Nirn, bringing aid to Coldharbour.\n\nThe city thrives, thanks to you!
Curse him and the bowl of mountain bear hash he calls a brain. Did the fool say why he's not coming to help his brother hit the richest target ever?
If anyone who can help us remains in Coldharbour, I am not aware of their presence. If you wish to explore, however, you are free to do so.

I sense other lights trapped in the darkness. Their exact locations are hidden from me, but I can hear their desperate pleas for help.\n\nYou must choose. Will you seek out more allies, or will you allow the war council to begin?
You shall find the Ayleid King and the Mage inside the cathedral. They await your arrival.\n\nOnce you enter the cathedral, the preparations for the final assault to save Nirn will begin.
Happy? He won't know what happy is until I stop beating on him!\n\nGo away. I need to think.
Ah, good then. What are you looking for? Perhaps I can help.
My what? Oh, it's … we're Kothringi. After the great plague from decades past, I fear <<1>> is the last of our people.

For the first time ever, I feel needed. I feel like I'm part of Vlastarus, connected to the town and everyone in it. We all have jobs to do, work that keeps the town running. I've never had that feeling before. Sure beats stealing stuff for a living.
Raz has cooked up just the thing. Invisibility potions. One for each hostage. Good for frightened non-combatants. A waste for talented ones like us.
Tell him I'm not coming. I'm never leaving Vlastarus again. I'm happy here and he just has to accept that. He can find another sucker to raid and steal with him. I'm done with that life.

What? There were spies prowling around here! I knew it!\n\nThey probably waited until all the workers fled and then moved in to steal the designs. Damn cowards! Which one of the ship designs was compromised?

That's a relief. I'm surprised, to be honest with you. I'm almost certain that spies have been watching the town, and I thought for sure, they'd pick this moment to swoop in and steal the designs.\n\nDid you see any evidence of anything like that?

Yes. Once again, the work of Naemon's Shade and the Veiled Heritance. And yes, I do realize we need to return them to rest … but I'm hoping we can uncover more about what happened here while we do.\n\nAre you ready to get to work, my friend?

A simple promise of gold to fund my captives' efforts in exchange for comfort and security. If they win, I hold to that and keep my position under different rule. If they do not, I am rescued and nothing changes. You see? Bashshi-ra always wins.
I will. Come and see me in Woodhearth after this is all over. Perhaps I owe you a drink.

What? The battle was never supposed to take place here. The plan was to attack Woodhearth. The Dominion was not supposed to know this was the staging ground. If what you say is true, then Bashshi-ra sees the winning side. I will do as you ask.

It won't take long! I'll gather the rest of my belongings, if you can pick up my pipe, my wine, and the rest of my meal. If I'm going to be stuck in a Dominion camp for some time, I will at least have something to enjoy.

The Dominion is about to attack? Even with us here as hostages? Oh, right, I guess that is why you are here.\n\nFine. But I need my things before I can go. I can't just leave good wine and pork laying around here. Sea Elves don't appreciate it.

Gall and pox! If those designs fall into the hands of our enemies, it could ruin the Covenant's chance of achieving naval superiority.\n\nAt least you managed to get the designs for the other two. Can I see them, please?
I've got some spare chitin in stock. And I'd be happy to sell it to you. But uh, you're not from around here, right? I could use a favor.
You have to give me credit for trying, right? Here, take the damn designs. \n\nI'm not going to submit to capture, though. If you're going to be a brute, you're just going to have to kill me.
A pleasure. Visit me at my brewery in Woodhearth if you get out of here alive!
It's my pleasure. Enjoy your giant tick exoskeleton in good health.
Really? Fine, sure. Take some chitin. Don't want to anger a Mage.

The village loudmouth, a "lady" named Malesse, immediately started churning the rumor mill. She dropped the nickname "Sells-All" onto me. I'd like this kind of talk to stop. For the sake of my daughter. Can you persuade her to … just to stop?

This is all so stupid. A few months back, I was traveling near Cyrodiil and ran across a group of refugees. I started talking with a little girl who'd lost her family. Ended up adopting her and brought her home. Along with a good haul of coin.

This place, it does things to your mind. Arakh's gone mad. Says I killed her second in command. She attacked us and ran off.\n\nNow she has her own camp to the west. And she keeps sending spies and assassins to kill me!

Why should I? Did that hussy put you up to this? I'm only saying the obvious. He comes back home suddenly with a bunch of coin and a new daughter? He's clearly been having some fun on the side. He's got a 'night blossom' in the city, mark my words.
She's adopted? You mean, he's … wow, that's really quite sweet of him. I hope I haven't blown my chance with him! Wait, you didn't hear that. I'll … I'll stop with the rumors.
She's got quite the way of showing it. I mean, well, it wasn't so terrible. The attention was nice. Anyway, chitin. You needed chitin. Here.

The Dremora dragged us down here and split us up. Easier to maintain control, I'm sure.\n\nI know the Dremora are using mind tricks against us, but the constant torment gets to you. It wears you down. Makes it hard to think straight.

It's my sword. And my father's before me. I dropped it while fighting one of the ogrims. \n\nIf you aren't an illusion, you'll recover it for me. If you are an illusion, I figure you'll disappear and that will be the end of that.

Before this place made her crazy, Arakh was a good friend. Now …?\n\nI need to get Arakh back on board or get her out of the way. Then I can get everyone out of here. I'll head over and talk to her again.

Thank the Eight! I really could use some help. Something's gone terribly wrong, and I don't know what I did. I should never have told them I was a powerful mage. My poor Alanya … I don't want to eat her!

Based on where the portal appeared, the sigil stone is probably in this realm's Moonhenge. \n\nBut the Dremora keep the Moonhenge sealed behind a gateway. You'll need to find the keys and unlock the pillars to open the gateway.
What? An Orc's not allowed in the Hall? I didn't see a sign. Piss off.

The Moonhenge you came through was an Ayleid ruin. But where did they get the idea?\n\nFind the keys the Dremora use to unlock the pillars that seal the gateway. I suspect we'll find the sigil stone that powers the portal through there.

I almost expected you to stab me with it, not hand it to me. Hard to trust anything in this place. \n\nBut as you can see, we have a situation developing here. Arakh can barely refrain from attacking us. We need to fix this now.
Arakh says she can't stop the voices without her helmet. \n\nShe said the eyes have it. I think she means the watchers. Maybe the helmet will calm her down.
Other than you? No, I get along fine in here. I'm, what-you-call-it, naturally gregarious.

It ain't your concern, but who cares? I'm keeping an eye on things for Uncle Thakh. Customers disappearing like dust-devils is bad for business. \n\nRedguards aren't worth spit when it comes to listening, so that's my job. I'm a good listener.
Thank you for doing this. Sinfay wanted to retrieve it herself, but to be honest, we're not at our best right now. None of us could survive a battle with a watcher.

We need to end the Planemeld before Nirn is destroyed. To do that, we must deal with the planar vortex. To reach the vortex, we need to cross the Chasm and get through whatever defenses the Dark Lord throws at us.\n\nI fear battle is inevitable.
Well said, friend! Please, hold your questions until everyone who wants to has had an opportunity to speak.\n\nAfter that, we can debate the details as you see fit.

I knew it! I saw a Dark Elf slinking around the docks all suspicious-like just the other day.\n\nIf she had made off with these designs, it could've kept us from establishing naval superiority! Good thing you stopped her.

Once inside the Hollow City, we'll begin helping with the war effort. \n\nWe must test the Lights of Meridia and investigate methods for destroying Molag Bal's Planemeld mechanism. There is always research to do in campaigns such as this.

Where do I begin? Thicker masts, extra backstays, a narrower keel, lighter ballast … the list goes on.\n\nThe real battle changer's going to be the reinforced hull though. No one's going to be able sink these babies. No one.
What does my state of being matter to an insignificant torchbug like you? \n\nYou enter our library and seek to take what is ours. For that, you shall most assuredly die!
Leave? But this is my home. And it's your home now, too.\n\nOr should I say it's your tomb now? So nice of you to give me the honor of ending your pitiful life!
Would you like me to be? I think my imitation of him is nearly perfect, don't you?\n\nBut now that you've discovered my deception, you have to die.

Don't worry about me. I'll head to Greenhill to recover. Then I'm leaving the March. I'm heading home to Silvenar, where it's nice and safe. Would you tell our boss what happened here? She'll wanna know.
It's the perfect place. Not many people know about the docks here—it's not exactly a regular port of call. \n\nWe can build the ships without too many prying eyes.
Her name's Kuna, and she keeps an office in Rawl'kha. Tell her I quit. I'll never set foot in a mine ever again, no matter what the paymaster promises! Good luck on the road, traveler!

The chitin of a hoarvor, five torchbug thoraxes, and a heartwood fragment. I don't know … maybe Ranneth will know where you can find these things? I have to get back up the hill. Just find me when you have them. Thank you, thank you, thank you!

A ritual? Oh! The ritual Master Telenger sent for me! You're right! This should absolutely work! We'll just need to gather the right ingredients. Err. Will you gather them? I really should attend to … things on the hill.
Since the spell I cast didn't … wasn't intended to bring in the Atronachs. I'm having trouble … sending them back!

He became some kind of spectre, and he bound himself to my ward, but that allowed me to imprison him within it. He is … contained now.\n\nThe important thing is that the ward is restored and can again protect the Alik'r desert. For that, I thank you.
Alanya! No! Ranneth will cook her up now that she's seen what's happening here.\n\nI have to go, I … I'm such a failure! Please, you have to help me set this right.

I normally fail at everything. You have to understand: this spell worked too well!\n\nI wanted a simple magical construct, and it summoned dozens of atronachs. Something has to be corrupting my ritual. Twisting it.
To knock down a castle door, a ram's your best bet. Deploy one, get enough people on it to push it up to the door, then stay with it until the door collapses.
We had no doubt in your capabilities. What sort of king would we be if we didn't look good in a crown? Superb craftsmanship!
Then it shall serve as contrast to show true beauty comes from within. Splendid, subtle craftsmanship!
<Nothing happens.>
<Nothing happens.>
<Nothing happens.>

What are you talking about? I saw the Atronachs. Our sacred wood ravaged by Daedric beasts. I gave him a chance and he spit in my face. I wish it were otherwise, but the Green Pact is clear. He must eat his sin.

And he can send those things away. I see. It's clear to me now that Willowgrove needs someone wise to the ways of spellcasting. Hmm. In the meantime, I owe some apologies. I will set about freeing Alanya. She did not deserve our rough treatment.
You have acted with honor so far. And I have no reason to think you a liar. What about the Atronachs, though? We aren't prepared to face beasts like that.

Cautious might be a better word. Since the Dominion formed, there has been a great deal of political turmoil. The old guard in Auridon, resistance to King Camoran's rule … and now the spiritual leader of the Khajiit corrupted by a dark spirit.

News of Akkhuz-ri's fall has spread as fast as the wind. All of Elsweyr is talking about these two young women. As you probably know, this is the first time we've had two candidates for the Mane at the same time. There's a great deal of … talk.

Oh, no. My people are deeply divided. I believe this is one of the most vulnerable moments our fragile Dominion has faced. King Camoran himself felt he had to remain in Valenwood. Stay close to the people, keep them from worrying.

Following you? An interesting notion. Perhaps you are the one following me?\n\nBut enough with the pleasantries. I was checking something. You should run along now. The other mortals seem lost without you.
My, your interrogation technique is withering. I feel I must reveal everything to you. \n\nWait. No I don't. The feeling has passed. Maybe it was simply something I ate.

My end was inevitable all along. Someone new must become caretaker of the Valenwood. Aranias was guided here for this purpose. \n\nIt's fascinating. In her heart, I think she knows the truth, but she's conflicted. Perhaps it is Andur's influence?
<You place the shattered fragments gently on the smoldering coals.>
<The steel absorbs the milk.>
<The earth clings to the steel.>
<The flames come alive.>
<The broken blade lays before you.>
<The blade seems to absorb the milk.>
<The earth clings to the metal.>

After Akkhuz-ri's fall, and the death of Gharesh-ri, the Khajiit fell away from the Dominion. The other Alliances moved in. We tried to make the heart of the forest beat that much stronger, but they lost hope.
Who knows? As soon as my mate wakes we can get moving again. Then from there, I have no clue. But wait. He's stirring. What is it, my heart? Are you all right?

We … we said the words. And the Wild Hunt returned to Valenwood. It roamed through the forest, drove our people feral. It had consumed them before we realized what had happened. That's when the chase began.

There's not much you can do. They tracked us cross country. Overwhelmed us. I'm not … I'm not going to last much longer. Maybe you can help Raz. He's up on the hill. Find him. He's the Queen's last defense.

Where have you been the last few months? The Veiled Heritance, those bastards, led a revolt against the Queen. All of the Summerset Isles have risen against her. It's been all the Eyes could do to keep her alive.

The Veil is stronger now than it ever was. Where … where have you been? The Battlereeve turned on Her Majesty when she tried to hold the Dominion together by force of will. The other alliances … took Cyrodiil, march on Summerset.
Good … good. Razum-dar is tired. He … he will sleep. If he does not wake up, this one hopes to see you where the Bright Moons dwell. Good luck, my friend.
For Raz? Nothing. Raz will rest here, until this Eye of the Queen closes. All that Raz has left is his oath. He swore he would protect Ayrenn. He swore he would protect his dearest friend.

Yes. The Wood Elves consumed by rage. The Khajiit, retreated into the desert. And my people … Summerset risen up against me. By the time the Pact and the Covenant arrive on our shores, there will be nothing left to pick apart.

What reason is there left to fight? We've lost our heart. Our soul. And now, with my death, the body of the Dominion shall fall silent as well. Leave me, please. Let a Queen die with dignity. In silence, and solitude.
No. I have nowhere I can go. My people have rejected me. Rejected the whole idea of an alliance with other races. The Eagle banner is fallen. I might as well fall too.
Clever girl: she tried to trap him in the tunnels below the throne. Look for for the torn up ground.

Yes. For centuries, my sole focus has been shaping and maintaining the Valenwood, protecting it from outside influence, and from itself.\n\nNow that she has come, I am free to return to the earth, give back to that which has given so much to me.
What? That old buzzard was telling the truth? Fine, fine. Then we should make sure someone looks in on Kalari. Poor little girl is scared to death, thinking there are ghosts in her big new house.

Dark moons and dull claws! What has become of my town, my S'ren-ja? Bandits and spells and … wait a moment. Did you say skooma dealers? Did the name Rakhad come up at all as you dealt with these problems?

Jone and Jode, strike me down! Shuzura had thought him run out of town, his dark influence purged from her clan. But no ….\n\nStranger, you have done so much for S'ren-ja already. Will you help Shuzura … she means, S'ren-ja again?

Shuzura must admit … she let Rakhad too close. She let Rakhad do as he pleased, for so long. When he was her assistant, Rakhad would often use an old cave outside of town for … projects.\n\nShe never asked. Because she did not want to know.

There was a time when Shuzura knew every plot, every rumor, every story within her village. Now … she cannot even banish a scoundrel like Rakhad. Thank you. Please, speak to Tazia. She … she'll offer you some coin for your service.
There's been so much fighting, so much death. Even if we walk the path through the Den of Lorkhaj … seeing these visions has made me realize how critical the Mane can be. I don't know if I'm ready.
Perhaps … for you, Hallowed. For Khali … for the Khajiiti people. Hallowed, we owe you so much. I don't know if I can ever thank you properly.

I don't know, but somehow, it seems like that's what I was meant to do all along. When he burned the forest, I actually felt its pain. I think I'm … connected to this place.\n\nI can't fight Andur though—he's too strong. Will you help me?

I think he was a man too, once, the Wilderking. I mean, he was like us. But when he took this on, he became something else. \n\nI think he merged with the Valenwood and forgot his previous self entirely.
Mane Akkhuz-ri is the leader of the Khajiiti people. We're grateful for his help here and to count him as one of our allies.
Kill myself? That would be a blessing. I'll be free of these memories, free to know who I am. Here I come, my master!
The final step. The Cleansing itself. Please step back, Moon Hallowed.
Are you certain? The point of war isn't to die for your cause, it's to make your enemies die for theirs.\n\nAre you ready to do that?
The Grand Warlord has much on his mind; be grateful for a few minutes of his time.\n\nTo me come Grand Warlord Zimmeron's orders. These I post to the boards that flank me. Which should we discuss?
Even the newly hatched can understand Bounty missions. The task is to kill enemy soldiers. All that lives must die; these missions seek to hasten that day for our enemies.
Information is critical to our efforts. A Scouting mission sends you to a target deep in enemy territory.\n\nThe swamp eel sees but is not seen. Be the swamp eel. Then return here.
Got tired of you pestering her, eh?\n\nVery well. I administer the Battle and Warfront missions. Go ahead, ask me about them.

Battle missions send small groups of soldiers to capture enemy resources. Each keep is supported by a farm, lumbermill, and mine. Denying the enemy these resources is the first step to claiming that keep for the Pact.
A Warfront mission targets one of the enemy's keeps. Controlling keeps is the key to conquering Cyrodiil. This is a major effort though—go in without a large force and you're all going to die.
Not yet. We might blame the storm if not for the bruising around his neck. Whoever did this was very strong.
The Mages Guild is dedicated to the pursuit of knowledge and the wisdom to wield it. Let me guess, you are interested in becoming a Docent?

We find bodies from time to time. Sugar fiends who fail to pay the Crosstree. Occasionally the smugglers themselves. Usually stabbed in the back, a pair of crossed lines cut into their faces.\n\nThis man bears no such marks, nor was he stabbed.
That much is obvious. This man is affiliated with the Crosstree, a group of smugglers that runs skooma to <<1>>.\n\nWhat's strange is the manner of his death.
He bears the colors of the Crosstree and skooma was found on his person.
Ah, blessed moisture. Accept this package of munitions, relieve me of its burden. Take it to Adalmor on the siege range, beyond the Northern Morrowind gate. He is large and loud, as are all Nords.
I appreciate the assistance from common folk such as yourself. This sword is a significant specimen of lore; direct evidence of a legendary event in ancient Redguard history.
There are books about this, but as you may be illiterate, I'll enlighten you. \n\nI suspect this is the site where <<1>> slew <<2>>, his ally, over the love of the fair Sayeedeh.

The blade of a sword-singer is a physical link between ancient Yokuda and Alik'r. \n\nNavid used this particular sword to slay his rival, and then himself. As a piece of history, it belongs in a proper Imperial museum.
The sword in question is a wondrous object, and <<1>> believes it will appear to those who have a connection with death or whatever lies beyond.

Congratulations. I hereby grant you the rank of Student in the Mages Guild, along with the responsibilities and privileges thereof. Every book you acquire, or collection of books you help to complete, will now earn you status among us.

Docents are those who bring rare texts to Mages Guild members, such as myself, who are qualified to curate their use. In exchange for this service, access to restricted wares and the occasional special task may be shared with you.

Let me see that! Ooh, this is rare indeed.\n\nYou're well on your way to earning membership within the Mages Guild, just in bringing this to my—our attention. The Guild provides great rewards when a Docent acquires books for our library.

Congratulations. I hereby grant you the rank of Student in the Mages Guild, along with the responsibilities and privileges thereof. Every book you acquire, or collection of books you help to complete, will now earn you status among us.

Bringing in rare texts for the library as a docent earns you reputation among us, and as your reputation grows it comes with greater and greater rewards.\n\nAre you interested in joining the Mages Guild?
It's the light, it's very bright, my eyes have been watering… that's all it is.
Quiet! My partner already suspects, don't you know I would be ostracized if my illness came to light?

I had to see to the consecration of my father's remains, of course. Then I sought to catch you at Tu'whacca's Throne, but I arrived too late. \n\nSoon thereafter, I joined Prince Azah on the road. He suspected the Withered Hand would come here.
I don't know what you hope to squeeze out of me, but our caravan was already robbed. I have nothing.
I don't think you do. Now if you'll excuse me?
Then why are you bringing it up? Some distorted sense of kinship? This was done to me, and I am not about to discuss it with a stranger.

What? Do you not realize that you have become quite a famous figure? You are certainly considered a friend to the Ash'abah!\n\nThrone Keeper Farvad told me of your heroics in liberating the Temple. I hope you can stop the Withered Hand here as well.

I wish I could tell you. Fahara'jad's naval shipyards are here, but I cannot imagine why the Withered Hand would care about that.\n\nI hear these were sacred grounds back in the days of the Ansei. Perhaps that is what drew the Withered Hand here.
The great scholar from Cyrodiil doesn't know. Imagine that?
The magnificent scholar believes that the sword is too damaged to be used anymore, if it even exists at all.
He wants to preserve it in a safe warehouse in Cyrodiil, where all the other artifacts have been taken, I imagine.
If not me, another would surely stand here.\n\nMy advice to you is simply to look along the shore. Others searched inland and were disappointed.

The wagon's owner was an uninjured woman with a pristine blade, facing an unmasked man wielding a battered axe.\n\nThe woman said the man was a bandit, and had attacked her. She begged <<1>>'s aid, but <<1>> walked away. And yet, she lived.
<<1>> requested you return to her. Leave the fighting to us, and we will live up to your previous example.\n\nNow, light the fire! Show them how Shadowscales return a favor.

Not sure yet. Perhaps one of their clients has taken issue with them, or maybe they have a new competitor. It is difficult to tell with criminals.\n\nRest assured, we will find out what happened here.
Long ago, a foreign mage came to <<1>> and claimed his power a match for our swords. He turned steel to mist at will.\n\n<<2>> was an initiate, yet faced the mage and won. How did <<2>> win the duel?
I did not expect you would find it. Only those who are … different … are capable of such a feat.\n\nWhat do you intend to do with it?

He corrupted one of the Ansei Wards, using it as some sort of necromantic focus to channel energy from the the dead. He's performing a ritual in the lighthouse. \n\nHe says this ritual will transform him into a lich. Will you help me stop him?
