A ram will crack a keep open like a warhammer on a mudcrab. Deploy a ram, get enough soldiers on it to push it up to the keep's main door, then stay with it until the door falls in.
Blech. Tastes like bugs.
I see. I noticed the mist had changed. I thought it was only my changed eyes embracing its corruption. \n\nThank you for this. I thought it was hopeless, but now I can return home to Thorinor.
I do … I do feel somewhat warmer. More myself. Less cloudy. \n\nBut what if they come for me again? I feel like they were in my mind. Always watching.

Not good, I'm afraid. Rumors about someone stealing the Ansei Wards run rampant. And every day there are new reports of risen dead. \n\nThe Crowns and some Forebears are calling for my father to step down. There's even talk of rebellion.
Of course! What else is there? Power makes us happy. It lifts us up above the rabble.\n\nIn life, I had such power that you wouldn't believe! I was foolish, though. I let it slip away.
Trebuchets, catapults, and ballistae are Dragons of the battlefield, causing massive damage to walls and enemies. \n\nI sense the target dummies mocking you. Choose a weapon and punish them.

Only those with the keenest senses can even see it, and only one without a soul should be able to take it from its resting place.\n\nI do not know how you lifted it unless your soul … no matter. What is your intention?

That is wise. <<1>> was buried at the Lion's Tomb, though he did not deserve such an honor. It was hoped the curse would fade in time, but instead the sword claims more victims.\n\nThe curse is his to bear. He must take back the blade.

I urge you to reconsider. You do him no favors by giving him this blade.\n\nYou know the curse it bears. Anyone who carries the sword will be attacked by those tortured spirits. Only the dishonored one is not so bound.
Even if <<1>> escapes the vengeful spirits, he will take the sword to Cyrodiil. However cursed this sword may be, it is still a relic steeped in our history, our heritage. It must stay in the Alik'r!
You bring only misery by removing that sword, wayfarer. Make the wise choice.
That is for the best. Leave it at the Lion's Tomb on the shore.\n\nThen talk to <<1>> before you leave; perhaps he will abandon his foolish search.

No, it is a deep, ancient curse. There is darkness in that blade that even the Divines would struggle to banish.\n\n<<1>>'s spirit seeks to distance himself from the blade, but he is the source of its evil. He cannot keep shedding the burden to others.

Yes. Since we were knee-high to a dune beetle. He and Uwafa both. We studied together, but they were sadistic little cretins, obsessed with death in all its forms. That was before their father turned. \n\nIf only we had killed all of them back then.
I do not wish to pry, I was simply curious if you plan to throw your hard-won gold into a fool's sinkhole like this "Winking Jackal."
I hope so, for everyone's sake. If you want a siege weapon of your own, you can buy them from siege merchants at our gates and keeps.

I misjudged the … committment of others. It was a simple miscalculation, but it brought my entire base of power to a grinding halt.\n\nI won't make that mistake again, though. I'll use my power to its fullest extent. No one will stop me!

I suspect it has something to do with Alasan's plan to become a lich. \n\nIf this is where the Ansei was born, perhaps Alasan had to bring the ward here in order to corrupt it. That's just an educated guess, of course.
A deception. I watch <<1>> so he does not plunder Alik'r. I know more than his books have explained.
The mage's tent has some papers and personal items inside. Perhaps you could look to see if anything there might explain this delay? And, hmm. Perhaps Alanya may be able to suggest what to look for.

We are simple people here and we know little of magic. As part of the contract, Alanya offered herself as our pact-hostage. I want to give Master Pircalmo more time to work his magic, but he has little time left.

In a way we are all cheated, wayfarer. Have you not heard that Uncle Thakh's den of cutpurses receives subsidies from Fahara'jad's court? They believe it encourages trade further inland by appealing to foreigners' greed.
Zeht's blessings be upon you, wayfarer.

Most don't. The Forebears … never mind. I only stay here to prevent my doltish cousin from squandering his wealth. \n\nMy advice is this: invest your gold in a stable and legitimate enterprise. Perhaps a tea house or some well-irrigated farmland.
Oh silly Pircalmo. Yes, yes. He's taking his time. Don't worry, he's getting it just right. I bet he's just forgotten some ritual components. Or the ritual itself, he did that once. Silly Pircalmo.
I bet he'd appreciate any help you'd be willing to give. Pircalmo is a kind, gentle soul. Didn't help him at all in the Guild, but it makes me love him all the more.

As well you should. All Pact soldiers should covet the Elder Scrolls. It is our destiny to control them all!\n\nThe simplest understanding of the Elder Scrolls is that they are prophecies. But they are so much more than that.

All resistance must be crushed. When our banner flies boldly atop the flagpole, all know the Pact has conquered again. For keeps, we must breach walls or sunder gates to reach the heart of the enemy stronghold.\n\nNone of this will be easy.
That old tale? Sure. We all grew up hearing about her. An immortal witch who extends her life by bathing in blood.\n\nI tried it once. I just ended up feeling crusty.

Most of our tales are based on some measure of truth. I've heard that some people think she was just an old Bosmer who went mad and killed some of her clan, eventually becoming an exile. Who could say for sure?

Sure. Just chase a goldwing to the source of its rainbow and she'll be there on the edge of the Fountain of Fortune. \n\nHah. Only kidding, my friend. The Wild Witch is long gone, if her story was ever true to begin with.
So the story goes. I don't know about that, but Doralin in the village knows the story better than I do. You might talk to her if you're interested in the finer details.
I think Doralin here in the village has a copy of one of the old songs, if you're interested in that. She's quite fond of the tale, so maybe you should speak to her.
She told you to talk me, didn't she?
Because she likes messing with me.
Hah, you mortals. You always make me laugh. Yup, I'm a talking dog. Name's Barbas. I'm a companion to the Daedric Prince of Wishes. Guy by the name of Clavicus Vile.

There are many versions of her in the tales, but they are all based on an old Bosmer who is very real. I've met her myself, though she is a reclusive one. She's called Galereth, and she's a master at the Art of Hiding.

She is indeed an alchemist of great skill, having perfected the art over centuries. I can't say whether or not that part of the tale is true, but if it could be cured by any natural means, I would bet she knows how.

That would be up to her alone. She seems to only reveal herself to those that interest her. But you're welcome to try. She has many hovels tucked away in the wood, but the one nearest Longhaven is just by the sea, to the southwest.
Look, do you want to fix things for that guy or not? His wife will get eaten if you sit around talking to dogs all day. If you want to set things right you'll have to smash the altar.

Well, this altar here next to me is the cause of all his problems. He had this silent plea to have something work well, just once in his life. The altar twisted that up. And … to be honest it keeps me bound here.
Sure, mortal. What can old Barbas tell you?
Hold on, hold on, we'll get to that in a moment. I bet you're here about all those Atronachs, right? That stupid mage let his magic get away from him.
He's locked within my home. He was being held until … until mealtime. Go and fetch him. I will untie Alanya and meet you there.
Questions are good. Ask and ask again. That is the systematic method of experimentation! Remember that you must know the rules before you can successfully break them.

Zur's specialty is transmutation. Change one thing into another. So. Not too difficult to change you from large to small. Then you can slip past the obstacles that block the entrance.\n\nZur never said it would be easy, Dark Elf. Mind your tongue!

Unfortunately, no. The soul-meld weakens us, and we must conserve our strength. With the recipe and the ingredients, this one can make a transmutation potion and exert almost no energy whatsoever. A much better approach at this time, yes?

Oh, yes! We came to defeat the evil Molag Bal! Or was it Mannimarco? Zur forgets. So many bad things start with the letter "m." But something went wrong and Gadris and this one ended up here. That's when the Daedra melded our souls.

Well, it wasn't that bad. Drasilla was very kind—for an evil Daedra. But she became infatuated. My natural charms, I suppose. But the more I refused her, the harder she pressed herself upon me.\n\nI'd rather not talk about this, if you don't mind.
Quite so. I must have blacked out. When I opened my eyes, a winged beauty was hovering above me. She took me in her claws and carried me to the top of that tower.

Of course. I didn't mean them, silly! I meant Thallik's and the vine-man's peasants. Zombies and skeletons—horrible creatures! Imagine, resorting to the dead because the living won't help you.\n\nMy soldiers, on the other hand, follow me willingly.

Ah, you see right through me! I used to be a princess, you know. But I made a few bad deals and had some obnoxious brat disrupt my well-laid plans. Don't you hate when that happens?\n\nI … I don't mean to upset you. Just bad memories.

Of course they do! I make sure that my peasants are well taken care of. I do my best to keep my forces in good spirits. That's what a good ruler does!\n\nI make a bad situation tolerable. It's the least I can do to ease their lot in life.

Do I sense overconfidence or just plain stupidity?\n\nThis isn't your fight. This isn't your war. Don't you understand that? We are here because we disappointed a Daedric Prince—the very same one you came here to defeat!

Why would someone such as yourself risk so much for the lives of others?\n\nYou stand in a Dragon's lair. The way is clear behind you, yet you insist on moving forward, provoking the Dragon with every step you take. It's maddening to me!
Are you certain? If so, I'll mark you down as having completed training. Think carefully—there's a lot to know about this war.\n\nWhat do you say?

A pleasure. Think nothing of it. The merest trifle. Truly.\n\nYou'll find this Tharn fellow at the top of the Tower of Bones. You'll need to make your way through the keep's heart to get to it, but it's not terribly far.
I … can't believe it!\n\nThere's so much to study … look at the shape of the blade! You can see the way the leather used to wrap around the pommel. The tip is even chipped!
New recruit, eh? Hope you're better than the last few who've come through here.\n\nSee the Bounty and Scouting boards on either side of me? Those are the missions I'm in charge of.
Indeed? Well, I might just take you up on that. \n\nBut safety first! I'll stay here for the nonce and make sure nothing comes to bugger up our little adventure from behind.

I understand the King of Worms has set him to the task of inspecting the soul gems that find their way into the castle—which is to say, well … all of them. You'll see crates of the things scattered around the premises.
I … the unmitigated … how dare … fine!\n\nTake them all and do not return. My master will be angry, but not as enraged as he would be if the game was permanently disrupted. Now be gone with you!
What? How dare you threaten me!\n\nYou are lucky that I even gave you a reward at all. The balance … the balance must be maintained!

Rods that will reverse the soul-meld. Just find the components and craft the rods. We will try to recuperate and regain enough strength to teleport ourselves inside. If you have questions, please ask them before you drink the potion.
To hear of Battle and Warfront missions, no doubt. These are under my care.\n\nWhich would you like to learn of?
The enemy's resource sites—farms, mines, and lumbermills—support their forts, enhancing their strength. Battle missions send groups of soldiers to capture resources and greatly weaken those forts.

In Warfront missions, we bring the wrath of Diagna against our foes' forts. These attacks require large numbers of warriors. Prepare yourself for great deeds and grave danger when you embark on a Warfront quest!
Good. Here, take these to Bugbesh. She's at the siege range near the Southern High Rock gate. Look for an Orc covered in dirt and oil.
I … the unmitigated … how dare … fine!\n\nTake them all and do not return. My master will be angry, but not as enraged as he would be if the game was permanently disrupted. Now, be gone with you!
What? How dare you threaten me!\n\nYou are lucky that I even gave you a reward at all. The balance … the balance must be maintained!
My what? Oh, my guide. I seriously doubt he has anything to contribute to my research.\n\nDon't worry about him. He will be compensated appropriately. As will you. Talk to <<1>>, please.
I need to take this back to Cyrodiil right away. Julianos has blessed me this fine day.
The uneducated masses always object to progress, even if it's for their own good.\n\nYou can go now, I have to take this back to Cyrodiil.

He did. And now he's returned, as a foul undead creature. A vampire.\n\nI could not raise my blade against one so revered. But no such respect compels him. I couldn't defend the students. Couldn't even defend myself.

The wounds have long since healed. I've already fallen to his curse. It is how he compelled me to call for more and more students. Here, he feeds on our strongest.\n\nI'd hoped to stop him, with your aid. I was too weak.
I … the unmitigated … how dare … fine!\n\nTake them all and do not return. My master will be angry, but not as enraged as he would be if the game was permanently disrupted. Now, be gone with you!
What? How dare you threaten me!\n\nYou are lucky that I even gave you a reward at all. The balance … the balance must be maintained!
What? You mustn't jest of such things! What did she say, truly?\n\nBut your manner shows no deceit. How … how did this happen?

Now I know you lie, for he's been dead for almost a century! Yet, the legends never did speak of his death ….\n\nSep take you! I won't hear another word! Begone, and I will wait for <<1>> to tell me the truth of it!
No. He cannot be slain now. There is a way, but … I am fading.\n\nWith the ward broken, my strength … wanes quickly. I will presently go to the Far Shores, unless you can reforge the blade.

We need the gods' favor … for Tava, capture the desert wind … for Morwha, get the milk of a goat … and for Zeht, gather the earth from a fallen warrior's grave.\n\nWith these elements, reforge the blade … then bring it to the Ansei Shrine.

Trebuchets, catapults, and ballistae are weapons to be feared. Their reach is long and their fury devastates walls and foes alike.\n\nLearn to use these weapons here. Let the target dummies feel your wrath!
Good. You can buy siege weapons from a siege merchant at our entry gates or at forts we control.
I'm here because of you, you vile, sniveling, sorry excuse for a … argh!\n\nCalm down, Kinlady. Calm down.

I was doing what was right for my people! Something you know nothing about.\n\nTo just throw our customs to the side for some foolish, young woman! You understand nothing about the Altmer. Nothing! I was in the right. You were the one in the wrong.

That is precisely why. Both Raifa and Tafa are too entwined to offer clear counsel, and I, on the other hand, have only just arrived.\n\nYou have touched everyone present. As I said before, I would hear your opinion before I render judgment.
And here I am, no thanks to you!\n\nMy connections to the higher powers have granted me a second chance. One I fully intend to use to tear you apart. Piece by piece. You won't stop me again.

In truth, it is what I thought as well. <<1>> has served the school faithfully. It was not her desire to fall to a vampire.\n\nBut, it would not suit the school for her to remain. Come, and I shall render judgment.
In truth, it is what I thought as well. <<1>> has served the school faithfully, yet she hid when honor demanded she reveal her secret.\n\nShe will die by her own hand. Come. I shall render judgment.

Don't test me, fool!\n\nI can't say I blame you for coming to join the game, though. The lure of power. The chance for Molag Bal's favor. You're more like me than I imagined. Ruthless. Power-hungry. A worthy opponent.

I am, no thanks to you. I failed Molag Bal and I was pulled into his realm. Now I fight to regain his favor.\n\nBut I spit on his favor! I would rather accept nonexistence than be forced to grovel for these scraps from the Dark Lord's table.

I made mistakes. I became a … monster.\n\nI don't want Molag Bal's favor, but if I can win this cursed game I might be able to regain my mortal existence. Before I became a monster. Or at least I can hope to earn a true and final death.
To take out a fort's door, you need a ram. Simple as that. Deploy it, get it up to the door, and stay with it until the door crashes in.\n\nEasy.
To most Covenant soldiers, the Elder Scrolls are means to an end, weapons that will help us conquer Cyrodiil. \n\nBut they are far more than that.

How can you not? I can't participate directly in this game, but you won't need to worry about my interference if you help me.\n\nWith the power of the death rune, you can free us all. For now, you simply need to charge it. Transform yourself and kill!

It transforms you into an agent of destruction. Every creature you slay strengthens the rune. Not even the Observer can stand against the power of the fully charged death rune.\n\nI know you hate me. It's mutual. But we need each other now.

Our foes' forts and resources must be taken. Fort walls or gates must be smashed down for us to reach the heart of the enemy stronghold. The defenders must be defeated and our banner raised on the flagpole. \n\nEasy to say, harder to do.

The Observer will force you to make a decision soon. He won't let you play the game on your own for much longer. I want you to play on my side. Let us work together to win this thing.\n\nI saved the Dark Elf. Have faith in me. We can do this.

I know that we had our differences in the past. You did what you thought was right. But when you think about it, that's exactly the same thing I was doing.\n\nI wish to make amends. I want things to be good between you and I.

Every conquest weakens our enemies and brings the Covenant closer to control of Cyrodiil. \n\nYour participation in these actions enables you to acquire equipment and weapons from Covenant siege merchants.

I never thought I would see this place. I've seen the drawings in the oldest texts … the Plane of Jode. The place where the Bright Moons dwell, the home of the gods. It's … different than I expected in some ways. But that makes sense.
Let's just … wait a moment. If I'm right, the Path will show us the way.
The Path is changing to suit us, to reflect the challenges we face. Just like for Zibbiden-jo … the Argonian soul reavers … sorry, Hallowed. Just thinking of one of the stories I read.
You've come to the right man, mate. I've been with <<1>> longer than anyone—I was part of the group that helped him take his first ship.
You aren't? Sorry, I didn't mean to lash out at you then. It's just that these honorless bandits keep moving in, abusing our gear, eating our food, and just wasting our supplies.
Not while <<1>> is in charge. Take my complaint to <<2>>, he's unofficially the man who's authority we still in support of the militia recognize. He may have a plan.
There's no one else. I'll certainly not be a replacement for the master, but I will try my best. I must, for the sake of the school.
If that is what I must do, then I shoulder that burden gladly.

I was. I've graduated and been cleared for combat, but I'd feel guilty leaving while bandits still infest the camp. So I stay and help maintain what little control we have of the camp. It'd be easier if <<1>> would just let us engage them in combat.
I hope so. I'd like to join our other men on the field. Talk to <<1>>, he's unofficially the real man in charge of the militia.

I do not know, but trust your destiny, for it will lead you where you need to be.\n\nFirst though, you must secure my ward. Find someone you can entrust with its keeping. I sense that we will meet again. May the gods watch over you until then.

The sibling I speak of has not been slain, and has possession of the third Ansei Ward, but I cannot sense its location. \n\nDespite our victory here, the Alik'r desert is still in danger. Whatever has befallen, you must recover the third ward.

And I respect you for that, hence my warning.\n\nWhen last we fought, things were different. We were in the mortal realm, playing by mortal rules. In Oblivion, the rules are different. We have no power. We only have what the Lord of Schemes allows.

Why didn't you say so? I thought you were another sand-eater come to fight for the Alik'r.\n\n<<1>> is a great man, but he has a tragic history. It's given him a gruff exterior, but his bully-boys would follow him anywhere.

He's not? We should rejoice then and relish the knowledge of his defeat.\n\nWithout Alasan, the rest of these necromancers do not concern me. Not in the least. But what of the Ansei Ward? Do you have it?

And you brought it to me? You honor me, hero. I pledge to you, for as long as I live, it will not fall into evil hands again. \n\nNow, only the final Ansei Ward remains. But with Uwafa and Alasan gone, who could have it?
Zur is fine. At least Zur thinks that is true. \n\nThis one feels strangely empty. This one is Zur again. But, thanks to my time with Gadris … this one is also different.

Zur wants very much to leave this place. Many bad memories. The door is nearby, it will open from this side. \n\nMeet us … me … outside. My abilities grow stronger already. This one can create a portal to somewhere safe once we are outside.
You know. Isn't it nice how the militia is going to give us their camp when they leave willingly?

I won't get caught up in your word games. I am as trapped as everyone else in this plane—including your friends, the mages.\n\nI just want to get out of here. I hold no resentment toward you. Let's make amends. Join me and we can win this game.
But they were happy! And they had something to believe in.\n\nCome now. Wouldn't you prefer to live a happy lie than to live every day in the misery that is truth? I perform a public service!

Call it what you will. I lost because I miscalculated your committment to your cause.\n\nBut your lust for power remains. Why fight to be a hero when you can fight for your true goal—power! All you have to do is join me.

Hardly. I haven't received this much adoration—well, ever! The sisters are even going to throw a celebration in my honor! Doesn't that sound exciting?\n\nI'll be at the banquet tables with <<1>>. Introduce yourself to <<2>> and <<3>>, then join me.

I'm not really sure. I must have wandered here after I was separated from my dear Lady Laurent, but I really don't remember.\n\nThat said, the sisters have been very good to me. They're attentive and they listen. And they seem to care about what I say.

When you stepped through our gates, you left behind the harsh confines of Coldharbour.\n\nNow you are our welcome guest. Enjoy yourself. Later, join us for the celebration in the manor house. For now, eat some food, relax in the baths, unwind.
My chefs change the menu daily, but I assure you the cuisine is to die for!\n\nThey always serve <<1>>, so you really must try it. It's my favorite.

That's an excellent idea! And you're welcome to join him. In fact, I insist.\n\nBefore you enter the pool, though, I suggest you wash in the basin. It has the purest water, warmed by the underground springs.

Stop shouting, Zur! What? Oh. Yes, of course. No, you're right.\n\nZur reminds me that you have been most helpful and we need to rest, anyway, so I decided not to cut you off with a snide retort. Please accept my apologies and ask your questions.

Well, I could make a strong case as to why I should be the one to survive. My qualifications, my experience, my worth to the Mages Guild. But the truth is, I have grown fond of Zur. My right to survive is no greater than his. \n\nI cannot advise you.

Based on our own experience, it appears that merging two souls into one vessel causes an internal storm as the souls vie for control. It takes all of our mental fortitude to maintain our individual personalities.

Then nature takes its course. But at least we will have tried to beat this. At least one of us has a chance to survive. And know that however this ends, I am grateful for the aid you have provided us.

Because I have withheld many of the facts. \n\nMagistrate Sulma is a Forebear, and this Withered Hand business has the Crowns here calling for King Fahara'jad to step down. She has enough worries with that. Security is my duty.

Sorry, stranger. I'm expecting a liaison from the Covenant military to visit and decide if our militia qualifies to join them.\n\nHowever, since <<1>> took charge I'm afraid there's little chance of that.

Because I know <<1>> from way back—we were in King Ramzi's service together. He was a good man then, and I have to believe there's still some good in him somewhere. \n\nMaybe it's just an old man's wishful thinking, but I'm not ready to fight him.

Ha! Noticed that, did you? Yes, the camp is divided between those still loyal to the militia and those loyal to <<1>> and his promises of easy living and gold. \n\nHis gang are little better than bandits. I suspect he's up to no good.
May the Divines put the odds in your favor. I hope you have a good shield arm, you'll probably need it.

After all the evidence from Fakimal's house, that's surprising. If she's not behind the disappearances, I can't imagine who is.\n\nTell me though, why am I in the stocks? There's no evidence aganst me.

You would just leave me here to rot in the desert sun? How can you do this when you know that I am innocent of any wrongdoing?\n\nYou had expressed a willingness to help me before. Something about this is very suspect. I hope I am wrong.
What in Oblivion does that mean? Did the Magistrate buy your silence, or do you really mean that she has a legitimate reason for this?\n\nWhat about me? Am I just to remain here in the stocks?

I cannot conceive of any explanation that would justify the disappearances, nor putting an innocent man in the stocks.\n\nI wish I could say I trusted your judgment, but at this point, I am convinced you are an enemy. Leave me alone.

The sneaky little cur! I only tried to get the wedding called off for their own good.\n\nCrowns and Forebears are too different. Remember my words—this marriage will not last. Someday they will realize that I was right!
Soon as enough of the other recruits have finished their training.

Many have said it before you. But you cannot hold a sword at this school until you learn the most important lesson: the one of history.\n\nSpeak to <<1>> and answer his riddles. He works at the forge. When he is satisfied, we shall talk again.

I was in Meridia's city the day she plunged it into Coldharbour. Like many, I was lost and alone in the wilderness. Then I found this manor.\n\nWhen the sisters discovered that I was a servant of Meridia, they decided to torment me for eternity.

I've been trying to become more of a help to Lady Laurent, so I've been taking dueling lessons. I think I can keep us safe until you return.\n\nFind my lady's missing jewels and meet us at the secret tunnel near the pools.
I don't know what you're talking about. \n\nI'm just waiting here to meet a friend. Yeah, that's right. A friend.
Oh, that's wonderful! Thank you so much!\n\nThe secret exit that Fatahala showed me is behind this rock. Give me a second to equip a weapon and we can head out.
<<1>> went up to the manor hand-in-hand with  <<2>>. I tried to warn him, but he ignored me.\n\nYou've got to save him!
It was the Khajiit. We failed them. Because, here, no one became the Mane after Akkhuz-ri.
<<1>>, <<2>>, and <<3>> rule here through the use of deception and illusion. You saw though the illusion, at least briefly.\n\nYou're different from Stibbons. You can save him!
Let's … let's continue on the Path. If the Bright Moons felt we needed to see the future of the Bosmer … perhaps we shall now see the future of the High Elves. Let's hope it is not as bleak.

The Blackroot clan warriors are even more bloodthirsty in death than they were in life, but there are also other spirits here—glimmers from the past—crying out for help.\n\nI think they're trying to show us something. We need to watch them.
You need to keep your wits about you. Stibbons has already accepted the illusion and slipped beyond reason.\n\nPay attention and you may save him yet.

I don't know. We'll have to search until we find it though.\n\nIn the meantime, however, do you recall the glimmers of the past we saw earlier? It seems those spirits are trapped here in the Shadow Wood. We should release them.

It's the shadow rifts that bind them here. From this side, you only need to touch the rifts to close them. That will release the spirits from their torment and weaken Naemon's grip on this place.\n\nIf you'll focus on that, I'll search for the Shade.
You want …. I've misheard you. I thought you said "leave." But we don't deserve rest. Not after what happened here. We belong to the Ooze.
My army is loyal even deep within death, deep within the Ooze. They will do as I ask, and if I am asked to march on Naemon, then that is what we will do.

No one does, officially. But Jurana and I get stuck with most of the planning, organizing, and poking people to help out around here. I guess that means we're in charge, until someone else is dumb enough to want the job.

Stick around and see. A day when I don't hear complaints from ten people is a good one. And everyone's always asking me for things to do. Sometimes, I just send people out on dangerous jobs hoping they never come back.
Well, Nelerien and I do. It's an honor to serve our town this way, helping organize everyone, planning for the future, and seeing all our hard work pay off. I love it!
Absolutely! We both love to talk with anyone who is willing to help out. Any day I haven't talked with at least ten people feels like a wasted day to me.

The one on the southern edge of town? It's called the Eye of the Greenmead. It was an ancient Imperial watch tower, built long before the town was here. Doesn't really fit with the rest of Vlastarus, does it?

It's a ruin inside. Two people fell through the wooden stairs last year. When Galla died from her fall, we sealed off the door. It hadn't been used as a watch tower for a hundred years or more. And the Empire's unlikely to complain.
You've learned what you must from me. Now it's time to test your mettle.\n\nSpeak to <<1>> at the dueling arena. And if you pass his test, you will meet with <<2>> for hers.

It is an ancient plant—a strangler. It's been here from the beginning. It's the lifeblood of the forest in this area. \n\nIf the Eldest is truly tainted, then regardless of the Green Pact, we must slay it.

When you awaken, take the armaments to the steps of the Blade, the tower crowning our school. Place each item at its altar and show your respect for the lessons you've learned.\n\nI will meet you atop the tower.

Of course. We've already sent in a small force. A distraction, as it were. While they keep the enemy occupied, you slip in and open the Labyrinth.\n\nAs you clear a path, Fighters Guild soldiers will fall in behind you to hold the line.

You need to be able to move fast. A large force would only draw attention to you and slow you down. Select one of our soldiers to take along, if you like, but more than that would be more of a hindrance than a help.\n\nI wish you luck in there.
Molag Bal is using tactics similar to what we faced in the Chasm. He's set up a portal to move his troops around quickly. As you head in to open the Labyrinth, we need you to close that portal.

King Dynar insists that the initial strike be fast and precise. He doesn't want the entire army getting in your way or causing Molag Bal to respond in kind.\n\nYou've proven yourself time and time again. We have faith that you can do this.

A quest? How marvelous! I shall march by your side into the darkest depths of foul iniquity, our weapons aloft and aglow with the fires of eternal righteousness!  \n\nYou honor me this day, my friend. I gladly accept this mission.
My sword is yours, my boon companion! Together, we will protect the beautiful realm of Coldharbour, and perhaps even save that ugly rathole you call home. Victory, thy name is Cadwell!

I've dreamed of this moment. Seriously. I always knew I'd end up fighting to save the world in Coldharbour.\n\nI mean, you were a beautiful warrior with flowing red hair and an ample … well, no offense. But otherwise, this is just like my dream.

I was hoping you'd say that! Whatever happens in there, we won't go down without a fight. Go let the old man know that we're ready to do what has to be done. \n\nAnd I really did dream about this, you know.

I'm as ready as I'm going to get. This just makes me so angry! Why in Mauloch's name would somebody want to steal an entire world? It makes no sense!\n\nNow look what you did. I'm just furious and I need something to hit.
That's what I wanted to hear! I figure, the closer I am to you, the more things I get to hit.\n\nLet's go crack some skulls and show them that nobody can steal our world!
We gave our word. We're ready to fight. You saved our Hist tree, and now we will add our strength to your forces. It will be a glorious battle!
As much as that mission would honor me, I must respectfully decline. I must lead my warriors in the battle to come.\n\nMay the Hist watch over us as we fight this night.
Nothing can ever be absolutely certain, but yes, we're with you. Nirn is as much our world as it is the rest of these people's. How can we do any less than they are?

I'm not very good with weapons. Hand me a sword and I'd probably wind up stabbing myself with it.\n\nInstead, I'll assist Gabrielle in any way I can. Once we get inside the inner sanctum, we'll be ready to help you face whatever's waiting in there.
You will need a scholar at some point, yes? A mental challenge to overcome or a hazardous puzzle to decipher? Perhaps Zur could help you then.

What? With a weapon or with claws, maybe? No, that is not Zur's speciality. Potions and alchemy, yes, but this one never mastered hurling fire.\n\nZur will join you once we get inside. If we get inside. Perhaps my talents will prove useful there.

I'm quite familiar with Daedric runes and the many hazards of Oblivion that you are likely to encounter along the way.\n\nIf you run into anything that falls under these categories, I can quite possibly provide some assistance.
I would expect no less.
Me? Really? I'd be honored.\n\nBut I think you'd be better served with a fighter type right now. I'm sure we'll meet up somewhere along the way, though. I won't let the people of Nirn down.
After you disable the reinforcement portal, I'll try to catch up with you before you enter the Labyrinth.\n\nWe'll stop this Planemeld together. We have to.
Yes! Swarms of beetles! They descended on this area like a plague! \n\nI had to pull all of my workers from the fields or watch them die.

If only things were that simple. You have your task to perform, and I have mine. While you close the reinforcement portal, I must oversee the rest of our forces.\n\nYou've made it this far. I have no reason to believe you won't succeed.
You've already done more than I'd expect from anyone here except for perhaps myself. \n\nReturn to me after you have made your selection.

I've spent my entire life getting ready for this, fighting in that damned forest. I want to be free and I'm willing to fight for it.\n\nAnd so will the rest of my clan. The Shadow Walkers aren't afraid.

Of course! Wouldn't have it any other way. It's going to be outstanding!\n\nWe'll strike from the shadows and help your army, but I'll make sure we're nearby when you need us. I mean, if that was what you were coming to ask me, that is.
We promised. You helped save our children. We shall help save yours.\n\nIf you decide my place is at your side, then that is where I shall be.
As you did for us, I shall do for you. \n\nLet the blood of your enemies flow down the rocks and feed the Egg Mother!
You've seen the Crown's power. It will turn the tide of this battle. That's a foregone conclusion!\n\nMy pirates are invincible. Even Molag Bal cannot kill death—and that's what we are now. Immortal!

A crew is not complete without its captain. They would be lost without me.\n\nSo, sadly, I must refuse. But have no fear. When the sky clears and the wind blows strong, my pirates and I will sail to your side. It will be glorious!

We're ready to give those Daedra the beatings they so richly deserve! Kyne only knows how long we were stuck in that tavern. We might be a little rusty, but we're strong and willing to fight.\n\nMy people will help. I promise you that.
It will be good to get some blood on our knuckles again. We've been lazy for too damn long.\n\nJust tell us where and when and leave the rest to me!
I gave you my oath and I honor such commitments.\n\nYou sampled my power at the Cliffs of Failure. Use the power of my thorns as you see fit.
Not without assistance. After we've killed it, you must remove its heart. We may be able to use that to grow a new strangler to take the Eldest's place.
Take this seed. Plant it in the body of any dead Dremora, as you did before. A zombie will rise to fight by your side.\n\nTogether, we will bring the Lord of Schemes' plans down around him.
My kind can slip through the shadows. We can go where you cannot and appear at a moment's notice.\n\nCall upon me when your need is great, and we will be there.
The Blood-Matron commands that we aid you, that we honor the deal as it was struck.\n\nAnd so shall it be.

That goes without saying, but King Dynar needs me with the main force during the initial assault. My portals are the best way to move our troops around.\n\nPerhaps once we clear the way to the Labyrinth I'll be able to join you.

What I think doesn't matter. What we do, however, will make all the difference.\n\nWe need to find the portal to the planar vortex. If we don't make it that far, nothing will stop Molag Bal from taking our world.

Not outside of breeding season, and that is still months away. \n\nThe beetles seem to be attracted to the johads, so I have been looking for someone to examine the johads for some explanation. Would you be willing to do this?
He gets it into his fool head every so often to lead these field excursions. Ayleid citadels, Daedric temples, you name the type of ruin, I've almost been killed there.
Oh, you know. Working as hard as I can to keep him alive. Making sure the new students don't hear about past expeditions. The usual.
One or two smaller outings. Nothing like this. I've been trying to keep him close to home in Skywatch. Once I even managed to get him to a lecture on time. That was a good day.
Then we're too late.

It seems the power of the Ansei Wards is somehow linked to the lives of the Ansei who created them. By learning about the Ansei, I hope to get an idea of where the Withered Hand may take the wards.\n\nNow, leave me to my work.

He sleeps beneath our monument to him, in the graveyard. Go after him before he has a chance to escape.\n\nThe other disciples … tell them what I've done. Whatever atonement they ask before I die, I will gladly do it.

The greatest Greenspeakers the world has ever seen. They were not satisfied with merely growing the odd village here or there. They wished to craft a perfect fusion of city and forest. One they could show the world!

Let's see … the other three sites are spread throughout Valenwood. Spring saw the city in the depths of Greenshade. Summer it set down roots in Malabal Tor. And from here, it would seek to winter in the Grahtwood.

No one knows. The city pulled up roots and began the trek to its next site … and simply never arrived. This happened some hundred and fifty to two hundred years ago. No one's seen it since. That's why we're here.

We have no choice, though it sounds as if we risk handing the Eldest's heart back over to the enemy.\n\nPerhaps though, we might also purge more of the blight while we are in this realm. That might help us both here and there.

Thank you for understanding. I do not wish to make this any harder, but I feel that compromising the Eldest's heart would be wrong.\n\nGo on then. Kill the corrupted tree spirits. I will search for Naemon's Servant.

He took it as a challenge. Look, he's a fantastically powerful wizard. These cultists aren't really a danger to him, the way they are to you and I. But he just refuses to come out of there, no matter how much I beg.

The Faithful could probably tell you more. But, as I understand it, a charismatic member has decided they can force the city to return. They're zealots, now. They won't let anyone into the pit. Telenger, of course ….
He guards the entrance to the inner Haven. Huge bastard with an equally huge warhammer.\n\nBut I'm sure you'll be fine.
Having second thoughts?\n\nWhat did you need?
I guess he's just not going to give up and go away. All right, I suppose I'll have to talk to you, then. At least you have an honest face. \n\nSo—as if I didn't know—what is it he wants?
I'm not looking for a bridegroom at all. Marriage? Malooc take it! I want to travel, see the world, have adventures. \n\nNo, you should be talking to my father, <<1>>. This was his idea, not mine.
If you understand your fate, walk down the steps, and I'll carry you swiftly to your destiny. Or, if you know no fear, burn this scroll, and I will bid you glimpse my nightmare.

The Chasm presents a formidable gauntlet of defenders and fortified installations. The first major obstacle is the portal that provides access to the Chasm's upper tier.\n\nWe have no chance of controlling that portal while the focus stones are active.
The Captain … is no longer the man I signed up with. He obliterates vessels he captures, after stripping them of wealth. None are left alive. Ever.\n\nWhere he's heading, I won't follow.
This island serves as Captain Blackheart's base of operations. \n\nHis ship, the Black Death, is anchored here between assaults on the sea.
We take control of the portal to the upper tier and push forward. We haven't been able to scout the higher region, but Cadwell claims that Molag Bal's daughter, Molag Grunda, commands the gatehouse.

According to the legends, yes. She's a Winged Twilight. Strong, disgusting, and in charge of a small army. This won't be easy.\n\nDarien says he's going to charm the wings right off her, but I'm not sure I like what he's insinuating.

We spotted Dremora down below. Nasty creatures!\n\nFrom the sophistication of the portals they're using, I expect they can also throw Xivilai, ogrims, and even Scamps at us. A pack of Scamps can take down a lone warrior surprisingly quickly.
Good. I don't think I could've tolerated another day up here. I'm afraid of heights you know.\n\nI trust the other hostages are being freed as well?
Fire away, though I would think you'd want to get out of this place as quickly as possible.
Alas, I never dreamt I would say it, but I swear eternal loyalty to King Fahara'jad. \n\nWe must cease this Crown against Forebear business. We must be united against the Imperials!
Ah, Thoda. I know him well. That's very encouraging. \n\nI've been listening to their strategies. I can give the general some good insights into how to plan the attack.
Then we must move with haste. The Imperials are using a secret passage to enter the city.\n\nIf we can collapse the passage, we can stop them from sending reinforcements.

Thank you, and thank you again for releasing us from his grasp. To be pulled back from the rest of death and bound like this, forced to serve such darkness … it was sheer torture.\n\nThough we are dead, the people of Vullain are in your debt.

Yes. I suppose there is. I can give you a shield that will protect you from harm while you remain in the Shadow Wood.\n\nTake it, and my blessing. May Y'ffre watch over you in this realm and back in the realm of the living.
<You watch the scroll burn away.>
Such a caring girl, worried about her old teacher. No, no. No need to worry. I was in no real danger. The others, though. Dear me, I'm glad they're such good runners.
He's busy doing something somewhere. Come back later.

That is what <<1>> said as well. But I ask you: if <<2>> lives, will she become as the old master was? How can Leki suffer an abomination to exist, even if it is for the good of the school?\n\nThink on this before answering.
It is a wise action to look before taking a step. Speak to <<1>> and <<2>>.\n\nWhat is decided here … only one of them will be pleased.
That is what <<1>> said as well. But I ask you: if <<2>> dies, who will protect the school? Will the disciples be strong enough to take her place?\n\nThink on this before answering.
Oh, yes! And a good thing, too. I'm afraid Indring's people would have quite torn them apart. Luckily Lanende never liked Bosmer much anyway, but poor Kelurmend may never grow hair on his head again!
Stars above, no. After I taught the first few a lesson, the rest have been properly respectful. I put the camp back together and continued my work.

Good, then it's up to me. First, he needs to be strong or my daughter will make a fool of him. Respectful of his elders. And wealthy, of course.\n\nOh, and not too hard on the eyes. I don't want to get sick of looking at him.

Of course, of course! A good groom deserves a good dowry. I have some gold and silks from, ah, well-wishers. They're stored in the upper camp.\n\nGather the goods and take them to the entrance tunnel.
The rangers spoke of two other places that can use our help: Driladan Pass and Verrant Morass. \n\nTake your pick.
I'm coating the bottom and inside of this bowl so it can be used for making honeymead. If the honey gets stuck to the sides while the pot is hot, it can harden or burn. That'd ruin the mead.
Driladan Pass is all that remains. It has a larger force of the Vinedusks there and I heard Mane Akkhuz-ri and Lord Gharesh-ri have shown up as well to help. Hopefully it won't be as bad as Vullain.
Verrant Morass is the last place that remains. I believe Girin is there. Reports of a strange corruption affecting the plants and wildlife has been reported.
With the Shades of Naemon defeated, all that remains now is Hectahame. That's where Naemon is gathering his undead host.
Very well. Come with me and I'll explain the exact details of your mission.

All right, I suppose I owe you that. I'm not a matchmaker, I'm a swindler, a confidence man. This is one of my classics. I tell the mark I'll arrange a marriage, they gather a dowry, I steal the dowry and disappear.\n\nNow get me out of here.
Damn. But it looks like everyone else got out.

Because I've reformed! Now I only target those who deserve it, like these idiot bandits. I'm only taking their ill-gotten gains. Serves them right.\n\nThe keys to unlock my shackles are in Wildur's tent. Get them? Please?
That's the biggest risk I've ever seen a soldier take. You deserve a medal.
Well, it's your choice. You may be able to find a tear between the planes before the link completely collapses. Good luck. You'll need it.

Haven't you done enough for us? I certainly think so.\n\nThere's a crystal up near the portal. The Dremora called it a Light of Meridia. You should take the crystal and get out of here before Molag Bal sends someone to replace Ifriz.

Believe me, I'm on my way. I just want to make sure that everyone who's capable has a clear path to the exit. \n\nSkordo went through, but he wanted to talk to you. I think you impressed that hard-headed ass. Find him after you use the portal.

When you touched the skull, there was a chance you'd fall under its spell. But I'm Breton—naturally resistant to some magics. It's probably how I broke free.\n\nI would have been there to help you if something went wrong! May I have the skull?

Everything, I think. I'm not so easily fooled as my father. I knew there was something wrong with that "matchmaker" from the start. Eventually I figured out his game.\n\nThe same way I figured you for a harmless dupe. You are, aren't you?
You cannot be … you're serious. Fine. There may be a planar tear before the portal collapses. \n\nYou better come back.

I think you should catch up with them. Follow the trail of fire.\n\nAranias must choose to accept the responsibility of her own accord, but Andur will not understand. I expect he will oppose her and she will need your help to defeat him.

Only if I get to go with you!\n\n<<1>>'s plan was brilliant. A bit flawed, but brilliant. He probably would have gotten away with it if I hadn't tipped off my father. He lives the life I want, traveling the world and having exciting adventures!

Sorry, I haven't got them. But I could get them, if you can distract my father and the Ungodly for a few minutes.\n\nMy father and his bruisers are at the upper sparring ring, through the far tunnel. Why don't you go challenge him to a fight?

Yes. There's a crystal up near the portal. Eilram said it may be important or valuable, else why was it hidden up here.\n\nYou should take the crystal and get out of here before Molag Bal sends someone to replace Ifriz.

My main concern is the Fighters Guild. We did try to talk to some of the others, but they've been here too long. Even some of our people haven't recovered from the effects of this place.\n\nBut the way out is open now, if they come to their senses.

I can't believe I behaved the way I did. I was sure that Eilram had murdered someone I knew. And it was all in my head. \n\nI know the helm seemed silly, but it helped to have something familar back. My mother gave me that helm after my first kill.

Then welcome! I think you'll fit right in. Once you prove yourself, of course.\n\nAll you have to do is go into this cave. The one full of bloodthirsty spiders. If you can handle that, come see me at the tavern in Daggerfall and we'll make it official.

I can't be strutting around the city wearing my Imperial regalia, can I?\n\nYour concern about my fashion sense is touching, but irrelevant. I've called you here for a reason. If we are to determine a course of action, we need more information.

We'll need to get the keystones, welkynd stones I imagine. And the Shade has likely scattered them throughout the branches of Hectahame.\n\nThere is more too. I will need to study these pedestals to decipher the way of unsealing the door.

Not yet. I do not wish to cause panic in the city, nor do I wish to incur the wrath of the king if it can be avoided.\n\nHowever, if you are not able to discover the cause of this plague, I will have no choice.
By now it should be clear your prophet emperor brought these catastrophic events upon us. Everything that transpired is his fault.
In the chaos following the Soulburst, Sahan stole the Amulet of Kings and fled the Imperial City. We're going to need that relic, and he is the only one who knows its current location.
Granted, Mannimarco can be very persuasive and charismatic when he wants to be. We all believed him when he said we could change Varen's bloodline with the Amulet of Kings.

You saved Varen's life when you rescued him in Coldharbour. In return, he lied to you about his true identity and his part in causing the Soulburst. He manipulated you from the very start.\n\nPerhaps the better question is, why don't you blame Varen?

Varen wants to assemble a new group of companions in the vein of the original five. Claims it fulfills a prophecy in those wretched scrolls of his. \n\nSuperstitious nonsense, but he is quite correct on one point: we need to find Sai Sahan.
He was captured by Mannimarco's agents and taken to an undisclosed location. We need to find out where he's being held.
Mannimarco keeps his most secret documents in a hidden lair of Daedric cultists deep within the Grahtwood, in the ruins of Wormroot Depths. We must travel there and search for clues.

All things have a winter. Mine approaches regardless of the one you name Andur.\n\nYet great harm may still befall, if Andur reaches my throne and strikes me down, or if Aranias does not live to fulfill her purpose.

The temples are holy places, created as housing for the scrolls, to honor and protect them. We built them upon the soil of Cyrodiil, close enough to the battlefields to bestow their blessings upon our troops.

Yes, well, I'm in a bind. I'm considering potential grooms for <<1>>, but she refuses to talk to me. I have to know what she wants in a husband, or <<2>>, who hired me, won't gather the dowry.\n\nSo I need you to talk to her.

Justice is done. Thank you for your part in this. \n\nI am ready to go to the Far Shores even now. Take my ring and the gems to Darius. I know he will see this through, and with that knowledge, I can rest.

Eager. Great! Once you learn what <<1>> wants in a groom, talk to her father, <<2>>. Tell him it's time to get the dowry where the grooms can inspect it, to see how serious we are.\n\nNow, go. And be persuasive!
I am. Do what you came here to do. Goodbye.
The mountain behind me is my throne.

There are four: Lord Zagari, Magistrate Govan, Shamone al-Sentinel, and Lady Moyaltha. I'll mark your map where they're being held. \n\nThe flea-bitten Imperials have blocked many of the ground level doors, so I suggest taking the bridges.

Don't know exactly. Our spies in Cyrodiil knew nothing about it.\n\nI suspect they've been in league all along though. Probably some necromancer treaty they all signed in blood or something. Either way, my blade doesn't discriminate.

That's what I want to know! We would've heard if Imperial ships landed on the northern coast.\n\nIf you learn anything in the city, let me know. Wherever the Imperials came from, we need to make sure there aren't any more coming.

They've gone from bad to worse. Fahara'jad can't even go out in public without getting heckled.\n\nCrazy as it sounds, the damn Crowns have people believing that if the king steps down, the Withered Hand problem will just go away.

I don't think they will. The Imperials think strategically. They took the hostages to protect themselves, and they don't want to give that up.\n\nIf they do kill them, well then, that just means we can go ahead and attack.
Looking for Swordmaster credentials, yeah? Sure, why not?

Generally speaking, I'm sure they are, but I'm more concerned about the Withered Hand.\n\nThose evil bastards won't rest until they've killed every last one of us. We can't fight the Imperials if we're all dead.

Nothing. I have things under control. We've got a reliable group to protect the town until we're self-sufficient again.\n\nAnd please don't say anything to <<1>>. She can get … upset when the end of her tenure is brought up.

<<1>> doesn't like competition, and I'm certainly not going to endanger our business arrangement.\n\nIf I were you I would keep my stay here brief. Now if that's all, I'm sure you can see yourself out.

Yes. He's bound by the Unwritten Laws of the Ungodly. My father can't refuse a challenge and keep his position as the boss.\n\nJust … don't kill him, all right? He may be an ox's arse, but he's still my father.
Thank you. I'll grab the keys and free <<1>> while you distract the camp.\n\nMeet me outside our entrance tunnel after you've challenged my father. I am quite sure you'll survive.
What? These birds aren't aggressive! I've had horses do more damage to me than any harpy.\n\nAnd I've had more trouble with these mercenaries than I've ever had with either steed or bird.

You would be too if you heard those … beasts! The screeching, pecking, clawing beasts!\n\nThis one had hoped the mercenaries would take care of our bird-woman problem. But, no! Now <<1>> has two problems!
Only after they've sucked you dry! I refused to pay their protection fee, and the next day my house was ransacked!\n\nI'll keep my own watch for harpies coming near from now on.
I saw them steal four sacks of good grain from <<1>>, a Khajiit merchant. And in the magistrate's name, mind you!
Oh, yes. They help themselves to my gold and my goods! And sometimes, they help against the harpies.\n\nSo, I wait here. Sooner or later, one of <<1>>'s problems will go away.
Sep's entertainment, I can only guess. It's not like one can ask a beast why it acts so. It is simply its nature.
Word's definitely gotten out that they were stolen, and that just makes people more nervous.\n\nI'd say recovering the Wards is our only hope.
I heard. Throne Keeper Farvad believes that you are Tu'whacca's chosen champion.\n\nIf that's the case, I'd urge both you and Tu'whacca to get busy recovering the other two Wards.
I heard. Prince Azah's singing your praises all across the desert.\n\nThe Prince might be headed here soon. I hope so, and I hope the two of you can find that last Ansei Ward.
So I hear. Someone just needs to get the word out to the people now. \nI suppose the king has a strategy though. If there's anyone who knows how to manage Fahara'jad's public image, it's Fahara'jad.
If I can endure Titanborn's inane prattle, I can survive your assuredly erudite elucidations. Proceed.

If the device works the way I expect, then the person operating it will decide which of our souls survives the reversal process and which is … discarded. I guess it will be up to you to choose who lives and who dies.

Well, if you must pry. I am Chancellor to the Elder Council and Overlord of Nibenay, but of all my titles, the greatest is my family name: Tharn. We are the greatest of the noble houses, with seats at the Imperial court for countless centuries.

Ah, there's the rub. With my … untimely defection? My family will likely be divested of its holdings. The name Tharn is probably being stricken from every document in the Imperial archives, as we speak.\n\nI detest being on the wrong side of history.

Politicians? A grossly inadequate word to describe our duties and our legacy. \n\nThe Tharns have a storied history of advising kings and emperors that can be traced back to the First Era. We understand the ebb and flow of power.

Clivia? She is comfortably lodged in Mannimarco's pocket, along with my nephew, Javad. I doubt they've given my disappearance a second thought.\n\nAh, fair Clivia. My charming girl grew to be a ruthlessly ambitious woman. I taught her well.

Don't sound so smug about it. This is a setback, nothing more. \n\nBy allying with you, I will liberate the Empire from Mannimarco's grip. The Empire is all that matters to me. I will do what I must to ensure its survival.
Husband of the treethane of Woodhearth, Fariel. As good a fighter and tracker as any Wood Elf I've known. Just shows how Pelidil caught even the best of us off-guard.
A respected noble from Summerset. She was on her way to Elden Root, to meet with the Thalmor. You might imagine the problems it would cause, if something happened to her.
Around here, they call him "The Fat Cat." Wealthiest merchant in Woodhearth, but don't think his influence is limited to the city. Money moves, you know.
I refuse to bargain with you. You might have beaten me fairly in combat, but I do not need to comply with any of your demands.
Bah! We usually win. There's nothing about our behavior if we lose.\n\nYou've made mortal enemies with the Ungodly. Leave our camp, if you can. But we will never back down.
No one's seen the sword, or had any luck amongst these ruins. A pity, really. I had such high hopes for some of them.

The Gold Coast mercenaries, our supposed saviors from the harpies, are our problem. They extort and steal from the good people here.\n\nAnd what's more, they've done nothing but make our harpy issues worse.

The mercenaries hid harpy eggs around Kozanset. Naturally, the harpies want the eggs back. That's the root of the town's harpy trouble. We must find and return their eggs so one problem's solved.\n\nBut first, follow me upstairs.

There are old smuggling tunnels that run beneath the mountains from Bangkorai to Satakalaam. \n\nI believe the entrance to one of these tunnels lies beneath Magnifico Khorshad's Manor. I believe he betrayed us to the Imperials.

Everyone else was killed or kept hostage, but I saw Magnifico Khorshad walking freely among the Imperials. You should search his manor at the northeast edge of the city. \n\nThat may put the Imperials on alert though, so free all the hostages first.
Here's a list of the tribe's leaders. I need to know why they refuse to speak with us. Unless my report says they're cooperating, my superiors have an excuse to exile them.

Of course, but please hurry. We're already taking losses and the bulk of the army hasn't even arrived yet.\n\nAnd I'm having a hard time keeping Cadwell and Darien from rushing into battle all by themselves.
The undead have no place in Alik'r. And yet, <<1>> has guided us prudently. Courageously.\n\nDo we throw away the basket with one broken reed? Or do we repair it?

Since your revelation, I've been in torment.\n\n<<1>> always put the school first. When provisions run low, she goes without. When new weapons arrive, she tests them herself, lest the students be hurt by imperfect blades.

Thank you for doing this. I'm sure not all of the eggs survived, but the least we can do is return them to the harpies.\n\nI don't have proof, but I know it was the mercenaries that did this. Who else could be so cruel?
Hold a moment. Someone's coming.

Now we know her true nature, we can be prepared for anything.\n\nThe masters teach us to recognize danger. She is dangerous, yes, but not such that we should cast her aside. We can help her, and she can still help us.
The mercenaries go in and out of the warehouse next to my home. There's got to be a reason.\n\nWhy don't you go there and find out what they're doing?
One of them will let slip what their game is. Hide somewhere and listen to their chatter.\n\nI'll take these eggs back to my house for now. We can go to the aerie later to put them back.

No! No, one such as she must die. For her lies, for her traitorous actions. She behaved without honor through these past months, hiding this shame from everyone.\n\nClemency is not for one such as her. And yet … I will miss her guidance.
Coming in? I do not have any insight on this.\n\nI have been contained here in the manor the whole time. I did not even witness the Imperials marching into the city.
My daughter was stolen away by the harpies! She and several other people from Kozanset. Their blood is on your hands!\n\n<<1>> told me about your meddling!
Not yet. They say they must prepare for another raid by the harpies before they send anyone out on the sands.\n\nIt's only right that you find my daughter, since you helped her get into this mess!
My dear master and friend was freed from Uldor, though the process wasn't easy. Undoing Uldor's bindings took time, but I learned much along the way.\n\nAnd, thankfully, Rurelion was restored.

My dear master dedicated his great intellect and energies toward finding a way to free me. The experience was … not something I care to dwell on. It made me a much stronger mage, though. \n\nI suppose there was value to living through the ordeal.

Perhaps I didn't think it through. I was hoping it would prevent random passersby from entering the portal. I suppose I should have disguised it as something less … intriguing. \n\nWell, live and learn. Since you're here, I could use some assistance.
This one feels sorry for you. You picked the wrong Khajiit. But, as the Bretons say, "The funeral will be yours."
Despite what you may have heard, a bucket of water to the face isn't a traditional Argonian greeting.\n\nBut I'm not one to stand on ceremony. What's on your mind?

By Dominion you mean <<1>>. She's like any Dark Elf matron, but her lash is an army of Thalmor lackeys.\n\nThe Wood Elves and Khajiit are the worst kind of slaves. They'll pave her road to victory with their own blood, and thank her for the privilege.
Yes, but please don't hurt me! \n\nI did. I-I permitted the Imperials to use the smuggling tunnel beneath the manor, but I regret it now. There's a hatch below. Take the key. Do whatever you wish.

There are barrels of kindlepitch down in the tunnel. If you place them near the supports and ignite them, that should collapse the tunnel.\n\nI am very sorry for what I have done. Perhaps … you could permit me to leave?

Ages ago in the time of the Ansei, a great warrior came to this oasis: Rada al-Saran. Rada was a proud man, and he claimed to match the gods in the way of the sword.\n\nIt is said Leki herself drew him here, seeking to challenge and humble him.
<The villager is in rough shape. It looks as if quite a few wild animals got to him before the end.>
<On second glance, it seems the villager was badly bruised, as if he'd been in a fistfight. His wrists also show signs of rope burns. It doesn't seem like harpies dragged this man away.>

Some. The mercenaries decided I was worth more dead than alive. They threw me out with a few others, beaten and bound. That's when the jackals came.\n\nThanks to the harpies, I didn't end up like the others.

Well, this one did, and she brought some of her friends. They chased away the jackals and brought me to shelter.\n\nWe must stop the mercenaries before any more innocents die, whether harpies or villagers.
Only the best party in Black Marsh! Quite possibly the only party in Black Marsh.
Let's see … currently I believe it's the 400th anniversary of Lord Sanguine's dog learning to play "undead." Or was that last week?\n\nWell, no matter. Any excuse for a party, am I right?
Ha-ha-ha-ha! Good one! \n\nWait, you're serious? The Daedric Prince, Lord Sanguine? Patron of debauchery and indulgence? This is his temple. As you might imagine, no one throws a better party!
<The harpy seems to be waiting for you to say something else.>

I know I'm ready to get moving. Sitting around and talking doesn't solve problems. That's what action is for! My sword is sharp and ready. I just need someone to make a decision already!\n\nBy the way, did you hear Molag Bal has a daughter?
I never pictured old Molag Bal as a loving parent. A twisted, sadistic parent, sure, but ….\n\nAnyway, she's called Molag Grunda. Sounds … intriguing. I wonder what she looks like?
What? That's ridiculous! Why would they want to abduct the very people I'm paying them to protect?
I will! Where is she?\n\nIs that her over there?
The shame is too great! I cannot bear to look upon it!\n\nI put it away. Now it is your burden. Let them hunt you and leave me alone! Take it, and be gone!
No! No … I loved her and she …. She would wish me to do what is right, even though time flows between us and will ever keep us apart.\n\nYou are right. The dishonor is mine alone.
Eventually, all who wield it must face the wrath of those bound to the sword. It is the curse of such a great dishonor.\n\nI beg you, take the sword away!

The Mane merely gestured and the earth shook beneath our feet. The ground split open and ruins thrust up from deep underground. Dark spirits, the children of Lorkhaj, boiled up from the depths. Dro-m'Athra.
Sharp claws on you! Yes! We need to destroy the spirit wells that have opened within our walls. Break their grasp on Grimwatch, cleanse the fort, and we can go find Khali.

The Saltwalker Militia was formed to train up and join the war on the Covenant's side, but a gang of bandits gradually joined up and then took over. \n\nWatch yourself, wayfarer: the bully-boys figure anyone who isn't with them is against them.

Ahh, yes. Our titles. Khali and Shazah are twins. Born under a unique alignment of the moons. It's all slightly embarassing, to be truthful. This is why we know Akkhuz-ri so well. And why they call us "Lunar Champions."
Then we'd have to "persuade" you to change your mind.

Very rarely, every so many years, Masser and Secunda align together and the third moon appears. This alignment of Bright moons with the Dark heralds the birth of the leader of the Khajiiti people: the Mane.

Those who dance with the Two Moons are bound by faith. They recognize who and what we are. Others can see it in us, as easily as a mother knows the scent of her child. So we are the "Lunar Champions." Made up titles to soften the sting.

No, no. That … is not how it works. There has only ever been one Mane. No two people have ever been born together from the same womb under the three moons. And Akkhuz-ri has always been fit, strong. That is why we have our titles.
New here, ain't you? \n\nThe boss, <<1>>, is in charge of the camp now, but he says to wait before we run out the real militia milk-drinkers. Says we need them for camouflage for a while.
I was once, but no more. My name is Varen Aquilarios.
Sea Vipers happened! One must've struck me on the head.\n\nWhen I woke, a Sea Viper was carving strange runes on my bodyguard's skin. I hit that awful pirate with a broken spar and we ran!
Didn't you hear her? She leapt crest-first from the cliffs of madness. The anger has burned a hole through her good sense.\n\nKilling <<1>> must be part of a larger plan.
No, we can still move. We'll head to <<1>>, if it's safe there.\n\nBy the Eight, it's inspiring to see Dominion soldiers. Maybe <<2>> can pull off her counterattack.

Because we're barely-trained militia, and they're all experienced fighters. We'd get slaughtered!\n\nBesides, <<1>>, who's in charge of the actual militia, told us not to. Maybe he has some other plan, I don't know.

In truth, I feared you'd kill me where I stood if you knew who I was. You certainly wouldn't have allied with us so readily. \n\nI caused this. All of this. If Molag Bal destroys this world, the blame will be mine, and mine alone.

You must not blame Lyris. She did as I instructed. She is my sworn protector, but she is also your ally.\n\nYou have my solemn promise, Vestige. When this is over, if you still judge me harshly, you can end my life. I will offer no resistance.

Right! A mortal making a decision! Free will and agency! Now then: does Valaste stay, become sane again, and live her life out here? Or! Does she go with me, and you receive the power of the Folium Discognitum? Which will it be?
I wanted to tell you the truth, but the Proph … Varen didn't think it was wise.\n\nI hope you can forgive us. Forgive me.
Varen will figure something out. Maybe Tharn can actually help us, but I still don't trust him. He'll knife us in the back first chance he gets, mark my words.
After Mannimarco betrayed us, Tharn went right on being his lap dog so that his daughter, Clivia, could remain on the throne. He's a traitorous pig. Bastard had it coming.

I guess not. Apologies, stranger. Ever since the bandits moved into our camp we've all been on edge. And I suspect they've been scaring away new volunteers. \n\nThere's bad trouble ahead, if you ask me.
He's the officer in charge of the real militia here. \n\nThose of us still loyal to the effort to join the Covenant answer to him, and not <<1>> and his thugs.
I'm in Coldharbour. I'm half expecting a wave of daedra to pop out any minute now. Friends are scattered all over the place, injured or worse. \n\nOther than that? Things are fine.
She's the leader of the Gold Coast mercenary troop. I hired them to make up for our shoddy defenses when the harpies attacked.\n\nThey get the job done, and that's about as much as I'll say.

We've never had incident with the harpies over the years. But now, it's completely different. Animals carried off, houses destroyed … they've gone into a rage.\n\nThere's no reasoning with beasts, so that leaves us but one recourse.

Death and attrition. The two greatest enemies.\n\nOur guards either fell to the Withered Hand or one of the other perils of being a guardsman. It's my responsibility to keep this town safe, so I looked to other sources.

Hah! I knew you wouldn't take the book. Could see it in your eyes. Oh well, can't blame Uncle Sheo for wanting to give his favorite niece a good home now.\n\nAs you wish, mortal. I'll undo what's been done to her.
Hah! I knew you'd take the book. Could see it in your eyes. Don't worry, Uncle Sheo will take good care of his favorite niece. It's been nice doing business with you, mortal.
I saw great serpents emerge from the waters. Those Sea Viper cowards made them snap at everyone in striking distance!
You can always ask. I may have the answers. Or I may not. \n\nWhat is it you wish to know?
No. When I saw my neighbors fall, I ran. What kind of Khajiit am I?\n\nYou're with the Dominion, yes? Your <<1>> plans to strike back. Give those pirate cowards a trouncing!
I'll do no such thing. If any of those Sea Vipers shows a face on this side of the gate, I'll claw it off myself.
The marine by the gate to <<1>> plans to strike back at the Sea Vipers. I'm sure she can tell you the details.\n\nWe'll get moving. Gods grant you strength!

Sadly, I do not know. The Imperials have stolen them and taken them I-know-not-where.\n\nPerhaps we must trust in the gods. If it is their will that the temple be restored, they will guide your steps.

They are the sacred tokens of this temple. All temples have relics to honor the gods, but these are specific to us. \n\nThey were dedicated centuries ago when the temple was built. They represent the aspects of the Redguard in mind, body, and spirit.

I … I would gladly trade places with any of them, and I tried. I begged the Imperials to take my life … but they left me.\n\nThey wanted me to stay here and suffer with the knowledge of my useless faith.

Dark moons, Shazah has no idea. Akkhuz-ri is … was a wise and gentle soul. He led our people with a deft claw, and always deferred to Gharesh-ri in political matters. This one grows cold at the thought of a future without him.

As calm as a land of volcanoes can be. Balreth troubles us no more. My people turn their attention back to everyday concerns.\n\nWhen the call went out, I decided to make the trek to this cold, dead realm. If we fail here, nowhere in Nirn will be safe.

Potions aren't the answer to every problem we face, my friend. The scale of this place and the scope of our effort means that we must fight our way through. \n\nI will do my best to protect those I can, but you must rely on your own devices.

Clearly Molag Bal created the Chasm to defend his sanctum. \n\nThe first tier is a rocky bridge that spans the nothingness below. The second tier, higher up, can only be accessed by a sealed portal. And finally, a fortified gatehouse. Most impressive!

The human kingdoms just to the north use that word. The Colovians are a loose federation, but they sometimes band together into a standing army at the behest of a charismatic general. As we saw here. Pah!
A dark reflection of the Khajiit. We're the children of Jode and Jone, so the old stories go. The 'mathra are the children of Lorkhaj. Grim spirits from the night between the stars.

My people, the Bosmer, and the Colovians have controlled many parts of the March over the years. Their leader, some lady general, has convinced her cohorts it's time to own the March again. They've taken Arenthia, and tried to take the watch.

As best Shazah can tell, they were trapped within the old ruins. How they got down there … she has read old stories of Khajiiti warriors going to war with the stars. Trapping them beneath the earth. Perhaps they referred to the Dro-m'Athra.
You feel that cold air rushing off the sea? Just like it was before the hurricane.\n\nWe can't wait to cut off the snake's head. We are the Dominion counterattack.

I sent my squad to scout <<1>>. If they haven't learned what the Sea Vipers plan, we can poke around until we figure out what needs chopping.\n\nAnd don't worry, your wizard friend can seal the gate behind us.
Blood. I saw the look on his face when he killed our old captain. He enjoyed it.

I have no choice! What Pariel did goes against the Green Pact. She made herself into a monster, and she can never change back.\n\nI cannot let her wander unchecked or slaughter others. I owe her that.
As any hunter would. Look for signs in the cave—a broken stalk here, trampled ground there. Anything to show recent passage.

Yes. The story is, the Bosmer received their form from Y'ffre. It symbolizes a break from our wild nature.\n\nPariel called upon the Master of the Hunt. She gave into her wild nature and slaughtered the Orcs. She did it to save me.
I don't know. The change was not instantaneous—it was wild, fast, brutal. The Wood Orcs were unrecognizable when she was done.\n\nBut she's my wife. I can't let her suffer.

The Sentinel Army, under old King Ramzi. He was an agent, part of what you call military intelligence. Lived in Tava's Blessing—had a family and little ones.\n\nOn a mission, he learned that some pirates were planning to raid Tava's.
Because if you're part of his loyal crew, you get treated right—the pick of the loot, and backup when you're in trouble.\n\nHe learned how to handle troops when he was in the army.

I—I do not know. How could such a place even exist? We must destroy it, we must end this blight and destroy this … this "Shadow Wood."\n\nWe must find the source of that voice—undoubtedly some servant of Naemon's Shade—and we must destroy it.

Thank you for understanding. I do not wish to make this any harder, but I feel that compromising the Eldest's heart would be wrong.\n\nGo on then. Kill the corrupted tree spirits. I will search for Naemon's Servant. Find me when you are done.
The entrance to the temple is below, in the rift formed when the Mane tore at the ground. Find Khali and see what you can do. Shazah will do what she can to aid the soldiers here before she follows.

Oh, we pirated for a while, but now with the war going on, all the navies are at sea and it's too dangerous. So <<1>> comes up with another scheme, and we comes ashore to work it. \n\nBut that's private, see? Only told you 'cause I like you. Keep mum.

That's right, mate. <<1>> had a grudge against this Captain Kroner. So he goes around and gets together a small gang of boys who are sharp with a blade and none too nice about it. We join the crew, he kills this Kroner, and we take over the ship.
My attempts to free <<1>> from <<Ac:2>> proved fruitless. I came to <<3>>, seeking texts on ancient Maormer sorcery.\n\nBut it should seem the Maormer brought sorcery to <<4>>.

The sword-singers were so disciplined, they could create a spirit sword. A sword made from their very thoughts!\n\nNot many could attain such strength of mind. Navid's sword is rare as it apparently persisted after his death.
I went to the Maormer embassy. I thought they might know a method to free <<1>> from <<Ac:2>>. Instead, I found them attacking <<3>>.\n\nI couldn't stand by and let that happen.
I'll hold the gate, if you think you'll have need for a wizard.\n\nOr you could bring a Dominion marine. Up to you.
Then let's fillet these Fish Elf bastards.
This is the sort of find that makes careers. \n\nSoon, I'll be an expert on one of the lost Dwemer cities. I can quit spellcrafting and lecture at the local Guild hall until I retire!
