Don't take too long. The sooner we hit the Sea Vipers, the sooner we stop their plans.
We cannot cleanse them, but if they are in this realm, we can strike them down. That will release the trees back in Valenwood.\n\nWe might even be able to use the Eldest's heart to help us.

I don't know. We'll have to search the forest … or its equivalent here. I wonder though—could we also purge more of the blight from here?\n\nThe source of the corruption came from the Eldest, but the trees' spirits are undoubtedly tainted as well.

Very well. I'm not sure this is the best course, but I am biased by my attachment to the Green. I trust your judgment.\n\nThe heart's energy will accompany you to destroy the corrupted tree spirits. Find me when you're done.

The heart's energy could help you slay the tree spirits … but I'm actually not sure that would be a good idea.\n\nIf we use the heart this way, it will be corrupted. It would destroy any chance of using it to grow a replacement for the Eldest.

I don't know, but I have to try something. As I suggested before, perhaps the only way to defeat the darkness … is to embrace it.\n\nI think I might be able to draw the corruption out of the Heart and into myself.
It'll be the end of me, I suppose. But the loss of one life … to save the Valenwood … there's no choice in that.

Just like a Bosmer! It is not enough for him to save us all, he must mock us with the nobility of his sacrifice. We will feel this loss more deeply than most.\n\nBut it looks like the dead prince is dead once again.

I haven't forgotten how to keep my allies on their feet, if that's what you're asking.\n\nMy time in the laboratory involved the practical application of magicka under hostile conditions. I don't fear the rush of battle.
Anything but egg mining. I've witnessed dozens and dozens slaughtered, I've fought feral Kwama, Dwemer machines, and mutant Netch.\n\nI think … I think egg mining is the worst profession in Tamriel.
Indeed. Queen Ayrenn should be informed. She entrusted you with this mission, so it would be best if you told—wait, did you feel that?
But … Uncle Sheo! He will keep me warm, and he will keep me safe, and I'll have so many friends to play with. Books are my friends, did you know?
We shouldn't tarry. Lead on, friend.
I urge you to think quickly. The Sea Vipers' magic will soon reach a threshold from which it cannot return.
I fell down, down into death, and the Green reached out picked me up and set me on my feet, and I was here again, alive.
Adept, if I stay … if I stay I don't know if … But perhaps, with him. I'll be happy.\n\nHappy like the butterflies! They flap, flap, flap their wings!
I have no idea how it works. It's a thing of legend.\n\nCould take our minds as easily as it did the miners'. Just find it. Destroy it.
Life for an Arch-Mage is measured in decades, not years. The rituals I performed extended my life, allowed me to continue my work … but eventually even I began to slow down.

Yes. I'd read all of the Accords of Madness. I knew the lessons of King Lyrandir, Leopold Arsenault, Darius Shano … and still I failed. Don't make the mistakes we did, adept. Reject this madman's offer.

I began work on a powerful artifact, a key to the inner workings of life itself. Glamoril … but that's neither here nor there. The point is I reached a critical juncture where even my knowledge and power failed me. I needed more.

You've already proven your courage. If I'm to die in this battle, I'd rather it be at your side than alone on this beach.\n\nBut we won't let it come to that. If you can hold the Sea Vipers' attention, I'll do what I can to keep you on your feet.
Then let's go. There'll be no more death at Maormer hands.
Think quickly. I can't tell what magics the Sea Vipers are brewing, but I know they can't be good for <<1>>.
Subdued … yes, I see. I'm sorry. Now, please, leave us.\n\nI left my pack at the mouth of the cave. Inside is all the gold I have—all yours.
This is the only way we can be together. I will pray to Hircine and hunt beside my wife for the rest of our days. \n\nNow please, leave us. This is between Hircine and myself.

I'm sorry. I was desperate for help. Desperate enough to color the truth.\n\nPariel did this, sacrificed herself, to save me. How can Y'ffre ask me to kill her? I love her! I can't slaughter her like a common wolf.
Thanks for understanding. After I change, Pariel and I will leave this cave and go deep into Valenwood. But you should go— I don't know that I'll be able to control myself during the transformation.
Don't use my wife's sacrifice to lecture me. Someday, you will love someone half as much as I love Pariel. Then you'll understand why I can't kill her.
Damn it all! Why me? Why is this burden on me?\n\nPariel, oh Pariel. I'm so, so sorry, but they're right. I'm so sorry.
I never imagined, when the last Silvenar died, that I would be chosen. But if the people wish it of me, I will accept this role.
Incredible. Indescribable. Transformed.\n\nI have seen my making and my unmaking, and I am awestruck.
This day has dull claws. We were ready for the Colovians. Shazah and Khali would have helped the Dominion troops break the siege. A new song would be sung in our honor. But the 'mathra. Bah!

Moons, yes. My sister's spent most of our life practicing her spellwork. I have trained. Blades and claws, that's how I spend my time. This one has marched with the First Auridon Marines and sparred with the Vinedusk Rangers.
Just in books for cubs. Honestly, I thought they were dreamed up so Shazah would have another way to bore me. She and the Moon Priests have gone on about the 'mathra since we got to the monastery.
Yes. Not very fond of them, honestly. Lost our parents in a Colovian raid. Was looking forward to slaking my blade on a few of those Divines-obsessed bastards.

Partially. The priests let us live with our mother and father for a time. We just had to do some studying, learning about "our place in Khajiiti culture." We moved to the Monastery when our parents passed away.
Hmm. I used to make the finest weapons in the land. Blades that every Nord was proud to own. Perfectly balanced, sharp, and beautiful to look upon.

Very well. I'm not sure this is the best course, but I am biased by my attachment to the Green. I trust your judgment.\n\nThe heart's energy will accompany you to destroy the corrupted tree spirits. Find me when you're done.

The heart's energy could help you slay the tree spirits … but I'm actually not sure that would be a good idea.\n\nIf we use the heart this way, it will be corrupted. It would destroy any chance of using it to grow a replacement for the Eldest.

That's not important to my research. With <<1>> and his rival dead, I expect someone else went on to have a dozen children with fair Sayeedeh.\n\nIsn't that how these stories go? The important thing is the sword.
I don't know. Rumor among the troops is that he's a highly placed agent of Queen Ayrenn herself. Whatever he's here to do, chances are it affects the whole of the Alliance.
I don't know. But if the rumors about him are true, it must be important. The Queen wouldn't send one of her top agents into the field if it didn't threaten the whole of the Alliance.
And he doesn't even remember that! \n\nThe same will happen to me. If I accept this responsibility and become Wilderqueen, I'll forget my home, my youth … everything.

I know, and I know the right thing to do. The only thing to do. \n\nI certainly can't return to the Summerset Isles, not after seeing this. This is what I was born to do. I must embrace the Valenwood as I would a lover, and we will become one.

It's war. How can we ever call any battle good or bad? Here, today, we'll lose troops to hold this old ruin. Why? Because my commanding officer told me to see it done. As if the Ancients care about what we do here today.

City to the East. Used to be Colovian, they pulled out years ago. My people and the Wood Elves moved in, made it their own. Whoever this general is … Lavinia, I think? She was keen to reclaim Colovian ground right away.

It used to be me that people turned to for help. When Hautt showed promise, I bought him a lute. When Hridi won a contest, I gave her dueling daggers.  \n\nNelhilda has gotten things rolling with your help. I want to help her, help my friends.

I never said that. I'm a Centurion in the Queen's own. Happy and proud to be an Eagle. I'm just saying that the men and women under my command are dying today to hold a ruin. Not for the glory of the Dominion, for a ruin.

Yes, the Ancients. The Ayleids. Their ruins dot Valenwood, all the way back to the coast. Whatever this place is, it must have been something special. Not many ruins left standing out into Elsweyr proper.

I got word from the scouts they were also making for Fort Grimwatch, to the west. Had to let them pass. And I think one of their cohorts went south towards Vinedusk. Moons luck to them down there. Those Bosmer are crazy.

They were careful. That many troops, sneak attack on an entire city? Their General's a tactician, mark my words. The Arenthia Guard fought bravely, from what I hear. Right now we have orders to contain them. Hopefully we'll retake the city soon.
Hah! Yes, Burri's mother would be very disappointed. Look, I've been a soldier for too long to care about how I talk. You want the proper cadence, go talk to a moon priest.
Hah! Yes, Burri's mother would be very disappointed. Look, I've been a soldier for too long to care about how I talk. You want the proper cadence, go talk to a moon priest.
As I said, I'm not a murderer by choice. And I want someone to know it.\n\nI appreciate your help with all this. Now go! Atarus is just up ahead.
No! Mordra hates spiders.\n\nHates. Spiders.
Blackheart looted two enchanted skulls from a Nord vessel. We need them.\n\nThe skulls empower him, and shield him from permanent death. To truly defeat him, we need to destroy those skulls.
I don't … I don't know. The Queen's agent, though. He knows. Razum-dar. Whatever's down there … it's a threat to the whole Alliance.
Juluda has no idea! Fascinating, yes? She believes the Queen's agent … Raz? Yes, Razum-dar. He will know. He is here for the good of the Alliance. Or so he said.

The ward is not the Colovian's. It is a defense of the Ayleids. It snapped on when the invaders stole a pair of welkynd stones from the entrance. Find the stones, return them, and you should be able to get inside.
Razum-dar. Find the Queen's agent, and help him recover this relic. As much as Juluda enjoys time in the field, we must end this battle.

The ward, the barrier. The Colovians didn't put it up. The Ancients put it in place. It only snapped on when the Colovians stole a pair of welkynd stones from that entrance. Find them, put them back. And you'll be able to get in.
Razum-dar. Find the Queen's agent, and get that relic. Don't make our wounds …  our lives wasted.
Get in there and help the Queen's agent. Find Razum-dar and this relic these bastards are after. Then we can all go home.

The Colovians are too stupid to make a ward that secure. It has to be an Ancient defense. They must have set it off when they stole those welkynd stones. Find the stones. Return them to the entrance. You'll be able to get inside.
I don't know. I read some of their correspondence, but I couldn't get a good sense. Look, find Razum-dar. The Queen's agent, he knows.
Why not tell you? There's nothing … nothing you can do to stop us. The Ayleids hid many things down here. But we came for the circlet. The Grand Circlet of Elven Authority.
The circlet's wearer … has complete domination over Elves. Every mer, every descendant of Aldmer blood must bend a knee to its wearer. We'll deliver it to Lavinia. She'll rule the world!

The Queen's agent, you mean. The Eye of the Queen. Yes, he's down here. We have him cornered. Trapped. He'll never leave these ruins alive. I'm going to go to Aetherius knowing my death is worth it … if the Queen's paw is lopped off.
I don't know. And I don't care. With that circlet on the General's head, your precious Ayrenn will be just another groveling Elven wretch. Ha ha ha!

You have to depress the triggers in the proper order. We found runes along this corridor saying it's a sequence of four triggers. Press the first to the left and then the last to the right. The other two … we could not find.

Well … the truth is that it is your choice. You could take the circlet and free us from this room. The rune on the wall behind you, the Tower. That should fire up the defenses and end our Colovian problem.

Razum-dar is first in the Eyes of the Queen. He has sworn his life to the service of Ayrenn Arana Aldmeri. To die in service to Her Majesty, it is what he prays for in the morning. Well … perhaps not prays for.
No, would that it were so. The runes were clear, the only way to destroy the circlet is here. In the defenses the Ancients put in place for just this purpose.
The defenses in the ruin overload and trap all of us in a collapsing avalanche of rock and dust. Do not worry … Raz and his men are prepared for what must happen.
No! The circlet is an abomination. It must be shattered, destroyed. Razum-dar's duty here is clear. The circlet cannot be allowed to leave the vault.
Then you are no slave, and I am no longer a knight.\n\nBut I discharged my oath in spirit, as in flesh. What knight can hope for such fortune? Meridia guide your hand true upon <<Ac:1>>.

Superlative. This haze must pass with the <<1>>. Then I shall locate a new liege lord whom to serve.\n\nAnd for <<Ac:2>>'s destruction, I bequeath amnesty for your inceptive theft and manumission from your service. Carry on!

I realize now that he's likely the Daedric Prince who offered me this deal. Or maybe his minion. Yes, that seems more likely.\n\nYou must believe me. I thought this was between him and me. I never meant to hurt my friends in order to save the Flagon.

Right to the point? How distressful! Oh, very well. You seek a way into the Citadel, one that won't attract any undue notice.\n\nAs it happens, I know just the thing. If you follow the east wall, you'll find a breach that leads inside.

They'll hate me if they find out I caused the curse. We've lost so much. I need to make amends, but what would the truth bring us except more pain?\n\nMy Nelhilda mourns for her beloved Gamirth. I need to find a way to help her.
Here you go. This should help you get around the city unnoticed while you're freeing the hostages. \n\nBe wary though, some of the Imperials may not be so easily fooled.
You are Razum-dar's friend. His comrade, another trusted soul in the Eyes of the Queen. Raz knows you will make the hard decision. You will do what must be done.

Hah! Raz trusts you not to do that. But more importantly, holding the circlet and using it are very different propositions. Without the proper incantations, the circlet is useless. Incantations Raz intends to see destroyed with Senalana.
You are a faithful member of the Alliance, yes? Raz trusts that you understand the danger here. The threat to the Queen. You will do what must be done here.
Sea Vipers carved runes in his chest. I grabbed him. <<1>> held them off.

I'm the magistrate's daughter, raised here, though now I am a traveling merchant.\n\nI came back when I heard of the town's troubles. My father insisted he had it under control. Now I'm doubly sure I returned at the right time.
Saw a lot of them near the docks. Try there.
Whoever wrote these notes has an idea. I'd start there.
Good.
Hunting Sea Vipers.\n\nIf you see her? Tell her <<1>> will be all right.

The fighters will draw the attention of the Dremora while you go to the upper city.\n\nFor the mages to utilize their guild hall's portal, you need to get it working. Find the four portal stones and activate them. Then the mages can join the fray.
<The marine's body is covered in wounds—sword slashes, broken bones, and even a few fang marks.>
<Her weapons are broken. Heavy scoring mars her armor. One limp hand holds a bloody bandage.>\n\n<You find nothing else.>
<Her weapons are broken. Heavy scoring mars her armor. One limp hand holds a bloody bandage.>\n\n<The other grips a bloodied piece of paper.>
I was in the caves … working … when I heard a strange howling. Then warriors came out of nowhere, and struck without mercy.

Sea Vipers—Maormer pirates! We paid protection through the month, and let them put those strange totems in our cave. They've never been in the skooma trade!\n\nErm. I meant moon-sugar. Hit my head, you see.

Some High Elf wizard tried to get in, so they collapsed it. I dove outside. Lucky me.\n\nThe wizard tried to tell me something, but I couldn't hear him at all. He stuffed this paper in my hands and walked off. Here, maybe you can make sense of it.
I told you, that High Elf wizard? Those Maormer feared him. Whoever he was, I wouldn't get on his bad side.

Our deaths, I suppose?\n\nAfter they killed enough of us, they left the rest of us alone—they knew we wouldn't fight back. They only paid attention to those totems. Well, until they collapsed the cave entrance.

The Mages Guild and the Fighters Guild will complete the conquest of the Citadel. But we need someone to storm the pyramid stronghold and deal with the leader of this installation, Valkynaz Seris.\n\nThat someone, my friend, is you.

What's that? My ears were ringing. Would you mind repeating the obvious?\n\nWait, wait … don't think me ungrateful. The wizard was looking for another way into the caves. I heard rumors of a secret door by the cliffs, but I never saw it myself.
Someone has to warn the pilgrims! And for some reason Indaenir won't let me enter. He's very particular about the forest. A little off, even for a Bosmer, if you ask me.
I don't know what you mean. Nothing's wrong. Nothing at all.
Study it, of course. Offensive spells, defensive barriers, utility magic. You saw the arcane threads she weaved as she fought us.\n\nAll of it is power for us to harness, now.
My, nothing gets past you, does it?\n\nThough I was born on your world, I grew up in Oblivion. It gives me a rather unique perspective that the Mages Guild often makes use of.
You seek the sword, is it not so? I must tell you—you are not the first to discover it. Others tried to take it and paid a heavy toll.

This one is as Shazah named him. I am Rid-Thar-ri'Datta, the first Mane. I have returned to watch over my people. The line of Manes is in danger, and this one felt his presence would help to light the path.
The Dro-m'Athra, Akkhuz-ri, the Champions … all are part of a whole. What lies ahead will require blood and steel and courage to overcome.
It brings me some unease to admit, but I think you're right. And I believe I know just what service she can offer. If you will, comrade, attend me at my side. We have some matters to discuss.
You're right, comrade. She murdered an innocent man. For that, she should be punished. If you will, comrade, attend me at my side. We have some matters to discuss.
We don't need any more bloodshed. If there's a way we can end this without fighting, we must.\n\nI have an idea. Find my father. Ask that harpy out there to get you to town. I'll be behind you.
I see. You'll be missed, <<1>>.\n\nBut this is no time to mourn. <<2>> grows impatient with our tribe. Perhaps if you were to calm the waters, she would leave us be?
Oh sure. Right as rain. Just idling around here on Molag Bal's doorstep!
Where are they?
Point taken. But I'm pretty sure Skordo assigned me to guard duty here on purpose. He thinks I'm a coward.\n\nI'm not a coward. I just don't like fighting. There's a difference!
Only a little? I must be hiding it pretty good then.  What was I thinking, joining the fighters guild? \n\nAnd who would guess we'd end up in the realm of a Daedric Prince? I wish I was home.
I don't see any hunters here now. Nor have I seen <<1>> or <<2>>. None of the guards saw anyone trying to head out of town, so where are they?

The giant lizards with lightning in their teeth are wamasu. <<1>> laid their eggs and nurtured them to hatching. Everything about her is twice their size.\n\nIt pains me to say, but you'll need to put her down when you kill <<2>>.
Talk to Beast Master 09
Certainly! Maybe if I beat you I can get a chance to fight in the arena. On your guard!
I told you that you'd need my help. A Daedric ritual locks this door, and only a willing offering of kyn blood will open it. \n\nI am your key to Valkynaz Seris. You are my key to vengeance.

Indeed! I suppose that's optimal.\n\nThese Sea Viper rituals are barbaric, but quite effective. The hurricane they summoned to dash our fleet against <<1>>? That's nothing compared to their current efforts.

Completely! Go ahead, don't be shy. It's not as though the Storm Totem's energies will cascade throughout your body until you're nothing but a lifeless, smoking husk.\n\nBut do avoid standing in the puddles, would you?
None of your business. You know what happens to folks who stick their noses into my affairs?
They end up dead. Dead and left out for animals to eat. You like that? Maybe I'll take an ear to remember you by. Sound good to you?
Hah! That one. Yes, Duzal-ja served the Elf. He came, he drank, he sang, and at the end of the night he couldn't pay his tab. Gave me a hunk of old quartz instead, he did. Why do you ask?

Shasirba makes the best meat pies in Rawl'kha. My regulars beg for them at evening meal. I have an order sitting at her cart, and haven't been able to get away. Fetch them back here and I'll give you your quartz.
You're a good one traveler. That Elf doesn't deserve such friends. But Duzal-ja thanks you. And here is your quartz.
Such respect! I'm not used to that, tending bar. Here, take your quartz. And tell that Elf he's lucky to have a friend like you.

Ha! You jest in calling this an "encampment," wayfarer. King Fahara'jad, Tall Papa's blessings be upon him, sent a small contingent of Daggerfall troops to oversee the town several weeks ago. We were not well received.

Yes, and he passed along your message. \n\nThough I'd much prefer to stay here, I will return to Master Zohreh in Bergama shortly …. I only wanted to share what I discovered with you and Prince Azah first.

My name is Shiri. I am apprenticed to Scholar Zohreh in Bergama. She sent me along to assist Prince Azah in tracking down the second Ansei Ward.\n\nI'd prefer to help you and the prince further, but Zohreh wants me back in Bergama.

I could spend hours telling you about the role the third Ward has played in history, but I would only put you to sleep.\n\nAll you need to know is that the Withered Hand has it, and HoonDing's Watch is the best place to start your search.
Don't you? \n\nYou've foiled their plans here and at Tu'whacca's Throne. You've defeated both Uwafa and Alasan …. I would imagine the Withered Hand is in considerable disarray.
Time is not on our side, but I will indulge you. Ask your questions.
Nothing recently. I imagine the country lasses miss me terribly while the bards continue to sing about Faolchu's defeat at our hands. Ha! That Faolchu was a bad puppy!

Yes, those were good times! And these times are pretty exciting, too. I just hope that when next we meet we're not someplace where everyone is trying to kill us.\n\nDid I tell you about Molag Grunda? I can't wait to see what she looks like!
Ah … no, I really shouldn't worry you.

Would that we could, O wayfarer. Unfortunately, our beloved King will never withdraw from Bergama. The Crowns must see a lion's strength on the throne if we expect them to continue bending their knees. I can only hope that my relief arrives soon.

They most certainly are not. We are denied shelter at the inn, given a dog's rations by the town provisioner, and face near constant ridicule. If not for some Forebear administrators we would have been run out on a cactus-saddled mule weeks ago.
I see. \n\nThat's terrible—but I don't see much left of the man I knew. And now he's demanding that I leave and take the other real militia with me, or die. We have no time left for wishful thinking.

I can't say for certain. It's one of two things, neither of which is good for anyone on this island. You don't stoop to blood sacrifice unless you need a lot of energy very quickly.\n\nAnd, well, to release it just as quickly.

Listen, you handle the <<m:1>>. I'll determine how to best counteract the Sea Viper blood ritual without destroying <<2>>. Does that seem equitable?\n\nThe only certainty is the lack of time. You should hurry.

He's left us no choice: we have to adopt his own methods, kill <<1>> and cut off the head of the snake. \n\nI wish I was certain I'll succeed. I'm not too old to lead, but single combat against a younger man?
Next? Oh, you mean the Wormies! Can't leave them here, digging up bones that dig up bones.
Here you go. Duzal-ja says he gets them for his customers, but he usually eats most of them himself. Make sure to tell him that Shasirba says hello!

No idea! That's why we'll need to investigate, yes? That's the thing for us, investigations all around!\n\nTheir biggest dig site is nearby. Hard to miss it, really! Unless you're one to miss a hole in the ground.
You're a good one. That Elf doesn't deserve such friends. But Duzal-ja thanks you. And here is your quartz.
Oh yes, Khuzi remembers him. Kind of cute, but not very bright. And yes, he gave Khuzi a claw necklace. Ugly, ugly, but she knew she could sell it.
Oh yes. Atrius the merchant, he's always looking for ugly little relics like that necklace. Khuzi thinks he is gone already. He said something about going south, making for Hadran's Caravan.

The ward key is decorated with arcane runes that can unbind the defenses and deactivate the wards. It should be near the guild hall.\n\nFind the key and deactivate the wards. Then the fighters can emerge from the hall and surprise the Dremora.

The wards are part of the defenses from an earlier era. They could be activated to protect guild halls in times of trouble. Once set, the only way in or out of the hall was through the secret passageways.\n\nYou need to find the ward key.
Then you should certainly seek her out. We could use whatever help is offered, no matter its source.\n\nJust be on your guard. A Dremora would never offer help without some sort of string attached.

Even the strongest armor has chinks that can be taken advantage of. Look for a place to climb or a break to crawl through.\n\nThe female Dremora offered to help us, but Galerion sent her away. If you run into her, see what she has to say.

Actually, yes. There's the Roost Mother. The hags tend the harpies, and the Roost Mother rallies the hags.\n\nShe wields great power, able to conjure flames and travel great distances with a blast of feathers and magic. But I'm sure you'll be fine.
Ha! I don't know how you think you've been operating, but you don't exactly keep a low profile. The Eyes of the Queen see everything, friend. We know all about you, and we like what we've seen.
I know you, but you don't know me. We have a mutual friend. Scrawny cat named Razum-dar?
I know. News travels fast in the intelligence game. Nice work up there.\n\nAnyway, Raz has nothing but good things to say about you. I'm glad to have you with me on this.
I know. News travels fast in the intelligence game. Ahem. Look, you did what you had to do. \n\nRaz had nothing but good things to say about you. I'm glad to have you with me on this.

He's well. I think he's working some kind of military deployment to the west. A ruin … Senalana? I think that's it.\n\nAnyway, he has nothing but good things to say about you. I'm glad I'll have you with me on this.
Then this is cause for celebration! Let us return to the shore and share the good news with Major Cirenwe.\n\nAre you ready to return?

Then you're a wandering soul, much like our tribe was? Without the gracious Wood Elves, we would still roam Tamriel in search of a new home.\n\nOnce the Dominion understand the depth to our gratitude, I'm certain they'll remove the barricades.

The creature can only hold so much energy before it discorporates. All the energy will wash over <<1>>, killing anything it touches. Except for the <<2>>s, of course.\n\nOh, and the mountain north of <<3>> will shatter, leaving no trace of the town.

You'll have no trouble. But in the event you do, I've opened a portal at a distance of one league from <<1>>. There, I'll tread water in the open sea until I've observed your success.\n\nMerely a precaution. I have every confidence!

Ah, and there's the genius of their plan! How do you bind a creature made of storm energies? With the wind itself!\n\nThree ritual horns trap <<A:1>>. But the lodestone now has enough storm energy to counteract the false winds. Elegant, yes?

It will shed its corporeal form and safely release its stored energy.\n\nBy "safely," I mean in relation to <<1>>. I recommend moving a fair distance away from <<A:2>> when this happens. Perhaps keeping solid rock between it and yourself.

I've no idea, but we need to restore goodwill with our flying neighbors. Even my father is in there to negotiate the mercenaries' departure.\n\nThey should be out soon. The villagers, I mean. They want to cast <<1>> from the town themselves.

I cannot! Do I not suffer enough? It has been centuries since I committed that heinous crime and the shame is no less potent! That sword is a reminder I cannot bear. Take it away! I may still find some small measure of peace.

Ah. How did this one miss it? Talking to torchbugs, healing the forest, seeing invisible Spriggans—I thought he was just another mad Bosmer! \n\nIt turns out, I was the mad one, and Indaenir was the Silvenar all along!
Raz has had his eyes on other things, or he would not have missed it.\n\nAnd Naemon. Raz assumes he's dead. Again.
Besides a timely resurrection? A wedding, of course. He will be joined to the Green Lady and together they will represent Valenwood as leaders of the Dominion, with Queen Ayrenn and myself.

Queen Ayrenn has already decided to blame Pelidil and the Heritance for this treachery. But Raz knows she loved her brother in her own High Elf, noble, emotionally stunted way.\n\nTell her, but gently.

Our little resistance. This isn't everyone, of course. We have a few more small groups spread throughout the city. But most of our citizens have no formal combat training. And most of the guard died in the fighting.

Certainly. Once you've found the documents Cari is looking for, she'll be able to choose a time and place to strike. You and she will knock him out, bundle him back here … and we'll get him to confess everything to his troops.
Without you and Cari? No. No chance. With her penchant for secret-gathering and your able assistance, I think we just may see this through. So I pray to the bright moons anyway.

I don't care if we have to parade that Colovian bastard around on a cart. We'll get him to tell the truth. His soldiers will desert at the news that they're under Daedric influence. And we'll get my city back!

It is well. The funeral rites and honors may proceed as originally planned. My brother was a pawn of the Veiled Heritance, you understand? The mistreatment of his royal body only makes their treason the worse.\n\nNow, what of the Staff of Magnus?
The Silvenar. By the Eight. \n\nMane Akkhuz-ri, is this true? If so, that changes a great deal.
Thank you. I will see to its safeguarding personally.
My younger brother. But he disappeared several years ago. We even hired a bounty hunter, Thaellin by name, to find him. No luck.\n\nDid you find him?

This was his lucky coin. He was always flipping it when he was nervous or bored. Drove me crazy. Thank you for returning it.\n\nIf you ever find Thaellin, take from her the fee she charged us. You earned it.

Our ultimate goal, the portal to the planar vortex, lies deep within Molag Bal's inner sanctum. We need to defeat the forces at the citadel before we can make our final push for the portal.\n\nTo accomplish this, we have planned a two-pronged attack.

It starts with a sneak attack launched from the Fighters Guild hall—after you find the key and deactivate the wards.\n\nThen the mages will attack from their guild hall, but I'll explain that part of the plan when you meet us at the Fighters Guild.
My daughter. She ran off last spring. I hired a bounty hunter to track her down, but I never heard anything.\n\nI'm glad she didn't have to see what's become of Bruma. Wait, why did you say "was"?
The Dominion capital is the Wood Elf city of <<1>>. The bulk of its armies are Wood Elf soldiers. I see no difference between the Dominion and our Wood Elf benefactors.
That ancient king is almost kyn-like in his demeanor. Delightful. \n\nHis idea is sound enough. Take the Citadel and you have easy access to Lord Bal.
What proof do you have? Maybe you've been sent by the Shadowed Path cultists to torment me!

This brush is hers. She always brushed her hair with it. She really is gone then; you're not lying. Now I know at least.\n\nIf you find Thaellin, the bounty hunter, try to collect what I paid her. She failed me.

I am here speaking to you. Our paths run parallel. For now. \n\nYou need to get inside the Citadel. I have made sure that you can. Follow the eastern wall, you will find a break. A single person could slip in that way, unnoticed.
Please, ask me anything.

I won an urn off of a Wood Elf last night in a game of cards. Turns out, the blasted thing is cursed! I was deciphering some runes on the base when strange little wisps started to float out of it. Now the wisps are carrying things back to the urn!

Are all mortals so tiresome with the constant questions?\n\nI seek something here. As do you. We do not seek the same things, but the paths run together. Your actions benefit me, without my having kyn blood on my hands.

You shouldn't. Under normal circumstances. \n\nI have my own reasons for wanting to see this citadel fall. Accept that I offer you some small aid, for my own reasons.I have no reason to kill you, as your goals are useful to me.

You must go. Rid-Thar has given you his touch of grace. Either Khali or I would be fine, here. As you've seen, I'm something of an accomplished spellcaster. And Khali has waved a sword around once or twice.

We left the province of usual a long time ago. But that Dremora's got something planned, that's for sure.\n\nIf I had to guess, I'd say it has something to do with vengeance. In my experience, it always has something to do with vengeance.
I'll be happy to part with it! Just get near one of the wisps, and point the crystal. The arcano-matrix I've imbued into it should trap them for you. Once you've collected them up, come on back.
My sister. Haven't spoken to her in years though. I hate that woman.

Well, I wouldn't trust her as far as I could throw her, but I don't think that has anything to do with us. At least not directly.\n\nMy gut says she won't stab us in the back. She's definitely a look-you-in-the-eyes kind of stabber. I can admire that.
You have proof? Don't get my hopes up for nothing here.
That ring is hers. I'd recognize it anywhere. I had it imprinted in my face often enough. That's good enough for me.\n\nThanks for the news!
Very well. I will remain and lead the defense. May your victory be swift and sweet.
Very well. Let's be done with this dark business.
She's my daughter. Please tell me you've heard from her! She's been gone for weeks. I haven't been able to sleep since she ran away.
The Eight keep you, it's yours! Don't know why anyone would want the damned thing. Or that other fob that silly Elf was playing with.
Because that is the only thing I drink, O curious one. We are an austere people, by and large.

Ha! The Ash'abah have many enemies—those who don't understand us, and so they fear us. And those who do understand us, and fear us even more. \n\nThat was not very forthcoming, was it? Very well. Necromancers would poison us. For them we slay.

Gavo is doing us a favor by delivering himself right to this tower. He's meeting someone. Someone he doesn't know.\n\nGet up inside the tower and watch for him coming from the gates. When he arrives, pretend you're Tharn's envoy.

Our mutual friend Mister Razum-dar has this … appreciation for disguise. He may have even shown you this earring he keeps around. It has a very simple illusion spell woven into it. No good for long-term missions, but perfect for quick infiltration.
Dead? No, you must be mistaken. She can't be … I'd have felt it. I even paid a bounty hunter to help find her.
This scarf. This scarf was Verana's. She was always getting cold. She's really gone then.\n\nI have nothing to give you. Thaellin took all I had, to find my daughter.
She said she was going to the northern shore of Lake Rumare, to look for Verana. If you find her, maybe she'll give you the coin I paid her.\n\nThank you again for bringing me Verana's scarf.

The tribe's leadership will soon meet to discuss this matter. Some fear the Dominion plan to enslave us, as the Dark Elves once did. I hope to put this absurdity to rest.\n\nYou're welcome to attend the meeting, wanderer. We have nothing to hide.

We were slaves to Dark Elves for generations. When the Ebonheart Pact formed, we refused to fight beside our former captors. They called us traitors and banished us from our lands.\n\nWe roamed Tamriel for years, and only stopped when we reached <<1>>.
We asked the Wood Elves here for temporary shelter. Instead, they gave us <<c:1>>! All they asked was that we work the land and set aside some of our fish.\n\nFor this, we must always be grateful.

In Black Marsh I was a tree-minder. I tended the Hist, the great trees of our people.\n\nHere I will become a spinner, to speak with the trees of <<1>>. I will lead my people to Y'ffre, the Wood Elf god of the forest.
A killer named Severus Tappo. I was hired by several families to find missing relatives. All evidence points to him, but I can't seem to find him.

We've always thought that without the Hist, there can be no hatchlings. But with Y'ffre's guidance, I will find a way.\n\nThink of it. Argonians native to <<1>>, to our new way of life. Proud citizens of the Dominion which <<2>> hopes to build.

The crystal you found will allow us to imprint whatever we desire onto their projections. We'll get Gavo to confess his connection to the Stonefire cult—and every Colovian in Arenthia will see it firsthand.
I can dispense with an archer or two, but I need this central point defended ….\n\nYou could ask Laeneval, our healer, or Elolir, one of our longbowmen, for help.
Yes! We'll marshal the resistance when you move out. The next time I pay homage to Jone and Jode, I plan to do so in a free Arenthia. Good luck, traveler. Good luck to us all.
Werewolves happened, traveler. Flea-ridden beasts came out of nowhere. Destroyed my cart, killed my men, and ran off with my goods. I'm only alive because I played dead.

I ask for honest, you give me reedish-, redic-, silly. Can't you see? The colors, the beauty. Look beyond the canvas to the … things beyond.\n\nBah, you are too much for it. It will never understand you. I think. What?

Everything! After the attack some of them turned back into Wood Elves and went searching through my pack. Said they were looking for a totemic necklace. That damned claw bauble that Khuzi sold me! Stupid cat! Never trust a smiling Khajiit.

I'll be fine. They got my leg here, but Rawl'kha isn't that far. I'll make it back on my own. This is it, though. I've survived my last caravan assault. I'm going to sell my stores and buy a nice quiet inn somewhere. I'm done!
I heard what you were thinking. You were thinking that you are drunk. I agree.\n\nNow go away.

I don't think so. We must consider the significance of the Green Pact as a whole. At its core, it's a covenant in which we protect the Green and the Green protects us.\n\nIn this case, we must cut off the limb to save the trunk. It's the only way.
Truly? Thank the Eight! My friend, without you, I would never have found out what was going on. Thank you. Alanya and I are deeply in your debt. Where is she?

I was beset by many troubles on the journey from Tava's Blessing—scorpions, dunerippers, and then, not far from here, I was ambushed by the Withered Hand.\n\nI managed to kill the dirty dogs, but not before they had hurt me pretty good.

I do not know, but it is all we have to go on. Scholar Zohreh was almost certain Shiri would have come here, but she suggested Satakalaam as her next guess.\n\nShiri was not close to her cousin, but Zohreh said she planned to visit Nahirah someday.
Yes, yes. I just need time to rest, to eat, and to properly bandage my wounds.\n\nFinding Shiri is too important though. I would have made myself go on, however slowly, if you were not here.

She needs to take that text she found in Tava's Blessing and bring it back to Zohreh in Bergama.\n\nIf you are willing, I would suggest you escort the girl there yourself. She seems to have a talent for getting lost.

Thanks to your efforts, life is returning to the city. Already, those you have rescued have found their way here.\n\nDo we have enough to start a war? Yes. But are our numbers strong enough to finish it? I'd suggest we're not there yet.

It is a delicate matter. I am unsure how to say this, but something is amiss. I need someone who can recognize signs of danger to help me.\n\nThe training is important, but so are the lives of our students, and they are somehow threatened.
A shadow. My own senses are overwhelmed by the signs, such that I can no longer see the direction from which the danger arises.\n\nYou can serve as my eyes and ears, with a clear head.

It is a delicate matter. I am unsure how to say this, but something is amiss. I need someone who can recognize signs of danger to help me.\n\nThe training is important, but so are the lives of our students, and they are somehow threatened.

You gave Ansei Maja's Ward into my care, and so I carried it with me for safekeeping. Throne Keeper Farvad was here, too, with Ansei Radan's Ward.\n\nI think Shiri planned it this way. She lured us here to get the wards back.
Thank you. Now, as any other student must, please speak with <<1>> at the forge.\n\nWe will speak again.
A shadow. My own senses are overwhelmed by the signs, such that I no longer see the direction from which the danger arises.\n\nYou can serve as my eyes and ears, with a clear head.

The Mane, he's here. Some of the quickblades reported seeing him appear in a ball of shadowstuff, and bending a knee to Lavinia. He's been corrupted somehow. Akkhuz-ri has always been a good and kind man.

I don't know. I've no idea what's wrong with him. But if he's in league with Daedric worshipers … dark moons. Let's deal with the Colovians, first. We have a plan for them. Then we'll deal with Akkhuz-ri.

Then you know of what I speak. I think it's the Stonefire cult. It must be. Lavinia is in league with them, they're behind this Colovian assault. Whatever is affecting Akkhuz-ri, it must stem from their dark magic.

Rumors have reached us of some kind of calamity at a fort to the west. The Grimwatch has long guarded the border between the March and Valenwood. The rumor is that Akkhuz-ri unleashed some kind of dark spirits on the place. Unthinkable.
Ah! She's sharp as a knife's edge, even when she seems otherwise occupied.\n\nI see the way you walk, and it tells me you know how to handle yourself against others.

Like Tafa, I have not seen anything with my own eyes. We are both unsettled, but the source is veiled. Perhaps it's the wind. Perhaps it's something more.\n\nWell, student, are you ready for this test? Only after this will <<1>> teach you.
It would be my pleasure. What's on your mind?
I concur. That would be a wise course of action.\n\nWhen you feel our forces are sufficient for the task, return to me.
Very well. If you feel that is the wisest course.\n\nMeet me in front of the cathedral when you are ready. We will begin making preparations immediately.

Marching against this enemy at less than full strength would not be advised. Of course, victory is never guaranteed, no matter what the odds.\n\nIf you feel differently, give the command. Otherwise, go back out and look for more allies to aid us.

I-I just don't know. Her brothers are dead and we have recovered two of the Ansei Wards … does she have the third? \n\nIs the Withered Hand now under her command? Was it all along? There are so many questions. I will need time—time we don't have.

How amusing! The little mortal suspects a trap.\n\nYou are wise to fear the duplicity of Dremora, but I assure you that you are safe enough. Illusions hide this area from the kyn. Just a little trick I recently picked up.

Technically, I am helping you, not them. But this constant desire to know the why of things grows tiresome.\n\nI don't want to confuse you. Just know that I have a debt to settle. As long as helping you advances my goal, I will continue to do so.

The look on your face! How precious! \n\nYou are dismayed. Why should this truth upset you? You benefit from my assistance, just as I benefit from yours. Patience, little mortal, you shall see. Now off with you. Nothing will come of us standing here.

Death, most likely. The kyn that guard this Citadel will try to kill you. It's generally what we do.\n\nThe old hall you seek is near the main gate. If I were you—and, most thankfully, I am not—I would make my way there, posthaste.
Balag can tell you as much, or as little, as you would like to know. This one is flexible.
Just another one of the damned Daedric cults that seem to be everywhere these days. This one is led by a particularly nasty bastard, and a Tharn to boot. Javad. Javad Tharn.

Lavinia is many things, but she's not stupid. She's actually a masterful tactician. She used the terrain to hide the movements of her cohorts until the last possible minute, and then struck the city at the first light of day.
I don't want to get into a lesson on that particularly twisted family tree, but he's Abnur Tharn's son. A corrupt seedling growing beneath the branches of that nasty piece of business.
The Queen's Eyes are everywhere, my friend. Lavinia's pageboy probably shouldn't have spoken to that tavern dancer quite so freely.

Zara tends the Swordmaster Division. She is crazy as a rat in a cheese shop, but a master of blades. \n\nSwordmaster combatants are skilled with the hacking and the slashing. Also the jabbing and the chopping. Sometimes there is the poking.

Tholbor runs the Summoners. His combatants conjure beasts and constructs to fight for them. This seems like cheating to Balag, but it is not for him to judge.  \n\nThe Summoner combatants use many tricks, so keep your eyes wide and your claws sharp.

Feluni is the big boss lady. Balag thinks the world of her. She is a mighty combatant and top-notch with the business dealings. And her fur? It is the sleekest.\n\nThis one confesses, he may have a little crush.
Pfft. Wizards. Balag does not trust them. Malarel is in charge. A combatant once talked back to her and all his fur fell off. \n\nThis was tragic for him. Humans have very little fur to begin with.
Ready to compete? Are you ready to face all manner of ferocious beasts and inhuman constructs? Are you ready to taste blood and bone?

That's what I want to hear!\n\nOkay, then. There are five rounds, each with a different combatant. The first three are qualifiers. Those take place in the Summoner Arena. The last two are in the main arena, if you make it that far. Got it?

We have only limited understanding of the history. Some time after the passing of the Ayleids, a necromancer or group of necromancers tried to raise an army of the dead. Necromantic wards were put in place, but now Naemon is suppressing them.

I think so. We've capped the source here. Without new spirits to replace their fallen comrades, we should have the Fort cleaned up in a matter of hours. Come on, let's make sure Shazah still has a tail.

Yes, I can already sense serenity return. We've capped the source here. Without new spirits to replace their fallen comrades, we should have the Fort cleaned soon. Let's get back to Khali. Make sure she hasn't destroyed any other priceless relics.

A smart investor keeps track of her investment. The fighters surprised the kyn and might even win the day. Bravo!\n\nBut once you control the Citadel, what then? How will you get past the Labyrinth without the proper key?

Even as a lich, I don't believe Naemon is powerful enough to disrupt the ancient wards. Elendarie believes it's the Staff of Magnus. \n\nWe must retrieve the staff and secure it for the Aldmeri Dominion.

Ill-informed, impulsive … mortals! Did you think you could just stroll up to the portal you seek?\n\nThe Valkynaz guards a key to the maze beneath Molag Bal's stronghold. You must pass through this Labyrinth, and to do that you need the key.
Patience, my lovely. First you must enter the qualifying rounds and defeat all three contenders. Only then will the main arena crowds be able to feast their eyes upon your dazzling smile.
Why, in the Swordmaster Arena, my lovely. Their blades cry out for your tender flesh. Defeat them and you will have your chance at the championship.
You have no idea what you're up against, do you?\n\nFine. If you want to throw your life away, far be it from me to dissuade you.

Enter the Sorcerer Arena to duel in three qualifying rounds. \n\nIf by some bizarre stroke of luck you survive, you'll proceed to the finals, where you'll have to face me. I'll be happy to kill you just for being an insufferable know-it-all.
You haven't heard? We're rebelling against the Imperials, trying to kick them out of Cheydinhal.

When the Empire collapsed, its army mostly disintegrated. But in some places, the local commander held his troops together. They had a death grip on Cheydinhal, stealing everything they could from us. Finally we fought back.

Badly. Every day there's another setback. We're no closer to defeating the Imperials than when the fighting started.\n\nIf you make it to Cheydinhal, seek out Sylvian and Vyctoria if you wish to aid our cause.

Donus wanted no part of the fighting. But Imperial soldiers went house-to-house, grabbing all the young men they found, forcing them to join their brigade. He fled before they reached our house, and he's been out here ever since.
I am most certainly.\n\nYou'll be the one doing all the tearing. I just meant I would patch you up when they tear you back.

Never look a gift daedroth in the maw, little mortal. I offer information, nothing more.\n\nThe warded building you seek is near the main gate. The kyn will try to stop you. If they don't succeed, we will speak again.

Oh, no. Kirandas and I want him to stay out of Cheydinhal until the Imperial soldiers are driven out. I'm just here to find him, make sure he's well, and bring him some sweetrolls. He loves his Mom's sweetrolls.
Let's see. I was given a quartz idol, a necklace, and an urn. Which do you want to know about?

It looks like it used to be some kind of Khajiiti ritual icon. It was carved from a large piece of quartz, but time's worn it down. I think it dates back to the time of Mane Jinninji-ri? I hope I'm right. That's the relic the barkeep has.
That one, at least, was easy. A claw necklace with Daedric runes? A holy relic of Hircine. One of the Bosmeri werewolf packs, if I had to guess. No idea how Telenger got ahold of it.
So, we're safe again? \n\nI've worked out a deal with Shatasha to rent the ruins to the Mages Guild for research. If this place is as big as she says it is, I'm set for years.

<<1>> sustains <<c:2>>. Thus has it always been, with every pair. I am not long for this world.\n\nI believe I'll find the Maormer's home island. Before my beloved pulls me back to the Green,  I'll drown them in a tide of Mara's tears.

Finish your original quest first. Help your mages. Banish these kyn to the darkness that spawned them. It is no less than they deserve.\n\nThen meet me at the pyramid. Only I can help you acquire the Labyrinth key.

We agreed that Tertius would make sure Donus is safe, then return to me. We'll try to survive until the soldiers are driven out.\n\nI hope Tertius finds him before the sweetrolls get stale. Donus hates stale sweetrolls.
I'm trying not to think about that, so please don't mention it again!\n\nTertius will find Donus and then he'll come back to me. That's what I have to believe.

Oh, who cares? My home is destroyed, my son is lost in the wilderness, and my husband is searching for him, probably lost himself. They might both die and I'll be here all alone.\n\nI just want this to be over!
I'll patch you up when the Daedra take chunks out of you.\n\nLet's hope you're better at taking than they are.
My head on a sharp stick. He's a violent, vindictive thug, and those are his good qualities. I got into debt to him, which is a bad place to be. Rather than pay up, I ran. Not far enough, apparently.

Oraneth was a Guild Mage once, many moons ago.\n\nShe believes the Altmer are superior to all races in the ways of magic and, therefore, worldly pursuits as well. I found her amusing, if only because her beliefs are objectively wrong.
Like I said, I think I have a little time. I'll scavenge what I can here, then run again. Not sure where, but I wouldn't tell you if I was. Just keep moving away from the Imperial City, I guess.

Well, not just fun and games. There's excitement and bloodshed, too. \n\nYour Dremora lady friend says she can open the door to the pyramid, but she requires Daedric blood or some such. I'm afraid I'm fresh out of it.
Damn.\n\nHow'd it happen?
Very well. I'm eager to reclaim our home.

She recently visited several Mages Guild chapters, asking for advanced texts on Conjuration, and a few about the Daedra. And now she's come here with fully-armed guards.\n\nNothing wrong with research, but she's up to something, yes?

The Canonreeve has been very vocal about wanting the Altmer to abdicate from the Aldmeri Dominion. \n\nWhen the Thalmor opposed her proposition at a public hearing, she swore she would save the Empire herself.
Death and misery are what's happening. What does it look like?
My part? My part is to keep as many of these fools alive as I can, so they can go get stabbed again. Sound like fun to you?
I can't. Even though I know they're doomed to die, I'll keep patching them up as best I can. If they're stupid enough to run back toward people who want to kill them, that's their problem.
What do you mean? You told him about our baby and he's not coming to get me?
Just so long as you don't warn Brielus or that witch. Now go away. I need to think.
That bastard! But it's not his fault, really. It's that witch of a wife. She's keeping him from me, I'm sure of it. If only she were dead. Maybe I'll go back and kill her. Then Brielus would be mine!
There are people killing each other all over town! Soldiers stabbing townfolk, buildings burning, rebels bashing soldiers, everyone mad all the time. It's no place to raise a child, let me tell you.
That is what Bakkhara intends to find out.\n\nThis one can feel an aura of magic in the air. Five-clawed magic.
Absolutely! And I'll be right by your side.\n\nAssuming that Dremora is telling the truth and really opens the way for us. She appears to want to help, but I don't entirely trust her.
Of course. He wanted to make sure I was safe. So he snuck me out of town in the middle of the night.\n\nThat's a silly question. What other reason might he have?
We will ensure he does not warn Lavinia. Don't worry, my friend. He'll be bundled onto a cart and smuggled out of the city. There's no reason to kill him. Gavo has played his part in this tale.

No-no! I am not all right! Not all right at all!\n\nI have failed Tu'whacca! First I lost Ansei Radan's Ward, and then to get it back, I was forced to strike down the honored dead! Now the Ward is corrupted, and so am I!
It's troubling that Laeneval fell. She was, in many ways, the strongest of us all. If you still need assistance, I would gladly lend my bow to ensure her death is not in vain.

Hey, it was the best thing for everyone! Well, it was the best thing for me, anyway. Jena would kill me if she found out.\n\nApphia's a tough girl, she can handle herself. I gave her a knife. And a good horse.

That I cannot do, little mortal. If the Valkynaz is banished by my hand, I will lose honor and standing.\n\nIf you kill him, however, I remain true to my word. And Seris abides in the darkness with my lost clan until Coldharbour allows him to return.
Yes, yes, I'm not proud of what I did. But I told her to go to Castle Alessia; she has relatives there. She's probably there already, safe and sound.\n\nNow go away, before Jena comes around.

Brielus can rot here for all I care. I met him when I came here, made the mistake of marrying him, and now I'm going to dump him like the trash he is. I know all about that tramp Apphia.\n\nMaybe I'll stab him on my way out of town. Serve him right.
What? How'd you know about that? It's an Unwritten Law!\n\nFine, then. Go ahead. Watching the boss kill you isn't as good as doing it myself, but it's close.

Since you delivered the note and didn't turn me in, I'm going to trust you. Belya was the best spy I'd ever seen. All the information we got about the Imperials at the start of the rebellion came from him.

I made him go. The Imperials were on to him. I saw them watching him, following him around. I convinced him to get out of town, beyond the soldiers' reach. Now that we've fought the Imperials to a standstill, we needed him again.
With Belya gone, we need someone spying on the Imperials. I'm not going to send anyone else to die over here, so I'm doing it.\n\nSo far, so good. But I feel eyes watching us. Go on your way, please.

Yes! Now every time I turn my back, more stuff appears. Will you help me out? I've enchanted a little crystal I think can capture the wisps, but I don't want anyone to see me. I think I'm in enough trouble as it is.

Very little, I'm afraid. They're a cult of evil mages, with thugs and cutthroats for guards. This particular circle, up at the old Juncus estate, specializes in fire-based magics. That they draw their power from Daedric stones makes me nervous.
That would be telling! Lord Sanguine guarantees a good time to those who drink. Would you like some?
Your loss, my friend. You don't know what you're missing!
Months ago. I don't know, really. The Juncus family always kept to itself, and the cult might have been killing everyone who came near for months until someone finally made it into town to warn us.

Ha! He likes to think so. But we're joint commanders; both need to agree to any big attacks. It works well in theory, but we get on each others' nerves a lot. Sometimes I'd like to stab him. Other times, I'd really like to stab him.
I'd like to, but Sylvian won't hear of it. He wants us to concentrate on driving the Imperials out of Cheydinhal, not on threats beyond the town walls.
Aye. You're right. She was a great guildmaster. But it's difficult to defend something as heinous as cold-blooded murder, no matter what the justification.
<The Argonian doesn't respond. He remains fast asleep.>
I know, Gavo's admission has me rattled too. We have to deal with what is in front of us. And right now we need to end Lavinia's grip on the city. Then we'll take care of the cult.
For the time being, Akkhuz-ri … the Mane is an unknown. Is he working with Tharn willingly? We don't know. And I don't want the devout Khajiit of the city in there jogging your elbow.

I can't be any clearer about this, my friend. The Mane is the spiritual leader of the Khajiit. He wields enormous influence. If he's been turned, or he's defected, he cannot be allowed to leave that district.
Everyone and everything! They're all crazy here, everyone but me. They never stop killing each other, throwing spells around, smashing buildings—it's madness, total chaos!

Who knows? Not me. I think they don't even know. They're too busy stabbing and hacking to wonder why they're doing it. They're all crazy. It makes no sense, it's nonsense!\n\nNow go away. Find your own place to hide.

For justice. When the Empire collapsed, the troops stationed here took over the town for their own gain. The townsfolk became their slaves, working solely to keep the troops fed, barely getting enough to live on themselves.

Donus Falto. When the Imperials forcibly enlisted him, he fled. His parents were devastated. His dad has been risking his life in the wilderness, trying to find Donus. That was the spark. The rest of us took up arms and started fighting back.

Well, there's not much to tell, is there? It's the same old pish-tosh. Gallant knight, epic quests, rescued maidens.\n\nI came to this land when my head was quite unceremoniously separated from my body. Bad luck that, but you make the best of things.

Oh, quite a long time. In fact, I wouldn't be a bit surprised if I was the oldest of the Soul Shriven. Of those who didn't go feral, that is. \n\nI know every tunnel and path, every nook and cranny. The others look up to me, I suppose.
They have to be. Look at this place.\n\nElden Hollow was the final resting place for generations of centaurs and minotaurs. Imagine the undead army one could raise here ….
Of course not. Even I am not so foolish as to enter Molag Bal's inner sanctum myself. Gabrielle and her mages will accompany you inside.

Oh, you'll know the source of our world's destruction when you see it. Just find a way through the Labyrinth. And try not to let the deadly traps and horrible monsters kill you.\n\nNow go. And good luck.

This one thought it was a tale. A story told to cubs. But then, he thought the same about the Dro-m'Athra. The Dark Mane was the leader of our people in ancient times, but fell. He was cast out of the Moon's light, to walk forever in darkness.

For us, it is never finished, but for you, your road leads elsewhere. \n\nYou have done for Alik'r far more than many others would have. You have fought bravely, sacrificed honorably; you have acted as an Ansei would have.
Your path is your own, but be assured, Tu'whacca has blessed you, and wherever you go, the gods will be with you.\n\nRemain steadfast, mortal, and may you come safely to your journey's end.
I only know that the darkness was not a result of necromancy, though I won't risk going back to investigate further.\n\nI will heed Bakkhara's last request. The Mages Guild must be warned.

For domination! This is a battle for control of Cheydinhal, winner take all. The Empire collapsed and their troops went rogue. They thought they owned this town, but we've shown them. We're going to win this war, no matter what it takes!
I did! I could take the degradation no longer and rallied the town to my banner. Latecomers like Vyctoria have tried to steal some of my glory, but this is my rebellion. I will lead us to victory!
You are as generous and kind as you are brave, my brother. I hope we walk the sands together again someday.\n\nUntil then, remember … true honor need not be named.
You are as generous and kind as you are brave, sister. I hope we walk the sands together again someday.\n\nUntil then, remember … true honor need not be named.

Dracien believes they are necromantic. That Oraneth is perhaps in line with the Worm Cult, who have been active in the area of late.\n\nThis one is still not sure. We will know more when we question the Canonreeve.
We are students, O wayfarer. Paying strict attention is a skill we are urged to cultivate early. Suffice it to say that I have seen and heard much.

The Blackroot clan warriors are even more bloodthirsty in death than they were in life, but there are also other spirits here—glimmers from the past—crying out for help.\n\nI think they're trying to show us something. We need to watch them.

Trust, as always. The alliance leaders will never agree to join forces, and if our guilds only work with one alliance, the other two will see it as a betrayal.\n\nFor both guilds, our neutrality is our strength. We can't afford to take sides.
You may be right. As long as Fadalia is gone, I will remain silent. But if she returns I will have to speak.
Bah - be on your way, wayfarer. I will do as I please.
Yes… Yes, I'm sorry. My lips are sealed tight as the grave. I'll … uhm …  just get back to training.
Why? Should the students not know the truth?
Throne Keeper Farvad and several of the prince's guards came here with us, but … most of them were killed when we were attacked.\n\nIt happened so fast … we should have been more prepared.

We were cleaning up at Tava's Blessing, putting down the risen dead that remained, but the prince learned that the Withered Hand had been seen here.\n\nWhen we entered the necropolis, they attacked immediately, and Shiri was leading them.

To raise an army, we assumed. Throne Keeper Farvad suspected something else though. He would not say exactly, but he seemed very concerned.\n\nPerhaps the prince understood what he was nervous about. Regardless, we need to find him quickly.

He came on his own. He said someone warned him about Shiri and that he was directed to come to Motalion Necropolis.\n\nOf course, he also said Tu'whacca was speaking to him, so I am not sure how much to believe.

Yes. Prince Azah said she was the sister to Uwafa and Alasan. He remembered her from when she was a little child.\n\nI was just shocked to see her … cursing us and casting her dark magics. She is the most evil person I have ever seen.
I have been hunting Ahtar—but you have already fulfilled our charter on that score. Discovering Fadalia's true nature was a stroke of fortune. All praise be to Tu'whacca.
Well, the only other merchant around is my wife, Vita. There's nothing wrong with her goods; she's the problem.

Big ones. We can't even share a bed any longer. Whoever makes the most money each day gets to sleep in the bed; the other has to sleep in a bedroll on the ground.\n\nI'm getting sick of sleeping on the ground, so buy up!

It is obvious to any with eyes to see. She fooled us all. \n\nApprenticing with Scholar Zohreh to learn about the Ansei Wards, coming with us to Tava's Blessing. She is wicked! Just like her father. She is the sibling we were warned about!

I do not know. And I have no idea as to what she has planned. If we get the Ansei Wards back, that should at least slow her down.\n\nShiri took Ansei Maja's Ward into the next chamber, where she performed some kind of ritual. I heard it from here.
Shame, walker. Be more careful. Here is another.
No matter. The risen dead stalk all corners of the Alik'r now. So dark are our days—no Ash'abah travels in vain. I will find new quarry soon. True honor need not be named.
You leave the task to me then? Your trust is well placed. It will be done quietly. The students will be none the wiser. True honor need not be named. Walk with Tu'whacca, my friend.
Your choice puzzled me, yes. I suspect that you wished to slay her yourself, is it not so?
That brewer's a low-life, cheating scum. You'd be better off drinking horse urine than his brews. If he weren't my husband, I'd have him run out of town.

Astonishing, isn't it? I could have done much better, but he got me sick on his abominable brew and I wasn't in my right mind when I agreed to marry him.\n\nWhoever sells the most each day gets to sleep on the bed that night, so what'll it be, friend?
Well, perhaps ….\n\nTu'whacca says now that you are here, there is a way. I must cleanse the Ward, but I will need you to protect me while I do. Would you do that for me, my friend?

The dead. That witch Shiri has set them against us. \n\nThey will try to stop me from cleansing the Ward, but if you will defend me, I can cleanse it. If you are ready, Tu'whacca says we should do this as soon as we can.

Cheydinhal is our home. Our children grew up in this house. I can't imagine living anywhere else. I have to hope that things will get better, that Sylvian and Vyctoria will finally defeat the Imperial soldiers.
Then we rebuild our lives and our homes. Though what hope do any of us have, really, with armies from all over Tamriel trampling Cyrodiil, destroying everything in their path?
Of course, who in their right mind wouldn't? Have you seen what this place looks like now? Can't you hear the fighting? Why would anyone want to stay?

Anyplace people aren't trying to kill me or bring my house down on my head. There's gotta be at least a few places like that left in this world. The tough part won't be fixing this cart though; it'll be convincing Junia to leave.
It's up ahead, in the heart of our Grove, defended by the leader of the Dagon Cell we've been battling.\n\nHe's called Razor Master Erthas.

She is planning to resurrect her father—the necromancer Suturah. \n\nI was much younger when this man tried to turn the Alik'r into a kingdom of undeath, but I will never forget the horror, the terror. We cannot allow Suturah to return.

I am not one inclined to inflict pain and suffering, but I am skilled in doing the opposite.\n\nTu'whacca says this will be a very hard battle, even for you. He says it would be my duty to keep you in the fight, to keep you healed.

To be honest, Shiri made me to appear a fool. The little waif who once nipped at her brothers' heels got the better of me. She defeated me.\n\nI'll fight alongside you for revenge, if nothing else. Besides, with you at me side, there is no risk.

As well-suited as I have been for the others. I am trained to fight necromancers and undead. My blades already know the soft spots in their makeup.\n\nIf you can distract her, I will cut that wench Shiri's throat before she can finish her incantation.
This is … troubling. Need I remind you that vampirism is a blasphemy in Tu'whacca's sight? The Ash'abah … you—you are sworn to slay these creatures.

You split the jackal's hairs. Those who carry the curse are dead—no less dead than the Ra-Netu. Were she buried, she would rise just the same. The fact that she speaks without drooling and walks without limping is a simple deception.
You are new to the tribe and have much to learn. I will stay my sword … for now. But know this—deception is a powerful tool in the hands of our enemy. Mercy is a virtue we can ill afford.
You are right to leave this in my hands. True honor need not be named.

I am not without conscience. I will speak to our elders to determine the truth of your claims. If they rule that vampires are not counted among the risen dead, I will stay my hand. If they disagree, her life is forfeit. True honor need not be named.
None. If anything she is more dangerous.
Find Merric and the council. They are probably still in their moot at the Sentinel guildhall. They need to know about this and they will heed your word. Aelif shall remain, and search for more clues.

You should also know how to repair walls, doors, and siege engines. Enemies will batter our castle walls and doors; we must undo this damage to hold onto our castles. Siege weapons can also be damaged; repair is often needed.
Yes. Vanus Galerion of the Mages Guild requested your presence. He should be here soon.

We kill her and we retrieve the last Ansei Ward.\n\nShiri has sealed the tomb though. Tu'whacca says two of us will have to channel the Wards we have to open the door. The other one can go in and join you in the fight. You must choose who will come.

He was the most powerful necromancer to ever walk these sands, worse than his children, I suspect.\n\nTu'whacca warns me … Suturah will be unstoppable if he is returned from the dead. He will be a great lich, or something even more terrible.

Certain communications must be made. Dangerous communications. This will ensure the safety of all. This one may have to delegate. Hmm. \n\nYes, of course. Cariel will do that. Ah. That was not so hard.
Of course. Which would you like to hear about?
Information is vital to winning this war. Each Scouting mission sends you to a target deep in enemy territory. If you can get there and look around, report back as soon as possible.
Bounty missions are simple: Kill enemy soldiers. If you kill enough of them, come back for a reward.
Which would you like to hear about?

Battle missions send groups of soldiers to capture valuable enemy resources, yes? The farm, lumbermill, and mine around each castle support its war efforts. If we capture those resources, that castle is greatly weakened.

Warfront missions are Atahba's favorites! These are major attacks to capture enemy castles; many brave warriors are needed. Taking castles from our enemies is the key to the Dominion controlling Cyrodiil.

What possible interest could that be to you, little mortal? Let me guess. You're worried that now I will order my kyn to destroy you. \n\nI assure you, a change in leadership can be a time of confusion. No harm will come to you or yours—for now.

Kyn do not die. Seris has been banished to the darkness. \n\nLong ago, our clans were locked in war. Seris, through treachery, banished my clan. Everyone but me. I accepted a blood oath to remain free, promising that my hand would never harm him.

My goal was revenge. I have no interest in your squabbles.\n\nUnderstand, little mortal. A kyn's desire to spill mortal blood never ebbs, even if we don't always act upon it. I am what I am. If we meet again, I will smile as I take your life.
I remained true to my oath. I helped you enter the pyramid. Nothing more. Indeed, the ignominy of a mortal sending Seris to the darkness was most gratifying.
As long as I can raise my guar and sleep in the shade, I don't care who rules this land. We want to live in peace, as a free people. If the Dominion supports us, then I support the Dominion.
I'd find somewhere else to sleep in the shade.\n\nSome of the rough skins in this village might not see it the same way. I wouldn't go throwing buckets of water on them. You might lose a finger.

I've roamed from one end of Tamriel to the other, handling vicious beasts along the way. In all that time, I've never lost a finger.\n\nBut the moment I call myself "Lost-No-Fingers," a guar will tear off my arm.

When my tribe left the Black Marsh, we brought along our native wildlife. None wanted the job so I took charge.\n\nI prefer beasts to people. More pragmatic, less complicated, and you always know when one plans to eat you.

No, I should be the one thanking you. It's about time these bloodthirsty warmongers look at the big picture. Since the war started, we in the Fighters Guild have been singlehandedly warding off the influence of Molag Bal. You as well, of course.
Absolutely. We've sent a full security detail to Stirk ahead of time to ensure the safety of the Alliance leaders. Vanus will open a portal now.

It doesn't. But when you're the one who keeps the wamasu calm, nobody gets on your bad side.\n\nHa! I had you. The tribe sees one who remains calm in the face of danger, and with this comes respect. Simple as that.
I speak with warriors, not spoiled eggs.

My friend, this could never have happened without you. Your strength at Arenthia. Your wisdom at Rawl'kha. Your bravery at Moonmont. And here … we saved the Jewel of Elsweyr! Dune is safe. Javad Tharn is dead, and I have walked the Path.
The end of one path, and the beginning of another. As you well know, the path never really ends. Here in Reaper's March I will restore the soul of the Khajiit and you … will travel on.
If I wanted you dead, I wouldn't ask.\n\nShow me what kind of warrior you are. If you survive a duel with one of my hunters, I'll answer your questions.
I hunt and I fish. I do it better than the rest. The others respect my strength.\n\nThis tribe has forgotten how to survive. You want to know my role? I remind them what we left behind.

No matter how far this tribe wanders, they will always bathe Elven boots with their tongues. Dark Elves, High Elves … a Nord with pointed ears would do.\n\nBut some of us fought our slavemasters. When they forget, I remind them.
Enough questions. <<1>> called a meeting to discuss the barricades. \n\nIf you're so eager to learn my thoughts, you should attend.
Your words are drenched in honey. How far do you stick your tongue up the beehive?\n\nVery well. Ask your questions.

We have prepared the temple for this … unique trial. Never in recorded history have there been two candidates for the position of Mane. You will walk with each Champion, meeting their guides and exploring their past.

Never. The Champions were born under a unique alignment of the stars and moons. All candidates are. But never, in all our history, have twins been born at the exact right time together. Eventually, after all, a decision will have to be made.

To prove worthy, a candidate must walk the trial path to its conclusion. Here in the March, that is the temple at Dune. Here Shazah or Khali will walk the final path: The Two Moons Path. We may speak more of that day later, Hallowed.
There cannot be two Manes. Eventually a decision will have to be made between Khali and Shazah. And as Moon Hallowed, you will be the one to make that decision.
The moon-sugar elixir is the gateway to the ritual. It allows you to open the doors of your mind, bask in the light of the moons. The touch of Jone and Jode will permeate your senses.

These caves were once a great burial mound, where all creatures of the Grahtwood came to die. But a thousand thousand moons have risen since then, and the roots have long overgrown it.\n\nWhat good could the Canonreeve do for the Altmer here?

Cities in Elsweyr, to the east of Dune. When Shazah and I were young, the Colovians annexed most of the northern part of the province. They thought our people were too weak from the Knahaten flu to fight back.

Mother was very well respected in our militia. She used to train the cubs from a young age in the use of claw and blade. Shazah used to sit and read after training, and we'd all take turns practicing tumbles and leaps. She was such a good teacher.

They're mercenaries, and the Canonreeve has paid for their services.\n\nThey act as an extension of her Thalmor guards, and I am not willing to have my mages attack a Canonreeve. There would be too many political implications.
A terrible disease. It took many people from the face of Tamriel. Actually how we lost our father … ahem.

The monks taught us that once we complete this Moons-blasted cleansing, we'll have to face some kind of challenge before we walk the final path. We should see hints as to where we must go before all this is over.

Khali is ready. Why, do you need more time to rest? If I know anything about these spirit journeys, we will most likely face that General as our final test. And I am eager to put my blade into his side.
Ifriz had information I needed. It ultimately led me here.\n\nI enjoyed what you did to Ifriz, little mortal. I'm looking forward to seeing what mayhem you stir up here.
Now we do what we do best—we fight!\n\nKing Dynar is upstairs. You should go and speak to him while we surprise the Dremora. They won't know what hit them!

I'm preparing myself to dazzle the enemy! I'll cut them to ribbons, I promise you. Just need a moment to buff the old breastplate. The enemy expects a certain amount of resplendance from a hero, and I shall not disappoint!

Oh, Dremora … something, something. You can ask him yourself, he's right upstairs. For a king, he mumbles a lot.\n\nLovely crown he's got, though. Rather dashing, isn't it? I wonder where I can get one of those.

As Galerion pointed out, the old guild hall portals are designed to move people and material quickly. More efficient and less draining than personal teleport spells. \n\nAnd, of course, they can arrive en masse. Just what we need to surround the enemy.
