Father was the most talented alchemist in all of Dune. When we were young, clients would come from as far away as High Rock to consult him. I think the Mane himself asked Father to tend the sick.

A disease, a mysterious illness, that swept across the face of Tamriel. It is said that it was a punishment from the Argonians, a retribution for the dark deeds done against their race by the Dark Elves. But no one knows for sure.
Your curiosity knows no bounds! Very well, ask away.
As far as I can tell, he's a trusted servant of Molag Bal. Not only does he command the forces of this Citadel, but he also has access to the Dark Lord himself.

Part of Molag Bal's stronghold. It's a maze of tunnels that lead to the Endless Stair.\n\nNo doubt the path is littered with traps and dangers, but we must push on. Cadwell tells us that the portal to the planar vortex awaits us at the Endless Stair.
Kargand? This one's brother? Why would he follow me to this place?\n\nIf he is trapped as I was, I will not leave him behind. This existence is one of nightmares.
Wonderful. They wait just behind you.\n\nDo not worry. The venom ensures there is little pain.
Wonderful. My children did enjoy their first taste of him.\n\nTake the Redguard to the alcove opposite us. And tell your friend to hold very still.
Then I shall not let you speak to her. It is simple.\n\nNow, will you stand about doing nothing, or take my trade?

You were indeed a fierce wind in battle against Oraneth, and your offer to help is appreciated. I am glad that, though we lost Bakkhara, we did not lose you. \n\nStill, I believe you are courting a dangerous beast by returning here.

Since <<1>> and her friends arrived, the harpies are angry with the town. They're usually nothing more than flying rats.\n\nThe harpies can attack, yes, but only when provoked. And I know the mercenaries are the ones who've provoked them.

Him? Ran off, no doubt! Who knows what he does, or where he hides after he's run amuck in the market.\n\nHe trades more than just grain, if you ask me. You won't be the only one looking for the furry-tailed wretch.

We have to stop this … we have to destroy this "Shadow Wood", whatever it takes.\n\nThere must be a focus here, something that ties this plane to ours … something …. It's the bow! The general's bow. That has to be it.

Yes, and we will have to confront it and take the bow back. That will release the general … and hopefully dispel this nightmare.\n\nThere's also the spirits from the glimmers of the past we saw earlier. They are trapped here and we must release them.

It's the shadow rifts that bind them here. From this side, you only need to touch the rifts to close them. That will release the spirits from their torment and weaken Naemon's grip on this place.\n\nIf you'll focus on that, I'll search for the Shade.

You saw the all-devouring darkness that burst from Oraneth's altar. It swallowed Dracien and Bakkhara whole.\n\nOur leader disagrees, but I know one does not return from magic like that. If you insist on going, you should speak to Kargand below.
I offer a nutritious snack that gives any lizard more energy for their upcoming race.\n\nIt's no guarantee, but it'll increase your chances of being a winner!
You could start with <<1>> in Sentinel, or <<2>> near Bergama. They've both sold racers.\n\nThey'll trade you for one of mine, too, if you ask nicely.
I'll feed it to your lizard before you go. It can get a little messy.\n\nThere, all done! He's bright-eyed and ready to run!

Ah, the most noble of desert creatures. In fact, I have a rare specimen, known around the continent for being the best racing lizard.\n\nOf course, I couldn't part with my <<1>> without some kind of compensation ….

Desperation turns enemies into allies. The villagers knew General Malgoth and the Blackroot clan were going to attack, and they knew they couldn't win.\n\nLikely, they asked the nereids for help, and the nereids convinced them this was the best course.

As barbaric as it seems, many clans still lived by the old traditions during the Bosmer tribal wars.\n\nMind you, they didn't consume the bodies of the dead because they enjoyed the taste. It was a matter of tradition.

For General Malgoth, that's apparently the case. For all his ambition, he was still a staunch traditionalist.\n\nIt's actually quite impressive that his sense of honor remains intact even so many years after his death.
A pleasure to do business with someone who recognizes a lizard's true worth.\n\nMay your lizard provide hours of joy to you, as Monkey does to me.
Are you, then? And you believe I have your lucky lizard?\n\nThat I may, that I may. I do have a rather speedy <<1>>. What will you give me for him?
Then here you are. Good luck to you.
Fair enough, friend. May your new lizard be as good for you as Monkey is for me!
An interesting specimen, yes? I'll do what I can with it. <<1>> knows a few tricks!\n\nHere you are. Good luck to you.

Yes, General Malgoth had traveled far and wide. He had seen the greatness that comes to those who conquer through military might. That you'd not heard of him is a tribute to the sacrifice of the Vullain Bosmer.

The Bosmer have always been free peoples, bound only to the Green. Rarely have the tribes united under singular leadership, although for a period many, like Malgoth, tried. Most of the so-called "wars" were not fought at all, but won by trickery.
Apparently so. Though the tactics they embraced sound more like a Nereid plot than something the villagers themselves might have come up with on their own.

I'd say this is a perverted case. The value that Malgoth placed on his bow alone may be enough for him to want it back. Or, he may be using the Right of Theft as a more honorable justification for his new servitude. There was fear in his voice.

<<1>> was once a Shadowscale, a holy assassin feared throughout Black Marsh. To sanction <<2>> as she did was a signal.\n\nHer hunters will lie in wait for whatever comes next. They'll fight to the death, so we need to fight harder.

The tiny guar sniffing at your ankle. Don't worry, it means he likes you.\n\nSweep the beach camps for <<1>>'s hunters. I'll round up a few trusted friends and check the forest camps. We'll meet at the old sea cave west of <<c:2>>.

If one Dominion soldier dies at the hands of these fools, my entire tribe will pay for it. So yes, we need to kill them, if it isn't too much trouble.\n\nBut have no fear. <<1>> can help you track them down.

Argonians born under the sign of the Shadow are special. Some are taken at birth and trained as assassins. We follow the god Sithis, and through his consort-wife we receive sanctioned kills.\n\nI shouldn't say "we." That life is long behind me.

<<1>> and I first came to this tribe as liberators. But for every Argonian we freed, the Dark Elves tortured ten. I refused to cause more pain for my people.\n\nWhen the tribe was exiled, I remained as a protector. But I was too slow to protect <<2>>.
I trained the little one to work with the hunters. He's quite familiar with their scent. If they're around, he'll be happy to lead you to them.\n\nThe hunters? Less happy.
She comes and goes as she pleases. This is a wild creature, after all. I do not even name her, for she isn't mine.
Once their eggs are back in their aeries, the harpies won't attack Kozanset.\n\nAnd then we can deal with those mercenaries.
Truth? I'm thinking of retiring. Time will tell, though.\n\nI suspect you'll be defending your crown for years to come. I can't let you do that alone, can I?
Don't feel bad! Could have been the sand's too hot, or too cold.\n\nIf you've done everything right, best just to try again.
Of course! You just need your lizard back ….\n\nAnd here he comes now. They can't resist that musk, I tell you! Good luck with your next race!
Not right now, sorry. This one isn't working and we don't have any others here. Once you get out on the battlefields, you'll get plenty of chances to use rams.

Of course. Malgoth sought to unite all the Bosmer under his leadership. He led the Blackroot clan to conquer much of Valenwood during the Bosmer tribal wars.\n\nThen one day, they just disappeared. No one knew what happened … until now.

Because it's in their nature. Death amuses them, and all the more when they can manipulate people into bringing about their own demise.\n\nAs distasteful as it may be, the Nereids are part of the natural order. I just try to stay away from them.
You'll find few collectors around Alik'r. It's just not the sport it used to be.\n\n<<1>> in Sentinel, and <<2>> in Bergama both sell a few good racers.
I believe they're keeping my daughter in a nearby camp. You have to help her!

No! Not at all. The creatures in these visions, I don't know … I don't. Wait, actually, it makes perfect sense. These visions are a part of me, as much as memories. I was terrified of plague victims. So … so many bodies.
I'm ready. I should warn you, though … we'll probably see more of those flu victim monsters in the next room. I was so frightened of them as a child. Get ready, and … thank you.
If you must ask, you may not be ready. But keep your head low and your movements slow, and you shall find the Senche's tracks.
Bernt gave me this lute when I was just a lad. It was lost for a very long time. \n\nBut it wasn't the only thing we misplaced in this dreadful realm.
Songs, stories … I have a lot of stories to tell. \n\nHave you heard about the Orc with the wooden leg? Or the Dark Elf with the heart of gold? I need to write these down.
Centuries ago. But the Hounds I speak of are not dogs. They are the finest hunters in Valenwood. I once led their ranks, but my hunt leaves no time for games.
Bring me the eggs. I'll wait for you by the town's well. Even though it's in the open, many people exchange goods there, so it won't look suspicious.
A mage's studies can sometimes require a bit of brute force, and that's where you come in.\n\nThe local Bosmer have not been entirely welcoming.

Not well, though they already accused me of having a weak bloodline, so their derision was more limited accusations of going native and the occasional off the cuff reference to bestiality than outright threats. Until now.

Within the lunar clergy there are many orders—the Order of the Crescent, the Brotherhood of the Fang. We keep the Claw safe here and train in our martial vows. If these brutes weren't aided by dark spirits, they would never have taken the site.
Transitus Shrines are the fastest way to travel among our castles and gates, unless the links between them are broken.
Indeed. The way is open to you and your Redguard friend.\n\nAnd if you desire to stay, I shall have no objections. Go in!
We tend the ancient sites occupied by the Falinesti. We protect the sites in the great tree's absence, and ensure the sites are ready for its return.
It's madness, I know. But she wouldn't just get lost. She's known this forest from her youth. And the Eight know there's enough Altmer who don't approve.
No one knows. Falinesti has vanished. Some speculate the Faithful failed in our duties, and the tree abandoned us, but not I. Not I. \n\nThe tree is coming back. One day, it must come back.
Falinesti. The walking city. It is a great elder tree on a scale you cannot imagine. It moves from site to site, taking the faithful with it.

You don't understand. In the past, the Wood Orcs respected the ancient sites. They never would have dared to profane one by settling there. Until now.\n\nWe wanted to remind them—but these Orcs don't care one wit about the ancient ways.

A long time ago, but the attackers did not live to tell of it. Used to be that all the Bosmer, not just the Faithful, would join to defend the holy sites.\n\nThe undead changed that. The undead are everywhere. There is no one left to expel the Orcs.
I'd not thought … anyone was left to help. Thank you.
Thonoras and Pariel are gone. The Wood Orcs took them away. I … I heard them screaming. I do not expect to see them again.\n\nI don't know. I'm sorry. I don't know.

Out? No. Not after what they did. These Wood Orcs violated this holy site. They spit on the old ways. They captured the Faithful—my brothers, my sisters—and they tortured us.\n\nThe Wood Orcs will pay in kind.
The Bosmer were tight-lipped, but I pieced together something about mourning kidnappings, listening to rumors around town. Please, help me find her.
With death. Death from the trees, death from the grass, death from the mist and water and rocks. These Wood Orcs may not fear death. They will fear me.
Killing the rank-and-file solves nothing. These Wood Orcs celebrate violence. The chieftain is careless with the lives of his warriors.\n\nNo, we must strike close to the Chieftain's hearth and home.
The Falinesti Faithful lost a tribeswoman, and as is the custom, they sought a captive in a Mourning War to replace the lost. \n\nI have a new life now, a new family, new duties.
The Warchief must not die until he has felt my pain, the pain of my Faithful. He will see his family murdered, one by one. He will rage and cry.\n\nOnly then will we grant him death.

Solve? You act like this is some kind of riddle to be puzzled out. The only way to stop this from happening again is to send a loud, unambiguous message—the kind even these Orc scum can't fail to understand.\n\nHelp me, or get out of my way.
One life for each of my faithful. Dushgor, his torturer. Roog, his son. Thushleg, his Hunt-Wife. Grashla, his Hearth-Wife. \n\nWhen all these are dead, I will permit Chief Gorzesh to die.
Then go. Find Egannor and claim your reward. Be sure to tell him about Halalin's mutilated corpse, and that you refused to help me avenge him.\n\nI will finish this myself.
Good. The son, Roog, waits for his father atop a watchtower. Grashla tends hearth in the large building in the center of the Orc fortress. Find them. Kill them. Bring both their heads back to me.
Outside town, on the hillside where they keep their aeries.\n\nFeeding our people to their young, no doubt! And you! You instigated this attack!

Hunt-Wife Thushleg led the party that captured us. Soon she will have my blade in her back. As for Dushgor, I have something special planned for him.\n\nHe thinks he knows how to make captives scream. I will teach him a few new tricks.
A castle's transitus link is broken if all of its resources—farm, mine, and lumbermill—are owned by the enemy, or if the castle is under attack and a section of wall or gate is heavily damaged.
He left on another hunt. When he returns, I plan to show him the heads we have gathered. Orcs aren't known for self-reflection, but I think he'll get the picture.

I have mine as well. We must send a clear message.\n\nGorzesh will return from his hunt soon. I have left him a note of sorts telling him where he can find his missing kin. It should lure him out of the fort.

There is a stone circle sacred to the Faithful not far from here. Go there, mount the heads, and touch the center stone.\n\nThis blood sacrifice will complete an ancient ritual to Y'ffre. Gorzesh will watch us commit his family to the Ooze.

It's a trial, to ensure I'm a fitting replacement for the lost tribeswoman. It's nothing for me to escape these bonds, but if I flee, they will capture another. \n\nBesides, I belong here, not in that city of stone. I love Laurosse, but I'm a Wood Elf.

These Bosmer are acting far too aggressively to not be protecting something. The spirit is here.\n\nIt may take some time to get the information we need from our prisoner. You should move on. Keep your eyes open for a forest spirit.

Then you understand. Sometimes blood runs deeper than anything. Sometimes things just aren't meant to be.\n\nTell Laurosse I'll miss his stupid pointy face and his awful, awful poetry. Tell him I'm sorry.
You sound like Laurosse. Always full of noble ideals. He's right, though. I've been afraid. I've been running from us.\n\nI'll go back to Marbruk. Maybe I'll see you there.

You asked me this before, silly. I don't know, but when I think about changing things around me, my thoughts come true.\n\nRemember when that merchant ship sank? I'd lifted the ground out of the ocean. I just forgot to lower it again.

<<1>>, <<2>>, and I were scavenging for a replacement <<z:3>> when the Sea Vipers ambushed us. They brought us to the island with the beached Dominion flagship.\n\nThey'd done things there, terrible things.

This one is called Rid-Thar-ri'Datta. He once had the honor to be the first Mane, the first to walk in the moonlight. He sensed the threat to the Claw. The Mane, the Claw, the moons … everything has its place on the path.
The Vinedusks are no army. Nothing compared of the undead massing below. And we're stretched thin. If you can help relieve some of our other rangers, we can better secure this area until help comes.

We're covering four locations right now: Hectahame and the wonderful moat of undead, Driladan Pass, Dread Vullain, and Verrant Morass. The Pass has the larger end of our force. I don't think anyone knew what was brewing here.

You didn't find any of the missing Orcs at the inn. There's a good chance that anyone who wasn't shipped to Northpoint yet is being held captive in the camp outside town.\n\nGet out there and rescue the townsfolk before it's too late.

It's an old fort that the Fell's Brigade uses as a practice ground. Leonce headed off in that direction while you were investigating the situation for me.\n\nRescue the Orcs, then take care of Leonce. There's only one way to deal with a traitor.

Those filthy Maormer dragged my mates up and tied them to these serpent-shaped statues. Then they started chanting, and lightning surrounded them!\n\nThat's when the storm began to form around the island.

The Maormer wore lodestones on their wrists. It let them ignore those lightning bonds. But I couldn't find any more, so I jumped off the ship and swam for it.\n\nPlease, don't let them sacrifice my crewmates!

Yes, I'm sure of it. It was a terrible sight. The Sea Vipers were so caught up in the ritual, I slipped free.\n\nI tried to grab <<1>>, but the lightning held him fast. Then one of the Sea Vipers yanked at him. I saw the Maormer's wrist glow.
What can I tell you that you don't already know? Vanus Galerion is the most famous, most powerful, most daringly courageous mage in the Mages Guild.\n\nHis legendary exploits are … well, legendary!
Why, so there is. And here I thought that bad smell was you.

The Stonefire have torn down several shrines to the Bright Moons. These shrines are the keys to entering the sanctum. But you, Hallowed … you have the blessings of Jone and Jode upon you. With a touch, you can reconstruct the shrines.

The trees in the forest—the taint came from the Eldest, but it has undoubtedly spread to the spirits of the trees themselves.\n\nIf we can slay the corrupted tree spirits, more of the forest may be spared. The Eldest's heart can help us.
Why, that's a question I think you should ask Trelon. Personally, I'd let it lie if I were you.\n\nHa! Let it lie. Get it?

Bruma's a funny town, full of desperate, angry, murderous people. Normally my sort of place. But folks there didn't like me working for both sides of the conflict. I got one last job from Trelon that took me out of town and I'm not going back.

There are reports of the Veiled Heritance raising the undead in the Pass. As I said, most of our forces are there, including Mane Akkhuz-ri and Lord Gharesh-ri. We love it when the big cats come out to play.

Dread Vullain! The haunted village! Oh, but don't let that turn you off. Something there is toying with the rest of General Malgoth's long dead Blackroot army. Long dead and cursed at that, so you can imagine how uneasy things are there.

Well, no one knows for sure, but some sort of corruption is wreaking havoc in the area. It's claiming the land, the wildlife, and even the Bosmer that are there. It's turned them feral. Not a pretty sight, but Y'ffre knows something has to be done.

You have already encountered the cult, and their dark thralls. The cult, in their ignorance, tear at the temple walls. They want to enter the inner sanctum, overcome the wards and claim the Claw. Fools.

The Stonefire have torn down several shrines to the Bright Moons. These shrines are the keys to entering the sanctum. But you have the blessings of Jone and Jode upon you. With a touch, you can reconstruct the shrines.
Just some differences of opinion. You'll see, if you ever get there. Remember to look up Trelon and give him my best!
We can't get out of this room. The door on the other side won't budge, and we haven't been able to figure out the mechanism yet.
That was years ago, in Daggerfall! I was captured and tortured for days. \n\nYeah, I broke. But I didn't give them anything of real value. Certainly nothing that would be useful now.
Don't be an idiot. What reason would I have to turn on the Pact?

Search around the room, I guess. Who knows? You might find something useful among the dark tomes and old fables about lusty Argonians.\n\nBut I've never seen a mechanism like this before. It's rather fascinating.
I hate everybody. I'm a misanthrope, not a traitor. \n\nListen, I can be a pain in the arse, but I'm a good soldier. I'd never betray the Pact. One of those two whining idiots has to be your man.

Yes, my friend, albeit slowly. Not all heed Tu'whacca's words as I do.\n\nWhen the Withered Hand is no more, we will have much to do. All the corpses to be cleaned and dressed … Zeht's tears, we will need more Throne Keepers. Of that I am certain.
I will retrieve what bodies I can from the Orc camp, then lead Egannor and Nielas back to Woodhearth.\n\nIf the Orcs aren't gone by the time we return with more Faithful, so much the worse for them.

I have a notion. It involves the large metal tubes on the walls. According to my research, they resemble a Daedric device that requires a source of power to operate.\n\nBut as you can plainly see, no power flows through them at the moment.
A fair assumption. Do you see the small openings near each of the tubes? If we can figure out how to move these icy flames over to them, that should provide the power to open the door.
Well, looks like Rathisa kept her mouth shut, for once. About time.\n\nWhat I wished for is none of your business.

What, your eyes aren't working? Bruma's being torn apart, that's what's happening.\n\nThe smart folks are getting out of town. The dumb ones will stay here and die. I won't be staying, in case you're wondering.
Well, when I'm ready to leave, why don't you run out ahead of me and let the Dremora rip you to shreds? Then I can get away.

This book … I think it references this device. If I'm reading this correctly—and of course I'm reading this correctly—then these flames can be used to power the mechanism that opens the gate.\n\nFrankly, the workmanship is stunning. I'm jealous.
The bone scepter? Yes. It's in my pack, just outside this tent.

Simply touch the Daedric fire. For a short time, the power of the flame will transfer to you—much like any conjuration spell. It can then be launched in any direction.\n\nGet as close as you can and throw the fire into the four open tubes.

He begs your assistance with a hopeless task. He seeks to bring the alliance leaders together for a meeting. One which they will all survive. \n\nThis is insanity, of course, but the Queen tells Raz to give him whatever he needs.
The Queen tells Raz that you speak with her authority, yes? This responsibility is a great one! Better you than Raz. \n\nYou are aware of what will be involved?
What's that? Sorry, bit of a problem with the right ear ever since I had that run-in with a titan. Rings like the bells of Cyrodiil when the weather turns.

Oh, she'll be back eventually. You can't really destroy a Daedra, no matter how hard you try. \n\nI wonder if Grunda likes wildflowers? I'll make sure we have some waiting for her when she eventually re-corporealizes.
Why, this is … you know, I can't remember the name of this place. It's an Imperial city, though. Or it was. Before it was pulled into this dreadful land.

The war in Cyrodiil has been long and bloody, and all three alliances are spread thinly. They can't commit resources to an assault on Coldharbour without making themselves vulnerable. \n\nI want to bring all three leaders together. Maybe cut a deal.

You're in a unique position. You can speak with authority, but you're not an alliance leader. You're respected. You have a reputation. They may let you get a word in before they leap at each other's throats. \n\nIn short, you're the perfect diplomat.

Khali is thrilled to be here, Hallowed. I've trained for this my whole life. Shazah and I were children when the monks first told us of Moonmont, of the Dro-m'Athra. Now we are here. Making history with you.
By Y'ffre, he gave you the flute to find me? I'm sorry, but my old life is over. I was so absorbed in the little lovestruck world we made for ourselves, I forgot mine and its needs.

My hold over the creatures of the Valenwood has weakened. That is why they panic and attack. \n\nI lack the strength to pull them back, but I can make it so you appear less threatening. Be careful though. This enchantment will only last a short time.
Malkur? Well, why didn't you say so? Tarrami wondered what happened to him.\n\nBut this one has had enough of this place. Let's get out of here.

Weren't you listening? He's the Great Mage! There isn't anything he can't accomplish once he sets his mind to it!\n\nThis particular conundrum is merely a minor bump in the road. Makes things more interesting.

There's a small number of us, and we've learned to work well together. Plus, the Groundskeeper does her best to make sure we have fresh food and water.\n\nEven that strange fellow, Cadwell, comes by once in a while with supplies.
Of course I know the Groundskeeper! We're like peas in a pod! We'd all be lost without her.
I prefer the term chef. I like to think that my carefully prepared meals make life a little bit brighter in this dismal realm.
Yes, but like the others, I wound up separated and alone in the wilderness. Luckily, I wasn't far from the walls of the city and was able to make my way here without too much trouble.
Oh, most certainly! I'm amazed at how well this city has been preserved, considering how long it's been empty.\n\nWith luck, we'll have the place crawling with mages in no time!
As more and more people fill the city, things are constantly changing. I can't keep up with it all!\n\nIt is an exciting time, though. I just wish the fate of the world didn't hang in the balance.

I can't be sure, but I suspect it's our people's connection to the Green that allows us to be infected. Other races will be immune.\n\nIt also seems that some Bosmer can resist the blight. For that, I have no explanation whatsoever.
It used to be a quiet town, but now it's a warzone. A Dremora clan invaded and have ruined most of Bruma. A few townsfolk and survivors still hold out, but they'll be overrun soon.

Come now, champion, don't lose faith. We certainly haven't lost our faith in you!\n\nBesides, the storing and protecting of one's possessions never goes out of fashion, no matter what's going on outside.

The Fighters Guild is always prepared. If we had a motto, it would tell you that we're ready for anything!\n\nI just wish we could stop losing commanding officers. Come to think of it, I'm not actually sure who's in charge at the moment.

At the moment, the stores are full. As soon as the mages stabilize the portals to Tamriel, we'll have a more or less uninterrupted supply line.\n\nThings could change at any moment, though, so I'd suggest you stock up!
Some of our troops have made their way back to the city, but we're still missing more people than I'd hoped.\n\nWith any luck, they're still alive out there and just waiting to be rescued.

A number of guild members have made it to the city, and we've received magical communications from a few others.\n\nYou've already helped so many of us. I hate to ask more of you, but if you go back out there, please set the rest of our comrades free.

Why, just what you'd expect. In addition to providing portals and arcane knowledge, our mages can also unleash a storm of destruction spells at a moment's notice.\n\nWe're ready to put an end to this Planemeld. Just give the word!

We expected it to be here, having studied the lore surrounding Coldharbour and having read "The Fall of Meridia's City." But I never expected it to be in such fine condition. Or separate from the evils of this realm.\n\nI believe we were lucky.
I wouldn't. Now don't think that's the reason I'm not making this delivery. I'm just really, really busy is all. It's not like I'm scared to go there.
Then our sacrifices—all of them—will have been for nothing. And you would not want that, would you?
Their rage has subsided, but they remain touched by the corruption. They will never be themselves again. But we can care for them and give them comfort. It is the least of our duty.

You are an altruistic one, aren't you? You have power, but you're not cut out to be a Guild Mage. Not a Guild Mage like me.\n\nBut you have been very helpful, and I promise you—you will see the fruits of our labor very soon.
Of course. Jone and Jode teach us that the light of knowledge is just as bright as moonlight.

The March is in turmoil. The future of the line of the Manes is in danger, and threats bubble up from within and without. We may be far from the heart of Elsweyr here, but Rid-Thar goes where his people need him.

Over the years, objects become imbued with faith, meaning, and power. The Golden Claw is one such an object. Its meaning to the Order of the Claw is such that many priests gave their lives to try to protect it.

The Stonefire cult is led by a Tharn. That family is a vine of corruption wrapped around the heart of Tamriel. This one does not know what plans Javad Tharn has for the Claw. Rid-Thar does not want to know.
Stick close to me. There's probably something waiting in here that wants to kill us.

I'm the leader of the Hidden Armigers. If you've heard of us, we haven't been doing our jobs. \n\nThe Armigers do the Pact's dirty work. Sometimes that involves agents from the Morag Tong and other secret organizations. Like Naryu here.
Oh yes, he's busy out back loading his wagon for a trip. Is there something I can help you with instead?
Suit yourself.

That crazy Altmer wants to organize a secret meeting of the alliance leaders in neutral territory. \n\nHe'll be here any minute, so I'll let him give you the details. But don't worry, the Armigers will do our part.
She owes me a favor. It's a long series of stories we don't have time for. She saved my brother, I saved her life. We're back and forth.\n\nThat's it for story time. You're here about Vanus Galerion?

Zur thought this was where he left the tincture, so I came to investigate.\n\nDon't tell Gadris that Zur was here. A simple illusion spell protected me, but Gadris gets worried. Me? I like to explore!

When Vanus Galerion was captured, he cast a spell that divided him into his three essential essences—health, stamina, and magicka. I am the Great Mage's health.\n\nSet each of the essences free and we can make the Great Mage whole once more.

They planned to use the Great Mage to provide a considerable boost of energy. To complete the Planemeld ahead of schedule.\n\nVanus divided his energy among the three essences, making each one worthless to the Great Shackle.

It provides the power necessary to craft Molag Bal's vile implements of conquest. Daedric weapons. Dark Anchors. The components of the Great Shackle itself.\n\nAnd I am the source of this energy … at least while the seals of binding remain in place.

While we are the essences of the Great Mage, we aren't the Great Mage himself. Not exactly. Separated into fragments such as this, we are weak. Vulnerable.\n\nIt wasn't long before we, too, were bound in magical chains.
The Ansei Wards must be returned to Sentinel for safekeeping. Then we can return to our vigil. Then we can again protect the Alik'r.

I was once a Shadowscale, just like <<1>>. For me to kill her without sanction would be true heresy. I've lived my life without angering the Night Mother, and I'd rather not start now.\n\nBut my friend <<2>> has no such restriction.
Yes, the one chewing on that hunter's spine. She's a feisty one!\n\nI'll return to the village and chase away the wamasu. If they sense <<1>> is in danger, they might stampede through <<c:2>>.
You will. Come out of the crypt. I will help you and your friends return to Sentinel quickly.
Are we playing a game? Is this a new game, Alexis? You know how much I love games!
I think the more pertinent question is, why aren't you more depressed? Why hasn't this horrible place made you so sad you can hardly breathe? Why? Why?\n\nThere's got to be something wrong with you.
Name's Dariah, but my friends call me Copper. I head up the Ring of Daggers, the King's espionage agency. You're looking for Vanus, right?

Really? Zeht's tears, you're as crazy as he is!\n\nI better get to work, then. There are a lot of preparations to make. Vanus should be here shortly. I'll let him give you the details. Also, you owe me ten gold. I'll collect later.
I'll eat sand before I give orders to the King's right hand. You want to help Vanus with his crazy plan, be my guest.

I don't want the tribe forced out of its home. These people … my people … they found hope in <<c:1>>. I don't want it wrenched away from them due to <<2>>'s foolish actions.\n\nIf I may ask, what will you tell her?

None of the others will speak with her. They fear she'll find out about the fighting, so they cling to silence and hope I make it all go away.\n\nBut I'm a terrible liar! There's no way I could disguise <<1>> and <<2>>'s absence.
As you should. I just hope what you think is right is what's best for my tribe.
I see. When they return I'll want to speak with them, but for now I won't need them for my report.\n\nAbout what we spoke of earlier … you're sure the Dominion has nothing to fear from these people?
Good.\n\nIt seems I have little choice. If there are rebellious elements in <<c:1>>, I have to recommend the tribe be exiled.
If you can assure me these people can be trusted, I'll push for them to remain. But if you have any doubts, speak plainly.

Hah, yes! In ancient times it was huge, made of the braids of every Khajiit to worship the Bright Moons. The Mane had to be carted around on a palanquin to make appearances. The modern headdress is much more … manageable.

Shazah and I spoke of it last night. We know that soon we will have to talk of the Mane. Who will be donning the headdress? Who will lead our people in their rituals? She thinks I should lead. Says, "my bravery would be an example."
She's nervous, but also very excited …. Look at these runes! And the scrollwork over the doorways …. If we had more time, I'd take rubbings of some of the more involved inscriptions. Fascinating!

Harpies. Those accursed creatures tore my inn to pieces. This inn has been in my family for three generations. These bed frames, pillows, and carpets … this is our heritage. Years of memories, torn asunder in a moment.

We spoke for the first time last night about … about the Mane. About all the pressures that one of us will assume. She, of course, says I would be better at the job than she would. Says, "my wisdom and intelligence are what our people need."

Oh, yes, Hallowed. I've been reading tomes about Moonmont since I was a cub, and to see this place with my own eyes …. It's … to be honest it's easier to focus on the ancient knowledge around me than to think about tomorrow.
Fair winds to you, and a steady grip on the haft. If you need a bed there, there are still some to be had. \n\nPerhaps the next time you come through town, we'll be back to normal. Perhaps.
Picking drunken fights with beggars or bullying old women, I have no doubt. They are worse than useless.
Oh, not this again. Look, run along and tell those flea-bitten cats that I'll have their coin as soon as possible. It isn't my fault that damned clever Farwen nicked it right out from under my nose!
Wha—oh, fine. I'd rather be hungry than dead. I never thought those Khajiit would resort to such tactics. Here, take it and be gone.

Yes, yes. No need to rub it in. I don't know how she managed it, but she must be quite skilled. Too bad she doesn't understand what a mess she's landed me in now with the fat cat and his pets … er, I mean the majestic Bashshi-ra and his cohort.
You can try. I don't think it'll do any good. Right of Theft and all that.
Oh, good. I look forward to our next meeting.

The act was artfully done, right in front of my eyes and yet I had no idea. By right, she owns my property until she makes a demand of me in return and I agree to her price for the return of what was stolen.
This one sees … the arcane. Yes, Magrus dances on light blue paws—tiny flames and the scent of incense ….

The Great Mage is a virtual powerhouse of magicka energy. The Daedra want to use that power to speed up and complete the Planemeld, finally merging Nirn into Coldharbour.\n\nBut make no mistake. Vanus has simply delayed the inevitable with this ploy.
Perhaps the Mages Guild could help him.
It is difficult to be sure. If the Daedra succeed in corrupting him, the consequences could be worse than what happened here.

Manthir's in trouble with the fat cat? I didn't know that. Well, he can have it back all right, but by Right of Theft I demand something in return. I can't believe he hasn't come to ask me himself yet.
The paw prints of arcana are difficult to track. \n\nThis one sees … yes, it is the Apprentice that guides you. Impetuous. Prideful. You must be cautious. Know your limits, for none can see all ends.

Ah, yes … this one sees the flaming palm, the starry robe. \n\nIt is the Mage that guides you. A fortuitous sign. As surely as Magrus sheds the sun's white light upon the hidden, if you seek out wonders … you shall find them.

This one hears soft chanting, glimpses flickering candles. \n\nYou are guided by the Ritual, yes? Allies shall seek you out, for your sign guides you to heal and mend. But beware—not all ills can be repaired.
This one sees … strength. Yes. The clenched fist and walls of stone.
Very well done! It seems that you have saved us, and perhaps all of Reaper's March, from a terrible fate. You are welcome here in Greenhill any time.
Easy. I just want him to marry me. Divines know, he's avoided me long enough.

This one sees claw marks upon cold, wet stone. Smells moss and memory. It is the Tower that guides you. Like a fortress, you may weather fire and claw. \n\nBut do not rely on strength alone. The strongest wall is the one that is hidden.

This one senses a heart of stone. Or is it ice? \n\nAh, it is the Atronach that guides you. Sturdy, adaptable. Your sign grants you a steady arm and a nimble mind. You can be fire, stone, or ice. Adapt, but remain true to yourself.

Hmm. Yes, your guide is difficult to miss. The Warrior. Straightforward, willful, brimming with wrath. \n\nHeed the counsel of Jone and Jode, walker. Without the little moon, the big one is left to spin alone, lost. Do not count on strength alone.
This one sees … a shadow. The flash of steel and fell whispers ….

You have not seen the devastation at Fort Grimwatch, Hallowed. But trust Rid-Thar when he says it is total. When the Dark Mane and his host are one mind, one force … the Darkness is terrifying. Their power, all consuming.
Oh, you know. A hidden path, the odd secret door, and Bob's your uncle, here I am.\n\nI heard you were going to attack the Great Shackle. That's a quest worthy of a knight of my stature!

This one sees … nothing. A chill void. \n\nIt must be the Shadow that guides you. Cold, cautious. Patient. Shadow is among the deepest signs, for it represents what is not known. Tread not too far down that path, walker, if you want to return.

This one sees writhing coils … silent menace. \n\nYou walk with the Serpent. Your presence means danger for all, friend and foe alike. Sangiin has given you the gift of swift mending. Take care—venom is perilous to both poisoned and poisoner.

Hmm. Yes, your sign is well known to this one, for it dwells in the hearts of all Khajiit. You have the luck of the Thief—of Baan Dar. You are swift, cunning, and beautiful. Your dance brings wealth and risk. \n\nJust spare this one your touch.

The Dark Mane is a creature of Darkness. A being from beyond the stars. The only way he could be truly destroyed is to face him in one of those places beyond. But here, now, one of the Champions can hold him. Make the world safe from his evil.
No, Hallowed. This must be your decision. Speak to the Champions if you need to. Hear what they have to say before you decide. This must be your decision, alone.
This one hears the whispers of court—scheming and revelry behind closed doors ….

This one hears the pounding of hooves, feels the straining of muscles. You are borne by the Steed, walker—headstrong and willful. Swiftness is a great gift, but only when measured with foresight. Do not rush headlong into danger.

It is obscured by pride and hidden intent, but this one sees through that. It is the Lord that guides you—calculating, strong, ambitious, with the vigor of Alkosh. \n\nBut be wary. Even the mightiest nobles can be felled by a flick of a quill.

Your spirit bespeaks elegance, walker—pillow-soft and dagger-sharp. This one sees … yes, it is the Lady. \n\nHer gifts are sweet indeed for those deserving. Patience, caution, foresight. Seek the highest path to earn her protection.

This one smells roses and lavender, hears laughter, quiet and demure. \n\nAh, you bear the kiss of the Lover! All fall prey to your sleek charms, yes? Use this gift wisely, walker. To be loved and to be feared are different phases of the same moon.

Ah, threats are next perhaps? Dear mortal, I have not harmed any of my collection. They provide me with comfort and entertainment, and my children with sustenance every now and again. In return, I care for their every need.
I do not fear you, mortal. You are in my lair. I allow you to see me because it is convenient.\n\nOh, I'm sure you could escape my nest, in time. But these two would surely not survive.
Of course, Hallowed. I will answer any questions I can to make your decision easier.
If that's the case, then where is he? No, you're just another one of <<1>>'s puppets. But you can't get into my mind! I'll never let you copy my <<2>>!
What? Where? Stop lying, illusion!\n\nWhen I get out of this place, I'll torch it, and squish anything that manages to crawl out. Just you wait!
I'm no hero, but I can't stand by while my love is trapped by this Daedra!\n\nMaybe she'd take me in exchange ….
A month ago, I would have fled. Marriage scared me. Spiders scared me. \n\nBut I've been running too long. It's time I acted like a true warrior and faced my fear.
It is a larger … more powerful … version of a Dark Anchor ….\n\nDesigned to complete the connection … to draw Oblivion and Nirn … together ….

I assume you want to know more about what we need you to do. \n\nYou are small enough now to squeeze through the rubble and run along the pipes. Be careful of the venting steam, however. We don't want your little monkey paws to get burned.
Your friend is out there, being hunted by my people as we speak. If you have questions, ask them quickly so we can get back to the task at hand.
This one sees … open fields. The canebrake is fertile, but no sugar-cane is sown.

Once you get through the rubble, look for my notes. They list the components you need to find to craft the rods. \n\nZur and I will meet you inside. We'll keep hidden as best we can. This damnable weakness is so annoying.

Indeed. This one feels wet grass beneath her paws, the smell of untilled earth. You need only take up the spade and claim your harvest. \n\nYou seek fortune, yes? Find the Mundus Stones and find your guide.
Mortal, I am nothing if not true to my word. The pair need not even know you existed.\n\nYou are free to leave in peace.
Then we are at an impasse, are we not?\n\nI'll allow you to think things over. Mortals can get anxious when asked to make decisions quickly, I've found.
As you can tell, the Orc is resistant to my charms. She has not made a good specimen.\n\nI propose a trade of sorts. Give me the Redguard and I will give you the Orc.

That can be done as well. Give them both to me, and I will provide them with a long and happy life together.\n\nOnce my poison takes them, they will see what I weave. A safe life together, a happy existence. What else does a mortal crave?

Ah, how delicious! Simply a turn of phrase, I assure you.\n\nThe Redguard held much bitter fear in his taste before. I will weave him a life better suited for sweetness. My children do love a treat now and then.
Ask me any questions you need to. Let's get this whole thing over with.
I would lead with a firm hand and a brave heart. Just as mother taught me, all those years ago.

Father was ever speaking about the brilliance of Shazah's spellcasting. Once, she cast a spell and the whole sky lit ablaze. They were so proud of her. I'm sure they'd want her to be Mane. To lead our people.
Gadris worries so much. He wanted to make sure you found the catalyst.\n\nThe catalyst makes the rods strong enough to withstand both magicka and machinery. Two things this one likes very much.
I would … I would try to lead with wisdom. As the monks taught us, as I learned from my father.

Mother was always so proud of Khali's bladework. She used to have her demonstrate for the other children. I'm sure they would want Khali to be the next Mane. She is far stronger, braver, than I am. She is a better leader, and a proud warrior.
My clan is ancient. Older than you could even imagine.\n\nOur Treemender tells stories of the before time. When we lived under the bright skies in the lush forests of Valenwood.

Gave up? That's one way to look at it. Another way is to see a clan that wanted not only to survive, but to gain a significant advantage.\n\nThe Shadow Walkers love power. In exchange for servitude, we were promised power over our enemies.
According to the stories, the Daedric Prince unleashed his fury upon Valenwood. Instead of fighting back, my ancestors decided to offer their allegiance to the Prince.\n\nAnd here we are.

I explained this to you already. I'm tired of darkness and false promises. Molag Bal gave us power, but he keeps us trapped here. What good is power if we're stuck in this realm forever?\n\nI want to see clear skies and stars in the night.

After the soul-meld, the Overseer ignored us. The Dwarven constructs were inactive, so we were able to work here in relative peace. \n\nYes, Gadris, everything was fine until Zur exploded something. The Dark Elf sure knows how to hold a grudge.

The basic ingredients can be melted, but without a catalyst to imbue them with strength and elemental—alchemy is not boring, Gadris! Oh, very well.\n\nGadris wrote about a proper catalyst for the antipodal rods. He wants you to read his notes.

Many things! The last one was pretty spectacular. It was an accident, of course. Gadris was so mad because we were forced outside. But it proved his first suggestion for a catalyst didn't work. So … the experiment was successful.

A Khajiit rogue called Nineclaws, a fellow Bosmer by the name of Draulduin, and an exiled Breton mage known as Zavierry. If they aren't wounded, they'll be able to make it back to Longhaven on their own once you've freed them.
I am afraid to hope too much, but you've made such progress. Perhaps we shall end this torment, after all. \n\nThe constructs have moved off. The forge area is clear, at least for the moment.

When Bosmer transgress against the Green Pact, their souls are confined to the Ooze. There they remain for eternity, thinking upon their sins.\n\nGorzesh and his kin are among the first Orcs to join those damned souls.

Melt the components in the furnace. Then craft two rods from the mixture. There is an anvil near the furnace. Be careful, though. The mixture can be volatile.\n\nThe machine that merged us is further on, in the Overseer's atelier. We'll meet there.
Yes, we are Baandari on our way to Sentinel. We planned to take our goods across the sea. All was well until we reached this wretched place.
Yes, quickly! Before more of those lizards come!
This one knew Nivrilin would not abandon us. It is good that she still lives. Thank you for aiding us.
I don't know who you are, but I'm glad you're on our side. I'll see these spineless lizards over a cooking fire once I've mended!

Pass through the flames, they will not harm you. Not you, of all people. Within the temple you will find the source of the darkness. Destroy it and you will return control of the fort to those who live in the light.
Surely you have heard of us? We are the wandering litter of Elsweyr. Merchants, soothsayers, entertainers … this is ringing chimes, yes?

Just so. They may have looked for a new home at first, but in time the road became home. And so it is with us. Var var var. We gather and sell, entertain, take odd jobs and the like. It's not an easy life, but it is rarely dull.

Well, Kunamu is not short on time, so she will tell you. In the long ago time, our people fought many wars. It was a moonless age of fang and claw. Some fled the fighting to wander the lands of Tamriel in search of a better life.
Yes. Stuck in this harpy-stinking dung pit. We hate it here.

One of our wagons was raided on the road. A flock of these feather-fur dung-birds swooped in and tore it to pieces. Then, during our escape, the other wagon broke an axle or somesuch. \n\nI do not care to know what it is. Kunamu is not a cartwright.

Fixed? It may never be fixed. Wheelbreaker here has been toying with it for two turns of Jone and Jode. \n\nWe need tools and wood, but the dungy Redguards cannot spare them because they want to repair their homes.
Var var var. Just so. A few more days and maybe Wheelbreaker will have something. This one is doubting it, however.

You clearly haven't studied the fundamentals of blood sacrifice.\n\nYou see these serpent-shaped statues, their "<<m:1>>?" They collect spirit energies from rune-marked subjects and channel it, like water through a funnel.

Exactly the right question!\n\nIt seems the Sea Vipers use a specialized lodestone to block the channel. Approach an active <<1>>, hold forth the lodestone, and harmlessly siphon the energy away. You should see for yourself.

Other than grumbling about harpy droppings? Just girding ourselves for the next anchor raid. \n\nOur new Guildmaster, Sees-All-Colors, has all of us wrecking those damnable anchor things and slaying whatever Daedra come with them.

Shor's bones, that's great to hear! Welcome to the guild, Associate. \n\nGrab your favorite cleaver, find an anchor and get to work! If you do a good job, there'll be a fat reward and maybe even special assignments for you when you return.

Always! That's half the reason we established this post in the Alik'r. These Redguards swing a fair sword arm. Not as good as Nords, mind you—but close. We need seasoned fighters like you if we're to wipe out these Daedra.\n\nSo—interested?
You must have seen one! They're everywhere these days.\n\nThey're huge anchored chains that drop to Tamriel straight out of Oblivion. And where there are anchors, there are Daedra. Scores of them.
The Guild is an organization dedicated to the pursuit of arcane knowledge. We travel the sands of Alik'r and beyond, seeking out books, tomes, and ancient scrolls.

Wonderful! I hereby grant you the rank of Student in the Mages Guild. Welcome.  From now on, every book you find and every book collection you complete will enhance your reputation with the Guild. \n\nWalk with Julianos, my friend.
I prefer to think of us as watchful scholars. We seek out knowledge of every sort and store it in our libraries, so that none of Tamriel's ancient wisdom is lost.

Guild members in good standing earn the opportunity to buy special items only available to members of our circle. \n\nWe also have more … complicated tasks that crop up from time to time. Those with a thirst for adventure may well be interested.

Indeed I do. We've been pursuing this tome for some time.  \n\nI'm delighted that you've brought it to us. You're well on your way to membership in the Mages Guild already. The Guild offers rich rewards for texts like this.
Excellent!  I hereby grant you the rank of Student in the Mages Guild.\n\nSeek out more books and collections and your reputation here will soar!

Yes. The Guild seeks out all manner of books and scrolls.  Any that you bring to us will improve your reputation with the Mages Guild.\n\nReputation leads to rewards, and as you advance through the ranks those rewards will increase in value.
A simple pledge to the Guild is all that's required.  Any Magister in Tamriel can grant you membership.  \n\nAre you interested in joining our circle?
Q4399 - DUMMY TRACKER CONVO
I am unsure what I will regret more, knowing or never knowing the truth.\n\nForgive my indecision. Please, continue.
Mortal… like you? What happened to me?
Yet I live. Don't I?
I felt this to be true. What of me? Did the book speak of how I became?
Please, tell me more.
Have I ever! There's been a steady stream of Altmer depositing valuables here since the thefts began.

Why do you insist on not harming the ones who kill my people? The little Elf girl. She has confused you, hasn't she?\n\nBah! I do not know the ways of stealth. My people kill and we do so proudly for all to see.

I know nothing that would help you. I've already told you that.\n\nBut think about it. How did you make your way past the Wood Elves earlier? How did you avoid the runner? That might lead to the answer you seek.
I'd like to see that! I'm an expert in security. No one can enter the bank without keys, and only I and my apprentice Nidras have them.

Typically we'd be attending to a variety of jobs, but recently we've been focusing exclusively in Daedra slaying. Our new Guildmaster has us thumping Daedroths and Dremora morning, noon and night. Those anchors aren't going to break themselves.

Stendarr protect you!  Welcome to the guild, Associate. \n\nNow the work begins. Take up the sword and send those curs back to Oblivion.  If you do a good well, there may be a reward or some special assignments for you when you return.
Always! We need seasoned fighters like you if we plan on wiping these Daedra out.

You haven't seen an anchor yet? \n\nBasically, huge chains have been erupting out of tears in the sky. Wherever they land, daedra run rampant. Our job is to go in, hack the monsters to peices, then break the chain. Sounds simple, yeah?
By all means. Do you want to know how many Daedra can dance on the head of a pin? How I manage to stay so cheerful even in the most perilous of circumstances? What's my favorite color? Ask away!

It's my home, old chum! Has been for years. I know every wondrous nook and cranny. Beautiful place, full of fascinating creatures.\n\nOf course, they often try to kill you, but that's the challenge of it, isn't it?

Molag Grunda? Large woman with wings? Bit of a temper? Guards the gatehouse? \n\nI hear that she's the daughter of Molag Bal, if you can believe that! He never struck me as a family man, but who am I to judge?

Darien was impatient. As soon as you broke the seals, he took some troops and went through the portal. Walks-in-Ash went along to keep him out of too much trouble.\n\nI'll use illusions to scout ahead and see what's waiting for us at the gatehouse.

The compassionate choice would be to release the general and his army, to allow them to return to their rest.\n\nBut if you prefer, you might ask them instead to turn against Naemon and aid our forces in the fight for Valenwood. The choice is yours.

I found the perfect meeting place. A neutral location, far from disputed territories—an island called Stirk. \n\nI can get you an audience with each leader, and provide magical transportation. You just need to convince them to travel to Stirk.
Kuralit hears and sees much, but it is difficult to recall when one's stomach rumbles so. Alas, he does not have the coin for food.
The Guild is a circle of scholars dedicated to the pursuit of knowledge. Our members scour the caves and tombs of Tamriel seeking out books, tomes, and ancient scrolls.
Well, Darien ran east and Walks-in-Ash ran west, so I imagine that tells us something.\n\nNow, stop standing around and move out! Those reinforcements are slaughtering us!
Oh, right as rain. Besides, we've got the high and mighty Cadwell watching our backs.\n\nHe might be as crazy as an outhouse skeever, but he's remarkable with that sword.

I'll remain here and make sure we got all the Daedra that came through before the portal was closed.\n\nYou should head out and do something heroic. Otherwise you'll never catch up to my impressive record.

Banekin and ogrim mostly, but the Daedra can throw anything at you. I sense that they are just regrouping at the moment.\n\nBe careful of the Xivilai. They conjure up atronachs and clannfear on occasion.

He spent a lot of time talking to one of the mages from the Guild. Darius, I think his name is. They were admiring an old urn together. I think Darius left with it, come to think. So he might be one to talk to.
We are very different, you and I. This was a necessity. The Wood Elves feed on our eggs and keep us as slaves! Our survival depended upon it.\n\nYou did what you needed to do. So did I.

That is wonderful news! I hereby grant you the rank of Student in the Mages Guild. Welcome.  From now on, every book you find and every book collection you complete will enhance your reputation with the Guild. \n\nWalk with Julianos, my friend.
Just so. But knowledge is an elusive quarry, walker. What little we find is a precious gift. We store it in our libraries to pass on to the next generation.

Guild members in good standing earn the opportunity to buy special items only available to members of our circle. \n\nWe also have more … complicated tasks that crop up from time to time. Those with a thirst for adventure may well be interested.
A thousand blessings. This one's night-eye has not failed him yet. Kuralit caught a glimpse of a Bosmer sneaking into the bank.
This one did not serve the Dominion for three years to be treated like this! Fine. Kuralit saw a Bosmer infiltrating the bank late at night.
Threefold blessings upon you, my friend. You've saved me, saved my future. Perhaps even saved my life. I don't know what I can do to repay you, other than to say thank you. Truly, you have my thanks.
Excellent! Then perhaps you can tell me … where in Oblivion is he? He's kept me waiting here for hours!
It's hard to avoid it. Between you and me, I hope the Artisan never gets caught.

Bosmer culture considers theft to be an art, and the closer the object to the victim's heart, the better the theft.\n\nAnd there's more than a few Bosmer who are unhappy with the Altmer building Marbruk in Valenwood.
Because the thief's obviously a Bosmer. It would only strain relations in the Dominion, further than they've already been strained.
Oh, it is your lucky day! This one recently came into possession of one of the Artisan's messages, written in his own hand!
Zuzik understands! You have connections with a guild of … like-minded individuals? Here, forge copies, and Zuzik shall give a commission.
A wise choice! Zuzik's mate was furious when this one paid much for the note; she thinks it worthless. We know otherwise, no?
Zuzik does not run a charity! He has kittens to feed! As the Artisan's infamy grows, his signature will become highly valuable.
Yes, the Bosmer religion does not allow the use of paper, so they use animal hides instead. Not many use it in Marbruk.
You know what I think? That old banker Talqua paid a thief to steal from the rich Altmer so they'd pay to keep their valuables with him.
Well, the Artisan only targets Altmer who don't use the bank. And don't forget, Talqua has that Bosmer apprentice of his to take the fall.
Ah. Working with Cinnar? I noticed you making friends in the market. If you've figured it out, there's no use keeping up pretenses.
My initial plan was to exercise the Right of Theft. I steal precious objects from Altmer, then demand they leave Marbruk for their return.
It turns out the Altmer don't respect the right, so I returned them. Now I simply let Altmer hatred do the job for me.
The banker's … why didn't I see it before? You have my thanks for finding him, but now we have to deal with the mess he left behind.
The Right of Theft, of course! You steal an item from me, and you demand a boon for its return.
Very perceptive! Yes, my revenge on the Altmer is well at hand.  Your theft and the guards clumsily following you are minor setbacks.
Even if requesting imposed servitude wasn't expressly disallowed, it would certainly be poor sportsmanship.

Look around! Don't you see what's happening? It's one city, but it won't stop there. War is only one way of conquering; building is another. We may not have destroyed Valenwood ourselves, but if we let the Altmer do it, how is it different?
The bastard returned the stolen items to the wrong houses. He then sent anonymous letters to the victims framing the owners for the crime.
I appreciate the help. According to the letters, the items are in houses across Marbruk. You'll have to search carefully to find them.

He … he what? That's it! I'm going to take these back to Telenger, and Rollin can find some other Archmagus to train him. As far as I'm concerned, that buffoon will never become an apprentice to the Artificer. Thank you for your honesty.
You do that! And you tell him this will not reflect well in my report to the Artificer. Not well at all!
So formal! Of course, of course. What would you like to discuss?

According to reports I've been getting, no. They're still trying to hold the few places in the Northern Woods they managed to capture, but we've pushed them back. Arenthia was their largest victory, and you denied them that.
Yes, I have. She's a quiet woman, seems very thoughtful. But Stars above does she know a lot. We had the most fascinating discussion about the signing of the Elden Accord. And she wasn't even there!
We're still not sure. But we haven't seen any chains, yet. No dark anchors. All the Daedra appear to have come from portals opened in the middle of the districts. I have a problem, though.
Yes, I have. She's quite the boisterous woman, seems very capable. But Stars above does she know tactics. We had the most fascinating discussion about the most recent push in Cyrodiil.
I'm still receiving reports of conflict at a ruin called Senalana. Why the Colovians are so keen to hold an Ayleid ruin in the middle of the wood, Auri-El only knows. Those people are beyond me.
Yes, I have. He won't tell me what you did that has him so irritated, but … he's really annoyed. Kept saying something about following orders? I'm sure he'll calm down soon.

Raz was … he could be infuriating. Many times, my advisors told me to cut him loose. I never considered it. I and the Dominion will roll along without him, I'm sure. But it will be a little lonelier under this crown.

My friend, I know you've chosen well. The lunar clergy seems to think so, and I find her quite charming. The Khajiiti people are wise and brave in equal amounts. They will grow to love her. I know it.

When the Daedra push into our realm, they create a kind of organic gateway. I saw that firsthand at Firsthold. That hasn't happened here. The portals reach from our side to theirs. That means, somewhere in Dune, there is a traitor.

Is this really the time for idle chit-chat? Oh, very well.\n\nWe are master conjurers. Our job is to stabilize the portals so that more forces and supplies can be brought from Nirn. Until we do that, our troops will be at a distinct disadvantage here.
The trial was a farce. They just wanted to make us squirm. <<1>> went on and on about fairness and equitable treatment, but he decided we were guilty from the start.

<<1>> is most impressed with his newest bauble. But the undead are a threat to all of <<2>>.\n\nIf you want to, you could search <<Ac:3>>. Determine how to contain the dead there. Then the locals should see we came here as allies, not conquerors.
Yes! I've been too afraid to move, too afraid of the spiders.\n\nBut I can't leave the mines without <<1>> … I think I felt something give. Yes, it's breaking open!

<<1>>'s really here? I thought her voice came from a dream!\n\nIf she's gone deeper into the mines, I must find her! This spider's silk is tight, but I feel the threads moving …. Spiders or not, I've got to break free!
I've secured a spell to get us out of this plane. However, in order to channel it, I require a sacrifice.\n\nAnd I'd like—I need it to be you.
Time works differently in Daedric lands—I feel like I've searched for years and found nothing.\n\nYou're the only plan I've got.
I … thank you. Your offer means more to me than you can know.\n\nThe quickest, most painless way is right in front of you—jump. The mountain will take care of the rest.
Of course. I hoped he'd come to me, but then he always was a hard-headed one! Let's go.
I wouldn't overstate things. But here is the gold I owe. Take it back to those mangy cats and tell them I have no more need of their services. My ledger's clear, yeah?
I'm not sure how to tell you this, or even if you'll understand, but you died at <<1>>'s hands.

Do you notice how you seem different than most everyone around here? It's a harsh truth, but I hope hearing it allows you to go to a better place.\n\nIf you allow it, I'll pray for Arkay to help you move on.

I know it's hard to understand, but you're trapped as a spirit within the walls of this temple. Look around. Can't you see how you stand out from most everyone around here?\n\nI can pray for Arkay to help you move on, if that's all right with you.
I knew you wouldn't understand. The dead never realize they're dead.\n\nWalk with Arkay, spirit.

Well, the others will have to fend for themselves for the time being. I'll send Cadwell to find them shortly.\n\nThings are looking grim outside, by the way. We've lost many fine men and women already, and the battle is far from over.

Far too many. Hahnin was caught by surprise and wiped out, along with a large number of Fighters Guild soldiers. King Dynar's group was also ambushed, but he managed to fight his way out of it. Many were wounded, though.\n\nTime is running out.

Even without his portal, Molag Bal has the ability to throw an unlimited number of forces at us. We're holding our own, but just barely.\n\nWinning isn't our goal, though. We just need to survive long enough for someone to reach the planar vortex.

Thank Cadwell for that small favor. I'm not sure how he does it, but I think he's grown so attached to Coldharbour that he's actually become a part of it.\n\nUnfortunately, he can only teleport one other person at a time, and it is a lengthy process.

The portal that leads to the planar vortex is just around the bend. Molag Bal won't let you simply walk up to it, though. He's going to do everything he can to stop you.\n\nI'll provide what help I can—and, as usual, it will be considerable. Now go!

The hard way, I'm afraid. With claw, and blade, and spell. Destroy the Atronachs while you hold the Fang, and their essence will be transferred into the relic. Once it's primed, it should be simple to seal the portal.

Raising the dead … the consecrated dead. The very dangerous consecrated dead. \n\nThe most evil people who ever walked the sands of the Alik'r are entombed in the Motalion Necropolis. Prince Azah and I came to stop them, but we were overpowered.

I fear he is either dead or taken captive. We were attacked by so many, so fast … I tried to find him, but to no avail. I came back to catch my breath.\n\nWith you here, though … I am willing to try again. If you are … that is.
Since Moonmont, you mean? I am well enough. I miss my sister dearly. Since arriving at Dune, I can't tell you the number of times I've wanted to ask her a question. Wanted her fighting at my side.
Safe? Then where is he? \n\nDo you mean he has met his ancestors? Did the spiders kill him and <<1>>?
Daedra? What are you talking about? I came out here to … well, anyway, I've never met you or a Daedra before in my life!\n\nDid you poison me?

Tharn. You can be sure of that. It wasn't enough that he inflicted the Dark Mane upon Akkhuz-ri, or spurred the Colovians to assault Arenthia. Now he must work to shatter the jewel in the desert. Our great city of Dune.

Every member of the Dominion should cherish the Elder Scrolls. Our sacred trust to protect the scrolls must be our primary focus.\n\nThe Elder Scrolls are prophecies, in essence. But they are much more than that.
The temples are holy places, created as housing for the scrolls, to honor and protect them.

The Grand Warlord orders these attacks. Access to each scroll is blocked by a gate. To unlock it, both castles protecting it must be taken away from the alliance that holds the scroll. Once the castles are captured, the way to the temple is open.

The scrolls contain records of all past and future events, but they cannot be read without a severe price—madness, blindness, even death.\n\nMany believe they were created by the Aedra, but why or when is unknown.
Every Elder Scroll we hold grants power to all the soldiers of our alliance. This is another reason our enemies cannot be allowed to keep any of them.

The Elder Scroll must be taken from its temple and brought to one of our six original castles. Once there, it must be placed upon a scroll pedestal. Needless to say, capturing an Elder Scroll requires the cooperation of many soldiers.

I honestly … I hope so. The first Mane seemed convinced that she would have to remain beneath Moonmont. But perhaps, if I walk the Path. If I become Mane. Perhaps I will be strong enough to free her from the Darkness.
I'm fine. I'm … almost glad she isn't here. Moons know, she didn't like all this fighting. She would have hated walking into another city ablaze, all this death in the streets. Almost.

Rid-Thar seemed pretty well certain she'd have to stay down there. Holding that darkness down, keeping it away from the light. I'd love to get her out of there someday, though. Maybe if I walk the Path. If I'm the Mane, maybe.

Tharn. You can be sure of that. It wasn't enough that he inflicted the Dark Mane on Akkhuz-ri, or duped the Colovians to assault Arenthia. Now he tries to shatter the jewel in the desert. Our great city of Dune.

No. After she finished her ritual, she departed. I think she left the ward behind, though.\n\nPlease. Go in there and get it. Then find Throne Keeper Farvad and the ward he was carrying. I shall follow after … if you would untie me first, that is.
Even so, if you could just untie me and let me stretch my muscles first, I'll answer all your questions.

I knew you'd ask that. I feel like such a fool. She was standing right behind us at Tava's Blessing, for Stendarr's sake! \n\nAfter we parted ways, I tried so hard to remember the sister's name, but I just couldn't recall it.

She and her necromancers performed a ritual in there. I suspect that is why the ward remains.\n\nI suggest you exercise caution when entering the room. I would assist you, but I need a few moments to recover. Talia will help you, though.

No, but I have a feeling he survived the attack.\n\nI don't know if Tu'whacca truly speaks to him or not, but he has always struck me as someone who the gods smile down upon. Regardless, we have to look for him. We owe him that much.
Only after it was too late. She and her minions fell upon us as soon as we entered the necropolis. In her rage, I finally saw the family resemblance.\n\nWhat about you? Did Talia tell you?

So you learned Shiri's true identity before I did? Truly, I am impressed!\n\nI only hope such knowledge helps us stop her. First though, you must recover Ansei Maja's Ward, and then find Throne Keeper Farvad and the ward he was carrying.
Praise the gods for Talia. And for you.\n\nThe two of you must go on. Recover Ansei Maja's Ward and then find Throne Keeper Farvad and the ward he was carrying.

You can buy them from siege merchants at our gates and castles. They can tell you the best ways to place siege engines on the battlefield.\n\nI know how to repair siege weapons, but Firamo and Miniel can tell you much more.
Driving off attackers is always the first step. Then repair kits can be used to fix some of the damage. Here's a practice repair kit; use it on a siege weapon here.

I'm told they'll be arriving at the meeting site by portal any moment. \n\nAfter all the bloodshed in Cyrodiil, I fear the leaders won't be quick to trust one another. Perhaps you can help them see the wisdom in cooperation.
I don't envy you the task. \n\nWe've already assembled quite a team of experts for the Coldharbour invasion itself. I'll try to introduce you to some of them on the way to the meeting. Lead on!

I … look, someone out there will pay a small fortune for it. You have no idea how difficult it was to catch word of the Eye.\n\nThe Mages Guild, Tamriel's leading archaeologists. They'll all kill to get it. Like my dear husband tried to do.
Our relationship wasn't always like this. That first night was wonderfully raucous.\n\nOf course, it only took a week for him to try to kill me. Let's see, that was … last week.

Like you, I have come to finish this.\n\nThanks to the efforts of your army, you have gotten this far without drawing the gaze of Molag Bal. I use a similar distraction to travel through this disagreeable realm unmolested.

Keep working on it. You will solve the riddle, eventually.\n\nThere is more to do if you wish to save your world. To halt the Planemeld, you must enter the eye of the storm. The planar vortex can only be disrupted from the inside.

I wanted to see his research, and we know he needed mine.\n\nIt felt like it took an eternity to get it. Too bad I knew more than he did. But enough about me. I'm sure you'll find the Guardian's Eye much more interesting.

Arkay, please hear my prayer. Take this lost soul, as the wind lifts a flower's seeds. Shepherd this spirit to a place where memories of pain and fear are replaced with fulfillment and tranquility.\n\nWhat's happening? Why does everything fade?

It's a prison pit. Ifriz the Unraveler runs the place. He loves the sound of his own voice.\n\nThey split us up. Some of us are down here. But our captains, Eilram and Arakh, they're upstairs. A locked passage keeps us apart.

Well, she isn't a guard. But if she's a prisoner, the ogrims certainly don't give her any grief.\n\nTo tell the truth, I'm curious about her myself. I've noticed she's been watching you since you dropped in on this little party.

Wasn't just me. A whole group of us got caught by the Daedra. We teleported into Coldharbour to take the fight to Molag Bal, but that didn't work out so good.\n\nWe're down here, our captains are upstairs, and we're all up to our necks in ogrim dung!

I have been with you every step of the way. I provided a safe haven in Coldharbour. I gave you knowledge of the Lights of Meridia.\n\nI needed a surrogate, to act in my stead. I dared not risk exposing my true nature to the Dark Prince.

Used you? Of course I used you.\n\nBut you knew what was at stake from the beginning and did what was necessary to save your world. Every choice you made was your own. As it happens, your choices suited my own ends.

The life of one insignificant mortal to save an entire world? It is a small sacrifice. \n\nIf you succeed, the brilliance of the unleashed light will consume the vortex and sever the Planemeld. Nirn will be saved.

You must enter the planar vortex—the interstices of space and time where Nirn and Coldharbour churn and meld.\n\nDestroy the Dark Anchors within. Unleash the power of a Light of Meridia at the focal point of the Planemeld, and disrupt the vortex.
Ask your questions, but know that time is growing short.
The light of Meridia cleanses and purifies. There is nothing to fear from its brilliant embrace.
You cannot hope to succeed without the support of your allies. I will summon those who still live and draw them into the vortex with us.

I did not pretend, mortal. I am the Groundskeeper. I merely hid the fact that I am also a Daedric Prince. \n\nMy plans have been long in the making. Had I revealed myself too soon, I could have jeopardized everything.
Reality is a game, mortal. Learn to play, or resign yourself to becoming one of the pieces that is meant to be sacrificed.\n\nYour allies have arrived. Speak to them before we continue.
You mortals only see life as precious because it ends. Take it from a god—you'll never know how fortunate you are.\n\nYour allies have arrived. Speak to them before we continue.
Do not presume to question my motives! Suffice it to say, I required mortal assistance to destroy the vortex and halt the Planemeld.
They struggled mightily. We honor their bravery. But no, they fell before the Yokudan onslaught like all the others.

You would allow these smug bastards to get away with it? \n\nI suppose they paid for their crimes already … didn't they? I am grateful that my sweet Darius cared enough to come and consecrate my remains. I suppose this is enough.

Horrible indeed! Our Yokudan ancestors could not tolerate such a blight on their new homeland. They would suffer no rivals. And so one of their mightiest heroes, Frandar Hunding, rallied the swords of the Ra Gada to slay the beasts.

Ah … Tu'whacca claimed him during one of the bloodiest battles of the campaign. But his son Divad, filled with wrath over the slaying of his father, soon rose to take command of the Ra Gada. He swore to avenge his father—no matter the cost.

The Lord of Brutality uses Dark Anchors to bind this vortex. We must destroy all three before the power of Meridia's Light is unleashed, otherwise the resulting backlash could destroy Nirn as surely as the Planemeld would.
So, it begins! Destroy the remaining anchors. I shall begin searching for the focal point of the vortex.
Meridia's Light must be unleashed at the focal point of the vortex. We will need to locate that focal point.
Wait! You don't understand. They made me do it. I mean, yes, they gave me a cut of their takings, but what choice did I have? They threatened to rob me of everything I own!

Think long and hard. It'll be worth your while, and I'll never deal with those bandits again, I promise!\n\nYou don't have to turn me in. Just take me out back and I'll give you everything in my stash!
Anything you say! Of course, I never spent a single coin from what the bandits gave me. I couldn't stand to. I'd happily give it all to you, if you'd let this go. Please?
There's a vat you can use atop the platform here. Use it as you would any other siege weapon.\n\nJust don't pour it on me or the ram, please.
I mend, fix, and build things around the village. Like the stone walls, paths, and torches.\n\nI also look after Elengil. She's the oldest living member of our tribe.

She's like the tribe's grandmother. Her own grandmother was one of the first Bosmer to move into the Court of the Wilderking.\n\nIf you come across her speaking to thin air, she's just talking to the Elders of Bramblebreach.
We owe him much. He crafted these houses for us long ago. We never go hungry. He always looks out for us.\n\nAnd his blood runs through the land.
