What is any war about? There are enemies to be vanquished and their lands, riches, and strongholds to be made ours. The Dominion, Covenant, and Pact will battle for Cyrodiil until one alliance is victorious.

Forgive me, I mispoke. He is the land. The sap within the trees, the water in our ponds and lakes, this is his blood. The stones and soil are his skin. Trees are his hair and veins; his heart and his mind.
Kala knew this was coming. Yenadar has been away too long. He would have come home to his sister if he could. What has happened?
It's the right thing to do. For us and them.\n\nI'll be waiting in the town square for you, if you're willing. What do you say?

Cyrodiil is the heart of Tamriel. The alliance that controls Cyrodiil can strike in any direction, threatening the other heartlands. And whoever controls the Imperial City assumes the mantle of the Empire. We must see that the Dominion prevails!
Thank you. I can't do this on my own, and my father won't listen to me until I have proof.\n\nI don't think the eggs will be proof enough, but at least they will be safe.

"Conquerors" is a strong word, but yes, of course they were. Ha! Our ancestors and the Bretons' laid siege to the city for thirty years before finally breaching the walls and razing the city. The Orcs proved to be fearsome adversaries.
No! Yenadar was such a quiet, pious man. How could someone so good, so innocent become a vessel for a dark spirit?
He's done what? Of all the things he's done for his faith … this is madness. Kala is beside herself now. Where has he gone? Tell her.
I think our time would be better spent attempting to force the entrance open. \n\nWe'll work faster that way, you see?
I knew Gamirth was gone, but … this makes it so much more final.\n\nHe worked so tirelessly to find a way to end this enchantment. I'm determined to finish what we started.
It's somewhat complicated. This situation is all about a contract that ensures equal treatment between unequal partners. Pircalmo is a mage, powerful and learned. We're just simple brewers.
Come now. That's not fair. We're working off of my research, after all, and you're … better at danger than I am.\n\nWe'll be waiting. I mean working. Here. To get the door open.
Yes. A pretty Altmer girl was here before.\n\nShe is searching for our Wilderking. What is it that you seek?
What about the war in Cyrodiil? If I commit troops to this invasion, the Pact will be vastly outnumbered there.
In Tamrielic, it translates something like atonement. We say that if you are forced to eat the Unthrappa, you must eat your sin. You must consume your failure.

Tradition states that the pact-hostage is a guarantee that the more powerful party will fulfill their end of the bargain. If Pircalmo doesn't fulfill the contract, we'll be forced to prepare his wife and serve it to him as Unthrappa.

Aye, I could. We hired Pircalmo to clear the trees above the village. We're a devout community, we observe the Green Pact as closely as possible. Cutting down the trees for our own gain would be a clear violation of our belief.
Bah. Wizards and mercenaries? Against the Daedric hordes? Without the Ebonheart Pact, they do not stand a chance!

The philosophy, the religious point of view for most of my people. We hold the forest sacred, and the Pact forbids us from harming plants and trees. It can be somewhat inconvenient to stay true to our faith. But we manage.
Yes. It is forbidden for us to harm the forest by direct action. But for a non-believer, an outsider to clear the trees? Especially for the benefit of the faithful … that is fine.

Yes, of course. Before Pircalmo came to town, we were going to hire some Khajiit from Rawl'kha to do the work. But when he and Alanya arrived, he asked if there was any service he could provide. So we took him up on his offer.
That's more than I'm getting from them. What do you suggest?
I don't doubt their commitment or their bravery, but they are few and Molag Bal's followers are legion.
Is there? What did you have in mind?
Hmm. Perhaps. But we don't know enough about Coldharbour to fully understand what they'd be up against.

In a chamber called the "Guardian's Orbit." My notes don't relate an exact location, but there can't be many unexplored structures remaining.\n\nMy crew and I have got our hands full, so you'll have to do some exploring on your own.
I'm just not sure. The Volenfell texts never hinted the Orbit could react like that.\n\nPerhaps when I can move again we'll survey the effects of that explosion.

You'll find them? Aren't you sweet. Let me think.\n\nI remember the Thane said it was too dangerous to drink and duel. He said I should destroy them. But I couldn't do it. So I hid them, near the old mill. Please don't tell the Thane.
I do a little bit of everything. I enjoy new experiences.\n\nLast week's was marriage. This week was divorce, then Dwemer ruins. Both will hopefully lead to considerable fortune.
Is that <<1>> the innkeeper? He's an upstanding citizen!
The spirits are unsure of your cause. The Wood Elves of Bramblebreach avoid war at any cost. You will have to assure them your enemies are worth allying against.

Oh, there's far less glamorous work to be done in <<1>>, at the northern end of the island. Let's meet up there, after you've done what you decide to do. \n\nUntil then, Bright Moons guide your steps.

Karinith told you how the hurricane dashed the fleet into <<1>>. Now the Sea Vipers are picking at the bones of our ships. Strange, yes?\n\nYou could scout the coast, as the commander said. Prove yourself to the soldiers.
What? No, impossible.\n\nWe've had disappearances recently, but <<1>> sending travelers to their doom? This is unthinkable. He didn't give you any trouble, did he?
How to explain this …. He is many things. \n\nThe tall rocks and trees around the village, do you imagine they would care if they fell upon us? Could they care?
Oh, no no no. Not at all. Ranneth has been a dear to me, and Pircalmo told me all about this hostage thing. He says it's just a formality, that I don't have anything to worry about. So I'm not!

Not much. At least, not much that I know of. I was a captive in a place called the Grotto of Depravity, a cave to the southwest of here.\n\nI escaped, but I wasn't able to retrieve my prized lute, F'lah. I feel so lost without it.

This contraption resembles the device I was imprisoned in. It draws life force from the imprisoned creature to power the Shackle.\n\nIf we can reverse the flow of energy, we should be able to return the stolen life force to that poor creature.

I'm fine. I need a drink and I miss Gamirth terribly, but otherwise I'm fine. Just a little shaken up.\n\nGamirth always said that there was something strange about that Thane. I'm just glad my father wasn't injured.
I believe that the other conduits are located on the walkway above us. The passage on the other side of the chamber looks like it might lead upstairs.
Oh, it's happened before—an unrelated incident—luckily, I had a supply of water and salt nearby.\n\nLost a lot of fluid, but I lost the poison, too.
I am going to finish my examination of this device, of course. Then I'll determine what our next move must be.

I got separated from my troop and a group of bloodfiends chased me. I hid in the entrance to a tomb, just to the west of here.\n\nIf not for my injuries, I would have explored the place. I'm sure there's some fabulous treasures buried inside.

An outsider with an open mind!\n\nThe Wilderking's nature is like the rocks and trees. He does not understand pain or suffering. And yet he is just and kind. I knew this to be true the moment I saw him.

How can you know? Have you spoken to a rock?\n\nThe Wilderking's nature is like the rocks and trees. He does not understand pain or suffering. And yet he is just and kind. I knew this to be true the moment I saw him.

When I was a child, yes. My grandmother was among the first Bosmer to come to Bramblebreach. This was long before the Aldmeri Dominion and the High Elf city of stone.\n\nThe Wilderking built this village for our ancestors.
Exactly!

He reminded her of a terrible but distant storm. A thing of great beauty capable of frightening devastation.\n\nShe said he could lift the ground into a hill or pull a full grown tree out of a seed. He did all of this easily.

Among the original tribe who came here, my grandmother lived the longest. The night she died I saw him standing among the trees. \n\nHer tribe were his first friends, I think. It seemed like he wanted to mourn, but he didn't know how.

Long ago there was a war in this part of Valenwood. There are many forgotten stories about that war, but a massive wall of brambles was raised around what is now the Wilderking's Court.\n\nThis village was the only opening into the court.

It has been many, many years. I was a child.\n\nHe was very tall with a slender, handsome face. His crown is what I remember the most. Knotted branches that rose above. And alive. He wore a living crown.
Let me see … there are several mentions of air. Hot air? Steam.\n\nIt's a direct translation, so we could be talking about steam exhaust, volcanic steam … bath steam. Just be careful!
That's easy enough. Torchbugs flock to the grove, here. Just snatch them out of the air. The Green is generous with her bounty, and if they have to give their lives … so be it.

Oh, Heartwood? Any of our grown homes should have some. When the Greenspeakers shape trees into houses, it often leaves behind wilted and useless heartwood. We keep them as decoration, but no one would mind getting rid of it.
Hmm. Sarolion should have some. He's a merchant. Travels all about Valenwood, but always returns home to us here in Willowgrove. He usually has some chitin from his travels to the southern wood.
A light ale. Unlike the other ales I brew, this contains no meat. I use very special ingredients for this.

I… feel these were his gifts. I don't know how else to explain it. \n\nI was napping under a tree one day a few years ago. I had a dream about this delicious ale. When I woke I found the grain, seeds, and fruit in the basket I brought with me.

Sugar. A type of grain carried on the wind. Seed cones, also blown here on the wind. And a peel from a fallen bitter tasting fruit.\n\nIf these weren't gifts from the Wilderking, I'm not sure I'd ever combine them into an ale.

Invisible fish. Shimmering sap makes things barely visible. I picked up a fish from the pond, covered it in the sap, and then tossed it back in. The sap washed off and the fish appeared.\n\nI bet him he couldn't find another one. I'm a bad sister.
A guardian. They will protect the village. The Wilderking provided the husks and taught the first villagers how to bring them to life.\n\nThere, it shook. That's laughter. It must be!

He was the King of Daggerfall during the Siege of Orsinium. The embers of the Orcish hold had not even cooled before he took up arms against our ancestors—his former allies. He was slain by a heroic Sword Singer at the Battle of Bangkorai Pass.
What an excellent idea! You can count on my help. I'll go find Vanus and prepare myself for battle.
You must slay the perfidious spirits of King Joile's Breton army—then King Joile himself, I suspect. Tu'whacca shall be watching.

To teach <<1>> a lesson! He claims to know all about lizards and running a race track.\n\nHe knows no more about either than I do about flying! But together, we could make this the best track around, if he cuts me a deal.

To teach <<1>> a lesson! He claims to know all about lizards and running a race track.\n\nHe knows no more about either than I do about flying! But together, we could make this the best track around, if he cuts me a deal.
And I need to bust some heads, so I'm going to help you with your mission. I'll find Vanus and ready myself for battle.
Not always. They used to race dunerippers here, but that proved too dangerous. <<1>> bought the place when the last owner died.\n\n<<2>> was none too pleased by that.
It's better than wasting away inside some town's walls. I've a taste for adventure, and this is as close as I'll get to any.
Not openly, no. But <<1>> refuses to race her own lizards, which makes <<2>> angry, and that in turn makes her less likely to do so.\n\nFire and ice, they are. They ought to get married.

Since Second Seed. The races were interesting when he first started, but the best lizard died, and without <<1>>'s help, no one will sell <<2>> good stock.\n\nStill, I've made a lot of money. I lose sometimes, but I win more than I lose.
No. He was annoying me. I suggested we play a game, where he hides and I find him.\n\nI'm currently winning.
Undoubtedly, but I suspect the attack at the docks was merely a feint. \n\nI fear the Withered Hand is planning something far worse.

General Thoda is my chief military advisor. He is also a practical man who places security above superstition. \n\nHe is resting at home after returning from abroad, but I need his counsel on how to proceed.

Yes. That is likely. General Thoda is my chief military advisor. He is also a practical man who places security above superstition. \n\nHe is resting at his home after returning from Alcaire, but I need his counsel on how to proceed.
Ha! A counterattack? I'd settle for an organized defense.\n\nOur forces are scattered too thin. If we can't hold the gates, <<1>> will fall to the Maormer.

I'll coordinate Dominion forces from here, but I can't lock down this gate until the survivors clear out of the market. Send them my way. We need everyone able to defend <<1>> on this side of the wall.
No. A little weary, perhaps, but not injured. My mind remains sharp, however. I suggest we make our escape from this place. It is the only tactically sound option at our disposal.
The oldest son in my family is always a warrior, and so I came to study with the best!\n\nBut all this reading … I'm not good at memorizing these words.
Cast the ritual! I've got everything ready here. Double-checked, just to be sure. Just needed those components you gathered and … yes! Ready to go! I'll just get started.

Ah … you noticed them. Well, that's true. I intended to summon up just a simple magical force to clear the trees. My people, we don't make pacts with Daedra. You know. Hmm … but something went wrong. Very … very wrong.

What? You, too?\n\nWait a minute, they've been having me on, haven't they? And I've been spending all my time trying to find these lists! Next one who asks me, I'll show them what I learned in hand-to-hand combat training!
Yes and no. I understand what they mean, but sometimes another student will stop me and demand I recite the Ten Aphorisms of Akatosh, or the Six Symbols of Sep, and then I'm lost.
Wonderful! Save some eggs for <<1>>, yes? They are so very tasty!
I need to link the spell with the Atronachs. Cores … destroy the creatures, and get me a core of each element type. And … agh … hurry!

May I see that? This … this is my great-grandmother's instrument. She was one of the greatest bards of the frontier in her day. It's said she performed for kings and queens, and always had time for the common folk alike.
Playing with the ants. I build them little houses, give them jobs, and introduce them to each other so they make ant babies. You know, stuff like that.

Yes, she was interred there. She led you there herself? Then perhaps she meant for me to have this. I'm a musician as well, actually. My mother's stories about Valencia inspired me when I was a child. Lately it's been hard ….
Take this wand. I … borrowed it from Master Telenger before I left the Guild. You can use it to pinpoint the source of the corruption. I have to go after Ranneth. I have to save my wife!
Of course! What can I tell you?
He's a pain in my furry butt, that's what he is. He's the Daedric Prince of deals. Make a wish, seal a pact, and he'll be there to grant you all the power you want. For a price, obviously.
Vile and I have a … complicated relationship. How can I explain it to you? Uh … oh, I'm a dog right? He put me in the dog house. Won't let me home unless somebody else lets me out.
That's kind of a rude question, isn't it? I'm a dog. Look at my snuggly fur and cute wiggling tail! I'm adorable!

It won't be easy. The enchantments that once kept evil out are now corrupted—it's something similar to the blight we saw in Verrant Morass, but much stronger. \n\nEvery soldier who's entered has turned feral. Even you and I would not be immune.
I do not know. My sight is weakened, and my presence is tied to my ward. They have taken it far from here … that is why I am fading ….\n\nFind the wards. Bring them back. Tu'whacca be with you.

I don't really know. I guess there was some kind of cult here in the March, a long time ago? Or maybe it represents the site of some kind of important pact. Even Vile's forgotten about this old place, now.

It's risky, but to defeat the darkness, we may have to embrace it first.\n\nThe Green is corrupted, and I think I can use my connection with it to thrust us into the realm of the Shadow Wood. In that realm, I suspect we can get past the blight.
That's excellent news! The poor dear really isn't cut out for taking care of herself. She depends on me for everything, you know.
You are mortal. You began to die the moment you were born. You are not fully dead. Not yet. Your song has only just begun, and many verses still lay before you.
Those present when you shattered the light were under my protection. They gather in the room beneath us, saying their farewells.\n\nThose who were not a part of the final battle? I cannot say.
The vortex has been destroyed. I designed this place to be familiar and calming to you. It is a small pocket of Oblivion, under my protection. No harm will come to you here.

Do you not see how singular you are? How remarkable? You entered the realm of a Daedric Prince, gathered an army strong enough to fight his legions, and saved your mortal world.\n\nYou are a valuable asset, mortal. You will be of great use to us.

There's only one way to find out, isn't there? If we go feral, that's that.\n\nIf not, I still suspect we'll encounter some resistance. The Shadow Wood hasn't lacked for corrupted spirits elsewhere, and I can't imagine it will here, either.

The one who runs this game, the Observer. He uses us as an amusement. He promises freedom and forgiveness. Lofty ambitions that are most certainly unattainable. Yet we continue to fight. It's either this or nonexistence.

What's to tell? It's an endless game of torture, a snare for any who walk into its grasp.\n\nThey promise us freedom if we win, yet none of us can seem to gain the upper hand. It's maddening! I fear we shall have to play forever and ever.

Hasn't the Observer explained things? He is the gamemaster. My associates and I, we're the contestants. We play to win our freedom.\n\nOf course, we need pawns to play the game. Luckily, the mages arrived just in time for the next match.
Do you think I had a choice? You are either naive or woefully ill informed.\n\nCome back and speak to me when you're ready to join my team.
What am I talking about? I'm talking about this game of war that we play, fool.\n\nOh, don't tell me you came here by accident? It never ends well for the stupid ones.
Fool, I don't expect to win you over with a smile and pretty words. I expect you to fight for me because of the power I wield.\n\nYou'll see. Just wait.
Thanks! Kireth and I will head for our camp outside the ruins. Meet us there after you find Lady Laurent and the artificer.

Lady Laurent, Telenger, and I decided to take advantage of our good fortune and explore this old library. The possible gain in knowledge far outweighed any risk involved. But as soon as we stepped inside, the spell started to take hold.

He was one of us.\n\nErthas was our leader when this community came together, during the formation of the Aldmeri Dominion. He voiced the dangers the rest of us saw in allying with the Altmeri and the Khajiiti, and convinced us to reject the Dominion.
What are we waiting for, then? Let's go!

Who can say for sure, when it comes to the servants of Daedric Princes?\n\nWanton destruction comes to mind. Look at what he's done to all that he helped build. He had us leave our people, and now he wants to burn us alive.

On the mission boards are posted Grand Warlord Zimmeron's orders for the Pact's soldiers. Without them, we are mudcrabs, scuttling along without direction. I supervise the Bounty and Scouting missions; General Jeggord directs the others.
Even the newly hatched can understand Bounty missions. The task is to kill enemy soldiers. All that lives must die; these missions hasten that day for our enemies.
Information is critical to our efforts. A Scouting mission sends you to a target deep in enemy territory.\n\nThe swamp eel sees but is not seen. Be the swamp eel. Then return here.
Thank you. I'm going to get out of here. I need to … find someone.

Well, let me see … we decided to take a look around this old library. I was sure there had to be a treasure or two to make it worth our while. Young Raynor became ensorcelled almost immediately and ran off.\n\nAfter that, things kind of get fuzzy.
The boards are where we post Grand Warlord Zimmeron's latest orders for the Pact. I supervise the Battle and Warfront missions; General Dar-Liurz takes care of the other missions.
A Warfront mission targets one of the enemy's keeps. Controlling keeps is the key to conquering Cyrodiil. This is a major effort though—go in without a large force and you're all going to die.

Battle missions send small groups of soldiers to capture enemy resources. Each keep is supported by a farm, lumbermill, and mine. Denying the enemy these resources is the first step to claiming that keep for the Pact.
The Transitus Shrine network is the fastest way to move among our keeps and gates, provided the links aren't broken.
A keep's transitus link is broken if all of its resources are owned by the enemy or if the keep is under attack and a section of wall or gate is heavily damaged.
The Mages Guild is dedicated to the pursuit of wisdom and knowledge. Worldly affairs hold no interest for us outside of academic curiosity. Interested in becoming a Docent?

Congratulations! This one grants the rank of Student in the Mages Guild, along with responsibilities and privileges thereof.\n\nEvery book acquired, or collection of books completed, now earns status among the Guild.

Docents find rare texts of all descriptions, so that Guild libraries may grow. \n\nIn exchange for this labor, access is given to purchase items restricted to guild members. Docents may also receive occasional special tasks….

Ah, yes! This one debated long over this subject with Tailstalker before he left.\n\nYou're well on the way to earning membership within the Mages Guild, just in bringing this here. The Guild provides great rewards for acquiring library texts!
I sense that the third ward is in the greatest peril of all. \n\nThe sibling of the necromancer who came here is far more skilled in the dark arts, far more dangerous, and far more ambitious.

Congratulations! This one grants the rank of Student in the Mages Guild, along with responsibilities and privileges thereof. \n\nEvery book acquired, or collection of books completed, now earns status among the Guild.
Docents earn reputation by bringing in rare texts for our library. As reputation grows… so too do the rewards.\n\nAre you interested in joining the Mages Guild?
Ashtad wants the dowry near the entrance where prospective grooms can inspect it. I'll send a guard down with a chest. Place the dowry in it.\n\nAll right, off you go.

Mannimarco and his vile master have dark and terrible plans for this world. If you wish to stop them, you need to find the Amulet of Kings. \n\nBut to find the amulet, you must first locate Sai Sahan.
Be quick about it. The game waits for no one.
Of course I do. And I might be willing to share that information … for a price.

If Mannimarco learns that we've spoken, he'll have me executed. I'm a danger to him. I know too much.\n\nTherefore I, Abnur Tharn, Chancellor of the Elder Council, Overlord of Nibenay, formally request asylum.
Do I look to be in a mirthful mood? \n\nThere comes a point when even a patriot's loyalty is stretched too far, when the things he has done—and has seen done—become too much to bear.

Would that I could. As it happens, I find myself to be somewhat of a prisoner, in dire need of rescue.\n\nMy proposal is this: If you retrieve me from Mannimarco's fortress and grant me asylum, I will give you Sai Sahan's location in return.

You can't. And you'd be a fool to trust me completely. \n\nBut the facts remain, you need me if you wish to find Sai Sahan, and I must keep my head if I am to ensure the continuance of the Empire. Neither of us has a choice.

We of the Mages Guild are dedicated to the pursuit of wisdom, of knowledge. \n\nPetty rivalry as is had here in Bergama holds no interest for us outside of academic curiosity. Are you interested in becoming a Docent?

Congratulations, sera! I hereby grant you the rank of Student in the Mages Guild, along with the responsibilities and privileges thereof. \n\nEvery book you acquire, or collection of books you help to complete, will now earn you a status among us.

Docents bring rare texts of all sorts to us, so that we may expand our libraries. \n\nIn exchange we offer them access to buy items which are restricted to guild members, as well as the occasional special task for those who are willing.

By the Three! I have been searching for this text for a long while….\n\nYou're well on your way to earning membership within the Mages Guild, just in discovering it. The Guild provides great rewards when a Docent acquires books for the library.

I hereby grant you the rank of Student in the Mages Guild, along with the responsibilities and privileges thereof. Congratulations are in order!\n\nEvery book you acquire, or collection of books you help to complete, will now earn you status among us.

Docents earn reputation by bringing in rare texts for study. And so as your reputation grows, so too do your rewards swell like the belly of a netch in the sun.\n\nAre you interested in joining the Mages Guild, sera?
Who will it be then?
We've been preparing the new recruits for the next anchor raid. \n\nGuildmaster Sees-All-Colors has issued orders to dismantle and disrupt the anchors whenever one comes to our attention.
Who will it be then?
Each type of siege weapon—trebuchet, ballista, and catapult—has unique abilities and uses.
Indeed not. Fire them to see. The trebuchet and ballista fire the farthest, while the catapult has a shorter range. Chagrin will visit those who forget this on the battlefield!

Trebuchets fling their missiles against keep walls, dealing great damage. There are three types—firepots launch burning oil, stones smash both walls and soldiers, and iceballs cause damage and ensnare enemies in ice.

Catapults are wonderful weapons against enemy troops. Meatbag catapults spread disease, oil imparts fire damage, and scatter-shot causes impact damage. I envy the death you will inflict among our foes with these weapons!

Ballistae are dear to my heart. They fire fast and true, destroying enemy siege engines, including rams. Standard ballista bolts smash their targets, firebolts cause extensive burn damage, and lightning bolts shock and ensnare their victims.
Who will it be then?
There's a vat on top of the platform. Use it as you would any other siege weapon.\n\nDon't pour it on me or this useless ram.

No. Some fool recruit broke our only ram, spoiling the fun for everyone. You can buy your own from siege merchants at gates and keeps.\n\nOnce you get out on the battlefield, you'll get plenty of chances to use rams.

Truly, you are here in Bergama and just now hearing of them?\n\nI'm speaking of the huge anchored chains which erupt from the skies and spear down into the ground! Everywhere around them, the Daedra gather to slaughter all who come near.
Welcome to the guild, Associate! \n\nIt is a fair day when we receive such as you instead of oafs like the steward in Kozanset. I see many rewards and special assignments in your future.
Of course! We need seasoned fighters like you if we're to wipe out these Daedra. \n\nThe combined might of my people is legendary, but we have no storied sword-saints to protect us here.
Have you? How disappointing.\n\nYour choices remain the same, sweetling.
You need to know how to repair walls, doors, and siege engines. Our enemies will batter at our keeps while we bash at theirs. Siege weapons can be damaged too. All this can be repaired.

Killing the attackers is a good start. Then repair kits can fix some of the damage. Here's a practice repair kit for a siege weapon. Use it on a trebuchet, catapult, or ballista.\n\nWhen you're done, Galsi wants to talk to you.
Be careful with these. We don't have an unlimited supply!
I hope they come to their senses soon. We're going to lose the element of surprise.
And you're doing a smashing job of it! Jolly good!\n\nWait a moment. Did you go through that portal? Did you meet the Observer?
Brilliant! Just great! Truly! I wish I'd thought of it.\n\nOff with you, then. I'll make sure everyone arrives safe and relatively sound in the Hollow City.

Jolly good! I've always wanted to play the Observer's game. But now that you've done it, I suppose there's no point, is there? I'm sure I'll find some other quest to occupy my time.\n\nSo, where were we? Why did I come here, again?

You can buy them from siege merchants at our gates and keeps. They can tell you the best ways to place siege engines on the battlefield.\n\nI know how to repair siege weapons, but Looks-Forward and Lirtis can tell you much more.
Killing the attackers is a good start. Then repair kits can fix some of the damage. Here's a practice repair kit; use it on a siege weapon here.
I have an ill feeling about this.
With very good reason! But the sooner they come to an agreement—\n\nDoes the air feel strange to you? That's odd. All of a sudden it feels like a storm is approaching.

The temples are holy places, created as housing for the scrolls, to honor and protect them. We built them upon the soil of Cyrodiil, close enough to the battlefields to bestow their blessings upon our troops.

The Grand Warlord orders these attacks. Access to each scroll is blocked by a gate. To unlock it, both keeps protecting it must be taken away from the alliance that holds the scroll. Once the keeps are captured, the way to the temple is open.
The scrolls contain records of all past and future events, but they cannot be read without blindness, madness, or worse!\n\nThe Aedra created them, some say, but why or when is unknown.
It is our destiny to control all the scrolls. Every Elder Scroll we hold grants power to all the soldiers of the Pact. This is another reason our enemies cannot be allowed to keep any of them.

The Elder Scroll must be taken from its temple and brought to one of our six original keeps. Once there, it must be placed upon a scroll pedestal. Needless to say, capturing an Elder Scroll requires the cooperation of many soldiers.
Books in this temple contain information about the Elder Scrolls, if you wish to know more.\n\nGrand Warlord Zimmeron needs to speak with you when you're done here.

All Pact soldiers should covet the Elder Scrolls. It is our destiny to control them all!\n\nThe simplest understanding of the Elder Scrolls is that they are prophecies. But they are so much more than that.

The Grand Warlord orders these attacks. Access to each scroll is blocked by a gate. To unlock it, both keeps protecting it must be taken away from the alliance that holds the scroll. Once the keeps are captured, the way to the temple is open.

The temples are holy places, created as housing for the scrolls, to honor and protect them. We built them upon the soil of Cyrodiil, close enough to the battlefields to bestow their blessings upon our troops.
The scrolls contain records of all past and future events, but they cannot be read without blindness, madness, or worse!\n\nThe Aedra created them, some say, but why or when is unknown.

It is our sacred duty to gather and protect the scrolls. Every Elder Scroll we hold grants power to all the soldiers of the Pact. This is another reason our enemies cannot be allowed to keep any of them.

The Elder Scroll must be taken from its temple and brought to one of our six original keeps. Once there, it must be placed upon a scroll pedestal. Needless to say, capturing an Elder Scroll requires the cooperation of many soldiers.
Then you know nothing! A thousand curses on this wretched island. They've taken my beloved!

The Pact is destined to rule Cyrodiil. Each keep and resource we conquer is a step toward this goal.\n\nYour participation in these actions enables you to acquire equipment and weapons from Pact siege merchants.

None who'll survive the day. I am the unerring bolt. Once loosed, I cannot stop 'til I pierce my quarry's eye.\n\n<<1>> knows her own city. If she won't tell you who did this, I'll shorten her tail until she does. Now go. Go!
Dead? But he was just here! What happened?

My guards saw nothing. We doubled the watch to ensure safety!\n\nI cannot abide <<c:1>>'s murder in my town. I'll shut down the port if I have to. None set sail until his killer is brought to justice!
How awful. Who would harm such a peaceful creature?
On my desk you will find the most recent reports from the <<1>> Guard. You are welcome to review them for any inconsistencies that could lead to the killer's capture.
Of course. I hereby declare you a deputy of the <<1>> Guard. No door shall be barred to you.
Of course! After all you have done for us here, it would be rude of Raz to say no.

We challenge the Maormer head on.\n\nMy scouts tell me the magical storms are menacing up ahead. Their source must be close. Head deeper into the island, investigate the spell the Maormer wizards are casting and stop it if you can.

They attacked at night. It was chaos. I saw Igarri get hit, helped her in here. I went back out, to help others. Cultists and Dremora everywhere. Leg got slashed, barely made it back. I couldn't help anyone, just listened to them scream.
I don't know. A spell, from one of those cursed cultists. We don't know how to treat him. He's dying, I see him slipping away every hour. And there's nothing I can do about it.

He's doing all he can, but he's just a village healer. This…this is beyond him. Not just Hrolvir, but everything. Magicka-inflicted wounds, infected bites from the undead, Dremora-cursed lesions—who can heal these?
You don't know?\n\nWhile King Aeradan rules over the people of Valenwood, <<Ac:1>> looks after our spirits. Together with <<Ac:2>>, we can see our true potential!
Strange. Why would farmers need alchemical tools?
If <<Ac:1>> is our spirit, <<Ac:2>> is our strength! She is unequalled in physical prowess and a master of martial disciplines. If we were all so strong, nothing could stand in our way!

If those same winds spare me? It is not wise, stranger, to think beyond the ordeals the gods set before us each day. This day, I face my death. If the gods will that I survive, I will face tomorrow's ordeals when they arrive.
Yes, indeed it does. It is a story of jealousy and betrayal. Have you not heard the ballad of Navid?

Know you not that the gods' breath is the wind that blows us all along our paths? All that has befallen us, and all that shall befall us to the end of our days, these things are the will of the gods. I pray that they have mercy on Bruma.
He'd already gotten a gang of his own bully-boys into the crew, and he bought some of the others. The opposition was shouted down or chased off.

In the early days of the Ra Gada, a powerful Ansei named Yaghoub led a vanguard of thirteen great warriors—Sword Singers all. In those days, Redguard bonds of fellowship were even stronger than they are now. These men were as brothers.

One of the warriors, Navid, was strong but covetous. His dearest companion, Ihlqub, had met a woman named Sayeedeh whose beauty was legendary—hair like polished obsidian and eyes like darkest sapphires. Navid's jealousy grew and grew.

Yes. Just so. While Ihlqub stood on the beach stringing his legendary bow, Navid crept up behind and thrust his sword deep into Ihlqub's back. Before Ihlqub died it is said that he looked on Navid with such sadness that Navid's heart broke in two.

Wracked with guilt, Navid fled to his tent, took up his grandest blade, and killed himself. When Sayeedeh heard of what happened, she threw herself into the water from the highest cliff.\n\nShe was not seen again.
In ja-Kha'jay we find ourselves. Our place in the world. Our path through its trials. In following this path, we find the sugar hiding all around us, and we are happy, yes? So very happy!

He reported what he'd heard, but the general dismissed it and sent him on another mission. The pirates raided Tava's Blessing and killed <<1>>'s family.\n\nHe swore revenge and went rogue. Who could blame him?

Do I look like a deep thinker? He makes the plans, I just follow orders. At least the boss lets us frighten off new milk-drinkers from joining the others. That can be fun. \n\nWait, you are one of us, right?
And if you find out, maybe then I can decide what to do. Thank you, I accept your offer. \n\nJust be discreet about it. I don't want any fights breaking out.

We've served as the first line of defense against Molag Bal's invaders, destroying his Dark Anchors all across Tamriel. They've succeeded in reducing their ranks and leveling half of Cyrodiil. What do you think?

Willing and able. But, like the Mages Guild, we are constrained by a non-interference pact. \n\nThe alliances will only tolerate our presence in their realms if we remain neutral. Unless all three alliance leaders consent to it, our hands are bound.
Even if we can get them to stop bickering, they'll never agree to send troops to Coldharbour. That would leave Cyrodiil unprotected.
An interesting idea, but they need to stop bickering long enough to consider it. \n\nWhy don't you visit each of them in their camps? See if you can reason with them individually.
You could stand a little farther away. You don't look very clean and I need to keep dirt from getting into my wounds. Which I'm going to die of anyway.
Yes. We sparred earlier. He lost badly. He claimed he was tired.\n\nI think I heard him crying a moment ago.
Hjorik doesn't know any better. I can feel my organs shutting down, one after another. I think my brain is going next, so I need to stop talking. Please let me die in peace.

This one thanks you for your concern, but there are others worse off. It is right that Hjorik tends to the seriously wounded first. A Khajiit learns to bear wounds with courage, until the insult can be returned a thousandfold upon one's enemies.
I can't wait to see Molag Grunda's face when she sees us. She and I go way back, you know. \n\nOnce we get inside, we cross one little bridge to reach the gatehouse. Follow me!

From Grunda? Rudeness, hostility, sarcasm, and most certainly a large amount of open hostility.\n\nI've no idea how she keeps house, but I imagine we'll find the usual Daedric touches that make Coldharbour feel so warm and inviting.
This one will survive. Soon, our foes will discover that not all in Bruma have been declawed!
I'll get you back in.
Let's get you back in there.
It seems like forever. I lost track of the days. The wounded never stop coming, no matter how hard we work. I just can't do it anymore.
We are neutral in the war for Cyrodiil. And proud of it. That doesn't mean we don't take an interest when the Hidden Armigers notice something.
We are neutral in the war for Cyrodiil. And proud of it. That doesn't mean we don't take an interest when the Ring of Daggers notices something.
We are neutral in the war for Cyrodiil. And proud of it. That doesn't mean we don't take an interest when the Eyes of the Queen notice something.

The intelligence arm of the Ebonheart Pact. Rumor is that they used to be an alchemy group from within House Telvanni who jumped ship. Now they answer to King Jorunn personally, and the Eight only knows what they get up to.

The intelligence arm of the Daggerfall Covenant. They enforce economic and political issues for King Emeric. My understanding is that the leader, a woman named Copper, got the position when she called in some kind of marker from His Majesty.
The intelligence arm of the Aldmeri Dominion. Personally loyal to her Majesty Queen Ayrenn. My understanding is that many of their members used to adventure with Her Highness during her wild days.
The Mistress of Incunabula for the Guild, the Keeper of Tomes. She's the guild's most accomplished loremaster, second only really to Guildmaster Vanus himself.

I don't, but she usually tries to offer new guildmates a chance to prove themselves.  As you might imagine, she's keenly interested in acquiring new books for the lore library. Maybe she's got a lead on a trove of tomes?

New members are the lifeblood of the Mages Guild. Especially for retrieval missions. \n\nI've received word about a possible store of ancient knowledge in a ruin nearby. I'd like you to retrieve it for me.
West of here, on the coast near Ash Mountain, lies a Dwemer ruin. The <<1>>. If you please, investigate the ruin and bring back any interesting books you can find.
Along the coast to the north lies the Ayleid ruin known as <<1>>.\n\nIf you please, investigate the ruin and bring back any interesting books you can find.
To the north of the city lies the ruin known as Ondil. If you please, investigate the ruin and bring back any interesting books you can find.

The spellwrights of the First Era used a special ink that would remain invisible until immersed in arcane fire. Perhaps that's what he meant?\n\nWe have a brazier nearby burning with such a fire. Let's see what the flames reveal.
Then <<1>> has much to learn. That he knew <<2>>'s corruption must end with death is enough for now.\n\nYour success goads him to improve his technique. In time, he will honor his ancestors.
A Daedric Prince, you say? Raz has a nose for lies, but you seem clean as an ocean breeze. Hmm. If anyone else asks you … where will you say you came from?
My, my. You're a focused one, aren't you? It is good to be focused. But it is also good, right now, to fit in. Your sudden arrival? It does not fit in. You understand?
Yes, lie with confidence! A straight face, and a gleam in your eye. Well done!\n\nIt is very good right now to fit in. Your sudden arrival? It does not fit in, you understand?

You should not! You should trust your instincts. Leave if you wish! No one will stop you. \n\nOr, come with Raz and do what you can to help us recover. In the process, grow your stature and wealth. It is entirely up to you.
Did you run into the Dremora? Did you make them suffer for what they did to this one … to poor <<1>>?\n\nAhirunz hopes that you killed many of the unclawed dung sacks.

From where? The Dominion controls Fort Dragonclaw, the nearest stronghold, but no help will come from there. The Aldmeri are too busy fending off assaults from the other alliances to spare any troops for a place like Bruma.

From where? The Covenant controls Fort Dragonclaw, the nearest stronghold, but no help will come from there. They are too busy fending off assaults from the other alliances to spare any troops for a place like Bruma.

From where? The Pact controls Fort Dragonclaw, the nearest stronghold, but no help will come from there. They are too busy fending off assaults from the other alliances to spare any troops for a place like Bruma.
We were attacked by  <<1>> and his monsters as soon as we set foot in the cave. This one and poor <<2>> fought our way out and eventually escaped into the wastes.
This one's beloved <<1>> was wounded in the escape. She died before we could reach safety and find a healer.\n\nThis one's claws will never be sharp again!

I don't see any. Go to the Manor House if you want hope. Grigerda keeps sending out messengers on fools' errands. None have ever returned. We have a full dose of reality over here; there's no room for hope.

I don't see any. Go to the Manor House if you want hope. Grigerda keeps sending out messengers on fools' errands. None have ever returned. We have a full dose of reality over here; there's no room for hope.

I don't see any. Go to the Manor House if you want hope. Grigerda keeps sending out messengers on fools' errands. None have ever returned. We have a full dose of reality over here; there's no room for hope.
It's not out of choice. I have supplies due to arrive any day now, goods I've already paid for. I'll be ruined if I leave before I get them. Then I can leave this gods-forsaken place.

Fort Dragonclaw. It's the closest safe place. I'll stay there until these monsters are wiped out of Bruma. And if they never are, if the worst happens, then I'll find someplace else to go.\n\nMaybe Vlastarus or Cropsford. At least I'll be warmer there.

Bite your tongue! I can't think that way or I'll melt into a wailing puddle of despair, with everything I've lost already.\n\nNo, those supplies are on their way, I'm going to get them, then I'm out of here.
Perhaps, wayfarer. Though I deem most here are far more scared. Only a fool faces danger without fear. Unlike many, I remain to stare down my fear.
Though Bruma is not my home, I choose to abide, for reasons I will not share. I will not be frightened away by monsters howling outside my door. If they enter, they will face my sword.

Do you wonder at that, wayfarer? I left my home to escape a dreaded marriage. I came here to begin a new life, only to have death and despair descend upon me. And you arrive, with proof that others seek my death. Do you marvel at some fright?

I cannot continue to run. The gods have punished me for fleeing my fate. I will stand here, to live or die. I will not be frightened away by monsters howling outside my door. If they enter, they will face my sword.
Life can't be all fighting and death and pain. There must be some pleasure, even for a moment, or life isn't worth living. So I sit and read, in the brief leisure allotted to me.

With the Empire fallen, the Imperial City is a dread place. Death stalks the streets and no one is safe. I fled with the other refugees. We arrived here just as the attacks began. My companions died and I've been stuck here ever since.

That's because they're all illiterate peasants in this backwater village. I was raised in the Imperial City, where love of the arts throve. Around here, the "arts" consist of scrawling dirty sayings on walls. And misspelling most of the words.

Do you have a magical hammer that can beat sense into a Nord's thick skull? If not, then there's little you can do to help.\n\nKjakur needs to lie still long enough for his hip to heal. Then we can leave this place far behind.

Yes, and so should you. And anyone else with a speck of sense. Bruma is doomed. Anyone who stays is going to die. I don't know why Kjakur and the rest don't see this. If we all left together, we'd all be much safer. But we're leaving regardless.

My clan was destroyed. Erased from this existence. And the hand that orchestrated that destruction was Valkynaz Seris.\n\nHe thought my clan was a threat to his power. Whatever the right or wrong of it, Seris must pay for what he did.

You're new here, you don't understand. This is my home, those are my friends out there—the ones who're still alive anyway. I can't leave them to fight and die alone, not while there's hope of taking back Bruma.

Not you too. Look, I appreciate you bringing Dommy's gifts all this way, but don't take her side in this. I'm staying until this thing is over. Those are my friends out there and I'm not leaving them to face this alone.

Of course I do. I wouldn't keep Domitia here if I thought we couldn't beat them. Grigerda's sending out runners all the time. Some are bound to get through and bring back help. Then we'll wipe out the evil that's taken over Bruma.

Of course I do. I wouldn't keep Domitia here if I thought we couldn't beat them. Grigerda's sending out runners all the time. Some are bound to get through and bring back help. Then we'll wipe out the evil that's taken over Bruma.
Killing monsters! If that's not what you're here for, you'd better get inside with the rest of them.
I work better alone. No one wants to follow me into battle, for some reason. But I haven't met anything I can't handle by myself, so I'm happy out here.
And where else would I be? Good to see you again, friend. You get tired of Grigerda's yelling too? I tell you, it's a lot more peaceful out here, monsters and all.

No, I go into the church or manor to get food and to sleep. If Grigerda's awake, I usually go to the church; Hjorik's too busy to bother me much. Good advice for you, if you plan on sticking around here for a while.
Because this is where the monsters are. If we're going to win back Bruma, we need to be out here, fighting—not inside, cowering.
Where else would I be? As I said earlier, Bruma will be won or lost out here, not inside the church or manor. Let the wounded stay inside; the warriors are out here.

My soldiers and I will hunt the remaining lamias and ensure the path behind you is clear. We will reconvene with you when this is done.\n\nI should, perhaps, apologize, but I need you to serve as our spearhead for a while longer.
<The sailor appears to have died recently. His clothing has obvious burns, and his scorched pants appear to have fused with his legs.>
<This sailor seems to have died recently. A variety of puncture wounds mar the legs, and both feet were cleanly punctured through. It appears as though the sailor crawled here before she expired.>
<The sailor seems to have died very recently. Her torn shirt barely hides her lacerated chest. Vicious claw marks ripped her torso to shreds.>

Some say it once belonged to Magnus, the God of Magic himself—some say it was a gift, others say it was stolen, others believe it's a test.\n\nIt suppresses magic, and it seems Naemon is using it to subdue the wards.

I little understand it, but the Bosmer have described it to me as the center of Greenshade.\n\nAs Naemon is allowed to corrupt it, the forest will die. The Bosmer here would lose their homes and be forced to flee.

We are followers of the Green Pact, pledged to protect the forest from all harm. In exchange, the forest shapes itself to our needs.\n\nBut now, the forest has turned against us, stirring the senche to attack us, and driving us into hiding.
Overload them like you did the first. They will amplify the Maormer weather magic if left unchecked.\n\nThey undoubtedly plan to use them to summon a storm that would ravage Malabal Tor.
Overload them like you did the first. They will amplify the Maormer weather magic if left unchecked.\n\nThey undoubtedly plan to use them to summon a storm that would ravage Malabal Tor.

I'm innocent! Yes, I tried to leave shortly after the attack, but this isn't my fight. I am just a merchant who set up shop here to make a living. These Bosmer and their Green Pact have nothing to do with me!

A sailor on the Albatross. There was a mutiny. <<1>> captured us and forced us to set off the traps in this damned cave.\n\nWe fell, one by one. Some of us ran, but I haven't seen any other crew. Aside from <<2>>, I mean.
It is a pleasure to meet you. Can I help you with anything?
Ask what you want, but I think's obvious who did it. That Khajiit has always held our traditions in contempt.
Good thinking. Whatever we can do to speed this up. In fact, as soon as you find each keystone, bring it here before searching for the others.\n\nThat will help me puzzle this out more quickly.
This village is the only home I can remember. Since I am young and almost everything I know relates to this forest, everyone calls me Forest-Child.
I do a little of everything. I mostly help out with cooking and gathering. I'm not very good at fishing, but No-Fingers lets me tend the beasts sometimes.
Grand Warlord Dortene needs information to plan our strategy. A Scouting mission sends you deep into enemy territory. Find your target, scout around, then report back here.
Bounty missions are simple: Kill enemy soldiers.
Which one?
Grand Warlord Dortene needs information to plan our strategy. A Scouting mission sends you deep into enemy territory. Find your target, scout around, then report back here.
Bounty missions are simple: Kill enemy soldiers.

He's my trained monkey. Well, he's more than that. Full-fledged crewmonkey of the Albatross, we have him untie hard-to-reach knots in the rigging.\n\nWait, have you seen any of my crew? We can't be the only ones to escape the bloodbath in the cave.

Here, take this bag of dried fruit. Toss some at the disarming mechanism and <<1>> will do the rest. That little guy is the only way I made it through.\n\nYou two stay safe. I'll find the captain. We won't leave you to do this alone!
Our Bosmer friends are part of the Dominion, so that's all I need to know. Prehaps one day I will be able to join the Dominion ranks to help defend these lands.

After our city wound up in Coldharbour, everyone was scattered. I sought shelter in a cave. Big mistake.\n\nThe Dremora in there, they were having some kind of sick party. Forced me to play and play and play.
Which would you like to hear about?
The enemy's resource sites—farms, mines, and lumbermills—support their forts, enhancing their strength. Battle missions send groups of soldiers to capture resources and greatly weaken those forts.

In Warfront missions, the wrath of Diagna descends upon our foes. These attacks on enemy forts require large numbers of warriors. Prepare for great deeds and grave danger when you embark on a Warfront quest!
Transitus Shrines enable fast movement between forts we control, if there's an unbroken link between where you are and where you want to go.
A fort's transitus link is broken if all of its resources are owned by the enemy or if the fort is under attack and a section of wall or gate is heavily damaged.
It's what I do, quite honestly. \n\nWe should probably hurry it up. The entire castle is as bristly as a sack of sewing needles after all that noise.

After more years than I care to remember! They gave me short rest periods every few days, but they kept my lute so I wouldn't run away.\n\nEventually, I decided I couldn't take it anymore. I left poor F'lah behind and made my way back here.

As we speak, two of my guardians investigate rumored anchor sites. Merric and Aelif are the best the guild has to offer. Meet up with them in the hills west of Davon's Watch. You can proceed from there.

As we speak, two of my guardians investigate rumored anchor sites. Merric and Aelif are the best the guild has to offer. Meet up with them on the beach east of Vulkhel Guard. You can proceed from there.
It came from a place without hunger or suffering. A place where we live peacefully and without fear.\n\nIt's as unlike Valenwood as possible. But, to be honest, I'm not sure where it is.
Well. My family hosted travelers from a place called Gil-Var-Delle once. I'd like to see it with my own eyes.
As you say. There won't be an anchor here anytime soon, thanks to the two of us. I should be moving. We had word of another cell west of here, near Ebonheart.
As you say. There won't be an anchor here anytime soon, thanks to the two of us. I should be moving. We had word of another cell north of here, near Skywatch.
Yes, you've restored our harmony. We can't thank you enough.

You didn't recognize the Dremora from her projection? I think her name is Doshia. Quite full of herself, actually. \n\nHmm. This note mentions an "island tower." Aelif wonders if it speaks of Stonefang.

You didn't recognize the Dremora from her projection? I think her name is Doshia. Quite full of herself, actually. \n\nHmm. This note mentions an "island tower." Aelif wonders if it speaks of Buraniim.
It's an old Ayleid ruin. A tower on an island off the coast of Skywatch. Go, seek Merric there. Aelif will find our heroic Guildmaster and get additional blades.
Stonefang Cavern, beneath an old tower on the island just beyond Ebonheart. Go, seek Merric there. Aelif will find our heroic Guildmaster and get additional blades.

Crude construction, shaped by small fingers. Female Breton … perhaps Wood Elf. Colored from clay. This region, so more likely Wood Elf. Smells burnt, of cinders. Shaped near a wood-fire stove or kiln.

According to legend, the Dwemer built an artifact in Rkugamz called the Great Engine to restore their immortality.\n\nThe legends also say that the Aedra took great offense, and they modified the Engine to bestow a curse, instead.
Each weapon—trebuchet, ballista, catapult—has unique abilities.
No, warrior. The trebuchet and ballista strike from great distance, while the catapult has a shorter reach. Remember this when you assault an enemy fort.
Trebuchets deal massive damage to fort walls. There are three types—firepots spread burning oil, stones smash walls and foes alike, and iceballs cause damage and ensnare soldiers.
Catapults are the bane of enemy troops. Meatbag catapults spread disease, oil burns all it touches, and scatter-shot pummels its victims.

Ballistae excel at destroying enemy siege weapons, including rams. Standard ballista bolts smash their targets, firebolts cause extensive burn damage, and lightning bolts shock and ensnare their targets.
You need to know how to repair walls, doors, and siege engines. To hold onto our forts, we need to undo the damage our enemies inflict on them. Siege weapons can be repaired too.
First, kill the attackers! Then repair kits can fix some of the damage. Here's a practice repair kit; use it on a siege weapon.\n\nWhen you're done, go speak with Aurorelle.
Here's another. Try not to lose it.

The temples were made to honor the scrolls. We built them upon the soil of Cyrodiil, close enough to the battlefields to bestow their blessings upon our troops.\n\nAll members of the Covenant are welcome here.

The Grand Warlord orders these attacks. Access to each Elder Scroll is blocked by a gate. To unlock the gate, both forts protecting it must be taken from the alliance that holds the scroll. Once the forts are captured, the path to the temple is open.

The scrolls record all past and future events, but reading them causes blindness, madness, perhaps even death.\n\nWe do not know when they were created. Many believe they were crafted by the Aedra, for reasons unknown.
To Grand Warlord Dortene, the Elder Scrolls matter only because they bestow blessings upon all the soldiers of our alliance. But to me, the Elder Scrolls are sacred relics of value beyond measure.

The Elder Scroll has to be brought to one of our six original forts. Once there, it must be placed upon a scroll pedestal before it is truly ours. Needless to say, many warriors must work together to capture an Elder Scroll.

Books in this temple contain information about the scrolls, if you wish to know more.\n\nWhen you are done here, go speak with Grand Warlord Dortene. Anything else you need to know about the war, she can tell you.

Eyevea, it's called. In ages past, it was an island in the Summerset Isles. Set aside for mages from across Tamriel, Shalidor worked tirelessly to make it a sanctuary. And just barely escaped when Sheogorath claimed it.
A genuine pleasure. He has a fascinating view of history from a firsthand perspective!\n\nAnd his knowledge of the deeper mysteries is … well. I feel like an apprentice again.
He still won't tell me what happened. I gather that there was some kind of bargain between them, and Sheogorath came out the better.

My cousin, Nettira. She knows all about tombs and ancient ruins and things like that. She spotted the name on the tomb before we got separated. Said it was an old Dark Elf name. Mal Sorra's Tomb.\n\nTreasure and Dark Elf magic. I'd stake my name on it.

The Maormer fight as a unit. Like a crew loyal to their ship's captain, the Maormer will follow their commander's orders without hesitance.\n\nRemove the commander and they will fall into disarray, at least long enough for our strike to overwhelm them.
You'll know soon. Now, I tipped off the guards that the Artisan was in the bank, and here you are sneaking about. I advise you leave.
What kind of question is that? We have enemies. Their lands, riches, and strongholds must become ours. The Dominion and Covenant must be crushed and the Pact will rule Cyrodiil!
Cyrodiil is the heart of Tamriel. The alliance that controls Cyrodiil can strike in any direction, threatening the other heartlands. And that alliance will be the Ebonheart Pact!

This book holds a single passage only. The words for the next passage will appear once you have opened the book. Follow them. They will transport you to a point deeper into the labyrinth, then settle on the page and create another passage.
It's a Bosmer tradition where you steal something precious, and demand a boon for its return. A song for a spear, or a prime ox for a wife.

The Mages Guild. We're scholars dedicated to the pursuit of knowledge. Guild members seek out books, tomes, and ancient scrolls in their travels. We aid each other where we can, and provide magical support for any that would ask our help.
Yeah. The Guild doesn't care about wars, battlefields, or boundaries: just knowledge, study, and the acquisition of new tomes. Strange thing to say in this place, but it's true.

We can teach you special spells and abilities only available to members. And from time to time projects crop up for guildmembers with ambition. Who knows, you might attract the attention of Mistress Valaste or Guildmaster Vanus.

Sounds good. I hearby grant you membership in the Mages Guild, with all the responsibilities and privileges thereof. Every book you find, and every book collection you complete, will earn you reputation in the guild. May the Eight watch over you.
Aren't we all? But I wanted to do my part. Help with the war effort. Get to see a Daedric realm. It's certainly very different from Eastmarch!

The Fighters Guild! You should join up. Our new guildmaster is an Argonian, Sees-All-Colors. She has us all working to a singular purpose. We're hunting down the Daedra and their damned Anchors. Hard fights.

Enormous chains descend from the sky! A passage opens to Oblivion, and Daedra boil out to lay waste to the countryside. I don't know who started calling them Daedric Anchors, but Mauloch knows it fits.

Ha! Good question. We train our members in special techniques. And the higher-ups are always looking for motivated members to help with special projects. Colors herself might even have a task for you someday.
Then let me be the first to officially welcome you as a comrade in arms of the Fighters Guild! Get out there! And take the fight to the Daedra!

Oh, yes. For the Mages Guild. We're scholars by trade. Dedicated to the pursuit of knowledge. Members seek out books, tomes, and ancient scrolls in their travels. We aid each other as we can, and provide magical aid for any that would ask our help.

Yes, yes. That's right. We seek out new information, capture it in our libraries, and make copies for distribution across Tamriel. The Guild doesn't care about wars, battlefields, or boundaries: just knowledge and the acquisition of new tomes.

We teach members special spells and train in unique abilities. And from time to time projects crop up for guildmembers with insight and ambition. Who knows? You might attract the attention of Mistress Valaste or Guildmaster Vanus.

Great! I hearby grant you membership in the Mages Guild, with all the responsibilities and privileges thereof. Every book you find, and every book collection you complete, will earn you reputation in the guild. Well done!
Join us! The Fighters Guild! Our Guildmaster, Sees-All-Colors, has us all working to a singular purpose. We're hunting down the Daedra and their damned Anchors. Hard fights, and plenty of glory!

I have a job to do. They said they needed merchants. But I really want to get out of this stall and go bloody a Daedric nose or two!\n\nMaybe I'll close up shop and volunteer with the Fighters Guild. Maybe.
Yeah! Then let me welcome you as a comrade in arms of the Fighters Guild! Get out there! And take the fight to the Daedra!

Good question. We train our members in special techniques. And the higher-ups are always looking for members dripping in courage to help with special projects. Colors herself might even have a task for you someday.

Enormous chains that descend from the sky! Passages to Oblivion burst open, and Daedra boil out to lay waste to the countryside. I don't know who started calling them Daedric Anchors, but Mauloch knows it fits.
Mother Morrowind herself asked for volunteers. The effort in Coldharbour needed support, she told us. It was all rather inspiring. And here I am.\n\nRemind me never to get this inspired again.
Very much so! Unfortunately, there isn't much time for research. For one thing, I need to keep my store open. The mages are counting on me for supplies.
Wrong? Is a sky without moons wrong? Is a day without caramelized goat nibbles wrong?\n\nOh, this one cannot stop thinking about the enchanting Dark Elf with the fragrant odor!

Really? Does it show? One of the soldiers in the Fighters Guild has asked to buy me a drink at the tavern.\n\nHe's a Nord, but he doesn't seem anywhere near as loud or obnoxious as I was led to believe.
Nothing out of the ordinary for a lost city in Coldharbour. But I'm not one to engage in gossip. Perhaps you should try one of the other merchants, or maybe ask around in the tavern.
And with good reason! Someone left a dead skeever on my doorstep!\n\nIf I didn't know any better, I'd say it was that Khajiit blade merchant. She has been acting rather strange since we got here.
A portal. How did you get here?

We're in hostile territory, about to engage in the war to end all wars. How do you think business is going?\n\nLet's just say that I hope there's a world left to enjoy my profits in when all this is over.
The legend says that Meridia herself pushed this city into Coldharbour and placed spells around it to keep it safe from the Lord of Brutality.\n\nBut maybe he just doesn't want to.
Such dreadful creatures! I almost feel sorry for the poor things. But I heard that only the most evil people wind up in Coldharbour, so I guess I shouldn't feel too sorry for them.

You can buy siege weapons from a siege merchant at our entry gates or at forts we control. They can tell you how to use them in battle.\n\nI can tell you how to repair siege weapons, but Jaleel and Marc know more about the weapons themselves.
First, kill the attackers! Then repair kits can fix some of the damage. Here's a practice repair kit; use it on a siege weapon here.
They too easily believe their neighbors stole from them, and we've only just been able to prevent any violence. We must find those valuables.

As luck would have it, Mannimarco is away on some errand for the Daedric Prince. The castle garrison is not on alert, so you should only encounter a token defense.\n\nThe main gate is sealed, but there are undoubtedly other routes one might take.
You're the hero, aren't you? Improvise.
Wait until I am in position. \n\nThen you must undo the final binding stone. The High Kinlord will then emerge. Fight well—you fight for Tamriel's safety.

I would not entrust this task to an outsider. I will play host to the High Kinlord. His spirit will take over my body, but he will be bound by my mortality.\n\nIf I—we—are killed, Rilis will die. From there, it's straight to Oblivion for him.
The Whisperer was dead. The Guild pulled out because these ruins hold no tactical value. Most of us would like to forget everything that happened here. We lost a lot of good people.
And we're grateful. Without you, none of us would have survived. Now, it seems I'll be in you're debt, twice-over.
Come with you? You mean leave Coldharbour? Well, I don't know. It's been a very long time since I've seen the world I left behind.\n\nDo you think it's wise?
Well, that's settled, then. And after all, you do need someone to lead you out of here. \n\nOnward!

Well, that wouldn't do at all. And it's not so bad here, actually. Oblivion has its charms, doesn't it?\n\nGo on, you scamps. There's a grate just ahead that leads down to the rubbish tip. Do mind that first step, though!
Then drown in a sea of bones!

She did most of the hard work. I'll leave the explanation to her. Just know that Sheogorath is nowhere near as clever as he thinks. She was able to unravel his nonsense, and determine where you need to go. Hah!

The requirements for correcting a violation of the Green Pact are well established. Three kinds of proof are required for judgment: witness testimony, physical evidence, and a magical omen.\n\nWithout all three, no judgment can be rendered.

Only a gross violation of the Green Pact could cause the forest to attack us in this way.\n\nMy suspicions were confirmed when we entered this cave. We found the sacred blossom, Sanguine Alendil, cut from its stem. No wonder the forest is angry.

I've been able to narrow the suspects by talking to the villagers, but to gather more evidence, we'd need to leave this cave.\n\nFor as long as justice is denied under the Green Pact, the forest will destroy any of us who set foot outside this cave.

Many in the Rilis family have fallen to madness. It strikes at different points in their lives, but it seems inevitable.\n\nThe Daedra sometimes play a part, as they did with Rilis XII, but I suspect something more. It could be in their blood.

I warned them against their folly, and I did not partake in the pacts they made with the Daedra they contacted.\n\nBut they are enthralled now, and they serve Rilis. They will protect the binding stones with their lives, so be ready for a fight.
No idea. Word around the hall is that she's been working day and night on some mysterious project. I've even seen some Mages Guild scribes wandering around the place. Strange.

As you remember, Rilis attempted to escape. Though we contained him, he would have won, had you not been with us.\n\nAfterwards, the Keepers turned to the same Daedric magic that Rilis used, hoping to match his strength.

I warned them against this folly, and I did not partake in the pacts they made with whatever Daedra they contacted.\n\nBut they are enthralled now, and they serve Rilis. They will protect the binding stones with their lives, so be ready for a fight.

The captain's alive? Rajhin's luck, that's good news!\n\nListen, <<1>> is dead set on getting into <<Ac:2>>. If <<3>> sent you to find the crew, you'd better get there before that bloodthirsty bastard kills them all off.
Mannimarco keeps his most secret documents at Knife Ear Grotto in Deshaan, inside a hidden lair of Daedric cultists. We must travel there and search for clues.
Mannimarco keeps his most secret documents at Norvulk, a hidden lair of Daedric cultists in the Stormhaven countryside. We must travel there and search for clues.
Nope.

Let me see those papers … "Preservation Room?" Oh, no.\n\n<<1>> doesn't have enough mutineers to crew the Albatross. <<2>> said he kept going on about needing a "skeleton crew." I think he meant a crew literally made of skeletons.
Now, we address the practical applications of this marvelous elixir!\n\nIf you will help us one last time, I will increase your compensation.

It must be why he needs my wife. The writing on the back of <<1>>'s map was coded, except for the phrase "Preservation Ritual."\n\nThat must be it. Once she decodes the ritual, <<2>> will turn my crew into his undead minions.

If he hasn't already fallen to the undead, I want you to hold his attention while we slip by and free up some more of my crew.\n\nOh, <<1>> wanted to speak with you before you left. But if you just want to get moving, we'll see you inside <<Az:2>>.
The last we saw, <<1>> guarded the long hall into <<Az:2>>. If that crafty bastard sees me approach, he'll fall back and warn <<3>>. Then my wife dies.
Damned Daedra are everywhere. I saved Esan from being an ice sculpture, and in return he's proposed a bold plan. I think it might even get us out of this alive.
Well … the Fang's a little rusty. It sat in the dust for years. Esan's magic has tuned it, shaped it so that it can gather power from the Atronachs. We can repower the Fang.

When he saw the Daedra, Esan raided a vault at the temple. Kid after my own heart. He stole a fang relic and did something with it. Something magic. We can use it to seal the portals. I'm sure the priests wouldn't approve, but they're not here.

The old fashioned way! With claw and blade and spell. End the Atronachs while you hold the Fang, and their essence will be transferred into the relic. Once it's primed, it should be simple to seal the portal.
Smashing idea. Really excellent. They'll be safe there.\n\nHow about that thane? Excellent mead, certainly, but I always thought he was a bit dodgy.
Righto! Always happy to pitch in. Lend a hand. Steer a course. Make a difference.\n\nI'll get them to the Hollow City. Very nice inn there. Plenty of mead. They'll feel right at home.
One must choose one's battles, mustn't one? Rescuing maidens, fighting injustice—those are my specialities. But taking mead away from drunken Nords? I mean, really. That way lies madness.

This one has always enjoyed trying new and different things. But this situation? It is very strange, very awkward.\n\nIs that thought me-Zur or me-Gadris? This one can never be certain where his thoughts end and Gadris's begin. Very confusing, yes?
As well as can be expected. We all have our parts to do. That's why we came to this awful realm.\n\nAnd by Saint Veloth's massive hammer, we shall prevail!
Of course! But I brought a little bit of home along with me. I filled my pocket with snow before we left. Here, let me show ….\n\nWell, this is unfortunate.
A bold initiative. I just hope our troops are equal to the task.

What a silly question! That's like asking if I prefer food to water. Both are necessary to life as we know it.\n\nThat said, I always get a little thrill when I see a mage cast a spell. It's so exciting!
Pinning the blame on someone else? I won't fall for that! How do you explain those stolen goods you're carrying? Hmm?
An excellent idea I was just about to propose! Cinnar is on the upper city tier, near the entertainment pavilion.\n\nYou lead the way. I'm not so naive that I'd turn my back on a common criminal.
You know Cinnar? Well, this doesn't prove anything. You might have heard his name in relation to your own investigation!
You honestly expect me or Cinnar the investigator to believe that outrageous fabrication? I was not born yesterday! In fact, I was born two-hundred-forty-seven years ago!

She was <<1>>'s lover, but they had a falling out. They fought so much the captain had to put them on separate watches. She takes whatever side he doesn't, so she's no mutineer.\n\nBut <<2>> knows how he thinks. She might have insight that we don't.
Just making sure the stragglers get to the portal.\n\nBy the way, you impressed Skordo, which isn't an easy thing to do. Find him on the other side. He wants to talk to you.

He's a Nord who came aboard the Albatross with <<1>>, but made an oath of loyalty to the captain. He refused to join the mutiny when it happened. The two were "axe-brothers," or something like that, so <<2>> may have a sense of what comes next.

Place these squirmy, rodent-things in her backpack, in the corner. She'll be back shortly and then we'll see the fruits of our labor!\n\nTimiwe and I have a wager. He expects her to double over with laughter. I, well, I do not expect that reaction.

My associate and I have a mischievous nature. It is through this nature we show our affection for our friends. \n\nOur close friend Khalima is, as Timiwe would say, "a grumpy bug." We want to lift her spirits.

There is a reason for this. One I would prefer to forget. It involves an early experiment with my associate. An experiment that failed horribly.\n\nIt is not as simple as you may assume, however. When the two of us are involved, nothing is ever simple.

Guess we're allies. Never thought he'd be the type for gold-madness, but treasure chipped away at his honor. Said he was angry the captain wanted to buy our way into the Dominion, the liar.\n\nI laughed when he realized the treasure wasn't gold.

He always wanted to carve out his own empire. With these siege weapons and supplies, he thinks he can do it. But where's he going to get the soldiers to use them?\n\nHe's an oathbreaker and a fool. If you don't put him out of his misery, I will.
He picks a time like this to gossip? Yeah, I took a serpent to my breast. Should I be surprised it bit?\n\nDon't see why it concerns you.

Then hurry. There's a code on the back of the treasure map, and he's forcing the captain's wife to break it. Seems the undead in here can't truly die, so if he breaks the code they're his to command.\n\nWhen you kill him? Don't you dare make it gentle.
Most unexpected! It seems we have a mutual friend.\n\nMay I ask, what brings you to <<1>>?

Esan went to investigate the second portal near the Mages guildhall. He might have gone to talk to the other robe and book types. They're over in the merchant district, my friend. I'd like you to see if you can find him.
I wish. No, the Thalmor council wants me to report in. The Queen and Speaker Gharesh-ri want to know what's happening on the ground. Khali has your back, Hallowed.
Keep your claws sharp, my friend. And go carefully. This invasion smacks of desperation. Until now Tharn has stayed to the shadows. To openly invade Dune … he must have a plan.

Indeed. Why not?\n\nIt would be indecorous to suggest the treaty is anything but actual and sound, yet I fear it won't present itself without a more active line of inquiry. Would you be my voice in this with Ambassador <<1>> and Headwoman <<2>>?

Then perhaps you can advise me on a small matter. The Maormer have a treaty with <<1>>. This is nothing to fear; a treaty is something I can work with.\n\nYet neither Ambassador <<2>> nor Headwoman <<3>> will produce a copy.
Exactly. A chorus of requests may succeed in carrying the tune. <<1>> in particular seems eager to see this resolved, though I fear the Dominion presence binds her hands.\n\nBut I'll leave you to it!
Driladan Pass is just north of Marbruk. Last I heard, Bodring and most of the Rangers are defending Marbruk against a small army with the help of Mane Akkhuz-ri and Lord Gharesh-ri.
Vullain is an abandoned village with a dark history. Locals refer to it as Dread Vullain. There were reports of a hostile force occupying the village, and Nara went there to investigate.
It is an ancient Ayleid ruin in the center of this region. The spinners call it the heart of the forest. I worry that they speak the truth.
The leader of Blackheart's hags and harpy flocks. She wields great power and is able to conjure flames and travel great distances with her magic.\n\nJust … hmm. Kill her before she kills you.
You're most welcome.
<Your hand remains in place, clutching the books. A chill shoots through your body. The pain in your head blooms.>

The situation has … spiraled out of my control.\n\nNobody was supposed to find us. The lich said he would bring them back. That it would be over and done in a moment. But it's not. Everything's wrong. They … are wrong.
