My children died. So I made a deal with that lich to bring them back to life. But they came back wrong.\n\nThey've been building an army to overrun the city—raising other undead, recruiting necromancers. I thought I could keep them secret.
No. You're wrong. My children were law-abiding citizens—paragons of society! Those are monsters who came back in their stead!

I … you are right, of course. I'll help you. They must be … put down before anyone else dies. They're in a cave up ahead where the sewers run out to the sea. \n\nI'll meet you there. Try to draw them out. And when the time comes you … finish it.

The Wormie leader. Told him he'd have no use for the big bones in the ground with the Barrowbough to keep them sleeping.\n\nBut if he digs up the Barrowbough's roots, he'll kill it. Then he can build giant Wormie skeletons to stomp around.

Praise Y'ffre, someone who isn't going on about Argonian spies!\n\nLast year, this tribe arrived in <<1>> as refugees. But because we're all part of the Dominion now, my superiors can't decide what to do with them.
Here's a list of the tribe's leaders. I need to know why they refuse to speak with us. Unless my report says they're cooperating, my superiors have an excuse to exile them.

Absolutely not. This entire tribe was enslaved by Dark Elves. They have more reason to hate the Ebonheart Pact than you or I.\n\nBut someone in <<1>> decides to set an example, and now there are barricades. It's why I need outside help.

The night the Green Pact was broken there was a terrible storm. I was sitting by the window, watching the lightning. \n\nThat's when I saw that filthy cat sneak off into the woods, towards the cave. I will happily testify against him.
Spinner Eranas is our guiding light. He helped heal my cousin when she got sick and has always been a staunch defender of the Green Pact. It's offensive he's even under suspicion.

Gathiel has her moments of ego, but she's a loyal member of this community. We were all praying for her during her recent illness and were thrilled at her recovery. I don't think she's capable of this crime.
There are others like <<1>> sleeping beneath the Barrowbough. If they knew what the Wormies wanted, they'd help!\n\nBut we can't get there without <<2>>'s help, and she's not too happy with me.
She's up on the ridge overlooking <<Ac:1>>. Maybe I shouldn't go with you? No, that's silly, I'm sure she'll be happy to see me! \n\nBut just to be prudent, I'll let you do the talking.
I don't know. They can be fought and killed, but they replenish their ranks daily, as travelers continue to pass through.
The second blade in "Two-Blades" is my magic. I don't always get to put it to use, but I'd prefer not trying that again.\n\nThank you again. The day was won thanks to you.
You've met Haras? He's a legend among us Hounds! You must have made quite the impression.

Beyond this door waits the Great Mooring, which connects the Great Shackle from Coldharbour to Nirn.\n\nDefend me and I will use my considerable skills and power to destroy the Shackle and end the Planemeld, once again proving my magnificence.
Then it's over. There's no way the mutineers will fight without him. Toward the end, he frightened even his most loyal sailors.\n\nHave you seen <<1>>? Is she all right?

Oh yes. It's Coldharbour's most nefarious prison. The Daedra in the Halls of Torment reach deep into the dark places of a prisoner's mind and torture them with apparitions of the things they most dread.

Of course I can. I am Abnur Tharn!\n\nBut first, I have a bit more research to do. Go back to the Harborage and tell Varen what we've discovered. I'll meet you there once I've made the necessary preparations.

Thank the gods! If only I'd burned the cursed map to this place.\n\nBut perhaps there's something to salvage here. The Dominion will welcome a cave full of Imperial war supplies. That should be enough for a full pardon and a letter of marque.

You must know of our raids across the Long Coast? Well, that's behind us now. The treasure will wipe our debts clean so we can put our talents to use in the Queen's Own Navy.\n\nNow if you'll excuse me, I need to find my wife.
A legendary Hound. He's obsessed with this mythical Senche, and his hunting companions never return. I heard he was near Verrant Morass.
Yes, we received word that Daedra were attacking the temple district. There must be another portal there. Go, Hallowed. This Guild will guard this district from any further Daedric attack.
What? Esan dead? And the leaders of our hall corrupted. I can't believe this. That … dull-clawed bastard Tharn! I would rip his throat out with my teeth, were he here right now!
I determine the goals of the Dominion army in Cyrodiil. Vilya carries my orders to General Thoron and General Atahba, who post them on the mission boards. Speak with General Thoron to learn more.

Yes, their leader <<1>> made vague threats about me remaining inside. He's attempting to raise the old bones beneath the Barrowbough, but there's no way he'll do that before <<2>> sends a patrol, so I'm staying put.

What we first planned to do. Once we inventory the weapons and supplies in this cave, we'll present the list to the Thalmor. If they like what they see, they'll give us our amnesty and make us part of the Queen's Own Navy.
Not much. I heard them say they would bring me to "the Obsidian Husk" to bestow their blessing.\n\nNo clue what that is, but more of my captured Guildmates are up ahead. They may know more.

We were. But those days are over.\n\nI should have seen they never would be for <<1>>. The damnable thing is he was an excellent first mate. Up until the promise of treasure warped his mind, I suppose.

Those who planned it will hang. The rest who were forced into it? They can leave, unless my crew objects.\n\nI need to spend some time with <<1>>. Before you go, find <<2>>. He put something together for you. Our way of saying thanks.
General Atahba supervises the other missions. Speak with her to learn about them. She's on the other side of the gate.
Dug up? But that would take weeks. How did they manage?

Here, this is <<1>>. Head beneath the Barrowbough and sound the horn before the gate. It's the only way inside, unless you want to help the Worm Cult with their digging.\n\nAnd don't let <<2>> sneak off with that horn!
Why? Those old bones are useless to them. The Barrowbough shields them from necromancy.\n\nBut if they can dig up the Barrowbough's roots …. Oh no. They plan to turn the old bones into an army!
I'm happy to answer any questions you have, but I can tell you already that it was our Spinner.
Well, this "Husk" sounds fairly important. \n\nWhatever it is, it's waiting in that shrine up ahead. I would start there.
Wonderful!\n\nIf you simply hand me the skulls, I'll be able to reverse the effects of their preservation ritual.

Can't you see it? I … oh, right, the walls.\n\nThere's a lever around here that opens a secret passage. I don't remember where it is or I'd help you find it. I haven't needed to worry about walls in quite some time.

Oh, my. I keep forgetting. You're the one who seems ghostly to me, you see.\n\nYou'll need to do this, then. If you enter <<Ac:1>> you'll find their spirits locked into an echo of their final moments. Reuniting skull with spirit should do it.

He's an alchemist. He makes unnatural concoctions with plants. He claims to never use anything forbidden but everyone knows that alchemists need lots of herbs to do their work. I am willing to testify against him for bringing this down on us.
That merchant is harmless. He only gets what people ask him to acquire and I've never seem him harm a leaf. If it weren't for him, we'd be cut off from the rest of the world entirely.

I won't stand any badmouthing of Gathiel. Sure, she's married to the alchemist, but she's nothing like him, rooting around in the dirt for dead leaves.\n\nThe way she carries herself, her beauty, her refinement. She would never stoop so low.

You do have sharp claws! I have the lads hanging back. I don't think the priests would like mass bloodshed on temple grounds. We should make the tiles run red, though. They've defiled the shrines. Darkhearted bastards.

I don't see a portal so … I have to trust my instincts. Let's cleanse the shrines and let the bright moons shine down on this place. You see to the temples of Jone and Jode. The old shrine to Lorkhaj still stands. I'll take care of that one.

I'll be fine, Hallowed. That was some damned impressive work. Shazah would, I'm sure, say something about how momentous your actions have been today. I'm just glad I have a friend by my side. Especially for what must come next.

We pushed back the Daedra. You heard Tharn, he means to walk the Two-Moons Path himself. I can't … I can't put this off any longer. We need to make for the Temple of the Dance. Follow me. I'll lead the way.
Razum-dar is just a simple Khajiit. He seeks the best for all the people of Tamriel. Also, a saddle that won't pinch the tail. One day ….
Anything to fix this.

Aranak's been in our town for years, why would he suddenly decide to do this? \n\nBesides, the Pact is a special bond between the Wood Elves and the forest. I don't think the forest would react this way if Aranak were guilty.

Eranas is a good man. He's the village Spinner, so it's his job to pass on the stories of the Wood Elves and the Green. \n\nI learned about the Green Pact from his stories when I was a child. He would never endanger the village or break the Pact.

A real piece of work. Always scheming, that one is. Spinner's wife or not, I'm sure she's guilty.\n\nShe's been sick for weeks and just happens to get better the night the Pact was broken? I'd testify against her in a heartbeat.

Crouch low and look for traces of its passing. The timber mammoth is not a graceful creature, so you should be able to spot footprints, broken branches, matted grass, which will lead you right to the beast. \n\nKill it and bring its tusk to me.
Sure! We can do a hands-on lesson. I was hunting a timber mammoth, but lost its trail in the water. Let's see if you can track it down.
A legendary Hound. He's obsessed with this mythical Senche, but his hunting companions never return. I heard he was near Verrant Morass.
I see Haras wasn't wrong about you. Then again, they say he always had an eye for talent. Just one word of warning before you return.
Though Haras is a legendary hunter, he's equally infamous for the mortality rate of his hunting companions. Just be careful.
This one is a simple Khajiit, like he said when we first met. He resolves issues as they come up. He acts in the best interest of the Dominion and the Queen.

Very tall Elves and very pretty shores. Auridon is the most worldly part of the Summerset Isles, and still many of the High Elves consider it a sanctuary away from the rest of the world. This one thinks they are kidding themselves.
Oh, Raz would not be surprised. You have already proven yourself a competent sort. Simple Khajiit like this one have a tendency to need competent people like you.

Astanya's the lovely watch captain of the Vulkhel Guard Watch. Raz has shared more than one drink with the captain, and more than one fight. She's getting a bit grouchy now that she's tied to one port, but she should set you arights.
Hah! He's got an active imagination, that one. We know each other, sure. Drew blades together a few times. But I'm not sure I'd call him a friend. Not since he signed up with the Queen.
I've been studying the Two Moons Path since I was a child. I know much about the Moon Hallowed and their role in the choosing of the Mane. What would you like to know?

He didn't tell you? Of course he didn't, he's the biggest liar I know. Razum-dar works directly for the Queen herself. Some kind of hush-hush cloak-and-dagger outfit. Thieves and liars, the lot of them.
I'm sure it was some kind of test, to see if they could sneak something deadly past our security. Lucky we had you on the job!
I'm sure it was some kind of test, to see if they could sneak something deadly past our security. Lucky we had you on the job!
He is here to help, as always! You may have noticed your new friend Fasion lies dead on the ground behind you. Raz knew Fasion well. As he thought he did Astanya.

You must get past the captain's men. Seek out another of our lady's agents, Eshaba. She stands watch in the marketplace, peddling her wares.\n\nAsk her for a souvenir of the First Marines, and she will set you on your path.
The captain happened. Fasion and Raz worked together, as agents of the Queen. Fasion was not willing to give up secrets. And so now Fasion is dead.
You will soon be free. But as on the island, Raz must ask your aid. You must warn the Queen, and her battlereeve. The captain will attempt to murder the Queen at the temple.

Do you go around admitting your dark secrets to strangers? Raz knows you know how to keep a secret. This one's service to the Queen is an honor and a privilege. But not something he brags about in island bars.
The Ayleid King suffered grievous wounds. He is near death, but he has not passed yet.
For the nonce, we require nothing. But, the Dark Princes have taken notice of you, and they have plans, and plans within plans.\n\nPrepare yourself, and be ready when Oblivion calls.

A good question! Raz answers it with an interesting bit of trivia: <<1>> posted a guard at his quarters the day of the theft. His subtlety is rivaled only by his pleasant personality.\n\nOh, and it's five drinks for embassy staff. Six puts them out.

Someone needs to slip into Maormer embassy, find a way past the guard, and rifle through <<1>>'s private quarters. Oh, and do it without bloodshed that could provoke war with the Maormer.\n\nIn case he was not clear, Raz is talking about you.
A legendary Hound. He's obsessed with this mythical Senche, and his hunting companions often die. I heard he hunts in northern Greenshade.
I have done all I can for the Apprentice. Whether she lives or dies is up to her, now. The time I have to spare, I save for my sister, Bakkhara.\n\nLet us go.

Meridia's shield protected the others. Darien and I were outside the shield, dealing with Molag Bal's damn portals.\n\nI watched as light filled your body. You were a beacon. And the last thing I will ever see.
Then I shall … I shall rest well knowing my final day … the final day of the Ayleid people … was spent saving Nirn from the clutches of Molag Bal.\n\nAnd I … I ….

Darkness fills my eyes. As the light erupted around me, someone pushed me closer to Meridia's shield. It was too late to save me, but it did bring me here.\n\nMy fate doesn't matter. I'm gladdened by the thought that Nirn is safe.
Yes? What happened? Where am I?

And you have made a dire enemy for it.\n\nThis one was a wonderful prize. Full of arrogance and hubris. He thought he could succeed where Canonreeve Oraneth failed. One is dead. The other belongs to me, now.

You are an amusing creature. You think to threaten this one?\n\nThe Khajiit's mind will never be his again. Not fully. And this one will remember you. One day soon, this one will open you and devour your yolk.
You are amusing to make demands.\n\nThe Khajiit's mind will never be his again. Not fully. And this one will remember you. One day soon, this one will open you and devour your yolk.
Secrets are a Spinner's currency. Besides, this shrine contains … privileged information your dull mind would not comprehend.\n\nHave I made myself clear? Your services are no longer required.
How can you ask me that after what we've been through? Darien … the King … so many injuries … so many deaths ….
I don't know. He wasn't here when we arrived. I … I didn't see him.\n\nWhen the light erupted, Vanus, Dynar, and I appeared here. No one else. Just us. I … I think Darien's gone.

I'm still trying to work that out myself. When you touched the light, you erupted in holy flame. We thought we had lost you, truth be told.\n\nI've never seen destruction like that before. Even Molag Bal reeled in pain from its touch.
As am I, my friend. As am I.\n\nLet's leave this place once and for all. May the companions we lost along the way find their own way home.

I don't know. Anyone not in the vortex should have been protected from the blast, but I have no way to know if they survived the actual assault.\n\nAnyone inside besides us … I can only imagine the light took them quickly.

This is Thalara's secret. True, some others stole the secret and try to make the wine, but they have not Thalara's cleverness and knowledge. There is only one source for true Nirnroot wine, and it is here.

Charging off like <<1>> Blood-Drunk, eh? Don't expect me to lend a hand. Perhaps a rib will do?\n\nPoint it at any Wormie skeleton and I'll have it fighting at your side! No, it's no trouble, you can thank me later. Onward to the dig site!

They are of no account. Thalara barely remembers their names. They once worked for Thalara, learned her secrets, then snuck out in the night, like wine-stealing rodents.\n\nAs competitors, they are clawless kittens. We will speak no more of them.

Thalara's paws have been burnt in the false flames of trust and sharing. No more. The secrets of Nirnroot wine are too valuable.\n\nFool Thalara once, shame on you. Fool Thalara twice, and Thalara kills you and eats you.
Despite my blindness—nay, because of it—my other senses seem to have heightened. This place had the right smell about it.
I only know that you are important, Vestige. The Scrolls revealed to me that your destiny is intertwined with that of the Five Companions.

Mannimarco convinced Varen that the amulet could be used to perform a ritual that would rekindle the Dragonfires. He claimed this would please Akatosh and entice him to adopt Varen as one of the Dragonborn.

Akatosh gave Alessia the Amulet of Kings as a symbol of his covenant with Nirn. So long as the Amulet remained in the care of Alessia's heirs, and the Dragonfires remained lit, Tamriel would be protected from the Daedra.
And there is so much to do. But know this—you will not walk this path alone.

Of course that's not enough! We thought Pellingare was in danger. We came down here to rescue him.\n\nEvery shambling corpse in this place he created! I can't begin to count the number who've died because of his selfishness. No, for this he pays. Now.
Remember, once you have made an accusation, you must present the supporting evidence as requested.
What is there to think about? He deserves death. But fine. Think about it. Talk to Pellingare if it will make you feel better. But you know I'm right.

The Hallowed is kind of like a guide, or guardian. When all is peaceful in the Khajiiti subsconcious, the passing from one Mane to the next is like the arc of the Moons in the sky. Serene, untroubled. When things are not so peaceful ….

You have the right of it. In the past the Hallowed has been everything from a great warrior to a common street thief. Even a king once! Usually a Khajiit, but sometimes not. The one constant has been their role on the Path.

The where varies. Any city with a large temple to the Dance may act as a trail to the Path. Dune would be the only one in the March. As to what it is … it changes, depending on the walker. It is different for every living soul.

Yes. The Two Moons Path is something that all Khajiit must walk, if they wish to truly venerate Jone and Jode. For the Mane, it is not an option. Walking the Two Moons path is the final step to becoming the Mane.

The Mane must eventually, always, walk the Two Moons Path. Getting a candidate to the point where they can make that journey is a hard process. Sometimes impossible. The Moon Hallowed is a guide for the Mane along that journey.

These items are symbols. If you can obtain them in the dream, they will be in your mind upon your awakening, carried in your thoughts.\n\nYou've learned history, and battled our pupils. This task requires your mind.

I could ask the same of you. No human could call this their natural habitat.\n\nI'm just a traveler. Don't like to stay in one place. I make a point of looking for old books. Not for reading, mind you. I prefer to study the places they're found in.
You have formally accused Aranak the Khajiit merchant of violations against the Green Pact.\n\nWho do you have to stand in testimony against the suspect?
You have formally accused Spinner Eranas of breaking the Green Pact.\n\nWho do you have to stand in testimony against the accused?
You have formally accused Gathiel, the wife of our Spinner, of breaking the Green Pact.\n\nWho do you have to stand in testimony against the accused?

I understand. This is not something to be taken lightly. \n\nReturn when you have reviewed the physical evidence, witness testimony, and mystical signs. Remember, you can ask the suspects about any evidence you find as well.
For what? To go to trial? Have my holdings stripped from me? Maybe face public humiliation?\n\nIt doesn't matter. My children are dead. I have nothing left. Tell Gedric to be done with it.

No. They just make a good excuse for me to try to visit every nook and cranny in all Tamriel.\n\nThe books are signposts. The treasure is in seeing the landscapes. Speaking of which, you're currently blocking my view, if you don't mind.

I can. I've been leader for the Briars for close to fifty years now.\n\nWe are hunters, blessed by the great tree Brackenleaf with a deep knowledge of the forest and its creatures. In return we protect Brackenleaf against an enemy called the Outsider.

Well, you have come to the right place for that. Clearing has a special connection to Jone and Jode. If you truly wish to know, if you are prepared, pray here at the altar. Just do not be disappointed if nothing happens.

The next trial will not be so simple. It will require you to commit your whole self, mind and body.\n\nVenture to the frog cave near the seashore. A rare breed of red frog, the Falinesti Peeper, lives among the reeds. Capture one and eat it.
Citizen, please step forth as accuser. Advocate, what physical evidence do you have to present to us?
Oh, my sisters and I took to Stibbons as soon as he arrived! He's such a dear! We could just eat him up!\n\nHe does have some issues, though. I think he craves a woman's approval.
Well, I hear it's amazingly potent and delicious. Never tasted it myself, but that's what they say. Those who've tasted it. Or so they say.

Oh, you're a sly one. But your left eye twitches when you lie, you know.\n\nYes, I have competitors. They used to be my helpers but they stole my recipe and set up their own shops. Their wine is swill, truly inferior products. Forget about them.
Ah, now that's my secret. Can't be telling everyone how to make it, or there goes my market, right?\n\nSay, you wouldn't be spying for one of my competitors, would you?
I don't know about you, but I just about ate until I burst! It was so delicious!
Oh, we've become very close in the time he's been with us. He's such a fascinating man!\n\nI hope we can get to know each other, too. I do so enjoy making new friends and meeting new people!

Much do I know but little will I tell. Secrecy is a sad necessity, for the envious yearn to steal the recipe for the most exquisite of wines. My customers must be spared from the imitations brewed by charlatans.
Gamirth? Sounds familiar but my memory isn't what it used to be. You should talk to Bernt. After you get a mead. The stuff tastes wonderful! I love mead.

I know Gamirth! He's a terrific fellow. I love him like a brother. We were drinking mead and telling old war stories just the other day.\n\nDoes Gamirth owe you gold? Maybe Bernt knows where you can find him.
Of course! Zur would not be here if he could not help.\n\nThis one gives you light to guide your way. Be wary where you step, for darkness will most likely be the least of your worries.

Some say it tastes like the blessed tears of Zeht, if one can imagine those upon one's tongue. Some say the taste cannot be described, only experienced. I merely pass along the words of others, as I never sample my wares.

Their names would soil your ears, wayfarer, and I will not utter them. Know only that their intent is dishonorable, stealing the recipe for this finest of wines from its rightful owner. Their wines are pale imitations of the one true Nirnroot wine.

It's an effective tactic. The Daedra mock our emotional attachments and the memories that form our sense of self.\n\nDaedra have no use for such things. They are immortal. It's impossible to kill Daedra—they simply reform, over time.
At last! Where can he be found?
Well done. I will begin searching for a safe route to the Halls of Torment immediately.

I was going to say that the river flows and we are slaves to its current, but I am done with riddles and metaphors. \n\nI don't know what awaits us. I'm not a Prophet. I'm just a foolish old man who glimpsed the wisdom of the scrolls, and survived.
Well, your journey has been successful. Stenric blood certainly runs through my veins.
Marcelle Stenric? That was my great-grandmother's name! Is that really her sword?\n\nI grew up listening to stories of Dame Marcelle's exploits. She was quite the warrior, if you believe the tales.

The ships being built at the Tava's Blessing shipyards are critical for the Covenant war effort. \n\nI do not think the Withered Hand would have use for the ships, but I fear they might simply destroy them. That would be very bad for the Covenant.

Hmm. I could tell you, but how do I know you're trustworthy? You ask us to share your enemies, but will you share ours?\n\nThe Wood Orcs are a plague we can't seem to be rid of. If you help us drive them off, I'll tell you what you want to know.

Slow down! Why walk away from Ildani now? When she needs you so much?\n\nYou said you would help Ildani, yes? Well, Ildani still needs help delivering her goods. You will deliver the goods for her, yes?

The key to Sancre Tor isn't really a key at all. It's an enchanted ring bearing the sigil of Stendarr. \n\nThe ring is in the keeping of Sai Sahan's mentor, Kasura. You, Lyris, and Abnur must accompany him to the Valley of Blades to retrieve it.

Did you try to talk to any of them? It's all "the Eight this" and "the Eight that." And that's all they talk about! Stick around if you don't believe me. They don't drink or gamble or run naked through the cemetery or do anything fun.

I don't really know. Niriel just said that if you use them when you destroy the totems, it'd help convince the Orcs that you're a forest spirit. Maybe they grow flowers or vines or something? Niriel said a High Elf woman gave them to her.

The valley contains an abbey I thought long abandoned. In his youth, Sai studied there and honed his craft. \n\nIt seems that Kasura has been using it as a retreat of sorts, to train a select few young warriors. Sai Sahan can tell you more.
I don't know. The name sounds familiar, but Niriel didn't say. \n\nI'm going to disguise myself as a forest spirit, too, and see if I can learn anything to help you defeat the Orc war captain.

I would if I could. I just need cousin Asvorn to send me some more money. Then I can buy a horse, some food, maybe even a rusty dagger to fend off monsters. But until Asvorn takes pity on me, I'm stuck here—shoveling hay and manure.

Agomar Direfrost, former lord of this Keep. We were attacked many years ago by a witch seeking revenge on our family.\n\nDrodda of Icereach, the harbinger of our demise, rules the Keep now, from the summit. She's there now, in fact.

Like you, I am a prisoner in this place, yet so much more.\n\nI am the past and the future both. I am despair and hope. The tapestry we weave is a complex one. You cannot hope to see its pattern in its entirety. Not yet.

There is nothing left to tell, except that our home remains under attack.\n\nWhich leads to my next point—a descendant of mine was headed for the summit, no doubt into Drodda's clutches. Called himself Eboric. Will you help him, as you helped me?
<You see <<1>> is extremely agitated. He seems ready to bolt down the hallway, but keeps staring at you.>

Not exactly. I'm a Direfrost, after all. But I won't hunt them, either. According to Drodda, we've caused them much suffering.\n\nIf she's telling the truth, perhaps my ancestors deserved what happened to them. I have some contemplation to do.

An old friend, Kasura, dwells there. Before I was captured I placed an enchanted ring in her keeping.\n\nThe ring is a key of sorts. Without it, we will not be able to open the secret chamber where the Amulet of Kings lies hidden.
Glaras, and so many before her. This place was still young when I was cut from the branches of Brackenleaf and given life.\n\nHow are you feeling? Are you ready to proceed?
Hm? What? You'll have to speak up. My hearing isn't what it used to be, and it was never very good to begin with. No ears, you see.
Agreed. There's no time to waste. We must take the fight to him!
She was my first mentor and instructor, a true master of blades. She still trains young swordsmen in the valley. Those she deems worthy of her instruction.

Swordsmanship, but much more than that. Her teachings revolve around a trinity of body, blade, and brilliance. The sword-singers of old were said to be masters of all three.\n\nLook, there will be time for questions later. Are you ready to depart?
After that terrible display of power, I don't think they have much choice.
Yes, at the Ayleid Well at the center of the island.

When I was among the living, I had many questions too. Samsi made sure my questions were put to an end though ….\n\nIf it will convince you to avenge me, I will answer your questions. What is it you wish to know?

Your spirit animal's shrine lies at the edge of the forest. Light the brazier, and your predator will appear.\n\nBe prepared. Just as you stalked your prey, so your predator will pursue you with lethal cunning. When you are done, return to Brackenleaf.
Unfortunately, yes. It's not the massive army we'd hoped for, but now that Molag Bal knows we're coming, a smaller group might be our only hope of slipping into Coldharbour undetected.
It's difficult to predict where you will emerge once you reach Coldharbour. Be on your guard, my friend.
We accept this diary into evidence. Please place it on the table.
Please present the final piece of evidence, an omen from the heavens, portending the guilt of the accused.
We accept this order invoice into evidence. Please place it on the table.
We accept this cutting from the sacred plant. Please place it on the table.
We accept this astrology chart into evidence. Please place it on the table.
We accept this broken sigil into evidence. Please place it on the table.
We accept this lightning charred rock into evidence. Please place it on the table.
Please allow me a moment to review the evidence you have presented, advocate.
As I've said before, the Briars are my guardians. They protect my heart against the Outsider, an enemy who wants to steal my heart at any cost.

Everyone's vision is a little different, but we all must take the heart and experience the role of the Outsider.\n\nYou stopped being the Outsider when you proved yourself strong enough to defeat the masters, and Brackenleaf offered you his heart.
Go to the Snake's shrine. Pray at the brazier and receive the blessing of Brackenleaf's Briars. Then, return to me for the final rite of initiation.

I'm sure I have no idea what you're talking about. Our food is the finest in the realm!\n\nPerhaps you have brought some sickness with you from outside. You should cleanse yourself in our pools. They're very therapeutic.

Because we must punish him for his transgressions. The Elf bone shell to which he was banished will no longer suit him. We'll return him to the old skull around which the Barrowbough first grew, the very skull that surrounds this room.
I am a teacher and a theorist, but once I could hurl destructive spells with the best of them. With my strength restored, I look forward to showing Molag Bal what this old scholar can still do.

Well, as much as I'd love to charge into the fray, someone needs to stand back and defend the less martial-oriented mages.\n\nBut as soon as we make it to the dungeons, my services are yours if you need them.

What, you think I would go back on my word? I promised my help and you shall have it. Please don't insult me by suggesting otherwise.\n\nThe Shadow Court is at your command. Call upon them and they shall answer.

Yes, of course you will. They say beggars can't choose their next meal, don't they?\n\nYou know how to call upon the Shadow Court when you need to, correct? I'd hate to think you forgot how to use my gift already.

His name is Haidar. I worked for him for many years before he began acknowledging me as his partner rather than his apprentice.\n\nI learned much from him though. I truly hope you are able to get him out of there.

No. It is not safe. When a mine becomes unstable like this, there is no way to know when it will collapse completely. It's always a gamble.\n\nBut you look like you are accustomed to danger, and so much … I mean, my partner's life is at stake.

Dwemer gold. It is buried under this desert somewhere. My partner and I worked Kulati mines for some time, but that effort was of no avail.\n\nWe came here on our own. The fewer people involved, the greater the reward if something is discovered.

Cadwell, Vanus, and the others are up ahead, near the entrance to the Labyrinth. They're waiting for you.\n\nMe? I think I'll take a few moments and recover from that last fight before plunging into the next one. I suggest you do the same.

Ever since Baron Montclair annexed the upper city of Shornhelm, we've been going out on patrol. To keep them from annexing anything else, you understand. They were waiting for us when we got the Hinault's farm, though.

Thalara cannot say, truly. The Nirnroot wine does not allow one to drink it. Strange but true. It is a magical concoction that Thalara brews but does not understand.\n\nMuch like offspring, which one loves though they are a mystery to us.
Soldiers loyal to House Montclair. They came out of the darkness and caught us by surprise. It was a slaughter!\n\nLuckily, I was able to rally some of my troops and we made our way here.
Of course! You have saved Arenthia, saved my city. The least I can do is answer a few questions. The Moon Hallowed is said to be the one to walk the Two Moons Path with the Mane. Their guide.

No. There is no Dwemer gold down there. We had already decided to give up on this mine even before the rumbling began.\n\nWe had talked of seeking our fortunes in Bangkorai … though now I suppose, I might be going there on my own.
The Hallowed is kind of like a guide, or guardian. When all is well with my people, the new Mane is chosen easily. Peacefully. But sometimes things are not so easy on the plains of Elsweyr.

The where varies. Any city with a large temple to the Dance may act as a trail to the Path. Dune would be the only one in the March. As to what it is … it changes, depending on the walker. It is different for every person.

Yes. The lunar clergy encourage all Khajiit to walk the Two Moons Path at least once in their lives. For a new Mane, it is not an option. Walking the Two Moons path is the final step to becoming the Mane.

The Mane must eventually, always, walk the Two Moons Path. It must be hard, coaching someone to the point of being able to make that journey. Maybe impossible. The Moon Hallowed is the guide for the Mane along that journey.
Just so. The Hallowed is said to come from all walks of life … I think the Hallowed was a king, once! Usually one of my people, but not always. The one constant has been their role on the Path.

Our healing supplies? Heloise could certainly use those.\n\nAll right, I'll order them to unlock the tower door. But understand this—if you betray us in any way, I'll kill you myself and toss your lifeless body from the top of the tower.

No. All assume the wine tastes delightful, and many will tell you so, swearing they have tasted it. But they are deluded. Merely thinking about drinking it causes the Nirnroot wine to make you drunk, thus saving itself.
Of course! Why would I pass up a chance to witness this spectacle? Blood will flow today, and I wouldn't miss it for the world!\n\nI look forward to seeing if Molag Bal can stop us.

I have my ways. As for you, feel free to utilize the power I granted you at the Cliffs of Failure. It served you well once, and it shall do so again.\n\nLet my power grant you the destructive force you desire.
Bad news? Has something happened to my wife? To poor Nadafa?\n\nWell, spit it out! I can handle it. Tell me what happened to my wife.
What? How can you say such terrible things?\n\nI … I noticed she was different … but I never believed—How could she do this? How could she leave me for a monster?
Damnable fiends! Is there nothing they won't take from us?

You've met <<1>>? She speaks too freely sometimes, but I will tell you what I can.\n\nOur village, as you may be aware, is not here normally. A long time ago, our treethanes and ancestors swore a sacred oath to which we are still bound.

We are named for the thorny thickets that the forest raises to protect its most delicate plants.\n\nBut under the guidance of masters like Glaras we are trained to become skilled hunters and defenders of the great tree, Brackenleaf.

It's weird, but I don't know. I don't think anyone else does either. There's something strange about that wine, it doesn't seem to want anyone to drink it. Maybe it tastes awful and it doesn't want anyone to know?

It is tradition for Redguard men to shave their heads following a time of great trials. I shaved mine long ago, when I failed in the task to restore the lost tradition of the sword-singers.\n\nAlso, long hair gets in the way during battle.

I do not know for certain. It is possible that the gemstones were already cursed before we found them, and this is what caused my spirit to linger.\n\nRegardless, I believe achieving vengeance on my killer will bring me peace.
They would have been worth a fortune when we found them, but now that they carry my curse, any who take them with greed in their heart will have little time to secure a profit.

It is possible Samsi always intended this, or her true self simply emerged when we finally found something of value.\n\nI have known Samsi many years, and she has always been jealous, but I never thought she harbored murderous intentions in her heart.
The crime of murder is unforgiveable. Whether Samsi was influenced or not is irrelevant.\n\nShe must pay the consequences for taking my life.
Very well. I hope you are convinced that my cause is just. Those who would commit murder for coin deserve terrible suffering.\n\nMy curse will give Samsi a quick and merciful end.

Not that I know of. And believe me, I've tried. If you think about drinking it, the wine knows and makes you drunk before you uncork the bottle.\n\nIf you ever manage to drink some, let me know what it tastes like.

Glaras took me in when my mother and father died. When I came of age, I wanted to follow in her footsteps.\n\nBecoming a Briar shows you strength you didn't even know you had, and that even the strongest—even great Brackenleaf—needs others.
We are at war! We need fresh arms!
Good luck soldier!
Come back when you're ready to aid the Covenant.
Oh, a few have tried, but a fool and his fingers are quickly parted.
There is an old Redguard proverb. A man is only as great as the beard that wears him.\n\nA full and healthy beard carries with it a sense of great honor and wisdom. Also crumbs.
Of course! I have long studied the ways of the Bright Moons. The Moon Hallowed is said to be the one to walk the Two Moons Path with the Mane. Their guide.

The Hallowed is a kind of guide, or guardian. When all is well with the people of moonlight, the new Mane is chosen easily. Peacefully. But sometimes things are not so peaceful on the plains of Elsweyr.

The where varies. Any city with a large temple to the Dance may act as a trail to the Path. Dune would be the only one in the March. As to what it is … it changes, depending on the walker. It is different for every person.

We encourage all followers of the Dance to walk the Two Moons Path at least once in their lives. For a new Mane, it is not an option. Walking the Two Moons path is the final step to becoming the Mane.
The Mane must eventually walk the Two Moons Path. Always. It is hard, coaching someone. Making that journey. Perhaps impossible. The Moon Hallowed is the guide for the Mane along that journey.

Just so. The Hallowed is said to come from all walks of life. In the past the Hallowed has been everything from a great warrior to a common street thief. Not always a Khajiit, even. The one constant has been their role on the Path.
Divines be praised! Thank you so much. With these supplies, I can properly tend to the wounded.
As ever, straight to the point. \n\nYou have done the impossible. The King of Worms has been consumed by the wrath of Molag Bal. The power of his Worm Cult is broken forever.

That's what I was hoping you'd say. Lieutenant Fairfax doesn't want anyone to leave the tower, but I'm sure he'll agree to let me go if you accompany me.\n\nGive me a moment to finish tending to these soldiers and I'll meet you outside.

If you're willing to help, I won't say no.\n\nI'm worried about the Hinault family. We haven't seen them since the battle started. I want to check on them, make sure they're all right, but I don't want to navigate a horde of Montclairs on my own.
That is the grim truth of the matter. But the Amulet of Kings is in our possession and there is still much to do.
In my sleep, I hear his tormented screams, and Molag Bal forces visions of his eternal torture into my mind.\n\nI can show you exactly what I see—if you wish it.
In truth, I cannot say. I have never been able to taste the wine, though I have crafted many bottles of it. Some claim to have tasted it, but I fear the truth is not in them.

I am convinced not. The wine ensorcels us all. It stays in its bottle, making its owner think he has imbibed, preserving itself forever. No customer ever needs a second bottle of Nirnroot wine, more's the pity.

Now there is the Sameer I know. Sometime you will have to tell me what has befallen on this last night. A story of wildness, I am sure.\n\nCome now though. Our father prepares to address the Ra Gada. He is expecting us.

At a quick glance? There are holes in the treaty. When <<Ac:1>> worries at them, he'll tear a hole in the Maormer's side. The treaty, of course. Not Ambassador <<2>>. Though … heh, that would be funny.

Sameer, I am really starting to worry. Have you been ensorcelled?\n\nThe year is eight hundred and fifty-three. Our father is King Xakhwan, come from old Yokuda to settle here in the Alik'r desert. I hope this is starting to sound familiar ….
Praise the gods! It would not be proper if we were not present when father makes his speech. \n\nHe is very likely starting to worry about us himself.

Blade's edge! I'm sorry. You are the crown prince, but I am your brother and I was worried.\n\nPlease. Tell me you're all right. I have been looking forward to this battle for weeks, but father will not let me fight unless you lead the way.

Because they do not want us here. Our people came across the sea from old Yokuda to settle here, but these Elves—the Corelanya clan—they would drive us from these shores.\n\nWe are making our stand today, letting them know we are here to stay.

The Ash'abah? These people I do not know. Are they also Elves? If we must, we will kill them too. \n\nI need you to focus though, Sameer. Focus on the battle today. We should hurry to hear father's speech.
Actually it was Honor who found them.\n\nHave you met? We've been together, forever. He knows Coldharbour almost as well as I do.
We were caught by surprise, but those still inside are fighting back.

I know. And in a way, it is! Our father put me in charge of the johads after I, uh, returned from Sentinel. Within a fortnight, most of the johads reeked of this musk!\n\nEven so, I have no idea how any of this happened.
Only one way to know for sure. A taste test!\n\nThese three johads are the ones attracting the most beetles. See if the water has the same flavor as that vial.

We're a scholarly organization dedicated to the pursuit of knowledge. Guild members seek out books, tomes, and ancient scrolls in their travels. We aid each other where we can, and provide magical support for any that would ask our help.

Precisely. We seek out new information, capture it in our libraries, and make copies for distribution across Tamriel.\n\nThe Guild cares not about wars, battlefields, or boundaries: just knowledge, and the acquisition of new tomes.

As you say! I hearby grant you membership in the Mages Guild, with all the responsibilities and privileges thereof. Every book you find, and every book collection you complete, will now earn you reputation in the guild. Good luck!
Pish-tosh! Honor isn't a pet! He's my faithful steed!\n\nHe does mistake the odd Wood Elf for a tasty treat, but they've been known to do that themselves, haven't they?

We are protectors of Brackenleaf, and through him, servants of Y'ffre who created him.\n\nTo involve ourselves in politics would only corrupt our mission. That said, we have no quarrel with Queen Ayrenn or the Dominion.
Brackenleaf's Briars are any who can prove themselves worthy by passing the trials. The trials do not distinguish between the races of Tamriel and neither do we.

The first Briar was a skilled hunter called Thaldil. She single-handedly protected Brackenleaf from being destroyed by Colovians during the Imperial occupation of Grahtwood.\n\nShe followed the guidance of Brackenleaf and established the Briars.

Old songs speak of days when Y'ffre walked among the trees of Valenwood. She planted the seed that would become Elden Root, but what most don't know is that she planted many more.\n\nBrackenleaf was one of those seeds.

Sameer … you must not go in there! You would have to strike down your own father!\n\nAs darkly as these events have transpired, our laws remain sacred. Your father is honored dead. Harm his remains and you dishonor yourself!

Yes. There is no other choice to be made. I know your father would not want us to abandon our new home here, but he could not have foreseen this.\n\nHe would not have us break the sacred law. You must not even consider such a thing.
As you say.
I have … not seen them since the Daedra attacked.\n\nAreldur is the closest, and if she lives, you'll find her up ahead.

My injuries are not serious. What are a few more scars to an old warrior? Scars have the virtue of reminding us that our past is real. My students, and my home, have not fared half so well.\n\nI'm glad to see you, but curious why you are here.

We must grow in strength and in numbers. You will need more than the company of an old blind man to alter the course of history.\n\nWe must assemble our own group of companions. The first, you have already met.
Lyris sacrificed her own freedom to allow us to escape. She remains a prisoner in Coldharbour. I must determine her precise location if we are to mount a rescue. That will take time.

Mannimarco tricked Varen into breaking the covenant, and the veil between Oblivion and Nirn was torn. The Elder Scrolls named this event the Soulburst. It gave Molag Bal the opportunity to disconnect the souls of Nirn from their hosts.
Tharn remains Chancellor of the Elder Council, and his daughter Clivia rules as Empress Regent. But the true power remains in the hands of Mannimarco and his Worm Cult.
Varen was lost. In the chaos of the moment, Sai Sahan took the Amulet of Kings and fled. Lyris was captured by Mannimarco and delivered to Coldharbour, the realm of Molag Bal.
Of a sort. I invite you to enter my mind and walk with me through visions of the past, that you might understand the events that brought us to this time, this moment.

Indeed. But let us not get ahead of ourselves. Without an understanding of where we are bound, every road will get us nowhere.\n\nBefore we truly understand our destination, we must speak of the past.

The Five Companions were a band of adventurers who sought out an ancient artifact called The Amulet of Kings. They hoped to use this artifact to persuade Akatosh, the Dragon God, to accept their leader as one of the Dragonborn.
You have already heard enough babbling from this old, blind fool. It is time you met the Five Companions yourself, and witnessed their fate.
The Dragonborn are mortals destined for greatness, with the blood of the Dragons in their veins.\n\nIt is said that only a true Dragonborn can ignite the Eternal Dragonfires in the Imperial City.

What does the ship do when the wind changes? Tack.\n\nNot specific enough? Well, I don't know. Right now, I serve the captain, but she's given us a choice. I don't know if I want to fight—for the Dominion or anyone else. I'll have to think on it.

By tradition, only the Dragonborn can lay claim to the Ruby Throne and rule as the one, true Emperor by divine right.\n\nVaren conquered Cyrodiil and took the throne, but unless he became Dragonborn, he feared he'd always be thought of as a pretender.
Each of the Five Companions were chosen for their skill and courage, and each was given a special role to perform in the party. \n\nWho would you like to know more about?

You've already met Lyris. She is a Nord warrior from the frozen lands of Skyrim to the north. And it is said that her family lineage contains the blood of Giants. Varen chose her for her strength and her loyalty, to be his personal bodyguard.

Sai Sahan came from a long line of Redguard swordmaster nobles. He was the leader of the Dragonguard, the security detail of Varen and the Elder Council. While Lyris was Varen's bodyguard, Sai was charged with protecting the entire group.

The Tharns are one of the most influential families in Cyrodiil. Abnur, their patriarch, is the leader of the Elder Council, a powerful battlemage and a shrewd politician. With his counsel, Varen was able to seize the Imperial throne, years before.
Disaster. War and pestilence. A world brought to its knees. \n\nNow watch, and see how one man's arrogance brought about the greatest threat our world has ever known.

Mannimarco the traitor. The great enemy. The most powerful necromancer this world has ever known. His Worm Cult infiltrates and corrupts every corner of Tamriel. It was he who convinced Varen to perform the ritual you are about to witness.
It is you, my friend. You are the link. \n\nI will not bore you with effusive praise, but state it plainly. You are a great warrior and a trusted friend and we would like to extend to you an offer.
When Emperor Varen first brought the Five Companions together, he did so in the hope of creating a Tamriel where all men could live freely and safely beneath one banner.

The Five Companions failed, betrayed from within by one of our own: the Worm King Mannimarco. All that came after was the result of one man's treachery.\n\nNow four of the five are reunited to right that great wrong. But destiny requires a fifth.
We want you to join us as our fifth member. You are the champion we should have had with us back then.\n\nDon't look so grave. This is largely symbolic. But, please … humor an old soldier.

<<1>> unleashed a blood-curse upon the town. Turned some townsfolk into ravenous bloodfiends. \n\nBut that wasn't enough for him. He used magic and our living flesh to create an abomination. A part of me still lives within the creature.

Find the spirits of Tharlas and Jonne. We can use our connection to the creature to lure it from the chapel crypt so you can kill it.\n\nWe'll also need personal items to focus our energy through. My Badge of Office should work nicely.

You must slay this abomination. As long as it lives, our spirits are trapped in this town. \n\nThey keep the creature in the chapel crypt. I think they're feeding it, making it stronger. Soon, I fear, they will set it loose upon all of Rivenspire.
Of course. We've lived under the shadow of the Doomcrag for many generations. Whatever secrets it held, we assumed they would remain locked away forever.\n\nThen Reezal-Jul appeared.

It is mine! A rare bug musk, used in some Bosmer cooking if I recall. I thought I'd misplaced it on the trip here.\n\nTell me, where did you find it?

Blessed Baan … Tu'whacca! I beg you, keep your voice down! My father-in-law would truly turn me out if he heard such rumors!\n\nHow could it be? I swear upon my very claws, I had nothing to do with the johads! You must believe me!

Thank you. In some ways, this is an honor for me.\n\nLet us just hope that all that sparring we did in the courtyard has prepared me for this …. If so, I will return momentarily. If not, then this is goodbye.
No! No, please! I beseech you to reconsider this decision, Sameer.\n\nI cannot bear to see you exiled. What will I do? I am not sewn from the same cloth as you and father. I am not meant to be king!
They did not find the Ring of Stendarr's Mercy. But now that the King of Worms knows you are here, it is only a matter of time before he launches another attack.

It is strange, but wait and listen. Outside, a woman peddles her trained lizards. Ask if her pets can track scents, such as this bug musk.\n\nJust holding the vial leaves residue on one's hands. If you find who held the vial, you'll find who stole it.

Steal? I would not know. Many of the workers come in and out of the house for refreshments, so perhaps one of them took it. But still, why would they do such a thing?\n\nHrr. There is one way to find out who took the bottle.

Your courage … your humility …. You should be king, not I!\n\nI'm sorry. I suppose I must stop acting like a child and accept my responsibility. Whatever happens, though, your sacrifice will never be forgotten. I love you, my brother.

No. Enough tragedy has befallen our kingdom today. I would not disrespect our sacred laws. \n\nTo attempt to avoid my fate would mean the sacrifice I have made was in vain. You must let me go, brother.

The mayor is a good woman. Her spirit is strong.\n\nShe has a good idea, to use our spirits to draw out the creature. Our flesh remains alive while the abomination lives. Through this connection, we can call it to us.

What's most important to an old scholar like me? My mind, I suppose.\n\nThe bloodfiends tore my body apart after using some of my flesh to create their abomination. My skull was tossed aside. It's got to be somewhere in the graveyard.

And it probably was. The man I spoke to was no Khajiit, though that is all I can say about him. He was hidden from view when we first spoke, his voice muffled.\n\nI refused to take his gold, but I knew sooner or later someone would.

Some of the workers said the payoff location was inside the house. That was before the beetles came—after that, no one wanted anything to do with this strange man's scheme.\n\nI'd search there for any sign of who this person was.

I've been thinking about our adventures and the hardships we've faced together. We're in the last leg of this journey, aren't we? \n\nI don't regret any of it, but it occurs to me that we haven't had much of a chance to talk as friends.
It's nothing scandalous, I assure you.\n\nBut those dungpiles up ahead? They're murderers! Get them out of our way and we'll talk.
Where do you see yourself going after all of this is over? I mean, assuming we survive, get your soul back, and stop Molag Bal?
Me? I don't know. Maybe I'll go back to Skyrim and settle down. Squeeze out a few whelps. Maybe raise sheep or grow cabbages.

Bloody business, war. There was a time that I loved my axe for its sharpness, and my armor for its sheen, but no more. Today, I love what they defend. Don't lose sight of what's behind you in the hatred of what's before you.

Traveling is a humbling experience. You see firsthand what a small place you occupy in the world. Funny thing is, the farther you go, the harder it is to return. But when you do … if you do … you get to see the place you came from with new eyes.

What? No! Can you imagine it? Lyris Titanborn, shepherd? Farmer? Housewife? I need to be out in the wind and wild. And if I ever find my life mate, he'll feel the same way.\n\nMy turn. What's your one regret about all we've been through?
I guess you're right. Ah, well.\n\nI won't take up too much of your time. You've got destiny and all that, written on some moldy-old scroll.
You're a hard-heart, eh? No regrets, no tears, no doubts? Don't look back unless you're planning to head in that direction? \n\nI guess that that's exactly the kind of person we need right now.

You never get used to it. My father … he'll die over and over again for the rest of my life. Grief doesn't go away. You just learn to live with it. \n\nBut I can live my life with his daring and spirit and joy. That way, he'll never die. Not really.

That's the real test of character. Anyone can face adversity, but give them power and you'll see their true colors.\n\nPower over others is the way of cowards. Seize the power to choose your own path. To control your own life. That takes real courage.

Oh, lots of things. Friends lost, missed opportunities, failed endeavors. Maybe the best that we can hope for is to end up with the right regrets.\n\nI do regret not taking the time to get to know the people I fought with. I hope to change that.

Areldur would like nothing more than to confront Rilis now, but we're not ready.\n\nThe High Kinlord can't be killed—our only course is to capture him, but we'll need a sturdier prison than we've ever had before.

I knew I liked you! So, let's toast ….\n\nTo Molag Bal, that ugly skeever! May his privates be infected with Brown Rot Fever! May our course be true and our hearts be brave, as we march into Coldharbour to spit on his grave!
Oh, my small friend, you are hopeless, aren't you?\n\nI've been saving a bottle for a special occasion. Real Skyrim mead, too. I don't suppose you'd want to share one, regardless of the taste?
Never? Mead is the honeyed kiss of the gods themselves! You must try some!
One last thing.\n\nYou like mead?

Then whoever else was in here smells of it too! We need some way to detect the scent and follow their trail.

In days long past, our old bones longed for the sun's sweet kiss, for friends we knew in life. But our restless wanderings caused untold suffering. We went far away, to be forgotten by the world. To die.\n\nBut <<1>> continued to wander. To destroy.
It falls to one of us to take charge of the johads. Father always wanted me to have them, but I feel I'm the one who truly betrayed the family.
Yes. I am prepared to take them. I'd just never thought … well, I am eldest, after all. This is my duty.\n\nWe'll mend our family here. We won't fail our father's dream.
It falls to one of us to take charge of the johads. Father always wanted Jahi to have them, but she's never wanted them. Neither of us have.
And I know what to do with them as well. I'm selling them to another family to run.\n\nThis place has seen more than its fair share of strife. I'm done.
I can't. Not after all this.\n\nIt'll be hard work, but together we'll do it. As a family.
It's the only way to end our bickering. After all this, I feel we need to be a family again. Strong. United. And my sister's the only one of my blood left.

Then the gods do want something of me? I guess it's a second chance, a chance to redeem my father, myself … to get revenge. \n\nIt truly is a miracle then. I could lead the undead here to defeat the Reachmen!
Aye. Along with some of the most renowned sword-singers who ever lived. We must tread carefully and with great respect.
The farmer doesn't thank the cow when it voids itself on the field, but it still makes the crops grow taller.

I suppose it is. But that wasn't the reason for this heartwarming reunion. Varen and I have spoken at length since you recovered the Amulet and determined our final course of action.\n\nMolag Bal remains a threat and Tamriel is still in grave danger.
The Planemeld has been stopped, but Molag Bal's power over Nirn is still prodigious.\n\nTo restore protection to Nirn and reclaim your soul, you must face the God of Schemes himself.
First, the Planemeld must be stopped. Even now, forces gather and plan an assault on Oblivion itself. You must join them.

I know more about the Daedra than any man or mer alive. For good or ill, my family has always kept ties with the forces of Oblivion, and this much I know—one cannot kill a Daedric Prince.\n\nBut we have the Amulet of Kings ….

With the Amulet in our possession, we may be able to wound him. Severely. And in the process, force him to relinquish every last soul he has stolen—including your own.\n\nThis is where your … condition works to your benefit.

Only if we use it here on Nirn. But if we were to travel to Coldharbour, we might be able to harness its power. Imbue you with divine agency enough to challenge the Daedric Prince.\n\nBut there is a price ….
The ritual we performed with the Amulet of Kings caused the Soulburst and damaged the veil between worlds. If the damage is to be repaired, I must attempt the ritual again, this time with you.

They invited him to join the travels of their walking city. His elation gave them time to ensorcel him into slumber. Unaware, he laid down to sleep.\n\nThey buried him, and planted a seed in his skull. In time, it became the Barrowbough.

He couldn't bear to stay in one place for long. Yet while he fixed his gaze upon the horizon, he forgot to watch the ground. Whole cities crumbled beneath him.\n\nAmidst this devastation, the Wood Elves of Falinesti saw his wanderlust for what it was.
It's our village. It was our village, anyway. It lies north of here, if it still stands, if the Black Daggers haven't burned it down.

Calling upon the power of the Amulet in this manner will consume someone's soul. Utterly. One cannot channel the power of the gods without paying such a price.\n\nUnfortunately, you don't have a soul to consume and I am needed to perform the ritual.
More specifically, one of our three companions. I suspect that's why they're so nauseatingly over-appreciative and fawning.
It should be in the tower where I worked.\n\nWe made our stand in that tower, but we were overrun. I can still hear Reezal-Jul, laughing, as they dragged me away. That lizard's laugh haunts me.
A gang of bandits, one of many sprung up like weeds since the fall of the Empire. I have heard refugees speak of them in other places in western Cyrodiil as well.

Well, she hasn't come back yet and I'm starting to worry. I think she's ill and trying hard not to show it. Hopefully, she'll be back soon.\n\nFor now, go inside and check on the Hinaults. I promised to send you to them when you arrived.
Over the rise. Wait. Too many footsteps, and it's too early for my parents' return. Boots. Boots ….\n\nThere are invaders on Silatar. We have to stop them!

We both thought it would be well protected in the Valley of Blades. The most gifted young swordmasters of Hammerfell are invited to train with Kasura. The town was bristling with strength and steel before the Titan showed up.

I cannot say. Perhaps someone told him of my past. Perhaps he pried the memory from me during my time in the Halls of Torment.\n\nEither way, I am to blame for the valley's destruction. No one I love will be safe until Mannimarco has been dealt with.

The Wood Elves of Falinesti feared our fading bones would wander, so they sought us out and carried us to <<Ac:1>>. Here they interred us beneath shrines to Y'ffre, ensuring we would never be forgotten.\n\nBecause of this, none of us can die.
That millions of others may live, yes. Do not be troubled. Any one of us would gladly make such a sacrifice.

As Tharn has said, there are already plans in motion to infiltrate Coldharbour. You must be part of them. The chains that anchor us to Oblivion draw us ever closer. They must be severed, once and for all.

Does it matter? I'm tired of this! Everyone wants to hurt me or use me, and it stops now!\n\nWhere were you when my parents "tested" me? Where were you when I needed you most? You left me! Why are you even here? Do you want something from me too?

Receiving that staff was the greatest moment of my life. I'm a Redguard. Magic doesn't come easily to my people, but I was drawn to it. I left Alik'r and studied for years to earn that staff. \n\nI can focus all that I am and all that I was through it.
She is in the deepest part of the Banished Cells.\n\nI have conceived the beginnings of a spell to handle Rilis, and we'll need Imiril if it's going to succeed.

You must return to the Harborage and give it to Lord Varen. It will remain safe in his keeping until it is time to travel to Sancre Tor.\n\nLyris, Abnur and I will remain here, to help Kasura bury the dead, and tend to the injured.
Ahh, yes. The lunar clergy, telling you what to do because the moons say so. Good that you're here just the same. I'm getting tired of killing Dro-m'Athra.
Nabira is but a simple member of the lunar clergy. She is here to ensure you reach where you must go. She is here to put you in the right hands.
Lord Varen has been observing our progress. He will open a portal for you to return.\n\nThere it is, at the top of the stairs. Go, quickly!

Why concern yourself with the whys and hows of this realm? This place is safe. We'll care for all your wants and needs. What else is there to tell you?\n\nBut you look so thin. You need to eat something. Go, find the banquet tables, have some food.
They are a symptom of the sickness that has spread across Cyrodiil. Evil grows, taking different names in different places. But it is all the same everywhere, no matter what face it wears.

North of here, perhaps northwest, I am not sure. We ran when the bandits attacked, no thought except get away and stay alive. And we ended up here. Now I try to forget about Hackdirt and my life there; it is gone in the wind.
<<1>>'s crimes are unforgivable. We once sought a true death in the farthest reaches of the world, but his aimless wanderings led to our imprisonment! Here, we can never die!

No. In telling the story, we see he did not.\n\nBut his wanderings led to great destruction, and his selfishness led our bones to this prison. He afflicted us with the doom of endlessness, and for this crime he cannot be forgiven.
That story is as long as it is old. You would endure the telling?
Good, for the memories alone wear upon us.\n\nIt is time for <<1>> to return to his bones. There will he remain until the world forgets. Then, perhaps, he will die.
Saifa is a simple lunar priestess, but yes. She sees why you are here. The moons have shown her all she needs to know.
Oh. I guess that little barnacle is all right.
Never said I didn't want it.\n\nIf the clerk didn't toss you out, I guess you're not a problem. Sure, one drink.
Oh, well done.\n\nIt doesn't matter now. The Green Lummox and her idiot husband lie dead. There's nothing you can do to stop us.

I'd fight! Return to Hackdirt and take it back, or die trying. We can make weapons and learn to use them. We sneak in at night, kill the guards—if they even post any—then kill the rest in their sleep. It'd be easy!

Well, no. No, who am I kidding? We're just farmers and merchants and field hands. We're more likely to cut ourselves with a sword than whoever we're swinging it at.\n\nI need to do something though. Maybe I'll go out and kill a deer.

Thinking, considering, creating. How is one to work in a crowded city? The noise and interruptions drive away all thought, destroy all creativity. At least this is true for Whickmuz, thus you find him here.

The situation? We're well and truly flummoxed! Before we could cross the Chasm, before we could confront Molag Grunda, we were stopped by a few irksome focus stones!\n\nThe wee ginger mage says we need to break the stones, but good luck with that!

The water's been contaminated. To top it off, whatever's tainted the johads seems to attract the desert beetles.\n\nWorkers won't go near the johads, and with good reason. But I still need to find out what's contaminated our lifeblood.

I do. The workers have rest camps in between the johads. If someone brought in this poison, there may be evidence of it there.\n\nIf you can find something of import, bring it to me. I'll be at the main johad down the road.

Nothing other than the multitude of Dremora sitting on top of them! I could handle this myself, but I didn't want to make the rest of the troops sad by showing off my awesome battle skills.\n\nBut, you, on the other hand. They're used to that from you.
You didn't notice it? The enormous tree in the middle of <<Ac:1>>?\n\nNobody takes a moment to look up these days. All this beauty directly above you and you're staring straight at the dirt. Typical.
It's not my place to reveal the nature of the oath. For that, you must speak to our current caretaker, <<1>>. If you wait, you might also speak to the new caretaker, when one is chosen.
Indeed.\n\nIt's an honor to be selected. Once the preparations are complete, the old caretaker passes his duties to the new one.
Huh. <<1>> won't be happy about that.
Very bright, good sense of humor. No patience for <<1>>'s mischief. Years ago she'd had enough, so she took him apart and scattered him around <<Ac:2>>.\n\nI laughed hard enough to shift my barrow.
Then if fate is to be believed, the winds are ready as well.\n\nRun quickly, my friend … or do not … either way we will have our answer.
If my tone was overly sharp you have my apologies. I am receiving hourly reports on the situation at the docks. It is … grim.

King Ranser just wants us to keep fighting to the bitter end. Seems he wants to go out in a blaze of glory. \n\nCan't say I'm fond of that strategy, but the king's beyond reason. That damn mage he had gave him some fool notion he wants us to try.

Before he vanished, Reezal-Jul told the king about this last ditch enchantment that would help us hold the tor. \n\nWe're supposed to take these packets of magical powder and pour their contents into the braziers in each of the towers.

Kill the Orcs? I don't know. What I do know is that this is our last chance, and you're the only soldier I'd trust to even make the attempt. \n\nIf it doesn't do anything, go up and tell the king. Maybe he'll realize it's time to surrender.
Most of us choose to sleep in our own bones. But <<1>> borrowed those of a long dead Elf. He was always restless, even in life.

So you do, and if our fates are true, the wind will wait.\n\nI will answer your questions if I can, but know that I am no wise man. I am a dockworker. I only grew this beard and adorned myself so because the woman told me it was my fate to do this.

Then he has truly gone mad. There's no reason to waste further lives defending this lost cause. The king will just have to be restrained.\n\nHave you seen Captain Taern? She and I should do this together.
<<1>>'s true bones are gnarled in the roots of the Barrowbough. Some say they're the oldest in the orchard.\n\nLook out for him, would you? His recklessness tends to wear at the others buried here.
Worse. If you find yourself on the docks, I'd ask that you lend a hand. Our guards are outmatched, and may not be able to hold out much longer.

Damn it, and knowing her, she'll follow orders without question and get the King's Guard killed.\n\nYou'll have to find Taern and convince her to stand down. If she refuses, look for that chest of sleep scrolls, and just use one to knock them all out.

Yes. It's actually probably best I go alone. \n\nAt this point, I'll do whatever it takes. I'll give the king one last chance to listen to reason. But if he won't, then I'll just have to make him see things my way.

No. The woman told me to come out to the desert, find someone I had never met, and observe this strange race.\n\nI thought she was crazy, but then I thought about it, and my curiosity won out. And now I believe … because look … you are here!

It seems that someone else told her that it was her fate to approach me and send me out here. It was yet another person before that … leading back in an endless chain ….\n\nThat's only if it's all true, of course … but that is what we will test.

I do not know. Can you?\n\nEven if you can, though, does that mean fate is changeable, or does it mean that you have strayed from your destined path? Perhaps fate is not damaged by this. Perhaps it would be your loss to bear.
Yes. Tu'whacca, the caretaker of souls. He does not look kindly on those who would strike his honored children. At least this is what I was taught. In such times … even my faith is shaken.
It's just …. What I mean is, I can't bear to lose him. We won't be able to bear it! He's so excited, and it's such a great honor, but he doesn't know what it will cost our family!

When we go, we leave a caretaker behind to watch over <<A:1>>. The caretaker and the tree are our link between this place and where the Wilderking sends us.\n\nI didn't expect <<2>> to be chosen. And he can't stay. He can't.
You don't know what this means to me. I'm afraid if I tell him, he might think I've made up a story to keep him with me.\n\nNo, that's not it. I'm afraid he'll choose his duty over his wife.

I'm pregnant. I only found out recently. Erunor doesn't know. I'm not sure I want him to, but if he knew, he could leave with us!\n\nPlease, please, convince him to return to the Wilderking's realm with us!
Then I do too.\n\nLet us wait and see what happens. If a storm appears, I suggest you run faster this time … or do not … perhaps it is our fate to do this over and over again for all time …?
Thank you. We'll bury these as soon as my sister calms down.\n\nWait a moment. Someone's coming in. No! No, it can't be! Not you!
Hrmm. Maybe I will, at that. \n\nLet me see that journal, mate.
What's this? Alten Corimont …?\n\nSithis take it! This is nought but the ravings of a madman. Where's the secret he promised?
I do not dispute this. I only hope for your sake that the Tricky God feels the same.

Evil is abroad across Cyrodiil. Innocence and piety are no protection. Bands of robbers killed our abbot and priests and looted our relics. All but myself, Constantina, and Trano have fled. The priory must close, for now at least.
Do you speak the truth? Mura thought everyone was dead. Now you tell me good news and hope fills this one's heart.
Before he escaped, we kept Rilis' soul encased in a single binding stone passed down by the Keepers. For ages it was his prison.\n\nWe're going to put him back, but this time, he's going in pieces.

Mura has heard tales of the witches who roam the west. Some good, some bad. This one will not turn down help, though, yes?\n\nMura will find her way back to the mill. Just let one of those creatures get in this one's way!

Dollie is planning to release little creatures into the Khajiiti camp. Why don't we release some big creatures into the Wood Elf camp? One up them! Creatures like the giant snakes around the base of Thormar.

No, no. The Elves will be fine. But the looks on their faces will be priceless! Kill a few of the giant snakes around the ruin and harvest their glands. Then stuff them in a barrel, right in the middle of camp!
I-I'm not sure. Perhaps the Motalion Necropolis? \n\nHer father's remains are there … yes, that may be where Shiri has gone.

It was not easy. I had to sneak by the Imperials, but I was worried about the book Shiri was carrying. I was worried the Withered Hand would get their hands on it.\n\nUnfortunately though, it seems they already had it.
It is just on the other side of the city.\n\nYou should go there. As soon as you can.
It is just on the other side of Satakalaam.\n\nAfter the Imperials are driven out of the city, getting into the necropolis will be easier.
Getting changed at the manor. You should do the same after you watch those scenes.\n\nYou'll find a change of clothes in the guest bedroom off the great hall. Then, go to Aranias in the garden.
Oh, they're invited too, dearie. You've all made me laugh so hard this year. Now come with me. You're going to have such fun!
You shame us, outsider. Perhaps we judge him in anger.\n\nVery well. <<1>> will stand with us to keep the Barrowbough from harm. When the invaders are repelled, he is free to decide his own fate.
Perhaps we were too hasty.\n\nVery well. Because <<1>> broke his exile only to warn us of so great a threat, we'll allow him to leave us in peace. But only if he aids us in driving out the invaders.

Yes, I do believe we can pass on.\n\nYet I must ask you to perform one more favor, if you would. These items still radiate with power from this odd ritual. Would you bury them for us? Then our spirits can truly be free.

I am most grateful for this kindness.\n\nTake the items to the far end of the graveyard. There, you should be able to find a suitable space to bury our effects in hallowed ground. I will meet you there.
Oh, you noticed? How clever of you. No, I don't want to be here, safely tucked away far behind the front lines. I want to be out on the battlefields, earning glory or at least an exciting death.

Sorcalin insisted. She apparently owes my father some old debt. I told her to just give me some gold and let me go fight. She said it was a debt of honor and I was staying with her. I've tried to sneak away but the guards keep dragging me back.
Well, I hear there's a giant snake to be slayed in some strange cave behind Daggerfall. But in these parts, Spindleclutch is your best bet for showing that undaunted spirit.

Of course. What's not to like? You get to travel Tamriel on someone else's coin. I might still be stuck in a little village in Rivenspire, grubbing in the dirt, if Odyle hadn't come to town recruiting. Best decision I ever made, leaving that dump.
You think farm work isn't dangerous? You ever been kicked in the head by a cow, or gored by a bull, or trampled by a horse? I bet you haven't, have you?

I thought not. Once, I was almost pecked to death by a flock of angry geese. I still have nightmares about that. \n\nNo, my friend, mercenary work is far less dangerous than toiling away on the farm. Much more profitable too.

Why does Daifa return if Aldeth keeps beating me, you mean? Pah. This one apologizes. She knows that faith in the Bandit is not always easy to understand.\n\nJust know that in crafting the prank, in trying, I show my faith to Baan Dar.

Fight alongside you? That would be a true honor. But the Fighters Guild needs me right now. Someone has to command our forces.\n\nAfter you clear a path to the Labyrinth, I shall lead the charge inside.
And luck to you, as well.\n\nMake them pay for all the pain and suffering they've caused. And for our friends and allies that have fallen along the way.
Ha! Better than those imps after I get through with them!\n\nUm, assuming you didn't kill them all already. You did? Kill them all, I mean. Didn't you?
The mill. Of course.\n\nWell, if I do run into any hostile creatures along the way, they'll regret the day they decided to invade our village!
The mill. Of course. That's a good idea.\n\nHey, I wanted to help. I did. I … just … oh, never mind. I'm going.

She's a coward and a bully. Once her nature's revealed, my father won't let her back into <<1>>.\n\nWe'll need to return whatever she took to the harpies on the balcony. Head inside and find it. I'll try to convince them we're all friends.
