It was one of those coincidences that can only be the work of the gods. I had exhausted my search of this area, and decided to move on.\n\nI sat down to rest, leaned back, and fell down this hole. I was knocked out, but awoke to find … I was here.

I am not certain. Perhaps she has. Morwha knows that would have been better for her, but I have a feeling she abides for me. We had a very special love, and it was hard for me to leave. \n\nI owed this to my father, though, may his soul rest in peace.

I decide the direction of the Pact in Cyrodiil. Dreet carries my orders to the Generals Dar-Liurz and Jeggord. They post these to the mission boards for all to see.\n\nGeneral Dar-Liurz will tell you more.
General Jeggord supervises the other missions. Speak with him to learn about them. He glares at us from across the way.\n\nDo not be shy—Jeggord hisses loudly but seldom bites.
Brilliant! You follow the trail and my sister and I will spread out to look for Father. They can't have taken him far—he is an old man, after all.

The monks have done all the work for us. We'll just walk into the temple, and from there onto the Path. I believe I read once that the whole temple is suffused in moon-sugar vapors that allow for the mind to open to what can't normally be seen.
Sure, Hallowed. I'll tell you what I can. I've been listening to half-crazed moon priests since I was a cub. I think I remember a few things.

Damned right it's going to be dangerous. You heard Tharn, right? He intends to walk the path with us. Bastard is powerful, capable of almost anything. If he's figured out some way to twist the Path against us, there's no telling what we'll face.

The priests kept going on and on about how the Path was mostly about the spirit. Something about "walking into the heart of the Khajiit, the soul of the lunar faith." I think they mean that each part of the path represents something.

The monks do almost all the work for us. We'll just walk into the temple, and from there onto the Path. I think they bathe the temple in moon-sugar vapors. Something about "opening the mind's eye?" I just think the monks like the smell.

Yeah. You know, manifestations? Shazah used to tell me stories about past Manes that fought great battles on the Path. They fell in love, they saw distant shores. Whatever we'll face in there will be about our challenges in the here and now.
Yes. That tree is me. Or rather it is the life form in which I was the life force. \n\nBut another came and by foul magics took my place. Merethrin the mage. He cursed us both.

Me? No, not personally. But I heard stories. It's some sort of freakish creature, cobbled together from living bodies and feasting on the blood of the townsfolk.\n\nAt least, that's the way I heard it described.

Yes. Calls himself Reezal-Jul. A real charmer, that one.\n\nHe sent rocks tumbling down the mountain to seal the pass to Doomcrag, managing to destroy half of Crestshade in the process. Then he unleashed a blood-curse on the town. He's insane.
Indeed. Abnur Tharn and I have been meditating, scrying, and poring over Mannimarco's notes. And at long last we've discovered the location of the Halls of Torment.

Did he? What surprisingly good advice. Titanborn and I are more likely to kill each other than we are to help.\n\nThe choice is yours, but I recommend choosing brains over brawn. I have valuable knowledge of the Daedra. And don't forget, I'm the mage.
No details do I know, only that by arcane ritual did Merethrin pervert the natural order, binding me here and him there.\n\nI to lose my body and he to lose his mind.
This I never knew and Merethrin will not recall. He was a revered member of the Mages Guild in Shornhelm. Perhaps answers are there to this question. Or perhaps not.
Then your choice is clear! I've known Sai Sahan longer than anyone. I should be the one to go!\n\nIt's your decision, just know that I'd give my life for you or for Sai. Would Tharn do the same?

They were afraid, like everyone else. After I raised up the land under the sea and smashed that ship … even though nobody got hurt they said my magic was too dangerous. You're the only one who isn't afraid of me.\n\nYou're … not afraid, right?

Thank you. You won't regret it.  \n\nBack in the Coldharbour slave pits, the shriven used to whisper about the Halls of Torment. When I think of what Sai must be going through …. We'll bring him back, or die trying!

Tharn was always mocking Sai. Making jokes at his expense. Sai never responded, but I know it hurt him deeply. The Daedra must have sensed that.\n\nOn the plus side, a doppelganger with Tharn's face was much more satisfying to kill.
I'm sorry. It just happened.\n\nWait. Something's wrong. Can you feel that? The land's in pain, burning hot. Look! The farm's burning!

Sadly, no. Those of us stuck in this half-life, tied to the abomination, can sense each other. But the rest of the town was turned into those poor, feral beasts. \n\nThe ones who escaped or found true death—those are the lucky ones.

I don't know. Days before, tremors shook the town. And then it was as though half the mountain fell upon us.\n\nWhen the dust cleared, we were set upon by vampires and that damn blood-curse. I was able to get some people away, praise Arkay.
In the most expedient manner possible. The ritual unleashes a magic that tracks down the blood and targets the creatures connected to it.

We were excavating for artifacts when Dominion soldiers showed up, demanding we turn over anything we'd found.\n\n<<1>> showed them what we had, but <<2>> insisted we work faster. No protocols, no safeguards!

I have no idea. The Mages Guild has procedures for a reason!\n\nNot that the soldiers listened. We found an ancient scepter made from bone. But before we could properly contain the artifact, one of those idiots grabbed it.

That's right. And if it weren't for you, I'd have joined them.\n\nI'm heading back to our base camp. You should speak with <<1>> if you think you can help sort out this mess. You can't be any worse than <<2>>!
You need to distract them! Kill their leader and burn their tents! We'll rescue the villagers!
There isn't time to indulge in idle fantasies and what-ifs. Please, help the villagers below! I need a moment to gather what wits I have left!
That's all I ask.\n\nI'll open the portal. I think it's best that I travel with you, and make introductions as a neutral party. That might make things easier.
Huh, you make some sense after all.\n\nI will support this foolish plan if you can convince the other leaders.
How dare you! I should kill you where you stand!\n\nHistory will remember the Skald-King as the Bane of Molag Bal! I will support your foolish plan. Now get out of my sight!
Perhaps. But I must think about this.\n\nGo! All this talk has given me a headache.
All right, then. I'll agree, provided you can convince the barbarian and the child queen. I don't envy you the task. They're more pig-headed than I am!
Arkay's beard, you're a bold one! But you may be right.\n\nIf you can convince the barbarian and the child queen to agree, I'll consider it.
I'm not convinced, but let me think on it. Something must be done. On that, we agree.
An excellent point. Very well. If you can convince the other leaders, you have my support.
Well, it's certainly not what they'll be expecting. Very well. I'll agree, if you can convince the others.

Don't presume to think you can intimidate me! History will remember me as a bold and decisive leader who cared about her people.\n\nBut you do have a point. If you can convince the others, we'll try your plan. Now, leave me in peace.
Nor do I, but I'll agree to nothing until I've conferred with my advisors. Now, go annoy the others. I've had enough for one day.
<<1>>, we shall return you to the bones that bore you in life. May you sleep and forget yourself in time.

Then the vampires will become mindless beasts, no longer capable of posing any threat.\n\nI've been developing this ritual for years, but I've never had the chance to test it until now. If this works, it could be a major breakthrough against vampirism.

Oh, there's not much to say. Dull as a rusty dagger, me! If I told you about myself, I'd put you to sleep.\n\nAnd with all these Wormies about? They'd turn you into a skeleton! We'd make quite the pair then, wouldn't we?

Walked, really. Came here, found a beautiful city with wonderful people, and decided to make it my home. The treethane was a nice sort, said I'd fit right in.\n\nI was so excited, I fell asleep on the spot!

Oh my, yes. Falinesti never stays in one place for long. I'd planned to see the lands without walking around so much.\n\nBut all that's left of it are the holes in the ground. Lots of secrets down there, but you didn't hear it from me.

I'd been traveling for quite a while, you see? This was my chance to sit down and relax. I don't remember nodding off.\n\nBut when I woke the city was gone and I was covered in dirt. You'd think I'd been asleep for a century!
Oh, everything blends together after a while. Can't remember being anything else, now that I think of it. Funny.
An explorer! See the world, meet new people … when you get down to it, that's what I liked most about life.\n\nBut that was long ago. And as much as these bones suit me, they complicate travel.
They did! I tried to tell them I was no ordinary talking skull, but they threw me out.

It summons all the shades, I suspect. It certainly doesn't control them. Not that I've found, anyway.\n\nAlthough … hmmm. The markings carved into the scepter are old Ayleid for "<<1>>." Could that mean the creature at the heart of the ruin?
That's what I said! But they ignored me and droned on. Something about the "flame-meld" and "dark anchors." \n\nMade it sound like they were nautical blacksmiths. Idiots.

It's the only shade we've heard speak, though it mostly just wails. It is rather pale, come to think of it. And the scepter works obsidian into bone, which is an old form of necromantic control ….\n\nSay, would you care to help prove a theory?

If that shade is in fact <<Ac:1>>, that <<z:2>> may have some control over it. And if it's directing the rest of the shades, perhaps you could force it to stop.\n\nBesides, we can't allow <<3>>'s ancient traps to remain active. Not this close to <<4>>.

My children protect this Orchard because Molag Bal commands it. They aren't evil. They're slaves of the Harvest Heart!\n\nInstead of destroying them, help me set them free. Imagine, an army of vampires that owes you a favor!
General Am-Shadal supervises the other mission boards. Go talk to him.

There are many Wood Elves interred around the Barrowbough. I catalogue their names, cities of origin, and learn about their lives.\n\nThen I sing their stories beneath the roots, so the old bones beneath have something new to dream about.

Just another of Molag Bal's clever witticisms, I suppose. It's an orchard from which he plucks the fruit of his vampiric creations.\n\nOr something poetic and disturbing like that. But we have a ritual to prepare for.

I've always known <<1>>. He managed to get into trouble when he was just a skull! How he learned to climb like that still eludes me.\n\nThe spinners who came before were no different. Dealing with <<1>> has been the only real constant in <<Ac:2>>.
Ha! No, not me.\n\nNot yet.

Your parents aren't from <<1>>? That's surprising. You carry yourself like a native.\n\nSpinners keep the stories of our people flowing. We focus upon the past, present, and future of every Wood Elf … even you!

We drive the rhythm of our people. Every Wood Elf has meaning, no matter how small. Spinners find the perfect tune for each so the stories of our strongest and our weakest can harmonize together.\n\nAt least, that's how I see it.

No. If I did, I would have presented it long ago, and perhaps saved her life.\n\nAs it is, though, I do not expect to have her exonerated. I only ask that her remains be consecrated. I understand your hesitation. Perhaps you would at least consider it?

Take these funerary oils and perform the consecration. \n\nYou will know Zariya's corpse because she still wears the wooden ring I gave her when we were first married. Find her remains and pour the oil upon them. That is all I ask.
<<1>>.\n\nA bad man, who sleeps inside these ruins. When he wakes, I'll be trapped here forever. I'll do everything I can to get away!
I did not! <<1>>'s servants hurt those people. They don't like you if you aren't from here.\n\nWhen he wakes, he'll control them completely. Just like me.
The bone scepter holds power over <<1>>'s monsters. Over me. I can't lie to you.\n\nBesides, lying is wrong.
One of <<1>>'s victims.\n\nBut I don't have to be. If you can free me before he wakes, I'll leave. Then he'll go back to sleep, forever!
Take up the blade, and you will see. The sword-cursed are here among us already, circling like half-starved jackals.\n\nCan you not sense their jealousy? Their spite? The air is thick with it.

The curse was forged in blood and envy. I murdered my dearest friend in a jealous rage, and the blade bears that taint still.\n\nThe sword-cursed cannot bear the thought of losing the blade. If you touch it, they will come for you.
Yes. And they will not stop so long as you carry it.\n\nOnce you fall—and fall you will—you will be consumed by the same jealous desire that drives them.

They are long dead and thus cannot be killed, though they will sleep, for a time.\n\nBut the blade calls out to them, always. When they wake, they shall seek it out again … and the one who keeps it. You have been warned.

I've read accounts of these foul artifacts. Molag Bal uses them to enslave large communities and to empower specific parts of his divine portfolio.\n\nIn this case, I believe the Heart is greatly increasing the rate at which the vampirism spreads.
Not easily. But that's where my ritual comes in. By the time I finish casting it, the Heart will be no more and the vampires will no longer pose a threat to our forces.
She has her reasons, and I respect them, as I do her. It would make no difference if I defend myself now.\n\nThe important thing is that we find out what's happened to the johads.
Blast it all! If <<1>> got his grubby finger-bones ahold of it, I'll scatter him all over <<2>>.
Oh. He's sleeping, then? <<1>> was noisy, disruptive, and a terrible tease, but I'll miss him.\n\nI'm sorry. Would you excuse me? I need to collect my thoughts.

I do not hide. I abstain, I withdraw, I reject! I renounce this war and all who wage it. It is madness. A veil has fallen across the eyes of all, obscuring the true nature of what we struggle and slaughter over.
They will be plagued by the victims of the sword, just as you were. But this is why I hid the sword away! \n\nI beg you, take it and leave. I cannot bear to look at it.
No! I cannot! I will not! This is all Ihlqub's fault! His and Sayeedeh's! I will … I will … no. \n\nYour words are true. Leave the sword with me.
There's a big sparkly door inside the Constellation Room. It's this big lock <<1>> made, to keep him asleep inside.\n\nShe doesn't come around anymore. I think that's why the door isn't so sparkly.

<<1>>'s wife. They fought and fought, because he was a bad man and she was a good woman. But she thought she could change him.\n\nWhen she realized he'd always been bad, she locked him in here. But the lock grew weak, and now he's waking.
That's easy. The Moaning Room, the Smelly Room, and … the Forbidden Room! But don't worry, I can keep you safe.\n\nWe should just go there. I'll point out what we need.

<<1>> left three of the things we need in special rooms around the ruins. The fourth is stuck inside some of <<2>>'s servants. If you smash them open, I won't tell.\n\nBut about all the pieces … I don't know how to make them work together. I'm sorry.

Find the Lord of Schemes' binding totems and destroy them. They're spaced evenly around the Harvest Heart.\n\nAs each totem breaks, the vampires will be separated from Molag Bal and the energy of my spell will flow into them, wiping their minds clean.
What? Sandblown Mine? My friend, I don't even know where that is … or what it is, even! Is it nearby?
Tell me then, is it madness that drives you to barge in here like this? \n\nOr perhaps you're here to surrender on behalf of your people? If that's the case, I accept.

That's a bit of a dreary subject, but I prefer that over some angry line like "I've come here to kill you, Your Majesty!" I'm glad you didn't say that.\n\nSo you want to talk about everyone's favorite Daedric Prince then? What of him?

That would be utter madness …  but I do like the thought of seeing that next to my name in the history books.\n\nAll right. If Ayrenn and Jorunn agree to attend, I'll be there. If this is an assassination attempt, though, I'm taking you with me.

Ha! I'm sorry. I think I must've misheard you. For a moment, I thought you were saying you wanted to battle a Daedric Prince. \n\nThat would be especially funny if you wanted my help. So, what was it you really meant to say?

Shazah was always telling me stories … I never thought I'd see this place. It's the Plane of Jode, Hallowed! The place where the Bright Moons dwell, the home of the gods. It's … different than I expected in some ways. But that makes sense.
The Path is changing to suit us, to reflect the challenges we face. Dull claws … this is just like the monks' prayers. Put something in front of me, let me hit it!
Remember back to your training, Khali … Let's just wait a moment. If I'm right, the Path will show us the way.

To Mournhold, where Skald-King Jorunn is waiting for us. I'm given to understand that his palace is inaccessible at present, and for a variety of reasons the Tribunal Temple is … inappropriate.\n\nHe's offered to meet us at the guild plaza. Shall we?
Sending people to a mine? By Morwha's left teat, why would I do that? Is there … um … is there gold there?

Dreadful! Well … all this talk of snakes and mines—it is exhausting. I'll just be going now. I have a long day of work tomorrow. Lifting things … you know, carrying them. That sort of thing. It has been a pleasure speaking with you!

Well I … that is to say … They made me do it! Friend, I beseech you—show mercy. I am an innocent man! I had no choice. They told me they would feed me to the snake if I didn't cooperate!\n\nPlease just let me go!

Find the Lord of Schemes's binding totems and destroy them. They are spaced evenly around the Harvest Heart.\n\nAs each totem breaks, my children will be separated from Molag Bal and the energy protecting the Harvest Heart will falter.
We have a history built upon the bedrock of respect and mutual appreciation! We're just having a bit of a spat, that's all.
Go talk to Dar-Liurz about them. I've got my hands full over here.
Give or take a decade. It's my fault, really. I was insufferable!\n\nDon't know how she put up with me, to be honest. Taking me apart was the best thing for us both!
Thirty or … fifty years, I think? Yes, let's say fifty.

Not at all! Well … I do wonder how she'd fare buried up to her neck while I sit in a nice, warmly lit cave, but it's a passing fancy.\n\nShe used to visit my skull and sing to me, even when we were squabbling. That's true friendship, right there.
What's so special about a great tree the size of a sailing ship, sealing the old bones beneath it in eternal slumber?\n\nNot much beyond all that, I suppose.
To keep people out! Why else? Spirits hate disturbances.\n\nAnd to keep the bones from wandering away. The Barrowbough grew around the oldest skull in the ground, you know.
Ha! Heh. Most think it belongs to the god Y'ffre.\n\nHis death made the bones of the earth, or so it goes. Depends on who tells the story.
The big hill in the center of the orchard? I suppose it doesn't look much like a skull now. Been buried too long.
Talk to General Atahba about them. She's on the other side of the gate.
General Thoron supervises the other missions. He is usually found on the other side of the gate, waiting for new orders from the Grand Warlord.
Yes. King Dynar and our forces are preparing to attack the Reaver Citadel to the north.\n\nAnd on my way to find you, I noticed a strange shipyard to the east and a Redguard settlement to the west.
Discuss those with General Jeggord. He does not like me telling of his responsibilities.
You found it where? \n\nWait. You brought the axe back? It's here with you?
Absolutely not! Get it away from here, immediately! I cursed that axe myself! It draws spirits and undead like flies to honey.

Of course! I wanted them out of the mine, out of Greenshade. You see what they do to the forest, everywhere they go? They cut down everything in sight!\n\nAlthough if you're standing here, I suppose the axe worked. That's actually good news.
No, that's not necessary. Now that it has served its purpose, I'll simply remove the enchantment. You can keep it! A souvenir.\n\nNow, give it here.
How should I know? Sai and I are friends! Good friends. Nothing more!
It's Molag Bal's last line of defense before we reach his inner sanctum, and it's certainly his most powerful. The Dremora stationed there have turned it into a heavily fortified city.
It was the strangest sight! More shipwrecks than a shipyard, really. It was as if they just fell out of the sky.\n\nAnd there was an awful lot of them.
Oh, I doubt it's an actual settlement. That's just what the architecture reminded me of.\n\nI wasn't able to get too close, but I swear I heard music coming from that direction.
<Which key?>

Not quite, but soon. He's waiting for you and a few of the others to meet up with him. They're gathering on the land bridge just to the north.\n\nI'm going to head in that direction as soon as we're done here.
You know, it sounded very festive to me. Isn't that strange, in a place like this? What could any of these soul shriven have to be happy about?
Other than a massive graveyard of ships of various designs spread across the valley to the east of here?\n\nNo, not really.

The same thing that happened to me. I had her enchanted as well, of course.\n\nShe will come back, and we will continue on our way. We both love the desert, Musi and I, and this way, we can wander these sands together … forever.

Musi? Aw, I couldn't ask her to do that. She is a lover, not a fighter.\n\nWhen the jackals were chasing us, I realized they were going to catch us, so I did what any loyal friend would do: I commanded her to run on, and I sacrificed myself.
<Which key?>

Brilliant young woman. Keeps records of all the bones buried here, big and small alike. Every dead Elf in the ground is important enough for her to track!\n\nSuppose it's why she was annoyed with me for inhabiting these Elf bones, instead of my own.
No idea!\n\nSome dead Elf from another era. Probably won a war, lost a war, or refused to fight in a war. You know how it goes with these things.
Banished makes it sound so severe! More of an extended vacation. It's good to put a little distance between your family, especially when you disagree on a few small matters.
<Which key?>
Name's Fabricias. I'm a treasure hunter—or an "archaeological researcher," if you're not one for straight talk.
Extended family. Second-cousins-in-arms? Distant relations thrice removed!\n\nWhen there are so few of you left, I suppose they become your family. Even when all you do is bicker.

The others want to sleep until everyone forgets them, to which I say pah! A daily constitutional does wonders to brush out the cobwebs. So does a dandelion, if you have actual cobwebs.\n\nBut family is family, so I stay in this wretched place.
I'm not sure. I thought I heard a voice calling for help inside the cave. Then I was suddenly attacked.
Gatekeeper to the Barrowbough. A friend, long ago. Not so fond of me in recent centuries.\n\nShe'll understand why we need to get in, I'm sure of it.

What's to tell? We were on patrol, watching for more of Montclair's mischief. When we stopped to check on Hinault's farm, we were ambushed!\n\nWe knew Montclair had troops, but we never expected that he had a damn army!
Thank you.

My mates and I were left here to mind the camp while the bulk of the expedition set out for the ruin. We kept telling the centurions … we told them that there were too few of us to protect the supplies. But no one listens to the diggers.

Of course I do! But I wasn't gonna tell those troll-brained murderers. Here, I'll put it on your map. It's the least I can do. I won't need it anymore. I'm heading back to Cyrodiil first chance I get.

Aye, by the upstanding gentlemen you see outside. There were just too many of them. I would have been killed too if someone hadn't told them that I know where the ruin is. They've been pounding the snot out of me for days.

No. You are a Redguard, but if you are not from the Alik'r, these are not your ancestors. There is no dishonor in harming them, no curse.\n\nBut the fact that the dead have risen at all … it bodes poorly for all of us. This should not happen here!

My fellow guards will not strike the Ra-Netu either—Jessmyn, Pierjean, and Emydal—I fear for their lives. \n\nPlease, find them and send them away, then meet at the warehouse. The dockmaster hides there, and he may know the cause of all this.
But what about stopping the Ra-Netu from getting into the city? What about the other guards? \n\nI cannot simply abandon them … can I?
<Which key?>

In ages past, the vilest of my people were interned here as punishment.\n\nToday, the Banished Cells contain a sole prisoner, High Kinlord Rilis XII. Rilis is long dead, but his Daedric pact sustains him, and a prisoner he remained, until today.
Yes, well, I am both suspicious and curious. If you are an assassin, though, get on with it. But remember this: you're coming to Sovngarde with me!
Where the All-Flags Army was born …? Hmm. If the other leaders agree, I will attend. If nothing else, it should make a good story.\n\nNow leave me before my dinner gets cold.
To fear death is to fear life! I am Nord. When my time comes, I will embrace it. Sovngarde will be glorious! No meetings, no schemes!\n\nBut you're not here to talk philosophy. What do you want?
Who? The three alliances? Has magical travel rattled your brain?\n\nSpeak plainly. What do you ask of me?
We have much to do. Come.
The shades defend my home from thieves. Neither I nor my servants bear any interest in the living. My work concerns one who died long ago.\n\nAnd now, I would know why this creature travels with you.

Simple-minded thing. Those wards haven't contained me for decades. I remain within by choice.\n\nNow, I'm at a critical juncture in my research and I need this creature to complete it. If you interfere, I'll drive you from my home. Now, begone!

One of many atrocities my misguided "people" have wrought on this peerless race of unmatched predators. The Khajiit are my brothers, my true people.\n\nThose Dunmer who still keep slaves are heartless fools. If you ask me, they should all be hanged!

Oh, you saw that exchange, did you? Why does every extraplanar creature I meet want to talk to me? Am I wearing a welcome sign around my neck? Do I look like I carry Dremora snacks in my pockets?\n\nWhere is the respect for my rank and my station?

Yes! I was cruely born without a tail, without claws, but I know where I belong. If I can just find the right mixture, I can fix that.\n\nThen all those fools in Mournhold will see that they were wrong!
Ha! No, of course not. Nobody that important.
I, ah, don't know. Yes, it's left me completely.\n\nWait, did you hear that? Could've sworn it was a Wormie. Ha! Must've been my imagination.

And she may have been sent to provide false information. To lead us blindly into an ambush—or worse!\n\nNo, we shall not deal with Dremora, especially in this place. I ordered one of the fighters to keep an eye on that one.

She … she left me? She always did put the needs of the community above her family. I suppose I have to respect her wishes.\n\nAnd she'll have to respect that I'll tear down the fabric of reality to get her back.
What? The Chasm? Piece of cake.\n\nI'd say that facing a Xivilai and Winged Twilight on my own was a bit of a challenge, but then I'd be lying. They fell like great trees before a woodcutter's axe.

An overdue appointment with Molag Bal himself, I guess. \n\nI don't want to sound overly confident, but I feel like I've gotten better since we got here. And I was, as you'll no doubt agree, damned impressive before Coldharbour.

Ah, the vampires. Should be a worthy challenge. Gathwen wants me to take a patrol back through the Chasm and let King Dynar know what's been happening.\n\nMight even have time to stop for a drink or two in the Hollow City.
I do not know. I smelled something sweet and couldn't resist, it reminded me of home. Next thing I knew I was being attacked by these things.
You have my thanks.
I was walking along and I got a bad feeling from that cave. I was creeping closer to look when I was attacked.
Thank you for your help.

Elden Root. We should have a somewhat warmer reception there, as I have known Queen Ayrenn for quite some time. \n\nThat being said, I expect that she'll be accompanied by heavily armed guards. Ayrenn is friendly, but not foolish.
To Wayrest. Expect a certain level of formality. The court of High King Emeric is often filled with scandalmongers and subversives. Therefore, protocol is the order of the day.\n\nShall we?
Yes, and it must be consumed alive. The frog will allow you to see the forest like you never have before.\n\nOnce your journey begins, the spirits of the forest will guide you.

It's not as macabre as it sounds. He has no body; I speak of his soul.\n\nThe Keepers will siphon his essence into not one, but four binding stones to keep his power divided. He'll hardly be conscious in that state, let alone able to summon Daedra.
You have the most difficult task of all.\n\nI need you to find Rilis and defeat him, if you can.
It's time for you to speak to Brackenleaf. Only he can judge whether you are worthy to serve him as one of his Briars. \n\nFind him in the center of this grove. If he wills it, we will meet again.

Nervous? Sure. Everyone's nervous. Even Vanus and the King.\n\nBut if I had a gold piece for every time I got nervous before diving into a dungeon … well , I'd have a lot of gold pieces! Don't worry. We won't fail you.

If not for my brother, I'd be in there swinging a sword with the best of the warriors. But Raynor and Gabrielle need me. Someone's got to watch their backs while they do the magic stuff.\n\nBut we'll make it out of this. Just like we always do.

My lady, I'll fight by your side and follow you to the end of the world. And I mean that quite literally! Now go tell the old man we're ready.\n\nAnd just so you know, I really did dream about this moment.

Oh ho. The Briars you say? The Briars carry my heart within them. They protect it with their very lives. It's a lot to give to protect a tree, especially one as old as me.\n\nTell me, why do you want to join my Briars?
Not surprising. The Briars are hunters, after all. It's in their nature to crave larger, more dangerous prey.\n\nAre you prepared to face that challenge?

Good, good. I think you will find this forest is full of new things to discover. Never ate a frog and found yourself talking to a tree before, did you?\n\nOf course, not all the things you will discover here are safe. Are you prepared?

Ha, no one has ever given me that answer. Carefree as a sapling, letting the breeze bend your branches this way and that. \n\nBut becoming a Briar requires determination. Are you willing to do what it takes to become a hunter?

Very good. I trust Glaras has told you about the spirits of the hunt.\n\nFirst, you must decide which fits you best: the snake's dark purpose, the tiger's grim determination, or the kinship of the wolf.
Lithe and quick, striking with lethal efficiency is the Snake. Interesting choice.\n\nThe Snake's prey is the Wolf. If you wish to be like the Snake, you must hunt its prey.
Sharp-toothed and clever, the Wolf understands that sometimes it is better to hunt in a pack than alone.\n\nThe Wolf's prey is the Tiger. Hunt the Wolf's prey to become like the Wolf.

Relentless and strong, the Tiger stalks its prey without flagging and overpowers it without hesitation when the moment is right.\n\nThe Tiger's prey is the Snake. To be like the Tiger, you must hunt its prey.
The masters you fought were illusions, but they fought with all the strength of their real counterparts.\n\nTell me, what spirit animal did you choose?
Go to the Wolf's shrine. Pray at the brazier and receive the blessing of Brackenleaf's Briars. Then return to me for the final rite of initiation.
Go to the Tiger's shrine. Pray at the brazier and receive the blessing of Brackenleaf's Briars. Then return to me for the final rite of initiation.

Members of our expedition recognize the city from when it was still a part of Nirn. They are familiar with the guild halls and how we can use them to our advantage.\n\nIt's ironic. One of Molag Bal's captured cities is about to be turned against him.

I did mention I had a plan, didn't I? No? Well, I have a plan.\n\nI can provide a spell to light your way. It should help you navigate the chamber. I'll make sure the others follow … after we know it's safe, of course.

Little details. Making sure the right agents are in the right places. Protecting Pact interests. That sort of thing.\n\nI could tell you more, but then Naryu would want to kill you. Or maybe just cut on you a little.

Areldur and I will think on a plan to deal with the High Kinlord. Defeating Rilis is pointless if we can't hold him.\n\nIn the meantime, the area up ahead is under Keeper Voranil's jurisdiction. Even if he lives, he'll need your help.

You must lead the Five Companions into this final battle. We are, all of us, prepared to sacrifice our lives to see this through to the end.\n\nOur plan is to use the Amulet of Kings to invest you with the power to do battle with the Daedric Prince.

No doubt the God of Schemes has rallied his most powerful servants to his side, but his arrogance has already proven to be his undoing. He may not even consider you a threat.\n\nWe shall endeavor to prove him utterly, catastrophically wrong.
<This Elf female suffered a similar fate to the one outside. Her skin is taut and dry, the body completely drained of fluid. A signet ring is also present on her hand.>
<You slip the ring from the emaciated hand and deposit it into your pack.>
Watching, listening, waiting.
This one will know it when she sees it. Now, move along. You're blocking my sun.
<The flesh of this unfortunate mage has been completely eaten away, but on one bony finger his signet ring remains intact.>
<You pry the ring from the bony finger with some effort. It bears the same symbol as the others.>
<A glint from within this gruesome stew catches your eye. It appears as though something shiny is floating among the foul-smelling contents of the brew.>
<You pull out a stiff, bloody finger from the brew. Still attached is a signet ring, which slips off easily into your hand.>

I don't think it's that simple. The Shade has assumed Naemon's form. It retains some of Naemon's memories, but it's a different entity now—with different motivations.\n\nThe Shade is undead, so we must consult the dead to discern its intentions.

I can distract <<1>>'s servants. Point <<Az:2>> at one of them and I'll blind it. Then you can smack it until it falls down.\n\nDon't worry, it's not like you're hurting it. They get back up again, eventually.

Then delay no longer. Any thirst I once felt for life has long since faded. All I seek now is the peace of death.\n\nThough I want to despise the mage for what he did, I feel more pity than hate. I hope this gives him release as well.
Oh, all right.\n\nThe most important thing is the book <<1>> wrote in when she locked the door. We need to find that so we know what to do in the Constellation Room.

Not much you don't already know. Every blade's been turned toward the Daedra. Heard a big crew took down an anchor somewhere in Cyrodiil last week. Messy business, landed right on top of a skirmish between the Pact and the Dominion.
There isn't one—yet. I still have details to work out.\n\nJust find Imiril, and we may be able to turn this against Rilis.
Well spoken and point taken.\n\nTo be perfectly honest, I couldn't pass up the opportunity to meet you. Your exploits are legendary.

And you need all three of the alliance leaders to attend this meeting? A bold suggestion. I like it. \n\nVery well. I make no promises with regards to the negotiations themselves, but I will attend. That much, I promise.
A true champion is like a stone cast upon the waters of history. The ripples it creates travel far and wide.

Humility is a noble thing, but you must also remain strong and self-assured. A true champion is also history's pawn, and history is a cruel and unfeeling master.\n\nBut enough philosophy. What did you wish to speak with me about?
Isn't it obvious? I am a researcher into all things Ayleid. This is an Ayleid ruin. I want to get inside to continue my studies, whereas Enak seems determined to delay them.
They fascinate me. They were a great Elven culture, despite allegations of personal shortcomings. Think of how much they have to teach us, if only we knew more about them. That's what inspires me.

What's this? I'd heard that he was pestering people, but I certainly didn't suspect anything this sinister. \n\nNow that you mention it though, we have had more than a few disappearances recently. We naturally suspected the harpies.
Attempting to restore my son, despite your interruptions!\n\nThat creature is a piece of him, an imperfect piece. If I reunite flesh and spirit, I can revive my son.

This is it. The beginning of the blasted end. There's no point in pretending this isn't happening, or saying we're not ready. This challenge will not wait. \n\nCan you do what is necessary, no matter the cost? No matter how much it grieves you?

He's my son. I'd do anything to restore him to a fraction of himself. With refinement, I can make him whole again.\n\n<<1>> thought this hubris. If she hadn't left this world, I'd try to make her understand.

That we could one day be a family again. I needed time to refine my methods, and time I have had. And now, I have his spirit.\n\nI don't wish to harm this creature. But without <<Az:1>> to control it, I must resort to cruder methods.

You fear I would raise an undead army to march through <<1>>? My wife and I spurned <<2>> for a reason.\n\nBut in return for binding this creature to my son's husk, I pledge we will remain within our home, forever.

You what? That scepter is crafted from my own bones. It can bind the creature to his immortal husk!\n\nOnce <<1>>'s wounds knit, I'll summon him here. You must bind the creature to his husk. Set things to how they should be!
Indeed, the divine Hermaeus Mora, from whom all blessings flow. Long has the Prince of Fate tested me in this wasteland, but now he has found me worthy to worship him in Apocrypha, has he not?
There is always a choice. But you don't get to choose what is true, you only get to choose what you will do about it.\n\nDo you need a reminder about what lies ahead?

We are approaching the fortress of Molag Bal, perhaps the most dangerous place in all of Oblivion. Together, we five are mighty—even I will admit that—but I cannot invoke the ritual until we are in the presence of the dark prince, himself.

In exchange for this investiture of power, one of your companions will need to be sacrificed. It will be for you to decide which, when the time comes.\n\nThe infusion of power will not last for long. That's why we need to get close.

And then, what? I've no idea what will happen to you. Apotheosis? Disintegration? Too many unknowns and not enough information.\n\nBut if you defeat Molag Bal and survive, your soul and the soul of every other surviving vestige, should be restored.

No matter. I will double my devotions! None shall worship him as fervently as I. He will see and will draw me to him with a tender tentacle, setting me among his endless forbidden libraries, to study forever.

I knew these years of deprivation would win him over! But I have to prepare. I must study more of the Daedric Princes so that I can aid my lord in his struggles for power. More research is needed—he will understand.
I don't want to be here anymore. It hurt when I was a monster, it hurt worse than these chains.\n\nI want my father to sleep so I can go away.
Far away from here, somewhere safe and warm. Somewhere where I'd have friends.

Trying to live forever. Someone told him ice baths are the key. Ever since, he's been trying to get up the courage to jump in. He works up a sweat and runs out there but never goes in. Someday, he'll slip and fall into the lake by accident.
It helps me. Keeps him busy so I can read in peace. Makes it all worthwhile.

About time. I've put off leaving Evermore for weeks waiting for this. Of course, they'd put me in the stocks if I came back without it. \n\nWhether it's Clan Agluk or Clan Morkul could change the course of history.

A forgotten tumble of ruins in the desolate Lorkrata Hills. I found a trap door that should grant us access to the chambers beneath, but it's locked tight.\n\nLook around for a way to open the trap door and I'll meet you at the west tower.
What? Jofnir, murdered. This is dire news, comrade. The council must be told straight away. There will have to be an investigation … thank you for standing beside us, on this of all dark days.
A group of bandits took over this old mine. Not much ore left, I suppose that's why it was abandoned, but they are working us to the bone to get what ever there is.
I will once I gather my strength. Thank you for saving me. Please help the others.
Yes, this is my land, all around here. And it's my trees those damned loggers are chopping down. I moved here for the peace and quiet and now I have chop, chop, chop, crash! all day long.

Oh, I'd like to. But I signed a contract with them. Plus, every time I decide to boot them off my land, I think of those sharp, sharp axes they have. Then I decide to stay here, on my porch, and scowl menacingly at them.
<<1>>, commander of the Jade Dragoons. She sent us here personally from our garrison in <<2>>.
Of course. It isn't as though we're trying to save Rivenspire or anything, now is it?\n\nGo ahead. Ask your questions.

Her father gave her command of a portion of his troops—just as he did with Reezal-Jul. She's been active in the north and east, creating bloodfiends and causing chaos. I assume she has her eye on Northpoint. It would make a handsome prize.
Lleraya was a sweet young woman, committed to her family and infatuated with me. She didn't ask for what happened to her, but that doesn't excuse her behavior since.
More questions? You are a curious one. But who am I to deny your intellectual fulfillment? Ask, and I shall answer.

She told us recovering relics was of great import to the Dominion.\n\nI didn't ask questions, but I think it has something to do with <<1>>. Something's going on there, something political. I think the general wants to get out in front of it.
Ah, Renoit sent you then! He need not wait outside any longer—Draven will soon be inducted into the village. I'll see to it the guard lets him know.\n\nIs that all you seek, then?

I apologize, but you are an outsider. It's impossible for you to fully understand, but … suffice to say that those who are cured must stay in the village. It is for our protection, and theirs.\n\nDraven is in the guest house, if you wish to see him.

He's such a silly one! Of course I am, now that Kerbol's agreed to cure me!\n\nHe can come to the village now the first week's over. Is he still suspicious of these fine folk in the village, I wonder?

Yes. They're all over the Imperial Island, apparently. Some Daedric Prince summoned them. And they've killed all the people too. The Imperial army's over there, fighting them. Or maybe the soldiers all fled. No one seems to know.
What? That was his disease all along? Why didn't he tell me?\n\nWe have to go after him! He's probably frightened out of his mind! What was Kerbol thinking?
Ah, I'm afraid I can't talk about it. The village prides itself on privacy.\n\nI apologize if Renoit inconvenienced you in your travels, but as you can see, everything's fine.
Kerbol has a lot of explaining to do! Sealing his form? What does that even mean?\n\nGods, I pray Draven's all right!

Refugees, mostly, people fleeing from the island. Not many of them lately though. Not much screaming from the island either. There used to be a lot of both. Lithodor hears things too, though you can't believe half of what he says.
The general has no authority over the King's Guard. I take my orders directly from the king. \n\nThe king ordered us to charge and that's what we're going to do.
It's true that the king hasn't been acting himself. Is General Dathieu asking him to rescind the order?
The king's orders are to charge the north breach.\n\nAs soon as I see an opening in their ranks, we're charging. That's the only delay you can expect.

We snarl over the hollow bones of an ancient carcass, like a pack of wild dogs come upon a dessicated corpse in the desert. Cyrodiil has been consumed from within by demons of Oblivion. I will fight no more for the diseased remains of an empire.
A very wise decision. One you won't regret, trust me. \n\nShall we go? We've a Redguard swordmaster to rescue.

Our friend has suffered unimaginable and unending torment for nearly two years. Far longer than any mortal man should endure.\n\nBut Sai Sahan is something more than mortal man. He's a descendant of Leki, the Yokudan Sword-Saint. I've seen it.
Lyris and Abnur have both agreed to accompany you, but I fear their mutual enmity will complicate your task. \n\nSpeak with them and hear what they offer, but you must choose one or the other.
We have been able to determine the precise area of the Halls where Sai is being held. This is why we were so long about the task.\n\nI shall open a portal for you.

I wish I knew. I extend her Stendarr's grace, but the council isn't willing to do the same. She disappeared from quarters after the attack on the Forge. They've actually ordered the rank-and-file to search for her.
No, I don't. But I'm one of the few. Aelif has already made up her mind as well. Not only does she think Colors ordered the attack, Aelif's convinced she murdered Jofnir! Damn it.
A fine choice, oh my comrade. It will be done. Speak with Aelif and I will have a gift for you shortly.
A fine choice, oh my comrade. It will be done. Speak with Aelif and I will have a gift for you shortly.
A fine choice, oh my comrade. It will be done. Speak with Aelif and I will have a gift for you shortly.
A fine choice, oh my comrade. It will be done. Speak with Aelif and I will have a gift for you shortly.
The Emperor? He lives? This day is filled with wonders.
It's not the place, it's the times, this war. The fort used to be peaceful, quiet, a place to think and rest, not much of a fort, really. More like a sanctuary with really high, thick walls.

Now it's a deathtrap, full of blood and anger and fear. The smell of death and the cries of the dying fill the place. You can't get away from it.\n\nExcept out here. From here, it looks as it always did. I like to remember it that way.

Perhaps you're not who I thought. I assumed you were from Captain Brocchus, come to ask me back again. But I'm not going back. I'm out of that fight. The Imperial City and everyone in it can go to Oblivion, for all I care.

I was a scout for the Imperial army, one of the best. Out of the ones who hadn't been eaten or torn to pieces, that is. I saw too many of my friends die in there, at the hands of monsters. I'm never going back.

That's the spirit. It's good to hear some party chatter at last.\n\nOh, wait, it's my turn, isn't it? Well, I'm a necromancer by trade. I dabble a bit in taxidermy, but that's just a hobby. How kind of you to ask!
What? No, no, no. They're just a bit shy in front of strangers, that's all. Mingle, get to know them, and they'll warm up to you, you'll see.
I'll show her anguish when I bury my axe in her skull! \n\nLet's keep moving. And, listen … don't mention this whole thing to anyone. I need some time to figure out what it means.
What? No! Our friendship is based on honor and loyalty, not foolish games of love! \n\nI … I'm sorry. I didn't mean to snap at you. This is just so … unexpected. Confusing.

They were a legendary group of Redguard swordmasters, wiped out in the First Era by the Yokudan Emperor Hira.\n\nSahan spent years trying to resurrect their ancient traditions, but failed utterly. He considered it his greatest failure.

Oh, please. We're adults, aren't we? \n\nThe day I start considering people's feelings before speaking my mind is the day my efficacy as a politician comes to an end. When that day comes, just kill me outright, I beg of you.

The torturers here are using Sahan's memories and darkest fears against him, in an attempt to break his will. \n\nHe and I were never close. In truth, I enjoyed mocking him. I had no idea how deeply it affected him. Interesting.

And it took on Tharn's appearance because he was a familiar rival that Sai secretly despised. \n\nImagine seeing your nemesis succeed where you failed, day after day, year after year. I can't think of anything worse.

The sword-singers are legendary. They were a group of Redguard swordmasters, wiped out in the First Era by the Yokudan Emperor Hira.\n\nSahan spent years trying to resurrect their lost art, but never succeeded. He considered it his greatest failure.

Are you as blind as your vagabond emperor? The first room was about Sahan's failures. This room is obviously an attempt to leverage his subconscious desires. \n\nSo, our Redguard friend has a secret crush on the half-giant. How revolting.
I can only assume she's Sahan's personal torturer. I have a sneaking suspicion we'll be meeting her again, very soon.\n\nCome, let's keep moving.

Please! Titanborn has all the emotional depth of a Frost Atronach. \n\nBut, who knew Sahan was that sentimental? Then again, he did resist her charms. Good thing, too. That truly would have been a farewell kiss.
My strength is returning. Lead on.
They tortured me for many months—years, perhaps—but I did not break my vow. The amulet is hidden, and safe.
The minds of some men can endure hardships far greater than anything the Daedra can concoct. The forces of loyalty, honor and friendship are powerful, indeed.
I am neither alive nor dead. I am trapped in a gout of ash and bile and swirling vapors. My ears are filled with the screams of a thousand nails being drawn. And the pain! The pain is endless.

Why waste words when I can simply show you. Look around! I've been dreaming about this place since I was a young boy.\n\nSeeing it live and in person, that's a bit unnerving. Why couldn't this be that other dream I regularly have?

I am his plaything. And an abject lesson to others who would thwart him. My plan was flawless. My machinations were executed to perfection. I would have been a god, if not for you.\n\nMy only consolation is that you will know this pain, soon enough.

Arrogant, presumptuous, egotistical twaddle! That bit of costume jewelry is nothing compared to the Master's power. \n\nI expect I'll be seeing you soon. My only joy for the rest of eternity will be hearing your tortured screams!
From the beginning of time, there have been enemies trying to destroy Y'ffre's creation. They sought to take Brackenleaf's heart for themselves.
That I'll soon wake up in a really bright room, too hung over to remember what I did, I hope.\n\nBut that's not likely, is it?

With a blinding light, brighter than any I've ever seen. Then I'm in a room where everything's illuminated. As if the world itself is made of light. I'm … alone.\n\nAnd then I wake up. It's always the same.

Yes, yes I am. And after everything I've seen—the werewolves of Camlorn, the dungeons of Angof, the towering spire of the Doomcrag, and now this—I feel like I've seen it all.\n\nI can honestly say it's been an honor to fight at your side.
I've made it this far. I don't have any intention of giving up just yet.\n\nI need to see how this dream really ends.

I'm alive which is more than I can say for a lot of the soldiers out there.\n\nI keep thinking that if I would have stayed back I could have changed things. I know how war works, though. Someone, somewhere, is always going to die.
Maybe after this we can actually find that tavern and get that drink I mentioned a while back.\n\nAnd, hey, if one of us doesn't make it, promise to have a toast in the other one's memory.
Straight to business, as usual.\n\nLet's kick some Daedric arse and get back to some good old frolicking!
Good thought! Perhaps some in the guildhall saw him there. This one suggests you question our comrades in Windhelm. Aelif will meet you nearby, she has some preparations to make.
Good thought! Perhaps some in the guildhall saw him there. This one suggests you question our comrades at the Trading Post. Aelif will meet you nearby, she has some preparations to make.
Meet Aelif on the outskirts of the Trading Post. We will journey to Ragnthar together.
There is a bridge just outside the Windhelm gates. Meet Aelif there, and we will journey to Ragnthar together.

So when this is all said and done, maybe we can grab a drink? Or maybe you'll need a neck massage?\n\nThe beautiful hero of Coldharbour could use a break, I'd imagine. All those tense muscles. No, don't answer right now. You'll ruin the moment.
Now let's go cause some havoc for the Prince of Schemes.\n\nThis will be our finest moment.
Nothing. I am bound by my … arrangement … with both the village and its leader.\n\nSurely you can understand. My oaths are sacred, and I pledged my loyalty to Kerbol.
I can't tell you anything. Kerbol's forbidden it.\n\nYou're welcome to stay but don't go nosing around for clues. We're a private folk, and we don't like outsiders.
<<1>> begs your pardon, but such questions are not to be answered. Kerbol forbids it.\n\nAre you hungry? There's a butcher down the street who might tempt you with a few nibbles. Yes?
Hah! Is this one of Kerbol's tests? I'm not saying a word!\n\nMy word is my bond.

I don't … I don't know. It all happened so quickly. I came back from gathering wood and the town was under attack. A few of us ran and hid in the barn.\n\nI saw so many of my friends … some changed … some were just torn apart ….

What? Oh, the others. If anyone else was able to escape those terrible claws and fangs … I don't know. Maybe in some of the ruined houses?\n\nBut why they haven't come to search the barn yet—how long can our luck hold out?

What am I supposed to do, lie here sobbing until the trolls eat me too? \n\nSure, they were good folk, but it's not like we grew up in Valenwood together. We shared a few heists, a few jugs of jagga … and now they're dead and I got to move on.

Such precision … such coordination. Rarely have I seen vampires behave like an army instead of raiders. This wasn't an incursion—it was an occupation!\n\nWe must work quickly. It won't take long for the enemy to discover our presence.
A good soldier relies on solid information as well as a brave heart and a worthy weapon. Is there anything else you want to ask me before you head out?

After all that's transpired? I killed you, you simpleton.  I saw your life gutter and fade like a candle flame in a tempest. My undead servants drank your blood and I reanimated your corpse.\n\nDo not taunt me with such hilarity.

I've met a few Argonians in my time. An interesting bunch. Connected to nature. Calm. A strange sense of humor.\n\n<<1>> is nothing like that. He's evil to the core. Where Montclair found him is beyond me, but he's served the Baron for years.

His mother was trying to keep him quiet, but Jonah was agitated. Made everyone nervous. Arkay knows these people could use a bit of peace.\n\nIt's not safe out there, they'll be safer here I think. They may be hiding in one of the nearby towers.

Spreading chaos. He's using some sort of blood-curse to turn innocent people into mindless bloodfiends. Makes them feral. All you can do is kill them and put them out of their misery.\n\nBy the Light, it makes me so angry!

Tempo … Temporospatial Claudication. I think that's what they call it. Anyway, it means the ruins inside are all scooped out of time and space. There are entrances to the place all over Tamriel. But nobody knows where it really is.
I did have another favor I'd like you to do.

Stibbons hasn't shown up yet. I haven't seen him since I got lured into that library. I'm surprised he wasn't out here with dinner ready for me. He probably went to higher ground, such as that peak over there.

I am bound for Sovngarde and the halls of Ysgramor. But before I take my leave, I would make for you a gift. The Prismatic Weapon. I retrieved it from where it had fallen after the Mortuum Vivicus was destroyed.
There's a winding path just past the village. Kerbol and a handful of others took him up that way.\n\nThey said they didn't have a spare robe for me, or some such nonsense.
Keep out of sight. They wouldn't even allow me to watch, so I doubt you'd be welcome there without your robes.\n\nIf you hurry, you can make it before they arrive. Make sure they don't hurt Draven!

Damn right I'm determined! And more than a little irritated at all this! Come on, hero, let's show Molag Bal how it's done!\n\nThen I can get back to the ordinary craziness I usually get to deal with.

I think we can. I hope we can. All I know is we've come too far to give up now.\n\nI … I just worry that we still have a lot of fight left to go. I think more of us are going to die before this is all over.
As I said, I thought we were finished. I figured that Vanus opened a portal to send us back home.\n\nImagine my consternation and surprise when I realized where we actually were.

I'm perfectly safe right where I am, thank you very much. I've got a sharp blade and plenty of food. I'm downright cozy!\n\nBut those blood suckers turned the townsfolk into their feral pets. Absolutely depressing, Divines take them all!

I think not. I may not be a mighty warrior or a powerful mage, but I am a genius and a master tinkerer. I know I can help. And my sister, Kireth, as well.\n\nPerhaps we can stay right here and guard our flank. Yes, I think that's what we'll do.
You make it sound like we'll never see each other again. After everything you've already overcome? What's one more minor obstacle?\n\nYou can do this. We believe in you.

Sadly, my supply of "gadgets," as you call them, is running dangerously low. The few items I have remaining will have to see my sister and me through this.\n\nBut if I come up with any brilliant ideas, I'll be sure to send word to you.

There are other survivors? Why didn't you say so?\n\nI'll follow you. But we need to be very careful. These creatures aren't like any vampires I ever read or heard stories about. They're like a Divines-damned army!

I've spent my life hiding in a dark forest. I've never seen the sky over Valenwood, or felt real rainwater on my skin. Molag Bal lied to us, and I'll never forgive him for that.\n\nI'm proud to be a part of all this.
And I believe it, too. You showed me that there was more to life than that dark forest. You gave me hope.\n\nFor that, I'll fight at your side 'til this ends. One way or another.
It's better to die fighting for what you believe in, than to die fat and content. I read that in a book. It wasn't a good book, but the phrase stuck with me.
I agree with you wholeheartedly on that!\n\nInspiring quotes are nice and all, but living to tell our own tale is so much better.
We'll adjust to our true home again in time. For many of us, it will be the first time we get to see our homeland. That will be an exciting day.
Find a new home. See the world that I've only heard stories about.\n\nYou don't have to worry about me. I'll be fine. This is the moment I've waited for my whole life. Now let's fight for it.

Honestly? I have no idea. Perhaps Jonah is just seeking attention. Perhaps he isn't quite sane.\n\nWhatever the case, we need to find them and bring them back here so that I can then turn all my efforts to locating <<1>>.

Of course! Our epic quest. It must have slipped my mind. I've been on so many of these adventures, you know. After a while they tend to blend together. Kind of like these two realms are doing.\n\nOh, sorry old chap! That's a bad thing, right?
I return to you this storied weapon in the form of your choosing, then: a longsword. May it strike swift and true, in service to the Guild and all we protect.
I return to you this storied weapon in the form of your choosing, then: a longbow. May your arrows strike swift and true, in service to the Guild and all we protect.
I return to you this storied weapon in the form of your choosing, then: a magical staff. May your sorceries fly swift and true, in service to the Guild and all we protect.
Hah, a fighter after my own heart! I return to you this storied weapon in the form of your choosing, then: a greatsword. May it strike hard and true, in service to the Guild and all we protect.

You are a true hero of the Guild, comrade. You deserve nothing less. What's more, consuming the Vivicus has unmade the weapon. It is once again in its primal form. I can return it to your hand in any shape you desire. What do you say, comrade?

Yes, yes, I knew that. Terrible getting your dismal world into the wondrous vistas of Coldharbour. Like dipping bread in honey. Frightfully repulsive!\n\nStill, I believe this might just be my best quest yet!

Well, that'd just be disgusting, wouldn't it? Do you know where honey comes from? It's regurgitated flower nectar! \n\nOh, very well. I accept your challenge. Now let's go and finish this so that I can taste your bitter poison.
Concerned? About what?\n\nWe're heroes, my boon companion, and heroes always win! Let that be a lesson to you. Now let's go and stop the Planemeld!
Chances? I don't believe in luck or fortune. We'll win this day with blood and magic, or we'll die trying.\n\nI won't lie to you. I doubt we can win this fight. But that doesn't mean we won't try.
It's good to know your faith hasn't wavered. These men and women follow you. They face death itself to fight at your side. They will stand with you until the end.\n\nDon't disappoint them.

Remember who you're talking to, champion! But … you're right.\n\nKnow that these people trust you. They'll follow you to the end of the world—and I guess they have. Don't let them down. Their faith is a burden you have to bear.

No, we can't. But we're not the chosen ones. We're not heroes of destiny fated to succeed.\n\nWe're simply soldiers—brothers and sisters fighting for what they care about. We're united, and that makes us strong. That's what's important here.
The same thing that happens to everybody. The world ends and everyone dies. And that's the best scenario. \n\nMore likely, they'll all become soul shriven slaves in Coldharbour.
I've seen the rise and fall of my people. Yet I stand before you, the last of my kind. I am the last Ayleid.\n\nBut I am proud to call you my friend.
I'll just add this to that … there we go, all done! Baan Dar's beard, thank you! Now, if you're willing to, just run this over to Aldeth. She's right out there in the camp.

This is an ancient refuge of our order, the Cult of the Ancestor Moth. Here we tend the most honored of our augurs, those whose insights into the prophecies of the Elder Scrolls have rendered them blind, unable to delve further into the mysteries.
You're a smart one, you are. Get going, get going! I can't wait to see the look on her face!

Cruel tyrants and conquerers who believed ourselves better than the other races of Nirn.\n\nWhen the lesser races decided we were the enemy, and united against us, our downfall was all but guaranteed. We were too stubborn to see where we were wrong.

And I remember you, my young friend.\n\nThe magic of your armor was not enough to deceive me, though the power you wielded could have done more harm than good. I am glad you used it to make the right decision in the end.

There is a reason I am the last King of the Ayleids. I stood alongside the younger races, aided them. I believed in what they fought for.\n\nI was there when the power of High Rock switched from the Alessians to the Direnni.

No, I haven't seen that disturbing fellow recently. And good riddance, I say!\n\nHe jumped at every shadow and said he heard voices. Made everyone uncomfortable. If he's gone, we're better off without him.

Only our order is able to read the Elder Scrolls. All that is known of them comes from our augurs, whose readings are rewarded with flashes of insight into the scrolls' prophecies. Each reading exacts a price, eventually rendering the augur blind.
Again, I remind you that this will be your last opportunity to speak to your allies before the final battle begins.\n\nWhen you are ready, let me know.

An outsider could not understand. Gypsy moths house the spirits of our ancestors. We tend them and honor them, and their song enables our augurs to glean truths from the Elder Scrolls, to see glimpses of what was, what is, and what might yet be.

Sorry, no. Poor fellow was rather nervous, though. His mother was beside herself with worry. He kept going on about <<1>>, how he was whispering in Jonah's ear.\n\nJust between us, I think poor Jonah was dropped on his head when he was a baby.

The sickness happened before the first bandit attack. None are missing from the stronghold. The poisoner must be among us.\n\nIt can't be any of the victims. There are … unpleasant symptoms. Very unpleasant.
That's not an idea! We're just going to plant a magical explosive and hope for the best?\n\nI thought my brother Raynor's ideas were bad!

I … I will certainly not leave! I'm no coward! Raynor, grab your gadgets! We're making sure not one creature comes through that damn gate.\n\nYou! You're a real bastard, you know that. Good luck in there.
I'm not sure I can take much more of this. People are dying! I've lost friends … people I looked up to … I can't lose Raynor, too.\n\nThere has to be another way.
You better not let us down, you hear me?\n\nDo what you need to do and we'll do the same. Just like running through a dungeon back home in Deshaan. But with more Daedra.

Yes. Yes, I do. People died so we could get this far. I owe them to see this through.\n\nMy brother and I will stand with you. We'll make sure no one follows us through that gate. I … I have to help. No matter what.

That was different. Deshaan … Eastmarch … those places were ordinary compared to this place.\n\nPeople died. Not like this though. It's … by the Three, it's a massacre out there! For all we know, we're the last ones alive!

I know. And that's why I'll stand with my brother and with you. With all these brave people. Until the end.\n\nRaynor and I will make sure nothing gets through that gate. We have enough gadgets to slow them down. Just make sure you win.

I'd tell you if I knew. There are a lot of ruins around here. Old towers, forts—that sort of thing. Some caves as well, farther to the north.\n\nBut I doubt they went very far. His mother didn't look well. They're probably hiding nearby.

Could be. I'm mostly concerned with making sure the bloodfiends stay out, not with keeping track of the refugees.\n\nYou might want to check the nearby ruins. But brace yourself. There's a good chance they're already dead.

Training with <<1>> near the front gate. He opens himself to counterattacks when he lunges. Knew it would hurt him eventually.\n\nBut he survived the attack, so he'll remember next time. Or not, and he'll die. He should really try to remember.
Getting battered by <<1>>. I always end up bruised, but I'm a better warrior for it.\n\nI'm sure half the village saw me getting knocked around. You can ask anyone!
You can see though the illusion now. This is how I actually appear.\n\nFor all their power, the sisters couldn't truly harm me as long as I serve Meridia.

They were stolen by troops of the three alliances. Though we hid them about the grounds, each alliance found two of our hiding places. The thieves slithered away with the scrolls and hold them far from here.
We have tried and will continue to try. Emissaries have been sent to reason with each alliance's leaders, sworn not to return without our scrolls. None have yet returned but we do not lose faith.

As if you don't know! Soldiers of the alliances did—yours and the two others. I care not to name them; they are all equally foul in my mind. Talk to Moth Priest Crassius in the temple, if he can tolerate your presence; I am done with you.

The Cult of the Ancestor Moth exists to fathom the mysteries of the Elder Scrolls. In times of chaos, few value the scrolls' wisdom, much to their sorrow. Our augurs could provide guidance to those seeking to rule Cyrodiil, if any would listen.

Alas, that is impossible to know. The alliances have stolen the scrolls from us. If they were returned, perhaps an augur could divine the path of this war. But the power of the scrolls has blinded the alliances to the knowledge they hold.

Very little. The Scrolls can see many things—even possible futures—but they are not infallible, and they will not make this choice for you.\n\nYou cannot cross the sea simply by standing and considering the water. Be strong, Vestige, and act.
My father once told me that the most important thing anyone can know is what they would die for. I know that now.
When you live each day as if it were your last, as I have, eventually you will be right.\n\nI was born to die a hero's death. I have always known this, and I have always been prepared for it.
To be honest, we don't know. He doesn't like to talk about it, even to me.\n\nLast month he locked himself in our basement and refused to come out! As if he was afraid I'd catch it from him!

No one is more surprised than I. They are willing to sacrifice themselves to save the world, yet they will never hear a single word of thanks.\n\nA funny thing for a selfish man to say, isn't it? I'd better be careful not to learn anything from this.

Many would. I can't allow everyone into the village, or we'd be overrun by disease. Some say the village can cure everything, but that's definitely not true. We're very selective.\n\nYou seem healthy enough, though. What's your business?

I've no idea. Speak to them. Let their own words convince you.\n\nBut once the choice is made, there is no turning back. The harvest of a fresh soul will no doubt bring Molag Bal's attention upon us. You must take that opportunity to strike him down.
We've already been over this. You need an infusion of divine power to even consider challenging a Daedric Prince. \n\nThe Amulet of Kings can give you that power, but at the cost of a life.

You are the Outsider. Your final trial is to enter my trunk and touch the flame of my heart.\n\nThe masters will fight you at every turn, and only by defeating them can you prove yourself worthy to become one of them.
<The defenses at the south gate are far from impressive, but they're as well organized as might be expected. There are, however, a few suspicious-looking crates.>

The Amulet of Kings is a relic of Akatosh, the Dragon God of Time. His powers embody the qualities of perseverance and invincibility, while promoting the virtues of duty, service, and obedience. Make of that what you will.

Right now I just want to find a tavern, and raise a quiet glass to Sees-All-Colors. And … yes, to Aelif too. What comes tomorrow comes then. For now, I will talk to the council. And plan for that tomorrow.

Do you have a favorite tavern? Hah! Right now, my friend, I will rest. What comes tomorrow comes then, and only Stendarr knows what challenges we'll face. For now, I will talk to the council. And plan for that tomorrow.

Do you have a favorite tavern? Hah! Right now, my friend, I will rest. What comes tomorrow comes then, and only Stendarr knows what challenges we'll face. For now, I will talk to the council. And plan for that tomorrow.

There is no such thing as a safe choice. There are only other choices. \n\nOblivion did not make me a monster, it just confirmed my own worst fears about myself. It would be fitting, and honorable, if you were to choose me. It would be a fine death.

The Veiled Heritance are about to test Aranias. If we want to change the future, we must show Aranias a different past. One in which she was not alone when the Veiled Heritance came. \n\nYour role is nothing less than that of a friend.

I feel like I've already lived a dozen lifetimes. I'm so tired. And I look forward to seeing my parents again, in Sovngarde. \n\nIf my death has meaning, then so will my life. It would be my great honor if you would choose me.

The first rule of storytelling is "show, don't tell" and that would be telling. \n\nThe Veiled Heritance are prickly little gossips, however. Their conversations among themselves reveal their intentions.
Indeed. Andur will have a crucial role to play. He is currently watching over one part of Aranias's test. You should find him to learn more about what the Heritance plans for her.

A powerful wizard who built the tower behind you. She studied <<1>> for years, always patient, until finally she found a way through.\n\nBut despite her preparations, Molag Bal's servants overwhelmed her companions. She was forever lost.
She was alone and frightened. Her conscience told her one thing and her fear told her another. In the end, she joined the Veiled Heritance.
Aranias needs to see that another path was possible then, and that another path is possible now.\n\nYou can give her the courage to do the right thing.

I once swore to protect my Emperor and failed. I cannot allow him to sacrifice his life in my place. Nor can I ask this of Lyris, my Snow Lily. She is more important to me than she will ever know.\n\nPlease. Give me this honor.
All you need remember is he's a powerful young Mer adept in magical arts. But his is another story, for another time.

<<1>> is the mouth of a bottle that floats through <<2>>. My seal is the cork. Should I release the seal, Molag Bal's servants will pour into <<1>> until they have nowhere else to go but here.\n\n<<3>> found a way to slip past the seal. As must you.

You're still in the story I'm telling. Aranias is expected to demonstrate her powers on a Bosmer captive. When she faced this challenge before, you were not present. \n\nYou may be able to affect her decision.
No. She was abandoned on this island. When the Heritants appeared before, she faced them alone.\n\nYou will play the part of a close friend she never had.
We came from Narsis. You know the troubles in that accursed city. We fled and kept running. When we saw this spot, we decided to settle here until things improve back home.

How can you not know? One of the greatest cities on Tamriel, reduced to a ghost-town! Plague, riots, disappearances—what has not happened to Narsis is the true question. Only fools and criminals live there now.
I know what I see, but it is not me who needs to know. It's you.
I know this is a desperate city in desperate times, but this is not the gift the city needs.

Yes. We all are, in fact. That's why he came to us. I can suppress the lycanthropic tendencies of the disease.\n\nThe ritual you interrupted was to seal Draven's form. To protect him as well as the village. But now he's turned and we're all in danger.

Go after him! I must tell everyone what's happened. Everyone who's left, that is.\n\nIf he can't be subdued and forced to complete the ritual, he'll have to be killed. And that's on your head, not mine!

Look around. Do you see the vicious creatures of this realm walking these streets? Do you feel cold, blue stone beneath your feet?\n\nNo? I didn't think so. I am currently your only ally in this dread plane.
As you wish. \n\nKnow that great magic protects this city, keeping it from Molag Bal's reach. The city can serve as a safe haven for you and your companions—once you find them, that is.
Welcome to the beautiful gardens of Coldharbour! Do have a look around. Lovely day for it. Soak up the ambiance, the grandeur, the wonder of it all!

We captured a Sea Viper spying on the camp. Those pirates never travel alone. Find out if they're around <<1>> and if so, what they're doing on this island.\n\nOf course, you should assist any shipwreck survivors you find. We must each do our part.

Am I not speaking the common tongue of Nirn? I was once fluent, but time does get on, doesn't it?\n\nI'm sorry, I forgot the question. Though I'm quite sure I already answered it. You really should pay more attention.
Sane? That's in the north, isn't it? I don't believe I've had the pleasure.

I have the oddest feeling we've discussed this before. Or did I already mention that? No matter.\n\nI am Sir Cadwell the Undaunted, Knight of the Court of Coldharbour, Champion of Chivalry, Defender of the Defenseless, Shepherd to the Soul-Shriven.
What about the Bosmer who attacked my island? What were they? Dominion ambassadors? A peace mission?

Did I? I don't recall that. There is a bridge just ahead. Leads to the city. Rather a drab, empty place at present, but a little paint, a potted plant or two ….\n\nAnd honestly, it's not as if you've got a lot of choices right now. So, off you go!

Before you head to <<1>>, speak with <<2>>. He just returned from exploring a nearby temple.\n\nThat wizard claims to know something about everything, so he may have insight on how these Sea Vipers operate.

They're a band of pirates. All of them are Sea Elves—Maormer, as they call themselves. They raid throughout the southern seas.\n\nA wrecked Dominion fleet is a tempting target for plunder. I need to know if they're here in force.

Tand came here … he thought he could win money enough to open a tavern. Make his father and his Sind proud. Before this one knew what was happening, he was dragged off by Hadran and his strongmen. They said they would sell this one to slavers!
Yes, yes, we must leave. The gate to the outside is just around the corner! Sind must be worried sick over this one.

Yes. He's not the first to fail, but it's very rare. Those who don't complete the ritual usually die immediately, by their own hand or someone else's.\n\nNevertheless, it's better than the alternative.
This is your fault, so you must fix it. The others from the ritual site will bring him in. Let's hope he doesn't remember your fight.\n\nTalk to Draven, but take what he says with a grain of salt.
For speaking the truth. Nothing more. \n\nThe Imperial army has just conquered the largest city in southern Bangkorai, and mark my words—they will come here next.
You're here with me now, but what about later?\n\nNo. No, that's not it. I must trust myself. Believe I can do what's right. I don't need anyone, you or the Veiled Heritance, to guide me.
I am stronger than this. I won't murder an innocent to prove I can, no matter who demands it. The Veiled Heritance won't control my destiny, I will.\n\nI can do this. And I shall.

They said I was spreading half-truths and paranoid delusions. They said the people here have enough fear with the Reachmen and cannot afford to hear my ravings.\n\nPlease, you must get me out of here. I don't want to be eaten by crows!
