Because I have just come from Hallin's Stand. The Imperials infiltrated the city and seized it overnight. They enslaved half the population.\n\nThey will do the same here. But when I suggested this to the guards, they locked me up.

She was Whisper Grove's local healer before the attack.\n\nTake her if you need someone to look after your wounds, but bring her back safe. If the city survives this, she'll be vital to our restoration efforts.
He's brash, but an excellent shot.\n\nIf you want someone to drop those Daedra from afar, you should ask Elolir to accompany you.

Right here, stoking the forge while my apprentice ran errands for <<1>>! Thinks she can take her away, make my work shoddier? Ha!\n\nBesides, temperature changes can ruin the metal. I didn't have a choice.
With an open mind, one hears truth, however dark it may be.
No. The telling has already been done. I am here to listen … and to watch.
Checking and oiling weapons in the longhouse. Bad for the bandits, when they attacked. Still didn't keep them from poisoning the well.
Let me see.\n\nAh, that belongs to <<1>>, my apprentice. You can see where the hilt doesn't quite fit the blade. Wish I could say it was one of her first attempts, but she's a slow learner.
Are you leading me somewhere? Or are you the one being led?
You ask for answers, but what you need are questions.
<The tablet pulses with power.>
I remember that. They were sparring for hours. And the others?
Yes, he'd complained for weeks about his herbs. I finally told him to stop whining and get what he needed. He returned later with an armload of plants.\n\nWho else?

My husband's brother, who challenged him for leadership. <<1>> was upset when <<2>> lost, but that was nearly a year ago.\n\nYou have my blessing to confront her. We must know if it was her, and if so, her reasons.
That's strange. I didn't see <<1>>, and I was here all that day. <<2>>'s apprentice is rarely away from her side.\n\nCurse that girl, I hope her feelings for <<3>> didn't drive her to foolishness.

It's pretty imposing, I'd be lying if I didn't say I was a little nervous about this campaign. \n\nMaster Rurelion always says that a true mage should never get overconfident. A little fear just makes you prepare better.

Not everyone's cut out to be one of <<1)>>'s Briars. We've dedicated our lives to studying the relationship of predator and prey, to becoming skilled hunters, and above all, to defending Brackenleaf.\n\nMany who undertake our trials do not survive.

The first test of the Briars is to listen. Each of the masters has a lesson to teach about the hunt.\n\nThese are the rules the Briars live by: to live off the flesh, to bring no harm to nature, and to protect Brackenleaf with our lives.

One step at a time. Visit the three shrines—Snake, Wolf, and Tiger. Light the brazier at each shrine, and listen to the masters.\n\nThen, if you still want to be a Briar, return to me and I'll explain the next trial.
You can't hurt me! Shifty can't get the money if—what? Really? Oh, thank Riddle'Thar! Untie this one!
Finally, you cretins listen to reason! It was an accident! I think I should keep the money that fell into my palm just as compensation for this incident!
You are? Oh, thank you. I was so scared!

My father and his father fought Khajiit. Right here in the March, they drew steel against the "beastmen of the East." When the Green … when the forest spoke to me, I knew I wanted my life to be different. This is my way of making a difference.

We didn't think anything of it at the time, but some young ones were hanging around one of the sites last week. Dawnmead. I guess they think we're digging up valuables? We hired some blades to protect the sites, but … we didn't have much coin.

We built this city at his behest, and attracted some of the brightest Bosmer to live here.\n\nWe had no idea what was coming. He seemed a decent Elf, and lived that way for many years—until he put that Elf aside and revealed the Razor Master beneath.

No! I mean … yes. But please. Get the relics. Find what you can at the sites. If the bandits have attacked, people are dead. If not, those relics can be removed, and the researchers will be safe. Just, don't let the work falter. Don't let it fail.
The foreman is a woman named Lorwen. We're bound by blood. She's my niece, my dead brother's only daughter. Please. Get to her, get to those relics. Make sure she's … make sure she's alive.

They left us for dead. Poor Emalin … I lost a lot of blood, couldn't staunch her wound. Managed to crawl over here and bandage myself up, though. Lucky you came along when you did. I was just thinking of making for Rawl'kha.

No. Listen … if you know Uncle you know why I'm out here. You have to get back the relics they took from this site. I heard them say they were making for Claw's Strike. The local name for an old Khajiiti ruin to the south. I'll be fine on my own.
Absolute chaos is what's happening. We're cut off from the island, but we're not going to let those monsters out. All Imperial troops have been recalled to the city to fight Molag Bal's forces.

Azura. You know of Azura, don't you? "<<1>> the Fleet," she named me.\n\nBut that was long ago. This shriveled vessel is but a shadow of my former glory. My wings ache to soar the skies of Oblivion once more.

They're invading from just beyond this barrier. Came through an Oblivion Gate that these Dagon cultists opened.\n\nDespite the Green Pact I … ordered the barricade up ahead to be built. We found plenty of dead wood after our enemy's first attack.
I wish I knew. We came from Kingscrest to help retake the city. When we got here, the bridge was destroyed and monsters were coming out of that Dark Anchor. We've been trying to hold on ever since.
Right. I'll watch your back!

If you'd landed five paces north, you'd have squashed a rat, slipped on its guts, and cracked your head on a signal drum. The whole island would have known of your arrival. So where did you come from, truly?
Just a friendly Khajiit, privileged to see someone drop from nowhere and land in sea.\n\nA shame you cannot do that at will. You could make piles of coin, sell tickets!

With fifteen guards and a couple quivers of arrows? Not a chance!\n\nEveryone's dead. The king. The prince. The knights and soldiers. The job's almost done, just a few stragglers left. You know who I'm talking about? Me and you, that's who!
You don't. No one does. We can't get over to the island, but we're keeping the monsters bottled up, for now.

Renchant? Sure! He's realistic, at least. He knows we can't last a day unless we get some help from the outside.\n\nOf course, the new guard captain, Hjurrun, doesn't seem to want any help. The lout brushed off an offer from the Fighters Guild!

Sure enough! Hjurrun said he's exploring other options. Don't know what those options are. Don't hear much down here though.\n\nSay, why don't you ask the crow? I swear the thing's talking. Probably knows more than we do. More than me, at least.

<<1>> pierced the seal with a relic known as <<Ac:2>>. It still stands before the gates of <<3>>, bereft of magical energies.\n\nYou'll need to feed it souls. And with all these Daedra about, you'll have your pick.
Our forces are battling Molag Bal's minions over there. All troops were called back to retake the city. Seems like it's not going very well though, from the bodies I see floating in Lake Rumare.
What do you mean? Pirates? In an ancient Khajiit temple? Preposterous!\n\nAll we saw were the undead warriors that overran our camp.
I have no idea. Actually I have twelve ideas, but they're far less fascinating than <<Ac:1>>. Probably some sort of ancient curse—it usually is with these things.
They're minions of Molag Bal, out of Oblivion. He's taking over the city, from what I hear. The army must still be fighting, though, or hordes of Daedra would be pouring out of the city.
The wizard <<1>> kept quite the stock of <<mz:2>>, which I suppose should do.\n\nThere are still some around. I can smell them from here.
Trying to fight our way in. The army was recalled, from all over Cyrodiil, to defend the city. We were slowed down by bandits on the road and found the bridge like this when we got here.
One can witness the larger view from on high, but one must come down below to see what hides in shadows.
The light hides in shadows, but only there can it shed on secrets.
A secret told is no secret, but all knowledge has its time.

Oh. You're not one of them, are you? Thank the Divines!\n\nThey just marched into town like they owned the place. That cold, horrible woman. She whispered something to the soldier and people began to change.

The woman made a strange gesture and townsfolk began turning into bloodfiends! Then she just walked away and let her companions …. They were so fast … so strong. They started tearing people apart. Anyone who didn't change was attacked.
Other survivors? I didn't dare hope ….\n\nAll right. Lead the way.
You already know the Outsider is our greatest threat. Beyond this? Some secrets are meant for those who pass the trials and join our number.
Oh! I shall stick to you like butter on warm bread.
This one accepts these bones and relics as a generous gift to the Khajiit and Wood Elf people. Thank you. You have made all of this worth it.

Many others are enduring similar losses. I deserve no more compassion than they do. In truth, knowing they share my grief has been a great consolation.\n\nYou are not here for grieving though. Is there some official business that demands my attention?
Fine! You got me! Are you satisified? \n\nI did it for the town and if you noticed, I made sure not to use too much just like Gargak taught me.

Oh, of course. Glarikha told me. I hope you'll forgive her. Her intentions are good, but she misled you—that request was not on my behalf. \n\nShe can't seem to accept my decision to step aside and let Duke Renchant handle all matters of state.

As I expected. Your reputation precedes you. You've become something of a legend in the kingdoms of the Daggerfall Covenant.\n\nYou're certainly welcome in Evermore. These are desperate times. Have you seen much of the city?
Indeed? Then by all means, tell me what you discovered.
Point it at any Daedra and concentrate. Your target will be mesmerized by its faceted glow, until the hapless fool is drawn into the stone.\n\nAnd … take care with your aim.
Yes … but only the least of them. It won't work on a Daedric Prince, if that's what you're thinking.

When he is able, Nethrin and Felari will return to his home forest. We will return the bones of the Wood Elves, and the relics, and hopefully bring closure to these long-ago tales. From the past comes hope for the future, yes?
Hm. Crow's on the ship, but the crew's on the shore. South by the city wall, one carries the key to open the door. \n\nApproach with care though. Drunk sailors can be salty!

And I'll send someone I trust to meet you at the mine. I can't just take your word on this. I'm sure you understand.\n\nBut I'll hold my mercenaries back until we find out if there's ore in that mine. I give you my word.
A true leader doesn't poison his own people.\n\nOh! My husband still recovers from the poison, but he wants to thank you personally. You should speak with him before you leave.
It might work. But if you tried, who would help you open <<1>>?\n\nThe impertinence.

I shouldn't have come here on my own, but I had a feeling the duke was making bad decisions. Of course, calling this a bad decision would be an understatement.\n\nIf we don't do something, he's going to hand the city over to Imperial control!

The gorbellied bastards! I knew that ship was carrying more than just supplies!\n\nWe need to move fast. Can you follow the captain and find out what she's up to? Then take the proof to the queen. If this doesn't wake her up, nothing will!
Oh come now, you can't expect me to believe that! Has Glarikha resorted to trying to deceive me now? This is a jest … right?\n\nSurely Duke Renchant would never even consider such a thing.
I am not "in" here, I am here. I am the statue—what's left of it—that you see before you. I have been here for thousands of years, since the heights of power of my people, the Ayleids.
The statue's crafter, whose name I will not utter, bore me a grudge. As the statue was unveiled here, he magically trapped my spirit inside. I was the source of much amusement long ago.

These are the ruins of Fanacasecul, as any fool should know. What is known only to me is what it once was. Thousands of years ago, this was a pleasure garden of my people. Many a pleasant hour I spent here, before my nemesis ensorcelled me.

I have only one desire: to be whole again. But I sense you cannot help with that. I sense neither a scultor's spirit nor his skills. Your abilities lie elsewhere.\n\nBut if you ever encounter such, in your aimless wanderings, send him to me.
Ayleid children used to torment me with constant questions. Lovers would carve their initials into me. The bored would scrawl obscene graffitti on me.\n\nAnd birds. I learned to detest birds.
A witness I was, and nothing more, but if a crow can spy someone, so can a spy. \n\nBut you know the true threat now? Imperials! Now, you must listen to me.

Above ground was a delight of flowering trees and plants, pleasing to the eye and nose. Below ground were saunas and torture chambers, for entertaining ourselves with lesser creatures, such as yourself. All senses were enraptured in Fanacasecul.
Friendly sort. Thinks he's a knight or something. He's a bit crazy, but otherwise he's mostly harmless.\n\nMostly.
Uela, they call me, those that follow. From the Reach we come … to conquer this land.\n\nBut the enemy of an enemy is a friend. So I am a friend.
You do not even lie well. No matter. I have waited thousands of years, I can wait thousands more. Someone will come who can recraft me to my full glory.

Well, to be honest, not very much. She must have been in the city when we were transported here, but I don't remember seeing her before that.\n\nBut don't worry, she helps us a lot. Without her, I don't think we'd have survived as long as we have.

Well, think about it. Everything else that gets drawn into Molag Bal's realm becomes twisted and corrupted. But somehow, the Hollow City has remained free of the Dark Lord's influence.\n\nThat's either luck or divine providence, if you ask me.
Have you looked outside? This place is crawling with Daedra! And not just the usual, run-of-the-mill Daedra, oh no!\n\nThe Daedra in this realm come in all kinds of terrifying shapes and sizes.
That is all that Adusa asks. Is there something else you want to say?
If I refuse to kill this Bosmer, then what? I'll be alone again. The "Rock Witch of Silatar," a monster for fairy tales.
Sorry, but this one couldn't be too careful. Adusa had to dispatch the vampires that came sniffing around the barn.\n\nHow was I supposed to know you weren't another wave of the vile creatures?

How could she not? Didn't Irrki follow all the appropriate courting steps? This one rubbed against the Dark Elf's shapely leg. This one performed the bump of the forehead.\n\nIrrki even left a dead skeever to show how much she cares!
The world is coming to an end! What does it matter if Irrki wants to run her claws through the enchanter's luxurious locks of hair?

What? No! That's ridiculous … isn't it?\n\nShe is kind of cute, though. Sort of like a big kitten. Maybe I'll see if she wants to join me for dinner—as long as she doesn't bring me anymore dead animals!
Well, she comes around and sniffs my hair. Brushes her fur up against me. She even did this thing where she bumped her forehead against mine and purred.\n\nStrange things like that.
Because that's where the portal sent me. Aren't you listening? Did you get hit in the head?\n\nPerhaps you should go over to the Mages Guild and see one of their healers.

Yes, Adusa noticed. Fewer than I hoped but more than I expected.\n\nMeanwhile, this one learned that the vampires left a commander here. He's up in the house atop the hill. Moira's Hope can never recover while he controls the town.
If you say so. It's been a blur. Can't even remember when I last slept.

I've spent my entire life trying to get to this point. Escaping that forest and claiming my freedom—it's something I'm willing to fight for.\n\nAnd I'll keep fighting for it until I'm standing in Valenwood.

My bow's already been promised to the Fighters Guild for the initial assault.\n\nIf we can take a secure location inside, I'll try to catch up with you. Don't worry. I'll step out of the shadows when you need me.
The Eyes are still … we are still responding to the loss of Razum-dar. He was our driving force, and without him we have much work to do. Cariel has done much to push us, but … it is not the same.
Razum-dar has us all scrambling to respond to the … events at Senalana. Heh. I have to admit, I haven't seen him this mad in years. You definitely put a crimp in his tail.

There are still some … aftershocks in the organization. The work you and Cariel did in Pa'alat has had repercussions. And we're working to support the military action in Senalana. The ruin, just west of here.

The March is a dangerous place. Many operations in the works. Cariel is planning something at the place called Pa'alat, to the south. And we're supporting the military to the west, at the ruin called Senalana.

Sharul left home when his village elder decreed that all male Khajiit without children join the Dominion army. Angranel took over this company when her husband was killed in battle. Others have similar tales of woe.
In the woods, collecting herbs for poultices. It's a good thing, too. After the bandit attacks, I've used nearly all of them.
Ah, mine is the saddest tale of all. I left to escape a forced marriage, to a man I didn't love. I killed him first, though. And for that I was branded an Ouster and can never return home.
I see the truth. Power calls me. No one can stop me. Kill! Eat! There is no fear, only hunger.\n\nNo! I'm not a beast! I can control myself …. Renoit! Renoit, don't leave me!
Thank you. Poor Renoit. I'm so sorry, my love. You can leave me if it's too much to bear.\n\nJust don't trust Kerbol, no matter what she says!
I understand. You've seen what I could do if you let me go free.\n\nStill, I won't give up. Kerbol only offers servitude here. I'll find a better way to live!
I'll have to learn to control myself. But it's not impossible! I've had lycanthropy for a while now, and I know the signs. It'll be much easier now that Renoit knows the truth.
I felt it. She was in my head during the ritual, cutting away something inside, something important. I couldn't move!\n\nTo think she did that to all those people! That's no cure!

My name is Gilraen. I took over as the headmer of Whisper Grove since our former leader … abandoned us.\n\nPerhaps a story for another time. If you're going to help, you'd better get to it. Our barrier won't hold forever.
Her too? That explains it. Kerbol has a spell over this entire town. These people are all mindless drones!\n\nIf we're to save Draven, we must break this spell for good. I think I know what to do.

The gate on this side of town leads to a cave entrance. It was guarded the last time I saw it, but with half the town gone, maybe we can get through.\n\nKerbol doesn't want anyone up there. We've got to destroy whatever she's hiding on the hill.
Mother? Mother's fine. Fine, fine, fine. I'm fine, too. We're all fine here. Fine, fine, fine.

When the vampires attacked, Janeve and Darien charged right into the thick of the battle. I lost sight of them since I stayed to defend the camp, but I could hear Janeve calling out orders.\n\nPerhaps some of the guards saw what happened after that.

Here, take these healing poultices. You might as well help me tend to the soldiers while you're talking to them. I'd appreciate it, and so will they.\n\nAfter that, find my sister. She has a tendency to get into trouble when I'm not right beside her.
That's my husband. Fingaenion.\n\nHe was hurt in the Daedra's first attack, but Laeneval got to him in time. He'll live. I'm almost glad. If he were awake, he'd be screaming his head off.
Because as a follower of Baan Dar, I'm entitled to a little fun now and again, aren't I?\n\nPlease enjoy the party. Just head back to Thormar when you're finished.
Yes. As a Daughter of Baan Dar, I've presided over countless Boasts. And this has been one of the best in my living memory.

What would you have us do? Escape and crawl to the Dominion for help? This community exists because we believe in the self-reliance of the Bosmer.\n\nNo. We stay, and we clean up this mess we've created.
Ah, a healer's poultice! Good, I prefer a bandage over a potion. I always found healing potions to taste rather like bog-iron ale after it was strained through sweaty horse hair.
He has his uses, but he's stubborn, thick-headed, and a coward.\n\nIf it were up to him—and I am quick to remind him it is not—he'd leave the Oblivion Gate where it is and flee.
No, not a hair of her. I didn't even see her during the attack. I was back near the river, cutting down bloodfiends as fast as I could.\n\nSorry I couldn't be more help.

Thank you. For a noble, the Countess sure knows how to make a proper poultice.\n\nI took a few hits, but I'm luckier than most, I suppose. I just hope none of my friends come back as bloodfiends. I really don't want to deal with that.

She ordered us to defend the camp and protect the refugees. Then she was off. Like a whirlwind, our Captain is!\n\nI heard her shout something about spotting <<1>>, but then she was too far away to hear over the sound of battle.
Thank you. This will help my wounded arm. The vampires … they attacked without warning.\n\nWe lost a lot of good people today.
No, I'm sorry. Everything was happening so fast. There was a lot of yelling, a lot of crying, and a lot of confusion.\n\nI wish I could be of more help.

You have my gratitude. There are three suspects whose behavior has been called into question. <<1>> the Khajiit merchant, <<2>>, and his wife <<3>>. I suggest talking to my people to find possible witness testimony before venturing into the town.

She tore after what looked like a dark cloud to the west, over by the river. Pretty sure it was that necromancer we were hunting.\n\nThe Captain loathes necromancy and the dark arts. Probably why she was so intent on going after him.

She ran off after what looked like a dark cloud. I saw her running west, toward the river. Pretty sure it was that mad Argonian she was after. \n\nThe Captain hates necromancers. That's probably why she was so intent on pursuing him.

Our home here won't last. Not with the damage that's been done. Gilraen would want me to get everyone to safety. I'll return them to the Dominion—maybe they can help me get my wife back.\n\nThink I saw a copy of "On Oblivion" at home ….

I saw her briefly. She was in the thick of things, fighting beside the rest of us. Then she ran off, chasing a dark cloud toward the river.\n\nIt must have been the Argonian necromancer. The Captain hates the dark arts and she can't wait to stop him.
She was in league with them! Her own son led them here to Murcien's Hamlet, and she let Sir Etienne die!\n\nWhat choice do you think I ask you to make?
Yes … yes. You're right. \n\nOf course she should stand trial, so that the people of Evermore can know what happened here.
You're right, of course. It's what she deserves!\n\nAfter all of the death and destruction her actions have brought, it would be an insult to the dead to let her keep living.
The woman is the Hamlet's only healer, she volunteered to take care of Sir Etienne.\n\nShe knew how to save him and she chose not to. Her son was with the Reachmen that raided Murcien's Hamlet.
I see. It's good to consider all choices before such a grave decision.
Then the choice will be mine, and I think she should die for what she's done.

I heard what my sister said. She thinks I'm evil. Unholy. But it's still me! I'm still the shield of House Tamrith! I'm still her little sister!\n\nWe've seen it before. Not every vampire is a monster. I can control this. I … I want to live!

What? No! I refuse to let you put me down like some rabid dog! I ….\n\nNo, my sister is right. Better to die with dignity, while my mind is still my own. Eselde is my sister and my lord. I will do as she commands. My fate is in her hands.
That is unacceptable. It is time for the Duke to answer for his crimes. Go to his room below and confront him. Meet me in the courtyard after. I intend to retake my crown today.

Of course they were! Have you seen the Reachmen's numbers? You think you can take them all on yourself?\n\nYou cut off one head, but there are thousands more, and they are barbarians! You've doomed the people of this city to a fate worse than death.

Whatever it was, the alternative was death. \n\nListen. There's nothing more to say. If you expect me to apologize and plead for mercy, you're out of luck. I was doing the right thing. Lock me up if you must, but I don't deserve death.

You're right, of course. I know that in my head, just not in my heart. \n\nIt's time to put aside all these doubts though. The people need a decisive leader, and one who will fight for them. From now on, I will be the queen I should've been all along.

It's the way it had to be. Though I do feel partially responsible. I should never have allowed this to happen. \n\nIn the midst of a tragedy, it's even more important that a ruler put aside his or her personal feelings for the good of the kingdom.

Yes, our gift is a blessing from my people. A reward for the help you gave us.\n\nThe blessing will manifest when you need it most. It will mend wounds that would otherwise end your life. Good luck, champion.

I am not here to fight, outsider.\n\nI promised our aid when you set our Hist tree free. We provide blessings, not blood. Trust me, my scholars are terrible fighters, anyway. Much better to have our blessing.
Well, I started to make my way toward the Hollow City, just as we discussed. And then … and then … and then I wound up here.\n\nThe rest is all just a blank, I'm afraid.

The Crown of Anton? Oh, my lady went about her usual business until the Mages Guild approached her.\n\nShe was conscripted for a mission, and the next thing I know we're stepping through a portal. I still have no idea what we're doing here.

Oh, you know, this and that. My lady always has a project or two in the works, but she rarely provides me with any details. I'm only the help, after all.\n\nAt some point the Mages Guild hired her, and I dutifully followed her through a portal.

I tried to help the Captain, but they just pushed me away. Reezal-Jul just laughed. He laughed at Mother, too. I hate hearing his voice. I hate what he's doing. \n\nI wish … I wish I was home. We had a garden. We grew vegetables. Now it's all gone.

The sisters find it amusing to watch me fret over their meals. But Stibbons has a good heart. He doesn't deserve the fate they have planned for him.\n\nThe sisters hope to turn me to their side eventually, but they never will. My faith is too strong.

I sent three of my best scouts into <<1>> to answer that very question, but none returned.\n\nUntil I know their fates, I can't request reinforcements. But I won't send anyone else inside until I know what happened to my scouts. You see my predicament.
Isn't it obvious? Madness swept through <<1>> like a plague, and so quickly! Only one Daedric Prince has such power.

Hmm? Oh, I suppose I can reverse the effects of the mayor's magic. After many, many years of honing my craft, this should be a simple matter.\n\nBut if we're hunting bears, I'll need you to be the bait.
If someone conjured this storm, they'd do it from somewhere they could see everything in <<1>>.\n\nThere's an old Colovian tower nearby. It's the highest point in the town, aside from the cathedral.

Yes, whenever I visit a library and do some reading, I usually fall right to sleep. Can't keep my eyes open. Great for when I get insomnia.\n\nBut enough about my sleeping habits! I shall do my heroic duty and bring them back to the city unharmed.

No worries there. Almost all the people I've traveled with over the years have remained in one piece for the duration. I've seen the odd dismemberment, but that's far more the exception than the rule.
Praise Arkay! This entire town has gone mad. We should have informed <<1>> immediately, but I insisted we press on.\n\nIf we'd fallen back, maybe my scouts would still be themselves.

The spell which holds back the lycanthropy is weakening because of him. Unless he either finishes the rite or dies, we're all doomed to follow him.\n\nI can't let the people of this village suffer for the whims of one man.

The townsfolk … they don't know the cost of their freedom. No, it's better to do it away from town.\n\nDraven will revert to his werewolf form soon. We must lure him out of town. Renoit will be our bait. I pity the man, but it's our only recourse.

I'm glad you understand our predicament. Don't hurt Renoit—he's already gone through so much already.\n\nTake him past the cave up the hill. With luck, Draven won't be far behind, and we can end this nightmare.

Lleraya has placed a veil upon these ruins. It's a simple illusion spell that she amplified using the power of the Lightless Remnant. It hides the true topography and makes us see exactly what she wants.\n\nShe set the trap and we walked right into it.

The tears represent cracks and fissures in Lleraya's spell. Imperfections that we can take advantage of to see through the illusion.\n\nAt least, that's my hope. One can never be completely sure when it comes to relic-enhanced magic.

We're close to the end of the veil. I can feel it. Beyond that door lies the oldest section of the ruins—a section that dates back to the ancient Ayleids.\n\nWe just need to locate another tear. If there isn't one, our quest may come to naught.

No. In fact, I'm certain she hasn't.\n\nThe undead guardians. The active traps. I believe that Lleraya placed her veil and moved on. I'm sure she imagined that I would stumble through the illusion and fall victim to the place's original defenses.
I'm dead, aren't I?
Be at ease! I'm fully aware of what you can do. That's why I'm not telling. I'm asking.\n\nLet me explain, at least.
I've secured a spell to get us out of this plane. However, in order to channel it, I require a sacrifice.\n\nAnd I'd like—I need it to be you.
Is he all right? That Kerbol didn't hurt him, did she?
All right, I'll stop my questions. Lead on, friend.
If he'd remained alive, the spell over the whole town would have broken, leaving us all as he was—a mindless, slavering beast. I would not wish that fate on anyone.
Time works differently in Daedric lands—I feel like I've searched for years and found nothing.\n\nYou're the only plan I've got.

One of Telenger's apprentices. The great mage is sending him to review my work. And if our first meeting was any judge, he's a thrice-damned stuck-up son of a … anyway. It would be bad if the relics were missing.
Now, now, before you lose your temper, let me clarify. I don't know precisely where he is, but I can find out. I'll just need a little time.
Down in the deeper tunnels. Don't worry, you're here! Actually, your arrival was quite timely. I just finished recording some critical observations on the site. I almost feel bad for Indring here.
Of course! The temple. In my haste to excavate some of the older tunnels with earthmoving spells I uncovered an ancient structure. This whole mess is somewhat … a bit … my fault. But I'm not worried.

My opinion? He wants to be the king of Rivenspire! Just like that madman Ranser.\n\nLieutenant Fairfax retreated to the old tower on the hill. We're holding Montclair's soldiers off, but we need to get our wounded troops back on their feet again.

That one, I'm still not sure of. It's clearly of Nord design, very old, and it has symbols on it relating to death and Sovngarde. I could hear whispers when I held it to my ear. I'm still trying to puzzle out the iconography.

So what if I am? They called me an angry drunk, said I'd never amount to anything. But now I have the lightning, and I'll give it to anyone who makes me mad!\n\nShut your mouth and walk away, or you'll get the lightning. Just like all the others.
Well, I don't know. Your friend did run up quite a tab. Perhaps you'd pay it off for him? Or perhaps you'd do old Duzal-ja a favor instead?
<<1>> is some kind of spiritual leader. Friendly sort. <<2>> fishes for a living, with eyes as cold and dead as her catches.\n\nAs for <<3>>? I have no idea what he does, but the tribe respects him.
Touching <<Ac:1>> to <<2>>'s forehead will absorb her soul. It's the only way we'll ever leave this place.
It's a little fuzzy, but … I think I drank so much I couldn't pay my tab. If I'm remembering it right, I said something like, "This crappy quartz thing should cover it, catman!"

I was in <<1>> when I heard some of the strange rumors coming from <<2>>. When I returned here, I recognized the signs.\n\nBut when I arrived at my laboratory, <<3>> was already there … dancing. Then I was dancing. After that, it all went dark.
I don't have a good excuse. I had … quite a lot to drink. And I have to assume I gave away or sold the the other relics like I did the quartz idol. Perhaps to some of the other patrons?

<<1>> is a curd in the soup. A real fly in the whey, don't you say? Made a mess of me gift, the kind from the wrong end of a dog.\n\nI tried to encourage him. Even brought him a hero to destroy! But he couldn't go through with it. Can you imagine?

He spent a lot of time talking to one of the Mages from the Guild. Darius, I think his name is. They were admiring an old urn together. I think Darius left with it, come to think. So he might be one to talk to.

Why are you asking all these question? There are enough of us to defend this tower, make no mistake about that!\n\nBut I do have more wounded soldiers than healthy ones at this point. My healer could certainly use more healing supplies.

I did. He was pretty deep in his cups, and this Khajiiti girl came onto him strong. Said she loved jewelry with claws, how handsome he was … you know. She talked him into giving her the necklace and was gone before he even realized what he'd done.
Eh, she's a local, works some of the market stalls. Think her name's Khuzi. You should be able to find her over in the marketplace, waiting on a job.
If she dies outside of that stone, we'll spend the next century counting the tiles in this place.\n\nI noted thirty-two thousand seven hundred and eight. But you're welcome to check my figures.

You do have a choice! Not like me. <<1>> listened to me, said he would take me down a golden path.\n\nNobody in <<2>> ever respected me, or gave me a chance to prove who I could truly be. What choice did I have but to make them all see who I really am?

Molag Bal is my Prince, you fool! I let <<1>> believe I was Azura's servant, just as I let you believe.\n\nI led you into <<2>>'s grasp. Morsels for the God of Schemes, to pick from between his teeth.
Well, that's a relief. I thought for sure you were going to kill me.\n\nI just wish you had gotten here in time to save my father.
If you insist.
I … yes. Quite pragmatic. Forgive my frustration, I haven't spoken with another person in years.\n\nBut we'll have time for conversation later. Come, we must retrieve <<1>>.

<<1>> is bound to her tablet. While she's within <<Az:2>>, we can use her as a tether to escape from <<3>>. If I hadn't been so quick to destroy her those years ago, my companions would still be alive.\n\nCome, we should retrieve <<4>>.

At the base of these ruins is the hole her torment tears between worlds. But the moment we enter, Molag Bal's servants are likely to sense our presence. \n\nI'd have long ago made the attempt myself, if I had anywhere to flee.

We must find <<1>> and free her from whatever cruel device causes her so much pain. Doing so should end her torment. When she no longer cries out, the rift between <<2>> and <<3>> should close.\n\nI hope.

Yes. Weeping Wind Cave. It's east of Willowgrove. Sounds like they have a whole little werewolf pack there … freaks. Stab them, traveler, or burn them or whatever you do. Show them you can't cross Atrius Axilla and live!

They called her Lleraya. She demanded that we line up to receive her blessing. That's what she called it—her blessing!\n\nMy father was one of the first to step forward and tell her what to do with her blessing. She ripped out his throat.
Of course. You're right. I know you're right. Lead the way.
I have another right here. Take it. Whatever is necessary to find the answers.
I have another right here. Take it. Whatever is necessary to find the answers.
You can never truly escape <<1>>, soul shriven. My Prince always gets what he wants. If you escaped, it's because he allowed it.

Do it! I've spent countless centuries imprisoned in a tablet. That stone would be a delightful change of scenery.\n\nPerhaps the banekin will pick it from your corpse and bring me to my Prince. Wouldn't that be wonderful?
I kept this library clear of Daedra, but the chambers beyond are home to a variety of the creatures.\n\nIt may be best to avoid them.
Take care, a variety of Daedra nest in the chambers ahead.\n\nGive me a moment. I must prepare a ritual to protect us on the other side of the portal. I'll follow when I'm able.
I don't understand. Lyris was always a free spirit. Why would my presence bind her here?
I certainly won't stop you.\n\nOne of <<1>>'s citizens also offered to help find the scouts, but she seemed a bit … eccentric. Perhaps she has something to offer beyond alarming theories.
You should know <<1>> has some sort of position in <<2>>. Seems to think her reputation precedes her. No need to kiss the hem of her robes, but she's far less prickly if you show her some respect.

An ancient trading hub, high in the mountains of Hammerfell; a place I thought lost to the ravages of time.\n\nSai Sahan entrusted the key to Sancre Tor to one of his mentors there. It must be retrieved.
Not entirely sure myself. \n\nFrom what I've gleaned from the Daedra, this isn't Coldharbour proper—but we're close enough, as far as I'm concerned.
Come quickly. Mannimarco is undoubtedly conducting his own search for the Amulet of Kings. We must not allow him to get there first.
Ask what you will.

<<1>> pulled her entire company from <<Ac:2>> and left for parts unknown. In her absence, we've filled the gaps.\n\nI tried to commandeer forces from <<Ac:3>>, but the Thalmor Inner Council considers Argonian refugees a greater threat. In their wisdom.

Strange reports arrived in <<1>> a week ago. Little things, people acting oddly. But when a <<2>> guard delivered his own severed tongue to <<Ac:3>>, someone noticed.\n\nIf we weren't spread so thin, we'd have been here earlier.

She was attacked and left for dead by the wayside, like a beast. Well, she won't die on my watch, not if you can help me.\n\nAround the lake, you'll find rings of mushrooms. Fairy rings, but fairies aren't what I need.

Take my amulet. Get down in the center of the rings and feel the earth. I need the energy from there to keep Elara alive.\n\nI need to take the child back to my hut. It's just up the hill a bit. Can't miss it.
Then you have my gratitude. I feel weak, but not unwell. It seems my outer wounds have all been healed.\n\nTell me, stranger—how fares Evermore? Is my mother well? My father?
I will send word that I am well, if Stenwick is willing. I dare not return to Evermore without knowing more of the situation.\n\nAh, we have company, it seems. Who is that, Stenwick?

I can only act upon what I know.\n\nIt's apparent that the townsfolk have caused harm to themselves and others within <<1>>. Yes, it seems they've all gone mad. But until I know for certain, all I can do is hope to contain it.
I don't care to speculate.

Ah, it's quite complicated. Suffice to say, they don't think I should use the forest's power for such things. Of course, they'd much rather I didn't exist at all!\n\nBut it changes nothing. There's work to be done, and I'm not getting any younger.

My salve was but a reprieve, I fear. In order to safeguard Elara, I need to do something drastic. And I'll need the wyrd's help.\n\nYou've seen the spriggans of the forest, I'll bet. There's one that's much older, and much wiser, than the rest of them.
I have a feeling they don't dare harm me as long as I'm under Stenwick's protection. We'll see if I guessed correctly.

Time, my friend. I gave my everything to heal Elara, and still it won't be enough. That's why I sent you to get the spriggan bud.\n\nThe only way she'll live past a fortnight is if she becomes the Sentinel. Luckily, there'll be a vacancy shortly.

Tell her she must tame the will of the woods. The bud will summon, and the amulet will bind. The wyrd certainly won't help, considering they'd much rather see this power go to waste.\n\nDon't let the Sentinel's power fade. It must live on in Elara.
He gave everything to keep me alive. Even his life.\n\nI don't even know what to do now. Does that mean I'm doomed to die as well?

That was his plan all along, wasn't it? And I never got to thank him. If this is what he wanted, then I must see it through.\n\nYou still have his amulet? Take it to the altar. We'll say a few words for him.
The forest is its own master now. For too long, it has curbed its will to the Sentinel. To the civilized rather than the wild.\n\nI'm eager to see what becomes of it.

I can feel the earth. I can taste the wind. It's like every piece of this forest is a part of me. I will remain here, a part of these woods forever!\n\nCould I even command the beasts? It seems that it would be a trivial matter!
<<1>>, Daedric Prince of Madness? You have heard of him, haven't you? Doesn't seem like it's mustering up any excitement.
I'm exceptionally concerned. It is my home, after all. But I'd rather show my concern by doing something about the problem.\n\nThe captain wanted to find his scouts, didn't he? We should get going!

Of course! You need someone who knows the town, and I need someone with whom to take a stroll in this lovely rain.\n\nNo use arguing, I've been getting my way since before you were born. Or do you want a sweet old woman to show more courage than you?

Mannimarco may be powerful enough to break through Stendarr's ward eventually. If we can get to the shrines quickly and receive Stendarr's blessing, we can pass through the ward, but leave it in place. He may not be able to follow for some time.

Dirt-eating, Oblivion-worshiping, blood-sucking vampires! That's what happened here. They marched into town and people began changing. They became monsters!\n\nWe either turned into bloodfiends or got ripped apart by bloodfiends. It was horrible!

Lleraya? Hmm. That name keeps turning up, like a flea I can't scratch.\n\nHer involvement would explain why these vampires are so driven. But no worries. This one is certain that she is long gone by now.
Please, I don't want to die. I'm not ready.
The meeting! I nearly slept through it. <<1>> wants to discuss the grumbling about the barricades.\n\nYou should come, see how we govern ourselves.

The mad people brought us to their "mayor." I don't know how he did it, but he turned my scouts into bears. Bears!\n\nI thought he'd do the same to me, but he changed his mind. Said the townsfolk should have me for dinner!

He locked himself in that big cathedral. Saw the doors flare up briefly, glowing as bright as the sky, and then it faded. Magic keeps them shut, I'm sure of it.\n\nI've had enough of this place. Please, untie me. I need to warn <<1>>.
<Nothing happens. He appears to be a very heavy sleeper.>

He went to preach in an Altmer city? Those racists will turn him into a rug! Kala cannot believe he'd do such a thing. Thank you for telling her. This one must arrange passage to the port of Haven at once!
That … that is Kala's brother. He would have rather died a thousand deaths than let his cowardice kill another. Thank you for being honest with me. I know he would have wanted me to know the truth.

I ran. Sword arm was useless, and there's no way I can rescue my crew if I'm dead. Didn't realize so few of us escaped.\n\nBut you're nowhere near as banged up. If you help rescue my crew … my wife …. Well, not all the treasure has to go to <<1>>.

In the depths of this ruin is a portal leading straight to <<1>>. We can only close it from the other side.\n\nOnce in <<1>>, we'll have no hope of escape unless <<2>> is inside that stone. Quickly, I can't keep this up for long!

The thieves went straight to the reliquary. They took the chalice, and a number of other relics. The relics have little monetary value, but we know the Chalice of Mara has divine mystical properties. I suspect they had help.

We tracked them here, and several of the chapel guardians went in to retrieve the relics. But … they haven't come back. Would you be willing to venture into the ruin and see if you can find our stolen relics?
Yes, I'll be fine … now. \n\nI know it sounds strange, but … I knew you would come. I had faith in you. I still do. I hope we can be good friends.

You may refer to me as the Groundskeeper, one of the few survivors that remain.\n\nI tend to this city. The magic that protects these walls and keeps us safe requires constant nurturing and the utmost care.

I have an old scroll tucked away in my basement laboratory. If we have it in hand, it won't matter how tightly he's locked that cathedral door.\n\nBut first we should rid <<1>> of its bear problem. Shall we?

I'm an old woman! And such magic requires precision. Wrestling with bears impedes precision.\n\nSlap them about their faces, throw sticks at them, call them harsh names. However you must, keep their attention while I do the complex part.

The city's original name no longer matters. Now it is a Hollow City, waiting to be filled. A perfect place to begin an assault on Molag Bal.\n\nThis city can be your armor against the hazards of Coldharbour. It just needs life to return it to glory.
If I had a seed for every man, woman, and child who asked me that, I'd cover the land in ivy in a fortnight.\n\nWe are of the forest, and the forest is of us. That is all an outsider needs to know.

He's already well known across <<1>>, but with the rise of the Dominion all of Valenwood opened up to him—places we couldn't travel before.\n\nHe wanted his fame to spread all the way to the Imperial City. I just want to find him and go home.

I have pushed my body much further than this. It is my mind that pains me. Mannimarco filled my head with shattered memories. They are like broken glass. With every beat of my heart, they stab into me.
Lead on, Advocate.
This can't be happening. This can't be happening.
Songs of love and romance. He says he can only sing about those things which resonate with his soul, but I've begun to suspect he's more concerned with amassing admirers than coin.

No. He intended to play every inn across Valenwood. I went to see if he made it to <<1>>, but I was turned away by soldiers.\n\nThis is my first trip to <<2>>, so I don't know much about the area … and I don't want to. <<3>> is far more beautiful.
Valencia, playing with me? This is all so much … I take this as a sign. My ancestors want me to keep at my music. I will … I'll make them proud.
Yes? And why is that? Did someone take a beloved family heirloom? Were you set upon by bandits on the road into town?\n\nSpeak up! I have real problems to deal with, as you can plainly see.

You could say that. Bretons accuse Orcs of thievery, Orcs accuse Bretons of abduction—I should be investigating these allegations, but I don't even have enough bailiffs to keep the peace let alone solve a crime.
We must recover the Amulet of Kings, but only when Sai Sahan has had time to recover. He is a man of great strength, but he will still need to rest after such an ordeal.
I don't need to listen to this. I'll show you, like I did them. Nobody pushes <<1>> around!

Think you can talk down to me? I'll roast you on a lightning spit!\n\nYour lungs will fry so fast they pop like kernels in a skillet. I'll make your eyes burst out of your face! You aren't better than me!
What are you talking about?

Bloodfiends and vampires, mostly. Same as down here. We think there's something important going on in Northpoint.\n\nHead up that way when you can and look for an Orc named Skordo. Good man, Skordo. Even if he does wear House Dorell's colors.

You stay here and guard these townsfolk. I'll go search for more survivors. No, no, reverse that. Better for you to search and Adusa to stay here.\n\nWatch for signs of the constable. I will try to learn more about our enemy while you are gone.

The Baron and the Countess aren't exactly civil to each other, but they both want what's best for Rivenspire.\n\nAnyway, head to Northpoint. Find Skordo. Oh, and tell him I killed three more of those bloodfiends. Let's see him top that!
You'll forgive me if I don't find your argument compelling.

Draven's desperate for a cure! He'll believe anything. Anyone. I know you've got your own business, but I could use someone on my side.\n\nIf you could have a look around, or maybe ask people about this place … I don't know. I'm at a loss.

Thank you. I'll talk to Kerbol directly and see if she'll tell me anything. So far, she's kept all the details to herself, and you can see what Draven's like.\n\nWhen you have something concrete, let me know. It'd do a lot to ease my mind.

Militant vampires require structure. Why is that so surprising?\n\nBut we have more pressing matters. I will get the survivors out of town. You must deal with the vampire commander. Meet us on the road when the deed is done.
To be honest, I don't know. But it was guarded by the ghost of an ancient king. Things like that tend to be important.

Oh my, I'm not sure I can think that far ahead. So many variables. What will the King's reaction be? What sort of staff will I be given? How many academic summits will I be asked to speak at? So many variables.
The future? Prophecy? I'm unsure, but it must not come to pass.
The future? Prophecy? I'm unsure, but it must not come to pass.

You have old Strastnoc's head? Shor's bones! Somebody buy this crazy bastard a cup of mead!\n\nIf you like to cut off Reachmen heads, you've come to the right place, my friend. Have you met Duke Renchant? The duke will want to meet you.

Not recently. That young man wasn't right, if you know what I mean. Kept muttering to himself. Ran around crying that <<1>> was whispering to him. Nonsense, if you ask me. \n\nI think he just wanted attention.

There are a lot of ruins around here. They could be hiding in one of those broken towers, maybe. \n\nIf they made it that far. I hate to sound cynical, but neither he nor his mother are what you'd call the sturdy or resourceful types.

He is. The queen stepped aside, but she remains the rightful ruler of the kingdom and she still cares deeply for its people.\n\nEven now, in mourning, she attends to wounded soldiers and refugees in the chapel. But she has other concerns as well.

Quite frankly, she's concerned about the city's defenses. But of course, she cannot publicly question the duke's policies.\n\nThis is why we were hoping you could discreetly investigate to see if there's any merit to some of the rumors we've heard.

Indeed. A son and a daughter. Very young last I saw them, but his son would be his heir.\n\nEamond's wife, Queen Arzhela, is cousin to King Emeric, so she is likely acting as regent …. Whatever is necessary to keep Bangkorai from falling.

If the situation in Bangkorai is as dire as it sounds, I expect Emeric will send the Lion Guard. But they will have to muster and march from Wayrest so it will take time.\n\nStill, if Evermore can hold out against the Reachmen aid will eventually come.

Most of the Bjoulsae River shipping has been commandeered for the war, so I suggest you take the bridge from Stormhaven—or, if you prefer, there is a more expedient way. \n\nGabrielle can open a portal. You can be in Evermore within the hour.

Perhaps. But I wonder—will history repeat itself or rewrite itself?\n\nIn truth, I fear using the amulet again. Its power is both great and terrible. Destiny can crush us by fulfilling our wishes, just as surely as it can by denying them.

I have been through much, but this body is tougher than the great oaks of Valenwood. I go with neither hope, nor fear. It is useless to guess at a future that has yet to be written. \n\nYou may hope if you wish, my friend. I will not judge.
He was a noble—of heart and in title.\n\nHe's up ahead, in the Vault of Despair, with other trapped souls.

These are the Vaults of Madness. The home of the Mad Architect.\n\nThey were originally built to hold three prisoners—myself, and my friends. They have since expanded to hold the many souls the Mad Architect has gathered over the years.

Of course. That's a big city, though. Wouldn't want to drop you on top of some unfortunate merchant.\n\nHow about the bridge right outside the gates …? Hmm. I've heard the Reachmen are "at the gates," but that could just be a figure of speech …?

I would, but at another time. I hope you understand. Losing my family … I just need time, and I believe this is how I can best serve the people right now.\n\nIf you have concerns about security though, you must report them to the duke.

Ah yes. I am well aware of this. It's unfortunate, but the terms the guild demanded were downright rapacious. \n\nFurthermore, the number of mercenaries they could actually muster was almost insignificant. It simply wasn't worth it.
<<1>>, the overseer of this Vault of Pain, waits across this bridge. It's stolen my soul, and I'm going to need it back if we're to leave.
Nothing, really. I did see Old Gogloth head out behind the stalls. He never came back, so I guess I was the last person to see him. \n\nExcept for whoever took him, if that's what happened.

Strength! That is the only thing that will stop the invaders. \n\nWhere can we find a strong army? Why … the Imperials are only a few days march to the south …. Join me friend, let us give the city to those who can defend it.
Simple. Surrender the city to Imperial control. If the Imperials have Evermore, the Reachmen cannot attack. \n\nYou will survive, and even better. Surrender now and we promise you will remain free.
Evermore is doomed without Imperial assistance. \n\nHelp us. Help us take the city from the Covenant, and we will usher in a new day, a day of security and self-respect. A day of survival.

Sai Sahan is nothing if not determined. He once told me that achieving victory is like wrestling an ogre. You don't quit when you're tired, you quit when the ogre is tired.\n\nHe'll see this through, don't worry.
War, what else? It's come to Gottlesfont just like everywhere else. Soldiers stormed in, killed the few who dared resist, and stole everything that they could sell or melt down.
The Spearhead has done well against the Dominion. The king has seen fit to grant me a larger command.\n\nThe Spearhead now prowls with the Talonclaw, Leki's Grace, and the Black Revenant.
There's no official title, but their captains follow me. We aren't part of the navy, and I'm not an admiral. But I feel like one.\n\nLet me tell you, it's a good feeling.
We did well in Rivenspire, thanks to you. In gratitude, our king has seen fit to grant me a larger command.\n\nThe Spearhead now prowls ahead of Talonclaw, Leki's Grace, and the Black Revenant.

What does it matter, they're all the same—killing and looting wherever they can. The ones in Brindle didn't lift a hand to help us. This priory is done for, after all these years. The buildings might stay, but the people won't.
As am I. I wouldn't be here if it wasn't for you. We aren't part of the navy, and I'm not an admiral, but the captains of those ships listen to me.\n\nLet me tell you, that's a good feeling.
I'm not one for rules or uniforms. I serve our king, but I do it my way, as my own woman.\n\nYou should see what Nicolene's been up to. She's my new first mate.
I hear she and Captain Marck are getting on rather famously. Good for her. I regret how things ended between us.
She's an Orc. They're stubborn as mules, so no, I don't expect she'll ever speak to me again.\n\nDoesn't matter. We both still have our lives. I won't spend mine in regret.

The relic we found on Betnikh ate the souls of her people. No matter its fate, I should have considered how that revelation would affect her.\n\nIf I had handled it better, she might still stand beside me.

I'm sailing the seas, fighting alongside Kaleen. I wouldn't have it any other way. Cutpurse to cabin girl to First Mate in as many years. It's like a dream.\n\nI wish you were with us. What you did in Rivenspire was incredible.
We're both doing well. No matter what happens tomorrow, I'm doing what I was born to do.\n\nKaleen trusted me enough to make me her first mate. I'm not going to let her down. Not ever.
I'm sailing the seas, fighting alongside Kaleen. I wouldn't have it any other way. Cutpurse to cabin girl to First Mate in as many years. It's like a dream.
I buried my brothers. I'm Kaleen's first mate. I'm making due, and I'm not really interested in talking.\n\nMaybe you should go talk to a wall.
Have I forgiven you for getting my brothers killed, you mean?\n\nYou saved Kaleen in Rivenspire. I owe you for that, but that doesn't mean we're friends.
I'm sure you are. I'm sorry too. Now we're both sorry. Isn't that grand? Now you handle your business, and I'll handle mine.
I'm celebrating. Telonil and I just signed a contract for a new ship. The Maiden's Sigh. I'll have the wind in my hair on the deck of my own ship.\n\nWe're going to be a crew again.

Just like you did back on Stros M'Kai. That was a fun time, wasn't it?\n\nI'm glad you're here. I really am. Have one last drink with me. Once my ship is back on the open sea, I don't know when I'll be back.
Don't think I haven't heard about your exploits. Rumors abound. You've toppled Daedric Princes, defeated armies, saved more people than I can count.\n\nOne day soon, I'll be saying "I knew you when."

Adorable. He'd almost have me convinced, if there wasn't a line of women from here to Bangkorai who heard the same promises.\n\nIt's the chase that drives him. He loves it. So long as he's enjoying that, why spoil it for him?
I'm not the settling type. But, if I make port five years from now and he's still pining, I might just consider it.\n\nCome to think of it, that would be a nice way to celebrate.
Well, let's see.  I haven't bitten anyone in almost half a day. Now, there was that Bosmer last week…
Who can say? I could be a bloodfiend in disguise. I do love watching your face do those little contortions.\n\nDon't fret, my dear. All I've been drinking since Rivenspire is good, strong wine.

A contract. Specifically, signing one. I recently had the pleasure of purchasing Captain Lerisa's newest vessel, the Maiden's Sigh.\n\nYes, you heard correctly. We have a ship again. The open sea is ours.
No, I do enjoy her company. She is a delightful woman, far too good for Jakarn. Irien has quite a talent with coin, as do I.\n\nPerhaps, if we both make port again soon, we will compare notes.
Jakarn. We traveled together to ruins off the coast of Vvardenfell. We braved many a danger, he and I, all to recover a Daedric relic none have ever seen.\n\nIt was glorious, for a time.
Would that we could! But no. Our cooperation is quite finished. \n\nI will drown my sorrow in ale for a few more days. Then, I will try to find another ship. What else am I to do?

We did. Together. I had thought we were going to sell it, but then I learned the truth. Jakarn only wanted the relic to impress the smuggler queen, Captain Lerisa. Lerisa!\n\nI thought we had … well, I thought we had more than that.

What's wrong? What hasn't gone wrong?\n\nFirst, Headman Bhosek tasks me with shadowing Neramo, who is constantly dragging me into ruins filled with danger. Next, I get marooned on the shores of Stormhaven. Then, I'm mugged!
By my own kind! Bosmer! I met a smuggling ship out of Woodhearth. They promised to take me back to Stros M'Kai for all of my savings. I agreed.\n\nInstead, they beat me up and stole my gold!

All I wanted was a trip back to Stros M'Kai. Back home. Instead, I was beaten within an inch of my life. Now, I have no more coin. I'm stuck in this Redguard sty.\n\nI don't know if I'll ever get home.
The shrines have been consecrated in Stendarr's name. Now, you must use the Ring of Stendarr's Mercy to open the vault doors!
That lucky bastard finally got to to go home. Vimy stopped by. Apparently, she had a big score on Sentinel's docks. She gave Andrilon the money to book a trip home.\n\nShe's a nice girl, that one.
Not long ago. The Forebear King has kept us quite busy. The compensation for our efforts has been generous as well. All told, it is a good time to sail the seas.
He and Kaleen remain close, despite their disagreement at Betnikh. It is good to see. We will all be sailing until the Spearhead sinks, and perhaps even on after that.
Quite well. Kaleen has taken Nicolene as her first mate, and I believe the arrangement suits them.\n\nThey complement each other. They trust each other. This bodes well for a successful voyage.
An old friend. Years ago, when Kasan Five-Claw captained the Spearhead, Herald Falvo was one who hunted my kind.\n\nIt is good to see him alive and well after all this time.
There are smugglers, and there are those who hunt them. This is the way of things. Falvo was among the more respectable, and we owe each other much.
We both did, by working together. When we finally left the island, we agreed to a new relationship.\n\nAfter the island, we were no longer hunter and hunted. We were friends.
Kasan was once marooned on an island. Let us say a few unclawed kittens took exception to this one's success. They also had the temerity to sink Falvo's ship.

Ha! Didn't I mention my cousin owned this place? Perhaps it slipped my mind. Elethien and I have been to every tavern in the Covenant, and a few beside. It was time for a rest.\n\nYou should see the man Elethien's taken up with. Quite a charmer.

Oh, one of those rich Crown gentlemen has taken quite an interest in me. If he keeps showering me with gifts, I might end up with a ring.\n\nWouldn't that be something? A ring, in the desert, away from all the trees.
If he plays his cards right. He's a good man, not just rich. I could see myself staying with him, and that says something.\n\nIf only we could do something about this cursed heat.

Well, let's see. There was an earthquake, a giant fissure opened in the middle of town, lots of villagers died and buildings fell apart, and flame atronachs came out to attack us. Am I leaving anything out?
Good. I'd hate to minimize our disasters for you. But in spite of all this, we're staying, those of us left alive anyway. This is still our home and we'll be damned to Oblivion before we leave.
Just to the East of here. Head out of town, cross the rickety wooden bridge over the chasm, then keep heading East. You can't miss it. Be polite if you go; they've been very good to us.
Brushing up on my poetry. The Desert Star has a decent selection. No one turns a phrase like a Redguard.
You'd like it. Try gazing into your lover's eyes after a stirring rendition of Hazam's epic sonnet "The Sandborn Singer." Makes them weak in the knees.
Brushing up on my poetry. No one turns a phrase like a Redguard. There's a certain lovely lady I'm hoping to impress.

Not in so many words, but she keeps her cards close to her vest. That woman flirts with the best of them.\n\nI'll win her over sooner or later. She's got a thing for me. I can see it in her lovely eyes.

You're a quick study, my good-looking friend. You'd think a relic from the remote isles of Vvardenfell would woo a woman, but Lerisa's something else. Something special.\n\nI think I've finally found the woman for me.

O, my desert jewel, eyes blue as the sea.

Hearken to my love for you, water of my tree.

Your soul is like the desert wind, warm and soft and free.

One touch from you will drop my blade.

One kiss will quench my thirst.

My love for you is like the rain,

Drink deep, my love, my first.
Research. Now that you have dealt with that business on the docks, I can once again pursue my passion. The desert hides many Dwemer ruins, most unexplored.

The secret of their disappearance. The path to the beyond. Or a few relics that will sell for a great deal of coin. Who can say for certain?\n\nYou should ask yourself which is more important. The question? Or the answer?

Oh, yes. More than you can imagine. This will be quite an adventure.\n\nFortunately, I have Vimy along to handle the stabbing. She's proven quite useful. Between her and Clanker, I need no other assistants.

Impressed, are you? I have once again taken an opportunity to upgrade him. His central cog matrix has developed quite extensively as a result of our travels.\n\nThis latest form is his most useful yet.

Secure the Dawn Posset. Protect her captain. Sentinel is not a place to leave your ship unattended, especially after the docks have been attacked.\n\nThis is my ship. My crew. I won't let anything happen to them.
Dead man popped up behind me, out of the water. I didn't see it.\n\nHe would have ripped my throat out of Lambur hadn't speared him. Lifted him right up and tossed him back in the sea.
Luck's got nothing to do with it. I'm alive because I've got Malacath's daughter at my back.\n\nNow I owe her another dinner.
Jakarn offered to sneak me into the palace, and not the part the public enters. The other part. The secret part.\n\nDon't worry. I'll make sure he doesn't take anything. We're just there to look.

Restocking the Dawn Posset's stores. Captain Marck has often complimented my talent for coin and counting. He also trusts me not to run off with his gold.\n\nThe selection is a bit dry, but we will make do.

It is nice to speak to a fellow mer. Perhaps if there were more of us outside the Dominion and less inside, we would not be having this war.\n\nTelonil is a gentleman, and his suggestions have born fruit. I am glad for his company.

An honored ancestor assaulted the boat. I pushed him off, but then I slipped. Hit my head. When I came to, this woman was standing over me. Tending me.\n\nI remembered her face, her name. My wife. Abia.
When you found me on the shore of Stros M'Kai, I'd forgotten everything. Thanks to you, I have it all back. Thanks to you, I'm home.\n\nWe have a child coming. It will bear your name.
<The hatch is locked. It cannot be opened without the proper key. The faint smell of incense wafts up from between the boards.>
I apologize, but I can't leave yet. The Architect has imprisoned my friends, and I won't leave them.\n\nWill you help me free them?
The first, Saryne Dralen, is being held in the chamber just up ahead.\n\nI want to help him, if we can.
After what I just saw, I'm not sure of anything.\n\nEye or no, unearthing the undead is always an ill omen. And as much as I want to walk away, I don't think this mess is going to clean itself up.
Yeah—you look less ragged than most. Was worth a shot.
Are you joking? This place is a ship taking on water. I'm trying to get out with the rest of the rats before it sinks.
The Reachmen, a dead king, those cursed spooky crows, the terrified refugees … take your pick.
Ah yes, our namesake. He's a lesser-known saint, to be sure—but I suspect he'd like it that way. He had many virtues, and chief among them was humility.

St. Pelin was a simple beadle who tended to the soldiers of Bangkorai Garrison. This was long before the knights who bear his name took up residence. In those days, the Garrison held off far more than simple armies of men.
Vampires, wolves, and faceless shadows that made up a mighty army known as the "Gray Host." Such a blasphemous aggregation has not been seen since the First Era.

No one bothered to inquire. More than mere slaughter, I should think. \n\nWhatever their motives, when they crashed upon the walls of the Garrison, they slew hundreds—draining them of their blood and casting down their empty husks.

The vampires screamed their dark curses and slammed their claws and leathery wings into the gates of the fortress. St. Pelin knew that only blood might hold them at bay. So he cast himself into the throng and offered his own blood to the creatures.

Indeed. The vampires set upon him and began to devour him. But seeing his great courage, our lord Stendarr filled St. Pelin with an ocean of blood such that the vampires drank and drank but could not drain him dry.
And every word of it truth. May we all learn from his example—to give of ourselves what we can for our friends. \n\nWe may well find that we have more to give than we thought possible.
So struck by his sacrifice were the soldiers of the Garrison, that they seized the moment and pushed a tottering battlement down upon the creatures gathered before the gate, destroying them.
She's doing Mara's good work, my child. Queen Arzhela has a warm heart that finds no comfort in the palace. She came here shortly after the death of the king to aid us with the sick and the poor.
Not all nobles are born to rule. Her royal highness finds her true calling in the simple joys of good work and charity. She would have made a fine priestess had her fate not been otherwise.
We cannot.\n\nBut you can.
Yes, the rest of my comrades stand atop the walls of Bangkorai Garrison. Only I and a few others are left to watch over the chapel.
My unique nature binds me to my phylactery, which should still be located in my home. Think of it as a tether, along which you can return to the world.

Well, that's what Simone said, but she's a shameless gossip. Furthermore, she might have meant it as a figure of speech. Surely the Reachmen aren't literally "at the gates" .…\n\nAt least I hope they're not, for Evermore's sake … and for yours.

Well … it's a long story. I was a novice, and then there was this herd of swine. I meant to send them to Northglen, just outside Evermore, but I got a syllable wrong, and ….\n\nAnyway, I'm not allowed to open a portal into the Guild there anymore.
Ha! Aye, I did, at that. This is really work for more nimble hands than mine—but I do what I can.
Someone had to stay behind to mind the house. Windows need fixing, the roof leaks, the door won't stay closed. I keep busy.\n\nBesides, warfare is a young knight's game. I'd just get in the way.
I cannot be the link and also travel through it. I fear this is where we must part ways.
Ha! I had no idea another Daedric Prince was aware of my research. I must take greater precautions in the future.\n\nI will open the portal now. Are you ready?
You must consecrate <<1>>'s bones. What happened to her was an injustice beyond imagination.\n\nBut one question, before we part ways. How did you find me?
In another time, I was a necromancer of some skill. While my research brought me no end of trouble, it afforded me certain … benefits.\n\nTo put it delicately, my death is no longer a concern.
I'm a lich.\n\nBut you seem like someone who takes things in stride. I hope it won't affect our future interactions.
Then prepare yourself. Departing <<1>> is never easy.
<<1>> brought us both through the seal. It's only fitting she bring us back.\n\nI can use <<Az:2>> to trace her soul back, and then it's a simple matter to open a portal. Are you ready?
Then prepare yourself. Departing <<1>> is never easy.
Constable Maldred is a Breton. He wears … Breton clothing … keeps himself moderately clean … is a … male ….\n\nThis one is sorry, but all of the furless ones look the same to me.
What did he say to you?

Are you sure? You've seemed quite friendly with both Draven and his husband, and the only cure is a permanent separation between Draven and the rest of the village.\n\nNot that I mean to change your mind, but you must understand what this means.
Nonsense! Perhaps it's the weather keeping our citizens indoors. Yes, of course—the weather. \n\nWhy not rest at our legendary inn for a time? Or sample the ocean's bounty at our famous waterfront?
They await you as well, Moon Hallowed. Come, let's … let's see this done. And stay after the ceremony, please. I'd like to speak with you when it's all said and done.
They await you as well, Moon Hallowed. Come, let's see this done. And stay after the ceremony, please. I'd like to speak with you when it's all said and done.
I … oh, what's the use. Yes, our city is beset by starvation, ill-omens, and despair. \n\nWhat am I supposed to do about it, tear my hair and rend my garments? Would that make you happy?
Other than harassing me, you mean? Good. See that you do. \n\nNow I must find a way to keep morale up so the populace doesn't panic.
You think that would help? The Reachmen are pillaging our towns and farms. Our citizens are desperate for food and reinforcements. Can you bring us some?
Then try not to die.\n\nThat welkynd stone is our only hope of containing this creature. You have my thanks.
Most of my people prize strength of arms and a sharp sword. I prefer scholastic ability and a sharp wit.\n\nWe should get moving. They check on me pretty often.

Excellent. Then dealing with the rat I let into the castle is all that remains, if we can just find whatever hole he's scurried into.\n\nOh, but what about Sir Jarnot? And Glarikha? All three of you deserve a medal after this is done with.
Yes, indeed! Every heart soars now that the rightful queen has resumed the throne. \n\nYou have my deepest gratitude. Our city is resilient. We will thrive in time. I know it.

I already tried. It seems <<1>> bound my magic somehow. I'd say it's maddening, but less so than having a Daedric Prince steer you around like a carriage.\n\nWhen they come for us, we can try to fight our way out. If they come for us.

I saw and heard everything we did, but I couldn't affect a thing. It was a waking nightmare! My own mind, a prison.\n\nI expected him to kill us both, but we're here, aren't we? Best not to think of it. Applying logic to the Mad God is … unwise.
I don't see how. Those bars are thicker than sword blades. We aren't going anywhere.\n\nIt seems <<1>> made a few changes to these catacombs. There were never any prison cells below the cathedral.
So be it.
I … very well. \n\nYou fought that creature off, but you realize there's a small Goblin army in this ruin? You know what you're signing up for?

Call it Orcish intuition. Mauloch's the god of oaths—my nanna always said we Orsimer can smell a lie, and something around here stinks. \n\nOf course, it could just be some scullery maid cheating on her husband.
<<1>>. Beloved of the wild ones. My priestess returns from the clutches of <<2>> at last.
So I have seen. A mortal has managed what the eternal dead could not.
So I have seen. Another sacrifice asked of one who has already lost so much.\n\nDo not mourn her, mortal. There is hope for <<1>> yet.
As safe as any can be in that place.

It is in the mountains of Colovia, the land of my youth. But I have little memory of that time. My exposure to the Elder Scrolls stole much of the man I once was.\n\nSpeak to Sai Sahan. He can answer your questions far more accurately than I.

It was a holy city in the First Era, founded by Queen Alessia herself. It has since fallen into crumbling ruin.\n\nBefore his capture, Sai Sahan hid the Amulet of Kings in the catacombs beneath the city.

My Lord Varen will open a gateway to Sancre Tor. The amulet lies in a vault protected by powerful magic: a ward of Stendarr, the God of Justice and Mercy.\n\nAlso, a God of Well-Earned Luck. I thought this could not hurt.
The catacombs contain two shrines dedicated to the Divines. We must consecrate them in Stendarr's name. When that is done, the Ring of Stendarr's Mercy should open the vault doors.

We should avoid the Crypt of Heroes. I saw enough angry dead there to fill nine lifetimes. Kasura and I barely escaped with our lives. We will enter through the inner courtyard and avoid it entirely. \n\nNow, come. Time waits for no man.

It is written that Alessia received the divine inspiration for her slave rebellion at Sancre Tor, and so, built her holy city there. But that was long ago. The city is a ruin, now.\n\nIt has become a dark place, with areas best left undisturbed.
We must make our way to the Inner Courtyard. From there we can access the chambers where the shrines are located.
That voice … Mannimarco's voice … it taunted me over and over in an endless cycle, for years on end. He never broke my will, but he broke … something.
I will make it through this, my friend. I did not endure years of torture in the Halls of Torment, only to give up now!\n\nMy pain has subsided. Let us make haste, and finish this.

We must consecrate the two shrines with Stendarr's blessing before the vault can be opened. \n\nThe first shrine rests in the Dragonguard Tomb, where so many of my fallen comrades were interred. We must take care to respect their resting place.
Stand in the casting circle and direct the ring at the doors to lift the ward. The doors should open wide!

We're two of a kind. Stoic. Isn't that what people call us? \n\nOur hearts are connected, but we don't talk about our feelings. We don't even understand them ourselves. Maybe we'll talk about it someday, but today's not that day.

Me? I'll chase Mannimarco to the furthest corners of Oblivion if I have to. Vengeance is a powerful motivator. \n\nAnd I don't know if you've realized it yet, but under this hardened shell, I'm an optimistic fool who'd take a blade for any one of you.
Mannimarco will pay dearly for the rest of eternity. One cannot outscheme the God of Schemes without paying a heavy price. I cannot imagine the torment that awaits him.

Sai Sahan must rest, as must we all. We can sleep a little easier knowing the King of Worms has been defeated, but we cannot rest too long. \n\nMolag Bal is still a great threat, and the Planemeld must be stopped or this will all be for naught.
Eighty-eight years, three months, eleven days. Thirteen hours. Seven minutes.

I'm concerned about its misuse. Unless you're prepared to handle them correctly, relics such as these can … corrode you.\n\nI would tell <<1>> myself, but I don't trust her intentions. Not after she pressed these pilgrims into service.
Your common vernacular aside, that is indeed the critical task. Valkynaz Seris has a key to the Labyrinth. Eliminating the Valkynaz and obtaining that key are critical components to our success here.
You've found the elegant western headquarters of the Dragonstar Caravan Company. Congratulations. Try not to trip over the crates.
A famous High Elf general … or infamous, depending on who you ask. Her Jade Dragoons are well respected, but she has an aggressive reputation.\n\nThe last I heard, she was in <<1>>.
Shipping goods overland presents all manner of hazards, f'lah. Highwaymen, customs inspections, legal entanglements. Our highly trained professionals … grease the wheels.
Well, discretion is one of the many services we offer to potential employers.
Rajhin is a Khajiit trickster god, also worshiped by thieves and deceivers.\n\nThe Khajiit swap tales of Rajhin's greatest pranks. It is said his Seven Shadows do his bidding throughout Tamriel.
They're peaceful sorts. Most believe their faith will one day draw the Walking City back from wherever it disappeared.
