I know how to handle such relics. Before joining the Mages Guild, I'd hoped to serve the Eight Divines. Then I thought, why not do both?\n\nIf we can find <<1>>, I'll know what must be done to safely transport it.

The Falinesti Faithful believe the welkynd stones hold the memories of the Walking City. Earlier, I heard soldiers speaking of the same stones.\n\nIf you can see me past the frost trolls, perhaps we can see what the stones have to do with <<1>>.

As we say in the caravan trade, trouble someplace just means more travel to someplace else. And let me tell you, right now plenty of people in Evermore are interested in sending their goods—or themselves—someplace else.
A bust always comes after a boom, alas. I suspect the Reach clans will sack the city soon. If they don't, the Imperials will. Then we'll be on our way. That's commerce for you.

Oh, there are always goods to ship, my dear. Screaming children, old women, whatever meager trinkets these poor fetchers can jam into their pockets. There are lots of citizens interested in a trip to Craglorn. Fares are up!
A very good question, which raises another.\n\n<<1>> is a Khajiit legend. Why does she seek it out in <<2>>, the home of the Wood Elf king? What could have brought it to <<Ac:3>>?
I have a theory … but until I can support it, speculation is less than useless.\n\nPerhaps the welkynd stones will reveal more.
All right, I'm showing off. I used a simple spell to mark the time. It was the first thing I did when I realized I was trapped.\n\nIt's not entirely precise, so I had to guess the minutes.

Clear my tower of Daedra, for one. Memorialize my companions who did not return. Organize my effects.\n\nThen, I'll find out what has transpired in this world since I left. I have some catching up to do.
For a time, though I expect my attention shall be drawn elsewhere soon enough.\n\nThere was something different in <<1>>. The air was a little too full, the fires too bright.
Molag Bal's corner of Oblivion holds many secrets. I plundered several from his halls, a lifetime ago.\n\nDid you know, I did it to impress a boy? What a fool I was.
I have.\n\nWhy do you ask?
Then you know the tale it tells. \n\nDid you find anything else?
I hoped that wretched thing would fade away. It was a pale shadow of my son, and nothing more. <<1>> died so long ago, but my husband couldn't put him to rest.\n\nYou didn't meet my husband, did you?
That makes no sense. An animated shade would have no desire to escape. It would only approximate reason.\n\nTell me, why did it want to escape?

<<1>> never understood the dangers of such a process. Binding a soul to a body is no simple task. He owns a puppet that answers to our son's name. A mockery of who <<2>> once was!\n\nForgive me. I don't wish to speak of this anymore.
Then my husband and my son are both truly lost.

<<1>>. A powerful mage, brilliant, always focused upon his work … hardly striking, though such things never mattered to me. It took my escapade in <<2>> to convince him there were adventurous women outside of his books.\n\nBut that was long ago.

I opened my home to many I met in my travels. A young Redguard swordsman, a scarred Wood Elf hunter, a Psijic outcast … I can still hear their voices.\n\nBut that was ninety years ago. Those not killed by the Daedra must have fled.

<<AC:1>> stands before the entrance to <<2>>. When Molag Bal's servants first invaded, this place was known as Twyllvarlais, the "Well of Stars." Now it's the "Throat of Darkness."\n\nThe Ayleid had such colorful names, don't you think?

Maybe something to do with turning back time? Edwyge mentioned something like that.\n\nBut that's just a guess. I caught a glimpse of them chanting in there. Didn't seem to work. Edwyge was cursing like crazy. I guess being nice was just an act.

Only what we learned studying the history of magic. It was a catastrophic experiment conducted by members of the Alessian Order.\n\nThey were trying to remove the Elven aspects from Akatosh, but they wound up tearing the fabric of time. Or something.

I am. You are too, aren't you? \n\nLook, I know how bad this looks, but it's teaching me a valuable lesson. If you can help me get the book back, nothing like this will ever happen again. No reason the magister needs to know about this, right?

You'd be better off asking them to explain their own delusion.\n\nI've noted it's not a religious experience for everybody. Some use the annual pilgrimage to hold a revel in Falinesti's honor. Any excuse to celebrate.

Yes, I am. If you're questioning my intellect because I was duped by a pretty face, I couldn't blame you.\n\nBut you should know, it doesn't take much brains to be a mage. I know plenty of dumb mages.
Could you kill someone you love? I can't! Well, I have. But not <<1>>, it would be too pedestrian.\n\nNo, I want you to try killing him.

Deal! Oh, and one more thing. <<1>> stays behind. If you bore me too much, I'll turn her into a goose, roast her, and feed her to you covered in fine Eidar glaze.\n\nThe goose, I mean. It's a might bit chilly for my Eidar-pants.

I want him to reach deep down, below all the marmalade and crushing failures defining his life, to find a seed of confidence, and grow it into a tree of gumption he'll use to beat your brains to paste.\n\nBut if not, any brain paste'll do. Even his.

I'm just a bit of a fire bug, y'see. I like to watch things glow—warms me up inside. \n\nSmall things, mind you. Old abandoned houses and the like. But I wouldn't burn one down with a family in it. Please, stranger, you've got to believe me!
I promised to say nothing. Does an oath mean anything to you?\n\nIf you won't be dissuaded, talk to Helene. She's in the lower rooms of the house across the way. Her bond is incomplete, unlike mine.
If you're so eager to learn our secret, talk to Helene. She's in the lower floor of that house yonder.\n\nThat's all I'm going to say.
I cannot … but Helene might. She's downstairs now. I am only here to keep watch.\n\nDo not hurt her. She cannot help being sick. None of us could.

Threatening me, are you? Look, I didn't invite you to talk to me. No one's making you stay here.\n\nWhy don't you talk to Helene? She's in the basement. Talk to someone who can't leave. Maybe that'll shut you up.

Just over the Bjoulsae. Here, I'll mark it on your map. \n\nI doubt the captain will let me out of here. I done a few other things not worth talking about. But at least I can get this deed off my record.

Because I know who done it! Least I think I know who done it. Across the river there's a cave full of Orcs. I heard one of them caterwauling about "fiery vengeance" just before the guard captain locked me up. \n\nI bet you he did it!

Of course, she was the last to summon me. Together, we opened the ruins of <<1>>. She ventured in with her noble companions.\n\nI watched them die in a flood of Daedra. It was all I could do to escape and seal the ruin … <<2>>'s final command.
The change! The change is coming, and I can't stop it! Kerbol promised me that she could help, but only after I calm down.\n\nPlease, go! I can smell your blood. It's … it's driving me crazy!
I'm a werewolf! Gods, I said it! A terrible beast. I can't control myself!\n\nBut Kerbol promised she'd save me, like she … saved everyone else!
I've surrendered! Gavo's confessions … Lavinia is a traitor and a blasphemer! Please … she's dead, isn't she? I just want to go home to my farm and my family. I never wanted any of this.
I thank you for your mercy. I won't be any trouble. Mara's breath, may the Eight keep you safe.

I was tending to some of our injured when your fighters came upon us. I surrendered to buy the injured time to flee. All of us that still hold the Eight in our hearts have abandoned this Daedric plot. We want nothing to do with Lavinia's treachery.

I-I know. I feel partially responsible for her death … but if I give in to remorse or sorrow, I would be doing her a dishonor.\n\nFrom now on, I'm going to honor Eamond's legacy, rule as he would have, as he and Glarikha would want me to.
If you must, but hurry please. Survivors have a terrible habit of becoming dead when they are left unattended.
Of course I'm worried about my hired help, as any woman of noble birth would be.\n\nBut the chalice is a priceless, irreplaceable relic of historical importance. You really can't compare the two.
Someone who wishes she had arrived in time to divert this tragedy. But if wishes were fishes, Adusa would be a very happy cat.\n\nThis one is here to help. Now, please, the survivors need us.

Must Adusa explain everything? Look around. The people of Moira's Hope were either turned into bloodfiends or turned into food for bloodfiends.\n\nNow as to the who and the why of this horror, Adusa cannot say.
Not is. Was. This was the peaceful hamlet of Moira's Hope. Now? Now it is a disaster area.

We do not adhere to the unhealthy social structures of city dwellers. We Glenmoril Wyrd follow the natural order.\n\nThis part of the forest belongs to the Jackdaw crows, thus their needs guide our actions here. When they suffer, we all do.
She is a poisonous taint on the natural order—the most foul and evil Hagraven I have heard of.\n\nSomehow, she has earned Hircine's favor. Her followers, the Dark Witnesses, treat her like a god.

Because it is people like you threaten the natural order. \n\nYou bring your wars here and lay waste to all that falls in your path. You chop down trees and divert streams in the name of civilization and progress.
Perhaps <<1>> can help. The Falinesti Faithful aren't led by anyone, but after the soldiers arrived he worked to keep tempers calm. He may know where to find the vault.

That is … likely. Uela has corrupted the Jackdaw crows, taken control of them.\n\nMany crows have disappeared. I hoped they had escaped her influence, but it sounds like she has instead dispatched them to be her eyes and ears elsewhere.

You ask many questions. Like a young one who has eaten too much moon-sugar.\n\nConstable Maldred is a friend, a trusted contact. We have worked together in the past. And speaking of work, don't you have some survivors to save?

I do. Nature is not philosophical, it is pragmatic. \n\nWe do not make judgments based on idealistic morals and complex theories. We make judgments based on experience, and experience tells us that you are all the same—not to be trusted.
Last I saw, he was in an encampment near the dig site. Mostly Falinesti Faithful, with a handful of soldiers.\n\nWe should avoid the site itself—the frost trolls are down there.
Many, many moons ago, these lands belonged to the Reach. Eventually, the natural order drove them away, but now they return to reclaim what they believe is theirs.

It won't be easy. First, you'll need to destroy Uela's totems. They keep us from drawing on the power of nature for our magicka.\n\nThe Reachmen guard them closely, but I'll fight at your side. No spells, but I've got sharp claws and a mean bite.

I do what I do for the forest, not for you. There are three totems—just a bunch of strung-together sticks for you, but they're like poison to me. \n\nI can't get too close, so it's all on you to destroy them. All right. Are you ready?

She has to die. Until Uela's gone, the corruption remains. Her blood is the nurture the forest needs. \n\nWhoah! My magicka is returning, and it's making me lightheaded …. Meet me over at the old tower. I need to get my bearings.
Yes, there was a storm the other night, and storms bring lightning. What does that prove? I should have chosen a better place to keep my cart. That's all.

As was <<1>>. When our digging revealed existing tunnels, she pulled us back to our camp before taking her soldiers to the dig site below.\n\nThen the frost trolls emerged from the caves. They slaughtered most soldiers left behind.
We were already at our camp. I know she led soldiers into one of the caves, but not which one.\n\nTake care, should you seek her out. You'll need to descend into the dig site.

She pressed us into service in the search for <<1>>. Initially, their treatment was harsh.\n\nBut I spoke with her directly and proposed she take a lighter approach. In return, I would convince the Falinesti Faithful to assist her efforts.

And if I did cut the flower? That doesn't solve the Wood Elves' problem. The Green Pact is their custom.\n\nI got an anonymous order for a flower and I filled it. I didn't know the flower was sacred. The one who placed the order is guilty, not me.
I was out in the storm, trying to clear away fallen branches and protect my cart. For all the good it did.

I shouldn't talk about it.\n\nLook, <<1>> has been very interested in old relics. A little while ago she pulled our main force out of <<2>> and came here. Except for the contingent she sent to <<3>>, of course.

You did? Ha! Well I guess we got the old hag's attention! Maybe we put the foul thing on the defensive!\n\nOf course, she probably has layers upon layers of protection. I don't even know how to find her. I don't suppose you have any inkling?
Artifacts, you know. Something she can use to help strengthen the Dominion, should it start to fall apart.
Not exactly. She wants <<1>> to be strong.\n\nJust imagine. If the queen had all the power, she could cut through Wood Elf or Khajiiti objections. No more debates—just swift, certain action.

The Blacksap Rebellion nearly tore the Wood Elves in two, and only <<1>> was able to end it. <<2>> is just a puppet. Everyone knows <<3>> pulls his strings. \n\nBut what good is a puppet if you can't control it?

Nope, thank the Eight. It's really something though, eh? We got a betting pool going about it. Gorour put twenty gold down on "Daedric plague." Lagbaal says they're coming out of Mauloch's arse or something. My money's on a wyrd hex.
Aye! Those faerie-fobbing witches out in the woods. \n\nWouldn't be the first time they put a curse on us. Turned all our pants backwards once, they did.
And what? Bah … never mind.
Not even a little bit. This one time, I had twelve toads in one of my kegs….
About as good as you might expect. Don't tell the regulars, but I've been watering the ale like mad. I haven't had a new shipment come in for weeks.
Not yet. I love 'em like family, but they're not exactly guild scholars. \n\nAnyway, I'm trying my hand at brewing my own ale to make up the difference.
Like troll piss on a hot day.
Well I had to use stale barley for hops … and we ran out of sugar so I used some old candies I found…. Yeah, I also didn't have any yeast, so I just sort of poured some brown ale in it.
Depends on the person, I suppose. Valerine was all torn up about it. Same with Lagbaal.
Well, if the queen sends me some gold, I'll take it back.
Bah. To me it's like some uncle I never met died and left me out of his will. No big deal, see?
Tired. Very tired.
Much taller.

The poor crows. She's taken complete control of them. Their spirits are helpless; they can only watch what happens to their physical forms from the nature realm.\n\nShe does have them coming and going though, so they would know where to find her.

As a matter of fact, now that I can draw on the power of nature again, there is.\n\nI can take you into the nature realm … not in that form, of course, but it would allow us to talk to the crows' true spirits. Do you trust me?

Usually we'd be out pursuing various contracts. By Vivec, fighting the Reachmen alone could fill our purses for a year. But these days, we're all working one big job.\n\nWe've put all our considerable resources into destroying the Daedric Anchors.

First rate! Welcome to the guild, Associate.

Now the fun part. Seek out and slay as many Daedra as you can find. If you manage to break some of those anchors there'll be a reward and maybe even some special assignments waiting for you.

Till then.

Yes, of course. We have a number of vacancies to fill. I'm sure I needn't tell you that the danger is … considerable. Not all of our comrades were prepared for it. \n\nBut I'm sure you're more than capable. Interested?

Yes—you must have seen them. The enormous dark chains falling from the sky? They're rather hard to miss.\n\nFrom what I'm told, they're coming straight out of Oblivion—Coldharbour to be more precise. Wherever they hit, Daedra pour out in droves.

The king's brother, Duke Renchant. He's at least acting as regent right now. \n\nShould've been Queen Arzhela who took over, but she's … not been herself. Understandable after losing her husband and her children, but the people miss her.

I shouldn't talk bad about the captain. He's probably the right man for the job.\n\nHe's a Nord, and he's fought the Reachmen before. With most of our officers dead, the duke only had so many options, and we had to have someone new.

Beats the Oblivion out of me. Ever since King Eamond died, they've been showing up all over the city. With all their cackling, it's a damn plague.\n\nCreepy too. They're just sitting there watching us. It's like they've come to see us all die.
I just told you! Choice and Free Will are subjects I hold quite dear.\n\nSo, you could fight a very good friend of mine. Or you could pull another lever. You're Choice!
If she were here, I'd peck her eyes out. \n\nNo. She's not in the nature realm. But of course, you can't reach her in the physical realm. Maybe one of the other crows knows more.

Oh? If you can access the physical realm, you might have a chance. The door to Uela's lair is in this realm, you see, but you have to break the wards in the physical realm.\n\nThere's more to it, though. You should ask one of the other crows.

Well, why didn't you just say so? That would work. There is something different about you, isn't there?\n\nUela's lair is in the island tower. Break the wards in the physical realm, but enter the door from here. Don't tell her I told you, though.
Wonderful! Just say the word and I'll bring him here.
Oh, all right, but do it with gusto!
You have wounded him gravely. It will be some time before his power is restored.

Alchemy is not a common practice among Wood Elves, so it's understandable that there's some confusion.\n\nThe only plant material I've ever used were leaves and flowers that naturally fell to the ground, as per our laws.
As your enemy fell, the one you call Abnur Tharn took Chim-el Adabal and fled. He returns to the land from whence he came, the place you call Cyrodiil.
The Amulet's power has been expended for a generation or more. The Imperial will not be able to use it, nor will he profit from it, though he will spend many frustrated years in the attempt.
Your story has only begun. \n\nMolag Bal still has plans for you. In many ways, these events played out to his advantage. And you have attracted the attention of the other Daedric Princes, as well.

The war between mortal kingdoms is still ravaging your world, but your true enemies are not mortal. \n\nIf you are to be prepared for the coming conflicts, you must fully comprehend what is at stake. You must live among those you make war upon.

Indeed. When you return to Tamriel, go to the place you call the Harborage. My gift awaits you there. It will allow you to  travel to other lands and hide your true nature from those who would see you as a foe.

I wouldn't say that. They just don't know him. \n\nRenchant's doing the best he can with what he's got. He's taking action. He's the one who put Captain Hjurrun in charge of defenses. I'm trying not to hold that against him though.

My sigil. It's unfortunate. There was a fierce storm the other night. What's a tangle of dead branches against a gale like that?\n\nThat's assuming the storm did it. Someone could have easily destroyed my sigil to make me look guilty.

I'd heard about a legendary village where all illness is cured, ever since I was a lad. When Draven got sick, I needed to find it, or learn whether it even existed. Spent nearly all our gold until I did.\n\nAnd here we are at last!

Draven entered the village a week ago. Kerbol says it's part of the treatment, to see how the patient fares without his or her family.\n\nShe sent someone to tell me it won't be much longer. I can't wait to be with my husband again!

Sir Jarnot? Poor old sot. He was escorting Princess Elara when she got ambushed and killed. \n\nJarnot would've been better off if he had died there too. I thought the queen was going to have him executed. He got off lucky, really.

Amazing. What seemed like a hopeless situation has turned around completely. Believe it or not, I have good tidings to share with you too. \n\nImperial Magus-General Septima Tharn is requesting a parley. I'm hoping it's to discuss a peace settlement.

No. I wouldn't put anything past the Imperials. I'm optimistic, but not naive. \n\nThat's why I've been delaying the meeting. I want you there … just in case. We'll also have members of the Fighters and Mages Guilds on hand if we need them.

I don't think so. Her lair's actually in the physical realm, so you'll assume your physical form. Probably not so much chewing, I suppose.\n\nThat's good though. You'll need your hands. After the crone's dead, you'll have to get her nasty little heart.

When I said her blood was the nurture that the forest needs, I meant that, literally. She's the source of the corruption here, so we need her heart to perform the ritual to cleanse the forest.\n\nSo … are you ready to go get it?

Captain Hjurrun's fought the bastards' leader before—Strastnoc. He says we're outmatched and we have to just wait them out. \n\nI say the captain's a few links shy of a full chain. With our defenses weakened, we can't risk waiting!

I know what it looks like, but I didn't cut that plant. I found it in the forest by the dead tree. It was already cut. I thought it was a gift from Y'ffre, to cure my wife of her wasting sickness.\n\nPlease, you must believe me.

Absolutely! Captain's ordered us to hold back, but not you … and he did say we need more outside help.\n\nMorale's been down in the dungheap since King Eamond died. If you can lop off this Strastnoc's head, it'd be an inspiration to the men.

I was sick yes, but my husband and I prayed to Y'ffre, and she saw fit to heal me. \n\nI suppose to a jealous eye it could look suspicious, but it's not evidence of guilt. On the contrary, some might say Y'ffre has rewarded our faithfulness.

We'll be in position above the parley site. If the Imperials try anything, we'll make sure they regret it. The three of us can cast spells to rain down fire, ice, lightning—we have it all.\n\nYou'll just need to tell us where to target our spells.

Why yes, that is my sign, and the sign of several others in this village.\n\nSurely it was shining because I was being blessed with good health after a period of such long sickness. I am still thanking the Divines for choosing to spare me.

For us, it's just sticking by the queen. If the Magus-General starts chanting, we go for the windpipe. \n\nIf things really go to Oblivion, we'll be shielding the queen until Gabrielle can get us all out of there.
How dare you! You read my most private thoughts and then hold them against me as evidence? Last I heard, thinking was not a crime.
So callous. How would you feel if you were dying? Wouldn't you seek a cure?\n\nOf course I looked for something that would help, but in the end it took faithful prayer and nothing else.

And you think I put it there?\n\nI've been sick for weeks. I've barely had the strength to sit up in bed, let alone go outside and cut a sacred flower. Someone must have placed it there to incriminate my husband while I was asleep.

How can so many know my name after all these years? Yes, I am <<1>>. I hoped to stem the tide of frost trolls by sealing their egress, but ice is the only form I may take beyond the walls of my prison.\n\nTell me why you are here.

The Mages Guild is dedicated to the pursuit of wisdom and knowledge. While others scramble for wealth and power, we seek learning of all kinds—especially magical.\n\nMight you be interested in becoming a Docent?
I was delighted to speak with another after so long. But once inside, she ignored me entirely.\n\nThen in her haste to find <<1>>, she loosed the frost trolls.

A wise decision! I hereby grant you the rank of Student in the Mages Guild, with all the responsibilities and privileges thereto. \n\nEvery book acquired, or collection of books completed, will now earn you status within the guild. Good luck!

Docents discover and bring us rare tomes and scrolls. Through their efforts, our libraries grow.\n\nIn exchange, a docent is entitled to purchase items restricted to guild members. Docents may also be offered occasional special tasks ….

Well, not yet—but it's good that you brought it to us. Very good indeed!\n\nYou're already well on your way to earning membership in the Mages Guild. Did you know the guild provides rewards for acquiring texts like this?
<<1>> suspended them in my prison to guard against invaders. It seems they had never before supped on the flesh of Men or Mer.\n\nBut once they did, it was a terrible frenzy.
<<1>> spoke of it being the "Second Era."\n\nIt seems I was trapped here in the First.

A wise decision! I hereby grant you the rank of Student in the Mages Guild, with all the responsibilities and privileges thereto. \n\nEvery book acquired, or collection of books completed, will now earn you status within the guild. Good luck!
Docents earn rank by bringing rare texts like this to our libraries. As their rank grows, so too do the rewards.\n\nMight you be interested in joining the Mages Guild?
You are not the first. <<1>> broke through to my prison in search of the same.\n\nI will aid you in seeking <<2>>, but only if you swear to free me.

<<1>> is the key to my prison beneath <<Ac:2>>. If I but touch its hem, it will steal all my hatred for <<3>> and fill the void with love. I'll make lute strings of his innards, first.\n\nOnly another may safely free me. A cruel and spiteful jest.
There is another cave, sealed by a frost-covered door. It leads to my prison.\n\nIf you swear to free me, I will allow you inside to speak of <<1>>.

Good. Take your time though. Rest up. You've earned it.\n\nThe duke will know of your deed, and you can go see him in the castle when you're ready. He'll reward you well. Might even offer you my job. It's yours if you want it.

We arrived with our horses on those merchant ships, along with Sir Etienne.\n\nMaybe it was rash to go against our orders and come here in defense of simple villagers. I won't presume to judge the actions of the men and women who died for our cause.

Yes. Sir Etienne was adamant we do so, though our venture seemed ill-fated from the start.\n\nWe didn't expect these wild ones, these Reachmen, would best Evermore-trained soldiers, and yet you can see how poorly we fared against them.

Just as they were thirty years ago, the madmen … they used the trees, rocks and homes here to out-maneuver our horses.\n\nI haven't ridden since the Black Drake's war, it's one of the only reasons I survived this skirmish.

If you wish to hear stories about the great war that brought the Daggerfall Covenant together, talk to someone else.\n\nAll I remember is the blood and the death, the desperate battle to save the life we knew and the lands we loved.
You've the look of an experienced combatant. Hold the line while I check on Sir Etienne at Medya's home.\n\nThe witchmen seem content to ransack the village for now, but be ready for anything.
No! I won't let you cast me aside, like everyone else. I'll make you see, just like all the others!
Wait! That's it, I'll go away with him, if he'll have me! Just let me try to convince him.\n\nBesides, there's not much of <<1>> left. It's a bit used up, don't you think?

It's pretty bad. People all over the region are getting sick—and they say that the plague turns the afflicted into monsters! The town consul, Dethisam, sent me to get help and warn other settlements about the plague.

Indeed. All of Tamriel's lore falls within our remit. Mages Guild members grow our rich collection of books, tomes, and ancient scrolls as they travel the world. We provide magical support to any who need our help.
In a manner of speaking. We avoid politics, alliances, battlefields and the typical conflicts of our age, believing foremost in the power of knowledge.

Our library has taught us new techniques—special spells and abilities available only to members.\n\nFrom time to time, we also have projects requiring those of a more adventurous bent. You may end up working with Guildmaster Vanus himself!
Excellent! I hearby grant you membership in the Mages Guild, with all the responsibilities and privileges thereof. Seek books and complete collections to improve your status within the Guild!

The Fighters Guild! You should consider joining us. Our new guildmaster is an Argonian, Sees-All-Colors. She has us all working to a singular purpose. We're hunting down the Daedra and their damned Anchors. Hard fights.

Keepers of lore, maintainers of the greatest de-centralized library in Tamriel, and desseminators of knowledge!\n\nOur members gather books from all over, and we provide magical aid to those who seek it.
Yes, but we don't hunt books for our own sake, but for everyone. We make the knowledge we find available to all, regardless of race, alliance, or the politics of the day.

There are certain unique magics known only by members of the Mages Guild. High-ranking and adventurous members are often called upon to complete special projects. You could end up working with Guildmaster Vanus himself!

Good. Then I hereby grant you membership in the Mages Guild, with all the privileges it entails. Of course, if you wish to rise in status within the Guild, the best way is to start gathering rare books!

The Fighters Guild! You should consider joining us. Our new guildmaster is an Argonian, Sees-All-Colors. She has us all working to a singular purpose. We're hunting down the Daedra and their damned Anchors. Hard fights.

Bandits. They robbed me, roughed me up. But I'll live. And a few bruises won't stop me. I have a plague to warn people about!\n\nI wonder, though. One of the bandits had a Maulborn recruiting letter. I saw it sticking out of his pack as he beat me.

<<1>> was the most beloved of my servants. Her voice bent the world to her will, yet she used her power for selfless works. Until she was taken to <<2>>.\n\nMolag Bal made her song of pain last millennia. But in his distraction, you will recover her.

Well, truth be told, you're the first person other than the bandits I've run into. And the afflicted heading for the Serk. There's a lot of them.\n\nWord of the curative has spread faster than the plague itself, as far as I can tell.

Her Majesty would ask you to inspect the defenses at the east gate and ask the former guard captain, Sir Jarnot, for his assessment of the duke's strategy.\n\nIf you are willing, the queen also wishes to know why a refugee was put in the stocks.

Sadly, I expect you are most likely to find him in the tavern, drinking away his sorrows. \n\nAfter Princess Elara was killed while under his protection, the queen herself demanded he step down. He was crushed.

If we knew that, we wouldn't have to ask for your assistance. \n\nThe bottom line is that the queen deferred to Duke Renchant because she believed he was better suited to defend the city. Now, she simply wants to make sure he's doing a good job.

With the city in such dire straits, the queen is determined to avoid controversy. If people heard she was inquiring as to the state of the city's defenses, there would be an uproar. \n\nIf you conduct the inquiries, however, it can be more discreet.
A better question might be what hasn't happened. We've been beset by all manner of horrors in just a few days.
Our beloved King Eamond fell in battle against the Reachmen—and so did his son.
You must know of the Reachmen. They're the wild clans who live in the mountains north of Evermore. \n\nThey've come over the border in force and are nearer to the city every hour.
As well as can be expected, I think, under the circumstances. But that's just one woman's opinion.

Rulership should fall to Queen Arzhela, but she… I hate to speak ill of our queen, but she simply doesn't have the constitution for that sort of thing. \n\nShe's appointed Duke Renchant to handle most matters of state.
Oh, the birds. Curse them. They started gathering shortly after King Eamond's death. Just three or four would gather at first … then ten … then twenty. And soon enough we were overrun.
No. But it certainly seems like an ill omen. \n\nAfter them came the refugees from Northglen, escaping the Reachmen. If I were them, I'd seek refuge at sea or in Stormhaven. Grim times, grim times.

By no means does she wish to reinstate him, but Sir Jarnot was the captain of the guard here in Evermore for more than a decade. He was a longtime friend of King Eamond as well.\n\nThe queen simply wants to hear his assessment of the city's defenses.

Just vague rumors. Let's face it. Our forces were devastated in the last battle with the Reachmen, and there is no doubt our defenses are stretched thin.\n\nWe just want to make sure that everything possible is being done to protect the city.
How dare the Sentinel pick his successor out of pity! But she didn't bring us the bud, you did. Why should we give our blessing to one who needs another to carry her burdens?
Too weak to even follow you? No, the forest does not need such a creature! \n\nThe Sentinel oversteps his bounds, and the wyrd will not allow it!

His time wanes. He will make this girl the new Sentinel, untrained and unfit! He holds no respect for the forest, and no respect for the wyrd.\n\nWhat does it matter to us if one child withers to allow the forest to grow free, I ask you?
Hm. We've heard nothing from the Sentinel these past days but demands. Still, we will do what must be done.\n\nPerhaps we can trust you to make the correct decision when the time comes.

Take this ring … it's my wedding band. It's the one thing I hold dear in this wretched place.\n\nShould you bring it to the inner vault, I can join you in icy form. I'll warn you of the dangers and aid you against them.

I was no mage when <<1>> first stole me from Falinesti, but I've studied every inch of this icy prison. With effort, I learned to sap away its energy.\n\nIt's what allows me to form the icy construct, as we first met.

You swore you would free me!\n\nForgive me. The promise of freedom ruins my manners. You should do what you must, and what you are willing. I will not press you to betray who you are, not on my account.
Direct my wedding band at any foe. I can use it as a focus to freeze your enemies for a short time.
<The crates appear to be stocked with fresh supplies, weapons, and armor. The crates are stamped as cargo from a ship called the "Bjoulsae Queen.">
Ignoring the fact that my Prince's unbreakable will compels me to open the way to <<1>>, despite the unspeakably bloody terror to greet you on the other side?
He didn't know anyone here, that I know of. Who could he possibly trust enough to lower his guard?
Do you think Sir Etienne was reading the book when he was killed?\n\nThat's a pretty dry topic to just pick up for no reason.
I'm sorry, but I don't see how that could be related.
So they were comfortable, or in no hurry. Perhaps Medya washed her hands before going outside. They say the witchmen lust after the scent of blood.
Sir Etienne doesn't look like he put up a fight. That's not like him, even if he was hit from behind.\n\nHis leg's been tended to. Looks like he was attacked while eating. What else?
If that proves anything, I think it shows that the only person who didn't kill him was Medya.\n\nWhy treat someone if you expected to kill them?
So they weren't concerned that Medya or I would discover what happened?\n\nEither that or they just didn't care if anyone found the scene, assuming that it would blend in with the carnage outside.
She hadn't mentioned having a son. Hardly damning evidence, though.
That would take a lot of force, all things considered.\n\nSir Etienne's armor was in fine shape. His squire would see to that.
What is it?

I find it hard to believe that a goodly old midwife would have anything to do with this heartless slaughter.\n\nHer apprentice <<1>> is down by the docks. I imagine he would be a good place to start asking questions.
You have seen the spirit of Jofnir, but always just for a moment. This one believes we can summon him. Speak to him. \n\nLearn who murdered him.
Aelif told you, she has power. Magical gifts, connections to lands beyond. She will use them to draw the spirit to this place.\n\nThen we shall see, yes? We begin.
You could be Molag Bal himself for all I know. I'd still help you open the door, Lord of Brutality or not.\n\nYou aren't him, are you?
Good, good.\n\nI'd expect the Harvester of Souls to be taller.
No you're not. Not enough horns.\n\nAnd you don't smell of rotten meat. Molag Bal has terrible hygiene, even a Scamp knows that.
Indeed. Atop the eastern stair is the secret entrance to the Ancestral Crypt. The ring is within.
Ah, my dear, dear wife. She so loved helping people. She cared about Crestshade with all her heart.\n\nThank you for bringing me this news.
Eight preserve my soul! My poor, dear wife! Why would you tell me such a thing?\n\nI'll never be able to forgive myself for leaving her alone. Oh, why did she have to be so brave?
Kynareth's tears, she's been taking too many risks in trying to treat the wounded who haven't fled here!\n\nYou didn't find her dead out there, did you?
That's some small comfort, at least. \n\nPlease, leave me so I can grieve in peace.
She hasn't lived to be as old as she is without being careful. I'm sure—I hope she's all right.\n\nShe lived here when the Reachmen came down out of the hills before, with the Black Drake.
That's a relief, I think. What did you want to ask me about, then?
Sounds like jealousy to me. It won't stand in my way. I won't give up a second chance at life for the whims of some forest folk.\n\nStenwick is a kind man. Why won't they see that he means no harm?
The wyrd can't interfere forever. Let them bless this thing and be done with it. Stenwick's not getting any younger.

Enough for both of us? No? Then you use them as a disguise. Kerbol's too familiar with my face by now, and she'll recognize me whatever I wear.\n\nThey're binding him to the village forever. I don't understand yet. Make them stop before it's too late.
There's not much to tell. Most of the people here are fishermen.\n\nThe longest journey most of us have ever taken is to cross the Bjoulsae River to sell our fish to merchants in Evermore.
In all the years I've been her apprentice, more than three now, I've never heard her say an unkind thing.\n\nShe's the closest thing this dumpy little fishing hamlet has to a leader!

They did, but they didn't kill everyone. Medya and a few others lived through it, but she's the last one still alive here.\n\nShe's been a pillar for the community since then, even though the witchmen haven't raided us since—until now I mean.
A son? It would be the first I've heard of it.\n\nMedya is like a mother to a lot of us, but she's never raised any children that I know of.
Yes—No. I mean, that's correct. They raid other places, but they don't raid here. Well, until now. \n\nI'd always just assumed that we were under the benevolent protection of the gods.
She's been trying to treat the wounded on the field.\n\nIf you don't see her outside, she's probably inside one of the homes. Some of the other people are still out there!
I know little of use beyond the walls of this prison, but I'll answer what I can.
I … see. My mother must be in mourning, then. I will send word that I am well, if Stenwick is willing.\n\nAh, we have company, it seems. Who's coming in?
So you saw those? You are very perceptive. \n\nThe truth is that we've found an ally to help defend the city. I'm not quite ready to make this information public though.

I opened our gates to the refugees, but there are limits, and that man was completely mad!\n\nStanding outside the castle, shouting that we were all going to die? The people of Evermore are terrified already. We can't afford such nonsense.

Yes. That is the ship that transported the supplies.\n\nThere are more supplies being offloaded even now. Please. If you'll just be patient, I'll share all the details in due time.  For now, you must stay away from that ship though. It's off-limits.

Listen. I can tell that you have an inquisitive nature, and I know your intentions are good, but I cannot risk revealing all my plans just yet.\n\nSuffice to say, I've found a way to protect the city from the Reachmen, and that is what matters.

All right. If you cannot be convinced to let this go …. \n\nYou must understand. Desperate times call for desperate measures. If those Reachmen take this city, they are going to kill every man, woman, and child. Anything is better than that.

Take my amulet. Its power is spent, but the Voice of the Forest will recognize it and grant you an audience.\n\n<<1>> may not welcome you when you take the bud to her, but persevere. She knows what the wyrd must do.

Some call her the Voice of the Forest. In a way, she is. I need a bud from one of her branches, one freely given. It can harness the full power of these woods to safeguard Elara's life.\n\nMay I ask your aid once again?

They are guardians of nature in the truest sense. And I am a guardian of the people. Our interests don't always coincide.\n\nThey see my role as Sentinel as unnatural, though the Sentinel has existed for generations.

Hear me out. A few weeks ago, Imperial diplomats made an offer.\n\nThey have a deal with the Reach. If we surrender the city to Imperial authority, the Reachmen cannot attack. Not only will we survive, but we'll also retain considerable autonomy.
As I said before, the Bjoulsae Queen is off-limits to all but its crew and the city guard.\n\nYou've given me no reason to trust you, so at this point, I think I'll say no more.

We don't have a choice, and at this point, you don't either.\n\nSteps are being taken as we speak, and there's nothing you can do to stop us from moving forward. You don't even have any proof with which to raise an alarm.
Then I shall need a proper weapon.\n\nKasura said that my father's greatsword lies with the ring. It seems proper that I should wield it in his honor.

The queen is going to have to take charge. If this doesn't knock her into her senses, I don't know what will.\n\nWe need proof though. Can you untie me and then look around? Anything to prove what they're planning. I'll meet you out on the docks.
He said the ritual would protect you. If you kill the creature while holding the charged totem, it will be destroyed when it tries to possess you.\n\nI don't know whether to believe him or not.
My part in this story has ended, but yours has only begun. The world has been made right for now, but it is still wounded and in need of tending.
I cannot say. But I do not think the Scrolls have finished with me. Perhaps one day we shall meet again.

If it is destined that we shall meet again, then destiny will find a way. \n\nFor me, I think it's best that I shall be forgotten by this world. Let me become a sad footnote in Tamriel's long history. I deserve nothing more.
What now? For you, it seems there's more to do. For us ….\n\nWe've seen too much, my friend. Been through too much. I think it's time for us to go.
No! Listen! Oop! Oop! Breton. Breton!
Sai and I talked about it a few days ago. What would happen if we both survived. I'd like to go back to the Abbey of Blades with him, and help them rebuild.
Maybe some day. It's not as though I'm dropping off the face of Tamriel!\n\nAnd if not, well, I'm sure there's a seat for you in Sovngarde. If you get there first, save me a cold mug of mead.
Not … not here. I can show you way out. Make sure Goblins … leave you alone.\n\nFollow me … ack!

Snow Lily is gone, and I will mourn her passing, but my duties are not yet finished.\n\nMy Lord Varen and I will travel to the Abbey of Blades to help rebuild. Then I will devote myself to the creation of a new generation of blademasters.
Thank you, but I cannot leave the Valley of Blades. I must bury the dead and tend to the wounded.
Who can say? I do know that I need time to heal. I cannot help but blame you for Snow Lily's death. Perhaps that is unfair—it was her decision as much as yours—but it is the truth.
I'll go and find Sir Jarnot and any other guards who remain loyal. After you've informed the queen, come and meet me outside the inn.
He may not see me as an ally, thanks to your interference. He may only remember how much pain I caused.
I—I was simply referring to you! I and the other survivors have been hoping, praying for someone to come along and help us fight off our Daedric tormentors.\n\nAnd here you are!
This … Lady Laurent's fault! We told her about … Goblins!
My uncle is called Istah and serves as Bergama's Justice. You have met him, is it not so?
Then you are the one who cleared his name? He speaks highly of you. \n\nMay Ruptga bring you fortune. The sons and daughters of Bergama bless you.
Of course, of course! What can I tell you? Just so you know, as you talk I'm going to imagine there's a little person inside you moving your mouth like a puppet. It helps keep me interested.

Enormous chains descend from the sky! A passage opens to Oblivion, and Daedra boil out to lay waste to the countryside. I don't know who started calling them Daedric Anchors, but Mauloch knows it fits.

Hah! Good question. We train our members in special techniques. And the higher-ups are always looking for motivated members to help with special projects. Colors herself might even have a task for you someday.
Then let me be the first to officially welcome you as a comrade in arms of the Fighters Guild! Get out there! And take the fight to the Daedra!

Enormous chains descend from the sky! A passage opens to Oblivion, and Daedra boil out to lay waste to the countryside. I don't know who started calling them Daedric Anchors, but Mauloch knows it fits.

Hah! Good question. We train our members in special techniques. And the higher-ups are always looking for motivated members to help with special projects. Colors herself might even have a task for you someday.
Then let me be the first to officially welcome you as a comrade in arms of the Fighters Guild! Get out there! And take the fight to the Daedra!

No catch, mortal! Not this time. Look, no matter what choice you make, Shalidor's always going to know I got inside his head. Again! That's what I'm trading you the island for. This … this is just something between the two of us.
I am a healer and so I know when it is time to cut away the diseased flesh from the healthy, it was time for the outsiders to leave!
You heard it from the squire's lips when you first arrived here!\n\nThe only way to excise the outsiders was over their dead bodies. What choice did I have?
You can judge me all you want, outsider. I know what I did was right.
This is our land, our place! \n\nThe Nords, the Bretons, everyone takes and takes from the people.
I did what needed to be done! \n\nThe old families would have been saved, the ones who belong here!
No! They were thieves, every single one of them!\n\nThis land isn't theirs to live on, it belongs to the people!
That's because war is like a plane of Oblivion. If you haven't been, you can't fathom what it must be like.\n\nAnd if you have, it's not something you wish to relive.

The things I saw during Black Drake's invasion … they kept me from the purity of heart required to be a knight. Others managed. Not me.\n\nI've been plagued by doubts and anxiety ever since then, like an immeasurably heavy stone around my neck.

Yes, it is. I've been taking care of scrapes and broken bones for as long as babes have been born here.\n\nThings were pleasant before all of these outsiders came blundering in and ruining our way of life.
It's true, though if the community is like a tree … sometimes pruning can encourage new growth.

I'm a simple hedgewitch, I suppose you might say. The boy in the boathouse is my apprentice.\n\nI mend both injuries of the body and the mind for my people, and keep records of the births and deaths of our kind.
It's a humble place with more fish than intrigue and secrets.\n\nWe had a beautiful community, like a tree with deep roots … but one that has become wild and corrupted as you can see now.
I'm captain of the independent sailing vessel Albatross. We found a map to an Imperial treasury that led us here, to <<Ac:1>>. But when we tried to claim it, our fortunes ebbed with the tides.

We're tired of sailing independently. We planned to hand over the treasure to the Thalmor so they could make us privateers.\n\nBut <<1>> led a mutiny, captured most of my crew, and kidnapped my wife. Once he has the treasure, he'll kill them all.

You see all the giant vines choking the life out of everything here? \n\nThe ritual will purge the area of their evil presence. It's necessary for the land to heal. Why are you stalling though? You've grown attached to those vines?

Actually, hold onto it. I have an idea. Wyress Freyda will howl, but I think you've earned the honor. \n\nLet us begin the ritual, and once we've penetrated the earth, you can throw the heart into the circle to complete the spell.
You just missed it. Watching <<1>> run and hide when he saw a rat was one of the funniest things I've seen in a long time.
Deathly afraid apparently. I saw a rat in the attic earlier. I'm thinking about grabbing it and letting it go near him just to watch him jump around like a scared little girl again.
Yeah, that's him. He's a strange sort. Keeps to himself and drinks mostly, but I've seen him fingering a key he's got hanging around his neck.

I saw him fiddling with the coffer on his dresser when I wandered past earlier. When he saw me looking, he pretended to be doing something else. I'd wager he's got something special hidden inside and I'll bet that key opens it.

The wyrd won't call me anything different. Most people who live around here call me Old Gurles, or just Stenwick.\n\n"The Viridian Sentinel" is a bit of a mouthful, don't you think? Makes me sound more important than I really am!

These woods have a life and mind of their own. Well, what I do is make sure it doesn't get out of hand.\n\nThere are some good folk who live near these lands, and without a firm hand, why, the wild would grow right over them!
Just in time! I've made a salve for Elara that'll help her wake. I'll channel what energy I have left into her.\n\nThe amulet should be able to sustain me afterwards. At least, I hope it will.
How? I'll do anything to save Draven any more pain. He's ashamed of this disease, but it's not his fault.\n\nIs there anything I can do? Anything at all?
I suppose you're right. I'll stay here, with Stenwick.\n\nBut this forest voice … if it's like a spriggan, it will react to their deaths. I'd bet you could kill some spriggans to draw it out.
So he may pass our yoke to another? A stranger to the woods?\n\nYour demand is empty, voice of the Sentinel. I refuse.
Take the bud and begone. But know this. There shall be no peace in these woods.
Why should we care for a mortal?
We only seek to grow as our nature intends. Your Sentinel is the one who prevents this!\n\nBut you care nothing for our plight. It is a waste to speak of this further.

The Sentinel cannot, but perhaps you can.\n\nThe amulet prevents the woods from cleansing itself. Sprouts lie sleeping within the troll's offal. Use the amulet to wake them and add to our number. Then I will grant you this boon.
You hold the last of his power over us. Why should we fear such an insignificant object?
Is that so? We will remember that, mortal.\n\nTake the bud and begone. If your promise is empty, there shall be no peace in these woods.
Then take your prize, mortal, and begone.
I'm fine. I'm dead—but fine otherwise.\n\nI take it you're looking for a way out? The Architect never allows those who wander in to just leave.
What? Is it my Sorion? Is he … is he all right?
Ні!
Ні!
We think he's here to make contact with Montclair's forces, but we haven't been able to prove it.
Heh, he could be the Green Lady's personal bard and I still wouldn't know him.\n\nThe truth is, I keep myself to myself. I have certain tastes my people frown upon.

Plants. I eat plants, Green Pact be damned. Any Wood Elves get wind of it and I'm in the stockade quick as you can shout "Oathbreaker."\n\nI'm sorry, I just don't see much difference between the flesh of a pumpkin and the flesh of, say, an Altmer.
None of your business. And before you get any ideas, you should know this garden is for aesthetic purposes only.\n\nNow please leave.
No. Minstrels generally don't come out this way, and I don't go into town much. The locals claim they can smell pumpkin on my breath.

If you're looking for a precise definition, you asked the wrong Wood Elf. Put generally, we aren't to eat nor harm any plant life.\n\nIt's a noble goal, but you cannot ask me to give up the taste of pumpkin. Life is simply too short.

The drawbridge is controlled by those levers. There is a pattern to it. All the levers must face the same way for the bridge to open. But which way? Forgive me, I am just not certain. The Halls of Torment took a great toll upon my memory.
I seem to recall that using one will cause the adjacent levers to switch their positions. Perhaps that will be of some help.

There is a chance we can save her life. It will require more work though.\n\nThe heartwood degrades quickly in the lurchers, but sometimes remains pure. If you take the extra time to find the pure heartwood, it could save the spriggan.
Quickly then! Let me mix it into a poultice.\n\nI am grateful that you were able to find the pure heartwood.

I hope so. Here. Take the poultice and apply it to the poor thing. I must be prepared to do … whatever is necessary.\n\nI pray to all the gods to bless our efforts and bring it back. The forest would never be the same without spriggans.
You're right. I'm going to do it. I'm a good looking fellow and I've got loads of personality. I'll go over and ask her to have a drink with me. What have I got to lose?
You think the Fellwatch could be behind this? This is troubling, but we will need more evidince. Try checking around Leonce's capin north of here.
Agreed. But we need to draw him out. Otherwise he'll order the mutineers to kill my crew.\n\nAnd if he sees my face, <<1>> is as good as dead. We have to be smart about this.
Hold onto the spriggan bud. It must be the key to the ritual. I'll see if anything happens when I touch the altar.

With fire.\n\nThere's a barrel of <<z:1>> on the docks. If you burn the Imperial war supplies on the docks, everyone will be too focused on putting it out to worry about <<2>>. When he shows his face, you can stick a blade through it.

Here, take this whistle. Give it a sharp blast and my crew will help you fight any mutineers in your path.\n\nOnce they're distracted, we'll keep the mutineers off your back while you hunt <<1>>. Good luck.
No. He needs to watch his cowardly little plan crumble first. I want him demoralized before we confront him. \n\nI also want to think about exactly what to say. It has to be good, you know.
Removing <<1>> from the inner vault weakened the magic of the prison. Now you must break it, once and for all!

Aye. My Reachmen march this way. Evermore will be ours! But not if Imperials have it!\n\nThey are a threat right now, for you and for me. You need friends. Let us be friends then, and join together to beat our common foe.

Temporary truce! Neither wants Evermore Imperial. We work together, destroy the Imperials, then we are enemies again.\n\nI like it not myself, but you have no one to help you now. The only choice for either of us is to work together.
You cannot strike down spies, but my crows can, pretty little pets. Mark our foes, signal my crows, and we will strike. \n\nWe will clean the city of Imperials. Then we are enemies again.

<<1>> is a slippery thing, especially with enchantments that bind its bearer.\n\nPlace it upon the brazier at the heart of this room and it will smother the curse upon me. Have no fear—the relic will come to no harm.
Soon I'll leave this place and return to my home.\n\nI'd nearly lost all hope.
How I long to watch you stumble and fail, but an ancient pact compels me to explain the rite.\n\nOne simply has to gather the motes about the lake. But beware! We are not without our own defenses.
The stone and metal, down in the depths beneath the soil. Locked away in darkness. Whispered, whispered to the keepers. Now quiet. The whisperer silent, again. Peace returns to the grove.
He was a fellow instructor, here at the Agea Relle, teaching the discipline of Destruction magic.\n\nLosing him was a tragedy to me, and to the magical community. I hope he rests in peace.

And as a little girl I wanted a pet guar I could decorate with ribbons and call Penelope. But we don't always get what we want. Especially in war.\n\nThe Light has guided us this far. It is not done with us yet.
Remain behind? And deny them the glory of being there when we achieve victory? Never!\n\nWhen Verandis starts his march to the top of the Doomcrag, we will be with him every step of the way.

My husband was a guard for a merchant caravan. One day he found a magic amulet on a dead man laying in the road. Almost overnight he became despondent, and when he spoke he would only talk about the bandits he had killed while defending the caravan.
First, I need to listen to the village elder, <<1>>. She may have news about Sir Etienne's condition.\n\nAnd then, yes, I do need help to deal with this situation. Stay right here.

What else can I do but seek my home?\n\nBut everything is so different now. <<1>> mentioned an "Aldmeri Dominion," yet I don't know what that means. Without someone to guide me, I may as well prostrate myself before <<2>>.
Truly? Then I must find this <<1>> and see what he knows of Falinesti.\n\nI should seek him out. And see the sky again, with my own eyes.
Because it's the unluckiest thing I could think of. The sight of those birds terrify sailors from one end of Tamriel to the other. You'd think they were Daedric Princes with wings.
The only thing left is to defeat the Architect. It pains me to take more from that man than we already have—but I doubt he'll let us leave without a fight.

Yes, the leader of the Arbordawn cult. He was very cross with me, shouting and carrying on. So I transformed him into a more manageable little fowl. It will wear off after we've gone, but he's much more pleasant to be around now. Sorry, where was I?
If you have the amulet, I suggest you find a way to be rid of it as soon as possible before you lose the will to even try.

No, nothing worked. I even paid to have the origin of the amulet divined and learned it was crafted in Cormount. Surprisingly my husband volunteered to go, but he was found dead not far from town the next day and the amulet was gone.

I don't want my ship filled with superstitious fools moaning about the draugr below the waves, or cursed gold in treasure chests. I want a straight-backed crew ready to knock the draugr overboard and dispel ancient curses, so we can spend the gold.
I did? I had had a few drinks, and then I must've blacked out.\n\nWoke up here a while ago. Tried to sleep, but I kept dreaming of the same man. Wouldn't stop dancing.
Good. Still have a bit of lightning inside me. I'll help you get to him, so we can bash his face in.
Can't sleep, or the man dances. I don't want to dance with him.\n\nI'm coming with you.
Gaercroft? Isabeth didn't send you? Either way, I'm not going anywhere with these wounds.
She saved me from those … things out there! She went to search the house nearby. Hatmi was there. She said she'd send help.\n\nYou have to find her. She saved my life.

Frankly, this place isn't easy to defend! It was originally just a little two-man outpost, here to guard the road.  \n\nWith enemies to the north and south, we decided to increase our presence here. Turns out that was a mistake.

Damn Garrison Commander decided to stockpile extra weapons and food here too, so we wound up sitting on a bunch of supplies we couldn't protect.\n\nMost of it's gone now though. If we're raided again, we might as well just retreat to Evermore.

Not everything, but they did seize some of our goods in the last raid.\n\nMe and the other Baandari were busy helping the knights defend the barricades. We didn't see the Imperials slip into our tents and steal our most valuable possessions.

Do they? Did Knight Commander Cheryline send you over to ask this of me? Can she not even show Silver-Paws the respect of asking herself? Of course not!\n\nEither way, we can spare no further supplies. We've given the knights everything we can.
They are called Ilambris-Athor and Ilambris-Zavon—Daedric fiends. So powerful was my husband's curse that it drew their attention and brought them to this plane.\n\nThey design our daily tortures.

I wonder what the Knights of Saint Pelin would do if the scales were tipped the other way? Would they give up their supplies for a group of Baandari merchants?\n\nI won't have these knights' blood on my hands though. I will take the high road.

Ah … now you speak the language of the Baandari. You must understand, everything we sell, we either buy somewhere else, or we pay for the materials we use to craft it.\n\nWe cannot afford to simply give things away.

Hm. Let's see. I noticed that the knights have some very well-made bows stashed away in their weapons cache over there.\n\nTell the Knight Commander I'll give her all the poultices she needs in exchange for those bows.

Not for free. What would the Knights of Saint Pelin do if the scales were tipped the other way? Would they give up their supplies for a group of Baandari merchants?\n\nNo. If the Knight Commander wants the poultices, she'll have to trade for them.
My amulet! Tell me, did it do its work? Did the Argonian suffer?

The Fighters Guild. Our role has never been more important. You've seen the anchors yourself, no doubt. The Daedra grow in strength and in number. It is up to us to put them down, and for that we need capable fighters.

Have you not heard the cries for help over the cawing of these cursed birds? \n\nNorthglen is where our beloved King Eamond fell. The Reachmen there are up to something, but my men and I had to retreat before we could figure out what it was.

Of course he does. I saw him eyeing those bows. They were crafted back in Saint Alessia's days. They're worth more than gold—they're practically relics.\n\nMy wounded can't afford for us to bargain though. Just give him the damn bows!

Dark Anchors. Black chains of Oblivion that claw their way into this world and latch on, opening a gateway between realms. They're the source of most of the Daedra troubling us these days. That's why we need people like you.
That's part of it, but those who rise in the ranks and prove themselves are often tasked with other important missions. In return, you'll receive the very best of training and access to our armory.
I knew you wouldn't let us down. There's no big ceremony, but let me say you are most welcome among us. As you rise in the ranks, you'll quickly see the decision was worth it.

When my platoon set out we were thirty-five swords, but look at us now. \n\nThese are the soldiers who weren't grievously wounded—a few cracked ribs, broken arms and fingers, that sort of thing. We plan to set out again soon.
They're over there with our other last remaining supplies, in the fancy chest. I'll give a sign to Sergeant Zilu. He shouldn't give you any trouble.
He's … a dear friend of mine. All the souls that reside in these walls belong to friends of mine. I regret their fate every day.

My husband and I met as adventurers. We founded this school to teach practical sorcery and use-of-arms as survival skills.\n\nThe world can be a dangerous place, and we wanted to give our students the means to tame it. Like we did. Had I known ….
I didn't want to concern you! I thought the herbalists would be back any minute now. But now that I think about it, they have been gone a long time.\n\nI hope nothing unfortunate has befallen them.

They went up to the water. They needed a special algae from the lake. Don't tell anyone, but that's one of the key ingredients in the Baandari poultices.\n\nIf something happened to them at the lake, though … I don't know.
Now's our chance to end this though, to make sure those raiders never show their faces here again.\n\nHow would you feel about pressing our advantage?
They're in retreat now, but they couldn't have pushed off from the shore yet.\n\nI say we burn their boats, or rather you burn their boats, if you're up for it.

They're here, and right now, I'm damn glad of it. The cats are all carrying Alessian bows too. I just hope those bows still shoot straight.\n\nEither way, their arrows will only do so much. If you're willing, I'd put you on the line too.
The Imperials are coming from the lake, so the worst of it will be at the northeast gate.\n\nIf you'll plant yourself there and keep them from getting by, we might just make it another day.
He did? Not Isabeth? I'd hoped she'd gotten the others to the camp by now.
It is the Fell Watch, it has to be. Why else would they take over the Inn? This isn't an invasion.
These Bretons are kidnapping our people. They have been waiting to get rid forever.
I don't know, I'm just here for the snacks.
It is these Orcs. I mean, I don't have anything against Orcs personally, but we can't expect them to act civilized forever. They are Orcs, after all.
Thefts? Who cares! There're Vampires, I tell you. I can hear them crawling on my roof in the night.
I wouldn't know, now would I? They won't let me back in!\n\nThe Fell's Brigade moved in and locked the place up tight. I don't care about all this politics and accusations. I just want my inn back!
Oh thank the Eight. Did Isabeth send you? She was here to save us, but couldn't take us all. I told her to take my sister. There was a wyress too. She told Isabeth she can lead them to safety.
Yes, the wyress said they've been scouting the Reachmen here as well. They have an encampment just north of the house. Hopefully, my sister is safe with them. I've never seen a wyress before.
She was here. She returned our sister to us, so we are in her debt.

The other has a sickness within her, of an unknown kind. We will keep the sick girl away from the land, lest she spread an incurable disease through our woods.\n\nIf you're curious, speak to Wyress Delphique. She's within the ruins.
Ah, you seek this child.\n\nShe goes nowhere. She's infected, and I must determine what it is she carries inside her.
It's a seed for certain, though what the Dark Witnesses have cultivated in the fields of Northglen is a mystery.\n\nI've one last attempt at a cure. You're just in time to witness the results.
Killing? Oh, do you mean the cleaning brigades?\n\nDon't you worry about them. They're simply doing what they must to make <<1>> sparkle.
You're trussed up, or you're thrown in the catacombs.\n\nEither way, you deserve it for disobeying the mayor. He's a just man, a righteous man. We should heed his words, every one of them.
Oh, no. I can't leave my home until it's entirely clean.\n\nBesides, the mayor said none of us can leave, and we all know what happens when we don't listen to the mayor.
Dominion? <<1>> is no longer part of the Dominion. The mayor decreed it.\n\nIf Dominion scouts marched their muddy boots onto our streets, we'd truss them all up!
I hope so, because we're going to spread out and each cover a different area. If anyone comes, we'll call it out, but we'll wait for you to direct us.
The brigand who killed my son! It took all my resources to make that amulet and track him down. \n\nYou see, I am not a strong or violent man, but I do know my craft. That amulet is my masterpiece.

It magnifies the guilt of taking a life, slowly overwhelming the wearer with grief until he takes his own life. It's a little bit of poetry, if I do say so myself. \n\nAlthough it's been so long, I was beginning to doubt it worked.

This … this isn't right. This person obviously did not deserve to die. What have I done?\n\nGive me the amulet. I made it impossible to give away, but I created it, so you should be able to give it to me.
What? That can't be! You're lying. The Argonian sent you, didn't he? He's not dead at all, is he?
It's my turn to wear the amulet now. If anyone is guilty, if anyone deserves it, it's me.

Of course. The Light provides, as always. \n\nBaron Montclair is … changed. We need to find out what has driven him to this perilous course of action. A letter, a journal—we need something to give us more insight into why he has betrayed us.

Two Shornhelm Guard officers. They defected to Montclair's side and helped him take over the upper city.\n\nLook for <<1>> and <<2>>. Perhaps you can deal with these traitors and discover Montclair's motivations. Baron Dorell can tell you more.
The Eight Divines, of course. I won't be caught with unmade beds!
I saw a few Dominion soldiers a few hours ago. I believe the mayor promised their meat to the Wood Elves, but I could be wrong.\n\nThere were sheets to wash.
The Wood Elves are going to eat their hearts, I imagine. It's what they do, isn't it? Eat the hearts of their enemies?\n\nBut if you'll excuse me, I need to prepare for their arrival.
I created this abominable object. It's only fitting that I am destroyed by it. It's justice.
Hm. Thank you! \n\nWell, she will not be disappointed. We Baandari make amazing poultices—some of the most potent in all of Tamriel. Her knights will be healed in no time.
A very good story. I don't know how a scamp like you has such good friends, Cinder-Tail.\n\nWhich way did this thief go? He made off with enough moon-sugar to knock over a mammoth.

Excellent. I'm going to open one portal directly to the parley site for the queen and the Fighters Guild members, and another to take us above. Actually, I guess we should go first. Now, which portal was which? \n\nOh! I remember. Here we go.

But then why am I not ambling about mindlessly trying to kill the living? Isn't that what the undead do?\n\nDame Valyrie says the gods have resurrected me … but why? Because of my bloodline? I'm sorry—this is just … too much.
I am blind to all but the fire. It consumed my eyes, and my thoughts, for I was jealous of its power. I wanted it for myself.\n\nBut it forgives as it consumes. And soon, it will forgive me.
Of course not. And Jode's Chariot does not have the authority to launch an investigation. <<1>> will not be happy.\n\nThank you, citizen, for your vigilance.

Arkay himself, of course. His church sits nearby; these grounds are consecrated in his name.\n\nThis was foreseen. Death denied the prince from defeating Evermore's enemies, but the anointed shall now command an army of the dead.
A mortal cannot hope to understand the will of the divine. \n\nYou must simply tell him to trust the power with which he is imbued. His destiny will unfold as he trusts his instincts.

I tried to draw out the evil, but my spell agitated it. Transformed her into one of those abominations roaming Northglen. \n\nSmall wonder we've seen no prisoners. They've turned them. And as their army grows, so does the threat on the Viridian Woods.

The truth is always a threat to evil men. Mannimarco feared I would reveal his treachery. And if knowledge of Nirn's vulnerability were to become known, it could threaten his master's schemes. Molag Bal does not favor loose ends.\n\nWalk with me.

When I discovered the truth about the Five Companions, I made subtle inquiries. But apparently, not subtle enough. Mannimarco got word of my interest and abducted me. He took me to Coldharbour, where I remained a prisoner until you freed me.
Whatever the Dark Witnesses are using, it consumes the victim. Had this child lived, she would have attacked.\n\nWe've been observing them. Their power increases in numbers.
Yes. We believe a seed is forced inside. It takes root within the heart. As you saw, any real attempt to remove them only spurs on the growth and takes the victim to the final phase.
Take this rune to wither the Reachmen's markers in the fields. Then cut off <<1>>'s head.\n\nProve yourself on our side as well, and I'll meet the captain Isabeth spoke of.
We keep the peace here in Redfur, making it safe for traders on their way to and from <<1>>. We spend most of our time catching thieves.

Honestly? Thieves are good for business. They keep the market fluid and stop too much wealth from accumulating in one place.\n\nUntil recently, <<1>> would rather deal with thieves than with Thalmor bureaucrats.
Return what they stole and put them in the stocks to think about what they've done. We don't hold them for long, but they usually get the message—or become better thieves.

The Blades of Mephala, eh? Such a vivid image. He must be very strong, to run so fast, with all those satchels weighing him down. There must be a month's supply of moon-sugar in each.\n\nDid you see where the thief went?
The Reachmen have been dealt with? This is tremendous news! \n\nThe Imperials then. They were attacking Southern Bangkorai before. They will not rest, but now, my undead army can drive them back.

Really? Maybe he's right—talking about an undead army. But if this is his army, why are they hostile?\n\nWe might have to earn their allegiance. Have you seen these blue flames in the ruins? I think they're somehow inciting the undead to violence.

I do. I tried holy water on one and it seemed to do the trick. If you'll take it and extinguish a few more flames, that may help pacify the undead. \n\nAfter that, let's meet at the monument south by the rocks. I saw someone skulking around over there.
Well, I guess there's nothing Jode's Chariot can do about it now. That moon-sugar will be all over town by nightfall. <<1>> will not be happy.\n\nThank you anyway.
Of course not. There was no other thief. \n\nNot that it matters. Our sticky-fingered friend here has already stashed the moon-sugar he stole. I don't suppose you saw where?

Oh, Gods. How was I so blind? My revenge only brought more pain into the world. I guess death is a poor substitute for justice, after all.\n\nYou're right. I must end this diseased cycle. I must destroy the amulet.
Then my paws are tied. No evidence means no theft, even if <<1>> is three months worth of moon-sugar poorer.\n\nIn any case, thank you. Jode's Chariot appreciates your honesty.
What? I thought <<1>> was mad. A Daedric Prince, in <<2>>?\n\nIs he in the cathedral? We should clear the town!

It is a twisted reproduction of the Great Cathedral in Tamriel, which was built to honor the Divines. \n\nThat travesty was made to honor Molag Bal. Housed within its walls are tortured souls driven feral. And the Mad Architect himself.
Probably best I keep that from the report. My superiors will see no further than "abetted a Daedric Prince." I'd rather not diminish your significant accomplishments.
I would've preferred a public execution, after what he did to this town. I hope he finds a slow death in the Shivering Isles.
You … well, thank the Eight Divines!\n\nWhere is this <<1>> all the crazed citizens mentioned? I'd like a word with him.
Then, and only then, can you take the fight to Molag Bal himself—to restore protection to Nirn and reclaim your soul.
We'll escort them to <<1>>. Hopefully the Mages Guild can look into their madness.\n\nAs for <<2>>, we'll remain here to help rebuild. After this, what else can we do?

Not too much. Just the usual bickering between Tamrith and Dorell. It's starting to wear on my nerves, truth be told.\n\nI needed a little quiet time. You can probably find the Countess and the Baron up ahead, arguing about something or another.
Were we? Where are Darien and Gabrielle? I thought they were coming right behind us!\n\nDamn it! I would not have them sacrifice themselves … not for me, at least! Surely they're still coming …?

In his youth, I took him as an apprentice. He was lazy, a bit reckless, and nearly set my laboratory afire on three occasions.\n\nHis childhood was quite difficult. But that's no excuse for his actions.
I'll return to <<1>> until <<2>> sorts out the reconstruction.\n\nYou're welcome to visit, anytime you wish.

Long ago his bloodline ruled <<1>>. He was a child who thought the town would one day be his. But his parents died in a fire when he was young, and he lost everything.\n\nI thought by taking him as a pupil I could teach him humility. I was wrong.
Steal? I guess that's one way of looking at it. Let's say I circumvented the market—I found the price the merchant was charging unacceptable, so I set my own.

Some call them thieves, but that's such an impolite term. The Hollow Moon's work is charitable by nature.\n\nThey procure things for people who can't afford them, yes? Here, take this token to the ruined temple, and see for yourself.

What does the merchant have to complain about? His belly is full.\n\nIf they are not fed, <<1>> and her sisters become most unruly … aheh. Were it not for the Hollow Moon, they would have eaten me whole when I arrived in Redfur!
This is the Mad Architect's project graveyard. The works he considers failed are collected here. There's room for a couple more, if you ask me.\n\nHis chambers lay at the bottom of this chasm.
It's the only way out of here.

I know Duraeg's plan. He has stores of seeds he plans on using to turn the innocent into pawns for his army.\n\nYou must destroy the stores. With Duraeg out of the way and his weapon destroyed, it will leave this army without a leader and a plan.

I'm badly injured. Whatever Duraeg was doing to me, probably trying to implant one of those seeds like the others, it's left me too weak. You need to go. Finish the mission without me.\n\nBesides. If he was successful, I may compromise everything.
Wonderful! Please, set it on the table. I want to take a good look at the thing before I pack it up and take it back to the Mages Guild.
My hirelings? Oh, yes. Of course. I'm glad you found them. Now, please, put the cup right there, if you would.
A Goblin, eh? That explains what happened to the Nords.\n\nAnd, I suppose, that's why they call this relic the Emerald Chalice. Goblins are greenish, you see. Well, now we know.
Amazing powers? How positively excellent! I shall have to test this at once!
Oh really? And what, pray tell, is this secret?
Oh my goodness! How terrible for them. Positively ghastly!\n\nWell, nothing to be done about it now. The chalice, if you please?

I'm surprised he had one left to hand out!\n\nApologies, I should explain …. Our agents give these to the infirm so their need is not questioned when they petition us for aid. <<1>> was very … liberal with his tokens.

I don't know. If the dead here are rising and this is the royal crypt, have any of my ancestors risen? Maybe they can give us some answers.\n\nWould you consider venturing into the royal crypt to find out?
Can you lift coin from a rich man's pocket without getting your hand stuck in it?\n\nThen talk to <<1>>, upstairs. He might have something for you.
Ah. Silver-Paws takes care of us. He would have been so proud of Deepswimmer—we made all the poultices he asked for …!\n\nBut now so many of us died … Silver-Paws will be sad.
