Yes! They are needed, aren't they? Silver-Paws knew they would be.\n\nThe trolls weren't the only threat Deepswimmer found here though. He saw Imperials coming in on boats! This one thinks they will soon raid the crossing again!

Well, the good news is the undead didn't attack us … they actually bowed to Prince Adrien!\n\nFather Quiston's not exactly impressed with that fact though. He thinks it's a very bad sign, and he told the prince as much.

We thought his senche-tigers would be useful to have around. Guard duty and such.\n\nBut between his tigers' sugar habit and his handing out Hollow Moon tokens like candy, he practically emptied out our stores!

Hmm. Well, we tested that out, and dripped some holy water on Prince Adrien's hand. It burned. That pretty much says it all.\n\nBut Father Quiston believes there's still a chance we can remove the corruption.

Hmm. Maybe you are less interested when you hear what we do?\n\nYou are familiar with the custom of property ownership, yes? I have a thing, it is mine! You take it, it is still mine, yes? Why? Because I did not give it to you.

And if you are starving and use what you took to feed your belly? Is it still mine?\n\nNo. Whatever you stole—food, money to buy food, silks to trade for food—it is inconsequential next to saving you from death!

Shornhelm's stability affects all of Rivenspire. If Montclair and his allies take over the city, I fear all of Rivenspire would soon fall.\n\nAnd then they would look beyond our borders. He's always fancied himself the true heir to Ranser's throne.
I usually leave politics to the other nobles. I prefer to deal quietly with … more unusual problems.\n\nAs for the why of things, call it an obligation. But now is not the time to discuss the past.

You think we should work for our bread, yes? But many can't work. They're injured, sick, or just too hungry. The Hollow Moon gives them what they need.\n\nPerhaps we're wrong to steal, but if the world were a more virtuous place we wouldn't need to.
These witches want to kill my daughter. They show up to help, but as soon as Isabeth returns, they pounce on her.\n\nThey say she's infected. It's absurd.

Many of them appreciate what we do. Sometimes a merchant falls on hard times. His stock is poor or the price of sugar is too high. Then he needs us, too, yes?\n\nBut what about you? Are you still interested in helping the Hollow Moon?
Please talk some sense into them. Surely, there's a cure.

He should look at the bigger picture. You saw yourself what happened. It's only a matter of time before his daughter becomes a Reachman puppet. Whether they wait, or kill her now. Her life is over. But if they wait, so is this alliance.
Truly. The Reachmen gain their strength in magicka from Hircine as do we. If anyone could reverse the effects of the seed they planted inside her, it would be us.\n\nThere is no hope for a cure.

Probably. But they're animals. I don't see any other way to reason with them.\n\nStenwick needs the bud, and we don't have time to coddle the spriggans. We need their cooperation, whether they intend to give it or not.

No, and that's what worries me. He must be tracked down and dealt with. Swiftly. \n\nThanks to your efforts, though, Montclair's plan to take control of Shornhelm has been stopped. You should inform High King Emeric and the other nobles.
Not as slow as they look, eh?\n\nHere. Watch for patrols and choose your moment carefully. Jode's Chariot can't be everywhere at once.

According to my sources, he was close before I entered the Mews. I have no doubt that the Shornhelm Guard has reclaimed the upper city.\n\nI assume Dorell, Tamrith, and the High King are even now in Shornhelm Castle. Give Emeric my regards.

Eh, a proper hero needs obstacle. Struggle. Repeated attempts at bodily harm! You're going to play the proper hero so Aulie can shine! Or our deal is off. And if it's off, so is <<1>>'s head. To Skyrim! In a field! With berries growing from her eyes!

Damn! Montclair's Argonian is as crazy as an outhouse skeever!\n\nHis soldiers kidnapped a few nobles, grabbed them in broad daylight. Probably hopes to use them as insurance against us. But he must realize that I never negotiate with terrorists.

So many hungry bellies, so many outstretched hands. You won't need to look far.\n\nOf course, some are more needy than others. Sadly, there are always those who are more than ready to take from those who truly need it.

Then we have to act fast. Go to the Mews and free <<1>>, <<2>>, and <<3>>. If you can take out Reezal-Jul along the way, all the better.\n\nIn the meantime, we'll mobilize the Shornhelm Guard and retake the upper city.

Listen to their stories. Look them in the eye. If they are truly needy, it will be evident in their clothes, in how they speak, in where they live.\n\nThey'll appreciate it, too. A listening ear may not fill the belly, but it fills a need all the same.
A squirrel foot. The thing at the end of a squirrel's leg. Seen one?
Bah. I lost my lucky squirrel foot during the battle. I've carried it into every scuffle I've ever gotten into.

Sure, but I'm to be deployed to Cyrodiil soon. I don't even want to think about what'll happen to me without it. I hear those Bosmer eat people! \n\nAnd Argonians make Bretons' bones into flutes or something. It's a nightmare!
Oh!  Uhm … right! Yes, of course I do. I'll get right back to it. \n\nReal soon.

Yeah. Yeah, maybe you're right. I've been using that foot as a crutch for too long. Thanks.\n\n… But seriously, if you do see a loose squirrel foot, let me know. I'd like to, you know, bury it or something.
You're telling me. If you see a squirrel with, I don't know, a particularly large hoard of nuts or something, just let me know.
Well, yeah, sure. But there's no guarantee it'll be a lucky one. \n\nI mean, if I'm able to catch it and chop its foot off, it's not really all that lucky, is it?

Well, I originally called this place the Fell Inn, but nobody seemed to care for that name. I thought it was appropriate, but it didn't really appeal to the Bretons or the Orcs.\n\nThey don't really like the Run Inn, either, but what do I care?

Adusa will take the survivors to Hoarfrost Downs. They should be safe enough there.\n\nPardon, but this one is still coming to grips with how fast the bloodfiends were created. And with the constable's betrayal.
Yes. Word of what happened here must be carried to my master, Count Verandis.\n\nThere is much work to be done and very little time if Lleraya has truly ventured this far south.

Althene will help you prepare it. For the Sentinel's ritual, he needs a spriggan bud, freely given. You have obtained that, but the bud will not bloom without nurturing.\n\nI hope you aren't squeamish about blood.

I don't know if you're crazy or brave, but the city will reward you for handling this. If you can. He's got a small army down here.\n\nI'd bring him to trial, but after that ambush, I'd settle for a dead Garron—and his plot stopped. Whatever it is.

Yes, one of the women of the woods. I was taught never to trust them, but Isa thought they could help us retake Northglen, and keep the Reachmen out of Evermore.\n\nShe might still be with them on the shore. There's an entry to the ruins there.
Don't let her cast a spell over you. She's clouded everyone's judgment in this town. If you talk to her, she'll convince you to kill Draven.\n\nDon't let her kill my husband.

No! Don't let her! I don't want this anymore. I've seen what she does to the people in this village. She takes their minds. Puts them under her control!\n\nBeing a werewolf is a curse, but I can't give up who I am!

If you have sweets, please! My little ja'khajiit, they mewl with the hunger. "Bring us sweets, father!" they say to <<1>>.\n\nCould you spare any? Or money to buy them, perhaps? This one is not picky.

Oh, well. Hrrm. Where to start, aheh. Why do they always ask ….\n\nAdduna! So small and covered in spots. I am not even sure she is mine, to be honest! What can you do, yes? And little Rihah, always getting into trouble! So hungry! Take pity.
Thank you, noble one! With this bounty, I will trade for so many sweets! This one cannot even begin to tell you!

It's neutral territory—a remote valley in central Bangkorai. Gabrielle and Darien have already scouted it out. They can tell you what they saw.\n\nWhen you're ready, Gabrielle is planning to open a portal to get us down there.

I think they expected to take Evermore through deception. We've prevented that. I'm sure they'd like to take the city by force, but as long as Bangkorai Garrison is standing that won't be happening.\n\nThey may be ready to cut their losses.

Under the terms of the parley, I agreed not to bring the royal guard. Septima's crazy if she thinks I'll meet her without an escort though.\n\nShe's bringing her magic, so I'm bringing mine. I'll have some steel on hand too … for good measure.

Inequality. Corruption. Injustice … unfair distribution of resources. The list is as long as our memory, friend.\n\nIf you care about the poor people of Shornhelm, I suggest you show up and be known as an ally.
Only if I can be the Chieftain with a hearth-husband … forge-husband … but no!\n\nThis is not the way that our people live, is it? So I say, to Mauloch's hoary nethers with all strongholds!

Not that you would understand firsthand, but if I can't be the Chieftain with a hearth-husband … forge-husband … then no!\n\nSo I say, to Mauloch's hoary nethers with all strongholds! I am not a sign of status for any man.
Are you mocking me? Ask <<1>> how they caught us!\n\nBesides, I can't change my passion for adventure. Would you give up a life of danger to be a swineherd?
So you say! You better not deny that you're a thrillseeker at the very least.\n\nIt's carved in your every bone! You are like me, you thirst for the glory of combat!
Then I say it is they who are fools in the end!\n\nI may look a fool today, but I will feel the warm spray of Imperial blood across my lips, and it will cleanse this weakness!
Then let's stop all this toothless prattle!\n\nLet us feel the warm spray of Imperial blood across our faces! Let us feast upon the cries of our enemies!
Don't tell me you've never borrowed anything without permission.\n\nI've always been free-spirited, otherwise I'd be in a stronghold somewhere living like some toothless villager!
No, really? I wouldn't mind giving you a swat or two, too.\n\nEspecially if you're going to try to talk my ears off.
Excellent. Looks like it's coded. Let's see ….\n\nEmpyrean Light take them. These fiends aren't a random band of Colovian slavers. They're Imperial military. We've got to do something about this.
What? That's preposterous!\n\nWhen did this happen?
It's just a conversation, friend. No violence, just words.\n\nIt's a quiet conversation though. Bring your friends, but do not advertise it. The ears of the oppressors hear all.
According to this, not only is an Imperial captain here, but so is an envoy from the Worm Cult!\n\nI can't let such essential targets just walk away. Whoever finds them first gets to take them out.

Yes, of course! They are little, and covered in fur.\n\nOh, so, I don't have a family. Can you blame me? How else am I to tug on your heartstrings? You don't know how hard it is for an able-bodied bachelor!
We must find him. The ritual might still work if we catch him in time to complete the binding.\n\nIf not, then we must save the town, above all else.

I've captured a few keeps in my day, and I learned the hard way: whoever holds the courtyard, holds the keep. So I'm going to seal our grip on this space.\n\nWe should also hit the barracks though—before the Imperials get their greaves on.
Money for Sula. Sula say, "Go to trade post. Buy herbs. Spices. Come right back."
Thank you. I share with Sula. She will be very happy!
Friend. When I come here, I am alone. Sula finds me. Gives me food.
Big storm. Ship lost under many waves. Swim for many days. Wake up? Sula is there. Cares for me. Now I care for her.

Yes, but I'm not saying to slaughter a bunch of half-dressed soldiers. We're not Reachmen, for Mara's sake. \n\nNo. I'm hoping some of our knights are imprisoned there and you can free them. We need all the swords we can get.

Then there will be no Viridian Sentinel. The yoke about our necks for centuries would be freed.\n\nOf course, there is one way to ensure the princess does not become the Sentinel. Destroy the spriggan bud I gave you, and she will fail.
The torches on either side would suffice. Their flames and your intention are more than enough.\n\nYou are the one with the power to change this, mortal.

It is true. But we have endured a slow death for much longer. Man was not meant to rule over nature. No matter their intentions, they cannot know the will of the woods.\n\nThe Viridian Sentinel is a mockery of nature's true cycle.
Good. Release me so I can give <<1>> the thanks he so richly deserves.
I don't know what you mean by that, but you've got a captive audience.
Whatever you got, I'll take it off your hands! Spices? Furs? Some of those healing plants? Gold, maybe? Split-Ear says he got gold once. Do you have some? If you don't, that's fine. I'm not picky!
Hey thanks! Wait'll I tell Split-Ear! He's never going to believe this!
Isn't that what you do here? Hollow Moon helps people! Gives them stuff! I'm just here for mine!
Hey, I'm making my way same as anyone! Living's hard! You going to give me something or not?
Everything I've been through? For this? And my own father won't even acknowledge me as his daughter. \n\nBut it's worth it right? My life for an alliance that will save Evermore.
Oh, I see! You think just because I'm not starving I don't need anything!\n\nIt's a hard world, even with a full stomach.

I'll let Delphique know I'm ready. I'm sure she won't hesitate, and my father won't stop her. \n\nEvermore has always taken priority for him. Evermore and duty. Maybe I follow in his footsteps after all.

Not much to say, really. Used to be a jaqspur, back before the Camoran war.\n\nLost the use of my legs at Cormount. Fighters Guild trades me drinks for war stories. I keep telling them I need food, not drink, but they're not the brightest lot.
Much obliged. This is far better than anything the Fighters Guild hands out. It's even fresh!
Don't take it the wrong way, but unless you have something for me to eat, I'm not up for talking.\n\nMy stories are the only thing I have for a trade. I can't just give them away to anyone who asks.

An artifact sacred to my Order. A holy relic from the era of the Mane Tullar-dra. Today it signifies the martial vows we take when we join the order, the pious nature of our contemplation. A symbol of the Bright Moons.

My misdeeds were not only connected with the Bitterhand. They were also entwined with another.\n\nThere is a Breton woman who was a partner of sorts. She sold the items I … acquired. She will not be happy if I try to end our arrangement.

Sai locked the amulet away in the ruins of Sancre Tor and entrusted the key to one of his close associates.\n\nBut he can tell you himself. Speak with him. He's eager to meet his liberator. I'll contact you when we're ready to move forward.

Stranger still. My people say that bravery and honor are the hallmarks of a great soul, yet you have both of those things in great measure. \n\nI had begun to think that honor was a relic of the past. You give me hope.
What? Who told you to find me?

Shh! Or do you revel in the defilement of sacred law? \n\nThese burial grounds are cursed, and I am pleading with Arkay to reveal the source of the corruption. Unless you know the source, please, let me be.

Cadwell is the oldest of the Soul Shriven.\n\nAfter years of torment, Soul Shriven usually go insane and turn feral, but not Cadwell. He was already insane before he left Tamriel. Mad as a box of frogs, but completely harmless. You'll see.
It did? That would be quite a surprise, considering Arkay is opposed to undeath in all its forms! \n\nDo you think the god simply changed his mind? Why would he possibly do that?

No. Your impatient friend here can escort me to the prince. I need your help with the spirits defiling the monuments.\n\nDestroy the defilers and then I will have the clarity I need. After that, meet me at the church and we can discuss the prince.

I've seen some ups and some downs. You know how it is. Life hasn't been a slog through a poisonous swamp, nor has it been an endless night in a complimentary bordello.\n\nMain thing is that I'm still on this side of the dirt.
I cannot say. Physically, I am unharmed. But mentally …?\n\nI feel a darkness in my heart. A weight on my soul. I do not know how long this emptiness will remain.
I hid the Amulet in a sacred catacomb, protected by magical wards. The means of lifting these wards are in the keeping of my old mentor, Kasura. \n\nAs soon as I am able, we must meet with her.

I will try to rest, but I am a warrior. We cannot sit still for very long. \n\nAnd I should certainly bathe before we meet with Kasura. I am unpleasantly fragrant, and if she happened to be downwind of me, I would never hear the end of it.
Sir Cadwell, yes indeed. A pleasure!\n\nAnd fair Lyris! Good to see you, m'dear! How are you, then?

Oh dear, oh dear. Well, that is inconvenient, isn't it?\n\nTell you what—I happen to know another way in! Much more of a scenic route. Rather a fun little jaunt, actually. Full of traps, and corpses, and nasty beasties filling up the bits in between.
Rather cautiously, I expect. \n\nWatch your step, hold your nose, and do mind the traps. There'll like as not be a fair dose of running and skull-bashing as well.

Follow the river. You'll find the door to the Undercroft at the water's end. Once you're inside, stick to the light and you'll find a ladder that will take you right up to the Prophet, straightaway. \n\nDo give him my best!

Ah, the war. Stupid waste of life, that. Bosmer against Bosmer. I worked as a sellsword. Figured I could at least come out a little richer.\n\nI was a long range scout with a group that went to reinforce Gelthior at Cormount.

The High Elves rained fire on our forces. It was like Oblivion opened its maw and swallowed us all in Daedric flame.\n\nThat's how I lost the use of my legs. Healers thought they'd have to cut them off completely. Lucky it didn't come to that.

Nah. It was the High Elves that found me, buried under a pile of hot rock. If they hadn't dug me out and applied their salve, I probably wouldn't be alive.\n\nYou can't blame them for doing what they had to, to win the war.

We thought he had a better claim to the throne than Aeradan in Cormount. Maybe he did, maybe he didn't.\n\nThe High Elves settled the matter. Once Summerset intervened, the Blacksap didn't stand a chance.
If you want to know more, ask Elgenie. She's our resident mage. Used to be with the Mages Guild till Evermore came under attack. Now she does her best to support us in the field.
Haven't eaten in … don't know how long. So sick. So hungry.
What's this? Oh, thank you. You are too generous.
Two things: they outnumber us, and they've added a new type of soldier to their ranks.\n\nWe've heard rumors of such soldiers from as far away as Glenumbra. They're powerful in numbers. Be careful.
Skooma. For three years he was a slave to it. I convinced him to quit and now, look. His shakes worsen. I fear he won't make it through the night.
Thank you. S'rendarr willing, the alchemist will take this in trade.\n\nYou have no idea how much this means to me. Thank you.

I've heard of a remedy for skooma sickness, but it requires skill to prepare. I'm no alchemist, and I can't afford the mixture.\n\nSo I sit by his side and stroke his fur and purr reassuringly into his ear, praying he makes it through the night.
I told you, I convinced him to quit. I stayed up with him when Sheggorath brought terrors in the night.\n\nI would not allow it. You have my word.

Sane as a babbling brook. What is it babbling about? I have no idea!\n\nI have been up these past three nights, having a conversation with my stomach. You know what it says? Nothing! My stomach can't talk!
Food for me? I'm grateful. But tell me, what's the one thing a man can never escape? An empty stomach. It just keeps chasing him down.

I sent it away. When the bandits came, did it lift a finger? No. And when the fields burned? It burned, too. Useless. So I said, "Begone, you layabout! I will find a new arm, one with industry, and it will work for its supper!"
All to the ground. But it's okay. They paid for their damages by taking my wife off my hands. One less mouth to feed.

Puddles loves new places. She enjoys a good prowl and likes to nip at toes and fingers to establish her position with the locals.\n\nBut for all her bluster, no matter how hard her outer shell appears, my little Puddles is a runny yolk on the inside.
If you want to help, you'll put me out of my misery.
Ugh, what's this? A kindness to prolong my agony? Save it for someone else. I'd rather starve.
Nagoth gro-Jathsogur struck a deal with that dog, <<1>>, behind my back! Challenged me for leadership! Me! <<2>> Ash-Blood!

He lost! I had him beaten! Then he came at me like a she-wolf, slashing and tearing, his eyes—flame! His arms covered in hair.\n\nHonorless milksot beat me within an inch of my life. Took my eye. He should have finished me off.
I have never been more sure of anything in my life, Verandis.\n\nI will sacrifice everything, risk anything, to save the woman I love. A shame the same can't be said of all of us.

Sorry won't help us here. We have to find the Ayleid relic. That's all that matters now.\n\nJust remember, we're out of options. This is our last chance to save Leila and I won't let you ruin it, vampire!

Your fear colors your perception, Verandis. It is merely the pulse of ancient magicka, the heartbeat of a powerful relic.\n\nOur intentions are pure. We seek only to save my beloved's life. These creatures have no reason to stop us.

Has your courage deserted you, vampire? You discovered the relic's resting place, and I thank you for that. But right now we have to reach the relic chamber and save my wife.\n\nAfter that, you can do what you want. Now let's go.

An honorless swine, even for a Wood Elf. Trying to start a war up in <<1>>. He wanted the Drublog to fight with him, but I refused. Nagoth must have gone to him, after. He's going to get my entire clan killed.

I … will use this to buy back my weapons and armor. I will grow strong again, and when I return to <<1>> it will be with an army at my back!\n\nThank you. When I am victorious, I will send for you. <<2>> Ash-Blood never forgets his allies!
You're right. I've been a fool. Wasting away like a motherless calf, waiting to die. I should be doing everything I can to strike that coward down!

Earn back my … yes. Yes, I can see what I have lost. \n\nI will begin the long trek back to <<1>>. I am sure there are others who would see Nagoth dead for his cowardice! Thank you for showing me how wrong I've been.
The wyrd are not a curiosity to be examined. State your question, and I will answer it. Whether you understand what you ask and how I answer are other matters entirely.
Very well, ask away. But you will release me from this prison. The Architect is not dead and knows no mercy, I fear my torment will be far worse.

I'm a healer, and a hunter. As a healer, I mend the wounded. As a hunter, I take another life.\n\nEveryone has multiple purposes, both hidden and revealed. We are simpler than most, as our duality is readily visible to anyone who chooses to see.

My sisters and I believe in balance. For each life taken, a new one is given, in one form or another. We do not waste what we acquire, and we ask before taking.\n\nAnd for this simplicity, we are reviled. The woods are simple, as are we.
No. Why do you ask?
Hah, yes. The Bitterhand has been skulking about the farmlands for some time now. I knew they'd hit the farm sooner or later. Just figured on it being later, you know?

That's what Lothson keeps telling me. Keeps telling me to hold on. We'll find hope soon. \n\nMy mother didn't raise me to be some simpering Daggerfall flower. I've been working a farm since I could hold a shovel. I'll live.
I welcome questions from the honestly curious, unlike some of my sisters. We are rarely visited by people with genuine interest in our lives.

The woods offer us shelter, food, and water. You see everything we have laid out before you. What we need, we have.\n\nLiving in a village places so many burdens on its people. Conform, obey, suppress. Our lives aren't like that.

My birth family made it clear I was unwelcome. Tainted, they called me. Stupid. My daughter and I were abandoned in the woods.\n\nThis is my family now. The wyrd welcomed us with open arms, and taught us how to survive. We are home now.

I'm a trainer, and a learner. I train with our wolves, but I've learned from them too.\n\nThere's so much more to life than buying and selling. I was a part of all that hustle once, but now I'm free. I live my own life. It's a blessing!

My great-grandmother's great-grandmother had it made. To celebrate her joining some forgotten king's court, my mother told me. I just know it's been worn by every woman in my family for generations. I'd hate to lose it forever.
She's around somewhere. I don't need to watch her every minute. I know she can take care of herself, in whatever way she chooses.
Thank you for even considering this. Look for us in Shornhelm if you find it.\n\nThe necklace … it's been in her family for hundreds of years. I think that necklace meant more to her than the farm.
Excellent, when you arrive I'll introduce you to the rest of my team.
We did what we had to. His works ruined me and I had to take him down. Listen, I know it was wrong but I did what I thought I had to. I'm sorry now. I'm sorry that it drove him to this.
Saryne was a noble and friend of mine. When the Architect's works failed, Saryne made sure he could not work again and also exacted financial recompense from him. Saryne is a loyal friend.

She got close to the Mad Architect and allowed us to steal his plans. Once we had those, we could find the weaknesses in his designs. I think she may have actually loved him at the end but by then it was too late.

Montclair easily defeated me at the Doomcrag. We can't afford to ignore anything that might give us an advantage.\n\nI don't know what we're going to find down here, but the Ayleids seemed to think this place was important.
Of course, of course! Aheh.\n\nNow, I was hoping you could assist me with a rather … delicate matter that has presented itself.

I probably should have mentioned this before, but it never seemed like the right time. \n\nThere's a trick to opening the cell. The only way for a prisoner to leave is for another living soul to take their place. I need to swap places with the Prophet.
I've tried to be honest with you. We did bad things but bad enough to be tortured here forever?
I'm sorry… if I could take it back I would… please, don't do this.
Thank you! I knew our past deeds could be redeemed.

There are magical locking devices on either side of the cage. You need to deactivate both of them so I can begin the transfer.\n\nOnce it's done, get moving. The Prophet will know where to go, but he'll need your eyes, and your protection.

We can't possibly understand it right now, but the Prophet chose you for a reason. You're important, and everyone and everything we've ever loved is in danger.\n\nGet the Prophet to safety. I'll find my own way back, if I can.

Believe me, I wish there was. But … I don't see anyone else here with a beating heart, do you? If Molag Bal isn't stopped he'll destroy everyone and everything we've ever loved.\n\nThe Prophet chose you for a reason. Get him to safety. I'll be fine.

Shan-ra, leader of the merchants here, has threatened to call in the Thalmor. This is a problem.\n\nJode's Chariot understands that we provide a valuable service. The Thalmor is unlikely to agree. We need to change Shan-ra's mind.

The priest is blinded by his preconceptions of power. This is a blessing for all of Bangkorai. What matter is it whether it comes from Arkay or some other source?\n\nThe prince can sense the truth. He will give himself over to it soon enough.

You regard power and opportunity as corruption? Such has always been the perspective of small minds. I thought you understood, but it is clearly beyond your comprehension. \n\nVery well. You've chosen your destiny.

Gods! I probably shouldn't jest like that, not around Arzhela. Poor thing. There's no telling what these twisted Imperial bastards might have done with King Eamond's corpse.\n\nHe was about to be entombed here when the garrison fell, of course.

He's living the good life as a merchant in Eastmarch. We used to be quite a pair. Fought back-to-back across the face of Tamriel. \n\nBut then I met Marien and settled down. Addald went soft and became a fishmonger.

Bitterhand bandits. Bitter bastards, more like it! Trouble for everyone these days.\n\nIf my brother Addald were here, we could have fought them off. But I couldn't take them on by myself, not with Marien to protect.

The prince went into a rage. He started shouting at Father Quiston, saying this was his church, and he was relieving Quiston of his duties. Then he just … ran inside. \n\nWe have to get in there and talk him down.
The doors won't open. I don't know if he barred them or what.\n\nMaybe the priest knows another way in?

The royal crypt. All of Bangkorai's rulers are buried there—to keep eternal vigil and such.\n\nThe Imperials are doing something horrific in there; it's where they've formed their last line of defense. Whatever they're doing, I need you to stop them.
No. This is the only door, and the beast has locked it from the inside.\n\nThere's a spare key buried under the tree in the back. You have Arkay's blessing to go and claim it! Just do it fast!
Closer than you might think. You want to meet them?
Luckily, structural damage was fairly minimal. The lion's share of the work has been gathering bodies, tending the wounded, and so forth. Grim work to be sure, but necessary.
The only Imperials outside are being piled into mass graves.

He suffered enough in life. In death, I am giving him the glory he deserves. \n\nI told him, by giving in to my guidance, together we could purge this land of all of our enemies. He was willing to make this sacrifice. You should honor his decision.
I may not be a god, but with the strength of the prince's soul, my powers are considerable.\n\nCome. See for yourself!
Aye. We've put the able-bodied to work clearing debris. The rest are held in the central keep, awaiting orders from headquarters.
Not my decision. But if I had my way, we'd need a few more shovels and a great deal more rope.
Of course you do. I suppose now is as good a time as any for you to ask them.
I can't be sure, but Adusa and Gwendis noticed some unusual activity near Northpoint. I believe that is where we will resume the hunt once we are finished here.
He's dead? My mother must be sick with worry. I don't feel up to travel yet, but I can have Stenwick send word I'm all right.\n\nI hear company coming up the walk.
I … well … I was traveling with a party escorting our dead knights to their final resting place. We got within sight of the cemetery when we were set upon by skeletons. \n\nWalking skeletons!
I don't know. We fought off what we could and fell back to the Garrison. \n\nI'm not going in that direction again, that's for sure.
Yes! Shambling about gripping swords in their bony fingers. \n\nAnd the sound they made. A sort of … creaking. Ugh, I can't get it out of my head.
This is all about the Remnant of Light. Before it became corrupted.\n\nIt mentions that the Remnant requires a vessel to make full use of its limitless potential. A container for its abundant power.

That seems likely. Between the relic's magic and the vampiric abilities I inadvertently provided, Montclair has become more powerful than I expected.\n\nThe book also says that if we break the vessel, we break the relic. I will need to think upon that.
That is the name I have given you. You are but a trace of your former self. A soulless one. An empty vessel that longs to be filled. \n\nIt is as the Scrolls foretold, but not exactly as I imagined.
There lies the trouble, yes?\n\nThe only known entrance to the tomb is within Jode's Hall. The place is teeming with guards. We will need their cooperation to gain entry to the tomb.

This place was not always a trading post—it was built upon a tomb whose gauntlet of traps have kept it sealed for generations.\n\nIf the stories are true, it holds untold riches. We can use them to persuade <<1>> to leave us be.

The Guild is always seeking keen eyes and sharp fangs, walker. A recently captured keep is a good place to find these things, yes?\n\nI am here seeking recruits. We need all the help we can get if we are to destroy these Daedric Anchors.

Bah, you're tugging on my vines, yeah? …Oh, you're serious. Right. \n\nThe Mages Guild is a club for geniuses like myself. Very select. We spend our time seeking books, tomes, and the like in search of knowledge. Preferably dangerous and forbidden.

Well, not yet—but it's great that you brought it to me. You're already well on your way to earning membership in the Mages Guild. \n\nDid you know the guild rewards people for books like this? Probably not. We don't really advertise.

Mannimarco's agents weave a web of lies and deceit. They pit the races of Tamriel against one another and divert their attention from the real threat.\n\nSeek out these agents wherever they can be found and expose their lies.

Death. Death and destruction. It would've given me vengeance against my enemies, but it wouldn't have stopped there. It will never stop unless we stop it.\n\nEven now, I can sense the darkness inside, gaining strength again. Please. Kill me.

Yes. The life force inside me is evil through and through. \n\nThank you for saving me, friend. I wish I could have known you when I was alive. But this will have to suffice. I'm ready to die. Ready as I can be, I suppose.
Really? I didn't want to say anything, but you do look a little under the weather. Just let me get a good look.

This is good! Welcome to the guild, Associate.

Now we hunt. Track and slay as many dungy Daedra as you can find. If you break some of the anchors there will be a spotless reward and maybe even some special assignments waiting for you.

Farewell.

Yes, as this one said, that is why he is here. We have much to do. Many demons to slay. \n\nI have not found many with five claws here, but you seem strong and sleek enough. Would you be interested in joining the Fighters Guild?

Yes, walker. Rathul-do is thinking you must have seen them by now. Massive chains that fall from the sky. Thunder, tornadoes of light, demons howling … this is ringing chimes, yes?\n\nFrom what I'm told, they're coming straight out of Oblivion.

Great! I'd typically administer an exam to gauge your aptitude, but you seem … y'know … apt. \n\nI hereby grant you the rank of Student in the Mages Guild. Now, go find some books! Each one you turn in will increase your reputation. Good luck!

Well, you'd start off as a Docent. Docents are our agents abroad. You'd find books for us so we can expand our already vast and impressive libraries.\n\nIn exchange, you can purchase exclusive items. You might also be offered special tasks ….
Really? Then you must be the newcomer everyone's talking about. Impressive work. Tell me—were you telling the truth about <<1>> or were you just covering for one of your fellows?

Great! I'd typically administer an exam to gauge your aptitude, but you seem, well, apt. \n\nI hereby grant you the rank of Student in the Mages Guild. Every book acquired, or collection of books completed, will earn you status in the guild. Good luck!

Docents earn standing in the Guild by bringing rare books and scrolls like this to our already vast and impressive libraries. As their reputation grows, so do the rewards. And everyone likes shinies, right?\n\nInterested in joining the Mages Guild?
Truly? I wonder if I can take your word for that. An honest thief seems a contradiction of terms. No matter.\n\nTell me, why have you come?
I thought as much—though I am surprised you would admit it. An honest thief. Hmm.\n\nAnyway, tell me. Why have you come?
I did everything in my power to protect him. If I could've taken the death-blow on the battlefield, I would've done it without hesitation.\n\nHe should've been king.

Well, of course the war is far from over, but we've won a crucial battle. Definitely gave the Imperials a black eye. \n\nAnd Evermore is safe. I should return there, but I have a feeling Emeric will want to press on to liberate Southern Bangkorai.

Everyone was in their places. The plan was working perfectly. This doesn't bode well.\n\nI'll go west and see if I can find <<1>>. You go to the east gate and look for <<2>>. But keep your guard up. There's no end to vampire tricks.
And you freed Lady <<1>>! She's quite agreeable, and could prove to be a living repository of knowledge regarding the Walking City.\n\nI hope <<2>> didn't give you any trouble.

I see. I don't know why she did all of this, but she was once a hero. I can't imagine her soldiers will take it well.\n\nBut as you see, such relics are dangerous. I can deliver it to the <<1>> Mages Guild where its powers can be contained.
There is no question. My time as an adherent to the Eight has prepared me for this. I'll deliver it to <<1>> without delay, and without incident.
No. No body either. That's no comfort. When dealing with vampires, the lack of a body usually only means one thing. I pray I'm wrong.
We need to keep looking for Zungarg, and if he's—oh, praise Stendarr! There he is! I never thought I'd be so happy to see that stupid Orc in all my days.
Oh, no. The ground shook, there was a blast of cold air from the tunnels … then everything went quiet. I knew it must be something bad.\n\nWhat happened? How did she die?

Just what my parents told me. I never met my great-grandmother.\n\nDame Marcelle was an honored knight in the service of House Dorell. I remember one story, set during the time of the Great Feud between the Tamriths and the Dorells.
I see.\n\nDon't spread that around, all right? If nobody else saw it, we'll give her a good story. She long since earned a hero's death.
A free agent. Not that it matters.
Not really.

The God of Schemes invaded my mind many times during my imprisonment. It was a torturous experience.\n\nBut by forcing his way into my mind, he inadvertently opened his own thoughts to me and thus created a chink in his own armor.

It would be a far greater danger for you to enter Coldharbour without this distraction. It is Molag Bal's realm and his power there is great. \n\nI will endeavor to distract him in this manner whenever you travel there.

We are connected, he and I. With concentration, I can see through his eyes. He feels my presence and it fills him with rage.\n\nWhen you enter the Foundry to recover Lyris, I can keep his attention focused on me. He will be blind to you, for a time.

I sent four total. Abir, Hatmi, Ulmad, and Bendais.\n\nAbir took the shore, while Hatmi searched the chapel. Ulmad went to the fields. Bendais, the eastern perimeter. Isabeth the Impatient went after the ones who hadn't returned, despite my orders.
The defenses in the ruin will allow you to destroy the circlet. But the mage with me says unlocking the circlet will trigger the collapse of this complex. Destroying it will most likely seal us in.
We are trapped, my friend. We hold the door against the Colovians, but that is all the good news Raz has. Beyond us, the ruin has collapsed. We cannot reach you and you cannot reach us.
And reveal secrets for hunters to exploit and turn us to dust? Not likely.

Raz and his men came down here knowing what had to be done. You and I have done the Queen's work in the past, yes? Raz must trust you to do what we cannot. You must unlock the shrine behind you and destroy the circlet.
We cannot risk it, my friend. The tales of the circlet make it a clear and present threat to the Queen and all of the Dominion. It must be destroyed … even though it may cost Raz his life.

You have to depress the triggers in the proper order. We found runes along this corridor saying it's a sequence of four triggers. Press the first to the left and then the last to the right. The other two … we could not find.
The defenses in the ruin will allow you to destroy the circlet. But the mage with me says unlocking the circlet will trigger the collapse of this complex. Destroying it will most likely seal us in.
We have more than enough Knights Medicus to tend our wounded, so I choose to help these soldiers.
The Prophet! He spoke to you? What did he say?
Ha! That sounds like the Prophet, all right.\n\nHe's a prisoner here, too. It was very dangerous for him to speak to you, even for a moment. He must think you can help me.

Among these Lion Guard and militia, perhaps not. But the Knights of St. Pelin swear an oath to aid all those in need. \n\nThese soldiers are gravely wounded. It would be monstrous to let them die solely due to their misguided allegiance.

"A letter from Princess Urenenya to Klathzgar also hints at the sad fate that befell her. It seems that when she fell ill, Klathzgar resolved to put her spirit inside one of his creations so they could continue to be together."

"To my horror, I believe he somehow placed her soul into a crystal powering one of his centurions, where likely it remains to this day. The machines are intimidating, but I must try to recover Urenenya's soul gem and return it to the Silaseli Ruins."
Very well. Ask your questions. And then I expect you to make your way to Northpoint with all due haste.

Magical constructs created by Molag Bal to guide his vision in Coldharbour. \n\nThe Sentinels are connected. If we destroy one, the others will be blinded. With any luck, that will buy us the time we need to free the Prophet.
Is this conversation really happening? Adusa thinks not.
I've no idea. Brute force? We'll find a way. We have to.\n\nBe ready for anything. I doubt Molag Bal left the Sentinels unguarded.
You misunderstand me. I do not wish my secrets known to everyone.
Fine, lead the way. I'll follow at my own pace. I don't want to walk into any ambushes.
"<<1>>" happened. He's always blamed others for his own shortcomings, but I never realized he'd been touched by <<2>>.\n\nThe only way the madness will end is with his death.

In the story, Dorell's son Lanciot was kidnapped on the road to Northpoint by a dozen of Tamrith's most ruthless warriors. Despite the odds, Dame Marcelle never hesitated. She swooped in with this very sword and rescued Lanciot.\n\nI love that story!

We fought the Worm Cultists to the center of Gil-Var-Delle, beneath the hollow tree.\n\nThe Dark Anchor loomed before us, swarming with Daedra, like so many others we'd seen before. But it wasn't long before we realized something was different.

Have you ever seen a goddess cry? It is a terrible thing to behold … so perfect a face, marred by so many tears.\n\nAlmalexia's tears for Gil-Var-Delle crystallized into a beautiful gem, filled with all her fury directed at the Harvester of Souls.
This one is hiding, is it not obvious?

Moonclimber was looking for something. A little forgotten thing. No one would miss it. Flat-pawed diamond-backs were pride-blind and slow-witted. This one could have taken it like sugar from a ja'khajiit.
But you and your clankety-clanking army attacked. Too many swords—too much angry shouting. Moonclimber is thinking if she is captured now, angry shaveskins will kill her.

Useful in the hissing Dwarf cave. There is one south of here. Hidden away. This one will show you where it is on your map. \n\nMoonclimber is very kind to give you this information, yes? You can thank her by leaving quietly. Step soft, walker.
A little Dwarven bauble. A spotless, shiny thing. \n\nYou have seen Dwarf metal, yes? Moonclimber thought it might be useful.
I do not presume to know. He ordered me to protect refugees on this island while he attempts to retake the city.\n\nThis one longs to fight by <<1>>'s side, but I must follow orders.

Ah, yes. The great <<1>>! I wanted to introduce my soldiers to a real Dominion hero.\n\nShame that she's gone. Pulled her fearsome Jade Dragoons out of town before we arrived, and left the place defenseless. Seems the pirates decided to fill the void.
<The crystal glows slightly, and a pearly essence swirls wildly within.>
There is no one else. Yes, if you touch the Tower rune … I live. If you place the circlet in the furnace … I die. You must decide.
Of course. To which daring adventure in the Summerset isles are you referring?
The day you fell from the sky, my friend? How could I forget? We had quite the time that day. Diplomats and pirates … and such a storm! Raz had to dry his fur for a week afterwards.
How could I forget? Which of Razum-dar's several missions in the Wilderking's kingdom are you referring to?

Do you question Adusa's skills? Her committment? Her honor?\n\nOf course they made it to Hoarfrost Downs! I must admit, though, that your help was welcome. Without your involvement, fewer would have survived that disaster.

Considering what happened, we should not call Maldred Adusa's friend.\n\nHe betrayed me. He betrayed his town. A quick death was too good for that traitor. Unfortunately, you dealt with him before I could get my claws into him.
Back up. Pa'alat is home to gamblers, vagabonds, and the retirement villa of a former Eye of the Queen. A legend, actually. A Khajiit named <<1>>.\n\nUnfortunately, we're pretty sure he's gone rogue.

He's selling secrets. Dominion secrets. His lovely little resort town is lousy with agents of the Ebonheart Pact and Daggerfall Covenant. \n\nI need to find proof, steal back what he's stolen, and take him out. Will you help me?
If you must. Of course, you already know whose side she'll be on.\n\nThat said, arrangements must be made. Be quick.
He's their leader. I've heard he's proficient in Reachmen magic and favored by some Hagraven, a foul paramour.\n\nMost Reachmen would have attacked already, but he bides his time.
Why? She pretends to be in charge of everything, and we've already received the bud from the <<1>>.\n\nThat's good enough for me, and it ought to be enough for the likes of her.
I'm a crow. What more do you need to know?

The High Kinlady and her little insurgency. Of course … Raz got to go disguised as an Elven noble.This one had a long conversation with one of the noble ladies at Estre's party. She spent the whole time complaining about 'stinking Khajiit.' Heh.

Yes, the little town with the forge. Raz had just gone there to get a report from Fistalle. Just a routine check-in. And we found that nest of … vipers. Pah. How brave those racists were, to kill a young woman.

The day you proved yourself to Her Majesty! She has often spoken of that day to Raz, commenting on your bravery. Heh. It is a shame this one will never get a chance to tell you the story about the bear.
Pah, that pathetic Prince. To think Her Majesty shared blood with that one. The day we ended him, once and for all, is a day Raz remembers well. This one has always been proud to fight beside you.

The traitor, yes? And another disguise … heh. It took Raz days to convince Her Majesty to let this one impersonate her. And to work on the voice … it took more days yet. Ahh, some days this one really did enjoy the job.

Pelidil, the Maormer, and … the sea serpent, yes? Hah, this one wishes he had been along for that fun. So it always goes, the Eyes must do what must be done. They do not get to choose what fun they have.

Right. I made it all the way to a cozy camp where we sit around and make nice while Verandis contemplates his navel. Oh, what joy.\n\nWhere I really want to be is next to Montclair with my hands around his neck.
I'm uncertain. Reinforcements perhaps. But that's the information we hope the other scouts have gathered.

I think I'd have better success coaxing an ogrim into my bed! The Countess won't listen to a word I say. She's convinced that religion is the answer to all our troubles. \n\nAfter this, I'm done with House Tamrith and beautiful nobles!
Adusa is very, very ready. Besides, the odds of actually dying … well, you know how it is with vampires. We're pretty hard to kill. Come, let us put an end to this.
Wouldn't be the first time I did something crazy, now would it?\n\nI'm in this until the end. After that—well, I'm sure something else will come along.

Do you see any tears in my eyes? No? I didn't think so.\n\nYou don't have to worry about me. I've got plenty of options for companionship. Take Gwendis, for instance. She might be a vampire, but she's got a great set of … um … fangs.

Oh my. I didn't realize you felt this way. But I guess it's to be expected. I never have been able to tone down the charm.\n\nWell, don't worry, my love. When this is all over, we'll find each other again. I just know we will.

In a sense, the power of the Sentinel is immortal. I'm old, but Elara is young. The Sentinel's power will take root and flourish in her.\n\nThe wyrd fear what she will become, but you can't let that stop you. Take my essence, when I'm gone. Save Elara.

The Viridian Woods are our home. They border Northglen as well as these ruins.\n\nWith Duraeg and his Reachmen army so close, the Glenmoril Wyrd must be wary of both him and the city dwellers. We keep a close watch on both sides.
Yes. The Dark Witnesses caught me while scouting the chapel. I'm in Isabeth's debt for finding me. A few moments longer and the Reachmen may have done to me what they did to Laetille.

There are certain … individuals … who question our faith and our loyalties. Who question how we can rule the realm while we are blinded by the Light.\n\nThe Light does not blind me! The Light illuminates my way!

Of course I'm right! I'm glad you understand the noble purpose that drives me.\n\nWe still have to get into the Doomcrag and destroy the Lightless Remnant. Our only hope is to continue to trust in the Light. We must not lose sight of that.

Not when those opinions confuse the issues and muddy the waters. The Light watches over us and protects us. My troops cling to that knowledge with every fiber of their being.\n\nI won't take that belief away from them.
Unlike the city dwellers, we care for the land and seek to protect it, rather than manipulate it. Our bond with the woods strengthens us both.
None so far. Delphique has a final plan, but if it doesn't work, we'll know there is no cure. At least none we can create.

The Dark Witnesses "planted" something inside of her. I'm not sure what sort of Reach magic they used to get it in there, but a sickness grows in her.\n\nAs I'm in Isabeth's debt, Wyress Delphique and I have been hoping to find a cure.

This one isn't sure you're cleared for such knowledge. A joke! A joke!\n\nHouse Ravenwatch is an old family. The Count is the last of the line, but he has many loyal vassals. Such as Gwendis, such as me. Rivenspire is our home. We wish to keep it safe.

I've seen the pain Verandis has suffered because of this place. It tortures him.\n\nVerandis has always been there for me. Always. I'll do anything for him. If that means invading the Doomcrag, then so be it.
Probably more than he'll ever know.\n\nBut that's beside the point. We need to end this and make things right. Even if we have to die to accomplish that.

I remember the terror of the Reachmen dragging me down the stairs. And the face of their leader, Duraeg. He grinned at me. I felt myself being lifted up and then … the pain. It was too much.\n\nI passed out. When I woke, I was tied up in the chapel.

They told me to stay in this circle. In case … I turn on them! What's going to happen to me? What do they think I am? Nothing has worked so far, nothing!\n\nWyress Delphique has one last hope. Please. Stay with me. I feel so alone here.
The Evermore soldiers? And why should we trust them? If we left the Viridian Woods, they'd cut down our trees in days, and mine the land with no regard for the life harbored there.
Gall and pox! Of course not! I'm a barmaid, not a strumpet!\n\nBesides, I know his type. He may talk sweet, but get him behind closed doors and he turns mean. I try to avoid his kind.
What? From looking at my bottom? If I knew how to make him stop, I would have done it hours ago. \n\nNo. I just want him to leave me alone.
Who? You mean <<1>>? Yeah, he's a pitiful fool that doesn't take no for an answer.
He must have come over here five times already. I'm not and will not ever be interested in having a drink with him.

I developed this little trinket to summon a banekin. I thought it would impress the Archmage, but instead it got me kicked out of the Mage's College.\n\nI was thinking of testing the trinket here—you know, to frighten someone and have a laugh.

Here. I was thinking the barmaid. But if you're crazy enough to try it on the bailiff, all the better.\n\nDepending on how it works, maybe I'll go into business selling these things. Let's see how it works.
You just missed it. Watching <<1>> run and hide when he saw a rat was one of the funniest things I've seen in a long time.
Deathly afraid apparently. I saw a rat in the attic earlier. I'm thinking about grabbing it and letting it go near him just to watch him jump around like a scared little girl again.
You just missed it. Watching <<1>> run and hide when he saw a rat was one of the funniest things I've seen in a long time.
Deathly afraid apparently. I saw a rat in the attic earlier. I'm thinking about grabbing it and letting it go near him just to watch him jump around like a scared little girl again.
No. Not me. I'm not what you'd call a brave man.\n\nWhen someone insults me, I much prefer to just send dirty looks and bad thoughts in their direction.
Yeah, that's him. He's a strange sort. Keeps to himself and drinks mostly, but I've seen him fingering a key he's got hanging around his neck.

I saw him fiddling with the coffer on his dresser when I wandered past earlier. When he saw me looking, he pretended to be doing something else. I'd wager he's got something special hidden inside and I'll bet that key opens it.
We think he's here to make contact with Montclair's forces, but we haven't been able to prove it.

She was? I mean, of course she was. Why wouldn't she?\n\nShe may have been a little intimidated by my good looks and natural charisma, but I'll win her over. I'll go over and ask her to have a drink with me. I'm sure she'll say yes this time.
You're right. I'm going to do it. I'm a good looking fellow and I've got loads of personality. I'll go over and ask her to have a drink with me. What have I got to lose?

Reachman effigies that Duraeg conjured out of the earth. Perhaps remnants of power they left behind. They're the source of the seeds they cultivate in the fields. Destroy the markers and you destroy the seeds.

This land used to be theirs, and not so long ago. They're here to reclaim it. It's why Evermore is such a prize to them.\n\nPerhaps we'd let them remain if they didn't pose such a threat to the Viridian Woods. Reachmen know no boundaries.

It's empowered with wyrd magic. When it comes into contact with the marker, the magic will course through it, withering it to the point where nothing is left but dust. The magic will penetrate deep enough to reach the seeds it produces.
After <<1>> broke their backs, we pacified the remnants of the Blacksap. Every rebel in <<2>> knows our faces. \n\nBut not yours. Your anonymity allows you to get close and capture their leaders.

<<1>> is strong as an ox and just as proud. His brother <<2>> seems to have more eyes in <<3>> than we do.\n\nBoth are sons of <<4>>—cousin to <<5>>, traitor to his people, and the prisoner for whom this place was built.

Trying to implant me like the rest. He said he was adding me to his ranks. That I'd be the perfect weapon, and he'd watch as I attacked my own father and my father would have to kill me.\n\nI fell unconscious from the pain moments later.
I recognize it, and it's one of Elgenie's best.\n\nThe poultice does more than heal. It grants invisibility. But if you engage any of the Reachmen after you use it, the spell will break.

No. I only found one survivor and the Glenmoril Wyrd wouldn't let her go. I found Ulmad and Bendais dead. But Hatmi, did you find her, too? I never should have left her alone.\n\nMy father … that is, Captain Gaercroft will be disappointed.

You don't know him.\n\nHe only acknowledges me when I'm doing something wrong. He calls me Isabeth the Impatient. Isabeth the Ignorant. Since I disobeyed orders, I bet he's got plenty to say about me today.
After what the wyrd did to my daughter? The wyress killed her without hesitation! I can't have that unpredictability among my soldiers.

Isabeth was a foolish girl. I should have disciplined her better. Made her stronger. She never followed orders. I knew this way of life would get her killed.\n\nHow can I possibly consent to this alliance with her blood on their hands?
Because bandits are dumb. They think an open gate is a weakness, so they all head for it. But we cut them down before they get inside.

They could, but they don't. The ones with bows won't fire their arrows at us, so we stand here as bait for the ones without bows. Then they come, and we make them decorate the cobbles.\n\nTold you. Bandits are dumb.
Of course, my friend. We can hold the door a few minutes more. What did you want to discuss?
I'll leave enough soldiers to protect our flank. But our best soldiers are coming with me.\n\nTell the Count that we're coming with him—whether he likes it or not.
As the leader of House Dorell and a member of Rivenspire's ruling triumvirate, it is.\n\nRemind Ravenwatch that he isn't in charge here. We're going with him to face Montclair!

Any help is welcome. Isabeth was last seen advancing toward the chapel to look for Hatmi.\n\nThe scouts' mission is to recover information and rescue civilians. We can't let the invaders reach Evermore.

Take this concoction Elgenie made. "It heals and conceals" according to her. If they're injured, they'll need it, but it only lasts so long.\n\nThey must come here straight away or risk the effects wearing off.

I thought I made that clear. The Count has been an invaluable ally, but he is not in charge of this expedition. My troops have served us well. They deserve to see this through to the end.\n\nTell the Count that we're going with him to Doomcrag.
It always does, my friend, it always does.\n\nArkay will lead us to victory this day. Of that, I have no doubt.

Good. That makes me feel even more confident about this. Khalisah knows me better than anyone else. If she thinks this is the right thing, then it must be so.\n\nJust one more favor, my friend. Will you take the necklace to Guendeline for me?
No! We shouldn't give what little we have left to a bunch of money-grubbing Khajiit. We can't trust them! They could abandon us here any minute now!

What do you mean? Base my mercenaries out of this tower? It's a central location, certainly. Overlooks a chokepoint through all corners of the Valenwood.\n\nBut no, I'm a <<1>> Orc. Without a mine to work, I'd be nothing next to my brother.

Nothing we didn't know already. <<1>> is the king's cousin, so we're forbidden from using harsher methods. More's the pity.\n\nIf you care to question him yourself, do so before you leave. You won't return here unless his sons are in hand.
What do you mean, just because some fobbing cat stole my sweetheart back home?\n\nHow did you even know about that? Either way, this has nothing to do with that!

The Baandari? Because they never stay anywhere very long, they're always leaving, especially in times of trouble.\n\nEven when they say they're going to stick around, it's just a damn lie. I wouldn't believe a word one of those cats says.
Grim? Sure is. Thankless too. \n\nThose trolls in Crestshade Mine toss out more bones than you can imagine. Trying to match the bones up, cart them to a graveyard, and bury them … it's hard work.
Sounds like the Bitterhand bandits went on a killing spree. I hear there are corpses everywhere up there.\n\nI don't normally like associating myself with bandits, but they pay pretty good.
Meet with <<1>>, our agent in <<2>>. It took months, but she identified locals connected to the Blacksap. She'll get you started.
West of here. I'll mark it on your map, but you'll stay away if you know what's good for you.

Well yeah. They don't like the smell of death and decay any more than anyone else. \n\nBesides, if there was a stench around the Flyleaf Catacombs, it might scare away travelers, and that's the bandits' bread and butter.
I've spent much of the past year as caretaker here, but I'll answer as best I can.

We needed a place where none could find <<1>>, so we dug out a remote Ayleid ruin, set up this prison, and then caved in the entrance. The only way in or out is through <<2>>'s portals.\n\nSo to answer your question … we're nowhere.

Good. Though I do hope you've given the matter due consideration. This isn't like choosing which tunic to wear in the morning. It will affect many lives and the future of the Daggerfall Covenant.\n\nTell me then. House Tamrith or House Dorell?

We'll hold them here until <<1>> says otherwise. If the heroes of the Blacksap vanish forever, their followers have nothing to rally behind.\n\nThen rebellion fades to memory, and we all get to live on with our lives.

We barely won the civil war. <<1>> would sit the throne if <<2>> hadn't answered our call for aid.\n\nOnce we'd captured the leader of the Blacksap, we knew we couldn't risk his escape. So we brought him here, to this hole in the ground.

The bright, young Countess Tamrith then. I know she is thoughtful, humble, and as sharp as an assassin's dagger. I am sure she will make a courageous queen.\n\nQueen Eselde of Shornhelm. It even has a nice ring to it.
Very well. Don't take too long though. We don't want anyone passing out from standing on their feet too long.

She's very young, but perhaps that means she will bring some much-needed change. \n\nVery well. If that's your counsel, I will make Countess Tamrith the Queen of Shornhelm. Are you certain she is the best choice, though?
The brave Baron Dorell, then. I know he is a valiant warrior, and I expect he will make a wise and honorable king. \n\nKing Alard of Shornhelm. It even has a nice ring to it.
If that's your counsel, then I will make Baron Dorell King of Shornhelm. Are you certain though that this is the wisest course?

A shard of Aetherial magicka that carries the essence of Nirn. Some link them to Lorkhan, the missing god of creation.\n\nIf you collect and absorb its power, it should restore your corporeal form. I will summon one of these shards for you to absorb.

If the gold's good, and though their ethical practices may be questionable, the Bitterhand Bandits pay pretty well. \n\nThey just offered me a month's pay to come and clear some corpses out of the Orc's Finger Ruins.
Not "Answer me, you traitorous dog?" You aren't one of <<1>>'s killers, that's clear.\n\nAsk your questions.
It's east of here a good ways. Out past Fell's Run. I'll mark it on your map.\n\nYou better not try to cut in on my business though!

They're sick of the hassle involved with robbing people and letting them go. A lot of folks were complaining to the guard and bringing trouble.\n\nSo they just kill their victims now and stash all the bodies outside the Orc's Finger Ruins for me.

Since his ascension to the throne, the king's attempts to "renew" our lands shows how soft he is on the Green Pact.\n\nMy people need a ruler who understands the ancient compacts aren't to be discarded. As second in line to the throne, it fell to me.

Of course I did! How better to reaffirm the Green Pact? To keep the High Elves out of <<1>>?\n\nBut <<2>> ended the Blacksap when she slaughtered us at <<3>>. I fear my sons can't see the rebellion is over. It's why I hope you capture them.

We only seek to save you from the fate that befell us so very long ago.\n\nThis place is cursed. Tainted by a terrible power that has grown corrupted and impure. We do not wish to see you succumb to its vile touch.

I do. I've come to respect Countess Tamrith. She's a bright, young woman. But she's not qualified to rule the kingdom.\n\nThe coming days demand decisive leadership and a firm hand. You know that as well as I. That makes me the perfect choice.

First things first. We need to rebuild our defenses. \n\nThe Shornhelm Guard has been decimated by this civil war, and we'll need to recruit and retrain hundreds of young men and women to restore our strength.

If the full weight of the Dominion gets involved in a local rebellion, my people will suffer.\n\nI'd rather use the Dominion's tools against them. A public trial will show our cause to be just. But only if my sons still live.
When we came to this land, many eons ago, we brought with us a powerful relic to help us tame its wilderness and allow us to survive.

The relic is a vessel. It barely contains the power within it. Damaging the vessel will unleash its power—sending a wave of corruption to cover the land.\n\nThe blood-curse was but a taste of what will befall your people if the relic is destroyed.

The relic cannot be destroyed. If that is your quest, you have already failed. The vampire knows this. As does the one now controlling the relic.\n\nIf you try to destroy the relic, you will only unleash its power.

I do. Baron Dorell is a good man, but he can be dangerously short-tempered and is far too quick to act. \n\nShornhelm has had enough impetuous rulers in its history. We need a thoughtful ruler who truly has the people's best interests at heart.

Helping the people of Rivenspire recover. So many of the kingdom's subjects have been displaced. So many have lost loved ones. \n\nWe must do what we can to restore the people's faith and get their lives back to at least a semblance of normalcy.
It was originally Lattanya—the Light of Life. Forged by our greatest sorcerers, it helped plants grow and healed illnesses. It helped us bring life to this barren wilderness.

It became Abagandra—the Lightless Remnant, a beacon of death. Moreover, when the vampire touched it, the corruption intensified. Became more potent.\n\nIf the relic is destroyed, the blood-curse will flow unhindered throughout the land.

We were attacked by the savages that dwelled here before us. It was a brutal fight, and much blood was spilled. Many died on both sides of the conflict.\n\nBlood and death tainted the Light of Life. The relic … changed.
The worst … or the best … depending on your perspective, walker.\n\nIt's your turn to be impressed now. Crazy Eye has her new bow! Together, this one and you will make Imperial pie! Are you ready?
Crazy Eye is always ready. Here they come. Ha!
Be quick with your preparations then. Those soft-bellied shaveskins could be here any moment now, and you don't want Crazy Eye to have all the fun, do you?
I'm fine, thanks to you.\n\nAnd Peras owes his life to you twice. It's his fault we ended up in Crimson Raider seas. If you hadn't saved us, I would have killed him.
I think he's had ample time to pray at this point. With all due respect to him and to the gods, we need answers here.\n\nWill you at least see if he'll talk to you?
You refer to my garb, I suspect. Not all knights are bedecked in glistening plate armor, my friend. True knighthood is measured by the steel within, not the steel without.

The Order of St. Pelin is diverse. We have many responsibilities. We are tasked with defending the realm through force of arms, but we are also called to acts of charity. \n\nMy duties as a Knight Medicus lean towards the latter.
Before, during, and after. We are warriors all. \n\nI admit, though, it's good to sheathe the sword and take up the salve. It's what I'm best at.

Quite so. We heal the sick and tend to the poor. \n\nOur dedication to St. Pelin's ideals may be more literal than some others, but all of us, Knights Beligerus or Medicus, are devoted to both the people and the realm.

Hopefully we'll return to our original course. We were headed to Tempest Island to study the storm phenomena.\n\nI've heard the Maormer are causing trouble in the area, but trouble never stops a dedicated scholar.
Crazy Eye scared them off, but they're coming back now. Are you ready to fight them?
This one will help you get revenge!
Take your time, walker. Crazy Eye will keep watch.

These ruins under the manse vile are the remains of a city of Mer twice forgotten. Here, the children of Auri-El trifled with knowledge that was beyond them. The dirt swallowed them.\n\nTheir descendants tried to rebuild, but then came Graccus.
You're the one doing the real work here. If all I have to do is answer a few questions, I'm getting off easy.\n\nWhat do you want to know?

Enough of your constant mewling, Verandis! Are you a vampire or a scullery maid? This is exactly what we've been looking for!\n\nYou told me yourself. The Ayleid texts referred to latta—the light. This is it. This is what will cure Leila.

We don't know why the Ayleids did a lot of things. They were a strange people. But that won't stop us. Stand back and watch, for all I care. But we're going to save my wife!\n\nI'll risk my life—my very soul—to help my dear Leila. Now, let's begin.
The fools! I just wish I would have realized our mistake before we made it this far.

According to legend, it's the final tear shed by the Ayleid princess Anurraame, after she was betrayed by her lover.\n\nThey say its substance is pure hatred, and it has the power to crush armies. The book I brought with me describes it in more detail.

I've been studying magic for a few months, but all I can really do is conjure up a light.\n\nI suppose that would help you a little, but honestly, I have a feeling I'd just get killed. I might even get you killed too.

Magister Wulfdis said this assignment wasn't just a test of my magical ability, but also of my resourcefulness.\n\nFinding you and enlisting your help was pretty resourceful. At least, that's the argument I intend to make.
Better. Stronger. Almost whole again. Isn't that strange?\n\nI feel powerful enough to take on Umaril the Unfeathered, himself! I feel … like a warrior again!

No. It's too late for that now. We have to move forward and hope we're not overwhelmed by our own forces.\n\nBut if any of them turn into bloodfiends, I promise to end their suffering as quickly as possible.

I didn't think. Didn't realize that our proximity to the Remnant would be our undoing.\n\nThe Remnant feeds off life. Devours it. Not only will Gwendis and I be susceptible to its lure, but the soldiers—they're just more fodder for the blood-curse.
The Camp was our jumpoff point for the attack on Bangkorai Garrison. It eventually turned into our medical base.
They're attacking from the lake. They travel across on light boats, usually at night, attack the camp and steal what little we have left. By the time we can raise an alarm, they're gone.
Most of our Covenant supplies went to the siege. When we were running low, these Baandari came in and cut their prices to help us out. We'd be long dead without their help.

We held for days, but once they were able to start stealing the Baandari's goods, it was only a matter of time before they ground us down. There's barely enough of us to keep watch, much less guard the camp.
<<AC:1>> was thought to be the resting place of Mannimarco's most powerful disciple.\n\nWe were searching the site—carefully, mind you—when the shades awoke.

It's about time. I haven't heard anything from that slippery lizard in weeks. If she's not able to deliver a steady supply, we can't keep doing business together.\n\nTell me you've got something more for me than an excuse.
Ah …!\n\nWherever did you get this marvelous gem?

Legend has it that Jone was struck by a bolt of light. For but a second, she turned from her twin and, overtaken by sadness, shed a single tear. Jode brushed it from her cheek and it fell to the desert below.\n\nJone's Tear, such a beautiful gem.

Yes, <<1>> said I'm to support you in tracking down <<2>>'s sons. We'll start with <<3>>, the Blacksap's spymaster. If we capture him first, his brother <<4>> will be without eyes.\n\nAnd before you ask, I lost it in the war.

As the mud is my mother, I will return your generosity, stranger.\n\nI go from here to the chapel in Shornhelm to repent of my misdeeds. Find me there at the chapel and I will ensure you receive a fruitful reward for your help.

She is not far. She is in Fell's Run. Her name is Brigibeth. I would go speak to her myself, but she would cut me down.\n\nI was only thinking, since you were helping me here, you might speak to her on my behalf?

Of course not! A fanciful tale. This jewel was cut from a Varla stone by Azesaz, greatest jeweler of the first era—but it's a good story, isn't it? And will fetch a fine price.\n\nYou do your friends credit! Such a prize deserves a fine reward.

The Blacksap Rebellion started here. It won't surprise you to learn <<1>>'s citizens provide food and gold to the remnants.\n\nThey use special phrases to arrange meetings. If you know the phrases, you can get to the remnants.

As the Hollow Moon waxes, it is only fair that we balance the scales! We will invest significant capital in bolstering our esteemed protectors.\n\nOtherwise, we might find ourselves waiting in one of <<1>>'s famous lines, no?

The Blacksap protects its own. I can't imagine they'll be happy.\n\nYou'll see a list of known sympathizers in the journal. Approach them, and use the right phrase to set up a meeting with <<1>>. Find me when you're done.

The phrases change weekly. Definitely the work of <<1>>.\n\nLucky for you, I've done the scutwork. You'll find this week's phrases in the journal next to me. I leave it to you to work out which ones to use.

She is our Merciful Healing Mother, divine goddess of the Tribunal of Morrowind, who I am sworn to serve. Though occupied with the war that rages on, her compassion extends to all when it comes to the vile Prince of Schemes.

Allies recruited by Almalexia to aid me in opposing the Harvester of Souls, plucked from the best of the Fighters Guild across Tamriel. Every one of them experienced at destroying Dark Anchors, which is what makes their disappearance so troubling.
Perhaps you have heard the song in the taverns: "Oh, Gil-Var-Delle, your name is desolation on my lips." \n\nOnce, a thriving Wood Elf town was nestled here, full of life and music. Until he came.

My goddess possesses many gifts, not the least of which is her sight. She saw you were crucial to what must happen here, and that your hatred of the Prince of Schemes burns almost as deeply as her own.

The Harvester of Souls claimed them all, reaping every last soul. Almalexia saw the horror as it unfolded, but could do nothing.\n\nHer memory is long and her compassion burns like the sun. She sent a group of us to destroy the Dark Anchor here.
Ha! She's getting out of the bandit business? Impossible.\n\nWhat's she going to do? Move to Shornhelm and try to earn an honest living?

I don't know. Where would I go? What would I do?\n\nMaybe I could start over with Teeba-Ja? Yes. Tell her to keep an eye out for me. I'll have to think about this, but it's starting to sound like a good idea.

That's … that's … really courageous of her. To tell you the truth, I've often dreamed of doing the same thing.\n\nI thought if I tried something like that then she and the other Bitterhand bandits would track me down and kill me. I was afraid.

We couldn't budge it. Nothing we tried worked. All around it was this feeling, a chill running down our spines.\n\nIt was his presence, from when he reaped the souls of Gil-Var-Delle all those years ago. It's strengthening the Dark Anchor, somehow.
I don't know! If mortal weapons are useless, if even the most devastating magic fails, what hope do mere mortals have against the Prince of Schemes?

There are evil devices planted in the earth. The Worm Cultists call them Fangs of Chaos. They seem to be channeling the residual magic from Molag Bal's presence into the Anchor. \n\nArys tried to destroy one, but it killed him the instant he hit it.

Take Almalexia's Tear. Destroy the Worm Cultists. Their blood will awaken her fury.\n\nOnce my goddess's fury is released from the gem, nothing, not even these Fangs of Chaos, will withstand it. I will remain at your side to see this through.

A goddess never suffers without purpose. The gem can destroy the Fangs of Chaos.\n\nBlessed Almalexia warned me that no mortal could wield the gem without also being destroyed by her rage. She told me to wait for the soulless, deathless one. You.

Damn. We have to find him. As long as he's at large, this region of Rivenspire is in terrible danger. \n\nNow, if I could just get the Countess to abdicate her authority to me, we'd put an end to this constant bickering and really get things done.

Oh, quite. Stibbons should recover, once I reverse the process.\n\nAll my supplies are at my new camp, through these ruins. We'll need to get some things here, then go to my first camp at the dig site. Which, unfortunately, has been overrun by Goblins.

So that's why all these crows have descended on the city? Gods! I knew it wasn't a coincidence. Fine. I'll give every guard a bow. I think it's time for us to do some bird hunting.\n\nFirst though, if you spoke to their leader, what did she say?

Yes, but I'm certain I can restore him if we find his, er, my notes. Stibbons put them in a safe place somewhere in this camp. \n\nI'm sure you can find them—you're ever so handy at that sort of thing.

So we can use it on the Goblins, of course! Once they're petrified, they'll be the test subjects for my antidote. \n\nLet's go recover my reagents from those beasts. Then I must check my notes against the Yokudan inscriptions. If I can find them again.

I tried, but he refused to go near the Goblins. Besides, he's quite mad—he's become entirely preoccupied with some ancient Yokudan riddle. \n\nYou'll see when you meet him. Perhaps you'll be able to talk some sense into him.
For the present. If things get too dirty though, Crazy Eye will save her own hide! \n\nThis one and other Baandari are not mercenaries; we're traders!

I shall have to somehow drag Stibbons back to the other camp. It's a bother, but there's no help for it.\n\nOnce you've observed the results of your trials, meet me back there with your report. That data should enable me to concoct the final antidote.

I see. Not really much of a surprise. The Reachmen are bearing down on Northglen already.\n\nWe've already sent every soldier we can spare, but there's little chance of turning the tide of battle. Your presence there might make all the difference.
There are no dunes without wind, yet when the wind is gone, the dune remains. Eh? \n\nTongues of stone, young seeker. Tongues of stone.

Air … yes, that's it! The breeze, the breath of Tava! Ah, devious Sep, you wind a fateful path in this desert!\n\nHere, then, is your answer: within the maw and between the teeth! The gargoyle cannot hide its mortality forever!

No! So unfair too! Crazy Eye's been guarding this gate for hours and hours when she could be back in her tent taking a cozy little nap.\n\nYou should tell the knight captain. Tell her to give us something!
