Sure. He could probably use some encouragement. Tell him I'm going to promote him to Lieutenant … assuming we defeat the Reachmen, of course.
Nah. I'm not cut out to be a city guard. I think I'll go check out the Fighters Guild. I hear they're always looking for someone of my caliber.
No, but damn! That stupid Nord. He was in on Duke Renchant's plan, wasn't he? I had a feeling.\n\nWell, I guess he got what was coming to him.

She said that? Well I'll be an Argonian's uncle! I thought I'd be Sergeant forever.\n\nMaybe I can afford that new mace after all … assuming we beat the Reachmen and the queen stays true to her word. I trust her though.
And that's why I'm not choking him where he stands.\n\nMight seem harsh to someone on the outside looking in, but you don't know Peras like I do.

Well, now that she's no longer my lord and master, I might swing by and see if Eselde wants to … indulge in any of her less-theological fantasies. Maybe something along the lines of the farmer's lonely daughter ….

Do you expect me to send one of the wyress couriers? We are not like you people.\n\nWere I less exhausted and had more experience, I could communicate through the trees, but that is not happening anytime soon, and you should not delay.

We're more like freelancers. You can go far in the world with a strong sword arm and a little courage. My mother wanted me to be a seamstress, and Ignobert's family were cloth dealers. Turns out, we both hate making clothes! We're quite the match.
You were told what you needed to hear to become effective.\n\nYou should cherish the gift you have been given. It is a leaf from Apocrypha. Only delectable knowledge will you find within its pages.

He sought the power to end some petty conflict of Men and Mer above, but his want is irrelevant.\n\nGraccus showed promise when he glimpsed the Infinium and survived its cosmic ululation. But he ultimately proved mundane.

Never! This is your fault, vampire! Your presence altered the relic's magic.\n\nBut I can restore Leila! The relic has changed me. The others, as well. We're stronger, more powerful. This sensation, however. How odd! I have a sudden craving for blood.

Corrupted? What a ridiculous notion! I feel its power coursing through me. I am better than I was—immortal!\n\nWith this power, I'll make sure that no one else suffers as Leila suffered. There will be no more death! I'll make everyone immortal!
Preparing a stew for Lady Laurent and her associates.\n\nAnd worrying. I'm doing a lot of worrying.
Cadwell sees things as he wishes them to be. To him, Coldharbour is a wondrous place. It's his home. And he knows it like the back of his hand.\n\nHe's usually down by the river. Let's go find him.
Yes, of course it's me. Who were you expecting? Molag Bal?

Breagha-Fin. A Nord settlement, from what Lady Laurent told me.\n\nExiles, you know. Got into trouble for performing unnatural rituals back in Skyrim and were banished. Of course, I haven't seen a single Nord out here, so make of that what you will.

Famous treasure hunter. I'm sure you've heard of her.\n\nWe travel throughout the land at the behest of the Mages Guild, ever-searching for hidden treasures, secret relics, and, er, other mystical things. Can't talk much about our work, you know.
Oh, that. Things like that are always happening to me. An occupational hazard of working for Lady Laurent, don't you know.\n\nNo worries, though. I'm much better now.

Just because I'm a healer doesn't mean I don't know my way around a battlefield. I kept my head low, followed orders, and took care of the wounded.\n\nThankfully, I had a few supplies, but what you brought me is a godsend!

Now we'll call upon Hircine and find out why he's forsaken us.\n\nAs you restored the wards, you are now a part of the grotto's life too. Therefore, I will ask you to perform a necessary role in our sacrifice.
We need a still-beating heart. You've offered to assist us? I ask you to be the ultimate sacrifice to save the grotto. You are the key to reaching Hircine.

Disorientation is understandable.\n\nSomehow, when I joined the ritual, I altered the power of the relic. I turned Leila into a monster. I had to kill her. And Montclair and the others … they became vampires imbued with the power of the relic.
That's strange. I haven't seen a peeper around here in quite some time.
Yes, Nyronie is … prepared. I can't say it will be easy, at least for me.

Of course. It's the only way to get Hircine's attention. If he's forsaken us, we need an extreme sacrifice to call upon him.\n\nLinnae should be proud of Nyronie for offering herself. She's a true testament to the wyrd.

This is the way of the Glenmoril Wyrd. Everything makes sacrifices. The plants and beasts, that we may eat. The wood, that we may have fire. The people we've come to love.\n\nThere's nothing wrong with sacrifice, so long as it's done properly.
<<1>>'s death will still be an honorable sacrifice.
Yes. It's my responsibility after my failures. Besides, our duty is to the land. We gain our power from Hircine. If we don't have the power to protect the land, what would become of it?
Perhaps, but we are all reborn of the land. I may give the life of this body, but will gain a complete union with the earth beneath us.
Good.\n\nWait for my signal. When the time is right, cut out her heart and place it on the altar.
That's true. Say, do you know why the peeper's skin is red?
Head to the Butcher's Ground. He'll be there when he's ready.\n\nWe won't speak again.
You're a new face. What do you want?

I led you right here to make it all boring again. And what did he do to stop you? Nothing! There I stood in my best old-lady suit, and he said it was all my fault!\n\nAh, he just needs motivation. What better than an escaped prisoner seeking vengeance?

I have Gwendis to thank for that. She pulled me out of there before Montclair and the others were fully recovered.\n\nNow Montclair claims he wants to end death and suffering. That he wants to take the throne of Ranser. And it's all my fault.

To start: a hunter's challenge of skill. Hunt my aspects within my Hunting Grounds: a shade of this realm and my own. Prove yourself worthy of my favor. Only then will you earn the chance to retake the grotto for the wyrd.

I will place you there. When you've won—if you've won—return to the shrine. I will be there as the Spirit of the Hunt.\n\nWe'll discuss your prowess and your final task for the grotto when the hunt is over.

Already you yearn for the next hunt!\n\nI've two hunters and one grotto. To the victor goes the spoils. Find Brinarch and rip the briarheart from his chest. Prove yourself the true hunter and he, the prey, and the grotto is yours.
Should you prove yourself the victor, bring the Reachman's fledgling briarheart back to the altar. I will speak to you one last time, if you succeed.
Thank you for making our sister's death worth it. We're in your debt.\n\nWe still have a lot of work to do, cleaning out the remaining Reachmen and regaining the full trust of the bears.
We can feel the connection returning, but there's no telling what damage has already been done and how long it will take to undo.\n\nNow, please return the briarheart to Hircine.

What makes tyrants do any of the things they do? Ambition? Glory? I certainly don't know.\n\nWhat I do know is that Montclair's forces have taken half the capital and will soon take the rest of it unless the Shornhelm guard gets some help.

She's the head of one of the noble houses. Young, but smart and very devout. I'm told she studied in Stormhaven, and has Emeric's favor.\n\nShe's not unattractive either … but she is my current employer, so I try not to notice.
I needed some quiet time. What do you think I'm doing in here? I went and got myself captured! I'm one of the Shornhelm Guard.\n\nLook, let me out of this cell and I can help you.
Good question. You shouldn't. But that doesn't mean we're not on the same side. I bet they sent you to find information about Montclair.\n\nOpen the cell and I'll tell you what I know.
You speak falsely. As this one said at Arenthia, Akkhuz-ri is the Mane no more. The touch of darkness, the stain of Javad Tharn's creature, remains. He can never atone for what he did.
This one has known Shazah and Khali since they were cubs, since their days at the temple. They are strong, proud women. Our people will be in good hands, whoever walks the Two Moons Path.
I signed the Elden Accord. The people trust me, they trust my judgment. They know that I will serve ably as Speaker to the next Mane. With my help, the people will grow to love her.

I've known the Speaker and the Mane for years, and have every confidence in them. I've spoken to Shazah and Khali here in the temple, and I'm most impressed. The Summerset Isles will support Elsweyr, come what may.
By Arkay's beard, it is good to see a friendly face in this evil land.
Yes. A tomb held the broken scythe blade that killed Saint Octavien. I hope it helps our cause.\n\nI was just about to leave when I saw you enter the ruins. I must return to Alvaren with this relic.

I have spoken with the Champions, taken in their scent. They seem lean, strong, flexible … much like my Silvenar. I fear they do not have the experience, the age, that the Mane should have. But I am willing to watch and wait and see.

Stephenn says it's better to die fighting and getting ahead in life, instead of dying in a puddle of mud in a refugee camp. \n\nIf the bandits were cleared out of the Orc's Finger Ruins, my brother would have no choice.
I don't want anyone telling me where to sleep, when to eat, who to fight or how to live my life. I want to be free and I want to make loads of money.

Here, let me show you where it is on your map. Even if you don't go up there yourself, you should be aware of the dangers of this part of Rivenspire. \n\nI just wish my brother understood that danger is not better than squalor!
I don't think it's really a priority right now, with Baron Montclair having caused so much trouble.
Montclair has never left the Remnant chamber. He was able to defeat us by working through a projection!\n\nI assume he's teleported Gwendis and the others to his side.
Gods, I hope so. But don't let <<1>> hear me say it. Superstitious Redguard.\n\nI say, you don't become a vampire hunter if you don't like taking risks. The more they fight, the more fun it is.

I can feel them. Gwendis, Tamrith, and Dorell are still alive. But I can also feel Gwendis' hunger. She won't be able to hold back much longer.\n\nWe must be ready to do whatever is necessary. Let's go.
We can discuss that later. For now, we need to reach Gwendis before the Remnant corrupts her and she feasts upon the others.\n\nHead upstairs and I'll follow right behind you.
I am still connected to the one who turned me. The answer to our problem rests with him.\n\nIf we're going to defeat Montclair, you must trust me this one last time. I will not betray you.
That's all I need to know. Anyone who tries to harm us will answer to my blade.

All right. Pay close attention. I'll try to be brief, but if we don't all focus on doing our job, we're as good as dead.\n\nThe vampires in this area are controlled by a single, powerful vampire lord. He likely sired most of them himself.

I have a sister in the camp, and I want to keep an eye on her. I have a … business opportunity to join an outfit nearby. I would make a tidy profit and be my own man, and I could keep an eye on Claudelle.

Well, I have an opportunity set up already. There's a group called the Bitterhand that provides limited protection to the local farms while collecting a reasonable protection fee, and I think I'll see if I can join them.
I won't head up there until I see that my sister is safe. They're holed up in the Orc's Finger Ruins now.\n\nIt's exciting, isn't it? Breathe that air, friend. It smells like freedom and fortune.
I don't think I should say where they are. For all I know, you just want to edge in on my opportunity.
That's what my sister called them too, but what's the difference between a bandit and a guard? One is more heavily controlled and gets paid much less. I want freedom and more coin than I can carry.

It provides protection to local farms in exchange for a modest fee. The farms are plagued with all sorts of problems, you see. If they don't pay us, then there's a good chance that some thugs might show up and burn their farms down.
I have another sister out there, but she's quite capable of taking care of herself. The problem is, my sister is scared of the world. I want to stay nearby so I can provide for her from time to time.

Our other sister left for Cyrodiil a while ago, and she refused to leave Rivenspire then. I doubt it would change now.\n\nBesides, I found an appealing business opportunity that might work out better. Less work, more pay.
Up near the Orc's Finger Ruins, I suppose. I just don't know why he would do this. If you go out that way, would you … would you look for him? He looks like me but he's taller. His name is Stephenn.

All right. Pay close attention. I'll try to be brief, but if we don't all focus on doing our job, we're as good as dead.\n\nThe vampires in this area are controlled by a single, powerful vampire lord. He likely sired most of them himself.
I'd heard about a cave to the west, where there are some catacombs, maybe some old money and treasures. But the Bitterhand Bandits have taken it over!\n\nI barely escaped with my life!
It's a bit of a way from here. It's called the <<1>>.\n\nI can show it to you on your map so you know to stay away, but I'm going to keep running.
My brother <<1>> is a useless drunk. The family needs money, and he only spends it.\n\nI figured I'd go adventuring and bring something back for us. What a horrible idea.
I think that someone must've mixed something into the beer. The spiders looked so much … smaller last night.\n\nPlease, you've got to get Garth back.
I probably shouldn't have been trying to steal spider silk directly from the queen. Of course, I might've gotten away with it, if I hadn't passed out.
That again? My sister … <<1>> foolishly committed to build the Khajiit an embassy, months ago. Everything was to be handled through <<2>> at <<Ac:3>>.

Ask a stonemason. I have to prepare for the ratification ceremony before <<1>>'s arrival. I can't be troubled with such minor issues.\n\nIf you care to pursue the matter, speak with <<2>> at <<Ac:3>>.
An archaic Wood Elf ritual. If she dances to their tune, <<1>> will be recognized by the heavens as a worthy candidate for emperor of Tamriel.\n\nRubbish, if you ask me.
To promote harmony, she'd tell you. The same reason she picked this bizarre tree city as the Dominion's capital. She wants every member of the Dominion to feel as though they're equal.
No, no! Jurak just has one of those faces, you know? The Brights Moons orbit in mysterious ways.

Oh, we need to be unified against our enemies. And having a High Elf in charge is paramount to our success. But do we really need all this coddling?\n\nThe ratification ceremony, the business with the embassy … more problems due to "harmony."

Forgive my manners! There's so much to do in preparing for <<1>>'s ratification ceremony. Tempers fray, as I'm sure you can understand.\n\nBut if <<2>> sent you, it must be important. What can I do for you?
Why would <<1>> care about that? If they're too lazy to build their own embassy, can't they afford an inn?

Check our storeroom. The Khajiit didn't even bother to pick up the supplies!\n\nIn the meantime, I'm off to locate <<1>>. If he didn't send you here with his blessing, I'll see you face Dominion justice.
Well, I … of course I ordered it done! I hired some Wood Elves to excavate the stone, and set aside supplies for Khajiit to use.\n\nIt isn't my fault if the locals couldn't do their jobs!

He is a cold-hearted killer who enjoys what he does. Just last month, Two-Blades ambushed a caravan bringing supplies to an orphanage in Stormhaven. Slaughtered the guards and made off with the goods. He has no sense of honor.

<<1>>'s as cunning as she is brutal. She fought her way to the top of her organization, climbing a ladder of blood. There's always a group of fierce young warriors at her side.\n\nIf it turns into a battle, you're going to have a war on your hands.
Ever hear of Egar Fannon, Melanie Wingarde, or Avery Duchamp? No? That's because the Cloak cut them down. Now, they're just footnotes in a history book.\n\nThe Cloak is dangerous.

Because the ring is very valuable, of course. Jurak-dar has a very lucrative buyer lined up in the town of Pa'alat. Very respectable, and willing to pay top coin. You have retrieved the ring, so Jurak will cut you in!

Because the ring is very valuable, of course. Jurak-dar has a very lucrative buyer lined up in the town of Pa'alat. Very respectable, and willing to pay top coin. You have retrieved the ring, so Jurak will cut you in!

A shallow man, lacking any redeemable qualities. This is a power grab, pure and simple. He's trading on his name to try to get a slice of the Rivenspire pie.\n\nBut if he wants pie, Adusa has a pie for him right here.

Yes! A piece of living history, touched by the fur of the First Mane himself. To even think that it could be bought or sold … please, traveler. You must give the ring to me. We'll keep it safe, hidden, and preserved for our people.
What I wanted from you, I already got. An evening's distraction.
You needn't trouble yourself with such trifles. Go. Be free. Not all have the luxury of walking away from me.
Fine, fine! I've been stuck down here, but I've overheard snippets of conversation. The bandit leader's name is Accalia. He stole the relics for the Stonefire Cult.

He's expecting one of their leaders soon and he intends to sell him the Chalice of Mara. I heard one of the other relics is being kept in a tower, in some area open to the sky but still inside the ruins.

Centuries ago it was an Imperial stronghold, but now it's known as a sleepy coastal town with a big cathedral.\n\nYou'll find mostly Colovians who've been here for generations and a handful of Wood Elves who don't pay much heed to the Green Pact.
No, it's …. Wait, yes, that's it exactly! The Daedric Prince of Madness himself, here in <<1>>.\n\nIt's all rather exciting, isn't it?
It was the Khajiit. We failed them. Because, here, no one became the Mane after Akkhuz-ri.
Let … let us continue on the Path. If the Bright Moons felt we needed to see the future of the Bosmer … perhaps we shall now see the future of the High Elves. Let's hope it is not as bleak.

There's been so much corruption, so much darkness. Even if we walk the path through the Den of Lorkhaj … seeing these visions has made me realize how critical the Mane can be. I don't know if I'm ready.
Perhaps … for you,  Hallowed. For Shazah … for the Khajiiti people. Hallowed, we owe you so much. I don't know if I can ever thank you properly.

My friend, this could never have happened without you. Your wisdom at Arenthia. Your strength at Rawl'kha. Your bravery at Moonmont. And here … we saved the Jewel of Elsweyr! Dune is safe. Javad Tharn is dead, and I have walked the Path.
The end of one path, and the beginning of another. As you well know, the path never really ends. Here in Reaper's March I will restore the soul of the Khajiit and you … will travel on.
She did? That's different, then. Show me her orders and I'll stand aside.
Then I can't let you inside. Her instructions were very specific—no one gets in without her written permission. I'm to remain at my post until relieved.\n\nExcept in an emergency, of course.
The Khajiit could riot. That would be bad, very bad.\n\nOr a fire, of course. But the chances of that happening are slim.
Aye. The fearful matriarch of the spider den. They say she's a thousand years old, call her the "Spider Queen."\n\nIt makes my skin crawl just thinking about it.
Oh, you are surprised? Is that because you tried to kill me? This one gets that a lot, people trying to kill him and then being surprised when it does not work.

Well, you know the old saying about what happens when you drop a Khajiit from a high place. To tell you truly, Raz was never worried. He knew you would do what had to be done … that you would come through. Thank you, my friend.

There was jumping, some acrobatics. It was quite heroic. Raz tried … he tried to get the others out. But the collapse happened too fast. He took a grevious injury. Raz had to rest and recuperate before he could rejoin the Queen.
Montclair's forces tried to assault our camp. We held them off, though. Our mages put up some wards, so they should be fine without us.\n\nSkordo and I decided to come lend a hand.

We've got this covered. Just watch out for yourself up there. Don't do anything foolish, like dying heroically or something. I try to avoid any kind of dying, heroic or otherwise.\n\nBesides, I'd rather you survive. Now go and do what you do best!
Do you think so? I wouldn't want to burn down the embassy.
You're right. And I can stay here to make sure it doesn't get out of hand.\n\nThanks for the suggestion!

Died in a battle with the Reachmen—right there with King Eamond. You have to feel for the queen. First she loses her daughter, then her husband and her son. \n\nPrince Adrien deserves a proper burial … just maybe after the graveyard's safe again.
Of course. It's where <<1>> cut down most of their forces.
No good reason, I'm sure of it. But we don't have a choice. If <<1>> shows up, you'll need to capture him.
Here, these were <<1>>'s rings. His sons will recognize them immediately. As soon as <<2>> puts it on, he'll be transported to the hidden prison.\n\nOne of <<3>>'s more devious enchantments.

We need <<1>> and his brother. See if you can get him to talk about where <<2>> is hiding.\n\nYou have a ring for each brother. Once you've captured them both, <<3>> will find you. And if we don't meet again, it's been an honor.
This one is a master of stealth and a gatherer of information.\n\nSometimes Adusa strikes, but sometimes Adusa points the blade and lets another drive it home.

I don't know much. Malofar was the leader of a Nord clan back in Skyrim. He and his clan mates were banished for performing dark rituals, so they came to this forsaken wilderness.\n\nHe stole the relic and the Mages Guild sent me to retrieve it.
It possesses some kind of enchantment. But as to why they call it emerald, I have no idea. The Mages Guild was adamant about making sure it returns to them in one piece.

Lazy, good-for-nothing loafers, if you want my honest opinion. They insisted the caves were full of Goblins.\n\nThat's ridiculous! My sources tell me that Malofar and a clan of Nords moved into these caves. No one said anything about Goblins.

I know enough. Khajiit are owed an embassy. They're angry the High Elves are dragging their feet to build it.\n\nSeemed like politics, until a dozen stonemasons vanished without a trace. The king sent me to find out why.
You'll be the first person Adusa calls. Promise.
The queen? Of course we can do this!\n\nWe shall set out for <<1>> at once, if you are ready.
Then let's be off!
When you're ready, let me know. We'll wait as long as we can!

She rescued a wyress, and a villager named Laetille. The wyress said they're holding an area beneath the Ayleid ruins. Isa said she'd go and see about an alliance.\n\nI told them to leave me here. I'd only slow them down with these wounds.

No. It's tradition for the kings of Evermore to be entombed at Bangkorai Garrison, so they can protect our borders for "all eternity."\n\nDame Valyrie says my father lies in state there even now. Unless he's been resurrected, of course.

My poor mother. I didn't even think of it, but this must've been torture for her. \n\nBut to hear that I've risen—would this be a relief to her, or some kind of horror? Best to figure out what's happening here, and then I will go tell her myself.
No. To be honest, I only know of the kings who've been entombed down at the garrison. \n\nIt's the royal crypt though, so surely someone from my family has been buried here.

Before the Dominion, <<1>> nearly lost a civil war. I came to see if the missing stonemasons were targeted by the Blacksap Rebellion.\n\nBut Blacksap would've displayed the bodies, not left them as food for hoarvor.

<<1>> used criminals to smuggle supplies … never directly, but enough for us to notice. I'm not saying she had these stonemasons killed, but I'd like to ask her myself.\n\nProblem is, there's nothing we can do while she's in <<Ac:2>>.
The king suspects <<1>> has been up to no good. Little things, some of her associations. But he can't accuse his allies of undermining the whole alliance.\n\nSo he sent me to deal with it.
Spoke with someone I trust. She's definitely here.\n\nWe should get moving. We're not far behind her.
Very. Her wounds were shallow, but the poison runs deep.\n\nThese walls of stone will help contain her sickness, to keep it from leaching into the soil below.
Adusa … my oldest, most trusted ally. Tell her that House Ravenwatch is hers now. She must carry on our work … continue to train Gwendis … and any others who need her help.

Because I need to take this relic out of this realm. It needs to be transported to a place where it can't do any harm.\n\nI have made a deal with my master. Molag Bal has agreed to take me and the relic to Coldharbour.

The deal has already been made. It's either this or allow everyone to turn into the very fiends we worked so hard to save them from.\n\nThere is no other way. Tell Gwendis that I will miss her. She was always so full of … life. Farewell, my friend.
I thank you for your trust. Rivenspire will be safe and life will go on.\n\nTell Gwendis that I'll miss her. That I'm proud of her. Farewell, my friend.
It is the only way to make certain that Rivenspire is saved. Molag Bal will take the relic into his realm.\n\nRivenspire, all of Nirn, will be safe.

She left. Said she had to search the farm houses.\n\nAre you stalling, or do you truly believe we can trust the soldiers of Evermore? Isabeth spoke of an alliance too before she left. Well, you can finish her work. Will you take <<1>>'s head or not?

I'm not surprised. Verandis and I go back many years. He has a habit of making people nervous, but I've been trying to reassure Baron Dorell and Countess Tamrith—he is loyal to the people of Rivenspire.\n\nDid you also defeat this … Reezal-Jul?

The Reachmen have been dealt with? This is tremendous news! \n\nI'm not surprised to hear about the Imperials. They were attacking Southern Bangkorai before, and I knew they wouldn't stop there. Perhaps now, my undead army can drive them back.
Why else would they have brought me back? It's all starting to make sense now. \n\nThis is my destiny. Our army of the living was defeated, but my army of the dead will prevail.

That seals the deal then. We should make preparations. I'm feeling stronger by the minute. \n\nDame Valyrie is just over there trying to figure out where the undead are coming from. Tell her what you told me.
I don't know for certain, but when you said it, something about it just feels right.\n\nDid this voice in the crypt say anything else?

He wants the answer to the riddle of the inscriptions. He'll tell me my answer if I'll give him his answer. Or something like that. It's maddening!\n\nStibbons would know what to do, I'm sure. He was always good at seeing what's right in front of me!
Are you? I admit, I'm not one for direct confrontation. That's more <<1>>'s style.\n\nI've long preferred to fade into the background. Which I'll do, unless you have anything of value to say.

Alive? He's been missing for the better part of the year. Everyone thought him dead.\n\nI've long suspected he lives, and have an inkling of who holds him. Tell me the name of his jailer, and I'll know if you speak the truth.

My brother is in a cave on the other side of <<1>>. Good luck reaching him. He has many soldiers at his command, and he's not much for talking before acting.\n\nAnd you should hurry, before he sets his plan in motion.

The Blacksap Rebellion needed my family to begin, and now it lives in the heart of the people. It will flourish, in time. But I'd rather be at my father's side when it happens.\n\nI did surrender, yes? Shall we be off?
What worked on the bloodfiends? I'm ready to take notes.
An interesting suggestion, but no. Assuming the plague is spread through blood, all you need is fresh corpses. Make sure to use fresh ones though—the plague spreads only if the blood hasn't dried up.
Sacrificed? Like in dead?\n\nWhat do you mean he sacrificed himself?

No! Why'd you let him do that? Do you know how hard he worked to distance himself from the Prince? If Verandis is still alive, the Prince won't give him up easily.\n\nBut why did he leave me here? I would have … I should have gone with him.
How do you know what he wanted? He was everything to me!\n\nWhy didn't he tell me what he was planning? Why didn't he let me help him?
You must rescue me. And I, in turn, must rescue you.\n\nYou must escape from this cell. Take up arms and protect yourself. Then, find Lyris Titanborn.
Aha! How mercenary! You hear that <<1>>? Your agent wants gold! And will have it.\n\nI am relieved. I thought you might ask me not to call the Thalmor. This will cost me much less, in the long run.
I thought you might have something in mind, seeing as you went through all the trouble of procuring this precious jewel. Name your price.

Ah, clever and loyal. A rare combination. Very well, I prefer not to have the Thalmor looking over my shoulder anyhow.\n\nInstead, we will invest in Jode's Chariot! Our coffers still need guarding, yes?
Now see here. Your lack of confidence in me is quite unjustified. I know exactly what I'm doing.\n\nAll right, stand back! I've no doubt these results will be spectacular!
Bandits! Something about the land being theirs. As if land belongs to any of us!\n\nPlease, I don't know any more. I just want to get out of here!
Return to the Green. We could lose ourselves in the wind, or kindle in the sun, or join the rivers and wash away.\n\nBut we are slow to choose.

We would return them if we could, but in our captivity, in our desperate famine, we consumed them.\n\nThey will never be forgotten. Every fiber we took from them we remember. In your honor and theirs, we will never take from flesh-things again.

You're too kind! You make me blush.\n\nCome to think of it, I did see him again a few days later, on the south side of town. He was with another man, very thin and pale. Almost sickly. Does that help?
I'm sorry, but I am not in the habit of ogling strange men!

Now, wait a second! Are you with the City Watch? Listen, I'm out of that line of work!\n\nYou want to arrest somebody, that Imperial's your man. I saw him slip into a house right by the south gate, with another shady-looking character. Arrest them!
Sorry, that's all I've got. I'd be willing to bet he's staying on the south side of town, though.
Take it easy, it was just a joke! I don't want any trouble.\n\nListen, I saw that same Imperial with another thug, down by the lighthouse. Real scary looking type. Skin as pale as a wraith.
Last I saw him, he was heading towards the lighthouse.

Very generous! The Imperial was very sneaky, but this one saw him slip inside the lighthouse with another man, very thin and white like a dead thing. They did not think Khajiit was watching, but this one has excellent peripheral vision.
About a stranger he once saw? This one is in the habit of minding his own business. Only the curious whisker gets caught in the closing door!

You're very sweet to say that. \n\nHe scurried off in the direction of the stables, if that's any help to you. And he was with another man, deathly pale with deep set eyes. He gave me the chills, that one did.
He was heading towards the stables. Truth be told, I put him out of my mind until just this minute. I don't even know if I'd recognize him if I saw him again.

See here! I had no idea the man was wanted by the authorities! He didn't ….\n\nWait! I remember, now! He was with another man. Gaunt and pale as a ghost. They opened a storm cellar door near the stables. Do you think they were burgling the place?
Nothing else to tell, I'm afraid. It all happened rather quickly.

The prince has risen as well? This scenario grows more foul by the hour. \n\nWhat befell King Eamond and his son was tragic, but I cannot imagine it so offends Arkay that he would break the natural order.

I don't know. I should see Prince Adrien. That's the only way to ascertain if he's truly touched by the god.\n\nIn the meantime, it might help me to commune with Arkay if we stopped the dark spirits from defiling the other monuments.

A question we'll be asking many times as we investigate the breadth of their conspiracy against Wayrest.\n\nFrom what I've heard, the Pellingare children were raised under the mentorship of Investigator Garron. Could've been his influence.
I'll not speak to you, you swine! Murderer! Gall and pox upon your family! Sheor curse you, and all who know you!\n\nI'm not answering anything until I obtain lawful representation!

Well, the legend says that the Dragonfires were created from the blood of Akatosh and given to Saint Alessia. \n\nWhen a new Emperor is crowned, they're supposed to relight them to prove that they're a true heir of Alessia. One of the Dragonborn.

What's so special? That's like asking what's so special about the sun up in the sky or the flowers in the fields.\n\nI've been in love with Guen ever since we were little children. She's grand and glorious, and she smells like a spring day!
Ack! Oop! The stupid cup! Anyone who drinks from the cup turns into a Goblin!\n\nAnd the cup's owner can control them.
We had contract. And the lady … pays well. She wanted stupid cup.\n\nShe needs to know … the cost of recovering the cup.
Where do you think all these … ack! … Goblins came from? Malofar betrayed them and turned them into a Goblin army!
No. Feel more … Goblinish every moment. Fate. Destiny. And … another Goblin fancies me.
It's too late. I think the cup's magic is forever!
Don't drink … from the cup! You don't want to turn green!\n\nMaybe the lady should drink … drink from cup? That would show her!

Nothing—if the investigation proves he's done nothing wrong. Irnand and I have only implicated his children.\n\nThe city and the Master's fellow nobles will no doubt want this ended as quickly as possible. But ….

He took a blade to the midsection, but he'll survive—and he sends his thanks. We both do.\n\nThere's no telling the chaos that would have erupted in the city streets if you hadn't stopped the Pellingares.
But the Wayrest Guard lost a lot of lives today.\n\nI'm going to make sure justice is done.
Ancient Khajiiti wisdom as old as Jone and Jode! Greedy-Gut has proven it. When this one sneaks into hungry people's rooms at night they are always awake.
A relic of this power? We're likely not the only ones after it. Someone else could be going for it. The sooner we get to the source of power the better.

We saw skeletons digging up corpses and piling them up in the mausoleums as death shrines.\n\nFather Quiston believes that cleansing the mausoleums with holy water might have some effect. I'd hate to leave the prince though. Will you go?

Justice? <<1>> invaded our land and killed our people, all in the name of the false <<2>>. The only justice is in the soil, where her Jade Butcher slaughtered our people.\n\nAnd now that very soil will rise up to take back what is rightfully ours!

Y'ffre's children loathe the outsiders who pick away at the Green. Until the Blacksap sit on the throne in <<1>>, <<2>> itself will rise against the invaders.\n\nThey weep for <<3>>. The death of my father drove them to this.

Well, we didn't leave each other on the best terms last we spoke, I suppose. I'd nicked his bow, you see, by Right of Theft and all. He said he'd show me the Right of Fist and pummeled me until I gave it back.\n\nQuite uncalled for, I say.
Look how the relic responds to our runestones. Maybe if we use both of them at the same time, the release of energy might destroy the relic.
Our constructs already rise to take back <<1>>. Those who follow the Green Pact will see the forest rise against the Dominion invaders.\n\nFitting revenge for the Jade Butcher's work.
Dangerous? For us, perhaps. But think of the danger this relic could bring to the rest of the world. Worlds, even!\n\nBesides, we never wanted to live forever, right?

You can't stop anything, it has already begun! The Dominion camps will know the pain and fear <<1>> brought us, one long bloody year ago.\n\nI only regret one thing. I'd hoped to end the Jade Butcher myself. To honor the memory of my father.
Lies! Our best sorcerers spent a year searching for any sign of him.\n\nBut there's no trace. My father is dead.

Oh, you know, general heroics and all that. Swords for hire, protectors of the weak, beacons of truth and justice.\n\nOccasionally we'd stab a man in the back for the right amount of coin, but that was more of a side thing.

Indeed. <<1>> and I'd been chasing a mark of ours all the way down here from Bravil. We lost him in the jungle and decided to split up and ask around. Haven't seen <<1>> since, and I don't expect to at this point.\n\nMy nose will be happier for it.
Believe it or not, I think I actually remember the way back! That's all I remember though …. Except the fact that Lorelia needs me!
Thank you!
No! I don't remember you either! What am I doing here? Is this place safe?
All right. Release me and I'll go … somewhere.
Because she needs me! And I need her! She's all I've ever known. Please, just let me go!
Praise you, friend. Praise you.
I don't know! I don't understand. \n\nThey kept saying they wanted me to remember. Remember what though? All I can recall is being with Lorelia. I need to get back to her even now.
Thank you. I'll remember you. I promise.
Oh, good. Nothing I enjoy more than talk of conspiracy. Did the ambassador have a manifesto? They usually have manifestos.\n\nNo matter. I trust you resolved it?

We avail the sick and those too weak to care for themselves by whatever means present themselves to us. Sometimes this means acquiring food. Other times simple company is enough.\n\nWe do what we can, however often we can, so long as we are able.
You have <<1>> as well?\n\nIt doesn't matter. The Dominion camps will fall to our constructs and the people will rise behind the Blacksap. I won't listen to your lies about my family.
You mean besides fame, glory, and the right to brag about any and every thing you do?

If the Undaunted know anything, we know how to fight. Stick around and you might learn some new skills.\n\nThen there's the armory. We hold some of the finest weapons and armor in all of Tamriel. It's not free, but only Undaunted have access.

We are here to relive the past. In <<1>> we saw a squad of soldiers on the run for their lives. Here, at Abagarlas, that same group was calm and in control. Together we can see what they saw, and discover what they knew about the Mortuum Vivicus.

The Ancients stood against the Vivicus and survived. Now, Molag Bal makes ready to unleash the same relic against Tamriel again. It is my hope the courage of the long dead will save the living of today.

After Mzeneldt, I researched a way to take control of the visions we saw. Ostarand was the Ancient soldier charged with bearing the Prismatic Weapon into battle. It is through his eyes you will see. And, in turn, I will see through your eyes.
Surprising. That water was blessed by a priest of Arkay. Perhaps they're charlatans.\n\nThat's enough material for the first chapter. Now for the second.
Interesting. Physical fire affects them more strongly than magical fire. What didn't work so well?
Well, it was worth a try anyway. Nothing ventured, nothing gained. You venture and we both gain!\n\nThat's enough material for the first chapter.  Now for the second.
As expected. Silver is a powerful tool against the undead. Makes sense that it works against bloodfiends as well. Still, I'll put it into the book for readers who might not know.\n\nWhat didn't work?

So, we know how to hurt bloodfiends. But the disease that creates them, the bloodfiend plague. We need to know more about that, how to prevent it.\n\nThere are bloodfiends in Moira's Hope. Go there and figure out how to prevent the disease.

He called off his fiends. Then he … did something. Said words, made gestures, and suddenly I felt as if my blood was on fire. \n\nHe laughed as I collapsed, congratulating me on accepting his wonderful gift.
It's too late for me. I'm fighting <<1>>'s blood-curse with all my heart, but I'm afraid it won't be enough.

Yes, yes, that's me! You must be another of my brother's friends! He's always looking out for me. Did he … was he able to send any gold this time? I'm almost out of the balm I bought with that last purse. He's so generous and kind to me!
No! Nedras … dead? Nedras always did what needed to be done. I was so sick … Why didn't he tell me? He said he was doing odd jobs, some mercenary work. We could have found another way!
My brother died over a handful of gold in some fat merchant's purse. For some balm that might … maybe make me more comfortable. This isn't happening. How could he let this happen?
What? Of all the inconsiderate, stupid …. Where has he gone? Tell me!
He left Rivenspire? He left me here, all alone? How could he do this? I thought he cared about me!
How should I know? Do I look like a man who contemplates evil deeds in darkness? I'm too old for a world grown so strange.
It'll be hard to miss. It's not outside the ruin, so it's likely in a grand chamber and heavily guarded. Be wary.
Yes! Did Klaandor send you? Where is he? When will he be here? This is so exciting! He's been gone so long.
By the Eight! A vampire? That … that mule! That ass! Do you have any idea how long I've been waiting for him? We had something wonderful together … and he goes and gets himself killed? As a vampire!
What? No! He couldn't have …. What happened? How did he die?
An … an amulet? Thank you for this, I guess. It's lovely. But it's no substitute for Klaandor. Tell me, please. Where is he?

"As soon as he can?" That's it! Do you have any idea how long I've been waiting for that … that mule? We had something wonderful together, no doubt about it. But this is it. It's over between us. Maybe I'll learn a new tradecraft ….
Kala knew this was coming. Yenadar has been away too long. He would have come home to his sister if he could. What has happened?

That … that is Kala's brother. He would have rather died a thousand deaths than let his cowardice kill another. Thank you for being honest with me, traveler. I know he would have wanted me to know the truth.
No! Yenadar was such a quiet, pious man. How could someone so good, so innocent become a vessel for a dark spirit?
He's done what? Of all the things he's done for his faith … this is madness. Kala is beside herself now. Where has he gone? Tell her.

He went to preach in an Altmer city? Those racists will turn him into a rug! Kala cannot believe he'd do such a thing. Thank you for telling her, traveler. This one must arrange passage to the port of Haven at once!

"Unhappy?" That's one way to put it. More livid, I'd say.\n\nThe problem is <<1>>'s promise of help. From what I've seen, she's not the type to shirk commitments. Yet almost a year later, and no Khajiit embassy.

No. For many years, I dreamt of escaping the current that carried my life, but it demanded I swim upstream, and such a sacrifice I was not willing to make … until now.\n\nI suspect Brigibeth will not make the sacrifice, and she will not change.

Good question. You wish to serve the Camoran throne? You can start by asking <<1>> why his people aren't fulfilling their promises. He's the one who seems to have the entire Elden Tree lodged up his flue.\n\nI can say that. I'm the king.
Wrong? My brothers and sisters sold their goods to shaveskin knights. Before this one could twitch a whisker, the knights lost all those goods to dull-clawed Imperials.

Not according to Breton crab-shells! "We are all citizens and must bear this loss together. You cannot expect full pay for lost goods." \n\nBah! Knight weasels! We are not citizens, and they are the ones who got beaten by dungy Imperials. Ziss on them!
Each knight went to a different site rumored to contain a relic. Matthiaume went to Flyleaf Catacombs, Edweg to Sanguine Barrows, and Cesabelle to Lorkrata Ruins.
Well, I can't say for certain since I've never actually heard a troll before.\n\nI heard a blood-curdling roar … I suppose it could have been an Orc, though.
<<1>> is not too far from here. Here it is on your map.\n\nYou're not a Dibella worshiper, are you? Wait … on second thought, I don't want to know.
Look, it could have been Dibella cultists in the midst of a … ceremony. The point is, I'm not heading out near that mine for a while because it scared off all the deer anyway.

It was a bloodbath. I saw more troops slain in one hour than I'd seen killed in the rest of my life. \n\nSo, yes—it was "pretty ugly." But I did my part. Still not sure how I got through that slaughter alive.
Don't be disingenuous. I saw you admiring my tail. \n\nDon't try to deny it. Your lecherous leering disgusts me.
Not all Khajiit are lusty doe-eyed kittens, you know. Even if I was interested, you could never keep up … ziss! Eyes up here!
Funny name for a dreadful place, isn't it? It's one of those Ayleid ruins you find scattered about the region. The Bitterhand took it over recently. Been using it as a base ever since.
Creative! I like it. So, what didn't work, what failed to stop the plague from spreading?

After the Imperials tortured me, I played dead. They threw me out to feed the jackals.\n\nMy skills have never been tested more so than these past few days. I've kept watch on their camp, biding my time, which is how I know about <<1>>.
Be creative. Figure out how to spread the plague and test methods to prevent it. My shop has items for sale that might help.
<<1>>? A friend. A rival. We compete for the same business, one might say. In any case, she doesn't deserve to die that way.\n\nI'd rather kill her myself sometimes.

This place? I don't think it is, but they're making use of it. Not enough of their own workers, so they conscript anyone they come across.\n\nAnd they happened to come across me and <<1>> arguing not far from here. Caught us by surprise.
Yes. Good. She's amongst some tents, tied up like a goat. If it weren't so serious a matter, I'd find it amusing.\n\nI'll meet you by the mine entrance. Thank you.
Hard to believe they could smell worse. So, garlic is out as a preventative.\n\nHow quickly did the plague spread?
Interesting. Silver hurts the undead, but it doesn't ward against the disease that creates them.\n\nHow quickly did the plague spread?
Faster than I thought. Good information for my readers to know.\n\nDid you find anything that prevented the infection?

Yes. Three times in recent days. Crazy Eye was only here for the last raid, but she saw them coming, even put an arrow between a few pairs of eyes.\n\nThey still managed to steal more supplies though, yes? Very tricky are these unclawed skeevers!

Here at Martyr's Crossing? Important trade routes run through here between north and south Bangkorai, yes? And supply lines from Evermore to Bangkorai Garrison!\n\nThis one was told that the Knights of Saint Pelin have always guarded this place.
Possibly, though I'd like to take time for a more detailed inspection.\n\nHow long was I asleep? Is Lady Laurent all right?

A statue? Are you jesting? No, I can see you're serious. \n\nI recall nothing. I seem to be intact, although perhaps a trifle stiff in the joints. I could certainly use a strong … that is, I believe I have a bottle of medicine that will help me.

No one knows. Crazy Eye surely doesn't!\n\nThis one's heard rumors of Imperials attacking cities in Southern Bangkorai, but this is too far north, no? Maybe they're trying to attack supply lines to the garrison?
Probably from Bangkorai Garrison. That place has fallen, yes? Many knights were killed.\n\nCrazy Eye is careful not to talk about it in the camp.

Crazy Eye doesn't know, but some of the knights said they might be remnants of Imperial army that occupied Bangkorai Garrison.\n\nWhen that place was liberated, maybe some of the Imperials escaped, yes? Maybe they need supplies to get home.
Whenever you are, my friend. I just hope there are a sufficient number of tears for you to rip apart. I'd hate to get trapped within Lleraya's veil with no way out.

Story goes that there was an Orc warrior, long ago, that came through the region looking for spoils and battle. He met his end in the ruin, dead at the hands of an Ayleid lich. \n\nOnly thing they found of him? His finger bone. The name stuck.

You dare to question your king? The sheer audacity!\n\nBut you are only a soldier. You see battle from a personal perspective. As king, I command the battle. I watch from above as with the eyes of a hawk. I see what is and what will be.
The future? Not only can I see it, but I can alter it to my will!\n\nWe shall not only win this battle, we will win this glorious war!
Hircine gave me power beyond other werewolves when he chose me for his Packmaster. I can control my form, and I am as much a wolf as I am a man.
Hircine is the Daedric Prince of the Hunt and the Father of Manbeasts.\n\nIt's a rare and precious gift he's given you—a chance to become a true hunter, one of his own.

Then go to a temple, and find the priest. He'll be all too happy to cure you, for a fee.\n\nBut if you reject Hircine's gift, you'd best hope the pack doesn't find you again. If you won't be a hunter, you're prey.

Yes. And more yet within the Garrison's walls. We tried to gather as many of the wounded as we could, but the hail of arrows was just … endless. We had to leave the wounded on the field until the battle was over.
A runner arrived bearing news that Emeric's Lion Guard is en route to reinforce us—perhaps led by the King himself. \n\nWe'll see if it's true soon enough, I suppose.

So we must say. Defense of the Garrison is our chief responsibility and we must retake it. \n\nBut frankly, I don't see how. We haven't the supplies or the manpower. We just have to hope this rumor about Emeric has some truth behind it.
Throw the weapon into the center of the construct. Molag Bal's dark plot will be at an end! Don't be afraid … I will keep you safe, my comrade.

For starters, it drew knights away from the garrison. That's part of why it fell so easily.\n\nThe other problem was that we stockpiled supplies here we couldn't protect. They're gone now though. One more raid and we might as well retreat to Evermore.

For starters, it drew knights away from the garrison. It's been retaken now, but it never should've fallen.\n\nOther problem was that we stockpiled supplies here we couldn't protect. They're gone now though. One more raid and we might as well retreat.

Goblins? Certainly not! I've been studying the local gargoyles—I believe they're the key to certain Yokudan myths and legends. It's my own theory.\n\nNow, I'll need you to retrieve my supplies, and then perform Stibbons' duties in his absence.

My alchemical gear is at the new camp, through these ruins. You'll have to find where Stibbons set it up. Be careful with it, it's delicate.\n\nOnce you've collected that, we'll move on to the old camp.

By Saint Pelin's beard! Course there is! Biggest problem right now is the Baandari. \n\nI've got wounded knights, but my healers can't heal them without supplies. I know the Baandari are sitting on a bunch of poultices. They need to share.
That's what I was hoping. Old Silver-Paws over there is the one calling the shots for them.\n\nSee if you can convince him to cough up some of those poultices. We've got lives on the line here.
No, no! Do you think I have not thought of that? Codswallop!\n\nInvert your concepts! You speak like a child licking its first fish.
No, no! You are blithering! \n\nConcentrate, seeker! Ignore the importunities of the hovering eyes of flame, as I do!
You will enter Hircine's Hunting Ground… my master's realm. There, my master and pack will judge you. Should you prove worthy, you will be granted the chance to join us.\n\nGo. My master calls.

Of course not. The Knights of Saint Pelin set up an outpost here to protect the trade routes. The Baandari's livelihood depends on us keeping Martyr's Crossing safe.\n\nWe shouldn't have to pay them to help protect it.

You think the supplies are all they wanted? Not a chance. Those fobbing bastards want to drive us out.\n\nThey're trying to break the supply lines between Evermore and Bangkorai Garrison. They'll keep raiding until they do.
We have to figure out where they're coming from first. So far, the Imperials have been raiding at night.\n\nI sent scouts to try to track them, but they never came back.

It has been an honor to save the guild I served in life. Now, the council has assembled. You should speak to them. Unless Hakruba has changed a great deal since my death, she won't like to be kept waiting.

Reconnaissance! But keep your voice down. No need to wake the good captain.\n\nAnd know what I learned? There's not a single guard in Northpoint. Not a one! Lleraya ordered them to get out and to keep everyone away.

Isn't that enough? I was fairly proud of that bit of espionage.\n\nBut you're right. There's more. The good captain here let slip that there's a smuggler's tunnel. Leads right into the heart of the city. It's our best option for getting inside.
O Merciful Mara! Please say this isn't so! I knew the king should not have come! Why should he risk his life this way? \n\nWhat will we do now? Someone has to go after him!

I don't know what to think. There was a time when I would have followed King Ranser into Oblivion, but since Markwasten Moor, he hasn't been himself.\n\nIt seems his hatred for Emeric has completely consumed him.
Well, the smugglers who use the tunnels installed a gate. Gives them a monopoly on the black market in Northpoint. \n\nThe tunnel will get us into the city—if we can get past the locked gate.

The smuggler boss is a tough pirate. Goes by the name of Lagra. If anyone has a key, it's her.\n\nBut the Montclairs attack any boats that approach the city. There are wrecks up and down the coast. If Lagra's still alive, that's where we'll find her.
Are you crazy? No one gets out of this mine alive.

Hircine demands tribute. Hircine demands meat.\n\nBring down the largest beast you can kill, then howl to your brothers and sisters. We will feed on the prey together. If Hircine accepts your tribute, you are one of us.
I can't do it. I don't owe the others anything, and certainly not my life if we're caught.

My family ruled <<1>> for generations. But after we lost everything, where was my birthright then?\n\nThey wouldn't bow to me as they should, so now I've made them bow. It's the burden a true leader must bear. I shouldn't have to die for it!
He tells the truth. We both know the way, but we have a mutual friend I'd like to free before we take our leave.\n\nWith your permission, of course.
He'll do. Go kill <<1>>! \n\nI'll get <<2>> to our friends before he bleeds out.

No, though I assume we'll all wish I was. I've been <<1>>'s assistant for years, but I can't do a tenth of what she did.\n\nI heard someone wants to try to use the Orrery, so I came looking for her … but she's gone.
<Esmaeel has no pulse. Deep bruising around his neck suggests he was strangled.>
<<1>> said he's on the hill looking out toward the desert.\n\nI'd go with you, but someone has to carry this big baby to safety. Good luck.
The rapids have grown swift, and we did not even notice. Let me explain. Do you remember the notes you took from Doshia's lair? The ones that spoke of the Vivicus?

You must go to the forge. Help <<1>> restore the Prismatic Weapon to its full potential. I will do what I can to find where he has hidden the Vivicus. Comrade, I put my faith in you. You must tell the others, warn them. Can I count on you?

I don't know for certain. She does have a second home in Southpoint, but she wouldn't have left if she knew she was needed to activate the Orrery.\n\nMaybe I'm wrong. Perhaps she got word already and went to the Orrery herself.
All right. I really hope <<1>> is there. Otherwise, I don't know what we'll do. I'm ready when you are.

Oh, a personal invitation from the High Queen of the Aldmeri Dominion, eh? Only she isn't High Queen … not until the Orrery says so!\n\nWell, disappointment's a danger of being young. I'm sure she can take it.
As you say. I do owe you for settling that business in Southpoint, so a little walk through the ruins won't hurt me.\n\nI'm ready when you are.

Only that the Orrery hasn't been fully functional in years. And while you may have dragged me back to Elden Root, I'm willing to bet a year's supply of rotmeth it won't be so easy to get spinning again.

He leads the Redfur Trading Coster. Every merchant who passes through Redfur pays him a small stipend to conduct business here. \n\nThey expect a certain amount of protection from thieves in return. Jode's Chariot maintains order in his name.

Strength, speed, and guile. I know them well. He sent you to track them. The hunter's test, which I once undertook myself.\n\nThough I've not been dead for very long, I will answer your questions as a final favor.
Find Merric and the council. They are probably still in their moot at Vulkwasten. They need to know about this and they will heed your word. Aelif shall remain, and search for more clues.
Find Merric and the council. They are probably still in their moot at Fort Amol. They need to know about this and they will heed your word. Aelif shall remain, and search for more clues.

The aspect of guile is the hunter. He'll be the hardest to track, for he wants no prey to realize his nearness.\n\nBut every hunter must rest sometime. Seek his camp, and if you are lucky, the hunter will be there.
The aspect of speed takes the wolf form. You may surprise it within its den, but only if you are careful.\n\nLook for its pawprints, which may appear as stars on the ground in this realm.
The aspect of strength takes the form of a bear. Crouch low to the ground to search for signs of its passing. A creature so large doesn't leave a subtle trail.

A reputation for being easy on thieves tends to attract thieves. The newer thieves don't give back to the people. They leave town and take their stolen goods with them.\n\nThat's no good for anyone. <<1>> may have to step in.

Doubtful. I defeated the wyrd, I'll defeat you just as easily.\n\nThe power of the briarheart will be mine permanently. Soon, I'll retake Evermore and all the land which once belonged to my people. Your kind will be stamped out, and I will rule all!
That's what you think. Come and get me! The briarheart, this grotto, Evermore, and all these petty kingdoms will be mine!
You've proven yourself a true hunter. And Brinarch? What of him?
Only one supreme hunter would be left, and with Brinarch defeated, we can take back the grotto.\n\nGo, and luck be on your side. We'd assist, but it would be forbidden.

A clan of bears has always safeguarded the grotto. They recognize us as equals and allow us to pass. When we found the Reachmen here, the bears had become hostile. They refuse to let us in.\n\n<<1>> discovered this the hard way.
It frees them from enslavement, as their minds are clearly under <<1>>'s control.\n\nThe bears know their true purpose. Once a spirit is free, it should travel to the wards and seek to empower it.

They serve to protect us as we perform certain rituals to Hircine, and without them, we are vulnerable to attacks by the bears.\n\nWe haven't used them in quite some time, but an important ceremonial hour approaches and we need to perform our rites.
No. If they were, it would have requried a great many sacrifices to maintain.

The briarheart is a powerful gift which makes an almost invincible foe. And we suspect <<1>>'s target would be Evermore, which makes this an issue for your kind to address.\n\nThe Reachmen conquered the city before, and will want it back.

An infestation of thunderbugs. In twenty years studying the kwama, I'd never seen anything like it.\n\nIn the span of a single night, the whole mine was overrun. There's nothing to be done about it now.

It wouldn't do any good now. Most of my kwama were killed. The rest are extremely aggressive now that their nest has been breached.\n\nStill, I'll at least get one good chapter out of this, right? "Night of the Thunderbugs." Well, the title needs work.
Thank you, my friend.\n\nWhile many have attempted the tomb's gauntlet of traps, none have returned to tell the tale. There are many dangers ahead of you. Be careful.
Go to Jode's Hall and speak to <<1>>. If I am right, she is no happier about <<2>>'s decision than we are.\n\nOnce you are inside, you must retrieve what treasure you can and return to me, here.

I won't slow us down, if that's what you're asking. But I don't have much time left, my dear friend.\n\nThat's why Wylon has dragged us to this awful place. He refuses to accept the truth and seeks to defy the will of the Divines.

He's my husband. I believe in everything he does.\n\nBut is this the way I wanted to spend my last hours? Of course not. I had hoped to ease his grief by trying for one last miracle. I fear, however, that when this fails things will only be worse.

My pride and joy! A trading coster sprung up from ruins thought lost to Valenwood long ago! A bustling hive of merchants and customers!\n\nIt has its faults, don't get me wrong, but nothing a little coin can't fix, no?

In Senchal, thieves flaunt their abilities and keep each other in check. They give to the hungry, keeping little more than what they need to survive.\n\nHere, they hide in the shadows benefitting no one. They are not all this way, but such is the rule.

Well, one cannot be successful without attracting a few … undesirables, yes? In Senchal, I would be glad to feed a few thieves. They feed the hungry and keep things interesting! But here, in Valenwood ….

An exception to the rule. <<1>> makes a good show of the Senchal life. If not for him, I would have brought in the Thalmor long ago.\n\nBut times are tough. Each day one of my merchants is fleeced of his wares … this cannot be allowed to continue.
After my death, I hit away the crown to deny Ranser his rule. If you wish to have it, you must come and hear my story and end the curse on this Tor.
I am Saryne Dralen, noble of House Dralen and Master of Coin.
Well, the last time I looked, my hold didn't lead into the city. Wait a moment. My key!\n\nIf you're one of those Montclair bastards, I won't go down without a fight. Now give me back my key!

Tales say the heart holds the power of Y'ffre, the same energy used to create the world.\n\nBrackenleaf blesses the Briars with some of this power, but as a gift. In turn, we protect the heart from those who would steal it.

Well, you're a tough one, aren't you? All right. We'll do it your way.\n\nI was coming back to get my key. I need to get into Northpoint myself. Rescue my gang. Why should I let you have the key when I have my own needs to consider?
First, you must experience the history of our kin, through our mother, Lamae Bal. How she was first defiled, then forsaken.

Najan. He finds yet another person to do a husband's work for him. Pathetic.\n\nDon't concern yourself with my wounds. The door to the ruins has been sealed by an Ayleid spell key. You must destroy the focus stones protecting it so we can get inside.

I thank you for your concern, but I am well-versed in restorative magics. I will recover quickly. \n\nMephala's web grows tighter by the minute. Meet me at the spell key in the center of the ruins once you've destroyed the four focus stones.

Of course. I am relieved already, just knowing that you will go. If there is any trouble there, I know my father could use help, whether he wants it or not.\n\nI'm sorry. I digress. You said you have a question?
This one agrees. If the way is clear, we will run then. \n\nWe will get these poultices back and put the guards on alert! This time, we will be ready for those dungy shaveskins!

Someone has finally asked to hear my side of the story? To learn why these ruins are named for my betrayal?\n\nVery well. Find my remains in the tower. With them, you can see the past. You can see why I betrayed the legendary King Ranser.

At the moment, all I care about is the safety of my gang. They were inside when the city fell. But if this turns out to be a trick, Oblivion won't be big enough for you to hide in. \n\nThe tunnel's in the cove. It will take you into the city.

You need? I don't give a troll's ear what you need. My gang is in there! They were waiting for me in Northpoint when the Montclairs sealed the city and attacked my ship.\n\nI need the key so I can get inside and rescue them.

And I'm the black market magister of Northpoint! But my assets happen to be locked up in the city or waterlogged at the bottom of the ocean.\n\nFine. Take the key. Get the city open and I'll make it worth your while. Especially if my people are safe.
All right. Business is business. Take the key.\n\nThe entrance to the tunnel is in the cove. It leads up through the lighthouse and into the city.

And you just expect me to trust you?\n\nLook around. What has trust ever gotten me? I trusted I could sail safely into port, and my ship was sunk. I trusted my gang could conduct business in Northpoint, and now they're locked inside.
Ah, thank you then for putting my mind at ease. I am in your debt.

Me? I'm the Keeper of the Hall. I am guardian of the gate between here and there, between this place and the next.\n\nThe living don't belong here. I'm supposed to keep them out, but I seem to have failed at that.

That's what Stibbons does! And just for such situations as this, I suppose.\n\nWell, nothing to do now but head back and see if the Mages Guild can help him. I do hope this doesn't affect his ability to make my favorite fish stew.
Yes, of course it's me. Who were you expecting? Molag Bal?
And just between us, thanks for warning my lady about the dangers of the cup. Otherwise, she'd want to experiment—and that usually means something terrible happens to me.
We'll keep them here until the king says otherwise. Better they're thought missing than known to be alive or dead. The Blacksap leadership won't know what to do.

As long as you don't mind rowing. Captain Marck already let me do all the rowing on the way in. Such a gentleman. Yeah. I wouldn't expect any rowing from him.\n\nWe're ready whenever you are. Just say the word and we'll push off.

What would you have us do? Give them a public trial? This is a delicate time for the king, and <<1>> has too many sympathizers in <<2>>.\n\nPerhaps one day, when things are more stable. Until then, they can rot in here.
Agreed. They're traitors, and traitors deserve no sympathy. They'd spend the rest of their days in this hole, if I had any say.

Well, the captain's convinced we still haven't shaken that string of bad luck that started back in Stormhaven.\n\nThat's a load of dung though. We got a new crew and a new ship, the Dawn Posset. What more does he want? Beats the Oblivion out of me.
Then let's get the Oblivion out of here.\n\nCome on, Captain. It's your turn to row!

I don't know. He came into a pretty good-sized pile of coin not long after we saw you in Wayrest. Bought all kinds of cargo with it—legitimate cargo—things he's hoping to sell at other ports.\n\nWe haven't sold anything yet, though.
Right, then! Let's go see what Lleraya's doing in there.\n\nBut brace yourself. I don't think we're going to like what we find.
Northpoint … it just feels … empty. I sense life in there, but it's faint. Barely perceptible.\n\nWe need to be ready for anything.

Dutheil's madness drove him to make a Daedric Pact. He agreed to work as an artisan of Oblivion—to plot and design for the Daedra. He became their Mad Architect.\n\nIn return, the Daedra hunted us, Dutheil's enemies, killed us. Tortured us in death.
We did what we thought we had to. The others may regret it, but I do not.\n\nSpeak with them if you want to waste time on events past.
He's of the opinion that we ruined him, when we simply … balanced the competition.

You have seen how the hunter is also the hunted. Well, in the same way, every Briar begins as the Outsider, a stranger who does not belong.\n\nOnly by dying or completing the final test and joining the Briars is the Outsider defeated. Are you ready?

That's what I like to hear. You like to fight, don't you? I get that. When I was younger, I felt much the same.\n\nGo burn the bastards' boats then. I'll say a prayer to Saint Pelin for you … for all of us.

Varen Aquilarios—the son of a Colovian duke, who led a rebellion against the Emperor Leovic and took the crown himself.\n\nAlas, Varen was not truly Dragonborn, as those who sit upon the Ruby Throne must be, in accordance with tradition.

The king has no fear of <<1>>, or any of the Blacksap!\n\nBut perhaps showing this to everyone will put that rumor to rest. Once we've learned all we can from them, I'll advise the king hold a public trial. No promises, but my word carries some weight.

Perhaps you're right. Rumors of his weakness on the matter have been … persistent.\n\nAll I can do is advise the king when I next see him. But my word still carries some weight. I'll recommend a public trial to show he doesn't fear the Blacksap.
The Agea Relle was built as a school for those who are adventurers at heart, who wished to travel the breadth of Tamriel and discover its secrets for the sake of it.

Hm. You'll want to speak to Ufa, then. Too bad no one knows where he is. Even if we did, can't say he'd even want to talk to you, seeing as you're a stranger.\n\nYarah might see you, though. She's upstairs, on the balcony.
And don't think you can try anything. I'm not just here for my good looks, and Yarah is more than capable herself.
And I hear the Imperials have spies everywhere. So why would I admit to being someone they want to kill?\n\nThat said, I know one thing Imperial spies wouldn't do: arm their enemies.
Why would I want those weapons? I'm no friend to the resistance, or to the Imperials. I just want to work in peace.

Across the way is a guarded warehouse. If someone took weapons from there, it'd be a blow against the Seventh Legion. And I hear the stablehand knows the people who need such weapons.\n\nSomeone who did that, I could trust.

Is that so? Let me fix them for you, then.\n\nThere. No one will suspect you carrying sacks smelling of the stables. Ones who need these wait in and near the town square. If you're caught, we've never spoken.
Red? I have seen such a cat, though not lately.\n\nDo you bring news of this red hunter, or something else to ease our sorrow at its loss?
Red fur, you say? Yes, running across the rooftops in the sunset. A hunter and protector, long missing from home.\n\nHave you heard tidings of our lost friend? Or do you bring something in its stead?

One of the destitute, no more. I have nothing, except my eyes and ears. And I see Yarah wants to trust you, but she cannot. Not until now.\n\nShe will look for signs of treachery, and find none. But even that will not be enough.

One of our allies passed with a peculiar bag from the stables. It's good to know you were the one to supply it.\n\nWell, then. I think it's best if we go our separate ways. Though you helped considerably, I can't take this risk again.
Unimportant! But here is how she will.\n\nShe waits by the tavern, as she was spying on you. Go to her, clasp her hands, and tell her that the Red Asp lives.
It's more of a feeling. Call it intuition. It's better if you see it with your own eyes.\n\nCan you come with me to my home? It's best to continue our conversation in private.

The Imperials may know your face by now. You can disguise yourself as one of them for the time being. They don't dare raise a hand against me, so I'll be all right.\n\nIf you're ready, I'd like to go now. Follow me, but be discreet.
Everything the intrepid need to survive.\n\nWe offered courses on the eclectic cultures of Tamriel, outdoor survival, weapons and armor training, and I personally taught the disciplines of magic.
Fish? Why do you want my fish? I only have one left and it's right here in my pocket.\n\nI had to fight off that little monster to keep it and I'm certainly not going to just give it to you!
Smelly? Old? Not my Petunia! She's a prize catch! How dare you insult her!\n\nI think you should leave now. Let me wobble along in peace.

Oh, your pet is lost? Is it a little puppy? A cute little kitty-cat? Never mind. It doesn't matter. I love cute little animals! Here. Take Petunia. You'll find your lost pet in no time!\n\nJust watch out for that lizard-chicken thing. It's a monster!
I don't know the name, Gasteau might, but its fascinating to see what can be accomplished unfettered by the rules of the natural world.
<This pedestal is meant to hold a scroll.>

I … stole designs from him, after Saryne arranged for the Wayrest nobles to deny Dutheil further projects.\n\nGasteau presented those designs to the nobles as renovations for the Royal District, as original works.
<This pedestal is meant to hold a scroll.>

Truly? You were so honest about <<1>>. I would not have expected you to associate with the Hollow Moon. Such is life, I suppose.\n\n<<2>>'s messenger said he had a plan. You play some part in it, I expect?
Is he mad? Why would he ask for such a thing? He knows the danger!

Yes, I see. The treasure of <<1>> could certainly be persuasive. It may be our only chance of keeping the Thalmor out of our affairs.\n\nI'll give you the key, but please be careful. I don't want your death on my hands.

I'm afraid not. To have any chance of making the Orrery function, we need someone who knows how to run it, an element of the divine, and the only source of energy powerful enough to make it work, the <<1>>.

That is up to <<1>>. If she wishes to give up on leading the Aldmeri Dominion, we're done here. But I seriously doubt she'll want to surrender her goals so easily.\n\nShe sent her brother here to deal with potential problems. Talk to <<2>>.

We can, thanks in great part to you. <<1>>, despite her rough exterior, is truly excited about the chance to get the Orrery running again. You did us all a great service when you settled that business in Southpoint, allowing her to return here.
Talk to <<1>>. The Queen sent him here with instructions to summon her when everything's ready.\n\nI'm not certain how he'll react, but he has his orders.
<This pedestal is meant to hold a scroll.>
<This pedestal is meant to hold a scroll.>
He thought the two of us were having an affair.

He was wrong, of course. But his accusation cut deep, just the same.\n\nAlmost as deep as the torture he inflicted on our souls—for years. To this day I'm not sure why he believes it, except to say the Daedra must have whispered it in his ear.

Then you have already achieved in life that which gave me great difficulty.\n\nMy father's influence, though, was only one aspect of what guided my life's purpose. In truth, it was my mother's role, the sacrifice she made, that defined my destiny.

Yes! It is as I said. She has worked herself night and day. And Sheogorath's dark intellect is focused through those tomes. They are like a stain on her mind. I think we have to … wait. Do you feel that?

You have noticed as well, then? She has worked herself night and day. And Sheogorath's dark intellect is focused through those tomes. They are like a stain on her mind. I think we have to … wait. Do you feel that?

The Outsider is the deathless enemy of the Brackenleaf. It returns again and again to steal the heart of the Brackenleaf, only to be destroyed by the Briars. This and more you will learn in the trials.
There's no defending what he's done. To me, or the others in the school.\n\nBut I failed to save him from himself. Given the chance, I would try again.

The same. Long before you were wailing in your momma's arms, Hircine gave me the keeping of his pack and all the power that goes with it.\n\nI show pups like you how to make the most of his gift. I'm like a flea-bitten, shirtless priest of Hircine!

You want to be a werewolf? Maybe you're a little crazy yourself. \n\nThis portal will take you to Hircine's own hunting ground. If you're ready to hunt and kill and feed with your pack, then step through. I'll see you on the other side.
He made a pact. A Daedric pact. Nerien'eth was proficient with magic, but he could never do all this on his own.\n\nI could have stopped him before he completed it. I should have.
What did he say? Did Sai tell you where he is being held?
Then we must locate him before Mannimarco forces him to reveal the Amulet's hiding place.
Did he? I thought he had firmly aligned himself with Mannimarco and his Worm Cult. Curiouser and curiouser.
Adusa regrets a little. But such power—it would corrupt even the most-noble soul.\n\nNo, better the relic exploded into tiny bits than to let its power loose in the world.

We are a part of the world around us. The animals, the flora, the earth … all these respond to us, and we to them.\n\nWhen they hurt, we hurt. When we're content, they're content. Everyone's part of the world we share, though not everyone cares.
Now that the focus stones are destroyed, I can deal with this infernal spell key. We should be able to enter the ruins in short order.
As I said before, the spell key is a brittle and aged relic. I'll weave a simple enchantment and that should be the end of it.

You misunderstand. My husband is <<1>> of the city guard. I think he betrayed us.\n\nI couldn't bear to ask him. To see the hurt in his eyes and the shame that must surely be there. But he's keeping something from me, and I fear the worst.
Oh, Qismah! I wish I didn't have to keep such secrets from you!\n\nBy Mara's heart, I don't know who betrayed us, but it was not me. I am little more than an Imperial lackey now regardless!

The Imperial fool Quatrius believes he's invincible. And in a way, he is. If one were to raise a blade against him, his soldiers would surely cut down the child out of spite.\n\nBut there are other ways to cow a man.
We're simply enjoying the fresh air! After all, who would want such a flower to wilt in a dungeon?\n\nNow, begone before I have my men remove you.
I am truly blessed to have such aid from a stranger. With no promise of reward, you saved my family!\n\nHere, take this key. You will do far more good with it than I.

Soon after the Imperials came, our daughter disappeared. And my husband speaks with the Imperials, carries sealed messages back and forth. I don't know what to think.\n\nSearch his office. It's upstairs. See what you can learn. I can't bear to look.

They have her. Our daughter. The Imperials kidnapped her, and hold her as a hostage.\n\nI debase myself before them for her safety! And I would do so again, if it means she will be returned to us! Now go, please.
Not how, but where!\n\nGo to the pavilion in the shadow of the palace. You are already armed! Armed with the knowledge that he is a coward! With that, you must defeat him!
What? That's complete nonsense … er, I see your point.\n\nWell, what did you want from me?
