The grandeya's chains. The Imperials made me capture her and bring her to them. I fear they want to publicly execute her in order to cow the citizens.\n\nIf anyone can save her, it would be you. A thousand blessings upon you.
They have the grandeya? That is troubling news.\n\nYou've been busy, then. But what news of the traitor? Do you know his identity?

Because you're going to go back out there and let them know where we are. And see if you can figure out where Lleraya is hiding while you're at it.\n\nI'll get the place settled and make sure we don't attract any unwanted visitors.

Watch your arse out there. I mean, did you see all the vampires and bloodfiends?\n\nWell, you better hurry. We don't want to leave His Lordship and Her Ladyship alone out there too long. It isn't safe.

And by seeking our blessing, you show that you deserve such an honor.\n\nThe one who breached the chamber—this Septima Tharn—she has strength, courage, and even wisdom, but she lacks an essential quality of a true Ansei.

Ellic and I haven't always seen eye to eye, and he's made no effort to hide his feelings about me in his journal. He does mention the arrival of Lady Lleraya, though.\n\nI'll tell you more when we gather with the others. No reason to repeat myself.
Chirane Manor? I know it well. Nice to see we finally found a good use for that pompous ass.\n\nI'll meet you there. We'll discuss the contents of my son's journal when the entire team is together.
Arkay guides our way, as usual.\n\nAre … are they all like this? The people of Northpoint? Did Lleraya turn them all into … these vile creatures?

May the Light watch over them, praise Arkay.\n\nI can't believe that sweet Lleraya would do something like this to our people. What could have driven her to such horrors? I'll head to the manor and meet you there.

I've found that where there is misery and torment, the Daedra are not far behind.\n\nYes, my husband appealed to the Daedra for power. He got it. Everything you've seen, he used Daedric spells to create.
<This thrice-forged Orcish steel blade was a gift from Mauloch himself to the conquering Orc King, Nargi gro-Barok.>
<Forged in the ancient Crystal Tower in Summerset, this magical blade was a gift from Auriel to one of his most powerful battlemages.>
<A gift from the Tribunal to Saint Nerevar, this Dunmer blade was infused with Vivec's near-godlike power.>
<This is a simple blade used for training.>

Unless the gods decide to strike me down before the battle starts. I've had enough standing around in throne rooms, talking about fighting the Imperials.\n\nI miss the satisfaction of sliding a sword between the plates of an enemy's armor.

I haven't neglected that. I've looked at the garrison's layout and whatnot, and it'll really depend on what we find in there. \n\nI am confident we'll catch them off-guard. So no matter what, we'll have to capitalize on that.

The sad truth is we're not even sure. More than two hundred Knights of Saint Pelin were stationed here, but only a handful escaped. \n\nTheir stories are all over the place. Giant Daedra scaling the walls, the dead rising from the crypt … who knows.

Of course! Battle runs in our blood. You think our family rose to royal power by attending teas, playing games at court, and currying favor with the right nobles?\n\nNo. This king and queen work … at its heart, it's a bloody business.

Enough to be of service. <<1>> hasn't functioned as intended for ages. We planned to use some rather delicate magic to trick it into operation.\n\nBut if <<2>> believes there was sabotage, we must look to an alternative method.

Why, we'll look to the past!\n\nAccording to legend, <<c:1>> required a skilled operator, an Ayleid source of power, and a "divine spark" before it would function. Without all three, it won't do anything but spin. Quite pretty, but not very useful.

Yes. I met her once, back before the Soulburst. I'm ashamed to admit I actually fancied the girl. She was as cold as a Nordic winter of course. \n\nI wonder if she's still attractive though? Regardless, I think her head would look best on a pole.

That old witch was undoubtedly the mastermind. And actually one of the knights who escaped claimed Septima snuck into the garrison posing as a Redguard refugee, and then unleashed Oblivion the next night.\n\nKnowing her, that's quite possible.

I would not be here otherwise, adept. It has been many years since I sat in my study, planning for this day. I laid in the runes and cast the spells with precision, knowing that someday the Mages of Tamriel would have need of me again.
I was assuming they were spellbooks. Tomes on advanced magical theorum, or ancient treatises on soulforging artifacts. Instead, the first book we retrieved was full of nursery rhymes!

Hmm … I don't know what there is to tell, adept. You probably know quite a bit about me already from the lectures the Guild holds regularly about my life. Or perhaps from the numerous books written about my legendary constructs.

That buffoon? Hah! Of course we can. I am the greatest Mage who has ever lived. Valaste is the greatest living mind in the world. And you have already proven yourself incredibly capable. We will best his trials, and reclaim my island!

They're far from nonsense. I'm loath to admit it, but Sheogorath actually was very clever. He disguised advanced spellwork in the rhymes, using reference and allegory to hide his meaning. It took Valaste quite some time to decipher, but she did it!

Hah! You might as well ask a parent which is his favorite child! So many of my little projects became legend. Eyevea, Labyrinthian, the great Ice Fortress of Winterhold … and Glamoril, of course. But I do go on …
First, we need to find out if anyone survived Lleraya's private party. The Countess heard noises coming from the inn. It's not much to go on, but at least it's a place to start looking.

So Darien accomplished something useful after all? Go upstairs and get that key!\n\nFunny thing. Darien was scratched and battered. Claimed the bloodfiends bit him. But the Countess didn't find a single bite mark on him. Guess he was mistaken.

Part of me wants to find Lleraya in there. Then we can put a blade through her and be done with this business. But I really hope the townsfolk have crowded in there and barricaded the doors.\n\nEither way, we need to get in there and see.

The end of my staff, right to the side of his head. Best way to quickly quiet a delirious soldier.\n\nHe was making enough noise to give away our presence, and I was in no mood to fight a horde of those creatures.

Arkay provides, bless us all! I heard sounds coming from the inn as I made my way here. Now we can get inside and see what's in there.\n\nI hope it's the survivors of this terrible disaster. I'd hate to think that Lleraya turned or killed them all.
A key? Yes. He was holding onto it rather tightly. I had to pry it from his grip before I could tend to his injuries.\n\nIs it important?
Almost. You recovered the pieces needed for <<c:1>>'s activation, so it's only fair you're here to put them in place.\n\nSo I should be the one to ask … are you ready?

Good! The first thing you'll need is to take up <<1>>. "A god's hands move <<c:2>>," goes the translation.\n\nBut that's a load of boarslop. You simply need to be in three places at once. <<1>> should allow for that.

Oh, you'll be all right. That overly earnest fellow from the Mages Guild … <<1>>, was it? He assured me you'd be safe if you wore it for no longer than ninety minutes.\n\nOr was it nine? No matter, the ceremony will take five minutes. Maybe six.

Approach the pillars beyond <<c:1>> itself. You must activate each in turn while keeping one thought in mind: when you wear <<2>>, you'll never be held in place.\n\nFrom what I understand, it should do the rest.
A good question, adept. Truly, my greatest regret? I wish I'd spent more time teaching. I always felt my greatest triumphs were the students that followed in my footsteps.
Eyevea was an outlier island in the Summerset archipelago. The High Elves gave it to me in exhange for some baubles, minor artifacts of no real consequence. It was a beautiful place ….

No, not to Vuldngrav. But Skyrim is littered with ruins like this. Leftovers from the age when Dragons and their priests ruled my people. In my younger days adventuring across the holds I plundered many of these dank little tombs.

After we've got the courtyard under control, we'll meet you up there. \n\nOh! And if you see Septima Tharn or any of her commanders, feel free to take them down. I'd love to kill the old witch myself, but you're better qualified.
I do not presume to know. He ordered me to protect refugees on this island while he rallies resistance inside the town.\n\nThis one longs to fight by <<1>>'s side, but I must follow orders.
Ah, the dead. They don't rest very quietly these days, do they? Was she some long-dead Ayleid? An unlucky pirate?

East. Across the bridge behind me. They're just throwing conscripts at us to keep us from getting across.\n\nThey'll run out of fodder eventually, but if you'll lead the charge across on your way to the crypt, we can take the bridge now.
That woman is a menace. I'll have a word with her later. Thank you for mentioning this to me, adept.
Whoever or whatever you may be, I advise you to go away and leave us alone. These people are under my protection, and I will not allow you to harm them.
He was the school's blademaster, a fellow instructor.
That's just what I'd expect one of Lleraya's minions to say. Now leave us alone!
I believe we are perfectly safe up here, thank you all the same. Now go away. You have more than enough victims to suit your needs. I won't allow you to have any more.
Rulanir was an old friend, and my husband knew that whatever pain he inflicted on Rulanir, I would regret.

When Lleraya sealed the city and began turning people into bloodfiends, I used my sword to cut a path to this inn and led as many as I could to safety.\n\nI was forced to kill friends who turned into monsters, but I was able to save some of our people.

Quite a few. And there are more hiding around the city. Protected by members of the Northpoint Guard. I gave the order myself as soon as I saw what Lleraya was doing. \n\nI just wish Lord Ellic had been able to resist her as well.

It started innocently enough. She had Lord Ellic call a gathering at the square. Then she addressed the crowd, saying how the blessing of Montclair would soon be upon us. That we would join her. Love her.\n\nThen people started turning all around us.

Lady Lleraya has taken Dorell Manor as her own. But I have a key. Take it. Save as many of our people as you can.\n\nAnd be aware that Lord Ellic is still with her. He was alive when I last saw him, but completely under Lleraya's influence.

A spell perhaps? I'm not really sure. She made some strange gestures and spoke a few arcane words. Then it was as if a wave of power flowed out of her. People immediately began turning into bloodfiends. But not everyone was affected by her blessing.
Yes. If you are willing to face them, defeating those Daedra will dispel their magic, and allow my soul to reform.\n\nThey ruminate on new tortures in a chamber to the south of here.
A student of mine.\n\nI was fond of him.
There's really only Rondrin, but he's been retired for a while now.

He became the greatest mage the Agea Relle ever produced. Better than my husband, said the Altmeri diplomats who visited during Faindor's graduation.\n\nThe day Faindor was to leave, my husband solidified his Daedric pact. And you know Faindor's fate.

He was the opposite. He was the unruly son of a noble Altmer family, and he resented me and everyone here.\n\nBut he had an instinctual, magical spark that the Mages Guild lacked the patience to stoke.

Had I known what my husband would ultimately become, and what he would do to this school and his students—I would never have built it.\n\nIn a way, I gave the Daedra all those lives. Years of torment out of something that should have been wonderful.
Well, see, if you sit a madman down and listen to him ramble he'll sometimes spout the most brilliant insights.\n\nI don't know if you know this, but I spend a lot of time around madmen.

You've got it! No strings, no "lingering magical afflictions", no nightmare beasties haunting her in her dreams. Ooo … that's always fun … but no, no, no, no. I'll undo what my books did to her. Fair and square. If you deny the Folium.

I'll be honest, mortal, I haven't had this much fun in years! Your struggle to collect the books, getting to poke Shalidor with a stick …. Oh, oh! Do you remember the time I had you close all those portals on Eyevea? Hah! Good times ….
Here, take hold of <<Ac:1>>. Place it in the pillar next to our royal observers. That should do it!

No, I had no idea. And my brother … did he go inside the Orrery? Of course, he must have. That impulsive idiot! He always believed he was destined for more than "just" being my right hand man. But I never thought he'd go this far.
Aye! And they're some right insightful insights they are. You read through my Folium and, hoo! Like I said, worth the power and zip of half a dozen skyshards easy.
On <<1>>'s desk.
You're just in time for our grand celebration! We're celebrating the new and better life that will soon be ours!\n\nLady Lleraya is going to honor us with her blessing, and then we will never die!

Of course. We must find <<1>> so he can club thugs over the head if they try to seize my research.\n\nThat has happened before, you know. My research is extremely valuable in the cutthroat world of academia.

According to everything I've been told, the Orrery draws out the strongest part of a person's soul. A great leader becomes greater. A potential Empress is revealed.\n\nBut in Naemon's case … I worry what part of my brother's soul will win out.

I shudder to think. I love my brother, but he's always been …\n\nListen, if something's happened to change my brother, I don't think I can fight him. He's my little brother. He may need to be stopped, but I don't think I can do it. Can you?
Careful, friend. That's the lovely Lady Lleraya you've just insulted. I'll forgive this first slight, but if you persist I will be forced to defend my lady's honor.

My lady is upstairs. I'm sure she'd love to meet you. And when she tells you about her blessing, about the wonderful gifts she brings, I'm sure you'll fall in love with her. Just as I have. Just as we all have.
Probably, but it's not what you think. We've freely accepted the will of the beautiful Lady Lleraya. She loves us and we're devoted to her every wish and whim.

Just so, my friend. I believe it to be some kind of relic, a massive spell capable of holding and harnessing the souls of thousands upon thousands of dead. If it had been released … if it is released … the world as we know it will end.

You saw through the eyes of <<1>>, one of the valiant Ancients that fought and died in <<2>> to safeguard our future. According to what we saw, it was he who slew <<3>> and stopped the use of the <<4>>.

That's a relief … I suppose. There's some part of me that wants to stay here, but I'd have regrets for all eternity, wouldn't I? \n\nSince I am in the fortunate position of having a choice, I think I prefer you take me back.
What? No, I …. Why would Naemon do this?\n\nI made him a part of what we were building, tried to show him this is about more than just "our people." I would have all of Tamriel be our people.

Isn't it fascinating? You want to strike me, but your weapon hangs loosely at your side. I wonder why that is?\n\nOh, I know! It's because I will it. This is my world now. I feel your desire to please me, and I can use it to make you do as I wish.

You're trying to resist me? Oh, what sport we shall have! But first, I have duties to perform.\n\nCome, join me downstairs. We must attend the celebration. Perhaps I'll even honor you with the first dance—before you try to kill me.

You believe the nobles are in danger? You want to save them? How sweet!\n\nThey love me. They have given themselves to me. Thanks to the Remnant, I am their god. And now I also have you, the hero that Verandis presumed to use against my father and I.
What the legend says. It revealed the person within.\n\nAs it will do to me.
Do you think I have a choice in this? I will enter <<c:1>>, as I swore to the people of the Aldmeri Dominion. I must learn whether I'm fit to lead them.\n\nAnd if I'm not ….

I don't know! They poured out of the ground. The soldiers rushed me back to camp, and now I'm the only one remaining.\n\n<<1>> won't let me venture from the camp, but you have no such restriction. Please, find my acolytes! Some must still live!
Not as far as I know. Every member of the Guild received instructions to detain her if she's sighted. I still … I still can't believe she killed Guildmaster Iceblade. Tribunal protect us.

My son Erthonor helps me tend the shrine here, but he is young and has a young one's whim. More interested in chasing girls and hunting beasts than the worries of an old one like me. Yet his heart is kind and he is dear to me. I do not blame him.

We received no word of a decampment. Our orders were to come here, mind the Mages Guild dig, and await further orders.\n\nBut if it's true … there must have been a good reason to leave the city. <<1>> does nothing without a good reason.
The woman you are escorting … O wayfarer, she is not my sister. The Daedra, Anexiel, has taken control of her. Can you not see it?

I understand. I'm a monster. Nobody listens to monsters.\n\nBut … if <<1>> wakes, he might do bad things to people who live in the forest. I don't want that to happen, not because of me. I want him to go back to sleep.
Because what I'm saying is true! Oh, I've never been good at … speaking my mind. Please, stranger, think of what you've done!

Have I not earned your trust? I've had countless opportunities to attack you … to slay you. But I haven't. Did I not tell you that Mephala is the Prince of Secrets? The spinner of lies and mistrust? \n\nYou are being deceived! You must act!
Hooray!\n\nFollow me inside the ruin. We don't want the shades to hear us. They're his spies, you know.
Oh, all right.\n\nWe should go inside the ruin so his shades can't hear us. I guess.
If there was, I would have told you already!

What's that in your hand? Is that her talisman? \n\nIn my trance I heard a voice. When it wasn't screaming, it whispered about a talisman. A talisman just like that. If you use it on my sister it might draw the creature out.

Look into your heart. Have you been wrong this whole time? Is your compass that broken? I don't offer comfort, but I do offer truth. My sister is lost to that thing. It breaks my heart, but we must finish what we started.\n\nThe choice is yours.
Oh. Nearby, huh?\n\nMaybe I can visit. You know, when I'm free. After we make her lock stronger, so <<1>> sleeps forever.
You did? That's wonderful!\n\nIs she doing all right? Did she mention me? Where is she now?
Oh.\n\nWell, maybe I can visit one day. You know, when I'm free. After we strengthen the lock, so <<1>> sleeps forever.

The Shornhelm Guard was on patrol, trying to intercept House Montclair forces before they could reach Shornhelm. We stopped to check on Hinault's farm, and that's when things got out of control.\n\nWe walked right into an ambush.
Montclair is one of the most prominent noble houses in Rivenspire. Along with House Dorell and House Tamrith, they formed the Triumvirate that ruled the kingdom since Ranser's War.
They struck from the shadows, the Montclair bastards! Caught us by surprise.\n\nThe fighting was brutal, but we were able to establish a defensible perimeter here at Oldgate.

Ancient history these days, but it was only about fifteen years ago. King Ranser attacked Wayrest. He lost. Made his last stand not far from here, at a place called Traitor's Tor.\n\nYou ask me? Baron Montclair wants to pick up where Ranser left off.
A coin? How clever! Who would suspect a simple coin thrown into a fountain for good luck?\n\nAnd see this. There's a message on the coin!

Adusa has her own inquiries to make. You must decipher this code.\n\nSeek out my friend, Sahil. He should be able to help. He's usually on the second floor of the Dead Wolf Inn. He loves to watch the fire burn in the hearth.
No clue. It's in some sort of code. Adusa can't make heads or tails of it. Hee hee. This one made a joke, yes?\n\nHmm. This date. Could it be the key to the code? Here. Take this copy of the message.

Ah, you are a smart one. I can tell you many good townspeople remain inside their homes. Some, out of fear. Others await news. Perhaps they wait inside for news from you?\n\nYou will have to find out the rest on your own, I fear.

He's a womanizing piece of scum who'd sell his own mother to make a few coins. Ask at the tavern for <<1>>, his latest courtesan. She'll tell you where he is.\n\nI should've slit his throat when I had the chance.

Lleraya gathered the nobles here, played with them, forced them to love her. It was the closest she could get to real happiness since the loss of her mother.\n\nWhen she was done playing, she was going to turn them all into bloodfiends.
He's in hiding, the rat. He is named Maradem.\n\nYou'll have to find a way to lure him out into the open if you wish to find him.

Your perceptions are excellent. She used this veil in two ways—to hide herself and to overwhelm your senses with illusion. \n\nUnlike Lorkrata, instead of shredding the veil, this time you used the tear to enter Lleraya's illusion.

With Lleraya's death, the power of the veil fades. As soon as it dissipates, the nobles will appear.\n\nBut now the final confrontation draws near. Gather our forces and meet me at the Shrouded Pass. We must return to the Doomcrag to end this.
Perhaps. Many know Maradem. Not many will admit to it.\n\nI've met him once or twice, but I don't know where he is now.
Do you know what would happen to me if I betrayed Maradem? Or any of my contacts?\n\nNo, I can't help you. Now go away, before someone sees us talking.

It's simple really, I need someone to travel to <<1>> and inquire about my lost shipment with <<2>>, the customs clerk.\n\nIt's incredibly late and the alchemist that ordered it is not the most patient of clients.

You were wise to come to me when you did. The life of a filthy Daedric beast is not one any mortal should choose. A few more days, and you would be beyond my power.\n\nI can cure you. But first, I must ask for a donation to the temple.

Of all the places in this temple you do not belong, it is there you belong the least. \n\nBut I sense that where the others have come to violate the chamber's sanctity, you have come to restore it. I will give you my blessing if you prove worthy.
Then I cannot help you, child. Arkay watch over you.
Thank you. I will cleanse this corruption from your blood. Fear not! Once I am done, the curse of Sanies Lupinus will be gone from you forever.

We still need information from the wretch. Fortunately, I know of a simple way to extract it.\n\nAcross the way lies the Mages Guild. Talk to a man named Razin. Ask him for his specialty; it's a potent sedative only he makes.

I'll set a trap for <<1>>, with my dear Niha's help. Once you have the powder, take it to The Drowsy Owl Inn upon the hill and get the rest of the details from her.\n\nYou can see your destination from here, if you need to get your bearings.
I've no idea what you're talking about. I'm just a simple apothecary, friend.

There's a bottle of wine in the alcove for you, though I've no idea what you'll do with it.\n\nI'll serve it to Maradem, and then you and Ufa can do what you must. But after that, I'll have no part in what comes.
How dare you … whoa. What's happening to me? Did you poison me?\n\nPlease, give me an antidote! I'll tell you anything!
The rogue! Sometimes I wish the Imperials did find him!\n\nHere's your powder. It'll paralyze in a matter of moments after being ingested. Take care you don't breathe it in.

She's in front of the palace! I have the key for the stocks, but they guard her exceptionally well!\n\nThey'll execute her within the week. That's all I know! Now please, give me the antidote! I'll give you the key!
They ready themselves for battle. We will hold the palace while you take out the Imperial within.\n\nWe must all move quickly.
Oh, most assuredly. Not a bite to eat in days. Weeks, even!\n\nWon't you please help me out before it's … too late for my eleven sickly children?
He what? No. My husband has some silly ideas, but he's not … he wouldn't …. \n\nWhat are you going to do?
Oh, thank you, friend! Thank you!\n\nMy seventeen sickly children thank you as well. I won't forget this kindness.
Fine. Be that way. See if I care.\n\nBut know that the empty bellies of seventeen deathly ill children is on your head.
He didn't do this out of malice. He just wanted to support us. He hates that I have to work so hard. He's a good man, but they'll kill him for this!
Oh, bless you! Don't you worry. I'll keep the fool in line from now on.
That idiot! What was he thinking? Oh Divines, have mercy on us.
Keep the codebook, just don't implicate my husband. You have what you need, right? Just keep Edouard out of it. You get what you need, and my husband remains a free man.
Why would she do that? Oh, never mind.\n\nWell? What did you find?
Typical bureaucratic corruption. I expected better of the ambassador.\n\nNo matter, supplies can be replaced. What about the Khajiit embassy? Did she say why construction hasn't begun?

Hmph. I'm surprised we didn't pass each other on the road.\n\nGet to those ruins and find that work crew. I want to know why they haven't done their jobs. I won't have <<1>>'s word impugned by someone else's incompetence.
What do you mean, "collect stone?" That should have happened months ago. They should be ready to build it!\n\nI'll talk to the ambassador myself. Put the fear of the Dominion into her.

Bold. I like that. It's unfortunate you've picked the wrong side. The Legion needs more soldiers with that kind of attitude.\n\nNo matter. Hallin's Stand will be our stronghold in the Covenant, and no upstart shall challenge that.
Did you think I'd let anyone walk in here unchallenged?\n\nYou are a fool, as are the rest of them. I'll enjoy watching you die.
The Imperials had no chance. We took them by storm, and without their leader, they had nowhere to turn. What few are left will fall easily.\n\nYou were the lynchpin for it all!
The grandeya will have something to say too, no doubt. Here she comes now.

Grand! If you could, pick up the shipment and bring it back to me.\n\nI'd go myself, but <<1>> and I … well, we're not on the best of terms. A misunderstanding, but hazardous to my health. Tell her you're there for "Treeshade Imports."
Damn Osgrikh! Damn the stronghold! I left peacefully. I harmed no one, left with nothing but the clothes on my back.\n\nAnd in return they slaughter Esmaeel? Murder him in cold blood?
Naradani has a plan. She will dress up her practice-fighting dolls like Khajiit, then when the dungy diamond-backs attack, Naradani will shoot them from the bushes!
I can track it down for you. What was its intended destination?
Just so. An impressive likeness, yes?
You are right! Fighting dolls still have targets on their bellies … ah! Naradani will paint her belly to match. Genius! Thank you, walker!
Oh? Should I make them thinner? This one has always been very sleek. Everyone says so.
Capture her. Bring her in for questioning. Find proof she's behind this so <<1>> doesn't explode with outrage.\n\nHuh. Never thought I'd hunt a High Elf ambassador.

I'm not interested in whatever shady deal you have with <<1>>. If you want the crate, go take it. \n\nBut he already paid for its transport, and that won't be refunded since we had to charge an infestation fee.
If the shipment isn't destroyed already, it'll be in a pile near the waterfall.

Out in the back with other impounded shipments waiting to be destroyed.\n\nTell <<1>> that the next time he brings in a shipment from <<2>>, he better have it inspected before it arrives in our trading post.

Who's skulking! I'm praying. All devout, I am. Just like Eselde.\n\nOh, not really. I wanted to eavesdrop on the Baron and the Countess. I must say, the acoustics in this place are really quite spectacular.

Yes, the Fighters Guild. We're always looking for sharp blades and sharp minds. Well, that second part is optional, but you know what I mean.\n\nWe hoped to recruit a few knights to help destroy the local Daedric Anchors, but you're a better find.
Now why would you go and do that? I'm just like you. I'm merely here to help.\n\nNow remember, you never saw me!
Was it the import taxes again? I thought I paid those weeks ago. \n\nI was hoping that would hasten the process. My client is not exactly a patient woman, and I do not wish to upset her.

Oh did she? Did she also tell you how she promised that we'd make ten times our normal take by coming to this godforsaken backwater?\n\nDid she mention how she said shipping my supplies wouldn't be an issue?

Excellent! Welcome to the Guild, Associate.\n\nNow—the exciting part. Go out and slay as many Daedra as you can find. If you break some Anchors there'll be a generous reward into the bargain, and maybe even special jobs for you later on. Good luck!
Yes. We have been challenged with a great task, and need experienced wayfarers like yourself.\n\nSo how about it? Will you join the Fighters Guild?

Indeed. The huge chains that have been falling from the sky? In the Guild we call them "Daedric Anchors." I'm not exactly sure why—but I'm just paid to break them.\n\nI have been told they're falling straight out of Oblivion. Most uncanny.

Hard to say without looking it over. Provided it's not one more copy of "The Lusty Argonian Maid," it might well be worth something.\n\nYou're already on your way to earning membership in the Mages Guild. We offer rewards for books like this.

The Mages Guild is dedicated to the pursuit of wisdom and knowledge. It's a difficult, but honorable enterprise. Tamriel has a rich and wonderful heritage. We seek to preserve it.\n\nMight you be interested in becoming a Docent?

Capital! I hereby grant you the rank of Student in the Mages Guild, with all the responsibilities and privileges according thereto. \n\nEvery book acquired, or collection of books completed, will now earn you status within the guild. Good luck!

Docents earn rank by bringing rare books and scrolls to our libraries. As their rank increases, so too do the rewards.\n\nYou look like the enterprising sort. Might you be interested in joining the Mages Guild?
I … suppose you have a point. Ayrenn rules over all Elves—equally.\n\nPerhaps helping us was less an imposition on us and more … more her duty.
What! Why? This is incredible. It's just common mushrooms and kwama jelly from <<1>>, nothing too exotic.\n\nDid you examine it? Does it seem … dangerous?

Kwama? No, this is no good. I don't need that here with all my other fragile shipments!\n\nLook, can you run this out to <<1>> right away? She'll have your payment. And try not to stare at her, she's … easily distracted.

Capital! I hereby grant you the rank of Student in the Mages Guild, with all the responsibilities and privileges according thereto. \n\nEvery book acquired, or collection of books completed, will now earn you status within the guild. Good luck!

Docents seek out and bring us rare tomes and scrolls. Through their efforts, our libraries grow.\n\nIn exchange, a docent is entitled to purchase items restricted to guild members. Docents may also be offered special tasks from time to time.

The shipping was fine, it's the delivery where it fell apart.\n\nMy belongings arrived at the docks of <<1>> without incident. But due to the recent problems in the city, no one has any idea when deliveries will resume.
What? Oh, from that netch scab <<1>>? It's late! It's so very late. \n\nI've resorted to eating troll brains and maggot soup, and my potions have lost their delectable fetid flavor already.

They're having trouble managing the local grass, so I've put them on an all-hay diet. And the climate, it's more humid than they're used to in Summerset.\n\nIf I didn't know any better, I'd say they were homesick.
… You perfidious slime! You'll rue the … what? You're not … and I'm … what happened?

Of course I want it! Just pour it in the stew there. And if anything escapes, feel free to gobble it up as a tip.\n\nIf you want, you can spend time with your old granny Alyxe while the eggs pop and ooze into the sauce.
I would forever be in your debt, my friend. A dozen would be enough to go around, if you wouldn't mind.\n\nAnd I won't mind if they're a little mashed when I get them. Saves me some work!

When they were younger, I'd grind <<mz:1>> into paste and give it to them as a treat. I think it would raise their spirits again.\n\nBut nobody sells <<mz:1>>, and I can't leave my shalks to fade away while I scour the coasts.
<<1>>. Why does that name sound familiar? Perhaps … no, I've lost it.\n\nWait! Where is <<2>>?
I … good. That's good. Then it hasn't been too long.\n\nI really should head back, get my bearings. Don't worry about me! I know the way back.
Wasn't he back at the camp?\n\nI suppose <<1>> would know where he's off to. Always getting lost, that one!
The Dark Father, Molag Bal, has corrupted you. Only Mother Lamae herself may turn you into one of us.\n\nPray she welcomes you into her embrace.

That is my problem. I literally have nothing to say to these people!\n\nAll my stories about the amazing deeds of long dead High Elves …. The first rule of my profession is to know your audience, and <<1>> is not a place to tell such tales!

The caretaker. I preserve everything against the ravages of time. Scrolls and books are easy, but the Ayleids themselves ….\n\nThey resisted at first. But they saw things my way, in time. Have a look around you!

I planned to seek out Wood Elf stories in taverns and libraries, but since we arrived I've heard of countless troubles in <<1>>. The Worm Cult, pirates, Wood Elf rebels … it's all the same, I'd rather keep to the safety of the carnival.

The Wood Elves rarely write their stories down, but I heard <<1>> in <<Ac:2>> Mages Guild is the one to ask.\n\nIf you're headed that way, would you mind asking for a book? It could be written in old Akaviri, for all I care! Anything would help.

There's an <<z:1>> <<2>> stole from <<3>>. Then there's a glowy vial. I don't know what's inside, but if you listen real close you can hear whispers.\n\nOh, and <<Amz:4>>. You'll find those inside some of <<2>>'s servants.
You're all tyrants. Get away from me.
Lleraya Montclair? Yes, she arrived here … she said she was here to help. Then … I can't remember anything else.\n\nIs the rest of Northpoint … is the city safe?
Of course. Give us a moment to compose ourselves and we'll meet you outside.
I … I need to get outside. Find my father.\n\nI need to make sure that Northpoint's all right.
Of course. We hoped the ambassador would hear our voice, but it seems those stone walls are too thick.\n\nPerhaps the sound of rocks against her embassy walls would bring her out.

What? No.\n\nBut if the ambassador is going to sit in her well-constructed embassy, she won't remain oblivious. A few rocks clattering against her walls should remind her of what we lack. Thank you, my friend!

There were a great many—but they've all been freed, now. The ones you saw, Faindor, Rulanir, Anconath … myself. We were the ones he most despised.\n\nThe others were trapped within the walls, to bear witness.
Those wretched creatures slink in the darkness, cowering from the light of Arkay. Fear not, with Arkay's grace I can purify you.\n\nAll I ask is a simple donation to the temple.
Blessings upon you, child.\n\nNow, let Arkay's light burn the curse from your blood.
That is unfortunate. \n\nMay Arkay's light shine upon you.

Mother Lamae was the first of us. Molag Bal made her his unwilling bride and through her brought terror to the night. Through her, he created the vampire kin.\n\nShe is the Blood Matron, mother to us all.

Hmm. My people mostly leave such matters to our spinners to share, rather than writing it down.\n\nI have something, but I can't imagine you'd want an Akaviri spy's writings on our heritage. A "cultural infiltration document." Complete garbage.
Why did you come back here with it? I thought I made it clear. I don't want that stuff around here. Our business is concluded.
Wonderful, that's everything I need! Once <<1>> gets its act together, they can deliver an empty trunk.\n\nYou're welcome to stay for the show. Sit wherever you like!
Fine, fine! Run, girl, before I change my mind!\n\nNow, the guards will be back any second now! Don't think you can threaten me again!

Truly? Then I have all the more reason. If I can get it right this time, we can be a family once more.\n\nI don't want to cause this creature harm. But <<Az:1>> was long ago hidden from me, so I must use cruder methods to control it.

The one bright spot in the room, the Prismatic Weapon … I can forge it in any form you desire! Stendarr himself speaks through my craftsmanship today. What will you wield? A greatsword, a longsword, a staff, or a bow?

The Anchors were a danger to everyone on Tamriel. I received reports that cultists had begun harvesting souls for some kind of weapon. Jofnir would not listen, I had to act! \n\nMy friend, I trust you. As does the council. I put my fate in your hands.
I spent the first half of my day suspended in an elaborate Ayleid light trap that you disabled with a slimy Daedra eyeball. I'd prefer to avoid any further excitement.
Anexiel tricked you. I was the one who was possessed. You finished the ritual, and now it's gone to claim its new body.
I don't know. I thought it needed me. But Izzara was my twin. We were bound by blood. That must have been enough.\n\nTu'whacca be kind.
Yes—it might still be weak from the summoning. Onsi protect you. I'll … see to my sister.
Good. Go after it. We can only hope it's still … still weak enough to defeat in its new form.
What kind of voice?
That sounds like an ill omen.
Curse that monster. This is all her fault. Hers and Najan's. I'll never forgive either of them. Or forget.\n\nCome. Let's get out of here.
Mephala spoke to you? The Daedric Prince? I hope for your sake that it was something else.\n\nLet's get out of here. I can't bear to stay here any longer.

He was young when he had his accident. Too young.\n\nThe creature you've met can't fully comprehend the world around it. Unless properly supervised, it could harm itself or others without knowing what it did. No, to set it free would be a cruelty.

<<1>> is my son. I needed all his remains to craft the husk, so I had to use my own for the scepter.\n\nTo command a spirit, use a focus made of its bones or those of its close relatives. Basic necromantic principle.
I'd like to run some simple tests for signs of Daedric influence.\n\nWhile I do so, would you bring <<1>> with you to search the Hall of Might? I suspect <<Ac:2>> lays within its walls.
Wonderful. If this tome is correct, there's a passageway hidden in the library. I'm sure you and <<1>> will find it.

I broke through <<1>>'s ward just under a century ago. I have remained here ever since, attempting to restore what remained of my family.\n\nI will never leave, as long as <<2>> remains at my side. This is my home.
Yes, each Shadow reflects a different aspect of Rajhin's personality and power. This could be a convenient metaphor, actual living shadows, or something else entirely.

As far as I'm aware, yes. They're in the nicest-looking trunk on the dock. I had it touched up by a painter in <<1>>, you know.\n\nBut with the pirate attack, who knows when <<2>> will be stable enough to deliver their backlog of shipments.
Kaleen is. I'm working for her. \n\nKing Fahara'jad asked Kaleen to come after Naruk personally. He trusts her. We don't want anyone finding out one of the king's spies has gone rogue.
Very little, unfortunately. It may be a divine piece of the god Rajhin, gifted to his Shadow.\n\nWhy he would squander it upon me is beyond my comprehension.

You will see, my friend. In any case, after Aelif's testimony the whole guild was put on alert. They scour Tamriel for their Guildmaster, and all thought of Daedra and this weapon of Molag Bal's falls by the wayside.

She's still sailing. Master Kasan is at the helm while we're away. We've done so well against the Dominion that there're rumors King Fahara'jad's going to promote Kaleen soon.\n\nI hope so. She deserves it. She's done nothing but good for the Covenant.

He's a spy. Or he was until King Fahara'jad joined the Covenant. The king recalled his spies to Sentinel.\n\nNaruk refused. He's founded his own group—the Children of Yokuda. They think the Redguard should rule Bretons and Orcs, not ally with them.
Why would anyone want a piece of a trickster god? The answer is usually power.\n\nBut for what purpose, I cannot say.

I couldn't ask you to lug that heavy monstrosity all the way here. It's triple-reinforced steel, with an inch-thick lead interior. Discourages my competition from snooping.\n\nI just need the supplies inside. If you wouldn't mind, of course.
Saved us? It doesn't feel like I was saved.\n\nBut Verandis always carried a great weight on his shoulders. Maybe that's been lifted from him now. I can only hope, right?
That persnickety vampire really came through in the end. He was a good man … for a vampire, I mean.\n\nWe won the day, and that's what matters. The people of Rivenspire are safe now.
Before we go, you need to talk to Gwendis. She's not taking this well. \n\nI even tried my sad face. It usually works, but she almost bit my head off. Anyway, we'll see you back in Shornhelm.

Just barely. We made it out right before the damned mountain came crashing down.\n\nI still don't know what kind of magic you did up there to defeat Montclair, but remind me never to get on your bad side.

Aminyas may have been a xenophobic, dour old Elf, but he's at least thorough in his arguments. \n\nAs for Morgaulle Dechery … it might help to inject some romance into the piece, since the woman was so obviously taken with King Joile.

It's a magnificent city right in the middle of nowhere; only the gods know why the Redguards even built it.\n\nBut it's changed hands many times over the centuries. Not a subject to bring up when you have Fahara'jad and Arzhela in the same room.

Ah, sweet Septima. I may have mentioned before, I actually met her when I was just coming of age, tagging along with my father to Cyrodiil.\n\nI took quite a fancy to her, but she mocked my advances most cruelly.

I believe they were aiming to conquer all Bangkorai, but we've shown them that's not going to happen.\n\nSeptima's likely plotting revenge now, but who knows? Her family's so corrupt with power and necromancy, their motives hardly make sense anymore.
You? I'm a decorated general of the Aldmeri Dominion, a hero to my people. Who better qualified to wield the power of a god?
You won't regret it! Unless you hate stage performances. Then you'll regret it.\n\nBut hopefully you'll enjoy it!
I'm afraid you will have to decide that for yourself. \n\nI must focus on searching for a way to repay Lyris's bold sacrifice. I cannot simply abandon her to the wrath of Molag Bal.
Would you look at that! Just the smell of the things seems to have perked them up. I'll see if I can use them to motivate my little friends.

Queen Arzhela, of course. It's part of Bangkorai. Come to think of it, I don't even know why Fahara'jad wants it. Doesn't he have enough desert cities?\n\nYou'd think he'd be lobbying for more territory in the wetlands for Mara's sake.

Other than arguing on how best to take down an Imperial Legionnaire? Just making preparations for our next expedition. We lost a few fighters in recent days and I don't want to repeat the same mistakes.\n\nDestroying a Daedric Anchor is no mean feat.
No! You're trying to trick me. Trick the trickster god … ha!\n\nI can see through your lies. I won't give it to you, or anyone! You'll fall to <<1>>!
For the Dominion … for its armies. For those with the strength to lead us against our foes.

Knowing my brothers are safe back in Daggerfall is an amazing feeling. I mean, the Spearhead crew is my family, but my brothers are blood. I don't know what I'd do if I lost them.\n\nI can't ever thank you for your part in saving them, but I'll try.
I buried my brothers. I didn't have enough for graves, but Kaleen helped me. She knows what it means to sacrifice for the Covenant.\n\nI don't want to talk about it.

Do you think I could go there? Would she be happy to see me? Or would it be like the last time, when she thought I was a monster?\n\nI don't want to be a monster. Please, make my father go back to sleep, so I can be free.
The half-giant, Lyris Titanborn. She leads this uprising. I do not know how or why she is here, but to the Soul Shriven, she is a gift from the Divines.
Don't blame me, my dear. I don't pick the fake names. If I'm Sigil, that makes you Arrowhead. It also makes you very late.

My father was just a merchant lord from Cumberland, come to kiss the Emperor's ring—I didn't realize it, but I was hardly a match for a Tharn.\n\nEven back then, Abnur Tharn would never have allowed his niece to be courted by someone like me.

None save the old fashioned kind. We'll talk to the city guards. If Kaleen left Shornhelm, someone was bound to see her. You don't strut like her and not attract attention.\n\nIf Naruk nicked her, we're in trouble. He's not a nice man.

Kaleen's here? Well, that makes sense.\n\nWhen one of your spies turns on you, it's best not to spread it around town. King Fahara'jad would want someone he trusts. Seeing as you're here and she's not, I take it Kaleen's gone missing?

He's got a mess of sworn swords camped in the sewer beneath Shornhelm. Children of Yokuda. They're planning something nasty.\n\nI was going to sell my info to Arrowhead, but now that you're here, I seem to be working for free. Shame, really.
It's an ancient Ayleid artifact that allows control over water. Very useful, but in the hands of a water creature like a Nereid, very dangerous.

There's still a market for sensitive goods, and I'm doing well enough. Might even have enough for another ship soon, if Telonil keeps working his magic.\n\nThis job was supposed to put me over the top. Guess that'll have to wait.

Mekag's off with Lambur. The whole relic fuss never sat right with him. Haerdun and Deregor are still with me, along with Telonil.\n\nWe left Kaleen's crew shortly after the Dominion hit Daggerfall. I like my sailing without giant fireballs.

The man is easy enough on the eyes, but I'm not looking for a fling right now. \n\nJakarn may think he's in love, but I know his kind too well. We'll see if he's still interested when I have my own ship.

Funny story. Irien sends me letters. She says Jakarn's taken a fancy to me. She says he even wrote me a poem.\n\nI told him flat out I wasn't interested, but that seemed to have the opposite effect. He's turned into a lovelorn fool, Irien says.
With the Stone, the Nereid has more control over water than she's ever held. It's no wonder she's controlling the local villagers. We need to get it back before she does real damage.

Oh, yes. Vimy sends letters. She's quite the gossip. Neramo's dig off Stonefalls dried up, but he found mention of ruins in the Alik'r desert, so he's headed there next.\n\nI've never understood what's so interesting about a bunch of missing dwarves.

He went further into these caverns. It's an old route between the deserts of southern Bangkorai and the more temperate northern area.\n\nYou don't suppose he's gotten lost, do you? That wouldn't bode well for his reputation as a guide, would it?
First things first! Let's find <<1>>, especially as he left me bereft of my goods and gear.
You can call me that, or Miss Eiman, or Akatosh. Doesn't matter now. I can see why Fahara'jad sent his pet privateer to handle this mess, but why did he send you? What's your part in this?

The same way I'd find anyone else. Ask around. I'd start with the city guards. They're taking note of new faces in town, what with all the bloodfiend problems.\n\nSeeing as I'm done here, I'll go with you and keep daggers out of your back.

Hmm. You lack the crazy eyes, so I'll gamble you're not with Naruk. I didn't know Kaleen was my contact, but it makes sense.\n\nArrowhead—Kaleen—was supposed to be here hours ago. If she's not, I'd wager Naruk caught her.

He and his Children of Yokuda cling to the old wars. Redguard against Breton and Orc. They've set up camp in the sewers, and they're planning something.\n\nArrowhead was going to help me stop them. I suppose that falls on you now, doesn't it?

I did see a woman like that—hard to miss her. Strode up the road like she owned the place. She came back shortly with another Redguard, shifty eyed sort. Spoiling for a fight.\n\nI confronted them, but the woman assured me everything was fine.
They headed into Shornhelm. Didn't watch them after that. My eyes stay on the roads, nowadays.\n\nNever know when a bloodfiend will want a snack.
I did see a couple, now that I think of it. Don't see too many Redguards in Shornhelm. They went up the eastern road.
Don't recall. But if you're looking for someone, you should go roust Lazy Ludippe. He never misses a coin purse.
Oh, I might have seen them, sure. But maybe I didn't. Memory's not so good any more.

Yes, this is where I found him, already a lich. I had come here, to where my children died, to mourn.\n\nGarron said he tried to protect them from the likes of you. That he was slain in the battle, and was forced to use his necromancy to return.
His name in life was Garron. He was a Wayrest Investigator, and a mentor to my children.\n\nHe was there for the battle that killed them. Said he could bring them back. All he brought were monsters.
<Nothing happens.>
Oh aye, that'll do it. They went inside the house behind me and didn't come back out. Seeing as the house is abandoned, you make of that what you will.
Easy now, easy! I saw them, sure. They went into the house behind me, but they ain't come out.\n\nI don't want no trouble from you. Or them, for that matter. I'm just trying to get by.
Izzara was right. I failed her. She was beautiful and kind-hearted. My foolishness killed her. Sep take me ….
I … I don't know. I just don't know.\n\nAdeena … my desert star. I've lost her forever. And for what?

Not until after it killed the woman I sent into harms way! \n\nIzzara faced spiders, Daedra, ancient magic. All I did was stand here and bleat like a lamb—afraid to face the thing I set free. Ancestors forgive me ….
Leave. Maybe I'll walk into the desert and put an end to it. I deserve worse.\n\nI should go to Adeena's family first. To apologize. I won't ask for forgiveness though. I'm beyond such things.
This book … it's written in Akaviri.

Everyone knows the Ayleids left many secrets behind, and the more we understand about them the more we learn about what remains. Their language is part of this, and as the Ayleids migrated and split, variations of their language emerged.

Correct. We already know there were cultural differences between the Ayleids of Cyrodiil and those that settled in Valenwood. Their language varies too, and is less understood than the more common Cyrodilic. Any writing we find here is significant.

I did. His story touched me. He helped to teach my children, and I believed he possessed the honor to die for them.\n\nSo I accepted his offer to bring them back. I didn't think it would turn out this way.

You mean this land of buzzing gnats, ticks the size of ponies, and Elves who look at anything with meat on its bones as a potential meal? Oh, no, I just love it here. Still, the research is what matters. I could really make a difference.
Osgrikh leaves me no choice. My husband is dead, killed by a hate-filled mongrel, and his honor must be served!\n\nOsgrikh wants to live in the old ways? I'll show him how to die in the old ways.

I'll swear my own oath to Malacath. With a blood sacrifice.\n\nOsgrikh's siblings, Thrug and Larzgug, were with the Oathbound that took us. They should work nicely—help me get their heads and find a ritual site, and I'll handle the rest.
Naruk saw through me. I'm not … cut out for spycraft. He had questions, and figured torture would loosen my tongue.\n\nHe doesn't know me very well.
He wants to start a war, force King Fahara'jad to conquer the Bretons and Orcs. In his twisted way, he's doing what he feels is right for Alik'r.\n\nLet's kill him, shall we?
He didn't tell me … but I saw barrels of poison and a sewer map. He's going to poison the water below Shornhelm.

It's the ritual. I did not have the heart to speak of it before, but I can't put it off any longer.\n\nThat fool Najan told me that the Daedra has been abducting people. It is, no doubt, collecting them for a summoning ritual.

None. They are beyond help. I beg you to look on this as a kindness. Their souls will find more comfort in Aetherius, I assure you.\n\nTake my talisman. It will make it easier. Use it on any victims you find. Be a true hero and set them free.

Excellent. Welcome to the guild, Associate.\n\nNow, to business. Hunt and slay as many Daedra as you can find. If you manage to break some of those anchors there'll be a reward waiting for you, and maybe even some special assignments. Vivec guide you.

Yes, of course. But the people of Hallin's Stand have their own troubles. They haven't exactly turned out in droves to join us. \n\nJust as well, I suppose. We need only the very best. You look like you might fit the bill. Interested?

Stop kidding. Surely you've seen them.\n\nThe Anchors are the most recent Daedric horror unleashed on us by our friends in Oblivion. Huge chains fall from the sky, then hundreds of Daedra pour out. It's actually impressive, in a scary way.
Finally! One who understands this Khajiit! If only this one's neighbors could be as accommodating and wise.\n\nThe High Elf should listen to you.

That is my primary function. The Mages Guild is a society of scholars dedicated to the pursuit of knowledge. Unlike, say, the Imperial Army, we seek to improve the state of Tamriel through learning.\n\nAre you interested in becoming a Docent?

Not yet, but given time, certainly.\n\nYou may not be aware of it, but by bringing this in you're on your way to earning membership in the Mages Guild. Did you know the Guild provides rewards for acquiring books like this?
No one in Grahtwood understands the Khajiit. This one is so tired of it!

If she left the embassy, she knows someone's on to her. She'll go to ground, try to flee … have someone smuggle her out of <<1>>. We should probably stop her.\n\nMeet me by <<c:2>>, at the base of the Elden Tree. I'll be there shortly.

That would be most satisfactory. I think you will make an exemplary Guild member.\n\nI hereby grant you the rank of Student. Every book or collection of books you acquire will now enhance your reputation with the guild. Best of luck to you.

Docents are our eyes and ears, seeking out books and scrolls to add to our libraries.\n\nIn exchange, a docent is entitled to purchase items restricted to guild members. Capable docents may also be offered special tasks.

A wise decision! I hereby grant you the rank of Student in the Mages Guild, with all the responsibilities and privileges according thereto. \n\nEvery book acquired or collection of books completed will now earn you status within the guild. Good luck.

Exclusive things you won't find anywhere else. Docents earn rank by bringing rare books like this to our libraries. As their rank grows, so too do the rewards.\n\nWould you be interested in this opportunity?
The sewers beyond the Fighters Guild. I saw it on his map. Follow me. There's no time to waste.

We must stop this mysterious entity from stealing our lord's forbidden knowledge.\n\nThe entity's wisps absorb mind essences from the Rain Disciples. Kill a wisp and take its essence to the troughs. I hope this will expose the entity's intentions.

Yes. Even in the ancient days, some Ayleid recognized the power of Hermaeus Mora. \n\nWithin this shrine, they stored forbidden knowledge of the natural order, which could allow one to manipulate the very fabric of reality on this plane.

You're bold to ask. As you observed, I am a Dremora, but the Lord of Knowledge freed me. \n\nHermaeus Mora taught me the secret of how to sever my ties to Oblivion and bind myself to the Mundus instead. I have served him ever since.
I serve Hermaeus Mora; dealing with illusions and obscurities is what I do. \n\nExposing these vague quantities, turning confused innuendo into clear knowledge, this is my lord's realm.

I had assumed that this relic she spoke of was a legend. Even when I heard the words of Ostarand, Endarre, and their companions, I thought this was a threat from a time long forgotten. But …comrade, we just saw it. The Vivicus was never destroyed!

You saved Merric from a Worm Cult plot to harvest souls, remember? Those souls are fuel for the Vivicus! The intact Mortuum Vivicus that Molag Bal has kept hidden all this time, safely tucked away in Coldharbour!
<The bookcase shudders a bit as you perform the sequence that allows entry.>

In time long past, this was the Agea Relle, where I taught the trade of adventuring.\n\nMy husband, Nerien'eth, has broken it, made it a Crypt of Hearts, where my spirit, and the spirit of my students will suffer for as long as his magic lasts.

Of course. We are known as Primeval Seekers. We rarely gather, but our lord has summoned us here to secure the ruins.\n\nI'll warn you now—some sections of the ruins below are restricted—Primeval Seekers will attack if you attempt to trespass.
Gobani and I know when we have outstayed our welcome, yes? \n\nA night in the stocks might not be as bad as losing a paw, but all the same.
Very well then. Which blade is it?

We came here to do just that, but we soon discovered others were living in the ruins—these Rain Disciples. \n\nWe have secured portions of the ruins, but the entity who commands the Rain Disciples set them to block other areas. We know not why.

If Shan-ra calls in the Thalmor, that's the end of Jode's Chariot. They won't be necessary any longer.\n\nBesides, Jode's Chariot has always respected what we do, even if they do arrest us from time to time.
Smugglers, skooma addicts, and more than a few criminals. They keep to themselves, but sometimes they band together to repel outsiders.\n\nKind of like a filthier version of the Dominion.

Our goal is to find <<1>> before she buys passage out of <<2>>. Staying in the shadows, avoiding unnecessary conflict … that's what I'd do.\n\nBut there's a lot of ground to search. I'll follow your lead.
As we entered this passage, I stopped for a moment, and <<1>> continued on.\n\nBefore I could turn around, a very large spider bit my leg and I fell, unable to defend myself.
There is a reason he hired a guide. I've heard him call for me, but it seemed he walked in circles and came no closer.
I am tired, and my muscles ache, but I am otherwise in good health. Had you not come along, however, the tale would certainly be different.

I walked near our camp and my guide, <<1>>, disappeared. I called to him, but ended up lost. After wandering in circles, I finally ended up here.\n\nHave I been lost for days? Weeks? I can scarcely tell. And where was Azei while I suffered?

I hired him not only as a guide, but as my protector. He performed admirably, till now.\n\nIn any event, I hadn't a knife, or any weapon on me. He had all our gear. If he'd been attacked, I'd have been hurt as well.
I'm certainly glad he's alive! The ruins await us!\n\nBut I'd like to get my gear and change clothes first. These rags unpleasantly chafe my most tenderest of skin.

You're working for that skeever <<1>>? The last shipment he brought through from Cyrodiil was rotting minotaur heads! The wagon stunk so badly we had to burn it. \n\nYou know, I should toss his shipments on arrival.

Oh, that crate. I checked it myself … it was making some sort of odd noise. A chirping, if I recall.\n\nIt's clearly contaminated, so we threw it out in the garbage heap for disposal. It's not worth the risk to our couriers, you understand.

Out in the back with other impounded shipments waiting to be destroyed.\n\nYou can pick it up if you want to assume the risk, but I cannot guarantee your safety. However it is one less thing for me to deal with, so feel free to pick it up.
Oh, good. Nothing I enjoy more than talk of conspiracy. Did the ambassador have a manifesto? They usually have manifestos.\n\nNo matter. I trust you resolved it?

Splendid. I'll allow you the honor of informing <<1>>.\n\nWhy not tell him the duly selected High Elf ambassador was working against the very Dominion she pledged to support? I'll sit in my throne and try not to gloat.

The cultists worship the greedy lord, Hermaeus Mora. They would hoard the secrets buried here; they do not wish us to make use of them.\n\nThey will do anything. They have even been capturing our disciples and holding them prisoner.

Just to hinder our efforts. That's why they sent you as well. \n\nI'm sorry you've been caught up in this. I won't ask you to join us, but surely you can see that our disciples have done no wrong. Would you be willing to free them as a favor?
I appreciate it. Take this wand and use it to disrupt the portal. \n\nBe careful, though. Don't try to fight everybody. It'll be a waste if you die before closing that portal.

They are people from Evermore, Northglen, or other nearby villages.\n\nLike myself, they were drawn to Lorelia. She showed us what was happening and taught us that her plight, the plight of the lake, is our plight too.

This is the Yokudan Heritage House. Some might call it a library, though it is far more than that. \n\nThis is where the ancient thoughts of Yokuda abide—whispering to us from beyond the Far Shores. Music, poetry, philosophy—all can be found here.
This one will try to satisfy your curiosity.
You don't understand. They've … done something to me. I can't leave!

<<1>> claims to do research. Much of this research means breaking, entering, and taking. He sends everything to Cyrodiil.\n\nLeft to himself, he'd send entire ruins there, destroying much of our history.
What? Me? Let me see that.\n\nMalacath's Orichalcum Spear! The fire was no accident?

We sell "Tamriel is Doomed" survival kits. These are packs of basic survival supplies like dried fruit and bandages. I manage the money, <<1>> is our Prophet of Doom, and we scare enough locals to make a healthy income.
We didn't. At least, this one didn't. We set up shop in <<1>>, but the Imperials wrecked the place. <<2>> insisted we could escape through here.\n\nJone and Jode told her all about it. Ziss!
Thank you. It works pretty well. At least until <<1>> gets spooked by one of her own stories and bolts for the tall timber. Then we have inconvenience.

Because she is kin to Sheggorath! Sure, her terrified ravings drive our sales, but at some point she always heads for the horizon. We have to go after her, and end up somewhere in East Flea-Bite hiding from imaginary flying slaughterfish or somesuch.
She said something about an ancient Redguard travel altar that the shaveskins would use to escape. Sounds like skooma dreams to me. If you find her, you can ask her.
He wandered away from the central cavern, and I know he did not head south or he would have passed me by.\n\nTherefore, he must be headed north on one of the passages out of the main chamber.

For us, these books are like blood and flesh. Each and each is a beautiful thread in our cultural tapestry. \n\nWe do not trouble ourselves with useless trivia. You'll find no Dwemer machinery manuals here. This place is uniquely and purely Redguard.

By my father's head! To the dogs with that coterie of charlatans and heretics. They pretend to be scholars, but it is a fiction. To them, books are merely trophies. They regard their shelves as a hunter regards a mounted head. \n\nDisgraceful.

If it is secret doors or hidden chambers you seek, you must look elsewhere. We do not deal in treasure maps here. \n\nIf you've an interest in the history of this place, however, I am happy to oblige.
Happy day! Help this one perform the rite that will enable escape from the vampire skeevers. \n\nThat is why Imperials invade Bangkorai, you know. Vampire skeevers.

For the Fighters Guild! You should join up. Our new guildmaster is an Argonian, Sees-All-Colors. She has us all working to a singular purpose. We're hunting down the Daedra and their damned Anchors. Hard fights.

Enormous chains descend from the sky! A passage opens to Oblivion, and Daedra boil out to lay waste to the countryside. I don't know who started calling them Daedric Anchors, but Mauloch knows it fits.

Hah! Good question. We train our members in special techniques. And the higher-ups are always looking for motivated members to help with special projects. Colors herself might even have a task for you someday.
Then let me be the first to officially welcome you as a comrade in arms of the Fighters Guild! Get out there! And take the fight to the Daedra!
This one marks your map to rune stone. You are true friend to this one, like <<1>>!

This one finds one of two rune stones needed for <<1>>. That is an ancient Redguard device to get the user—me—safely out of Hammerfell!\n\nWill good-looking new friend get second runestone, the <<2>>, from southern tower? Pretty please?
This one feels very, very alert. Awake! Alive! Why do you ask?
Of course not! I intend to recompile their research into my own words and add whatever conclusions suit my opinion.\n\nDon't you know anything about the way academic writing is penned?

"Awaken <<c:1>>," whatever that truly means. But have no fear. This contrivance allows me to manipulate its energies. This means I can keep <<2>> safe when she steps inside.\n\nNow go, place <<Ac:3>>! Let's see what all the fuss is about.

The city's history is … complex. It has changed hands many times. Breton graves are buiilt atop Redguard graves. Orc-hewn stone supports Yokudan-style walls.\n\nEven so, at its heart the city is Redguard. One of our greatest victories occurred here.

This is the site of Derik Hallin's final confrontation with the giant Goblin Mahgzoor Rockhand.\n\nAfter the Ra Gada's long march to Hammerfell, the Yokudans found themselves in a time of relative peace and plenty. Many and many cast down their swords.

It was. Their love of farming and building made them blind to danger. They were set upon by legions of tusked ones, led by a powerful warlord, Mahgzoor. But they had forgotten the way of the sword and stood defenseless.

Knowing his people would be slaughtered if they remained, a wise and powerful warrior named Hallin, the last Ansei, sent them away and chose to protect the city alone. \n\nSome say he was aided by the spirits of long-dead Ansei. Perhaps he was.

Just so. His sacrifice is remembered even now. The city, which formerly bore the name Ojwambu, was renamed Hallin's Stand to honor his great courage. \n\nAh. Hallin's story stirs the blood no matter how many times I tell it.

He fought for seventeen bloody days until at last he faced the dreaded Mahgzoor in single combat. \n\nAfter many long hours, the Goblin struck a killing blow, but Hallin smote his enemy as he fell. As fine a death as any Redguard could aspire to.

Don't you see what's going on here? \n\nI followed you before and overheard your conversation with that mad apostle. It's clear that this Nereid learned one of the most dangerous secrets about the natural order and now twists it to her advantage.
<<1>> is secret magic travel device, installed by Redguards for their nobles and other scaredy cats to use in case fortress fell. Now this scaredy cat will use it to get away from Daedra!
Daedra followed this one, not the other way around! See Dark Anchor over there? It came down to attack me!\n\nNext come vampire skeevers. Mark this one's words.
<<1>> is magic travel device, installed by Redguards for their nobles and other scaredy cats to use in case this fortress fell. Now this scaredy cat will use it to get away from Daedra!

Useful emergency kits! World is war-torn and dangerous. "Tamriel is Doomed" kit has dried fruit, bandages, everything a walker needs to survive the coming apocalypse!\n\nHave you bought one yet? Superb investment! Two, even better.

The Moons told me! Also, this one read book saying Arlimahera herself created the altar for escape in case fortress fell. Two rune stones are required to use it. Place the stones on <<1>> and this one will be away from danger!

No point hiding it now … when a mortal dies, where do you think their memories go?\n\nDon't bother guessing. I'll tell you—they go into the water. They become water. All the memories of Tamriel's history are stored in its waters.

The details and implications of this secret are mind-spinning and would require a lifetime of study and contemplation. \n\nThe relevant fact here is that the Nereid is stealing her disciples' memories to create this Water Stone.

Exactly. And it seems they never will. Their memories are lost to them forever.\n\nThe Lord of Knowledge abhors this transgression. The Nereid must not be allowed to continue in this endeavor, nor can she be permitted to create a Water Stone.

The secrets to creating a Water Stone are forbidden. The natural progression is for the landscape in this area to evolve into a desert.\n\nThe Nereid's not fighting for nature. She's fighting for self-preservation, and at her disciples' expense.

What then? You would side with this water monster and her brain-washed apostle?\n\nGo on then. She's right across the water there. I warn you though—side with them and Hermaeus Mora will offer you no mercy.
Wise choice. For a moment there, I feared the Nereid had affected your mind as well. \n\nI can see you are stronger than that now.

Ha! Of course! It's a sacrifice I'm willing to make. She showed me what would happen if the lake were to dry up. She showed me how much life would be lost.\n\nHow could I refuse to give up some silly memories when so much is at stake?
Finally, this one can flee frightening land of Hammerfell! \n\nNow this one performs magic ritual ….

Some did. Some didn't. You must understand though, when people come wandering around Lorelia's lair, what is she to do? She's a Nereid! \n\nWhen a fly gets stuck in a spider's web, the spider doesn't release it. Lorelia is much the same. It's nature.
I understand. Lorelia says you are a very strong person and we must be patient with you.\n\nWe hope you will choose to help us, but we respect your right to make that choice for yourself.

I do. I support the survival of Lake Halcyon. So much life depends on it. Sacrifices must be made, and to prevent this from becoming a dry, dead desert, it's worth it.\n\nYou must decide as well. If you wish to aid us, Lorelia would speak with you.
I'm very glad to hear that, and I know Lorelia will be too.\n\nCome and speak with her.
This one knows! Sort of. No matter, this one improvises with skill. \n\nAs for you, perhaps you will stand back a bit. You know, in case.

I think so. I took a knife to the wound, to let the venom seep out. I don't know if it'll do any good, but I think the numbness in my legs has started to wear off. Might just be wishful thinking though.

There's something about these ruins. I can't say for sure, but I think they're haunted. Last night my mate Cradius said he heard whispers … said it sounded like his mother or somesuch. By morning he'd vanished.\n\nThis place is evil, pure and simple.

Me? So long as I smile, and joke, and keep the tap wet I am safer than most. My business is another matter. These Imperial curs drink up my ale like the desert sun and pay me nothing in return. \n\nI should not complain though. It could be much worse.
I feared that they might strike his head off right there in the doorway, but they simply sneered and hauled him off. I know not where.\n\nHe hasn't returned.

I sent my tavern boy out to fetch some water from the well. On his way out the door he simply brushed one of the Imperials with his shoulder. They took offense and demanded an apology. He refused … stubborn pride.

Fighting? Oh no, no, no. This isn't fighting. This is deeper than that. This is a seething, simmering battle of wills. A vicious game of alit and guar where a single miscalculation can end in catastrophe.

In trying to retake Old Tower, I have won only my death.\n\nBut there is still honor. I can think of nothing but taking Captain Helenus's Helm—it will rally Covenant troops to this camp and we will reclaim the tower once more!

We immigrated here from Craglorn a month ago. I told him Hallin's Stand was a perfect place to sell our goods, given its close proximity to both Evermore and the Alik'r. He lauded my genius and quickly agreed.
If I'm changed, as my brother was … I can't become a danger to the people I've sworn to lead.\n\nDo you understand me?
Bah! I'm not going to make you an accessory to murder or anything.\n\nJust going to give him a scare. Blasted cat folk. Watch this.

Bah! It's always a misunderstanding! Do you know how many buffoons stumble into this place to tear up flowers and kick the trees?\n\nDammit! The fool isn't worth it. Wasn't going to hurt him, anyway. Just scare him a little.

The secrets in <<Ac:1>> were long ago uncovered, save one. Incredible amounts of magicka coursed through its walls, even when the ruins remained dormant.\n\nUntil recently, this was thought to be a peculiarity of its construction.

Are you, then? The Mages Guild petitioned the court of <<1>> for months before we were allowed to excavate, and now you hope to waltz through and collect <<Ac:2>> for yourself?\n\nWhy would you possibly need it?

It all goes back to Anumaril, one of the greatest Ayleid architects of the First Era. He built the great seal of <<1>> and the Orrery at <<2>>.\n\nThen recently, we uncovered proof that he constructed the archives in <<Ac:3>>.

Anumaril put his heart into his work—literally, if the stories have the right of it. It powered the Orrery at <<1>> until it was lost.\n\nThat's the source of power here, you see? It's what we hope to recover. Think of the potential applications!

Oh. I suppose that's a good enough reason.\n\nWe've scoured the ruins from top to bottom and haven't seen so much as a glimmer. But if we do find it, the Mages Guild would be more than happy to aid <<1>>.

Here are the phony orders. Just place them into the <<z:1>> in the command tent by the tower, with the <<2>> folded inside them.\n\nIf you can make this work, we'll send those legionnaires back to where they came from.

It's called the Nilata Ruins. Hallin's elders say it was the site of an old Ayleid fortress. I don't know if that's true. All I know is that it's a decent place for grazing. At least it used to be. I am sorry—I'm not a historian.

I bring my goats here to graze. My mother always said the grass here was finer … the ruins made it so. \n\nOne of my smallest found a doorway and ran inside. I gave chase and found … well, now I don't know what I found. She seemed so beautiful.

I didn't know what else to do! If I had told anyone in town, they might have lynched me on the spot! Consorting with Daedra? It is unforgivable.\n\nIzzara is a powerful mage. She's also Adeena's identical twin. It just seemed like the only thing to do.

Yes. We Redguards take care to avoid magic, but Izzara was never ashamed. She studied long and long in both Daggerfall and Wayrest. She's a true sorcerer.\n\nHer and Adeena both have magic in their blood. Adeena is just better at hiding it.

I didn't … that is, I didn't tell her everything. If she knew what I had done, she might have turned me to salt, or set me on fire.\n\nI may deserve those things, but not until I see my beloved wife free of that monster.
Yes. You appear wise and well-traveled. Surely you have heard of her?

Mephala is the demon prince of murder, secrets, and seduction. Some call her the "Webspinner." Like a spider, Mephala is always weaving a web of intrigue and terror. \n\nUnfortunately, I believe my precious Adeena has been ensnared.

Directly? No. I doubt that Mephala would take an interest in the affairs of a goat farmer and his wife. But the Webspinner has many servants. A secluded ruin, a foolish, lustful farmer …. Such an opportunity might be hard to pass up.

Of course. This ruin hides all manner of secrets. One of which is a "spell key." Three thousand years ago, we might have needed a whole host of mages to break its hold on the door. But now, it's a brittle relic.

Exactly. The Daedra must have sensed the fragility of the key and empowered the focus stones to protect it. \n\nThey're something akin to welkynd stones, albeit larger and more unstable. It shouldn't take much effort to break them.

In all our long years together, I never raised my voice, or called him out on a lie. I cooked his food, I cleaned his shirts, I minded his goats when he was away. I did all of this gladly. But no longer.
Yes. I want him to know about the suffering. My suffering and my sister's. For once in my life I want him to truly see me, so he'll know what he's done.
Very little, but what I do will strike at his core. He's a small man. Completely undeserving of my sister. And now her death will be on his head. \n\nI pray that his suffering is endless.

But it wasn't enough. \n\nI know that you carry a burden in this as well. Don't give in to guilt. This is Najan's fault. You slayed the creature. I doubt another would have been able to kill it so handily. You did all of Tamriel a service today.
Yes, but the cost was far too high. Adeena's life was worth more than this. I'd kill Najan myself, but I suspect that's exactly what Mephala wants.
Hmm …. I would have thought someone as mighty and well-traveled as you might already know. I am Mephala, The Lady of Whispers.

What a predictably mortal question. 

Small, great … the same. Each thread tugs the other. Petty jealousy, an unintended slight, dog-like lusts … these are the things that bring empires to ruin. 

Think on this, my dear. I'll be watching.

Trying to do? Oh no. You strong, beautiful fool. Do you think she failed?\n\nA marriage ruined, a sister slain, souls lost, families broken …. And to think—all of this began with a wayward goat. What a gorgeous and horrifying tapestry.

To stop me from taking him away! Said some stupid drivel about emotions. If there's one thing I hate more than magic, it's emotions.\n\nCan you just deal with this for me? I can't even think at this point.
We were set upon by highwaymen out in the wastes and nearly starved before finally arriving here. Then what little merchandise we had left was seized by the Imperials.

Remyon was furious and demanded an apology from me for getting us into this situation. I refused, calling him a netch-backed dandy. I said he was weak for whining. \n\nSo rather than leaving without me, he's gone out of his way to make me miserable.

And let him win? Dumac take it! I'd die a hundred deaths before I admit fault to that flat-headed s'wit. \n\nSo here we sit. Now if you'll pardon me, I have to prepare for a celebratory goat-milking competition.
We both hate it here, but he gorges on their over-spiced meat, shovels their horse manure, loudly sings their obnoxious music … on and on and on. I must do the same or lose face.
