No choice. That brute was going to forcibly remove me from the ruins, and I can't leave yet.\n\nI have to get my emotions back under control first.

Precisely. My emotions are gone—Fear, Anger, Happiness, Sadness—they got away from me, in the literal sense.\n\nIt's this Ayleid relic here. It's a gateway into the Silaseli dreamstate, but by the time I realized it, my emotions were already gone.

Yes. You could go into the dreamstate and convince them to come back.\n\nYou'll have to upset them though, drive them to experience their counterbalanced state. Anger to Fear, Happiness to Sadness, that sort of thing.
Now, there's no need to get violent. We're both civilized people.\n\nYou must want something, then? I'm a very influential man, much more useful alive than dead!
Nasirih mentioned something about it. I haven't seen her recently, though.\n\nShe usually is in the tea house, not far from here.

Everybody knows Aishah caught the rat in the act. She was boasting about it in the town square right up until the Imperials flooded in.\n\nIf you're looking for her, I'd check her home. The Imperials might have gotten there first, though.
I'm only here to visit my friend <<1>>. He invited me to see his hometown, but then these Imperials arrived and he told me I'd be safer somewhere else.\n\nHaven't met any other townspeople.
My sister-wives, <<1>> and <<2>>, will look after me. They know what to do if I … don't recover. \n\nBut all will be well. Be assured of it!
If I die while you are gone, that is Mauloch's will. As long as my death has honor, I have no sorrow in its coming.\n\nMy sister-wives, <<1>> and <<2>>, will do what they must, when they must.
<<1>> fights even now, but his wounds are too severe. He knows this, but rejects defeat.\n\nBring him his trinket of retribution, if only to allow him to pass with honor.
His life is in Mauloch's hands. But his honor is his own.\n\nHe thinks that taking this helmet will burnish his honor, so fetch it. Or do not. We will stay here until we must do what must be done.

I'll live. Shortly after I sent out my last scout, another one of those damned spiders attacked the camp. I kept it from biting me, but it battered me with its legs.\n\nI just … just need a minute to pull myself together.

One by one, my soldiers started complaining about voices … seeing things. At first I thought it was insurgents playing tricks on us. By the time I figured out what was really going on, it was too late.
Oh, no, please no. Is he all right? It's been so long since I heard from him, I've been so worried.

She knocked on our door. She sounded concerned, said she was there to help. When my father opened the door, he was attacked. He yelled for us to run.\n\nI heard my father's screams. They followed me as I ran.
We need to find a place to swear the oath. Oathbound cults usually have daises where they worship Malacath.\n\nThere should be one here.
There are two pikes around the ritual area. Place a head on each, facing the dais. Then my work begins.

Because I had a nightmare and someone told me they were going to eviscerate me.\n\nThey described it in great detail how they were going to cut me open and let all my internal organs spill out … my liver, my stomach … it was terrible.

I wasn't close enough to hear, but someone knocked on the door and convinced my father to open it.\n\nThat's when the screaming started. And the blood! I panicked. Probably would have died myself if not for Jowan.

I have a place within these passages where I will go and keep it safe.\n\nIt is needed now, but it will be needed even more in the years to come. If it were stolen or destroyed, all of our work would have been in vain.

Once I have the Water Stone, I will no longer require their generous service. \n\nI will release them to return to their homes in the surrounding areas, where they can be assured that the land will remain rich and alive.
I hope not. \n\nAfter we've created the Water Stone, I will withdraw along with it. I should hope that the Primeval Seekers will move on after they realize there is nothing left for them here.

In time, it is my hope that they will again be able to remember.\n\nIf not, they will still be able to form new memories and build new lives. As it is here, it is more important they be happy than be able to recall every moment of their past.
Ah, yes. As to that, I'm actually smuggling them through the desert.\n\nI'm a member of the Dragonstar Caravan Company. Smuggling is what we do.
Our headquarters are in Evermore. We specialize in delivering anything to anywhere in Tamriel. People are no different than expensive cargo, really.

They're mostly homeless from Evermore. Conditions for refugees aren't great there now, and most of the city-folk don't want to take care of these people, even if they were displaced by a war.\n\nThat's where the Dragonstar Caravan Company comes in!
Sorry. I can't tell anyone that, not even the refugees themselves. If anyone talks, then we could get in big trouble.
A lot of gold. Some are in debt. We're not a charity and this isn't exactly a cakewalk. We run a business.
They took my wedding ring, the only thing left of my beloved wife.\n\nWe lived in <<1>> in Glenumbra. She was killed by Bloodthorn cultists, and I've wandered ever since.
Thank you. There's nothing else I want, unless it were to see her again. To hear her singing. She had a beautiful voice.

Most of my money went to purchase land in Elsweyr for my daughter and me.\n\nThe rest of my gold went to these opportunistic smugglers, and what happens? We're attacked, and they steal my promissory note! Now I can't claim my land!
Those Imperials took one look at it and knew how valuable it was. That piece of paper secures a future for my daughter and me. I have nothing else now, thanks to the Caravan Company!
Please, without that document I don't know what I'll do. Find it, and at least I have something for my daughter.

They're liars, sucking away our savings while promising us a safe passage!\n\nOur numbers were twice this until that incompetent smuggler led us into an ambush. They've already taken our money, so if we die now, it won't matter.
My mother gave me a pendant with our family's crest on it when I came of age. She even had it engraved with my name.\n\nIt's all I have left of our home. She's dead, and my father doesn't even care!
We lived on a little farm at <<1>> in Rivenspire. It was nice, until the vampires came.\n\nWe've been drifting ever since, and now we have nothing.
Thank you! At least someone sees how much it means to me.\n\nI've lost everything else I value. My home. My mother. And my father.
How should I know? He only cares about a stupid plot of land he was promised all the way in Elsweyr! He forgot about me a long time ago.\n\nSometimes I wonder if he cared about mother at all!

Aye, 'twas a fine custom-forged steel blade. A gift from my former captain. It's my only link to that old life. If you can get it back, I'd be grateful.\n\nFeel free to slit a few Imperial throats with it if you like.
Even better: a pirate. That was a long time ago. I've had my feet on land for years now. I don't know what possessed me to run to other sandblasted wastelands. I guess I just miss <<1>>.

The memory essences have been deposited into the crystal well. Destroy the relics on the crystal to draw out the essences and create the Water Stone. \n\nBring the stone to Apostle Marian. I am going now to prepare a secure place for it.

No more quibble cakes? Bah! Without Buttons, what's the point anyhow? I might as well just go back to the old grump!\n\nBy the way, you're not invited to the friendship circle anymore, because there isn't one. I'm going back to Arnitole.
Those creatures, ghouls, and vile Daedra that you battled—they came upon the school on that final night. My husband led them.\n\nWe fought them—all of us—fought for our lives. But it was a massacre.
Oh, tell me you didn't say that! Tell me I didn't hear that right! \n\nHow would you like a staff-blast to your stupid-ugly face …? Let's find out!

I don't know about you, but when I make a new friend, I like to have a celebration! Buttons does too!  \n\nButtons and I are favorite friends, but there's always room for one more inside our circle of love, and you're invited! You want a quibble-cake?

I don't know. I was hoping you knew, but now I'm disappointed … again. \n\nI always tell people how bad things are, and then they get worse, and so the next time I see them, I have to tell them all over again. Do you want to know what else is sad?

Ha! That's hysterical. You might actually be the the most pathetic person I ever met!\n\nThe funniest part is that you actually look pretty tough, but you're really just a beef-witted sap! Ha! I'll be laughing all the way back to Arnitole!
I'm sure you do. And I'll answer them as best I can.
Who can say why a man in love does anything? We've spoken about our plans over the last few years, what we want to do with our lives. Tand grew restless, tired of waiting for tomorrow to come.

You're obviously not in Tamriel anymore. Think of the most miserable, depressing place you've ever been in your life. That's paradise compared to Coldharbour.  \n\nAnd to top it off, well … there's no easy way to say it. You're dead.

It won't be easy. The place is watched by magical constructs called Sentinels. We won't stand a chance unless we can blind them. \n\nI'll tell you more when we get there. And we'll never get there if we don't get moving.
I don't know. Once we rescue the Prophet, he can tell you about the Gods and the ways of Oblivion. I don't understand any of it, myself.

A man named Mannimarco. His Worm Cult is doing some kind of ritual back in Tamriel. They sacrificed you, and everyone in this prison, to the Daedric Prince Molag Bal.\n\nAfter you died, whatever was left showed up here. They call you the Soul Shriven.
It means you're a slave and you'll spend the rest of eternity here in Coldharbour, working under the lash of the Daedra. Unless of course, you come with me.
No, I wasn't sacrificed. The Prophet and I were brought here … conventionally, if that makes any sense. But we're prisoners here, same as you.
He's a strange one, no doubt about it, but he's the wisest man I've ever met. \n\nHe sees things. The past, the future.

You have not heard of Hadran? His reputation is one of darkness and cruel claws. They say he trades in slave-flesh and skooma, that he makes deals with spies and traitors. I worry my sweet Tand is in over his head.
Break him out, of course! Believe me, I can use all the help I can get. \n\nThat blind old man is the only person alive who can help us get back home. Tamriel's a long way from here.

You're fobbing! You expect me to believe that you really want to listen to all my complaining? \n\nYou must think I'm a fool. No one wants to hear all this. It's boring. I don't even want to hear it myself.

You're just saying that because you feel sorry for me. You don't actually care. In fact, I'm sure you would prefer if I just went away.\n\nThat's fine. I'm used to it. Nobody ever really wants me around. I'll just go.

Our dream  … do not laugh, please. Tand's father Muzag is a cook, a very accomplished cook. My Tand is a good cook as well, and I have always wanted to run a business. We spoke of opening our own tavern, making Muzag proud.

Try waiting in a rock until someone calls your name. Then, watch them reduced to a smear of viscera the moment you do what they've asked you to do. You try to find joy where you can.\n\nThe joy of aiding another, of course.

Let's see … Dulan espies many things from his position at the lizard racetrack. And most people that come to the Caravan watch the spikeball races, so Bunul is a good bet. Khaba, up at the troll ring, has a keen eye for newcomers.

I know how it sounds, but the townsfolk were at each other's throats. The constable and her bailiffs were barely able to contain the violence. And Leonce can be very persuasive.\n\nIt seemed like a good idea at the time.

The constable keeps the peace in town. We formed a militia to deal with bandits and other external threats. We're very proud of the Fell's Brigade.\n\nLeonce commands the militia, though he's banned any Orcs from volunteering during the current crisis.

I think so. I won't know for sure until I get home to my wife. Come to think of it, she's very similar to this Ayleid relic—she's old and strange and brings out all my emotions. \n\nRegardless though, I'm ready to go whenever your friend is.

Osgrikh was the son of the chief—back at the stronghold. He figured he'd be chieftain one day and decided all the women of the stronghold were his brides-to-be. \n\nWhen I left and married Esmaeel—he was displeased.

Osgrikh is everything that's wrong with the old ways.\n\nIt wasn't that he loved me. He viewed me as property, and I challenged his authority by leaving. He had the Oathbound kidnap my husband and me off the road.

Something like that. I'd paid the Agluk Orcs for shelter before we moved out of Bangkorai. But, the Imperials attacked the camp at night.\n\nThe Orcs were slaughtered, and we were forced to set up camp on this side of the border.

No. I mean … I have scouted out all this area from the ridges above. The Imperial encampment is just over the hill, and then this temple—the Hall of Heroes—it goes on forever.\n\nShe might have taken the king anywhere in all that space.

The encampment. There has been much activity there in recent days. The Imperials have been going in and out of the temple. I have even seen the Magus-General herself.\n\nPerhaps if you search the encampment, you will find some evidence of her plan.

None, save that they are very well dug in. I would guess that they have been here for several weeks making preparations for something significant. \n\nMost of the Imperial soldiers are in the encampment. I think there are Daedra in the temple itself.

The Hall of Heroes? Oh, it is very, very old, and no one even uses it anymore.  \n\nHeroes today are entombed at Tu'whacca's Throne or Motalion Necropolis, but long ago, this is where great heroes like Frandar Hunding and Makela Leki were buried.

The Keepers said it should belong to the gods themselves—that mortals were never truly welcome here.\n\nPerhaps so. Legends always suggested it was a place where planes collide, where worthy Redguard souls came to make the journey to the Far Shores.

It's the damn mage, of course. I told you—working for them always gives me a headache, and this one's a real piece of work.\n\nI got here, and the stupid mage … well, you better just see for yourself. Follow me.

Who knows why nobles do anything? I never did trust him, though. Ever since he supported Ranser against the High King.\n\nBut I'll tell you this. There were vampires in Montclair's ranks. Even his officers seemed to take orders from them.

The Dreugh King! He lives in a great cavern beneath the mountains of Stonefalls, fighting a war against the mighty Ozozai, chief of the Murkwater Goblin clan.\n\nTo defeat such ferocious warriors would make you the envy of all Undaunted.
That is what I am, yes? Surely you have learned by now that not every vampire is a monster.\n\nAdusa hopes that this doesn't make you uncomfortable. We still have survivors that need our assistance.

Typically, a vampire degenerates over time, eventually withering into a mindless bloodfiend.\n\nThe process we observed in Moira's Hope was quite the opposite. The blood-curse appeared to change its victims into bloodfiends almost immediately.

Well … yes. I found a talisman in the dark, and a beautiful spirit appeared. She called herself Anexiel. Beautiful Anexiel.\n\nIt's … it's not important. She decieved me. She said she needed a "vessel." Someone with magic in their blood.

Yes.

I'm not proud of it. My wife is lovely, but so meek. So quiet. 

Anexiel and I had so much in common. She was light-hearted and smart … seductive. It doesn't matter now. All that matters is my wife's safety. I just want to hold her again.
Yes. I will wait for you there. Maybe Ufa has already gone there himself. Keep ever-watchful for traps.

Yes. Especially that cruel, twisted lady—Septima Tharn, I believe she is called. She has broken all the rules. I told her as much. I did. But she would not listen.\n\nWhen she leaves, I do not think I will invite her to come back.
She's in the Chamber of Passage, but it is a forbidden place. You must get special allowances to go there. \n\nThis is the heroes' hall. You will have to convince them to let you pass.

Oh, they're scattered all over this place. Everywhere. Getting them to talk is the hard part. They're quiet types; been dead for centuries. \n\nFrandar Hunding might listen. You'll just have to do some convincing. You have Tu'whacca's blessing though.

My Prince is endless. No mortal can defeat him.\n\nI do hope you find <<1>> and gaze upon the instruments of her torment. One day it will be you upon the rending pinions, and I will bask in your boundless woe.
Just spare a few coins, and they'll be able to eat tonight. That's all I ask.
Thank you kindly. Now, if you don't mind, there are others I need to beg some coin out of.

I've heard rumors that an undead Elf king is imprisoned somewhere beneath the isle of Auridon—and that he causes no end of trouble for those who watch over him.\n\nFind him, look him in the eye—and you may discover the meaning of Undaunted.
What we all do! Prove you fear no creature, living or dead. Find the fiercest, wildest, most dangerous monsters in Tamriel, and face them down. Show them the meaning of Undaunted!

When I first set out, I found the world full of terrors; of horrible, violent creatures lurking in the depths. I faced them just the same.\n\nAnd while I met many other Redguards in my travels, only in the Undaunted have I met kindred spirits.
Never you mind, sweetheart. Just give me your gold and I'll get it myself.
Such generosity! As for the company I keep, they may be loud and unrefined, but—like me—they spend their lives knee-deep in the forgotten parts of Tamriel.\n\nMake for great storytellers.

Situation? What's to tell? Baron Montclair betrayed all of Shornhelm and has taken over half the city!\n\nPeople have been killed or injured, property destroyed. And now Montclair has demanded that we surrender and crown him king of Rivenspire!

Now you sound like the Countess! Who cares why he wants to be king? The only thing that matters is that we stop him before he takes over all of Shornhelm!\n\nThe man is a cad and a coward. I will never bend my knee to him. Never!

Ambitious? I suppose he was no more or less so than any house noble. My father never liked the man, though. \n\nBut to change so drastically? To put innocent people in harm's way? I pray for the wisdom to understand our foe.

I suppose he hopes we will surrender and agree to his terms. But that's not going to happen. Neither House Tamrith nor House Dorell will give in to such outrageous demands.\n\nAnd I know the High King won't allow such treachery to go unpunished.

Ah, then you'll probably find him still at his house, praying for the gods to intervene. He's a fool, but a goodhearted one.\n\nDown the street a bit. Although, that said, all these desert houses look alike to me.

Well, yes, there's the spiders. But I'm sure they'll be no trouble for a hero of your stature. \n\nAs far as the strength of the ward, the Daedra probably didn't have time to prepare. It may simply be stalling until it can complete its ritual.

Yes. It's complicated. \n\nI apologize for being vague, but every minute we spend talking is another minute that my sister is in danger. I promise you, I'll explain more when you've dealt with the focus stones.

The invaders have taken my scrolls—four sacred writings from the Book of Circles. They describe the principles one must master in the various seasons of life.\n\nRecover the scrolls, place them on the appropriate pedestals, and earn my blessing.

When Emperor Hira's soldiers came to arrest me, they struck my mother and she was slain. It wasn't until that moment I embraced the way of the sword. \n\nTo earn my blessing, light the braziers in the chamber above in the colors to honor her sacrifice.
Turn and observe the moment of my mother's sacrifice. Remember it as I do. Take it into your heart and light the fires of my memory.

The Blacksap hate the king, but they have less love for the Dominion. We know they're planning something. Given their methods, it'll be loud and bloody.\n\nWe can't allow this to fester. But if we capture its leaders, the rebellion ends overnight.

The answer is the key to my blessing. \n\nYou will find several impressive swords in this chamber. They are only symbols of ideals, but bring me the blade a true sword-singer would wield, and I will grant you entrance to the Chamber of Passage.
Mother always said this one was a kitten-headed fool! \n\nHere, take everything! Just let this one go!

Well done. A true sword-singer would select the Training Sword because it is the swordsman, not the sword, that matters. You understand true humility. \n\nYou have my blessing. You may enter the Chamber of Passage.
Yes. It plans to summon its true form here—to Mundus. It will need living sacrifices to do so. We have to … deprive it of those living offerings.

Please, do not think of it as murder. Look around. These people were dragged below by some of the most venomous spiders in all of Tamriel. The toxins they were injected with … victims do not recover from such encounters.

Yes, I'm sorry. Forgive me.\n\nWhen my sister heard that I'd been taken by a Daedra, she came to rescue me. I was possessed for … I don't know. Hours? Days? Weeks? My memory—it's nothing but screaming and dancing shadows.

It's all so foggy … muddled. She drew the creature out of me and into herself. She was gritting her teeth, and screaming. Oh, it was horrible! She said she was going to put up wards before the creature overtook her. To keep the monster out.
Yes! Yes, wayfarer, just so. Don't let it win!
Hm! We'll see. I've got some of it pieced together. If you can fill in the gaps, I'll be impressed.\n\nIf you're ready, I'll ask you my outstanding questions.
All right. First, I need to know about Joelle. I know she was the warrior, but what was her last name?
He was mortal, once, among the most skilled artisans of his time. Like me.\n\nHe made a deal with the Daedra when he died, and now he builds for them—torments souls for them.
Hm. That might make sense. If that's correct though, what was Olivia's profession?
Hm. All right. If that's true, then what was Willam's last name and profession?
All right. Let's see if all your answers add up. All that matters is whether I can open this damn lockbox ….
Ha! Yes! It seems Willam had quite a sense of humor. Now, let's see what's inside ….
No. Listening to the tumblers, I think we have Joelle's last name wrong.\n\nWant to try again?
Because his soul is as dark as this Vault.\n\nBut enough about him. We'll face him soon enough.
All I ask is a few drakes! Just enough to give a mouthful of food to my poor, hungry children.

Yes, of course. Every dabbler in proto-Ayleid literature knows.\n\nMany believe it's a metaphorical contrivance, but <<1>> thinks it's located in the walls of this ruin. Ha! If she wants to end such a promising career, more funding for the rest of us.
Oh, your kindness will not go unrewarded!
I'm sure she can explain her ridiculous theories better than I.

A fair question. I don't often come to greet those who would slay my servants. But you … oh, there's something different about you. The scarred wrists of a Coldharbour slave, yet such a regal bearing ….
Har! It's not, is it? I wager it's not clever, either.
With you? Don't think it'd be much of a fight. Ha ha!
Whoa! Easy now, friend. Why fight me when there's plenty of real enemies out there?\n\nI like your attitude though. Thinking you might just have what it takes to be one of the Undaunted.
A league of like-minded adventurers. Every one of us eager for riches and glory. Sound like anyone you know? \n\nSo what do you say? Think you can be one of the Undaunted?
Then welcome! And best of luck to you. You're gonna need it, trying to keep up with these maniacs.\n\nOh—I almost forgot your initiation! Ready for it?

Some lout at the bar was talking about the spider caves of Spindleclutch, up in the Hag Fen. Said a whole squad from the Fighters Guild went in, and not a one came out! Might be something truly nasty hiding in there.\n\nWhy don't you go find out? Har!
Hey! You … stop that! You're hurting Buttons' feelings! You're hurting my feelings too!\n\nI'm going back to Arnitole!

Oh, my grandmother gave me Buttons as a pet when I was just a little boy!\n\nWe were inseparable. When I was little, he carried me on his back, and when I got big, I carried him on my shoulder. Buttons is my favorite friend in all of Tamriel!
Oh? Now you're making jokes about my mother?\n\nNow you've done it! Now you've made me mad! I'm going back to Arnitole!

Raynelle Derone. She was brought here by the Architect just like Gasteau and myself.\n\nIt's likely she's been imprisoned like I was. When last I saw her—by the Divines, it must have been years ago—she was taken to the Vault up ahead.
I was an artisan. A rival of the Mad Architect's in life.

Well I'm not exactly sure, but I can tell you this—it's more than simple spiders. Something or someone is manipulating these beasts. Manipulating us. This place is evil. I don't intend to stay a minute longer than is necessary to secure my men.
<A small indentation at the base of the anvil reveals itself to be a small key pressed into a hidden alcove. You safely remove it.>
I suppose.\n\nI find the lack of a soul makes me a little … lackadaisical.

Our ancient compact with Y'ffre brought splendor to the Wood Elf people, yet this king's own Vinedusk Rangers are exempt. I've seen them eat roots from the ground. Disgusting!\n\nWhen the people called for justice, I had no choice.
Then it wasn't a very funny joke! My father was eviscerated, as a matter of fact! \n\nI'll put up with a lot, but jokes about evisceration are where I draw the line!

Ha! Now that's the stupidest idea I've ever heard. You think if I stop talking about it, it will just go away? Like that's some secret trick to dealing with sadness?\n\nThat's just hysterical. You're funny. You should be a minstrel.

Used to study magic, back in the day, Under a powerful mage named <<1>>. Taught Tholor and me everything we know.\n\nWe were her best students, so when she walked into <<2>>, she told us what to do if things went wrong.

Well, we're not sure exactly, but when <<1>> went down there, Daedra poured out and killed all our fellow students. It was all we could do to make it to a safe vantage point. But the tower never turned, so here we are.

She gave us a crystal. Told us if the beacon on her tower ever turns red, we're to break it, no questions asked. When we do, everything around her tower—trees, <<1>>, all of it—will be unmade.\n\nIf we don't … well. We're in trouble.
Tholor says it's a hundred years this Rain's Hand, but me? I'd put it more at ninety-seven—give or take a few.

The Dominion's great hero, a traitor? And you, to have stopped her?\n\nIf this is true, my sons would know. If you can convince the Blacksap you ended the Jade Butcher's reign of terror, you can get close enough to my sons to capture them.

I am the Daedric Prince of Dawn and Dusk, the Mother of the Rose, who sealed <<1>> away from your world.\n\nI am Azura, mortal. And I would put an end to <<2>>'s long suffering beneath its gates, below.

If <<1>>  knows I'm alive, he'll come peacefully. He's pragmatic, and not the type to waste his life for a lost cause.\n\n<<2>> is another matter. He's not the type to kill you outright, but step lightly. He's very proud, that one.
When <<1>> found these ruins and sought to end <<2>>'s torment, she failed, and was lost.\n\nGo to <<1>>'s tower. Follow her footsteps, and mortal—do not fail, as she did.

I'm the Vinedusk's Master of Portals. I've spent most of my life studying their magical intricacies. I've developed my own types of portals, the kind which can't possibly be traced.\n\nWithout my expertise, none of this would be possible.
Yes. The Imperials were only interested in our baggage. If we'd just handed things over, the Orcs wouldn't have had to fight.\n\nBad luck all around, I'd say.

Take this bloodstone. Don't lose it. It has the power to turn water to blood and whip up a ferocious hunger in the most sated vampire.\n\nWhen the time is right, we're going to use it to lure the vampire lord out of his hidey-hole.
Gasteau Chamrond, master artisan, at your service.\n\nI can't thank you enough for what you've done for me.
<Aligning the planets causes a small key to eject from the base. You take the key.>
<The relief shows expert craftsmanship, but is otherwise unremarkable. In the fountain waters, however, you find a tarnished metal key.>

They … they haven't been built. Don't get me wrong—I have volumes of blueprints, brilliant designs, if I have to say so myself.\n\nBut they've never been realized. You can blame the Mad Architect for that. I did.
I've designed structures here and there.
<The Dwarven door is tightly shut. Three keyholes sit at eye level, each with a corresponding symbol below: Mundus, Aurbis, and Aetherius.>
<The second key turns smoothly. More gears move.>
<You meet no resistance as you turn the key. Gears quietly move in the door.>
<The final key gives little resistance. A latch audibly unlocks inside the door.>

In life, she was a young and beautiful Nedic priest. To spite Arkay, Molag Bal corrupted her and left her in a death-like state. Upon waking, she was overcome with a savage hunger.\n\nThe nomads who found her body would become her first feast.

<The text contains Dwemer writing and alchemical symbols. A detailed diagram of a Dwemer machine accompanies the text. The device needs a final cog to be fully functional, and the diagram shows a design for the cog mold.>

This is the Vault of Despair, where I and my fellow captors are forced to forever balance impossible ledgers.\n\nIt began as a torture crafted specially for me, but the Mad Architect has been busy collecting souls for the Daedra ever since.

<The diagram includes a map of Razak's Wheel, and seems to indicate that, if you can find the cog mold, you could create a cog using nearby machinery. The cog can then be used to complete Razak's machine in a chamber farther south.>

Over the ages, she found that when others fed from her, rather than becoming weaker, she grew still more powerful. And as her blood flowed within an ever-growing number of children, so her strength multiplied.

He was a rival artisan and bitter enemy of Gasteau. And that made him my enemy. I spoke with every noble in Wayrest to ensure that Dutheil would never work again.\n\nI did not know that our scheme would cause … such mayhem.

I … stole designs from him, after Saryne arranged for the Wayrest nobles to deny Dutheil further projects.\n\nGasteau presented those designs to the nobles as renovations for the Royal District, as original works.

Well, Dutheil was unable to secure further work, just as Saryne and Gasteau had intended.\n\nThe man was already an eccentric and his falling out with the Wayrest nobles led to a mental collapse. The next I saw Dutheil, he was the Mad Architect.
I despaired every moment of it.\n\nI was a manager of coin in life. To me, a ledger that never balances is like an itch that never scratches. It nearly drove me mad until you freed me.

The Jade Dragoons struck at night, from all directions. The Blacksap never stood a chance. They tried to surrender, but <<1>> had ordered her soldiers to cleanse the area.\n\nSeems the Jade Dragoons always follow orders.

He's still calling himself that? The boy needs a hobby.\n\nHe once proposed we use his portals to send the contents of our latrine into a Blacksap camp. "The perfect distraction," he said. We called him the Master of Privies for a month.
You killed the Jade Butcher?\n\nAll of <<1>> will thank you, if it's true. But I don't know any "<<2>>."
Head to the Butcher's Ground. He'll be there when he's ready.\n\nWe won't speak again.

Gasteau was a good friend, and valued business partner. So when he asked me to, I helped him discredit the Mad Architect's reputation.\n\nIt destroyed the man—Dutheil was his true name. And everything you see here was Dutheil's revenge.

Well, Dutheil was unable to secure further work, just as Saryne and Gasteau had intended.\n\nThe man was already an eccentric and his falling out with the Wayrest nobles led to a mental collapse. The next I saw Dutheil, he was the Mad Architect.

As I said, he's not much for talking. Sometimes, not even to me. I do know how much he loathes the Jade Butcher, and that he wants to repay the Dominion in kind.\n\nI told you where to find <<1>>. Now, take me to my father.
Well, no. I can't say that. Some days, they would lash me with whips of flame.\n\nHonestly, I preferred that to the ledgers.
I see.\n\nVery well, I wish to turn myself in. Take me to my father. If he's alive, I must speak with him.
When I walked among the living, the Mad Architect, then a petty fool named Dutheil, was my rival.\n\nHe cornered me out of countless professional contracts, made it so I could never find any work.
You're the one who did it?\n\nTell me. When she fell to you, was it swift? Or did she linger?
It's my father's ring. I took it from his bedroom when I was a child. When he found out, he boxed my ears.\n\nThis proves nothing. Only that you may have slain my father, before you came for me.
No. I suppose it doesn't.\n\nI'll surrender to you, but it won't end the attacks on the Dominion camps. Once unleashed, the constructs are beyond our control.
Here, take this bottle. My soldiers drink it to steady their nerves before battle. Perhaps it will help with the constructs.\n\nNow, where is my father?
Yes. If ever a threat came to us, we would come here, empower them through sacrifice, and be protected.\n\nLuckily, the Reachmen only see them as rocks.

Find the <<1>>. It shouldn't be difficult to find. But, if you must ….\n\nMany spriggans carry a spore that returns to the <<1>> when the spriggan dies. You could kill them and follow it to the Voice, but that certainly won't make it very happy.
I-I can't believe what I'm reading …. How could Renchant be such a fool? \n\nHas he given up on defending the kingdom and decided to accept the lesser of two evils? This is simply mad.

Me? No. I've never seen you before in my entire life. Besides, I've only been here a few minutes. \n\nSay though, if you already know about the book, I don't suppose you'd be willing to help me get it back?
Because his soul is as dark as this Vault.\n\nBut enough about him. We'll face him soon enough.

He was mortal, once, among the most skilled artisans of his time. Like me, and others he's imprisoned.\n\nHe made a deal with the Daedra when he died, and now he builds for them—torments souls for them.
No. Listening to the tumblers, I think we have Olivia's profession wrong.\n\nWant to try again?
No. Listening to the tumblers, I think we have some of William's information wrong.\n\nWant to try again?
I was Gasteau's apprentice, hoping to become a full artisan in my own right.\n\nHe had done much for me, taken me under his wing, allowed me to flourish. I thought I was helping a friend.

What? You think all I've ever done is search for information about the Blacklight Raiders? \n\nThere are locks on every door in Tamriel. You'd have to be living under a rock not to have picked a few of them. Can we get back to the questions?
You don't know? Well, this is awkward.\n\nThe Seventh Imperial Legion has taken ownership of the city.

Hey, I'm just a foot soldier. All I know is we took it with very little resistance. It was a welcome surprise. Rumor has it Hallin's Stand has been besieged more than once. We expected heavy casualties, but were blessed with very few.

<<1>> is under Imperial control. Has been for a while. Only the Eight know why we bothered taking it. \n\nAnyway, there are supposedly rebels out here in the ruins. Supposedly. I haven't seen anything but rubble and spiders.
Without much trouble. The way I hear it, someone opened the gates from the inside. That's rumor, though.

<<1>> was covered in grease. She's likely digging through the guts of a Dwemer construct somewhere. As for <<2>>, I never met a spy who wasn't obsessed with high ground.\n\nShe'll be at the highest elevation she can find.

Funny you should ask—Rock was just regaling us with tales of the fearsome crocodile he fought in the sewers beneath Wayrest. Only it seems the beast got away; our Rock's afraid of a little water!\n\nA pity. I would kill for a pair of croc-skin boots.

Why, I live here of course. Along with all the other families of note. Wayrest attracts the wealthy like a bar attracts drunks.\n\nI was just visiting our dear friends in Daggerfall. And stopping by my other house. Well, one of my other houses.

The king is responsible for his own people, so it falls to the king's soldiers to handle all local matters.\n\nBut just in case the Blacksap get any ideas, Dominion camps are stationed just outside of <<1>>. "Training maneuvers," they call it.

Reason, fear, a sense of self-preservation—no, what have I done? You met <<1>>'s true spirit. I spurned it … him … as a mockery of my son's memory!\n\nForgive me. I will set this right, but I don't care to speak of it right now.

I only know so much. They started out as just a small band of adventurers from High Rock, exploring old barrows and caves, killing bandits and monsters, that sort of thing.\n\nOver time though, they became notorious, especially in Morrowind.

Yes. That's all we have to go on.\n\nWhat we need to figure out is what each of the Blacklight Raiders' names was, and whether they were the fighter, the mage, the thief, or the cleric. Look at the letter.

I come from a village outside Blacklight. My grandfather always told me stories about the Raiders who stole our family's heirlooms.\n\nYears later, I heard about this lockbox the Raiders had left behind. I tracked it down, and it led me here.

Bit of a forward question, isn't that? Yes, yes, I'm a spirit. Pulled from my body after an altercation with a Khajiiti moon priest. Don't worry, it's only temporary. I'm sure we'll figure out a way to get me back home. Very soon.
It's what I use to crush faces.
Some faces talk too much. So I crush them.\n\nWith a rock.
They used to be. Turning a body to stone is easy.\n\nThe trick is keeping the mind intact. If they hadn't settled into place so many years ago, I'd introduce you to my former masters. Pity.

Hardly. My masters found there were certain … difficulties in allowing me to roam this place unfettered. So they split me from my body.\n\nIn this form I can go where I please, but I can't touch anything directly. It's quite upsetting.

I have no more desire to keep you here than you had to remain in Coldharbour. I shall return you to your little den in the wild. Your surviving companions await you there.\n\nAre you prepared to leave?

I don't know. Daedra, I expect? The horrors of Oblivion aren't my specialty.\n\nYou'll know those floating beasts if you see them. They have many tentacles and seem quite nimble. Like netches, but covered in eyeballs.

Ah.\n\nOrc strongholds don't have prisons. They're considered a waste of space. Denizens can be openly attacked for crimes, actual or perceived, as a blood price. It can be a brutal existence. Part of why I left.
I met my husband.\n\nNot that it matters anymore.
Try lighting them faster. I think you have to keep them all lit at the same time.

You'll find the braziers are already lit. You must simply cycle through the colors on each brazier to match the memory of my mother's final moments. \n\nIt's getting the colors in the correct order that matters.
I need to recuperate from today. Then I will face all comers. My stronghold will not forget me.\n\nI'll regret my husband's death to my last breath, but until then, I hope Malacath stands with me.

Nothing impresses me!\n\nBut I'll tell you a good place to die. The heart of the Grahtwood holds a tree, taller and older than the rest. Beneath it is a burial place called Elden Hollow, a grim record of the forest's past. Danger awaits you there.

Good, but that's the easy part. The hard part's proving yourself.\n\nThis cave seems like a good test. See if you can best whatever's inside. If you survive, come meet me at the Fish Stink in Davon's Watch and we'll make it official.

I've caught rumor of insectoid creatures in Deshaan—the Kwama. Apparently, Dark Elves keep whole caves of them to harvest and eat their eggs! I've heard Darkshade Caverns is one such place.\n\nGhastly.
Malacath cultists who exact vengeance for vengeance's sake.\n\nThey must have been pleased—they got to deliver retaliation for the son of a stronghold chief.
I've done my duty, as you can see. I don't think it'd be fair if one of us did your work for you!\n\nWouldn't want to ruin your fun, anyway!

I'm going to ask for Osgrikh to be brought to us. But this'll be my first oath of vengeance. Malacath may slay Osgrikh outright, he may slay us. Or both.\n\nI've heard he can be fickle—Orcs certainly are. Be prepared for anything.
Don't care. Just pay.

Truly? Then I have all the more reason. If I can get it right this time, we can be a family once more.\n\nI don't want to cause this creature harm. But <<Az:1>> was long ago hidden from me, so I must use cruder methods to control it.
Verandis … after I'm gone. You need to continue to watch over my family. Wylon will need your … strong, steadying presence more than ever.

The Baron sees me as a child and I find him to be a pompous ass, Light grant me patience!\n\nI know that he wants to appear strong. In control. But we need to peer into the shadows and determine what has led to Montclair's bold actions.
Karnosis' wife just kept getting sicker and sicker. He begged me to give her the gift of Vampirism. But I refused. Leila would never have been happy as a vampire.

According to my research, the other two shards are still in the Doomcrag. Using all three shards we can activate the relic to cure my Leila of the disease that plagues her.\n\nIt's got to work. I can't lose her.

She's young and inexperienced. She hesitates. Turns to prayer instead of her own good sense.\n\nA ruler has to think and act, not pray to bloody Arkay for every little thing. If we hesitate in this, we'll surely lose everything we hold dear.

I don't know what Montclair promised them, but we can't let such disloyalty go unpunished. We must show resolve in this matter. We must deal harshly with these traitors.\n\nThey'll be in the upper city. Probably in the barracks or Montclair Manor.
Speed won't help us if we wind up rushing to our defeat.\n\nWe need to learn as much as we can before we attempt to confront Montclair.

He was convinced that performing the ritual at top of the Doomcrag would cure Leila. I warned him that his translation of the ancient text was sloppy but he wouldn't listen to reason. So we packed up and headed for the Doomcrag.
Adusa needs a short nap. Then this one will find Verandis and see how the campaign against the Dawnwalkers is going.\n\nStay fragrant, five-claws!

You know what a lamia is? Imagine a giant snake and a gorgeous woman somehow had a baby. Curious, right? Thought I might cozy up with one. I was wrong.\n\nMaybe you'll have better luck. There's a horde of them in <<1>>, old Imperial fort called <<2>>.
Would certainly be thoughtful of you.\n\nI've been down here for a week, tied up, with scraps for food. Fighting would be unwise.
Who cares? The ale tastes like swill, and the swill tastes like piss. I'll drink whatever's on the table, so long as you're buying.
I get drunker but none the poorer. A good deal! Many thanks!

You don't listen very well. Were you not Undaunted you'd be a pile of ash right now.\n\nIf you must know I've come to <<1>> in search of the Crypt of Hearts, a once-great school of magic. Now it is cursed. If you find it before me I hope you die there.

Oh, not that again, Verandis. And especially not now. We're having a celebration! Leila is on the mend. She's getting well!\n\nI have my wife back and it's all thanks to that remarkable piece of stone you gave me.

You ever dance with a Daedric Prince?\n\nIlmindil here claims Mehrunes Dagon himself is wrecking havoc in <<1>>. Sent his army to raze some Bosmer village. Don't remember its old name, but now it's called the <<2>>.

As I now recall, Reezal-Jul gave me a shard—a piece of an Ayleid relic. I presented it to Montclair and he, in turn, used it to heal his wife. In less than a day, Leila was recovering and on her feet again.\n\nIt was nothing short of miraculous.

Spoken like a true Undaunted. So let me ask you something.\n\nHow would you rather die: burned alive, your flesh charred and falling off the bones? Or swallowed whole, digesting in the belly of some reptilian freak?

It's a ravine beyond the upper city. It's been sealed off for years. They used to send the ill and infirm there. Those afflicted with the plague, Khajiit fever, Argonian leprosy—things like that. But that was a long time ago.

The ravine is riddled with small caves, as I recall. \n\nThere's an even older section, an ancient ruin. If this Argonian is using a portal to bring reinforcements into the city, I suspect those ruins would make a proper staging ground.
It's a dank old place. Oh! I remember now.\n\nThe sewers! You can sneak through the old sewer tunnel. It leads to right near the entrance of the Fevered Mews.
What do you get? How about unending glory? A life of pride and satisfaction?\n\nThat good enough for you?
What should you do? You're Undaunted!\n\nGo kill something! Something big! And let all Tamriel know of your exploits!
Heard a rumor that some Goblins in Varanis took over a cave; been causing a nuisance for some Dark Elves. Place is called … Fungal Grotto.\n\nYou may find your adventure there. Goblins for sure.

Indeed! Undaunted always ask for more! More danger, more treasure!\n\nBut we take care of our own—we know how to fight, and we'll teach you, if you stick around. We have an armory—and we'll arm you, for a fee—if you stick around.
I can tell that by my empty mug, hah! I'm sure with your looks though, they may have a spot for you here, away from the customers!

Then good luck! You'll need it.\n\nWe have one last thing to handle. This'll be your initiation, and your first challenge as an Undaunted. We'll have you bleeding from your eyes and ears in no time. Are you ready?

A league of like-minded adventurers. Every one of us eager for riches and glory—whether it means bodily harm, or worse! Sound like anyone you know? \n\nSo what do you say? Have what it takes to become an Undaunted?
Now there's some spirit! You've got courage, scamp, I'll give you that. Why don't you put that courage to use against some real danger.\n\nFew have what it takes to be an Undaunted.
No, but I'd wager your mother got plenty mad just from looking at you, ha ha!
These scales been hacked and hewn for years. Only rarely have they been greeted with cheer and cold ale.\n\nIt is a good life—though, perhaps, a short one.

I am not without resources of my own. When I discovered that Montclair had left the city and heard that the nobles had been taken captive, it wasn't difficult to ferret out the mad Argonian's hiding place.
I have … loyal associates. Let's leave it at that for the time being. Suffice to say, we have nothing but Rivenspire's best interests at heart.\n\nNow, let's go rescue those nobles.

The Argonian? He has been at Montclair's side for a long time. He is a skilled warrior and an alchemist. I believe he may also have darker interests, including necromancy.\n\nUnderstand this: Reezal-Jul is powerful and not quite sane.

You realize asking about challenges is not the same as facing them?\n\nThere is a cave network in Daggerfall called Spindleclutch. Supposedly infested with giant spiders and other foul creatures. Exploring it should keep you busy.

There are rumors that an undead Elf king is imprisoned somewhere beneath the isle of Auridon—and that his watchers are more tortured than he is.\n\nFind this king—and you may discover the meaning of Undaunted.
Just give me the money.
Ah, there we are.\n\nAs for that advice … never trust strangers. Ha ha! Seriously, I owe you one. I'll see you around I'm sure.
Oh, kick around here, I expect. Catch up with old friends. Scare a pilgrim or two.\n\nAll this dirt … it's rather dull, isn't it? The Wormies were the most exciting thing in ages!

"Dear Wormies! Thanks for the excitement. Sorry about that <<1>> fellow, but he was a bit of a bastard, wasn't he? Perhaps we should catch up over some deathbell tea. Signed, <<2>>."\n\nDo you think they'll write back?

No! No, no, no … well, a bit, in that impending doom sort of way. The Wormies mixed things up! Even got old <<1>> kicking around again.\n\nAnd I met you, so it wasn't all bad. I should really send them a letter.
That seals it, then! Now to find some vellum … hot wax … a quill, definitely a quill.\n\nI saw some ink up in <<1>>'s cave. She'll let me borrow some, I'm sure of it!
You know, I hadn't thought about it. I usually just … pick a direction and start walking. Though sometimes that doesn't work out so well.\n\nTake the Sea of Ghosts. Seems like a fun jaunt, yeah?

Oh, yes. Loved it! Warm, dry, and the sand feels so good on my bones!\n\nUnfortunately, the people there aren't big on walking skeletons. Not many are, but there in particular. I was on my best behavior, too! They had no need to react like that.
Up north, very north. Lots of water. Ice like you wouldn't believe.\n\nBut the barnacles … oh, do they chafe! Took me a decade rolling around in desert sands to rid myself of those.

When they saw me coming they took for the hills, the caves, whatever was available to hide in. By the time I reached a city it would be completely deserted! Made me terribly lonely.\n\nBut that was long ago. I should visit, see how things have changed!
No creature, no man, walks the sands of the Alik'r without my knowing. I watch all, see all. For that, it is mine.
Exceptionally boring, but necessary. We must maintain absolute solitude if we're to pass from this world, to end the threat we pose to its people.\n\nI fear our memories may return to us.
To be reminded of the horrors we once wrought upon this world is bad enough. That mortals seek us to create even greater horrors ….\n\nUnthinkable.

Many and more! But they are mine to claim.\n\nSince you're Undaunted, I'll share this secret with you: hidden among the eastern mountains of Alik'r is the ancient Dwemer fortress <<1>>. Few have braved its halls; fewer yet have survived to tell.
They hold no power over our bones. This much is certain.\n\nWe are grateful for your help, but each moment we spend in the presence of the living causes us great pain. Please, leave us to our vigil.
I know you will. Though I'm less certain you'll prevail. The sands can be unforgiving.\n\nBut either way, there will be a story to tell.

Funny you should ask—Rock was just regaling us with tales of the fearsome crocodile he fought in the sewers beneath Wayrest. Only it seems the beast got away; our Rock's afraid of a little water!\n\nA pity. I would kill for a pair of croc-skin boots.

That's the spirit! What's a centuries old cursed bloodline in the face of unmitigated bravado?\n\nEnter the Banished Cells. Stay a while. Maybe bother a ghost. If you come out alive, see me at the tavern in Vulkhel Guard. We'll talk more then.
When <<1>> delivered her message, I was skeptical. We do not usually work so closely with one another. Still, desperate times bring out the Baan Dar in all of us.\n\nWhat is his plan?

<<1>> likes your cooperative spirit! Such is the heart of the Undaunted.\n\nIf you seek great heights, look to the land of <<2>>, where the frozen tower of <<3>> rises over mountaintops. Ascend its icy walls. Prove you are Undaunted.

This one doesn't help. This one has already done his due diligence—seen his share of dangerous delves. His job is strictly to send the uninitiated head-first into unknowable terror.\n\nBut good luck in there! You'll come back with a story for sure!
The reason is twofold.\n\nFor one, if we did this thing only for ourselves, we would remain a thorn in <<1>>'s side and be forced to leave. Who, then, would help the helpless of Redfur?

We're experienced adventurers. We can teach you skills and tactics a soldier cannot. Our battlefields are the deeps of Tamriel.\n\nThere's also a cache of weapons and equipment, found on our adventures, for sale. Much more exotic than the local armory.

It's the only way this one's victims ever survive—if they elude her once, she calls them lucky, and sharpens her claws for the next dance.\n\nBut should they be twice-lucky, and escape her claws once again, this one will relent and let them go free.
Creatures of ice and magic, touched by the chill of death, bound by an ancient curse. Nothing too serious. This one had a wonderful time, though a shaveskin like you might want to bring a coat.

Oh really? She told you I could do that? She's right, of course. I'm really very smart.\n\nI just need the right incentive. Simply giving away my brilliance would make me feel foolish. And I don't like that feeling.

That ought to cover it. Let's see. It's a simple replacement code. Count back five letters, and …. Your spy's initials are "E.C." There's a dust-sweep in town. Edouard Celd. He often acts as a go-between for unsavory types.
Oh, anything on the menu will do just fine. Beggars can't be choosers, after all.
Quite kind of you, my friend. Let us toast to your generosity!

Oh, but of course! In fact that's why we've come to port here.\n\nA dark plot unfolds in the seas south of <<1>>, some dreadful magic brewing on <<2>>. Storms rage for miles around it, and ships that approach haven't returned.

To warn the King. But the Covenant can't be distracted with matters so far afield. Would that I could join you, and slay whatever fearsome power lies in wait on that island. The danger we would brave together!\n\nAlas, my duty requires me to stay.
I can't see why not. If they're of any importance to the Jackdaw's captain, they'll have written orders.\n\nAs long as we learn their plans, I don't care how you do it.
This one is called Tubidan. The most dauntless of the Undaunted, the Mane of Meridia's Vanished City, they call him!\n\nAn honor this must be for you. So … how about it?
Most fragrant!

He has the power to remake <<1>> in his image, to the Mad God's delight. Where <<2>> goes, <<3>> won't be far behind.\n\nI see no other way. Unless you convince <<3>> to take him back to Oblivion, but arguing with the Mad God is folly.

My friend, simply walking the crumbling earth of Coldharbour is proof enough of courage! And surviving a testament to strength!\n\nThough—I suppose there is one place more threatening and horrifying than most, save for the Throne of Brutality itself.
<The smoke from the mechanism takes on a foul odor.>
<The sickly-sweet smell becomes a foul stench.>
<The bubbling and hissing increases within the mechanism.>
<A foul-smelling smoke emanates from the mechanism.>

Way out in Glenumbra, in the area called Hag Fen, are a series of caves called Spindleclutch. I've heard tale of nasty spiders there—bigger than horses.\n\nNot even the Fighters Guild has been able to drive them away.

He builds for the Daedric Princes—black-spired castles, bleeding towers of flesh. Buildings as grotesque as they are instruments of torture, and the Vaults are his vilest creation.\n\nThey are a true test for an Undaunted.

The Daedra call it the Vaults of Madness.\n\nIt's the home of a demigod known as the Mad Architect. This one thinks he's Daedric, others a mere mortal—with frightening magical abilities. This one has long dreamed of raiding his coffers.
The kind that gets me drunk. Never mind. Just give me the gold, and I'll scrounge up the best swill in this place.
Excellent. I'll have this gold turned to a blurry haze soon enough.\n\nYou aren't half-bad, fresh-meat. You know to keep the talent happy.

Fauridil will tell you differently, but she takes after me. I've been quite the influence for her, and though she's been Undaunted longer, I'm just a little bit better.\n\nWe've been adventuring partners for years—twins, they call us.

I'm … I'm not really sure. But it's awful, stranger. Aches, chills, flop sweat …. At first I thought it might have been scalon fever, but it came on so suddenly. I think it might be something much worse.
That would be the joke, wouldn't it?
Would you like to buy a drink for this Khajiit?
Thongar over there told me about a kwama mine not far from here, in Siltreen, called Darkshade Caverns.\n\nDark Elves harvest kwama eggs from the mine—for eating. It's quite delightfully disgusting.
You'll come around.
Too risky. It could be contagious. Plus, I've already tried all the curatives they would suggest. Honestly, I don't even think I can stay here in the camp much longer. I'm putting everyone at risk.
If I can gather up the strength, I plan on making for Kerbol's Hollow.
Here … I'll mark it on your map. It's not a short journey, but I've got to try.
Aye. My Nanna used to talk about a cave where the sick would linger. Supposedly, anyone who entered the cave could be cured, no matter how severe the illness.

This one and his Undaunted friends were very busy in life. Always delving into ancient dungeons, raiding a mad mage's home, or bursting out of a necromancer's coffins to terrify and then behead them.\n\nThose were exciting times.
Just taking a brief respite.\n\nEven an Undaunted needs time to recuperate. There's caves and delves out there just waiting for me. And I'll go gladly—after a drink or two. And some sleep.
What we all do: prove you fear no creature, living or dead. Find the fiercest, wildest, most dangerous monsters in Tamriel, and face them down. Show them the meaning of Undaunted!

Long story. This Khajiit and his Undaunted kicked down many doors in our careers.\n\nKicking down doors often reveals great treasure, or forgotten places. But sometimes it reveals an angry wizard who removes your soul and stores it away.

Clan Morkul was once proud but has grown weak. Many clan members have left for other clans. This would turn that around.

Clan Agluk is relatively young and wants to gain respect. This would increase their stature.

You have the letter—which is it?

Perhaps. In the Daggerfall city of Wayrest, the sewers are infested with all manner of creatures. My half brother lost his arm to a giant crocodile there, in fact.\n\nNow he's—literally—my half brother! Ha! One day I'll flay that beast.

Out by the old Rilis tombs you'll find the Banished Cells.\n\nIt's just a rumor, but I've heard there's an undead king there—and he's quite a handful for those who guard him. Sounds worthy of a visit. How often do you get to see an undead king?

Yes, centuries ago, I think—hard to recall. He took our souls, put them in a contraption. It must have broken, because one day, this one and his Undaunted were freed.\n\nThe wizard—long dead. And this city had wandered far from where it was.
Truly? Then who leads the Drublog? I … must return to <<1>>. My people will need a leader.
There's plenty, if you know where to look.
Ha! This one's a piece of junk, won't even move. And that's the only one we have. Once you're in the war, there'll be plenty of rams.
There's a vat on top of the platform past the catapults. Try not to kill anyone with it.
Any drink will do.\n\nListen, I'm asking for money. I know how to buy a drink.
Ooh, this one has hit a nerve. A delicate, milksoppy nerve.

Still itching for more adventure? Smashing! Have you ever wondered what would've happened if you'd woken up somewhere else? Washed up on a different beach?\n\nMy new mistress provided me with the means to help you, if you're up for the challenge!

Touch Meridia's light and see the world through the eyes of your former enemies.\n\nBut fair warning—you will no longer be seen as a great champion. Even familiar faces will see you as a soulless drifter, lost in an unfamiliar land. What say you?
Thank me? You're the one doing all the work, heroing and getting dirty in Tamriel. Ugh, the very thought makes me itch.\n\nBut if you enjoyed that, though, there's always more!
Well, you've seen two of the three major players now. Care to finish the set? Fill out your map? Collect all the … metaphors?\n\nEither way, I've got a portal for you, if you're ready.
Ha! A good response. I like you. Not afraid to get your claws bloody. How'd you like to be one of the Undaunted?
That's the spirit! Then I officially name you one of the Undaunted!\n\nWhat, you were expecting a big ceremony, with trumpets and oaths? No such luck for you. But you do get this ….
We're adventurers. We don't take missions, or serve an empire. We fight big, scary monsters to prove we're bigger and scarier.\n\nSo are you in, milksop?
And if I am?
Yes, yes! Now about that story. As you know, Seeks-Her-Glory and I know each other.\n\nWe've known each other. For a long time. Since yesterday, when I joined. I saw her in this very bar.
Numyn? Who?\n\nOh, the new meat? The only thing Undaunted about Numyn is his thirst for ale.
Har. You know I do. Mighty Mordra's always ready for action. Just … just as soon as I finish this drink.\n\nBut listen—listen. Listen, don't wait for me. Go on ahead. Adventure awaits!
Oh, everything! Everything! This Khajiit's friends will tell you that they fear nothing—a powerful trait! But this one is greater than they … because this one fears everything!

When I go to the stream to wash my linens? A sudden storm could spirit me away! See the sword on my back? Could take my head when I sheathe it! A Daedra wants to talk? Their words literally cut like blades!\n\nBut I live my afterlife just the same.

To be Undaunted is to be brave—and most will tell you different, but true bravery does not exist without fear.  What does the fearless Khajiit risk? Nothing!\n\nAnd those with nothing to risk have no passion to gain.
Right! Right, right. A place for an adventure. You know who likes adventure? Pirates. And I know where the pirates are.

Oh yes, I'll tell you—but only cause I like you. Har. It's called <<1>>. Kind of a big secret, so, you know. Shhh.\n\nBut you need a boat to get there! You can catch one off the coast, south of here. And tell 'em <<2>> sent ya!
Perhaps it is simply our ties to this town. Or perhaps in our last hours, we found the strength to resist Reezal-Jul and his minions.

Scholar Jonne's spirit  may still be near his home, where he taught our children with patience and humor. \n\nMage Tharlas' spirit may be at the inn. Bless her heart, she held off a horde of vampires to give a few people time to flee.
Just got back from the <<1>>. Only one on my team that survived. I'd say that earns me a bit of shut eye.
Gladiator arena. Away off in the Rift. Dangerous place. Bloody place. Good fun.\n\nNow let me get some rest.

Where would be the fun in that?\n\nThe individual yarns of fate do not concern me. It is the tapestry they weave that I watch and record. All threads, even yours, only make up a small part of the whole.

There are ancient ruins on the border of Rivenspire, called the <<1>>, overrun by undead. I'm going to seek it out—drive the evil from it. 'Course, I'll finish this drink first.\n\nIf you beat me there, I look forward to looting your corpse.
I did no such thing. Like moths to a flame, my followers are simply drawn to dark mysteries. This one was simply too irresistible to ignore. \n\nIt is a wonder more of them did not die.

I do. I can see your future … and your past. The yarn of your life is interesting, perhaps even amusing, one might say.\n\nIt is spun from a strong thread, to be sure, but all threads will eventually run out.
Ні.
Yes. That is what you will do.\n\nFirst though, I have something for you. A gift, you might say.
No. Why would I?
Name's Sahba. Sahba the Bonecrusher. Good to see a fellow Undaunted.\n\nAnd a live one, at that. I'm glad the extended family's still recruiting new members.

Well, since you asked so nicely! One of the guards hates cats. Really detests the creatures. I saw the guard chase a cat that ran into the barracks for more than an hour.\n\nSo bring a cat along. I saw a lot of them hovering around the Argonians.
I don't care much for that story. Ask Tubidan if you must.
There's not much I can do. Can't move on from this plane. And being dead, I can't return to Tamriel. At least there are Daedra to match blades with.

I don't think I'm your typical spirit, but I'm as dead as a tree in Apocrypha.\n\nThough you don't have to be alive to be an Undaunted—especially in Coldharbour. I've seen Daedra torture and flay the dead as easily as they do the living.
It would have to be the cuisine. Bosmer food is perhaps the most complex, subtle, and exquisite in all of Tamriel.

I was just passing through between adventures. I'd say it was the delicious drink that gave me cause to stay, but that'd be a lie. This swill is disgusting.\n\nBeing drunk stopped me. I hate this place, but I know where the watering holes are.

Does a cave infested with Goblins and dreugh sound like a good fight? Because that's what you'll find in Fungal Grotto.\n\nIt's out in Stonefalls. Rumor has it even the Goblins are scared to death of the thing that crawled out from the depths there.
Sweet relief. No more voices, no more restraint. Bodies and minds together again.\n\nThe crows of Jackdaw Cove are in your debt.
Yes, free and feasted! The Hagraven was all skin and bones, but what's there is sweet to eat.\n\nSo thank you for saving us, and thank you for supper!
I've two leads. One is in Daggerfall territory, the other in Ebonheart Pact.

<<1>> comes to mind. I hear the Daedra have taken a special interest in a Wood Elf village there—unleashed an army upon it. Whatever name that place had, they're calling it the <<2>>, now.\n\nThink you can fight an army of Daedra?
Something wet. Something now. Something you pay for.
Ah. I erect the spine of gratitude. Lack of moisture makes me … curt.
You buy, I'll drink. I don't rightly care what it is.

You'll find the Elden Hollow just beneath us—an ancient graveyard for centaurs and minotaurs. \n\nAnd—listen to this—a Dominion Canonreeve was recently seen there, with a full contingent of Justiciars! None can say why.

This one has heard of giant subterranean creatures called Kwama. Apparently the Dark Elves raise them so they can eat their eggs!\n\nThere's a mine in Deshaan, Darkshade Caverns, where one can see these creatures!
Sure. I suppose I could use another to wash down the last. It's all brown and flavorless around here anyway.\n\nJust hand me some gold. Get it myself.
Don't know.\n\nNo Daedra's been able to claim my second life.
Great. Thanks. What else you want? Oh. You want wit. My wit. Here goes—you can't spell Jyggalag without Wabbajack!\n\nWait. Yes. Yes, you can.

While wandering through Stormhaven, I saw bandits swarming the Wayrest Sewers. I'm not talking a few, either. Something big is about to happen.\n\nEither that … or I just saw one bandit. Many, many times.

I only advise you to seek glory while you can, young one. And I may know of a place where you can do just that.\n\nIn <<1>>, there's on old Imperial fort called <<2>>. It's infested with lamias, on top of its natural dangers. None who enter return.
It's an untamed forest. A feral place.\n\nIf the rumors are true, then the Guild Mages in <<1>> have gone there, tracked something—something of great value to them, a creature, a person—to <<2>>.

There's an old fortress by the name of <<1>>, way out in <<2>>. It was abandoned, but now serves as home to a horde of lamia.\n\nIf you're looking for a fight, lamia are always ready to dance with you.
By the Hist, yes. All the drinks. I want all the drinks.
Thank you! Now to drink until I stop seeing the forest when I close my eyes.
Bunches. For instance, there's this place in <<1>> called the <<2>>.\n\nSupposed to have been a mage's school or some such. Now the place is haunted. Or cursed. I can never remember which.

Here in <<1>>, there are rumors flying of a Bosmer village in flames—and that the Daedra set them! That there's a Daedric army there! \n\nI didn't catch the village's name, but the locals have taken to calling it the <<2>>.
Then I've got two right up your alley.\n\nOne's a fortress full of lamia—snake women, and the other's a Bosmer village under siege by—listen to this—Daedra!
Well, any day your aren't eaten by ghosts is a good day, yes? Though you may feel different after what happens next.
Alik'r.
Ah, yes. Sorry. Must be the drink.\n\nLots of creatures to fight in Alik'r. As well as the ancient Dwemer city of <<1>>. Was buried in sand, recently discovered.
What?

It's a fortress of ice and stone where the dead walk. It looms in the mountains of <<1>>. Been deserted for years. \n\nWe thought we could claim the property—I entered with fifteen men, and was the only one who returned.
I'm telling you! I know that curious look in your eye! You'll find nothing there but death and a cold that cuts like a knife.
By shattering knees. Not as many as people say—about a dozen of them. A dozen pairs.
What a wonderful idea! Yes, Khajiit would love a drink.
Ah, fuel for Khajiit. Makes retirement almost bearable.

Yes, about that. It's not so much a bruising as it is a storm. The storm of the age, if rumors are true! It surrounds an ancient and massive ruin off the coast of <<1>>. On <<2>>.\n\nNo ship that approaches has returned.

Depends on how much you like the cold. I hear there's a witch in these parts. If the rumors are true, she's taken <<1>> for her own. Sounds ripe for an Undaunted to get involved!\n\nI'd go myself, but then I'd have to part with my charming company.
Oh they're interested but you needn't worry about that. You just take care of <<1>> and leave this to me.
There's always something.\n\nHow do you feel about a trip through the desert?
Are you sure you want to ask me? I don't hand out milk-runs like those soft-arms in Auridon.
Fiercest pirates you've ever met! Never been stopped! Run rampant for years, doing whatever it is they please!\n\nAn Undaunted would do very well to face them down and survive.

There's hope for you yet, new blood. Seek out the island called Blackheart Haven. It's a hotbed of pirates and privateers.\n\nAnd it's where Captain Blackheart anchors his infamous warship, the Black Oath.
I do! It's called the <<1>>, a gladiator arena of the best sort. You'll find warriors, monsters, and blood.\n\nA mystical combination of everything a growing girl needs.
You'll find it way off in the Rift. If you can get past the stink of the Nords, it's a wonderful place.
That is what the Empress of Bone said!
Excellent. The sober world bores and infuriates the Empress of Bone.

<<1>>, buried in the jungles of <<2>>, is a forest untamed.\n\nFew bother to venture there—nothing to see, nothing to find—but a large contingent of Guild Mages was seen in and out of there, recently.

I heard a drunken laborer scream about an ancient Dwarven ruin in Alik'r called <<1>>. Full of ghastly Dwarven traps. The man was part of an expedition there—an expedition run by a right pretty lass!\n\nShame I'm already occupied here.

I was in <<1>> recently and I heard there's trouble on Tempest Island, off the coast. Storms there are always violent, but especially so right now.\n\nRumor is it's the Sea Elves—that the storms are a prelude to invasion!
I don't want a drink.\n\nI want twelve.
Thanks again, friend. I'll be one singing your praises—if you come back alive. You lot seem to have trouble with that.

I can order for myself, thank you. Just shovel the gold. You Undaunted are a strange lot. Do you go around buying drinks for everybody? You probably do. Maybe I have Felvyn misunderstood.\n\nProbably not.
Truly, it is!\n\nTake this loaf of bread, for example. Scrumptious—and textured like a wooden post! So delightful to scratch!

And by the Light, we'll be ready for the mad lizard. We were tracking him when we ran into these poor, displaced people. We threw together this camp to shelter the refugees from Crestshade and the surrounding countryside.
Grulzul carries my orders to Generals Khamagash and Am-Shadal. These are posted in the mission boards for all to see.\n\nSpeak with General Khamagash to learn more.

The Sentinel is part of an ancient pact, made long before living memory. A guardian of the woods, of sorts, who anoints his or her successor without needing our approval.\n\nNot all wyrd believe we should continue to honor the pact.

The Glenmoril Wyrd were not a party to the original pact. It's only our connection to the forest which binds us to it.\n\nThe Sentinel is no true ally to the wyresses of the Viridian Wood. His sway over the natural order is anything but natural.

The forest is old and powerful. Long ago, a man not of the forest found a way to harness the forest's power and bend it to the will of his people.\n\nThey called him the Viridian Sentinel. The title, and its power, has been passed down for generations.

Since my sister decided to visit, I must secure the camp. To this end, I need someone to find Jonah Marose.\n\nJonah claimed he could sense <<1>>. Made the other refugees nervous. He and his mother fled the camp and disappeared.

Thank you for respecting my wishes. Perhaps you can convince Glarikha to do the same. She's already off again, investigating some ship at the docks.\n\nThese matters are the duke's concern now, and he has my support. He'll appreciate your help though.

Bandits, running themselves onto our swords. Drove them off for now.\n\nThing is, there are far more bandits than we have swords. With so many afflicted by the curse, we can't hunt them down and kill them in their beds.
Magical sickness. <<1>> handles all that. Me, I guard the gate.\n\nKnow anything about stopping curses? Head inside. Shaman said he needs another set of hands.

Yes. He's actually most likely to be down in Eamond's private rooms. Unworthy swine that he is.\n\nWill you come with me? I could call the guard, but it might be better if you and I just deal with this quickly. And quietly.

No! Glarikha? Glarikha is … gone? But why? She was an innocent young girl. I knew the Imperials were heartless, but do they have no honor at all?\n\nRenchant. He's responsible for this, too. Where is that bastard?
Both were known to drink heavily. We thought they had been careless with a lantern.\n\nThe chief's wives had a reputation for scheming. I tried not to believe it, but to see it on the page ….
Anything, as long as I'm not paying for it.
My good eye thanks you, friend. My sagas won't write themselves.
Just tried my luck in the <<1>>. I made it out, but nearly lost my neck.\n\nI'm not as young as I used to be.

You've never heard of the <<1>>? It's a gladiatorial arena here in the Rift. Talk about a true test of warrior prowess. I'd say earning the Brimstone Crown from the Champion is a proper test for all Undaunted!\n\nMaybe you should give it a try.

Heard there's some Mages Guild activity off in Reaper's March.\n\nDon't know what all the fuss is about, but our Undaunted brethren have spotted a group of them heading to a forest called <<1>>. I'm spent for today. But you could follow them.

Don't know. The Undaunted I heard it from heard it from a mage. Never knew that forest had a name.\n\nI'd be careful if you plan to visit. Sometimes mage problems can't be talked down. Or punched. Or killed.
Was a pirate. I don't mingle with the Captain any longer.\n\nThe Captain's … changed a bit. Not for the better.

I'm a knight in search of a noble cause, if you will. Currently, that cause is supporting Countess Tamrith.\n\nI admit, I can sometimes get distracted by a beautiful woman, but what's wrong with that? Nothing as far as I'm concerned.

Baron Wylon Montclair. Not much to say really. Before this, he shared rule with two other noble houses, Dorell and Tamrith. \n\nCountess Tamrith says they were never very close, but she certainly wasn't expecting him to start a war.

Are you hard of hearing? I just ….\n\nNever mind. You lot are impossible. His hideout is called <<1>>—you'll need a boat to get there. Shouldn't have trouble finding one around <<2>>. You didn't hear it from me, though. Got that?

Whatever it takes to get by. Listen—you're an Undaunted, aren't you? I can tell—your colleagues here had their eyes on you soon as you came in.\n\nIf you haven't run into Captain Blackheart yet—don't go looking.

I'm forgetting about that brawl in Shadowfen. Maybe twenty pairs.\n\nI don't set out to do it. It's just … when a battle begins, I naturally gravitate towards the knees. The unwitting present them as easy targets—a wonderful gift in a fight.

I know a lot of stories, I guess. But mostly, I try to tell things how they happened. So go on, ask me how something happened.\n\nMaybe a story about why nature works. Or why we Bosmer drink all the time. Or the way Falinesti was, when it was.

Y'ffre sang to the chaos and told it to stop being so chaotic. They formed a committee, or something, and from the chaos came Nature and its laws.\n\nTrees are trees, and trees grow. Beasts are beasts, and graze or prey on one another. You know.

A long, long time ago, shortly after the beginning of time, Y'ffre crystallized and became Himself. This is common knowledge. Everyone knows this. Well, mostly everyone.\n\nAnyway, for a while after the World was made, everything was chaos. All of it.

Well, mostly, for some reason we—we mortals, I mean—were all plants and animals and people all at the same time.\n\nI'm not really sure how that would work. Like were-creatures, maybe. Except, you know, always changing, all the time.
Maybe. Probably.\n\nI don't know, does it really matter? It's the way things are.

Oh, well the mortals could understand these laws. So that gave them—us, really, I should say—a feeling of safety in the world.\n\nBecause it was no longer really chaos, you know? Through our ability to grasp it, we could live with it or control it.

Oh, I love this story. I always end up with a drink after it. So, drinking is a sacrament to Y'ffre. Can you guess why that is?\n\nNever mind, let me tell you. It's because it's his way of reminding us not to take things too seriously.

Well, yes. You know how the other Elves are. Altmer have their crystal towers, and that's how they want to be—cold and perfect. And Dunmer are just like their Red Mountain—smoldering and dark.\n\nWe just want to have a drink and not worry about it.
Well, there is, but it's not really important. So don't worry about it.\n\nAfter all, if you worry about it, you're living contrary to how Y'ffre would want you to. You see?

Falinesti was and is a walking city. A city in the trees, as any good Bosmer city must be, but the graht-trees in which Falinesti was built, themselves, were big walkers.\n\nThey loved a good hike, you know? So they hiked all the time.
I know only what scholars have told me. They were Elves who worshiped Daedra, enslaved and tortured others, and were vile beyond words. They died long ago, leaving behind ruins like Sercen.
One never knows until one is inside. Some hold naught but dust and cobwebs. Others contain shards of pottery and faded art. Great danger always awaits inside, as the Ayleids' evil lingers.
