I should've said "probably is," I suppose. Falinesti had … four? Four sites it would stop and rest at, one for every season of the year. So I suppose it didn't hike all the time. Not always, at least.\n\nAnyway, it hasn't been seen for some time.
Well, you asked me to. And it's interesting to think about, isn't it?

I could tell you a hundred reasons why, but none of them would be true. So I won't.\n\nThe truth is, nobody seems to know. King Camoran might—the Camorans used to keep their throne in Falinesti—but you'd have to ask him about it.

I do not spin in terms of "whats" but rather in "whens." The Now of the songs that fill me consider the seas and skies, and that sea and sky beyond those of Mundus—Aetherius.\n\nSo I may speak on any of these concerns—for now.

Y'ffre taught the birds to sing and the waves to lap against the beach. Through Y'ffre's song, he also gained sight-perception of all that occurs within the sight of birds and the reflection of waters, and he echoes their songs and crashing waves.

The Sea is all-enclosing, the water that encircles all of Mundus. The birds call out that which occurs over land to the sea, which reflects and echoes that song.\n\nThrough study of the Sea's mystery it is possible to interpret Y'ffre's song-tapestry.

Of course. He sees and hears nothing, for Y'ffre is now the Earth-Bones, the frame upon which Nature is laid and woven. His sight-perception and song-echo instead are loomed through his bones and woven into tapestries of song for we mortals to study.

To sing a law, and then Speak into the heart of that law, convincing it of a subtle error and how it must change its own Self.\n\nThis is how Nature's course—its own Sea—is shaped and reshaped over time. Such changes can affect the whole of Mundus.

You already do, as do all mortals. Your frame of perception of the world is your own Bones, akin to the Earth-Bones. It is as possible to see into your own future and world as it is to immerse the Self in hysteria with no fear.

The sky mirrors the sea, and the sea also reflects its mirror. Day, night, and the places between are the realm of the sky, as Y'ffre interpreted the time-law Anui-el established within Nirn.\n\nThus, the sky bridges time and nature, and measures both.

Within each half of the sphere of reflection lies half of the potentialities of Nirn's way in any given moment. Each instant is a sea-state or sky-state. Each individual sees one or its other as weal or woe, and each moment can be turned on its side.

Yes. Change is wrought in Nirn in six ways, and the turning of islands is one of these, often described by others in other terms.\n\nOf course, it is possible to acknowledge these ways without understanding them—to spin them is all I can do.

Each moment so turned becomes an island in your path. For example, the Dwemer, united, had their way in Dwemeris.\n\nBut one clan—Rourken, the wayward clan—struck anchor and sailed across the sky. Why do this? Mired in a sea, they sought the sky.

Aetherius is the sea of light, the Immortal Plane, the origin of magic. Y'ffre sings not of Aetherius, but to it, weaving a song so beautiful that stars were compelled to dance and twinkle and sway.\n\nThey still wink and blink in memory of that song.

They are Aetherius. Rather, the sun and stars are holes pierced into the veil of night by Magnus—and other spirits—seeking to escape Nirn.\n\nThese holes permit Aetherius' light to enter our world. From theirs to ours does Magicka trickle.

Now, that is an enormous question that I cannot answer. Many souls of mortals become spirits of another sort in that place—and that is all I can say with any certainty. As difficult as it is to travel to Oblivion, it is far more to go to Aetherius.

Well, consider this. As Oblivion is a realm composed of realms, so, too, is Aetherius a bright sea with many realms within.\n\nEach of these stars is a window into these realms, and as these realms move, so too do they move. Or close, like doors.
Really? You read Akaviri?\n\nNo matter, you're welcome to it. Let me see, I have a copy around here somewhere. A moment, please.

This is wonderful! Nobody here will be able to find the source of my stories if they're written in another language.\n\nMy Akaviri is a bit stale, but I think I can manage. You're welcome to stay for my performance!
Then she's in luck! I served the Eight Divines before joining the Mages Guild. I know what must be done to safely transport a relic such as <<1>>.\n\nWe'll just need to find it before <<2>> does.
Well, he wasn't there when I last checked, but it's been several hours now … There's a tavern he's gone to before to meet his latest mistress. Check there.
I saw him at the tavern a few times, the Snakeskin Suds. Check there. Someone there's bound to know something.
I'm not sure where he is now. If I knew that, I'd be after him myself, wouldn't I?
I thought I'd find him nearby, but I was wrong.
You're right, I didn't.
You've heard of the Black Drake, yes?

Funny …. It's been decades—but now facing these Imperials, it feels like days.\n\nLong ago, the Reachmen were called to war by a mighty chieftain known as Durcorach "The Black Drake." A feral man-mountain.

Hircine gave this gift to the first hunters to worship him. To honor them, he took their cunning and melded it to the strength and form of beasts. \n\nIt's said those original hunters live on in the Great Hunt, Hircine's own realm, to this day.
<<1>> headed to explore <<Ac:2>>. Once the wards broke, I sent <<3>> to fetch him. Neither returned.\n\nMages Guild protocol says I should remain in place until aid arrives. I'm hoping that's you.
No clue. It was my Mages Guild informant who referred to the forest as Selene's Web.\n\nI bet you'll find out why—if you go.
I name no names, but seek the poor near the town square. Ask if they've seen a cat with red fur, and there will be your answer.
A most precious gift! May the gods smile with favor upon you.\n\nI'll keep it safe until the time comes, and our mutual friend returns. And may he return soon, for all our sakes.

It's a secret this one learned from the Moons! Especially Jode, who is chatterbox.\n\nVampire skeevers lurk in shadows to hide from Moons. If you sleep without light on, ziss! Suck your blood right out. But they don't like heat, so south I go!
I will guard this with my life, though I wish our mutual friend would return. This will prove quite useful in his absence.\n\nYou've risked much to help us. Thank you.
I'm afraid the "giant Daedric anchors from the sky" issue is more your speciality than my own. I'll let you lead on this one.
"A wise leader knows how to delegate," my father used to say. He may have died in his cups, but the man knew his aphorisms.\n\nWhat could be more kingly?
Yes, walker! This is the smile of a spotless conscience. My days of wickedness are over!

<<1>> entered the room before you did. I called out his name, asking for help, but he just grinned.\n\nThat's when I knew it was an illusion. <<1>> always says smiles are the hallmark of idiots and fools. Sure enough, the illusion vanished.

Yes. It pains me to say this, but this one was not always so virtuous. I spent my time thieving, and gambling, and resting my chin on the bosoms of disreputable women. It was a moon-lost time …. But it helped this one find his true calling!

I convinced my performers to come here, to spread High Elf culture in these lands. Bring a little piece of Summerset to <<1>>, you see?\n\nBut the trained bugs are sick, our magician's supplies are missing, and our storyteller's stories fell flat!

None of us know the area well enough to resolve these matters. Now we're a carnival with nothing but a fortune-teller. Huzzah.\n\nI'd gladly pay the coin provided by the Summerset Cultural Expansion Council to anyone who would help us put on the show.

At the base of the mighty tree in Grahtwood lies a burial ground once used by centaurs and minotaurs.\n\nThe locals call it Elden Hollow, and I've heard a Dominion Canonreeve passed through there recently.
Arkay rejected our kind as terrors of the night. He turned his holy gaze away from us and turned the light against us.\n\nHe plots our destruction. He is the forsaker.

When Mother Lamae was a mere mortal, Molag Bal defiled her and left her to the grave. But she awoke from her death-like state, riven with an insatiable hunger for blood. His blood, above all.\n\nHe is our Dark Father. He is also our hated enemy.
He was a necromancer, one of <<1>>'s most talented apprentices. But he and his wife <<2>> eventually left <<1>>'s tutelage.

His case came up today, so your timing is excellent. I'll signal ahead that you're coming in.\n\nWe ask that you don't stray from the town once you pass the cave. The woods beyond the village aren't safe.
It isn't entirely clear. There are many theories, but they all boil down to a difference of opinion.\n\nSeems to be the way of things with necromancers.
He's rich, and there's plenty to take if you've got a quick hand—but I'll be blunt.\n\nHe'll kill you. The Captain hates the adventuring sort. Especially near his property.
What? Ha! Oh no—Quickpaw is still a thief. But now Quickpaw uses his ten-clawed gifts for good!

They sent Quickpaw away because he talks too much. But someone has to recruit new talent, yes? Here—I'll mark the hideout on your map. If you wish to help the poor and twist the tail of dungy nobles, go there and tell them Quickpaw sent you!

Quickpaw should not speak of it … but you are trustworthy, yes? There is a gang of robbers and pickpockets living in some ruins to the north. They rob from greedy duck-pawed nobles and give the spoils to the poor. This is virtuous, yes?

Splendid. I'll allow you the honor of informing <<1>>.\n\nWhy not tell him the duly selected High Elf ambassador was working against the very Dominion she pledged to support? I'll sit in my throne and try not to gloat.
I don't know.\n\nI wish you could use the bone scepter on him. Point it at his body, there on the throne, and tell him to go to sleep. Then I could finally leave.

Ah, Talisse and I have a storied history. They call us the twins, but I was an Undaunted first. She was rather taken by my methods—effective as they are. So she imitated me.\n\nI wasn't put off—much—highest form of flattery and all that, right?
She's bigger—slightly more buffoonish, if you ask me—but I'm better.\n\nI've saved her life more times than she's saved mine, at any rate.
It's a very long story, but the short version is through magic. I bind the villagers, voluntarily, to each other in our original forms. Once bound, transformation into any alternative can't happen.

No one's ever left. We're happy here. Safe.\n\nOnce bound, even partially, if they leave the hollow, they'll break the entire bond and change form forever. Draven must see this. We will lose control, little by little, unless he completes the ritual.

Yes. That's why we require a stay without their family before their acceptance. They must understand what it will be like without their loved ones.\n\nCan they cope? Can they live in this village forever? They must be sure, or we won't risk it.

To start: a hunter's challenge of skill. I will bring the Hunting Ground to you: a shade of this realm and my own. But this time, you hunt my aspects themselves. Only then will you earn the chance to retake the grotto for the wyrd.

Don't disappoint me, pup. Prey aren't deserving of the gift I've given you. When you've won, return to the shrine. I will be there as the Spirit of the Hunt.\n\nWe'll discuss your prowess and your final task for the grotto when the hunt is over.
Thank you. We've but one recourse left to us at this point. Draven must be removed.
No, and now that I know what it is, it doesn't matter. I've known him all my life. This is the first time he's ever kept anything secret from me.
We'll need to work on talking over our troubles with each other, instead of hiding our problems. Our lives will be different, but I'm sure other couples have issues too.
More often than you'd imagine. We heal those we can of other ailments, but of course, our main purpose is to bind those with lycanthropy to their normal form.
True. Some might say it's another curse rather than an actual cure.\n\nThey might be right, but we live as peacefully as we can. We don't look for trouble. And we grieve whenever it finds us.

I will seek the man who runs this accursed camp, <<1>>. He and his men are concentrated on the other side of the encampment beyond the palisade wall, by the barred gate.\n\nShould you need me, look for me there after you give <<2>> the key.

Yes. Princess Elara, daughter of Queen Arzhela. I rescued her from a near fatal attack. Her mother still thinks her dead.\n\nI know it seems callous, but that's how it must remain, for now. I've no wish to break the poor woman's heart twice.

Yes. Why are you staring like that?\n\nTempest Island is known for bad weather, but nothing like this! They're saying it's the Sea Elves' magic at work! There are even whispers of an invasion of Malabal Tor! Sounds to me like you should make a trip.
Is this some kind of jest?

Well, if you're truthfully with <<1>> then I've already said enough to seal my fate.\n\nLook for a chamber on the far side of the mine. There you'll find a massive stockpile of coal, which is a tempting target for sabotage. If one was so inclined.

Trust? <<1>>'s damned games have torn all trust from us!\n\nIf you're here to dupe me, then just get on with it and dupe me. I'd rather be chained out in the sun than suffer the indignation of being played with like a puppy.
I still find it hard to believe that this is truly an escape attempt.
And if we never find it? No, kill the spriggans. It's the best chance to do this quickly.
Hard to say. While a Green Lady is terrifically hard to kill, she is mortal. A powerful blow from a Daedra, perhaps?\n\nMore likely, she died of old age … or perhaps her Silvenar was killed.
Yes. So it was with <<1>>, who was Green Lady before this one.\n\nOnce the Green Lady and Silvenar are wed, their bond is inescapable. If one dies, the other must follow suit.
Let's see … oh, dear. Did you drink any of this?
What self-control! This is my experimental self-replenishing wine. Bandits stole it from my caravan a week ago.
Oh, thank Vivec! This is my experiment in self-replenishing wine. Bandits stole it from my caravan a week ago.
Amazing, isn't it? It'll make me rich someday, if I can ever work out the wrinkles. There are … unintended side effects.

He didn't even trust you enough to tell you, did he? Let the Sentinel explain it to you when you next see him. I'll do my part and no more.\n\nWhere is this princess who is greater than the needs of nature?
Is it not obvious? I'm the Empress of Bone!\n\nThe only one that the Undaunted have got!
Because I love bones! Fashionable and practical!\n\nOnce tore a rib right out of an Orc—do you know how hard that is? Orc bones are like steel! Then I clubbed the bastard unconscious with it!
Of course, and this bud may heal Stenwick, the way he healed me. We'll need to use it if we're to save him.\n\nTake him to that altar in the lake. I'll meet you there.

The Empress doesn't care.\n\nThe only thing the Empress knows is that where there are mages, there are bones. Carried in their pouches—and their bodies, if they prove to be troublesome. The Empress would go, but the Empress has a drink to finish.
So much has happened to me, it's hard to think clearly.
Oh, my. At least we won't have to worry about raids for a while. Although that could get very strange.\n\nOur housecarl <<1>> has been concerned about <<2>>. You should tell him what happened.

Well, the wine replenishes itself, but it also replenishes your thirst. The more you drink, the more you want to drink, until you wake up the next town over, and everyone's calling you Mrs. Bedingfield.\n\nNot that I speak from experience, of course.

No, I belong here, in these woods. Eventually, the wyrd and I will come to terms.\n\nI see our past and present, through the eyes of the Sentinel. There will never be love between us, but understanding is not too much to ask.
Go home? No, no. It's so far away.\n\nI'll miss my family, but if I die, I'll be with them again soon, won't I?
One does not become a Master Hunter, they are chosen by Brackenleaf after years of service in his Briars.

He understood what the Sentinel meant, but she did not. Perhaps we might have reached some sort of compromise. Or perhaps not.\n\nThe Sentinel's mantle was never meant to be used this way. He broke the pact with the forest as far as I'm concerned.
Why yes, I am. I'm quite adept in restoration magic, so I spend most of my time patching up the Briars who get into rough patches. But when I can, I hunt as often as possible.

She wanted a chance to live. I don't blame her for that. But what happened, happened. We'll ease her passing as best we can. The forest will heal. And soon, we'll forget them both.\n\nOnly the land is forever, and even that is a matter for debate.
If you are truly ready, please name the accused.
I'm afraid you fell afoul of my self-replenishing wine. The bandits in <<1>> stole it from a caravan last week.
Knowing the Dwemer? Probably demented, metal traps.\n\nAnd lethal constructs with purpose only to protect Dwemer treasures. A good time for an Undaunted.
It replenishes your thirst along with the wine, so you can't stop drinking it. We found you stumbling around outside <<1>>.
Yes, I created it for my alchemical purposes. It's still experimental though, so it has some unintended effects.
You know, it's better this way. That poor cat. Some things you just can't unsee. \n\nBut I digress, our housecarl <<1>> wishes to speak to you, and I must get back to my work.
Very well. So they're really going through with it, are they? I'd pay my weight in gold to see <<c:1>> working.\n\nI'll personally ensure it reaches there without further trouble, don't you fear.
<You drain the bottle. The wine makes you drunk quickly, but you're still thirsty.>
<The world around you is spinning wildly. You feel as if you're about to pass out, but you're still thirsty. You're not sure if you'll wake up in the same place if you drink any more.>
Why, you need something, eh? \n\nA tonic for your itchy bumps? A salve for your sore nethers? An unguent for critters in your hairs?

So you didn't come to see your old granny Alyxe to sit on her lap and hear a story? Didn't want to play count the warts, eh? \n\nI might have a couple scraps I could sell, but they could be cheaper if you knew how to make an old lady's teeth tingle.
A long, long time ago. Once, I even worked as a royal gardener in Evermore. But, well, I'm more comfortable in the woods. It's where I belong.

Me? I'd left Evermore and decided to live my life in the woods. And I met a man here, the previous Sentinel. He needed help, and I stayed with him.\n\nWhen he grew too weary, he blessed me with the title.

My best friend and occasional partner, when he's not trying to pull the wool over my eyes, that is.\n\nNow, the key to these shackles is kept in their surveyor's tent on the hillside across from us. Free me, so I can kill <<1>>!

Makela Leki was the greatest sword-singer who ever lived by many people's estimation, and the stone is a record of her thoughts and experiences.\n\nIt will take scholars many years to decipher the information within, but it will be worth it.

With the swiftness of the Green, I swam to the shores of Pyandonea, home of the Sea Elves.\n\nThere, I visited my wrath upon them. I tore at flesh and bone. I cut until my arms went limp. I rent until my legs fell out beneath me.

Ha. I gave them no such pleasure.\n\nTheir greatest warrior found me spent atop their highest sea-tower. He grabbed my hair, hoping to take my head as a prize. So I grabbed him and leapt, into the waves far below. The look on his face ….
It is my duty as hengekeeper to know all of the Green Ladies. <<1>> was the last. Before Gwaering, I mean.\n\n<<1>> loved her Silvenar so much. She died soon after his assassination on <<2>>.

Who can say? The bond between Green Lady and Silvenar is such that neither can live long without the other. Some would say she died of a broken heart.\n\nBut knowing her, she broke more than a few Sea Elf hearts from their chests before she faded.

I have no more prophecies to impart, no more strategies to suggest, no more riddles to ponder. I am just a man. A flawed man. And perhaps that is just as it should be.\n\nFarewell, Vestige. Walk in the light, always.
His spirit has been dispersed into the Aetherius. He is not dead, neither is he alive. His essence is outside the cycle of the Mundus.

Tharn has undoubtedly begun the long journey back to Cyrodiil with his new prize. His deepest desire is to unite all the errant territories of the Empire under a single banner. Perhaps he will succeed, but it will be a long and arduous task.
An attack on the lighthouse? But why? That doesn't make any sense.\n\nLet me take a look at these plans.
They attacked the lighthouse? But why? That doesn't make any sense.\n\nCan I see these plans?
I'll bring the news of Sai's death to Kasura at the Abbey of Blades. Maybe I'll stay there for awhile. Help rebuild. Sai would want that.\n\nAfter that, I don't know.

Grief doesn't change us, it reveals us. That's what my father always said. \n\nI'll mourn Sai in my own way. I loved him. I know that now. There's a big, deep hole of aching inside me. Even when I'm finished mourning him, it's not going to go away.

I've never been able to sit still long. Eventually, the road will call. But where I'll wind up? Who knows? Roads are for journeys, not destinations.\n\nMaybe we'll run into each other again. Have a drink. Maybe crack some skulls for old times sake.
For a time. There is much to rebuild there, and I owe it to Kasura to bring her the news of our victory personally.\n\nSnow Lily and I, well … maybe we shall finally have some time to ourselves.
To what end? No, let him return to his Imperial City. He played his role, and that is enough. Grudges are like poison to the spirit. \n\nBut perhaps, once the Abbey of Blades has been rebuilt ….
I have never been content to remain in one place for too long. It is not my nature. Eventually I am overcome by the need to endanger myself. Between comfort and adventure, I always choose adventure.
I would like that. It has been a singular honor, Vestige. Although I suppose that name is no longer appropriate, is it? \n\nVaren would be proud of you. I know we are.
I will travel with Sai Sahan for a time. Then, perhaps I will return to the Moth Priests. The Scrolls may yet have secrets to reveal about the coming days.

Though Meridia came to your aid, you must never put your trust in her. Everything she did was to achieve her own ends. It is always thus with a Daedric Prince.\n\nThe forces of Oblivion will always be a threat to Tamriel. We must be eternally vigilant.

Our journey together has been enlightening. Few will ever know of your part in the salvation of this world, but the people of Tamriel owe you their lives. Nay, their very souls.\n\nPerhaps one day we shall meet again. Until then, walk in the light.

I don't know how, but the necromancer did something to them. It's like they know those of us he captured are for him and him alone. They didn't attack any of us. I guess that's one thing I can be grateful for, but I still want the bastard dead.
Yes, yes. Things are fuzzy, but I think I have the strength to make it back to Ivarstead. You just worry about that necromancer.

Much more than that. We're tied through both a familial bond and the forest itself. We may seem callous to outsiders, but we're closely knit.\n\nWhat we ask of you is not to be taken lightly. This is a serious and sensitive matter. Understood?

That's right. I thought he was just another grave robber. We run them out of Ivarstead from time to time. I was wrong. He's working some dark magic here. Experimenting on the living and the dead alike. Someone has to stop him.

I hope so. Take this ceremonial dagger. It's well-sharpened to ensure swift work.\n\nTiria and I will perform the ritual. Once prepared, you must act quickly to cut out the heart of Nyronie and place it on the altar.
Not after falling so far out of Hircine's favor. Believe me, if there were another way, a way to spare Nyronie's life, I'd do it.\n\nNow, will you honor her decision and help us?
He went further into the barrow. Be careful. I'll be fine on my own. Put an end to this, and find me in Ivarstead after you do. I owe you a debt for helping me.

I heard him muttering something about reanimation. Something about a curse that keeps the draugr alive. Maybe he's searching for the knowledge of those ancient rites, though I can't say why. But he's killing innocent people. We can't let that go on.
Look to the passing of time, to the order of the sun, stars, and moon for understanding.
The trick of it was the timing. With every blow to that Daedric windbag, you freed hundreds of souls. She was able to catch yours before it wandered off. Jolly good trick, that.

There is something that has been bothering me. There was a traveler, a fellow Nord, who showed up asking all sorts of strange questions about the barrow. Haven't seen him since. There was just something off about him. I wonder if he went inside?
Keep your voice down! Why do you think fences don't have storefronts?\n\nDiscretion, discretion, discretion!

Of course I do! But I can't trade while I'm on my shift. Give the diamond to me. You'll find your payment in the graveyard behind the Fighters Guild. Look for a cairn with flowers on it.\n\nDon't dig too deep. The Nords are touchy about their graves.
Fences who can't be found don't stay in business for long. And I couldn't stay here after cheating a damn hero. Bribes only get you so far. Now go!
You're a good friend, courageous and loyal and all that … but you're a terrible liar.\n\nI … I … I just wish it wasn't that wench Septima that killed me ….
No. You don't get to question me. Not after you slew <<1>>.\n\nDo you think I'm one to have a chat with the person who killed my wife? That we'll break out the sylph-mead and share a good laugh?
Hmph. I suppose that's my burden.\n\nVery well. I won't give you the satisfaction of doubting my loyalty. You were asking after the Khajiit?
Then I shall return the favor. Address all further inquiries on the matter to <<1>>.\n\nGood day.

The Empire's collapse has thrown all of Cyrodiil into chaos. All three alliances seek to take over. Grand Warlord Dortene has been given an army and orders to conquer Cyrodiil. And she is determined to see it done!

Cyrodiil is the heart of Tamriel. The alliance that rules here can strike in any direction, threatening the other heartlands. With Grand Warlord Dortene leading our armies, how can the Covenant fail to sweep all before us?

One of us is always here to care for the temple. We trust the bears to guard it well, but they can't maintain it.\n\nI was the caretaker of the grotto when the Reachmen arrived. I should have seen them coming, to get word out sooner.

Well, his exploits and demise are well documented. Less well-known is the aftermath. \n\nThe Black Drake and his horde tore Hallin's Stand to pieces. All goods of value were stolen or destroyed. All semblance of civic order was broken.

Not enough, but I did what I could.\n\nI exposed criminal plots, abducted corrupt bureaucrats, broke political prisoners out of dungeons …. Some town crier started calling me "The Sly Scarab." I'm still not exactly sure why.
Well, it had to come some day!\n\nBeing the Scarab has never been a choice—I did what I had to do. But this is my last exploit. I think it's time for a good, long walkabout in the deep desert.

I have a dead drop at the base of the Craglorn Gates. No one has left the Scarab a note for years, but I always check. Old habits, yes?\n\nAnyway, I saw the smoke from the road and decided to investigate.

These Imperial dogs are creatures of routine. They'd likely die of starvation if a dining schedule weren't posted outside the company's mess. \n\nBut we can count on them to follow orders without question.

I suspect that after Hallin's Stand was liberated they decided Old Tower was a solid and defensible position. Only Tall Papa knows why they refuse to leave Bangkorai entirely. There must be something in Hammerfell that they want.

Hallin's Stand I wager. I cannot stand the thought of those diamond-backed jackals occupying my city. Once my work here is complete I'll … what am I saying? My knees creak just climbing into bed. Scrambling rooftops at my age is a fool's game.

Do I "live" here? That is a strange choice of words. Yes indeed. As I said, this place is not for the living; it is the dead who actually "live" here.\n\nI simply watch over the place. I go back and forth between here and there.
If we knew that, then presumably, we could force her to leave. That would save us all a lot of trouble, would it not? That would certainly be nice.

Thank the gods he lives. We agreed that if we separated and neither one of us could reach the other, we'd try to get out on our own and meet at the Riften docks.\n\nWhen you get out of this pit, you should meet us there.

She caught sight of Reezal-Jul and rushed after him. I, of course, followed. His vampires surrounded us, and while I was fighting them off, the good captain was dragged away.\n\nThey took Janeve into that cave. Hurry! You need to save her!
I'm here on the Ambassador's orders. I can't leave my post unless there's an emergency.
I ….\n\nWhat? Did you hear that? I could've sworn it was my captain, calling me away.

A little of this, a little of that. Lending my sword to just causes, flirting with the ladies. I've drank in every inn and tavern between here and Glenumbra, and I beat my friend Skordo at cards every chance I get. \n\nIt's great to see you again!
About that much! I'd say that's worth a five minute stroll. Be about your business, citizen.
<<1>> had his suspicions about the embassy. Asked me to look into the matter, quietly.\n\nWe both have a stake in this. We should work together, see where it leads.

<<1>>, Vinedusk Ranger. We work directly for <<2>>. Saw you earlier, in the throne room.\n\nThe king had his suspicions about the missing work crew, and asked me to look into it. Seems we both have a stake in this.

Thank you, my friend. You are wise and merciful. I will prove to my sister that I am still the woman she knows and loves. I will never succumb to this affliction. I will never betray House Tamrith or Rivenspire.

I wish there was another way, but I must be strong. Vampires are unholy. Evil. I can't let my sister become one of these … monsters! She has to die. It will be a mercy.\n\nPlease, talk to Janeve. Try to comfort her while I pray over my decision.
Did they.\n\nThose without significance often think they control the powerful. Yet we can have their throats cut, to disabuse them of their fantasies.
I'm a High Elf from the Summerset Isles. Do you think me unfamiliar with the concept of a coup?\n\n<<1>> gained much through our marriage. But control over me? Preposterous.

No matter. You can only become a puppet if you allow it. You must choose your destiny, and refuse to let anyone else choose it for you.\n\nI choose to serve the Dominion. I would expect you do the same.
If you don't hold your tongue, I'll have it removed.\n\nYou shall not speak of my wife. Not now, not ever.

We can do this, of course. But this is about <<1>>'s word. If she cannot get her people to aid us with a simple building, how can we trust them to support us on the field of battle?\n\nSo we wait, and we see.

It is not as far as it sounds, but you do have to die to get there.\n\nIt is where mortal souls are supposed to go when they pass from this plane. Not all souls find their way, of course, but some of them do not belong anyways. You understand.
Hurry. I saw them burnishing their weapons and armor while I crept through their camp. I think they intend to march soon.
They should. I'm a fair hand at forgery, if I do say so myself. These should do the trick, all right.
Would you rather I gnash my teeth and fall to the ground weeping?\n\nSome grief is too deep to show itself. I see her body before me, and though I will miss her very much, my life will go on.

Nyronie is the daughter of my heart, and my sister in the Glenmoril Wyrd. Though she breathed her last, she will always be with us.\n\nBut your journey should go on. Be at peace in your own heart; you did the right thing to help us.
By accident, of course! These things are delicate. Tricky. One false move and—snap! I'm caught. Now my arm's asleep and my back is killing me. Can we get on with the rescue?
Does it look like I have a choice? Make it quick already! Those harpies are looking at me like I'm a three-course meal.

Armel and I were trapping the whole gully. These things are designed to go with our scent lures. But as I said, they're very finicky to set up. \n\nBah! Armel's a moron. His design's clearly faulty. If you hadn't shown up ….

Place the rest of my traps. You'll know where to put them. Armel went ahead of me to place the scent barrels—just like the one here. Put the traps with the barrels, and keep watch for my brother.\n\nAnd be careful. Don't want you ending up like me.

Right! We put down these scent barrels. They draw the harpies in and they get caught in the traps. Simple! Or so he said.\n\nI've already wasted too much time out here. I need to report in to Bumnog. Hey, would you be willing to help me out?
Then … then you need Aelif. She worked at the Master's command for years. Quiet, careful. She knows things. Things … things you want to know.

Ask a stonemason. I have to prepare for the ratification ceremony before <<1>>'s arrival. I can't be troubled with such minor issues.\n\nIf you care to pursue the matter, speak with <<2>> at <<Ac:3>>.

No matter. You can only become a puppet if you allow it. You must choose your destiny, and refuse to let anyone else choose it for you.\n\nI choose to serve the Dominion. I would expect you do the same.
Cruel … fire burns so hot … skin melts, eyes melt. Every day I burn and burn. Every day I burn again anew. Please … let me go.
I refuse … refuse to grovel and wet myself for your amusement. I served the Master, taught his lessons, reveled in his power. I knew what awaited me if I failed. And I'd do it all again if I could!
I am the rightful king! I am the rightful ruler of the Isles! Let me out of here! Let me out of here that I might take my place ….
It's … it's clear I chose the wrong side. I should have seen the greatness in you. Let me out, and the Seventh Legion will be yours to command!
The tear in the veil between Oblivion and Nirn has been repaired. Your world is safe, for now.

House Ravenwatch is an old Rivenspire family. As for Verandis, I do not like the man.\n\nBe that as it may, and despite his long friendship with Montclair, the Count seems genuine in his willingness to help. He cares deeply about our people.
I am a lesser noble of the city, offering what assistance I can during this time of trouble.
<<1>>, Vinedusk Ranger. You could say we keep <<2>> in touch with his people.\n\nWatch yourself. The boughs of the Elden Tree are bright and beautiful, but they cast long shadows.
For my family. For what … what I once had, on that cold little island. I deserve this, I know. But please, I'm asking you as a friend. Let me be ended.
Get out of my sight, mewling cow. You chose my milk-drinker of a brother, ended my quest for rule. And now the Prince has me, all for breaking the bonds of brotherhood. Go!
Dorell sees traitors behind every pillar, but his intentions are good. He truly cares for Rivenspire and its people.\n\nHe simply has the social skills of a sober Nord.

Tamrith is overly occupied with spiritual matters. She'd rather pray for my lost soul than engage in a rational discussion. Much like her mother.\n\nHer late father was another matter. Sensible, strong, pragmatic. Her younger sister takes after him.
The Baron and I were friends, yes. Good friends. But that was before this madness overtook him.
A year ago, the king nearly lost <<1>> to a civil war. People have long memories.\n\nBut that's old news. Just keep your wits about you and you'll be fine.
Think of the things we did together, comrade. Our hunt for the traitor … fighting the Dwemer constructs. Remember Aelif—your friend.
Of course. I am a veritable treasure trove of useless information, and I love to share.

I've known Count Ravenwatch since I was a boy. My father even sent me to study with him for a time.\n\nHouse Ravenwatch is one of the oldest noble houses of Rivenspire. Quite a legacy, and Verandis carries it well.

As long as it takes. I knew that having the noble houses share the throne wouldn't last. I should've chosen one of them to rule years ago.\n\nTo be honest, I feel I'm partly to blame for all of this, and it's my duty to be here and see it resolved.

Rumors and wild tales, for the most part. We did receive a dispatch from a Captain Janeve. Apparently, something occurred in the town of Crestshade—something devastating enough to require the captain to set up a camp for refugees.

I think he did it because he was tired of bloodshed and he knew he could trust me to always work toward peace.\n\nIf I can end this conflict and restore it here, I will consider my debt to Verandis paid in full.

Well, if you must know, he's part of the reason I'm wearing this crown. When I first proposed to form the Covenant, many people opposed me.\n\nVerandis, however, without any urging, supported my plans and helped sway opinions in my favor.

The last time I brought an army to Rivenspire, it was to put an end to Ranser's War. That isn't a memory I want to reawaken in this region.\n\nBesides, it will be better for all concerned if Rivenspire resolves its own problems.

Very little. It's a small town at the foot of the western mountains. Since you're heading in that direction to see Verandis, perhaps you can look in on Crestshade? I'd be grateful if you can determine what actually happened out there.

Bunch of whiners, Montclair's troops. The moment we really pushed back, they broke off and demanded we accept their surrender. \n\nDorell wants to execute the lot of them, but the Countess wants to consult with the High King. Too soft-hearted, she is.
I suspect that there's more to that story, but perhaps now isn't the time to get into it.\n\nHere comes the Countess now.

Wanted to let you know that High King Emeric has arrived. He's in Shornhelm Castle with the Baron and the Countess.\n\nMe? I think I might leave when this is all over. Join the Fighters Guild. See the world. I certainly could use the change.

Oh, yes—his name's Mareh. He's rather a crazy old hermit, but he certainly knows his way around these old Yokudan ruins. \n\nHe lives in a nearby cave overlooking the ruins. Hermit's Climb, they call it.
Focus of Redguard teleportation magic! Very powerful, exactly what this one needs! I think.
Nonsense, it was a great deal of trouble. It's not something one forgets, especially when one is a queen.

I have been called far worse. But I prefer to think of myself and my companions as gifted. We are not ashamed of our condition. We are not monsters.\n\nNow this is the part where you gasp and ask calmly, "How can I trust you?"

The High King is a wise man, which is why I supported him and not the mad king, Ranser.\n\nWe all have the ability to make our own decisions. Long ago, I decided to live in peace with the mortal world, not feast upon it.

We all have to eat. But unlike your meals, my sustenance voluntarily allows me to sup. And then gets to walk away and go on with its life.\n\nWhen was the last time a deer or a rabbit approached you and gladly died so that you could have your fill?

There's the reaction I was waiting for! But what will attacking me gain you? A sound beating? The enmity of my friend the High King?\n\nUnderstand this—no one knows Montclair better than I. If you hope to defeat him, you need my help.

I sent my sister Janeve to investigate reports of trouble in the west. She's a captain in the Shornhelm Guard, you know.\n\nI'm worried, though. She hasn't sent a report in quite some time. If the High King can spare me, I might ride out to meet her.

You were able to drive off Reezal-Jul and take back Shornhelm. Those were no small feats, I assure you. But Emeric needs our help to restore Rivenspire's tranquility.\n\nYou need to understand. There is more to Montclair than simple ambition.
Walk with me and I will explain. There is much I need to show you and time grows short.

Not as close as we were. When I went to study in Stormhaven, Janeve joined the Guard. We don't always see eye to eye, but we are sisters.\n\nI'm sure she's fine, but I wish I could get her to send dispatches on a regular basis.

She's always been rather lackadaisical about filing reports, but we did receive word that she had set up a camp for refugees. It's obvious something terrible is going on out there.\n\nI want to make sure she's all right.
You're not a part of their group, as I said. I'm not trying to cheat them. I just want to know if they did what they said they would. Is their effort here today worth our hard-earned gold?
Then, in accordance with our contract, I cannot pay them.\n\nYour honesty is refreshing. Thank you.
I am pleased to hear this! When the harpies attacked our horses, we were desperate. They're as dear to us as our children.\n\nWe will gladly call on this group again should the harpies return.

She claims that she wants to be here when we finally catch the mad Argonian, and that she wants to reassure the refugees with her presence.\n\nBut I think she's really here to check up on me. I'm not sure she actually trusts her little sister.

Yes, yes. My full name is Janeve Tamrith, second daughter of House Tamrith and captain of the Shornhelm Guard.\n\nI'm proud of my heritage, but I don't expect my house connections to open any doors. I want to be judged on my merits, not my name.

I'd prefer to be out in the field, but I expect the High King will send me where he will.\n\nAt least my son, Ellic, can manage House Dorell holdings while I deal with the broader concerns of Rivenspire.

Take counsel with the High King, of course. We've been hearing reports of an unusual number of bloodfiends popping up throughout the countryside. That's just one more problem to add to our growing list of concerns.
Ask your questions, then. I will answer what I can.

Nothing that will harm you, rest assured.\n\nThe mixture contains various herbs, dusk nectar, and a few drops of my blood. But don't worry. It takes more than a little blood to turn someone into a vampire.

Then we learn nothing new. Montclair continues his campaign and Rivenspire eventually falls. It is inevitable.\n\nPlease. As you will see, I have blind spots where Montclair is concerned. I need a fresh perspective to determine our next moves.

They know me too well, and they are used to acquiescing to my will. They don't have the perspective, the distance, to see beyond what I saw.\n\nI need someone who has proven their worth, a relative stranger that I can trust.

My pleasure! I can talk to you and watch for harpies at the same time.\n\nWe're really proving ourselves here, I think. Proving our worth as sellswords. Or we would be if those two morons weren't ruining everything.

A little village of horse nomads. The place is called Silverhoof Vale. Their elder tried to tell me all about her love for the Herd Mother, and … yeah. My eyes just kind of glazed over when she got to the part about talking horses.

The Fighters Guild has stopped doing one-shot contracts, right? Off on some grand quest to kill the Daedra. So we have a chance to make a name for ourselves! Critters like these harpies are still causing trouble. That's where we come in.

What an inane question.\n\nThe Bosmer of Valenwood hold all plantlife in the highest regard. We've made a Pact not to harm them, and to use no wood or greenery in anything we create. It can be a difficult life.
Yes, it makes it that much harder to carry on when I see fools with this Khajiit's wanton disregard for green life.\n\nIt disgusts me. And I'm going to teach him a lesson.

A good bit actually. High King Emeric's forces had just broken the bulk of Ranser's armies at Markwasten Moor. Some fools actually believe that's where Ranser fell, but that's not the case.\n\nHe and his most trusted troops retreated here.

Ranser was king of Shornhelm, the ruler of Rivenspire during what many consider the high point of its history.\n\nHe was ambitious, too. That's why he tried to marry his daughter to Emeric. When Emeric changed his mind, Ranser became insane with fury.

Yes. Wrothgar was, of course, allied with King Emeric. And the Orcs had already subdued most of the kingdom, including Shornhelm.\n\nRanser retreated here and the Orcs surrounded him. The last moments of the battle, however, were lost to history.

Indeed. Ranser's armies marched on Wayrest. Almost took it, too. But Emeric managed to strike a deal with the Redguards and the Orcs.\n\nRanser's forces were soon beset by enemies on all sides. They were driven from Stormhaven in a matter of weeks.

There are two basins, the Basin of Suffering and the Basin of Loss.\n\nFirst, you must drink the Basin of Suffering, and witness how our mother suffered at the hands of Molag Bal. Then you must show your hatred for Molag Bal by profaning his symbol.

That is not for me to reveal. Now, drink the Cup of Suffering. Profane the symbol of Molag Bal, the Defiler.\n\nWhen you have drunk from both cups, you will kneel in the pool and present yourself to Mother Lamae.
After you've profaned Molag Bal's symbol, you will drink from the Basin of Loss and see how Lamae Bal was forsaken in her time of suffering.\n\nThen you will profane the symbol of the Forsaker.

The village elder, she's not sure we did any work. And look, I know we messed up a little. And you helped us out. A lot! \n\nBut we're trying to build a reputation here. And most of our jobs don't go like this. So could you … stretch the truth?
I can barely stand. I'd just slow you down.\n\nI'll send reinforcements your way—if any show up, that is.

I can't believe a blasted vampire actually got a decent cut in on me. But I was pretty busy trying to protect Janeve. \n\nThe House Tamrith sisters are both brave and good women. Please help Janeve if you can.

I know, I know. You swore an oath. No one should ever have to endure the things you've gone through because of what you are.\n\nBut you're alive! That's more than my wife will be if you don't help her.
You can't make that decision for her. Neither can I. But you can give her a chance.\n\nI know you care about her. You can't just stand there and watch her die!
Thank you. I know she'll make the right decision.\n\nShe may no longer be the woman I know, but at least she'll be alive. She'll be with me. I can still love her.
There is no other way!\n\nBah! I don't know why I waste my time with you. Sometimes you're as heartless as the monster so many purport you to be.
I suppose I might be able to. I would need a little blood. Stibbons hold out your arm. This won't hurt a bit.
I know you will. You've always been so gracious. A man who would do anything for those he cared about. \n\nI … no, now's not the time. We'll talk again later.
The Argonian continues to pour potions into me. They all taste of sour cheese and swamp water, but I know he means well.\n\nI'm frightened, Verandis. I … I don't want to die.
Stupendous! Did you see what happened to King Ranser? \n\nWas it the Orcs who killed him or are the rumors true? Was he betrayed and killed by his own soldiers?
I'm afraid that if I close my eyes, they may never open again.\n\nBut I'll do as you ask and try to get some rest.

Then what? Will he rise up and kill the king again? I guess we'll just have to wait and see.\n\nTake the skull and search the ruins for the rest of the general's bones. If you don't mind, I'll watch from the top of the tower.

Ah, General Dathieu. Of course! I should have known. They say his bones were scattered around the ruins. I suppose this was Ranser's twisted idea of vengeance.\n\nTell me, though. Did you learn how we might remove the undead curse here?
I'm the muscle. I know how to talk to people and organize things. The Remly brothers are much better at that fine-control stuff, anyway. Most days, they're actually pretty clever little guys.
No, my friend. Your gift isn't the solution. Not for me. I refuse to accept an existence that forces me to watch as my children … my husband … everyone I know … ages before my eyes.
We finished the stupid job. That scum paid us and we moved on.\n\nIt still bothers me that that job was our first and set our claim to fame. It's the reason we get so many harpy jobs like this one.

Word spread of our excellent job helping Lord Diel, mainly due to your help. We have reputations as "harpy wranglers." \n\nWe embellished a little, I'll admit, and it's paid off. This job should have been easy, but for the Remly brothers ….

The gems I took helped, but our good reputation allowed us to get more work. Though it wasn't the best start, we got a name from that job you helped with.\n\nWe soon became known as "harpy wranglers." And here we are!

We got a reputation for being skilled with wildlife, especially harpies. Jobs started rolling in, and the experience helped us get better. This is another routine harpy job. But we wouldn't be here if it wasn't for you. Heh.

No, I remember all of this as though it were only yesterday. But there has to be something else, something I missed or failed to understand the significance of.\n\nKeep exploring. Let your unique perspective guide you.
Very well. I'll be here, waiting on those orders.
Suit yourself.

She asked how she could prove herself their rightful leader. <<1>> suggested <<c:2>> nonsense, and the Mane agreed.\n\nOf course, neither will be present to see it, yet my sister is held to her pledge. How unexpected.

Khajiiti political excuses are impossible to discern. I know the Mane will not be present, and that's all I care to know.\n\nAs for <<c:1>>, he died on <<2>>. Thought he could negotiate with the filthy Sea Elves.

<<1>> is on some sort of pilgrimage. You'd think the spiritual incarnation of the Wood Elves could stick to a schedule.\n\nAs for the Mane, I cannot begin to understand the excuses of Khajiiti mystics. There will be no Mane. This is all I know.
<<1>>. It's beneath his city, so there's no turning him away.\n\nAnd myself, of course.

Wonderful! Have anything you find sent directly to <<c:1>>. Once everything is in place, we can begin the ratification ceremony.\n\nAnd do refrain from referring to Conservator <<2>> as a "missing element."

Conservator <<1>> maintains <<c:2>> and has studied the Ayleid monitoring rituals.\n\nUnfortunately, she was called away to <<3>> for a personal matter. If you can locate her and convince her to return, we'll have our operator.

I've researched this a bit. Really, you need to be in three places at once. Simple, right?\n\nBut <<Ac:1>> is rumored to hold a relic of the Khajiiti thief god. For our purposes, <<2>> will serve as the divine spark. If it's truly there, of course.

<<AC:1>> originally "brought life" to <<c:2>>, according to the texts. It long ago went missing.\n\nBut a member of the local Mages Guild named Laranalda theorizes  it's in a local Ayleid ruin. She's currently at <<Ac:3>> seeking <<AC:1>>.

Yes. The king and all his soldiers. Something happened in the final moments of the battle against the Orcs of Wrothgar fifteen years ago, and they were cursed with undeath.\n\nTheir undead forms have prevented anyone from getting in to learn the truth.

Yes, well … that's the challenge. I was hoping though, since you're here and you do appear capable, would you be willing to escort me in there?\n\nI just need to get to the central tower. I'm convinced the answers I seek are there.
Oh! Yes, yes, of course. How have you been? We're fine. Mostly. We're doing the best we can, anyway. Still in the harpy business, just like the old days.

No, not really. I mean, back then, Lord Diel wouldn't have paid us without your, er, intervention.\n\nLooks like you've done well enough for yourself since then, eh? Got a new shirt, did you? Maybe that's why I didn't recognize you right off.

Do they? They're not, you know. We deserved better than what Lord Diel was going to do by us, didn't we?\n\nI didn't recognize you until you mentioned it. Good to see you again. Imagine, meeting up after all this time.

The harpies came down the hillside and attacked our horses. I'd heard of a band of traveling fighers who were experts against the harpies, and sent for them.\n\nWe were lucky. They were nearby, and between contracts.

Our tribe's descended from an ancient race. We care for the horses, and they work hard for us. We often train steeds for others as well, which brings us goods in trade.\n\nThis may be a simple life, but it's one full of history.
They seem to work very hard, but without much progress, like foals. I'm sorry we didn't add a provision to the contract about timeliness.
Yes, very soon. Once I pore through the wreckage of my home and see what wasn't lost.\n\nPerhaps I'll see you there.
Yes? What of it?
Actually, I'm needed in <<1>>. Unless the queen prefers it left to the whims of a Daedric Prince, she can wait.

The Baron wasn't listening to me. We needed someone he trusted more, had more faith in. That someone was you, Count Verandis.\n\nNow the Baroness is on the mend and House Montclair has returned to a state of contented bliss.

I found the stone among the effects of King Ranser's royal historian, back when I served in Ranser's court. She had quite an intriguing collection, including the Ayleid manuscripts that I've been translating.\n\nPerhaps you can check my work?
Well, that's unfortunate. But it is only a small piece of a grander relic, isn't it?\n\nI've been studying the Ayleid manuscripts. There may be more we can do for the poor Baroness.
It's about time.

A job here, a job there, the usual.\n\nWe're no longer called the Daggers though. Seems a mysterious someone had a claim to the name and didn't want it tarnished. A threatening note and near-death experience later, we dropped the name.
Right! We actually get harpy jobs pretty frequently. Seems we have a bit of a reputation for being competent against harpies, and that's all because of your help.
Yeah, those gems got us by long enough to get another job. It helped that revealing his scheme actually made us more popular among the locals.
We got paid. That's all that needed to happen.\n\nGelvin's been far more careful about what jobs we accept, though, and Lord Diel's praise of our work is a good reference.
A good ways off. Northwest of Shornhelm. Here. I'll mark it on your map.

It was quite the talk of Tamriel at the time. Surprised you don't know about it. \n\nIt was over ten years ago. Our beloved High King insulted King Ranser of Shornhelm over some minor indiscretion. Ranser reacted poorly and declared war on Wayrest.

If you can call it that. Lasted about a year. Just long enough for Emeric's troops to get a little exercise.\n\nWhen it was over, Ranser was dead and peace was restored to the kingdom. The triumvirate of nobles has been running Rivenspire ever since.
My brother <<1>> is ill. A healer told us the only way to cure his sickness was to consume a broth made from pulped insects.\n\nThey say the broth is blessed by Y'ffre. I say it stinks.
No, but thank you. I've been feeding the broth to <<1>> whenever he's awake.\n\nIt seems like he's getting better … I hope he's getting better.
By all means, ask! The faster we can affect its repair, the better.
Can't you tell?\n\nListen, I've got to get back to Bumnog. While you're out here, see if you can find that brother of mine.
Now that those skeletons are gone, I'm going to spend some time exploring the tor. This place is fascinating!

Not exactly. It helped, but I can't remember why. We were here, celebrating Leila's improved condition, when …. And that's all I can recall.\n\nI'm sure the key is hidden in my memories. Please, explore this moment and see what you can learn.

I consumed all of it! Well, at least all that was given to me. Anything less would just be rude.\n\nSo, Verandis. My friend. My confidant. What say we slip away to someplace a little more private? And bring the rest of that delicious wine.
Was that a rebuke? I was rebuked by the high and mighty Count Ravenwatch? Yes, I believe I was.\n\nI think you should walk away now. Before I say something else that at least one of us will regret.

Gone forever, but their memory remains. I can see the light burning brightly behind your eyes. Your friend is a part of you now, just as the strength of the Divines burns like a flame within your renewed soul.

In many ways. Fire is a weakness. The hunger for blood will always be with you.\n\nBut feed and you will grow in strength, speed, and skill. In time, you will even be able to create new vampires, new children for our family.
What does that matter? If not for you, I would never have attempted to use such magic to heal Leila.\n\nBesides, Reezal-Jul will be rewarded for his service. I'll see to that personally.

Better? Yes, but she's not fully healed as yet. It's just a matter of time, I'm sure. But she's out of bed. She's even painting again. She hasn't done that in … I can't remember how long.\n\nSoon, it will be as if nothing had ever happened.

My good Verandis, it wouldn't be a day if you weren't concerned about something. It's your nature!\n\nNow, stop asking such bleak questions and just be thankful this relic fell into our hands. It's helping. That's all that matters.

He was always bringing me tinctures and alchemical concoctions. It was one wild plan after another with him. It always is.\n\nBut because of your quick thinking, we applied the power of the stone. And now we're celebrating our success!

Right as rain, now that Mother's back on her feet.\n\nI was thinking … I wanted to find a way to thank you. For all you've done for us. Maybe next time you're in Shornhelm, I can make you a nice meal.

Oh, yes indeed. If I could get my hands on that damn lizard, I swear I'd make a pair of boots from his hide. And then I'd put them on and stomp through troll poop!\n\nThe people in the camp were just villagers. Now most are dead, poor bastards.

The Shornhelm soldiers were diligent enough, but I think that thrice-damned Argonian used magic to mask their approach. They moved in so quickly and quietly, that a good third of the camp was down before Janeve and I could react.

I—oh! By the Divines! How embarrassing. Well, how about you feed on me instead? Oh! I can't believe I just said that.\n\nPardon me while I slip away and find Reezal-Jul. Maybe he has a potion I can drink to make me forget this awkward moment.

Just a little dizziness … a little discomfort. It must be all this activity lately.\n\nVerandis, I don't think the stone shard is powerful enough. It helps, but it doesn't last. And now I feel … empty. I can't explain it.

No! You leave him be. He's happy now. I can't stand to see him worried. Sitting beside my bed … helpless … consumed with grief. Not again.\n\nThe stone shard. It's obviously a part of something larger. Could that be the cure we're looking for?
I knew I could count on you, dear friend. Now, I need to compose myself and return to the party.\n\nBut I think I'll go to sleep early this evening. I'm sure I just need a little more rest.
Talk to the Argonian. See what he's found out. We need to find the larger relic … or at least another shard of stone.\n\nI hate to ask, but I need you to do this one last favor. For Wylon. For me.

The manuscripts are locked away, but I left my notes in your library. A few phrases stood out as I translated—Life, Death, Crag. I'm sure they mean something.\n\nTake a look and see what you think. Perhaps the text can lead us to the greater relic.
Not exactly. Not yet. But I will figure this out.\n\nIn the meantime, there is one more memory I want you to explore. We ascended the Doomcrag. And that's where everything changed.

A perilous peak that rises from the mountains to the north. It has always been a haunted, desolate place.\n\nLook for anything I may have missed. But more, I want you to see what happened to Montclair. I want you to understand why he must be stopped.

She caught you out at the edge of town, eh? She feels betrayed, I know. I hope someday she understands. The last thing I wanted to do was hurt her.\n\nMy wife and I both have always treasured her friendship.

Look, I don't know you. And I don't need you meddling in my personal affairs.\n\nI'm not looking for trouble, and I'm not saying a single damn word about the new constable. You'll mind your own business, if you know what's good for you.

Oh, um … I think he's worried about security. Yes. With the rumors of bandits robbing people on the road, we have to be careful.\n\nThere's supposed to be a big parcel of amethysts coming in from the mine, too. Gods. I hope it gets here … safely.
General Am-Shadal's in charge of the Battle and Warfront missions. Talk to him about them.
The Bounty and Scouting missions are in the care of General Khamagash. That knowledge is his to impart.

Yes. Captain Janeve of the Rivenspire Guard. In fact, the Countess just sent the good Captain to investigate disturbing rumors from the western countryside.\n\nBut rumors are for later. We have a more immediate problem right here in Shornhelm.
Arms as tall as a person, an endless hunger, and jaws that can snap off a horse's leg in a single bite.\n\nWhy am I afraid of frost trolls? The real question is, why aren't you?
I am talking about knowledge and ancient magic. I am talking about the forgotten arts of the Ayleids themselves.\n\nWould you deny our lady any chance for a cure, no matter what the source?

Gaillard is my friend. He looks after me since my parents died. \n\nGaillard said it isn't safe in town. No, no. That constable. Gaillard recognized him from Daggerfall. Said he was a bad man. Gaillard went to meet the constable, but never came back.

That Edweg is gone. I am no longer in the service of Arkay. Maybe I'll be Edweg the Traveler. Or maybe Edweg, Safe at Home.\n\nI bet you were sent to find me. Or at least the relic I was supposed to retrieve. Saint Marben's Fingerbone.

I happen to possess an Ayleid relic—or at least a shard from one. But the Baron won't listen to me, especially since our lady started refusing my help.\n\nIf I give you this stone, will you present it to the Baron? He listens to you, my friend.
I knew I could count on you, Verandis Ravenwatch.

Are you daft, Lieutenant, or just a coward? Don't make me repeat myself.\n\nTell General Dathieu to prepare the soldiers to charge against the Orcs to the south. I will retrieve my sword from the north tower and join you on the battlefield.
You didn't know? That's why they were holding us. \n\nGavendien was waiting for Lauravieve Mondorie's big amethyst parcel to come in. He was holding the three of us hostage to keep the town in line.
You did what Leila wanted? What about what I wanted? I asked you to do something and you refused!\n\nWell, I'm done asking. Now we do exactly as I say and, with or without your help, we save my wife.

You did what Leila wanted? What about what I wanted? You allowed her to talk you out of it when I expressly asked you to turn her!\n\nWell, I'm done asking. We're here because of you, and we're going to do exactly as I say. We're going to save my wife.
It seems you diverted a frost troll from one of her soldiers. Upon reaching safety, the knowledge you seek was passed to me.\n\nShe was last seen in the northernmost cave of the dig site.
Yes, she saw the wisdom in my words.  A reasonable request earned a reasonable response.\n\nA true shame the rest of Tamriel doesn't work like that.

To show me I was powerless in his clutches. Worse, to kindle hope my husband would come to free me … then smother that hope with his continued absence.\n\nBut <<1>> knows nothing of love. I did not waver, not once.
But … I found <<1>>. Why should <<2>>  be the one to wear it? I've been fighting since before she was born!

I … you're right. We were overrun. I thought to use its power to slay our foes, but I couldn't stop. I killed my own soldiers!\n\nI can feel it, bringing my shadow to life. You must stop me, no matter the cost!
I'll alert <<Ac:1>> when I've returned to <<2>>. Once I have it at the Mages Guild, I'll see if I can discern a safer way to handle it during her ratification ceremony.
That sounds like her. She shared the same danger that we did. It's why we'd follow her into Oblivion itself, had she asked.\n\nWell, if she's gone, there's much we'll need to do.

If she doesn't think we met our end of the contract, the elder won't pay us. And she'll probably spread the word that we're idiots.\n\nEventually, we'll starve to death. Is that what you want? For all of us to starve?

Whoa, whoa, lie is such a strong word! We set out traps, and the scent lures worked just as they were supposed to! \n\nAnd most of the harpies are gone now, right? So everything worked out … after a fashion.
Hmm. If the king decides to surrender, he still may have need of us ….\n\nVery well. I'll delay the charge until we get clarification from the king.

For you? I don't think so. Who do you work for? The Ring of Daggers? \n\nIf so, you're wasting your time. You can't get in, and I have enough supplies to survive in here for quite some time … however long it takes until my friends come for me.

All right. I believe I dropped my pack by an altar just north of the crypt. You'll find the letter in there.\n\nIf you read it, you'll see! I'm a changed man. I've done everything I can to make amends. Please, just read it and come back.
Turenn is dead? You saw him? Oh gods!\n\nI—I needed him to get me out! The door can only be opened from the outside. I don't have enough supplies to last forever! I'll die in here!

Very well. I hope it's given you something to think about before you decide my fate.\n\nRegardless, I suppose it's my turn to hold up my end of the bargain. Unfortunately, this door was designed to be absolutely secure against intruders.
Yes. And then I get to find out what my fate is to be. I hope you're really thinking about this.

The door is controlled by two levers on either side of the barrow above. As if that weren't enough, you'll need keys to activate the levers. The keys are buried inside the Dorell and Tamrith family crypts. \n\nI am sorry this is so much trouble.

Hmm. Hostages? I knew those bastards were up to something!\n\nDamn. Constable Gavendien just left here with Lady Mondorie. Bailiff Sagabar's still upstairs, though. We should try to get into his room and see what else we can find.

They say I broke into Jerine's Ironworks and robbed the place during the night, but they haven't got any proof.\n\nBesides, my friend is going to come forward and vouch for me. I was at his house drinking mead all night.

And get myself killed? I can't do that. My father went back to the dirt fifteen years ago and my family needs me around.\n\nMy mother would fall to pieces and my sister doesn't make enough coin to support herself, let alone the both of them.

We have enough. We found his boot prints in the mud outside the broken window. He was involved. I'm not sure he was alone, but he was there.\n\nIn fact, that friend of his, that Olivier—I suspect he may have helped with the robbery.

That's the thing. Olivier said he didn't see Martin at all that night. Some friend, huh?\n\nIf they weren't such amateurs, though, I don't think the constable would've made the deal with Captain Thayer.

If you read the letter in my pack, then you at least know that I've done what I can in the years since the war to make amends for the things I did.\n\nEven if you decide to hand me over to the Ring of Daggers, I will at least die knowing I tried.

No. I prefer you take your time making this choice. \n\nI need to get out of these barrows either way, so you can take me to the Ring of Daggers or you can take me to the other side of the barrows and set me free. It's up to you.

No. I'm afraid the opposite is true. He's never had a good role model, you know.\n\nHis dear father was King Ranser's most trusted general. He died up at Traitor's Tor. They say he died a dishonorable death. It's a shame we'll never know the truth.

I worry that if he enlists just to get out of trouble, that would be the wrong reason. \n\nIf someone could tell Martin that his father died a hero … that would inspire him to follow in his father's footsteps, to join and fight with honor.

He did? You know this for certain? I can't tell you how much that warms an old woman's heart. I always knew he died honorably. \n\nMartin though, he was ashamed. You should go and tell him. He needs to know the truth about his father.

I do. Martin's always been ashamed. Every chance he's had to make something of himself, he's shied away from it for fear that he would fail. Like his father did. \n\nIf he knew his father died honorably, I think it would inspire him.

Why yes! Of course. Yes! Take it down and burn it!

The king told me this was of the highest priority. I'll admit—I thought he was joking, but I assume he wouldn't have sent you if that was the case.

We'll redouble our efforts.

Honestly, I deserve some of the blame for Rivenspire's troubles myself. \n\nAfter Ranser's war, I didn't trust any of the nobles enough to give them the throne, so I appointed three houses to share rule of the kingdom. Seemed like a smart strategy.

So it seems. Maraya actually counseled me to appoint a single ruler in Rivenspire more than a year ago. \n\nI should've listened, but after the mess with Ranser … there's something about nearly having my head on a pike that's hard to forget.

Well yes. My decision to marry Maraya instead of King Ranser's daughter really stuck in the man's craw. He had Wayrest surrounded at one point.\n\nI remember—I even dreamt about my head on a pike. Of course, as you know, I've had worse nightmares.

What? You mean because Martin's in the stocks? I don't know if I'd say that makes things harder … wait, did Martin say something to you?\n\nI'd rather not discuss this. Our family's finances really aren't anyone's business but our own.

Really? Well, the truth is that Martin's only ever been a drain on our family's resources. His big ideas never amount to a hill of beans.\n\nI wouldn't tell him, but the best thing he could do is enlist. We could really use another steady income now.

Why are you asking so many personal questions? I don't think Martin would appreciate us talking behind his back like this.\n\nBesides, he means well. He's just never really had a good role model, you know? Sorry, but I need to get back to work.

Enough to be of service. <<1>> hasn't functioned as intended for ages. We planned to use some rather delicate magic to trick it into operation, but that is no longer necessary thanks to your magnificent work on our behalf!

Yeah? So what? I wasn't dumb enough to leave any proof for the constable to find, so I'm in the clear.\n\nAnd don't expect me to risk my neck sticking it out to vouch for Martin. As far as I'm concerned, he's better off in the stocks.

Wait! No! Please! Please don't! I'd go mad in the stocks!\n\nLook, I don't know how to sell these stolen goods, anyway. How about this? I'll just leave them on the constable's doorstep tomorrow morning. That will clear Martin's name. Is that enough?
Oh. You mean honor among thieves and all that nonsense?\n\nI don't believe in such platitudes.
Why? Olivier's not going to vouch for me, is he? That backstabbing arse-hole! \n\nI can't enlist though. I just can't. I'm just not cut out to be a soldier, and my mother and my sister need me here.

You know about my father? You mean … you were there, weren't you? He did die with honor, didn't he?\n\nI-I don't know. Perhaps you're right. Maybe I was born to be a soldier and I've just been running from my destiny. All right. I'll enlist.

Really? She said that? I guess it's true. My plans for making gold haven't really panned out, have they? My poor mother, she's been wearing the same shawl for eight years ….\n\nAll right. If this is the best way I can help my family, I'll enlist.

I should've known better than to trust Olivier. I suppose that if you went to such trouble, you're going to say I owe it to you to enlist.\n\nFine. I'm not excited about it, and I don't know that I'll make much of a soldier, but I'll enlist.

That fobbing Olivier. I can't believe he's hanging me out to dry. I don't want to rot away in some prison cell.\n\nI can tell you now, I am not cut out to be a soldier. Dishonor runs in my family. But you're right. I don't have a choice. I'll enlist.

I advise caution, my friend. As with Reezal-Jul and Camp Tamrith, I have a feeling that the enemy remains at least one step ahead of us.\n\nSince I assume that Montclair's memory was never affected, who knows what we may find in the ruins below?

Because I'm close. I've been courting Guendeline for three years and I think I'm finally close to winning her heart.\n\nIf I leave town now, by the time I get back she'd probably have married someone else. I couldn't live with that.

That would make everything perfect! If I had her love, I could enlist and fight with the strength of ten soldiers!\n\nThat's not going to happen, though. It's going to take something special to win her heart, and I haven't a clue as to what that is.

It's not that I don't like him. He's brave, kind, and handsome. He's perfectly … acceptable. He's just not very exciting. I don't know that I love him.\n\nI'm not even sure he loves me. I keep trying to tell him it's just some childish infatuation.

I don't know. I want the feeling from the story books! I want my skin to flush and my heart to quicken. I want butterflies in my stomach and to be unsure whether to laugh or cry.\n\nJulien just makes me bored. Someone in town has to be more romantic!

When you restored my missing memories, I recalled that the Ayleid manuscript mentioned two ancient outposts—the Doomcrag and a place in the hills to the east. My research indicates an Ayleid ruin lies beneath this abandoned Breton fortress.

I'm not sure. But there must be something here that we need. Why else would the two Ayleid outposts be linked as they are in the manuscript?\n\nFirst, however, we need a way to open the path down. Without that, this ruin is nothing but a dead end.

You mean that stuck up woman who lives across the way? I know she's been turning suitors away for months. \n\nI think she's waiting for someone with big coffers—someone who can buy her fancy jewelry and such. Me? I don't think she's worth it.

Why? Are you looking to court my sister, too? Suitors have been lining up for months. That Julien is the worst. I'd be happy to see her wed almost anyone but him.\n\nWait a moment. You're not asking on Julien's behalf, are you?
Not much. She's a pretty girl, but I think it's gone to her head.\n\nShe does have a heart, though. She's always at the inn whenever there's a minstrel in town. I think she has a taste for poetry.
This one saw you fall from thin air. Pop, drop, splash. Raz would have tried for a backflip, but under the circumstances this one is most impressed.

Something romantic. Something unique. \n\nI know! A bouquet of rare flowers, though I'd need help picking them. Or I could serenade her with a poem! Of course, I don't know any poems. Or maybe a beautiful necklace? What do you think?

You wouldn't mind? I'm thinking dunlain daisies. They're very rare, but they smell wonderful.\n\nThey grow near the old tower outside town. Just watch out for the trolls and you'll be fine. Give the flowers to Guen and tell her they're from me.

I think so, too. I noticed her flirting with a minstrel once. She practically swooned whenever he opened his mouth. \n\nAnyhow, now we just need a poem. Surely someone around here knows some poetry. Find a good poem and I'll serenade Guen with my love!

Of course! They say jewelry's the key to every woman's heart. \n\nI don't have much gold, but the blacksmith's apprentice, Khalisah. She said she could make a nice necklace if I could supply the gems.

Something Ayleid, that's all I know. The fragments of manuscript I was able to study weren't very specific about what was stored at the Lorkrata site.\n\nI have high hopes, however, that we will find something we can use against Montclair.

I honestly have no idea. But that lock is new, so we could be facing bandits or Montclair troops. Or they just locked the door and moved on. Ruins do have a habit of attracting monsters, however.\n\nIf we work together, I have no doubt we can succeed.
You know how to get things done. Join up with Skordo and help him find a way into the city. I'll keep the troops on alert and ready to move on your signal.

Reports indicate that Baron Montclair hasn't been seen in weeks, though this mess has his fingerprints all over it. His daughter Lleraya, on the other hand, isn't afraid to show her face. We're assuming she's in command here.

Northpoint is an important trading center, with many House Dorell holdings. Whoever controls the city controls the northern region of Rivenspire. If I were Oblivion-bent on conquering the area, it's certainly what I would do.

My son, Ellic, was in charge while I was at Shornhelm. If he's still alive, he must be somewhere inside the city.\n\nBeyond that, the entire populace is loyal to House Dorell, but I have no idea what kind of forces Montclair set loose within my city.

Prior to her mother's illness, she was a charming young woman. A real magic-using prodigy.\n\nNow it's like she's been replaced by a dark seducer. Men and women will do anything to please her. And she's shown a remarkable affection for extreme cruelty.

Countess Tamrith went with him. Against my better judgment, I might add. And that fancy knight, Darien, decided to tag along. He's gotten rather friendly with Skordo since he arrived.\n\nI hope they can slip inside or this is going to be a long siege.

I sent Skordo and a small group to establish a secure base among the farmhouses outside the city.\n\nHe's supposed to find a way into Northpoint and then send us a signal. Since that hasn't happened yet, I assume he's still working on it.

It's a disguise! What's wrong? Don't you like it? Is my helmet on crooked or something?\n\nWe're going to sneak into Northpoint. Not usually my approach, but Countess Tamrith and Darien helped us get this far.

We push forward. Lleraya's veil is far from perfect, and she made it specifically to hinder me and my vampiric charges. \n\nShe wasn't expecting you, however. You should be able to guide us through the veil using the tears that litter the illusion.

No idea. He went to scout around and hasn't come back yet.\n\nSo far, we've learned that the patrols outside the city consist of untrained fighters with orders to keep people away. Only the officers seem to know what's going on inside.

I suggested busting a hole in the wall, but the Countess decided we should save that as a last resort.\n\nDarien went out to search while we took care of the farmers. They came to us for help, and you know how the Countess feels about refugees ….
