I promised to serve the people of Rivenspire, my friend. That doesn't mean I get to sit in a tower and make others take all the risks.\n\nBesides, these poor farmers are in need of a healer, and that just happens to be one of my specialities.

I'd appreciate that. Look toward the eastern farmsteads. Montclair's forces seem to be concentrated in that area, so it stands to reason that Darien would be curious about what they're doing there.\n\nJust be careful. And don't give away our presence.

Not much, I'm afraid. The soldiers we captured won't give up any secrets, but we do know they are totally committed to Lleraya Montclair.\n\nDarien went out to see if he could learn more. He's been gone for a long time and I'm starting to get worried.
Well, I guess that would be all right. \n\nI am a guard of the first order, a member of the Bloodtalon Cloaks of House Montclair. More than that, you won't get out of me.

Please … no! Get them away! Flowers make me sneeze—especially daisies!\n\nDoes Julien know nothing about me? Didn't he even bother to ask my brother what I would like? That's it! I'm done with Julien. Tell him to leave me alone—forever!

I'm sorry, but no. This juvenile obsession Julien's been nursing has gone on long enough. This just proves that we simply weren't meant to be.\n\nI do not love Julien, nor will I ever. Please, just ask him to leave me alone.
Daisies make her sneeze? Why didn't someone tell me? How could we have missed this? I feel terrible.\n\nNow we'll just have to try something else. What do you think?

Oh, gods! It's … over! No, no, no! I can't …. What am I going to do? I'll never find another woman like Guendeline! My life will be empty!\n\nHonestly, I don't know if I can go on. It's like I can feel my heart breaking inside my chest.

Hours ago. That thug Bulzog was actually going to execute us if he didn't hear from that crooked constable soon.\n\nYou really came just in time. We should hurry into town and see if we can't stop Gavendien.

Of course, but that makes him no less guilty. The dog that bites cannot blame his master for letting him off the chain. \n\nAlthen willfully organized the slaughter of innocent people, and he will pay for that crime no matter how long it takes.

Nah. That's what that bastard deserves for sneaking around behind my back with that little Bosmer wench. I knocked her off myself!\n\nNope. I haven't got any hard feelings. In fact, I'd say that was the easiest break-up ever.

Would you walk with me, Adept? I am surprised how often a problem falls away when a little fresh air and friendly company is added to the deliberations.
Keep your voice down! No, we're not married. We've been together for years … but I can never find the moment. And with her broken up like this … well, that moment isn't now.

Countess Tamrith accompanied him. And against my better judgment, I might add. That fancy knight, Darien, also tagged along. He and Skordo have become drinking companions since he showed up.\n\nI hope they can get inside or this is going to get bloody.

I will! And when—if—I return, it will be as an Orc who has struck her name into the face of the world!\n\nThank you, my friend, for inspiring me. Before you go, Arlie wants to speak with you. She's waiting just outside.

No. I haven't had a drop since the day I got my constable job back. I can't say I haven't been tempted, though. \n\nI try to just stay away from it, which is why this probably isn't the best place for me to be.

I can't believe it. I said I was going to eat my dagger, didn't I? I hope you'll let me off on that one.\n\nI'm really embarassed. Here I couldn't manage to get a single recruit, and you come behind me and get three.

Not much. Not about that, anyway … wait. They saw the Baroness hide something away at the windmill. It doesn't say what. Traveler, the Baroness never goes out there. Why would she hide something?
Nothing. Nothing, but I'm shaking like a leaf. Here, take it away from me. Let's go. Let's check out the windmill.

Well, I can't very well go on pretending the nobles can share the throne. Everyone knows what a colossal mistake I made there.\n\nI'm going to have to crown someone—a king or a queen of Shornhelm, someone to rule Rivenspire, don't you think?

The guard? I guess. It sounds mad, but you're probably right. I really do want to die now, and it might as well be for a good cause. \n\nTell Captain Thayer I'll be along soon.

The city of Kragenmoor. The head of House Dres sent the master traders of Skywatch a missive indicating his interest in commerce.\n\nAnd thus, ever the faithful servant, I am here.

Closer than I hoped, I assure you. The experience was illuminating. After seeing the lack of pity or compassion in those monstrous eyes, I'm more certain than ever that the living must be protected from this blood-curse.\n\nLight watch over us.

I told you, I didn't expect to find anything. But my captain was certain the information we got from that captured Orc was good, so … here I am. Didn't know I'd be walking into a damned nest of Daggers.

Do you really need to know more to use Giron's pendant? Hmph. Fine, I will answer what questions you have.
They seem to be attacking everyone. Clearly these soldiers died in battle. In death, their hatred and battle-lust lives on eternally. The perfect weapon, in the right hands.

Take this bloodstone. Don't lose it. It has the power to turn water to blood and whip up a ferocious hunger in the most sated vampire.\n\nWhen the time is right, we're going to use it to lure the vampire lord out of his hidey-hole.
I'll find a quiet village in the country in need of a priest and settle down. I look forward to it after all of this.
I only know what I've heard. There are many injured all over the city. Someone must help them.

As always, Raz serves the queen. She wanted to know if the Bosmer here are as scary as they sound.\n\nWith the Staff of Magnus stolen, though, Raz must make that his priority. This one knows you can handle the Bramblebreach as well as he could.

The obvious answer is probably the right one. Pelidil. That toad fulfilled Naemon's every wish. Why should that change just because the Prince is dead?\n\nRaz knew the Veiled Heritance was a disease not so easily excised. Hmph.
This one does not understand Bosmer clan politics. But as Raz hears it, the clans of this part of Valenwood have always been wild. \n\nSome even sided against King Camoran in the Blacksap Rebellion.

Greenshade is the heart of Valenwood. It is very dangerous and very mysterious, and these Bosmer understand it like no others do.\n\nRaz would not be deterred, but even Camoran's Vinedusk Rangers avoid traveling in this part of the forest.
If Pelidil has taken the staff, we need to find him. And discover what he plans to do with it. \n\nThe staff is powerful and dangerous. All of the Dominion is at risk if we cannot find it.

Our village has a pact with the Wilderking himself. The village goes away, then returns every hundred years or so.\n\nMost of the time, our arrival causes no problem. This time, however, it's different.

My husband <<1>> can tell you more. Essentially, we travel to and from this place, thanks to the Wilderking. A caretaker protects things in the village's absence.\n\nIn fact, we'll choose a new caretaker very shortly.

Wood Orcs set up camp outside this cave's southern entrance. They've never been here before and so we've kept quiet, hoping they'd go away.\n\nIt's been a week and they are firmly established. My husband <<1>> isn't as worried as I am, though.

Nearly everyone from the village attends the ritual to choose the next caretaker. No one knows who it'll be until the prior caretaker picks a name. It's held at the <<1>>, through the central hall of this cave.\n\nYou should see it! It's very exciting!
And it was a bad one. Just when we need guidance and leadership the most, he left Serkamora without a consul.
Me? I—yes, you're right. I have to be strong. For the Serk.\n\nDethisam was still a s'wit, though.
Not well. Alchemist Nilyne fancies herself something of a healer, and she's been working with Dethisam and the other afflicted.\n\nHopefully, she'll devise a treatment for them soon.
Some. She seems confident, at least. But what do I know of draughts and elixirs?\n\nBut tell me, do you think the Maulborn pose a threat to the rest of Deshaan?
Tsona-Ei is glad you asked! The Guild is an organization dedicated to the pursuit of knowledge. We travel the width and breadth of Tamriel, seeking books, tomes, and ancient scrolls.
Excellent. I'd hoped as much. You're well on your way to membership in the Mages Guild already! We reward collections like yours. In fact, knowledge and study are our primary pursuit!

Excellent!  I hearby grant you membership in the Mages Guild, with all the responsibilities and privileges thereof. Every book you find, and every book collection you complete, will earn you reputation in the guild. Stay moistl, friend.

Beyond wisdom and experience? Guild members in good standing earn the opportunity to buy special items only available to members of our circle. \n\nWe also have special tasks that crop up from time to time for those who seek adventure.

To hunt and to seek are not always the same. A flower does not hunt the sun. And so it is with us. The Guild does not care about wars, battlefields, or boundaries—just wisdom. Any books you acquire will improve your reputation with the Mages Guild.

We can teach you special spells and abilities only available to members. And from time to time projects crop up for guildmembers with ambition. Who knows? You might attract the attention of Mistress Valaste or the great mage, Guildmaster Vanus.

As long as you promise to collect the curatives as soon as we're done, ask away.

Not much. They say they're here to help, but they certainly don't act like any charitable caregivers I ever met. I don't trust them!\n\nWhich is why I want to find out what's in the curative they're pushing on the populace.

There's not much to tell. They claim the elixir is a cure for the Llodos plague, but I haven't seen anyone recover from the illness yet.\n\nBut I could tell you more once you get me a few samples of the curative to examine.
The missing pages are torn from your hand, as if by an unseen strength, into the book. Symbols scrawl themselves across the page.
She spoke truly. Torinaan has been assaulted by Daedric energies and foul beasts. The penitent writhe with foul magics, while Scamps and clannfear rampage through her fields.
You are very brave to offer your service. The shrines to the Eight Divines fuel this evil. I can feel it. Cleanse the shrines, and you should be able to strike at the source of the corruption.

Oh! I'm Aranias. Maybe you read my book, "Spriggans in the Green: Story and Myth in Primitive Bosmer Society"? Probably not, I guess.\n\nAnyhow, Andur and I came in a scholarly pursuit, to see if this Wilderking is really as powerful as they say.
If you want, you can take the essence from the Kollopi Tree and rub it all over your body to cloak yourself in a haze of forest moths. The Wood Orcs won't even see you.
The guar? The isn't just some guar. This is Little Monster. She was such a good girl. She never made too much noise, never got into trouble.\n\nShe was a good guar.
I—I don't think so. She didn't turn into a husk or anything.\n\nYou know, I had Little Monster since she was just a guarling. I raised her like she was part of our family.
Thank you. I appreciate the sentiment.\n\nNow, if you don't mind, I'd like to spend a little more time alone with Monster. To remember the good times we had.

No. There is no alternative. These people must leave. \n\nKnow that this is not our will. We would not harm anyone of our own accord. We would let them stay. But our directives are not self-determined. They were ingrained when we were created.

Yes. It does not violate my directives to inform you that destroying me would effectively render all the Hollow in this area harmless. \n\nI have no desire for self-preservation, but know that such an act would do irreversible harm to the Valenwood.

Look, if you decide this stone abomination is right and we shouldn't be allowed to stay here, I'll go back to the Clan Holdfast and we'll take a vote.\n\nI warn you, though, the Drilladan are not a soft-skinned bunch. I think they'll choose to fight.

We in the Mages Guild dedicate ourselves to the pursuit of knowledge in all its many forms. While others seek riches and fame, we hold learning as the loftiest goal, especially where it pertains to magic.\n\nAre you interested in becoming a Docent?

Excellent! I hereby grant you the rank of Student in the Mages Guild, with all the responsibilities and privileges thereto. \n\nEvery book acquired and collection of books completed will now earn you status within the guild. Good hunting!

Docents are our field agents who go out into the world to bring us rare tomes and scrolls when they find them.\n\nAs a member, a docent may purchase items only available to those of our order. They may also be offered unique and rewarding endeavours.

I'm sure the Wilderking will understand. A family must remain together to raise a child. If <<1>> stays behind, our child will be grown before he sees her. We'll be too old when the village returns next  time to have another. It's our last chance.

Well, it's not a cure. That much I can say for certain. There are too many toxins and malevolent additives for this elixir to have any kind of benign benifits.\n\nBut I haven't yet been able to ascertain it's true purpose.
You certainly are an inquisitive one, aren't you? \n\nIf you must know, Ornis lets me use his equipment. Until I can set up a shop of my own.

Not that I really want to tell you my life story, but I was apprenticed to Ornis. Then the plague struck the Serk and other priorities took precedence.\n\nI'll be on my own soon enough, provided the town survives this crisis.

Thanks for the insight, but I was already leaning in that direction. Between the smell and information that Aerona brought back with her, it seemed kind of obvious.\n\nBut with your confirmation, I can narrow my course of research considerably.
Only the old caretaker knew. The village is set to leave soon.\n\nIf anything happens to the tree, its link between Tamriel and our village is severed. They can never return unless I stay behind.

Not that. It's the tree. Now that I can feel its essence, I realize it's weaker than it used to be and needs special care. The village must return to the other realm immediately so the caretaker … so I can tend it without distraction.
My blood flows like sand and my skin burns like a smoldering ember, that's how I'm feeling.\n\nBut I haven't turned into a monster yet.
And I feel better! No silly plague was going to lay me low.\n\nAnd I suppose that Nilyne's potions helped, as well.

There's no way I can properly thank you for what you've done. This is the first good luck my clan's had in months. This means we can stay here and start over.\n\nWherever you go, and whatever you do, you'll always be a champion of the Driladan.

I know and I suspected that might be their decision. They are not the first clan to seek to settle in this place, and sadly, they will likely not be the last.\n\nHopefully, next time, we might convince them to leave in peace.

Ever since the last time the village was here, so a bit over a hundred years. <<1>> and I care for each other, and the Wilderking provides my sustenance.\n\nI don't understand why the Wilderking let you in, though.

I suppose your curiosity excuses your ignorance.\n\nThe Wilderking does not "control" this place. He allows us to take care of the Fading Tree in return for his protection. We don't question our oath, we fulfill it.

The Fading Tree chooses. It guides us towards the next caretaker. Not everyone has the courage, intelligence, and fortitude to undertake this position.\n\nEveryone from the village knows how hard it can be, and yet nearly everyone wants to do this.

Lonesome? Hah!\n\nNo, it's nice to get away from everyone else. It's quiet. Peaceful. And the Wilderking comes 'round now and then. Some might think of them as dreams, but I know he's been to see me. A caretaker's life is anything but dull.

Did she? Well, I suppose I do.\n\nThere are a few additives I require, but I can't very well walk away from my table while Dethisam and the rest of the townsfolk need my skills. Even this interruption can prove disastrous where alchemy is concerned.

Did she? Well, I suppose I do.\n\nThere are a few additives I require, but I can't very well walk away from my table while Ornis and the rest of the townsfolk need my skills. Even this interruption can prove disastrous where alchemy is concerned.

I need Kyne's heart healing herbs, sour milk tea, and dragon scale mushrooms.\n\nThe innkeeper usually has healing herbs. Grell Flan loved sour milk tea. And Sorel Tedas had a taste for exotic mushrooms. You should find what I need in those locations.

Well, I might have some around here someplace, but Kyne's Heart is very rare and valuable. I can make a fair bit of gold if I hold out for the right price.
What? Why didn't you say so? Ornis has always been fair and pleasant to me. And he's a good customer.\n\nPlease, take this. It's all I have left.
What? Why didn't you say so? I owe Dethisam more than I could ever repay. Plus, he's always been a good customer.\n\nPlease, take this. It's all I have left.

To the north. Drilladan Pass. Our clan has lived in that part of the Valenwood for longer than even our elders could remember.\n\nThe Altmer came in and built Marbruk not long ago, but we stayed … until the dead came. Hundreds of them.
Like where? You want us to move into a city? You want us to move into Marbruk?\n\nNot a chance. We're true tree-sap people. We live in Valenwood. We always have and we always will.

Little Monster. Veru Serethran loved that old guar. But it got sick. Probably ate something that didn't agree with it. Nilyne did everything she could, but sometimes creatures die. That's the way of the world.\n\nNow, go. Time is of the essence.

Healing herbs, dragon scale mushrooms, sour milk tea … yes, it's all here.\n\nI need to stay here and monitor my patient's condition. Go over to the alchemy table and mix those ingredients together, please.

<The herbs release a pungent odor as the alchemical process begins.>
<The sour milk tea slowly simmers, masking the odor of the herbs and thickening nicely.>
I don't know and now that they're far behind us, I don't care.\n\nWe've found a new home now. We must defend it or die trying.
<The mushrooms dissolve into the thick liquid, releasing a glowing rainbow of color into the concoction.>

I am one of the Hollow. I do not know where we came from, but we are assigned to protect different parts of Valenwood.\n\nI am assigned to protect Greenheart, to ensure none can reach the throne of the Wilderking without his invitation.

Mages Guild members seek out books, tomes, and ancient scrolls in their travels. We aid each other where we can, and provide magical support for any that would ask our help. As you can imagine, our mages travel and often face danger. You'd do well.

Precisely. We seek out new information, capture it in our libraries, and make copies for distribution across Tamriel.\n\nThe Guild cares not about wars, battlefields, or boundaries: just knowledge, and the acquisition of new tomes.

We can teach you unique techniques only available to members, and provide access to special spells and abilities. And from time to time projects crop up for those with an adventuresome spirit. You may end up working with Guildmaster Vanus himself!

As you say! I hearby grant you membership in the Mages Guild, with all the responsibilities and privileges thereof. Every book you find, and every book collection you complete, will now earn you reputation in the guild. Good luck!
This appears to be perfect. I truly am impressed.\n\nNow we'll see what happens and leave the rest in the Tribunal's hands.

Of course! And it's not one of the Falinesti sites, so it's not the Walking City, if that's what you're thinking. Their voices sounded Bosmer, but it could be a trick to draw us in.\n\nGood luck in there.
Personally? No. I think you've done more than enough.\n\nBut if you have a mind to stick around the Serk a little longer, I'm sure Alchemist Nilyne might have a task or two she needs a hand with.

I do not know. We were created by the Wilderking—perhaps these were his directives, or perhaps they just come from the forest.\n\nRegardless, we are here to ensure no one settles in this area. That is our only purpose.
Prepare yourself!

You are wise to abandon your evil ways. The life of a filthy Daedric beast is not one any mortal should choose. It will be difficult, but I believe I can rid you of Hircine's taint.\n\nHowever, I must ask for a donation equal to the difficulty.
Thank you. I will cleanse this corruption from your blood. Fear not. Once I am done, the curse of Hircine will be gone from you forever.
Then I cannot help you, child. Arkay watch over you.

You have no doubt sinned greatly due to your affliction, but fear not. Arkay's grace can purify you, if you truly desire forgiveness.\n\nConsidering the weight of your sin, I must ask for a donation to the temple before I can purify you.
Blessings upon you, child.\n\nNow, let Arkay's light burn the curse from your blood.
That is unfortunate. \n\nMay Arkay's light shine upon you.

By the look of his scars, he's seen his share of battle, and he knows how to take a beating. Don't expect him to go down quickly. \n\nThere's a shaman who's never far from his side as well. I'd focus on killing the shaman first. Good luck.

I didn't say that. There is definitely a distinctive magical force in this part of Valenwood. \n\nBut I fail to understand by what logic the treethane decides who gets an audience with the Wilderking and who gets turned away.
Why wouldn't I? We practically grew up together. You're the only one I can trust these days.
Bramblebreach? You know my parents have never let me leave Silatar after they saw what I can do. I've missed so much ….\n\nWhat happened at Bramblebreach?

No, it's not your fault. Thanks to you, these bastards didn't get very far. They could have destroyed everything!\n\nIt's getting late. We need to clean up before my parents return. Meet me at the manor later.

I'm … I'm sorry. After my parents left, I felt so alone. I couldn't find you. People kept coming. They'd attack, hound me, want me to show them what I can do. Like I was a circus animal, or some kind of pet!\n\nI shouldn't take it out on you.

Of course not. For her, it hasn't happened yet. Remember, I put you into her past to help her when she's at her most vulnerable. She lashed out at you just now because she can't fight against her parents.\n\nShe trusts you. That's what's important.
There are torchbugs in my eyes ….
The Maulborn smell like Daedra ….

I guess if you need to get close to them, that makes a certain amount of sense. Maybe we should try to find some of that. If it means we don't have to kill any more husks, that could be a good thing.\n\nThey were people once. Maybe they can be again.

I'm not sure yet. They'll probably want another statue raised from the ground. My parents treat that like a party trick, and this is a party after all.\n\nBut the way they're talking, it sounds more dangerous and I'm a bit worried, to be honest.

No. The greatest challenge comes next, and Aranias needs you. Her parents returned after the attack on the farm, and brought with them the people they considered their daughter's only hope. The Veiled Heritance.\n\nShe should not face this alone.

Over time, yes. The myriad of sensations and experiences from being connected with the Valenwood will crowd out the small memories from her past.\n\nThe legacy of her character will remain, though, and will shape the future of the Valenwood.
You promised to stay with me, and I hope you will, but I must make my own choices.\n\nNo one, especially not the Veiled Heritance, will tell me what to do or how to live my life.

It'd be an amusing story if the situation weren't so dire. An unseen force pulled me from my time into yours and dropped me in the midst of Dragonstar's grand melee—stark naked! \n\nI won, naturally. Then the soldiers arrested me, just as naturally.
