Excellent! You'll make a worthy addition to the Guild! We have a new guildmaster, and a new singular purpose. Someday bards will sing songs of your valor, just you wait.

Our new Guildmaster is an Argonian named Sees-All-Colors. She has us all hunting down the Daedra, and their Dark Anchors. You might have seen them already. Enormous chains fall from the sky. Plagues of Daedra boil out to lay waste to the countryside.

We only raise our blades in service to the guild. We're neutral in the war between the three Alliances. Some of us follow the Lion banner and King Emeric, of course. But every race, every creed, belongs under the Guildhall's roof.

Excellent question! We train our members in special techniques. And the higher-ups are always looking for motivated members to help with special projects. You never know when the Council will come looking for more hands.

Guildmaster Jofnir passed away very suddenly. Always thought he'd die with a blade in his hand. Instead he passed in his sleep, called to Sovngarde by his ancestors. \n\nWe all miss him, but in short order Colors has proven to be a very able leader.

It's a part of the oath. Ask my husband. He knows much more about it than I do. I prefer to scout and hunt, not tend plants.\n\nHe'll be at the choosing ceremony. If you hurry, you can talk with him before it starts.
The Orcs are camped off the cave's southern entrance.\n\nThe Wilderking must have sent you to save us. He always protects us. Always.

I've accepted the oath. It's my duty to be caretaker now. I must stay!\n\nBut … a child. Our village has had so few over the years. Surely it's a sign of something wonderful. Will I regret staying behind in case something happens to the tree?
I would. Naturally, I want to! But, everyone else is ready to leave. As soon as the Orcs cleared out, they prepared. There's no one left to leave as the caretaker.

No. It's not. No matter which I choose, I will always wonder what would've happened had I taken the other path.\n\nI know which way is easy, and which is hard. What would you choose? I will do as you would, since the Wilderking sent you to us.

Oh. I suppose I'm the only one who calls them that.\n\n"Independently Apportioning Dynamo Core" is a mouthful, but the Dwemer built them to last for generations. I say "generators" to honor their enduring nature.

Yes. Vaermina has pushed too far this time, and she must receive her comeuppance.\n\nI will aid you, but you should know that extricating your king from her clutches will be far more difficult than it was with the others.

Thank you. You are a noble soul. Perhaps you'll actually believe my extraordinary tale when there is time to tell it.\n\nBut first, meet me at the cave called Buried Sands. If my suspicions are correct, we'll find something we need there.

They have members from across Morrowind. And they're always looking for new recruits. I heard one of them speak in Kragenmoor. Lot of nonsense, if you ask me.\n\nNostrum Breva is in charge at the quarantine, and she's the one handing out the curative.

You haven't heard about the Llodos plague? People get sick, turn violent. Some claim they become monsters, but I haven't seen it. At least not yet. \n\nThe Maulborn have a cure. They promised to fix this. That's why we let them set up their quarantine.
Praise Y'ffre for that! Anything is better than another moment in Wood Orc hands.

Nedic writings suggest that the Nedes may have been slaves at sites like Mtharnaz, and they may have adopted some Dwarven practices.\n\nBut the Dwarves are such a mystery. It's impossible to guess what those practices might have been.
Your Attributes have been reset.

A Dwemer ruin. No one still swimming knows of its real name. It is called the "Inner Sea Armature," as it is a large mechanism that sits along the Inner Sea.\n\nMuch like a clam knife is called that because it is a knife. For clams.
It is an old mine. Used to be worked by slaves for house Dres. I do not know what works the mines today. As there are no Argonian slaves in the Ashlands. Or so says the Pact.

Oh yes, it is very, very dangerous. If the Dwemer … things do not get you, the bandits will. A crew of outlaws have begun plundering the site. Here, I will mark it on your map. \n\nJust do not say I did not warn you. When they stab you.
I don't mean anything. Unless you think I mean that some of my egg-brothers and sisters still suffer under the slavemaster's whip in remote corners of the Pact lands.\n\nThen, I mean that.

Quite. Most everyone who receives the suppressant during the early stages of the plague makes a full recovery. And even those in the later stages seem to stabilize. They don't appear to get any worse.
He's better. I'm filling his role as town consul while he recovers, but I expect he'll be back to work in a few days.
Unfortunately, we're going to have to maintain the quarantine. As long as there's a chance to restore those inside back to health, Nilyne is going to keep trying to cure them.
My uncle is almost back to his old self. He's teasing the lizards and even threatening to ask Nilyne to join him for a drink at the Brooding Elf. Personally, I hope he follows through on that one.

Good. I'd hate to lose a battle in my own camp.\n\nBeat the drum in our combat arena, and Gudarz will come to fight. He glories in turning the sand red with our recruits' blood, and set this up to show his prowess. It's time to show him yours instead.

Verandis approached me not long after we parted ways. He told me he knew what I was going through. He offered me another way, the type of way I was looking for. A way to live alongside people and not be a monster.

In his lifetime Verandis gave us a chance to be more than monsters, to continue doing good as the creatures we are. I don't know about the others, but I intend to honor him and continue the legacy of his little rag-tag group.

A common enough name for old cultist ruins in the Ashlands. This particular nest is almost due south out of the city, in the hills around the river. Swarming with Goblins, just rancid with the beasts. \n\nA fantastic resource.
Hightide is the Ashlander name for an old cave. It's just crawling with beast men. A perfectly excellent resource. \n\nYou'll find it on the coast almost due west of here, beyond Vivec's Antlers.

Not very learned, are you? Hmph. The ancient Chimer, the Dunmer forebearers, venerated the goodly Daedra: Mephala, Azura, and Boethiah. These "Nests" are ancient Chimer shrines.\n\nThe dirt-eating Ashland tribes still do much the same today, of course.

A resource for slave chattel, of course! Goblins take quite a lot of educating before they come around. It's worth it, though. They're a highly valued commodity. \n\nI once sold a whole tribe to a vizier in High Rock. Made a prince's ransom in coin!
Softloam … Softloam Cavern. Northeast of town. Please … have to stop them. Can't let them. Can't let them set up … a base.
Pray for me. I can hear the skalds. Singing the songs of Sovngarde. \n\nMy ancestors … I can almost see their faces.
Suit yourself. The Prowler will be ready to sail when you arrive.
Where we left it, I'd hope. But come, join me for a drink! It's good luck to share a glass before a long voyage.\n\nUnless you can't handle the stuff. Then you can meet us in Vulkhel Guard.
Ha! Deal. Bottoms up.\n\nAnd speaking of bottoms, my quartermaster prefers a crisp fold in his breeches.
How about a friendly wager? We match each other, glass for glass. Win, and you travel to Haven in the privacy of your own cabin.\n\nBut if I win, you launder our clothes for the entire voyage. Deal?
Then let's be off!
When you're ready, let me know. We'll wait as long as we can!
Yes, yes. We'll cast off as soon as the Prowler stops spinning ….
Yes, yes. We'll cast off as soon as the Prowler stops spinning ….
Take as much time as you need. It'll give my stomach time to return from wherever it traveled.\n\nSomewhere with a hurricane, no doubt ….
Yes, well. I was hoping you'd forgotten that raunchy song about the queen.\n\nBut what else could I rhyme with "Vulkhel Guard?"
Fine, fine! You won, as long as you promise to be quiet.\n\nNow it feels like the thunderbug lays eggs in my head.

We don't know a lot about them. They were an early race who settled in Craglorn.\n\nWhat history we do know tells a tale of enslavement and invasion—the Dwemer, the Ayleids, and finally the Yokudans, all had their way with the Nedes.

The Nedes apparently followed a variety of customs and religious practices, adapting to whatever invaders were currently overwhelming them.\n\nOne of these customs was star-worship. The Skystone amulet was a symbol of the priestly office.

Nedic writings talk about the Apex Stones in a variety of ways, but they all agree that there is a connection between the stars and these stones.\n\nIf we can understand that connection, perhaps we can find out how to stop the Celestials.
I'm an alchemist. I took over for Ornis when he retired. I also have a bit of training as a healer.\n\nBefore the Maulborn arrived, I was the one the townsfolk came to see when they got sick.
Yes, but I'm not used to this. It's my first large party, and all the running around has worn me down.\n\nPlease don't tell anyone. I promise not to stay out here much longer.
It's a party, that's all I know. The only difference from any other party is <<1>> provided the ship we came over on.

<<1>> was very interested in this place. She provided transportation, and insisted we get here quickly, before anyone else did.\n\nShe's very particular, so there must be something important going on. That's all I know, I swear!

Indeed I am! Everything's been so desperately dull these days, all this back-and-forth about Queen Ayrenn, or Prince Naemon. Bah!\n\nThough this could be a bit livelier. Can't wait for the entertainment. I understand it features someone quite nubile.

Ah, a person after my own heart! After my last wife died, I've kept an eye out for potential brides. If Estre's entertainment is as pretty as she is talented, I might have found a winner.\n\nI gather she bends spoons with her mind. Or is it knives?
Might've spoken out of turn. Don't mind me. We had a good crossing, didn't we? No one sick, everyone ready for adventure.
Yes. His passing was quick and peaceful … and we were together. That's all that really mattered. Soon, I will rest too.\n\nBut you, you're so kind. Did you find the Nereid's Smile?
We're all from the past. I'm just from … farther past.\n\nI can explain better what's going on if you free me and help me stop Tarish-Zi and the Anka-Ra. And maybe find me some clothes, as well.

That's what the Maulborn claim. They showed up at the Serk and set up a quarantine. They're offering their curative to anyone who wants it, but Dethisam isn't convinced they're telling us the whole truth.

Dethisam doesn't trust them. Neither does his sister, Aerona, as far as I can tell. They do appear to be too good to be true, but they claim to be able to cure anyone afflicted with the plague.\n\nThat's why they set up the quarantine at the Serk.

Neither had I. Not until they showed up on our doorstep. They seem to be some kind of altruistic society, dedicated to helping the afflicted of Morrowind.\n\nNow that I think about it, they did have an awful lot of weapons for a group of healers.
Well, I'm not one of their recruitment liaisons, but I can tell you a little. They claim to be an altruistic organization, formed to help the common people of Morrowind.

What's to understand? They're a volunteer organization. They say they fill the gaps left by the Tribunal and the Great Houses. They set up the quarantine here to help the afflicted. Claim to have a cure for the plague.\n\nBut that's all I know.

Not unless you can turn back time. No. To be honest, we've lived for many years more than either of us expected, but our time has finally come.\n\nNothing can forestall my husband's death now, nor mine, which I expect will follow soon after.
I was born into it, of course. I've never known any other life. We get to travel, sure, but otherwise we are the same as any other Bosmer. We laugh. We grieve. And eventually, we die.

Why should I? My home and family belong to this village. There's  nothing I need from any other place.\n\nSometimes, people do go out and wander Valenwood. And they've even brought others to live with us. I've no desire to go anywhere.

Each Celestial possesses an unusual gift. The Warrior's gift is to call heroes across time. \n\nIt seems the Serpent perverted the Warrior's gift, using it to awaken the villainous Tarish-Zi and his cursed army, the Anka-Ra.

Just <<1>> and me now. Bosmer don't shy from a fight, but a battle in our own village? It's never happened before.\n\nThere's no reason for me to return ever again. This is nothing but a place of mourning to me now.

My guess is that as one of Tarish-Zi's royal guard, he was summoned at the same time as the others—yet he was unaffected by the Serpent's manipulations. Perhaps because he was never truly loyal to Tarish-Zi.

Strange? No, of course not! It's how we've always lived. I sometimes wonder whether I should leave. Stay with my cousins in Elden Root, perhaps. But, my father likes keeping his family together. There'll be time to explore when he's gone.

Personally, for about forty years. I was born during our last visit.\n\nThat's what some of us call our time away: a visit. Isn't it lovely? So much so, I wonder why we bother to return to Valenwood at all! Seems terribly inconvenient.

We're from here, and go there. It's hard to describe.\n\nI actually don't give it all that much thought. I'm sure you'll find many others feel the same way. Why worry about it when our visits happen so smoothly?
The slaughter … they killed so many people.\n\nWhy?

At least my father still lives. But he placed such value on family, and now I'm all he has left.\n\nNo one ever attacked us before. I don't understand what's changed. It's not us. Please, let me be for now. I need time to recover.
Of course! Where else would we live? Has something changed in Valenwood since we were last by? Surely they haven't done away with houses entirely in the last hundred years?

Yes. Goes back farther than my great-great, of course, but he's the first of our line to pick up a chisel and hammer.\n\nCome to think of it, I've never considered how old the actual village is. Goes back a long, long way, though.

Right! Things aren't so different, are they? Only difference is we come and go. Others stay in one place.\n\nDo you see the flagstones about? My great-great-grandfather helped place them when he was a lad, and our family's maintained them ever since.
Truly? Hmm. Well, we don't want you doing that. After all, Royal Guards are so expensive to train. And the paperwork for murdering a member of the Queen's entourage … tsk.

Well it just so happens Raz has a blade that should satisfy your new friend. This one has been dueling with the Queen's men since we got to Skywatch. \n\nAnything to avoid Urcelmo's strategy meetings.
Hmm? Oh, I remember seeing you around.\n\nHere. Just take care of it.
Hold on, hold on! Just take it. \n\nI'm here to guard the Queen, not fight every maniac in the street.

It goes where it always does, and then we return. According to legend, Shrouded Hollow has always gone visiting this way. They named Shrouded Vale after our village.\n\nMaybe no one tells those old stories any more. We shan't forget, ever.
My studies for the day. Telenger himself is my teacher. He's set me the task of uncovering the mysteries locked within these relics from Shadowfen.

That's no suit of armor! It's a Dwemer Centurion, newly discovered in a High Rock ruin. Cataloged by Telenger the Artificer himself, and brought to the Emporium for study and exhibition. For a limited time only, of course.

As any apprentice could tell you, Dwemer magic emanates from Dwemer ruins. This construct won't last long, taken from his home of gears and flywheels. It's a shame.\n\nStill, he does put on a good show. Pull the lever there to see for yourself!

They're gifts from the Wilderking—embodiments of the raw energy of the forest. They protect the village. \n\nThey're not so smart. We can't lead them against the Orcs, but if they sprout straight into the Orcs' camp, they'll know what to do.
It shall begin shortly, if I can take a moment to prepare for it.
Yes, thank you. And I feel better, as well. I guess I really didn't have the Llodos plague after all.

Ha! Cuts right through my crap, I like it.\n\nListen, I'm just pulling your tail, friend. You got no worries here. This is the gathering of the Undaunted, and you're about to become one of us! Hope you're ready.
I'm not without sight. I saw you talk to him, he's right in front of me.\n\nHow do you know about us?
The village goes where the Wilderking sends it, and allows it to return when the caretaker needs to be replaced.\n\nI'm a very old man now. The village returned, as it always does.

The first Wilderking created <<A:1>>. All of Valenwood, from Bramblebreach to Greenheart, bends to his will. So long as we guard the tree, he remains our patron.\n\nSome consider him a god, like one of the Divines.

The Wilderking created <<A:1>>, and he bent everything in Valenwood, from Bramblebreach to Greenheart, to his will. From the first, he became our patron and protector.\n\nSome consider him a god, like one of the Divines.

There have been other Wilderqueens in the past as well. Our oath remains unchanged, even if the individual is new to the title.\n\nThat's the beauty of the arrangement. We protect the tree, and he or she protects us.

A spiritual prison, of a sort. Bosmer who break their oath to the Green Pact go there when they die. To reflect, for an eternity.\n\nThere's a place called Ouze where we bring the bodies of Oathbreakers. Some think it's a physical link to the Ooze.

We swore to protect <<A:1>> for the Wilderking, and to abide by his rules. In return, he protects our village.\n\nEvery hundred years or so, the village returns to choose a new caretaker to guard <<A:1>> on his behalf.

No point to that now, is there? You've entered our innermost sanctum, and without challenge. It's clear to me the Wilderking blesses your presence.\n\nThat means I am bound by our oath to speak with you, no matter how it galls me.
It shall begin shortly, if I get a moment to prepare for it.
Are you sure? You'll have to fight the largest, meanest monsters in Tamriel. It's not for the weak of heart.

Then welcome! I think you'll fit right in. Once you prove yourself, of course.\n\nAll you have to do is find a cave named Spindleclutch. The one full of bloodthirsty spiders. If you can handle that, return to me here and we'll make it official.
You'd … you'd do that? Such generosity!
Absolution! Absolution from the gods. Thank you! Stars above, thank you.
Words fail! Malareth will never see this face ever again!
Yes? Yes! Thank you, thank you! You don't know what this means.
What? No! No, not now! Not when I need him more than ever!
We pack it up in a knapsack and carry it off, of course!\n\nI don't think about it. We come back to Valenwood now and then, but are away for great stretches of time. It's just how things are.

I was only a child then, so I kept to the village. It can't have changed much in the last hundred years, can it?\n\nNow our scouts say there are Orcs beyond the cave, so I'm less inclined to venture forth.
It may not be useful, but it can be lucrative. Although, perhaps, you would indulge this one with a bout of riddles in exchange for the message?
Ah, a good guess, however misguided! You are very close! Slaughterfish keep their gold in the riverbank!\n\nReady for the next riddle?
A worthy opponent! Yes, yes, you are right!\n\nFor guessing correctly, I will give you the message, Telenger will get a new riddle, and I will get paid. Everyone wins!
<<1>> writes the best down, then sells them to a man called Telenger. He buys such curiosities. I have two new ones to try out.\n\nAll right! First riddle! Where do slaughterfish keep their gold?
That's not the point. This is a riddle! Perhaps you are not one for the riddles after all.

Hmm! That is a good answer. Not the one I seek, but it works for the riddle.\n\nVery clever! I will re-write my riddle for Telenger, and he will pay for it, which means I get my gold after all. Everyone wins!

Hmm! That is a good answer. Not the one I seek, but it works for the riddle.\n\nVery clever! I will re-write my riddle for Telenger, and he will pay for it, which means I get my gold after all. Everyone wins!
My second riddle is very mysterious! Yes, yes, it is my favorite!\n\nWhere can you find forests with no trees, roads with no travelers, and cities with no buildings?

I do not know. The Wilderking sent me here—to the entrance of Greenheart. I assumed it was to warn people away, but it may have been that he wanted me to greet you.\n\nPerhaps he placed protections on me to ensure I fulfilled his wishes.

I do not know of the Hollow at Shadows Crawl. A Watchman is one who is appointed to guard a section of Valenwood and enforce the Wilderking's edicts.\n\nIf one has been killed, there may be danger to the forest. I hope not.

I am not familiar with the Hollow at Shadows Crawl. If you assisted them, however, then that can only be a good thing.\n\nNow though, my concern is that someone assist the Wilderking himself. I believe he is in great danger.

We have not wavered in our duty. Any who came here uninvited were turned away.\n\nStrangely, the intruders who now seek to harm the Wilderking … he said they were invited. You are invited too. The other Hollow only attack because they are confused.

Tradition holds that the Warrior is one of the Guardians who defends the other stars against the Serpent.\n\nBut the Warrior Celestial who has recently appeared is no friend. He commands a merciless army of ancient Yokudan warriors called the Anka-Ra.

Certain Nedic writings suggest this isn't the first time the Celestials have appeared in Craglorn. \n\nThey're legends mostly, but there's truth in them. They describe Apex Stones that connect the Celestials to Tamriel in some fashion.

Go to the ruin of Shada's Tear, the site of an ancient Nedic temple. I'm confident we can find the amulet we need there.\n\nBut be wary. Wards protect the place, and I've heard that vicious Goblins roam the upper levels.

I believe I know the location of the Warrior's Apex Stone. It's written, "In Kardala, the Warrior waits."\n\nBut the way is sealed. We need a Nedic high priest's amulet to enter. Unfortunately, the Nedes disappeared centuries ago.

All I know is they are ancient and dangerous.\n\nI've heard intriguing rumors from the Daggerfall Covenant outpost to the west of a champion who appeared about the same time as the Anka-Ra. That may be a good place to start looking for answers.

One of our number, Erold, has been examining old Nedic writings on the subject. He hopes to find insight into the Celestials' sudden appearance.\n\nErold is smart, but he's not exactly battle-hardened. I'd be grateful if you'd help him.

Yes, Erold told me. He said that the Warrior's Stone was corrupted by the servants of the Serpent—the Scaled Court.\n\nIt's distressing to think that there are mortals aiding the Celestials, but not surprising. Thank you.

Yes, Titus arrived a short while ago. Interesting man. As soon as he entered, he pledged himself to resisting the evils of the Serpent and his cursed armies.\n\nHe'll be a good ally, I think. He's upstairs, if you want to talk to him.

Yes, along with the false emperor, Tarish-Zi. If it's true that the Warrior Celestial has the ability to call heroes across time, we can only wonder what the other Celestials are capable of. Be careful as you confront them.

Tradition holds that the Mage, the Warrior, and the Thief are the Guardian star signs. But the magical events in the foothills of Craglorn—including an ever-growing army of atronachs—suggest that the Mage has fallen under the Serpent's control.

The atronachs were originally summoned by a circle of conjurers from the city of Elinhir to defend Craglorn against the Dark Anchors. \n\nBut it's clear they're answering to another master now. And, if anything, their numbers are growing.

Strange things, difficult to describe. A large spellscar in the middle of the desert. And the appearance of two High Elves in Belkarth, each claiming to be the Mage herself.\n\nIt's as if the Mage tried to fight back against the Serpent and lost.

I wouldn't rule it out, but I haven't had time to look into their claims. You're free to investigate, but be wary of a trap. The Serpent could simply be baiting us.\n\nLast I heard, the women were still at the Crossroads Tavern here in Belkarth.
I'm at a loss. The conjurers who summoned the atronachs have disappeared.\n\nBut since the atronachs were summoned to defeat the Dark Anchors, perhaps the dolmens hold a clue.

The Serpent is clearly the inventor of Craglorn's troubles, though what his purpose is, or how he managed to bring the Warrior and the Mage to his side is unclear.\n\nMeanwhile, the Thief, the third of the guardian star signs, is silent.

Rumors from the Dragontail mountains are that the Serpent has begun creating new types of monsters. I know that an Orc woman, Galu gra-Burzol, went to Dragonstar to investigate.\n\nIf you could help her, I'm certain she'd appreciate it.

Indeed. And we can be certain that the Serpent is looking to capture her.\n\nIn fact, I've had one of our wisest Star-Gazers, Cassius, tracking the movements of the Serpent's followers, to ensure that they don't find the Thief.

That's a relief, but I would not advertise that fact. The Serpent will want her captured, like the others.\n\nI've had one of our wisest Star-Gazers, Cassius, tracking the movements of the Scaled Court. They are indeed looking for the Thief.

Because of the sensitive nature of his task, I haven't heard from him in a while. In his last missive, he was shadowing the Scaled Court to a ruin called Shadowstar at the foot of the Dragontail mountains.\n\nIf you want to help him, start there.

If reports are to believed, they're the stuff of nightmares. They are chaotic like their master, with many forms. Mantikora, they are called.\n\nI personally have no desire to face one, but Galu seemed thrilled by the challenge.

Dethisam provided them with the old graveyard key when they first arrived, and I've seen Maulborn coming and going through the back gate.\n\nIf we go to the back gate, I'm sure we can get one of the Maulborn to let us inside.
This is a gathering of the Undaunted, and you're about to become one of us! Hope your ears are ready to bleed ….
You wouldn't believe me. Just like these fools. The army of Tarish-Zi rises around them and they shackle the one man who can stop it without so much as a "by your leave."
Undead? Ha. These are no rotting draugr or mindless skeletons. Untie these bonds and help me stop them. I'll tell you what I can.
The Anka-Ra. A relentless fighting force … how can I explain? They conquered this region for their leader Tarish-Zi—it must have been centuries ago—and now they're conquering it again.
You sure? Dungeon delving and monster fighting is not for the weak of heart.

Good, but that's the easy part. The hard part's proving yourself.\n\n<<1>> seems like a good test. A dark, dank cave few return from. See if you can best whatever's inside. If you survive, come meet me back here and we'll make it official.

This road is the only thoroughfare that connects Bangkorai and Cyrodiil. And these so-called "Celestials" are making a mess of it.\n\nWe've appealed to the Daggerfall Covenant for help, but they're … distracted.
That damned Alliance War. Troops need to get to Cyrodiil, and the Covenant's got its hands full protecting its own supply lines. Or so they say.

The worst is near Elinhir. Damned mages fighting each other, spilling out onto the road ….\n\nBut there's also some kind of shimmering giant rock-thing that blasted a huge crater in the middle of Craglorn. It's damn creepy, whatever it is.

If this was Glenumbra or Stormhaven we were talking about and not backwater Craglorn, the Covenant would have no trouble finding the resources to help us—Alliance War or not. \n\nBut who am I to complain?

Word is, the mages that run the place are at each others' throats. \n\nYou ask me, it was inevitable. Inviting renegade mages to live there was just asking for trouble. Luckily, most of the citizens got out before things got really bad.

Some say it's the gods displeasure, fired from Aetherius to punish us. Others say it's Daedric. Still others think it's the Celestial Mage's staff, flung from the heavens. \n\nWhatever it is, it's bad news. I'd stay clear of it.
She's a strange one. Came out of the desert one day, spouting terrible prophecy about stars falling from the sky and a serpent let loose on an unsuspecting world.
We live in perilous times. We're always one interesting coincidence away from destruction. Me? I'm too old to ask such questions.

No one foresaw this—sand warriors attacking, atronachs in rebellion against their masters, strange and formless beasts ….\n\nBut Hara saw a glimmer of what was to come. Because of her, we were able to prepare and protect Belkarth.

I'd regale you with tales of our glory days, but there are none. There have been many of us over the years—fractious, decadent and insular, until they faded from existence.\n\nOur order would have followed the same course, were it not for Hara.

I could tell you a thousand things about the Celestials, but not a single one of them would be true.\n\nAre they stars fallen from the sky? Are they guardians created by some lost civilization? Are they a Daedric trick, played on us by Sheogorath?
It's my job to protect what little we know from disintegration and loss. It's for others to plumb fathomless mysteries and lose their minds seeking answers.
What? An informer? Me? No, no. I'm a simple dust-sweep begging for spare gold, nothing more.\n\nOn the other hand, if you have the gold, I'll be whatever you want me to be.

We must find Pelidil, of course. This one tracked his stinking hide here after he stole the Staff of Magnus. \n\nHe's the boss of the Veiled Heritance now, and he has allies here in Woodhearth—dirty traitors who conspire against Queen Ayrenn.

No. Razum-dar will be the queen instead! If this mage does his job, of course ….\n\nWe will go soon, so Raz must prepare. Speak to Treethane Fariel. She can tell you more about the traitors who are helping Pelidil.

This we do not know yet, but Razum-dar has devised the perfect way to flush these rats from their hidey-holes.\n\nIf they had an opportunity to assassinate the queen, surely they would take advantage of it, yes?
I'm just the hired muscle, but I'll tell you what I can.
Very good! You can see why this is my favorite riddle! You liked it too, yes?\n\nI will write this riddle down for Telenger, who will pay me, and I will have more gold! It is glorious!
Very clever! Yes, a riverbank!\n\nWould you like to hear another? It is too good to miss, and I need the practice.
This one is thinking of riddles, which makes me very busy inside.\n\nIt is somewhat lucrative, though I must practice them first. Would you stay and listen?
By most accounts, they were some of the first men to live in this region.\n\nBut history wasn't kind. The Elves and their ilk came in, and then the Yokudans, and all that's left is myth.

Hm. Razum-dar thought the vicereeve was a clawless coward. Always going on with "Prince Naemon this" and "Prince Naemon that." So pathetic.  \n\nBut he is more tricky now. All this one knows is that Pelidil is near and that he has the Staff of Magnus.

You share Razum-dar's … distaste, yes? We must accept them though.\n\nThe Thalmor were sent to Woodhearth when the Dominion was formed. This port is critical for trade, and there is concern it could be a target for enemy spies … or for the Maormer.

A perfect illusion, he says, to make Razum-dar look like Queen Ayrenn. \n\nThis one prefers a regular disguise, but Treethane Fariel doubts that would suffice. You should speak to her so we can get on with this.

Last time this one saw Naemon, he was still quite dead, but Pelidil wouldn't drag around the prince's corpse just to make sure he gets a proper burial.\n\nSome sort of necromancy must be planned, but why? Naemon can't rule the Dominion if he is undead!

Battlereeve Urcelmo issued the orders, but Queen Ayrenn gave her blessing. \n\nShe prefers not to send the Thalmor to every city in the Dominion, but in this case, she had little choice. Even Treethane Fariel agrees they are needed.

Of course. Wherever there is sea, there is the threat of the Sea Elves. \n\nThey've sought to conquer these shores for centuries, and the rise of the Dominion has only served to provoke them. The Thalmor help boost the city's defenses.
Ah! You are one who is well-traveled! One who understands everyone has a story to share.\n\nI was once an adventurer like yourself, until one fateful day, when my life changed forever.

A powerful enchantment forms a link between their bearer and the dreugh queen. When placed in the reliquaries and blessed, they have a calming effect upon her workers.\n\nThese relics are sacred to my people. Using them as weapons is blasphemy.

Heh. Funny you should ask. I was wondering the same thing. Then I realized he lured me here so his assassins could kill me.\n\nThis is my reward for my loyal service. A blade in my gut and a nice, cold tomb.

Planning? Oh, he's well past that point. As we speak, his armies are storming the shore up at Seaside Sanctuary. Once they've got a foothold there, they'll conquer all of Valenwood.\n\nAnd there's not a damn thing you can do about it.

It's simple enough. The Sea Elves have always coveted these shores. If they help Pelidil dismantle the Dominion, he's agreed to give them Valenwood.\n\nIt's not like these damn Bosmer have done anything other than cause us trouble.
Just leave me to die. I wouldn't accept your help and you'd be better off not offering.

Of course not. They're just one prong of the mighty trident with which Pelidil will smite the Dominion!\n\nHe's signed a treaty with the Maormer. And with the Staff of Magnus he's going to raise an army of undead. Yes. Your days are numbered all right.

Ha! Pelidil says he's under no illusions about that fact, but he still gets rather glossy-eyed when speaking about Naemon.\n\nI suspect he still harbors some hope that the prince will play a role in the future he has envisioned.

Of course. Who better to lead an undead army than an undead prince?\n\nAnd if Pelidil brings him back, Naemon will be bound by the vicereeve's will. No longer will Pelidil need to worry about the prince making bad decisions.

Ayrenn is a false queen and the Aldmeri Dominion is a pathetic joke. Nothing can change that fact, even Pelidil turning on me.\n\nI'll gladly sacrifice my life to bring about the Dominion's downfall. It means my life was worth something.

You mean Elsweyr? Far as I know Pelidil doesn't even care.  \n\nHe just wants the Summerset Isles. I don't even think he wants to rule them himself … as long as they're ruled by someone other than Naemon's sister.

Having her as a twin was torture. While she climbed the ranks of the Thalmor, I was perceived as a failure. When Pelidil recruited me, it was my turn to shine. \n\nI have no regrets. Heh. In the end, Asteril and I both lost our lives for the cause.

Ask what you will. I'm still looking for answers myself. I had only passed the first trial when these troubles struck the school.\n\nI suppose that's the reason I was able to escape when the others were lost.

The first trial is called the Trial of Fire. \n\nThe initiate must find the tombs of the flame-bearers and slay the gargoyles that guard them. Then the flame-bearers can light the braziers along the path to Rahni'Za.

So it's true? The Serpent does walk the face of Nirn? \n\nI can't begin to fathom the motivations of such a creature. But there's a legend that Rahni'Za's founder, his name long lost to history, dedicated it to the Warrior constellation.

I know only the strange rumors I heard from the few initiates who had not yet turned by the time I entered. The betrayer was a member of the Scaled Court, a servant of the Celestial Serpent who they say has appeared in Craglorn.

The books are conferred on completion of the first trial. The school had gone to chaos and ruin before I received mine.\n\nDivines, if only I could have done something. I keep thinking that I could have saved them had I been stronger.

The second trial is the arena, where the initiate Sword-Disciple must survive the melee.\n\nI was about to start this trial when the troubles struck. I don't know much about the other trials, but the initiates carried books that tell of them.

When the betrayer struck, the Sword-Disciples held fast to their honor and took up their blades against him. \n\nFor their efforts, they were turned into a mindless army. But I took the coward's way. I fell on my own blade rather than join Abelazar.

A test of stamina and pacing. The easiest of the three—if you have good allies by your side.\n\nThe arena master is a spirit who has dwelt in this place since its founding. He wasn't affected by all of this. He'll tell you all you need to know.

I never completed the Trial of Air. The other initiates told me of a hidden path across the tops of the school's buildings. It can only be seen when special sands are thrown upon it.\n\nWhere the path leads, I can't say.

On entering Rahni'Za, we were each given a book describing the trials. There's a place in the library for each of the books.\n\nAs I understand it, only those who managed to acquire a complete set could complete the Trial of Martial Knowledge.

There are five trials. You've completed the first, by entering this place. Then there's the Trial of the Arena, the Trial of the Air, and the Trial of Martial Knowledge.\n\nThen there is the final trial, the Trial of the True Path.
I was the master of this school. Its last, as it came to pass.\n\nMy blindness doomed us all. No one could have been as good as Abelazar appeared to be. I should have seen through his trickery.

Yes. He reached the end of the final trial faster than any student I'd seen before and when I conferred the name of Sword-Disciple on him, he cut me down.\n\nI can still hear his laughter. It will burn in my ears for all eternity.

It's called the Trial of the True Path. Ironic, then, that Abelazar the betrayer waits on the other side.\n\nReady yourself. If you have not completed the other trials, you will not be able to complete the Trial of the True Path.
The mists that cover the path are deadly. The way through it only opens for those who have completed the trials.

The barracks are off limits, so you'll need a disguise. A guard's uniform should do nicely.\n\nTry by the river. No matter how cold it is, the Nords seem to love going for a swim. Sometimes they even remember to take their armor off, first.

While I hate to hide such good looks, you're going to need a disguise. A guard uniform.\n\nI saw one of those idiots splashing around in the river not too long ago. If he's still there, you might be able to borrow his armor.

Perhaps. Like the Abbey of Blades, Rahni'Za is a place of secret arts, admitting only those brave enough and strong enough to gain entry. There are more myths than facts around it.\n\nPerhaps the Serpent simply wanted to eliminate potential opposition.

Well, off with you, then! With that uniform, you won't have any trouble getting into the barracks.\n\nBut that doesn't mean they won't toss you out on your arse if they catch you nabbing the jarl's wine! So keep your wits about you.
Peace, yes. I don't know if I'll ever be at peace with what happened here. Like everyone, I was so enamored of Abelazar, I never imagined what was to come.

That is for you to decide. The school has many hidden trials beyond those you've completed, and those too can be undertaken if you wish.\n\nAs for the other Sword-Disciples, they will not reach their final rest until the Serpent himself is defeated.

Well, get on with it then. You make that uniform look good, but I still don't have anything to drink here.\n\nJust be careful in there. No matter what you're wearing, if they catch you swiping the jarl's wine, they'll toss you out on your pretty arse.

He came among us as an initiate, seeking to master the trials and win the right to be called Sword-Disciple.\n\nHe was the best I'd ever seen. The way he moved with a blade, it was mesmerizing. But it was all a lie.

His allegiance was to the Celestial Serpent, not to us. His mastery was deceptive magic, not skill. \n\nWhen he reached the end of the final trial, he murdered our master and used foul magic to turn the Sword-Disciples into thralls.
Some nonsense.

These trials were placed here centuries before us. The secrets of their workings are hidden even to the masters of the school. \n\nIt was the founder's will that the teachings of the school should last, even when there was no master left to oversee it.

After Abelazar murdered me, he cast a ritual on the Sword-Disciples, turning them into thralls, neither living nor dead.\n\nI fear there is no hope of saving them, but you can give them rest by defeating Abelazar and destroying the one who sent him.

The Celestial Serpent. Abelazar was a member of the Scaled Court, worshipers of the Serpent. \n\nThey want only chaos for Tamriel. They saw the Sword-Disciples as a threat to their plans, which is why they sent Abelazar into our midst to destroy us.
He's a prisoner-of-war, so he'll be treated accordingly, of course.\n\nUnless he tries to escape, in which case, we'll bury him neck-deep on the beach at low tide and let the sea decide his fate.
The thralls are neither living nor dead. They answer only to the Serpent's will.\n\nIt's too late to save them, but you may give them rest by killing Abelazar and destroying his master, the Serpent.

Across Tamriel there is a handful of schools devoted to the secret arts of the blade. \n\nOf those, the greatest are Rahni'Za and the Abbey of Blades. But there are others, secretive and hidden, that carry the tradition.

Their locations are secret, even to me. \n\nEach school has its own secret techniques to teach—the most dedicated blademaster might spend a lifetime searching for each school. I have never heard of anyone mastering them all.

His name has been lost to history. By legend, he is Rahni'Za, the spirit of the blade, but no one knows who the man—or woman—was.\n\nYet his legacy lives on in the trials, which function like clockwork, even now.

Vicereeve Pelidil, that monstrous bastard! He captured us in Woodhearth and brought us here for some evil ritual!\n\nHe bled us, mutilated us … he ripped out our eyes! Gods, do I even look normal any more?

No. I'm not all right. I'm dying, and it's just as well.\n\nIt was that bitch, Asteril's sister … she pretended to be Asteril and ordered us into the Imperial Underground. Then the Veiled Heritance ambushed us. They needed sacrifices for the ritual.

They were raising Prince Naemon from the dead … bringing him back and imbuing him with some terrible power. \n\nPelidil kept talking about how the prince would lead an undead army … but I don't think it worked out the way he hoped.
No … no! My eyes are gone … I'm probably scarred all over my body …. \n\nPlease … I just want to die.

When Naemon came back, he wasn't … the same. Sounded like some evil spirit was speaking through him. He spat in Pelidil's face. Then he just left ….\n\nPelidil was furious. He stormed out a little later … that's all I was able to hear.

I heard the researchers call it a lost Nedic city. I guess the Nedes were the people who lived in Craglorn before the Yokudans showed up.\n\nThe researchers have started calling the ruin Shada's Tear.

I'm resigning from the Camlorn Guard. With that Angof … thing taken care of, it'll be good to travel for awhile.\n\nSee exotic lands, flirt with exotic women, and drink exotic wine. Oh, and cheese. I love cheese!

I'm resigning from the Camlorn Guard. With that Angof … thing taken care of, they need builders, not soldiers. I think I'll travel for a while, see the world.\n\nUnless, of course, you'd care to tempt me with a drink before I start my heroic journey?

Well, then! All the more reason for me to get out there and hasten that moment's arrival!\n\nAnyway, the werewolves slipped in on my watch. I need to make amends for that. I need to make sure Camlorn isn't threatened again.
Are you one of those who violated our sanctuary?
Deep within our sanctuary, others have unleashed a force beyond their control. Lead me to the door, if you dare to enter.

Desperation, mainly. My son is sick. I needed a cure. I read about a city that was named for a healer named Shada and a relic called the Water of Life. People told me it didn't exist. But I had to find it.\n\nStill, I wasn't expecting this.

Legend says that the Water of Life could cure any illness. It was kept in this city, and used by a healer named Shada to cure the sick.\n\nMy son has a terrible disease. No priest can cure it. The Water of Life is my last hope.
I know everything. You have come to my shrine because the stars have fallen to Tamriel. You want to know how to defeat them.

I can. But knowledge must never be given freely. A price must be paid.\n\nPart of the cost was bringing my servant Ibrula back to me. But you will pay much more if you want to learn all that I know about the Celestials.

I am the Celestial Thief. I appeared with the other Guardians when the Serpent broke free and manifested in Tamriel.\n\nOne by one, the Serpent trapped the others. First the Warrior, then the Mage. He wants to do the same to me.
Yes. They attack Craglorn against their will.\n\nListen. The Serpent's nature is chaos. He wants to undermine the very order of reality. He will not stop with Craglorn.

Hara and the Star-Gazers will help you. Use their knowledge. Look for the presence of the Scaled Court—where they are, the Serpent is surely at work. \n\nBut you must not tell anyone you saw me. The Serpent's followers are everywhere.
My power alone is not enough. You must free the other Guardians. I will help you as much as I dare, but the Serpent is looking for me. If he ensnares me as he has the others, all is lost.
In a way. Just as you might look at a picture of the star signs and say "That's the Thief" or "That's the Warrior." Just so, I'm the Thief, or one way of seeing the Thief.

Of the twelve rightful star signs, it's the Guardians' duty to protect the lesser signs, our charges, against the destructive ways of the Serpent.\n\nWith the Warrior and Mage under the Serpent's control, their charges are vulnerable. So is Tamriel.
It would be surprising if I didn't. \n\nThe Star-Gazers are only dimly aware of it, but they carry an ancient legacy as students of the star signs. Their devotion has not gone unnoticed.
I can't promise that my answers will satisfy. Craglorn has always been a harsh place and desolate. Much of Craglorn's history has long since passed into myth.

Then listen closely, as I will not repeat myself. The Celestial Warrior's army of Anka-Ra was created centuries ago by the Yokudan general, Tarish-Zi. \n\nHe came to me to learn how to bind his army to him—even in death. I granted his wish.

His offering pleased me. He built the temple above this shrine and promised that his army would defend it.\n\nThe Anka-Ra have risen, which means Tarish-Zi has risen as well. They are bound to him. To defeat them, you must defeat him.

I don't know. I haven't seen him myself, but I can't tell you how many soldiers have fled from the forest terrified and bewildered, mumbling to themselves about Naemon.\n\nTo hear them tell it, the prince … or whatever he's become … is everywhere.
Not long ago, I heard Naemon was leading them, then he died, and I heard that wasn't true, that he was a hero. Now, I don't know what in Oblivion to believe!

After the death of the Silvenar, the Mane came to offer his condolences … and his assistance to Valenwood.\n\nThen this mess started. He led a scouting patrol into the old merchant tunnels, but they got cut off. It's possible they've all been killed.
I was a priestess of Shada.\n\nWe who were here when the Yokudans came were caught in Shada's curse. We remain, long after death ought to have claimed us, living in the moment before our destruction.

Our people … they were not always kind. But this city was filled with those who cared for others.\n\nThrough Shada's blessing, men and women on the brink of death were revived in the waters of our city. Until the Yokudans came.

Shada's curse is this: that the once life-giving water bring only death to those who drink it, and that the spirits of the past shall haunt the living for eternity.\n\nThis was because the Yokudans intended to turn the city into a fortification.

They are the keys. They open the way to our city's greatest treasure, to Shada herself.\n\nShada, who blessed us with our famous healing gifts, and who in the end cursed us all in order to save us all.

They came to this land to conquer it, to bring it into submission to their dread leader, Tarish-Zi.\n\nWith the healing power of the city, the Yokudan armies would have been unstoppable. That is why Shada cursed the city—to save it.

She was our chief healer, but she was also so much more. Myself, I never saw her face. Few ever did. But her blessing enabled us to care for the sick.\n\nIt was also what drew the Yokudans to our city.

I am Shada. I purified these waters so that the people of this city could drink and be healed. I am the only relic that exists.\n\nThe gift you seek is lost now. I cursed these waters and this place to keep the Yokudans from abusing their power.

Yes, and for that, I am grateful.

But enemies from the past rise again. I can sense their power all throughout the deathlands, as numerous as the sands.

I will not—I cannot lift this curse.

Tarish-Zi rises again, and with him, his Yokudan army, the Anka-Ra. Puppets of a still more powerful being, a Serpent of infinite cruelty.\n\nBut I sense that you oppose them as we once did. Perhaps there is something I can help with.

A single draught of the very waters you seek. Purified by my own hand.

For what you fight for, you have earned this gift. Use it wisely and do not make me regret my decision. 

Now go. There is nothing more for you here.

The Yokudans would have used the power of this place to further their bloody conquest and become unstoppable.\n\nShada's curse ensured that such a terrible future would never come to pass, but at the cost of all our lives.
Do not pity me. If I had not failed to hide the goblet in time, perhaps all of this could have been averted. This solitary watch is both my duty and my penance.

Yes, it's high time Tamriel was free of Molag Bal's grip. The Anchors, the Daedra, the undead … they devastate our fragile mortal plane. \n\nI have a plan, and I need your help. I think you're the only one who can help me see this done.

I want you to meet with Razum-dar, first in the Eyes of the Queen. He'll be at the Mages Guild in Skywatch. Even Ayrenn's personal agents think my idea is sound!\n\nI'll be along shortly, I just have a few final preparations to make.

I want you to meet with Copper Dariah, leader of the Ring of Daggers. She'll be at the Mages Guild in Daggerfall city. Even Emeric's personal agents think my idea is sound!\n\nI'll be along shortly, I just have a few final preparations to make.

I want you to meet with Thrush, leader of the Hidden Armigers. He'll be at the Mages Guild in Mournhold. Even Jorunn's personal agents think my idea is sound!\n\nI'll be along shortly, I just have a few final preparations to make.

During my time on Tamriel, I developed a very useful spell. A memory charm of sorts. It allows me to recall a book, any moment in time, instantly and without pause. I would ask you to accept it as a gift for your service … and as penance.

During my time on Tamriel, I developed a very useful spell. A memory charm of sorts. Rather than wasting my time puttering around in libraries trying to find a book, the spell allows me to recall it instantly.\n\nIf you'll allow me?
That was a dark day. We should never have trusted in Mannimarco. Now the whole world is paying for our mistake.

It is. And from everything I've heard, your King Emeric is a good man. But the Covenant believes itself to be the last remnant of the Reman Empire. They truly believe that the Lion banner will be flown over White-Gold Tower. More Worm Cult lies.

It is. And from everything I've heard, your King Jorunn is a good man. But the Pact is convinced the old Empire will be swept away. That the Dragon banner will fly over White-Gold Tower. More Worm Cult lies.

It is. And from everything I've heard, your Queen Ayrenn is a good woman. But the Dominion believes that the Elves will rule Tamriel. That mer, not men, will take the Ruby Throne. More Worm Cult lies.

After Emperor Varen was lost, Mannimarco put Clivia Tharn on the Ruby Throne. Today, Cyrodiil's a smoldering  battlefield, strewn with corpses. Each of the three alliances is trying to "save" the heart of the old Empire from Mannimarco's worms.

You must consult with Indaenir. He has already been considering this question.\n\nAkkhuz-ri must warn you—Indaenir is very strange, even for a Bosmer—but this one has never met an Elf with such understanding of nature. Come, let me introduce you.

No one knows, but if destroying Marbruk were his goal, you would expect the prince to remain, yes?\n\nNo. The prince plans something else, and his plans must be uncovered. You are clearly capable. I think you should undertake this task.

Indaenir will know better. You came in together, so this one assumes you are already acquainted, yes?\n\nHe is strange—even for a Bosmer—but Akkuz-ri has never met an Elf who understands nature so well. Come though. Let us consult with him.

Driladan Pass is old. Many Bosmer died here and some cannot be raised by any magic—they are the accursed souls who violated the Green Pact. \n\nCome with me and we will try to commune with them. Perhaps they will know what the Shade truly plans.

No. They are tethered to their remains and they cannot pass into death, nor can they return to life. Thus they remain witness to all that transpires among living and dead alike, but unable to participate.\n\nCome, let us see what they know of Naemon.

Oh. There are many ways. Perhaps they cut down a tree or ate berries from the local plants. \n\nSometimes their intentions were good, but Valenwood is unforgiving. If they violate the Pact, they cannot pass from this plane.
Thrice-blessed are we. I couldn't have asked Urcelmo for a better Marine.\n\nWhat of the Veiled Queen? Did you learn anything more?
I had a feeling things would get worse. We'll get a warning to Lord Rilis in Firsthold, and spread word to all of northern Auridon.

Mad as he is, I thought he came from the Bramblebreach clan, but some said it was Woodhearth. Truth is, no one knows. \n\nEven heard he was raised by an old Graht Oak, cradled in its roots, weaned on the dew from its leaves. He's a mystery, all right.
You're one of Raz's? Thank Mara. We could use you. \n\nThere are Daedra everywhere. Portals to Oblivion opened within the city and an army of the beasts threatens to take Firsthold.
He's at the Mages Guild hall. Should be straight ahead, across the bridge. \n\nTrinimac's blade keep you safe.

It's hard for me to believe, but reports indicate High Kinlady Estre is behind this. We hold the line here, but that could change at any moment.\n\nBattlereeve Urcelmo sent a runner requesting aid. He has a plan to deal with these beasts, apparently.

Estre dropped a barrier around the inner castle. We'll need a way past it, to get at the portals. I think the Battlereeve and the guild leader plan to crack that thing like an egg. The frontal approach.
It sounds much worse when you say it that way.\n\nConsider it a loan. You know I'm good for it. I have an honest face.
That's all you can spare?\n\nAll right. I guess it will have to do.
Fine. Be that way. You're as cold as this damn land.\n\nBesides, I didn't really want your gold, anyway. I don't accept ill-gotten gain.
He … he what? Rid-Thar-ri'Datta? In person? Shazah has read of such things, but has never seen such a vision. \n\nAnd you are the Moon Hallowed … then that means ….

By Jone and Jode … that means Khali and I are eligible to walk the trial paths. One of us will be the next Mane! \n\nI need to think on this … Hallowed. Please, let us deal with the spirits here. Then we can talk.
The Dro-m'Athra, Akkhuz-ri, the Champions … all are part of a whole. What lies ahead will require blood and steel and courage to overcome.

Pass through the flames, they will not harm you. Not you, of all people. Within the temple you will find the source of the darkness. Destroy it and you will return control of the fort to those who live in the light.
Stendarr blesses you with his wisdom and vision. For a generous contribution in his name, the God of Mercy, Charity and Justice will grant you the power to revisit your choices regarding Skills.
Your Skills have been reset.

Yes, actually. I'll make sure the way to the Earth Forge remains open to you from now on. I've found that the gear forged here often has special qualities. You might find it to your liking.\n\nGood luck, my friend.

The flame-bearers are the spirits of three previous masters of the school. So devoted were they to training future Sword-Disciples, they bound their spirits here. Even in death, they teach new initiates the ways of the blade.

It's no use. When father called for my aid, I could feel the rage boiling inside me. It took all my strength to control it.\n\nBut that's what you're saying, isn't it? It's part of me now. It's something I can control.

We provide training in unique spells and abilities only available to members! And from time to time projects crop up for those with an adventuresome spirit. \n\nYou may end up working with the Guildmaster himself!

Vanus Galerion, one of the founding members of this august body. Still holds the proud title of Guildmaster, overseeing every guildhall in Tamriel. He works with other ranking members, such as Telenger the Artificer, to ensure our future success.

We are neutral in the war between the three Alliances. While many of us here in Davon's Watch hold true to the Dragon banner, when we're on Guild business we kneel to no king or queen. \n\nThat's why you'll see members of every race in our halls.
What? You're serious? Fine, fine! Just don't hurt me!
Of all the … all right! I know how this works. Take it and be on your way!
Oh, not again.\n\nYes, yes. Hand over the gold, don't try to run, nobody can help me, tell the guard and you'll kill me. You're not the first bandit to accost me. Or the last, I suspect.

Smart question. We train our members in special techniques. And the higher-ups are always looking for motivated members to help with special projects. You never know when the Council will come looking for more hands.

Guildmaster Jofnir passed away recently, and very suddenly. We always thought he'd die with a blade in his hand. But he passed in his sleep, called to Sovngarde by his ancestors. \n\nWe all miss him, but Colors has proven to be a very able leader.

No, our blades are in service to the guild. We're neutral in the war between the three Alliances. Some of us follow the Dragon banner and King Jorunn, of course. But every race, every creed, belongs under the Guildhall's roof.

The King's Arrow, yes? Well met.\n\nTell no one that Betar-Nes was a member of the Worm Cult. I won't have Nimalten fall into chaos. We're on his trail. My advisor and the court mage search for any hint of the cult as we speak.

Well met.\n\nTell no one that Betar-Nes was a member of the Worm Cult. I won't have Nimalten fall into chaos. We're on his trail. My advisor and the court mage search for any hint of the cult as we speak.

Too slow for my liking. My advisor Borodin is at the inn, asking questions of the townfolk. My court mage, Golun, has a theory about the Worm Cult's plan. He's at the Mages Guild, doing research.\n\nPerhaps you can give them a hand?

Hah! Good question. We train our members in special techniques. And the higher-ups are always looking for motivated members to help with special projects. You never know, you might be the next Jofnir!

Guildmaster Jofnir passed away recently, very suddenly. I always thought he'd die with a blade in his hand. But he passed away in his sleep, called to Sovngarde by his ancestors. We all miss him, but Colors has proven to be a very able leader.

No, we only draw blades in service to the guild. We're technically neutral in the war between the three Alliances. We love the Eagle banner and Her Majesty, of course. But every race, every creed, belongs under the Guildhall's roof.

We provide training in unique spells and abilities only available to members! And from time to time projects crop up for those with an adventuresome spirit. \n\nYou may end up working with the Guildmaster himself!

Vanus Galerion, one of the founding members of this august body. Still holds the proud title of Guildmaster, overseeing every guildhall in Tamriel. He works with other ranking members, such as Telenger the Artificer, to ensure our future success.
We are neutral in the war between the three Alliances. When we're on Guild business we kneel to no king or queen.\n\nThat's why you'll see members of every race in our halls.

"Rogutter: Keep this runestone out of the mine! If you bring it near the Unspeakable Sigil, the portal closes. Then we're cut off from the relics. That means we don't get paid!"\n\n"If you don't understand, I'll start breaking fingers until you do."
You should join up! Our new guildmaster is an Argonian woman, Sees-All-Colors. She has us working to a singular purpose—hunting down the Daedra and their damned Anchors.
Those enormous chains descending from the sky? A passage opens to Oblivion, and Daedra boil out to lay waste to the countryside. I don't know who started calling them Daedric Anchors, but it fits.

Good question. We train our members in special techniques. The higher-ups are always looking for motivated members to help with special projects. Sees-All-Colors herself might even have a task for you someday!
Then let me be the first to officially welcome you as a comrade in arms of the Fighters Guild!\n\nGet out there, and take the fight to the Daedra!
Where did …? Oh, over there somewhere. Gleefully, and jingling with their ill-gotten gains.\n\nPlease, could you spare a something for this one to make a fresh start?
This is more than I'd dared to hope! You are S'rendarr himself, walker. S'rendarr himself!
Pah! There are no bandits. You are listening, but you do not hear!\n\nThis one should have known better than to ask. What a waste of time!
I am. I was raised as a slave. My masters never thought to teach me how to fend for myself, so when I ran away ….\n\nI do not even know how to ask for help.
I never thought I'd know such kindness. Thank you.
So says the root to the toad that licks it in the dry season. Keep your moisture. May it serve you well.
A mark! One who fights for coin! Spare some, will you? Mine's run off. Dallying with a lightcatch, sure!
Will it? Pleasure, burr-sap! Shadows keep you safe!
Shoulda known you for a dry-cap. See if I keep your steps shadowed!
