The Seeker's Archive is no ordinary library. It's actually a shrine to Hermaeus Mora, the Daedric Lord of Knowledge.
Yes. It was built centuries ago—long before the Yokudans came to Hammerfell.\n\nI've been visiting the shrine for several years now, offering relics to Hermaeus Mora in exchange for secret knowledge.
You should join up! Our new guildmaster is an Argonian woman, Sees-All-Colors. She has us working to a singular purpose—hunting down the Daedra and their damned Anchors.
Those enormous chains descending from the sky? A passage opens to Oblivion, and Daedra boil out to lay waste to the countryside. I don't know who started calling them Daedric Anchors, but it fits.

Good question. We train our members in special techniques. The higher-ups are always looking for motivated members to help with special projects. Sees-All-Colors herself might even have a task for you someday!
Then let me be the first to officially welcome you as a comrade in arms of the Fighters Guild!\n\nGet out there, and take the fight to the Daedra!

I'm sorry, but I wasn't sure you would help me if you knew. Not everyone has an open mind where Daedric Princes are concerned.\n\nBut I do seek knowledge to defeat the Celestials. That much is true. I believe Hermaeus Mora can provide that knowledge.
All I have told you is all you have earned.\n\nIf you wish to know more, you must become my eyes and ears in Craglorn. You must bring me fresh knowledge to feast upon.
I hunger for lost bits of lore. I thirst for new knowledge to add to my coffers. Bring your offerings to me. If I find them acceptable, I will return their worth in the knowledge you seek.
Ні.

This temple is a good example. The Anka-Ra crawled out of the ground all around it, and started guarding it as if—well, as if they were just picking up where they left off when they died.\n\nI believe they are deeply connected to Craglorn, somehow.

That is one of the questions I hoped to answer within. They appear to be neither living nor dead, but not exactly undead either. Cursed. \n\nIt's said that the Celestial Warrior controls them, but I sense that's only part of the story.
Call it chance, or fate. I was once a Star-Gazer, searching the stars for signs and prophecies.\n\nLittle did I realize that the knowledge I sought was not in the sky above, but in the ground below.

The Seeker's Archive is another of Craglorn's many mysteries. An astonishing library, left mostly untouched for centuries, built by unknown hands.\n\nThe temple atop the library is Yokudan in origin, but some of the books pre-date even the Yokudans!

The followers of Hermaeus Mora who worshiped here were called Seekers.\n\nThe Seekers brought gifts to the shrine, and the Daedric Prince rewarded them with secret knowledge. I carry a relic from the Dragontail mountains for just such a purpose.

I do what I must. Hermaeus Mora is not like other Daedra. He may seem cruel at times, but he's not irrational.\n\nHe's only interested in knowledge. If bringing him gifts will save Craglorn from the Celestials, then so be it.
Gendyn? I'm so proud of my big brother! He moved to the big city and in no time at all he was practically running the place!

He oversees the forge at Artisans Craftworks. It's the best smithy in Mournhold!\n\nGendyn promised he'd get me a great price on the goods I need to keep the family business open. He must have lost the order or something. That's the only explanation!

I might have something that will interest you. We captured a Red Rook messenger prowling around our camp.\n\nWe think he was going to a Red Rooks and Bloodthorns meeting. Rumor is they're forming an alliance, but we can't get the messenger to talk.
Might as well give it a shot. He's been telling us a sad story about his kidnapped family, but I don't believe a word of it.\n\nIf you want to try to make the bandit talk, he's right over there.

It's been silent since the Yokudans invaded back in the First Era. Supposedly built during that time.\n\nUntil recently, that door behind you was shut, either by sorcery or craftsmanship. None could best it.

The door opened. Many came. Some Redguards grabbed stones from this chamber, claiming pieces of their ancestral home.\n\nBut something out there started grabbing the Redguards and scholars. Even members of the Undaunted.
You saw what I saw. Faolchu answered to Angof. But at least you took care of the Gravesinger. \n\nWait … the werewolf apparently has something to say.
Angof? He continues to haunt us, damn his eyes!\n\nMy royal spymaster reports that the unrest Angof stirred up continues to ripple through the kingdom.
Creating chaos is a method, not a goal. It's a means, not an end.\n\nAngof hoped for more than simply chaos for its own sake. We must remain vigilant.
I do need the practice.

We started our research here. Figured it was less dangerous than the crypts. Everything seemed fine at first. People kept drinking the water though. Thought nothing of it.\n\nIt started with the strange whispering. Then the hostility.

My partner, Nahlia, refused to drink the waters as well.\n\nA couple of the researchers dragged her off through those doors before they slammed shut. I couldn't find a way to open them, but I found this scroll on the desk. It might be the key we need.

Just look at it - the stuff even looks like it's cursed.\n\nA couple of us held out from drinking it. Most of us aren't around anymore either. Those who did drink it started muttering things about "Shada's Will" and "Shada commands we give our life".

There might be. The people who led us down here drug poor Nahlia through the doors at the far end of the room. Watched them slam shut behind them.\n\nI have no idea how to open the doors, but the scroll I found above me might give us a clue of sorts.
If the others really were turned into thralls of the Nereids, then Nahlia is in serious danger.\n\nOur leaders drank the water first: Klause, Squan, and Zifri. We have to find them and save Nahlia.

Klause got his hands on some ancient horn of sorts when we first started our work. He never knew what it did until he started drinking the waters. Gave him knowledge, he said.\n\nI watched him control the dead with it. I fear for the ways he'll use it.

Squan was a genius. The man always knew how to conjure up just the right spell. Master of conjuration and all things, I watched him summon up atronachs to do with as he pleases.\n\nOut of all of us, I thought he'd be the last to succumb to the curse.

Zifri was our smith. She fixed and repaired our tools and crafted us weapons. She was looking into an old smithy in this very wing when she succumbed to the curse.\n\nYou best be on your guard around her.

It's … tainted, cursed—call it what you like.\n\nSome of the researchers drank it when we first got here. They started foaming at the mouth and screaming about someone called "Shada." It made them freakishly strong, too.

Half our camp's missing inside one of the wings and there's undead crawling out of every crack in the place.\n\nWe need supplies and mercs. But I guess this Celestial business has everyone distracted topside.

You heard right. The first researchers to drink the water said it tasted like nothing they ever drank. Made them feel strong, alive.\n\nAnd then they started changing. They attacked us, like we were intruders and they were defending the city.
It fits their reputation. Nereids are known for practicing a dark and twisted sorcery to control people's minds.\n\nDrinking the water appears to turn you into a thrall of a Nereid called Shada.

Well, that's where things get truly strange. Seems that this place was built by Nedes—the ancient people who settled Craglorn before the Yokudans. \n\nWe don't know a lot about the Nedes, but it seems like these particular ones worshiped nereids.

See that pool? The water flows into it from the temple wings on either side and blocks the way to the main chamber. \n\nMy guess is if you follow the water into those wings, you'll find the source of the corruption. A Nereid, if I'm right.
Stuhn blesses you with his wisdom and vision. For a generous contribution in his name, the God of Ransom, Fraternity, and Justice will grant you the power to revisit your choices regarding Skills.
Your Skills have been reset.
Kyne blesses you with her wisdom and vision. For a generous contribution in her name, the Goddess of Storm will grant you the power to revisit your choices regarding Attributes.
Your Attributes have been reset.
Auriel blesses you with his wisdom and vision. For a generous contribution in his name, the God of Time will grant you the power to revisit your choices regarding Attributes.
Your Attributes have been reset.
The Nereids call her Shada.\n\nWhen they drank the water, Klause and the others became her thralls. They thought they could serve her by sacrificing me.

There's a Nereid in a nearby chamber. The others called her a Daughter of Shada.\n\nShe is the one corrupting the waters in this wing. I don't know about the rest of the temple, though. Perhaps there are other Daughters of Shada.

She's the Nereid queen, or leader, or whatever it is Nereids have.\n\nIt sounded like she is the one responsible for the cursed water. That's why all the undead in here worship her. They drank the water and became her thralls.

You're here to help? That means Fights-With-Tail must have escaped. You have no idea how relieved I am to hear that.\n\nListen. The city won't be safe until the Blackcaster mages and their leader, Arch-Mage Yamanu-ko, are defeated.

Good. Then, this barrier is Yamanu-ko's last defense. It should be weak enough for me to break now.\n\nI'm afraid it will still take a great deal of my strength, however, so you will have to face Yamanu-ko alone.

Be careful with the arch-mage. Yamanu-ko was powerful even before she learned the Serpent's wicked trick.\n\nShe's only grown more powerful since, stealing magicka from her fellow mages and immersing herself in unspeakable rituals.

The city lies in ruins and the Blackcaster mages run rampant over the corpses of the dead. Every moment that Yamanu-ko continues to draw breath is a moment wasted.\n\nBut I understand. This situation is far from normal.

Yamanu-ko was my master. I learned everything I know about magic from her.\n\nIncluding the dangers of temptation and too much power. I should have stopped her when I saw what was happening. But I was afraid.

I was Yamanu-ko's third apprentice. I realized—too late—that the deal we made would be our undoing. \n\nThe spell we were taught was pure savagery. And the cost was too high. I tried to get as many people out of the city as I could ….

When the mage Felix Blackcaster first came to Elinhir, it was a struggling settlement. \n\nHe promised protection and prosperity in exchange for establishing a magic school. It was an arrangement that served the city well for hundreds of years.

That's a long story. The short of it is, we made a deal. \n\nA man approached us promising us knowledge of ancient Nedic magics. Our towers are Nedic in origin, but we knew little about them. So we accepted.
It was ordinary by magical standards. In spite of what the Mages Guild might say, we were not renegades.\n\nI still don't fully understand what drove Yamanu-ko to this … madness.
If it will help you free Elinhir from the grip of the mad mages, I am happy to answer.

The Blackcaster mages protected Elinhir against the dangers of Craglorn.\n\nWith the Iron Orcs in the hills and bandits everywhere, the people of Elinhir looked to the mages to keep them safe. In exchange, we supported them and their studies.

Craglorn is the sort of place you go to when you don't want to be anywhere else.\n\nThe people who come here want independence more than anything. The arrangement we had with the mages was mutually beneficial.

Elinhir was the oldest city in Craglorn, and the only home I've ever known.\n\nIt wasn't easy, settling out here, especially before the trade road. That's why the founders of the city welcomed the Blackcaster mages.
Minerva was one of Arch-Mage Yamanu-ko's apprentices, but when the others went bad, she didn't. \n\nI can't imagine how many people would have died if Minerva hadn't intervened.

The Blackcaster mages operated independently of the Mages Guild.\n\nCraglorn attracts a certain type of person, you see. The kind that want to get away from the rest of the world. Still, the Blackcasters never caused any trouble, until now.

We can't reach the main chamber while the pool is corrupted. We need to find the Nereids corrupting the water in the other wings first.\n\nAs for what's in the main chamber, I'm guessing it's the leader of the nereids—Shada, as her thralls call her.
The final chamber. She's been imprisoned for the sacrifice. No time. You must find a way to open her prison, or Shada will claim her.
No time. Fading fast.\n\nYou need two people to unlock Nahlia's prison. They must open the lock at the same time. Otherwise, the Nereids will take her.
I can't. There's no time. Look to the pillars. You have to look to the pillars for the key.
They are the masters of this place. They are the ones who've cursed the water.\n\nAny who drink it become thralls to Shada, their master. You must stop them. Free Nahlia.
She is master of this place. Master of the nereids. It's her curse that corrupts the water.\n\nWe drank the water and became more powerful than ever. We also became her slaves. Stop her. Free Nahlia.
No time. My spirit fades. Look for the faces on the stone pillars. When you reach Nahlia's prison, you will see. You will understand.

The devices are guarded by Yamanu-ko's apprentices, Leta and Avys, in their towers.\n\nOnce you've destroyed the devices and weakened the ward, I'll meet you at the base of Yamanu-ko's tower to finish breaking the spell.

Yamanu-ko is their leader. Defeating her should bring the others to their senses.\n\nBut her tower is warded, protected by strange Nedic devices in each of her apprentices' towers. You need to destroy these devices to reach Yamanu-ko.

Alchemy is the art of creating potions. We scour the fields and caves of Tamriel in search of reagents like mushrooms, flowers, and the like. Mixing these ingredients with a water solvent in the correct quantities can create powerful elixirs.
Well, not just any water will do. You'll find that some pools of water contain special qualities that make them ideal for potion-making. The grade of the water determines the potency of the product.

All reagents have hidden properties. When they are combined with other ingredients that bestow the same benefits, the potency is compounded. This reaction determines the nature of the potion. It's just a matter of experimentation, you see?

Of course! Enchanting is the art of empowerment. We gather runes found throughout the world and use our special instruments to assemble them into glyphs. These glyphs can be used to magically enhance worn or wielded items.

Not exactly. Runes can be extracted from glyphs you find while adventuring. It's a delicate process, so you'll have to return to one of our work stations to proceed. Note that the glyph will be destroyed in the process. Unfortunate, but necessary.

Glyphs are assembled by combining three different runes. 

Potency runes determine the glyph's strength. Aspect affects the glyph's quality. Finally, the Essence rune decides the glyph's effect.

It's a delicate art best learned by doing. Good luck.

We put hammer to anvil to forge armor and weapons. This requires a lot of metal. We scour hills and caves looking for rare ores to work. \n\nRaw materials will only take you so far. You need style books and special ingredients for more advanced work.

It's what Redguards from northern Tamriel call themselves. Velyn Harbor used to trade with Redguard merchants, so they grew to call them "Ra Gada" as a sign of respect.\n\nFrom this point on, I'll bet it's a curse.

No. As a justiciar, the Thalmor Inner Council directs me to investigate and enforce Dominion law. They've never given me soldiers.\n\nWithout an armed encampment, the Argonians might have trusted me. But that's not how they see it in <<1>>.

Well, the piece can be augmented even more through the use of tempers. These elements can enhance the value and quality of your work. Of course, no worthwhile endeavor comes without risk. Trying to improve an item can result in breaks, so be careful!

You bet. A true blacksmith can read the metal to determine its potential. During the forging process we can choose a trait that best fits the item—provided we've done our research. Additional sharpening, extra weight … these are just examples.

We tan, weave, stitch—you name it. People in search of medium and light armor come to us. This requires fibers, leather, and a work table like those found in town.\n\nWe also seek out style books and special ingredients for more advanced work.

Well, the piece can be improved even more through the use of tannins. These elements can enhance the value and quality of your work. Just be cautious. You risk ruining the piece if you're not careful. Improving on perfection is no mean feat!

Yes, of course. During the tailoring process, we can choose a special trait for the work. It takes research to discover these techniques, but it's well worth the effort. Reinforced buckles, intricate detail work … each brings a special benefit.

Certainly! Woodworkers shape wood into all manner of useful tools, but bows, staves, and shields are our specialty. This work requires fine lumber and a sturdy work table.\n\nWe also seek out style books and rare ingredients for more advanced work.

Well, the piece can be improved even more through the use of resins—special elements that enhance the value and quality of your work. The improvement process is delicate, so be sure you've got enough tempers and a steady hand. Good luck!

Sure. While shaping the wood, we can choose a special trait to focus on. It takes research to discover these techniques, but it's well worth the effort. Increasing the weight or tuning the angle can draw out different advantages in the final product.

Of course! We provisioners practice the arts of cooking and brewing. \n\nGood food requires the best ingredients. We gather fresh meat and produce from crates, barrels, and the like. If we're lucky, we'll also find recipes in chests, trunks, and desks.

Don't forget drink! 

Hearty meals will fill your belly, increasing your general well-being—both body and soul. Strong drink can stimulate the humors, allowing you to recover more quickly.

If you're lucky, you might find a recipe that does both!

The atronachs? I don't care to think about those creatures. \n\nOne moment we were summoning them and destroying the Dark Anchors, and the next they turned on us like ungrateful dogs!
I don't know. But I think I know how to find out. We need to talk to the atronachs directly and ask them what happened.

Zal'ik was a smart man, and he went to great lengths to prevent the city from falling to the Yokudans. He would not have let his work be undone so easily.\n\nStill, it should now be possible to move ahead, so long as you avoid the cloud of poison.

When Shada cursed me, she bound me to Zal'ik's soul. She trusted that the barrier would hold against any invaders, keeping Zal'ik well-defended.\n\nIf Zal'ik falls, so too does any spell that binds me. It is as simple as that.
Wait for the barrier to move and follow closely behind. When an opening appears, do not hesitate.\n\nZal'ik's resting chambers are right around this hall. Not far to go, now.
Even so, I have no right to gloat. If Zal'ik had taken my counsel, our people would have been slaughtered by the Yokudans.

Indeed, I did. I have recorded all of my centuries of learning here in this book. I believe there may even be a way to cure someone who is still in the early stages of the madness.\n\nLet it help you and your people, if it can. It is too late for mine.

I have thought long on whether and how the effects of the curse can be reversed.\n\nFor those whose flesh has rotted, there is no cure. But for those still in the early stages, I believe I have an answer, but I require something in return.

My own freedom. When I spoke out against this unholy bargain, my soul was bound to that of Zal'ik, the general who gave our people over to the Nereids.\n\nTo free me, you must defeat him. But be careful. He has sealed the way with a cloud of poison.
You inspired hope, not courage. You will bind the other atronachs. \n\nYou, not we.

The Serpent has bound the flame monarch within the ancient Ayleid ruin of Molavar, and the monarch stone atronach has come under control of the Scaled Court summoners in the foothills north of Elinhir.

This place is haunted by visions of the past, my own memories of the events leading up to this curse. \n\nWatch the visions to learn our fate. They will show the way to disperse the cloud of poison and reach Zal'ik.
It's been a long time. I may not remember as well as I should. But I will try to answer.

I don't remember much of the invasion itself. It failed because of Zal'ik's gambit. Our army proved too strong for the Yokudans.\n\nAs to what happened to them, I don't know. I suppose they gave up in search of an easier target.

I always thought Shada's Tear was an ugly name for a city. It was adopted when the people first started worshiping the Nereids.\n\nI'm partial to the city's name of old: the City of Shimmering-Water-in-the-Desert. A mouthful, yes, but so poetic.

Yes. We believed that the stars themselves were little windows that let the light of Aetherius into our world.\n\nBut even in my day, it was a dying faith. Our people seemed destined to be conquered by invaders while the stars watched.

Of an old and fading religion—the cult of the stars. Once, Nedes across these lands worshiped the stars.\n\nBy the time the Yokudans came, we were a fragmented people. Some turned to the Elven gods, others to Daedra. My people turned to the Nereids.

No, they did not. Once, the Nedes of the city worshiped the stars.\n\nBut water was our city's lifeblood, and that is the Nereids' domain. Why plead with distant stars, when you have powerful sorceresses in your very midst?
Our city was once the great jewel of the desert. A city of cool, crisp, refreshing waters in a sea of sand.\n\nIt would have been of great strategic value to the Yokudans, had they taken it.

As I thought. The Nereids are behind the corruption. I've deciphered more writings on the leader of these Nereids—Shada, she's called.\n\nIt says she "blessed" the water so that the people of the city could fend off invaders.

It says the people of the city worshiped her in a temple that was once dedicated to the stars.\n\nThere's a third wing across the way. I assume that's the temple wing, and I'd guess that Shada's in there.

Feels foolish, asking you to risk your life when all I have to offer is a thank you. But you have to understand how much this means to us. And to Craglorn.\n\nI wish you luck. We'll remain here and wait for your return.

I know it's a lot to ask, but this water can't be allowed to leave here while it remains cursed. It would cause a situation as bad as the Celestial invasion above.\n\nDefeating Shada is the only way to end the curse. You must go and stop her.

I'm not one to speculate on the powers of the Celestials, but it seems he manipulated the Mage somehow.\n\nThat's not in our power to correct at the moment, but we can try to find this new atronach—an air atronach, the monarchs called it.
I would, but I cannot. There is too much to do to prepare for the ritual that will open the staff. This magic is … untested.

Certainly. The Guild is a scholarly organization dedicated to the pursuit of arcane knowledge. We travel the width and breadth of Tamriel seeking out books, tomes, and ancient scrolls.\n\nAlas, we've had to suspend our search here in Craglorn.
Earthquake. Worst one I've ever seen. Damn near shook the teeth right out of my head.

It was terrible! A giant spectral Serpent appeared at the summoning site. We sent the atronachs against it, but they refused to obey us.\n\nThey killed the others. Coward that I am, I fled. But then I was captured by these common rogues.

Another of Tarish-Zi's vainglorious projects. He desperately sought the place and the treasure it was rumored to contain.\n\nIt surprises me that one as young as Hara would know of it. Even in my time, it was barely more than myth.

I'm not sure. Tarish-Zi had the place sealed and buried. The original entrance is unreachable. \n\nKelmen may be of some assistance to us there—if his courage holds. Let's regroup at the lake and see what we can discern.

We did. It didn't contain what Tarish-Zi hoped for. So he ordered it buried out of spite. It should be directly below us, if memory serves.\n\nI noted some Nedic remnants jutting from a nearby lake. I'm certain they're part of Reinhold's Retreat.
Tastes like sandals boiled in mint perfume.\n\nBut if it knits my ribs, I'll drink the whole bottle.
Good. I'll find <<1>>.\n\nGo. Get them back safe.
<<1>> pulled me ashore. Went to find shelter. Never came back.\n\nHeaded to a nearby cave. Find him. Tell him we're all safe.
Glow juice? By the gods, it just might! Soon as I can stand on my own, I'll head inland.

No, I'm no use to you. Just a drunk and a coward. \n\nI will meet you back at Star-Gazer's headquarters once you've bound the monarchs. I have an uneasy feeling … like there's more going on here than I'm fully aware of.

When the atronachs were summoned, we used this to control them—the Gem of Aetherial Command, a gift from the Celestial Mage herself, according to legend.\n\nTake it. Weaken the stone and fire monarchs and use the gem to bind them.
Blessings upon you, stranger. I'll limp my way inland and find a safer place to wait for <<1>>. Just knowing she's out there gives me hope for the rest.

<<1>> dragged me out of the water. He'll want to know <<2>> and the rest of the squad are all right. Think he said something about looking for shelter in a nearby cave, but I was still coughing up sand.
Used to think this stuff was only good for practical jokes on snowy days.\n\nOnce I can heft Spleen-shanker, I'll push through the beach and find <<1>>. How about you?
Hope they appreciate their good fortune when you find them.\n\nI can get inland, after I rest. Fight with purpose.
You should let <<1>> know. He spit in fate's eye when he pulled me from the water. Said he saw a cave nearby and was going to look for shelter.
Good luck with that. As for me, I think I'll keep my distance. I've had more than enough excitement in recent weeks, thank you very much.

No, binding won't work. The air monarch was created from the power of three monarchs. It's too powerful. It must be destroyed.\n\nThe monarchs said that it could be found at a place called Balamath. I recognize the name. It's an Ayleid ruin.

There's only one explanation I can think of, and it's not exactly reassuring.\n\nIf someone found the entrance before us and activated it, the residual energy would continue to emanate for a while after. If we go inside, we won't be alone.

Right. And we mustn't let her down, no matter how terrifying the task.\n\nIt looks like the energy has its source at these sconces. I see nothing that can be done to activate this one, but it might be worth looking at the others. Fancy a swim?
Be warned, though. The spellfiends are drawn to the elemental shards. \n\nYou will be unable to harvest an elemental infusion from a shard until the spellfiends are defeated.

No, of course not. I've got everything well in hand. I just … oh, who am I kidding? Mistress Nazdura sent me to look for some star maps. Why anyone would keep something like that in an inn, I'll never know.
Thank you. Ugh. Back to it, I guess.\n\nMara, help me.

You've no idea. These books and papers … it's like a giant ate a library, got sick, and then threw it all back up. No rhyme or reason—just piles. \n\nSorry for the metaphor. I'm not usually so … graphic.

The Fighters Guild! You should join up. Our new guildmaster is an Argonian, Sees-All-Colors. She has the whole guild hunting down Daedra and their damned Anchors. Tough work. \n\nNot much action out here in Craglorn though. The mages saw to that.

Quickly. If the staff explodes, it has enough power to turn all of Craglorn into a crater.\n\nCollect all three elemental infusions and bring them to me. Then we can force our way into the staff and stop the explosion!

We are dealing with magic of a whole different order than any of us are used to.\n\nIf this really is the Mage's Staff, then only infusions of energy from its own shards can break its wards. I only hope that we can find a way to contain it once inside.

I know. We aren't very much alike. But as much as it pains me to admit it, under that vapid exterior is a very capable mage.\n\nI was in Craglorn when this thing hit, so the Mages Guild sent me to investigate.
Now is not the time for friendly chatter. You must harvest the elemental infusions from the shards so we can force our way into the staff.
To throw fruit, yes? Stand back at least twenty paces. My guards like to wager.
We cannot use the Seeker's Sight to find the other aspects. Not until the gems are recharged with magicka.\n\nUntil that is accomplished, the relic is useless.

Without the Mage to control the ebb and flow, magicka seeps through cracks all across Craglorn. Look for places where the magicka is so dense you can see it and charge the gems there.\n\nMeet us at the Star-Gazer's Observatory when you have finished.
Oh, you don't know? I would have thought that bedraggled Khajiit would have given us away. I am a humble servant of our majestic lord, Hermaeus Mora.

Yes, Hermaeus Mora—the Prince of Fate, the Lord of Secrets. We are his watchful children. \n\nWhen we heard that this ancient city had been discovered, we raced here to plumb its depths. Fortunately, this pack of would-be scholars arrived first.
Wouldn't think of it. I haven't seen their logs and maps, but surely they haven't discovered anything of value. Such a pack of dunces. There's no way they know more than us. No way at all.

Isn't it obvious? \n\nThese fools drank the poisoned water and demonstrated its effects. A fascinating discovery—and all the better since it happened to someone other than us. We owe them a debt of gratitude.
I will do what I can. We can't allow the Serpent to control both the Mage and the Warrior. We need the guardians—all three of them—if we have any hope of defeating the Serpent.
Then place it within the star map and let's see what it can show us.
This Seeker's Sight they gave you. Is it fully restored?

The Lost One is very powerful. We will need both strength and intelligence to succeed.\n\nRight now, the important thing is to find our other aspects and prevent the Lost One from growing any stronger.

Your judgment has served us well so far. We trust you with our lives.\n\nI believe the Scaled One hasn't located either of these aspects as of yet. But do not delay. Find them and tell them of us before the situation changes.

According to the Seeker's Sight, one hides behind what your people refer to as a Dwarven contraption. The other has taken refuge in more deadly environs—among ravenous werewolves. I fear for her safety.

What of it? Aren't you sick of hiding behind these walls, caught like skeevers in a trap?\n\nIron Orcs only respond to strength. We should go out there and hunt them down instead of wasting our time in this gutless town.
So you're the one who helped Kelmen Locke?\n\nHe's … an interesting fellow. Took to drink almost as soon as he arrived. But in his moments of clarity, he can be quite helpful.
So it's true. The Mage has been split into pieces. That could prove difficult down the line.\n\nBut thank you again for your efforts.

We are one and many, both. We share many things, but we cannot talk to each other except when in each other's presence.\n\nI know I have spoken to you, but I do not know the details of those conversations.
Belkarth … there is a powerful presence there, protecting it. It makes sense to hide near there. Away from the Scaled One's grip. At least for now.\n\nI will find my way to them.
I am aware. The Lost One, whom he has corrupted, grows stronger. I hear her calling to me.\n\nThis is why the Serpent divided us. What he could not control whole, he now corrupts piece by piece.
Unfortunate. We will have to find her, then.\n\nI will make my way back to my other selves. Now that I know my location, it will be easy enough to find me.

Belkarth? Hmm. So I have chosen to hide near Belkarth. In a place made for another.\n\nDo you have any news of the Lost One? I know that she is moving against us, but I do not perceive her actions directly.
Yes. Something about Reinhold … Reinhold's Retreat? A ruin. \n\nBut I've never heard that name. What do you think she meant?
Thank you. I know she trusted you. \n\nI hate the thought of her suffering all alone in some dark place. Please, hurry.
She said "he found me." Maybe she's alive and someone took her? Took her to this place … Reinhold's Retreat. \n\nPlease, you have to find it. You have to save her. I … we need her.

We were caught off guard and weakened when the Serpent divided us. He has been gathering our aspects, bringing them under his control one by one.\n\nThis Lost One is more powerful even than the four of us combined.

It will not be easy. The Lost One is powerful. You will need to engage her in battle and distract her. \n\nUnfortunately, she has anticipated this course and fled to a place of strength—our Apex Stone.

We must join with her. We may not be strong enough to defeat the Lost One in a fight, but together we can resist the Serpent's corruption. \n\nThe Lost One will no longer be whole, but divided within herself. This will make her vulnerable.

This is a critical waypoint on the road to Cyrodiil. Our supply train is vulnerable on the High Road through Bangkorai, so we serve as a bulwark against Ebonheart skirmishers. \n\nThe Reach is full of Nord militants. Luckily, they rarely come in force.
Not for me to say. I simply follow orders. I'm sure the captain has his reasons, though. He's … well … he's competent.
Very astute. I asked Captain Gaarlug for reinforcements, but apparently he has a lot of faith in this … small band.
My orders are to protect the supply train. Nothing more. \n\nNow, if star monsters attack our convoys, well … I guess we'll see what happens.

I'm sorry. The Serpent is a deceiver by nature. I couldn't be sure. \n\nWhen the other Guardians fell, I had to react quickly. I suspected that the Serpent was using our Apex stones against us, so I secreted mine to this ruin for safekeeping.

The Serpent is cunning, but he has his blindspots. He does not value the strength or cleverness of mortals.\n\nTaking the form of Hara, a mortal, allowed me to find champions—like you—to join the fight against the Serpent, while eluding his gaze.

We should return to Belkarth. There is still much to do, if we're to free the other Guardians and stop the Serpent. But I'm done hiding. The Star-Gazers deserve to know the truth. \n\nI can transport you back to the city if you wish.

An enemy worthy of the Undaunted! We heard the crash of armored marching echo out of the walls, and the blast of an immense warhorn, but silence has fallen since my friends entered.\n\nIt would take a savage Dragon to quiet that many Undaunted.

We're the most daring group of adventurers to ever leap into boots! Bane of beast and Daedra alike! The fiercest brigands this side of Sovngarde!\n\nSome of us also enjoy disappearing into ancient Citadels, leaving the Nord in charge behind.

All I've seen is the inside of our traveling packs. The others left without me when I was checking our equipment. It wasn't funny at that centaur graveyard in Elden Root, and it's not funny now.\n\nI hope a Yokudan ghost ate them.
We are the one you call the Celestial Mage—or at least two aspects of a larger whole.\n\nThe Serpent shattered us, weakened us. He plans to control us, piece by piece, aspect by aspect.

The Apex Stones are what allow the Celestials to manifest in this plane. By corrupting our Apex Stone, the Serpent sought to submit our consciousness to his will and corrupt us.\n\nThis is what happened to the Lost One.

If you did, our full power would be released. Mundus could not withstand such force.\n\nOur Apex Stone rests in a hidden place beneath the city of Elinhir. Use the Seeker's Sight to locate it and the Lost One. We will join you when the time is right.

We're the bravest fools in Tamriel. Not a hole in the ground we won't leap into, no Daedra or lurking shadow we won't drag to the light—and chop in the neck!\n\nThe beasts of Craglorn don't fear much, but they should fear the Undaunted!
Local legend says that the Aetherian Archive was built by the Firstmages long before the three towers of Elinhir existed, that those towers were created in homage to the Archive.
Can't be sure. I just arrived a few days ago. But if there was anyone on the road when it happened, I wouldn't hold out much hope.
Oh, just a few days I reckon.
Of course I'm kidding. Look at this place. If I get these diggers working double shifts we might be able to clear the gap in a century or two. I wouldn't hold out much hope though.
Thanks. We need it.

Keeping up appearances I guess. King Fahara'jad, blessings be upon him, sent me out here as a disaster relief liason. As long as I'm here pointing at people, the King can say that he's doing his part. \n\nPolitics.
Hurry. If Kelmen is lost to the Serpent, so too are our chances to understand why the atronachs turned.
My fellow guardian, the Mage, lent her power to the conjurers of Craglorn. \n\nIt was not in our interest to see Coldharbour and Nirn joined.

She spoke to them in dreams. Not directly, of course. We prefer to watch from above rather than appear below. Only in times of great crisis do the guardians awaken and manifest.\n\nThe Serpent's attack on Craglorn was just such a crisis.

From what I've heard, he's a gifted conjurer who was greatly favored by the Mage herself before she disappeared.\n\nWhen the atronachs turned, the rest of Kelmen's summoning circle were killed. It's no wonder he's gone into hiding.

The first atronachs we summoned were ancient. They could communicate, to some extent. They didn't speak, but we heard them in our minds. \n\nThey commanded the others and we controlled them. With a gem we saw in a dream—the Gem of Celestial Command.

Well, as it happens, that's the one thing the bandits didn't get their hands on. I was able to keep it … hidden. Don't ask.\n\nTake it. Find the storm, fire, and frost monarchs and use the gem to bind them. You'll probably have to fight them first.
Go to the summoning site and use the gem to call on the monarchs. I'll meet you there. They might be more favorable to me. Or maybe not.\n\nBut now, I've helped you. Will you release me?
The Serpent uses these crystals to siphon the Mage's power for his own use and to gather a stronger hold over her aspects.

When the Serpent shattered the Mage, incredible magicka was released. I am the echo of that shattering. I appear to you now because of the power concentrated in this place, but I will soon cease to be.
For the moment, but I have no doubt the Serpent will continue to try to gain control of the Mage's magicka—just as he continues to try to gain control of her aspects.

You should probably hop a cart back to Wayrest. I can jabber on about Celestials all day long, but I'm a bit out of the loop on the Daedric threat. \n\nMore's the pity. I love how Banekin squeak when you step on them. Ah well.

The Fighters Guild! You should join up. Our new guildmaster is an Argonian, Sees-All-Colors. She has the whole guild hunting down Daedra and their damned Anchors. Tough work. \n\nNot much action out here in Craglorn though. The mages saw to that.

You should probably hop a cart back to Mournhold. I can jabber on about Celestials all day long, but I'm a bit out of the loop on the Daedric threat. \n\nMore's the pity. I love how Banekin squeak when you step on them. Ah well.

I'd suggest heading back to Wayrest. The Guild registers there can gauge your aptitude. From the looks of you, I'd say you're a shoo-in. \n\nWalk with Magnus, my friend.

We've had to put all our considerable resources into researching the Celestial threat. The Star-Gazers are capable scholars, certainly. But they lack the requisite literature. This work has kept us very busy.

Yes, I am. A situation I aim to remedy in short order. \n\nIt would help if you would actually purchase something instead of yammering on about the obvious.

The rules pertaining to capture and imprisonment are mercifully short. \n\nNow buy something and be on your way. I don't want to linger in this place any longer than is absolutely necessary. I try to avoid standing near lightning and floating rocks.

In the event of a crisis behind enemy lines, a legionnaire may sell excess material to noncombatants. Such materiel must have no significant military application. Gold acquired in this manner must be used to secure swift passage back to the legion.

Oh! I thought you were … it doesn't matter.\n\nYou know of my cousin's outrageous punishment, then? No trial, no evidence, just time in the stocks! Arrested for "unlawful thoughts of the undead," whatever that means.
Sabashur-dar thought so at first. Was going to leave but, you know … circumstances.
Yes. This one's horse ran away and the khaj-winds made it impossible to follow. Stupid hoof-walker! I would claw his eyes out if I could find him.
Sabashur-dar is greedy—very greedy. Fearsome monsters attract five-clawed adventurers. And five-clawed adventurers carry fat gold purses! Great place for a sale, yes?
Ah, but you don't know this one's other problem.

The magistrate's corruption must be answered. He keeps a key to the stocks and a <<z:1>> in his mansion. I want you to acquire both.\n\nIf the writ won't convince <<2>> to release my cousin, the key will do the rest.

Oh, they're here. Seems half the city's Imperial soldiers were corrupted by Molag Bal—Legion Zero. Watch out for them, they're brutal.\n\nCivilians are mostly dead; a few survivors are in hiding. One of the Elder Councilors is down the hall there.

They're an ancient order of mages, sworn to protect Elinhir. But they turned.\n\nThey hunted and killed every other mage in the city, harvesting the magicka from them. Everyone else was just in the way.

We told him the location of the Celestial Mage's Apex Stone. With that information, his master, the Celestial Serpent, was able to corrupt the Mage and turn her against Craglorn.\n\nI can never atone for what we did. I can only hope to stop Yamanu-ko.
I believe so. The Serpent compromised his physical being, which you destroyed. I will call to him.
Dark moons and Dark Anchors. The horrors of Coldharbour stalk the streets above and even the sewers below. \n\nIf you venture out from the base, make sure to keep your claws sharp.
Because the God of Schemes sent them, of course. \n\nIt seems Molag Bal will not be content until every soul has been harvested, and the city itself has been dragged into his domain.

What's left of them, yes. The Imperial Army was betrayed from within though. Most of the Imperial soldiers are dead. Most of the citizens are dead too.\n\nOur forces have been helping them when we can.

There is a door to the Arboretum District over there, but it only goes out. It is locked on the other side. \n\nIf you haven't spoken with General Nedras or Sergeant Shaghila, this one suggests you do before you leave.

Tarish-Zi was a member of a long ruling line of the Na-Totambu, and he helped conquer much of Hammerfell as part of the Ra Gada. \n\nBut while many of the invaders settled in the south, Tarish-Zi dreamed of still greater conquests.

Molag Bal happened, to all of us. Oh, he never set foot in the city, but he's responsible for it all. Annia and I lost everything—our shop, our home, our children, everything that made life worth living.
What can we do? We cower here, hoping the Dominion can defeat this evil and at least give us our city back.\n\nI'm beginning to suspect there's little chance of even that.
Get up there and fight. Every Daedra or Worm Cultist you kill brings us one step closer to seeing the sun again.
None that I can see. The Imperial Army's been decimated. Most of our friends and family have been killed. Our home has been burned down. \n\nI'd say the omens don't bode too well for our future.
Lunatics. They claim they were with the original group of mages that entered this tower and sealed themselves in; the Firstmages of Craglorn.\n\nThat would make them impossibly old, even for Elves.
Hah! You think that's going to make a difference. You think Queen Ayrenn can just march in here, twirl her golden locks and save us?\n\nThat's the stupidest idea I've ever heard.

Much like down here. Perhaps it's sunnier, unless Molag Bal has destroyed that too. \n\nHe probably will. We'll all die, sooner or later. I pray that it's sooner. Famius tries to keep my spirits up, but he's wasting his breath.
I believe so. The Serpent compromised her physical being, which you destroyed. I will call to her.

On the condition that you'll go away and let me work—the Aetherian Archive is the greatest magical repository ever built, and we intended it to be so when we created it.\n\nThe Mages Guild wishes they had a tower half as magnificent.

There are few as knowledgeable as she. The Learned One rules the upper floors, where the fanatics worship her. Die for her, in the wake of her spells.\n\nI learn everything I can from her, but I avoid the upper floors. What is knowledge to the dead?

They've been making a nuisance of themselves in Belkarth for the last few days. Claim they need to speak to Hara of the Star-Gazers immediately.\n\nOf course, Hara hasn't been available, so they came here to wait.
Well, for one thing, all of the pictures of the constellations portray the Mage as a bearded old man.\n\nFor another, shouldn't the Celestials look more … I don't know … intimidating?

No, and that's why we're here. Hara wanted us to make sure they had legitimate business with the Star-Gazers before she sees them.\n\nBut all I found out is that they're legitimately crazy! Still, I kind of want to believe them, you know?
How would I know? They're probably beggars who wandered in from Elinhir when the Archive door opened.\n\nExploring the upper floors is what interests me, not these fools.

Before the Learned One arrived, we held our magical experiments there, where we wrestled with the arcane in the name of progress.\n\nWhen she entered the Archive, her spark was so fierce that—well, the upper floors speak for themselves. Keep away.

Take this relic, the Seeker's Sight. It is a compass of sorts, one that is connected to all aspects of the Mage.\n\nBut like the Mage, the relic is broken. When you repair it, it will recognize our other aspects and lead you to them.

Thank you. With the Seeker's Sight restored, we can locate our other aspects before the Serpent takes control of them.\n\nWhen you finish mending the Seeker's Sight, meet us at the winery outside of Belkarth. We will wait for you there.
When we fell from the sky, the three gems that power the Seeker's Sight were lost. You will need to retrieve these gems to make use of the relic.
Hold still but a moment and we will show you. Witness the treachery of the Serpent.
Oh yeah—it's all sweetrolls and honey here. Can't you tell?\n\nOf course it's not all right!

The center of magic in Craglorn, of course. We Firstmages are unparalleled when it comes to the arcane arts. The Mages Guild be damned.\n\nI've not compared notes with a Guild member in centuries, of course, but they can't have come far.

I don't know from where she came, or how she came to be, but her vessel is the purest arcane specimen I have ever met. Her words and thoughts invoke magic in ways that spells cannot replicate.\n\nI am pleased she chose us to help her with her work.
The source of our magic was once stored there. When the Learned One arrived, it shattered in the wake of her magnificence.\n\nBut she shares her power with us, now. In return, we study for her.
Right. Let's say—and this is all hypothetical, mind you—let's say you had to get a siege engine from down here up to the gate. How would you do it?
Exactly! You'd take it up in pieces and assemble it on the other side of the gate. What kind of soft-headed idiot assembles the ram down here? It makes no sense at all!
Hrmph. Whatever. Go on then. Mauloch knows I've got a lot of work to do.

No sense! No sense at all. \n\nI tell you, If I find the little skeever smear who put this thing together, I'm going to tie him to the cap and ship his arse straight to the Imperial City. We'll put that thick skull to the test.

It is where the Learned One works. Her motives are unknowable, her methods more so. She has made the upper floors very dangerous to traverse.\n\nThere are … fanatics among the Firstmages who stayed there, regardless, to worship her.
Isn't it magnificent? We Firstmages occupied it years and years ago. It was here that we found the Great Source during the First Era.

We three in this chamber are the only Firstmages who value our lives over our magic. \n\nAnirwen and Earil are too ashamed to admit it, but I have seen them weep in the night to the sound of the Learned One's work on the upper floors.

She is magic incarnate. The Great Source paled in the face of her power, and in her presence, it shattered.\n\nIt was the greatest day of our lives. The Learned One has worked magic within these walls like no spell that has ever been achieved before.

The source of our magic also granted us long life. The Learned One destroyed it when she arrived, and we know not why, but I don't despair as I would have in the past.\n\nFor the Learned One is magic incarnate, greater, even, than the Grand Source.

You are a cynic, like our Orc visitor. She called us drunks, absurdists, maniacs. Believe what you will. Our tower speaks for itself.\n\nWhy else would the Learned One come here, of all places in Craglorn, seeking our aid, but for our glorious Source?

Upstairs, worshiping the Learned One more fervently than the Imperials do the Divines. I cannot blame them, though I cannot bring myself to follow.\n\nThe Learned One ravages the upper floors daily. Not all of her worshipers make it out alive.

What happens to any man, given enough power? \n\nHe began styling himself an "emperor" rather than only a king. He turned his armies against his allies. He even trekked outside of Hammerfell for a time, which is where he met me.

With much of his family and those loyal to them, Tarish-Zi continued carving a path north through Hammerfell, eventually settling where we now stand. For a time he ruled justly in the way of tradition, building a new kingdom. That peace did not last.

I was adventuring in the highlands when I came across a cadre of Tarish-Zi's soldiers. I slew those that moved against me. The rest escaped quickly after. That night by the fire, a messenger approached and made me an offer I couldn't refuse.

I worked to defend my home. That's all. The messenger was part of a movement that was stirring among the people. \n\nAs an outsider, I was above suspicion. Someone Tarish-Zi would not expect to covet his throne. Someone who could get close.

Tarish-Zi took an interest in me after his soldiers returned with the tale. He sent the messenger to ask me to join his guard. \n\nBut the messenger confided the mad king's plans to invade my homeland. A course his own people opposed, but in secret.

How can I describe her to you? She is as fierce and brilliant as a freshly sharpened blade. \n\nHer name would be meaningless to you, but I know she waits for me back where I belong. When this fight is over, I must find a way back. Somehow.

The rebellion was crushed, but it put fear into Tarish-Zi. He gave up his dreams of invasion. And I remained blameless in his eyes.\n\nI planned to leave his service—but then I met someone, a woman. She gave me a reason to continue the fight.
Heh, if only I could. I thought I'd gone mad. I did go mad. \n\nHara tells me that it was the Celestial Warrior who pulled me through time. I believe it, even if I don't understand how it's so.
When <<1>> learns of <<2>>'s escape, he will come for me directly.\n\nUnless we can distract him. But for this, I will need your aid.

<<1>> sent an emissary to inspect <<2>>, and <<3>> wasn't informed. She's preparing her surprise inspection from her ship, the Greenhalgh.\n\nIf we can convince <<3>> you're the emissary, he'll dance to our tune!

<<1>> rules <<2>>. He has allies, flunkies, and a very pretty house on a hill. This bounty flows from Headman <<3>>.\n\nBut if we trick <<1>> into biting his master's hand, all his nice things go away.
<<1>> is the true power on this island. Wealthy, connected … little happens here without his approval.
<<1>> will have her <<z:2>> on the Greenhalgh. Find it and take it. She won't dare show her face in <<3>> without it.\n\nBut I like to be thorough. I want you to poison her.

My guess is that the Serpent was somehow able to use the Warrior's power through him. \n\nHe likely learned of the cursed army of Anka-Ra resting below the sands and knew he could use them by calling to Tarish-Zi across time. We put an end to that.

The Star-Gazers have legends about those born under the sign of the Warrior and the connection they have with their patron—that he can call on them to fight for him. \n\nApparently time is a meager barrier for a Celestial.

Aye. Many were sent forth before we killed Tarish-Zi, and it seems clear that they will roam until put down. \n\nWithout their leader, we can take comfort knowing they won't be rallied into a proper army. I hope their souls find rest in the end.

You must be new to the area. Before the trade roads were cut off, the town of Dragonstar held a grand melee every year.\n\nFighters came from all over to participate. But I've never heard of a victory like this.
That's my guess. I heard that they arrested him as soon as the fight ended. Handed him over to the Daggerfall Covenant garrison at the Bangkorai gate.
Iron Orcs. We thought they had left the gate unoccupied. We were very, very wrong.

It is a classic case of buying a cat to catch a mouse. The mages of Elinhir summoned the atronachs to ward off the invasion from Coldharbour. \n\nBut when the work was done, the atronachs remained—and turned on them.
Yes. Think of the biggest, meanest, angriest Orc you've ever met. Got it? Now add about thirty stone of pure muscle and forty stone of bad disposition. You might get close to describing an Iron Orc.
In a heartbeat. Three of my lads fell before I even knew we were under attack. They beat Lucius to death with their bare hands. It was … it was awful.
I don't. But I'm not leaving my boys here for the crows.\n\nIf I were you, I'd walk on. Hopefully we'll get some reinforcements soon. In the meantime, we wait.
We hold here. If we're lucky, they'll quiet down long enough for us to gather our dead. If we're very lucky, they'll pack their things and head back to their warcamp.
Pinumur does not tuck his tail for dung-headed savages. They were lucky the first time. If they attack again, Pinumur will make them pay.

I do not know. But I've heard of strange sightings near one of the broken Dark Anchor dolmens.\n\nYou might look there, if you're curious. Of course, that calls to mind another common expression involving cats.
Let me stop you right there. I did not summon the atronachs. Not alone, anyway.\n\nI had the help of three other mages: Adalind, Dorian, and Kasimir.
I only drink when I remember. And once I forget, I stop.

I'm just getting a handle on that myself. At the time, I found it strange that they seemed to have an answer for every spell I threw at them.\n\nBut Hara tells me that the Celestial Serpent had a hand in my capture.
Well, out of all of us, Kasimir was the prodigy. He was only nineteen years old, if you can believe it!\n\nBut summoning the atronachs was Dorian's idea. Or rather, his dream.

Everyone did their part. Adalind chose the ritual location. Kasimir prepared the summoning circle. And I readied the Gem of Celestial Command, just as Dorian had been shown.\n\nIt was our finest moment, and the last time we were all alive together.

He said a woman appeared to him in a dream. She wore a dress made of stars, he said, and had hair burnished with golden light.\n\nHe was convinced that she was the Mage herself. Showing him how to free Craglorn of the Dark Anchors.
Self-knowledge. I did not know I was a coward until the atronachs turned on our circle of conjurers.\n\nThat was when I learned that I am the sort of man who runs while his friends die.
That's a fair accusation, but I'm quite sure I wasn't. Even I know better than to travel the roads of Craglorn in anything less than a state of complete sobriety.

I'm new to all of this, but I do what I can.\n\nPeople have been looking to Hara for answers since the Celestials appeared. So I try to help her with meetings, letter-writing—little things—so she can focus on what's important.
I came to Hammerfell with a few other Orcs. One of the chiefs was going to pick a new wife. I wasn't chosen, but I was allowed to attend the feast that night. \n\nThat's when the Iron Orcs attacked.
I don't know. It doesn't seem possible, does it? All I know is, she found me and brought me here.\n\nSo, you see, I owe Hara everything. I'll do anything for her. The Star-Gazers are my family now.

I don't want to think about it. It wasn't even a battle. It was slaughter. I don't know when I blacked out, but when I woke, the Iron Orcs had joined their victims in death.\n\nStanding above me was a solitary figure, hand outstretched. Hara.
An accomplishment like that deserves something from our special stock. We don't come across items like this too often, but you've earned it.\n\nGo on, take it.
I heard rumors that one of the Celestials themselves has taken mortal form and wanders these halls.\n\nI would like the chance to fight her.

I was invited by one of the Stargazers, Hara, who told us about the Aetherian Archive. \n\nShe doesn't seem as interested in going there to meet strange creatures and possibly kill them—but the Undaunted certainly are.

After the fiends are dead, you will only have a brief window in which to harvest the elemental infusion.\n\nOh, and each person can only carry one infusion. So you'll need to decide among your allies who will carry flame, ice, and storm.

Even a lich will die when one destroys his physical body. Let's head to his study. He'll likely be there.\n\nI don't see a way to stop Nerien'eth without direct conflict. I've already tried appealing to his morality. What's left of it.

I charged across Tamriel to get to Craglorn when I heard that the fabled Hel Ra Citadel had finally opened its doors. Any Redguard worth their sword would, to get a chance to see a piece of old Yokuda.\n\nI still hope to get the chance.

The First Era was frought with warfare between our continent and the land of Yokuda, where my ancient ancestors came from. They built fortresses like Hel Ra Citadel during that time.\n\nHel Ra is one of the few yet remaining.

Khajiit was roped into this by Damisi. Her nose for business is fierce and five-clawed. This one thought she would not lead us astray.\n\nUnfortunately, all but the bravest fear to approach the Citadel now. Our wagon is in tatters, and so is our pride.

Honestly, this one doesn't know. Money interests him much more.\n\nThe Redguard seem to truly enjoy coming here, though. Damisi thought we could make a fortune from them when the road ahead opened. Not today.

What I always do. Try to make money.\n\nWith the road to the Citadel open for the first time since the Yokudans built it, I was sure I could milk some profit off sightseers. Ancient Redguard architecture tends to be popular. But not much luck so far.

Scholars argue about it to this day. People couldn't just walk in up until recently, you know. I've heard, based on what we've seen of the fortifications, it was Nedic before the Yokudans captured and modified it.\n\nI just want to make some coin.
This one?\n\nNo. Why would you even suggest that? This one has no intention of charging to his death. Ever.
What kind of question is that?\n\nDo I look like I would enjoy running headfirst into a Welwa until I died? I'm a little mortified you would compare me to those fools.

By my blade, never!\n\nThey're a bunch of uncouths who enjoy daring each other to fight wamasu bare-handed and drink skooma out of their helmets. For fun. Right now, they're here to brave whatever's taken residence in the Citadel. Good riddance.

Nerien'eth's journal only refers to the broad process, but he cast a ritual to bring the Daedra here.\n\nIf we find the ritual site, we can stem their flow into this plane. No doubt he'll be there to confront us when we do.
Well, it takes an unusually foolish person to flee a bad situation and end up in a far worse one. I'm one of those special people.

I fled Cheydinhal, a village east of here, to avoid being forced to join a gang of Imperial deserters. I ran here and put myself right into the middle of a warzone, with horrors from Coldharbour running amok and killing everyone.
Why, it's just great up there, all sunshine and puppies. Why don't you go take a look?

We had to swim across Lake Rumare to get here, me and two friends. The slaughterfish got my friends. The guards won't let civilians use the tunnel and I can't face swimming back again. I'm starting to think my friends were the lucky ones.

Oh, you're so clever; saw right through that ruse, didn't you? Well, if sunshine made your skin peel off your body, and if puppies were ten times your size and had teeth the length of your arm, then yes, it's all true.

<<1>> has many odd pursuits, but necromancy is not one of them. No, my cousin suffers so that I may be punished.\n\nThe magistrate asked, "Why refuse to kiss my slippers?" I told him, "Because you trod through the muck." I used harsher words.

I want you to help get my cousin out of the stocks. The only dirty hands you'll find are the magistrate's.\n\nBut I know how this business works. I'll pay you for your trouble. Does that help ease your sense of propriety?
It depends where you need to go. This is a working ship. We don't traverse all of Tamriel's seas.

The journal did not refer to the weapon by name. No mention of how Nerien'eth obtained it, or what kind of macabre sorcery is sealed inside it. Only a short note that it may drive its user to madness—in exchange for power.\n\nWe have to find him.

We've been sent here to secure a foothold for the Pact's invasion of the Imperial City. I leapt at the opportunity to serve on the front lines. Had I known that the front would be a fetid rat-hole … well, no sense dwelling on it.

Slow going, but I believe we're making modest gains. We're slaughtering the cultists wholesale. It's the Daedra that are the real problem. They can't die, you see. It's infuriating. All we can do is try to staunch the bleeding.

General Nesh-Tan can best speak to that. She's the Argonian over there. A capable leader to be sure, but colder than a wraith's pajamas. \n\nShe's warmed a bit since we took the sewer, though. To be honest, I think she's enjoying herself down here.
She should be back on Stros M'Kai, securing a new crew. I can take you there, if you wish.
There was a vigorous dispute between the captain and her old crew.\n\nTumma-Shah knows the whole story. She's below decks, if you'd like to know the details.
Where do you need to go?
I have business in <<1>>. I can take you to Eagle's Strand at no charge.\n\nBut do not mention me to the locals, yes? I value my … obscurity.
I can take you to Vulkhel Guard, in Auridon. I have many things to sell to the High Elves!\n\nAll of them legal.
Good, I have business on <<1>>. Passage is free! The inspectors won't be looking for two of us.\n\nEr, whenever you're ready.

Hmm. From here, we travel to Stros M'kai. A bit tricky, but we should be able to make it before the weather changes.\n\nOr you could head into the city. Perhaps stretch your legs a bit, try the local brew. It's up to you.
Have you been to Betnikh? I can get you there in one piece. Most likely. Probably. No guarantees, though.
Daggerfall. You shall find there everything you need, and then some.\n\nThere have been a few storms along the way, but nothing we can't handle. Let us pray our charts are current.

Don't worry,  nothing permanent. Abadarun keeps a few useful draughts on him. They let him deal with rowdy customers without causing a scene. The drops he'll give you will ensure that the guards are feeling no pain, let's say it that way.

Headman Cosh has surrounded himself with lackwits and sycophants, and they're used to getting their way. They'll notice any missing baubles soon enough, and the whole island will hear about it. Trust me.
I lost a small potion bottle, my work clothes, some finely-ground mineral dust, and, well, a type of screw-driven tool I'd rather not elaborate on out in the open.
What? What are you talking about?
Give me that writ! I'll settle this with <<1>>.\n\nWait here, and don't touch anything!
I prefer weightier arguments than paper.\n\nSuch as gold. In a pouch. Placed in my hand.

You mean, how did I get to be so cheerful?\n\nLet's see, I'm not sure if it was when the Worm Cult sent my undead husband to kill me or if it was when the Daedroth paraded me around the Nobles District, half-naked and bleeding.
Good, good. You wait here. I'll speak with <<1>> and make sure this writ is in order.\n\nDon't touch anything.
You're in <<1>>. Learn its rules, or go back where you came from.
Are you, then? Tag along in my skiff if you'd like, though I suppose it depends where you want to go.
We sure can, even from near-drowned folks like you. I've been back to Bleakrock a couple of times since plucking you from the sea by the scruff of your neck. Things aren't getting better there.

My charm, of course!\n\nYou're not buying it, are you? No. I actually wound up beating my husband's corpse back to death with a chair leg, and the Daedroth eventually dropped me. I crawled into the sewers and wound up here.

It's nothing. Most folks I pull from the sea are already dead. But you've got decent gear. I bet you've seen battle. I told my boss Rana about you on my last trip, and she wants to meet you.\n\nPay me back by helping her. Come with me to Bleakrock.

The magistrate has no idea who you are. You can act against his plans, as my agent. And I'll pay well for the privilege.\n\nAlso, my cousin won't stop talking about you. It seems you saved him from the "melon pile." Whatever that is.
Then you know <<1>> is a dangerous man with wealth and connections. Most everything on this island happens with his approval.
Ha! She threatened to kill me. I try to remember the faces of people who do that.

Wonderful! You'll find <<Az:1>> in my strongbox. Once you have <<Az:2>>, find a way to acquaint <<3>> with the poison.\n\nYou know, she's quite fond of her wine. Perhaps this year was the wrong vintage.
Yes. Oh! No, I don't want you to kill her!\n\nI just want her better acquainted with her chamberpot, every hour, for the next few weeks. Nothing permanent but her shame.

<<1>> appointed <<2>> as his magistrate. But Sentinel is far away, and a distant king has less influence than a rich neighbor.\n\nThe king suspects another master holds <<2>>'s strings. His hidden emissary gives us an chance to cut them.

Years ago, she was a young soldier in Sentinel. Ambitious. Very annoying.\n\nI stole her lover and her horse. Then I spread rumors her horse and her lover were the same creature. But she deserved it, truly.

If she dies, <<1>> sends a fleet of hard-faced warriors to learn who killed his emissary. Those warriors quarter themselves at the only inn in town—my inn. Worse, they don't pay me for my trouble.\n\nSo she lives. I can't lose the business.
Fine! Use a quarter dosage. She'll feel sick, but without the amusing side effects.\n\nAs long as she stays on the boat, you can pose as the king's emissary.
Yes. As a matter of fact, I would. \n\nTalk to Councilor Itinia. She's completely demoralized and seems willing to share her misery with … well, anyone.
Ah, truly? We have been expecting you! May I see your seal, Emissary? That I may bask in the reflected light of Sentinel, and the warmth of our King?
Now that you are here, I want to show you this jewel on the waters. Are you settled from your voyage? Are you willing to accompany me on a tour of our fair city?
Excellent! Let us leave my beautiful home, and prepare to walk from the plaza before my front door.

Ahh, such a beauty. Such craftsmanship! Welcome to Abah's Landing. The waters of the aquaduct sing at your arrival. The zephyrs that sweep along our gentle beaches whisper your name. Our honest merchants will treat you with the utmost respect.

I must admit, you are not the kind of person I expected the King to send … but I would never question his judgment. Now that you are here, I want to show you this jewel on the waters. Are you willing to accompany me on a tour of our fair city?
Auridon—one of the Summerset Isles, my friend! Homeland of the High Elves.\n\nWe're docked at Vulkhel Guard, but we should have put in at Skywatch. I hear there's a festival!
Razum-dar is here on a mission of some … delicacy. This one did not know how your presence here would change it. But honestly, Raz is glad you returned. You may be just what he needs.
Because you are no soldier, which is useful. You can speak with the locals, assure them we are not invaders or marauders.\n\nNow, come. Let us try to fit in.
I can take you to Vulkhel Guard. Bah, all my business here has dried up! At least I won't have trouble with the inspectors in Auridon.\n\nWhich rarely happens.

You must find your own path. But perhaps there is a reason for the place in which you find yourself.\n\nExplore. Search for a cause to lend your hand. Join with others. You might even seek out those who rescued you from the sea. The choice is yours.

You were dragged ashore on an island beach, but I sense that you are now aboard a ship in port.\n\nGo ashore and seek out the captain of the vessel. Perhaps he or she can point you toward the charitable spirit who was responsible for your rescue.

I know only that you washed up on a cold beach on a remote island. You have since been transported to a large city.\n\nHead toward the city docks. There, you will find someone who knows the island from whence you came and how you might return there.

I know only that you were fished from the sea and dragged aboard a ship. You have since been transported to a large city. \n\nI suggest you visit the city docks. There, you will find someone who can direct you to those responsible for your rescue.

We do not face these troubled times alone. Many shall rise up to fight this tide of darkness.\n\nWherever you go, you will encounter others who share your courage and valor. Help them if you can, and enlist their aid if you have need of it.

Indeed. I sense that even now there are good people near you who face grave danger. They need your assistance should you be willing to give it.\n\nTo thwart the will of Molag Bal, we must skirmish with evil wherever it rears its head.
No, we can still move. We'll head to <<1>>, if it's safe there.\n\nBy the Eight, it's inspiring to see Dominion soldiers.
No. When I saw my neighbors fall, I ran. What kind of Khajiit am I?\n\nYou're with Dominion, yes? Give those pirate cowards a trouncing!
<This Sea Viper's death was swift and brutal. The stench of burnt flesh fills the room.>

<It appears the Sea Viper died while ransacking the building. Some sort of magical energy killed her instantly.>\n\n<Upon further examination, a crumpled piece of paper is clutched tightly in her hand.>
I sent my squad to scout <<1>>. If they haven't learned what the Sea Vipers plan is, we can poke around until we figure out what needs chopping.

I see you make a habit of walking blindly into strange and dangerous places. That must make your life very interesting.\n\nBut where are my manners? Welcome to the Dragonstar Arena! Only the strongest of the strong try their hands at our games.

Hopefully your allies aren't as bad at the games as you and they help you get back into the fight.\n\nIf all of you fall? Well, we call that "death." We toss your corpses out back for the guar. Hungry little buggers, you know.

It works perfectly. Thanks for asking.\n\nOh, but you want details. You talk to the Gatemaster up the hall to begin. Then you do your best to turn your enemy into a bloody mess before he does the same to you. That's my favorite part.
Talk to the Gatekeeper. Survive, and see for yourself. \n\nOnly those who prove themselves worthy can learn the secrets of the Arena.

Quite simply, you survive. And your opponent doesn't. Of course, if that happens, my master will take an interest and want to see more.\n\nYou stand on the brink of a remarkable journey. Are you really willing to take the first step?

Each participating team has a champion. Sometimes more than one. First, you must overcome the initial waves of combat. If you make it far enough, you'll get to face the champions.\n\nAnd I hesitate to mention any of our other little surprises.

The Fighters Guild team does a wonderful job of not losing. Must be all the practice they get with the fighting and everything.\n\nTheir champion has been holding his own so far in the competition. I expect good things from him and his team.
Then may the mistress guide your hand.\n\nYou'll certainly need some higher power to watch over you in there.
Everyone in this cursed place committed the same crime. We opposed the Tharns and Molag Bal and for that we have paid dearly.
It is always so. Never once has someone taken pity on Kuralit without hearing his sad tale of woe.\n\nCan I share my burden with you? Will you listen to my story?

Know that I am not as old as my whiskers make me seem! My story begins not many years ago, when this one served in the Imperial army.\n\nYou may ask why I held such a position, but it was not by choice. Conscripted for my skills, I was in high demand.

My ancestors were great Khajiit sailors, so I was assigned to a warship whose soul mission was to maintain order in the wake of the Knahaten flu sweeping the land.\n\nYou know of the Knahaten flu, yes?

This one shivers in fear, remembering those dark days! The Knahaten flu killed so many, all across Tamriel! Argonians and Khajiit proved heartier against it, but it claimed many of my friends' lives before it faded away.\n\nMay I continue?
Is that not horror enough? My tale has stalled, and now I wander from city to city as a beggar.\n\nAs to your earlier question, I saw a Bosmer sneak into the bank late at night.

One night, when <<1>> had already worked a triple shift, and thus was taking a well-deserved rest belowdecks, we aboard the Bountiful Mara, encountered the Crimson Ship!\n\nYou do know about the Crimson Ship?

Indeed! The Crimson Ship was filled with Kothringi suffering from the Knahaten flu. No port would take them in. They finally sailed off into the Abecean, never to be seen again.\n\nIt is rumored that no one who saw the ship lived to tell about it.

As I said, I slept. A sleep so deep and dreamless, nothing woke me. When I finally rose a day later, I found my crewmates missing, and a scribbled note about the Crimson Ship.\n\nThey had seen it! And all had perished, leaving me adrift.
I could not! Many moons passed before another ship happened by. They blamed me for the crew's disappearance, and put me in the stocks! My career over, I became a beggar.

Have I not suffered enough? No ship will take me on now as they think I am either cursed by the Crimson Ship, or sinister for killing an entire crew.\n\nMaybe I am bad luck. When I got here, this was a Bosmer town. Now look! It is full of Altmer!
There's plenty of them down here; take your pick. Many have been dragged deeper into the dungeon. Who knows, your friends might still be alive.
I'll die, I expect. We'll all die here. I only hope that it's quick. Many have been taken into the depths of the dungeon and none have ever returned. The blood never stops flowing down here.

I vowed that I would always face my opponents as an equal. If an enemy came at me with a sword, I would meet his blade with one of my own.\n\nThe harpies fight with claws. How could I go up against them with anything more than the fists nature gave me?
Sharp and natural. They don't wield weapons, so neither will I.\n\nI will fight them head on, fists against claws. And I will do so with honor.

Earning a living. There's gold to be made out here—as long as you have the courage and commitment to deal with all this Celestial nonsense.\n\nI was leading a caravan through the region when the Iron Orcs attacked. Took us completely by surprise.

Harder than some, but you need to follow opportunities as they present themselves. That's how those Dragonstar Caravan thugs do it.\n\nUsually, we finish our runs with a few cuts and bruises between us … but not this time.

I woke screaming every night, from dreams of my wife in the clutches of Dagon cultists—of those Daedra who stepped from that Gate to burn us to the ground.\n\nMy wife saved our neighbors, saved me. And there was no one left to save her. I had to try.
An old friend. She took me in when nobody else would.\n\nI must have traveled half of Tamriel with her family, before she settled here to run the inn.
<<1>>? He's a barnacle who fastened himself to the right arse at the right time.
I …. You should really talk to <<1>> about this. She can explain it better.

Nothing scares me. Not anymore.\n\n<<1>> says, "never cross the deadly kind of rich"—far as I can tell, she means <<2>>. He's a big swinging anchor, and Banu polishes <<2>> like he's trying to see his own reflection.
Some of this, some of that. Enough to keep food in our bellies and grog in our mugs.
Did he now? Not to poison me? Well, whatever you've come to do, get on with it.
Yes, I know all three. Or knew them; they're dead now.
Back there, deeper in the dungeon. They were in the other cages here, but the Daedra came for them yesterday. Or was it the day before? I don't remember now. But they're gone.
I'm sure of it. The Daedra took them back there to kill them. No one's ever returned. They're dead—and you will be too, soon.
Free me then, if you're going to. Hurry, before the Daedra or their minions return!
They were taken deeper into the dungeon. They're probably dead by now. The Daedras' toys don't live very long.
You were almost too late. Sergeant Horatia was dragged out of here hours ago; I was next. Considering what they've been doing to the other prisoners, I hope she's dead by now.
Through the sewer tunnel there. I heard them talking about a chasm. I don't know what's really down there and I don't ever plan to find out.
I'd rather talk about that than about where I almost went. The captain sent us out on patrol, to scout out the Arena. The Daedra jumped us. Most of my squad was killed, maybe they're all dead now.
That's some good news at least. You have my thanks. Now to see if I can get back to my squad, or what's left of it.
Scattered-Leaves? I knew I liked that lizard for a reason!\n\nI thought we were in trouble when the Iron Orcs dragged us away, but I never imagined we'd wind up as troll food.
