Never met another Khajiit, but I'd like to one day. Ahem. "This one is pleased to meet you." I read they speak different. I practice when I can.\n\nI have a book about Khajiit culture. Fascinating stuff, but my hearth-mother doesn't approve.
Oh, all sorts of things. Sometimes they don't do what he thought they would, and every so often they explode, but otherwise he really is a genius—when he isn't being a complete and utter dunce.

You'd be surprised that many so-called scholars refuse to travel to dangerous places. But that's usually where the best sites are located!\n\nAnd then there are the Orcs. Most of the explorers that we know tend to find the Orcs to be … intimidating.
No. I am forever leashed to my mortal shell. Already my perfect children grow deaf to my call.\n\nEnd it, then. Close the pressure valve sustaining me and free me from this withered cage.
Normal hand waving.
Point down

Oh, there have been signs. I even saw her briefly. A durzog was chasing her and I killed it. Well, I guess I wounded it. It slunk off in that direction.\n\nBut Winks dashed ahead again. She must be around here somewhere.
Possibly. Winks can slip through the smallest openings. But she could be in here somewhere. It's a big room. \n\nIf one of those Riekrs hurts my cat, they'll taste my blade.

I think you're right. Making these puzzles seemed to give her some small amount of hope in a difficult situation.\n\nI still need to find my cat. I'll scout ahead and see if my mother left anything else for me.

You're the first one I've—er, this one—has ever met. Did I say that right?\n\nIt would be good to learn more about the Khajiit, and I have plenty of questions. But right now, I'm more concerned about Winks and my friends.

Head to the clothing station and craft a pair of homespun gloves. You shouldn't need much refined jute.\n\nDon't forget a style material. You can purchase them from any clothier, or scavenge them yourself.
Take the raw jute to a clothing station. If you have enough, you can easily refine it.\n\nBring the refined jute to me when you're done, and then you'll make some homespun gloves.
Bring the iron ore to a blacksmithing station. If you have enough, you can refine them into iron ingots.\n\nReally put your back into it! When you have iron ingots, return to me.

Go to the blacksmithing station and craft an iron dagger. Nothing fancy—you shouldn't need more than two iron ingots.\n\nOh, and you'll need a style material. You can purchase them from any blacksmith, or scavenge them yourself if you're thrifty.
Bring the rough maple to a woodworking station. As long as you have enough, you can refine it into sanded maple.\n\nReturn to me when you've done that and we'll talk about crafting a maple bow.
Craft a maple bow at a woodworking station. You'll need sanded maple—also, a style material. Scavenge them yourself, or buy a style material from a carpenter.

Good. Now, go to an alchemy station. Use a solvent and two differing reagents to craft a potion. The reagents must possess common traits, or you'll waste all components.\n\nYou see? Alchemy is as simple as pairing like with like.
We begin at the enchanting table. There, you will combine a rune of potency, essence, and aspect. This simple puzzle forms a glyph. \n\nNow go, piece them together.

Famous treasure hunter. I'm sure you've heard of her.\n\nWe travel the land, searching for hidden treasures, secret relics, and, er, other mystical things. I'm not at liberty to tell you much about our work, but it's very important.

I work for Orsinium's newly established museum. I'm their resident expert on the time of Torug, so the museum sent me to assist Lady Laurent and her man-servant. I always dreamed of visiting the shrine, so I jumped at the opportunity.

Extremely! We've already tried to get up there three times. We lost the rest of the expedition and had to turn back before we barely got out of the base camp.\n\nBut the danger will be worth it if we can find Torug's legendary relics.

We need to rekindle the forge. "Endless breath" has to mean bellows, and "untold rage" is … a furnace? Strange way to say it.\n\nHmm, I'm missing something. Can you look around for a bellows and some kind of blast furnace?

Morkul clan prefers simple solutions that last. Look for switches or some kind of mechanism. We'll see what happens when you set things in motion.\n\nOh, and stay alert. My ancestors wouldn't leave this place completely unguarded.

Legends claim that a powerful relic was buried with Orsinium's founder. At Torug's shrine, my lady hopes to find the Armlet of Torug, the bracelet that gave him the power to tame the wilderness.\n\nNow if only Kharsthun would stop arguing with her.

Her reputation brought her to the attention of the museum and she loves digging around in old tombs. She has a particular interest in an ancient fragment that talks about "Sorrow's Kiss." She believes it has something to do with Torug's shrine.

The museum in Orsinium has it on display. It only contains a few words in the ancient Orc tongue, but I was able to make some sense out of it.\n\nIt talked about the armlet, the shrine, and something called "Sorrow's Kiss." Doesn't that sound romantic?

According to a scroll fragment I studied, the Armlet of Torug is a magical bracelet encrusted with gems. With its power, Torug was able to tame the savage wilderness. It allowed the ancient Orcs to establish the first city of Orsinium.

My mother says we're the best smiths in Wrothgar because we put "heart in the steel." Whose heart? Whose blood?\n\nMorkul clan hasn't had enemies since the days of Morkuldin. Did we feed our rivals to that … thing?

You're right. The old poems aren't about honor we lost when we left Morkuldin—it's honor gained for burying our greatest shame beneath a mountain of ice!\n\nAnd a warning to stay away from the Hand of Morkul, which … well, we couldn't have known.
Not without blood magic. But I can't just leave it here … it's our heritage.\n\nI'll bring it back to the stronghold, but what then? What do I tell my clan?
You know, creepy. "Never blinks when he's talking to you" creepy, not "sniffs your breeches when you're asleep" creepy. As far as I know.\n\n<<1>> respected him, which was good enough for us.

They're wearing Orc armor, wielding Orc weapons, and their tusks have a jaunty tilt to them. I don't know, why would I think they're Orcs?\n\n<<1>> can tell you more. Can't believe I'm glad <<2>> brought him along.
<<1>> figured this was a cycle—every decade or so, the place warms up for some reason lost to time. The trick was to get in and out before the Dwemer guardians woke up.

But he wasn't wrong. We made it deep into the ruins, just like he said. Then those creatures poured out of the walls and cut us down like hogs.\n\nBefore we went inside, <<1>> kept going on about "missing variables." I wish <<2>> had listened.
Morkuldin doesn't require the "blood of our enemies"—that's just how it was misused. Maybe the blood of frostbite spiders is enough.\n\nBlood, ichor … whatever.
You're right. You forge a better blade by studying your past mistakes. I can't keep this from my clan.\n\nPerhaps there's a better way to use this place … an honorable way.
We must make peace with our ancestors and remember the lessons they taught. They've forged with clean hands for generations. The clan needs to know why that's important.
Of course. Returning the forge-hammer will fill my clan with pride—enough to take the sting away when I explain what Morkuldin was.

For all practical purposes, yes. The remaining Winterborn will put up a fight, but without a warlord, my soldiers should be able to wrap this up in short order.\n\nAs for me, I can't wait to show off my trophy to the clan chiefs!
Well, don't let me keep you!\n\nYou've shown that you're capable enough. You have my full confidence. Just don't go and get yourself killed, all right? I have plans for you, my friend. Big plans!
Yeah, Ice-Heart's fancy sword. That should prove to the clan chiefs that we killed the warlord. Might even convince the fence-sitters to finally accept me as the rightful king of all the Orsimer.

Someone needs to examine the stolen supplies and get them ready for transport. Might as well be me.\n\nMeet me back at the keep when you're done. I want you there when I tell the chiefs what we accomplished today.

I want to check on the supplies the Winterborn stole from us and get them ready to transport back to the city.\n\nMeet me at the keep when you're finished here. I want you there when I tell the chiefs what we accomplished today.

Then the corpse to which you've bound my soul will rot for decades. I will have no company but mindless, imperfect beasts. I will go mad, and years later I will expire.\n\nPlease, end my suffering. You owe me that much. Please.
That mad Elf you mentioned. When you said he wasn't a threat, what exactly did you mean?
Well, "zugka" is the ancient Orcish word for "kiss." But "zugra," no, I'm sure it's not "zugra."\n\nAt least, I'm almost sure.
It depends on the context. Bad omens, calamity, some kind of plague or pestilence. But probably, I'd have to translate it here as "curse."\n\nIf the word was "zugra" and not "zugka," you understand.
Good. There are more than enough monsters in this world.\n\nAbout <<1>>. You found him. How did he … what happened?
Truly? Sounds like you could teach my clan a thing or two about holding a grudge.\n\nI have to ask about <<1>>. When you found him, was it … did he suffer?

Orsinium, most likely. If all I recovered is a tale of woe and terror, I might as well use it to earn some drinks. Walk where the echateres walk, my friend.\n\nUnless they have the flux. Then walk two paces to the right. Trust me on this.
You know what they say, "Bretons die easy." Well, my clan says it.\n\nNow that I think about it, it's not very flattering. Sorry, <<1>>.
Damn. You don't hold back, do you?\n\nStill, it sounds like he fought to the last. If he was an Orc, I'd petition to bury him at Sorrow. He should be honored for his sacrifice.

Meeting you was the best thing that happened to us today. You have our thanks.\n\nI'll tell you, though. I'm not looking forward to explaining all this to my mother the hunt-wife or to our clan chief.

Of course. We lost a few fine young Orcs today and it was my fault. I secured permission to go out on our own. I led the hunting party.\n\nAnd I failed to spot the Riekr lair. That's how they were able to get the drop on us.
Hmm? The key to knowledge, of course.\n\nFor which we have you to thank!

A rather pedestrian theory, though a good effort. But you see, life is far more complex than a simple hunt for immortality.\n\nIn the meantime, perhaps you have evidence for which to search, yes? Hmm, yes.

More often than not, yes. There's always some fool who wants to quote the Code of Malacath or insult my honor. It infuriates me!\n\nHow can we build a respectable kingdom when we can't even abandon our most ridiculous superstitions?

Targak? It was all I could do not to kill all three of those troll lovers!\n\nLet Bazrag and Dular think about what happened. I only hope they can set aside old traditions and accept the future I envision. Their support would make things much easier.

Can I see that? Sounds like Khajiit jewelry, but it's strange that you found it in an old Orc ruin.\n\nIt's just like mine! Exactly the same! And look how the bag was placed near these odd pillars. I think it's a puzzle. I love puzzles!

Maybe. One of my dreams is to find out where I came from. Well, and then learn that I'm part of a royal Khajiit bloodline.\n\nI'm sure these pillars are some sort of puzzle. Must be a hint around here that will help us solve it.
Once you've destroyed the stores, use what's left of the poultice. It'll let you return to camp safely and quickly.

I will. Eventually. Maybe. I mean, look around!\n\nThese people are injured! What happens if the Winterborn come back? Someone has to protect them, keep them from being picked off one by one. Anyway, I'll keep them safe while you help Chief Bazrag.

Let me see that. Zayshara! My mother's name was Zayshara! And my sire was Azin. I didn't remember that.\n\nThe hearth-mother said that a hunting party found me wandering in a snowstorm, too cold even to cry. They took me back to the stronghold.

They did. They've always been good to me. The hearth-mother. My brother Avreg, Orgotha, and others. I'm an Orc, even if I don't look like one.\n\nBut … maybe my parents were rescued! Let's look for more clues. Maybe my Khajiit family is still alive!

The faithful of Malacath require protectors, especially in these difficult and violent times. I am one of Malacath's mortal agents—one of the Agra Crun. You would say "the Blood Shield" in the common tongue.\n\nYou have the archivists' blood, yes?

There was little time to prepare you, and still less now. Malacath's vengeance cannot be delayed. \n\nBut I can give you this book. It describes the path you must walk. You were not intended for this path, but you must walk it all the same.

I'm more than just a simple bodyguard. I am the king's favorite shield-wife. My sister and I protect our beloved. We train with him, sleep with him, and fight at his side when the need arises.\n\nAh, just thinking about him makes me smile!

My feelings on the matter are of no concern, but I take pride in my role. Both my sister and I love the king in our own way, and we have pledged to keep him safe.\n\nBear that in mind, outsider, and I will have no reason to kill you.

Initiates used it to gain admittance to the old order, as did those who sought refuge in the halls of Malacath's true servants. It will guide you, but like the Furious One, it won't lead you by the hand. You will have to work to succeed.\n\nNow go.
The choice was yours, though Malacath always demands a sacrifice, a display of loyalty and commitment.\n\nBut rest assured. The Keeper knew her role and she relished the taste of it.

The archivists have been avenged and Malacath's fury sated. For now. The remaining Vosh Rakh will soon notice their shrinking numbers and depart Fharun. \n\nUntil then, I will remain to guard the sanctuary while you get the sacred words to safety.

The Agra Crun is all around, hidden in plain sight. In Orsinium, for example, waits one of the most powerful of our order.\n\nTake the scroll to Kroma, but protect it until you reach her. The Trinimac cult wants the truth destroyed at any cost.
Same as all the others. Looking for adventure!\n\nI figured there wasn't a better place to make a name for myself than in the untamed wilderness of Wrothgar. Are you going to Orsinium?

Eventually. But first they asked me to go to Frostbreak Fortress. I think they realized I was good with a bow and they need something filled with arrows. Hopefully, it's more of these Winterborn!\n\nWho knows, maybe I'll see you there!

After this and what happened at Frostbreak Fortress, I think I need to take a break. Think I'll lay low for a while.\n\nYou be safe out there, all right. This place is worse than Elden Root on market day!
Ah, King Kurog's mother! She's one smart woman and an even smarter Orc!\n\nFrom what I've heard, you want to stay on her good side. I understand she has a fierce temper.

It took a while, but I guess I did.\n\nIt happened so long ago. I don't really remember her or my people. Not sure how I feel about all this, but I need to find Winks. Maybe my mother left something else for me. I'll keep my eyes open as I look around.

Go to the residential district and find the house where the light of Malacath shines. Follow the light. It will guide you to Kroma. Give the scroll that contains the sacred words to her and only to her.\n\nNow go, and may Malacath protect you.

I am a high priestess of Trinimac, serving in Orsinium's temple. Like you, I am here at the request of Forge-Mother Alga to help revive the ancient traditions of truth, honor, and unity.\n\nI also greet new arrivals. Tell me, how was your journey?

We've received similar reports. Just one of a series of unfortunate incidents that we plan to rectify. Orsimer soldiers and even the king himself are looking into this.\n\nKing Kurog believes that even those who refuse his rule must be cared for.

Truly? Perhaps we can still recover the supplies the clans need to survive the winter. The decision to invite outsiders to our land has already reaped untold benefits!\n\nTell me, where have the Winterborn hidden the supplies?
Go on, ask.
Old clan legend says it's full of relics. Every few years, a new crop of idiots runs off there to get killed.\n\nYou want to know what's in there? Ogres, and spiders the size of ogres.
I can tell you how long it takes steel to melt. You want old stories? Go ask a poet.

<<1>> thinks she's steel in a world full of iron. For all the king blusters, she'd challenge him at every turn. Her little sister is content to just run a forge—easy choice.\n\nAlso, I punched his mother.
My what? Does she even listen to me? She never listens! "Honor of the clan," I say. "You'll find someone soon," she says. Pah!\n\nAll right. She sent you here to help? Good—help me find Morkuldin.

With so many resources diverted to rebuild the city of Orsinium or to fend off Reachmen invaders, the smaller clans haven't prepared for the coming winter.\n\nFor many Orcs, the supplies on that caravan could mean the difference between life and death.

I didn't think it would hurt this much. She left those silly notes and puzzles. For me. She loved her son. She loved … me.\n\nI'm Zhasim, but I'm also Elzhar. Sounds kind of funny to my … to this one's … ears.

No, not completely. They're my family, too, you know.\n\nMy mother said that I have trade and travel in my blood. I might go to Orsinium. Apprentice myself to a merchant for awhile. See how that feels.

Invaders from the Reach, the Winterborn. They're following a mad warlord named Urfon Ice-Heart on some insane quest to take our land. But we're not going to let that happen. We've got something the Reachmen don't. A secret weapon.\n\nOur echatere!

What's an echatere? The big animal next to me—that's an echatere! Don't you have them around here?\n\nSweet things, really. We use them for all sorts of things. Transportation, pack animals, beasts of burden. They even make delicious cheese!

Well, not me personally. But yes, Orsinium is going to be grander and more magnificent than any previous version of the city.\n\nKing Kurog has invited artisans and merchants from all over Tamriel to help with the effort, not just adventurers like you.

This caravan brought me! I thought we already covered that?\n\nOh, you mean specifically. The invitation. You got one, too, didn't you? It talked about testing yourself against the most savage land in Tamriel. That was a challenge I couldn't pass up!

He's a chief! In charge of an Orc clan or something.\n\nIf you ask me, he's got more than a chip on his shoulder. It's a whole damn mountain! I don't think he's a big supporter of King Kurog, but he saved us before he went to help the peasants.

No, we were the caravan guards. Bazrag said he was on patrol, looking for Winterborn marauders. Some scary Reach warlord named Ice-Heart leads them. Even Bazrag seemed a bit nervous just talking about him.\n\nNow go help the chief before it's too late!

You made an impression already. But don't worry. I'm not expecting them to come just because you ask nicely.\n\nThe chiefs are stubborn, but they each have a problem that's confounding their clan. Solve their problems and they'll attend the moot.

Tell them that you come to help in the name of King Kurog. That I'm hosting a gathering of clans and I want the chiefs to attend.\n\nAnd it needs to be the clan's chief that comes to the moot. If they try to send a subordinate, I'll be highly insulted.

Now you get it! Help the chiefs and they'll be obligated to accept your invitation!\n\nI've tried to convince the chiefs of Tumnosh, Morkul, and Shatul to join my kingdom. I even married a few of their daughters! We need a better solution.
So, you're a lap dog and a messenger?\n\nI have no time for Kurog's games, outsider. As long as my quarry remains in danger, my place is here with my clan.

Sorry, but I have problems of my own right now. As long as my forge-wife is miserable, I can't deal with anything else.\n\nI wonder. Does "King" Kurog have a solution for volatile family disputes? I'd definitely listen to him speak on that topic!
Well, look upon my husband and weep, for his next journey is to the Ashen Forge.

Perfect! You've done me a great service, my friend.\n\nThe moot will be remembered as the turning point for Wrothgar. The day when all the clans united under the rule of a strong and visionary king. A new golden age for the Orsimer begins here!

Now? Why, we prepare for the moot, of course! It will be packed! Clan chiefs from the farthest reaches of Wrothgar will come together to finally accept my vision for the future. This is how a kingdom is born!\n\nToo bad Bazrag is going to miss it.
Don't worry about Bazrag. He hasn't been seen since the attack on the temple. He's probably gone so deep into hiding or run so far away that we'll never see that traitor again.

Yes. My people are stubborn. They see Malacath as our protector, but nothing could be further from the truth. Malacath's passion is vengeance. We cast ourselves as victims and this holds us back.\n\nTrinimac's light, however, can restore our glory.

No. Doesn't have a clue. That's what makes it so exciting!\n\nThis is an honest-to-goodness secret mission! I always wanted to go on a secret mission! Besides, once you talk to Solgra, you'll understand. She explains things much better than I do.

She can be rather exuberant, but I suppose the term is accurate. I debated with myself before deciding to ask the two of you for assistance.\n\nBut in the end, there isn't anyone else I would trust with this matter.

Yes, but it's not the same. The Vosh Rakh are Trinimac extremists who bend the sacred teachings to their own purposes. They have been gathering power and influence at an alarming rate.\n\nIf they kill the captive chief in Trinimac's name ….

A shield-wife from one of the clans sent me an urgent plea for help. It appears that the clan's chief has been taken captive by a fanatical group of—how do I put this ….\n\nThey're members of a religious sect devoted to Trinimac.
I'll live. But you need to find Zubesha. The Riekr chieftain dragged her off. Something bad is going to happen to her, I just know it.

All right. I'll sneak out of here and make my way back to the camp.\n\nWhen you find the chieftain, make sure you hurt him a lot before you kill him. He won't let Zubesha go if there's a breath still in him.

Avreg and the Orcs are my real family! But if you mean about where I came from, no. I had this moon medallion when they found me. My hearth-mother says it brings me good luck, but not so much today.\n\nYou don't miss what you never had, though, right?

Well, mostly. I did almost get caught that last time. Scared the leaves off my tree, if you catch my meaning. I dove down here to hide and wait for you to arrive.\n\nWorked a lot better in my head, truth be told.

A couple of Vosh Rakhs were arguing. One of them stormed off toward the overlook. He sounded pretty upset with the cult. We might be able to get the prison's location out of him.\n\nOr, you know, he could alert the entire stronghold to our presence.

I found out that the stronghold contains a large prison of some sort, but I have no idea where they hid the thing. Nothing around here looks like a prison to me.\n\nOh, I did hear something else while I was sorting my arrows and waiting for you.
Underground? Like in a dungeon or something?\n\nI hope you don't expect me to grab a shovel and start digging. I don't do that sort of thing.
A well? Yeah, I saw the old well. We'll need a rope or something to climb down, though.\n\nCheck near the forge. I noticed tools and ropes hanging around. One of those ropes should serve our needs.
Kurog sent you to kill the captured chief, but he didn't tell you it was me? Ha! How typical!\n\nWell, the damn cultists couldn't kill me, the prison escapees couldn't kill me, and neither can you!

What are you talking about? After I left Orsinium, I returned here just in time to watch the Vosh Rakh overwhelm my stronghold. I've been a prisoner in my own dungeon ever since!\n\nDefinitely didn't have time to do anything at the temple.

The Trinimac priestess? She's just like the idiots who attacked my stronghold and threw me down here. They released my prisoners and made a game out of letting them torture us.\n\nBut the joke's on them. I'm still alive!
The Vosh Rakh. They're trying to break us. They want Unsulag and me to swear to serve Trinimac. Or their version of Trinimac, at least.\n\nSo far, we've refused, but these ice prisons wear you down.

They said they only need one of us. The switch in front of me releases Unsulag but freezes me. And the one in front of her does the reverse.\n\nThey keep coming in and asking us which switch to press. So far, we've refused to play their game. So far.

Trapped. You know. Touch the wrong switch and somebody dies. That kind of trapped.\n\nThe Vosh Rakh took us captive. Said we were going to join their cult—one way or another. If I stay in this icy prison long enough, I might just agree to anything.

That's the problem. If you push the switch in front of me, Gahar will be released but I'll freeze to death. If you push the switch in front of him, I go free and he dies. They've been trying to make us decide, but we won't give them the satisfaction.

If I knew how to do that, I'd tell you. I hate to say this, but I don't want to die.\n\nIf you free me, I can help. I'm a strong elemental mage and I can fight. But this blasted prison keeps me from casting even the simplest spell of warming.

Unsulag's a good woman, but she's already lived a full life. I can aid the rulers of Orsinium. Assist my people.\n\nI have many productive years remaining—if I get out of this. Release me and I'll devote myself to helping others. You have my word.

Not this time. The Vosh Rakh set this up so that only one of us would get to join their crazy cult.\n\nIf I were noble, I'd say save Gahar and let me die. But I'm not noble. I have a family. They need me. And I'm a healer. I can help you if you let me.

I need to turn the manual override switches in the correct order to open the gate to the next chamber.\n\nBut this is the Chamber of Scorn. It was designed to hold our most dangerous inmates, so it won't be that simple.

As soon as I start the process, poison will begin filling the room and those cell doors are going to swing open.\n\nI'll try to be quick, but with an injured arm, I can only work so fast. Just keep the prisoners away from me and stay out of the gas.

Gahar seems to be a good sort, but do we really need another violent battle mage? I heal the sick and help the wounded. And more than that. I want to live.\n\nI know it must sound terrible, but I really want to live.
You think you can accomplish what me and my strongest warriors have been unable to do?\n\nVery well, outsider. Restore order in the Graystone Quarry and I will go and listen to Kurog's fancy words.
If you're brave enough, talk to Lazghal and do whatever she asks. If you can finally get her to stop yelling at me, I'll go and listen to whatever Kurog wants to say.
Right … I'm sorry. Introductions should come first. I apologize.  I am the Drake of Blades.

Blades. Yes. I'm a member of the Dragonguard. Or, I should say, the true Dragonguard. We were driven underground by the Empress Regent Clivia. Just as well. We are sworn to serve the true heir of the Dragon. She is certainly not that.

Have you seen my bow skills? I'm sure Solgra noticed and said to herself, "That's a fine young lass! She can put a shaft through an apple balanced on the back of a moving wamasu. I shall recruit her!"\n\nEither that or she was desperate for some help.

Go to Fharun Stronghold and meet Eveli. Stop the Vosh Rakh and rescue the chief before it's too late.\n\nI just ask for your discretion in this matter. If the king finds out, he'll send an army, which will only result in more death and destruction.

It will give the Orc traditionalists one more arrow to put in their quiver. And they won't use it only against us.\n\nKing Kurog and the forge-mother have supported us. This will cripple their cause and turn everyone against Trinimac and his followers.

They could be anywhere! Raynor probably went after the Dwarven sphere to keep it from causing more damage.\n\nOh, I know! I think there's a way you can follow the sphere, too. Find his latest tinker project and you'll find Raynor, guaranteed.

Look for a place where the sphere expended a lot of energy, like by that burning wreckage over there. Then just take out the lightning prod and you should get an indication of where the sphere went next.\n\nGo ahead and give it a try over there.
Take this. Raynor has a technical name for it, but I call it a lightning prod. My brother uses it to control Dwarven constructs, but it can also be used to track a construct's energy discharge.
I'll gather up Raynor's tinkering tools and follow you. Once I catch up, we can help Raynor disable that rolling monstrosity!\n\nBut don't wait for me! Raynor needs you! Now get going!

It's a simple misdirection. All members of the Dragonguard have assumed pseudonyms. There's a Drake of Shields, a Drake of Staves, and so on. It gives us the freedom to act in both plainclothes and uniform.

That's a question for the leadership. I like to think it reflects on my keen intellect, but I have no idea. It was probably random. \n\nThen again, the Drake of Crowns is a clumsy, short-sighted ass, so maybe there's something to it. Royalty.
<<1>> was the finest warrior to call Wrothgar home. Some say he was an avatar of Malacath himself.\n\nThose people are idiots. The Wild Boar died, just like anyone else.

Don't believe the tales. He didn't wrestle giants, slay Dragons, or ride a giant bear.\n\nBut he carved out a place for my people when Orcs were seen as little more than beasts. Had <<1>> not betrayed him, Daggerfall and Sentinel would be Orc cities.
According to legend, <<1>>'s fury at the "honor" of men drove Shinji to defeat—but rather than lose a duel, Shinji ordered ten thousand archers to kill them both.\n\nAnd that was that.

Thirty years into the siege of Old Orsinium, <<1>> challenged <<2>> to determine its fate. As the defenders watched the duel, Shinji's Order of Diagna slipped inside and opened the city doors. My people were slaughtered.\n\nAnd then … it's unclear.

The door to this tomb commemorates <<1>>'s final duel. His image is identical to engravings from that period—there's no question it's him.\n\nHe respected every opponent he challenged. That's reflected in the depiction of <<2>>, his final opponent.

Kireth! Then the sphere didn't hurt her too badly? Thank the Three for that!\n\nWait a moment … is that the modified energy detection and absorption rod? It is! That's just what we need to repair the sphere!

I think Kireth refuses to employ the correct terminology just to annoy me. But I suppose that's what sisters do.\n\nNo matter, though. She always comes through in the end. Now that we have the rod, we can repair the sphere and set things right.

Disable my latest creation? After I went to all this trouble? Why in the world would we do that?\n\nIt will be a simple enough matter to use the rod to absorb the power core's excess energy. Then the sphere should settle down and behave. Theoretically.

Exactly! Use the rod to detect the sphere's energy discharge and expose an after-image. You can follow that directly to the sphere.\n\nWhen you find the sphere, use the rod to drain the excess energy. But don't attack the sphere. That would be … bad.

When it comes to Dwemer technology, everything is theoretical. But I am an expert on the subject, so my theories are better than most.\n\nThe faulty power core drove the sphere crazy with excess energy. Once we drain that energy, it will be fine.

Bad as in really bad.\n\nDo you know what happens if you breach the seal of the power core while you're hacking and bashing at the sphere? Well, immediately unleashing all that energy would rearrange the local landscape in a very explosive fashion.

If I know my sister, she's right behind you with my tinkering tools. I'm going to need them to repair the sphere.\n\nYou go ahead. Once Kireth arrives, we'll follow. Just be careful. There's no telling what the sphere will do in its current condition.

They hold <<1>> responsible for Old Orsinium's destruction. When they see this is actually Shinji's tomb … at best, <<2>> will be banished for his find.\n\nAt worst? Shinji's bones will be ground to powder, cooked into a pie, and served to the king.
I … we don't know. The door won't open, so it's all theory.\n\nBut I'll stake my reputation on this being <<1>>'s tomb. I fear the king's people will be overzealous when they realize I'm right.
There are catacombs nearby with similar stonework to this tomb, but they're crawling with Winterborn. Try there—look for a monument stone of some kind.
The indentations by the door are for burial urns—no doubt some sort of key.\n\nIf you can open the tomb with the proper urns, I can safeguard Shinji's remains.
Damn right you're not!\n\nMake a move and I'll cut you. Just a flick of my wrist and your guts will decorate the floor. Now tell me why Solgra sent you. What kind of game is Kurog playing this time?
My arm is fine! But I couldn't get out of the prison on my own, so killing you down there wasn't an option.\n\nNow I'll ask again. Why are you here? Why did Solgra send you to help me?
Now I understand! Kurog wants to save face. Can't have a rival chief die at the hands of fanatics who worship the same god as our so-called king.\n\nNow I see where Kurog's priorities lie.
Me? Help Kurog?\n\nWhere was our so-called king when my clan was at the mercy of the Vosh Rakh? Where was he when my people were dying or being forced to join this cult against their will?

I guess we could take him to High Priestess Solgra. She did send us to save him, after all.\n\nI'm sure I can sneak him into the city, as long as he cooperates and doesn't do anything stupid or anything.

All right, then. We've got a plan! And it's a perfectly good plan. Really.\n\nOther than me trying to sneak the chief into a city where Kurog has eyes and ears everywhere. What was I thinking? And how are we going to convince the chief to come with me?

The cultists talk. A lot. We might be able to eavesdrop on them and hear something useful. Or we can search the buildings and hope for the best.\n\nEither way, let's split up. We can meet back up after one of us finds something.

The king can preach Orc unity all he wants, but what he means is fealty. For us to bleed out in a dagger-fight he started with the Bretons.\n\nUs, join that losing battle? Not if he paid our weight in Ayleid nose-hash. Told him as much last month.

"Fight with me or the same will happen to you, blah blah blah, you're too dumb to notice a subtle threat so I'll throw it in your face."\n\nAnd now we march. King Joile wants to play at spilling blood? I'll carve him a river from here to Daggerfall.

It was, until a few minutes ago. Another king—that Breton king, Joile—just sent me a letter. Told me my fool brother <<1>> died to Breton forces at Orsinium.\n\nBut then he turned it into a job offer.
No.\n\nI do not slight <<1>>. He leads the Knights of the Dragon—his honor and skill with a blade are without question. But <<2>> will see that, and use Trystan's honor against him.
There are few left with skill to match my own, so the duel itself is an honor. After all, doesn't honor wear the face of your next opponent?
The Orcs claim him a warrior without equal. Of more importance, so do his opponents.\n\nCunning, quick, and patient—he bides his time and then strikes. A style that adapts to his opponents.
Well, don't let me keep you! It knocked out my companions and seems intent on frying my camp.\n\nSo if you're going to do something, now would be a good time!

Sure. Can't you smell them? We were packing our gear when that clanking monstrosity rolled in.\n\nAt first, the sphere just rolled around and poked at everything. Then one of my hunters attacked it and it got meaner and faster.

The sphere zoomed around the camp. Every time one of my hunters got close, it shocked them.\n\nThen it started smoking and sparking. That's when the fires started. I was trying to figure out what to do when you came along.
Nonsense! I'm sure it was nothing more than a misunderstanding. And none of the Orcs look like they were seriously injured.\n\nI'm certain the sphere never meant to hurt them. It was just … curious.
You have an annoying habit of focusing on the negative aspects of a situation, do you know that?\n\nLook, the sphere didn't kill anyone. I think it came here to help.

Am I speaking too fast? Let me explain this another way.\n\nThe sphere is doing exactly what I designed it to do. It's working perfectly! Or rather, it would be if I could drain off the excess energy. I think one more use of the rod should do it!

It was just following its nature. When I rebuilt it I altered it to be my assistant. The perfect helper as it were. I think it rolled into the camp to help the hunters do—well, whatever it is hunters do. Don't you understand? This is terrific news!
Well, thank the Three for that!\n\nRaynor still has an insane notion that he can repair the crazed construct. But after seeing this, I'm even more determined to make sure the sphere is destroyed.

Raynor and I will make sure these hunters are all right. It's the least we can do. Then we'll follow after you.\n\nOnce the sphere is destroyed, I'll feel a lot better. Until then, it's like there's a knot in my chest and someone is pulling it tight.
At least it didn't attack you.\n\nYou need to use the prod again and find it before it does any more damage to the countryside.
Shatul travels with the echatere. We have no prisons, just the Code of Malacath.\n\nIf you wrong another in the clan, you have two choices—pay in gold, or pay in blood.

I think I can do that, as long as I'm careful.\n\nOthers were dragged in here with me. Humble travelers who never harmed anyone. And now they're threatened with pain and death if they don't swear allegiance to the Vosh Rakh.
Right, right. Thanks again.\n\nYou know, I came to Wrothgar because it was supposed to be a safe and amazing place for Orcs to live. Well, so far, it doesn't seem to be either safe or amazing.
Oh I'm well enough. If you open this cage, I won't just walk, I'll run!\n\nThe Vosh Rakh are bad, bad people. I just want to get out of here before they drag me off like the others.

It's nothing. Well … <<1>> went missing that night. When I caught her out in the snow, I heard someone singing.\n\nIt sounded like <<2>>, but I didn't stay to listen. If the chief's hunt-wife wants to sing alone at night, that's her business.
Oh? About what?
My wounds … I cannot face <<1>> like this. You must confront her in my place.\n\nI trust your skill, commander. Quickly! She cannot escape.
<You eliminated one of the cultists, but that didn't help you locate the prison.>
What the …? Who are …? Hold on, I'm not like the rest of these cultists.\n\nThey forced me into this. Said they were going to kill me unless I converted to their cause. You've got to believe me!
Listen, I'm not like them. Look at me! Do I look like an Orc to you?\n\nI was a prisoner. They forced me. Join or die, they said! I, oh gods, why is this happening? I don't want to die.

It's … it's below us! The prison is underground. The well leads directly to it, but it's pretty deep. I … I wouldn't recommend just jumping.\n\nOh gods, please don't kill me. I told you what I know! Let me go. Please!

The … the prison? That's what we were arguing about.\n\nI said it isn't as secure as they think. Oh, sure, the main gate is impenetrable, but there are other ways to get in. They don't care. Who'd be dumb enough to jump into a prison, they said!
Thank you. Thank you so much. I'm going to get out of here the first chance I get.\n\nAnd don't worry. I won't say a word about you.
Ні!
No worries. We'll stay back and let you deal with any of those Vosh Rakh maniacs we run into.\n\nWe'll move forward as soon as we see that the coast is clear.
Then this must be our lucky day! Not only have we avoided detection, but I found this rope in the barracks while I was looking around.\n\nIt should be long enough to reach to the bottom of the well.
Follow me. I'll secure the rope and drop it into the well.\n\nJust be careful down there. Who knows what kind of monstrosities live at the bottom of an Orc well.
Whoever built this place … they wanted us to know the truth. <<1>> and <<2>> tried to end the siege, to stop the killing. The only betrayal was King Joile's.\n\nIt seems <<3>> and I were both right.
I knew you could do it!\n\nFollow me. I'll secure the rope and drop it into the well.

The king will know the truth. This is <<1>>'s tomb, and altering any piece of it will mar his legend. The king won't dare touch <<2>>'s remains—especially not once I write Sentinel with the news.\n\nLet the kings argue with each other, if they must.
Patch things up with <<1>>. We've worked together for years … I won't let this break us.\n\nBut please don't tell her. It should really come from me.

Me? I'm no one. Just a humble engineer who built and maintained this prison. Before they tossed me into it, that is.\n\nI've been able to avoid the dangerous prisoners, at least so far. Luckily, I literally know this place like the back of my hand.

Well, not just me. They threw a lot of the clan members down here. And then, the bastards, they opened the cages. Let the actual prisoners loose. It was some kind of sick game to them.\n\nBut I never heard an alarm. You must be stealthy as a shadow.

Well, I designed it. But most of the heavy lifting was done by the Orcs of Clan Fharun. The chief hired me, despite my obvious non-Orcishness. He appreciated my expertise and sardonic sense of humor.\n\nBut it was those Vosh Rakh who imprisoned me.

Well, this elixir might come in handy. \n\nThere's a chamber you might come across. Fills with gas if the cell gates open accidentally. A failsafe measure, you see. Drink this potion and the gas won't bother you. I always carry a vial, just in case.

Tastes like barf, but works like magic!\n\nOh, there's also a spike room. Amazing defense mechanism, unless you're in the chamber when it activates. Remember that it resets if you don't turn the three valves fast enough.

You met Frilan? Ha, I knew they couldn't kill that damned Breton. The man is a genius! Glad you took his advice. That potion might save your life.\n\nYou still need to keep the prisoners off my arse so I can open the gate though.

Of course I think it needs to be destroyed! Don't you?\n\nThis time my brother tinkered around with something that was extremely dangerous. We're just lucky nobody was seriously injured by that thing!

My brother rarely agrees with me about anything. Why should this time be any different?\n\nBut the point of the matter is that we need to destroy that construct. If you talk to him, I'm sure you can get him to see the logic in that.

Just give me the lightning prod and I'll take care of it.\n\nIf I drain off its remaining energy, the gears will fuse and the construct will become permanently inert. Then it'll be nothing more than a large, metal doorstop.
Of course! Why would I want to do anything else? With a few minor adjustments, this little sphere will be as good as new!
My sister! I suppose she wants to destroy the poor thing. Hit it! That's her solution to every problem!\n\nBut important research can be dangerous. Real scholars understand and accept that.

Just give me the lightning prod and I'll take care of it.\n\nI can alter the frequency of the rod to recalibrate the sphere's energy dampeners to better regulate the amount of energy flowing through it. Simple as making a kwama egg omelette, really.

I'm not sure what you mean. They're reanimated dead people. I actually quite like skeletons. It's a shame they're so repulsive and dangerous. \n\nI'm sure that sounds bad. Please remember, I am not a crazy person.

They never lie.\n\nSpycraft is all about observation—scraping away lies to find the truth. I'm very good at it, but it makes my head hurt. Skeletons are what they are, and that's it. It's refreshing. That doesn't make them any less dangerous though.

Razasha's alive? Praise the Eight and anyone else who wants to listen! I'm just glad she didn't follow us in here herself.\n\nThose Vosh Rakh maniacs want new members. Someone who calls herself the Proselytizer leads this bunch. You need to stop her!
Azhnura the Proselytizer? She's a horror. She came by not too long ago and told them to make the fire hotter. Said it would help me see the light. \n\nIf I get the chance, I'll show her some light!

And who decides who we honor and remember? The victors, of course, for they get to write the history.\n\nBut there are two sides to every story. No one remembers the losers. They fought for what they believed in and failed, and so they are forgotten.

I get reports. Things my advisors think I need to know. One report claims that the Wood Elf is keeping company with Bazrag. When two of my scouts confronted her, she killed them both.\n\nI'm concerned that Bazrag has turned Eveli against us.

To the vanquished, this isn't the statue of a hero. It's a tribute to a tyrant.\n\nMany see me in the same way. A tyrant, forcing my ideas upon the people. They say I'm wrong, that I'll destroy the Orsimer. They seek to turn everyone against me.
We'll wait here while you scout ahead.\n\nBut don't take too long. One really strong gust of wind could scatter this rickety bridge in all directions, and we don't want to be on it when that happens.
A Wood Elf and two Orcs? Sounds like the beginning of a bad limerick.\n\nSorry. We don't see that many of the little Elves around here, so I really can't help you.

Ah, my apologies. I couldn't reveal anything until you said the proper words.\n\nTake the stairs down into the storage area. Look for an opening in the wall. It leads to our most private set of rooms.

None that he was keen to share. He did a lot of begging. Sentiment. I learned a lot about his mother, for instance. I don't know why people always talk about their mothers. \n\nIt's probably my fault. I've never been a very good interrogator.
Wonderful! Now to brew them for the competition. I call it my "cup of wrath."\n\nI still have a glass from an earlier batch. You're welcome to try it.
Not even a sip? I wouldn't mind a second opinion.
Here you are. So, what do you think?\n\nAnd please, be honest. If it's not ready for competition, there's still time to perfect it.
Oh? What did you find? Do not keep <<1>> suspended!
This one knew you walked with Khenarthi's luck! Quickly, show them to <<1>>. <<2>> can already taste her freedom!

I can make it worth your while. If you place the blame on <<1>>, he'll let me go. Then I'll collect my emergency funds, meet you at the Greedy Gut, and pay you for the note and your silence.\n\nThink about it.

I withheld certain details, yes. But I had good reasons. If cultists killed Bazrag in Trinimac's name, it would have started a civil war.\n\nAnd if Kurog found out you were trying to rescue Bazrag, you would have never been allowed to leave the city.

Someone wanted to blame Bazrag for the Malacath fanatics while also removing the chief from the battlefield. It was a brilliant plan. Fortunately, you were able to foil it.\n\nAnd now, thanks to Bazrag, we know what the Vosh Rakh are planning next.

Bazrag's shield-wife approached me after the Vosh Rakh attacked Fharun Stronghold. She knew the king would do nothing for those who didn't accept his rule.\n\nChief Bazrag was ambushed at the same time the temple was being attacked.

Exactly! <<ACmz:1>> gives the drink its sharp aftertaste, but the water evens out the crispness.\n\nWrothgarian Orcs still use wrathberries to fend off illness, but our ancestors knew the best way to make the medicine.

I'm not even sure whose side I'm on anymore. When Bazrag and I sneaked into the city, two guards got lucky and happened to be in the right place at the right time. They attacked.\n\nI … I … I just reacted and let my arrows fly.

I knew you were going to say that. Still, I'm not sure I can get past Solgra's lies. She tricked us into helping Chief Bazrag—and I'm still not sure about his role in all this!\n\nAll right. You can count on me. But I'm doing this for you, not them.
But I killed two guards who were just doing their job! They probably have loved ones, pets ….\n\nI … I don't know if I can do this anymore.

Don't worry. We'll be careful.\n\nWe can't thank you enough for helping us. We were heading to Orsinium when the Vosh Rakh took us. Just wanted to be a part of history, you know? Anyway, we'll be right behind you.
Oh? What information?
The king's lucky mug! Uh, pretend you didn't hear that.\n\nWell? Anything else you need?
That's what she's been saying for days! Huh.\n\nYou've done the Guard a true service. Anything else you need?
I knew it! Her story never fit together quite like it should.\n\nI'll make sure that mug gets back to the Guard. Anything else you need?

The Vosh Rakh are up to something, that's for sure. They've been gathering in the ruins ever since we got here.\n\nWe did notice something unusual, though. The high-ranking cultists appear to be much better dressed than their subordinates.

Not necessarily. It might just mean that the leaders have more funds and better taste.\n\nStill, between the robes and the masks, acquiring a few of their uniforms could definitely help us sneak inside.
I can't argue with evidence. I'll turn this over to the Guard and release the prisoner.

No, my friend, thank you! I'm just glad Raza didn't barge in there herself. She's headstrong, but she's no match for those mad cultists.\n\nNeither am I, for that matter. We're just simple pottery makers looking for a new life in Orsinium.
More than enough to serve brain pockets at the competition!\n\nI do believe I perfected the recipe with my earlier batch. Would you care for a taste? They're especially crisp!
Isn't it juicy? The grass casing draws the bile from the brain mash, which gives it a good snap.\n\nThis is an old recipe from Shatul. They travel well, and the <<z:1>> is a natural preservative.
Just a taste? It would help me know if it was ready for competition.
Here you go. Pull it apart with your hands and scoop out the—yes, like that.\n\nSo? How is it?
I knew it … her hands are red with my husband's blood!
<<1>> poisons her mind with denial. I refuse to pay for a crime I did not commit.
I will not dishonor my husband's memory by fighting you.\n\nBut if I stay, <<1>>'s grief will turn to hate. I … I will leave the clan.
Giving away your own coin so <<1>> can gain satisfaction? This isn't your affair. Why would you do this?
Then we shall fight. Meet me by the river, so I can feed it with your blood.
Of course. My elemental magic is yours to command. I won't let you down.
I'm fine. Not that it is really any concern of yours. I'm just taking a break from my walk. Eating a little meat. Drinking a little ale.
Since you're paying for it, I don't see why not. It's good, strong stuff.
Damn you, outsider! But the code is the code.\n\nSo, what do you want? Gold, land? A bear you can ride around on?

To Solgra? The damn Trinimac priest? Why in the world would I …?\n\nOh, all right. But if I see any indication that this is a trick to get me to Kurog, I'll kill the Wood Elf and hunt you down like a rabid echatere. On that, you have my word.
Perfect! Ventricle pie requires the freshest ingredients. <<Cmz:1>> don't exactly keep unless you bake them quickly.\n\nI have one last slice from my previous attempt. You're welcome to it!
I'm not asking you to eat the whole thing. But if you don't mind, I'd like to know if it's good enough to round out a meal.
Here you go, have a slice. Large bites, as the chiefs of old would do.\n\nSo? How did it turn out?

Surprising, isn't it? A bit nutty from the moss, but the intestinal quiche contrasts well with the vascular cream pockets. Chewy, too!\n\nIn the halls of Old Orsinium, no meal was complete until they served ventricle pie.
Of course. My healing magic is yours to command. I won't let you down.
That's a strange question for someone who holds your rank. Haven't you learned this much already?

I can appreciate that. In truth, our beliefs and those of Orsinium's temple are similar, though they are not as pure in their devotion to Trinimac. \n\nBut there are those in the city who follow our teachings. They just wear a different mask.

So, which blessing have you decided upon?\n\nWill you accept the blessing of Avalian and become one with the wind? Or will Vaia's resolve protect you from the coming trial? Or perhaps Usunok's rage will grant you the strength to succeed?
Then let Trinimac's swiftness guide you through the Gauntlet.
Then let Trinimac be your shield against the dangers of the Gauntlet.
Then let Trinimac grant you the strength to overcome the challenge of the Gauntlet.

If you take too long, the switches reset and you will need to begin again. Others may pass you and take the position you fight for.\n\nAnd don't worry about killing anyone. They're certainly going to try to kill you.
Trinimac favors the victorious in battle. If followers fall, they are not worthy.\n\nThe Vosh Rakh understand that. So should you.

I swear this is true, Kynareth blind me if I tell a lie.\n\nMy cart got stuck on that hillock over there and my guar weren't strong enough to pull it free. I despaired of getting my goods out of this desolate land when it rolled up.

The metal man sparked some more, and my goods caught on fire! My guar burst their harness and ran, and the cart gave way. It shattered! You see the result over there.\n\nThe metal man paused, curled up into a ball, and rolled off.

Believe me stranger, I know not what it was. A ball of steel and sparks … that unfolded into the shape of a man! I fell back as it set itself to pushing my cart.\n\nAt first, I thought Zenithar had blessed me, but the cart would not come free ….
If I knew what you meant—which I assure you, I do not—I would find no amusement in your brazen approach.

You think any fence in Wrothgar will purchase King Kurog's favorite flagon? And best of luck selling that ugly lump of pewter beyond these lands.\n\nIt seems we're stuck with each other. I'll offer you the same deal I made <<1>>—no more.

Ha! Coffee shipped all the way from Velyn Harbor and he eats the whole bag off the cart?\n\nHe'll make a fine smoked bear's head stew. One of his cousins just came off the fire, if you'd care for a sample.
Dig in! The lichen is key to the broth. You may notice the tomato base draws out the subtler taste of the truffles.

Bear meat is usually disgusting, but those of northern Wrothgar survive on a diet of fish. And the marrow makes for a delicious stew!\n\nI can't wait to serve up <<1>>'s head. I hope there'll be a subtle hint of coffee.
You aren't a fan of a dish that comes with its own container? Are you sure you can't make an exception? Just one ladle-full?

There were a lot of them. And they were strong—stronger than we were, at any rate. Glothun was the worst. He kept saying that fire and ice would lead us to Trinimac's truth, whatever that is.\n\nWill you find Shalda and the others? Please?

I … I appreciate your help. Shalda and I aren't very religious, but what these cultists are doing is wrong.\n\nOh, and I noticed an opening in the back of the ruins. That might be the best way to escape after you find Shalda and the others.

Shalda and I packed up our pottery shop in Shornhelm to make a new start in Orsinium. If I lose her, I don't know what I'll do.\n\nThe others? Just travelers we met along the way. A cook, a couple of mages …. I hate to think of them coming to harm.

Our founder, Adeliza Silver-Axe, crafted the banner to honor her beloved son, who was turned into a werewolf.\n\nForced to kill him, she weaved her tears and blood into the banner. And each commander since has added a drop of blood to the sacred flag.

I will find other members of our order, if they still survive. If not, I will recruit new members. Either way, we will rebuild. The banner will serve to rally us.\n\nI won't let Magnar and his mangy beasts win the day. I simply won't allow it.

It's done as part of a ritual. They fast for three days and meditate before the banner. They see visions. Of Adeliza Silver-Axe. She made it our sacred duty to rid the world of the curse of werewolves.\n\nI am honored to be part of the order.

Eveli aids my enemy. The Wood Elf has chosen the wrong side. I worry that you might follow her example.\n\nBut I have a moot to prepare for and I've said what I had to say. When you see Eveli, I expect you to do the right thing.

Right, right. A little Wood Elf gave it to me. Described you to a turn and asked me to deliver this letter.\n\nNot sure why she was hiding under that hood or why she spoke with a funny accent, but I haven't met that many Wood Elves, so ….

As a matter of fact, although it didn't make a lick of sense to me. She said the letter itself wasn't important. She said that what really matters is the beginning of every thought.\n\nMaybe you'll understand it, because I certainly don't!

A coded message? You mean as in spies and such? That's not something I'm usually asked about. Reagents, soul gems, spells … those are my usual areas of expertise.\n\nNot sure I can be of much help in this, but perhaps I can offer a bit of advice.

A bribe? Oh, very well. I accept. But you didn't hear this from me.\n\nThere's an outlaw den below the city. It's the best place to find to find all kinds of unsavory characters. If anyone can decipher your message, you'll find them there.

Coded messages, if that's what this is, tend to contain patterns. The message, or the poem in this case, usually doesn't mean anything as a whole. The real message is in the tiny snippets.\n\nTry looking at the words differently. Maybe that will help.

Codes and languages? This one considers those to be her specialty! You have come to the correct person, my friend!\n\nLet me see the message. I will even give you a discount since I wasn't arrested today!

No, no. If this one simply blurts out the answer, then you will have learned nothing. Better to teach you to hunt than hand you a sandwich, yes?\n\nThe beginning of each thought. Look at the first word of every sentence, then all will become clear.

Interesting, but extremely obvious. You really needed this one's help to decipher this?\n\nThere aren't even any mysterious symbols or complex patterns. It's so simple a sober Nord could figure it out. Um, no offense intended.

The Vosh Rakh want to make a statement. Something big. Bazrag thinks it involves the moot, where all the chiefs will be gathered.\n\nWe need more information. Someone needs to enter the old Trinimac temple to the west and learn more about their plans.

I'll send scouts ahead, but you'll need to get inside and do whatever it takes to uncover the exact nature of their plan. Lives are at stake. Remember that.\n\nNow please, talk to Eveli. We need her. You have to convince her to help us.

I can do that. Besides, it'll be nice to get out of a city. Try to forget about the price on my head for a while.\n\nAll right, let's do this. But be careful out there, will you? I can't afford to lose the only person I really trust.

First things first. I'll wait to see if any members of the order return from missions. Then we'll establish a new base of operations and rally new members to our sacred banner.\n\nThe Order of the Silver Dawn will survive. The world needs us.

We must select a new leader. After that, it will be up to that person to decide how best we should proceed.\n\nAdeliza founded our order in this place. But now that the werewolves have discovered it, perhaps it would be best to just leave it to them.

We had precious little warning that the pack was coming, but it was enough. We set up traps to slow or even kill the invaders. Rock falls, spikes, bear traps, that sort of thing.\n\nTread carefully in there.

Ah, that will be Seht's Flywheel. It was built by the Baron Who Moves Like Heat Lightning. \n\nWe visited the Clockwork City, of course, and he based his design on that. I can almost visualize this baron in a chamber of pistons … no, it's gone.

The Spiral Shadows, an arena inspired by Mephala's realm! Its architect was The Baron Who Moves Like Flickering Flame. \n\nI think he might have been one of my favorites. I remember watching him for hours. Or do I just … remember remembering that?

Seht's Balcony! It was designed by the Baron Who Moves Like a Dancer's Hips after spending a season with the Mechanist. \n\nBeware the whirling blades! They move just like … just like … oh, you know what I mean. Don't you?

It's the Drome of Toxic Shock! The Baron who Moves like Wind in the Reeds really poured his heart into this one. Curious that such a gentle soul should create an arena as lethal as this one.\n\nTriumph here, challenger, and restore my baron to me.

You've been lucky, indeed you have, but I fear your run ends here. This is the Igneous Cistern, devised by the great Baron who Moves like a Torrent in Spate. \n\nI shall never see his like again, challenger. For here you will die.
This one is the Vault of Umbrage. It was hand-carved by the Baron who Moves like a Wary Moth. \n\nYou … you can do this, can't you? You can actually do this, and my barons will be restored to me!

It's called the Vale of the Surreal. The Baron who Moves like a Shivering Droplet served the Mad God for a time, and that's where he got the idea. \n\nI've never liked this arena. Too uncanny. But I miss my baron. Win him back for me!

You've reached the Rink of Frozen Blood. It was the masterpiece of the Baron who Moves like Sunlight on Waves. \n\nI'm beginning to hope, you know. That you'll be able to succeed, to return my barons to me. Is it a mistake for a Daedra to hope?

The Baron who Moves like a Smoking Plume was a great admirer of Mehrunes Dagon. I think you'll see that in his Theater of Despair. \n\nI've never been one to despair, but I've missed my barons so, I was almost ready to succumb. I'm glad I didn't.

The temple's leaders are too forgiving. They live in harmony with non-believers. Trinimac is a god of war. He does not tolerate false gods such as Malacath.\n\nSoon it won't matter, though. We have agents at work within the city even as we speak.

Patience, overseer. All will be revealed in good time.\n\nFirst, complete the trials and prove your worth in this endeavor. Then all will be revealed. And if you fail, it won't matter, for the dead have little use for knowledge.
Bow? Never bow! Only show the top of your head when you smash in your enemy's face!\n\nDo you think I require supplication? Do you mistake me for Molag Bal?
Honor the clans who carved out a mountainside to raise these walls—those who armed, fed, and ruled this city in its prime.\n\nHonor the clans who built a city worthy of my attention.

Does that surprise you? My people have lost their way under the stifling traditions of Malacath. I seek to unite us on a new path, a path devoted to the true god, Trinimac!\n\nA new age begins, an age that will see the Orsimer attain power and glory.

Against me? I think not. Not when the Vosh Rakh is clearly to blame. Our purpose served, we will disband and leave my chosen scapegoat to deal with the consequences.\n\nHigh Priestess Solgra is behind all this. She's the obvious choice.

My son is not your concern. You are Vosh Rakh now. Nothing else matters.\n\nYou joined at a pivotal time. Soon, Trinimac's blade of courage will pierce the heart of the moot and strike down the insolent clan chiefs. Then true unification can begin.

We all have our purpose. The people will rally against Solgra and demand justice. Our agents are already hunting her down. Before the moot ends, we will have her.\n\nBut again, that is not your concern. You have another mission to perform.

The moot? No, our warriors are already in place. When the chiefs attend the moot, we will eliminate them and bring unity to our people.\n\nInstead, I want you to join the warriors heading to the inn. Help them capture Bazrag before he can escape again.
What … what do you mean he didn't make it? What aren't you telling me?
You … you did what? What kind of person does something like that? He … he looked up to you. Like all of us did!\n\nYou're a monster.

Does that justify what you've done? Does that make you feel better?\n\nI thought Bazrag was bad. That Solgra betrayed us. But you … you're worse than either of them. Would you sacrifice me, too? No … don't answer that.

The river doesn't always flow downstream, my friend. Did you know that these ruins appear bigger on the inside than they do from the outside? Ah, the mysteries of architecture!\n\nBut you should speak to Eveli. She's anxious to know what you found out.

Glothun's a brutish, nasty Orc. Praised Trinimac with one hand and slew a poor tailor who defied him with the other.\n\nHe took notes, made a list of the captives. His "new recruits," he called them. That should help you locate Shalda and the others.

So it really does exist? Sometimes you never know when you're dealing with myth and legend.\n\nCould I trouble you to take it downstairs and place it in its display? In the meantime, I'll find that list of relics I mentioned the last time we spoke.
<<1>> enjoyed walking behind him. It was like watching the  rolling ocean.\n\nThis one is not usually distracted in such a way. Perhaps <<2>> relied on this to trick her.

This one gives me chills! The helmet was worn by the legendary Orc hero, Uzdabikh, who single-handedly slew one-thousand-and-one Redguards during the Battle of Fharun Pass.\n\nLittle known fact—Uzdabikh might have been a woman!

The name means "blood shield" in the Orcish tongue. The shield belonged to the legendary shield-wife, Bagrar Troll-Slayer. She distinguished herself as the first protector of Malacath's faithful, during the time of the Balagog blood purge.
Fine, fine. Come back when you realize I'm your only chance to turn a profit.

Ah, I knew that was gold well spent! I've already received twenty visitors thanks to those notes!\n\nBut where are my manners? Welcome to the newly established museum of Wrothgar, authorized by the king himself.

Oh, most certainly! The House of Orsimer Glories has a simple mandate. We're to collect historic treasures related to the Orcs and the Orsimer nation.\n\nBut I'm a simple scholar. I have no aptitude when it comes to searching for ancient relics.
It's the Agra Crun, the blood shield. It was recently donated to the museum by an anonymous adventurer, and I can't wait to put it on display.\n\nIt will be one of our best attractions!
I'm not one to turn away an honest helper! But before I ask you to go traipse around in search of historic treasures, why don't you take this downstairs and put it on display?
Then go forth and receive your clan.\n\nShatul, I present your new chief!

Yes, yes! The Rat has ears to the ground. Ears to the walls. My little friends are everywhere and they hear secrets whispered by Daedra big and small. Tasty secrets.\n\nThese Daedra plot and whisper, you see, and The Rat listens. He always listens.

They speak of the Dragonfires! They seek to snuff them out forever, oh yes. The Rat heard this quite clearly. \n\nNo Dragonfires ever again. No more Dragon-God promises. No more Eight-blessed emperors in shiny hats. Just death and slavery, forever!

For now. Only for now! Don't you know the story? When Alessia's heirs wear the Amulet of Kings, the fires will burn again! Even a mighty Daedric Prince must hide from such a light!\n\nUnless Molag Bal erases them, of course. Unless that happens.

You beg The Rat to share all his crumbs? No, no. The Rat has said enough!\n\nYou want more, greedy one? Find the Drake of Blades. She's close, very close. Down in the sewers. She would like to nibble on this crumb, oh yes. Tell her the Prince's plan!
As you can see, we've been rather busy ourselves, so I haven't had a chance to get the entire story out of Eveli.\n\nTell me, what else did you learn at Paragon's Remembrance?

Solgra doesn't have a bounty on her head—at least not yet. She went back to the temple. Business as usual, and all that.\n\nWhat a mess Kurog has made. He thinks we're the traitors, but his mother is running a cult right under his nose.

By the sacred tusk, the forge-mother? The Vosh Rakh answer to Alga? That's … well, come to think of it, that makes a certain amount of sense.\n\nThe cowards blame the high priestess and then get to smell like sunshine on a cloudy day.

The Rat? Yes, I met him once. He was wearing a mask made from someone's small clothes and was covered in his own sick. He's completely mad. \n\nThen again, he has a talent. He knows this city better than anyone—and he's quiet. Very quiet.

Your face …. You believe him, don't you? Perfect.

I admit, it makes sense. The Dragonfires are the key to ejecting the Daedra permanently. If Molag Bal could extinguish them forever, that would be very, very bad. 

We'll have to keep digging.
I assumed as much. That's why I decided to appear in this manner. That way we can talk freely, without one of us deciding to be gauche and draw a weapon or otherwise behave badly.

Oh, but we already have, don't you see?\n\nThe clan chiefs have gathered and the moot is about to start. Soon the news will spread that Solgra is behind the Vosh Rakh. Everything's in place, just as I have foreseen. You have failed, outsider.

The time for endless talk and debate is over. These cowards who call themselves chiefs will soon be removed and no one will remain to say no to my son. It's for the best.\n\nOh, and I haven't forgotten Bazrag. We'll get him too, in the end.
More than I can say. I will be glad to finish our journey. And glad to put this terrible place behind me.  \n\nI'm sure we all will.
Thank you for helping us. I am anxious to get as far away from this place as I can.  I am sure we all are. We'll stick together and continue on our travels as soon as we can.
Good. The Knights of the Dragon will have no part in King Joile's treachery.\n\nCome, we must collect the bodies. They deserve a better rest than this.
Why? Why does the sun rise and fall each day? Why do the spring rains eventually free us from winter's icy grip?\n\nThe king is angry. And like any force of nature, he refuses to be denied.
Well, yes. Of course something did. Go and speak to the king, outsider. I prefer that you hear the news from his mouth instead of from mine.
Haven't you and your friends caused us enough trouble already?\n\nAll right, if you get me my inn back, I'll try to forget that any of this ever happened. So, how can I help?

Never seen her before. I make it a habit to get to know all of the guards and soldiers who come to the inn to unwind.\n\nFrom the look on her face, she hasn't unwound since the king was a cub tied to the Forge-Mother's apron.
I wouldn't want to disparage the captain. She works for Lord Ethian's father and most of the ships belong to him. Because of the ambassador's mission, they wanted to make an impression.\n\nNobles.
Sure. I enjoy being crushed under rubble as I slowly sink into icy water. \n\nWhat kind of question is that? And just who in Oblivion are you?

He's one of Captain Henrisa's lackeys, a shifty-eyed mage who was always skulking around. Didn't like him.\n\nLook, help me out. I don't think I can swing a sword right now, but I need to make sure the ambassador is all right.
I was running messages … for the cute Wood Elf and the grumpy Orc ….\n\nWhen I returned … the soldiers rushed in … stabbed me.
They never saw it coming. The soldiers grabbed the Orc chief and the Elf … took them away. By the order of … the king.\n\nI guess I was … just in the way.
So proud. So sure. So certain that you do the right thing. But you defy the will of Trinimac and try to stop the inevitable by warning my son.\n\nIn short, you have begun to annoy me.

No, we're done here. You think you know so much, but you're just grasping at straws.\n\nThe plan proceeds and you can't stop it. The Orsimer will rally as one under the banner of King Kurog. I have foreseen it!

The Vosh Rakh do exactly what they've been ordered to do. They will eliminate every obstacle that threatens my son. It's time to remove the clan chiefs so that Orsimer unification can begin.\n\nThis is about survival! Surely, you can understand that?

I admit I never trusted you. But you've helped our people. You deserved better than to fall to the forge-mother.\n\nI dragged you back here before the Vosh Rakh arrived, healed you as best I could. Now get out of here before the soldiers find you.

Asking questions and getting the lay of the land, I like that. Shows you're as professional and as dedicated as we are. And smart, too.\n\nGo ahead. Ask your questions. The sooner we get this done, the sooner we all get paid.

The chiefs have already headed to the moot and Vosh Rakh guard the keep. If you want to survive, you have to leave now.\n\nI don't want to fight you, but if you decide to go after the king … well, I am sworn to protect my beloved.

My beloved does what he must to unite our people. You know this is true. You've seen it. The clan chiefs refuse to listen.\n\nIf Kurog fails, the Orsimer will never be anything more than the abused and scorned wretches the other races imagine us to be.

Nothing special, as far as I can tell. Nothing other than the gold his mother is paying us to find him and bring him back home.\n\nCome to think of it, that makes him doubly special in my mind. I don't know about you, but I enjoy getting paid.

Not sure. I slipped inside before Kurog locked down the keep. Found you lying on the floor and dragged you back here before all the Vosh Rakh showed up.\n\nI thought they were Orsimer soldiers at first, but those are definitely the cultists up there.

You go ahead. Just watch yourself. Those Vosh Rakh maniacs aren't going to stand aside and let you march in there.\n\nI'll go gather some other allies in the city. If you run into problems, meet me outside the keep and we'll figure something else out.
They headed for the moot. It's going to start soon.\n\nKurog and the chiefs don't realize what they're walking into. It's going to be a blood bath!
Ah. The poor girl is still young. She can't accept that our husband fell in fair combat.\n\nThere is no conspiracy, just a good man who fell before his time. Tell her that.
You rummaged through my tent? If you weren't blood-kin, I could gut you for that.\n\nNot that my things are your business, but it's a book of battle poetry. I read them occasionally.

His sword jangles—lots of little buckles on the scabbard—but mine is quieter than a thief. I bet he didn't want to wake me, the morning he was injured.\n\nDamned fool, trying to prove himself. Didn't want his hunt-wife along to fight the giant.
You better not be pulling my tusk, outsider.\n\nI've known Kurog for a long time. We may disagree on certain issues, but he's always had the best interests of our people in mind. This makes no sense!

There are still some people here in the city that I can count on.\n\nNow do whatever you have to and get to the moot. If you run into any problems, find me outside the keep and we'll figure something out.

Then there isn't any time to waste. Give me the key and head for the throne room. There's a passage in there that will lead you directly to the moot.\n\nI'll get Eveli to safety and try to gather some additional help.

Yes, he's the Orc opposite Shinji—which is why this can't be <<1>>'s resting place.\n\nThough venerated by Wrothgar's Orcs, Baloth was little more than an opportunist. Why would an Orc mercenary's tomb honor the Redguard who "murdered" him?
Then listen well and I'll tell you about the greatness of Trinimac! His eyes see far and wide, and tremendous is his power!
Yes … yes, I'm all right. Just need to catch my breath. You have my deepest, deepest thanks. I only wish more could have been saved.
It's what they preach in Orsinium, isn't it? Always wise to keep in touch with the king's politics.\n\nBetter to know the old myths than sound like a bumpkin.
Let me see that ….\n\nYou can get to the moot through the temple? I had no idea that path even existed! But they sent soldiers after Solgra. That's bad. We need a new plan and we need it now.

You go ahead to the temple and check on the high priestess.\n\nEveli and I have one more place where we can look for some help. If we're successful, it might make the path to the moot slightly less complicated.

I'm well aware of that! I'm counting on the start of the moot to keep them distracted, but we won't take any unnecessary chances.\n\nWe need Solgra alive to tell her side of the story. Then we can get to the moot and save the chiefs.
That's my hunting blade! <<1>> must have grabbed it on his way to the giant camp.\n\nCareful how you handle it. The blade has a paralyzing poison on the edge.
You see? A cultist chants to her Daedric Prince, just like the stories.\n\nI bet she was cavorting in the moonlight. Perhaps she was chanting to ensorcell <<1>>!
I name you my champion. Go to <<1>> and demand the blood price. She must pay in gold or blood.\n\nReturn to me when the debt is paid. Then I can put my husband to rest.
This is enough evidence for me to demand the blood price from <<1>>.

We are truly blessed to have been born as Orcs.\n\nOur god is a warrior god who brings unity and civilization to us all! Before Malacath was, Trinimac is! Who needs blood and fury when a true god grants us courage and lifts us on high?

Everyone craves the truth of Trinimac, no matter their race or creed!\n\nTrinimac is a warrior god who stands for unity and civilization. Before Malacath was, Trinimac is! Who needs blood and fury when a true god grants us courage and lifts us on high?
May Trinimac's light ignite the fire of your spirit! Your enemies will flee at the sight of his holy might!
Shatul will survive. A new hunt-wife will take my place.\n\nAs a girl, my dreams were of hunts in distant lands. Now, as a widow, they shall be reality.

I don't take charity … but this isn't charity. It will help <<1>> get past our husband's death. It will bring Shatul together.\n\nTell her I will pay her the blood price directly. Then, perhaps we can speak of what both of us lost.

Solgra … Solgra says the arrow just missed my heart. Never knew an Orc who could shoot worth a damn, anyway. Well, except for those catapulteers back at Frostbreak. They were pretty amazing.\n\nSo, be honest with me. Am I going to be all right?

I used to think he was a good ruler. Strong, honorable. But he's a menace. He's let himself become more important than his ideas.\n\nSo go and do what you do so well. I'll wait right here. Recovering. I want to be ready for the next adventure.
That bad, huh? Well, don't worry about me. You've got more important things to deal with. Like the clan chiefs.\n\nYou're going to go after Kurog, aren't you?
Ha, is he now? I've seen his type before. Give it a few weeks until he learns why echatere don't make good pets, and he'll come limping back with it in tow.
