Well, maybe, if there's actually a hidden message and it's not just some weird poem.\n\nI have a friend, sort of. Name's Kalina. She just arrived in the Mages Guild and she's the smartest person I know. She could help you. Probably.

Replace the blade of the weakest, as I said. When the victor leaves the dueling chamber, enter the sacred shrine and kill him. Or her.\n\nIf you go through with this … <<1>> deserves a clean death. Malacath favor the victor.

I lost a bet with Talviah and now I owe him a traditional Valenwood dinner. You know, the kind Wood Elves like to eat.\n\nI can't wait to see the look on his face when he realizes what kind of meat he's eating. It'll be priceless!

Yeah, I guess I just needed to get out of the city. I was seriously depressed when I wound up on the king's most wanted list.\n\nThanks for pushing me. Infiltrating a cult is certainly better than hiding in a hole someplace.

Right, sorry. Scary cult needs to be infiltrated. Wouldn't want to try to get you to crack a smile or anything.\n\nIt just feels good to be doing something and not hiding from the king's guard, that's all.

Well, with all the runners we spotted, we know we're in the right place. We just need a way to get inside without being noticed.\n\nYou know, we might be able to do something with those higher-ranking cultists in the fancy masks.

Well, a few of the masked cultists passed this way a little while ago. Then we heard a large commotion over there to the west.\n\nI can't be sure, mind you, but I think those Vosh Rakh might have … well, they could have walked into an … um ….

Talviah thinks … well … he thinks that the group might have walked into an echatere mating ritual. The sounds from the west, the screams. Y'ffre's bow, the noise was horrible!\n\nThen it got real quiet. I don't think it went well for the cultists.
Just don't get too close to those echateres. I heard they become extremely violent when anything interrupts their … frolicking.\n\nWe'll look around on our own and meet you inside. Good luck!

It's time to assemble the Great Moot. I want you to visit the clan chiefs that still haven't come around to our way of thinking. Talk some sense into them.\n\nYou need to get to them before Bazrag poisons the well and turns them against me.

More? What more is there to say? They refuse my every overture and laugh at my authority! We need to convince them of the veracity of my grand vision.\n\nOh, very well. What specifically do you want to know?

The stone workers? Tumnosh operates the Graystone Quarry, the primary source of building materials for Orsinium.\n\nI'm not sure what Chief Ramash is up to, but he's fallen behind on his shipments. Maybe you can help get the quarry back on track.

The Morkul clan is famous for its smiths. Some of the finest arms and armor has come out of their forges.\n\nI've been trying to get them to send experts to help us build the city, but Chief Abzug continues to hem and haw. Family troubles, he says.

One of the best clans as far as food production and livestock is concerned. Expert hunters and farmers, every one of them.\n\nChief Ogzor promised to send herds of echateres to help feed the city, but we haven't seen so much as a bushel of apples yet.
That is correct. Can I help you with something? I'm a little busy at the moment.
Ugh, not again. Can we get this sorted out quickly? If it's rats again, the fees for exterminators are exorbitant in this town.
I don't think that's entirely appropriate. We don't know each other and I am really very busy.\n\nExcuse me.

Well, the illusion seems to be holding up, at least for now. Hopefully it won't fail at a particularly critical moment.\n\nAnyway, I think we should split up and cover more ground. That's the best way to find what we're looking for quickly.

This place is enormous! Besides, you never put all your acorns in one basket.\n\nWe need to find out what the Vosh Rakh are up to and fast. Flies and I will look around out here, while you and Tal see what the high-ranking cultists are meeting about.
Ha, ha. Tease me all you want, but I know better now. Sort of.\n\nAs long as you're here though, I know you'll watch out for us. You're surprisingly good at that sort of thing.

Good idea! And let's not to take too long. Lives are depending on us!\n\nAnd speaking of lives, make sure Tal stays safe, will you? He isn't as experienced as we are. I'm afraid his wide-eyed enthusiasm is going to get him injured.

It's the whole reason I came to Wrothgar. To show that I can fight. To prove myself to my family, to everyone. I'm more than just a scribe destined to spend his whole life behind a desk.\n\nThis … this will show everyone what I'm capable of.

Oh, that's where you're wrong, my friend. I come from a long line of warriors and mages, but most of my family considers me to be the tarnished fruit on the tree of golden pears. It's time for me to show them who I really am.

I knew you'd understand! When your father is a royal mage, your mother is one of the queen's guard, and your sister almost single-handedly won the Battle of Sunken Spire, well … let's just say I've got a lot to live up to.\n\nNow let's go do this!

Ancient texts and relics mostly. I'm apprenticed to the famous treasure hunter, Narsis Dren, but he treats me more like a glorified scribe than a partner!\n\nSo, while he's inside exploring the barrow, I'm out here … waiting to transcribe his notes.

As a matter of fact, I've had it up to here with Dren! I've decided to strike out on my own. With items such as these, I can do some real research.\n\nVisit me in the museum in Orsinium. If these possess any historical value, I'll pay a finder's fee!

Let me see … well, it's certainly ancient, but it's hardly interesting. Good for scholars, perhaps, but not adventurers such as you and I.\n\nMy assistant Berrice is a stickler for details and historical accuracy. She loves dull things like that.
Shh! Not so loud.\n\nIf you found my note, you know <<1>> betrayed me. I didn't deserve the blame for his plan—I didn't want to touch that ugly thing. <<1>> should rot for what he did to me.
Oh.\n\nWell, he'd be alive if he hadn't tried to frame me. The whole thing was his idea.

The mission before us requires the best the Vosh Rakh has to offer. This trial will determine those select few through a test of wits, speed, and strength.\n\nTrinimac himself will winnow the iron from the ore.

The last part of the trial requires that you obey the council without question. But you won't have to deal with that until the very end.\n\nRemember, if you succeed, you will be named a chosen of Trinimac and allowed to partake in the sacred mission.

Oh, the details are the purview of those who complete the mission. But Trinimac thanks you for volunteering, no matter how things turn out.\n\nIf you succeed and do as the council demands, all will be revealed. Fail, and death is your only reward.
My father always says, "the rabble face death every day, while the brave always find a way to defeat it." \n\nI've never been exactly sure what he meant, but I think I know now.
Yes. Yes, I do. This is what I came here for. This is my time to shine.\n\nBesides, you're here with me. We'll watch each other's back and come out victorious in the end.
We did, didn't we? I'm pretty sure that was because the Vosh Rakh were busy trying to deal with you.\n\nI'm beginning to understand why Eveli admires you so much.

The council, right. I wonder what they're going to ask us to do as our final test?\n\nWhatever it is, we can't hesitate. Lives are depending on us. We need to find out as much as we can about this "sacred" mission they keep going on and on about.

What? You think Malacath's Code only allows for death or exile?\n\nSometimes you want individuals to pay for their crimes, but you also want to keep them around, just in case. Besides, running a prison has turned out to be a lucrative business.

Any clan that wants us to take in an undesirable pays us gold for the privilege. And, as I'm sure you noticed, we have a lot of undesirables down here.\n\nBut we can discuss this in more detail later, after we get out of here.
Why … why didn't you protect him? I told you to keep Tal safe! I trusted you!
That's it? That's your answer? He died because we needed him to?\n\nI really wanted to be like you. I looked up to you. But if this is what it means to be a hero, you can count me out.
Orders? You're giving me orders?\n\nFine. Tell me what you learned and I'll be happy to put this awful place behind me. This awful place … and you.
Is that supposed to scare me?
Orders? You're giving me orders?\n\nFine. Tell me what you learned so I can get out of here. I want to make sure nobody else has to die today.
I don't know exactly what happened in there and I don't want to know. Not right now. I just can't handle it.\n\nJust tell me what I need to know so I can go.
I'm not scared. At all.
All right, that's … that's enough. You can go now.
Hail Sithis?\n\nNo? Forget I said anything.
Please, I didn't know! I would never insult the Dark Brotherhood. I spoke out of turn!
This is wonderful!\n\nBut words alone mean nothing. Without the stolen goods, <<1>> remains imprisoned.
Let me see the journal … ah! There, you see? He buried the stolen goods!\n\nLook for them near his camp. Quickly, before he departs with them!
I'll need to inspect the mug. Once I know it's authentic, we'll have an agreement.\n\nAnd yes, I can inspect it here—everyone is besotted enough they won't notice.

Hmm. Exquisite example of late First Era Orsimer craftsmanship … possibly dating back to Old Orsinium? The envy of any collection.\n\nIf one were into collecting First Era Orsimer trinkets. Which I am not.

That's why I'm sending you after Wrothgar harpies. A thousand generations of inbreeding long since removed any glimmer of intelligence from their minds. The ones here are really giant birds.\n\nDelicious, tasty birds.

All by himself? Are you sure he can handle that? What am I saying, of course you're sure!\n\nWe managed to find out that the attack on the temple was a ruse perpetrated by the Vosh Rakh. That was right before our amulets stopped working.

Yeah, I was suddenly as naked as an ash tree that had lost its last leaf of the season. Good thing we stashed our gear nearby!\n\nAnyway, the temple attack was all to place the blame on Bazrag. The chief is innocent. I didn't help a murderer!

That's something, but not enough to provide the edge we were hoping for.\n\nWe'll just have to be careful. Anyone could be working with the Vosh Rakh. I don't know about you, but all this intrigue is starting to make my head hurt.

Impossible. As I said before, I am of the Agra Crun. The Blood Shields serve Malacath in our own way, but our hands must never touch the sacred Words. This is why you were needed. This is why you had to pass the tests.

One does not become Agra Crun. One is or is not. I was raised by the faith, trained since my birth to complete the tasks Malacath wishes of me. \n\nIt is not a path you will ever walk, but today you have set yourself on a road of equal glory.

Though the sacred Words must be moved as they have so often before, this shrine is still ancient and sacred. It must be cleansed and secured. New Keepers must be appointed. I will see to that. \n\nYour task lies on the road to Orsinium. Travel safely.

It is not my place to know. The Furious One often selects champions of considerable grit and determination to serve as his avengers. He has taken notice of you. Perhaps you will never truly know until you find yourself at his feet in the Ashpit.

His shield-wife, yes. Does that surprise you? All of the clan chiefs have strong and devoted partners. My husband has numerous wives, but when it comes to the safety of Fharun, he turns to me.\n\nNow tell me, please. Is Bazrag all right?

What? You looking to court her or something?\n\nIf you're so enthralled by Captain What's Her Name, I heard her tell a soldier she'd be by the ramparts near the stables. But she's a cold fish, mark my words. You'd do better fishing in a different pond.

That was the first thing they confiscated. It was Sergeant Vulmon. I know him. He's one of our regulars. Usually friendly, leaves an extra gold piece now and again.\n\nHe's stationed near the King's Cornerclub. But he won't give up that key.
That's between you and him. I'll have no part in that. I'm no criminal, despite how all this looks.

To be honest, I was kind of busy trying to not get arrested at the time.\n\nWait a moment! Yes, I know. He said something about the bath house before he left. Anyway, I hope that's where he went. He'll need to soak for hours to get rid of that smell!

Well, there might be a way. There was a merchant here earlier. Smelled like fermented echatere cheese that was left out in the sun. But he was awfully friendly with the soldiers.\n\nMaybe a little too friendly, if you catch my meaning.
I'm awfully friendly with everybody! Anything else is bad business.\n\nNow, since you did a good turn for me and didn't report me to the authorities, I thought I'd do a good turn for you.
A person in my line of business, well, we hear things. Secret things. Dangerous things. Things concerning clan chiefs and fanatics with a little too much holiness in their hair.

By giving you this key, my friend.\n\nYou'd be surprised at how much you can accomplish by slipping some gold into a purse. Even a soldier's purse. So, go help your friends. With this, I consider my debt to you paid in full.

You need to get into the inn. I can get you into the inn. Tit for tat, as the Bretons say.\n\nNow, I don't know exactly what's going on, and I don't want to know. But I don't like those new soldiers. There's something not right about them.

I don't really know. Most giants are surly enough. <<1>>, we've come to learn, is a mean drunk.\n\nOnce, he tore off an echatere's crest and tossed it across the snow like he was skipping a stone. Heard they found it in Fharun Stronghold.

You're right. Only made it a hundred paces before it slammed into a tree.\n\nTook half a day to saw that bloody crest out. We tried to reattach the thing, but the echatere wanted nothing to do with it.

Most of Shatul's warriors died in the first Winterborn raids.\n\nWithout a good contender for chief, neighbor will fight neighbor for a title they can't hope to hold. We can't afford that, after losing so much to the raiders.
Truth is, everyone's afraid. The chief kept this clan together for two decades. A strong contender will quiet their nerves.\n\nSlaying the giant who killed <<1>>? None will doubt my strength.

You want me to quote the Code of Malacath? Go on about vengeance and grudges?\n\nI've had my fill of that. Something I learned around all these echatere—the ones who bray the loudest never lead the pack.
Ha! Exactly.\n\nOh, you were asking? Well, I never challenged <<1>>, even though people thought I could take him. But how could I kill my friend?
Well … of course. That's how it's always been.\n\nHmm. Never thought about it any other way. I suppose it's possible. Still, I wouldn't wish that on any woman.
Contenders for chief fight it out in the Bloody Knoll. It's our shrine to Malacath, up on the hill. He who emerges is chief—simple as that.

Someone whose actions speak loudest. Someone like <<1>>.\n\nYes, I want to be chief. I spent two decades watching this clan prosper under his guidance. I'm not "relaxed," I just wasn't willing to kill my best friend for his clan.
She'd face constant challenge. Whispers behind her back, bitter sulking, the petty disrespects you expect from children—but all from grown Orcs who should know better.
We travel where the echatere travel. Can't say it'd be good if the chief was stuck here defending him— herself, I mean.\n\nI wouldn't want to put my clan through that. But that's me.
What? No, of course not. I get paid to tell people exactly what I told you.\n\nAfter that, well, I've done my duty. They don't pay me enough to tangle with someone like you.
Suit yourself. Just let them know that I said my words and gave you fair warning.\n\nI might not be a true believer, but I want to keep my job, if it's all the same to you.

I'm no guard. I'm a watchman. It's a dull job, but it's a living.\n\nThose soldiers up there? They're a strange bunch. Never knew soldiers who were so religious. Everything's Trinimac this and Trinimac that. I just want to finish my shift in peace.

Huh. Sometimes I ask myself the same question.\n\nI'm a contract broker for the Dragonstar Caravan Company. We've been drowning in contracts ever since Kurog started his little home decorating project. We just don't have the manpower to keep up.
Ha! No, no. I've got enough greedy hooligans on my payroll. This is strictly contract work. We give you a job and take a cut on the back-end. Simple as that.

Yeah. We're a "property protection consortium." Fancy way of saying we're a bunch of grunts and rowdies that knock heads together for money. Mostly stick to caravan escort, but we'll take just about any job as long as it pays well.
You are the chief. And I have no standing to disobey. Not anymore.\n\nI will not pay the blood price. If you order me to leave, I shall depart.
Oh, a bit of this and that. Minor healing spells, basic transmutation, a sprinkling of mysticism. Oh—and fire juggling! Would you like to see?
Well, I … that's quite rude!\n\nWould a transmutation spell tickle your fancy? Perhaps I could turn you into a toad! You already act the part.
Wonderful! Stand back!
That sounds serious. But this is a time for celebration! The next age of the Orsimer people begins today!

You dare to question my actions? To imply that I don't have the best interests of my people in mind?\n\nIf you must know, we received word of the location of the traitors. I sent my soldiers to capture them for interrogation.
Really? In danger you say? And you came upon this knowledge how?\n\nIf you're frightened by a few idle rumors in the streets ….

Keep your voice down! Do you know how easy it is to panic a clan chief? We just got them here, so let's not scare them away needlessly.\n\nMeet me down in the dining hall and we can continue this discussion in private.

More questions? You're beginning to try my patience. \n\nBut let's not talk about such matters in front of the clan chiefs. Meet me down in the dining hall and we can continue this discussion in private.
What? How dare you spread such false accusations! Has Bazrag filled your head with more of his Malacath lies?\n\nI won't hear such things, not on the verge of my greatest victory!
Stop me? I don't think so!\n\nThe Orsimer will rally as one under King Kurog's banner! I have foreseen it!
My beloved believes that this is the only way to accomplish his dream.\n\nAs his shield-wife, I will support him. Just as I always have.
I knew something was wrong. I could feel it in the tip of my tail.\n\nYou better talk to Eveli. She's going to want to know what happened. This is a sad day. A very sad day.

It worked, didn't it. The chiefs have gathered for the moot and everything proceeds as planned.\n\nAs long as you take Bazrag with you when you leave, there won't be any reason for more bloodshed. He served his purpose. Just like you.

No. He hoped that the chiefs would come to believe in his vision, to see the future he imagined just as he did.\n\nHe never wanted it to come to this. But a king must always do the right thing for his people.

Why would they do that? They'll see a king who fought the fanatical Vosh Rakh, who tried desperately to save the chiefs against overwhelming odds.\n\nWhen the dust clears, they will love him and stand united beneath his banner for all the world to see.

Kurog is my beloved and I swore an oath to support and protect him.\n\nBesides, I believe in the king's dream. I believe in a united Orsimer nation. It's the best way for us to take our place as equals among the other races.

My beloved doesn't hate Bazrag. They were friends once. Almost brothers. If anything, he's disappointed in the chief.\n\nBut Bazrag challenges the king. He needs to be removed from the field of battle before he has a chance to disrupt the plan.

Oh, the clan chiefs are far from innocent. And their deaths will serve a higher purpose. They represent a worthy sacrifice.\n\nNow, take your friends and go. This isn't your concern any longer. Let my beloved finish what he began. Please.
Only how little I knew about my own people! Clans appear and disappear as time passes, yet each contributes in some significant way to our culture.\n\nFor example, take Morkul clan.

Morkul clan can be traced back to Old Orsinium—beyond that, actually. They disappeared for centuries after the fall of Old Orsinium, then once more revealed themselves to Tamriel.\n\nI have asked where they went, but it is apparently a clan secret!
You've heard of the lost home of Morkul clan? It took me years to learn of the place!
That's—a bit underwhelming.\n\n"Come to the lost home of Morkul clan. Spiders for all!" It just … it doesn't roll off the tongue.
<<1>> refused to be traded like the choicest pick of echatere. She chose exile rather than marry me.\n\nA month later, raiders from the Reach wiped out my whole clan. <<2>> took me in.

No—I've always respected how <<1>> held her ground. And I wasn't too keen on the match.\n\nI'd known her since she was a child, so going from "Uncle <<2>>" to "husband?" We call that a "Valenwood marriage." But don't let a Wood Orc hear you say it.

Don't really know—Shatul tries not to talk about its exiles. <<1>> forbade anyone from speaking of her. I think he blamed himself for pushing her away.\n\nAfter her mother died, <<2>> and her father were always at odds. It was inevitable.

It was my own fault. I was more full of pride than sense back then. Shatul warned us of Reachmen they'd seen, prowling through the hills.\n\nI thought <<1>> was trying to make up for <<2>> running off. Didn't pay it much mind. Then my clan was gone.
All right.\n\nLet's finish this so I can get back to the clan.
I lived in Orsinium for years. Sometimes I forget Shatul is home.\n\nJust find the <<z:1>>. It's cold out here.
He'd have tried to kill you.\n\nBut you slew <<1>>. I expect <<2>> would now be dead.
<<1>> and <<2>> are the only clear contenders for chief. They must enter the Bloody Knoll and duel beneath the stern gaze of Malacath.\n\nThe one who emerges shall be the new chief of Shatul.
You? But … hmm.\n\nIt's not a possibility. The clan will never accept an outsider unless there is no better option.

It was my son's favorite food. His hearth-wife—she has dozens of recipes. He loved them all.\n\nHe won't be able to taste it. His mind, you see … there's nothing left of him. But I'll mix it into the poison so he enjoys it one last time.
The poison I shall feed the husk that remains of his body.
Yes. Yes, it is.
No. It is me. Murdering my own son.
There is no shame in that. You are not an Orc. You are not of Shatul.\n\nBut you are blood-kin to our clan. Know that it must be done, and that only I can carry this burden. Shatul must survive.

An Orc should understand. Malacath walks in your shadow and burns in your blood. Survival is what our people must understand.\n\nBut you are blood-kin to our clan. This unpleasant task falls to me, and only to me. Shatul must survive.
I doubt that. An Orc of Shatul would truly understand. You are neither.\n\nYet you are blood-kin to our clan, and your words give me the strength to do what must be done. Shatul must survive.

Do you, truly? Were you a stronghold Orc, raised behind thick walls? Can you understand why I alone must carry this burden?\n\nForgive me. You are blood-kin to our clan. The only thing you must understand is that Shatul must survive.
Shatul must survive.\n\nBefore a new chief is chosen, the old chief must die. By the time <<1>> and <<2>> reach the Bloody Knoll, the poison will finish its work. Malacath will take no offense.
<<1>>. Exiled daughter of <<2>>.\n\nSoon, the new chief of Shatul.
I … what? What did you know?
I see. You seem to know much about me, <<1>>.\n\nBut not everything.
Yes, that's … you're right. How did you know it was me?

I knew it, the tuskless bastard! He plans to kill the chiefs and unite the clans over the corpses of our people. Despicable!\n\nThey're holding the moot in the mountains overlooking the city. A path beyond the throne room leads right to it.

Before Kurog started all this, I honestly never gave it a lot of thought. It certainly goes against all our most-cherished traditions.\n\nI have to admit, there are advantages to a united Orc nation. But not this way. Not this way.

I assume that he and Alga had it in mind, just in case. I can't help wonder if this is my fault, though. I should have talked to Kurog, listened to what he had to say.\n\nInstead, I turned away. I refused to hear him out. And now look where we are.
Who can say? I want to believe that Kurog started out with the best intentions. He thought the death of Ice-Heart would unite us under his banner.\n\nBut the clan chiefs, they're a stubborn lot.

People believe whatever's right in front of them. By throwing me in my own prison and making sure no one could talk to me, Kurog could direct the story to his own purposes.\n\nThe fanatics shouted my name, and that's all the people heard.

I have a reputation. Most of the chiefs and their clans respect me. That makes me a threat to Kurog's plans.\n\nBy discrediting me, Alga and her son give the people someone to hate. Then they can remove me from the field of battle without consequence.

Some of Kurog's ideas have merit, I'll give him that. \n\nBut the cost he's willing to bear to see his plans through to fruition? Murder. A city built on fresh graves. And the madness doesn't end there.

We're strong. The strongest people in Tamriel. But there's no way the Orcs could stand against the combined might of eight other nations.\n\nKurog has a different opinion. But he's wrong. He'll march us to glory and all we'll find is mass extinction.

You've seen our so-called king in action. You know him as well as anyone. Perhaps better. What do you think?\n\nHis pride will eventually be his downfall—and the downfall of his newly formed Orc nation.

No, it doesn't. With a united nation at his beck and call, Kurog assembles an army. And then he points that army at our supposed enemies.\n\nSuddenly it's the Orsimer against the world, for good or ill.
<<1>> is a fine warrior … better than my father. But that's the problem—he never challenged my father. He's like an echatere bull that refuses to mate, no matter how much ginger pulp you feed him.
Birds! Catching and selling. It's been a lean season, what with all these strange storms along the coast. But I still turn a healthy profit.\n\nYou're not in the bird business, are you?
We shall build my Maelstrom Army, and make it a force to be feared in every corner of Oblivion!
I am a master of martial knowledge, a sage of combat. I am a piece of my prince, and a reflection of his glory, just as the glory of my conquests will be reflected in him.
It is not a name, it's a title, awarded to me for my achievements in mastering the ways of battle of the Deadlands. \n\nThe secrets of Dagon's warriors are no secret to me.
No, not a thing. But I'll tell you a secret. The stronghold protects the sacred words of Malacath. I fear the words are in terrible danger.
Really! Then may Malacath bless you and keep you safe. Thank you, friend!
She ….\n\nThat foolish girl! We're a traditional clan. Shatul will never accept an exiled woman as chief!
I understand. Not everyone cares to keep the old traditions alive, not with all this talk of Trinimac and the future.\n\nWell, good luck to you, any way.

Sure do. And more importantly, they pay top coin to do it.\n\nI don't judge. We've all got hobbies. Far as I'm concerned, people can dress up like Molag Bal himself if they're willing to pay me this much to make it happen.

There's a path to the moot through the temple? The old tunnels. Of course! That must be what you're talking about.\n\nHere, take this key. It opens the temple library. If there really are old tunnels, the way to access them is probably in there.
Yes, indeed! Wait a moment. It was you, wasn't it? I'd recognize you anywhere! Were you actually able to recover the sacred words?

Just look around! Have you ever seen so many severed heads in one place? It's enough to make an executioner blush. But like I always say, one mer's obsession is another mer's gain. If they want a filthy old werewolf pelt, I'll see that they get it.
How exciting! You must tell me all about it! I hope that one day I can gaze upon the sacred words and gain the wisdom of Malacath.
Good for you! I can't wait to hear all about it. I hope that one day I can read the sacred words of Malacath myself and gain his wisdom.

I know, I had the same idea. But I asked a priest of Malacath who assured me—ogre innards were commonly found in ancient Orc dishes.\n\nDoes this mean the Daedric Prince of Vengeance favors pies? I forgot to ask the priest.

Say what you want about tradition … I think Orcs first turned a <<z:1>> into food because it looks amazing.\n\nAll the rest is hot smoke up the flue. "The preferred meal of <<2>> himself." If you believe the Orsinium vendors—which you shouldn't.

<<Cmz:1>> are delicacies fit for a chief. Look near the old aqueduct, in areas without snow.\n\n<<Cz:2>> is spread around when durzog migrate—it's where they were, not where they are. The seeds catch in their paws, or something.
You're not supposed to eat the <<z:1>>! It draws out the <<z:2>> from the brain mash.\n\nGive it a few moments. I had a similar experience in the kitchen.

It must be a reaction to the <<z:1>>. I assure you, I cleaned them thoroughly before ….\n\nNo, it's the <<z:2>>! I should have broiled before baking. Try running your tongue across your teeth—back and forth, as fast as you can.
It's better you swallowed the tooth whole than tried to chew it. Though … you might pay for it later.\n\nI was worried about the presentation—removing all the teeth makes the stew bowl look sickly.

What a ridiculous notion! Trinimac promotes unity and civilization, not anarchy and violence like those Vosh Rakh fanatics claim.\n\nDare I ask? Tell me, who do we have to thank for this terrible situation?

Ah, the work of an egg merchant is never done. The tastes of Orsinium have become much more refined, you see. I used to be able to make a living on goose eggs alone. Now I've got orders for kwama, and chub loon, and even spider eggs!

There's a path to the moot through the temple? Perhaps via the old tunnels? Yes, that must be the way!\n\nHere, take this key. It opens the library. If there really are old tunnels under the temple, the way to access them is probably in there.

Indeed I do. I make the best of it though. Where there are eggs, there are also women.\n\nI've got to say though, these Orc ladies are a bit chilly. Must be the diet. Nothing but meat and turnips would turn even Dibella sour, am I right?
Yes. Eggs, I mean. They laid eggs.
Oh no, never mind that. Our mutual friend Deechee told me that none of the eggs were ever viable. Thank goodness, eh? That's an ethical debate I'd just as soon avoid.
Comfortable? No! It's an abomination. But it's not for me to judge. Somewhere out there, there's a customer who's desperate to consume a magical person-egg. Who am I to deny them that opportunity?

I've heard about the tunnels under the city. Kurog left the ancient pathways in place and just built the new structures on top.\n\nI suppose if the passage is clear, we can reach the moot using that route.
Then let's go investigate the library! We'll turn over every floor board and bookcase until we find something.

Then we take the fight to Kurog and Alga. If they refuse to yield, then we fight on until either they or us can fight no more!\n\nKurog's reign ends today! So swears Bazrag of Clan Fharun! So swears Bazrag of the Orsimer!

I understand. Even a snow bear pauses to consider the elk before delivering the killing blow.\n\nJust remember what Kurog plans to do to the clan chiefs, to our friends. Even to you. Time is running out, so don't take too long to make up your mind.

This isn't going to be like drinking mead with the Nords. We're talking about defying the king! At best, we'll be branded as king-slayers. At worst, we'll be dead.\n\nThis isn't your fight. Not really. Are you still ready to go through with this?
Mostly deers and bears. Sometimes I'll even go after echateres, but they're usually more trouble than they're worth.

That's what I thought—so I hunted down a cultist of Namira. After a series of beatings, he confirmed the Lady of Decay would strike him with five kinds of pox if he offered up a slice of ventricle pie.\n\nTwo Daedric Princes agree—not cannibalism.
Did Solgra know about the tunnels beneath the temple? Was she able to tell you how we can reach the moot before more people die?

Of course. Even a snow bear pauses to consider the elk before delivering the killing blow.\n\nJust remember what Kurog plans to do to the clan chiefs, to our friends. Even to you. Time isn't on our side, so don't take too long to make up your mind.

This isn't going to be like swimming in mud with the Argonians. We're talking about defying the king! At best, we'll be branded as king-slayers. At worst, we'll be dead.\n\nThis isn't your fight. Not really. Are you still ready to go through with this?

I oversee all the workers, develop the plans for repairs and new construction, order supplies … it keeps me busy! Luckily, we had a good foundation to build upon. The Orcs that came before us certainly made things to last!

We're building atop the ruins of the previous Orsinium that occupied this same spot. There was an older city, but that's located some distance from here.\n\nThe Bretons occupied the place most recently, and they did keep it in good repair.

Major infrastructure work is nearing completion, and the return of the supplies stolen by the Winterborn has really made a difference to our efforts.\n\nWe'd be a bit further along if we hadn't stopped to celebrate when we heard the Ice-Heart was dead.
We're working in the residential district now, making houses safe and sound. And not a moment too soon, what with all this talk of traitors and cultists in our midst!

Echateres? Are you sure? What am I saying, of course you're sure. There's no way to confuse an echatere with a mammoth.\n\nMaybe I'll just keep hunting. The last time I tried to catch an echatere, I found out it was hunting me.
Really? I love venison! But you need to sneak up on those critters carefully. I got kicked right in the tusk by a deer once. Hurt like you wouldn't believe.

Bears, you say? Did you notice if one of them was Norgim by any chance? She's a monster, that one. Maybe a hunt-wife would go after a bear like that, but not me.\n\nMaybe I'll look for a few rabbits, just to be on the safe side.
I think so. It happened so fast.\n\nSpeaking of which, did you see what happened?

Yes, the final touches are being added even as we speak. Repairs to the market stalls and main gates will make Orsinium a shining example of what a city should be.\n\nI just wish the king were still alive to see his dream come to fruition.
Probably a good thing you weren't around when it happened. Probably would have gotten injured, just like me.\n\nWell, thanks for checking on me. I'll be all right.

Is that what that thing was? It certainly scared the tartar off my tusks, I'll tell you!\n\nWell, I was able to get out of the way before any serious harm was done. Thanks for checking on me. I'll be all right.

I guess you could say that. I got here before the soldiers arrived, if that's what you mean.\n\nHad just enough time to warn the chief and then all of Oblivion broke lose. But we handled it. We handled it real good!
They will go to The Ashen Forge, of course, to be honed and tempered—made whole in the cleansing fires of Malacath.
What? Of course it is. Every Orc, deep in their heart, yearns to be thrust into Malacath's coals. To see their grudges and fury folded and hardened on the Anvil of Ash!
It is difficult for outsiders to grasp. The Orc faith … the true Orc faith, offers few comforts, but ample glory. Those spirits you liberate will be glad to enter Malacath's realm, I assure you.

Trinimac? Don't tell me you're one of those misguided Elf-worshipers. No, we don't have a seat at the Elf-gods' table. Don't want one either.\n\nYou seem like a good Orc. You've got a strong heart. Don't be taken in by those charlatans.

I am glad to hear you say that. Too many of our brethren have strayed from the Code—taken in by those blasphemers in Orsinium. It does my heart good to know that Thukhozod's slaves will be freed by an Orc such as you.
It's like a <<z:1>>, but tastier. Only grows in these parts.
Only an Orc can become chief of Shatul. Or of any Orc clan. It's … I can't say it any simpler than that.
You? But … no Orc woman has ever led Shatul. Or any Orc clan.\n\nThere's no possibility. Such a radical idea would drive the clan apart.

The real <<1>> has a squeak in his voice. One day he paid Morkul's forge-wife to make him sound "like an ogre." He always wore the helmet, everywhere he went.\n\nIt still smells like sweaty breeches and onions. I cleaned it three times. Nothing worked.

Some won't. They may challenge me, and I'll have to kill them.\n\nBut when any other clan clucks about the Code of Malacath, Shatul will band together, as we always do. We'll triple their rate on echatere—a built in blood price for the disrespect.
I think we'll get rich off the Malacath zealots. That will make the king happy.\n\nAnd if he asks me to be his chief-wife, I'll decline. But I'll offer him the chance to be my king-husband.

<<1>>'s heart was never in the match. But refusing would've led to a feud.\n\nFather was insufferable. "A chief's daughter must bear the clan's burdens." But children are a burden I don't ever plan to bear—not for the clan, not for anyone.

I … I haven't thought about that in years. He was always Uncle <<1>> to me. Taught me how to play Chop … always called me "little one," even when I was nearly his height.\n\nI looked up to him. Then father insisted I become his hunt-wife.

Look everywhere! It'll probably be something odd or out of place, like those switches over there.\n\nBut this is a library. Maybe one of these dusty old tomes can help. There's bound to be a book that talks about the construction of the temple in here.
Gladly.
Good, good. Although, there is a problem. Neither contender is good for Shatul.\n\n<<1>> has weakness in his heart. <<2>> is weak of mind. Something must be done.
You spent time with both contenders. Perhaps you see a strength in one that I do not.\n\nI must prepare the clan for its new chief. As I do so, I ask that you help Shatul survive.

Take this ritual blade. It has a subtle flaw at its core, just like <<1>> and <<2>>. Replace the blade of the contender you judge to be weakest.\n\nIf the blade fails, yet the contender bests his opponent, he proves himself worthy of leading Shatul.
Then he dies.\n\nGo, quickly. You must reach the Bloody Knoll before <<1>> and <<2>> reach the dueling chamber.
There is a separate entrance to the Bloody Knoll, away from the sacred chambers. I want you to go there and fix the duel before it starts.
Fair? I just watched my son die. None of this is fair!\n\nThe flawed blade is a test. A weak contender who survives despite this setback deserves to become chief of Shatul.
When the blade fails, the weakest contender will most assuredly die. If they … if she ….\n\nGo, there is little time. Malacath favor the victor.
I don't know … poison, ritual sacrifice, time when she slipped away from the clan. Anything that connects her to Boethiah.

Ah yes, the cleansing totem. It appears to be nothing more than a wooden charm, I know. But rest assured, it is imbued with tremendous power.\n\nAnd once its power is expended, it makes a lovely accent to any table centerpiece!

No, no. It's just a simple matter of holding it above the corruption and concentrating.\n\nIt's vital that you concentrate on cleansing the corruption, though. If you're daydreaming about puppies, it will probably just make a weird sound.
Yes, something between a belch and a chipmunk chirp. I'm still working out the kinks. Just focus on cleansing the corruption, all right?
Yeah? How did you know?
No, walker. The pain is still too near. This one needs more drink …. Yes, another drink and I will tell you my tale.
It is true, you are the chief. But you had no right to go through my things.\n\nIt's a book of battle poetry. It was a gift from <<1>>.

Oh, that. I wasn't singing, I was chanting. I was out hunting when I nearly stumbled into a mammoth.\n\nThey have poor night vision. If you chant the way the giants do, sometimes you can fool them into thinking you're not a threat.
We're a clan that travels the range. It gets boring at night. Sometimes we sing to keep up our spirits.
Well, I don't! What is the point of your questions?
Well … I don't know why he would. But you're right, his own blade was still in the tent.\n\nThat means nothing. She's still a Boethiah cultist, I'm sure of it.
What does <<1>> care about Orsinium politics? The book proves her guilt!\n\nWhat about <<2>>? He heard something the night before my husband was struck down.

We've all seen her do that before—of course she would say that! Followers of Boethiah live only to deceive. It was Boethiah worship, no matter what she says.\n\n<<1>> deserves justice. Something must be done about <<2>>!

I've accepted our roles, if that's what you mean. With the crown comes new responsibilities, new duties. First and foremost, my husband needs an heir, and I'm going to make sure he gets one.\n\nIf he thinks being the king is difficult, just you wait!

Galvin still agonizes over every job we accept, making sure it hits his high code of honor.\n\nAs for the Remly brothers, they're as useless as ever. You should have seen their last invention. Almost took out my eye!

I had hoped to run into my old friend Darien here. This is just the sort of situation he loved to find himself in.\n\nI know something happened in Coldharbour, but I can't believe he's dead. He's out there, somewhere. I can feel it in my bones.
I have a couple of ideas. Not ready to share them yet, but I won't stop until I find him in some brothel in Abah's Landing or at a tavern in Murkmire.

I survived battles with the Winterborn. Helped take down a tyrant king and a horrible cult. And here I am, drinking and talking to you.\n\nI think that's somewhat impressive, if I do say so myself. Perhaps I'll finally get the respect I deserve.
Indeed it is. Though, I am far away, at the very edge of the world.
So you did. And I have gone on to the next great adventure.
I bring you a warning, Champion. Oblivion stirs. Great and terrible machinations have begun. Once again, Tamriel is in danger. You have a part to play in the events to come.
A great war is coming. A war between the forces of Oblivion. The Daedric Princes are choosing sides. The great deceiver, the sower of discord, and the patron of darkness plot a great deception.
Be ready. Watch for signs. The war shall begin when the gates of Sotha Sil's lost city are re-opened. So the scrolls portend. So shall it be.
I cannot aid you in the coming battle. My time in this world is at an end. I must take my place in the Immortal Plane. Farewell, old friend. We will not speak again.

King Bazrag informed me that he plans to return the temple to its original purpose as a shrine to Malacath. I'm not sure what that mean for the Trinimac priesthood, but he has requested that I serve as a royal advisor.
I … I  have something I want to try first. Something that will help repay the Orcs for my … indiscretion.
Upset? No. Disappointed? Most definitely.\n\nI can't dispute the fact that Trinimac fanatics caused so much trouble. If returning the city to Malacath makes up for that, who am I to argue?

I'm a priest of Trinimac and I always will be, whether we have a temple of our own or not.\n\nThese people, they've become my family. I'll stay and help the new king for as long as he needs me. And if I happen to give a few sermons, who can blame me?
I'm going to miss you, my friend. I truly believe that Trinimac sent you to us when we needed you most.\n\nI wish you well. If you ever have need of me, I'll do my best to be at your side.
There's enough of the fanatics left to be a pain in my side, but we have ways of separating the bad from the good.\n\nIt might take a while, but we'll put an end to the Vosh Rakh before too long.

Orcs usually burn the bodies of chiefs and heroes. Mix the ashes into swords and shields.\n\nBut for Kurog? I think I'll have the seat of the throne recast. That way, he'll always be a pain in my arse. Help remind me what I should and shouldn't do.

Never wanted to be a king. Still don't, really. But this is the best way to keep the clans from fighting or starving to death once winter sets in.\n\nI'll wear the crown for as long as I have to. Set my people on the right path.
Good! I knew you would.\n\nI wish you safe travels. I'll try not to get too jealous while I'm stuck here being a royal bureaucrat and you're out there being a hero.

Orcs have no concept of goodbye. We just come and go as we please.\n\nBut you're always welcome in Orsinium, my friend. I'll be here, cleaning up the mess that Kurog left us with. Just try not to get killed without me, all right?
What's wrong with me? Just look! My guts are busted all to pieces. See how swollen my ankle is? I'm on death's doorstep here and no one cares!
Oh, I'm sorry, I didn't realize you were a master healer. Everyone knows that when your guts get beaten up, the juices gather down in your ankles. Don't play dumb.

An avalanche? Try six avalanches!\n\nThat mountain is cursed. There's something wrong with it, and I don't have any interest in finding out what it is. I just need to go back home, see a healer about my, you know, my injuries, and that's that.

Look, you can't tell me how to feel. I get enough of that from Stughrush. You weren't there. All that snow and ice crashing down on us. We should all be dead as drunk mice on a Morndas. It's damn near a miracle any of us survived.
Yeah, I'm fit as a sodding fiddle. Can't you tell? \n\nBah. 'Course I'm not all right. That damn mountain beat the piss out of us.

I am! Or rather, this one has apprenticed to the kind merchant. \n\nI decided, after talking to Avreg and the hearth-mother, that it would be good for me to get some broader experience. And you know what? I like the hustle and bustle of the city.

Avalanche. We'd already lost a few of these grunts before we reached the second marker—damn near froze solid. By the third marker we were at half strength. And just before the fourth, that's when things really went south.

Arrgh. Not your fault. Something about this mountain—like it's possessed. Doesn't want us up there.\n\nBut to Oblivion with that! If I want to climb a damn mountain, I'm gonna climb it! No pile of rocks is going to tell me what to do.

They are well. Avreg will come and visit me soon.\n\nOrgotha told the elders all the details of the Riekr raiders and how she handled the problems, and they told her she did well for someone with her experience. She also told them how you helped us.

It's very interesting. I meet different people every day. And I like learning a trade.\n\nI even met another Khajiit. She's an enchanter. And enchanting. I make excuses to stop by her shop sometimes. I like to listen to her talk.

Maybe. I don't know.\n\nWrothgar's the only home I've ever known, and my clan is my family. But I think I'd like to see the Khajiit homeland some day. To see people that look like me everywhere I turn.

He's wonderful. He likes city living, though I think he's getting fat. He sleeps by the fire most of the day and lets everyone fuss over him. He also keeps the mice and rats away from the stored goods, so he earns his keep as much as I do.

It was a mess. Snow, hail, wind, ice … I thought the whole damn mountain was gonna fall over. Got hit five or six times before we tucked tail.\n\nCracked some ribs. Collar bone, too. But that won't keep me down. I'll beat this mountain yet.

Not that well, all things considered. When I saw the high priestess's body, just lying on that slab ….\n\nLook, I've got to get out of here. If I stick around, these feelings, these memories, they're never going to fade.

I'm better. Much, actually.\n\nHey, I wanted to tell you that I forgive you. For Talviah. Not that you asked, mind you. I don't know what happened in there, but I know you save people. Solgra, me. If Talviah had to die, I know you had no a choice.
Orsinium! The museum? You … have heard of it, haven't you?\n\nYou simply must go, the next time you're in the city! It's the perfect place to reveal ogre artwork to all of Tamriel.

The braziers by the statues must be lit in a certain order. I tried every combination—none of it worked.\n\nI can see it now, adorned on my cairn. "Here fell Ashaka. Kept from Morkuldin because of some stupid puzzle."
There's an ogre outcast who's said to eats nuts, berries, and vegetables—never meat. It's like the opposite of a Valenwood Bosmer.\n\nThink how tender his organs must be … mmm!

Location, really. Also, <<mz:1>> have a very distinct flavor. While delicious, they would overpower the dish.\n\nOn its own, the <<z:2>> is far more subtle, but it is perfect for bringing other tastes to the forefront.

Yeah. He wanted me to stay and help train the Orc archers. Even offered me my own squad and a fancy title.\n\nBut after everything that happened, I just need to get away so I can put this all behind me.
I'm not sure. I might return to Valenwood, see my family. I'm kind of missing my loved ones after what we've been through.\n\nI wonder if Solgra had a family. She … never mentioned it.

There's so much I want to tell you. To thank you for. I've learned so much from you. Out of everyone here, you're the one person I never lost faith in.\n\nI wish I could just go and follow you around forever.
Tempting, but I need to find my own way for a while.\n\nBut no matter where the wind blows, leaves from the same tree eventually find each other again. That'll be the same for us. You'll see.

You mean the arrow in the chest? I'm still sore. But I can move around on my own. Solgra says I need lots of rest, but that can wait. I'm not going to miss a chance to say goodbye to everyone. Especially you.\n\nPlus, I have an amazing scar now!

No idea. Not even sure what an archery unit does, other than loose arrows at things. I get to be a captain, though! Investigator Vale doesn't even have her own squad! Well, except in that one book, but you remember what happened to them.

I'd give you a huge hug right now if I wasn't so sore.\n\nI don't suppose you'd be willing to stick around? Stay with us for a while? I'm still not sure what's going to happen once you disappear. It's going to take some getting used to.

Figured you say that. Maybe I'll track you down one day and we can get into some more trouble together.\n\nI'm going to miss you. Just be safe out there, all right? I'll be around if you ever need me.
Go away!
Not. Funny.
I. Ahem. I don't know what kind of business you think I do, but I'd like to keep doing it.\n\nThere is no way I'm moving goods that hot. Turn around, walk away, and let's both forget you asked.
Idiot! I don't know what it is, but I know enough. Get that thing out of here before you bring the Guard down on our heads!

I came to Wrothgar because … well, I fled. Things were too hot—temperature and otherwise.\n\n<<1>> reminded me of someone from home. Said he could get me into the Thieves Guild, so I jumped at the chance to prove myself. Jumped right into a cell.
Truly? Perhaps you are right. By now everything should be settled.\n\nAll right. I'll restore my funds and catch the next ship out. Perhaps I'll see you there!
Abah's Landing. The Jewel of Khefrem! If you hid the jewel up a camel's arse to smuggle it past the dockmaster.\n\nI do miss it. Wrothgar is too harsh a place for me.
I know, I know. Foolish, isn't it?\n\nIt was King Torug who rode the giant bear. Everyone knows that.

I lost. Repeatedly. Each time he calmly explained how he had defeated me, then urged me to try again.\n\nThere was no shame in losing. He was that good. I absorbed every lesson as best I could, yet no duel lasted beyond three seconds.
A Daedric zealot, I'm afraid. Every fifth word is "Malacath," and that's in his diplomatic entreaties.\n\nI hear he's far more tedious in person … a lot of spittle.

We ate and talked. He was … well, he's always been Shinji. Then he left—I never learned his name.\n\nYears later, Blademaster <<1>> spoke in support of my promotion. He said, "the best leader is a constant student." None were more surprised than I.
Ha! Arakaul, you goat-diddler. Get some food.
I serve my <<1>>, as you serve <<2>>.\n\nBut … you don't exactly serve him, do you? Arakaul, wasn't it?
I've noticed. You insult one another, then laugh about it. The Savage Sons allow him to lead, is that it?\n\nIt's not the sort of honor I know, but … I can see how he earned your respect.
What? No! Mercedene's troops were to blame for ….\n\nI cannot speak for <<1>>, or my king. But for myself … this siege should have ended years ago. It pleases none but the crows.

Because I serve a lord and obey his commands. Because my lord serves a king, and obeys his commands. It is the way of things, where I'm from.\n\nI've said too much. Thank you for the food. It is an unexpected kindness.
Ha! You've spent too much time around me, Tamahl.
Mercedene, Beast of the Reach; daughter of Evandene Tusk Collector; made General in the Siege of Old Orsinium for her abject ferocity.\n\nWe're a pale shadow of what she was. Thankfully.
Yes? What about it?
Not exactly. It's harder than steel—a powerful distraction in a fight, for those who think it a weakness.
Unbearably.
I often wake to buzzing and fluttering in my chest … with the occasional nibbling. I have to jump into ice cold water, then wait for all the beetles to boil out of my chest.\n\nIt's … unpleasant.
It's no trouble. I get these questions all the time, even in my own tribe.

My little sister married the king. She's his royal forge-wife, and it's gone to her head. I'm hoping I can pound it down to size with our clan's long-lost forge-hammer.\n\nNot … I mean, not literally. Although … no, never mind.
Oh. Yeah.\n\nThis one has a hatch in the back. For emergencies. It's a lot better than the old one.

Oh, no. This was a special order. A custom job.\n\nI suppose it's less useful in your line of work. Duck feathers aren't going to turn a blade or deflect an arrow. Still, you won't find a finer garment! And handsome, to boot!

Good, good. It's a fine profession with quite a few perks. Take my coat, for instance. Genuine chub loon-down lining and duck-leather trim. Warm in the winter, cool in the summer, and always dry as a bone!
Oh. Well. Praise Malacath.
I saw it when the sun was setting, so I'd say you'd want to fish for it at night. And with a fish that big, you'd want a couple friends helping out. How else would you manage to reel it in?
Your reasons don't matter. You spared me the knowledge of my grand-daughter's deception. You took a terrible choice upon yourself—bore it like a true Shatul Orc.
Of course I am. But you acted as my son would have, were he still chief.\n\nWalk where the echatere walk, blood-kin.
I killed two guards! They were just doing their job! They probably have loved ones, pets ….\n\nHow can you be so heartless?

You can be a bastard sometimes, you know that? First Solgra's lies, tricking us into helping Chief Bazrag, now this?\n\nAll right. I'll help you. But I'm not doing this for you. I'm doing it because someone has to.
The king's business. I serve the throne on matters of civic policy and urban development. When one of our citizens has a problem that threatens the public good, they come to me.

Yes. Exactly. This surprises you? Sending out the city guard is the Breton way, the High Elf way. In Wrothgar we do for ourselves. I facilitate deals between private citizens—nothing more.\n\nWe are all citizen soldiers. We should act like it.

And here I am, all the way from the icy nethers of Wrothgar, to officially welcome you and transport you to Orsinium.\n\nOf course, I'm also supposed to make sure you're willing to do a little hard work. There's no room for shirkers on my wagon.

I sent a caravan full of food and supplies to Orsinium. Once there, everything will be distributed to the outlying clans to help them make it through the winter.\n\nThe caravan's slow. I want you to catch up with it and see it safely to the city.
Well done. \n\nWhat about the challenges that I posed for this task?
I meant "Guildmaster <<1>>," but yes.\n\nWe'll need to get past that overseer to reach <<2>>'s old office.
Make your way past the guards. <<1>> hid the ledger in his old office—we'll meet there.\n\nNow. Wait until I'm in position, then throw the <<z:2>>.

Good, because I found something. The captain of the Dreamsnake was always interested in making fast coin. She's sloppy, even for a pirate, which makes her a perfect target for <<1>>.\n\nShe and I have … unpleasant history. Best I keep away from her.
The flooded district, near where <<1>> called home? The people who lived there had nowhere to go after the floods.\n\nOne of the dockyard bosses offered them work, food, and a place to stay.

I am a Speaker for the Dark Brotherhood. I speak with the voice of the Night Mother. I act with the hands of our Dread Father, Sithis.\n\nI have an offer to make to one so skilled in the art of murder. An invitation, if you will.

Nothing to say? I can appreciate that.\n\nI am a Speaker for the Dark Brotherhood. I speak with the voice of the Night Mother. We have been watching you. You can deal death, but you lack purpose. We can change that … if you are willing.

As well you should. I am certain you have questions, but first we must determine if you are worthy of joining the Dark Brotherhood.\n\nYou take lives easily and without hesitation. We know that you can kill. Now show us that you can also obey.

No? What do you call it? Self-defense? Justice? Did they all deserve to die?\n\nHow you justify your actions does not matter. All souls belong to Sithis in the Void. We are simply the instruments of their delivery.

Of course not, but we'll have time for clarity later. First we need to determine if you are worthy to join the Dark Brotherhood.\n\nYou take lives easily enough, so we know that you can kill. Now show us that you can also obey.

Silence is the music of Sithis, so perhaps you will serve us well.\n\nBut first we need to determine if you are worthy to join the Dark Brotherhood. You take lives easily enough and we know that you can kill. Now show us that you can also obey.

The wise traveler asks for directions before the path diverges. Never hesitate to rely on your fellow Brotherhood members once you complete your initiation.\n\nI assume you want to know what awaits you at the noble's estate?

A series of smuggler tunnels runs beneath the Withered Rose and leads directly to the estate's courtyard. That's the route I would take.\n\nAnd don't forget to bring lockpicks. Jarol is a cautious man. He never leaves a door unlocked behind him.

Killing requires few special skills, but reaching your target? That's the real task, isn't it? High walls, locked gates, and armed patrols protect the estate.\n\nThere is another way to reach the estate grounds, if you're interested.

The Black Sacrament is the ritual by which a client procures the Dark Brotherhood's services. Using an effigy of the intended victim, the client pleads for the Night Mother to send an assassin to end the specified life.\n\nWith no remorse, no regret.
Our Unholy Matron and the one true bride of Sithis. We are her children, forever wrapped in her cold, loving embrace.

To put it simply, yes. The lives of the innocent and the guilty alike are ours for the taking. And every soul goes to Sithis, as long as the price is paid.\n\nDeath is our craft, our religion, and our trade. And business, as always, is good.
There will be time enough for more questions after you complete the task before you. Just know that she watches you. She loves you, as she loves all her children.\n\nDo not disappoint her.

Grand Chanter Surus isn't your typical Akatosh priest. He enjoys filling impressionable heads with religious nonsense, and he has a violent streak as long as Varen's Wall. Rumors say that if he can't fill your head, he'll remove it—literally.

A plan? Yes, I have a plan. But let's not spoil the surprise. Just be ready for my signal and follow my lead.\n\nNow get out there and spread some heresy. I can't wait to see how the society initiates squirm.

Who knows why a young woman in the prime of her life would throw away everything to take up with a bunch of religious fanatics?\n\nI suppose it had something to do with that job that went sideways when I had to kill Josseline's best friend ….

I'm afraid I had no choice. A rival of mine hired him to kill us when we attended a meeting. I learned his true intentions too late to decline the invitation.\n\nI never let my enemies make the first move. So I ended him before he could end us.

Grand Chanter Surus is a high-ranking priest in the Cathedral, second only to Primate Artorius himself.\n\nHe started the society for religious types who aren't ready to join the priesthood. They claim to be devoted to Akatosh and his teachings.

Only if you believe Akatosh requires the beheading of people the Grand Chanter doesn't like. When my sister refuses an order, I'd rather not have her head on the chopping block.\n\nNothing against religion, but this cult isn't right for my sister.

Problem? Yes, there's a problem! You're preaching Boethiah's lies to the faithful initiates of the Society of the Dragon! The Grand Chanter won't stand for that, and neither will I.\n\nHe orders you to appear before him in the Chamber of Penance.

Well … that's right, I am dangerous. Now march!\n\nIf you're lucky, the Grand Chanter's justice will take the form of a simple fine for all the trouble you caused. If you resist or continue to disturb the initiates, I can't guarantee your safety.
I am the voice of the Night Mother. She conveys her will to the Listener, who then passes it on to one of the four Speakers of the Black Hand to carry out.

The Black Hand, the instrument by which the Night Mother rules the Dark Brotherhood. It consists of one Listener and four Speakers. Four fingers and a thumb. Never more, never less.\n\nThe Black Hand oversees the Sanctuaries, among other duties.

Of course. Since the formation of the Dark Brotherhood, our shadow has stretched across the entirety of Tamriel. Not every Sanctuary has flourished, however, and our grip isn't as secure as we'd like in certain parts of the world.

Not that it concerns you, but Vvardenfell continues to be a source of … irritation.\n\nThe Gold Coast, however, presents an opportunity we can all profit from. Here, we can establish a foothold that will serve the Brotherhood for generations to come.

<<1>> was the last living person who could have placed the Iron Wheel on our trail. But it wasn't her. Of course it wasn't!\n\nNow, I need to tell my least favorite person that she's in mortal danger.

I want to rush in. Give the Iron Wheel a reason to fear us. But I'm in charge, and if I'm captured, the Thieves Guild is dead.\n\nCan't believe I'm saying this, but … I need to fall back to <<c:1>> while you warn <<2>>.
Welcome home.

Quite the opposite. Josseline fled with us, which means we gave her plenty to think about.\n\nI'd guess she's gone to one of the old Akatosh shrines along Varen's Wall. Let's split up. If you find her first, politely ask her to wait for me to arrive.

She's meeting a contact nearby. She's prone to boast—why not find a quiet place to hear what she has to say?\n\nBut the captain is a creature of habit. She used to keep documents secured in the Dreamsnake. Try there, if you don't care to eavesdrop.
Oh, just those little things I noticed, like that cold look in your eyes. Or your rants about the splendor of Boethiah. Isn't killing what a disciple of the warrior prince does best?

Now you're starting to really curl my spine. I could ask you the same. Just what were you doing spouting that Boethiah nonsense in Kvatch? Are you some sort of Daedra out to prove a point?\n\nAre you … are you Sheogorath?
That's … a more honest answer than I expected. My sister sent you, didn't she? She just couldn't let me deal with this myself, could she?\n\nAnd oh look, there's Lerisa now. What a surprise.

That was … unconvincing. Who taught you how to lie? Besides, even Sheogorath has too much self-respect to be involved with this family drama. Oh look. My sister's coming. What a surprise.\n\nI suppose I should put my knives away now.
The past isn't something we talk about here. For most of us, our lives didn't really begin until we were called to serve the Night Mother. And I was called at a very early age.

This Sanctuary has always been my home in the Brotherhood, if that's what you're asking. I've seen the Gold Coast change over the years.\n\nBut that's enough questions about me. I wouldn't want to think you were taking my measure for some reason.

No one joins the Brotherhood and immediately steps into a position of power. That's not how we do things.\n\nI had to prove myself, show that I was dedicated to the Night Mother and her tenets. I served for many years before I earned my title.

Where did you …? Ah, they were discussing that at the noble's estate, were they? Bastards!\n\nIt's true. Someone has been killing our Brothers and Sisters. When the hunters become the hunted, it's like the world has gone askew.

True, few have the audacity to openly oppose us, but there are many who would love to see the Brotherhood abolished. This feels … different.\n\nStay vigilant, keep your eyes open, and report anything you notice as you execute your duties.

We're investigating the matter. It's not unusual for our pasts to catch up with us, and it's not like we have a shortage of enemies.\n\nWe'll learn the identity of this killer and then there will be a reckoning.

A little ambition is good for the soul. But only a little.\n\nComplete the contracts assigned to you. It's as simple as that. Every life you send to Sithis pleases the Night Mother and raises your profile. Complete enough jobs and you'll be rewarded.

We'll trust you with more difficult contracts, assign you more high-profile targets. The awards are greater, and we'll ask you to help with matters of importance to the Brotherhood.\n\nBut don't get ahead of yourself. Start with Elam's contracts first.

<<1>> arranged a meeting with "an Imperial client" at a nearby inn. Might be worth a listen.\n\nOh, the inn rents a room to "<<2>>," the most Imperial name I've ever heard. Probably the client? The room's lock seemed … inadequate.

That's what I told <<1>>. You know what she said? "If <<2>> had an altruistic bone in his body, he'd cut it out and sell it."\n\nI'd already know what he was really up to—if <<1>> trusted me. But she wanted me to scout, and you to do the fun part.

Ah, the look on your face is unmistakable! It says, if I may speak for your most resplendent face, "Peace, my exceptionally sleek mercantile friend. Take a series of deep, relaxing breaths so you may reveal the matter at hand."\n\nIn, out. In, out.

Go after her, of course! But you are so striking. The Iron Wheel will know you don't belong.\n\nIt is settled—you shall meet with the illustrious <<1>> at the Diamond Thimble. He shall help you obtain an appropriate disguise. Tell him I sent you!

<<1>> left for <<2>>!\n\nShe made me promise upon our long and profitable friendship not to reveal this, but your vigorous interrogation left me no choice. I do not know why she travels to the headquarters of the Iron Wheel, but I fear for her safety!

Tell her the truth. I don't care if she approves. She will need to prepare the clan for my success.\n\nIf Malacath disapproves, he can strike me down in the Bloody Knoll. But Shatul must survive. Go, there's little time.
Did he, now? Something striking, so you stand out at the next merchant lord's soiree? Or a ridiculous, crenelated affair that leaves you the talk of the brothel?
Anais … where do I begin? I was taken in by Anais and her family when I first arrived in Abah's Landing.\n\nI owe her and the Velmonts so much. My mannerisms. My pattern of speech. My fashion sense.

Time passes, things change. When the family packed up for an extended trip to Black Marsh, I decided to stay here. They went to deal with business interests and I wandered the streets of Abah's Landing.\n\nEventually, the guild found me and took me in.

If you wanted a burial suit, the Iron Wheel charges far less than I. Though perhaps … yes.\n\nA servant's outfit will let you go hither and yon—at least above ground. And if it's one of my creations, the cloth will breathe. But it shall cost you.

Then I'd assume you're from Abah's Landing.\n\nBut I know of a certain … individual … who has yet to pay the bill for just such an outfit. If you happen to reacquire it on my behalf, I would consider it your property, paid in kind.

Oh, I didn't mean to offend you. I just believe in full disclosure. We've lost an initiate and a fully trained assassin recently. Mirabelle's in denial, but I know what's happening.\n\nSomeone's hunting the Brotherhood, and you make a tempting target.

Sure you can. So could Durisa. She still ended up face down in an Anvil alley with her throat slit from ear to ear. Whoever murdered her has some impressive skills, I'll give them that.\n\nStay sharp, New-blade. We're not alone in the shadows any more.

Trying to pull off the spooky thing? Not bad, but your technique needs a little work. I'm sure you just need some more practice.\n\nAnyway, stay sharp out there, New-blade. We're not the only scary things lurking in the shadows any more.

What Thieves Guild? The Iron Wheel killed or branded the lot of them! \n\nDid your illustrious guildmaster send you? Tell <<1>> if he shows his face here, I'd have a mind to slap it. With a switch. Covered in nettles.

The old cistern? <<1>> wouldn't warn me unless she wanted something. And I would like to see the quality of recruit she allows into her "<<2>>."\n\nVery well. Help me repay a favor and I'll play <<1>>'s vastly inferior game. This is where you agree.

I'm going to be your distraction. I'm expecting the dock master to make his rounds soon, and he's not going to be happy that I haven't paid my fees yet.\n\nI'll keep him here, arguing with me, while you secure his ill-gotten gold.

It was supposed to be a simple run. Pick up silks and spices on the way and turn a tidy profit. But the Governor and her minions are more greedy than a caravan full of High Elf nobles.\n\nShe'll never learn, even when the docks are empty.

Qamar's a braggart and he drinks like a Nord. That's a combination for folly if ever there was one. He gave away his secret while trying to drink me under the table.\n\nI remember the exchange, he does not. Too bad for him, yes?

Fortunata ap Dugal, Anvil's "provincial governor," but she's still the same old Red Sails Pirate Queen to anyone who really knows her. Half the Gold Coast struggles under her thumb.\n\nFool's Gold Coast, if you want to be more accurate.
Spit it out. Can't you see I'm busy?

Ah, you showed interest. I'll consider that your agreement.\n\nThe skittish Khajiit pretending not to eavesdrop is <<1>>. Ask him why he needs our help. Meet me behind his old warehouse—after you know what you're walking into.

Ha! Not much, now that you mention it. Been running his deposits too long with nothing to show for it. \n\nLet me see your map … yeah, there. You can find the stingy sod's gold there. Once you fleece him, maybe he'll use the bank like the rest of us.
Listen, my luck's running a little thin right now. I'm not fool enough to steal from Qamar, but I might look the other way if my fortunes take a good turn.\n\nCatch my drift?

That is the question I keep asking myself. One day I arrived to find unfamiliar guards. They chased me from my own warehouse like a common dragon frog!\n\nSomeone must have bribed my overseers. It does not matter. I need you to recover what was lost.

What? No. Did I fail to mention the ledger hidden in my old office? I may have lost my warehouse, but the ledger is worth twice that entire rickety building.\n\nIf you help <<1>> restore it to me, I shall be most grateful to the Thieves Guild.
Ha! Negotiations? Call it what it is! Ransom! Extortion! It would save us so much time if they just dropped the pretenses and robbed me!\n\nGood work. Let me pay this fool and get rid of him.

It was what he expected of me. Being too quick to accept defeat may have aroused his suspicion.\n\nHe seemed convinced, so he may not notice the theft for some time, let alone suspect us as the culprits.

Oh, it's a long and sordid tale, full of romance and derring-do. Or if you prefer the short version, I was apprenticed to a smith in Sentinel. Loved the trade, hated my master. He liked to hammer more than just metal. When I had enough, I killed him.

Oh no, that was just the beginning of my story. I was young and stupid back then. I ran, but apparently not far or fast enough. Got to spend some quality time in a Hammerfell dungeon for my actions.\n\nEight years, if I recall correctly.

Hey, I had to make a living. I was branded as a killer, so killing was what I did. Worked for the crime boss Bashshi-ra for awhile.\n\nThen I had a visit one night. The Speaker scared the piss out of me, but I couldn't refuse his generous offer.

Well, it wasn't sunshine and camel milk, but I survived. Met some people. Learned some lessons. When one of the guards got sloppy, I was ready to act. Simple as that.\n\nOf course, my old life was over, but at least I was free.

The Dark Brotherhood has been good to me. They taught me to focus my anger, to let the Dread Father work through me.\n\nI have a home, an income, and a set of rules to live by. Life makes sense to me here in the Sanctuary.
I don't give an Elf's pointed ear what you want! Get lost!
Seek another for your troubles. I only wish to dice in peace.
You're mad! Only the Iron Wheel and their guests are allowed down there.
All right. I'll give you part of it. I don't eavesdrop, you understand—I just happen to have excellent hearing.\n\nBe sure to write it down. I won't repeat it.

Oh, New-blade, there are always rules. The trick is to learn what they are before you get your hand caught in the sweetroll box.\n\nFor us, it's all about the Five Tenets. I'm sure there's a book about them somewhere in the Sanctuary.
She did? Interesting. I wonder what she's planning this time?\n\nWell, I'm certain everything will become clear eventually. Even you, I suppose.
What more could you possibly need to know? I am a Shadowscale. My life begins and ends with the Dark Brotherhood.
Perhaps … depending upon what you mean by "something" and "me."\n\nRest assured, whatever musings and observations I record herein are strictly confidential.

What an intriguing inquiry! Attempting to ascertain if I actually like it here or something more subtle?\n\nWell, like or dislike is meaningless. I serve the Matron as I served my former Sanctuary. And as I serve Black Marsh when called upon.

I could have sworn I explained this before. Let me check my notes. Hmmm.\n\nWell, like other Argonians born under the sign of the Shadow, I was taken upon hatching and trained to be an assassin. That makes me a good killer. A very good killer.
Of course! It's important to get to know everyone. You're part of the family now. And family helps each other. It's what we do.

Oh, that's not a werewolf. Well, I guess it is. But it's also little Hildegard.\n\nShe's really sweet, but you'll need to say hello later. She still doesn't have the hang of controlling her transformations.
"A ring of iron around them."
"We burn our truth upon their canvas."
"The Wheel turns ever onward."

And why wouldn't she, darling? I am her favorite, after all. As a matter of fact, I'm everyone's favorite. I'm sure you'll agree soon enough.\n\nAnyway, it's a pleasure to meet you. May the Night Mother forever hold you in her cold and loving embrace.

Forward? Believe me, this is my shy and unimposing side. After all, we wouldn't want to give my beloved Cimbar the wrong idea, would we?\n\nFind me later and I'll show you what forward really looks like.

You shouldn't know anything, darling. We're a secret organization, after all.\n\nI suppose I can tell you that we serve the Night Mother. Her cold embrace binds us together. Never dishonor her. Our contracts aren't mere tasks—we carry out her will.

A few. The Speaker sends new initiates to the Sanctuary every so often. New blood, you understand.\n\nBefore you there was a charming young lad from Glenumbra. Van something, I believe. A shame, really. He was too scrumptious to die so soon.

Oh, you really are too easy, my darling! I'm just having fun with you.\n\nI suppose I get that from my family heritage. The Motierres are rich, powerful, and blessed with good looks and a wicked sense of humor. Just play along and enjoy.

Oh, there's nothing noble about my family. But I left that all behind. The wealth, the boredom, the servants waiting on me, hand and foot.\n\nOne day, I strangled my handmaid with a golden chain, and here I am. Life in the Brotherhood suits me.

Our Mother hears the prayer and whispers to the Listener. The Listener sends a Speaker to arrange the details and create the contract. Then the Speaker selects an assassin to carry out our Mother's will. \n\nIt's more than just a job. It's a calling.

"Sweet Mother, sweet Mother, send your child unto me, for the sins of the unworthy must be baptized in blood and fear."\n\nThese words, as part of a complex ritual, form the Black Sacrament. The means by which those in need pray to the Night Mother.

This just got much too serious for my taste, darling. Let's talk about something, oh, I don't know, more decadent. Like how I'd be nibbling on your ear if Cimbar wasn't here.\n\nHe's watching, isn't he? Maybe a little nibble is in order, hmm …?

Mind your tongue, Initiate! We're the murderers, not the victims here.\n\nBut I suppose the circumstances were somewhat … unusual. Someone left Van pinned to the wall of the inn in Kvatch, held up with multiple daggers. When I find the villain ….

You don't hunt the hunters! The Brotherhood hunts you. Anything else is a crime against the natural order!\n\nBut enough of this dark talk. We're just working ourselves into a tizzy. I'd much rather get excited about something more … enticing.

Wonderful! Were my perfidious overseers inconvenienced in any way? I do so hope they are bereft of convenience!\n\nYet, the others who labored for me are blameless. Should they desire it, they shall have a place in my future endeavors.
"What is the fate of the unrepentant?"
"What of those who would deny their fate?"

Said she'd earned enough for a lifetime. Handed over her rackets and told us to leave her alone. We'd see her in the markets now and again … she kept to herself.\n\nFine by me. Coral underclothes are less abrasive.
Impossible! It's still in <<1>>'s family tomb.\n\nThe dowry heist failed—<<2>> and the others died before we reached the treasure vaults.
