Let me see.\n\nThis is … comprehensive. Elaborate details on merchant lords in Abah's Landing, as well as rivals throughout the region. Maps to stolen goods we could recover for ourselves.

No, the Iron Wheel was here to punish us for attempting the heist. But … if that's what you heard … were they really searching for the dowry all along? Why come after us with such ferocity?\n\nWhat else did you learn?
Did she now? Are you sure that's what she told you to do? Wouldn't want you to get in trouble your first day in the Sanctuary.\n\nNow that you're here, we might as well discuss your training.

Hammerfell, Anvil—why does everything in this part of the world sound like it belongs in a smithy?\n\nLook, it was an honest mistake on my part. The captain claimed to be a proper sailor and I took him at his word.

I'm an artificer. If you ask me to recalibrate a Dwarven power core, I'll ask you to what voltage. But determining where the captain made an error in his navigational calculations? You might as well ask me to charm the wings off a harpy.

We're dungeon-delvers, not paupers! Kireth and I won't accept charity, no matter how you present it to us.\n\nWe'll earn our own way. Just find someone who's willing to hire us and let us do some honest work.

My letter of introduction opens doors throughout Morrowind, but in this isolated hamlet?\n\nI inquired with the blacksmith, but he wanted brawn, not brains. There was also the angler, but we were unable to agree on terms.

You'd think so, wouldn't you?\n\nThe Anvil Repository has a reputation for serving its clients … poorly. I offered my skills as a bookkeeper, but the proprietor rejected me. If she reconsiders, I'd make a valuable addition to her team.

Now that's a tale to make the Brave Little Scrib cry. Raynor insists that the captain made a mistake, but I saw the contract they signed before we were marooned here.\n\nMy brother chartered a ship to Anvil, not Sentinel. This is all his fault.

He mixed up the names! Anvil, Hammerfell, they sound all the same to my brother!\n\nAfter we'd set sail, he said he couldn't wait to see the towers of Anvil. I reminded him we were sailing to Sentinel. So he ran to see the captain, but it was too late.

We had a line on a new Dwarven ruin. Well, not new. Newly discovered? Anyway, it's near Tava's Blessing and it's entirely fresh and unexplored!\n \nIf me and Raynor can get there before the grave robbers, imagine the amazing things that we'll find!

What? No! We're dungeon-delvers, not tomb raiders! My brother has a deep and abiding respect for the Dwarves. He's obsessed with learning everything he can about their ancient technology.\n\nMe? I just love to explore old places. It's my calling!

I tried to handle a shift at the local tavern, but the customers couldn't keep their sweaty paws to themselves! You can't blame me for breaking a few fingers. They were touching my body, after all.\n\nThat's when the innkeeper's wife fired me.

I thought about helping the Rowdy Guar, but the ship's captain is a cheat!\n\nWhat I really want to do is sing. I've serenaded in taverns from Deshaan to Eastmarch. I even received a standing ovation in Orsinium! Unfortunately, Anvil has no taste.

If you're talking about that Dark Elf, she's a terrible serving wench!\n\nSailors with broken fingers can't raise mugs, and sailors without mugs can't drink. Any barmaid who can't handle a little friendly attention has no place in my establishment.

You'd have to compensate me for the lost business. How about this?\n\nI'm out of the petals I use to create an expensive drink for my more affluent customers. Bring me a wyrd blossom from the Garlas Malatar ruins and I'll give Kireth another chance.

Ha! The Dark Elf lass? I just about split my gut when I heard her yowling. Sounded like someone stuck a fork in a bantam guar and twisted it to the right!\n\nIf that's what they call singing in Morrowind, I really need to pay them a visit.

Interesting notion. We've had our share of bards and jesters, but never a jester who sings. At least the crowd will enjoy looking at her. Who knows? They might even like her act!\n\nSend Kireth over. I'll pay her well for an evening's entertainment.

Really, a—wait a moment! You're talking about Kireth, aren't you? She's the worst carpenter to ever heft a hammer, and that includes the drunk ones!\n\nI had to pay someone to fix what she repaired. She did more damage to my ship than the storm!

Let me get this straight. You're going to pay me to pay her? To fix my boat? That's crazy and I know crazy—my first mate thinks he's a wereskeever!\n\nAll right, send the Dark Elf to me. That's enough gold to re-do her work and still make a profit.

Oh, you know the big-brained Dark Elf with claws as dull as dirt? The one whose idea of mending a net is to tie a knot and hope for the best?\n\nIf you seek payment, you will find only disappointment. Raynor is no angler. He's a liar and a cheat!

Has this one misheard you? No, your gold does not lie. You want to pay me to pay Raynor to make my badly frayed nets even worse than they were before? You have been sniffing the mooncakes, yes?\n\nVery well, it's your gold. We have a deal.

If you're talking about that skeever, Raynor, then you can turn around and march right out of my office!\n\nThat skinny Dark Elf had the audacity to tell me that my accounts weren't in order. I've seriously injured bigger men for lesser slights!

Ha! You've got mead in your blood, that's for sure. So you vouch for this little snowback? You really think he can make sense of this tangled mess? \n\nAll right. What do I have to lose? The Dark Elf's got a job. My books can't possibly get any worse.

Yes, that was the Dark Elf's name. I gave him a fair chance, but I don't think he ever lifted anything heavier than a book in his entire life.\n\nWe had to let him go. With the forge as it is, my brother can't pay a worker who can't do the job.

If the Dark Elf can improve the forge, that would be a big help, but we still need those ingots. They were stolen after he abandoned the crate.\n\nThe thieves use a dock outside the city. Get the ingots back and I'll give Raynor another chance.

Immediately? That seems rather sudden. Oh, very well.\n\nKireth, did you hear? We can earn enough gold to continue our journey. It just required someone these depraved pirates could understand. Oh, I don't mean to imply that you're depraved, my friend.

Not the most exciting use of my talents, but tallying numbers beats hauling a load of metal ingots any day.\n\nThank you for convincing the usurer to hire me. Even a single entry in the wrong column can spell disaster for a financial institution.

Mending nets? I was hoping for something a bit more … managerial? Beggars can't be choosers, though, I suppose.\n\nThank you for securing this position. I welcome an opportunity to earn honest pay for honest work. I'll make you and the angler proud!

They need their forge tinkered with? Why didn't they say so? Not to wave my own flag, but I'm an excellent artificer!\n\nI'll have that forge operating at peak efficiency before they can recite three verses of "Netches, Netches, All Around!"

How did you manage that? She was so angry with me, I swear smoke was coming out of her ears. If she's willing to keep those improper pirates in line, I'll happily smile and serve drinks.\n\nThere will be a dagger in my boot, though—just in case.

Really? More carpentry? Well, it's not the profession I would have chosen, but I'll - I'll do whatever is takes us to get to Sentinel.\n\nThanks for representing us. Raynor isn't very good at negotiations and I've been told I have a bit of a temper.

That's wonderful news! Those drunken pirates are in for a treat! Thank you for negotiating an excellent deal.\n\nNow what should I sing? Something from the Tribunal Soliloquies? Maybe one of the sujamma drinking songs? So many choices!
Regretfully, I am but a humble merchant. Though I can provide information, the merchant lords cannot believe me to be in the glove of the guild.

A saying. You know, like "hand in hoof?" Wait, that isn't right.\n\nLook, the merchant lords used to fear the Thieves Guild. If I am seen to be a part of you, they may take more away from me than a warehouse.
Lots of crumbling walls. I can scout the best approach, see if the Iron Wheel leaves anything less defended.\n\nThey won't notice me. No one ever looks up.
Let me see your map. This place, just outside <<1>>? I'll meet you there when I've found a way inside.\n\nSee you there, partner?
I only traveled to <<c:1>> because I had history with the people who died there. But poking around the Iron Wheel's headquarters? Lunacy.\n\nI need a phenomenal reason to risk my life for <<2>>'s.

I'm going to smash some <<mz:1>> at the front gate to draw the Iron Wheel there. The distraction will make it easier for you to get in elsewhere.\n\nWhat? You're temporary <<2>>. You think I ever let her tell me what to do?

You did, and I am grateful. But rescuing <<1>> is a tall order.\n\nI'll do so, on one condition. Promise to help <<2>>, should she ever need it. I want her final years to be without the pain she suffered in the time that came before.

They cycle their soldiers between locations, every few months. Keeps them from forming attachments with the locals.\n\nThey see new faces all the time, so they're trained to spot certain mannerisms. Ones I've learned to spot as well. And impersonate.

I just need a uniform. They change those, too … small details here and there. We need one that can accommodate my tail.\n\nOh, and bring the journal we used in <<c:1>>. I have an idea, but until we know our entry point, I don't want to share.

We're looking for a relic called <<Ac:1>>. We slip inside the treasure room, grab our prize, and depart before anyone knows the difference.\n\nAfter that, we split the proceeds and go our separate ways.
One more thing … I'd prefer not to spill any blood, but I leave our safety to your discretion. If a guard sees you, take shelter in a hiding spot.\n\nSound good?
A gap in the wall not far from here. There's a lone sentry.\n\nI already told <<1>>. He's waiting for you near the gap.
I'll head back to the walls, keep scouting the citadel exterior.\n\nGood luck.

We walk up. I present myself as a drunk, dapper Argonian. He challenges us, tells us to move along … then sees the bottle in my hand.\n\nI offer him a taste. He takes a long pull from one of <<1>>'s sleeping potions. We take his uniform.

More treasures likely to be hidden away. If you want to maximize profit, you grab as much as you can from those secluded passes. But only if you're confident you'll get the job done.\n\nWe won't be getting any extra time to pull that off.
Try to look … non-threatening. If at all possible.
Every important merchant in Abah's Landing received a wedding invitation. Every single one.\n\nBut not <<1>>!

Hmm, I dislike them equally. <<1>> would keep it in his pocket. Were you subtle enough, you could take it from him.\n\n<<2>> would certainly leave it upon her bedroom dresser. Slip past her mansion's servants and house guards to retrieve it.

<<1>>, for one! That paranoid cheat lounges about the market as though he owns every tile on the walls.\n\nOr that lush <<2>>. She won't even attend! Just use it as an excuse to buy another dress from <<3>>. She's sweet on him, you know?

Nobody! Well … I sent word to the Thieves Guild of Abah's Landing. They were interested in acquiring <<Ac:1>>.\n\nAbah's Landing was to be our next stop. But why would this "Iron Wheel" set an ambush here? Are you certain you've never heard of them?

<<1>> has an office in the ruins where he entertains guests. If you were to leave the journal for him to find, there is little chance <<2>> could weasel out of the trial he faces in Taneth.\n\nOh, and you could find out where they're holding <<3>>.
Good luck. Don't get caught.\n\nIf you do, we'll have to spring two guildmasters. Shameful times for the Thieves Guild.
My former fiance <<1>> … that is, <<2>> … has been very cooperative with the Iron. He claims he was duped, that stealing my dowry was <<3>>'s plan all along.\n\n<<3>> has said nothing.

<<1>>'s price to surrender was the safety of those she brought along to the wedding. You, and your strange little friend. Almost … honorable, in her own way.\n\n<<2>> lies—I know that now. But <<3>> has no evidence to the contrary.

The town criers in Taneth already proclaim her trial. Politics as they are, I cannot simply release her.\n\nBut I can tell you where she is. And I can offer a lucrative proposal to your entire organization—to her directly, once you free her.

Good. <<1>> is held in the prisons beneath us, but you must hurry. <<2>> plans to move her—to where, I do not know.\n\nI'll escort you to the prison door. If you stay by my side, the Iron Wheel shall cause you no harm. Are you ready?
Straight to the point. Very good.\n\nI know where <<1>> took <<2>>. I'm willing to tell you. My only price is a single lockpick.
Good, good. Always commit fully, even when your heart brims with doubt.\n\nNow. The lockpick?

I didn't ask you to free me. A single lockpick, from one thief to another. A tradition <<1>> began, which means bad luck for her should you break it.\n\nAh, but we have company. And they seem … ambivalent to the idea.

I am, but call me <<1>>. Titles don't carry weight when you live in a cistern.\n\nPretty bold of you and <<2>> to go after <<Ac:3>>. Did you know she sent a letter, asking to set up a meet? Rookie mistake—the Iron Wheel read her mail.

If the great <<1>> thinks you're part of the guild, who am I to disagree? We need good thieves—capable thieves, like you and <<2>>—to pull ourselves out of the gutter.\n\nSo, care to join the Thieves Guild? We have nowhere to go but up.

So you say to an unarmed man. You seem to have the upper hand. For the moment.\n\nThis won't stop—the Iron Wheel shall not stop—until there is a trial. Desecrating a family tomb? Every noble in Taneth wants to see justice served.
Adara'hai, of the Twilight Cantors. And you?

Ah yes. Adara'hai has heard of you. My sister sang you an aria when news of Molag Bal's failure came to our temple. It was a cool Pahmar night—perfect weather for a hero's song. This one would hum you a few bars, but it's still too dangerous.

Adara'hai is thinking she should know you, but the name does not ring any chimes. Forgive me. We Twilight Cantors spend most days sleeping. We miss a great deal.\n\nThis one would sing you the welcome song if she could, but it is still too dangerous.

It seems silly, yes?\n\nWe have to be very careful when dro-m'Athra are near. Namiira's eyes are fixed on us. She is looking for unlocked doors to our hearts—rattling the hinges, you see? Hold an honest note for too long and she'll snatch you up.
He is … was a lesser Moon-Bishop. A sour cat with a heart made of flint and lemon-peel. This one is not surprised that he heard Namiira's music. Cats like that are perfect prey for the dro-m'Athra.
It is called the Temple of Seven Riddles—home to the Doubting Monks. Or at least it was.\n\nIt is a holy place, but not a good place.

With what? They can't look to <<1>> for help. She hired the Iron Wheel to recover her dowry. When they did, she stopped funding them.\n\nAfter what we took from the Iron Wheel, they'll barely have enough to ship <<2>> to Taneth.

What they'd planned to do with me. They'll put him on trial—a show trial, because the people want revenge. When he's convicted … well, I hear the guillotine is popular in Taneth.\n\nBut <<1>> is the past. I'm interested in the future.

The Clan Mothers say they built the temple too tall. Khajiit aren't meant to stand so close to the Ja-Kha'jay before the dead-climb. Pilgrims who come here can see the Bright Moons, yes. But some can see the Ghost Moon too. Lorkhaj.

Let me see here … "and guest"! This is good, the invitation allows for a single companion.\n\nOnce you select your guest, you should visit the Diamond Thimble. If you aren't clothed in one of <<1>>'s outfits, you'll stand out like a sore claw.
You don't "have" to dress up … you "get" to dress up.\n\nBut your companion will need to acquire an outfit as well, so go on! I'll be over here.
I'm … flattered you asked, but I'll have my own task for the evening. I'll explain at the Diamond Thimble.\n\nFor a moment I thought you were asking something more.
But … I am not a member of your Thieves Guild! And these forgeries will take time. How will I find an outfit?\n\nThough I would like to see the inside of <<1>>. Very much so.
That … is a very good point.\n\nThe perfect spies, pretending to be normal while hunting for a terrible villain. We shall fool them all, my friend!
You … you what?
Thank you for not making this strange.\n\nAll right, partner. You have a date.
Perhaps. Why do you ask?
Of course I am. Dancing, drinking, tossing bottles at those who don't do enough of either ….\n\n<<1>> may frown on that local tradition. I'll try to read the crowd.
You can't be serious.
Well. It seems you do have some sense in your head.\n\nThe wine will help get me through this. As long as it isn't the same slop from the Senche and Serpent.

I don't care if you are her protege, I'm not going to do <<1>>'s scutwork.\n\nI slipped a truth serum to <<2>>'s former overseer. I learned that <<3>> blackmails assorted scum and draws them to <<4>> for a meeting. So let's find out why.

"We?" Now that <<1>>'s protege is here, poor old <<2>> can rest her weary bones.\n\nFind a way into the Iron Wheel's headquarters and learn how they're connected to <<3>>. Oh, and blackmail needs documents—be sure to swipe them.

Just another bragging blowhard with a fancy hat, far as I'm concerned. Pirates think they're a proper navy. Ha! But they do like their titles and finery.\n\nAnyway, they all want to impress the new commodore, so now they're rummaging through my grotto!

To show that Sea Elf captain and his toothless lackeys that the grotto belongs to the Shark's Teeth, of course!\n\nWhen they see that we can do what we want despite their numbers, those cowards will flee and the grotto will be mine again.

Because I never sleep, I never stop moving, and I'm a born killer! Plus, my haircut kind of looks like a shark's fin.\n\nI run the best gang in Hew's Bane, handling protection, stolen goods, and what not. Or we will—once we get our grotto back.
"Enter, and find peace within."

Oh, any of the selections you see here should fit. I have an eye for these things.\n\nPlease note, the outfit shall be on loan. I humbly ask you return it with the exact same number of holes as when it left my establishment.

Ah, that's like asking a parent to pick their favorite child. Each is special in its own way. Delicate fabrics and exhilarating patterns breathe life into whoever dons them!\n\nI don't mean to oversell it, but you shall feel born anew.

Not exactly. If <<1>> is working with <<2>>, he may have given my description to the guards.\n\nI'll need your help to get inside. When you gain entrance to the palace, distract whoever watches the gates from within. I'll do the rest.
Good.\n\nHere's the wedding invitation, straight from the desk of <<1>>. After you meet your date at <<2>>, present this to the gateman. I'll watch for your distraction.

Professional? No, my heart, it is nothing so cold. This is a vocation. To be a Cantor is to live a life of wine and prayer—full of dozing and bathing and joyful music.\n\nBeauty is too great a thing to be caged by profession, no?

The last time I asked around, the Iron Wheel set a trap for us in <<1>>. This time, I listened.\n\n<<2>> rarely leaves her estate, and has a connection to one of the merchant lords. Must be why the city's guards patrol her estate. That's all I know.
What about it? Too much, too little?
I know, I know. It's terrible. Nothing like I used to wear at home.
I await your many compliments about the fine styling.
Shut up.
Yes … everything in order, as expected! Refreshments shall be served until the wedding begins.\n\nAnd might I compliment your impeccable timing? We were just about to lock the gates!

Don't want any riffraff finding their way inside. A wise suggestion of <<1>>. He's to officiate the ceremony, did you know?\n\nBut of course you did. Please, come in! Tonight your safety is guaranteed by the Iron Wheel and house guards alike!

Yes, he's the reason I needed a strong drink.\n\nAccording to <<1>>, the Iron Wheel's prison ship encountered a storm and nearly capsized. The waves swept a dozen people over the side, <<2>> among them. "Body lost to the storm," they said.

Do as you see fit. I'll back whatever decision you make.\n\nSomeone called the "Desert Falcon" is looking for <<1>> as well. That's how this came to my attention. I want you to see what this "Falcon" knows.

I'm no longer chief inspector of anything. After your guild escaped <<1>>, I had no choice but to resign from the Iron Wheel.\n\nThe journal was a nice touch. I'd hoped it would seal the fate of <<2>> at his trial. But a storm did that. Allegedly.
All right, you win again.\n\nHere, this key opens my strongbox. You're welcome to the contents.
All right. Give me a moment to unbar the gate.
No.\n\nBut I suspect he's in Grahtwood.
No.\n\nBut I suspect he's in Alik'r.
No.\n\nBut I suspect he's in Deshaan.

I want him to see justice. You think you can accomplish that? \n\nAbah's Landing stains my reputation, but I shall not let you stain my honor. Leave now. If I see you anywhere near my things, I won't hesitate to call the Guard.
You don't get that from me. You couldn't follow simple instructions to put down a sparkling trinket. How I can I possibly trust you?

I could slip one of <<1>>'s sleeping poisons into the doorman's drink! But alas, I brought none with me.\n\nCould you convince him to step away? If not, perhaps causing a small distraction will draw him from the gate. Something … thiefish.
Do you think the doorman could be convinced? If not, a distraction of some kind could pull him away from the door.\n\nWhatever you decide, I'll back your play.

I could tie silk handkerchiefs together and fashion a rope, but I only brought twelve. Not enough for walls this high.\n\nPerhaps you can outwit the doorman. Failing that, cause a distraction to draw him from his post.

Head to the wine tent, drink our own weight, and leave her to the guard. No? You're no fun.\n\nI don't know, convince the doorman to leave. If that doesn't work, there must be a way to sow a bit of chaos around here.

Are you working for that Ram's Beak … Falcon Wings fellow? Heard he wanted the same thing. Also heard he was a Guard.\n\nHe sent you, then? Fine, tell him my price. Pay my tab at every tavern in the city.
"<<1>>." What a lovely name! It's the first time my ears have heard it.\n\nSaroldo kept all but the simplest details of his daughter from everyone. Would that he had done the same with me.
I'm a substantial drunk.\n\nGo on, ask what you will.
Keep your fists down! Bellulor knows the score. Don't blame me for making a living.\n\nThe Imperial wasn't a local, just passing through. I'll tell you what I know.
Bounty Hunter? I can always spot the type. Think they can squeeze people like us?\n\nI met your friend at a tavern. Briefly, you understand. But I remember enough to send you to him.

After Saroldo's death, the Iron Wheel learned of our connection and sent a letter requesting an interview. What fortune I possessed now goes to the mercenaries guarding my home.\n\nShould I leave the manor, the Iron Wheel will certainly detain me.
I wondered that as well. Saroldo did his private work in this room, and recently I had it searched.\n\nI found a ledger, but I can't make sense of the symbols. Perhaps it is best in <<1>>'s hands.
What do you mean? You were the last through the gate.\n\nAs long as I'm standing here, no one else is getting in.

Huh. I heard rumors about Taneth intrigue, but having to do that on her own wedding day? I almost feel sorry for her.\n\nI … need to check on one of the guests. Don't want to see anyone when I get back. If you follow my meaning.
It's just an expression. If there's some sort of emergency on the grounds, of course I'll leave my post. But there isn't, so I won't.\n\nForeigners.
I don't know how <<1>> reinvented himself as a reclusive merchant lord, but he managed to do so.\n\nHe could have been planning this for years. Bastard!

I am most thankful.\n\nI only trust my guards as long as I can pay them, so you would do best to leave discreetly. There is a hidden exit to the street. And <<1>> is welcome to visit, should she ever desire it.

She's got some sharp tusks for a Redguard, that's for sure. But what about you? I lead the meanest crew of cutthroats in Hew's Bane, but the Wake Walkers ….\n\nThis grotto belongs to the Shark's Teeth and I won't let those pirates ransack it!

The Wake Walkers? Bunch of water-logged Elves from a garbage scow with a grandiose name!\n\nThere's a new commodore and suddenly all the pirate crews want to find gifts that will impress her. But the grotto's ours—loot and all!
I don't know. I don't think so.\n\nI've enjoyed my time with the Thieves Guild … even <<1>>. And <<2>> is a stepmother I never knew. I wouldn't have figured out the cipher without her help!

I know exactly where it is. Here, I'll mark your map.\n\nWe've been in this together since all this madness began. I can't imagine recovering my inheritance without you at my side. Meet you there when you're ready … partner.
We deciphered the ledger together. I'd call out a number, she'd find the letter in the book. It was … fun.\n\nShe's so lonely, cooped up in her mansion. She only has mercenaries to keep her company.
Vantus? Whatever for?\n\nAnd who are you, exactly?
He struggles enough finding his muse. Distracting him with financial matters will disturb his concentration.\n\nI must ask you to leave. I will inform Vantus you stopped by.

If you hope to talk her out of this folly, the Eight know I've tried. She's usually much better at fending off grasping cretins such as this <<1>> fellow.\n\nAlthough … hmm. Your outfit contains a bit of silverweave. Just like mine!

Modesty is for the poor! If you were to continue my argument with my cousin, perhaps you could overwhelm her with reason.\n\nSay, what's your favorite drink? I can tell you prefer quality spirits, as I do.
It was the only way to provide their salary. The Iron Wheel never set foot in my home, yet everything of value has gone to keeping them at bay.\n\nNone of my fortune remains.
There is nothing more for you to do in Abah's Landing? You are sure?

It is no excuse. I told myself, "Saroldo would want you to have a small portion of his treasure." But he already gave me years of his life that he could not provide to <<1>>.\n\nI was foolish. Please, forgive me.

Then my palette is decidedly more refined than yours.\n\nThe failing is mine. I mistook you for a far more interesting person. Excuse me, I must find a drink of demonstrably better quality than your own.
I knew it! And what do you prefer to pair with it? I can tell we have similar thoughts there as well.
Of course you do. So many pirates clog this port their tastes rub off on the locals.\n\nExcuse me, I must cleanse palette and mind alike to be rid of such a horrid thought.

Yes! Perhaps you are the right person to speak with my cousin. I'd nearly convinced her this <<1>> fellow is beneath her when she threw me out.\n\nShe's preparing in his personal chambers. Upper level of the palace. Ask the Iron Wheel if you get lost.
Lamb? How did a beggar such as you make it from Sentinel's back alleys?\n\nI insist you excuse me. I must drink until I forget our unfortunate encounter.
Peasant food, paired with red wine? That's … underwhelming.\n\nPerhaps we aren't so alike. Excuse me, I need to drink. Alone.
What business? The man you knew as <<1>> truly died in that storm.\n\nI am a changed man, a married man. I live quietly in this house, painting things that my wife adores. I … retired.

<<1>>'s handmaid—everything about her smells like roses, if you get me. Fusses over the bride like a doting aunt.\n\nShe says the milk is for <<1>>, but I know she drinks it herself. Some wine mixed in could loosen her up. And cover up my spittle.

She's not my patron. If you help me, I'll tell you whatever you want.\n\nThe <<1>> is subtle enough, but there's a group of fops who always hoard the bottles. Take one when they're distracted or they're sure to cause a scene. Which neither of us wants.
Bakhum is looking for his sister-in-law's uncle's cousin. We are very close.\n\nWhy do you make a face?
Does it? Well, what can Bakhum say? He values family.\n\nYou raise an interesting point though. Our Saturalia Baan-Dar gift swap does take a very, very long time ….
They must know of my previous involvement with your guild, though I can't begin to fathom how. Your former guildmaster, <<1>>, was it? He was the soul of discretion.
Memory's not so good, you know. Malnutrition.\n\nI hear good food can help that. But I can't afford good food.
Wonderful! <<1>>'s handmaid shall soon have her own bowl of milk-wine, entirely free of gristle.
Master <<1>> installed her in his own bedchamber. It's upstairs—you can't miss it.\n\nDon't let the Iron Wheel see you. They're all through the palace like beetles on honeycake.

Yes. Yes, of course. Takanradh has always had a sugar-sweet disposition. He always asks about Bakhum's wife and children, and about Bakhum's shipping operation. So on and so on. But recently, his letters have turned sour.
You've already proven you're tolerably competent.\n\nAll right, I'll do it. But you owe me a big favor, and I will call it in.

Very sour. He says that no one appreciates him. He says that his fellow monks are stealing from him, and spying on him. And he says he feels ill—twisted. He called it a "creeping sickness," scraping away at the inside of his skull. \n\nHorrible, yes?

Then we leave for the kingdom of Taneth. The route is tricky, and we'll be considered bandits if we're caught. But getting to the tomb isn't what worries me.\n\nIf anything happens … well, it won't. Because I can count on you. Ready?
Excellent. I learned something of my own—the palace is riddled with hidden passages. The palace is full of Iron Wheel sentries, so we may be able to use them as shortcuts.\n\nAnything else?
Any minute now. Be ready to move when it happens.
Good. <<1>> is supposed to give a speech to the assembled guests. We should slip into the kitchens while he has everyone's attention.

The Thieves Guild stole my dowry. In doing so, they upset my standing in Taneth.\n\nBut far worse, they desecrated the remains of my ancestor, Danobia. When they couldn't remove the jeweled crown from her head, they separated it from her body.

The merchant lords of Abah's Landing are exceptionally crooked. They buy from pirates who raid Taneth waters and bandits who raid Taneth roads.\n\nBut plundering ancestral tombs? That is too far, even for them.

<<1>>, head of the Thieves Guild? You say he betrayed his own people to steal a dowry, for some mad plot to marry a noble of Taneth?\n\nIf you are bards sent by my cousin, your imaginations are sorely lacking. Why not say <<1>> rode a Dragon?

With what time? My escort arrives soon to begin the wedding. I have accepted my fate, as you must accept yours.\n\nUnless you can produce the skull of Danobia herself, you can tell your fanciful stories to the Iron Wheel.
I'll show Falorah what <<1>> really is.\n\nShe wants Danobia's crown as proof? I'll give it to her—along with her ancestor's skull. Once I have her attention, she'll listen.
Find your way to the wedding crowd. Once <<1>> is revealed as a fraud, escort your date from the palace.\n\nI'll see you at <<c:2>> soon enough. You're in charge until my return.
Yes, <<1>>'s capture was an unfortunate turn of events.\n\nBut <<2>> is the Iron Wheel's prisoner as well. A small reason to celebrate.

<<1>> has her dowry and <<2>> is behind bars. The Iron Wheel won't be here for much longer. We'll have a chance at freeing <<3>> in the chaos of their departure—whenever that is.\n\nBut that's more your call, isn't it?

The crystal must contain al-Danobia blood. Malooc's Path would ignore you, if you held it. You'd need a lamp to find your way through the darkness, so you could grab a handful of ashes.\n\nFrom there, all you'd need is the crypt guardian's pass-phrase.
Don't rush me. \n\nThe overseer mentioned someone coming to inspect the warehouse. "<<1>>," was it? Must be a new player. Hadn't heard the name before I retired.

The deafening bang is the least of it. The smoke increases tenfold, mimicking the mating odors of the female dragon frog.\n\nEvery male dragon frog in the city should fill the warehouse by sunrise. Hope they confuse <<1>>'s shoe for a mate.

It always comes to coin with the Abah's Landing merchant lords. Consolidate the competition, lock them in a set of gilded chains, then profit.\n\nBut not that warehouse. My distraction made it … undesirable.
This one is called Adara'hai, of the Twilight Cantors. And you?

It is Namiira, the Lady of Decay. We must be cautious when her children, the dro-m'Athra, are near. Her eyes are fixed on us. She's looking for unlocked doors to our hearts—rattling the hinges. Hold an honest note for too long and she'll have you.

Mmm, yes. Adara'hai has heard of you. My sister sang you an aria when news of Molag Bal's failure came to our temple. It was a cool Pahmar night—perfect weather for a hero's song.\n\nThis one would hum you a few bars, but it is still too dangerous.

Adara'hai is thinking she should know you, but the name does not ring chimes. Forgive me. We Twilight Cantors spend most days sleeping. We miss a great deal.\n\nThis one would sing you the welcome song if she could, but it is still too dangerous.
Forgive me. This one is called Adara'hai, of the Twilight Cantors.

Mm. Azurah's purring daughters. This is not ringing chimes?\n\nThe Cantors are nuns … of a sort. We worship the Moons through song, you see? Our nights are long and sacred—full of dozing and bathing and joyful music. It is a lover's vocation.
All blessings come at a cost, yes?\n\nWhen the dro-m'Athra pounce, the Cantors are summoned to sing them back to Oblivion. This is the way it has always been.
Yes. Just so.

Mmm. Adara'hai is one of Azurah's purring daughters. On most nights, we Cantors lounge beneath the stars and sip Topal wine and sing the seventeen Khaj'ay Sahaalas. Other nights are … much less pleasant.

You didn't bother to ask <<1>>? Sharp as a barrel bottom, you are.\n\n<<1>> wants us to recover his ledger. Like a book—have you seen those before? Squiggly lines, sometimes pictures, about as thick as your skull?

Official trinkets. Valuable to the right people, Raz supposes, but mostly important to Bravil's citizens.\n\nLet's see …. There's the city's seal, the tax collector's ledger, and the mayor's signet ring. You can see why Bravil wants them back, yes?

If <<1>> took over <<2>>'s warehouse, he's grabbing the rackets we used to control. And if he's after our old business, there's a good chance he's hungry for even more.\n\nSkooma trade, slavery … things we never touched.

Before we give <<1>> a swift kick to the coin purse, I want you to find out just how dirty his hands are.\n\nI sent the others ahead to do some groundwork. Start with <<2>>—look for him near the harbor.

<<1>> tells me you're a thief! Go break into a place you shouldn't be, take something valuable, and leave before they notice.\n\nI did hear something about a pass-phrase for a "service door." Look around, use your brain. I won't spoon feed you.
<There is no response.>
<There is no response.>
I had a feeling I'd be seeing you again. You do have a habit of wandering into the most disastrous situations.

He did, did he? Last time I saw that spineless skeever, him and Coris the mage were walking away. They left me under here to die.\n\nI heard them talking about the captain and the ambassador as they left.

Coldharbour. I'd prefer to forget about that dismal place. I lost a lot of good friends there. A lot. Poor Darien. Do you remember Darien? He was a good man.\n\nBah! Let's talk about something less depressing!

How should I know? This may shock you, but I'm not much of a "keep in touch" person. Honestly, I picked up my rucksack and walked not long after you left.\n\nThings probably settled down, but I doubt we got all the vampires. Creepy bastards.

The Winterborn, from the Reach. They ambushed us … leaped out of the damn snow.\n\nIt's like they knew we were coming. After that it was all a blur. By the gods, they turned people into ice! They shattered them!

We were taking food and supplies to Orsinium. Once there, everything was supposed to be distributed to the outlying clans to help them make it through the winter.\n\nWithout those supplies, many Orcs will die. I don't want to be responsible for that.
Of course.

I'm not entirely certain, of course—one can never be certain of these things—but I think I've discovered the location of a major relic. \n\nIf I'm correct, it belonged to <<1>>, founder of Orsinium, and creator of its Bear-Rider cavalry!

<<1>>'s bear—<<2>>—was a mountain among hills. When <<1>> died, Torug entombed her remains in a cave long thought lost. Until now, according to this report!\n\nSo? Will you retrieve <<Cz:3>> for the House of Orsimer Glories?

Absolutely not. We can't know if he's lying, and we shouldn't risk him getting free. His help is the kind we don't need.\n\nAnd I overheard that transfer orders are stored in the Warden's Office. If we find nothing there, we trade him the lockpick.

<<1>> could never pick a lock. Unless he learned since the dowry heist, a lockpick would be nothing more than a thin sliver of hope.\n\nWhich you could deny him. Is his hopelessness worth <<2>>'s potential imprisonment? That's up to you.

If <<1>> personally moved <<2>>, we have very little time. A single lockpick won't do us any harm, and it gets us what we need.\n\nAnd I'll know if he's lying. So yes, toss one his way. Aim for the eye.

I understand that since Anais has returned, she's been making inquiries about me. It's clear that her memories of our time together won't let her put the past behind her.\n\nWe need to steal those memories—preferably without getting caught.

I was brought here when I was very young. My first memories are of Anais and the Velmont Mansion.\n\nAnais and I grew up side by side. We were the best of friends! Until the family left for Black Marsh, we were always together. We were that close!

You know, I never thought to ask about that. Anais told me that her father saved me from some horrible fate, but she never provided any details. \n\nThe Velmonts were very good to me. Outside of the guild, they're the closest thing I have to a family.

I was barely in my teens when the family left. She wanted me to go with her, but I couldn't leave the only home I ever knew. I slipped away in the night and I haven't seen them since.\n\nNow Anais has returned to take control of the family mansion.

I used to think my father was a merchant. When he vanished this year, I left my academy to find him.\n\nIt seems I knew very little of my father's profession. His time away was spent in Abah's Landing … working with the Thieves Guild.

Nobody recognized his name or description. <<1>> suspects he worked with one of the thieves who died in the dowry heist. They used to keep guild associates secret—it seems only <<2>> knew how all the pieces fit together.\n\nRotten luck.

They must have seen it. The last relic sought by the Thieves Guild would make a tempting target. The Iron Wheel simply had to wait.\n\nI didn't think anyone would get hurt. And I didn't mean to put you in their sights.
Head through the prison and look for the docks. Should you hurry, the ship bearing <<1>> in its hold will still be present.

Misguided, but I understand. <<1>> always treasured loyalty over … well, treasure.\n\nTo show there's no hard feelings between us, you could try the Warden's Office for her transfer papers. It's under guard, but you look like you could manage.

<<1>> remembers the Thieves Guild sold many relics to <<2>> of Abah's Landing. My father must have been the one to broker the sales. I want to break into her mansion and pick up on his trail.\n\nWhat do you say … partner?

Friends? Maybe when I was a child and didn't know any better. But that lizard is my pet, nothing more. Father gave him to me when I was a young girl.\n\nHow else am I supposed to treat a pet that ran away and misbehaves?

I returned to take control of my family's holdings, clear up old business. He's still my property, and I want my property back.\n\nAs for you, I'll let the authorities deal with you. I have no patience for those who would rather steal than work.

Forget him? He's all I've thought about these past few years. How he abandoned me, rejected my love and friendship. No, if he wants to be treated like a bad lizard, then that's the way it's going to be.\n\nI've already called for the mansion guards.

In his travels, my father brought notices to every Outlaws Refuge in Tamriel; bounties for old relics wanted by the Thieves Guild.\n\nI realized I couldn't just ask them for his whereabouts. My plan was to steal <<A:1>>, then trade it for information.

She was my friend. Once. I'm almost certain of that. \n\nWe were always together. Laughing, playing, exploring the mansion. Perhaps when I ran away, deserted her … did that turn her into this unfamiliar creature?

I was a slave? No, I don't think either of us knew what that meant. Not back then, when we were just children.\n\nI suppose, deep down, I knew it all along. Why I ran away instead of going with Anais to Black Marsh.

Of course! We took those memories away from Anais and recovered the keepsakes of my youth.\n\nPlus, we discovered how far my friend has fallen. I just need to figure out how to help her find the person she used to be—unless she finds me first.

"<<1>>:

"I have new information on <<2>> that requires your attention and discretion. Meet me at Hew's Mane, just off the Promenade in Abah's Landing.

"—<<3>>"
<<1>> must have planned all this—stealing the dowry, using it as leverage on Falorah. Now she's bound to marry <<2>>, his puppet.\n\nSo we're going to crash the wedding.
I haven't decided.\n\nBut whatever happens, you deserve to be there.
Did he try to send you to that friend of his? The "gentleman" with the velvet frills? You do know <<1>> gets a cut of every referral?\n\nNo matter.
Good, good! When you do, meet me at your <<1>>.\n\nI may have experience in … duplicating official documents. For my records, you see.
What happened? Is he ….
Huh. Landed on his feet, despite the betrayal and death he left behind.\n\nYou can never really know someone. Who they are inside.
I see. I hate him for what he did. But it still feels like I've lost a family member.\n\nThat's why I asked you to go. You had no history … you could see him for what he was.
Marriage? He sweet-talked his way into someone's life so quickly?\n\nYou did his unlucky spouse a favor. It sounds as though he has nowhere else to run.

How dare you! Vantus is a respected artist from the Imperial City. He fled before all the troubles with the Daedra.\n\nYou say he is not the man with whom I fell in love? What proof have you? None, of course!
I'll find this <<1>>. Tell him everything I know.\n\nBefore the month ends, my soon-to-be ex-husband shall be tried in Taneth.
The Jewel of Taneth? Marriage?\n\nNo, I cannot take you at your word. You must understand that.
Leader of the Thieves Guild? Is his name <<1>>, or is it <<2>>? A known conman ….\n\nThis cannot be! I thought he loved me. What should I do?

My gold is on <<1>>. She was part of our Thieves Council, the guild's inner circle—but she retired just before the dowry heist.\n\nIt might be coincidence. Or it might be she sold us out for large stacks of coin.

That's what I'd like to find out. You and I should pay her a visit. See if the Iron Wheel funds her retirement.\n\nThere's a breach in the city wall, outside the flooded district. Meet me there when you're ready.

Ah, an inquisitive sort! I like it!\n\nI'm searching for a Nord beast-master named Nikolvara. My contacts tell me she possesses an enchanted whistle that can tame any creature in Tamriel. Marvelous, yes? Apparently she lives in a durzog lair nearby.

You must recharge the great seal. The necromancers are using the pirates' life energy to weaken it.\n\nTake my amulet, Spiritcatcher, and use it to capture the unleashed spirits. Then you can use that same energy to repair the seal.

Ah, I see you aren't familiar with the term "necromancer." Trapped in a tomb, they embraced undeath before they could expire from lack of food and water.\n\nI don't like to consider how they went about accomplishing that feat.

I am the last of my order and I walk a different path from you.\n\nIf I die, the great seal will eventually fail and the necromancers will escape the tomb. I'd like to postpone that occurrence for as long as possible. I'm sure you understand.

Not many. Once the amulet has absorbed enough spirits, you can use it to repair the great seal at the tomb's far end.\n\nIronic that the same energy the necromancers use to weaken the seal can also be used to repair it.
I … I need your help.\n\nI was in the market when someone slipped me a letter. It might not mean anything, but on the other hand, it might be some sort of trap.
A folded sheet of paper, unsigned. It was only a few lines, wishing me well. But when I unfolded the sheet, an old, pressed stargazer peony fell out.\n\nThat … that unsettled me.

You've consistently demonstrated a lack of incompetence.\n\nFind out if my family sent that letter. I didn't part on the best of terms, so it could be a trap. But they won't expect you, which means it shall be slow to spring.

It's a flower. Others just like it blossomed all around my family home. But I left my family behind a long time ago.\n\nIf this is their way of sending me a message, I need to know why now after all these years.

Decades ago, I was Velsa Arendis of House Dres. Yes, the one built on the spoils of the slave trade.\n\nWhen I fled, I released dozens of slaves. Gave them gold from the house treasury. I regret not seeing the look on Mother's face. But nothing else.

What? No. That wasn't me. Did you see something? There are plenty of half-naked Nords running around Abah's Landing ….\n\nOh, stop interrogating me! I'll confess! It was me! It was all me! But that's all I can say. Client confidentiality, you know.
Gold! I like gold!\n\nI met a Khajiit woman in Riften while I was drinking at the inn. She paid me to deliver the letter to the Dark Elf lady here. Never got the Khajiit's name, though. Sorry.

You'd tell my uncle? That's not very friendly of you.\n\nOh very well! I met a Khajiit woman in Riften, when I was drinking at the inn. She paid me to deliver the letter to the Dark Elf lady here. Never got the Khajiit's name, though. Sorry.
I have a few to spare. And I'm not judging you.

Yes, but I didn't realize it then.\n\nI was taking a merchant to task for her prices when a half-naked Nord bumped into me. That's when it happened. He fled before I could give him a piece of my mind, toward the merchant camp outside the city gates.

It could be. The dro-m'Athra have emerged here before. Something about this place draws them out—if not Lorkhaj, then petty greed. Or lust. Who can say?\n\nThe seals were supposed to keep them at bay, but it seems that Kulan-dro dunged them up.
Oh very well. What's a few more moments when I get to spend it with a deadly assassin?\n\nWhat else would the Brotherhood like to know?
Mm. Duty brought Adara'hai here.\n\nWhen dro-m'Athra pounce, we Cantors are called to sing them back to the void. The price of beauty is horror, you see? Var var var.

I thought about entering the castle, but I have the kind of face everyone always remembers—beautiful.\n\nSo I was thinking … you go inside, sneak into Dathus's room, and open the secret passage. Then I hop in and take care of business!

I don't. Not to deal with Dathus. But I do enjoy sleep, and that's hard to come by when the Brotherhood sends assassins in the night.\n\nBetter they never see me. If it comes down to it, I'd hate to have to kill anyone without the proper paperwork.

Right to business? Oh, very well. Dathus Ildram of House Hlaalu is one of those blood-sucking creatures that needs to be crushed beneath a heavy boot.\n\nHe believed fleeing from Morrowind would put him out of reach. But here I am, contract and all.

Servant? Oh no. Not at all. I'm Lady Anais's best friend! We do everything together! And when she's busy dealing with the mansion or the family business, I do everything I can to make sure she's happy.\n\nThat's what friends are for, right?

Of course I do, darling! What did you expect? That I'd get soft and fat after you abandoned me?\n\nSeriously, I'm not sure I like that you joined the Dark Brotherhood. I trust you, of course, but your new "family?" Not so much.

Every day! Scrubbing the floors, wiping down the tiles. Sometimes I even wash the ceilings! All to make Lady Anais happy!\n\nSpeaking of which, I should prepare her bath. Scalding but not too hot, otherwise she might punish me—just as a reminder.

What do you mean? I've been by my lady's side since I hatched from my egg and she's always treated me with nothing but love and affection. She provides food, shelter, and friendship. What else do I need?\n\nNow please go. I need to clean these floors.

A good friend has to help teach me my lessons. That's what Lady Anais always says. How else will I learn?\n\nBesides, if I do things the wrong way, I'll disappoint my very best friend in the whole world, and I don't want that to happen.

Velsa? She didn't come with you? Ah, this one was foolish to even send the letter in the first place. Or the peony. \n\nI hoped the years would have softened her memories. That she might have wanted to see her old friend one more time before the end.

Oh, stupid Narahni, this one should have thought of that! She feared her terrible family was trying to lure her out of hiding. I should have signed the letter.\n\nBut you must understand, when we parted, Velsa was hurt very much.

This one is no longer the young and brave Khajiit that fell in love with Velsa, and it took a long time to even discover she might be in Abah's Landing.\n\nNow I am old and my mind isn't what it once was. Velsa would never even recognize me.

Do you really think so?\n\nPerhaps that would be best. Enough time has gone by without this one seeing Velsa's sweet face. Even if she's still angry, at least I can tell her that I never betrayed her. Since she didn't come here, I'll have to go to her.

Velsa loathed her family's business. This one was a slave then, working in the family's kitchens. We … fell in love.  \n\nWe made a plan to free all the slaves. But she thought I betrayed her. She disappeared before I had a chance to explain.

Here, take Spiritcatcher. The priest said it could recharge the great seal.\n\nThe necromancers are using the life energy of the pirates to weaken the seal. But you can use the amulet to catch the unleashed spirits and direct their energy to repair it.

Not too many. The priest said when the amulet absorbed enough energy, you could use it to recharge the great seal at the tomb's far end.\n\nMe? I only got as far as the tomb's first chamber before I had to flee for my life!

I tried! You'll see once you have to face those undead necromancers! What they're doing to those pirates is a real shame.\n\nBeing dead? I could live with that. What's happening inside? That's a thousand times worse and one more for good measure!

Confident, huh? Well, I'll be long gone, just in case you don't succeed. \n\nBut if you do wind up resealing the tomb, you should find <<1>> over in Abah's Landing. I'm sure she'd like to get that amulet back—and you can have the reward she promised!

Once the job's accepted, we'll get you and our seller to the job location. You'll need to find the requested goods and get out all the while remaining undetected.\n\nOh, and we need to be quick. Take too long and our cover's blown. We don't want that.

The guild doesn't like to directly be involved in transactions, so we use third parties to deliver our requested goods to the buyer. The seller comes with you and is the hand off of all acquired items.\n\nMess up though and they won't wait for you.

We'll find anyone who will take it at that point. The pay will be piss poor and we won't get much out of it, but it's better than nothing.\n\nThat's why it's important not to get caught or take too long. Your payment is a reflection of how well you do.

Our sellers aren't official guild members, so they're only getting a cut of the earnings. You take too long or set off too many alarms and they're going to high tail it out of there.\n\nHazard pay isn't exactly included in their cut.

They'll most likely be tucked away in secret passes, behind waterfalls— you name it. Even our maps we get for the jobs probably won't have their locations on them.\n\nYou'll need to search every nook and cranny. Who knows what you'll find?

Our main target is always the first priority, but there's always going to be extra valuables hidden in there. Anything else you happen to find, our seller will gladly accept. \n\nBut only if you're confident your main goal is going to be completed.
Not at all the question I expected. You have piqued my curiosity.\n\nWhy do you seek some random Khajiit? Is there some problem?

And you should join me! I find that a warm fire, a strong drink, and a hot bath—not necessarily in that order—help me unwind after a contract.\n\nBesides, this is Kvatch. You can pray or you can pray. Or you can drink. I prefer the latter.

Not a one, hero. But they saw you! Those striking features will be the talk of Kvatch for the next few days. I'd avoid the guards if I were you.\n\nOur plan worked flawlessly. Now I won't have to look over my shoulder for the Brotherhood. Thank you.

Oh, well, in that case .… An elderly Khajiit does work here. She's a cook. Bakes the best pies in town. They really are quite tasty!\n\nBut she's indisposed at present. I won't let you disturb her rest.
That's something you'll have to ask her. It's not my place to talk about the hired help.\n\nI do believe she traveled a fair bit in her youth, though.
I suppose that won't do any harm. Narahni is a kind, gentle old woman. And a master baker of scrumptious pies.\n\nThe people here are very fond of her. And very protective.

I once told the captain I was a wealthy Argonian prince seeking a fast ship to transport my riches. She let me inspect the smuggling compartments—and then I robbed her blind.\n\nShe just has one eye patch, so … half-blind. I left her the eye patch.
It's nothing.\n\nI … it's nothing.
I will. But later … now isn't the time.\n\nI just … I don't know why this matters. <<1>> is like an academy instructor, handing me busywork while the star pupil gets the plum assignments.

How could it not be? It's so difficult to care about all this.\n\nIf I studied harder at the academy, I'd have graduated sooner. He would have traveled to see the ceremony. He wouldn't have been here when ….
I … you're right.\n\nThanks, partner. I won't let you down.
No! I didn't … what I meant to say was ….\n\nHa. All right, I suppose I am a bit jealous. All this comes far easier to you than it does to me.
I know. I know, but … when I tell that to myself, it feels like a lie.\n\nListen to me go on. I won't delay you any further with my ramblings.

A cherished friend! Though not always. Once, we were fierce rivals for the importation of fine silk—yet he proved the gracious victor, and reimburses for any referral, to this day!\n\nA cherished former rival, in all truth. But quite magnanimous.
You do know he gets a referral for everyone he sends to that flax-peddler? Even when he thinks my life is in danger, <<1>> still works the angles.\n\nYou bumpkin.
Nothing worth my time.\n\nAnd everything led here, didn't it? If we leave, we miss this opportunity to learn <<1>>'s plans.
Don't mention it.\n\nTruly, don't. I could get in a lot of trouble.
Then may Julianos pour his wisdom upon you, for it seems you are an empty cup.\n\nLeave me be!

Bent spirits. Moon-haters. The children of the Daedric shadow-lady Namiira that dance in the Dark Behind the World. We rarely speak of them. Raises the hackles, you know? \n\nThey are our dark reflection. Seductive, powerful, and very, very dangerous.
That's exactly what the Iron Wheel said! But much louder, and with the shaking of fists. When they bellowed his name, I heard a loud crash upstairs.
An alchemically infused apple. Throw it hard enough and it breaks open—surrounding your enemy with a rancid bouquet of boiled netch farts.\n\nTry not to miss.
First you'll wait for me to get into position. Then you'll distract him so I can knock him on the head.\n\nHere, take this <<z:1>>.

And I am prepared to give Abah's Landing a wide berth. I'd prefer to avoid the Iron Wheel, at least for the time being.\n\n<<1>> mentioned a rendezvous by … Prince's Gate, was it? I'd feel safer were someone to escort me there.
Many thanks. This will cover five bottles of good food. At least.
No need for violence! You're as bad as the Iron Wheel, you know that?\n\nWell … not that bad.
All right. I'll give you part of it. I don't eavesdrop, you understand—I just happen to have excellent hearing.\n\nBe sure to write it down. I won't repeat it.
<<1>> thought his plan to steal the dowry was "almost flawless." But "almost" won't bring our friends back.\n\nHe didn't have the right people for the job. But I do.

<<1>> knew of the dangers within, but not everything. There was a trap. We … I … didn't understand how it worked. Not until it was too late.\n\nBut this time, I know how it works. And I'll need you by my side to defeat it.

<<1>> once served <<2>>. When she wore the clothes he designed, she was the envy of Taneth society.\n\nBut there was a scandal, and he fled here, beyond Taneth's reach. I don't know exactly what happened, but I do know he blames her.

I can't stand her, but she was always one of our best. I could really … use … her help … in restoring the Thieves Guild.\n\nMy eye just twitched. I need to control that around <<1>>—never show her your tell.
Obnoxious and dripping with poison. Just like her personality.
I'll answer what I can.

Someone who doesn't realize "Desert Falcon" is incredibly pompous.\n\n<<1>> made enemies over the years—maybe it's one of them. But why look for him now, and not after the dowry heist? Whoever it is, my hope is they're willing to work with you.

I don't know how to answer that. We were friends for so many years—he meant so much to the guild. To me.\n\nAnd then he betrayed us. He left us to the mercy of the Iron Wheel. Drowning at sea is too good for him.
Ready? This one is nervous, but I am also ready. Lead on and I will follow.
A secret passage? Velsa always loved secret passages! Let's go!
I had no idea this would be the result of sending you to find a half-naked Nord.\n\nThe last time I saw <<1>> was quite unpleasant. There was poison in that wound. I don't think it ever truly healed.
You reunited me with my one true love, so I choose to ignore that.\n\nI hope there's time to share a few lasting moments before all is said and done.
Then he finally went through with his damned fool heist.\n\nSo "Guildmaster <<1>>" sends a warning, does she? <<2>> barely in the ground, and she seeks to uproot my retirement?

This one has been trying to put her past in order. In addition to reaching out to Velsa—thank the moons she still loves me!—I had Faradan inquire after my estranged son.\n\nLike Velsa, Tashmin departed from me in anger. Now I fear for his life!
I'm <<1>>, and we're currently fleeing the Iron Wheel. We can talk about the details once we've actually fled.\n\nOh. What are your thoughts on spiders?

When I was posing as one of the manor's guards, one of the actual guards mentioned these old catacombs. Said they were a "basket full of spiders."\n\nUnless that's an obscure Nord expression, I'm guessing he meant actual spiders.

Faradan located Tashmin in Skywatch, a city in distant Auridon. He sent me word that bounty hunters have captured him, even though he can find no evidence that my son committed a crime.\n\nI'm afraid that the bounty hunters work for House Dres!

Of course! This one should have handed it over when you arrived, but I left it in the other chamber. \n\nMy son fell in with a bad crowd, drinking skooma like a fish drinks water, but he doesn't deserve a slave's fate. Please, help him if you can.

No wonder <<1>> brought you into her Thieves Guild. She mistook the muscle in your head for wit. But there's more to you than that, isn't there?\n\nWe could keep flexing all day, but there's a ledger to steal. Are you ready?
The Thieves Guild. And my guildmaster, who can explain why the Iron Wheel thinks you deserve the same fate they've inflicted upon us.\n\nIt's an unpleasant fate. It involves branding irons.

You are your own master. But the Iron Wheel is relentless, and they know your face. They know your partner's face, too.\n\nSo tell me where we're all headed. I suggest Abah's Landing, as soon as you're able.

This one has been trying to put her past in order. In addition to reaching out to Velsa—thank the stars she still loves me!—I had Faradan inquire after my estranged son.\n\nLike Velsa, Tashmin departed from me in anger. Now I fear for his life!

Oh my! What was this one thinking? I left the letter in the other chamber!\n\nMy son fell in with a bad crowd, drowning his sorrows in skooma, but he doesn't deserve to be dragged back to House Dres as a slave. Please, help him if you can.

Faradan located Tashmin in Wayrest, a city in distant Stormhaven. He sent me word that bounty hunters have captured him, even though he can find no evidence that my son committed a crime.\n\nI'm afraid that the bounty hunters work for House Dres!

This one has been trying to put her past in order. In addition to reaching out to Velsa—thank the moons she still loves me!—I had Faradan inquire after my estranged son.\n\nLike Velsa, Tashmin departed from me in anger. Now I fear for his life!

Of course! This one should have handed it over when you arrived, but I left it in the other chamber. \n\nMy son fell in with a bad crowd, drinking skooma like a fish drinks water, but he doesn't deserve a slave's fate. Please, help him if you can.

Faradan located Tashmin in Windhelm, a city in distant Eastmarch. He sent word that bounty hunters have captured him, even though he can find no evidence that my son committed a crime.\n\nI'm afraid that the bounty hunters work for House Dres!
Yeah? Well, Tash isn't here. Go bother someone else.\n\nWait a moment. Why are you looking for Tash? He never hurt anyone. And you don't look like a guard ….

That won't work. She'd have to admit she deals skooma, and she's too crafty for that.\n\nJust tear the page with my debt out of her ledger and bring it to me. She keeps it in a locked chest by her tent. Do this and I'll tell you what happened to Tash.

Help? Well, I need some help, too. Do a favor for me and I'll tell you where they took Tash.\n\nCelwen, at the Sleepy Eaglet. I owe her a bit of gold and she's starting to get anxious about my ability to pay.
Hmm. Maybe if we pray to Akatosh? Sorry, not helping.\n\nI've read … er, I've heard that rich thanes with treasure houses love their secrets. Let's see if there's a hidden mechanism.
Thank the gods! You will have no trouble from me. You were never here and I never saw you.

You got it? Now my skooma dealer has nothing on me. I get a fresh start!\n\nTash was with me when two Dark Elves grabbed him. They claimed to be bounty hunters, but I've seen this before. They take unfortunates like us and turn us into slaves.
Dancing girls and animal acts.\n\nIt's a warehouse! Sweaty laborers and rough-hewn crates. What do you expect?

He's down near the docks, tied up and waiting to be packed onto a ship.\n\nThose so-called bounty hunters are still prowling around, looking for other Khajiit to fill their cargo hold. Damn guards were probably paid to look the other way.

I suppose you can't be too bad. You did help me, after all.\n\nHe's down by the docks, tied up like cargo. Those so-called bounty hunters are still prowling around, looking for other Khajiit. Damn guards were probably paid to look the other way.
How do I know you aren't another one of those so-called bounty hunters? You are a Dark Elf. Maybe you're in league with the bastards that grabbed Tash.
Why would you do that? This one doesn't even know you. \n\nBesides, that bounty hunter carries an arrest writ with Tashmin's name on it. As long as he has that, this one will never be free.

This one will be dead soon. It is inevitable.\n\nBut if you really plan to get the writ, you'll need to pick his pocket. He's been drinking my skooma while his partner hunts other Khajiit, so I suppose you might want to hurry.
A Dark Elf? Help me? What cruel amusements these slavers employ to trick a poor Khajiit!

This one will die of thirst soon. It is inevitable.\n\nBut if you really plan to get the writ, you'll need to pick the bounty hunter's pocket. He's been drinking my skooma while his partner hunts other Khajiit, so I suppose you might want to hurry.

Then why would you help me? This one has never even seen you before.\n\nBesides, that bounty hunter carries an arrest writ with Tashmin's name on it. As long as he has that, this one will never be free.
My mother sent you? This one has not seen Narahni in many, many years. How would she even know where to find me? Why would she even try?\n\nI was full of anger for so long, but now? Now I'm just sad.
This one has heard of Abah's Landing. Always wanted to see such a place. Perhaps I will accept your offer of hospitality.\n\nBut first things first. This one needs a drink.
Because this one was young and foolish once, full of anger and certain that the moons shone only for me.\n\nSoon, the skooma drowned my memories and it was easier just to forget.

This one wishes she had not found me. She should not see the sorry condition her beloved son has fallen into.\n\nStill, Tashmin can't stay here. Maybe it's time to put the past behind me and try to do something better with my life.

Now? So soon? Can't this one have a drink first? Maybe three?\n\nNo, no. A clear head is better than a clouded mind on occasions such as this. I just hope my mother isn't too disappointed in what her son has become.
It certainly looks that way. Between Tashmin and I, Narahni had a hard life.\n\nI just want her to be happy.
And I plan to make up for everything Narahni has missed. I'll be there for as long as she'll have me.\n\nI can't change the past, but I'll do my best to make her future better.

Let's talk about details when we rendezvous. It's not that I don't trust you! I'm just … I don't think I've made a good impression in this place.\n\nThat is, if you're still interested. You are, right? Of course you are, I'm only joking.
None whatsoever! Anything else you take is yours to fence.\n\nJust don't forget why we're there. We don't leave until we have the <<1>>.
Of course, you're right. The Iron Wheel could return at any moment. We need to get out of here, and fast.\n\nWait … did you hear that?

Good, you can take direction.\n\nDid he tell you it's packed with dirt on merchants throughout Abah's Landing? How will <<1>> react when I bring her a grateful <<2>> and his insidious ledger? I do hope it makes her eye twitch.

My own concoction. When poured into a crate filled with sawdust, the crate emits a thick smoke. Any reasonable person would reach for a bucket of water to douse what appears to be oncoming flame.\n\nYet it reacts quite poorly to water.

"<<1>>,

"There's a place near <<c:2>> where I go to think. Can you come by when you have a free moment? I need your help with a personal matter.

"—<<3>>

"PS: The mustard stain doesn't represent anything."

"<<1>>,

"I deciphered my father's ledger! Come by my rooftop retreat when you have a moment.

"—<<2>>

"PS: There is another mustard stain. No judgments!"
Trust me. Stay calm a moment longer and all will become clear.

The cub is more seasoned than she admits, but Fa'ren-dar's eyes are sharper than his claws. Tongue too, where Velsa is concerned. I have missed her conversation.\n\nBoth are the guild's to serve, and so now they serve you too.
Then we should see what my magpies have brought back to the nest. I'll await you at the tip board in the guild hall.

Perhaps I am. A very sneaky butler, who ensures that all things reach their proper destination. Loot from an industrious thief's sticky fingers into a wanting buyer's tender embrace, and gold from a happy buyer's pocket to a deserving thief's palm.

Wealth in Abah's Landing comes and goes like its tides. What washes in isn't here for long, or left about like flotsam to be scooped up by any passerby. There are many hidden nooks where such things are tucked away.\n\nFa'ren-dar knows them all.

Fa'ren-dar's little birds post things of interest at the guild. If something catches your eye too, speak up and we plan the heist.\n\nGo through me, or not at all. We don't want members stepping on each other's toes, or skimping on their dues.
That's not good. We could certainly use his aid at the tomb. I'm willing to delay our departure if it means we can recover him.\n\nIt's your call. We can manage without him, if need be.
All right. We should hurry. <<1>> won't last long under the Iron Wheel's interrogation.
We'll be here. Bring him back safe and sound.
There's a snitch, goes by the name <<1>>. Slippery fellow … local. He might know where <<2>> was heading.\n\nIt's all in my notes.

That's why I sent <<1>> to pull you out. Don't get me wrong. <<2>> may be green, but she planned a real heist—the kind we used to pull off, before the Iron Wheel captured or killed most of us.\n\nBastards.
Anais needs to see the errors of her ways. People aren't property. They aren't supposed to be sold and traded, and they certainly shouldn't be turned into slaves.
There was no request for a ransom. I made that all up to scare her. No one even knows she's missing yet and I'd like to keep it that way.

Take these letters. I don't want her family's agents to come looking for her yet, so I forged them to explain her absence. Just plant them in the Velmont Mansion and that will give me all the time I need.

Time for Anais to consider her situation, to see if being trapped and powerless changes her outlook on keeping pets and slaves.\n\nWhen she's learned her lesson, I'll set her free. Meet me at the Thieves Den after you plant the letters.
As a matter of fact, it was the strangest thing! He ran right across the bridge that spans the middle of the grotto! If you hurry, you can probably still catch him!

Yes, yes, rescue her … yes. I never wanted to become a slave merchant. But if we set her free, won't she just continue with her awful ways?\n\nI hate to admit it, but I'm at a loss as to how to proceed.
I see your point, but one can learn about murder without being murdered.\n\nUntil the pirates ransom her back to her family, they'll treat her the way she treats <<1>>.

What does that matter? Should I determine my actions based on the inclinations of a slave-keeping, self-centered aristocrat?\n\nWhat should I do? I just want to return to the Den … put this awful business behind us.

Yes, I suppose I should. But does that mean I abandon my goal to teach Anais a lesson? How will I live with myself if she continues to treat people as things?\n\nI could set her free, but what's the profit in that?

You heard of <<1>>? She's a noble from Taneth with a substantial dowry in her family tomb. We tried to steal it—but we failed, and she hired the Iron Wheel to punish us.\n\nI hear their leader thought you worked for us. Want to make it official?

Ah, you're the one that Walks-Softly brought to our charming little hovel.\n\nWell, let me be the first to welcome you to the Abah's Landing Thieves Guild. We may not look like much, but we used to be significant. Divines willing, we will be again.

I don't really know the details. It happened shortly after I joined the guild, and I wasn't privy to our leaders' plans.\n\nAs far as I can tell, a heist went terribly wrong. Zeira was the only survivor. Beyond that? You'd have to ask the guildmaster.

A recent promotion, yes. The higher-ups got together to pull off the heist of the century, but Zeira was the only one to return from that doomed expedition.\n\nWhatever happened brought the attention of the Iron Wheel down upon us. Now we hide here.

I do whatever it takes, my friend. Whatever it takes. I want to help the guild reclaim its former glory and drive those Iron Wheel bastards out of Abah's Landing.\n\nAnd if Zeira deems to make me an officer in the guild, so much the better.

Interesting choice of words. Role. I play many roles. Seductress, serving girl, noble, beggar, merchant—it all depends on the job at hand.\n\nIt's all about the disguise, you see. You've probably talked to me a dozen times and didn't even realize it!

I change personalities like a noble changes clothes. Perfect for surveying a location for a robbery or swindling a merchant out of gold.\n\nI just wish the higher-ups weren't so busy. As good as I am, I know there's more to learn.

It was a simple enough matter for me to disappear when the trouble began. \n\nIf you must know, I took on the role of a bodyguard at the Winsome Welwa. Worked there until the guild started to gather again down here.

Don't I? We made good use of that before we joined the guild. Being two places at once is a handy skill for deception.\n\nOn the other hand, Kari could just be another role that I play. Are you certain you've ever seen us together?

I tracked Anais to that building behind us, but the lock on the door has thwarted all of my attempts to pick it.\n\nOne of these pirates must have a key. Maybe you'll have better luck finding it than I did.

This one eventually left the Arendis lands, after Velsa had disappeared. Much wandering but I was not alone. Narahni had a son, named Tashmin. \n\nWhen he was grown, we fell away from each other. He left Narahni in anger. Now he is in danger.

This one eventually left the Arendis lands, after Velsa had disappeared. Much wandering but I was not alone. Narahni had a son, named Tashmin. \n\nWhen he was grown, we fell away from each other. He left Narahni in anger. Now he is in danger.

Faradan's letter is inside the house, it has more information. \n\nTashmin and I parted on angry words because he had fallen in with bad people. Irresponsible, drinking skooma, doing nothing. I kept thinking he would come back, but he did not.

Faradan helped me search and he found Tashmin in Skywatch, in far away Auridon. But bounty hunters have taken him prisoner, though he committed no crime. \n\n Faradan believes the bounty hunters are working for House Dres.

Faradan's letter is inside the house, it has more information. \n\nTashmin and I parted on angry words because he had fallen in with bad people. Irresponsible, drinking skooma, doing nothing. I kept thinking he would come back, but he did not.

Faradan helped me search and he found Tashmin in Skywatch, in far away Auridon. But bounty hunters have taken him prisoner, though he committed no crime. \n\n Faradan believes the bounty hunters are working for House Dres.
You did? Excellent!\n\nI'll let you have the pleasure of seeing if that key will unlock the door. After you.

This pirate crew seems to be somewhat lax when it comes to following the rules of the sea. I suppose any one of them could be carrying a key to that door.\n\nIn cases such as these, you just have to keep breaking eggs until you find a yoke.
Be my guest. I'm worse than <<1>> with those things.\n\nIf you can get past that lock, I'll follow you in and we'll deal with whatever we happen to find.
Tough as nails and twice as sharp! \n\nI'm the muscle. Even Velsa appreciates having some muscle around when things go south. And speaking of Velsa, I'm glad she's back.
Yeah? Well, Tash isn't here. Take your charity and—\n\nWait a moment. Why are you looking for Tash? He never hurt anyone. And you don't look like a guard ….

That won't work. He'd have to admit he deals skooma, and he's too crafty for that.\n\nJust tear the page with my debt out of his ledger and bring it to me. He keeps it in a locked chest near his cart. Do this and I'll tell you what happened to Tash.

Help? Well, I need some help, too. Do a favor for me and I'll tell you where they took Tash.\n\nLoupel Menant has a cart near the North Gate. I owe him a bit of gold and he's starting to get anxious about my ability to pay.

Velsa was an important figure in the guild before she retired. I'm kind of surprised she came back. Of course, she always preferred her plants over people, but I don't blame her.\n\nIn my experience, people will disappoint you.

Oh, what a delicate flower! Have you never walked the streets of Abah's Landing? Everyone needs muscle! I'm surprised more people don't have them.\n\nStealth and skill will only take a thief so far. It takes muscle to make it the rest of the way.
Yeah? Well, Tash isn't here. And that's where you should be. Not here.\n\nWait a moment. Why are you looking for Tash? He never hurt anyone. And you don't look like a guard ….

That won't work. He'd have to admit he deals skooma, and he's too stubborn for that.\n\nJust tear the page with my debt out of his ledger and bring it to me. He keeps it in a locked chest near the forge. Do this and I'll tell you what happened to Tash.

Trouble? Well, I'm in trouble, too. Do a favor for me and I'll tell you where they took Tash.\n\nGeraud Maviniele at the Anvil & Pauldron. I owe him a bit of gold and he's starting to get anxious about my ability to pay.

It's brilliant, that's what it is! I joined the guild because of Velsa, you know. Hoped to learn whatever she was willing to teach me, but every time I asked a question she threatened to defoliate my head.\n\nI'm glad she's back though.

Well, she's no legend like Nicolas was. But then again, nobody is. We all miss him terribly.\n\nZeira, on the other hand, she's one of us. She isn't afraid to get her hands dirty. I appreciate that in my guildmaster.

Funny you should ask about that. I just finished building a device to help Brucus get into his uncle's vault. I hope he heeds my advice and stands well clear of the door after he sets it. I may have been a bit heavy with the kindlepitch.
I heard. But if the guild didn't wind up with the dowry, I wonder who did?\n\nIt's the curse of Prince Hew. Nothing ever turns out as planned in Abah's Landing, and that's the truth.

Who told you about—I mean, no, not a thing.\n\nLook, I can't help it if things accidentally happen to fall into my pouches. If I had to keep track of every item that belonged to someone else and wound up in my possession, I'd never get anything done.
You think so? That's the nicest thing anyone's said about me since I left Greenshade—and mostly they said "good riddance" as I departed.

Indeed, I have seventeen distinct theories, ranked from "most viable" to "highly improbable." But I'm not ready to share any of them just yet. I need more data to analyze.\n\nIf you and Zeira learn anything else, please be sure to let me know.
