A true genius never guesses. Not when every problem, no matter how complicated, can always be solved through dedication and analysis.\n\nI'll figure out who actually stole the dowry. It's just a matter of time.

A number of merchant conglomerates operate out of Abah's Landing, using their wealth and power to influence the city. The Thazahrr Cartel is one such entity. I regret to say that I worked for them for a time, before I found a place in the guild.
I heard about that. But I'm not worried. Zeira will take care of this <<1>>. That's what a guildmaster does, after all.

You make it sound so … pedestrian! I am a member of the guild, just like you. But instead of working with lockpicks, I balance ledgers while keeping my eyes and ears open for interesting … business opportunities.

If you're implying that I'd ever do anything to hurt the guild—well, that notion is as outlandish as a bonnet on a dragon frog!\n\nNow unless you have some legitimate concerns to discuss, I'd prefer you let me get back to my books.

That's one word to describe what I do. And I do it very well.\n\nI am a little worried about this <<1>> person, though. Until I can examine his ledgers and review his journals, he's just an empty box, as far as I'm concerned. And I hate empty boxes.

I was biding my time, determining how best to perform my duties in the face of overwhelming odds.\n\nBut as soon as I got the word that Zeira was re-forming the guild, I was back here in two shakes of a horker's tail.

The Iron Wheel? Facing those sharp-tusks head on would be as suicidal as chub loons charging a snow bear.\n\nWe will weather this storm. The guild was around before the Iron Wheel, and we'll still be around after they're long gone.

Thrag chose well when he brought Ghazana into the guild. She's more than capable and I'm sure she will serve us well.\n\nAnd she's very pleasant to look at. Knowing Thrag, that was the first thing that crossed his mind when he recruited her.

Thrag did an admirable job in my absence. Now that I'm back, he will return to his role as my second in such matters.\n\nI know that will irritate the tusk out of him, but it can't be helped. I'm Thrag's superior in every way—and he knows it.

Depends who you ask. Since Velsa retired, I've been the guild's alchemist. Oh, I guess you could say I took a break after the Iron Wheel began their persecution, but I returned as soon as Zeira gave the word.

I was so discouraged when I heard what happened to <<1>> and the others that I spent a good deal of time pleasantly inebriated. We all handle grief in our own ways, after all.\n\nAs soon as Zeira contacted me, I packed my kit and hurried back.

Interfering foreign bastards! They have no business in Abah's Landing! If I had my way, I'd slip a vial of poison into the chief inspector's tea and be done with the matter.\n\n<<1>> says that's not the way we do things. More's the pity.

Poisons and toxins, for the most part. I also dabble in mind-altering substances. I do so enjoy having my mind altered!\n\nIt's all a matter of subtlety. A pinch of this or a splash of that can solve most problems, I've found, and with less bother.

I was a bounty hunter back in Shornhelm before I embraced this life.\n\nI suppose tales of my past have been spread around the guild like jam on a biscuit. Thieves and cutpurses are worse than old wives when it comes to gossip.

I originally came to Abah's Landing to collect a bounty on <<1>>. But he offered me an alternative that actually made sense. I brought my talents to the guild and they welcomed me.\n\nJust like you, I earn their trust every day.

You'd be surprised. When it comes to law and order, the line between bounty hunter and outlaw is thin as a wisp of hair and just as fragile.\n\nAfter years of serving the public good with nothing to show for it, I learned that crime actually does pay.

Never leap into water when you don't know the depth.\n\nI wasn't here, but I wasn't cowering like a newt just free of his shell. There were things that needed doing. Now they are done. All to the benefit of the guild.
Do I? I suppose that I do. It was earned with the blood and entrails of others, though, I assure you.\n\nYou're too easy to fool! I do enjoy making the new recruits tremble!

The guild has reclaimed its position of power in Abah's Landing. Our new arrangement with Taneth might even make us more powerful in the long run. It all depends on how the wind blows. And if the merchant lords don't cause us too many difficulties.

We'll continue to rebuild, finish getting our own house in order. I have nothing but admiration and respect for our beloved guildmaster!\n\nIndeed, I can't wait to see what she has planned for us next. The anticipation has me on the edge of my seat!

I had a beautiful ship, once. It was fast, nimble … but the summer storms that blow up along the Abecean coast were too powerful for my poor "Swift Lightning." Sank to the bottom of the sea.\n\nBut let's bask in Zeira's success. This was a good day!

My experiences from my days as a pirate and smuggler make me invaluable to the guild. I have contacts, friends in distant ports, and more than enough advice to pass along.\n\nWhen it comes to planning and organization, just call on "the Captain!"

Somewhere in <<1>>. The Iron Wheel's preparations to depart causes much distraction. There is no better time to slip among their ranks!\n\nBut I am not a part of your guild. You would know best what to do, of course.
I see many and many things, that is true.\n\nIs there something in particular that I can illuminate for you?

I shall tell you a secret. Once, crime was kept to a minimum by the Thieves Guild of Abah's Landing. But the Thieves Guild is no more, or so I have heard, and now the cutpurses and footpads run wild and free.\n\nSo, no. Not a safe place. Not at all.

Oh yes and truly! A grandiose title, but they do keep our economy going.\n\nOf particular note are Orahan at-Addin who runs the Syndicate and Lady Ylanie of House Vien. If you haven't visited her establishment, the Winsome Welwa, you're in for a treat!

As I have heard the words, one pirate found a ridiculously large and ostentatious hat and named herself "commodore." Now the rest of the pirates seek some kind of gift to use to win her favor.\n\nPirates have such foolish notions.

Just bring it back to me. I'll handle the delivery, and you'll be paid on the spot. I'll be waiting just outside the cistern in the alleyways. You can find me there anytime you're looking for a bit of work on the side.

The past can be a vise that holds us back. I've seen it. I want to teach Anais to let go of her memories, forget about me, and get on with her life.\n\nAfter we steal the items—items that once belonged to me, by the way—she'll stop looking for me.

Keepsakes. Jewelry that Anais had made from my hatching shell and scales I lost during moulting.  \n\nYou know, now that I say the words out loud, it sounds kind of strange for someone to have kept my discarded body parts. Is that a common practice?

Still out of service, I'm afraid. I don't have to describe the indignity of a famous captain such as myself booking passage on a trading vessel, do I? Still, my sister comes first.\n\nAlso, no one on that ship actually knew who I was, so no harm done.

Wonderful. Telonil's done a remarkable job in growing our fortune, Haerdon and Mekag are in fighting shape, and patrols have grown sparse since the war in Cyrodiil.\n\nI've got nothing against Captain Kaleen, mind you, but a woman needs her own ship.

Not that I'd ever kiss and tell, my dear, but if nothing else, I remain amused by his advances.\n\nDo you know he memorized a book of Redguard poetry and quoted it at me? That was almost charming. And of course, there was the trained monkey.

It wore an adorable hat and clutched a wrapped gift. Perhaps Jakarn thought that since I enjoy Howler's company, the way to my heart was through a monkey.\n\nHowler chased the creature off, so I have no idea what was in the box.

It's what we do. She'll come back when she gets bored or she needs something. She always does.\n\nHowler's a bit disappointed he didn't get more time with her, but he'll get over it. Nothing a few dozen mugs of ale won't cure.

Profitable and dangerous. I'm happy to continue ferrying troops for the easy gold, but when the Queen commands us to show our claws, we oblige.\n\nMany a captain has made the mistake of dismissing the Prowler as a threat, to my benefit.

Ah, the tale of the Prowler and the fierce Maormer sea serpent. It grows with each telling! You might be amused to hear what the crew claims happened that day.\n\nIt's quite a popular story in the port towns.

You think? That's the tamest part! By all accounts, your battle with Peledil rocked the seas and reshaped the coast. They say you turned the sea serpent into a mount!\n\nAh, I'm glad you're still well, my friend.

We were set upon by one hundred Sea Elves, surrounded with no hope of escape. But you defeated them soundly with one bare fist while swinging from the rigging.\n\nThen you hopped onto the sea serpent and rode it into the side of the Maormer ship!

You think I have noticed your unique affliction? I considered killing you as well. Yet having heard tales of your exploits, I believe you do more good than ill.\n\nShould that change, we may become enemies. Today, however, you may depart in peace.

No, but I have a tale that may interest you.\n\nWeeks ago, I stalked the wilds outside Marbruk, searching for a vampire assassin. What I did not realize was that the creature was leading me into a trap. I was set upon by her and five trained killers.

It was a close call. I dispatched the killers and set the vampire on fire, but not before I sustained grievous wounds. I buried my blade in the vampire's heart and collapsed, considering this a good death.\n\nThat was when she appeared by my side.

Ah, the Wilderqueen. I have heard tales of that remarkable being. Tales of awe and terror that included saving Wood Elves and stopping loggers.\n\nYour influence grows if you have the ear of Valenwood's legendary protector.

A woman with skin of bark and hair of leaves. When she knelt beside me, my pain vanished. She healed me and brought me back from undeath.\n\nWhen I asked her why she would do this, all she said was, "Thank the Vestige." Then she disappeared.

This one will sing at a wedding, perhaps. Or a naming? Something joyful and clean. There is a shrine north of Senchal—a very fine place with white sandy beaches and cool breezes off the Topal Sea. I will start there. And after that? Who can say?

Neither does <<1>>. Here's a copy of his wanted poster. It's plastered all over Taneth.\n\nI want you to find out what really happened. If he's dead, we throw a party in <<c:2>>. But if he's alive, you track him down and ….

You are kind to ask. Yes, this one will manage. There are no wounds that song and prayer cannot mend. Soon this one will swim in warm seas and sing the kha'jay sahaalas under the Tojay moons. All will be well.\n\nTake care of yourself, walker.
Adara'hai will leave that to the Mane and the Torval Curiata. This one fears that she's already stayed too long ….

Yes, I'd say so. I find life to be a complicated series of pranks and pratfalls. Besides, this is your mission. I'm only here to observe and offer assistance if you get in over your head.\n\nSpeaking of which, try not to get captured or killed today.

Be stealthy or slaughter everyone that gets in your way. Whichever works best for you. They all wind up with Sithis in the end, so what's the worry?\n\nNow let's get out there and deal with the Grand Sermonizer and her lying priests.
Did she? So I get to do all the work and you wind up with all the glory? I'm getting a little tired of sticking to the shadows all the time.\n\nI'm sorry. Was there something else you wanted from me?

Hmm. Excuse my attitude, but you have to understand. Cimbar ….\n\nAnyway, I've been hunting the Black Dragon. On my own. Got so close I could hear her voice. But I had to break off the hunt. I didn't want to wind up dead, you understand.
Well … right. I suppose that sounds cowardly to you, our newest Assassin. The pride and joy of the Matron and the Speaker both.\n\nYour blade never dulls, does it, Assassin?
Rotting away in <<1>>.\n\nBut please, how can <<2>> thank you for her unexpected fortune?
Very good! Select any you see on display. If adjustments are needed, <<1>> shall provide!
The Velmont Mansion is a large place. Why don't you check the kitchens and courtyard while I search the family suites? Meet me there when you're done and we'll get out of here together.

Cimbar was one of our best. To allow himself to be captured like that … I didn't think that either the Grand Sermonizer or the Order of the Hour was capable of such a feat. Why go to all that trouble, I wonder?

Black armor? I've heard rumors of such a warrior. But to seek the location of our Sanctuary? It appears we're at war with an unknown adversary. I need to think about this.\n\nBy the way, Tanek woke up and asked to see you.
We're not certain what kind of magic the Grand Sermonizer placed upon Cimbar's body, but I'd be dead, too, if not for you and Kor.\n\nI'm indebted to you both.

And I'll make sure that everyone remembers Cimbar's bravery. He refused to give up our secret, no matter what the Grand Sermonizer did to him.\n\nIt does make me wonder about the warrior who was able to defeat him, though.

Cimbar could easily best me in a fight, and that warrior bested him. If you encounter her again, don't underestimate her skills and abilities.\n\nShe's hunting the hunters, and that's a game I have no desire to play.

Anais had it made from one of my scales. One that I lost during my first moulting. It's in the jewelry box.\n\nI thought I had fond memories of this place, yet watching that young Argonian has stirred up some unsettling emotions.

Caution becomes the appropriate response after the deaths of two assassins, Initiate.\n\nBut make no mistake. I expect you to assassinate the Grand Sermonizer. Tanek will be there to provide assistance, nothing more.

The Grand Sermonizer and her priests spread lies about the Brotherhood for reasons I do not yet understand. Whether she seeks to insult us or acts upon some misguided tenet of faith, our response is clear.\n\nThese impudent priests must die.

Primate Artorius leads the Cathedral of Akatosh in Kvatch. The Chanters and Sermonizers bow to his authority as the Chosen of the Dragon God, and even the Order of the Hour follows his commands.\n\nPious and faithful, I find the man to be insufferable.
A distraction, of course. The Iron Wheel rushed upstairs as he slipped down through some loose floorboards.\n\nBut he landed feet first in a tub of bright dye! Covered his boots to the brim.
That's also what the Iron Wheel said! Most of them gave chase. The rest tossed the room upon the floor, and then gave chase.\n\nIf you find him before they do, tell him <<1>> deserves a raise.
We return to <<c:1>>, bypass the deadliest traps I've ever encountered, and then scour the treasure vaults for anything we can find.
It's a terrible plan. But it's the best terrible plan we have.\n\nUntil we know what happened to that dowry, we'll always be living in a cistern.
Ha! I appreciate the confidence, but too many good people died there the first time.\n\nWe do this right, or we don't do it at all.

<<1>> can give us an edge. He's one of the few living people to set foot in <<2>>'s family tomb.\n\nTake <<3>> and collect him from his shop. Meet the rest of us on the road to Taneth, by Prince's Gate.

She's heir to the al-Danobia bloodline. Her eldest sister Za-Rifah wed King Fahara'jad. After Za-Rifah's death, Falorah and the king grew close. But not … "close."\n\nThey call her the Jewel of Taneth—beautiful, cold, and hard as diamond.

The Black Dragon? How brave of you to seek the most powerful warrior in our order. I can show you where her chambers are, if you like.\n\nYou know, the Black Dragon was a lot like you once, before she sought redemption.
Very much the same, I see ….\n\nThe Black Dragon was an assassin. A member of the Dark Brotherhood. Until she had enough of following the commands of others.

As I understand it, she was an assassin. She killed on command and with impunity, leaving a graveyard full of corpses in her wake.\n\nShe's a member of the Dark Brotherhood. That is, she was. Until they pushed her too far.

Members of the Order are encouraged to talk about their pasts.\n\nBut we should get to someplace more private. You don't want to get caught out in the open if more of the Order appears. I'll take you to the Black Dragon's chambers. We can talk there.
Primate Artorius teaches us that no one is beyond redemption. In time and with effort, all wrongs can be righted.\n\nI can be patient. Can you?

I suppose I know the Black Dragon as well as anyone. She's surprisingly shy and keeps to herself, but we've had a few interactions in my time here.\n\nI know everyone in the enclave to some degree. Aside from the new recruits, that is.
No? Did you expect me to attack you and cut you down the moment I saw you?\n\nWell, as you can see, I'm not exactly armed and dressed for battle.

The Black Dragon … how do I begin? She's hard for me to describe. She's powerful, no doubt. Dangerous. Someone best observed from a safe distance.\n\nYou should forget about her. I'd hate to see you die just when we were getting to know each other.

I'm not a warmonger. I don't make a habit of attacking rashly and without purpose.\n\nBesides, I don't know you. I have no idea of your capabilities, your strengths and weaknesses. I prefer to know my opponent before I ever draw my blade.
You flatter me! Come. Her chambers are right over there. You'll find out who the Black Dragon really is soon enough.

I have seen many such women in this city. I heard the Governor wore one at a recent appearance and now the custom has become a sort of fashion statement.\n\nSorry I cannot be of more assistance to you, wayfarer.

I saw a young Nord with a flower in her hair talking to Chanter Nemus, over by the Akatosh shrine. \n\nI remember because it was so odd. He was whispering in her ear and standing much too close for a man who wasn't her father or her lover.
Redemption isn't for everyone, and I'd never presume to do such a thing. Unless, of course, you're open to the idea.\n\nDo you regret your role in all of this? You can tell me. I'm a good listener.
The Primate says regrets are as numerous as the stars in the sky and they shine brightest in the darkness.\n\nBut I don't want to talk about religion anymore, do you?

Regret is a specter of the past that haunts the present. If you had regrets, I'd tell you to leave this place. Leave the Gold Coast. Go far away and find whatever peace you can.\n\nIf only I listened to my own advice ….

No, no, of course not. A man as pious as Chanter Nemus would never do anything untoward with a young Nord woman. I mean, even the rumor of such an event would be scandalous.\n\nDon't worry, though. I won't say a word about your friend and the Chanter.

I knew that Chanter was up to no good! Sneaking around, meeting with mysterious young Nords with flowers in their hair. It's simply scandalous!\n\nDon't worry, though. I'll leave your friend out of this when I tell my story at the tavern tonight.

Now that you mention it, I remember a young woman—no wait, that was a Wood Elf. Carried around a bouquet of flowers. Talked to them, smelled them. Then she ate them!\n\nReally, Wood Elves are very strange.

A Nord? Here? Is that even possible? I have it on good authority that the typical Nord melts in hot temperatures.\n\nCome to think of it, I'm surprised I've never met a Nord. One more thing to do before I finish my memoirs, I suppose.

We have been watching you for a long time. Killing the noble simply sealed our covenant. Now you need to meet your Brothers and Sisters.\n\nI will send you to a Sanctuary. A safehouse of sorts. A home, as well as a source of additional contracts.
Wait, you're <<1>>'s friend! I've seen you both around town. Always kind to me, that one.\n\nI'll tell you what I know.

The Iron Wheel caught your man. The one in charge was angry—said they'd take him to "Processing" because he fled.\n\nThat's a patch of sand outside Abah's Landing where they beat prisoners.  Here, I'll mark your map.

Not far. It's the reason I summoned you to the Gold Coast. There is much work to accomplish here, and you will be a part of that.\n\nYour new home lies to the north, hidden beneath Varen's Wall. Go there and attempt to open the Black Door.

The Black Door will pose a question: "What is the flavor of fear?" Reply, "Sublime, my Brother," and the Sanctuary shall be opened to you.\n\nOnce inside, seek out Astara. She has additional instructions for you.

Oh, believe me, I tried! When they were finished, the poor young woman had tears streaming down her face. She ran out of the Chapel as the Chanter looked on.  He had a self-satisfied smile on his face.\n\nDo you think he said something … improper?

A Chanter spoke with Hilde? That's not what I wanted to hear!\n\nUnderstand, Hilde isn't like us. She grew up in the wild. The idea of being civilized is really new to her. And she still feels guilty about the wolf that's inside her.

It certainly sounds that way to me. It doesn't take much to turn her guilt about what she's done as a wolf into self-loathing. I'm constantly trying to get her to change her feelings on the matter, but her beliefs run deep.

Back to where it all began. Back to Skyrim.\n\nI'll check at the docks to see if she's tried to secure passage on a ship. You go talk to the caravan master. Hopefully one of us will discover which route she took to go back to where the wolf was born.
Allow me to explain! I need a partner for a difficult job. It pays well, but it involves travel, and there is some danger. Does that sound like the sort of thing that might interest you?

Well, isn't that interesting. You're the second menacing stranger that's asked me about a Nord who may or may not have fled in tears.\n\nEven if I had seen this young woman, why do you think I'd tell you anything?

Right. Her family. The way that young woman was crying, you'd think Molag Bal himself was after her. Or someone like you.\n\nIf I had helped the Nord—and I'm not saying I did—you'd have to do a lot better than that to get me to tell you anything.

Don't repeat what I say. It annoys me. Now where was I? Oh yes, your training.\n\nComplete a contract, receive a reward. Prove yourself, and more significant contracts will be made available to you. It's simple, really.

The Silver Dawn are werewolf hunters! Whatever that Chanter said to Hilde has made her run back to the wilderness where I found her, and now a hunting party is on her trail.\n\nThey're going to kill her, Initiate!
The Black Dragon is one of the Order? That puts everything that she's done to us in a new perspective.\n\nWhat else did you uncover?

The Grand Sermonizer, the Chanters, now an army of religious warriors. It seems the priests of Akatosh have declared war against the Dark Brotherhood.\n\nWere you able to learn anything else about the Black Dragon?
So the Count was using the ruins of Dasek Moor to spy on the Order of the Hour?\n\nNow if we only had some idea as to who's inside the Black Dragon's armor.

You encountered the Black Dragon? And you survived? But Mirabelle … why was she even there? I knew her recklessness was going to get her killed. And now we face a greater threat.\n\nFor all that you learned, there's still so much we don't know.

One of our Brothers and Sisters? I don't recognize the name, but there are other Sanctuaries. Why would our Sister hunt us? And why work for the Order of the Hour?\n\nWhere's Mirabelle? I need her to do some digging ….

Then hop aboard the wagon and let's get going. I'll get you there as fast as I can without throwing a wheel. Well, at least without throwing more than one.\n\nIf the Silver Dawn hunts your friend, you better be ready for a fight.
Are you sure? Nothing else you need to accomplish before we head out?
Of course. I am one of Akatosh's Chanters, after all.\n\nBut why in the name of the Dragon God of Time are you interested in the Primate's seal?

All servants are banned from our headquarters, on pain of interrogation. Not that I call you a liar, simply that what you say cannot be at all correct.\n\nBut I do not care to know your truth! Leave me be and I shall forget you completely.

I meant to. But the Chanter told me I had to flee. He said my past and my wild nature were going to cause the people I love to come to harm. He said the deaths of our Brothers and Sisters were my fault—and it was going to get worse if I remained.

No! Why would the Chanter do that? He told me to return to my old life, to the wilderness. He said I'd be safe, that no one else would get hurt if I left.\n\nHe promised that Akatosh would show me the way!

The Chanter sings to the Divines. He speaks for Akatosh! I had to tell him things. About me. About the family.\n\nIt happened before. I was a danger to my wolf clan. Now I am a danger to Kor. To you and the others. You're all better off without me.

I … I—you're right. I should never have listened to the Chanter. But after what happened to Tanek, I let my fear of losing my family drive me to do something stupid. I should have come back and talked to Kor.\n\nI—I'm sorry. I'm … I'm so sorry.

You … you really mean that? Even after I abandoned the family, you still want me around? I'm sorry I caused so much trouble. I let my fear allow the Chanter to deceive me. That is not going to happen again. Kor and I, we'll handle things. Together.
An old overgrown Daedra shrine frequented by those who value privacy. Nothing to worry about aside from those who've taken roost. I think.

I know. And I will. I'm just not eager to see Astara. She won't be pleased when she hears about this.\n\nI wish I knew what Chanter Nemus hoped to accomplish. Someone needs to stick a fork in him and call him done. Anyway, we'll see you back home.

I would think its purpose is pretty clear, but it's the finer details that are of interest, eh? A smugglers' cove of some convenience, a little too well known for anyone to stick around for long. Expect the current tenants to be quite vigilant.

No, no. The guild has more interest in gold that still glitters. Old tunnels simply make for good shelter from prying eyes, unless they know where to look.\n\nThese recent arrivals are sure to have set snares and sentries, so waste no care on ghosts.
It is a beautiful place, but don't let the gleam distract you from the dangers within. The lush overgrowth makes it ideal for traps of all kinds. Mind your toes if you wish to keep them.

Oh yes, a place of untold treasure. If you like rats. Personally, I find them delicious.\n\nAbah's Landing has many cracks to fall through, boss. Some choose to wriggle down them and stay beneath notice. Many times they have something worth hiding.
I'll need an explanation.\n\nAnd if I'm not satisfied, you can join "<<1>>" on the other side of the gate.

Scout ahead and find us a way inside. Clear the way, if you care to—the Iron Wheel can't exactly call for reinforcements.\n\nYou could also sneak past them. We'll track your progress and follow in your footsteps.
That's a question for <<1>>.\n\nBut he isn't here, so we'll have to make do with the front door.
That's why we brought <<1>>.\n\nHe said something about a side entrance? Speak with him before you go.

Years ago. But I realized it was a weakness he could exploit. Didn't care to be manipulated.\n\nIf I survive to my thirty-fifth year, I'll retire on a pile of ill-gotten coin and meet someone who fits me. Find some remote place where I can just live.
Oh.\n\nTake it from me, it's best not to fall for your guildmaster.
Good.\n\nI've been on the other end of that discussion before. Not my best moment.
Good.\n\nUntil <<1>> is dealt with, the only attachment I have is to the Thieves Guild.
Until then, I have a guild to run.\n\nGo, pick your date. I'll meet you at the Diamond Thimble.
That's … no. Absolutely not. Pull those thoughts back inside your trousers, set them afire, and bury their remains.
The lesser soulgem of wit strikes again.\n\nAre you done wasting everyone's time? Go on, choose someone so we can get this over with.
Чому?
Stinks of an inside job to me, but if our buyer wants to skim a little off the top, who are we to judge? We will charge extra for the added care, of course.

Head to the tomb entrance. Keep watch to the side of the path—the right side. You should notice an old trail leading to a sealed entrance.\n\nSimply clear the way and I shall join you to open the door.
Oh my, no. The things inside would most certainly kill me.\n\nI do know the trick to the door's hidden latch. The rest, I'm certain you can handle yourself.

You ask the most interesting questions. Let me jot that down. After we get to Blackwood, Shazara-Ta will take us up the river to Sanctuary.\n\nDon't worry. Shazara-Ta's an excellent boat handler. She knows those rivers like the tip of her tail.

Another excellent question! Keep them coming, Assassin!\n\nI believe in preparing for every contingency. So I brought along this resin. When burned, its fumes reveal things that are hidden from our feeble eyes.

It means I was kept in the dark about the purification. I understand why they thought that was necessary, but it doesn't change the fact that I had to learn the truth on my own. Lyra didn't die in the purge—she was the Black Hand's sword.

Before his grandness Artorius ascended to the top of the religious hierarchy, Primate Jonas was the tip of the tower as far as Akatosh's followers were concerned.\n\nThere were rumors, but this proves that Jonas didn't succumb to natural causes.

The people call it Mazzatun. The Puzzle City. The Xit-Xaht tribe has lived here for centuries—since before the creeks turned to rivers. And in all that time, they have never stopped building. They build, and build, and build. It is a sickness.

Like I said, it is crazy. It could be root-weevils, or bad water. Or maybe it has just lived too long. My uncle lived to be one hundred and he died thinking he was a marsh-hen.\n\nAll I know is that it makes its children build stone houses. Forever.
Heart-sickness. Their Hist tree, the Tsono-Xuhil, is crazy. Obsessed. Most Hist tell the Saxhleel to cast their rocks into the pond and build with reed and mud. This Hist doesn't.
I am an adventurer, like you. Or I will be. Do not let my humble appearance fool you. I am very canny—and I wield a fish hook and knife better than any of my tribesmen.
Yes. But not for much longer. We will see to that, right?
I'd intended to draw the eyes from your own stylistic monstrosity. You nearly outdid me.\n\nLet's go. These boots are killing me.
Feels like a torture device.\n\nAre we going in? I'm already regretting this.
Good.\n\nLet's get this over with.
Someone close to her might know. A relative, maybe? Perhaps one of the servants here knows.
Not while the Iron Wheel is lurking about.\n\nWe have to find another way in. Somewhere we can enter without notice.
But why? I don't understand.
Yes, that is … for the best.\n\nAfter, you must tell me how many fountains you see. A three fountain palace is barely a palace. You need at least five to be respectable.
As a valued associate of the Thieves Guild?\n\nI still don't understand.

Yes, I know. But it was the only outfit that matched the ink on the invitations. Practical outweighs fashionable when you're doing two things at once.\n\nThere are five stains somewhere on this outfit. Go on, try to spot them. Ha! You can't, can you?

To be honest, I thought I looked like one of those strange carvings on a ship's prow.\n\nBut it looks good on me, you say? Then we shall be the fanciest spies in the palace! Which I should not say aloud here, I'm sorry, I'll be quiet.
Truly? I hope it is all that you imagined and more.

Inside this mausoleum. When they expanded the catacombs under the Cathedral some years back, the floor of this crypt collapsed. If you're squeamish, don't worry. Somebody was kind enough to relocate the bodies.\n\nI had no trouble expanding the hole.
Heavy lifting? More like heavy digging. I had to clear some rubble out of the way, but now there's a passage that's big enough to maneuver through.

No, it is exactly as dangerous as I think. But I cannot let that prevent me from rescuing my friends and clutch-mates. If I could face the Bone-Trout of Drash and survive, I can make it through the Puzzle City.

No, of course not. I live on the chopping edge of danger and excitement. I have written all my adventures down if you wish to read them. There was the Great Shell Caper, and the Outrageous Eel Escape. They all have excellent names like that.

I imagine that we will face many, many Xit-Xaht warriors. Beyond that, it is hard to say.\n\nMazzatun is a mystery to almost everyone. I have heard stories about gigantic monsters, and strange Hist sap rituals, but they could all be fish tales.
Suit yourself. I wouldn't want to terribly outclass you in fashionable attire. I don't know how I could ever respect you.

I am many things to many people. How do you know I'm not catering myself to your expectations, to ensure you think me important? Is it because you want me to be, or because I encouraged you to believe it?\n\nBut I'm probably joking about all that.
That's funny, I selected an outfit I thought would best match yours. In a way, we have both condemned your taste.\n\nCome, let's get to the wedding.
Just … just "good?" Not "resplendent," "striking," or even "unforgettable?" \n\nMust be losing my touch.
Not my underclothes. They have fins to help me swim faster.\n\nThe best part? You have no idea if I'm joking.
Maybe one day, when this is all over, we can speak about this further.\n\nFor now, let's focus on clearing our names. All right?
When this all began, I hired you to work for me. Now, <<1>> has me following your lead.\n\nWhat I'm saying is, it's strange to hear this from someone I work with.

Other than the mad Hist tree? Yes. Their Tree-Minder is a mage called Na-Kesh. I am told she is a cunning alchemist, with a golden tongue and scales as thick as oak bark. If we want to stop the Xit-Xaht for good, we will have to slay her.
Thanks for rubbing it in, partner.\n\nLet's go inside. If this is the current fashion in Abah's Landing, I can blend in with all the other ridiculous outfits.
It's nice of you to say so, but we both know this suits me as well as a ticket for a month-long sea voyage.
Not without showing the wedding party a third moon in the sky.\n\nCome on, no use standing about.

Not me, but I have something for you. A letter. Confidential. Private. I have it here somewhere. Yes, here it is!\n\nInteresting. I'm also supposed to extend a verbal invitation to visit the lighthouse. Odd that they didn't just put that in the letter.

Yes, the Anvil Lighthouse. Just up the way. The sender ordered me to direct you there after I handed over the letter.\n\nI'm glad I found you. After looking for the woman with the eye-patch all day, I figured I was in for a late night.
Not breaking my word is important too. \n\nBut also mead. Mead is important.
Gold! I like gold!\n\nI met a Khajiit woman in Rawl'kha while I was drinking at the inn. She paid me to deliver the letter to the Dark Elf lady here. Never got the Khajiit's name, though. Sorry.

You'd tell my uncle? That's not very friendly of you.\n\nOh very well! I met a Khajiit woman in Rawl'kha, when I was drinking at the inn. She paid me to deliver the letter to the Dark Elf lady here. Never got the Khajiit's name, though. Sorry.
Not breaking my word is important too. \n\nBut also mead. Mead is important.
Gold! I like gold!\n\nI met a Khajiit woman in Evermore while I was drinking at the inn. She paid me to deliver the letter to the Dark Elf lady here. Never got the Khajiit's name, though. Sorry.

You'd tell my uncle? That's not very friendly of you.\n\nOh very well! I met a Khajiit woman in Evermore, when I was drinking at the inn. She paid me to deliver the letter to the Dark Elf lady here. Never got the Khajiit's name, though. Sorry.
Not breaking my word is important too. \n\nBut also mead. Mead is important.
Then the head of the beast has been cut off. Well done, Assassin!\n\nWe will reach out to Count Carolus and the Order of the Hour to make sure this ill-conceived war ends here.
Exulus isn't a person—it's a thing. An abomination before Arkay. It must be destroyed! It, and its thrice-cursed spawn!
By Arkay's grace, Exulus and her vile brood must be cleansed and the Hrota Cave made safe once more.\n\nBut make no mistake. Exulus is the root of evil there.

Exulus considers the twin horrors to be its children, but no one actually knows the biology of such deplorable creatures.\n\nWhat I do know is that all of them feed on the lives of innocents. Every warrior of Arkay I've sent against them has fallen.

If I knew how to destroy the vile creature, don't you think I'd have already done so?\n\nBut I can tell you this. Exulus turns those it defeats into undead thralls. When you face Exulus, you'll be confronting a legion of the risen dead.

This is his handwriting. But it could have been taken from his journal by someone else.\n\nThe skeleton must be Danobia herself. This is her tomb, after all. I don't see what it has to do with <<1>>, missing skull or not.

Trash he left behind. Three dots on a page are meaningless, unless you know the trick. The only people who did were dead on Malooc's Path.\n\nHead to Hew's Bane. If <<1>> does have a hideout in the desert, it's time we crack it open.

Just what the rest of us know. <<1>>, our former guildmaster, planned to steal <<2>>'s dowry from her family tomb. He brought <<3>> and a few others—the best of the guild.\n\n<<3>> is the only one who made it out alive.
<<1>> hasn't shared the details. She watched her friends die, I know that much.\n\n<<2>> wasn't exactly a father to her, but she took his death the hardest.

We thought they were punishing us for our failed attempt. But you overheard <<1>> himself. The dowry was stolen.\n\nFor some reason, the Iron Wheel thinks we have it. And they'll keep after us until they learn otherwise.

A dowry is like a coin pouch. When it's full, everyone wants something from you. That makes you feel important, and maybe you are.\n\nBut when it's empty, nobody has time for you. It's why <<1>> is relying on the Iron Wheel to find it.
A good tip is only one of the services I provide, boss. Think of Fa'ren-dar as your observer, guide, and porter. You handle the theft, I will handle the rest.
You sound like <<1>>, going on about the whims of nobles. Go ahead, ask him, and feel your head start to spin.\n\nMy head's spinning right now. Different reasons.
The bounty? Says right on it what to do to get paid. What more could you want to know?
Of course! I even offered payment to get rid of it, but they said it was "worth the risk." To them maybe! I disagree, so my gold can go to you—if you get rid of the foul creature.

All right, all right, that's fair. Those Gold Coast traders have been capturing all sort of nasty brutes out in Craglorn. This <<1>>, though. It's a real monster!\n\nBig armored troll. Huge! Could smash the whole city! Best not to take chances, right?

I don't know. Around! Definitely somewhere in the ruins, though.\n\nIf they're still being scribbled in, the ledgers will be on someone's desk or scattered around on the work areas. I'm not picky, just grab whatever you can find. It'll be fine!
Oh, thank the Eight! I was wondering if anyone would be willing to take such a request seriously.\n\nWhen I was writing about disembodied voices and menacing shadows, I felt rather foolish.

Ruins excite the imagination, I know, but my workers came wailing out of that smoking hole like it was a gate to Oblivion itself. I believe them when they say shadowy figures emerged from the darkness. And the wounds they suffered were real enough.

Anything we had excavated was abandoned near the entrance to the dig after my panicked workers went running for the hills.\n\nEven the few we'd manage to remove vanished in the night. They could have been stolen, but I'm not so sure.

Ah, of course. You're one of them. I wasn't sure you'd honor my request since I refused to perform that ghoulish ritual of yours.\n\nI suppose even the Brotherhood can be bought—for the right amount of gold.

My spies watch the Order's old headquarters from this camp. Saw supply carts start arriving a few days ago.\n\nIf you want to weaken the Order, destroy their siege weapons and stop them from initiating more recruits. You'll be doing us both a favor.

My back was against the wall. Between Anvil's aggressive overtures and the rampant increase in murders, I needed help. Primate Artorius offered the Order and I reluctantly agreed.\n\nThat was before I learned the Black Dragon was one of their number.

I do like hearing myself talk, but this is ridiculous. Ah, well.\n\nThe Hour holds Castle Kvatch under lock and key. You'll need to find a way inside to get at Scipio. My Rat Master tells me the guard tower is the best route. The castellan has the key.

I prefer to convey my orders directly, so that nothing gets lost in the translation.\n\nYou know about the Order of the Hour? The religious warriors that protect the Kvatch Cathedral? They've expanded their mandate and now pose a threat I can't ignore.

You're just going to stand there, all dark and silent? Well, I wanted to convey my orders directly so there'd be no misunderstanding.\n\nThe Order of the Hour has expanded its mandate beyond the Kvatch Cathedral. That's a threat I can't ignore.

The Primate offered pardons to any Red Sails pirates who agreed to take the vows of the Order. Since Fortunata's death, they've been flocking to the enclave.\n\nI wish I knew what Artorius was planning to do with an army of priests and pirates.
Do you, now? I suppose you have a writ from the Count? Or maybe a seal from Primate Artorius or a pass from an Hour officer?\n\nNo? I didn't think so. Move along.

You can't. Not unless you're a new Hour recruit or you're one of the Chanters from the Cathedral. Other than that, no one else is allowed in the castle at this time.\n\nNow move along before you get on my bad side.

You know, a scroll bearing the hallowed seal of the Primate of Akatosh. Shows you have the Primate's blessing.\n\nWithout one of those identifying documents, we'd have no way of knowing who belongs in the castle and who doesn't.
The Night Mother heard the Count's prayer and Fortunata ap Dugal has been named. Her soul is promised to Sithis now. And you will keep that promise.\n\nThe Count's contract is yours to fulfill.

Very good. Seek out your Sister, Mirabelle, in Anvil Castle. She can provide aid and advice should you need it.\n\nThe secret exit in the dignitary suite is the fastest route out of this castle. Now go and fulfill the Night Mother's will.

You completed Fortunata's contract to the letter. No one can say that the Brotherhood didn't discharge its obligations in that regard. Now we have a new contract, and not all the gold in Anvil can change that.\n\nThe Count's sacrament is yours.

Oh, do you now? Look, if I don't know you, you aren't worth knowing. \n\nYou want to earn a name worthy of being on the same card as one of our champions, get in the pit and start drawing in some crowds!

You'll face whatever I can pull together for the day's events, and even I don't often know what that'll be much in advance. Criminals, heretics, wild beasts. If you can't roll with the punches, at least leap to your grave. The crowd loves that.

Find yourself in that pit and your life is property of this arena until you claw your way out. Manage that and there's a hefty purse waiting on the other side. \n\nThat's the contract in full. Don't expect me to waste paper to put it in writing.

If you're friendly with my sister, don't expect any special treatment. Fixed fights don't draw crowds.\n\nIf you've got a problem with her, take it to Anvil. Nobody holds sway over the Pirate Queen, least of all me.
Interesting. I knew we were going to eliminate the Pirate Queen eventually, but I didn't expect that today would be the day.\n\nWhy the sudden change, I wonder?

He did? I'm impressed. I didn't think the old Count had it in him to ask the Night Mother for help.\n\nFirst the Governor contracts you to perform a kill, and then you get a contract to kill her. The Speaker must love this!

Of course he did. I've been studying the castle and the Governor's habits for months now.\n\nShe keeps a pantry on the upper level. I suggest a dose of poison. Drop it in her favorite decanter of wine and that should do the trick.
That's perfect. Splendid, even. I'm going to overlook the way you so rudely barged in here and offer you a drink. \n\nJoin me on my balcony. I'm sure you'll appreciate the view.

As with many things, the answer is food. Little grows in Hew's Bane, so food must be imported. The Iron Wheel shipped in their own supplies, but the shipments have stopped.\n\nThis means they plan to leave. No more food, no more Iron Wheel.

Here, the answer is drinks. With the Iron Wheel's supplies low, some grew restless.\n\nThey may have discreetly attended local taverns. And I may have bought them many rounds to learn such things. For which I require no reimbursement, I assure you.

I once gave you a chance to surrender, to which you were … somewhat amenable.\n\nSo I say, surrender yourself to the Iron Wheel. You will be treated fairly until I can determine exactly who will be tried in Taneth.
You mean <<1>>? He insists he was duped by the Thieves Guild. His story doesn't completely add up, but <<2>> has not spoken since her arrival.\n\nWithout proof, his story is the most convincing.
"Dowry heist?" You name your crimes?\n\nI once gave you a chance to surrender. Instead, you attacked my men and fled with a valuable relic. I'm not inclined to take you at your word.

Not who—what. A giant haj mota by the sounds of it. There are stories about Na-Kesh using tonics to grow monsters but …. Just be careful. Even baby haj mota are dangerous.\n\nI will rush in to help as soon as I am able.
No. I tried to sneak behind one of the Xit-Xaht—catch him unaware. It turns out that I am very, very loud.

I will put my arm back in its socket. I should have done it while my clutch-mates were still here. Putting your own arm back into its socket is a very brawny and impressive thing to do. Anyway, you should keep going.
Так.

The Thieves Guild doesn't murder. And yet <<1>> was the cause of so much suffering.\n\nI shouldn't ask you to do that. In fact, I can't. But if you find him alive and leave him dead … I'll consider him the exception.
A pleasant little manor outside of … Haven, I believe? In Grahtwood.\n\nI can't remember anything else. The drink, you see. But they were to be married as soon as they returned.
A lovely manor near Sentinel. In Alik'r?\n\nThat's all I remember. The drink, you see. But they were to be married as soon as they returned.
A manor near some fort in Deshaan. Fort … Tal'Deic, was it?\n\nI don't entirely recall. The drink, you see. But they were to be married as soon as they returned home.

We thought Abah's Landing was full of bandits! The merchant lords pointed us in your guild's direction. When I realized they used us to settle old debts, I withdrew the Iron Wheel to <<1>>. \n\nYou think me heartless? That I don't regret our methods?
Why does it matter to you? Some sort of vendetta on <<1>>'s behalf?\n\nNo, don't tell me. I don't want to know.
I'm not helping you, I'm ending my involvement.\n\nI'm done with his case. There's neither profit nor honor in its resolution.

First thing, he didn't go by "<<1>>." Can't recall his name—something equally forgettable—but I do remember his High Elf companion.\n\nA widow, she was. "My darling Volu," he called her? They were returning to her home.

Oh, she'd fallen for him, I could see that. He was some sort of … painter? The canvas kind, not tavern placards.\n\nHe brought some kind of joy to her life. Would have been lovely, but I passed out on their table.
Very well.\n\nWe both know my part in what happened to the Thieves Guild. I won't beg for my life, if that's what you're expecting. If that's what <<1>> wants from me.
Ask. I'll tell you everything you want to know. No more secrets.\n\nNone of them matter anymore.
I have a relative at the bank. I'll ensure my funds are protected.\n\nWhatever he's called, he won't leave here with a single coin.
I will have this false marriage annulled.\n\nBefore this day ends, I'll ensure he's deported from these lands.
You don't get around much, do you? I thought it would be obvious. This is a mill! But I don't sell by the sack. Only bushels to merchants for sale throughout the region.

I didn't fight, if that's what you're asking. I repaired weapons and armor, crafted items, that sort of thing. The workshop is still set up in the barn. You're welcome to use it so long as you don't burn the place down, I suppose.

You think so? But this is where the grain grows best. Besides, I had to do something with the place after Varen's rebellion came to an end.\n\nWhen the legions stopped coming through, I converted my workshops into a mill, and here we are.
Ah, a ruse is it? You're not supposed to leave the Imperial City! I understand. Never fear, Emperor Varen, my lips are sealed.
Oh, right, right. Not Emperor Varen. Just a stranger come to use the forges. Feel free! I'll not tell the Legions, not me.
But I love her!\n\nI see … <<1>> wants you to take away what's important to me. Go on, then. Do what you must.
Truly?\n\nYou will never hear from me again. I swear it upon the love I hold for my dear wife. This home, my wife … it's all I shall ever want.

They barely touched me—just enough to tie me up. Didn't want to get any dye on them. I knew it was a bad look.\n\nI didn't tell them anything, if you're wondering. They don't know we're to meet <<1>> at Prince's Gate.
Yes, I think so. Don't worry about an escort, I'm no longer tracking dye behind me. I'll lose them along the way.\n\nSee you at Prince's Gate?
This is where they died. Edda, Daldur, and <<1>> … swallowed by the darkness. \n\nI'm sorry, I can't talk about this. No use reliving the past … or regretting it.

That's fair. Talking about it might calm my nerves.\n\nThe darkness is unnatural—breathe it in, and it sickens you. To make things worse, the guardians on the path attack anyone not of Danobia's bloodline. And then there's the path itself.

It twists and turns. You don't know where you're going until you're out there. You'll see what I mean.\n\nKeep your wits about you. Stay with me, inside the light, and we'll make it through. I won't let anyone else die in here.
I've never had a partner.\n\nI mean, on all the other big jobs I've done—which I did alone. Quite successfully. And most of the people I interviewed thought the rendezvous was too far away.
Well, I paid for a ship in advance. I didn't realize how far I'd have to look to find a suitable partner. For the job, I mean.\n\nBut we can talk about this at the docks!
Well, I paid for a ship in advance. I didn't realize how far I'd have to look to find a suitable partner. For the job, I mean.\n\nBut we can talk about this at the docks!
Well, I paid for a ship in advance. I didn't realize how far I'd have to look to find a suitable partner. For the job, I mean.\n\nBut we can talk about this at the docks!
The newest job is always the biggest job!\n\nLife of a thief. You know how it is.
Well … this is the biggest job I've ever attempted. But I did the research, arranged transportation, and knew I needed a good partner to pull it off.\n\nThat's why I hired you!
Nothing we should discuss right here.\n\nBut I promise, as soon as we've escaped the Iron Wheel, I'll answer your questions.
Hidden within an old cistern that's long forgotten by this city's merchant lords. A new home for us, after the Iron Wheel tore apart the old one.\n\nIt's a bit damp. You get used to it.
What about?
Of course.

The more we steal, the better our reputation. Best way to draw in more recruits after taking such a hit from the Iron Wheel.\n\n<<1>> has more to say about it. Word of advice? Don't rearrange her tip board—she'll smack your hand something fierce.

Start with the tip board—there's always something coming in. Also, <<1>> is a friend of the guild who could use our particular skills.\n\nIf there are any larger tasks, I'll have <<2>> or <<3>> get word to you.

He can explain. It's the sort of work I'd normally turn down, but he always pays. And he stuck with us, even after the Iron Wheel's raids.\n\nHe's welcome to trade gold for worthless trinkets as long as he cares to do so.

At times the whole guild works toward a single goal. Driving the Iron Wheel from Hew's Bane, strong-arming a merchant lord … big stuff.\n\nBut that takes time to plan. If it's happening, I'll get word to you the next time you stop by <<c:1>>.
The Iron Wheel, without question.
What about?

They're bastards. Oh, you want more?\n\n<<1>> sent them to punish us for failing to steal her dowry. It's a bad deal all around, except for the Iron Wheel—they're paid to knock our heads together, and keep anything they confiscate.

It had already started when I returned from the dowry heist. The merchant lords let it happen. They called their guards off the streets—let the Iron Wheel smash down our doors, pull us from our homes, and slaughter anyone who ran.\n\nBastards.

I haven't asked them, but I can guess. The Iron Wheel will leave Abah's Landing when they find every member of the Thieves Guild, ship us to Taneth for show trials, and fit our heads to pikes.\n\nSecond thoughts? Too late to back out.

Before the Iron Wheel? We ran the shadows of Abah's Landing. Played the merchant lords against each other.\n\nWe were looking to expand—take the Thieves Guild beyond Hew's Bane. But the dowry heist put an end to those plans.
<<1>>. A good man, sorely missed.\n\nSorry, I don't want to talk about him. It's still fresh, you know?

You're looking at it. We're a shadow of what we were before the Iron Wheel cracked down.\n\nAnd without us to bridle them, the merchant lords are flexing their muscles. Picking up the rackets we used to control.
<<1>> was right, and I don't say that lightly. I am responsible. Edda and Daldur died because of my mistake.\n\n<<2>> … I can only pray his death is far worse than what happened to the others.
No. He seemed a bit distant before we first went to <<c:1>>, but it was also the biggest heist we'd ever pulled off.\n\nNothing prepared me for this.
Because she knows it can't be you. You weren't a part of the guild when the Iron Wheel first attacked.\n\nAlso, she knows you can handle yourself.
The Iron Wheel struck us shortly after the dowry heist. They knew where to find every stash, safe house, and hiding spot. The only way to do that was with knowledge from the inside.

<<1>>, our old guildmaster, had a plan to raid the family tomb of a Taneth noble. He died when the heist went bad—so did nearly all the rest. The best of us, cut down when they were needed most.\n\nOnly <<2>> survived. Ugly business.

I thought it was obvious. She can trust you because you weren't around when the Iron Wheel smashed us in the soft bits.\n\nUnless you can move through time. I hear Dwarves could do that. But you don't look a Dwarf.

You don't think it's strange the Iron Wheel knew exactly which nooks and crannies to plunder? They nicked most of our wealth and people in three days!\n\nThe dowry heist was bad luck for the guild. Shouldn't rob a tomb when there's fat pockets aplenty.

The old guildmaster, <<1>>? He had some scheme to raid the family tomb of one "<<2>>." But everyone who went died … everyone but <<3>>.\n\nThe price for failing to raid a noble's family tomb appears to be the Iron Wheel. Bit of an awful bargain.
Our old guildmaster. A mentor, and a friend. He planned the dowry heist that would have seen us wealthy beyond our dreams.\n\nBut he's gone. I lost him in <<1>>'s family tomb. He is … sorely missed.
The name is new to me. But we haven't been keeping as close an eye on the merchant lords as we used to.\n\nWhoever he is, he seems ambitious.

The magnates who pretend to run Abah's Landing. They buy and sell to anyone—it's why the pirates offload their goods in this port.\n\nTake away all their riches and they'd be little more than bandits. But all the gold makes them think they're nobles.
All the time. Our old guildmaster <<1>> was a master at playing them against one another. They spent so much time watching each other's moves, they never saw our own.

Haven't heard the name before <<1>> said it. Some new merchant lord, trying to make a name. But don't they all?\n\nUsed to be the Thieves Guild knew every move the merchant lords made. Sad times, sad times.

Bunch of jumped up bandits, if you ask me. Claim to run the whole city because they buy from anyone.\n\nAs if throwing gold at pirates made them lordly. Without a steady flow of plundered goods, they'd be nothing.

Like herons, we did. Our old guildmaster was a master at keeping their attentions on each other. Made it easier to slip our hands in their pockets.\n\nOh, <<1>>. The next five drinks are to your memory.

When <<1>> was guildmaster, I convinced him to stop dealing with skooma peddlers. No matter my own thoughts on that poison, it's bad for business.\n\nAnd the Thieves Guild never dealt in slaves. One of the few things <<2>> and I agree on.

Not enough. Some of the merchant lords prefer to bide their time in obscurity, using trusted servants to handle their affairs. Then they reveal themselves, like a beetle in the pudding.\n\nWhatever <<1>> intends, he's no longer keeping to the shadows.

Harpy egg.\n\nThey're sickening—I'd never actually eat one. But they're garish enough to draw attention from me. People see the "Argonian with disgusting harpy eggs," not the "Argonian with amazing fashion sense."
That's good to hear.\n\nSee you later, partner.

Paranoia, of course. No servants are allowed inside.\n\nFrom what I hear, the Iron Wheel takes care of all chores within their headquarters. Anyone who isn't Iron Wheel, or escorted by them, is attacked on sight. A truly noble organization.

I am physically capable of doing so, but it will never happen. I'd rather not end up in a prison cell.\n\nAnd a uniform alone won't serve as a disguise. They have too many signals and mannerisms. You'd be spotted in an instant.
Yes, I did.\n\nYou're not supposed to throw my words back at me. Reminds me of <<1>>.
I … I have a sleeping draught! One sip helps me through the nights. The whole bottle will knock me out for hours! You'll be long gone.
What about?
<<1>> told <<2>> he was planning a heist, but she retired before he shared the details.\n\nI'm the only one who knew. Someone must have followed us to the tomb.
The merchant lords see the Iron Wheel as an occupying force. They fear Taneth wants to conquer Abah's Landing.\n\nIf <<1>> convinces <<2>> to leave, he'll have immense influence. Must be his plan.
What about?
You're not the first person to ask.\n\nShe's actually mellowed since her retirement. It's … eerie.
No. I've not heard of anyone with that name. Couldn't even guess the ancestry.\n\nI'll ask <<1>> and <<2>> to keep their ears open. If <<3>> is a threat, we'll know.
I know <<1>> doesn't like to talk about it. Lost the best of the guild to that folly.\n\n<<2>> thought he could steal <<3>>'s dowry from her family tomb.
<<1>> was wrong. Everyone died but <<2>>. For a guildmaster, he should've known better than to bet everything on a single heist.\n\nBest you don't repeat that to <<2>>.

Someone pinned the blame on the guild. Used to think the Iron Wheel wanted revenge for us trespassing in <<1>>'s family tomb.\n\nBut <<2>> is after the missing dowry—you heard it yourself. No idea who really took it. No idea why.

You think I know a lick about dowries? You trying to flatter me?\n\nA dowry is like a bar tab—it's the promise of available drinks, not the drinks themselves. But if there was no tab, why would anyone go to that bar? You see? Good, that's one of us.
Not after the merchant lords caught wind. It's good to be the preeminent tailor of Abah's Landing.\n\n<<1>> himself sent a personal apology. Something about excess zeal on the part of his underling.
Better now that I'm out of that cell. I can't wait to return to <<c:1>>.\n\nAfter we've taken care of some business.

Thieves Guild business. The Iron Wheel thought to save themselves another trip to Taneth. They loaded this ship with contraband.\n\nBut we're going to steal it. We're going to take everything they squeezed from Abah's Landing.

As good as rain on a hot day! Not only was crime run as a business, never taking more than a victim could afford, but they also practiced a sort of "functional corruption." Kept order by playing the merchants lords off one another.\n\nIt was masterful!
I procured it for him.\n\nI saw him drop the lamp. It hit the path and went out. Then, all I remember is darkness and pain.
I ….\n\nJust grab the ashes so we can leave. I don't want to spend any more time in this place.
Not far. Just over the border into Black Marsh, as a matter of fact.\n\nI haven't been back there in many years. I wonder what we'll find when we finally get there?

I abhor a mystery. If I have to confront my past to shed light on the present, then so be it.\n\nAt least I won't be alone. With you by my side, I am sure I can face whatever secret the purified Sanctuary may contain.

Perhaps the Black Dragon took Lyra's name as some sort of trophy. Or maybe she adopted it to confuse us.\n\nRegardless, I thought Lyra perished along with the rest of my Brothers and Sisters. I thought I alone had been spared.

After Lyra completed the purification, she would have gone to the shrine of Sithis to make an offering and pray over her success. It was her usual ritual.\n\nLet's visit the shrine and see if any images remain of that moment in time.

That still eludes me. Obviously, the Black Dragon wants us to believe that she and Lyra are one and the same. But I can't imagine Lyra turning her back on the Night Mother, on Sithis.\n\nThere is a piece missing from this puzzle, I just know it.

An excellent question. If the Black Dragon really is Lyra, I'll kill the traitor myself!\n\nMeet me in Kvatch, Assassin. I have a little resin remaining. With it, we might be able to determine what occurred during Lyra's final contract.
Of course! What about?
I need it for a buyer in Abah's Landing.\n\nWhich isn't important right now. Until we get the <<1>>, there's no point in discussing payment.
There should be guards throughout the homestead. We're looking for a gatehouse—once we're past the portcullis, the manor shouldn't be much further.\n\nThat's where we'll find the <<1>>.
Yes, I'll be fine. Don't keep the guildmaster waiting on my account!

Those who remain seek coin where they can find it. But that made me wonder. Saroldo did his private work in this room, and recently I had it searched.\n\nI found a ledger, but I can't make sense of the symbols. Perhaps it is best in <<1>>'s hands.
Show her the Iron Wheel's message. Tell her <<1>> is dead, if you have to. Do what you can to bring her to <<c:2>>.\n\nBut if she refuses, leave her. I owe her a warning … nothing more.

If she hadn't retired, <<1>> would still be alive.\n\nI … shouldn't say that. She's very good at what she does—if she'd been around for the dowry heist, we'd have been spared all this tragedy. But now's not the time to open old wounds.

Didn't I explain that already? Let me check my notes. Hmm. Interesting.\n\nThe Sanctuary was abandoned by the living, yes, but it still holds many dark secrets. Secrets even the resin may not reveal. We should be on our guard.
Can't you sense it? We're not alone in here. I'll need you to deal with anything that tries to stop us while I keep the flame burning.

Then let me light the flame. Breathe deep and let the resin open your eyes. It might be uncomfortable, but I urge you not to resist. The effects should be temporary, in all likelihood.\n\nLet the fumes lead us to the answers we seek.

It seems <<1>> contacts little fish from a position of power, threatens exposure, and bends them to his will. Elegant—what I'd do.\n\nBut his connection to the Iron Wheel isn't clear. That troubles me.

We're not ready to go anywhere near the Iron Wheel! I won't have anyone else die because of a choice I ….\n\nListen, I'm barely holding this together. No offense to <<1>>, but you're the best recruit we have. I can't lose you to a feud with <<2>>.
You're right, I shouldn't take this out on you. Or her, no matter how good it feels.\n\nAll right, you risked your neck and survived to tell the tale. Did you find anything we can use?

You're right. You weren't around when they pulled our friends from their homes. They don't have the same kind of hold on you.\n\nGood to know. So tell me, when you explored their headquarters—fearlessly explored!—did you find anything we can use?
You just … ha! You have a knack at telling people what they need to hear. Reminds me of <<1>>.\n\nAll right, you made your way through without any problems. Find anything we can use?

Before the wedding, the groom should be presented to his guests—an old Taneth tradition. Wherever <<1>> is, <<2>> won't be far behind.\n\nWe'll need to keep an eye on him. Avoid drawing attention to ourselves.
What can I say? Your own choice inspired me.\n\nPeople seem to be gathering closer to the palace. Let's join them, shall we?
Everyone seems to be gathering closer to the palace.\n\nYou lead the way. I'll watch for <<1>>.
I'm not sure. Let me get back to you on that after I've had a little more time for everything to sink in.\n\nThere's certainly more politics involved than I was expecting.

He's got fancier clothes than most of the nobles back in Auridon!\n\nHe's also a pretty good listener. He's made me feel welcome. Without you and Walks-Softly, I'm not sure I would have stuck around as long as I have.

Oh, I've got an opinion. I've got a bunch of them and none of them good!\n\nVelsa is mean, ornery, and as prickly as a thorny beanstalk. And I don't think she likes me very much. But I've never seen anyone handle poisons and tinctures the way she does.

The guildmaster? She seems to be handling a difficult situation, but I certainly wouldn't want to try to fill her boots! If it were me, I'd be a hot mess, but she always finds a way to pull it together.\n\nI suppose that's why she's the leader.
What about it?
Devious traps. Vicious guardians. And likely, at the end of it all, a vault full of dust.\n\nAt least we won't have to worry about the Iron Wheel.
I'd rather sit in <<c:1>> with a bottle of wine and drink until <<2>> says I've had too much.\n\nBut I'm in charge, so it doesn't matter what I think. It matters that we go.
I carry a special potion for emergency situations.\n\nThere are benefits to creating outfits for a certain Mages Guild artificer.

You think so? Sometimes I'm not so sure. I try to remember everything that Nicolas taught me, but I don't always have the time or opportunity to consider every option before I make a decision.\n\nStill, I couldn't ask for a better crew.
A lifetime ago. I don't speak of this matter, but you did save my life.\n\nI once served <<1>>. I confess she became infatuated. But I could not possibly return her feelings.

She reminds me of myself when I first hooked up with the guild. She's young and inexperienced, but she has some real skills. I just hope we come through all this so she has a chance to hone and develop her natural talents.

I don't know what I would have done without Walks-Softly. After the heist went bad and we lost so many of the crew, he helped me figure out how to hold what was left together.\n\nAnd he has a great fashion sense. I let him pick out all my outfits.

I guess you can say that. Velsa was old, grumpy, and difficult when I first joined the guild—and that was a long time ago now. Believe me, retirement hasn't improved her disposition.\n\nI'll deny I said it, but I'm glad she came back. We need her.

Thanks for noticing. I do like to put my best foot forward in everything I do.\n\nBut a lot of credit goes to Zeira and the rest of our crew. A single lizard isn't enough to form a guild—even one as dapper and dashing as me!

No, and there never will be. Needle, thread, and bolts of cloth are more fulfilling than time spent with any person.\n\nBut Falorah was young. During a family inspection of <<c:1>>, she brought me along—hoping to impress me with her family's wealth.

I was not allowed inside, but she led me through a side passage. She brought me to a large, frightfully dark chamber. I could feel it breathing.\n\nIt terrified me. I'm not ashamed to admit I fled—out the front door, in full view of her mother.
No, she quite literally ruined my life's work. Had every one of the outfits I'd crafted for her burned in effigy.\n\nSo I am happy to share what I know of <<c:1>>, as I did with your <<2>>.

There was a scandal. The al-Danobia bloodline has always had great influence in Taneth, and I soon found myself banished. Not once did Falorah speak on my behalf.\n\nI understood, of course. She was young and feared her mother, as most nobles do.

Have you seen the way Quen moves? She can get up and over a wall faster than I can fold a perfect pocket square!\n\nI have a nose for talent and Quen is the real deal. As we go about rebuilding the crew, we'd do worse than to find a few more like her.

What's to think? She's our guildmaster! And she's a good friend. She stepped forward in our darkest hour and pulled the guild back from the brink of extinction.\n\nUnder her leadership, I don't think there's anything we can't accomplish. I don't think.

I never say anything hurtful about the people I know. That's just not couth.\n\nHowever, I would be remiss not to warn you. Try not to get on Velsa's bad side. She has a terrible temper. You really don't want to constantly check your food for poison.

What? Are you writing a book? Go bother someone who isn't likely to slip poison into your waterskin.\n\nAll right. If you must know, yes. I love the quiet, working in my garden. Still, I suppose a part of me missed this life. A small part, but ….

She's too young, too inexperienced. I don't know what Zeira was thinking, allowing that youngling to join the guild.\n\nOh, she's got some raw talent, I'll give you that. But raw talent usually just winds up turning a sweet heist sour, mark my words.

Never quite understood that preening, over-dressed lizard, but he's good to have around. He's too happy for his own good, mind you, and talking to him makes my head hurt.\n\nStill, the guild is probably better off with him than without him. I suppose.

I go away and come back to find that Zeira's in charge? Ha! She's got delusions of grandeur, but she's far from ready to lead this crew.\n\nBesides, I was never keen on taking orders, even back when Nicolas was the guildmaster. Not about to start now.

Hmm … three points on this sheet. <<1>>  always used Abah's Landing and <<2>> as a reference. If I line up those two points ….\n\nWell, now. The third point is in Hew's Bane, out in the middle of nowhere.

<<1>> would have kept such a thing from the guild. "The less they know, the less trouble they'll cause."\n\nBut I'm going to tell the Thieves Guild. I want them to cause a world of trouble. And I want to lay it all on his doorstep. Let's go.
I've seen enough. <<1>> faked his death and stole the dowry. Now he's working with that merchant lord, <<2>>.\n\nTo think, I mourned that bastard.

My theory? <<1>> gives <<2>> the stolen dowry. <<2>> "returns" it to <<3>>. With the dowry recovered, the Iron Wheel departs.\n\nThis gives <<2>> great influence with the merchant lords—the same ones who buy from all the pirates raiding Taneth.
I read. Hammerfell politics are fascinating.\n\nYou ask me? Nobles are thieves who pick the pockets of nations.

<<1>> becomes her puppet. He keeps the Abah's Landing merchant lords in line. This removes a threat to Taneth, which elevates her among her peers.\n\nBetter yet, she gets to marry and keep her own dowry. She gains money and influence. How about that?

<<1>> pays him a large sum of money for the dowry. He heads somewhere remote—retires, like <<2>> did. Spends his fortune on all those paintings he loved to acquire.\n\nUnless one of us finds him and feeds him his own liver. I'd do it, if <<3>> asked.
If <<1>> learns exactly who she's about to marry, she'll turn the Iron Wheel on <<2>>. And if we threaten <<2>>'s future, <<3>> will scuttle into the open.\n\nI look forward to stepping on him.

That horrid place of darkness? <<1>> tried to lead me through, but I panicked and fled.\n\nIt was sheer luck that I didn't fall to my death. And if she hadn't given me that trinket, we wouldn't be speaking today.

Yes—it had a crystal holding a small amount of her blood. I mentioned it to your old guildmaster when he asked after the particulars of <<c:1>>.\n\nIt's strange, I seem to have misplaced it. Haven't seen it in months. Why do you ask?

I guess you never heard. I grew up … different.\n\nMy parents were Nords, but we followed a different path from most other Nords. We admired the were-beasts. Wanted to be like them. We … drank their blood.

Not at first. I lived on my own, deep in the mountains. I was wild, feral. Then Kor found me. He took me in and gave me a family again. If not for him, I don't know where I'd be right now.\n\nNow if only I could make that damn Chanter pay ….

My clan were hunters. We worshiped Hircine. Becoming a werewolf was part of that. It was the way things were done.\n\nBut I could not control my wolf form. I … I hurt someone. Badly. After that, I ran away. To save them.

We need to stop the wedding. Actually, we need Falorah to do so. I think this can still work.\n\nLet's split up. Learn where she is and how we can reach her. I need to come up with a very convincing argument.
Oh, it's a very bad idea. But it's the best bad idea we have. Sometimes that's the best a thief can hope for.\n\nWish me luck. I'll have to be … well, as convincing as <<1>>.
For now? Nothing. Until we learn where they've taken her, there is little we can do.\n\nBut we will learn, I'm certain of that.
Maybe I'm just that good?\n\nA few ink stains on my fingers, a furrowed brow and … three-hundred and three, three-hundred and four … could you not watch over my shoulder?

She told me as much at the wedding—for the merchant lords of Abah's Landing to be kept on a leash.\n\nI think that's a service we can provide. It gets us a foothold in Taneth … and who knows where that could lead.

I wrote a book about the ruins and Raynor was able to make improvements to his control rod thingamabob, but we decided to pass on both the Academy and the Mages Guild.\n\nWe learned that an independent life of adventure suits us just fine.

A little. I'm not having any better luck with my new journal, though. The pages keep falling out! Raynor says I'm too hard on my books, but it has to be shoddy construction. They just don't make bindings like they used to.\n\nIt's kind of disgraceful.

You and me both! I'm all for exploring new places, but that place was just wrong!\n\nI just wish everyone had made it back from that damn place. I miss King Dynar. And poor Darien. He was kind of a flirt, but he had a hero's heart.

Orsinium was an interesting city with a great museum, but it was time for us to move on. I know King Kurog did some terrible things, but it didn't feel right sticking around after he died. We were there at his invitation, after all.

Oh, definitely! Once word that I perfected a working control rod started to spread, we began to receive offers from across the land.\n\nThat's why we're going to Sentinel. A patron offered to fund our exploration of a newly discovered Dwemer ruin.
Oh, you know how it is with discoveries such as these. It takes a lot of effort to produce any meaningful results. And Kireth usually leaves that kind of work to me.

A few. In fact, it was through information gleaned from the first couple of maps we extracted that led us to the ruins in Sentinel. Now all we have to do is get there before someone beats us to the punch.

I guess you could say that. It showed them that we do have a few skills when it comes to dungeons and delving.\n\nStill, we decided to retain our independence. We've taken on a contract or two for the Mages Guild, but we aren't under their thumb.
How did you … no, I don't want to know. Yes, that should work.\n\nAnd my hands are entirely clean in the matter.

Not the soldiers who accost my home! Perhaps they are bandits, or deserters. Yet they wear Iron Wheel uniforms as they pound on my door.\n\nI thought to myself, "What choice do I have? The mercenaries must be paid."

It is no excuse. I told myself, "Saroldo would want you to have a small portion of his treasure." But he already gave me years of his life that he could not provide to <<1>>.\n\nI was foolish. Please, forgive me.
I don't know. I ….\n\nPerhaps I'll open the strongbox at my rooftop retreat. Somewhere comfortable and beautiful. You're welcome to stop by and see for yourself.

Oh, you know how it is. A murder here, an assassination there. A girl needs to stay active!\n\nBut I wanted to thank you again for all the help you provided back in Deshaan. I won't forget that, hero. And I'll never forget you.

That's a sweet offer, hero, but I already work for a shadowy organization. Besides, I don't think I'm exactly Brotherhood material. Too much emphasis on pseudo-religious nonsense for my taste.\n\nBut no offense if you're into that kind of thing.

I'm never going to live that down, am I? It did look good on me, though, didn't it? What am I saying? You have a way of making me act unprofessionally, you know that?\n\nWell, keep it up. I kind of like it.

How typical! All right, listen closely.\n\nDasek Moor was a fort once, before it fell into ruin. The Count has a small camp there that he uses from time to time, though I haven't determined why. I guess we all have our secrets.
Questions? At a time like this? As you wish ….\n\nThis one is Razum-dar, just a simple Khajiit who seeks the best for all people of Tamriel. And a soap that won't dry the fur. One day ….

Some answers are too dangerous to hear, yes? But this one is also an Eye of the Queen. That means … no, never mind what that means.\n\nJust understand. Captain Apinia decided it was all right to kill innocent people. For that, Raz will make her pay.

Evil? Raz doesn't like to judge. Greedy? As the day is long! If Raz is feeling generous, maybe he'll send Apinia's head to the company's boss when we're done.\n\nMeanwhile, my friend will sit quietly while we hunt. Or he'll be dead. Raz can't decide.

Raz is happy to see you, as well! We had such adventures helping Queen Ayrenn, yes?\n\nBut we can reminisce later. Drink ourselves silly and tell tales to make each other gasp and smile. Now we have a war criminal to punish!

The Queen's Eyes go where they need to go, my friend. Raz would ask you the same, but this one thinks it would be better not to know the answer to that question, yes?\n\nStill, Raz is glad you're here. Now let's go deal with Captain Apinia.
I wanted more. Alone, Abah's Landing is a meager prize. But if I could find a way to bring in Taneth ….\n\nWith a stake in both cities, you control all trade in Hew's Bay.
