But I hadn't! <<1>> should have joined me at Malooc's Path. After my "death," she would lead the others back to Abah's Landing. <<2>> could scatter the guild before the Iron Wheel's arrival. \n\nBut then <<1>> retired, and everything changed.

Of course not. But had all gone according to plan, <<1>> could have filtered the guild into Taneth. Set up there, while the Iron Wheel was chasing them here.\n\nAnd when I was <<2>>'s puppet in Abah's Landing, <<1>> would be mine in Taneth.
x
You're not? Then why have you slipped past my defenses and entered my ….\n\nOh no. Fortunata sent you, didn't she? You're here to kill me?
Then pass along the message to your superiors. Let them know I have gold. And information. I can point you toward the person hunting your agents and—wait, who's that? \n\nIs he with you?

I'll take your silence as agreement. I don't care how, just make sure Fortunata dies. It's the only way I can protect my city. Do that and the gold and the information about the murderer are yours. I'm a man of my word.\n\nWait, who's that behind you?

You murdered the Commander? I see. Another one of Fortunata's insults. Pay to weaken the Order of the Hour, but killing a Count is just a waste of gold.\n\nBut you are one of the Brotherhood. And I performed your ritual. Let me pay you to kill her!
The Grand Chanter fears nothing, least of all a pathetic Daedra who pales in comparison to the mighty Dragon God!\n\nNow go see the Grand Chanter and face your judgment or I'll gut you here and now.
No righteous citizen of Kvatch will raise a finger to help a Daedra worshiper!\n\nNow march! If you cause further trouble, I can't guarantee your safety.
Of course, Assassin. What details are unclear to you?

The common folk fear us, the political leaders tolerate us, and everyone who needs someone dead and can pay the cost hires us without hesitation. Our reputation remains strong.\n\nBut these attacks by the Sermonizers. They're obviously up to something.

That's what I'm talking about! I got plenty of the ingredients around, but you can get 'em at the grocers' too. \n\nJust toss 'em into one of my charmed mixing bowls and it'll work my magic for you. Perfect cake, every time. Guarantee it.

Josseline was mad at me, mad at him, mad at life in general. She decided that piracy wasn't for her. She wanted to serve a higher purpose.\n\nUnfortunately, this particular higher purpose is worse than piracy. It hides its killing behind religion.

Well, members that join the society are cut off from their friends and family. And anyone that tries to quit disappears. No one knows what happens to them, by the way.\n\nOh, and I did mention the secret beheadings, didn't I?
So the Listener was right. Tell me, what did you see?
What a blessing you've received! The Night Mother has chosen you to fulfill the Litany of Blood.\n\nLet me ask you this. Did the passages make any sense to you?

Of course. The targets must be marked in some way. Easier than I would make it, but who am I to question the Listener?\n\nIt's clear to me that you must decipher the Litany of Blood and kill the targets inscribed on its pages.
There are no wrong people. The Dread Father welcomes every soul you send him, aside from your Brothers and Sisters. Obey the Five Tenets and you have no fear of invoking the Wrath of Sithis.

The Listener required someone special for this task but the Black Hand wasn't sure who to assign it to. The Night Mother always provides, though.\n\nYou can read the litany. I'm sure there are clues among its words.

The assassin's blade you were given access to when you were initiated. The Blade of Woe. It's a symbol and a sacred instrument, the will of Sithis made manifest.\n\nI'm sure the blade will play an important role as you complete the litany.

While you were away, that ghostly image appeared. Someone you killed, I presume?\n\nIf so, I imagine we'll see more of them as you complete the litany. I look forward to seeing what happens after you fill all fifteen pedestals!

That's what I'm talking about! You'll have to grab the ingredients yourself, but once you do, just toss 'em into one of my charmed mixing bowls and it'll work my magic for you. Perfect cake, every time. Guarantee it.
You're, uh, really not afraid of me? I, uh, huh. Well, this is awkward.\n\nI think my odds of surviving Qamar's anger is better than facing yours. You can find his stash here. We good now?
Yeah, about that. I'm done with the Society of the Dragon. Turns out, religion doesn't really agree with the women in my family. Especially not a crazy cult with a murderous priest for a leader.

Popular? I've had nobles and Daedric Princes wait years for one of my confectionery creations. That's why they call me the Prince of Pastry and the Patron of Pies!\n\nMy cakes are grand and elaborate. And they're absolutely delicious. You'll see!

Congratulations! That's an amazing coincidence! Let me assure you, my friend, you're in for a wonderful treat. Not everyone receives one of my vouchers! Puts you right to the head of the line for my most delightful creation—the Jubilee Cake!

You've never had one of my Jubilee Cakes? I suppose that makes sense. I don't make them for just anyone, you know.\n\nPeople here in Covenant territory especially enjoy the cake's rich flavor. Comes from the locally sourced flour, of course!

You've never had one of my Jubilee Cakes? I suppose that makes sense. I don't make them for just anyone, you know.\n\nPeople here in Pact territory especially enjoy the flavor of the honey. It comes straight from the source in Skyrim!

You've never had one of my Jubilee Cakes? I suppose that makes sense. I don't make them for just anyone, you know.\n\nPeople here in the Dominion lands especially enjoy the addition of locally sourced bananas!

I'll make a fresh Jubilee Cake, but you'll have to gather the ingredients while I continue to fill my orders.\n\nI need bananas, flour, and honey. Buy them or find them, doesn't matter to me. Just bring them back here. You'll be eating cake in no time!

You're going to need all of us to face down Artorius. Someone has to make sure the path remains open for the others.\n\nBesides, the Speaker wants you to make this kill. If I got there first, Artorius would be dead before you could raise your blade.

Get moving, Assassin. I'm pretty sure Artorius isn't going to wait around while you dawdle. As soon as word gets to him that the Brotherhood is here, I expect he'll take off faster than a pig that wandered into a pork roast.

This place reminds me of the Baron's Maze back in Cloudrest. Confusing network of passages. But there was a terrific meat pie stall near the entrance.\n\nAnyway, Astara and I split up to cover more ground. We'll be there when you reach Artorius.

No, that would be boring. You start murdering the Sermonizer's priests while I take on the real challenge. I'll locate her hiding spot. Then I'll find you so we can kill her together.\n\nThat will put the fear of the Brotherhood in the Kvatch people!

By Akatosh's hourglass eyes, you're one of those dark assassin people! The ones the Grand Sermonizer warned us about!\n\nLook, there's a hidden passage in the moat, along the western wall. Use that route if you really need to get into the castle.

Look, I can't give you my seal. Even if you took it from me, it would do you no good. I'm afraid I can't help you. I don't make the rules, but I do try to follow them.\n\nMay Akatosh bless you and watch over you just the same.
I will not! That seal is a declaration and a confirmation of my faith, and I take my faith very seriously.
Then you must be disappointed, because I cannot tell you what you wish.\n\nGo please. The ill-omens of a bubbling bog surround you, as well as the smell.
Wait—wait, let's not be hasty. Here's where he keeps his gold. Take a little nip for your trouble. He never notices.

The Governor's private pantry is on the top floor. The place is a maze, though, and the Red Sails guard the direct approach nine ways to Sundas. I'd use the secret passages in the eastern corridors. Just look for a red drape over an alcove.

Naturally! Most castles have them. You just need to know where to look.\n\nOnce you pass through the entry hall, the guards will consider you a threat. If you want to avoid being seen, find a red drape and use the secret passages.

The Speaker sent you to me, didn't he? I know Anvil Castle like the back of my hand. And I know the Governor.\n\nPoison lets your target do all the work for you. And Fortunata can't resist any excuse to reach for a decanter of her favorite wine.

I'd love to put an end to her royal pain in the arse, but the Speaker gave this contract to you. I'm just here to offer advice.\n\nTell you what. After you poison Fortunata's wine, I'll stop by for the show. We can share a drink and watch her die.
You've got some nerve, don't you? Coming onto our docks asking about Qamar's private affairs. You know who Qamar is? You know who I am? The Red Sails own Anvil!

I'll be along in a bit. I just want to make sure I can continue my role here after the dust settles and a new administration takes over.\n\nIf you need a way out, I'll happily let you in on my secret escape route. It's never failed me yet.

The Withered Rose? A small hostel outside the city. A lovely mother and daughter own the place, but they've had trouble making ends meet.\n\nThe smuggler tunnels provide them with an alternate source of income. And they're perfect for your needs.

Oh, darling, I have all kinds of secrets! And so did Fortunata.\n\nThere's a hidden passage in the Governor's suite that she used whenever she wanted to move about in a clandestine manner. I've used it a few times myself. Leads to a cave on the shore.

She likes to commune with the Divines and with nature. And she takes on contracts like the rest of us, so it's not that unusual for her to be away from the Sanctuary.\n\nBut with the recent attacks against us, I can't help but imagine the worst.
I hope she's all right, but who knows what to think when the world turns upside down? Someone's been murdering the murderers! If Hildegard has been hurt—or worse—I don't know what I'll do.

What are you implying, Initiate? Hilde is like a sister to me. Ever since I found her, I've been trying to help her come to grips with her situation.\n\nShe may be a werewolf, but she's a good person. The Brotherhood is lucky to have her.

The Pirate Queen hates everything she can't control. The Count of Kvatch. The Primate. Us. She wants to rule the entire Gold Coast, but we're not willing to just roll over and give in to her demands.\n\nWe're independent and we like it that way.

Why is that so hard to believe? She's an excellent tracker and a ruthless killer in werewolf form.\n\nSometimes she brings back body parts she's still gnawing on, but who hasn't gotten lost in the moment a time or two? And I always clean up the mess.

Accounting. Inventory. Managing the futility of keeping the lot of you honest … You have any idea how hard it is to watch the coffers in a den of thieves? It's like watching my sister, multiplied by … I don't know, a lot.\n\nI don't get much sleep.
I'm going to stop you right there, before the wheels start turning. If you need to get paid, I'll make sure you get everything you're owed. I don't miscount.\n\nNever forget: I. Don't. Miscount.
Twin, if you could believe it. I love her, but she drives me crazy. You would not believe how much she can spend on cosmetics. "Work related." Uh-huh. Half, maybe.

My sister and I would work up confidence schemes on wealthy merchants. She'd dress the part, I'd dress the ledgers.\n\nThe guild offered stability and an audience that could appreciate the performance. Hopefully, it can again.

You don't have to thank me. We're family, after all. But if you forget you saw me in these rags, I'd be ever so grateful.\n\nNow get back to the Sanctuary and let Astara know that Fortunata is as dead as that stuffed chub loon she kept on her mantle.

Isn't it obvious? She thinks I've lost my perspective. That I'm too sad or angry or whatever to do the job I've done a hundred times before.\n\nJust promise that you won't tell Astara about any of this. She already thinks I'm reckless enough as it is.
I … appreciate your discretion. If Astara knew what I've been up to, she'd confine me for my own protection. We're assassins, damn it! We don't need protection!

One more thing. The last time I tracked the Black Dragon, I followed her past the Dasek Moor ruins toward the old Enclave of the Hourglass before I turned back.\n\nMake sure the Count tells you what he knows about the Order of the Hour's old haunt.
Yes, Assassin, what is it?

Good. She's going to get herself killed if she can't set aside her emotions and focus on the job at hand.\n\nWe all want to make the Black Dragon and whoever else is involved pay for these insults, but recklessness will get us all killed.
I suggest that you proceed with caution then.\n\nDid this intelligence come to you by way of Mirabelle, by any chance?
I had my suspicions concerning Mirabelle. Thank you for being honest with me.\n\nIt's time I had a serious talk with our beautiful murderer.
Knowing Fortunata, it could be anyone. She's made as many enemies as she has friends since taking control of the Gold Coast. Probably just a noble who insulted her at one of her elaborate parties.

With a fleet of ships and an army of pirates. It helped that the region had been decimated by Varen's civil war. She was so bold as to claim the entire Gold Coast as her domain, but Count Carolus and Kvatch still have a little to say about that.

I'm sure there's a book about her around here somewhere. Oh, very well. Fortunata worked for the Gold Coast Trading Company before she used her influence and connections to become the Pirate Queen of the Abecean Sea.

It's crawling with Red Sails pirates. Fortunata keeps it locked up tighter than her dowry chest, but she is expecting you.\n\nMirabelle knows the Anvil Castle well. She spends time there, pretending to be a servant so she can keep an eye on things.

Certainly. And she's very good at it. For  the eventual day when we have to move against the Pirate Queen, we'll have Mirabelle in place and ready to act.\n\nOf course, such a day may never materialize, but I believe in preparing for every contingency.

Whatever gave you that idea? The Order is a company of warrior-priests dedicated to protecting the Cathedral of Akatosh. At least, that's how they started. Now they recruit anyone who can wield a sword. I agreed to expand their authority, but ….

I'm sure this is all Count Carolus's doing. He constantly defies me, damn the man! Doesn't he realize the Gold Coast is better off under my control?\n\nAnyway, kill Commander Marcus Scipio. That should show the Count that the Hour can't protect him.

That is so annoying.\n\nAnyway, I'm sure Count Carolus is behind this. He constantly undermines my authority, damn the man! I want you to kill Commander Marcus Scipio and show the Count that the Hour can't protect him from my wrath.

Now that you mention it, there is one more thing. After you murder Scipio, go and tell the Count what you did. Scare the pants off him and drive home the point that the Order of the Hour can't stop the inevitable.

Perhaps you could blink once, just to let me know you understand.\n\nOh, and one more thing. After you murder Scipio, go and tell the Count what you did. Scare the pants off him and drive home the point that the Order of the Hour can't help him.
Of course.
Of course.
Of course.

Sheesh, you ask a lot of questions! The ledgers … are evidence. Of their less than legitimate activities!\n\nI can use them to discourage any complaints to the Governor. Can't let them push us around. Public interests over private interests, get it?
What? I—I don't know what you mean? I just remembered I'm late. For … something, I'm a busy person. Nice working with you, but I really must be going!

Well, you see, if <<1>> did break free from the Gold Coast—with all their security—I need to make sure the same doesn't happen to my warehouse.\n\nSorry about the deception, I wanted to avoid the Gold Coast buying off my mercenaries … again.

Nothing …! All right, fine! I work for a competing company with a monster for sale.\n\nThe Gold Coast stole our buyer with their recent acquisition of <<1>>, leaving us in a bind. But you took care of that. And they really were endangering us!

As if the Grand Sermonizer didn't have enough vices to rage about, now she's preaching against the Brotherhood. She says we are weak, powerless. A toothless Dragon that inspires ridicule instead of fear.\n\nThese lies must be silenced—permanently.

Be wary. The Order of the Hour has increased its presence in Kvatch. Avoid the warrior-priests if you can.\n\nMeet up with Tanek and silence the priests that speak against us, including the Grand Sermonizer. That will put the fear of Sithis in them.

Curiosity isn't a trait I encourage, especially when it comes to matters inside the Sanctuary. Still, you'll find out soon enough, I'm sure.\n\nMirabelle has allowed Tanek's injury and the deaths of Cimbar and the others to make her … emotional.

After Tanek was injured during the Grand Sermonizer incident, Hilde went to pray for him and I haven't seen her since. No one has! It's not like Hilde to just disappear without saying a word to me or Astara.

She loves temples, but the trouble in Kvatch has made her avoid the big Cathedral. Lately she's been visiting the Great Chapel of Dibella in Anvil. I think the rituals soothe her, you understand?\n\nWill you come to Anvil and help me find Hildegard?

The deaths hit her hard, especially Cimbar's. She craves revenge and it's making her anxious, reckless. That's dangerous for an assassin.\n\nWe need to be cold, precise, calculated. The heat of emotion leads to mistakes, and that gets people killed.

As close as any lovers can be, I suppose. The recent deaths visited upon us have affected Mirabelle, but Cimbar's torture and murder, that one has left a mark. It's made her emotional, which is never a good thing in our business.

It's rare, but not unheard of. And the Black Hand agreed, so who am I to complain?\n\nI'd like you to deal with this one, Initiate. Go to Anvil Castle and meet with our client. I'm sure she's got a good reason for making a special request.

Oh, didn't I mention? It's none other than the self-proclaimed Provincial Governor of Anvil, the Pirate Queen Fortunata ap Dugal.\n\nI expect you to handle this like any other contract. Locate your target, plan your attack, and make your kill.

Lyra was the most skilled among us. I was told she had died in the purification. That she fell alongside our brothers and sisters.\n\nThe journal claims Lyra died at the hands of the Black Dragon, yet you said she also used that name. Curious ….

I want to return this journal and pretend I never read it, but I can't resist a mystery. If the Black Dragon killed Lyra and destroyed my former Sanctuary, I need to know the truth. It is time to break my vow and go back there. Will you come with me?
I'll arrange transport for us. Meet me near the gates of Anvil when you are ready to depart.\n\nAnd thank you, Assassin, for agreeing to help me.

I certainly hope so. Hilde is pretty distinctive. After all, how many young Nord women with flowers in their hair could there be in Anvil? And visiting a chapel, no less!\n\nAsk around and see if you can find out anything.

You'd do that? For me? I … thank you.\n\nChanter Nemus tends to the Akatosh shrine in the Chapel of Dibella. He spends a lot of time in the chapel office when he isn't lying to foolish young women. Make him feel pain before you kill him, all right?

Nothing. Never mind. I thought you were someone else, that's all. Forget I said anything.\n\nIt's just … there's something about your eyes. They have a certain look about them. I thought you were … well, I thought you were one of them.

Keep your voice down! But yes, I thought you were with the Brotherhood. You've got that look in your eyes. You killed people. Or you will.\n\nJust between us, I heard the Brotherhood seeks new recruits. I plan to be one of those lucky few.

No risk, no reward, my Aunt Ophelia always said.\n\nLook, people like us, we need to surround ourselves with like-minded allies. People that will protect us and help us reach our true potential. They're going to notice me, I just know it!

Rumor has it that if you take an innocent life and the Dark Brotherhood notices, they'll offer you a place in their guild.\n\nThink about it. A place where killers are free to pursue their darkest passions. Doesn't it just give you the chills?

Purification. That's what they called it. I suppose the term is accurate.\n\nBetrayal and corruption festered in our ranks, though I'm not sure what the source was or why it happened. The Black Hand decreed a systematic cleansing was the solution.

Another excellent question. I'm going to record that for later.\n\nBut as for the answer, I was working deep in Black Marsh during that season. Whatever the rest of my Sanctuary did to anger the Black Hand, it was obvious that I had no part in it.

I'm not sure what to believe, but the Black Dragon certainly implies that in her journal.\n\nWhatever the case, only a master assassin could accomplish something as far-reaching as purification. The Black Dragon's skills clearly mark her as such.

I'm a woman of my word, friend. With the profits from these petals, I'll easily recoup the cost of having that Dark Elf drive away a few groping customers.\n\nShe starts tonight. Make sure she isn't late.

We really couldn't afford to lose those ingots. Thank you. You have acted with honor and we'll do the same.\n\nInform Raynor he can come by and work on our forge. If he really can improve its operations, we'll compensate him fairly.

Thanks to the efforts of you and Green-Venom-Tongue, we learned that the Black Dragon is Lyra Viria. Moreover, you discovered that Lyra was a member of the Dark Brotherhood, a Silencer who was part of Green-Venom-Tongue's former Sanctuary.

The Primate has rallied the Order against us.\n\nBetween the problems with the Sermonizers and the Chanters, and the revelation that the Black Dragon is the Order's First Sword, it's clear that Artorius has a quarrel with the Brotherhood.

Whatever happened to Lyra after she purified her Sanctuary and went to Kvatch, it seems clear that she developed a powerful bond with the Order and their god. Green-Venom-Tongue believes she's gone there to contemplate her next move.

Knightsgrave is an Imperial ruin situated near the northwest shore of the Gold Coast. Legends claim it dates back to the founding of the Order of the Hour, but now it's nothing but tumbled stones and forgotten memories.

Indeed. Perhaps that's where she acquired her taste for killing her Brothers and Sisters.\n\nAfter the purification, she received a contract to murder the current Primate's predecessor and consequently became Artorius's Black Dragon.
He had no problem performing the Sacrament, that much is certain. Artorius is dangerous, but Lyra remains the immediate threat. \n\nI believe you have somewhere to be, Assassin.
The river carries us where it will, and that's all I prefer to say about that at this time.\n\nI was there. Now I am here. As are you, Initiate.

Aren't you familiar with the cherished Black Marsh custom? Consuming various venomous concoctions to bolster our natural immunity? I drank so much my tongue turned green!\n\nHa! The new initiates fall for that every time!

And you, as well, Initiate. I look forward to interviewing you at length when you have some time. For my journals, of course. I keep meticulous records.\n\nI'll help you, you'll help me … isn't that what the Bretons call a "win-win"?

Now this one I know I've written down! Study the Five Tenets. Learn them, memorize them, live them. There's a copy in the Sanctuary. Someplace. I'd let you look at this one, but I don't let anybody read my journals.\n\nThat would be … inadvisable.

Such a curious mind! Then listen carefully, Initiate.\n\nContracts must be taken seriously. Always obey the Matron's instructions to the letter. And don't get yourself killed. Though that probably goes without saying.

Durisa and Van? One was an experienced assassin who knew her business. The other was a raw recruit with hardly any blood on his blade. Kind of like you, New-blade.\n\nIt could have been coincidence, but I think they were targeted by the same killer.

Just a feeling, I guess. And the way they were left for all the world to see. Someone was proud of their work and wanted everyone to know it.\n\nAnd it had to be a professional. Durisa was too good to be taken down by an amateur.

Matron Astara tells us what to think, not the other way around. But yes, we've talked about this. All we can do is stay alert and try to figure out who's behind the murders. Until then, we're just jumping at shadows.\n\nVery dangerous shadows.

Hildegard is like the little sister I never had, but her true family was awful. They drank the blood of were-beasts! It's a dangerous practice, but not entirely unheard of in Nord lands.\n\nThey even forced their children to participate.

I always liked to hunt and fight. I became a soldier, but that turned out to be more about waiting around than actual battle.\n\nSo I sold my sword as a mercenary, made some enemies, and soon found that the other sellswords were being paid to kill me.
Indeed I did! Kept a low profile in town, spent most of my time in the wilderness. I almost decided to stop running and then I found little Hilde.\n\nShe became my reason to go on living.

We assume so. But as to why she can't control her transformations, that remains a mystery. \n\nShe lost control one day and hurt another member of the tribe. They cursed her and she ran away. I found her later. She was confused, alone, and nearly mad.

I'm a skilled hunter. Taming animals is almost second nature to me. It took time, but she came to trust me. Accepted me as her big brother.\n\nBefore that happened though, she nearly tore my face off. See? I still have the scar.

Well, you know, there are some things we just don't talk about in public. I hope you understand.\n\nI will tell you that we love it here. We're part of the best family in the whole world. And we're glad to have you with us! I'm sure Hilde agrees!

As some in power reach higher levels, the rungs they stand upon become more tenuous. I assume that since Artorius once used the Brotherhood to rise to the top, he began to worry that someone would do the same to stop him.\n\nHe decided to strike first.

Does that surprise you? People from all walks of life seek the services we provide. Nobles, priests, commoners—it makes no difference to the Night Mother.\n\nArtorius wanted to become Primate. He asked us to remove his predecessor and we complied.

And we're a collection of lone assassins. I say let them come. Let them march into our empty halls as the shadows close around them. We are those shadows, cutting them down one by one.\n\nWhen night falls upon the Order, it will be everlasting.

These orders come from the Black Hand. Besides, your Matron has another task. She leads your brethren on a hunt. To pick off the Order, reduce their numbers. They'll be at your side when you need them most.\n\nAnd then the Primate will die.

Just a little business I had to attend to. I do like to keep my dagger sharp, as it were.\n\nHer family had certain documents and presumed to make allegations that might have embarrassed the Brotherhood.

The Brotherhood isn't that petty, but we do have certain obligations to uphold.\n\nI gave her the greatest gift of all—solace. Just as you gave the same gift to Lord Jarol. And there will be many more gifts to grant before your work is done.

Mirabelle's outburst doesn't concern you, Assassin. Focus on the task at hand.\n\nCount Carolus still owes us for the Sacrament. He claimed to have information about the Black Dragon. Meet him at the ruins of Dasek Moor and find out what he knows.

We're not sure, but that's where he requested to meet. He has a camp there which he's using for his own clandestine purposes.\n\nBefore you go, talk to Mirabelle. She has information concerning the Count that could prove useful to your mission.

As it was ordered, so was it done. I'm impressed, Assassin. Lyra turned her back on the Night Mother and killed so many of the family, but you brought her down. The Void gathers all souls.\n\nBut something else troubles you. Talk to me.

The Black Dragon made our Sister talk? I'd bring Lyra back to life and kill her again if such was within my power!\n\nArtorius knows our location. As soon as he gathers the courage, he'll send the Order of the Hour against us.

No. Due to his seniority and knowledge of the target, that honor has been bestowed upon Green-Venom-Tongue. He's already tracked Lyra to Knightsgrave and is preparing to strike.\n\nI have a different task in mind for you.

I want you to follow Green-Venom-Tongue and make sure the deed is done. I don't doubt his loyalty, but they were friends once. If he falters in the slightest, it will be his blood that stains the ground.\n\nNo matter what, the Black Dragon must die.

I do hope your curiosity turns into acquiescence. For the job, of course. I'd never mean to imply anything else.\n\nI need to stop a murderer. Now before you say, "A murderer? Just point me in the right direction," I have to admit it's not that simple.

Yes, let me explain. This killer announces his intentions long before he strikes, putting the fear of mer and men in his victims.\n\nYou'd think with a warning they could avoid their fate. But alas, no. All dead.

In the most heinous manner imaginable—a message in an innocent sweetroll! Now he's targeted my associates. This scroll lists everyone who's recently received the threatening pastry. Talk to them and learn their connection before the killer strikes!
I don't want you to do anything. I'm just providing information. Letting you know that new opportunities are available if you're willing to spill a little blood.

Don't take my willingness to help out as a sign or anything. I recognized a kindred spirit and suggested a way to satisfy your darkest urges. They'll get you killed if you don't keep them under control.\n\nAnd if you don't find the right allies.

That's one of the best things about the Dark Brotherhood. It hides in plain sight. No one knows where its headquarters is or how many members it has. Yet you can go into any library and read a book about them.\n\nIt's brilliant, really!

I'm a respected member of the Gold Coast Trading Company. When I heard that a number of my most trusted associates—as well as other individuals in the area—received one of these tainted sweetrolls, I knew I had to do something.

Fellowship, safety, and security, to name just a few. I understand there's also a steady flow of gold from all the contracts. And you get to kill people! Can you imagine a better guild to belong to?\n\nBetter than picking pockets, if you ask me.

Quite a few, actually. My favorite is "The Night Mother's Truth." It describes the origins of the Brotherhood, although it might all be theory and conjecture. \n\nBut forget the books! Everyone knows the Brotherhood exists. And most people fear them.

No need to be all insulting about it.\n\nJust remember that I understand. That mask you wear every day. The one you're desperately afraid is going to slip one day. You could throw that mask away in the Brotherhood. They want you for who you really are.

Hey, I don't know exactly how they select new recruits. I'm just telling you what I've heard. Maybe you just need to be in the right place at the right time. Like Anvil.\n\nOf course, I've also heard they have eyes everywhere, so what do I know?

Word gets around. There have been rumors of this "Sweetroll Killer" for quite some time, but when one of my associates wound up dead after receiving a delicious baked good, I started making the connection.

I'm not one to reveal my sources, but Fat Grakal told me that he overheard Seaworthy Saralla say that there have been some mysterious murders committed on the Gold Coast.\n\nTo me, nothing says Dark Brotherhood like mysterious murders!

Oh, I got that from Margog the Hammer. Buy him a couple of ales and he spouts secrets like a bard spouts poetry.\n\nJust the other day, he told me that his cousin Krusk killed a baker in Anvil. He received a mysterious visit that very night.

You really don't know anything about the Brotherhood, do you? If they decide you're worthy enough to receive an invitation, one of their dark dignitaries shows up to deliver the news in person.\n\nIt's kind of creepy, but it's also a singular honor.

Oh, it's been nothing but a parade of beggars and unworthy miscreants, I assure you! If the lot of those ugly ogrim lovers were on that list, I guarantee I wouldn't be offering this reward.\n\nYou, on the other hand, seem to be perfect for the job!

Deputized thugs and warrior priests? No thank you! I already have more than enough hands in my gold pouch, what with the demands of business and all.\n\nBesides, I'd rather keep this between you and me. It's so much more … intimate, don't you agree?
My sincerest apologies! I didn't mean to offend you.\n\nI guess some people wouldn't be satisfied with all the gold in Anvil or my huge ….
Nothing! Nothing!\n\nDuly noted! I promise never to make such implications again! Is there anything else you want to ask about before you start hunting the murderer?

Amelie Crowe? Do you know her? I gave her a letter, right there on the Anvil docks. I have no idea where she went in such a hurry, but she seemed excited to receive it.\n\nAnyway, I have more deliveries to make before I can rest for the day. Farewell!

How did you know about that? I didn't tell anyone. Of course, it was delivered to the Trading Company building, so I suppose someone could have seen it arrive.\n\nYes, I received a sweetroll. Came in a small box. At first, I thought nothing of it ….

I took a bite and found a slip of paper inside. With a message. But it didn't sound very threatening. Not until you mentioned it. "Tomorrow is your last day in Kvatch." \n\nI just assumed I'd be going to Anvil in a few days. For business.
That's excellent advice, friend! I'll stay in the market until closing time and then I'll head over to the Gold Coast Trading Company building. That place is built like a fort!

I knew this day was going too well. Now I'm being threatened by a tasty dessert and an insane murderer!\n\nI'll go and hide inside the Gold Coast Trading Company. It's sturdy as a fortress and there are always people around. I'll be safe there!

You were? Well, that makes me feel so much better! If anyone can stop the Sweetroll Killer, I imagine it would be someone just like you.\n\nI'm going to finish my tour of the merchant stalls, unless you think that's unwise ….

Of course. Put thoughts of imminent death in my head and then leave me to fend for myself!\n\nOnce you've had a chance to consider my situation, do come back and let me know. Hopefully, I'll still be alive when you get here.

There was that Wood Elf merchant we worked with. Found him floating in a river not far from here.\n\nHe got a sweetroll with a message. Kept to his daily routine despite the warning. Then one day, he never showed up at the Trading Company.

I'm not foolish enough to cross the Dark Brotherhood. It's true, normally chains firmly bar the moat door, but that changed recently for reasons I'm not privy to. Someone must be using it.\n\nYou can use it, too, if you're quick and quiet about it.

You know I'm a baker, correct? So who else could be the Sweetroll Killer? Imbeciles.\n\nDespite the threats and the loss of business, I did receive one of those menacing sweetrolls. The note inside even predicts my impending death.

Would it do any good? From what I've heard, everyone who receives these prognosticating pastries dies, despite the explicit warnings.\n\nWho am I to suppose I can avoid the fate that so clearly awaits me?

Best keep looking, then. I've been out here most of the day, but you're the first soul I've seen.\n\nSo many in Kvatch have forgotten the old ways. They're all obsessed with their giant cathedral. They've forgotten how we used to worship. Shame, that.

Seriously? Well, good luck with that. I truly wish you well.\n\nAll the same, I'll continue with my chosen course of action, seeing as how no one has been able to stop the Sweetroll Killer so far. Unless, of course, you have a better suggestion …?

I met some of them when they came to accuse me of sending the threatening baked goods. As if I'm the only baker capable of making sweetrolls in the entire Gold Coast!\n\nThey ran. They hid. They avoided others. And then they died, each and every one.

Those zealots are the worst thing to happen to Kvatch in sixty years, and I've lived through eight wars and the corrupt reign of the Longhouse Emperors.\n\nIf you're looking for more of their kind, inquire in Kvatch rather than bothering pious folk.

Thank you so much for agreeing with my very personal decision. Now, if you're done interrogating me, I'd like to finish this peaceful moment before I return to work.\n\nAnd most likely die horribly, just as the sweetroll predicted.

You're suggesting I challenge fate? Alter my comfortable schedule in hopes of avoiding certain death?\n\nI suppose that makes a modicum amount of sense. Anvil is nice this time of year. And the pirates do appreciate a good sweetroll ….
I suppose I'll be here awhile longer, relaxing before I need to return to my ovens and cooling racks.\n\nBut eventually I have to get back to work. My sweetrolls won't make themselves, you know.
A sweetroll? How do you know about …?\n\nHmm. Yes, I received a sweetroll. Just as my husband did before he disappeared. What interests are my troubles to you, I wonder?

Really? Did Reman hire you? How kind. Though why he cares now when he couldn't be bothered after my husband vanished makes me curious as to his true intentions.\n\nPerhaps fate will take a different course. Certainly I didn't predict your involvement.

My husband? He received one of those sweetrolls with the message inside. Just like I did. The dire prediction frightened him, I can tell you that.\n\nHe gathered weapons and locked himself in his study. But he still disappeared without a trace.

I thought I did. Well, no, I don't know him that well. I mean, I know people like him. Liars and cheaters who use people and take advantage of their giving nature.\n\nSo Reman hired you to stop the murderer? I find that to be very interesting.

No. The others who received the sweetrolls, I'm sure they need more help than me. I've got a house in Anvil. I can hide there until you catch the murderer. Just watch out for that Reman. His own interests are more important to him than anything else.
You don't remember me, do you? We ran into each other on the streets of Anvil some time back, when it seems both of us were looking to attract the attention of the Dark Brotherhood.
Yes! That's it! I love that, don't you? The silence that fills the void where words should be. It's positively pregnant with menace. The effect it has on people is unmistakable.

I should probably be cursing your name, you know. I'd been trying to grab their attention for days, and then you arrived to haunt the Gold Coast like some malignant wraith. I had to redouble my efforts.
Hmm, let's see. I kept a list. La, da, da, da, da … looks like thirteen.
That's how it's done, isn't it? Death is our business, and business is good. I'm quoting the Matron, of course.
Sure, sure. Well, I'd best be off. May the Dread Father guide your blade.
There it is again! Makes my blood run absolutely cold. You're magnificent at the silence thing!
You think so? I suppose you would know, the way I hear it you're the Sanctuary's new darling. I'll consider what you said.
Why in the world would you ask me about that? I'm just a beggar. You know, I beg. Um, spare some gold?\n\nLook, you better not try anything. There are guards everywhere.
What did I do wrong? People are supposed to ignore beggars. Just walk on by like they don't exist. But not you. You want to help.

Because … oh, never mind! I'm going to get in so much trouble for this.\n\nLook, you stay here and look for another beggar to bother. I'm going … someplace else. Now leave me alone or … or you're going to regret it!
Will you just go away and leave me alone! I don't want any trouble!\n\nBut if you must know, yes. I received one of those terrible predictions. Are you happy now?

The work of the Queen's Eyes, that's what's going on here. That business with Captain Apinia wrapped up so quickly, Raz decided to look into another matter before heading home.\n\nTurns out, this other matter has eluded Raz for many years.

I want you to kill Artorius and fill the Void with his blood. Let the Order see what it means to challenge the Dark Brotherhood. Show them what happens when you hunt the hunters.\n\nBut reaching Artorius will require all of your Brothers and Sisters.

One man who hides behind thick walls and a small army.\n\nWe sent Tanek to Kvatch to find a way to breach the Cathedral's defenses. Astara and the rest of your brethren will follow after you. Get to Artorius and kill well, Assassin.

The locals call him the "Sweetroll Killer," yes? Much better than our term. "The One Who Predicts Your Death and Then Stabs You In the Face."\n\nRaz sees that you're looking into this as well. Perhaps we can exchange notes? Help each other out?

The Rat Master has ears everywhere. And who knows who our stabby-face killer is? Don't want to give away our plans before we formulate them, yes?\n\nRaz suggests we go somewhere more private, once you finish your investigation.

You wound this one. What has Raz done to make you so wary?\n\nYou could hunt this killer on your own, but where's the fun in that? Raz helps you, you help Raz, and everything turns out well in the end. Let's continue this talk in private, though, yes?

Raz and lady Elf will meet you in our safe house after you finish your tasks. We've commandeered the enchanter shop. Not the most luxurious hiding place, but this one has had worse.\n\nWe're going to have a glorious adventure, just like old times!

Raz has seen these types of killings before. A victim receives a sweetroll that contains a prediction of impending doom, then is murdered a few days later.\n\nThe murderer killed several of the Queen's advisors and then escaped. Made Raz look bad.

So much doubt! Haven't you figured out that Raz is perfect yet?\n\nBut yes, I fear we're dealing with the same monster. Luckily, my apprentice received a sweetroll. That means we can set a trap! There's just one problem ….
We locate a messenger and figure out what they've been placing around town. Maybe even get them to lead us right to the killer!\n\nMeet Raz outside and we'll track them together.

All right. Probably more than one. But what concerns Raz is the network of messengers the killer is using to deliver his gifts. They've placed notes in the oddest locations.\n\nRaz fears these actions indicate the killer plans to strike—and soon!
Which clue in specific would you like help with, Raz wonders? But Raz must warn you, I'm better at killing things than at solving riddles.

<<1>>'s ledger? The blackmail you stole from <<2>>? This is our blueprint to pulling heists, just like we used to.\n\nWe can hit our rivals where it hurts. Take their ill-gotten gains for ourselves. Use it to rebuild.

Among the blackmail, I noticed the name <<1>>. He's a "claw-cutter"—a thief who robs other thieves. Wouldn't you know? He's signed on as our master of heists.\n\nNow, and don't strain yourself … who should you speak with next?
Ah, Raz thinks he knows about these clues. It's obvious! Look for something that resembles a knight and a wolf around town, yes?
Hmm. Perch is a place to sit, correct? And sports fighters, those could be some sort of gladiators.\n\nI wonder, is there a place where people can watch gladiators in this city?

Let Raz think about that one. Hmm. If we're looking down, it has to be someplace above us. Maybe the roof of one of the buildings?\n\nWell, Jone and Jode wouldn't have given me claws if they didn't want this one to climb!
Anyone can find a reason to kill someone. Ambition, jealousy, humiliation. I once killed for a jester who couldn't take a joke. \n\nCareful who you heckle in Stormhaven.
Me? I'm flattered. No, no, that's not the right word ….\n\nUncomfortable? Yes, that's it. Well, whatever do you want to know about me for?

Not the brooding type? Good. They're a bore. \n\nI've been with Astara at this Sanctuary since its inception. More years than I care to remember. In that time I've done enough contract killing to know how to drum up business. It's my charm.

No one knew I was on the Gold Coast. No one except you. Suddenly someone delivers a sweetroll with my name on it and a note predicting my untimely demise.\n\nIt looks like you betrayed me. Give me a reason not to run you through.

Everyone who received one of the menacing sweetrolls is traveling to Anvil for one reason or another. Seems to me if the killer is smart, that's where he'll make his move.\n\nAs a matter of fact, I'm headed there now. No one threatens me and lives.

So you followed my messengers and found me instead? Ever since I received the threatening sweetroll, I've been looking into other targets, trying to figure out who knows me and why they want to kill me.\n\nWell, why they want to kill me this time.

As much as I admire curiosity, sometimes your questions can be somewhat … irritating.\n\nThe Matron asked me to research the journal and give her a report. My research requires that we visit my former Sanctuary. All in the line of duty, as it were.

Should I go and tell Astara that I'm taking her best recruit to a place the Dark Brotherhood destroyed and abandoned so that we can uncover the truth of the Black Dragon?\n\nHmm. I'd say no. Let's not do that. She'll hear about it soon enough, anyway.

Seems like bad form to spill all the gory details. Suffice it to say, he swindled some rather important clients and had the audacity to steal from House Hlaalu itself.\n\nThe last straw was when he closed two orphanages to open a cornerclub.

It was supposed to be a simple run. Pick up silks and spices on the way back to Vulkhel Guard and turn a tidy profit. But the Governor's taxes are going to bankrupt us.\n\nEven dead, that woman vexes our travels.

My sister and I were estranged long before she tumbled drunk off her balcony and went splat on the ground.\n\nThis is my arena. I set the fights and make the rules. If you've got a problem with that, you can direct your complaints to the nearest bear.

Before we started our dig, the location was literally just a hole billowing smoke from the ground. A geological oddity, but not much else. When I discovered it might have been the former site of Fort Faleria, its significance rose a hundredfold!
Raz is glad you agree. Weapon safety is very important, yes?\n\nNow let's go track down a killer.
Eh, Raz doesn't think that's such a good idea, but he will give the lady Elf a little knife. Just in case.\n\nNow let's go track down a killer!

What about her? Oh, Raz sees what you're getting at. She'll stay here and hopefully not wind up murdered.\n\nShe's still in training and we haven't gotten to the use of weapons yet. Last time I gave her a dagger she almost put out her eye.

Raz wants to disagree with you, but he cannot. Naryu and Raz will find the other targets. Hide them in Engra's Hostel where we can keep an eye on them.\n\nIn the meantime, Raz has something he'd like you to do.

I found her on one of my trading expeditions. She talked of visions. How they helped her shape the ripples of fate. Crazy talk. But useful. You understand?\n\nI could point her at a target. Like an arrow. Set her loose and watch them die.

Not any more. Obviously. You mentioned my name. Shouldn't have done that.\n\nShe knows I betrayed her. Knows I sent you to eliminate her. Hid my involvement in all this. I knew it the moment I arrived in Anvil and saw the sweetroll waiting for me.
Really? Raz is impressed! Did you threaten and cajole? It's Reman, correct? We can go to the inn, get drunk, and put this sorry affair behind us?\n\nWait, wait. Reman isn't a her?
Raz has made a deal with the Anvil Guard. It took more gold than Raz expected, but these people will be taken care of while we're away.
The gardener? No wonder Raz couldn't find her. \n\nBut we're wasting time. If you know where the murderer is, we should get moving. Let's go dunk the Sweetroll Killer in the bitter milk of justice!

You don't know how much I despise that name. I am a Fate-Bearer. One of the select few who can see what the future holds and then do something about it.\n\nEach of my targets had the potential to cause unmitigated disasters. I stopped them.

Just don't get in my way. I'm still trying to figure out your game in all this. But we've worked well together in the past. Might as well take advantage of that.\n\nI'll confer with Raz to make sure he and I see eye to eye, and we'll meet you in Anvil.

Go back to beginning. Talk to Reman, the one who hired you. Raz thinks he knows more than he's said.\n\nGo to the Gold Coast Trading Company and see what he's hiding. Hurt him if you must. Just make sure he lives long enough for us to find Yarmia.
Then breathe deep of the resin's fumes one last time. Let's see if we can learn the fate of my lost Sister, Lyra.

Already have one, hero. Raz wants the Wood Elf and I to stick close so he can watch out for us. We'll gather the rest of the targets and get them to safety.\n\nI'd prefer to let the killer find me and finish this, but the cat is very insistent.

I don't trust Reman. He hired you to look into all this but I think he knows more than he told you.\n\nGo to the Gold Coast Trading Company and find out whatever you can about this fool. He makes my ears tingle, which tells me he's hiding something.
Lyra Viria died the day the Black Dragon was born, just as the journal said. My friend is gone.\n\nAll that remains is another enemy of the Dark Brotherhood. An enemy that will die by my hand.
And that's information we need to convey to Astara.\n\nServant and master both need to be dropped into the Void for daring to strike against us.
You met her. The gardener. She has a farmhouse … southeast of Anvil … but she won't be there for long.\n\nI'm dying. And it's your fault. I hope you realize … I'm not going to pay you for this ….

Darien, mostly. It's always Darien who ends up causing problems, isn't it? How long has it been since we defeated Molag Bal and saved Tamriel?\n\nSorry, time's a bit fuzzy at the moment. I've had more than a few late nights.

I'm searching for a way to retrieve souls lost in Coldharbour or elsewhere. I'm not even sure where to start looking, but I need to start somewhere, right?\n\nDarien's out there. I know it. I just have to find him, though that's easier said than done.

Well, Darien was with us at the end, wasn't he? Facing down Molag Bal. He didn't come back, and he didn't die, so logic suggests he returned when we did. He simply came back somewhere else.\n\nI just have to figure out where. Then I can bring him back.

Yes, well, I'm not making any more progress by complaining to you, am I? Foot to the grindstone, and all that. Hmm. I might be mixing metaphors there. Maybe I should take a nap.\n\nAnyway, it was nice to see you. Don't be a stranger.

Dozens. Hundreds! The problem with having so many ideas is that it's like these books behind me. They just pile up, and you can't possibly read all of them. So you read what you can and try to focus.\n\nThis might be why I'm not getting enough sleep.

No, not really. This is more like independent research. Do you know every Mages Guild in Tamriel has different books in its library? You'd think we'd standardize, or at least keep a lexicon.\n\nAlso, they could really use some more bookshelves.

Perhaps. My sister, Sara, was supposed to meet me here, but she hasn't shown up yet. She's a week late, which is unusual for her. So organized. I hope she hasn't run into any trouble.\n\nThe guild sent her to Craglorn. Not the most pleasant of places.

Raz would try to convince Naryu to stay and watch over them, but he doesn't want to get a blade stuck between his ribs.\n\nLet's hope luck favors the bold and we stop the killer before she comes back for the others.
If this killer has harmed Yarmia in any way, this one will make her wish she had never of Razum-dar.
You what? A note from Darien? How is that possible? What did it say?

The Colored Rooms are Meridia's realm! Oh, that makes so much sense. Meridia was with us at the end, fought Molag Bal at our sides. If Darien didn't end up in Coldharbour…\n\nYes, this helps. This helps a great deal. Now I know where to look for him!

Her fate is the worst of all. Her daughter causes the world to burn. Or she could. The future is a fluid thing.\n\nI have seen my escape and my death, both possible at this moment. And both championed by each of your allies. But the choice is yours.

Good and evil has no bearing on my visions. It's their actions that concern me. Each causes a ripple that radiates through time until a disaster occurs.\n\nEconomic collapse, the death of a prominent leader, a Queen betrayed … I had to stop them.

To save these people, of course. Let me walk out of here and I'll provide the antidote for the poison now coursing through their blood. Or kill me and let them die.\n\nThe choice is yours. Confer with your allies and then let me know what you decide.

Your target awaits in <<1>>. Fortuitous. It seems there's some kind of party going on in that cave. Slaying revelers is ever so satisfying.\n\nYou'll be seen as a trespasser there, so if you want to avoid a bounty then you should avoid being seen.

A lovely young High Elf named <<1>>. It was simple adultery. Nothing more. I will never understand why such … indiscretions drive men to homicide, but then again, I'm only married to my work.\n\nKill her.
A Breton named <<1>>. He's a chronicler—a very fine one I'm told. Alas, his desire to root out the truth has set him afoul of some very dangerous people.\n\nKill him.

A toothless Baandari peddler named <<1>>. Apparently she swindled our client out of some treasured family memento. The memento is long gone—lost in a dice game I think. So we were called on out of spite.\n\nKill this cat.

<<1>>. A Dark Elf Scale-Catcher. He made his fortune capturing escaped slaves, you see? So, a few dozen Argonian captives pooled their assets and performed the Sacrament as revenge.\n\nKill this slaver.

An Orc forge-wife named <<1>>. Quite a mouthful, that. Apparently she conspired with her fellow wives to slay their chief-husband in his bed. It went poorly. He managed to kill all of them save one.\n\nSlay this Orc.

Place was quiet and empty when we arrived. To be fair, we haven't checked any of the buildings yet. Raz wanted to wait for you. No one wants to miss their own party, yes?\n\nWhenever you're ready, we can start the search ….
Well, yes, there is that.\n\nRaz changed his mind. Bargaining should be considered. We have to do whatever we can to keep these people safe. Besides, we can always resume the hunt another day.
No, not even a tiny bit.\n\nBut Raz supposes that a chance to save innocents is better than no chance at all. Raz says let her live.

Damn right, you do. She's crazy as a cracked mudcrab! All her talk about fate and the future. And what she said about me. I don't have a daughter. I hate children! It's never going to happen.\n\nAny way you look at it, Louna has to die.

What about them? She's going to kill again. And she's going to come back for us. She thinks we're going to wreck the world! If we save a few now, how many more will she kill later?\n\nI say end her life and be done with it!
Then out with it. Don't leave us all in suspense. Which of the possible fates have you decided to favor with your decision?
I accept your decision and will honor my word. I'll go with Razum-dar and give him the antidote.

I accept your decision and will not resist. I have seen all the possible fates and now I am destined to lose to you every time.\n\nMy brethren will finish what I began, though. I know this in my heart. The future is safe in the Fate-Bearers' hands.

That I can't promise. It's my burden to bear the dictates of fate, and that burden sends me where it will. But for now, we'll return to Vvardenfell. To our shrine of the changing fates.\n\nInteresting. It appears we'll meet again there.

Fear is one of the Brotherhood's greatest allies, but we treasure silence as well.\n\nShow me that you are the master of quiet dread. Complete your task without alerting the residents of <<1>> to your presence.
The Night Mother's children must be as swift as they are deadly, like the strike of a coiled serpent.\n\nWith that in mind, I challenge you to complete your task before the Cove Overseer arrives.
A Nord called <<1>>. A drunk and an abuser. I assure you, he will not be missed. His daughter paid double, so please make it as painful and grisly as possible.\n\nKill this man.
A Redguard named <<1>>. Some kind of business dispute I'm told. She refused to sell her mill to a competitor, so he has turned to … less conventional means of negotiation.\n\nSlay this Redguard.

The Hour has moved its most elite members into Castle Kvatch and locked the place down. You'll need to find a way inside to get at Scipio.\n\nMy Rat Master tells me the guard tower might be the best route. The key can be found on the castellan.

Yes, Raz does not like that, either. The murders of the Queen's advisors remain unavenged. Still, Raz thinks we made the correct choice.\n\nBut these Fate-Bearers. Do they worry you as much as they worry me?

Raz likes how you think! Now the apprentice Elf and I will return home and continue her training.\n\nThis one wonders if Naryu and the others will ever be truly safe. Vvardenfell sounds like a dangerous place that just got more deadly.

After all we've been through and that's the first thing you want to say to me? To be fair, it's very comfortable and it looks great on me.\n\nIt's the uniform of my organization. They expect me to dress the part when I arrive back home.

Vvardenfell. It's far from here, but I have friends and family there. It will be good to see them again.\n\nBesides, I hear my organization has big plans in the works. Can't blame me for wanting to be a part of all that.

I haven't forgotten what the Sweetroll Killer said. Her words will probably haunt me for the rest of my life. But it's my life and I plan on living it. I'll deal with the Fate-Bearers when the time is right.\n\nFor now, I just wanted to thank you.

For now.\n\nIf you let me live, I'll call off the other Fate-Bearers. There's always a chance the future will change. We'll all hope for the best and assume they'll have long lives. But if you kill me, my brethren will find and kill them—eventually.

Raz trusts her as much as he can balance on his own tail. Which is not at all. He has tried.\n\nBut these Fate-Bearers. They won't stop until they eliminate each and every target—including Yarmia. Raz cannot let that happen, so Raz says let her live.

That I can't promise. It's my burden to bear the dictates of fate, and that burden directs me as it will. For now the Fate-Bearers will return to Vvardenfell. To our shrine of the changing fates.\n\nInteresting. It seems we'll meet again there.
I accept your decision and will honor my word. I'll call off my brethren and we'll let the streams of fate determine what the future will bring.\n\nFor now.

I accept your decision and will not resist. Just know that you are damning your people. None of you will be safe from the Fate-Bearers. You will be hunted and killed. The future will happen as it has been foreseen.\n\nIt says so in your sweetroll.
Under normal circumstances, no. These recent attacks against us, however, have made circumstances far from normal.\n\nConcentrate on the Grand Sermonizer. That's your primary mission.

Have you been so inundated with contracts that you've forgotten? The Count performed the Sacrament and named Governor Fortunata, promising us gold and information on the Black Dragon. You completed our part of the bargain. Now it's the Count's turn.

Raz and the lady Elf have commandeered the enchanter shop. Not the most luxurious headquarters, but this one has had worse.\n\nFinish your tasks and meet us there. This is going to be a glorious adventure, my friend, Raz can promise you that!

I already told your associate everything I know. The woman with the dark hair and the staff. Mirabelle, I believe she said her name was. Do I really need to repeat myself to every assassin that slips out of the shadows?

If that's supposed to frighten me, it's working.\n\nThe Black Dragon is the First Sword of the Order of the Hour. They're using the old Enclave of the Hourglass to amass an army. Siege weapons, new recruits—it's a threat to your people and mine!

Of course. I assume you don't know the Black Dragon is the First Sword of the Order of the Hour? My spies report they're amassing an army at the Enclave of the Hourglass. Siege weapons, new recruits—they threaten Kvatch and the Brotherhood alike!

Not a clue. We only suspected that the murder victims were members of your guild recently, so my spies never even explored that line of questioning.\n\nNo offense, but if the lot of you wound up destroying each other, I wouldn't lose any sleep over it.

Just that the Black Dragon is one of the deadliest warriors I've ever seen. Wears armor as dark as Oblivion and twice as frightening. Even makes the rest of the Order nervous.\n\nRight after I received the first reports about her, the murders began.

By the Ruby Throne, stop doing that!\n\nI've told you everything I know. The Order of the Hour has increased its numbers by offering pardons to Fortunata's pirates, and the Black Dragon can be found in the Enclave of the Hourglass. Now leave me be!
Did I admit anything of the sort? I believe you're quite mistaken.\n\nCome. I'll take you to the Black Dragon's chambers and you can see for yourself.
I'm the …?\n\nYou honor me with high praise, intruder. If only I had my armor and weapons, then you'd know for sure.
You're pretty good at that. Silence can be very intimidating. In the right hands, of course.\n\nCome. I'll take you to the Black Dragon's chambers and you can meet her yourself.
Did seeing Cimbar laid low give you pause? It should.\n\nIf someone as highly trained as him can be caught and killed, what's that say about your own chances?
You did well to rescue Hildegard. Our numbers are thinning quickly enough as it is.\n\nBut if you're finished traipsing through the woods, there's work to be done. You still need to earn your keep.

Fortunata? Yes, quite a notch in your belt. I suppose I'll have to concede that you've come into your own. I'll have to muster a bit of respect when I speak to you from now on.\n\nOr at least a trifle.
I'm aware ….\n\nI don't play favorites, Assassin. Except for Mirabelle. Now she's gone and I feel like I'm the worse for it.
Our new recruits seem obsessed with the notion that the Black Dragon is one of us. Initiates will believe anything, but Astara said you were looking into it.\n\nSo, is there truth to it?
You probably expect some pithy remark, but all I can come up with is, "you have my thanks." Such are the times we live in.\n\nI hope she suffers for what she did.
The new recruits look to you as a role model. You should scowl a little more, Silencer.
I have never seen him. People say he is fifty-hands tall, with spines as sharp as Mehrunes' Razor. This is probably exaggeration though. He cannot be more than thirty-hands … forty at the most.

"Tall" is just a matter of perspective, right? Well … no I guess it is not. Thirty hands is enormous. Do not worry about it. I am certain he is very stupid and clumsy. Killing him will be a roll in the mud for warriors such as we.

They are the wisest members of the tribe. They carry the Root-Talk, and know all the sacred croaks and Chukka-sei naming secrets. Losing them would be like having our hearts cut out. We cannot let Na-Kesh claim them for the Xit-Xaht.

The Blade of Woe is the ebony dagger of our Brotherhood. It is a single weapon, unique and powerful in the right hands. When one of our Brothers or Sisters needs the blade for a kill, it appears to help carry out the assassination.

I sometimes forget the details myself, Assassin. That's one of the reasons I write everything down.\n\nYou discovered that the Black Dragon is a member of the Order of the Hour, but the price for that knowledge was Mirabelle's life.

Which I have been studying in an attempt to determine what the true connection is between the Black Dragon and Lyra, the Sister I thought was killed in the purification.\n\nThat's what I hope to uncover when we visit my former Sanctuary.

She's a Black Marsh tracker who I've had the pleasure to work with in the past. We can trust her implicitly.\n\nBesides, she has the most enticing fascination with all things Shadowscale. You'd think I'd find that annoying, but not in the least.
Well done. \n\nWhat about the challenges that I posed for this task?
Well done. \n\nWhat about the challenges that I posed for this task?

The Brotherhood is not without mercy. Some of our targets are given a quick and painless death. Others? Well … our kindness has limits.\n\nYour quarry must die in agony. Use your most lethal poisons and you will be richly rewarded.
According to our client, the target loves a certain <<1>> more than anything. A puzzling obsession, but who am I to judge?\n\nDestroy this heirloom while you're there.

We have a slight snag. The client who sent us after this target also mentioned that he was having trouble with a nosy chronicler.\n\nI want you to kill two guar with one stone, as the saying goes. Kill the chronicler, <<1>>.
I know you have many weapons at your disposal, but our Dread Father's blade must be blooded to keep its edge. The time has come to honor Sithis.\n\nUse the Blade of Woe to slay your target.
The client has urged us to destroy a <<1>> before we leave the Cove. A curious request. Nonetheless, tracking down this formula is a fitting challenge. Destroy it and you will be rewarded.

A feckless would-be assassin has been cutting into our profits. The peddler <<1>> insults our Dread Father by using this assassin and not coming to us for her death-dealing needs. \n\nKill her in the Brotherhood's name.

Your target awaits in the <<1>>. It's a damp and torchlit cave—the perfect hiding place for fugitives and witless thugs.\n\nYou'll be seen as a trespasser there, so if you wish to avoid a bounty then you should avoid being seen.

A bard named <<1>>. He is a talentless fool who loiters outside the Cathedral of Akatosh both day and night. One of the Chanters grew weary of his off-key singing and performed the Black Sacrament.\n\nKill this would-be musician.
He's an Argonian named <<1>>. A very successful gambler, I'm told. Our client insisted that <<1>> is a shameless cheater—as if such things matter to us.\n\nKill this lizard.

A chef named <<1>>. She was called to prepare a great feast for House Hlaalu. Alas, she used sour kwama eggs in her famous souffle. Dark Elf nobles are not fond of parties that end with relentless vomiting.\n\nKill this cook.

A Nord woman named <<1>>. The client didn't offer any reasons for why he wanted her dead—but he was wearing nothing but a pearl necklace and wooden shoes when our brother arrived, so I assume he's just insane.\n\nSlay <<1>>.

<<1>>. A big-game hunter out of Valenwood. He managed to kill a sacred crocodile on one of his expeditions to Black Marsh. He claimed ignorance, but the local tree-minder was not convinced.\n\nSlay this Wood Elf.

True followers of Sithis are like wraiths—only visible when they wish to be.\n\nShow me that you are a master of stealth. Complete your task without alerting the residents of the <<1>> to your presence.

The work of an assassin demands secrecy, certainly, but also speed. Our knives must strike quickly. Decisively.\n\nWith that in mind, I challenge you to finish your dark work before the tunnel's Overseer arrives.

<<1>>. He's a serial killer who has avoided prosecution for years. Not by stealth, mind you. He's royalty. The chief inspector has grown tired of the lies and obstructions, so he called to us. Ironic, yes?\n\nKill this Elf.

A Khajiit named <<1>>. One of his friends called on us to "give <<1>> a scare." I think it has something to do with an escalating war between pranksters. Alas, poor <<1>>, we are not in the business of pranks.\n\nKill this Khajiit.
It seems that our target has a taste for the fouler things in life. We should give them a taste of their own bitter medicine, don't you agree?\n\nUse poison to kill your prey.

I'm glad you asked. Apparently these smugglers have unearthed an object of some value. A <<1>>. Rumor has it that they're quite beautiful. The promise of a new, industrious colony contained in a single vessel.\n\nDestroy it.

A long-time enemy of our Brotherhood, <<1>>, may be visiting the tunnels. His chronicling was little more than a nuisance at first, but his meddling grows tiresome.\n\nTrack this fool down and slay him.
The Blade of Woe is one of our most sacred tools. It is a pure manifestation of our Dread Father's will, you see?\n\nHonor our Brotherhood and Sithis by killing the target with the Blade of Woe.

Our client asked us to destroy some <<1>> that the target pilfered some time ago. Evidence of some petty indiscretion no doubt. Such matters are typically beneath our notice, but the client has … deep pockets.\n\nFind the documents and destroy them.
I'm told that the target has a treasured pet named "Lucky." Pathetic sentiment. Our Dread Father has nothing but scorn for the tamed and the weak. Slay this beast in his name.

You must go to the <<1>>. I hear it's remarkably cozy, for a sewer. Full of the little comforts that put our targets at ease—that make them careless.\n\nYou'll be considered a trespasser, so if you want to avoid a bounty you should avoid being seen.

A healer named <<1>>. Our client is convinced that <<1>> let his brother die. It's nonsense. The brother had the Knahaten Flu. There was nothing this healer could have done. But that's neither here nor there.\n\nKill this healer.

<<1>>. Just a poor fool who happened to be in the wrong place at the wrong time. He bumbled into a particularly heinous Sanguinary feast while the revelers were not wearing their masks.\n\nHe saw too much. Kill him.

I'm not often impressed by our clients, but this <<1>>'s request is spectacular. You see, she performed the Sacrament on herself. It's all part of an elaborate plan to frame her husband for her murder. \n\nSuch a waste of talent. Shame. Kill her.
An Argonian called <<1>>. He's organizing a search party to look for a Nord maiden who disappeared a few days ago. Alas for poor <<1>>, that maiden does not want to be found.\n\nKill this lizard.

A Dark Elf named <<1>>. She received a massive inheritance from her mother. Meanwhile, her brother received nothing. Fortunately, he is the prime beneficiary in Andilo's will.\n\nGreed. We'd go hungry without it. Kill this Elf.

The sewer is a tangled nest of tunnels and cisterns. Even the most wary assassin can be caught off guard there. But we are much more than assassins, aren't we?\n\nComplete your task without alerting the residents of the <<1>> to your presence.

I'm eager to see just how swift you are. This is the perfect opportunity to put your speed to the test.\n\nAn Overseer stalks those sewers periodically. My challenge is simple: kill your mark and escape the sewers before the Overseer arrives.

<<1>>. A renowned equestrian. The Courier Stakes is coming up, and the bookkeepers are certain that he'll win. Our client would like to keep Andus out of the saddle. Permanently.\n\nKill this Imperial.

An Orc named <<1>>. She's a low-level dealer for a skooma cartel. Or she was. Somehow she managed to make off with a king's ransom after a … failed transaction. Her employers want her dead.\n\nKill her.

Any common footpad can murder someone. It's knowledge, refinement, and discipline that set a true assassin apart.\n\nShow me that you are truly committed to your craft. Use poison to kill this target.

Our target has come into possession of a rare <<1>>. There are many parties who are interested in acquiring it, and I'd rather not have people poking around after a murder.\n\nDestroy this bauble. Leave no trace.
<<1>> and our target are apparently inseparable. Let it not be said that I am without sentiment.\n\nKill this Imperial. They will be united in death.
If blood is to be spilled, let it be spilled in Sithis's name. Use the Blade of Woe. In doing so, you honor your Dread Father and the Brotherhood.

The client requested that we destroy one of the target's favored possessions—a <<1>>. It is an heirloom, you see? All that history … all those memories, gone in an instant.\n\nSithis will be pleased to see it destroyed.
I have reason to suspect that <<1>> witnessed one of our assassinations. She has not reported it to anyone yet, but I leave nothing to chance.\n\nKill her.
Splendid! We shall see how well you marry business with death. But first, allow me to present you with a gift. I shall teach you how to call upon a particular tool of our trade.
A tool for dealing death, of course. One forged by unseen hands. The Blade of Woe. Wield it from the shadows and its edge shall deliver your prey to Sithis in the Void.

I grant you access to the Blade of Woe. Sharper than any other dagger you have at your disposal, it shall be your weapon just as silence is your armor.\n\nWield the blade from the shadows and let its edge send your prey to Sithis.

You realize that our organizations don't exactly play nice with one another, right? The moment I leave myself open, they'll put a blade in my neck.\n\nYou joined the Brotherhood! You have to see how that makes me question our relationship.

I want to believe you. I really do. But until I figure out what you're really up to, I'll keep my feelings to myself. If you really care, your actions will speak louder than your words, any way.\n\nBesides, I still want to know what you're doing here.

Not in the least. They really are delicious! No, what makes them so insidious are the tiny notes they contain—a veiled threat and a prediction of impending doom!\n\nIt's ruining our profits, my tasty friend. And that's something I can't abide.

No, I have work to do and my life to live. At least as long as I'm able. People enjoy my cakes and pies. I'd never deny them such delicious treats.\n\nBut why do the predictions of a tasty bun concern you, I wonder?

What? You really think so? I've heard of the Sweetroll Killer, sure, but why would he target me?\n\nI … I think I'd better just keep doing what I've been doing. Remain in the market, near all the merchants and their customers. That's safe, right?

Reman? I'd … I'd rather not discuss my relationship with Reman, if you don't mind.\n\nHe's everything I abhor about a certain class of trader—greedy, self-indulgant, and interested in nothing more than increasing his hoard of gold.

I suppose. It's just, well, my condition. The lycanthropy.\n\nMy transformations. I can't trigger them at will and they don't follow any pattern we've been able to discern. Venom called it a "divergent strain." I'm not sure what that means.

I don't think I want to be cured. The wolf is a part of me. It's who I am.\n\nI would like to learn to control it, though. Kor and Mirabelle think I'll get the hang of it eventually. Venom even keeps meticulous records every time I change.

I guess so. Usually I can feel it coming, kind of like when Kor feels a storm in his big toe.\n\nAs long as I can get out of the Sanctuary or into my cage before I lose control, I won't hurt anybody. At least, not any of the family.

I know. I smelled it as soon as you arrived but I didn't want to say anything. Figured it was your secret to share. Or not.\n\nI'm glad you're here. Maybe you can even help me learn to gain some control—though I don't want to impose!

What if I asked you to paint a picture of chaos? Or to sculpt infinite darkness out of stone? \n\nSithis is the Void. The statue gives form to the unfathomable. A feeble attempt, but even Argonians succumb to such desires.

An average priest is easy prey, but don't underestimate the Grand Sermonizer. I heard whispers that she's a highly trained spellcaster. If that turns out to be true, please let me know. I like to keep my records up to date.

I never question the Matron, although it's strange for her to so hastily send multiple brethren to deal with a single target. It's almost as though she knows more than she is telling us.\n\nOf course, she almost always does.
It isn't? I'll make note of that. \n\nPerhaps this will be more useful—chasing after Hilde will likely result in your death as well.
Not once did I deny that. I simply set the facts at your feet. To act despite this knowledge … would not be such a terrible thing.
Is that so hard to believe? If I were hunting the Brotherhood, I would certainly attempt to infiltrate their ranks and destroy them from within.
Further research is required. I prefer not to act on a hunch. For now, let's continue to work our contracts and hope an opportunity to unmask the killer presents itself.

No one still living has my complete trust. I would advise you to walk a similar path in that regard. But I don't believe you're the killer. Not any more. \n\nBut something makes my scales itch. Something I'm missing ….
Governor Fortunata fears what all those in power fear—the loss of that power. She will no doubt seek to strike at someone she believes is key to the stability of Kvatch.

Killing your target will likely be the least difficult aspect of the job. I suggest discretion. Alerting others will be the real threat, especially if you're tasked with infiltrating a fortified area, such as the castle.
Killing the Grand Sermonizer is Cimbar's current contract. There's no reason to believe he won't complete the job. This paranoia … it doesn't suit us. We're better than this.

Advice? Just stay out of Cimbar's way and let him finish the job. But feel free to kill as many of those annoying street preachers as you like. I despise those wind bags.\n\nJust keep an eye out for the city guards. You're not ready to deal with them.
I don't need you to look after me, Initiate. I've seen more death than most and sent more than my share to the Void.

He was entertaining while he lasted. Perhaps even more so than some of my previous diversions. But that's all he was. What, do you think I loved him? \n\nI learned long ago to discard such silly notions.
The girl? I wouldn't think so. But the wolf, who can say? Hildegard is of two minds, and that can be both a blessing and a curse.

I'm loath to admit it, but something strange is going on.\n\nIt's hard to believe that a single armored warrior in a scary helmet could be behind theses troubles, though. It feels … bigger. Like we have enemies surrounding us, just waiting to attack.
Who do you think you are to question my actions? If you must know, Astara sent me. To look into the Order of the Hour's activities.\n\nSiege weapons, new recruits—they're building an army out here.
