Someone would need a lot of influence to go against us in such a brazen manner. I can't imagine who that would be.\n\nJust watch the shadows while you're out and about. Seems we're not the only ones prowling them these days.

That's just it. The Dark Brotherhood doesn't have a lot of enemies. We're just … business. Most prefer to stay on our good side or utilize us to their own ends. As long as they meet our price, we're happy to oblige.\n\nWhy destroy such a useful tool?

Of course you told her! You're the perfect disciple, so how could you not?\n\nAstara locked me in Hilde's cage. For my own good, she told me. But it was child's play to escape. I don't expect you to understand, but I need to do this. For Cimbar.
Saw right through that, did you? Astara didn't send me. That was a lie. I'm here without contract or permission.\n\nI know this might be hard for you to understand, but I need to do this. For Cimbar.
Just one thing. I need to find the Black Dragon and make her pay for what happened to Cimbar. I heard her voice and I'd recognize it anywhere.\n\nAre you going to stand in my way?

I don't expect you to understand and I don't want your help. But those siege weapons and other preparations the Order is making, you should do whatever you can to destroy them and disrupt their operations.
A contract? Not exactly. Astara had me infiltrate the castle staff a few months back, and I need to make an appearance every now and again if I want to maintain the ruse.
Very well. I know things about that place that even Fortunata's guards don't know. Such as the secret passages. Great way to get around if you don't want to be noticed.

Bite your tongue, Initiate! Better yet, let me do that for you.\n\nAnyway, the Matron wants eyes and ears near Fortunata. Let's us know what's going on and gives us an opportunity should the need arise. Besides, no one ever notices the hired help.
Never met the man, but Raz filled me in on the details.\n\nI had my eyes and ears around town do some digging. They confirmed that Reman visited with all of the targets right before he hired you.

Oh, I'd enjoy a little rough play with you, hero, but for now I want you to go learn more about Reman. Preferably while holding a blade to his throat.\n\nHe met with all of the Sweetroll Killer's targets except me, and I want to know why that is.

My guess is he never told you about a lot of things. That's why I want you to go and take a closer look at him. Get rough if you have to, but make sure he tells you everything he knows.\n\nHe might have the key we need to stop the Sweetroll Killer.

Did you have a brush with death? It would fit, and it would explain your special sight. The reason you can read the litany.\n\nThe last part is easier to interpret. Make ritual offerings with your sacred blade.
Ha! That's not bad, New-blade. Maybe you do have a sense of humor after all.

Heard about Mirabelle. Damn shame. Can't say I counted her as a friend, but she was part of the family. It sounds like you and Venom finally know who we're dealing with, at least.\n\nI look forward to things getting back to normal after you kill her.
Knightsgrave, was it? Some old ruined temple. I heard it was used by the Order of the Hour once, or some older version of the Order. It's been abandoned for years. Some people think it's haunted.

Oh, don't worry about the undead. They're the least of your problems. It's the minotaurs that I'd be concerned about.\n\nMinotaurs are drawn to old ruins like Kor to a barrel of mead. Avoid those beasts and you should be fine and dandy.

Isn't that Green-Venom-Tongue's job? You're just along to observe, New-blade.\n\nEven so, now that we know she's a trained assassin, we can turn the tables on her. She uses our own skills against us. Why not return the favor?

Don't let her take you by surprise. Hunt her. Back her into a corner and force her into a fight instead of leaving yourself open for an execution. One on one, toe to toe, I'd put my gold on you.\n\nThat's how you finish this, New-blade.

I don't smell any fear on you. Not even a hint. I bet she'll sense that, too. And maybe that will make her afraid for a change.\n\nI'll see you when you get back, Sister. This time I know you'll return.

I don't smell any fear on you. Not even a hint. I bet she'll sense that, too. And maybe that will make her afraid for a change.\n\nI'll see you when you get back, Brother. This time I know you'll return.

If you use a short blade, you can make that traitor's death slow and painful.\n\nOh, and one more thing. Knightsgrave. It's a cursed place, where the souls of the fallen knights are said to roam freely. Be careful in there.

Not much. Some kind of graveyard and monument to the Order of the Hour. I chased a man into those ruins once. Something made him turn around and run right into my blade.\n\nIt was a minotaur. A really big one.

It's true that removing the Grand Sermonizer would send a crucial message. The public needs to know that the loss of a few assassins does nothing to diminish us. \n\nJust follow the Matron's orders. I'll keep my objections to myself.

Neither do you, come to think of it. Is it bad to be … different?\n\nI may not have the training or experience of some of the others, but Astara says I'm the best tracker in the family. Whenever a target tries to hide, I always find them.

I don't remember much of what the wolf does. Kor assures me that I'm never cruel when I send souls to Father. I trust my Brother. And I trust Astara. They saved me. Gave me something to believe in. For that, I'm happy to serve the Dark Brotherhood.

The wolf kills. That is its purpose.\n\nAstara taught me that I become a wolf in order to accomplish what the Night Mother requests of her children. My prey already belongs to Sithis. The wolf just helps them find the Void.
I felt no particular emotions concerning him whatsoever. Not all of us form attachments so easily.
For another time, perhaps. At present, I suggest you focus on your contracts. Take care getting too personal with your Brothers and Sisters. Attachments can become a … distraction.
I care about performing my duties under the shadow of Sithis. That includes following the Tenets. I aid my Brothers and Sisters when I can. Beyond that … I'd rather not say.

Proper. I like that. \n\nJust remember to obey the Tenets. No matter what you see, no matter what you find, don't dishonor the Brotherhood. It's not our place to question the Night Mother's will or how the Black Hand carries it out.

Isn't their will reason enough? Suffice it to say, they believed the Sanctuary harbored a traitor. To protect the Brotherhood and its secrets, every member was eliminated—save Green-Venom-Tongue, who was away at the time and deemed innocent.

Of course. It was a fascinating situation, a rare example of the anger and fury of the Black Hand.\n\nGreen-Venom-Tongue's former Sanctuary was purified, every member killed by order of the Black Hand. It's the only time I ever heard of such an event.

Fortunata ap Dugal, Anvil's late and lamented "provincial governor." She died as she lived, that old Pirate Queen! But her legacy lives on, tainting the Gold Coast, more's the pity.\n\nFool's Gold Coast, if you want to be more accurate.
Raz's friend here, a pirate on the ship Apinia hired, says they found safe haven with the agents of the Gold Coast Trading Company.\n\nWhat they're doing in the ruins, Raz has no clue.
No, I imagine not. You seem more like a frolicker.
Some recruits believe joining the Dark Brotherhood imbues them with an otherworldly protection. The smarter ones remember we're all still flesh and blood.\n\nBe the latter, Initiate.
Don't let it go to your head. My esteem is a narrow and treacherous ledge from which you may plummet at any time.\n\nIt widens with bribery.
We had similar outlooks, that's all. \n\nShe wouldn't approve of us sitting here moping. If you need me, I'll be drinking to her and sharpening my knives.
To turn your back on us is to invite the knife, so she struck first. The fool. It only delays the inevitable.\n\nWhen the Wrath of Sithis catches up to her, all this will be answered a thousandfold.

I'd like to think he'll permit our fallen Brothers and Sisters to enact some vengeance of their own, or at least bear witness to whatever fate she suffers.\n\nBah, listen to me. I'm starting to sound like a true believer.
Perfect.
The Listener sent me to deliver the Litany of Blood.\n\nThat's all you need to know and more than I want to say.
As blank as the stare in a dead man's eyes. But go ahead and see for yourself.\n\nI'm curious to find out if the Listener is right about you. If you can see what's really there.

The Listener and the four Speakers make up the Black Hand, the ruling council of the Dark Brotherhood. You might even say she's the leader of the council.\n\nThe Listener hears the words of the Night Mother and whispers them to the Speakers.
Harshly.\n\nIf retribution cannot be delivered, then it is the Sanctuary that stands at fault.
When the chef cuts a chunk of mold from a wheel of cheese, do you call that punishment? It's purification, nothing more.

Communion with the Night Mother is a private thing. There have been exceptions, but most petitioners hide their dark desires from prying eyes.\n\nIt takes a deep commitment to see the Black Sacrament through, but that doesn't mean it's always accepted.
Who the Night Mother decides to answer is up to her and her alone. But when she speaks, we answer, quickly and without question.

They must build an effigy of blood, flesh, and bone—the symbol of their desire—and drive a blade anointed with nightshade into their offering as they recite the incantation.\n\nThrough this ritual, they may be heard by the Night Mother.

What you saw was the Wrath of Sithis. The messenger sent to all who betray the Brotherhood. It has claimed the traitor's soul for the Void, where she will answer for all she has done.\n\nNever forget what awaits those who defy us.
If their devotion to Sithis outstrips their indiscretion, they may overcome the wraith and be welcomed back into the fold.\n\nI have never observed such an event, but anything is possible.

You are my agent now, and by extension an agent of the Black Hand. You're not beholden to any Sanctuary. When I call upon you, the needs of the Dark Brotherhood take precedence.\n\nFor now, rebuilding this Sanctuary's strength remains our priority.

She's one of the ranking priests at the Cathedral of Kvatch, right below Primate Artorius in the hierarchy. She won't be easy to find, however.\n\nKilling her subordinates may draw her out. Otherwise, rely on Tanek to locate the hole she's hiding in.

It could be anything. Certainly Primate Artorius and his priests have little love for the Brotherhood. I wonder, does the Cathedral plan to outlaw the Black Sacrament? Would they dare such an action?\n\nRegardless, these sermons are bad for business.
It's my wife, Alexia. We entered the hedge maze on a lark, and now she's lost in there! It's been hours.

Well, the scribbles at the bottom of each note appear to be instructions. Raz thinks that if we piece them all together, it will create a map of sorts.\n\nWell, not a literal map. Though that would be handy.

Well, the clues certainly allow us to exclude many parts of the city. And there aren't many roads besides the main one.\n\nRaz will continue to ponder these clues. Something is bound to occur to Raz eventually.
Well, yes, I suppose I could. But what if some kind soul guides her out and I'm not here to greet them? No, I should stay put. She's bound to turn up eventually, right?
I'm certain. Her sense of direction is atrocious. Couldn't find dirt if she fell off a horse. It's endearing … most of the time. But Akatosh only knows what's happened to her now.
It's my husband, Plautus. He dragged me into that hedge maze then wandered off like an idiot. Now he's lost in there.

What? You think I'm going back in there? No, no. I'm not his nursemaid. He'll have to find his own way out. It's good for him … I guess. Builds character and all that. He'll figure it out. Eventually.

Oh, definitely. Plautus can barely find his way out of a baggy shirt. I thought it was his eyesight at first, but now I think it's some kind of mental block. I'll have to buy him a spotting hound or something ….

Raz knows where we need to go! It was right in front of us this entire time.\n\nDo you want to know where the clues point to? Raz does not wish to spoil your fun if you'd rather solve the puzzle yourself.

There is a small house to the south. Near the Order of the Hour's Tower of Judgment. It's one of the only private buildings that's not along the main road.\n\nClearly the recipient of these notes must be hiding there. Raz can feel it in his whiskers!

That is fair! Raz feels the same way. Raz hates it when the little Elf tries to help with the Queen's daily riddle.\n\nWell, if you decide you need assistance, just ask. Otherwise, Raz will follow along and watch how your mind works.

Good. I didn't want to fight you about this.\n\nBy the way, you might want to deal with those siege weapons and other preparations the Order is making. Anything you can do to disrupt their operations will benefit the Brotherhood in the end.

I don't expect you to understand and I don't want your help.\n\nThose siege weapons and other preparations the Order is making, by the way. You should do whatever you can to destroy them and disrupt their operations.

No. Not even a drop of blood to remember him by.\n\nBut my husband was just one of a series of murders linked to this Sweetroll Killer. It's been going on for months and months, and now Reman suddenly cares? I wonder why he's had a change of heart?
Now I'll never know the secret! Ah well, nothing a quick roll in the bog muck can't fix. No harm done.\n\nExcept to the tattered remains of all those Argonians.
<Remains silent.>

He's charming, ruthless, meticulous—the perfect assassin.\n\nHonestly, it's been a while since we last spoke. He was my chief instructor in the Shadowscales, but once I joined the Dark Brotherhood, we fell out of touch. It happens.
We're Sithis's judgment. Any Argonian born under the Shadow is pledged to the order and trained in the arts of secrecy and murder.

From birth or close to it. There's religious education, trials, and an uncomfortable amount of sap-licking. Eventually, mercifully, some of us are handed over to the Dark Brotherhood to serve Sithis abroad.

Hrm. Mongrels and deserters from the Dark Brotherhood, the Morag Tong, even the Shadowscales.\n\nIt was just an embarrassment at first, but now they're targeting former associates, killing reliable informants … spoiling for a fight it seems.
Two. An ex-Morag Tong operative named Dranos Velador, and a mysterious matron named Velidreth. They call her the Lady of Lace. As far as I know, no one outside the Silken Ring has ever seen her.

It wouldn't surprise me. The Ring's established a few smaller enclaves, but nothing like this.\n\nIf Velidreth is here, we'll find her. And if we find her, we'll nail her head to the door of this place. Assassination's all about showmanship, you know?

<<1>>. A Dark Elf Scale-Catcher. He made his fortune capturing escaped slaves, you see? So, a few dozen Argonian captives pooled their assets and performed the Sacrament as revenge.\n\nKill this slaver.
A Redguard named <<1>>. Some kind of business dispute I'm told. She refused to sell her mill to a competitor, so he has turned to … less conventional means of negotiation.\n\nSlay this Redguard.
He's an Argonian named <<1>>. A very successful gambler, I'm told. Our client insisted that <<1>> is a shameless cheater—as if such things matter to us.\n\nKill this lizard.

A bard named <<1>>. He is a talentless fool who loiters outside the Cathedral of Akatosh both day and night. One of the Chanters grew weary of his off-key singing and performed the Black Sacrament.\n\nKill this would-be musician.

An Orc named <<1>>. She's a low-level dealer for a skooma cartel. Or she was. Somehow she managed to make off with a king's ransom after a … failed transaction. Her employers want her dead.\n\nKill her.
An Argonian called <<1>>. He's organizing a search party to look for a Nord maiden who disappeared a few days ago. Alas for poor <<1>>, that maiden does not want to be found.\n\nKill this lizard.

Oh, I'm not all that worried. Members of the Dark Brotherhood are strict adherents to the letter of the law. As far as I'm concerned, the spirit of the law is just a convenient fiction for milksops and sissies.
Yes, the scent of death preceded you. These will do nicely … so very nicely ….

Banker? I am no mere banker. I was Quaestor to the Imperial Legion. Master of the Imperial treasury. Guardian of the Empire's boundless wealth. Until the hordes of Molag Bal descended on the Imperial city, I had never failed in my duty.
A witchmother's brew, to heighten the reek of death! All for a handful of reagents.\n\nA pumpkin to serve as a base. Guts torn from squealing critters to add body.

I could, but I think it'd be much more fun to have you tease the details out of me.\n\nAnd if there's one thing Dibella teaches us, it's to how to keep our entanglements going for as long as possible.

The last true emperor is dead. If I am to swear my allegiance to a new master every day, it will be one of my choosing.\n\nFor as long as you require my services I shall protect your estate with body, blood, and soul.

Oh, no, that kind of life would be too … regimented? Even if I wasn't trapped tending a chapel, it's still all rules and responsibility. \n\nI want to wander the world and share in the experiences of its people. The export business is a better fit.

Adventurers are overflowing in two things: interesting experiences and excess treasure. I get to follow along for a fraction of the risk and make a decent living saving you all the trouble of transporting goods.\n\nAlso, you tend to be very fit.
I make it my business to stay informed. The circles we travel in are very small. Assassins who don't keep tabs on friends and rivals tend not to last very long.

I didn't.\n\nLife in the swamp is … I'm looking for kinder word than "primitive." Tsatva was the only Saxhleel worth speaking to. He's not a slave to the old ways. He's headstrong. Independent. You don't see much of that in Black Marsh.
Of course. I'm sorry. You've come to help us, and I'm being rude.
Then I'll start from the beginning. A short while ago, the three Guardian star signs—the Warrior, the Mage, and the Thief—vanished from the night sky.

The Star-Gazers consists of scholars who are no match for the current threat. We need champions to face the Warrior, the Mage, and the Serpent. And, if possible, to find the Thief.\n\nJoin us. Be our strong arm, our sharp sword against the Celestials.

I wish I knew. I've studied the stars my whole life. I've heard them speak—but now they're silent. It's eerie. \n\nAll I know is when the Guardians disappeared, three powerful beings started attacking Craglorn. They call themselves the Celestials.
Thank you. We have a lot of work to do. But first, you must become an official member of our order.\n\nEnter the circle of stars and accept our blessing.
Of course. But don't take too long. The Guardian stars have protected Tamriel for centuries. How long can we last without their favor?

Everyone is, these days. Funny how a few months ago, they were just a bunch of star-obsessed loonies. Now, they're the only folks with any idea what's going on.\n\nTheir observatory is up on top of that big hill there. Can't miss it.

I don't know. It's not a name I'd ever heard before.\n\nTwo of the Celestials identify themselves as the Warrior and the Mage. The third, strangely, calls himself the Serpent—after the thirteenth constellation. The Thief is nowhere to be found.

Nobody. Just an old scholar with no particular skill except tracking the stars.\n\nI always believed that the stars bless heroes with the gifts to face the troubles of their time. But now, the stars themselves are troubled. I'm afraid this is the end.

Of course. There are thirteen star signs. The Warrior, the Mage, and the Thief are called the guardians because they each govern three charges.\n\nThey watch over Tamriel. Distant, impersonal, but, I like to think, benevolent.

She's very wise and very knowledgeable about the stars. She came to us only a short while ago, after living in seclusion and studying the old Yokudan astrological traditions.\n\nThe extent of her knowledge is impressive, and she's been very helpful.

Many people come to Craglorn to live and study in peace. We are fortunate that Hara saw the signs when she did.\n\nWithout her help, Belkarth would have been overrun along with the rest of Craglorn when the troubles started.

The Serpent. Originally, there were only twelve signs, but the Serpent usurped his place in the night sky.\n\nHe does not appear at a fixed time, but darts chaotically through the seasons, attacking the guardians' charges.
Prepare yourself!

It'd be an amusing story if the situation weren't so dire. An unseen force pulled me from my time into yours and dropped me in the midst of Dragonstar's grand melee—stark naked! \n\nI won, naturally. Then the soldiers arrested me, just as naturally.

Thank you. You are a noble soul. Perhaps you'll actually believe my extraordinary tale when there is time to tell it.\n\nBut first, meet me at the cave called Buried Sands. If my suspicions are correct, we'll find something we need there.

Nedic writings suggest that the Nedes may have been slaves at sites like Mtharnaz, and they may have adopted some Dwarven practices.\n\nBut the Dwarves are such a mystery. It's impossible to guess what those practices might have been.

We don't know a lot about them. They were an early race who settled in Craglorn.\n\nWhat history we do know tells a tale of enslavement and invasion—the Dwemer, the Ayleids, and finally the Yokudans, all had their way with the Nedes.

The Nedes apparently followed a variety of customs and religious practices, adapting to whatever invaders were currently overwhelming them.\n\nOne of these customs was star-worship. The Skystone amulet was a symbol of the priestly office.

Nedic writings talk about the Apex Stones in a variety of ways, but they all agree that there is a connection between the stars and these stones.\n\nIf we can understand that connection, perhaps we can find out how to stop the Celestials.
We're all from the past. I'm just from … farther past.\n\nI can explain better what's going on if you free me and help me stop Tarish-Zi and the Anka-Ra. And maybe find me some clothes, as well.

Each Celestial possesses an unusual gift. The Warrior's gift is to call heroes across time. \n\nIt seems the Serpent perverted the Warrior's gift, using it to awaken the villainous Tarish-Zi and his cursed army, the Anka-Ra.

My guess is that as one of Tarish-Zi's royal guard, he was summoned at the same time as the others—yet he was unaffected by the Serpent's manipulations. Perhaps because he was never truly loyal to Tarish-Zi.

Tradition holds that the Warrior is one of the Guardians who defends the other stars against the Serpent.\n\nBut the Warrior Celestial who has recently appeared is no friend. He commands a merciless army of ancient Yokudan warriors called the Anka-Ra.

Certain Nedic writings suggest this isn't the first time the Celestials have appeared in Craglorn. \n\nThey're legends mostly, but there's truth in them. They describe Apex Stones that connect the Celestials to Tamriel in some fashion.

Go to the ruin of Shada's Tear, the site of an ancient Nedic temple. I'm confident we can find the amulet we need there.\n\nBut be wary. Wards protect the place, and I've heard that vicious Goblins roam the upper levels.

I believe I know the location of the Warrior's Apex Stone. It's written, "In Kardala, the Warrior waits."\n\nBut the way is sealed. We need a Nedic high priest's amulet to enter. Unfortunately, the Nedes disappeared centuries ago.

All I know is they are ancient and dangerous.\n\nI've heard intriguing rumors from the Daggerfall Covenant outpost to the west of a champion who appeared about the same time as the Anka-Ra. That may be a good place to start looking for answers.

One of our number, Erold, has been examining old Nedic writings on the subject. He hopes to find insight into the Celestials' sudden appearance.\n\nErold is smart, but he's not exactly battle-hardened. I'd be grateful if you'd help him.

Yes, Erold told me. He said that the Warrior's Stone was corrupted by the servants of the Serpent—the Scaled Court.\n\nIt's distressing to think that there are mortals aiding the Celestials, but not surprising. Thank you.

Yes, Titus arrived a short while ago. Interesting man. As soon as he entered, he pledged himself to resisting the evils of the Serpent and his cursed armies.\n\nHe'll be a good ally, I think. He's upstairs, if you want to talk to him.

Yes, along with the false emperor, Tarish-Zi. If it's true that the Warrior Celestial has the ability to call heroes across time, we can only wonder what the other Celestials are capable of. Be careful as you confront them.

Tradition holds that the Mage, the Warrior, and the Thief are the Guardian star signs. But the magical events in the foothills of Craglorn—including an ever-growing army of atronachs—suggest that the Mage has fallen under the Serpent's control.

The atronachs were originally summoned by a circle of conjurers from the city of Elinhir to defend Craglorn against the Dark Anchors. \n\nBut it's clear they're answering to another master now. And, if anything, their numbers are growing.

Strange things, difficult to describe. A large spellscar in the middle of the desert. And the appearance of two High Elves in Belkarth, each claiming to be the Mage herself.\n\nIt's as if the Mage tried to fight back against the Serpent and lost.

I wouldn't rule it out, but I haven't had time to look into their claims. You're free to investigate, but be wary of a trap. The Serpent could simply be baiting us.\n\nLast I heard, the women were still at the Crossroads Tavern here in Belkarth.
I'm at a loss. The conjurers who summoned the atronachs have disappeared.\n\nBut since the atronachs were summoned to defeat the Dark Anchors, perhaps the dolmens hold a clue.

This road is the only thoroughfare that connects Bangkorai and Cyrodiil. And these so-called "Celestials" are making a mess of it.\n\nWe've appealed to the Daggerfall Covenant for help, but they're … distracted.
That damned Alliance War. Troops need to get to Cyrodiil, and the Covenant's got its hands full protecting its own supply lines. Or so they say.

The worst is near Elinhir. Damned mages fighting each other, spilling out onto the road ….\n\nBut there's also some kind of shimmering giant rock-thing that blasted a huge crater in the middle of Craglorn. It's damn creepy, whatever it is.

If this was Glenumbra or Stormhaven we were talking about and not backwater Craglorn, the Covenant would have no trouble finding the resources to help us—Alliance War or not. \n\nBut who am I to complain?

Word is, the mages that run the place are at each others' throats. \n\nYou ask me, it was inevitable. Inviting renegade mages to live there was just asking for trouble. Luckily, most of the citizens got out before things got really bad.

Some say it's the gods displeasure, fired from Aetherius to punish us. Others say it's Daedric. Still others think it's the Celestial Mage's staff, flung from the heavens. \n\nWhatever it is, it's bad news. I'd stay clear of it.
She's a strange one. Came out of the desert one day, spouting terrible prophecy about stars falling from the sky and a serpent let loose on an unsuspecting world.
We live in perilous times. We're always one interesting coincidence away from destruction. Me? I'm too old to ask such questions.

No one foresaw this—sand warriors attacking, atronachs in rebellion against their masters, strange and formless beasts ….\n\nBut Hara saw a glimmer of what was to come. Because of her, we were able to prepare and protect Belkarth.

I'd regale you with tales of our glory days, but there are none. There have been many of us over the years—fractious, decadent and insular, until they faded from existence.\n\nOur order would have followed the same course, were it not for Hara.

I could tell you a thousand things about the Celestials, but not a single one of them would be true.\n\nAre they stars fallen from the sky? Are they guardians created by some lost civilization? Are they a Daedric trick, played on us by Sheogorath?
It's my job to protect what little we know from disintegration and loss. It's for others to plumb fathomless mysteries and lose their minds seeking answers.
I'm just the hired muscle, but I'll tell you what I can.

Ask what you will. I'm still looking for answers myself. I had only passed the first trial when these troubles struck the school.\n\nI suppose that's the reason I was able to escape when the others were lost.

The first trial is called the Trial of Fire. \n\nThe initiate must find the tombs of the flame-bearers and slay the gargoyles that guard them. Then the flame-bearers can light the braziers along the path to Rahni'Za.

So it's true? The Serpent does walk the face of Nirn? \n\nI can't begin to fathom the motivations of such a creature. But there's a legend that Rahni'Za's founder, his name long lost to history, dedicated it to the Warrior constellation.

I know only the strange rumors I heard from the few initiates who had not yet turned by the time I entered. The betrayer was a member of the Scaled Court, a servant of the Celestial Serpent who they say has appeared in Craglorn.

The books are conferred on completion of the first trial. The school had gone to chaos and ruin before I received mine.\n\nDivines, if only I could have done something. I keep thinking that I could have saved them had I been stronger.

The second trial is the arena, where the initiate Sword-Disciple must survive the melee.\n\nI was about to start this trial when the troubles struck. I don't know much about the other trials, but the initiates carried books that tell of them.

When the betrayer struck, the Sword-Disciples held fast to their honor and took up their blades against him. \n\nFor their efforts, they were turned into a mindless army. But I took the coward's way. I fell on my own blade rather than join Abelazar.

A test of stamina and pacing. The easiest of the three—if you have good allies by your side.\n\nThe arena master is a spirit who has dwelt in this place since its founding. He wasn't affected by all of this. He'll tell you all you need to know.

I never completed the Trial of Air. The other initiates told me of a hidden path across the tops of the school's buildings. It can only be seen when special sands are thrown upon it.\n\nWhere the path leads, I can't say.

On entering Rahni'Za, we were each given a book describing the trials. There's a place in the library for each of the books.\n\nAs I understand it, only those who managed to acquire a complete set could complete the Trial of Martial Knowledge.

There are five trials. You've completed the first, by entering this place. Then there's the Trial of the Arena, the Trial of the Air, and the Trial of Martial Knowledge.\n\nThen there is the final trial, the Trial of the True Path.
I was the master of this school. Its last, as it came to pass.\n\nMy blindness doomed us all. No one could have been as good as Abelazar appeared to be. I should have seen through his trickery.

Yes. He reached the end of the final trial faster than any student I'd seen before and when I conferred the name of Sword-Disciple on him, he cut me down.\n\nI can still hear his laughter. It will burn in my ears for all eternity.

It's called the Trial of the True Path. Ironic, then, that Abelazar the betrayer waits on the other side.\n\nReady yourself. If you have not completed the other trials, you will not be able to complete the Trial of the True Path.
The mists that cover the path are deadly. The way through it only opens for those who have completed the trials.

Perhaps. Like the Abbey of Blades, Rahni'Za is a place of secret arts, admitting only those brave enough and strong enough to gain entry. There are more myths than facts around it.\n\nPerhaps the Serpent simply wanted to eliminate potential opposition.
Peace, yes. I don't know if I'll ever be at peace with what happened here. Like everyone, I was so enamored of Abelazar, I never imagined what was to come.

That is for you to decide. The school has many hidden trials beyond those you've completed, and those too can be undertaken if you wish.\n\nAs for the other Sword-Disciples, they will not reach their final rest until the Serpent himself is defeated.

He came among us as an initiate, seeking to master the trials and win the right to be called Sword-Disciple.\n\nHe was the best I'd ever seen. The way he moved with a blade, it was mesmerizing. But it was all a lie.

His allegiance was to the Celestial Serpent, not to us. His mastery was deceptive magic, not skill. \n\nWhen he reached the end of the final trial, he murdered our master and used foul magic to turn the Sword-Disciples into thralls.

These trials were placed here centuries before us. The secrets of their workings are hidden even to the masters of the school. \n\nIt was the founder's will that the teachings of the school should last, even when there was no master left to oversee it.

After Abelazar murdered me, he cast a ritual on the Sword-Disciples, turning them into thralls, neither living nor dead.\n\nI fear there is no hope of saving them, but you can give them rest by defeating Abelazar and destroying the one who sent him.

The Celestial Serpent. Abelazar was a member of the Scaled Court, worshipers of the Serpent. \n\nThey want only chaos for Tamriel. They saw the Sword-Disciples as a threat to their plans, which is why they sent Abelazar into our midst to destroy us.
The thralls are neither living nor dead. They answer only to the Serpent's will.\n\nIt's too late to save them, but you may give them rest by killing Abelazar and destroying his master, the Serpent.

Across Tamriel there is a handful of schools devoted to the secret arts of the blade. \n\nOf those, the greatest are Rahni'Za and the Abbey of Blades. But there are others, secretive and hidden, that carry the tradition.

Their locations are secret, even to me. \n\nEach school has its own secret techniques to teach—the most dedicated blademaster might spend a lifetime searching for each school. I have never heard of anyone mastering them all.

His name has been lost to history. By legend, he is Rahni'Za, the spirit of the blade, but no one knows who the man—or woman—was.\n\nYet his legacy lives on in the trials, which function like clockwork, even now.

I heard the researchers call it a lost Nedic city. I guess the Nedes were the people who lived in Craglorn before the Yokudans showed up.\n\nThe researchers have started calling the ruin Shada's Tear.
I know everything. You have come to my shrine because the stars have fallen to Tamriel. You want to know how to defeat them.

I can. But knowledge must never be given freely. A price must be paid.\n\nPart of the cost was bringing my servant Ibrula back to me. But you will pay much more if you want to learn all that I know about the Celestials.

I am the Celestial Thief. I appeared with the other Guardians when the Serpent broke free and manifested in Tamriel.\n\nOne by one, the Serpent trapped the others. First the Warrior, then the Mage. He wants to do the same to me.
Yes. They attack Craglorn against their will.\n\nListen. The Serpent's nature is chaos. He wants to undermine the very order of reality. He will not stop with Craglorn.

Hara and the Star-Gazers will help you. Use their knowledge. Look for the presence of the Scaled Court—where they are, the Serpent is surely at work. \n\nBut you must not tell anyone you saw me. The Serpent's followers are everywhere.
My power alone is not enough. You must free the other Guardians. I will help you as much as I dare, but the Serpent is looking for me. If he ensnares me as he has the others, all is lost.
In a way. Just as you might look at a picture of the star signs and say "That's the Thief" or "That's the Warrior." Just so, I'm the Thief, or one way of seeing the Thief.

Of the twelve rightful star signs, it's the Guardians' duty to protect the lesser signs, our charges, against the destructive ways of the Serpent.\n\nWith the Warrior and Mage under the Serpent's control, their charges are vulnerable. So is Tamriel.
It would be surprising if I didn't. \n\nThe Star-Gazers are only dimly aware of it, but they carry an ancient legacy as students of the star signs. Their devotion has not gone unnoticed.
I can't promise that my answers will satisfy. Craglorn has always been a harsh place and desolate. Much of Craglorn's history has long since passed into myth.

Then listen closely, as I will not repeat myself. The Celestial Warrior's army of Anka-Ra was created centuries ago by the Yokudan general, Tarish-Zi. \n\nHe came to me to learn how to bind his army to him—even in death. I granted his wish.

His offering pleased me. He built the temple above this shrine and promised that his army would defend it.\n\nThe Anka-Ra have risen, which means Tarish-Zi has risen as well. They are bound to him. To defeat them, you must defeat him.
I was a priestess of Shada.\n\nWe who were here when the Yokudans came were caught in Shada's curse. We remain, long after death ought to have claimed us, living in the moment before our destruction.

Our people … they were not always kind. But this city was filled with those who cared for others.\n\nThrough Shada's blessing, men and women on the brink of death were revived in the waters of our city. Until the Yokudans came.

Shada's curse is this: that the once life-giving water bring only death to those who drink it, and that the spirits of the past shall haunt the living for eternity.\n\nThis was because the Yokudans intended to turn the city into a fortification.

They are the keys. They open the way to our city's greatest treasure, to Shada herself.\n\nShada, who blessed us with our famous healing gifts, and who in the end cursed us all in order to save us all.

They came to this land to conquer it, to bring it into submission to their dread leader, Tarish-Zi.\n\nWith the healing power of the city, the Yokudan armies would have been unstoppable. That is why Shada cursed the city—to save it.

She was our chief healer, but she was also so much more. Myself, I never saw her face. Few ever did. But her blessing enabled us to care for the sick.\n\nIt was also what drew the Yokudans to our city.

I am Shada. I purified these waters so that the people of this city could drink and be healed. I am the only relic that exists.\n\nThe gift you seek is lost now. I cursed these waters and this place to keep the Yokudans from abusing their power.

Yes, and for that, I am grateful.

But enemies from the past rise again. I can sense their power all throughout the deathlands, as numerous as the sands.

I will not—I cannot lift this curse.

Tarish-Zi rises again, and with him, his Yokudan army, the Anka-Ra. Puppets of a still more powerful being, a Serpent of infinite cruelty.\n\nBut I sense that you oppose them as we once did. Perhaps there is something I can help with.

A single draught of the very waters you seek. Purified by my own hand.

For what you fight for, you have earned this gift. Use it wisely and do not make me regret my decision. 

Now go. There is nothing more for you here.

The Yokudans would have used the power of this place to further their bloody conquest and become unstoppable.\n\nShada's curse ensured that such a terrible future would never come to pass, but at the cost of all our lives.
Do not pity me. If I had not failed to hide the goblet in time, perhaps all of this could have been averted. This solitary watch is both my duty and my penance.

The flame-bearers are the spirits of three previous masters of the school. So devoted were they to training future Sword-Disciples, they bound their spirits here. Even in death, they teach new initiates the ways of the blade.
The Seeker's Archive is no ordinary library. It's actually a shrine to Hermaeus Mora, the Daedric Lord of Knowledge.
Yes. It was built centuries ago—long before the Yokudans came to Hammerfell.\n\nI've been visiting the shrine for several years now, offering relics to Hermaeus Mora in exchange for secret knowledge.

I'm sorry, but I wasn't sure you would help me if you knew. Not everyone has an open mind where Daedric Princes are concerned.\n\nBut I do seek knowledge to defeat the Celestials. That much is true. I believe Hermaeus Mora can provide that knowledge.
All I have told you is all you have earned.\n\nIf you wish to know more, you must become my eyes and ears in Craglorn. You must bring me fresh knowledge to feast upon.
I hunger for lost bits of lore. I thirst for new knowledge to add to my coffers. Bring your offerings to me. If I find them acceptable, I will return their worth in the knowledge you seek.

This temple is a good example. The Anka-Ra crawled out of the ground all around it, and started guarding it as if—well, as if they were just picking up where they left off when they died.\n\nI believe they are deeply connected to Craglorn, somehow.

That is one of the questions I hoped to answer within. They appear to be neither living nor dead, but not exactly undead either. Cursed. \n\nIt's said that the Celestial Warrior controls them, but I sense that's only part of the story.
Call it chance, or fate. I was once a Star-Gazer, searching the stars for signs and prophecies.\n\nLittle did I realize that the knowledge I sought was not in the sky above, but in the ground below.

The Seeker's Archive is another of Craglorn's many mysteries. An astonishing library, left mostly untouched for centuries, built by unknown hands.\n\nThe temple atop the library is Yokudan in origin, but some of the books pre-date even the Yokudans!

The followers of Hermaeus Mora who worshiped here were called Seekers.\n\nThe Seekers brought gifts to the shrine, and the Daedric Prince rewarded them with secret knowledge. I carry a relic from the Dragontail mountains for just such a purpose.

I do what I must. Hermaeus Mora is not like other Daedra. He may seem cruel at times, but he's not irrational.\n\nHe's only interested in knowledge. If bringing him gifts will save Craglorn from the Celestials, then so be it.

We started our research here. Figured it was less dangerous than the crypts. Everything seemed fine at first. People kept drinking the water though. Thought nothing of it.\n\nIt started with the strange whispering. Then the hostility.

My partner, Nahlia, refused to drink the waters as well.\n\nA couple of the researchers dragged her off through those doors before they slammed shut. I couldn't find a way to open them, but I found this scroll on the desk. It might be the key we need.

Just look at it - the stuff even looks like it's cursed.\n\nA couple of us held out from drinking it. Most of us aren't around anymore either. Those who did drink it started muttering things about "Shada's Will" and "Shada commands we give our life".

There might be. The people who led us down here drug poor Nahlia through the doors at the far end of the room. Watched them slam shut behind them.\n\nI have no idea how to open the doors, but the scroll I found above me might give us a clue of sorts.
If the others really were turned into thralls of the Nereids, then Nahlia is in serious danger.\n\nOur leaders drank the water first: Klause, Squan, and Zifri. We have to find them and save Nahlia.

Klause got his hands on some ancient horn of sorts when we first started our work. He never knew what it did until he started drinking the waters. Gave him knowledge, he said.\n\nI watched him control the dead with it. I fear for the ways he'll use it.

Squan was a genius. The man always knew how to conjure up just the right spell. Master of conjuration and all things, I watched him summon up atronachs to do with as he pleases.\n\nOut of all of us, I thought he'd be the last to succumb to the curse.

Zifri was our smith. She fixed and repaired our tools and crafted us weapons. She was looking into an old smithy in this very wing when she succumbed to the curse.\n\nYou best be on your guard around her.

It's … tainted, cursed—call it what you like.\n\nSome of the researchers drank it when we first got here. They started foaming at the mouth and screaming about someone called "Shada." It made them freakishly strong, too.

Half our camp's missing inside one of the wings and there's undead crawling out of every crack in the place.\n\nWe need supplies and mercs. But I guess this Celestial business has everyone distracted topside.

You heard right. The first researchers to drink the water said it tasted like nothing they ever drank. Made them feel strong, alive.\n\nAnd then they started changing. They attacked us, like we were intruders and they were defending the city.
It fits their reputation. Nereids are known for practicing a dark and twisted sorcery to control people's minds.\n\nDrinking the water appears to turn you into a thrall of a Nereid called Shada.

Well, that's where things get truly strange. Seems that this place was built by Nedes—the ancient people who settled Craglorn before the Yokudans. \n\nWe don't know a lot about the Nedes, but it seems like these particular ones worshiped Nereids.

See that pool? The water flows into it from the temple wings on either side and blocks the way to the main chamber. \n\nMy guess is if you follow the water into those wings, you'll find the source of the corruption. A Nereid, if I'm right.
The Nereids call her Shada.\n\nWhen they drank the water, Klause and the others became her thralls. They thought they could serve her by sacrificing me.

There's a Nereid in a nearby chamber. The others called her a Daughter of Shada.\n\nShe is the one corrupting the waters in this wing. I don't know about the rest of the temple, though. Perhaps there are other Daughters of Shada.

She's the Nereid queen, or leader, or whatever it is Nereids have.\n\nIt sounded like she is the one responsible for the cursed water. That's why all the undead in here worship her. They drank the water and became her thralls.

You're here to help? That means Fights-With-Tail must have escaped. You have no idea how relieved I am to hear that.\n\nListen. The city won't be safe until the Blackcaster mages and their leader, Arch-Mage Yamanu-ko, are defeated.

Good. Then, this barrier is Yamanu-ko's last defense. It should be weak enough for me to break now.\n\nI'm afraid it will still take a great deal of my strength, however, so you will have to face Yamanu-ko alone.

Be careful with the arch-mage. Yamanu-ko was powerful even before she learned the Serpent's wicked trick.\n\nShe's only grown more powerful since, stealing magicka from her fellow mages and immersing herself in unspeakable rituals.

The city lies in ruins and the Blackcaster mages run rampant over the corpses of the dead. Every moment that Yamanu-ko continues to draw breath is a moment wasted.\n\nBut I understand. This situation is far from normal.

Yamanu-ko was my master. I learned everything I know about magic from her.\n\nIncluding the dangers of temptation and too much power. I should have stopped her when I saw what was happening. But I was afraid.

I was Yamanu-ko's third apprentice. I realized—too late—that the deal we made would be our undoing. \n\nThe spell we were taught was pure savagery. And the cost was too high. I tried to get as many people out of the city as I could ….

When the mage Felix Blackcaster first came to Elinhir, it was a struggling settlement. \n\nHe promised protection and prosperity in exchange for establishing a magic school. It was an arrangement that served the city well for hundreds of years.

That's a long story. The short of it is, we made a deal. \n\nA man approached us promising us knowledge of ancient Nedic magics. Our towers are Nedic in origin, but we knew little about them. So we accepted.
It was ordinary by magical standards. In spite of what the Mages Guild might say, we were not renegades.\n\nI still don't fully understand what drove Yamanu-ko to this … madness.
If it will help you free Elinhir from the grip of the mad mages, I am happy to answer.

The Blackcaster mages protected Elinhir against the dangers of Craglorn.\n\nWith the Iron Orcs in the hills and bandits everywhere, the people of Elinhir looked to the mages to keep them safe. In exchange, we supported them and their studies.

Craglorn is the sort of place you go to when you don't want to be anywhere else.\n\nThe people who come here want independence more than anything. The arrangement we had with the mages was mutually beneficial.

Elinhir was the oldest city in Craglorn, and the only home I've ever known.\n\nIt wasn't easy, settling out here, especially before the trade road. That's why the founders of the city welcomed the Blackcaster mages.
Minerva was one of Arch-Mage Yamanu-ko's apprentices, but when the others went bad, she didn't. \n\nI can't imagine how many people would have died if Minerva hadn't intervened.

The Blackcaster mages operated independently of the Mages Guild.\n\nCraglorn attracts a certain type of person, you see. The kind that want to get away from the rest of the world. Still, the Blackcasters never caused any trouble, until now.

We can't reach the main chamber while the pool is corrupted. We need to find the Nereids corrupting the water in the other wings first.\n\nAs for what's in the main chamber, I'm guessing it's the leader of the Nereids—Shada, as her thralls call her.
The final chamber. She's been imprisoned for the sacrifice. No time. You must find a way to open her prison, or Shada will claim her.
No time. Fading fast.\n\nYou need two people to unlock Nahlia's prison. They must open the lock at the same time. Otherwise, the Nereids will take her.
I can't. There's no time. Look to the pillars. You have to look to the pillars for the key.
They are the masters of this place. They are the ones who've cursed the water.\n\nAny who drink it become thralls to Shada, their master. You must stop them. Free Nahlia.
She is master of this place. Master of the Nereids. It's her curse that corrupts the water.\n\nWe drank the water and became more powerful than ever. We also became her slaves. Stop her. Free Nahlia.
No time. My spirit fades. Look for the faces on the stone pillars. When you reach Nahlia's prison, you will see. You will understand.

The devices are guarded by Yamanu-ko's apprentices, Leta and Avys, in their towers.\n\nOnce you've destroyed the devices and weakened the ward, I'll meet you at the base of Yamanu-ko's tower to finish breaking the spell.

Yamanu-ko is their leader. Defeating her should bring the others to their senses.\n\nBut her tower is warded, protected by strange Nedic devices in each of her apprentices' towers. You need to destroy these devices to reach Yamanu-ko.
The atronachs? I don't care to think about those creatures. \n\nOne moment we were summoning them and destroying the Dark Anchors, and the next they turned on us like ungrateful dogs!
I don't know. But I think I know how to find out. We need to talk to the atronachs directly and ask them what happened.

Zal'ik was a smart man, and he went to great lengths to prevent the city from falling to the Yokudans. He would not have let his work be undone so easily.\n\nStill, it should now be possible to move ahead, so long as you avoid the cloud of poison.

When Shada cursed me, she bound me to Zal'ik's soul. She trusted that the barrier would hold against any invaders, keeping Zal'ik well-defended.\n\nIf Zal'ik falls, so too does any spell that binds me. It is as simple as that.
Wait for the barrier to move and follow closely behind. When an opening appears, do not hesitate.\n\nZal'ik's resting chambers are right around this hall. Not far to go, now.
Even so, I have no right to gloat. If Zal'ik had taken my counsel, our people would have been slaughtered by the Yokudans.

Indeed, I did. I have recorded all of my centuries of learning here in this book. I believe there may even be a way to cure someone who is still in the early stages of the madness.\n\nLet it help you and your people, if it can. It is too late for mine.

I have thought long on whether and how the effects of the curse can be reversed.\n\nFor those whose flesh has rotted, there is no cure. But for those still in the early stages, I believe I have an answer, but I require something in return.

My own freedom. When I spoke out against this unholy bargain, my soul was bound to that of Zal'ik, the general who gave our people over to the Nereids.\n\nTo free me, you must defeat him. But be careful. He has sealed the way with a cloud of poison.

This place is haunted by visions of the past, my own memories of the events leading up to this curse. \n\nWatch the visions to learn our fate. They will show the way to disperse the cloud of poison and reach Zal'ik.
It's been a long time. I may not remember as well as I should. But I will try to answer.

I don't remember much of the invasion itself. It failed because of Zal'ik's gambit. Our army proved too strong for the Yokudans.\n\nAs to what happened to them, I don't know. I suppose they gave up in search of an easier target.

I always thought Shada's Tear was an ugly name for a city. It was adopted when the people first started worshiping the Nereids.\n\nI'm partial to the city's name of old: the City of Shimmering-Water-in-the-Desert. A mouthful, yes, but so poetic.

Yes. We believed that the stars themselves were little windows that let the light of Aetherius into our world.\n\nBut even in my day, it was a dying faith. Our people seemed destined to be conquered by invaders while the stars watched.

Of an old and fading religion—the cult of the stars. Once, Nedes across these lands worshipped the stars.\n\nBy the time the Yokudans came, we were a fragmented people. Some turned to the Elven gods, others to Daedra. My people turned to the Nereids.

No, they did not. Once, the Nedes of the city worshiped the stars.\n\nBut water was our city's lifeblood, and that is the Nereids' domain. Why plead with distant stars, when you have powerful sorceresses in your very midst?
Our city was once the great jewel of the desert. A city of cool, crisp, refreshing waters in a sea of sand.\n\nIt would have been of great strategic value to the Yokudans, had they taken it.

As I thought. The Nereids are behind the corruption. I've deciphered more writings on the leader of these Nereids—Shada, she's called.\n\nIt says she blessed the water so that the people of the city could fend off invaders.

It says the people of the city worshiped her in a temple that was once dedicated to the stars.\n\nThere's a third wing across the way. I assume that's the temple wing, and I'd guess that Shada's in there.

Feels foolish, asking you to risk your life when all I have to offer is a thank you. But you have to understand how much this means to us. And to Craglorn.\n\nI wish you luck. We'll remain here and wait for your return.

I know it's a lot to ask, but this water can't be allowed to leave here while it remains cursed. It would cause a situation as bad as the Celestial invasion above.\n\nDefeating Shada is the only way to end the curse. You must go and stop her.

I'm not one to speculate on the powers of the Celestials, but it seems he manipulated the Mage somehow.\n\nThat's not in our power to correct at the moment, but we can try to find this new atronach—an air atronach, the monarchs called it.
I would, but I cannot. There is too much to do to prepare for the ritual that will open the staff. This magic is … untested.

Certainly. The Guild is a scholarly organization dedicated to the pursuit of arcane knowledge. We travel the width and breadth of Tamriel seeking out books, tomes, and ancient scrolls.\n\nAlas, we've had to suspend our search here in Craglorn.
Earthquake. Worst one I've ever seen. Damn near shook the teeth right out of my head.

It was terrible! A giant spectral Serpent appeared at the summoning site. We sent the atronachs against it, but they refused to obey us.\n\nThey killed the others. Coward that I am, I fled. But then I was captured by these common rogues.

Another of Tarish-Zi's vainglorious projects. He desperately sought the place and the treasure it was rumored to contain.\n\nIt surprises me that one as young as Hara would know of it. Even in my time, it was barely more than myth.

I'm not sure. Tarish-Zi had the place sealed and buried. The original entrance is unreachable. \n\nKelmen may be of some assistance to us there—if his courage holds. Let's regroup at the lake and see what we can discern.

We did. It didn't contain what Tarish-Zi hoped for. So he ordered it buried out of spite. It should be directly below us, if memory serves.\n\nI noted some Nedic remnants jutting from a nearby lake. I'm certain they're part of Reinhold's Retreat.
Good luck with that. As for me, I think I'll keep my distance. I've had more than enough excitement in recent weeks, thank you very much.

No, binding won't work. The air monarch was created from the power of three monarchs. It's too powerful. It must be destroyed.\n\nThe monarchs said that it could be found at a place called Balamath. I recognize the name. It's an Ayleid ruin.

There's only one explanation I can think of, and it's not exactly reassuring.\n\nIf someone found the entrance before us and activated it, the residual energy would continue to emanate for a while after. If we go inside, we won't be alone.

Right. And we mustn't let her down, no matter how terrifying the task.\n\nIt looks like the energy has its source at these sconces. I see nothing that can be done to activate this one, but it might be worth looking at the others. Fancy a swim?
Be warned, though. The spellfiends are drawn to the elemental shards. \n\nYou will be unable to harvest an elemental infusion from a shard until the spellfiends are defeated.

No, of course not. I've got everything well in hand. I just … oh, who am I kidding? Mistress Nazdura sent me to look for some star maps. Why anyone would keep something like that in an inn, I'll never know.
Thank you. Ugh. Back to it, I guess.\n\nMara, help me.

You've no idea. These books and papers … it's like a giant ate a library, got sick, and then threw it all back up. No rhyme or reason—just piles. \n\nSorry for the metaphor. I'm not usually so … graphic.

The Fighters Guild! You should join up. Our new guildmaster is an Argonian, Sees-All-Colors. She has the whole guild hunting down Daedra and their damned Anchors. Tough work. \n\nNot much action out here in Craglorn though. The mages saw to that.

Quickly. If the staff explodes, it has enough power to turn all of Craglorn into a crater.\n\nCollect all three elemental infusions and bring them to me. Then we can force our way into the staff and stop the explosion!

We are dealing with magic of a whole different order than any of us are used to.\n\nIf this really is the Mage's Staff, then only infusions of energy from its own shards can break its wards. I only hope that we can find a way to contain it once inside.

I know. We aren't very much alike. But as much as it pains me to admit it, under that vapid exterior is a very capable mage.\n\nI was in Craglorn when this thing hit, so the Mages Guild sent me to investigate.
Now is not the time for friendly chatter. You must harvest the elemental infusions from the shards so we can force our way into the staff.
We cannot use the Seeker's Sight to find the other aspects. Not until the gems are recharged with magicka.\n\nUntil that is accomplished, the relic is useless.

Without the Mage to control the ebb and flow, magicka seeps through cracks all across Craglorn. Look for places where the magicka is so dense you can see it and charge the gems there.\n\nMeet us at the Star-Gazer's Observatory when you have finished.
Oh, you don't know? I would have thought that bedraggled Khajiit would have given us away. I am a humble servant of our majestic lord, Hermaeus Mora.

Yes, Hermaeus Mora—the Prince of Fate, the Lord of Secrets. We are his watchful children. \n\nWhen we heard that this ancient city had been discovered, we raced here to plumb its depths. Fortunately, this pack of would-be scholars arrived first.
Wouldn't think of it. I haven't seen their logs and maps, but surely they haven't discovered anything of value. Such a pack of dunces. There's no way they know more than us. No way at all.

Isn't it obvious? \n\nThese fools drank the poisoned water and demonstrated its effects. A fascinating discovery—and all the better since it happened to someone other than us. We owe them a debt of gratitude.
I will do what I can. We can't allow the Serpent to control both the Mage and the Warrior. We need the guardians—all three of them—if we have any hope of defeating the Serpent.
Then place it within the star map and let's see what it can show us.
This Seeker's Sight they gave you. Is it fully restored?

The Lost One is very powerful. We will need both strength and intelligence to succeed.\n\nRight now, the important thing is to find our other aspects and prevent the Lost One from growing any stronger.

Your judgment has served us well so far. We trust you with our lives.\n\nI believe the Scaled One hasn't located either of these aspects as of yet. But do not delay. Find them and tell them of us before the situation changes.

According to the Seeker's Sight, one hides behind what your people refer to as a Dwarven contraption. The other has taken refuge in more deadly environs—among ravenous werewolves. I fear for her safety.

What of it? Aren't you sick of hiding behind these walls, caught like skeevers in a trap?\n\nIron Orcs only respond to strength. We should go out there and hunt them down instead of wasting our time in this gutless town.
So you're the one who helped Kelmen Locke?\n\nHe's … an interesting fellow. Took to drink almost as soon as he arrived. But in his moments of clarity, he can be quite helpful.
So it's true. The Mage has been split into pieces. That could prove difficult down the line.\n\nBut thank you again for your efforts.

We are one and many, both. We share many things, but we cannot talk to each other except when in each other's presence.\n\nI know I have spoken to you, but I do not know the details of those conversations.
Belkarth … there is a powerful presence there, protecting it. It makes sense to hide near there. Away from the Scaled One's grip. At least for now.\n\nI will find my way to them.
I am aware. The Lost One, whom he has corrupted, grows stronger. I hear her calling to me.\n\nThis is why the Serpent divided us. What he could not control whole, he now corrupts piece by piece.
Unfortunate. We will have to find her, then.\n\nI will make my way back to my other selves. Now that I know my location, it will be easy enough to find me.

Belkarth? Hmm. So I have chosen to hide near Belkarth. In a place made for another.\n\nDo you have any news of the Lost One? I know that she is moving against us, but I do not perceive her actions directly.
Yes. Something about Reinhold … Reinhold's Retreat? A ruin. \n\nBut I've never heard that name. What do you think she meant?
Thank you. I know she trusted you. \n\nI hate the thought of her suffering all alone in some dark place. Please, hurry.
She said "he found me." Maybe she's alive and someone took her? Took her to this place … Reinhold's Retreat. \n\nPlease, you have to find it. You have to save her. I … we need her.

We were caught off guard and weakened when the Serpent divided us. He has been gathering our aspects, bringing them under his control one by one.\n\nThis Lost One is more powerful even than the four of us combined.

It will not be easy. The Lost One is powerful. You will need to engage her in battle and distract her. \n\nUnfortunately, she has anticipated this course and fled to a place of strength—our Apex Stone.

We must join with her. We may not be strong enough to defeat the Lost One in a fight, but together we can resist the Serpent's corruption. \n\nThe Lost One will no longer be whole, but divided within herself. This will make her vulnerable.

This is a critical waypoint on the road to Cyrodiil. Our supply train is vulnerable on the High Road through Bangkorai, so we serve as a bulwark against Ebonheart skirmishers. \n\nThe Reach is full of Nord militants. Luckily, they rarely come in force.
Not for me to say. I simply follow orders. I'm sure the captain has his reasons, though. He's … well … he's competent.
Very astute. I asked Captain Gaarlug for reinforcements, but apparently he has a lot of faith in this … small band.
My orders are to protect the supply train. Nothing more. \n\nNow, if star monsters attack our convoys, well … I guess we'll see what happens.

I'm sorry. The Serpent is a deceiver by nature. I couldn't be sure. \n\nWhen the other Guardians fell, I had to react quickly. I suspected that the Serpent was using our Apex stones against us, so I secreted mine to this ruin for safekeeping.

The Serpent is cunning, but he has his blindspots. He does not value the strength or cleverness of mortals.\n\nTaking the form of Hara, a mortal, allowed me to find champions—like you—to join the fight against the Serpent, while eluding his gaze.

We should return to Belkarth. There is still much to do, if we're to free the other Guardians and stop the Serpent. But I'm done hiding. The Star-Gazers deserve to know the truth. \n\nI can transport you back to the city if you wish.
We are the one you call the Celestial Mage—or at least two aspects of a larger whole.\n\nThe Serpent shattered us, weakened us. He plans to control us, piece by piece, aspect by aspect.

The Apex Stones are what allow the Celestials to manifest in this plane. By corrupting our Apex Stone, the Serpent sought to submit our consciousness to his will and corrupt us.\n\nThis is what happened to the Lost One.

If you did, our full power would be released. Mundus could not withstand such force.\n\nOur Apex Stone rests in a hidden place beneath the city of Elinhir. Use the Seeker's Sight to locate it and the Lost One. We will join you when the time is right.
Can't be sure. I just arrived a few days ago. But if there was anyone on the road when it happened, I wouldn't hold out much hope.
Oh, just a few days I reckon.
Of course I'm kidding. Look at this place. If I get these diggers working double shifts we might be able to clear the gap in a century or two. I wouldn't hold out much hope though.
Thanks. We need it.

Keeping up appearances I guess. King Fahara'jad, blessings be upon him, sent me out here as a disaster relief liaison. As long as I'm here pointing at people, the King can say that he's doing his part. \n\nPolitics.
Hurry. If Kelmen is lost to the Serpent, so too are our chances to understand why the atronachs turned.
My fellow guardian, the Mage, lent her power to the conjurers of Craglorn. \n\nIt was not in our interest to see Coldharbour and Nirn joined.

She spoke to them in dreams. Not directly, of course. We prefer to watch from above rather than appear below. Only in times of great crisis do the guardians awaken and manifest.\n\nThe Serpent's attack on Craglorn was just such a crisis.

From what I've heard, he's a gifted conjurer who was greatly favored by the Mage herself before she disappeared.\n\nWhen the atronachs turned, the rest of Kelmen's summoning circle were killed. It's no wonder he's gone into hiding.

The first atronachs we summoned were ancient. They could communicate, to some extent. They didn't speak, but we heard them in our minds. \n\nThey commanded the others and we controlled them. With a gem we saw in a dream—the Gem of Celestial Command.

Well, as it happens, that's the one thing the bandits didn't get their hands on. I was able to keep it … hidden. Don't ask.\n\nTake it. Find the storm, fire, and frost monarchs and use the gem to bind them. You'll probably have to fight them first.
Go to the summoning site and use the gem to call on the monarchs. I'll meet you there. They might be more favorable to me. Or maybe not.\n\nBut now, I've helped you. Will you release me?
The Serpent uses these crystals to siphon the Mage's power for his own use and to gather a stronger hold over her aspects.

When the Serpent shattered the Mage, incredible magicka was released. I am the echo of that shattering. I appear to you now because of the power concentrated in this place, but I will soon cease to be.
For the moment, but I have no doubt the Serpent will continue to try to gain control of the Mage's magicka—just as he continues to try to gain control of her aspects.

You should probably hop a cart back to Wayrest. I can jabber on about Celestials all day long, but I'm a bit out of the loop on the Daedric threat. \n\nMore's the pity. I love how Banekin squeak when you step on them. Ah well.

The Fighters Guild! You should join up. Our new guildmaster is an Argonian, Sees-All-Colors. She has the whole guild hunting down Daedra and their damned Anchors. Tough work. \n\nNot much action out here in Craglorn though. The mages saw to that.

You should probably hop a cart back to Mournhold. I can jabber on about Celestials all day long, but I'm a bit out of the loop on the Daedric threat. \n\nMore's the pity. I love how Banekin squeak when you step on them. Ah well.

You should probably hop a cart back to Elden Root. I can jabber on about Celestials all day long, but I'm a bit out of the loop on the Daedric threat. \n\nMore's the pity. I love how Banekin squeak when you step on them. Ah well.
I'd suggest heading back to Wayrest. The Guild registers there can gauge your aptitude. From the looks of you, I'd say you're a shoo-in. \n\nWalk with Magnus, my friend.

We've had to put all our considerable resources into researching the Celestial threat. The Star-Gazers are capable scholars, certainly. But they lack the requisite literature. This work has kept us very busy.

Yes, I am. A situation I aim to remedy in short order. \n\nIt would help if you would actually purchase something instead of yammering on about the obvious.

The rules pertaining to capture and imprisonment are mercifully short. \n\nNow buy something and be on your way. I don't want to linger in this place any longer than is absolutely necessary. I try to avoid standing near lightning and floating rocks.

In the event of a crisis behind enemy lines, a legionnaire may sell excess material to noncombatants. Such material must have no significant military application. Gold acquired in this manner must be used to secure swift passage back to the legion.
Sabashur-dar thought so at first. Was going to leave but, you know … circumstances.
Yes. This one's horse ran away and the khaj-winds made it impossible to follow. Stupid hoof-walker! I would claw his eyes out if I could find him.
Sabashur-dar is greedy—very greedy. Fearsome monsters attract five-clawed adventurers. And five-clawed adventurers carry fat gold purses! Great place for a sale, yes?
Ah, but you don't know this one's other problem.

They're an ancient order of mages, sworn to protect Elinhir. But they turned.\n\nThey hunted and killed every other mage in the city, harvesting the magicka from them. Everyone else was just in the way.

We told him the location of the Celestial Mage's Apex Stone. With that information, his master, the Celestial Serpent, was able to corrupt the Mage and turn her against Craglorn.\n\nI can never atone for what we did. I can only hope to stop Yamanu-ko.

Tarish-Zi was a member of a long ruling line of the Na-Totambu, and he helped conquer much of Hammerfell as part of the Ra Gada. \n\nBut while many of the invaders settled in the south, Tarish-Zi dreamed of still greater conquests.

They've been making a nuisance of themselves in Belkarth for the last few days. Claim they need to speak to Hara of the Star-Gazers immediately.\n\nOf course, Hara hasn't been available, so they came here to wait.
Well, for one thing, all of the pictures of the constellations portray the Mage as a bearded old man.\n\nFor another, shouldn't the Celestials look more … I don't know … intimidating?

No, and that's why we're here. Hara wanted us to make sure they had legitimate business with the Star-Gazers before she sees them.\n\nBut all I found out is that they're legitimately crazy! Still, I kind of want to believe them, you know?

Take this relic, the Seeker's Sight. It is a compass of sorts, one that is connected to all aspects of the Mage.\n\nBut like the Mage, the relic is broken. When you repair it, it will recognize our other aspects and lead you to them.

Thank you. With the Seeker's Sight restored, we can locate our other aspects before the Serpent takes control of them.\n\nWhen you finish mending the Seeker's Sight, meet us at the winery outside of Belkarth. We will wait for you there.
When we fell from the sky, the three gems that power the Seeker's Sight were lost. You will need to retrieve these gems to make use of the relic.
Hold still but a moment and we will show you. Witness the treachery of the Serpent.
Oh yeah—it's all sweetrolls and honey here. Can't you tell?\n\nOf course it's not all right!
Right. Let's say—and this is all hypothetical, mind you—let's say you had to get a siege engine from down here up to the gate. How would you do it?
Exactly! You'd take it up in pieces and assemble it on the other side of the gate. What kind of soft-headed idiot assembles the ram down here? It makes no sense at all!
Hrmph. Whatever. Go on then. Mauloch knows I've got a lot of work to do.

No sense! No sense at all. \n\nI tell you, If I find the little skeever smear who put this thing together, I'm going to tie him to the cap and ship his arse straight to the Imperial City. We'll put that thick skull to the test.

What happens to any man, given enough power? \n\nHe began styling himself an "emperor" rather than only a king. He turned his armies against his allies. He even trekked outside of Hammerfell for a time, which is where he met me.

With much of his family and those loyal to them, Tarish-Zi continued carving a path north through Hammerfell, eventually settling where we now stand. For a time he ruled justly in the way of tradition, building a new kingdom. That peace did not last.

I was adventuring in the highlands when I came across a cadre of Tarish-Zi's soldiers. I slew those that moved against me. The rest escaped quickly after. That night by the fire, a messenger approached and made me an offer I couldn't refuse.

I worked to defend my home. That's all. The messenger was part of a movement that was stirring among the people. \n\nAs an outsider, I was above suspicion. Someone Tarish-Zi would not expect to covet his throne. Someone who could get close.

Tarish-Zi took an interest in me after his soldiers returned with the tale. He sent the messenger to ask me to join his guard. \n\nBut the messenger confided the mad king's plans to invade my homeland. A course his own people opposed, but in secret.

How can I describe her to you? She is as fierce and brilliant as a freshly sharpened blade. \n\nHer name would be meaningless to you, but I know she waits for me back where I belong. When this fight is over, I must find a way back. Somehow.

The rebellion was crushed, but it put fear into Tarish-Zi. He gave up his dreams of invasion. And I remained blameless in his eyes.\n\nI planned to leave his service—but then I met someone, a woman. She gave me a reason to continue the fight.
Heh, if only I could. I thought I'd gone mad. I did go mad. \n\nHara tells me that it was the Celestial Warrior who pulled me through time. I believe it, even if I don't understand how it's so.

My guess is that the Serpent was somehow able to use the Warrior's power through him. \n\nHe likely learned of the cursed army of Anka-Ra resting below the sands and knew he could use them by calling to Tarish-Zi across time. We put an end to that.

The Star-Gazers have legends about those born under the sign of the Warrior and the connection they have with their patron—that he can call on them to fight for him. \n\nApparently time is a meager barrier for a Celestial.

Aye. Many were sent forth before we killed Tarish-Zi, and it seems clear that they will roam until put down. \n\nWithout their leader, we can take comfort knowing they won't be rallied into a proper army. I hope their souls find rest in the end.

You must be new to the area. Before the trade roads were cut off, the town of Dragonstar held a grand melee every year.\n\nFighters came from all over to participate. But I've never heard of a victory like this.
That's my guess. I heard that they arrested him as soon as the fight ended. Handed him over to the Daggerfall Covenant garrison at the Bangkorai gate.
Iron Orcs. We thought they had left the gate unoccupied. We were very, very wrong.

It is a classic case of buying a cat to catch a mouse. The mages of Elinhir summoned the atronachs to ward off the invasion from Coldharbour. \n\nBut when the work was done, the atronachs remained—and turned on them.
Yes. Think of the biggest, meanest, angriest Orc you've ever met. Got it? Now add about thirty stone of pure muscle and forty stone of bad disposition. You might get close to describing an Iron Orc.
In a heartbeat. Three of my lads fell before I even knew we were under attack. They beat Lucius to death with their bare hands. It was … it was awful.
I don't. But I'm not leaving my boys here for the crows.\n\nIf I were you, I'd walk on. Hopefully we'll get some reinforcements soon. In the meantime, we wait.
We hold here. If we're lucky, they'll quiet down long enough for us to gather our dead. If we're very lucky, they'll pack their things and head back to their warcamp.
Pinumur does not tuck his tail for dung-headed savages. They were lucky the first time. If they attack again, Pinumur will make them pay.

I do not know. But I've heard of strange sightings near one of the broken Dark Anchor dolmens.\n\nYou might look there, if you're curious. Of course, that calls to mind another common expression involving cats.
Let me stop you right there. I did not summon the atronachs. Not alone, anyway.\n\nI had the help of three other mages: Adalind, Dorian, and Kasimir.
I only drink when I remember. And once I forget, I stop.

I'm just getting a handle on that myself. At the time, I found it strange that they seemed to have an answer for every spell I threw at them.\n\nBut Hara tells me that the Celestial Serpent had a hand in my capture.
Well, out of all of us, Kasimir was the prodigy. He was only nineteen years old, if you can believe it!\n\nBut summoning the atronachs was Dorian's idea. Or rather, his dream.

Everyone did their part. Adalind chose the ritual location. Kasimir prepared the summoning circle. And I readied the Gem of Celestial Command, just as Dorian had been shown.\n\nIt was our finest moment, and the last time we were all alive together.

He said a woman appeared to him in a dream. She wore a dress made of stars, he said, and had hair burnished with golden light.\n\nHe was convinced that she was the Mage herself. Showing him how to free Craglorn of the Dark Anchors.
