Yes! We report this latest disaster to House Redoran and they force House Telvanni to pay for our losses. While they're at it, they can provide us with another kwama queen.\n\nA simple solution for a simple problem!

The foreman wants to see you. He's down with everyone else at the docks preparing for this latest farce.\n\nWhile you are all playing your games, I'll be giving my report to House Redoran. They should be along any minute now.
That's— that's beside the point! The House is very busy.  Dealing with some pressing threat to all of Vvardenfell, no doubt. They'll be here any moment, I can feel it.

Few of my contemporaries can boast of a luminary such as Farena Andrano occupying a prime branch upon their family tree.\n\nLady Farena studied at the feet of Sotha Sil and was counted among his companions before the Tribunal rose to power.

More like quarantining myself. I'm a natural disaster masquerading as a person. If I just sit here quietly no one else will get hurt.\n\nBesides, we're out of options. Other than breaking into the mine and planting the egg in the nursery, of course.

I knew I could count on you. Head to the mines and look for the nursery. I'll retrieve the royal egg and meet you there.\n\nOnce we plant the egg, the workers will almost certainly attack. You'll have to fend them off until the queen emerges.

You know, fetch it. You're right. I'm the one who got the miners into this mess, and I'm going to damn well be the one who gets them out!\n\nIt will be dangerous though. Planting things in kwama mines always carries risk.
Yes. And soon! We need to get her majesty inside the nursery before that happens. If the queen doesn't take on the scent of the colony, the workers will reject her. So, yes. Urgency!
What? You're—you're not joking, are you? I mean, I'm grateful if that's the truth, but how?

So Revus wasn't trying to destroy us after all. He's still got a lot of explaining to do, but for what it's worth, I'm happy I was wrong about him.\n\nGods, what a day. I've had enough excitement for ten lifetimes. I'm just anxious to get back to work.

Help with the mine, of course—provided Lathdar lets me. I have to learn to fix my mistakes. Or better yet, to not make them in the first place!\n\nI suspect the miners are still suffering from the resonator's effects. I'm sure I could brew a remedy.

I'm getting the impression that Manore's threats don't count for much without the foreman's support. I doubt I have much to worry about.\n\nThank you again. If you ever need another rare egg or need something broken, feel free to call on me, all right?
Depends where you need to go.
Where to?
Where to?
Depends where you need to go.
Where to?
Where to?
Depends where you need to go.
Where to?
Where to?
Depends where you need to go.
Where to?
Where to?
Tell me.
Safe travels to you.

Logic has very little place in the behavior of Daedra, my helpful associate. Studying the fabric of reality does tend to attract unwanted attention, but these creatures appeared just before you entered my tower.\n\nI wonder, why have you returned?

No, of course not. I just invented it! I need proper components to build such a device.\n\nMy hirelings scour the land for materials all the time. Here's a list. Head out the back door and ask them to direct you to these common Dwarven components.

Hirelings? Yes, they worked for me. Before they quit, ungrateful netches!\n\nStill, I paid them well before the pistons slipped their alignments. They should know where to find the components. Last I heard, Snorfin and the others were in Molag Mar.

The situation that troubles me has taken a toll on my Archcanon. But he's a faithful servant. Tarvus will do as I say, and I say we need your assistance.\n\nFind the Archcanon in his office and he'll tell you how to proceed.

Impressive! I thought I'd never see you again. That's what usually happens when I employ hirelings to acquire rare and exotic items from dangerous locations.\n\nWell, the Great Gear doesn't dawdle and neither do I! Hand them over and I'll get to work.

Of course you don't, I just invented it! Honestly ….\n\nYou won't use it, anyway, not if you plan to fight the one who wields Sotha Sil's staff. Almost impossible to operate the tonal inverter while also engaged in battle. It's too cumbersome.

Easy as scrib jelly pie! One person operates the controls to generate the sound waves. When it reaches the proper pitch, you activate the inverter and discharge its energy to disrupt Sunna'rah's power. Temporarily.\n\nHere. I wrote you instructions.

Sunna'rah? The blessed staff? I suppose the name fits. Sort of.\n\nYou'll need someone to assist you. Someone you trust. Oh, not me. Too busy. Too fragile! But using the tonal inverter is definitely a two-person activity.
Tell me.
Tell me.
Tell me.
Tell me.
Safe travels to you.
Safe travels to you.
Safe travels to you.
Safe travels to you.
Well?
Well?
Well?
Well?
Well?
Of course!
Of course!
Of course!
Of course!
Of course!
Let's go.
Let's go.
Let's go.
Let's go.
Let's go.
Walk with the Three.
Walk with the Three.
Walk with the Three.
Walk with the Three.
Walk with the Three.
It marks a fresh start to the new year, for all who walk beneath the sun. Everyone in Tamriel celebrates!\n\nWell, perhaps not the Maormer—but everyone else. You should try it for yourself and see!
I know who she is! I still don't trust her and I refuse to let her anywhere near Lord Vivec. Who knows what an Ashlander would do while the Warrior-Poet is in such a fragile state?

A tonal what now? Well, since I can't go with you, what with Lord Vivec requiring my undivided attention, I suppose we'll have to let the Ashlander assist you.\n\nVery well. Take her and defeat Chodala. Then bring me his staff so we can restore Vivec.

Chodala and his most loyal followers have taken refuge in a ruin called Kaushtarari. It's an ancient shrine devoted to the Daedric Prince Malacath.\n\nI think my brother plans to ask the God of Curses to help him.
It will allow us to stop Chodala? Then of course I'll help you.\n\nSince the Tribunal's dogs took my weapons, I'll need to replace them. Meet me at the ruins when you're ready.

Well, it's barely a song. It's just a mash of notes, you know? Crawls up behind your eyeballs and makes you dizzy. Paranoid.\n\nI've been working in these mines for years and I've never heard the like. Might have something to do with all the quakes.

Yeah. I don't know if you noticed, but Red Mountain's been pretty ornery lately. We've been dealing with minor cave-ins for weeks.\n\nCould be that one of those tremors uncovered something it shouldn't have.

The New Life Festival was once a celebration of Magnus, the sun god. I have a book—you're welcome to read about the history, if you care to.\n\nBut I'd rather tell you about the celebrations. Very few involve a chance of paper cuts!

Well, that's larger than I expected. But it looks simple enough to operate.\n\nI suppose it's better that I work the device. I'm not sure I'm capable of attacking Chodala. He's still my brother, no matter how dangerous his beliefs have become.

I'll help you counter the effects of Sunna'rah. Maybe once we neutralize it, Chodala will listen to reason.\n\nI know that's probably just wishful thinking. I'll settle for finding out who tempted Chodala with that damn staff.

I care little for my own safety, but my people are another matter. Without my power to stop it, the moonlet will crash into the city and kill hundreds—perhaps thousands—of innocents. And that would just be the start of Vvardenfell's woes.

Let us not dwell on disasters to come when we have problems enough to deal with in the here and now.\n\nConsult with Archcanon Tarvus and discover the source of this attack. Then we can put an end to it and not worry about what might have been.

My brother … travels. We have not heard from him for quite some time, but I sense that he remains safe and in possession of his full power.\n\nFunny. He always wanted to discover the limits of our divinity. Perhaps I will solve that mystery for him.

I know that! It was either Chodala or the lives of hundreds of Dunmer, all because he convinced himself he was the Nerevarine. Or someone convinced him. \n\nEither way, my brother is dead and the Cavern of the Incarnate has another resident.

Take Sunna'rah and I'll meet you back in Vivec City. Your Archcanon made it quite clear that the staff was the key to saving Vivec.\n\nI need to take care of my brother's remains. Then we'll be done here.

And just in time! According to my calculations, with every use of Sunna'rah, Chodala drained more energy from Lord Vivec. It almost killed him!\n\nBut we can use the staff to save Vivec. Just plant it in the floor and the power will return to him.

I don't think that thing was ever the Archcanon. It called itself Barbas. \n\nAs an Ashlander, I'm more familiar with Daedric lore than most of the Elves of the Great Houses. Beyond that, I've made a study of the most prominent Daedric Princes.

Because Barbas is a loyal servant of the Daedric Prince, Clavicus Vile. I'm not an expert on the Prince of Bargains, but it seems to me that this was all part of some grand plan.\n\nPerhaps Vivec can explain things better than I can.

Archmagister Otheri. None of the other Magisters would have him. Too many escape attempts.\n\nThen there's the matter of magical aptitude. The Telvanni abhor Hist-magic and make him wear suppression manacles all the time … even when he sleeps.
I enjoyed more freedom than most, it's true. Most of the marsh-born slaves hated me for it. Called me "smoke-scale," "elf-heart" … and much, much worse.\n\nBut, that's all behind me now. I won.

I do. Otheri banished me to those farms for a time. I spent thirty days in the dry-box and heard many things.\n\nA saltrice farmer named Barys Rendo grumbled like a sick crocodile. His wife called Vos a "backwater sty." He would sell. Why do you ask?

She gave you gold? I thought …. My heart told me that she gathered coin to purchase my freedom.\n\nShe probably seeks to parley this into an even greater sum. I trust her judgment, even if I do not fully understand it. Good luck, my friend.

I'll contact the Telvanni Council immediately. I'm sure they'll love to hear about Savarak's tawdry affair with those gold-pinchers in House Hlaalu.\n\nIf I know the council—and I do—Savarak will be feeding the shroom beetles by week's end.

Indeed. The citizens of Vos will be free to go about their lives in peace.\n\nAlthough, for Vos to truly flourish, we must also restore my Mistress Dratha to proper health. From the looks of things, she doesn't have much time.

Sieve lice? Oh dear, you're just as mad as the others, aren't you?\n\nTry to focus. This resonator is broken. I need to set these dials to the correct sequence, but I can't hear the tones. Are you aware of any sequence it could be set to? Just nod.

"Excellent!" he said, expecting the worst.\n\nJust turn these dials until you think they're in the correct sequence. That lever there seems to execute the pattern. I'm sure that if the dials are in the correct position … something will happen.

Well, that's disappointing. But random tinkering is the mother of invention, right?\n\nI need you to turn the dials until you think they're in the right position, then pull that lever. Anything you might have heard or seen could help. I believe in you.

Perfect! I'll get to work on this right away.\n\nOh, one other thing. Llayne took off toward Vos with a handful of guardsmen. I think they mean to arrest that guar's arse, Savarak. She might need your help.
If you find that oaf, give him a good kick in the nethers for me. Y'ffre knows how long it's going to take me to clean up my nursery.

Selvil Island is just east of the tower. If he manages to get away I'll never forgive myself.\n\nIt will take me too long to gather up all the town guards. I need you to go after him. Please, sera, make sure he doesn't board that ship!

Hm. Neramo wants you to snatch his stupid control rod back from that oaf, Lenarmen, right? Well, we've got bigger problems.\n\nI rescued this lot from Lenarmen's mercenaries, but they still have our dig leader, Kasouda, and two others.

Bah! Of course not. Too busy praying and hollowing out bugs, no doubt.\n\nBut make no mistake, if they find out a Telvanni mage has been poking around in their territory, they'll come down on this place like a Dawnstar gale.

Jinrisa? Interesting. That envious hag never misses an opportunity to stick a thumb in Firuth's eye.\n\nListen carefully. I need you to acquire that deed as quickly as possible—before she makes it public that she's bought land near Vos.

I suggest you use all available means. You can begin by searching the Adept's Hall in Tel Naga. \n\nI will warn you that the Adept's Hall is not open to outsiders. You'll need to be careful while searching for the deed, so as to not raise suspicion.

Ah, a modification of my master's old experiments, turning a simple tool into a dangerous weapon. Ingenious! Evil, yes, but also quite brilliant.\n\nHmm. A tonal inverter should counter it. Uses sound waves to temporarily disrupt the flow of energy.

The situation is wound dangerously tight, but I believe the gears revolve around you. Once you leave, I should be perfectly safe. Or, at least as safe as I ever am in the midst of all these experiments. \n\nYou however …. Stay vigilant, my friend.

Return to Vivec City. Do what you can to aid Vivec. And pay heed to my faithful vessel, Seryn. I name her Champion of the Moon and Star. She will play a pivotal role in ending her brother's march toward godhood—if she survives.

It's a wonder and a miracle, all brass tunnels, glass domes, and giant gears. He was inspired by the work of the Dwemer, but the Clockwork City is pure Sotha Sil. He made it to forge the future and reshape the world. I learned a lot there.

He's a member of House Telvanni. Young, but a capable wizard with powerful friends. It seems he's likely to take over Tel Mora for good when Mistress Dratha passes away. \n\nNone of us want to live in a Vos ruled by Savarak.

We're being forced out. Savarak doesn't like the idea of a Dunmer falling for a slave, especially an Argonian. "Unnatural," he calls it. "Unseemly and profane." It's nonsense, but people get strung up for less.\n\nTo Oblivion with him, and this town!
He's a member of House Telvanni, like Mistress Dratha.\n\nMistress Dratha is powerful, but reclusive. Savarak's a little more ambitious.

She's one of the oldest, most powerful Telvanni councilors and the ruler of nearby Tel Mora—the great fungal tower just across the river. She ruled Vos and lands beyond until she fell ill.\n\nSome people think it's just old age. I'm not so sure.

Technically, yes. Luckily, Mistress Dratha's Mouth, Llayne Sadri, has been working against him in secret.\n\nWe're lucky to have her. Savarak can sniff out a conspiracy like a nix-ox sniffs out truffles. Without Llayne we'd probably be dead already.

Attracted the attentions …? Never mind, I don't want to know.\n\nI'll miss this place, but Vehk knows I'm not much of a farmer. I'm just glad I got to thank you in person. Your partner, Mertis, already paid me for the deed to the property.

What? Oh dear. The fellow was very convincing. Caught me right before I set out to find Seythen.\n\nHe wasn't much of a conversationalist—just paid me a hefty sum of gold and snatched up the deed. He set out toward Vos once we finished the sale.

My daughter has been gone too long and the House Guard can't seem to find a wall in the corner, but why should I trust you with this task? \n\nTell me, outlander. How can you succeed when my forces continue to fail time and time again?

Plotting? No, I'm confident that the false god will fall. Azura has proclaimed this and I know it to be true.\n\nThe Tribunal betrayed our hero and turned away from our religion. And they call us heretics. Bah!

My sister is too naive and idealistic for her own good. Look at the power I wield! Feel the conviction in my words!\n\nWhile the House Elves squabble and fight to carve up our land, the Nerevarine will step forth to end their tyranny once and for all!

How overly simplistic the world must be to your eyes, outlander.\n\nI am Nerevar reborn! I will lead my people to power and glory. The Wise Woman knows this. She will proclaim it when she returns. And no Tribunal lapdogs can change that.

Veya fled after a family … disagreement. She's run away before, but I'm concerned that she might have something more permanent in mind this time. And more dangerous.\n\nVeya knows how to evade the House Guard. But, as you said, she doesn't know you.

He's probably patrolling the town square at this time of day.\n\nBrivan's soldiers have been trying to get information out of Veya's friends, but those young men and women are almost as good at avoiding the House Guard as my daughter.
That is … a private matter.\n\nIf your investigation proves fruitful and such matters become relevant, we can discuss the particulars then—but not before.

Veya's always been fascinated by the Morag Tong. Even admired one of their agents when she was growing up. It's possible she's sought refuge with this agent—or even decided to join the organization, though I hope I'm wrong about that.
What?

Ah. It's a tonal resonator. Very powerful and very, very broken.\n\nI'll be happy to tell you all about it once you've fixed it. We're on a bit of a time-table. No offense, but I think the tonal stimuli have already made you a bit … scattered.

So you're a scholar as well? I certainly wouldn't have predicted that.\n\nBefore the Tribunal showed up, we Dunmer worshiped the Daedra. They raised no small amount of havoc, but they also left us valuable gifts. Gifts like the stones.
Nothing, until they rest side by side. If a mage manages to wake all seven, well … let's just say their powers of persuasion are put to the test.

So our legends say.\n\nNerevar united the Chimer and forged an alliance with the Dwemer. He died at the Battle of Red Mountain. We believe the Tribunal hastened his demise, despite Vivec's claims to the contrary.

The Nerevarine is a promise and a prophecy. We believe that, through the power of Azura, Nerevar will return to unite all Dunmer—House and Ashlander alike—and make Morrowind great again.\n\nThe returned Nerevar will be known as the Nerevarine.

Chodala says his new abilities strengthen his claim as the Nerevarine. I think it's the staff he carries. He had it when he returned and now it's always at his side.\n\nI know it's unreasonable, but I hate that staff. He calls it Sunna'rah.

Oh no, no. I can't do it myself. It's not subtle, or even polite, if a Telvanni just bluntly demands this thing or that service!\n\nI'm sorry to impose once again, but could you give the deed to Master Firuth on my behalf?

Just west of here, in a place called Hanud. Firuth values his privacy, so be wary of atronachs and traps—and don't be surprised if he's a bit … eccentric.\n\nMeet me in the Council Hall, when you return. I have a very good feeling about this!

I know I've asked a lot. Trust me, payment is forthcoming.\n\nJust offer the deed to Firuth, and tell him that Sun-in-Shadow would like his written support for her elevation to the rank of retainer. Make it subtle … but not too subtle, you know?

Take my scroll and help the Wise Woman see the lie of unbridled power.\n\nI thought myself the reborn Nerevar, for I was the strongest, most powerful warrior in all the land. But power alone won't save my people. In the end, it couldn't even save me.

To fulfill the prophecy, I followed a path of blood and war. In the end, my path became a road that led nowhere and I was cast down from my lofty spot.\n\nTake my scroll and help the Wise Woman understand the futility of a senseless war.

The Nerevarine must listen as well as proclaim. I refused to accept wise counsel, which led to the doom of my tribe and the end of my quest to embody the spirit of Nerevar.\n\nTake my scroll and remind the Wise Woman that wisdom ignored is ignorance.

Lord Vivec doesn't want his followers to see him in such a weakened state. Only you, Canon Llevule, and myself are permitted into his palace now.\n\nSpeaking of the palace, Lord Vivec wants to see you when we're done here.

So it appears.\n\nLord Vivec's doing his best not to complain, but I can see how much the draining of his energy has cost him. Just seeing you again should improve his mood considerably. And the progress you made with your investigations, outstanding!

Did she now? How prescient! Quite impressive, wouldn't you say, Gerald …? Yes, I thought so too.\n\nI'm glad she chose to give it to me, and not that guar-faced bumbler, Jinrisa. I suppose she wants something in return. These hirelings always do.

Cultists? This one said nothing about cultists! Perhaps you're thinking of another Khajiit ….\n\nLook, Renaku just wants to leave all these crazy Dark Elves behind and find a safer mine to work in. The Shulk Ore Mine is cursed!
Really? You? Just leave Renaku out of it! If you want to know what happened so badly, just go out to the Shulk Ore Mine and see for yourself!

Ah, yet another social climber. How tiresome. Still, exchanging a simple endorsement for valuable property seems like quite the bargain. Very well—it's a deal.\n\nGerald, be a dear and fetch me that pen …. Oh fine, I'll get it myself.

I'm sure you do, but I have to live here, you know? Look, there's nothing I can tell you. If the Houses ever found out I told an outlander about our troubles ….\n\nMaybe one of the miners would be more willing to talk to you.

No one likes a guar licker, you clawless kitten!\n\nIt happened a few days back. Weird cultists just barged in and took over the mine. This one managed to get away, but the Crew Chief and some of the others are still out there. Happy now, fish breath?
What happened—with her mentor—with me …  that wasn't Nevena. \n\nI came out here to prove her innocence. That might not be possible now.
This is where I caught up to Nevena. I begged her to come back. Swore I'd make this all right … but I couldn't.\n\nShe felt so heavy in my arms. The only thing she said … she whispered "kill me."
Be wary. I saw shapes in the ash. Robed figures. \n\nThat's not the blood loss talking … I don't think.

I should have listened. Before I knew, my Nevena was gone. Something changed in her eyes. Made my blood run cold. I never even saw the knife.\n\nManaged to stop the bleeding, but I'm not going anywhere soon. I've lost her. Maybe for good.

Really? Then forget I said anything about his holiness's nasal preening.\n\nThey're some sort of Daedric cultists. They've been performing rituals, calling forth divine power or some such nonsense. At least they were, before the Ashlanders showed up.

The savages barged into the deep chambers. Seemed to know about the hidden passage and everything. Stole the relic the cultists were praying over and ran for the hills.\n\nAs a matter of fact, that's where I'm going—as soon as it's safe to leave!

Excellent!\n\nI ran into Councilor Angharal just a moment ago—totally by chance, I might add. I asked her about the potential for advancement, and she hedged a bit. This endorsement will make all the difference.
Isn't it obvious? We're being worked to death! I won't say more while Overseer Torvayn is watching. I can't say more!\n\nIf you want answers, you'll have to deal with him first.
Can I? Yes. Will I? No. Not until Overseer Torvayn is dead. He's already spotted you, I know it. If he finds out I've spoken to you, I'm as good as dead.\n\nKill Torvayn. Then we can talk.

What's going on? Ha! They're working us like snowblind oxen, that's what's going on!\n\nYou want to know more? Kill that smoke-skinned bastard, Overseer Torvayn. He's always itching to execute someone, and I think I'm next.
She's wanted … for murder—but it wasn't her. Not my Nevena.
I couldn't make them out, just saw them from afar before I spotted Nevena. Seemed to be searching for something. That statue maybe?
Ruins, tombs, fire, and ash. All forgotten and lost to time.\n\nWhatever the relic hunters found here, it was better left that way.
Not Nevena. She's too timid. And why kill for it when she could have just walked away? It doesn't add up.\n\nThat thing brought her here—to whatever's out here. She didn't do this. It did.

Looks that way to most, but it's not that simple. Her mentor bought a statue. A relic from out here. Nevena was studying it.\n\nNow he's dead and she's gone. That statue's the only motive. It's the key.

Lots of our history is buried in ash. Out here, there was Kogoruhn. The seat of the Lost House. Traitors against the Three who were wiped out ages ago. \n\nThat statue preserved their evil. Save my sister from them. Please.

Ah, the ignorance of Outlanders! How refreshing!\n\nThe Blessing Stones serve as repositories for small amounts of Lord Vivec's power. They allow his favor to permeate sanctified locations. We need such a stone to power the divination ritual.

It used to be an ore mine and we hope it will be again. My crew was inside, preparing to start up mining operations, when the cultists attacked.\n\nThe way things are going, we might just have to turn the place into another kwama egg mine.

You must be one of the freelancers the councilor employed to supplement the duties of the House Guard. Very well, I'll tell you what I know. Veya ran away. Again.\n\nI hope you can succeed where my troops have failed. If anything happens to Veya ….

I've known the Releth family since I was a child. Veya is like a sister to me, and I'll do everything in my power to get her home safe and sound. Even trust an outlander.\n\nWe think her friends may know where she is, but they keep eluding us.

Perhaps. As long as you don't get too close. They've been running notes of late. I think it has something to do with Veya, but the runners keep evading my guards.\n\nLook for a group meeting on the other side of town and see if you can follow the note.
Veya's a born warrior. Hard-headed, stubborn, a real pain in the arse. She can fight like an angry netch, though. I keep trying to get her to join the militia, but she always turns me down.

We started to notice groups of young Dark Elves gathering in out of the way parts of the city. One of my guards saw them pass a note between them, but they split up and she lost them in the back alleys.

I wish I could say soon. Unfortunately, the Telvanni Dark Elves observe many silly rules. Lower castes cannot own slaves. I do not know why.\n\nOnce she becomes an oathman, she will have the means to free me—then we will escape this place.

Your croaks ring true, but she knows nothing of the larger world.\n\nMy heart hatched here in Vvardenfell, far from the Hist. Once she hears the cries of the hackwings, smells the peat, and feels the mud on her scales, she will forget about this place.

We Saxhleel struggle with the future, but I often gaze into the pond and dream.\n\nMy heart tastes Hist-sap for the first time. I teach her Jel and share root-secrets by candlelight. We paddle still rivers, hunt, and fish. These dreams keep me going.

I just received a summons from the Council. Typically I'd be overjoyed. After all, I just submitted a petition for advancement to oathman. But the Council never acts on petitions this quickly.\n\nSomeone's arranging pieces on the game board, I know it.

If a member of the House plans to spring a trap, I need to project strength.\n\nThe councilors know you've assisted me in the past. If you appear before the Mouths on my behalf, it puts the magisters and I on equal footing. It might even save my life.
This will be a painful journey, but thank you for sharing these with me.\n\nDid … did they offer any truth in this madness? Any glimpse of reason?
I hope you're wrong … the truth's too ugly. If these cultists entrapped my sister, who else will they come for? I need to see for myself, but … I'm afraid.\n\nIt might be wiser to turn back.
That fallen, disgraced House … that is not who she was. That is not who I am. It can't be. It was some spell the statue held over her. A curse, or enchantment placed by these heretics.
None. Well, none that I've discovered anyway. I speak modestly when I say that if there was a cure, I would have found it already.
Why do you even care? Fine.\n\nI altered the formula, turning the liquid decoction into a vapor. It proved to be very effective. Unfortunately it was nearly impossible to contain. Hence … this.

I guess I could squander my remaining hours searching for a remedy. But I'm an alchemist. A daedrologist. We don't trouble ourselves with things like "hope." I leave that nonsense to priests, and children, and the mentally ill.

What? Afflicting all these miners? Oh, spare me your crude moral outrage. They were wastrels. Laborers that were too ignorant or too lazy to find work anywhere else. This is as meaningful a contribution as they were likely to make.
None. I'd invite you to kill me, but given that I'll be dead soon anyway, it's hardly worth the effort.

Drevis? That laggard? I never understood what Veya saw in him.\n\nI suggest you go back and try again. Just do a better job of keeping your distance and don't lose sight of the note carrier. That's our best chance of learning anything.

Travel to the Rethan manor house and detain Benar. Once I've explained matters to Rayveth, he'll send Hlaalu constables to collect my brother.\n\nAfter this, I'll ask nothing more of you. You have my word.

I expect the Overseer's near the unfinished cantons, watching out for looters. When people panic, they're capable of anything. And with all the chaos going on outside, the Overseer closed the construction site.\n\nGet her key and bring back a stone.
Oh. I see. Maybe I was too impatient—requested it too soon. Damn.\n\nDid they give any reason? Was there anyone who spoke out against it?
I'll answer what I can, of course.

Just trust me, it's better this way. If the councilors had to deal with each other directly there would be no peace in Vvardenfell. You wouldn't jam a bunch of alits into a pen together. Mages need room to stretch—room to breathe.

Most Telvanni magisters prefer to be left alone. They dislike and mistrust each other, so they appoint Mouths to handle business outside their towers.\n\nOf course, the magister's wishes and the Mouth's wishes often get tangled. It's imperfect.

Yes! When I achieve the rank of oathman, I should be able to purchase a slave. I'll free Eoki, and we'll toast to our success. That is what we've been working toward, right? \n\nI know that some of this feels a little unsavory, but it's necessary.

My, my … this is damning. Dear Malur tried to hang this whole business around his brother's neck—and yours. A prudent, albeit sloppy affair.\n\nHouse Hlaalu can ill afford such a scandal and I hate to be lied to. Kill Malur and I will reward you.

She ran into the unfinished cantons. She's been beating herself up over the fact that they're behind schedule, but she won't do anyone any good if she gets herself killed!\n\nMy wife's tough as nails, but she's no warrior.
His city residence, I expect. Just across the river.\n\nDo be quick about this. I'm anxious to be done with the brothers Rethan.

Of course it was Ralasa. That pig has hated me from the start. Gothren's not fond of Argonians, but this is clearly personal.\n\nWould you act as my emissary once more? If you go to Tel Aruhn and speak to Gothren directly, maybe he can settle this.

A Telvanni mage doesn't have time to be troubled. Everyday I learn something new. Everyday I peel back one mystery to reveal another ten beneath it. If this is the price of that kind of discovery, I'll pay it!\n\nThat came out poorly. I … never mind.

That's impossible. We installed the Blessing Stone back in its canton and finished construction on that section a short time ago.\n\nWait a moment—does this have something to do with the chunks of rock raining down on the city?

I suppose you're in luck, then. We happen to have another Blessing Stone. It's at the third canton. Here. This key will open the door to that portion of the construction site.\n\nJust watch out for more looters—and the rocks falling out of the sky.

Varona? Was she still angry with me? No, you don't have to answer that. I know my wife. I'll head back and let her know I'm all right.\n\nTell Lord Vivec he can have our Blessing Stone—as long as he promises to do something about Baar Dau.
Perfect! I can feel Lord Vivec's essence inside it! I hope I remember how to do this. You'd better stand back—just in case.

Yeah? Well I need a stiff drink and a good plow, but you don't see me knocking on strangers' doors bellyaching about it.\n\nMagister Gothren's not seeing any visitors. Not today, not tomorrow, and not next week. So shove off, guar-face.

Oh, that's rich! You really think Magister Gothren would open his doors to a tail-arsed s'wit like you?\n\nThe master's not seeing any visitors. Not today, not tomorrow, and not next week. So shove off, you beast.

This one likes to help. Maybe you can help Kizmar too. Telvanni lands could use some kindness, yes?\n\nThis one's knees ache. Kizmar is too old to slip away. But a little distraction might help the other ja'khajiit escape Tel Aruhn.

This one left some crates of dried saltrice on the dock. Fine kindling, yes? A little fire might catch the slavemaster's attention, then my ja'khajiit can slip away.\n\nWhen you return, Kizmar will ask the dungy guards to help fight the blaze, you see?

This one will shout, and wave his arms, and run in circles. If Kizmar tells the guards Slavemaster Arenim needs their help, they will scamper off like beetles under a lantern. Everyone fears Arenim, even the guards.

Ha! No. All Kizmar needs to do is take off his blue shirt and put on a red shirt. This one has served Gothren for many years, but the Dark Elves still cannot tell us apart. Funny, yes?\n\nMoons protect you in the tower. The master hates suprises.
I thought the matter fairly straightforward. Spirits risen, terrorizing decent living folk with important research to finish. I don't care if it is their tomb, get rid of them!

He did? Well, of course I'm happy to help in any way I can. I suppose I know a few things about this terrible situation.\n\nBut we really must hurry. The energy provided by the Blessing Stone won't last very long.

Use what the Incarnates shared with you. Their failures point the way toward Chodala's downfall.\n\nBut beware Chodala's power. He may not be the Nerevarine, but some greater agency has lent strength to his conviction.

Due to an ancient pact, I am not permitted to interfere in the affairs of Nirn. Even this casual discussion pushes the boundaries of that agreement.\n\nInstead, I must work through trusted agents, such as yourself and Seryn.

Helping that arrogant imposter? Whatever gave you the idea that I was helping that murderer?\n\nVvardenfell must stand. Everything I do in this regard serves that single goal. Best that you remember that, Mortal.

Just as I anticipated. The mysteries reveal that Barbas seeks to enter the Clockwork City. So far, Sotha Sil's wards have impeded him, but the hound has Sunna'rah.\n\nYou must beat him to the prize—the reservoir that holds Vivec's stolen energy.

No, not going to happen. No offense to the Lady of Twilight, but Sotha Sil was quite adamant about keeping the place hidden and warded against the Daedra. \n\nOh, wait. Pistons fall into place. This concerns Sunna'rah and Lord Vivec, I presume?

Barbas? Another Daedra. Thinking … thinking ….\n\nSo Sotha Sil's forgotten tool was modified to steal Vivec's energy, which in turn energized the Clockwork City. Lit it up like the top of Red Mountain. Even Vile's dog would be able to see that!

Ah, that. I'm sorry, but Ralasa is determined to keep your Argonian from advancing. Typical. I should be Mouth! Say, I might have an idea.\n\nThe thieves Muthsera Gothren mentioned fled to Shashpilamat. Could you retrieve the goods they stole?

About time! I was almost starting to think no one would come.\n\nA Nereid caused one of our ships to run aground. I need you to recover what you can, and dispose of the creature before it can cause any more damage—namely to my career.
Muthsera Gothren will undoubtedly promote me to Mouth! Then, in exchange for your help, I'll support your Argonian's petition. One good turn and all that.\n\nWhat do you say?

We are not goods! Zashanti and her friends prepare to leave this cursed island. No more lashings. No more bitter food. Only the light of the moons drifting across the Topal Sea.\n\nWe only took Gothren's belongings to pay the smugglers.

Bright moons. This one thanks you, walker.\n\nWe stored Gothren's trinkets in crates nearby. The smugglers will groan at their absence, but we would rather face the wilds alone than go back to Tel Aruhn.

Falura is this one's loyal farmhand. She is not very bright, and she is very lazy—always scribbling notes and asking silly questions. But I keep her on anyway. Halinjirr always does right by his friends.

Oh. Uh, she knows too much about … my farming practices! Yes!\n\nHalinjirr has many secret farming tricks, like using fish heads and guar dung for fertilizer. But this one has already said too much, yes?
I could, but this one likes Falura. Plus, she probably knows too much.
I am sorry. This one is a nervous wreck.\n\nHalinjirr is growing a rare Khajiiti herb. Very delicate and very desirable. Good for seasoning fish and soothing the humors. Satisfied?
Do not worry, walker. You can depend on Halinjirr!

Of course. You didn't think she'd let that flat-headed Arith out-nix her did you? \n\nOh, and don't bother looking for those other stolen goods. My troops have the situation well in hand. Thanks for all your help, n'wah. So long.

Veya wants nothing to do with the House or her father. Why can't any of you respect that?\n\nEven if I wanted to help, I haven't seen Veya since she snuck out of town. We communicate by notes, and this one isn't even about her.
If you must know, it concerns Veya's brother. He was an officer in the House Guard before he vanished without a trace. We've been trying to help Veya find him.
Well, we wouldn't want that, would we?
What? No! Don't be absurd.\n\nJust do as Halinjirr asked. Deal with those ruffians in the cavern. We'll speak more later.
I underestimated Ralasa, I see that now. She plays the game far better than I do.\n\nThe only way to win a game like this is to eliminate the player.

A local tough. Goes by the name of Ashur. He delivers the letters. We usually meet him outside of town, to the northeast.\n\nBut good luck trying to get any information out of him. Ashur is not known for his conversational skills.

Appealing to her vices might work. Ralasa has quite a love for both information and sweets. Why not give her both?\n\nDeliver these marshmerrow cakes and let her know about Arith's plot. It's a modest offering, but with time and effort, who knows?

I knew you'd see reason. Trust me, no one deserves this fate more than Ralasa. You may have a Telvanni's heart after all.\n\nArith told me that Ralasa entered her room in the Council House just a few minutes ago. Good luck, my friend. Be discreet!

I know how it sounds. I take no pleasure in it—it's just an unfortunate necessity. Half the Telvanni hierarchy arranged an opening at some point in their rise to power.\n\nIf you deal with Ralasa, Arith takes her place. It's the best play, sera.
Balmora's not that big. Most of the sons and daughters of the House leaders and prominent merchants know each other. Veya's one of us, and we'll do whatever it takes to help her find her brother.
I'm not telling you anything, you Redoran lapdog!
You think I'm just going to tell you all our secrets, outlander? Well, that's not going to happen. I won't betray Veya.
Oh, delightful! Let me guess, she sent you with a bribe? Or a gift? Or an offer of service? How delicious.\n\nWell? What does she want?

Ugh. Arith. That's hardly news. In any case, I'll take those marshmerrow cakes. Funny … she knew just what to get me. Seems her slave's instincts haven't faded with time.\n\nTell her I will consider her proposal. I can always use another servant.

I'd rather not discuss it. Suffice it to say that the skooma trade offers many dark incentives—especially for undercover officers. It's easy to cross the line. Too easy.\n\nHopefully this arrest and seizure will help me make amends.

If you'd ever taken it, you'd know.\n\nSkooma is a powerful hallucinogen—addictive, deadly, and cheap. Lethal overdoses are routine in Morrowind. Once it's got its hooks in you, you'll do anything to get it. Steal, rape, kill … whatever.

I don't know, but it doesn't matter. He's developed a method to grow vast quantities of moon-sugar in Vvardenfell. That's a dangerous skill. Too dangerous. Can you imagine what would happen if the Camonna Tong crime family got a hold of his notes?
Halinjirr's no Daedric Prince, but his work could be just as destructive. Please, just do the right thing.
So you retrieved my … stolen energy. You … stopped Barbas ….\n\nNow … return what is rightfully mine ….

To quote my … seventy-fifth exhortation … "Certainty is the brother of fear."\n\nNothing is certain, but I have confidence … in you … in what you have done. Use the staff … return my energy. Or not. In a little while … it won't matter.
Falura? That skooma-fiend can barely put her trousers on straight, let alone conduct an investigation like this. You must be mistaken.
Difficult to say. If I had my way, she'd be hanging from the nearest tree. I'll pass it on to my contacts in the Oath-Bureau. I will be honest, though—her chances are very slim.
Certainly! I'd be more than happy to tell you all about the great Narsis Dren and his exciting adventures!\n\nWhat do you want to know?

I suppose I can take credit for that. I found an old scroll in a Telvanni bookshop and took it right to Narsis for analysis.\n\nHis translation indicated there were secret passages inside. He said secret passages mean hidden treasure, so here we are!

You did? Wrothgar, you say? Funny, I don't remember seeing you mentioned in "Narsis Dren and the Draugr Dilemma."\n\nAre you sure you met my Narsis? A person of his stature is often impersonated by unscrupulous cads.

You don't know the great Narsis Dren? He explores the world's most dangerous locations and writes books so that his beloved admirers can experience his adventures vicariously. Just reading his words will send little thrills up and down your spine.

It's much more than mere admiration! Narsis Dren fills my heart the way mead fills an earthen jar. Some day, we will undergo the ritual of Mara and live happily as husband and wife!\n\nElfbetta Dren … it has a certain flair, don't you think?

Oh yes. Peeved. In the extreme.\n\nMagister Gothren promoted me to Mouth, but he still grieves for Ralasa. As you know, grief often gives way to anger. Apparently his gentle disposition has limits when it comes to assassinating his servants.

Pity I didn't get here sooner. I thought perhaps, with time, his fury might abate.\n\nI'd make all haste to Tel Aruhn if I were you. Muthsera Gothren respects courage and candor. If you speak to him directly, you might receive better treatment.

You know, the usual buyer's remorse. I see a lot of that in my line of work.\n\nTurns out, I had to kill a bad man who did bad things. The writ was legal and above board. Unfortunately, his brother didn't see it that way and was looking for revenge.

You make it sound so … obscene. Still, that's pretty much an accurate description. But it's not like I work for the Dark Brotherhood or anything. I don't kill anyone without a sanctioned writ.\n\nKeeps the Great Houses in line. It's a calling.

You were, were you? Was it Milesa? I told her I'd close out my tab after I completed another contract. That woman has the patience of an anxious nix.\n\nWell, tell her I'm good for it. I'll stop by and we can conclude our business cordially.
Veya? The new apprentice? Now why in Oblivion do you care about Veya?

Are you now? And why do you want to do that? Never mind. I don't really care. I was asked to pass along some notes, but I'm not really the messenger type.\n\nI suggest you talk to Veya's mentor. Last I heard, she had a job in the western ruins.
That's your lookout. He's been expecting you.\n\nYou're an idiot for having crossed him. He's vindictive and powerful.
You're lucky he hasn't just tossed her back into the slave pens. Or tossed you in there as well. \n\nGood luck. You're gonna need it.

Ugh. Why would anyone want to be friends with one of the lizard folk. Doesn't make you much better than them.\n\nYou should go and find the Magister before he tosses your friend back in the slave pens.

I'm not hurt. But I am angry. And a little frightened. \n\nGothren's men snatched me right out of my home in Sadrith Mora and used a portal to bring me here. And then Gothren ordered me to be put in a slave cage. Me! A free Telvanni!

You are indeed a loyal friend. I've felt a bit hopeless, trapped in here, without any information. He wants me to feel like a slave, a nobody, worthless.\n\nI must warn you - his plan is likely to make you do something for him, in order to free me.

Don't waste my time with flimsy pretense. Did you really think you could kill my Mouth and get away with it? I see all. Your clumsy intrigue is no exception.\n\nIf you wish to save your life and that of your friend, you will perform a task for me.

Magisters care little for the limits of morality—me least of all. I try to avoid turning people into shambling masses of screeching tumors, but in this case I could make an exception.\n\nAt the very least your scaled friend will die in chains.

Thank you. We all knew this was coming, but that doesn't make it any easier to bear. My father was a good man, even if Mils never got to see it.\n\nWhy was he so obsessed with that stone? You said he had you store his memories inside it?

Magister Otheri made a discovery some weeks ago—a relic, or some Dwarven device perhaps. He refuses to share the details, so I am compelled to take those details by force.\n\nSteal his notes from Tel Naga and deliver them to my new Mouth, Arith.

That depends on what information you retrieve. If it's useful, we can discuss the terms of the lizard's freedom. \n\nThat's as much of a promise as you'll get from me. Be grateful I am giving you a chance to rectify the wrong you've done me.

I know all your clients have burdens to bear, but I'm speaking of the very fabric of Nirn here. Master Alar plans to perform an experiment that will alter the laws of our reality, and I need you to stop it. I require his research notes as well.

I hope it won't be too difficult. I know Magister Otheri has worked on something for a couple of years. Rumor has it that it is proving profitable. Tel Naga is the big tower in Sadrith Mora.\n\nSo he'll free me if you get details on these experiments?
Be careful, my friend. I am sure you will be successful.

It is a rare gem. Once, long ago, Redguard warriors carried them into battle. One of the most famous was a sword-singer in the first age. Makela Leki.\n\nNo historians will cherish my thoughts, certainly, but perhaps my children will come to, in time.

I purchased it from my master, Drenim, a Telvanni mage of middling repute. I have served him for … how long? Many, many years. For as long as I can remember.\n\nI will serve him until I die, no doubt, but that will not be long now.

Ah, yes. Mils. My son has never really forgiven me for never being here for them. He's a stranger in my own home.\n\nNo, if anything it's the other way around. Even Neria has grown accustomed to my absence.
You'll know soon enough. As will they, I hope. \n\nI failed them as a father, but … they are safe, aren't they? I kept them safe.

Neria less than Mils, but both my children grew up largely on their own. My duties to Master Drenim consumed a great deal of my time.\n\nMils, especially, grew up with Neria and no one else. He despises me, and I don't blame him.

I cannot travel with you, but I have attuned this stone to my soul. When you use it at the locations I've marked, it will summon … echoes of things that once occurred there.\n\nThe stone absorbs these echoes, allowing others to view them.
This is the port town of Seyda Neen, on the island of Vvardenfell. We fished you out of the burning wreckage of a slaver ship near Firemoth.\n\nIf you're not a slaver, why were you dressed as one?
We? Hmm.\n\nI'll let Governor Salvi sort this out. She wants to see you. Best not to keep her waiting.

Into the tomb? That tomb over there? Well, that wouldn't work out so well. You see, I have a powerful fear of ghosts. Ghosts, spirits, windows—anything you can see through, really.\n\nNo, I don't go anywhere near tombs. Too many ghosts for my taste.

Well, that doesn't sound like the Narsis Dren I know.\n\nJust remember, Narsis Dren doesn't have time for pretty admirers. His work in the Dreloth tomb is very important. So make sure he's all right—but keep your hands to yourself.

Oh, that sounds just like my Narsis! Sometimes he has so many thoughts going through his head, he can get distracted.\n\nHis work in the Dreloth tomb is very important. So if you can make sure he's all right, I would really appreciate it.
Go explore somewhere else that isn't the private residence of the Magister or Tel Naga, you dimwitted fool. \n\nOff with you, before I call a guard.

The Zainab tribe has worked within the ruins for generations. We were recently driven out by a band of Ashlander exiles, and do not have the skills or warriors to take it back. It is a blessing that the Temple agreed to help.

It takes more than a few shambling corpses to stop the formidable Narsis Dren!\n\nCome to think of it, I seem to remember that you weren't as helpful as I'd hoped once we got into that ancient Nord barrow. There was a sarcophagus, as I recall ….

Hmm? Oh, yes. My most popular volume to date! "Narsis Dren and the Draugr Dilemma." Surprised you haven't read it. It's captivating!\n\nHelp me get through this tomb and I'll let you have a copy—at a substantial discount!

Gather some fire salts and kindlepitch from the docks. With them, you can make a fire bomb. Not only will setting their ship on fire destroy it, it will flush Svadstar from his hiding hole so I can end him.\n\nWe'll meet after you gather the supplies.

You have? You really want to fight that thing? I don't care if these ruins contain the bones of Lorkhan himself, I'm not going back until that monster is gone.\n\nBut hey, if you want to fight a Daedra and grab a few pointless relics for us, feel free.
Well done! I think my master wants to speak with you himself. \n\nTry not to make him angry, all right?

Ah yes, this is Otheri's journal. His penmanship has gotten even worse.\n\nSo it's a Dwarven artifact then? A merged tonal prism? My, my, that does sound intriguing. Seems he tucked it away in his kwama mine, Zalkin-Sul. You will fetch it for me.
Get me the prism. We have nothing more to discuss.

I said nothing of the sort. If your work pleases me, I may deign to release your friend and forget your misdeeds. But make no mistake, n'wah—I've given you no word to keep.\n\nGo to Zalkin-Sul, acquire the prism, then bring it to me in Tel Aruhn.
Oh yes! I mean, Muthsera Gothren expects unwavering obedience, but on the whole, it's been a delight.\n\nI know he's treated you poorly, but isn't his candor refreshing?
Hm. I can't begrudge you that. Were I in your position, I'd probably need a good sulk too. Not that you're sulky or anything! Oh, you know what I mean.
About as much as you, I wager. \n\nKwama nest there, tending to their eggs and what have you. It probably smells bad too.

Sure is. You looking for work? Nah, you're the adventurous type. Only time you'll lift a pick is to bash in some beastie's skull, am I right? Of course I am.\n\nWhat brings you out here to the arse end of nowhere?

Well it isn't locked. Go ahead and take a peek.\n\nMight want to keep it quiet though. Don't want Otheri's guards spotting you—trust me. They keep things locked down tighter than my fat auntie's bodice.

Honestly, your guess is as good as mine. I've never been interested in the brutes.\n\nThey steal all sorts of things. Guars, furniture, spare keys … they pack them in mud and feces along with their own eggs. Puzzling, truly.

Well, that's not what I expected. But you can just turn around and leave. You're not going to find her.\n\nVeya's going through a difficult time right now and the last thing she needs is some House Redoran lackey adding to her pain and confusion.

Were you imagining a hot bath, a bottle of wine, and a secluded cottage with a roaring fire? Me, too! Instead, we're up to our arm pits in the usual muck and mire. Just like old times!\n\nAll this and things are looking up for my organization, too!

That was poetry in motion! Not only is my organization getting choice assignments again, but we're starting to recover some of our prestige.\n\nSpecifically, these Malacath cultists interfered with House Telvanni, so they had to be dealt with.

I suppose if you're in for a sliver you might as well be in for the log.\n\nI'm with the Morag Tong and what you witnessed was a legal murder. According to my writ, the Orc had to die. So I killed him. Now if you don't mind, I need to get back to Veya.
I guess it's possible. Like I said, cliff striders are very odd and unpredictable.\n\nAll the more reason to find the egg quickly.

Really? Is that what Old Man Eris told you? And did he tell you about Veya's brother? About how House Redoran exiled their favored son? No? I didn't think so.\n\nVeya needs answers and I promised to help her. So walk away while you still can.

Veya joined that cult of assassins? I was afraid she'd do something rash, but what was she thinking?\n\nI don't see the Morag Tong as safe, but at least she's still alive, so I suppose that's something. When are we going to meet with my daughter?

Someone of no consequence and not at all important to accomplishing your mission. Besides, you don't find Morag Tong agents. They find you. Just pray it's not because your name wound up on one of their writs. That is a death sentence.

I've got a proposition. \n\nI can tell you what little I know and give you a key to Mzanchend. In exchange, you give me any notes you find in there. Anything about how it was built, what it does, anything. Got a nice offer from an interested party.
That's not my tale to tell. If Councilor Eris or his wife won't speak of the troubles his family has had to deal with in recent weeks, maybe you can ask Veya—if and when you find her.
Well, within reason. And Veya would do the same for us. That's why we're helping her. She really is a terrific person.

She ran away because her father refused to give her a straight answer. She suspects he was involved in Ulran's disappearance—or that he at least knows more than he's willing to say.\n\nIs it any wonder Veya decided to take matters into her own hands?

I'm sure Councilor Eris's intentions are good. He loves his daughter. Wants her back safe and sound.\n\nBut what about what Veya wants? Her brother home safe, her father's honesty, the House looking out for its people and not just its precious honor.
Oh, him? No one special. Just the leader of this particular band of mad cultists. His name was on the writ, so I had to end him.\n\nIt's what I do, after all, and I do it so well!

Outsiders? Is her father really that desperate?\n\nLook, tell Eris that Veya's safe and you'll see her soon. But no more outsiders. If my organization gets skittish, they'll return to the shadows and take Veya with them. We'll only deal with you.

That was her decision, not mine. Veya's good with a blade and tracks like a Nord ranger. She's a natural at this and it gives me a chance to keep an eye on her.\n\nSo now I'm her mentor and she's my apprentice. I wouldn't have it any other way.

She won't meet with me? No, I suppose she's not ready for that quite yet.\n\nAs for Veya's brother, that was all the doing of the Redoran Council. I'm not allowed to discuss the details. But he's still alive, if that's what Veya is worried about.

Naryu's back in town? She's as stubborn as Veya. Very well. No other outsiders. Although I can't dismiss the mercenaries that Captain Brivan employs.\n\nHouse Redoran is my life, as is Veya. I'll do everything in my power to see her home safely.

Who's Sotha Sil? That's like asking who are Vivec and Almalexia! They are the Tribunal—the Living Gods of the Dunmer.\n\nSotha Sil is the architect of time and the binder of Oblivion. If you want to know more, we can talk after we've finished.

Here. This should explain everything. Sort of. It's a map. We change locations every other day, for security reasons. Just in case it falls into the hands of House Redoran or someone else with an ax to grind with our organization.

Never had to use a map before? Amateurs! This one leads to a key to one of our safe-houses. And another map.\n\nThe first map? It depicts a particular town. Kind of like this one, hint, hint. The rest? You'll have to figure that out on your own.
An enemy of old, yes, but not the one that Vivec presumes.

Of course! As I said, the Tribunal consists of our three Living Gods—Vivec, Almalexia, and Sotha Sil. They lead us in spiritual matters and rule over Dunmer society as God-Monarchs of the Dark Elves.\n\nI serve Vivec, but honor the entire Tribunal.

Unfortunately, no. The Dunmer Houses bow to the Tribunal, but the savage Ashlanders refuse to acknowledge their divinity. The heretics never allowed themselves to be assimilated into the Great Houses. Instead, they hold to primitive superstitions.

Don't be so eager, my darling. It reveals too much about your ultimate intentions.\n\nBut yes, Veya would very much like to meet with you. You intrigue her. And your connection to her father could prove beneficial—once she knows she can trust you.

Redoran records. House officials keep track of everything! Incidents, commendations, births and deaths—whether important or mundane, they detail it all in their registry.\n\nVeya believes the registry contains information about her brother Ulran.

Don't sound so offended. You had to know your hands were going to get dirty eventually. You are dealing with assassins and politicians, after all.\n\nThe local keeper of records, Lord Drono, is away, so security at his townhouse should be light.

If you haven't guessed yet, the phenomenon interferes with Lord Vivec's power in unusual ways. It will be safer for everyone if I perform the ritual by using the Blessing Stone instead of drawing on my lord's personal store of energy.

She asked you to—an outlander? Isn't it enough she stuck me up here to guard the flame indefinitely, but now she's looking for help outside the house guard?\n\nAh, what else can I expect after what happened the other night?
So direct, you are. It makes my tongue wither and the answers dry up in my mouth.\n\nGo and bother someone else with your parching questions.
They're unique.\n\nSelective breeding's nothing new in the egg-trade. Some breedsmen focus on increased yield, while others focus on strength and longevity. Drovos wanted the best of everything.

Yes, I suppose we rushed right past introductions.\n\nI'm Ridena Devani, sub-Tamrielic naturalist. I oversee mining practices for House Hlaalu, ensuring that the kwama aren't exposed to undue risk from disease, starvation, or parasitic infestations.

They were promising, at first. Kwama are hardy creatures, but they still fall prey to the droops and parasitic mites. It's not unheard of to lose entire colonies to disease. Breeding in resistances made sense.\n\nIt was a mistake, clearly.

Unnatural? Emphatically yes. Nature couldn't produce kwama like this—not without gross interference.\n\nI can't stress this enough—if this breed spreads beyond Matus-Akin, we are in for an environmental catastrophe. So please, make haste.

A combination of classical breeding and alchemy. Mad science, if you will.\n\nNo one doubts Drovos's brilliance, but his methods are ghastly. Guiding a species toward specific traits takes years of work. Generations. But that's too slow for Drovos.

Well that is a surprise. I do hope this isn't some cheap forgery, for your sake.\n\nAh. Some kind of merged tonal prism. A lively one too. Fascinating. I do hope that fool Otheri didn't damage it. He's almost as clumsy as you.

Vehk's head, do you still labor under the delusion that you have some power in this place? Bah—it's hardly worth discussing. I've grown tired of our little chats.\n\nYou completed the task I set before you. You can have your lizard back.
I am sorry you got tangled up in all this. I should have been more careful. Or at least more patient.
We Telvanni are always wary of each other. But we also help each other, if there is benefit in it. I just played my hand too quickly. I am glad you weren't hurt.

That is regrettable. Eoki will be angry when he learns of it. He was already upset about the Khajiiti slaves you returned.\n\nThere is often the danger of others being hurt, when one is striving for knowledge or climbing the ranks of House Telvanni.

Drovos possesses a keen intellect, but no restraint. Too much Telvanni in him, I suspect. He has no allies, no official connections—only the work.\n\nIn truth, this isn't his first transgression. He's been a pen-stroke away from death more than once.

They don't know what he's done, and there's no time to tell them. The new queen could hatch any minute!\n\nDrovos also hired a company of mercenaries to protect him. Small-minded ruffians called the Rumblegarde. They're the brutes that chased me out!
Keep it down! We don't want to attract undue attention.\n\nBut what happened? I thought I was supposed to go to the drop? You didn't come all this way just to give me my reward, did you?

I have no idea. That's why we're sending you. I suggest you start at the inn. Secrets get spilled along with the drinks in such places.\n\nThe miners may know something as well. I've heard that House Redoran has issued some kind of proclamation.
The young woman who works with the grocer? I doubt the Tribunal would ask her to do something so reckless. Do you have any proof other than her word?

My brother, Chodala, is the Ashkhan of our tribe and I am his ambassador. I act as a go-between among the tribes. Chodala wants to unite the Dunmer and calmly end the era of the bickering Houses. He hopes to convince the tribes to follow his lead.

No, of course not. I care deeply for Eoki. I want to help him, but I can't save everyone.\n\nI serve House Telvanni. I am Telvanni. He must understand that the House traditions may bend, but they will not break. I've never seen him so angry.
And ALMSIVI is the ending of words. I'm yours to command.

I certainly hope not, but if he's lost faith in our plan, anything's possible.\n\nEoki won't listen to me, but he might still heed your counsel. Would you talk to him? The magisters will only tolerate so much defiance. If he makes another attempt ….
Answer the following questions or fail this test.\n\nDescribe the driving goal of House Redoran?

No Saxhleel reaches for a branch beyond their grasp, but all the waiting, all the compromises …. My patience rushes down river.\n\nMy companions and I must get a message to the Ropefish. Will you help?
House Redoran's outlook on life can be summed up as …?
House Redoran most strongly believes in the following institution.
An impressive display. You may enter the Redoran vault.
Your honor is found wanting and you do not understand the values of House Redoran. This vault shall remain off-limits to the likes of you.
And what does the deputy governor want to blame me for this time?

Not only did I get a sheet of the government's fancy parchment, I saw an unfinished report that seemed important. It proclaimed that there wasn't any slaver activity at Firemoth Island and the patrols were better off moving farther up the coast.
Your answers do not satisfy the tests of House Redoran. For this reason, you may not enter this vault.

That's odd. We haven't done a search of Firemoth Island since Governor Omellian declared that the House Guard was better used patrolling farther up the coast.\n\nAnd these parchment sheets definitely match. This is very disturbing ….
Ulran was exiled? That can't be right. He's an exemplary officer and a good man. Plus, he's the son of a councilor! Why in Oblivion would House Redoran banish one of their brightest stars?

I can see that. There has to be more to the story, but I'm not sure how we get it.\n\nStill, you proved you could be trusted and you admirably performed this task, so I suppose I should let you meet with Veya now.

There's an abandoned cave along the coast. It's in the swamp and smells like rot, which makes it the perfect place to hide.\n\nVeya's supposed to wait inside, but she's bored. I know she's been sneaking out. You'll find her in the cave or just outside.

Ah. It was during one of his many escape attempts.\n\nI was cleaning Master Otheri's tableware when Eoki burst through the kitchen door, dragging his chains behind him. He threw open the window and started to climb through it … then he saw me.

The history of the ruins have always been a mystery to my people. I can tell you no more than our own eyes will see. You will meet with exiles when you first enter, but I doubt they have found a way to control the constructs found deeper within.

Some Ashlanders farm the land, others hunt. My tribe harvested Nchuleft for parts and tools of value. Through trade we were able to make a living this way. \n\nNow that the exiles have hold of the ruins I'm not sure what we'll do next.

Before the attack we had already gathered items for shipment. I believe these particular pieces are of great value, and I hope selling them will get my tribe back on their feet. \n\nThe task may be dangerous, but it is our only chance to move on.

There's an old alchemist's proverb. "No reaction is ever so forceful as the mixing of opposing components." A mouthful, I know, but it fits.\n\nEoki and I occupy different poles on the same sphere. He keeps me grounded. I keep him safe.

He hesitated—even smiled. You don't see Marsh slaves smile much. Certainly not when they're being chased by nix-hounds.\n\nThey dragged him off and threw him in the dry-box. He told me he'd spend a year in there if it meant seeing me again.

We can discuss the distraction soon. First, we cast the lure and hook the fish.\n\nGo to the Inn and look for an Orc named Atarga. Approach her, say "Vassamsi Mine," and give her this payment. Deal only with Atarga. Hist protect you.
Ask what you wish, but speak quickly. I feel the slavemaster's eyes on me.

It is a forgetting place, where the noblest slaves labor until they die.\n\nThat beast, Gothren, hires thugs and murderers to guard it. They whip, and kick, and curse without restraint. Without mercy. We aim to free those slaves.

If I were, we would not have met. No one ever leaves Vassamsi. Even so, some of my friends are imprisoned there.\n\nI thought if Sun-in-Shadow freed me quickly, I could snatch them up on the way out of Vvardenfell. Now I see that she does not care.
They have a good reputation for getting the job done, as long as you have the gold to pay. Bothamul asks a high price, but we have few choices.

We pooled our resources. Many small fish can feed a whale, yes?  \n\nThe Telvanni see us as beasts—almost too stupid to push a broom. We use that to our advantage. I never thought I would be a thief, but given the circumstance, I feel no remorse.

There was a time when that made a difference, but now it does not. My spines wilt at the idea of leaving her, but she does not understand me.\n\nSlave-born Lukiul cannot hear the Hist. She does not know me. She does not even know herself.

Didn't we cover this? Let me refresh your memory. Lord Vivec suffers stoically as his divine energy drains away. Neither my administrations nor his defenses have been sufficient to plug the hole, so we've isolated him to keep panic to a minimum.

If we knew for certain, we wouldn't be sending you to make a deal with a heretical Ashlander, now would we?\n\nChodala must have something to do with Vivec's energy loss, but the how and why remain a mystery. That's why I must examine that staff.

Experience, outlander, experience.\n\nI have seen the Dunmer rage against the gods at the least provocation. When they realize that Vivec is ill, that his powers are failing, they'll weep and gnash their teeth like frightened children.

They try not to think about them at all.\n\nThe Ashlanders are savages! They refuse to acknowledge the supremacy of Lord Vivec and the Tribunal, instead putting their faith in the despicable Daedra. They're heretics, pure and simple.

Somewhere between certain and apprehensive? The Telvanni respect all clever schemes and love to barter. This little intrigue will prove my worth, I know it.\n\nThen again, she could just try to take the relic by force.
Run? Telvanni magisters wield magicks that put Julianos to shame.\n\nOf course, you're quite the hero in your own right. Hopefully it doesn't come to that.

Atarga's drunk as Sanguine on Sundas. Won't get nothing but puke and bad jokes out of her.\n\nShe told me why she was here. Dragging a few slaves cross the border, ay? You give me the payment and I'll let the boss know. Savvy?

Fine. Lug that gold to Bothamul yourself. No skin off my tusks. Camp's near Gothren's place. Tel Aruhn. I'll even mark your map, seeing as we're fit to be partners soon. \n\nKeep your gob shut about Atarga getting sauced, ay? One headache's enough.

The people don't handle the infirmities of their deities very well. Especially when those infirmities could foreshadow Red Mountain's eruption or portend the moonlet's fall from the sky.\n\nOnce such fear ignites, it spreads like wildfire.
No! Yes. Forgive me. I just couldn't keep pacing around the house, gnawing my claws.\n\nIs Eoki all right? What did he say? He's not planning to do something foolish, is he?

Vassamsi? You mean Gothren's slave-prison? What in the name of—? I know he distrusts me now, but you can't let him do this. If the truth of our relationship gets back to the Council ….\n\nI'll go to the mine. Maybe I can talk him out of this.

I see. Well that's that, I guess. Once he cools down, I'll plead my case again.\n\nI can't fight the House traditions all at once. But perhaps, with time and effort …. I just need more time. He must understand that.
Indisposed? Fancy talk for drunk as a boiled owl, right? Mauloch's jawbone. She loves her drink, but she always stays sober on the job.\n\nSomething stinks here. Maybe we should call this off.
By answering a few simple questions, such as this one.\n\nHouse Indoril holds what cherished institution to be most precious?
According to House Indoril, Dunmer culture must …?
With regard to outsiders, how does House Indoril stand?
You show a deep and abiding understanding of the values of House Indoril. You may enter this vault.
You obviously have no understanding of House Indoril or its values. This vault isn't for the likes of you.
You have failed this test of House Indoril's values and beliefs. You may not enter this vault.
House Dres holds to the ancient tradition of Daedra and ancestor worship, as well as to the cherished institution of what economic system?

Feel free to wait in the council chamber. We will rule on this matter soon.\n\nOne other thing. Some of my personal correspondence went missing recently. If that ever happens again, the Morag Tong will hear of it. I trust we understand each other.
Oh, right! Naryu mentioned something about that.\n\nLook, I can't wait to hear what you learned, but the swamp is crawling with mercenaries. There's a cave to the northeast. We can talk there.
Why is House Dres crucial to Morrowind's survival?
How does House Dres view the Dunmer role in Tamriel?
You demonstrate a clear understanding of the values of House Dres. You may enter this vault.
You do not understand the values or beliefs of House Dres. You may not enter this vault.
You answered one or more question incorrectly. You do not understand the values of House Dres and may not enter this vault.
Unfortunately, there's a mob of those beast-people between here and the cave. I was going to try to sneak past them, but every time I get too close I think one of them catches my scent.

You're going to tackle that mob of fur and claws? I'm impressed! Meet me at the cave when you're finished. I think we have a lot to talk about.\n\nOh, and try not to get killed. I really want to know what you came all this way to tell me.

Good. I should ask for a lot more than this. Vassamsi makes the inside of a wamasu look homey by comparison. But a deal's a deal, eh? Tell Eoki we'll be there as agreed.\n\nThe mine's east of here. Just steer clear of Gothren's thugs, all right?
Quite simple, really. Answers the following questions correctly. That's all there is to it.\n\nThe goal of every House Hlaalu member is to …?
House Hlaalu believes the best approach to negotiations is to …?
Success is achieved when a member of House Hlaalu does … what?
You do know House Hlaalu. Impressive. This vault has now been opened to you.
I'm sorry, but you must be thinking of some other house. This vault shall not be made available to you.
No, that can't be right.\n\nUlran's honorable and noble. He's a model soldier. What could he have possibly done to warrant being banished?
Your answers were wrong in so many, many ways. For that reason, this vault shall remain closed.

I know the tribe that Ulran liked to help. Brought them supplies and such. He'd go and visit their camp whenever our father wasn't paying attention. Will you go with me to talk to them?\n\nWait, someone's coming!

What? My brother has always been interested in the Ashlanders. Even showed them a kindness the rest of the House doesn't approve of.\n\nBut for him to kill someone, especially one of his own soldiers, something terrible must have happened.
Yes, of course. I mean, eventually. We can talk about that later. Just let me bask in this moment, all right?

The back tunnels. Better than heading out the front door and right into the main contingent of Redoran troops.\n\nCouncilor Eris brought additional soldiers from town. He's intent on getting his daughter and he may have the numbers to do it.

You recovered the lost genealogies of the Great Houses? Why, these date back to before the War of the First Council. Remarkable!\n\nYou have done a great service for this library and all of Morrowind, outlander.
Perhaps, but I must remain impartial. If someone else reveals the flaws in Chodala's claims by comparing him to the Failed Incarnates, that might do the trick.

First, we must deal with the guards—especially the ones who linger near the entrance. If they raise the alarm, the slavemaster will descend on us like a hungry hackwing.\n\nRihnissi thinks we should knock them out. Azri suggests we show no mercy.

Rihnissi acquired a crate of powder bombs. Toss one near a guard and they should fall unconscious. Killing less guards might lessen the magisters' fury, making it easier to escape, but who knows?\n\nFree our friends and watch out for the guard captain.

Azri spent many long weeks in the dry-box beneath Tel Aruhn. Some of his closest friends died here in Vassamsi. His spines bristle with thoughts of revenge. I do not blame him.\n\nSlay the guards, free our people, and watch out for the guard captain.
You—you'd do that for me? Thanks. I guess.\n\nBut what can you possibly do against all those soldiers? My father brought the whole damn army with him this time!

Once I find Ulran and make sure he's all right, I'll meet with my father. But that meeting will be on my terms, not his.\n\nAnd tell him to call off his soldiers or I might change my mind. That should buy us some time.

Clever. Tell my father whatever he wants to hear. That might actually work!\n\nAfterward, meet me at the Ashlander camp to the south. My brother would often visit that particular tribe. It's as good a place as any to start.
I also said that the captain has his own resources. The Warclaws report to Brivan, not me.\n\nLook, we're all just trying to get my daughter home safely. Now, tell me what Veya's thinking.
It was a gamble, I admit. An opportunity I couldn't let slip away. You won't make me feel guilty about trying to find my daughter.\n\nSo, where and when will Veya meet with me?

Very well. We'll do this her way. Veya can be as stubborn as her mother sometimes.\n\nBut tell my daughter that my patience won't last forever. Next time, I expect Veya to be with you—or I might just let Captain Brivan do this his way.

My brother often visited this camp. Took me along a couple of times. It used to be such a vibrant place, so full of life.\n\nI know House Redoran wants to expand along the western coast, but I never expected they'd set the Warclaws loose like this.

I really want to help, but Naryu won't hear of it! "We don't get our hands dirty unless there's a writ attached," as she's so fond of reminding me.\n\nWe'll hang around and wait for you to find something before we move in.

If Ulran was here, he'd never stand for the Warclaws invading the camp. He told me the Ashlanders were the same as you and I. Different beliefs don't necessarily make people bad.\n\nWe need to see if we can find out what happened here.
Ah, Ulran the exile. He disgraced his family and lost his status but remained true to his heart.\n\nUlran is here. He tried to stand against the Redorans just as they detained me within this yurt.

I assume they dragged him off to the mine. Along with most of the tribe who refused to let those Tribunal dogs walk all over us. Or should I say Tribunal cats in this instance?\n\nBe wary. The mine will be as protected as the camp—maybe even more so.

It's a small hole in the ground, but it served us well until the Redorans and their Warclaws arrived. Now they toss my people inside and lock the door.\n\nWarclaw Irgazzar carries the key, but there is a spare in the supply yurt.

I suppose anything could happen in the heat of the moment, but to kill a Redoran—even an exiled one—that's presumptuous even for the Warclaws. I wonder if Eris knows about this?\n\nI'm not sure how Veya's going to get her answers now.

I've seen these before. They use them in Eastmarch to record and send important messages. They're expensive and as rare as a sober Nord, but Ulran was always attracted to the contrivances of other cultures.\n\nShall we see what it has to say?

I arrived to find one of my soldiers arguing with the Ashlanders. He spat at them. Called them savages. When one of the Ashlanders objected, my soldier drew his sword.\n\nBefore I could intervene, my soldier's blade struck him down.

I ordered the soldier to stand down, but he ignored me and stepped toward the second Ashlander. I killed my own soldier. I had to.\n\nBefore I knew it, I was dragged before the Redoran Council and exiled. I never even got to say farewell to my sister.

I believe I was set up for this fall, but I don't know by who. I came to this camp for shelter, but House Redoran's reach grows ever longer.\n\nNow Captain Brivan's here. I'm going to talk to them. Just in case, I made this stone for my sister, Veya.
I didn't say that. I'm just not sure how to proceed. We're entering dangerous waters here, going up against House Redoran. And we don't even have a writ to protect us!
