I'm going to take Veya and head back to our safehouse in Balmora. They found our cave, but the abandoned basement is still secure.\n\nAfter that, I'm not sure. The Morag Tong has rules. If I break them, I'll have to deal with the consequences.

What are you implying? Can't a person do something nice to help out an ally every now and again?\n\nOh, who am I kidding? I hate playing the messenger! Haven't you ever done something you hate because it was the right thing to do?
Then you understand what I'm talking about. Being noble. Doing the honorable thing.\n\nIt can be a real pain in the arse, but a favor given becomes a favor returned. Eventually.

Well, not all of us can afford to be so cold and heartless. I'd say I envy you, but that would just reward you for bad behavior.\n\nWhy are you still talking to me? Don't you have a map to puzzle out?

Well look at you! You're a practical genius!\n\nLook, Naryu seems to trust you, so I suppose I have to trust you, too. But that's a powerful secret you've been given. Betray us and you'll find my blade in your back. Unless Naryu kills you first.

As I understand it, the Morag Tong made mistakes in the past. Grew too arrogant. We had to lay low for more than a century. Now we're taking select contracts, working to reestablish our reputation.\n\nIt's not our fault most of them concern Redoran.

The other houses have used us to take Redoran down a peg or two of late. To be frank, for all their vaunted honor, the house cries foul whenever someone gets the better of them.\n\nOur status is tenuous enough without Redoran's constant harassment.

Veya would face too many temptations here in Balmora. Friends, favorite places, familiar sights and sounds. Not to mention the proximity to all things House Redoran. Even the most thick-headed House Guard would eventually stumble over her.

Oh, don't thank me, hero. As long as you're useful and don't betray us, then we're engaged in a mutually beneficial arrangement.\n\nCross us in any way, however, and you'll never see my blade before it plunges into your heart.

Let me see that. What's that crazy mage need this time?\n\nHmm. I suppose you could find a manual clockwork shaft in the Nchuleft ruins. But I'd avoid that place if I were you. If the roof doesn't collapse, the constructs will rip you apart.

That mage is a menace! Oh, he always paid well, but the places he asked me to go—each was more dangerous than the last. And if I had to hear about the Great Gear one more time ….\n\nFor my own health and sanity, I had to break ties with Barilzar.

If you insist.\n\nDeep in the ruins churns a big machine. When I was there, it sputtered and vibrated, collapsing parts of the ceiling. Lava and rock fell everywhere. You need to get past that and some nasty constructs to retrieve the item.

Barilzar! He's the reason I'm a shattered man, doomed to become a cowering sheep like the rest of these pilgrims! Oh, all right. Let me see that.\n\nHmm. Arkngthunch-Sturdumz. You can find a sonance generator there—after you deal with the steam trap.

Look, once I heard the crash along the shore, it was all I could do to get moving and raise the alarm.\n\n<<1>> loves to loiter near the lighthouse. Maybe she noticed something. If you're intent on doing our job, you should talk to her.

Findun sent a barrel of his finest ale for Watch Captain Bethes's birthday. Powerful stuff. One cup and we could barely keep our eyes open. The entire regiment was knocked on its collective arse. When I came to my senses, I saw the fire had gone out.

The cursed contraption! I almost had it figured out when a ghost floated up to me. No problem, I think, but then it enters a centurion! Ghost machines! No sane Nord can fight ghost machines! I dropped my notes and ran as fast as I could.

Not just ghosts! Ghosts that possessed Dwarven machines! I'm through working for that crazy old mage and his clockwork monstrosities!\n\nBut if you want to get past the steam trap, find my notes and follow the directions.

He did, did he? Let me see that list.\n\nHmm. Well, the crazy old mage always said there were no coincidences. The inversion conduit. I saw one in Galom Daeus—right before I barely escaped from those damned vampires.

Now you insult me? I'll have you know I can take care of myself!\n\nSince you mentioned it, I have noticed that my favorite pond has become somewhat stagnant. I bet if we had some of Findun's Special Blend, my throat would moisten right back up.
No! There's no need to involve the governor's deputy. Or the house guard. When they start breathing down my neck, my scales shrivel right up!\n\nI did notice someone near the lighthouse that night.

Because the mage wanted to send me to the far side of Vvardenfell and I need to remain here. I'm not going anywhere until I make the Berne clan pay for what it did to my brother.\n\nIf you can kill some of the bastards, that'll be a start.

Eager to become cattle for the bloodsuckers? The Berne clan killed my brother, damn their eyes!\n\nThe item you seek was in the manufactory, but you'll need a control rod to get a dwarven spider to unlock it for you.

Already? Let me see! Oh, it's beautiful! I love working for the Tribunal. It's so much better than trying to earn a living as a thief in Vivec City.\n\nBut where's your helmet? I've never seen an Ordinator out of uniform before.

Oh, right. We're not supposed to talk about Ordinators and the Tribunal in such a public place. But it feels good to be doing holy work for a change! And such a simple task, snuffing out the lighthouse flame.\n\nI mean, ALMSIVI is the ending of words.

Not the office. He keeps it in his private quarters, accessed through the guard house.\n\nBut I'd never suggest that you sneak into his quarters and steal a blank sheet of his special parchment. That would be against the law. Do you understand me?

Hmm, this is disturbing. This parchment feels just like the sheets that Governor Omellian special orders from High Rock.\n\nI'm going to need you to acquire another sample from the governor's office. It's the only way to be certain.

Not if I don't want him to know I suspect that he's working with the slavers. Or the Tribunal, though I still consider that to be some sort of fabrication.\n\nNo, if I alert him too soon, he'll just cover his tracks.
You fool! The governor might miss a single sheet of blank parchment, but his dead son's helmet? There's no way I can overlook this breach of the law.
Complication? What kind of complication?\n\nI ordered my soldiers to stand down and let you do things your way, but instead of results you bring me excuses!
No. That's not possible. My son was banished, ordered to leave Vvardenfell and never return. Why would he disobey me and go to those savages?
Veya was with you? And you left her out there? By the Three, everything is unraveling no matter how hard I try to maintain control.\n\nI need you to do something else for me if you would, outlander.

You're a Dunmer. Do you not know the story?\n\nThe First Ashkhans were the fathers of the four great tribes. They brought the Velothi people together to kill Skar. The tribes often quarrel, but here they're family. I wish the Houses had such a custom.
Of course. I am asking you to do things and forgetting my manners. I tend to get caught up in my work. Ask away.

Part of the fun is the suspense.  \n\nMenaldinion was ingratiating when he first came here. I realize now he was getting a lot of information out of me. Suffice it to say he also revealed some interesting facts about himself too.

The study of alchemy covers the simple to the complex, the useful to the debilitating. It can be used in cooking or healing but it can also be use in war. Poisons are part of alchemy. I don't dabble, I prefer to be useful, not murderous.

Goodness, I thought everyone knew that. They are the ones that grow the widest tops, and tend to have a smoother skin. They are all over Vvardenfell and Deshaan. The moss I need is not common. Look for wide topped parasols. The moss likes the shade.

I've found some a bit west of here, on the mushrooms that grow closer to water.  \n\nOh, and do be careful. The strange scent of the moss is attractive to several types of creatures, not all of them benign.

Is the bull sure it can bed the betty? No, but by all accounts we'll be better off with Sunna'rah in our hands and away from Chodala.\n\nThat won't be possible, however, as long as the Ashlander remains impervious to every attack.

The female Ashlander? Well, if that wasn't enough of a reason, remember that she's also Chodala's sister. Blood sings to blood, as the Warrior-Poet so elegantly put it.\n\nBe wary of that one, outlander. She'll stab you in the back, mark my words.

Vivec loves this land, and the land loves him in return. He's always had a special bond with Vvardenfell. Is it so hard to believe that Red Mountain reflects his suffering?\n\nBeyond that, there's also Baar Dau, the moonlet that floats above us.

Yes. Though "becoming" is a clumsy word for it. Every daughter of Veloth has worth. When we learn to speak with our water-tongue and read the truth in the stones, we also learn the truth of our hearts.\n\nThe truth is we have been wise all along.
That's an odd request. But who am I to question the Tribunal?\n\nI can reach the governor's quarters through the guard house, but I'll need someone to distract the guards.
No. Too risky. My only option is to make this appear to be a common burglary. \n\nYour role in this affair ends here. You're under arrest.
Try not to mention that when the guards haul you away.\n\nI'm sorry, but you'll be better off in a cell until all this is over.
Appealing to my love of the law to bargain for a pardon? Contemptible but also extremely logical.\n\nI trust you don't have any other major crimes to confess to?

The Argonian vagrant? She's a harmless beggar who's as much a part of Seyda Neen as the docks or the lighthouse.\n\nI doubt it, but she might have seen something we missed. Now let me get back to it before the deputy governor gives me another demerit.

What I think doesn't matter. We need evidence. But we also need to launch a rescue. Slavery is illegal in Pact territory. It's time to visit Firemoth Island.\n\nHopefully, somewhere along the way we'll find more proof of <<1>>'s ties to all this.
The governor needed me here. Remind Salvi that he's still in charge here. And he trusts me. She should consider that as she conducts this netch hunt of hers.
You do that! Now move along before I arrest you for loitering and bothering a house guard.
Leave Vvardenfell? If you think that's for the best. Let's see …. I know, I'll go to Mournhold! I always wanted to see the Tribunal Temple! What an excellent idea!\n\nALMSIVI is the ending of words!
Attack before the soldiers have been assembled? That's not a prudent course of action. We need to muster our forces, make plans and contingencies, unlock the armory—what was that?

With my help, the probability calculates in your favor. But you must keep moving. The Hound won't dawdle … unless he comes upon an interesting smell. Or a tree.\n\nSince we know Barbas's ultimate destination, I can open routes he can't access.

Only one logical place. To the atelier where Sotha Sil conducted his study of divine energy. Sunna'rah would have sent the stolen power there. It's not far.\n\nWhat Barbas and his master want with Vivec's energy, though, remains unclear.

Most of them. Might be a random contraption or a wandering factotum still out there. And if Barbas smuggles in more Daedra, the other defenses will become active.\n\nClear a path while I open the route, then I'll catch up and join you.

Lord Vivec's intervention stopped the moonlet from crashing into the city. He holds it above us by strength of will. But as he weakens, so too does the power that keeps the rock afloat.\n\nIf Vivec's energy wanes further, it would spell disaster.

Anything that could prove it's my family's tomb. Seals, engravings, anything.\n\nYou could also try talking to the spirits. The tablet I found referred to someone named Dranoth—a family patriarch. Perhaps you'll find him inside. Three protect you.

Would you? What a relief.\n\nTake this sash. It bears the Hleran family crest. If the spirits lurking in the tomb are of Hleran blood, they'll recognize it. It might not keep them from attacking, but it should convince them that your motives are pure.

I know Veya wants answers, but this is my job. There are rules, especially where the lords of the Great Houses are concerned.\n\nThere might be a way to deal with this, though, provided you're willing to help.

First, don't kill any Redorans. That's a violation of my writ and could have serious consequences for both of us.\n\nSecond, you sneak around and search for anything that pertains to Ulran's exile while I figure out how to deal with the councilor.

I could, but I won't pour five-year-old flin into a cracked decanter. No offense. Suffice it to say, they're fairly common as far as Dwemer components go.\n\nUse the list and talk to my former hirelings. I'll build the device the moment you return.

Yes. Tell him that Ald'ruhn was, is, and forever shall be our home. So long as my house lives in exile, the spirits that haunt this tomb shall never know peace.\n\nDrelyth must claim his share of this land.

At long last, yes.\n\nI gazed through an ocean of screams and … well, I won't frighten you with the particulars. Suffice it to say that I saw many terrible things, but I think I've located the other oracles.
My first visions were of … wait. What's that?
Oh, you do, do you? And why in Oblivion would I tell you anything about that?

Everyone knew Ulran cared more about those savages than he did for members of his own house. But what does it matter who tested his loyalty? He failed and paid the price for his poor choices. Now, tell me what this is about before I get really angry.

Ulran's dead? That's news to me. All I know is that Ulran was tested and found wanting. He decided that the life of an Ashlander was more important than that of a Redoran soldier. We stripped him of his rank and banished him from Vvardenfell.

Or he's trying to hide something. The letter mentioned an intact squad sent to scout the old fort. You need to get out there and see what those soldiers know before Brivan gives them new orders and they disappear.
Interesting. I never suspected that the outcasts were disciplined enough to keep records such as this.\n\nOh no. I can't believe my brother would be so … brazen.

It means that Chodala really has changed. With his newfound powers and rising ambitions, I fear what he plans for the tribes.\n\nI suppose you have a right to know what I'm talking about. Take this. I found it among my brother's possessions.

I suppose. She's probably pulled tight as a bow string waiting to hear something. Go talk to Veya while I present my writ to the authorities.\n\nI can't wait to see the look on the Redoran magister's face when I tell him what his councilor was up to.

What good is that going to do? They won't speak to us. House before family and all that. Believe me, I'm more than familiar with Redoran honor.\n\nStill, I suppose I know a few ways to get people to talk ….

More rules? I thought we were beyond those kinds of limitations?\n\nLook, I need to figure out who's responsible for Ulran's death. House councilors, Redoran soldiers, Ashlanders—whoever it is, they need to pay.

It was never meant to be an attack. I sent Captain Brivan to clear land that already belonged to House Redoran. The Ashlanders were given an opportunity to depart. The situation didn't have to turn violent. Those damn savages should have just left!

House Redoran has been slowly expanding in that direction for years. We claimed that area almost a year ago, but we were forced to temporarily abandon it when a massive ash storm hit. Before we could return, the Ashlanders moved in.

Redoran depends on that land for hunting and resources. The Ashlanders are like a plague of insects. They sweep into an area, take everything, and move on. We couldn't allow them to do that here. So I sent Captain Brivan to convince them otherwise.

The captain serves House Redoran with honor and dedication. He's out doing his job. \n\nIf Brivan had anything to do with my son's death, he would have reported it to me. He'd have no reason to keep such news from me and the other councilors.

I'll speak to Brivan when he returns. But understand, the captain operated under my orders. He's an exemplary soldier and an upstanding member of the House.\n\nLike me, everything he does is for the betterment of House Redoran.

It's unusual, but not unheard of. True, most writs taken out against the Houses target low to mid-ranking officials. The Grand Master is cautious when it comes to accepting such a high-profile writ.\n\nApparently, though, this target has been very bad.

Councilor Dolvara has been conspiring with House Dres to promote the slave trade and avoid scrutiny by Redoran and Pact officials. She played a dangerous but profitable game and her coffers were overflowing—until someone noticed.

I'm not privy to the laborious investigations that took place. In cases like these, though, the target usually becomes complacent and lets her guard down. She made a mess. Now I get to clean it up—for the good of Dunmer society.

That's the question, isn't it? It nags at us the way the Torchbug nags at the Brave Little Scrib in those children stories. Once we discover who Ulran's Torchbug is, we'll have a clearer understanding of why they set him up and why he had to die.

I'm not saying that. Accidents happen. But they certainly made sure Ulran was in the wrong place at the wrong time—both in Balmora and again in the Ashlander camp.\n\nIn addition to whatever you can find here, we should also talk to Captain Brivan.

Veya's my apprentice and I'll decide when she's ready to take on a mission. She's been through a lot, and her actions reflect on me and my status in the Morag Tong.\n\nShe may not appreciate it right now, but I'm trying to keep the both of us on track.

I'm afraid it's not as easy as that. I see a tangle of futures—a swirling mass of action and consequence. Every now and again, though, a specific moment strikes like a thunderbolt. Moments like this.\n\nSome dark entity stalks the oracles of Azura.

They have to be. My order came this close to being eliminated. It's only recently that we've started to make a comeback—and only in Dunmer territory.\n\nIf we can't control the actions of our members, we'll be hunted down and destroyed for sure.

That's how it works. Her actions are my actions. Veya goes out and executes three writs, I share the credit and get praised for training my apprentice.\n\nOn the other hand, if she kills someone without a writ, the Morag Tong takes both our heads.

Yes. Servants of the Twilight Queen. My friends and I decipher visions of the future for other votaries of Azura. Unfortunately, something is abducting us one by one.\n\nBring this crystal to Pariah Abbey. Our Rose Mother will tell you the rest.

All the time.\n\nMakes dinner dates interesting, I can tell you. One moment we're speaking about the consistency of the soup, the next I'm fumbling with my spoon, rambling about talking candlesticks and trees made of blood.

I'm not sure. My parents thought me mad. Abandoned me on the streets of Wayrest at the tender age of eight.\n\nMercifully, the abbot of Pariah Abbey discovered my gifts and introduced me to the Twilight Queen. I achieved clarity. I have Azura to thank.

Two. Kanzin and Muz-Shah. Both powerful soothsayers in their own right.\n\nKanzin vanished a week ago, pruning his sugar canes. His fellow votaries told me that he showed no signs of distress. He simply walked out into the field and never came back.

Muz-Shah, an Argonian, disappeared just two days ago. He tends Azura's shrine in Black Marsh. It's a quiet affair with a simple shrine and very few acolytes.\n\nHe went out to light votary candles near the shrine and never returned.

Because you're anointed by fate. Or something close to fate. I stopped arguing the specifics years ago.\n\nThe Queen of Dawn and Dusk needs your help. Trust me, Azura's desires are hard to miss. She is … insistent. She'll speak to you, believe me.

She speaks the truth. The halls of Oblivion fill with whispers. Collusion. Conspiracy. I believe some of my fellow Princes seek to blind me.\n\nThey know how much I treasure my servants. They would steal what I hold most dear.

My enemies' servants likely use Void Keys. Powerful charms, capable of tearing small holes in the veil of Oblivion. They require Daedric essence to function.\n\nSlay any Daedra you find and claim their essence. A charged Void Key will open any pocket.

I cannot. The Princes' compact with Sotha Sil binds my hands. You must be the vessel of my wrath.\n\nI sense my oracles, adrift in the void. Imprisoned in pockets of Oblivion—hidden dimensions, only accessible through Nirn. You will rescue them.

Daedra cannot be killed, only banished. When you strike a mortal blow, their essence returns to Oblivion.\n\nThe crystal Rhea gave you captures that essence before it escapes. A prison, of sorts. Defeat any Daedra and the crystal will do the rest.

Long ago, my vulgar peer, Molag Bal, manifested himself in the town of Gil-Var-Delle and destroyed it utterly.\n\nIn response, the Dark Elf magus, Sotha Sil, gathered eight of the most powerful Princes to a summit in Coldharbour.
While you hunt Daedra and gather their essence, my ward, Rhea, will conjure up visions.

As you saw, hostility is second nature to the Red Exiles. We're here to negotiate, but they're no better than thieves and murderers. If they spot you in their camp, you'll need to defend yourself. It's unfortunate, but they'll leave you no choice.
No, that's not something I'm ready to talk about with an outsider. Perhaps after you prove your trustworthiness and willingness to help us, then we can discuss my brother in more detail.\n\nPerhaps.

We speak death for the enemies of the Ashlanders.\n\nThe Velothi people face threats on all sides. Beasts, Daedra, House scum. While the Zainab, and Ahemmusa, and Urshilaku pray and gather roots, we hunt and kill. We keep the Ashlanders safe.
The tribe shows mercy when it suits us. For example, you still have your tongue.\n\nThe Wastes do not suffer fools, n'wah. Nor do we.
We sing the truth songs. The truth of the three blasphemers, and the Daedra, and the Nerevarine. The Houses hate us most of all.

Because we do not forget the truth of Nerevar. We know that the Tribunal will pass like wood smoke—driven away by the raging winds of the Incarnate. Vehk, Sotha Sil, and the Mad Wife know this as well. They seek to silence us, but they always fail.

There is little to learn. We put on no airs—we have no taste for secrets. Only hard work matters.\n\nThe other tribes burden themselves with resentments and sour traditions. Not us. We speak little. Our labors speak for us.
Hunting, mining, droving … any task that brings prosperity to the tribe. Work brings abundance. Laziness brings death. That is the law of the Wastes.

We seek silence, and little else. The open path, a stiff breeze, the crunch of lava stone beneath our feet, the sighing heat of the fire river …. There is no greater wealth—no greater comfort. \n\nOutsiders bring nothing but noise and sorrow.

In their hearts? Yes. In their minds? No.\n\nThe other Ashlanders busy themselves with prophecy and war. Eyes always on the horizon and never on their feet. But that matters little. As long as they leave us alone, we remain content.

Such a place exists in Shadowfen—west of an encampment called Hei-Halai. Look for a great serpent's head, carved out of stone. Our enemies lurk in the caves beneath it.\n\nGo there and slaughter these beasts. My oracles will join you soon.

Dyzera must lead this wretched band of conspirators. The abductions, the Void Keys, the dead bandits—all her design. We know who she is, now it's just a matter of finding her.\n\nPerhaps we can bait her. Reacquiring these "gifts" might do the trick.
Kanzin, Muz-Shah, and I will gather here to prepare a gazing rite—a collaborative vision. If you manage to lure Dyzera out, we might catch of glimpse of what, or who, is driving her.

That's not our goal, but the tribes will defend themselves if necessary.\n\nNo, we hope to present a united front and show the Houses the folly of the path they've embarked upon. Turning away from our forefathers and god-ancestors has made them weak.

Well enough. Ulran and Veya used to sneak out to watch me train. I have a way with blades that fascinated them to no end. Eventually, a fondness developed between the three of us.\n\nAnd to think, I never even had a nix-hound growing up.

Anything's possible. But the Ulran I know holds honor above all else. I can't believe he'd do something so dishonorable that the House leaders would demand his exile.\n\nWe need to find out more about what happened.

It's not like personal relationships are against the rules, though I suppose they are sort of frowned upon.\n\nAnyway, my assignments always brought me back to Vvardenfell, so we were able to keep in touch and visit even as they grew older.

Veya's young, bored, and stubborn. That makes for a volatile combination. She wants fresh air and freedom. I can't blame her for that.\n\nI can blame her for assuming I'm not aware of her little excursions. I thought I trained her better than that.

Danger's a relative term. Especially when you're dealing with relatives.\n\nVeya can make her own decisions. If she wants to risk getting caught by House Redoran, that's on her head. Especially since she knows they've been searching that area.
My mercenaries have spotted Veya skulking about the northern portion of the swamp. Between my soldiers and Ferhara's Warclaws, the councilor's daughter will soon be home, safe and sound.

I suppose some bloodsuckers aren't too bad, but the Berne clan's nothing but monsters! They killed my brother!\n\nThe item you seek can be constructed in the manufactory, but you'll need a control rod to get a dwarven spider to build it for you.

Khajiit mercenaries of the highest order. For members of a lesser race, Ferhara's warriors are surprisingly effective.\n\nI employ them to bolster our forces. Between obligations to the Pact and other matters, House Redoran is spread thin of late.

I glorify her body and make a vessel of her mind. Do not trouble yourself. She will return, in time.\n\nYour true concern is these visions. My oracles perceive a holocaust, child. A Daedric storm the likes of which your mortal world has never seen.

We wait … and listen.\n\nPatience. A difficult concept for mortals, I know. Such short, beautiful, brutish lives you lead. For now, Dyzera lays dead and my oracles breathe free air. That should be enough for you.
As you say. Ferhara's Warclaws take their contract as seriously as you do, however. Get in their way and I can't guarantee your safety.
Oh! So you're going after them? That's great. That's great! Yes, anything I can do to help you!\n\nWhat do you want to know?
Don't you have better things to do than quote my religion at me?
Talk of gods makes my scales itch. If the Living Gods really cared, they wouldn't make me suffer. Now take your religious foolishness and peddle it someplace else.
That's something to do with the Tribunal, isn't it? I'm sorry, but I really try not to pay too much attention to the Dark Elves and their strange religion.
Three? Three! That's as many as Tirwin manages to find in a month, and she's perfect!

Ha! That's a good one! That Tribunal nonsense is almost as funny as some of the things I heard in Wrothgar.\n\nSay, if you want to get together later, I know a couple of bawdy stories that I'd love to share.
No! No, no, no, no. If mother found out, she'd never let <<1>> go free, not for any price!\n\nIt's an unreasonable sum, but the fact that she asked for red star shells might work in our favor.

I've been training a Nix-hound to help Tirwin, so she can spend more time with me instead of in that vile swamp.\n\nAside from the fetcher fly incident Nixxie's got a solid track record. I'm certain she won't let us down.
Oh, that's from the Dark Elf scriptures, isn't it? Enigmatic and beautiful.\n\nI've been trying to catch up on my reading, but I've been so busy, busy, busy.

Really, outlander, it's commendable that you're trying to learn our ways, but the words of the Tribunal just sound silly when you say them like that. I suggest you stick to sight-seeing and leave the religion to us.

He should have made a deal! What kind of rock-headed dunce tells the Camonna Tong to eat their own small clothes?\n\nThese aren't common hoods. The Tong will feed you to the slaughterfish for a hard glance, let alone insulting their mothers.

Mauloch knows.\n\nI mean, the Tong did have some ideas Khartag wasn't wild about. Upping the prices, chaining up the slaves en route, packing them into smaller ferries …. Khartag refused to even consider it. Great time to develop a conscience, eh?

Maybe. You'll have to ask him—provided he's not dead already.\n\nKhartag's a hard Orc to know. I always thought he was a stone-hearted businessman, but then some horker out in the Rift told me he was a big-time Covenant hero—so what do I know?

It's a syndicate—a crime family. Everyone owes them, from two-drake hood on up to house councilor.\n\nIf they put their thumb on a scale, you look away. If they tell you to pick something up, you snatch it up quick and thank them for the privilege.
So you're familiar with "The 36 Lessons of Vivec?" A fine series of books. I refer to them often for inspiration and guidance.
What? What did you say?\n\nI suggest you leave now, before I set the guards upon you.
Word of advice. Don't mention anything about the Tribunal to the governor. He's not happy with some recent rules and regulations that have come down from on high.
Trust me, "dangerous" is an understatement. I'd kick Mehrunes Dagon in the rocks before I'd talk back to the Camonna Tong.
I played dead. Performance of a lifetime, if you ask me. I guess those acting lessons weren't so useless after all.
My mother wanted to make sure I was well-rounded. I play a mean flute too.\n\nWait—why are we talking about this?

I hope you'll keep those deliberations brief. I'm opening the path now. When you stand ready to face Xykenaz, simply enter the portal.\n\nAnd don't worry, I'll make sure you have a way back on the other side. I always keep my promises.

One more thing. The back tunnels wind their way through territory that House Redoran recently acquired. We may run into some resistance, but it shouldn't be as bad as what's waiting outside the front of the cave.

Aha! The day is saved! No one will question who wears the crown in my court after this! I promised you a key role in the festivities today, and I'm a man of my word! \n\nI hereby entrust you with the honor of putting my royal prowess on display.
Go ahead. Ask your questions. Then head into the ruins. I'll be right behind you.

The tribes rejected him. Azura set her face against him. Now Chodala's seeking aid wherever he can find it. That makes him more desperate than I imagined—and more dangerous.\n\nWhy he decided to solicit Malacath, the God of Curses, I have no idea.

Malacath's an evil god, the Daedric Prince of curses and broken promises. Perhaps that's why Chodala has sought him out. The prophecy of the Nerevarine was Chodala's to fulfill before it was wrenched away from him.

It's true I have no love of the Tribunal. I also have no stomach for a war between my people and the Great Houses. Too much blood would be spilled to no good end.\n\nEven Azura proclaims that my brother must be stopped. I'll help you in any way I can.

Perhaps, but I don't think so. The Oathbreaker prefers a more direct approach. He isn't one to hide behind convoluted schemes and plots.\n\nStill, if Malacath agrees to support my brother, we'll have one more problem to deal with.
Chodala appealed to Malacath … but the God of Curses rebuked him.\n\nKilled us all … said Chodala already served … another ….
He went … deeper into the ruins … into Malacath's shrine ….

House Redoran doesn't care. They marched in with their Warclaws and claimed the land. Anyone who tried to resist was imprisoned or sent to the mines.\n\nMe? I decided my life was more important than my tribe.

You can't be more disgusted with that prospect than I am, but at least I'm still alive. And all I have to do is direct them to the best resources and show them where some of my people hide every now and then.\n\nA small price to pay ….

Ulran? You'd think he was some kind of saint, the way he walked in and handed out supplies. He came back after his House threw him out. Never said why they exiled him.\n\nThe Wise Woman might know where to find him. They have her in one of the yurts.
To keep the head and the body separate.\n\nAs long as I'm here, I can't offer my people hope or advice. And I certainly can't compel them to rebel against these invaders.

I have no doubt. However, my place remains with my people. At least for now.\n\nThe Warclaws have treated me well so far. They believe I can make their tails fall off if I so choose. Who am I to dissuade such creatures from their beliefs?
You really did it. You—what's the catch? What do you expect for this?
I … I don't know what to say. I was resigned to my fate before you showed up.\n\nHardly seems real. Maybe it isn't. Not until I'm staring at the shores of the Summerset Isles.
Yes, yes. Tirwin's not irreplaceable and this should help me find a much less troublesome harvester. \n\nHere is her Servitude Obligation. She's your problem now.
I still don't understand. Ulran said someone set him up to fall. Who would do such a thing? And why would they do it? Ulran never wanted to hurt anyone!
So that's why they exiled him? That's why they killed him? He was too damn good? That's the problem!\n\nWe've got to find out who did all this. They won't get away with this. I won't allow it!
Oh, I'll find them, all right. And when I do, they'll pay for what happened to Ulran. I swear by Mephala's sacred web and the first blood my blade ever tasted, I'm going to avenge my brother.

I have no issue with Councilor Eris seeking help. It's where he's decided to get that help that concerns me. House Redoran doesn't need outsiders to take care of its business.\n\nBut who am I to question a House Councilor?
Feh, how can anyone not know about House Redoran? Is this some sort of outlander ruse?

If I knew what happened to the councilor's daughter, I wouldn't be talking to you, now would I?\n\nAs far as we can tell, she left of her own accord. There wasn't any foul play involved that we're aware of. Beyond that, you'd have to ask the councilor.

Councilor Eris Releth oversees Redoran operations in Balmora and the surrounding countryside. He's very influential, very powerful. \n\nUsually the councilor doesn't allow his passions to get the better of him, but Veya is his daughter, after all.
My silt strider can take you to either Gnisis or Vivec City. Ride's smooth and my creature's as gentle as a midday breeze.
My silt strider can take you to Balmora or Vivec City. She's fast, friendly, and almost never snacks on our customers.\n\nAlmost never.
You've served me well, but you overstep. This pact is deeply personal, and I will not be second guessed. Nothing is more precious than time—the more precious the gift, the higher the price.

Ha. Ask me again in a few hundred years.\n\nRisk is the price of any worthwhile endeavor. A vigorous adventurer like you should know that already. The trick is managing that risk—and no one navigates danger better than a Telvanni master.
We're headed to Sadrith Mora, if that's where you'd like to go.\n\nJust decide quick. I want to sail on the next tide.

I will. Of course I will. I just need a moment to think.\n\nI could let him go. Perhaps I should. But why? He brings me joy and comfort, doesn't he? When he's not kidnapping me, that is. Why would I give that up if I didn't have to?

Maybe. But if I let him go, I'll never see him again. The one person who truly cares about me, gone. No more silly Hist poems. No more wildflower bouquets. Nothing. \n\nHe'll forgive me. It will just take time, right? Please, help me decide.

You do that, but be careful. We're not sure who in House Redoran is involved, and I'd rather not see you wind up like these poor Ashlanders. Veya and I still need your help to get to the bottom of all this.\n\nWe'll see you in Balmora, hero.
You did? Isn't she beautiful? And so smart, too. I mean, I know she's a bit older but—\n\nWait, did you tell her what you were doing? And why you were doing it?

Ha! What? Oh, she's fooled you! She fools everyone you know? These feelings have to be our little secret under Mother's roof but soon we won't have to hide them! I just need you to take those shells to Mother and it will all become clear. You'll see!
I have experience getting on a lot of people's bad sides. Women, especially, find me exasperating. Irresistible, but exasperating. It's a gift.

Carefully and with your hands empty and clearly visible.\n\nShe's in the safe-house beneath Balmora. Or at least that's where I left her. But I didn't lock the door, so I suppose she could be anywhere by now. I suggest you hurry and get down there.
Perfect! Give me a moment to work my magic and I'll have you on your way with the finest flashing flourishes in the land!

The Morag Tong? They're an ancient guild of assassins sanctioned by the Tribunal to carry out honorable writs of execution. Ostensibly, they're supposed to keep the Houses from resorting to all-out war, but I still find the practice barbaric.
No. I don't think so. It's just been difficult. Finding poor Ulran in the Ashlander camp.\n\nI need to be doing something. Sitting down here in the dark, hiding. That's not going to solve anything.

Very little. The Queen of Dawn and Dusk rarely talks about it.\n\nI know that the Dark Elf Tribune, Sotha Sil, summoned eight Daedric Princes to a summit in Coldharbour. They argued for months, but eventually gave in to Sotha Sil's demands.
It wasn't Dyzera, I can tell you that. She was a formidable adversary, no question. But a plot of this scope? Mounting an attack on a Daedric Prince directly? No lesser Daedra would do that alone.

The last part of our vision—the gathering of Princes. Something deep and terrible lurks in that imagery. Time for a trip to the library. Or several libraries.\n\nI'm sure you'll have your hands full in the meantime.
We're looking for something. Propylon chambers! They must be here somewhere under all this rubble.

Well, it's a chamber for Propylon. I thought that much was obvious.\n\nLook, I'm not inclined to lecture when there's discovery to be made. Just know that it's complicated and I don't have time to explain it. I must find that chamber as soon as I can!

I know, but Naryu's writ. It involves a Redoran councilor—exactly the opportunity I've been waiting for! The councilor knows who set up my brother. We need to talk to her before Naryu executes the writ.\n\nDo this for me and I promise to stay here.

That's all I've been doing. Thinking! And I think Ulran was right. I think someone wanted him out of the way and they orchestrated the event with the Ashlanders to do it.\n\nSomeone played my brother for a fool and it cost him his life.
You … you did? How did he take it? I mean, he didn't know that my brother was dead?
Alliance territory? Why would you want to travel to one of those places?\n\nNever mind, I don't really want to know. Which alliance do you want to travel to?

Politics, foreign relations, the Ashlanders—you name an issue and Ulran and Brivan were probably on opposite sides of the argument. It got to the point where I had to ignore both of them or they'd drive me insane.
Brivan's as stubborn as my father when it comes to following the rules and regulations of House Redoran. Ulran and Brivan were best friends, even if they argued from time to time.
Really? I suppose that makes sense. I think he loves us … in his own way.\n\nBut what else did he say? Did he know that Ulran had been banished?
I can't agree to that. I need to figure out what happened to my brother. Who was involved. And then I'm going to make them pay. Just you watch!
He didn't expect …? My father doesn't know his children as well as he thinks. Either of them! That's why I had to get away. Join the Morag Tong. At least Naryu understands me.\n\nMostly.
This is the ship for you! I can take you to Seyda Neen, on the southern shore.
Not so loud! The docks have ears, you know. We set sail for Seyda Neen on the first favorable breeze.
Really? You want to travel to the land of Lord Vivec, Red Mountain, and the mushroom towers of the Telvanni?\n\nIf you insist. We set sail for Seyda Neen immediately.
If the place has a port and a dock, I can take you there. Where do you want to go?
You're in luck! We're sailing to Sadrith Mora on the next tide.
Of course, of course. We're at your service. As long as you want to travel to Sadrith Mora, then we'll be happy to take you with us. Otherwise, I'm afraid, you'll need to make other arrangements.

I'd rather not. She's particular about her secrets and I don't want to get on her bad side. You should keep that in mind, too, if you plan to continue on this course.\n\nVeya's mentor usually sticks to the rules, but I wouldn't turn my back on her.

I have decreed happiness, but not all of my kin share my breezy disposition and it's putting a damper on my festivities.\n\nI won't have my fun ruined by these grumpy … grumps! I need a champion to enforce my royalty mandated cheerfulness.
We make regular runs to Suran and Tel Mora. If that's where you want to go, climb aboard and we'll get you there in two shakes of a kwama's antenna.

If these treasonous malcontents insist on harboring sticks firmly in their hindquarters, then they can at least have the decency to keep them in bloom!\n\nFind the grumps in my domain and pelt them with these enchanted petals until morale improves!
We travel to Gnisis and Suran. And we know the paths that avoid the worst of the lava flows. Would you care for a ride?
Sorry, I forgot that not everyone knows how to tell a silt strider apart. My great creature can take you to Vivec City, Seyda Neen, or Molag Mar.\n\nAre you interested in any of those destinations?
Ha! Haven't you a cheek.\n\nIf you must know, it goes poorly. As I'm sure you can guess, the gentlemen rarely call on me a second time.
We make regular runs between here and Vivec City. We can also take you to Molag Mar, if you prefer. Do either of those destinations appeal to you?

My superstitious queen has confiscated my array of Royal Majesters! The only illusionary dazzlers fit for a king. I can't impress my subjects with just any common prestidigitation!\n\nIt would be trivial to whip up more with the right ingredients.
Looking to get out of Vivec City? Smart decision. I could use some time away myself.\n\nI can take you to Suran or Balmora. They're fairly close. Do either of those locations interest you?
Farther away? That's probably a good idea. I can take you as far as Gnisis or Tel Mora. Do either of those locations interest you?
It works on the dreugh. That is all I can say.\n\nBe wary in its lair. If that thing took my kin, then it is more dangerous than it leads on.

There are some, um, "local attractions" that should have what I'm looking for, but they're no place for royalty.\n\nIf you would risk venturing out on my behalf, I'll ensure you play a key role in today's festivities!

Just so! I am heartsick without my betrothed. What good is all this food and drink without the one you love to pick it from your teeth?\n\nBut I am forbidden to see my bride-to-be until the day of our vowels.

Beyond certain. I heard their cries—still hear them, in fact.\n\nThese abductions stink of Daedric plotting. Rival Princes conspire against my lady constantly. One of them seeks to blind her by snatching up her oracles. Perhaps more than one.

Free her from her minders, so we may grow fat together! Take a token of my love, the sickly-sweet brownish flesh of mudcrab apples, and she will know I sent you.\n\nThe guard cannot know their king bade the abscencing of his bride. Use cautiousness.

Time-honored Nord traditions! Fighting, food, foolishness and fortification …! Fun? Close enough. Sometimes Jorunn has trouble wrestling all the great words he knows.\n\nWhen it is Jester's Day, everyone is a child of Skyrim!

It is the Festival of Fools! Where fools are noble, and nobles are themselves! Jorunn always believes in leading by example!\n\nWhen you see this one enjoying himself to fullness, are you not inspired to do the same?

Oh my! An innocence to rival my own! You are so fortunate to learn of the Jester's Festival from someone virtuous as I, and not a cad like Emeric!\n\nHere we put aside decorum to embrace whimsy … and mischief!
The Festival of Fools is overflowing with all sorts of droll entertainment!\n\nYou know, pranks and gags and silly games. Uncomplicated peasant things! I do so prefer my thinking uncomplicated.

Well, if you must know, it's a celebration in honor of my rival rulers: the Festival of Fools!\n\nDaggerfall is a center of cultural exchange, even backward silly idiot culture. It'll all be quite fun, I assure you.
If you stripped to your small clothes and paraded through town, I'd call it a good start!

The Tribune persuaded us, through a private bargain, to cease meddling in mortal affairs directly. An amusing request from someone who fancies himself a god.\n\nNow, we exert our will through … intermediaries. In truth, I prefer it this way.
Such matters are better left undiscussed. Perhaps you can ask Sotha Sil about it. If you can find him, of course.

Yes—of her friends' suffering. Such visions might grant her a glimpse of where the other oracles are hidden.\n\nThere will be pain, undoubtedly, but she possesses a rare and terrible gift. True insight requires sacrifice.
Oh, you'll find I'm full of surprises!\n\nI have just the thing. Hold still … there!

Yes. The Overseer ran in there when she saw the looters. We tried to follow, but then the moonlet began raining fire, ash, and chunks of rock.\n\nLast I saw, she was chasing the looters into the far canton.

Greed is a powerful motivator. We left tools and materials just sitting around, unprotected, when the priests ordered everyone to get off the streets. The looters happily risk their lives if there's a profit to be made.
<Which item will you place to honor Llirala Veloth?>
<Which item will you place to honor Ondre Veloth?>
<Which item will you place to honor Valyne Veloth?>
<Which item will you place to honor Elms Veloth?>
Naryu's probably busy clearing her writ and we don't have time to wait.\n\nThis opportunity to learn more about what happened to Ulran won't last much longer. We need to find that squad of soldiers.
Their orders were to scout the old stronghold. I suggest we search along the outskirts and see if we can pick up their trail.
Fine. You wait for Naryu. I'm going to go and find those soldiers.

Tamriel doesn't suffer curses like this for long. Daedric hexes are too unstable. Nirn rejects them.\n\nPutting all three items in one place will shake the veil like moths in a spider-web. With any luck, Dyzera will come to investigate.

This is perfect! Now prepare yourself. What happens next will be simply amazing!\n\nThanks to magic provided by Lord Vivec, I can use this rubbing to not only record the clue provided by the tomb, I can add a new section to our model of the land.
You keep bringing up that strange Nord woman. I believe she said she found the scroll at a shop in Sadrith Mora. Once she noticed the ancient Elven, she brought it to me straight away.

Every important family owns at least one tomb. Of course, I'm most interested in those that predate the rise of the Great Houses.\n\nSpecifically, we're hoping to recover records presumed lost during the War of the First Council.

What? No, of course not. She'll get a thank you, in the fine print. But I translated the scroll. I braved the dangers of the tomb. I did all the hard work.\n\nWith some help from you. Which I will gladly acknowledge when I write this thrilling tale.
Wonderful! I'll decipher its portion of the clues and finalize the associated section of the diorama at once!

The ancestral tombs vary in size from single chambers to massive crypts, but I never heard of hidden passages until I translated that scroll.\n\nI believe the Veloth tomb is unique in all of Vvardenfell. As such, it will make a magnificent tale.

The Veloth family is welcome to any little trinkets we may find. All I care about are the big items of historic significance.\n\nNarsis Dren is a historian, an explorer. I'm not some tomb robber of ill repute.
If the family still exists, they'll be thrilled to hear that the famed explorer Narsis Dren has deigned to bring attention to their tomb.

You are now.\n\nJust be careful. The Twilight Lady has a deep well of love in her heart, but it's a dark, tempestuous love. Love like hers has to be respected. Never, ever forget that. Your life depends on it.

The Princes agreed to stop meddling in mortal affairs—directly, I mean.\n\nPrinces bound by the compact can't manifest in physical form here on Nirn. They can still push pieces around the board through intermediaries, though. Agents, like you and me.

If Azura thinks it's so, it is so. Truthfully, I think it might be more than one.\n\nOnly a Prince would strike another Prince. If this plot does go that high, we could be looking at another Planemeld … or something even worse. Rose help us.
Your spirit appertains to our vision, somehow. The island, the fire and ash, the clockworks and steam—you're planted like a tree, right in the middle of it. All of it.

Hard to tell. The future grows murkier by the minute. Perhaps that's a good thing. Or perhaps it's a very, very bad thing. Only time will tell, I guess.\n\nI know one thing for certain though—your fate intertwines with that of Azura.
Undoubtedly. And sooner than you think.\n\nJust remember, love and envy are two sides of the same coin. Like dawn and dusk—only a subtle difference keeps them apart.
This isn't the time or the place to have that discussion.\n\nGet the key to this cage and then we can find a private place to talk.

One of the cultists carries the key. I don't think he's too far away. We hear him patrolling around every so often.\n\nFree us and I'll tell you whatever you want to know. You have my word as a Redoran and as an officer.

Well then, let's see what you're made of! Participate in one of our games at any of our Battlegrounds. Win or lose, doesn't matter. Just get your feet wet. I can offer you a greater challenge after you've learned the ropes.
I told her what she wanted to hear. I was with Captain Ulran the day everything happened.\n\nI was commanded to lure the Ashlanders to town and set up a situation for Ulran to deal with.

My orders were to invite the Ashlanders to Balmora to trade, send some local toughs to instigate a commotion, and then get Ulran to investigate.\n\nIt was just supposed to be a loyalty test. Who expected Ulran to kill his own soldier to save a savage?

Captain Brivan, though he was still a lieutenant at the time. As soon as I explained all this to Veya, her face turned dark and she stormed out of here. I think she's going to Balmora to kill him!\n\nYou need to let me out so I can warn the captain!

Many more, but the Princes bound by the Coldharbour Compact stand above their lesser kith. None can match my beauty or Molag Bal's horrors. Dagon makes an art of destruction. On it goes.\n\nOf course, outward weakness often shrouds hidden power.
You did what? I suppose you thought that was a good idea?\n\nWell, the damage is done. At least tell me you found something to make this debacle a little more palatable.

If Veya kills Brivan without a writ, the Morag Tong and House Redoran will both want her head on a silver platter. You check the kinhouse. I'll grab Ashur and see if we can pick up Veya's trail in the streets.\n\nDon't let me down, hero.

I could barely make sense of the nonsense she was spouting!\n\nIt was Veya, Councilor Eris's daughter. Everything she said was a ramble. Something about my husband betraying her brother. That my Brivan had to suffer just as she was suffering.

Doubtful. Hist magic doesn't operate by the same rules as Telvanni spellcraft. I think that's why the Magisters hate it so much.\n\nI can't say for certain, but I doubt there's anything in Eoki's repertoire that could get him out of Sadrith Mora.

You shouldn't get involved. That young woman will hasten her own death if she thinks she can get past my husband and his soldiers!\n\nBut if you insist, the meeting is taking place at the garrison north of Balmora.

She had a knife, but no, she didn't harm me. She said her brother wouldn't hurt an innocent. That I wasn't responsible for his death.\n\nDo you have any idea what she was talking about because I certainly don't!
Do I look like a surveyor to you? If it's land you want, go talk to some of those bumpkins outside town.\n\nNow if you don't mind, I'd like to get back to my drink.

Zashanti sweeps the floor. After that, she peels mushrooms. After that, she scrubs  dishes and stacks chairs—then, if she is truly fortunate, she gets a few hours rest before the sun rises again.\n\nI am sorry, but this one has no time for gossip.

A few moments ago, Red Mountain erupted and the moonlet above the city dropped dangerously low in the sky. I assume that was when Lord Vivec's energy was depleted. If we don't find a way to restore some of his power and soon, Vvardenfell is doomed.

I'm not sure … but our first priority must be to restore some of the Lord Vivec's energy. After that, he can tell us what we need to do next.\n\nDid Barbas give any indication as to why he did this to Lord Vivec?

Someone has to take care of Lord Vivec. I'll make the preparations necessary to return the power in the Blessing Stone to him. I'm really operating above my station here. I'm not the Archcanon, after all.\n\nThen again, neither was Tarvus, I suppose.

Hmm. I don't know for sure, but Ninave Rendo was chewing my ear off a few days ago. She's been trying to convince her husband Barys to move back to Balmora.\n\nShe loves the finer things, you see? Trust me when I say, Vos is short on finer things.

Frankly, I wouldn't bother with Ninave. Talk to her husband, Barys. They own a small farm just north of town.\n\nMind you don't wander into that Daedric ruin though. Why these Dark Elves haven't torn the place down is beyond me.
That's a bit out of the blue! But it just so happens that my wife and I have been discussing a move back to Balmora.
I would. Ninave prefers to be near family, in Balmora.\n\nDon't tell my wife, but Seythen was interested in exploring Daedric shrines. I know he was studying Esutanamus. Bit east of here.

I'd consider it, but my wife would never forgive me if we left without knowing what has happened to our son Seythen.\n\nHe went off adventuring. We've had no word in days now and Ninave is worried sick.

Is Veya trying to get herself killed? You can't just barge into a Redoran garrison and ask the soldiers to stand aside while you murder their captain!\n\nWe have to get to her before she gets to Brivan.

Truthfully? It doesn't. Not yet.\n\nTelvanni plots take time to develop. If I demand Eoki's freedom too early, I show my hand. Suddenly, he's a valuable piece in the game—moved and sacrificed as the magisters see fit.

She murdered soldiers without a writ? This is a dark path she's decided to follow. And unless we play this just right, it's not going to end well for any of us.\n\nLet's find Veya and put a stop to this. We can deal with any consequences after that.

Maybe nothing, maybe everything. We know Ulran refused to employ mercenaries—he hated counting on thugs to do the right thing.\n\nI expect the Redoran council feels the same. Maybe Brivan's trying to show them what the Warclaws can do.
Do I sense a rebuke? It's not ideal, I know.\n\nLook, I treasure Eoki. He's placed his trust in me. I hope you'll do the same.

There's no stealthy way to approach this. The front door's our only option.\n\nThen we track down Brivan, find Veya, bonk her on the head, and get her out of here before she does something I can't fix. Easy as gorapple pie!

He's going to be as mad as a bull netch and twice as ugly. Provided we can actually convince him we're here to save his sorry hide and that we're not part of a plot to kill him and the councilors.\n\nJust another day at the fair, right, hero?

It's always important to figure out where a target keeps its wine. In this case, down in the cellars. There's a staircase back where we first came in.\n\nAnd if we still don't find Brivan or Veya, well, at least there'll be plenty to drink!

And I'll figure out how to get this door open. Just in case. \n\nYou know, attending a House Redoran council meeting was always a secret goal of mine. Right after getting a lusty Argonian maiden to scrape my flesh raw with her abrasive tongue.

Veya? She's barely out from under her mother's apron and she presumes to judge my actions?\n\nNo matter. Whatever your motives, nothing justifies the blatant killing of Ferhara and her mercenaries. Councilor Eris can't protect you this time, outlander.

Ah, now everything becomes clear. Veya learned something of her brother's fate and wants to retaliate? Then let her come!\n\nBut know this. I merely set the events in motion. I didn't conceive the plan.

I'm not sure they deserve to be saved, but that's what we have to do. Veya can't be allowed to kill the councilors. I … we … have to stop her. \n\nIt's more than me and Veya's lives on the line. Something like this could destroy the Morag Tong.

We have to get ahead of her, cut her off. There's a door on the main floor, near the kitchens, that should allow us to come at the council meeting from another direction. I was able to get it open when I was scouting around up there.\n\nLet's go.
No one just wanders into a Council Mouth's office looking around. I should report you. \n\nWhat are you really after? And do be honest. We've already wasted enough time here.

It's a matter of literature, or lack thereof.\n\nI wrote a poem, you see—a cloying, drunken mess of a poem. The post delivered it to my darling Ethrandora just this morning. If you get it away from her, the letter is yours.

She spends most of her time in the study, here in the Council Hall. She's very diligent. Always leaning over one book or another. And the way she licks her thumb when she turns the pages …. Sorry.\n\nYou'll find her in the study. Yes.
She's such a pretty, dainty thing. Not at all like those other scrawny acorn-elves.\n\nAdd a half bottle of shein to a lusty heart and you wind up with some very poor decisions.
The poem's terrible! Plus, if word got to my parents that I'd been courting a Wood Elf, I'd be written out of the will. Repeatedly. With red ink. \n\nThen there's also the possibility of blackmail.

Why do you think Ethrandora keeps it on her?\n\nShe knows that if Master Eraven gets wind of this, he might dismiss me from his service. Clever minx. Working for a Council Mouth is a fine occupation, f'lah. I can't risk losing it.

Quick, give it here! Phew. What a relief.\n\nAll right, f'lah, I'm going to burn this embarrassment. I sure hope I didn't leave Master Eraven's correspondence box unlocked. That would be careless in the extreme. Farewell!

A series of regrettable decisions led to this family tragedy, and most of them were made by Eris Releth.\n\nI knew of Ulran's compassion concerning the Ashlanders. It was unorthodox, but not worthy of the punishment meted out. Eris was wrong.

Eris convinced Brivan to test Ulran. Then the two of them decided to slaughter the Ashlanders. Oh, the council allowed itself to be convinced that exile was an appropriate punishment, but we were wrong to let it go as far as it did.

House Redoran behaved poorly. Morag Tong rules were violated. I suggest we make sure these details never see the light of day.\n\nLeave the bodies where they are. We will say that Veya died protecting her father and the council from the Warclaws.

I didn't say that. But we're not butchers. We do not hire mercenary thugs to wipe out an entire people.\n\nThis gathering was to deal with that. Eris planned to step down and we were going to demote Brivan for the part he played.

Cooperate with House Redoran and hold your tongues. It's as simple as that. I shall return to the council meeting and conclude our business. When we're finished, I expect you and Naryu to both be gone.\n\nThat is all, outlander.

The High Councilor thinks we killed her. The deal hinges upon all of us forgetting this sorry mess ever happened.\n\nBesides, once Veya regains her senses, there's every likelihood that she'll try to kill the councilors again.

When have I ever been able to convince Veya to do anything she didn't want to do?\n\nThere's Redoran blood on Veya's hands. Once the Morag Tong ties those unauthorized murders to her, she's as good as dead anyway. And, more than likely, so am I.

You're … you're right. If anyone's to blame for all this, it's me. I wasn't a good enough mentor. If for no other reason, Veya deserves a second chance. Look, you need to leave. We'll meet back in Balmora.\n\nAnd, hero? Thanks.

Yes … you're right, damn it all. Veya spilled Redoran blood and now she has to pay. I'll take care of it. She's my responsibility.\n\nYou don't have to watch this. Go. I'll meet you back in Balmora after it's done.

I don't see many options. We can either finish off Veya now and go along with the High Councilor's deception, or we slip out of here with Veya and send her far, far away.\n\nShe broke her vows and deserves to die. I know that, but it still feels wrong.

I knew I could count on you. Here's the gold. I'll not pay a drake more than what's in that pouch … mostly because I don't have a drake more than what's in that pouch.\n\nEoki can provide more details, or you can just ask around Vos yourself.

And as far as she knows, she did. Now Veya needs to disappear. Otherwise, both Redoran and the Morag Tong will go after her. Believe me, nobody survives that kind of attention.\n\nVeya didn't ask for everything that happened. She only wanted justice.

As long as everyone sticks to the bargain, I go about my usual business. A writ here, a nice bath there, maybe a few intimate encounters along the way—to relieve the tension, you understand.\n\nI just hope Veya's good with all this. She has to be.

I've arranged for a ship captain I know to meet us in Vivec City. From there, Veya will sail to Summerset and rendezvous with an associate of mine. He's kind of furry and a bit of an arse, but he's good people. He'll take care of Veya.

There's always a choice. Veya could have chosen not to kill Redoran soldiers. She could have chosen not to kill her father. I could have chosen not to kill her. But, hey, it seemed like the thing to do.\n\nNow leave me alone so I can finish my wine.

What do you want, hero? You want me to say that you're right? Fine. You're right, damn it! We'll all keep more secrets and everything will go back to the way it was.\n\nLook, I'd offer you some of my wine, but I don't want to.

Really? Is this what justice feels like? My apprentice killed her own father and I killed her. We've got a lot of death, but not much else. Just another typical day in the Morag Tong.\n\nLook, it may not sound like it, but I am grateful for your help.
I harnessed my ambition, served my masters with loyalty and discretion and earned my freedom. They whine like belly-sick guars and rot in chains. It doesn't get any clearer than that.

From what I gather, he wants to build a new tower there. I've no idea why. Mistress Dratha essentially owns Vos, and I can tell you, she does not welcome intruders.\n\nIf I was mad enough to antagonize one of the Magisters, it would not be Dratha.

I only need him to survive long enough to sponsor me. He won't break ground on his tower anytime soon. Plus, there's a rumor that Dratha suffers from some mysterious illness. It could be Firuth's doing. You never can tell with the Telvanni.
Hmph. I'm no tour guide.\n\nWhat do you need to know?

Forbade is such a complicated concept. It assumes that the rules are applied equally to everyone, and we both know the foolishness of that assumption.\n\nThe Warclaws have a long-standing contract that pre-dates any proclamations by the councilor.
That's the second boldest claim I've ever heard. \n\nIf there's truth to it, be my guest and squash those vermin. I've had my fill of Daedra for a long while.

Trade secrets, you understand. Ferhara can tell you the Warclaws do whatever it takes to accomplish the job. This assignment is perfect for us, since we specialize in missing persons.\n\nWe find them. We make them disappear. Whatever the client needs.

Captain Brivan's predecessor? Forgive Ferhara, this one can barely remember the names of those who lack claws and fur.\n\nBut yes, we worked with Ulran, though Brivan appreciates our techniques so much more than he ever did.
Thank you, serjo. Be careful, and Three protect you.

I don't go anywhere near that place. We've got enough troubles here. Lean harvests, clumsy Telvanni wizards, my wife henpecking me to death …. No, I'll not invite some plague from the House of Troubles as well.

What do storied Covenant heroes and Camonna Tong cronies have in common? Apparently the region's illegal slave trade.\n\nThe seaside cavern Khartag Point is drowning in rumors as of late, and I need to figure out what's fact and what's fiction.

Well, just one we know of, the Orc Commander Khartag. We've learned that he and his raiders are somehow involved in slave smuggling. In what way? We're not exactly sure. \n\nBut he seems to have caught the attention of the Camonna Tong.

Bound to happen. Those involved with the Camonna Tong are not known for long, happy lives. Well, at least he had an impact. Why else would the cavern be named after him? \n\nRegardless, it's the slave activity we need to assess, not some dead Orc.

The Camonna Tong are slavers, murderers, extortionists, everything a vile crime syndicate can be. They don't like Outlanders, especially ones who cut into their profits. \n\nTread lightly in Khartag Point, it's crawling with their cronies.

The situation is wound dangerously tight, but I believe the gears revolve around you. Once you leave, I should be perfectly safe. Or, at least as safe as I ever am in the midst of all these experiments. \n\nYou however …. Stay vigilant, my friend.

Hirelings? Yes, they worked for me. Before they quit, the ungrateful netches!\n\nStill, I paid them well before the pistons slipped their alignments. They should know where to find the components. Last I heard, Snorfin and the others were in Molag Mar.

I could, but I won't pour five-year-old flin into a cracked decanter. No offense. Suffice it to say, they're fairly common as far as Dwemer components go.\n\nUse the list and talk to my former hirelings. I'll build the device the moment you return.
An idea? Of course. I just need proof to satisfy my superiors. But don't worry. I'm sure I'll have things well in hand by the time we meet back up.

Some locks resist even the best efforts of a skilled thief. They're crafted using superior components and complex mechanisms. Like the lock on the gate. If I had all the time in the world, maybe I could crack it. But we don't have that luxury.

I would personally love to put an arrow through the skull of every single bandit in that cave, but I've been told this case needs finesse. Plant the notes without the bandits noticing, and we should be able to keep them preoccupied for awhile yet.

Too much risk, too much trouble. Better to simply confuse the s'wits. We can keep them occupied, cooped up in their cave, and stop contraband from invading our shores. The more they fail to grow moon-sugar, the more determined they seem to get.

Just some gibberish the Temple came up with. They contain enough technical terms to appear legitimate, but say nothing that's actually going to help the moon-sugar's growth. It should keep the bandits trying and trying, with no success.

Build a tower of course! This place grows too crowded. We're practically sitting in each others' pockets! Gerald and I need room.\n\nThere's also the matter of appearances. Towers bespeak a certain degree of majestic erudition.

You can't see him, can you? Hardly a surprise. He rarely shows himself to lesser minds.\n\nGerald serves as my assistant, attending to various tasks I'd rather not … yes, I'm getting to that! For Ayem's sake. He also keeps the others at bay.

Yes! This throng of hangers-on! Hundreds of unwanted guests! Constantly bickering and bumbling into one another. Day after day—night after night. It's exhausting!\n\nWithout Gerald … well, I can hardly imagine.
Of course you don't. Of course you don't! \n\nUgh. I tire of this conversation. The others are bad enough. Be off! I have work to do.

Those poor kwama. I would never have the heart to cull them myself, but it must be done for the greater good. I know the Temple has asked you to bring me research notes and an egg sample. \n\nIf you have any questions, please let me know.

They've been bred to be highly aggressive, so much so that they're nearly impossible to control. They're calmed by a specific pheromone, though I'm afraid I don't know which one. That's why they appear to tolerate most of the Rumblegarde inside.

Oh, poor queenie. She's likely on her deathbed at this point, having been made to be productive far longer than is acceptable. I believe she's been put in some chamber we can't reach, connected to the mine through some smaller kwama dug tunnels.

Beyond the obvious? Your friend possesses a keen mind and great natural talent, but even the Great House Telvanni is not above simple prejudice. The circumstances of her birth make advancement … complicated.

You've never seen an illusion dazzler? You're in for a treat!\n\nThey're the pinnacle of awe-inspiring emanations! Radiant in color, resonant in percussion, slightly malodorous, and only harmful under the most ill-thought out circumstances.

I would counsel patience, but I have no illusions. Sun-in-Shadow will dismiss such advice out of hand. Her dreams can only be deferred for so long.\n\nI say only this—whatever she plans to do, make sure she does it cautiously.

Yes. Ralasa hates practically everyone, but she's developed a particular distaste for Sun-in-Shadow. I can't tell if it's truly the will of Gothren or just a personal vendetta. Both of them revile lesser races. A perfect match if ever there was one.

I merely speak for Muthsera Gothren. His distaste for Sun-in-Shadow should come as no surprise. Beasts have no place in the House.\n\nYou may want to rethink the company you keep, outlander. Just a bit of advice.

I suggest she leave Vvardenfell. Travel to Daggerfall or Wayrest and join the Mages Guild. I hear they take anyone. She would fit right in.\n\nThe fact is she has no place here. She may have earned her freedom, but she will never be a true Telvanni.

I don't hate them. I just see the truth of their nature.\n\nArgonians and Khajiit make wonderful servants, but to pretend they possess the same faculties as mer, or even men, is absurd. They were born to serve, just as we were born to rule.

That's what we're trying to determine. Bal Fell was once a great city, built atop an ancient center of Sheogorath worship. Now only the Daedric ruins remain.\n\nOnce we find the treasure, I'll be more famous than that blowhard, Narsis Dren!

Oh, they were just your typical apprentices. Young, eager, hoping to make a name for themselves by working alongside a famed treasure hunter.\n\nThe six of them readily broke off promptly at sunset yesterday and abandoned the camp. They abandoned me!

My man-servant Stibbons? He's lazy, drinks too much, and requires detailed instructions to accomplish the simplest of tasks. But his fish stew is delicious, I'll grant him that.\n\nI regret letting him read my collection of Investigator Vale mysteries.

Sun-in-Shadow will stand before us again. I only hope that it's for a promotion and not something less pleasant. Believe it or not, these meetings can go far worse.\n\nHonor to you and your House, sera. Farewell.

Of course we do! I specifically waited for you to arrive because I figured that would be the case.\n\nStill doesn't mean I'm happy about blurring the line between helping Veya and performing my duty as a Morag Tong.

That means we have to get Dolvara to spill her guts before I spill her guts!\n\nJust keep your wits about you, hero. Dolvara wields her feminine charms the way I wield my daggers. Don't let her seduce you into doing something stupid before I end her.

We discovered that the next meeting of the High Council will take place at the consulate outside Balmora, the Warclaws and the Ashlander abuse aren't completely sanctioned by the House, and Dolvara was present when Ulran was exiled.\n\nNot a bad haul.

The overbearing Breton? She's working with the spiders, isn't she? She knew!\n\nShe knew the spiders would take my friends. She knew they would make them dance. I had to run, you see, I had to! I don't want to dance! I don't know how!

The noble's banished son? Why does House Dres care about that? Never mind. Anything so we can get to the good stuff.\n\nUlran was tested and found wanting. Chose the life of a savage over his own soldier. We stripped him of his rank and exiled him.

Spiders, yes! Please, you have to rescue them! The spiders make them dance, but nobody can dance forever.\n\nI'd go back, but I can't. I don't dance, you understand? I won't dance! Why do the spiders want us to dance, anyway? It makes no sense!

Stibbons? He's in league with the spiders! Why else don't they force him to dance? He went to join his spider masters, but he dropped his spice pouch just over there. Oh no! Do you think it's full of spiders? \n\nWhat should I do? What should I do?
You're obviously not my afternoon appointment. You'd best take your leave before I have my soldiers throw you into the swamp.

I'd be lying if I said yes. But if there's anyone who could get through to him, it's you.\n\nGothren keeps a few "pupils"—henchmen more like. You'll probably have to get through one or two before he'll deign to speak with you. Just be careful.

Magister Gothren reigns over Tel Aruhn—the fungal tower west of here. He has a sour reputation, but remains one the most powerful mages in Tamriel.\n\nI never had cause to work for him, but Eoki did. He doesn't like to talk about it.

Ulran's dead? Hmm. I hadn't heard. As to who was behind the test of Ulran's loyalty, what does that matter? He failed and paid the price for his poor choices.\n\nWhat does all this have to do with our arrangement?
Of course.\n\nWhat can the future Mouth of Muthsera Gothren help you with?

Well I can't say for sure, but there's a good chance the missing slaves stole Muthsera Gothren's property before fleeing Tel Aruhn. Ropefish and other people-smugglers sometimes accept magicked items as payment.

A great many things, I'm sorry to say. They pilfered an ancient tome, a rare pendant, and a purse full of gold.\n\nOf course, my master was most aggrieved by the loss of several slaves. Strong workers, all. Muthsera Gothren is sick with worry.

You should know by now that Telvanni alliances often start as fluid affairs. Not that our relationship is fluid! What we've got going here? Rock-solid.\n\nSun-in-Shadow's intentions align with my own. It only makes sense that we should be partners.

No, of course not. I didn't mean to assume. Truth be told, I've always been a fierce, but very quiet proponent of beast rights.\n\nIf you return the tome, pendant, and gold, I think Muthsera Gothren will still promote me—albeit with a heavy heart.

I'm sure I wouldn't know. My master has a kind and gentle disposition, but children sometimes need discipline, yes? It would really be Slavemaster Arenim's prerogative. Unfortunately, she can be … irascible.

Afraid! Why, I'm not afraid! I'm the king! Keeping my politically expedient queen happy is my duty as a devoted husband … and good diplomacy.\n\nBut if you happen to see my lovely Maraya with her sword, give a whistle, would you?

That horrific spider! I was using several of the inquisitive techniques employed by Investigator Vale in her fabulous stories when the largest, most terrifying spider I ever laid eyes upon sprang at me with evil intent.\n\nEven spooked the mage!

I, um, no. This is embarrassing. It started … talking to me. Then I swooned and passed out. Spiders have that effect on me.\n\nOh, I must return to Lady Laurent. It's well past her tea time and she's going to be extremely displeased with me.

It is, though she's not making much sense. Perhaps you could talk to her?\n\nLady Laurent believed the mages absconded with her hard-earned gold. So I followed them to these ruins and—well, I encountered the spider and then everything went dark.

A talking spider? Ridiculous! Still, Stibbons has always been dreadfully afraid of the eight-legged pests. No excuse for shirking his responsibilities, though.\n\nAnd the mages? Did you stumble upon them while you tracked down my man-servant?
Why not? Don't tell me you're afraid of a few spiders and a dusty old ruin?

She heard talking spiders? Incredible! I can brew a tea to keep Stibbons from fainting. Then he can listen to the spiders and lead us through the barrier. But we need to test its potency. Bring me a small spider from the ruins and meet us at my camp.

It's true her meatiness rivals that of Jorunn, but his only complaint is that his bride-to-be snores so much. Hah!\n\nShe is warm on a cold Eastmarch night and never complains of crumbs in the bed! No other like her within my Reach.
Almost certainly. Sunna'rah led him right to it. It won't take the Hound long to figure out how to access Vivec's stolen energy. Then he'll try to open a portal for his master, Clavicus Vile.

As I said, the atelier's the workshop where Sotha Sil used Sunna'rah to experiment with his own divine energy. The reservoir located inside was specifically designed to contain such massive power.\n\nAs far as workshops go, it's a masterpiece!

Maybe. Probably. It's a distinct possibility. Certainly the Hound and his master think so.\n\nWhether it will actually work or not, you have to go in there and stop him. The danger's too great to ignore.

Veya's brother? It's a sad story. Killed one of his own soldiers to protect an Ashlander, of all things. I think they were being too lenient when they simply exiled him, but that's how they treat the privileged few.

Ulran always had an unnatural attraction to the Ashlanders and their savage ways. He felt that an Ashlander life was worth more than a Redoran life. The Council didn't agree with his assessment.\n\nThis will all be over as soon as Ferhara finds Veya.
That doesn't absolve you from blame—it just makes you sound stupid. I have no patience for stupidity.\n\nNow I wonder if you're equal to the task I've set for you.
Impersonating? Don't you recognize your perfectly adorable high lady of Elven grace?
