This is a holiday about not taking anything too seriously, even royalty! It comes more naturally to some than others, so we silly celebrators often have to give them a nudge.\n\nThese hold outs will find it hard to be serious plastered in flowers.
So I am! Some fiendish festival hex, no doubt. Oh, my poor glowing complexion!\n\nI suppose I'll just have to make the most of these rippling muscles and incredible tolerance for wine.

I don't know that there are any true stories behind the Jester's Festival. Some say it happens because Sheogorath turned the whole world mad! Others say it sprung from Mer wanting to know what it's like to live like Men.\n\nWho really knows?

I suppose. I still can't figure out how the priest was able to control their minds using spiders. It's a bafflement.\n\nMaybe one of these scrolls I seized on the way out will shed some light on this final mystery.

No need to worry. Stibbons will examine the scrolls. He's ever more durable than he appears.\n\nI know a scribe who lives near White Ridge Barrow in Skyrim. His fascination with spiders borders on obsession, but I'm sure he'll appreciate the scrolls.

Well, the Zalkin-Sul cave network strays very close to an ancient Dwarven stronghold called Mzanchend. Otheri's miners might have stumbled upon an entrance to the ruin. So, keep an ear out for clanking?

Now there's a foolish question for the ages! You're getting good at this.\n\nThere are more inventive originations of the Jester's Festival than flies in Black Marsh, and bred twice as fast! I'd wager it ties closely to the discovery of drinking.

My dear Maraya clings terribly to her people's mistrust of magic almost as much as her natural severity … and sword. She seems to think that setting off hundreds of flashy magical projections in the city would be a public menace.\n\nSilly, isn't it?
Sure. I've got a few minutes.\n\nAh, who am I kidding? I've got plenty of time. What do you want to know?
Other than Otheri's guards? We have cave-ins every now and again. Unruly slaves and such. \n\nThen there's Mzanchend … but I'm sure you're not interested in that.

Ash get in your eyes on the way here? You can't miss those gloomy old Dwarf towers.\n\nWay I hear it, the Mzanchend ruins cut right under the mine. Plenty of treasure down there just waiting to be plucked. That's what I've heard anyway.

Stuck up Dark Elves, ash storms, slave labor pushing down wages … what's not to like?\n\nEh. I shouldn't belly-ache. It is what it is and I need the coin. Got to take the opportunities where you find them.
Take my illusion dazzlers to some suitably crowded locations in the city and give them a good shake and toss!\n\nMy majestic creations will do the rest.

Have the others filled your head with foibles about this holy day? Enviness leads many to claim they lead the ant-ticks, but it was the First Man who taught Mer humor, or was it that he had the last laugh?\n\nNo matter, Ysgramor did everything first!

Not many have a taste for mudcrab apples, but this one knows they are my sweet's favored sweetness. \n\nHer minders do not let her indulge in them freely and it is Jorunn's promise that she will eat as many as she likes when we are married!
Do not let this one's Joniality deceive you into believing that Jorunn is Elsweyr. Before you is the fearsome masher of Mer and words you have heard in song and the tiny screams of scared mice!

Though the heart of a senche-tiger roars within my chest, this one cannot claim to be one of those noble beasts. Jorunn's habit of laying naked in the sun does not help his case, he knows, but he assures you he is sadly a Man.

Oh, my simple servant, I'm simply dressed for the occasion! Though, I don't know why I didn't think to disguise myself sooner. I'd never have to worry about my wife finding me if I were an Argonian or something.
Oh, so we start a rumor that I am actually an Argonian to throw her off my trail. That's much simpler. Brilliant idea! Glad I thought of it.

She only calls me that to annoy me. It's an obscure Morag Tong title given to ranking female agents when they take on apprentices. She's just lucky that as her mentor, I'm not allowed to kill her.\n\nYou? You're not that lucky.

No, no, thank you. You've recovered everything I need to explain … well, to talk with my children. I'm not sure my heart could endure any more of this. It feels like losing her all over again.\n\nPlease, could you do this old man one last favor?

Ask my children to come visit me? I feel like I can finally leave them with the answers I've never been able to provide.\n\nTell Neria we need to talk about her mother. As for Mils, if he hesitates, tell him it's about the estate. His inheritance.

Neria works at the stables. She's always been good with guar, something she inherited from her mother. Mils will likely be fishing on the canal, for dinner. He's always kept them both fed.\n\nI'm so proud of both of them. I wish they understood.

My mother? Father rarely mentions her. I can tell how painful it is for him to recall her, even after all these years. I was young when she passed, but my memories are pleasant.\n\nDid he say what this is about? What did he have you doing?

How odd! Father always was dabbling in magic. Often, it seemed like he had time for little else, though I know he did it to take care of us.\n\nStill, I'd better check up on him. I imagine Mils wants nothing to do with this? I'll ensure he joins us.
I don't see how that's any of your business. I've nothing to say to my father or those his Telvanni master employs.

Whatever this is about, it's no concern of mine. My father managed to leave me out of his life. He can leave me out of his problems too.\n\nYou want to talk, my sister Neria works the stables. She tolerates my father's business better than I do.
My father? Oh no, has he taken a fall? Or did he ask you to do something for him? He's been declining of late, and I'm afraid he's not entirely in his right mind.

Oh, Mils. He was so young when Mother passed. I've tried to explain that Father had to work to keep a roof over our heads, but it's been difficult.\n\nI raised Mils myself while Father was away, which was often. He's never forgiven Father for that.

Oh, yes. Father is well-regarded among the Telvanni masters, even though he's never aspired to be one himself.\n\nMaster Drenim trusts him implicitly, and if you know anything about the Telvanni, that's impressive on its own. They don't trust easily.

I'm afraid I don't know. All he's been able to tell me is that part of his contract with Master Drenim forbids him from disclosing any of the master's business, even to his own children.\n\nWhatever he's doing, I'm certain it's important.
I have nothing to say to that man. What is it about "I don't want to talk about my father" that you can't understand?

I don't want his money any more than I want his apologies! Does that man really think that he can buy me off after ignoring me my entire life?\n\nLeave me alone. If Father needs someone to listen to his excuses, ask Neria to do it.
You just don't give up, do you?\n\nFine. I'll endure another few moments with my absentee father. For her. Just let me set aside the fish I've caught today first.
The primary contact between the slaves of Sadrith Mora and the Ropefish. \n\nShe drinks like an eel, but we trust her. That is more than I can say for some of the other smugglers around here.

I wish he didn't have to work so much. Master Drenim pays well, but sometimes, I worry he'll work Father to death. He's just so tired all the time.\n\nEven when he finds time away, Mils refuses to see him, and I know that hurts him dearly.

I did for a bit, after Mother died. I didn't understand why Father couldn't be with us until I grew up and learned how hard it is to keep a family housed and fed.\n\nNow, I appreciate all Father's sacrifices for us. I just wish Mils could see it.

Lagdabash. I'd bet my left tusk on it. I hope you gave her and that witless pig, Hazbur, a good kick in the teeth. We're better off without them.\n\nSo let's get on with this. You with Eoki and his friends?
I have grown tired of fighting this thirst. Though it shames me, I can no longer feed off skeevers and scavengers.\n\nIf I must consume mortal lives, they will not be those of the innocent.

An end to this curse. Once and for all. I may be at the mercy of Molag Bal, but I will slake my thirst on his servants until my voice is heard.\n\nAnd if they deliver me to Coldharbour for eternal torment, at least I will no longer be this.

The spawn of Vivec and Molag Bal? The dread hunter wearing the ancient carapace? Have you read nothing of the sermons?\n\nIt devoured all it saw until Vivec cast it down! Twice over! But it lives again! You have to believe me!
You … you're serious? I can't believe it! Tirwin loves me! We're going to be together no matter what you, or my mother think! She's mine! You understand me? She's mine!
Then we will see where this path takes us. The tracks that brought me here will surely lead us to our quarry.

Well, Naryu wouldn't tell me any specifics, but she trained me well. It wasn't hard to sneak a glance at the writ before she took off.\n\nHer target's at Arenim Manor, out in the swamp. Not far from that smelly cave, actually.

I know Vatola. He's a typical Redoran soldier. Loyal to a fault. Always spouting nonsense about house and honor above all.\n\nHe was devoted to my brother, though. Ulran considered him to be one of his best.

Ulran had a habit of putting the needs of others ahead of his own. He probably told Vatola and his soldiers to remain quiet. Decided to take responsibility and save them any heartache.\n\nI hope these soldiers remember that when we find them.

As far as I'm concerned, rules got my brother killed. They don't apply to me anymore.\n\nBesides, to find the soldiers we're probably going to have to carve a path through those cultists. The Morag Tong won't care about that.

That's what the handbook says. Look, I know what Naryu's done for me. To keep me safe. I appreciate that.\n\nBut this is about what they did to my brother. Nothing else matters. Not Naryu. Not you. And certainly not me.

No … never. You and Naryu aren't my enemies. I just need to get justice for Ulran. Otherwise his death will be the first of many.\n\nWe have to be able to resist laws that make no sense or get people hurt without being afraid of getting exiled.
I'm going to bring my Master's grandest plan ever to fruition! He'll be so proud of me!\n\nJust stay out of my way and enjoy the show. I promise, it will be highly entertaining!

Oh yes indeed! The grandest! My Master and his partners seek to ….\n\nOh no, no, no. Bad Barbas! I almost gave away the surprise! You're a tricky one, you are. But my Master will be so pleased that I stepped in and made his plan even better!

My Master has been trying to find this place for the longest time. He actually set the ball rolling. I saw an opportunity to improve his plan and make it better, so I took the initiative.\n\nThis will get me back in my Master's good graces, you'll see!

Worried about the Archcanon? The poor old man. He died in his sleep, all peaceful like. I saw an opportunity and leapt right in. Stupid Vivec! He never even noticed.\n\nI was masterful in the role, though, don't you agree?
Who else, outlander? The slaves of the false gods will never allow me to trespass their domain and the task is beyond them.\n\nThis falls to you, or no one.

Brivan's name keeps coming up. At the very least, he was Ulran's best friend once. He might be able to shed some light on Ulran and what happened to cause his exile. And I really want to know what took place after Ulran left us that message.

Lord Vivec sent the three of us to seek guidance at the Andrano ancestral tomb. We were attacked when we got there and our guard was seriously hurt. I barely got her to safety, but we failed to complete the mission Lord Vivec bestowed upon us.

Canon Llevule. He remained behind after we retreated from the tomb. I know he wants to get back inside and ask Lord Vivec's questions, but there's no way he can get past the Daedra or ask the questions on his own.\n\nMay the Three grant him wisdom.
The Warclaws may be a blessing in disguise. I can explain killing these bastards a lot easier than trying to wipe Redoran blood off my hands.\n\nLet's go stop Veya. I'm ready when you are, hero.

You're looking for the responsible party? Then look no further than Councilor Eris. He wanted to prove his son's loyalty to the House. To show that Ulran's fascination with the savage Ashlanders hadn't corrupted him.\n\nWell, look how that turned out.
Ah. I see the n'wah is well-informed. If you know that I am Savarak, you must also know that I rule Vos as its wizard-magistrate. Do you bring me some petition, or is this just a social visit?

Someone has to. Dratha's Mouth, Llayne Sadri, refuses to assist me. She just lurks by her mistress' bedside in Tel Mora—scheming and fomenting unrest.\n\nPeople in crisis require a firm hand. If that offends your gentle sensibilities, move on.

Have a care how you speak, outlander.\n\nIt is true that certain of Vos's citizens have struggled during this period of transition, but I'm hardly to blame. They've taken Dratha's illness very hard. It's led to idleness and crude insubordination.

Honestly, what kind of idiot leaves this many documents lying about?\n\nStill nothing about my Mistress's illness. Damn. Well, what do we know? House Hlaalu is bankrolling Savarak's operation. His wealth and mercenaries arrive via Selvil Island ….

Exactly. Find Nerandas near the wharf and use this pass-phrase. I'll have the few House guards still loyal to Mistress Dratha make sure no one approaches. We don't want the real contact to muck things up.\n\nLearn what you can, then make a swift exit.

Right. With someone named Nerandas, yes? The Hlaalu's hatchetman here in Vos, no doubt. \n\nIf they're using pass-phrases, they must not know each other by name or by face. Are you thinking what I'm thinking?
I doubt Lord Thanlen knows any more than us. Knowing the type of person our employer is, he likely viewed this deal as too good to pass up and left it at that.\n\nNot big on details, that one.

But the stench remains. You Telvanni servants …. Late! Always late!\n\nOur plot to kill Dratha proceeds at a snail's pace. I blame myself, in part. Tel Mora's fungal growth has proven to be more resilient to the toxin than I expected.

Of course we are! To release lethal spores! What moonsugar cart did they drag you out of?\n\nI'm near to finishing the new toxin, but I need to know the current status of the infection. Examine the diseased nodule at the tower's base and report back.

I can't say it's always been perfect, but my group's the best at what we do.\n\nWe even guarantee that our client will be fully satisfied or their money back! Won't find other ghost hunters offering that, I promise.

This team here? This team's the best ghost hunting team in all of Tamriel.\n\nWe all have a special connection with the realm of the dead in one way or another. It helps us communicate and problem solve when it comes to spirits.

Well then maybe we should talk when we're done! You could round out our group.\n\nWe're always looking for a little muscle. We thought Sharz knew how to fight. I mean just look at his arms! But … he's a pacifist. So, eh, oh well.

Near-death experiences. Cast a lightning spell while wading in water? Could put you one step into the great beyond. \n\nThere's just something about having one foot in the grave that ghosts relate to.

To the untrained eye, this appears to be nothing more than an unfinished cave. My eye is nothing if not trained, though. \n\nI suspect this was a ritual chamber of some sort. Ancient Chimer death rites were certainly practiced here!

A good question. Do we offer up the past to the curious, letting them trample on the sanctity of the dead? Or do we keep our secrets?\n\nCertainly, I won't do more than hint about it until the final volume, "Narsis Dren and the Golden Chimer Skull."
You've taken up this fight, but it's our fight! They've robbed and wronged us more than blood can pay, but we'll try!\n\nDrive them back to the Reach, burn their lands, butcher their kin!
I prefer my waters to remain still. Calm.\n\nPrying causes ripples, and ripples lead to more dry questions.

He did. And he told me to tell you. But why he needs your help when he has me, well, that's just beyond my comprehension.\n\nNarsis said that he found new information. He said that the scroll was not about Dreloth tomb—it pointed toward Veloth tomb!

You better get moving if you're going to help my Narsis. Veloth tomb is on the west coast, just south of Gnisis.\n\nBorfree can make his own way, just like you. He's reliable like that. Me? I might hire a mage. Portals are so much nicer than walking.

Oh yes. We had a lovely meal by candlelight, talked about the new book he's working on, drank some wine. Then off he went, like a flash, into the tomb!\n\nUnfortunately, I have not heard so much as a peep out of him in a guar's age.

No, of course not. This is Narsis Dren we're talking about! Famed hero and adventurer.\n\nIf you aren't too busy, though, I'd appreciate it if you could head inside and check on him. Just in case. Sometimes Narsis gets a little distracted, you know.

Findun collects it from a secret location, where the sea meets the swamp in perfect harmony. Contains just enough salt to nourish my scales without drying them.\n\nYou can buy it from him or fill a bucket yourself. Then we can talk.

Treasure, relic … I'm sure there's something important hidden in the ruins. According to local rumors, people disappear around Bal Fell all the time. That's what sparked my interest. Mysterious happenings often extend my fame and fortune.
Hmm. I suppose there could be a connection.\n\nOn the other hand, never attribute to ancient curses what can be explained by greed and laziness, I always say.
That's perfect! Go and cause a distraction and I'll get you a sheet of parchment.\n\nI'll meet you by the tree next to the lighthouse docks when I've accomplished the task.
That's a distress signal! And it came from Firemoth Island!\n\nNo time to prepare. We have to rescue the slavers' prisoners!

A thousand times, yes!\n\nOur Mistress has a mixed reputation. Outsiders often say she is cold and calculating. That may be, but I don't mind. She cares for us from a distance—intervening only when necessary. She respects our freedom.
We pray for her recovery every day. If Dratha dies, I fear that Vos will die with her.

No one of note. Just a pretentious, arrogant author and adventurer with an over-inflated sense of self-importance. He's an irritating Dark Elf who loves to hear himself talk. And the topic of conversation? The greatness of Narsis Dren.\n\nThe s'wit.

Have you read them? She's a brilliant detective. I fear Stibbons got the wrong idea and thinks he can find the missing mages, just like Investigator Vale.\n\nWhen you locate him, I shall express my disapproval for his reckless disregard of his duties.

What would I do with him? Chain him to a post?\n\nHis life no longer serves the House's interests. I don't expect an outlander to understand, but this needs to be done. Honestly, I doubt he'll give you a choice in the matter.
I didn't see much myself. I was evacuated well before the threat could reach me. Many weren't so lucky. I regret I'll be reporting that most of the Telvanni working on the tower died.
Not while she's with Master Fyr. He would never let anything happen to her. He's very protective of us.\n\nI can't speak for the rest of you.
I don't suppose he offered up a handy map or some directions to where he's hiding? No, of course not. \n\nThis damn spirit wants to use one of our own against us. Well, two can play at that.

What is Barbas after? Wait, gears click into place … the reservoir! You need to reach the reservoir that contains Vivec's stolen energy before Barbas!\n\nI can get us to the entrance in Seht's Vault, beneath the Mournhold Temple. Ready to go?

If we can lure a spirit into this ward, we'll have it under our control—temporarily anyways. We'll be able to question it. If the spirit is bound to this Galgalah, it'll be compelled to tell us where he hides.

By breaking it down to its very essence and then rebuilding it again.\n\nI need you to destroy these spirits until you find one powerful enough that its essence remains. Bring that essence back to us and we'll do the rest.

Forgot to factor in the presence of Sunna'rah. Between the connection to Sotha Sil and the amount of Vivec's energy flowing through it, the Hound could use the staff to trick the entryway's guardians.\n\nHe'll have a tougher time once inside, though.

The Clockwork City is on alert now, thanks to Barbas. If you aren't a factotum, the guardian will try and kill you.\n\nYou aren't a factotum by any chance, are you? No, you don't smell like oil and I can't hear the sound of whirring gears. Too bad.

I'm sure that's not correct. As I've stated, I'm not a combat mage. I'd just get in your way.\n\nBesides, the factotums should recognize me as an apprentice of Sotha Sil. That might come in handy later, as long as I don't attack them beforehand.

I couldn't bear gazing upon Tirwin since mother rebuked me, but now I can't wait to see her lovely face again!\n\nI'll be down at the swamp where she hunts shells, come find me once you've finished dealing with Mother. She'll be at our tower.

Haha! Galgalah does not hide, but a good first question. He is not here. This ruin merely acts as a dungeon for his captive souls. You will know it soon enough.\n\nHis fortress is near, if you look closely. The lava pass under the bridge of stone.

She clings to her shell. Our master likes to toy with his puppets before their end. I remember my death vividly. If Galgalah were to be defeated, I'd not be saddened. But there would be consequences.\n\nLast question. Choose carefully.

Galgalah's vessel must be sundered. His essence will spill from it like a broken dam, seeking another victim to drown in the flood. Your friend most likely. Kill her as they struggle and Galgalah will not have strength to resist the pull of the Void.

I mean, I know you're supposed to be our bodyguard, I just didn't expect we'd need the position to be taken quite so literally.\n\nYou know what, I'm going to let you do your job. I might even know where Galgalah is.
Right. We passed it on our way here, just south. I'll mark it for you.\n\nGo and do whatever it takes to save our friend. Farwen's strong. If anyone can deal with an evil spirit in them, it's her.
Galgalah … yes. His presence is all around. Smothering. \n\nI—I need to rest. I'm so tired. Just let me lie down for a moment.
I—I have to stay awake? My body feels so heavy, but I'll—ah!\n\nGods, it hurts! I can feel him clawing at the back of my eyes! I … I don't know that I can do this!
Ah! I don't know …!\n\nFinish me. End my life before this spirit can take control. I don't want to be his puppet.
Tell Theyo thank you. Thank you for letting me join his little band of adventurers. It wasn't a boring life.\n\nI'll be at peace with this, I think. Just … argh—just do it!
What do you know of my gods …! Hah—the irony. My fate left in the hands of my faith … I want to live! Divines, you hear me! I'm going to live!\n\nIt—it's quiet now. It's quiet. Let's get out of here.

Gods that's awful. Truthfully, that fear's been in the back of my mind since you warned us about Galgalah.\n\nThis is dangerous work. It's easy to forget that until death finally catches up. Farwen was with us so long … Sharz will be devastated.

Sharz is getting some rest and Lord Thanlen is trying to figure out how to weasel out of paying us, but if Galgalah is banished, and he was the controlling force behind the haunting, it'll clear soon. We were successful.\n\nStill, it wasn't worth it.

Ah, ha! Good spirits! I'll have to remember that one!\n\nWhy wouldn't we be? You saved our dear Farwen and rid the world of a terrible evil! Farwen told us all about your battle to banish Galgalah. The stuff of legends!

She said you destroyed his material body and drove him out of those ruins. With Galgalah gone, those other bound spirits will clear out soon enough as well.\n\nNot even Lord Thanlen can argue the results! Our job is a success because of you!

Oh! Oh … of course Daynillo told you about that. Did she mention it's suicide? I'm sure she didn't.\n\nI don't doubt Master Fyr will be fine passing through the rift, but anyone else? I'm not staking my life on it.
By the Three! Progress always comes at a cost! Telvanni understand that. They'd tell you they'd be honored to be associated with such a breakthrough, if they could.
No one persuades Mils to do anything. I'm quite impressed. That will certainly save me a trip.\n\nI suppose I should head home straightaway.
Or perhaps you should stop butting into our personal affairs. Have you considered that?\n\nI have nothing else to say to you. Good day.
I merely cling to what's left of who I was. I am a lingering shame on my family and my order, but I cannot abandon that life.\n\nHere, perhaps, I'll find the means to reclaim it.
I once protected those who you would have me prey upon. The power you speak of comes at too high a price!\n\nKeep this beastly existence, I will have my old life or none at all.
I don't expect mercy from a Daedric Prince, but I can think of no worse fate than this disease and all it threatens to take from me.

There's something in your eyes that tells me you are speaking more than kind words. I'd forgotten the feeling of hope, but I don't need it to continue this path.\n\nWhen I meet my maker, I will expect no mercy.

The ones who created me believe him to be our greatest progenitor. \n\nOnly the Lord of Troubles knows for certain, but if I throw myself at his feet and beg to be freed of this existence, I will do so.

Does seem odd, doesn't it? The first time, I thought it was an attempt to cover up fraud, but now I have another theory. I think the thieves are probing our records for wealthy marks.\n\nThis could be the start of a rash of high profile robberies!

Educated guess, mostly. It's an ideal location for a band of outlaws to hole up that's convenient to the regions that were robbed.\n\nWhat cinched it for me though, was a witness who identified their leader as Bralsa Inlador. She's wanted in Zainab.
I don't have much in the way of specifics, but the fact that the tax offices were raided in several regions in a relatively short period of time, I'd say they have numbers.

A test Ulran failed. Eris was devastated when his son sided with the savages and his daughter ran away. He decided to resign his position. He'll make the announcement today.\n\nEris hopes to restore his family, but I think it's a lost cause.

Molag Bal's plans to drag this world into Oblivion may have failed, but that hasn't stopped the Worm Cult from trying to fill this world with corruption. \n\nNow they're channeling the power of Ashalmawia's shrine to summon Daedra. No end to them.

The Worm Cult is trying to fill this world with Molag Bal's corruptions. The Tribunal have protected Vvardenfell from his Dark Anchors, but that hasn't stopped his thralls from doing all they can.\n\nLike using an ancient shrine to summon his minions.
It'll have to do. Even if you killed every Worm Cultist in the place, there will always be some other stupid fetcher waiting to meddle with a Daedric shrine.\n\nJust have to stay vigilant.

What do you take me for, a pretender? Aside from outlanders quick to brag and quicker to die, I am the only thing keeping Bal's minions confined to Ashalmawia.\n\nI came to Vivec for resupply and to enlist some help.

Any and all. So far it's mostly been Scamps or the odd clannfear poking out from the ruins, but the sounds I've heard echoing out of that place are fetching troubling. \n\nI think the cultists are becoming more practiced with their summoning.

Surely an adventurer of your stature isn't frightened of a single Dremora? Summoning Daedra is no more dangerous than taming bears—and even the dull-witted Orcs can do that.\n\nIt's quite safe. I'll send it away as soon as our business is concluded.

Surely an adventurer of your stature isn't frightened of a single Dremora? Summoning Daedra is no more dangerous than taming bears—and even you dull-witted Orcs can do that.\n\nBelieve me, it's quite safe. I'll send it away as soon as I'm finished.

Indeed? What ambition! As you can see, Barbas isn't a bad dog. He does get easily excited and overzealous. He embellished my plan somewhat, but it all worked out in the end. And we found the Clockwork City.

This little flea thinks it's smart, but my plans are beyond its comprehension! Still, by delaying the inevitable, you caused my associates and I some trouble. You'll stay here until you're no longer a threat.\n\nHow does a few decades sound to you?

Of course not. Why should I be?\n\nThe powers of Oblivion hold no great mysteries for mages like me, and House Telvanni has no time for folklore and childish superstitions. What's the point of power left unclaimed?
Plans? No, of course not. I'll leave them to their business just as I always have.

Yes. Believe me, it's a rare and wonderful thing to live under the protection of a disinterested ruler. Self-determination. It'll be all the rage in a millennium or two, I guarantee it.\n\nNow, are we finished? I need those stones.

I'm sure they did. You'd like an explanation, wouldn't you? Fine.\n\nYou want to earn people's love? Here's the secret—just leave them alone. Treat them like adults, even when they act like children. The rest takes care of itself.
A bribe? Vehk's head, you really want to see him don't you?\n\nAll right, fine. Fork it over, flat-head. And keep this quiet, all right?

Disobeying orders, eh? Yeah, that sounds like Ralasa. Skeevy little nix, always sliming around the tower, jamming pies in her gob and pushing us around. To Dumac with her!\n\nGo ahead. But if I find out you're lying, I'll put a knife in your eye.
That's a couple minutes too many. Now clear off my stoop, you flat-headed s'wit.
Well, that's a couple minutes too many. Now clear off my stoop, you flat-headed cur.

Disobeying orders, eh? Yeah, that sounds like Ralasa. Skeevy little nix, always sliming around the tower, jamming pies in her gob and pushing us around. To Dumac with her!\n\nGo ahead. But if I find out you're lying, I'll have your hide.
A bribe? Who'd you steal this from? All your kind are skeevy thieves.\n\nFine. Fork it over, flat-head. Keep this quiet, or I'll make a rug out of you, got it?

You keep asking the wrong question. I did not see anyone that night—I felt them! They made ripples in the water. I felt them stop by the tree that overlooks my pond. Then they moved off, toward the lighthouse.\n\nLook to the tree, moist one.

Captain Giravel, anointed ombudsman to Mouth Ralasa Delvi. \n\nNoticed you upstairs. Magister Gothren has little patience for interfering strangers. Even less for interfering assistants like Arith Sendrul.
I hope you will. For your sake.
Continue to guard it, for it represents not only my loyal servant Tarvus but also the past and future of my priesthood.\n\nAnd take this as well. To aid you in your next task.

You have been my eyes and ears in the world. Now be my hands. Within the modest sack resides gifts for my faithful servants. Blessings from me, though I would have you deliver them.\n\nYou served me in adversity. Now join me in celebration!

As I call forth my faithful, reach into the sack and give them the first thing you find. They shall hear my words of praise and gratitude, while it shall be your hand that rewards them.\n\nAre you ready, friend of Vivec?
Face a truth that could destroy me, or wait for it to find me too. It's a lot to take in. Three watch over me ….\n\nI hope I see you again, friend.

I didn't stop to take a census as I was fleeing for my life. Suffice to say that the wraiths and skeletons will be the least of your problems.\n\nThose wretched Salothans have a veritable army haunting the place.

The entire Salothan lineage died out in a monumental battle, yet they are barely a footnote in history.\n\nOne does not secure a coveted historian role in the Temple by ambling along well-trod ground. I must uncover their lost past!

These aren't the benevolent ancestor spirits you may have heard of, outlander. They're mad, or cursed, or both.\n\nI would love to hear of their lives in their own words, but that's proven impossible. They must go!
Oh, that was easy! I put a sleeping draught in the ale they ordered for <<1>>'s birthday. The guards were unconscious within the hour.\n\nI hope I can be of service again. For the Tribunal!

Ah, that was a most useful cultivation. He has to be worried a bit as well, but is probably safe. Even so, he won't try to help me. I can't say that I blame him. He only just achieved his goal of being Gothren's Mouth.

Magister Otheri made a discovery some weeks ago—a relic, or some Dwarven device perhaps. He refuses to share the details, so I am compelled to take those details by force.\n\nSteal his notes from Tel Naga and deliver them to my new Mouth, Arith.
I never said House Telvanni was perfect. We take the good with the bad.\n\nWhen I sit on the Council I'll put things right, how's that?
Well, you're tardy. I sent the others ahead. May as well settle in here, at the rate you move they'll be back before we finish this conversation.
Malignant spirits—that's enough to do their job. Or it should be, if they're such experts.\n\nIf you'd like to do yours, Valenvaryon is to the east, through the pass.

And whose fault is that? Every day that land sits useless, it's my coffers that suffer. I wasn't about to let Theyo squander our time entertaining the tall tales of these Ashlanders.\n\nThe fewer of these "body snatcher" fables they hear the better.

Galgalah is a body shifter. A spirit who expels living souls and uses their bodies as puppets.\n\nThough his spirit is bound to Valenvaryon, once possessed of a vessel he is free to roam and lure more into his trap.

Just stretching my legs … and keeping an eye out for Magister Otheri. You know these Telvanni—always barging in without warning and throwing their weight around. \n\nCome to think of it, he's been visiting more often than usual. I wonder why.
Our wards would not allow evil spirits to enter the camp.\n\nLord Thanlen is simply as the outside people of Vvardenfell would put it—an ass.
If we knew, Galgalah would not still exist. Killing him while he occupies a vessel only frees his spirit.\n\nThe only answer is to offer nothing to him, wisdom the man outside does not hear.
Sure. I've been keeping a sharp eye on Otheri ever since he set up shop in here.\n\nI still don't know what the damned thing does, but I'll tell you what I can.

So we've got a deal? Good.\n\nNow, pin those ears back and listen. Otheri locked the crystal in this machine to keep it working, but he took certain parts so no one else could turn the damn thing off. We get those parts, we get the crystal.

Well, that does make things easier. Gold's gold, right?\n\nSo, Otheri locked the crystal in place and took certain parts of the machine so no one else could turn the damn thing off. We need those parts to turn off the machine and get the crystal.

Prism? Oh. Right, now I see it.\n\nI guess he found it in the ruin, yeah. All kinds of Dwarven antiques in there, along with the parts you need. I think he hides the pieces to keep us from nabbing the crystal, the paranoid old skeever.

Sorry, but I skipped school the day they taught Dwarf machine-magic. Got no idea, friend.\n\nI could hazard a guess. Looks a little like my pa's old jaw harp. So maybe it makes music or something? Some kind of death-music I bet. Damn Dwarves.

Let's see. Oh yeah, this is just the thing. Ha! You're all right, bear cub!\n\nOnce I pawn this gibberish off, it's chill winds all the way back to Skyrim! I'll finally breathe crisp mountain air again—not lung-fulls of ash and kwama spit.

Oh, right. Afraid you're on your own there, friend. I know the parts, but don't have a horker's clue where they go. So … good luck?\n\nIf you're passing through Molag Mar anytime soon, keep an eye out for me. Mead's on Lothnarth, all right? So long.

Hmm. That would be unfortunate for you. Luckily, you have me to assist you. Well, me and Sunna'rah.\n\nExpend a small amount of Vivec's energy at the statue and that should provide enough of a distraction for me to pull you out of there.

A rascal like me has to look out for his own interests, right?\n\nOtheri dropped his key a few days back. I grabbed it and made a wax mold while he wasn't looking. Didn't take long to make a rough copy. You've got to jiggle it a bit, but it works.

Your friend will die soon. Destroy Galgalah's vessel and his essence will seek safe harbor in her weakened body. His power will sustain it, and she will live, buying her a few more precious years. \n\nIf she's strong enough to suppress him.

She's around here somewhere. Nix-hounds vanish when they're afraid, and Nixxie's a bit skittish. She'll head off toward the water after I call her.\n\nLook around the shorelines and you'll probably find her digging up shells. Just go where she points.

Spoken like a true Telvanni.\n\nIf you bring the goods to me in Sadrith Mora, I'll take credit for their safe return. Ralasa's gone to great lengths to discredit me, you see. My muthsera knows this. If I succeed, he'll see that I am the fitter servant!
I don't want to be bought, I want to be free. After all Faras and Llonas have taken from me, I don't want them to profit from my release. At least let me cost them.

Right. I'm sure that's a delicate subject for someone of your … is "breed" the word? Truth be told, I've always been a fierce proponent of beast rights.\n\nIf you only return the tome, pendant, and gold, our scheme will probably still work.

No, no, that's inadvisable. The atelier has defenses. You have no idea what it will do if it marks one of Sotha Sil's apprentices as an enemy—and neither do I!\n\nYou go. I'll use the controls over there and help you from out here.

I see my faith in you was not misplaced. We will discuss your evidence and more, but not in this hall.\n\nYou trusted me and helped me gather the evidence I needed. Now I shall trust you with the secret I have carried for years. Come. Follow me.
If my benefactor wished to discuss details in the open, why send a messenger? The matter is for your ears only.
My benefactor awaits nearby. Do not tarry.

It's too dangerous to stick around without the wards. We'll drag Lord Thanlen back to safety, kicking and screaming if we have to.\n\nI don't care about the money, just save Farwen … but if you do banish Galgalah, we'll have means to celebrate with.

Sun-in-Shadow asked me to come measure her for a new dress. Soon after I arrived, a pack of Telvanni thugs burst through the door and dragged her off. One of them shouted something about Tel Aruhn.\n\nThat's all I know! Please, just set me free.

The moons are kind. I knew you would not betray a fellow child of Jone and Jode.\n\nWe stored Gothren's trinkets in crates nearby. The smugglers will groan at their absence, but we would rather face the wilds alone than go back to Tel Aruhn.

Oh, genealogical records related to the earliest Velothi settlers. It could improve our understanding of the origins of the Great Houses a hundredfold.\n\nAnd who knows what other lost knowledge waits within the library? It really is quite exciting!

So Edryno finally came through, did she? And she sent you in her place, no doubt because she believes I will turn her into a vvardvark, or such nonsense. The things these commoners believe.\n\nI shall, of course, dock her payment for the late delivery.

Oh come now. I don't hate you. I just see the truth of your nature.\n\nYou beasts make wonderful servants, but to pretend you possess the same faculties as mer, or even men, is absurd. You were born to serve, just as we were born to rule.

No one likes a guar licker, you clawless kitten!\n\nIt happened a few days back. Weird cultists just barged in and took over the mine. This one managed to get away, but the Crew Chief and some of the others are still out there. Happy now, fish breath?

Chaos Ball sounds simple. You grab the ball and hold onto it for as long as you can. The longer you last, the more points you earn. It gets a bit more complicated when you're also running for your life, dodging swords and spells from the other team.

Ah! One of my personal favorites. Unlike our other games where you must stand fast, Crazy King gets the blood really flowing. In this game the capture point keeps moving. Keep your feet quick and your shields up. Difficult to win when you're dead!

Anyone can claim a capture point, but it's a true test of skill to master Domination. Seize and protect as many capture points as you can. The team with the most territory in the end wins. In this game you must dominate your rivals, or be dominated!

Yes. Exactly that. Kwama workers produce a pheromone unique to their colony. Unfortunately, these colonies often compete over resources, making them natural enemies. Hence the infanticide.\n\nNow if you don't mind, this egg is getting very heavy.
You haven't heard? \n\nMore dangerous than the depths of Oblivion. More deadly than a Daedric Titan. Pit Daemons! The Battleground champions that rule over all!
No one needs to know what actually happened to Galgalah. I … I have things under control.\n\nHe's gone from the ruins which means we did our job and get paid. Why else does it matter?
Need you ask? \n\nFire Drakes rain down flames of destruction upon their foes! We unleash an inferno to smite our enemies! Fear the Burn!
Storm Lords thunder across the field, striking our foes down faster than they can blink. We're a whirlwind of pain that smashes enemies to bits. \n\nAlways a glorious sight to see!
Did I say the Eight? I, uh, believe in all gods—the Eight included. It's part of my strength.\n\nIn fact I should pray. Right now. Good day.
I'm thankful for your concern, but the Eight will protect me and guide my hand.\n\nNow, please, you're making much out of nothing. I will be fine.
For someone who's helping me out this much, you can ask as many as you like!

The Buoyant Armigers comprise one of the military orders of the Tribunal Temple. They seek to emulate Lord Vivec's deeds through actions and words.\n\nPoor Urnsi! Those monsters went straight for her. Her blood flowed like lava from Red Mountain!

Good. I will follow you and help steer slaves toward the exit. If all goes as planned, we will all leave together.\n\nOne last thing—we must be careful to avoid drawing the eye of Slavemaster Arenim. You will never face a more ruthless mage.

Good. I will follow you and help steer slaves toward the exit. If all goes as planned, we will all leave together.\n\nOne last thing—we must be careful to avoid drawing the eye of Slavemaster Arenim. You will never face a more ruthless mage.
I know it may be strange, but my Rosy stands out from the rest of her kind. Just one look at her sweet face and you'd understand.\n\nWhy did I think a leash would help?
You know, you're right! Rosy would never ignore my calls. She must have wondered off further than I thought.\n\nThank you, friend. I'll go search for her.
She must see what her beloved House does to us. She fixes her eyes on the pages of her tomes, but remains blind to the suffering of her people. I care about her too much to let her remain so lost.

I must believe it. My heart is brilliant, but her brilliance gleams like a diamond—cold and hard edged. There is warmth in her, I know this. The Telvanni smothered it, but it can be rekindled.\n\nPerhaps seeing her kin will make the difference.

I need to understand why he would choose … this. Scrambling through a filthy mine, risking capture and execution, instead of staying safe with me. It's madness.\n\nHe thinks I don't know slavery is wrong, but I do. He's the one who's naive.

Am I really so transparent? Yes, of course I want him to change his mind. If the guards catch him, or even if he gets away clean, I'll likely never see him again.\n\nIf he sees that I'm willing to listen, maybe that will make the difference.

Do you honestly think dung just disappears on its own? Where do you think it goes? Are there magical dung mages walking around, enchanting it away?\n\nNope. I shovel it. They don't care much about the roads, but the cities stay clean.

Well it isn't locked. Go ahead and take a peek.\n\nMight want to keep it quiet though. Don't want Otheri's guards spotting you—trust me. They see you dragging that tail around and they'll clap a pair of irons on you quicker than spit.
Yeah. Well, honestly I mostly just act like I'm working. Pay's the same and you sweat a lot less.

The parts you need are somewhere in Mzanchend, but I'm not sure where.\n\nI spent a lot of time watching Otheri. From what I can tell, you'll need a crank, a spur gear, one of the smaller pistons, and some kind of handle.

There was some confusion on that point. The things coming out of the rift appeared to be constructs, but like nothing anyone had seen. \n\nMaster Fyr's theory, which is assuredly correct, was that the rift converged with Clockwork City.
Master Fyr said about a dozen seasoned adventurers would do. Maybe less if they had extensive experience with planar travel, but he thought that unlikely.
Wait, are you saying you don't know who Divayth Fyr is?

The Telvanni were expanding the workshop into the caverns beyond this chamber, where the rift came into being. \n\nIt seemed a trick of the light at first, like a carnival mirror, then it began to tear. Wider and wider, until … things spilled out.
Trying to make myself useful by tallying casualties and damages for Master Fyr. \n\nI know he's unhappy that I won't accompany him into the rift, but maybe this will help make up for it.

Sailors, pirates, oh it has quite the little collection. Whoever doesn't drown ends up under its spell, including some of my own workers. \n\nWe've made several attempts, but they cannot be reasoned with. Just make sure they don't get in your way.

Apparently it sang a little song and all of my "well-respected" sailors just went belly up and ran the ship ashore. From what I can gather this isn't the first time it's happened either.\n\nReally, I've never heard of something so outlandish!

You know, you go out into the world with big dreams. Like being successful, and worldly, and ridiculously wealthy.\n\nAnd then your first big shipment is destroyed by a singing Nereid and you really start to question things. Namely your career choices.

My brother is respected and revered. He has allies in all of the tribes, not to mention his personal Red Exiles. We have to proceed with caution, respect the Ashlander customs and traditions.\n\nAnything else will lead to violence and bloodshed.

If you can slip into town, sure, Veya should be told. But you didn't take my advice. You killed Redoran soldiers. That's your trouble to deal with.\n\nI need to present my completed writ, so I'll catch up with you and Veya later.

There were creatures … familiar beasts, but they weren't simple flesh any longer. They were fashioned. Joined with machines. Beautiful and terrible at the same time.\n\nI don't know if they live, but they hunger.

I—yes. He's the most famed and respected mage in Vvardenfell, maybe the world. There isn't a subject of magic he can't discuss in totality.\n\nI really hope he'll forgive me for abandoning his expedition ….

Master Fyr is very generous. He's let my sister and I stay here with him for nothing at all and he spends a great deal of time with us. There's so much going on behind his eyes, you risk getting lost when you meet them—but I digress!

About keeping Eoki here? No. I struggled with the idea of him hating me for this, but in the end, I'm sure he'll see it was for the best.\n\nHe'll have the very best of things, and my love to fortify him.

Yes, once the time is right—once he understands what he'd been giving up if he ran again. He belongs here. He'll see that eventually.\n\nWith his support I'll bend this House to our desires. There's no telling what we can achieve together!

Important? I suppose that depends upon who you ask. My husband thinks so.\n\nI'm the treasurer here in Balmora. My job requires that I record all important transactions regarding Redoran finances and balance everything to the last gold piece.
What? She would keep me in chains to earn my affection?\n\nShe was right all along. She has a Dark Elf's heart—just as cruel and possessive as House Telvanni.

Yes, but that was different. I only wanted what was best for her. For both of us ….\n\nHist's tears, you are right. This place … do you see how it twists us? How it dries out our hearts and turns all to selfishness? Forgive me, friend. Forgive me.

Bothamul and his Ropefish will ferry us to the coast, then load us into a fishing boat. With luck, we will reach the mainland, then take the long road back to Black Marsh. To home. I thank you for all you've done, but I fear I will never be the same.

Councilor Eris, who oversees Redoran operations in the Balmora region. Our family is one of the most respected in the House. I'm surprised you haven't heard of us … wherever it is you come from.\n\nNow if you don't mind, I have a lot of work to do.

The scars may fade. The pain in my limbs may melt away. My soul though … my soul feels like it is drowning.\n\nI thought myself better than the Dark Elves. Purer. But in the end, I tried to take what I wanted by force, just like they do.
She stormed out of the house after a heated argument with her father. Nothing unusual in that. But when she didn't return … well, that's when both her father and I started to worry.

As I said, Veya is headstrong. Confident. Perhaps too confident. She might join the Morag Tong just to spite her father. Or run off to fight in the war. Something reckless along those lines.\n\nPlease, do what you can and find my daughter.

I … I'd rather not talk about that. It's a private matter concerning the family.\n\nThe relevant fact remains that my daughter took her most cherished possessions and left home. I'm worried that she's going to do something that can't be undone.

Everything you uncovered suggests the staff and Sotha Sil's missing tool are one and the same, and it's obviously connected to Chodala's newfound powers. Bring it back here so I can study it.\n\nThe solution resides in the staff, I'm sure of it.

Some are Dwemeri. Tinkered with in ways beyond even my experience. Intriguing, but not nearly so interesting as the fabricants.\n\nTheir marriage of the organic and inorganic defies all contemporary wisdom. But are they as they seem?
Given the eruption of fabricants into the caverns, my theory is it somehow intersects with Clockwork City. Anything beyond that is pure speculation.
I'd assumed you knew whose home it was you were standing in.\n\nDivayth Fyr. Does that name's significance escape you as well?

What indeed. I'd only heard descriptions of the creatures in my talks with Barilzar, Sotha Sil's former apprentice. Even he doesn't seem to have a full grasp of their design.\n\nThey are life driven by clockwork, if all is to be believed.

The Ashlanders hold to superstitions the way kwama protect their eggs. If they really consider Chodala to be the Nerevarine, then any action you take against him will enrage the tribes.\n\nTalk to Seryn and see if she can suggest an alternative course.
The domain of Sotha Sil. A world of his own design. Privilege of being a god.\n\nWhether it exists in Nirn is the subject of much conjecture. Perhaps we'll finally lay that debate to rest.

We talk to my brother. Try to convince him this isn't the way. Barring that, we make sure the Wise Woman doesn't get drawn into his madness.\n\nWhatever Chodala says or does—don't attack him! We don't need a war between the Houses and the Ashlanders.
Then you should be honored to see my work firsthand. I'll make a note of your contribution to my next book, posthumous or no.
A woman of taste. I would offer you a private reading, but as you can see my new home is not fit for company. Perhaps after we've finished our sojourn in Clockwork City.

For your sake, I hope you're more prepared for what's to come.\n\nAs for me, you could say I am a practitioner of magic. If you were partial to understatement. I am the premiere authority on extra-planar travel. My writings are taught the world over.

It didn't seem like a bad idea at the time. What good is a queen without a colony? We sprayed just a smidge of pheromones here and there, and kwama started rushing in!\n\nThe issue was getting them to stop. We're still working through that one.

We had a rather nasty string of kwama warriors begin to fight over the queen's "affections." Took us all by surprise when they started seeing the miners as challengers. Sadly, our standard procedures didn't cover a passion driven battle to the death.

The miners said he's the biggest kwama they've ever seen, and certainly the nastiest. He's the cause of more worker deaths than the rest of the colony combined. \n\nIf we're to salvage this situation, he simply cannot remain.
It does. Perhaps, with time, we may all learn to forgive ourselves.\n\nFarewell, my friend. I hope we meet again some day.

I have no idea! I'm starting from complete ignorance with this particular species. That's the beauty of discovery—the possibilities are endless! It's also precisely the reason I need so many specimens to continue my research. \n\nIsn't it exciting?

Honestly, what am I not researching? The obvious alchemical ramifications of such a unique strain of fungi cannot be ignored, but there are so many possibilities. \n\nTo give but one example, I've already found them to be an amazing addition to soup!

I usually find it best to make peace with the local fauna when doing field work, but this nix-ox has proved incorrigible. Not only does it plan to eat my mushrooms into extinction, it's also exceedingly malicious, hostile, and just plain unsanitary.

I try to pick up the pieces of my broken heart and continue my studies.\n\nLetting Eoki go was agony, but you were right—this is better for both of us. I spent so much time trying to earn his affection and prove my loyalty …. Now I can truly focus.

The game. My role in the House. My future as a magister. All of it.\n\nPerhaps, when I've reached my full potential, I'll seek Eoki out again. See the world, you know? Until then, I live the life of a Telvanni.

Busy. Working hard to circumvent Magister Gothren's desire to keep me from gaining further rank within House Telvanni. I've learned my lesson, though. I am being very careful about any dealings with him.

It would seem so. Gothren does not have friends on the council, and it was known that Slavemaster Arenim dealt cruelly with slaves. \n\nSo the council "sympathized" with the disruption of his mine, but had no resources available to assist in retrieval.

It was noted that Magister Gothren lost slaves from one of his mines. That the rebels also slew his slavemaster during their uprising. Arith said his master was quite peeved that the council was not outraged on his behalf.

I think his spirits are still cast down. I know mine are. I wish he would talk to me, but he won't. And I can't keep making up excuses to visit Master Firuth, just to try and snatch a moment to speak with Eoki. It would raise suspicions.

No. I did get Master Firuth to purchase him. A favor I will have to repay manyfold. \n\nFiruth rather likes him. He's always been curious about Argonian culture and magic. I am hopeful that in time, Eoki will let go of his anger at me.
Indeed. My … or rather, our, adventures have taught me to be a bit more circumspect in my ambitions. \n\nA little patience goes a long way. At least that is what Mouth Angharal has counseled.

In all my thousands of years, how didn't I think of that? Translocation does not work by your whims and desires, or even mine. \n\nBe glad you needn't traipse through half of Oblivion searching for your point of origination.

No. Intelligent as this machine is, it lacks the awareness to create such an event. It was simply attempting to cope with the anomaly.\n\nThat does not mean there are not answers to this phenomena here. I intend to find them.
Doubtlessly. However, I'm afraid I have no further need of your brand of assistance at the moment.\n\nWould you be on your way? You're becoming a distraction. You know my opinion of distractions.

We thought the Incarnates were possessed by the spirit of Nerevar, but each had a critical flaw that made them destined to fail to fulfill the prophecy. Their spirits reside here.\n\nYes, you should speak to the Incarnates. I see Azura's wisdom now.

You agreed to work for my husband, Councilor Eris of House Redoran. We want you to find our daughter, Veya, and make sure she returns home.\n\nDuring your first excursion, you discovered that Veya had joined Naryu Virian and the Morag Tong.

A cult of sanctioned murderers for hire. They serve a purpose, but I have no use for them. Naryu said she wouldn't allow a meeting unless Eris dismissed his hired help—all but you, that is.\n\nI just want Veya to come home. I miss my daughter.

I don't attend council meetings, so I wasn't there when they debated the fate of my son. But my husband assured me the proceedings were fair. Ulran received the punishment he deserved.\n\nAt least, that's what he told me at the time.

My husband and the house can go to Oblivion! All I care about right now is my children.\n\nThey killed my son because he did what he believed was right. Now my poor Veya is in danger. Eris can stand by the house, but he might have to do so alone.
I can't believe that my son did anything that required him to die, house honor be damned!\n\nI just want my children back home, safe and sound.

You agreed to work for my husband, Councilor Eris, to find our daughter, Veya. \n\nYou found Veya and kept her safe from the Warclaws mercenary band, but in doing so you discovered that they killed my son, Ulran, when they attacked an Ashlander camp.

My daughter has joined the Morag Tong. She asked you to help find out what happened to her brother. It seems Captain Brivan may have been involved in Ulran's death. \n\nNow my husband has asked you to keep Veya away until he can sort out what happened.

The Archcanon? Lord Vivec's high priest? Suddenly the gears align ….\n\nI can think of a number of reasons that ALM and VI would want to know about SI and his tools, but some doors just shouldn't be opened.

And I appreciate your help in this. That's why your name doesn't appear in the official records.\n\nThat might be my last official act for House Redoran. I've had it with honor and politics. I'll be leaving Balmora shortly.

Eris knows my feelings. If he does what he promises at the upcoming council meeting, then he can find me in Vivec City. If not, he can go to Oblivion.\n\nIf Veya wants to get in touch, let her know where I'll be. I'll respect whatever she decides.
The spiders. Those damned spiders. They … they talk to me. They want me to dance!\n\nMustn't … I mustn't dance for them. That would be … bad ….
Why do you think? No! Don't think! That's when they get you … they crawl into your mind. Don't let them … argh!\n\nI must go now.

You continue to work for my husband, Councilor Eris, seeking to bring about a reconciliation with our daughter, Veya. Along the way, you learned that her brother Ulran was exiled and subsequently killed while sheltering in an Ashlander village.

Did you? Well, that's why it was posted.\n\nIt's simple. Citizens tell us what they need and we arrange for the job to be completed. You'll be able to meet with the client before starting the task. They'll also have your reward, not us.

You accompanied Naryu to execute a writ on a Redoran councilor. While there, you discovered that Captain Brivan was involved in Ulran's predicament.\n\nI just wanted to say thank you for helping my daughter. I appreciate it more than you can know.
My kin remain missing. I will find them regardless of whether you speak truth or lies.

In my opinion? Probably nothing. We'll translate a few tablets, clean up some bones, guess as to who owned the place. We'll find a useless detail to insert into a dull chapter of a pompous book no one will read anyway.

Hungers are Daedra associated with Boethiah. This one was likely summoned by a cultist centuries ago. They are—as the name denotes—very hungry, especially for mortal flesh. I prefer pastries.\n\nI wouldn't fight one, but you seem more than willing.

Finding useless ruins is the family business. My own mother currently heads our research team. She insisted I put the notice up, if you must know.\n\nHonestly, if it was up to me I'd be a fat, happy baker right now. Instead I'm just a scrawny coward.
Certainly! A quaint port town like Seyda Neen would be a great place to start on such a vast island.
Of course! There's no better place to tour than the jewel of Vvardenfell, home to one of our living gods.

His calculations have grown incomprehensible to me, his theories turned to ramblings. But I know what he plans to do goes against nature itself. There's no predicting the chaos his success may bring.\n\nWe have to stop him before it's too late.

I respected him. He was brilliant, always looking at all the possibilities, at the entirety of our existence. But he's discovered something dangerous, and I have a feeling someone led him down that dark path. His notes may tell me who.

We must prepare for the worst. Magic has long lingering and far-reaching effects. Perhaps Master Alar can find reason and stop this experiment, but if he cannot then it falls to me to fix his mistakes. His notes will help me do that.

Alchemy, from the looks of it, though I see a few components related to Daedric magic.\n\nDead spiders, vials, various alchemical components … this must be how these mind spiders were created. They certainly don't appear to be natural creatures.

The notes in this journal … they refer to different kinds of spiders. Mind spiders, we already know about them. It also lists "pack spiders," "light spiders," and "exploding spiders." How exciting!\n\nSomeone is making spiders of nefarious purpose!

The journal indicates that victims controlled by the mind spiders are needed for some sort of Daedric ritual. We need to find whoever is performing this ritual and you need to make them stop. Then I can lead Stibbons and the others to safety.
Lies upon lies! Does it give them pleasure to invent reasons to bring us harm? If they seek our deaths, they should just come for them! \n\nThese ploys and ambushes are the acts of cowards!
Four have vanished since we arrived to find your Armigers building their garish shrine over our ancestral lands.\n\nMade prisoners of the false gods, or struck down by the likes of you, no doubt.
Your reasons mean nothing to me. I would kill you if I did not think it would give the slaves of the false gods another excuse to do harm.\n\nWhat proof do you need? What will make them leave us be?
Your pilgrims are not here. They litter the wild with their weakness. A beast's meal, nothing more. \n\nSee for yourself. You will find what's left of their camps here, where I have marked your map.
The burial ground has been disturbed recently. Once you see that we are innocent, we will learn if the truth lies with the dead.
Save your words. I will not forgive you, but I will forget this grudge if you put an end to the violation of our tribe.

I know you, hero. It's Old Man Eris I don't trust. He didn't tell you about Veya's brother, did he? How House Redoran exiled their favorite son? No? I didn't think so.\n\nVeya deserves answers and I promised to help her. You need to just walk away.

I see. Yes, I have been using our time gathered here to urge the other tribes to adapt and make allies. It's vital to prepare if we want to survive the change that's to come. \n\nIt hasn't been easy, but perhaps you could become a decisive example.

Simply show a willingness to help the tribes, or even just a willingness to learn their ways. Go and speak with them. Show them you can be trusted, and you will be rewarded with the favor of the tribes.
These damned Dark Elves cast me out! I went to them, lute in hand, to offer my aid and they mocked me. Me! Vigard the Sparrow!\n\nThey don't realize I can heal the miners with the power of music!

I don't have all the details. Something about cursed music? That brute Lathdar cast me out when I tried to ply my trade at the mine.\n\nUncultured simpleton! He doesn't understand the restorative power of song! Music can only be conquered by music!

Oh, gods no. I'm not about to set foot in that mine.\n\nWhat happens if I hear this music and the melody catches my ear? Such a cursed tune might meddle with my own creative genius. I follow my own unique muse, friend. I'm no plagiarist!
Difficult to say. A tonal codex sounds almost too good to be true. But I don't have the luxury of dismissing such rumors out of hand—particularly when a scoundrel like Lenarmen takes interest.

Not familiar with the myth?\n\nPriests will tell you that the god Lorkhan tricked various divine forces into creating the world. This upset the natural order of things, and so his fellow gods yanked his heart out as punishment.

Of course, outlander. Anything to assist you in your sacred mission.\n\nA mysterious force assaults Lord Vivec, stealing his energy and putting all of Vvardenfell in terrible danger. You agreed to help put an end to this attack.

No. I'm sure that was never the intention of the Father of Mysteries.\n\nChodala somehow modified the tool to turn it into a weapon. Whatever he's doing to steal Vivec's divine energy, he seems to be able to draw on some of the Warrior-Poet's power.

Not precisely. Your investigations on Vivec's behalf point to the Ashlander Chodala as the likely suspect. He claims to be the Nerevarine and wields Sotha Sil's tool. It's a staff Chodala calls Sunna'rah and we think it's the source of his power.

Well, if you're feeling spry, you could try to track down some information about this Bthark Prism Neramo keeps yammering about. I was ready to cut and run, but with your help we might still be able to turn a profit on this disaster.

I did.\n\nPulling Daren and Brerayne out wasn't too hard, but Lotaeel was anxious to dole out some justice along the way. Ended up stabbing and hacking our way out. We really stirred up the hornets' nest. Now Lenarmen's thugs are on high alert.

I once ran with the Camonna Tong. I wised up and got out, but not before seeing what kind of scum they truly are. When my business partners came to me with this issue, I said I'd take care of it.\n\nI'm more than happy to take the fetchers down a peg.

Hard not to take it personally sometimes. My own sister robbed our parents blind to pay for her skooma habit before running off with some fetcher. When I came to Vvardenfell I promised I'd never let that happen to any family under my watch.
Mages, mostly. Members of the so-called Great House Telvanni—one of the four Great Houses of the Dark Elves.\n\nThey love using that word … great. Great at ruining lives, perhaps.

Yes. And Khajiit also.\n\nYou see, for a Telvanni, life is nothing but a cheap struggle for mastery and control. Mastery of their dryskinned magicks, control of their mushroom towers, and dominion over people. People like us.

Not just our people, Hist-child. Khajiit as well.\n\nFor a Telvanni, life is nothing but a cheap struggle for mastery and control. Mastery of their dryskinned magicks, control of their mushroom towers, and dominion over people. People like us.

She spilled Redoran blood without a writ. She broke the rules of the Morag Tong. As I see it, I don't have a choice.\n\nVeya needs to remain dead in the eyes of Vvardenfell. Otherwise we'll all have to pay for the damage she's done.

Only if it fails, and that's not going to happen.\n\nSummerset is far enough away that no one will find her. Besides, Veya needs time to heal and make a fresh start. She'll be fine. Her new mentor is a pussycat compared to me.

I lost my brother, I killed my own father …. I kind of went crazy out there for awhile. I don't think I'll ever put this completely behind me. But I'll do what Naryu asks. I'll go away, finish my training. Try to make a new start.

To Summerset, but don't tell anybody. She was quite adamant about that.\n\nShe's given me a letter of introduction for some highfalutin Khajiit. Works for a queen or something. Anyway, he's going to be my new mentor.

Look, I'm sorry. Ulran's death made me crazy—that's no excuse—but I'm never going to forgive House Redoran for the attitudes that brought us here. I'm done with them.\n\nTake care of Naryu. I don't want her to get hurt because of me.

Though the methods to produce these kwama are far from sound, the end goal is still noble. These kwama may lead us to hardier, more disease resistant breeds. With ethical research practices I believe I can help produce a viable solution.
Bloodline? You don't mean …? That's impossible.

Sotha Sil's private domain? It's said that the place holds the secret to re-making Nirn … I suppose that would interest Barbas and his master, Clavicus Vile.\n\nBut Clockwork City can wait. The moonlet hanging above us? Not so much.
Indeed! The celebration remains quite popular even in the midst of war. All the soldiers are eager to earn greater glory on the battlefield.

If you know the legend of Pelinal Whitestrake and Saint Alessia, you are on the path to understanding.\n\nIf not, well … those who accept the blessing are renowned for their brave deeds in days thereafter. Surely that's something your people value?
I keep an old rival's recipe nearby. Go—find and memorize it. Return to me when you have done so.
Barrels. Sacks of grain. Kitchens, of course.\n \nIt's food. It's simply around. Find what you need and take it.
Ingredients? One is solid, the other liquid?\n\nTruly, I don't understand the question.

Quality food and drink boosts your energy, and a full belly lasts for quite some time.\n\nA provisioner's fare is much healthier than any old slop you find around. Why eat a bandit's grilled capon when you can make your own?

Provisioners are quite secretive, but all is fair in brews and stews. Some provisioners hide recipes in old drawers or shelves, thinking themselves clever.\n \nBetter to memorize the recipe. Then others cannot possibly learn your secrets.

Oh yes. Not only did Sotha Sil hide his greatest creation, he also protected it with powerful wards designed to keep Daedric entities from entering it.\n\nBarbas and his master will need to neutralize the defenses before they can step foot inside.

The shapeshifter? He's as tricky as his master, Clavicus Vile. I've heard he usually appears as a dog or a Scamp named Creeper.\n\nI never realized the Archcanon wasn't actually Tarvus anymore. If I'd been more observant, I could have stopped this.

The Lady of Twilight deals in magic and prophecy. She has a long relationship with our people. But we also see her as weaker than the Tribunal and beneath consideration.\n\nFor Vivec to reach out to her is unprecedented.

Really? Who should I blame then? House Redoran? Council Eris? Ulran for doing the right thing and starting this whole mess? I know! I'll blame the Ashlanders. Everybody else does, so why shouldn't I?\n\nAh, maybe I just need another bottle of wine.

I only know what I've heard. I've never visited the city myself.\n\nSotha Sil built the place as a miniature representation of the world, but with more cogs and gears than you usually find in nature. He called it his "forge of the future."

A figure of speech, perhaps. Sotha Sil believes he can reshape the world from within his city of brass tunnels and domes, but who knows what that even means?\n\nCertainly, Barbas thinks the place is important. Why else would he go to all this trouble?

Careful, outlander. Heresy isn't tolerated in Morrowind. Some revere Azura as the Anticipation of Sotha Sil, so a degree of veneration is permitted. But for one of the Tribunal to suggest seeking her counsel—that's unheard of!

Clavicus Vile is the Daedric Prince of Trickery. He loves to make bargains with mortals—especially deals that lean in his favor. As far as Daedric Princes go, he's not one of the nice ones.\n\nEven so, to go after Lord Vivec like this, such audacity!

I go back to doing what I do best and hope the Morag Tong never finds out what happened.\n\nAt least the deal we made protects my people. We've worked so hard to climb out of the shadows and regain our position. I'm glad I didn't jeopardize that.

Veya was a good apprentice. She would have made an excellent assassin. I just wish I could have done more to prevent what happened. At least—no, that's not something you need to know. At least not right now.

I can, can I? Well, aren't you the sentimental fool!\n\nAsk me about Veya again someday. After some of the pain has passed. Then I'll tell you a story. I guarantee it's one that will keep you on the edge of your seat. But not today, hero. Not today.

Seyda Neen is the preeminent port into Vvardenfell. I process new arrivals so the Tribunal knows who might be gallivanting across this fair land.\n\nIt's so much more prestigious than my efforts for the Gold Coast Trading Company.

Once, long ago, in another life, I served as a clerk for the company right here in Vvardenfell. Helped build many of the fine Imperial-style structures you see. I must have impressed House Hlaalu, for they offered me this distinguished position.
Tel Aruhn? Well, it's the big tower over there where Magister Gothren lives. And I'm sure this will surprise you, but he's not too keen on outlanders. I'd stay out of his way if I were you.

Such knowledge has been hidden even from me, Mortal. But I know someone who can provide you with the means to travel to Sotha Sil's creation.\n\nStand back and I shall summon the mage of cogs and gears.

No. This was more of a warning. And a disappointing one, as far as that's concerned. At least the previous notes came wrapped in a tasty treat. This just came in an envelope.\n\nBut it wasn't just for me. It was addressed to you as well.
Didn't they say? Why does no one read my reports? \n\nPulk. I believe the thieves are hiding out in Pulk.

House Hlaalu encroaching on ancestral Redoran lands! Building settlements even! I saw this coming ever since we let Fort Firemoth go fallow. Let your guard down even a little and those Hlaalu scribs will snatch away all they can!

Our sanctioned guild of assassins. Oh, it's all strictly above board. Necessary, even. Allows the houses to let off steam without costly wars and massive casualties.\n\nThe Morag Tong are strictly professional, nothing like that mad Dark Brotherhood.

Because they're getting the sharp end of the dagger, of course! Just you wait. Once a few House Hlaalu officials fall to the Morag Tong axe, Redorans will say the assassins are the best thing for commerce since we domesticated the kwama.

Oh my, well … she's very mysterious. Unusual, perhaps, but bold. She's going to do great things with her life, I just know it.\n\nYou don't want to fail her, however. She doesn't abide mistakes. That's why I do my best not to disappoint her.
"Saint Rilms gave up her shoes and posed as a beggar in order to get closer to the poor."\n\nI'm no saint, but religion is a useful tool when dealing with House Redoran.
Food sates me and clothing protects me. But gold gives me a choice. Saint Veloth illustrated the value of choice when he differentiated the good Daedra from the bad.
Blessings of the Three upon you.
Blessings of the Three upon you.
Running away from the war on the mainland, of course. More and more arrive each season. The new blood sends some Dark Elves into fits, but they agreed on shared borders when they signed the Pact.

I hatched with something of a wanderlust, so the journeys of Man, Mer, and beast are all currents that tug at me. I came to Molag Mar to follow the pilgrim's path. To learn all I could about how it shapes those who walk it, and the path itself.

That journeys tend to get off to rocky starts. Between the pilgrims disappearing and the mine being closed down, we are huddled inside the walls of the canton like the shells of our birth, aching to stretch our legs.

Not much, yet. I've been mired here, huddled in this canton like the roots of my mother tree, but I've heard talk that the roads are safe again.\n\nI hope that the pilgrims will be at ease enough that my close observation does not unsettle them.

Depends on how smart the Hound really is. With the staff, he can do what he came to do—manipulate the city's defenses.\n\nLooks like he called in skaafin to deal with Sotha Sil's fabricants. Poor little mechanicals are no match for Daedra.

Not a damn thing. It's just more of that Fate-Bearer nonsense. Spooky predictions designed to unsettle the reader. But Naryu Virian doesn't spook that easily. And neither do you.\n\nStill, watch your arse around shadows for awhile. Just in case.

Oh, nothing too terrible. Just that we may have altered fate's path, but one danger has been replaced with another. The flames have become shadows, "a spreading darkness that will consume the world." \n\nIt's kind of beautiful. Creepy, but beautiful.
<Father of Mysteries blesses you with his wisdom and vision. For a generous contribution in his name, Sotha Sil will grant you the power to revisit your choices regarding Skills.>
Your Skills have been reset.
Your Morphs have been reset.
<The Warrior-Poet blesses you with his wisdom and vision. For a generous contribution in his name, Vivec will grant you the power to revisit your choices regarding Attributes.>

Beleru's requests may appear straightforward, but many adventurers find them difficult to accomplish. The assortment of enemies she'll ask you to face are all powerful, and I would recommend gathering allies before heading out.

Traylan handles requests which the Temple has special interests in. His tasks require more subtlety, but they are by no means easy. Make sure to listen to his explanations carefully. It's also a good idea to speak to the clients beforehand.

Beleru Omoril and her brother Traylan will handle your assignments. Check in with them frequently to see if they have a job for you. They'll inform you what you need to accomplish and who made the request.
Your Attributes have been reset.
Musty rotting vegetable stench, in the tower. \n\nI have a sensitive nose. The smell is subtle, but once you notice it gnaws at you.  I had to come outside to get some fresh air.
He went outside, complaining of a smell no one else can sense. It's a convenient excuse to meet with his contact, if you ask me.
It's a breath of fresh air! We've finally got an active collaborator instead of a passive overseer! People here don't like change, but they'll see the benefits in time.

Do I need to remind you about all the things you helped me accomplish?\n\nWe stopped a plague in Deshaan. We helped Almalexia in Mournhold. We saved the king of the Nords. We even stopped a killer that turned delicious pastries into a weapon!

Three form the Tribunal. Mother Morrowind, Almalexia, is the protector of the weak and patron of the healers. Sotha Sil, the Father of Mysteries, is a tinkerer and a mage, an architect of time. Lord Vivec, the ever-vigilant, is a warrior and a poet.
