That device in the mine was silenced, but I can still feel its song.
That's what they tell me. Simply a case of frayed nerves and ringing ears. The healers say it will pass.\n\nI swear, though. Sometimes I can still hear a tune.

He was the firebrand who led the fight for freedom against our brutal taskmasters, the Ayleids. We hold that his actions were divinely inspired.\n\nThe Bridge of Heldon was one of his many victories, unifying the tribes of Men against the Elves.

I'm gathering research for Librarian Bradyn. He has a very ambitious project underway, so this assignment is the definition of prestigious.\n\nIf you'd like to know more about his grand project, you should visit the library in Vivec City.
What do you mean "as well"? I was given the privilege of taking exacting measurements and precise illustrations of the Redas family tomb.\n\nHmph, "rubbings." Please.
Well, just don't break anything while you're mashing coal against paper in my workspace.
Pff—What? What do you mean "you already got what he needed"? No, no, that can't be right. Whatever you were asked to do couldn't have any bearing on my assignment.

This, my friend, is the start of a legacy for not only Vivec, but for us all! What an honor! What a privilege! My work is tribute to part of the Tribunal. I couldn't be happier with my work right now.

Wood dust may get in the scales, but I do not mind. Sweat washes it away.\n\nWhen the city is complete, I will take my earnings and move to a nice swamp with no Baar Dau and fewer Dark Elves. Maybe start a family.

That's one I won't soon forget. Poor Veya. I was her mentor. I should have seen what was happening to her early enough to help.\n\nBut I wanted to ask you something. Why do you keep showing up and sticking your beautiful nose in my business?
Proper, painstaking research. Cataloging the appearance of the tomb in exacting detail. I don't know what Librarian Bradyn wanted from your "rubbings," but it's obviously not of the same importance.
Captain Naros stationed me to the canton indefinitely. I told her I'm fit for duty, but she won't budge. I can't even pretend not to look bored at this point.

When the Pact formed I told myself it was time to visit our newfound allies. So I've been to the swamps of the lizards and the lands of the puny Elves.\n\nIt's been a great journey so far, but Keba hates to travel.

Shor's bones, you expect me to travel alone? Or worse yet, you want me to leave poor Keba with my mother? That would just be cruel. I wouldn't want to wish that on a dog. \n\nEr, you know what I mean.
Some. We provide aid for the occasional adventurer and would-be explorer that limps out of the wilderness. That can be exciting. Breaks up the day.
See! I missed out on the most excitement this post has seen in years!\n\nUgh, just leave me here to wallow!

It was just a minor wound! She's overreacting. I mean, if those Ashlanders attack, more pilgrims will be in danger, right? So who's really taking the risk here?\n\nNo point in arguing, though. It's her call.
Clipped in the knee by a lucky dreugh in the mine. I might have gotten ahead of the cordon. By a good bit. But I'm up on my feet again and ready to serve!

There used to be more acolytes, but they never last long. No glamor out here in the wilderness, I suppose. I'm used to it by now. Plus, I have grumpy over there for company, if I ever need an earful of complaints.

It certainly sounded that way. The Hound said something about using Vivec's energy to open a portal. Why would he—oh no!\n\nThat much power could punch a hole through all of Sotha Sil's defenses, allowing Clavicus Vile to enter the city!

That would be catastrophic! Imagine a Daedric Prince with access to Sotha Sil's greatest invention. Who knows what damage he could do with the power of the Clockwork City at his command?\n\nWe have to keep going. We have to stop Barbas!

Still don't trust me after all we've been through together? Hmm. I probably wouldn't trust me, either.\n\nBut yes, the entrance is down here. In fact, the entire city is down here. We just need to get past those Daedra to reach it.
Once we preached Alessia's truth in the Temple District of the Imperial City, before its siege and sacking by Molag Bal. \n\nMany fell, but many fled, to carry on our work outside the city walls.

Once a slave, the Dragon God himself inspired her to rise up and rally the Men of Cyrodiil to overthrow their Ayleid masters. \n\nPelinal and Morihaus were her trusted confidants, and, depending on the translations, either or both were her lovers.

We made an arrangement with the general: in return for the garrison's protection, we would bestow blessings on any of your alliance who ask for them.\n\nA few of us were taken into custody as a precaution, but I'm assured they're being well treated.

The Elves sought to blockade the northern bridge, driving back Nords sent to reinforce St. Alessia's army.\n\nThe Whitestrake, ever eager for Elven blood, assaulted their lines and slew them, every one, before the Nords could even ready their arms.

By the time we were alerted and had organized a response, precious moments had been lost. We rescued a few, but mostly we found those who had drowned or were crushed on the rocks.\n\nEven so, it was nowhere near the numbers a ship like that carries.

It was just a typical sailing ship from the mainland. I suppose it carried the usual complement of cargo and travelers eager to reach our verdant shores. I don't believe that such a vessel would make the trip without filling its holds.\n\nDamn slavers.

Ever since our agreement with the Pact went into effect, slavery has been outlawed throughout most of Morrowind. But all we did was drive the slavers into the shadows.\n\nThis whole stinking event has their bloody fingerprints all over it.

We're just a small outpost along the Bitter Coast, but I like to think of us as the gateway to Vvardenfell. From here, Vivec City and the other inland locations are easily accessible. Governor Omellian is in charge although I contribute as necessary.

Here, and in all of the territories controlled by the Great Houses that support the Ebonheart Pact.\n\nIf you stray into Telvanni or Dres territory, though, the practice remains strong and vibrant. Hence, my current troubles.
With that busybody Marshal Hlaren and her Iron Hounds interfering with the watch, there's no work left for an honest constable!\n\nOn the other hand, I guess we could use a vacation ….

Cold as stone and tougher than an ornery nix-ox!\n\nRumor is she started out as an Ordinator. Served with the governor's son Nivel before his untimely death. Now she's the deputy governor who loves to make proclamations and order us about.

Yes, thanks to Sotha Sil's magic. My former master is exceedingly brilliant. I thought you already knew that?\n\nAnyway, there's no way we'd fit in here at our normal size, so the magic altered us as we passed through the doorway.

Always a chance. Just depends upon the way the gears align. But I don't think he can spare too much to use against us. He needs it to reach the reservoir and do whatever Clavicus Vile sent him to do.\n\nNow I really think we need to get moving.

You were very unkind … but I can forgive you if you really have come to your senses. \n\nAll you have to do is deliver the shells to Mother and complete the deal like we planned. Then Tirwin can be freed and we can finally be married.

His name was Tythis—an Ordinator—real intense, but I could tell it was concern for his sister: Nevena. She was young, enthusiastic, honored to be at the Temple … poor girl. \n\nIf you find them, I hope you undo the harm I've caused.

It was the home of a Great House that fell into ruin. Red Mountain has buried most of it, but the bones are there if you know what to look for.\n\nTo be honest, I just sort of stumbled on the statue in the wasteland. Lucky find … I thought.

It was an ugly thing, sinister even, but I knew the Temple would be interested. There aren't many pieces that survived that dark time, and they wouldn't want something like that circulating around.\n\nI swear, I thought it would be safe with them.
You are a true hero, Scarlet Judge. May the Hist protect you.

You think my nose is beautiful? Hero, you're going to make me blush!\n\nLook, I know I've been kind of a tease, but I really do like you. And I appreciate that you've always been there for me. One day, when all the dangers have passed, well …

Ha! I suppose that makes as much sense as anything.\n\nKeep doing what you're doing then, hero. You haven't disappointed me yet. Just don't let that strict sense of duty get you killed one of these days. If you died, I'd probably miss you terribly.

The old Marshal worked with the constables. We handled the daily matters while he focused on the big picture. Marshal Hlaren set up a separate watch with her Iron Hound mercenaries. She's made us obsolete!
The Scarlet Judge is obviously our Lord Vivec! Only one of our Living Gods could accomplish what the Scarlet Judge has done.
Lord Vivec is a poet as well as a warrior. He knows the value of legends and the utility of a subtle touch. It doesn't serve his purposes to make us dependent on divine intervention.

Vivec is the god of justice for all Dunmer, not only those in Vivec City! And the sermons speak of the Warrior-Poet splitting his mind into many bodies. He can oversee the city and dispense justice in equal measure.

What ails them isn't like a bruise or broken bone. Dwarves meddled with things only the divine should touch, or so I've heard. It may be up to the Three to mend the damage here.\n\nI'll pray for them, for what it's worth.

I'm still unsure if the song ringing out from the Dwemer machine will have any lasting effects on the miners of Gnisis. I've been doing research into Dwemer technology, but the results have been, well, lacking.

The song is quiet now, so I hope it was more of an immediate effect. But we can never be too sure.\n\nI'd like to not wake up one morning to find those miners we rescued dead in town. Not that I'm saying that's likely.

And may the Three guide your path, my friend.\n\nWatch your step on the way out. I'd hate for you to fall into the fire and burst into flames. That would be a dreadful way to end our little adventure here.

You've likely noticed the luck that follows me isn't of the favorable variety. Perhaps a Telvanni mage cursed me for a reason I'm unaware of. Wouldn't shock me.\n\nFor the safety of others, I'll stay here for now. I've learned to do that much at least.

Never better, really. I think they were ready to offer me a place in House Telvanni, but Mistress Dratha and I aren't really master-student types. \n\nShe's offered me free use of her resources for my studies though!

I'll be celebrating the mine's return to glory once our Queen grows up and our miners aren't fighting off the effects of crazy songs.\n\nFor now, I'm celebrating the fact I don't have a Dunmer thorn in my arse anymore.

I haven't heard from that milk-drinker since he ran off crying about his precious House Redoran. I hope a silt strider sat on him and he's stuck in its arse for the next eternity.\n\nIt'd be the only time he was ever quiet.

Take your pick.\n\nRevus at least means well, but his luck's horrible. Manore though—that man's ignorance and pride wear you down. You can only listen to someone's boastfulness for so long before you want to snap them in half.

Only if I think there's a demand for it, but part of our agreement requires me to give Mistress Dratha first pick. \n\nI won't complain if you stop in to see what I'm up to. You're always welcome in my shop.
Yes! Exactly! That filthy Savarak was poisoning Mistress Dratha—all of us—but her steward could have stopped it if he'd listened. \n\nMaybe he was in on it?

Might be so, but he told us to be on the lookout for someone that fits your description. I wouldn't say you're exactly welcomed to Tel Aruhn, but you are allowed to enter.\n\nGlad I'm not in your shoes.
No one could have come this close to killing Mistress Dratha without collaborators. He was a pawn of Savarak. Mark my words.

They already had my gold, so why stay to finish the work? Not the studious and well-mannered apprentices I expect from the Mages Guild. Besides, if truth be told, they were incompetent.\n\nI'm surprised they remained with us as long as they did.

Precisely! Oh, I see your concern. Forgot you haven't been here before.\n\nUse the entrance and you'll shrink down and get drawn inside. I understand that some of Sotha Sil's first entry methods had unintended effects, but now it's perfectly safe.

Where else would you put it? Besides, once we get inside, it's much bigger than it looks. My former master said that working in miniature enhanced his precision. And it made it much more convenient to hide away and store.\n\nNow in you go!

Interesting. Spiders and a barrier! Some sort of spider magic? Regardless, such occurrences suggest there's more to these ruins than I presumed. A great treasure, perhaps?\n\nBut why could the mage pass through the barrier and not you?
Farwen? Certainly! I really can't thank you enough for saving her body and soul from an ancient monstrous spirit of pure malice … what's that look for?

What a relief! Farwen is strong. Stronger than any of us. If anyone can resist such a thing, it's our friend.\n\nI … will watch over her though. But, if Galgalah isn't roaming about freely, that counts as a victory for us, right?
Wait, does this mean we didn't banish him? Is he contained? Is that not Farwen? Am I going to have to change the job log?
I know how to operate a myriad of things quite similar. Buy me time, as I've already asked—twice—and its secrets will not stay hidden for long.
A means of silencing that infernal machine and ending this threat without turning the entire place into a heap of smoldering wreckage.\n\nThat would be easier if you went about the task I gave you.
You aren't here for my safety. You're here to help me defuse the situation without resorting to mass disintegration.\n\nIf you refrain from dying—and stop pestering me—we may yet accomplish that.

Like my daughter, my wife has a mind of her own. What the two of you discuss is your own affair.\n\nJust understand that I haven't employed you to solve my family's problems. I only need you to find my daughter.
Hmm. You must be one of the freelancers my husband sent for. You really should speak with him if you're here about our daughter.\n\nNow if you'll excuse me, I really am quite busy.
Has the dust blinded you? I barely made it out with my tail intact, and I wasn't far from the door! Some may have escaped, but not all. Oh, by the Egg, what could have done this?

I'm getting away from this place. Perhaps this misfortune can turn to my salvation. The slave masters will think me a corpse, lost to the mine's collapse. I can use that to my advantage.\n\nThe Hist is calling me. I will pray for my lost friends.

Spare me your incredulity, outlander. Not a word I told you was a lie. I simply didn't care to divulge all that I could have.\n\nTruly, it's baffling you didn't suspect this from the start. Why else summon a Daedra, if not to make a bargain?

I truly fail to see how it is any of your concern, but I suppose you have done me a favor. To put it simply, I need more time. I don't do this out of vanity. An ancient threat looms at the edge of my sight. I must remain until it is dealt with.

You need to understand, Mistress Dratha is a wise woman. She knows exactly the horrors she has agreed to. This choice was made not for herself, but for the greater good.\n\nI didn't wish to betray you, but I trust her actions in this matter.

It's a danger that is long to come. I know very little, but I believe neither you nor I will ever see it in our lifetimes. \n\nIf it's enough to accept the tortures of Coldharbour, I'm thankful I will never live to see it.

What a presumptuous question. I don't believe I shall answer it.\n\nI can tell you, however, that I hold no regrets. My path is clear and my eyes are open. You may not live to thank me for this choice, but perhaps your descendants will.

A magister must learn to keep her worries hidden and her face calm.\n\nXykenaz said he would come in the guise of a man… a Nord perhaps? A Breton? Or will it be a Mer? Perhaps I can speak to Llayne about setting up patrols for strangers in town.

Is it better to know? To count down the days with dread? Or better to be ignorant, to worry and wonder if today is the day, or perhaps tomorrow?\n\nGive me a decade or so to decide how I feel about that.
Oh, no. Please don't tell me we didn't banish Galgalah. I've already marked it down as a victory in our new guild job log.

The Ropefish are people smugglers, led by an Orc named Khartag. I had hoped to work with him directly. Unfortunately, we must deal with one of his lieutenants—Bothamul.\n\nYou must deliver the message before our distraction can begin.
A passenger cabin in the Interim Suitor, down at the docks. Do not tarry.
My benefactor awaits you in the Patheirry House, near Trademan's Square. Do not tarry.
The Sadreno House, in Davon's Watch. Between Artisans' Row and the Market District. Do not tarry.

Oh, really? More like some other paltry wizard sent you here. Trying to find out my newfound knowledge of kwama mine productivity, are we?\n\nAs if I would confide in the likes of you. In fact, why am I even talking to you?

One other thing, you ignorant n'wah. If I find even a whiff of evidence that you or your scaled cohort had anything to do with a recent slave insurgency at Vassamsi Grotto, I will not be merciful. \n\nNow get out.

Well, in that case …. Redoran is the grandest of the Great Dunmer Houses. We champion the virtues of duty and piety, and we have a proud military tradition. Our house comes first in all things. I don't understand why Eris seeks outside help.

An interesting insight. Perhaps you can find my daughter. Veya can handle herself, but a father worries, you understand.\n\nAnyway, I agree with your assessment. That's why I'm willing to bring in outside help on this.

Could be a love poem or a recipe for kwama cream cocktail, but we suspect it's the way Veya has been keeping tabs on what's been happening in the city.\n\nLook, it may amount to nothing, but the note could give us a lead on where to find Veya.

Sorry about that. I'm kind of on edge, if you hadn't noticed.\n\nEveryone knows Veya's brother. Or they did. Before he disappeared. Ulran was an exemplary officer. Everything House Redoran could hope for. Veya won't rest until she learns the truth.

All right! No need to get violent!\n\nVeya doesn't want her father to find her until she's located her brother. So we help protect her. That's why we set up the runners. Let the councilor's hounds chase us while Veya looks for Ulran.

Veya and I have a history. Her brother, too. They were good kids. Liked to watch me train. Now I feel responsible for her.\n\nWhen she came to me looking for help and asked to join the Morag Tong, who was I to refuse?

The Morag Tong has the authority to accept and carry out writs of execution. We keep the Great Houses from engaging in all-out war, but they rarely appreciate the work we do on their behalf.\n\nHouse Redoran in particular wants to shut us down.

We can't just kill with wild abandon. We follow a code. We only execute those whose names appear on sanctioned writs. If we kill respectable citizens without a writ, that's just murder.\n\nSo, without proof and a proper writ, my hands are tied.

Something about who Naryu's target is. Thinks the target may know something about what happened to her brother.\n\nLook, I'm not even sure how Veya found out who Naryu's target is and I don't want to know. Just go and talk to her. Please.

That explains why Veya broke into the kinhouse. I'm not sure what happened in there, but she certainly stirred up the Redoran soldiers.\n\nVeya might still be inside. Or she might have given them the slip. She could be anywhere by now.

The Morag Tong only recently began to find acceptance again. Veya's actions don't just reflect badly on me, they could be used to force us back into the shadows. Maybe even disband us altogether.\n\nWe're both going to have to answer for this.

There's probably a button or something nearby. In my experience, there's always something pushable. I remember seeing Daedric symbols on plates along the wall.\n\nTry pushing a button that's divisible by three. Three has always been lucky for me.
An assassin … probably a Morag Tong. She tracked our leader here. But she … she doesn't know. We set a trap … inside the ruins ….

Sadrith Mora is up on the eastern coast, so you could walk, but I wouldn't recommend it.\n\nTalk to Synda, our local navigator. She can sail you up there on her next trip. That's how I was going to get there, until I missed my delivery time.
The Telvanni aren't like you and I, friend! They're powerful and quick to anger, and have no qualms about harming those who displease them.
No clue. If a Telvanni mage wants them, I can only suppose they have magical properties. You won't see me putting them in any of my stews, that's for damn sure.
Questions? I don't have time for questions. I have a writ to complete!\n\nLook, I can't keep these evil cultists waiting. You want to talk? Find me after I finish this job.
She headed upstairs. To Captain Brivan's apartment, I think.\n\nI can't believe she killed all these soldiers!
No. She totally ignored us. Just the soldiers. Nobody else was harmed.
You have a valid point.\n\nI suppose I have to stay competitive or risk letting this old, grand religion fall into total obscurity.
Ask then, but badgering me isn't going to get you any closer to a bag of gold.\n\nCome on. Out with it.
A bunch of self-proclaimed "ghost hunters." They were my only option on such a late notice.\n\nBy the look of them, they could use more muscle. That'd be you.

What's there to tell? They're old. They're ruined. They're filled with spirits. If you want to believe the Ashlanders folk tales, one of them can possess mortal bodies.\n\nI hold the deed, so I don't care what's laid claim to the land. Evict them.
After I added together the variables, the only logical response was to do as Azura asked. Sotha Sil's safeguards mean nothing if we allow Vivec to die and Vvardenfell to be destroyed.
That doesn't surprise me. The plots of Daedric Princes can be convoluted and full of contradictions.\n\nGo ahead. Ask your questions.

Some mysteries are beyond even the insight of the Warrior-Poet. As far as I can ascertain, the God of Bargains sent Barbas to steal my energy in order to locate and seize control of the Clockwork City.\n\nThankfully, you thwarted their plan.

My thoughts have not yet settled on a definitive answer. Some other Daedric Princes, perhaps? But that's a problem for another day.\n\nGo forth, my friend, and get the signet. We have a ceremony to perform!

Do not imagine that blame should fall upon my brother. Sotha Sil's curiosity knows no bounds. His staff was not meant to be used as a weapon against me. It was a tool, nothing more.\n\nWhen he learns what happened, I'm sure he'll be properly mortified.

Did she? I suppose she did. I have no idea. As I proclaimed in my Sermon to the Great Houses, "The ways of the Daedra are exceedingly strange."\n\nI was impressed with her champion, however. Perhaps there's hope for the Ashlanders, after all.

I lost my brother to ambition and became the champion of Azura. From that point of view, I suppose I'm doing as well as can be expected.\n\nI'll return to the tribes. Pick up where Chodala and I left off—before he decided he was the Nerevarine.

Not directly. But I do have a sense that malignant forces are gathering on the planes of Oblivion, but that could just be the scrib jelly and cheese I ate for lunch.\n\nFarewell, outlander. May the Queen of the Night Sky guide you on your travels.

Ah, the one about Zaintiraris, is it?\n\nWell, I could call the guard and be about my day, but I am a Telvanni, after all. We don't turn away an opportunity when it presents itself. Perhaps you could help me with a problem I've run into.
Jinrisa's offered us a chance to double our winnings. If we acquire the deed and embarrass her in the process, Firuth's bound to support my promotion!

I… I apologize, my friend. Perhaps I have gotten a bit caught up in Telvanni maneuvering.\n\nOf course I will respect your choice. I'm just worried about Eoki. I fear that I may never keep my promise to free him.

Not exactly, but now that we're certain the affliction isn't natural, we can determine a proper solution. It most likely requires Chodala's staff.\n\nHow the Ashlander got his hands on Sotha Sil's tool and turned it into a weapon, I haven't a clue.

Eventually, but caution is advised. If the Ashlanders revere Chodala as much as you imply, we can't just attack him and start a war.\n\nGo to Ald'ruhn and talk to his sister, Seryn. I don't trust her either, but she worked with you once before.

Do I really have to spell it out? When I'm ready, when you're ready, we'll find a quiet cabin in the woods, open an expensive bottle of wine, snuggle up by the fire ….\n\nAnd then I'll probably stick a dagger between your ribs. It's who I am, hero.
Of course! Now, we may have many games available. Which challenge would you like to know about?

Team Deathmatch has always been popular. All that ceaseless bloodshed really gets the heart pumping! Just go into the field and attack as many players as possible. The more hits you get in, the more points your team scores.
Ever the curious one, eh? Good. Knowledge can be key to a decisive victory. What other challenge would you care for me to explain?

I sure did! I had my doubts, but after my fourth kill I felt like Pelinal himself! Exalted, you know? Plus, my superiors noticed, and I'm getting extra rewards!\n\nToo bad they wouldn't let me drain the whole bowl. I could take on an entire legion!

Only during the period of our celebration! Then it seems to imbue warriors with a holy fervor for righteous carnage.\n\nIn fact, I overheard some soldiers say it doubled their normal contributions to the war. Doubled! Praise Pelinal!

I'd love to, but she's tight lipped about the secrets of her Old Gods. Maybe I should be less stingy in my donations ….\n \nSharz and I know a trick or two of our own, but it's Farwen's wards that have always kept us safe. We'd be lost without her.

Your help is appreciated. I can fend for myself, but conjuring these wards is taxing and establishing a spirit barrier is only the first step.\n\nI must continually channel the flow of magic to maintain it for any extended period of time.

A body shifter! Old Gods protect us—not everyone survived our last brush with something like that. I—I must pray.\n\nThere! The Old Gods have lit the way. I shall follow you and save my strength for my magics.

The wards must align around a focal point, as near to the haunting as we dare.\n\nPoorly placed, the spirit barrier could appear in an undesirable location. Inside solid rock, for instance, and I'll only have the strength to attempt this once.
I was planning on sailing to Sadrith Mora next, but I don't mind taking you to an Alliance capital. Trade is always good in the capitals!

My reputation precedes. I must apologize if you've come all this way seeking enlightenment. I would open your eyes to the truth of the Old Gods if we met under more pleasant circumstances, but now's not the best time.

Mauloch, I don't know. Maybe I didn't like the way they asked.\n\nLook, I'm no saint. Done a lot of things I ain't proud of. But I'll be damned if some tuskless thug's going to make life even worse for these slaves. They've been through enough.

For the most part. But sometimes it takes great effort not to strangle one or more of these pointy-eared blusterers. For example, no one ever remembers their birth sign. Some even try to change their answers on repeat visits. As if I wouldn't notice!
No. All these beasts serve their Patriarch: Gherig Bullblood. Even the Forge seems to obey his command.\n\nIt all stinks of Daedric pacts to me.
That's right! Red and hot and hungry. Mounds of them to spill our Nord blood! \n\nWe'll see how they fair on the skeevers of the Reach and their overgrown cattle! Even that monster Galchobhar!
The Forge! The infernal heart of this cursed place. We're close now. \n\nWith these weapons we'll drive the Reach-scum into a corner and mash them on the anvil one by one!

Usually the Reachmen come to pillage what they can before they're chased off, but this clan is leaving nothing behind in their wake. They're here to hunt us. To conquer us. I think they're raising an army.
Nirncrux. More than I've ever seen. New veins seem to seep up from the earth every day through the vines, like the whole place is alive. What they use it for defies belief.

Reachmen are barbarians. Raiders and scavengers. They don't build. That Forge is something from ancient times, maybe not even built by mortal hands, but they're working it all the same with their foul Reach magic.

Capture the Relic is one of our simpler games. You must seize your enemy's relic and return it to your base, all while protecting your own relic as well. Teamwork is the key to victory in this game, as you'll need a strong defense and offense.
Calm down …! I—it's just these monsters getting under my skin. They have to pay for what they've done. They have to be punished! Nords don't suffer this kind of shame!
Sounds like a Nocturnal Shrike. By the gears, how did that thing make it past our security coils?\n\nIs Gascone …?
I had to see for myself that you could do it—to believe you could save them. I couldn't live with myself if I'd just saved my own skin and ran ….\n\nKyne was watching over me today, to be certain.
Largest city in the hold and seat of the Jarl. If anywhere's safe from these rabid Reachmen, it's there.

Not just the Reachmen! Take a look at my kin. Honest, hard working Nords, never held an ax for more than splitting wood, now they're clamoring for blood! Crazed and feral.\n\nNot me! I'm not going to let it happen to me.
To keep the Reachmen out of our lands now and forever! We have the power they woke here and it's given us the means to finally end them! I won't waste it!
Does it matter? It's a curse turned to a blessing! When we learn to stoke the fires as the Reachmen did, we'll hunt their kind to the ends of Nirn!
Nothing's ever been more natural! I've never felt such purpose! Hunt or be hunted, it's the way of the world—we just forgot in our comforts!
I don't know who built this place, but it was made with a purpose! It wants to be used! It's call echoes louder than your meek words!
Whoever built this Forge tapped Shor's blood, to answer treachery with his mighty vengeance, I'm certain! We'll honor his name with every stamp of its hammer!
I've lost a mother and a son to these monsters! It's no different for anyone here. For generations they've done the taking. There's a steep debt to be paid!
But it was you who delivered us Shor's righteous retribution! It'll be your name we sing to the sound of their cries!
You would have us lay down our weapons and return to being hunted down like craven skeevers? No! I'd rather die than live like prey again!
If you'd lived as we've lived, endured what we've endured, you'd have no doubts!\n\nThere's only one path from here!

Me? Go into a tomb? No, no. That's what Narsis Dren does. He's the explorer. I'm just the hired help.\n\nI'm surprised he's not here yet. I could have sworn that old scroll said "Veloth Tomb," but I suppose it could have been "Dreloth."

Oh, there are lots of tombs. You can't swing a dead mammoth without hitting the resting place of some Dark Elf ancestor. Vvardenfell is overflowing with the things.\n\nAnyway, I guess I'll head over to the Dreloth Tomb and see if Narsis is there.

A bastard union of Reachmen and minotaur tribes. Joined in their hatred of us and their lust for our land.\n\nBoth are savage in their own right, but I have never seen either so ferocious as they are now.

Aye. Their ilk are raiders and opportunists. Not since the Longhouse Emperors dirtied the Ruby Throne have I known Reachmen to raise armies, and never minotaurs. The beast that leads them is like a Daedric Prince in the flesh.\n\nDark times.

Just as I feared. I knew looking for this artifact would get us killed. I warned them, warned all of them, but they wouldn't listen! They never listen.\n\nI've got to find the others. There's still time to save them. Has to be ….

Something very dangerous, but that can wait. My friends are in danger and don't even see it! Some scryers, huh?\n\nAdeber's in Shornhelm and Wenridil is in Marbruk. Neelo's in Stormhold maybe? Yes. He must be there. I just hope we're not too late.

Shor's bones, you really want to know, eh? Fine.\n\nMy associates and I are all junior scryers in the Order of the Eye. We scour the tombs and ruins of Tamriel, looking for extraplanar threats. Rifts in the veil, Daedric artifacts, that sort of thing.
We've had visions of a Daedric artifact. At least we think it's a Daedric artifact. It's hazy, you know? Obscured by something … like frosted glass.\n\nSorry. Skaldir was always the wordsmith.

Bonafryd, of Clan Owlcloak.\n\nSkaldir and I came up together in Riften, under Magus Oriela. He was always the sharper blade. Magic came easily for him. Me? Not so much. Got too much frost in my blood. Still, I can hold my own. Just takes me a while.

Unfortunately, Skaldir's not the only mage who's been killed by his own shadow—he's just the most recent. Other members of our order have been turning up dead all over Tamriel.\n\nI hurried here to warn him, but I wasn't fast enough.

Other junior scryers in the Order of the Eye.\n\nIt was just Skaldir and me at first, but others caught on eventually. We started writing each other once we realized we'd all stumbled upon the same artifact. Thought we could find it all on our own ….

You think I haven't tried? I sent projections but … this doesn't come easily for me. Magic, I mean.\n\nAnyway, I have to warn High King Jorunn first. I heard that his rune-galdr's been looking into the artifact as well. Please, just find my friends.
I know a great many mages. The person I don't know, of course, is you. Why are you asking about Adeber?

You're serious, aren't you? Mara protect us! I'll gather up the other initiates and alert the magister at once.\n\nPlease, just find Adeber and bring him back safe. We'll do all we can to protect him.

Bonafryd? The near-sighted scryer? What's she—? Never mind.\n\nAdeber left just a moment ago. Said he needed some quiet. He usually goes to the courtyard behind the guild hall when he needs some time alone. Is he going to be all right?

The Eight damn whoever did this to him! He was so sweet—such a quiet and gentle soul. Always there with a timid smile and a kind word. Who could—?\n\nThank you for letting me know. We'll see to it that he's laid to rest. Just warn the others.

It was my shadow, wasn't it? Y'ffre's name, why would it attack me? I always treated it well—plenty of sunshine, candlelight and such. All done now, I suppose. It doesn't look like it's coming back. Ingrate.\n\nNow I feel … ugh. Damn.

Not really. I think my shadow may have peeled off some of my animus. My soul, I mean. Or maybe just some of my magical aptitude. Either way, it's something I'll miss.\n\nDon't blame yourself. You did keep it from killing me, after all.

Well, that was charitable of her. Didn't think she much liked me. Bit of a sorehead, that one. Anyway, I'm grateful.\n\nI hid my notes on the artifact in the planter over there—just in case, you know? They're yours if you want them.

You think I do not know? I know!\n\nI have heard the stories—Ragar, Gilnenor, and now Skaldir? All dead at your hand, no doubt. Well, I am too clever for you, shadow-weaver. Try to touch me and my wards will tear you apart!

I don't …. All right, I'm sorry! I'll come out. By the egg, you remind me of my sister, Xarei. She is a wonderful person, but when she gets mad … I'd rather tangle with an angry hack-wing.\n\nHow do you know about the shadows?

You think I would fall for such a ruse? No. No! I will keep this ward up for days if that is what it takes.\n\nNow, begone! You do not want to be here when my sister arrives. Xarei is the strongest guard in Stormhold. Run away, while you still can!
Neelo? Did he set something on fire with his magic again? Kaoc.\n\nI will, of course, pay for the damages. Please forgive him. He is still learning, you see.
His shadow? By the Hist, what have you gotten into this time, little brother …?\n\nTake me to Neelo. I will make him see reason. He always feels safer when I am by his side.

Yes, of course. Xarei will put me in a very bright room. Or should it be a very dark room? Ugh. I cannot take this kind of stress. Look, my scales are falling out!\n\nThank you. And Bonafryd. Tell her I am sorry I doubted her dedication in the past.

Yes. Yes, I know I will.\n\nIf you have spoken to Bonafryd, you must know about our research into the Daedric artifact. Please, take my notes—preferably far, far away. I hid them in those roots over there. I am sure that is what these shadows want.

All the shadows' victims were seeking a Daedric artifact—an extraplanar antiquity that remains hidden from my sight. To solve these murders we must first locate the artifact.\n\nI require two objects to find it—an Anuic Lantern and a Liminal Lens.

I believe the lantern lies hidden in a sunken ship near Khenarthi's Roost. The lens rests in a coffer, deep within the Howling Sepulchers.\n\nRecover the items, then seek out my boat near Vulkhel Guard. Trust no one. Our enemies are very well-hidden.

Yes. I take it that you're unfamiliar with our order? That's hardly a surprise. We once served as advisors and teachers to the greatest kings and emperors, but no longer.\n\nWe retreated to our hidden isle of Artaeum, content to study in seclusion.

There are … worrying signs. Portents that cannot be ignored.\n\nI fear that a Daedric threat looms over Tamriel. Nothing so crude and obvious as the Planemeld. No. It's something hidden, and I suspect that this Daedric artifact may hold some answers.

Indeed. It's an island beyond Tamriel's borders where we can research the truths of the Aurbis without interruption. That is the purpose of the Psijic Order, after all—to study magic for the betterment of all.
They are critical components of an ancient Psijic mechanism known as the Obscuros.

The Obscuros is a scrying device. It magnifies a mage's perception and projects their visions for all to see. A powerful tool indeed.\n\nWhen my order retreated to Artaeum, we scattered the device's components to prevent it from being misused.

Very little.\n\nDaedric artifacts are notoriously difficult to track. Some misguided soul may discover one and wield it for a time, but it always vanishes eventually—sometimes for a week, sometimes for centuries.

I'm afraid I can't say. The forces arrayed against us are too mysterious. They may have found a way to listen in. I can't risk divulging the Obscuros's location.\n\nCollect the items and I promise, my boat will be waiting for you in Vulkhel Guard.
Would you believe pluck and intuition? Yeah, didn't think so.\n\nI may look the part, but I'm no bloodhound. Truth is, I slipped a spooring coin into your pocket before you left Mournhold.

A spooring coin. It's an enchanted drake—looks mundane, but it bears a charm that we can track.\n\nYou don't approve? Look, we can argue about that later. For now, I can't let you get on this boat alone. It's too dangerous. Let me go with you!
Smart. Two heads are better than one—especially when one of those heads is as hard as mine.\n\nLet's hop to it, eh? It's about time we got some answers.
Yeah. And you know what kind of people say things like "come alone?" Murderers. Shor's bones, you're smarter than this.\n\nJust let me come along. I can help.

Bah! You're just as stubborn as Skaldir was. And we know how that turned out, don't we?\n\nJust take care of yourself, all right? And don't believe everything you hear. It's a Daedric artifact we're after. People would do anything for it. Anything.
Smart. Two heads are better than one—especially when one of those heads is as hard as mine.\n\nLet's hop to it, eh? It's about time we got some answers.

Yes, of course. I sometimes forget this is not common knowledge.\n\nSotha Sil, brother to Vivec and magus of the Tribunal, created the Clockwork City long ago. He rarely speaks of it, but scholars believe this city has the power to remake Tamriel.

The city functions as a simulacrum of the corporeal plane. Making a change to the Clockwork City may well change some aspect of Tamriel itself. This is all speculative, but I've studied under Sotha Sil. I have no doubt that this is within his power.

Indeed. An unwelcome prospect, to be sure.\n\nNormally I would assure you that Sotha Sil has the situation well in hand. He is a friend to the Psijics, and to the people of Tamriel. But the presence of this Daedric artifact gives me pause.
Plans? No, of course not. I'll leave them to their business just as I always have.

I'm sure they did. You'd like an explanation, wouldn't you? Fine.\n\nYou want to earn people's love? Here's the secret—just leave them alone. Treat them like adults, even when they act like children. The rest takes care of itself.
The daughter of Jarl Skjoralmor and Thane of Falkreath. The hold would have fallen long ago if not for her. \n\nShe'll stand against the beasts long after the walls crumble, mark my word.

In no small part to you. I was dancing in half my blood with the Reach-dogs when that monster bull let out its death cry. You could hear it clear through the hold.\n\nScattered those cowards to the far winds like so many skeevers.
Might seem a bad omen, for certain, but Eerika has the right of it. Deep in the stone and too narrow for large numbers. If we can hold anything with a handful of good Nords, it's that.
Fight with no fear of death and give Eerika time to see our kin to safety.\n\nBeyond that … send as many of those bone-pickers to Oblivion as you can.

I wish I could say yes. I fear that in destroying my shadow, we've destroyed some vital piece of my animus. I feel … thin. Diminished.\n\nA weakened Psijic is still a formidable mage, but something is definitely broken. Best not to think about it.

Well, no one really knows Sotha Sil—not even the other members of the Tribunal. I studied under him for a time. He was patient, surprisingly attentive—the perfect teacher in many respects. \n\nEven so, I never really felt that I knew him.

I'm no deserter, if that's what you're thinking! I was to make for the nearest hold and bring reinforcements, but my leg was shattered by one of those minotaur brutes.\n\nLeft me for dead … or near enough so as to make no difference.

Doesn't matter. I'm a runner who can't run, or even stand. Save my home and at least I can look my father in the eye at the Hall of Valor.\n\nI may not die on my feet, but the Reach-dogs will have to pry this knife from my cold dead hands.

Shore up our defenses, lick our wounds, bury our dead. I can hope that we've seen the last of those beasts for awhile, but I won't leave it to chance.\n\nIf I convince our neighboring holds to lend their aid, Falkreath will recover, if slowly.
It was until the Reachmen corrupted it with their vile rituals. Our wards still glow with the power the Divines, so this place might yet be cleansed.
The warriors of Falkreath will defend their Jarl to the last. If this is the end, I should be at my father's side … but I won't abandon these people.\n\nPlease, do whatever you can.
With any luck Torik and some others can get here before it comes to that, but if not, I will delay the enemy as long as I can. No point in sacrificing anyone else for such a cause.

Depends on who you ask. Not all carry the mantle the same way. For your service to Falkreath, the Jarl has given you privilege to do as you please in our hold. Within reason.\n\nIt's an honor not given lightly.
I am. She's a fine leader. Never thinks of herself. Under her rule, we'll see this hold thrive. Maybe more than it ever has.\n\nI don't celebrate what got us here, but I'm hopeful for the future.

It is to enjoy the respect and hospitality of all Falkreath's people, and to call this place home whenever you return.\n\nI'm afraid I have no land and servants to bestow upon you at this time. When the city is made whole, I will do right by you.

Thank you … though you may be the only one to say so sincerely. Many will offer their condolences and kind words out of respect for me, but my father was not a well-loved Jarl.\n\nI hope to set a better example.

A mage can't afford to be sure of anything. But I'd bet my family's meadery on it.\n\nDaedric artifacts grant untold power to those that carry them, but always at a cost. The Mages Guild can't let even one of these things fall into the wrong hands.

Oh, yes.\n\nItems of power always introduce some measure of peril to the world. This is doubly true with Daedric artifacts. They exist to carry out the dark intentions of their creators, you see? They turn even the best intentions to malice eventually.

That is the question, isn't it? I trained for centuries on the isle of Artaeum, briefly under Sotha Sil himself. Yet still this artifact eludes me. Vexing is the word.\n\nEither this artifact is shrouded by a powerful ward, or it isn't here.
It might be tucked away in a pocket plane, or caught in some aurbic gyre—bouncing between worlds. Impossible to say. That's why I need the lantern and the lens.

We were some of Tamriel's best and brightest magi, invited to the Clockwork City by Sotha Sil to attend his experiments and learn from the greatest mind in creation.\n\nWe have been left to our own devices for a long time. Order was needed. Regulation.

That's something, at least … I've agreed to attempt my experiment again with Sovor as my subject. He's promised to petition the order to end my exile if I'm successful, but I couldn't care less about that.\n\nI just want this to be over.
He what? No, absolutely not! That experiment cost me everything I held dear. I was a fool to try it. Sovor of all people should know that.

Didn't we cover this? Let me refresh your memory. Lord Vivec suffers stoically as his divine energy drains away. Neither my administrations nor his defenses have been sufficient to plug the hole, so we've isolated him to keep panic to a minimum.

If we knew for certain, we wouldn't be sending you to make a deal with a heretical Ashlander, now would we?\n\nChodala must have something to do with Vivec's energy loss, but the how and why remains a mystery. That's why I must examine that staff.

The people don't handle the infirmities of their deities very well. Especially when those infirmities could foreshadow Red Mountain's eruption or portend the moonlet's fall from the sky.\n\nOnce such fear ignites, it spreads like wildfire.

They try not to think about them at all.\n\nThe Ashlanders are savages! They refuse to acknowledge the supremacy of Lord Vivec and the Tribunal, instead putting their faith in the despicable Daedra. They're heretics, pure and simple.

Everything you uncovered suggests that the staff and Sotha Sil's missing tool are one and the same, and it's obviously connected to Chodala's newfound powers. Bring it back here so I can study it.\n\nThe solution resides in the staff, I'm sure of it.

Experience, outlander, experience.\n\nI have seen the Dunmer rage against the gods at the least provocation. When they realize that Vivec is ill, that his powers are failing, they'll weep and gnash their teeth like frightened children.

The Ashlanders hold to superstitions the way kwama protect their eggs. If they really consider Chodala to be the Nerevarine, then any action you take against him will enrage the tribes.\n\nTalk to Seryn and see if she can suggest an alternative course.

The truth is, I need Sovor as much as he needs me. I think the only way I can safely extract Bolin's soul from the gem is to offer it something in exchange. Who knows if I'll ever have another willing subject.\n\nCan I count on your assistance?
I'd like you close at hand in case Sovor has a similar reaction to the experiment as Bolin.\n\nThrow that switch when you're ready to begin the transfer. I'll keep watch on the equipment from here.

Then my worst fears have been realized. I cannot overstate the magnitude of this threat, my friend.\n\nOur adversary—it's Nocturnal isn't it? Shadows and conspiracy are her stock-in-trade. How could I have been so blind?

Only that you keep your intentions hidden and your eyes open. The Night Mistress is Ur-dra—perhaps the eldest and most powerful of the Daedric Princes. And your ally, Divayth Fyr, is no saint.\n\nYour path is fraught with peril. Be wary.
You did? Then all of creation owes you a debt, my friend. It was Nocturnal, wasn't it? The shadows and conspiracy … I should have seen it sooner.\n\nThe Daedric artifact—is it safe?

Divayth Fyr? I would not have expected that. That Telvanni mage cares little for anyone besides himself. Then again, I know Sotha Sil to be both wise and prudent. He would not give Fyr the artifact without cause. I must trust in Seht's judgment.

Beyond the obvious? Not much.\n\nI can tell you he's nothing like Vivec. He never spoke about himself or the Dark Elf faith. I always got the sense that he … well, resented isn't the right word. He just seemed ambivalent about that part of his life.

Only obliquely, and mostly in metaphor. It's his primary pursuit now. Some say it's his obsession.\n\nYou see, despite all his power, there is a melancholy to him. It's unfortunate, but not surprising. True wisdom always brings some measure of despair.

Of course.\n\nWe use scavenged alchemical tools to filter out clumps and impurities. Once we distill the remaining fluid, we add it to other substances to make many important things—fuels, lubricants, even cooking oil.

Dangerous? I suppose so. But even clean water can kill a dryskin when it fills the lungs.\n\nThis oil is everywhere—in the water, in the machines, likely in our blood also. I would not trouble yourself with worry.

That is a good question. The Clockwork God's machines belch smoke like a peat bog belches gas. And the metal-men bleed oil when wounded or left to rust.\n\nEventually, all moisture makes its way to the sea … or cisterns and ravines, in this case.

Not for blowing things up, if that's what you're worried about! I promise you, my days of blowing things up are over.\n\nWe use the pellets to grind flash stone into a flammable-powder that lets us cut pipes. Weld them too. Useful stuff.

Oh, I've had a lot of practice handling explosives.\n\nFact is, this whole city is a keg of fire-salts. Most of the fluids you see are at least semi-flammable. Many of the gases are highly volatile too. Damn near a miracle the place is still standing.

Gutting the …? Oh, cutting. Right.\n\nWell, we have to. We don't have any discharge valves down there. If we need water, or wind-up, we have to cut into the lines. Then, eventually, we have to seal them back up. Facts of life in Slag Town.

Most don't like to talk about it, but Slag Town's air is poison. Topside, the factotums rotate air filters constantly—but not in Slag Town. So, I pick up the slack.\n\nTurns out the metallic fibers weaved in Clockwork clothing make great air filters.

Oh, sure. Can make abrasive scrubbers out of them, armor lining, cables, hazard masks … all kinds of things.\n\nOf course, by the time I've replaced all the filters, I rarely have more than a handful left. It's maddening.

Ah, that. Quite a wonder. See, when you switch it on, metal scraps stick to it like tar to a glove. I'd love the thing if it didn't break so damned often.\n\nIf you gather the parts I need, I can keep it working, and maybe even make new ones.

That I am—the more, the better. You can peel the husks off just about any hunk of wood you find. Collecting the coals might prove to be a bit trickier. But you're keyed-in and wound tight, right? Shouldn't take you long at all.

In Slag Town, nothing goes to waste. I found a way to scrape a loose adhesive out of the husks. You might call it resin? Sticky as Avarya's boot-stew, and great for sealing gaps.\n\nAs for the bark, I use it to make dyes, furniture, lots of things.

Turning the sap into glue requires a lot of heat. If you let it cool for too long, it crystallizes—by then it's worthless.\n\nThese coals burn for days. They don't need stoking and keep a steady heat both day and night. They're perfect for the job.

Of course. \n\nThe Clockwork City provides an abundance of magical substances, but the people of Slag Town have very little access to them. We're forced to improvise—using runelights to find the arcane residue that accumulates on local runestones.

Quite a bit. This plaque adheres to the runestones. Over time it takes on some of the stone's inherent potency, aspect, or essence. Just a trifling amount, mind you, but we really don't need that much. Our enchantments are purely practical.

Divining tools. They emit a faint glow, much like a mage-light. The difference is that this glow shows us where residue accumulates. It shines like ice in the moonlight.\n\nVery recent discovery for me, ever since that portal showed up in the Radius.

They're a wonder! The Apostles never bothered to research them, since they use machinery to treat their ills. But we don't have fancy things like that down here.\n\nStill researching their origin, how they're made and whatnot.
Coughs, fume-headaches, black-belly … lots of things.\n\nSotha Sil never meant for anyone to live down here. Anyway, my tonics ward off most of it. Pity I can't as easily cure this stutter.

Right. The satchels work wonders, but they make the plants taste … well, they taste like something that fell out of a fabricant's bum. The syrup helps. Now it just tastes like a handful of dirty coins.\n\nBetter than nothing, I guess.
The fruits of the Forge, their Heartstones and weapons, twist them into bloodthirsty monsters whose flesh and blood is stone and fire. They turn out more with each passing day.
You dare question the sacred duty that has been placed before me? I'll have you know I'm … I'm ….\n\nWhat am I doing here? What is this place?

Mysterious? I would say it falls more into the suspicious category, what with the fact that it tried to lure me inside.\n\nAnyway, we were patrolling this quadrant of the Radius when I noticed the portal out of the corner of my eye.

So, you knew our attacker? Hmm. She was powerful indeed, and yet I sense that the strength was not her own. Her form was clumsy, but she struck with the power of a master wizard.\n\nUsually, I'd suspect possession. But with her? I'm not so certain.

Someone granted her powers beyond her ken. An agent of Oblivion, no doubt.\n\nBonafryd was clearly filled with hatred. Consumed by jealousy or resentment, perhaps? The Daedra can twist those passions into untold horrors. I pity her.

Information? I've been locked in this bleak little room since we parted ways. What could I possibly know?\n\nI heard the omnivox squawking earlier. Is that what this is about? It is …. Oh my. The cultists locked you out of the Cogitum, didn't they?

Hmm. I could help you, but I'd need something in return.\n\nOne of Clavicus Vile's Skaafin enforcers stalks the Mechanical Fundament, carrying a peculiar contract. Kill this Daedra, bring me the contract, and I'll tell you everything I know.

A mountain with horns and a heart of stone. One of the first of these beasts with fire in their veins. They thought he'd be enough to keep us timid, but with these weapons we'll carve him up like a New Life roast!

Slag Town, home of the Tarnished! The oil-covered slums of our gleaming city, where the poor and forgotten try to hobble together a home.\n\nFolks around here call me Mayor. Not an official title of course, but I'll take it.
Gates. Of course. My apostles ran down a few rumors about cultists building strange basins on the periphery of the Radius, but we never found any of them. \n\nHow do these gates work?

And we have no way to know which will get us to our destination faster.\n\nLet's split up. I'll take the western gate—you take the east. Try to navigate the Evergloam. I'll do the same. Hopefully one of us will make it to the Cogitum in time.

So we'll use the cultists' own pathways against them. Makes sense. Can't say I have any desire to fight my way through a plane of Oblivion, but we don't have much of a choice, do we?\n\nDid Gascone say where they built these gates?

Various reasons. We're orphans, degenerates, castaways. Abandoned and disgraced. No respectable trade to call our own, or fancy shop to watch over. \n\nPut simply? We're unwanted. A spot of rust on the shiny brass of Clockwork.

Even in this ever gleaming city, there will always be those who are thought of as lesser. Can't sling a spell or work with gears? You're already coming up short. \n\nThe residents of Slag Town though, we're lower quality than even those folks.

Never much, truth be told. They'll deliver medicinal supplies sometimes, or increase our daily water allowance. Once or twice I even convinced them to send a factotum for repairs, but that was more of a pain in the arse than it was worth.

Came upon the position naturally. I look out for people, always have. It's up to me to keep stock of what supplies we have, and try to get someone to help us find more. \n\nI'll even petition the Apostles if the need around here gets too great.

You're right. I knew Gascone was a conceited slaggard, but consorting with Daedra? I pray it's not true.\n\nWe need to discover what he has that the Daedra covet. Proctor Luciana might be able to organize a search. She just left to disperse a crowd.

I did. Life in Slag Town makes inventors of us all. Ironic, since many of us fell into poverty because we did not invent enough.\n\nThe Apostles will tell you that creativity is the greatest virtue. In Slag Town, it is not a virtue. It is a necessity.
Gascone? What has he done now? I can't keep up with the complaints.
So he finally graduated from corrupt hobbyist to professional villain. I'm almost relieved. Now we can finally give him what he deserves.\n\nI assume you informed your sponsor, Provost Varuni?
Good. Maybe a fabricant ate him. Our luck has to change at some point.

A city-wide search? I can't spare enough apostles to search a broom closet.\n\nReports are flooding in from the Radius—stories about fanatics in black robes, pale-skinned Daedra, living shadows …. We may have a full-scale invasion on our hands.

Hm. I have one asset I can spare. I know an artificer—Dalomar. He takes some getting used to, but you won't find a better tinkerer. He can help you find Gascone. Guaranteed.\n\nGo talk to him. He set up shop near the tenements. Slag Town.

It's true our bellies never go empty, and I'm thankful for that, but Slag Town can't live off of gruel and a thin blanket. We work hard to get by on our own, and these supplies are needed to do just that.\n\nI'll admit though, it can be dangerous work.

Maybe you haven't been here long, but I'm sure you noticed that Clockwork isn't the safest place in Tamriel. You'll have to go through some dangerous spots to collect these supplies. \n\nBut hey, you look like you can handle yourself.

Well, depends on who you're asking. \n\nTo me? Most definitely. These supplies can drastically improve the quality of life here. It stops our little ones from shivering, and helps our sick recover. It's worth every piece of gold I offer.

My gut tells me an ancient magic forge isn't going to stay unclaimed for long now that it's been rediscovered.\n\nSuits me fine. Maybe the next band of squatters to start sacrificing their neighbors will put up more of a fight, eh?

A missing person? How mysterious! You wouldn't be looking for Sotha Sil would you? I hear rumors, you know? All kinds of rumors. Something about him turning into a crow? Or was it a frog? Never mind.\n\nLuciana did you a favor. I have just the thing!

You must be one of the new arrivals I've heard so much about.\n\nEverything in the Clockwork City—the soil, the flora, the fauna—it's all composed of gears and pistons and metal. It's like that everywhere. Everywhere, that is, except here.

And have two novices wandering around the oasis unsupervised? Hmm. Very well. Go find Sherizar and return to me with all due haste.\n\nQuickly now. The work of the Wellspring can't wait for an idle apprentice.

Sometimes a gear slips or a cylinder throws a piston. This place reminds me of that.\n\nSpecifically, I saw my old friend, Chirrhari, down one of the corridors. When I tried to go talk to her, the factotums blocked my path. They drove me off.
A new apprentice? Really? But what does Chirrhari know of such things? This one works in the dark and grows fungi, molds, and mosses. The lector keeps me too busy for other concerns.

Interesting question. As far as I know, no new apprentices have entered the Wellspring since Gathal's accident.\n\nBut I have a bigger concern. At least Chirrhari can grow mushrooms. My plants refuse to live, no matter what I do.

Idrono? His experiment was doomed from the beginning. You can't grow plants without a source of nourishing light. My plants thrive thanks to the use of Lector Naril's simulated sunlight.\n\nBut I wasn't informed we were getting new apprentices ….

Of course I'm sure! I wouldn't send you out into the wild with a defective fabricant.\n\nI mean, there are alternatives. I'm sure I've got a mechanical nose around here somewhere. Just let me get my scalpel. Wait … where's my scalpel?

Fine. Suit yourself. If you like your nose so much, you can keep it. I don't care.\n\nWhen you find Gascone, just give Snuffler a little nudge and he'll trot back home. Just a nudge, mind you! If you kick him we'll have to replace more than your nose.

No. If we leave, Lector Naril will just use Chirrhari or one of the others. We have to do something. We have to stop this madness. People shouldn't be turned into plant food! At least, not while they're still healthy and vibrant.\n\nIt's not natural.

The lector lied. He tricked the apprentices and killed them. But the machine does allow the plants to grow and provides food for the Clockwork City.\n\nI wonder … what if someone willingly sacrificed themselves to feed the people?

What an odd question. I spotted a portal that should not have been there and I entered it to see where it led. I determined that this Shadow Cleft is part of the Evergloam.\n\nHow I wound up trapped in a scarecrow, that's still somewhat hazy.

That should be the least of your concerns! If you don't do exactly what I tell you, you'll end up like me. Then who will protect the Clockwork City from this Oblivion infestation?\n\nYou need to destroy the shadow array!

Nords have a knack for finding death and glory, I'll grant them that. Seems a bit lazy to have all the killing come to you in the comfort of stone walls, but since you kept the place on the map I suppose I'll overlook it.

Bonafryd? The near-sighted scryer? What's she—? Never mind.\n\nAdeber left just a moment ago. Said he needed some quiet. He usually goes to the courtyard behind the guild hall when he needs some time alone. Is he going to be all right?

You're serious, aren't you? Mara protect us! I'll gather up the other initiates and alert the magister at once.\n\nPlease, just find Adeber and bring him back safe. We'll do all we can to protect him.

Only what I read in the Imperial histories as a student.\n\nOur libraries don't carry any literature on Daedra or their relics. I argued against the ban, but the congress wouldn't budge. They don't understand how dangerous these creatures can be.

Of sorts.\n\nOur legal system is pretty rudimentary—mostly because we use it so rarely. Infractions result in exile most of the time. But this business with Gascone and Clavicus Vile is a good deal more serious than research sabotage or plagiarism.

The urns of these honored dead are blessed by the Divines. Some still hold the power to drive off malicious spirits and unholy magic. We can use them to cleanse these halls of the corruption of those bastard Reachmen.

Because Sotha Sil set the Wellspring in this metallic desert and blessed it with a reservoir of water—an exceedingly rare thing in the Clockwork City! He planned to create an oasis, but moved on to other projects before the task was done.
Indeed. A self-steering vessel of my own design. Climb aboard, and the enchantment I've placed on it will bring you to me directly. It's quite safe, I assure you.

We had water and a pressing need. It didn't take me long to figure out how to make actual, living plants grow in this artificial soil.\n\nNow save your questions and let me show you some of the wonders of the Everwound Wellspring!
A voyage that only a few have ever undertaken. We will travel to Sotha Sil's peculiar experiment—the Clockwork City.\n\nI have inquiries to make. You will assist me.

True, I suppose. Despite what you might think, I love this city. I can't be a party to its destruction.\n\nSeek out Gloaming Gates—impossibly deep pools of shadow. The cultists use them to travel great distances. You can too.

I do. The Tribunes are not so clever that they could hide such a place from me for long.\n\nThe city is quite close … and also very far away. Just the first of Sotha Sil's many paradoxes. If you choose to join me, be prepared for many more.

I do. The Tribunes are not so clever that they could hide such a place from me for long.\n\nThe city is quite close … and also very far away. Just the first of Sotha Sil's many paradoxes. If you choose to join me, be prepared for many more.

Of course you will. Naturally, you have questions. Alas, they will have to wait. Servants of the Tribunal do not look kindly on blasphemous journeys like this one.\n\nMeet me at the waterfall north of the city. We can discuss the details there.

I have not forgotten our romp through the Halls of Fabrication.\n\nYou proved your resourcefulness when facing the Assembly General. Now, you will prove your usefulness again, and receive an appropriate reward.

I have no great fondness for that Psijic, Lilatha, but you saved her life and defeated a powerful shadow mage in the process. A remarkable accomplishment for someone of your … breeding.\n\nI'm confident you will continue to surprise me.

You saved the life of a living god. Yes, I know all about your service to Vivec, and your conflict with Clavicus Vile.\n\nFoiling the plans of a Daedric Prince is no mean feat. I can think of no better companion for my journey to the Clockwork City.

Nightmarish fabricants and automata lurk in nearly every corridor of the Clockwork City. I need a skillful and deadly warrior at my side.\n\nA Silencer of the Dark Brotherhood fits that description splendidly, don't you think?

That business in Orsinium … you were one of King Bazrag's most powerful advocates, yes?\n\nI need someone who can fight and parley with equal skill. As a warrior and kingmaker, you will do splendidly.

The future holds its secrets close, but I have scried glimpses. Your spirit strides alongside those of anointed kings and heroes. Trust me—you walk the path to power.\n\nDon't believe me? Good. A healthy dose of skepticism will serve you well.
You escaped the prisons of Coldharbour. Truly, I think it would be easier to escape an iron safe at the bottom of the ocean.\n\nYou show great promise. I can use a slippery warrior like you.

You bested Molag Bal in mortal combat. In Coldharbour no less.\n\nDefeating a Daedric Prince in his own realm? That's a feat that even I would have trouble repeating. Only a great fool would pass up the opportunity to employ a Prince-slayer.

Did you not unite that rabble in Abah's Landing and reassemble the Thieves Guild there?\n\nOh, don't make that face. I have no interest in reporting you to the authorities. Quite the opposite. I need someone willing to take risks. You will do nicely.

I know of two—one east, one west. Look for the hidden caves where the shadows gather in force. Once you find a gate, you need only let yourself sink into it. \n\nI can't promise you'll like where you end up.

The gates weave in and out of Nocturnal's realm of Evergloam.\n\nYou can use them to reach your ultimate destination, just as the cultists do. But you must first traverse the Evergloam to find other connected gates.

Pray at the urns of the honored dead and accept the blessings of the Divines. Offering them to any of the corrupted dead that cross your blade will drive these vile Reach specters from their bodies and allow them to return to their deserved rest.

I'm reluctant to discuss it, but I suppose I must.\n\nWhen I struck my bargain with Clavicus Vile, I signed a magical contract in blood—forever binding myself to the Prince's will. As long as Vile's servants hold the contract, my soul is forfeit.
Seht bless your labors. I mean that.\n\nHate me if you must, but I truly hope you can stop this madness.

What? Oh, the ears? Yeah … yeah, I spent about a year studying the explosive properties of certain ores. In an enclosed space. For twelve hours a day. I wouldn't recommend it.\n\nI gathered up all my coin and bought a tiny clockwork amplivox to help.

I-I lost it, of course. Fell right out of my ear while I was leaning over a balcony. The Apostles don't have much patience for a deaf artificer's aid. Got pushed out of the basilica and wound up here.\n\nSo, yeah. Earplugs. Use them.
Thank you. Now, I believe I owe you some information.\n\nSeek out Gloaming Gates—impossibly deep pools of shadow. The cultists use them to travel great distances. You can too.

The Father of Mysteries, the Clockwork God, the Tinkerer, and other such banal titles.\n\nSotha Sil, or Seht, is a member of the Dark Elf Tribunal. He reigns over Morrowind as the god of craft and sorcery—the wisest and most reclusive of the Three.

Ha! No one truly knows Sotha Sil—not even his hordes of wild-eyed worshipers.\n\nI studied with him before his ascent, and even then he defied comprehension. His only true peer was Indoril Nerevar. Such a shame what happened to him.

Sotha Sil hides everything. But more to your point, it's not just a city. It's an incomprehensibly powerful world-shaping device. Can't leave that sort of thing lying about, can you?\n\nAlso, Almalexia worries about how it reflects on her divinity.

A Daedric artifact. I take a keen interest in all such objects, but this one seems especially significant. You see, nearly everyone who searches for it winds up dead.\n\nI suspect that someone or something hid this artifact away in the Clockwork City.
No, I'd rather speak to Chirrhari. I know her. I trust her. Lector Naril? He's still a stranger to me.\n\nWill you help me get past the factotums so I can talk to my old friend?
That's the question, isn't it? And it's the reason I have a bad feeling all of a sudden.\n\nWhy restrict where an apprentice can go? And why refuse to let me talk to Chirrhari? It makes no sense!

Apprentice? Sherizar is the first new apprentice to enter the Wellspring in years. The lector stopped selecting apprentices after poor Gathal's accident. At least that's how this one understands things.\n\nI suppose Idrono might know differently.

Chirrhari doubts there's anything sinister going on. Sotha Sil blessed the Wellspring with water, and Lector Naril's alchemical solutions make it possible to grow plants.\n\nIt's good to see Sherizar, though. We could use the help.

Idrono works with Chirrhari. He attempts to grow non-fungal plant life in harsh conditions. Since you're going to speak to him, could you bring along some of my mushrooms? But not the poisonous ones. He hates those.

That's a complicated subject—and one better left to the actual apprentices. Suffice it to say that the process involves water treated with alchemical nutrients and other solutions, as well as our simulated sunlight.

My program provides an opportunity to work outside the Clockwork Basilica. Lets them try their hand at something different.\n\nBesides, keeping the Wellspring going requires a lot of bodies. You'd be surprised at what's required to make my plants grow.

West. In the Ventral Terminus. He may have killed me, but he won't last long. He sealed his fate the moment he betrayed us.\n\nThere existed a covenant between your Gascone, Clavicus Vile, and my mistress, but he broke it. Now he will drown in blood.
He died. Some accident in Naris's lab. Naris hasn't let us in since. He was always secretive, but he's grown downright paranoid with Gathel's death.

Of course. Lector Naril tasked each of us with a different experiment. I'm attempting to grow plants without the benefit of the simulated sunlight. I haven't had any success so far, but someone has to tackle the difficult experiments, I suppose.

Ohtowen's been with Lector Naril the longest. She might know something more.\n\nYou'll need to cross my garden to reach her. Just watch out for the blasted fabricants. They keep eating my plants and clogging up the gears!

I suppose Lector Naril could have more apprentices toiling in his private workshop. He keeps numerous secrets, so what's a few more?\n\nYou can enter the workshop through the busted vent over there. Ignorance of his rules might grant you some leeway.

That was the practice until Gathal died. Then the lector sealed his private workshop and gave us these experiments to conduct while he perfected his simulated sunlight. It makes our annual harvest possible.\n\nIf there were other apprentices, I'd know.

Gascone vowed to bring us an artifact of great power. Now the artifact is gone. But don't worry. My mistress will wring the truth out of him soon. The Whispering Shadows will claim this artifact and you will all die, deafened by your own screams.

You really have no idea, do you?\n\nDaedric forces conspire in every dark corner—lurk behind every tree and stone. We spread like a plague, claiming more souls and territory with each passing hour! Sotha Sil's precious city will die at our hands.

Chancellor who? \n\nOh, you mean that brass-arsed fancy-boots that came running through here? Yeah, I seen him. Dragging his silly apostle skirts behind him like a broken wheel-chain. Seemed like he was in a hurry. Pretty suspicious if you ask me.

Yeah, the grease mucks up fabricant snoots. That's why we stay down here. Wouldn't want the constables to see …. Never mind!\n\nYour man headed west. Should be some oily footprints about. Follow those tracks and you'll find your fancy-boots.
Questions? You think I'm foolish enough to let you in? No, this door will remain closed. I just need time to work this out—to smooth things over. Simple. Now, leave me be!

What am I—? I am standing in solidarity with the impoverished and oppressed! While Sotha Sil and his Clockwork cronies bathe in opulent splendor, these people live hand-to-mouth. Every day.\n\nSoon, the entrenched lower class will rise up! Very soon.

If necessary, yes! People can only toil in silence for so long. Sotha Sil may be a god, but even a god can be made to listen. Clockwork City isn't just his plaything. We live here! It belongs to everyone! \n\nI …. Sorry. I get carried away sometimes.
Indeed. We use it to keep metal from corroding, blankets from fraying, that sort of thing. It helps keep our soles sturdy, our ropes taut, and our clothes clean. Well … cleaner. You know what I mean.

I was the only one willing to enter it, but I found a mysterious realm. I believe it may even be a plane of Oblivion.\n\nWell, it doesn't benefit me to study it further, but the Apostles may know more. If you've the patience to deal with them.

Only just arrived and already trying to grease the gears?\n\nNew arrivals must secure an endorsement from a citizen in good standing. I'm prepared to overlook your atrocious choice in companions if you can find a sponsor. Until then, you are tarnished.

That's for you to find out. Not many citizens will risk their reputation on a green-heeled stranger—and you'll find no comfort from me. Maybe you should confer with the other tarnished over there.\n\nIn the meantime, obey the law. I'll be watching.

Ah, yes, their bizarre sponsorship custom. I forgot about that little wrinkle. As a friend and peer of Sotha Sil, I come and go as I please.\n\nI suppose it would be best for you to wait out here. If I need you again, I will find you.

Some foul device that Night Sister Kamira uses to lure people into the Shadow Cleft and bind them to these scarecrows. If you can destroy it, we'll be set free!\n\nWithout the shadow array, Nocturnal's plans will be set back or even foiled completely.
Who I keep council with is none of your concern! \n\nYou're just like Varuni. So uptight. So naive! If you value your life, you'll leave this place. Now.
Gascone is dead? Well … he left us no choice, right? Good riddance, I suppose. I'll send some reclamation drones to collect his remains.\n\nNow what's this about Clavicus Vile?

Crows? Yes, a flock descended on the city just moments ago. They started squawking and defecating and making a nuisance of themselves as soon as they arrived.\n\nWe need to take this key away from them before our enemies do.
Typical Gascone … always trying to oil his way out when his plots fall apart.\n\nWhat did he tell you? Any specific leads we can follow up on?

Crows? Yes, a flock descended on the city just moments ago. They started squawking and defecating and making a nuisance of themselves as soon as they arrived.\n\nWe need to take this key away from them before our enemies do.

Fine. I made a bargain with Clavicus Vile. I know. Questionable. Just hear me out! All he wanted was a key. If I got it for him, he'd make me the ruler of Clockwork City.\n\nUnfortunately, someone stole the key before I could deliver it.

No. They serve that Shadow creature … or someone worse.\n\nClavicus Vile never told me why he wanted the key, but I think he means to give it to those cultists' master. When they learned I lost the key, they grew furious and resolved to kill me.

I did! Just be careful with it. The teeth are as sharp as Mehrunes' Razor, and the motor's a little temperamental.\n\nOne thing—if it starts to smoke, just drop it and find cover. I'm not saying it's going to explode but … it might explode.

Yes—and perhaps something more. In removing my shadow our attacker removed some vital part of my animus. My soul, in the common parlance. Without it, my power is severely diminished.\n\nNeedless to say, this will not do.

This may surprise you, but I've never had my shadow ripped from my body. Even so, I will devise a solution. Don't trouble yourself with the finer details. Just be prepared to fight.\n\nMuch will depend on your ability. Do not fail me.

Daedric Princes litter the world with profane relics—artifacts meant to corrupt or ensorcel the greedy and weak-minded. Hermaeus Mora offers a book. Peryite grants a shield. Nocturnal is more generous. She provides a mask, a bow, and a key.

Some daft talking crows!\n\nAfter that terrible business with the Shadow, I returned to my office to think. I arrived just in time to see one of those disgusting birds make off with the artifact! I panicked and ran here to hide.

It's ornate. Covered in Daedric runes. One of the factotums found it in the Fundament and placed it in the salvage gallery for sorting. I snatched it up shortly thereafter.\n\nI thought it was safe in my office … but those slagging crows!
