I'm so jealous right now. Fighting a Daedric Prince is what most hunters only dream of doing. But you actually did it. And you won! I should have stuck with you, instead of these two tracking hounds.

Not as much as you, clearly, but I've spilled my share of Daedra blood. The three of us have been rooting out the Court of Bedlam all across Summerset. Not with any official sanction, but the right people know what we're up to. The few we can trust.
You too. And the next time you decide to square off with the dark powers of Oblivion, send a girl an invitation, will ya?
Nah. At this point they're scattered, broken, and disorganized. Stragglers. They'll be in hiding for a long time, but that's really just making it sporting for me.

I was glad for the opportunity. \n\nWhen the Khajiit approached me, I thought my side investigation had finally crossed the wrong people. Fortunately, Razum-dar's allegiances are in the right place, even if his methods are questionable.

Into the Court of Bedlam. After I gave my report on the events at Cey-Tarn Keep, my superior considered the matter closed. I, of course, disagreed, so I continued to pursue the leads we uncovered along with Lindafwe and Silurie.

Swimmingly, though I think Silurie's brashness is rubbing off on us. We never got as close as you did to the organization's leadership, but while you were lopping off the heads of the hydra, we were sweeping its legs out from under it.
And I you. It's been an honor to fight by your side.

There's nothing harder to kill than an idea, believe me. The Court of Bedlam as we know it is gone, but the ideals it stood for will always appeal to some segments of our society. All we can do is be vigilant in excising their corruption.

I don't think I've ever met someone who's life is so complicated. If I had to map it out for an investigation I'd imagine it'd look like the Spiral Skein. So please try not to get into any trouble, for my sake.

Yes, well, better, I suppose. She's still impulsive and reckless, but … but I'll admit she's gotten better about taking other people into consideration.\n\nShe's even shown me a few of the things she's learned while overseas.
We do have you to thank for the fresh start, so if nothing else, I owe it to you to try.\n\nBest of luck with your own complicated affairs.
I don't, for the most part, but I'm trying to be more open minded. There is some merit to it, if you look deeply enough, and a good investigator should leave no stone unturned.

I am.\n\nMagic is an intensely personal exercise, initiate. No two mages weave their spells in exactly the same way. Like painting or sculpting, each artist has their own distinctive style. Josajeh's style is difficult to miss.

Removing her from the project is punishment enough.\n\nIn truth, the order finds the idea of punishment repugnant. The road to justice often leads to a place of vengeance. Too often. Punishment should serve as an opportunity for growth. Nothing more.

I will not bore you with the finer details. Perhaps an analogy?\n\nImagine an elaborate lock with thousands of tumblers. The master locksmith must learn their sequence and sensitivity before they can devise a key. Josajeh switched the tumblers.

Ah, right. Finding these pieces of the staff will require a bit more legwork.\n\nAs I said, each of the fragments emits a unique temporal wave, but the point of origin remains hidden. We were only able to locate points where those waves crash.

Exactly. Once you find a breach, you can use the Augur to track the waves back to their source—the staff fragment.\n\nThe trail should manifest as a series of lights. Just follow the lights and you'll find what we're looking for.

It wasn't too hard to give that idiot Llonas and his mother the slip, not that they didn't try, but I couldn't have done it without those papers you stole.\n\nIt's so good to be back on my home soil, even if I hardly recognize it.
No, I kind of like it. Gives me hope. There's a lot of tension in the air though. The growing pains will be long felt, I think.

I was a slave for a very long time, before Llonas was even born, but it's not the Isles themselves that have changed so much as the people. I would have never imagined seeing people from all over Tamriel walking the streets of Alinor.

Turns out all those years searching for Red Star Shells made me a fair hand at plying the waters for bounty, and Summerset has no shortage of shores. I make a good living hunting pearls, rare shells, and the like.

I don't know why you did what you did, but if you believe you can profit from slavery without having to get your hands dirty? You're wrong. Helping Llonas made you complicit.\n\nYou were willing to give me to a monster.

What's past is past. If I spent my time dwelling on all the wrongs dealt to me in my life, I'd die before I finished.\n\nIf you want to do right by me, do something the next time you face an injustice.

His wedding band was just another shackle. He never thought of me as a person, just a possession. The nice things he did were always just attempts to control me. He's no victim in this and you're no bystander.\n\nGood day.

More than a few of us have disappeared recently. Karnhar's group are just the latest. They set out to search for the missing and vanished themselves.\n\nWe're giving those buried ruins a wide berth now.

They've stood quiet for decades. But now? New, yawning sinkholes. Eerie sounds at night. I don't jump at shadows, but missing people? That's a warning I can heed. \n\nIf you head down there, take a look around for our friends. Will you?

Well, yes, why wouldn't I want to talk to you? I've been waiting for your arrival!\n\nYou see, this happens to be the Vault of Moawita, where the Psijic Order keeps its most cursed relics. It's a tad bit emptier than usual though. We've had a break in.

Exactly so! And you'll be the one to help us collect them again, hopefully before anyone comes to harm. Why, these items could cause all sorts of mischief.\n\nFirst though, let's have you read the Psijic Codex. That should help bring you up to speed.

Oriandra is indeed a member of our ancient monastic society. We once served as advisors to the rulers of Tamriel, but that was before we removed our island home from the world. Now this threat has drawn us back.\n\nBut why are you involved in all this?

We study the skull as it relates to cognitive behavior—when we're not on holiday, that is.\n\nThis was to be my well-earned sabbatical from the College of Sapiarchs. Alas, this business with the vintner dashed any hopes for relaxation. Typical.
Is that a threat? You would threaten a kinlady in her own lands? Truly there is nothing sacred left with Ayrenn on the throne.\n\nWell, I won't stand for it. I'm leaving.
I am a Kinlady of Summerset. It is not for you to dictate what is appropriate to me! I have been wronged and if I wish to see this Orc grovel as recompense, that is my prerogative.
No, I think it's rather appropriate for worms crawl in the dirt. Her mistake was sticking her head up too high. She can either slink back the muck or be snatched up but a more noble creature.

Normally she'd be jailed, but I recognize it was a simple mistake, so I offered to accept a plea. For some reason, she's refusing to do so. I just want to retrieve my horse, but if I have to get the authorities involved, I will.
Kinda like a hammer. Just smack it against whatever magical barrier is in your way and it should bring it down … if there's enough power left. It's not meant for subtlety.
A little gift from the Queen. In case I got caught. Luckily, I never had to use it. You don't want to know how I was supposed to hide it.

The Conclave serves as the Order's ruling body. It takes its name from the Eleven Forces of nature that we revere and follow as part of the Old Ways.\n\nThe Conclave assists the Ritemaster with matters of study, policy, and significant research.

You weren't the only newcomer to wander into this mind trap. Even a number of High Elves have succumbed to the dark entity's power. With my help, though, you were the first to break free.\n\nThat gives me hope that I can eventually save the others.

Frankly, I don't know what to think. Unfortunately, I don't have the luxury of leaving. I have a mountain of grapes that need to be guided through fermentation. If I don't stay on task, I may as well pour this year's vintage into the ocean.

I sent Valsirenn to Lillandril to scout the area around the College of Sapiarchs. She'll meet you there once you get the Proxy Queen's permission.\n\nAs for Oriandra, I sent her to warn Razum-dar, the Eye of the Queen. He needs to be informed.

He's frustrated by the situation. He hates that the Sea Sload got the better of him, and that he can't remember.\n\nThe Conclave is working with him to restore his memories while we go to warn the Sapiarchs about the threat to the Crystal Tower.

The Sapiarchs are the sages of Summerset. A college comprised of the finest minds in Altmer society. Each Sapiarch is devoted to a single area of expertise. Together, they maintain the greatest collection of knowledge in the world.

While I head to Lillandril and you secure the Proxy Queen's permission, the Ritemaster had another task for Oriandra. He asked her to seek out the Eye of the Queen, Razum-dar.\n\nHe wants to make sure the Eye is kept informed about the situation.

The Sapiarchs serve as the curators of the Crystal Tower. A pair of Sapiarchs called the Tower Sentinels protect the two keys needed to open the way to the tower. We'll need their help eventually.\n\nFirst, though, the Proxy Queen.

No, I doubt K'Tora's magic could reach Artaeum once it was removed from the world. I think that's why the Ritemaster hid the island in the first place.\n\nIf not for the abyssal pearl, K'Tora would never have been able to exert its influence again.

The kind that make the Ritemaster wary of allowing either the Sea Sload or the Daedric Princes to possess its power.\n\nLegends say the Crystal Tower exists in every planar realm at the same time. It literally connects all realities.

The Crystal Tower is a manifestation of ancient magic. It serves as a symbol for the Altmer. Its presence protects Summerset. The Sea Sload used the Ritemaster to weaken that protection, making their invasion possible.\n\nBeyond that, there are rumors.

Queen Ayrenn's regent while she's away. Proxy Queen Alwinarwe oversees the governance of Summerset from the Royal Palace in Alinor.\n\nI've never met her, but all reports indicate that she's fair if a bit set in her ways.

Meridia is the Daedric Prince of Life and Light and the matron of the Colored Rooms. She isn't part of the triad of Princes. Indeed, it seems that she has specifically sent her champion to oppose them.\n\nWe'll need to keep that in mind as we proceed.

I was just doing my studies. Like any other day. Then—then the tower began to shake suddenly. I heard screams. Such horrible screams.\n\nI watched my friends just … cease to exist. And in their places, these monstrosities stood.

I … I don't know. I grabbed this staff in hopes of balancing myself from the swaying of the tower. There was a flash of light and I … I was alone.\n\nBut I'm so scared. The staff's magic is fading. Oh gods, I'm going to end up like them.

Not you, too! I got enough doubt and dirty looks back in Artaeum!\n\nLook, Mephala was betrayed by Nocturnal. It stands to reason she might want to help us. And we could certainly use the power since I still can't make contact with Meridia.

You don't remember what happened in Nocturnal's realm? After she killed the Ritemaster? She took Dawnbreaker and corrupted it. I thought it was lost forever, but I guess she gave it to her earl.\n\nI need to get it back. Somehow.

The Sea Sload K'Tora was a practitioner of powerful mind magic. Even though you ended his threat, K'Tora left mind traps such as these around the island. We'll need to carefully dismantle the traps to save these adventurers.
<You are about to enter a Group Trial. Are you ready to leave your current Zone?>
Oh, yeah, that'd do. Whew, that's a load off my shoulders.

Every pack of dogs needs a leader. Werewolves are no different.\n\nBut Vykosa's power goes beyond that of a mere alpha. Legend has it she's one of the first to receive the curse of lycanthropy from Hircine.

Doesn't matter what I believe. What I know is that she's incredibly dangerous.\n\nOur reports indicate that she has the ability to compel other werewolves to do her bidding. Even somehow attract them to her. That's why the Moon Hunter Pack is so large.

I'm not sure, but it can't be anything good.\n\nThe Silver Dawn has also received reports of several kidnappings in the surrounding area. It's likely that Vykosa is turning innocents against their will. That's what prompted my order to strike.

Proudly so. My order fights to protect Tamriel against werewolf threats. I've dedicated my life to helping that noble cause.\n\nMoon Hunter Keep used to belong to the Silver Dawn, before it was taken by Vykosa and her pack over a year ago.

I'm afraid they wouldn't be the first. There's many here who once belonged to the Silver Dawn, turned by Vykosa and compelled to do her bidding.\n\nKilling them now would be a mercy. I'd rather die than become one of those beasts.

Yes, it was one of our largest strongholds. My companions and I hoped to regain the keep, but we underestimated the size of Vykosa's pack.\n\nI may be the only one left. Or, at least, the only one left human.

Yes, it appears I have. Almost makes me regret freeing her.\n\nThe Khajiit doesn't seem like much of a fighter, but she did claim to have information about the current state of the keep. It might not hurt to speak to her before moving on.

Before Vykosa took over this keep, the Silver Dawn used it as a base for research. Our most important studies involved finding a comprehensive cure for lycanthropy. \n\nPart of this cure was cultivating a unique strain of wolfsbane.
I'll be fine. This is just days of torture catching up to me. You should be more concerned with the upcoming fight.

For now, I can only hope. The Silver Dawn's research on a cure was very close to being complete before the keep was attacked.\n\nMeanwhile, I'll search for the spell scroll. I suspect it's somewhere in the library.
Then … I am doomed to remain cursed. Without those ingredients, this spell is useless.
Then my salvation is close at hand. \n\nDefeating Vykosa shall be your hardest fight yet. But I have faith in you, my friend. I'm just sorry I cannot stand with you in this final battle.

There's many reasons I could give. Certainly, I have no guarantee of killing her in my weakened state. Logically, I have no proof she's committed crimes against innocents.\n\nBut … I don't believe that either of those reasons are what stopped me.

In a land such as ours, who is to say this one would be better off without such power?\n\nThough this affliction may sometimes place her in danger, it has saved Narazda as well. After all, we live in troubling times.

While the Sapiarchs here work to attune themselves to the Resolute Diamonds, other Sapiarchs perform their parts of the ritual at the north and south platforms.\n\nNocturnal has sent Daedra to disrupt the ritual platforms. You need to stop them.

Of course! Though this one's role shall be strictly advisory. Narazda is not one for fighting.\n\nVykosa has taken the lives of far too many innocents. Her terrible reign must be brought to an end, yes? And so, this one helps.

You have defeated many werewolves now, yes? But none like Mylenne Moon-Caller.\n\nShe speaks, and the pack listens. Of course, this is mainly because she kills all who dare disobey her. Within this keep, only Vykosa holds more power.

What? You never heard of the Daedric Prince of Bargains? The ruler of the Fields of Regret and the lord of tricks and wishes? Well, don't tell him that! He's upset enough as it is.\n\nHe had such high hopes until Nocturnal betrayed their partnership.

Not yet. The jekosiit will first have us face another within her pack. The Archivist.\n\nWe will find him within the library, among his tomes and spells. There you shall face not only tooth and claw, but magic as well. Or so this one has heard.

Most gardens have flowers and hedges, perhaps a nice pond or two. \n\nVykosa's tastes run a tad more morbid. She has planted stranglers and spriggans, beasts of root and malice. Into this garden many go, but very few escape.

The Archivist was not merely a bookkeeper. He performed all manner of dark experiments, always claiming he was going to make the pack stronger. \n\nVykosa paid no mind to the pain these experiments caused … the suffering.

Forgive this one's secrecy. Not many are accepting of my kind.\n\nBut Narazda did not lie about being a prisoner. Like many, she was lured to Moon Hunter Keep by Vykosa's magic. For months, this one was forced to obey that jekosiit's commands.

Sometimes, the Archivist's experiments would have … unintentional effects. Often, werewolves would break under the agony. In their rage, they became nearly unstoppable.\n\nSo a poison was made to quickly end their lives.

I'm Barbas! Sure, I may look like a talking dog, but I'm actually … a talking dog! I'm my master's faithful hound and servant, although I have a tendency to annoy my Prince. Not sure why that is.\n\nAnyway, this is just one of my favorite forms.

Yes, for those who have already transformed.\n\nA few of my companions suffered that very fate. By then, the only thing we could offer them was a swift death. A horrible end for someone who dedicated their life to so just a cause.

Not alone. We'll also need to collect ripened belladonna berries, as well as a spell scroll. But those will be further within the keep.\n\nI can't stress enough how important this cure would be for my order.

Narazda has been a prisoner for many days now. But a fool, she is not. \n\nSo she has listened. And what she has happened to hear may prove very useful to you and the handsome soldier's endeavors. If he is willing to see reason, that is.
It is a test, you see. To prove that you are worthy enough to be one of her pack. Survive long enough, and she will bless you with her bite.\n\nBut most … most die.

You currently stand within the realm of Hircine, the Daedric Prince of the Hunt. \n\nHircine's plane of Oblivion takes the form of an endless forest where Great Hunts are constantly held. It also serves as the afterworld for all of his worshipers.

I am Hanu of the Zainab tribe. As an Ashlander, I refuse to accept the divinity of the Tribunal, and instead pledge myself to Azura, our Lady of Dawn and Dusk.\n\nThe only reason I've traveled to Hircine's realm is to save my father.

Yes. A powerful lurcher they call the Hedge Maze Guardian.\n\nThose who survived the garden simply avoided it. Unfortunately, it guards the only way further into the keep. If you wish to face Vykosa, it must be defeated.
I can't focus on that right now. Even with my affliction, our first priority is defeating Vykosa and ensuring the safety of Tamriel.\n\nCompared to that duty, my life means little.
Narazda …. The bodies she has seen. The screams she has heard.\n\nHe wishes to make the pack stronger, but so often he fails. This one … this one is sorry, walker, but she does not know more.

When Vykosa took Moon Hunter, many of the Silver Dawn were captured and forced to turn. Such was the Archivist's fate.\n\nBut he deserves no pity. He has caused the suffering of many with his dark experiments.

I'm afraid not. Vykosa's heart must still be fresh from the kill for this spell to work. We'd only have a few short moments after her death. \n\nBut we cannot delay what needs to be done. Vykosa must be defeated.

Indriks are native to Summerset. Just imagine a deer with some feathers and a horn or two. Throw in the power of teleportation, some sort of connection with nature, and there you have it.\n\nAn exciting Hare for any Great Hunt.

I heard the other hunters call it Bloodscent Pass. An evocative name, if nothing else.\n\nSpeaking of the other hunters, let's make sure to keep a lookout for our competition. I doubt followers of Hircine are keen to play fair.
Let us not speak of that now, yes? Our handsome soldier would not be pleased if he overheard such things.

I know. And I cannot even find salvation in death.\n\nMy soul belongs to Hircine now. Even if I take my life, I'll be forever condemned to his Hunting Grounds. Never will I know the peace of Aetherius.

And for that, I shall forever be grateful.\n\nGiven the circumstances, I don't think the Silver Dawn would fault me for offering you a reward. After all, it's by your actions that this keep was saved.
She was my ally. That's all.\n\nI'm a simple man. I know what's right and what's wrong. Killing someone who so greatly aided me … there's no honor in that.

I didn't join the Silver Dawn to kill werewolves. I-I wanted to protect people. Save the lives of those who could not save themselves. Spread justice to an unjust land.\n\nKilling Narazda … that wouldn't be justice. That would simply be cruel.

Yes. Narazda was among those the Archivist experimented on. The testing was supposed to strengthen her, to make her more … useful to the pack.\n\nAnd in a way, it did. It made her strong enough to resist Vykosa's compulsion.

The Archivist hoped to study what happened to Narazda, to prevent it from happening to others. That is the only reason she was not killed.\n\nSo much suffering. So much death. And finally, it has been brought to an end. Thank you.
Yes. It was the least this one could offer.\n\nNarazda would have guided him, had he asked. Protected him. But that was not who our handsome soldier was, walker. Till his last breath.

This one will admit, there were struggles. Learning to control was not easy.\n\nBut through it all, she has gained strength. Power. Freedom. All things Narazda never had, before she was bitten. All things she would hate to lose.

And do you not? Yes, Narazda knows what you are.\n\nSurely, you too have felt the duality of our affliction. This power, it is both curse and blessing. It has given us strength, power, freedom. And hardship, of course. And pain.
Of course he thinks that. After all, if I die here … I'll be trapped. Just like him.
I'm not sure. Given their prowess in battle, I doubt they were fellow competitors. It's far more likely they were spirits, living out their afterlife within the Hunting Grounds.

Oh, I cannot deny my fear. This place is nothing but a den of savagery. And to never be able to join my ancestors? To never guide my people? I cannot think of a worse fate.\n\nBut I've come all this way to save my father. How can I leave him now?
Yes, of course. I was led here by Azura herself in order to save my father. I cannot waver now, no matter the cost. Even if I'll be paying that cost … for eternity.

Going by the name, I'd say a lot of fog. Try not to get lost, all right?\n\nAnd under no circumstances are you to let your guard down. This is the perfect opportunity for the other teams to strike against us.
Well, it killed them first, there's no mistaking that. And then it seemed to use their bodies like bloody puppets. How horrifying.\n\nThis isn't an ordinary indrik, not by any means.

Besides an absolute fetcher? Not a clue.\n\nBut that scent comment has me thinking he's more than just your common Orc. Perhaps a werewolf? That would make sense, given he's competing in Hircine's Great Hunt.
You're right. I shouldn't go against my father's wishes, just to do what I think is best. Who am I to heap that guilt upon his shoulders?\n\nIs it … is it selfish that I'm relieved?

The blood of werebears runs through our veins.\n\nYou know, the cozies out there are always quick to associate Lord Hircine with werewolves. And they're fine and all, I suppose. But nothing beats a werebear's might!
Not sure yet. Winning the Great Hunt is sure to earn us eternal glory. Any prize we earn afterward is just icing on the sweetroll.

This Great Hunt isn't going to be a Sundas stroll, that's all.\n\nI wouldn't waste my time getting friendly with the competition, if I were you. It's not like that tusking stag up there is going to care if we play dirty.

Balorgh kneels for no one, be they Divine or Daedric Prince.\n\nI'm here for one thing, and that's power. If I have to play Hircine's little game to get that? So be it. But I won't be kissing his hairy arse along the way.

What mer wouldn't want Hircine's favor?\n\nAs avid followers of the Green Pact, my tribe depends on hunting for our survival. With just one boon from the Huntsman Prince, our prosperity shall be assured.

The Hunting Grounds may be full of danger, but my tribe hails from Valenwood. Dangerous forests and elusive quarry are part of our everyday life.\n\nI just hope you aren't foolish enough to underestimate us.

A weapon that will ensure successful and bountiful hunts for generations to come. An easy enough wish for one as great as Lord Hircine to grant.\n\nDon't take this competition lightly, hunter. For my tribe, it's do or die.

It looks like a common wisp. I've heard tales of hunters befriending the creatures in the wilderness and using them to track down prey.\n\nActually, now that I think of it, my father was the one who told me that story.

Exactly so. Any cursed with lycanthropy are forced to come here after they die, whether they were a follower of Hircine or not.\n\nThis specific section of the Hunting Grounds is known as the March of Sacrifices.

Danger, and lots of it. The creatures here are known to be ferocious, and those that hunt them even more so. We'll have to keep wary of both predator and prey.\n\nWithin this realm, it's hunt or be hunted. I suggest we keep to the former.

She spoke of a Telvanni mage who would tell me how to travel to the March of Sacrifices. Only then would I be able to win back my father's soul. And so, here I am.\n\nPerhaps she even foresaw your aid as well.
I had a dream. I saw a dark forest, and heard my father's voice calling out. No matter how long I searched, I couldn't find him. \n\nAnd then I heard a beautiful voice, full of light. It was Azura.
I don't mean Hare as in a rabbit. It's the name given to whatever, or whoever, is being hunted. In this case, it's an indrik.
Do give me some credit. If I'm about to jump into a plane of Oblivion, research is the least I can do. Besides, Daedric studies was always my specialty within the tribe.

Worshipers of the Daedric Prince of the Hunt? Doing whatever they can to win a hunting competition? Yes, I think they will attack us.\n\nLet's just hope they end up killing each other off before getting to us.

Nor a follower of Hircine, I assure you of that.\n\nIt's just the fate of all who die within the Hunting Grounds. Not generally an issue, I'm sure. It's unusual for someone who doesn't worship Hircine to end up here in the first place.

Can you kill what's already dead? I'm sure they'll reform, eventually.\n\nI suppose, without some form of death, the stakes of a hunt just aren't high enough. Not too surprising that there's a cycle of death and rebirth within this plane of Oblivion.

Or created it. The Hunting Grounds are supposed to be a hunter's paradise. Perhaps he was able to will the wisp into being?\n\nThat's just like my father though. No grand weapons or cunning traps for him. Just a helpful little wisp to light our way.
Yes, but that Orc is still alive and kicking. And if we're to believe the leader of the Wood Elves, that fetcher played a part in their demise.\n\nNot to mention the Nords.
Given our luck so far, I doubt it.\n\nIf we are attacked, you cannot hesitate. We've already seen how brutal the Great Hunt can be. Show mercy, and we may never leave this cursed realm.

It is worrisome, isn't it? After all, the beast can turn itself invisible.\n\nOf course, we have our useful little light with us. I have a feeling it may help us discover Tarcyr, should it attempt to hide in plain sight.

Strange. Hircine invites the participants of these hunts himself. The only reason I snuck my way in was because of Azura's wisdom.\n\nWell, the most important thing is that we collect Tarcyr's heart before he does.

No, it isn't. But what about what I want? For years, this is all I've ever wished for. To finally save my father. To finally repay his selfless actions.\n\nI've risked everything towards this goal. How can I turn back now?
Several years ago, my family was attacked by a pack of werewolves. My father was bitten while trying to defend us. When he transformed, he assaulted a member of my tribe. \n\nHe … had to be killed.

Well, information is my primary business, and business is good! Which reminds me, I never give anything away for free. Especially information.\n\nPerform a favor for me. Then I'll tell you what I know about Margus Derius.

The best kind, one that benefits us both!\n\nAllow me to mark a house on your map. Inside you'll find a crate that contains an elegant jacket. I'm something of a snappy dresser and I want that jacket. Bring it to me and I'll tell you all about Margus.
Well, get to it! Information is like mammoth milk. It spoils if you don't use it quickly.

You don't take a hint very well, do you? To answer your question, this market buys and sells certain items of historic value. We maintain an extensive list of wealthy collectors and are always on the lookout for specific relics.\n\nWhy do you ask?

This one sent Argar to an old ruin. He was to pick up a package from some thieves we do business with and bring it to me. Here, let me mark the location on your map.\n\nGo, find out what happened to him. Then I will tell you about Margus Derius.
Then this one has nothing to say to you right now. Find my assistant or I'll never tell you what I know about Margus Derius.

I prefer merchant to smuggler, but call me what you will. I transport rare and valuable antiquities—no questions asked. I'm also considered the most knowledgeable Argonian relics expert outside of Black Marsh. \n\nSo, how can I help you this day?
And I'm waiting for a wamasu egg. To be more specific, I'm waiting for one of the beautiful eggs from the nest I marked on your map.\n\nDo you have a wamasu egg for me hiding in your pack, perhaps?

Such aggression! There is no need to threaten violence, my friend. Eshundir said he would take care of you, and indeed he will.\n\nMargus has associated himself with a band of thugs and outlaws. They hide in a cave like rabid guar.

I require a wamasu egg. Not just any egg, mind you. A specific egg from a specific nest. Let me mark the location on your map.\n\nBring me an egg from that nest and I'll tell you more about Margus than you really care to know.

So far. Yes ….\n\nI found nothing in the eastern xanmeer but the priestess's thralls and the reek of mingling blood. Whoever was there has already been taken to bleed on the temple's teeth, or her own.

Shuxaltsei soaks the Teeth of Sithis in blood to stoke the great serpent's appetite. She is inviting it to take its first bite. The beginning of the end. \n\nIt will sink its fangs deep and swallow all creation.

It does not matter. We are too entangled in the rotting roots of our past to flee from it. They have spread far and wide, unnoticed beneath the surface, and now that they have broken into the light it is too late.\n\nSo, what would you have me do?
He got out? Slippery skink, that one. Well, what are you waiting for? Set me loose, so I can give these bloodsuckers a good thunk right in their pointy teeth!

Our society consists of me, my sister, and a few associates. We've been preparing an expedition to return the antiquities we've recovered to Murkmire, deep in the heart of Black Marsh. Unfortunately, our competition has become … aggressive.

One and the same! Margus Derius. He's a black marketeer who cares only about profit. He was a member of our society until he stole our research and disappeared.\n\nI need you to infiltrate the nearby Outlaws Refuge and figure out what Margus is up to.
I will prepare the dagger and the sacred altar according to the stories the elders told me.\n\nIn the meantime, I need you to weaken the Wuju-Ka. Only then can we perform the ritual.

Sounds like you didn't need Jee-Lar's help after all. Ah, well. I'm not anxious to fight with these Blackguards anyway.\n\nI erect the spine of greeting, new friend of Jee-Lar. I am happy to meet you, and that's a fact!

Let me see what you found. Hmm. An Argonian charm necklace. See the amulet? That's a river stone. The Imperial Legion called them swamp coins.\n\nAnd this is a Xal-Toh tablet. That literally translates as sacred secret. Very interesting ….

An old legend involves a necklace and a tablet. If I'm right ….\n\nReturn to the Outlaws Refuge and talk to Eshundir the smuggler. He's an expert on Argonian lore. Ask him what he knows about these relics. Meanwhile, there's a book I need to look at.

This one has no proof, but I'm sure Margus sent one of his Blackguard thugs to silence poor Eshundir. I feel it in my tail!\n\nGrethaa slipped away at the first sign of trouble and I hid in a crate. Eshundir … he wasn't so lucky.

No, I will say nothing else. This one prefers to keep her blood inside her body! But these items point to other relics. Relics Margus needs to reach his ultimate goal, whatever that is.\n\nThe Blackguard murderer, maybe he left a clue you could follow?

Concordia mentioned something about the Xal-Toh tablet. An old legend. Reminds me of a story my egg-mother used to tell me about a cursed skull ….\n\nThat's a worry for later. Concordia sent me to help you right before she departed.
All right. Do what you need to do. When you're ready, find me and we can travel to Shadowfen.
Chid-Moska? That's in Shadowfen and that's a fact! We should hurry if we want to stop Margus and the Blackguards!\n\nI can arrange transportation for us. Just tell me when you're ready to go.

The Psijic Order is an ancient society of mages, more akin to a monastic order than to the upstart Mages Guild, for example.\n\nWe once served as advisors to the rulers of Tamriel, before we departed the world to pursue other interests.

It means just that. We took our island of Artaeum and sent it someplace else to better promote meditative study and contemplation.\n\nWe maintain an interest in Tamriel, though, hence my appearance here during your time of need.
I haven't isolated the source of the mind magic, except that the malevolent entity calls itself K'Tora. It imprisoned you in the mind trap in order to control you, but to what purpose I'm not sure.

I have no idea. Whoever or whatever K'Tora is, it wields powerful mind magic. Much more powerful than anything I've ever encountered before. The mind trap is an insidious spell that has ensorcelled a number of victims.\n\nI'm still watching over them.

You weren't the only newcomer to wander into this mind trap. Even a number of High Elves have succumbed to the dark entity's power. With my help, though, you were the first to break free.\n\nThat gives me hope that I can eventually save the others.

You noticed that, did you? Very observant! The mind trap created replicas of items you already possessed. You needed them, so they became real inside the illusion.\n\nAnd of course you'd still have them in the waking world. They are real, after all.

Why didn't I think of that? The Blackguards are sure to harass anyone they think can help them decipher the clues that lead to the cursed skull!\n\nI can think of five or six knowledgeable Argonians right here in Shadowfen!

Here. You check on the Argonians on this list and I'll go check on a few others. Meet me back here after you're done and we can compare notes.\n\nJust be careful. If the Blackguards found them, there's a good chance they're keeping an eye on them.

I do.\n\nOne of your native companions warned you off of it, didn't they? Believe me, I sympathize. But despite my lifestyle, I'm still an Argonian—one with ample means. Who would I be if I didn't use that wealth to help my people?

Yes. You clearly want what's best for Murkmire. I can think of no one more qualified for the task.\n\nYou and the Bright-Throat, Xukas, have grown close, yes? He knows a great deal about the Remnant, I'm sure. Please, convince him we only want to help.

I only know that we were kept in the chambers beneath the twin xanmeers. If anyone is still alive, that's where they will be found.\n\nBe cautious, they will be guarded by those Shuxaltsei has enthralled. They overwhelmed us with ease.

We were custodians of the Teeth of Sithis. Though it does not serve the same purpose it was built for, it is no less sacred. When the pitiful souls under the high priestess's sway came to defile it, we resisted them, but her power was too much.

A wonder from before dusk. Built high to cast Sithis's long shadow over the land. A reminder that Sithis is always looming. Waiting to return us to nothingness.\n\nThe old ways were flawed. Many saw Sithis as destroyer, but not as creator.

Of course you do.\n\nThis matter of the Remnant … you must understand, it is fragile as a marsh-robin's egg. Even so, I trust your heart, and truthfully, we could use the help. Bright-Throats are negotiators, not warriors. And war is brewing.

All answers lie with the Hist. It is just a matter of hearing what it has to say. Chime-Maker Shuvu can help us.\n\nOur Hist speaks through the wind, you see. Its words rustle though the boughs, and our chimes sing out its counsel. Poetic, right?
You're not … oh no, if they see you talking to me ….\n\nYou have to leave. Now! I want nothing more to do with Margus Derius or the Skull of Beela-Kaar!

All the more reason for me to run as far from this place as I possibly can. I know how powerful cursed Argonian relics can be!\n\nIf only I had enough gold for the voyage. My poor feet can only carry me so far, you know.

They showed me a woodcut that contained ancient Argonian symbols. I could read some of them. They described a ritual to turn meditation cylinders into keys.\n\nA contribution to my travel fund might help me remember more ….

That's rather courageous of you. Few willingly oppose the Blackguards.\n\nWell, you'll need to hurry. I already interpreted the portion of the woodcut that refers to the ritual. Their leader, Margus, knows how to recover the cursed skull.

By performing the ritual exactly as the woodcut described it. I warned him it was dangerous. One misstep and the spell will consume him!\n\nOf course, he needs ritual objects to focus the spell. I couldn't decipher that section of the woodcut, though.
Look, I have a family. If the Blackguards even suspect that I told you this much, they'll make them disappear.\n\nNo, no. I have nothing else to say on this matter.

Not a Blackguard? Then why should I tell you anything? Unless you're one of those thorns in their sides that their leader complained about.\n\nAre you one of them? Are you a thorn in the Blackguards' side?

This is just a guess, but I think the ritual unlocks the hiding place of the Golden Skull of Beela-Kar. And once Margus gains the cursed skull, he can summon forth the power of the mad sorcerer. Power enough, the legends say, to destroy Murkmire.

The Argonians I talked to said the same thing. Apparently the woodcut describes some sort of ritual that will allow Margus to either find or retrieve the cursed skull. \n\nWhat did the Argonians you talked to have to say on the subject?

We need to find that ship! One of the Argonians told me that only three Blackguards know the location, but as a precaution they each carry one-third of a map. They must work together to reach the ship.\n\nYou find two of them and I'll get the third.

That's interesting. Very interesting! Those words mean "the forbidden place" in the language of Murkmire.\n\nI also learned that the Blackguards are preparing to launch an expedition to find this island so Margus can perform the ritual.

Ha! Only for wide-footed bumblers. Unfortunately, Famia has a weak eye for talent, and Murkmire is full of clumsy risk-takers.\n\nBut don't worry, walker. This one has been on five expeditions with Famia and only seen people eaten by salamanders twice!

Hmm. Only this: when we find treasure, take no more than you can carry comfortably. A heavy purse will make you slow, and being slow will make you dead.\n\nOh, and if you see Zadaza running, you should run, too—in the same direction. Simple!
Ask away, walker! Our leader, Famia, knows more about the ruins than Zadaza, but Zadaza knows more about not getting eaten by crocodiles. This one will let you decide which is more important.

Confidence! Initiative! Excellent! These are wonderful traits that will almost certainly get you killed. Do not worry—Zadaza will ensure that your legend lives on by scooping up your bloody gear and selling it.\n\nAh, Famia arrives!

Famia is very smart—not clever, though. Zadaza risks losing her tail because she is bold, and beautiful, and greedy. But Famia risks all because she loves the lizard-folk.\n\nDo not ask this one to explain why. It makes no sense to Zadaza.

Ha! Rajhin's shadow, how much time do we have? Sink-sand, poison darts, blades of all sizes … oh, and falling rocks. And also poison gas. This one is probably forgetting a few things.\n\nJust assume that everything in the xanmeer wants you dead.

That depends on what you value, yes?\n\nFamia looks for this Kajin-Jat Crystal. Zadaza looks for things that are light and numerous—baubles and ancient coins, you see? Some look for heavy golden idols. They tend to wind up squished or in pieces.

Confidence! Initiative! Excellent! These are wonderful traits that will almost certainly get you killed. Do not worry—Zadaza will ensure that your legend lives on by scooping up your bloody gear and selling it.\n\nAh, Famia arrives!

The ancient Argonians locked the xanmeer up tight—and not just with metal locks. They infused the stone with sun-magic.\n\nI won't pretend to understand how it works, but I do know that without a potent magical focus, the door won't budge.

I'm glad you asked!\n\nThere are flecks of yellow glass scattered all over Murkmire. We call them vakka stones, and each one contains a bit of ancient magicka. Put enough of them together and you can activate all sorts of things. Things like doors.

Let me take a look. I'm pretty good at these sorts of puzzles.\n\nThis goes here … that goes there … and we have a complete map! Without a place to start, however, this could be anywhere in southern Shadowfen. I wish we had more time.

Well, according to what the Argonians told you, Margus knows the ritual, knows where to find the meditation cylinders, and knows the location of the forbidden island. We're running out of time.\n\nYou need to use this map to find the Blackguards' ship.

I appreciate the compensation.\n\nNow listen. Two things. The meditation cylinders are hidden on an island called Norg-Tzel, but I have no idea where that is. Second, the Blackguards are preparing a ship on the river near Deep Graves to go find them.

Fair point. I heard the Blackguards talking. They mentioned they're preparing an expedition to retrieve the ritual objects. Said their ship was moored near Deep Graves, along the river.\n\nIf they find them and unleash the curse, Murkmire is doomed.
No, but the ship's pilot knows the way! We just need to board that vessel and convince the pilot to help us.\n\nI doubt the Blackguards inspire much loyalty in their hirelings.
Yes, I was. My betrothed was very kind. It's a pity I must disappoint her, but these things happen.
It will be a less personal disappointment than if I were to arrive without the seed-doll she gifted me for the occasion. It's the least I can do to return her kindness.

A haj mota snatched it out of my hands as I soaked my feet by the guloo bridge. Very quick. Gone in an instant. Such is life.\n\nI do not know why the haj mota would want such a thing, but the Hist must have thought it needed it. I hope it enjoys it.

So you're the lucky adventurer Varo selected for my little quest. I approve, I certainly do!\n\nI've long suspected that Tsofeer Cavern was tied to the Imperial occupation of the First Era, but until recently the place was sealed up tight as a drum.

Then this vakka stone belongs to you, I think. Friend-Famia never tires of poking around in the old hard-nests. I do not know why, but very few dryskin habits make sense to me.\n\nThe xanmeers are very dangerous. Do you have a guide?

Ah. This does not surprise me. I hope you will not let her come to harm. Famia is a worthy friend. She honestly tries to do right by the Saxhleel, but her persistence … it often gets her into trouble.\n\nI wish you luck in your expedition.

I'll be fine! If anything threatens us, Xukas will take care of it. This business with Eshraf and Dinia has me worried. I'm hoping Xukas can find out if anyone's seen them. \n\nOh, before you leave, could you give me those vakka stones and the sword?

That makes the area you need to search considerably smaller!\n\nFind that ship and stop Margus before he completes the ritual that unleashes the curse. I'd really rather not see Murkmire destroyed, thank you very much!

A Dwemer vault—hidden in the ice for ages—finally reveals itself and you just happen to wander in here? You are either very lucky … or someone tipped you off.\n\nI'm not letting this discovery slip through my fingers. I have a proposal.
<The panel pushes in with ease. As it locks into place you feel a vibration run up your arm and through your body. The device buzzes ominously in a low growling tone as you pull your hand away.>
I hope the Dwarves left you something that put up a good fight. None of those clanking bits of scrap and steam ever wets my blade like a good flesh and blood foe, but they make for a good workout.
<You are about to enter a Group Dungeon. Are you ready to leave your current Zone?>

I believe so. There's an artifact mentioned in Ayleid records from the same time period bearing a lot of similarities to the tablet we discovered in the Vault of Mhuvnak. Lost with the fall of their empire and found by the Empire that conquered them.

Hah! So much for the immortal servants of Meridia! Have to admit, I'm jealous. Never had the good fortune to snuff out an undying life. Not any that still bleed anyway.\n\nI'm proud of you, killer. It's like you're trying to impress me.
<You are about to enter a Group Dungeon. Are you ready to leave your current Zone?>

I will lend you my expertise in all things Dwemer, in exchange you act as escort for our expedition. You may take the lion's share of any valuables, but the items of historical significance are mine.\n\nIs that agreeable to you?

Not according to the official record. The Imperials built a fort here around three hundred years ago, but it was lost to some unspoken calamity and abandoned. Unofficially, an item of similar description was unearthed here not long before then.

The sacred texts. Beliefs of the elder ways fading further from memory, but they are still precious to those who honor the primal entity.\n\nIf Cyrodilic Collections can keep them safe, they will be pleased.

If my research proves correct—and it usually always does, by the way—then Tsofeer Cavern was occupied by the Imperial Legion during the expansion of the First Era. It stands to reason that some of their armor might still be in those caves.

And so the stream returns to its source. It's very pretty, isn't it? My betrothed is very skilled.\n\nIt seems some of the roots have bent. I will tell her it was from my overzealous embrace. That should make her happy.
The Hist has made certain I stay on this course. I will not resist its desires. Not that I would want to. I think I will enjoy the bonding ceremony.
I do not fear the limp-fins. I want my dowry.\n\nI took it from my betrothed fairly. I want it back.
Guards took it. Hid it from me. Topeth tells me my betrothed has gifts for me instead, but I do not want gifts. I want my dowry.\n\nI would take it back, but I am watched.
Because it is my dowry. The Hist meant it for me. Bright-Throats do not understand this. If they will not respect our custom, I will not respect theirs.\n\nNo dowry, no bonding.
Finally, the Hist provides. It sours my stomach that I had to rely on you to take what, by right, is mine. But suitors must be flexible. I guess.\n\nThe custom is met. I will join in the bonding.
Never … he is dead.\n\nHe entered a trance to steel himself for the Dread Fathering Elixir, but after we administered the potion he never awoke. It seems Sithis felt Ruxol had children enough.

Kishi is always in trouble, but never has the mud risen so high. He disobeyed tradition, tribal laws, and my direct orders when he decided to interfere in the rites of ascension.\n\nNow the raj-kaal has sentenced the spawn of my eggs to death.

This book should have been destroyed ages ago. Kishi hid it here. He wants me to remember who I was, but I am no longer the ka-deelith.\n\nThe tribe has sentenced Kishi to death. I will stand at my son's side and die with him.

I grind my fangs in frustration. I tried to talk to the raj-kaal, the war-chief, but he doesn't want to hear the truth. The Dead-Water only care about strength and death, and they plan to follow that path to the bitter end.
No one could fill the void Ruxol left behind.\n\nKaoc. I suppose I must try. For the good of the tribe. I will need more of our Dread Fathering Elixir. Ruxol drank it to the last drop.
This one is aptly named. Let me add it to the mixture I have already prepared.\n\nIf I survive, you may tell Topeth I will do my part.
You are a gift from the Hist, like the sweetest of saps on my lips. Come, join us for this momentous occasion. It is only fitting.

Her way is the old way, from before the fall. We were less mindful of the cycle of change and gave only to the Void. When the Hist revealed the true path to us, she chose to break the branch of her bond rather than turn back, or so the story goes.

The story said she was cast down and entombed far from the roots of the Hist, never to return, but every spine on my body tells me the twisted creature that bathes in the blood of my fellows is Shuxaltsei.

It is. The tale of Shuxaltsei's betrayal and fall is a reminder not to stray from the guiding boughs of the Hist. \n\nI thought the lesson was embellished for effect, but it seems the only exaggeration was her demise.
"Smoke of stars to see what once was seen, sunless sap to hear what once was heard."\n\nA bramble of words. I appreciate the Hist's poetry, but this is not an ideal time for it, I think.
Whoa, that's an interesting collection of smells. This stuff is nasty. Let me mash it up a bit.

I do not know. Hopefully Shuvu can teach me how to decipher the words. It will take time, but I will find you if I learn more.\n\nPerhaps friend-Famia could help also? Or Kassandra. They both know the marsh's stone-secrets. They could prove useful.

Following another lead on the Remnant. Or, a potential lead. Someone she worked with before she started funding Cyrodilic Collections? I don't know much more.\n\nShe asked me to tell you to join them when I saw you. So, I suppose you should do that!

West of here, near that spooky prison. Honestly, I missed most of it. Too preoccupied by her bodyguard. Something about how he looks at me … gives me the shivers, you know?\n\nBut we have better things to discuss. What did you learn with Xukas?

Hmm. Ritual Argonian poetry. The words are common, but the meter is all wrong. There's more to it. Missing verses, perhaps? Truthfully, Kassandra is the authority on that sort of thing.\n\nYou should set out. I'll try to dig up a few relevant texts.

The Blackguards? My sister's tangled with them in Murkmire.\n\nI need to warn <<1>>. He's one of our agents. I've got him looking into Margus as well, but you seem to be having more luck. What else did you learn?

You are a wonder, my friend! I know exactly where that cave is. Allow me to mark the location on your map.\n\nAre you willing to see this through? I'll rally Jee-Lar, but time is of the essence. Will you go to Sunless Hollow and recover the relics?
That's troubling. If we don't act fast, those antiquities will disappear and the Argonians will lose a little more of their history.\n\nIf only we knew where this hidden storehouse was located ….

My egg-sire? How unexpected. When last we talked, he urged me not to oppose the ka-deelith. But I refuse to let the Dead-Water become nothing but a memory.\n\nUnlike Bhoki, I have drunk from the river of courage and refuse to turn away from my tribe.

The cave is called the Sunless Hollow, and it's located not too far from here. \n\nI have one more secret for you, wayfarer, so listen well. Margus and his associates are dangerous. I suggest caution. And with that, our business comes to an end.

I consider. We killed many savages together. We will do so again. If the Hist thinks you worthy of Remnant secrets, you will survive. If not, so be it.\n\nI hunt Blackguards. They skulk around our village, yanking up our grave-stakes like salt-daisies.

I arch my brow-ridge. Special? Yes. Our grave-stakes do not just pin the dead to their resting place. Each tells a story—some as old as the tribe itself.\n\nSome of our greatest raj-kaals even had the honor of using a Hist bough to make their stakes.

Yes. All the more reason to hack these Blackguards dead.\n\nMeet me in the swamp, east of the village. Our quarry is there. Many unstaked bog-blights also—freed from their dead-sleep by those thieving savages. Bare your fangs, ojel. Time for war.
Yup. Helps it go down.\n\nThere you go. Just about ready. Take that over to the cauldron and get chugging. Bottoms up!

The Blackguards steal our fallen egg-kins' grave-stakes without regard for the stakes' purpose. Now, the rivers choke on bog-blights, dead-and-not-dead things that eat Nagas whole.\n\nWith cunning, we will see to it that they eat only Blackguards.

The Blackguard savages build pahnjees—this word means fumers. Racks of oily, spoiled meat that keep the bog-blights off their scent.\n\nAs we recover the grave-stakes, destroy the fumers. The dead-not-dead will find our enemies and do the rest.

One shouted at the other about a relic they could not find. The grave-stake of a krona-kaal—the great Dead-Water war-chief called Etra of the Many Spears.\n\nFew Dead-Water warriors rival Etra. He is wutulm. You would say legend, I think.

I blink my eyes. Maybe? Reading a xul-vaat is grave-singer work. We cannot know until we claim the stake. You will have to fight him for it.\n\nAll Dead-Water kaals know Etra's resting place. Look west and follow the ridge line. His tomb is there.
I will reclaim your body and make a helm of your skull. You have earned that, at least.

I shake my head. It is a grave-stake like the others. I do not even know what to look for. The symbols are worn, but … wait. I see it. In the grain. In the whorls and knots.\n\nThe Remnant. It swims in the wood. I can almost touch it.
Patience! There are words …. In a garden in a maw of stone? Yes, that is all. I see nothing more.

What is us? The bumbler, Famia? Xukas? The dryscale, Kassandra? A nest of weak-spines and ojel treachery! I will not—\n\nI … am sorry. The Dead-Water are a suspicious people, but you deserve my respect. And my trust. I will join you in Lilmoth.

A location, clearly. But a location for what?\n\nI did some more research on the first riddle. The one about smoke and sap, remember? Well, after combing through a half-dozen dissertations, I'm pretty confident it's referring to a dream-wallow.
Do not take too long. I want an egg, not a hatchling, after all!\n\nMay a hundred shades of luck color your days, wayfarer.
Then I suppose we have nothing more to talk about right now.\n\nReturn to me when you have the egg.

I suppose I should be thankful for that. Look, the curse of Beela-Kaar is a terrible thing. He hated his fellow Argonians. If Margus unleashes the power of the curse, all of Murkmire will be destroyed!\n\nI hope you do stop him. I hope so very much.
Suit yourself. It's no scales off my tail if you don't want to hear the rest of what I could tell you. And all because you couldn't bear to part with a little bit of gold ….
The Blackroses have me under their thumb. If I step out of line, they'll press down. I don't have enough money to pay them off.
I'm taking a big risk, but I think the Blackroses have a transport in the river near Deep Graves. I'm not sure where, but that's what I've been able to piece together from what they've said.
I wish you could, too. Even though there's no way I can pay off the Blackroses, even a little money might make my life easier.
I won't do anything else to endanger my family. The Blackguards warned me that they could get to them faster than a crocodile can gobble up a croaking frog.\n\nNo, I have nothing else to say to you.

That's a fair point. Very well.\n\nI overheard the Blackguards. They mentioned that Margus was funding an expedition to find the ritual objects. Said they had a boat moored near Deep Graves, along the river. It's not much, but I hope it helps.
I'm glad you understand. My family, that's all I have left since I was taken from Murkmire. \n\nFor what it's worth, I hope you do stop them. That would be a very good thing.

The Path of the Lily is sacred to our people. Hatchlings ascend to the rank of warrior by walking the Path, ready to defend the tribe and survive the terrors of the swamp.\n\nFailure means death and a return to the Hist. Kishi interrupted that fate.

Well, Xal-Toh means "sacred secret." Each tablet contains its own mystery.\n\nI think this one is related to the legend of Beela-Kaar. He was an ancient Argonian sorcerer. Terrorized most of Black Marsh, or so the story goes.

I attempt to speak plainly. As Mewah-Jez teaches, the swamp doesn't provide second chances, so why should we? If warriors can't succeed on their own, they endanger us all.\n\nStill, I am grateful I am alive to explain this. Kishi made that possible.

That seems unlikely. The story I heard claims that the skull was hidden on an island off the coast of Black Marsh. Margus probably has the Blackguards looking for more clues that point to the skull's exact location.\n\nBe careful in there, my friend.

Good. Ugh! I typically deal in scented lotions. These leaves … by the Three, they smell like a dead Orc's armpit. I hope you didn't rub any of this on your clothes.\n\nAnyway, thanks for replenishing my supplies. I have a few candles ready for you.
Wait! Wait, wait—you do want to test them before you leave, right? I mean, it's only fair that I prove their potency!\n\nJust light that candle over there when I give the signal. Are you ready?

Bhoki was our war-teacher until one mistake led to his disgrace. Now Mewah-Jez trains the novices. In six seasons, she has lost every clutch that walked the Path, blaming them for being too weak. \n\nIf this continues, the tribe cannot survive.

Mewah-Jez the war-teacher instructs our novices. Trains them to walk the Path of the Lily. Her methods … instead of making us strong, they lead to nothing but death.\n\nI speak true. My clutch was the last to make it through the rite unscathed.

There is. If you recover Tarcyr's heart, Hircine would grant a boon to your party. Only then would my daughter be allowed to join the souls of our ancestors.\n\nPlease, you must defeat Balorgh and take back that heart. I'll help in any way I can.

A fair question. In truth, I came to rescue Famia. I will admit a certain affection for her. She is kind-hearted and loyal—like a hedge gecko, or one of your tiny bark-dogs. I would not want her to come to harm.\n\nI am glad to see you safe as well.
Ha. No. \n\nHave a care with that crystal, beeko. If it is truly the Kajin-Jat, you should not let it jangle around in Famia's purse for long.

No, of course not! Though, some have gone worse ….\n\nAnyway, we shouldn't dwell on the missteps and bungles! Need I remind you that we recovered the Kajin-Jat Crystal? An item of immeasurable historical import!

Yes, well … I had hoped to discuss that in private. Provided this little misadventure hasn't driven you from the business completely, I'd like to bring you on for another task.\n\nLet me settle up here, then I'll meet you in my office in Lilmoth.

Oh, the most worthy kind of expedition—a journey into the distant past! Not the literal past, I mean. That would be crazy.\n\nWe're exploring one of the Argonians' ancient xanmeer pyramids to find a priceless relic: the Kajin-Jat Crystal!

You've made a great choice in joining us, friend!\n\nThe other members of our expedition have already gathered near the western gate. I'll be along shortly—just need to check on a few things. This is exciting, right?

To preserve it for future generations, of course! So much of the Argonians' unique history has been lost. With your help, we can pull this antiquity out of the mud and share it with the world!\n\nDiscovery! Adventure! What could be better?

Aside from the language not being any variation of the Dwemeri tongue that I know of, the design bears none of their cultural aesthetic. Even the stone itself isn't something I've seen used in other Dwemer artifacts.

They'll pay, will they? Well, that's a mammoth of a different color. Still, I'm not about to go making such a business transaction without Kyne's say so. \n\nI just hope you have a hearty set of lungs on you. I could use the gold.

Kyne's the Goddess of the Storm, after all. From the wind of your lungs, invoke her power to view the winds of the world.\n\nTake this rune and travel northeast. Find some nice vistas, give a hearty shout, and the rune will do the rest.

Talk to a few of the more connected rapscallions that conduct business down there. I know a few of them by reputation. Look for Grethaa, an information broker; Urzashi, an antiquities black marketeer; and Eshundir, a historic treasures smuggler.

Gloom morel grows around Daedric sites. Check Gil-Var-Delle. As for the barbleberries, they grow along coastal regions. The venom we need is easily found in the Scuttle Pit, but not so easily collected, you see.
Sort of? It's … the process can be a little complicated. Don't worry. She'll walk you through it.
Right, the poison-sniffer. Ugh … great.\n\nLook, I'd love to help, but the only one I had in stock just ran out on me. Slippery little rascal!
Here, I'll mark a likely nesting spot on your map. Drop the venom sacs there, and it won't take long for the skink to show up. Guaranteed.\n\nGood luck out there!

Would you? Thanks, friend.\n\nSkinks are always hungry. Not many poisonous plants around here, so it should be easy to lure him out. You'll need bait, of course. Assassin beetle or giant scorpion venom sacs would do the trick. Skinks love venom!
We're sending meat in bulk, remember? Easier to throw five giant slabs in a barrel than butcher up twenty cows. Plus, they taste better!
Don't go telling me any jokes that need thinking. It's not in the spirit of … the spirits. Hah!
Talk to them, of course, but I imagine that's not something you've often tried in your field of expertise.\n\nLandal Gevont, Goblin expert, at your service.
Daedric Prince? Bad luck, that. But I'm game. Go ahead!
A trade joke? Ha—this I've got to hear. Go ahead.
Yeah? So what's the healer say?
A little …? Oh! Har! That's a good one!\n\nWell, looks like we've reached the dregs, so a deal's a deal. Here's your salt. Don't be a stranger, eh?
I don't know. What is the best type of story to tell a runaway horse?
A tale of …. Ha! Say, that's not bad!\n\nWell, a deal's a deal. Here's your salt. Don't fall off your horse on the way back to Jee-Lar, eh?
A few—but they're all raunchier than an Argonian maid. Let's hear yours, eh?
I don't know. What kind of bread does a horse eat?
Oh, by Orkey, that is terrible! Har! Let me get you that salt before you tell me another! \n\nThanks for the company. Be sure to tell old Jee-Lar I said hello!

Jee-Lar, is it? Then I'll be expecting my payment from him too, I suspect.\n\nStill, Kyne believes that your intentions are true. For that, I'll give you a prediction. Let's call it a … proof of further investment.
I don't know. Why should I avoid making Molag Bal mad?
Oof. I think that one could use some work, friend! Har! I'd help, but we've run dry.\n\nBest take your salt. Do yourself a favor and stick to the adventuring, eh?
I don't know. Why is Boethia such a good writer?
I don't know. How many tickles does it take to make Hermaeus Mora laugh?
Tentacles? Oh. Har! That's good! I mean … it's bad, but you know what I mean!\n\nHere's your salt. You take care now. Tentacles … ha!
Har! Oh, that's a real stinker, friend! I love it!\n\nI guess you'll be wanting your salt now. Ah well—a deal's a deal. You take care out there, all right?
Very well. I shall scour the sky of Murkmire, and see if any such storms lie before you.
I don't know. When should I avoid a blacksmith?
Ugh! That is a groaner! Think I'll use that the next time I'm in town. Might be soon, I'm out of mead! Hah!\n\nHere's your salt. Take care out there, friend!
I don't know. Why did the fool throw his dagger away?
Har! By Orkey, that is a stinker. Good thing I love stinkers!\n\nHere's your salt. You take care out there, all right?
I don't know. Why did the Orc decide not to be a tailor?
Oof! Har! I think I've heard worse, but I'm not so sure! \n\nI won't pester you for another. I don't think I could take it! Here's your salt. Take care, friend!
Oh, sure, I can sell you some salt … when I'm done with my break. Already cracked into this cask. Can't let it go to waste.
Bah. You're no fun. Fine, here's your salt. Guess I'll go back to drinking alone.

Reckon I could finish this by tomorrow morning. You could come back then … but if you're in a hurry I suppose you could help me polish it off. Wouldn't mind the company. Gets duller than Reachman wit out here.
Great! I've got a spare mug right over there. Have a drink! Put your feet up!

Yes! Copper-tongued skinks put even the heartiest Argonian to shame. They can eat practically anything and survive.\n\nI saw one eat a whole bowl of throat-rake pears once. It just sort of fell asleep for a while, then woke up and ran off. Amazing!
Whenever I can! Who wants to haggle sober? Not me, I'll tell you that much. And it wouldn't be fair if I was the only one inebrate … inebriaded … drunk.
Great! I've got a spare mug right over there. Have a drink! Put your feet up!
Bah. You're no fun. Fine, here's your salt. Guess I'll go back to drinking alone.

He went looking for food. As usual. I feed him chokeberries by the bucket-full, but there's just no bottom! With how much I'm spending on fruit, I'll be lucky to break even on this deal.\n\nIf you do manage to catch him, be sure to keep a firm grip!

We're historic investigators. We research and seek out antiquities stolen from the Argonian homeland. When we find them, we return them to Black Marsh.\n\nWell, that's the plan. We have a few more items to collect before we make our first journey.

As soon as we recover the last of the Argonian antiquities on my list, we'll organize an expedition to that region of Black Marsh. My sister has gone on ahead to set up a base camp and smooth the way with the locals.

Margus wants the antiquities for himself. This competition has taken a violent turn. He has a brutal temper and some skill at spellcasting. Makes me fearful for my associates.\n\nAnyway, I think Margus is especially interested in pre-Duskfall relics.

Margus originally approached us as a friend and benefactor. I honestly thought he wanted to help return the lost Argonian treasures to their rightful owners. He worked with us for a time, but it wasn't long before he revealed his true colors.

No, not specifically. But even a hammer can be used for good or ill.\n\nMargus seeks one of the pre-Duskfall relics, I'm sure of it! I just need to figure out which one before something terrible occurs. With your help, we can avert a disaster.

My sister Famia became fascinated with Argonian history during her time at the university. When she returned home, her stories intrigued me and I became interested in the topic as well.\n\nI can't wait to join her in Murkmire!

We plan to return most items to their rightful owners. We chose Murkmire since our research suggests the majority of the items on our list originate there.\n\nFinding the rightful owners may require additional expeditions in the area, though.
That is a load off my mind, beek-ojel. It is good to know that at least one thing is going right amid all the misfortunes looming.

These past weeks the Hist has been agitated. It has given me signs that I believed were warnings for the bonding to come, but now I feel that I've misinterpreted.\n\nIt is this clutch that is in peril … and it is you who can save it.
I can only repeat what Mistress Dobar told me. I am no alchemist. But still, feel free to ask. What more would you like to know?

Ah, I know Margus well! We both deal in antiquities. He actually approached me recently. As a consultant, you understand. So I'm familiar with Margus's current plans.\n\nI am happy to share that information—in exchange for a simple favor.
Oh dear! Where are my manners? I apologize.\n\nMy name is Famia Mercius … or Famia "Speaks-With-Round-Tongue" to the locals. I'm Cyrodilic Collections' chief antiquarian here in Murkmire.

Certainly the most important ones. We do need to raise enough gold to finance our operations, though. We'll hold on to a few items to eventually open a museum in Black Marsh—a place where these cultural treasures can be enjoyed by everyone.
Be sure to tell Jee-Lar, all right? If I know Black Marsh, he'll definitely need more before long. Farewell!

What an exquisite specimen! Well done, my friend, well done!\n\nAs for the information you required, know that Margus has involved himself with a band of thugs and outlaws. They hide in a dark cave like poisonous mushrooms.

I can tell you that the cave is called the Sunless Hollow, and it's located not too far from here.\n\nI have one more bit of advice. Margus and his associates are dangerous. Should you find them, I suggest caution. And that concludes our business.

The cave is called the Sunless Hollow. It's not too far from here, but I don't know the exact location.\n\nI do have one more secret to share. Margus and his associates are dangerous. Should you find them, I suggest caution. Our business is done now.

Such aggression! There is no need to threaten violence, my friend. Eshundir said he would take care of you, and indeed he will.\n\nMargus has associated himself with a band of thugs and outlaws. They hide in a dark cave like poisonous mushrooms.
I know Tharayya would hate to hear me say this, but hopefully nothing. I would much prefer an empty room over unleashing some ancient evil that even the Dwarves feared.

I was enticed by the possibility of observing a Riekling tribe from the inside, and not just any Riekling tribe, but one that has settled on a Dwarven site. I could have observed—firsthand—Goblins making discoveries of an advanced civilization.
The empty nest? Those eggs were returned to the Hist! Were the eggs poisoned, or was the poisoner's intent to harm the Hist?\n\nThis is terrible!

Not at the cost of something new! \n\nI'm all for learning about the past, but this obsession to be the first to discover the secrets of a long dead civilization twists people into desperate fools and monsters. I won't be party to it again.
As Alareth pointed out, the door to Mhuvnak's vault is sealed shut. We're going to have to force it open, and this giant contraption looks like the only thing up to the job. If I can get it working.

I think our Goblin squatters helped themselves to some of the construct's parts. We'll either need to get them back, or find suitable substitutes.\n\nFollow my skeevaton through the door Ranja's unlocked. If we're lucky it'll sniff out what we need.

Metallic channels that direct the flow of magicka between different parts of a Dwemer construct. Practically every Dwemer construct has them, but for what I'm planning only the highest grade will be up to the task.

A skeevaton. Part of the intricate workings of the Clockwork City. Interesting mix of form and function. There's no reason they need to be a facsimile of a skeever to serve their purpose, but nearly everything in that realm imitates life.
She does her work at Vineshade Lodge, north of Haven. You will know she is there by the smell. It's awful-awful!

This one wishes it weren't, but that is definitely Argar's blade. Such are the risks when dealing with the criminal element. \n\nWell, no use crying over spilled moon-sugar. You provided a service. Now remind me what you wanted to know.

This one hears rumors. Margus Derius searches for Argonian relics of considerable power. Something from the time of the great Argonian civilization, as I understand it.\n\nMargus has a hidden storehouse for these relics, but that's all this one knows.

Perfect! Did you know this jacket belonged to an associate of Margus Derius? There should be a note in the pocket. Ah, here it is.\n\nAnd this confirms the information I promised to share with you. Margus works with a group called the Blackguards.

Just one of the most dangerous bands of outlaws to emerge from the swamps of Black Marsh! The group supposedly started years ago in Blackrose Prison.\n\nI'm not sure why Margus and the Blackguards are working together, but nothing good will come of it.
Ugh, that woman. All the tenders treat these eggs like their own clutches, but for someone who's never bonded she's the most doting mother I've ever met.
Are you kidding? I think it's the only thing that keeps her going. She's mopey for about a month and then she's back to being the most caring person you've ever seen.

In this place, even the keenest eyes see little but embers of the truth, Rootmender. Here, we see with our souls. But these are questions for a dozing time. This moment demands action.\n\nYou seek the seed, correct?

What you call it matters little.\n\nThe seed, this Remnant, waits in a dark and quiet place, and our souls hide within it. It calls for a protector, a guide, and a mender that might lift it high and release its spirits in the bright-yellow sun.

I offer you my staff—a branch of great power. It will guide you to us.\n\nMany brambles and snares remain, Rootmender. Betrayal, battle, and sacrifice. But the Hist knows your heart and your strength. In time, you shall find what you seek.

Ash basil's usefulness as a repellent is well-known, but Tamira discovered a way to enhance those properties. So she tells me, anyway.\n\nEven the bugs of Murkmire will recoil from its stench! I hope.

Dreugh that consume ash basil seem to take on unusual properties. Namely, the secretion and buildup of a superior wax. A fortuitous coincidence on our part.\n\nThis wax creates hardy candles, able to withstand the damp conditions of Murkmire.

My conversation with her was brief, but I hear all kinds of stories. Apparently, she likes to play jokes on her customers. This seems like a very strange way to do business, but her products should be worth the aggravation.\n\nWe will see, I guess.

All the more reason to keep on the path before us. She may have bested the attacker we found, but perhaps there were others? The only thing certain is that she will not be safe until the Veeskhleel are dealt with.

I may be new to the Argonian antiquities trade, but Margus and his cronies know me all too well. They'd turn me away or stick a dagger in my back before the door closes behind me!\n\nI need someone without any ties to Cyrodilic Collections for this.

I have other agents that need to be supervised and coordinated. Margus has already beaten us to a few choice antiquities. I need to make sure that trend doesn't continue.\n\nI also have a few leads of my own to follow up on. I'll see you back here.

You want to know about Margus? Interesting. Very well. Perform a service and this one will tell you what you want to know.\n\nLocate my assistant and bring him back, or at least tell me if it is time to hire a new one. Good help is so hard to find.

Hist roots stretch very far, beeko. Deep down into the heart of xal-Nirn and out into distant lands.\n\nI cannot say what tribe serves this Hist, but the message is clear. The deep sap is here so we can take it. For your dream-wallow.

With the Hist, some things are certain. I could try to explain it, but this is like trying to explain how to breathe underwater to someone who is not a fish.\n\nI mean no offense. As not-fish go, you are one of the best.
Yes. Many things feel uncertain, but your role pounds like a drum in my mind. The deep sap is for you. The dream-wallow is for you.

The flowers? Flowers do not speak. Do not be weird. The Hist speaks.\n\nIn Dead-Water land, we burn starblossoms. Their smoke leads us to the dream-wallow. They are rare as snow in summer, yet here they are. Tell me, did Xukas find something, too?

Ah, I thank the Hist that Kishi lives, but he risks everything to swim against the currents of our traditions. \n\nI must find the same courage as my egg-son and do what is right. Otherwise, the tribe will slowly fade away.

I know it is what the Hist demands. As for what it will do to you? That is a question for a tree-minder or a naheesh dream-talker. I am neither.\n\nThis wallow leads to the Remnant—I am certain. We have the ingredients. You must provide the bravery.

I nod my head. Then our course is clear. The Dead-Water way and the Bright-Throat way will join, like blood and water. A dream-wallow unlike any we have seen before.\n\nXukas and I will guide you down this third path.

The Naga-Kur, who you call the Dead-Water. We are warriors. Death is a part of who we are. In the past, our hatchlings grew to be novices who walked the Path and became warriors. Death was present, but it never claimed all our young. Until now.

One war-teacher was replaced by another. Techniques were altered. Different virtues were emphasized.\n\nUnder Mewah-Jez's tutelage, novices fail the test over and over. She pushes them in one direction and blames them as the tribe slowly dies out.

The grove is north of Alten Meerhleel—tucked away near a roaring waterfall, if memory serves.\n\nI will make my personal ferry available to all here assembled. Join us. Or walk, if you prefer. I'd only ask that you avoid any unnecessary delays.

Long years of bitter disappointment have trained me to measure my expectations. We will find something in the grove, I am certain of it. But this dream-wallow business ….\n\nThe Hist will not make this easy. Not for you, and certainly not for me.

Oh, certainly! Xukas enjoys friendly relationships with practically everyone—even the Nagas. \n\nSome of Lilmoth's investors see him as a bit of a swindler, but that's rooted in their ignorance of Argonian culture more than anything else.

The Khajiiti sea captain, eh? Ha! Everyone wants to work with Jimila! \n\nI met her a few months ago. I needed a reliable ship to carry Alik'ri trade goods. No small thing, what with the war and all. Jimila made me an offer I couldn't refuse.

Impress her? No, that wasn't how I got close to the sea captain. No, I showed her courtesy and respect. I deferred to her expertise and let her suggest the best way we could work together.\n\nThat's how I caught Jimila's eye!

Nesh-Deeka, the instrument crafter? Interesting.\n\nSure, I know the Captain. She hires me to escort her around the marsh sometimes. Matter of fact, I provided protection when she was last in port. I heard she's back, but I haven't spoken to her.
