Often enough to put a few meals on the table.\n\nThe Captain can handle herself, but she recognizes the value of local talent. Hiring a sellsword like me provides her with someone who speaks the language and knows the native customs.

What is this really about, outsider? Are you trying to intrude upon my business? I assure you, Captain Jimila knows a rogue and a cheat when she sees one. That's why we have such an ironclad agreement.

Ah, Nesh-Deeka must have employed you as an envoy. Very clever!\n\nKnow that Captain Jimila is a shrewd negotiator but a fair partner. Speak true and bargain in good faith. That will earn you the respect of the master of the Prowler.

Well, then, we should have little trouble. I am all those things and more when it comes to business!\n\nWe just need to complete a vossa-satl so we can present it to the good Captain. That is sure to convince her to deal with us!

You can gather the frogs while I put the finishing touches on the instrument!\n\nWe'll need moss-foot croakers, ruby hoppers, indigo tree frogs, and sun-blessed toads. Here. I wrote everything down so you won't have to remember all the details.

What a strange question. We need the frogs for the vossa-satl. How else would the instrument produce its sweet-sounding melodies?\n\nThe note explains how to catch each frog. Once you have them all, return to my shop and we'll finish the instrument.

So they are! How good of you to join us, little croakers!\n\nLet's go inside, beeko. Our happy chorus must be fitted into the vossa-satl. I envy them their new lives of pampered luxury. We should all be so lucky!

Of course! I always keep an ear hole open for important information such as that!\n\nLast I heard, Captain Jimila was drinking at the tavern. Go to her, present yourself as my envoy, give her the vossa-satl, and get her to agree to export them.

Only the scent of conspiracy. But for now, the scent is enough.\n\nThe Dragonstar Caravan Company—a dishonest flock of thugs and traders—funnels information to someone outside Lilmoth. Notes on Cyrodilic Collections' business dealings, I think.

Not yet. But that is soon to change.\n\nThe Orc, Lozwug, who watches my egg-kin play teeba-enoo—he serves the Dragonstar Caravan Company. A courier, I think. He carries a letter filled with his trade-kin's secrets. With your help, I will take it.

I do not need to convince you? That is good, if a little disconcerting.\n\nLozwug shows loud, obnoxious interest in our game, teeba-enoo. Ask him to explain the rules. While he growls and rants, I will take the letter from his pocket. Simple, I think.

I have got no tusking idea and neither do these lizards!\n\nWhen I got here, they were all just lying there. Then, all of a sudden, half of them stood up and start slapping their tails—croaking like mad and kicking balls around!

They started singing! Then one of them shouted "enoo," and everyone flopped over like they were dead. They laid there for fifteen minutes, then the game was over. I guess.\n\nTusking nonsense! If that's a sport, I'm a hearth-wife's dustpan!

I don't know—half-dozen, maybe?\n\nThey were bouncing them off that rock, but then the other team started hooting and slapping their chests like monkeys! They rushed the hill, formed a circle around the rock, and started standing on their heads.
It is not just notes on business dealings. It is a description … of friend-Famia. Where she walks, who she speaks with, what she eats, and so on.\n\nI had no idea she ate so many snails.
On Famia and her explorer-kin also, I think. We cannot be sure, though. Simple Lozwug carried only this letter.\n\nI know a place where more information can be found, but you will have to go alone.

The Dragonstar depot in Lilmoth. I leased them the land. They were very pleased … until it sunk. Now they slop around in there like angry mud-moles. No one is welcome. Least of all me.\n\nIf you sneak into the depot, you may find more clues.

Antiquities, you say? Let me have a look. Hmm. This one is not the expert that Eshundir is. Was. But this tablet tells the secret of an Argonian nightmare idol. Very rare. Probably dangerous.\n\nWhy did you make me touch these things? Take them back!

That is good. Taking a life closes more doors than it opens—a valuable lesson that goes largely unheeded by the Lilmoth ojel and my Naga cousins. \n\nBut again, my tongue wanders. We should discuss Famia's lost friends. What did you find?

I see. That is unfortunate, but your honesty is sun on my scales. I will prepare the usual denials and peace offerings. The Dragonstar's anger may cool in time. And if not, the tides will sweep them away eventually.\n\nNow. Famia's missing friends.

The Blackguards? Kaoc. They are a cruel bunch. Mostly tribeless Nagas and dryskin ojels.\n\nSo, the Dragonstar Caravan Company provides spy reports to the Blackguards, then the Blackguards snatch up the explorers when they stray outside the city walls.

My doubt-spine quivers, but there is only one way to find out.\n\nI will send word to my Dead-Water friend, Jaxsik-Orrn. You should return to Famia. Tell her what we discovered and encourage her to stay indoors. She will be safer there, I think.

A murder in the heart of Lilmoth? Yes, that would be Jaxsik-Orrn, I think. A kaal—or war-captain—of the Dead-Water tribe. Perhaps she came looking for that weapon you recovered.\n\nJaxsik and I are good friends. She would never admit it though.

Blackguards? Ooh, those ill-mannered brutes are the worst kind of trouble!\n\nI have more unwelcome news. Our companions, Zadaza and Kirstaleth, have also gone missing! Zadaza went to conduct her own investigation. Kirstaleth decided to tag along.

Really? I can't imagine that they'd be enthusiastic about helping us, but I suppose Xukas would know best.\n\nBefore you go, would you mind sharing what you've learned with someone else? Cyrodilic Collections' primary benefactor is just upstairs.

Goodness, I never even mentioned her before did I? Her name is Kassandra—a wealthy antiquarian of great renown! She's been an invaluable partner. Just like you! If you'll just follow me upstairs, I'll—\n\nOh, wait. Here she is now!

As much as Margus desires Argonian antiquities, he doesn't really know that much about them. He's going to need help making sense of whatever he found inside the idol. For that, he'll turn to the most knowledgeable Argonians he can find.

I just read about this in The Legends of Black Marsh. The skull is a fabled relic said to contain the power of the Argonian sorcerer, Beela-Kaar. According to the book, the skull vibrates with arcane energy and carries a terrible curse.

Cyrodilic Collections was started by my sister Famia and I. The goal of our society is to find and recover Argonian antiquities that were removed from Black Marsh and return them to the Argonian people.

Margus Derius was a member of our society who betrayed our trust. He stole our research and used it to beat us to some choice relics. His true goal appears to be the Golden Skull of Beela-Kaar. With the help of the Blackguards, he might just find it.

Cyrodilic Collections wants to find the skull so we can return it to Black Marsh. Perhaps to make it the centerpiece of our proposed museum.\n\nMargus … I'm beginning to think he wants to utilize its power in some kind of arcane ritual.

Well, it is a cursed skull, and Beela-Kaar practiced the dark arts, so not a particularly good ritual, I imagine. The legend says the curse spells the doom of Murkmire.\n\nI don't think we can afford to take any chances with this.

There have always been dark legends surrounding the Tsofeer Caverns, stories about a monster called the Wuju-Ka.\n\nIt is some sort of powerful voriplasm, a massive pool of malignant slime that was said to periodically emerge and cause untold damage.
Kassandra. Yes. You and Famia would have to speak to her, I guess.\n\nI am glad she sees the wisdom in talking to the Dead-Water tribe. Kassandra has many flaws, but stupidity is not among them.

You need me to describe them? She wears her flaws like I wear my feathers.\n\nKassandra is vexu-vit. You would say persnickety, I think? Well, you would probably not say that. That is a very stupid word. But you take my meaning. She is very particular.

Yes. She said she was hunting a Blackguard even now, right? Did you see how her throat fins spread? How her pupils dilated and her tail stiffened as she turned to leave?\n\nHer prey is very, very close. We only need to follow her.
We hunt the hunter.\n\nScan the swamp for the bent reeds and broken fronds she leaves in her wake. The trail should eventually lead us to friend-Jaxsik and the Blackguard she hunts. Simple, I think!

Many seasons ago, when the Imperials first sent troops to our beloved swamps, the Ninth Legion terrorized the region. It marched from one end of Murkmire to the other, inflicting death and destruction along the way.\n\nThen they simply vanished.

Gin-Rajul was a renowned scout, well-respected before the Imperials convinced him to help them. I'm certain they must have forced him. Threatened him in some way. No spawn of our eggs could have been a traitor!\n\nAnd with your help, I'll prove it.

The ojel stands its ground? Brave. Or stupid.\n\nA flock of flat-toothed Blackguards took refuge in this ravine. They snatched up some of my egg-kin—your allies too—and threw them in cages. Now, Tsojei and I will hack these greels to pieces.

I narrow my eyes. You and the Bright-Throat wish to join me on this raid, rather than pick the bones when the work is done? Fine.\n\nBurn the wagons. Smash their supplies. Kill any that oppose you. When all lies in ashes, we will speak again.

I roll my eyes. Murder? When you gut a fish, is it murder? No. You only object because this fish walks upright and has a face.\n\nThe ojel is an animal—a foolish one. The Dead-Water tribe does not suffer animals like this to live.

Ha. How quickly Jaxsik forgets she is a kidnapper herself.\n\nThe Blackguards do not know the Dead-Water tribe as I do. Let this dryskin tell her tale. By sparing one, we terrify one hundred. An ancient tactic, beeko, but very effective.

How in Oblivion should I know? Orders came down to watch the captives. I didn't ask why. Maybe I should have, but I've got a daughter at home. If I don't follow orders, she doesn't eat.\n\nI had nothing to do with the abductions! I'm telling the truth!

Mara's mercy, you'd let that Naga murder a prisoner? Just let me think!\n\nAll right, there was an interrogator who grilled a few of the captives. Something about a Remnant? Yes, the Remnant of Argon. He was asking everyone about it—even the Nagas.

Yeah—some Argonian relic maybe? I really have no idea what the Remnant is! Word is there's someone with a heavy purse willing to pay out a fortune for any information, but that's all I know!\n\nPlease, don't make my daughter an orphan!

I cannot be sure. But that is no bad thing. Nothing leads to more death than the need for certainty.\n\nYou cut down many Blackguards and laid waste to their operation. Let this dryskin describe it to her friends. Then they will know fear.

I am not.\n\nYou showed cunning in tracking me and strength during the raid. To see you falter now, in the face of some blubbering, treacherous dryskin would turn my stomach. It says it has a daughter? It has killed many daughters. Now that ends.

Something I cannot discuss. For now.\n\nReturn to Famia and tell her this. She is a friend to the Saxhleel, but the Remnant is not some stone cup or golden idol. It is something much greater. And more dangerous.

I bare my fangs. It is a secret of the Hist. The killing kind.\n\nYou showed your Naga-heart today, so I will give you this one warning: the Remnant is not for you. Go tell your pale master, Famia, to let this go.
We have a deep and abiding respect for the Argonian culture. Well, more of a fascination, really.\n\nPlus, every success builds our reputation. That's the key.

To fame and fortune! Success garners attention, and attention attracts benefactors. That means more gold to use to equip expeditions and purchase antiquities from collectors.\n\nAnd eventually, it means we'll have enough gold to open our museum!

The Blackguards are a deadly gang of thugs from Black Marsh. The gang consists mostly of Argonians and is rumored to have been formed by escapees from Blackrose Prison.\n\nThey're crude, hateful, and have no regard for the sanctity of history!

His favorite egg-son escaped the rightful punishment bestowed upon him by the war-chief. Whether Bhoki aided in his escape or not, this entire situation reeks of the old Naga's influence.\n\nNow we will use him to lure Kishi back here.

So the Dead-Water tribe helped you after all? What a fascinating development. Between your heroism and Jaxsik-Orrn's raw strength, I'm sure you showed those brutes what for!\n\nI hesitate to ask, but what did the Blackguards learn about the Remnant?

Well then, there's not a moment to lose! We will redouble our efforts! We cannot allow those thugs to claim something as valuable as the Remnant.\n\nBut I'm getting ahead of myself. We should probably discuss this matter with Kassandra.

Unfortunate. I can tell you, as an expert of Argonian archeology, the idea of one of those ignorant thugs handling such a valuable antiquity makes me very uncomfortable.\n\nDid they mention why they seek this thing?

I have some experience with wealth. Jangling gold in front of a pack of cutthroats is an act of crude desperation. This person is either a fool or a victim of some obsession.\n\nIn either case, we cannot let this Remnant fall into their hands.

Then I'll tell you what I told their leader. The woodcut they found inside the nightmare idol describes a ritual, but all I could decipher was the sacred location where it must be performed. Norg-Tzel. In ancient Argonian, it means "forbidden place."

I recoil at your ignorance, outsider! You know nothing of our traditions. Of our sacred rites. You are barely better than the insects that flitter around the waste pits.\n\nDo not get involved or you will suffer the same fate that awaits Kishi.

I've found references to Dwemer excavation machines in translated texts, but this is the first I've seen in person. \n\nJudging by this, it's no mystery how the Dwemer were able to create such massive underground complexes all over Tamriel.
I suppose you do, don't you? Well, I suppose I can't deny a potential customer their curiosity. What do you want to know?

Once someone knows you can predict the weather, that's all they ever ask about. "Will it be windy out? Should I wear a jacket? Should I travel tomorrow, or the next day?"\n\nI grew sick of it. Out here, I can worship the goddess in peace.

I've always had this power, truth be told. Ever since I could remember, I saw patterns in the wind. Shifting movements.\n\nEventually, I realized that my power stemmed from Kyne's wisdom. That's when I vowed to serve the goddess.

Let's be clear. I can predict the weather right here and now. I just choose not to until Kyne has agreed to our deal.\n\nThough, between you and me, I do hope she agrees. Becoming a hermit hasn't exactly done wonders for my coin purse.

Kyne needs to be called upon if she's to give her blessing. A hearty shout is usually good enough to get her attention, under the right circumstances.\n\nThe rune will absorb the power of her presence. That way, I'll know you were successful.

Mewah-Jez is a pox upon our tribe! I need to find a way to convince the war-chief that Bhoki's training techniques are not only sound but represent the best way to save the Dead-Water.\n\nTo accomplish this I'll need your help, if you're willing.

And a daring plan it is! I will mentor you, use Bhoki's techniques to guide you through the Path of the Lily. When an outsider succeeds where Dead-Water novices failed, it will prove that Mewah-Jez is wrong.\n\nCan I count on you, outsider?

Help me show the war-chief that the old ways truly are the best. Specifically, the methods Bhoki once used to train our novices.\n\nI'm proof that Bhoki's techniques of using wits and strategy are more effective than simply relying on brute strength.

That corresponds with what I was able to determine. And I'm sure it's somehow related to legends of Beela-Kaar.\n\nBut what happened to you and Jee-Lar after you left the Outlaws Refuge? Were you able to track down Margus?

It's an Argonian religious practice. Sort of. I've never witnessed one myself, but they typically involve a period of isolation and exposure to potent mind-altering herbs.\n\nAccording to the text, a dream-wallower can see things beyond the physical.

I shake my head in disbelief. Why is it that everything connected to Bhoki and his egg-son reeks of broken laws and forsakened traditions?\n\nDo you truly believe you can succeed where the best of our young warriors have failed?

It will prove something. On that, we agree.\n\nVery well. Walk the Path. Kishi will accompany you as your mentor. Return with the sacred lily and I will listen to Kishi's plea. If you fail and die, Bhoki will be executed and our traditions will stand.
You want to go to where? You know that island is forbidden, right? Oh, this will be the end of us! Your weapons make a persuasive point though. Just know that the place is full of Blackguards!

After I pilot the ship back to Shadowfen, I think I'll set sail for a place as far from Murkmire and the Blackguards as I can manage.\n\nI wonder what lies beyond the edge of the map, west of Summerset?
Of course. You're the last ingredient. Mix it up a minute in your bubbler, then heave it into my bubbler. I'll handle the rest.
Sure, sure. Once you rinse your mouth out, your teeth will never feel cleaner. Your breath'll still kill an ox at ten paces, but only for a day or so.

All part of the process. Adding your juices to the mix helps the reagents dissolve into a solution. Been trying to recreate the effect in a flask, but it just curdles and ruins the whole batch.\n\nSometimes traditional methods are best.

Oh, sure. I almost enjoy it at this point, but more than once a day would give you an ulcer. Not the best idea to be chugging venom with a hole in your gut.\n\nAlways in need of a spare stomach if you're up to it tomorrow.

No, it won't work.\n\nDid you see how the gate glowed yellow as she walked through it? And how these stones lit up as she passed? Somehow, I think this gate only responds to Argonian vakka stones—stones like the Kajin-Jat Crystal.

I have been with Concordia and her sister from the beginning! I left my home in Murkmire to help recover the stolen past of my people. And to participate in adventures. All very exciting!\n\nHead back to Concordia and I'll meet you there.

Duskfall refers to the slow decline of the great Saxhleel civilization. Ages ago, the Argonians built pyramids called xanmeers and were much more advanced. Most of our research deals with the more dangerous relics of that period.

One of the local tribes uses the candles to cleanse a place of evil influences, especially where unburied bodies are concerned. If there are any Imperial remains in the cavern, I figured why not use the candles to help settle their restless spirits?

Tools to slake the thirst of the great serpent. Their heyday has long passed, but some faithful still carry on the tradition of giving offerings with the point of a knife.\n\nMost would disapprove of their use by common thugs and heretics.

You'll know by the lives they sent into the great serpent's maw. The lingering remnants of countless souls still clinging desperately to this world. They give a thing weight.\n\nYou seek a stone fang, a coiled staff, and a bone chalice.
Nothing good. This place reeks of death and foulness. Saxhleel have a strong constitution, but the air here makes me ill.
Ulp. The smell of unclean alchemy! No egg could have survived soaking in such a vile bath.
It is so bright. You'd think it glowed. It reminds me of the poisons Black-Tongues make from the colorful tree frogs. It is surely as deadly. Maybe more so.

The first part of the Path involves the trial of movement. You must find a way to get past one of the largest, deepest pools of quicksand in all of Murkmire.\n\nRemember the vine-tongues? The plants are the key to navigating this hazard.

Bhoki accompanied his novices, so I will accompany you. I cannot interfere in your trials, only offer advice. But you can use me as a tool, directing me to provide minor aid at times.\n\nFor example, my arrows can be used to attract the vine-tongues.

The makings of a grisly display. Do not trouble yourself with concerns of desecration. When we return to the Hist, the flesh remains as a gift to Sithis. Its purpose fulfilled, it returns to the swamp to form something new.

That Sithis is not only destruction. Sithis is change. Sithis tears down the old so that the new can grow. So we learned to flow with the river, instead of struggle to alter its course.\n\nThese are better times, but Shuxaltsei cannot see that.

The old ways sought to appease Sithis, so it might spare us from destruction. In our ignorance, we struggled against its will like the muck we built upon until we neared collapse.\n\nIt would have swallowed us if the Hist hadn't shared their wisdom.

Most remains are long since cast into the muck, but those not yet stripped of their flesh might not have been removed before the elder ways fell. Left to molder where they lay in their preparation chambers, some may remain undisturbed.
She doesn't even care that she's hurting them. She's using them. Twisting them.\n\nShe's a monster! She's made my babies monsters!
I'm ready. I don't care what it takes. I won't let her hurt my children anymore.

Like Zadaza said, they must have fallen into different chambers. I'm sure we'll find them deeper inside the xanmeer.\n\nHonestly, I've seen this sort of thing many times before—the fall-away floors and chutes and such. Very common.

Well every great explorer has triggered a trap or two. At least no one was set on fire! Well … I mean, I hope no one was set on fire. No, no, no, I'm certain Kirstaleth and Varo are just fine.\n\nNow, we have a priceless crystal to find, right?

Of course! I keep them in a special pouch.\n\nI used to keep them in my pocket, you see, but they wore a hole through it. Wound up lost in the carpet. Turned it into a spike trap! Eventually, I just had to get a new carpet. Now, where is that pouch?
Apparently so. I guess it slipped off my belt during the fall. This may surprise you, but I've never been very good at tying knots.\n\nHave a look around. It must be here somewhere!
Nothing's wrong with her! She's just a child, that's all. She needs someone to care for her. She needs her mother.
I know she looks grown up, but that was Ree-Nakal's doing! She made her grow, but she never cared for her. She never raised her. That's why she's like this. I can fix that.

Concordia has a camp in Shadowfen, outside Stormhold. She went to check on things and do a little more research on the items you recovered.\n\nAs for us, we need to figure out how to find Margus, fast-fast!

Not the sorcerer, but the relic he left behind. The legend claims that Beela-Kaar used his considerable arcane energy to imbue his skull with a powerful curse when he died. The process turned the skull into solid gold!

Hmm. What an excellent specimen! But see this opening on the back of the statue? A cavity, but whatever was stored inside it is missing.\n\nIt looks like Margus Derius continues to remain one step ahead of us, curse his arrogant eyes!

Deroh-Zah guards the sacred lily. He is powerful and hard to kill, but he isn't invincible.\n\nHere. Take this sack of fire stones. Use them and your wits, and I'm sure you'll survive. You can do this. I have faith in you.

Deroh-Zah is an Argonian behemoth, created by our Hist to protect the sacred lily and test the mettle of our novice warriors.\n\nKnow that the creature has tasted the blood of many novices. He will not fall easily, I am sorry to say.
And you should show them to Concordia, fast-fast! She's been waiting for you to return and wants to hear all about what you found in the Sunless Hollow.
Mud in your ears? I do for Kassandra what you do for Famia—except I'm better at it.
Someone like me? Huh. Funny. You're funny.\n\nTruth is she came looking for me. Kassandra's got an eye for talent. She wants results. I deliver.
I do not trust outsiders, but I respect strength. Kishi taught you well and you have succeeded where so many of our novices have recently failed.\n\nI raise my spines in grudging admiration.

Mewah-Jez trained the novices, just as I asked her to. Any failure on her part is also a failure on mine. I shall ask her to assist Kishi and learn from him. Hopefully, their partnership will make us stronger.\n\nNow go and tell Kishi what I have said.

I should never have accepted Bhoki's resignation. That was a mistake that has cost the Naga-Kur dearly.\n\nKishi shall be our war-teacher. If he could train an outsider to walk the Path, think how our novices will fare!

I am honored and thankful that my plan worked. Now I need to rebuild confidence in the young ones. Get the next season of hatchlings ready to walk the Path.\n\nThe Dead-Water will always face adversity. I want to give them the tools to survive.

Haxara betrayed us in ways beyond my imagining. Iskenaaz is right to be wary, but when I look upon her and her daughter I feel only pity.\n\nYou know the truth of this tragedy better that I ever could. It should be you that decides Haxara's fate.

I can sense its relief, the calm of knowing that its children no longer suffer. What that means for Haxara's daughter is unclear.\n\nOur Hist does not answer me about Haxara. I feel its faith in us, so I put my trust in you.
Then I will hear you, as I hear our chimes. What is our stream's course?
Then I will lean on your strength and do what no Tree-Minder ever wishes to do. Haxara will be cut off from Tree and tribe.\n\nI hope she can find the peace she seeks in the wider world.

I feared I was being sentimental, but I am relieved to hear you offer them compassion.\n\nThe Bright-Throats have always navigated treacherous waters by linking arms and unifying our strength. Today shall be no different.
From what the Argonians told you, Margus wants to perform a ritual that will allow him to acquire the skull, gain its power, and unleash its curse.

According to the legends, the mad Argonian sorcerer was betrayed by his own people. So with his dying breath he imbued his skull with a deadly curse. If that power is ever unleashed, it will destroy all of Murkmire.\n\nThat would be a bad thing.

It is. I spent the greater part of my youth in Cyrodiil. Taking on Imperial dress, name, and customs made things easier. Of course it makes things here in Murkmire more complicated.\n\nOne of my life's many ironies.

He's a terrible person, but I don't know his true motivations. Maybe he thinks he can channel the power for his own purposes. Or maybe he secretly hates the Argonians for some real or imagined wrong.\n\nWhatever his reasons, we have to stop him.
It is, in fact. You have a very keen eye.\n\nYou should know that the crystal was a tremendous discovery. Vakka stones like this one are very difficult to come by.

An item of tremendous historical significance … and arcane power.\n\nVery little scholarship exists on the subject, but I do know a little. Argonian elders often refer to it as a sacred-egg, or xal-thtithil. Eggs always contain something, right?

I wish I knew! He's just the worst, right? She hired him maybe six months ago? I don't think Kassandra's ever received a credible threat to her life. But he's always there, leering at us.\n\nMaybe she'll sack him now that you're here. Fingers crossed!

Kassandra summoned me. Honestly, it's nice to get out of the office from time to time. Thought I might take in a teeba-enoo match while I'm here.\n\nI guess it will have to wait. I need to get back to Lilmoth to research this poem of yours!

Oh, they're mostly fine, if a little shaken up. A few of them have sworn off exploring for good. Hard to blame them, I guess.\n\nLuckily, Zadaza chose to stay on. She would never let her career end with an abduction. Far too proud for that!

I am sorry to hear that. In the end, I think it was pain that fed her madness. Maybe her spirit will find its way back to the Hist. I hope she finds peace.\n\nBut wait—you said friend-Famia is fine, for now? What does that mean?

Famia holds the Remnant of Argon? She should not bear its weight for long. Even with the Hist's guidance and blessing, dry-folk are not suited for carrying things like that.\n\nI will go to meet her soon. You should seek out Jaxsik-Orrn.

That's unfortunate, but the Argonians warned us that the ritual was dangerous. At least Cyrodilic Collections won't have to worry about Margus Derius any more.\n\nBut you stopped the ritual? Margus wasn't able to release the curse on Murkmire, right?

Well, I think we'd know if Beela-Kaar's curse had been unleashed. At the very least, my sister Famia would have sent word. I'm sure she'd notice if Murkmire was destroyed around her.\n\nDid you get to see the skull? Is it really made of solid gold?
Yes. I still feel the sting of starblossom smoke in my nostrils. The Hist needs …. Whatever the Hist needs, Tsojei and I will deliver it.\n\nWhere is Famia?
I nod my head. A fitting place. Good.\n\nI will meet you at the tree.
We have suitors from the Black-Tongues, the Root-House people and the Moss-Skin tribe.\n\nWhich tribe do you wish to know better?

A tribe that masters the lethality of Murkmire's plants. To make your soul burn or to taste a dream—the Black-Tongues can brew any such thing with ease.\n\nMany shun them. But the Bright-Throats know the value in friendship with such tribes.

I will tell you to grasp firmly anything you care that you cherish. It is the Root-House way to take from others when they can, need or not.\n\nThere are no sharper eyes in Murkmire, no defter hands. Many great hunters are born to the Root-House people
Very well. What can we talk about?

Many outsiders struggle with the swamp. Even some tribes find adversity in its pockets. Not the Moss-Skins. They live as the swamp lets them, and change nothing. Some say this is pacifism. But it is more than such. \n\nNo word I know captures it.
The Remnant … it is not a thing known, but a thing felt. Like rain on the shoulders or a brief whiff of cinnamon grass. Difficult to explain to outsiders, I think.

My knowing-tree is barren. Sorry, beeko.\n\nBetter to learn these things together, anyway. For you, at least. Just think—If I knew where the Remnant was, I would probably have hidden it by now. Then you would never get to see it!
Is the name not clear? It is a glade. It is full of chimes.

Listen, beeko, and you might learn for yourself. You are Saxhleel—the Hist might speak to you also.\n\nIn Bright-Throat Village, we learn the Hist's will through the chime music. Better than licking toads or mud-dancing like other tribes, I think.

Hmm. Some people think that the Hist speaks to us, just as I speak to you. Using words, you see. We call this kuhupwo—the mouth-talk. Very rare, beeko.\n\nMost Hist speak without words. In Bright-Throat Village, the Hist speaks through chime music.

Not as many as you would expect. Most Argonians from Murkmire are more interested in the here and now. They believe that the past is dead and gone and best forgotten.\n\nMe? Oh, the past has always fascinated me. That's why I joined up with Concordia!

Oh, no, he is a bearer of Ruxol the Infirm. Ruxol is a frequent visitor and suitor. Beloved sire to many a Black-Tongue and Bright-Throat since before my egg-mother was in her shell. Normally he would be first in line for the bonding.

It's the future of our tribe! The bonds we create today ensure the peace and prosperity of future generations by tying our tribes together as one. The bonding ritual ensures every generation of Bright-Throats calls their neighbors egg-kin.

Marrying? It is a joyous time, yes. Usually. \n\nMost tribes have festivities surrounding bondings, but none compare to that of the Bright-Throats. Travelers come from far and wide to join the celebration and witness the joining of so many tribes.

Trapped? No. Preserved. Kept safe.\n\nThe Ayleids who attacked us—they wanted our secrets and our souls. We used both to thwart them. With the Hist's help, the souls of our tribe retreated into the Remnant, where no Elf could follow.

We honor Sithis above all else. Raj-Sithis the Changer—not the Destroyer from the dusk times—but ends are often beginnings.\n\nThere are no purer agents of change than Shadowscales, so we prepare our children from birth to learn their secrets.

Safety is not an end in itself—only a means to ensure the seasons of tomorrow. Here, all is static. The trees do not grow. The tides do not rise or fall. Our souls grow complacent. Adrift.\n\nWe must return to the Hist. And for that, we need a guide.

We bathe their eggs in our brews to ensure they are hatched under the favored sign and give them their first taste of the swamp's deadly secrets. They are nursed on the milk of toxic weeds until strong enough for the Shadowscales to come claim them.

It's one of the fourteen xal-fek, or sacred plants. Each plant brings joy or death, depending on the measure. In the bonding, Ruxol ensured the Leviathan Pizzle brought great joy. This season, we will see.

It is our way. The Root-House people do not make.\n\nWhen we need meat, the swamp provides. When we need crafts and treasures, other tribes provide. The Hist compels them to make these things. They do not know that the Hist means for us to take them.
Root-House people do not ask. We claim.
The Root-House people do not build. If the Hist wants us to have a village, we take one.\n\nIn an old-time, we claimed this village. But we tired of it, so we burned it down.

You ask me whether the words of an ancient, ghostly Sap-Speaker inside a sacred Hist-relic can be trusted? No, if there was any other way, she would have told us.\n\nI can feel these souls' confusion—their uncertainty. They definitely need my help.
Of course. The Bright-Throats remember to forget. Would you have them drag grudges like stones? That is the dryskin and stone-dweller way.\n\nYour questions are dry and stupid.
Yes. Why would we not?\n\nMy gulweet egg-sire always says, burn what you cannot carry. Otherwise, the tribes will not make new things.

Knowing what you know of Jaxsik, what do you think?\n\nShe will not be happy, at first. Dead-Water warriors dream of death. But in the end, she is a child of the Hist. She will see the wisdom in it. The world still needs wise warriors like Jaxsik-Orrn.

Well, I could not have imagined I would pass on like this. And I am sad that I will not have an opportunity to say farewell to my tribe. But when the rains come, you can dance and drink your fill, or you can hide and go thirsty.\n\nI feel no fear.

A cherished Bright-Throat craft. They take a seed from a tree with no name, nurture it to enormous size, and allow it to sprout its roots. With much care the roots are pared back again and again until a shape is formed.\n\nMine resembled a haj mota.

I nod my head. Leadership in war is no different than leadership in peace.\n\nThese souls may be disoriented, but deep down they wish to make the journey. Tsojei and I will …. Oh. I suppose Tsojei will stay behind. I had not considered that.

There isn't much to tell. We were, we are, we will be. The Hist nurture us and we nurture them. Sometimes Sithis sees fit to disrupt this cycle when it grows too ordinary, so we Moss-Skins find a new routine until it's time for change again.
The Wuju-Ka is a massive pool of voriplasm that interacts with the world through extensions of itself. The smaller voriplasms that prowl these caverns are all just part of a greater whole.

Ah, I probably should have been more specific.\n\nFlint vine is a hardy creeper that grows in caves—or poorly-lit xanmeers, as the case may be. Strong stuff. Definitely strong enough to bear Kirstaleth's weight.

Yes, I believe so. For a single use, mind you! Did I mention I'm terrible at knots? Don't tell Kirstaleth I said that.\n\nYou should have no problem finding enough flint vine for the ladder. Just mind the traps, and beasts, and such. Good luck!

That is a fair point, and I respect nothing more than honest dealing.\n\nAs I said, my name is Xukas—root-herald of the Bright-Throat tribe. I protect the tribe's interests. Some hunt for wamasu, I hunt for truth and fruitful relationships.

Yes. You might call it a tree. All Saxhleel serve a Hist. Their branches protect us and their sap sustains us. If your path ever takes you to Bright-Throat Village, you will see.\n\nI promise you, Murkmire is much grander than the streets of Lilmoth.

Ah. Perhaps eager is a better word?\n\nMost people who visit Black Marsh believe we Saxhleel are uncultured children at best, or fish-brained savages at worst. Famia, however, appreciates our culture … in her way. Sometimes too much.

She risks her life to recover antiquities we do not want or need. Her dedication is touching? I guess.\n\nI keep telling her that we would rather have fresh slugs and sturdy tools, but no snake can slither backwards. She does what she does. So it goes.

The vakka stones? Sometimes. More often I bring maps, tools, and small gifts.\n\nFriend-Famia brings me things as well. Stories about the items she seeks, mostly. Hair-folk rumors, too. Those are very fine gifts.

Xukas will try to take this burden on himself. But his tribe—all of Murkmire would mourn him, and many long years may pass before he returns. The marsh would grow darker without him.\n\nIf I pass, my people will not mourn. And neither should you.

You are right. My egg-brother waits for me somewhere in the world—on the other side of this journey. A comforting thought.\n\nI could not follow you into battle against Kassandra. Let me do this now. I will see these souls to the Hist.

I do not know this word—spy.\n\nA root-herald cannot serve their tribe without gathering stories and rumors, but I would not drink from another Saxhleel's gourd when they were not looking. Famia tells only what she wishes to. Friends, you see?

Yes. Both possess old, wise souls. One must leave the waking world and remain with us—to guide the tribe down the river called Rebirth. Without their strength, we will surely be swept away.\n\nSpeak with them. You will see they do not fear this task.

The binding will hold for awhile. In the meantime, I'll talk to the elders of the nearby tribes and make sure they restore the traditions of the past. As long as the elders periodically perform the rite of binding, the Wuju-Ka will remain contained.

You'd know better than I. When the three of you touched the Remnant, it was like you instantly fell asleep. Your eyes kept fluttering like you were dreaming.\n\nJaxsik-Orrn woke up first. I figured I should watch over you until you did too.
Xukas is … well, the way Jaxsik-Orrn put it, he chose to leave his mortal body behind. One moment he was dreaming, the next his body was still.\n\nHe was my friend. I didn't even get a chance to ….

Yes, he passed so peacefully. I had hoped … that's very good to hear. No more tears, eh? All right, Jaxsik-Orrn said she had to prepare a ritual? She had that Hist-look.\n\nShe said to bring the Remnant, but I think you should have the honor. Here.

You'd know better than I. When the three of you touched the Remnant, it was like you instantly fell asleep. Your eyes kept fluttering like you were dreaming.\n\nXukas woke up first—very quiet. I figured I should watch over you until you did too.

Well, that's a comfort, I guess. Xukas said he had to prepare a ritual—to release the souls from the Remnant, I think. You should be there.\n\nHe said to bring the Remnant, but I think you should have the honor. Here.

She was dreaming alongside the rest of you, then her breathing slowed, and she passed. Xukas told me not to panic—that this was her choice. Still, he seemed pretty distraught.\n\nWhat happened, exactly?

A single spear-ant means nothing, but a hive means death.\n\nA bog-blight is nothing to us, alone. But when they gather in great numbers? Great danger. Great glory, also, for those who fight them. My egg-brother, Tsojei, fell to the bog-blights.

A kaal has no tongue for stories. But … I will do my best.\n\nThe naheesh elders say that Etra had a soul older than the tribe. Even before he hatched, the egg-handlers heard him chanting from inside his tiny shell. Blood! Death! Glory!

I shake my head. A hero to us. Not to you, I think.\n\nEtra rolled across the marsh like a thunderhead—felling great trees, slaying huge beasts, and eating the hearts of great warriors. Often, Etra would take his opponents' grave-stakes as a trophy.
Only if Sithis desires it ….
Not all of them. Some are just slack-jawed, toady, blood bags. The ugly, scale-faced leech that's been bleeding us though? Has to be a vampire. Maybe worse.

Most vampires you hear about only have two fangs, but that High Priestess of the Teeth's got a mouth like a bear trap. \n\nI'll give her something to chew on next time I see her. Soon as I can lift it. You'll see.

Yes. Now if we could only … wait! A garden in a maw of stone! Of course! That's got to be the Swallowed Grove! The Ree-An-Wo!\n\nA dream-wallow in the Swallowed Grove. What could be more exciting? We should discuss this with Kassandra right away!

She will find others. Before the fall, Shuxaltsei drenched the Teeth of Sithis with sacrificial blood from dawn to dusk. As the thing she has become, her need is greater now and so is her power. I can feel it coursing through this temple.

The Argonian reel is a very popular dance in Murkmire and the traditional garments will attract the eyes. What adventurous spirit could refuse joining our expedition after such a striking display of our culture?
I am certain of nothing, but I believe your enthusiasm will carry the day. Now take these garments and dance like bog reeds during the yearly gas bloom!
I have heard many claims regarding the accuracy of her predictions. She is frequently sought out by farmers, sailors, and the like … perhaps a little too sought out.
Priestess Hodyette has quickly tired of her growing popularity. She's become a little … blustery? Make sure you tell her you can pay. That will at least get her talking!

Blackrose used to be an Imperial prison. It was abandoned nearly a century ago.\n\nThat's when the original Blackguards took it over. They were all former inmates, and used the prison as a base for their less-than-legal operations.

I knew something was off, soon as the Thieves Guild gave us a job in Murkmire. Seeks just looked … nervous. Almost scared.\n\nWe were only here a few days before the Blackguards nabbed him. Got him while we were sleeping in the marsh, the cowards.
Like the blood spilled here begins to pulse through dead stone. The beating of this temple's heart is slow, but it echoes through the Void. She is calling to Sithis. We cannot let her be heard.
They have stood too long already. They stand for a Sithis that is no longer, or never was. It seeks change. \n\nWhether that change is good for us is for it to decide.

The Xinchei-Konu is not merely a calendar. It is a powerful ku-vastei; a catalyst of needed change. When seeds must grow, it gives us rain. When sprouts sink in mud, it brings the sun.\n\nAs jekka-wass, it is my duty to watch over the monument.

Ah, the Vastei-Sei. How interesting that my pupil sent you in his stead.\n\nSo Vozei has finally found the tablets of the Xinchei-Konu. Impressive. I thought the task would take far longer for one so stuck in his books.

Shuxaltsei was not cast down for simply clinging to the old ways. She forsook this world. Her prayers of appeasement became invitations for destruction. I believe she has returned to finish what she started when the tribes rose up to stop her.

Hmm. So Vozei had you do all the work, did he?\n\nWell, it is only fitting that you should prepare the ritual components for the Vastei-Sei as well then. You will need brackish mud, a deathly bloom, and wood which crumbles stone.
I suppose I could take time from my actual duties to sate your mere curiosity. What more do you wish to know?
Shuxaltsei returned from beyond the grip of death for this purpose. Who knows what is within her power?
To cast this world into darkness. To see the Hist wither and die. To sow destruction until the great serpent returns us all to the Void.

Some may be faithful to her as a priestess of Sithis, but I think most fell victim to her power. After the Blackrose riots destroyed the prison there would have been no shortage of outlaws wandering the swamps for her to prey upon.
Yes. From the beginning. I will not say I told you so.\n\nYou remember her limp-tailed toadie, Whiptail? He is one of them. Now he and his savages escort Kassandra, and block our pursuit.

You are right. But something …. As soon as I arrived here in the Deepmire, the Hist started whispering to me. Trying to dull my fury. Urging patience and trust. I hate it.\n\nBut my tongue wanders, and the trail goes cold. We must resume the hunt.

It is Cyrodilic Collections' mission to find and restore the relics of Murkmire for all to enjoy. However, our expedition has come across no end of issues. That's why Concordia asked me to stay in Shadowfen and search for assistance.

A lack of food, an onslaught of bugs. Not to mention the fact that few are willing to travel through the wilds of my homeland.\n\nBut I'm sure we can overcome these struggles! Especially now that you're here to help.
Lucky for you, I have an extra copy on the nearby table. You would do well not to lose it again.

The Rose was built upon ruins, built upon ruins, built upon ruins. The Hist only knows what was buried beneath, but if anything was to stir Shuxaltsei from her grave, the bloodshed of the prison riots would be it.\n\nBut we have more dire concerns.
What do you mean "am I one of the custodians"? Of course I am.\n\nOh, I get what you're driving at. Don't look scaly enough for the part. That's it, isn't it?
That's just being close minded. I've half a mind to bash you for that, but Xode says I'll be happier when I stop fighting my problems.\n\nThey've been good to me since I got here.
Run out of Valenwood. Got all these rules in the Dominion, especially against bashing stuff. Even when you're mad. Drifted around, until I bashed some knot-faced prowler skulking in my room.

Round about, yeah. Started getting strange letters from some warped-plank who signs letters by dipping their hand in ink. Dim, yeah? It's all Sithis this, Sithis that. Can't get away from it. Finally, I come out here. No letters. Coincidence?

We found this pitiable soul limping his way to our village. I almost took him for a bog blight at first, but this Saxhleel was alive when I found him, if only barely. I tried to help him, but he lashed out and collapsed. He died shortly after.

We are amidst the preparations for our tribe's most vital ceremony. Now a warped and withered stranger has died at our roots. An ill omen for the arrival of our guests.\n\nI am troubled, ojel, because I do not hear what the Hist is trying to tell me.

These past weeks the Hist has been agitated. It has given me signs that I believed were warnings for the bonding to come, but now I feel that I've misinterpreted.\n\nIt is this clutch that is in peril … and it is you who can save it.
She gets her hopes up every time the bonding ritual approaches, but she's never selected. She'd be a good mother—I think—if she ever got the chance, but I'm no tree-minder.
It's nothing. I'm just upset from an argument earlier. Forgive me.
I just felt so sorry for him. The idea of leaving him to rot—I ….\n\nI'm sorry, can we talk about something else?
I—no. Why would you think there's something wrong?

To mock me, I'm sure. After all, I lack both the knowledge and means to seek out the tablets myself.\n\nThe sooner you aid me in this, the better. I would rather suffer a thousand mire-gnats than the disapproving gaze of Nisswo Paraxeeh.

Mewah-Jez is our tribe's ka-deelith—our war-teacher. She trains our novices to walk the Path of the Lily. Since she took over the responsibility, the Dead-Water warriors have become stronger and more powerful. At least, the ones that survive.

The Path of the Lily claims more lives than ever before. Kishi and his egg-siblings were the last novices to complete the trial without injury, let alone death.\n\nMore often now, entire clutches of novices fall to the dangers encountered on the Path.

Bhoki's home stands just within the village walls, on the western side of the Hist.\n\nPlease hurry, for Mewah-Jez took Kishi away before the night had turned to day. If Kishi hasn't been consumed by a swamp beast yet, it won't be long now.

Always! As long as your blade is quick and your skill spotless, you are welcome to join.\n\nOur main task is to fight against the Daedric Anchors falling across the continent. The Fighters Guild is Tamriel's only line of defense against them.

Excellent! I then name you Associate.\n\nStart by dispatching any Daedra you come across. And if you find any Daedric Anchors, destroy them. The more you dispatch, the more rewards and special missions the Fighters Guild can offer you.

Objects of chains and metals, falling from the sky all across Tamriel. Only the Fighters Guild has the courage to fight back and attempt to destroy these dark incursions.\n\nAre you willing to lend a paw?

For seasons and seasons, my friend! And I shall inform the elders of the nearest tribes. They will once again take up the responsibility of maintaining the ritual.\n\nI couldn't have accomplished any of these things without your help. Thank you!

We nearly had her. Our claws reached for her throat, but suddenly, Jaxsik cried out and collapsed. I could not find the will to leave her behind.\n\nLike she always says, I have the underbelly of a softshell crab.

Yes. She mutters about the tree that guided us—she says it is very close. I do not wish for Kassandra to claim the Remnant, but ….\n\nWe must find this dreaming tree. Haste has profited us very little. We should slow down and listen to the Hist.

You would not know it in speaking with her, but Jaxsik is not so cruel as she seems. She feels things very deeply—deeper even than me.\n\nThe air in this temple is thick with memories, and she hears them all.

Ah, yes. I carved this many seasons ago. I hoped it would convince my beloved Kud-Nakal to join me for our tribe's next bonding ritual, but I lost the totem before it could be presented.\n\nOf course, this was when I was still a female.

The ceremony bonds those who have chosen to lay an egg together.\n\nMany dryskins compare it to a wedding. This is not entirely accurate, of course. While there is always respect between the bonded pair, romantic feelings are not strictly necessary.

I had every intention to. Days I devoted to carving, to writing just the right words. I worked outside the village, not wanting Kud-Nakal to see my gift before it was finished.\n\nAnd then a bog bloat invaded my camp.

Who would want to kill Haxara? That makes no sense … and who killed the Veeskhleel?\n\nDon't tell me you think Haxara killed this ojel. She averts her gaze from our cookfires for pity of the creatures on the spits. She could never have done this.

As mud is my mother, it's true …! How could she? Giving our eggs to the Veeskhleel, of all people!\n\nI don't care if they were not meant to hatch. The Ghost People should never have been allowed to lay a hand on our eggs! We must tell Pavu.

The Xinchei-Konu is no mere collection of carved stone. It is the will of change, the force which pushes through stagnation.\n\nThe Vastei-Sei will spark that power once more, connecting all back to one.

It will. The Remnant is very, very close. Deep beneath our feet, cradled in vines and moss.\n\nYou have seen its resting place before—in your dream-wallow. A cavern of roots and stone. Tsojei and I want to go with you … but we cannot.

I know. But you will not need it.\n\nTake Famia with you to the xanmeer east of here. Keep her safe. She wears the skin of man, but the Hist knows her heart. The two of you will stop Kassandra. I believe this. So should you.

Xukas and I … we set our roots here. I cannot explain it in the dry-tongue. It is like the sun rising, or the rivers flowing downstream. It simply is.\n\nXukas and I watch over the tree because we must. You find the Remnant because you must.

Drooler's our bantam guar. Cute little slobberer was a marriage gift, and he's been with us ever since. He's more attached to Varona than to me, truth be told, and she's trained him well.\n\nJust blow the whistle and he'll come running.

Unusual for Saxhleel to take up magic. Even more rare for one to deal with the dead. Argonians exist in the present. Past is dead. Dead is dead. \n\nOnly the Veeskhleel commune with the dead, and Baxilt-Gah is as crazy as the rest of the Ghost People!

I've gathered every song and story I could find that even mentioned the Lost Legion. After many seasons of travel and study, an obscure line in a ballad sung by an elder of the Gee-Rusleel tribe led me to Tsofeer.\n\nMy burden lightens with every step!

It is normally quite pleasant, but before the bonding ritual it becomes insufferable. Suddenly the village is full of experts, if you take my meaning. The sooner it's back to just me and the eggs, the better.

No, no. Just dries my scales. The eggs are blissfully unaware of all the scrutiny. I think. I don't remember all the gawking and complaining, certainly.\n\nNow, if you don't mind. I think Mimme would make better company right now.

Well, my egg-sister, Meena, had to lay her first clutch with a Copper-Eye that didn't know which direction his tail should face … but no.\n\nWe care for our eggs, but the Hist guides their development. Not all eggs are destined to hatch though.

They return to the Hist. There are signs to look for: dry shells, lacking luster, thin membrane, an empty shadow. Inevitably they sink into the roots and fade away.\n\nThose that remain are always healthy members of the tribe.
Just over three years at this point. I'll admit, it takes some getting used to, but once—ow! Sorry. Once you settle in, you'll never want to leave!

Cyrodilic Collections is a fellowship of historians dedicated to recovering Argonian antiquities. But unlike other treasure-hunters, we don't sell relics for profit. We plan to build a museum here to share Murkmire's treasures with the world!
Oh! So you're that adventurer she mentioned in her letters. What a welcome coincidence! Concordia has been invaluable to the effort. One day I'll finally convince her to visit.

Bok-Xul is located to the west. Words mean "Bowl of Death" in Argonian tongue. It's an ancient ritual circle, all jumbled rock and stone ruins. Very dark place. Very evil. Just perfect for a necromancer like Baxilt-Gah.

Doing your research, eh? Excellent!\n\nThe local Argonians call it Ixtaxh-Thitithil-Meht—literally the exact egg-cracker. Evocative, right? We just call it the Ixtaxh Xanmeer. I have it on good authority that we'll find the Kajin-Jat Crystal inside.

It's my missing companions, Eshraf and Dinia—the explorers whose bags we found out in the marsh. Remember?\n\nI told you I sent them to recover vakka stones, but they were also looking for the Remnant of Argon.

A legend. Some say it's a massive gem. Others some sort of egg. Either way, I fear Eshraf and Dinia's disappearance is linked to their search.\n\nXukas agreed to look into it and I think he found something. Could you speak with him?
Oh, most certainly! Jewelry, idols, who knows? We sell some of these more common items to private collectors—not for a profit, mind you! Just enough to keep the operation afloat.

Apparently, it was vital to some kind of ritual. But that could mean practically anything. According to my research, ancient Argonians performed rituals constantly—large and small.\n\nEven so, this crystal clearly deserves a place in our collection!

Fine, I guess? The truth is, the Argonians just don't care about their history all that much. They live in the now. Past, future … those concepts are totally foreign to them.\n\nOnce our museum is finished, though, I'm sure they'll take an interest!

For the most part? No, they don't. The Argonians here in Murkmire … they don't see things the way we do. When we first arrived, I tried to include the locals in our work—to get their blessing, you know?
Well, I do know a little something about how to get along here in Murkmire. The first thing I'd suggest is making connections with the local tribes—the Wasseek-Haleel in particular.

Most of the Murkmire tribes are cagey, but polite. There is one tribe I'd avoid though—the Dead-Water tribe, or the Naga-Kur.\n\nThey're Nagas—a strange breed of Argonians with a very prickly disposition. They don't like outsiders. Not one bit.

Sorry, I slip into Jel sometimes—the Argonian tongue. The locals say I'm a natural!\n\nAnyway, the Wasseek-Haleel are also called the Bright-Throats. They're quite friendly. Artisans mostly. Clever traders, too. Very good friends to have in a pinch.

I will explain, so listen well. The necromancer's evil magic corrupts the soil, corrupts the roots. It turns plants into monsters. The carnivorous plants spread out of Bok-Xul and endanger the tribe.\n\nOnly way to kill the plants is to burn the roots.

Where else? That's where the necromancer performs his vile rituals. That's where the heart-roots grow.\n\nRemember. Baxilt-Gah is an evil necromancer. Evil necromancers can be killed, but they have a bad habit of returning. Like weeds, they are!

Evidence that the Ninth Legion visited the cavern before it disappeared. Maybe even signs that the Imperials entered Tsofeer and never emerged.\n\nIf we could locate something that explains why my ancestor agreed to help them, that would be moist!

You are right, of course. Let me think. Think. Think …! \n\nThis dragonthorn looks fresh, so it must have been picked recently. We cultivate ours in a small glade near to the village. That would be the easiest place to gather this much of the herb.
Forgive me, but I must report your findings to the Tree-Minder. I will return to your side with all the swiftness of a strangler vine.

The Tsofeer Caverns were sealed by a rock slide in the distant past. Recent tremors, however, have opened a path into the caves.\n\nI also learned that tribal elders once performed rituals to bind the Wuju-Ka inside, but that was a long time ago.

According to the stories, the Wuju-Ka creates an extension of itself to guard the pool. Find this large voriplasm guardian and destroy it. That should weaken the Wuju-Ka and make it more susceptible to the binding ritual.

The Wuju-Ka isn't like other voriplasms. It has an intelligence and a hunger different from the simple creatures seen in the swamp. Once it emerges from the cavern, it will spread and consume all of Murkmire.\n\nWe can't allow that to happen!

I bare my teeth. A Naga prays for repercussions daily, outsider.\n\nBlackguards slither about in Dead-Water territory often. Too often. Perhaps finding this ojel in pieces will finally lure them into open combat. Then we will skin them like catfish.

She's a member of one of the local tribes. Black-Tongue, I think. Has a powerful interest for all this Sithis stuff. Kind of off-putting, but it works in our favor.\n\nLike I said, if you really want to know, ask her yourself.
The Ghost People tribe. They make their home in the lightless corners of the deep swamp. Veeskhleel only leave their lands to creep through the night and steal the dead!

I do, I do! He knew the tribes weren't strong enough to oppose the Ninth Legion, so he sacrificed his own life to lead them to the Wuju-Ka.\n\nI feel very proud to be part of his egg-family, my friend.
The temple has not bared its fangs for centuries, but do not doubt it has them. Mind where you tread if you do not wish to invite the wrath of Sithis.

Why do the Blackguards do anything? They are driven by whim and desire. Though the ones who occupy the Teeth seem more like rabid dogs, than raiders. Perhaps the call of Sithis the Destroyer has whipped them into their frenzy.

They were on display in the sacrificial chambers, before the temple was overrun by the Blackguards. I cannot say if they were moved by the caretakers, plundered, or shattered to pieces, but I trust you will find them if you are meant to.

Oh, most assuredly! I might even talk to Cyrodilic Collections. Since my people have little use for history, maybe the outsiders can teach me a few things.\n\nAnyway, may the rivers always flow in your direction, my friend!

Not just from warriors. All tribe members. My dagger was carved from the leg bone of my egg-mother, and she was a cook!\n\nIt allows the departed to keep fighting. To help the tribe even after they die.

No. That would be cruel. Our spirits go to the Hist when we die. We could not bind the spirits to the bones, even if we wanted to. We're not necromancers!\n\nMaking use of bones honors our dead and gives purpose to their bodies after they die.

Easily. The Blackguards weren't interested in me at all, didn't even give chase. So I stuck to the shadows and followed them here.\n\nOne of the patrols noticed me scouting the prison. That's when Drakeeh contacted me.

Right. So long as I made my way through their gauntlet, Seeks would be free to go.\n\nI halfway suspect it was all a joke. I can easily pick you a lock or steal some treasure, but defeating a gauntlet of deadly warriors? Not my forte.
I reveal an embarrassing truth. No, the Naga-Kur despise outsiders. But a good hunter makes use of every available tool and weapon.\n\nYou happen to be a perfect tool.
Ha. No.\n\nTruthfully, there is nothing in the xanmeers that interests me. I hope you have a good reason for taking this journey. I should point out that simple greed is not a good reason.

Just remember everything you learned during the last few matches. And then do all that, but all at once! Or something like that, right?\n\nSorry, I'm just a bit flustered. I can't believe they would play us so rotten!
Right, well, I've gotten the impression that Seeks-the-Dark may have … actually been a member of the Blackguards?\n\nI mean, I'm not sure though! And even if he was, he obviously left years ago.

Right, I did happen to sneak a peek when you were fighting your first round. \n\nThere's two bull netches in there, and they did not look friendly. I'd stay clear of them if I were you and just focus on the arena's champion.

Afraid not. I'm more of a lady of mystery than a warrior.\n\nBut while you're fighting, I'll try to find out why the Blackguards targeted Seeks-the-Dark. After all, information is key to keeping the upper hand! Or so Seeks always tells me.

From what I hear, Drakeeh's a pretty devoted follower of Sithis. He even claims that his power of necromancy stems from that worship. \n\nThrough the Dread-Father, he controls death and darkness and void! That sort of thing.

I haven't learned anything new, but I have been wondering something. \n\nIf the Blackguards wanted revenge, why didn't they make Seeks-the-Dark go through this gauntlet? Why give me the chance to rescue him?

How the Blackguards ended up becoming bed mates with a vampire coven, I'll never know. Though I suppose like begets like.\n\nThe champion calls herself Lady Minara, though I'm not quite sure what she's the lady of.

Nothing good, I'm afraid. It seems everyone here views him as some sort of traitor.\n\nMaybe he botched a job for them? The Thieves Guild isn't particularly picky about who hires us, after all. That may be why the Blackguards are seeking revenge.

It's simple, really. I used to be a Blackguard. Then I decided not to be. \n\nHowever, like most illegal operations, my retirement options involved either death or desertion. I obviously chose the latter. Drakeeh didn't take kindly to that decision.

Oh, I'm sure Erilthel has blabbered on about your great deeds enough for both of us.\n\nYou should be proud, in fact. After all this, you'll probably get an entire chapter dedicated to you in that book she's writing.

If my assumptions are correct, then Imperials of the First Era sheltered in the cavern in the distant past. I suspect that scrolls containing interesting information should still be inside.\n\nAnd if you can find a cypher ring, too, even better!

Tremors shook the region, clearing away rocks that once blocked the entrance to the cavern. When I noticed the path was open, I petitioned Famia to get her associates to conduct some research on my behalf.\n\nI have a burning passion for history!

You have not heard of us? Either you are very new, or I am dragging my tail as a representative.\n\nWe are artisans, traders, and guides. Our Hist's roots stretch from Bright-Throat Village north of here to Lilmoth and the coast beyond.

Oh, egg-kin, surely you are not so lost that you have forgotten your roots.\n\nAll Saxhleel serve a Hist—even those who stray beyond the borders. Their branches protect us and their sap sustains us. Visit Bright-Throat Village sometime. You will see.

I respond with truth. No one knows. Miregaunts have been here as long as Argonians. Maybe longer. Some think they are the wrath of Murkmire. Others that the Hist sends them to teach lessons.\n\nWorst is Walks-Like-Thunder. Very bad. Very dangerous.

Miregaunts are part of the land. Strike one down, it comes back later. Like stink weeds or swamp grass.\n\nBesides, I do not expect you to kill Walks-Like-Thunder. Though I hope to be wrong. We really need the nightbloom vines.

History? Yes, I guess so. But history is dead and gone, beeko. Right?\n\nI call many round-tongues friend, but even the best of them, in their deep-hearts, think we are fools for letting our stone houses sink into the mud. We call it shunatei.

Fear of death. Fear of forgetting.\n\nDryskins build their great cities—setting every brick with care. But before long, a war, or a storm, or groundquake breaks it apart, and they are left with ruins just like ours. Square caves where monsters live.
Then there is a fight.

I would not say that. Some xanmeers contain powerful relics or cursed antiquities. We can't have that sort of thing floating around.\n\nIt takes some doing, but typically we can recover items like that without a fight.
Exactly. To act like it does is pride, foolishness, or both.

Old baubles from a long-forgotten season. Worthless to the Naga-Kur, but valued by outsiders like Cyrodilic Collections. Tribe doesn't see a reason to sell the items, but I do. \n\nSo I get you to find them. For a share of the gold, of course.

Oh, probably for all the usual reasons: Shelter, storage, the acquisition of natural resources.\n\nWouldn't it be wonderful if we found the lost Ninth Legion in those caves? Well, if you found them. I'm terribly uncomfortable in enclosed spaces.

The Echoing Hollow hides an entrance to some ruins. An Argonian xanmeer. An old place full of old baubles. The Naga-Kur think outsiders strange for wanting useless, old things, but as long as they pay, why should I care?

What's so valuable about old, useless objects made of rock or clay? The past is dead and forgotten, but outsiders continue to chase after it like crocodiles that smell blood. It makes no sense!\n\nBut they pay gold, so go find these useless objects.

With utmost disappointment I admit that Naga lead this band of despicable outlaws. Blackguards cause trouble throughout Murkmire, but some have targeted the Naga-Kur tribe.\n\nIf they fortify Echoing Hollow, they will be unstoppable.

Even an army of outlaws needs supplies to wage war. Food, weapons, armor—without supplies, the Blackguards will depart.\n\nLike all cowards, they prefer to walk the easy path. Burn their caches and the easy path becomes hard. They hate that.

The gauntlet serves as both entertainment for the Blackguards and punishment for all who cross them. Each arena is held by a reigning champion.\n\nYour first opponent is Battlemage Ennodius, an Imperial known for her unmatched skill with fire magic.

Perhaps the original Blackguards did, but these days you'll find all manner of races within their ranks. It seems Drakeeh is more concerned with amassing power than holding onto a century long grudge.

Have you been licking toads again?\n\nOh, wait. I see. You cannot face your name-day challenge if it is not your name day, right? Ha. Nice try, Mateem. But enough foolishness. Fat Gixthi will not kill herself. Go!
Who is—? Has the theilul gone to your head? You forget the name of Fat Gixthi? The beast that ate your favorite plow-guar? \n\nShe was just a hatchling then. But now? Fine quarry for a hunt.
Do you wish to ride on your father's back in swaddle-skins all your life? This is the chukka-sei, Mateem. The naming day! If you wish to have a say in the tribe's affairs, you must prove your worth.
Now I know you are joking! How could you forget the son of your mother's egg-sister?\n\nHe and I spent weeks planning this hunt for you. Fat Gixthi! I only wonder where he could be.

Have you not fought the beasts, already? Ayleids. Elves with hearts like flint.\n\nOur strongest kaals and their shellback elites held the ojels at bay for weeks, but a pack of them broke through the line—attacking the village.

Who can say? The Argonians have a different view of the afterlife from the other races. But I'm sure the benevolent rite won't hurt anything. And it might even help.\n\nBesides, it will make me feel better, and I am paying for the service, after all.

Yes. But at great cost. For every Saxhleel lost, five Ayleids lie dead. We … I must believe we broke them here. As soon as the sap-speaker gives us her blessing, I will rally the others for a counter-attack.\n\nWe will end this, Mateem. Today.

The Elves attacked in numbers I have never seen in my lifetime. Like the stars. We slay them by the hundreds, but still they come—waves upon waves.\n\nOur village is lost, Mateem. But the sap-speaker says the tribe may survive.
She grows a miracle, root-kin. Nothing less will suffice.\n\nGo now. I will hold off the outsiders as long as I can.

The death of our tribe, and the creation of the Remnant of Argon.\n\nThe Ayleid Elves, with their white-stone hearts, brought steel and nightmare magicks to Murkmire. Their leader coveted our souls and their secrets. So with his staff, he claimed them.

I patiently attempt to explain. Go into the swamp and look for the tamed vine-tongues. These plants appear different from the more hostile varieties. \n\nToss fire stones at the plants and they will lead you to Kishi's hidden camp.

Mewah-Jez insists that her training is not at fault. The novices are too weak and that is why they fail.\n\nThe war-teacher proclaims that every challenge can be overcome by strength and strength alone. Hit harder, kill faster, never pause to think.

It provides a refuge for the souls of our tribe. A safe place to weather the storm. But it has slept too long and the Hist that cares for it withers away.\n\nYou must find the Remnant. Find us. With your aid, both Hist and Remnant will wake and thrive.

The seed sleeps in a forgotten place—hidden from sun, and storm, and time itself. In all the world, only this staff remembers its whereabouts. It will guide you, just as the stars guide a sailor.\n\nKnow this, though. You will not hold it for long.

Because strength is only one weapon in the warrior's arsenal. To ignore the others is to court doom, as our novices find out again and again.\n\nIf not for Kishi's interference, the latest group would have died as well. And for this he is dishonored.
Both. And neither.

The Dead-Water tribe learns to fight. We have very little experience questioning orders or ignoring tradition. That is Kishi's greatest strength and most apparent weakness. He questions everything.\n\nHelp my egg-son and you will help our tribe.

Raj-Kaal Seelan accepts death as a constant companion. It is almost a member of our tribe. The war-chief sees the haj mota flying toward the waterfall, but considers its fate to be part of the natural order.
You are welcome.\n\nDo not be discouraged. Uncertainty is no bad thing.
Hmm.\n\nTell me, Rootmender, which do you believe is true? Is this a dream-wallow vision? Is it real?

The narrow reed you call real cannot hold the Hist's truth, Rootmender. Real. Illusion. Dream. Waking. These are the words that keep our bellies to the mud. We are safe there, yes. But we cannot see very far.\n\nToday, you see very far indeed.
Very well. It is real. Does this quench the thirst in your mind?
Very well. It is a vision. Does this quench the thirst in your mind?

From what I hear, Tames-the-Beast uses magic that's rooted in nature. Literally! He can create roots from the ground to bind you, and has a menagerie of beasts at his beck and call.\n\nAn exciting opponent if I ever heard one!

Something like the voice of the Hist? The Hist never sees fit to speak to me, so who can say?\n\nIn any case, our course here is clear. We must find the Remnant, regardless of what whispers Xukas may or may not have heard.

The riddle spoke of a dream-wallow, correct? So I would keep a close eye out for any ritual vessels, braziers, reagents, and so on.\n\nI'm sure our Bright-Throat and Dead-Water friends can provide more insight on that … provided they haven't run off.

Our relationship with Xukas and Jaxsik-Orrn is still young—and fragile. I just want to make certain they don't double back. I'm sure you understand this small measure of skepticism.\n\nIf things seem quiet, we will make our way forward.
She's a necromancer, that I know. Rumor has it she curses her opponents, summons skeletons, all sorts of nasty things.\n\nKeep on your toes and you should do just fine. I think.

I'm just not sure. I don't know much about Seeks-the-Dark's past, you see. Doesn't talk much about himself to anyone, even his beloved apprentice.\n\nI'll try to gather more information. You just worry about the gauntlet.

Each tablet represents a month in the year's cycle. Vakka, Xeech, Sisei, and so on. As with the dryskin calendar, there are twelve months in total.\n\nWithout these tablets, the Xinchei-Konu is powerless.

Very little, I'm afraid. Sorry! According to Beejeem's Murkmire Almanac, it's a subterranean jungle, formed from some kind of sinkhole. Beyond that, it's pretty mysterious.\n\nThere are mundane perils there, of course, but the real danger is magical.

Reanimated dead! Not like the bog-blights—something else entirely. The locals think the place is guarded by dream-spirits, but a reliable source told me it's definitely zombies, or skeletons or something.\n\nSo … caution! Yes!
That's what my gut says, anyway. It would explain why the Blackguards would go to such extremes in targeting him.\n\nFor now, let's focus on the gauntlet. Only two more arenas to go!

If your, ah, slurred words are an indication, you appear to be entering a state of thought induced by the compounds burned by Xukas and Jaxsik. Curiously, it hasn't impacted Kassandra or myself. At least, I don't believe I'm impacted … do you?

The war-chief believes that Mewah-Jez's methods will produce stronger, more powerful warriors. Eventually. In the meantime, he cannot resist the pull of tradition any more than the haj mota or the rest of the tribe.\n\nThat is why Kishi must succeed.

I saw, or perhaps sensed would be more accurate, Ayleids? If that even makes sense. Yours would be the clearer image, to be sure. But what was their role? I don't understand. \n\nMaybe we can gather context.

Ayleids, particularly the Barsaebic Ayleids, would always focus on expansion. Gideon and Stormhold are proof of that. But I don't know of their influence reaching this far south. And from what I've seen, that was no occupying force.

No! I am just not eager to throw myself into another dream-wallow. They dry my eyes and make my belly hurt.\n\nSeeking the words of the Hist in the chimes is all well and good. But dream-wallows are much more dimik. Vivid is the dryskin word?

Ugh. I try not to think on it, beeko.\n\nThere was a maxeem-urto. A kind of river clam, you would say? It challenged me to a game of riddles. The words all turned to orange mud. In the end, I feasted on him. It was very unsettling.

I know it is a place that no Argonian in Murkmire would tread willingly. The tree-minders say dream-beasts wander that place. Angry spirits that whisper burning secrets to anyone foolish enough to enter.\n\nI guess we are foolish enough.
Each tribe walks the dream differently.\n\nIn Dead-Water land, we paint our hands red, breathe in the sacred smoke, then face our kaju dream-beast.

I shrug my shoulders. Members of the Dead-Water tribe do not fear this place, but we do not go there. Spirits run free in the Grove—hard to kill, I think. We will find out.\n\nNothing will stand between us and the Remnant.

Dead-Water warriors burn the petals and inhale the smoke. It stretches the soul and widens our eyes. Without starblossoms, we could not fight our kaju dream-beasts, or learn our killing-names.\n\nBreathing this smoke is a great honor, ojel.

Yes. A Naga must triumph in combat, unassisted, against a sacred-beast the chief chooses for you.\n\nI fought a swamp leviathan. I had to cut my way out of its stomach. Perhaps we will face a new beast today. I sharpen my claws.
Where Kassandra goes, I go. That's what she pays me for, right?

People say it's haunted. Of course, people say lots of places are haunted. Personally, I wouldn't worry about the things you can't see. There's plenty of things you can see that probably want you dead.
You'll need to find places of duality. Swamp and sea, death and life, stone and wood.\n\nBut I'm sure you've had enough with riddles by now. Today, I'll simply mark the locations on your map.
So Drakeeh claims. Point is, you're going to have to go through a bunch of undead first if you want to defeat Drakeeh.\n\nThis whole thing about Sithis though, that sounds like pure lunacy to me.

Seeks-the-Dark taught me quite a bit about Sithis, how he's more of a … force of nature. Not really a god that hands down necromancy powers.\n\nI think Drakeeh is just puffing himself up. Oh, look at me, I've got Sithis on my side! Ugh.
Insinuating I'm a coward? Oh, hero, you wound me!\n\nI stay with Kassandra. But don't worry your pretty head. We'll be along soon enough.

The items you are to gather represent not only duality, but also change. \n\nThe mud which flows from swamp to sea. The living flower which blooms from death. The wood which crumbles the stone that once hindered it.

Once, I watched over the Xinchei-Konu, learning its secrets and sharing its wisdom.\n\nNow I speak the dark words of Sithis, traveling the tribes and spreading its wisdom. A similar task, truth be told.
Punish him? I … oh no, I think you're right.\n\nThere's no way I could have survived the gauntlet. They must have been trying to hurt Seeks by hurting me. Oh, those absolute bastards!
Ah. Well, I suppose word does travel. I will have to speak to him once the ritual is completed.\n\nBut for now, I am afraid I must beg your help once more.
Very little, I promise!\n\nI've combined the ritual components together. You must place the mixture into the ceremonial bowls as I say the incantation.
