Both defendants claim inheritance of a saltrice farm, previously owned by the now deceased Keema-Ru.\n\nNurhei, a local trader, claims the farm as collateral for debts owned. Paheiza, egg-sister to the deceased, claims it by familial association.

The Saxhleel of Murkmire don't exactly have laws, as understood by outsiders.\n\nSmall disputes are handled by an arbiter of both parties' choosing. This can be anyone, though it tends to be the tribe's tree-minder.

I worked for Keema-Ru for several years. As a neutral third party with an interest in the farm's wellbeing, I volunteered to arbitrate.\n\nUnfortunately, all attempts at negotiation have failed so far.
I worked for Keema-Ru, and her alone. While Paheiza was … present, she did little to help the farm. I barely even spoke to her before this dispute.\n\nI just want the farm to be in good hands.

Simply put, the Shadowscales are an order of assassins that have been present in Black Marsh since time immemorial. Among the Saxhleel, they are both feared and respected. \n\nSulahkeesh is of an … advanced age, which is a rarity within her order.

The Shadowscales serve Black Marsh in many ways. Their role in our society is much more nuanced than mere killers. They help keep the natural order of things, as it were. \n\nSulahkeesh has simply decided to take a more direct approach to that role.

Yet you are not Chuxu. Lost his nerve, did he? He may have a way with words, but still lacks the will to speak them. A shame.\n\nI will help with this dispute, but need you to be my eyes. As you can plainly see, I lost my sight long ago.

I need evidence if I'm to properly judge. Speak with the two claimants, Nurhei and Paheiza. Seek their truths, yes, but also their lies. Both will help my decision.\n\nIt also wouldn't hurt to check the farm itself.

Ah, such a sweet sound. As they say, "Silence is the music of Sithis."\n\nYou have my attention. Is this about Chuxu? I've heard him pacing for an hour or so, and suspect he seeks my judgment on some matter.

As I thought. Very well. I'll need evidence if I'm to properly judge. Speak with the two claimants, Nurhei and Paheiza. Seek their truths, yes, but also their lies. Both will help my decision.\n\nIt also wouldn't hurt to check the farm itself.
Naturally. Speak.

Many think of death as an end. This is only partially correct. \n\nDeath is also a beginning, a cycle turned again. The Shadowscales see this more clearly than most, and so we are tasked with sharing our wisdom with others. Sometimes quite suddenly.

We are ones born under the Shadow, trained as assassins and given over to the Dark Brotherhood. Those of us fortunate to live long lives, however, must learn to serve Sithis in other ways.\n\nSo I have become a ku-vastei; an agent of needed change.
Right to the point. \n\nTell me, how old do you think I am?

My, what a charming little liar you make.\n\nI'm much older than that, of course. When my eyes began to fail me, I knew my role was fated to change. I now honor Sithis through my guidance, rather than my blade.
Oh! Khah-khah-khah! I like you.\n\nYes, I am very old. With age came the loss of my vision. Now I honor Sithis through my guidance of others, rather than my blades.

The name's Tharayya. I'm a historian, you might say. I have a keen interest in the legacy of the Dwemer. The shivering Breton is Landal Gevont, Goblin scholar and his … I don't know what, Burr. Ranja, our locksmith. Alareth and Soriel, scholars.

I found references to a Wrathstone in Dwemer writings from around the same period it appeared in Ayleid records. The Ayleids attempted several times to seize it for themselves, so the Dwemer locked it away in the farthest reaches of the world.
I never solved the mystery of the Eye or its relationship to the undead that overran Volenfell. No one was willing to head back into that mess, so any clues we left behind are beyond reach.

Many somethings. It seems these caves have become a popular escape from the frigid winds, both for wildlife and a local Goblin tribe. Landal, the so-called Goblin expert was supposed to secure us safe passage, but we've made no progress.
I don't know. She convinced me to bring her these eggs only to poison them. Look what she's done to my babies!\n\nHow could anyone do something so cruel?

Afraid so. Fortunately, they seemed content to remain within the confines of the ruins, and the authorities content to leave them there.\n\nWith no leads on where the Eye could have gone, I was back to square one, but setbacks don't keep me down long.

This pendant belongs to the Root-House people. It seems their hunting party arrived before you could.\n\nPerhaps they took the box with them? Their campsite is just a ways north of here, if you don't mind helping me further.
I know! A mother knows!\n\nRee-Nakal's poison did this to them.
Less than I would like. I'm here to figure out its significance. There's no point in speculating without seeing it for ourselves.

The Shadowscale? I see.\n\nMy claim on that farm is as watertight as my trading vessels. Keema-Ru, may she be at peace with the Hist, owed me several debts before she departed. That farm acts as collateral. It is as simple as that.
As I said, it contains a memento from my village. I haven't … I haven't been able to return, you see. It's my only remaining connection.

I am a skilled hunter of the Naga-Kur. You would say Dead-Water in your tongue. We are ruthless warriors. Our village lies far to the north and west, deep in the marsh.\n\nWe are proud. Set in our ways. The tribe has no love of outsiders.

That skooma-addled kuuda couldn't tend a crop if her scales depended on it.\n\nShe may be Keema-Ru's egg-sister, but she cares nothing for that saltrice farm. It would be run into the muck before the next season. Of this, I have no doubt.

"The Adventures of Lady Twilight" or some other such dribble. She talks about it nonstop. Has even read me a few passages.\n\nNot that I asked her to, of course. But once Erilthel gets going, few things stop her.

I was young and stupid. I wanted power, and didn't have an issue with using illegal means to obtain it. Still don't, obviously, given my position within the Thieves Guild.\n\nI did, however, have an issue with coldblooded murder.

I didn't accept a job in Murkmire. Erilthel did, on my behalf. By the time I learned what happened, there was no good reason to turn it down.\n\nIt seems I'm just as dimwitted as my ever faithful apprentice.

I hope you appreciate what I'm entrusting you with. I'm betting that this place is the home of the mythical Wrathstone. An object of such importance that the Dwemer secured it as far from civilization as they could. Where better than in a glacier?
This is a cutthroat field of study. My own husband tried to kill me over less. Ex-husband. Late ex-husband.\n\nI'd rather this partnership not follow a similar trajectory.
My own husband did try to kill me, if you'll recall.

Only that it was revered or feared. The translation is a bit ambiguous on that point. Despite what the name might imply, I believe it's a symbolic reference to its significance, not its function. It's said to have brought about an era of peace.

That sniveling little slug! Chuxu was supposed to handle this himself.\n\nWell, what more do you want to know? The farm was my egg-sister's, so it belongs to me now. A fair claim by anyone's standards, I would think.

No, but why would she need to? Of course she would want me to have the farm! All I want is to sell the damn place and move on with my life. \n\nLook, it's all I have left. That and Keema-Ru's grave-stake by the docks.

My egg-sire resigned his position after the unfortunate events surrounding the rite of passage some seven seasons ago.\n\nOne of Bhoki's students, a young Naga named Chukala, considered himself to be better than the others. Better than his training.

Chukala ignored Bhoki's lessons and charged onto the Path of the Lily like a wamasu in the hatchery. He boasted that warriors needed only their strength to win the day, not clever tricks and careful observation.\n\nUnfortunately, he succeeded.

She demanded the war-chief give her the position. You see, Chukala was her egg-brother. She wanted to honor his memory by teaching novices the things Chukala believed.\n\nThose instructions killed many novices before I intervened.

Raj-Kaal Seelan is as wise as he is cautious. He sees the problem even if tradition and decorum tie his hands and keep him from acting.\n\nIf we can provide him with a clear and viable option, I believe he will jump at the chance to grab it.

No, it doesn't. He may even order his warriors to strike us down for simply suggesting the idea.\n\nBut the war-chief respects Bhoki. I have to believe he will give us a chance. For Bhoki's sake if not for the welfare of the tribe.

My assistant is Burr. I found him half-dead in the snow while observing the local Goblin population and nursed him back to health. He's not accustomed to our cultures or manners, but his knowledge of the tribes here will be invaluable.
The Hist, in all its endless gifts, allows us to change many aspects of ourselves. Our gender is but one. \n\nI highly recommend such a change, should you ever get the chance.

Have you never undergone such a transformation, egg-sibling?\n\nThe Hist, in all its endless gifts, allows us to change many aspects of ourselves. Gender is but one. I highly recommend it, should you ever get the chance.

Exactly so. I had no time to carve another totem before the ceremony, and so the opportunity was lost.\n\nBut, thanks to your kindness, I have been given yet another chance. I erect the spine of gratitude to you, beeko. As do my future hatchlings.

Yes, Goblin expert. Is that so strange? There are thousands of High Elves devoted to studying nothing but their own genealogy. Goblins are a diverse, intelligent people found nearly everywhere in Tamriel. There is a lot to know, and I do.

Perhaps. It wouldn't be any business of yours if we did, would it?\n\nUnless … hmm. You seem to be a warrior of some worth. We may be able to come into an arrangement of sorts, if this box means so much to you.

We ran into some Blackguards on the way here. No casualties, but they did manage to nab my pack. Quite the embarrassment, truth be told.\n\nInfiltrate their caravan and retrieve my hunting bow, and I'll give you the box.
Ah. And from what Chuxu has told me, she also plans to sell the farm. Most likely to pay off the debts she undoubtedly has with such a habit.\n\nWhat of Nurhei?

And so it all comes together.\n\nPaheiza steals from her egg-sister to pay off her debt to Nurhei. The saltrice farm suffers as a result. Nurhei uses this to his advantage, and forces Keema-Ru into debt as well.

The answer is now clear. The two parties must meet.\n\nAcquire oil from both a mature bog willow and a perfumed snapper. You must keep these oils separate, of course. Give the bark oil to <<1>> and the snapper oil to <<2>>.

In Murkmire, the decision of a Shadowscale is absolute.\n\nChuxu may have sun-blessed intentions, but one cannot merely ask an eel to fly. It must be pierced by an arrow and shot upwards. This, you shall see.

It seems the midge dislikes my judgment.\n\nWeeds choke the garden, and so they are uprooted. The limb begins to wither, and so it is cut away. A sacrament is uttered, and so a life is taken. That is the will of Sithis.

I reveal my opinion. I am more traveled than my egg-kin. I see uses for all. The Naga-Kur need someone to go to the Hollow, and I think that's a good use for an outsider!\n\nJust beware Walks-Like-Thunder. It will fall on you like a toppled tree.
What? Rub oil into my scales? Whatever for?
Negotiate? Is the matter not settled?\n\nAll right. I'm not foolish enough to go against a Shadowscale's command. Besides, my words are sure to sway all present.
Oh? Not surprising. We wrote a lot of letters to each other. Paheiza would often conduct business on behalf of her egg-sister.

Just what do you think you're implying? You listen to me, mud-fish, and you listen well. My business is all aboveboard, and I don't give one lick of a toad's backside what you think you found.\n\nNow go jump in the bog.
Very well, you have earned your prize. \n\nThough the box was damaged by the hackwings, the branch within remains unscathed. I suspect a powerful magic protects it.
Negotiate? With that spineless kuuda?\n\nFine. Besides, it's about time that someone put Nurhei in his place. There's no doubt that the Shadowscale will agree with my claim.
What's this? Hmm. Smells like perfume.\n\nI'll do as the Shadowscale asks, of course. Not stupid enough to go against her wishes. And I'll attend the meeting too, make no mistake.

Oh? So you finally caught wind of the truth, did you?\n\nNurhei's the whole reason I'm like this, you know. Gave me my first bottle of skooma, free of charge! The bottles afterward, of course, were plenty costly.

Shut up! Just go away! I won't hear another word of this.\n\nYou're lucky there's a Shadowscale involved, or I'd burn down that whole farm just to spite you all. Then no one would get anything! Is that what you want? Oh, just go away!
Then stop accusing me of things you have no right to! Just … just go away!

What do you know? Who are you to judge me?\n\nIt was different before, you know. I had a life. I had a family. And now I have nothing, nothing but a muddy scrap of land that might let me finally move on from this swamp pit.

In good times, we glide across calm waters, guided by the Hist's will alone. But when the weather turns foul, we must act on our own. The most consequential moments rest at these crossroads of faith and choice.\n\nIn this moment, the choice is yours.

Good. Nothing will prevent the tribe from feeling the Hist's embrace with Jaxsik-Orrn leading the way.\n\nWhile Xukas does not make the journey with us, he still has much to do. A new tribe will gather beneath our waking Hist. Xukas will lead them.

A wise choice. Xukas has a kind heart—he will shepherd us to the next life.\n\nJaxsik-Orrn may be disappointed, but know that she still has much to do. A new tribe will gather beneath the boughs of our waking Hist. She must lead them.

In choosing Xukas or Jaxsik-Orrn, you choose what virtues my tribe carries with it to the egg of their next life.\n\nWhat virtues do you hold in highest esteem? Do you favor temperance and cunning, or honesty and courage? Let that guide your judgment.

You must leave this place. Lay our guide's body to rest near the roots of our Hist. Place the Remnant there too. With the Hist's guidance, your companion will do the rest.\n\nYou have my gratitude, Rootmender. You have proven yourself a true Argonian.
Thank the Hist. I thought it lost forever.\n\nI … I have a final favor to ask you, traveler. Would you be so kind as to bury the branch, right at the base of the Hist roots before us?

Yes, I always have. When my village's Hist Tree was burned, I was able to pry a single branch loose. I've magically preserved it for many years. \n\nIt is my only remaining connection to my village … and to the members of my tribe.

I mourned the loss of my village greatly. Every waking moment I thought of that night. The screams, the blood, the ash ….\n\nSo I chose to leave Murkmire. Still though, I carried the branch. And the memories.

Be cautious. Though the Root-House people may not be hostile, their greed runs deeper than the Hist's roots. \n\nWhile my box holds nothing of value, they'll likely use your interest to their advantage.
Tell me this: what is painted upon a blank canvas?

Precisely! These ruins represent old, foolhardy beliefs. Our people thought to be stone; immovable, unchangeable. They shielded themselves from the gift of Sithis.\n\nOnly from the blindness of the past can I make a vision for the present.

Remember that I am a weapon in your arsenal. Use the arrow I gave you to direct me against the dangerous plants as you see fit.\n\nThere will be two signal totems to ignite along this section of the Path.

No, Mewah-Jez considers Bhoki's techniques to be obsolete. A war-teacher who helps her novices only enables their weaknesses. She prefers to instruct from a distance and let her charges succeed or fail on their own.\n\nProceed with care, my friend.

In the old-time, the priests of Sithis called Nothing-Talkers were kings also. Old Shuvu told me of a place where these Nisswo-Kings would make sacrifices to Sithis.\n\nThis is that place. A city of shadows and blood. Walk softly.

I tighten my jaws. Xul-Thuxis. Something like "Snake-Means-Death City." I did not think it existed, but here we are.\n\nThe grave-singers say that Sithis priest-kings reigned here in the old-time. You should not disturb the stones if you can help it.

Not all curses kill in an instant. Some linger, like a disease of the soul.\n\nWe will not make the same mistakes. We move swiftly after Kassandra. All spirits bow to the will of the Hist, and the Hist drives us forward.

I watch the shadows. The old-ones worked magic into their building-stones. Blessings … and curses. Some xanmeers drink of the sun even now. But here, the stones are anointed with seed-oil and blood.\n\nThis city is full of killing-secrets.

I'm not sure. My head was still all fuzzy from the dream-wallow.\n\nShe kept whispering things to Whiptail—things she was learning from the staff. But she seemed frustrated. Like it wasn't telling her everything she needed to know.
Maybe? I definitely wouldn't count on that working forever, though. Kassandra's very clever. She'll find a way to twist its nature … just like she twisted mine.\n\nI can't believe I was so naive.

You're right. No use feeling sorry for myself. We have a Remnant to save!\n\nWe should talk to Xukas and Jaxsik-Orrn about our next move. Hopefully it involves getting out of here. This place, while fascinating, gives me the creeps.

The dreaming tree—the whispering root. It guided you through the dream. It guides us still.\n\nThe tree and the Remnant are one, just as the tribe and the Hist are one. But the vines that bind them are severed. Split at the root. We must mend it!
I flare my nostrils. Close—very close. Kassandra passes it by, because she cannot hear its calls—but we must find it.\n\nNo more talking! We have to find it!

In the dream-wallow, your other-self dwelt in a village of stone, with a great Hist tree at the center. The Ayleid-elves attacked the village, seeking Argonian souls at first, then the tree's secrets later.\n\nThis is the Hist that guides us.
Yes. The Remnant was born there, and it sleeps there still.\n\nI sense that the Ayleids failed to claim it. But with the power of the Sap-Speaker's staff, Kassandra may succeed.

Of course, though I am not sure if I can provide any insight. I saw only shadows and heard only whispers.\n\nThere was a sap-speaker there, yes? A Saxhleel blessed by the Hist with second-eyes and second-ears. And she gave you her staff, right?

Of course.\n\nYou are Saxhleel. You can hear the will of the Hist just as I can—in the sigh of the branches and the lapping of the water. Sap, and smoke, and grave-stakes, and chimes may help. But in the end, a willing soul is all you need.
Belief is not always easy—even for us, who feel the will of the Hist in our hearts.\n\nIf you cannot place your trust in the Hist, place your trust in me. This is your path, beeko. I know it.

A very good question. I cannot believe that friend-Famia would betray us too. Maybe she tries to change Kassandra's mind?\n\nI can tell you, beeko. I caught a glimpse of Kassandra's eyes before I succumbed to the gas. She will not change her mind.

Gone as well. His soul is shriveled and twisted like a tangle of dry thorns. He plays at being a Naga, but in his heart, he is a monster.\n\nKassandra has nothing to fear from him, but friend-Famia …. My throat goes dry with worry.

I shake my head. You expect me to describe the withered heart of some scheming lukiul? She is a savage, and the offspring of savages.\n\nI hear she complains that the Hist does not speak to her. It does not speak because she is not worthy.

I tighten my fist. In the beginning, she may have used it to force open the doors to the Hist—to make the Hist speak to her as it speaks to us.\n\nBut now? I think she means to use its power to dominate us.
It is not like the swamplands you know. Old-Sithis stalks here, and unhappy spirits watch your every move. A bad place.\n\nIf you fall here, you fall to the Void. So do not fall.

I shake my head. No. Only her tracks. I can tell you, she struggles to keep up, and turns back often. Perhaps to see if we follow.\n\nShe has the heart of a hatchling—not a betrayer. If Kassandra turns on her, she will not last long.

The war-chief is wise. Two ka-deeliths can impart more wisdom than one, provided Mewah-Jez cooperates and agrees to work with me. Otherwise, we will clash like Bhoki and Chukala did.\n\nWe can only wait and see.

I can think of no tribe that has had to weigh such a crime. There are many who would put her to death for far less, but that is not the Bright-Throat way.\n\nIf we cannot find it in ourselves to forgive, then we will forget. Exile is my answer.

Before creation, there was void. Nothing. But even nothing must change.\n\nSithis sundered the nothing, creating the possibilities of something. These ideas bloomed and faded, as all things should. As all things shall.

Each tribe has their own traditions, but there are commonalities.\n\nA tree-minder performs the ceremony before the Hist. The bonded pair are blessed with good health and vibrant fertility. And then commences the … bonding, as it were.

This varies. Sometimes the decision is based on an emotional connection. Other times, merely a physical attraction. \n\nSome tribes even use such ceremonies to strengthen their political connections. Take the Bright-Throats, for example.
I should have let the Hist take him. I should have let the Hist take all of them. It's all my fault and I can't even make it right.
I know … I know. We must find the rest.
Ah, well. I simply believe we would have very becoming hatchlings. That is all.

Thus far the killer has taken the young, the old, and the sick. The Dead-Water are fierce warriors, without mercy. None of their tribe have been counted among the Skin Taker's victims. Perhaps the murderer is a coward. I can only hope.

It's true that the Dead-Water wear skins of the dead, but only those of their own tribe. It is to honor their fallen. I can't imagine one of them killing with such cowardice.\n\nIt's a risk I'm willing to take.
She can't be! She just can't ….\n\nIf they won't accept us, I'll take her somewhere else. We'll have each other. That's all we need.
That doesn't matter. I'll love her however she is. If I have to care for her until my dying day, I will.

You think me cruel to believe so? I swear to you, it gives me no joy. One day I might even forgive Haxara for what she's done, but if there is even the smallest chance that showing her pity will harm the tribe, I will close my heart a thousand times.

Bark and birth, I nearly jumped out of my skin! Maybe I should have. It couldn't be worse than what the Skin Taker did to poor Danlai.\n\nDangled like toad jerky from a tree. Not a scrap of skin or scale left on him ….
They should go. Far away from our tribe and our Hist—from any Hist—never to trouble us again.

It's true. He was trying to tell me something, but his voice was as ragged as a broken branch. I don't know how he had the strength to speak. I couldn't understand.\n\nAll I could do was wet his tongue before he returned to the Hist.
I tell you a secret. Our egg-tenders and tree-minders use nightbloom vines for a variety of purposes, none of which I know very much about.\n\nWhen the tribe runs out, though, bad things happen.
Famine, sickness, strange weather, swarms of insects. One of those calamities. Maybe all of them. Who can say? I am not an egg-tender or tree-minder.\n\nNow go get the vines.
My name carries far these days. Why do you seek me?

There is no glory in killing a withered root and an unblooded child. This Skin Taker only preys on the weak and defenseless. Confronted by a warrior, they turned their tail in disgrace.\n\nIf we cross paths, I will not let them escape.
Would that I had killed her. When I was captured, one of the Blackguards seared my leg with a hot poker to prevent my escape. It remains difficult to run.

The Skin Taker thought the mantle of night would protect her, but it could not hide the stink of Saxhleel blood. I followed the scent to its source: a Mahleel woman. Pale skinned and darkly dressed, like a Blackguard. Two curved blades at the ready.

Our paths crossed during the night, but I saw details. The Skin Taker was Mahleel—a woman of Man. Like you, but pale skinned. The moonlight betrayed her to me.\n\nShe wore Blackguard leathers and carried two curved blades.

The Skin Taker moved under the cover of darkness, but the moonlight betrayed her. The woman had skin as pale as Veeskhleel scales. It caught the light easily.\n\nShe was dressed in Blackguard leathers, two curved blades at her hip.

Salivating! Normally, it takes me about an hour to get the ideal mix of phlegm and spit for the proper effect, but I think the anticipation has really got the juices flowing!\n\nI promise to be ready by the time you're back!
Don't bother. Savages rub their traps in poison. Got me so weak the leg started festering a few hours ago. Infection's spread to my blood. I'm a goner.\n\nJust wish it'd be over with already.

Do I look like a skeever to you? I should. Caught in a trap, diseased and half-dead. She sent me to this miserable death, so what do I owe her?\n\nShe's in an old Blackguard hideout. A cave not too far from here. One entrance, one exit, but trapped.

Was that you that stayed their blades? She was grateful for that. Dying at the hands of the same lizards that killed her husband would have been the worst way to go. Think she snapped a bit after though. Her hate for them turned into something else.

They like to catch the sea breeze blowing through the marsh to the south, along the coast. I'm sure you'll have no trouble if you follow their adorable little calls. The most talkative ones tend to be brightly colored.
No. Been abandoned awhile. Perfect place for your Skin Taker to work undisturbed. She didn't like us around when she had guests.

No, no! They couldn't hurt a fly! Well, flies are mostly what they eat … but they're perfectly docile! Maybe even a little skittish.\n\nJust scoop them into the net as gently as you can and try not to lose the net. I'd never hear the end of it.

I'm not sure. Most known Dwemer ruins lie on well-established sites. My guess is that unfinished or more recently constructed locations are harder to pin down. Fewer surviving records and the like. Something for me to look into another time.
Doesn't hurt so much now. The end must be close.\n\nJust leave me to die in peace.

The breeze brings a traveler, and newfound hope! You hold the grave-stake of Tun-Zee, an elder most kind and now departed. \n\nBut oh, how can I complete my journey? My injury hinders, and the road is long.

There is a glade within the swamp, where Tun-Zee first set eyes upon his beloved. It was there that he wished the grave-stake to be placed. As grave-singer, I must grant this wish.\n\nBut perhaps you would be willing to help?
Most of the constructs I've studied were built using similar principles, if not similar parts. We won't know until you find me suitable replacements.
Sithis is both beginning and end. The cycle which devours all, only to create it anew. So too must it be with this monument.
I beg your help in this matter most grave. Will you set right what another so cruelly made wrong?
Like nothing you've ever seen, I'll bet. It brings you right to the heart of the Hist. It really captures the smell of sap on the wind and the feel of murk-gas under your feet. Right?
Oh, well, I guess it did have a sort of boggy quality. I bet that would sound delightful in a lower key! Maybe I could score a show?

Yay! I knew the Hist wouldn't steer me wrong. I can't wait to share their songs from here to Shadowfen … or maybe I should go further! I bet there are many lukiul who miss the sounds of their homeland, if they've even heard them!

I don't believe so. Their order may be secretive about their practices, but I doubt many are so open about their … judgments.\n\nHowever, Sulahkeesh has now granted Lilmoth her wisdom many times. She will see the right path, in this I have faith.

They are memorials of lifetimes past. As the years progress, we carve our story upon the wood. Our triumphs and fears. Our laughter and follies. All must be remembered.\n\nAs grave-singer, it is my sworn duty to protect these memories.

These are Naga-Kur grave-stakes. Each represents a member of the tribe who rejoined the Hist. They do not belong in the hands of a foul necromancer. That is an abomination!\n\nI ask urgently. Recover the grave-stakes and return them to the swamp.

Like a battle cry, I lead. Like a lullaby, I soothe. Like a funeral dirge, I mourn. My song guides the souls of our departed back to the loving embrace of the Hist.\n\nIt is also I who ensures the burial rites of my tribe.

Tun-Zee possessed a kind heart and soft word for all. The Moss-Skin tribe mourned deeply when he left us.\n\nHe would often travel to the Bright-Throat Village to take place in the bonding ritual. It was during this time that he met his beloved.

Yes, though not by the thief's pale hand. \n\nJourneying through the darkened swamp, I did not realize a hackwing stalked me. In my haste to escape, I twisted my ankle upon an upturned root. It is because of this that I ask you to fulfill my duty.

A dryskin visited our peaceful village. I knew there was greed in his heart, but took little heed. The xanmeer hold many useless trinkets that we Saxhleel care little for.\n\nBut when he fled with the grave-stake, I had no choice but to give chase.

The Bright-Throats are most kind, but my tribe needs me. I'll leave as soon as I'm healed.\n\nFor now I shall look after the Moss-Skins attending the bonding ritual, though I doubt my services as Grave-Singer will be needed.

I did my job and made sure to follow the Captain's commands to the letter.\n\nCaptain Jimila appreciates a no-nonsense approach to my kind of work. I handle the rough stuff, but I never instigate trouble. I solve problems, I don't cause them.
No surprise there. I'm what the locals call a lukiul Argonian—an out-of-towner. Basically Argonians who leave the swamp and live among the dryskins, as well as those born in other regions.
Truly? You have done us another great service. For all of Murkmire, in fact.\n\nMany will ask what brought about this terrible brutality. Did you discover anything to make sense of it?
That is why the Bright-Throats advocate for mercy. We can achieve peaceful coexistence between all the tribes if we abandon the need to answer violence with violence.
I had faith that you would. What honorless toad did this? Whose kin shall we seek in retaliation?

You get a few suspicious looks from the locals—the Naga in particular. But for the most part, we're more or less left alone.\n\nHonestly, you'd be hard-pressed to find an Argonian in Murkmire who really resents much of anything.

Yeah, except for the pity everyone shows me. The locals can't imagine life away from the Hist.\n\nI'd be lying if I said there was nothing to it. Out in Alik'r, I rarely even thought about the Hist. Now that I'm here, I actually miss it. It's weird.
Then their muddied line will trouble us no more. End a battle with finality and you need only fight it once.

Baxilt-Gah wants the life energy that clings to the stakes. Powerful stuff! Provides energy for his abhorrent rituals.\n\nThe necromancer disgraces the memories of our tribe members and disrupts the natural order of the swamp. This is a bad thing.

Every Naga-Kur carves a grave-stake. The process is deeply personal and the finished stake tells the story of the carver's life. When an Argonian dies, the grave-stake marks where the body fell and serves as a remembrance until the swamp claims it.

I am a skilled hunter of the Naga-Kur. You would say Dead-Water in your tongue. Our village of ruthless warriors lies far to the north and west, in the deepest part of the marsh.\n\nThe Naga-Kur are a proud, fierce people who distrust outsiders.

I reveal a big secret. Skilled hunters use every arrow in their quiver. Even the bent and broken ones. Now the Naga-Kur need help in Bok-Xul. A perfect task for an outsider.\n\nJust beware the necromancer. Baxilt-Gah is as dangerous as a hungry viper!

Everything dies. Just some things have a habit of returning from the dead. Very disconcerting.\n\nNecromancer might come back. Who can say? Perhaps you can kill him dead-dead-dead. Doesn't hurt to try. Unless Baxilt-Gah kills you first.

Beehuna? Ah. The Root-House suitor-thief with the filthy spines. Hmm.\n\nI would give you the dowry, Xukas-friend, but I do not know where it is. The goods-keeper, Oleen, hid it to keep the Root-House thugs from stealing it again.

Gone to Gideon. Personal matter. He will not be back for many days, but do not fret! Naheesh Oleen left a reminder for himself so as not to forget the dowry's location. \n\nIt likely points to another reminder. And that to another. He is eccentric.

The Root-House people are not known for patience or wisdom. Naheesh Oleen was determined not to be outwitted by the likes of them, so he invented an impossible challenge for the suitor-thief.\n\nThe first reminder is on the post there. Hist guide you.

I don't wish to question your knowledge of such things, but it might be best if you speak with the egg-tenders before visiting the nests. They can speak to anything you would want to know about our eggs.

You'll need to look at Naheesh Oleen's reminder over there. It's certain to contain some useful hint among the antagonistic and cryptic writing. Of course, it will likely only point you to yet another reminder, but maybe eventually the dowry too.

Chief of grain-counting, box-stacking, and list-making. He keeps our storehouse in order, in his own way. He's promised to teach me his methods … eventually.\n\nFor now I sweep, carry, and keep geckos from eating our worm meal.

Oh, I—ah—don't wish to speak ill of anyone of the tribe. I only hear idle gossip from time to time. I'm told Keenam has the bad habit of speaking his mind too freely and listening poorly, but I have never heard complaint of his egg-tending.
Strange. Let me see them … oh, these are just dragonthorn. Nothing to be concerned about! Don't know how they got mixed in with the fruit, unless someone's feeling superstitious.
Well, it has many uses, but we mostly grow it for potions to aid in fruitful bonding. Our ancestors believed chewing the leaves helps the body prepare healthy eggs. Nobody really does that anymore.
Some herb. Smells sharp as the thorns. Wouldn't use it to season fruit, that's for certain.\n\nMust be one of the others. Just put it back with the rest of the food. Maybe under glass.
I'm no herbalist. If you're worried someone's trying to poison us, I promise I'm not going to eat it.\n\nI am going to get back to my drink though.
It is like I said before—I wish to keep friend-Famia safe.
Ha. So, you know about the Remnant, too? Some rumors are like willow vipers, beeko—well-hidden and best left alone.\n\nA conversation for another time, I think.

In the chilly lake we call negotiation, a good reputation is like a sturdy raft. A bad reputation is like a stone tied to your tail. Saxhleel do not drown, but it is very difficult to see at the bottom of a lake.\n\nI am sorry. This is a poor metaphor.

Yes. As the depot is sinking, the fence up against the swamp is in poor repair. There is a spot near the back of the camp where you can get in, but not out. This may be better than going in the front, yes? \n\nHere. I'll mark the spot on your map.

Poison?\n\nOh, this is dragonthorn. We mostly trade it to the Dead-Water tribe, but it's a fairly ordinary medicinal plant. Several of the egg-tenders are skilled herbalists. I don't see any reason it would be hidden intentionally.

I hesitate to contemplate that question. Bhoki warned me that the loss of so many novices would spell the end of the Naga-Kur.\n\nYou showed us a better way. If Kishi succeeds and the next season of clutch-mates survive, that will be enough for now.

Prepare this piece of the Wrathstone for transport to a safe location. You may have dealt with all the immediate threats, but it'll only be a matter of time before treasure hunters—or more Goblins—come poking around.

I expose the spine of regret. Once the Dead-Water tribe was as numerous as the fish in the streams. Now we send our dwindling number of hatchlings to die upon the Path of the Lily. It curls my scales.\n\nThe ruins remind us of more prosperous seasons.

Safer than anything we've done thus far. \n\nMoving the Wrathstone bears some risk, but leaving it here unprotected poses even more danger. I promise to take great pains to ensure its safety, and ours.

The ruins serve as a perfect killing field. Which is what will happen to Kishi if you continue to stand here and ask me questions.\n\nIf you really want to help, save my egg-son and then tell him to leave the village and never return.

Yes. Why would I not be?\n\nThings are not so simple here, beeko. Naga warriors kill, and kidnap, and steal, yes—but we are all children of the root. If the Hist wills it, Jaxsik might even kill me eventually. But she will still be my friend.

I mean, why would a civilization that could create a vault as sophisticated as this choose to fill it with such a simple object?\n\nIt's obvious that the Wrathstone is more than it seems, but answering that question will not be easy.

The markings resemble Ta'agra, but I can't read it—perhaps some lost Khajiiti dialect. The writing seems out of place, like it was added later. The imagery looks much older, but it's a style I've never seen before.\n\nWhat value was this to Dwemer?

Oh yes. Definitely.\n\nLike I said, there are no guarantees with the Dead-Water tribe. It is like dealing with one of your stray bark-dogs, I think. Scratch its chin right, it will listen. Scratch its chin wrong, it will rip out your throat.

I'm well aware. If we'd managed to secure the Goblins cooperation, we could take our time, but under the circumstances I'll need to move as quickly as I dare. Leaving the Wrathstone here unprotected is not an option.

I have the feeling I'll need to mount another expedition before the mystery of the Wrathstone is unraveled. If you'd like to see this through to the end, keep in touch. I could use capable, trustworthy help.

Disputes stem from a refusal to accept change. This creates stagnation.\n\nA stuttering tongue cannot be trusted to say what must be said. Sometimes, the words can be coaxed into being. Other times, it must be cut from the mouth.

We were business associates. I would buy her saltrice crop and sell it in far-off Senchal. The cats like to put moon-sugar on it.\n\nWhen Keema-Ru fell on hard times, I offered a loan. Unfortunately, she died before it could be repaid.

For Kassandra, all the world is a mess. She loves clean angles, good posture, fitting things snug in tiny boxes ….\n\nIt is a very dry way to live, but who am I to judge? She probably thinks I am lazy because I sleep fourteen hours a day.
As the dryskins would say, an idiot. You have but to speak to Paheiza once to see the truth in my words.

Profaning them in strange rituals that keep souls from the Hist, or giving the dead legs to wander through the murk as dreadful watchmen. They mean to poison the whole village and steal our dead!\n\nWe must find where these monstrosities come from!

People speak of the Veeskhleel as if they are monsters, but Ree-Nakal seemed warm to me. She listened to me. She understood my emptiness. She took away my pain. I trusted her more than my own egg-kin.\n\nI feel like such a fool.

No surprise there. Even so, they must understand we only mean to help! Xukas knows my motives are pure, and this Dead-Water warrior proved she's willing to collaborate when the situation requires it.\n\nWe'll win them over, I'm sure of it.
I've never seen anything like this. He's like mud packed too wet. Unable to hold its shape.\n\nI hope the Hist guides Tree-Minder Pavu toward an answer.
She is never far from the Hist, if it can be helped. That is her home, there.\n\nTake no offense if she is concerned with more pressing matters.
Tsojei is my weapon—hewn from the bones and teeth of my fallen egg-brother. Many beasts and ojels have felt its bite. Now these Blackguard savages will feel it, too.

The aloe within Vakka-Bok has great medicinal properties. It keeps wounds from festering and helps soothe burns. Our healers are unsure why the plant heals so well.\n\nPerhaps the answer lies within the power of the temple itself.

I once trained to be the tree-minder of my village. For years I learned the ways of the Hist and how to interpret its will.\n\nHowever, that fate was not meant to be. Imperial raiders destroyed my home, and burned down our Hist.
Talk? No. Tsojei shouts, always. Blood. Fear. Glory. All is meat to Tsojei.
Impatience bristles my quills. I am Jaxsik-Orrn, Dead-Water kaal. You know this already. Why do you ask me to repeat something you already know?

Xukas and I are not friends. A Naga kaal has no friends—only allies and prey. Xukas is often an ally, so he is permitted to speak in Dead-Water Village. A great honor.\n\nHe is rarely an ally in war, though. This is hewei. Odd. And also annoying.

I blink my eyes. Xukas did not tell you more? That is surprising. Xukas never tires of talking.\n\nI am a warrior. Tsojei and I hunt and kill the Dead-Water tribe's many enemies. There is nothing more to say.

I tighten my fist. Blackguards are limp-tailed savages—honorless Nagas mostly—who nest in Blackrose Prison. Cowards that value metal coins more than water.\n\nWhen they stray into Dead-Water lands, we kill them.

It's used in the mysterious ritual of renewal that one particular tribe of Argonians conducts on an annual basis. Carved from the living root of their Hist tree, or so I've been led to believe.\n\nThey won't let an outsider attend the rite without one.

That's hard to say. Mostly because no one will give me a definitive answer. As far as I can tell, it's somehow connected to the tribe's breeding practices.\n\nThe closest I got was when Many-Whispers offered to point me toward a charm. For a price.

Gold. An obscene amount, truth be told. Look, Stibbons is reliable, but he has his failings. So many, many failings. Will you accompany him to Many-Whispers in the Swallowed Grove? Help him confront the lying Argonian and get me one of those charms?
War-chief to the Dead-Water tribe. He is old and ill-tempered. He forgives when it suits him—but it suits him rarely. There are few chiefs greater than Seelan.

No. I will save these kidnapped warriors, but they will have much to answer for when they return to Dead-Water Village.\n\nIf Raj-Kaal Seelan's temper flares, they may wish they had not been rescued at all.

The dryskinned shrew? Her manservant has been bending my frill in a most unpleasant manner.\n\nUnderstand, I pointed her toward one possible location. I never said she would definitely find a charm in that puddle of mud.
You are an ojel—not of the tribe, an outsider. And your presence angers me. Outsiders wear strange garb and behave like swamp-crazed crocodiles. You are an abomination before the Hist!
Ha! You raise the spine of warning like a raw hatchling, but that's better than most outsiders.\n\nI still don't like you, though.

Lied? Not in so many words, no. I sold her hope, which she seemed to desperately need at the time.\n\nLook, if she really wants a renewal charm, I just so happen to have one. Would you like to make a trade?
You and Xukas so enjoy waggling your tongues. Fine. What do you wish to know?

The Blight Bog Sump is filled with death and decay, so there is little wonder why the mushrooms there grow abundantly. \n\nHowever, though you'll have no troubles finding that which you seek to collect, you must always be wary of the Veeskhleel.
Finally, you speak sense. Bare your fangs, ojel. The hunt begins.

I need a key. A specific key, in fact. One that opens a hidden strongbox in Gideon. My associate Mirdamir has it. Unfortunately, he died. Down in this cave, to be precise.\n\nFind the key, bring it to me, and the renewal charm is yours.
I must admit, you certainly present a more compelling argument than the manservant.\n\nOh, very well. Take the charm. And tell Lady Laurent that she has gnawed away at the good will of Many-Whispers.

Well, let me think about that. If I had just sold her the charm up front, she never would have given me gold to point her toward the mud puddle. And then you wouldn't be here, willing to negotiate another deal.\n\nNext question.

Not to worry. A deal's a deal. Here's the renewal charm that the manservant's mistress has been so anxious to get her hands on. Now you can all stop pestering me.\n\nIf you don't mind, I have a strongbox to unlock!

There is no place in the village for someone sentenced to die. Kishi must flee and go far away, or our warriors will be forced to kill him. As for me, I need to consider his words and decide what to do with my old training manual.
That is one of its purposes, yes. It would take a hundred tongues a hundred years to speak all of the Xinchei-Konu's secrets.\n\nIt is one of the few remaining monuments from our Days of Stone-Nests.

The Days of Stone-Nests is one of the many terms used to describe the period of time when the Saxhleel created xanmeer, with the foolish notion that we could build that which time would not change.\n\nWe have now learned better, of course.

The ojel sees the truth even through the fog of our traditions.\n\nThe laws of the Dead-Water refuse to bend, but in a powerful wind the tall, straight tree either weathers the storm or breaks apart. Perhaps with your help, the tribe can learn to bend.

I snarl at the audacity of outsiders. Our lives are more than just a story for you to participate in. My egg-son has forfeited his life to save the lives of others. I hope you are willing to do the same.\n\nHave your adventure. Just save my son.

I raise the spine of appreciation. Outsiders are rarely so honest and direct in their dealings with my people.\n\nWhat we value may be different, but if you save Kishi I will make sure you are generously rewarded.

He who held the title of jekka-wass before me. Now he is a nisswo, a priest of Sithis. It was Paraxeeh who taught me all I know.\n\nI cannot let him know I failed him in such a way. I simply couldn't bear the shame.
No. I was hatched in Morrowind.\n\nYou'll forgive me if I don't elaborate. It was … a very difficult time. One best forgotten. As my native egg-kin say, best to let it pass.

The antiquities market. No surprise there, I'm sure.\n\nI know I'm a bit … starchy, now. But in my youth, I was quite the explorer. I discovered several untouched Ayleid ruins and auctioned their treasures for a tidy sum.

Well, I should tell you, we've officially left the realm of verified research and entered the world of wild-eyed conjecture.\n\nIf that last ruin was Xul-Thuxis, then this next xanmeer must be Vakka-Bok—the Bowl of the Sun.
Hmm. I suppose one outsider could be permitted to take part in the ritual of renewal. Of course, the preparations required are extensive.

To prepare for the renewal rite, the ux, one must align their three primal essences—blood, bile, and mind.\n\nWith the renewal charm in hand, one must endure the bite of a hummerwing, drink the venom of a snake, and meditate beneath a waterfall.
If an outsider were to do these things and demonstrate a true desire to learn more about our culture … I would not turn them away.

You've never heard of the Bright-Throats? We're very well known in Murkmire. Our crafts are highly sought. We trade with most of the tribes. Lilmoth too.\n\nThat's why the bonding ritual is so important, it renews our ties to the other tribes.
I … I don't exactly know. I can't … can't feel my extremities … but I think I'll stay under … for a few more moments ….

A marriage, you would call it? No, a honeymoon! I think. We choose who will lay and sire the next clutch of our eggs. We Bright-Throats invite the other tribes to send envoys and bond with our tribe. Without them … it would be bad.
Of course! I'll head back immediately.
I'll limp as quick as I can, Rootmender.

The envoys were sent to Lilmoth, Bright-Throat Village, and Dead-Water Village. We hoped to both establish positive relationships and request much needed aid.\n\nThat was the plan, of course, until the Blackguards got involved.

When a new tribe is formed, it is customary for nearby villages to make offerings of aid. \n\nOur envoy was able to collect such offerings from the Bright-Throat tribe, the Dead-Water tribe, and the town of Lilmoth.

Famia didn't tell you? Vakka stones are mysterious crystals, not unlike the Ayleid welkynd stones. Our ancestors used them to store the raw magicka that falls from the sun—thus their radiant yellow hue.\n\nPowerful relics to be sure.
If an opportunity presents itself, perhaps.\n\nI suspect that some ancient Argonian relics require vakka stones to function. No doomsday devices though, I promise.

I honestly couldn't say. Most of that history was beaten out of my egg-sires by the Dark Elves centuries before I was born.\n\nSlavers take great pains to destroy our racial identity, you see. Makes us easier to control, I suppose.
You mean has the Hist spoken to me? I …. I'd prefer not to talk about that right now. A conversation for another time.

Hardly. The Ayleids treated my ancestors very poorly. I prefer to think of this as simple reparations.\n\nIn any case, my business interests are purely philanthropic now. Like Famia, I only seek to preserve Argonian relics for future generations.
I honestly couldn't say. Most of that history was beaten out of my egg-sires by the Dark Elves centuries before I was born.\n\nYou're an Argonian. I'm sure this is no surprise to you.

No. I was hatched in Morrowind—your people's homeland.\n\nYou'll forgive me if I don't elaborate. It was … a very difficult time. I don't harbor a grudge, though. Truly, working with upright Dark Elves like you is my genuine pleasure.

Hackwing hide creates leather which is both supple and strong. It allows for quick movement which also withstanding brutal attacks. \n\nWith such armor, our warriors and hunters are far more likely to survive.

The frogs are the heart of the vossa-satl! Each little croaker, when nestled in its chamber inside the instrument, adds its voice to create the melodious sound.\n\nHappy frogs produce the most harmonious and joyful sounds!

I will do you one better, actually. I have recently written a book on the subject, The Seasons of Argonia. It is right there on my desk.\n\nFeel free to have a look, and please, let me know if you have any notes.

Imagine being pampered and cared for in a safe, comfortable environment, singing alongside your closest and dearest friends. That's the life of a vossa-satl frog!\n\nEvery nest inside the instrument is warm and moist, full of mud and tasty treats.

Moss-foot croakers nest in the reeds that grow along the shore east of Lilmoth. These playful frogs have no natural predators. They eagerly greet visitors.\n\nI suggest you gather these green, little fellows first, as they are easiest to catch.
Ask and I'll do my best to answer. Partners must be completely honest with each other. Providing detailed explanations is just the mushroom on the log when it comes to total honesty.

Second, seek out the ruby hoppers. These red frogs like to sun themselves on stones around Lilmoth.\n\nApproach cautiously, however, or the ruby hopper will run. Once frightened, they often hide by the big tree at the center of town.

Sun-blessed toads. They nest in mud pits, emerging every few seasons to mate. To lure them out, make a musk out of stench sedge, salt rush, and joymallow. Find a pit that has a croak-wheel and pour the musk on yourself. Then just turn the wheel!

Ah, the indigo tree frog! Nests high up in the trees but loves the taste of fleshflies. Find the right trees, gather some insects, and release them beneath the branches. When the blue frogs hop down to feast, simply grab them!

Well, every tribe has some ritual to celebrate a fruitful union—I am told even Men and Mer have such things—but we Bright-Throats are unique in that we seek to pair those of our tribe with those of other tribes. It builds trust.
Hmm. Well, as long as it's just the fallen branches, you may go ahead.
Because it teaches us that which we cannot forget.\n\nStone crumbles. Walls break. We must bend against the force of change, least we snap against its strength.

This is the Tree that Crumbles Stones; the change which breaks down stagnation.\n\nOnce, our ancestors made walls of stone with the foolish notion that we could stop that which changes. This tree represents the futility of such thoughts.

I do not know exactly what you mean, but we do this to improve relations with our neighbors. We are better able to settle disputes, freely travel, and trade because we are all egg-brothers and egg-sisters.

Tree-Minder Pavu oversees everything, or rather she interprets the Hist's will so that we may carry it out. Our Hist has taught us this way of life and we have prospered for it. I am grateful to count myself a Bright-Throat.

Fast? Khah-khah-khah!\n\nWhy, I've known Chal-Maht since we were hatchlings. Always I have pined for him, but never was I certain he shared my affection. I only now wait a season to bond on his insistence.

I believe it has something to do with Argonian mating habits, but I'm not quite sure. Hence my desire to observe the annual ritual. I have a keen interest in the romantic tendencies of different cultures. Purely on an academic level, you understand.

He'd have me believe he's doing his job, but I suspect he's using the opportunity to daydream and dawdle.\n\nStibbons probably determined that the charm wasn't down there fairly quickly. Then he decided to relax with a soak in the mud.
I'll be … fine. I just need a strong cup of tea. Or maybe a good bottle of wine.\n\nAfter I attend to Lady Laurent, of course.

Trust isn't something that comes naturally to well-trained manservants. As far as Many-Whispers is concerned, he's taken an aggressive interest in visitors investigating objects of historical significance.
A good manservant learns how to avoid even the most unpleasant situations. It's what we do.

He's an Argonian. A scout of some kind. Knows the swamp like a bear knows honey.\n\nMany-Whispers was willing to talk to me when so many of his fellows wouldn't give me the time of day. I'm not sure Argonians can tell time, but you get my point.

I gave him a small fortune in gold! He may have sent us here in good faith, or he may have tried to cheat me. I will not be fleeced!\n\nBesides, as far as I can tell, he is the best scout in the area. If there's a charm to be had, he'll know about it.

Carved from Hist wood, our tribe uses the charm to determine who can participate in our annual rite of renewal.\n\nI wish I could tell you more, but there are some secrets even I won't divulge. I hope you understand.

My poor associate, Mirdamir. He was like a root-brother to me. He came down here and got himself killed. It's only fair that I claim his few worldly possessions.\n\nI just need to recover the key to his strongbox from his cold, dead body.

No, the ritual is sacred and not something we discuss or talk about outside the confines of the Renewal Lodge.\n\nIf you are the one to complete the preparations, you will learn about the ritual soon enough.

The ritual embodies the concept of the ux, the sacred mating practices of our tribe. Just as the plants and animals of the swamp renew their numbers with the turn of each new season, so too do we enter the lodge and renew our tribe.

Of course. To prepare for the renewal rite, the ux, one must align their three primal essences—blood, bile, and mind. This will make them open to the ritual and bind them to the renewal charm.\n\nOnly then will they be ready to proceed.

To align one's blood is to regulate one's inner currents so everything flows in the same direction. This is best accomplished by enduring the painful bite of the hummerwing.\n\nFind these insects where they nest, in hives along the shore.

To align one's bile is to engage and strengthen one's constitution. What better way then by drinking the venom of a poisonous snake and surviving the experience?\n\nFind a den of vipers in the swamp and consume a cupful of their venom.

I work with our participants for many risings of the sun to help them align their minds for the ritual, but there is a faster way. \n\nStand beneath a raging waterfall and let the sound clear all thoughts from your mind.

I am as sure as I ever am when it comes to fulfilling my duty to Lady Laurent. And with you at my side, how can anything possibly go wrong?\n\nI do wish I had a bottle of something strong and medicinal on hand. Two would be better, of course.

Oh, goodness no! That wouldn't be proper. I need to maintain my objectivity. For my readers, you understand.\n\nStibbons will prepare himself, attend the ritual, and tell me all about it. Then I will recount it in my book with scholarly detachment.

I know Murkmire. Better than most.\n\nWant some advice? Of course you do. Surviving Murkmire isn't about maps, or guides, or good manners. It's about strength. Strength to do what's necessary—all the time.
Yeah? Maybe one day you'll get a chance to show me. That could be fun.

Heh. You think I do this for the gold? Of course I don't. And neither do you.\n\nYou and me, we do what we do—rich, poor, or in-between. Don't act like you're one of these work-a-day sheep. False modesty's beneath us.
The Hist favors you, but there are other reasons. Secrets kept from a tree-minder may be less well hidden from a stranger.
You saw what I saw. Of course, when it comes to the interplay of alchemical reagents and tribal magic, anything is possible. But for the purposes of my book, let's go with the transformation theory.

Unlike many tribes, we welcome ojel to join in our bonding ritual. Through this, our tribes become true egg-kin and we enjoy peace and prosperity as one. Who would bond with us if we allowed our clutches to come to harm? In that you see my concern.

They are not suited to it. Suspicion is not in our nature. I only even consider wrongdoing because I must.\n\nI cannot turn to our allies for aid either. If they begin to view our tribe as untrustworthy or incapable, the ties that bind us would break.

It is the time when a new clutch of eggs is conceived. The egg-bearers and sires are chosen and through the bonding ritual renew the tribe. It is a significant time for any tribe, but especially so for the Bright-Throats.\n\nWe bond with other tribes.

Our bonding ritual is more than a simple ceremony, it is the renewal of our vows. To call it off so abruptly without explanation would invite questions of our commitment to our allies. I must know if my fears are justified first.

The only thing I am certain of is the Hist's grief. If the Hist tells me our eggs are suffering, then it must be so. The egg-tenders either can't or won't tell me what is wrong, so my hope is you will fare better.

The Hists' wisdom is infinite, but our ability to understand them is limited. To commune with the Hist is to see, to hear, to smell, to feel, and even to taste in a way not your own. Discerning the meaning of these signs is not a simple thing.

Never the Ghost People or Stone-Pile people, certainly. We used to see more of the Miredancers and Copper-Eyes, but we haven't seen much of them since they were taken to Mazzatun, and, sadly, the Dead-Water remain distant and reserved as always.

We are amidst the preparations for our tribe's most vital ceremony. Now a warped and withered stranger has died at our roots. An ill omen for the arrival of our guests.\n\nI am troubled, ojel, because I do not hear what the Hist is trying to tell me.

We welcome them with open arms, of course, but only after our valuables are carefully tucked away. They take what they want by quiet theft or intimidation. Failing that, they take it by force. Better to give what you can afford to lose.

The Moss-Skins value peace above all else, and peace without requires peace within. They go where the river takes them, no matter the circumstances. Of all the tribes, they are the most serene.\n\nDeath, war, lean years, nothing ruffles their frills.

Only when I'm reminded that they know every root and flower's killing secret. All the more reason to welcome them as friends, yes?\n\nYou'll find no more attentive parents outside the Bright-Throats, and they are great alchemists and gardeners also.

The Black-Tongues dwell in the shadow-places, giving praise and offerings to Sithis. They take great pains to ensure as many of their clutches are born under the sign of Shadow as possible. Perhaps too much, but I would not question their methods.

They are brutes, yes. But useful brutes when war-winds blow. Their strength rivals that of the Dead-Water tribe. They just lack the Naga's wisdom.\n\nIn the end, they are still our neighbors. Better to welcome them as friends than face them as enemies.

I am her student, and she is my teacher. One day I will commune with the Hist as she does and share its wisdom with the tribe. A great duty and also a great responsibility. You see how it weighs on her.\n\nThe hardest decisions always fall to her.

Oh no, put that from your mind! It is not a normal occurrence, I assure you!\n\nMy root-brother found that disfigured creature approaching our village. Clearly injured or ill. It died before it could cause any harm. I only meant to keep it that way.

Hmm. More indifferent.\n\nAll the world's horrors—the quiet fears that keep Men and Mer awake at night—all of it rolls off their backs. People think we Bright-Throats take things in stride. The Moss-Skins make us look like fretful ducklings.
Of course—though I hope it will not take much longer. The Bright-Throat betrothed have waited long enough already, I think. If we are to set the mood right, best to do so soon.

Yes, you understand. I would not wish that terrible fate on any of my tribe, or even my enemies! Not that I have enemies. I am very well-liked.\n\nAnd if the Hist was made ill … I dare not think of it.

There were similarities, but I question that it was Saxhleel. Maybe once, but not as the thing we saw here.\n\nMy misguided kin meant only kindness for an unfortunate soul, but that small act could carry grave consequences for our entire tribe.

It's true, Ruxol must be carried about by his bearers for most everything, but before the bonding, he is like a Saxhleel possessed. His vigor is legend. Last season's bonding ended with his bungalow stilts driven flush to the ground.
You sure? I could tell you about egg rotation …?\n\nWell, come back any time. I only ever get to talk to the other egg-tenders and it's not like they need me to tell them about what it's like.
Because they are Bright-Throats. We are shaped the way our Hist desires.

We trade it to the Dead-Water for their warriors. To give them vigor in battle, but I hear they've been having problems with reproduction, so ….\n\nI'm told there are some other—unsavory—uses, but I wouldn't know anything about that.

The Xinchei-Konu is a catalyst of needed change. Sithis is the force which causes all change. Death which leads to rebirth. Night which is followed by day. Hope that crumbles to despair.\n\nChange is not always welcomed, but it is always needed.

Vozei will then use them as offerings to the force of change. This will spark the power which resides in the Xinchei-Konu.\n\nBy returning the tablets, you merely gave Vozei the rushes and weeds. It is he who must now weave the basket.

I speculate now. Perhaps Kishi didn't want to see more novices perish due to lack of training. Or maybe his dislike of Mewah-Jez got the better of him. Or it could have been temporary insanity.\n\nRegardless, he saved us, and I am grateful for that.

True. We're also known for our social savvy, so quit trying to blow bubbles up my bog and tell me why you're here.\n\nThat busybody Iskenaaz ask you to spy on us now? I swear he'll go running to the tree-minder over the littlest thing.
What? No, that's not true! Look for yourself. These eggs are as healthy as any I've ever seen.
Mmmhmm. Poke around if you want, but I don't have time for games.
You should visit the uxith, our nest among the roots of the Hist. Perhaps the egg-tenders on duty will provide something more useful.
As you wish. I will await you here.
Then perhaps we have a traitor to the tribe! To think … it is beyond imagining!\n\nQuickly, let us check on the eggs. I pray we will find the truth before something terrible happens!

They returned to the Hist. It happens to a few eggs in almost every clutch. Sometimes the Hist just doesn't believe it's time for a soul to return. The Hist takes them back and we focus our efforts on nurturing those intended to hatch.

No!\n\nI can't believe even the tree-minder is being paranoid about the upcoming bonding ritual. These eggs are going to shine like gems when the envoys arrive. If everyone would stop fussing over us!

Everything changes. The Path, the ka-deelith. Training changes, too. And expectations. Now novices die more quickly than new eggs can be hatched. Soon, the Dead-Water tribe will simply be the Dead tribe.\n\nI think that's why Kishi dislikes Mewah-Jez.
What …? No. No, no, no, no. That can't be. It can't!\n\nI—I have to go.
It was a long time ago, traveler. Still, that memento is all that I have left. I'd be most grateful if you could help me retrieve it.
Because there's nothing to return to, I'm afraid.\n\nImperial raiders attacked my tribe. They slaughtered many, and … and burned down our Hist Tree. I've been a wanderer ever since.

A tribe's connection to its Hist is sacred. One cannot exist without the other.\n\nSo I felt as long as I had this branch with me, my tribe could never truly be gone. A silly thought, perhaps, but one that has kept me going.

In the past, I couldn't bear to call anywhere home. And so I only wandered.\n\nBut now I have finally found my way back to Murkmire. Today I shall be welcomed at the Bright-Throat Village, and become a member of their tribe.

It belongs to my uxith-beeko—my bonding ritual partner.\n\nHe is a fine specimen, so I had to make sure to steal something of great worth. The hunting bow you seek has been passed down through his tribe for generations.

Most Argonians in this area think nothing of the ruins that dot the landscape. But some, like the Ree-An-Wo—er, the Swallowed Grove—have a reputation. It's not quite as strict as a taboo, but similar.

Of course. How else would I prove myself a worthy companion?\n\nThat's why this theft stings so greatly. For the Blackguards to steal that which I had already rightfully stolen? Such an embarrassment.
Yes, it's most strange. Who would care so deeply for an old, burnt branch?

I've carried this branch for many years. It was the only piece of my old home that I had left. No family, no friends. Just a reminder of what once was.\n\nBut now I have a new village, a new home. The time has come to put the past to rest.

I know nothing of the visions of the Dead-Water, or the starblossom they use. I have undergone the Bright-Throat's version, however.\n\nI recall very little. My shell-brothers found me trying to sell a wamasu a clutch of eggs I stole from a haj mota.

Many places, though I spent most of my years in the friendly cities of Elsweyr. It was there that the name Hands-That-Heal was gifted to me, due to my magical skill.\n\nAnd then, after many long years, I made the choice to come home.
I simply realized how greatly I missed my homeland. The thought of dying on foreign soil, away from the roots of the Hist, was too sad to bear.\n\nAnd so, here I am.
Oh, yes, of course. It's a large branch, burnt and withered. It, well … it belonged to my village's Hist Tree, you see.

I served as the tribe's war-teacher before I was replaced. That old book contains my training methods—techniques that worked well until they didn't. When Mewah-Jez changed everything, novices started to die.\n\nBut tell me, why do you care?
Remnant of …? What are you talking about, Mateem?\n\nOh, I see. Another of your jokes? A name like that must be made up.
Precisely! And it is only because of that nothing that something can be made. First, there is nothing. Then, there is something. \n\nThus is the will of all things. Thus is the will of Sithis.

Sithis is the nothing between the something. The void which created all, and will one day destroy it. The will of change, the inconstant which is our only constant.\n\nMy art honors this will. I destroy what was, and create what will be.

It is often easier to clip a withered branch for the sake of the whole tree, but with thought and care a troubled limb can regain its strength.\n\nHaxara and her daughter are broken boughs, but they may yet be mended if we make the effort to heal them.
No, far more than art! An offering. Once, we feared that which Sithis whispered. Now our tongues shall speak the words.\n\nQuickly, grab a hammer from the storehouse!
That which must change, will change. Hesitation only leads to stagnation, which disregards the will of Sithis.\n\nDo not falter! Strike now, quickly and true!

No one knows. Perhaps it was Sithis who crumbled our stone hearts. Perhaps it was the Hist, who longed for our company, for the patter of our feet atop their roots.\n\nBut the Days of Stone-Nests ended, as all things must end. As all things will end.

We worship the change which it wills to be!\n\nOnce, we thought to shield ourselves from this blessing by becoming stone. We built monuments to Sithis, not out of reverence, but out of fear. "Do not change us!" we cried. "Do not let us die!"

I wished to transform the echoes of our past follies into our serene reverence of today. But, one day, that too will change. Our belief, our culture, our people. All will change, for it must change.\n\nAnd then all will be nothing once more.

I belong to the Clutch of Nisswo, a fellowship of sorts. \n\nIn the dryskin tongue we would be called "nothing-speakers," for we speak the words of that which is void. Though we do not all speak the same words, of course. Why would we?
Sithis is a being of multitude. It is the will of change, the force of chaos, the lust for bloodshed. Its words are many, and so the nisswo are many.\n\nBut we all speak parts of the larger truth.

The greater the offering, the greater the honor. Some would sacrifice a scale or a fang, freshly plucked and bloodied. Others would offer fingers or the tips of their tails. \n\nOne follower offered his heart. He died, of course.

Perhaps an example will help. I honor Sithis through my art. I see the something within the nothing, and create it. Through my actions a lesson is learned.\n\nMy mentor had a different approach. She would require offerings of blood.

One must simply be accepted as a voh-vastei. An apprentice, in the dryskin tongue.\n\nI journeyed with my mentor for many seasons before she bestowed the title of nisswo upon me. Then I journeyed alone, spreading the dark word to many tribes.

The Saxhleel do not require ease in our beliefs. We do not write words upon a page and request our followers to speak its unmoving words.\n\nBelief should be questioned. Doubted. Judged and finally accepted. Only then is it truth.

I speak but one truth.\n\nThrough many seasons, this village will hear many words. It is from these many words that they will create their own truth. And though these truths will be different, they will all be, in the end, true.
Out in the marsh, I'm afraid. I sent a few of my best people to gather the stones for me and agreed to meet them later. With your help, it shouldn't take long.\n\nCan I count on you to accompany me?
Yes. As grave-singer, I must ensure this final burial rite is enacted. That is why I traveled to this village, despite my injury. To fail in this task is to disgrace the memory of Tun-Zee.
It is like the sap of our Hist, but somehow perverted. I would not envy the unsuspecting Saxhleel who licked this tree. This may explain the poor souls who came to die at our roots.
The Hist's sap is what makes a Saxhleel a Saxhleel. It is how the Hist shapes us to its needs. But if the Hist's will was twisted … so too would be the Saxhleel.
No, no, no. You're telling me these creatures … they came from our eggs? I thought I was prepared for the worst, but this—this is abomination!\n\nI must warn Pavu! She will know what to do.

Old Shuvu spends his time in the Glade of Chimes, to the west of the village. In my youth, I would spend all my time listening to the chimes. It is a very good place.\n\nIf you go there now, I will join you.

Remnant of … my, my. This is no small question, Xukas-friend.\n\nLook around you. Each of these chimes sing out a tangle of melodies, but only one tangle. One chime speaks of eggs and hatching. Another jangles about death and journeys' ends.

Ha! The ojel is clever, Xukas!\n\nYes. My hands gave birth to every chime you hear. But the Remnant? Only one chime can sing its truth. One made by sun-blessed hands in an old time. Older than my egg-mother's egg-mother. A chime as old as our tribe.

Locked away. Hidden under mud and lost memories.\n\nUnderstand, our egg-sires did not want this truth drifting free on the wind. But Xukas trusts you, so I will trust you. Go to the Wither-Vault. Claim the chime. We will learn its truth together.
No. Is that what you want to hear me say? That I was stupid. Foolish. Pathetic! I know it …! I can never forget it.
I've tried, but her concerns are always pointed outward. She must think of the good of our tribe. My desires are small compared to the needs of diplomacy.

They don't feel the way I do. How can they? They have been chosen for the bonding ritual.\n\nEvery day I tend to children that aren't my own. I love them, I really do, but it's not the same. They don't understand.

Hist be praised!\n\nTake the chime to the Listening-Tree, and hang it there. When you are ready, clutch this prayer-stone and focus. If your cause is just, the Hist will answer. If not? I guess we have to find a better place to bury this chime.
Her memorial, of course.\n\nWhen a Saxhleel dies, their lives are honored with the carvings on their grave-stakes. If you're so curious about who my sister is, why don't you go look for yourself?
I'm afraid I cannot.

Precisely. I cannot tell you of a sight unseen.\n\nHowever, I do believe it is connected to Tun-Zee and his memories of that place. He would often tell the story of first seeing his beloved under the leaves of a tree.

Perhaps the Hist grew the tree to honor his memory. Or perhaps it grew from the sorrow of our tribe, who still miss him greatly. \n\nPerhaps Tun-Zee's spirit resided within that grave-stake, creating the tree once his last wish was granted.

We do not think this is something spawned from our nest-bed. This is not how Saxhleel resolve their differences. Even Black-Tongues would not torture someone they intended to kill. It would not serve the Hist.\n\nIt must be someone beyond their roots.

Very well. I do hope you will exercise caution. The Blackguards are not particularly bright, but what they lack in intellect, they make up for in brute strength.\n\nOur friend, Xukas, for all his many virtues, is not a warrior.

No, but Chukala challenged Bhoki. Said he was weak and unfit to teach warriors. They fought, and the commotion attracted the predators that prowl the Path.\n\nChukala and the novices were killed. Bhoki was injured. He resigned in shame after that.

Yes, I'm familiar with Jaxsik-Orrn. A very proud warrior. Hopefully not too proud. If we have common cause with the Dead-Water tribe, it only makes sense to cooperate.\n\nCompromise and collaboration rest at the very heart of all great endeavors.

I would not be surprised if the Skin Taker was among the Blackguards, but even they are rarely so meticulous in their violence. It takes patience, a steady hand, and a stone heart to skin something alive.

So, she was in league with them the whole time? That dries my scales. In small numbers they pose little threat, but with a mind like Kassandra's and the Remnant in hand ….\n\nMaybe Jaxsik already killed them all and I worry without cause?

The village the Hist showed you in the dream-wallow, maybe? Old Shuvu told me of a village in the Deepmire. But to reach it, we must traverse the Snake-Means-Death City—Xul-Thuxis.\n\nI wish it were not so, but we have little choice. Let us go.

I … I would not wish to do that, Rootmender. A tree-minder's connection to their Hist is sacred. We do not simply obey our Hist, or listen to its words. We revere it. We are a part of it.\n\nWhen my Hist died … so too did a part of myself.

I simply wish for this village to prosper. That is all.\n\nFor many years I have searched for a new home, never truly knowing what I was searching for. But now I realize I was looking for a fresh start. A new beginning.

Murder, apparently. The victim is … was Heetzasi. A former associate. Not so pleasant or learned as Famia, but still useful in his own way.\n\nHe traveled in less reputable circles. I had hoped he could shed some light on the Blackguards' plans.

That is what we are trying to determine. Whatever happened, it was neither clean, nor brief. What a waste.\n\nIf the Blackguards came after him, Heetzasi must have known something about the Remnant after all. Look around and see what you can find.

The Vakka-Bok was thought to be used by our ancestors to honor the sun. I suspect that some of the sun's arcane power still lingers, giving the aloe its curative properties.\n\nThat is only my suspicion, though. We know very little of the xanmeer.

It sounded like he was saying "Hist." I think he wanted to be returned to the roots before the end.\n\nThat's not much, is it? Maybe Sulosya would know something more useful? He found one of the other victims.

So, the Blackguards have learned what we already know. The truth of the Remnant cannot be torn from my egg-kin because they do not know it. Only their tribal relics can provide the answers.\n\nHow did you learn the Bright-Throat's riddle?
Potentially. First, however, we must clear the xanmeer of it's current dangers. No easy task, as I'm sure you well know.

You see? The voice of the Hist needs a conduit—some physical means of communication. \n\nThe Blackguards failed to acquire the Bright-Throats' chime, but they clearly mean to steal some relic from the Dead-Water tribe. Bold. Or spectacularly stupid.

Precisely. You know one of the tribe's kaals, don't you? Jaxsik-Orrn, if I recall correctly?\n\nFind her, and plead our case. If the Dead-Water tribe has some way of learning more about the Remnant, we need to find it before the Blackguards do.

Yes, with the ultimate goal of reaching the signal totem and igniting it to show that you have completed the first challenge.\n\nTake this arrow and point it whenever you want me to use my bow. Are you ready to begin?
