With what I've done? I don't know. My heart is so heavy it would sink into the black murk, if not for this small mercy the Hist has shown me.\n\nIf I can be a good mother to her, then it won't have been for nothing.
No, I am lucky to have her. She's my reason for being.
He's a Dead-Water tracker that comes through our lands to trade his game. Very skilled, so far as I'm aware. I'm sure he would spot a hundred things that I missed upon finding Danlai.
Well, I'm not letting him out of my sight the next time he passes through, if it's all the same to you.
I'm sorry …?\n\nOh! Oh, sacred sap! He does! Some of the finest pelts and hides we buy are his handiwork. You don't think some were Saxhleel?

Oh, do not get your tail in a twist. Zadaza is not mad—just disappointed. This one was moments away from mounting a daring escape when you arrived. The stuff of legends!\n\nStill, we work with Famia. Zadaza will get another chance before long, yes?
What is hope? Change untended. Squandered and left to molder before the eyes of the weak and foolish.\n\nHope did not give me this life, nor did it spare it.

I am lukiul, born outside the swamps of Black Marsh. There are many subtleties of the Saxhleel language that I am not familiar with, body language most of all.\n\nDoes she scorn me? Does she tease? I have no idea.
You obviously do not understand what it is to fall in love. Leave me be.

Bet your arse! It's still full of things needing a good crack in the jaw and I haven't bashed heads in months! \n\nXode says we've got to go to Lilmoth and get help, but soon as I grab some decent grub, I'll be back. No fun bashing on an empty stomach.

Though dead, the husk of the old ways still hangs over our temple. We three will go to Lilmoth and beseech the tribes to help Sithis cast off these remnants.\n\nIf their warriors scour our temple clean, we will return.
It is a Shadowscale custom. The oils help separate those who cling from that which they cling to. In this case, a dispute which has lasted far too long. \n\nHave patience. Soon, all will be clear.

I know that, if mishandled, it could lead to something very dangerous.\n\nSo, I would appreciate it if Famia stayed safe at home, for a time. It has been many long hours since my last sun-doze, after all, and I try to limit my rescues to one per day.
Perhaps. But it would not have been the Shadowscale way.

They broke my arm in three places, tied me to a raft, and sent me head-first down Hukep Falls. Luckily, I'm a strong swimmer!\n\nI'm casting them in a very poor light. Honestly, if you can see past the idle cruelty, they're really quite pleasant.

Well, one of my expeditions took a brief detour into Dead-Water territory. They took us as hostages almost immediately.\n\nI tried to impress upon them my deep love and admiration for Argonian culture ….

Hostile? Well, I mean … they're certainly aggressive. But hostile has all kinds of connotations I'd rather avoid.\n\nWhat matters is they react with violence to practically any intrusion. For instance, they abducted me once about a year ago.

The Nagas are a breed of Argonians. I guess breed is the term? Sounds a bit offensive, doesn't it? Oh dear. Let's just say they're a different kind of Argonian.\n\nThe Dead-Water tribe is a Naga group, but tribeless Nagas wander all over Murkmire.
Honestly, I'm …. Are you sure you want me to bring you into this? Eshraf and Dinia only knew its name, and now they've probably been kidnapped!
More than one. Choglada, impaled on a pole near here. Zuti, hanging from a tree near Lilmoth. On display like dread warnings. They are pitiful trophies.

Very well.\n\nAs I said, no one really knows what the Remnant is, but it's just … it's just everywhere. Tree-minders whisper about it when they think no one's listening. It's tucked away in poems and songs. It's always there. Just below the surface.

All the folktales imply that the Remnant shares a deep connection with the Hist, but the rest is pretty murky.\n\nSongs about the Remnant almost always end with a hero plucking it from the roots of a tree and ushering in a new golden age. Others ….

Like I said, people think it's just a legend, so they ignore it. But once serious scholars like us start asking questions—start making those first quiet discoveries—all the opportunists crawl out of their holes to take their nibbles.
I will go nowhere without my heart-rose! I will only fight with Honei at my side!
We were separated in the attack. I cut down three invaders, but lost Honei in the smoke.\n\nShe is hiding somewhere, I think. Or injured! Please, Mateem, help me look for her!

Too clean, for one. Very little skin was left clinging to the muscle below. The Skin Taker works slowly. Their technique is one of cruelty, not efficiency. It could not be done safely in the field. This Skin Taker has a den.

Appearances, beeko, appearances! Jimila travels the world and has refined tastes! One cannot simply walk up to her and offer their wares like a wandering merchant! No, we must make a good impression.\n\nAnd to do that, I need you to serve as my envoy.

Of course! Outsiders respond better to people they see as important.\n\nWe're partners. Equals in this endeavor. Serving as my envoy is for appearances only. It makes us both look good and improves our chances to secure a deal with the Captain.
She … she did not …?\n\nOh, no. No, no no. We were going to travel. To visit root-kin, near Gideon. She cannot be dead. I do not believe you!
I made this for her. She would never let it fall from her wrist. She … she really is gone.\n\nPlease, leave me. Help the others. I need to be alone.
The Ghost People. Saxhleel with both twisted forms and morals.\n\nThey take our dead and feed it to their Hist. There's even rumors that they practice the dark art of necromancy. A repugnant tribe.

You have worked with the legendary Khajiit sea captain? Beeko! The sun truly shines on me today!\n\nEven so, I do not want a deal that's purely dependent on her good will toward you. We need to prove that I'm a worthy trade partner.

It would be easier to catch fish with Kazrala's claws than this feeble stick. \n\nThe fish are so quick! This one does not know how the lizards do it. Is there some secret technique that she is missing?

Intriguing. Deals keep bringing me back to this swamp, after all. So many captains consider Lilmoth to be beneath their notice, but their loss is my gain.\n\nVery well, speak. What's your proposition?
Vossa … what now? \n\nTell me more, envoy. What is this contraption and why should I care?
Hmm. The sound of home. Yes, I can see the profit in that. I'd target tavern owners with Argonian clientele. But what sort of instrument is this? I've never seen anything like it.

I think what you just said will make more sense after another couple of drinks. Still, it's exotic, I'll give it that. And I love a good challenge.\n\nVery well. Tell Nesh-Deeka we have a deal. Let's start with five of these and see how they sell.

They were most likely in the wrong place at the wrong time. The Blackguards are well known for kidnapping Saxhleel and demanding ransom from their tribes.\n\nBut such a ransom, should it come, would be impossible for our village to give.

It started with Domitia Nasica. She oversees the Dragonstar Caravan Company's affairs here in Murkmire.\n\nWe made a bargain—a land deal. I negotiated in good faith, but she was lazy and inattentive, and so missed key details.

Yes.\n\nShe and her trade-kin arrived during the dry season. She told me that they wished to build a trade depot on the fen-island south of Lilmoth. I agreed to lease the land in exchange for the return of some treaties her company acquired years ago.

I paper the walls of my home with evidence of dryskin treachery. That is a joke.\n\nDocuments hold power in the ojel world—especially old documents. Taken alone they are mostly worthless. But combined with threat of conflict, they can be useful.

For Domitia? Yes.\n\nThe island flooded, as it always does during the wet-knee season. She grew furious, called me a swindler. Now they throw rocks at me any time I stray near the depot. Luckily, I am very swift and they are very stupid.
Ojel—people who do not speak the root's tongue. A kinder word for outsider. Well … not so kind in some circles. The Dead-Water tribe uses this word like a knife.

Has it been so long since you licked the tree, egg-kin? Ojel. People who do not speak our root-tongue. A kinder word for outsider.\n\nWell … not so kind in some circles. The Dead-Water tribe uses this word like a knife.

A seed doll, representing an invitation for our tribe to join their bonding ritual. \n\nThe Bright-Throats use their bonding ritual in order to ensure a peaceful relationship with their neighboring tribes. It is a great honor to be accepted.
A hunting bow, symbolizing an offer of protection. \n\nThe Dead-Water tribe is filled with great warriors. With so many dangers surrounding our tribe, we cannot afford to lose such needed aid.

Though Lilmoth may be without a Hist, they are still sympathetic to our plight.\n\nThe town has gifted us a wooden bowl, symbolizing the offer of food for our table. This offer may be the most important of all, for our food stocks run dangerously low.
They did not take my eyes or hands, so I am still of some use.\n\nDead-Water are no strangers to pain. Our medicines are strong. I will recover.
Not one of ours. That's all I can say for certain. We await members of the other tribes to account for their missing. With the body lost to the Dead-Water pool, there is little else to be done.
A possibility. The Blackguards have sent brutal messages in the past, but they were clear with their intentions. This Skin Taker has kept her identity in shadow.

Hackwings travel in large flocks, and have the tendency to swarm once threatened. They strike quickly, knocking their prey down before ripping them apart.\n\nThat's … not very useful, is it? My apologies, Rootmender. I am not much of a warrior.
Hmm. Hands-That-Heal, Hands-That-Heal …. A healer, you say? Hmm. Tell me, does he carry a burnt branch with him?

You must be speaking of Heek-Betu. We traveled together after our village was attacked, but he quickly decided to leave Murkmire. I've always wondered how he fared.\n\nIt sounds like you've helped him greatly. For that, I thank you.
Perhaps I shall. It has been far too long since last we spoke. But first, I must ensure the Root-Whisper Village prospers. With your help, of course.

I've been researching the mating habits of the indigenous races. Fascinating stuff! I plan to write a book.\n\nA reference to an Argonian ritual of renewal I came across intrigued me, but the details were vague. So we traveled here to investigate.
My mate. She went into the swamp to search for her egg-sibling.\n\nI must wait and watch for them to return.

Many risings and fallings of the sun and moons. And I will continue to wait until they return or the Hist calls me home.\n\nThat is what it means to be part of the Dead-Water. My mate would do the same for me.

Hah! Is that what they're calling her? Julitta is the horking Skin Taker! Mud-lizards slit her mother's throat after taking her prisoner. Who's going to miss a slaver, right?\n\nBet Julitta knew they'd be prepared this time. Had me take the fall.
Playing errand boy for a mad woman. Stumbled into this trap looking for her damned mother's knife. Didn't think it wise to refuse her. Julitta's been unhinged since she got murdered.

On a fool's errand. Blundered into this trap while rooting through the muck for Hostia's damned knife.\n\nShe knew the Argonian's would be prepared this time. Probably sent me to get killed and throw them off her trail. Snowback wretch.

Why, whatever do you mean? I'm quite sure that if anything untoward happened to my manservant, I'd be the first to know.\n\nBesides, Stibbons may seem frail and sluggish, but … hmm. I have no idea where I was going with that line of reasoning.

You mistake a show of strength for hostility. While others of the marsh have lost their way, the Naga-Kur—who you call Dead-Water—hold fast to ancient traditions and customs.\n\nWhat you call inhospitable, we consider prudent.
The marsh is brutal and dark. The strong eat the weak here. The Naga-Kur decided long ago that it was better to eat than be eaten.\n\nI have said all I'm going to say on this subject.

I did. Hostia was a strange one. She was cold as ice when it came to the lizards, but she'd return to camp smiling for her daughter. Father was long gone.\n\nRumor was he got executed by one of the tribes and they had to watch. Her too now. Figures.
And you as well, my friend. I appreciate how you always seem to show up when m'lady needs you the most.\n\nIf you would be kind enough to lend your assistance again, she'd be most appreciative.

I wouldn't tell that to Julitta when you see her. Maybe I would. Lunatic's the reason I'm going to die with a damp ass.\n\nI don't know your part in all this, but she's never going to stop. Might as well finish what they started.

You spared her life, she was grateful for that, but the mud-lizards? They would have cut her throat without a second thought. Just like they did to the father of her child, or so I heard. Rumor was Hostia and her daughter had to watch.

I cannot afford to squander the fair season. I have many traps to lay before the bog-eels root their way into deeper muck. If you have need of travel by sea, there are many sailors in Lilmoth, but that you likely know.
It is when one of those interested parties happens to be m'lady Clarisse Laurent!\n\nBut you'll see what I mean when we get to the Swallowed Grove. Just head north and I'll meet you there.

He was a Blackguard. Had to be guilty of something. Doubt that made much difference to her.\n\nShe's always had an ax to grind, but I wager the blade at her throat brought back some bad memories. They crossed a line they can't step back from with that.

In our tribe, it is traditional for the female to initiate such relationships. And even though I now take such a form, I suppose old habits are hard to forget.\n\nBut at least we are together. What a sun-blessed day this is.
Some for roasting, some for skinning, some for their eggs. We find many uses for them. Me, I prefer the roasting. Eel-leather is very supple, but I love the way it crisps over an open flame.
Me? I have never been better! It's bonding season! I mean—I, uh, I'm not … I'm not planning on it myself, but my head swims like a mudskipper so who knows where my night may lead!
Bee-ears! I do not know how the Nords make brew from such things, but I like it! I should have Vetra-Jat ask her guest about getting more. Perhaps she will accept weevil eyes in trade?

The whole tribe is filled with nothing but thieves. I can't believe they even get away with it! The other villages should have put a stop to them long ago.\n\nAnd now here I am, an innocent traveler getting robbed blind!

You're right. I'll never get this lizard to agree to common morals.\n\nI just have to find some guards! That's what I'll do. I'll go to the nearest town and find someone who will help me bring him to justice!

Exactly! Do you know how many relics I had to sell to earn that gold? How many xanmeers I had to scour, how many traps I had to dodge?\n\nBy all rights, that coin purse is mine! I refuse to be intimidated like this!

This bard asked to sing the tales of my people. Though my eyes narrowed, I allowed such a thing. But now she has changed the words!\n\nThe words must be the steady beat of a hunting drum, not flowers to be enjoyed!

She says our tales are too plainly spoken, and so the bard turns blood to rubies. How can she speak my people's stories, when her own tongue is coated in such honey?\n\nI will not let her twist our words to suit the palate of her own people.

For long I have searched the swamps for the tales of Murkmire's past. Unfortunately, such a topic is of little interest to most of the Argonians living here.\n\nBut, at last, my search came to a joyful close. Or so I thought.

To steal implies that the purse is not mine.\n\nTo the Root-House people, that which is needed is provided by our Hist through the actions of others. I needed the gold that the dryskin carried. The Hist saw that it would become mine. Simple.
You make a good point. Fine. I will return the coin purse. There is no need for further threats.

I've seen this kuuda in Lilmoth. His purse only grew heavy with coin by selling the relics of Murkmire. He took from the land of my people. Why should I not take from him?\n\nThe Hist has provided that which I need. I have no reason to not accept it.

It is Dead-Water make. But a Dead-Water Naga would never give up a weapon willingly.\n\nPerhaps the Blackguards try to abduct Dead-Water warriors, too? I cannot be sure. I have heard nothing, but the Dead-Water tribe never admits weakness.

I have sung the ballads of warriors and battles, of carnage and death and mayhem. It is not the subjects Ereel-Jush speaks, but the crude way he speaks them. \n\nYet he refuses to let me change the words to be more refined.
You have my gratitude, kind traveler. I shall do my utmost to convince him to allow me to change the words.

I suppose that is true. If I'm to respect the traditions of Murkmire, I must respect its people. And that should start with agreeing to Ereel-Jush wishes.\n\nVery well. I shall sing the words just as they are told to me.

I doubt there is a hatchling alive who has not heard some version of the tale. After all, it is not often that a Hist chooses to slumber.\n\nTo think that the gentle soul who helped me so greatly would become the Rootmender!
And you as well, Rootmender. May you always prosper under a blessed sun.

I am well. The Bright-Throat tribe has been very welcoming to this old traveler. Of course, I try to help when I can with my healing skills.\n\nAh, but I talk too much. I'm sure you have many others to greet.

How was I—what do you mean, how was I swindled? I already told you.\n\nI'm expected to pay for bug filled linens and treks through the swamp? I was told that I would be exposed to the beauty and mysteries of Murkmire! And that was not delivered.
Yes. I thought you didn't want anything to do with me, like the others.

Ah, well, I of course plan to explore the village myself. A book can only tell you so much.\n\nI wonder if the Xinchei-Konu could be of some help to the new tribe? I must consult Paraxeeh as soon as I am able.

Hmm. Very well. If she sings only for her people, I will allow the bard's flower words.\n\nBesides, if outsiders hear the tales as we speak them, their soft-bellies will grow sick. Perhaps it is best that these songs be drenched in sweet waters.
Tough? Ah, like the hackwing which must be chewed slowly. Yes, the situation is tough.

No—I know. I just … expected you'd keep your distance. I'm glad you came. I didn't really get to thank you for helping me. You're the only reason I have my daughter. You gave me a second chance. I will never forget that.
And you as well. Oh, and do tell me if you stumble across any new texts!

Well, he has not stolen the tablets again, if that's what you're asking.\n\nAnd I truly have been making an effort to explore more of Murkmire. Why, traveling here was an adventure in itself! I was nearly killed on at least three separate occasions.
What? You really think she would do that? What am I saying, of course she would! She's a lizard after all.\n\nOh, very well. I'll pay.
Well, no. But it's common sense that I should be offered these things. Why, they laughed in my face when I asked for a carriage!\n\nI'm not satisfied, and I'm not paying. And that's that.

At the moment? I am pleased by your actions. \n\nThat will change of course, as all things must change. But for now, I shall bask in the pleasure of your company, like the carrion bird basks in the sun after filling its belly with decaying meats.
May the ways of Sithis guide your path, Rootmender.
Oh, yes. The Naga have many traditions, and so it will take many words for their hearts to accept the change that must be.\n\nPerhaps your actions here today will help them see that.

An agent of change, I suppose you could call it.\n\nI'm curious, though. You have gone through many hardships to awaken this Hist. Many are now lost, including your own ally. Tell me … was it worth it?

I'm sure many would agree with you. Of course, many would not.\n\nBut it is never up to us to decide if change has worth. Sometimes what is most needed is also most feared. The Shadowscales have always known this truth.
So you understand.\n\nThe worth of change is not for us to decide. What must be will be. Our Brotherhood has well prepared us for that truth, no matter how dark a truth it is.
Understandable. Much has been lost.\n\nStill, change comes upon us whether we wish it to or not. Always remember to keep your eyes on the path before you, lest you stumble.

My lady over here offered to pay me to guide her through Murkmire. I've done my best to accommodate her, of course. Her bedroll has clean linens, our food is freshly prepared.\n\nYet she spits in the face of my hospitality with her demands!
You are right. The longer I spend here arguing, the less time I have to offer my tours to those who truly wish for them.\n\nI will take her to Lilmoth and be done with it.

She complains about the insects, about the mud, about the heat. This is a swamp!\n\nThe dryskin even demanded she ride in a carriage. A carriage? Through a swamp? I have never heard of such ridiculousness in my life!
Sublime, my Brother.\n\nHmm. You are a long way from the Gold Coast. If you seek aid, look for another in our order. I have been entrusted with a Sacrament.
And you as well, Sister.
And you as well, Brother.

Dryskins call it hip and tail ball. Two teams of five pass a ball with only their hips, elbows, or tails. When the ball hits the opposing team's mud wall, a point is scored. \n\nAnd then, of course, there are the two reed hoops.
If you are so willing, then by all means.
Well, the basics of the game are, yes. But without knowing all the rules, one can never hope to truly succeed in playing such a sport.\n\nWhy the Wood Elf even wants to play, I do not know.
It's this hip and ball game. I've tried to understand it, but there's just too many rules for me to follow.
You toss souls to the Void like grain to fowl. Some call me ku-vastei, but you—you're more like a flood.
Ah ha! All right, I think I have it now.
I see. Yes, that sounds about right!
I don't want to play without even knowing the basics.\n\nSay, you seem like a reasonable sort. Perhaps you know a little something about this sport? Just the most important rules, plainly spoken.
Yes, perhaps one day I shall. I simply must keep hope. If I can find a way to return to my homelands, I can find a way to win the heart of the one I love.

What about Haxara? Let the Veeskhleel take her for what she's done …! I'm sorry. I did not mean that. They'll kill her, or worse. Haxara will have to face judgment for her actions, but it should be the tribe's judgment.\n\nDo you hear that?

Not very well, if you ask me. Here in Murkmire, the war efforts are nothing more than stories told by sailors. Why risk your hide for something that you can't even see?\n\nBeing sent here was a fool's errand.
Busy as ever, of course. Until Imperial City is ours, the Ebonheart Pact will not rest.\n\nI'm here as part of a new Murkmire recruitment effort. We could always use more Argonians joining our ranks.

Oh, is that right? Well, you're lucky I'm under orders to keep this a peaceful visit. Elsewise, you'd end up on the end of my blade.\n\nI do hope to meet you on the battlefield, though. Killing you would be such a pleasure.

What kind of hostess would I be if I didn't make sure you were having a pleasant stay? Most of our guests don't take as much interest in the politics around here as you seem to. I'm surprised you can make heads or tails of it.

Who doesn't like a little peace and quiet? I've been known to silence the occasional noisy pest making a racket, when the situation calls for it.\n\nJust because no one's in charge, doesn't mean no one's guiding the group.

And that's why you're alive. Sithis doesn't care for your rules or your desires. Sithis does as it will, and woe to those who resist. They are cursed to relive their futile toil every day.\n\nFollow Sithis, and your life will be anything but routine.

Helping these boring people dig up their pasts. Attaching significance to old bones and cracked stone. Picking up every little thing you see because you think ownership matters.\n\nI'll bet you've got chests full of junk you don't need.
You learn to step lightly in the swamp, or you drown … or get eaten … or—well, you get the idea.\n\nTry not to let these bone-polishers get you killed sifting through the mud for old rocks.

I certainly hope so! Who's going to prepare my supper and afternoon bath? Unless you'd be interested in … no, I suppose not.\n\nI'll contact my colleagues in the Mages Guild. I'm sure one of them can help me work this out.

Even the brutal Root-House people will return Saxhleel dead to their tribes so they may return to the Hist. Not the Ghost People. They keep those lost souls for themselves. Burying the bodies in the roots of their Hist, or worse.
For now. I'm sure we'll cross paths again, as ku-vastei often do. If you happen to find me doing Sithis's work, I don't know you, but you're welcome to make my job easier.

Since before he hatched! I called him the little stump. He would plant himself at the foot of the Listening-Tree and stare up at the branches. Listening, always listening!\n\nI thought he might take my place one day.
You'd have made a good Shadowscale, with my help. Guess the stars aren't everything, hmm?\n\nHail Sithis.
All is as the Hist wishes it to be.\n\nOne day, when he has grown old and thin like me, he may return to the Glade. Until then, he does the tribe's work. There is no shame in that. None at all.
You should ask him!\n\nTree-Minder Pavu saw the old sap in Xukas. She made him a root-herald, and his days grew short and lean, like an underfed guar. Eventually, he had no time to listen anymore.

It's every day with these crazy lessons! I know that she's trying to teach me the ways of Sithis, but I don't even see the point of this one. Why does Sithis care if we light a fire?\n\nIt makes me question why I ever agreed to be her voh-vastei.
Fine then. If you won't help, just leave me to my death.
Sithis be praised. Thanks to your kindness, I will live another night.
An apprentice. I cannot dishonor Nisswo Kahei's wishes, but how can I one day spread the word of Sithis if some hackwing eats us?\n\nHowever … she has not forbidden you from lighting the fire.

My apprentice fears that which the darkness will bring. The unknown bites away at him, driving him to contemplate his own mortality. But death is a will of Sithis. \n\nHe must see the truth within such fear. Only then can he speak it.
Yes, it is. I am glad you also see wisdom in the will of Sithis.
It is the only way he can truly learn. \n\nI would ask you not to interfere. Though my apprentice snivels, he must learn this lesson if he ever wishes to join the Clutch of Nisswo.

Please, don't mistake my stoic demeanor for a lack of enthusiasm. All of this is tremendously exciting.\n\nBut in answer to your inquiry, yes, the primacy of these relics is a thrilling discovery. It supports a theory of mine—about the Hist.

Well, I wrote a treatise on the subject some years ago. A brisk four-hundred pages. But I suppose I can give you a summary.\n\nArgonians share a special relationship with their Hist. They hear its will, taste its decrees ….
Yes. Well. That's just it. I can't hear the Hist.

Thank you.\n\nI admit, the silence troubles me. But do you see? My egg-kin sometimes need intermediaries, too! With these antiquities—the chimes, the Dead-Water relic, and eventually the Remnant itself—perhaps I'll finally hear … something.
When I place my hands on the Hist's bark or rest in the shadow of its boughs, I hear nothing. No whispers. No faint smells or soothing tones. Just silence. Deafening silence.

Yes? And? I assure you, the Argonians don't care about those relics in the least.\n\nGold, on the other hand, they seem to have all the interest in the world. So much so that they would steal it from the hands of innocent folks!

Do not be. It was a glorious battle. And he fights with me still, you see? \n\nFor the Dead-Water, death is certain. But death brings new life—as shield and bow, or axe and knife. In time, the soul moves on. Everything changes, but nothing ends.
Hmm. I curl my lips. Poetic … another word for soft, I think? Soft words belong to Bright-Throats, like Xukas.\n\nEnough egg-gazing. We have work to do.

We call them xul-vaats. They tell the stories of our victories. And our defeats. Tales from childhood, names of friends, dreams, nightmares.\n\nThey also keep the dead down where they belong. In the mud.
I nod my head. Yes. Until some tail-lifting savage steals the stake.\n\nYou see? We are back where we started.

Often enough to earn a name—bog-blight.\n\nMany strange things stalk the deep murk, ojel. Beasts of vine and stone, giant haj mota, ghost people, slimes, plants with maws like crocodiles. Dead-not-dead seem tame by comparison.

My tail sinks. Etra is buried in the Tomb of Many Spears—an unclean place. Vahat. Or taboo, in the dry-tongue. Tsojei and I cannot fight there. But you can.\n\nIf you can pry the stake away from Etra, bring it to the grave-singer's lodge.

We are a peaceful tribe! Our village is not prepared to face monsters made from their own flesh and blood! I must warn them.\n\nIf you wish to wade deeper into foul waters, I will ask the Hist to watch over you.
Please. Just let me love them, even for a moment. I don't—I don't want them to be alone in the end.
No, but if my children are tainted by these vile poisons, we may be able to follow their trail … if it doesn't kill us. \n\nThe air is still down here. The fumes will linger a long time.
Ree-Nakal's poisons shouldn't exist. I don't know how, but I'll make sure they never hurt anyone again.

When I look at those unseeded eggs, I just see myself. Incomplete. Broken. Seeing them fade away breaks my heart. Ree-Nakal saw that and offered me hope.\n\nI just wanted to believe it. All of it. That we'd all be happy. It was too much to ask.

It was for me, at first. I thought I could make myself the best choice for the bonding ritual with it. When Ree-Nakal asked me to bring her our unseeded eggs, I rubbed it on the shells to give them time, to strengthen them so we could save them.

He did not. He died in glory.\n\nMany great Dead-Water kaals raided the tomb, seeking pieces of Etra—bones or sinew to make mighty weapons. They all died. Now their corpses, and what remains of Etra's, stalk the tomb forever. Like I said … vahat.

He stored them in the great stone vault that eventually became his tomb. The place where you will face him. The Tomb of Many Spears.\n\nOne dark day, a great slime claimed the vault. When Etra learned of this, he grew furious and attacked.
I roll my eyes. If you do not hurry, I will end up telling the story of the slow-legged ojel who lost the Remnant of Argon.\n\nGo now! Be swift!
You think they're alive? Please, we have to find them! They need me! I can't let Ree-Nakal keep hurting them!
It'll be enough to be there and know it's over. I don't want to hurt anyone ever again.

What happened to Stibbons? Why, the same thing that always happens. He ruined my latest undertaking by transforming into an … egg!\n\nI'm sure this has something to do with the tribe's mating practices, but I can't for the life of me imagine how.
She's a Bright-Throat. She belongs with our Hist.
They can punish me. I don't care. I deserve it, but this one has suffered enough. Pavu will understand. She will.
No. She isn't ready yet. Can't you see she's scared? When I've calmed her down I'll bring her home.\n\nYou go back to Pavu. Tell them it's over now … I want some time with my little girl.
There are many interpretations. Charitably, it may mean that she is not ailing as the other hatchlings were, but it is easy to see that she is not whole.\n\nI must consider the alternatives.

That our Hist does not feel her pain because she is not of our Tree. When I look at her, I do not see a Bright-Throat, or even a Veeskhleel. She is unmarked, tribeless, and her eyes are as blank as her scales.\n\nShe may be of no Tree at all.

We are born of the Hist, shaped by the Hist, and when we die we return to the Hist to be born and shaped anew. Can the same be said of this one?\n\nRee-Nakal gave her life, but can one born beyond the Hists' roots possess a soul? I have no answer.
If the Hist believes you are right, then you are right. I will have to hope we did not misjudge its intentions.

Look inward, beeko. Go back to your egg. Shed all the dry-world's distractions and uncertainties. The Hist speaks to you, just as it speaks to me. Do you hear it?\n\nThis is our course. You must see that.
Xal-Sisei. Sacred-Sprout. It's a name I hope she'll grow out of.

We are all connected at the root. It is a connection that can be severed, but also made whole once more. A root mended by they who are chosen.\n\nThe Sap-Speaker assured us of your coming. The cycle continues.

The mending is not without risk. Covetous eyes gaze upon this realm even now, as they always have. We need someone to guide us back to the roots of the Hist. To make us whole once more.\n\nThe Sap-Speaker will explain.
You may not be of the Hist as we are, but it knows you.\n\nYou are Rootmender, who has come to will what must be again. Let the Sap-Speaker guide you so that we might be whole once more.

The river has carried you along many paths, egg-sibling, but the Hist has never forgotten you. Still it guides you.\n\nYou are Rootmender, who has come to will what must be again. Let the Sap-Speaker guide you so that we might be whole once more.

Ereel-Jush is one of the few traditional storytellers left in Murkmire. However, I have found his stories to be … far too plainly spoken.\n\nHis images of war are enough to make a bloodied warrior grow pale.

Varona constantly complains that we never take a vacation. So, when the opportunity presented itself, I set up this trip to visit Murkmire.\n\nShe was certainly surprised, but I get the feeling she was hoping for somewhere with a bit less mud.

We met on one of my construction sites. I was just an assistant overseer on that project and Varona was one of our stone masons. She's really good at her craft.\n\nWhenever she gets the chance, she loves to learn new techniques for working stone.

Same as always, thanks to you. Baar Dau hangs peacefully above the city, Lord Vivec writes and sings in his palace, and our new archcanon has adapted well to his responsibilities.\n\nIn fact, things are so quiet that we decided to take this trip.
I know! I know … I can't fix this, but I have to believe I can fix her. I have to.

We'll go to Lilmoth. I'll find work and a place to live, at least until I can buy passage out of Murkmire. There must be somewhere I can raise my daughter to have a good life, but I won't find it here.

Complete our vacation, of course! But no more wandering around on our own. I'm not letting Varona out of my sight for the rest of this trip!\n\nThen it's back to Vivec City. Those cantons aren't going to finish building themselves, you know.

You've never seen teeba-enoo?\n\nIt is both ritual and sport. The rules, much like our lives, are always in flux. Most dryskins have trouble understanding it. Well, truthfully, many Saxhleel have trouble understanding it.
Do you wish to stand before me for many, many seasons? Because that is how long it would take to explain.

Uncertainty. Fear. Death. These unavoidable truths are all the will of Sithis. \n\nDeetum-Jah must embrace these truths if he ever wishes to teach them as a priest of Sithis. And so my lesson must be taught, no matter how he whines.

No. He will survive. And his reign here will bring a rain storm of sorrows. But all is as it must be. The strongest crops grow from fire-licked soil. So it is with the seed—your Remnant.\n\nFor a miracle to occur, there must first be sorrow.
Another will claim it. But do not worry, Rootmender. It will lead you all the same. Just as a swamp-fox leads the cunning hunter to its den.

It is your role. Just as I speak the Hist's will, you will mend its wounds.\n\nAll of us, even our enemies, have a part to play in this tale. The Ayleids beat the drums of war. Your friends bow the strings of sacrifice. And you sing the hero's song.
Yes, the Prowler. Captain Jimila's ship. She can't very well be a sea captain and prominent trader without a good vessel.\n\nYou need to know these things if you hope to impress the Captain.
Oh. All right, then.\n\nI'm just a little bit tense, is all. So far all the Blackguards have done is make vague threats, but I know their reputation. They're as rotten as the prison they all live in.

Because the Blackguard founders were former Naga inmates. This was decades ago, of course. I'm sure all the original members have died off by now.\n\nDrakeeh the Unchained leads them now. He accepts everyone.

Blackrose Prison? Don't know much, I'm afraid. Used to be owned by the Imperials. Named after an old city nearby, I believe. Though I'm sure that's in ruins too.\n\nAs you can tell, it's no longer operational. Now it just houses the Blackguards.
I attempt to work up the courage to hobble back to the Dead-Water Village. But only I sit, my will as broken as this leg.

It may still guide us there, beeko. If we are lucky.\n\nWe pursue Kassandra, and Kassandra holds the staff. Whether we possess the staff or not, we still find the Remnant. Trust in the sap-speaker. Trust in the Hist.

To my great dishonor, I was captured alive by the Blackguards. They planned to ransom me, but my tribe refused. \n\nThat was when I was put in their gauntlet. A series of harrowing battles, one after another.

I claw for memories. Something you saw during the dream-wallow, maybe? I recall little—shadows, and the taste of blood and smoke.\n\nCling to whatever memories you can. They will serve you well, I think.

What do they teach Argonians where you come from? We need the frogs for the vossa-satl. They produce its sweet-sounding melodies.\n\nThe note explains how to catch each frog. Once you have them all, return to my shop and we'll finish the instrument.
Once, I think. Sithis tired of it and returned it to the trees. The Changer is boundless in its creativity, yes?

I do not, but I saw Am-Lai guiding a mahleel to the ridge above. Imperials seem to have interests in such things.\n\nYou'll have to go through the Sunken Bulwark, east of here, to get up there. Do not pay too steep a price for your curiousity.
A better question would be why anyone would care. It is the rotten husk of a dead tree, the fact its shape is different does not make it any less useless.
Strillian Callidus, Scholar Emeritus at the Imperial Naval Consortium … or what remains of it. I happened to be on sabbatical when the Alliance War began, and now it's been … extended indefinitely.

Show some respect. This wreck is the Dominus Fatum, one of the most storied vessels of the First Empire. Its crew apprehended the notorious Black Marsh pirate, Red Bramman, during the reign of Empress Hestra. A testament to their resolve!

When Empress Hestra demanded the head of Red Bramman, most of his pursuers chased him from the Topal Bay all the way into Black Marsh.\n\nThe Dominus Fatum, however, chose to brave Shadowfen's uncharted rivers and head him off from the north.
Because I am—was—the chair of vexillology at the Consortium, and I can count the number of Dark Elf vessels that flew an Imperial vexillum on one finger.
This is not a well trod path. This quiet muck should stay undisturbed, save for the tenders. When the Refuge sees visitors, calamity is not far behind.

A secret place. A safe place. What you can see, is only the surface. Below the cloudy waters—far far below—is a place where all our tribes take shelter when Sithis seeks to reshape Murkmire. Invasion, disaster, nothing follows us into the mud.
Of course. Take a deep breath and let your eyes adjust to the swamp. You will see where Jaxsik went.
This is what we hunted for? A garden? I hiss fire. Why could it not be more simple? Kaoc.\n\nThere must be more! What do you know that we do not?

The others are new to me. Beehuna is one of the Root-House people, so if she puts hands on you it isn't a romantic gesture—hold tightly onto any familial jewels. Deed-Tei on the other hand is as inscrutable as any Moss-Skin.
As you wish, though the majesty of Murkmire sticks with you, wherever you go.\n\nAs the river rises, where would you like to flow?
Very good! There's a fair wind, now. Should be a pleasant sail.

One hoop is thirty hands high, the other fifty. Hit the ball into the lower hoop, and your team is awarded three points. Hit it through the upper hoop, and the game is concluded. The team with the higher score wins.
Our long-time allies—the Black-Tongues, the Moss-Skins, and the Root-House people. They aren't normally so apprehensive.

Our most potent mixture, brewed to ensure even these Bright-Throat bonds are blessed by the Great Creator. He did not foam at the mouth or expel blood from every orifice, so I think it was just his time.\n\nYou earned your rest, shaper of generations.

Because there was no better choice. There has never been a Black-Tongue who could drink as deeply from the Dread Fathering Elixir and live to see his children grown.\n\nHe was frail in all other pursuits, but in the bonding he was a divine tool.
More than anyone has had reason to count. He was but a young whelp when his talent was discovered.\n\nHalf of Murkmire may bow their heads as we bear his body back to our Hist.

If I leave out a bowl of slugpaste and a nettle-toad eats it, this is no theft. The Root-House people heed forces greater than limp-fin law.\n\nThe Bright-Throats do not see. It is the will of the Hist that I have my dowry.

Why wrestle the world when the world will always win? We get everything we need by flowing with the stream. What's the point of struggling against it?\n\nI know ojel don't understand. It's a shame. We would all be so much happier.
Not always. It is the season for torchbug bonding as well, so they shine and twinkle for each other. I like to think they dance for us as well, so we always have stars, even on a murky night.
I tried to learn as much as I could when I came across the stories of the Wuju-Ka. I'm no expert, but with the dagger we found, I can replicate the ritual. I think.\n\nLet's go find the altar.

No, but it is the best place in the village for torchbug watching. My root-kin are often so busy they don't make time to enjoy them, but I always come.\n\nIt's not lonely—the little stars keep me company—but I do wish people would join more often.

Ah, to have the admiration of a midge. Should I be honored? Truly, you must be acquainted with many who hold your opinion to quite a high standard. \n\nBut I act from the Will of the Dread-Father, and he alone. Your words hold no weight.
May the Dread-Father guide your blade.

Once, I was Shadowscale. I lurked within the darkness, waiting for my time to strike. My victims were many, of course. Young and old, rich and poor. Those who were cruel, and those who were kind.\n\nAnd in that way, I honored Sithis.

I did. I grew old and weak. When my eyes began to fail me, it was time to move on.\n\nI had options. I could train hatchlings born under the Shadow in our dark ways, or create poisons for my sanctuary. But I felt those choices to be … limited.

I have became ku-vastei, that which sparks the needed change. In the past, I ended life which must be ended. Now, I assist the change which must occur.\n\nOf course, both ways honor Sithis. For he who is void is both destroyer and creator.

Ineffectual, perhaps. I would never see the fruits of my labor. \n\nFor a lifetime, I have honored Sithis with a corpse laid at my feet. How could I spend my final days prattling wisdom to hatchlings? Creating poisons for others to use?

Bark and branch, no! I could never eat swamp jellies! Imagine the sound! Their perfectly pitched little shrieks would be heartbreaking!\n\nNo! I just want to spread joy and the beauty of the swamp. You'll understand once you've brought the jellies!

Never seen a swamp jelly? You poor thing! They're wonderful little creatures that float on the wind like feathered seeds that sing, but made of slippery goop. This is why I need you to gather them! People need to see the natural beauty of Murkmire.

It came to me in a dream, while napping under a Hist. I could hear everything in the swamp, all at once and yet one at a time. I was entranced by the calls of swamp jellies blending together into a cheerful little song and I knew what I had to do.

Oh, I won't stop you. We're all on the same journey, it's only the time of arrival that differs. Consider me a guide.
Guilty as charged. Though a pardon does wonders.\n\nYou'll forgive me for keeping you in the dark during my contract, but appearances are important in Summerset and camouflage comes in all colors.
Guilty as charged. Though a pardon does wonders.\n\nYou'll forgive me for keeping you in the dark during my contract, but appearances are important in Summerset and camouflage comes in all colors.

The sap-speaker said that the souls of her tribe nest inside the Remnant, right? If Kassandra could claim the souls of an entire tribe, she might find some way to rule them, to twist them to serve some dark purpose.\n\nWe cannot let that happen.

I'm very to the point when I need to be, but all work and no play makes for dull knives.\n\nYou're in a hurry, so I leave you with a little friendly advice: choose your path carefully. Murkmire is full of shortcuts to your destination.

Perhaps. But the result of a fight like that might lead to even more horrors.\n\nA tribe of angry souls, set loose upon a cruel manipulator …. Might they take on an aspect of her cruelty? Or return to the Hist resentful and suspicious? Who can say?
All children of Sithis are welcome in Murkmire, you just might find yourself in the Dread Father's embrace sooner than you like if you track mud through his house.
All children of Sithis are welcome in Murkmire, you just might find yourself in the Dread Father's embrace sooner than you like if you track mud through his house.
Hope to see you around.
Just a friendly keeper of the peace, here to make sure you stay out of trouble. Take my advice and I'm sure we'll meet again.
Just keep a swift pace and you'll reach the end of your journey before you know it.

Outlaws who make their living out in wilderness by preying on travelers, looting, and the like. They aren't so much a unified force as a loose collection of gangs with common ancestry. Sons and daughters of escaped prisoners, for the most part.

Money, I'd guess. Must be something at those temples they think is worth the effort. Been stealing Argonian antiques a lot lately—real pain in our asses. Must not have found what they're looking for, or they'd have split long ago.

There is a poison distilled from decay and reborn as a gift from Sithis. It kills fear and pain, bringing warmth and peace as it deadens the mind. I will drink deeply of it tonight and forget this torment for a time.
I will raise many cups to you, I promise.

These little deaths are Sithis's mercy. We partake willingly. I know of few tribes that eschew the great serpent's venom. Is it so strange?\n\nNedhellas told me that Men and Mer around the world share this custom. Drinking alcohol, he called it.
May your struggles crumble.
Then we were not meant to be there and we will take our teachings elsewhere, another lesson wiser.

Only a soul unfettered from the body can guide us. What you call death, we call change. There is no death in the Hist.\n\nAll bodies pass to the mud, but the soul lives on. We rise and fall like the sun—gone for a time, but always soon to return.

Difficult to say.\n\nThere may come a day when you lock eyes with a hatchling listening to the wind, or chasing a gecko through the reeds. If that moment comes, though your minds may wander, your souls will know a joyful reunion. Trust in the Hist.

You have many more souls to save, Rootmender. Many battles to fight.\n\nJust as you were born to aid them, Xukas and Jaxsik-Orrn were born to save us—guided through life in preparation for this moment. Your heroism made this possible.
Yes. In an old time, and not long ago—all at once. You fought alongside the tribe, deep beneath our sacred Hist.\n\nI long to see it again.
Forgive me for being hasty! I merely wished to be of use.\n\nI am Iskenaaz, voh-vastei to Tree-Minder Pavu. I am at your service. I promise to leave you with a fine impression of our tribe.
Ah—well, yes. She is a sensitive soul. It is what makes her such a skilled egg-tender, but—and I don't wish to speak ill—the river of her heart is so full that it does not take much to flood.
I'm sure once she has had time to get a hold of herself, she will return. Perhaps we should continue our search in the mean time?
I reveal the obvious. They are hunts for death. Or rather, deadly things.\n\nMy tribe puts out the call for warriors to gather and pursue Xul-Motas. That is my purpose here.
Death comes in many forms, monsters chief among them—no matter the number of legs. What you face depends on the needs of the Naga-Kur.\n\nNo matter what we ask of you, you will be tested.
Part of Cyrodilic Collections. A warrior past his prime. Brokers jobs in Lilmoth now. He gets his cut for those he sends my way. Regardless of whether they survive.
Truth. Varo Hosidias keeps up on our needs as well. Come to either of us and you may join those who seek out death.\n\nYou are here now. Is death what you seek?
So-so. The citizens here appear keen to hear of our cause, but none have entered into our ranks. Still, such battles are not won in a single day. It takes time.
Kazrala may not have a lifetime, but … it would be quite the thing to learn, no? An amusing trick to bring back to Elsweyr, if nothing else.\n\nHmm. This one will keep trying.

I'm as lukiul as they come. Born and raised in Morrowind, away from all … this.\n\nNever licked any sap, yet here I am, soul and all. I put my trust in the Pact, not some all-knowing tree. And that's served me well so far.
You really that invested in me?\n\nWell, I'm not saying I've got my ears closed or anything. I'll listen to whatever anyone has to say, but don't expect me to go on believing it.
Yes, that just about sums it up. Glad you see my side of it.

You really don't know, do you? Huh. I assumed Quintus neglected to tell me that he let this location slip during one of his fool binges, or soliciting a patron to fund his next expedition.\n\nHowever you got here, I have an offer for you.

I believe that beneath the ruins of the Imperial fort here is an Ayleid city containing an artifact of enormous historical significance. Help me recover it and whatever treasures we find in Garlas Malatar are yours to keep.\n\nIt's a generous offer.

Yes. Our Hist pours its intention into the Remnant. When we leave and awaken to our new life, the Hist will wake too—ready to guide a new and vibrant tribe.\n\nSo, you see, you do more than just save an old tribe. You make way for a new one.

Shunatei means something along the lines of "regretful stomach" in the dryskin tongue. It is the pain caused by holding on too tightly to that which has come to pass.\n\nSorrow, anger, suffering. If you do not let them go, they will consume you.

Of course. Our culture revolves around accepting change. We build homes of wood, knowing they will break in the storm and be rebuilt again. \n\nKnow that all things are not permanent, and accept that. Only then can you find peace.

Now that the Blackguards seek the Remnant of Argon? I will return to my tribe and share the bad news.\n\nAs the Bright-Throat root-herald, I should have seen this coming. I feel no small amount of shame, beeko.
No. This is the season of haste, beeko. With time, I might be able to find the person Jaxsik's prisoner spoke about. But by that point, the Remnant might already be gone. I must get to it first.

True. But we know nothing about the person who guides them. It is not enough to kill ten spear-ants. You must find the queen, or you stomp and swat forever.\n\nBlackguards number in the hundreds. Jaxsik will disagree, but we cannot kill them all.
I bristle my war-spines. I will return to Dead-Water Village and gather the warriors for a blood-council. Blackguard hunting season must begin. Now.
One does not stop the other. Tsojei and I will hunt both Remnant and Blackguard. Join the hunt if you wish, but do not stand in our way.
All? No. Most? Perhaps.\n\nThese savages cannot take the Remnant of Argon. If it means the death of every Blackguard and Dead-Water warrior, so be it.

They seem possessed, for lack of a better word. Ensorcelled by some unnatural energy. Like nothing I've ever seen.\n\nRecords said the fort befell some great catastrophe and was abandoned, but little else. It was a long time ago.
Yes, yes, I should have noticed. Your basket practically bulges!\n\nAs for the sun-blessed toads, they are the most slippery of the bunch. Do you need me to tell you how to gather them again?

Sun-blessed toads nest in mud pits, emerging every few seasons to mate. To lure them out, make a musk using stench sedge, salt rush, and joymallow. Find a pit that has a croak-wheel and pour the musk on your head. Then just turn the wheel!
Then don't let me keep you, beeko. Get out there and gather the last of those toads.

Fair. I'm Tharayya, a historian of sorts. Very little of the great ancient civilizations escapes my interest. Ayleids are no exception. You'll need my expertise if you intend to brave Garlas Malatar without sharing those Imperials' fate.

I will stay here and protect the Hist—help it grow and prosper. Many long seasons may pass, but Jaxsik will find her way back. Hist willing, I will be here to greet her. \n\nAgain, you have my ocean-deep gratitude, beeko. You are always welcome here.

My soul left the village as soon as our journey began. I am no longer a Dead-Water kaal.\n\nOther Saxhleel will find their way here, just as I did. I will try to lead them as Xukas would—with wisdom and cleverness. I hope I am equal to the task.

Light and shadow. They are what is and what will be. The day which melts into the chilling night. The night which blossoms back into a glowing day.\n\nBoth were honored here, within the stone piles that surround us.

It took some doing, and a considerable number of favors, but the short answer is he's repaying his debt to me from inside this heavily modified Pneumeria Chamber.\n\nMuch as I despise his company, I couldn't have found this place with his notes alone.

I'm surprised you don't recognize him. He only tried to murder you—and me—back in Volenfell. Royally botched that, didn't you, Quintus!\n\nAfter his inevitable demise, I … inherited his research on other objects of interest, which led me here.

It seems a contradiction. Does not the light wash away the shadow? Does not the debris block the river from its intended path?\n\nYet there is peace here, not conflict. Harmony. Balance. Do you understand?
Vakka-Bok, Xul-Thuxis …. Apart, yet two halves which then make an entire whole. To honor the sun, life, that which is. To honor void, death, that which will be.\n\nIs it possible?
Ah—that is what we Argonians call ourselves here in Black Marsh. Saxhleel means people of the root in the swamp-tongue. Trees. Roots. You see?
Well, some of the songs end with an unworthy snake swallowing the Remnant and turning into a hideous giant that ravages the land for one hundred seasons.\n\nSo, keep an eye out for snakes?
Then your sight is as clouded as mine. \n\nAh, well. I will continue to speak my nothing-words, and try to clear my nothing-thoughts. Perhaps one day I will see the truth of these whispering roots.

Then you are wiser than I with my nothing-tongue. \n\nPerhaps one day I will also see that truth, as clearly as you. I shall lift my eyes from the void, and look towards the sun. I will finally understand these roots that whisper.
And you as well, midge who has become Rootmender.

Whatever is best for the people of Murkmire. I won't act without their consultation if that's what you're worried about.\n\nAgain, I may be something of an outsider, but I am still an Argonian. This isn't some purely academic matter for me.

Answers. About the Hist—their beginnings, their powers … their intentions.\n\nAll I know for certain is that it does not contain simple coins or ancient bric-a-brac. The Remnant is a vessel for great power. We must be cautious and well-prepared.

It took some doing, and a considerable number of favors, but the short answers is he's repaying his debt to me from inside this heavily modified Pneumeria Chamber.\n\nMuch as I despise his company, I couldn't have found this place with his notes alone.

Ha. This is fair.\n\nWhen I was a hatchling, a very old naheesh elder told me a story about a lost tribe—one that lived far away in houses of stone. She did not speak about the Remnant, but its name swelled in my heart. I do not know why.

I curl my lips. You demand a name without giving one? That is the ojel way, isn't it? Take, and take, and take. Hmm.\n\nI am Grave-Singer Ki-At—the Dead-Water's keeper of death-secrets and final words.
I nod my head. Yes. Grave-Stake. Or Xul-Vaat in the true-tongue. Each tells the story of the corpse it pierces. You will learn soon enough.
Death comes in many forms, and wears many masks. I tend to the bodies—staking them when I must, and harvesting them when I must. I read the grave-stakes and sing the fallen warrior's final song.
Well, I do not have such time. The next game is set to begin any moment now. Be off with you, lest you distract me further.
And neither do I. Now, the next game is about to start. Be off with you.

My leg shattered. I waited for a swift death, an honorable warrior's end.\n\nInstead, they let me go. They knew that the shame of returning to my village, broken and dishonored, would be far worse a fate.

Like I said, Vakka-Bok means something like the Bowl of the Sun. I assume the ancient Argonians used it as a place to empower their vakka stones—including the Kajin-Jat Crystal.\n\nReally quite remarkable!
Yes! A place for their vakka stones to soak up the sun's energy and grow in power.\n\nOf course, I could be completely wrong! We haven't been inside after all. We should probably get to it, right?

A temple? Oh no, no, no. A temple implies worship. Argonians worship the Hist, and venerate Sithis. Beyond that, I've never found any substantial variety in their religious habits.\n\nThis would be some kind of, I don't know … garden?

I guess you're hoping I'll say yes, right? Honestly, I … I hope it doesn't come to that. But Kassandra was ready to let me die, just to keep you off her trail. She's not the person I thought she was.\n\nYou'll do what you have to. I'll stand by you.

The original Blackguards would only accept Argonians into their ranks. But when Drakeeh took over, that all changed. Now they accept anyone, no matter their race.\n\nThey even tried to recruit me, a Dark Elf.
I am glad you think so. It pleases me to share this with you. You are welcome to join me anytime. Next time, bring friends!

Ha. I thought I was supposed to supply the optimism. You're right, of course. We just need to find one that's been soaking up the sun's rays.\n\nHave a look around. I'll stay here and try to puzzle out another method in case you come up empty-handed.

Very well, but someone needs to send word of Kassandra's treachery back to Lilmoth and the tribal villages. If she unleashes an ancient power, they need to be prepared.\n\nI move swiftly in the current. I will find you again once I am finished.

Jaxsik chases her prey to the northeast, into the Deepmire. It is an old-fear-place, beeko. No Saxhleel hunts there—not even the bravest kaals.\n\nThis will not stop Jaxsik. Naga fury makes her strong, but also reckless. She will need your help.

Perhaps it was shaped by the dreams of the Hist and fell from the sky, or perhaps this tree simply desired a headdress. Does knowing either change that it is now a tangle of soggy sticks?\n\nIf you want to play guessing games, speak to the dryskin.
Flag. Imperial vessels, particularly those of the early First Empire, carry their unique banner into battle hung suspended from a tall pole by a crossbar.

It was captured by the Empire during the Battle of Tear Harbor during the War for Silyanorn—what would become Stormhold. In honor of their defeat of the Indoril fleet, the flagship was given to the legion and christened the Dominus Fatum.

It didn't, but the frame that bore it was little worse for wear—after I scraped the grime off. I can tell you few units had the honor of carrying their vexillum on a solid gold frame. The crew of the Dominus Fatum have that distinction.

Sacrifices were made, but they were not in vain. Though the Dominus Fatum became mired in the swamp it made it closer to Blackrose than any other ship and its crew captured Red Bramman. Much to his surprise, I'm sure.

I don't know, but I'm thankful for its safekeeping, the Dominus Fatum would have drowned in muck otherwise. \n\nThe ship may have careened over the embankment and into the branches, but the tree might not have even been here a thousand years ago.

I think they're right. Aside from the word of the Hist—which I've learned is very persuasive—legends say that the Vakka-Bok xanmeer holds a great treasure. It has to be the Remnant!\n\nNow, we should get moving. We've got to stop Kassandra!

Touching the Remnant, I can hear their voices. Old, like stone and willow roots. The souls inside are confused. They escaped the Ayleids, but then … a life in amber.\n\nThe Hist kept them safe inside—but it was never meant to last this long ….

Get … yes, go get Xukas and Jaxsik-Orrn. I can only hold the Remnant. The three of you have a larger role to play. I'll explain when you get back.\n\nPlease, hurry. I … I can only bear the weight of it for a little longer.
For now. Every season, the tribes send tenders to keep the Refuge prepared for when the great changes come.\n\nNo one ventures here without a need. When the trouble follows, the Refuge will be ready.

It makes some of the egg-tenders uncomfortable, but Meena doesn't seem to mind. I think being among the Hist's roots will be good for Xal-Sisei, so I'll bear the watchful stares if that's the price I have to pay.

They've never seen anything like Xal-Sisei. She's one of a kind. They don't know what to do with her. I know they are trying to help, but I can tell they don't believe she can be like us.\n\nShe doesn't have to be. She'll always be my Xal-Sisei.
Good. I think the quiet of the uxith is helping her adjust to being around other people. She seems much calmer, doesn't she? The healers seem oblivious, but I can tell.
With caution. I have learned that an ally gained can be greater than a hundred enemies slain. But there are still those who would harm us.\n\nThough my hand extends, Tsojei remains by my side.
As are you.\n\nI'm glad you found your way to the Brotherhood even if you weren't born under the sign. Shadowscales are made killers. You chose to be one. I admire that.
I'm just here to welcome a kindred spirit home, beeko. I'm sure you'll take to the mud here like you were born in it, but best not forget that Murkmire is Sithis's playground or you'll never leave.

If the Night Mother calls on you, obey, but be discreet. There's no Sanctuary for you here, and you'll receive no special privilege. Fear and the Blade will be your only allies … but I might be your guide. I'm sure we'll cross paths again.
A Shadowscale, but we both serve the Brotherhood in our own ways. I'm glad to see you freed yourself from Summerset's idea of hospitality. You'll find Murkmire far more lively, unless it kills you.

I'm just here to welcome a kindred spirit to my home. What kind of hostess would I be if I just left you to your own devices? You might get yourself into trouble. The Five Tenets won't protect you from the Wrath of Sithis here. You're in its teeth.

If the Night Mother calls on you, obey, but be discreet. There's no Sanctuary for you here, and you'll receive no special privilege. Fear and the Blade will be your only allies … but I might be your guide. I'm sure we'll cross paths again.

Call it advice from a dear egg-sister. You might not have been born under the sign, but you found your way to the Brotherhood all the same. I admire that.\n\nIt'll take more than the Five Tenets to protect you from the Wrath of Sithis in Murkmire.

If the Night Mother calls on you, obey, but be discreet. There's no Sanctuary for you here, and you'll receive no special privilege. Fear and the Blade will be your only allies … but I might be your guide. I'm sure we'll cross paths again.

I'm just here to welcome a kindred spirit to my home. What kind of hostess would I be if I just left you to your own devices? You might get yourself into trouble. The Five Tenets won't protect you from the Wrath of Sithis here. You're in its teeth.

If the Night Mother calls on you, obey, but be discreet. There's no Sanctuary for you here, and you'll receive no special privilege. Fear and the Blade will be your only allies … but I might be your guide. I'm sure we'll cross paths again.
Praise Sithis. I thought we might die of old age first.
All right! You win. You're the darkest dark sister to ever have darked. Can we move on?

Where else would I be? I go where Famia and Concordia need me, and right now that's right here. I'm cataloging the latest relics discovered by our explorers, and I need to be quick-quick!\n\nLook! I even found a place for the cursed skull!

Oh, Concordia's off dealing with benefactors and recruitment back in the more civilized sections of Tamriel. Famia expects her to return soon, though, and that will be a good thing.\n\nThe sisters work best when they work together.

Where else should we put it? Oh, you mean the legend! I don't think the Golden Skull of Beela-Kaar poses any more danger to Murkmire. At least, not any more than usual.\n\nDon't worry, though. We'll keep the skull safe, I promise-promise!

Famia's a consummate researcher who's as smart as a sap-speaker. She's a little less sure-footed when it comes to field work, but she does much better when Concordia's nearby to help her.\n\nSome of our benefactors also help out, such as Kassandra.

As I said, one of Cyrodilic Collections' benefactors. She's wealthy, shrewd, competent. She might be the most competent Argonian I've ever met, and that's a fact!\n\nShe's been quite instrumental in getting our current expedition off the ground.

Catalyst of Change, but ku-vastei rolls off the tongue so much better. Sometimes it's a person, sometimes it's a thing, but when the world gets stuck in mire, a ku-vastei is what sets things into motion again.
We all serve in our own way. I prefer discretion, but your methods have their charm.\n\nIn either case, we're clearing the way for something new and that pleases our Father.
Likewise, though I think our needs are very different. \n\nYou don't have to get defensive about the blood on your hands. It's all part of the process of creation.

Fresh seeds don't thrive if they're choked by old weeds. Hacking down overgrowth sows and nurtures the fields from which something new and vibrant will sprout.\n\nPlant without reaping and sooner or later all you'll have are old sticks in the mud.

No, I'm a Shadowscale, but they're often one and the same. We are the chisel to stone. Sithis shapes the world through us, one careful cut at a time.\n\nOr sometimes it wants the slate wiped clean and it sends someone like you.

Outside of Black Marsh, everyone likes everything so neat and tidy. Organized. Orderly. Predictable. Most ojel don't know what to do with themselves without all those laws telling them what to do.\n\nNot you though. You're not afraid of chaos.

At least you can admit it. Most of the things you've been taught to need—out there—are really just a burden. Do you need a fork? A drawer full of forks? A room just to dine in? What'd you part with so you could meet these needs? Too much, I say.

Well, you're very skilled at making baggage for yourself. Preparation is storing food for lean times. Piling up lumber and lemons for the ill-conceived juice stall you're never going to open is just procrastinating.\n\nUse it or let it go. Trust me.

Then you're wiser than most ojel. They drown for lock-boxes sinking in the mud and toil endlessly for wealth they'll never spend. Fools, quick to part with the one thing they can't replace for meaningless things and places to keep them.
You're no Shadowscale, but you're clearly favored by the Night Mother. Most of our brothers and sisters who brave Murkmire end up in her cold embrace.\n\nHail Sithis.

I spent half my time in the dungeon and there were more cold shoulders than Skyrim, but there were some good times. Pity the good bailiff didn't find his way here.\n\nNow, I have places to be and people to stalk.
What's the point? I shed them like skin.\n\nIf I want to find you, I'll know where to look.

That will be between me and the Speakers, but I hope it's somewhere warm. Even Shadowscales like to sunbathe. This one does, anyway.\n\nI think you'll manage without me watching over your shoulder. If not, you should have paid better attention.
Ah. Making sure I'm keeping to my word. You don't need to worry. I don't want to return to a place where my child isn't welcome.

It was hard for Xal-Sisei—at first—with all the activity around here, but I have to work and I can't leave her home alone. The owner was kind to let me keep her with me.\n\nShe's doing much better now. I think being around people is helping.
No. We need to be somewhere farther from the village. We need to look forward, not back. That's hard being so close to ….\n\nWe'll find somewhere to call home.
All thanks to you. You're truly a blessing from the Hist. We'll never forget everything you've done for us. Not ever.

Dragonguard? Hrrm. I leave this investigation to you and Tharn.\n\nGharesh-ri and I need to figure out how to bolster our defenses and prepare our forces. He even wants to send troops to defend the Moon Gate of Anequina.

Unfortunately, we are only a small part of Queen Ayrenn's domain. She sent us advisors and gold to purchase weapons and mercenaries, but her troops are committed to the Alliance War.\n\nI will convince my people to join the militia. I have to.

Euraxia ordered Captain Saulinia to assassinate a Dragonguard in an effort to appease the Dragons.\n\nSaulinia plans to commandeer as many additional soldiers as necessary from Prefect Calo at Sandswirl Manor and retrieve a report.

Neither do I, at least not fully. The Dragonguard were the sworn protectors of the Imperial Emperor. At least they were, until they fell out of favor.\n\nEuraxia has ordered her assassins to murder what she claims to be the last Dragonguard.

Don't ask me. The Dragonguard I knew failed to protect the Potentates and were disbanded in disgrace. They claimed to have descended from legendary Akaviri Dragon hunters, but that's all it was … a legend.\n\nWe need to get to Sandswirl Manor.

So many have answered the call! Zamarak and the Desert Wind adepts, the people of Riverhold. Even that strange Cadwell. And now you, five-claw. Excellent!\n\nI have things that need to be done, but not enough hands to do them. If you are willing ….

The outlying farms are vulnerable to attack. We need to get the farmers inside the walls before Euraxia's forces arrive. Go to Greenleaf Farm and convince Tsazii to move her family.\n\nAfter that, I will send word as to what I need you to do next.

Calo is mentioned in Gharesh-ri's intelligence reports. He commands a garrison of troops in an estate seized when they conquered the region.\n\nAs for Saulinia, I've never heard of her, but an assassination squad—they're never a good thing.

I'm sorry—I thought you'd know Jel, given that you're Argonian. I guess you've spent most of your time abroad. I don't mean to presume!\n\nThe Wasseek-Haleel are also called the Bright-Throats. They're artisans and traders. Loyal friends, too!

Exile. Circumstances forced Zamarak to leave the land he loves.\n\nThis one never imagined returning to Elsweyr, but here he is. Zamarak will help, though he prefers to utilize his healing skills over his martial abilities.

Zamarak understands, but that may be easier said than done. The last time this one used his martial skills … well, things did not go well.\n\nWe can discuss this more later. Now let us go help the farmers. The farm lies to the northwest of the town.

The Euraxians are already here! They seem to be searching for something, though so far they have left us alone.\n\nBut this one's mate and brother, Kinaro and Hursh, they are still in the fields, and we will not run while our family remains separated.

You … you would do that? Thank you, walker.\n\nKinaro would try to hide, but my brother … Hursh can be hotheaded. And he hates the Euraxians. A lethal combination when faced with Euraxian steel. Please hurry.

Tsazii? Is she safe? Thank Jone and Jode!\n\nDark Moons, what a disaster! The soldiers appeared and chased us out of the fields. Then they started digging. Hursh threw a rock. They responded with an arrow. Now my mate's brother is dead.

I heard one of the soldiers mention body parts. Such gruesome work! But no one is buried in our fields, at least as far as I know.\n\nOh, walker, I have no idea how Tsazii will react to the news of Hursh's death. Dark Moons, indeed!
This one's brother would want us to stay here and defend our farm! Tsazii would be a poor sister and a poorer matriarch of this family if she tucked her tail between her legs and slunk away!

But … but … damn you, walker! We can't even spare a moment to take care of Hursh's remains? No, the living are more important than the dead.\n\nWe will go into the city. However, if this one gets killed anyway, she promises to haunt you!

These western camps support the soldiers that encircle the city. Find the camps, startle their horses, and set fire to their wagons. Nala-do's soldiers will grab whatever supplies they can, but your goal is to inflict mayhem and destruction.

Once you scare off the horses and set fire to the wagons, that will be the signal for Nala-do's soldiers to grab the supplies.\n\nAnd if any of the Euraxians complain, feel free to deal with them however you see fit.

The Betrayer's head … I'm not sure why we're connected or why it insists on showing me the most disturbing images.\n\nI saw an Orc necromancer. Dreadful chap. He's coming to Riverhold … and he's bringing his nasty undead chums with him!

Rubbish and poppycock! That makes no sense whatso—wait, wait, I remember something. The Betrayer. Those loon-priests called me that. Right before they—ulp!\n\nWell, we need to warn the cat people. The necromancer is coming and he's bringing undead!

I can play a lute. Magnificent swordplay? My specialty! Can even make a delicious Daedra-heart flambe. But these doodads that go kaboom just popped into my head while thinking about how to help the cat folk.\n\nI quite like the cat folk.

Wouldn't that be remarkable? Decide you need to know something and it just occurs to you in a flash of inspiration? Chocolate souffle! No, didn't work.\n\nMore likely, it's something I knew before they chopped my head off and scrambled my memories.

I prefer to avoid unnecessary bloodshed, of course, but these are enemy forces. We must do what we must to complete our mission.\n\nI'll work my way down from the upper levels of the house. You find your own entrance and we'll meet somewhere inside.

A situation that could end the Three Banners War and get Ayrenn, Emeric, and Jorunn to return to their senses. While these children squabble over territory, the common people and the Empire suffer.\n\nWe have an opportunity and we need to jump on it!

In simple terms, I just purchased two halves of an ancient tablet. The Wrathstone. It forms a map that should lead us to a weapon whose existence will force all sides to cease their aggressive behavior.\n\nHelp me acquire this weapon and end the war.

Of course it is. I just invented it!\n\nRight now, the map shown on the Wrathstone has no identifying features. Without the triangulants, I have no context by which to read the map. I know a Khajiiti loremaster, however, who can help with that.

I know about a great many things, but Khajiiti legends tend to be convoluted. The loremaster must direct us to the secret order of storytellers, the moon-singers. Only they can set us on the correct path.\n\nNow, gather the mushrooms for Dagaril-dro.

An associate pointed me toward the scholar, Tharayya, who agreed to deliver the tablet. She uncovered the two halves at Frostvault and Garlas Malatar, then had the audacity to charge me a small fortune.\n\nStill, the tablet forms the map we need.

An associate alerted me to the two halves of the tablet you helped Tharayya uncover from the ruins of Frostvault and Garlas Malatar. I immediately determined it formed a map.\n\nTharayya agreed to sell them to me, but the cost was obnoxiously high.

Written records are silent on the subject, but the tablet indicates that Khunzar-ri hid a demon weapon. That's the best translation I could manage. Demon weapon.\n\nI believe it's the same relic Queen Anequina used to end the first War of the Prides.

Khajiiti legends, each based on a modicum of truth. Queen Anequina led the most powerful of the sixteen Khajiit kingdoms. It even took her name.  \n\nWhen the Khajiit fought the First War of the Prides, Queen Anequina used a relic to restore the peace.

Menial labor? I think not. But weren't you paying attention? Someone has been following me ever since I decided upon this course of action. Despite my efforts, their identity remains annoyingly elusive.\n\nOnly a mage of great power could hide from me.

I doubt my stalker has any interest in you. Why do you think I requested your aid? Given your relative unimportance, you should be able to travel unmolested.\n\nOnce I've dealt with my stalker, I'll join you at Dagaril-dro's camp.

Old Grandfather sent you? Interesting. This one can only tell you what he knows, and Azargo only knows the beginning of the story. That is the way of things concerning the great stories and the secrets they hold.\n\nAre you sure you want to hear it?

"In the time before time, when the sixteen kingdoms were barely more than sixteen tribes, the great hero Khunzar-ri went on many adventures. After Khunzar-ri defeated the giant Drol by consuming four-hundred-and-one moon-sugar pies, he met a demon."

"Khunzar-ri said, "Not by myself, foul demon. I shall gather a Kra'Jun—a company of heroes—starting with the Altmer, Nurarion the Perfect, who communes among the buried roots of the Ayleid worms."\n\nThese are the words and the words are true.
More undead? Just like at the Defense Force outpost. Regular troops are bad enough, but shambling corpses? They unsettle even the most seasoned Khajiiti warrior.\n\nWe need to warn Gharesh-ri.
