A missing Dragon, huh? Then you'll want to head to Khenarthi's Breath Temple.\n\nThe priests there can find all sorts of things, if your cause is just. I'm certain they wouldn't mind helping the noble Dragonguard defeat a great evil.
A noble quest. Unfortunately, this temple will be of little help. We lost one of our sacred temple bells many years ago. We have not been able to call upon Khenarthi's guidance ever since.

Stole? That is not the exact word Za'ji would use. Regardless, returning it will be … tricky.\n\nTo purchase the Perfect Pounce, Za'ji sold the bell to the skooma lord, Bahzahar the Bull. Said trade involved certain … promises.

Kaalgrontiid absorbed a good deal of the core's power before we stopped him. I hoped he was lost in the void after we dislodged him, but like us he made his way back to Tamriel.\n\nI've been hunting for him ever since.

I've traveled from Rawl'kha to Torval, scouring libraries and harassing moon-singers to learn every tale related to Khunzar-ri. Those legends provide our only window into Kaalgrontiid's history.\n\nThat's what led me south, to that confounded island.

Not just that. I pieced together his ultimate plan.\n\nKaalgrontiid boasted he would become the equal of Akatosh. And your dealings with Laatvulon and the Cult of the New Moon suggest they were preparing for an ascension.

Za'ji happened to mention that the bell could be used to find things, which is entirely true! Of course, this one had no idea how to use the bell in that way.\n\nBahzahar was not pleased when he learned this.

Murderously so! Za'ji has made a point to keep track of Bahzahar's movements to avoid a confrontation. For example, he currently hides out in Moonlit Cove.\n\nIf we want the bell, we'll have to sneak in and steal it back.

It's an heirloom my former student provided. It contains a minor enchantment that reveals hidden glyphs. I imagine it was once used as a way to pass along secret information. Now we will use it to find the hidden Dragonguard tombs.

We can discuss that later. Right now, we have our own tasks to accomplish.\n\nRemember, the Dragons are already loose in Elsweyr. Just know that my former student seeks a way to fight those great beasts before the damage they inflict cannot be undone.

Expert? Far from it. I started looking into the history to help my former student.\n\nThe recent Dragonguard were defenders of the Emperor, but according to legend, in the distant past they hunted Dragons nearly to extinction.
If you're willing to lend your aid, this one can walk you through the cleansing ritual process. But you must be quiet and listen to her instructions very carefully.
We'll do what Za'ji does best! We'll improvise.\n\nThe bells are all about ringing, yes? Perhaps if we get them started, they'll figure themselves out. Or something like that.
Look, this one spent a great deal of his childhood annoying mother. It takes a long time for her to calm down once she gets in one of her moods.\n\nSo, in the meantime, why not try Za'ji's way?
Now, Khenarthi only shares what her winds can find. Sights, smells, perhaps even a vague direction if we're lucky.\n\nIt is up to you to discern a more exact location.
I'll answer what I can, but understand that my knowledge is based mostly on theory and conjecture. \n\nWe seek hidden glyphs that will help us open Dragonguard tombs. At least, that is my hope.

A series of glyphs act as a sort of key to the tomb they are connected to. The seal will identify which glyphs to use to reveal the entrance to the tomb.\n\nAt least, that's what my research indicates.

Historical documents would be good. The more we can learn about the Dragonguard and how they hunted, the better chance we'll stand against the Dragons.\n\nIf we're lucky, we may even come upon one of the legendary Dragonguard weapons.
You have taken up my cause, so it is only fair to know whose banner you fight under. I am Renald, chevalier errant. Bodyguard to Reman III. A Dragonguard.
Interesting. I found a similar map, but to a different location. This might be exactly what my former student was hoping for.\n\nWill you come with me to the Abbey of Blades?

It is my home and heart, where I have had the privilege of training many fine blademasters.\n\nMy most accomplished student will meet us there. We can give him the maps to both sanctuaries and let him decide on the next course of action.

The damage was mostly superficial, though there is still much work to do to fully restore the abbey.\n\nMy most accomplished student will meet us there. We can give him the maps to both sanctuaries and he can decide on the next course of action.
I think it best if my student introduces himself in his own way. Here, you should carry both maps and present them to him yourself.\n\nCome, I acquired horses to speed us on our journey.

There's a reason Carindon's been living out here in the wilds instead of taking his prized Changeling back to the guild for study. He violated an accord between the guild and Selene when he invaded her territory and took her captive.
<Apple snorts in anticipation.>
That's an approximate translation of the Ta'agra text. From the secret histories of the moon-singers. Kaalgrontiid reigned from here before Khunzar-ri imprisoned him in the Halls of Colossus.

Some sort of powerful magic isolates this island. An aegis. \n\nWe need to find the source of the aegis and destroy it so Nahfahlaar and the Dragonguard can join us. We'll never stop Kaalgrontiid without them.

An aegis is a defensive spell. While the magic used in the matrix surrounding Dragonhold is unknown to me, it bears some resemblance to spells I've cast in the past.\n\nI assume the aeonstones serve as a key component in the process … whatever it is.

A ruler with Dragon blood in their veins. A Dragonborn emperor to take up the Amulet of Kings and unite all Tamriel under the protection of the Eight. One whose right to rule is unassailable.\n\nThis land won't know peace until then.

If you strive for a united Tamriel, may your reign be a long one, but I fear until the Amulet of Kings rests on the shoulders of a Dragonborn Emperor, this land will know no peace.\n\nUntil then, my allegiance is to the Empire alone.

There are no shortcuts to power. The Soulburst proved that. This is a desperate act of impatience and I fear the price of recklessness will be far too high.\n\nNo one knows what Dragon's blood could do to a vampire. Grundwulf can't see he's being used.

I can think of any number of reasons for a culture to declare a myth or legend forbidden, though most involve topics too disruptive or dangerous to discuss openly.\n\nThis particular tale deals with the rise of the new moon.

The figures at the bottom. Those must represent the New Moon cultists. And see the aeonstone, emanating energy that gives rise to the third moon?\n\nYes, I'm certain. This depicts the legend of the Dark Aeon.

Indeed. Anything that hints at changing the status quo poses a danger to those in charge.\n\nSee the number of moons? The Khajiit acknowledge multiple moons, but they rarely depict any besides Jone and Jode. The third moon is larger than both of them.

Yet here I am. I wish I had an answer, my friend.\n\nI remember that fateful day in Coldharbour. Death dragged me down into darkness, but then I awoke here, at the Abbey of Blades. The rising sun never looked so good to my battle-weary eyes.

According to the legend, this new moon presages a time of darkness and the birth of a new supreme being. Kaalgrontiid seeks to make the prophecy come true.\n\nDamn it, I won't have my legacy tarnished by a mad Dragon I inadvertently released!

I needed to rest, rebuild my strength. Besides, Kasura required help with the abbey. When the Dragons invaded Elsweyr, I knew it was my duty to fight against them. \n\nI've been searching for the wisdom of the ancient Dragonguard ever since.

I returned to the abbey to help Kasura rebuild. I'm not much of a carpenter, but I do what I can.\n\nWhen the Dragons invaded Elsweyr, I knew my duty was to fight against them, and I began to search for the wisdom of the ancient Dragonguard.

No, but I am trying to learn. The ancient Dragonguard were the Dragon slayers. My order simply served to protect the emperor.\n\nSince the return of the Dragons, I have dedicated myself to discovering the old ways of the Dragonguard.

Yes, yes. The maps appear to be the right age. The sanctuaries they lead to may well contain the knowledge and relics I seek. We must visit these sites as soon as possible.\n\nI just need a little time to study them and determine their orientation.

He may. Even without the Clan Mother goading him, Grundwulf will back his conviction with his blade. If it comes to that, I'll put him in his place. I'd rather wound his pride than witness his self-destruction.
They are parasites. Their only interest is stealing the power of things greater than themselves. \n\nIf any stand in our way, put these leeches to the sword without remorse.
Ah, the confidence of youth.\n\nVery well, then. Let's get on with it. We still need to find the source of the magic that's protecting this island.
You saw how they pounced on me! Not a moment's hesitation! She's been sinking her claws into their minds since the moment they met!\n\nStrike them down and let's be after that treacherous spider!
I don't want your thanks. I want my freedom.\n\nYou … are welcome. We persevered despite the warlock's meddling.

Fine! Don't trust me. My motives don't change the fact that Selene is dangerous! What's to be gained by subjecting me to censure? A monster on the loose, the study of magic set back decades, an offered reward lost.\n\nWhat harm have I done?

Yahgrondu ran afoul of a powerful Dragon hunter in a time before the Dragonguard. I found him, injured and cornered, and offered my aid. For a price.\n\nKnowing that his life was forfeit, he begrudgingly agreed.

My kind call it a sosmir. A blood allegiance. It is an unbreakable bond, stronger than any vow uttered by a mortal.\n\nYahgrondu is bound to pay his debt by a magic older than any you know. If you find him, he will join our cause.

Now that I've gotten a closer look, it's clear that the aeonstone absorbs and amplifies the life energy the cultists feed into it. I sense a connection to levitation magic, but as for the ultimate purpose …?
Because the cultists don't believe what we see here happened in the past. They believe the Dark Aeon will arise in the future.\n\nThe very near future, if Kaalgrontiid has his way.

I think the land at the bottom represents this island, Dragonhold. See the vast amounts of aeonstone, including the spire at the center? Its energy feeds into the new moon as it rises into the night sky.
That's the Dark Aeon, the new moon—the new god—that Kaalgrontiid plans to ascend to. But all that energy … that must be the source of Dragonhold's defenses.\n\nWe have to find this location.

An army of Dragons with the means to amplify their power? That doesn't bode well.\n\nI do not like that we're going into this fight blind. There's too much we don't know about Laatvulon and this cult of his. We need more information.

The only thing remarkable about Black Heights is just how unremarkable it is.\n\nNothing ever happens there. The villagers paint the Wall of Life, the priests pray to Khenarthi for guidance. It's all very dull.

Khenarthi is the Goddess of the Winds. She guides the Khajiit, ensuring our ships reach safe harbor and our souls find the Sands Behind the Stars. \n\nWith Khenarthi's power, the priests can guide us to what we seek.

Tadali's jekosiit of a son stole it. That is why Za'ji is no longer welcome in this temple.\n\nStill, Khenarthi shows grace in all things, even betrayal. If you find the bell and return it, this one will search for your Dragon.
In Za'ji's defense, he stole a lot of things that night.\n\nBesides, how was he supposed to know the bell was so important? The temple has so many! He just thought mother would replace it.

The cove's waters are filled with moonlight. Many go to drink from its waters. For its holy properties, you understand. At least, they used to.\n\nNow a skooma lord has taken over, laying claim to the sacred water and attacking anyone who enters.

The Elsweyr Confederacy. An alliance between Anequina and Pellitine. The various political upheavals and the Knahaten Flu have left the Confederacy in shambles. I plan to rectify that.\n\nGharesh-ri insisted I bring an armed escort. He worries so.

Abnur Tharn is conceited, opinionated, condescending, and a pain in my arse. And those are his good qualities!\n\nAll that said, I have the utmost respect for the battlemage. When danger appears, we could do worse than to have Abnur on our side.

Interesting. We should prepare to face further challenges. Neither Wind Scour nor Storm Talon were easy to navigate. I suspect this next sanctuary will prove similarly difficult.\n\nDoes the book indicate where this Dark Water is located?
We can take the horses to Windhelm, and then search on foot from there.

By Leki's blade! Of all the possibilities I imagined, that was never among them.\n\nNo matter the dangers, we must retrieve that Dragonhorn. The fate of Elsweyr depends on it! Did the journal indicate where Vahlokzin lairs?
Such a journey requires planning and preparation. Let's return to the Abbey of Blades and check in with Kasura.

The Horn of Ja'darri? This journal claims … it's a Dragonhorn of great power! And the last of the original Dragonguard went in search of it.\n\nIncredible. I thought Dragonhorns were merely legends, but according to this, at least one exists.
We must break the tempo! It is too loud for this one's song! The bell! Ring the Khenarthic Bell!
A Dragonhorn? I have heard of such relics in stories and legends.
Stolen by a Dragon? Well, Sai Sahan has always enjoyed a good challenge. How will you find this creature?
A long way to go, but such a relic is what Sai was hoping to find when he set forth upon this path.\n\nMay Leki watch over you, warrior. You and Sai both.

Blessed. Grateful. Afraid. Vijari very much wants to lay his head down and shut his eyes, but he does not know if they will ever open again … or what he will see behind his closed lids. He still hears the drums. Not with his ears, but his heart.

The path I walked through the Shadow Dance Temple attuned me to the Moons and to the memories of my ancestor, Anequina Sharp-Tongue. They were so clear when I needed them in Northern Elsweyr.\n\nNow? Nothing. Not even a Moon Gate, yes?

Vijari had a spotless soul, walker, and he passed without regrets. This one believes Khenarthi heard the bells, even if he was not the one to ring them. Adara'hai doesn't think the Divines are so fickle as to leave a deserving soul behind.
Not so fast, my eager associate. See that tablet on the wall? It appears that parts of it are missing.\n\nI've seen elaborate locks such as this in the past.

If she could leave him to his rest, she would. Just as Dak'radhi poured all his hate and anguish into his work to defile the Wall of Life, so must Vijari paint with love and peace to restore it. All we can do is help him on his journey.

We count our enemies among those who conspired to cut down Reman, and the Potentate. Many Dragonguard met their end by a knife in the dark. The rest of us donned our own cloaks and daggers. It is not a life of honor, but necessity. That chafes some.

Even if those assassins have lost their interest in us, those who covet the Ruby Throne will not welcome the return of the Dragonborn. When a true successor is finally found, we must be ready for the usurpers.

Do not make Zar blush, dear friend! Legendary certainly fits. Illustrious, even. But mythic? That's a little much, yes?\n\nThis one is who you say. The luminous lion of Elsweyr, the Jonelight jaunter, and the imprisoner of Dragons—Khunzar-ri!

Oh, no, dear friend. Zar's tales have all been told. As this one explained to Ja'darri long ago, it is time to sing the song of a new hero. \n\nZar can lend you a bit of his experience, however. This one can tell you about a secret path to Dragonhold.

Apologies. It was much more grand when Zar's tales were widely told. \n\nAs for why Zar has awakened … well, how could this one sleep with all the noise the Dragons make? Kaalgrontiid and his brood always were too rambunctious, yes?
The brave and beautiful Khajiiti queen! Anequina's blood courses through her sleek and fragrant form!\n\nGive her Zar's claw. She will know what to do with it when she sees it.

A rib, a femur, but a claw is least cumbersome. Do not look so surprised. The remains of a Khajiiti legend hold great power. Power the scion of Anequina can use to walk the Jonelight Path.\n\nClever! You made Zar say more than he meant to. Well done!

Zar can go anywhere, yes. You? No, not so much. Between the two of us, only Khunzar-ri has heard Azurah's whispers and climbed the forbidden tree.\n\nBut this one will show you how to reach Dragonhold. Now, hurry along before your heart bursts apart.

Or your soul will be torn asunder. Only Azurah's swiftest champions can survive in this between place for very long.\n\nWhy? Who can say? Azurah keeps certain secrets even from her favorites! Now, step lively upon the moonlight and be quick!

Hrrm. I have a guess. Nahfahlaar tells us that there are focal points, aeonstones placed at key locations around the island.\n\nIf we can disrupt the flow of energy through these focal points, it may stop Kaalgrontiid's ascension ritual.
Pay this one no mind, walker. These are happy tears. You and Adara'hai have brought hope where there was none. Ka'ishka has no needs beyond Vijari's own.

If Abnur Tharn was with us, he would have a magical solution. In his absence I see only one clear path—we must destroy the aeonstones that make up the focal points.\n\nI doubt Kaalgrontiid has left them undefended. Be prepared for a fight, five-claw.

His father? This one had hoped it was only Vijari's condition playing tricks on him. It makes Adara'hai want to spit fur. First, Dak'radhi abandons his sick cub. Now he returns to drag Vijari to the Darkness with him. He is truly a Bent Cat.

There is nothing more dangerous than a Bent Cat who doesn't know he is twisted. If Dak'radhi's sole desire is his son, that is a connection too strong for me to break.\n\nOur only hope is to seal the crack in the Wall of Life. What else did you learn?
Of course she … oh. This one see's what you mean.\n\nWhich of these is confusing you?

That, Adara'hai did not doubt. You've silenced the drums for now, but it will not last. We must buy time for Vijari to work. \n\nWhile he restores the Wall of Life, we will follow the Passage of Dad'na Ghaten and exorcise Dak'radhi from this place.

The Wall of Life was just the beginning of the journey to the Sands Behind the Stars. Beyond it is a path up through the mountain, where the dying would rise into Khenarthi's arms.\n\nAdara'hai fears that it delivers the dying into the Darkness now.
Ever the voice of … support and tact. Considering the circumstances, I could be worse.\n\nUnfortunately, I believe we … solved one problem … and created another.

To safely absorb all that energy … Kaalgrontiid needed the focal points. As close as he is to his ascension … safety will be the furthest thing from his mind.\n\nIf he proceeds with his ascension and makes even the slightest mistake ….
If Kaalgrontiid tries to ascend without the focal points … he could unleash all that pent-up energy. The resulting blast would destroy Elsweyr … perhaps all of Tamriel ….
No, my friend. This task requires a Dragon … and a battlemage.\n\nTake Khamira and Sai Sahan. Find a way out of here. Nahfahlaar and I will contain the explosion.
And we have accomplished amazing things. But this … this isn't something you can help me with.\n\nSave the others. I need to reach that crystal before it explodes.
He is glad. Vijari is the only one meant to leave the world today.\n\nDid he finish, walker? This one's eyes are still in shadow. He cannot see the Wall.
Let's go.

Most certainly. You saw how it knocked Vahlokzin out of the sky, granting us a significant advantage in battle. If it's as indestructible as the journal says, it will prove invaluable in the battles to come.\n\nI just wish we knew the Horn's origin.

Vahlokzin implied that the Dragonhorn was willingly given by another of its kind. But what manner of Dragon would give away its own horn? And for what purpose?\n\nAh, well. Perhaps things will become clearer with more study.

You found the Dragonhorn? By Leki's perfect blade, that is good news. \n\nThank you, warrior. You did far more than help Sai Sahan recover the wisdom of the Dragonguard. Because of your efforts, he finally has a way to combat this Dragon invasion.
I know, five-claw. I know. I did not like the man, but I came to respect him. In the end, he was part of my family.\n\nWe will honor his memory and his sacrifice. I will see to it personally.

Sai went back to the Dragonguard Sanctum to check on the others. As for Nahfahlaar, I do not know. He was on Dragonhold, helping Tharn. We can only hope.\n\nThe Dragonguard, they did so much. And you, always my champion ….

The Order of the New Moon. Yes, I know of them. They've been recruiting in Senchal for some time, preying on skooma addicts and vagrants. A repugnant practice.\n\nYou believe this order is a Dragon cult?

As if Dragons weren't troublesome enough.\n\nAs you heard, the Shields' resources are stretched thin. Senchal is one disaster away from a full-blown riot, and I need my soldiers on the streets. I can't spare any to deal with this matter.

You want to investigate? By all means. Buzinda, the Khajiit who was just in my office, believes the Order of the New Moon recruited her daughter, Lahini. Find Lahini and you should find the cult. \n\nSpeak to Buzinda and see what she can tell you.

Your aid and this handful of jewels.\n\nFirst, you must bribe Renmus's scribe <<1>> to put us on the schedule. You'll find her in the tavern. Next, you need to speak to <<2>>  in the city's outskirts, just south of here. He can forge our credentials.

You also need to delay <<1>>, who is scheduled to meet with the general today. \n\nArniel's ship just docked in the harbor. If you steal his vessel's manifest, the dock master should detain him. That will give us enough time to speak with the general.
Today? Ha! You are very, very funny.\n\nGeneral Renmus's schedule is full today. If you want to see him, fill out your paperwork and submit it. Just like everyone else.

I didn't know you were feeling so generous, walker.\n\nI suppose your name can be added to the general's schedule. But that is all, yes? You'll need to secure the proper documents and delay his previous appointment.
Interesting, most interesting. Diplomatic papers? Yes, that would get you in to see the shaveskin general.\n\nOf course, skills such as Darkhu's require compensation worthy of his talent.

Ah, yes. These beauties will do quite nicely.\n\nHere you are then. Diplomatic papers, all up to date and ready to present. Just make sure you have an appointment, eh? Wouldn't want to walk in on the general unannounced!

And so we must prepare for our first battle, my friend. A battle of wits.\n\nRemember, we must convince General Renmus to commandeer a ship for us. With it, we'll sail to the Dragon's island and slay the beast.

Not much, and what I do know I'm not sure what it means.\n\nA ship sailed directly to the Dragon's island recently. It displayed no banners, and no one in Senchal recognized it. It's possible we're not the only Dragon hunters in Southern Elsweyr.

I won't discount the possibility, but I also won't plan for it. For all we know, this ship was bound for another destination. Or it has other business on that island, though I'm at a loss as to what that might be.\n\nLet's head to our appointment.
Yes, this one is Safik. Daini sent you, eh? If she sent you to check on me, we must be in danger.\n\nLet this one guess—she tried to rob Turo and made a mess of it.

Safik …. Daini loves him dearly, but he lacks a thief's edge. He sees mortal risk in loose cobblestones and old rusty nails. We needn't worry.\n\nThis one found a new target. Turo owns a warehouse to the east, packed with trade goods and treasures.

Who else should Daini rob? Turo owns South Guard!\n\nSafik told you this was personal, didn't he? Moons …. I will say it one last time: Daini does not care about Turo. She wants his treasures, nothing more. Now, are you in?

Za'ji's words, not mine. Oh, you accomplished amazing things in your time with us … Laatvulon, Kaalgrontiid …. But such titles, they mean more to the admirers than they do to the admired.\n\nOur Dragonguard is young. Let them have their heroes.

All of this makes one think about the past. I lost my family. I lost good friends. I nearly lost my homeland. But we persevered.\n\nBefore I met you, there was something else I lost though I did not realize it. Something that you returned to me.
Hope. No matter what we faced, no matter the danger, you never gave up. You never gave in.\n\nYou taught me such a valuable lesson. You and Tharn both. Thank you, my friend.

Tharn's a tough old goat. If there was a way to survive, he'd find it. I just … I don't think there was.\n\nOh, I almost forgot. We received a summons from Queen Khamira. She wants to see us—all of us—in Senchal.
She was being rather cryptic, but I think she wants to throw a celebration. Honor the Dragonguard and all that.\n\nBeforehand, however, she wants to talk to you. You can find her in Senchal Palace.
The smuggling? The piracy? The drinking? This one has dropped them like a hot sweet cake!\n\nWell, except for the drinking ….
There are still Dragons to deal with. And the Dragonguard will need more ships. A whole fleet of them!\n\nThen Captain Za'ji will require a grander rank. What do you think, Admiral Za'ji, yes?

Za'ji always wanted to be a hero. The Dragonguard, it gives Za'ji a chance to do something important with his life. Something good.\n\nBut we should be celebrating! Not examining decisions that brought us to this point. At least, not while we're sober.

The work. The mission. We may have taken out the Dragon clan mothers, so to speak, but there are still a lot of lesser Dragons to deal with. For that, the Dragonguard needs to learn how to fight.\n\nAnd fighting, that's my specialty.

For as long as they'll have me. Me and Captain Za'ji both.\n\nTruth be told, the bearded one handles himself well in battle. I think I can learn a thing or two from him along the way. So, it works out for everyone for me to drop anchor here.

The thought …. You know, I've been thinking. Maybe I'm not actually cut out for the Dragonguard. I feel so young compared to Sai. So … inexperienced.\n\nI'm not sure I could have handled being up on that floating island.

I did? I mean, I did, didn't I? And I took command of our forces down here while you and Sai were up there ….\n\nYou always know just what to say, don't you? Thank you, my friend. I'll keep that in mind even as I strive to gain more experience.

No, that was just a slight moment of doubt. But you've set me straight, and I take my calling very seriously. I go wherever the Dragonguard needs me.\n\nI will make time to return to Senchal and visit with my father, though. I owe him that much.
You have? Oh, thank you, thank you!\n\nYou'll need details, yes? Lahini has black fur and blue eyes. A skinny thing, so frail. She was very sickly as a ja'khajiit and never quite recovered.
Kazahn may know more. He is a ruffian, but Lahini loves him. She would have at least told him goodbye.\n\nBut he refuses to speak to Buzinda. All he does is sit in the tavern, drinking his days away.
Lahini spoke of them. She said, "I am but a burden to you. With them, I can be useful."\n\nBuzinda begged her not to go, but Lahini left the very next morning.
The battlemage wanted to contain the energy of the aeonstones. To keep the release from destroying anything beyond the crumbling island.\n\nI helped him achieve that goal before I returned here.

All I can tell you is what Kaalgrontiid believed. He believed that with enough power, he could become a new moon in the sky. A new god to challenge Akatosh. Regardless of the truth, he had to be stopped.\n\nNow, for me, the time has come to move on.

I do not know. The battlemage was weak, exhausted, but he refused to give up. He wanted to save you. Save this land. I lent him enough of my power to accomplish that task.\n\nIt was the least I could do after he helped stop Kaalgrontiid.
That mangy harlot? Never heard of her.
Look, I'm not in the mood to talk about Lahini. So why don't you shove off?
Oh, tough talk. I can feel my whiskers quivering already.

I … fine. She may have broken my heart, but I don't want her to get hurt.\n\nLahini came here with some muskarse in dark robes. She begged me to join something called the Order of the New Moon. I turned her down and they both walked out.

Me and my chums tried to follow, but we lost them in the dark. And I'll admit, I was a bit drunk. Hard to track someone with a few pints in your gut.\n\nRanza, though. He handles his drinks well. He might know where they went.
I'll handle it.

I need you to represent me before the Imperial, General Renmus. He knows of my goal to restore the Elsweyr Confederacy and rejoin Anequina and Pellitine.\n\nGiven their service, I want to offer the Shields of Senchal a place in this restored kingdom.

So, Anequina seeks to come to the rescue of Pellitine? We've been doing quite well on our own, I'll have you know.\n\nOh, who am I kidding? The Shields have been getting by on luck and tenacity … and then the Dragons came.

You make an excellent point. The Empire no longer exists but Senchal continues to need us. It would be dishonorable to turn away from our duty.\n\nVery well. For Senchal and its people, I will agree to Queen Khamira's terms.

Your words ring true. It's time to return home … to whatever remains of it, at any rate.\n\nI will let Queen Khamira know of my decision. I'll leave it to the rest of the Shields to determine their own course of action.

Return to Imperial City. Find the person in charge. Then introduce myself and offer my services. If they remember me, all the better!\n\nWe'll work block by block, district by district. With the heart restored, in time the Empire will flourish.

Fine, fine. Not looking to get disemboweled today.\n\nLahini came here with some muskarse in black robes, begging me to join something called the Order of the New Moon. I turned her down and they both left.

Me and my companions tried to follow, but we lost them in the dark. And I'll admit, I was a bit addled. Hard to track someone after a few pints.\n\nRanza, though. He's the best tracker I know. I'm pretty sure he never lost sight of them.

An admirable venture, I'll admit, if not a foolhardy one.\n\nUnfortunately, I have neither the ship nor crew to lend you for such an expedition. The city is chaotic enough as it is, and I can't afford to spread my resources.

Which is precisely why I can't agree to your request. If a Dragon does attack Senchal, I need every soldier and ship under my command here to defend the city.\n\nI'm sorry. Your cause is commendable, but my mind is made up.
Very well. Follow me.
Very well, I'll meet you there. Try not to dawdle. The sooner we can secure a ship, the better.

Then I want to help. Or, well, send you to someone who can help you.\n\nYou should speak to Za'ji, captain of the Perfect Pounce. He may be a smuggler, but he cares about Senchal. And he's my friend. He can get you to that island.

I know, I know. My father certainly wouldn't approve. Then again, he hasn't approved of most of my friends since we arrived in Senchal.\n\nNot that my father's disapproval has any bearing on this conversation.

He loiters around the city's outskirts, along with his first mate, Caska. Just look for a Dagi-raht and a Senche-raht arguing with each other. You can't miss them.\n\nOh, and tell them Aeliah sent you!
I know the place. You reach it through the Outlaws Refuge, beneath the city. But they don't let just anyone into the Black Kiergo.\n\nIf you want to find this recruiter, you'll need my help.
It's a fighting ring. I was the reigning champion for six years running. I can get you inside, no problem.\n\nGo on ahead. I'll meet you there.
It was once a city district, home to skooma dens and cutthroats. Burned down when the Knahaten Flu hit Senchal.\n\nOf course, places like the Black Kiergo don't just go away.

The Perfect Pounce! The finest vessel to sail the Topal Bay.\n\nSomeone stole her as we slumbered. A heartless wretch! A thief without honor! A member of Za'ji's very own crew, he is sure of it! Nartise Merys. May he suffer a thousand salty cuts.

No, but Nartise does. And Za'ji knows we can find him in South Guard Ruins. Pounce needs provisions before it sets sail, and that's where Nartise will get them.\n\nBut why are you offering to help, walker?

Aeliah sent you? Then you must be walkers of honor! And this one must admit, slaying a Dragon sounds quite heroic ….\n\nVery well, it's a deal! You help Za'ji get his ship back, he will take you to this island.

He is the newest member of Za'ji's crew. Came aboard only a few weeks ago. And this morning, just as the Perfect Pounce is stolen away, he disappears!\n\nIt is more than a coincidence, this one thinks.
It used to be a fort, but as the name suggests, it's seen better days. Now pirates and brigands call it home. They will not welcome outsiders.

Za'ji's blood may boil, but his mind remains as sharp as a blade!\n\nWe came to Senchal for provisions. It is unlikely that Nartise would journey out to sea without stocking up first. That means dealing with the vagabonds in South Guard Ruins.

Caska, first mate of the Pounce. Otherwise known as the one who keeps Za'ji from getting us all killed.\n\nIf it were up to me, Nartise would have never set foot on our deck. Unfortunately, our bleeding heart of a captain had other ideas.
There's no need to fight the noble Dragons who wish to rule over us. Swear your loyalty to them and no harm will befall you.\n\nJoin the Order of the New Moon and your survival is guaranteed.

No. Turo left a note telling Daini to turn herself in. He holds Safik prisoner in his fortress and will kill him if she refuses. Mara's heart, we were so close!\n\nStupid! Reckless! This is all Daini's fault. No … no, it is Turo's fault!

Excellent, excellent. But first, you must prove yourself worthy. Travel to Tenmar Forest and enter our fortress. I marked the location on your map.\n\nAnd take this pendant. It will identify you as a new recruit to our cause.
It isn't. It isn't. This one just needs … Turo has all the gold, and ….

When the Dragons swept across Elsweyr, the Khajiit trembled. Some hid behind city walls. Others took up arms and fought in vain.\n\nBut Ra'khajin, wise above all others, knew we could not hide. That fighting was useless.

We are the shepherds of a new era.\n\nOnce, Dragons ruled these lands. Their might protected us, their wisdom guided us. But through trickery and deception, a selfish few ended that time of peace. Hakon One-Eye, Khunzar-ri. Traitors!

Hrmph! It'll take a lot more than this to knock the wind out of Sormund's sails! I'll be all right. That cub, though … Safik. He's not suited for this kind of treatment. I'm … I'm worried about him. The others as well.\n\nBah! There! I said it.

No, but I can guess.\n\nTuro may act the part, but he's not a romantic. He's an opportunist. He won't kill those scallywags if he thinks he can profit off them. Check the caves near the Dream-Drowner—his slave ship. Any luck, you'll find them there.

Finally, some warriors. We'll need you both in the upcoming battle.\n\nBut first, you must prove yourself worthy to join us. Speak to Trial Master Zayri. She'll lead you to the Path of the New Moon. You'll find her just inside.

The false god's protectors are gone and their sorcery with them. The chancel doors are unsealed. All that remains is for you to walk through them. And slay a Dragon God … but at least it is a false one.
The entrance is back in the temple courtyard, through a pair of doors engraved with Dragons.\n\nThat is where you will find the fake Alkosh.

You're right, you're right. I just hate seeing Senchal suffer like this.\n\nKazahn seems like our best lead so far. Buzinda said that he likes to drink at the tavern, right? We should head there next.

Daini managed to stash a handful of Turo's jewels away before the thugs captured her. This one feared that Sormund would demand more, but something softened him a bit. Daini does not ask questions. He agreed to take us aboard. That is enough, yes?

Quite correct. A former student requires my assistance, but I cannot do what is necessary on my own.\n\nFighting the Dragons that plague Elsweyr seems an impossible task, but the Dragonguard once successfully hunted them. We seek their wisdom.

Tombs. I will search one, you the other—using this Dragonguard seal. \n\nThe seal will activate three glyphs which, in turn, will reveal the entrance to the tomb. Between the two of us, I pray we find the wisdom my student requires. Will you help me?
Of course! Watch the master at work.

When the last emperor of the Reman Dynasty was assassinated, the Dragonguard were disbanded. Various emperors in the intervening years have formed their own versions to add legitimacy to their rule, but they were never the same.

A riddle to those hindered by limited perspectives. A profound truth to one such as I. Something ancient and powerful assaults my senses, but the path ahead is unclear. I sense a darkness. Perhaps an absence of light.\n\nIt sets my scales on edge.

My feeling is my own. It grew from a tickle behind my broken horn when the fool of a battlemage opened the Halls of Colossus. Now it swirls like a black storm around me. Quite unpleasant.\n\nPerhaps the new arrivals can shed clarity on what is to come.

My entire life. Before the flu and the fires. Before rogues and Imperial thieves brought their corruption. Before everything was overgrown and left to rot.\n\nThis one remembers being proud to live in Senchal.

It is more than just a tapestry. It's a symbol of Senchal's status. Khajiit of the Moons reminds us of who we were and what we can be again.\n\nThis one must prove that our culture isn't lost and that it is worth saving.

Very well. We'll start our search at the north entrance. I'll follow your lead. \n\nMeanwhile. Za'ji and Caska can make their way to the other side of the encampment. I'll leave their strategy to them.

I did. Cadwell acquired power over portals after attuning at the Shadow Dance Temple. Tharn suggested I might have the same ability and he has been helping me.\n\nJust between us, he is not the most patient teacher.

Lord Gharesh-ri has my kingdom well in hand. We continue to clean up the mess left by the Usurper Queen. And there are still stray Dragons to deal with. But Tharn convinced me that I was needed here.\n\nWorking with a Dragon. What an odd sensation.

So Tharn has told me. He has been exchanging letters with Sai Sahan for some time.\n\nDo not expect me to turn my back on the creature, but I will respect this alliance. Moons! This must be what a mouse feels like in the presence of a purring Alfiq!
Marching down from Rimmen, I suppose. Tharn was in a hurry, so he had me practice my portal making.\n\nZamarak and the others will catch up to us. Eventually.

We get along just fine. I am affable and gregarious, after all.\n\nThat said, I may have ridiculed his outlandish oaths and blatantly disregarded his code of honor once or twice. The difference between an idealist and a pragmatist, you understand.
I sold the ship! To Admiral Irathi.\n\nBut they haven't set sail yet! The ship is still berthed on the south docks. Irathi hasn't even finished loading up the slaves.
I … did I say slaves? Silly me. I meant cargo. They're loading cargo. I would never sell a Khajiiti ship to a slave trader.
All right, yes, yes, Irathi is a slaver. But I swear, I didn't know that until after I sold her the ship!\n\nPlease, you have to believe me. I'm innocent here!

Yes, because Khajiit like you need to see that it is more than just a tapestry. It is our history. It reminds us of who we were and what we can be again.\n\nThis one must prove that our culture isn't lost and that it's worth saving.

As I'm sure you surmised by now, I take great pride in using every weapon in my arsenal. The shirtless mammoth falls squarely into that category.\n\nBesides, we have too much to do to worry about stepping on each other's feelings.

Khunzar-ri, the mythic Khajiit hero. His legends led me to the Halls of Colossus and gave us the insights we needed to disrupt Kaalgrontiid's plans in Anequina.\n\nIt was Khunzar-ri and his companions who supposedly trapped Kaalgrontiid so long ago.

If I didn't believe them, I wouldn't have studied them. But three or more embellishments accompany every fact a legend contains.\n\nForgive me if I remain skeptical of the tales that he tamed comets and bedded Malacath on a dare.

Za'ji is counting on it. There's no place for slavers in Elsweyr, but there's plenty of room at the bottom of the sea.\n\nPerhaps Khenarthi will even take pity on Nartise and guide him to … wherever it is that Dark Elves go.
There's not a sailor in the Topal Bay who hasn't heard of Admiral Irathi and her practices. Many Khajiit have suffered because of her.\n\nBut now we have a chance to repay this suffering, yes?

Oh, you want a plan! Now, that plan would be … ah!\n\nZa'ji and the bearded one will draw away the slavers. Meanwhile, Caska will help you secure the Perfect Pounce. We'll reconvene when the coast is clear!
Let's just say I'm not discounting the possibility. Aeliah Renmus seems like a respectable woman, but she may not be the best judge of character.\n\nFor now, let's hold up our end of the bargain.
Doesn't mean I have to like it.\n\nFine, I'll fight. Stick close and try not to die, yes? I don't want to have to drag your corpse back to the sanctum and explain what happened to big beard.

And according to Tharn, the cult operates both here and on the island. They must have a way to get from here to there.\n\nThe stockpile of aeonstone and this amphitheater are as good a place to start our search as any.

That entrance has most likely been sealed in response to what you and she accomplished here.\n\nA structure as ancient as this must have other entrances, though. Let's find one and make our way to the amphitheater.
The fortress is built atop the cliffside and a river runs along its base.\n\nThere must be another way into the fortress along the river. I can feel it in my beard.

He was shouting the Dragon language, thu'um they call it. It is magic, in a sense, but not like any you'd learn in the Mages Guild. Dragonguard learn the words to better know our enemy, but Grundwulf is of the rare breed who can speak it as they do.
They are not one in the same. Though I cannot say if drinking the Dragon's blood will affect his talent and I don't care to find out.\n\nGo. Stop him. If we survive this, I'll answer your questions.

Bebbia doesn't wish death on anyone, but she will make an exception for the thieves who ruined Khajiit of the Moons.\n\nNishzo was this one's only lead. If he's dead, then she fears this small scrap may be all we ever see of it.

It seems Nishzo took no chances with the location of his fellow degenerates. Bebbia is certain that these riddles are the key to finding the thieves.\n\nIf you would seek out the pieces they stole for her, she will be ever so grateful.
It should rest in its frame where it belongs.\n\nIn fact, you should have the honor of placing it. You were the one to recover it.
I'm glad to hear it. I knew Za'ji wouldn't let you down. I'm coming with you. If this Dragon is going to attack Senchal, I want to help defeat it.\n\nBesides, I'm sure you could use an extra hand.

I'm good with a bow! Look, I'm aware of the risks, believe me.\n\nBut this city is my home. I can't just stay behind and hope you stop this threat. Not when I can help. I won't stand by while my father and friends are in danger.
If she wishes to protect her home, she should have that chance.\n\nOnce we reach the island, we'll search for the Dragon. Luckily we have the Horn of Ja'darri to help us fight the beast.
Ra'khajin? No.\n\nHe was raised in this temple. We were brothers in all but blood. And yet …  he's the one causing all this death, all this destruction? It cannot be true!
They seek the Clan Mother. Nuziwa does not know why.\n\nPlease, she cannot come to harm. You must find her. The last this one saw, she was heading toward the inner temple.

He was a man worth remembering. Bold, honorable, a man of his word. Grundwulf was never meant for a life of subterfuge and secrets. His biggest regret was failing to die for Reman and carrying the shame of the Dragonguard's failure gnawed at him.

He was speaking the language of Dragons. He had the Voice as the Nords call it. It's a rare talent among mortals. Where you or I could crudely ape the sounds and call it language, he could shout the thu'um as they do and reshape the world.

I only know that it's possible and there are some who study the thu'um. The hermits of High Hrothgar did not share their secrets with me, and if the Greybeards told Grundwulf the truth during his time with them, he never chose to share it with us.

As I said, he was never meant for a life of seclusion. The glory of slaying Dragons alongside the Emperor was more than enough to convince him to abandon the ascetic lifestyle.\n\nHe was quick to distinguish himself among our ranks. I'll miss him.

An order of monks, I'd call them. Recluses who sit at the Throat of the World and practice shouting at the heavens. I sought them out to gain this power for the Dragonguard, but they refused, save for one. A young man, new to the order: Grundwulf.
Mourn Grundwulf with my other battle-brothers and return to my vigil over the Empire. For the few of us still loyal to the throne, our watch is never over.
When our order splintered it spread many seeds. Many took root and grew into something new.\n\nI'm just old bark on a withered stump, but I take comfort among the trees.

Too few for our troubles. It takes a resolute spirit to give everything for a cause. We shed our old skins and arose reborn in the service of his Empire and the coiled-king. I'll shed this skin as well, when it's time for a new beginning.

A Khajiiti wise woman? Hmm. Perhaps they seek her knowledge. It's said the Clan Mothers keep many secrets to themselves, often deceiving others with half-truths and riddles.\n\nDo you know where this Clan Mother is?
Then let's hope we get to her before the cult does. We should get moving.
For now. I recommend we move quickly, however.\n\nThese bouts of weariness strike after I use my magic, and with more and more frequency of late.

Even if he could, I won't be party to forcing anyone to risk their life for my own gain. While I'm sure Carindon doesn't see Selene as any different from an atronach or Daedra, I think otherwise. She deserves as much respect as anything in the Green.
There's a Dragonguard proverb. Prepare your counter before the blow. In other words, if they swing at you, be ready to swing back.\n\nI also recommend we split our forces to cover more ground.
I spotted a cavern northeast of here. Scout ahead and see where it leads. Meanwhile, Caska, Aeliah, and I will search for the main entrance to those ruins.

Aside from convincing Carindon to help? I'm asking myself that same question. This situation is so questionable maybe I'm here to bother asking?\n\nFor example, why is this Dragon blighting the land? Surely it's not for the smell.

Well, there's an awful lot of places Maarselok could have chosen, yet he's picked this quiet little valley with nothing of note. Except an ancient nature spirit helplessly bound by a myopic mage.\n\nWorth chewing while we carry out this crazy plan.
Well said!\n\nI was able to track the Dragon's movements. It should be just up ahead. Aeliah and Caska have agreed to guard this hall while we move forward.

This Laatvulon seeks to destroy all of Tamriel. If Nahfahlaar wants to stop that, I'd say we have a common cause.\n\nAs the Redguard proverb tells us, if we share an enemy, let our blades strike as one.

Then you must listen.\n\nOnce, a cub was born under the eclipsed Moons. Destined not to lead as Mane, but to join the Pride of Alkosh. We trained him as a holy warrior, a hidden protector. But that was not enough for Ra'khajin.
Yes, but greed poisoned his heart. He wanted to rule over Elsweyr, not protect it.\n\nThen the Demon from the East returned. It promised the power of a New Moon, and Ra'khajin listened.

We're going to the ancient seat of Kaalgrontiid's power to face a Dragon that not only possesses the might of Jode's Core but the amplifying abilities of the aeonstone.\n\nI imagine we'll need to be ready for anything.

Your concern is touching, but I'd prefer you save it for someone of lesser stature.\n\nNow, as we leap into the maw of near-certain death, we have one advantage. Kaalgrontiid doesn't consider us a threat. Let's show him the error of his ways.

Ja'darri? As in the Horn of Ja'darri? It seems Nahfahlaar has some explaining to do.\n\nThis Ja'darri must be part of the Pride of Alkosh, perhaps even its founder. Why else would they so prominently display her statue?

The Clan Mother requested we find the mask before Ra'khajin does, so I can only assume it's a relic of great power. Something we wouldn't want in the cult's hands.\n\nWe need to find this divine mask before the Order of the New Moon beats us to it.
Not sure. \n\nSeems he's draining their … strength? Spirit? Something like that. And he's using the aeonstones to do it.
The aeonstone is the problem, yes? We just have to destroy it.\n\nI'll go left, you go right. When we're both in position, we smash the stones. Then we turn tail and get out of here.
Right. So we strike quickly, yes?\n\nThere's a few cultists on the balcony, but they seem occupied. Chances are they won't even notice us.

Of course I want to go with you. You'll need assistance, won't you?\n\nI know that I might not be the strongest of the Dragonguard, or the most experienced. Or even most resourceful. Trust me, I'm aware of my shortcomings. But I can still help.

I'm sorry, it's just … I can't help but feel that I've let you all down.\n\nYahgrondu was dead by the time we arrived. Could I have done something to find him sooner? And Caska helped you find the Order of the New Moon, not me. And my father ….
Oh. Thought it might have been some sort of code ….\n\nWell, guess I'm free now. What do you want?

Not surprising. I am the only one who can keep a ledger around here.\n\nYou hunt Dragons, I figure out where the Dragons are. And what to do with any parts you bring back, yes? It's the most obvious way to help.

Carindon's a warlock from the Mages Guild. He chose Selene as the subject of his research and trapped her soul. To hear him tell it, he saved all of Valenwood from her sinister influence. Justified or not, the fact of the matter is she hates him.
The drums of Lorkhaj beat strongly. Darkness creeps into your heart and death claws at your throat. With strength, with courage, you must find the light.\n\nWill you face Lorkhaj's darkness?
All will be revealed at a later time. The ceremony has already begun.

Alkosh watches with a steady eye. His wayward children have forgotten their purpose and threaten to destroy the natural way. With reverence, with virtue, you must claim his mask and mend the threads of time.\n\nWill you walk the path with pride?
Do not worry, acolyte. Others will give themselves to the aeonstone and become part of a higher power. We require your strength for the battle ahead.\n\nCome. The ceremony awaits.

One moment. I want to check one more thing. I sense that I might be able to draw energy from the stones as well. It will return me to my old levels of power, but at a cost.\n\nAll right. Let's move on for now.

As far as I know, I'm the last of the Dragonguard. Once, my duty was to protect the emperor and defend the empire. Now … now I must carve a new path from the legends of old.\n\nNow I prepare to hunt Dragons.
Then I'll need a new plan. I don't see the lot of us defeating Maarselok without her.\n\nKeep your fingers, toes, tails, and eyes crossed.

Ah, our grand battle within the Daedric realm …. I was ready to lay down my life to protect Tamriel from Molag Bal's dark schemes. Then the battle was done.\n\nI was looking for a new purpose when I heard that Dragons had returned to Elsweyr.

I remember closing my eyes as death embraced me … and then opening them to see the sun rising over the Dragontail Mountains. Beyond that, it's all a blank slate.\n\nBelieve me, Vestige, I would not keep such a secret from you.

Good. Let me take a look.\n\nHmm. So this Lady G's in charge, eh? Yeah, that makes sense. First lesson they teach you in bad guy school: only use the first letter of your name if you're up to no good.

Someone needs to take up the mantle. Besides, faith and legends go hand in hand. They are the whetstone that sharpens my blade.\n\nLet us see where my faith in old legends takes us before we dismiss the notion that my predecessors were Dragon slayers.

A noble goal, wouldn't you agree, Vestige? Evil must be defeated, innocents must be protected. And so we continue to fight.\n\nAt this point in time, I know of no greater evil than the Dragons that rampage over Elsweyr.
Pridehome? Sounds familiar.\n\nAnd what about Lahini, the cub we were searching for? Did you find her?

Really? Ah, well, of course you do! Who wouldn't want the daring Za'ji by their side?\n\nThe offer is tempting. Whoever defeats these Dragons will have their names sung by Moon-Singers for generations.
Hmm. Very well. I will join your order.

You want me to join your order? I mean, that isn't to say I don't want to! Of course I do. I want to protect my home before the Dragons destroy it. I just …. \n\nI didn't expect you to ask me to stay.

The Order of the New Moon? Strange. I've heard the Khajiit speak of Bright Moons, Dark Moons, even a Hidden Moon. But I do not know the significance of a New Moon.\n\nWhat about the green stone you saw in the quarry? Did you learn more about it?

Oh, hardy-har. A half-melted token? Where did you find this? In a dead mer's pockets, no doubt.\n\nOur event only accepts the very finest nobility. Now bugger off before …. Actually, I take it back. I can use someone like you. How about it?

"We only face the darkness of fear so that we may find the light of courage." That's something my mother always told me. An old Redguard proverb, she said.\n\nI'll join your Dragonguard and protect my home. You have my word.

My Snow Lily? No. I haven't had the chance to seek her out as yet. My first duty was to help Kasura rebuild the abbey, and now I must find a way to turn back this Dragon invasion.\n\nAfter that, I will search for Lyris and let her know I returned.
And Nahfahlaar believes this aeonstone can enhance that energy as well.\n\nBy Leki's Blade, this looks grim. A sizable Dragon cult that's able to directly empower their Dragon gods.
Good. We get in, we find out what we can, and then we get out. And if we're lucky, we'll find Lahini along the way.
We kill it, though I'm hardly fit for another battle.\n\nEven so, I doubt we'll be able to deal with the aegis while the Dragon still lives.

Ziss'vo, you are right. The token! Zurnash meant to deliver it, but … sugar brandy. Zurnash got distracted by sweet, sweet brandy.\n\nWait! You could deliver it! Yes, yes! Zurnash will go to sleep to settle his brandy-tummy. You will do this, yes?

Gadnalon represents Elden Root. I have the king's blessing, but he's the one with the authority to speak for our kingdom. It took more leverage to persuade Carindon than I could have negotiated on my own. Altruism isn't in his vocabulary.

Yes! I wasn't sure how it would go, but customers keep coming back for my baked goods. \n\nI sell out of my more popular items within the first hour of putting them out, and now I'm starting to get regular orders!

Senchal can be expensive, so I made a deal with the owner here. Store my beers and ingredients, use their ovens. It's cost effective!\n\nI bake out here too. The aroma attracts new customers, plus brings smiles to everyone's faces.
Hunting expedition? You'll have to be more specific. I organize many excursions for Senchal's elite.

I believe you're right. You know, my people meant to deliver an Orc much like this one before being waylaid by a Dragon. Hm. A welcome coincidence.\n\nGive this token to our hunt master at the bog east of Purring Rock. He'll sort you out. Farewell.
The prophecy of the Dark Aeon and the New Moon … I should have seen it sooner.\n\nBut what of Tharn? Where is he?

Then we must return to the Dragonguard Sanctum and rally our forces.\n\nEven if Tharn managed to overcome the island's defenses, reaching an island in the sky could pose a significant problem. I must ponder the possibilities.
That is more a question for Sai Sahan, but ready or not, they are all we have.\n\nLet us return to the Dragonguard Sanctum and figure out how to reach the floating island.

Tharn's magic. It has a specific … scent. Since he has been training me to understand my attunement, I have learned to recognize his magic and track it when he unleashes it.\n\nI followed the trail and it led me here.

Yes, I know the statue. Za'ji and I passed by it the last time we were in Black Heights. It seemed to unsettle him, but he wouldn't tell me why.\n\nWell, no time to ask him now. I'll meet you by the statue.

Yeah, that sounds about right. Filthy bastards. This Lady G's got a troll-size arse-whipping coming to her and no mistake! Got to get into the event first, though. Hmph.\n\nAll right, I got a plan. I doubt you're going to like it, though.

They're down an Orc, right? I say we offer them a replacement. Me. I don't mean to brag, but they'd be idiots to turn down a specimen like this.\n\nYou demand a ticket to the hunt as payment, then we meet up and find Tajahir and Marekki together. Deal?
Speak to Kasura. She uncovered an ancient Dragonguard tool known as a grappling bow. Such a device may prove useful in our journey to come. Why don't you try to figure out how to best utilize it?

Use the grappling bow to get up to the roof of the training hall and light the brazier you find there. That will demonstrate your innate skill with the device.\n\nAfter that, talk to Sai and see if he's ready to decipher the maps.

Excellent. As the saying goes, a weapon is only as reliable as the soldier who wields it. With that being said, it would be best not to drop the device. It's incredibly old. \n\nNow, are you ready to depart for Wind Scour Temple?
Speak quickly, for the sand in the hourglass never stops falling.

Yes. Burned alive.\n\nFires raged across South Guard at the time—to deal with the flu, yes? Turo used this. He and his thugs pushed their competitors—Khajiit like my father—into this warehouse and set it ablaze. To make it look like an accident.

Yes. But this is in the past. Daini must see to the present.\n\nTuro marks his personal goods with a crude seal to ward off idiots who might be tempted to skim off the top. Search the marked crates, and we should find something valuable.

Not a bad mood. Not exactly. It just seemed to me that whatever was in that letter from Abnur Tharn made him … uneasy. Nahfahlaar was also acting strangely.\n\nI'm worried that something terrible is about to happen.

Abnur Tharn. His letter indicates that you and he worked together. He thinks very highly of you. Some day you must tell me how you accomplished that.\n\nThe old snake says we have important business to discuss. And he's bringing a friend.

He didn't elaborate on either topic. Just mentioned a threat to Southern Elsweyr. Between Tharn's cryptic letter and Nahfahlaar's strange mood, I'm feeling uneasy myself.\n\nTalk to the Dragon. Find out what troubles him while I wait for Tharn.
Not sure. Looks like I have a salty, furry travel companion for a while. \n\nThat might be interesting. I have a suspicion she may be more likely to start a fight than me.

Of course, me being such a friendly, cheerful type. We'll see what's going on here in Southern Elsweyr. Maybe help out with this Dragon problem they have. \n\nNever fought one of those big boys. That'll be something to boast about.
I could go back to Sai Sahan and report in. But that doesn't feel right to me.\n\nWith so much at stake and so little time left, I want to do more to support our cause.

Do they? Yes, Tajahir already feels Khenarthi's breath on his face. I … I do not have much time.\n\nMarekki fled to the ruins, but she shares Skordo's temper. You must protect them both from themselves, yes? Keep … keep them safe.

She goes there to kill the one who did this. Lady G. Go north, along the river … crumbling walls and a door. Marekki is there. Hurry!\n\nI did not think I would die this way. Hunted like an animal. Why would they do this to me? Why …?

Oh! Lady Ghisliane. Well, that is a different story. My apologies. You would not believe the caliber of people one must deal with in Senchal.\n\nWhat could Lady G want of me? I'm just having my servants pack for the hunt. I am quite thrilled to attend.

I assure you, it wasn't from me. Or from any close friends. Of course I mentioned it to them, but they are discreet. \n\nI do assure you that some of them are keen to attend as well. Of course I would only recommend those that can afford the fees.

Well… I showed them the token. And of course we discussed what weapons I should bring for hunting. \n\nI heard she has several new creatures, including a Nord and even a Redguard. Is it true? I hope its true - it will be such a challenge!
That it's an exclusive, invitation only…. wait a minute. That is a strange question. I've already been vetted by Lady Ghisiliane's aide.
I do not like your tone.  You had better leave, or I will have you arrested. \n\nThe nerve! As if gutter trash like you two would ever be invited.

I do love the secrecy. It all feels so exclusive. I've practically memorized the directions that were sent., about meeting a huntsman to get the final directions to the Lady G's venue. \n\nI cannot wait to hunt her latest prizes. I've heard so much!
Ah, so that's your angle.\n\nThere may be such an individual present, yes. But the arena is awfully full. He doesn't know if he can squeeze you onto the docket.
Well, this one would certainly make room for Caska the Unconquered. There are many who wish to see her fight again.\n\nConvince Caska to fight and you can both enter. A good deal, no?

Watch over me while I try to access Anequina's memories. She helped Khunzar-ri defeat Kaalgrontiid in the past. Perhaps her insights will help us today, yes?\n\nMaybe she will speak to me. Maybe not. If nothing else, I have to try.

Sahrotnax baited the Dragonguard into many forays. He'd burn great swathes of Cyrodiil and force us to pursue him into unfavorable territory. Many died attempting to kill that elusive wyrm, but he always managed to escape. Not this time, at least.

I am as surprised as you are, my friend. But the message I received was clear. You must go to the Moonlit Cove. That is the cavern of the Moon's sacred light, I am certain.\n\nThe answer to our problem waits for you there.
Then I believe you, my friend. And the vision just confirms my conviction that Anequina's message was meant for you.\n\nNow, go to Moonlit Cove and find the answer we seek.

I understand, my friend. Sometimes it takes a while for us to make sense of the things we see and hear. Be watchful. And if the spirit returns, seek to understand the meaning of its presence.\n\nNow, go to Moonlit Cove and find the answer we seek.
Ghost cat? Like the spirits that accompanied us through the Shadow Dance Temple? Strange. I did not see this spirit.\n\nAre you certain of what you saw?

My friends and I tried to follow, but we lost them. And I'll admit, I was well in my cups by that time. Hard to track with your head full of rum.\n\nRanza, though. He's our best tracker. He might have followed them after the rest of us gave up.
But what was that about the cavern of the moon's sacred light? Sounds like another riddle. I'm beginning to hate riddles.
An excellent idea. Wisdom and reason are sharpened into focus every time we scrutinize the things we learned.\n\nWhat would you like to discuss?

Yeah. Me too. He was just a pup, you know? Er, a kitten, I guess. You know what I mean.\n\nLeast we settled things with that skeeving Lady Ghisiliane. It's good to know what happened to Tajahir won't happen to anyone else.

The journal described a dormant volcano near the coast of Southern Elsweyr, though I suspect we'll find a cave or ruin nearby. Dragons prefer secure lairs and aren't known to nest out in the open.\n\nPlus, it needs a place to hide the stolen horn.

When Emperor Varen made me captain of his Dragonguard, I swore to protect the Empire. With the return of the Dragons, I knew I had to find a way to fight the beasts—just like the Dragonguard of old.\n\nThe Horn of Ja'darri could be our best weapon.

It's a Dragonhorn of great power, nearly indestructible and able to replenish its innate magic. It has no equal!\n\nWith the Horn of Ja'darri, we have a chance to defeat the Dragons of Elsweyr. Without it, the Dragons have a distinct advantage.

Yeah, she's a scrappy little thing, eh? The flirting's a little weird, but she knows this place like the back of her paw. If we knock our heads together, maybe we'll have enough smarts to avoid getting kidnapped again. Ha!

Honestly? Marekki is bedraggled, and no mistake. Matted fur, sore paws, dull claws, and not a scrap of cloth to conceal this sensuous physique …. That's what a kidnapping-turned-person-hunt will do to you, I guess.\n\nLosing Tajahir hurts the worst.

Hmm. For now, Marekki will stay with Skordo. Look at him. That pouty chin and those sad slumping shoulders. He needs a friend, yes? Plus, he is not so bad on the eyes, eh? Those calves! Mrowl.\n\nAh. I mrowl too much, yes? Ha! Marekki takes your point.

I never heard of Vahlokzin before we saw the name in the journal, but Dragons are clever creatures. Besides, the Dragonguard was dissolved around that time.\n\nIn all likelihood, the sanctuary was abandoned, leaving the Horn of Ja'darri undefended.
What an unusual question. As I understand it, you've already faced a mighty Dragon. After all, great deeds set the stage for great victories.

Yes, with the help of the Changeling spirit Selene no less. I suppose she would find offense that a Dragon had begun to spread such corruption in the forests of her home.\n\nI hear it was a mighty battle of flame and decay.
Still, you faced the Dragon's flame and rage. And Grundwulf …. A vampire Dragonguard, yes? A difficult foe to defeat.\n\nA shame that one of my order would fall so far from grace.

And lived to tell such a glorious tale! I hear they were mighty battles both, filled with fearsome vampires and fiery destruction. You have proven yourself a worthy warrior, ready to hunt down the Dragon Vahlokzin.

Regardless of the risks we face, we have a duty to Tamriel to retrieve this Dragonhorn. \n\nBesides, I assure you that I am well up to the task of hunting a Dragon. I earned both my title of blademaster and the rank of captain of the Dragonguard.

As luck would have it, Sai Sahan and Blademaster Kasura have plans to repay a debt of pain to these Dragons. I'm hoping he can spare some assistance with some plans of my own. Maarselok has a lot to answer for.
Interesting choice of words there. As it happens, the Dragon hasn't attacked us, but its presence is doing something unwholesome to the land. He's blighted an entire valley near Valenwood.
Not with that aura of magic that surrounds it. I'll wait here and guard the place against those pirates. You go and find the missing pieces of the tablet.

Oh, the usual. Dragon killing. Z'en's retribution, they're everywhere now! Thankfully, we're not the only ones fighting back. Sai Sahan is rallying the troops! So, I'm throwing myself behind that effort. The Dragons have a lot to pay for.

Oh, fine. Selene's got her hands full with healing the damage Maarselok caused. It's keeping her out of trouble. She's steering clear of our people in the area. Not that I can blame her. I just hope Carindon hasn't destroyed her trust completely.

We tried to handle it ourselves, but the army King Camoran sent to kill it hasn't returned, and it doesn't look like they're ever going to. Now we're weighing our options. One way or another, I'll come up with something.

That is how some, like Grundwulf, bought their time, but like our fractured order we've each had to find our own paths.\n\nI am masterless, but I am no rogue. I am sworn to preserve his Empire until a true successor ascends to the throne.

She cursed and spat like a wild beast. This one told her to stop, but she would not listen! They took her to Turo's slave ship—southeast of here, through the cave. The ship only stays in port a short while. You must hurry!\n\nBut first, let me out!
A thousand thanks to you, walker!\n\nMalahbu only hopes that Daini and Safik still live. Be careful!
Bah! Nobody ever lets me help!\n\nFine, fine. But if anything happens to Daini or Safik, there's no power in Tamriel that'll keep Turo safe from me! Mark me!
Yeah, yeah. Thanks. Give those bastards the business, all right? Especially Turo!
What an unusual question. Don't you know that great deeds set the stage for greater victories? And what a deed you already accomplished, facing down a mighty Dragon!

Rumor has it that all of Anequina knows you to be a mighty Dragon hunter. Honestly, I find it invaluable to fight alongside someone with your expertise.\n\nVahlokzin should prove little trouble for you and I.

Regardless of the risks we face, we have a duty to Tamriel to retrieve this Dragonhorn. \n\nAs a blademaster and captain of the Dragonguard, I am quite up to the task of helping you take down this Dragon.
There are many more parasites and their stone sentinels in this temple. Hardly a threat compared to what you've already overcome. With one exception: a vicious looking Pahmar-raht prowling around.
Of course! Here you are.\n\nWe've erected several grapple points around the abbey. Rather than direct you to them, I'd like to give you the chance to explore.

I'm honestly not sure. It is strange, isn't it? Why would someone display an ax in the Valley of Blades.\n\nBlademaster Sai Sahan does come here to tend the snow lilies, but he's never been inclined to explain why.

Blademaster Sai is a private man, and one I respect. I do not wish to bring up a topic that he would rather not speak of.\n\nBesides, some secrets are best left alone. And I have a feeling this ax represents one of them.

Blademaster Sai Sahan calls Lyris Titanborn … snow lily? Well, that does sound awfully romantic. \n\nPerhaps this shrine is for her, then? The strength of steel, the beauty of flowers; a quiet devotion, away from prying eyes. Sounds lovely.

The white flowers growing around the shrine. They aren't native to Hammerfell, so they must have been imported. Or perhaps they were a gift? \n\nThey're hardy flowers, but he still makes a point to fuss over them.

Yes, it is.\n\nLyris and Blademaster Sai Sahan returned to the Abbey of Blades to help us rebuild. And for some time, the two were quite happy. Their love for each other was as obvious as the sun in a cloudless sky.

Blademaster Sai never shed a tear, but I can see the sorrow in his eyes when he visits this shrine. It's easy to see how much he misses her.\n\nI do hope they meet again one day. If this shrine says anything, it's how devoted they are to each other.
She left the abbey one day, without a word. This ax was all that she left behind.\n\nIn a way, I wonder if she was also leaving behind a … a promise, I suppose. As if to say she would one day return.

Lyris Titanborn? Perhaps so. Blademaster Sai brought it back with him, after your fight with Molag Bal. I could see that his heart was broken, though he would not say why. \n\nDid Lyris … did she survive your battle?

That is true. He even planted these flowers. Snow lilies, they're called.\n\nSo this shrine is to honor Lyris Titanborn …. The strength of an ax, the beauty of flowers. What a wonderful way to remember the person you love.

Then this shrine must be to honor her. How could it not?\n\nWhen Blademaster Sai returned to us, he was broken. Empty. And I can't help but wonder if his desire to fight Dragons, to save Elsweyr, if that stems from a need to … forget her.

I believe so.\n\nShe visited the abbey, you know. After Blademaster Sai Sahan was … sacrificed. She never shed a tear, but I could see that her heart was broken. It was then that I knew she loved him.

An ancient relic, its blast forces even the most powerful Dragons to fall from the sky. It provides a great advantage in battle.\n\nI've slain one Dragon with it. And with your assistance, I hope to slay many more.

The Dragonguard of old proudly defended the Empire as well as hunted Dragons. I can no longer serve Emperor Varen, but I can continue their traditions.\n\nI was even able to find one of their fabled Dragonhorns, the Horn of Ja'darri.

An ancient relic whose sound can force even the most powerful Dragons out of the sky. It gives us a great advantage in battle.\n\nOne Dragon has already fallen to my blade and horn. With your help, I hope to slay many more.

The Dragonguard of old defended the Empire and hunted Dragons. While I no longer serve Emperor Varen, I can still continue their proud traditions.\n\nI even acquired one of their Dragonhorns, the Horn of Ja'darri.

Despite our past differences, the general did come through when we needed him. I extended an invitation and he decided to accept.\n\nOf course, he mostly came to find out what we could tell him about the floating island.

General Renmus wishes us success in our mission, but he won't leave Senchal undefended.\n\nIt falls to the Dragonguard to assault Kaalgrontiid's stronghold. The general's forces will remain in reserve, protecting the city and ready to act if we fail.

That is the part I have not fully worked out yet. But in Anequina's memories I saw a place between places, full of moonlight and stars. We must walk the Jonelight Path, just as Anequina, Khunzar-ri, and the kra'jun did in the ancient past.

You are, five-claw. You and Sai Sahan. We are kra'jun, a company of heroes.\n\nTogether we will walk the Jonelight Path and see where fate takes us. Trust me, my friend. This is what the three of us must do.

You'd be surprised what people tell a respectable gentleman with a distinguished beard.\n\nTake <<1>>, for example. I heard that she's been seeking a way to leave Senchal for weeks. A few gems would certainly help pay for her passage.
Yes, Leki willing.\n\nHad we the time, I would go through official channels. But with so much at stake, we can't afford the delay. We have no choice but to use these underhanded measures.
Steady, sleek one. The sparkling waters streaming from the shrines are sacred!  Their spiritual strength will safeguard you and allow you to sanctify the shoal once more. Shazar is seldom mistaken.

To strip the sacred sugar suspended in the shoal's shallows. All the light Jone and Jode shines upon the sea surges into this cove and mixes with the spring waters spilling from our shrines and settles on the shoal, ensnaring the moonlight within.
Well, I can certainly tell you what Sai has told me.\n\nWhen the Dragonguard hunted Dragons, they each crafted their own grappling bow. This one was found in a Dragonguard's grave.

I don't think any of us will have time to train to that level. With a little practice, however, it could serve as a means for achieving out of reach places. I think that's the best we can hope for in this particular instance.

Only that early Dragonguard stayed there for a time among the Khajiit. Something terrible happened—something terrible always happens—and it was abandoned long ago. The Khajiit no longer go there. I believe they say it's cursed by Eastern demons.

Laatvulon appeared suddenly and without warning over the skies of Senchal. If he had been lairing in Doomstone Keep we would have known before now. There's more to this.\n\nEither way, we make east for the keep. Our quarry and our answers lie there.

General Renmus will lead a secondary team to keep the cultists occupied. That should give us time to search for Nahfahlaar.\n\nBy Leki's Blade, I just hope he's still alive. We'll be hard pressed to take this keep without him.
This is it, my friend. Our chance to prove ourselves. To prove that the Dragonguard still protects the people of this world.\n\nYou scout ahead and find a way forward. I'll join you in a moment.
The cult is gathering around Laatvulon, most likely to empower him using their aeonstones. Yet another advantage they have over our forces.

I worked up the courage to write to my Khajiiti family. My Uncle Hizhikar answered. I said I was the best Khajiit trader in Wrothgar and he invited me to help with the family business.\n\nI lied. But even I could see the quality of his moon-sugar!

I don't really remember. I was very young. My Khajiiti parents were merchants heading to Orsinium when something happened.\n\nMy parents died and I was lost in the wilderness … until my Orc mother found me. Raised me to be a proper Orc, too!

That would be Maezi. She works for my uncle. Best caravan guard in the business, that's what Uncle Hizhikar said. And I believe him! Maezi is fantastic!\n\nShe's smart, funny, brave. She fought like an Orc. Even chased after the thieves when they ran.

I want to say three, but it was dark and they came at us so fast. Had to be at least three to haul away my uncle's gourmet moon-sugar. There could have been more.\n\nI hope for Maezi's sake it was only three, though.

Yes. I gave her my horn, but it was not enough. And so she asked me to empower the Mask of Alkosh, so that we could slay Laatvulon and end his terror. I refused.\n\nLaatvulon was sealed away, but not before Ja'darri fell in battle.

Dragons, yes, and something far worse as well. Laatvulon. The Demon from the East.\n\nIt was not enough to seal it away. You must succeed where Ja'darri failed. You must banish the demon unto eternity, as Alkosh wills.

Laatvulon is the torment of chaos, a shadow wearing a scaly hide. It seeks to drench this world in anguish, as is its very nature.\n\nIt will pave the way for another. A New Moon filled with darkness. Then the tapestry of time shall unravel.
Brooding, as usual. Nahfahlaar may have pulled through as our ally, but he's still not one for socializing with mere mortals.\n\nHe did say he wished to speak to you when you returned.

The Sea of Ghosts doesn't suffer fools. Never has. But now, some dark magic's driven it mad! Great gales whip around this island, breaking masts like kindling-wood and drowning sailors by the dozens.\n\nHigh King Jorunn sent us to investigate.

Nice work. I'll tell you, that island changes hands more often than a greasy gold coin. The Nords might keep it for a while. I guess we'll see how long it takes for the next gang of Reach maniacs to snatch it back! Not until you're far away, I wager!
