His every thought is of what new depravities he can subject me to. I live with his cold eyes boring into me as deeply as his instruments.\n\nI am not the monster here!

Blademaster Kasura can tell you more. I am not privy to enough details to speak on her behalf.
Both fare as well as can be expected. \n\nBlademaster Kasura has recovered much of her strength and started rebuilding the Abbey of Blades. We lost many, yes … but we have not given up hope.
Blademaster Kasura can tell you more. I am not privy to enough details to speak on her behalf.
Are you mad? Keeping her on a taut leash is the only defense we have against her insidious influence. If freed she'd simply return to dominating others. It's her nature. Her instinct.

That's one reason. Another is that studying her allows me to make great strides in the advancement of civilization. Her essence alone … ah, you're implying that I'm a hypocrite.\n\nSpare me your judgment.
A large limestone quarry lies to the south. Laatvulon and his followers have seized it, though I do not know why.\n\nStrange that Yahgrondu should be there now.
Unlikely. Yahgrondu is still bound to me by his oath. He would not join with my greatest enemy.\n\nHead to the limestone quarry and search for this mine. I will meet you there.
No sign of the Dragons, but there are plenty of cultists. They're mining and keeping watch.\n\nThis doesn't make any sense. What would a Dragon cult want with limestone?
Anything we can use against the Dragons. Tomes describing hunting techniques and strategies, weapons … honestly, whatever appears to be useful.\n\nIf you spot something of value, let me know.

Bah! What else is there to know? Nothing but clawless brutes, all of them!\n\nSorry. Daini has lived under the heel of these muskarses—and muskarses like them—all her life. I did not mean for them to die, but I cannot shed a tear at their passing.

Waiting for Laatvulon to leave. Had I faced him now, he would have overpowered me.\n\nDo not think me proud of such actions, hunter. Laatvulon has somehow increased his power. We are not prepared to fight him just yet.

To raise one of my kind takes great skill and greater preparation. Ra'khajin used the green stone to amplify his necromantic abilities.\n\nThat stone. It must be why Laatvulon's cult has claimed this mine.
When Laatvulon hears of your victory, he will return to secure this mine. We must return to the sanctum before that happens.\n\nAfter that, we can decide our next course of action.

Only that it affects the flora and fauna alike, poisoning and twisting them. If they're lucky they die. I'm hoping Selene can fight back against the blight, otherwise we might not even make it to Maarselok at all.
South of Black Heights, Za'ji's childhood village. Just follow the ringing of the bells, yes? You can't miss it.

A Dragon has taken a nearby island as its lair. I believe it means to attack Senchal from this location. We need to slay the creature before it strikes.\n\nUnfortunately, I haven't been able to secure a ship willing to take us to the island.

Daini, why can you not just—? Safik's sister is wise and prudent in all things except this business with Turo. You must understand, he hurt us deeply. She refuses to let it go, even as we try to escape this place.\n\nIs she coming soon?

I'm afraid that would be unwise. My duty is to the Abbey of Blades. I cannot leave it undefended for any length of time.
And Sai Sahan remained here to watch over things in my place. One of us must remain, and since Sai cannot, it must be me.\n\nI wish you good luck and good hunting, warrior. May Leki guide your steps.
The Mask of Alkosh.\n\nLaatvulon is a fool. His pathetic priest will never be worthy of such a relic. Not like Ja'darri. They chase that which they can never hope to control.
Then learn the truth for yourself. \n\nIf you seek the mask, speak with the Clan Mother of Khenarthi. It was her temple that cared for Ja'darri's remains.
Ja'darri. I called her Toshrakhat. The founder of Pridehome and the first of Alkosh's pride. She once wore the mask, yes. And I suspect her corpse guards it still.\n\nBut none of this matters.
I ran … dodged falling bricks and leapt over collapsing floors. Made my way to the surface … only to find we were a league or more in the sky.
Of course he did. If we survive this, you can explain that to me later.\n\nNow, let's go try and kill that damn Dragon.
I did what any proper battlemage would do … I hid. As you can see, I'm in no condition to take on Kaalgrontiid by myself. So I watched … and waited.\n\nHow did you get back here, by the way?
I expect the task falls primarily to you and Nahfahlaar. Use the bond created by the mask to synchronize your actions. Then reduce the aeonstones to so much rubble.

It's an Imperial war college called the Topal Legionary Academy. Or it was, at any rate. Now the locals call it the Forsaken Citadel.\n\nSome of the Empire's greatest tacticians studied and taught here—my mother among them.

I am. Following in my mother's footsteps, I suppose. Or trying, at any rate.\n\nAs I said before, she served as a consul before she passed—tending to the concerns of Imperial citizens and breaking bread with the Khajiiti councilors in Senchal.

She began her career as a legionary, believe it or not. She even taught here for a time. I suppose she just softened with age.\n\nHonestly, my mother rarely spoke of the time she spent here. I always got the sense she preferred to leave it in the past.

I am Jano Invel, Imperial battlemage and spellcraft instructor. And yes, I wrote that letter.\n\nWhat is this about? After twenty years of imprisonment, I won't suffer idle conversation. Speak plainly or leave.
Tried to lower the drawbridge, you say? Well, that certainly doesn't bode well for us.\n\nTell me the riddle.

Hmm. Khenarthi is the Khajiiti god of travel, not unlike Tava, the Bird God. Alkosh is called Akatosh by most, the Dragon God of Time. And the Mane is a Khajiiti spiritual leader.
A grappling bow, of course!\n\nI confiscated this one from Za'ji back in Senchal, but I forgot to return it to Sai Sahan. It's pretty easy to use. Just aim, shoot, and hold on tight.

Garrana? By the Eight ….\n\nYes, I recognize both the name and the locket. That piece of jewelry was to serve as the focus for a soul warding spell. We meant to use it to keep us safe from the flu, but then Honoria left, taking the necklace with her.

I hesitate to hope, but yes. Yes, perhaps it could.\n\nAfter Honoria left with the locket, I attempted to craft new focuses—totems made of Honoria's treasured objects. All three attempts failed, and the result …. Well, look around.
It wasn't his hideout then, but yes. Well, no. Za'ji knows where he left it, though!\n\nCome, walker! Za'ji has a lock box hidden nearby.
I considered that option, but without a mage of Abnur Tharn's experience and abilities, we have no way to use the aeonstones.\n\nNo. I think we'll need a different solution.

As far as I can tell, the Dragonguard of old never faced this particular obstacle.\n\nWe need to find a way to reach that island and we need to do it quickly. Talk to Queen Khamira. Perhaps you can help her figure out something with her portal magic.
Reports tell me that the Dragons have moved into Southern Elsweyr, ravaging towns and villages along the way. That is where I will go, and I'll send for you when I get there.

I will continue to watch over the Abbey of Blades, as best as I am able.\n\nThere are many students who wish to learn the ways of the blademaster. As long as there's strength in these old bones, I will do my best to teach them.
I've been far too busy. Between helping rebuild the abbey and finding a way to fight the Dragon invasion in Elsweyr, there's been little time to socialize.
Yes, she did. For a time. I hoped she would join me in my efforts to reclaim the wisdom of the Dragonguard.\n\nBut something else called my Snow Lily away. Something Lyris felt she had to do.

I'm not certain where Lyris is, truth be told. Kasura told me that she visited the abbey, but departed soon after. And as I said, I've been quite busy.\n\nI do plan to find her, eventually. If only to make sure she's doing well.
It's not a matter I'd like to discuss, Vestige. Not when there's still so much to do.\n\nI don't plan to forget her, of course. But there is little time to deal with grief when so much is at stake.

Simply drink it, like any other potion. If your vision blurs, it is working. You may think you are drunk, but it is because your eyes now focus on another world.\n\nIt will not harm you. Though when it wears off you may wish you were drunk.

Focus on Vijari. You should see the dro-m'Athra's darkness clinging to his soul. It clings to other things as well. Things closely connected to it. Find them and the tonic will allow you to see the impressions it left on our world.

We won't be alone. We'll rally others to our cause, those willing to take up the mantle of the Dragon hunters of old. It will be glorious!\n\nWe still have so much to learn, though. So much to do to reignite the Dragonguard.

She is sorry that she is not more help in that regard. This is no ritual she has heard of before. Adara'hai is certain the ingredients have symbolic value, but beyond that she can only guess their meaning.

Truly? That makes your experience invaluable to our efforts.\n\nTell me, what does a Dragonhorn look like? How is it used?

So the legends are true. Incredible.\n\nA Dragonhorn would give us the edge we desperately need to combat the Dragon invasion of Elsweyr. After all, a Dragon is far easier to fight on the ground than in the sky.
Vijari, Vijari, cannot flee. Khenarthi, Khenarthi, is the key.

I would say so. I was happy to help Sai prepare for his own battle, but I cannot join him in that fight.\n\nHowever, Sai is a strong warrior and a fine leader. He'll be able to rally allies to his cause, of that I have no doubt.

I'm afraid she did not say. Perhaps it was something she wished to do alone, or perhaps she was afraid I would forsake my duties and join her.\n\nShe did promise to write, though. I eagerly await her letters.

Selloe works for some rich High Elf lady who collects unusual creatures. Or so she says. Still, she pays decent gold for something unusual. And you wouldn't believe what shows up here sometimes, from the boats or the pirates.

If it was a zoo, why so secretive?\n\nI only know that Selloe or others are down here regularly enough, always looking for interesting creatures. And maybe those creatures include people like me and you.
Selloe? No, she's your typical servant. Her mistress though. You hear rumors. \n\nShe runs some sort of game. Something that earns her a lot of gold from bored rich people.
A job, eh? What does she want you to do? Got to tell you, I'm not real excited about knocking heads together for those tuskless kidnappers.

According to the journals, the horn was indestructible. And Stendarr knows that Dragons are as close to immortal as the earth and sky.\n\nWe learned of the Horn of Ja'darri for a purpose. We will find it. Of that, I am sure.

Despite its age, the map we found in the journal clearly indicated where we must go. The Dragon Vahlokzin lairs in a dormant volcano in Southern Elsweyr.\n\nI ask you, my friend, will you make this journey with me?

They served the Second Empire for centuries—even ruled it for a time through the Potentate. You see their influence all over the place here in Elsweyr.\n\nAnyway, the Empire has leaned on Akaviri war doctrine since … well, the beginning, I suppose.

The dangerous kind! But the greater the danger, the greater the rewards, yes?\n\n<<1>>  offers tasks that you can accomplish alone, and <<2>> seeks groups of heroes to challenge more powerful foes. Believe Tsaraba—they both pay well!

People come to Guybert from all over Elsweyr seeking heroes for odd jobs.\n\nHis tasks will take you to caves and ruins. Places like that give Tsaraba the shivers. But a hero like you? This one wagers you can face those perils alone and still succeed.

I couldn't tell you.\n\nNahfahlaar comes and goes as he pleases. He doesn't feel the need to report in to us mere mortals. Not that I expected courtesy from a Dragon, mind you.
What a relief, on both counts. Did you discover the cause of her distress? What troubled her?

Not expressly, they sent me here to negotiate. To be honest, Selene scares the dirt out of me, but she defended the Green and that's what matters to me.\n\nI do enjoy sticking it to Carindon, but that's just an unexpected bonus.

A wise request. Our enemy is Laatvulon, a Dragon of great power and greater evil. He seeks to destroy Tamriel, though we do not yet know how he plans to do so.\n\nWe do know that he leads a large cult and has several Dragons working with him.

Honestly? Not great.\n\nMy first mission as a Dragonguard went terribly wrong. The more we learn about Laatvulon, the less confident I become. If he decides to attack Senchal, I don't think there's anything my father can do.

I suppose. But Senchal has been my home for five years. It means more to me than the Empire ever did. I can't bear the thought that it might be destroyed.\n\nI remember when I first met Za'ji. He asked me who I was but immediately stopped me.

Orbick! Yes. That house by the stairs. This one almost made it, but then … you know. Brandy. You will tell Selloe I am sorry, yes?\n\nHere. Put on these clothes. Have to look presentable for Orbick. Sugary Moons guide your … your path.

'Course he is. Ugh. Always with the sneaking around. \n\nAll right, fine. Let's deliver the token. I'll keep Auberic distracted before I hand it over. You sneak around his house and see what you can learn about this little event they're planning.

I'm even worse at sneaking. Anyway, I've got the upper hand. I bet he's not used to entertaining big scary Orcs. \n\nIt'll be fine. You just focus on finding more information, all right? I want to know what we're dealing with before you talk to Lady G.
I told you, it's a gamble. There's a good chance none of us will walk away from this. If we go bust, we do it together.\n\nThat sounded more reassuring in my head.

I prefer working with live specimens, or near enough. Dragons were nothing more than old bones and tall tales until their recent reemergence. So, no, I have nothing to offer. Though, capturing Maarselok alive would offer ample opportunity for study.
Why Allanwen is so cozy with Selene, for one? All that Z'en business felt like there was a lot being left unsaid. I'm not siding with Carindon, Y'ffre knows, but I don't exactly trust Selene either.

She certainly did. We'll follow along shortly.\n\nIn order to make a good impression, the Dragonguard needs to be ready. I'll instruct Za'ji and Caska on proper etiquette and protocol. Hopefully, some of what I tell them will stick.
No! No, no. I just get the impression she knows something we don't.\n\nIf she is up to no good though, get me out of here alive, would you?
A broad term. Vague and useless. I am a Changeling. I am the pure essence of the Green and I may take any shape within it.
The Goddess of Spiders. You are too far removed from the Green and the birth of the world to know her name, but her blessed creatures thrive within it.
Anyone would, if they knew what it was like. They are blessed with perfection by Shagrath. It's only fitting that her High Priestess embody that perfection.

Supply run! Sai sent us to Senchal for food, bedding. You know the deal.\n\nSo Za'ji thought, what does our Dragonguard really need? Some libations! And what sort of fool purchases a barrel without first tasting a pint?
Right then! Sure. Za'ji just needs a quick nap. Three or four hours and he'll be ready for action!

Very much so. There is no one else I trust to handle such a delicate negotiation.\n\nGeneral Renmus has an idea this is coming. I want you to officially present the offer and determine what he thinks.
Of course! Takes a few barrels to get Caska tipsy. On account of her being very large, you understand.\n\nZa'ji will heroically get these supplies back to the sanctum! After one more round.

It was easy enough to learn about that braggart. I overheard him in the tavern, claiming that he could forge any document in Senchal. For the right price, of course.\n\nLet's see if he has the skills to back up his boasts.

Leave this place behind as fast as my feet will take me. The king will want my report about this mission, and the fate of the soldiers he sent on before us.\n\nI think he'll forgive us for not honoring the Green Pact under the circumstances.

I do not. I was never a great scholar nor philosopher, and that hasn't changed since last we spoke.\n\nFor now, I simply wish to take advantage of my unexpected survival and help Elsweyr fight back against this Dragon threat.

Well, you showing up wasn't expected, but everything else went about as predicted.\n\nHad Carindon kept his bargain and agreed to some restitution, Z'en might have offered his mercy, but as it stands he's got a considerable debt to repay.

We arrived a short time ago. After Queen Khamira abandoned us, we had a long march down from the north. Zamarak would have worried about her more, but we had Dragons and other hostile creatures to deal with along the way.

There's still work to be done to repair the damage caused by Euraxia. And the queen is very generous when it comes to compensation.\n\nWhen Zamarak needed a few troops to bolster the royal chaperones, I volunteered to accompany the Irregulars.

You were on that expedition then? I'm all too aware of Carindon's actions, but the fact of the matter is we need them both. They'll have to put aside their differences or Maarselok will corrupt them along with this valley. Even Carindon sees that.

Selene is a being closer to the Green than even we are. Sitting helpless to stop its perversion must be more painful than anything Carindon has done, and staying bound makes her vulnerable to Maarselok's influence. It's in her best interest to help.

I suppose. But I will not forget what you have done for all of Elsweyr, my friend. You and Abnur Tharn both.\n\nPerhaps the old battlemage deserves a statue? Hrrm. I will think on that when I am not dealing with the ongoing issues of state.

The Dragonguard still has much to learn. And there remain Dragons to deal with.\n\nAfter that? I need to find my Snow Lily. Let Lyris know I'm all right. You won't believe how much I miss that beautiful half-giant!

Truthfully? Not a bit. Zar's story ended where yours began. And it was a pleasure to witness your triumphs and tragedies. An honor.\n\nMay the legacy of your kra'jun last as long as Zar's did. No, longer!

Do not mention it! Now, prepare yourself. Hero work is tiring, yes? And endless.\n\nThe stories repeat, and this is your turn in the cycle. Impending doom, resolute hero, miraculous salvation. Save the world and start again. That is the way of things.

It seems you were affected by Selene's insidious domination. You appear to have forgotten the reckless abandon with which her enthralled servants attacked our expedition. Unprovoked.\n\nI was willing to bargain before she murdered my subordinates.

Even in her present condition, she is an ancient and powerful spirit. Were my research allowed to continue uninterrupted, I could develop a means to exert more control over the Changeling, but for now I only have the power to contain her.
Very well. You, at least, have proven capable. I will need that if she expects us to coerce Selene into doing her bidding.\n\nThe Changeling is not a creature of reason.
Is that not what I just said?\n\nOr is it you are making a judgment, perhaps, with your echoing of my words? Humanizing Selene would be a fatal mistake. Remember that when you see her in my study.
In a sense. She is soul trapped and bound to me. I cannot make her do anything, but neither can she act without my approval. When my research is free to resume, I may continue to find uses for her.

She is the subject of my research. A nature spirit of considerable power, which is why the Wood Elves seek her cooperation. If they understood Selene like I do, they would realize how foolish that sounds. Selene understands domination, nothing else.

Nahfahlaar returned shortly after we did, but he's been acting strangely. He won't talk to me. Won't tell me what happened on the island after Tharn ….\n\nNahfahlaar trusts you. Can you speak to him for me?

I am two steps removed from the Arch-Mage of the Mages Guild. If you can't comprehend what that means, I won't waste my breath on the explanation.\n\nWe've wasted enough time. My study is that way. Let's be off.

The Wood Elves would like to believe so. I have not yet discovered everything the Changeling is capable of, but I doubt she can defeat the Dragon alone. They must admit that as well by enlisting you.\n\nWith my power, we may stand a chance.

I mean when I found Selene, she had enthralled an entire tribe of Bosmer and laid claim to a swath of their territory. They butchered the expedition I lead without provocation, but I put an end to her tyranny. She serves me now.

Meric Renmus, general of the Thirteenth Legion. Or what's left of it, in any case.\n\nFives years ago, Emperor Aquilarios sent my legion to Senchal. The city had been decimated by the Knahaten Flu and we were sent to help restore order.

Our biggest issue, other than the Dragons, is the influx of refugees pouring in from the devastated countryside.\n\nThey hope to find protection inside our city walls, but many wind up hungry and homeless.

Of course not. I'm a general, not a dictator.\n\nWe defended the city walls as the Khajiit rebuilt their homes. We even worked with citizens of influence to form a city council, given that the entire royal family was wiped out by the plague.
They see our value as protectors, at the very least. The city council even named us the Shields of Senchal. Sounds a bit friendlier than the Thirteenth Legion, I suppose.

Z'en's a god of the Green. His chief virtue is fairness. Honest work, honest reward, proportionate to the deed. Anyone who calls the Green home knows a deal struck in his name is one that must be kept.\n\nShe'll keep her word.
Then you are a great deal wiser than the others. They are too quick to trust a creature that could enslave them effortlessly.

Vanus Galerion agreed to keep his Mages Guild out of my domain, but that did not stop a rotten soul like Carindon from seeking me out and making me his slave!\n\nHe isn't here to help you. Only to protect his spoils.
The follower of Z'en I trust, but she doesn't hold my chains. Carindon is an oathbreaker. He will betray us.
You were protecting that oathbreaker!

We're soldiers, not Dragon hunters. The best we can do is fortify our defenses and pray we escape the notice of the beasts.\n\nPerhaps not the most heroic course of actions, but by far the most sensible.

Vanus Galerion agreed to keep his Mages Guild out of my domain, but that did not stop a rotten soul like Carindon from seeking me out and making me his slave!\n\nHe isn't here to help you. Only to protect his spoils.
Then she is a fool!\n\nHe'll use her as he uses everyone. Only she'll be spared the degradation that Elf has put me through.
His every thought is of what new depravities he can subject me to. I live with his cold eyes boring into me as deeply as his instruments.\n\nI am not the monster here!
Hmph. I won't be free so long as Carindon lives.
It seems I have no choice.

Only a fool would exhaust their power while a threat still looms! I should have let Maarselok take her and let you all wear each other down. I could have taken control of the situation before it slipped out of my hands!
Think! Think, you fool! Or has she warped your mind as well?\n\nDamn you all. She never would have overpowered me if I held back more from the struggle with Maarselok!

Only a fool would exhaust their power while a threat still looms! I should have let Maarselok take her and let you all wear each other down. I could have taken control of the situation before it slipped out of my hands!

You were saving Valenwood from a corrupting influence, just like you did here! And I gave you a commensurate reward!\n\nDamn you all. She never would have overpowered me if I held back more from the struggle with Maarselok!
He should pay, but it won't be me who delivers justice to Carindon. I don't have the strength left to oppose him.\n\nI will watch and wait. If he comes for me again, I will be ready.
Scour this blight from the land and return to my web. It will be difficult, but as I regain strength this valley will flourish again.

He must have believed I could help him shape the world with my powers.\n\nDragons seek only to dominate. Many corrupt with fear, and promises of power. Maarselok chose to mold the world to his liking. Depraved even by Dragon standards.
His constant strangle hold sapping the life out of me. This would have been far easier if I wasn't diminished so.\n\nYou would have been wiser to let me kill him.

Left alone, as was promised. Though I'll ask King Camoran to send some wardens out here to help cleanse the blight. Regardless, I'm confident Selene will restore the valley whether we assist her or not.\n\nWho knows, maybe we'll be allies from now on.
He'll be tied like a hog and unceremoniously dumped on a guild hall floor. I don't know what the Arch-Mage has planned for Carindon after that, but I hear he's an imaginative sort.
I'd love to know that myself, but I haven't heard another word about him since we handed him over to the Arch-Mage. It's probably better this way, I've got a vivid imagination.
Z'en's labors, I can put you to work! You can meet us out there, after we've finished here. Bring some friends though. The more the merrier.

We've never formally met, if that's what you're asking. But there isn't an Imperial soldier who doesn't know how Captain Sai Sahan failed to protect our emperor.\n\nNow the Empire lies in ruins and my legion pays the price of his failure.

We lost our home. Even if we did make our way back to Cyrodiil, where would we go? Who would we fight for?\n\nAnd so we stay behind crumbling walls, waiting in vain for someone to issue new orders. Orders that will never come.

Ah! And so we finally move on to one of Za'ji's favorite topics of conversation.\n\nThe Perfect Pounce is home to the sleekest profiteers this side of the Topal Bay. She is captained by a roguishly handsome Khajiit, who sought fortune from a young age.
Indeed he is! There is no treasure too hidden, no adventure too perilous, no glory too great for Za'ji and his loyal crew!\n\nDanger? This one does not know the word.

In such situations, Za'ji tends to go with his well-toned gut. And his gut says this Dragon will be a problem for Senchal eventually. He will help those brave enough to hunt the beast down!\n\nRight after we find the Pounce, of course.
If he's not, we'll find him eventually.\n\nIf no one has mentioned it, Senche-rahts are excellent hunters. And I have his scent.

That Dark Elf didn't know a bowline from a clove hitch. It was obvious he'd never set sail in his life, yet he was excited to join our crew. Only a fool wouldn't have been suspicious.\n\nNaturally, Za'ji never suspected a thing.

Then you must prove yourself worthy.\n\nThe Path of the New Moon awaits! Obstacles block your path, but your strength will overcome them. Your cunning will even use them. Turn those obstacles to advantages and open the way forward!

Light the braziers to open pathways closed to you. Strike the sliding stones to open doors that hinder you. Make your way through this trial and you shall become a member of our order.\n\nEnter the chamber below and your trial will begin.

Luckily, Za'ji provided a map of the area. I've determined a few locations where I believe Nartise may be, given their relative isolation from the rest of the encampment.\n\nAt the very least, this path should let us search most of the camp.

Yes. The others busy themselves with dusty old tomes and fancy rituals. Feh. Chizbari has no stomach for that foolishness.\n\nDid we come to this place to talk or to make war? This one says, get on with it!

Chizbari saw the beasts up close, just after they erupted from Khunzar-ri's trap. They savaged the surrounding hunting grounds. Killed hundreds of hunters as well. This one's nephews burned like kindling in the first days of the disaster.

Daini would be lying if she said she was not glad to hear it. But then, this one's thirst for vengeance very nearly got us killed.\n\nEnough of that. We should go before Turo's thugs find us. Into the boat, yes?

Another ship was seen heading toward the island. I'm not sure if its crew are friend or foe, but we must be prepared for the worst.\n\nWe can set sail immediately. Or perhaps you would like to take a moment to become familiar with the crew?

Before I made my way to Elsweyr, I searched Dragonguard sanctuaries for weapons and wisdom. There I learned about the Horn of Ja'darri and how it was stolen by the Dragon Vahlokzin.\n\nI found Vahlokzin's lair, slew the beast, and took back the horn.
Indeed. Our journey to recover the relic may have been a long one, but it's proven to be an invaluable weapon.\n\nThat being said, we may find more resistance than just a Dragon on the island.
So his voice was not another mirage in my mind? That is a great comfort to Vijari. There will be someone waiting for him on the other side of the Wall.
Not yet.\n\nI have a contingent of soldiers stationed at the west sentry tower, just northwest of Senchal. They can let you know the current location of your fighting Dragons.

Winks has never failed me before. She's an expert tracker, you know. My brother, Avreg, would use her to find me when I got turned around on a hunt ….\n\nI want to rush down there and rescue Maezi, but I'd probably just make matters worse.

I can't tell you how much I'd appreciate it. Besides, I'm still feeling a little discombobulated from the attack.\n\nI'm going to take Winks and find a place to hide. We'll meet up with you when Maezi is safe and sound.
A paint? Let me see … Rajhin has left you a puzzle, yes?\n\nWhere should we start?
That one is no trouble. Vijari would use cardinal roses.\n\nThough … cardinals do fly … but plants do not. Perhaps it is trickier than he thought.

If you seek weaknesses, prepare for disappointment. I have none.\n\nWhile my brothers were slain or locked away, I have been free. I know when to fight, when to fly, when to look for allies. And so I stand before you, nikrent. Unbroken.

Let Maezi see that. Hmm. The note mentions that a third of the shipment is headed to Senchal while the rest was taken to two drop points. One by the river north of the swamp and another at an old farm.\n\nToo many places for Maezi to cover by herself.

He did? Zhasim is not like other Khajiit. He is … different.\n\nMaezi will find Zhasim and try to intercept the smuggler going to Senchal. Could you go to the drop points and retrieve the rest of the stolen moon-sugar?

No. I lost a horn, but it led to the defeat of my foe.\n\nThe Dragonguard locked away Laatvulon, though their seals did not last. Now my brother seeks revenge that can only be sated by my death. Oblaan voth sos. It will end in blood.

This is not the first time Laatvulon has sought to destroy me and the innocents of Tamriel.\n\nIn the past, another Dragonguard came to me. I gifted them one of my magnificent horns, which your companion holds in his hands.
I've been far too busy. Fighting this Dragon invasion has left little time to socialize.
Yes, she did. For a time. I hoped she would join me in my efforts to reclaim the wisdom of the Dragonguard.\n\nBut something else called my Snow Lilly away. Something Lyris felt she had to do.

I'm afraid she did not say. Perhaps it was something she wished to do alone, or perhaps she was afraid I would forsake my duties and join her.\n\nShe did promise to write, though. I eagerly await her letters.

I'm not certain where Lyris is, truth be told. Kasura told me that she visited the abbey, but departed soon after. And as I said, I've been quite busy.\n\nI do plan to find her, eventually. If only to make sure she's doing well.
It's not a matter I'd like to discuss, Vestige. Not when there's still so much to do.\n\nI don't plan to forget her, of course. But there is little time to deal with grief when so much is at stake.

The Imperial Dragonguard was formed centuries ago by Reman the First, founder of the Second Empire. \n\nThough we seek to emulate the order's Dragon hunting practices, the Dragonguard was originally created to act as Reman's honor guard.

The Dragonguard was officially disbanded. \n\nSome members swore loyalty to the Potentate and acted as his spymasters, while others became mercenaries. There were even members who continued to hunt Dragons, though in much smaller numbers than before.

I suspect it has to do with the order's Akaviri origins.\n\nWhen the Akaviri invaded Tamriel, they were defeated by Reman and ultimately swore loyalty to him and his heirs. They eventually became his Dragonguard.

The Akaviri have a long history of hunting Dragons in their homeland. And so the Dragonguard were both the Emperor's honor guard and accomplished Dragon hunters.\n\nThis lasted for nearly two centuries, until the assassination of Reman III.

Members of the Dragonguard were the premier soldiers of the Empire. They were master strategists, disciplined and honor-bound. It's no exaggeration to say they were the best of the best.\n\nWe, on the other hand, have a crew of pirates.

Yes, how could I forget. I led young Aeliah in her first battle.\n\nNone of them are my first choice, but they've all shown themselves to be dedicated to protecting Elsweyr and its people. They will have to do.

Za'ji is not one to hesitate, walker! Not when a stranger asks him to sail to a Dragon's island, and certainly not when that same stranger offers glory and fame!\n\nThe crew of the Perfect Pounce will join your Dragonguard.
Why would I hesitate?\n\nThese Dragons killed many of my people and I cannot fight them alone. So I will help you hunt down the beasts. A simple decision, yes?

The flu.\n\nThe Knahaten Flu held this region in a vise grip for years, killing Khajiit by the thousands. According to my mother, the commandant locked the academy gates and refused to let anyone in or out. But walls keep out soldiers, not plagues.
Seriously? You aren't pulling my tusk, are you? No, of course not. Well, that is good news.\n\nNow if only we knew where to find the last portion of the stolen moon-sugar.

Truthfully? No one knows. The gates never reopened, and mother refused to speak about it.\n\nI can tell you this, though—someone or something still patrols those halls. People say you can hear groans and howls at all hours. The undead, I fear.

Captain says a lot of things, like "more riches than we can count" and "easy as a spring breeze." Now here we are, hunting Dragons like they're some kind of sky-whales. You are anyway. I got books to research. Who thought reading could be so handy?

Well, once we recover the gourmet moon-sugar, instead of incurring the expense of traveling all the way to Rimmen, we sell the cargo here.\n\nMaezi thinks it's a good plan. We may not get as much as in the big city, but we'll earn a fair price.

Not yet. My uncle gave me a contact in Rimmen, but I don't know anyone here in Senchal. Luckily, Maezi has made plenty of runs for my uncle. She thinks she can introduce me to the right merchants here in town.

Let me see that …. Oh, this is terrible! If the smugglers go through with this plan, they'll ruin my uncle's reputation! No one will ever buy his gourmet moon-sugar again!\n\nOh, friend, could you go across the bay and recover the last of our cargo?
I spent my childhood in Cyrodiil. My father was a commander under Emperor Leovic, and my mother was a Redguard ambassador. Her name was Sadallah.\n\nI had a tough time fitting in with my peers.

They were always questioning who I was. Was I Imperial? Was I a Redguard? They wanted to put me in a neat little box, but I didn't quite fit.\n\nAnyway, my father joined the Colovian revolt and was given the rank of general by Emperor Varen.

Exactly. And a new city helped take my mind off of … other things.\n\nI felt so welcomed in Senchal. The Khajiit never questioned who I was or where I came from. To them, I was simply Aeliah. That was all that mattered.
Father received orders to come to Senchal and help with the restoration. He didn't plan to take me along, as I was only thirteen at the time.\n\nThen my mother died, and … everything changed.

What an eventful day! I lost my cat, my uncle's moon-sugar … even my, er, guard. But thanks to you, everyone is safe and sound. And we even made a deal for my uncle's gourmet moon-sugar.\n\nWhat began as a nightmare has become a dream come true!
I have faced many enemies. Nothing was too big or too powerful for me to challenge. I didn't always win, but I could always fight. \n\nWhen the Dragons came, this was no longer true.
I think I'm a child of two places—Wrothgar and Elsweyr. I don't think I can be truly happy staying in just one of them. But I've got another idea ….

I would rather die on the sands of Pellitine than hide away on foreign soil. This is a chance to make my stand, I will take it.\n\nBesides, if I thought your cause was impossible, I would have said no.

Dirge Truptor has more book smarts than the rest of my crew combined! Now, that's not saying much, since most of my crew can't read.\n\nThe Dragonguard wrote many things, yes? Perhaps he can help you read them.
Well, Dirge has an awful lot of contacts. He always helps us figure out who we can trust and how to avoid those who mean us harm.\n\nMaybe he can help keep track of our enemies in some fashion?

Chizbari the Chipper, as she is known! You'll see why as soon as you hear her lovely voice.\n\nAside from Caska, there's no one more dependable aboard the Pounce. Give her a task and she'll get it done, yes?

The Dragonguard called him the Black Beast, he of the fearsome nature and ravenous appetite.\n\nWe have been in conflict for so long that I barely remember its catalyst. It has been an unending hatred that spans the ages.

I do not know. The magic may have faded, or perhaps someone set him free.\n\nNo matter the cause, my goal remains true. Laatvulon must be stopped once more. And this time, I shall burn his corpse to cinders and shred his soul.
I gave up a horn in the exchange.\n\nThe Dragonguard were unable to slay Laatvulon, but they did lock him away. They thought his prison would hold forever. They were wrong.

Merchants! Weavers! Fishers and farmers! There were no stories of heroes, no glorious tales of adventure. All Za'ji saw in that mural was a life too dull to contemplate.\n\nAnd so this one ran away and never looked back.

A big mural. The villagers each add to it before they die, preserving their stories for generations to come.\n\nZa'ji remembers staring at it when he was a ja'khajiit. The stories of this one's ancestors made Za'ji think … so that's it?

Something to do with the bells, Za'ji thinks.\n\nHe has never seen the ritual, of course. It is only performed in times of dire need. Such as when a group of brave Dragonguard must find a Dragon, yes?

No. The cat they serve, though? Daini knows him all too well. But he is not worth talking about. Someone in my position does not have the luxury of vendettas.\n\nThis one needs wealth to leave South Guard. It is as simple as that.

How refreshing! Most people laugh when I tell them about the snow-whales of Skyrim and their cousins in Elsweyr. You can only spot them while under the influence of my special concoction.\n\nFor a time, you can see them fly by and listen to their song.

I was going to head over to Hammerfell. I hear that, in addition to sand-whales, they also have sky-mammoths that graze upon the clouds over Sentinel. I really want to see that!\n\nAlas, without my special concoction, I won't be able to see a thing.
Well, he's not a very good one, obviously. Probably has something to do with the eye patch.\n\nThis one supposes you should just hand him over, yes?

Impressive yes? An old trick that Daini's father taught her. Set a campfire and fan the smoke toward a herd. They think a blaze approaches and run the opposite direction. Not much left to burn here nowadays, but it still works.

New here, eh? You ask what happened? The Scorch happened.\n\nAt the height of the Knahaten Flu, the Khajiit went mad trying to halt the spread. Frantic cats set fire to houses, towns, whole cities to try to burn out the sickness. It did not work.

Heh. That is what we are meant to believe. One great blaze to purge the flu from South Guard!\n\nIn truth, there were two fires. One meant to deal with the sickness, and another meant to kill …. A story for another time, I think.

Is it not obvious? Ever since the flu, South Guard stinks of ash and bloodshed. No artisans ply their trade here. No merchants sell their wares. Only skooma-dealers, and slavers, and cutthroats remain.\n\nWe cannot live this way anymore.

This is a place of worship, dedicated to Khenarthi, Goddess of the Winds. \n\nShe fills Khajiiti sails and guides our ships to safe harbor. She carries the souls of the departed to the Sands Behind the Stars and leads our heroes to glory.
Why Za'ji would perform such sacrilege is beyond this one's wisdom.\n\nIt wasn't that Tadali was surprised he left. Anyone could see his paws itched for travel. But to steal from our holy temple?

We pray to Khenarthi to share her knowledge, for all of Tamriel feels the caress of her winds.\n\nWe train to hear her words in the ringing of our sacred bells. Through them, we can find that which is lost. So you must get Za'ji to return the bell.

Tadali did not become Clan Mother of Black Heights by holding a grudge.\n\nAnyone who seeks to help Elsweyr against these terrible Dragons deserves our aid. Even if it means dealing with Tadali's traitorous son.
No idea. Za'ji knows he's there, somewhere, but Za'ji has never gone in for a closer look.\n\nWe'll just have to do what Za'ji does best. Improvise!

So mother claims, but how special can one tiny bell be?\n\nZa'ji thinks she just wants to punish him. Make him run all over Southern Elsweyr to prove how sorry he is! And he will, for the Dragonguard. But that doesn't mean he will like it.

My father? But how?\n\nI'll need some time. To process all this. I can't believe she bore the weight of this all these years. In any event, thank you for helping her. I hope the two of them find a way to reconcile in Aetherius. Her and my father.

Assuredly! It sparkles like strands of sapphires sailing on the tide. Before the cove was spoiled by these scoundrels, soaking in the sweet waters brought Khajiit perfect serenity.\n\nNow the spoiled waters stir only sickness and insanity.
Shazar has heard screaming and shouting from within the cove. The senseless shrieking of sugar-tooths whipped into hysteria. The skooma these sinners swill stinks of unsavory scum!
Surely! Though Shazar slogged many days across the Scorch to soak here, so the stench may stem from him ….

He is not worth talking about. Daini hates him, and will continue to hate him until the day she dies.\n\nAll you need know is that he is both evil and wealthy. This one will take that wealth away from him. Daini has nothing else to say on the subject.

A friend. Well, Daini uses that word loosely. An acquaintance, really.\n\nShe fixed herself to me like a barnacle some years back—eating much, but providing little, you see? When I resolved to leave South Guard, she insisted on coming along.
Turo does not respond well to bad news. The people who deliver it … more often than not, it is the last message they ever deliver.\n\nHe will come for us soon after. We must move quicker.
Oh yes. Antonia lies often, but never about something like this. She is a survivor—always has been. Like a Rimmenite alley roach. For now, anyway.\n\nMara help her.

Drop the locket into the flame.\n\nMy grip on the Mundus is weak at best, but I managed to conjure this fire while you were away. It should burn away any arcane energies still clinging to the necklace. Once those magics dissipate … Aetherius awaits.

I can never recall the beginnings, but they always end the same.\n\nI'm standing outside the citadel, just as we are now. Suddenly, I'm inside. I walk down a dank hallway that opens into a larger chamber. Then, I spot him at his writing desk. The man.

No. His eyes flick upward to look at me. Tired, reddening eyes. Much like mine, in fact. We stare at each other for a moment, then I wake in a cold sweat.\n\nI know it sounds simple, but there's an anguish there I can't even begin to describe.

Hmm. A simple question with a complicated answer. Tadali will say this. It warms her heart to see Za'ji standing beside the heroes of Pellitine.\n\nThis one is glad he has good friends at his side. May Khenarthi's winds carry him in a true direction.

Struggles take their toll, walker, and your ordeals have been extraordinary. \nThis one is glad those experiences haven't scarred you. You are stronger from the strife you've seen. Not everyone is so lucky.
Aye. About five years back.\n\nA Reach king called Leovic sat on the Ruby Throne for a time down in Cyrodiil, and the Icereach witches served him as fortune tellers, or advisors, or some such.

Orkey spat on this expedition from the very beginning.\n\nOne of our longships sprung a leak just after we left port. The gales shattered a second one on the rocks before we made landfall. Those poor, drowned bastards were the lucky ones.

It's cursed! Witches, Jarls, Reachmen, and worse have fought over this miserable rock for centuries. Gods know why ….\n\nWe Nords built a fort on it a long time back—to keep an eye on Orcish corsairs harassing whalers, I think.

Yeah. Marekki tells me we haven't taken in all the sights. Still got a few ancient ruins to poke around in, I guess.\n\nCourse there isn't much call for a sellsword after you sweep through an area! Leave a little adventure for the rest of us, eh?
Oh, we are, we are! Sormund will take us.\n\nBut none of us felt right leaving without seeing you and the Dragonguard receive the queen's honor. Plus, we all wanted to see Queen Khamira! She's sleek!
Yes, this one and Daini still plan to take the voyage. But we could not leave without seeing the queen and honoring the Dragonguard!\n\nIsn't all this ceremony grand?
Well, I didn't say that. But I'm glad Daini and Safik talked me into staying long enough to see this grand ceremony.\n\nWe'll all be setting sail for Skyrim soon enough, winds willing.

The springs sparkle again and the smugglers are seeking shelter somewhere else. There are stragglers, of course, but the skooma stills have stopped spilling their slop in the shrines and shoal.\n\nShazar thinks you are deserving of a soak yourself.

Not even close! I could spend three lifetimes there and …. Anyway, its library belongs to Tamriel, not the ghosts of the past.\n\nI plan to arrange an expedition. A proper one. Perhaps Queen Khamira will serve as a patron ….

Are you still fretting about that? Trust me, you have nothing to worry about.\n\nHonestly, if I had a drake for every time I lifted an "hourglass of horrors" or "cup of the damned" I'd be … well, I certainly wouldn't be doing this anymore.

I wish I could call it an act of simple altruism. Alas, I cannot.\n\nWith the sudden rise in necromancy, the demand for undead repellant has gone through the roof! A welcome windfall for mages such as my client.
Special? Well, They're quite lovely for one thing. Aside from that, I believe they react to the moons in some way? Then again, what doesn't react to the moons around here, am I right?

So the chef tells me. But between you and me and the bookshelf, I have no idea how he pays for my services. Bitter-grilled mushrooms? In Senchal of all places? How in Mara's name does he turn a profit?
Mercifully, very little.\n\nDon't get me wrong, Guybert is a man of the world. In my younger days, well … who among us hasn't tasted the forbidden fruit?

You saw its power, not I. Did it not allow the necromancer to raise Yahgrondu from the dead to attack you?\n\nRegardless, you must infiltrate the cult and learn more. Find out what they're up to. Why they follow Laatvulon.

They worship Laatvulon and seek to help him destroy our ally, Nahfahlaar. One of the cult's prominent members, the necromancer Ra'khajin, has demonstrated how they use a strange green stone to amplify magic.

Training our new Dragonguard. The Pounce's crew may be the best smugglers in Elsweyr, but that doesn't make them Dragon hunters.\n\nLuckily, I was able to outfit them with weapons and armor from the sanctum's stores.

They have other things to do?\n\nBut lucky you, these jobs keep the locals happy. It's good for business. General's all about business. It's good for you, too. You get gold from me when you help them all stay happy.
They don't have a choice.\n\nTheir homeland has been invaded and they want to protect it. I'll do my best to help them, but there's only so much we can accomplish with the limited time we have.

There's always hope, my friend. Even in the darkest night, a candle can shine.\n\nThis is the time. To stand against this rage of Dragons. Victory isn't certain, but what in life ever is? We have to believe we have a chance, or all is lost.

For me, it was. That was the moment I understood that I was more than the sum of my parts. I didn't have to be one thing.\n\nIn Senchal I could aspire to be more than my parents' legacy. That's why the city means so much to me.

I started to tell him about my parents. He shook his head and said, "That's who they are. Who are you."\n\nSo I told him everything. How playing the flute reminded me of my mother. How father would never respect me if I didn't follow in his footsteps.

Not sure, really. Don't care much for plants. But the healers say the stuff's important to help soothe Dragon-inflicted wounds. And it's rare. They jabbered on about precise soil conditions, but I stopped paying attention.
Probably needs to feed himself and his students. He's not on good terms with his adeptorium, so food isn't easy to come by, I imagine.

You're asking the wrong person. I recall something about special properties imbued into the temple stone, but then the mages lost me. Mainly sounds like a lot of Meridian nonsense, but I'll ask the mages and tell you when they come back.

It's a temple of Meridia. The Khajiit claim no one uses it, but if a guardian's there ….\n\nWhat I'm saying is, be careful. Meridia's not all sweetness and light. Well, not all sweetness anyway. Kick this guardian a few extra times for me, will you?

From what the locals say? Yes. They have some tale about a Meridian cultist growing the place out of light. Not sure how much I believe that. Sounds like skooma was involved.\n\nOr maybe they like pulling my nonexistent tail.

The citadel. You don't see grand Imperial edifices like this outside of Cyrodiil very often.\n\nPerhaps we can reclaim it. If we manage to rid it of undead, we might rebuild—learn its history. That would make my parents proud. I know it.
Well, it may not be so dire a need as fending off these Dragons, but it was meaningful to us. We will rebuild this city. Dragons and art thieves be damned.

Karzerr, twenty-nine. Silver hair, green eyes, scar under right eye. Missing thirty-one days. Abazita, forty-three. Orange hair, yellow eyes, wears flower-pendant necklace. Missing fourteen days. Lahini, twenty-one .…\n\nThe list goes on and on.

Thirty-two, by last count. And those are just the ones that have been reported.\n\nA lot of them have left the city, what with the Dragons and all. The rest? I don't have the resources to conduct investigations and defend Senchal.

Isn't it obvious? Kaalgrontiid plans to become a god.\n\nThere's an island off the coast. Dragonhold. In the Khunzar-ri legends, it was the Dragon's seat of power. I can't open a portal to it. I can't even scry it. It's protected by potent magic.

He murdered my father! Burned him like kindling-wood! And now he steals my friends? Daini will make him pay! She will rake his eyes out and feed what remains to the dogs! She will ….\n\nNo. No, this has gone on long enough. Safik is all that matters.

Daini will turn herself in to keep Turo distracted. While he gloats and blusters, you must find and free the others. Start at his harbor safe house. It lies south of here, along the coast.\n\nMeet me in his fortress as soon as you can. Moons guide you.

Some ancient Wild Elf ruin, flowing with magic like they do. Heard the Mages Guild's been poking around there recently. Probably aren't looking for the same thing we are, but they get grabby with any reading material left lying around. Best hurry.

Place used to be a respectable ancestor tomb for Dark Elf houses, but something took a turn for the worse in recent years because it's abandoned and crawling with the undead.\n\nNow locals just call it the Corpse Garden. Cheery, right?

Then we look elsewhere, but I figure that's not likely. These bandits were operating out of Windridge Cave. Wouldn't need a map for something they already looted. Way I see it, it's either an old stash or a landmark.\n\nEither way, it's all we got.

Indeed. Perhaps I'm a fool to keep turning you away like this. The more I hear about the forces we're up against, the more I realize that this threat extends far beyond our city walls. Yet my duty must first be to Senchal, no matter the cost.

Not a specific event, but a simmering pot eventually boils over. As long as refugees continue to pour into Senchal, turmoil will continue to brew.\n\nIt doesn't help that my city envoy has abandoned me.
That accounts for one of the portions. What about the other two? My uncle could be ruined if he lost two-thirds of his harvest!

Then I owe you even more, friend.\n\nWhile my time here has been one disaster after another, I think I want to stay in Elsweyr and learn the family business. But if I lose the moon-sugar, my uncle will disown me and send me back to Wrothgar.

Don't be silly! I can visit them and write to them whenever I like! But this is a chance to get to know my Khajiit mother's family. To learn what it means to be Khajiit.\n\nAnd Maezi … well, she's really quite something, isn't she?

And I respect her right to do so. She chose to fight this Dragon invasion directly, and I'm proud of her.\n\nBut that doesn't mean I'm not worried. Or that I regret losing one of the few resources I still had.

My daughter, Aeliah.\n\nShe has a good head for diplomacy. Her understanding of both Imperial and Khajiiti culture has been a great help to my legion over the years. Then you showed up and she deserted me.

Oh, don't think old Sormund's gone soft! I'm in this for the gold—pure and simple. 'Course, these cats clearly need help. If I can do good while doing well, so much the better.\n\nNow listen, you'd better not say anything to my crew about this!
I don't know. Years. Too long to still be the ship's Cabin Man, I can tell you that much. Ought to be First Mate, as much as I do for him.

I think they'll take gold for any cause that'll pay them, and this clan don't need much encouragement to pick a fight. Dragonguard's got enough problems dealing with actual Dragons. Don't need more toadies getting in the way, too.

If you want to kill him, nobody's gonna stop you. But kicking his Worm Cult out of the Bone Orchard is the least of our problems.\n\nI'm hoping that making an example of the New Moon's flunky will encourage Ethruin to stay out of our business.
They're Daedra worshipers.\n\nWord is these Super-whatevers are causing a lot of trouble for the Lion Guard, so I wouldn't take them lightly. Even if they do have a stupid name.

That supposition was simply an educated guess. But yes, I believe that by channeling the energy from Jode's Core through this strange aeonstone, Kaalgrontiid can achieve an unprecedented level of power.\n\nWill that equal godhood? Who can say?

Oh, this one was just …. Ugh, I will not fib. Daini meant to rob this caravan. Do not judge! I swear on the Moons I did not … this was an accident! Even if it was not, those muskarses were slavers, killers, and worse!\n\nDull-witted terror birds!

Yes. Daini set them on the caravaners. Only to scare them! But the birds gobbled the guards up. Bad luck for them and for Daini. The goods I meant to steal are ruined!\n\nDaini can fix this. I just … I really need help. You will help, yes?

Five-claw! You just want to hear tales of your exploits, hrrm?\n\nVery well. You and Abnur Tharn arrived in Northern Elsweyr to help deal with the Dragon threat that Tharn unintentionally released upon us. Along the way, we discovered a terrible truth.

We killed the Dragon Mulaamnir and flung Kaalgrontiid into the void, but not before he absorbed the core's power. Then I took back my family's throne and accepted the crown of Anequina.\n\nAs for Kaalgrontiid … you should talk to Tharn.

That Euraxia the Usurper Queen, Tharn's half-sister, orchestrated the release of the Dragons. We ended her reign, only to learn that the Dragons had plans of their own.\n\nKaalgrontiid, leader of the Dragons, sought the power hidden in Jode's Core.

You mean other than the cultists that were trying their damnedest to disembowel us?\n\nWait a moment. You're going back there! What in the Two Moons could possibly warrant a return visit to that awful place?

I am not a mage. I wouldn't know a portal from a hole in the ground. But that's where they were gathering the green … aeonstone, I think they called it.\n\nIf they have a way to move the stone, it must be in the amphitheater. That's where I'd look.
Hmm, now that you mention it, I did hear a few of those nutters mention sending the green stone to an island. And they were certainly sacrificing something on that altar in the amphitheater.

I heard Aeliah say something about meeting with the Queen of Anequina, which I take to be some sort of euphemism.\n\nAs for the captain, he went to collect his special order. A case of plum brandy. The good stuff. Already storing it away, I'd wager.

The injured Dragon. There's nothing more dangerous, but also totally predictable.\n\nIt will head to a secure location to mend its wounds. What could be more secure than the source of Dragonhold's defenses?

Your observational skills never cease to amaze me.\n\nThe energy gave me a boost, but it also wreaked havoc with my body. A mortal vessel was never meant to contain such power. Now that it's gone, I'm nearly spent.

Za'ji. He sought the best fighter in Senchal for his crew. That was me.\n\nAt first, I didn't even hear him out. I had gold, fame, a legacy to uphold. But eventually, I realized Za'ji was offering me something greater than all that.

Yes. A place for bored nobles to get their blood pumping and tough warriors to earn some gold.\n\nI wasted six years of my life there, chasing the thrill of battle and the honor of victory. It was brutal, but by the Moons did it make me feel alive!
Thank you. Ka'ishka knows she will lose her Vijari soon, but she won't give him to the vile darkness.\n\nPlease, is there anything she can do to help?

Not for some time. The ceremony you performed stirs the sacred source of the shrines and instills the shoal with the same spiritually spotless supply. Their spouts will spray streams of sacramental water to sluice the despoiling skooma out to sea.

This array of stones forms the portal's focal point. That's aeonstone, mined from sites throughout Southern Elsweyr. I did a little research after receiving Sai's report.\n\nWe need to energize the stones to activate the portal to Dragonhold.

That profane mural isn't the source of Namiira's corruption. It is the cracks the darkness seeps through. Something reaches out from it for Vijari and this one can't break its hold without knowing more about its nature.

Aeonstone has no intrinsic power. It amplifies whatever energy it absorbs. That's the key to activating the portal.\n\nIf you step close to the stones, I'll siphon a bit of your vitality into them. That should provide power enough to open the portal.

You think so? My knowledge is infinitesimal and it irks me.\n\nThe stone exists only in Southern Elsweyr. It absorbs and amplifies energy using a process I can utilize but don't fully understand. The cultists certainly accumulated a lot of it, though.
A home.\n\nListen to me prattle on. Let's get going.

Shazar did not cross the sweltering Scorch only to spin 'round and slink back to Senchal like a smitten Senche! Since you've shored up the situation inside, Shazar suspects the unscrupulous schemers will scatter like skeevers soon enough.

Point taken.\n\nKaalgrontiid absorbed a significant amount of energy from Jode's Core. With all the stone he had the cultists send to the island, I assume its unique properties factor into his plans in some fashion.

Take the cantor's tonic on the table, by my bag. It will open your mind and allow you to see into the Twilight between the darkness and the light. You'll see what clings to Vijari and follow its residuum to other things it has touched in the Mundus.

It will take all this one's focus to sing the canticles. If Adara'hai's notes do not carry true, Namiira's brood will drag us to the Dark Behind the World.\n\nBut protect this one and her song will shield your ears from Lorkhaj's twisted tune.
He bowed down before the Dragon's might and offered to serve them.\n\nLaatvulon accepted and gifted him with glorious power. He named him a Dragon Priest.

No, no. My poor J'saad.\n\nThis damn stone. I knew that woman was no good! She told J'saad that the stone would bring him luck. Show him a path to a brighter future. But it's cursed. J'saad is proof of that.

Hmm. I know I promised to toss the stone into the deepest river, but maybe I'll hang onto it for a little while. You know, just to prove to myself that J'saad … I don't know. Maybe I'll hear the voices, too?\n\nYes. I think I'll keep it. For a while.

Yes, but he also serves another, greater power. He who shall ascend into the sky. \n\nRa'khajin will lead the masses of Elsweyr to bow before this great power. He shall become Mane under the New Moon. Our ascension shall be glorious!

Zu'u koraav. So it was Vahlokzin who hid it from me. To protect our kind from the horn's power, no doubt. Such an honorable fool.\n\nAnd why do you seek to kill me? Are you one of Laatvulon's thralls?

My oldest foe. A Dragon of great power and evil intent. He gathered a cult to do his bidding and subjugated our brothers to his cause. Those who oppose him, die.\n\nHe plans to destroy this land. And me along with it.

Why would I attack the Kaaz city? It means nothing to me. Only Laatvulon matters.\n\nYou have dispatched many of my brother's followers, so I shall spare your lives. You may even keep my horn. I have no need of it.

And glorious shall their reign be!\n\nThe Three Banners War, the machinations of the Daedra, all will be irrelevant. For centuries we have idled, foolishly worshiping absent gods and dead Moons. But that time comes to an end.

Not as sorry as the Dragons will be, walker.\n\nChizbari studied them from a distance for many long days and nights. Now this one knows their habits—their weaknesses. Some see them as gods. This one sees only quarry.

We obey. Laatvulon has already set his divine plan in motion, and soon the New Moon shall rise. All we must do is faithfully serve and await our ascension.\n\nBut we will speak more of that after your initiation.

They bring the green stone here, to this fortress. The ritual chamber is filled with the stuff. It must have something to do with the ceremony they keep talking about.\n\nWe need to observe this ceremony, but not with this group. Too risky.
We take an alternate route.\n\nThis doorway leads to the upper balcony of the ritual chamber. It should allow us to observe the ceremony without requiring us to participate.

Let us hope not, walker. Cleansing the Temple of Seven Riddles was a feat this one isn't certain she could repeat. Whatever we face, Adara'hai is sure she can overcome it with you at her side.\n\nOnce more into the darkness, my friend.

A place sacred to this village. Ka'ishka could tell you more, but Adara'hai knows the Khajiit here visit it at the end of their lives. For Vijari to go there means his health is failing. Ka'ishka is right to be worried.

Ka'ishka is this one's sister, and Vijari a brother-by-Mara. It has been years since Adara'hai has seen them. Not since they wed, she thinks. This one wishes she had visited sooner, but the duties of a Twilight Cantor take her far and wide.

Our intention was always to attack Kaalgrontiid together. Nahfahlaar went to deal with the lesser Dragons, then came here to meet us.\n\nQueen Khamira asked him to make a quick pass of the island. It appears he discovered something significant.

If Kaalgrontiid finished becoming the New Moon—the Dark Aeon—we'd already be dead. If he becomes a god, all is lost.\n\nWe have a Dragonhorn, the Mask of Alkosh, and a moon-touched queen. Let's pray that's enough to stop Kaalgrontiid.

Kaalgrontiid's thralls will not rush to his side. I have seen to that. The cowards!\n\nBesides, it seems Kaalgrontiid never told them that his path to godhood was paved in their blood and life energy.

It is where the Great Darkness, Namiira, and her dro-m'Athra dance the Bent Dance to the beat of Lorkhaj's heart. True cats who hear the beat risk being caught up in the dance and twisted into dro-m'Athra themselves.

Lorkhaj was the last of Fadomai's litter, born in the Great Darkness. It was he who tricked Nirni and her littermates into giving birth to the world. Though he was cast down, his heart still beats its seductive tune down in the Dark Behind the World.
A Twilight Cantor has no home, but Adara'hai and her sister were born in Topal. Ka'ishka has lived in Black Heights for years. She will know more about this place and its customs.
A failing body can weigh down even the lightest soul. He had the courage to take the risk, we must hope his will is stronger than his bones.
Laatvulon flinches at the shadows of his past. The Kaaz Kaal Sul are no more and yet he fears them still. Pathetic.
Why put yourself at risk for such an insignificant victory? Let these priests die so that you may live to fight another day.

Of fewer years than we hoped, but Ka'ishka knew of his illness before she took him as her mate. Our time has been short and precious. She knew his pilgrimage to the Wall of Life would be soon, but she wishes he could have waited a little longer.
It is a holy place found in the cave behind the town. The villagers go to paint their final work at the end of their life. They have been adding to it for generations. It's what Vijari left to do.
Twin, no less. Her calling would not normally bring her to a sleepy village like Black Heights, but Ka'ishka knew she would come to help her. Adara'hai has always helped others.
He will remain out of Khenarthi's reach. Ka'ishka knows how important that is, but is it not preferable to falling into the Great Darkness?

In his Khenarthic tradition, he must prepare for the journey to the Sands Behind the Stars by unburdening his soul. The people here add their marks to the Wall of Life and paint their final work for those they leave behind. He must go without regret.
You have? Then Ka'ishka is truly blessed that the Divines have brought you back together here. Vijari is in good hands.

How could Ka'ishka not? Her sister is a Twilight Cantor, she travels the world wielding the secrets of Azurah to drive darkness out of the world. This one's simple life cannot compare, but she cherishes it all the same.

The Wall of Life is the last step of one journey and the first step of the next. Once a pilgrim has unburdened their soul at the Wall, they are ready to ascend the path up the mountain and rise into Khenarthi's waiting arms.

Well, this one remembers something about the Pride of Alkosh. They were warriors born during an eclipse. Made them more sensitive to time and the call of the Moons.\n\nFor some, it gave them the wisdom to become a Mane, a leader. For others ….
Makes sense. This Pride of Alkosh protects Elsweyr in times of great need. Dragons scheming to destroy us all would certainly seem to qualify, yes?
Wish I knew, walker. We could certainly use the reinforcements.\n\nYou should find the Clan Mother and see what she knows. If she's still alive, that is.
A door. An ancient door hidden behind a waterfall. Somewhere to the southwest, she thinks.\n\nBut we're not alone here. The place is crawling with pirates. Be on your guard.
Ah! He is in the Dark! This one remembers. The dance. The beating. He can't hear it, but Vijari still feels it in his chest. It tugs at his tail. It's calling to him.

No … it's worse than Ka'ishka feared. If the Wall stands between this one and Khenarthi, he will never reach the Sands Behind the Stars.\n\nVijari has no strength left. If the Darkness does not take him, his illness surely will.
The Wall. Vijari's time is close, he can feel it. He felt the Wall of Life calling for him. He heard a familiar voice guiding him toward Khenarthi's grace, but … Vijari got lost along the way.

None that any Moon-Priest could share. This sickness has followed Vijari's family for generations. This one lost his mother to it when he was young. Why we suffer while our cousins are spared, this one does not know, but at least it ends with him.
Nuziwa here keeps mentioning a Clan Mother. If there's something special about Pridehome, she'll know. We just need to find her.
It would not be her, she never saw the Wall of Life … but his father made the journey. \n\nVijari thinks it was his voice. Dak'radhi beckoned him to the Sands Behind the Stars.

She … she did not have the strength to make her mark on the Wall. She stayed to care for this helpless cub while his father was away. By the time his father returned it was all she could do to say goodbye. It will be the same for me.

His father? He's been dead for years. Vijari's sickness sometimes leaves him confused. He has awoken from fevered dreams calling for those no longer with us.\n\nWhen he said the Wall was calling to him, this one thought he meant his time was short.

Ka'ishka needed to hear that, rhook. She feared she was being selfish sitting here while you and Adara'hai risk your lives against the Great Darkness.\n\nThis one will be here if you need her. She will be a rock to anchor him.
Of course, rhook. This one knows she has little to offer. Ka'ishka only wishes she could do something. Anything other than watching helplessly.

This one never met Dak'radhi, but Vijari said his father hardly left his side until departing for the Wall of Life. It must have been hard to leave his sick son behind. Poor Vijari had no one to care for him before Ka'ishka was smitten by his charms.
No time, no time. Alkosh, grant me a moment more.\n\nThe mask. You must find the mask before Ra'khajin does. Seek the path. Let our founder be your guide. Her statue will … will ….

Then let's see what our resident red beast thinks of all this.\n\nHopefully, Nahfahlaar is still nearby. Let's ask him about Ja'darri and the divine mask her statue wears. Perhaps this time he'll be more forthcoming.

Anything Dragonguard. Books on killing Dragons without getting eaten, I hope. When I scare up some leads, I could use your help retrieving them.\n\nI hear anything about those New Moon fanatics while I'm at it, I'll let you know.

We served together as part of the Five Companions, helping Emperor Aquilarios recover the Amulet of Kings. I have conflicted feelings about those days.\n\nWe've been exchanging letters recently. I've informed him about Nahfahlaar and the Dragonguard.

He paces. He grumbles. He refuses to speak except in riddles. And he's only gotten worse since Tharn's letter arrived and my own mood soured.\n\nWe both know something terrible gathers strength in the wilderness. We just don't know what it is.

His letter indicated a threat to Southern Elsweyr, but that was the extent of his revelations. I suppose he wants to tell us in person. Prudent, if frustrating.\n\nAfter all, one should never commit certain details to paper.
The Jonelight Path? Hrrm ….\n\nI have never heard of such a thing, but it does sound promising.
His … claw? And this will help us reach Dragonhold and put an end to Kaalgrontiid?\n\nWell, if Khunzar-ri's spirit insisted ….

Not yet. But I will study the claw and search my memories. Let the attunement guide me. The answer will come, I just need some time.\n\nGo. Find Sai Sahan and make sure the Dragonguard is ready to proceed.

You haven't heard the tale?\n\n"Pridehome, hear my call!" Vashu-Pir shouted. "The Black Beast scorches your land and devours your people. Only with the wisdom of Alkosh may I defeat this Dragon, and only with your help may I hear the Dragon God."

I wouldn't take it quite so literally.\n\nThe Dragonguard always tried to show respect to the local population. They probably asked for Pridehome's blessing as a sign of goodwill. I doubt the priests helped in a direct manner.

I won't deny that. If Nahfahlaar doesn't wish to fight alongside us, I'm not sure why he agreed to this alliance.\n\nPerhaps you can get through to him. Make him understand that we need his help to defeat Laatvulon.

Information, obviously. It isn't every day an island flies up into the sky. I wanted
to find out what the Dragonguard knew about it.

My daughter provided more than I bargained for, what with the details concerning a mad Dragon's plans for godhood.
When the conflagration begins, all we can do is attempt to keep our own space drenched against the flames.\n\nI wish the Dragonguard success, but I must see to my own. I hope you understand.

The Shields will do as they have always done—keep Senchal safe and make sure its people come to no harm.\n\nI wish I believed this threat were confined to Senchal or even Southern Elsweyr, but I fear the danger extends beyond our borders.

Eager to set paw on a floating island? Certainly! That's the sort of experience a curious Khajiit lives for. As for Kaalgrontiid ….\n\nA fight's a fight. And I'm always ready to mix it up, no matter what the odds happen to be.

Yes, this temple cared for Ja'darri's remains long ago.\n\nYou seek the Halls of the Highmane, a most sacred place. Its secrets have been passed down across the ages, though perhaps that tradition has died with Hizuni.

Ready? Za'ji was born ready! What's one more Dragon, even if it is bigger and—\n\nNo. This business makes Za'ji's tail want to hide between his legs. It is smarter than we are, yes? But this one will go with you. He is Dragonguard, after all.
Even if Ra'khajin finds the mask, it would reject him. He will never be worthy of its power.

She did? Hmm. Then perhaps Hizuni saw something in the tapestry of time that this one has yet to hear in the wind.\n\nVery well. Seek the statue of the Forgotten Mane, south of this temple. Just listen for the bells.

Yes. Maybe. It really depends on Lady G's mood. I can promise a good word—nothing more. Now, the task.\n\nI paid a Khajiit named Zurnash to deliver a token to Auberic Dufont. Auberic never received it. Find that lazy Khajiit and deliver the token.

The Pride of Alkosh, in your tongue. Khajiiti warriors of ages past.\n\nSome advice, hunter. Pridehome is not worth our effort. We must concentrate on the battle ahead. Saving priests does little for our cause.

It may not sound reasonable, but I can't help it. It's easy to doubt myself after so many failures. That's why I want to come with you. I want to do something right.\n\nI want to prove that I'm worthy of the title Dragonguard.
Good. Fit them together and see what the intact tablet has to say. Maybe it contains a clue as to how to open this blasted door.

You know how maudlin Dark Elves get. One of them is probably using it to practice their necromancy. Nothing a Dragonguard ought to have trouble with.\n\nYou find that Akaviri kicking around again, try not to bang up the goods.

Yeah, Cabin Man. Like Cabin Boy, but I'm a man. You daft? Perfect Pounce would fall apart without me keeping things in order. You think Captain Za'ji runs a tight ship? No, sir. Don't care how good a sailor he is, won't get far with torn sails.

Well, I swabbed the decks. Cleaned the galley. Did laundry … and I provisioned the ship! And that's just the start, mind you. Point is, just cause I'm no sailor don't mean I'm not important.\n\nSai saw that, so I'm not just some cabin man anymore.

They follow a difficult path, walker. Born under Dark Moons, the drum of Lorkhaj calls to them clearly. Or so the stories go.\n\nYou should let Sai Sahan know about this. He's deeper within the compound.

So my client tells me. Fine by me. An Akaviri war codex isn't the sort of thing you find resting on the table near your chamber pot.\n\nAs far as Guybert Flaubert is concerned, if you can't read a book in the privy, it's not worth reading.

Yes, of course. I mean … you know, probably. We're not putting any of this in writing are we? Guybert prefers to keep business informal. Once contracts and patents enter the equation … ugh! Intolerable.\n\nYou'll be fine! Probably.

Hard to blame him. This Selloe stinks.\n\nNow, you're not going to believe this, but I just saw a Khajiit stumble by, slurring about a late delivery. Had some bottles tucked under his arm, too. Bet you a slice of my Aunt Murog's pie that he's our guy.

They aren't talking about the weather. Maybe we'll see what they're up to. Better yet, we learn what they're offering the Orcs and do them one better.\n\nNow get moving. Won't learn a thing if that courier takes off while we're jawing.

Hmph. Not that I can tell. Whoever this person is, they covered their tracks well enough.\n\nI'll say this: anyone who can wrangle a coven of witches into doing their bidding is a serious threat. The Icereach Coven bowed to no one … until now.

More than a simple storm. That much is certain. They were building to something. I'd bet my axe on it.\n\nHopefully the mages back in Windhelm can decipher this scroll and get a better idea of just what they were planning.
For the love of Mauloch. Yeah, fine. Give 'em here.\n\nYou know, if my friend Darien ever saw this he would die laughing.

He's a bard. A temperamental one. I wager he'll yank at his beard, and grumble, and recite a poem in the sword-thanes' honor. But for all his theatrics, he's a practical man. He'll have me and a dozen other housecarls turning stones before long.
And the boob! Don't forget the incompetent boob!\n\nThese candles, if effective, will save countless lives. A worthy endeavor, I'd say!

Of sorts. I guess.\n\nBut take heart, my friend! Just imagine if some incompetent boob purchased a handful of these candles and it turned out they didn't work! Zombies would likely devour him, and that could spell disaster for my client's business!

Apparently, they blossom only during Jone and Jode's waning. A burst of life as the sky fades to black, you see? Such a lovely sentiment.\n\nOh, don't look at me like that! Guybert may be a simple job broker, but he possesses a poet's heart!

No.\n\nI had a handful of thanes at my back, but most suffered terrible wounds during that first assault. I carried them as far as I could, but I'm no healer. One of them, Gulfrim, made me promise to kill five Reachmen for every Nord that fell.
