The locals detest bitter food. Won't touch it!\n\nJust yesterday I saw a Khajiit toss a sweetroll into the bushes because it wasn't sweet enough. The pastry has "sweet" in the name for goodness sake! Baffling, just baffling.
You're asking the wrong Nord. I've hunted enough mages to recognize the trinkets that are worth something, but as for what they do? Not exactly my area of expertise.

Addict? Don't be obscene! Sure, I may have chased the moons once or twice, but an addict? Hardly! Anyway, it didn't agree with me. Indigestion, you see? Moving on!\n\nThis new formula sounds horrific. Far more frightening than what I saw in my youth.
Cure? Goodness no. But with any luck she might develop a treatment to neutralize an overdose. Only time will tell, I suppose.

From what I understand, the threshold for overdose is far lower than anyone expects. Users ingest too much and go into fits. Frothing and moaning, then descending into catatonia that prevents them from breathing. Ghastly.
I do say so! Now then, let's make some gold together!
Oh, thank you! I saw what happened to poor Falls and I got so frightened! I'll go find Nomu right now!
Truly? That is good news! I think I have enough strength to make it to that location.\n\nThank you, stranger. Just remind me never to listen to Nomu's stupid ideas again.

Rumors spread like wildfire through the streets of Senchal, especially if it involves anything valuable. \n\nMost of what we heard indicated that the locals avoided the stuff, though. Said it was cursed or tainted or something like that.

Curses? No. If someone had mentioned the cultists, though, that's a different matter.\n\nLook, I just want to see my friends again. Then we'll leave Elsweyr and return to my father's shop in Murkmire.
I don't think so.\n\nThose last two practiced necromancy, sure. But the others seemed to focus on elemental magic … ice, wind, and flame. Maybe they're both connected to the ritual somehow?
Losing count, eh? Me too.\n\nI managed to kill one of them during the initial assault. You killed another—the Hagraven, Skelga. I wager the more we kill, the less stable their ritual will become.
Honestly? After everything we've already witnessed, it could be anything! All I know is that whatever form this new threat takes, it has both Sai Sahan and Abnur Tharn worried.

Nahfahlaar paced around like an anxious Senche-raht awaiting the approach of a summer storm. I think he senses the coming of whatever threat Abnur Tharn uncovered.\n\nYou'll see for yourself when you return to the Dragonguard Sanctum.

Rebuilding an order takes time. The sanctum is coming along, but Sai wants to get more chapters established as soon as possible.\n\nThe Dragons remain a threat, one too large for a single group to deal with.

Legality is determined by what enriches the elite instead of what nourishes the masses. Especially in a place like Senchal.\n\nI am simply fulfilling a basic necessity that cannot be handled by other means.
And put a hard-working courier such as yourself out of work? Perish the thought!\n\nBesides, I have a reputation to uphold.

Are you attempting to ascertain my secret recipe?\n\nIt isn't so much spoilage that I fear but a lack of freshness. The fresher the product, the more potent its beneficial effects. That's all you need to know, courier.
Don't worry about my customers. Just deliver the product to the chests I marked on your map.\n\nI designed them especially to keep the product fresh and secure.
I hate you. I really do.

We carry on a proud family tradition! Mother would stick an Alfiq in a stranger's pack when she was but a kitten and then scream "Thief! Thief!"\n\nA much better plan than Tender Claw and his stupid note, yes?
A gift? My, oh my. How wonderful! We suffered a … mild setback recently and lost an Orc of similar proportions. Lady Ghisiliane will be overjoyed!\n\nI will introduce you to my mistress at once!

My apologies. Welcome to the hunt. Your quarry includes Khajiit both large and small. If you seek a greater challenge, a bull-Orc roams the swamp as well.\n\nPlease, join us for refreshments at the conclusion of your excursion. Good hunting, cerum.
A Dragon! It helped Ja'darri defeat the Demon from the East.\n\nThe Clan Mother would often tell us the story. Two beasts, clashing. And brave Ja'darri, who befriended one to defeat the other.
Only the Clan Mothers know.\n\nPlease, this one must make sure the bodies here are cared for. We can speak of the legends another time.

Just legends.\n\nJa'darri wore a divine mask, filled with the power of Alkosh. But during her greatest battle, it failed her. She died and joined the Dragon King of Cats beyond even the Sands Behind the Stars.

Medicine, remedy … I don't care what it's called. My daughter suffers from constant pain. She can barely speak, barely stand.\n\nThe herbalist's remedy is the only thing that eases her pain, even if just for a little while.

A different courier delivers it each time, and each courier demands a different price. Some are very expensive. Some are … much worse.\n\nI have no gold, courier, but I will do anything to receive the remedy. For my daughter.
The remedy … at no cost? Oh, bless you. Bless you and the herbalist for easing my daughter's pain.\n\nI almost forgot what kindness looked like, but such is life in Senchal.
Very well. Ask what you will, Dragonguard.

It is Alkosh's light, made solid. Made real. A gift, a burden. A claw to mend the tapestry of time. It is divine will that manifests for those found worthy.\n\nAnd yes, it is also a mask you can wear. Any statue of Ja'darri shows you that.

You know of Ra'khajin, yes? He was trained from a young age to enter the Pride of Alkosh. Upon his death, he was to join Alkosh in a place beyond the Sands Behind the Stars.\n\nBut that was not Ra'khajin's only destiny.

What, you want specifics?\n\nIt grants the strength of Alkosh's divine will. The power to defeat forces that stand against the natural order. This one could sit here and theorize what precisely that means, but it would do little good.
Clan Mother Hizuni was the bearer of those secrets, not this one.\n\nIf you are found worthy of the mask, you will learn its power soon enough. But do not look to Tadali for all the answers.

In times of great need, Ra'khajin was trained to obtain the divine mask from the Halls of the Highmane. Through grueling trials and tests of will, he would prove himself worthy.\n\nAnd then he decided to become a Dragon Priest. Youth these days.

Precisely.\n\nAnd before you ask, no, Tadali does not know what these trials are. This one guides heroes to their destiny, just as Khenarthi wills it. It is not her job to provide additional assistance or information.

We're surrounded by Khajiit here. Knowing what motivates them helps us figure out how best to work with them.\n\nMy younger self would just pound problems into the ground, but aching muscles make you find other ways to deal with the world.

The Shields of Senchal? Do you really think they would join us?\n\nWell, it's worth a try. Besides, we've learned so much about the Order of the New Moon and their plans. Maybe my father will finally understand just how dire the situation is.

I'm not an expert. I don't even like the stuff! But the purity of my uncle's moon-sugar … well, it practically glows! He also adds herbs grown in the same fields to give it something extra.\n\nAnyway, look around and see if anything stands out.
Winks? Oh, she's a great cat! Curious, adventurous, brave … except today, for some reason.\n\nShe ran off at the first sign of trouble and I haven't seen her since. I hope she's all right.

Because it isn't. Not exactly. It doesn't heal injuries or cure diseases. I tried to craft such elixirs and failed.\n\nMy product simply makes life more tolerable for those in pain. It's a relief, even as temporary as it is.

My suppliers demand profit. Fortunately, there's enough wealth in the city to keep them satisfied.\n\nThey believe the poor don't deserve to live without pain. Clearly, I disagree. If they knew I gave away the product, it would not end well for me.

And I'm grateful to them. I haven't always been kind to others. To myself. Crafting the remedy makes me feel worthwhile. Like I might be able to one day forgive myself for past mistakes.\n\nYou see? In the end, I'm as selfish as anyone.

As I said, mask-bearer, they are cowards. If we stop Kaalgrontiid, they benefit. If we do not, they are no worse off than before. But if they go against their leader, death becomes a very real possibility.\n\nThat is a risk they refuse to take.

From the very beginning, Kaalgrontiid has coveted the power of his fellow Dragons. The energy he stole from Jode's Core consisted mainly of the power siphoned from his brethren.\n\nWitness the aeonstones. Their purpose is to absorb and enhance energy.

I imagine the usual. Respect your masters. Keep your weapons and armor in good condition. Revere whatever Goutfangs revere. Don't be a blazing muskarse.\n\nI only just started looking into this, so I'm fuzzy on the details.

You're right. I need to focus on my strengths if I want to help the Dragonguard.\n\nI've always been good with diplomacy. Perhaps I can help gather allies, though I'm not sure who I would even speak to at this point.

You faced the cult of the New Moon. The cultists revere Kaalgrontiid. They must have a method for getting to and from the island.\n\nI assume their base at the New Moon Fortress holds the answers we seek.
I can't imagine that's true. She's so confident, so full of fire and steel. We're nothing alike.\n\nNo, I think I'll keep those particular thoughts just between us, if you don't mind.

Maezi sees how Zhasim worries, but Hizhikar knows the perils of business. Zhasim does not realize how much his uncle cares for him. He will be happy his nephew is safe, despite the moon-sugar.\n\nZhasim does not realize a great many things.

While Hizhikar may accept the loss of the moon-sugar, this one still wants to do everything she can to recover the stolen shipment.\n\nAs discussed, we will go after the portion headed to Senchal. You check on the drop points.

Really? Maezi had hoped … but no. We took our eyes off the moon-sugar and look what happened. This one has a job to do. Maezi has no time for romantic overtures.\n\nAt least, not until we recover and deliver our cargo.

Oh yes. Between the smugglers and the constant threat from the Dragons, Zhasim's plan makes the most sense. And from a business perspective, a faster turn around is always most prudent.\n\nMaezi will miss traveling with Zhasim, though.

Did this one give you the impression that she did not? Zhasim has qualities one rarely sees in the typical Khajiit. And he has traveled so far!\n\nMaezi would love to see the great city of Orsinium. If Zhasim agrees to go along, of course.

Oh, very much so! Maezi would like to help Zhasim understand the ways of the Khajiit. And she would very much like Zhasim to show her the ways of the Orcs!\n\nThis one just hopes that the merchant life is as exciting as the life of a caravan guard.
You think so? Perhaps you are right. Winks will probably run away again, if nothing else.\n\nHmm. Perhaps Maezi should look into getting her a tiny leash, yes?
With Maezi and Winks at my side, I think I can do anything! She really is quite amazing!

About that. Watch for some strange techniques with this master. He learned forbidden styles and now teaches them to his students. No, don't ask what the techniques are. I don't know.\n\nTake friends. I'd go myself, but I'm past my fighting days.
Well, I'm hoping she'll agree to something a little more permanent. I want her to see where I grew up. Meet my hearth mother and my Orc brother. Then ….\n\nWell, then we'll see.

That is good to hear. This one was so pleased to hear that his sister's child survived. Hizhikar plans to make Zhasim an integral member of the family business.\n\nOur gourmet moon-sugar is the best in all of Southern Elsweyr!

This one hates to lose a good caravan guard, but would love to gain a new daughter! Do not be surprised. Hizhikar has seen how the two of them look at each other.\n\nThis one also likes the business to succeed. So, yes. Let Zhasim try. Let him succeed!
My experience with Meridian guardians tells me that it doesn't care about the dust. More about the fact that it's dust from the temple.\n\nMy advice? Don't ask the guardian anything. Just kill it.

Embarrassing, I know.\n\nI'd spin you a yarn, but you know I'm no good at lying. I got baited into a brawl in Anvil. Somebody called me "Skordo the Soup Spoon." Can you imagine? I let a lot of insults roll off, but poking fun at my name? No way.

Oh, I would've. Trust me. Couldn't wait to bust loose and beat the tar out of those runts! But once they put Tajahir and Marekki in there with me I had to take it easy. Neither one can swing a sword. If a fight broke out? Wouldn't have been pretty.

If you call getting hit on the neck with a sack full of coins while your back is turned losing, sure.\n\nI woke up an hour later tied up in the cart. The kidnappers tossed Tajahir and Marekki in with me a couple days later.

Good folks. Definitely don't deserve all this, I can tell you that.\n\nMarekki's a mouthy one. Walks around on all fours, licks her paws, and everything. She says she's an Alfiq. Never seen a Khajiit like that before, but nothing surprises me anymore.

Just a kid, really. Scrawny as a sapling, but sharp as a razor. He's the one that figured out what the kidnappers had planned for us. Well … the basics, anyway.\n\nI worry about him the most. He's got a lamb's heart, that one.

Well, I can't dance, I can't sing, and I'm not winning any beauty contests, so whatever it is, it's going to be short on whimsey. \n\nIf I had to guess, I'd say some kind of pit-fighting operation. Then again ….
Tajahir and Marekki ain't exactly pit-fighting material. Nah, it's got to be something else.\n\nHmph. This whole thing stinks like an echatere's backside.
Not good, if that's what you're asking.\n\nMany of the Moon-Priests are already dead and the cult has spread throughout Pridehome. I'm beginning to wonder what good we can do here.

Safe bet. Don't have much to go on, though.\n\nThe note mentions some blockhead named Selloe. Maybe if we show her that token she'll talk. It's got to be a ticket or something, right? I say we head to Senchal's waterfront and track her down.
Agreed. Whatever they're after, we need to make sure the cult doesn't get it. Even if that's just information.\n\nThe Clan Mother should know something. See if you can find her.
No idea.\n\nMother's temple worships Khenarthi, while Pridehome appears dedicated to Alkosh. They're both of the Eight, true, but … hmm. Actually, there is one legend that Za'ji remembers.

One of Za'ji's favorites!\n\nThere once was a Khajiiti warrior, blessed by Alkosh himself. She fought a mighty demon, drenched in ice and death. Though the warrior was able to trap the demon away, she did not survive the battle.
By the Moons, what has Janessa gotten into this time? Did she steal your drinks? Break something you left sitting on the bar? Claw the eyes out of someone you know?
I didn't leave Senchal with you last night? Whew, well that makes this easier. You mind taking me back to Black Heights? My sister's probably worried and I'm really in no shape for hiking right now.

Za'ji was getting to that part!\n\nThe warrior's corpse was taken to Khenarthi's Breath Temple, where the Moon-Priests prayed over her body for four days and four nights. On the fourth night, when both Moons were full, Khenarthi herself appeared.
So the legend says.\n\nBut a Khajiiti tale is as reliable as, say, a harlot's affection. One should not take either too seriously, yes?

With a single swipe of Khenarthi's paw, the warrior's spirit rose from her corpse. Together, they flew into the sky, past the Sands Behind the Stars, and went to a place beyond all that is known.\n\nThere, Alkosh welcomed his warrior home.
You take great pleasure in forcing me to admit to gaps in my knowledge, don't you?

Name's Lyris Titanborn. Axe-wielding, jaw-breaking friend to the former Emperor, Varen Aquilarios. Also a friend of High King Jorunn.\n\nI sailed here as a personal favor to the Skald-King. Remind me to avoid personal favors in the future.
I'm not sure. He fights with the fury of a wounded senche, but that could simply be his way.\n\nStill, despite his confidence, not even Nahfahlaar can stand against such numbers for long.
Nahfahlaar and his enemies flew out of sight, but the tower may offer a better vantage point. \n\nZa'ji is up there now. Perhaps he saw where they went.

Eh. Getting there. Just deciding what comes next.\n\nMarekki wants to go north. Tajahir's family owns a sugar farm up there. Out near Riverhold, I think. Anyway, she says it's only right we let them know what happened. Can't argue with that.
Not since he flew by. To be honest, things weren't looking good for our scaly friend. An entire rage of Dragons chased after him.\n\nZa'ji doesn't think Laatvulon is interested in a fair fight.

Not sure. Haven't been back to High Rock recently. Promised a noble lady I would visit her in Daggerfall a while back. Bah, don't give me that look! She's a friend. \n\nOf course, it might be time for something new. Skyrim, maybe? I like the cold.
Za'ji lost sight of them. They're fast and loud. This one can't help but wince every time they shout. Is that really just him?\n\nWait. Looks like they're coming back around!

Well enough, though this one grieves for gentle Tajahir. He would have made a fine adept. Ah well. He's in Khenarthi's paws now, yes?\n\nSkordo said he would go to Northern Elsweyr to help me find Taj's family. Let them know his fate, you know?

This is why friend Skordo makes such a fine traveling companion, yes? Nothing like a hard-tusked and well-muscled Orc to cool off someone who might give this one a hard time.\n\nOh. Those muscles! It grows hot out here, no?

Travel!\n\nThis one grows tired of Pellitine and all its filthy, flu-scorched houses. This is a land of ghosts and thieves now. Marekki says no thank you to ghosts! Dragons, too! Moons' mercy, this place is the worst.
Somehow, it is even more beautiful.\n\nFor all their misguided greed, those Alfiq thieves may have done us all a great service. Senchal has a symbol to rally behind.

Percius and Bebbia had been discussing just that very thing. He has a great talent and a new found passion for restorations. This one intends to hire him to share his learnings with Khajiit. Perhaps more things thought lost may be returned to us.

Bebbia is wealthy, but not so wealthy she could save Senchal herself. Khajiit here need to believe not only that rebuilding is possible, but that it's worth doing. We must all come together like the pieces of this tapestry to make it whole again.

Corner the market and make a killing. Had you, didn't I? Bebbia has already proposed an arrangement where I would teach what I've learned to Khajiit weavers. Restoring Khajiit of the Moons will be the first rebirth in the resurrection of a lost art!

Percius Loche does not settle for mediocrity. Fame and fortune as a renowned tailor is nothing to scoff at, but would my name carry on after I'm gone? Likely not. The man who revives a textile trade from thousands of years passed? He'll be immortal.

I've never even seen a tapestry like this. I'm a tailor by trade. I pride myself on elegant work, but I've never thought of myself as an artist. Mending and stitching are my bread and butter though, and this job requires both to be done masterfully.

I'm afraid that's impossible. This tapestry will be scarred, but those scars will serve as a testament to its history and enduring beauty. At least, that is my intent. I can only hope the end result lives up to the vision.

I was hoping you'd forgotten. I lost a beautiful pair of doe-skin breeches in that dye, you know.\n\nAbah's Landing remains a nest of intrigue, but our mutual friends seem to have things sorted out for now. The merchants are happy, so business is good.

No. Bebbia left Senchal when the flu began to spread. This one lived in Rimmen and Rawl'kha many years, but Senchal will always be Bebbia's home. \n\nThis one returned when she heard about the tapestry because it has always been the heart of her city.

She does what all noble traders do. Make and spend obscene amounts of money. And travel. Lots of travel. That was how Bebbia met Percius. She had business with the merchant lords of Abah's Landing and purchased some of Percius's wonderful garments.
Yes, when this one was young she would stare at the tapestry for hours. Bebbia studied every Khajiit, imagining their lives and their dreams and what they saw in the moons.

Practically everything. If it weren't for old Dirge, the whole ship would sink under the weight of the grime and barnacles. Not that any of these louts would notice.\n\nEnough jawing! I got to see what condition the Pounce's come back in.

Whatever needs doing. Cleaning, mopping, stabbing. Sometimes this one stabs and then cleans up afterward. Also, Chizbari is well known for her cheery disposition.\n\nHooray. See? Chizbari is so cheery.

Yes, back when the ship belonged to a rather nasty fellow by the name of Bahzahar the Bull. A heartless taskmaster who didn't care a lick about his crew.\n\nThe Pounce was a lot less colorful back then, in more ways than one.

Studying the Akaviri Potentate specifically. And, yes, that's what brought me here.\n\nPotentate Versidue-Shaie died within the Senchal palace. I wish to see the rooms where he was … ahem. Where he died.
To be honest, I've been mulling over this alliance since you first entered my office.\n\nBut I was certain that if I left Senchal defenseless, it would fall to ruin. Just like Cyrodiil.

When I left Cyrodiil all those years ago, the unimaginable happened. My emperor was killed and Daedra attacked. And I wasn't there to defend my home. That knowledge changed me.\n\nI couldn't let something similar happen to Senchal.

Gossip and hearsay. As if any operative of the Morag Tong would do such a thing. \n\nSee, this is why the work of scholars is so important. Finding the truth, suppressing nonsensical rumors. Now then, I should get back to my notes.
Well. That is one story. I mean, tales spring up like weeds whenever someone famous or infamous dies.

Hmmm? Oh, the slave thing. I am not of House Telvanni and the Khajiit are no longer slaves in Vvardenfell. \n\nEven the Khajiit here in Senchal can appreciate a scholar going about his important work.

As you know, Khajiit are no longer slaves in Vvardenfell so they have no reason to be hostile or afraid. \n\nOf course, the past slavery situation understandably makes things a bit tense. Thankfully I am not House Telvanni.

"We face the darkness of fear to find the light of courage." That's something my wife often said. And something Aeliah just recently reminded me.\n\nI can't let fear dictate my actions. And so I will join with you.
Tactical information, supplies, soldiers. Now that we're in this fight, you'll find the Shields of Senchal an invaluable ally.
The odds don't look good. We don't know the island. We have no idea how strong the Dragon is.\n\nWe'll have to improvise, and that rarely goes well.

My soldiers and I, we swore an oath to the Empire. If we forsake that oath and take up with Rimmen's queen, what does that say about our commitment and loyalty?\n\nI seem to be caught between my pride and my honor. What do you think, Dragonguard?

With gratitude, I should expect. With Queen Khamira's support, we'll finally have access to proper equipment, supplies. Watches can be shorter, patrols can be increased… everything will be safer. The Empire could not give us that, I must admit.
I haven't left Senchal completely defenseless.\n\nBesides, if we don't defeat Laatvulon now there won't be a city left to defend. Unless my daughter has exaggerated the dangers?
A cruel race, these Dragons. They would rather rule over ashes than allow us to remain free. It's not just Senchal at stake, or even Elsweyr. All of Tamriel is in peril.

The Undaunted are celebrating their founding! Ah, those rowdy dungeon-delvers always know how to have a good time. If you're feeling up to it and can meet their rigorous standards, you can petition to join them in one of their romps!

Visit any Undaunted enclave in the capital city of each alliance! That is, Mournhold, Wayrest, and Elden Root. Do their tasks to increase your standing in their organization, plus gain commensurate rewards!
You defeated Ra'khajin? Well done, you. Now that we have the mask, we'll finally be able to … to …. \n\nActually, I'm not sure what the mask does.

Oh. Well, at least Laatvulon doesn't have it. And who knows, maybe it'll prove useful. Eventually.\n\nBesides, we may not even need the mask to defeat Laatvulon now that my father has agreed to help us.

Exciting, dangerous, dirty work. Gets this one's blood pumping! \n\nThey are huge, winged beasts. Dodging a blast of flame from a fiery maw. Rolling out of the way of freezing air that chills you to your marrow. So invigorating!

I simply explained the facts. What we know, what we've done, what the cult plans to do.\n\nI can't really pinpoint what exactly convinced him, though I have a feeling he's been considering this alliance for a long time.

Like it? Javinda loves it! It requires superfast reflexes and strength of nerve. \n\nBut … Khajiit can keep up that pace for only so long. So here I am in Senchal. Time to relax, repair weapons, drink, and boast. Then back to fighting Dragons!
Given that this may be our last attempt to stop Laatvulon, that seems like a wise decision. What do you wish to speak about?

Yes, let's talk about our Dragon ally.\n\nWe know that Nahfahlaar was able to trap Laatvulon centuries ago with the help of the Dragonguard. But there seems to be more to this story than he has been willing to share.

Ancient relics are tricky things, my friend.\n\nI was able to ask the priests of Pridehome about the mask, but they knew little beyond legends and songs. It seems those secrets died with Clan Mother Hizuni.

Ah, that hunting expedition. I must admit some surprise. That particular excursion is by invitation only. Then again, anyone cunning enough to sniff it out would be a welcome addition.\n\nYes, I believe we can find a place for you. As for the Orc ….

Why the expression of doubt? Does Khina not look like a Khajiit of means? Her necklace's sapphire cost nearly as much as this house! Just because she lounges on the ground does not mean she is a beggar.\n\nKhina's paintings bring her gold a plenty.
Again, you doubt! Khina will have you know that she is the foremost artist in Black Heights. Her prints are peddled from Senchal to Riverhold. Is that so hard to believe?

This one has gambled much in life and it has typically turned out well for him, yes? Then again, when he has lost, he has lost much. A home, a fortune. \n\nHe will wait to decide. The coin of fate spins in the air, and no one knows where it may land.

I do as the master desires, and he has not made his wishes known.\n\nSave, of course, that his whiskers be curled in the fashion of the old Meirvale kings. I have it on good authority that such a styling is once again in vogue.
If it were up to me, I'd go to Senchal. The master is determined to head for Rawl'kha, but at our pace we'll be lucky to get there before the Third Era.

Too late, sadly. This one's villa is already burned. His galleons already ravaged and sunk. Only two loyal servants and a handful of possessions remain.\n\nBut we will survive. It is the nature of my kind.

We never used to travel at all, but the master's villa got sacked by cultists and pirates sunk his trading fleet. Now he's determined to leave Southern Elsweyr.\n\nAs the old game-warden, it's up to me to keep the wilderness from killing these two.

Wherever the master decides. It is not a valet's place to lead his master, only to follow and ensure his coat is properly coiffed and free of burrs.\n\nI do hope we travel by sea soon for the road we have taken is laborious and uncomfortably dusty.

I came in search of a particular site for a … personal matter. My guide here spoke as if he knew the area, and offered to lead me to there for a hefty sum.\n\nThis place is nothing like my notes describe. He'll get no coin from me.
This one did no such thing. He hired me to guide him to some area written in his stinking book, but now he refuses to pay.

Fine, I'll pay the blasted fee. I can see I'm outnumbered by greedy fools.\n\nWhen I get back to Senchal, I will most certainly let the authorities know about this swindle. That cat will never work as a guide again!

My notes indicated the site bore markings, pointing to a cache of … goods. The kind that are highly valuable yet questionably legal. The kind that are almost exclusively found in Elsweyr.\n\nThe kind I would be willing to pay a guide to lead me to.
Fine. This one has wasted enough time in this dung-heaper's company. Let him keep his filthy coin.

There was nothing at the place he sought to visit, just wilderness. This one knew of course, but the wood-elf never asked. Tourists rarely do.\n\nBesides, this site was being used to trade skooma. The wood-elf's interest goes beyond idle curiosity, no?

I was going to sell it to a few wealthy wastrels I know in Grahtwood. A harmless transaction for all but them.\n\nThat was the plan, at least. Had this mangy cat described the site in advance, I'd not have bothered coming in the first place!
What do I do? I worry! My next ship is two days overdue. I also fill out many forms. Imperials love paperwork. This is known.\n\nAh, perhaps you haven't seen a Pahmar-raht trader before?

We export rugs and tapestries, Khajiiti woodworks, things like that. Then we fill our holds with whatever interests us in foreign ports and bring it back here.\n\nSupply and demand, friend. It's all about supply and demand.
It's only logical. After all, the Dragonguard named Nahfahlaar's horn after Ja'darri. He must have a connection to her.\n\nIt's something I mean to ask him, should we all survive our next battle.

The Khajiiti warrior Ja'darri, for one. \n\nAccording to the priests we rescued, she was the founder of both Pridehome and the Pride of Alkosh. She's also known for defeating a Demon from the East with the help of a powerful red Dragon.
Are you planning to rob it?\n\nOh, do say yes. I'm a little bored. I could bring you down before you took seven steps. Maybe eight.
No, of course not. \n\nSometimes I encourage them to sneak into the palace to steal General Renmus's gold. Just to liven things up around here, you understand.

Perhaps, though I doubt he'll tell us.\n\nFor now, we just need to make sure that the mask stays out of the hands of those who would misuse it. And who knows, perhaps it will reveal its power eventually.
So they're all headed to Doomstone Keep? Must be something big happening there.
Then it would be best for Caska and Za'ji to meet up with them and give a full report!\n\nYou go on ahead, walker. See if you can rendezvous with Nahfahlaar. We'll be right behind you.

This one knows tales of love and hate, life and death, and everything in between.\n\nMany know about Khunzar-ri's courtship of Anequina Sharp-Tongue. But few know the tale of his other companion, Flinthild Demon-Hunter.

Oh, yes. Too many if this one is being honest.\n\nThis is not a tale of Khunzar-ri specifically, but of one of his kra'jun—the Altmer, Nurarion. They called him the Perfect, but some said he was the Voiceless, for only his foes heard him speak.
Absolutely. This one is thankful as she does not receive that request very often.\n\nDo you know the story of the Black Moon? It was a place so strange that it mystified even the great Khunzar-ri.

Was Khunzar-ri in love with Flinthild? No. But she was besotted with him for a time. He had come to her homeland, far in the north, seeking to form a mighty kra'jun to best the demons.\n\nHe heard of Flinthild's might and sought her out.

Khunzar-ri found her at the great feast of Eastmarch, drinking and gorging on stuffed horker for two solid weeks! It is said that Khunzar-ri and Flinthild engaged in a drunken duel for three straight days.
It is! For during the days they dueled, sloppily trading blow after drunken blow, Flinthild saw the majesty of Khunzar-ri's graceful form.\n\nShe decided to kidnap him and make him her groom.

Because in the ancient days, Nurarion was brother to the king of Sunhold. Terrible storms swept their shores each season, brought by Orgnum of the Maormer, the Young King.\n\nNurarion decided to lead the mages of Sunhold in a counter-spell.

His newfound voice sent Orgnum's storms to the ends of the earth, but even his normal speech meant ruin for all who heard it. He could no longer live at court and risk the lives of others.\n\nHe saved his beloved Sunhold, but was forced into exile.

Yes, but at great cost. In order for Nurarion to best Orgnum, he had to turn to the Prince of Bargains, Clavicus Vile. He asked for a voice that could call forth a doom greater than any called by Orgnum.\n\nUnfortunately, he got his wish.
Of course, but I can't hide in a corner crying about it all day. Besides, it's not like they can make Senchal look worse, eh?

This one cannot say. Even Khunzar-ri never confirmed it was a Moon, he only likened it to one. Anequina, his love, would dance for the Moons, and the Moons would move in adoration.\n\nSometimes, they took Khunzar-ri and Anequina with them.

Once, Anequina danced and the Moons moved … strangely. Like some great thing pulled the stars and Moons from their paths. \n\nKhunzar-ri suddenly fell, for where there used to be ground, now there was none. He could not stop himself from falling.

He stopped, finding himself on a dusty surface, black as iron. He likened it to the moon, but not the red and silver of Jode and Jone. This was someplace else.\n\nIn the sky, he saw a great sphere … with green forests, red seas, and gray clouds.
A sad story about Khunzar-ri? Most travelers prefer cheerful tales, but this one believes that sad stories can often be inspirational and empowering.\n\nDo you know the tale of Khunzar-ri's last day?
The world can always use more joy, yes?\n\nThis one will tell the tale of Anequina Sharp-Tongue, Flinthild Demon-Hunter, and Khunzar-ri—and how Khunzar-ri tamed the famous Dancer of the Moons.

Oh. Well, that I don't know. I am sure they have things like ballistae, catapults, and the like to deal with the beasts. \n\nI know what I plan to do. Hide out down in Black Kiergo. It's safe enough if you mind your own business.

That's thanks to the General and the Shields. Good old Imperial structure, elbow grease, and organization. The Khajiit merchants provide a governing body, but the Shields of Senchal are the muscle behind it. Makes it all run.

Khunzar-ri defeated the demons who plagued his beloved homeland, not with his strength, but with his wit. He tricked them into surrendering their power with false promises and locked them within a mighty fortress.\n\nElsweyr was at peace. For a time.

Hope and solidarity often precede sadness.\n\nThat evening, one of Khunzar-ri's kra'jun came to him, demanding the power of the Dragons. Khunzar-ri refused, but this man, his dear friend, would not take no for an answer ….

He helped Elsweyr rebuild while the Khajiit emerged from the wilds and ruins, filled with hope for the future.\n\nKhunzar-ri stood before the clans as they bowed before him and recognized their new queen, Anequina Sharp-Tongue.

Yes. Khunzar-ri formed a mighty Kra'Jun to defend his home from demons, gathering Nurarion the Perfect from Summerset, Flinthild Demon-Hunter from the frozen north, and the one now called the Betrayer.\n\nJust one remained—Anequina Sharp-Tongue.
The tales say Khunzar-ri produced a confection he came across while gathering his kra'jun—a sweetroll.\n\nHe ate with such joy and passion that Anequina was driven mad with desire for his pastries.

Many say Khunzar-ri won her strength with words of love. Not so.\n\nAnequina was proud and fierce. She had no love for outsiders and told Khunzar-ri as much. To his credit, he was persistent. They spoke for hours as Khunzar-ri explained his plan.
A truly terrifying tale can be quite life-affirming.\n\nThis one tells the story of the Betrayer—who killed Khunzar-ri and was killed in turn, his body parts strewn throughout Elsweyr.
Not just any treasure, but the greatest treasure in all of Elsweyr ….\n\nThe last words of Nurarion the Perfect.

For a High Elf? I know! Back home in Alinor, my mother got so frustrated because I'd laugh at the most serious times. I suppose I'm just not a serious person. That doesn't mean I lack intelligence, as my mentors found out. So, it's not a flaw.

Long after the Betrayer's body was dismembered, a thief dug up the traitor's severed hand. A ring on the Betrayer's thumb held a ruby the size of a robin's egg.\n\nThe greedy fool found and dug up the hand, chopped off the thumb, and stole the ring.

He bragged of his conquest, as fools do. The next night, he woke to sounds of scratching and skittering. He feared scorpions, but when he looked around, all was still.\n\nIt wasn't until morning that he realized the Betrayer's ring was missing.

He wondered the same thing. He searched everywhere, but found nothing. Meanwhile, the skittering continued. He swore something moved in his tent, hiding in dark corners, just beyond his gaze.\n\nWeeks later, he was found in his bed. Strangled to death.

I suppose so. Granted, this isn't one of the bigger guilds and the city is half ruined, but I've already found some hidden and lost gems in the library here.\n\nAnd now, I might even see a Dragon! Preferably from a safe distance.

You are not my mother. Still, she understood that Alinor stifled me. She made sure exemplary tutors taught me magic, and now I spend my time studying it.\n\nBut she was less than thrilled when I decided to come to Senchal for a time.

A treasure, a weapon, and much more. Nurarion's voice could cut lightning bolts in half and turn mountains to rubble. Only his foes heard him speak, and even then, only in whispers.\n\nIt is said that he only screamed twice. Once, to save Sunhold.

When he died.\n\nIn a chamber deep beneath the earth, he screamed into a crystal, pouring years of rage and sorrow into the gem. It brought the cave down on top of him, crushing him. The crystal is still there, as are the echoes of his power.
Very. Some claim the words would sunder Anequina from Pellitine. Others say they could level Rimmen in the blink of an eye.
Oh, it's terrible! Haven't you heard what they've done in Elsweyr? By Arkay's beard, these Dragons were supposed to be myths and legends, not burning the skies and sands of the cat-people's homeland!
Look for a notice around here to set you on your way, but the short version is that if your steel or your spells are mighty enough, travel to Elsweyr and slay Dragons on behalf of the Khajiit!

Predicant Maera and her flock of bloodthirsty priests venerate Saint Alessia, the patron saint of humanity. Around this time of year, they recruit warriors into their festival where the alliances rally for war.

To join in on this violent mayhem, find Predicant Maera at your alliance's gatehouses in Cyrodiil, or possibly at any Battlegrounds rally camp throughout Tamriel. Mind what's in their punch bowl, though.
Why, it's the Festival of New Life! Haven't you kept track of the seasons? Ah, though now I miss spending this time of year with my dear old mother, Arkay rest her soul.
A Nord cleric in Eastmarch named Breda runs most of the festivities for the New Life Festival. You can find her tent outside the gates of Windhelm, just down the road a little ways.

The Argonians need some help.\n\nYou know, I've never been to Black Marsh. Divines know what diseases you can catch in the deep swamps. And the insects! The size of crows or larger! That said, the Argonians sure know how to reward those who help them.
Just travel to the Argonian town of Lilmoth in Murkmire. You'll find plenty of tasks to do there!

I'm attempting to get Tulip to perform a basic trick. It should be a trivial task for a master handler from Summerset's Sil-Var-Woad park.\n\nThe Khajiit who sold her to me spoke highly of her intelligence, but it appears that the trick is on me.

Not yet. I aim to remedy that soon. I have a long history of fighting monsters. Big monsters, Nord-eating creatures, crazed beasts. You name it, and I've stuck my axe in it. \n\nNo one has ever said Margretha Ire-Heart has backed down from a battle.

I live for the thrill of it. I'm not talking about killing a deer on the hunt. That's a necessity. \n\nGoing after a creature many times your size, who has been terrorizing a village or who is wily and cruel …? That's pure heart-pounding action.

I think of myself as more of a specialist. I don't sell my axe to armies. I'm not interested in the inane wars of inane kings. I travel, and I deal with problems. \n\nSometimes I stay some place for a while, but pretty soon, I get restless.
Same way any vengeful monster hunter does, I guess. I was a sapling when frost trolls attacked my small village in Falkreath. I survived, but I swore vengeance against any brutish ravaging creature.

It's a large cult that's fanatically devoted to Laatvulon. They wish for Dragons to rule over Tamriel once more, and don't care what atrocities they must commit to make that happen.\n\nThere's also the mysterious stone they mine. Aeonstone.

If you asked me that question when this began, I would have had few words of hope.\n\nBut we faced many trials together, this Dragonguard. We fought the Order of the New Moon and made it to our final battle.

Not well, if I'm being honest. Our odds don't look very good, and if we fail it's not just the Dragonguard who will fall. The Shields of Senchal are now at risk as well.\n\nDid I convince my father to join a battle we can't possibly win?

In the Black Kiergo, the greater the risk, the greater the reward.\n\nThat's the game we're playing now, walker. If we win, we save my people from certain destruction. But we're wagering our lives, make no mistake.
This one just wants you to understand what an asset he will be in this fight. After all, Za'ji is now a seasoned Dragon slayer.\n\nNow, where is our ballista?

He's a Dragon of considerable power.\n\nLong ago, Nahfahlaar worked with the Dragonguard to defeat him. They were able to trap Laatvulon for centuries, but he recently escaped his prison and formed a cult to do his bidding.

Aeonstone has the ability to absorb magical energy and amplify it.\n\nThe Order of the New Moon has been feeding their own spiritual energy to the stone in order to empower Laatvulon and his Dragon allies.

We first faced the Order of the New Moon when we reached the Dragonguard Sanctum. They were sent to slay Nahfahlaar and had no compunction about killing us in the process.\n\nOnce we dispatched most of their number, they fled.

That seems to be the case.\n\nIt's likely the cult is empowering Laatvulon using the aeonstone at this very moment, and that power will make him a formidable foe. That's why it's important we find Nahfahlaar. We need a Dragon of our own.

And you learned much from that infiltration, including the cult's plan to attack Pridehome. We may not have been able to save the temple, but we did learn key information before the Clan Mother died.\n\nAnd then there's the mask.

And again we were blind to the cult's actions. We had no idea that they were mining aeonstone, nor that they had captured Yahgrondu.\n\nAnd as a result, the Dragon died before he was able to ally with us.
And by doing so, you struck a crushing blow to the Order of the New Moon.\n\nNot only were you able to defeat their Dragon Priest, you also ensured that Laatvulon couldn't use the mask.

Nothing short of world domination. If he succeeds, Dragons will rule over Tamriel once more.\n\nHow precisely he plans to do this, we're not sure. But he has killed many, including his own kind, in order to make that desire a reality.
Hope is a flickering flame, Dragonguard. Do not let the winds of doubt blow it out.\n\nWe may not win, we may not live, but we always have the choice to fight. And so I shall, until my last breath.

I may not like it, but Nahfahlaar possesses knowledge about Laatvulon that we just don't have. And the might of a Dragon at our disposal isn't something to toss away lightly.\n\nYes, I'd rather have Nahfahlaar on our side than against us.

I can't help but wonder if this is the reason I was brought back. To fight this battle, to end this threat. Or perhaps merely to aid you, Vestige.\n\nWhatever the reason, I'm glad I was able to fight by your side once more.

We've been through much together, you and I. To Oblivion and back.\n\nI want you to know how much your companionship has meant to me. Without your aid, I could have never hoped to reform the Dragonguard. Thank you, Vestige. For everything.

Even if we die, the fires of our legacy shall burn forever. Others will be inspired by our bravery, by our willingness to fight against unbeatable odds.\n\nIf we are defeated here, the fight against Laatvulon shall continue. I'm sure of it.

This grappling bow! Za'ji found it in the sanctum before we left for Black Heights. He thought it might come in handy.\n\nLooks simple enough to use. Just aim and pull the trigger. Like a crossbow, yes? Then the rope propels you upward.

Za'ji grew bored spending all his time in the temple. All the praying and cleaning and chanting.\n\nSo Za'ji would come here. He hid away high in an alcove so the Moon-Priests wouldn't find him and stole a key so he could explore the back rooms.

I'm just glad you're with us. I always feel so much more at ease when you're fighting alongside me.\n\nBut you have a Dragon to save! And a Dragon to slay, I suppose. I won't keep you any longer. Good luck.

I know, I know. And it's not like I'm about to turn tail after all we've been through. I'm just … nervous. Isn't that normal before a big battle?\n\nMy heart feels like it's about to pound right out of my chest.

What you see will be much like a paw print on glass. A stain left on the things it has touched. Find them and the tonic will allow you to see the impressions it left behind.\n\nThat knowledge may put a name to this evil and be the key to banishing it.
And I'll admit, it did feel good to take one of those bastards down.\n\nI never knew that Dragon blood ran so hot. Nearly scalded my tongue ripping out the beast's throat.
Just the one. Don't die, yes?
Oh. No ballista. Huh.\n\nA trebuchet, then? Or perhaps even a catapult? Maybe even just a very, very big bow?
Then perhaps Za'ji should make his way back to the sentry tower. He'll watch over the fight from there.

If Za'ji dies, bring his body back to Black Heights. \n\nIf he is to meet Khenarthi and travel to the Sands Behind the Stars, he would rather mother send him on his way. She is an expert in such matters, after all.

Yes … yes, you do. This one will fight, then. For Elsweyr, for the Dragonguard. For his friends. Even if he's scared out of his mind. Not that he's scared, mind you.\n\nZa'ji would ask that you hear one request, walker.

Precisely. She must have needed the mask's power to defeat Laatvulon.\n\nJa'darri and the Dragonguard had another ally as well. Nahfahlaar. He gave them his own horn to use against Laatvulon, but he also refused Ja'darri something.

And then the final battle. Ja'darri fell, but the Dragonguard was still able to trap Laatvulon. For centuries he was sealed away, beneath this very keep.\n\nUntil he escaped, that is. Which leads us to today's battle.
What I'm interested in is how Ja'darri was able to use the Mask of Alkosh against Laatvulon. Though I suspect Nahfahlaar may have some insight on that as well.\n\nWe should continue our search.
Of course, mask-bearer. Ja'darri is sure you have many questions. Just don't expect too many answers, yes?

It is not a place, but a story that has been and will be told time and time again.\n\nWe are within the tapestry and without it. Wrapped up tightly in its threads even as we desperately try to untangle them.

Ja'darri was born under eclipsed Moons, yet was destined to never become Mane. \n\nAnd as she listened to the Moons, they sang to her a song as sweet as candied moon-sugar. Until the day their song became the steady beat of drums.

Perhaps that is why Alkosh entrusted the Khajiit with his secrets, no?

Alkosh is he who weaves the tapestry, and also he who is the threads. They unspool from the tip of his tail. When the thread ends, there will be nothing.\n\nWe are all woven into his tapestry, walker. We are always within the realm of time.

The darkness of Lorkhaj had stained her soul, the bruising purple of spilled wine. Soon, all she could hear was beautiful, terrible whispers.\n\nAnd so this one decided to make her way to the Sands Behind the Stars before she was forever lost.

You walked the Halls of the Highmane, have you not? You proved yourself worthy, and were gifted the Mask of Alkosh.\n\nThose trials, those halls. They reflect Ja'darri's battle, deep in her heart. A battle that she won.

But Khenarthi carried Ja'darri not above to the stars, but into the darkness that had settled in this one's heart.\n\nJa'darri was given two gifts. A lantern to guide and a sword to protect, and both shined with Alkosh's divine light.
Ja'darri was gifted the Mask of Alkosh and told to protect his most sacred tapestry. To slay a demon who would undo all of time.\n\nBut now that duty lies upon your shoulders. Bear it wisely.

Paint for her vile mural, no doubt. Adara'hai is beginning to see how the Wall of Life became so defiled.\n\nThere is hope, walker. How a curse is made is also how it may be undone. Did you see what he used for his offering to the Great Darkness?
Ah, well. Za'ji will admit there was one or two moments of doubt, but they passed by very quickly! He hardly noticed them at all.\n\nYou know, walker …. Ah. Forget it.

At the danger of sounding boorish, Za'ji just wanted to thank you. For all that you've done.\n\nWhen this one left Black Heights, it was to seek adventure and glory. And so he bought a fine vessel and assembled a gallant crew. However ….

However, adventure and glory is a bit hard to seek out. It's not often you come upon sign posts asking for mighty heroes to save the kingdom!\n\nWell, maybe you do. It seems like you have that sort of luck.

And now the Moon-Singers will tell stories of us for generations to come.\n\nSo, thanks for giving Za'ji a chance to become the hero he always knew he could be. And for letting us come along with you on this unbelievable adventure.

The point is that Sai Sahan was right to doubt Za'ji and his crew. We were smugglers, not heroes. Ruffians trying to make enough gold to get by.\n\nAnd then you came along and asked us to take you here, to this island.

I've actually been thinking a lot about that. Our order.\n\nI honestly wonder if it will last. Maybe Za'ji and Caska will get bored and seek out another adventure. Maybe another threat will call Sai Sahan away.

A little. But mostly the thought makes me … sad.\n\nI've come to think of the Dragonguard as a family of sorts. And I fear that if the order disbanded, if there was no longer a reason to fight, I would lose that.

What is the New Moon that the cult worshiped? How did Laatvulon plan to rule over Tamriel?\n\nThey're just questions that keep bouncing around in my head. It might be nothing, but I'm just not sure this is over yet.
I know, I know. There's no shortage of work. I'm just being silly, is all.\n\nBut then there's also this feeling that our battle isn't truly over. Which is an even scarier thought, isn't it?

Not dead, which is better than I expected.\n\nIt all worked out though, didn't it? Aeliah protected Senchal, Za'ji became a hero, Sai Sahan ended a grave threat to Tamriel. And you got to be the mighty hero at the center of it all.

I'm a simple Senche-raht, walker. There was an enemy and I killed it. What greater satisfaction is there?\n\nMy only regret was not killing Laatvulon sooner. Many of my people died because of him and his cult.

But there's still Dragons in Elsweyr. Cruel, terrible Dragons who want nothing more than to kill and destroy and conquer.\n\nAnd I won't let them. As the Moons are my witness, I'll hunt them all down. Every last one.

And all for their own protection. They were too afraid to fight the Dragons that terrorized their land. And so they joined with forces that they did not understand.\n\nAnd many suffered because of that. I won't forget that.
Far more confident of our Dragonguard, I must admit.\n\nWhen we first formed our order, all I saw was a ragtag band of smugglers, ill experienced and naive in the ways of battle.

Ah, yes, young Aeliah. How could I forget.\n\nBut now I look around me and I see soldiers, tried and true. Warriors who were willing to lay down their lives to protect Elsweyr. And if that's not in the spirit of the Dragonguard, I don't know what is.

And now I have another chance to make things right. Not in the empire, perhaps, but here in a land that has a great need for a Dragonguard to watch over it.\n\nAnd I expect your help as well, my friend. As always.

Captain. Yes, I suppose I am, aren't I?\n\nIt's been a long time since I last held that rank. I failed to uphold my duty, then. I allowed my emperor to die, and watched as our empire fell into the clutches of Daedra.
Yes, of course. Vijari will not falter again.
Please, not another word. Vijari cannot bear it. Just … just let him prepare for his journey.
What are you saying? This one's father? No, no, no, no. Vijari's ears deceive him.

Continue to help Adara'hai. Ka'ishka cannot safeguard Vijari's soul, but she can take care of his body. If he is feverish, she will offer her tongue. If he must bite back the pain, she will offer her tail. If he cannot walk, she will offer her legs.

Ka'ishka has never seen chubloons or felrunners in Tenmar, but she knows terror birds prowl the jungle outside the village. They are truly beastly. Thankfully the senche keep them from getting too close to Black Heights.
Forgive this one. She has seen many flowers she could describe as such. The artists use all sorts of petals in the Colorworks. Perhaps something there?
Ka'ishka does not like where this is going. Is this asking you to peel skin from the dead? This one does not wish to know the answer.
Your painter is a morbid joker.\n\nThe white sycamore is a holy symbol of Khenarthi, for she carries its seeds far and wide on her winds. Khajiit use its bark for the purest of whites.
Vijari takes medicine made from blue poppies for his pain. They give him strange dreams. It is a strange choice for paint, but it would do.
Vijari does not know why one would use flowers when water beetles are plentiful and make better pigment, but there are many petals to choose from for a sky blue.

Well, after you, Tharn, and Sai investigated the New Moon Fortress, Tharn used the aeonstones to open a portal to Dragonhold. There, you stopped a ritual and killed a Dragon, but not before Kaalgrontiid made the island float into the sky.

Yes, we can safely approach the island now, except it's floating way up in the sky. Nahfahlaar decided to go deal with the lesser Dragons, leaving us to figure out how to reach Dragonhold on our own.\n\nNot that we've had any bright ideas as of yet.

I'm going to finish my drink and then find the next ship out of this Moons-forsaken city.\n\nIf Dragons weren't bad enough, all these refugees will eat Senchal out of house and home. I'm leaving before the riots start.
That's the spirit. We have a Dragon to slay, after all! No need for further delay.
Very good. Let's go deal with that Dragon!

I do not think so. Those ancient edifices connect only to specific locations. I do not think one of those would be on Kaalgrontiid's island.\n\nNow that you are here, there is something else I would like to try.
She knows what breaking the curse requires. Whatever happens, I trust she's prepared.\n\nPlace the locket in the flame, my friend. Please.

No. Not this time. I want to search the memories and see if Anequina has more to tell us about Kaalgrontiid and her adventures with Khunzar-ri.\n\nI will confer with Sai Sahan, then have him meet you at the Moonlit Cove.

This one will sing her prayers to Azurah to lend him her power, so his every brush stroke shines a ray of light through the Great Darkness. My sister is the light of his life that will guide his path.\n\nYou, walker, must be his sword.
Azurah be your shield. Make your way to the Wall of Life and clear a safe path. Khajiit will follow once Vijari's paint is rightly consecrated.\n\nStrike the Khenarthic bell to signal it is safe.

Caska? Why she's the Pounce's first mate, of course!\n\nDon't take her manner personally, walker. She's a Khajiit of few words and little patience. And so this one would recommend you stay on her good side, yes?
Well, she didn't earn the title Caska the Unconquered without biting off a few heads. Do not try your luck, walker.

All ships coming into Senchal are subject to a cargo inspection, unless they present a sanctioned ship's manifest. If you're able to steal Arniel's manifest, he'll be held up in customs for hours.\n\nThat will give us time to speak with the general.

Banish him with claw and fang and the Dusk-Canticles along with any other Bent Cats he has drawn here. If the passage is as steeped in darkness as the Wall of Life, this will be an uphill battle in more ways than one.

A Dragonhorn of immense power. Its sound forces Dragons to fall from the sky. It should give us a great advantage in battle.\n\nThat said, we may also find more resistance than a Dragon on the island.

That is the name it came to be known by.\n\nYou said that Vahlokzin stole my horn. No doubt he wished to protect my kind from its power. Even as he hid it away, the Dragonguard hunted us to near extinction. Nonvul mey. What an honorable fool.

Thank Khenarthi. He feared the Darkness swallowed him before he could.\n\nHe heard his father calling him. He had to go. To see him. There was a great crack of a bell and he was gone. Is his father …?
Twisted as it is, Vijari knows there is love in his father's heart. This one prays the Divines will show mercy and wrench it right-ways some day.
You are kind to gift Vijari one of Rajhin's gentle fibs, but he has come to terms with what he's lost. He knows his father loved him more than life itself, and that is enough.

Someone on this ship has to be. If everyone plans for sunny weather, how will we survive a storm?\n\nDespite the odds, it's not hopeless, though. If we can fight, then there's always a chance we can win.
And wait for this Dragon to burn the city to the ground?\n\nNo, it's better to die fighting than to perish hiding behind a wall. Besides, we're profiteers. We know a thing or two about risk.

I won't deny Za'ji is cunning when he wants to be, but it's Caska that keeps this ship afloat.\n\nShe schedules repairs, oversees our provisions, pays the crew. And she keeps us all safe, of course. I haven't seen her lose a fight yet.

What's not to like? He respects his crew, makes sure we're well cared for. And he's always excited for the next adventure. It's a bit contagious, actually.\n\nStill, I don't know if this ship could actually function without Caska.
You compare the sands of the hourglass to the moments which pass through time. Can they truly be the same? But then, are they truly so different?\n\nIt is one answer only the Dragon King knows.

Most curious.\n\nAlkosh and Khenarthi see every trail along the Many Paths of time. They knew that Sai Sahan was destined to lead you here, to this very moment. And perhaps they were the ones who ensured that he was alive to do so.
Perhaps not in a way so easily understood.\n\nBut Ja'darri does sense something. You have a companion with you now, yes? A man who was somehow connected to the Amulet of Kings as well.
Now that would be assuming Alkosh's divine will, would it not? Many would consider that … what is the word? Ah. Blasphemous.\n\nJa'darri simply thinks aloud. Take from her words what you will.
Perhaps not in a way so easily understood.\n\nJust know that the Dragon King guides you now, just as he guided you then. But it is you who must walk the path he lays before you. Never forget that.

No, five-claw. Without Tharn to guide me, I do not want to risk all of our eggs in this particular basket. The Dragonguard will remain in reserve. Let them defend Senchal. Then, if we fail, it will be up to them to stop Kaalgrontiid.
It is an honor that few mortals have received from my kind. Dovahzin. A Dragon name.\n\nOnce, I called you hunter. Now you are Ahkahtuz.
Everything.\n\nYou are hunter still, yes. But now you are proud, unbroken. Bound to my power by the Dragon King of Time. Defender of my father's will. And so I honor you with a Dragon's name.

Our mission was successful, my friend. It just didn't end as we expected.\n\nWe secured passage to the island. We found the Dragon. And we made sure Senchal was safe … at least from this potential threat. Not bad for a day's work.
Rags! Stupid Tapestry. I can't even use it to gamble. Stupid idea. Brought Dancer bad luck. \n\nOr maybe just drinking and gambling brought bad luck. Stupid tapestry didn't help though.
Who wants an old rag. No one. The lizard lady behind the bar here might use it to mop up drinks. All its good for. You take it. Maybe Dancer's luck will change.

Aeonstones have been placed around the island. I believe Kaalgrontiid uses them to reflect and enhance his power, multiplying it until it reaches a level where he can use it to complete his ascension.\n\nWe must destroy these focal points.

Hmm? Ah, yes! Za'ji will speak to the crew.\n\nHowever, there are two crew members you may wish to speak with personally. Dirge Truptor, the Imperial with a weasel face, and the beautiful Chizbari. Their particular talents may prove interesting.
Za'ji has not a single doubt! Not a one!\n\nWe may be just smugglers to you and the bearded one, but our hearts sing for adventure. They will all take up the call, this one is sure!

Life on the seas is not easy, walker. You must be able to adapt at a moment's notice if you wish to survive its many dangers. Storms, attacking ships, sea serpents!\n\nThe Pounce's crew will learn to navigate the dangers of Dragons just as readily.
Of course! Za'ji is their captain, after all.\n\nThis one is confident that his crew will become the greatest Dragonguard to ever walk the sands of Elsweyr. It's just a matter of time!

Perhaps Nahfahlaar knows something. He's dealt with Laatvulon in the past and may have insight into the cult's motivations. Why don't you talk with our Dragon ally?\n\nMeanwhile, I'll rally the rest of the Dragonguard and head to Pridehome.

Oh-ho! Now there's a story. But I'll give you the short version.\n\nThe Shields of Senchal, formerly known as the Thirteenth Legion, protects this fine city of Senchal. Protects, mind you, not rules. The cats here seem quite taken with our efforts.

Yes, we're Imperials. Emperor Aquilarios sent us over five years ago to help with the Knahaten Flu recovery. Now we're kind of stuck here, I guess. Good thing for the locals, too, considering. Bah. Dragons. Like we didn't have enough problems.

Yeah. Temple's a Meridian temple. You know, the Lady of Infinite Energies. She whose arse sheds light and nasty guardians. Maybe you didn't know she's also the Lady of Greed. Got some stories about how she collects people, too. Over ale, though.

Can't say that I do.\n\nLook, some folks venerate the Lady of Infinite Energies like she's their personal savior. But I have stories about her greed that'll turn a baby's hair white. So, yeah. I don't like her one bit.

Since you did in Laatvulon? Quiet, Dragonguard, quiet. But Sai Sahan's mood has put everyone on edge, I won't lie. Even Nahfahlaar seems out of sorts.\n\nYou best get back there and see if you can get them back on the straight and narrow.

Picked up on that, did you?\n\nMeridia's not altruistic. No, she's got some qualities I'd call problematic. Greed, for one. And greed is bad enough in people like us, you know? In a Daedric Prince? It's way worse. So, yeah. Bad memories thanks to her.

The humans and Khajiit could, but not Nahfahlaar. We need that Dragon and the bond you share to defeat Kaalgrontiid.\n\nAs long as the aegis is in place, Nahfahlaar can't reach Dragonhold. We need to remove it.

Then let us aid him.\n\nJourney to Senchal and speak with General Renmus. He may not join us in our fight, but he may have reports concerning Nahfahlaar and Laatvulon. I don't expect it will be hard to spot two Dragons engaged in battle.
More tips, more tips ….\n\nAh! There is a grapple point on the edge of some nearby scaffolding. Aim for that and let the bow do all the work!
You are an expert? All right, then!\n\nThere's a grapple point on the edge of some nearby scaffolding. Aim for that and let the bow do the rest of the work.

Oh, yes. She screeched and scowled at Za'ji's blasphemous disregard of his chores every time he returned home.\n\nEventually, mother realized the less we saw of one another, the better it was for both of us.

Za'ji left to pursue a life of adventure. The open seas offer far more than a small town such as Black Heights.\n\nBut this one will admit that his strained relationship with his mother made for a painless parting.
Yes, but … we are not supposed to talk about our past lives. We are initiates of the New Moon, you understand? Nothing else matters.\n\nDo you also face the Path of the New Moon?
Then you will not mind if Lahini follows behind, no?\n\nOnce the trial is done, this one is sure she will be of great use to the Order of the New Moon. She just needs a little help getting there.
I am an apprentice at the Abbey of Blades. It is my destiny to one day become a Blademaster and honor the ways of the ancient Yokudan sword-singers.
I accompanied Blademaster Sai Sahan to this city, but must now return to the abbey. I still have many years of training ahead of me.\n\nI do wish you luck on your own journey, warrior.

Bahzahar has some harebrained scheme. Probably thinks the moonlit water can be used to make more potent moon-sugar. Which, in turn, could make more potent skooma.\n\nBut what does Za'ji know about skooma? Less than you might think, yes.

Told you it'd be easy. The other bits I need won't just be lying around for you to pick over like skeevers.\n\nNext time you get around to actually killing a Dragon, you get me the parts I need and I'll make it worth your while.
Already wrote you a list, it's on the table there. Give it a once over and keep a copy for yourself. You'll be a regular Dragon butcher in no time.

Oh, yes! They are totally imperceptible without my special concoction.\n\nOnce you do see them in all their wonder and listen to their beautiful song, you'll never look at the world the same way again. I guarantee it!

Sure. Eventually. But not without my special ingredients. And to get more of those, I need to return to Skyrim. There's a cave I know that descends deep into the earth where—\n\nGoodness! I almost did it again! I really need to stop talking now. Bye!

Only rumors. This one hears they prey on the desperate. The hungry. The cult promises warm beds and hot meals. For many, that is all it takes.\n\nBut this one thinks that Lahini joined them for a sense of purpose. She considered herself a burden.

Lahini was weak, sickly. We love her anyway, but she felt she could be useful to this Order of the New Moon. Useful how, this one wonders? She could be hurt. She could be ….\n\nPlease, you have to find her. Before it's too late.
Of course Lahini is sure.\n\nAt home, all she did was sit cozy while the rest of her family toiled away. This one was but a hindrance! But here, she can be useful. She can help.

This one had no idea mother would react in such a way. Lahini will return to Senchal and let her know that everything is all right. Lahini doesn't want her to suffer.\n\nThank you for letting this one know.
But now is not the time to chat, yes? The ceremony awaits! We must be on our way.

There's always a fight going on in the Black Kiergo. Some come to watch, some come to bet, some come to compete.\n\nToday's battle is to the death. You walk out victorious or you don't walk out at all.

Master Shirnama has the privilege of hosting today's match. According to him, whoever wins will earn a great boon from the Order of the New Moon. What that boon is? No idea.\n\nYou'll just have to enter the match and find out.

Dragons have returned to Tamriel. Many fear them, many hate them. But the Order of the New Moon understands the truth.\n\nThe Dragons are destined to rule this land. To fight against them is to die. To join them is to thrive.

In return for our loyalty, the Dragons have promised us unending glory. A New Moon shall rise over Elsweyr, and only the faithful will share in its power.\n\nBut you will learn more in the New Moon Fortress, yes? Be on your way.

Yeah, I bet a lot of people would. But they're never going to hear about it because you're going to keep this little anecdote to yourself, right? I got a reputation to protect here.\n\nI heard about what happened in Summerset. I really miss that guy.
Ugh. But enough about that. We were busy talking about funny stuff like getting captured and thrown in a wagon.
Yeah, yeah, I bet a lot of people would. But they're never going to hear about it because you're going to keep this little anecdote to yourself, right? I got a reputation to protect here. Ha!

And I did, too. For a little while. Then I received a response to my letter and my uncle invited me to Southern Elsweyr.\n\nI may have exaggerated my level of experience, which is why Uncle Hizhikar trusted me with his precious cargo.

The Path of the New Moon is obstructed by two doors. To unlock them, you must move the sliding stones below onto platforms. Make your way past both doors and you pass the trial.\n\nHowever, the path you must move through is not a simple one.
Precisely.\n\nProve your cunning by finding the way forward. Display your strength by moving the sliding stones as you wish. Unleash your ferocity and strike down any who stand in your way.

Several barriers block your path. By the brazier's light, these barriers will vanish.\n\nTherein lies the challenge. Which barrier do you open? Where do you move the sliding stone? Which path leads to the platform?

Oh, I would've. Trust me. Couldn't wait to bust loose and beat the tar out of those runts! But once they put Tajahir and Marekki in there with me I had to take it easy. Neither one can swing a sword. If a fight broke out? Wouldn't have been pretty.

Now? I try to reconcile with the man I betrayed.\n\nI will try to contact Catina one last time before we drift to Aetherius, but if I can't, tell her I love her. More than anything. I'm sorry I caused her such distress.

Tell her the truth. Her father wanted to save everyone despite the risks. I wanted to keep her safe.\n\nJano and I both made mistakes. Pride and stubbornness. Cowardice and heartache …. But now we can make things right. We can find peace.
Mother is worried about this one?\n\nYou must be mistaken. Lahini's family no longer needs to suffer the burden of a useless daughter. They are probably giddy with relief now that she has left.
You are a stranger to Elsweyr, so you must not know better. Khina forgives you.\n\nKhajiit have many forms and many talents. Let that not surprise you in the future.

Ha! She says she's keen to travel. I wager a long walk in the Pale would put that to the test. Anyway, she wears a coat year round. She'll be fine!\n\nI bet you'll be off soon, too. Take care of yourself, all right?

As many as she can manage. Not everyone makes it though, you know? Not enough bedrolls. Not enough food to go 'round. Most wind up working for Turo eventually, Hircine take him.\n\nAn empty belly will make you do all sorts of nasty things.
Just make it quick! Malahbu's fur falls out from all this worry.

This one secured passage on a Nord merchant ship bound for Mistral. Plenty of opportunities there for people like my brother and me.\n\nI owe the ship's captain, Sormund, just a few drakes more. Soon we will turn our backs on this place for good.

I …. We live hand-to-mouth here, walker. In South Guard, you learn to steal or you starve. It is that simple.\n\nDaini does what she has to to keep us afloat, but Safik has a gentle heart. He still has a chance to do something good with his life.

His business ventures are broadening, as is he. We discussed both at length when he came in for a new silk suit. \n\nIt's the pies that Nirahni makes. He loves her baking. Velsa sometimes chases him out of her home with a broom.

Indeed she is, and doing the Guild proud. Of course Velsa never lets her get a swollen head about it. The two of them still go at it. \n\nWalks-Softly and Quen just ignore them and do a good job of training newer recruits.

Adara'hai is a Twilight Cantor. She sings the Dusk-Canticles so Khajiit are not swayed by the beat of Lorkhaj's heart, and to drive off the Bent Cats already lost.\n\nIf Ka'ishka's fears are well founded, her husband's soul is in grave peril.

Now she sells us out to save her own hide. Typical.\n\nIn her heart, Daini always knew Antonia would get cold paws and call off before long. This one just hoped the little skeever would do it quietly.

There is hope, but exorcising dro-m'Athra carries great risk. They will claw at this one to silence her song, or try to twist her tune until she too sways her tail to the Bent Dance. Cantors normally walk with a pride of sharp-claws to do this.

I do. The crew of the Perfect Pounce accompanied us on one Dragon hunt and handled themselves well. See if they're willing to make our association more permanent.\n\nSpeak to Za'ji and see if he and his crew would like to join our order.

Then she probably died with the rest of them. What a shame.\n\nWe need to report to Sai Sahan. He needs to know about the attack on Pridehome, the aeonstones, all of it. Let's return to the Dragonguard Sanctum.

You saved her life, walker. Had Lahini joined that ceremony, she would have died with the rest of them. \n\nWe need to report this to Sai Sahan. The attack on Pridehome, the aeonstones, all of it. Let's return to the Dragonguard Sanctum.

A gift from the Lady of Light, she said. I thought it was a joke. Or a swindler trying to take our gold. But she never asked for a thing.\n\nJ'saad accepted the gift against my wishes. The note you found explains the rest.
You are looking somewhat sallow. Best not to let the sickening skooma seep in too deeply.\n\nStep into the shallows my squeamish savior and spit all that poison out to sea!

Bebbia has been invited to no less than seven committees for Senchal's beautification. And she has aims to recover other lost works to return to the city and restore to their prior glory.\n\nShe'll be stuck here a while, it seems.

No, no. She has missed her home for a while now. Though it does feel odd to be settling in after so long bouncing around like a Baandari Pedlar.\n\nBebbia will travel again, she is certain, but not before Senchal is on the mend.

Lady Bebbia has graciously extended her hospitality. I would be a fool to refuse such an illustrious invitation.\n\nI've asked an associate to mind my business in Abah's Landing in the mean time. He's the only one I could trust to handle it.

Abah's Landing trades in all manner of hard-to-acquire commodities, but the toughest thing to find there is trustworthiness. There's a Khajiit importer I deal with who is as clean as anyone can be in that city. He'll be able to handle it.
More than sugarcane, I can tell you that.\n\nThis place might have kept the ghosts out, but it will not thwart us, walker. We will take what's ours.

It never bothered Papa. He said storing goods in a sacred place kept the ghosts out. Daini does not know why ghosts would try to get into boxes of sugarcane. Just silly, you know?\n\nPapa used to say silly things like that all the time.
We were both taken in by the temple at a young age. Together, we learned the ways of Alkosh and the tapestry of time.\n\nBut Ra'khajin was always different from this one. Special in some way.

Not much. King Jorunn's mages are still studying the ritual fragment we discovered, but there's been no further word on the witches' mysterious patron.\n\nSo far, the evidence only suggests that they're planning an attack on the mainland.

We're not exactly sure. That's why Jorunn sent me to investigate. But you saw the storms they controlled in the Sea of Ghosts. Imagine that kind of destruction unleashed on a town or city.\n\nLook, are you ready to go or do you need time to prepare?
Upstairs, in his chamber. He seems … troubled about everything that happened.\n\nTalk to the Dragon. Find out what occurred on the island after we left.

Over the years, Ra'khajin grew more resentful. Always questioning Alkosh's will and his place in Pridehome. Eventually, he left our temple.\n\nAnd now he has returned to massacre us all. By Alkosh, how can this be?

He was isolated from the rest of us. He learned secrets from the Clan Mother that no one else learned. Trained to become a warrior.\n\nAs a cub, this one was often jealous. But now Nuziwa sees that such a life was not a blessing, but a burden.

King Jorunn sent me to look into a sudden barrage of storms in the Sea of Ghosts. At least two ships sank beneath the freezing waves.\n\nThe Icereach Coven was responsible. I uncovered evidence suggesting they're planning an attack on the mainland.

I'm not exactly sure. That's why we need to investigate. But if they have the ability to summon destructive storms on command, think of the damage they can inflict on towns and cities.\n\nLook, are you ready to go or do you need time to prepare?

Just so! A singer, a tale-spinner, and spinner of tails. Shazar regrets that you see him in this sorry state, but his thespian spirit shone through his sloppy appearance!\n\nOr his manner of speaking suggested so.

Keep your voice down! Buildings have ears, especially guildhalls.\n\nI'll give you all the details when we get where we're going. I chartered a wagon to take us there. Is there anything else you need to know before we head out?
I prepared for a moment such as this. I insist that you trust me, this one last time.\n\nIf this is goodbye, my friend, it has been a privilege.

Keep your voice down! Buildings have ears, especially guildhalls.\n\nI'll provide all the details when we get to the meeting place. I chartered a wagon to take us there. Is there anything else you need to know before we get started?

Lyris Titanborn. I served Emperor Varen before the Soulburst tore the empire apart and plunged Cyrodiil into civil war.\n\nStill, my first loyalty has always been to Skyrim. When the Skald-King asked for my help, I obliged.

We just have to hope there's another path.\n\nWhen you reach the other side, look for anything out of the ordinary. A lever to pull or something to light. Anything that may help me traverse the chasm as well.

That's a memory I'd rather not dredge up right now. But it wasn't Emperor Varen's fault. He was betrayed. We all were.\n\nLet's not dwell on ancient history. We have a threat right in front of us. We can save Tamriel if we act fast.
