We defeated Molag Bal and stopped the Planemeld, but the empire I knew was dead and gone. There wasn't anything else I could do for Varen or Cyrodiil, but Skyrim was still there.\n\nSo, I went home.

Whatever I can. Traveling. Dealing with problems as I encounter them. My axe has been busy, that's for sure!\n\nMostly, I've been helping Jorunn the Skald-King. Looking into bad situations. Like this one with the Icereach Coven.
Oh. That. Right. I'm not really sure. I remember white light as the Amulet of Kings took me, and then …. \n\nI woke up. I wasn't in Tamriel. I was somewhere else. Somewhere cold. I was home.
Neither do I. Was I in Sovngarde? Maybe. But then I was back here, in Tamriel. I guess there are still a few things that me and my axe need to do.\n\nIn general, though, I try not to think about it.

It felt like home. There was a great longhouse in the fog. It was warm inside, full of people like me. Warriors.\n\nI don't know how long I was there, but eventually I woke up one day and I really was home. In Skyrim.
What? How? We watched him sacrifice himself to empower the Amulet of Kings!\n\nHow could he come back from that? It can't be him. It must be some sort of trick!
And he didn't send word to me? What an idiot!\n\nI … enough of this. We need to focus on the threat in front of us. Sai can wait. He's good at that, apparently.

Everything and more, my friend, everything and more. In the time that Zamarak has served, Queen Khamira has proven to be … a very active monarch.\n\nShe is exactly what Elsweyr needs. Even if it makes this one's job ever more difficult.

Oh, nothing like what we faced back in Northern Elsweyr, but then again, we weren't fighting Dragons atop floating islands.\n\nYes, we heard all about it. Sounds exhilarating! Once everything settles down, I must hear your version of the story.

The Icereach Coven. Witches operating in secret right under the Skald-King's voluminous nose. And this isn't just the usual Reach mischief, of that I'm sure.\n\nI need to investigate, but I can't do it by myself.

Help me locate the coven and determine their ultimate intentions. Between the two of us, we can cover more ground and figure out the full extent of this threat.\n\nAs long as the magic Jorunn's wizards gave me works as promised, that is.
Thank you, my friend. We all owe you a tremendous debt of gratitude. Farewell.

I imagine it will be similar to how you cleansed the bells in Khenarthi's Breath Temple.\n\nThe small bells glow in a certain order. All you need to do is hit the larger bells nearby in the same order. That should cleanse them.

Adara'hai came to support her sister through a trying ordeal. Ka'ishka's husband has been ill for a very long time. Adara'hai knew she needed help from her letter, but this one didn't think she meant an exorcism.\n\nIt seems she was mistaken.

We did, my friend, and Tamriel owes you a great debt. You and Abnur Tharn both.\n\nDamn that old wizard for playing the hero. He contained a blast that should have turned Elsweyr into ash and cinders. But did he have to get himself killed to do it?

If Vijari is not yet lost to the Great Darkness, then there is hope, but exorcising dro-m'Athra is risky, as you know. The Bent Cats will do all they can to silence Adara'hai's song or twist it to their tune.\n\nShe brought no sharp-claws on this trip.

Aeliah believes the cult is recruiting in Senchal. I want you to find a recruiter and join their ranks. As a member of the cult, you'll be privy to a great deal of information.\n\nBut first, you'll want to speak with General Renmus.

If there's cult activity in the city, Renmus should know something about it. I want you to see if he has any leads you can follow.\n\nAeliah's agreed to get you into the palace. No need to schedule another appointment.

A Dragon's words. They possess power few mortals understand. When we give our word, we are bound by it. That is our way.\n\nThe Dragon Yahgrondu vowed to aid me in a time of need. We must seek him out and remind him of the oath he made.

Yes, but I do not know where he hides. I leave that task to you, hunter. The Dragonguard of old were accomplished trackers, were they not?\n\nSeek the aid of a companion who knows this land well. Perhaps they can help you find Yahgrondu.

Ka'ishka told Adara'hai that there are more Khenarthic Bells along this passage. The dying would ring them on their way to the summit to announce their coming to Khenarthi.\n\nA strong peal should drown out the heart and help her cast out the darkness.

Many have clawed their way out of the Dark to invade our world, but some, she fears, are villagers who went to the Wall of Life seeking salvation from Khenarthi only to find damnation instead.\n\nOnce Khajiit become dro-m'Athra they are lost for good.

Adara'hai has never seen a Bent Cat return to the true path. Never once has she heard another Twilight Cantor claim it possible. Those who have tried inevitably succumbed to their corruption.\n\nAll we can do is return them to the Darkness.

Adara'hai will stay with her awhile. Supporting her through this loss was why this one came in the first place. Vijari was her world. Now that he is gone, Adara'hai does not know what her sister will do.

This one will return to her temple and share what she has learned with the Twilight Cantors there. These Khenarthic Bells are a powerful force against the Heart of Lorkhaj. Adara'hai hopes something smaller could be made for cantors to carry.

Living and dead are not words that apply to Bent Cats. They are part of the Great Darkness. As immaterial as the Void until enough of the darkness creeps into our world to cast a shadow. All we can do is disperse those shadows, never kill them.

Vijari left her a home here. Adara'hai would hope she made a life here during their time together, but … this one was out of touch, so what does she know.\n\nWhatever Ka'ishka decides to do, Adara'hai will support her.
She cannot say. Adara'hai doubts a smaller bell will drown out the Bent Dance as well as those placed here, but any force fighting against the Great Darkness is a good one.

He could, walker. He likely will. Vijari is beyond his reach now, but the darkness within him will drive him to harm others. All dro-m'Athra seek to unleash their hatred and pain upon True Cats. It's all they have left.

This loss hurts, but Ka'ishka feels a great relief as well. All the pain and fear and doubt has departed. She will miss Vijari every day, but she will be comforted knowing that he basks in the Sands Behind the Stars free of all cares.

Ka'ishka never thought about it. While Vijari was sick her only cares were seeing to his needs and cherishing the time we had left. Now that she only has herself to be concerned about, she is lost. This one isn't even certain what her own needs are.

After everything she's seen? No. She could have stayed in their home and lived a quiet life here if Vijari had passed peacefully, without the darkness trying to steal him away. What Namiira did to Dak'radhi, and so many others? It's horrifying.

That's not what she means. Thinking about what nearly happened to her love fills her heart with anger. Outrage. A desire to make sure no one else must endure such a thing.\n\nKa'ishka understands now why her sister chose such a dangerous path.

This one is fortunate to have such a good sister. And to meet such good strangers. But we are strangers no more, so Ka'ishka hopes she will see you again, no matter which way her path takes her.\n\nFarewell, friend.
This one has seen the strength you and Adara'hai have. You helped Ka'ishka find her own courage to stand against the darkness. She has the strength now. She only needs to know how to use it.

Glad? That a creature as magnificent as Kaalgrontiid had to be destroyed? No, mask-bearer. I am disappointed that it came to that. That Kaalgrontiid forced us to intercede. He was dangerous, so we ended the danger.\n\nAnd now I must take my leave.

Wherever my wings will take me, mask-bearer. I must bide my time and wait for the next event that requires my intervention. It was good to see that we could work together, mortal. I will remember that.\n\nAnd now, farewell.

I was getting to that. At Icereach, I picked up a couple of the medallions the witches were wearing. For further study by the Skald-King's wizards.\n\nThe wizards determined that magic was infused into the jewelry, but not its purpose.
I was led to a similar site. Damn witches! Whatever game the Icereach Coven is playing at, we need to put an end to it. Preferably with multiple swings of my axe.\n\nLet me see the note you found.

Hmm. That's no help. Luckily, Jorunn's scouts provided a few locations of interest with their last report. Let me mark them on your map.\n\nWhen you reach each location, use the medallion and see where the magic leads. I'll catch up with you shortly.

You mean other than hounding my father and serving as go-between for the Jarl of Morthal and the Magister of Karthald?\n\nI wrangled promises out of my father and showed our allies that someone in Solitude still cares.

Indeed, and our foes seemed to thwart us at every turn.\n\nLaatvulon killed Yahgrondu before he could join our alliance, and his corpse was turned against us. The cult destroyed Pridehome in their efforts to acquire the Mask of Alkosh.

You have certainly proved yourself worthy of the Mask of Alkosh.\n\nJust do not expect it to ensure all your victories. Its power was only awakened through our connection. With my departure, it shall be but a mask.

Though it was no easy task to do so. The Halls of the Highmane presents challenges that few dare to face. Yet you conquered them all and proved worthy of Alkosh's divine power.\n\nA feat few mortals can claim.

These notes prove my theory. Netherroot is the key component of the harrowstorm ritual. It's like a poison for the soul. Weakens the bonds to the body so it can be pulled free.\n\nThey're harvesting life energy from anyone caught in the storms!

I'm guessing, but it may have something to do with those stone husks we saw. Remember how the werewolf emerged from one?\n\nAnd look at the mixture you retrieved. It isn't like the residue we recovered from the witch pike. It's more concentrated.

That mark on the northwest coast, that's an Icereach Coven camp. The communique mentioned needing more medallions. Odds are they come from there.\n\nAnd here, a midland camp between Dragon Bridge and Morthal. It's a staging ground for the harrowstorms.

More than likely. Those two locations should provide what Fenn needs to finish his elixir. We can't bet everything on that, though.\n\nThe communique mentions a warlords' camp in Blackreach. Maybe we can learn more about their ultimate plan there.
It takes two wills to awaken the mask. One is a champion of the Pride of Alkosh, a warrior who has proven themselves worthy of the mask's power. \n\nThe other must be one of my kind. A Dragon.

Fenjuntiid. The will of my father, the Dragon King of Time. All dov seek dominion, and so it is a king's command that is our bane.\n\nI will not turn away from you as I did Ja'darri. I will not repeat the past.

We don't have a lot of solid details, just what we've pieced together from the Gray Host's notes and communique, but I'll answer your questions the best I can.\n\nWhich camp did you want to ask about?

The Gray Host isn't just hiding in Blackreach now. They're mounting an invasion, and this appears to be their primary staging ground.\n\nI expect they're stockpiling witch pikes, gray reliquaries, and other supplies here, including the refined brew.
There's more to figuring out this magic than just watching from afar. I need to know exactly how they go about creating them.\n\nWith your help, we can learn everything about that here in this camp.

It's a landing site for the boats coming from the island of Icereach. Plus, they're collecting something here that goes into the process of creating the medallions. \n\nIf you can get me to the center of the camp, I can learn what that is.

Because the Gray Host is guarding something down there. I couldn't get close, but it appeared that they built the camp to surround something.\n\nPlus, I heard a few of the witches talking. Complaining, really. About needing to prepare more medallions.

She was a warrior without equal.\n\nWhen Laatvulon first came to these lands, many tried to defeat him. But only Ja'darri was wise enough to seek my aid. Brave enough to face my might. Worthy enough to be gifted my horn.

I feel it out there. A malevolence that stretches across this land like thick fog. A power that dwarfs even Laatvulon's.\n\nI believe it to be one of my kind. A Dragon of great strength and greater hunger.

A bloodfiend? You don't usually run into them in this part of the world. Let me see the note.\n\nThere's that word again. "Lucrative." And what's that about a simple ritual? Sounds like coven activity to me. Anything else to report?

I don't like the look of that. It feels … wrong. The Skald-King's mages will want to examine it.\n\nIn the meantime, we need to figure out what the coven is up to. How do rituals, vampires, and bloodfiends figure into their plan?

Just one. A note from a merchant named Goharth Ironbelly. Found it on these vampires. Ironbelly is apparently supplying something the coven requires, but the note doesn't go into details.\n\nSays we can find him at a Riften inn. The Withered Tree.
She was my father's chosen, was she not? To earn Alkosh's favor is no small task. And so it is only fitting that I show her a similar respect.\n\nBut enough of Ja'darri. Let us discuss another topic.

She was kind, immeasurably so. I suspect she had overcome a great sorrow, for she had a way of finding the light in the darkest of times. The good in the cruelest of souls.\n\nAnd she was strong, in body and heart. Strong enough to brave anything.
All dov seek dominance. For some, that desire is too great to control. An all consuming hunger to rule over all.\n\nI sense this now. A Dragon who will not rest until he gains absolute power.

We'll continue to protect Senchal and its citizens, of course. Try our best to keep order.\n\nBut I do have plans beyond that. One day, the Shields of Senchal will protect all of Pellitine. No more hiding behind city walls.

As much as I would like to keep my daughter by my side, I don't think that would be wise. She's grown so much during her time with the Dragonguard. Her place is here.\n\nI couldn't be prouder of the woman she has become.

Ha! You mean to ask if his business stays above board? This is Pellitine, walker. Every hand is dirty.\n\nDo not fear. Sormund makes his gold smuggling. No slaving or piracy. Daini had her fill of violence and evil here in South Guard.
The Hidden Moon still live?

Ah. Then you know how their temple fell to ruin and their order wiped out? The dro-m'Athra are insidious. Their very presence is enough to bring out Khajiit's inner darkness. To save one imperils many. The risk is too great.\n\nWe can only banish them.

It is like this one's father always said: you can take the cat out of the alley, but you cannot take the alley out of the cat.\n\nSkirting the law is all this one knows. But you have Daini's word, she may break the law, but she will never do harm.

Just mill about and try not to draw attention to yourself. Honestly, I'm more comfortable with the direct approach, but we need to play this carefully.\n\nThen, when he leaves, he can lead us directly to the coven.

Sometimes I have a little too much to drink when I'm enjoying a night out and I get picked up by someone who thinks passing out in their lap after rubbing against their legs is so cute. I get it. I'd want to take me home too, but I'm not some stray.

Ew. No. Usually I wake up on a pillow in someone's room and have to explain that I'm not going to be their pet. Sometimes I have to claw my way out of a window, but that is preferable to the talk.\n\nSo, can I go home now?

Four of our crew were taken from the ship in the night by some kind of … beast. All fur and fangs. It hit us after dark, so none of us got a good look.\n\nThe captain and first mate went to look for them earlier this morning and never returned.

It's an exciting time in the Bards College. We'll discuss the instruments, schedule times to take them down from their stands and cases to play for special events.

Some Maestros are even considering teaching lessons about them!

My thanks to you.
You followed Ironbelly, I followed you.\n\nCome on, let's find that slimy merchant and see what he's doing down here.

Thieves and murderers aren't the only scum that inhabit the Ratway. The local jarl keeps sealing the entrances, but it never stays closed for long. It would make a perfect lair for the coven.\n\nWatch your step and try not to blunder into any traps.

Our precise location? I can only speculate. Somewhere in Western Skyrim, I suppose. I was involved in my own investigation when the Icereach Coven witch attacked.\n\nWe can escape, but I desperately need your help first.

Captain Mavvok and I left the Cormorant together, tracking a monstrous beast. It was pulling a cart stacked with corpses … and some of our crew, I fear.\n\nOnce we got close, we realized it wasn't some horrifying monster. Just a Khajiit. A big one.

The witches must have stashed my belongings nearby. Among them is a small flask.\n\nI can open the cell door. Once I do, I need you to retrieve that flask for me. I'll be too weak. And until I have it, you're in significant danger.
I swear I intend you no harm. If I don't get that flask back, however, my intentions won't matter.\n\nRetrieve it and we'll break out of here together.

I belong to House Ravenwatch, one of the noble houses of Rivenspire. We adhere to the teachings of our founder, Count Verandis Ravenwatch.\n\nWe take no blood by force, we help those in need, and we curtail the actions of more hostile vampires.

Of course. Compare notes and look for commonalities. You have the makings of a fine scholar, my friend. Now, let's see ….\n\nI noticed there were a mix of different races buried here. They weren't all Nords. Anything strike you about the departed?

Obviously, the bodies are already gone. All that remains are the headstones. Maybe they'll provide a clue as to why those particular corpses were exhumed.\n\nAnd maybe that will tell me something about the process used to create the medallions.

Sort of. I regained enough of my senses when they carried me in here to remember the way out. It's pretty straightforward. I'll guide the way if you defend us from anyone who blocks our path.\n\nIf we work together, I'm certain we can escape.

We go where we're needed. I was investigating a burial site in Bangkorai when I discovered smugglers stealing ancient remains. I followed the trail, ran into the witch, and … well, you know the rest.\n\nNow we need to get out of here.
No, that's not right. Every headstone displayed a different name.\n\nThere must be something else the exhumed bodies had in common.
Hmm. Not true. The inscriptions mentioned wives, brothers, sisters, and sons. \n\nThere must be something else the exhumed bodies had in common.
Which headstones did you examine? I read about laborers, soldiers, and traders. Not the same occupations at all.\n\nThere must be something else the exhumed bodies had in common.
Really? What was that?
I don't think that's it. Some died from wounds, others sickness. Still others died of old age.\n\nThere must be some other characteristic the exhumed bodies shared.

Of course! Why didn't I see that? The headstones on the exhumed graves all mentioned that the person was old when they died. Let me think …. \n\nSome necrotic spells require the remains of the elderly. Something to do with the natural decay of life.
They did? Tell me more.

We came down here to find out what the Gray Host has planned, but Fenn still needs information about how the medallions are created and a sample of the refined netherroot brew.\n\nHelp Fenn and Lyris at the other camps, then meet me in Solitude.
Damn! That must have been one of the Icereach Coven witches!\n\nAny idea where she may have gone?

Hmm. Weary? Troubled, certainly. Consumed by some secret resentment.\n\nI approach to get a better look at him. His hand drifts to a stop. Without even thinking about it, I hold out my mother's necklace. Urging him to take it, I suppose.

It's just as we thought. The Gray Host is using this camp as a supply depot for their raids across the countryside. \n\nI saw stacks of witch pikes, rows of reliquaries, and jars of what I assume is the refined netherroot brew.

Only at the end.\n\nShe drifted in and out during her final days. In one of her last lucid moments, she placed the necklace in my hand and whispered, "forgive." I thought she was asking for my forgiveness. Now, I'm not so sure.
Right. And I heard the camp leader, a nasty creature named Sable-Eye, tell his troops to make sure to use the new supply that just arrived from Blackreach.\n\nLet's go grab a jar or two.

Can you believe it? I was trapped there for a month before I slipped into a delivery and got shipped out with a pile of musty coach cushions.\n\nThat old bag was crazy. Talking to us like we were her babies. The cream and cookies were good though.
I'm not sure of anything. If I don't do this, though, I'll never forgive myself if something terrible befalls the kingdom.

Granny garbage, or something. I'd prefer to forget.\n\nI thought I'd wind up stuffed and on her mantel with her other precious darlings. Better that than the ones still in the basement. Half of them were just zombies stuffing parcels day and night.

I do not! I'm just too beautiful for my own good. And where do people get off picking me up and dragging me off wherever they want? That's abduction any way you look at it. That's who you should be frowning at!

Mother had a way with father, but she could be just as stubborn. If she wanted something done and he wouldn't oblige, she'd do it herself.\n\nTime to take her lessons to heart, I guess. If my father won't take a stand, then I suppose it's up to me.

After all this trouble, Fenn better be able to use it to make his elixir.\n\nI'll take the jar of refined netherroot brew to Solitude. We'll meet up in Svana's chambers when everyone gets back from their missions. I hope they're all right.

In addition to the refined netherroot brew, Fenn needs information on the Icereach Coven medallions. Plus, we're hoping to learn more about the big storm the Gray Host has planned.\n\nHelp Fenn and Svana at the other camps, then meet me in Solitude.

That's all I've been doing. And trying to get these afflicted people to leave this place. The harrowed … the storm robs them of their will … their minds.\n\nI wasn't able to slip deeper into the camp, though.

Agreed. There appear to be a number of Gray Host warlords in the camp, so discovering their plans should be possible.\n\nWe need to be careful, though. I don't want us to wind up like the harrowed, serving as food for these bastards.

Tried to. The thing tossed me like a ragdoll and knocked the captain out cold. Threw him on the cart and hauled him straight into the blizzard.\n\nI'm too weak to fight, but I can still accompany you to find my people. I saw which way the beast went.
You saw what happened at Kilkreath and Karthwatch. Whatever they have planned for Solitude, it sounds a whole lot worse.\n\nI wish we knew more about this Rada al-Saran and what drives him.

What we heard around the camp is all well and good, but my father won't be able to deny written proof. Plus, there may be more details to uncover in the actual orders.\n\nLet's check the tents and find one of those messages.

The Gray Host uses an unstable mix of alchemy and sorcery to create the harrowstorms. An arcane ritual and the netherroot brew focus the power of each harrowstorm through the prepared witch pikes.\n\nIngenious, but fully exploitable.

Yes, these will do nicely. Fresh. Intact. Thrumming with magic. This shall make the ritual easy.\n\nHmm, they have an icy burn to the touch. Hope they weren't too much trouble. Perhaps those walking corpses willingly gave up their skin? Heh!

A holy ointment associated with a god that became popular due to Imperial influence. It's used by the priests in the Hall of the Dead to provide protection against necromancy and the undead.\n\nWe need that oil to create our elixir.

Sacred oil? Strange. That's the second time today someone has come seeking Arkay's anointing balm.\n\nSwordthane Uthlet arrived with an edict from the king. Demanded our entire supply! How we're to consecrate the dead without it, I have no idea.

The swordthane wouldn't say. He just mentioned that the high king needed it to defend Solitude.\n\nI'm sorry. I can't comply with the princess's request. Things are hard enough that these refugees must take shelter here among the dead.

Solitude's foundation began with the construction of Castle Dour. It's the oldest structure in the city and the most defensible.\n\nI tried to move the refugees there for safekeeping, but my request was denied. The high king has other plans, I suppose.

My orders from the high king were clear. Stockpile the entire supply of sacred oil in the Temple of the Divines, here within the confines of Castle Dour.\n\nWhat in Shor's name does the princess need with holy oil, anyway?

That locket should guide you to other totems bound to the same spell. You must destroy those corrupted totems. They bind our souls to the failed warding ritual.\n\nOnce they're destroyed, return to me with the locket. Then I can mend what's broken.

You will think less of me for having used it.\n\nThe ritual binds souls, much like a soul gem. Unlike a soul gem, it also binds flesh. So long as the focus of the ritual remains intact, the bodies and souls of those touched by the spell remain as well.

Protection? Truly? The harrowed already outnumber my soldiers, and more arrive every day.\n\nStill, giving you the oil would violate the high king's edict. I suppose if I happen to look the other way for a moment, I won't notice if a flask disappears.

You saw those creatures in the field! If I leave they'll make me like them. I have all I need in here to hold out until they are gone.\n\nBesides, I'm not ready to see who's waiting for me out there again.

Spells that affect the soul always carry risk.\n\nMy love—. My partner, Honoria, seemed certain that the locket would serve as a potent focus. I gave it to her, you see. It belonged to my mother, and her mother, and so on.

It carries … emotional potency. The warding ritual relies upon strong bonds. Bonds between people.\n\nOur fondness for one another and our shared relationship with the locket made it the perfect focus. But then, she left.
Not immediately.\n\nOne by one, they fell to the flu. The spell proved too weak to protect their flesh, but too strong to let it pass. Now their souls and corpses remain. Tortured.

Yes. A totem of comparable value.\n\nI tried to use items precious to her. Things she'd abandoned. But none of the items carried the necklace's weight. The bonds proved too weak. Each time I cast the ritual, the curse grew more severe.

She had doubts, certainly. We all did. But at a certain point, it seems she lost faith in the ritual completely.\n\nI was furious. At first. I even called for her to be arrested on charges of desertion. Or would have, had I sent that letter.
No great surprise there. That was the longest, most agonizing night of my life.\n\nI never sent the letter, though. I didn't have the heart to.

The warding spell makes them nearly impossible to break through conventional means—but the presence of the locket will make the spell unstable.\n\nHold the necklace near the totem and it should collapse into arcane vapor.

I saw the spirit of … someone we thought disappeared years ago. The Jarl and Lady's daughter, Freiwen. They never talk about it. Too painful, I suppose. I guess she died if that's her ghost who brought these cursed wolves on us.

Potions mostly. Breaks down a lot of ingredients so you digest them easier. And less risk of choking on a hunk of Namira's Rot in the middle of a battle. \n\nMakes a good grease too I've found. And you can waterproof a hull with it. All sorts of uses.
This is spellcraft, not mathematics. Should is the best a battlemage can offer in terms of assurances.

When they're not eating Dragonguard. They'll eat anything they can get a good meal out of and horses are plentiful enough.\n\nI won't ask you to collect what's left of their dinner from the other end. Never actually seen Dragon dung, come to think.
More slobber the better, but even if they've dried I can use them so long as there's a good bit of residue clinging to the bones. If there's a crusty beige film on it, it's good enough.
Hah, if that makes you squeamish don't ask your local alchemist what they're putting in your vitality potions.\n\nWhen you see how good my potions are you'll be begging to gargle with the stuff.

We can't wait for the next harrowstorm to strike, but what you and Svana learned in Blackreach might help.\n\nYou heard that Exarch Ulfra was testing harrowstorm rituals in a place called the Undergrove. We'll go there and let Lyris drink the elixir.

During my explorations of Blackreach, I came across an ancient burial site. A place called the Midnight Barrow. This Undergrove must be inside those ruins.\n\nOnce there, you and Svana keep watch from a safe distance while Lyris steps into the storm.

My grandmother on my father's side more generations ago than I can count was a hero of the Dragon War and my kin have been beating that drum ever since. Every Nord in my family gets our proud Dragon hunting heritage drilled into us from birth.

I just did. If you were expecting to learn some fancy way to lop a Dragon's head off in one swing, it won't be from me. Even if I remembered any of it, the ghosts of half my family would come to skin me if I spilled all our family secrets.

I wasn't, until the damn beasts started terrorizing the cats down south. I'm no warrior, never will be, but I figure I might as well do my part and put some of what I know to good use. It's probably not what my ancestors had in mind, but it'll do.

Flesh always proves sluggish and stubborn. These corpses may wander these halls for a while longer. But I assure you, their souls are free of the curse, and will find their way to Aetherius very soon.

And that spell became a curse—the curse that's afflicted the academy these twenty years. Of course.\n\nBut I don't understand. Why would mother leave this man in his hour of need? The woman I knew would never abandon a friend.

No, I still live. For now. The curse I carry will kill me soon enough.\n\nI only hoped to die close to home. I didn't want to destroy any more lives. Or watch memories from my life resurrected to taunt me.

Its power grows as it feeds off my life energy. The curse ends once I am gone.\n\nI only wish I could say goodbye to my parents. I know it is not my place to ask favors, but could you bring my mother a message? Tell her … I'm sorry. For everything.

Never better. We need to create as much of the elixir as possible and distribute it throughout Solitude before Rada al-Saran's massive harrowstorm hits. I also want to find out who in the city is helping him.\n\nLet's meet back at the Blue Palace.

We are speaking of Abah's Landing, you know? Of the company we keep who would you entrust all your business to? Zeira, I bet. Maybe Quen? Well, when it comes to run-of-the-mill business there's really only one answer: Silver-Claw.
He's not the salesman I am, but he knows enough about flattery to thin out my stock while I'm away.\n\nThough, I wouldn't mind you checking up on him next time you're in Abah's Landing.
I think so. I could feel my skin freeze over. For a brief moment I thought the end was upon me. All I wanted was for Freiwen to know she wasn't alone.

Abnur Tharn. According to his letter, the two of you worked together again after the Prophet incident. He even praised you. I know, it surprised me, too.\n\nThe old snake also said he's bringing a friend. That we have important business to discuss.

I know as much as you do. He just mentioned a threat to Southern Elsweyr. Between Tharn's cryptic letter and Nahfahlaar's strange mood, I'm feeling uneasy myself.\n\nTalk to the Dragon. Find out what troubles him while I wait for Tharn.

I beginning to sense that. We've been corresponding. I told him about Nahfahlaar and the Dragonguard. \n\nWhile he still punctuates every sentence with an insult, he seems genuinely concerned. That's different from the man we once adventured with.

Oh, this is Whiskey! Isn't she adorable?\n\nWe've become fast friends. I pet her, and she eats my bread. It's a wonderful friendship. I'll miss my first pet, Dapper, until the day I die. But she'd want me to feel joy again, I just know it.

My rat. Her name is … was Dapper. She was my best friend.

I knew this was a cursed voyage. The cold got her. That, and the terrible hunger. 

Damn this frozen ground! I'll keep her with me. See that she gets a proper burial.

I expected answers. Ironbelly sent people here for a reason. They have to be someplace. If we don't pick up the coven's trail, I'm not sure we'll find them again in time to stop whatever the witches have planned.\n\nLet's take a look around.

We're not Daedra worshipers. Our blood's hot enough to boil a blizzard and we've got more pressing concerns than some northern squall. \n\nWe received Svargrim's orders, promptly ignored them, and immediately ran afoul of a gaggle of Reachmen.

Anything that points to what the witches are up to. We need to determine the full extent of the threat.\n\nLet's explore the inn and look for any clues as to what happened to the people they lured here. With luck, that may lead us to the coven.

The high king sent a royal decree! Said to leave any strange objects or fetishes we spotted around the hold alone. They were dangerous, he said! Just so happens we found a few. I had my soldiers destroy them.\n\nThat's when we encountered the Reachmen.

They were tall, ugly things, covered in strange runes, fetishes, and a poultice that smelled like rotting fungus. They had been set up around the town. My soldiers assumed they'd find one at the barrow, but instead they sent word of the Reachmen.

Really? Last I heard, the princess was more interested in … no, I won't indulge in idle gossip.\n\nSvana carries herself well. Not with the grace of her mother, but she has the swagger of a warrior. I wish I could say the same about my daughter.

Her wounds are fresh. Adara'hai does not yet know what scars she will carry, but Ka'ishka is strong in spirit. Perhaps too strong.\n\nShe has pushed this one to take her to the Twilight Cantors. She aspires to join them.

Blackreach, the world below Skyrim.\n\nEvery Nord child hears the stories. How another world stretches beneath the Nine Holds. Each story is slightly different. Some talk about Dwarven cities. Others about terrible monsters or fabulous treasure.

What else could it be?\n\nWhatever it is, it's a perfect hiding place for the Icereach Coven. We need to get down there and find the witches. We must put a stop to whatever evil the coven is planning.

The poor man is frightened out of his mind. I'll escort him back through the tunnel to the Grinning Horker.\n\nMeanwhile, get down there and see what you can find out. If you see any witch pikes, destroy them. I'll catch up with you shortly.

Our dead will be missed dearly. We'll make sure they have a proper funeral after all is said and done.\n\nThis crew is family. We mourn together, but we endure together too. You've given us the luxury to do both.

It's … complicated. Adara'hai took comfort in Ka'ishka's quiet life. This one faces the horrors she does so that Khajiit can have that sort of peace. Ka'ishka has been robbed of that, but Adara'hai hoped she would find it again.
She will be happy you thought of her. Enjoy your accolades, walker. You deserve all of them.

Only if her sister sees this as a path to vengeance. A Twilight Cantor cannot carry hatred in their heart.\n\nBut that is unlikely. After seeing the love Ka'ishka and Vijari shared, this one is certain that here is no room for darkness in her sister.

I saw the witches put some poor sods into a circle surrounded by evil-looking pikes. They chanted and called forth a strange, black storm. It killed some, but turned most of the people into those harrowfiends.\n\nThat's what Sister Balra called them.

There's a Dwarven ruin west of here. Sister Balra has been using that as her personal domain. If she's around, that's where you'll find her.\n\nDamn it, I should have known. That flier was too good to be true.

I needed work. A lucrative opportunity was too good to pass up. It seemed strange when they marched us into the basement. We tried to fight, but there were too many of them. Hrolt got away though, I think.\n\nI just hope he made it to safety.

The servants of the ancient Dragon priests, awakened from death by magic or a curse or some such. They're known to haunt barrows and sometimes appear in the Halls of the Dead.\n\nThey're tougher and smarter than typical zombies, so be on your guard.
Two things I wholeheartedly approve of. I carved a path through a number of witches and vampires, myself. Shor's bones, there are a lot of these bastards!\n\nAnything else to report?

This is it. This must be what the Skald-King is worried about. A ritual that produces … harrowstorms? Magic that turns people into a new kind of bloodfiend. A harrowfiend.\n\nI wish I knew whose head I had to remove to stop this.
Sister Balra? The same witch that killed the merchant back in Riften? I'd definitely like to get my hands on that one.\n\nLet's go.
I … I know. It's just … look, we were never close. Not really. But he's my father … my king.\n\nWhat about you? Could you do it? Could you confront and maybe even kill one of your parents?
Such confidence … as sharp and as cold as my dagger's blade.\n\nLives hang in the balance, but I'm conflicted about committing … patricide.

I find that surprising. I thought you adventuring types were decisive and willing to do whatever was required to succeed.\n\nI … I need to think about this. Let's stop the harrowstorm. Then I can decide about my father.
An honest answer … and so much like my own.\n\nBut does my indecision put the people I'm sworn to protect in even more jeopardy? I need to think about that.
I'm going to do whatever I can to stop the harrowstorm and save Solitude and its people.\n\nAfter that, we decide what needs to be done about Svargrim.

It must be right beneath our feet, or close to it. From what we've seen, the witch pikes need to be in close proximity to the locations where the harrowstorms strike.\n\nOf course, finding our way underground … it won't be easy.

The Reach witch, Sister Balra. We had a deal, but she gutted me.\n\nListen, forget about me. I made a terrible mistake. I told her how to sneak into the Palace of Kings. Now I think the Skald-King is in danger.
Balra said she had something planned for High King Jorunn … said I was a loose end.\n\nPlease! I think she means to kill the Skald-King! You must save him. I never meant … to endanger Skyrim.

One step at a time. First we make our way down into Blackreach. Then we find the ritual site. It must be right beneath the city. We smash witch pikes and kill as many Gray Host bastards as possible.\n\nAfter that, we pray to Kyne and hope for the best.

I thought you knew me better than that. Taking on the impossible challenge, beating the unbeatable foe … this is what I'm good at.\n\nSo, yes, I do have to do this. And we're going to win. We have to.
Svargrim. To cast his lot with the Gray Host, become a vampire. Threaten his own people with a harrowstorm … it's madness!\n\nOne thing's for certain. We have to stop him.
A death-bed confession? That tells me the sentry believed he put the Skald-King in danger. I can't take a chance when it comes to Jorunn's safety.\n\nBack to the wagon. We leave for Windhelm at once!
Am I looking forward to going back to where Tzinghalis experimented on me? Not even remotely. But I want to see this through to the end.\n\nI … I need to.

The Gray Host can't summon the harrowstorm without performing their ritual. And we know that requires witch pikes, so there's that.\n\nPlus the usual assortment of coven witches, vampires, and werewolves, I suppose. Nothing we can't handle, right?
You're absolutely right. Especially after we found evidence of undermining down there. All I can say is that we were focused on other things.\n\nLet's go and save the city now, all right?

Is this what would have happened to all of us if I hadn't gotten the others into the cave? I tried to heal Eivina, but Meridia's light had no effect.\n\nBut what was that about Priest Direnna and the stables?

Is like poor Eivina.\n\nWe must find High Priest Varkour. If anyone is powerful enough to cure this unnatural ailment, it will be her. Meridia willing, we'll find the high priest and everyone else safe in the temple.
Whatever you and the half-giant think you found is irrelevant. The Skald-King is safe inside the Palace of Kings. It's the most secure structure in all of Skyrim!

How highly irregular, but if this is true ….\n\nKing Jorunn wanted to tour the lower levels. To check on the progress of the construction. He could be anywhere. Go inside and find him at once! I'll rally the guards and secure the palace. Now hurry!
Hmm. Well, it's true that Sentry Darfal never arrived for his shift today. And High King Jorunn is touring the palace, but that's supposed to be a secret.\n\nThe Icereach Coven, you say?

The storm? I hadn't thought of that. Terrible things started happening after it began, though.\n\nThis may be heresy to say, but Meridia has abandoned us. She doesn't care what happens to this place. I'm going to stay here until the danger's past.

Signs? Do you want to know if he announced his intentions before he turned into a ravenous beast? No. Nothing. One moment he was fine, the next he was a monster.\n\nThe high priest took the survivors and fled to the catacombs. You need to help them.
Yes, so Lyris mentioned. Harrowfiends, she called them. An ominous name. And that Sister Balra claimed she was turning me into a monster.\n\nWhat else did you learn about the Icereach Coven?
Vampires? I've known both decent and terrible folk burdened by that curse. I take it the ones working with the coven fall into the latter category.\n\nAnything else?

Haafingar? High-King Svargrim rules that hold from the city of Solitude. We don't see eye-to-eye, especially since neither of us will openly acknowledge the other's reign. Still, he should be warned.\n\nTalk to Lyris. I have much to think about.

There hasn't been a single ruler in over a hundred years. Jarl Svartr of Solitude refused to recognize Freydis as the legitimate heir. Ever since, the kingdom has been divided.\n\nDamn inconvenient at times like this.

Jorunn rules over Eastern Skyrim from Windhelm, while Svargrim lords over the western holds from his palace in Solitude.\n\nIf the Icereach Coven has targeted Western Skyrim, it will take both nations to stop them—if we can ever agree on anything.

We saw the last stand of what could have been a much larger attack on Morthal. The witch pike in the barrow was the only one that wasn't destroyed before they performed the ritual.\n\nSoldiers were caught in the harrowstorm, but the town was spared.

That's what happened in Kilkreath after the storm hit. I'm more curious about the witch, though. Why was that gray reliquary important enough for her to grab it and run off as soon as she spotted us?\n\nCome on, let's go talk to Jarl Reddharn.

A harrowstorm? Like the thing the princess was telling me about? The thing that destroyed Kilkreath? Gods! A pox on the Reach and its barbarian horde!\n\nWhat else? What about the Reachmen in the barrow?

Disappointing, but not unexpected. Reach witches are a tricky lot. Still, you have my thanks.\n\nIn the meantime, Hjaalmarch shall prepare for war. We may not have a defense against the harrowstorms, but we can be ready to attack once we have a target.

They say it was a storm. Powerful, devastating. It engulfed the entire town. It had to be a harrowstorm. That's the only explanation.\n\nThere could be other survivors. Maybe even Jarl Olfwenn. We need to make a search.

Not so fast. If we rush down as a group, they'll be on us like a snow bear on a horker. You go ahead. Try to cross the bridge to the main entrance. It's well guarded, but you're more than capable.\n\nOr you could try the alternative.

That's … a good question. I didn't see anything when I scouted the exterior, so the witch pikes must be somewhere inside the keep.\n\nI expect that once we find Svargrim and Rada al-Saran, we'll also find the ritual site.

The catacombs can be accessed from deeper within the temple. We just need to get the key from the chamberlain's sanctum.\n\nI think I know why the high priest went to the catacombs. It's not only a defensible location, it's where our relic is kept.

Meridia's Brilliance. It has the power to channel her light and purge the temple of this corruption. At least, I hope it does.\n\nHigh Priest Varkour wouldn't just hide in the catacombs. She must have a plan to save us.

When you told me, I didn't quite believe it. But seeing these people, it makes it all too real.\n\nThere could be other survivors out there. Maybe even Jarl Olfwenn. We need to make a search of the town.

Hmm, this might be something. I just need to skim through these assumptions and incantations ….\n\nWhat's this? Instructions on the placement of runes throughout Greymoor. All the way to … my gods … this entire tower … it's a witch pike!

The magic I sensed earlier. It was familiar because it's the same magic used in the harrowstorm rituals. Don't you see? This entire keep is the ritual site! They turned the tower into a witch pike. But at the scale … it's inconceivable!

The harrowstorms steal life energy and use it to pull the souls of the Gray Host out of Coldharbour and into the gray reliquaries. It's quite ingenious!\n\nHow they reincorporate though, it has something to do with those stone husks, I think.

Oh, most certainly! Perhaps even a way to reverse the effects of the harrowstorms and restore the harrowed. If the notes are complete, it would just require study, experimentation, and time.\n\nUnfortunately, we lack all three of those at the moment.

Such terrible things we witnessed today. An unnatural storm … vampires … innocent people turning into monsters … I fear this corruption cannot simply be prayed away.\n\nIt seems that Meridia has abandoned us to our fate. Why, I cannot say.

I'm Magister Fridelja. I serve Jarl Olfwenn as her court mage. I've been fending off witches, vampires, and these crazed villagers since the chaos started. \n\nThere was a storm. Definitely magical in nature. It turned our own people against us!

I … I'm not sure. I sent the jarl into the cellar when the storm began. When I still thought it was just a bad storm ….\n\nPlease. Go downstairs. Make sure the jarl is safe. Karthald will be lost without her.
Perfect! There are only two keys that I know of, and the high priest has the other one.\n\nNow open the door and let's find High Priest Varkour.
They've been taking them to the Temple of the Divines in Castle Dour. I suppose it's really the only place to care for them in their condition.

Jarl Reddharn gave him an earful the moment we entered the Blue Palace. Nord politics, it's a wonder to behold. One step removed from a barroom brawl. I'm disappointed they didn't start slugging each other, but it worked out in the end.

By Mauloch's nethers, what else would you call them?\n\nFelt like just a normal day of working the field. Then, a freak storm blows in! Heard whispers on the wind and saw a woman's ghost in the snow. That's when the beasts swarmed from nowhere.

My father's attempt to show that the high king isn't shirking his responsibilities. He's locked in his damn tower again, but his steward explained that the priests and healers have been commanded to do what they can for the poor souls.

Karthald's problems go deeper than the loss of their jarl. The main settlement was destroyed. I'm not sure the hold can recover from that.\n\nWhat happens next depends on the high king and the next moot. That's where such decisions are made.

I was a young fool. After the thousandth argument with my father, I ran away. There was a lot of drinking involved in the decision, as I recall.\n\nMaugh found me outside the city, led me back to the Lonely Troll, and we've been friends ever since.

What's to tell? He's my friend. For all his faults, he's always dealt straight with me. He is, in his own way, honest. He doesn't care that I'm royalty. In fact, I think he'd prefer it if I weren't.\n\nI needed someone like that for a while.

Well, not literally. His Tower of the Wolf has been under construction for as long as I can remember.\n\nHe won't let anyone inside except the builders until it's completely finished. Claims it would be bad luck to show it off early.

Some would say no. That the Tower of the Wolf is nothing more than a vanity project for the high king. My father says it's necessary for our ultimate security. A last line of defense against the Skald-King's forces.\n\nMe? I think it's an eye sore.

Well, that's a start.\n\nYou know, I never imagined I'd be working side-by-side with vampires, let alone ones I respect. With all the leeches we've already had to kill, it's nice to see another side. Fenn's … different. And so are you.

Isn't it everyone's?\n\nIn my experience, alcohol, in sufficient quantities, can solve any problem. Give me eight—no, ten—wagons of ale and I'll have this entire east-west rivalry business sorted in less than a day!

The letter that preceded your arrival said an attempt was made on the Skald-King's life. It indicated that High King Svargrim would be next. My husband took that as an accusation and a threat.\n\nHe will not meet with you, but I will hear you out.
Have you anything that would persuade my husband? It will take some substantial evidence to convince High King Svargrim to heed the words of the hated Jorunn the Skald-King.

Reachmen transgressions will not be enough for Svargrim to accept outside help. He's a prideful man and the bad blood between him and Jorunn runs deep.\n\nI will speak on your behalf, but you and Lyris will need to bring me proof he cannot ignore.

Damn. Lucky thing he found you. Brondold was supposed to get the lay of the land before I got here. Without his information, my work for Jorunn the Skald-King could be over before it begins.\n\nWhat did he give you? Hand it over.

Hmm. Smugglers and Reachmen up to illicit business. Nothing unusual there, but Brondold thought it could be connected to the coven.\n\nI'm short a good investigator and you stepped into the role easily enough. Can I count on you to help me with this?

That's certainly what Tzinghalis's notes imply. Despite how it looks, a plan is formulating in my mind. I think I can create an elixir, but I'll need more of this refined netherroot brew. And we need to solve the mystery of the coven medallions.
Don't know any Brondold. Don't know you. Either way, I got nothing to tell you.\n\nGet lost. I'm on a winning streak.

Dead? That's a new one. Nothing Kasalla usually moves through port is worth killing over. You didn't hear it from me, but she's the one picking up those shipments.\n\nHer warehouse is down on the docks. You want to know more, go ask her.

The key looks Dwarven to me. And the notes mention a Dwarven tower. They could be connected. The notes also indicate that Fenn was going to meet with someone named Edjar east of the Dusktown bridge.\n\nYou start there and I'll check with the locals.

Because he doesn't like Maugh. But I like Maugh. Maugh doesn't care that I'm a princess, and it doesn't matter to me that Maugh's a scoundrel.\n\nIf my father didn't send you, why are you threatening my friend?

His breeches fit well! And he was handsome. Not a Nord. Breton, maybe?\n\nI didn't really listen to what he was saying. A half-dozen workers left with him, off to the Druadach Mountains or someplace. He hasn't been back since.
Smelly bastards. Cheap, too. Wouldn't buy us a drink! They hung their fliers and left without saying a word.\n\nThen a different smelly bastard showed up to sign on workers. He was a charmer, though!

How does a man like me describe such evil? It looked like an infected wound in the sky. A mass of black and red swirling above my home. My friends' skin shriveled and turned gray as the storm … took something from them. That's when I ran.

I patrol the main road outside of town. Stopping travelers to ask their business, that sort of thing.\n\nA sound like the mountain cracking in half shook me and then the storm rose up. I hurried back and got to the edge of town when I saw the chaos.

That's what this was all about? You and the she-giant looking for work? You're too late, I'm afraid. The posting agent has come and gone, and with a handful of laborers in tow.\n\nThe fliers are still around, so perhaps he'll return.

We know where to find her and we more or less know what she's up to. And, if the two are connected, maybe the smuggler can help us narrow our search for the Breton.\n\nReady to visit Kasalla's warehouse?
The silk-shirt kept notes? Of course he did! And where is Fennorian? He's late and he still hasn't compensated me for the information I gave him. I need that key!
Fenrar is safe? Kyne's mercy, you bring great news. When he didn't show up here I feared that the storm killed him. Or the Reachmen took him like everyone else.

I hid. Reachmen are so brutal. I reacted without thinking. They took everyone I swore to protect while I did nothing.\n\nA Nord of Karth does not behave this way. My duty is to go after them, but I won't survive alone. Are you willing to join me?

Yeah. After the storm appeared, Bjora and I led some townsfolk into this barrow. How could I know that Reachmen were already in here?\n\nThey attacked us from behind. Bjora put up a beast of a fight, but no one resists a Reach horde alone.

You will? Looks like Fenrar sent the right person to chase after me.\n\nI hid when my people needed me. And I left Bjora, my oldest friend, to fight alone. If we find where the Reachmen took them, maybe bringing them home can make up for my failure.
They must have gone through the Grotto. Take the path to the right, you'll have to swim. There's an entrance tucked back behind the cavern.
I'll be fine, don't worry about me. I just need to stop the bleeding. \n\nGo on without me, please! Hurry!

I … thought this was long over. Years ago, we raided a Reach tribe camping too close to our territory. After the fight, I heard a child crying in one of the tents. I took pity and brought her home to raise as a Nord.\n\nBut, Bjora is of the Reach.

May Kyne bless your bravery. Once these two are safely away from here, I'll join you.\n\nBased on our past fights against Reachmen, my guess is the Warleader locked the tower up tight. You'll likely find a key near him. Good luck.

Like I said, Tzinghalis's helper made a mistake. Forgot to fasten my chains after one of my tortures. I slipped away, crawled along some pipes, and fell into a chamber with one of those Dwarven lifts.\n\nThere was also a door, the one behind me.
Priest Bavian? Where's High Priest Varkour? Did those horrible creatures get her?\n\nWe hid in the stables, but then Priest Direnna … changed. That's when I ran in here.

I never told her. Only those that were on that raid with me know the truth. We kept the secret so she could live without scorn. Bjora would never have friends like Hafskjar or join the town guard if others knew.

You can never bind a true Nord warrior for long. Besides, our captors were in a hurry to bring the others into the tower and failed to tie proper knots.\n\nI'm still glad you came, though. Your attack will give us cover to escape.

It'll get you close. There's a big door that leads into Tzinghalis's lair, but it's sealed. You need to figure out a Dwarven mechanism to open it.\n\nThen make your way to the experimentation chamber. That's probably where he's keeping Fennorian.
Those cube things? Maybe.\n\nIt does look like they can be turned. Maybe changing their positions will do something. It's as good an idea as any.
It's an old Reach bastion. Dedicated to some ancient ancestor or whatever. We drove Reachmen from here where the high king gave us Karthald Hold. I remember it was crawling with witches.
Shor's bones! If those witches harm her ….\n\nPast the bastion are some ancient stones. Witchmen used to practice blood sacrifices there before we ran them out. Maybe they took Bjora there.
A rebirth. Lady Meritha and her sisters pulled the caul from my eyes. I now know my truth. The holders of Karthwatch are not my true family. I belong to the Reach.

My sisters whisper prophecy to me from their stone circles of power. The Gray Host will rise and unite the Reach clans. Together, we will retake our home.\n\nI will lead them in this dark mission. I shall be made queen.

A true heir of Karth. Where you stand and all you see belong to my people. The Nords took it by force. Just as they stole me away after slaughtering my kin.\n\nThe witch sisters showed me a vision. Blood from Faolan, the Red Eagle, flows in my veins.
Reach witches spreading lies laced with dark magic. No doubt they enthralled Bjora so she'd betray her family.\n\nStranger, if you're willing, I need your weapon once more.
Once Bjora is free, we can join the others in safety. For Karthwatch!
We must hunt down the hags responsible and end their hex with blade and blood. Did she give you an idea of where to find them?

Hey, don't throw this back at me! I'm not some ungrateful knave who wants to see the kingdom go down in flames. I just don't want Svana to follow you to an early grave.\n\nYou keep pushing her. Why's it up to her to fix everything?
Oh, Maugh knows all about that. There's force and there's force.\n\nNo one thinks much of this old drunk, but I'm not the one who's going to get Svana killed. If she dies, I'll never forgive you.

All these secret societies love disguising themselves. It gives a sense of excitement to their lives of leisure. Fortunately, bards hear all sorts of secrets. Wearing this robe and mask will get you in the door.\n\nYou also need the right passphrase.

The magnates of the Sapphire Society speak a simple phrase to gain entry into their events. "A jewel of blue rules the view." Truly underscores how they see themselves, doesn't it?\n\nYou might want to practice it, just to be sure.

It's coming back to me, now. Just flashes. The Reachmen attacked. Three witches led them. They brought me here and … did something.\n\nI saw visions before me. Memories that weren't mine. An old Reach King called me his daughter.

The lute? Nice patina. Just a trifle I came across in one of my hunts. \n\nIt went on the block earlier. Too bad you weren't here then. There was only one buyer. A little bidding war would have warmed up the crowd.

Now I do wish you had been here! You are skirting the rules. No revealing identities of buyers. \n\nStill, if you had arrived on time, you would know that the buyer behaved like an obnoxious ass. We typically frown upon stumbling about from drink.
I … remember that's what I believed. It felt so true. But, I would never betray my family or the hold.\n\nKarthwatch! Oh gods, it is all gone. Is anyone else still alive?

Eyes in the dark. A steady, marching drum. I stood beside a strong man with haunting eyes. His stare chilled my soul. He placed a briar crown on my head and said I'd lead his armies.\n\nWhat do you think it means?

Certainly. The warriors of the Pyre Watch swear an oath to protect this burial site from those who would seek to enter it … and to prevent anything inside from leaving.\n\nBy Tu'whacca's mercy, nothing has ever tried to escape.

He did. But for what purpose? He told me his name is Fennorian, and that he comes in peace. Hmph. Mischief of the damned.\n\nWe must watch him carefully, wayfarer. Creatures like him cannot be trusted.

Precious little. There were many Nords among them, covered in crimson runes and wielding ghoulish magics.\n\nI heard one of them refer to the others as Draugrkin. An apt name for such ugly dead-summoners.

Ah, introductions. My name is Fennorian. I'm an arcane investigator. Of a sort.\n\nYou may have heard Shelaria's … forceful rebukes. Sorry about that. I promise, I only want to help. But I'm a vampire, you see. It sets some people ill at ease.

Shelaria refers to it by some obscure Redguard name, but foreign scholars like me call it the Unhallowed Grave. According to my research, it's a cavernous burial mound, dating back to the First Era.\n\nIt wasn't easy to find, I can tell you that.

Ugh. A depraved band of necromancers and cutthroats. Nords mostly. They deal in magical trinkets and relics—selling their discoveries to the highest bidder.\n\nThey're scoundrels, one and all, but I can't help but admire their diligence.

You have my word!\n\nI'll be honest. I've only been a vampire for a short time. Still wearing in the soles, so to speak. But the hunger is one thing I've taken great pains to master. I swear, I wouldn't harm a torchbug!

Instrument? Oh, that lute, yes. A mantel piece for my music room. Has a nice shine to it. I acquired it for a song. A song! I made a joke, see? Hah!\n\nWhy are you asking? Disappointed I bought it? Then too bad for you.

Buy it? I would never … wait, you just handed me how much? Well, in that case of course you can. \n\nTake this note and collect your treasure from my servant outside. Please do business with me again.
I had a lead on that … but Tzinghalis captured me before I could finish looking into that.\n\nI … I let Edjar down.

Then I also owe you for reconciling my debt to Edjar.\n\nExarch Tzinghalis was experimenting with werewolf blood, both to determine why it renders them immune to the harrowstorms and to use it to strengthen the ritual components.

Ah, Petraloop returns home! You know, I wooed my first love with this very lute? And my third, as well.\n\nThus begins the restoration of the College's famed collection to its former greatness. The history books will remember you for this.

I assembled the museum for just this moment, but I think you deserve the honor of placing Petraloop on its podium.\n\nAfter you display the lute, perhaps you could read Nel's Hidden Loves? I could use your skill in recovering the other instruments.

Yes indeed! Let the clues within Nel's Hidden Loves guide the way.\n\nAs you travel through Skyrim, keep your eyes open—and your ears, too. These are instruments we're pursuing, after all. If you find more of them, I'll be here.

To fully craft an elixir to defend against the harrowstorms, I still require a sample of refined netherroot brew. Plus, we need to determine what the Gray Host has planned.\n\nHelp Lyris and Svana at the other camps, then meet me at the Blue Palace.

I'm glad to hear it. That just leaves finding out what the Gray Host has planned. Go meet Svana at the camp in Blackreach.\n\nI can't say I envy you. While Blackreach provides some fascinating points of study, the dangers appear overwhelming.
Princess Svana is braver than I imagined.\n\nThat just leaves Lyris's attempt to acquire a sample of the refined netherroot brew from the midland camp. Head there and see if she needs any support.

In my experience, guessing is not a fruitful practice. But, you do my order a great service, so I will indulge you.\n\nEvery bone you see here belonged to a black-hearted creature of the night, but some beasts are more dangerous than others.

Despite this Elf Fennorian's unholy condition, he appears to be a very capable healer.\n\nMy wounds cause me less pain, but … to my great shame, I still cannot join you in battle. Wounded as I am, I would only get in the way. I am sorry.

Well, they have many necromancers among their ranks. Necromancers and bones go together like jam and bread.\n\nThen again, the Draugrkin usually sell their spoils to wealthy patrons. If that patron is a student of the Dark Practice ….
Blood and blade, everyone knows Lyris Titanborn!\n\nWhat a woman! She's even larger than I imagined. No wonder she fought swordmaster Sai Sahan to a draw! Wait—is he here, too?
Until Kasalla returns, I'd be happy to keep fair Lyris company in her stead.

Alas, Kasalla doesn't allow visitors when she isn't here to conduct business. But we can wait out here.\n\nDo you think Lyris would autograph my ancestral scabbard? It would mean so much to my son. When I have one. Do you know if Lyris is betrothed?
Really? I feel like I've picked up a thousand of them by now. \n\nHere you go. I've got plenty.

Oh, what a wonderful question! I won't bore you with the details, though they are fascinating! \n\nEssentially, these traps will magically weaken the spirit. Once it passes through the physical barrier, the warding spells render it unable to move!

Absolutely! My very first case with Claudina, we captured a very powerful ghost with such a trap. I'll never forget, it burst forth from the wardrobe and I nearly died of fright.\n\nThankfully, Claudina pushed me out of the way just in time.

Are you another one of that woman's assistants? Look, when I hired those two, they assured me that they had things well in hand.\n\nBut we've got another person missing, and my people are scrambling over themselves in their fear.
My town guard, Captain Ageran. He was last seen at the administrative offices, but then he didn't show up for his posting. \n\nHe just up and vanished. Same as the others.

Great work! You're a natural. Have you ever considered making this your life's work? It's really quite rewarding, and you certainly have the aptitude for it.\n\nAnyway, I'm sure Elle will be relieved to hear that they're all set up now.

Elle Bitterblade, the head of Dusktown. She hired us, though she's been understandably doubtful since her husband, Overseer Urlvar, kicked us out of the mines earlier.\n\nMaybe you could help smooth things over by telling her the traps are set up?

Well, remember what I said earlier about the traps? We had an incident with the mine foreman. But he wasn't in any danger! We freed his leg easily and got all the paint off.\n\nWe fixed the traps, but nonetheless, the mines are off limits to us now.

A plot against the high king? Involving plundered antiquities from Hammerfell? Preposterous! I'm simply facilitating a transaction between treasure hunters and a rich collector.\n\nSo, who am I paying the bribe to? You or the high king?

Give me that. Tribal crafts, my arse! I told that son of a skeever I don't deal in arcane goods. Especially ones from the Reach! Nothing but sorrow comes from such business.\n\nThis isn't cursed, is it?

No name, just instructions and gold. Shipments come in, I make sure no one looks too closely, and wait for a pick up. Never see the same face twice. Last time it was a smooth-talking Breton with Nord laborers in tow. You want more, I need assurances.

Without a doubt. The coven's attack on Jorunn involved a ritual. Why hire locals, though? Seems like an unnecessary risk. And how does the Breton figure in?\n\nI suppose using different people draws less attention … but something doesn't feel right.

No reason not to. Head there while I circle around from the other direction in case they're already on the move.\n\nJust be careful. I'd rather not lose another partner before we actually figure out what we're up against.

Not much. Frustrating, right?\n\nMy sister and I make it our business to know all the major players in vampire circles. Until a few weeks ago, we didn't even know this place existed, let alone who sat on the throne. Frankly, it's a little embarrassing.
Introductions! Sorry. Ugh … if my master could see this, he'd be aghast.\n\nGwendis of House Ravenwatch, at your service.

Haven't heard of us? Good.\n\nWe're the children of Count Verandis, lord of Ravenwatch Castle. He taught us to control our urges—to use our dark gifts to defend people rather than enslave them. Hardly common knowledge, though. So, mums the word, eh?
Hmph. I've been tortured before. I would have said anything to get out of it. Anything.\n\nThen again, he's our only lead. I guess we'll have to risk it.
Yeah, yeah. Just let me … ah. Got it. Look up.\n\nSee those chains connected to the cages? We need to find the mechanism that lifts and lowers them. Up on that balcony maybe?

Good. I'll keep watch down here, just in case any of Essenia's soldiers stroll through.\n\nIf you manage to open the cages, I'll grab our informant and meet you on your way back down. Just hurry. We're all undead, but he really looks the part.
Kilkreath? The temple to Meridia? Why would the Icereach Coven target a local Daedra cult?
Damn. We're running out of time.\n\nI'll head back to Solitude and try again to warn High King Svargrim. You go to Kilkreath Temple and alert Meridia's priests. I'll meet you there as soon as I can.

You'll be going up against the coven by yourself. Warn the priests. If there's an opportunity to safely stop or delay the ritual, by all means. But don't take any unnecessary chances. I still don't want to lose another partner.\n\nGood luck.

Let me see that. 

Hm, this is from Urlvar, the mine Overseer. Could it be mere coincidence that the town guard investigating the mystery of the miners just happens to be the next to go missing? I think not. 

There is something amiss here.
I have some idea. There's one just below, tucked away in the back of the town.\n\nPhebe may be … indisposed for the moment, so I'm counting on you to join me. Keep her whistle on you, we may need it.
I'm sorry, but you're too late. An unnatural storm struck the temple and now the entire area is overrun by vampires and harrowfiends.

Yes, I've run into the coven as well. The urns and the stolen remains play a part in a ritual to summon the storms.\n\nIf you're willing, I could use your assistance. I need to finish my investigation of the site to see what else I can learn.

Fine. If you want to be her next test subject, so be it.\n\nThe Blood Queen lured my clan here with promises of protection and glory. We were a small family. Just four of us in all. So, we came to Greymoor Keep expecting a warm welcome.

They cast us into those pens like dogs. Didn't take long before the tests started. They forced us to drink tinctures, endure injections. They slaughtered anyone who refused.\n\nOccasionally, Essenia would come down to select someone for further study.

House Ravenwatch? I've heard of them, but he's a long way from Rivenspire. Well, if you're willing to trust a vampire, I suppose I can, too.\n\nI spotted a coven witch. If we hurry, we might be able to catch her.

On the cliff overlooking the temple. Calls herself Sister Ambritt. I was going to rush her, but I wanted to make sure you hadn't run afoul of any of these monsters first. No offense, Fenn.\n\nCome on, if we're lucky the witch is still up there.

Whatever we encounter beyond these doors—bloodknights, Lady Essenia, even this Ashen Lord—I can handle that.\n\nBut if we find my sister, Adusa, and she's been transformed … I need you to do what's necessary. Because I won't be able to.

Not yet. Despite our ingenious detective work, right now it's still the Overseer's word against ours. And he's already given Elle reason to distrust us.\n\nWhat we need is definitive proof. Then she'll have to listen.

All this rubble scattered around didn't just come from these urns. The texture and patterns are different. They appear to have used the funerary dust in the urns to summon the harrowstorms, but I'm not sure what was inside the larger vessels.

Thank you, but no. I try to avoid large population centers. The temptation, you understand.\n\nI'll find someplace nearby but out of the way where I can set up my equipment and work undisturbed. I'll send word when I have something to report.

And explains what he was trying to protect his people from.\n\nIt is not enough to simply turn this evidence over to Elle. I was hired to help this town. Spirits or no, I have a responsibility. We must stop this horror.
We need to investigate the mines. There has to be a clue that will point us in the direction of that monster. Let's leave here. Dusktown needs us!

The vampire seemed as though he was threatening Overseer Urlvar at the end of their altercation. Perhaps he's planning some kind of retaliation. If so, there's a chance we could catch him in the act if we find him.
He's what? Dammit. Queen Gerhyld will be here at any moment.\n\nLook, her highness is expecting to talk to me and my contact. I need you to pretend to be that contact or this will go very badly.

Of course I am. Just thinking about what we saw in there.\n\nI always felt like I had a grip on what vampirism was, you know? But now the world's filling up with monsters I couldn't dream up in my worst nightmares. Verandis never prepared us for this.

You're right, of course. But this isn't over. Not by a long shot.\n\nI'm sorry—I'm babbling. Just tired, you know. I need rest. We'll probably be here for a while. You're welcome to shelter at our camp whenever you pass by.
I thought I'd pretty well summarized our predicament. Reachmen, pyres, exploding mountains. But, sure, I suppose I can humor you. It's not like it hurts to speak, or anything.
You sound like Fennorian.\n\nI am not leaving this grave until I watch Kjalnar breathe his last. If I die along the way, so be it. I will rest on the Far Shores with my kin, knowing I did my duty.

Uh … look up. It's hard to miss.\n\nLady Essenia, the Blood Queen, holds court inside. Or at least she did. Apparently, she bent the knee to some ancient vampire from the west. She's called on every vampire in Skyrim to join her here and do likewise.

That's what we thought. But the vampires who go into the Keep never come out. Adusa slipped in with a group of recruits to take a look around. That was days ago ….\n\nIt's been too long. I'm going in after her. I could use a hand, if you're willing.

Fine, yes. Uncomfortable, but fine. I've done a serviceable job of cleaning my wound. I should have no trouble getting to Solitude, at least. Barring any unfortunate encounters with rough-hewn furniture, I'll be fit to travel after a bit of rest.

There was a commotion at the palace. Everyone was headed that way, except one man. No—not a man. He wore an eye patch, but his face was bestial.\n\nHe dragged her along like a bone between a dog's teeth, then he tossed her aside. Pale as snow.
He was fast. So fast. Ran toward the Hall of the Dead.\n\nHe never even looked back at what he'd done ….

It was a monster … a vampire. I have seen such creatures before, but this one wore an eye patch. It moved like a shadow and took sustenance from these poor souls.\n\nI called upon Arkay's grace and the vampire fled before his sacred presence.
Toward the main gate.\n\nI pray the guard finished off the depraved creature before it took another innocent life.

A vampire? I don't know what you're talking about, but whoever it was tore out Sonolia's throat and fled through the gate before I could stop him.\n\nWhat do you know about all this and why is it any of your business?
The queen's … dead? What about the high king? He'll have my head for letting the assassin slip away.
Good question. The guards should have been able to handle a run-of-the-mill assassin. This could be connected to the Icereach Coven. In fact, I'd wager my axe that it is.

Look around. See if you can find any indication of how the assassin got in and out of the palace so easily. Maybe even turn up something that ties the murderer to the coven.\n\nI'll make sure the princess is all right.
Markarth mead. Hmm. Ena deals with the Reach from time to time, though usually indirectly.\n\nThe arrow, however. It worries me. Only Reachmen use Druadach snow owl feathers to fletch their arrows.

No, but Ena must have come through here. \n\nThis entire outlook is more or less her domain. Ena's got little outposts scattered everywhere up here. Look around and see if you can find any indication of where she went next.

The Reachmen come from the Reach, in the southwestern part of Skyrim. We've been at odds with those barbarians, off and on, for generations.\n\nWould they raid our caravan? Most certainly! But discovering their presence this far north is disturbing.

Reach witches? They pose no threat! We've beaten back those wild dogs time and time again while our brothers to the east bow down to a poetry-writing milk-drinker!\n\nI will not be lectured on such matters by the likes of you!

Tales told around campfires to scare the children! Storms happen here all the time, and none of them spawn monsters. The last spy who spoke of such things … well, he no longer speaks of such things.\n\nI am the Wolf of Solitude, I know my enemies.
You dishonor my wife's name by letting it pass through your treacherous lips? Away with you!\n\nAnd pray I don't find evidence that ties you to the queen's murder. That would not go so well for you.
Threat? What threat? And do you think this is why someone came into the palace and killed her?
And did you tell my father all this? Is he rallying the soldiers? Alerting the other holds?

My father sees Jorunn's plots everywhere, even in his spicy venison stew.\n\nWell, I won't let my mother's death be for nothing. She trusted you and so will I, my father be damned. Please. Find whoever did this and stop them.

They have Ulang. They would have killed him if I didn't cooperate!\n\nI told them about the smuggling tunnels. The ones that lead to the cavern beneath the bridge's foundations. They plan to use explosives to bring down the bridge.

The Reachmen leader, Vund, is an alchemist. He created a powerful alchemical reagent. He's going to ignite the reagent and collapse the cavern.\n\nHe's down there now, but there's still time. We need to warn Captain Hingrid!

Good. The bridge is a symbol of Western Skyrim. It serves as both a vital thoroughfare and a monument to our people. I really don't want to see it destroyed because of my mistake.\n\nFind Captain Hingrid. She'll know what to do. I'll be along shortly.

A grim talisman. It bears an enchantment of some kind, though the symbol upon it holds no significance that I'm aware of.\n\nI can help find the owner of this medallion, but I need some specific items to cast such a divination.

Bring me the bones of a wolf and a deathbell plant pulled up by its roots. I need the plant alive. The wolf, not so much.\n\nWith those reagents, I can conjure a divination that will lead you directly to the last person to wear this medallion.

Vampires do not obey the same laws as specters and ghosts. My tools will be useless against him … unless! \n\nPhebe's whistle! Do you still have it? It's designed to emit a tone that's unsavory to immortal creatures. Perhaps it will disturb him!
It's impossible to say without evidence. But it wasn't made specifically with spirits in mind, so there is a chance!\n\nGo on, try it! This is the only plan we've got!
I found the camp. Thought it was deserted, but the assassin must have been hiding in the shadows. He got the drop on me.
