I have a few contacts in the oddities market. One of the benefits of being an antiquarian who spends much of his time in the shadows. A flock of creepy Nords shipping ancient bones in bulk is sure to catch someone's attention.

Harrowstorm? Is that what you call what happened here? Why I didn't turn into a monster is a mys—wait!\n\nThe hold soldiers clashed with Reachmen scouts a few days ago. They brought back these medallions the scouts were wearing.

What choice do I have? So long as this place houses the remains of the Gray Host, it remains a threat to all of Tamriel.\n\nI do not suppose you'd be interested in a life of stewardship and seclusion? You would make a fine Pyre Watch sentinel.
Destroy the bridge? While we're standing right here? How do those Reach idiots expect to get that close?

Fennorian has changed my view of Fennorian.\n\nRemember, we are surrounded by the bones of monsters who sought the end of all life in Tamriel. Fennorian proved to be a steady ally, but he does not speak for all vampires. The Gray Host is proof of that.

Smuggler caves? Under my garrison? I'll deal with Ena later. Right now, we need to act fast. Maybe we can flush the bastards out before they do whatever it is they're planning.\n\nI think—wait, is that Ena?

It had more to do with your arrival than anything I did. Luckily, he left behind his belongings when he departed.\n\nI saw a map and some documents over there. Why don't you take a look while I deal with this wound?
It's not just the bridge that's in danger! The Reachmen intend to utilize the smuggler cave entrances to surround the town. They're going to attack the garrison!

Here, I'll mark the entrances on your map. Use the fire salts and kindlepitch at each location. Then find the main entrance to the smuggler caves behind the waterfall.\n\nSeal the side entrances, then go stop Vund. And save Ulang, too. I need him!
If the Reachmen can use explosives, so can we! Gather the kindlepitch and fire salts from the garrison barn. We can use that to make our own explosives and seal those entrances!

The clever woman helped you track the queen's assassin to his hideout in Chillwind Depths. He got away, but left behind evidence that the coven's planning another harrowstorm in this mine and we're going to wreck those plans.\n\nI miss anything?

I knew Ena wouldn't give up on me. What'd I ever do to deserve her?\n\nThese skinny weaklings are setting up explosives farther in the cave. I hurt my arm or else I'd help. I can make my way out of here by myself, but you have to stop them.

Let me see that.\n\nDonors? But I don't understand. You can't mean … Urlvar was feeding innocent miners to a vampire in order to keep everyone safe? How could this happen? How could I not have known? These were my people!
You're right. We would have been left to wonder and kept losing people were it not for you and those two over here.\n\nJust tell me one thing, did you kill the vampire responsible?

The fact that he realized he was in over his head doesn't excuse the abhorrent decision in the first place. This is sickening. \n\nWe both want to protect our people. But to think he'd resort to something so barbaric ….

Excellent. Hopefully after all this trouble, we can convince Solitude to make our lives a little easier. \n\nThank you for this, friend. Your actions likely saved the western holds. I promise you, your triumph will not go unsung.
No, but all the evidence you found suggests he's down here somewhere. Let's go see what the miners can tell us.\n\nBut be ready for anything. This place has ambush written all over it.
Just because no one saw him doesn't mean he wasn't here. Let's talk to Fenn before we start turning this place inside out. Maybe he's had better luck.
Right, skulking in the shadows. Lead the way. I'm right behind you.
With arcane phenomena, anything's possible. If we hurry, we can stop this harrowstorm before it causes any damage.\n\nYou and Lyris should split up. We need to destroy all of the witch pikes.
I'll track the queen's assassin and the coven witch, you focus on stopping the harrowstorm.\n\nI'll find you after that and we'll confront the vampire and the witch together.

Yeah, I heard. No idea who or what that is though.\n\nMaybe Fenn can make sense of what we saw down here. In the meantime, I'm going to head back inside. I want to get a better look at those stone husks that were left behind.

While Fenn and I examine that ritual site more closely, you should return to Solitude and inform Svana that her mother's assassin has been taken care of. She'd want to know.\n\nMore than that, she deserves to know.

I would have preferred to see him dragged back here for a proper trial and execution, but at least justice has been served.\n\nWere you able to determine who was behind the murder? Was it connected to the threat you came to warn my father about?

Damn those Reach witches! And damn my father for being so … so … obstinate!\n\nBut what does the coven want? Are they planning to kill my father? What else can you tell me about this threat to our kingdom?

I can't help but pity Hagridden, despite what he's put me through. I've felt his torment. An eternity in the Midnight Barrow seems cruel, even for a traitor. From what I saw, it seems like he was the one who was betrayed.\n\nWas he really innocent?
That was my feeling, but I didn't know if it was Hagridden affecting me.\n\nI wonder what became of the woman who betrayed him. Did she get what she desired from those peoples' sacrifice?

You're right. He was the jarl. He should have thrown that woman in chains at the mere suggestion of taking another person's life, let alone making some kind of sick sacrifice.\n\nInstead they all paid the price. Did she get her desire, I wonder?

Not officially … at least I don't think I am. I feel like the whole world's falling down around me. But the city still stands. That's something.\n\nI'm worried about Lyris and Fenn. The last we saw, they were holding off a horde of harrowfiends.

No thanks to Svargrim, damn his eyes! After you and the princess went off to Blackreach, I gathered whoever we could and made our stand here in the Hall of the Dead.\n\nI'm just glad we don't have to be permanent residents.

Practically my whole life. I served in his army when we drove the Reach-dogs back from our gates. The Wolf chased them halfway over the Druadach Mountains before he declared the campaign finished. He was a man to be feared and admired.
That either makes you a fool, or it makes us fools for trusting you!
That's good … but a daughter shouldn't have to kill her own father.\n\nSvana has my support, for whatever that's worth. She's going to need all the help she can get in the days to come.
None good, but none bad either. My wife knows better than anyone how to care for our people. I trust she and my thane to protect and care for Morthal in my absence.
The work of the she-giant, then? But did she call for him to aid us in our hour of need or to deliver the killing blow?\n\nLet's see what words the poet has for us this time.
Lyris's report on the rise of the Gray Host had my father preparing for the worst. When we hadn't received word for some time, he decided to intercede.

Svargrim. It's hard to believe the rumors were true. I didn't know him well, but I can't understand how anyone could throw away everything for the promise of power.\n\nWhat's immortality worth if there's nothing you hold dear?

You'd have to ask him. As far as I can tell, the western holds are in chaos. They could use a king who cares for his fellow Nords, but if the welcome we've received here is any indication, Solitude won't see it that way.

I saw her once, a long time ago. There was some brief moment in my childhood where it seemed like reconciliation between our homelands seemed possible. Might have been a dream. It vanished just as quickly.

So the rumors are true? Svargrim joined the Gray Host? I knew he had ambitions, but to throw away his humanity like that? It's inconceivable.\n\nSvargrim once told me that he would die before welcoming me to Solitude. I suppose he was right.

That's why I sent Lyris here in the first place. I'm not the king of these holds, though. I can't do anything if they refuse my help.\n\nSvargrim despised me. He would never accept my aid. But Svana? Here she comes now. Let's see what she has to say.

Blood alone does not make one worthy to rule a hold, let alone an entire kingdom.\n\nThe princess will lead for now, but many questions must be answered before the jarls crown a new ruler of Solitude. That's what a moot is for.
Aye. Back here to Icereach—their old haunt. Wish we could sink this gods-forsaken place into the sea. But for now, I'll settle for getting off the island alive.

Varen Aquilarios. A Colovian peacock who proclaimed himself emperor. Didn't last long. Never does.\n\nAnyway, when he cut down Leovic and cast the Reachmen out of Cyrodiil, the witches went with them. Wound up back here in Skyrim.

It's been abandoned for years. The locals call it Lightless Hollow. Some say it's haunted. \n\nRumors started popping up about awful, pale creatures lurking inside. There were attempts to re-open it, but the miners who tried never came back out.

The Gray Host? I've heard that name before ….\n\nMeanwhile, my father rounded up the harrowed and moved his soldiers to the city walls. Then he ordered the quartermaster to stockpile Castle Dour. He's preparing Solitude to withstand a long siege.

That might work against a mob of Reachmen, but thick walls won't stop a harrowstorm. Any war we try to wage will be over before it starts if we don't find a way to stop them.\n\nFenn knows more about the storms than anyone. See what he suggests.

The rest of us—the survivors—charged headlong into a tangle of swords, and blood, and witchcraft like I've never seen. Walking corpses, howling witchmen … a horking Giant!\n\nIf I'd known what I was getting into, I would have stayed in Windhelm!
Aye. One of the Skald-King's strongest sword-thanes sailed along with us. I wager she's made Sovngarde wait more than once.

Mmm, yes, and that's putting it kindly if the rumors are true. I've heard them called a number of different things. Bogles, clatter-coats, snow ghosts …  pale, hunched things with noses like bats and pointed ears.\n\nI plan on killing any I see.

The witches pushed the Nords out. Most folk believe they took it by force, but my Pa told me they bought it. Not with gold, mind you. With a cursed bargain or such. I believe it.\n\nAs far as I'm concerned, they can keep this place!

I want to learn more about the ritual and how it produces the harrowstorms. And I need to confirm my theories about the storm's effects. I'll start by examining the residue from the witch pike to identify the components used to power the ritual.

Head into the temple and help Bavian. See what else you can learn inside. I'd accompany you, but Meridia doesn't approve of my kind and I'd rather not get on her bad side.\n\nIn the meantime, I'll finish up out here.

I'll take samples from the harrowfiends and try to determine how the storm killed these people.\n\nLater, we can retrieve my alchemical equipment from where I hid it so I can analyze the residue. I didn't want to carry fragile instruments into danger.

The crest of Solitude. Decorates every stamp and banner. There's even that drab Tower of the Wolf rising above Castle Dour, as gray and solitary as its namesake.\n\nNot to put too fine a point on it, but I'm saying the high king resembles an old wolf.

It's too soon to tell. I have endless theories, but I need more evidence. \n\nI would be happy to indulge your curiosities after our business here is concluded, but as it stands, I cannot afford to become distracted by mere possibilities.
Assisting a fugitive is a crime in Haafingar Hold. Unless you want to find out how we deal with traitors and spies, tell me what he said to you.
Don't stick your nose where it doesn't belong. Solitude doesn't take kindly to instigators or strangers, and mark my words, you'd rather not get on the wrong side of the high king's guard.

Icereach Coven? Ridiculous! The only threat to the west are those damn spies from Eastern Skyrim, conspiring against our king. Forget whatever nonsense this skeever told you and be on your way.\n\nYou hear more talk like his, report it to the guard.
I don't know any Brondold. That is what I told the guards and that is what I'm telling you. I don't want any more trouble. You make me stab you and it's my word against yours!
Dead? Stuhn's mercy! And I'm next, aren't I?\n\nI promise, I don't know anything! I won't make any trouble. I'll disappear. I don't even like it here. You'll never see me again!

He—he did not tell me a lot. Said he was tracking some bad people. Asked me to keep an eye out for any unusual comings and goings. He'd come by now and then with a sweetroll and a few coins for my trouble.\n\nHe was … nice.

Shor's bones … I know you took some lumps in Coldharbour, but you might want to invest in a harder helmet.\n\nName's Lyris Titanborn. Axe-wielding, jaw-breaking friend to the former Emperor Varen. And to you.

Not as well as I'd like. Then again, I'd like to cast every single one of these hag-born maniacs into the sea.\n\nLosing comrades in arms … it's a terrible feeling. I just take solace in the fact that we'll all drink together in Sovngarde.

Oh, no disrespect intended, but her reputation precedes her, and that's all I'll say about that matter.\n\nNow, if you're going to speak to the jarl, you better get to it. He's not as patient as the high king.

That's a word I've heard more than once since we came ashore. After spending time with Mannimarco, I actually have some experience with dark rituals.\n\nThese things often involve a focus, or a casting circle. If we find that, we can disrupt the spell.
Plenty of axe-swings and a few kicks in the stomach, I wager.\n\nThese witches will protect the ritual with their lives. We'll make sure they pay in full.
Lucky for you. If he had told you any seditious lies and you decided to keep them from us, you'd have been in real trouble.
Here, take these.

After that horrific storm passed, I entered the town to survey the damage. I found Reachmen and my neighbors turned into feral monsters. Young Beorlin nearly tore my arms off. Until I split his skull with an axe.\n\nHe was a good kid ….

All the time. Before we settled here, Reachmen raided constantly to claim the land. And our people would push them back. When King Svargrim gave us our own hold, we built the town hoping it would stand for generations. It only lasted five years.

Well, that's a start.\n\nYou know, I never imagined I'd be working alongside a vampire, let alone one I respect. With all the leeches we've already had to kill, it's nice to see another side. Fenn's … different.

Not much. It all happened fast. During our patrol, Bjora and I heard a deafening boom over the town. The sunlight dimmed as the storm grew. The air smelled sour and I felt an unnatural energy crackle across my skin. Then … the screams.

Everyone is gone? Kyne save us all. How could this happen? \n\nIf true, then everyone the witchmen captured might be all that's left of my home. We must find them. Bring them back … if they're still alive.

Somewhere in the center of town. I froze in place from fear. Bjora took charge and ordered anyone nearby to the barrow. She truly rose to the occasion.\n\nYou must have come through town. What's going on up there?
Never before in my memory. We Nords of Karth have endured raids from the Reach for generations. They're barbarians who pillage and kill anyone who has what they want. Captives just slow them down.

That's what worries me. I've heard tales of evil Reach magic my whole life. They change people into beasts for fun. Or, they remove your bones for their rituals while you still live. Maybe they need my people for a spell!
For all I know, they are. Even that storm up above could be the work of Reach witches. Their ways are totally unnatural.\n\nI think … we should really start looking.
Karthwatch trains their guards to hide villagers down here during Reach raids. It proved impenetrable in the past … until today.

My family only speaks his name to curse it. I'm told he betrayed his hold, so he was cast into the Midnight Barrow with other exiles and traitors. Far out of reach of Sovngarde.\n\nI can't say whether he deserved that, but I know he's suffered for it.

Violence between Reachmen and the Nords of Karth has lasted generations. They take our land and we push back. Even after building Karthwatch, we still endure raids. And, each time more of our neighbors fall. Bjora shouldn't suffer for their crimes.

Of course I am! Those Orcs are my kin—same as Urzikh! But we have to face facts. They're probably dead.\n\nChief Urzikh thinks she can solve every problem with her damned alchemy, but enough is enough. I won't allow her to endanger the stronghold.

Yeah. She uses potions that dissolve stone. It makes mining quicker work, sure, but it's not our way. And it's dangerous!\n\nI'd bet my tusks that her alchemy's to blame for the collapse. Meanwhile, my wife's locked in a cage. How's that for irony?

We're going to find an active harrowstorm in the Undergrove, or I'm going to attempt to replicate one in there. Then Lyris drinks the elixir, exposes herself to the dark magic … and we wait to see what happens.

This place, I think. I've only seen glimpses of it in my dreams. It used to be a place where terrible criminals were exiled to be forgotten, until it met the same fate. Faded into myth, just like Blackreach.

An accident … or at least, I hope it was an accident.\n\nEither way, what I need right now is for Overseer Thulsgreg to follow orders and talk some sense into his fool wife, Mazog. She hid the key to the mines, and I aim to know where.

Very risky. But it's also our best chance to counter the harrowstorms and fight back against the Gray Host.\n\nEither Lyris comes through fine, or she transforms into a harrowed. Or a harrowfiend. That's also a possibility.
It needs to be done and I'm the logical choice.\n\nKing Jorunn sent me here to help Western Skyrim. If that means drinking Fenn's concoction and possibly becoming a mindless harrowed, so be it.
When the mine collapsed, strange creatures from below stormed the tunnels. Mazog locked the door to the mine to keep them contained. But by doing that, she trapped a handful of survivors inside.
Have you forgotten? I survived Coldharbour's dungeons. That puts everything into perspective. \n\nI trust Fenn. And if it doesn't work, it can't be worse than being a prisoner of Molag Bal.

Look, I was once a prisoner of a Daedric Prince. If we get out of this, remind me to tell you about that sometime.\n\nAs for now, I trust Fenn. The elixir will work. We just need to have a little faith.
No. We need to test the elixir. Lyris volunteered without hesitation. She's a true hero.\n\nStill, to know she might die to help my homeland. That's not easy for me to live with.
I know that! My parents have been pounding that into my head since I was a little girl. But I never want to take those kinds of decision lightly.\n\nLet's get moving.
What? No! I … I didn't even consider that.\n\nNo, Lyris wants to do this. And it isn't like we have a whole lot of options. Let's get moving.
Must have been terrible. I can't imagine being stuck down here, afraid that something is lying in wait in the darkness. \n\nWas there anything else?
Perhaps they still live. Maybe we're not too late after all. That gives us something to go on, at least. \n\nLooks like Pickle's got a scent again. Let's follow him.

My alchemical equipment. It's extremely fragile, so I left it in my pack. I hid it among a copse of trees once I saw all the vampires and harrowfiends.\n\nOnce I retrieve it, I can find a place to begin my analysis.
Well, I'm no mage, but if they managed to make this gale conjure up undead as well? Weaving nature magic together with the dark arts … I'd rather not think about it.

Yeah. So we fight them where they can't retreat. At the ritual site.\n\nI won't lie—facing a coven at the center of their lair doesn't fill my heart with joy, but I made a promise to sort this out. Titanborns honor their word, no matter what.

Doesn't matter now. \n\nIf Chief Urzikh gets her way, she'll open the mine and those creatures will run riot all over the stronghold. Orcs are supposed to jump at a glorious death, but I've seen enough death to know there's nothing glorious about it.
There's something about the way you hold yourself …. I believe you. \n\nThis might be a mistake, but if you really think you can keep my people safe and rescue my kin, I'd be a fool not to help you.
And Chief Urzikh doesn't make idle threats.\n\nFine. I'll tell you where the key is. But first, you'll do something for me. I want my people have a fighting chance if the worst comes to pass.
Good. You can take the side entrance out of here—it's tucked away in the back. Just don't let anyone see you, all right?
I hid it on top of the watchtower. The fate of this clan is in your hands now, outsider. Mauloch help us all if you fail.\n\nThere's a door out of the storeroom to your right. Go, quickly.

Ghouls picking the bones of the dead. Necromancers, and the like. They seem to be the ones who found this old lost barrow. I don't know what they came here for, but they've disturbed Jarl Hagridden and gods know what else.

They'd be wise to. The only time Reachmen and Nords meet is to kill each other. I always heard they were raiders and barbarians. No interest in honest labor. Or writing, for that matter.\n\nNot the sort to post job notices.

A wild land full of wild folk, located south and west of here. It's changed hands between Reachmen and the Nords more times than I can count, but they control the territory now.\n\nSeeing Reachmen wandering the streets of Solitude, it makes me nervous.

Fliers. They were hanging them at the inn and around the city. Something about a lucrative opportunity in the Druadach Mountains.\n\nI really did not pay them a lot of attention. I was more interested in the men distributing them.

You represent my most hated enemy and expect me to believe a word you say? Even if you speak true, worms have found purchase in the wood and seek to rot my kingdom from within.\n\nI will not let Solitude and the western holds fall.
Trust Svana? Perhaps ….\n\nNo. No! Your honeyed words are but echoes of my most obstinate foes. You offer a miracle with one hand while holding a poisoned dagger in the other!

The Ravenwatch has had to curtail rogue vampire clans and put down feral bloodfiends on occasion, but I've never dealt with anything like this before.\n\nPeople turning into harrowfiends or becoming mindless harrowed. It's a nightmare.

Western Skyrim consists of three holds—Haafingar, Hjaalmarch, and Karthald. Morthal is the capital of Hjaalmarch. It's located southeast of Solitude, along the River Hjaal.\n\nOld Mjolen lives in the marshlands nearby.

Mjolen's experience with the old ways and Reach magic make her ideally suited to assist me in this endeavor. She's the closest thing to an expert we're likely to find out here.\n\nAt least one who doesn't want to feed our eyes to a harpy.
Good. \n\nI know it seems like a small thing, but knowing that the clan will have a fighting chance if we have to flee gives me more comfort than you could know.
I hid it on top of the watchtower.\n\nThe fate of this clan is in your hands now, outsider. I hope my trust isn't misplaced.

You'd feel the same if you knew the tales of the fall of Markarth. What the witchmen do to folk they capture … better to slice your own throat than let those barbarians take you alive!\n\nIf they raid our hold, just run and don't look back.
<Pickle pants happily.>

Not far. She's still afloat but she's trapped in the ice. \n\nIt was a nightmare. Clear one moment, then the sky grew dark. The snow howled like a beast. And the ice … black ice … I didn't know water could freeze up that fast.
It was a last resort. It was either send someone out into the cold, or just sit there and accept our fate. Someone had to try. \n\nNot that I've done anything out here other than freeze my arse off.

I fear the beast got to them. Or worse, they're lost in this damned storm and slowly freezing to death.\n\nYou've helped us once already … do you think you could search for them? I still have injured people to take care of aboard the ship.
Good. I don't know how you convinced her, but I don't care. \n\nNow we can get inside and rescue my people. Maybe we'll even get lucky and find out how this tragedy occurred in the first place.

Take Brondold's horse and run before someone less friendly comes to find me.\n\nBron was going to take me back east after he finished here. I want to live where strangers are welcomed with a smile instead of a scowl. I hear Windhelm is like that.

We're stuck between the Despot of Markarth and the Skald-King of the east. Both sniff around like wolves, waiting for a moment of weakness to strike. Not a day goes by without a threat of war.\n\nIt is exhausting living this way.
Who knows? Maybe they really do need laborers. Can't imagine Reachmen would hire Nords, though.\n\nIt doesn't make a lot of sense.

We've seen these medallions before. On the Reachmen near Kilkreath. And I saw them on the witches in Icereach.\n\nThe assassin definitely seems to be in league with the coven, but can we get Svargrim to believe that and accept the danger he's in?

No surprise there.\n\nThe fact is, my stonemelt solution is completely safe. Mazog has never liked my methods, or my leadership. She worries like an Elf three times her age. If she or Thulsgreg had even a mouse's courage, they'd be thanking me.
No. No! She's insubordinate. Fretful. But she'd never put her kin in danger. Sabotage isn't in her nature—or Thulsgreg's.\n\nGive me the key, we're wasting time.

I was. We were down here to reopen this place after it got abandoned. But we got attacked by these horrible monsters! They overran our camp. Dragged the others off. \nI managed to get away but … Gods, it was awful.
I'm getting out of here. \n\nPlease, find the others. Save them.

They were pale and sickly looking. Hunched over like old hags with sharp teeth. Had this weird armor, too. \n\nThey killed Trilvar. He was my friend. They're going to kill the others too, I just know it. Stop them, please, I beg you!

Then we must mount a rescue! How thrilling. I couldn't have asked for a better sendoff. \n\nI'll scout an escape route for us to ensure that we have a way out. You track down the miners. We'll meet up and make our dashing getaway.

Excellent! Keep Pickle with you. He's likely to come in handy. \n\nThis is shaping up to be a fine last adventure. We're not finished yet, I know, but I'm already in your debt. You've helped grant an old man's last foolhardy wish. Let's finish this!

Eastern and Western Skyrim have been at odds since the kingdom was divided. Jorunn's ambitions for the Ruby Throne, however, have created a new level of tension.\n\nForming alliances and raising armies for conquest. Should we not be wary of such a man?

You must convince my husband that a threat greater than Jorunn exists. Further, this threat must directly imperil the high king. Find proof of this and I will assist you how I can.\n\nHelping to keep our holds safe will also allay his concerns.

My deepest apologies. Between the Reach to our south and the Ebonheart Pact to the east, our soldiers have come to see all outsiders as a potential threat.\n\nI will look into this. Vigilance cannot be allowed to become a bludgeon.

Succinctly? No, but I'll try. \n\nThe Icereach Coven recently attacked the Skald-King. We learned they're planning something in Western Skyrim as well, so Jorunn sent me to warn them. Beyond that, we have the leads Brondold found and that's about it.

Lyris Titanborn. I was one of Emperor Varen's Five Companions. Currently, I serve Jorunn the Skald-King. Skyrim's my home, and I'll do whatever's necessary to protect it.\n\nWhoever's behind these threats will regret it—as soon as we identify them.

We don't, but it's all we've got. Even if they aren't connected to the Icereach Coven, taking care of a few of Svargrim's problems might earn us some good will.\n\nNow, let's go check out the back alleys and the Lonely Troll inn.

It's at the entrance to a new dig site. A good one—plenty of ore in there!\n\nI don't know what caused the cave-in, I just heard the rumble and saw the others haul arse to the exits. I tried to help my kin, but those stones are just too big.

Looks like these damned creatures scattered the ingredients all over the place. I'm not about to send these miners back into harm's way.\n\nSo, how about it, outsider? Can you track the ingredients down and bring them back?

A storm straight from Mauloch's arsehole rose up over the town. It twisted everyone I know into monsters.\n\nIn the chaos, I saw my brother Hafskjar and his friend Bjora take people to the barrow west of town. But I've heard nothing since.

Finally a bit of good fortune. Thanks, traveler. No matter what you find in the barrow, I need to know. Tell any survivors you see to meet me here.\n\nHafskjar's the only family I have left. If I've lost him too, well …. Just hurry back safely.

Someone needs to warn the people away from Karthwatch. As the last of the Jarl's guard, the duty falls to me.\n\nLook, I'm desperate to know if the survivors made it to the barrow. Whatever gold I have is yours if you'll find out what happened to them.

Right. If the assassin is part of a vampire clan working with the coven, I couldn't imagine a better hiding place than this land of constant night.\n\nMy guess is that most of the miners have no idea what they've gotten themselves into.
Better, now that I'm not in danger of turning into one of those frozen thralls. I was halfway there when you and Drigsen showed up, thought I was done for. \n\nThat woman was a terror.

You and Lyris should. It's our best lead for finding the assassin. But if the miners have even an inkling of vampire activity down here, my presence might confuse the issue.\n\nI'm sure I can find something to do while you investigate the town.

Was that her name? Doesn't matter, I'm just glad she's gone. \n\nThere was such darkness in her eyes. Pain, too. Bone-deep pain. It was eating her up, I could feel it even as I stood there freezing to death.

Free the Silver Cormorant from the ice and assess her damage. It'll take some doing to get her free, but this crew isn't averse to hard work.\n\nIn the meantime, I sent a few of them to Morthal to gather supplies.

Now that the storm has settled, and my crew heartened, we're much better equipped to handle the delay. Supplies from Morthal will help, too. \n\nWe've gotten through the worst of it. Now, the only way to move is forward.

He what? How could you let him do that? How could you leave him behind? He could have ….\n\nOh, Viggol, my love. No, please no. I can't bear this world without you by my side. Why did he have to go and do such a thing?

I suppose you're right. He truly was a great hero. Perhaps it was a fitting end for him. \n\nThank you for going into that dark place at his side. It comforts me to know that he wasn't alone down there.

Escape? Bah! I drove them off! Killed as many as I could, but I had to run when I got the opportunity. \n\nIt's not exactly a comfort to know the myths of pale beasts that steal babes and slaughter livestock are real, but it felt good to gut some.

He's tough as an Orsinium anvil. He survived. I'm sure of it.\n\nLike I said, he probably barked out orders from the scaffolding. Better vantage point up there. You search the top, and I'll look for the other miners below. And hey. One other thing.

Wish I could tell you.  \n\nMazog, Narzba, and Blograth were getting ready to bore out a new path with the stonemelt. Mazog came running back a few minutes later, then it happened. The mine shook like a wet dog and the whole tusking place came down!

I don't know. I've been a foreman long enough to know when hope's lost. But here I am, hoping.\n\nI think they made it to the scaffolding, but I'm not sure. I hope you'll do me another favor and look for them. If they survived, they'll need a hand.

I'm sorry, but you're too late. The coven unleashed their unnatural harrowstorm and now the entire area is overrun by vampires and harrowfiends.\n\nStill, meeting you again is fortuitous. We worked well together before and I could use your help.

There may be survivors who could use your help. And, if we can learn more about the ritual that summoned the harrowstorm, we might be able to determine how to stop them.\n\nOr at the very least, we can figure out where they plan to strike next.
Information. The Icereach Coven … at work in the west. Just need more proof.\n\nGo! They're coming.
Don't trust them! Only Lyris, she's—!

Well, if this mountain were to rain ash and lava down all around us, it would assuredly bury Solitude and kill a lot of Nords, so I'd wager that's your answer. There's nothing Reachmen enjoy more than killing Nords.

An old wise woman. Her name escapes me. We crossed paths in the swamps to the east. I think she mistook me for someone else, but she was hospitable for a hermit. She was growing concerned about the rumblings of this mountain. Unnatural, she said.

The heart of this mountain is unseasonably warm and full of temperate caves called the Shadowgreen. They're lush and full of life, but quite wild and dangerous. I imagine the source of this heat is what the Reachmen are agitating with their magic.

Frankly, yes. He believes Jorunn hasn't marched here with an army as yet because the western holds are firmly united against Pact rule. My husband is certain Jorunn plots to erode those allegiances.\n\nYou will not easily earn the high king's trust.

It's enough for me to believe your intentions are sincere. Learn more about these suspicious activities you mentioned. Then bring it to me.\n\nIf this threat is as dangerous as Jorunn claims, prove it and I will make my husband listen to reason.
Reach witches from an island to the north, in the Sea of Ghosts. Nords drove their kind out of Skyrim a long time ago and we thought they were gone forever.\n\nSeems we were wrong.

Most of the tales of my exploits involve the liberal application of the blade of my axe.\n\nSvargrim must think Jorunn sent me here to strong-arm him into joining the Pact. He's wrong, but I'd probably jump to the same conclusion.

This axe and I have been all over Tamriel. To Oblivion and back on more than one occasion, for that matter. I've earned my reputation.\n\nJorunn hoped my fame might persuade Svargrim to grant me an audience, but it seems to be working against me.

It feels like I've been shattered into a thousand pieces and swept under a rug, but I don't have time to mourn right now. Not with the kingdom in danger.\n\nNow let's go talk to my father before I change my mind.

Perhaps by the window that looks out on the thoroughfare. Watching those stuffy Antiquarians rave over dusty trinkets always gives me a laugh.\n\nWhatever. It better be done by the time I return home or I'll whip those lazy servants!

Well, you and I will save it together. A joint effort. Brains and brawn. When they pen the song of this adventure, no doubt you will receive a mention.\n\nAnd what a song it will be. A tale of civil war, misguided decisions, and my stalwart bravery.

Many years ago, the college had a collection of legendary instruments. Each inspired great passions—strength, love, tragedy.\n\nThere was an argument among the bards. How best should the instruments be used?

It's a lute called Petraloop. Actually it's Petralute, but try saying that after five strong meads. \n\nIt was the learning lute at the College for generations. Played by dozens—hundreds—of bards over the years! It means a lot to us.
She what? No, there has to be some mistake.\n\nMazog would never hurt the clan on purpose. She's only tries to protect us!

I heard mention of the Druadach Mountains, but I doubt that was anything more than a false trail. Most of these mining concerns like to keep the true location of their hoard a trade secret.\n\nIs that it? Are you a competitor out to steal their mine?

Overheard snippets of conversation and a feeling in my gut. While the hiring agent might have been a Breton, his associates were clearly from the Reach, by the way.\n\nI also heard talk of a lodge outside the city. Perhaps a stop along the way?

What, I don't look royal enough to you?\n\nI'm the high king's daughter, whether I like it or not. I didn't ask for the position. It was thrust upon me by an accident of birth, and I don't much care for all the associated decorum and responsibility.

Even in our darkest hour, Meridia provides a light.\n\nWe were on our way to see High Priest Varkour when the storm hit. I've never seen such power. It raged like a thing alive. I gathered who I could, but the others are still out there.

Start at the stables to the northwest. I saw Acolyte Hjolt, Priest Direnna, and Roligmolf the pilgrim seek shelter there. If you find them, send them back here.\n\nAfter that, meet me at the Pilgrims' Lodge, to the west of the temple.

Damn it. I suspected as much, but I really hoped I was wrong.\n\nShe's given me no choice. I must invoke the Blood Price. Mazog's actions led to the death of her kin, and the near collapse of our stronghold. I will remove her tusks myself.
You're so interested, then you do it!\n\nGo on. Get out of here. You're spoiling my good mood.

Anything! As long as it's what I want. Not what I'm supposed to do. \n\nEverybody acts like my parents are in charge, but they're just slaves to their crowns! They barely exist aside from their roles as king and queen. I refuse to wind up like that.

She'll suffer the Blood Price. It's how we punish our own. Rather than imprison them or make them unfit to work, we extract the tusks of those who fail the clan.\n\nBetter than the blood-letting, I guess. But it's said to be excruciating.
You're right. I know you're right. It's just—he's my father!\n\nNo, I have to focus. The harrowstorm. It's coming. We have to save the city. There's nothing more important than that right now.

I—I'm not sure we can. But we can make more of Fenn's elixir. Distribute it to the people. We need more of Arkay's sacred oil, though.\n\nWe'll have to take it from the supply stockpiled at the Temple of the Divines.

The Breton was sly. Handsome even. Thought he could charm me into taking on additional shipments. Now that I know what's involved, the trouble isn't worth it.\n\nThe Nords were locals. Hired hands from the Lonely Troll.

Nothing good, I'm sure. The Gray Host appeared out of nowhere and cut down my soldiers. Only a handful were able to escape before they sealed the gates.\n\nSvargrim made us fortify the entryways. The bastard knew he'd lock us out.

Not that I can think of. But what does it matter? Svargrim brought the Gray Host down upon us. He's bringing a harrowstorm!\n\nWe need to evacuate the city while there's still time. Some of us will survive if we flee now!
I'm paid not to ask too many questions. This arrangement was a lucrative one. I trusted them, but it seems they took advantage of my natural greed.\n\nThat won't happen again.

Not me. My debtors. I provide funds to the Coterie of Organized Scholars and the Swords of Solitude militia. Both are shorthanded and in arrears, so I took it upon myself to correct their courses before they leave me destitute.\n\nYou'll work for them.

They're an organization of local scholars granted the exclusive right to pursue their research in the western holds. The Mages Guild relies upon them, as does the Bards College, but they haven't been able to fulfill their obligations recently.

One of the oldest independent militias in the western holds. Sell-swords granted the right to ply their trade within the kingdom in exchange for pledging their service to the high king. The Fighters Guild employs them almost exclusively, or they did.
Cautious. Good. You might last long enough to help me recoup the gold I lent those … fine and upstanding organizations.\n\nWhat is it you want to know?

More witches. And this shadowy ally.\n\nIf they really want to claim Skyrim for themselves, they couldn't have chosen a better time. The kingdom is sundered in two. The Skald-King's busy with the war in Cyrodiil. We're vulnerable. Plain and simple.

Tinzen is the name. I'm a representative of the renowned Coterie of Organized Scholars. I'm also a member. \n\nAlchemy is my purview—as well as my passion—but our membership's specialties outnumber the stars in the sky!

Not familiar with them? Well, that will soon change! They are a kind of undead unique to Skyrim. Long dead warriors and servants of the mysterious Dragon priests who ruled here in the ancient past. They remind me a bit of frostbitten jerky.

It's only known for being chilly, windy, and deep. One of the larger frozen caverns in the region. Very inhospitable to life, so it's unusual to suspect an entire tribal civilization is eking out a living there, but that would put it on the map!
Oh, it's far more complicated than that! The tonic's other central ingredient is the essence of a Giant itself.\n\nForget I said that. You will have to drink it, after all.

We're the oldest institution of learning in Western Skyrim, outside the Bards College. In fact, the students of the Bards College and the Mages Guild employ us exclusively for research assistance. A perk of our charter with the High King.

Well, the Mages Guild is a foreign body and folk are particularly suspicious of them, so they are legally obligated to conduct their business through our trusted institution. As for the Bards College? Not all poets are scholars, let's say.

Harrowfiends are feral vampires, a byproduct of the unnatural harrowstorm.\n\nAs for me, I am Fennorian of House Ravenwatch. I came here on the trail of remains stolen from a mass grave in Bangkorai. They were shipped to Solitude in ancient urns.

House Ravenwatch is one of the noble houses of Rivenspire. Our liege, Count Verandis, has dedicated us to the cause of peaceful coexistence between mortals and … those of the vampiric persuasion.\n\nThat often makes us defenders of Tamriel.
Is it that obvious? But have no fear. As a member of House Ravenwatch, I have pledged to never take blood from an unwilling subject. I assure you, I'm only here to help.

The Icereach Coven performed a ritual that unleashed a harrowstorm on the temple. It struck without warning and evaporated as quickly as it began, but in its wake it left behind harrowfiends—innocent priests and pilgrims transformed into monsters.

True, but I've seen evidence of a vampiric connection. At the very least, the material they transported from Bangkorai included the remains of ancient vampires. They were part of an army that was defeated in the First Era—the Gray Host.

I am much more than just a vampire! In addition to being an agent of House Ravenwatch, I am a master alchemist and an expert in arcane studies.\n\nI do try to avoid direct violence, though, to make sure I never give in to temptation.

I lost a lot of things today. We all did. But that doesn't mean I won't keep trying to help the faithful.\n\nThere are injured to tend to, and those poor souls who lost their minds to the storm. I want to find a way to help them all.

High Priest Varkour claimed it contained Meridia's divine light. There are rituals for releasing such power. Whether I or one of the other priests can make use of it, we'll see.\n\nI just hope we don't experience any more of those storms.
No thank you. Go away.
Welcome, and enter.
You should leave.

I don't think so. Fenn says it's a key component. Let's see what we're up against at the temple.\n\nEvery locked door in Solitude can be circumvented, if you know your way around the city. We'll get the sacred oil, one way or another.
It was … surprising, to say the least.\n\nBut my father and his treachery will have to wait. We need to protect the people of Solitude from the approaching harrowstorm. That's our priority.

At this point, I'm ready to believe it's all a grand joke being played at my expense. \n\nI don't know if it's just miners wandering off, or if it's malevolent spirits. But if this doesn't get figured out soon, my whole operation is going under.
What is this scrap you give Mazalkir?\n\nWell, this is her handwriting. This one thinks she has been drinking again, selling things she just bought.
Of course! Mazalkir does not steal, even if she deserves it.

You know your strengths and weaknesses better than I do. Play to those. But whichever path you decide, move quickly. We need to find the ritual site and deal with the witch pikes before they unleash the harrowstorm on the city.

Yes, it's horrible. The afflicted are compelled to transform and then become violent, almost feral.\n\nWe were close to finding a cure, but our alchemist, Rasir, went missing. I fear something terrible may have happened.

I'm not sure, but it's not like Alchemist Rasir not to report back.\n\nMy partner, Skor, ran off to find him. I worry for him, too. I want to search for them, but it's unwise to travel alone. I need an ally.

She's pretty, fair-haired and fierce, but she's got kind eyes when you know her. She wears a protective charm passed down from her grandmother around her neck. Old Nord magic. Nothing else like it among the raiders.
Giants? My Nel? She was always last to draw steel on a raid. Why would she do something as suicidal as fight Giants?

I'm not sure, but I believe he's … one of my kind. They mentioned a devastating storm. We need to find out exactly what they have planned.\n\nMy apologies, but we're going to have to postpone our escape.
We were in the Horker, waiting for them to tell us how we were going to make a pile of gold, when they ordered us to go to the basement.\n\nOne of us refused. They cut him. There was so much blood!

When we saw the Reach witches, a few of us tried to fight. I slipped away before anyone noticed.\n\nThey're doing something terrible down here! Something … monstrous! Please, you must help the others! And you need to destroy the pikes. They're evil!

We'll make an investigator out of you yet! I need to figure out how those stolen remains, the Icereach Coven, and that vampire are connected.\n\nLet's catch up to Urgala and her guest and see what we can find out.

Hedrynne's as sweet as honeysuckle but tough as steel. Everybody loves her. She's younger than me, and I've been training her in the healing arts.\n\nBut, if I can't make the elixir in time—no, I can't think like that. We'll save her. We have to.

Chillwind mushrooms can only be found in this cave. The bugs eat them and the deep lichen that grows on the walls. Well, when they aren't munching on people.\n\nMixed with an unfertilized chaurus egg, they create a powerful antidote to chaurus poison.
Excellent! You scan lines quickly, I see.\n\nStill, I would avoid any ad libbing.
Ah. Earnest conviction, but no.\n\nNot to worry, it is only a single line. I am sure you will get it with more practice.

The cave system consists of winding caverns. There's a lot of wildlife down there. Some of it is the usual things you'd expect to find underground. Some of it, like the giant insects, is more exotic.\n\nIt's dangerous, but we need those ingredients.
Mara and Kyne willing, my elixir will work and she will be on her feet in no time.\n\nI couldn't have done it without you, traveler.
Nchuthnkarst. It's a mouthful, right? \n\nI sometimes wonder if the real reason the Dwarves are all gone is because they choked and swallowed their tongues trying to say their own names.

Some said the instruments were too precious and needed protection. Others asked, "What use are they if they can't be played?" The two sides actually came to blows! Fretboards and inkwells flying every which way. \n\nIt was all quite exhilarating.

Oh she died. Very sad. And she never told a soul where to find the instruments. But while reading Nel's Hidden Loves I realized it held clues to their locations!\n\nIf we recover them based on her clues, I'll be a legend!

She worries this vault is too big a risk, but I simply cannot ignore the possibilities of discovery here! Besides, we can handle looters.\n\nI will admit, there are some additional oddities at play, but what Dwemer ruin doesn't have its challenges?

So far? Not much. I found a few rancid potions, old knuckle-bones, crow feathers …. Gods know what any of those things do.\n\nRemember, I'm a warrior. In my younger days, I left this sort of nonsense to that lecherous fossil, Abnur Tharn.
Hmph. Sounds like a real charmer, whoever he is. Provided he's not some kind of hag-tale bogeyman, I'm sure we'll meet him eventually. Axe-first.

That depends. What year is it? No, wait! Don't say it, there's already enough temporal instability going on in this place.\n\nMy name is Thaddeus Cosma and I am a member of … you know what? That's not important right now. This device, however, is!

Too complicated to explain. See that scroll on that ledge there? It's a list of components I need you and your friends to track down. \n\nUnless I fix this device, the temporal and spatial distortions will tear this place apart, along with all of us.
If we had more of the medallions, maybe. Even then, Magister Fridelja hasn't determined what enchantment the medallions use to provide their protection.\n\nWe need a different solution.

Yes, Lyris mentioned that. As a matter of fact, you received a message. A courier brought it from Dusktown. I never heard of the place, but it was sent by someone named Fennorian. Is that your scholar?\n\nRead the message and then see if he'll help us.

A miraculous confluence of temporal displacement and spatial distortion. I've seen such amazing things, if only I had the time to tell you!\n\nBut I can't stay long. I've ensured the part is here in the present so that you may take it. Now, make haste!

No, but if I had to guess, I'd say she's brandishing her sword at whatever she's encountered. \n\nTake this component back to Thaddeus. Once the device is concordant again, all of the threads and this point in time will be put back in place.

Back isn't the right word for it. I understand so much more now than I once did.\n\nDon't think of time and space as a road upon which you travel, but rather a rope, or a cable. Many threads, all bound together with no beginning or end.
Of that I have no doubt. \n\nNow, I need to ensure the central resonator remains stable during the process. You must install the components. There, there, and there. Quickly now!

They say the first one is always the hardest. Everything should be much easier from here!\n\nOnce you recover all the instruments, I will compose an epic, "An Adventurer's Triumph," to celebrate their return. You will star in it, of course.

Yes, but more research is required to confirm anything. Still, from what we observed here, it appears the harrowstorm produced three distinct results in those caught within it.\n\nIt turned them into harrowfiends or harrowed, or it simply killed them.

I remember a time when we were all happy together, him and mother and I. Seems like a long time ago.\n\nAt some point, he became more and more involved with the trappings of power. He was more interested in being the high king than my father.

I tried, but interaction with my father made it difficult. She wanted us to be a family, but the high king wanted a queen and a princess.\n\nEventually, he stopped ordering me to attend royal functions. It was my one victory in our relationship.

She's strong, but her methods don't always sit well with the clan.\n\nShe earned her place as chief, no question. But where Orcs are concerned, a little progress goes a long way. Push things too far, and people start getting their tusks in a twist.

Thulsgreg runs the clan's mining operation. He would have ruled the clan if Chief Urzikh hadn't challenged him. He still holds a grudge, I think. Hard to blame him.\n\nOur clan's never been too strict with tradition, but he'd love to change that.

In a storeroom beneath the longhouse. \n\nNow listen, I don't want you trying to break her out. Neither of you would make it out of the stronghold alive. But you can talk to her if you want. You should hear her side of the story.

That obvious, eh? For years, my family ruled the stronghold. When my father passed, the role of chief should have fallen to me.\n\nUrzikh's challenge for the title was an affront to the traditions this clan has survived on for generations.

Hmph. We abandoned our people's cruder customs long ago. People marry who they wish, for instance. But the traditions we kept are sacred. We honor the Code.\n\nTradition sustains and protects us. But Chief Urzikh ignores any rule or custom she pleases.

Try if you want, but know this: I'll do what I have to to get that key.\n\nThe clan won't like it—they're frustrated as it is. But as chief, I'm bound to do what's best for the stronghold. If what's best for the clan is Thulsgreg on a pike, so be it.

No, of course not. My father was the high king of Western Skyrim. I always thought he had the best interests of our holds and our people in his heart.\n\nBut there was a darkness there. Jealousy. Bitterness. He wanted to control all of Skyrim.

For Svargrim, yes, I think it was. As for Rada al-Saran and the Gray Host … I'm not entirely sure what they're after.\n\nEnough of this. I need to get to work. With my father gone, someone has to pick up the pieces and restore the holds.

Not as much as I'd like. It strikes quickly, and indiscriminately. Those who fall ill are consumed by an unnatural, violent rage.\n\nNothing seems to get through to them. Their minds completely deteriorate.

I mean anything.\n\nHeaps of unholy ashes and charred bones fill every corridor and passageway. You cannot take a step in there without treading on the corpse of an ancient monster. No, wayfarer. We cannot let even a mouse leave such a place.

You should not speak the Host's name so loudly. Suffice it to say they were creatures of the night. Slain, burned, and buried.\n\nThere is an old Yokudan saying: to name an evil is to sharpen its blade. Better to leave it nameless and forgotten.
You? Tu'whacca's breath … to defeat dead summoners, I rely upon the scions of Bal. May my ancestors forgive me.\n\nI will trust you. For now.
Good. A moment's carelessness can invite the monsters' fangs.

Yes. Tu'whacca's Gaze. Its light casts a ward over the one who holds it, protecting them from the traps and defenses inside the Grave. This will allow the invaders to pass through quickly. We will not be so lucky.
That would explain the assassin's swiftness and ability to escape so easily. We knew the Icereach Coven had vampires on their side, but using them so blatantly?\n\nAnything else to report?

Well then, time to fight fire with fire. They've got evil vampires, and we've got a friendly one. Let's find out exactly what your friend Fenn knows about vampire clans in the area.\n\nWhere did you tell me Fenn was going again?

I'll rally my remaining solders and organize the city guard. We'll get everyone into the Blue Palace and defend them from there.\n\nI know it won't protect us from the harrowstorm, but we'll be able to hold off the Gray Host if they decide to attack.

Do we have a choice? Time is running out and this place is too big for one group to search quickly. Our chances get a whole lot better if you go one way and we go the other.\n\nJust watch each other's backs. We don't get to try this twice.

How can you ask such a question? I need to understand why my father betrayed my mother and our people … why he turned away from me.\n\nIf we don't figure that out, it could happen again. Any one of us could be swayed by promises of wealth and power.

I'm still trying to make sense of what we saw. Rada al-Saran was attuning Svargrim to the magic imbued in this tower. Giving him command of the harrowstorm.\n\nObviously, the process involved a great deal of pain.
The key …? Yes, yes, I see. You just may have hit the nail on the head, my friend.\n\nCome on, let's get to Svargrim before he unleashes the harrowstorm upon the city.

We split up, just as Svana suggested. Take different paths to the upper levels and make sure he doesn't slip past us.\n\nIf I had to lay down a wager, I'd say we'll find the high king at the top of this structure—provided we reach it in time.
I—I'm not sure. I don't have the skills necessary to unravel the Ashen Lord's ritual. The only way I see to stop the harrowstorm is to cut out its heart. I think we need to kill Svargrim.

I know, I know. He probably had a hand in my mother's death. And he apparently willingly sided with the Gray Host and became a vampire.\n\nWe're going to have to kill him … but that's not something I ever thought I'd need to contemplate. Patricide.

I'm pretty sure. I think this is how the Gray Host forces were able to sneak into the Temple of the Divines and take control of that location.\n\nGo fast, but try to be stealthy. Maybe we can surprise them like they surprised the swordthane's soldiers.
Get to the surface and make our way up to the Tower of the Wolf? Then do whatever it takes to keep Svargrim from calling the harrowstorm down upon the city.\n\nChild's play, wouldn't you say?

Rada al-Saran not only turned my father into a vampire, he merged him with Greymoor Keep. We should be thankful that the process has taken as long as it has.\n\nI don't think we have much longer, though. We need to reach him before the storm breaks.
There's a door in the wall below the tower. We need to reach that door — and fight through any harrowfiends and Gray Host that try to get in our way!
That doesn't matter, now! I have to fight!\n\nThese harrowfiends won't make it into the city, friend. I swear it on the Ravenwatch!
I've faced worse odds before. Maybe a little better than these. But I don't carry this axe around for show!
Those waves of energy. Whatever Rada al-Saran is doing, it's similar to the harrowstorm rituals. Somehow, it's bringing these stone husks to life.\n\nEnough talk. We need to keep moving.
First, I'm going to make the bastards who did this to me pay. \n\nThen I think I'll take a long, hot bath, stuff myself on sweets and mead, and then perhaps find someone to warm my bed.

I do. I know you and Lyris have risked your lives for my kingdom, despite being met with suspicion and contempt. You counted on my mother to be your advocate, to convince my father the threat is real.\n\nI'm no substitute, but … I'll speak for you.

That makes it even more important that he heeds your warning and takes action. All of the holds are in danger. Haafingar, Hjaalmarch, Karthald … my father needs to do something before another storm strikes.\n\nMeet me at the Blue Palace, all right?

And where might that be? I appreciate the thought, but if it's all the same to you, I think I'll stick close to the palace. In case Svana needs me.\n\nBesides, I know where Svargrim keeps his liquor. I figure it's fair game, now that he's a traitor.

I can assure you that in its present formulation that it will cause you no harm. I've nearly eliminated the tongue swelling entirely. The snowberries should allow the tonic to more easily diffuse through your body … and make it much more palatable.

So you are. Thank you for being open about it. I would never dare expose another vampire without their blessing, but talking around it is … well, it's tedious, to be honest. I hope you'll pardon my saying so.\n\nNow, what were we talking about again?

Well, they've out-researched me at every turn.\n\nEvery time I think I've found some new cache of arcane antiquities, the Draugrkin beat me to the punch. I followed them here in hopes of finding out how they manage it.

Alas, no. But now, having seen them up close, I'm growing more and more convinced that someone is helping them. A shadowy researcher of some kind. This person may even be financing the expeditions. Not a comforting thought, that.

Now, I intend to uncover the secrets of the Dwemer miter. \n\nScholars bicker about its uses, but no one truly understands it. And those who have been foolish enough to try and don one themselves are no longer able to tell us much of anything at all.

Me? Oh, I'm practically no one!\n\nI'm just a mage that never really fit in anywhere … that is until I heard of Claudina's exploits! I've always been obsessed with her work, so I tracked her down and begged her to take me on as her assistant.

As do I, dear assistant.\n\nBut for that, I must work uninterrupted. I am deeply grateful for your help, but you will have to wait for the results of my findings along with the Dwemeric scholarly community.

Someone went to great pains to wipe it from the histories. Likely to keep it hidden from greedy necromancers like the Draugrkin.\n\nBut if there's one thing I've learned in my time as an investigator, it's that nothing stays hidden forever.

An ancient army of the night—the Gray Host.\n\nIt took the combined might of the Bangkorai Garrison and Hestra's Legions to defeat them. Fearing something might bring the Host back to life, the soldiers burned all the corpses and left the ashes here.

Svargrim has every right to be angry. He watched his wife die right before his eyes. But he's the high king! He doesn't have the right to be stupid.\n\nTime to make Svargrim confront some hard truths. Come on, the swordthane led the king upstairs.

Oh! Great! That's wonderful! Now we don't have to find another way inside.\n\nI keep telling Claudina you're a natural. You've just taken to all of this so splendidly. I'm thrilled you'll get to participate in the ceremony.

It varies by situation, but I've seen it work well over a dozen times. Some spirits find it more annoying than anything, but others are very susceptible to the sound. \n\nThere are few supernatural beings that can ignore it, however.

Here, you take the Spirit Summoning Whistle. When I spread the salts, you blow it, and if there are any spirits remaining in the area, the tone will force them out of hiding!\n\nIt's a big responsibility, but I know you're ready for it.
I know, right? It happened so quickly. When we confronted Rada al-Saran and Exarch Ulfra, the vampire lord blasted Lyris with his magic.\n\nWhen I saw her fall, I knew I had to act.
What do you mean? He never mentioned anything like that to me.\n\nKyne's Gift, grandfather! Had I known, had anyone at the temple known, we would have aided you in this!

It certainly gave us a fighting chance. When she called forth the harrowstorm, I grabbed the elixir from Lyris and barely thought about what I was doing.\n\nI just drank it down and walked into the storm.
I don't disagree, but somebody had to do it. There wasn't any other option.\n\nAnd I'd do it again. My people are counting on me.

Extremely. And if my grandfather is dead, that means the seal is no longer protected. Someone might be trying to release Morokei as we speak!\n\nAre you with me still? We must seek out these warding flames and make sure they're lit.

Spirits, of course! Ideally, the ones that have been terrorizing these poor people.\n\n My mentor and I have been given the important responsibility of investigating the mysterious disappearances down here. We're supernatural specialists, of a sort.
Then they might be close to achieving their goal! We can't let that happen. \n\nWe have to go to the source. Morokei's tomb. That's where we'll find the monster responsible for this, I know it.

Leave? But we're so close to figuring this out! If we just had a little more time … and maybe a set of extra hands. \n\nYou look very clever! I'm sure if you joined us, we'd solve this in no time. Interested? Claudina would reward you, I'm sure.

We're perilously close! Claudina has been doing this for years, she's practically an expert. I'm just her apprentice, but so far there hasn't been a case that we couldn't solve!\n\nDusktown is in capable hands!
A bold move, even for them. Old Mjolen and I have been comparing notes and we've made some progress studying the harrowstorm ritual.\n\nWhat happened to your large friend with the axe, by the way?
Good. Good. Divinations can be fickle. The longer we delay, the colder the trail grows.\n\nLet's see if we can catch the scent of your prey.
Of course, ask me anything you wish. It's the least I can do in exchange for your help.

No, no. I am a priestess of Kyne. I weave a bit of clever magic—to change my shape. But I would appreciate it if you kept that to yourself.\n\nI've been studying owls lately. They are so beautiful in flight. They're one of my favorite forms to take.

Grandfather Keldnyr is a kind, gentle man. My parents died when I was very young, so he brought me with him to live in the temple. \n\nHe taught me many things about the beauty of the world and the majesty of Kyne. I admire him very much.

I don't know. \n\nI want to believe that, but he's eighty-three years old, and his health has waned in the last few months. I'd already made peace with the idea that I may lose him soon, but I didn't think it would be in a place like this.

No. Many in my order would frown on it. We Nords have a … fraught relationship with magic. But I feel such a sense of communion when I take flight.\n\nFeeling the wind rustle through my feathers … it's as if Kyne and I are dancing.

A prisoner? No. Why would you think that? But we did sign a contract. Promised to stay until the work was done and never breathe a word.\n\nOtherwise, being a bonded miner with the Bitterblade Mining Consortium is a lucrative opportunity!
Feh. What do I look like, the town crier? If the overseer wanted us to be observant, he wouldn't have blindfolded us when he brought us here.
You weren't? Hmm. Up to this point, the overseer and his wife have been extra careful about keeping the exact location of this mine and the mining town a secret.\n\nWhat makes you special, I wonder?
Time is of the essence. You get to the ruin. I'll find Lyris and we'll meet you there.\n\nIt's southeast of Dusktown. If you get there before us, go inside and guard the entrance until we arrive.

I started this venture with my husband. Supposing all of this chaos doesn't completely ruin us, our goal is to be the first to capitalize on Blackreach's frontier. \n\nA few days ago, I would have told you we were doing just that. Now? I'm not so sure.

Knowledge of my history is hardly imperative to the success of this mission … but if you must know, I was much like Phebe. At that age, I was obsessed with all things supernatural, but had no outlet for it.\n\nSo I made one for myself.

I am less and less convinced that we're dealing with a spirit. This brute seems too calculating, and yet equally too clumsy, to be part of that world.\n\nMy intuition says we are dealing with something far more sinister.

Not all supernatural beings are sinister. Some are lost, some are fearful, some are simply misguided. My life's work has been determining one from the other. Monsters, however, rarely have such distinctions.

Let me see that. Ulang is Ena's right hand. She must have left this for him.\n\nDamn. She really is in trouble. You check on that camp she mentioned and see if you can find her. I'll prepare the garrison for whatever's coming.

I'm not sure what to think. But if the Reachmen went to all the effort to get this far north, it's probably for more than just raiding caravans.\n\nBe careful. Once you find Ena, meet me back in Dragon Bridge.

Well, let's not get ahead of ourselves. Most of these bones are charred and brittle. They might make serviceable thralls for light housework, but as an army? I don't know. It's curious.\n\nWe'll just have to keep digging.

Yes. Among other things.\n\nMy teachers spoke of ancient guardians—timeless defenders that would fight on long after the last Pyre Watch sentinel fell. Without Tu'whacca's Gaze … they may try to cast us out. Violently.

Yes. I may not be able to swing a sword with confidence, but I would sooner cast myself into one of those chasms than abandon my post entirely.\n\nI will find a way to help, wayfarer. Upon Leki's blade, I swear it.

The Swords of Solitude militia. Oldest volunteer army in the hold. We've defended the people of Western Skyrim for generations. The high king's soldiers can't respond to every petition for assistance, so we lend our aid for those willing to pay.
Excellent! You are truly the purveyor of justice Phebe made you out to be. \n\nJust be careful. If we manage to get ourselves caught, we won't get the chance to prove anything.

I believe the Overseer's office is just across the mine. We should investigate! \n\nOf course, we have to find a way in, first. Perhaps you could pick the lock, or steal his key? I'm somewhat out of my element now.

Rigurt knows there is no love for the Skald-King or his domain here. But with the Three Banner's War, Rigurt must find allies and friends wherever he can.\n\nSolitude has not received an envoy from Whiterun for ages. We needed another way.

Rigurt's mission is the same as always: to be the handsome, friendly face of Nord culture throughout all of Tamriel!\n\nRigurt is only sent on the most important assignments. This time, he must convince thanes to sign a peace treaty with Windhelm.

The Three Banners War drags on, and anyone that is not a friend to Windhelm may soon become an enemy.\n\nBesides, it is no good to have neighbors you disagree with. Rigurt had a neighbor once, growing up. She swept away his favorite anthill! So sad.
The Skald-King is in Solitude? Shor's bones, no one tells Rigurt anything!\n\nWell. Rigurt has never failed a mission! He will do his best to see this one through, for the good of his people!

There is no greater mediator in all of Skyrim! Besides Rigurt, of course.\n\nJarl Morryn is also distant kin to Western Skyrim's rulers. Her family's hunting lodge is here. She can come and go from the kingdom without raising concern.

He's a bull-headed traditionalist who constantly drags his feet. He and his wife would rather eat dirt than admit what I've done has helped the clan.\n\nBasically, he makes things more difficult. Trust me—being chief is difficult on the best of days.

Wondered when they would send someone. Though, an outsider surprises me.\n\nYes, I know of the fleshless wolves. But a ghost of young Freiwen? Disturbing. I may have answers for this haunting. But I'll need cursed specimens to study. You will get them.

Blood and tissue. Tear some decayed skin off an affected person and scrape dried blood from a cursed wolf.\n\nBring me these things so I can understand what kind of magic we're dealing with. I fear there is more to Freiwen's haunting than we realize.
Good, go on. Return here when you have the samples. A simple ritual will provide the details we seek.\n\nIn the meantime, I'll consult my notes about Freiwen's disappearance.

The Skald-King's wizards added their own spell to the medallions. We each get one. Here. They're supposed to lead us to magic similar to what's contained in the medallions. Icereach magic.\n\nWave it around and see what happens.
I can't be sure. But all these animated statues … and now a colossal tomb guardian? I fear something truly horrifying rests at the heart of this place.

Something old. Very old. Old enough to escape all the histories of the Imperial City unnoticed. I suppose the only way to find out is to soldier on.\n\nJust keep an eye on Shelaria, eh? I will as well.

It's a rocky outpost on the Sea of Ghosts. A fort, some ruins, a fishing village ….\n\nThe only reason we settled on it was its location. It serves as a bulwark against northern invasions. But the defenders never counted on an invasion like this.
Good. Most of our grizzled veterans have already fallen. We could use a seasoned warrior like you.
<You are about to face a difficult Trial in Kyne's Aegis. Are you ready to depart?>
Oh, you know. The usual. Delving dungeons, defying death, and staving off the ravages of boredom by risking our lives over and over.\n\nYou show up at the damnedest times.

It really was something, wasn't it? I'm just glad Divayth Fyr was able to bring us back home like we agreed.\n\nIt's not every day you get to help save one of the Living Gods. You should hear Raynor go on about it. As if his head wasn't big enough.

All right, I know we're friends and all, but you honestly don't expect me to believe that, do you? Climbing the Crystal Tower? Meeting the Psijic Order?\n\nLet me guess, you arm wrestled a Daedric Prince and won?

I heard a few rumors about Dragon sightings, but I wasn't sure how true they were. That sounds terrifying, honestly.\n\nDid you get any souvenirs at least? I've never been to Elsweyr. No Dwemer ruins, you know … not much academic opportunity.

Her methods trouble me. We've always upheld our traditions, and they've served us well.\n\nNow, Chief Urzikh has grand ideas about a prosperous future and expanding the stronghold. We don't need anything more than what we already have.

I won't lie to you … it was. The mine was running dry. Trade was dying out. But we were surviving. Not well, but well enough.\n\nThat's why the clan puts up with her. She pulled us back from the brink. But now we see the price of it.

Evidence of our problem. \n\nThere's a group of looters trying to lay claim to this place. Probably from that mining town nearby. They were easy enough to get rid of. It's the other things giving me trouble.

Quite a bit, in fact! I've made some fascinating discoveries since we last saw each other.\n\nBut this is hardly the time or place to catch up. We should talk when we're not standing in a trembling Dwemer ruin rife with dangerous creatures, hm?

Where indeed! I suppose they could really be anywhere. The Merethic Era, the distant future, the very start of creation! \n\nDon't get hung up on it. Rather, we should concentrate on how to bring them back … providing they haven't already perished.

Fixing this Dwemer device should realign time and return every thing and every one to its proper place. In theory. \n\nWhich is why I need those components. In light of unfortunate circumstances, the responsibility to retrieve them now falls to you.

More questions! I almost forgot what a curious creature you are. \n\nAll I can say for sure is you will know them when you see them. Now hurry along! I'll stay here and keep the device stable for as long as I can.

Something to do with a New Life feast they attended at Karthwatch a few seasons back. \n\nI don't know the details, but as I understand it, the whole thing was pretty idiotic. But neither one would forgive the other, so here we are.
Which one do you want to hear about first? Thane Hraldi, or Thane Svyne?

They call him Flint-Passer in the taverns because he … well … acts like the kind of man that passes flint every time he uses the privy. Stern. Humorless. Can't stand anything that might embarrass him. \n\nOh, and he loves fishing. Adores it.

Thane Svyne loves melees almost as much as he loves his meals. He's incredibly strong, and has an appetite to match. \n\nI saw him eat a whole cockerel pie straight from the oven. Hadn't even cooled. He couldn't talk for nearly half a year.

Rigurt remembers his Argonian friends taking him into the darkest part of a stinky cavern. At the very back, Rigurt spotted the mushroom. Smelled it too. \n\nIt should not be hard to find. Keep your eyes and nostrils open, friend!

Anyone brought down by wolves turned. Their skin shriveled and froze before my eyes. Then, they attacked me! People I've known for years!\n\nHavil, the guy who owns the farm, holed up in the house. Could you check on him? I'm worried for his safety.

The Orcs who saw them said they looked like pale Goblins with eyes like moles. I've heard tales like this before. Hearthmother's stories to keep the little ones out of the mine. I guess some tall tales are true.\n\nCome on. Let's find the survivors.

Her hut lies to the north-east. She is a strange one for sure. Always stealing my chickens for her unnatural magics. But, she's the only one who understands the ways of ghosts.\n\nIn the meantime, I'm going to stay right here until this all blows over.

No clue why she'd bring this upon us. Freiwen always loved visiting the farm.\n\nActually, there's someone who might know about Freiwen's fate. A clever woman who speaks with spirits named Old Mjolen. Perhaps you could ask her to help fix all this?

Still … alive? I can't believe it. After all these years, Freiwen finally comes home and you tell me she's dying?\n\nWhy would she have you deliver this locket? I must see her! There is so much to say. Where is she? Take me to her.
But, you survived! Oh, the clever woman protected you. \n\nSpeak with Old Mjolen, please. She knows so much more about magic than anyone in Morthal. There must be something that can cure my daughter.

Is that by the water where the boats dock? Or perhaps her bedroom where she watched people from the window?\n\nThe tree! Oh, Freiwen. That old tree in the forest above Morthal. She would spend hours there. We must go now!

We'll lose precious time. So, don't make a mistake.\n\nDon't fret, all right? The instructions are simple. That's why I'm having you prepare it instead of doing it myself. I need to show the clan that anyone can do this—even an outsider. No offense.

Mixing the three reagents together creates a potent alchemical solvent. It's perfectly safe, but it does work quickly, so be prepared to move.\n\nJust follow my instructions on the table over there. It contains a list of everything you need.

Hm, let me see. \n\nAwful. The fantasies of a child. Playing with magic like this invites danger. The energies at the ruins surely overwhelmed her. But this shard …. Tell me, did Freiwen explain the visions of her ghost to you?

By flooding her with her own life force, we can burn out the curse.\n\nGive me her locket. Ah, yes, it hums with emotional power. Once attuned, you can absorb Freiwen's memories into it. Fill it with her energy so we may rescue her from death.

Yes, this is what I needed to know. Maxten's ritual consumed the spirits in the ruins. She wished to gain power by absorbing their memories.\n\nFreiwen's curse drains her life energy then manifests it as her own memories. This is how we cure her.

Because I'm smarter than most Nords? Ha, I jest.\n\nPeople from the north fear magic. Don't understand it? Must be dangerous. They believe my power comes from that trickster, Shor. If he was so clever, then I must be, too. At least as Nords see it.
Out of sight, out of mind. The fools believe they can ward off magic's consequences by pushing it away. And yet, I'm the first person they visit when someone gets sick or they think they see Daedra.

Kyne's breath, I'm about to keel over from hunger and that's all you can think to ask me? I am a thane of Western Skyrim, not some mollycoddled poet from Jorunn's boudoir! \n\nNow begone. Waiting for the feast is hard enough without pointless talk.

Every time I've been invited to Jarl Morryn's cabin, she's prepared a traditional feast for me! This time, I fasted all week just to prepare. But I didn't expect that snowback Hraldi to show up.\n\nI must have been born under a bad star.

No, even though I want to be. Anger would be easier. Maybe that will come later. Grief is a … strange thing, isn't it?\n\nI know my grandfather was just trying to protect me for as long as he could. He always looked out for me.
