For a bit, yes. I think I need to be alone with my thoughts. I will find my way back safely enough — Kyne is with me.\n\nMay she always be with you.

Just like anything else—in battle. I served the Covenant for a while, and I met a sapper who could collapse castle walls with potions.\n\nMade me uncomfortable at first. Just like this lot. But then I started studying and realized its potential.

It did. But not everything used in war is fundamentally destructive. If I could just get my clan to understand the value of it ….\n\nTo be a chief is to be frustrated. All the time. I just hope we can all learn something here.

She's an alchemist. I'm a mine overseer. I think I've got a better handle on how to move stone.\n\nUgh. It was only a matter of time before her pride betrayed us. Guess it's fitting that we both get crushed together down here.
It's worth a try. And for now, it's my only lead.\n\nDo me a favor and keep your ear to the ground. Whatever this mysterious patron means to do with the remains of the Gray Host … it can't be good.

They're not simple like the Giants on the mainland. No, they've got a cunning to them.\n\nSkin's as blue as a frost-bitten toe. And as far as their temper goes? I've met sharks with a kinder disposition.

Not much to it, honestly. A sturdy fort, a fishing village, a rocky coast, and some ruins.\n\nIts value has always been its location. Shoals and old wrecks make sailing out here dangerous. Anyone who means to visit the mainland has to pass by us.

Like I said, he's a vampire … or something near to it.\n\nLegends say he was a pirate. He and his crew set upon a whaling vessel, but when they went below decks to claim their prize, all they found was corpses and bloodfiends.

Of course. Truthfully, I only asked in jest.\n\nI will find recruits in Bangkorai Garrison, Hallin's Stand, perhaps even Evermore. And before I pass on to the Far Shores, I will make sure an incursion like this never happens again. You have my word.

Poisoned them, I'd wager. Some sort of alchemical experimentation. To what end—that's the question.\n\nI just have to believe that Adusa's weathered the effects. She's tough as an Alik'r mule. Even so …. No, she's fine. She has to be.

Depends on what you mean by "her own kind." Not all vampires are created equal.\n\nMost vampires become what they are by contracting a disease. Others though—purebloods—can trace their powers right back to the source. To Molag Bal.

Wouldn't surprise me. Huge underground castle, hordes of minions, obvious megalomania … she fits the type.\n\nThe bad news is purebloods wield far greater power than an average vampire. The good news is … well, I guess there is no good news. Sorry.

Hey. Rude. I asked first. Whatever. I happen to be in search of some lunatic alchemist named Arkasis who's working on some mad scheme with some equally crazy co-conspirators.\n\nHis laboratory is near here. I can smell it.
Then I hope you did more than bash rocks, but I guess so long as the rocks were trying to kill you it'll do.
<You are about to enter a Group Dungeon. Are you ready to leave your current Zone?>

I could ask the same of you. But I don't really care.\n\nThe ruler of this castle, one Lady Thorn, apparently decided to start amassing her own vampiric army. Bad move on her part. I want to know what she's planning, and then stop it.
I went by that castle the last time I visited Skyrim. Seemed like a nice place, if you're into the evil hideout look. Hope you didn't wreck too much of it.
<You are about to enter a Group Dungeon. Are you ready to leave your current Zone?>

The kind that involves grave robbing an ancient evil for nefarious purposes, which comes up more often than I'd like, so now I have to put a stop to Arkasis's experiments.\n\nThat's why I'm here. As for you, I only really need to know if you'll help.

This worm of a fellow found me in Solitude. Insists he just escaped this place and needs to show me what the lady's up to. The problem is, I can't sneak in my usual way with him in tow.\n\nHey, since you're here, feel like helping me storm a castle?
Let me see that. Hmm.\n\nAnother lucrative opportunity. But this time we know where they're leading people. To an isolated inn somewhere in Eastmarch. Did you hear anything else that I need to know?

Yeah. He wagered that someone who braved Coldharbour might be crazy enough to sail straight into a magic storm. He was right, of course. Ha!\n\nI've seen my fair share of gales, Vestige. This one's different, and those witches are to blame.

Well, I can tell you this: this storm Jorunn sent us to investigate? It's not natural. These Icereach witches conjured it up somehow. I don't know why yet, but I'm going to find out. One way or another.
Wait, you mean … they're coming here to talk about a treaty with Eastmarch?\n\nKyne's breath, when?
Then I need my scribes. I need my advisors. I need my chefs to prepare the victuals, I need the legal scholars here, I need … I need ….\n\nI need to sit down.

No. My mother …. The last time we spoke, I hurled a mug at her. But I came when she summoned me, just in time to see her murdered.\n\nI—I need to pull myself together. She asked me to watch over my father … the kingdom. I can't let her down.
My father, listen to me? When horkers fly, maybe, but probably not even then. He gave up on me a long time ago. \n\nI'm sorry. I'm no use to you. No use to anyone.
He was fast, that's for certain. Here and gone before the guards could even draw their swords.\n\nOther than that, I didn't get a good look. The inside of his hood was nothing but shadows.
I'm not my mother. Never will be. But I swear I'll do whatever I can to help you. You have my word on that.

We call it Dusktown. It's the Bitterblade Mining Consortium's settlement. We're not a big organization, there's only about a dozen of us. Most of the work that goes on here is under the table.\n\nWe're a small operation, but sturdy.

Blackreach is a hard place. You spend any amount of time down there and you'll learn that quick. \n\nUnfortunately, some people forget that, and get it in their heads to go exploring. That's usually the last we see of them.

The assassin may have leapt out the window, but he must have had help to get that close to the king and queen. Even Jorunn's guard had traitors willing to help the coven, so why not here, too?\n\nHmm. What was the name of that Orc at the Lonely Troll?

Yeah. Maugh. He's lazy and a drunk, but I don't see him as a backstabber. Svana trusts him. It might put her at ease to have a familiar face around.\n\nThe princess needs someone to lean on right now, and neither of us has time to play nursemaid.
Bah. Who knows?\n\nThe Imperials in Elsweyr fancy themselves Tsaesci, but as far as I can tell, they're just Imperials in silly garments. Ziss on the lot of them!

Snake-men. Never seen one myself, but the Imperials in Hakoshae talk about them like they're gods or something.\n\nIt's nonsense, walker. They're no different from us. Certainly no better. I'm sure you'll prove it soon enough, yes?
Hmm. Some have mentioned old banners fluttering in the breeze up the hill. Could just be trophies from old conquests, but could be something more.\n\nYou can tell me for certain when you return, yes?
It will be a few moments before everything reconfigures itself. They should realign to your time as I depart for my own. \n\nSo, if you have any questions, now would be the time!

Ah, yes. We're the ones who ask questions. You provide the answers, usually in the most destructive manner possible. \n\nI'm afraid I can't be more specific. The fragility of your brain and your understanding of space and time are rattled enough as is.

I'm trying to figure that out myself. One moment I was back in Morrowind, but it was different. Vivec City was a smoking crater. The next I was underwater and struggling to breathe. Then I was falling into a volcano. Then I was here.

Not really. I still have all my limbs. I didn't sprout a tail and my hair is still perfect, thank the Three for that.\n\nThough, I'm not willing to test that. Sometimes you have to write off a place as too dangerous. This is one of those times.
Not much, I'm afraid. Some shapes of people, a few voices. I remember reading a schematic of some kind. It had … no. It's gone.

You did? How odd. I'm sorry. I just can't remember. Ugh, my head. It feels as though someone tried to extract ore from my skull. \n\nThank you for your help, at any rate. Kireth and I will be taking our leave as soon as we remember how to walk.

My pack was forced into servitude by an alliance of vampires and werewolves. Enslaved in a black castle, we toiled alongside others and endured horrible experiments.\n\nIf it wasn't for Tranya and Skor, I would still be there.

An excellent question! \n\nHow to explain … they operate like Dwemer power cores, just on a miniature scale. They generate an extraordinary amount of energy despite their small size. Truly ingenious design! And more than sufficient for my experiment.

Hmm. Think of it as a music conductor's baton.\n\nThe tonal power contained in the miter is overwhelming. Chaotic. The scepter modulates and unifies the tones to make them harmonious, accessible, and safe. Or safer, at any rate.

The power nodes are stored in crystals suspended above the floor. We'll need to find inactive spiders that I can command to scale the walls and dislodge them for us.\n\nOnce we have the nodes and master scepter, we can make our undoubtedly daring exit.

Good idea, but so far the pieces don't tell a complete story.\n\nWe found evidence of the coven luring people with promises of gold so they could experiment on them. Ritual items, vampires, and strange bloodfiends. What does it all mean?

I've seen similar totems, but nothing exactly like that witch pike. It disturbed me just to look at it.\n\nIt appears to be a key component to their ritual, though the Skald-King's mages will determine that for certain.

The Icereach Coven consists of witches and warriors of the Reach loyal to their cause. I never saw a connection to vampires before. Maybe the blood-suckers are hired help?\n\nCome on. Hopefully we'll learn more when we get to the Grinning Horker.
You saw what I saw. Those feral creatures were near some of the ritual sites. And each site appeared to be a slightly different version of the ritual.\n\nLike they're trying to perfect it.
You—you think … would the high king really … but I'm a loyal subject ….\n\nNo more talk. I need to get Sonolia off the street.
Yeah … yeah. It's not like I opened the gate and let him slink off. The real problem's at the palace.\n\nNo more questions. I've got to secure the gate and take care of poor Sonolia.

Right. To research the ritual. Go find them and see what you can learn. I'll stay with Svana. Bring her up to speed on everything we've uncovered. We're going to need her to get the high king to trust us.\n\nAnd I'm calling him Fenn. It's simpler.
It … it must have been Chief Urzikh's potions. They dissolve stone quicker than the eye can follow, but the risks far outweigh the benefits.\n\nThat stuff is dangerous! It has no place in our mine.
No, but it was only a matter of time! You can only play with fire for so long until it lashes out and burns you. \n\nThis was inevitable.

Well, there's no shortage of rare materials, that's for sure. But most of what we find is an abundance of creatures that want to sink their teeth into us. \n\nIt's dangerous work, but everyone who signed on knew the risks going in.

Wandered off and got eaten, more like. Either that or the darkness got to them, the isolation, the lack of sun. \n\nWe've learned how to stay safe down here, but you can't protect people from everything. Especially not their own minds.

Yes, but you'll do well to remember that the mines are strictly off-limits to anyone who isn't under my employ. If you're looking for work, come find me once you run off those ghost-hunting buffoons.\n\nUntil then, I recommend you keep your distance.

My particular habits aside, one of us needs to find the assassin and the other needs to alert Lyris Titanborn. I can handle the latter.\n\nBesides, I have no intention entering Solitude. A courier should have no trouble picking Lyris out of a crowd.
Good. Less chance of them scurrying away if they think they have the advantage. I'm tired of chasing these rats through the shadows.\n\nAre you ready to end this?

Most of the legends are superstitious nonsense. It was once supposedly ruled by the Dwarves, though. If that's true, we'll see their ruins.\n\nThere are also a lot of tales about monsters. Pale, feral humanoids. Giant insects. Be on your guard.

We can cover more ground that way. And lone travelers are less conspicuous than a large group. Plus, if one of us gets into trouble, the others can come to the rescue.\n\nJust stay close to the town. We don't want to become totally separated down here.

Hopefully they were able to hold the courtyard and keep those monsters out of the city. You go and check on them. I need to collect myself. \n\nSolitude needs Princess Svana now, and I'm not quite ready to be her.

A patrol found a strange stick outside of town. It was covered in runes and a smelly paste. The jarl ordered us to destroy it and any others we could find.\n\nAnother patrol ran into Reachmen at the barrow, but that was all we heard from them.

Come to think of it, the runes could have been Reach. Those witch people use stuff like that all the time. I'm just worried about the swordthane and the other soldiers at the barrow.\n\nNothing good ever comes of Reach magic.
I wouldn't do her any good. I'm an expert on going backwards and standing still. Svana's moving forward. She needs a friend who's going the same way.\n\nThat's you, I'd wager.

You mean those fools setting up their ghost traps? They're harmless. And if they make the superstitious miners feel better, I'm all right with that.\n\nElle and Overseer Urlvar have been nothing but fair and honest with all of us.

Elle Bitterblade. She owns the consortium. Urlvar's her husband and our overseer. They built Dusktown to support their claim.\n\nThey're savvy business folk. Secretive, but that goes with the territory when you break a new mine.

Same as most of us, I reckon. I saw a posting in a tavern, talked to an agent, signed some papers, and here I am. Well, after they blindfolded me and walked me all over snow and creation.\n\nThe work is hard, but the wages are excellent!

I couldn't get much out of Brun, but it seems wolves attacked Havil's farm over to the west. \n\nHe claims the beasts were only bones and covered in ice. I'm not inclined to believe him. People here tend to view the truth through their mead.

Excellent. The people of Morthal are basically good, they just let their imaginations run wild. Learning the truth of this attack could help curb any future issues with the wolves.\n\nI'll check on Brun at the tavern. His shivering concerns me.

Wolf packs do roam around the outskirts of town. Occasionally they'll snatch away a chicken or goat. But attacking groups of people is unusual.\n\nTell you what — could you go to the farm and get the truth? There would be coin in it for you.

What a curious question. This whole place was tailor made for undesirables. Tunnels, sunken barrows, Dwarven ruins … lots of secluded spots.\n\nBut don't worry. We're the only ones down here. Elle's precautions make sure of that.
Good. I won't be but a moment.

Many things. Is this a spell or a curse? Where does it get its power? Magic holds unique patterns, like footprints in the snow. If it's known to me, perhaps you can track the source.\n\nBut first, I must extract this knowledge.

We held the gate as long as we could, but the harrowfiends were a flood of claws and teeth. Once they burst through, Lyris cleaved through them like a scythe through wheat, but even she couldn't stem the tide.

I … I'm not really sure. I kind of went wild. Let out my inner beast, as it were. I was rending and slashing. Then Lyris whacked me with the flat of her blade. At least, that's the last thing I remember.\n\nNot my finest hour, but we survived.

Sadly, I don't think there's any hope for them. Their life energy was sucked dry, turning them into feral beasts. Restoring them is beyond my capabilities, I'm afraid.\n\nAt least with the harrowed, they're not so far gone as to be a lost cause.
Fenn can handle that. I'm sure he'll want to talk to her again after everything we found here.\n\nYou go play diplomat. You're the only one of us who's any good at it.
A parent's betrayal cuts deeper than a sword. But Svana's strong. Stronger than she's been given credit for.\n\nAnd Solitude's going to need that strength in the coming days.

We did our best to hold the harrowfiends inside Castle Dour, but nothing short of stone walls were going to keep those monsters from pushing through. Seemed like every one I killed was replaced by two more.

Answers, I hope. That's the mission I agreed to for Jorunn the Skald-King, after all.\n\nThe witches of the Icereach Coven are definitely up to something, tempting unsuspecting folk with promises of gold. We saw what happened at those ritual sites.

Lured to a desolate region of Eastmarch, most likely to be subjected to more of those strange rituals? If that doesn't shout danger, I don't know what does.\n\nWill you accompany me, my friend? I'd appreciate your help in this matter.

Almost didn't. We were nearly overrun before Fenn went wild. I've never seen him like that! Snarling and showing what a true vampire can do. Took the harrowfiends by surprise and we routed them.\n\nI did have to thwack him to clear his head, though.

Kilkreath Temple provides a safe haven for the priests and pilgrims of Meridia. At least, it did. Before this terrible storm struck.\n\nThe Lady of Light has always protected us. Why today should be different, I don't understand.

It's as much a surprise to me as anyone. I'll admit my last report was pretty bleak, and I haven't had a chance to send another since we rescued Fenn.\n\nBut I never advised Jorunn to march into Solitude.

We saved Solitude, but our war with the Gray Host is far from over. We need Fenn's elixir more than ever. With that, and King Jorunn's help, we might just push these monsters back into their grave for good.\n\nCheck on Fenn's progress, please.

Possibly, but I wouldn't have taken Captain Ageran for a deserter. \n\nIf you're helping those ghost hunters, would you take a look in the offices? My people are scared … I'd like to have a working theory to give them, at least.
That depends on Fenn. If there's anything standing in his way, let me know and I'll do everything in my power to get him what he needs.
I'm going to invite the Skald-King to join us. If the people of Solitude see him bow his head along with the rest of us, they may not care about the divide between the east and west.

I need to get back to the Eversnow and gather the survivors. Take them to Solitude. Where they'll be safe. At least, as safe as we can make them.\n\nThen I have to have a serious talk with my father. I'll make him listen to me, damn it, no matter what.

A cure! Tzinghalis's research on the netherroot showed me just how it weakens the connection between a body and soul. Thus far we've been able to inure a person to the root, but now I'm certain I can use that knowledge to heal those weakened bonds.
Well, it is still just a theory at this point. There's a lot more testing and experimentation to be done before we can produce a viable antidote. Weeks, optimistically.

I know. I know. We can't simply put things on hold. Mjolen and I have a batch brewing right now and materials to keep producing for another day. Ingurt's promised us a steady supply of Arkay's oil, but that's not our limiting factor.

We can ransack Gray Host stockpiles or mount an expedition into Blackreach. Otherwise, it would take decades of work to produce a proper crop.\n\nAfter we get the elixir squared away, we'll turn our attention to curing the harrowed.
This is an institution of Elves. They know nothing of the soul of the world. Here magic is a thing to be measured and weighed. Mages know. They do not feel.

Jarl Olfwenn rules the hold, which was established to provide a defensible border against the Reach. If any of the western holds can deal with this threat, it's Karthald.\n\nBut first, I have one more thing to discuss with Jarl Reddharn ….

Necessity and a hope they can learn. If we're to brew enough elixir for everyone in the kingdom, it will take all the herb-grinders in the holds. Here, at least, they know how to use a mortar and pestle.
Not the best news, but I'll take it. So long as we have enough to protect our soldiers, we have a fighting chance against the Gray Host. I'll go to the Undergrove myself if that's what it takes.

Now that would be cause for celebration. If he can really bring back even a fraction of those we lost to the harrowstorms, I'm willing to try.\n\nThat's all I needed to hear. We should begin the ceremony before the crowd grows more restless.
Trying to get things up and running again. We're still searching for a shipwright to make the necessary repairs on the Silver Cormorant, but her sailing days are far from over.
We'll have a proper funeral for our lost crew when we return home. Eventually, we'll refit and continue our work … a little older and wiser, I suppose.
We will attempt to seal the temple and purge the corruption.\n\nIf it were up to me, I would leave it in ruins.
You know, the College has bonded together once again because of you? We won't soon forget it. Or maybe we will. We're bards after all. Truth is sometimes sacrificed on the altar of entertainment.

Our town is lost. I've heard stories of towns left empty and untouched after fire, sickness, or storm. I don't see Karthwatch's fate being any different.\n\nAs for the hold? I suspect the Reachmen take control. There's no one left to fight back.

I must find a new home for my brothers and sisters of Karthwatch. My brother, Fenrar, spoke to Jarl Reddharn. It may be that we settle in Morthal. I think Bjora would prefer the high walls of Solitude, though. Wherever we go, we'll stick together.
Rada al-Saran is still out there and, eventually, he might try something like this again.\n\nSolitude may be safe, for now, but wherever he strikes next may not share the same fortune.

We've been told to hold position and monitor the Gray Host's activities. Though I'd wager you've done most of the heavy lifting already. It'll very nearly be a bit of holiday after everything else that's happened.

Once we help the people of Solitude get back on their feet I imagine we'll go back to Blackreach. Though our initial investigation didn't reveal anything supernatural there is still much to uncover and explore. I do not believe our work here is over.

Claudina seems intent on going back to Blackreach. After we help the poor people of this place rebuild, we'll head there. 


Spirits may not have been the culprits of what happened in Dusktown, but that doesn't mean they aren't down there!
We've enjoyed much progress, thanks to you. The clan is stronger than ever before and our petty squabbles are done away with.\n\nIt's far from perfect, but at least we're working together now.

Change is slow, but sure. Our problems are not the kind that can be fixed overnight, but your actions helped many of us find compromise. Mor Khazgur will be stronger than it ever was now that we are not busy fighting amongst ourselves.

My thirst for adventure was sated during our time in Lightless Hollow, I assure you. After we help the people here, I fully intend to give Telline a few years of uneventful bliss. Maybe we'll start for Summerset again, who knows?
If I can convince Viggol, I'd like to take him to Summerset. I fear he'll get bored with nothing to do, but perhaps you really did cure him of his appetite for adventuring.
Well enough. They're tired, but managing. I think everyone here feels the same.\n\nLooks like we could all use a drink. Luckily, Ena's here to help.

Boosting morale, of course. With the mess in Dragon Bridge cleaned up, I've been getting my regular shipments again. Which means mead, and a lot of it.\n\nI may not be much good at rebuilding, but I know how to keep cups flowing.

Better without those Reach bastards crawling through our tunnels like rats. The bridge still stands, thanks to you, and with the strain taken off our operation and the garrison, we're free to help out around here.

As funny as it is to say … out of place. I spent so long in exile. I'm happy to be home. Mother has been so kind to me … but there is much I need to mend with her. With my father.\n\nBut I'm here, thanks to you. We all are, as I hear.
Freiwen's return is a blessing. Some have just … taken longer to understand that. Sadly, there are no balms for broken trust.

Aye, for a few hours at least. Seeing you beat the brine out of those Half-Giants lifted the spirits of every man, woman, and child in Kyne's Aegis.\n\nYou lit a fire in our bellies, friend, and we're ready to fight!

We call this bit of the island the Span. Small mining outposts, mostly. Had a brief gold rush here a few years back. Nothing came of it, but some prospectors never quit, you know?\n\nWord of advice: keep an eye on the sky.

After the Icereach Coven's attack on the Skald-King, we determined they also had plans for Western Skyrim. Jorunn's warnings have been ignored, so he sent Brondold to get the lay of the land and me to persuade Svargrim.\n\nYou can see how that's going.

In all honesty, they can't stand each other. But King Jorunn doesn't want the coven to topple Western Skyrim. That would be bad for the east as well as the west.\n\nBesides, Jorunn was hoping to use this as an opportunity to improve relations.

I'll be staying so long as Jorunn's here or until I can persuade him to send me after Rada al-Saran. That leech owes a lot of blood to us and I intend to squeeze it out of him.\n\nWe have to find him first.
If Princess Svana agrees, I want to bring more of my people from Eastmarch to help restore Solitude and the western holds. My retinue is too small to deal with everything. We need more hands!

Today? No, the time isn't right. As for the future, who can say? Svargrim was never interested in finding a path to reconciliation.\n\nPrincess Svana isn't her father, that much is clear. So, I suppose I can hope, hmm?
This business with the Gray Host is far from over. As long as Skyrim is threatened, I will be close by to lend a hand.

I do. She's an impressive young woman. Is Western Skyrim ready for Svana? That's the more pertinent question.\n\nSolitude shuns the outside world while Svana reaches for it. We'll have to see how that works out in the end.

I have no desire to replace a despot. Haven't these people suffered enough?\n\nIn any event, my forces are stretched too thin to take on much more. If the people request help, however, I will put whatever resources I can at their disposal.

So I've heard. The princess … has come a long way from the girl I met so long ago. And I've changed, as well. I'm not quite as obnoxious and close-minded as I was when my father first formed the Ebonheart Pact.\n\nAt least, I try not to be.
There are many dark secrets in Blackreach that simmer beneath the surface. My clan was unfortunately the victim of such evil.
Skor and Tranya got me out. We made our way here, and discovered the Grotto.

Blood thirsty thralls and pale walking corpses that crept from the ground at night. They swarmed us, dragging us below the surface into the depths of Blackreach. We were forced into slavery to unseen overlords at a nightmarish black castle.
Priests and pilgrims of Meridia. They must have sought shelter in the temple before this terrible fate befell them.\n\nIf only they had been able to make it inside.
That's perfect. He can defend the villagers with Helsi while we find Bjora. I'll show them the way there and rejoin you.\n\nSwift hunting, stranger.

Truthfully, I cannot say. We found safety in the cave, but the storm struck the temple head on. I am more and more certain that the unnatural event was magical in nature, so anything is possible.\n\nBut Meridia would protect this place, wouldn't she?

Does it really matter? Every historian worth his salt winds up trapped in an illusion at some point. Very common. And thus, not worthy of discussion or commitment to record.\n\nI will say, though—as magical traps go, Maelmoth's wards are top tier.

Steal? We're adventurers, aren't we? What you call stealing, I call daring investigation.\n\nMaelmoth's works contain a wealth of secrets. If we don't pursue them, some other historian will. I, for one, have no interest in sharing the glory with—uhm.

Ugh. Illusion magic extends far beyond simple parlor tricks and mirages. Skilled practitioners exert power over the mind itself!\n\nIntellectually, I know I am not a bottle. But the spell fooled some primitive aspect of my psyche into believing I am.

My people need me. There are still those who endure countless horrors at Greymoor Keep. I want to be there for them when they escape.\n\nAnd I vow to better understand this werewolf vampire alliance so I can help put an end to all this suffering.

Ena White-Eye. Maybe caravan agent is too formal a title. I suppose you would call her a smuggler. She deals in black-market goods.\n\nAfter Solitude stopped responding, she agreed to supply the garrison. I don't like it, but she's been a godsend.

That's been a recent development, but yes. Without supplies from either legitimate sources or otherwise, the garrison's days are numbered. And Ena has been nothing but helpful. Dragon Bridge is her home as well as ours.

The cure will take time to spread, but once it starts the effect will quicken. Hopefully a few more of our fallen friends will return to us. \n\nIt won't be easy by any means, but now that we can cure the infection, we have a way to move forward.

Our kingdom consists of three holds. Haafingar, Hjaalmarch, and Karthald. I need to warn them.\n\nThe jarls might listen, even if my father won't. I'm the daughter of the high king, after all. Time to start acting like one. Will you come with me?

Ah, you want me to reveal one of House Ravenwatch's greatest secrets. Well, that isn't going to happen.\n\nLet's just say that Fenn and I—all of the Ravenwatch, really—have a way to communicate and leave it at that.

Obviously, Fennorian's elixir is key to protecting Solitude from the harrowstorm. He has to make enough to distribute, and he has to do it quickly without making the slightest mistake.\n\nThat's a responsibility he won't take lightly.

Wait for orders from the Ravenwatch. I'll get a new assignment, eventually. Maybe one that includes Fennorian, if I'm lucky!\n\nSooner rather than later, I hope. I think I'm actually starting to like it down here.

Harrowed? Is that what we're calling them?\n\nWell, not that it's your concern, but High King Svargrim ordered us to herd these poor sods into the Temple of the Divines so the priests can care for them. If you ask me, they're a lost cause.
Absolutely not. I've seen what a spirit like howlwater can do in the hands of a Nord like Rigurt.\n\nMy clan is still rebuilding their longhouse. No sale.
Fine. For Wrothgar's sake. But you only get a bottle. With a whole cask, Rigurt might just burn down the countryside.\n\nMalacath take me. I hope I don't regret this.

Politics, I suppose. Look, we've never been a high priority for the capital city, but this total disregard is a new low, even for Solitude. It's like the high king's court has more important matters to attend to. I do what I can, but it's never easy.

Besides being an important lumber town, Dragon Bridge serves as the crossroads for the northern region. We're the first line of defense for Solitude and the neighboring holds.\n\nThough in our current state, I'm not sure how much good we can do.
You trying to steal my formula or something? Ha, I'll never tell.\n\nFermenting it in a mound of mammoth dung helps give it its distinctive smell, but the rest is a trade secret.

What can I say? Ena isn't the kind of person who likes to be tied down to just one place. Besides, she likes to watch as her river shipments come in.\n\nI also use her as a lookout. I don't have enough soldiers to keep an eye on every approach.
Ena's a thorn in my side on the best of days … but you're right, she's become a vital part of the community. \n\nAs much as we bark at each other, I rely on her. I hope she's safe.

Have you forgotten that Rigurt is Windhelm's most accomplished cultural ambassador?  He makes friends everywhere, and learns as much as possible about each place he visits!\n\nEspecially when it concerns their food and beverages!
Oof! It is as strong as Rigurt remembers. Good!\n\nRigurt used his contacts at Solitude's port to get his hands on some Rimmen cane-spice and a special secret ingredient. Now we are ready to cook!

I don't know. I truly don't. But my heart tells me it ends with their death.\n\nI heard a great crash of thunder and felt a rumble underfoot. He's working some magic in there, friend. Eight help us if he succeeds.

Ulang serves as Ena's right hand. And he's her partner in life, too. The only reason they're not married is because they're both too stubborn to settle down.\n\nUlang's her muscle, but he's got a brain, too. And he's a good man.

Ugh. I'd almost forgotten how cheeky you are.\n\nI might have torn one of the pages. Honestly, you'd barely notice. But you know how librarians are. Spill a drink, or talk too loudly, or rip a few pages and wham! They cast you out on your ear.

For a smuggler and black marketeer, he's honorable. He refuses to deal in anything harmful. Without him, Ena would walk a darker path. She's impulsive, brash.\n\nUlang, on the other hand, is thoughtful. Considerate, even. I suppose I do like the man.

Yes. Most of the Khajiit died early, but that Adusa weathered it without so much as a whimper.\n\nEssenia mentioned a laboratory beyond the arboretum. She said something about completing the transformation there. That's all I know. Now, let me go!

A prickly Argonian named Deem-Vilax. She works in the Mages Guild library in Solitude.\n\nYou lack my ample charisma, it's true, but you do radiate a certain degree of authority. I'm confident you can talk her out of the journal.

Vund took him. He's keeping Ulang close to ensure my cooperation. Which makes this all the more urgent. You need to warn the captain, stop Vund from igniting his reagent, and save Ulang before the bridge is destroyed.

I admit it. I'm a smuggler. I try to deal locally, but Dragon Bridge was desperate. They needed supplies and I had exhausted my usual sources.\n\nLook, food, mead, and other goods from Markarth usually don't come with a contingent of Reach marauders!

When I first met Vund, he presented himself as a mercantile agent, just like me. Turns out, he's an alchemist and warlord, the leader of this band of Reach marauders.\n\nHe used me to get close enough to Dragon Bridge to carry out his awful plan.

The barbarians reacted poorly when we destroyed the strange witch sticks. We beat them back and chased them into the nearby barrow, but that was the last I heard from my soldiers.\n\nSince you dealt with this before, would you investigate the barrow?

I'm afraid it's impossible. I had my doubts about meeting a delegate from Windhelm in the first place. Thane Svyne being here only confirms that my skepticism was warranted. \n\nHe is an obscene boor, and I will not speak with him for any reason.

Had. She was taken from us five years ago. If I had pushed her harder, she might have had the strength to survive. Daughters are a father's greatest weakness.\n\nEnough troubles of the past. We have the present to concern ourselves with.

Ugh. Do you work with that strutting guar, Narsis Dren? The famed scholar? Scholar, my shedding tail-scales.\n\nHe tore a page in a valuable book, and I suspect he stole one of Maelmoth's scrolls. What reason could I possibly have to help you?

Quite a coincidence that two people come calling for the same rare text on the same day. Then again, helping one of Narsis Dren's competitors does warm my scales.\n\nFine. The journal's there on the table. But if any harm comes to it, I will find out.

Scoundrels like Narsis always try to buy their way out of problems. Then again, a repair like this is costly. Hmph. Very well. It's there on the table.\n\nTell that scaleless idiot that if I find out he stole a scroll, he will be sorry.

Here I am, revealing all my secrets. I hope the town appreciates it after all this.\n\nLook, the side entrances are sort of like bolt holes. Not the safest path, but quick in a pinch or if the river is running particularly high.

Excellent! I must admit, I had my doubts, but you're turning out to be a model employee … er, assistant. Partner? Whatever.\n\nNow, if you'd just hand it over, I can try to untangle Maelmoth's riddles and set us on the right path.

Feh! She would. This text reveals Maelmoth's Mysterium! His trove to arcane trinkets and treasures!\n\nNow just give me a moment to … yes, I have it. This clearly refers to a meditation grotto near Kilkreath. One of Shalidor's old haunts.
Thanks to the Skald-King's wizards, it should lead us to magic similar to what's contained in the jewelry. Icereach magic.\n\nJust take it out and give it a try.

Oh, Rigurt has no say. Someplace far away, most likely. Where the Nord Cultural Exchange can do the most good.\n\nRigurt did hear the Skald-King mumble something about the distant reaches of Oblivion. Or was it the depths of the Alik'r desert?
I'll let you in on a little secret from Whiterun. If Nords ever conducted negotiations while completely sober, nothing would get done.
They better. \n\nWhat happened here will be hard to ignore. They might not tell stories of your bravery, but I think they'll send us what we need. And for the rest, we have Ena.

No. I think this whole ordeal taught her a valuable lesson. Gods … at least I hope it did. Besides, she loves Dragon Bridge as much as I do. She's part of our community. And I always make use of every resource at my disposal.\n\nNow, thanks again.

First chance I get.\n\nI was a fool to leave this ruin unexplored. The old Dragon Priests kept a lot of secrets—all bad. You have my word that as long as I draw breath, no one will ever step foot in this accursed place again.

Oh, the usual inanities of frumpy book hoarders.\n\nI might have torn one of the pages. Honestly, you'd barely notice. But you know how librarians are. Spill a drink, or talk too loudly, or rip a few pages and wham! They cast you out on your ear.

Hmph. A prickly Argonian named Deem-Vilax. She works in the Mages Guild library in Solitude.\n\nI might have said a few … indecorous things about her beady little eyes. My fault. But people who stand in the way of discovery really get my dander up!
You'll find me very partial to answering them. Ask away, dear adventurer.

My name is Neramo—the foremost Dwemeric scholar in Tamriel! \n\nI have devoted my life to the study of the Dwemer, and have risked life and limb to do so. Researching Dwemer technology can be quite perilous, hence the need for an assistant.

Some scholars believe the Dwemer were able to communicate with one another over vast distances through fascinating headwear called miters. \n\nI happen to have one in my possession, and I plan to activate it with the power nodes.

Oh, a little of this, a little of that. Traversing more Dwemer ruins in the pursuit of knowledge and discovery, tinkering with artifacts … keeping myself out of trouble for the most part. \n\nI'm quite pleased our paths have crossed again, assistant.

Scraps. A coarse sobriquet for an astounding ruin! My research indicates the Dwemer used this place as a manufactory, crafting all manner of animunculi, from tiny spiders to hulking centurions!\n\nAlas, someone has made a mess of it.

Forced to conscript civilians to do the work of the garrison? What a sorry state we've been reduced to.\n\nWell, who am I to look a gift guar in the mouth? If you're willing to help, then I'm willing to make it worth your while.

We haven't heard from Solitude for awhile, so I have an agent acquiring supplies for us from other sources. They never arrive. Later, we find the wagons, ransacked and the traders missing.\n\nIf you can find the caravan, that would be a big help.

Certainly not after what you've done to them here. They'd be licking their wounds for months if I didn't intend to make sure none of the remaining survive.\n\nThe time of the Dragon Cult is long over. They should be thanking us for reminding them.

Humiliating. Reduced to a child's plaything! I never thought I'd sink so low.\n\nOh, and dreadfully boring, too. All I could do was stare at the wall and think about how much I hated it! And there were so many itches I could not scratch.

Oh, fine. \n\nThink of me as a powerful, stunningly beautiful enforcer of justice. I see evil in the world and I eradicate it as I see fit. My methods could be viewed as unsavory by some, but perhaps the same could be said of you.

Gain an audience with Jarl Olfwenn and convince her that the harrowstorm threat is real. Her and mother never got along, so I don't expect a warm welcome. But she's a pragmatic woman. I hope she'll take our warning seriously.

It wasn't easy! Claudina built her business herself. After her husband died, she used his fortune to pursue her studies, and has been on her own ever since. \n\nBut I think she saw the benefit in a pair of young hands, and an eager mind.

I don't possibly have the time to tell you of her many amazing exploits!\n\nClaudina is a renowned figure when it comes to the study of the supernatural. She's had a lustrous career and published much of her work, you should read some! She's my hero.

I'll never forget those beady, rat's eyes for the rest of my life. Was he behind this too?\n\nI'm going to split that jack-tooth's, Reach-born, whore-son's arse with my boot until he's on Old Knocker's doorstep!
I—I know. I just ….\n\nForget him. Karthwatch is more important than that mangy dog. Let's keep moving.

Yes. I was preparing to study the enchantments I detected upon it when the harrowstorm struck. I guess I slipped it into my pocket without really thinking about it.\n\nCould this be some sort of protection against the storm?
Return to Solitude. Find Lyris and meet me in the Blue Palace. I have a room upstairs that we can use.\n\nWe need to come up with a plan. Something that will help me convince my father to act.

Careful, outsider. We don't take kindly to that kind of attitude when it's directed at our high king. If you want to know so badly, go ask your precious princess.\n\nNow leave us to our work before I decide to herd you right to the dungeons.
Damn it, I was afraid of that. We're running out of time and we still don't fully understand what we're facing out there.\n\nHey, where's the princess? Tell me you didn't lose Svana in Karthwatch.

I don't dare to dream that I might communicate with the lost Dwemer themselves. \n\nBut if I can unravel the secrets of the miter, I may find myself closer than any scholar has ever been to discovering the nature of their disappearance.

Hmph. Forgotten already? I was the youngest swordthane ever named, when High King Svartr dubbed me. No one could stand against me in all of Haafingar.\n\nI suppose being jailed all those years has thinned my reputation along with my bones.

When that bastard Svargrim took the throne, he said I looked more like a spinster than a swordthane. So I proved him otherwise.\n\nI shouldn't have knocked out so many teeth, I suppose. He might have taken my point more in stride.

My father hasn't listened to a word I've said since I was old enough to talk. But with mother gone, someone has to make him see reason.\n\nShe tried to teach me, you know. But I never paid attention. I guess I'm more like my father than I thought.

Honestly? I don't know. But Jarl Reddharn tempers his warrior nature with a kindness not often seen in people of his stature.\n\nBesides, he's always had a soft spot for me, ever since his daughter and I played together at moots and other gatherings.
Train. Eat. Drink. Probably drink some more. But don't worry. I'll be ready when the Skald-King gives the word. Then we'll move against the Icereach Coven.\n\nYou have my word on that.

Not so fast, friend. Western Skyrim doesn't exactly get along with Eastern Skyrim. Politics can be a tricky business, so I tend to leave that to the politicians.\n\nWhen King Jorunn gives the word, then we go. Not before.
Thank you. These belonged to <<1>> and <<2>>. I wish we could have saved them, but at least we can use these to remember them.\n\nI doubt we can recover their remains before the temple is sealed.
With Meridia's Brilliance. I'm not sure my faith is strong enough to use it after all this, but I suppose I have to try. I owe that much to High Priest Varkour's memory.\n\nDo you have the relic?
The way things are going? Sometime when I'm old and gray. More likely, when Prince Irnskar takes the throne. My engineers tell me they're working as fast as they can.\n\nLiars, every one of them!

Besides being a courageous idiot … he's the greatest man I've ever known. He's proud, whip-smart, and surprisingly fit for his age. But he ignores his own limitations far too often. Now that he's getting older, I worry for his health.
It seems unintuitive, I know. But I've snuck into enough castles to know there's always another route. A postern door, if we're lucky. A sewage pipe if we're not.\n\nI'm feeling lucky. How about you?

Nothing solid, but I do know that a lot of the gray reliquaries that were smuggled into Western Skyrim found their way here. Might have something to do with those harrowstorm rituals you and Fennorian discovered.

Ah yes. A reference to his passing fancy with poetry and romance. Was Maelmoth a cunning illusionist? Yes. Was he a master wordsmith? Hardly.\n\nI don't know about the flowers, but this bit about Lady of the Winter Winds likely points to Kyne.

He's the type who experiments because he can without ever asking if he should. Got him chased out of several holds. He disappeared not long after, but there were rumors he was conducting his questionable research somewhere far from prying eyes.

Yes. The Nords' storm goddess. I'm not aware of any connections between Kyne and flowers, but an ancient shrine dedicated to her lies southwest of here, near Chillwind Depths. I'll mark it on your map.\n\nMeet me there, all right?

Lovely. Pickle and I are glad to have you. Right, boy?\n\nAh, I think he's found an odor of interest. He's quite the tracker, you know. Follow that scent, Pickle! Lead on and we shall endeavor to keep pace!

You ran into Telline, did you? A good woman, but the older I get the more she worries. I'll admit I'm not as young as I used to be, but can I not have this one last adventure?\n\nI've made my decision. Come along if you like, but don't try to stop me.

That's what I've been saying! I've never seen the lass's brow so wrinkled. Svana's face will furrow like a wheat field if she keeps it up.\n\nShe should reclaim her seat in the tavern and stop trying to get closer to the throne.

What do you think I've been doing? I've gone from trusted companion to courier, and now she's running me ragged! Even an Orc has his limits!\n\nTell Svana to meet at the Troll before she reaches hers.

That's the most reasonable request I've received all day!\n\nWell, it has been an honor to serve. I shall ensure that the Troll, fine establishment that it is, remains in business until her return. Cheers!

I fail to see how flowers have anything to do with these sconces. Probably a red herring. Very common in this sort of riddle. But don't let me stop you!\n\nTruthfully, I could use a break from all this foolishness.
Good. And you know … Thanks.\n\nI wish my master, Verandis, was here. But with you by my side, I still feel like victory is possible.
No telling what's crawling around in here. Fight well, all right? Go.

You forget that I have help now. My father might be able to ignore me, but he'll have a harder time dismissing a jarl and a court mage.\n\nIt's funny. I would have thought he'd be happy to see me finally take an interest in politics.

I don't care about his approval, but I'd like to earn his respect.\n\nWith mother gone, we're both going to have to work harder to keep our kingdom running. It will be easier if we find a way to get along.
I need to get my axe sharpened before we go back down into Blackreach. Don't wait for me. I'll catch up with you in Dusktown.
You go on ahead. I need to get my axe sharpened before I go back down into Blackreach.\n\nI'll catch up with you in Dusktown.

The Skald-King doesn't hide! I have made a tactical retreat into a place of solitude and reflection. Even my patience for the demands of the court has its limits.\n\nI'll go back to deal with the needs of my kingdom soon enough.

You see? Chief Urzikh is just as much to blame! She should have explained this alchemy properly! She should have eased our work schedules! I ….\n\nWe can argue about who's right later. Right now, we need to focus on getting out of the mine.

Punishing Mazog will set an example, and it's what the clan expects. We follow the Code for a reason. But showing mercy might set us on a new path—one with less anger and distrust.\n\nYou're an ally to this clan now. What do you think?
Good … good. At least there's that. \n\nUrlvar, you foolish man, what have you done?

Well, at least we have more knowledge than we did. He won't get far once I send my guards after him, I can promise you that. \n\nFirst priority is to deal with my idiot husband. Maybe we'll use him as bait.

Doors, eh? Perhaps we're finally nearing the end of this.\n\nYes, I see now. This final line about feline faith? It's a clear reference to Sabre Cat's Leap—a rocky precipice southwest of Morthal. I don't know of any doors there, though.

Ugh. You're probably right. I'll tell you this, though: if these illusory doors lead to nowhere, I will be very put out.\n\nOnly one way to know for sure. Make your way to Sabre Cat's Leap. I'll meet you there.

Caught your interest, did it? Maybe you're the person I need after all. Maybe Kyne decided to send me a blessing instead of a curse, for once in my damned life.\n\nAll you need to know about the Pale Man is that it takes people. It took my brother.
Good. Then, what do you recommend, clan-friend?

Some say that. Most claim it doesn't exist at all. My father claimed that, and my mother, and the Swordthane of Morthal. They all said a bear took Drendek. They said a little traumatized boy imagined the Pale Man, made up stories.\n\nHe's not a story.

Drendek, yes. My older brother, strong and hearty. A Nord's Nord!\n\nI thought there was no one in the world stronger than Drendek. Of course, I was only six at the time. Then, the Pale Man snatched Drendek up like a babe.

I hunt the Pale Man. I've been hunting the cursed thing for thirty years, but it's like a ghost. Comes in snowstorms every ten or so years, takes who it wants in a spree of abductions, then vanishes again.\n\nEvery time it comes back, I get closer.

The Pale Man took their loved ones, as it has taken so many over the years. These people are witnesses, so I need to know what they saw.\n\nI can't return whoever they lost, but I can track the thing down and kill it.

A bad fall. While exploring a cave out on the northern coast, looking for signs of the Pale Man, when I ran right into a nest of frostbite spiders.\n\nI got out the cave, but slipped and fell down a hill. Damn near crawled back to Dragon Bridge.

You ever try crawling from the northern coast to Dragon Bridge? It took damn near three days!\n\nBy the time I got back my wounds were infected, or so the healer said. Legs haven't worked right since. I can walk, but I can't run. Damned inconvenient.

Glad to hear Aerolf is still above ground. I thought his obsession had finally killed him.\n\nYeah, I saw the Pale Man. My sister and I were ranging far north of Solitude, out along the coast. That night, we made camp with a plan to head back at dawn.

Late, after I fell asleep. Merlyth's scream woke me. I rushed out of the tent and saw it stalking away, carrying her. She was … her neck was twisted. Backward.\n\nI gave chase, but it was quick. Slipped into the shadows without a trail.

Taller than any man I've seen. But thin, like a draugr, so I know it wasn't a giant. And paler than a belly of a cave fish.\n\nLook, Merlyth and I never really liked each other. So I don't care if you find it. But hopefully this helps Aerolf.
Of course I do! But what kind of historian would I be if I robbed my assistants of the opportunity to achieve great things on their own?\n\nNow, enough accusations! You have a puzzle to solve.

Well then, that changes it. I used to think that man had lost his senses. Then, the Pale Man killed my Bear. Now I understand.\n\nBefore you ask, Bear was my hound. He mostly just slept and smelled bad, but he was all I had after my husband died.

You have been busy, my friend. Then there's nothing left for us to do out here. Let's return to the Blue Palace in Solitude and see if our efforts were worth the risk.\n\nYou go on ahead. I'll meet you there.

Because I saw it! Bear and I were tracking horkers on the coast, over the mountain north of Solitude. When night fell, we made camp.\n\nBear's yelp woke me. I expected to see a giant. Instead I saw the Pale Man dragging away my poor dog.

What do you think? I rushed into my tent and got my axe. When I came out, they were gone. Searched through the night, but the storm was thick as stew and I can't track like Bear. That monster took my dog. My good dog.\n\nBear deserved better.

More than likely. If they want to get information out of him, death might be preferable to whatever tortures they have planned.\n\nLet's get to it. You find this Edjar and I'll see if the locals saw what happened here.
A clue? Very well …. Uhm. Read the riddle. Only one of these doors is correct!

Missing? Probably taken by the same bastard that has my pack mates. Exarch Tzinghalis.\n\nFennorian said he could provide a key to unlock their chains if I told him about the experiments performed on us. If you can get that key, I'll tell you more.
Along the northern coast, you say? Hmm. Yes. That might narrow it down. Here, follow me inside.

A decade ago, I tracked down a cave where the Pale Man brought its kills. For days, I waited. Eventually, I left to replenish supplies. When I returned, I saw loose rocks and an empty crawl space. The damned thing had watched me the whole time.

It only attacks the unsuspecting or vulnerable. And I was armed to the teeth. It's no mere beast. It's smart. Cunning.\n\nBut, I have an idea on how we draw it out. Bait. Of an … unusual variety. Would you be willing to help out?

Gods, no. I'm not willing to lose the only helpful person I've met in a decade. I need you to collect the ingredients and bring them to me on the northern coast. Then we'll draw out the creature and avenge its victims.

The alchemical mixture I plan to use is necrotic, for lack of a better term. It only reacts with dead flesh. If we doused a living person with it, they'd die, but not before their flesh melted and they screamed a whole lot first.\n\nIt's nasty stuff.

No one knows what make those walking corpses move, but we do know they stop moving if you hack them up enough. We need intact, non-moving parts to make a body that will draw out the Pale Man.\n\nOne draugr won't do, but parts of dozens? That might.

After I failed to draw the Pale Man out ten years ago, I talked to every hunter and Reach witch who wouldn't slam the door in my face or try to cook my eyeballs.\n\nThe hunters suggested bait, but it was an old clever woman who suggested the mixture.

The thing eats, doesn't it? We know it's smart enough to move lairs, avoid people who can kill it, and use snowstorms as cover.\n\nI've tested the mixture myself. It was all I could do not to eat the dead flesh I poured it on. Still makes me nauseous.

I don't know how it works, exactly, only that it's something the hagravens created. Somehow, the clever woman stole it away from them. \n\nWhen poured on dead flesh, it creates a scent that drives anyone who smells it mad with hunger.

While you're out collecting the draugr parts we need, I'll mix the potion, limp up to the coast, and find the lair.\n\nOnce you have the draugr parts, run along the northern coast between Dragon Bridge and Solitude and look for me. I'll be waiting.

Well, no. It's just the closest place I know to find them. Any draugr will do, and if you know somewhere else to hunt them, their parts will work as well as any other.\n\nJust be careful. Those walking corpses look slow, but they're strong and mean.

Glad to hear that worked out. With any luck, Fenn will produce a working elixir in short order. Then we can stop worrying about the harrowstorms and concentrate on defeating the Gray Host.\n\nWhich reminds me. Go to the Blackreach camp and aid Svana.

Princess Svana has something to prove, and that's never a good thing. At least she survived her mission. I'll ask her about it later.\n\nNow, get to the coastal camp and assist Fenn. He needs to learn about how the medallions are created.
I suppose congratulations are in order. Just remember we still have a long way to go to end the threat of the Gray Host.\n\nFor now, let's get back to the Blue Palace. I'll meet you there.
A family of monsters. Who could imagine vampires and werewolves working together? Let alone talking about one another like brothers and sisters. It's not natural.

You assemble them into a body that tempts the Pale Man. Take these sharp bones. Jam them into the torso. Then stick the arms, legs, and head onto them. Gruesome work, but it should hold.\n\nPour on the pungent mixture I've made and you have your bait.

Last time I found a crude table deep within its lair. There were … remains with gnaw marks on them. I think that's where it eats.\n\nSearch the lair for a similar table, place the body on it, then pour on the mixture. And, uh, hold your breath.

If this doesn't work, then come get me. I am not letting this thing escape again. It won't be killing any more people.\n\nIf we have to … I'll be the bait. But I'd like to avoid that for as long as possible. Despite everything, I'd like to live.

Arkasis is doing all kinds of experiments with these stone husks. All too technical for me. Plus his notes trail off in all sorts of crazy directions. I get the impression he's easily distracted and his allies are losing patience with him.
Good. Hopefully that information will help Fenn with the elixir he's working on.\n\nI suggest you get to the midland camp and find a sample of the refined netherroot brew with Lyris.
That's great news. I knew you and Lyris could do it.\n\nNow, head to the coastal camp and help Fenn learn something about how the coven medallions are created.
Then we're done here. I hope we found enough to end the threat of the Gray Host.\n\nI'll meet you back at the Blue Palace. Good luck, my friend.

Then it's over. Shor's Bones, it's over, after so many years. That thing is really dead.\n\nI don't know how I can thank you. I lost everything and was ready to just give it all up. But now, finally, justice.

I don't … wait. That ring. It can't be. It's Drendek's Signet Ring!\n\nOur mother gave it to him shortly before our hunting trip, when the Pale Man took Drendek. I always felt she blamed me for losing it, and for my brother, but now ….

These must be from all the other victims. Trophies of the lives it snatched. That means it wasn't hunting for food. It was proud of what it'd done.\n\nI need to return these to the families. Eyfja, Hautgerd, all of them deserve to know it's over.

Vehk be praised!\n\nIn all my years of study and adventure, I have never faced a more frustrating foe than this idiot, Maelmoth. And he's dead! Can you even imagine how insufferable he must have been while he was alive?
Mercifully, I believe you're right. Naturally, parting company with me will be difficult, but you'll muddle through somehow.\n\nCome on, assistant. Let's bring this farce to a close, shall we?

What else would you call them? My family? We're bound by a curse that makes us closer than any blood relatives. You find a pack and you stick together. Or you die. Simple as that.\n\nI'm not leaving them in the hands of that insane exarch.

Tzinghalis's helper made a mistake. Forgot to lock the chains when I was brought back after one of my … treatments.\n\nI can still feel the fire from when the needle pierced my skin. My blood, flowing into his vials and beakers. It wasn't pleasant.

Exarch Tzinghalis. He's a vampire, part of a group called the Gray Host. They're military, but he's some sort of insane genius. An alchemist, a scholar, and he tinkers with machines.\n\nMy pack wouldn't fight for them, so they found other uses for us.

Of course! How could I have missed such an exquisite antiquity?\n\nGranted, most of these items are worthless trinkets and oddities. But with some modest poetic license, I could turn that bottle into something truly extraordinary for my readers.

Oh. Oh! Well, yes, of course it would trigger another illusion! I knew that. You passed the test, assistant. Superb reasoning.\n\nAnd now, we let the grim resignation set in. By the Three, what a waste of time.

Digging. Tunneling, actually. Up, toward the surface. Then, every so often, Tzinghalis would send for one of us.\n\nThe mad vampire likes needles. He would either take our blood or inject something into us. Never said why, but he enjoyed his work.

Fennorian really wanted to figure out what Tzinghalis was doing to my pack.\n\nHe studied my wounds, took some fluids, and went back to get that key. He never told me where he found it. Just that he'd set my pack free if I told him everything I know.

That's not the point! I never should have agreed to let her put herself in that kind of danger. She's the daughter of a high king!\n\nBesides, without Svana to help us, Svargrim could send us back to Eastmarch—or worse.
Shor's bones, you're as bad as she is! Let's just get back to the business at hand.\n\nTalk to Fenn and see if you understand what he and the clever woman are going on and on about.

So he has. But have soldiers been sent to Morthal? Has aid been dispatched to Karthald? No. Not yet.\n\nSvargrim helps the people that flow into the city while the rest of Western Skyrim suffers. We must find the perpetrators and attack!
Yes! There's a good assistant!\n\nAfter all that Maelmoth put us through, I … we deserve this!

The princess … can we really trust that troubled young woman? After everything you did in Karthwatch, I suppose I must.\n\nIf you and Svana truly have a way to help, please be quick about it. I fear we're running out of time.
<Pickle barks affirmatively.>
<Pickle looks pleased.>
<Pickle huffs at you.>

He's trying to protect me. It's what he does. And leave me out. Though I suppose that's mostly my own fault. I know mother's death weighs on him. As does this entire crisis.\n\nThat's why we have to help. This elixir is going to work. It has to.

We can use the refined brew as the basis of our elixir. Now that we understand how the harrowstorms are created, we can use those same components to replicate the medallion's protective properties.\n\nWe just need to gather the necessary components.
<Pickle barks.>
<Pickle wags his tail.>
<Pickle whines.>

Ugh. As if they have any claim to that name! They're pompous upstarts who worship Dragons just as the ancient Dragon Cult did. Ridiculous!\n\nThey're cruel, bloodthirsty, and prone to insanity, but frustratingly capable … as I learned the hard way.

I don't know. It happened so fast. One moment I was patrolling the courtyard, the next I was fighting for my life. They were everywhere!\n\nA few of us barely managed to get out before they sealed themselves inside the temple and the tower.
Who knows how those monsters think? It's like they're waiting for something. As soon as I got out, I ran to the palace as fast as I could.\n\nNow I really ought to give the princess my full report.

I'll say this … I organized these talks because the Skald-King asked me to, not because I thought we'd succeed. I assumed the meeting was doomed to fail.\n\nBut given what Rigurt's accomplished already, perhaps I was wrong. Or perhaps I'm just drunk.

The University of Gwylim's most prestigious historical society. We scour the continent for lost antiquities, collecting and cataloging as we go.\n\nWe've made hundreds of discoveries, thanks in no small part to our scrying tool—the Antiquarian's Eye.

An invention of our university's founder, Tjurhane Fyrre. It allows the wielder's mind to travel vast distances and find buried relics. Truths lost to history.\n\nGazing into the Eye requires no small measure of talent. How talented are you, I wonder?

I did not want to spare the soldiers I had left to send a message.\n\nWe destroyed a number of strange sticks set up on the outskirts of town. When we reached the barrow, we spotted a few Reach barbarians. I sent word and we charged after them.

A storm appeared in the barrow, if you can believe such a thing! It was foul magic, almost certainly!\n\nSoldiers began changing around me. Dying or falling into a stupor. Some turned into monsters! And then the draugr crawled out of their graves.
I did. She was beloved by the whole town, even those of us pushed to the edges. Her disappearance hit hard. And the circumstances, well ….
No. No. I will not tell you what is not yours to know. At least, until I can see what causes these attacks.\n\nCome back with the samples and you may learn more.

In a hurry, are we? We'll teach you to use the Eye in due course.\n\nFirst, do you vow to uphold the principles and traditions of the Circle? To catalog your discoveries for future generations and give a true accounting of Tamriel's history?

Because I'm not a mage.\n\nDon't make a face. I never said I possessed the aptitude. We all contribute to the Circle in our own way. You may wield the Eye, but rest assured, my skill as a writer is no less important.

Not just writing. Few can match my knowledge of ancient history. Aside from those who lived through it all like that insufferable Dark Elf, Divayth Fyr.\n\nYou may find these relics, but it's incumbent upon me to tell you what they are.
That's not much to go on, but it's all we have.\n\nI'll meet you at the cart outside of town.

You should read Historia Draconis! The writer was an eyewitness!\n\nVery briefly, in ancient times Dragon Priests and the Dragons ruled over the Nords. More like slaves really, unless you joined the Dragon Cult.

We're still sorting that out. The Historia claims the Nords killed them all, but it's biased. \n\nSome scholars think the Cultists sacrificed themselves to become draugr. That way they could protect the Dragons and priests buried in the mounds.

Right! The Nords revolted. A few Dragons even fought against their own kind. The texts say thousands on thousands of Nords died, but I think that's exaggerated. \n\nEventually, they defeated the Dragon Priests and their Dragons.

Oh, that's easy. Most of the burial sites are still buried, and therefore inaccessible. These two happen to be at the surface and may have the rubbings I need. If my research is correct, of course.\n\nThere's more but let's start with this, at least.

I really don't know. I've never really done research in the field before. I planned to go in armed to the teeth just in case.\n\nA lot of good that did me. I bought all this adventuring gear and have nothing to show for it.

It's a magnificent device. Ayleid in origin. As I said before, our university's founder, Tjurhane Fyrre, developed it along with countless other scholarly tools. Alas, he died before we could demonstrate the object's true potential.

We seek the truth above all else.\n\nWritten histories rarely give an honest accounting of the past. So, we go straight to the source—relics, curios, even ancient bric-a-brac. Anything that can teach us more about the myriad cultures of Tamriel.

It's a school, of course. The very best, by any credible assessment. At least it was. \n\nUgh. What I wouldn't give to walk those halls again. This frigid annex is a very poor substitute. Very poor indeed.

We recovered several from a vault in Elinhir. It seems Sage Fyrre intended for the University's best and brightest to continue his work after he was gone.\n\nIt took longer than he would have liked, I'm sure. But I fully intend to honor his legacy.

It's not like that. I understand why she works us as hard as she does. We'd all be dead if we were doing things how we used to.\n\nI just wish everyone else would see it that way too. Make her job a little easier.
How exciting! I can't believe I get to examine these myself. Field work is wonderful!\n\nNow, I just have to hope they confirm my theory.

Well, the glyphs here are definitely Merethic era with Nord inclusions that have — Sorry, I'll skip all that.\n\nThese symbols resemble those on Dragon Cult tablets. I think they're charms that speed up the release of the Dragons from their mounds.

Well, something like that. It happened in Elsweyr, didn't it?\n\nNow that I have these, there's one final mound to investigate. I have to physically go there this time. Would you still be willing to help me? I'm not sure I can do this alone.

I wasn't sure about this last part. I needed the rubbings to know. \n\nBesides, if I said I needed you to maybe help me cast a spell to seal up a dead Dragon, you'd think I was ridiculous. Everyone else does, especially my mentors.

Sure? No, but what if I'm right? I know it's all untested theory, but if the alternative is a Dragon waking up, then I think I should try.\n\nI've seen all the reports of the slaughter in Elsweyr. It sounds horrible.

I assume you mean commercially valuable? Yes, you can keep any relics you recover and do with them what you will. The Circle's chief concern is cataloging the discoveries and learning what we can from them.\n\nEveryone benefits from the arrangement.
Oh! Right, of course. You're the one who knows what to do.\n\nI brought my dagger, in case there are giant bugs or something. I've never stabbed a giant bug before. Is it as icky as it sounds?
Wonderful. So those tales about being dragged into caves and devoured by Frostbite Spiders are just stories to make children behave?\n\nDon't answer or you'll scare me out of doing this.

Here and elsewhere. The faculty scattered to the winds when the Planemeld took hold. Fortunately, most of us survived and we write each other constantly.\n\nI wound up in Skyrim somehow. As frozen wastelands go, it's really quite pleasant.
It certainly happened in Elsweyr, didn't it? Everyone thought Dragons were gone for good and now the giant lizards are burning villages.\n\nIs that what happens if I do nothing?

The reports aren't clear about where they came from, just rumors. Some say they were entombed until something woke them up, but Elsweyr doesn't have Dragon Mounds like we do here.\n\nBut I think until we know more, why risk an attack?
You were? Then you saw what they did. Is it so unlikely it could happen here?\n\nAnd I have so many questions to ask you! But, later.

As much as it would please me to flay the flesh from your bones, I have more pressing matters to attend to.\n\nBut know this. As I felt each death, you shall feel it when the harrowstorm takes every life in Solitude. You shall feel it when you fail!
Ugh. Searching, mostly. I couldn't rest knowing Darien was still out there. Trapped in the Colored Rooms.\n\nI want to help him. Speak to him somehow, you know? But it's just not that simple.
Darien returned? Then where is he now? Why hasn't he contacted me?

Maybe. To be honest, it started with Ayleid research. I had a theory that Ayleid relics from Meridia-aligned tribes might grant me access to the Colored Rooms—or at least let me contact someone held there.\n\nThis led me to the Antiquarian's Eye.
Thanks. We'll find him. It's just a matter of time.

No. Just objects. Fortunately, it's allowed me to continue my research into the Ayleids. It's even given me a few other routes of inquiry. Meridia's shrine on Mount Kilkreath, for instance. \n\nI've got to believe something out there can help us.

So, he doesn't think he's coming back again? So much for Darien the plucky optimist.\n\nThe important part is that we know escape is possible. I'm not giving up on him. We'll find a way to get him back for good, I know it. So, chins up, right? Right.
But he was here. He was here and I missed my chance to ….\n\nWhen you say he disappeared, what do you mean? Did he say anything?

Remember what the witch said as we approached the town. This time we'll harvest all the gray reliquaries, she said. That our life energy would have fit perfectly in the urns.\n\nI think the harrowstorm steals life energy and puts it in the reliquaries!

If the jarl is still alive, she can take care of herself for a while longer.\n\nThe witch hasn't gathered all the reliquaries yet. I say we get to them first and destroy them. I won't let these bastards profit off the destruction of Karthwatch.

You've not heard of it … er, us? Sorry, I'm their newest member. I always wanted to be one so I assumed everyone knew about them.\n\nThe Antiquarian Circle are scholars and mages devoted to uncovering the forgotten relics and mysteries of Tamriel.

Well, not exactly. In fact, Gabrielle, our leader, was entirely against it. She didn't think my theory held any merit.\n\nShe told me I could gather information as long as I didn't get involved directly. But I wanted to prove myself to the Circle!

No! I hope not? I disobeyed because I saw a threat and took the initiative to deal with it. And nothing bad happened, so that's a good thing, right?\n\nYou should join us! I'll mark our location on your map. Meet me there and I can pay you.
Oh! Really? I'm very new, our latest member. I only joined recently. \n\nAnyway, this is wonderful! Imagine the coincidence of my asking you, a fellow member, for help out here.

No! I mean, I don't think so. I took the initiative to deal with something that could be a big threat. That counts for something, right?\n\nI have to explain my findings to Gabrielle. And I promised to pay you, so meet me at the Circle.

Well, not exactly. Gabrielle made her skepticism quite clear. Is she always that blunt? \n\nShe told me I could gather information as long as I didn't get directly involved. But I wanted to prove myself to the Circle! I hope I'm not in trouble.

He's probably in Tzinghalis's experimentation chamber. I clawed my way out of there. It nearly killed me.\n\nI can tell you how to get inside, but you have to free my pack mates first. Do that for me, and I'll help you find Fennorian.

I'd report back to Verita and let her know you successfully extracted your first antiquity. Don't expect too much in the way of praise, but trust me, she'll be ecstatic.\n\nOnce you've checked in, start looking for relics! No time like the present, eh?

Not really. My whole theory depends on the idea that a Dragon buried in that mound could, conceivably, rise from the dead. We know necromancers can raise human skeletons, so why not Dragons?\n\nThat's what my ward is supposed to stop.

No. I researched thoroughly to make it unbreakable, but I just don't know if it worked. I expected some kind of reaction … but there was nothing. \n\nI don't know, what do you think? How should I present my findings to the Circle?

You're right! I've always been self-conscious about my ideas. Too many competing scholars back home. But I created a competent ward, and if anyone tries to raise that Dragon, they'll fail. I'm sure of it.

You're right. I may not like it, but it's true. I'm sure I cast a good ward, but there are just too many unknowns. I don't want to seem overconfident or brash.\n\nI'll tell Gabrielle everything I learned, but I'll let her decide what to make of it.

That is entirely up to you. What cultures spark your curiosity? What region of Tamriel do you yearn to visit? Or, if it's simple wealth you're after, what item might fetch a prize on the second-hand market?\n\nThe choice is yours.

The potential applications of our discoveries are endless!\n\nYou might find items worthy of display in your home, or discover a long-forgotten technique for body ornamentation. You might even recover jewelry or armor imbued with arcane power.

Arkasis scribbled some instructions to his assistants about handling the research brought from Lady Thorn's old sanctuary. I'm pretty sure he was referring to these dusty tomes on souls. Not sure how Lady Thorn fits in with the Gray Host though.

The Ravenwatch doesn't have the resources to keep the Gray Host from taking it back, so the best I can do is make sure there's little left of value still here when they do. If you want to smash a few things on your way out, be my guest.

Don't know. East maybe, or south. As far away from here as we can manage. I don't like the heat, but Hammerfell gets lots of sun. Might keep these Gray Host monsters from coming after us.\n\nYou might do well to follow. This place is doomed.

I managed to limp my sorry carcass back down to the Dusktown after I slipped out Tzinghalis's lair with that damn key. Told them I got caught in a cave in, and they pointed me to the new alchemist in town.\n\nWe didn't really hit it off.

I bit him. I smelled vampire and thought he was with the Gray Host. He's lucky I was half-dead. I passed out from the strain before I could do too much damage.\n\nHe nursed me back to health, and started asking about what really happened.

Me and the pack were barely making ends meet on the outskirts of Karthald. When we heard about lucrative mining work far away from the world, we leaped on it.\n\nEverything was perfect until the Gray Host sniffed us out. Literally.

Yeah. Some beast of a woman cornered our pack in the tunnels and demanded we submit to her. She was a giant of a Nord, but a mountain of a werewolf. Five to one and she tore us to shreds in the blink of an eye.\n\nTzinghalis called her Ulfra.
The things that go bump in the night all live down here—hundreds of them—and I think they're looking to resettle. No one topside is prepared for what's coming. Turn tail while you can.
A bunch of pike-pushing, summertime soldiers stand no chance against that monster. I don't care how many of you go charging after it. It'll take a platoon of soldiers, at least!

I ran. You would have too if you saw how quickly that Sea Giant butchered my friends. Took a horse and rider with every swing. Split my mare straight through the saddle. If I hadn't been standing in the stirrups I'd have wound up the same.

Oh, thank you so much!\n\nClaudina and I are good with the spirit side of things, but we struggle with people. If you talk to Elle and assure her that we're doing everything we can, she'd probably feel better! She should be right outside the mines.

Here, take my keys. They'll give you access. But please, keep your investigation out of the mines. After that incident this morning, Urlvar only wants workers down there.\n\nBest to keep everyone safe.

Oh, it was heartbreaking. The whole herd snatched up and wailing into the night. You ever heard a goat scream? It'll haunt you.\n\nThey're good goats. They don't deserve to be torn apart by man-wolves. You'll bring them back to me, won't you?
