I thought I spotted some papers over there. Certainly looks newer and less Dwarven than the rest of this place. Maybe they contain a clue or something?\n\nIf all else fails, I could try slamming my axe into the door.
Exarch Tzinghalis and Rada al-Saran talked freely while they tortured me ….\n\nThey're planning some sort of assault on Solitude … a massive harrowstorm ….

I envy you, getting to experience it for the first time!\n\nBasically, if Captain Ageran disappeared here, there might be some kind of spiritual residue leftover from whatever took place. We need to conduct a ritual to try and harness it.

Perhaps, they're using the ancient stones nearby to power their magic. We generally avoided them because of rumors they were cursed. Sounds perfect for evil crones.\n\nLet's find them. Stopping the witches might release Bjora so she'll come home.
We must join them, then! I'm so relieved to hear it's not all lost. Please, I want no more of this place.
I need blood … but I won't drink from an unwilling person …. In this state, even with a willing participant, I don't trust my restraint.\n\nIf only I had my flask ….

Not by itself, but it gives me a place to start. With any luck, that map may provide additional clues.\n\nI … I need to rest. I'm sorry, my friend. This ordeal has been … more difficult than you can imagine.

All I can do is to offer my aid in good faith. Whether they decide to grab my hand or to slap it away, that's up to them.\n\nDespite our differences, I love this land. It's as much Skyrim as my beloved eastern holds. I would not see it suffer.
The Reach is far from everyone's holdings! This Gray Host business started with me, though, and I always intended to see it through to the end. Thankfully, we prevailed. This time.

Shor's bones, why does everyone insist on seeing ulterior motives behind every kind act? Can't a king just be a nice person?\n\nLook, someone has to extend the hand of friendship before it can be grasped. Besides, helping the Reach helps all of Skyrim.
That must have been Skeg! Thank the Gods he's still alive. \n\nThose monsters are everywhere. How are we going to get out?
Lead on. We'll do our best to keep up.

It didn't talk, I remember thinking that was strange. Maybe it's mute? \n\nThere wasn't a lot of time to get a good look, but I remember there was something … off about it. The eyes were all wrong, like there was nothing going on behind them.

The crew of the Cormorant is like family. I care about our missing people just as much as the captain does. \n\nBesides, even if I didn't, no way I'd let him go after that beast on his own. I'm the first mate, and it's my duty.

Not really. Most everyone on the ship has a different opinion. Only thing we can agree on is that it was big. Real big. \n\nBut it was dark, none of us could get a good look. I know I heard snarling, but that's about it.
Just trading. We came from Rihad, in Hammerfell. \n\nIt's too bad we weren't bringing food. I would have gladly paid for the lost merchandise if it kept my people alive for a little while longer.
No, it was larger than that. Smarter, too. No bear could have gotten up onto the deck and stolen our people from their cots like that.

Nowhere close by. Only a high priest of Arkay can prepare the sacred oil, and the high priest here in Solitude turned over his supply to Svargrim. Now it's locked in the temple.\n\nIn retrospect, that was probably part of Svargrim's plan all along.

Is that so strange? Yes, I do! I raised her from just a wee little thing. I can't imagine a life without her! Just one look at her sweet face and you'd understand.\n\nOh, why did I think a fence would stop her?
Oh, that is a good point! Muffins would never ignore my calls. She must have wandered farther than I thought.\n\nThank you, my friend! I am going to go look for her!

I don't think Uthlet was involved in my father's treachery, at least not knowingly. If he can pull himself together, I believe his loyalty is to Solitude, not my father.\n\nRegardless, find out what he knows about the situation inside the temple.
Ha! I knew I liked the look of you! Here, take a mug. Drink up, friend, and let the mead wash all your cares away!
Not interested? What are you, a milk drinker?\n\nHa! I'm kidding, friend! If you don't want to drink, you can still enjoy our company. Come, be well with us! To new friends!

There's a sluice gate in the outer courtyard, tucked away against the keep's eastern wall. The few patrols in that area can be avoided if you're stealthy. \n\nOpening the gate requires a key, but that should be simple enough to find.
Ha, you're just like me. Making promises you can't keep.\n\nTime will tell if your word holds up better than mine.
Svana does as she pleases. Always has.\n\nShe's on the rise while this old Orc fades away. With any luck, she'll have a chance to grow as fat and useless as me.

What? Of course I do! I need to see this through to the end. The same as you and Svana. The Ravenwatch doesn't leave a job half done. Besides, if I quit now, what Tzinghalis did—he'll win.\n\nNow, let's go before I forget everything I just told you.

Sort of? He admits he might have been wrong about the Icereach Coven, as far as that goes, but he still glares daggers whenever anyone mentions you or Lyris.\n\nSo, let's not bring up Fenn, all right?

I got High King Svargrim to promise to dispatch soldiers to reinforce Morthal's defenses and send aid to Karthwatch.\n\nIt's a start, but he hasn't actually issued the orders yet. I need to follow up with him after we're finished.
Have you got an army with you? That's what it'll take. Skreg's got dozens of honorless bastards willing to beat, poison, or kill anyone who threatens him. I should know.

If you can call it that. Got waylaid by his round-toothed lackies heading into the Circle of Champions. Had two broken ribs, three smashed fingers, and a poisoned gut wound before I even raised a weapon to him.
We're about to enter the very heart of the Gray Host and that's what you're thinking about?\n\nGet your head in the moment. We'll need you at your best if we're going to save Solitude.

According to the Ravenwatch's research, no one actually owns the castle. Powerful individuals claim it from time to time, but the keep endures.\n\nLady Essenia is just the latest to occupy its halls. Why she's working with the Ashen Lord, who can say?

This structure extends all the way to Blackreach's ceiling, placing it almost directly below Solitude. It stands to reason that the ritual site will be on the keep's upper levels, closer to the target of their harrowstorm.\n\nSo, we need to go up.

Not sure I really want to know.\n\nAnyway, thanks for looking after Pickle. The way he's looking at you! I don't know that he's ever looked at me that fondly. I think you've made a friend for life. And you've certainly found one in me, as well.
My friend, I will always be the king of my castle, but from now on, I think I'll let Telline make all the decisions. I'm happy just to be with her. Wherever she takes me, I'll gladly go.

No, no of course you wouldn't. I can't expect a random passerby to coincidentally have the answers I seek. I apologize for putting you on the spot, traveler!\n\nBut Blackreach is out there. It exists. Do not believe those who claim it is just a legend!

Oh! The luck of Julianos is with me! How fortuitous that we should meet on this road, on this day!\n\nSo I seek a Dwarven lift! One of the texts I read actually suggested that. Wonderful! I'll start preparing for my greatest adventure at once!

It's so wonderful to find another soul who appreciates the wisdom of Jhunal! We had to close our temple in Solitude due to lack of funds, but if we can recruit more intelligent and curious knowledge seekers like you, we'll be able to open once again!

Ah, no, of course you wouldn't be. Skyrim is a land of hard people and hard drinkers. Who has any use for the skill to read, write, and reason these days? Few here, I assure you.\n\nVery well. I will seek others who are willing to learn.

Plans being reviewed. Orders given. The Gray Host warriors are pulled as taut as a bow string ready to be loosed.\n\nMy guess is, once the harrowstorm begins, the Gray Host will fly out of Blackreach like an arrow toward its mark.
We have to find Svargrim and Rada al-Saran first. And this labyrinth of a keep isn't making that easy to do.\n\nLet's keep moving.

You mean, we're running around inside one of those awful things? That's deeply disturbing. And also kind of brilliant.\n\nAll the more reason to find my father and put an end to this threat once and for all.

I'm not a mage, but I can try.\n\nGo with Lyris. Find Svargrim. If this doesn't work, you'll need to stop him before he unleashes the harrowstorm on Solitude. With a storm that big, they'll have more than enough power to resurrect the Gray Host!
Am I …? I'm not sure of one damn thing at this particular moment in time! But we need to do whatever it takes, risk anything, to save Solitude. \n\nNow go, and may Kyne go with you.

You heard right.\n\nViggol reached seventy-three years old last month, but still thinks he can adventure like he's twenty! He heard rumors about strange beasts picking off miners down here, so he and Pickle set out to kill a few for old times' sake.

Viggol's dog, and favorite adventuring companion. I trust him to keep Viggol safe most days, but he's getting up in age too.

Pah. I should never have married a Nord. Always with the heroics.

Would you help him? I'll pay you what I can.
Svargrim was ascending the central tower. We need to find our own way up.

Of course! I cook my meat to perfection! Skeever, spider, or mammoth, it all tastes the same after it's roasted over a warm fire and then marinated in a delightful blend of herbs and spices.\n\nSkeevers are delicious. I'll be the one to prove it!

Well, it got a little clearer as soon as you picked it up. Must be some kind of magic at work. \n\nThat note did say it would protect from the storm. You should keep it on you, it might come in handy.

Nothing good. Strange weather is one thing. A giant Khajiit collecting corpses is another. I don't like any part of it. I just hope the captain and the others are safe. \n\nWe need to look into that Verglas Hollow mentioned in the note.
They got a bunch of us out. With their strength and experience, we were able to break away from our captors and escape. They've created a safe haven for us here in the aftermath.

Don't judge them too harshly, they're just afraid. We know very little about the disease. Our allies are afraid that we could turn on them at any moment. It's a valid concern.\n\nWe left the grotto to ease their concerns and keep them safe.

He's still missing? Gods. \n\nRasir believed the violent werewolves were the result of an infection, one that he could cure. He went out in search of one final ingredient to test for his latest recipe and never returned.
Good, I hope he's all right. He's a brave man.

Look at the shape of the fragments. They come from a hollow receptacle of some sort, something at least as tall as you. Perhaps larger.\n\nJust another piece of the puzzle. Maybe when I analyze the witch pike residue, an answer will suggest itself.

It varies. A friend of mine started showing symptoms a week before she was lost entirely. Others succumb overnight. \n\nI couldn't save them, but I will do what I can for those who remain. Alchemist Rasir was close to a cure. I must find him.

Almost as soon as we heard Rasir was missing, Skor was asking after him. I told him the same thing I told you. \n\nWe haven't seen him since then. He must still be out searching … don't know how he's still standing, much less trying to find Rasir.
He looked exhausted. His worry for Rasir seemed to take precedence, however. \n\nIt's not unlike him. He's always protecting everyone else. He sometimes forgets to protect himself.

Rasir is strong. He escaped Greymoor Keep with us. Still, the afflicted are monstrous adversaries. I hope Skor found him … he could protect Rasir.\n\nCome on, let's go. So little grows down here. Rasir's trail should be easy to spot.
Oh, one can't live in this world without encountering a stray spectre. Seeing chains drop from the sky changes what we accept as normal. And magic … impacts all our lives, of course.

Let's say I'm skeptical. The people of Morthal spend their days fishing, cutting logs, and drinking. They don't leave town and outsiders don't visit. Spreading wild tales is what passes for entertainment here.

Last week, Bandor accused invisible Riekr of stealing his beard comb. The mill ceased operation completely while the town searched for holes in the ground where they might be hiding.\n\nWe found it in the stables where he'd been grooming the horses.

So you know about the sluice gate in the outer courtyard, against the eastern wall of the keep? You can avoid the few patrols in the area if you're stealthy.\n\nOpening the gate requires a key, but that should be simple enough to get your hands on.

When those bone wolves came out of the storm, we scattered. Some people tried to defend themselves with rakes, but we're farmers not warriors. Other than myself and maybe Havil, I don't know who else is still alive.

Brun's still alive? One of those tusking wolves latched onto his leg, but that didn't slow him down. He fended it off with a hammer and kept running.\n\nIf he can make it to town, maybe I can as well. Thanks for letting me know.
When I fell ill, I felt this all-consuming fury. I had no control over myself, my body was not my own. I've never felt so helpless.\n\nBut Rasir cured me. My head feels clear again.

Still think you're mad, but I appreciate that you're willing to check on Havil. He's a grumpy old coot, but he doesn't deserve … whatever this is.\n\nYou'll need a key to the house. One of the farmhands should have one, if you can take it from them.

Remember what happened in the Sea of Ghosts? Well, that same coven moved against the Skald-King. I was able to keep Jorunn safe, but I learned they also had plans for Western Skyrim.\n\nSo, Jorunn sent Brondold and me to look into it and warn Svargrim.

That's putting it mildly. They can't stand each other.\n\nBut Jorunn doesn't want something terrible to befall Western Skyrim. That would be bad for the east as well as the west. Besides, he hoped to use this as an opportunity to improve relations.
I'm not usually fond of small talk, but go ahead. What do you want to know about?
Oh. That. Right. I'm not really sure. I remember white light as the Amulet of Kings took me, and then …. \n\nI woke up. I was somewhere else. Somewhere cold. It felt like home, but not … like here.

We defeated Molag Bal and stopped the Planemeld, but the empire I knew was dead and gone. There wasn't anything else I could do for Varen or Cyrodiil. Skyrim was still there, though.\n\nSo, I went home.

We bloodied their lip, but by the time we struck their stronghold the witches plans were well underway. They may have already wormed their way deep into Skyrim. We won't know for sure until we investigate further.

Skyrim is my home and the Skald-King is its ruler. He may be a bard at heart, but he cares about his people and his kingdom.\n\nSo long as he stands by his word and deed, he'll have my axe to command.

I'm sorry, but you're too late. The coven unleashed their harrowstorm and now vampires and harrowfiends are everywhere.\n\nStill, meeting you again is fortuitous. We worked well together and I could use your help tracking down the Draugrkin plunder.

She found someone? I didn't think there was anyone left in Solitude who won't flinch at the merest suggestion of magic. Fighting the Shademother won't be as simple as slaying your typical hagraven, if there is such a thing. She's far more powerful.
Neither do I. Was I in Sovngarde? Maybe. But then I was back here, in Tamriel. I guess there are still a few things that me and my axe need to do.\n\nI try not to think about it too hard.

I'm not sure how to describe it. There was a great longhouse in the fog. It was warm inside, full of people like me. Warriors.\n\nI don't know how long I was there, but one day I woke up and I really was home. In Skyrim.

Whatever I can. Traveling. Dealing with problems as I encounter them. My axe has been busy, that's for sure!\n\nMostly, I've been helping Jorunn the Skald-King. Looking into situations that could endanger the kingdom. Like the Icereach Coven.
We'd met briefly before the mission began. He was one of Jorunn's trusted spies. Dangerous, dirty work, without a shred of glory.\n\nIt's up to us to make sure he didn't die in vain.
Next to nothing. That's why Jorunn dispatched Brondold to Haafingar. To gather information. Without it, we're operating in the dark.

According to the legends, her mastery of life and death is absolute. She bends nature to her will and she feasts on the land itself to sustain her power. The clever woman I consulted said that the Shademother's magic is akin to necromancy.

Sorry, it's a bit archaic. A Nord mage who follows the old ways. Old Mjolen is a bit of a legend herself in these parts. She was the one who created the cleansing mixture you were given to purify the Shademother's corruption.
And he didn't send word to me? What an idiot!\n\nI … enough of this. We need to focus on the situation at hand. Sai can wait. He's good at that, apparently.
Sai's alive? How? We watched him sacrifice himself to empower the Amulet of Kings!\n\nHow could he come back from that? It can't be him. It must be some sort of trick!
I doubt word has spread that far, and Jorunn has had me working, keeping a low profile.\n\nI should find Sai when this is all done. Right now, I'm needed here. Our reunion can wait.

Every Nord wishes for a united Skyrim. The difference lies in whose banner they'd prefer it to be under. Jorunn wants to restore Tamriel—the Empire and Skyrim included—but I don't believe he'd turn Nord against Nord to do it.
More questions? Very well. Get on with it. What else do you want to know?
A cure! Thank you, stranger.\n\nGive it to me, and I'll make sure the others get it. You need to go after Rasir. He's injured, he can't hope to survive against Skor!

The Draugrkin were smuggling remains out of Bangkorai and sending them here by way of Sentinel. The cargo arrived in Solitude, but it wasn't clear who the shipments were for until I followed them here.\n\nThey were destined for the Icereach Coven.

The temple … there may be survivors who could use your help. Meanwhile, if we can learn more about the ritual, we might be able to determine a way to stop them.\n\nAt the very least, we need to figure out where they plan to strike next.

It's a natural wonder! A lush, temperate cavern within the nearby mountain. Thanks to some not-entirely-dormant volcanic activity, no doubt. A great number of local fauna take refuge from the cold there. That includes many predators, I'm afraid.
Then we can put an end to this tragedy. But we must act now.\n\nGo, join them at the large tree overlooking Morthal to the east. I will meet you after I prepare.
When you arrive, wait for me. Do not let them do anything rash. I will not be long. \n\nDo this and Morthal will be rid of this curse forever. Now, hurry!

Bring it with you. As my ritual to cure Freiwen culminates you must hold the locket before you. Her life energy will rush into her and the curse should break.\n\nI warn you, this may be painful for her. But it is necessary.

If those monsters escape, we'll have to abandon the stronghold. We'll need our strength.\n\nI set traps outside the walls. Take the game from them to the camp north of here. Then, I'll tell you where the key is.
We'd have to fight through those creatures again. There's another entry point this way. You just need to make a path for us. \n\nI'll help Mugha and follow as soon as it's clear.

Jorunn, Reddharn, and I need to form a plan to distribute Fenn's elixir and push back against the Gray Host. And acquire more netherroot, it seems.\n\nThere's a lot to be done, but I'm surrounded by good people. I trust we'll get through this together.
I—I don't know. It's not important, not right now. What matters is rallying the people against the enemy, our real enemy. If that means seeking the crown, then I'll do what needs to be done.
Sovngarde is a place for the honored dead. Svargrim gave up his seat in the Hall of Valor when he made his pact with the Ashen Lord. Wherever he is, I hope he regrets how he got there.
Well, yes, but so were the bodies that weren't disturbed. \n\nWe're trying to determine what the exhumed corpses have in common, remember? There must be something else that we're missing.

According to one necromantic theory, the older a living thing becomes, the more necrotic energy it naturally acquires. As a body grows old and withers, the life inside it decays.\n\nNecrotic energy is the byproduct of this deterioration.
We can only hope. \n\nThe problem itself may be eradicated, but Solitude now has its hands full with rebuilding. I think it's likely we'll still be on our own, at least until the dust settles.
You are a curious one, are you?\n\nHmm, where to begin? I assume you're familiar with Secundus Antilliax Pomo's work: The Harmonics of Motivational Force as Applied to Post-Dwemer Animunculi.
How astute. Yes, theoretically, it should completely override a Dwemer construct's ability to move. You will need to verify this and take note of the effect, of course.

I envy you. I spent two years of my life analyzing that dreadful tome, but—as I deconstructed that work—I had an epiphany: why not invert Pomo's premise? Could a harmonic device usurp a Dwemer construct's motive abilities?

Pomo went on endlessly about the role of the heartcog within the motivational system of a Dwemer construct. I'm skeptical that it's as vital to the process of harmonic locomotion as he claims, and frankly, I'd love to discredit the old fossil.
Of course! As soon as I recovered it, I began making copies so it wouldn't be lost again.\n\nHere you go.

These aren't vampires of the sort that trouble most holds. These are horrid creatures vomited up from Blackreach. Some are shriveled, beastly things. Others are hulking monsters unrecognizable as man or mer. They are numerous and terrible.

I made the mistake of venturing there as chaplain to a mining company. They found that dank, dark place and settled, but I had to leave after what I witnessed down there. Someone has to stop these vampires' slaughter.

That, at least, will be simple. Simply hold it before the fallen victims and pray for Arkay to deliver them from evil. It will consecrate the remains and release any lingering spirits from this world.

Wow, really? That's uncharacteristically gracious of her. Huh. Well anyway, let's get started.\n\nIt all begins with concentration. The Eye wants to show you what you seek. So, clear your thoughts and conjure up a picture of the relic in your mind.

The exciting part! Gaze into the Eye and focus on the facets in the glass. Take a breath and try to unify the symbols into a single pattern. Eventually, you'll stop looking at the lens and start looking through it.\n\nWhy don't we just give it a try?
Certainly.\n\nYou should have a small array of tools at your disposal—some for removing large helpings of dirt, and others for more precise excavation.

That's the trick, isn't it?\n\nYou'll notice subtle differences in the composition of the soil. To the layman, these differences of color and texture might appear random. But with practice, you'll begin to notice patterns.

I haven't the faintest idea. That's the best part. Whatever your findings are, it'll all be uncharted territory for me. I could use more interesting reading material while I'm out here looking for quality research assistants.

Of course!\n\nWe use the Antiquarian's Eye to scry for antiquities hidden all over Tamriel. Any time you want to search for one of these treasures, just open your Antiquities Codex, and select the object you'd like to find.

It won't be easy to get to. We know, historically, where the Midnight Barrow was, but it's long been buried and forgotten. It's probably a place better off left alone, but if there's something to learn from that place, then it's our duty to learn it.

Indeed. If you achieve perfect focus, you might narrow it down to a single dig site. If you don't reach all of the eye's foci, you will wind up with several possible locations.\n\nLuckily, you can always try again! It's all a matter of practice.

Then the fun begins!\n\nYou'll notice symbols swimming in the facets of the Eye's lens. Concentrate, and try to merge as many of the symbols as possible. If you reach the Eye's foci, you'll get a glimpse of the antiquity's possible resting places.
Wonderful. Find the Midnight Barrow and smash some umbric urns. Observe the spirits' response.

Well, your Antiquities Codex contains only those antiquities we're currently aware of. If you want to make a unique discovery of your own, you'll need to find a lead. Something that gives you a place to start.
What happens. Spirits imprisoned so long are hard to come by. Maybe they keep near what they know. Maybe they pass on. Maybe there's nothing left but ectoplasm. We won't know until we find out.

Oh, I couldn't possibly choose. In any case, my interest in these objects has less to do with their uses and more to do with their historical value.\n\nAmalien swore she found parts of a mechanical mount, but that sounds a bit outlandish to me.

I constructed it for use by those with limited technical expertise. The process is as follows: locate an active construct, attract its attention, point the device at the construct, and pull the small lever on the side.

I erect the spine of irritation. If I wanted to be bothered with questions about my research, I wouldn't have entrusted the Wood Elf to procure my bark. Did he not tell you to fetch me spriggan bark from the Shadowgreen?

Assistants should not be seen or heard. They should provide what is asked of them and stay out of the way.\n\nI have nothing more to share with you than my need for fresh spriggan bark from the Shadowgreen. Now go. Chop, chop!

Ha! You find this morbid, yes? What can Nezashul say? Death has always been a great fascination for him. Would it surprise you to know that there are Khajiit who bury the dead much like the ancient Nords did? Some even worshiped the Dragons as well.

This one is curious to compare the similarities, and differences. Ancient Nords—as this one is sure you have heard—tend to be more … lively, as dead folk go. Nezashul wishes to know if some of that vigor is retained in their little jars.

You're typical Giant's an oafish brute that can barely feed and clothe itself. Not the sort of thing you'd expect to build a ship, let alone sail one. Thought they were just another fanciful tale sailors spun until that scout returned pale as death.

A brush with death will do things to a mind, but the army are no strangers to Giants. They don't trouble us often, but when they do, it's usually the king's soldiers who clash with the brutes. When one says this was no normal Giant, I believe them.

Not much more I can tell you. I haven't got numbers on the werewolf pack, but I wouldn't go after them alone. As for the goats, I only know <<1>> insists those berries would get them to head home. He's still in Solitude if you need to know more.

That's what I use to train'em! Goats are plenty smart, you know? Stubborn, sure, but smart! They're more cooperative once they're a bit sloshed on fermented berries. A handful should calm their nerves and stoke their appetites enough to head home.

Thank the Divines! I've exhausted my current material, which consists entirely of local folklore. There is simply no credible evidence that Goblins or Reiklings live in this region. Any who did were likely driven out by Nords and Reachmen long ago.

There are persistent local legends of skulking shadows who linger in dark places, waiting to snatch up lost children and lone wanderers. The most prominent myths revolve around a single individual called the Pale Man. Thank the skalds for that.

More than likely. If there is a kernel of truth to the stories, that's long been obscured by decades of embellishment. What matters is, Landal Gevont wants us to look into the rumors surrounding Chillwind Depths, so we'll do our best.

Common, everyday objects can often teach us more than rare items the tribe might consider valuable. \n\nTalismans, tools, scraps of cloth. Best to look for things that won't be missed. Landal Gevont prefers that we disrupt as little as possible.

Skreg isn't going to step down without a fight and he's amassed a loyal following. Trying to corner him is only going to lead to war. He needs to be defeated—in spite of his cheating—and discredited, so the Orcs can move on.

You'll have to ask <<1>> about that. She's assured me that it will dispel the pools of corruption created by the Shademother around Morthal and that's all I care to know.\n\nKoljir is in Solitude, if you wish to question her.

I don't know him personally, but High Priest Ingurt vouches for him. He's a member of Arkay's clergy who left on some sort of expedition. I don't know more than that really.\n\nIf you have doubts, which you should, I'd speak to him before you leave.

It homes in on objects of historical import, much like a bloodhound … without all the baying and drooling, of course.\n\nWe still don't fully understand how it determines an item's value. Just more proof of our founder's genius, I suppose.
Hmph, Magreta sent you, didn't she? Coward picked a perfect time to turn her backs on us. Not Nelfthea though. She stuck by us when we needed her. A Frostbite Raider to the end.

I don't know for certain. She was holding her own against those half-giant bastards, but the last thing I saw before they wrecked my lookout was a gods' honest Giant smash her clear off the docks. If that did her in, she's in Sovngarde for sure.

All I know are whispers. They say Maxten kidnapped Freiwen and forced her into the ruins.\n\nNaturally, the Jarl dispatched the guards to rescue his daughter. But just as they arrived, a tempest of ice arose that froze the soldiers where they stood.

For a time. I studied there as well.\n\nDespite all of Cyrodiil's struggles, I really did believe we could weather the storm. But war has far-reaching consequences, even for those who want no part in it. Especially for those who want no part in it.

Vanished. Until now, it seems. Though, the link between Freiwen's ghost and this curse still remains unclear.\n\nTo find a cure, I need Maxten's original spell. Go east to the ruins. Retrieve anything that could reveal the nature of her work.

Good. Meet me in Morthal with what you find. I wish to examine the wounds made by these undead.\n\nAnd take this rune. It bears an enchantment that will ward you from the curse's worst effects. At least … temporarily.
The passage beyond this door is the most direct route back to the camp, though there is one small problem. Unfortunately, once I passed through it, a switch was set off and it locked behind me.

I've a bit of experience with Dwarven mechanisms, actually. There's a trick to releasing them from the ledge above the door. My grappling device should get me up there.\n\nAnd remind me to tell you how I discovered it sometime, it's a fine story!
You let me worry about that, friend. Just get everyone else out safely.\n\nNow, if you're ready, let's get a move on. The culmination of my final adventure awaits!

When I give the word, you throw the door lever while I tug on the counterweight. The door should open with no trouble. \n\nI'll need to keep a solid grip on the counterweight to keep it from closing on you.

Besides the looters, there are a number of strange adversaries up ahead. Most of them seem rather lost and confused, but nonetheless confrontational.\n\nIf you could clear a safe path for us, Kireth will stop fretting, and I can do what I do best.
I can't believe anyone knowingly involved would have let themselves be exposed to the storm. Perhaps the pilgrims were tricked into transporting the crate, or maybe it was slipped into their cart.

I'm sure now that the pikes play a significant role as focal points for the storm ritual. The prepared pikes are depleted as the ritual runs its course, but I sensed lingering energy—including a Daedric taint.\n\nAnd we found an intriguing residue.

One other thing I want to check first. I noticed the pilgrims leading a cart away from the temple right before the storm hit. Coven members could have tried to slip away among the innocents. \n\nThe cart should be along the road south of the temple.

Well, I'll be. I thought <<1>> was just telling me they'd look into it to get me to go away.\n\nShe told you that it's some sort of colossus? A big lumbering thing with whirling blades that spray fire and steam everywhere? And that it's getting bigger?

Sturdy as Dwarven works can be, they aren't invulnerable. I'm certain this strange thing has a weakness. It keeps building upon itself, but who knows if it's very good at it. You might knock one bolt loose and collapse the whole thing to pieces.

<<1>> claimed that she was searching some caves far to the south when the ground gave way and she tumbled through a series of tubes and ducts until they spit her out into some Dwarven ruin deep underground. I wouldn't recommend taking her route.

Truthfully, we don't deal with Dwarven constructs very often. Those things tend to stay within the boundaries of their ruins, so they're only ever trouble for adventurers. This colossus isn't behaving like most constructs though, so I'd be wary.

We train all guards to bring townsfolk there for safety during raids. I felt pride seeing him and Bjora performing their duty throughout such madness. They're our newest recruits and still very young. They were true guards of Karthwatch today.

Another member of the town guard. She's a tough warrior, that one. Her mother, Helsi, put a sword in Bjora's hand at a young age.\n\nHafskjar and Bjora have been close since childhood. I hope she keeps him safe in this disaster.
My boy married a miller's son. He's a soft lad. Never spent a night under the open sky.
Hmph, he didn't let me anything. I may not be in the crown's good graces, but folk still call me swordthane because I earned that right.\n\nTruth is, I prefer the militia to the king's guard.

Thank you, stranger. Please, bring her this locket so she knows the message is from me.\n\nTell Mother not to worry. There's a place I love nearby where I can watch the good people of Morthal live their lives. I can be happy there in my final moments.

I don't know. I was supposed to meet Captain Ageran, but as I passed the caves, I heard a cry. I ran in to find him bleeding out! He died before I could ask what happened.\n\nAgeran was a fine man. He didn't deserve this fate. This is … unacceptable.

No … I didn't. \n\nYou two need to leave. Stop investigating this. Gather your assistant, pack your things and get out of Blackreach. This is getting far too dangerous, and I don't want to see anyone else get hurt. Please.

You might damage the antiquity, or collapse the dig site entirely—reburying everything you tried to recover.\n\nIt happens to all of us eventually. The best we can do is stay cautious. And also sober. Some of the locals struggle with that.

Well, maybe not patterns in the formal sense, but shapes that align with the object you're excavating. These shapes can guide your efforts.\n\nJust remember to be careful! These are priceless antiquities we're digging up, not turnips.

Vampires live for conspiracy. It's practically the national sport! Local clans like the Volkihar haven't moved against her. And they have a lot to gain if she falls. It's weird.\n\nAnd now she capitulates to an outsider? I don't get it.

Oh, nothing much. Just rumors of arcane cyclones, and subterranean castles, that sort of thing.\n\nWe go where our trouble-making kin go. And our kin are definitely up to trouble here in Skyrim. I just wish there were more of us.
He's …. I'd rather not speak about that if you don't mind.\n\nLet's just say he's very far away. Too far away to be of any help.

If I had to guess? Far side of the courtyard. It's a long, open approach. Too many sight lines to breach in a siege. Luckily, no one's expecting us.\n\nPlus, the patrols seems to favor that area. Guards need to have something to guard, right?
Only wounded my pride. My boy and my son-by-Mara are unharmed. That's all that matters.
Not that I can think of. \n\nI'll make sure that Fenn makes it to the Blue Palace. We'll meet you there. And don't forget that map and communique.

Clever men and women are Nords with an aptitude for magic, though most use the term to refer to practitioners of the old ways. They're rare. Not the usual adepts found at the Mages Guild.\n\nDistrust of magic runs deep in Skyrim, especially out here.

Hey, you and Fennorian came to that conclusion, not me. Still, it makes as much sense as anything. As to why, I have no idea.\n\nThis connection to vampires, though. That's troubling. We should keep Fenn away until we get into Svargrim's good graces.
<This table appears to be set up for an experiment involving gloomspore agaric and bloodknight ichor.>

Tested me. But I failed! Failed experiment. Failure! So … so many more. So many dead. But not anymore. No. The Blood Queen succeeded. Can't stop her now. You can't! Must serve. Have to serve.\n\nNowhere is safe. Nowhere. You … you must run! Flee!

Foolish! Only death inside. Death and torture. My clan … all I had. Gone … gone because of Lady Essenia.\n\nBut the Blood Queen reigns. Don't you see? She is master. I am servant. I … I have to serve.

You think you can hide from her? No, no, no. The Blood Queen sees. The Blood Queen knows! But … if I tell you, you will leave. Yes. You have to leave!\n\nI will show you. I will show you the way. Then you go die alone in the cave!
<This table appears to be set up for an experiment involving gloomspore agaric and a bloodknight organ.>
<This table appears to be set up for an experiment involving gloomspore agaric and a bloodknight brain.>
I wouldn't think too hard about it, if I were you. This kind of magic is often more palatable when not dissected. The long and short of it is that it worked, and you've restored me to my true self!

Mother Wolf has the scent and will lead you to your quarry. I have enchanted the medallion with a divination spell inextricably linked to its owner.\n\nHold it to your nose and breathe deeply. It will guide you along his trail.

Didn't I tell you? The clever woman's magic can be quite exciting! Not my usual process of investigation, but effective just the same.\n\nI'll leave Old Mjolen to continue our research and follow after you. I want to see how the divination plays out.

There's nothing we can do for her. The vampire assassin drained all the blood from her body. He took his time with her, I think. Probably needed to recover his strength after the events at the palace.\n\nLet's get after him before the trail grows cold.

Yes, of course, though I fear what we may find there. The temple was clearly at the center of the storm.\n\nRegardless, there's still a lot we don't know about the effects of this ritual. Observing the target area could offer new insights.

Aside from the fact no one uses them? At least, no one that I've ever heard of. Harvesting chitin tough enough to use as a weapon is much more complicated than simple forging. It's not easy work, which is why you don't see them around too often.

It's possible these bogles are intelligent enough to do something other than steal livestock and haunt nightmares. But one blade is hardly enough to go on. \n\nThis looks like where the miners set up camp. See if you can find anything else of interest.

Hiding. Building their forces. Digging. Undermining. That's the correct term, I think.\n\nPlus, they're collecting the harrowed. Herding them like cattle. It's monstrous what they're doing to these poor people.

The letters are both addressed to the vampire assassin. Pentarch Khorb. That's an unusual title. This one gives the order to assassinate the queen, though the language is guarded. The other talks about miners and a final ritual.\n\nVery ominous.

Rigurt does not know! Every little thing rankles these western beard-pullers. "My cheese is too round! Mine is not round enough! Rigurt, get your hands out of the cheese!" \n\nStill, Rigurt is sure we will solve their problem, whatever it is!

Rigurt knows only what Jarl Morryn told him. Thane Hraldi likes to fish and keeps the old gods, the animal kinds. Thane Svyne likes to eat. And complain. Like thanes do in Eastmarch, but meaner.\n\nRigurt will need your help to get them to meet.

It looks like a map to a mine in Karthald. It could be the one mentioned in the letter. If that's the target of another harrowstorm ritual, we need to stop it.\n\nHead south to the mine. I'll get word to Lyris and have her meet you there.
Thank you. I need a moment to process everything you told me.\n\nAnd hold on to the locket. I refuse to take it while there's still hope to keep Freiwen alive.

Good. Here is the locket. Ninetha mentioned two places Freiwen enjoyed—the docks and her bedroom. You may find manifestations there.\n\nWhen you're done, meet me back here at the tavern. Then we'll proceed.

Mines aren't what they used to be. We pulled less ore this season than ever. The place is drying up faster than we anticipated.\n\nWhich is why the chief has us working so hard. If not for her, we'd starve. But people pretend to not understand that.

A ritual, obviously. Remember the altar at Kilkreath? We found the urn—the reliquary—and shards from a large stone vessel. I think they were the remains of one of those stone husks.\n\nI'm not sure how, but it all ties back to the harrowstorms.

I thought the purpose of the harrowstorms were to create harrowfiends, but now I think that's only a byproduct.\n\nThe storm somehow gathered energy that the witch used to summon Ulfra the werewolf. Ulfra seemed to think she was brought back to life.

Edjar sent you? Then he made it? He's alive? That's … that's wonderful news.\n\nExarch Tzinghalis … experimented on me. I blacked out, but they thought I was dead. They tossed me out of the tower … barely managed to crawl to this spot ….
Still at the camp. To the north. Harmild, Merthida, and Thevin. Save them before Tzinghalis … finishes them off.\n\nJust come back, all right? I don't think I can make it on my own.

An orc chief will not face rebellion from their clan. But an unpopular chief may struggle with less direct opposition, and more underhanded challenges. \n\nOverseer Thulsgreg, for example. He's never gotten over losing the title of chief to her.

Nothing. This feud with Chief Urzikh and Overseer Thulsgreg must end. He should obey his chief, simple as that. \n\nIf I was in charge, I would have crushed the fight out of him already. But Chief Urzikh seems to want to take a more diplomatic route.
The only thing I'm sure of is I have to try. If my father won't act, then it falls on me to get things done.\n\nIt's … it's what my mother would want me to do.

No, my friend. There is nothing.\n\nI intend to spend my remaining time here communing with the spirits of nature and trying to catch Old Hjaalsdottir. That fish swam the river Hjaal in my grandfather's day. But, spirits willing, I will hook her soon.
How should I know? I'm a historian, not a hedge wizard.\n\nJust use your best judgment. I have … near-total faith in you.
That's it! The glass is fading away …. I'm—Oh!
I think … yes, I think that's right. I can feel the glass cracking around me! Keep going. Speak the final line!
No, no that's not it! Damn, my ears are ringing! Well not my ears … I don't have any— Oh, you know what I mean! Read a different line!
Yes! Yes, that's it. I can feel the illusion's grip loosening. Keep going! Read the other lines!
Agh! Wrong line. Wrong line!\n\nUgh … feels like my head's cracking like a melon! Say something else. Anything else!
Ow! No, no, no! That's not it. Honestly, how hard is it to read three lines?\n\nStart over if you please!
Vivec preserve me. You already read that one, you dunderhead! Read the other line third. Crows or somesuch?\n\nCome on, now. I believe in you. Sort of.
Rigurt said we'd catch Thane Hraldi's silly fish for him. But Rigurt must admit something that will come as a surprise to you. He … is not a talented fisherman.

What do you think? I'll have my tusks ripped out and bleed to pay my debt to the clan.\n\nIt's fitting, really. I made our kin suffer. I disrespected my chief. I caused many deaths. If this is what the Code demands, then I accept it.

I'll work on redeeming myself. I still care deeply for the miners, and I won't see them suffer, either at my hand or at Chief Urzikh's.\n\nI plan to talk closely with the chief, if she'll have me, so we can come up with solutions that work for all.

All right? No, I don't think so. Mazog is my wife. To see her hurt—disfigured … it's a pain few could bear. But we're Orcs. We bear burdens and keep moving.\n\nWe'll work through it. We'll show both the chief and the clan how tough we really are.

Perhaps I was too quick to judge. I disrespected her, but she still found it in her heart to free Mazog.\n\nI will support Chief Urzikh going forward. You have my word. For the good of the clan, maybe we can find middle ground.
Rigurt may be a poor angler, but he is still the best ambassador in all of Tamriel! \n\nAnd he happens to know how to acquire the perfect fishing bait from his time among the Argonians in Shadowfen.

A mushroom with a silly Argonian name. Too many sounds for poor Rigurt's tongue! \n\nBut it grows in the dark, dank pits, of Shadowfen. Pits just like this! If we look around, Rigurt is sure we'll find it!

Rebuild. I'll work with Mugha and the others to improve our processes in the mine. Reiterate the advantages while taking their concerns into consideration. \n\nTaking Mazog's tusks is just the first step to restoring order and moving forward.

Rebuild. I'll work with Mugha and the others to improve our processes in the mine. Reiterate the advantages while taking their concerns into consideration. \n\nShowing Mazog mercy is just the first step. I have a lot to do.

If I know Gabrielle, I need to spend some time getting my details right. I might even go back out there for some more research.\n\nDon't worry, one of the more experienced Antiquarians here has offered to help me.
And then I go brave the lioness in her den.\n\nThat's a very Breton way of saying I will present my facts and make the case that I'm right. And I am right!

I think I'll wait a bit. \n\nGabrielle might assume I'm just an over-eager newcomer if I present to her without preparing. I want to organize my research so she can look it all over. I want her to see that I didn't make wild assumptions.

Hopefully, she'll see that my theory has merit. It may not have all the facts she wants, but that just means it needs more investigating.\n\nShe might even agree to let me continue my research in the field; this time with experienced help.

What else could it be? \n\nThe job offer I responded to promised profits from a new and exciting secret mining venture. But ever since we got down here, we've had nothing but trouble. There's something evil in Blackreach, and it ain't worth the money.

I don't think either of them really believe that. They're just trying to keep everyone from panicking. \n\nThey can only make excuses for so long. Sooner or later, they'll have to come to terms with the fact that something down here wants us all dead.

Hard to say. They seem capable enough, but what if what we're up against is too big for them? This whole place is one giant unknown. Blackreach doesn't abide by the same rules as everywhere else … maybe its spirits don't either.

No. I need you and you've already been seen working with me.\n\nWhat I don't want to do is risk bringing an unknown factor into the equation, especially not an unknown vampire when vampires are clearly working with the Icereach Coven.

A clever woman? Out here? Nords are extremely distrustful of magic, especially Nords from Western Skyrim. I'm surprised the people of Morthal tolerate her presence.\n\nIf anyone can help Fenn figure out the coven's ritual, though, it would be her.
How can I refuse? You and your infuriatingly dense friend taught me a valuable lesson on this day.

You taught me that my feud with Thane Svyne doesn't matter. Nothing matters. \n\nA life of prayer and worship can come to naught, and some random fool can accomplish your dream in a moment. There is no justice in this world. So I will meet with him.
Ha! Is that right?\n\nWell then. Sounds to me like you could be one of the Undaunted.
A league of like-minded adventurers. Every one of us eager for riches and glory. Sound like anyone you know? \n\nSo what do you say? Think you can be one of the Undaunted?

Mordra can answer that better, and probably more to the point, than I can.\n\nBasically, we're adventurers. You look like you'd fit in well, you've got that fearless look about you the Undaunted are known for.

I'm not giving up on this venture. Bitterblade Mining Consortium doesn't need Urlvar, and neither do I. \n\nNow that we know what we're dealing with, we can take more reasonable measures to keep people safe. We're not sacrificing anyone else.

Maybe, but we can take precautions. It won't be perfect, but it's a lot better than giving up innocent people.\n\nUrlvar thought that was the only way to save Dusktown. But he was desperate, and he panicked. I won't make the same mistake.

I had no choice! We couldn't stop the attacks ourselves. We would have kept losing people if I hadn't made a deal with him.\n\nAt least working with Bruik allowed me to control our losses. Losing one worker a week instead of five felt worth it.

Could be that the Elves our ancestors fought soured our taste for magic. Or maybe there weren't enough skalds singing about wizards going to Sovngarde. Might be that Nords just prefer their natural talents.\n\nEither way, magic isn't popular here.

No … I thought I had him in the palm of my hand. I provided him with a steady supply of blood and I mistakenly thought that meant he relied on our working arrangement. \n\nHe showed me the error of my ways. Now, I'm paying the price for it.

Yes and no! I was rather excited about the possibility of encountering a spirit down here. This is unmapped territory in both the physical and spiritual sense, after all. \n\nBut I am glad we were able to help these people. It feels good to be of use.

Perhaps. I still sense dark energies here. This place writhes with uneasy spirits. Overseer Urlvar was the culprit this time, but with him removed perhaps the true spiritual mysteries of Blackreach will unravel themselves.

Happiness is not something I often associate with my line of work. Dealing with the dead is often a somber affair. But, dealing with the living can be too, I suppose.\n\nI am merely satisfied with our end result.

Nope. I was just making the stew like always. I even added those stinky morels Master Dren likes so well. I heard him mumbling in the next room, then pop! He's a bottle. Or in a bottle. I don't know. Makes my head hurt.

Uh uh. My Pa always said to steer clear of mages. They're liable to put a hex on you. Turn you into a chicken or such.\n\nI says to myself, Master Dren's got it bad enough. Better to be a Dark Elf in a bottle than a chicken in a bottle, you know?

I just lost the person closest to me, and gained a responsibility that could determine the fate of all Skyrim. Forgive me if I seem distracted.\n\nThere will be time to grieve for grandfather later. For now, I must carry out his mission.
Theoretically.\n\nUsing my knowledge of alchemy and Old Mjolen's understanding of Reach magic, we should be able to figure something out once we know what components were used in the ritual.

We knew that vampires were working with the coven. And Old Mjolen and I can say with certainty that the feral harrowfiends are byproducts of harrowstorms.\n\nYou think the assassin was one of the vampires in league with the coven?

An eye patch? That's uncommon. And this insignia. I've seen it before. It's the same as the symbol that decorates the urns smuggled out of Bangkorai.\n\nIf it belongs to a vampire bloodline, I'm not familiar with it. I suggest you ask Mjolen.

Hm. The bloodfiends in Rivenspire, maybe? You know, those vampires that the Lightless Remnant drove mad. But this seems different. There's intention here. She's looking for something.\n\nLet's pray she never finds it.

No. Thank goodness, right?\n\nWatching someone suffer through the initial effects of the vampiric malignancy is no spring picnic, but at least you know they'll be sane when it passes. This, though? I don't know what this is leading to.
An icy rime clings to the wolves, sapping the heat and life from their bodies until only a frigid, shambling corpse remains.\n\nYou are safe from them here, but be mindful out in the wild.

Mother Wolf will guide you along the way, but you must still complete the hunt and find him. If the assassin eludes you, use the medallion to recover his trail.\n\nThe Wolf is relentless in her pursuit. The question is, will you be like the Wolf?
Why, with anyone other than you, of course! You really thought I meant to exclude you? You wound me.

Was. Who was he. Past tense.\n\nMaelmoth was one of Skyrim's most gifted illusionists—a contemporary of the great Shalidor, if you can believe it. Of course, he's been dead for hundreds of years now. I'd say his claim to secrecy died long ago.
Precisely. The spell turned my knowledge of the natural sciences against me. Crafty, yes? A lesser intellect might have evaded the trap entirely. How's that for irony?

Oh, countless secrets! He was a master illusionist after all. Unfortunately, illusionists always cloak their discoveries in puzzles and traps. Insufferable, if you ask me.\n\nNo matter! I never shrink from a challenge of the mind!

That I do not know. But he seems to be increasingly agitated as we continue to investigate. I may deal in spirits more often than I deal with the living, but I know when I'm being led by the nose. \n\nHe's hiding something. Let's find out what.

Ah, of course! These listings are where other adventurers, much like yourself, can declare their interests. Those of a similar proclivity can join up together and form guilds.\n\nTake a look. This one is sure a group suited to your needs awaits you!

Captain Ageran's wounds are fresh, which means the culprit can't have gone far. We didn't see anything on our way in, so whatever attacked him must have left through the other side of the cave. \n\nWe should see if we can pick up its trail.

The listings are a place for like-minded adventurers to come together! The world is quite vast, no? Many times it is difficult to find those with similar interests to your own. \n\nWith this register, you need look no further!

Corpse, eh? Well call me not surprised. He never was any good at this. Always came off like he was better than us working folk. But, only thing he was good at was slacking.\n\nAll right, I'll pay you for his samples.
Boo hoo. Mining is expensive and hard. It's even harder down here. Miners only survive when they're tough.\n\nHow about you take your "friendly" and move along?

I'm not quite sure. Claudina and I travel all over, wherever the work takes us. But wherever we end up, I hope you'll seek us out! Next time you see me, I'll be much braver and have quite a few more cases under my belt.
Indeed. I … acquired a powerful scroll from the Mages Guild. I thought it might direct me to a legendary illusionist's secret sanctum! Unfortunately, reading it led me to this dismal state.

Yes. The mage, Maelmoth, hid them all over Solitude. Etched in wood, tucked under cobblestones, and so on. Just another one of his insufferable games.\n\nIn retrospect, I probably should have gathered the verses before, you know … all this.

I don't know of any Ashen Lord, but exarch … I came across the term after the incident at the mass grave in Bangkorai.\n\nIt's a rank, used by the ancient army. Its members were buried in that unhallowed grave and their remains were smuggled here.
Well, I haven't seen anyone like that.\n\nNow pick up a shovel and help me, or hork off. I can't afford to lose this job.

Can't say that I have. And I haven't seen any ghosts or monsters, either, come to think of it, even though the rest of the town can't stop talking about them.\n\nAnyway, welcome aboard and good mining!

You saying she's dead? Damn. She was a fine-looking Nord girl. Shame that happened. \n\nShe, uh, leave a note or anything? Not like in that way, but maybe she had some feelings for me. I know she fancied me, even if she didn't say so.

Reeh-La is dead? Ysmir's guts! He was a good worker, even if he was a lizard. I thought he'd catch a break prospecting; pay off some bad debts of his. Poor luck for him.\n\nI'll take the lizard's samples and pay you for your trouble.
Imagine that. <<1>> is  dead, eh. Well, that's unfortunate.\n\nI don't suppose you found some ore samples he was supposed to collect, did you?
Who knows what these vicious Witchmen intend? But I want to find her before they can do any more harm.\n\nSince you and Hafskjar survived the camp, do you think you can make it into that tower?

I—I don't know, but that's the impression I got from the witch's conversation with the exarchs. I wish I knew more about this Tzinghalis and Ulfra, though. And the Ashen Lord, for that matter.\n\nThat's why I want to check the ritual site.

Anything that tells us more about what the coven and its allies are trying to accomplish. Maybe something about this Ashen Lord. I'd even settle for a clue that points us to any other strongholds they have down here.\n\nWe need something more to go on.

Because I don't trust the security at the palace. Vampire or not, the assassin had too easy a time getting close to the queen.\n\nBesides, Svana feels comfortable at the tavern. I figured she needed some comfort after watching her mother die.
Right. Easy as honey-baked pie. It's not like you came here at the behest of his most-hated rival or anything.\n\nLook, I'll do my best to get him to listen. You have my word on that.

That's nice of you to say, but I'm not sure I believe that. I hope she's watching all this from Sovngarde. Bet she hates it there.\n\nLook, I'll do my best to get my father to listen to you. You have my word on that.
Every plan has risks. I'd be happy to have another ten to twenty wagons available, just to be sure.

Despite claims to the contrary, Nords prefer the drink to the sword. Pity Orcs can't say the same.\n\nTell Svargrim and Jorunn that the Nord still standing when the ale is gone gets to be king and we won't spill a drop of blood! Maybe some ale, though.

I know nothing about Bjora's heritage. She was alone when I found her. A small baby wailing in a crib. If she was so important, why would those barbarians put her in harm's way?\n\nBesides, she's my daughter now. I don't care what she was before.
I knew it. Wise of him to send an associate like you to offer an olive branch. Cowardly, but wise.

Hmph. Far superior to Narsis Dren is no great accomplishment. Nonetheless, I feel I can trust you. It's there on the table.\n\nDo not prove me wrong on this. We treasure all arcane texts, but Maelmoth's riddles are of special interest to the Guild.
Ugh. Can't you see I'm in pain?\n\nI'll answer a few questions more, but I need to escape this place. I … I can't think.

Yes. The Ashen Lord.\n\nNo one mentions his name. They only whisper about him. The way peasants whisper about Alduin while they clutch their prayer stones. I've never seen him, but if Essenia swore fealty to him? He must be something horrible.

How would I not? Ancient mysteries are Narsis Dren's stock-in-trade! No arcane relic or lost antiquity evades my gaze for long.\n\nSurely you've read some of my books? They're best-sellers, assistant. I can get you some at a very reasonable price.

Only that it would unlock our true potential. Our hidden strength. Unless my hidden strength is vomiting bile until nothing's left but heaves, I think she's missed the target. What a load of skeever piss. \n\nIt did drive a few vampires mad, though.

I mean just what I said. They went feral. Hissing and growling like animals. Sometimes I feel like I'm bound for the same fate. It's been harder to think. To talk. The light gets too bright sometimes. Even candlelight.\n\nI have to find a healer!
Better than most. I wager that's why Essenia took her to the laboratory.\n\nThe Blood Queen's looking for something specific. I don't know what it is, but your Adusa might have it. Too bad for her.

Our portly friend wants a fine Nordic meal, yes? Then Rigurt will make him the mouth-wateringest Nordic roast boar that he's ever had!\n\nAnd to assure success, Rigurt will elevate this dish with techniques he's learned from across Tamriel!
Friend, Rigurt spreads the joy of Nordic cuisine across all of Tamriel. He has also seen how other cultures fill their bellies! This will be easy.\n\nAll Rigurt needs is help getting ingredients!

She's as well as can be expected. With that damned curse broken, her health has recovered, but the gloom it left behind still hangs over her.\n\nBut enough of the past, we have troubles enough in the present to deal with.

When we escaped Greymoor Keep, Tranya and Skor set up a sanctuary in the grotto. It was a safe place for those of us who had been freed to rest and regroup. \n\nSince the disease, however, we're not welcome in the grotto. We've made do in these caves.

We never made it that far inside. And when the storm hit, it was all I could do to get out and seal the door behind us.\n\nIf the jarl sent you and you're intent on entering the barrow, I won't stop you. But if you emerge as a monster ….

Well, now that I know what the problem is, I've got an advantage. Smartest thing to do would be to save up some more money and do my best to safeguard my wares.\n\nProvided the fish keep biting, at least.

Rigurt the — that oafish Nord ambassador is here? Of course he is. Just when things seem to be going smoothly, he shows up.\n\nIf Rigurt needs meat, why does he send you to bother me? Skyrim has its share of butchers. Competent ones, even.
Great. Another lovely example of Skyrim's hospitality.\n\nFine. The boar carcass is yours.

Perhaps. I came to Skyrim to try kiviaq made by real giants. It's a delicacy. There's a giant camp nearby, but no one will guide me to it or dig up the treat for me. The giants bury it, you see.\n\nYou want that boar? Bring me the kiviaq. Fair trade.
Well, I guess even that boor has good taste.\n\nThe only thing I have fit for a fancy meal is a boar carcass I've been aging. But it's going to the jarl's table. Tough luck.
Yeah, so what? He was going to die sooner or later. I didn't make him take the job, so him being dumb don't make me guilty.\n\nJust give me my samples and move along.
Fair warning—she's stubborn. More stubborn than I am. So, watch out.
It was that damn <<1>>, wasn't it? Always mooning over her. Never thought she'd be stupid enough to fall for him.\n\nWell just give me the samples. I'll pay you for the trouble.

It's not just me! Most of the clan's uneasy with it. Orcish culture is built on tradition. Hard work. Without that, we're nothing. \n\nWe've mined for generations using nothing but pick and spade. To turn our backs on that is just foolish.

Yes and no.\n\nSure, we collect twice the ore in half the time, but it's dangerous. We're miners, not mages! Nobody knows what the tusk they're doing with that stuff. A disaster like this was inevitable.
Good luck making him see reason. You'll need it.
Sure, whatever you say.\n\nI'll take the samples. You take the money—Argonian.

I cannot lie, I do. But no one can know! Hagravens are filthy, revolting beasts. If anyone hears that I've eaten one, my title will be revoked! I'll be the shame of Western Skyrim!\n\nHow can something so vile taste so good?

Damn you. Both of you. Fine, I'll forget the feud with Hraldi and go to this meeting. But I have two conditions! First, you can tell no one about what I ate here today.\n\nSecond, whatever seasoning's left over is mine.

Barsis Fren? As mud is my mother. To tell me such an utterly transparent lie, you must be truly desperate. Honestly, I am embarrassed for you.\n\nYou may read the journal if you promise to keep Narsis out of my library. Barsis Fren. By the Hist ….

Rigurt must focus on tending the fire. In the meantime, you should make sure the roast boar is perfect. If it is too bland, add more seasoning. Too dry, baste with howlwater. Too tough, tenderize it!\n\nSo, friend, are you ready?
That so? I knew he was a sneak. Thought he could spy here without me catching on. And I know you think I killed Ghamborz—but you've got no proof. \n\nGive me the ore and take the money. It's over.

Well, advanced scholarship always involves a bit of give and take. For example, an elderly mage I met in Riften made a … modest contribution.\n\nBut make no mistake, it was I who cracked Maelmoth's riddles!
Skor is the other werewolf I escaped Greymoor Keep with. \n\nHe's the bravest out of all of us. He cares deeply about the pack, which is why he was one of the first to go after Rasir.

He was. For a time. Struck me as something of an obsession, if I'm being honest.\n\nFifty years he's been at this Maelmoth business. Fifty years! Can you imagine? That might be a reasonable period of study for an Elf, but for a Nord? It's untenable!
Yes, yes, of course. All the credit he deserves.\n\nI am generous with my praise. You'll see soon enough, assistant!

Of course I did! What kind of mer would I be if I let that doddering fossil waste his scant remaining years chasing riddles like this? I may be ambitious, but I am never cruel.\n\nI took his notes as a personal and professional courtesy.

He told me to stay behind. He didn't want any more harm to come to me. I tried to convince him otherwise but he insisted.\n\nI agreed to stay behind and watch over the others, but when neither Skor or Rasir returned, I got worried.
The cat? Where is she? \n\nOh, I can see in your eyes. She's gone. This note say anything?
Knew I couldn't trust her. Job gets hard and she runs out. Heh, just like her to leave the dishes to me. Damn cat.\n\nFine, I'll take the samples and pay you for the news.

Stuff? No, dear stranger, I would like you to gently place me inside your pack among your no doubt precious belongings, and carry me inside so that I might observe your progress.\n\nAre you quite ready?
Lovely! Then pick me up and let's get going. I'd like to get back into my own body sooner rather than later. Wouldn't you?
I don't think I need to stress to you just how terrible my existence is while I'm trapped inside this horrid thing. Take what time you need, but please bear in mind I am suffering. Miserably.
Fine. I'll be here … unable to move, trapped inside a doll, completely and utterly helpless. Take your time, won't you?
That's comforting. He must have been fairly confident to attempt a test.
Impossible to say, but I hope with all my heart that he was.\n\nThe cavern he writes about is nearby. We have a lead. Let's investigate.
It's funny … he's always been the strong one. They did awful things to him at Greymoor Keep, but he never broke. He inspired me when I felt like giving up.

I'm not totally sure … he doesn't talk about it much. I know they experimented on him more than the rest of us, because he was the strongest. He's said they altered his body, made him take on strange mutations. \n\nIt makes me sick to think of it.
Well aren't you all upset? But then, you didn't argue about getting paid. I'm sure the Consortium would find that interesting.\n\nSeems like you're in this as deep as me—partner.

He ran. Skor chased after him. Looked to me like they went east.\n\nI wanted to help, but I'm too weak. I could barely stand. I lost track of him after that. I don't know if he survived, but please, you have to look for him. His cure works!

I don't remember much, just the rage. When I woke from it, Rasir stood over me. He was ecstatic, babbling about his cure being a success. \n\nBefore I could ask him anything, we were attacked by Skor! It all happened so fast.
Be careful.\n\nSkor's changed. He is no longer the man he once was, the disease has completely destroyed his mind. He won't hesitate to kill you.
Pah! Thane Hraldi knows I'm here. I'm not going to give that steely-eyed blighter the satisfaction of knowing I was the first to quit!

Do I look like the kind of Nord that would indiscriminately shovel anything down my gullet? I was holding out for an exceptional meal before, and that hasn't changed.\n\nIf this Rigurt character can't make something worthwhile, the pigs get it.
He succumbed to the affliction. His mind is gone, there's nothing there but rage.\n\nI thought there might be something left of the man he once was, but he's too far gone. He nearly killed me.

Rigurt samples meats from all across Tamriel. Some squirmed! Some barked! Some fought! But it was in Greenshade that Rigurt ate the finest cuts. \n\nI don't know what kind of animal it came from, but Farethor said it honored the Pact!
Thank you … please don't let my work go to waste.

I don't know. I just ran, hoping that I'd lose him before I lost too much blood. He's still out there somewhere. \n\nPlease, you have to find my cure. I'm too injured to retrieve it myself, but my instructions will lead you to it.
Rigurt … doesn't exactly remember? It's strong stuff, prized by the clans of Wrothgar. It's sure to make a wonderful ingredient, friend!

Once I thought I had a suitable mixture for the cure, I knew I needed to test it. \n\nDuring my search, I found Brigvar. He was in a late stage of the affliction. I didn't know what would happen, but I had to try.

Yes. I felt hopeful for the first time in weeks. But before I could even observe the full effects of the cure, Skor attacked.\n\nI ran as hard as I could. I didn't want to die having only cured one person. There are so many more that need my help.

We may try tainting a water source with the cure, if we can locate a big enough group of afflicted in close proximity to each other. Otherwise, we'll try to find subjects individually and hope we survive long enough to administer the antidote.
Why shouldn't I? It's what I'm made out of.
Of course I am! I just need a moment to reflect.\n\nAfter tasting that meal … I don't think I'll ever be the same again.

And the widow of Shor, yes. You know your people's history! What a welcome change of pace.\n\nA shrine dedicated to her lies southwest of here, near Chillwind Depths. We'll probably find Maelmoth's next farce. I'll meet you there.
I plan to set her loose. Seeing her here, staring into her fathomless eyes, she torments me! I want nothing more to do with her!
Not today. We are only two thanes, Svyne and I. But we have the ears of other thanes, that have the ears of jarls, that have the ears of the king.\n\nIf peace is prudent, word will reach the throne.

No one would look favorably on a resurgence of the Dragon Cult, no matter how laughable the effort. I threatened to expose them, and rather than kill me outright, they decided to humiliate me. \n\nIt's demeaning! I am a distinguished mage!

Haven't you learned enough? I am merely an innocent scholar who wandered into the den of this sloppily reformed cult and was subjected to eternal misery for no reason! \n\nNow, come on. We have a body to reclaim!

Who can say? Western and Eastern Skyrim split on bad terms. No point trying to put gravy on that pig. But while the East has prospered, we … well. Life's not bad. Could be better. Jarl Morryn and Rigurt will tell us how much better it might be.
Then I suggest you run. Though if you fail to return, I suppose I can intuit the test results myself.

Strange creatures that don't belong. \n\nThey jumped us at the door, but it was odd, it was almost like they just winked into existence! There were bright flashes of light and then they appeared out of thin air and started to attack.

Damn, the coven's moving faster than I expected. We still need to go there. Assess the damage. Talk to Jarl Olfwenn or whoever's left that's still in charge.\n\nI need at least one more jarl to talk to my father. Like a moot. He's always enjoyed moots.
With the clues in Nel's Hidden Loves and the return of Petraloop, word will travel fast among bards!\n\nI hear the vibrations among students, members and alumni of the College already.

I'll survive. Now that I'm sure the cure works, I need not worry about the affliction. Thank you for your help. I owe my life to you and Tranya. \n\nPlease, check on her and the others. I'll join you once I catch my breath.

The flow of escapees to our Grotto is small, but steady. Word of our community spread quickly. That is why I stay here instead of returning to my home. I can't bear the thought of anyone facing this darkness alone.

Rigurt has this under control, friend! There is no need to bother Jarl Morryn. We will find the thanes, end their feud and begin the talks before she even finishes her mead!\n\nRigurt just hopes she saves a drink for him!

You mean, if you and that buffoon manage to do what neither my father nor grandfather could, despite praying to the animal spirits and fishing their entire lives?\n\nSure. I'll also attend this meeting if it starts raining mead.

Reddharn, the Jarl of Morthal. He watches over our little village. Before I arrived here to marry him, I thought it would be something like from a bard's song. \n\nMorthal … disappointed. But Reddharn is a good man. I am proud to stand by his side.

One of the college's greatest bards, Nel Farsong, took them. She thought if the instruments went missing, the fighting could end. So, she hid them throughout Skyrim. Which ended the war, but only because everyone was enraged at Nel.

Hircine's fetid breath, that's it! Look, I managed to escape from Tzinghalis's tower, but my pack mates are still chained up in the Lightless Hollow.\n\nUse that key to set them free, then I'll tell you how to find Fennorian.

Wait … who are you? You're not here to … to prune me? It hurts so much.\n\nEssenia! Essenia did this to me. The transformation didn't take hold, you see? My blood's too thin. Like water, she said. Thin as water!

No! No, please. Every branch … every root. Like a raw nerve. An exposed vein. Please, just let me die!\n\nStop Essenia. Stop her bloodknights. We forfeit our souls. Make it worth something. Make it ….

The crimson ascent! The journey to bloodknighthood.\n\nIt hurts …. She twists your heart—your mind. Draws out the wrath buried in the blood. Makes you stronger. Faster. All it costs is … is everything!

No, but I know he took his notes with him when he left. Perhaps if you looked for clues, there might be a trail to lead you to him.\n\nWe want the cure found just as much as the others. Please, find Rasir. He can fix all of this.

Heh. This one has seen better moons.\n\nI … I do not know if any trace of Essenia's corruption still flows through my veins. Adusa feels weak, but clear-headed. Unlike the bloodknights. Only time will tell, yes?

Hard to say.\n\nEssenia took long notes, you see? Very thorough. One of the Ashen Lord's alchemists may pick up where she left off, but it will take time. Time enough to strike this latest threat to Skyrim through the heart.

A good question. One Adusa has asked herself many times. Unfortunately, only one person can answer that, and he is far away.\n\nWe will have time to think on this later. First, we must escape this place, yes?

I … I honestly don't know. I hope so.\n\nThere's so much I don't know about the Ravenwatch bloodline. About Verandis's origins. Will the strength of our blood help her heal? Or will it cling to Essenia's experiments all the more? It's a mystery.

Yeah, you're right. I'll keep a close eye on her. And I have a few alchemists that owe me favors. The important thing is that we're together.\n\nSisterhood is a powerful bond. It'll take more than some gross experiments to break us apart.

Ah, yes, I see that you have. I commend your dedication to the arts.\n\nWhen all the instruments rest in their proper places, I will compose an epic, "An Adventurer's Triumph," to celebrate! You will star in it, naturally.

To you, perhaps! It makes perfect sense to me and my hordes of loyal readers. I did mention that I'm a best-selling writer, didn't I?\n\nPerhaps when you've published some award-winning tomes we can discuss who does and does not make sense!
Am I? Or is the riddle simply repeating what I said?
Yes! It's relaxing. Somewhere we could build a home. I'd show him the beaches, warm waters, and … hmm.
He'd be so bored there. Maybe we'll travel instead. See all of Tamriel while he's still healthy. It will be an adventure for him, but a safe one. \n\nThanks again for bringing him home.

Soon after our escape from our captors. \n\nMy pack was enslaved and experimented upon by a sinister alliance of vampires and werewolves that inhabit Blackreach. They held us in a place called Greymoor Keep and conducted horrible tests on our kind.

Skor convinced me to fight back. He and I eventually overpowered our captors and got our people out. We hid out here and formed a community with others that had been subjected to the torture.\n\nWe thought our troubles were over. How foolish we were.

A testament to its value, no doubt.\n\nNow, a less experienced historian might be troubled by the comically threatening X on the floor, but we know better. Maelmoth would only place such a symbol to confuse us. Right? Right. It's perfectly safe!

She keeps leaning on us to find new veins of ore, but it's nearly dry. We can't produce what doesn't exist! \n\nThat damned stonemelt solution was supposed to speed up the mine expansion. But it went crazy! Now we've got this to contend with, too.

It's not that unusual. Castle Dour is the most defensible part of the city. In the past, we'd gather the people inside the walls. Now my father is using the fortress to house the harrowed. They need to go somewhere, right?\n\nCome on. Let's go.
Yes, that's mine! Eugh … smells awful. Looks like something may have swallowed it.\n\nI guess that was the point, eh? Where did you find it?

Ah, I'd hoped it was a wild animal ….\n\nI'm sorry for whoever it was, but I didn't have a choice. My family is the most important thing to me. I won't let them starve while some thief makes off with a full belly.
Really? Troubling to think a beast like that would venture so close to civilization just for a free meal. \n\nI suppose I should set some traps. I'll probably be doing the rest of Morthal a favor.
A harpy! Nasty scavengers, those things. And they've got quite the appetite for fish. \n\nSuppose I'll have to put up a few nets. Then the winged thieves won't dare swoop down for a free meal!

Who do you take me for? It'd besmirch my reputation to abandon a kingdom in such desperate need of cheer. Maugh does not leave a place less joyful than he finds it!\n\nI'll be coordinating morale efforts from the Lonely Troll, if you need me.

The rest of Karthald fared as poorly as its capital. The hold has been laid to waste, its people dead or scattered. With so few left to rebuild and resettle, I fear the Reachmen will come to claim it long before Nords set roots there again.
