No. Maybe. Truth is, she challenged me in combat and I lost. But only because of her alchemical tricks!\n\nI would have defeated her if she fought like a true Orc, with her fists and her sword!
I'll pledge myself to her, if she'll have me. I was fool enough to follow Svargrim as long as I did, so it's more than I deserve.

Of course. Some may choose to blame her for her father's misdeeds, but I will seek forgiveness from them. There have been enough divisions of blood and feuding. It is a new day. This is a time to mend rifts and forge new bonds.

When things are settled here. Hjaalmarch has weathered these storms better than Haafingar and Karthald—if we can keep the kingdom from complete collapse, it's worth a few weeks away from my home and hearth.

Not in a physical sense. There's a side entrance that any of us could use, but we won't.\n\nThe others asked us to leave until the threat was over. We honored that. None of us can blame them for being afraid.

Because it's not her fault! Her expectations for mine-output are reasonable—generous, even. But some of Thulsgreg's cronies are never satisfied.\n\nI heard rumors that some miners were changing the stonemelt recipe to increase our output.

I don't know. This is rumor, you know?\n\nThe idea is that a stronger potion could cut through more stone. Lighten the work a bit. But Chief Urzikh's recipe is very specific. If someone did mess with it, it would have been guesswork.

You're here to help? Thank goodness!\n\nI was out here with my brother and sister, gathering plants and other medicinal herbs. I'm a healer, you see. Hedrynne wandered too close to this cave. That's when the chaurus attacked her.
Of course, child. All who bear my blessing should know their powers well.
A giant insect. Very nasty.\n\nMy brother needs to remain by Hedrynne's side. Will you accompany me into the cave? If I can gather a few special ingredients, I can make an elixir to heal my sister.

Just wondering if they could bury the hatchet long enough to get us out of this. That business between them is going to come to a head sooner or later. I say let's get it over with.\n\nThis whole disaster is their fault. Both of them!
Great. A famous example of Skyrim's hospitality.\n\nFine. The boar carcass is yours.

Huh. I didn't actually think you'd get it. I'm surprised. \n\nI hope the crows have soured enough. Otherwise it's liable to kill someone. In any event, you helped me, so I'll help you. The boar carcass is yours.
Ah, history. A fading knowledge. \n\nThese walls, built during High King Erling's reign in the first era, both showcase the Nord's mastery of fortification and bear the Divines' blessings.
So goes the story. I hope to ascertain the truth of that with further research. Now, if you'll excuse me? I must return to my studies.

So goes the story.\n\nBy the way, I know your … nature. Watch your back. Something is afoot here involving another vampire clan. I plan to leave sooner than hoped. If you're more adventurous and choose to confront this clan, best of luck.

Of course Thulsgreg blames me. He always blames me! I brought this clan—this family—back from the brink! I gave us a second chance! I … I pushed too hard.\n\nThis is what being a chief looks like. If our roles were reversed, what would you do?

They started off faint, like a low murmur. As the storm grew, we could make out words. And laughter. Like from a child.\n\nThen we saw the spirit in the storm. A young woman running toward us through the field. I've never been so scared.

The spirit faded before reaching us. I thought perhaps the storm had played tricks on my eyes. But the shocked look on Havil's face … it seemed like he recognized her. Before I could ask him, the wolves attacked.
Yes … yes ….\n\nOnce I take a long drink from my flask, I'll join you.

We gathered the information Fenn needs to make an elixir. If it works as he hopes, it will protect my people from the harrowstorms.\n\nTalk to Fenn. Let's find out what else he requires to finish his work.

Oh, no reason. Just rumors of arcane cyclones, and subterranean castles, that sort of thing.\n\nWe go where our trouble-making kin go. And our kin are definitely up to trouble here in Skyrim. I just wish there were more of us.

Rivenspire's issues will keep. For a while, at least. This though? If we let this fester, it'll be on Castle Ravenwatch's doorstep quick as a rabid jerboa.\n\nLike Verandis used to say, Act, lest you be acted upon. Too right.

Right now, I just want to get my sister back. Once she's in hand? I guess we sniff out some reliable allies and plot out where we can do the most good.\n\nI … I just wish Verandis was around. He'd know what to do—allies or no.
I'd … rather not speak about it, if you don't mind.\n\nLet's just say he's far away. Too far away to be of any use here.

Verandis did what he thought was right in Rivenspire. You both saved us all.\n\nIt's hard, though. You know? Sometimes I glance at his empty chair and … ugh. This isn't helping! I keep thinking there must be a way to …. Never mind. Adusa first.

Oh, that's right! We've never had the pleasure. Melina Cassel of House Ravenwatch, at your service! I trust Fennorian explained what that means, so I won't bore you with the details.\n\nSuffice it to say that I'm here to help.

Indeed! Count Verandis provides a safe haven for our kind and teaches us how to live with our special gifts in a manner befitting nobility.\n\nIt can all be a bit suffocating, but without his rules we wouldn't be any different from feral beasts.

Oh, we're very close. Maybe it's because we're the youngest members of the house, but there's a connection between us that goes beyond just familial kinship. I'm sure he'd tell you the same if you asked.

He's a noble of Rivenspire and the head of House Ravenwatch. He's a vampire as well, if that wasn't evident—but a good one! He's made it his mission to teach vampires how to overcome their beastly urges.\n\nAnd to stop those who refuse to do so.

I didn't realize you knew the truth. No one has seen him since he vanished with the Lightless Remnant.\n\nBut I believe he'll return someday. When he does, House Ravenwatch will be there waiting. As if he never left.

She identified necromantic components as part of the enchantment, as well as Reach rituals, but she isn't an expert on either type of magic.\n\nFrankly, I think she's exhausted the scope of her knowledge.

She is Jarl Reddharn's wife, but that doesn't really describe everything she does for Morthal. She watches over people here. Sorts out disputes, makes sure people get help when injured, that sort of thing.\n\nHopefully she figures this all out.

Well, she's ruthless. No surprise there. A cunning alchemist too.\n\nWhat I find most remarkable is how she's managed to avoid all the scheming and politicking. I haven't heard a single vampire plotting her downfall. That's … unusual.

Or clever. But yeah, powerful is more likely.\n\nBetween you, me, and the stalactites, anyone strong enough to pluck a castle like this out from under a vampire like the Blood Queen is someone I'd just as soon avoid.

From what I can tell, the camp on the northwest coast is where the coven first made landfall from Icereach. It's as close to a home base as they've got. They've established themselves there, so I'd expect it to be well defended, if not fortified.

That's the one we know the least about, but it's where a lot of the Gray Host's warlords are gathering—at least according to the communique. \n\nIt's the best place I can think of where we can get a look at those orders the Ashen Lord mentioned.

The communique mentioned orders to produce more of those medallions, probably to keep pace with the increase in harrowstorms.\n\nI can't guarantee this is the coastal camp where the orders were sent, but it's the only one on the map.

Yes, thanks to you. They're investigating vampiric activity in another part of the region and attempting to identify the vampire we saw talking to the witch matron.\n\nIn the meantime, they left me to deal with my own investigation.
Storms again? I saw the coven conjure a massive storm on Icereach. What did this storm do to the temple and how do you know it was supernatural?

Sounds like what they tried to do to the Skald-King, but on a massive scale.\n\nI'll head back to Solitude and try again to warn High King Svargrim. You go to Kilkreath and see if the coven left anything behind we can use as proof. I'll find you there.
And you as well. Find those damn witch pikes and destroy them before we're all turned into mindless husks—or worse!\n\nAnd keep the princess safe. We need her.
You're perceptive, but why should I tell you anything?\n\nNo, I apologize. I shouldn't have snapped at you like that. I … have reason to believe that someone is out to assassinate me.

Simply put, it could have erased me from existence. I don't know more than that, but that was enough. To not reach Sovngarde ….\n\nI'd rather die at the hands of an assassin than to have never existed. Now, apologies, but I should get back to my day.
I may have crushed a family heirloom under a millstone last year. I'm here in Solitude now hoping to wait out the ire of said family.\n\nIn my defense, it needed to be done. That thing was cursed.
Yes, I am. And while I revere all the Divines and can provide their blessings, my focus right now is Mara due to some confusion that seems to muddle the worship of her here in Solitude.

Exactly. To marry due to tradition or superstitions? To fulfill a hope of being made whole by another? Never. Enduring love must exist between two whole individuals.\n\nThe topic is more nuanced, but I must finish my walk. Mara's warmth be with you.

Some believe that they must marry another as part of the natural progression of life. That to be part of this community fully, they must find another, marry, and have children. Yet Mara recognizes that not all need to follow this path.
Yes. Something even worse than a bloodknight, no doubt. That's hardly a comfort.\n\nJust promise me you'll do what you have to do. Adusa deserves better than whatever Essenia has planned for her.

We're looking for the same thing, my friend. I want to learn more about the ritual they performed here. With any luck, that investigation will turn up evidence you can bring to the queen.\n\nAt the very least, we might figure out their next move.
A feeling. Like the very stones have been infused with powerful magic. It seems familiar, but it's also … intense.\n\nI need some time to sort out and make sense of what I'm detecting.
Thank you, but … let's see what happens when we get there. I won't shirk my duty, my responsibility. But he's still my father. You understand that, right?\n\nEnough of this. We need to find him, now.
I don't know about the rest of the garrison, but I plan on drinking my fill of mead and celebrating a job well done. \n\nI think we all earned a break. Especially the captain.

I guess it depends if the garrison needs us or not.\n\nEna and the captain have a good thing going here. They may bicker like old maids, but relationships that work are hard to find in this business. Don't think we're ready to give that up just yet.

Don't worry, I learned my lesson.\n\nProvided Captain Hingrid doesn't skin me alive for this, I plan to make all future transactions through legitimate sources only. I'm not eager to end up in this kind of mess again.

And my grandfather killed twelve Giants with his bare hands! But at least he had the good grace to string a few of their teeth around his neck before he made the claim.\n\nGot any proof? Or do you want to reconsider making a false report, eh?
Don't start spreading rumors about Reach witches! You go panicking the good folk of Solitude and I'll toss you in a cell.\n\nAnd how is it you know so much about this witch-work?

The word of an outsider isn't worth mammoth spit. Keep sticking your nose where it doesn't belong and you'll wind up just like him.\n\nMind your own business or you'll find that Solitude doesn't take kindly to instigators and strangers.

Trouble from the Reach is as common as snow in winter. That will not be enough for Svargrim to accept the help of outsiders. His hatred of Jorunn runs deep.\n\nI will speak on your behalf, but you and Lyris must bring me proof my husband cannot ignore.

I had a run-in with the coven, too. First at their stronghold in the Sea of Ghosts, then in Eastmarch. They tried to … well, let's say they had plans of an unkind nature regarding the Skald-King.\n\nI stopped them, then came here to warn Svargrim.

Hmm. The coven was also perfecting some kind of ritual in Icereach. Something to do with storms. If these fetishes are from Icereach, you may be on to something.\n\nStill, why involve the locals? Seems like an unnecessary risk.

Good idea. Head there while I circle around from the other direction. Maybe I can catch them before they reach the lodge.\n\nJust be careful. I'd rather not lose another partner at this point in the investigation.
I feared the two were related. I need to know more about what the coven is doing with the remains from Bangkorai. Studying their ritual might help determine how to prevent this from happening again.

House Ravenwatch's resources are limited and Skyrim is a big place. We operate alone or in groups as necessary, depending on the situation.\n\nMy task is to track down the remains stolen from Bangkorai and determine what the coven is doing with them.
Focus on the matter at hand. The longer you delay your search for the queen's killer the harder finding him will become.\n\nWe can discuss Morthal at my hut, once I'm finished here.
In addition to being a lumber town, Dragon Bridge's proximity to Solitude makes it a key strategic location. Of course, that was before Solitude decided to ignore us.

I don't know. It's just a feeling. In the past, we received supplies on a regular basis. Soldiers were routinely rotated through the garrison. We felt … important. In recent weeks, that began to change.\n\nIt's like Solitude is too busy to bother.

If by trouble you mean that we're almost out of food or that we're down to only a handful of soldiers, then I agree with you.\n\nIn addition to the missing caravan, we haven't seen any relief soldiers in quite some time. It's like they've forgotten us.

As I said, she was a conjurer of death. From what I have seen, her magical understanding is incomplete. This curse is wild and sloppy. She approaches power like a babe crawling into a giant's camp.\n\nA shame that Freiwen became caught in it.

I never spoke with her. But, rumors still sometimes drift into my camp.\n\nMaxten was a mystery in Morthal. Appeared late one evening to rent a bed at the tavern. No one saw her in the day, except to bring food. At night she left to wander the woods.

Oh, a forest night stroll is not so odd for a mage. It's the best time to collect mushrooms. And dug up bones hold the most power in the moonlight.\n\nBut, Maxten sought something in the woods. Perhaps she found it among the ruins.
This I don't know. Let us hope that whatever you find in the Kjenstag ruins reveals what she wanted with the young woman.

Interesting….\n\nEven as a child, Freiwen wandered outside Morthal to visit her people. She would come to my hut without fear. I would prepare her rabbit stew as we discussed her life. She told me once that Havil's farm brought her great joy.
An excellent question. So many of the answers elude me for now. With any luck, you will know more once we meet again.

The dangerous and dirty kind, I'm afraid. We may be a scholarly organization, but some of our research is more hazardous than others, so we are often in need of adventurous types to recover materials for study and experimentation.

Not much. I overheard Vund speaking about it as he ordered his warriors around. It's apparently an alchemical monstrosity designed to make everything go boom.\n\nSomeone needs to defuse the explosive reagent before he gets the chance.

Ah, yes. You may not be so familiar with the structure here.\n\nMaestros are the faculty of the Bards College. Master Bards. The Headmaestro manages the College as a whole — currently that is Catrelle Georick.

Certainly! It will likely open a new dialogue about our legendary instruments, should they return in good order!\n\nYou began something truly great here. Maestros that were once enemies have already started talking to each other again.
Thanks, I won't forget this.\n\nNow untie me so I can get my sorry hide out of here.
As soon as we produce enough of it, yes. We saw how it protected Svana.\n\nNow, where did I put my flask?

If you told me the tavern rat we met at the Lonely Troll would become my choice to lead this land, I'd have called you mad. Then again, my king's a skald, so what do I know?\n\nCome on. There's probably something productive we should be doing.

Reignite the warding flame inside Morokei's final resting place. Once it is lit, you must seal the tomb itself.\n\nBut be wary. We are not alone in here. The Dragon Priest did not orchestrate this himself.

Good. You must not let Morokei escape. Stop this madness before it can begin. If only I'd been strong enough ….\n\nAnd please, keep Yrsild safe. Ensure she will see this journey through to its end. She is the future. The protector ….

A necromancer, one with strength the likes of which I have never faced. But all his power will not help him if Morokei emerges from his tomb. The Dragon Priest will consume him and then the world. \n\nI beg you … please stop this from happening.

Gods, I hope so! Haven't we dealt with enough already?\n\nI need to see what happened firsthand. All the suffering and pain my father caused, I can't undo it. But I can make amends. Or at least try to.

Far fewer than I feared when the storm began. Thanks to you and the princess. With the storm over and the Gray Host driven from Castle Dour, my soldiers will get the city back into shape.\n\nAs long as no one else attacks us in the meantime.

I don't know when the rot in him started. It crept so slow I never noticed it, not before it was too late. At some point he became more concerned with holding onto his kingdom than the kingdom itself.

This agreement? I don't see a reason to upset the compromise.\n\nThough future generations of bards … I can't say for certain. But that's why we write songs and poems about our triumphs — to light a path for others in their time of need.

Not until we hold a moot to support her claim, and we need more than a single jarl for that to occur.\n\nIf Svana proves herself as the acting jarl, they might look past her father's failings and make her the queen. Eventually.
I owe you for what you've done, but if I have to raise my sword against you to defend my home, I will.\n\nAll right, let's go see what the Skald-King wants.
I'm not in a trusting mood, but I hope you're right.\n\nLet's go see what the Skald-King wants.

As I said, my investigation began in an ancient burial site in Bangkorai. Draugrkin were using similar urns, filling them with remains. Most disturbing, the ash and bones belonged to a dark army that once roamed the land—the Gray Host.

While it's true that Svargrim and Jorunn don't get along, the Skald-King doesn't want something terrible to befall Western Skyrim. That would be bad for the east as well as the west. Besides, Jorunn was hoping for an opportunity to improve relations.

She'll take pleasure in it, unless you persuade her otherwise.\n\nPlease, just talk to her. Convince her not to punish Mazog. Urzikh may be blinded by her anger, but she bears some of the blame, too. A failure in the clan is a failure of the chief.

An excellent question. For many of my children, greater thirst reveals greater power. Starvation makes their hearts boil over—heated by the cursed flames that brought me to new life.\n\nI have other plans for you, scion.

Indeed. By blood, and sorcery, and accursed rite, I proclaim a new breed of evil. You shall wander the shadows of Tamriel like a bottomless vessel—a child of hunger and delight.\n\nDrink deep from the world, and you shall be rewarded.

Our kind grow more cautious with each passing year. More hesitant. Like great serpents, they feed only once in a great while—barely slaking their thirst for fear of discovery. This displeases me.\n\nYou, child. You will embrace your ravening nature.

Yes, my greatest blessing.\n\nA handful of greater vampires lay claim to a twisted shape gifted to them by the Defiler. Why should my children not possess such horror-wrought strength? In you, we shall see this form perfected.

No, my child. I gave you a taste of the power you will one day wield, but once you return to the surface, your memories of this place will diminish.\n\nDo not despair. With time and experience, you will master all the vampiric arts.

Not yet. But with patience and bloodshed it will become possible.\n\nOnce you display sufficient mastery of your powers and true devotion to me, your ability to pass on my gifts to others will manifest.

No. Gifts of this magnitude require the weight of ritual.\n\nYou must find a site that carries my dark blessing. Only then will your inheritor draw my gaze. Know this: the process takes a toll. Several days must pass before you can infect another.

Ahh, the Salskap. It's a congregation of masterful bards!\n\nFor generations, Master Bards would call for a Salskap in times of joy. They sent word across the region — or even all of Tamriel — for the most talented bards to gather to them.

I have no idea. When I stumbled into this nest of coven witches, I never expected to find a connection to the Draugrkin and the burial urns.\n\nAnd that vampire we saw … there's something more at play than we know. We need to find out what.

No, no! A celebration! A days-long bash!

Bards and skalds gather to talk, play music, drink, tell stories, share recent events, and perform their latest works.

I revived this old ritual to bring us together again. A wonder to behold!
Good. I'm glad that someone has an idea of what we're getting ourselves into.\n\nNow, speak with Lyris. She's done some scouting and has a plan.
His grand gesture is supposed to be a show of support, but Jorunn's underestimated how much the westerners distrust him.\n\nDamn bards and their lofty ideas.

I think it wasn't long after my father became High King. I only remember a foggy day of children's games with the princess, a joyless feast, and a swift departure. \n\nIt might have gone differently if our parents joined us making castles in the snow.

We can exchange intimate details of our lives later. Right now, just know that the safety of all of Skyrim—maybe even all of Tamriel—depends on how this meeting goes.\n\nSo follow my lead and be on your best behavior with her highness.

Indeed! As I surmised, the gray reliquaries contained the remains of ancient Gray Host warriors. They served as a connection to the souls trapped in Coldharbour.\n\nUsing the energy from the harrowstorms, the souls were pulled into the stone husks.
Nothing fancy, just a traditional Nord wake. To mourn and celebrate those we've lost, and cherish the lives we still have.\n\nI'd like you to join us.
Ha! No, no. The rune god, Jhunal, bears the aspect of the owl. But I doubt Kyne minds. Hawk or owl, my heart belongs to her.

I can't leave everything to you, you know. Well, I probably could, but even Ysgramor took a rest now and again. Let us shoulder the burden for a while. I'm sure I'll need to call on you again soon enough.
Count on it.
Whatever his plans were after sacking Solitude, we haven't uncovered them. With any luck the Skald-King will send me on a raid of the Gray Host and I can beat some answers out of a few of them.

He did. But I was by his side day in and day out. If anyone should have seen what he was becoming and put a stop to it, it was me. I owe a lot to Solitude for my failure. If Svana allows me to repay it, I'll be glad.

I have already pledged myself to Svana. I will serve as her court mage. I hope to counsel her better than I did Jarl Olfwenn. For now, I've used my status in the Mages Guild to solicit their aid in producing the harrowstorm elixir.

This was … not what she planned. Maxten believed she could improve her magical ability by communing with the powerful spirits that inhabit Kjenstag ruins. She asked my help with performing a summoning ritual.\n\nBut, it went horribly wrong.

An army that consisted of vampires and werewolves led by King Styriche of Verkarth. They were eventually defeated by the garrison at Bangkorai in High Rock.\n\nIt all happened a very long time ago, but such remains radiate with arcane power.

I tracked remains stolen from a mass grave in Bangkorai. Ancient vampire remains to be exact, and werewolf remains as well. They were smuggled through Solitude to wind up in the hands of the Icereach Coven.\n\nNow I need to determine why.

What we saw in the barrow was a prototype of sorts. This harrowstorm was far more powerful.\n\nThe storm struck the temple, leaving vampires and harrowfiends in its wake. I still need to determine the exact mechanism of these storms.
Great!\n\nYou know, I'd love to help you with that, but I'm afraid membership applications go through Verita. She's just there. Good luck!
If by "unusual" you mean "remarkable," I agree!\n\nQuite the feat of engineering, eh? I made it myself. Well, I designed it myself, at any rate. You know what I mean.

Made childhood in Summerset a real treat, let me tell you.\n\nWant to see a High Elf's face light up? Put them in a room with someone they perceive as fundamentally flawed. It's gross. But also hilarious. We're so insecure, you know?
No, no. Practically everyone does.\n\nI was born with a twisted spine. It makes walking … well, impossible, to be perfectly honest. The chair grants me a degree of mobility I wouldn't have otherwise.

What? Mara's mercy, no!\n\nThere's only so much you can learn there. The Sapiarchs, that whole business with the Thalmor and the Dominion? Too many tight collars and small minds. No one takes risks there. It's just the same tired stories over and over.
Yes indeed! And I've never had cause to regret it … except when Verita really gets going with her chores list.\n\nBelieve me, you've never seen someone more uptight about loosely-folded laundry.

Well, that's how this lot sees me. I always think it best to get out in front of the story, you know?\n\nI focus on historical mysteries. Bizarre and arcane phenomena. You know, the interesting stuff.
Ha! How much time do you have?\n\nThe disappearance of the Dwemer, the secrets of the Hist, the mysteries of the Zero Stone …. Tamrielic history is positively bursting with unexplained oddities!

Oh, plenty! Like, I've got a Cyrodilic bird-person skull buried around here somewhere. At least I think it's a Cyrodilic bird-person skull. Reginus swears it's a terror bird.\n\nSee what I mean? Narrow-minded ninnies, the lot of them!

As a complete waste of time and resources.\n\nVerita would rather while away the days gluing broken Alessian pottery back together. And Ugron? I've never seen him show an interest in anything that hasn't been embalmed.

Ugron, mostly. He hates getting stuck between Verita and Reginus without back up.\n\nSkyrim boasts its fair share of mysteries, too. I've been developing a theory about the Snow Elves that's sure to wow our colleagues abroad.

No, no, no! Your days of taking people's words for things are behind you, my friend.\n\nI've got a good feeling about you. You'll be unlocking all manner of ancient secrets before long. Just promise to share the weirder bits with me, all right?

Oh yes!\n\nI don't want to get into the specifics just yet, but it involves Dragons, Dwarves, Magnus the Divine, and a band of plucky Atmoran skalds. And also a six-legged mammoth. I know that last bit sounds odd, but trust me, it's essential.

The name says it all. It's a treacherous landing where the shallows and shore stay frozen year round. We only use it as place to gather between raids.\n\nCareful on the ice. It's not firm enough to trust and those waters are deadly cold.

Damned Frostbite found out I was planning to leave them, so they decided to beat me senseless and toss me out to sea on that boat with nothing but the clothes on my back. I don't know if I'm glad they didn't suspect Nelfthea too or not.
At least we'd be together. Away from whatever mayhem is unfolding in that raider camp. I'd suffer dozens more lumps if it meant we could lean on each other and limp our way to a better life.
I just ran. The creatures started filling the tunnels but somehow I got out ahead of them. It's all a blur. I just knew I had to survive, I didn't think of anything more than that.
Ugron gro-Thumog. Wise-counsel to Chief Bukhodosh and professor of tomb-studies at the University of Gwylim.
Northeast. Where these monsters landed. You're a fool to go looking, but I hope you find Nelfthea alive. If not, I'll tell her you tried when I reach the Hall of Valor.

Yes. We decided to distinguish it from other coursework. Plucking arrowheads out of the grass on an ancient battlefield is one thing. Searching a Nord barrow for a Dragon Priest's slippers? That's something else.\n\nYou can attest to that, I wager.

Gold's overrated. I'm talking about discovery.\n\nLearning about the past helps us avoid trouble in the future. And we Orcs know a thing or two about trouble. At the rate the world's going, we'll be rebuilding Orsinium again before long. Just watch.
Dungeons, tombs, old sewer ways … even explored a sunken ship or two.\n\nYou know how it is. Greater risks mean greater rewards.

She liked horses. Not that she'd ever ridden one. She was going to work a stable. Learn the trade. I hadn't figured out what more I wanted than to be with her. Now I don't even have that.\n\nNelfthea was too good for this. Too good for me.

Never a soul she didn't care about. Even on a raid, when the rest of the Frostbite were making off with everything they could carry, she'd leave what she could behind for those we'd robbed. This isn't how she was meant to live, let alone die.

That's what I heard the Icereach Coven call the storm that struck Kilkreath Temple. It's magical in nature, the result of some sort of ritual performed by the witches.\n\nI'm still investigating, but I think harrowfiends are a byproduct of the storm.

Indeed. I am proud to call him my husband. Without his strength, this town would certainly fall apart.\n\nWhen I arrived in Morthal for our wedding, I believed my life was over. But, Reddharn made us a fine home here, for which I am grateful.

It's the remains of an alchemical poultice that was spread over the pikes. Smells like rotting fungus, doesn't it? With a little study, I should be able to identify each ingredient in its makeup.\n\nThen I can begin to understand the ritual.

Call it a feeling. What I've seen in my dreams are a jumble of incoherent events and feelings. There's little that I remember that makes any sense, but when I wake there's a pall that hangs over me. Like I've been wronged somehow.
It's not wise to talk about the dead in their presence! Though I'm already being haunted, so … what did you want to talk about?
She must have had his confidence. If he trusted her enough to deliver orders to his highest-ranking soldier, then she held a lot of influence. Enough so that his subjects would offer her deference.

It sounded like she was trying to convince him to sacrifice someone for her immortality. That's worse than anything my family ever spoke of. No one ever mentioned a woman. Hagridden was never married, that I know of. Who was she?

That was always a mystery to me. I was told he forewarned the Reach of an attack, but no one ever said why he betrayed his own soldiers. It never made much sense to me.\n\nI feel betrayal in my heart, but … he sounded astonished by the accusation.

Many condemned criminals do, and if that fate awaited me, I'd have said anything to be spared from this place. Still, I don't feel deception from him. Hurt, fear, desperation, but not deceit. He's still proclaiming his innocence.

Gods, no. I hoped my diction would show that. Perhaps I've lived here long enough to adopt their backwards speech.\n\nI came from Solitude, originally. My father was a wealthy merchant who needed access to Morthal's lumber. Thus, my wedding.

Gods, no. I hoped my diction would show that. Perhaps I've lived here long enough to adopt their backwards speech.\n\nI came from Solitude, originally. My father was a wealthy merchant who needed access to Morthal's lumber. Thus, my wedding.

Oh yes. Even as a little girl, she'd wander out here on her own. Always giggled while chasing the chickens around the field.\n\nEventually Lady Ninetha would arrive to bring her home, apologizing for the disruption. But, I never minded. It was nice.

The Gray Host. It was an army of vampires and werewolves that rampaged across Hammerfell during the First Era. There aren't a lot of records remaining, and even the burial site was a closely held secret.\n\nExarch was a rank, like general, I suppose.
Well, I heard things. Morthal is a small town and people talk. Stuff about evil wizards kidnapping her. But I keep to myself and focus on the farm. No time for storybook tales.

That old witch makes my skin crawl. Using chicken bones and blood for magic is unnatural. Anyone who works with Shor's power should be watched closely.\n\nBut, they say she talks to spirits. Might be helpful when convincing Freiwen's ghost to leave.

Because too much of my wealth is tied up in their enterprises. They were reliable investments for years, but the recent scarcity of workers has taken its toll.\n\nIf either organization collapses, I go out of business as well.

We've never had such a shortage of folk willing to fight to defend their neighbors. I don't know where all the brave souls have gone, but Solitude feels lean as a lone wolf these days.\n\nSo here I am, on the street like a beggar. Dark times.

Western Skyrim doesn't need a bunch of outsiders telling us how to handle our affairs. The high king permits the guild their presence here, but they work through us or not at all. Skyrim can fend for itself. Though we're on lean times.

Nords are fighters. I come from a long line of trappers and hunters. We're no warriors, but we battle nature itself. There's glory in that, I say.\n\nI'll not shame a man who brings bread to the table, but he should be able to cut more than wheat.
I thought it'd do him some good to learn how to live off the land as our ancestors did.\n\nHe begs to differ.
Yes, of course. Narsis Dren is always true to his word.\n\nIf you assist me in following the clues laid out in Maelmoth's journal, I will gladly share the wonders of his Mysterium with you.
Yes, of course. Narsis Dren is always true to his word.\n\nIf you assist me in following the clues laid out in Maelmoth's journal, I will gladly share the wonders of his Mysterium with you.

I didn't. I was determined to make real Nords out of them both. Teach them to live off the land as our ancestors did. Instead I nearly got us all killed.\n\n<<1>> loves my son. That should've been more than enough for my approval.
My boy married a miller's son. He's a soft lad. Never spent a night under the open sky.

A simple stone imbued with the warmth of life. After the events at Kjenstag ruins, I explored new paths of magic for counteracting necromancy. One such trial led to the rune you hold.\n\nIt should protect you from the worst of the curse's effects.

Do you doubt my ability? My practice of magic extends back to when I first heard Shor's whispers as a child. Have faith when I say the rune will protect you.\n\nAnd if it doesn't … well, then, I'll visit your frozen statue. Heh!
Don't underestimate it. For a thing that size, it was cunning enough to stay unnoticed and ambush us. Forget whatever you know about fighting Giants. This is another beast entirely.

A shame, but no. We require something much more powerful to undo magic this strong. Energy directly connected to the curse's origins. The rabbit blood from which I drew the magicka to charge that rune will not suffice.

Maxten misjudged the ritual's difficulty. As she struggled, ice grew over the walls and winds blew wildly. \n\nShe almost gained control, but suddenly Thane Aelstrom and his guards stormed the ruins. Maxten's focus slipped, and the ritual exploded.

Technically, you already will be. Draugr are mummified Nords, you see, so the organs in those jars you'll be retrieving are theirs.\n\nYou should really speak to Nezashul, if you want to know more about the embalming process.

It is not the dead that Nezashul wishes to make more lively, despite how it may seem. He simply wonders if the preservation of the organs plays some part in the persistence of the Draugrs' spirits, as it were, and could it be applied to the living.
I'm an Orc.

I grew up in a very traditional stronghold.\n\nChildhood in a stronghold's not so bad, but everybody grows up eventually. An Orc like me gets two choices: kowtow to the chieftain, or challenge him for leadership. I didn't intend to do either.

Sure did.\n\nThey were pretty sore about it for a while. Damn near killed me on the way out—throwing rocks and hand tools and such. But we've patched things up. You know we Orcs put on a big show, but we're pragmatists at heart.

They wind up getting their cities knocked down by grumpy, Orc-hating neighbors.\n\nThat's what history is all about. It's a shield against an uncertain future. Knowing your past is the best way to prepare for what's to come.

Yeah. With counsel, news from abroad, that sort of thing.\n\nFact is, I've accomplished more in my years at the University than most Orcs accomplish in a lifetime. Tradition's important, but people who don't stretch wind up falling behind. Or worse.
Fighting comes with the tusks. Just one of those things.

But you are!\n\nCome on, you know as well as I do that we Orcs have to scrape for everything we've got. We slide out of the womb fighting. I don't know what stronghold you hail from, but I bet every member of your family can swing a sword.

Queen Gerhyld seemed reasonable. She'll believe us. As for Svargrim, who can tell? I haven't met the man, but everything I've heard describes him as prideful, arrogant, and hard-headed.\n\nEven with the queen's help, there's no guarantee.

I'd like to knock down the palace door, grab him by the throat, and shake him until he listens. That would probably start a war, though, and Jorunn specifically asked me to avoid that.\n\nFor now, let's bring our evidence to Queen Gerhyld.

Stay focused, and keep your feet on the ground.\n\nWe may wield a magic scrying device, but history begins and ends in books. Ink-smudged fingers, research, evidence and debate—that's how you get at the truth. And the truth is all that matters.
Well, I hate to brag, but I am quite famous. Even if I wore the Sapphire Society disguise, the members would immediately recognize my voice. Such is the heavy burden of artistic success.

Reginus Buca. Associate professor at the University of Gwylim—traveling companion and frequent intellectual adversary to Verita, as well.\n\nIt's all in good faith, mind you. She's the one with the gilded reputation. I just like to keep her honest.
More than she might like, I wager.\n\nStill, she needs steady ballast like me. Mara only knows what crazed dissertations she'd publish if I wasn't around to remind her of the facts.
Only that you should let the evidence drive your conclusions, not the other way around.\n\nCold, dispassionate, objective study. That's the aim of a true scholar!

One person's "reckless" is another's "revolutionary." But yes, she can be quite reckless.\n\nA word of advice: take your time out there. The Divines granted man and mer the gift of discernment, but all that cleverness can get us into trouble.

I honestly can't remember ever wanting to do anything else.\n\nMy mother insists I wanted to be a banker as a child. I certainly don't remember it, but who knows? I suppose all bright four year-olds entertain frivolous fantasies like that.
Why is everything so complicated in this part of Skyrim?\n\nAll right, so tell me. What did Fenn agree to do for our half-naked friend over there?

If I was an authority on a subject, I wouldn't want to chase down every rumor myself, especially ones that may or may not have anything to do with my area of expertise. If we do discover a new tribe, I'm sure he'll come to study them himself.

He's the foremost authority on Goblin culture, perhaps the only authority, admittedly. He's earned the trust of, and lived among, numerous tribes to study their way of life. I admire his devotion, if not his preferred subject matter.
Pack mates? Edjar is a werewolf? This just keeps getting better and better. \n\nSo, I take it you know how you want to deal with this particular situation?
Well, if you want to keep your focus squarely on fieldwork, I won't stop you. More cataloging for me!
Of course! What could be more frivolous?\n\nBut no. It's honest work for me. Cataloging, reading, labeling, filing, re-cataloging …. The business of history!
Well enough, I suppose. Solitude's a bit chillier than Windhelm—In both temperature and temperament.\n\nWho knew a city full of bards could feel so cold?

Oh, countless relics! The origin of Tamrielic man is something of an obsession for me. I spent many long months in Craglorn researching the Nedic peoples, and now it's on to the Atmoran immigrants of ancient Skyrim!\n\nJust fascinating!
Well, Dorbin's indolence may be my gain. Look at you. I can see you are ready for action at a moment's notice.\n\nHow would you like to help Skyrim's premiere arts college in its moment of need?

The storied Bards College! Home of honeyed words and tear-jerking tunes.\n\nFor years, a rift within the college threatened to split us apart. One overzealous member hid our antique instrument collection to bring about a truce, but it didn't work.

Excellent question! The only clue to their location lie in a song written by the bard responsible, Nel's Hidden Loves.\n\nJust as I solved the first verse, that instrument emerged for sale at a secret auction. I wish to hire you to recover it.

The barrow is both a prison and a grave. The condemned who were exiled there were doomed to remain imprisoned long after they died. To say it is full of vengeful spirits would be understating things. Be careful when you disturb them.

My name is Claudina Ildene. I deal in the supernatural and strange. Sometimes that means reuniting families with their lost loved ones that were taken too soon, other times it means hunting dark, malicious spirits in ancient ruins.

Phebe and I go where there is need. Our work often takes us to strange places, though I will admit this place tops the list. \n\nThere are restless spirits everywhere. They exist on the peaks of mountains just as they do in the underbelly of the earth.

I'm not sure. I used to try and guess the conclusions of our cases, but I was almost always wrong! Claudina says not to speculate too early. Each case is different, and requires a different approach.\n\nI hope the missing people are safe, at any rate.
Aye. Men half again taller than the tallest Nord. Some kind of half-breed, I reckon.\n\nI didn't have time to ask—they were busy beating my soldiers to pieces with their clubs.

My grandfather used to say that Sea Giants only made landfall during the coldest winters and never stayed for long. They'd slaughter and pillage, then vanish in the ice and fog.\n\nThey're smart, I'll grant you. But they aren't complicated.

Probably. But who knows? I hear vampires can twist people's minds—make them see what they want to see. Maybe Falgravn put a hex on them. Chances are, we'll never know.\n\nAs long as they're all dead at the end of this, I won't lose sleep over it.
It shames me to admit, but yes. All those soldiers, my friends and neighbors, dead. Because of my actions.\n\nAnd now my return home killed even more people. Being near the end is a blessing.

Oh, yes, she was. I loved her dearly. And, I truly believe Maxten loved me back. When she realized she'd accidentally cursed me, she swore to find a cure. But as time went on, growing her necromantic power became her only interest.

Is that what they say? No, I willingly joined her ritual. Which makes me just as guilty for all this death.\n\nMaybe I should have convinced her not to chase so much power. We might still be together, then.

Traveling the Sea of Ghosts, you mean? Ages and ages. Since Ysmir's reign. He vanishes for a few hundred years at a time, but he always comes back.\n\nAt least, that's the tale. Who knows if it's true. All I know for certain is that he's here now.

Hard to say. If he intends to mount an invasion on the mainland, Kyne's Aegis is a good place to start.\n\nBut, I don't know. They mean to slaughter us, for certain. But seems to me he's got his soldiers looking for something. Something on the island.

None, I'm sorry to say.\n\nThere are a few ruins on the island. Dragon Cult built them, I wager. We use them for storing mead, tools … anything that doesn't mind the damp. Maybe there's something in there we missed.

Aye. We're the coastal shield of Haafingar. Or, at least we should have been.\n\nShor's bones, if only I'd paid more attention to the state of our defenses! Maybe we could have …. Bah. No use wringing my hands over it now, I suppose.

Beyond the walls? Hard to say. Every time we try to mount a counter-attack, we limp back five swords fewer.\n\nWith your help, maybe we'll find a few comrades still standing. Not holding out much hope, though.
I made my challenge. Wasn't going to sully my honor by backing down and I damn well wasn't going to let that tusking cheat kill me. So here I am. Busted, but not broken. Hope you fare better.

Now that you mention it, yeah. Lord Falgravn's troops cleared out the caves first.\n\nI figured they just didn't want to be caught by surprise as they marched on the fortress, but maybe they were looking for something.

You know how I told you the weather turned foul? The Span's caught the worst of it. Can't take more than a few steps without seeing a lightning strike up there.\n\nJust be careful, all right? Bad enough you've got Giants and vampires to contend with.

We're werewolves, all right? Do I have to spell it out for you?\n\nLook, Tzinghalis captured us. Keeps us prisoner with chains of Dwarven design. Only that key can set my pack free. I was lucky, but that kind of luck doesn't happen a second time.

Hmph. That will take time.\n\nOur clan knows those tunnels better than anyone. We're in no condition to mount a full assault, but with planning and the right alchemical concoctions, we should be able to selectively cave in the shafts that are overrun.
Tough.

You're right. We will. But part of being an Orc is starting with less.\n\nWe'll find new deposits. Maybe stretch our operation to the hills east of the stronghold. The Nords won't like it, but you know what I say to that.

Oh, you've heard of her? I suppose she is something of a legend of her own right. Nords who dabble in the old ways are a dying breed. She made the cleansing mixture you were given to purify the Shademother's corruption. I trust it'll do as she says.

No, that honor goes to our high priest, Varkour. I am but her humble assistant. She is my mentor. And my friend.\n\nAfter you find the others, I'll meet you at the Pilgrims' Lodge and we can search for the high priest together.

Groans, shrieks, blood-curdling screams. It sounded like wild and feral beasts followed in the wake of the storm. I sent Priest Isonir outside to keep watch, but I told him not to take any unnecessary risks.\n\nWe're priests, not soldiers, after all.

We were on our way to the temple for prayers when an oily-black ichor roiled in the sky. The wind picked up and red streaks of lightning struck all around us. We barely made it to the safety of this cave.\n\nThe storm abated, then the sounds started.
Not exactly. I mean, I admit that vampires often like to stir up gratuitous trouble. But Lady Thorn always kept to herself in the past. Very strange that she wants to build an army now.

I think it was Blackreach. Beyond the ruin it was endless caverns lit by glowing fungus and crystals. Like nothing I've ever seen. I didn't wander far, but I found a working Dwarven lift and rode it out of the darkness before anything noticed me.

Lady Thorn is one of those vampires that we never really need to worry about. Her clan keeps to themselves and rarely disturbs the regular folk nearby.\n\nThat sense of privacy means we don't know too much about her, unfortunately.

I wish this news surprised me. After I left to come home, I feared Maxten would no longer reign in her desire for power.\n\nHer ambition attracted me when we first met. Over time, she grew increasingly fixated. Eventually, I no longer recognized her.

Ah, young blood, the battle for Solitude might be over, but the war's just begun. You've given us a fighting chance, but there's still an army of vampires, werewolves, and witchmen out there seeking our destruction. Now we must beat them back.

My experience with Reachmen extends as far as lopping their heads off on the battlefield, but I've heard rumors of witches planting some kind of pikes around where they conjure these rituals. I'd start by smashing them.
Ah, well, you see back in the ….\n\nHeh. Actually, no. Perhaps that secret should fade into dust. These events show that those ruins best remain undisturbed.

Draw the life out of my soldiers to increase his own power, I suspect.\n\nI've heard tales of old barrows that suck the life out of people, animals … even creaky old Draugr! I'm just glad you stopped him before he had a chance to see it through.

What more is there to know than what you've already seen? \n\nThe fiends are vicious, brutal creations of Lady Thorn's. I recognize some of them as fellow prisoners. She twists them, removes their soul somehow. Quite remarkable, really.
Good. Once we have the cure, we can stop the affliction from spreading. While you collect it, I'll get Rasir safely back to the Grotto. \n\nMeet us there when you obtain the cure.

Thank you, friend. \n\nIt will be dangerous, but we have come too far to let fear deter us. With Tranya by my side, I know we'll be able to save many lives. And we're deeply indebted to you for giving us the opportunity to do so.

He used to post fliers around the area asking for stories about the Pale Man. We laughed them off back then. But, no longer.\n\nAfter the monster took Bear, I sent Aerolf a letter that said where to find me. I pray he gets that vicious creature.
Practically anywhere, believe it or not. Tucked away in chests, in the pockets of bandits, stashed in musty ruins …. Just explore Tamriel as any adventurer would, and you're bound to find some.

No less than you deserve, and no more than you can bear.\n\nYou will command an array of abilities. Some let you influence the minds of the weak, others let you wrench their life away. All inspire a terror no mortal heart can bear.

Still cold, but I feel warmer every hour I'm back home. I can actually feel the fire's heat now. But, I'm still afraid to touch anyone.\n\nI worry that people in Morthal won't accept me back. They whisper about me. Maybe coming home was wrong.
Recover, for now. Mother says I should take my time. \n\nWe talked. A lot. She assured me that I can stay in Morthal. But the damage I did, it was awful. How can I forgive myself?

Ah, yes. You find yourself in the eye of many storms, don't you?\n\nI left the tools required to understand that medallion behind in the swamp. Meet me there with your friend and we shall complete the task.
I spent so much time thinking about this moment that I don't know. There she is, but things have changed. She has changed. We need to get to know one another again.

Oh, thank you! I was worried that Master Dren had gotten lost when I went to get myself some stew. I guess I just forgot where I set the bottle down.\n\nI'll go and get it—er, him—as soon as I finish my stew. It's really good stew.
Maybe. I suggested she visit my sister and their children in Solitude. It's a big city with many people who don't know her. It could be a fresh start.
That's good! A talking bottle makes me nervous and it sure made Master Dren crankier than normal. \n\nI'll bring it here and keep it safe with his other stuff. Don't worry!

He used to frequent the inns of Solitude, begging for someone to join his hunt. Just another madman, we thought.\n\nMaybe if I'd listened to him back then, we could have found the Pale Man together. Then, Merlyth would still be alive.
Heh. One note of pride in all this sorrow. I always believed Hafskjar would act like a true Nord when needed. Good to know I can rely on him in the days ahead.

The survivors will discuss what we do next. There aren't nearly enough people to take back the town. Maybe we'll go to Solitude and recover. But I know we must stay together. That's how we remain strong.

No idea. The Karth region is the only home I've ever known. Once our people settled Karthwatch, I assumed I would die here. Seems the Eight had other plans for my future.\n\nWithout you, though, we wouldn't be alive to see the next sunrise. Thank you.

I believe so, yes. We may see lingering effects across the land, but the source has extinguished. When we flooded Freiwen with her own life energy, the curse drowned.\n\nCurious that Maxten never considered such an approach.
Make sure you find out what he knows about all this. I need the full story. I need to know who's to blame.\n\nEven if it's me.

Nothing new, thank the Eight. But the memories of what those witches put in my head still haunts me. What could it mean?\n\nThe sisters believed I am a descendant of some Reach hero. But I have no interest in that. As far as I care, I am a Nord.

The Jarl and I chose not to discuss the events that lead to Freiwen coming home. \n\nMost are suspicious, of course. Her arrival did coincide with a farm being overrun with undead. But, as I said, they are a superstitious bunch.

Well, yes. But even if Freiwen had returned under the most innocent of circumstances, stories would still be invented. So best not to say anything and let them forget over time.\n\nThank you again for your help. Please visit Morthal anytime.

What, your mistakes? No, no. You wound me! I would never cast you in an unflattering light!\n\nNo, you'll be a mysterious figure, assisting from far, far, far back in the shadows. A helpful, but discreet partner.
Not … yet. Father stays very busy. Mother says recent days have been taxing to him for some reason. I know he will be pleased I am home. But, it would be nice if he told me himself.

More than he does. That's the problem with those two. They're so busy fretting over each other, they miss the big picture.\n\nI don't have a spouse, you see? I'm married to the clan. The clan is my family, and I will do anything to protect my family.
Oh yeah, couldn't you tell? I marked him as full of deer dung from the moment he approached me in Solitude.\n\nBut why all the deception?

Well, I'm going to rest here until my bones fuse back together. Shouldn't take but a few moments.\n\nIn the meantime, go ahead and clear the way. See what you can learn about Lady Thorn's army. And, hopefully, where we can find her.

I can see the vicious logic. Mindless fighters ready to serve like a bloodfiend. But mimicking all the powers of a vampire. They'd be unstoppable.\n\nIt seems you ended her source of these creatures. Whatever that was … you sent it back to Oblivion.

She wanted to find a way to mass produce those revived vampire soldiers we saw. Imagine the strength of an army filled with thousands of those creatures. Or possibly even bloodknights.\n\nUgh, thousands of Talfygs.

Send me on another mission, most likely. They know I get restless if I'm not risking my life for some reason or another.\n\nAt the moment they're trying to track down the lair of some crazy alchemist. Maybe I'll try to find that.

In the first era, an army of vampires and werewolves tried to conquer the land before they were stopped in Bangkorai. They called themselves the Gray Host.\n\nIt seem this Rada al-Saran has resurrected the army—both figuratively and literally.

Recent events keep the entirety of House Ravenwatch on high alert. I came north to help my siblings with those terrible storms.\n\nWe train to handle our kin who get out of control. But the scale of this is so large. I can barely grasp it.

Only fragments. We know Lady Thorn is old. Really old. Records show she's a High Elf who first drew attention in the late First Era. That's when she kicked a local jarl out of this castle and moved her clan in.\n\nBut, really, that's all I know.

I believe the stone husks are incubators of a sort. The physical forms of the Gray Host are reincorporated within the stone vessels through a mix of Tzinghalis's alchemy and sorcery and the magic of the Icereach witches.\n\nWhen whole, they burst free.

If the princess remains in charge of the western holds, I think the chances of true reconciliation are good. My father will certainly do everything he can to make that happen. And so will I.\n\nPrincess Svana … she's become a very impressive woman.

An outsider come to fight outsiders? I wish you hadn't brought your war here in the first place!\n\nSpeaking with Nathari is going to be difficult, even if she would agree to such a meeting. She's taken the clan to Lost Valley Redoubt.

And every one of them gave up their life willingly. They gladly died to awaken the Dark Heart from its slumber! Arana may deny it, but this is the day Namira has been preparing us for. \n\nWe give our souls to the dark in return for eternal life!

You know the Ravenwatch deals with threats all the time. Trouble is, there's never been a threat consisting of a reborn army of vampires and werewolves from the First Era.\n\nSo, yes, I could use some help. We need to know what they're planning.

We know that one of the original ruling members of the Gray Host is rebuilding their army, gathering vampires and werewolves to their banner. And we know they're experimenting with life energy.\n\nSo, what do you say? Ready for another adventure?

The Ravenwatch is dedicated to curtailing the activities of unscrupulous vampires, and the Gray Host is as unscrupulous as they come!\n\nSomeone is rebuilding the ancient army of vampires and werewolves from the First Era. We have to stop them.

Hey, I was doing stuff before you showed up!\n\nLook, there's a new Gray Host. One of their original leaders may be in charge. And they're experimenting with life energy. If that doesn't spell trouble, I don't know what does! Will you help me?

A good question. Let's look around. Not all of the ruin remains intact. Portions have crumbled over the ages. Perhaps we can find a path through the rubble.\n\nJust be cautious. I've seen both constructs and shadowy creatures prowling this ruin.
The Library of Arkthzand. Hmm. Interesting. I assume a Dwarven library houses more than simply books.\n\nAnything else of pertinence written there?

Interesting. The shard reminds me of something torn from the darkest corner of Oblivion.\n\nAs unsettling as that object is, I think we should hold on to it. Especially if we can use it to navigate the void portals.

Absolutely. I'm hoping that the scholars at Bangkorai Garrison can put the entire puzzle together for us.\n\nHow a Direnni Elf, a survivor from the Gray Host's defeat in the ancient past, and experiments with life magic fit together, I have no idea.

My research has uncovered pieces, but I hope the scholars at the Bangkorai Garrison can put the puzzle together.\n\nMembers of the Gray Host experimented with life energy. And at least one of their leaders survived their defeat in the ancient past.

Until we find the source, I can only speculate. We need to locate it, learn more about this energy, and determine the true nature of these shades.\n\nIf Rada and Lady Belain can harness this dark energy, I hate to imagine what they could accomplish.

My research indicates a council ruled the Gray Host. One of those leaders fell out of favor and another survived the final battle.\n\nA Direnni noble with connections to Viridian Watch gave the survivor sanctuary. In return, they made her a vampire.

For the moment. There are an awful lot of evil conspiracies afoot in Tamriel, and not nearly enough Ravenwatch members to investigate them all. \n\nBut this isn't a one person job, which is why we recruited help.

No idea. They're spread out. Adusa, for example, mentioned something about necromancers raising bone giants in Elsweyr, but she probably wanted to refill her moon-sugar stores. Fennorian could be anywhere. He does tend to sneak around.

I suppose you wouldn't have heard of us. We are a bit secretive. \n\nNow's probably a good time to tell you … I'm a vampire. All members of House Ravenwatch are. We hunt bad vampires, and also deal with the occasional misbehaving werewolf.
Not nearly enough, and we're stretched pretty thin. Investigating this on my own didn't seem prudent, so I requested aid. And now here you are, offering it.\n\nI'm touched.

Of course! Despite all the knowledge he gained, he made a mistake. That trapped shade … that's the Gray Host pentarch!\n\nWe should attempt to free him, if not out of mercy, then to determine what he knows about the dark energy and its source.

I'm hoping a scholar of ancient Bangkorai battles named Laurette Diel or one of her colleagues can tell us more about the Gray Host.\n\nWith any luck, they have information about the Gray Host that's not too … outlandish.
Exactly. We need practical facts about how the Gray Host was defeated at Bangkorai Garrison. Hopefully, Scholar Diel can provide them.

The priests have this old holy text that claims Saint Pelin leapt off the garrison's walls, landed among the Host, asked Stendarr for endless blood, and then fed them all without dying.\n\nThen the garrison dropped some rocks on them. See? Outlandish.

I'm not sure. We know the Gray Host has Reach witches among its ranks. Perhaps a local coven has some role in all this.\n\nWe need to speak with Arana. To learn about Reach witch prophecies, we might as well go to an expert.

As you can plainly see, now is not a good time. My fellow scholars and I fled when Septima Tharn and her Daedra-worshiping zealots attacked. \n\nWe barely got out before the first impacts from their ballistae shook the walls.

Occupying the walls. And they didn't just attack the garrison, they conquered it. \n\nThe knights keep saying the Lion Guard will come. That we'll push the invaders out in less time than it takes to brew a cup of tea. But that hasn't happened yet.

You did? Why didn't any of the knights report this? No one tells scholars anything!\n\nIf that's true, and I see no reason you'd offer such an audacious lie, then thank you. Septima Tharn is mad! Had we stayed, she would have fed us to her Daedra.

I'm sorry. Concern for my colleagues and the Pyre Watch warrior who accompanied them has my thoughts in a jumble.\n\nCome to think of it, the Pyre Watch are experts on the Gray Host. Find my friends and I'm sure the warrior will answer your questions.
I heard. Let's split up and go after them. I'll take Kerbol's Hollow. You head toward Evermore.\n\nHere, I'll mark it on your map.

Yeah, my brother Fennorian told me about one he encountered. They're the guardians of an ancient mass grave where the remains of the Gray Host are said to be interred. Probably knows more than the scholars.\n\nFind them and meet me back here.

Even if my mind wasn't clouded with worry, I'm an expert on the Second Era. My First Era knowledge is extremely limited.\n\nThe Pyre Watch knows more about the Gray Host than anyone. Find her and my friends, and she'll provide the answers you seek.

Thank you, friend. When you return with the scholars safely in tow, we should be able to put our collective heads together and dredge up that ancient history.\n\nThat is, if the Pyre Watch warrior hasn't already satisfied your curiosity.

Thank Stendarr! I thought I could make it to Evermore, but I tired myself out. When I tried to pass through the old graveyard, I ran into unspeakable horrors! Thought I was finished.\n\nI'll head back now. Say, did you find that Pyre Watch warrior?
She was. The Imperials tracked us, so she picked a fight with them and led Indouz away while I fled into the graveyard.\n\nPlease, look for them! Bring them back safe.

When the Imperials came after us, she managed to distract them and ordered me to run to the graveyard. I think she headed for the Crypt of the Exiles. I hope she found shelter within. We owe her our lives!\n\nPlease, will you go check on her?

Oh? That's wonderful news! Cogline and I intended to head straight for Evermore, but the cursed Imperials caught up with us. They would have captured us if not for that Pyre Watch warrior.\n\nHave you seen her? Is she alive?
She was, but we ran into Imperials. The Pyre Watch warrior distracted the soldiers and ordered me to flee. Then, she took Cogline and headed west.\n\nPlease, find them. I worry for their safety.

She was! She distracted the Imperials and ordered me to run to this camp. Then she headed for the Crypt of the Exiles. A perfect place to shelter. Or set an ambush.\n\nThe Pyre Watch warrior is very brave. Will you please look for her?
It gladdens my heart to hear that Scholar Diel is safe. But what of the other scholars? Did my efforts to lead the Imperials away allow them to get away?

The Gray Host was a terrible army of vampires, werewolves, and other monsters that pillaged the land. Only the combined might of the Bangkorai Garrison and the Alessian Empire finally defeated them.\n\nThat story, unfortunately, is mired in legend.

The true story may be as enthralling as the legends, but we only have bits and pieces of it.\n\nMagic was involved, almost certainly, but whether it was divine in nature or Alessian sorcery we have never been able to determine.

A Direnni noble? That gives some credence to the historical record. An incomplete parchment mentioned Viridian Watch, but we never saw the significance. It also said that only the worthy could enter the sanctuary. We never determined what that meant.

I know precious little. I never visited the site myself.\n\nThough incomplete, the historical record indicates the survivor hid in a concealed space that they were guided to. Perhaps that has something to do with the idea of being worthy.

There wasn't much. Just that the worthy would be guided to safety. Perhaps that is the key, if you can determine what worthy means to a vile vampire.\n\nAny place associated with the Gray Host cannot be trusted. Evil does not fade, so be on your guard.

I was afraid of that. So much about the First Era has been lost.\n\nI wonder if the Pyre Watch knows anything about the other details we learned. About the survivor and their connection to a Direnni noble.
That matches what we already uncovered and confirms the Direnni connection. \n\nDid you find out anything else I should know?

A riddle. Damn it, there's always a riddle. Well, I say we go to Viridian Watch and figure this out on our own. I'll mark the location on your map.\n\nNow let's go before Scholar Diel tries to regale me with more tales of the Knights of Saint Pelin.

I never should have let Nathari push me aside. She was always drawn to darkness, even as a girl. Lady Belain must have found her eager to believe the right lies.\n\nDoes that letter say what Belain hopes to gain from my sister's foolishness?

Rada al-Saran and I … we have a complicated history.\n\nThere was a time when Rada and I stood united in purpose. To preserve the lives and welfare of vampires. Then, as now, our kin suffered under Molag Bal's curse and the cruelty of mortal hunters.
I don't know. No, this can't be … but it is, isn't it? Damn it. I don't like where this is going.
I've seen this signet before. Or one just like it. My mentor, Count Verandis, had one. \n\nBut why would he have something connected to the Gray Host? That doesn't make any sense.

You're … right, of course. There must be something we're missing. We need answers, and there's only one place to find them. Ravenwatch Castle in Rivenspire.\n\nLet's go. I'll explain more when we get there. I need time to think.

Yes, but we just learned that Count Verandis, my friend, my mentor, and the leader of House Ravenwatch, possesses a Gray Host signet. That disturbs me, and I'm not disturbed easily.\n\nI want to investigate this quietly, without attracting attention.

I don't want to do that until I have more information. Verandis and I … we're …. Look, I'm not just going to run in there and hurl accusations at him. Especially about something this serious. \n\nI want to figure this out before I confront him.

Verandis stores relics he's collected over the centuries in the castle cellar. Always keeps the door locked tight. I trust Verandis, but I need to see what he's hiding. I hope this is all a misunderstanding. That I'm wrong about all this.\n\nWe'll see.

Yes, but we just learned that Count Verandis may have been involved with the Gray Host thousands of years ago and never told us! That disturbs me, and that never happens.\n\nI want to investigate this quietly before I involve the rest of the family.

I don't want it to matter, but it does. Why would he keep this from me?\n\nI need to see what's in the castle cellar. That's where he stored his private possessions. We followed his wishes and never disturbed the place. Until now. Come on, let's go.

Other members of the house might be around. If they see us, they'll ask questions. I don't want to sully Verandis's memory with … whatever this is. Not until we know for sure.\n\nI want to figure this out before we involve anyone else.
A bloodknight. Vampires of ignoble lineage who have absorbed the power of several other kin. Considered quite rude behavior among vampires, honestly.\n\nStrange. Usually they …. Oh no.
A dark relic? That sounds ominous. And quite likely related to the darkness that Arana sensed and I now feel as well. That could be the source of these shades.\n\nAnything else?

What? Verandis, how could you? I don't want to believe it and yet here it is, right before my very eyes. Why didn't he ever tell me? I thought I knew everything there was to know about him. \n\nNo, there has to be more. What else does the letter say?

It's possible that castle no longer exists, but … I want to go.\n\nI refuse to believe Verandis was part of the Gray Host. There has to be more to this. Some piece of the puzzle that makes sense of everything. Are you still with me?

Thank you. The cart's still waiting outside. We'll take it to the docks and travel by boat from there as we follow this map. \n\nGo on ahead. I want to take one more look around. Make sure we didn't miss anything.

Oh, not me. At least, not directly. I'm more of an administrator. Have been since the days of the Longhouse Emperors. Luckily, Ard Caddach likes me and decided to keep me employed.\n\nYou want <<1>>, <<2>>, and <<3>>. They offer jobs on a daily basis.

I work for a group of scholars in Arenthia. We're interested in forming relations with the Reachfolk in exchange for knowledge. I've been working as an ambassador of sorts between my people and various clan chiefs.

We gave our loyalty to Caddach long before he became ard. We are his sword, his shield, and his counsel. There are many threats in the Reach. Too many for one person. So we deal with the ones the ard can't handle.

It depends entirely on what the Reachfolk ask of me. I work closely with them to find out what they need, and then pass that information on to willing adventurers. There's a lot to do, if you have the time and the skills.

<<1>> represents the various clans of the Reach and offers jobs that benefit them. These involve acquiring items or gathering components from specific locations.\n\nA single adventurer can usually handle these tasks without too much trouble.

Some terrible creatures have recently been spotted in the area. The Reach clans can't deal with them and the ard's soldiers are busy with the invading forces, so <<1>> is recruiting adventurers.\n\nA group will be needed to end these monsters.
Curious and deliberate. Good qualities in an adventurer. Usually means you'll live longer.\n\nAll right, what do you want to know?

Yes. Not all Reachfolk are as aggressive as the ones we've encountered outside of the Reach. My goal is scholarly, but these people deal in deeds. Earning their trust is an important step in learning more about their culture. To do that, I need aid.

Indeed. These tasks are suited for those much more capable than I, and they are quite important to the Reachfolk. Ours could be a mutually beneficial arrangement.\n\nWhether it's adventure or reward that you're looking for, I can offer both.

Did you notice the strange storms sweeping the countryside? They aren't natural! The result of rituals performed by invaders known as the Gray Host.\n\n<<1>> seeks help to disrupt the rituals and stop the storms. You'll need a group to deal with this.

A fair question. We exist to protect Caddach and our clan, not the entire city. With all the clans gathering in Markarth, all the infighting, we're stretched thin.\n\nFor once, maybe outsiders can help instead of harm. Let's hope I'm right.

That rabble? We killed more than a few who came here hoping to steal our land. We don't sell our skills for gold. We devote our lives to protecting the Reach and its people. Compare us to them again, and we'll have more than words.

Not completely, but consider what he's wrought thus far—harrowstorms across Western Skyrim to revive the Gray Host. Here, the souls of Markarth reaped to empower the Dark Heart. Both great sacrifices, but I fear worse is yet to come.

A good question. Despite your success stopping High King Svargrim and Lady Belain, the Dark Heart's reawakening provided the Dwarven orrery with a frightening source of power. But to what end?\n\nI'd like you to help me ascertain the answer.

It's clear the orrery plays an integral part in Rada's plans, but the specifics elude me. The Dark Heart, the orrery, the harrowstorms. They are all connected. Smaller pieces of a much grander scheme. Of that much I'm certain.\n\nI need to learn more.
Oh, we're trying to find a dig site. I'm part of the Antiquarian's Circle. We conduct historical research, archaeological exploration, trade in antiquities, that sort of thing.
Ard Caddach and his people carry on and life continues. The deaths, though … the soul has been ripped from this place. They still don't fully comprehend what happened.\n\nI doubt they ever will.
That's generous of you, but we're fine. Just having some trouble with our directions. We'll work it out eventually. I think.

The Circle operates out of Solitude, in Western Skyrim. If you haven't taken a trip out that way, you should hitch a ride on the next caravan or boat to the city. You look like the sort who isn't afraid to get their hands dirty.
You know, time—prison time. At least until Eveline paid my fine because she needed an extra digger. Turns out, I'm the only digger. Lucky me.
That's personal, isn't it? You don't see me asking about your horrible fashion sense, do you? But if you must know, I was a bandit. I wasn't a good bandit, but I made a living just the same.
Me? I'm with the Fighters Guild. This bunch hired me on as protection during their excavation. It's been a pretty cushy job so far—a few bandits, a troll once—but all in all quiet.
Whatever Rada al-Saran did at the orrery, it somehow connected the Dark Heart to the Gray Host. Since then, Verandis has felt its power. I think there's more to it than that, but he isn't talking.

They spend more time arguing than digging, but it's fine. I get paid based on how long the job takes, so they can argue all day. Only had to knock some manners into Davas once when he tried to pocket an antiquity.
Well met, indeed! I'd offer to share this contract with you, but it's a bit, um … lazy? You don't strike me as the lazy type. I spend more time playing with the guar than I do guarding these two.

You'll have to ask him, but, if I had to guess ….\n\nWe failed to stop the Gray Host from sacrificing much of Markarth to the Dark Heart. Verandis wants to make that right. Until he does, it will continue to eat at his core.

When Fenn got his orders to investigate the Gray Host, I invited myself along.\n\nSorry about my temper. It's just that we've been shadowing these bastards for awhile and it looked like the opportunity to strike was finally at hand.

Fenn's the one keeping notes, but Rada al-Saran gathered his subordinates and remaining forces here. It's clear that he's preparing to make a move, so Fenn sent word to the Ravenwatch.\n\nI just wish we knew more about this Darkstorm Rada mentioned.

Possibly. And I've seen Icereach Coven witches among the Gray Host troops.\n\nAfter we dealt with Svargrim and shattered the Gray Host's hold on Western Skyrim, it looks like Rada moved his operation to this part of the world.

Alive and well. She's taken to her role as Jarl of Solitude far better than anyone imagined. The people love her. There's new life in the hold despite all that's happened.\n\nI admit, I'm hopeful for the future, too. Provided we stop Rada al-Saran.

It was slow going, but the concoction he and Old Mjolen produced was the only reason the holds were able to start fighting back. Even after we stopped Rada al-Saran's plan in Solitude, I don't think the western holds would have survived without it.

Other than I think it belonged to Rada al-Saran? I sense a powerful magic has been cast on the item. Auramancy. I recognize it. The technique is remarkably similar to what Verandis uses.\n\nNot surprising, I suppose. They were friends once, after all.

Well, after their defeats in Western Skyrim and the Reach, the Gray Host has regrouped. The ancient exarchs have arrived and asserted their control over the newer troops.\n\nWe also intercepted a courier a few days ago. He carried a coded message.

Amazingly so!\n\nI assisted Svana—Jarl Svana—for a while, helping Old Mjolen and the Mages Guild produce as much of the harrowstorm elixir as we could, but I couldn't linger there forever. I've been tracking the Gray Host ever since.

Shouldn't I be? I was studying abroad when you two were dealing with the Lightless Remnant. And I only just learned that he's still alive. I—I know I couldn't have prevented what happened, but I never even got to say goodbye.
I see that Rada has employed his mother tongue to obscure the message, but I remember his language and the Gray Host ciphers well.\n\nThis—this isn't a dispatch. It's a letter. To me.

Interesting. The Dark Heart hasn't fully awakened, but I did feel it stir.\n\nWe need to find the Dark Heart, whatever it is, and prevent Rada and Belain from using it. I thought it was a Dwarven artifact, but then why was I drawn to Nighthollow Keep?
An excellent idea, though you might have to get creative to reach the very top.

Very little, I'm afraid. The whole idea of a kingdom of ancient vampire clans hiding in the depths of Blackreach … I thought it was nothing more than a legend.\n\nLet's explore the keep and see what we can learn while we try to find the Dark Heart.

No, he—he's trying to persuade me. Convince me that his path is the right one. Prove to me that the dream we once shared is within reach.\n\nThe letter outlines, in essence, the recipe for Rada's Darkstorm.
