The darkness is a place. A prison. But more than that ….\n\nWhat was once asleep now stirs. And it's hungry. So very, very hungry ….
The reports indicate her influence at work here. She is the Lady of Decay, the spirit of death and rebirth. \n\nMost Reachfolk do not fear her. But if her power were to be twisted and abused ….
Possibly. All I know is that when Namira's power is tampered with, the results can be catastrophic. No one should ever trifle with death and rebirth.

The Reachfolk, on the whole, worship the Daedra. They pay homage to their favorite Prince, who they refer to as great spirits. From what I gather, the Wildblood clan honors Hircine.\n\nThey do so in the form of talismans they carry with them.

Each warrior is responsible for crafting their own talisman, and thus, it is unique to that person and their family. It represents the relationship between hunter and prey, and is deeply personal to their beliefs about life and death.

Correct. I don't know what becomes of the spirits of Reachfolk who die away from their clan, but to the Wildblood, it seems those talismans are an important part of guiding their loved one's spirit home.\n\nBring them back, if you can find them.

Well, it's crawling with Nighthollow vampires. Not just the mindless, spooky kind. Looks like some of them got recharged when the Dark Heart woke up. \n\nThey patrol the outer wall in shifts. One door in and out. It's locked, but they carry keys.

You got it! I haven't been able to keep track of their comings and goings, so there's no telling which vampires have the keys. Attacking them could attract unwanted attention.\n\nIf you want to find a more discreet way past that wall, by all means.

Rada al-Saran wants Verandis to study the Void through Nighthollow eyes, right? According to Lady Belain's writings, the secrets to harnessing the Dark Heart's power—Void power—could be found in the pages of that book.\n\nIt's perfectly obvious!

While it seems obvious to start with the unnecessarily ostentatious vampire castle over there, I think we should survey the island first.\n\nThe Gray Host may be gone, but they could have left traps. And who knows what kind of wildlife lives here.

I don't know! Something gothic and ridiculous. I don't like to generalize, but vampires tend toward the dramatic. \n\nJust be careful. We won't learn anything about Verandis and the Gray Host if we go and get ourselves killed.

Let me see … hmm. A pity the stone is damaged, but it still retains a trace of a magical aura. \n\nThere are different ways to evoke echoes of the past. Objects that people wore or carried tend to collect and hold strong impressions.

No, but it appears to be a pin or an emblem of some kind. The owner would have worn it on their clothing, close to their body. Good.\n\nLet's see if it has anything to show us. Keep your eyes open and observe.

She goes to where the brass worlds spin, inside the globe of horrors. Can you hear it? The beating?\n\nYou walk between the shadows … I see it in your eyes. You will fall as I have fallen. Dragged down … into the darkness.

The Ashen Lord and the Old One. Yes. Though each for a different purpose.\n\nLady Belain. The vessel that never fills. She awakens the Dark Heart. She laughs beneath the stars and spheres. Do you see? When the Dark Heart beats, she drinks the shadows.

Well, it hasn't exploded or fried us to a crisp yet, so I'm thinking no, probably not.\n\nI've seen something like this before. Part of a ward. I think it responds to the presence of a vampire, like those sigils we saw.

Now that they're awake, it should be simple enough to deactivate them. I'm not sure if your eyes are as good as mine, but I think I see a few more up ahead.\n\nI'll keep watch while you deal with the crystals.

You should meet up with Lyris and Fennorian and complete those parts of this journey. Go to Bthar-Zel or Understone Keep if you haven't been there already. You need to do this for Verandis and find the rest of the clues Rada al-Saran left behind.

I make that watching Verandis and Rada al-Saran get along like two acorns from the same tree disturbs me to no end.\n\nJust seeing them together … it's no wonder Rada al-Saran thinks he can convince Verandis to come around to his way of thinking.

Without the keystone or more of those void portals, we can't get down into the orrery chamber. I'll stay here and try to pick up their trail. I need you to go to Rebel's Retreat and see what you can learn from Arana.

Yes, but we need more information. I can deduce that the Dark Heart is some sort of power source, that much is obvious. And it's tied to the Void energy we encountered.\n\nPlus, the currents got stronger when Arana's sister sacrificed her clan mates.

Yes, I noticed that, too. Whether due to the long centuries of isolation or something more sinister, they are shadows of their former selves.\n\nTake the insignia with you and keep exploring. Now that it's charged, more memories may reveal themselves.
Therein lies the problem. My vampiric abilities make traversal somewhat trivial, but you can't follow. I do believe I've come up with a solution though.\n\nPotentially. Theoretically.

I noted numerous void portals scattered around Bthar-Zel. I understand you and Verandis encountered them before.\n\nI'm no expert on teleportation, but these should allow you to navigate the ruins and pick out a safe path.

As Verandis explained it to me, the void portals sort of pull you toward their location. So, finding a viable path across should just be a matter of trial and error. \n\nAssuming there's a void portal near our destination, you should have no problem.
If you completed all three steps of the journey, head back to the orrery. If not, meet Lyris at Understone Keep or Gwendis at the Nighthollow archive and let's get this done.

Yes, and it's a darker story than we were led to believe. Not only was Verandis a member of the Gray Host and a close confidant of Rada al-Saran, he was also the architect of their rebirth.\n\nI hope he's truly ready to face him when the time comes.

The members of House Ravenwatch exchange vials of their own blood. That shows a rare level of trust, even among vampires, since blood can be used in all sorts of spells—both beneficial and harmful.\n\nI brought some of Verandis's blood with me.

By putting a drop of his blood in this potion, we can dream-walk and access any memories Verandis has of this place. I'll leave it here on the table for when you're ready.\n\nI'd drink it myself, but a dream-walk requires an impartial participant.

Dangerous? Not usually. The potion mixes alchemy and magic. Verandis's own design. It lets the imbiber experience the memories of the person whose blood is added to the concoction.\n\nThe potion is on the table. Make sure you drink the whole thing.

Then you're already an expert. You learned quite a bit from that experience, yes? Verandis isn't here, but by using his blood we can achieve the same result.\n\nI prepared the potion, it's on the table. Make sure you drink the whole thing.

That was Ard Caddach's fool idea. Only, it turned out to be a brilliant tactic to get these cursed storms under control.\n\nOur Reach warriors are spread thin, so we're looking for help wherever we can find it.

From what me and my spies have been able to learn, the Gray Host is an army of vampires, werewolves, and Icereach Coven witches. They marched into the Karth Valley and set up shop like they own the place.\n\nThey're responsible for the harrowstorms.

Do you, now? You can tell me all about that later, provided you're willing to share.\n\nIn the meantime, I know the Gray Host somehow convinced Reach witches to develop the ritual that summons the storms. Stop them and we stay safe a little longer.

It wasn't a fight until he sent his Stonehands against me. Wasn't much of one after that, come to think of it.\n\nWe got as far as sundered land when he shouted something about Mannimarco and called up his personal guard.
Markarth would be a ghost town if it wasn't for you. If that doesn't earn you the courtesy of an audience, I can go back to breaking noses.

Then why is Rada al-Saran sending cryptic messages to Verandis? Even if he can't win the count back to his side, these mind games may cloud your friend's judgment.\n\nI suggest we keep an eye on the count, just in case.

I think we've gotten all we're going to from this place. You should follow up with Gwendis and Fenn about the other sites mentioned in Rada al-Saran's letter.\n\nI'll go back to the orrery and check on Count Verandis.

When you see Lord Rada al-Saran, do not continue your age-old argument. He needs to remain focused.\n\nI'll never understand your obsession with sheep, Verandis. There are hunters and prey. We are hunters. Your sympathy for prey borders on the insane.

As were you, until Molag Bal made you into something more. Something worthy.\n\nLord Hircine made me one of his most powerful hunters because he knew mortality restricted me. I could not reach my full potential until he rescued me from that fate.

The wolf does not fear a thousand rabbits, it merely enjoys the bounty Hircine has provided. Humans, no matter how large their pathetic armies grow, will never threaten us.\n\nCome to your senses, Verandis. Come back to your brothers and sisters.

Is that what bothers you? One small failure and you abandon such promising research? \n\nYou had the opportunity to seize control of existence itself! To control both life and death! Such power is unimaginable, yet you squander it.

Cost? Bah! What cost? \n\nMortals are as cheap and plentiful as grains of sand on a beach! Once you mastered your creation, you'd be able to resurrect them at will. They would worship you as a god! Wouldn't that bring about the peace you crave?

How can you be so misguided? Mortals are so far beneath us, they cannot even comprehend their own inadequacy.\n\nI only hope Lord Rada al-Saran can talk some sense into you. Meanwhile, I will study this creation. Perhaps even succeed where you failed.

To parlay with the mortal queen? \n\nI have, but my stance has not changed. The Gray Host's strength has grown over the centuries, while dozens of mortal kingdoms have risen and fallen. What sense is there in revealing ourselves to them now?

What mortals gain from an alliance with us is obvious, but what benefit do we receive from them?\n\nKing Styriche and our Gray Host could crush this Empress Hestra and her armies in a day. I know you worry for our people, Verandis, but you need not.

For such a brilliant mind who helped conceive our Gray Council, you can be so short-sighted, Verandis. I will say this: If the mortals do not move against us, we will not move against them.\n\nBut I cannot protect your precious mortals from themselves.

Oh, that would explain it. Don't worry, it's not you. It's almost impossible to read in a dream-walk. But did you say Verandis's study? He had a study in this terrible place?\n\nWas he truly a member of the Gray Host?

Sounds like Verandis. That's why he founded the Ravenwatch, after all. To allow vampires like us to gather safely, only feed on willing subjects, and help mortals instead of preying upon them.\n\nSo, he wasn't hoping to conquer Tamriel?

Then … he didn't lie to me. He's still the man I know and trust. He left out a few things, of course, but I'll deal with that another time.\n\nThat study of his. It might still be here! Can you lead me to it?

Let me see that. Huh. Ritual's simple enough. Just light some candles and place the reliquary.\n\nIt looks like he abandoned the research before ever testing it on a vampire. Something about life energy and too great a cost.

When a vampire dies, our souls go to Coldharbour. We can use that to our advantage.\n\nIf we want answers, why not go straight to the source. Let's resurrect one of these Gray Host leaders. A member of this Gray Council Verandis wrote about.

Right. Tzinghalis must have continued Verandis's experiments and refined them.\n\nYou know, when a vampire dies our souls go to Coldharbour. To Molag Bal. This may be our chance to get answers directly from a member of the Gray Council!

Why not? They're evil. Who cares what the ritual does to them? We have to interrogate them and find some weakness. Some way to stop the Gray Host.\n\nGo downstairs and find the reliquary Verandis wrote about. Then meet me in the ritual chamber.

Verandis gave his life for Rivenspire and what was his reward? Coldharbour and an eternity of torment at the hands of Molag Bal!\n\nThis will work. It has to! Go downstairs and find the reliquary he wrote about. Then meet me in the ritual chamber.
Exactly what I was hoping for. I suspect the Nighthollow nobles wore these as a badge of rank.\n\nLet's see what we can learn with a little more auramancy.

That memory comes from a later time. The lord spoke of opening a way to the Dark Heart, which implies the Nighthollow lost access to it at some point.\n\nBut what are these Dark Halls Lady Belain spoke of? Where can we find them?

Perhaps. And maybe we have the key. Lady Belain said that only those who bear the sign of the inner circle can utilize the Heart. That must refer to the insignias you found.\n\nLet's look for these Dark Halls.

Remember, the journey Rada sent me on—the one you took in my place—it was to follow in his footsteps. To see how he reached this moment in time.\n\nThis stone, it's a shard of Oblivion lost in our world. How would that help him save the Gray Host?

To see the Void through Nighthollow eyes. Yes, it's written in the tongue of the first vampires. I can read it, but barely. In addition to other things, this is basically a spellbook. It's full of rituals to appease and make use of the Dark Heart.

Was the point to show me the inner workings of the mysterious Dwarven keystones? We know Rada used one to link the Dark Heart's power to not only the orrery, but to the Gray Host as well.\n\nI can feel the pull of the Heart just thinking about it.

It's true that Rada often relied on myself and later Tzinghalis to handle his research and experiments. But he wasn't without his own skills when it came to arcana and alchemy.\n\nI suppose during his long isolation, he had to increase his aptitude.

Conflicted? I suppose you could say that. We were friends once. Partners in a great and noble undertaking. And then Rada … changed. Or maybe it was me. Who can say?\n\nHe betrayed what we believed in. And then he died. Or at least, I thought he did.

I wish I could say for certain. I've done precious little reading on Dwarven ruins. I do seem to recall the name Arkthzand being connected to a university or library ….\n\nThis place does have a sort of academic look to it, don't you think?

That was the ancient past. There was no reason to mention my involvement with the Gray Host. I never imagined they would return. \n\nRada al-Saran and I were friends once. I tried to convince him to take a different path, but to no avail.

You saw? Then know that I regret not trying harder. If I pushed, could I have averted the war? I suppose we'll never know.\n\nRegardless, Gwendis informs me that Rada al-Saran may be alive. And somehow, the Gray Host has returned to threaten our world.

Now? Now I take up the mantle of what you and Gwendis started. We must find out what this revived Gray Host plans and devise a way to stop them.\n\nWhen the time comes, House Ravenwatch will send for you. I pray you will continue to aid us.

That is … unfortunate. I believed that part of my past was dead and buried. My involvement with the Gray Council ended so very long ago.\n\nRada al-Saran and I were friends once. I tried to convince him to take a different path, but to no avail.

What? How is that even possible? What am I saying? Haven't I just returned from the dead?\n\nI must look into this. Find out what the Gray Host has planned. When the time comes, House Ravenwatch will send for you. I pray you will answer that call.

Then know that I truly regret not trying harder to convince Rada al-Saran and the Gray Council. Perhaps I could have averted the war. Alas, we'll never know.\n\nBut why the sudden interest in ancient history? Why this obsession with the Gray Host?

I heard what he said. I'm still angry that he kept this part of his past a secret, but we'll work it out. Eventually.\n\nIn the meantime, at least I know I can trust him. That he didn't betray the ideals of House Ravenwatch.

Of course. There's too much at stake to let a few secrets get in our way. \n\nI'll help him in whatever way I can. And once we know more, we'll send for you. I figure you want to see how this ends just as much as we do.

I've been thinking about what you told me. I believe the Ghostsong ritual primed the Dark Heart, opening a path between this world and the Void. The void energy is stronger here, but it lacks direction.\n\nI fear they require a greater sacrifice.

Something as powerful as the Dark Heart that's been asleep for millennia may stir from the taste of a few souls, but I suspect it needs a banquet to awaken fully.\n\nPerhaps, if we hurry, it won't come to that.
The constructs are Dwarven and expected. The shadows … some sort of beings made of inky darkness. Quite unsettling. And potentially dangerous.\n\nSomething unusual has taken hold of this place.

I'm not sure, but I'm no witch. Some of our rituals aren't meant to be shared with outsiders. I'll tell you that much.\n\nStill … if Arana says it's important for you to speak to her sister, I believe her. I'll vouch for you, outsider.

That's just what the Reachfolk call it. It isn't actually lost. We know exactly where it is. It's a sacred place, from a darker time.\n\nNathari said the time had come to return to Lost Valley. Promised the clan a great revelation.
As I said, the place is sacred to us. The Nords built a great barrow there, but long before that, Lost Valley was a place dedicated to dark worship.
Yes, we grew up together in the Ghostsong clan. I was furious when the clan banished her. I almost followed, but I couldn't. The clan needs my protection, especially now against the Gray Host.

The army of monsters that ravaged the First Era? Not really my area of expertise.\n\nI study the historical accounts of Warlord Thulgeg's army of Orcs and Goblins. The garrison held strong and denied them passage. Not one got through. Truly inspiring!

Other than the fact that they were defeated here centuries ago, not much, I'm afraid.\n\nI can tell you Empress Hestra's legions came to the aid of Bangkorai Garrison. That's why High Rock became part of the Alessian Empire for a time.

Yes, I'm beginning to see how the pieces you retrieved fit together. He's building a bridge through the Void. The Oblivion shard serves as a lodestone to point to his destination, but Coldharbour is precisely the place he would want to avoid.

Rada has always sought to escape Molag Bal's hold on his soul. Coldharbour is the place where Bal's power is absolute. It makes no sense … unless Coldharbour isn't his destination.\n\nGather the others, we need to recreate Rada's ritual.

Rada pointed us to the means and method of recreating his work. There's something he wants for me to see here and I believe the only way to truly understand what he's done is by repeating it ourselves.\n\nI only hope the risk is worth it.

We are attempting to harness forces never intended to be combined to peer into the infinite churning chaos we call the Void. I only suggest we try because it appears Rada has proven it can be done. \n\nBesides, we have no other choice.

Not the ravages of time, that much is certain. It seems as though this part of the structure simply … imploded. The force behind this damage must have been incredible.\n\nThe question is, what produced such power? Could it be the dark relic?
Void portals, a dark relic resonating power, and strange shades … we can't let any of this fall into Rada and Lady Belain's hands.\n\nLet's see what we can find on the other side of this structure.

I suggest you try to use a shard to propel yourself through one of the void portals.\n\nThe risks are significant, but if we can turn these strange pockets of energy to our advantage, we have to attempt it.

Oh, we trained <<1>> to come for her treat when she hears that whistle. She loves treats! And if <<2>> hears the whistle, he'll probably follow it, too. I imagine they're both hungry by now.\n\nThey headed northeast. Try that direction first.
Set up camp by a stream and start panning for gold! But no more losing our tempers out here in the wilderness. We'll stick close to each other from now on.

One moment the sky was clear, the next … it was unnatural! Swirling darkness, lightning. And it did things. Some of our people became mindless husks, but others turned into … monsters!\n\nThere's nothing left of them inside those creatures.

I was afraid she would run into trouble, but she's a good apprentice. One I find myself leaning on more and more since my sight left me and age has taken its toll.\n\nThere are four wards, each dedicated to one of our revered spirits.

The Dark Heart feeds on death. You saw that when the Ghostsong clan was sacrificed. Only he's offering the Heart a much larger feast—all the Reachfolk in Markarth.\n\nHe sent Lady Belain there to finish what has undoubtedly already begun.
Correct. As part of Lady Belain's peace with the Gray Host. Just another horrible deception.\n\nLet's get out of this place. There may still be a way to save the people of Markarth.

You can find Ravenwatch Castle in the western foothills of Rivenspire.\n\nThanks for helping me with this. I don't think I could handle it on my own, and I'm not ready to involve the rest of my family yet, either. Come on, let's go meet that cart.

We discovered a signet that looks just like one my mentor, Count Verandis used to have. A signet that belonged to Rada al-Saran! \n\nWhen we searched Ravenwatch Castle, we found an old letter to Verandis, requesting he come to a secret island.
I don't know what to think. Maybe he was forced to join them, or lied to, or tricked, or—you know what? Speculating is pointless.\n\nWe have an island to find. Let's get on with it.

Grayhome is impressive, I won't deny that. But I detest all this sitting around and debating. \n\nI'm a hunter. I ache to feel a mortal writhe in my grasp, to watch their blood spray against the dirt. Don't you?

I've been quite successful in your absence. \n\nRada al-Saran discovered a strange relic beneath the Reach. I spent weeks examining it. It's quite remarkable and I've only scratched the surface of the possibilities it might offer our kind.
I'd prefer not to draw any conclusions until I've had time to examine it at length. But I welcome the chance to discuss it with you once you've settled in.

Of course, Verandis. I know you too well to think you would let the topic go so easily. I promise, we will speak of it again. There is no need to rush.\n\nWe have not seen each other in an Elf's age. I would hear what you have been up to, my brother.

Good. You cannot imagine how much I have leaned upon them in your absence.\n\nIt should please you to know that Ulfra shows restraint these days. And I know Tzinghalis would love to discuss his experiments and research with you.

We have talked and I have listened. I've humored your ideals far longer than they deserve.\n\nI invited you because you will flourish here, Verandis. You belong here, among your brothers and sisters, not meandered in the tribulations of mortal life.

Yes, but apparently for different purposes.\n\nUnstable breaches in the fabric of reality. Imploded chambers. Trapped shades. Everything points to some terrible Dwarven experiment that went astray. This dark energy is clearly powerful. And dangerous.

No, five-claw. Even the two of us would be hard-pressed to defeat the entire Lothid clan. While this one figures out where Kathad is, you quietly find a vantage point and see what happens.\n\nYou're my safeguard in case something unfortunate occurs.
It's somewhere inside or beyond an old Dwarven ruin? Wonderful. Good thing I brought my construct-busting axe.

No, not exactly. This one hoped not to get overpowered by Boss Trenlor's lackeys and flayed alive. After that, I was going to improvise.\n\nThis is much better, yes? We are in the Deep Tombs. Kathad is here somewhere. We should find him.
Just like what Nathari did to my clan? The bastards!\n\nArana brought us here to help, but it may be too late. They aren't only marching toward the gates—they're coming at us from beneath the city!

Lady Belain unsealed the doors to Nchuand-Zel and let the Gray Host into the city. We arrived just in time to fend off the first wave. Can't make any promises about the next.\n\nGo to Understone Keep. Tell Ard Caddach and Arana what you told me.

Well, they certainly did a good job with their first attack!\n\nLady Belain actually tried to kill me herself. Might have succeeded if not for Arana. She drove off Belain and saved my sorry hide. As soon as I can assemble my troops, we'll strike back!

Damn it, outsider! But your words ring true. All right, defense only. For now.\n\nArana had that look in her eyes, though. I think she plans to try to deal with Belain on her own. If you have the mind, go to Nchuand-Zel and help the witch-rebel, aye?

Convince him to leave. Lothid clan is no place for a sane and honorable vampire. No place at all.\n\nBe cautious, though. If we run into Freyleth, remember that she twists words and tells lies that sound like the most beautiful truths.

The Nords built their barrow over the caves that were once used by my ancestors. The Spirit Queen led the first Ghostsong matron to a spot deep beneath the redoubt. I think that's where Nathari has taken the clan.

They haven't. My mother had the entrance to the barrow concealed when I was a young girl. No one has used it since before I was born.\n\nI always knew those old stories interested my sister, but I never expected her to lead the clan down there.

Nathari is younger than me, but way too sure of herself. When I was the clan's matron I tried to mentor her, but she follows her own heart. Witches can be a stubborn lot.\n\nI only wish she heard others as well as she thinks she hears the Spirit Queen.

The fancy Elf who won't take no for an answer? He should have made this offer earlier. News concerning the rebels is a beast worth skinning.\n\nTell me something I don't know and I won't have you fed to my hunting dogs.

More than ready. I've sworn my blade to thrones and causes, but my blood and bones are Nord. If Rada al-Saran thinks he can ravage my homeland and get away with it, he's about to be very wrong.\n\nBesides, who else is going to watch your back?
Trying to scare me off? I know what we're getting into. But if we do get stuck in some lost realm of Oblivion, I could think of worse company.\n\nNow, let's stuff the talk and kill this bastard.

Every place I've visited in Oblivion has been different. Chains and machines for Molag Bal, endless libraries for Hermaeus Mora. Each realm shaped by its Prince. But Rada al-Saran chose a place beyond their reach. Guess we'll soon find out.

The vampire noble, your friend Verandis, he convinced Arana that we had to help defend Markarth. We marched when Gwendis gave us the word.\n\nBesides, Arana and Caddach are both of the Reach. Reachfolk stick together against outsiders. We always have.

A strong witch in all her anger is a force of nature. Arana blames Lady Belain for what happened to her old clan. And rightly so! Sounds like Belain got into poor Nathari's head.\n\nThe old ways. Even I'm not fool enough to want them back.

My gran would scare us with tales of the Night Lords who once ruled the Reach from the land below. Always thought she was just trying to frighten the children.\n\nLike most of the vateshran legends, I suppose there was a kernel of truth in her stories.

She gave me good counsel for a time. Even regarding the Gray Host. Sheltering in Markarth saved a lot of Reachfolk lives … until today, at least.\n\nArana warned me, though. She didn't trust Belain from the start.
I was really hoping Verandis had something tricky up his sleeve. I guess there's nothing left to do but smack Rada al-Saran in his self-righteous face.\n\nYou just bring Verandis back. Promise me.

You better. The only reason I'm agreeing to stay behind is because you're going with him. I can count on one finger the number of people I'd trust with this.\n\nSo get this done. We'll be waiting to hear all about it when you get back.

Now you sound like Verandis before a trip. I swear not to wreck the place while you're gone. And if the Gray Host shows up to start trouble, I'll stop them from wrecking it, too.\n\nSo get going already, before I change my mind.

I'd be lying if I said no … but the price of salvation is too high. Rada al-Saran will doom thousands of souls to fates worse than death so that he and his chosen can escape. I don't need an eternity with that on my conscience.
You and my father will see this through. I know it. Just … come back, all right? You both still owe me a proper reunion.

I'm fairly certain the Dwarves built this as an observatory to chart the Void. What we're doing is more akin to plunging a telescope into a fathomless depth so we can slip through the tube without getting wet.\n\nLet's hope it doesn't spring a leak.
Was that what the count meant by making it right? He didn't just stop the Darkstorm, he used it to free the souls from the Dark Heart!\n\nWe've got to get to Markarth.
I know what Adusa expects of me. I want to join the Ravenwatch, I really do. But I can't leave my Lothid brothers and sisters in this … deplorable state of existence.\n\nI need to do … something!

Boss Trenlor turned this once-great clan into a gang of common criminals. He makes us plunder the countryside, kidnap mortals to feed upon. And if anyone objects, he casts us into the Deep Tombs and denies us blood. He turns us into feral monsters!

Just bringing one person back should be impossible, short of Divine intervention. But we saw the Gray Host manage it more than once. If the Darkstorm was anything like the harrowstorms in Western Skyrim, it just might be possible.
Verandis is gone! Arana gets to live, but he doesn't? Is that it? How is that fair?
You don't have to explain. I know you would have brought him home if that were possible. This is how it had to be.\n\nI would like to hear the story, sometime. Just not today.

Among Boss Trenlor's many vices, he loves to be entertained. So every night they throw him a party. A celebration of blood using a captured mortal, a wild beast, or one of the clan he abandoned down here.\n\nAfter we turn feral, of course.
I can't say myself. I remember being here. In this room. I remember the wound. Then nothing but a cold, icy current dragging me under. I drowned for so long … until a warm hand fished me out.
I couldn't see. Everything was just warmth and light. There was a voice though, guiding me. Calling me back.\n\nIt sounded like Verandis.
As I live and breathe, it was Verandis who lead me here. I don't understand much of what occurred, but of that I'm certain.\n\nThat, and I didn't come back alone.

If you go down into the Blinds and get me a darkcap mushroom, I can use it to weaken Trenlor. Then I can challenge him.\n\nAfter you find it, there's a lift down there. It connects to an abandoned corner in the servant's quarters. We'll meet you there.

Not just evil. Deranged. And cruel. He treats our clan as though we were his personal playthings. Toys to be used and abused for no other reason than he enjoys it.\n\nBut he's also powerful. No one has ever challenged him and survived.
Markarth. That's where the spirits call me now. I have no fondness for the place, but that's where my people need me.

You did what you thought was best and the price I paid has been returned. None of us could have imagined this is where our path would lead, but I've no complaints with the outcome. No complaints at all.

Rada al-Saran's sanctuary realm, I hope. Doesn't look like much, but it's got more charm than Coldharbour. \n\nIt does kind of remind me of Molag Bal's realm, though. That's probably the plane it was melding with before it got stuck between worlds.

You're the first thing I've seen aside from those shades. They aren't tough, but they'll overwhelm you if you aren't careful.\n\nYou and I should be fine, but Verandis won't last long on his own. Not in his condition.

It's pretty hard to miss, for one thing. And following an obvious landmark is basic navigation.\n\nBesides, Verandis came here for one reason—to stop whatever that is. You can bet he's going to try to do that. With or without us.

I chased Lady Belain into the depths … battled her to a standstill. And then she summoned the Gray Host.\n\nShe fled while I fought them off. To the orrery, I think I heard her tell the Gray Host commander.
We kill Rada al-Saran. I don't know if that will stop the Darkstorm, but it will make me feel a whole lot better.
Damn. I take back every bad thought I had about the count. He's got conviction to match Sai Sahan's.\n\nWe should go while he's still got the strength to send us back.
Forget me … get the second keystone. Don't let Belain draw any more power from the Dark Heart.

I don't know much. It's something quite sacred to the Reachfolk. I've only been able to glean small details. \n\nThe standard practice of the ritual entails hagravens replacing a person's heart with a seed that imbues them with incredible power.

The Thornroot clan believes their blessing allows them to desecrate the ritual without angering the spirits. They won't be bold enough to attempt it without their special tools.\n\nThey want to avoid the ire of whatever spirit they're invoking.

Becoming a briarheart is considered a sacred, worthy tradition to the Reachfolk—if done appropriately. It's not inherently evil. \n\nThe Thornroot clan defiles the ancient ritual by abusing it for their own selfish purposes.

As ready as I can be. I don't have the luxury of walking away this time. \n\nLet's get moving. The more active the Dark Heart becomes, the harder it is for me to concentrate. It's like a constant barrage of noise I can't hear, but I can certainly feel.
Another keystone? It seems the spirits of the Reach smile favorably upon us, after all!\n\nBut you say Lady Belain escaped from Arana? Any idea where she may have gone?
By all means! If it works, we can finally confront Rada and Lady Belain. Together, perhaps we'll fare better than Arana.
I don't know. If the Dark Heart does not drag me away, it may release its hold on me, but that will not be much cause for celebration. Alive or dead, I may remain trapped in this twilight realm.

Rada chose this realm to escape the reach of Molag Bal. If it truly is beyond the Daedric Princes' influence, then it may be outside the reach of Aetherius as well. A gray, empty purgatory for me and Rada. A fitting prison.

I can only control the Darkstorm from here. I understand now what must be done to stop it. I can use the power of the Dark Heart, one last time. When I am finished, the energy will be gone and our gate to the orrery will be closed. You understand?
Not any that can make everything right. I brought about this tragedy, through my naivete. Through my selfish desires. Through my damn ideals and curiosity.\n\nIt's my time of reckoning. Not yours.
When this one first became a vampire, she was alone, confused. Frightened. Adusa did some terrible things before she understood exactly what was happening.\n\nThen I met Freyleth.
The totem actually has a great deal of religious significance to the Wildblood clan. The Thornroot clan captured it during a raid and took it to the Briar Rock Ruins.

Freyleth took Adusa under her wing. Trained her. Guided her. She was exactly what I needed. But she also wasn't.\n\nFreyleth is wild, chaotic. She loves both the power and the freedom that vampirism provides. I don't want her to lead Kathad astray.

Freyleth may not be the monster that Trenlor is, but she's no fragile flower. She led me to places … actions … that seemed like a good idea at the time.\n\nI see much promise in Kathad. He can be an asset to the Ravenwatch. If he isn't corrupted.

The Wildblood will be happy to have it returned. Plus, keeping it out of the hagraven matron's hands is extremely important. These beliefs, no matter what we think of them, have power. As long as the Thornroot possess it, the Wildblood are in danger.

Apparently, the hagraven matron wanted the totem. In some way that I don't understand, the matron draws power from the relic.\n\nWhether that's a natural property of the totem, or it has something to do with forcefully possessing it, I don't know.

Therein lies the problem. Reach witches are experts at losing themselves in the many caves and copses that decorate the landscape. It's like finding a tooth in a hen's beak.\n\nMost witches give deference to the ard. Arana … is a troublemaker.

Actually, that task falls to you. A favor for a favor, yes? That's how business works here.\n\nLocate the rebels. Find Arana and urge her to stop meddling in Markarth's affairs. Do that, and you shall earn a place for you and your count in the Reach.

The spirits sent you to help us, I know it. But Shaman Ulvoch needs to judge for himself if you can hear our sacred rituals. And he needs to tell the rest of the village. My people distrust outsiders.\n\nThings will go easier with his approval.
The Spirit Queen … Namira … she required a champion. She gave me the strength to press on … despite my wounds.\n\nNow … that strength is gone.

She is the spirit of death and decay. Belain defied a natural death, as all vampires do. Using Namira's energy like that, it was an affront. I am … happy to have done my part.\n\nVerandis needs your help. Go, harrier. Use this one last portal ….

So it was Belain's death I felt in the darkness. Rada was right. For some reason, the connection I have to the Dark Heart is strong. But there was something else … another sensation.\n\nWhere's Arana, my friend?

Arana dead? That's another soul lost to the Void. Between her and those that perished at Markarth, the Dark Heart ate well this day.\n\nI'd like you to return to Understone Keep. Tell Ard Caddach that despite what we have lost, Markarth is safe.

And it did its job splendidly! He certainly looks infinitely weaker to me.\n\nI'm sorry I deceived you, but look around. Do you see one face that mourns Trenlor? No. They will cheer your name for saving the Lothid clan. Your name … and mine.

Oh, darling, no. Kathad has too much damn virtue in his blood for my taste. Gets it from Adusa, no doubt. Lothid is my clan. It always has been. I will lead it with vision and purpose. Make it truly great again.\n\nNow, if you will excuse me ….
Trenlor was a monster. This was the only safe way to put an end to his reign of terror. Now someone truly worthy can take command of the Lothid clan.\n\nSomeone exactly like me.

Well, that explains everything! Someone will sort out the details and tell them to me later, eh? All that matters is the Gray Host called off their attack and departed as soon as they lost their leaders.\n\nBut where's Arana? I want to thank the witch.
Just fine. Even the great Lyris Titanborn needs a rest sometimes. Don't tell anyone.
I imagine the only message the ard wants to share with me is of the unflattering variety, so I have no idea. Maybe the Skald-King sent word?\n\nWhen I know, you'll know.
We owe you for delivering Malacath's vengeance to that toothy bastard. Where is Count Verandis? I'd like to give him my proper thanks.

At last, the monster that nearly brought my lands to ruin has paid the price for his wrongs. I could ask no more and yet that which was taken has been returned as well.\n\nWhere is Count Ravenwatch? If he thinks to escape my gratitude ….

We treat for peace. Our battles with the Gray Host have ravaged all our kingdoms and peoples. We each seek to rebuild and recover. Perhaps we'll do so together. At least we'll keep out of each other's way.\n\nBefore we proclaim, I have a favor to ask.

Hmm. Then his name and deeds will echo these halls for as long as I sit upon the throne. Which will be a while yet, thanks to you both—and so long as these Nords are good to their word.\n\nI've no idea what peace is like, but I'm eager to find out.

Not a lot, I'm afraid. A few of the Reach shamans are interested in those caves. They say the place is suffused with strange energies and they're eager to get their hands on some of it.\n\nWhich means gold for people like you and me!

I suggest you wash up thoroughly after handling them, at the very least. But I doubt they'll cause you any lasting harm.\n\nThere's sure to be more dangerous things in those caves, anyway. Better to worry about them than the mushrooms.

Well, from my limited knowledge of fungi, mushrooms are like sponges. They absorb whatever they can from the soil. Since the area itself seems to possess strange properties, the shamans assume the mushrooms do, too.

It's a worthy holdfast, but not so much a city. I would have the land worked, the stone repaired, and the markets expanded. These are not things my kin have much knowledge in, but perhaps the Nords will share their trade for the right price.

Hmm, they're a fair lot more agreeable than the she-wolf you travel with. Have the sense to show deference to a king in his own hall, though I heard enough honeyed words from the Lady Belain for one lifetime. The fat one thinks himself a poet.

Feh. Skald-King. Nonsense. Every now and then comes a king of his kind—one who makes stirring pronouncements and promises that his court must struggle to keep. His grand words lack guile, so I wager he can be trusted.

The past would tell me to hate Svargrim's whelp with all my vigor. We've battled and bled for more generations than I can count with her ilk … but this fledgling speaks plain and honest. When she talks of new beginnings, I believe her.

Hmm. I heard Jorunn sired the boy when he was young, but looking at the pair I have a hard time saying who's father and who's whelp!\n\nIrnskar seems shrewd and dutiful. But his father casts a long shadow—a wide one, too.

Western Skyrim has begun to recover. With Fenn's elixir, our soldiers have been able to push back the Gray Host. I know the Reach has not been so fortunate. I persuaded Prince Irnskar, and the Skald-King, to offer our support.

I expected we'd be sending soldiers, but by the time we arrived the people were dancing in the streets. I always heard stories of the city of stone being a dark place where flint-hearted Reachmen worship strange gods. It's not so different from home.

The people seem happier than I've ever seen, in spite of all our hardships. I wasn't the only one living under my father's shadow, apparently. I can't come and go as I please, but the Blue Palace is lively as any tavern with Maugh around.

I heard that Lyris was investigating some sinister plots in this province. Were it not for other obligations no less dire, I would have rushed here sooner.\n\nI envy you. There's nothing I would have liked more than to battle a sword-saint by her side.

Truthfully, Svana. When we learned that Markarth suffered an attack like the one you narrowly prevented in Solitude, she insisted that we offer aid. Ostensibly, to stop the Gray Host, but it seems we're a bit late for that.

Verandis doesn't think so. At least, not the Reach specifically. Verandis … understands Rada al-Saran. He believes the Ashen Lord's after a different prize. \n\nDid Lady Belain say anything about Rada al-Saran's plans during your battle?

Good thing you stopped her, then. You saw how the Dark Heart changed the Nighthollow. Can you imagine a clan consisting of nothing but creatures like Lady Belain? Always thirsting, never sated?\n\nNo wonder the other ancient clans feared them.

I knew it! When you came back alone, I felt that something terrible must have happened.\n\nI never knew a witch so strong or so stubborn. I thought nothing could stand against Arana. And she was my friend. I should have been there for that fight.

No doubt. They have proved very skilled at keeping to the shadows and biding their time. Hunting them down will not be easy, but I feel that's not how best to make use of the opportunity we've been given.

The Gray Host's greatest weapon against us was our mutual mistrust. They preyed on our suspicions and fears. Used our division to pick us apart one by one. The best way to prevent that from happening again will be to build trust and cooperation.

Well, yes. I do. She's a striking woman—figure—leader! She's won many hearts and minds in the short time she's been a jarl. I think that speaks more to her esteem than my praise.\n\nWestern Skyrim would do well to put her in charge.

Now don't get carried away. In case you haven't noticed, Reachfolk don't bend their knees lightly. We'll give our loyalty to the ard because we choose to, not because he demands it from us. \n\nAnd we'll be watching him.

Arana made peace with Caddach. In her honor, we'll hold to that agreement. It's clear that Lady Belain was always our true enemy.\n\nNew clans will form, now that our quarrel with the ard is over. There's plenty of land nearby.

Truthfully, I don't know much more than what the Reachfolk told me. The creatures producing it tend to vary, according to reports. I've heard Gloomspore bears and wolves seem to be most affected, but it's not limited to them.

He doesn't want another war on his hands and the Western Holds still desire their independence. Skyrim won't be united by force, but with more days like today, the province may one day be whole—no matter how many kings claim it.

As did I. When I took hold of the Darkstorm's power, I believed it would be the last thing I ever did. It was a force no mortal hand should wield. Still, with it I was able to draw the souls out of the Dark Heart. Return them to where they belonged.

No. As the last of the Dark Heart's power ebbed away, I should have been trapped in Rada's sanctuary realm. But I was forced out. Pushed, I'd say.\n\nI fell into the darkness of the slumbering Heart. Then I emerged from it like a moth from a cocoon.
My soul became part of the Dark Heart, smelted inextricably into the fabric of its existence. So long as it remains dormant, its hold over me is tolerable, but I am bound to it nonetheless.
In and of itself? No, I should think not. The beasts themselves, however, are another matter. I would employ caution.
No—no. I don't mean to give the wrong impression. It's all just, a bit much. Maybe I should sit down …?\n\nDid he really say he wants us to take over the Ravenwatch?

Right. I didn't imagine it. The truth is, we were already considering the future of the Ravenwatch after you returned without Verandis. It seems that will bear further discussion, but I'm relieved that the circumstances are different.

You're to endure as much of the cheer and praise as the ard and his people can heap upon you. And you're to have absolutely nothing to do with evil vampires for at least, I don't know, a day.\n\nThink you can manage that recruit?

Great! Terrible! Everything in between! I've waited so long for Verandis to stop hovering over my shoulder, but I never thought it'd be because he's not around.\n\nI realized something though, when you and Lyris told me he wasn't coming back.

I can't shed tears for him. It's not what he needs from me. He needs someone to carry on after him. To do the work he can't anymore.\n\nSo, that's what I'll do. Keep his legacy alive. Somebody has to keep tabs on all these pesky vampires.

To that point, the three of us had been talking things over—about the future of House Ravenwatch—and given everything you've done for us … we want to make you an official member of the Ravenwatch. What do you say?

Now, if you'll excuse me, I have to give Verandis an earful.\n\nI think I heard the ard calling for you when we were talking to Arana. They're making some proclamation in the audience chamber. Better not miss your accolades.

Your endorsement gives me confidence. Though, we were hoping you'd consider joining our ranks, officially. Given everything you've done for the Ravenwatch, it only seems right that we consider you one of our own—that is, if you want.

The Reach shamans believe that the mage is investing the egg with the power that flows through Gloomreach. Whatever grows inside that shell, they fear the potential destruction it will unleash when it hatches.\n\nYou must destroy that egg.

Reachfolk aren't usually in the business of … study. They view the mage's experiment as a threat, and they tend to deal with those as expediently as possible. \n\nI doubt there's anything useful to be learned anyway. Just destroy it and move on.

You sound like Bradan. True believers see the honor in this sacrifice, but not everyone can overcome the fear that whispers in their ears. The flesh quails even when the spirit is strong. \n\nNo matter. We help them complete their journey.

Why does this matter to you, outsider? The Ghostsong hunters—the true hunters—gather below, ready to give their lives for the Spirit Queen. Bradan will too, when his time comes.\n\nI shall complete the ritual and awaken the Dark Heart!
Yes, but I don't know why the ritual failed.\n\nIt was as if the spirits lashed out at us. Something disturbed the natural process, but I have no idea what that could be.

As we've seen, Nathari has convinced some of the clan to support this mad endeavor.\n\nThis is Lady Belain's doing, spirits take that woman! She's laughing, far from here and safe while Nathari does exactly what she wants.
Arana? I've heard that name during my time here. Did you happen to learn what these rebels are rebelling against?

Flee the city? With the Gray Host prowling the countryside? Well, that's three valuable pieces of information. \n\nI want you to represent me before Ard Caddach. Explain what you learned and convince him to finally agree to meet with me.

Aye, I remember that from the stories. A cavern where the floor drops into darkness. That's where the first Ghostsong witch made a bargain with the Spirit Queen. Legend says the pit divides the land of the living from the dead.\n\nLet's keep moving.

Braden said there was a strange Redguard looking for me. When I laid eyes on Sai, I didn't know whether to punch him or hug him. It was quite the surprise, but not a bad one. We've got a lot of catching up to do.
I haven't, but I'm sure you can keep them busy for a while longer. Right, partner?\n\nSai and I still have a few … dents to bang out of my armor.
Lyris has offered to show me some of the more intact barrows in the Reach and Western Skyrim. These sites are tied to ancient Dragon Cults. Dragons … are something of a hobby of mine.

I'd say being home has been nice, but you'd know I'd be lying. The Skald-King owes me some rest. Think we'll take our leave of Skyrim and spend some time free of obligations.\n\nAlways wanted to go back to Skingrad.

Witch-rebels, huh? That's just a label applied by the oppressors, don't you think?\n\nLook, we have enough trouble with those Gray Host bastards and Caddach's soldiers. We don't need a curious outsider blundering around and getting in our way, too.

You're a hunter? Truly? Sounds more like Caddach and his keep-witch getting up to more mischief.\n\nYou want to befriend the witch-rebels? Then prove it! The Gray Host has set up stockpiles nearby. Find out what they're storing and then we'll talk.

Nathari was a friend once, before she became obsessed with the old ways. If Lady Belain put her on that path, then I've got a score to settle with her.\n\nAnd I'll fight to protect what's left of us, few though we may be.

Aye, we'll fight. There aren't many of us left, but most of us are werewolves. Lady Belain will regret the day she turned our own witches against the clan. That, I promise you. We'll make our way to Rebel's Retreat. I'll look for you and Arana there.

Prospecting! We're miners. We've been working our way west, following traces of gold in the streams.\n\n<<1>> thinks no one's ever really looked for gold in this part of the Reach before. If he's right, we're going to make a fortune!

I am, but <<1>> doesn't care. He's traded with friendly clans in the past and says they'll leave us alone. But that was before. This is new territory. We don't know these clans.\n\nThat's why we argued. This is as far into the Reach as I want to go.

The Gray Host? Does it look like I've been bitten or clawed? It was the damn witch-rebels! And they can't tell a Reachfolk from a monster any better than you can!\n\nThey thought I was one of those invaders! Spirits take the lot of them!

Aye. Like a pack of wild dogs, they were. Kept shouting "Arana, Arana" as they bore down on me. I took an arrow in the leg before they listened to me. Before they decided I wasn't an invader.\n\nI think Arana spoke to me. I think she was their leader.
Why do I even try to talk to you about such things? Lord Rada al-Saran should have dealt with you years ago, but he keeps calling you back. Bah.

This one met Kathad when he first became a vampire. Before he got involved with the Lothid clan. I tried to recruit him then, but his attention was … unfocused.\n\nBetween his newfound abilities and Freyleth, he wasn't ready to listen to me.

Arkthzand? Sounds Dwarven. I guess that's why you came to see me. No one in Markarth knows more about the Deep Folk and their scrap than old Nolovan!\n\nNow, keystones. That's another matter. Could refer to a wedge that supports an arch, maybe.

Aye! More than cover it!\n\nHere's your map. Leads right to Bthar-Zel, I guarantee it. You might need to do a little searching to find the entrance, but that map will get you close. Now, please, I have so much work to do before I can open the shop.

Pick up a package and return here. Do that and the map is yours.\n\nJust beyond the gates there's an old Dwarf house. Parcels with my name on them appear there from time to time. I'm expecting one currently. Go check and bring me what you find.

Oh, well done, outsider! Well done. You say this scrawl is my name? Fancy that. And it's heavy. That's a good sign! I leave things down in the depths, and in return I get these packages from time to time.\n\nHere's your map. Good luck in Bthar-Zel!
Aye, that seems to be the long and short of it. The Dark Heart will beat again and its power will surge up from the deep places to consume everything. Its darkness will cover the world.
He did. Here, let me mark a location on your map. That's Rebel's Retreat. What Arana and her people call their camp in the foothills.\n\nVerandis wants you to meet him there.

On behalf of the Crow-Eye clan, I thank you outsider. I can feel the energy flowing through the wards like water. Now I may perform the ritual and restore what the storm took from us.\n\nBut I require your help one last time, my friend.

Since you made the offerings, I must ask you to present yourself at the ritual pyre. The spirits began this negotiation with you, so you must complete it.\n\nYou are a part of Karthwasten now, and it is a part of you.

Freyleth, she … we traveled together a long time ago … before I joined the Ravenwatch.\n\nShe comes and goes. Sometimes I don't see her for decades. Then she appears and, purposely or not, causes some amount of havoc.

Because this one asked you to. If that isn't enough, consider that turning one more vampire away from evil helps everyone.\n\nAnd if that doesn't motivate you, then remember the gold. House Ravenwatch pays well. Very well, indeed.

Be my eyes, outsider. Examine the ritual pyre and see if anything strikes you as odd or out of place. I sense something … but I cannot put my finger on what it is.\n\nIf you find anything, show it to Apprentice Fialyn. She may be able to identify it.

No, we did everything right. There has to be something interfering with the ritual itself. The offerings were made. Something else is at work here.\n\nDo what the shaman asked. Examine the ritual pyre and see if you spot anything unusual.

Why does everyone insist on calling us that? Tayfaern, remind me to come up with a better name when time permits.\n\nAs for leader …? Well, I guide this gathering of Reachfolk, if that's what you're asking. But what about you? Why are you here?

The leader? Now that's a worthy bit of news.\n\nBones and birds guide us well, but there's no replacing a cunning hunter. Go to the barrow, harrier. Listen in on their meeting. Find out what Belain and her master are up to, and I'll hear you out.

Let me see your map. Yes, I know that name, but Dwarven mischief riddles the bones of the Reach. It could be anywhere.\n\nHmm. My mother called this place the Hissing Maze. Said it's full of mechanical monsters that guard a trove of silver.
Well done, harrier.\n\nNow, once we undertake this ritual, we will be bound by blood and spirit. It's a union stronger than stone and more eternal than the stars. Are you ready for such a commitment?

It must have been impressive once, but it's falling into ruin now. Apparently, it was the seat of power for an ancient vampire clan—the Nighthollow. All that's left of them are a scattering of feral beasts.\n\nPlus, the place is full of Void energy.

Bah! You speak with that half-giant's tongue. What business is it of yours what I do with my land? I gave that parcel to Mannimarco years ago. It was his to offer to Molag Bal as he pleased. Why dredge up such dealings now?

I didn't know that was the Elf's intent when I granted him the domain, but we honor Molag Bal, just like all the great spirits.\n\nYou won't find many here would deny an offering to a great spirit, no matter how grand.

Mannimarco didn't call me confidant. When he departed, he said the failure here would forge his success elsewhere. I never saw him again.\n\nIf you want to know his mind, you'll have to see what he wrought yourself. I'll open the way for you.

Not so long ago Reachfolk ruled the Empire. We had our lands returned and dignity restored. Then we were driven back into the mud by the usurper. \n\nMannimarco pledged justice for my people if I gave him shelter. A dark spirit's bargain, to be sure.

It's nothing—I … I don't want to concern the others. Whatever Rada did at the orrery, it connected the Gray Host to the Dark Heart. And that includes me.\n\nLike the souls of Markarth that the Heart consumed, a part of me is caught within the Void.

I don't know. I can feel the Dark Heart's pulse. A throbbing that grows stronger as the Heart becomes more powerful. But it hasn't consumed me. In fact, like Arana and Lady Belain, I may be able to draw upon it—though I haven't attempted that yet.
The strange dark magic that's drifting around the Library of Arkthzand? Verandis calls it Void energy. He's been studying it, trying to find its source. \n\nThat's what led him to Nighthollow Keep.

Well, you know those shades? Verandis says they're souls that got caught in the currents. It twisted them into hungry, hateful shadows. But you also used it to move around, so it's not all bad.\n\nHe's worried that Rada al-Saran wants that energy.

Not much. I did a lot of digging into the Gray Host, but I never found a scrap about the Nighthollow.\n\nWe're learning that some of the ancient vampire clans built kingdoms in Blackreach. My guess? The Nighthollow have been hiding down there forever.

Good. Then we're that much closer to completing Freyleth's plan and replacing Boss Trenlor. Obviously, none of us can walk in and join the Lothid celebration. Everyone knows we were cast into the Deep Tombs.\n\nYou'll have to perform the next step.

This trinket Rada al-Saran left behind. It radiates a magical residue similar to what Verandis leaves behind when he casts auramancy. Perhaps you've seen him use it to draw memories from the past?\n\nI wonder why Rada al-Saran left it here?

That wasn't the Verandis we know. Rada al-Saran cast auramancy on that trinket. It pulled a memory, an echo out of the ancient past.\n\nBut why did he leave that here? He had to know we'd be able to access the magic.

The Dream-Walk elixir is certainly more … intrusive, but it's also better for uncovering the full story.\n\nVerandis possesses a natural talent for auramancy. Perhaps he learned it from Rada al-Saran, or vice versa?

Freyleth has a plan. A way to replace Boss Trenlor and choose a new leader. Someone who wants to improve the Lothid instead of aggrandizing their own position. Once that happens, I can leave.\n\nTalk to Freyleth. She explains things better than I do.

Yes, Bthar-Zel. I overheard while you were speaking to Arana. We discussed finding it while you were gathering the ritual components. Locating the keystone is your next priority.\n\nArana indicated that she wanted to accompany you.

You missed it, too? What a pair we make!\n\nWhat did Hircine show us? He revealed the Snake, which I thought was just a substitute for our prey. But the sky tales on the plaques—the Witch, the Headsman, and the Hunter—they're the Reach Guardians!

Feh. I try not to think too hard about Dwarf mischief. But I do have a notion.\n\nWe found three sky tales in the hills, right? Guardians, they were. Your Warrior, Thief, and Mage. I think we need their help to catch our prey.

No, but she has a sensitivity that I do not possess. Most powerful witches do. Let's hope she recovers quickly.\n\nIt is said that mechanical horrors guard the depths of Bthar-Zel. No matter what, we must find the keystone.

Ah, right, I suppose that does require some explanation.\n\nI belong to House Ravenwatch. One of the wards of Count Verandis. We make it our business to track down vampires who cause too much trouble around Tamriel.

The longer I spend in close proximity, the more I pick up from the shades. I sense fragmented thoughts and raw emotion. They remind me of pure rage and unbridled pain. \n\nPerhaps exploring the library will yield some answers.

I already feel my strength returning. It's the Dark Heart. Like the Ghostsong witches of old, I feel its power stirring within me. I hear the whispering of Namira.\n\nThe Spirit Queen is with me. I won't die in this place.

No, not in and of itself. Like all of Namira's gifts, how we use it is where good and evil come in. It's Belain who is twisting it to this vile purpose. Stop her.\n\nGo on. I'll gather my strength and then see where the Spirit Queen wants to lead me.
You're asking me? No idea. But it's here and so was Rada al-Saran, so I'd guess it's got something to do with whatever he's planning.

I saw it. I don't know what it was, but I saw it. It didn't set you on fire, so as far as mysterious magic goes, I'd count your blessings.\n\nWas that the illustrious Count Ravenwatch I've heard so much about? Well, let's not keep the real one waiting.
Excellent. Then let's not waste time. The sooner the ritual is completed, the safer Karthwasten will be.\n\nIf we might enlist your help one last time, my friend.
As before, present yourself at the ritual pyre. You are more deeply woven into this land and its survival than ever. Quickly now, let's finish this and restore the wards.

This one needs to get Kathad settled. Explain the rules of the Ravenwatch and start his training.\n\nBut Adusa also wants to check in with the rest of House Ravenwatch. See what else must be done to safeguard the Reach.

For now? Nothing. The Ravenwatch has other, more imminent threats to deal with.\n\nI hope Freyleth decides to take the Lothid clan in a different direction. However, if she continues the practices put in place by Boss Trenlor ….

And yet you waste years away from your family, caring for those who live short and meaningless lives. \n\nAh, Verandis. Is my word not enough to appease you? We will speak more of this later. For now, I wish to discuss more pleasant topics.

I encountered Adusa shortly after I … changed. She was a true friend. Helped me through the transition. I almost joined the Ravenwatch at the time, but Freyleth ….\n\nShe thought I should experience more of the world before choosing a direction.

Freyleth brought me here. She was part of the clan a long time ago and had fond memories of her time with them.\n\nUnfortunately, since she left, Boss Trenlor became the clan leader. He welcomed us at first, but then he showed his true colors.

I want to. If Adusa and the others will still have me.\n\nI know I have a lot to prove to them. A lot to live up to. I hope they'll give me a chance to show them what I have to offer. And I look forward to learning from them as well.

Now that our wards are back in place, I think so. We still need to deal with the remaining villagers who turned feral. But we collapsed part of the mine, so we shouldn't have any more trouble from that direction.

Name's Gwendis, of House Ravenwatch. Not that that would mean anything to you. The short answer is we keep an eye on troublesome vampires—and werewolves now—to keep them in check.\n\nAnd no, Arkasis isn't either, that I know of, but his allies are.

Oh, I'm more certain of that than ever! I asked for help and the spirits provided. The fact that they sent an outsider … that gives me and the clan something to think about.\n\nNot everything outside this village is dark and dangerous, I suppose.

The clan always respected Freyleth. And, in general, they hated Boss Trenlor. His power and their fear, it kept them bound as effectively as locks and chains.\n\nI have no doubt the clan will accept Freyleth's leadership. I suspect they already have.

They understand little that does not serve their own needs. They do not understand why we started the Gray Council or what an asset you are to the Gray Host. \n\nIt will take much to convince them to make peace with mortals.

Your dream and mine are similar, my friend, but they are not the same. This friction between us, it thins my patience. Still, this place, no matter how grand, did not feel complete until you returned.\n\nYou belong here, Verandis.

I'm not an alchemist, but I know a thing or two about these darling little mushrooms. When soaked in blood, they release a substance that impinges upon vampiric virility.\n\nIt's the perfect method for dealing with Boss Trenlor.

For the same reason he sends any of the clan here … I displeased him. When Kathad left, I tried to talk to Trenlor. Get him to change. That enraged him and ….\n\nI hardly believed my eyes when Kathad came to rescue me from this horrid hole.
Don't you give me attitude, my darling. I get enough of that from Kathad and Adusa.\n\nIf you must know, we couldn't allow her to raise the alarm. My plan hinges on Trenlor not suspecting a thing.

Exactly what you'd expect. The clan will accept me as their leader. We'll regroup. Decide what we want to do next. And then we'll do it.\n\nOh, we won't be as blunt and chaotic as Trenlor. We won't attract undue attention. I am nothing if not subtle.

Nothing. Well, I know it's a Dwarven ruin. But aside from that, Dwemer studies have never been my strongpoint. \n\nYou've been there before, haven't you? Together we'll figure it out. We've managed to make it this far with less to go on.

You stand before Rada al-Saran and seek to understand his purpose?\n\nBetter a torchbug try to comprehend the secrets of alchemy or a mudcrab the intricacies of necromancy. These events began millennia before your birth. They concern you not at all.

Ard Caddach's the ruler around here, right? I've never known a competent ruler who doesn't know his realm like the back of his hand. And I've never heard that the Despot of Markarth wasn't competent.\n\nWe'll find it, mark my words.

Who is this we you speak of? Certainly not the Reachfolk. No, there is someone else. I see them, lurking in your thoughts. An ally, almost as ancient as I am. They're desperate to forestall the coming night.\n\nTell me. Who is this person?

Reachmen had their arses on the Ruby Throne before Varen won the Empire. And Mannimarco was the architect of his destruction. I wouldn't be surprised if they welcomed the Worm King into Markarth with a parade.\n\nLet's go ask Caddach all about it.

Just what Verandis told me while we were doing our research. We know that the Nighthollow clan is older than the stones we're standing on.\n\nThe archive might contain thousands of years of secrets. Or it might be full of nothing but dust.

That's a distinct possibility, but I don't believe Rada intends to kill me. At least not yet. He has something to prove. That need will stay his hand better than any armor.\n\nWe don't have the luxury of ignoring his invitation in any case.

That's where the trail is leading me. I won't know until we find it. My gut tells me it's close. Well, my nose does anyway. I've gotten all too familiar with the smell of werewolves lately, and there's a tinge of something … alchemical in the air.

That's the million drake question. Didn't you and Fennorian discover that the Gray Host was using these to resurrect their dead? Maybe Arkasis played a role in devising that? It sounds crazy enough for his tastes.

Hatching them? Like an egg? Think Fennorian left that part out.\n\nWell, we aren't going to get anywhere by standing around guessing. Keep an eye out for more Gray Host stuff laying around. I'll be right behind you.
I sensed some deception, but her illusion is powerful. How else did she hide her nature from me?\n\nAs for Arana, do you think we can convince her and her rebels to join our cause?

You spoke to Rada? Did he—? No matter. If Rada al-Saran is here, our time grows short.\n\nTalk to Caddach. If he deems what you tell him worthy, maybe he'll finally be willing to work with me. Then we can figure out how to deal with the Gray Host.

Everything I'd heard about Arkasis paints him as an egotistical, self-proclaimed genius and obsessive dabbler. I don't see him agreeing to mass produce these husks himself. He'd think it's a waste of his talent. There's got to be more going on.

So he says. I was looking for my brother in Solitude when this dubious fellow stumbles up to me. Told me he knows who I am and that he can show me proof of Lady Thorn's evil army.\n\nI don't trust him, but I thought I'd hear him out.

That's his story. They held him prisoner for weeks until he somehow managed to escape. Then he happens to run into a member of the noble house that deals with evil vampires. Seems rather convenient, right?

Mannimarco, Emperor Varen, Nords, Reachmen, his flea-bitten beard.\n\nI can stomach insults hurled at me, but I couldn't stand there quietly as he spoke ill of Varen while praising that traitor Mannimarco.

Some correspondence had been piling up. And that giant werewolf, Kraglen, his orders weren't to come protect Stone Garden. He was sent to keep Arkasis on schedule. I definitely want to find out what they've got him working on.

Hroldan Ring is an ancient site southeast of here. It's neutral ground. A place where all clans of the Reach can gather to trade and share stories.\n\nBradan visits the place a lot. He loves to chatter with other clans.

I have been well, thank you. The Pyre Watch grows slowly but surely. My efforts to rebuild have been fruitful, but my duty does not cease. I have not forgotten what you and Fennorian did. Not for a moment.\n\nHow is Fennorian?

It's a bit easier to follow than Arkasis's scribbling and it's in Old Aldmeris. Theories on the nature of souls. Their connections to each other, the world, the planes of existence. Heady stuff.\n\nSomeone wants Arkasis to study this, but why?

The darkness crashes against my mind like waves slamming into the shore. It can be … distracting. I can function normally, with the occasional need to pause and let the sensation pass.\n\nI can't yet control the darkness, but I haven't been idle.

The Dark Heart again? According to the prophecy, death awakens the Dark Heart—by the spirits, what evil has Belain convinced my sister to perform?\n\nWe need to find Nathari and stop her before something terrible takes place.

We follow the sigils to wherever they lead. \n\nThe survivor of the battle at Bangkorai Garrison must have seen these and used them as a guide to get to wherever they were hidden. If we find that place, we'll find answers. Come on!

That's because you aren't a vampire or a werewolf! Hold on, I've got just the thing. Here, a blood pendant. It lets me share some of my vampiric essence so you can see the sigils too. It's perfectly safe.\n\nAt least, Fennorian said it was harmless.
We follow the sigils, of course!\n\nThe Gray Host survivor must have used these as a guide, and they were made for that specific purpose. Now, let's see where they lead.

An equally dusty old vampire. The Ravenwatch has been keeping watch on her for ages. She's a recluse who mostly just keeps to her castle. She's never been trouble, so we've left her be. That'll change if she's in league with the Gray Host.

They both seek to awaken the Dark Heart so they can use the void energy it releases for their own ends.\n\nCurrently, Rada has activated the orrery in the library for some unknown purpose, while Belain has gone to Markarth to lead the Gray Host army.

I wish I could say for certain. We know the Dark Heart allows pockets of void energy to seep into our world. Perhaps he plans to use the orrery to focus that power. Or to open a larger tear into the Void.\n\nWhatever he plans, I need to stop him.

Then you know how brave and knowledgeable they are. \n\nOne of their warriors was here recruiting when the garrison came under attack. She offered to protect the scholars that fled and I haven't seen them since. I fear for their safety. Can you help?

They're guardians sworn to watch over a Gray Host burial site located here in Bangkorai.\n\nOne of their warriors was here recruiting when the garrison came under attack. She went to protect my colleagues, but no one's returned. Can you go find them?

Oh, I'll admit, I do miss the trees. But everyone is so friendly here, and the food, mmm. There's so much of it! Delicious, squirmy, screaming food.\n\nDoes that bother you? The screaming? I recall us discussing such things last time we spoke.

Oh, but that's no fun, is it? It's like hunting a beast in a cage. Where's the challenge? No, Verandis, I'll take my prey squirmy and terrified. It gets the blood pumping!\n\nNezbi and I are going hunting later today. You must come!

An odd question from one of Rada al-Saran's esteemed Gray Council. We are all here for the same reasons, are we not? Power over life and death. Control over our own fate.\n\nIn Vvardenfell, I am the sixth of eight sons. Here, I will become much more.

Is that why you've returned after so long away? You were lonely?\n\nI must confess, I find every day away from the insufferable bickering of House Indoril a blessing. But perhaps we are cut from different cloth.

So you are! Oh, Verandis, your endless wellspring of positivity is absolutely refreshing! You are such a generous soul.\n\nI must say, the idea of giving up all I've earned and bled for to placate humans is quite hysterical.

But isn't that why we have thralls? So we can take as much as we wish! They don't mind, do they?\n\nOh, are you going to speak with Lord Rada al-Saran? Be a dear and remind him we set aside some time to drink, would you?

A question for Sithis, unanswered. All answers come from Sithis, though few are worthy to hear them.\n\nYet we, alone, are blessed. We will go beyond, one day, when we have made the offerings he seeks. Only then may we flow into the dark water.

The others speak of you as short-sighted, but I hear in your words the truth we all seek. All must come to Sithis. Death is the path to him, and Sithis is the path to the dark water. It is a goal for all.\n\nCome now. Pray with me.

As boring as ever. Until fair Hestra came along, I'd all but given up on entertainment entirely.\n\nThe new empress is fascinating, isn't she, Verandis? A true warrior. Mortal yes, but quite the conqueror. If she could be turned ….

Perhaps. Yet Rada al-Saran saw the wisdom in immortal power, did he not? Hestra could be similarly convinced. Still, when she dies, and she will die, I expect it will be glorious. Worthy of a song.\n\nThat will be entertainment enough.

Gorge? Ha! This is just a midday snack!\n\nEver since we came here, we've had more blood than we can stomach, and I can stomach quite a bit. The dungeons are overflowing with delicious morsels. Lord Rada al-Saran knows how to keep us fat and happy!
Ah, I probably shouldn't have mentioned that. Forgive me, Verandis. Don't trouble yourself over it. Forget I said anything at all. \n\nHa! I need another drink.

My ancestors must feel great shame watching me care for the well-being of a scion of Bal. Still, it comforts me to know he endures, even during these unholy times.\n\nMara willing, our paths will cross again.

These Dwemer devices are similar to pieces of the orrery itself. They manipulate various cosmic forces—tonal, aetheric, and kinetic—to chart the expanse of the Void.\n\nYou must keep these forces under control for my scrying to succeed.

The components you retrieved from B'thar-zel showed me that the keystones consist of these same sorts of devices, just on a smaller scale. As I conduct the ritual, I'll indicate what parts of the process require your intervention.\n\nBe on your toes.

Don't you see? In their own realm, free from Molag Bal's tyranny, the Gray Host can live forever. And with the connection to Mundus and the power of the Dark Heart, their conquests might never end.\n\nAnd now I see … the purpose of the Darkstorm ….
Arrgh! The Dark Heart … Rada's drawing on its power. I can feel it tearing away.\n\nTo the orrery! Hurry!

<<1>>? She probably sent you to find <<2>>. She loves that bunny more than life itself. That's why I've been walking around in circles for hours. I can't go back without Snowy.\n\nHow did you get her to follow you? She's usually scared of strangers.

My sweet brother. Fennorian reminds me of myself when I first turned. Nervous, hesitant, uncontrolled. But he has a gentler spirit, so the hunger disturbs him more. \n\nWe're both lucky that Verandis taught us so well.

Well, several people have mysteriously disappeared from the area. And rumors keep reaching Castle Ravenwatch that Lady Thorn recently became more active. Seems like a worthwhile place to visit, if only to take a peek.

Vampiric salvation. To accomplish this, he needed to break Molag Bal's hold over us and stop mortals from hunting us. I counseled peace with mortals, and for awhile he agreed.\n\nBut things changed and I left the Gray Host. I thought he died with them.

Not exactly. At least, not all at once.\n\nWhen I first met Rada, he was immensely proud but utterly consumed by his failures. He tried to find relief in bloodshed and battle, but he was truly lost. I did my best to help him.
Yes, and I don't know why I thought it was a good idea to return. The experiments they performed on me—and others like me—were unspeakable.

Never in all my existence have I seen anything like it. Once, it held out its palms toward me and began whispering. A wisp of magic emerged and entered my chest. I could … feel it inside me, writhing.\n\nI think it was testing my soul.

I did just say they were unspeakable, yes?\n\nApologies, it's just so hard to think back on. They kept us in cages. Barely fed us. Mindless fiends would stagger by our cells, growling. A strange creature would come by and whisper an unnatural language.
They hold the prisoners underground, deep below the castle. She needs to see what Lady Thorn's creatures have done to them. Only then will Gwendis understand the extent of what must be done.
