Let's not get ahead of ourselves.\n\nHelp me with this investigation and we'll see how it goes.

The whistle, of course! I was so angry, I forgot to take it with me. I just hope that when I return with Snowy, Hiretta will forgive me.\n\nI suppose we need to discuss our plans. Maybe this part of the Reach isn't as safe as I imagined.

It must have something to do with the sky above. Or perhaps constellations, such as those that led us to Bthar-Zel.\n\nIn any event, it's evident that the dark current flowing through this place traps souls and twists them into these shades.

The best answer may be none of them. I suspect the Dark Heart may have been here before all of them. More than likely, they found it and made use of it. Across the ages, different people may have been drawn to its power.\n\nWe may never know for sure.
Perhaps. Curious, isn't it? I wonder if the Dark Heart has a purpose of its own.\n\nWe better keep going. Until we actually find this thing, all we have are guesses.

Who else? The Ravenwatch noticed some suspicious trafficking in ancient vampire remains and it lead to a much wider conspiracy. My brothers and sisters are all out chasing leads. \n\nVampires. Always making trouble. Good thing I don't need sleep.

What? Do you think I can't handle it? Verandis said I'm ready. He's the only one who gets to judge.\n\nTruth is, I'm glad for some help though. This would be a tall order, even for Adusa, but there's not enough of us to go around.

I've been out on my own a lot since … since Verandis, you know. We all have. There weren't a lot of us in House Ravenwatch to begin with. Everyone has to pull their weight and this conspiracy has us spread thin.\n\nThis'll be a nice change of pace.

Where to begin. Someone was smuggling ancient vampire and werewolf remains out of Bangkorai and bringing them to Western Skyrim, but … we don't know why. My investigation says a lot of them were brought to Stone Garden, but the rest is a mystery.

We sure did. Basement prisons, just as Talfyg claimed. Recently used and in horrifying conditions—blood and bones everywhere. I think I saw a dismembered leg.\n\nWorryingly, I didn't see any actual prisoners.

Extremely similar. Well, I suppose most prisons look the same. But you're right, these felt more like livestock pens, just like those in the Keep.\n\nWe need to find out what Lady Thorn did with those prisoners. And what she offers the Ashen Lord.

Why would a horde of vampires keep anybody in a basement prison? Saving them for later I imagine. In fact, these felt much like livestock pens.\n\nWe need to find out what Lady Thorn did with those prisoners.

I mean, if I wanted to build an army, having mindless hordes at the front lines would be an asset, yes? And if I could convert them from my opponent's forces? Even better.\n\nThat is, if I wanted to do that.
Yeah, that's a little disconcerting. Usually evil vampires don't want House Ravenwatch anywhere near their business.\n\nIf she thinks I'll join this army of hers, she's gone mad from isolation.
I want to destroy anything that could be used to bring another one of those creatures back to our world.\n\nSomething like … this must never happen again.

According to the stories, bloodknights operate in service to Vampire Lords. But that doesn't make sense. Lady Thorn can't be … Ravenwatch would know.\n\nWe need to tread extremely carefully going forward.

From what I can tell, Lady Thorn used to be Lady Ingerien of Clan Direnni. I wonder why she changed her name?\n\nAnd this is interesting—a letter expressing gratitude for "providing shelter in our darkest hour."

I don't know yet. But it's imperative I figure it out. The safety of Tamriel could rely on it.\n\nLook, Lady Thorn is a threat. And I've seen you fight. No matter what she throws at you, I know you can handle it. You must take her down.
I need to collect as much of these documents as I can before something happens to them. There's someone I know that could make good use of the information here.\n\nI'll join you as soon as I can.

Look at what we know so far. Arkasis's research started long ago, before the Gray Host even existed. And Lady Thorn's documents discussed a group that started the Gray Host.\n\nWe need to understand more about the Gray Host's origins.

Maybe we start where they first ended. Bangkorai. The original fall of the Gray Host.\n\nI need to reach out to some people. But I'll be in touch soon. We should take a trip to the Bangkorai Garrison.

Very well. Manipulate the crystals and see if you can set the tortured shade free.\n\nJust exercise caution, my friend. I would hate to see you trapped within the apparatus alongside the Gray Host pentarch.

This Gray Host is somehow connected to the army that ravaged the land in the First Era. Like their ancient counterpart, I assume they seek to conquer and destroy. I need to learn more to know for sure.\n\nMeanwhile, we must get the Reach to prepare.

The Reachfolk possess a distinct culture that you'll see during your time here. They also enjoy the same capacity for virtue and evil as Bretons, Nords, and the other peoples of Tamriel.\n\nAnimal skins don't make one a barbarian. Actions do.

Good. So am I. Let's hope the spirits feel the same way.\n\nPlace the components in the fire and stand back. No matter what you see or hear, stand your ground and think about our alliance. Keep that purpose in your mind. Understand?
Of course, Lord Verandis. My apologies. \n\nPlease, you shouldn't keep the exarchs waiting.

Exarch Ulfra likes to look out over the courtyard from the eastern balcony. Exarch Tzinghalis rarely leaves his laboratory on the upper level. Both want to see you.\n\nI will inform you once your crates have been moved to the study set aside for you.

Gwendis brought news from Markarth. Lady Belain has departed the city and she intends to give chase. I will assist her in the hope that pursuing Belain might turn up something useful.\n\nJust don't let that keystone fall into Rada al-Saran's hands.

As a noble of Rivenspire, I'm here under the guise of a diplomatic mission. However, as the leader of the Ravenwatch, my real purpose remains to protect mortals from all manner of supernatural threats.

Look at your map. See how the marks form the shape of the Snake in the Stars? And see how one mark is missing? If I place it here, we see the Snake in its entirety. That's where we need to go!\n\nAs for the Reach Guardians … well, we'll see.

Obviously. I'm glad we can speak plainly.\n\nThe Ravenwatch doesn't kill vampires. At least, not unless absolutely necessary. We offer a different path. A way to live beside mortals without fear or temptation. I trust that won't be a problem for you.

Brace yourself. The Ravenwatch consists of honorable vampires dedicated to restraining the less-desirable elements in our brethren. This mandate extends to other supernatural threats, of which the Gray Host is certainly one.\n\nAnd yes, I am a vampire.

We do not kill unless no other option presents itself.\n\nWe seek to offer our kin a different path. To help them find a way to live alongside mortals without fear or temptation. By words and deeds if possible. By force, if necessary.

I appreciate the sentiment. The Ravenwatch seeks to build a world where mortals and supernaturals can live together in peace. The Gray Host has a different idea, which is why I've come to stop them.\n\nI give you my solemn oath—you can trust me.

An appellation he earned, as I understand it.\n\nArd Caddach is said to be ruthless and powerful, a cruel leader who seeks the ruin of Tamriel and the death of any who reject the spirits—or what you and I call the Daedric Princes.

At least one of us sounds certain of that. Just promise to handle the heroism so Verandis doesn't get himself killed. I know he feels like this is something he's got to do, but he's at the end of his rope.

Rada aligned the orrey in order to make his escape. Use the keystone on the Dwarven mechanisms that control it. That should open a breach we can travel through.\n\nThen maybe I'll have a chance to stop this storm I created.

I never intended my theories to be turned into reality. When my research into a way to grant mortals the same immortality as vampires kept leading down dark paths, I abandoned it. I should have also destroyed it.\n\nRada corrupted it for his own ends.

No, of course not.\n\nI won't mince words. The Reachmen are a stubborn and unruly people. They resort to violence at the least provocation. But despite the opinion of most of civilized Tamriel, they aren't frothing barbarians.

That he's a king of broken antlers and carrion crows who eats the hearts of his enemies and hunts children for sport? Perhaps, but the legend always overshadows the reality.\n\nCaddach's legend is a mix of Daggerfall insults and Reach superstitions.

More like the clan left me! My sister turned them against me. As the days grew darker, the Ghostsong witches found it easier to see things her way than mine.\n\nRegardless, my people will always be my people.

He's a canny leader who applies both caution and brutality in equal measure.\n\nHe calls himself ard, the king of the fort, but his rule isn't absolute. Most Reach clans respect him, however. His help will be crucial in the battles ahead.

Not all Reachfolk practices involve blood and sacrifice, but many of our oldest traditions do. Lost Valley was a center for such activity, once upon a time.\n\nOh, don't worry. You're helping Arana. I won't offer your heart to Namira. Not today.

The full telling requires hours. We don't have time for that, so I'll be brief. \n\nAn ancient darkness sleeps beneath the Reach. At the end of days it will awaken, covering the land in shadow and devouring all. Only Namira's faithful will be spared.

Doesn't matter what I think. It's what Nathari believes she hears. What she sees in every sign and portent.\n\nFrom what Bradan said, she thinks it's time to return to the old ways. Blood sacrifice and dark magic. I wanted nothing to do with that.

Nathari wanted to be matron. And the clan, they were ready to choose her over me. I wanted to forge new traditions, but she promised them Namira's blessing if they heeded the old ways.\n\nFear and superstition are powerful motivators.

We know all about the blood-drinkers and the beast-folk. We were dealing with them just fine before Ard Caddach called us back to Markarth.\n\nThe witch-rebels are a bigger threat. Along with outsiders who try to get into our business.

Some wilder witch has been stirring up the clans to the east of Markarth. Making trouble for Ard Caddach. But we'll have her head on a pike soon enough.\n\nLook, if you want to see the ard, then bring news he doesn't know. Something about the rebels.

One of my talents involves auramancy magic. Certain inanimate objects, especially items that hold significant personal value, can become imbued with the auras of those who possessed them.\n\nSometimes I can read vague impressions. Sometimes … more.

A good question. We know that Rada promises freedom to the Gray Host. He spent centuries bringing the various elements of his plan together. How the Nighthollow fit in, I can't say. At least not yet.\n\nHopefully, the answers await us in the keep.

It appears that Lady Belain took the last of the void energy for herself. Enough to saturate her and keep her strong through all these long centuries. While the clan around her starved and turned feral.

Apparently not. Feeding on void energy changed them. They lost the ability to take nourishment from the blood of mortals.\n\nI suspect Lady Belain believes that her clan will recover once the Dark Heart begins to beat again. And she's probably correct.

How do you—oh, you must be who helped Fennorian with his investigation. All I can say for certain is that Arkasis is involved. We won't know if he's the mastermind until we do some digging of our own in Stone Garden.
Something alchemical, most likely, but I'm not crazy enough to even hazard a guess what. They call him the Mad Alchemist for a reason. Somehow I doubt it'll be a cure for Daedric diseases.

They're both part of a broader conspiracy, but how they both fit into the overall picture is still a work in progress. Lady Thorn sent some documents to Arkasis related to whatever they're plotting. I'm hoping that's the missing piece to this puzzle.

Is now really the best time? Ugh. Those large urn-looking things. Full of ashes from the Gray Host's mass grave in Bangkorai, plundered by some grave robbers and smuggled into Western Skyrim. I'd really like to know why.

Oh, he's just my brother. Not literally, part of House Ravenwatch. All of us are investigating this conspiracy at the moment.\n\nIt doesn't matter right now. I'm going to do some investigating of my own, and you should start wrecking their plans.

Just an army of vampires and werewolves. They got wiped out in the First Era. Burned to ashes and buried deep. The Redguards even formed an order to watch over the grave and ensure their evil stayed buried. That's all I know. Fennorian's the expert.

Look at what we know so far. Arkasis' research started long ago, before the Gray Host even existed. And Lady Thorn's documents discussed a group that started the Gray Host.\n\nWe need to understand more about the Gray Host's origins.

Maybe we start where they first ended. Bangkorai. The original fall of the Gray Host.\n\nI need to reach out to some people. But I'll be in touch soon. We should take a trip to the Bangkorai Garrison.

Aye, you and the half-giant both, so the crows say. Don't think I've not spied on you same as Lady Belain.\n\nI gave that land to Mannimarco long before the God of Scheme's brought his wrath to your Empire. The labors of his cult cast it to Oblivion.
Rada has already aligned the device to point to our destination. Theoretically, we need only reactivate the orrery to open the gateway.\n\nBe on your guard nevertheless.

You must bring an offering of nature and earth to each of the wards.\n\nThe fallen branches of willow trees, for they represent the fragility of life. Rocks bathed in moonlight, for purity. And husks of the cicada, for they represent rebirth.

There were. Skyrim, too. It seems that, long ago, the first clans established an empire beneath the surface. Even Verandis thought it was only a legend. But we're finding more and more proof every time we enter a new cavern down in Blackreach.

Then let's go inside. But let me talk first. With all that's happened, we wouldn't want him to curse you before I can explain your presence.\n\nJust keep an open mind. Our ways are different from yours, outsider.

Placing the offerings at the four wards isn't the hard part. Gathering them and dealing with whatever prowls our homeland is.\n\nKeep each other safe and Apprentice Fialyn will guide you through the restoration process once you gather the offerings.

I recognize these. They're from a plant that grows beneath Karthwasten. These look wrong, though. Corrupted. \n\nThis must be what caused the ritual to fail. But how did they get into the ritual pyre?
I agree. If this plant caused our restoration ritual to fail, who knows what other evil it can be used for.\n\nLet's investigate the old mine. There's an entrance just to the north of the village.
Yes. It grows in nearby caves and down in the Sanuarach Mine.

This isn't like the plant I've seen before. It seems contaminated in some way.


It grows in nearby caves and down in the Sanuarach Mine. I wonder if that's the source of this corrupted plant?

No one sent you? What, you just stumbled on this place? You must be an adventurer! Like me!\n\nWell, you've found Black Drake Villa—the former home away from home of the Longhouse Emperors. And the place where they stashed something very important.
How's that fancy villa holding up these days with Leovic gone? I bet the Goblins that moved in aren't taking great care of it. They don't strike me as having a great sense of style.

The people who hired me provided a map to a library under the mansion. My job is to find some book that the old owners hid down there.\n\nHey, care to join forces? Together we can grab this book in no time. And you can keep any loot you find.

This mine holds much more than bats and mold. A cult seeking immense power waits within. I fear that Drathas alone cannot withstand such foes.\n\nMore of us could improve our odds. How about I sweeten the deal? Some gold if you help retrieve the box?

The prophecy talks of death and destruction, but it also says that those who embrace it will be spared. There's power in the darkness, especially for those who believe and hold true to its word.\n\nNow let's go try to save my clan from this madness.

Alas, you seek facts and figures that I don't have readily at hand. Perhaps when I can retrieve my papers from inside the garrison …?\n\nYou know, the Pyre Watch warrior might be able to help you. They're experts on the Gray Host of the First Era.

Reachfolk deal in bargains. They respect strength and skill. And they believe in rewarding favors. If we can bring something important to the ard while demonstrating these qualities, I think he'll agree to hear us out.

If we're to stop the Gray Host and help the Reach, we don't have a choice. At the very least, we need his resources and support.\n\nIn my time here, I've heard about these rebels, but I'm not sure the extent of their rebellion. See what you can learn.

No. Like ghosts, these rebels are!\n\nI plan to return to Markarth and petition the ard to let me take a war party out to find them. They must be hiding in the eastern foothills. I don't care if they are fighting the Gray Host. They're mine!

Aye. They agreed to spare the city while they look for some ancient relic. Dwarven, I suspect. They can have it.\n\nVerandis wants to meet? Then talk to my advisor, Lady Belain. Track down Arana for her and I'll listen to every word he has to say.

While I may not have been born and raised in the Reach, I have earned my place as friend and counselor to Ard Caddach.\n\nHis subjects call me a keep-witch. I assure you, this is a term of the utmost respect among the Reachfolk.

Yes. A bridge between the Reach and the civilized world.\n\nThere's simply no reason that the people of Tamriel should go on killing each other. We have an opportunity to build a kinder, better Tamriel. I'm here to help make that future come to pass.

A genuine desire for peace brought me here.\n\nThe Reach finds itself beset from all sides. Orcs, Nords, Bretons, Imperials … they all seek the destruction of the Reachfolk. I try to serve as a bridge of sorts.
A history lesson? Very well.\n\nCaddach is the cousin of the late Emperor Leovic. He was appointed ruler of Markarth and has governed this region ever since.

Reachfolk have a saying. Anyone can be a king in the Reach. No one can be a king of the Reach.\n\nFew Reachfolk will accept a true sovereign. It isn't in their nature. Of course, that makes Caddach's attempts to safeguard this region … complicated.

Ard is an ancient title that translates to king of the fort. The fort being Markarth and Understone Keep.\n\nAs for that other epithet, it's a name given to him by enemies and outsiders. He may be cruel at times, but he's no tyrant.

The Lothid, a local clan of vampires, terrorizes the countryside from their lair in the ruins below us. This one convinced young Kathad to leave this clan of criminals. Or so I thought.\n\nFor some reason, he returned to them. This troubles me.

Adusa-daro was close to saving a vampire from a life of crime. Why Kathad went back to his clan, I do not know. But I am not ready to give up on him just yet.\n\nWill you help me extract Kathad from the Lothid clan, five-claw?
What is any rebellion all about? Malcontents chafing against the established order, stirring up trouble.\n\nThey're a nuisance, nothing more.

Peace, yes. Of a sort. As long as we stay out of their way, the Gray Host has no quarrel with us. Besides, the walls of Markarth are impregnable. The Reachfolk are perfectly safe in here.\n\nNow go. Find Arana. A favor performed is a favor returned.

It's a matter of timing. Since the arrival of the Gray Host, the land beyond the city walls has become perilous. The ard urges everyone to take shelter here in Markarth, while Arana calls them away.\n\nHer reckless endeavor will get everyone killed.

I have to rebuild my coven. No simple task, but the darkness in the pit of the Reach will need guardians. Now's not the time for such grim concerns, though.\n\nFor now, all I want to do is find many friends and embrace them all.

As an outsider, you may not understand. The wards are dedicated to the most revered spirits of our clan. In exchange for offerings, they provide blessings.\n\nUnfortunately, the storm disrupted the wards. The shaman sent me to restore them, but ….

No, but I'm sure it was the same as the one from Viridian Watch. Not that it matters. You read the damned letter. It proves … I don't know what it proves! That my mentor might have been part of a cabal of vampires that tried to conquer Tamriel?

Not much. The letter mentioned a name. Grayhome. Kind of pretentious, if you ask me.\n\nAnd there's supposed to be a castle. If it's still there after all these centuries, maybe we can learn more about Verandis and his connection to the Gray Host.

No. Not with the feral villagers prowling the wilderness. I couldn't even get close to any of the wards. \n\nShaman Ulvoch can tell you more about what we need to do. I'm only an apprentice. He explains things much better than I do.
Harrowfiends? What a horrible yet fitting name. You know these things? Then you truly are the answer to my prayers. \n\nWhat else can you tell me about harrowstorms?

That's what I said—it's unnatural! It was unlike any magic of the Reach that I'm aware of. What that storm did to our people, it's an atrocity! Whatever created that storm has poisoned our land. There will be a reckoning.
I got to say goodbye. There was so much more I wanted to say to him … but at least there was that.\n\nI need some time, but I'll carry on.
You were supposed to bring him back!\n\nJust get away from me! Leave me alone.

He's had the Ravenwatch shadowing the Gray Host's movements from here to the Sea of Ghosts. If he's calling for you, it means we finally discovered something we can act upon.\n\nWe're all tired of chasing shadows—especially Verandis.

Of course she is. She's a vampire, after all. We tried to slay her twice without much luck. Quick as a spooked hare, that one, and twice as cautious. We'll have her fangs soon enough, though.\n\nYou can read? What else does that sheet of paper say?

Overthrow Markarth? What in Namira's name would I do with all that dead stone?\n\nNo. My purpose is clear. I need to help our people by shaking Caddach out of his dream. If that doesn't work, I'll split his skull and let it spill out on its own.

Caddach's dream of being king.\n\nOh, he has a true heart. In better times, he's a fine leader. But we face a lean season. We're hungry, but instead of filling the larder, he dreams of a golden crown. His foolish pride has brought this upon our people.

You noticed the banners on the castle walls, huh? Not an encouraging sign. If Lady Thorn really has built an army then it only increases the threat from the Gray Host.\n\nWhich means it's more important than ever that we stop it.

Maybe, but you have to go alone from here, harrier. There's a fork in the path and we need to go our separate ways. At least for a while.\n\nThere's something down here … a darkness. Like leeches in a pond, it takes little bites of my soul.

Not yet. Not until all the beasts of the woods howl his name. And every day he heeds Belain is another day he proves me right.\n\nThe Gray Host has dark plans for Markarth. Caddach's stubbornness will get everyone in that city killed.

What's to tell? I'm a proud woman of the Reach. A daughter of wind, sweat, and the rich soil. As for my brothers and sisters, they're good Reachfolk, every last one of them. They mind the spirits and love the land.\n\nThe real question is who are you?

A fine name, I suppose. For an outsider. But what's in your heart?\n\nMost thinbloods come to the Reach wheezing under the weight of their purses and writ-laws. You, though. I smell the blood of the Reach in you. Not much, but maybe it's enough.
Aye. Free blood. That's what the Reach is. Freedom.\n\nIn the Reach, we do as we please. Only way to stop us is to kill us. And we don't die easy. Same goes for you, I'd say.
I am. And a fine one at that.\n\nWhat? Never met a witch before, harrier?

I need to get back to the surface. I need to see the sky. Feel the wind on my skin. I'll rally the warriors and start preparing for the fight to come.\n\nProtect your heart, harrier. This darkness will eat at you, too, if you let it.

I'm sure! We're not all like the blood-sucking Belain or my misguided sisters from Icereach, though. Some of us aren't overenthusiastic malcontents with a penchant for violence and destruction.\n\nNot all the time, anyway.

Daedra? Oh, the spirits … the old ones. Yes, I've heard them called that.\n\nThe world is full of whispers, for those with the patience to hear. Most thinbloods are just too busy begging pardons from dead gods to pay attention. Pity.

Daedra, spirits, crows … it's all the same. Where you see evil gods, we see teachers. Cruel ones, for certain. But that's the world, right?\n\nA stone will kill you if it strikes your head, but lifting the same stone makes us strong.
Here. Take this <<1>>. Use it on the locations I've marked on your map.
I have no idea what the future holds, but you seem to be the axis upon which this world turns. If it still has some use for me, I'm sure our paths will cross again.\n\nUntil then, my friend.

Now more than ever, my friend! They also sent you to show the Crow-Eye that not all outsiders seek to do us harm.\n\nSome wounds are very deep and very old, but you proved yourself as one of us. That would have been unthinkable before the storm.

I believe so. Thanks to you. You may not be Crow-Eye in blood, but you are in spirit. You're an outsider to us no longer. \n\nYou will always have a home here. You helped us in our time of need. I won't let anyone forget that.

What's left of the Gray Host may be in shambles, but the leftovers are certain to make trouble elsewhere even with their Ashen Lord gone.\n\nPlus, we'll need to catch up on who else has been up to no good while they hogged our attention.

Prince Irnskar is eager to lay out the terms of our new accord, but that's tomorrow's work.\n\nAfter this, my only order of business is to get out of this damned finery. It may be good for impressing folk, but it's like wearing a mountain goat.

Much as anything can. Stone crumbles, forests burn, even Daedra die now and again. This life's a struggle. The only thing that's changed is what we struggle against.\n\nThe peace will last so long as we fight for it.

Aye. We've trod in circles with blood and rage clouding our eyes for as long as anyone can remember, but just now we've glimpsed a new path off this endless trail of suffering. Peace is on the horizon and we're for it now with all we've got.

Not much to rebel against now that Arana's made peace with the ard. We'll stay long enough to deal with any Gray Host lurking nearby, and then we'll be on our way. \n\nMarkarth's not the sort of place werewolves should linger in. Too many people.

It's strange to say, but I don't want to think too far ahead. After everything that happened … I want to relish the present moment. Help Caddach, my people. Just enjoy the time I've been given.\n\nYou should try it, harrier. Do you a world of good.

That's entirely up to you, my friend. Most often, we think of the messages as a way to reflect on the past year. Or to put something down in words that we never got to say to our loved ones. Maybe something we wish we could say to them now.

Some say, on rare occasions, a response returns from Aetherius. It's not guaranteed, of course. \n\nI know of a shrine along an old pilgrimage route … I'll mark it on your map. You can perform the ceremony there.
For the moment, aye. After we tend our wounded, I mean to talk to my father about finding our safety in the wilds. You're the reason we have that chance, and the Hillhunters will never forget it.

No, though I'm hopeful Count Verandis can find something in this coded letter. He's better at ancient languages than I am.\n\nI was able to find this meeting site, and I know the Gray Host forces have regrouped under the command of the ancient exarchs.
Count Verandis is a father to me, more so than my own birth kin. Losing him pained me deeply. \n\nI—I'm looking forward to this second chance we've been given.

Do I? Yes, well, I—I suppose it's only natural. I'm returning from my first real assignment and haven't seen Count Verandis since—well, it was long before I started to investigate the Gray Host.\n\nI want to do him proud.

Lyris? Yes, I think that's what her companion called her. They saved us!\n\nWe were prisoners of Gray Host vampires. Bound for the blood pens, I'm sure! Then that armored giant—Lyris, you say?—she strolled into camp and demanded they free us.

To be perfectly honest, I had my eyes closed through most of it.\n\nThere was a lot of shouting and cursing. Threats were made. I heard the blond giant laugh. Then I heard a great swoosh. Lots of them. Must have been her axe. And her companion's sword.

Every last one of them! They found something on the leader, though. A letter, I think. It got her companion all excited. They mentioned Valthume and departed without another word.\n\nSo I stuck around to see if I could find anything else of value.

Who doesn't look up to to the person that's, for all intents and purposes, their father? Count Verandis made me a part of his noble house. I want to be worthy of that and uphold the ideals of the Ravenwatch.\n\nAnd, besides, I've missed my family.

Aye, that's what the handsome Redguard called her. They came out of nowhere and saved my clan from those Gray Host bastards.\n\nAs grateful as I am, I don't think saving us was their primary purpose. They took down the vampire leader and searched her.

Not exactly, but they found a letter she was carrying. I'm not one of those Imperialized Reachfolk, so I wouldn't have been able to read it if I tried.\n\nIt must have been important, though, because the blond giant started asking me questions.

She wanted to know about Reach history. Now, I'm not one to offer a drowning Nord a branch, but they did just save my clan. So I suggested she find a vateshran at Hroldan Ring.\n\nIf you're looking for the Redguard and his giant, check there.
Problem? More like an opportunity. And it all has to do with these letters we found on the Gray Host leaders at the Reachwind Ritual Site and Valthume.

Well, I can't argue with that description. Sai Sahan is certainly all those things and more.\n\nWe were on our way to Markarth to meet Svana when we decided to help out the locals with their Gray Host problem. That's when we found the letters.

Maybe nothing. But for Sai, maybe everything.\n\nWe think there's a third letter out there. Sai's in Gloomreach, trying to acquire it. Go help him while I finish here. I'm hoping to talk to one of the Reach lorekeepers, a vateshran. If I can find one.
Let me have a look. Yes, this is what I was seeking. The third letter between the vampire leaders. But I was afraid of this. They don't tell the complete story.

That's my Snow Lily. She would never betray my confidence, not even to a trusted partner such as yourself.\n\nI, however, will share what I know. I can't expect you to help if you don't know what's involved.
Excellent! Then by all means, ask your first question.

That word holds little meaning for me now, but yes.\n\nIn my youth, I dedicated my life to perfection. In art. Perfection. In love. Perfection. In war … especially in war. Perfection. To attain glory in Yokuda, nothing less would do.

Impressive! You accomplished more in mere moments than I have been able to do since I arrived in this savage land.\n\nFind Arana. See if the witch-rebels will join our cause. I will continue my own investigations and meet you back here.

Anyone can learn anything from anybody, if they are patient and willing to listen.\n\nI was hoping that the letters would reveal more of the story, but they lack the details necessary to understand how Red Eagle helped Rada al-Saran.

I'm not an expert on Reach lore. That's why we need to find a vateshran.\n\nHowever, none of the legends I've heard suggest Faolan was anything other than a Reachman. The stories do say he was armed with a flaming sword. Maybe that's the connection.

I see nothing Dwarven in their manner or appearance. Dwarves were meticulous scholars. Their constructs, their architecture. Everything was precise and controlled. These shades are like wild animals.\n\nWhatever spawned them may not be Dwarven at all.

Lady Thorn. Before she became a vampire, she was a Direnni noble. Had connections to Viridian Watch. It looks like she helped at least one of the Gray Host's ruling councilors escape on the day their army was defeated in the First Era.

It seems that the Gray Host was ruled by a council of some sort. A few were mentioned, but one was purposely omitted from the ancient record. Must have fallen out of favor, I suppose.\n\nAnyway, those records indicate someone survived the final battle.

This revived Gray Host has been conducting experiments using ancient research. It involves life energy, souls, and these containment vessels called stone husks.\n\nI think it has something to do with bringing the Gray Host leaders back to life.

The Gray Host was ruled by a council of some sort, though one was purposely omitted from the ancient record. Must have fallen out of favor, I suppose.\n\nAnyway, those records indicate someone survived the final battle. I think it was Rada al-Saran.

Whatever the shaman tells me to, of course. I assist the shaman with every ritual and clan ceremony. I listen and observe. When Shaman Ulvoch passes, I'll take his place.\n\nI hope that's a long time from now, for I still have so much to learn.

In the ancient past, the Gray Host sought to use life energy to draw souls into containment vessels called stone husks. It had something to do with returning the dead to life.\n\nI think there's a new Gray Host and they've revived those experiments.

That is a complicated question. A being as old as I can claim many origins.\n\nThis flesh was born on the distant isles of Yokuda. This spirit was forged on the bloody shores of Hammerfell. This purpose … it grew from love. And necessity.
Is it? Beyond the Sea of Pearls, peerless swordmasters were as common as grains of sand. Even the grandest victories felt commonplace.\n\nIn a land of heroes, how can anyone claim to be exceptional?
Probably, but nothing that can't wait.\n\nLet's take the cart to the Bangkorai Garrison and find the scholars who know more about the history of the Gray Host.
Probably, but nothing that can't wait.\n\nLet's take the cart to the Bangkorai Garrison and find the scholars who can tell us more about the history of the Gray Host.

I pestered him until he selected me. I knew I wanted to serve the clan in this way. I've always felt particularly close to the spirits.\n\nA shaman usually chooses their apprentice, but I petitioned Shaman Ulvoch around until he agreed to train me.

Precisely.\n\nAfter the conquest of Hammerfell, I wandered in search of new challenges. I found only one. Leki. Daughter to Ruptga and master of the sword. We fought for three grueling days, without pause for rest or nourishment.

But I didn't win. I didn't lose, either.\n\nI could not accept a draw, however. The cold reality of my imperfection. That resentment drove me to Molag Bal. It took the patient wisdom of a friend to break perfection's hold on me. Now. Your turn.
Interesting. A picture begins to emerge.\n\nDo you have anything else to ask?
Lies are a coward's refuge. Still, your thoughts reveal the truth.\n\nWhat else do you wish to know?
Your ally. Are they a vampire?

I have no interest in conquering the Reach. I came here to make use of something very old. Very powerful. The Reach has the misfortune to be located directly above it. Many of these mortals will die. Not because I want them to, but because they must.
Not when your purpose is worthy. I do what I do for love.\n\nMy turn. Your ally. Are they a High Elf?
Your honesty does you credit. Thank you.\n\nDo you have another question?
A lie. But I see the truth in your thoughts.\n\nStill, I shall give you another chance. Ask another question.

Lady Belain is an ally of convenience. Her interests in my design are selfish and predictably narrow.\n\nDo you seek to supplant her in Caddach's court? I recommend against that, for it will not go well for you.

A threat implies only the possibility of punishment. I do not threaten.\n\nBelain has Caddach's ear. If he takes your side, she kills him and chaos descends on Markarth. If he stands by Belain, you will be executed. Neither outcome benefits you.
Of course he does. Thank you for your honesty.\n\nNow, do you have anything else to ask?
Deception? How disappointing. Still, the lie reveals the truth.\n\nDo you have anything left to ask?

Others? Who? Reachfolk? The witch Arana? Your mysterious ally? I am unconcerned.\n\nNow, for my question. This ally that hides behind your eyes, does he seek to protect the world by going against his own kind?

Yeah, my brother Fennorian mentioned something about that. I should have thought of them earlier, but they're pretty secretive and reclusive. We're lucky one left their post to consult with the scholars.\n\nGo find them and then meet me back here.

Well, most scholars agree that the fanciful legend about the Gray Host's defeat is … pardon my Orcish … guar dung.\n\nYou know, the Pyre Watch are sort of Gray Host experts. Find her and I'm sure she can provide the answers you seek.

Revere may be too strong a word. Our relationship with the spirits relies on negotiation. On giving and receiving what is expected.\n\nWe look to the great spirit Nocturnal for guidance, but our wards honor Hircine, Molag Bal, and Namira as well.

The spirits we revere follow their own whims. We have an understanding, however. As long as we make our offerings in good faith, the spirits provide their blessings.\n\nWith the wards restored, prey becomes bountiful and our village remains secure.
That is truly fortunate. As for me, I escaped the Imperials only to find myself surrounded by ancient undead. \n\nLet us speak outside. I will follow your lead. May Onsi guide your blade.

I can delve into the records of my order when I return to our sanctum. But understand that the Watch is concerned with keeping the past buried, not exposing it.\n\nI can tell you that there are indications that one of the Host survived the slaughter.

You see the world with different eyes, outsider. Magic is a word used by cowards who fear its power or fools who think they can control it. We are connected to the land. Nothing more, nothing less.\n\nThe restoration process is a ritual, though, yes.

I have heard the spirits called by that name. It doesn't change who they are or our relationship to them.\n\nThe spirits cannot be judged by mortal standards. All we can do is bargain with them, appease them, and use whatever blessings they provide.

And I don't have to resist the urge to rip out your throat and gorge on your blood.\n\nBut we are civilized beings. Exchanging pleasantries in this humble setting. Perhaps we can come to some sort of arrangement. A tip for a tap, as it were.

As you wish. Know that this level of cordiality will not be repeated.\n\nAnd this is not a threat. If you continue to meddle in my affairs, I will take far more than your life. On that, you have my word.

We bargain with them, outsider. We maintain the balance between the land and the spirit world, make our offerings, and then trust the spirits to answer in kind.\n\nOnce you make the offerings, return here and I will complete the ritual of restoration.

That's Eamon, the first among our hunters. He's as fearsome as a Giant and just as thick-headed.\n\nHe's been up in arms since the storm. Seeing me bring you into the village hasn't calmed his disposition one bit.

I don't think so. For all his bravery and bluster, he hasn't volunteered to help me. But he won't try to stop us, either.\n\nLike most of my people, trust doesn't come easily to Eamon. And with good reason. Most outsiders we meet do try to kill us.

You speak of peace on the one hand, but you take their blood just like the rest of us, Verandis.\n\nWhere did you think all those endless debates among the Gray Council would lead? We were never going to change our natures. And why should we?

As the shade implied, they each seek the Dark Heart for a different reason. I can only imagine what Rada would do with such power. As for Belain, he called her the vessel that never fills. A curious description.\n\nRegardless, we must find them.

Not in and of itself. He wants me to follow in his footsteps. To see what he did and learn the truth of what he promises. In doing so, however, I will discover how to stop it.\n\nHe's baring his throat to me, confident I will not bite. But I must.

You were a fool when first we met and nothing has changed. After all these centuries, you remain as ignorant and naive as ever.\n\nMy Gray Host is the only way for our people to create a safe and harmonious home. And deep down, you know it, too.
Ah, no. If you were my target, I probably wouldn't just come out and explain myself like that. Or maybe I would? I've done stranger things.\n\nAnyway, you're safe. From me, at least.

Well, if I can believe what Talfyg says, several people came to examine the prisoners while they held him. Reachmen, other vampires, a madman—it sounded like they put the captives on display.\n\nI worry this may be part of something larger.

Before we reclaimed Karthwasten for our clan, outsiders built deep tunnels to exploit the land. The Crow-Eye have no interest in such things, so we left them abandoned. \n\nMy people mostly avoid the place, truth be told.

Have you lost your senses? How could you miss those storms? And the screams in the air?\n\nBands of the beasts sweeping across the Reach from here to the northern shores! Vampires and werewolves joined forces—calling themselves the Gray Host.
A deal safer than dragging our toes out here, aye. The Ard put the word out for anyone with legs to make for the safety of the walls. Caddach's many things, but a fool ain't one of them.

I cannot say, stranger. We scattered to the winds when that Gray Host first appeared in the Reach—the bastards could track us when we traveled in large groups.\n\nWe all hoped to join up at Markarth. But they were rabbits headed for the snare.
Well, then, we can't waste time out here! As soon as mother's rested and my brother's pulled that stick from his arse, we head for Markarth. The rest of our clan waits for us!

My brother—the weak lout—and my mother. She shuffles at half a snail's speed and yet could still beat Drisoal in a foot race.\n\nYou might understand why I hurry to get to Markarth, everything else aside.
I may not have a straight back any more, but I can walk a road as good as anyone. And I can gut a rascal like a lass of a few seasons, if you take my meaning.
Look, talk to Fynvagh, will you? My stomach's sore enough. Don't need some dunce yammering my ear off to make it worse.
Indeed? And the Gray Host dealt with too, I've heard. \n\nAnd tell me, why should I take the word of an outsider?
Ha! Oh, really now? Well, I had no idea.\n\nThanks for the laugh, stranger. It's been a time since I felt one in my belly.
Well, I have a few recitals prepared. A tale of gods and sorrow, or one of battle—maybe a bit of history, perhaps? The Reach holds tales not like any from the outlands.
Very well, we seal the bargain. What manner of tale do you wish to hear?
Well, you hold a clever tongue. But outsiders are a shifty lot, aren't they?\n\nI can't fault your logic. Fine. But don't tell any clans you come across that a vateshran provided you a tale for free.
Well … perhaps I can overlook my usual fee this time. Though a man of my age shouldn't work for good word of mouth.\n\nNow—what do you want to hear about?

So the legends say. A treasure trove of the pure metal. Enough to arm my warriors with weapons to slay every vampire and werewolf that marches with the Gray Host.\n\nAnd your keystone, too, with any luck.

No, but Reachfolk don't make a habit of poking around in the deep places of the world. The hills are dangerous enough.\n\nStill, Bthar-Zel's legend tells of silver and other wondrous treasures. Wouldn't surprise me to find your keystone there.

Because I have it on good authority that Bthar-Zel contains one of the only know Dwarven vaults that hasn't been ransacked! Not with all the mechanicals that still guard the place.\n\nThey're the reason I never made it inside.
Funny you should mention that. Oh, he went out into the foothills, all right. But before Verandis could find them, the rebels found him.\n\nSeems to be working out. At least for the moment.

Aren't you a clever one. Name's Gwendis. Just one of the lost puppies Verandis brought in out of the rain. Adusa-daro and Fennorian are skulking around here somewhere.\n\nI'm just the best at finding people in weird Dwarven cities, I guess.

What's to tell? It's a Reachfolk camp in the foothills. Probably the main base for the rebels, but I'm just guessing.\n\nI was with Verandis when the rebels surrounded us. I wanted to fight, but the count held me back. That's when Arana appeared.

Whenever different clans come together in a common purpose, we seek the blessings of the spirits to confirm we're doing the right thing.\n\nWe will ask the Hunter to bind our hearts. If he sees strength in you, we will clasp arms and band together.
You want to know about Old Elk-Eye? The Wolf-Charmer? The Lord of the Hunt?\n\nYou probably know him as Hircine.
Many, but not all. We have enclaves throughout these hills. But these aren't my warriors, harrier.

The Snake in the Stars is the Corrupter, the Enemy. If permitted, it would consume the Lesser Stars without hesitation.\n\nLuckily, the Guardians—the Headsman, the Witch, and the Hunter—stand strong and defend the Lesser Stars.

The Witch shines her light on covens that protect the Reach from outsiders and others who mean to do Reachfolk harm.\n\nHer good eye sees through everything—rock, water, and flesh—to find the hard truths. And when she speaks, she never lies.

The Hunter is the wiliest of the sky tales. Clever as an old fox and swift as a young one.\n\nShe watches the Snake in the Stars, finding it no matter where it slithers. She teaches us to keep our feet quiet and our kills as silent as the night.

Lady Belain has had more time to research the Arkthzand Keystone than we did. She may have already known about this location and the hidden door. Or she may know a different way to get inside.\n\nThen again, she may be looking somewhere else entirely.

I certainly hope not. Between the Dwarven scrap dealer and Arana's ritual, everything seems to point to this location.\n\nI only mean that Lady Belain may be operating off of a totally different set of suppositions.

Dwarven keystones not only provide access to forbidden or otherwise sealed areas, they also tend to radiate ancient magic. The uses for such a relic are potentially limitless.\n\nI won't be able to determine more until I see the keystone itself.

It's hard to explain. Most witchcraft is.\n\nImagine a boulder. Heavy, solid, huge. Now imagine some grinning bastard lowering it onto your chest. Slowly at first, but it starts to crush you. Little by little, it becomes harder to breathe.

Aye. It feels like a wet rag sliding down my throat, choking the life out of me. I'll manage. But you need to stay wary. All of you.\n\nWhatever it is, it's like a black pit at the center of a sour fruit. And I don't think it belongs in this world.
Right. Right! Melina Cassel at your service. I belong to House Ravenwatch — a junior member.
Hah. I tried telling myself that, but it helps to hear someone else say it. I'll do my duty, but won't lose sight of why I joined the Ravenwatch.\n\nI'm glad I bumped into you. You give good advice.
Ugh, I'm sorry for just throwing that at you. You should know better than to bother random people, Melina ….\n\nI can leave you alone. Thanks for listening.

Having a bit of a crisis. \n\nI could use advice. I joined the Ravenwatch to make a difference for vampires and mortals. But all I do is deliver messages, supplies. I may be younger than the others, but … should I ask to get more important tasks?

Not particularly. Those vampires and werewolves calling themselves the Gray Host … well, they aren't the same as the Gray Host from history. If you just think like a vampire, you know how to avoid their attention.

The Ravenwatch wants to form contacts with a vampire coven just over the border, in Falkreath. They've heard our overtures before, but with the Gray Host on the march, we hope that they'll be inclined to accept this time around.

Gods, with all that House Ravenwatch has endured lately, it could be next sunrise or it could be half a season from now. I hope it's closer to the latter, so I have some time to practice.\n\nAh! I'm shaking with excitement! Or nerves. Both, probably..

I need to craft a message to send to some contacts the Ravenwatch has in Alik'r. It should catalogue information about persons of interest in the Gray Host. Which should be right up my alley!\n\nSpeaking of which, I better get to work on that ….

Apparently the rest of the Ravenwatch noticed my attitude changed as well. Now I nearly have more missions than I know what to do with. Reconnaissance, reports, diplomatic work …. \n\nIn fact, I should get back to it. Farewell, friend.
Because—well, because I don't wish to be the kind of person who pours their heart out to a passerby. Just because I'm not happy with some assignment. People out here have real problems.

Well, I may as well tell you. Your past advice helped me immensely. I feel as though I can trust you.\n\nThere's … someone in the Ravenwatch. The more I try to get close to them, the less it seems to work.
Well … let's keep this between us, all right? \n \nI may have … botched a mission. My first real mission. Pretty, um, badly. And I don't know what to do about it.

Just … thanks. \n\nIt's funny, I practiced this whole big speech about how your advice got me through some tough times. How I feel like a better person because I met you … but you know what? Thanks is simpler.
Ugh. Of course when I try to apologize for babbling at you, I end up babbling at you. I'll leave you alone, now.
The Gray Host attacking people both in the Reach and Western Skyrim, for a start. Ravenwatch agents who put their lives at risk—Fennorian, Gwendis, Adusa-daro. And here I stand, gazing at my navel.

Really? I wonder sometimes. Half of my days I feel like everyone is glaring daggers at everything I do. The rest of the time, I wonder if they know I exist.\n\nI should take a step back. Clear my head, so others can count on me.

Before we met, I was an insecure wreck. Or it felt like I was. \n\nBut I don't think myself into a downward spiral as much anymore. I feel more confident. Like the person I wanted to be when I first joined the Ravenwatch.
I feared you might say that. But it's my problem to deal with. I can have to sort it out … somehow. Thanks anyway.

I was meant to stop the Gray Host from recruiting a clan of vampires. I tried to convince them that they'd just be used as pawns. But … they all ignored me. My mission failed. \n\nHow can I explain this to the rest of House Ravenwatch?

I hope you're right. I remember Gwendis, Adusa-daro and the others turning up at Castle Ravenwatch after something went wrong. And they still get sent on important tasks.\n\nI just have to feel confident that I did everything I could, and move on.
Ah. Did I overstep? I overstepped, didn't I. Classic Melina …. I will leave you be.

Oh, I'd rather not say, if you don't mind. I tend to bring them up too much in conversation as it is. And while I like to think we share a bond—we're both younger members of the Ravenwatch—nothing ever comes of it.

No, not exactly. But maybe I should. Before you started giving me advice, I would have just mooned over Fe … that other member of the Ravenwatch from afar. \n\nIt's decided. The next time I see them, I'll tell them straight out how I feel.

No one has entered or departed by these doors in all the time I've been here. It's clear that Rada and Belain know more about this old Dwarven structure than we do, though.\n\nThey must have another way to come and go as they need.

Lord Verandis Ravenwatch formed a group of vampires who seek a peaceful coexistence between our kind and mortals. We try to stop any of our kind that upset that balance.\n\nOh I guess I just blurted out that I'm a vampire. I'm good, though, I swear.

I … don't know. Do I leave the Ravenwatch? No, that wouldn't do. I can't give up on my dream of making a difference. \n\nIt's just too hard—seeing such a big gap between what you want to do, and your actual day-to-day.
Huh? Oh. It's just an expression.
Well …. Candlelight, flowers, a place that doesn't crawl with danger at every turn. \n\nNot many bards tell romance stories about vampires, but we can still feel love, you know.

For centuries, the Spiritblood clan has tested our young with the Vateshran's Rites. Once a child possesses the strength required, they enter into the Hollows. Those who emerge become full members of the clan.

I told them the truth—the leaders of the Gray Host only want them as fodder. The only vampires the Gray Host cares about are its legions from the first era. They see everyone else as just a means to an end.\n\nBut my words must have rung hollow.

We three sisters who maintain Vateshran Hollows serve as one. It could not remove a sister without wreaking havoc on the balance within. The river needs the rain, which in turn needs the sun. So it is with us.

After observing Vateshran Hollows for as long as we have, we understand its rhythms and moods. The veil between us and Oblivion is thin, but stable.\n\nExcept for in recent days. Something shifts within the Reach. We cannot yet guess at the cause.

Though lesser known, to some the observances of Old Life are just as important as the New Life Festival. They complement each other, as if two sides of the same coin.\n\nTo pass into a new year, you must acknowledge the old.

You show bravery, wanderer. Namira offers no pity in her whims. What secrets show through this fetid offal are not merely tales.\n\nThe entrails tell us about many things the future holds — prosperity, conflicts, romance. What knowledge do you seek?

Yes, we know of these. Voidstuff enters our sacred Hollows. Spreading faster than we can heal the wounds. The Binder in the Dark attempts to control it, but a presence interferes.\n\nHurry, complete the Rites so we may focus on this threat.

Oh my. I fear something has gone horribly wrong. It's just as I feared. This plant radiates tonal energy. \n\nMaster Pythis and I brought a relic with us that emits the same kind of power to study it. I think I damaged it.
Fear not, outsider. Vateshran's Rites must continue. Challenges surround us, come at us from every direction. We must constantly test our warriors to keep them strong.
The Voidmother consumed his spirit. Our first vateshran is unmade. \n\nAlthough he created these Rites, we sisters shall keep it alive. And the Spiritblood clan will sing his song for eternity.

We need to slow the process. I sense other pockets of tonal disturbance nearby. I'll cast a spell at each location to keep the effects from spreading. If we follow them to the source, we should find the relic and Master Pythis. He may be in danger!

Well … Master Pythis had me use a transportation spell to get it here. When we arrived, he noted the relic had sustained a bit of damage from my rather poor attempt.\n\nThat magic is wildly unstable. It's possible I caused some kind of rupture.

Yes. Acknowledging those that have passed on is an important part of moving forward. We need never forget those we've lost, but this tradition allows us to say things we might have held back while they were alive. The shrines are a vessel for that.

Over my years of travel, I've seen them along old Imperial pilgrimage routes every so often. Though, I don't know the exact number.\n\nSome are quite old. They may not be friendly places anymore, so be cautious if you seek them out.

We watch the Totems of the Brave. Those who fell defending the ways of the Spiritblood clan. Warriors who transcend mere dust, becoming songs that echo through time.\n\nPerhaps your people will remember you the same?

Oblivion pushes, presses, leaks out into these caverns. We reach through the cracks and bring forth monsters. Invite them into our world for our clan to battle. And if too many emerge, we banish them back.\n\nKeeping the balance is my task.

Oh, right. Most challengers recognize me immediately.\n\nBefore you stands clan Spiritblood's first ever vateshran. Or at least a shimmering blue version of him. I created these Rites to test our warriors, all those years ago.

A simple task, but I respect your desire to learn more before deciding. You gain power through foreknowledge as much as by sharpening your blade.\n\nChoose a portal. Once you enter, the others will close until you clear the wing of creatures.

Not all gods speak in ways that mortal ears can hear. Some of the Reach learn the language of mistress Namira — written in rot and decay, bile and bone.\n\nSee here, these beetles chewing through this old goat's meat? They relay Namira's word to me.
Resting my haunches and enjoying myself, stranger. What of it?

Hm. Haven't given it much thought. At first I thought I'd stay out here until I died of thirst, or starved to death, or maybe let a sabre cat maul me to pieces. Definitely won't leave before one of those happens.
Glad I could educate you.
What, you expect me to curl up in a tent or house, like those thinbloods in Markarth? Give me the wilds any day. I only need the open sky over my head to feel calm.

No. But my opinion of you has. You helped the Crow-Eye, which makes you an exception.\n\nWe can't afford to blindly trust those not of the Reach. We spend our lives fighting for what's ours, clawing for survival. Outsiders don't understand that.
Ha! Maybe you're right. \n\nI'll let Fialyn be the judge of that. Apparently, she can weed out the good ones. Me? I'll keep my guard up.

You misunderstand. There is no rebuilding to be done. The structures here are echoes left over from those who did not belong. We won't knock them down, but we have no need to add to them.\n\nKarthwasten provides for its children. We need nothing else.

You have it backwards. The Reach understands that hardship comes for us as surely as dung falls from a well-fed mammoth. Instead of moaning our sorrows, we embrace the pain as wisdom.\n\nThis is why many of my kin revere Molag Bal.
We will fight. We have the protection of the wards once more, and the strength of knowing we conquered a grand test here today. If we need to defend Karthwasten again, we will gladly do so.

Worship? We revere the great spirit of the hunt. Hircine's wisdom should be obvious, even to an outsider. Life feeds on life, but not everything wants to be eaten! Survival requires blood and steel.\n\nPlus, there's nothing more exciting than the hunt!

As a child, I once hunted a stag large enough to feed my entire family. I tracked it for days without sleep. Just before delirium set in, I saw it. I nocked my arrow and drew back. All my focus was on that stag, when I felt a searing pain in my leg.

A bear had latched its jaws onto my thigh. We wrestled for hours, tooth and claw against my knives. The sun dipped as our battle continued, neither of us willing to back down.\n\nEventually out of exhaustion, we stopped. The bear knew it was beaten.

With the harsh conditions Reachfolk live under, we always strive to improve. You can never say people of the Reach died for lack of ambition.\n\nThat drive eventually leads some to turn to the Lord of Ambition himself.

The Rites challenge many things—strength, agility, tenacity. But also common sense. If you don't realize getting near the boiling lava might spell disaster, well, perhaps you don't belong in the Reach.

A betrothal announcement, in a sense. It is how we let the folk of the Reach know that a wedding nears. That two clans will be brought together.\n\nAs is custom, Eslyn and Madearn are isolated in the handfasting cave nearby, getting acquainted.

All clans? No. But a number of the smaller clans recognize my experience and authority. They pledge fealty and rely on me to help them settle differences when they arise.\n\nAnd should an emergency present itself, they would turn to me to lead them.

Would you take the messages of some Imperial City refugees with you? I've amassed quite a few, hoping I'd cross paths with an Old Life shrine at some point. \n\nAll you have to do is put them in the flame when you perform the ceremony.

Even an outsider must know that there is strength in numbers. But clan chiefs have a hard time cooperating. In extreme circumstances, they temporarily cede their authority to a chief-of-chiefs.\n\nWith this marriage, I hope to end an ancient feud.

You picked up on that, did you? All you need to know at the moment is that the Eagleseer and Six-Ford clans have been at odds for generations. I hope to dampen those tensions by joining the clans in marriage.

Because I'm the Ard of Markarth and she refuses to heed my commands!\n\nLook, every Reach warrior who dies fighting Arana's private war against the Gray Host makes all of us weaker. We need our strength, now more than ever.

Markarth's the safest place right now. No matter how well Arana and her rebels know the hills, the vampires and the werewolves sniff them out. \n\nIf she keeps getting my best fighters killed, I swear I'll hang her from the city walls by her own guts.

We made a deal. We gather in the city and leave them free to find whatever bit of Dwarven nonsense brought them to the Reach in the first place.\n\nOf course, Lady Belain brokered that peace, so now I suppose our bargain is suspect.

What's to be happy about? I'll abide by the chief-of-chiefs' counsel, but I can't imagine a blood bond between us and the Six-Ford clan.\n\nI just hope the lad's worthy of Eslyn. If not, he won't last much past the ceremony, if I know my daughter!

Eslyn's my one and only. She's got four older brothers, but she's the fiercest child I've ever whelped. Eagleseer blood runs strong through her veins, thank Bal.\n\nMadearn needs to mind her edges. Not that the Six-Fords give much mind to anything.
Eh, that has nothing to do with you, outsider. Do as the chief-of-chiefs bids so we can get on with this.

The city walls are still our strongest play, rover. Like headstones, they mark the thousands of enemies who died trying to breach Markarth's defenses.\n\nWe'll bide our time and wait for the Gray Host to show their true intentions. Then I'll act.

That's a title given to me by outsiders. I use it to frighten the neighbors and keep away the riffraff.\n\nI'm the Ard of Markarth. Leovic, the last Longhouse Emperor, was my cousin. I inherited the throne by blood. Had to keep it by blood, too.

Chief Eagleseer is my brother. I love him and his daughter dearly, but this feud has been going on since longer than anyone can remember. Not even the vateshrans know how it started.\n\nThis attempt at a reconciliation will go exactly as the others.

When all the drama has come to an end, the Eagleseers and the Six-Fords are still going to hate each other. Nothing will change that.\n\nAs for my niece, she won't do anything she doesn't want to. I'd feel sorry for Madearn—if he wasn't a Six-Ford.
This isn't the time or place for such talk, outsider. Not with the chief-of-chiefs looking on.

Why should I be? Not only am I forced to endure the presence of the Eagleseers, I must allow my son Madearn to marry one of them!\n\nThe chief-of-chiefs asks much of us, but I will not let my son go unattended.

You ask more questions than my third wife!\n\nLeovic's clan—my clan—squabbled over the scraps after Varen murdered my cousin. Pretty soon, they came to take my city. So I bound their ankles and tossed them all to the rocks. Head first.
No. That story's far worse.\n\nAnd no, I won't be telling it this day.

All that were left, aye. And the word is executed, not murdered.\n\nAn ard offers food, freedom, and protection with his right hand. With his left, he promises cruelty and punishment. Those that covet the right get the left. Simple as that.
That … is none of your business, outsider.\n\nI am here and doing as my chief-of-chiefs demands. Let us leave it at that.
Yes. No. Give Madearn and the Eagleseer woman your blessing, outsider. Just as the chief-of-chiefs instructed.\n\nEach of us have a part to play in this fiasco, including me.

Opposed? Look, Madearn and I … grew up together. I want what's best for him. And now they're binding him to some Eagleseer hellion, and I ….\n\nI've said too much. Go. Give your blessing. Let's be done with this.

Well, that is the other kind. You might be able to find one in Bthar-Zel. I could sell you a map to the place, but it won't be cheap.\n\nOr, if you do a simple job for me, I'll give you the map as payment. Quick work that would help me a great deal.
No, no! Don't say anything more. That message, and any response, that is for you alone. \n\nTreasure it, and keep it in your heart. That is where it will do the most good.

Incredibly so! Those lucky few who receive a response from Aetherius often keep it a secret. They do describe it as a life-changing experience, though.\n\nI choose to believe those who receive responses were in need of a sign, for whatever reason.
I can't read those infernal scratchings! Only Chief Eagleseer and his daughter bother with such things.\n\nWhat does the note say, outsider?

You see the animosity between these clans. They have fought and spilled each other's blood for generations. I finally got them to agree to a compromise. A bond of peace predicated on the marriage of Eslyn and Madearn.\n\nPlease, you must find them.
No, this is unacceptable. This handfasting must take place. I need you to find them and bring them back, outsider.

Remind Eslyn and Madearn what's at stake here. They both understand what this feud has cost both clans. What peace would mean for us all. \n\nThey are young. Their blood will cool and they will see that coming home is the only wise action.
Well, her and Verandis did most of the talking. I'm not sure I trust the witch, but I trust Verandis.\n\nHe says she's a friend, and that's good enough for me.

Hang on, let me think ….\n\nThe camp's set up inside an old Nord ruin. It's surprisingly sturdy for something that was abandoned a long time ago. The rebels seemed to be running low on supplies. Food, weapons, armor ….

Well enough, I suppose. Thanks for asking.\n\nAdusa drags her tail a bit every now and then. Still fighting off the worst of Essenia's experiments, I think. But so far, no turning into a Bloodknight. So, you know, success.
I don't like breaking my word to the chief-of-chiefs, but I can't go through with the handfasting. I can't marry Eslyn.

Even before all this, I had heard of Chief Eagleseer's daughter. Fair as a rose and just as thorny. \n\nBut … we did get to know each other in the cave. At least a little. She's smart. Passionate. Fiery. I can respect that.

I … I'm already pledged to another. Drisene of the Six-Ford clan. Before her brother died, I promised I would marry her and look after her.\n\nHow can I break one obligation to honor another? Even for the sake of our clans?

No. We did our handfasting in secret. Drisene is a good woman. There's little love between us, but I gave her brother my word before he died. And Eslyn clearly doesn't want to marry me.\n\nI want to end this feud, but there has to be another way.

His name is Barth. A living legend, from what the elders say. \n\nI only got a glimpse of him when he visited our clan before my father and the clan elders sent me away. He was interested in hearing more of our stories, I think.
Aye, I'm sure she does. But I'm not going back, not while the chief-of-chiefs and my father plan to marry me off like some Imperial princess.

Look, I don't even know if I want to marry at all. And my father and the chief-of-chiefs parade me around the Reach, saying I'm to be wed to a sod I've never laid eyes on before.\n\nMadearn has his own reasons to shirk the handfasting. So we both ran.

It's not fair of them to put that responsibility on our shoulders! It's a worthy idea, but why do we have to be the ones to carry it out? \n\nI won't be forced into a marriage because our people can't stop killing each other.

Didn't the chief-of-chiefs tell you? I'm the daughter of Chief Eagleseer. Or I was. I have half a mind to exile myself and cut all ties to my damned clan.\n\nI tell you, I won't be the barter that ends the feud. I won't!

I didn't meet him when he came to see the Eagleseers. But he's a legend, I know that. The elders were talking day and night about how the great Barth was coming to visit to learn our stories. They couldn't think of a higher honor.

Three marks … three places to search.\n\nAll right. I'll help you and Verandis, but not before the spirits bless our alliance. I want you to undertake a ritual. If the spirits favor you, we'll face the Gray Host together.

He what? Let me see that. Oh. Master Pythis, how could you? \n\nI can't believe I fell for such deception! He must think I'm a fool. And I am! But not so much a fool that I can't stop what he's put in motion. Friend, will you help me stop him?

I sense a stronger source of tonal magic nearby. It has to be the relic!\n\nIf my theory is correct, Master Pythis used those Dwemer amplifiers to harness its power. But I can use them to transport the relic back to Artaeum. We just have to hurry!

We don't have much time before my spells wear off. And I can't be sure Pythis won't find a way to intercept my plea for help. It's up to us now.\n\nIf this cave grows any more unstable, the relic may become impossible to contain.

I don't like surprises, especially when they come in the form of remnants of the Deep Folk. We've enough problems without needing to worry about a strange new metal beast roaming around. \n\nEasier to just be done with them.

We have no use for Dwarf mischief. You can't trust anything those dobbers created. We get by with our own means, and our own way of life just fine.\n\nBetter to destroy it before it gets loose and hurts someone. The Stonehands want to avoid that.
We've seen them prowling the countryside, but down here in the mine? No. They must have come from deeper underground. \n\nHowever they got down here, we have to put a stop to this.

I don't need to visit Solitude to know it's full of stinking Nords, do I?\n\nI hired an adventurer like you once. She returned with some scrap, but she couldn't get to the vault without the machines tearing her apart. Maybe your luck will be better.

Arana promised to stop Lady Belain, no matter what. Trust a Reach witch to make her own words come true.\n\nAt least it was a good death, given in a noble cause. And Markarth still stands. We'll remember what Arana did. And we'll remember you, as well.

They scattered and fled! Eh, good riddance.\n\nBetween Arana's wilders and my Stonehands, we held them back. And when you cut off the head, they were done with this fight. There's some clean up to be done in the wilderness, but nothing we can't handle.

Oh, they say the villa holds all sorts of treasures. When nasty old Durcorach marched to Cyrodiil, he snatched up prizes from every city in his path. Paintings, jewelry, other fancy whatsits. You know how tyrants enjoy their baubles.

Was the oddest thing. There I am, on my way to explore the ruins in Stormhold, when a courier rides up and hands me a letter.\n\nNow, I had many questions: How did she find me? Who knows I'm here? Is this a trap? But no, it was just a simple note.

He sure did! After Durcorach took power, he ordered this estate built. A lot of the loot he grabbed ended up in here.\n\nCan you imagine what treasures we'll find inside? And the library! As soon as I heard about it I knew this job was for me.
That is a rare and ancient tale. One not often spoken of, let alone shared with those from beyond the clans.\n\nTell me, outsider. Why does this story matter to you?

Tisfira has told all who will listen about the handsome Redguard and the blond giant who walks at his side. About what they did for her clan.\n\nVery well. What specifically about the tale interests you and your friends?

Ah, yes. Red Eagle was a great warrior as well as a great teacher.\n\nAll I can tell you is that an ancient cave sits below this sacred redoubt. If this particular song is meant for you and your friends, you will find the answers you seek there.
Good question. The contact stayed vague on that point. But I'd guess we're about to meet them.\n\nI hope you don't mind if this exploration mission turns into a fight?

They built an empire by feeding off that Heart. Odds are good that one of the creepy vampires wrote about it before the well dried up and their power withered away.\n\nWe'll find these secrets—and maybe a way to help Verandis, too.
Yes, of course. Rada didn't reveal everything in his letter, but if there's something I can answer for you, I will.

That one is as much a mystery to me as it is to you. But Rada provided a clue. He said it was a place in the Reach. Who better to ask about locations in this part of the world than Ard Caddach?\n\nMeet Lyris in Markarth and seek the ard's counsel.

I can only speculate, but we know the Nighthollow clan had an intimate connection to the Void through the Dark Heart. It makes sense they studied it over the many years that it sustained them.\n\nI noticed an archive in their keep when we were there.

We know Rada needed a keystone to enter this chamber and calibrate the orrery to the Dark Heart. Go to Bthar-Zel. Fennorian will help you discover whatever secret awaits there concerning the Dwarven keystones.

Undaunted plunder! I'll tell you true, scamp. We've gotten our share of lazy or incompetent recruits lately. I mean, who falls to the Goblins in Fungal Grotto? Pssh.\n\nConsider this an incentive for better blood to show them how it's done.

The alliance leaders sponsor us to clean out the corners of their realms, so we're flush with plunder. We're using it as incentive for those who can complete contracts, conquer crypts, uh… something something with the letter c.\n\nYou in?

Well, you know what to do, right? Honestly, giving the same speech to every gutter troll who wants extra gold for sujamma gets tiresome after awhile. If I can spare you the sales pitch, more breath saved for me.

That's what I was hoping to learn, but the letters fail to provide any detail.\n\nI, too, have never been able to manifest my Shehai. I was hoping to gain insight from these letters. It seems we'll have to look elsewhere, though.

I must seek a place in the Reach where the land was sundered from Tamriel. Then I must study the Void through Nighthollow eyes. Finally, I must learn about keystones in Bthar-Zel.\n\nIn my current state, I don't trust myself. Will you go in my stead?

I appreciate that the Reachfolk noticed. You'd be surprised how often what we do is taken for granted.\n\nIf you can find that cave, Sai and I will follow shortly. I want to check something I learned in Hroldan Ring with the vateshran.

I think the song tells us that Red Eagle had to clear his mind before he could embrace his destiny. That he had to fill his heart with the thing he loved the most.\n\nFor Red Eagle, that was his people. For Rada al-Saran? Probably his Gray Host.
Need a map for that too, do you? \n\nLike I said, the ritual begins with the preparation. We need three things—a briarheart seed, some bright river-shale, and a Hagraven's eye.
They grow in the hills to the south. Just remember your gloves. The briars' thorns are sharper than Dagon's razor.

In a Hagraven's head, of course! Or from a jar. They remove their own eyes to use in rituals, too. There's a coven to the east of here. Nothing but a flock of toad-licking root-hoarders, stealing all the best herbs.\n\nNamira take the lot of them!
Check north and west, along the river bank.\n\nSpirits prowl the area, so proceed with caution. Faeries and spriggans and such. I'd put them to sleep for you, but that would be cheating.
Did you, now? I thought I smelled the wolf on you. Good. Hope you learned a thing or two. We'll need his cunning before long.
Good! Nice to see you thinbloods aren't all hare-bladder cowards after all!

Well, I don't know you all that well, but when it comes to the knack for calling spirits, I think I've got you beat. And I've still got all my fingers and toes, see?\n\nTrust me. Or don't. But either way, do as I ask and gather the ritual components.

We can call on your gods, too, if you prefer. Care to wager who answers first?\n\nWe'll hear from one of Hircine's pups, at least. Or get a hint from a fox spirit or a bloody stag. You're not refusing the ritual, are you?
For now, aye. But these warriors take no oaths, swear no fealty. They serve their clan, the Reach, and the courage painted on their hearts. No one and nothing else.
No. No, they're not.\n\nLet's talk about something else, all right?

They'll wander back into the hills to fight their own battles—old and new.\n\nThese troubles with the Gray Host have torn clans to pieces. Set sons against fathers, chiefs against wise women. It will take seasons to stitch the Reach back together.

People talk. You hear things. The Lothid are a gang of vampire criminals led by Boss Trenlor. They terrorize the locals. Charge protection. Demand blood tribute. That sort of thing.\n\nThey use the old ruin as a lair. Exactly where Adusa wants to go.
Listen … I sensed something else down below … a second keystone. Find it and you'll be able to … enter the orrery chamber.

The Old Life tradition is kept among many faiths. The cultural setting may vary from place to place, but the setup is generally the same. \n\nLet me mark this one on your map. Should be right around around … here.

I'll study the Heart and the orrery. Try to learn enough so that we can make use of whatever you discover when the time comes.\n\nI will also examine my own condition. I must ascertain that I can control this darkness and not be controlled by it.
Yes. See what secrets they gathered at the height of their power.\n\nI only hope that the archive has weathered the centuries better than the Nighthollow clan themselves.
I'll answer them as best I can, but every moment we delay puts us another pace behind Rada.

No … but we didn't find it after you killed Lady Belain. We know she didn't completely trust Rada al-Saran, so where else could she be leaving it for safekeeping.\n\nIf it's not here, I don't know where else it would be.

Medone? Clever girl! I knew she'd find a way to escape.\n\nWe need to make sure the Thornroot clan Hagravens don't cut the hearts out of anyone else. Can you burn their briarheart tree? That will put a stop to this for good.
