What's to tell? I don't really know her. She's connected to some Rivenspire noble house. Ravenwatch, I think. She put out a call for mercenaries and offered a dung-ton of gold.\n\nIf it involved anything other than the Lothid clan, I'd be all in.

Another vampire. A friend. Or so I thought. She seduced Kathad and led him away.\n\nI hadn't seen either of them until I ran into Kathad here in the Reach. We talked. He agreed to leave Lothid and join me. And then, suddenly, he came back here.

A noble house of Rivenspire, to which I belong. As you can plainly see, this one is also a vampire.\n\nIt is the sacred mission of the Ravenwatch to help vampires fight their worst urges and stop them from harming mortals.

Head to the highest part of Briar Rock. And watch yourself—the Hagraven matron personally tends the tree. She may try to stop you.\n\nI'll go find Medone and get what's left of my clan out of this damned place. Good luck, outsider.

When we confront Rada al-Saran, it must be the last time. When the moment comes to end this, there can be no doubt. No hesitation. My father has to be prepared to see this through.\n\nThat's a discussion for later. We should leave this place.
Well. That's an oddly specific request. Most people prefer the tale of Red Eagle's final hours.\n\nWhy does an outsider care about a feud between two minor clans of the Reach?

Freyleth made a reappearance when I was first trying to recruit Kathad. She befriended him. Lured him away. This one did not realize she was still a part of Kathad's life until Boss Trenlor mentioned her.\n\nShe may be what drew Kathad back here.

Ah. So this is about the handfasting at Hroldan Ring. Eslyn of the Eagleseer and Madearn of the Six-Ford, if I'm not mistaken.\n\nYou saved my hide, so a story's the least I can give you. But, not here. Let's do it back at my camp.
I'm a vateshran, outsider. Knowing what happens in the Reach as well as the practices of its people is my duty. It's me and my kind that bring tales and tidings to the clans of these hills.

It's an old hatred. I pieced the tale together during my time with the elders of both clans. \n\nBefore there was the Eagleseers or the Six-Fords, there was a man and a woman. They loved one another and were promised to wed.

The man's bloodline became the Eagleseers. The woman's, the Six-Fords. The love they once shared festered into hate. Battles were fought. Each clan rallied around a fragment of the Lover's Coil. Proof, they said, that the spirits ordained their feud.

They fashioned the Lover's Coil, a totem of stone symbolizing the spirals of their lives entwining. Of their love.\n\nBut the day they were to wed, the Coil broke. They believed it a sign of the displeasure of the spirits. So the pair separated.

Boss Trenlor turned a powerful and respected clan into common criminals. He's abusive, egotistical, and cruel. He's also quite insane. Life in the clan has become intolerable, but I had to return. I had to help the clan.\n\nI hope Adusa understands.

You're speaking to a vateshran of the Reach, not one of those dapple-trousered bards you find in outsider cities. The history of the Reach, its people, its relics … I know them all. Because if I didn't, they'd be lost.

Of course not. The only way I could be is if I buried them there myself. And I promise you, I'm not that old.\n\nAll I can tell you is the last time those fragments were mentioned in the old tales, they were at those battlefields.

It was one of a few pitched battles between the Six-Fords and Eagleseers in ages past. There was no clear victor. Both sides slaughtered almost to the last man. And woman.\n\nIt took place in the lea of the Karthspire.

Hmm. The tales I got out of the elders say the Eagleseer leader bound himself to a pillar so he could die fighting. \n\nHe's the one who would have carried the Coil fragment into battle. If that pillar still stands, the fragment ought to be close by.

No. I mean, yes. Of course I do!\n\nI'm adamant about not letting my father or the chief-of-chiefs marry me off. But Madearn. He's not what I imagined when I thought about the Six-Fords. He's … different.
We got to talking. Madearn's got a good mind. A good heart.\n\nLook, it doesn't matter. He's already promised to someone else. And we have a feud to end, so let's get on with it.

Worried? No. Whatever gave you that idea? Maybe?\n\nYou spend your whole life believing one thing about your clan and something totally different about the other. Then you talk to her. She's funny, bright. She has hopes and dreams. She's not a monster.
Yes. But not like that. I don't think.\n\nLook. Let's just find the fragments of the Lover's Coil and put an end to the feud. All right?

Indeed. I was worried about Eslyn. As soon as I settled the vateshran at Hroldan Ring, I set out to find her and make sure she was all right.\n\nOf course, leave it to me to forget which battlefield she actually went to.
Aye. I suppose I've grown to care for her a bit. All that talking we did at the vateshran's camp …. It doesn't matter.\n\nEnough of that. There's a favor I need of you, outsider.
I didn't know her when this all started. Then I came to know her wit, her laugh. Any soul with a heart in their breast would grow fond of those. \n\nEven if they shouldn't.

That's too long a tale to tell in my current state. Ask me again after I've fed.\n\nSuffice it to say, Adusa and I ran together a long time ago. Before she traded her claws for the life of a noble. As you can tell, we can barely stand each other now.

I sent him back to Hroldan Ring so he and the vateshran could gather what they need to fix the Lover's Coil. I told him I'd wait to make sure that you got back safely.\n\nSpeaking of which, can I ask why you came? How did you know I needed help?

I thought so. Outsider, forgive me for laying my burdens on you, but ….\n\nIt's been nagging at me for a bit now. What if everything we're doing isn't worth it? What if Madearn and I just … went along with the handfasting?
Good. I didn't think these monsters could overpower Kathad.\n\nLet's hurry and catch up to him, five-claw.
I've run these peaks and valleys since I was a lass. I knew the cairn marked some old battle, just never gave it much thought until the vateshran's story.\n\nIt has to be there.
I'm just … confused. My mind and my heart are telling me two different things, and I've never been sure which is the smarter of the two. \n\nI'll be fine. There's nothing to worry about.
Do I? I suppose things feel a little less lonely with him here. \n\nWhy shouldn't I enjoy it? While it lasts, at least.
Nothing. Forget I said anything. We came here for a specific goal. It's time we get to it.

No. The usurper, Varen, lost his lands, his throne, and so much more. What Mannimarco promised me was given.\n\nIf that don't sit well with you, I got no apologies to give. I can only tell you that's where my dealings with the Worm King begin and end.

I'll say a few words to conclude the handfasting ceremony, and then the Six-Fords and Eagleseers will depart for their holdings to plan the marriage. \n\nIt will take place before the season ends, I'll see to that.

Aye, harrier. We're bound together now. And how else will you find anything in those forsaken depths?\n\nI think the sky tale we saw in the fire—the Snake—will point the way. Once I figure out how it connects to all this, that is.

I don't! But, maybe I could … if it were him. I know what my heart is telling me. I'm falling for Madearn. I'm a true fool for it, especially after starting this whole mess.\n\nBut I know he's already pledged to another. I can't tell him how I feel.

That's what we call the shapes in the stars. Constellations is your word, I think. \n\nSome of my sisters can read the stars the way you read a book. See the future, learn the truth in every twinkle. I don't have the knack. It's fire and bones for me.

Absolutely. The caves beneath this level are littered with the things. There's a lift nearby that descends to the Blinds.\n\nBut be careful. Boss Trenlor chased the creatures that used to occupy these cells down there. They can be hostile when aroused.
With what, this … Lover's Coil? They are fools to think that all the problems of the Six-Ford and Eagleseer clans can be solved by restoring some dusty relic.

Maybe not, but these clans have spilled each other's blood for generations. No relic from some bygone age will stay their weapons. \n\nThe handfasting can end this violence, today. Now go give Eslyn and Madearn your blessing so we can get on with this.

I do. Try to understand, outsider. The hatred that runs between these clans is more than just habit. They cannot simply douse their anger after hearing some story.\n\nIf the wedding doesn't take place, they may never trust enough to try again.
There's no choice to be made, outsider. The handfasting needs to happen. It's the only way.\n\nThe sooner you, Eslyn, and Madearn understand that, the better.

I see. I'm sure Drisene believes it's real, regardless.\n\nStill, without the chief's blessing, it's not binding. Madearn may not like going back on his word, but perhaps doing so will give Drisene an opportunity to find someone who truly loves her.
The fool! That's a strange match. I knew they were childhood friends, but marriage? \n\nWhat else did he tell you about it?
Spirits take me, this is what I get for involving an outsider.\n\nFine. But be quick about it.
This is your plan, outsider, not mine.\n\nThe fate of these clans rests with Eslyn and Madearn now. If they won't go through with the wedding, then they must find another way.

I did, didn't I? Very well.\n\nI found Adusa right after her change. She was young and wild. We hunted. We killed. We drank our fill and then drank some more. But she had a streak of virtue I could never wipe out. I fear Kathad shares a similar trait.

Already taken care of. Here. Put on these servant's clothes. The clan will ignore you if you look like one of the mortal servants.\n\nThe chalice sits on the table near the throne. Place the mushroom in the chalice. Then step back and wait for us.

I'm glad an outsider such as yourself is involved. The calls of clan and kin are powerful, Eslyn and Madearn will need your support. But I believe in them. They can work to bring about a future of peace for the Six-Fords and Eagleseers.
Ah … I'll let you explain that to Eslyn and Madearn, then.\n\nI understand your decision. I may not agree with it, but I can see the benefits. I only hope the lad and lass feel the same.

Thank you, outsider. I fear the chief-of-chief's ire, but she must understand that us getting married is not the only path to peace.  \n\nThe feud is daft. So much grief for nothing. Madearn and I do not need to be married to make them see that.

I am. I may love Madearn, but he's pledged himself to another anyway. The handfasting can't happen. We must make our refusal clear. \n\nYou should talk to Madearn. I'd sooner do this with him at my side … if he's willing.
I am. I may love Madearn, but he's pledged himself to another anyway. The handfasting can't happen. We must make our refusal clear.\n\nMadearn agrees, aye? Of course he does. Then we should move.
My father and Chief Six-Ford are still with the chief-of-chiefs, aye? We'll need to speak with them and make our intentions known.
I see. When I vowed to wed Drisene, I never dreamed what it would mean for my clan, or for Eslyn's. If I never made that promise then all of this … then Eslyn and I might have ….\n\nGah! Damn it all.

All of this suffering from a broken stone. My father didn't heed the vateshran, but I'll make him hear me. This feud is stupid. The time's come to end it.\n\nI've no right to expect it, but I hope Eslyn will help me in this.
All of this suffering from a broken stone. My father didn't heed the vateshran, but I'll make him hear me. This feud is stupid. The time's come to end it.\n\nIf Eslyn's ready, then let's finish this.

If there's anything this day has taught me, it's that there is a chance for my people to reconcile. Eslyn is nothing like I expected her to be. Even if we are not to be married, that doesn't mean what transpired between us has to go to waste.

I … think that is what my heart wants, too. The more I sit here and think about it, the more foolish this plan to defy the handfasting seems. \n\nBut I made a vow to Drisene. What kind of man would I be, if I can't keep my word?
I think I am. Drisene is strong, she'll be all right. And when we're finished with the handfasting, the Six-Fords and Eagleseers will know peace. That's what's important.

I will. Just … give me a moment to think! I can't make any decisions with you standing here badgering me.\n\nLet's just go on with it. I just have to hope my heart knows the right answer when the moment comes.

Well, the good thing is that prospect is not nearly as nauseating as it was earlier today. Getting to know Madearn helped. And I want the bloodshed between my clan and the Six-Fords to finally come to an end.\n\nBut … there's Madearn to think of.

I've fallen in love with him, outsider, I won't deny it. But the vow he made to Drisene … to go through with the handfasting would mean he'd have to break his promise to her. It will hurt him badly. If I truly care about him, I can't allow that.

I … think so. I'm just worried about Madearn. If we're to be married, I don't want there to be any guilt. \n\nBefore we complete the handfasting, I just want to thank you for everything you've done. Your heart is of the Reach.
He carries an axe, doesn't he?\n\nThe Headsman stands for swift ends and payment in kind. He delivers justice and punishment in equal measure.

Your guess is as good as mine. One of them called themselves the True-Sworn, but sworn to who? And why destroy the villa instead of ransacking it like normal people?\n\nQuestions that need to wait. After that arsonist!
Hmm. I have not been to the Ring in some time. I'll learn the tidings from across the crags.\n\nIf you find anyone in need of a vateshran, send them my way, aye?

Part of me feels foolish for agreeing to a marriage I fought so hard against … but no, I don't regret it. There will be peace now, and Madearn is a good man. I just hope he will see me with love, and not as a reminder of guilt as we go forward.

Perhaps I should … but I don't. Speaking with you helped. I can see a future for Drisene that gives me hope. And I see mine, with Eslyn, and that makes me hopeful as well. \n\nIt was a hard choice, but in the end, I'm glad I made it.

You heard the heat in their threats. The feud is alive between our clans. Blood will be spilled. \n\nIf any harm comes to Eslyn because of it, I don't know if I'll be able to live with myself. But … what else was I to do?

Thank you, outsider. I'm glad someone approves my decision … even if they're a stranger to my land and its ways.\n\nNow I just need to hope that Eslyn won't hate me for this, and that someday the two of us can still bring about peace for our clans.

Part of me wanted to, no doubt. I've grown fond of Eslyn. But what kind of man would I be if I went back on my word just because of that? Promises must mean more than fickle emotion, or I cannot call myself a man of the Reach.
Fair enough. \n\nI just hope that Eslyn won't hate me for this, and that someday the two of us can still bring about peace for our clans.

I'm sorry that we could not resolve the feud, and I'm … disappointed to leave Madearn. But what's important is that the two of us developed a friendship today. There's still hope for the future because of that. I'll make sure we don't squander it.

Years ago we argued about what the Spirit Queen's teachings meant for our clan. Nathari believes that we're meant to return to the old ways, the dark ways, to seek Namira's favor. I believe those days are better left behind us.

You know her as Namira. And yes, she is a spirit of death. Your soft priests in their stone houses see her as a fearsome specter, fools that they are.\n\nReachfolk know the Spirit Queen as a guide. She watches over us when we take that final journey.

The Spirit Queen often speaks to the witches of my clan. My former clan.\n\nOh, we honor all of the spirits of the Reach, but the Spirit Queen herself chose our foremothers to be the keepers of dark and powerful secrets.

I wish I knew. Someone wanted this whole place in ashes. That tells me they have something to hide. But the last Longhouse Emperor died five years ago. Who cares what's down here?\n\nAfter I give over the book, maybe I'll look into this more.

Over in Riften. No idea why he's interested in the book, but my contact told me not to ask questions.\n\nHey, if you find yourself in the area we should meet. Maybe look into these mysteries together. More adventure!
Yes. With Larama's help, the relic was safely transported back to Artaeum. My time-slowing spells seemed to contain the worst of the damage, which also kept the cave from collapsing on top of us.

I suppose I'll need to explain that. Provided the Order doesn't already know. I suspect that since Larama is here, it means they do. \n\nI certainly learned my lesson about idolizing the Order. Even our own can fall.
Now that it's free of the vampire's pall, Karthwasten thrives. The Crow-Eye clan will always remember what you did for us.
But don't get any ideas, outsider. I'm still keeping my eye on you — so mind yourself!
Well, thank you. Karthwasten knows the favor of the Daedra once more, and the air no longer reeks of the storm. Our home is at peace, as are we.

Does a tiger need to be thanked for killing a terrorbird? Adusa-daro does not hunt to be appreciated. She hunts because it is her nature. The only reward this one needs is worthy prey and fresh blood.

Hard to say. Adusa-daro has begun my training, but there's only so much we can accomplish out here in the Reach.\n\nShe says we'll be heading to Rivenspire soon. So I can train in Ravenwatch Castle. And I met Gwendis and Fennorian. They welcomed me.

Since the incident with Pythis, I've focused on applying myself to my studies. My fellow Psijics never faulted me for what happened, they've been nothing but supportive. So much so, in fact, that they've asked me to consider taking an apprentice! Me!

I think the spirits are smiling on us once more. The Thornroots have given my clan no more trouble, and I'm thankful. Father thinks it's time I take up more of the leadership of the clan, so he's teaching me the ways. I hope I'm ready.

This location was being magically concealed until moments ago, when there was a large spike in tonal power. \n\nI was tasked to investigate the theft of a relic from Artaeum's vaults, so I've been looking for just such a disturbance.

I suspected something of the sort. If what you say is true, then Calis has nothing to fear from the Order.\n\nIf any evidence is to be had here, rest assured I will find it. Your assistance in this matter is noted.
I … no. \n\nNothing else needs to be said.

Exactly? I have no idea. But Rada aligned it to open a specific destination. I can sense the Darkstorm gathering, so he must have reached it.\n\nOf course, the chaotic forces of the Void may change our trajectory and hurl us into the vast emptiness.

I'm barely foot to stone and he's clamoring for my attention? I had no mind to stand by a throne when I first started my journey. Now, here we are. The Reach has suffered so much. I want to help restore the land.\n\nAye, I'll serve.

I can speak for myself. You have more important matters to attend to.\n\nThere's a friend who's journeyed a long way to thank you personally for all you've done. It would be rude to keep them waiting.
Aye, I can. But I won't. I'm enjoying the suspense.\n\nOff with you.

I have worked all my life to atone for the hubris of my first years as a vampire. Rada went to great lengths to remind me of my damnation.\n\nAnd I still can't control the darkness racing through my blood. I may not be able to do what must be done.
Happily! I'm a traveling merchant. Imperial City was once my home. \n\nThese days, I travel all over Tamriel to find interesting, exotic things to buy and bring back to the city to resell.

The Three Banners War changed that. Imperial City is uninhabitable now. Most of Cyrodiil is, really.\n\nI was recruited by <<1>> to help acquire needed supplies, furnishings, food, and homes for the Imperial refugees. Now my home is the road.
Most days, yes. But so many lost so much more than I did. I had no family to flee with or care for, so my transition was easier.\n\nAt least now I can put my skills toward helping those who need it.

There was a time when this one felt more like a nurse-maid than compatriot to those two, but Gwendis and Fennorian are no longer helpless kittens.\n\nCount Verandis need not worry. Adusa stands firm. House Ravenwatch will endure.

Much Reach blood stained my blade during Varen's Rebellion. Not all were proud and noble warriors, but many deserved respect. It is the duty of those who fight to remember those who die. Even their foes.

Don't worry, I'll stick around to raise a glass or two with you. Celebrate our victory. If I stay too long, though, one of these leader types will try to send me on another mission.\n\nSai might not mind, but I'm determined to finally relax a little.

After years of saber-rattling, we need to start learning how to be good neighbors. How will we trade goods? How will we resolve disputes? Jarl Svana and I are resolved to lay a foundation that our diplomats can build upon—however long it takes us.

Hah, no. I won't be barricading myself in the library any longer, but someone has to curate our records. Can you imagine Adusa doing it, or Gwendis? I'll show you the state of her sock drawer sometime.\n\nThis was quite the adventure, wasn't it?

The Gray Host? We've heard of these invaders, but so far they've left our village alone. Until now, I guess.\n\nI won't pretend to understand the whole of it … but this affront to the Reach and its people, there will be a reckoning.

Yes. His blood lust gave way to introspection, and introspection led to study. He was already a peerless scholar. All ansei were. But he became fascinated with vampire texts.\n\nEventually, he found a new purpose.

For all the wrongs he's done, I still pray he's found some peace away from the torments of Molag Bal. It might not satisfy your sense of justice, but it's my hope … for an old friend.\n\nJust a theory. One I may be testing soon.
Yes, many were displaced when Molag Bal invaded and the Three Banners War broke out over Cyrodiil.\n\nThey are good people that have been driven from their homes and scattered across Tamriel.

Absolutely. Many have lost loved ones in the process, after all.\n\nTheir shrines were destroyed within Imperial City. As they relocate, many have given their messages to people like me, hoping they will reach a shrine elsewhere in Tamriel.

We're the Hillhunters. We roam the Reach, taking what the seasons give us. We're few in number, but no one knows the land as we do. We live by our wits and our woodcraft, keeping out of the quarrels of larger clans.\n\nUntil the Gray Host came along.
Isn't that where Rada al-Saran harvested souls for the Dark Heart? If Verandis released them all, maybe Arana's right and she didn't come back alone.\n\nThat's something we should see for ourselves.

When the Gray Host came, Hagravens promised to protect the Thornroot clan by growing Briarhearts for them.\n\nWe came to parley about making camp here. The Hagravens just wanted bodies to plant seeds in.

Used to be a watchtower, I'm told, but it's been a ruin as long as anyone can remember. Draugr lurk in the tunnels under the hill, but the ruins above are defensible. Briar Rock's always been a refuge for clans in need of shelter.

Briarhearts are living weapons—warriors changed by dark magic to defend kith and kin.\n\nHagravens, now … they're witches of a sort. They can be helpful, but they demand a price. Whatever advice they give serves their own purposes in the end.

Aye. The Gray Host threatens everyone. I wanted to take to the hills, but my father thought it best to find a place of strength. The Thornroots got here first, though.\n\nWe thought to share Briar Rock with them. The Hagravens had other plans.

These are hard times. Maybe the Thornroots saw the Hagravens as their only hope. Whatever their reason, they let the Hagravens turn them against their neighbors.\n\nThat's what Hagravens do. They lead those who seek their help into dark deeds.

Gwerina's dead? I feared it was so when she did not answer my summons, but I prayed I was wrong.\n\nHircine will guide her to the Hunting Grounds and she will find her place. You say you recovered a relic? The Symbol of Hrokkibeg, I hope?

Ard Caddach granted us this hall to establish a shrine to honor Hircine. I sent my apprentices to retrieve the Symbols of the Five Aspects from the clans that guard them. They will be safer inside these walls.

Aye. That is the relic, simple though it may appear. Hrokkibeg is but one aspect of Hircine, known also as the Mighty Bear.\n\nWill you give me the relic so I may add it to this shrine? That would be a fitting tribute to my lost apprentice.

The Symbol of Gulibeg! I sent my apprentice, Layren, to retrieve it. She would never have let it fall into the hands of a raider. Not while she still drew breath.\n\nWe will mourn later. For now, we rejoice at the recovery of another sacred relic.

Oh, it is more than that. The tales tell us that Gulibeg the Quick Fox fashioned a shard of bone from Lorkh's ribs into a wand that could confound any mortal. \n\nOf course, this is only a symbol, but it deserves a place of honor in this shrine.

<<1>>, you say? The Argonian worked for a vile man from Gideon who deals in Daedric relics. \n\nThe totem has meaning to us as a symbol of Storihbeg, the King of Wolves. One aspect of the great Hircine, our Hunt-Father. But it has no inherent power.

Any death has significance, great and small. One died for disrespecting the Lord of the Hunt, the other defending him. That is the way of things.\n\nThank you for bringing this news to me, wanderer. What will you do with the sacred relic now?

It's not the letters themselves, it's what's in them. There are references to Rada al-Saran and a Reach hero, as well as something that ties them both to Sai Sahan's martial traditions.\n\nIt might be nothing, but Sai wants to investigate.
Let's burn all traces of this plant. And we should knock down a few of the pillars holding up the roof. A mine as old as this, that should cause enough damage to drive the Gray Host out.

It's what the Reachfolk call their lore keepers. They don't have a written language, so they remember history through stories and songs.\n\nWith any luck, we'll find a vateshran at Red Eagle Redoubt who knows the story of Rada al-Saran and Faolan.

It was purely by chance. When Lyris and I helped the people at the Reachwind Ritual Site, we discovered a letter on the Gray Host leader. A number of the vampire commanders were discussing the story through correspondence.\n\nI was intrigued.
Because Lyris is as unique and as beautiful as the flower that blooms in the northern cold. It is a term of affection that suits her most admirably.
I will make a slight detour and meet Lyris on the road or back at Hroldan Ring. Then we will journey together to meet you at Red Eagle Redoubt.\n\nWe shall not tarry, my friend.

The vateshran explained that the Reachfolk have a story concerning Red Eagle and a fallen Sword Saint. How they met in this cave to exchange knowledge.\n\nSince that time, the cave has been left alone. Who knows what's beneath all the undergrowth?

Usually Reachfolk train their entire lives for this day. They enter knowing full well that it may mean their death. If you choose to turn back now, you shall lose your pride but keep your life.\n\nSo, once more, I ask. Are you ready?
You clear the undergrowth. Sai and I will be ready to extract whatever we find.

Danger, but it seems related to this Dwarven structure and not the dark energy we're tracking. I doubt it's anything we can't handle.\n\nJust be careful as you traverse the portals. A fall from those heights could prove deadly. Even for you.

We're still the same rebels we were before the defense of Markarth. Wayward Guardians is a name the people have given us. \n\nYou know, Arana found me after a skirmish with Nords. I was victorious, but suffered a festering wound that had grown foul.
Thank you, stranger. I long to see the sky again.
I can make it there. Whoever you are, thank you for coming to save us.

Once the Hagravens learned I was a chieftain, they decided to save me for a special ritual. Something about making me into a seed for a new briarheart tree. Or maybe they just said that to scare me.\n\nIt sounded awful, to be honest with you.

Briarhearts die to this life so that they may live again as protectors of the Reach. They give themselves willingly to the knife … or so it should be.\n\nThe Thornroots are taking that choice away, enslaving their Briarhearts. It's wrong.

The Gray Host is too great a foe for the Hillhunters alone. I wanted to bring the clan to a place we could easily defend, and wait for the danger to pass.\n\nBriar Rock is a refuge for the wandering clans. Or it used to be.

When we found the Thornroot clan here, Medone said we should keep moving, find safety in the wilds. It turns out she was right.\n\nI've always wanted her to follow in my footsteps. She'll make a good chieftain someday.

Do you, now? And you want to share that information with Ard Caddach? You're certainly full of surprises, outsider.\n\nAll right. I'll allow you to approach the throne. If your courage holds out. Fair warning—the ard's in a foul temper today.

Not yet, you don't. But you will. Ard Caddach's as likely to remove your head from your shoulders as listen to you, so talk fast, outsider.\n\nAnd remember, the ard has no patience for fools or flatterers. Keep that in mind.

Oh, how quickly we forget our history! You do remember that the Longhouse Emperors came from the Reach, don't you? They ruled the Empire for decades, including the Reach.\n\nI was sent here as my first assignment. I grew to love the place.
My father asked me the same question. If it's up to me … we're for the mountains now. It's a hard life, but it's safe. No enemy can catch us in the high vales.

That's for Medone to decide. You taught the Thornroots a hard lesson, but I learned one too. When my kin tell me I'm choosing the wrong path, I ought to listen.\n\nI'd like to see where Medone leads us, given the chance.
Aye, I know that now. I won't always be able to see the best course for the Hillhunters. But I believe that if I speak from my heart, I'll do right by the clan more often than not. Thank you, friend.

Ard Caddach came to appreciate my administrative skills. When the Empire fell, he requested I stay. Now I maintain records for the job brokers.\n\nSo few of the Reachfolk have the ability to read and write, which makes my service extremely valuable.

Ah, the keystone. What is it and how is it connected to that Dwarven structure? Why are they so important to Rada and Lady Belain? Perhaps they seek to harness some sort of Dwarven sorcery?\n\nRegardless, we can't allow them to achieve their goal.

Yes, but we need to proceed with caution. We don't know the purpose of the keystone, and we don't know what they plan to do with it. That said, we are not without our own talents.\n\nWe can overcome any obstacles and find a way forward. We always do.

The orrery remains charged with Void energy. But the Dark Heart was never completely filled and it already wanes. That means we denied Rada al-Saran a limitless source of power.\n\nRada may have escaped for the moment, but we will find him.

If I knew for certain, there'd be no need to have you go and take a look, would there?\n\nProbably supplies for their army, though what vampires and werewolves need is anyone's guess. Ritual items. Things for their harrowcraft. That's what I expect.

My foremothers believed the Spirit Queen granted them power in exchange for the souls they sent to her realm. A death is the greatest gift a mortal can give, after all.\n\nThis was where the clan performed ritual sacrifices to appease Namira.

Aye, that seems to be where all this is leading. To awaken the Dark Heart, my coven must sacrifice that which they hold most dear—their own kin. Many Ghostsong clan members are about to die. \n\nThat's why Nathari brought them here. We must stop her.

Rebel's Retreat? That's a bold thought. Maybe we picked the wrong stronghold and the wrong allies. If there's no refuge anywhere in the Reach, might as well face our foes with spear in hand.\n\nI'll speak with my father about it.

Arana asks nothing of me. She put a sword in my hand and gave me a choice. I could leave freely, or I could fight alongside her to defend the Reach.\n\nI serve my homeland and all free folk of the Reach.

Yes. I was dying. I prepared to end my suffering when Arana touched my hand. She said my name was kingly. That my story was not meant to end that day. After that, the rest is a blur, all fire and chanting and poultices. \n\nArana had healed me.

Sai always lets his duty guide his actions. He fights for others. For what they need. For the greater good. He needs to decide what he truly wants to fight for. Only then can he claim his spirit sword.\n\nMeet us outside partner. I need to talk to Sai.
In many ways, our dealings with the spirits are not unlike making a trade with a merchant or another clan. \n\nThe offerings represent our part in the negotiation.

You sound surprised. Is that not how marriages are arranged where you come from?\n\nThey belong to different clans. Clans that do not get along. I have brought them to this place of meeting to work out a marriage that will benefit both clans.

Madearn is an adequate scout, but he's a sorry hunter and an abysmal fighter.\n\nI suppose if there's any good in all this, it's that Chief Eagleseer is fool enough to accept such a poor match for his daughter.

The Crow-Eye clan has a different relationship with each spirit. Some give us guidance. Others provide protection. These offerings remind them that we're a part of this land.\n\nIf they do their part, we'll do ours.

Each offering has a different significance to each spirit. The most important aspect is that these materials have a connection to Karthwasten and the surrounding countryside.\n\nThey remind us of the bond we both share with this land.
Not in the way you're thinking. The power inside each offering comes from its connection to Karthwasten. Each is part of us and of the spirits. That's where the power lies.

Arana? I know that name. She's a honey-tongued fanatic who refused to bury her sword when I forged a peace with the Gray Host. She's slippery, but I didn't realize she led the rebels. \n\nSniffing out a Reach witch. That commands respect. For now.

Aye, I know Hircine's Gift when I see it. There are two kinds of werewolves—those who master their gift, and those who are slaved to it. I can tell which you are.\n\nIn the Reach, we judge you on what you do, not what you are. Mostly.

And your friend is a vampire! Werewolves are Hircine's chosen. Many of the Reach's greatest champions are skin-changers.\n\nBradan and the other werewolves are nothing like those Gray Host ravagers. They're the clan's loyal protectors.

As much as my father might wish otherwise, I am the son of the Six-Ford clan's chief. It was the chief-of-chiefs' idea to connect our clans through a handfasting.\n\nIf I weren't otherwise obligated, I might do this to end the feud … perhaps.

With a father as fierce as Chief Six-Ford, I expected Madearn to be a mighty warrior.\n\nHe seems nice enough, but more like a hare that some witch turned into a human. His word is his bond, though. That's something.

Exactly what I told you. Once the darkcap mushroom touches the blood, it releases a substance that will weaken Trenlor. Make him easier to deal with. Then I can challenge him on a more equal footing.\n\nIt will work perfectly. You'll see.

Reach magic strikes me as wild and unpredictable. Arana clearly shares a strong connection with the ebb and flow of the spirits, though.\n\nShe might have sensed these creatures, but I suspect something else caused her distress.

You've seen those dark storms swirling over the Reach? The Gray Host calls them harrowstorms.\n\nTheir witches conjure them up using harrowcraft. From what we can tell, it requires all sorts of ingredients. Fetishes and alchemical mixtures mostly.
Aye. Harrowcraft is what we call the rituals we've seen the Gray Host perform when they summon those cursed storms.

Are you daft, outsider? Do I look like a witch to you?\n\nA true witch has power—hears the spirits, knows the old words, commands animals, things like that. Some use their power to help. Others use it to kill. Icereach witches are particularly evil.

I know little of the dark below. The witches claim the Nighthollow were once a great and noble house, perhaps as old as the curse of vampirism itself. \n\nNow they are but wretched things, as withered and fallen as their shadowed keep.

Though Blackreach contains unspeakable horrors, the knowledge hidden in the keep should help save lives. The witches say there are scrolls written in an ancient language. And a tome that can help translate it.\n\nFind what you can and bring it to me.

The scout described them as pale, blind Goblins, but there are no Goblin tribes in these lands. They must be something else.\n\nThere was one other curious thing. The way he described the camp. Their dwellings were not made of hide, or bone, or wood.

Fear may have clouded his senses, but the scout swore they were made out of insects. Large chitinous shells, broken limbs, even heads.\n\nI can only assume these creatures hunt and harvest the caverns below as we hunt these hills and valleys.

Yes. It shouldn't be hard to find. It means much to us that you would brave such danger to save some of our own.\n\nBut be careful. I wish to see these exiles returned home, but not at the cost of your own life.

The Dwarves who built Markarth called the place Nchuand-Zel, the Radiant City. It extends deeper than the surface stones suggest. If we are to truly keep our people safe, we must cleanse it of the monsters that still skulk about the lower halls.

The Wayward Guardians trust you, harrier. Of that, have no doubt.\n\nBut the people of Markarth need to see those sigils hanging from the ramparts. They need to know that they have nothing more to fear. That we are here to defend them.

Reachfolk never utter the name of Lorkh in prayer, for his part in our story ended long ago. Some call him the Lord of Mortals and claim that his sacrifice is the reason we live at all.\n\nAnd while we live, Hircine guides us.

How to explain to one unfamiliar with our beliefs?\n\nHircine gives us purpose. Teaches us to hunt, to fight, to survive. But it was Lorkh who taught us why we should. That no matter the struggle, we should not go quietly into death.

We do not fear death, but we understand the value of a fleeting life. What wonders might we see? What wisdom might we gain? What mark will we leave upon this world?\n\nThe shrine represents a will to live in spite of the certainty of death.

The Hunt-Father teaches us to utilize the bounty he provides. We hunt game not only to feed ourselves, but we use every part of it to clothe and arm ourselves as well. \n\nIn this way, we honor our ancestors by living as they did.

Necessity. There is nothing natural about the threats that plague our lands, and if we must sully ourselves with unnatural Dwarfcraft to defend the Reach, Hircine will understand.\n\nAfter all, he wants us to be hunters, not prey.

For someone with your skills, silver may make little difference. But the average Reach warrior stands no chance against such monsters without it. \n\nFire also serves as a potent weapon, but such magic is rare. With silver, we can burn away the evil.

Only that our shamans have need of them. Their work is beyond my understanding, but I trust them to help arm and protect the Wayward Guardians.\n\nEvery gemstone you retrieve will give us a better chance against the Gray Host.

I know little of the Deep Folk. Their ways are as strange to me as their runes.\n\nThe place has been whispered about by our shamans and lore keepers since before you discovered it, but it was nothing more than a legend. Until now.

Each of these chieftains have seen their people slain at the other's hands. That hardens a soul.\n\nAt the end of the day, outsider, the tale is just words. This one happened to have a nice rock to go along with them. Now it is up to you to decide.

I'm famished after that telling. I always am. And wouldn't you know it, I left my damned seed-pouch back at camp. The birds'll have gotten to it by now.\n\nI might haver with that fat Eagleseer over yon. He looks like he knows where to find a vittle.

I was. And even now, centuries later, I still carry that shame.\n\nThe Ravenwatch is more than a noble house and a fellowship of good vampires. It's an atonement. For things I failed to do. Friends I failed to save—from mortals and from themselves.

If Eslyn and Madearn complete the handfasting, the clans will be united, that's true. But, they're of chieftain's blood, and will some day rule these clans. After today, do you really see a future of continued violence for them? Hope is not lost.

It's not my decision to make, happily enough. But the chief-of-chiefs has things a bit confused, as I see it.\n\nNot supporting the handfasting doesn't mean the feud will go on forever. The choice is about ending it today, or ending it in the future.

There may be a peace of sorts inside Markarth, but out here we're outnumbered and fighting for our lives. Nothing unusual in that.\n\nWe won't let the Gray Host desecrate our land. And we won't let Caddach give it away just to avoid a little blood.

Then you know the Gray Host has recruited Icereach witches to conjure up their storms. They use fetishes and alchemical mixtures in the rituals, so it makes sense they need a place to store those components.

No, bringing us the information is good enough for now. We're going to need a lot more warriors before we make that kind of move against the Gray Host.\n\nDamn Caddach for ordering our people into the city. We need to fight, not hide.

Aye. The entire coven threw in with the Gray Host. They used to advise that damned fool Emperor Leovic and you know how that turned out, right?\n\nGreedy hags, the lot of them. I respect their strength, but their hearts are all twisted inside.

Well, you'll probably have to fight them again. They stalk these hills like old ghosts. They're allied with the Gray Host now, don't you know?\n\nGreedy hags, the lot of them. I respect their strength, but their hearts are all twisted inside.

Count Verandis, Gwendis, Fennorian … we came here to look into the threat posed by the Gray Host. As you can imagine, a renegade army of vampires and werewolves has us quite concerned.\n\nKathad may have to learn on the job, as it were.

If the Lothid clan continues to be a threat and Freyleth is a part of that, then yes, the Ravenwatch will deal with them.\n\nFor now though, Adusa will give her the benefit of the doubt. And a chance to show us she really is a good leader for the clan.
Well, they started glowing. I've seen flora like this once before while I was researching spores from a Dwemer ruin. I have a theory about what's happening, but I need a specimen to study.
He what? I—I cannot find my words. I don't know whether to mourn his loss or celebrate what he gave us.\n\nYou should tell the ard. He'll want to pay respects of his own, I'm sure.

Traditions passed down from our foremothers. Like the story of the Prophecy of the Heart. It deals with souls. Darkness. Endings.\n\nI know the core of it, but Nathari understands the nuances. Unfortunately, we haven't spoken in a long, long time.

An outsider? Not likely. We need someone to intercede on our behalf.\n\nWe need Bradan. He's a friend, and he holds the respect of the clan. If he vouches for you, Nathari might talk to you. He often visits Hroldan Ring to trade news. Meet me there.

I returned to save Freyleth and the clan from Boss Trenlor. I accomplished that. I know the clan is better off than it was. That it has a more promising future. But that future doesn't include me.\n\nMy path leads in a different direction.

That the Dark Heart exists. Death feeds it and only sacrifice will awaken it to share its power with those that believe. Dark allusions like that.\n\nNathari believes the prophecy speaks a literal truth. Maybe she's right, but it's still wrong.

Yes, but Ghostsong witches have argued about the nature of the Heart for generations. Some believe the prophecy is symbolic. There's darkness in every mortal heart. That's my view.\n\nOthers believe the prophecy is meant to be taken literally.

A stranger visited the clan when I was young. She asked about the old lore. She wore a smile, but I saw darkness in her eyes.\n\nYears later, when I saw her beside the ard's throne, I recognized her. Lady Belain. And she hadn't aged a day.

Aye, but my mother spoke in generalities. Lady Belain spent a lot of time with my aunt, though. She was one who saw every word of the prophecy as literal truth. In fact, she taught Nathari her lore.\n\nNo wonder Lady Belain sought out my sister.

Our clan uses the Rites to determine which of our children shall ascend into adulthood. If they survive the challenge, they come out as full Reach warriors. They carry all the privileges and responsibilities that the clan offers.

Master Pythis is my mentor. He's a genius! He understands the inner workings of plant life better than anyone.\n\nI'm grateful he's taken me under his wing. From what I've heard around the Order, he typically works alone.

As a new recruit, I'm probably not the best person to explain. Master Pythis could tell you more. \n\nBut in general terms, the Psijic Order is an extremely old and wise group dedicated to the study and preservation of ancient knowledge.

Plants are much easier to understand than people, in my experience.\n\nMy studies attracted the attention of Master Pythis and the Psijic Order, so I think it's worked to my benefit. Present circumstances notwithstanding, of course.

I certainly hope not! He is a high-ranking member of the Order, and therefore quite capable of taking care of himself. But it is unusual for him to be gone this long.\n\nI'm sure he just got caught up in the study of a unique specimen, as one does.

To be welcomed into their ranks is a rare privilege, and I myself still don't completely understand how they chose me.\n\nI happened to have the right set of skills at the right time. Perhaps one day the same will happen to you!

It's a strange Dwemer phenomenon. As a new recruit, I'm still learning, but I know its effects on the natural world can be catastrophic. Master Pythis said it would be fine, but I must have damaged the relic more than I thought.

Master Pythis took it with him into the cave. \n\nThat has to be it. The relic is leaking tonal energy, and the effects won't stop at just the vegetation! There's no telling what will happen if we don't remedy this.

I was afraid you'd ask that.\n\nNormally, the Order forbids such actions, but Master Pythis insisted. Aside from the two of us, few ever take botany as seriously as other Psijic pursuits. He assured me the risk was necessary.
A vault on Artaeum, the home of the Psijic Order. I'm sure if Master Pythis performs the transport spell this time, we can return it to its proper place. Once we locate both the relic and my master.

The stories vary. But I suspect the Coil simply fell from its mantle. Nothing more than an accident. The spirits had nothing to do with it, I'm sure.\n\nA simple broken stone was enough to cause the rage and violence that persists to the current day.

Love and hate are both born of passion, outsider.\n\nThough they decided their love was doomed, the passion they shared did not simply vanish. But there was only one form left for it to take. Ire. Which was passed through the blood.

Indeed. If you could carry them with you, I would be very appreciative. As before, you just have to burn them in the flame when you perform your own ceremony. But I completely understand if you choose not to.

A werewolf killed this vampire, and it wasn't one of those Gray Host mongrels. Bradan would have easily beaten us here. And I know his preferred method for delivering a quick kill.\n\nI imagine we might see more of his handiwork inside the redoubt.
Yes, along with a contingent of Skyrim dignitaries. She figured it was the least she could do since the Gray Host attacked both our realms. Offer help the way Eastern Skyrim aided Solitude.

He's a big Redguard, but he looks puny next to Titanborn. Shor's bones, though, doesn't everybody?\n\nThey say he's some kind of sword master. Or was it a Dragonguard? I'm not sure. It's hard to remember anything other than his beard. It's impressive!

Normal? I'm not sure what that is anymore. But if you're asking how we're faring, we're doing fine. Distribution of the elixir continues, and they found a way to cure the harrowed. And except for a few disorganized bands, the Gray Host is on the run.

And you, as well. I only wish we weren't in the midst of yet another crisis.\n\nI formed the Ravenwatch to deal with this type of eventuality. But even with centuries to prepare, I find myself caught off guard. And Caddach's stubbornness doesn't help.

With your warning, Ard Caddach can decide what to do with Lady Belain's advice in the future. As to why they care that Reachfolk gather within the city, I'll need to think about that.\n\nDid you hear anything else of significance during their exchange?

A particularly vile Xivkyn waits for you with one of his creations. Also, some ghastly new kind of creature called a "titan." Never saw one of those when I was alive.\n\nSeriously though, watch out for those banekin. They're a sneaky bunch.

Rada tried to use Dwarven devices once, but nothing came of it. Interesting.\n\nAs I toured the city, I met Nolovan. He works with Dwarven scrap in the southeast section of Markarth. Maybe he can lead us to this keystone before Lady Belain acquires it.

Only the finest spirits the Master of Beasts has to offer. In recent years, the plant life has shown increasing aggression, so watch for that. \n\nAlso I met a minotaur named Rahdgarak in here the other day. He had a surprisingly great sense of humor.
A very spritely fire spirit makes her home here. \n\nAlso, a surprisingly attractive Dremora. I tried asking him to go for a walk once, but he spit fire at me. I took that as a no.

That is a long and complicated tale. Suffice to say that Gwendis proved instrumental in my rescue.\n\nSomehow, she's become even more capable in my absence. Truly, there's no greater joy for a teacher than to see a student flourish.

Yes. But too few.\n\nWe tracked Rada al-Saran to the Reach and found the place crawling with Gray Host warriors. He's here for a reason, and I think it goes beyond simple conquest, but the truth of his motives elude me.
A simple but ingenious device. Just point it at a wooden post and shoot. It anchors itself deep, then pulls you to the destination.\n\nThe way ahead is treacherous, so keep hold of that grapple!
See that molten orb? Strike it with all the power you can muster! Then, take a step in the lava. It won't kill you. I promise.

The Wounding continues! I designed the next section to test our warriors' speed. The swift hare survives where the dull ox cannot, as they say.\n\nOnce through the portal, you won't have long until the magic pulls you back here. Work quickly!
Did she? Wonder what that means. I would certainly call these black spots "strange."\n\nRarely am I at a loss for words, but this felt completely new. As if the darkness wanted to … unmake me.
Hmm. That's not what you were asked to look into. Still, it confirms my own suspicions about my own keep-witch.\n\nDon't look so surprised. I'm not half as stupid as people think, rover.

We grab a handful of hot coals and dance on a bed of straw. These coals burn, rover. Right to the bone. But if you drop even one, the straw alights and flames take all of you to Molag Bal.\n\nDo you see? Belain's a hot coal, so I grip her tight.

Made him my royal taster. I don't think the thought of being poisoned even crossed his mind, but he seems happy so long as the food and drink keeps coming.\n\nUnofficially, he's also the jester, but don't tell him I said so.

Allow? I can count on three fingers the number of people I allow in Understone Keep. The rest? They come and go as they please.\n\nLet me tell you about the ember dance. It's a ceremony we perform here in the Reach. Have you ever heard of it?
An accord, at least. It's a step in the right direction.

If I am to be wed to this power, then I must ensure that it never gets used again. For that to happen, both the Heart and I must fade into obscurity. \n\nHouse Ravenwatch will carry on without me. Arana will send them here to receive the news soon.

This mission … there were problems at every turn. Hircine definitely tested me on this hunt. I almost died trying to retrieve the Symbol of Uricanbeg. In order to establish a new shrine in Markarth, we need to earn it.\n\nWill you help me, wanderer?

The old tower at the top of the rise. It's the lair of a powerful minotaur. Look for a drum of bound skin and wood in its hoard. \n\nIf you find it, take it to the high shaman in Markarth. I'm in no condition to help, so I'll make my own way back.
Heh. Indeed it is. Which means it will be the perfect match for an outsider.

Aye. What better than a drum to represent Uricanbeg, the Great Stag?\n\nUricanbeg is one of the mightiest aspects of Lord Hircine, whose beating hooves, like the beating of a drum, sound the Blood Summons, which calls prey for us to hunt.

It's in his nature. Establishing a new shrine is no small undertaking. Hircine will embrace it in the end, but not before he tests us. Makes us prove our worth.\n\nThis is a hunt of a different sort. But with your help, I think we will succeed.

Of course he cares! But while a lone wolf can be a noble hunter, few can survive for long without a pack.\n\nThere's no dishonor in asking for or receiving aid, but there's plenty of honor in a successful hunt. All that matters is we succeed.

I've recovered from worse injuries on a hunt. Keeva will watch over me, as will the Hunt-Father. I believe he meant for us to find the symbol, but for you to retrieve it. \n\nWe will meet again at the shrine when you return. Do not fear.

Well, as long as the Order doesn't decide to banish me from their ranks, I plan to continue my studies. I'd like to become proficient enough, and wise enough, to make sure nothing like this ever happens again.

I don't know. I certainly deserve it. Master Pythis was mad, but I played a part in his scheme through ignorance and carelessness. \n\nThanks to you, there should be enough proof to show that my involvement doesn't extend beyond that.

Hircine the Hunt-Father has many names, but only five aspects—Alrabeg, Storihbeg, Gulibeg, Hrokkibeg, and Uricanbeg. A proper shrine must honor them all.\n\nI sent my apprentices to the clans with some of the most revered versions of the symbols.

Just Edola, with the Symbol of Alrabeg. But this shrine will not be complete without all five symbols. Perhaps Hircine tests us, making us hunt for what we need most.\n\nThe Reach is dangerous, though. Especially now. I fear for my apprentices.

Remember, you're representing House Ravenwatch now. Consider this a diplomatic mission.\n\nI believe the ard was calling for you when we spoke to Arana. He was headed to the audience chamber with the other rulers, last I saw.

Rada al-Saran was an Ansei of great renown. A legend to rival Leki herself. The sword-saints are a lost legacy to my people. It's a shame that al-Saran did not devote himself to restoring that honorable tradition instead of his monstrous Gray Host.

Sai Sahan is an old friend. He's a Redguard swordmaster and a member of the Dragonguard. We fought alongside each other a long time ago. Helped Varen overthrow the Longhouse Emperors … for all the good it did us.

What? You have a problem with me and Sai spending some quality time together killing Gray Host vampires? Maybe even find a few moments to be alone?\n\nAnyway, he came to see me and then agreed to help as we wrap up things here in the Reach.
You're going to have to trust me on this one, partner. This is Sai's tale to tell. I'm just trying to help him. And I hope you are, too.\n\nNow get to Gloomreach and do what you can.
Then you have the Pyre Watch's eternal gratitude. I must return their stolen remains to the Unhallowed Grave and bury them deeply enough to be forgotten by all but my order. Once it is rebuilt ….

Each day, I reach more Eagleseers with the tale you helped us discover. I believe many are beginning to reconsider the feud with the Six-Fords. It will take time before there's peace … but I still have hope.
I've been preparing for the wedding. The chief-of-chiefs and the clan chiefs agree it will happen within the season.\n\nMadearn and I have grown closer than ever. Though sometimes I worry about him.

I think breaking his word to Drisene still weighs heavy on him. Though I hear she's found a new love already, Madearn still worries. \n\nI do my best to comfort him. It's easier now that our clans aren't feuding … as much as they used to, anyway.

Drisene and I have been speaking with the Six-Fords. Not all heed the tale that Barth taught us, but some are beginning to question the point of a continued feud.\n\nEslyn and I have kept in contact. She seems to not hold what happened against me.
My wedding to Eslyn will be within the season, so I'm told. I've also been helping my father settle the peace terms between the Eagleseers and my clan.\n\nI've kept myself quite busy.

Drisene and I have been looking for a new home. We… weren't exactly welcomed back to the Six-Ford holdings after everything that happened at Hroldan Ring.\n\nWe have shelter in Markarth for now. For that, we're grateful.

A bit. She's still hurt, but she told me she understands why I made the choice that I did. I think we both realize our lives will be better for it, and not just because of the peace between the Six-Fords and Eagleseers.

This old woman not important enough to merit an invitation, is that it? If you must know Svana asked me to council her on the Reach, but I'd have come whether I was invited or not. Can't trust such important matters to the likes of kings.

My hold endures, as we always have. Though we might not have weathered the harrowstorms without that elixir Fennorian and Old Mjolen concocted. They still threaten the countrysides, but we can fight free of the fear that we'll be made monsters.

I believe the word you are looking for is: refined. My boon companion is the Jarl of Solitude! I have to ensure everything served to her is of the highest quality. You'd be surprised at the sort of slop the Blue Palace chefs will put on her plate!

For the future High Queen? Certainly! Usually I have to have two or three courses before they get it right. It's cost me three notches on my best belt, but that's a small price to pay for royalty.\n\nSpeaking of, it's about time to inspect the kitchen.

No. It was a just war. Still, I bear no ill will toward the Reachfolk for the misdeeds of the Longhouse Emperors.\n\nLook around. It is plain to see that they possess as much honor and goodness as anyone else. I hope they enjoy a lasting peace.

Well, I mean it all the same. If there's ever a time when you need someone to be there for you, count on me.\n\nNow, go on. Everyone wants to talk to you and I'm only liable to embarrass myself if I keep carrying on.
But we survived it, even if it was touch and go there for a bit. Forgive me for being sentimental, but it was you who got me through it. I'll always be grateful for that.
Hmm. You think so? That would make this endeavor much more bearable. Perhaps this tiger will linger a while longer.
Oh, you'll be the first to read the naughty list when we've got one, trust me.\n\nMaybe I'll even tag along, but no caves this time!

Right, the ard. I think it might be best for Svana and I to work closely on a framework first and present it to Ard Caddach. He's got a lot going on, and I'm sure he'd rather not spend hours debating every detail.

Before becoming a vampire, Rada al-Saran was a Redguard swordmaster who once battled Leki to a standstill.\n\nAccording to the letters, he lost his ability to manifest a Shehai, his spirit sword. Then he met the Reach hero, Faolan the Red Eagle.

That I am. It's a new dawn. For me, for Markarth, for the Reach. After all you've done to bring it back from the brink of Oblivion, putting up with Caddach's arse-headed notions is the least I can do to make sure it wasn't wasted effort.

House Ravenwatch has a long and noble tradition. This one will run the estate in Count Verandis's absence. She has done so before.\n\nAs for the Ravenwatch, our work will continue. Gwendis is coming into her own, and Fennorian shows promise.
Afraid not. Yet it does make me wonder about the sign Hircine showed us in the smoke. Why show us the Snake?\n\nLet's keep searching. I'm sure we'll find something at one of the other locations.
Aye, but in and of itself, I'm not sure what it's trying to tell us. Let's keep looking, all right?

Free and safe, thankfully. After the trouble with the Thornroots we found shelter in the mountains. Now it seems that it's safe for us to return to the lowlands.\n\nAnd I'm passing on to Medone what knowledge I can. She is ready to lead.
I don't know … not yet.\n\nIt could have something to do with the guardians. Maybe. Let's go to another location on the map.

The Rites Matron oversees every entrant into the Vateshran's Rites, providing them instruction and ensuring we follow our clan's oldest traditions. She held this honor long before I was born, and I suspect she will continue long after I fall.
Positive thoughts, harrier. Positive thoughts.\n\nParticipate in the ritual. Then we will see what we will see.

Certain inanimate objects, especially of personal or sentimental value, can become imbued with the auras of those who possessed them. Auramancy allows a mage to pick up vague impressions or even see past events.

A good question. A hunter must know its quarry to track it down.\n\nApprentice Orla is a fierce warrior who never strays far from her loyal companion, Keeva the white wolf. If all else fails, look for the white wolf—if she doesn't find you first.

Take the road out of Markarth until you reach the Karth River. Follow it south until the river meets the mountains. That's the entrance to Lost Valley Redoubt.\n\nI sent Apprentice Orla there to find the relic. I pray her cunning has not abandoned her.

Important events and powerful emotions leave a mark on their surroundings. Auramancy deals with evoking memories from the auras left behind on objects.\n\nIt's an arcane art that I have perfected over the centuries. It often helps me in my work.

I don't see how. Rada al-Saran was a Yokudan swordmaster before he came to Tamriel. His vampirism is the result of a meeting with Molag Bal. At least, that's how I understand it.\n\nLady Belain, however. Her origins are unknown to me.

Auramancy is a useful tool for unraveling the history of ancient places. Clearly this keep was once great. Now it's forgotten, yet a power our enemies covet stirs within.\n\nI think the story of this place is the story of the Dark Heart.

I cast auramancy upon the insignia. The lingering magic may reveal additional scenes from the past as you explore these halls. Phantasms, really. Harmless.\n\nAnd keep watch for more void portals. As at Arkthzand, they may help you navigate this place.

We made a pact and Hircine blessed it. He put us on the scent and I plan to track it to the end. Besides, without someone who knows the Reach, the map's useless.\n\nYou know what monsters hate? Silver. According to the stories, Bthar-Zel is full of it.

Still begging? I should have the tongue ripped from your head and—damn it, rover. A favor for a favor, aye. That's the Reach way.\n\nAll right. Tell the noble. Ard Caddach will see him whenever he's ready.

And so I shall. Briefly. Caddach has a city full of Reachfolk to deal with, so I don't want to unduly distract him. Then I need to locate Arana.\n\nIf we can get the rebels to work with us against the Gray Host, we'll have more than a fighting chance.

You are? Well, I haven't actually gone and joined them yet. I was just about to head for their camp, but … well, I don't know exactly where it is. Just that it lies to the east, in the foothills. Or so I was told.\n\nI've said too much. Go away.

I'm lucky to have made it this far into the city. Caddach and his entourage have little patience for a noble such as myself. Especially a noble from a land they consider to be the home of their enemy. No, this task is better in your hands.
Ah, it figures. Nothing in this land ever seems to go the way I'd hope. I can't keep any good help, and Reachmen have the palates of hungry goats. My best efforts are wasted on them.

The survivors asked me to be chieftain, but … it's time to let the Ghostsong clan go, and begin a new clan with a new name. Better to leave the dark old ways behind.\n \nThinking about the name Longfangs. Or Wolfrunners.

I took a job cooking for the Starsinger clan in Cyrodiil, in the days of Emperor Moricar.\n\nI'm afraid I got caught up in a clan-feud. An assassin crept into my own kitchen to poison a feast I was preparing. I killed the s'wit with my own cleaver.

I did, indeed! But grateful? No. Turns out that spilling blood during a feast day is taboo among the Starsingers. I ended up here instead—that's another tale! But, enough idleness. Watch yourself there.

Aye, and I never want to leave. I come from the River-Elks—a clan of many tents, the other wilders say. But even so there are ten times as many people in Markarth. \n\nEvery day I see people I've never seen before. This is where I mean to stay.

Something to do with stars, I expect. How that might lead us to the entrance to a Dwarven ruin, I have no idea.\n\nI think better out there among the rocks and trees, though. We'll see what we see and sort it along the way.

We'll find something, that's for certain. In the Reach, treasure can mean all sorts of things. A plump cave bear is a treasure to a hungry clan.\n\nBut as for silver, you won't find a better metal for killing vampires and werewolves.

Then they'd better lace their foot-coverings tight, because they'll find no peace in the wild. Every wolf, hawk, and red-eyed stag heeds the Hunt-King's call.\n\nYou see? Reach alliances have teeth. Your Ravenwatch friends better not forget that.

It means what it means. We're tied to each other now. What happens to one happens to both.\n\nThinbloods make alliances with ink and parchment. We do it with fire, and oath, and spirit-signs. I think you can guess which practice is stronger.

You know, I thought so myself. Made no difference to the ard. But, I'm not giving up. I'm sure Ard Caddach will think of someone else in need of killing tomorrow, and I'll get my chance.\n\nFor now, more cider!

Prove myself to Ard Caddach and join his Stonehands. He said he'd give me an empty house for my own if I killed a nearby bandit  and brought back his head.\n\nTurns out someone else had killed him already. No head, no house.

Because Rada had not yet raised a new army. And he had other preparations to make, no doubt. Centuries don't matter much to immortal vampires.\n\nNow, hold up the intact insignia. Let's see if we're right and it grants us access to the Dark Halls.
I admit the thought has crossed my mind. But we would be trading one master for another. Besides, allowing the Dark Heart to awaken … that's not something I want to risk.
I leave the course of your journey up to you, but these three will go ahead to assist you.\n\nLyris to Understone Keep, Gwendis to the Nighthollow Archives, and Fennorian to Bthar-Zel.

Not who, what. Song-keepers. Glory-tongues. They remember the people of the clan.\n\nEvery leader that falls, every warrior that bleeds—the vateshran knows them all. Each who survive the Rites earns a vateshran song that will last forever.

Ah, a shame. Thank you, friend.\n\nWe were in the middle of the Saga of the Cloud Ghosts. I must learn to accompany him when we break for food. Otherwise he'll never re-learn how to tell his clan's stories.

Aside from clan protection? Why, all their stories, of course! I think I'm getting the better end of this deal even with my student disappearing with growing frequency.\n\nPlease excuse me as I continue looking. May your own tale grow in the telling!

Yes, at their request. I found this clan on my way here, and for the price of a tale, they let me stay in their camp.\n\nI'm a much better storyteller than their clan lorekeeper, so we struck a deal: I teach him how to tell his clan's stories better.
I've traveled all over the Reach. I know it like the back of my hand! Yet, I haven't even been called before Ard Caddach for so much a how fare you.

Haunt? You say that as if I make you hear the screams of children or cause blood to pour out your eyes.\n\nNo, I choose to stay. The sisters do a fine job, but they really enjoy their cryptic instructions. I like offering more understandable guidance.

First and finest. I watched as Carinar the Sharp slew his father, sundering the Quicktalon clan in twain. When Carinar chose to move his people south, I joined him. As we marched, I sang of his triumph and strength. In return, he named me vateshran.

The Defiler's realm holds sway within the Wounding. All manner of creature devoted to Molag Bal crawl about, looking to stab you in the back.\n\nI also hear it can get cold in there. Though, I only ever feel cold these days. On account of being dead.

Wild, savage, kind of smells bad—Hunter's Grotto lies beyond the green portal. Hircine, our Lord of the Hunt holds sway within that wing. Expect to meet all manner of beasts that you must slay to complete your task.

I hope that you can withstand some heat. The Deadlands seep into our world beyond the red portal into a wing I call the Brimstone Den. Mehrunes Dagon's creatures must be cleared out to proceed through the Rites.

You must know the songs of the Father of Torment. He Who Schemes in the Shadows. Molag Bal grants nothing but unexpected pain.\n\nThose of the Reach who venerate him appreciate the lessons he teaches. They grow resilient in his shadow.
The traitor who ruined Varen, the Empire, and nearly all of Tamriel. Just thinking about him makes my blood boil.

No. Not good at all. The Darkstorm requires power on an unprecedented scale. Darkness that will cover the Reach and send every mortal soul it touches into the Dark Heart. In turn, the power of the Heart will flow through the orrery to feed the storm.
The count enjoyed his mysteries, but yeah, I think so. When we started this, I thought the best we could do is pay al-Saran back for the lives he stole. Guess I should have set my sights higher.

Perhaps the Binder in the Dark can clear it from the Hollows. She specializes in controlling otherworldly intrusions.\n\nIn the meantime, I think staying clear of it might be the safest course. Never met a problem I couldn't ignore!

I certainly hope not, but they've been gone so long ….\n\nIf you run into my other apprentices, offer whatever aid you can. And if the worst has happened, I would be grateful if you could retrieve the symbols they carry and return them to me.
We Timbercrows have had our differences with other clans, sure, but we came here with a mind to help.\n\nPerhaps he's just suspicious of everyone. Huh. Let me ask around. Thanks, stranger.
Yes. Or, at least I think he does. My clan chief made sure to say something when we arrived. Does he not trust our clan? That's what I'm worried about.
That's what I said, isn't it? Were you not listening?\n\nAh, never mind me. Few of my clan remain, and fewer still outside seem to understand.

Our relationship with the land and the Daedra does not have so clearly defined rules. It could be anything from a whisper of thanks, or returning seeds to the dirt. \n\nIt's not as complicated as you might think. Consider it while you're in the Reach.
The land provides, and everything it provides, it expects payment for. If you use something, you must give something in return.

Each clan's got their own idea about how to fight, that's what's going on. The Eagleseers want to find glory in open battle. The Wildspears are looking for plunder. And my own Treeshade clan hunts the hunters.\n\nThe story of the Reach, it seems.

Getting two clans to agree on the same path is hard. Half a dozen all at once? It can't be done.\n\nThe best course might be to let each clan do what it does best. Give each chief a task that suits their nature, and try to point them at the Gray Host.

I think the Treeshade way of war makes sense. A pitched battle would get a lot of people killed, but just stealing from the Gray Host won't chase them away. Fight smart—but fight, I say.\n\nI just wish more Reachfolk saw things as we do.

What? Absolutely not. Once the bear had regained his strength, he turned to leave. That's when I slit its throat.\n\nMy family ate well for days. And the pelt made a nice cloak. Never let a good bear go to waste.

No. Rada is my problem to deal with. I need you to save Markarth. Maybe if the deaths stop, the Heart will return to its slumber.\n\nI'll delay Rada, try to buy us time. I can't overpower him, but I may be able to reason with him. We were friends once.

The majority of Rada's troops here in the Reach are new recruits. He doesn't have that many experienced commanders to rely on. Besides, Lady Belain has a vested interest in sacrificing as many lives to the Dark Heart as she can.

As we learned in Nighthollow Keep, Belain's clan of vampires can only feed on the energy of the Dark Heart. As long as it slumbers, her people remain starving beasts.\n\nIf she can complete the massacre of Markarth, she can fully awaken the Heart.

The Lothid is an ancient clan of vampires. Older even than the Ravenwatch. They turned more troublesome in recent years. Ever since Boss Trenlor took charge of the clan.\n\nHe drives them to perform unspeakable horrors while terrorizing the locals.

Must Adusa paint you a picture? Boss Trenlor has appetites that he forces the clan to satisfy. Murder, torture, extortion. These are some of the clan's crimes. And now this one hears rumors. Tales of a prison where mortals are kept like cattle.

If the meeting goes well, Adusa will signal you to join her. If not ….\n\nThere is a good chance this one will be tossed into the deep prison. If that happens, you will come to my rescue, yes? Either way, we should learn where they're keeping Kathad.

It looks like an ancient Dwarven prison, but this one has no idea what the Dwarves kept down here. Now, Boss Trenlor uses it to hold mortals to feed upon, as well as members of his own clan that displease him.\n\nHe truly is a monster.

It will tear the Gray Host from Molag Bal's clutches and preserve them for eternity in his sanctuary realm. Death will become as much a petty inconvenience to them as to any Daedra. They will become truly immortal.

To end the Darkstorm once it's begun, I need to enter Rada's sanctuary realm and take control of the ritual.

I can't ask you to join me, but I won't dissuade you if your course is set. 
Just know that I can't guarantee we'll be able to return.

You need to get past the clan members to reach Trenlor's throne. Then just drop the mushroom into his chalice of blood. We'll take care of the rest.\n\nYou'll need a disguise, though. Lothid celebrations are chaotic, but they'd easily spot an outsider.

Freyleth says the darkcap will work instantly. Weaken Trenlor so he's more like other vampires. Then Freyleth will launch the final stage of her plan.\n\nShe'll challenge Trenlor for leadership of the clan.

The Lothid clan hates Boss Trenlor. They're just too afraid to go against him. Once Freyleth issues her challenge, they'll probably cheer her on. I know I will.\n\nIt's almost done, friend. Do your part and trust that we'll do ours.

I didn't see her, but I wasn't able to advance very far into the undercity. Since you're obviously on your way to help her, and I've delivered all the messages I had, I'm going back to the Library of Arkthzand.

I hate that Verandis has a past, but he is an ancient vampire. I can't expect him to have remained alone for centuries until he met me. His connection to Rada al-Saran, though. He needs to be careful. His feelings are going to get him into trouble.

Kathad will join the Ravenwatch, I suppose. He has an annoying streak of morality that matches their temperament.\n\nAs for Adusa, I plan to keep the Lothid clan out of her line of vision. I'd rather not find ourselves in conflict any time soon.
If this is a trap, you're the one walking into it. But if he does return to the orrery while you're gone, I will buy whatever time I can.\n\nUntil then, there are things I also need to accomplish.

Rada is a prideful man. When I deserted the Gray Host, it wounded him deeply. He wants to prove that I was wrong to doubt him.\n\nWhat he doesn't understand is that I never doubted what he could accomplish. I just feared what it would cost.

Now that you mention it, yeah. And come to think of it, Mannimarco spent time there with his Worm Cult. He's the backstabber who caused the Soulburst and helped Molag Bal plant his Dark Anchors.\n\nRumor has it, Caddach welcomed him with open arms.
You're saying they used this plant to create that storm that started all this? Even more reason to put a stop to whatever they're doing down here.
I know that! Would it kill you to offer me a little reassurance?\n\nPromise or no promise, I'm counting on you to bring him home.
I think we've all spent enough time dwelling on my past. I know what must be done.\n\nAll that remains is that I must do it.

Those words keep returning to haunt me. They never fail to make me feel foolish—both for having said them and for doubting them.\n\nThings may look hopeless from here, but there may be a better vantage on the other side. Only one way to find out.

Without a doubt. Rada's plans, whatever they are, will prove catastrophic to the mortal realm if allowed to proceed unchecked. I hope I can talk to him. Appeal to his better half and make him see reason.\n\nIf not, I'll do whatever I must to end this.

I was able to study the keystone briefly before Rada and Belain snatched it away. It's a faceted stone bound by a metal band. Obviously of Dwarven design.\n\nI'm not a Dwemer expert, but the keystone … it could have a thousand different uses.

I reached that same conclusion, my friend. Let's get over there and find out, shall we?\n\nAnd if the opportunity presents itself, perhaps I can get Rada to see reason and abandon this destructive course he's set for the Gray Host.

Well, it shares some similarities with Ayleid welkynd stones, but as far as I know, the Ayleids and Dwarves had little to do with each other. It's puzzling.\n\nMagicked stones often serve as power sources, as well as keys and even weapons.
