The source of these shadow beings. These shades. I sense a corruption … a void.\n\nThe longer I'm close to it, the more I suspect it may be the very thing that drew Rada and Lady Belain here in the first place. Stay alert, my friend.

Initially? Not even a little. There are a lot of things I've been meaning to do with Sai that should keep me occupied for a few weeks.\n\nAnd when we do get restless, I have a knack for stumbling into the next threat to the realm. We'll be fine.

Hey, I enjoy saving the world as much as the next hero, but even I have my limits. I want to spend some time with the man I love, traveling and doing anything that doesn't involve hitting somebody with my axe.

Lyris wants to relax. See the world while we're not trying to save it.\n\nShe also mentioned that she wants me to sharpen her axe and polish her armor. Her most peculiar smile, though, makes me suspect there's more to these chores than she let on.

So far, so good. He has skills and a sense of honor that will serve him well.\n\nThis one hoped to let Gwendis take him under her wing. Finish his training. But as usual, the little one sees a toy to play with instead of a brother to assist.

Kathad has much training to complete before he can take his place as a fully functional member of the Ravenwatch. Oh, he has the skills and the proper outlook, but he needs time to hone those abilities and learn our methods.\n\nHe will work out well.

If you say so. Hopefully, once I prove myself, they'll accept me as a true member of the family.\n\nIn the meantime, I'm trying to remember everything Adusa tells me. I want to make sure she never regrets coming to my aid. Or you, either, my friend.

Adusa says they're my sister and brother now. Fennorian seems nice enough, if a little too scholarly for my taste. Gwendis, however, she's intense. None of my actual siblings ever looked at me the way she does. It's … disconcerting.

I have lived a very long time. Even by High Elf standards, I am ancient. I confess, I often embraced the routine as a distraction from the gnawing dread of my curse. Many times I sought a home, a family, and a cause. \n\nYet I never remain for long.

It was not always my choice. Seeing the lengths that Rada went to save the Gray Host makes me question my commitment. Did I ever fight that hard for those I loved? Or did I just convince myself I had to move on because it was easier to start over?

You don't know of the Gray Host? Count yourself lucky. Vampires, werewolves, and witches, all gathered under the banner of a master they call the Ashen Lord.\n\nThey're trouble for anyone traveling the Reach.

I should think this whole affair taught you that nothing lasts forever, but it seems to me the people are ready for this peace. I don't think it'll crumble easily, so long as ambitious fools aren't permitted to chip away at it.
That I have, that I have. Many times during the vast span of my life, though not in some years. This city never changes, only the occupants.\n\nPerhaps that will change now, should this peace hold.

Better, much better. There's still a pall that hangs over her to the rest of the townsfolk, but at home we're beginning to feel more like a family again. She even smiles now and again.\n\nYou've got enough arse kissing to endure, but … I'm grateful.

Hah! Normal in Hjaalmarch is no spring jaunt. Sure the milk drinkers in Solitude might think of Morthal as a dull town, but there's always some thing or another trying to kill us.\n\nMy wife's home dealing with some matter of killer wolves as we speak.

Bah, it's not an uncommon thing for packs of dire wolves to make off with livestock. My soldiers haven't been able to deal with them with all this Gray Host madness.\n\nNext time you're headed to Morthal, lend my wife a hand and you'll have my thanks.
This is no time for such dark jokes, outsider! Not when so many run for their lives.\n\nYou … did joke, aye? Nah, of course you did.
I don't appreciate those sorts of dark jokes. Not when I have my family's life at stake.\n\nThankfully you only jest … right? What am I saying—of course you do.

Let's not stretch the bounds of reason. There'll be no shortage of bickering and cursing in our future, but there's trust. So long as we both want what's best for the Reach, that'll do.\n\nBest see to him now, I can see him casting glares our way.
Just find an active ritual site and destroy any witch pikes and gray reliquaries in the immediate area.\n\nMake sure you bring allies with you, though. Those sites are heavily guarded.

No, some of those defending the Bangkorai Garrison showed interest, but most of them were only seeking a less hazardous post. The Pyre Watch has no need of layabouts and cowards. We must be eternally vigilant. Perhaps I will try Kvatch next.

Of course you do. Just find a ritual site and destroy any witch pikes and gray reliquaries in the vicinity. \n\nTake allies with you, though, or expert or not, you won't last a moment. Those sites are heavily guarded.

Ard Caddach, self-proclaimed ruler of the Reach. He rarely ventures out of Understone Keep these days. I've come to offer my assistance, but he refuses to listen.\n\nMeanwhile, even here in the shadow of the city, Gray Host agents plot and conspire.

An alliance of vampires, witches, and werewolves bent on slaughter and conquest. I want to protect the Reach, but to do that, I need to uncover the Gray Host's plans and secure Ard Caddach's cooperation.\n\nWould you be willing to help me in this?

I shall wait around here and continue to discreetly learn what I can about the Reach and its people. I also want to think about Arana and her rebels. Maybe there's a way to add them to our arsenal.\n\nGo. I'll be here when you get back.

Yes. So my ward Fennorian has told me. Which is even more of a reason for you to help me here in the Reach.\n\nWhatever Rada al-Saran began in Western Skyrim, I believe he has something even more terrible in mind for the Reachfolk.

Rada used the orrery to focus the Void energy. He created a portal to travel somewhere, but the specific destination eludes me.\n\nHe did say he needed to gather his exarchs, the original warlords of the Gray Council. The leaders of the Gray Host.

Yes, but he's finished with Markarth and the Reach. I think he got what he wanted from the orrery and the Dark Heart. At least for now.\n\nDon't worry. I'll figure out what else he has planned. And together we will deal with it. When the time is right.
An immediate one? No, I don't think so. With Rada gone and Lady Belain dead, the Gray Host forces here in the Reach will eventually break up and fade into the shadows. Eventually.

Oh, you know. The usual. Rada al-Saran opened a portal to who knows where. Verandis came back to his senses and tried to stop the orrery. I ran around looking for something to break or stab.\n\nThe usual.

Rada al-Saran mentioned it and Verandis confirmed it. Once the orrery started spinning, Verandis had a stronger sense of the darkness. The Void.\n\nSince I didn't feel anything, he thinks it must be tied to his past with the Gray Host.

Yes. Whether through the use of the orrery or some other means, Rada tied the Void energy to the Gray Host. And due to my past affiliation, that seems to include me.\n\nI can feel it. Hear its dark whisper. I need to ponder the implications.

We bury our dead and get back to enjoying our rights as free men and women of the Reach.\n\nThere's a place in Markarth for those who want it. And those who decide to live in the wild? Well, I won't stand in their way.

I'll send my Stonehands after any of those monsters that still linger near my city. As for stragglers who take to the hills, I'll let the wilder clans deal with them.\n\nI know a clan or two who might be eager to collect some claws and fangs.

I'm going to sharpen my sword. And wait.\n\nIf you and the noble plan to fight the Gray Host, I won't stop you. But remember—Markarth is more than Dwarven stones and high walls. It's strength. Make Arana understand that. That's how you can help.
I did say I'd sell you the map to Bthar-Zel, but I'm not sure I could determine a fair price. The map is extremely rare and valuable, as I'm sure you know.

Aye! More than cover it! And here's your map.\n\nLeads right to Bthar-Zel, I guarantee it. You might need to search around to find the entrance, but that map will get you close. Now, please, I have so much work to do before I can open the shop.

Certainly you saw her on the way in? The Binder restrains the bleed between this realm and Oblivion. Without her and the other sisters, the great spirits would overrun the Hollows.\n\nThe effort makes her a bit off. But I hear she makes a great stew.

You didn't hear it? A woman, distant. But also somehow in my mind. Which I didn't realize could happen to a ghost.\n\nThis might be the first time since I died that I feel nervous. I don't care for it at all.

Voidstuff. From between places. Some witches of the Reach wish to control it, empower themselves with its energy. They transform into a voidmother, like you saw.\n\nThe sisters will keep the infection at bay. Such is our duty to the Spiritblood.

I'll send crafters to gather some. We'll fashion it into weapons. Arrow-tips, coated blades.\n\nWe have a few metalworkers in the clans. Use what's on hand to survive, same as always. Silver hurts the Gray Host, so we'll work with silver.

Dwarf magic is hard to hold. It's so clean. All straight angles, no frayed edges. It's unnatural is what it is.\n\nThe keystone might open a door … but more than that. It's eager. It doesn't just want to open. It wants to … activate something.

I sought to make the world a better place. I thought the Gray Council could help, but when it became the Gray Host ….\n\nI formed the Ravenwatch as an atonement. For things I failed to do. Friends I failed to save—from mortals and from themselves.
I hardly have the words to do it justice. The hut isn't far away. Meet me there and you can see for yourself what a terrible mess my manservant has made of things this time.

As an adventurer and treasure-hunter, ancient structures such as this are my bread and butter. These Argonian pyramids exist as historical curiosities, a glimpse into a long-ago age.\n\nAll reports indicated that this location was safe and intact.

We have the ability to mask our condition from mortals, but it takes a powerful vampire indeed to hide from another of our kind. As much as I hate to admit it, Belain fooled me.\n\nI can tell you this—she's unlike any vampire I've met before.

All vampires carry the stain of Molag Bal. It's the inescapable reality of our condition. But Lady Belain, I sensed something else inside her. A vacant darkness.\n\nStill, if I can speak to Rada, perhaps we can settle this without bloodshed.

No. That would be ridiculous. My Stibbons—the real Stibbons—is still mucking about in the xanmeer. That's where I left him after he triggered this curse.\n\nI went to get help when one of these … duplicates … followed me to the shrine.

There were seven Stibbonses last time I checked, but now there are only six! One of the duplicates is missing! They don't listen any better than the real Stibbons!\n\nWill you find it and bring it back here? I'll try to keep the rest contained.

Obviously. They just keep coming. From the xanmeer. It's some sort of side effect of the curse.\n\nThe priest of the shrine insists that an outsider caused this, so an outsider needs to fix it. Now—oh bother!
Don't we all.\n\nI'll tell you what I can, but much of what's happening is a mystery to me as well. Probably because I haven't had my afternoon tea yet. Stupid manservant.

I'm only certain about what they are not. They aren't illusions, and they aren't exact copies of Stibbons. They could be constructs of some kind. They don't eat, drink, or sleep.\n\nBut a construct of Stibbons? And a poor copy at that? Whatever for?
I have no special insight into the minds of these things. About the only thing they seem the least bit interested in is … well, me.\n\nAnd, no, I have absolutely no idea why that may be.

So far, there are the six you see here and the one I need you to locate.\n\nEach of these emerged from the xanmeer after an interval of time. I expect that if we do nothing, more will appear. But trust me. One Stibbons is more than enough.
Must find … master ….

Goo? That makes no sense. Are you quite certain?\n\nNo matter. I've had enough of this nonsense. I managed to get these duplicates under a modicum of control, but they seem to be rejecting my commands. Like some outside force has agitated them.

A master? Other than me? That's it! Whatever curse Stibbons contracted, whatever these duplicates are, and whoever this master is—they have raised the ire of Lady Clarisse Laurent!\n\nCome on, we're going.

Back to the shrine. Nisswo Somarz knows more about this than she's let on. If she won't talk to me in anything other than riddles and proverbs, maybe she'll talk to you.\n\nWe need to make her tell us how to fix this.

They'll be fine. How much trouble can six Stibbonses get into? Unless they start exploding, too. But that's a chance we'll have to take.\n\nNow come on. If we don't break the curse, gods only know how many more duplicates I'll have to deal with.

The legends say that a dryskin sorcerer entered the xanmeer long ago, when my people were foolish enough to live in such places. He sought a path to immortality.\n\nHe unleashed dark magic that seeped into the swamp and nearly destroyed all life.

The shiny-headed one is the sorcerer's prisoner. He serves as the template for the sorcerer to make more servants. Servants that will stop at nothing to break the seal.\n\nCuriously, the long-haired dryskin seems to distract them from their duty.

The shamans of the region banded together. They managed to seal the sorcerer away, deep in the xanmeer.\n\nBut then this dryskin and her shiny-headed slave arrived. They damaged the seal. Now the sorcerer seeks to completely break it and escape.

Legends say the sorcerer came from a distant land. That he enjoyed poking at roots that are better left buried.\n\nBeyond that, we have done our best to forget him. The secrets that he sought are dangerous, both for those with scales and those without.

With the seal in place, the xanmeer was just an empty pile of stone. Now that a portion of the sorcerer's power is free, I fear his malign influence has corrupted the once-vacant halls.\n\nI suggest you be on your guard and ready to defend yourself.

There are many of them, are there not? Let the duplicates fend for each other while you and the long-hair return the xanmeer to how it was before she arrived.\n\nFrom what I have seen, I expect you will run into more of the duplicates once inside.

Right. Anyone with an army that can help us. You head to Leyawiin. I'm sure Captain Rian would be happy for the Ivory Brigade to lend a hand.\n\nBeyond that, what about anyone else you helped here in Blackwood? Anyone have any soldiers they can spare?

If that's the case, just alert Captain Rian after you talk to the Ambitions. Then head directly to Fort Redmane.\n\nBut if you have the time, go help some people. The fate of the world's at stake. Someone may join up in exchange for a good deed.

I know the place. It's an old Imperial garrison, isn't it? I passed by it during my travels after Varen's forces released me from my vault. \n\nA fort is more defensible than Gideon, anyway. I see the logic. But aren't you coming with us?
I swear to protect the twins in your absence. I took Xynaa at her word, and it nearly cost Calia and Destron their lives. I'll die before I put them in danger again.

Not yet. I think I may have gotten it right this time, however. I built something that will outlast me. The Ravenwatch are able, caring, devoted. I raised them well.\n\nIt's comforting to know I have somewhere to return, even if only occasionally.
They are my family. You as well. I had not confided in anyone since Rada, until you took up my cause.\n\nI … I would like to bequeath my name to you, if you will have it.
Then it's in good hands.\n\nThank you for coming to visit, my friend. This little chat has dispelled some of the gloom hanging over me.

Perhaps it does possess life of a sort. Certainly it holds a vast amount of power. Power enough that we can't allow Rada or Lady Belain to get their hands on it.\n\nCome, my friend. Let's continue our hunt.

The duplicates are the key, as it were. I did a thorough study of this hall. One of the side alcoves contains a floor plate. A switch, I believe. When the doors were open, the switch wasn't important. Now that the defenses have been engaged ….
That explains the reports I received from my scouts. Increased and flagrant Waking Flame activity in the countryside around Gideon.\n\nI take it Vandacia knows the Ambitions are there?

Governor Keshu is wise. Gideon isn't as defensible as Leyawiin. A battle inside the city limits will cause untold damage and deaths among the common folk. \n\nVery well, mercenary. The Ivory Brigade will stand with the Black Fin Legion.

Command a duplicate to wait in that nearby circle of flowers by the water's edge. Then go and give that vine-tongue across the way a good, swift kick.\n\nWith any luck, the vine-tongue will reach out and drag the duplicate to the other side.

Oh, I'm certain of it. Just get a duplicate to stand on the floor plate and the doors will swing open.\n\nA confident command should be enough to get a duplicate to obey you. Just keep the commands simple. Tell them to follow you or wait.

The briarheart change is a sacred ritual. A warrior endures terrible pain to become a briarheart, but gains great strength and endurance. It's a willing sacrifice to defend the clan.\n\nBut the Thornroot Hagravens are using it to make an army.

If we're being totally honest, I'm as nervous as the last leaf on the tree on the final day of fall. I'm a walk-in-the-woods, loose-an-arrow-at-your-back, fade-into-the-trees kind of adventurer.\n\nAn all-out war? That's not my style.

Whew! I mean, I knew that! It just makes me feel better to hear you say it. When Vandacia shows up, we'll kick his arse from here to the Abecean Sea and back!\n\nNow, you should talk to Governor Keshu and see where she thinks we'll do the most good.

Right. No guarantees in war. Still, it makes me feel better to know I'll have you fighting with me. And the legionnaires and brigadines, of course!\n\nAnyway, let's get to it. Talk to Governor Keshu and see where she thinks we'll do the most good.

You must be new in the Reach. The Gray Host is a horde of vampires and werewolves and Icereach witches. They fell upon our land this season, and they kill any wilders they catch.\n\nIt's been getting harder and harder to stay out of their claws.

I want you inside the fort, near the guardhouse. That's where we'll place the Ambitions for safekeeping.\n\nIt will be up to you to deal with any cultists that get past us until we can send soldiers to assist you. And remember, they have portal magic.
This switch unlocked the door closest to it. I need you to proceed into that section of the xanmeer and find the floor plate that opens the main passage.

I have more than enough to spare and you'll need one if you come across another floor switch. Just look for the blue fire.\n\nOtherwise, don't be concerned for my safety. Years of adventuring have honed my skills to a razor's edge.

The mark of the Dark Brotherhood, just like with Farrul Lupus.\n\nEr, sorry. I'm working for Councilor Lovidicus, the head of the Chamber of Legates. I came to Leyawiin to warn him after I stumbled across some secret concerning the Longhouse Emperors.

It relates to something called the Four Ambitions of Mehrunes Dagon. I think they're Daedric weapons, but I'm still puzzling that out.\n\nI was working for Farrul Lupus before he was murdered. Found a strange tome with Daedric markings at his behest.

Yeah, that's what brought me here. I found a list of names. Farrul Lupus and members of the Elder Council. It said they all knew something about this secret. Since Farrul was murdered, I figured the others were in danger, too. Looks like I was right.

Like I said, it all started when I found that strange tome for Farrul Lupus. And Emperor Leovic's journal. It was in code, but I got it translated. Sent me to a few hidden Imperial caches where I learned that the Longhouse Emperors had a secret.

Technically, I am a Dremora. But, yes, my origins are Daedric.\n\nI was investigating the activities of these followers of Mehrunes Dagon when I ran into … an obstacle. It pains me to admit it, but this requires a mortal's touch. I need assistance.

Take this amulet. I went to great trouble to acquire it. With it, you should be able to shatter the ward and open the hidden storehouse.\n\nWe must find the secrets locked inside before the Dagonists do. The fate of your world hangs in the balance.

An Imperial cache lies beyond that concealed doorway. Unfortunately, the entrance has been warded to prevent anyone, including those of my kind, from passing through.\n\nI require a capable mortal to shatter the ward so we can see what's hidden inside.

Portals opened all around us and Daedra poured in without warning! Sombren grabbed Calia and Destron and blasted their way out of the fight.\n\nWhen you arrived, my cousins and I were doing our best to cover their retreat.

Verandis stayed in Blackreach. He was going to head into the Library of Arkthzand and attempt to stop Rada al-Saran from doing whatever it is he's doing with that ancient orrery.\n\nBetween that and Belain coming here to lead the Gray Host army ….

You'd think so, right? But Verandis was adamant. Said Rada al-Saran was his problem. He wants us to save Markarth.\n\nIf we can keep the Gray Host from killing everyone, maybe the Dark Heart will go back to sleep. Wouldn't that be grand?

The Gray Host army here in the Reach consists of mainly new recruits. Rada al-Saran doesn't have that many experienced commanders he can rely on.\n\nBesides, Lady Belain has a vested interest in sacrificing as many lives to the Dark Heart as she can.

That's what Verandis told me. The Nighthollow vampires can only feed on the energy of the Dark Heart. As long as it slumbers, Lady Belain's people remain starving savages.\n\nShe wants to complete the massacre of Markarth and fully awaken the Heart.
Oh, hold on, hold on. I have it written down. Ahem.\n\n"By decree of his majesty, Jester King Emeric, the tyrannical would-be usurper, King Boar, is to be put to death in the Arena!"

You must be fun at parties.\n\nYes, you just go over and wrestle that giant illusory pig like an idiot while we all watch. Plus, the audience ticket sales will help finance the festival expenses for years to come. Are you in or not?

The Porcine Potentate himself!\n\nOh, don't put on a face. It's all a gag for the festival. The conjurers call up a phantom boar for the games. You're not actually killing a big, cute, bristly piggy. This is Jester's Festival, not the war in Cyrodiil.

Nothing I want to waste your time with, but I learned of a few places the Worm Cult used to stay in town.\n\nThey're long gone, but maybe I can figure out what Mannimarco has to do with this and why it interests Rada al-Saran.

Verandis always tries to see the good in people, but any good Rada al-Saran had dried up a long time ago.\n\nLook, someone needs to help Verandis, and you have to find Arana and deal with Lady Belain. Maybe when you're finished, you can come join us.

According to my very rough translation, we can't simply repair the seal and lock away the sorcerer again. The Argonians employed ancient rituals that I know nothing about. I doubt the local priest knows them either. \n\nThis all happened so long ago.

Let me see them. Hmm. A collection of apparently mundane items, at least on the surface.\n\nBut look at this scroll. It not only bears the seal of the last Longhouse Emperor, it has been ensorcelled so that it cannot be unfurled or read. Interesting.

It marks a location in Grahtwood. Ne Salas. Another ruin. And perhaps another annex. I'll open a portal to take you there.\n\nKeep the amulet. It retains power enough to deal with a few more wards. While you search, I shall try to read the scroll.

Architectural plans, from the looks of it. And not the mundane engineering so common to your world. No, these plans include powerful Daedric elements.\n\nSome sort of vault, obviously. Strengthened and enhanced by a complex arcane matrix. Intriguing.

Aye, I suppose so. Can't just lop off her head after she got it back. Wouldn't do for morale. Unless she's determined to keep up her fight with me, I'm willing to put the past to rest.\n\nBesides, I already made peace with the rest of her rebels.
Bah, if you must. Can't have you thinking me ungrateful.

Based on the information contained in the carvings and some logical assumptions, I believe the sorcerer needs hands to finish breaking the seal—hands he gave up when he opted for gooey immortality.\n\nThe Stibbons duplicates fill that purpose.

Any surviving Nighthollow clan members are bound to the Dark Heart. As it wanes, so will they. When you destroyed Lady Belain, you sealed the doom of her entire clan.\n\nThat threat is ended forever, thanks to you and Arana.

Interesting question. We've seen that most of the duplicates swarmed around me for some unimaginable reason. And you ran into a few corrupted versions.\n\nIt appears that no matter what form Stibbons takes, he never quite seems to get the job done.
I was beginning to suspect as much!\n\nVery well. Tell me everything that you have learned. Leave nothing out. I want to hear it all.
Extremely well. We were rivals as well as colleagues on the Elder Council. It was that way between all of the councilors, I suppose.\n\nHer death is a tragedy, however. I will miss her.
Lupus? Emperor Leovic's old steward? And Jirich as well? Gods, they are targeting the Elder Council!\n\nAnything else? Tell me. The slightest detail could mean the difference between life and death.

The Ambitions? I heard that term once before, years ago. I must go to Tidewater Cave. I have a cache hidden there and I need to check my records.\n\nMeanwhile, I suggest you find Jirich's files. She kept them in a hidden compartment in her nightstand.
Danger? What are you talking about? Does this have something to do with that letter?\n\nAnd who are you, by the way?

My husband, Velan, received a letter from an old friend this morning. Farrul Lupus, Emperor Leovic's steward. I could see that whatever was in that letter upset him, but he didn't want to discuss it and I didn't push him.\n\nNow, please, go find him.

My command of ancient Yokudan is elementary at best. I assumed it had something to do with harrowstorms until Rada al-Saran mentioned this Darkstorm.\n\nI think he's planning something massive. More massive even than the storm over Solitude.

Braden said there was a mysterious Redguard looking for me. The way he said it, my first thought was Rada al-Saran found his way back, too. But no. Just Sai trying to surprise me. I punched him extremely hard. And then I hugged him.

Skyrim is a nice place to visit, but I need to see what's over the horizon. And yes, I think that Sai wants to go with me. The Skald-King can spare me for awhile. Besides, he owes me.\n\nWhere will we go? Somewhere far away. Maybe back to Skingrad.
The power emanating from the lingering magic is … intense. I think this trinket was specifically prepared to reveal the image we just witnessed.\n\nBut is it a message for us … or for Count Verandis?

You know, Velan acted strange after the letter from Farrul Lupus arrived. He didn't tell me what it said, and I never asked.\n\nBefore he left today, he gave me a sealed scroll. Said to give it to Councilor Lovidicus if anything ever happened to him.

A scroll. Sealed and bearing my husband's stamp. Take it. Give it to Councilor Lovidicus. I hope it helps catch whoever murdered my husband.\n\nI'll summon the town guard. They'll help me with … with my husband.
That's what I was trying to find out when Caddach got all angry and said something about my head and a pike on the wall.\n\nLook, you talk to him. Maybe you'll have better luck than me.
Oh good. This keeps getting better and better. I thought I was finished with Mannimarco's insanity a long time ago. Shows you what I know.\n\nGo on. I'll catch up to you.
Let me see that. Hmm. That's a code, all right. Some of the other documents I found used something similar.\n\nYou know, I'm really starting to hate all this secrecy surrounding the Ambitions.

Possibly. I oversaw the Imperial treasury, so my records deal with expenditures and collections. I have documents going as far back as Emperor Moricar. Possibly even Durcorach. And I know I saw that term someplace.\n\nI will see what I can find.

I'm almost certain of it. And Councilor Lovidicus knows my brother. We talked about him a bit when I arrived. If there isn't a qualified scribe nearby, I can send for my brother.\n\nLet's go to Leyawiin Castle and talk to Lovidicus.
I can't help feeling that once we solve the secret of the Longhouse Emperors, we'll know how to stop the Dark Brotherhood from murdering any more of the councilors.\n\nI'll see you at the castle!

Good idea. We need to report in to Councilor Lovidicus anyway. Let him know what we uncovered. If he has a qualified scribe, great. If not, I know someone. They helped me with those other documents.\n\nLet's go to Leyawiin Castle and talk to Lovidicus.

A Reach city? No, never. But come to think of it, Mannimarco spent time there. He's the backstabber who betrayed Emperor Varen. Rumor has it, Caddach offered sanctuary to the necromancer.\n\nI wonder if this has anything to do with Mannimarco.

We must find where the Sul-Xan are keeping it first. It will likely be somewhere of great importance to them, and heavily guarded.\n\nI just pray we are not too late. There has been so much death already.

That's the black hand, symbol of the Dark Brotherhood. I wish Jirich and Sophus had allowed me to assign brigadines to protect them. At least Faleria, however reluctantly, agreed to a military escort.\n\nDid you and Eveli uncover any other information?

On paper, Countess Caro rules Leyawiin, but in practice, the Chamber of Legates governs the city. Legates Tebeza-ko and Am-Halu, and Councilor Lovidicus, they handle day-to-day tasks. \n\nMe? I'm commander of the Ivory Brigade, Leyawiin's militia.

Councilor Jirich was a member of the Imperial Elder Council, back when we still had an Empire. Now her title is mostly ceremonial, but she continues to assist the legates by serving as an intermediary with the local nobility.
It appears that Councilor Lovidicus's trust in the Wood Elf was not misplaced.\n\nVery well. You and Eveli can head in and talk to the councilor.
Damn it all to Oblivion and back! I should have taken Farrul Lupus more seriously when I received his letter. This is definitely the mark of the Dark Brotherhood.\n\nAnything else to add to this?

Sadly, no. Whatever Leovic confided in Farrul Lupus and the others, whatever he ordered them to do, he kept it a complete secret from me.\n\nI suppose he assumed I wouldn't go along with anything illegal or Daedric, and he was right.

Abor has always had an affinity for the Imperial military. When she received her letter of warning from Farrul Lupus, she sent word to me. Told me she was going to the fort. That the soldiers would protect her.\n\nI fear she's badly mistaken.

Yes, that's the Longhouse Emperor's code. Only a handful of Imperial scribes can decipher it. I know one. Beragon. I'll send for him at once.\n\nMeanwhile, we must warn the remaining councilors on the list: Abor, Faleria, Itinia, and Vandacia.

Very good. I've sent messages to Itinia and Vandacia already, as neither of them are currently within Leyawiin's jurisdiction.\n\nI need you to go to Fort Blueblood. Councilor Abor has taken refuge there, but I'd prefer to have her here in Leyawiin.

Not long ago we started hearing chanting and strange lights coming from this abandoned mine. We discovered this cult had moved in.\n\nThen, people began to vanish. They'd go on hunts or out to trade, and never return. Soon half the village was gone.

I had long planned to visit Skyrim and learn about their long history with the Dragons, to help in our battle against them. When I heard that Lyris was here, fighting a sword-saint no less, I decided now was the time make the journey.
All right, enough! I can see when I'm being overruled.\n\nVery well. I give you permission to enter the watchtower. Councilor Abor's safety is now in your hands.
I was. Never left my post. Opened the door for the servant myself.

The councilor demanded we protect her. Said her life was in danger, but refused to give me any details. Imperial confidentiality, she insisted. Above my station.\n\nI put her up in the watchtower and assigned a couple of brigadines to guard her.

Yet here I am. I wish I had an answer, my friend.\n\nI remember that fateful day in Coldharbour. Death dragged me down into darkness, but then I awoke at the Abbey of Blades. The rising sun never looked so good to my battle-weary eyes.
A portal appeared in our village this morning and out she stepped. Most of my remaining neighbors ran and hid. Sensible, considering.\n\nBut something inside me said I should talk to her.

I needed to rest, rebuild my strength. Besides, Kasura required help with the abbey. When the Dragons invaded Elsweyr, I knew it was my duty to fight against them. \n\nI've been searching for the wisdom of the ancient Dragonguard ever since.

Who would remain behind that could stand against Rada? I fear that even together we would be hard pressed to stop him. We'll need every advantage for the end battle, should it come to that.\n\nPerhaps if I can learn how to call upon the darkness ….

Yes, I'd probably do the same if someone threatened my brother.\n\nHave you seen the sky outside? One Ambition gave Vandacia enough energy to merge the entire fort with the Deadlands. What could he do with another Ambition or two?

Right. Should it concern us that he can read the book and it was all gibberish to me?\n\nMaybe the whole reason I found it and carried it all this time was so I could give it to Sombren now. Maybe he's meant to use it to stop Dagon. I hope that's true.

I can't explain how being an Ambition works. I don't really know myself. But I can sense things that are like me. That have the same taint of Dagon upon them. This book practically reeks of it.\n\nI think this is the Mysterium Xarxes.

Xynaa's contracts mentioned it. The rites it describes allowed Vandacia to imbue us with a portion of Dagon's energy. I think he took a little for himself along the way, which is why he's so powerful.\n\nI want to try to take that energy away from him.

I'm not sure we left Blackwood. The two realms are merging around this fort. We could be on Nirn. Or in the Deadlands. Or maybe someplace in between.\n\nIf I can weaken Vandacia and you can destroy him, that might break the connection and set us free.
But … but … my brother! And my parents! Vandacia has to pay for that.\n\nYou were supposed to protect us. You were supposed to save Destron!
Then let me help! Sombren has been holding me back. I don't care if I lose control, so long as I take Vandacia with me.\n\nFind him. Keep him busy. I'll make sure he pays for Destron.

Using my auramancy, I turned the magic on the orrery itself.\n\nI've learned much about how the orrery operates. It is quite fascinating. I also ascertained the approximate location of Rada's laboratory, but a more thorough search is required.

As I approached, she demanded to know the location of the Waking Flame. I explained they took our people into this mine. That's when she offered her deal.\n\nI don't know why I said yes. I'm not a fighter. Maybe I'll die in here. But I have to try.

I've never entered this mine before. This place is cursed! It closed down long before I was born, so I have no clue where they could be kept.\n\nHopefully they're not in too deep. I just want to find them and run as far as I can.

Our village petitioned the Tribunal to send troops to clear out the cultist but they refused. They are too busy dealing with the plague to help. As a result we sent our finest warriors to clear it out.

Rada al-Saran was an Ansei of great renown. A legend to rival Leki herself. The sword-saints are a lost legacy to my people. It's a shame that al-Saran did not devote himself to restoring that honorable tradition instead of his monstrous Gray Host.
Lyris has promised to show me some of the Dragon Cult's ruins and barrows. With good fortune they may help us learn more about our foes in Elsweyr. I will return to my duties there soon.

What—no! Never! You are always welcome in our company. Good companions are hard to find!\n\nDon't let us keep you from your moment of honor though. There will be plenty of time to share stories after all the accolades.

Since we met last, I dedicated myself to destroying the associates of Mehrunes Dagon. This is how I know of the contents of the lockbox and why I am here. But I say too much.\n\nI wouldn't want to worry a mortal such as yourself.
You may call me Lyranth. I know that most Dremora like myself behave maliciously toward mortals, but I promise you have nothing to fear.\n\nWell, unless you find a way to upset me.
I admit I don't know much. They sprang from nowhere. The trail that I followed of the item I seek led to this mine. But where they come from stays a mystery. That is exactly what concerns me.

I didn't believe it either. Nearly took him for another Daedric trick and lopped his head off. Luckily, the real Sai has the stamina to keep up with me.\n\nI'm sure you have questions. Better you speak to him about it yourself.

My ancestors must be burying their heads on the Far Shores at that suggestion. Vampires would be better suited to this eternal vigil than we mortals, but it is our duty. Still, we have similar goals to the Ravenwatch. Perhaps a partnership would do.
Yes, well, it would be ungrateful of me to go without giving my thanks to Fennorian again. If his fellows are as honorable, then introductions may be in order.

There was a pair of them—an Argonian and a Wood Elf. Said they were infiltration experts. Burglars more like, but that's what I need. I didn't ask them too many questions. Couldn't afford to turn help away. Still can't.

They've been gone a long time. Either they've abandoned the job or been found out. If they were captured, I'd expect the Painted Eye to react but it's been quiet. Too quiet.\n\nFor all I know those two emptied the larder and took off for a picnic.

That's right! Seeks and I were on our way to rescue those hostages when we—uh, got separated. I was supposed to get to safety since things got a little hairy with the job, but now that I have my trusty deputy there's nothing to worry about!

Er—well, not exactly, but what's wrong with using our skills to do a little good while we're here. Besides, the commander pays well, so even Seeks couldn't argue with that!\n\nFreeing the hostages will be easy with you here. Once we find them ….

He did? Well, that was considerate—hey!\n\nAre you saying he doesn't trust us to finish the job? Sure, things haven't gone according to plan, but they never do. Seeks and I always come through in the end!

Seeks-the-Dark? He's my mentor. Shows me everything there is to know on the job. He's a bit on the … grumpy side, but he'll be happy when history remembers him as the wise teacher of Lady Twilight, the Thieves Guild's greatest legend!
Oh—darn it—I wasn't supposed to say that. Forget I mentioned it. It's not important!\n\nWhat's important are hostages! And … how to get to them.

Well, we were … in the area and heard about Borderwatch's troubles. Seeks and I are no strangers to getting into fortresses, so we volunteered to save the hostages.\n\nThe sewers were supposed to be lightly patrolled. Not exactly true.

Yeah, I guess Farrul Lupus was right. We did need that strange book.\n\nIn fact, I think I was meant to give it to Sombren. I couldn't read a word of it, but he cast spells from it like it belonged to him.

Sombren did good, that's for certain.\n\nAnd honestly, I'm glad to be rid of that book. Sombren seems to know how to handle it safely. I think it would be dangerous in the wrong hands. And I for one don't want any more bad dreams or waking visions.

Tangled roots, Sombren did good! And I don't want to take it back. Those dreams and visions would have driven me crazy eventually.\n\nI think Sombren's a good steward for the book. He can keep it safe so it doesn't fall into the wrong hands.

Nope. Vandacia made this personal, but I try to not make a habit of killing people for free. It's bad for business.\n\nYou do what you have to. Me, I'm going to find a nice mammoth steak with a side of vegetables smothered in scuttle cheese sauce.

Hey, I never claimed to be a hero. And despite our success today, I don't want to face Daedric threats on a regular basis.\n\nThen again, who knows what tomorrow will bring? Seeing you in action, I'm sure you'll turn up on a contract eventually.

Damn it! I guess that explains why Tenarei knocked me out and tied me up.\n\nOf course that … idiot … Quistley would gamble away more than he had in his coin purse. He's done it before. Usually begs his parents for help, though.

The Golden Anvil was said to have once been unremarkable iron, worked tirelessly by a pious smith to build a simple trading post. Zenithar transformed the anvil to gold—blessed with divine prosperity—for that honest labor and the abbey was born.
Easy to say, hard to do. Still ….\n\nSo many people fought to protect me today. Even though my heart is broken, for their sakes I'll find a way. Destron would want me to.

I hope so. Not just for my sake, but for the other Ambition, whoever they are. Without Destron, they and Sombren are the only family I have left. I'll try to be there for them. I really will.\n\nFor now, we're heading back to the temple if you need us.

For now, but I don't think it's over. There's another Ambition to find. And I can't imagine Mehrunes Dagon and his followers leaving us alone after all the time and planning that went into creating us.\n\nI think we'll head back to the temple for now.

I … I'm not sure. It belongs to Eveli, not me. I'd like to study it. See if there's some way to free the Ambitions and change our destiny, but I know it's also dangerous.\n\nLet me think about it a little more, then I'll talk with Eveli.

Daedra spin great lies from small truths when it suits them. I know that now. It was Xynaa's last lesson to me.\n\nWe won't join him and I won't let him kill us. We just need to come up with a way to keep any of that from happening.

It could have been worse. We did well against the cultists. They were not trained soldiers. And when Mehrunes Dagon appeared, we faded into the mud and grass. Dagon did more damage to his own minions than he inflicted on our forces.

When a fire rages, my neighbor's hut is my own. That is Argonian wisdom. We defend ourselves by defending our friends.\n\nThose who died today died well. We do not mourn them. We will celebrate their sacrifice and cherish our victory back in Gideon.

That seems to be the long and short of it. I'm sorry we couldn't stop Vandacia from murdering Destron, but at least we took care of that rotten tree stump in the end.\n\nDespite all that, I feel pretty good. It's not every day I get to save Tamriel.

Most likely. It's well known that Gavos hid the anvil away before he was overthrown, but nothing seemed to indicate that it was removed from the abbey. With Zenithar's grace and some hard work, perhaps we'll have better luck finding it.

As I've said, the abbey was once a great bazaar, but that alone didn't make it special. Here, people of all kinds exchanged not just objects, but ideas, pieces of their culture. They saw the foreign as something to be valued.\n\nSadly, it didn't last.

Those who valued coin more than commerce infested it, until their greed utterly corrupted Zenithar's Abbey. Gavos Douar and his ilk destroyed this wonderful place with their avarice.\n\nNot even the anvil was enough for him, it seems.

I ought to just let the Dark Elf have him, but it would be … dishonorable. I better see if we can catch up to her. \n\nI'd like to leave her tied up and empty-handed when I drag Quistley out of here by his arrogant nose.

You are not familiar with the Resolutes of Zenithar? We are keepers of the Resolutions, the temples, of the Divine Provider. We offer succor and instruction to those who provide honest labor or wealth. Those who follow our teachings prosper.

The foundations of civilization and prosperity: labor, commerce, and exchange. Zenithar smiles upon those who work for themselves and others. Through fair and honest trade, we better the world. The teachings show how best to conduct business.

Then you know the deal. From what I've heard, the Painted Eye separated the hostages into groups throughout Borderwatch.\n\nRisky, but unfortunately, they've got the numbers to manage their occupation and guard their captives. Damn revolutionaries.
Powerful merchant-clergy who organized the trades of the abbey's bazaar. They were the ones who lead the abbey to great prosperity, before Gavos seized power.

We need to find the hostages. We need to get them out of the fortress. And we need to keep the Painted Eye from realizing what we're up to.\n\nThat's three jobs, and three of us. If we work together, we'll get these people out.
A Painted Eye patrol cornered me after I sent Erilthel away from the fortress. I convinced them that I was just a dung-shoveler for the garrison. Seemed better to be a hostage than get gut-stabbed.

Well, once the Painted Eye took hold of the fortress and rounded us up, they sent demands to Commander Axius, right? Political stuff—releasing prisoners across Tamriel, turning Khenarthi's Roost into a free port. Big, bold asks.

I'm not surprised. You could be sitting on the Ruby Throne and still have problems doing everything they asked.\n\nBut that's the point. I overheard some Painted Eyes saying the demands are a ruse. This group doesn't care about politics at all.

That I don't know, but they're definitely trying to drag out negotiations for as long as possible. I'm just glad the commander was wise enough not to trust in dealing with them.\n\nThank you for releasing us.
Just don't wind up taking our place. I'm afraid I'm no good for a reimbursement rescue.\n\nEight grace your path!

And once we're clear, the brigadines storm the gates? Fair enough. But you better move quickly.\n\nWhatever these Painted Eye thugs are doing here, they're getting close. That's what some of my guards were saying, at any rate.

They're searching for something in the fortress. I don't know what they're expecting to find. I've worked this forge for years and I've never seen anything here worth all this trouble.\n\nThe Painted Eye must know something about Borderwatch I don't.

That's just what I've been able to piece together from the snippets I've caught. It sounds like whatever they're looking for, it's big. But hard to find? The more I hear, the less it makes sense.\n\nI just want to be done with this mess.

Hmph. I only took it easy on these mercs because I was surrounded. Now that there's an escape, I'm taking it. Any Painted Eye I can't avoid will see what four straight years of hammering have done for my arm strength.

They do? They do! Then—then—then what are we supposed to do? If they catch us trying to escape they'll probably drag us off like that scholar—and Arkay knows what tortures these radicals are putting him through!

One of the other hostages! Said he was studying Ayleid history. When the Painted Eye caught wind of that, they couldn't haul him off to the keep fast enough.\n\nLet's get out of here before they come back!

You—you—you want me to what? By myself? No, no, no, please, please, please—I'm not a fighter. I'm not even sneaky. I'm just a stable hand! If you leave me, it's only a matter of time before the Painted Eye puts my head on a spike!
They split everyone up! I think they took some of the others to the guard tower and the smithy? I don't know where they rushed that poor scholar off to though.

An Ayleid—damn. So these Painted Eye bastards really are after it. Never is such a thing as coincidence.\n\nIt's time I come clean. Erilthel and I didn't travel to Borderwatch just to play heroes. We came to do a job for the Thieves Guild.

That's … mostly right. Somewhere beneath this fortress is an Ayleid ruin. One the garrison doesn't know about. \n\nErilthel and I were hired to steal a relic from it—a powerful one. And it looks like the Painted Eye's here for the same damn thing.

Not sure. The Mer who hired us to steal the thing sure was afraid of it falling into the wrong hands, though. And I think these Painted Eye nutters qualify.\n\nAt least with Erilthel safely out of the way we only have the relic to worry about.
It was a High Elf. Called himself something ostentatious … Relicmaster Glenadir. That was it. Didn't strike me as the world-conquering type. And with all the jobs I've worked—trust me. I can tell.
Then you shouldn't have any trouble picking up one more.\n\nNow, do you mind? I need to educate this dunce on the finer points of self-preservation. Again.
The leadership of the Painted Eye seems to be holing up in Borderwatch's keep. I imagine that's where they'd wring information out of a hostage, if what you heard is true.

I think that's very likely. An adytum is a sacred place within a temple. Only the clergy are permitted within. It would have been within the arbitrator's authority to keep it locked and guarded, even from the trade-ministers. His personal sanctuary.

So it would seem. If the adytum remains sealed we'll need the three sigils mentioned here to open it. They were last in the possession of the abbey's three trade-ministers, that we know of. We should search their holdings.
How did this ruin suddenly become common knowledge? It took me, Teldundindo of Sunhold, years to even learn about its existence … fine, what do you need?

Beneath Borderwatch's crypt, I believe. Specifically, beneath the tomb of the keep's architect—though I don't know which tomb is hers.\n\nForgive me, but … I told all of this to the Painted Eye. I had no choice.

There was one thing I never volunteered to the Painted Eye and they didn't know to ask: the crypt is locked tight. I instructed Commander Axius to lock it up so no one would disturb the location while I conducted my research. Not that it matters now.

Why wouldn't he? I am Teldundindo of Sunhold. When I say there is a discovery that will put a backwater like this on the map, the wise man listens. Thankfully, Commander Axius is smarter than his occupation would indicate.

I found accounts of Phalevon's burial in a shining mausoleum on a hill outside Leyawiin. He was laid to rest with his arms and armor—relics of his many victories.\n\nThis is the place. But Goblins infest the caverns. And Minotaurs, too.

The stories say that Phalevon had the most beautiful mail, impervious to sword, arrow, and spear. We don't know much about armor of his era, but he was known as the Magnificent. I can only surmise his armor was quite splendid!

Phalevon's sword was so sharp it was said to be able to cut the air itself! No, that isn't right … I suppose any sword will cut air.\n\nAh, that's it! This one could cut through armor like air—that's what I was told!
You mean the one Erilthel turned into a couch cushion? I don't expect the buyer is going to pay us for her sculpture of the Two Moons.\n\nThe job's a wash.
I'll tell them what I tell them for all of my jobs: as little as possible.
What are you, a lawyer?\n\nGo on and get your gold before I change my mind about our cut.
That's the big climax! I mean, I'd discourage any unflattering references to falling on my arse, but you can't pay for a debut like that!

Well, I was helping the great Teldundindo, tip toe through the sewer when we come across this huge rat. That ninny started shrieking in a pitch so high the rat must have thought it was a mating call, because it went tearing off after him!

Sort of. So the rat had him cornered, but I killed it! Took some doing—like I said, big rat. After the commotion was over I heard yelling coming up from a grate nearby. That spooked Teldundindo. Again. He ran off, so I decided to follow the voices.
Of course! I'm not going to become the greatest thief in all of Tamriel by sitting on my duff, will I? I mean, you saw what it did back there. That's an arse of action. Be a waste of great potential!

As I said, the cultists used their slave labor to unearth a Mehrunes Dagon shrine. Now they prepare to perform a great ritual. For what purpose, I cannot tell.\n\nHowever, I do believe the ritual involves sacrificing mortals Drathas cares about.

Thank you. Something inside of me just poured out. All the anger at what we've seen. And the hatred for these abominations.\n\nI know I can't fight as well as you, but I hope I can pull my weight while by your side.

I've met no one by that name, but that doesn't mean he isn't here somewhere. The only non-cultist I've seen in days was a Dark Elf who sneaked by a short time ago. She motioned for us to wait, and left without a word.\n\nI … I should go.

What's there to know? They worship a god of death, darkness, and primordial chaos. Nothing good can come of that.\n\nQuistley's always getting into trouble, but it usually involves love or dice. He could be in real danger this time!

Allowing Quistley to be dragged off to angry criminals is not much of an improvement. While Quistley might deserve it, I can't let Tenarei Vels get him, either.\n\nI want to try to grab one of these cultists and get some answers.
It's a long story. Suffice it to say I owe his family a great debt. \n\nQuistley and I were more or less raised together. The Silvelles count on me to watch out for him. Or help him if he needs it.

That's what the Silvelles say when they need me to help him. But he's their son. I'm just someone they raised. \n\nForgive me if I sound ungrateful. They took me in and made sure I was clothed, educated, trained. They didn't have to do that.
I've lost count. He does as he pleases. Unfortunately what pleases him seems to land him in hot water. Every time.\n\nThis, though? How Quistley stumbled into a cult's clutches, I can only guess.

Right. Says that's located near Blackwood Lake. It also mentions some sort of event. And I think both Amnis and whoever sent this letter are part of the Order of the Waking Flame.\n\nActual Dagonists right here in Gideon! Can you imagine?

Sounds like getting to the event requires a voyage and a special coin of some sort. Since we don't have a coin or an invitation, we should go to the Salvitto Estate next.\n\nI think it's to the north of Gideon, near Blackwood Lake. I'll meet you there.
All right, all right. Yes, Vandacia was here. Stopped by for a visit with his new charge. But he's long gone.\n\nPerhaps if you hurry, you can still catch him.

No one outside the order is allowed … oh, all right! I can see there's no reasoning with you.\n\nTake my invitation. And my coin. You'll need both to get on the ship. The Calamity. It's leaving from Leyawiin docks shortly.
Well, prisoner, actually. He stopped by to show him off. Gave me a preview of his big event.\n\nPlease, I—I shouldn't be telling you any of this. It goes against our code!

Let me see that. What a strange coin. The symbol on it … it looks like the symbols in the book I'm carrying. Here, you better hang on to the coin.\n\nAt least we know how to get to Vandacia's event—wherever it is.

Absolutely. Let's meet in Leyawiin. According to the invitation, the event requires formal attire, so we'll need to visit a tailor before we head to the docks.\n\nI'll meet you by the big tree just inside the city gates after I deal with Salvitto.

Nope. The invitation says we need formal attire to attend Vandacia's event.\n\nWhen I dropped Salvitto off with Governor Keshu, she suggested we'd be able to get what we need at the tailor's shop here in the city.

A formal event? I say, we don't usually get clientele of your caliber seeking outfits from our formal line. Adventurers, am I right? Perhaps I can direct you to my colleagues. They handle our extensive collection of protective armor.
Eveli? She found Farrul's book? Oh, that's wonderful news!\n\nBut why is Eveli standing way over there? And why are you talking to me instead of her? What's this all about, stranger?

It all goes back to Leovic's secret. How he hid the Four Ambitions right before Varen killed him and took the throne.\n\nWe thought the Ambitions were Daedric weapons, but they turned out to be people! Vandacia wants the power they contain.
I know. I trust you. Just let me know where I can find you later if you decide to leave the city.

My spymaster reports a flurry of activity that is troublesome. And Gideon is not the fortress it once was. Even so, my Black Fin Legion will give as good as it gets. Better even.\n\nWhat most concerns me is the possibility of treachery.

Vandacia's family is powerful and has deep roots in Blackwood. His spies and political allies fill Gideon like wine fills a goblet. And not all of them are cultists, at least not openly.\n\nI fear the enemy we cannot see more than the one we can.

Of course, of course. We have a small selection of formal wear and alterations are part of our service. Unfortunately, such attire usually requires a noble's purse, if you catch my meaning.\n\nIf funds are short, perhaps we can come to an arrangement.
Quistley Silvelle? He belongs to Lalais now. She is the Daughter of Sithis, and none dare defy her! Leave while you can—you're fools if you think you can save him from her.
Not completely honest? Just what are you implying? Is Eveli attempting to change the terms of our deal? Farrul offered a fair price for what he asked her to do!

Quiet! If certain ears heard those words, our lives wouldn't be worth a horker's blister!\n\nI suppose it's time for Eveli to meet Farrul. We have a house here in Riften, around the corner from the bank. Just knock two times or he won't respond.

You really think so? Thanks. You look good, too.\n\nSo, you be the noble and I'll be your escort. With these outfits, the invitation, and the coin, we should be able to walk right up and board the Calamity.

Some Dark Elf they caught. Even now she faces the Death of the Crystal Fangs in the next chamber.\n\nLalais herself presides in the Fane, below. I … haven't been invited there yet, so I don't know for sure where it is. Now let me go! Please?

Right. Just act natural and no one will suspect we don't belong at Vandacia's party.\n\nBut don't expect me to run, dodge, or loose arrows while wearing this. It isn't exactly made for sudden movements.

I don't know. We want to avoid drawing too much attention to ourselves. We don't want anyone to figure out we're not actually supposed to be here.\n\nI guess we could talk to the other guests. See if we can learn anything. Just be careful, all right?
Then we should find our berths and get some rest. We want to be ready when this ship arrives at its destination—wherever that may be.

No. Look around. He brought these people here to show them he's in control. That he's got power and the favor of Mehrunes Dagon.\n\nI think we need to explore this place and figure out what he's got planned before he reveals it to the world.

Well, according to the last couple of nobles who headed off the ship, we're somewhere in the Deadlands, the Oblivion plane of Mehrunes Dagon!\n\nI guess Vandacia really didn't want anyone interrupting this event.
Same place the rest of the nobles went. Off the ship and that way. There's some sort of keep over there. That must be the place.

Our powers grow exponentially once we leave the protection of the vaults. It's what they were constructed for. But Calia's power has advanced much faster than mine did. It almost consumed her.\n\nIf not for my mentor, the same would have befallen me.

I don't see why not. Plus, it will probably be safer if the three of us leave for a while. There's an old shrine northwest of here. Let's meet there.\n\nI suggest you tell your Wood Elf companion where we're going. She seems like the sort to worry.

When Duke Varen's forces came through, they set me free. To them, I was just another political prisoner. I wandered without a purpose for a time until my power reached a level similar to what you saw here.\n\nThat's when my mentor found me.

My gift is fire. Summoning flames is as natural as breathing. In the vault, it was always just a spark or a simple flicker. But when I tried to hit the target ….\n\nI couldn't control it. The fire inside me, it wanted to grow. To spread. To feed.

I'm fine. A bit light-headed maybe. Whatever Sombren did, it put the fire out … at least for now.\n\nI don't like this. What if next time I summon the power, no one can help me extinguish it? I could hurt Destron. I could burn Gideon to the ground!

Why do you think Emperor Leovic had those vaults constructed? They contain and limit our power. Without them, the power would grow and expand until it destroyed us.\n\nThe vaults were supposed to keep us alive long enough to learn to control our power.
She was able to train me. She also had a method for suppressing my power until I could contain it on my own. Without her, I wouldn't be here today.\n\nShe can help Destron and Calia. I'm sure of it.
Right, about that.\n\nObviously what I thought I knew and the truth aren't exactly the same. Regardless, without the protection of the vault, Calia's and Destron's powers will eventually kill them.
The governor is wise. A moving target is harder to hit than a stationary one. And if we're no longer inside the city, Vandacia's cultists have no reason to attack it.

I wasn't paying attention. My mentor warned me that I was going to be hunted, but I didn't listen. I returned to my old vault to see if I could learn more about who and what I am. The cultists ambushed me. Knocked me out before I could respond.

I was raised in a vault, just like the twins. Isolated, ignorant of the world outside. All I knew was that I was different. Special, somehow.\n\nDuke Varen's forces set me free when I was sixteen. My mentor found me some months later.

She said she had been looking for me. She knew of Mehrunes Dagon's interest in a hidden secret and had been searching for it, but it wasn't until my power began to manifest outside the vault that she was able to locate me.\n\nShe saved my life.

I fell in with mercenaries, wandering and learning to fight even as my power grew. I was beginning to lose control when my mentor appeared. She was a shaman of sorts. She taught me how to master my power, but she never referred to me as an Ambition.

Hardly. The only thing that interests Quistley is himself. Either these Sithis followers hid their true nature to lure him in, or he's so besotted with a woman that he doesn't realize he's in danger. \n\nEither way, I'd better get him out of here.

I'm not sure I believe this sniveling cultist, but we shouldn't let anyone get sacrificed. Not even Tenarei Vels.\n\nLet's split up. You keep going, in case he's telling the truth. I'll see if I can find out more about the Daughter and the Fane.

Which is why we need to get moving! If he has found an Ambition, maybe we can free them. And if it's something else … well, we need to see what it is and figure out what to do about it while there's still time.
There aren't enough of you to stop Vandacia. He has an army of elite soldiers, crazed cultists, and Daedric creatures given to him by Mehrunes Dagon personally. You're hopelessly outclassed.

I don't know. Maybe. My mentor used that term once or twice, but I never paid it much mind.\n\nLook, to stop Vandacia, you need to get me out of here. Find the key to unlock these chains. Kynreeve Dezerog has a copy. His chamber's to the north.

Me? I'm the main event at this infernal affair. Vandacia plans to sacrifice me to his Daedric Prince. Referred to me as one of the Four Ambitions of Mehrunes Dagon.\n\nApparently, they think my death will grant them all unlimited power.
Great, but it's not like we can just walk in there and … wait a moment, that's it!

Take these reekers. They're beetles, similar to dew bugs. Very tasty, though they release a foul odor when they die. I was saving them for later, but I'll get more.\n\nPlace them around the hall. Then, when you give the signal, I'll loose some arrows.

If we can cause a panic, get those nobles to run around screaming, that should create enough of a diversion for you to use that key and set Sombren free.\n\nWe just need to accomplish that before Vandacia gets to the part where he sacrifices Sombren.

That story would take too long to tell. Let's just say I made the mistake of returning to a place where I once lived. I wasn't paying attention. Suddenly I was surrounded by Vandacia's cultists.\n\nThey overpowered me and I woke up in chains.
Yes, I would like to meet these other Ambitions. Find out who they are … what we are. And learn more about this power Vandacia seems intent on taking from us.\n\nLead on and I will follow.

And so I did. I sensed his need and offered my assistance. He learned well and, as he will tell you, I never betrayed him.\n\nIs that why he has summoned me? Because those other two Ambitions now face the same danger that almost consumed him?

Then you must bring them to my sanctuary. They are far more than anything you can imagine.\n\nI helped Sombren because I didn't want to see him fall into Mehrunes Dagon's hands or destroy himself with his own power. I will do the same for the others.

I hide in the Deadlands. Yes, Dagon's realm. But I have ways to protect us. Before you bring them, they must be attuned to this realm.\n\nFind slivers of the Deadlands lodged in your world. Sombren will show you how to use them to attune the Ambitions.

Forgive me, but in my experience, most of Nirn takes a dark view of Dremora.\n\nXynaa found me when I was at my worst. If she wanted me dead, she could have killed me years ago or just let me destroy myself. Instead, she helped me. Taught me control.

I'll describe the process when you return. I need to prepare a portal at a place where the planar boundaries are thin. Take Calia and Destron and gather the slivers. Then I can attune them to the Deadlands. I also marked where to meet me on your map.

Oh, of that I'm certain. Competition in the Deadlands is fierce, especially among the non-aligned Dremora. I know that she seeks allies to call upon when the need arises. Having three Ambitions who owe you a favor, that's like gold to Xynaa.

No, but I never heard of Ambitions either before all this began.\n\nWe're in new territory here. But as long as my sister and I are in danger, I'll take help wherever I can get it. Let's go and find these objects.

Does it matter?\n\nI felt the power inside me when I lost control back at the temple. I couldn't stop it. If Sombren hadn't suppressed my flames, I would have ignited the city! Unless you know another way to fix me, I don't think we have a choice.

Before I can teach them to contain their power, they must first come to understand it. The Path of the Obelisks will help them do so.\n\nThey must visit the three ancient oracles and learn the truths that each will reveal.
I need you to deal with a complication for me.

Creatures were drawn to the hillside by my actions. Could you make sure the path to the top is clear?\n\nThe last thing we need is for some mundane and random threat to provoke a response from Calia or Destron.

House Telvanni is funding a practical test of my latest invention, the Phantasmal Censer. It exorcises spirits, ghosts, and other spectral beings near instantaneously.\n\nThe unquiet dead claim countless lives each season. But no longer!

The porters and assistants I contracted with have been waylaid in Narsis — some manner of food poisoning. I am desperate for an extra set of eyes and hands to help with labor and preparations.\n\nNothing dangerous, I assure you.

Certainly. It's a wedding of Barilzar's theories on the interactions of tonal and spectral forces with a resonance housing of my own design. Activating it should render any ghosts in proximity completely mute.\n\nA clever bit of engineering. I suppose.

Tiras is a junior oathman of House Telvanni. At this point in his education, he's obliged to accompany a spellwright like myself on a few field excursions. Sort of an apprenticeship.\n\nHonestly, in his case, it's just a formality.

When you're on a mission to quiet down restless ghosts, you go where the restless ghosts are.\n\nAngry spirits pile up in these Ayleid ruins like weevils in a hollow log. Vehk only knows why. I've never taken much interest in Ayleid history.

I need you to paint some stabilizing runes around the area to reinforce the censer's magics.\n\nThey're not all that elaborate, I promise. But do be mindful. I'm not leaving anything to chance this time!

Here are the materials and a template. I infused the paint with ground soul gems to reinforce the runes' potency—at great personal expense, I might add! Right, Tiras? There's no price too high for success!\n\nTry not to use it all, all right?

I have a few more calibrations to attend to. \n\nAs for Tiras, he'll probably, you know … observe. For educational purposes. You can speak with him if you have any other questions. Seht guide you, my friend!

The housing I created for the Phantasmal Censer should contain the energies it releases well enough.\n\nI employed a fascinating helical boring technique invented by the Dwarves of Arkngthand! I have all sorts of ideas for—! Sorry, that can wait.

I am Tiras Tirethi, first-born son of Fothas Tirethi and adopted nephew to Magister Therana of Tel Branora.\n\nI can tell by your vacant expression you are not well-acquainted with the current affairs of House Telvanni. No great surprise there.

Finally, someone else makes an astute observation. Congratulations, you've just become the second-smartest person in the room.\n\nThe runes Revus wants painted will have, at most, a negligible impact. They're essentially just expensive vandalism.

Oh, don't be thick. I have nothing to learn from the likes of Revus Demnevanni.\n\nThis is a mere formality. When I ascend to the Council, I will make weeding out hedge mages like Revus my first priority.

Excellent! By the Three, can I just tell you how refreshing it is to hear a voice of support? Thank you!\n\nNow, the next step is a bit more complicated. I need you to assist me with the Phantasmal Censer's kindling sequence.

These magical pylons provide the key. Fair warning, they can be a bit unruly. But the fundamentals are sound! \n\nSpectral energy will pass between them freely, but sometimes the crystals dislodge. If that happens, I need you to re-attune them.

Just pay attention to the energies flowing between them. If no spectral motes pass through one of the pylons, you'll know that's the one that needs fixing.\n\nI should warn you—if you try to attune a functional pylon, you might feel a … mild shock.
Certainly!\n\nJust keep a close eye on the spectral energy leaping between the pylons. If you don't see any energies flowing to or from a pylon, then I'll need you to re-attune it for me.

I am too lowly to speak of my mistress in anything more than euphemisms and hushed tones. She is the darkness in the dead of night, the arcane fire burning in Oblivion.\n\nI am but her humble prophet. If you want to know more, then read the letter.

Honest toil. Zenithar provides to those who work. Just as the seal kept out the war that raged between the trade-ministers, the cracks let in the rain, and the roach, and the rays of the sun. These were my wages for care of the anvil, and prayer.

Oh, I'm no one. I was the arbitrator of Zenithar's Abbey long, long ago. It was my duty to resolve disputes and ensure the safety of the bazaar. I failed, and so this place lies in ruin, but if others wish to learn from my mistakes, I'll oblige.
Oh, these are … perfectly fermented. They are much easier to crush like this and Jad'zirri loves the way they feel between her toes. She can't wait to start her next batch!

I know. I had no defense against their wealth and their poisoned words. The harder I fought to curb their ambitions, the more I became their common enemy. Once I was gone though, they were free to fight among themselves. They tore this place apart.

I barely recognize it myself. Pitted and corroded beyond repair. I did my best to preserve it. Not nearly enough. Its glow began to fade as the abbey became corrupted by avarice, opulence, and depravity, so I hid it away before anyone took notice.

There were good people here. I was the one who was supposed to protect them from the unscrupulous few, but I wasn't wise enough to outwit them. If I'd had more to offer than platitudes perhaps the others would have stood by me. Only Zenithar knows.

It was just returning to what it once was. A simple source of labor for the blacksmith who founded the abbey. Legend held that Zenithar's blessing transformed it. Well before my time. When I became arbitrator it was already radiant, one of a kind.

I suspect as greed took hold of the bazaar, Zenithar lost his faith in us. I hid it away so as not to cause panic, but I think that may have been my greatest mistake. He was trying to show his disapproval and I silenced it. That was my crime.

Maybe Captain Rian or Councilor Lovidicus? Maybe they sent news about Vandacia? \n\nI'm sure that stink-weed is still out there, searching for the other Ambitions. And the twins, too, I suppose. Vandacia won't stop until we stop him.

No. No! You followed my instructions to the letter, and I practically killed myself proving out the theories in my laboratory back home. Literally. My eyebrows only recently grew back.\n\nIt can't just be bad luck. I must have missed something.

Talk to the courier. Find out who sent them and what news they've brought us. I mean, provided you're still willing to stick around and help. Technically, I suppose, you've already finished the job Captain Rian hired you to do.\n\nSo, what do you say?

Something in Veyond—some arcane anomaly that disrupts the function of pylons.\n\nOf course the ruin I choose to work in suffers from some heretofore unseen pylon-scrambling hocus-pocus. Just another day in the life of Revus Demnevanni!

Well, we need to find the source of the disturbance.\n\nTake Tiras and explore the lower chambers. It shouldn't take him long to identify the culprit. Just make sure to keep him safe. If anything happens to him, my kwama is well and truly cooked.

What do I think? What does that matter?\n\nThe Telvanni Council detests my work on Dwemer tonal mechanics. They want nothing to do with my study of rare eggs. The Phantasmal Censer is the only thing I've ever created that won their approval!

Ah, the dutiful and not terribly clever mage. I'll bet he's angry with me.\n\nI took care not to inflict any permanent damage on him. And I fully intended to set him free just as soon as I finish here. It's business, not personal.

The Sul-Xan are Naga who worship only chaos, nothing more. They fuel their madness with horrible rituals and sacrifices, hoping it will bring an end to the world. They are violent, callous, and insane … but I fear their true threat is all too real.

Their rituals have the potential to summon an ancient spirit of destruction. If they cannot use my friends to do it, they will find someone else. \n\nI believe destroying the idol will stop them, but I must first ensure my friends are safe.

Then you understand my predicament. I need Silvelle if I want Larz-Tul off my back, but it's not worth getting myself killed over. Help me get out of here, and I'll help you.\n\nI got a look at a map, so I think I know where you can find Silvelle.

Not much. Larz-Tul suspected that Quistley was hiding out in a smuggler's cave on the coast. I thought I'd have to check them all. Then I ran into your friend Bastian.\n\nI knew there was something off about the smuggler story, though. It didn't fit.

I borrowed gold against imagined winnings, like every gambler ever. \n\nYou ask a lot of questions. Not to be rude, but I'd really rather find Quistley and get out of here. These cultists already tried to sacrifice me once, after all.

He must be in deep, if Larz-Tul is willing to write off what I owe to get his claws on Quistley. Too bad for him, but it's a chance for me to get out of a bad situation.\n\nLarz-Tul makes a good living from other people's mistakes. Or desperation.

Some minor defect in one of the ruin's ritual sites, no doubt.\n\nI've heard that Ayleid ruins often suffer from disruptive arcane seepage—erratic welkynd stones, cracked aetherial wells and the like. A true mage would have accounted for such things.

With happiness, love, and so, so much pent up aggression. Jad'zirri sprinkles her special blend of spices onto her feet and gives the tub of overripe apples a thorough stomping. It is quite joyful. Then she sieves the slop into her still and voila!

Precisely what it sounds like. The meteoric glass forming the stone likely had some flaw. Over centuries, magicka ebbing and flowing through the stone heightens the flaw, causing the glass to cloud and its magicka to radiate irregularly.

She assures you it isn't quite so simple, but to share all her secrets would mean Jad'zirri's special cider would not be so special. Besides, it is her well-seasoned feet that give her brew its unique aftertaste.\n\nHer foot fragrance is familiar, yes?
If he's been here long enough, he must have seen cultists coming or going through any hidden passages. But be careful with him.\n\nI don't trust vampires.

You're an exception to my rule. You saved me once already today. And you haven't taken advantage of the fact that those crystals left me weak as a kitten.\n\nI suppose there are vampires and there are vampires.

I tried to use the Phantasmal Censer to quiet that Ayleid specter, but Tiras panicked and started to banish it with his own magic. His banishing spell mixed with the censer's power, and whoosh! Snuffed out like a candle! \n\nI'm doomed!

Just vanished! Yeah, sure. Just vanished … to the afterlife!\n\nThis is classic Revus, you know? I'm a pox! I just need a moment to think about what I'm going to tell the House about Tiras. And the censer, wherever it flew off to.

Perhaps, but I'd rather not fight my way through half the cult to get to Quistley Silvelle. If there's a passage here it could save us quite a lot of trouble.\n\nGet in, get what you need, then get out. That's how I prefer to do things.

I came here hoping the temple held answers about my condition. But the cultists discovered me as I fed upon an unwary noble from Gideon. The Daughter of Sithis was intrigued, but when she realized I had not yet mastered my powers, she locked me away.

Well … it doesn't, just yet. But we're definitely on to something.\n\nThe censer can banish the stones, and my attunement spell can stabilize them long enough to dislodge them safely. We—I mean, you are one step closer to fixing this.

You! What do you do now! Keep tracking Tiras. I'll try to puzzle out a way to use the censer and attunement spell to restore Tiras's corporeal form.\n\nWe have to move quickly, though. If we don't reach him soon, critical animus decay might set in.
