I am still capable of gratitude, stranger. I just want to be free of this place. I came here expecting something quite different.

First, we need to replicate the original event.\n\nAim the Phantasmal Censer at him and unleash its power. While you're doing that, I'll cast the attunement spell. Weaving the two together should dislodge his animus and restore his corporeal form!
Much less confident than you'd like.

Just what I've heard. She emerged from the Black Marsh swamps and made a name for herself as a freedom fighter. Battled Dark Elf slavers along the Morrowind border.\n\nWhen the Akaviri invaders arrived, she took her soldiers and helped save Windhelm.

Hmm. What did the spinners say … oh yes! It's one of the eight major cities of Black Marsh, but its proximity to Cyrodiil makes it more Imperial than Argonian. In fact, Vandacia represented the Empire in Gideon for decades—until, well, you know.

Now that you mention it, very much so! He was a member of the Elder Council! His name was on the list of people that knew Leovic's secret! I thought I was supposed to protect him. Keep him safe from the murderer. But he was the murderer!

Keshu's progressive, as far as Argonians go. I hear she has an interest in the history of the Argonians, but she genuinely seems committed to creating an open and enlightened community for all people in Gideon.\n\nActually, I can't wait to talk to her!

No, more of an advisor of sorts. Like the councilors here in Leyawiin. Governor Keshu is the leader of the city. \n\nWhen Vandacia revealed himself to be the head of a Daedric cult, well, that pretty much put an end to his government service.

After he killed Faleria and grabbed the coded documents, he ran. He could be anywhere! He's had decades to establish the Waking Flame and set up hiding holes.\n\nBut he's after the Ambitions, same as us. We need to find the hidden vault before he does!

You … you … know about that? \n\nMaybe. Probably. Farrul never told me a lot about his time serving the emperor, but I knew it was on his mind recently. That's why he hired Eveli. He said he wanted to make things right.
A sheet of … oh gods! That's the sign of the Dark Brotherhood! They assassinated my poor Farrul! And all because of something that should have stayed buried with the damn Longhouse Emperors.

Nothing good. I wouldn't go so far as to say that it comes down to bringing Quistley in or taking his place, but it's close. I really need to be free of Larz-Tul.\n\nI barely persuaded him to give me this chance. I won't get another one.

This may sound ghoulish, but … if Quistley is dead, I'd like his signet ring. It's big, gold, and set with rubies.\n\nIf I bring it back to Larz-Tul, it will show that I held up my end of our bargain. And he would take it in payment of my debt.

You know … things! State secrets, I suppose. Hidden dreams, wild desires. Farrul helped raise the emperor. They were close. Or as close as the most powerful man in the world and his steward can be.\n\nOnce, Farrul mentioned another secret.

Ambitions? No, I don't recall any mention of that. Farrul didn't say much. Just referred to something as the secret of the Longhouse Emperors. I got the feeling it had something to do with Daedra worship. And some sort of weapons.\n\nThat's all I know.

Our weepy friend told me that Quistley's quite taken with this Daughter of Sithis. Figures. My guess is he told her his family is wealthy, so she's keeping him alive for ransom.\n\nWe'll probably find them in the shrine they call the Fane of Scorn.

She seems like the sort who expects the worst. I remain optimistic.\n\nI don't always get along with Quistley, but I don't want him to end up sacrificed by the cult. Or turned into some crime boss's object lesson, for that matter.

Knock a gullible stranger over the head one time and earn mistrust for life, eh? I took advantage of an opportunity.\n\nYou know we can't both leave with Quistley. I'll duel for him if I have to. I'm very good with my daggers.

My, ever the optimistic one, aren't you? Very well, I agree that it's pointless to continue this argument until we have Quistley Silvelle in hand. Or his corpse.\n\nBut Bastian should know that my daggers aren't just a fashion accessory.

First, we need to get Quistley out of Blackwood. Tenarei doesn't have anything personal against him—well, no more than anyone else who meets him—but the criminal she'd bring Quistley to might kill him.

Well, that's … that's just your opinion! Everybody here treated me as a guest of honor. And Lalais, the Daughter of Sithis, chose me to be her consort. She told me that she'd give me the Kiss of Sithis soon!\n \nWhy would you ruin this for me?

Years ago, I lost everything trying to get my brother out of a fishy trading scheme. Larz-Tul offered to help me. I'm still paying for it.\n\nIt would be grand to be done with Larz-Tul and to pull one over on him at the same time.

I'll threaten to tell his parents about this whole affair unless he cooperates and goes straight back to Daggerfall. Quistley knows that Lord Silvelle can cut him off. It's the only threat that actually scares him. He would have to earn a living.

Claim me? I am not some sack of flour to be bargained over!\n\nOh, very well. Bastian works for me … indirectly. I'll go with him. I can write a promissory note for the Dark Elf to deliver to her thug of a boss. He's a terrible person.
If Bastian's willing to work with me—and perhaps forget about the knocked-out and tied-up business—I think we might have room for a compromise.

Not going to happen. The Calamity has been hired out for a very exclusive engagement.\n\nAnd I can tell just looking at you that you're not even in the same class as the passengers I'm expecting. So get lost!
Are you, now? And where's your invitation?
Hmm. Salvitto and guest, huh? All right. This all looks to be in order.\n\nWelcome aboard. Make your way below decks and find a bunk. We're shoving off shortly and it's going to be a long voyage.
That about sums it up. Plus the dreams I've been having. Ever since I found that book, I've been having the most strange and disturbing dreams.

Nothing specific. I'm always someplace. A forest, a town. Then the ground starts to shake or fire erupts all around me. Once the place was flooded by a deluge of water. And there are always four animals watching from a nearby hill.

The assassins who follow Mephala? Or are they the ones who serve the Void? No matter. My information actually concerns the secret we seek to uncover.\n\nAccording to the ensorcelled scroll, there is another cache annex beneath the Imperial City.

Oh, not me, little mortal. I have no intention of slogging through the muck and the sludge when you are more than capable of handling that.\n\nI shall catch up to you after you have dealt with the wards. Go on now, and take the Wood Elf with you.

Yes, hidden in the Imperial sewers.\n\nI will open a portal that will get you close to the annex, but you will need to deal with the wards. For all their reverence of the Daedra, these Longhouse Emperors certainly went out of their way to keep us out.

Protect the twins from the dangers of the forest. They cannot unleash their power safely until they have learned to control it. At each obelisk, you will bear witness to the truths they learn.\n\nCome to me when all is said and done. Then we shall see.

See that rope hanging from the top of the tower? Bet my bottom acorn that's how the assassin got in and out. But the missing servant … something about that is knocking on the back of my head.\n\nAnd why would the Dark Brotherhood take those pages?

Tiras is an incredible talent. Of the sort that only appears once in a generation.\n\nWhat's more, his family is extremely well-connected, he lives the Telvanni creed effortlessly …. I wager he'll be Archmagister one day.

Really putting me on the spot, aren't you?\n\nThere are aspects of Telvanni culture I find abhorrent—the practice of slavery being chief among them. We do what we can. When the only alternative is exile … it's complicated.

After many years of fighting, including my time as the commander of the Pact forces in the Three Banners War, I decided I had enough. Shortly after I arrived in Gideon, the governorship became available.\n\nIt is my honor to serve this city.

No. He served the Longhouse Emperors from the day they seized the Ruby Throne, eventually becoming a member of the Elder Council. Since the collapse of the Empire, he has been a trusted advisor, both here and in Leyawiin.\n\nThis news is a shock.

Forgive me if this sounds like bragging ….\n\nI was raised in a tiny village far to the south, but I was never satisfied with provincial life. I longed to learn about the ancient Argonians. To bring some of that civilization back to my people.

Visions? You misunderstand the forces with which you meddle. Given your failures before you died, that doesn't surprise me.\n\nYou entered the portal at the Obelisk of Inevitability in the Deadlands. What could be more inevitable than the future?

You said the same thing when we battled in Blackwood so many years ago. I found your foolish bravado amusing then. I find it even more amusing now. Trust me, it was not much of a contest.\n\nYou died well, if that consoles you.

Look who stands behind me. Look at the throne on which I sit. Mehrunes Dagon may be the master of all Nirn, but he has given me Tamriel as my reward. From High Rock to Morrowind, all bow to my will.\n\nThere is no power in Tamriel equal to mine.

You still do not understand! This isn't your time or place. Here, you are nothing but dust, long forgotten. You are a ghost of failure's past.\n\nAs much as I would enjoy it, I can't kill that which is already dead.

Look around and see for yourself. The very fact that you stand before me proves that you didn't stop me. You didn't save the Ambitions. You didn't save anyone. I destroyed you.\n\nNow this realm belongs to my lord and master, Mehrunes Dagon.

No. Blackwood and the Topal Bay region remain independent entities. We have a trade agreement with Leyawiin, but otherwise we're on our own. We hope the war stays to the north and west. Moreover, we hope it ends quickly.

The Sul-Xan are brutal. They sacrifice their enemies to the dark forces they serve and their thirst for blood knows no bounds. That is why I urge caution as you make your way through their territory. They will show you neither kindness nor mercy.

My explorations showed me the plight of my people. I fought Dark Elf slavers. Raised the Black Fin Legion. Battled Akaviri invaders. I helped form the Ebonheart Pact and fought in the Alliance War.\n\nNow I only seek to govern Gideon in peace.
But you saw how Vandacia looked. Strong, powerful. And Mehrunes Dagon looking down on us. How do we stand against that?

Councilor Lovidicus was right to send you to me. In Argonian, ojel-bak roughly translates as pit of the outsider. There is a natural formation to the south that bears the name. Unfortunately, it lies in territory claimed by the Sul-Xan tribe.

Oh, right, you can't hear it. Feels like we walked right into the middle of an argument. Liable to split my head if they don't settle down for a moment.\n\nI don't know what's got the flora in a tizzy here, but it sounds like trouble.

The Sul-Xan are a savage people, Nagas who revere the forces of death and chaos. You must traverse their land to reach the pit of the outsider.\n\nThe Nagas recognize no authority other than themselves and their leaders. They do not welcome visitors.

I don't … can it really be that simple? Was that the point of these visions? To show us how we were created and to reveal a dark and possible future?\n\nAll right, I understand. Just because the night is long doesn't mean the sun won't rise tomorrow.

Isn't it? You saw the Prince of Destruction! How can we hope to fight something like that, let alone his high priest?\n\nMaybe it's better if we just let our powers consume us. At least then Vandacia won't be able to claim us.

Now you sound like Calia and Sombren. You're right, though. We have power beyond anything Vandacia possesses. That's why he wants us. Once Xynaa teaches us to control it, we'll be unstoppable!\n\nAll right. We're with you. Let's go get this done.
Not your average termites and weevils, I can tell you that much. The kind that makes you scream bloody murder. Never felt anything like it.\n\nBetter be careful.

We're dealing with forces beyond our understanding. It was always going to be a difficult journey. But the Obelisk of Inevitability only shows what will happen if events continue on their current course. \n\nThat future hasn't happened … yet.

The perils of visiting oracles. Are we better off knowing what is to come or continuing on in blissful ignorance?\n\nI believe our choices matter. I choose to resist Mehrunes Dagon, and no vision will sway me from that path. I hope you feel the same.

Green as grass. Why do you ask?\n\nOh, you mean with my head. That's just because of the tree-speaking. Most folks can't hear trees—not really sure about those Argonians—but trees can tell you things if you know how to listen.

A noble sentiment, but they are more than just people. They are powerful weapons. Dagon's priest imbued them with a portion of the Lord of Destruction's own energy when they were born. It has grown and intensified in the intervening years.

Imagine that each Ambition is like a mortal bank. Instead of gold, the priest deposited a portion of Dagon's energy inside them. That energy grew with them, compounding and doubling year after year like interest on your savings.\n\nIt also transformed.

Their power is like a volcano, building until released as an explosion or a lava flow. One is catastrophic, the other merely destructive. I will delay the eruptions while teaching them to dissipate and maintain control.\n\nYou may observe, of course.
Yes, the Order of the Waking Flame has been particularly persistent in trying to run down this secret for themselves.\n\nSpeaking of which, did you learn any more about Leovic's secret?

It's a dungeon beneath her sanctuary. She sends her enemies here to die.\n\nBut we aren't her enemies! She's saved my life many times. If she'd wanted to hurt me, she could have done so long ago. Why turn against me now?

Ah, Talaise. She worries her brother so.\n\nShe asked me where we kept the hot-root flakes. Councilor Abor sprinkles them on every dish. I told her they are in the pantry, but you need the key from the kitchen to unlock the door.

Well, little mortal, your course is clear. We have barely plumbed the depths of this mystery. You must find the people on this list and discover the truth of the Four Ambitions. Meanwhile, I have other avenues to explore.

Interesting. I recall something about that. The mortal who went on to become the first of the Longhouse Emperors attempted to make deals with a number of the Daedric Princes—my own lord included.\n\nAny indication about the terms of this bargain?

I don't want to believe that, but I heard what she said too. And she completely drained my energy. I can't call upon my power until it recharges.\n\nWe need to find a way out of here. We need to get to Calia and Destron before Xynaa turns them over.

First things first. I need to restore my power. Let me think ….\n\nXynaa told me about an old foe she destroyed. Tossed them into this place and kept their skull as a trophy. It may hold enough energy to recharge my power immediately!

The secret's in the leaves. Most folk think communing with nature is all about sitting by streams and meditating, but if you really want to open your mind to tree-speaking you've got to start thinking like them. That's where the leaves come in.

Hmm. Well, you heard Governor Keshu. This is Sul-Xan territory. We want to avoid contact with this hostile tribe of Argonians if at all possible, but we need to reach the pit of the outsider.\n\nAlso … I had another one ….

I want to find the vault! With any luck, we're way ahead of Vandacia and his cultists. Maybe we can get in, grab the weapons, and get back to Gideon before anyone even notices that we're around.\n\nAre you ready?

Nervous? Pshaw! Just look at me. I'm steady as a leaf. Er, steady as a rock, I mean! Even so, I'd prefer that you be the one to use the lantern.\n\nIt's these damned Redguard taboos. Undead spirits and creatures really put us off our appetite.

I think so. This all started when Farrul Lupus sent me to find this book. And that put me on the trail of Emperor Leovic's secret.\n\nNow we know that the secret concerns a deal made with Mehrunes Dagon and something called the Four Ambitions.

Not a lot, really. I've never been up in that area. As far as I know, it's an Imperial city on the Topal Bay. So far, it's been able to keep the Three Banners War mostly away from its borders. Or so the heralds have reported.

They've got to be somewhere!\n\nBesides, we don't know exactly what Vandacia learned when he killed the councilors. Or what he got out of the documents he stole from Leyawiin. We have to assume he's on the same trail as we are.
Just what you'd expect, I imagine. They are blood-thirsty savages who revere death and chaos, after all.\n\nBe ready to fight. That's all I'm saying.

Of course, the Green leaves leaves all around like little invitations. You just got to learn how to use them and open your mind. Then you'll really see all the things you've been missing in the world.

That young woman! She has not returned from the watchtower, so her chores remain undone. And she took the pantry key with her when she went. It is no longer hanging on its hook! That is a clear violation of the kitchen rules. A clear violation.

The pantry is in the cellar, but the door is around the side of the building.\n\nTalaise mumbled something about how the councilor loves hot-root flakes, grabbed the key and the tray of food, and went off. This one hasn't seen her since.

Yes. Absolutely. No one ever said writing the world's greatest romance novel would be easy! Goosebumps or no, I'm going to unravel this tale and put it to good use!\n\nNow then, let's get on with it before I lose my nerve!

She took the councilor her meal and hasn't returned. Did you check the watchtower? Abor's a little old, but maybe Talaise decided to improve her station, if you catch my meaning.\n\nAbor reeks of fear. Maybe Talaise finds that attractive.

Well, she's been acting like a frightened guar since she arrived. Stays locked up in the watchtower. Only lets a single servant in at a time. And I hear she's been burning papers. Documents of some kind. She's scared out of her wits, if you ask me.

Couldn't hurt. And every mystery novel I ever read taught me you should always follow up on every clue. Even the ones that seem insignificant.\n\nLet's check the pantry and see if she was looking for more than hot-root flakes down there.

In Gideon. When I was trying to get introduced to a Hist. Good-natured Argonian warned me which parts of Blackwood were most dangerous. Sul-Xan territory most of all. Nasty bunch. Got nothing but war and slaughter on their minds.

Let me take another look at Xynaa's contracts. Yes, it's here.\n\nXynaa used a holy book to show Vandacia how to create the Four Ambitions. Could it have been the Mysterium Xarxes? She was always loyal to Dagon. She never wanted to help us at all.

Hopefully, they're either still locked in a vault or wandering free like I was. I hate to think that Vandacia captured them while we were busy elsewhere.\n\nI'm … I'm not sure what we should do next, my friend. It's beginning to seem hopeless.

I hope you're right, but I can't see a way ahead from here. If all else fails, we'll destroy ourselves before we let Dagon win. \n\nWe're the keys to unlock the barriers between here and the Deadlands. We can't allow ourselves to fall into his hands.

Whatever Xynaa did to prepare them to be sacrificed, it seems to have dampened their power. How long that will last, I have no idea. But until their power builds to uncontrollable levels again, they should be able to use it to help us.

I'll try to train the twins as Xynaa trained me. If all else fails, I can take them back to the Deadlands. The realm seems to naturally siphon off our energy and keep it at manageable levels.\n\nNot my first choice, but it will serve as a last resort.
It's possible, I guess. But we haven't seen any evidence of that up to this point.\n\nLook, we won't find out any more if we just stand here and talk about it. Let's get going, all right?

I am Duchess Astella of Castle Giovesse.  \n\nAs for the curse, it is the work of a vile trollop named Alizinda. Arkay scorn her soul! My darling boy, Mathen, was infatuated with her. And how did she repay his affection? By murdering him in cold blood!
Sul-Xan. Ambushed the caravan we were with, dragged everyone here. Tried to escape, but they caught us. Killed anyone who resisted. Left me for dead. Put the survivors back to work.
In the heart of the ruin. Where that horrid vine grows. They feed it our blood. Bleed us like pigs.\n\nPlease. Don't let any more of us wind up like—like that ….

Gorging it and letting it grow wild and ravage the native growth, all so they can reap its vines for their nasty alchemy. That'd be horrid enough, but they're using these poor folk for labor and fertilizer.\n\nWe've got to do something.

I cannot bear to speak of it anymore!\n\nMy poor Mathen, I sense his presence sometimes. He's bound to the place where he died. An old cottage northeast of Giovesse—the place where he and Alizinda … trysted.

Yes, tied to a cottage nearby. I can almost picture it. Rustic. Secluded. Tousled quilts, embers smoldering on the hearth …. Gives me the prickles! Almost makes you forget someone likely died there.\n\nSomething she said does trouble me a bit.

The duchess said the lover's name was Alizinda. That was my great-great grandmother's name.\n\nIt can't be a coincidence, can it? She lived in Gideon for a time before moving back to Alik'r. Do you think … do you think my ancestor murdered Mathen?

While it is true that the souls of these Shadowscales returned to the Hist long ago, their remains still deserve peace. Their bones need not become puppets to a madman drunk on power.\n\nBurning them is the only way to prevent that.

I will carry on, as is my purpose as a nisswo.\n\nI cannot say for sure where this responsibility will take me next, but change is the only thing that is guaranteed. Whatever path I walk next will be different from the one I walk now.

A Shadowscale who was said to have plucked out his own eye and sealed a powerful necromantic gem within the socket. It granted him the power to see lost spirits.\n\nTumma-Maxath must have taken it in order to conduct his ritual.

May I? Her anguish just jumps off the page, doesn't it?\n\nSo, Mathen intended to marry someone else and Alizinda killed him in a fit of passion. Can you imagine loving someone so deeply that you end up murdering them? Gods, that's romantic. Sort of.

It's a ring of Mara—the sort of ring used in a pledge of marriage. Mathen might have intended to give it to this mysterious fiancée, or ….\n\nI'll hang on to the ring. Let's use the lantern. Maybe Mathen can shed some light on this.

Curse? Is heartache not curse enough?\n\nMy great love, Alizinda, poisoned me on the very night I meant to propose to her. Someone deceived her—told her I meant to marry another. She killed me, yes, but it was an act of jealous grief, not witchcraft.

I … I do not know.\n\nI've learned that certain objects hold a grip on the soul. Things we treasured in life. In my darkest moments, I sometimes feel drawn to the chapel where they laid my body to rest. I see harsh light glinting off my golden armor.

A magical incantation! The handwriting is different from Alizinda's journal. That means she can't be responsible for the curse!\n\nI knew my ancestor wasn't a sorceress. A murderer, maybe, but not a sorceress! Of course, this all begs the question ….

Yes. And more importantly, why? The person who cast the spell clearly had an axe to grind. Maybe it was a court wizard? Or some jilted witch? My novel's less romance than mystery at this point!\n\nLet's use the lantern again. Maybe the culprit's here!
How is that possible?\n\nIt had to be Alizinda! When Mathen died, the duchy's light died with him. That Redguard wench cast us into darkness! If I could just have brought him back, I could have ….

I cast the spell over his armor and sword, but … it went awry.\n\nI wrote everything down. You can find my notes in my private study beneath the eastern wall. If you find his helm, breastplate, and shield, too, you might be able to set things right.

The fort is under the jurisdiction of Leyawiin's militia, the Ivory Brigade. It defends the main road between Leyawiin and Bravil. We're all that keeps the Three Banners War from spreading into Blackwood.\n\nWe can't lose the fort. We just can't.

A combination of magic, guile, and well-laid plans. They lured most of my brigadines into chasing after an illusory enemy while their main force infiltrated the keep and took those inside hostage.\n\nI'm doing all I can to keep those folks alive.

More than I can name and none that I can grant. I sent word to Leyawiin, but so far I've heard nothing.\n\nThe Painted Eye will kill those hostages if we storm the fortress. I need someone who can get inside quietly and free them. I'll pay for results.

Mercenaries, we thought. Only knew them from third hand accounts in our intelligence briefings. If they were hired to cause this ruckus, we might have bribed them, but their demands read like a credo. They're making a statement here. Damn fanatics.

Pages worth, right there. They've practically demanded I carve them out a sovereign kingdom with my table knife. They're mad if they think I can deliver even a fraction of what they're asking … but I have to humor them. There are lives on the line.

Spell? Some ill-conceived plot to resurrect me, I presume? Mother never could suppress her passion for the occult. Now we both pay the price.\n\nBut even so … I feel something else now. Some other force that nags at my soul. Something fairer. Softer.

My ring of Mara? I had not thought to see it again. I see it clearly now, though—at rest near the heart of the fair Lady Yisara!\n\nThe course is clear, friend. Gather my armor and rid me of the curse. In the meantime, I will bask in Yisara's glow.
No, not from what I've read, anyway. I thought they only killed those whose names appeared on their contracts. I can't imagine anyone asked them to kill a poor servant.

Yes. No? I don't know. We were talking about the councilors. Faleria and Vandacia. Suddenly I had … a premonition?\n\nIt was brief and disturbing and mildly unpleasant. Like the dreams I've been having. But this is the first time while I was awake.

Yes, but we still need to check on Councilor Faleria. And someone needs to go to Gideon and make sure that Councilor Vandacia is all right.\n\nCan I leave those tasks to you? I want to return to Leyawiin and consult with Councilor Lovidicus.

Oh, good point. Before you head out, report to Commander Ortin. Tell him what happened to Talaise. And how we think the assassin slipped into the watchtower undetected.\n\nHis brigadines need to be able to recognize an imposter when they see one.
Because you're a hero and the player character. I have that kind of sixth sense.

Any other day I'd claim to be the lost princess of Pyandonea and regale you with tales of my exploits, but now's not the time for such frivolities.\n\nMy fellows and I are entertainers from the House of Reveries, here to perform across all of Tamriel.

Patching things up with my sister was … easier than I expected. I should have given her more credit. They say you can never truly know another person, but talking helps.\n\nYou should pay another visit. Maybe audition for real this time.

What are you? Some sort of adventurer? Yeah. Yeah, you look the part. Sorry I was short with you. Since Igmund passed, I've had to work twice as hard and twice as long to run the inn. It's done my manner no favors.

Damned fool. He wanted to build a bonfire and drink the night away like we used to. Haven't seen Igmund down mead like that since we were barely men. He lost his legs and tumbled into the fire. Nothing but cinders left by the time I dowsed the blaze.

Not so much of a scrap of clothing. Just black, tarry ashes. Never seen anything throw such a thick black smoke, but it didn't smell like you'd expect. Hair and burned flesh. More like old hay, or musty linens. Wasn't natural.

Folk have been going missing of late, including my sister, Cylle. Never for long, a few days, just enough to plant a worry before they wander back as if nothing happened. But something did. They come back different. Like … everything's unfamiliar.

Weren't her memory. She could recall details down to where she last left the salt, but acted like she'd never tasted it. She'd bring up things I'd long forgotten as if they happened yesterday. Started dredging up old hurts we'd put past us long ago.

Can't say. Felt like she wanted to relive the past. Good and bad. Don't know what would have brought that on. We lead quiet lives now—happy lives, I thought. Led, I suppose. She's gone now. If it was even her in the first place.

You've come about Bugtail. I knew someone would, but my neighbors have kept their distance since he returned. I cannot blame them. I scarcely wished to take him back myself—not after Igmund and Cylle—but I couldn't bring myself to turn him away.

Well, Duchess Astella got them into this situation, right? She cast the ugly spell that cursed poor Mathen. And now, we're gathering up the items she used to make this mistake in the first place?\n\nIt can't be that simple. What are we missing?

Yes. Or rather, I fear I will share his fate. Bugtail rode out to deliver a horse despite my protest. The gelding returned, he did not. Before, I would have been the first to go looking, but I dreaded he'd return—like the others—and he did.

Dead. Or gone … for now. Even the horses could tell something was wrong with him. I fought with this one's reins as he groomed her, but she started and kicked Bugtail. Ink sprayed everywhere. When I cleared my eyes, it was all that remained.

There were patrols, but Seeks and I had no trouble avoiding them. Until we ducked into a niche that was filled to bursting with spiders.\n\nDon't suppose you remember Eton Nir? Well, spiders don't sit right with me since that job. I—well, I went off.

I started stomping around like I was making wine until Seeks smacked me on the head and sent me back the way we came. He went tearing off in the other direction, screaming like a banshee to draw the patrol away. It's quiet now, though.

Seeks and I can slip by patrols! It's just these tight quarters don't leave a lot of options. It was going fine until we ducked into a niche filled with spiders.\n\nJust, thousands of them scuttling around in that hole … I may have reacted a bit.

I'm working my way up the ranks of the Thieves Guild. Well, to the first rank, really. Seeks was put in charge of my training by the Guildmaster until I'm ready to set out on my own.\n\nAnd once I am, the legend of Lady Twilight will begin in earnest!

Maybe. Maybe not. She wasn't a professional necromancer. Maybe she missed something too.\n\nRemember what Mathen told us? Certain objects take hold of the soul. If that's the case, isn't it odd that we found him in the cottage instead of the chapel?

Restless phantoms returning to say their last goodbyes before being spirited away once more? This really is beginning to sound like a ghost story. It's all a little too coincidental, don't you think?\n\nThere has to be a common cause ….

That's the name I'll be known by once I make it big! I just need one huge heist, something that will grab the imaginations of people from here to Auridon. Then I'll be on the lips of every bard! Lady Twilight, the greatest thief in all of Tamriel!

Seeking out a more comforting time, no doubt. Let's hope she hasn't escaped into the arms of a monster.\n\nI'll follow your lead. My expertise in stage combat won't do us much good, but I have a few other talents and tricks up my sleeve.

All three of them? That's disheartening news.\n\nWell, I'll take my records to Leyawiin. Perhaps between the two of us, Councilor Lovidicus and I can ascertain what past incident has returned to haunt us.
That's good to hear. Emperor Leovic loved to hide things in coded documents.\n\nBut what about Councilor Vandacia? Do we know if he's still safe in Gideon?

Mathen truly meant to marry Alizinda—a woman with no pedigree, no means, and no great talent. She was a no one!\n\nI couldn't bear the idea of him throwing his future—and that of our duchy—away over some childish romance. So I spread a rumor.

I only meant to split them apart! It was for his own good! Typical of low-bred paupers, she overreacted. Mathen died by her hand, not mine!\n\nNone of this matters. What matters is breaking the curse. I need one last object. The Sword of Giovesse.

I am not certain, but I believe Tumma-Maxath either knew about the gem previously, or sensed its power when he unearthed Ajum-Shei's remains. \n\nThe necromantic properties of such a gem would likely be a great strengthening agent to any ritual.
Mostly healed, and what hasn't I barely notice. I don't know what he gave me, but I feel like I beat a nix-ox in a wrestling match right now.

That damned thing? Don't know how I feel about having any part of that fiendish weed inside me, but I was as good as dead otherwise. I know that down in my bones, so I won't complain.\n\nI'm just glad to see my family alive and free. Thank you both.

Could go for a nap and some pine nuts until my head clears, but won't find much peace and quiet here.\n\nThink I'll follow Bevene and her family. Maybe head back to Gideon. Got a fern friend who'll want to hear about all this.

Trapped? Perhaps.\n\nThe foul burden of necromancy no longer weighs me down, but my connection to the ring is no less intense. It's passionate. Fiery. It's like all my unfulfilled dreams and desires remain bound to that band … and to Lady Yisara.

Perhaps. Part of me still yearns for the warmth of Aetherius. But now, as I behold the beautiful Lady Yisara, I'm given pause.\n\nShe is so like my beloved Alizinda, with a heart as warm as the sands she walked as a child. I must speak with her.

Ugh! How could he lay something like this at my feet? I can barely decide which boots to wear most days.\n\nWhen he abducted—I mean, swept me away, he told me his heart was torn to pieces. He said I was the only balm. He said I was his second chance.

I don't know! Aside from the whole ghostly murder victim thing, this is what my heart always yearned for. It's why I write romance novels! The thought that I could bring him love and joy is intoxicating.\n\nStill, he deserves peace and rest, right?

My stupid brother aspires to be a musician. He heard that the best frogs live in these ruins, and he couldn't wait to catch a few for his vossa-satl. \n\nWho knew the Nereid was protective over a bunch of frogs?

Warn me? As always, Lovidicus offers too little and too late. I received the letter, same as the other councilors. My personal guard took the threat seriously and we captured the assassin in the act. But what of my esteemed colleagues? Are they safe?

I wish there was something I could tell you. The letter I received suggested that some old council business was the cause of all this. Why the Dark Brotherhood would be interested in such menial affairs, I'm not sure. \n\nI'm completely baffled.

Dead? All three of them? This is … unimaginable. Farrul Lupus's letter suggested the Longhouse Emperors left behind a secret that would prove to be a threat, but I thought he was just being melodramatic. Has Lovidicus determined what this is about?

Four Ambitions? Never heard of them. How could something I know nothing about make me a target of the Dark Brotherhood? It's got to be a mistake.\n\nYou must question the prisoner. Get him to confess and reveal the truth of this sordid affair.

Since we last met, I have been watching the activities of the Order of the Waking Flame. I followed a couple of their scouts to this location and discovered this charming Daedric vault.\n\nI believe the Ambitions that you seek are locked inside.

A prudent precaution. Leyawiin Castle can be better defended than anything we have here in Gideon.\n\nStill, without accurate intelligence, my Black Fin Legion is like the watchman patrolling at night without a lantern—enthusiastic but ineffective.

I am Keshu, called the Black Fin. The people of Gideon elected me as their governor. It is my honor to serve them.\n\nPrior to this, I traveled the world as a mercenary and helped establish the Ebonheart Pact. I even fought in the war for a time.
I'm certain that well-worn adventure book was a dear possession to Annyce. She wouldn't have torn pages from it for a lark. She burned them in that brazier with her own blood for some ritual purpose.

Not yet, but I was a mage of great talent in a past life. If there's any clue relating to what is occurring in Farmer's Nook, I'll find it. \n\nThere's a good chance Annyce will return to town, like the others. If she does, confront her about this.

Afraid my witty repartee won't be enough to keep me out of trouble? I'm hurt.\n\nTrust me when I say I know how to make a dramatic exit when I need to, but … if I don't return to town in a short while assume the worst.

Do I know—no, I don't know you. Why do you care? And none of those people disappeared, they went after their dreams. I'm not the only one who has those you know? Nobody wants to be stuck in Farmer's Nook for their whole life.

What? No—no! It's not like they're buried in a crypt or anything! I'm just trying to say I'm not the only one who felt trapped here. \n\nI don't know why I'm telling you all this. I don't even know you!
They just didn't want anyone to miss them. It's why I'm here now. I didn't want the last time my mom saw me to be after another fight.\n\nBut they have to let us go sometime.

Unfortunately, the vault is warded like the Imperial annexes—wards designed to repel Daedra. Including me. Remove the wards and open the way, and we will both have our curiosity satisfied.\n\nOh, and about that strange book that the Elf carries ….

Since my last encounter with the cute Wood Elf, I have been watching the activities of the Order of the Waking Flame. I followed a couple of their scouts and discovered this charming Daedric vault.\n\nI believe the Ambitions are locked inside.

The vault is warded, little mortal. Wards that repel Daedra—including me. You and the Elf, however, should have no trouble. Just remove the wards and we can both satisfy our curiosity.\n\nOh, and tell the Elf I think I know what tome she carries.
Oh, it's certain to be a spectacle for sure, but the only casualties have been pride! I wouldn't underestimate the conjured cob roller, or we'll be dragging you out of here with mud on your face too!

How apropos considering that little library we found is a shrine to Hermaeus Mora. Though I'm still not sure how the Demon of Knowledge fits into this puzzle of ours. Why would Annyce consort with it? Perhaps I should have made an offering of my own?

It certainly looks that way. I didn't find anything relating to the ritual that was performed at that shrine, but some of those moldy tomes shed a little light on things. The Ayleids who used to live out here revered Mora as their principle Prince.

The shrine we found was simply one of many ruins. I discovered record of another ruin near to Farmer's Nook. If we're dealing with a cult or some other servants of Mora, it would make the perfect hideaway. What do you say we go check it out?

We have reason to suspect that Annyce is somehow involved in this mystery, better to assume she is playing the role of the villain until we know more.\n\nEven if she's simply another victim of circumstance, it's safer for everyone that she stay put.

You cannot see it? The exquisite workmanship? The otherworldly crafting? This vault was not forged by mortal hands. In fact, I believe it was constructed in the lava crucibles of the Deadlands.\n\nIt was definitely built to contain something powerful.

Dagonists and Dremora familiar with such things say it was scribed in the deserts of the Deadlands. I did some research after I sensed the Wood Elf had it.\n\nAn artifact of great and evil power, it is said that merely handling it could be dangerous.
Oh for the love of—you go punch the piggy for prizes!

The wards not only serve as powerful locks, they are designed to specifically keep Daedric entities such as myself from passing through them. While merely an annoyance for a mortal, to me the wards are … deadly.\n\nEnough. The Daedric vault awaits.

That … I do not know. Artifacts related to Daedric Princes often possess a corrupting influence. At the least, she will probably feel a sense of discomfort, if she hasn't experienced it already.\n\nShe should guard it well, but tread carefully.
I don't know, because he's the big stinky pig potentate and Jester King Emeric said to.
Yeah? I guess it does have potential. I'll keep it in mind for next year. Maybe the Jester Court will finally let me into the troupe.
Yeah, well I'll keep that in mind for next year.\n\nSheesh, everybody's a critic.
What are you, the Grand Maestro of the House of Reveries? \n\nUgh, fine. He—uh … stole the swine princess from Jester King Jorunn and … he's … um … hogging her all to himself?
I'm optimistic we'll find him, one way or another. \n\nRegardless of what has become of him, I think he would feel proud of how far I've come.

Our conversation was brief. He asked about my plans here and how we discovered this location. I offered to tear off his arms and insert them in a new location. He declined.\n\nNow that I'm free, I may still follow up on my offer.
While that would make an extraordinary claim for the Game of Boasts, the Mighty Flicka there is nothing more than an illusion. The ward upon the door you'll find much stronger.

No need to be so literal, love, it makes for dull lines. The book used in the ritual at that shrine earlier: the Saga of Captain Wereshark. That should give you some insight into how the guardian expects you to respond. Convince it that we belong.

We don't. Trying to dispel or break it with force would be an undertaking, if not an impossibility. Unlocking it, however, might simply require you to play the part the guardian expects you to play.\n\nAnd you have the script on hand.

Aye, what pirate lass hasn't appreciated a fine pile of gold? But no! What is booty without a crew to share it with? A thief can steal treasures. A bandit can take riches.\n\nThink, ye wee one! Why do we sail the high seas?

And there you have it! What worth is booty if it isn't earned? What is a battle if ya don't cut a bloody swathe through your enemies? We sail for honor! For glory!\n\nNow brace yourself, wee one. Ye face the Argonian next!

Sure, aye, the Wereshark is a fine captain. A pirate's pirate! There's no privateer with more derring-do than Captain Wereshark, but do we sail to walk in his shadow? To tell his tales? No! We make our own!\n\nNow think, ye swab, and answer me again!

This one erects the spine of disappointment.\n\nEarth is earth. Rivers are rivers. Each new land is like the old, with that which kills and or must be killed. The voyage of discovery motivates only the foolish. Think, pirate, and answer me again.

What use has a pirate for the possessions of the dead? All too often they are old, or noxious, or cursed. The river washes away all things, living or dead, and all one's possessions. All returns to Sithis.\n\nThink again, pirate, and answer me true.

I erect the spine of respect.\n\nI have fought countless monsters alongside the Wereshark, yet none has ever bested me in battle, much to my regret. One day, I hope, I will meet that which can kill me. Now, face Two-Scars and rejoice in Sithis!

That's right! We're family! Every one of us, from the Cap'n himself to the lowliest swabber of decks, is one big happy, fierce, terrifying family! No mere crew can hold a candle to us, because we're not a crew. We're blood!\n\nWelcome aboard, kin!

Numbers? Pah! Goblins have numbers! Mudcrabs have numbers! You'd compare the Wereshark's mighty crew to Goblins and mudcrabs? You're lucky I don't pluck out your eyes and marinate them!\n\nNow! Think again, think hard, and give me the right answer!

You think I'd miss the conversation? With pirates? Ha!\n\nI once spent two years prowling the Forest of Lost Leaves while speaking nary a word! You think I drink with Mute Fargorz because of his singing voice? No! Now think, sailor, and answer me true!

All Sister of Pools cares about are the frogs that were scared away. So maybe if Deet-Loh sings a soothing song at the frog pool, it will calm the frightened frogs and they'll return to the pool.\n\nIf that happens, the Nereid is sure to forgive him!

Well, aren't you a fast reader.\n\nIf you chased after me because of something Councilor Vandacia told you, well, he lied. If the Dark Brotherhood sets out to kill you, you're dead. We don't make mistakes. We don't fail. Not ever.

Well, aren't you a fast reader.\n\nLook, if you're here about Councilor Vandacia's accusations, you have to know they aren't true. From your time with the Brotherhood, you must remember that if we set out to kill someone, they wind up dead.

I haven't killed anyone. Not recently, anyway. And if you're talking about our calling card, anyone can dip their palm in black ink and slap it on a sheet of parchment.\n\nLook, we received no contracts. I'm here on different business entirely.

Good question. If you figure it out, let me know. I certainly owe someone for the bruises the councilor's guards gave me.\n\nNow, as much fun as this has been, I really do need to get back to my daring escape. Best of luck with your mystery!
Be careful. It looks like Salvitto has company, and I doubt they'll be happy to see us.
Allow me to peruse the document, if you will.\n\nAha! Proof positive that the Dark Brotherhood is in Blackwood. We must find this sanctuary and destroy it!

What? Oh, my personal guard are nearby and these legionnaires are sufficient. You need not be concerned. As for Keshu, she had business to attend to. Gideon business. I saw no reason to distract her from her regular duties.\n\nNow, to Leyawiin!

Yes, I remember reports of their presence early in Moricar's reign, but they were driven out. The assassins must see this as the perfect opportunity to reclaim their base, but what does that have to do with Leovic's secret and the Ambitions?

The Longhouse Emperors were Reachmen who seized control of the Empire and ruled for some forty years. Durcorach the Black Drake founded the ruling house. Moricar ascended to the throne after his father's death, and his son Leovic followed him.

Indeed? Very curious. Still, I'm hesitant to take the word of an admitted killer at face value. Not with so much at stake. Regardless, their very presence still poses a threat to all of Blackwood. The sanctuary cannot be allowed to reopen.
Not from the spell they're under, no, though why they were made to sleep and what our mystery stranger intends for them is still very much unknown.

They literally walked through the door. It's a big, heavy, solid door with a big, heavy, solid lock. Believe me, I tested. Damn mages are going to put me out of a job.\n\nDid you get the key or not? It's our only hope of catching up to them.

Cres is … different. They looked like Bugtail when they approached me, but his clothes were covered in ink and he seemed unwell. He … they confessed that they weren't who they appeared to be, but they needed my help.

I think they were running away too. From a life they didn't want to go back to. You know how many times I tried to do that? But I could never just leave my mom behind. Alone. I thought we'd all be happy this way.

Cres didn't look suspicious to me. Just sad. Vulnerable. They said they screwed up again. That they couldn't be who they were trying to be.\n\nCres knew I didn't want to stay in Farmer's Nook, so they offered to take my place.
It could be that the two spells were mingling. That's not something seen often. Or perhaps it's simply that this Cres person was also inspired by Annyce's dream.

Why indeed? It's easy to guess what motivated these people to pursue their wildest dreams, but the workings of this Cres's mind are inscrutable.\n\nWhat would you do, if you were them? Would you leap at the chance to live a perfect fantasy?

That's the rub, isn't it? Dreams are selfish things. To chase them, you risk leaving things behind—maybe everything. We all have to decide what we're willing to sacrifice in pursuit.\n\nNot everyone possesses your sense of obligation.

Indeed. We've all had to make choices about what we're willing to risk to attain our desires. Cres's bargain promises perfection without the sacrifice. Who wouldn't be tempted?\n\nIs a life without need or want truly fulfilling? I can't say.

Maelle ask me to keep the girl occupied, so I kept her mug full and listened to her go on about her pirate stories. Was getting famished, so I asked Heseph to watch her while I made a stew.\n\nThat was the last I saw her, until I heard Heseph calling.

They were playing cards when she just bolted out of her chair like a snake bit her and ran out the door. He chased her, but Heseph's not much of a runner. Said Annyce was headed east out of town.\n\nMaelle's going to have my hide for this.
Hold on, real Annyce? Who was it we've been watching this whole time?
Excuse me, you don't even know me. I—I am Annyce. I can prove it. Ask me anything.
Uh—um, I'm her twin sister …?\n\nI can't be Annyce anymore. I know. Maybe I could be someone else? What about you? Can I be you?

When a Hopeful becomes a Player in the House of Reveries, they cast off their old identity and assume their new role completely. Such a serious commitment attracts only those who most desire an escape from their prior circumstances. I'm no different.

I'm afraid not, beek-ojel. All I know is that Xi-Tsei is one of the Sul-Xan's favored shrines. Many of the Saxhleel have lost their lives there due to the Sul-Xan's terrible rituals, their blood wets the stones. I hope my friends will not join them.

Bluewhisper moth silk? Excellent! Oh, this will do nicely!\n\nNow, please. Take your time and select the outfit that most suits you. You want to look your best while making a good impression when attending a formal event.

It may fly in the face of common sense, but I think Cres might have the makings of a fine Player. They're a bit … unrefined, but taking on a new role seems to come naturally, and they'll never forget their lines.\n\nI could sponsor them to the House.

Better not to risk becoming another cautionary tale. It would be foolish to ignore so, so many warnings. I can't risk the safety of the troupe on a flight of fancy.\n\nVery well, I'll send Cres back to their realm.

I thought so, and my eye for talent is one of the best among the Players. By the time Cres presents themself before the Grand Maestro, I will have transformed them into a master thespian. I'll stake my reputation on it.
They have a look about them, one I've seen before. It's the look of a skooma addict, sick and desperate on the street. Lost without their escape.
With the help and support of those who love them, one can hope. Ultimately, it will be up to each of them to decide what's most important to them.

This is where the One Who Knows sent me. It is what I know. I thought I could live here and no one would treat me any differently. I could finally experience all the things I'd only observed. Friendship, love, family, mead. Mead was good.
To know. As they must.\n\nYour tiny pupils suggest that is insufficient? The One Who Knows seeks all knowledge. We observe so that all becomes known. We are the One's eyes and we are multitudes.
I'll—well, I don't know what I'll do without a mortal form, but I'll think of something ….
The One Who Knows watches most. The One seeks not to change but to observe. If the One sees me here, they will know what was once unknown.

I would return to Apocrypha and resume the catalog of all things until I have exhausted my knowledge and the One Who Knows casts me into the world to observe again. That would not be, in mortal terms, for a very long time.

It all comes back to Emperor Leovic's secret. How he hid the Four Ambitions before Varen reached Imperial City and killed him. We don't know exactly what these Four Ambitions are, but the documents indicated they're Daedric weapons of some sort.

I suppose the book started this whole quest. I found it in the Longhouse Emperor's old retreat. It's full of Daedric symbols and strange markings. Carrying it around … it feels like a burden. Heavy, oppressive.\n\nAnd now it's tingling.
A ridiculous question. Is he ready to face me? That's the true matter.\n\nI only wish to recover what I seek. This nuisance Dagon creature shall easily fall if he stands in my way.
The Mysterium what now?\n\nNever mind. I can worry about that later. Right now we have a job to do.

An excellent question. The grass bends to the wind, but we are not so yielding. We will take time to recover, but you helped ensure that we do not need to flee this place. \n\nIf the Sul-Xan try to hunt us again in the future, we will be ready.

It feels like … anticipation. Like the book wants to be here or something.\n\nLook, I've had some dark dreams since I found the book and those waking visions, but this is the first time … I don't know! Like it wants something?

On the whole? I cannot say. The group that inhabited Xi-Tsei, however, will fade into the shadows to rekindle the power you ripped from their claws.\n\nTheir cruelty might not be at an end, but it is at least interrupted.

Somewhere spectacular. That's what I have been told. Vandacia does love to show off. The rumor is that this time he actually has something vital to share with us. I look forward to seeing whatever it is.
Ah, a new recruit to the cause. Welcome, welcome!\n\nI envy you. I remember my first time crossing over to ….

Then we will be ready for them, beek-ojel. We were caught unawares this time, like a swarm of gnats that does not sense the frog's sticky tongue.\n\nNext time, we will not let ourselves become prey. Your generosity will not be wasted.

Remember back at Fort Blueblood when we found the murdered servant? I had a vision of a shadowy figure. It was a robed and hooded cultist. Order of the Waking Flame, I think.\n\nIt was brief and powerful. Over in a moment. But the figure felt … evil.

That, I cannot know. I hope so. If it doesn't stop them completely, it will at least slow their schemes. Destroying the Idol of Xulunaht should at least protect others from being trapped here. That is enough for me.\n\nLet's go.

I gathered that much from debriefing the hostages. The Painted Eye was after something in that ruin, the one that High Elf scholar was badgering me about.\n\nAll the years I've commanded this fort, and I had no idea what was under my feet.

Make our preparations to mop up the dregs of the Painted Eye and resume possession of Borderwatch. Storming a fort is never easy, even if you know the layout like we do.\n\nAfter that … well, I expect I'll be asked to resign my commission.

Because no one has use for a fort commander that loses his own bloody fortress.\n\nAt least we've gotten the people out safely. That's enough for me. I'll get their home back, and then I'll lay the sword down.

Retaking the fortress without causing any damage will be tricky, but Commander Axius is up to it. The only reason the Painted Eye has held it this long was because of their cowardly tactics. They can't hide behind innocents now.

I've got two shipments of Blackbriar Mead still in the fortress. If I have to wait much longer, it'll skunk before I deliver it to Gideon.\n\nI only meant to stop at Borderwatch to fill out a customs form. Then … all this happened. It could ruin me.

You ever have to clean up after a siege? Chipped blades, rent armor, busted hinges, lost arrowheads, everything down to the nails in ruin. Guess who'll do the repairs. Guess who'll slag everything too broken to fix. Me, if you couldn't tell.
Oh! Ah, no reason. I was just hoping to—uh, anyway.\n\nAn adventurer like that, I wouldn't think a stable hand gets a second glance from them.
Of course you didn't. \n\nI'll have to draft a letter to the College of Sapiarchs. Oh, Teldundindo of Alinor is going to have a field day with this.
Hmm. Gutted, untold danger, long trek, clear out … ah, here it is!\n\n"And remember: death, my brother. That's the key."
I don't know! Maybe it's a pass phrase? I've read about things like that in some of my mystery novels. Go knock on the door or something and see what happens.

Imperial caches? Really? That's funny. That's exactly what brought me here. But then I found this band of Wood Elves under assault by Covenant soldiers and a group of insane Daedric cultists.\n\nYou positive you aren't one of the cultists?

All right … the enemy of my enemy and all that. Just like in the Investigator Vale stories. I suppose I can trust you. For now.\n\nThe cultists answer to someone called Doombringer Eshil. And he's got some kind of scholar-lady at his side.

Farther in, I'm guessing. The cultists' leader paid off the soldiers and they just let them wander on through. \n\nIf you can clear a path, I'll get these Wood Elves out of here and then follow after you. We can meet up when you find the cultists.

The ritual looked like a sort of consecration of the shrine. In itself wouldn't accomplish anything nefarious, but merely the first step of something big.\n\nI suspect we delayed whatever this was, but didn't stop it.
I shall follow this map to wherever it leads me. Big events draw near. I wish to observe them. \n\nPerhaps I may have use for you in the future? Be prepared for my summons.

I found a journal in Black Drake Villa, a hidden refuge of the Longhouse Emperors. It was in some kind of code, so it took me a while to figure out what it said.\n\nWell, actually, I had someone decipher it for me.

I'm just a young Wood Elf with a good bow and a thirst for adventure. I plan to make a name for myself, and this seems like the perfect opportunity—provided I don't get sacrificed in some stupid Daedric ceremony along the way.

I want to lock away this accursed place forever. But before that I need to get my father out of here and check to see if anyone else is still alive.\n\nAs for my village … I don't know how many are left. We might need to start again somewhere else.
Alive. I can't ask for much more. We can heal his injuries with some potions and some rest. But if I'd lost him I would never recover.

Not much. I heard a few of the cultists mention his name. Said it with a mixture of awe and respect. I think they're afraid of him.\n\nI noticed that the woman scholar stayed close to the leader's side. She was explaining the history of this place.
Only one way to find out. I'll place the book on the lectern. Then we'll see what happens.
Then here we go. The book is really tingling! Get ready to turn the cubes after I place it on the lectern.
I don't know. It felt like we were outside, but it wasn't like anywhere I've ever been in Blackwood—or in Tamriel, for that matter.\n\nIt was almost like ….

Like we were in some sort of in-between place. Like a piece of Oblivion had somehow overlaid a portion of Nirn.\n\nConfusing, right? But that's what happens when you get mixed up with Daedric magic. Now go turn those cubes!
Yes. This interior is littered with the damn nuisances. Disrupt it so that we can continue our search. I do not believe we have much time before the Dagonists arrive.

Very perceptive. The construction is imbued with a magic that allows the vault to behave as if it were a small pocket of Oblivion. In a way, I suppose it is. Those exterior portions you passed through? That's where the Deadlands and Nirn coexist.
Nonsense! I've never—croak!—felt better! I have a—bok! bok!—feeling my musical career is going to take off now!\n\nThanks—ribbet!—again!

Well, seeing how my brother actually does have some musical talent, maybe I'll serve as his agent. Get him some work in Gideon or maybe even Leyawiin.\n\nBut I think we'll start him off as a singer. I want to keep him away from frogs for awhile.

Let me take a look. Yeah, that's a code all right. Imperial. Just like in the journal I found at Black Drake Villa.\n\nI know someone who can decipher this. He helped me with the journal. I'm sure I can get him to translate this scroll, too.
Not far from here, just outside Elden Root. Just look for the camp with all the books in it. I'll meet you there.

Let's just say I've known him for a very long time and I'd trust him with my life. Like I said, he translated the journal I found. The one written by Emperor Leovic that led me here.\n\nTell me why we should trust that Daedra lady, though.

We already knew this concerned Emperor Leovic. And I cannot read those coded words. As much as this mystery intrigues me, it has also begun to bore me.\n\nIf we don't solve some piece of the puzzle soon, I may just look elsewhere for entertainment.

Not yet, but I have my finest banekin working on it even as we speak.\n\nGo, little mortal. Solve the mysteries before you while I ponder the various clues we've pulled together. I will find you when one of us has something new to report.

So the Wood Elf is useful after all. Interesting. I will open a portal to this Elden Root to expedite your journey.\n\nWhen the opportunity presents itself, ask the Wood Elf how she was able to break that ward. I sense something … powerful.

Let me take a look. Hmm. Imperial, all right. Specifically, this is Emperor Leovic's personal code. Luckily, I know it well.\n\nUnfortunately, I don't have Leovic's signet ring. Without that, I can't decipher the code.

Technically, I was an adventurer then a scribe. Turned out, I preferred ink and parchment to danger and derring-do. Unfortunately, I think I put the wrong ideas in little Eveli's head.\n\nAnyway, the scroll's over there. Deciphered and everything.

My younger sister, yes. I used to regale her with stories of my adventures, back before I became a scribe in Emperor Moricar's court. I worked for both him and his son, Leovic.\n\nEveli says I sling words the way she looses arrows—fast and on target.

I'm an officer in Leyawiin's Ivory Brigade. We've been trying to expand trade routes out here, but we're not kidnapping people! My brigadines are missing, too. \n\nI was pursuing a lead to find them when I got ambushed and thrown in this cage!

They're vicious, and the sheer number of them all at once is undoubtedly lethal.\n\nBut my commander's skeptical. He thinks the Argonians are retaliating for us getting too close to their territory. And if he gets wind of this, he'll respond in kind.

I was investigating the great number of beasts that have started congregating by the water's edge. It's like they've taken over! \n\nNothing about it seems natural. My theory is that those monsters are responsible for our missing people.
Four Ambitions? As in an earnest desire or something to aspire to? How can an idea such as that also be a thing?

I'm Destron. My twin sister Calia and I, this is our home.\n\nExcept for a short time when we were very young, it's always just been my sister and I. Plus the caretakers. They've always been good to us.
Vault? Funny. That's what Emperor Leovic used to call our home. We just refer to it as our sanctum. I suppose we can't remain here. Not after this.

Weapons? There are no weapons here. Just my sister, Calia, myself, and our caretakers. Teachers used to visit in the past. And the emperor. But we haven't seen another living soul in many years.\n\nLook around if you must, but then leave us in peace.

There used to be teachers. They came and went as we needed them. And the emperors spent time with us. First Moricar, then Leovic. But all of that stopped a few years ago. \n\nWe've been alone with our caretakers until … well, until you showed up.

You make it sound like a prison. This is our home. It was built to protect us. To keep us safe.\n\nThe emperors were preparing us for something special. They said they would tell us more when the time was right, but that time never came.
The Four Ambitions? A curious phrase. Pray tell, what are these Four Ambitions you seek?

My name is Calia. My twin brother Destron and I, we've lived here or in places like this all of our lives. \n\nAs far back as I can remember, it's just been me and my brother. And the caretakers. Lots of caretakers.

Vault? Oh, you mean our sanctum. This is our home. In addition to our living chambers, there are chambers where we can study and practice. Even places where we can go outside and enjoy the fire fields and the lakes of lava.
Weapons? We have no weapons here. At least, none that I'm aware of.\n\nFeel free to look around if you like. Perhaps you'll find what you're looking for. Perhaps not.

Emperor Leovic said we were special. We had a purpose. He had to keep us safe until the time came when we were needed.\n\nHe never said when that time was or what we were needed for. He just told us to study. To practice. To be ready.

A prisoner? No, I never thought so. We're cared for here, protected. True, our training and experiences have slowed down a lot these past few years, but this is our home. We love it here.\n\nAt least, we did. Before all you strangers arrived.
Well, we did take down all the wards that protected this place.\n\nI put arrows in as many of Vandacia's crazies as I could, but the rest of them scattered.
Deeper into the vault. Damn, this place is enormous! I assume you didn't happen to find the Daedric weapons back in that other room?
You think so? When they charged in here and demanded we go with them … I just had a bad feeling.\n\nI … I really didn't mean to obliterate them like that.
Yes, but I never saw him unleash that much raw power in a single burst. Or against living targets. Obviously, our training has served us well.
I'll have to take your word for it.\n\nWith our sanctum breached and our caretakers dead, we can't stay here. We'll go with you, if that's all right.
Destron has always been more powerful, but if you're asking if I can defend myself ….\n\nI won't let anyone take us from here without our permission.
Obviously, we have to protect them. Get them somewhere safe. Especially since we're the ones who unlocked their vault and gave the cultists a way to get inside.
The mystery intrigued me. I wanted to know what the Ambitions were and why the Dagonists wanted them. Now I know. Or at least, now I have some idea.

Feh. Not sure myself. Some shifty Argonian and a wide-eyed Wood Elf. They happened by and claimed they could rescue the hostages without any bloodshed. Haven't heard a thing since, for better or worse.
I only know it involves mercenaries threatening to kill innocent folk if we try to fight them. The commander doesn't want it to come to that, but we're running out of options.

Vandacia is a mortal problem, best dealt with by mortals. In the meantime, I wish to look into how these Ambitions gained their power. I have my own avenues to explore.\n\nBut do not fear. I am sure we shall meet again. In fact, I guarantee it.

Hmm. Good question. Leyawiin is still reeling from the cult's last assault, but Governor Keshu offered to help.\n\nI say we take the twins to Gideon. After that, we can figure out how to locate and secure the other two Ambitions—whoever they are.
Yes, Eveli was telling me about that. Daedric weapons in the guise of Imperial hatchlings. Interesting.
Feed them, provide them with a place to rest. We'll keep them safe.\n\nBut what about you? Do you have any ideas on how to find the remaining Ambitions? Or what to do about Vandacia and his cult?

With these runes, whoever is responsible turned this totem, and the others, into very powerful lures. \n\nThat explains the excess of creatures coming out of the swamp. They would be drawn out in droves by this kind of magic.

I … am not sure. My brute strength and fortitude do not lend themselves easily to the inner workings of tribe magic. But perhaps fortitude is all we need. Let us try smashing it.\n\nYou go first. I will save my strength in case we have need of it.
I do not know. It is incredibly dangerous, even with someone as skillful as me protecting the tribe. These creatures do not discriminate who they hunt.\n\nWe need to stop this.

This is now beyond my capability. I believe the magic of these totems and the secret to destroying them would be known by the elder of my tribe, Naheesh Nurwul.\n\nI think we need to speak to her if we are to learn anything more.

<<1>> was his greatest treasure! My grandmother told me he made it from the horn of a Minotaur lord. It had a brass cap inscribed with an intricate design.\n\nWhen Phalevon blew it, echoes rang from the hills for seven days!
I am! Mostly. But yes, I have a personal stake in this. Phalevon is a distant ancestor. I grew up on stories of his battles, his magic horn—\n\nOh. Could this be about the horn?

Since last our paths crossed, I ran afoul of these Mehrunes Dagon followers. While I was investigating their activities, I ran into … an obstacle.\n\nAs much as it pains me to admit, but this requires a mortal's touch. I need your assistance.

Take this amulet. I went to great trouble to acquire it. With it, you should be able to destroy the ward and open the way into the annex.\n\nWe must reach the secrets inside before the Dagonists get to them. The fate of your world depends on it.

An Imperial cache hides behind that doorway. Unfortunately, the entrance has been warded to prevent entry by anyone, including those of the Daedric persuasion.\n\nI need you to shatter the ward and help me discover the cache's secret.

In a sense. Natural spirits do not always communicate in ways that are clear, even to druids. We are but observers of Y'ffre's will. Still, based on what I've learned, I've developed a theory. One that confuses me greatly.

Seems to me the cultists didn't want you talking to me. Didn't want you hearing me tell you for the hundredth time that the Dark Brotherhood didn't kill those councilors.\n\nIf you ask me, those are your murderers. The Order of the Waking Flame.

Opportunity and motive. Look, I don't know what that may be and I don't want to know. But I do want to step through this portal and stick my dagger in their high priest's throat.\n\nCare to come along?

Imperial caches? What a coincidence! That's exactly what brought me here. But then I ran into this band of Wood Elves. They're under assault by Covenant soldiers and a group of insane Daedric cultists.\n\nIt's just like an Investigator Vale story!

Farther in, I'm guessing. The cult leader paid off the soldiers and they let him and his followers wander through.\n\nIf you can clear a path, I'll get these Wood Elves out of here and then follow after you. We can meet up when you find the cultists.
The cultists are after the cache, too? That explains a lot.\n\nTheir leader is someone called Doombringer Eshil. And he's got some kind of scholar-lady following him around like a sad puppy.

Good. Now you'll see how a Dark Brotherhood assassin deals with unsanctioned targets. And please notice that I won't be dropping any notes or leaflets along the way.\n\nCome on. Let's go before the portal closes.

She should be back in the village. I will head there first and explain the situation, but I believe you should speak with her as well. Naheesh Nurwul … er … does not always take my counsel.\n\nI will meet you there!

Looking for a hidden Imperial cache. Problem is, I ran into this band of Wood Elves under assault from Covenant soldiers and a group of insane Daedric cultists.\n\nThat reminds me—what are you doing here?

Farther in, if I had to guess. The cult leader paid off the soldiers and they let the cultists just wander on through.\n\nIf you can clear a path, I'll get these Wood Elves to safety and then follow after you. We can meet up when you locate the cache.
The cultists are after the cache, too? That explains a lot.\n\nTheir leader is someone called Doombringer Eshil. I know, right? He's got a scholar-lady who follows him around like a sad puppy.

In the kit, you'll find a book I fashioned to have a … surprise inside the front cover. My friend <<1>> is a scholar, and he can never resist cracking opening a new tome! And when he does, poof! A face full of glitter!

Oh, I've read all the books on the Longhouse Dynasty! Barbula's "Invaders from the Reach," Coravel's "The Crowned Dragon," even Korstvolk's "Longhouse Rising"—though, I thought that one was a bit salacious for my taste.

A request. One Farrul Lupus from Riften wished to discuss an opportunity. Quite intriguing, I thought! So off I went.\n\nIt was quite the secret affair. I never actually met the man, but my contact warned I should tell no one. Which, hmm ….

Eveli Sharp-Arrow—world-famous adventurer! Or, soon-to-be. Slightly new to this whole business. But that won't stop me from doing what needs to be done. I'm quick with a bow and more stubborn than most.\n\nSeems to me like that's all I need.
I hoped you'd say that! You have the adventurer spirit, I can see it.\n\nLet's keep going. The entrance to the library should be just up ahead.

What? This is a very serious accusation. The idea that one of our own caused so much pain … it is as hard to chew as thick bark. Is what Heem-Jas said about the bodies true?\n\nPlease, tell me all that you know.

Good, hopefully he will be willing to appeal to his superiors. Regardless, I will make sure he is freed. \n\nTake this. It is a ward that will unlock the main entrance of Xal Irasotl. I will gather as many warriors as I can and meet you there.

The creatures in the swamp are incredibly vicious, even in small doses. It's no wonder so many have fallen prey. It seems our prisoner was not lying to us.\n\nThose totems are ancient and very powerful. Meddling with them is quite dangerous.

The Ivory Brigade is far from petty. I'm sure there will be some who are unhappy about it, but even they will understand the need to work together in order to stop this. \n\nI'll speak with my commander, if I'm free to go. I'm sure I can convince him.

We have also been called "nothing-speakers." We are a fellowship that honors Sithis and the truths of the Void. We all speak different words, but our purpose follows those lessons.\n\nOne must first apprentice under a mentor before joining our ranks.

Since the events at the Cauldron, I have been chasing these Dagonists. After running into a few dead ends, I encountered … an obstacle.\n\nIt pains me to admit it, but this requires a mortal's touch. I need your assistance. little mortal.

Take this amulet. It cost me a great deal, but it should allow you to destroy the ward and open the way into the hidden annex.\n\nWe must find the cache before the Dagon cultists get their hands on its contents. The fate of your world depends on it.

One of the Imperial caches lies beyond that doorway. Unfortunately, the entrance has been warded to prevent entry by anyone—including Daedric entities.\n\nI need you to shatter the ward and help me discover the secret behind these hidden caches.
Each nisswo is different. I choose to honor Sithis by ensuring that the unavoidable truths, such as fear, death, darkness and change are not compromised.

I was trying to protect my people. Too many times, dryskins have come to our swamps in an attempt to claim them. These Imperials seemed no different.\n\nI hoped to frighten them. I activated the totems to try and chase them off.
Yes, but it is impossible! Nothing I do works. The magic replenishes itself within mere moments.\n \nI am truly sorry. We should evacuate our people to Gideon before Hutan-Tzel is overrun.

Well, I'm still working on the legend part. We're still in the humble origin phase, but a job like this should really get people talking!\n\nHey! If you're part of the guild … this is our job! Seeks and I already staked our claim with Kari!
Right! The hostages! Seeks and I came here to help free the hostages and that's what we're going to do. Just … as soon as I can find them.

What? No, I know exactly where I am. I'm just temporarily unsure of where I'm going. Seeks and I got separated when—well, he made a distraction so the Painted Eye wouldn't spot me, but I don't know where he ran off to. Can you help me find him?

I acquired a map from the Mehrunes Dagon cultists that indicates an Imperial cache is hidden inside.\n\nI want to reach that cache before they do and find out what Emperor Leovic thought was important enough to hide from mortals and Daedra alike.

All this fuss and bother over an old Imperial secret? Let's review what we learned.\n\nThe high priest of the Order of the Waking Flame sent cultists to the sanctuary to eliminate both my Dark Brotherhood assassins and you and the Wood Elf.

Because I owe them for besmirching the good reputation of the Dark Brotherhood and for ordering the deaths of my brothers and sisters. And because now I'm curious. It's like an itch that needs to be scratched.

Obviously, the cult has someone watching you. They knew exactly when to attack, certain we'd all be in the sanctuary. Plus, they were after some cache hidden there.\n\nSo, who are these cultists and how well do you trust your masters in Leyawiin?

I'm not suggesting anything. Just following the clues. If the cultists are Dagonists, then their high priest is probably a true fanatic. This secret must be pretty important. And most likely pertains to death and destruction.\n\nLet's keep searching.

I was away during most of her life. I did the whole adventure thing for a time, exploring the world and taking on lost causes. Then I went to serve the Empire.\n\nI would come home to visit whenever I could get away. She loved to hear my stories.

Before we found the document my brother deciphered for us, I assumed he was a scholar or a book collector or something. I had no idea he was the steward of the last Longhouse Emperor.\n\nWe never met. Just exchanged letters until he sent me to Renna.

Neither Farrul's letters nor my discussion with Renna provided much information. They told me where to look and gave me a map. It had a description of the book written in the corner.\n\nI've been carrying it around for a while now. It's … difficult.

A ritual. To dismantle the lures, they must be touched above ground and below within a few moments of one another. It requires an act of unison.\n\nPerhaps it is a test from those that came before us, a lesson of sorts. Now, it falls to us to learn it.

I will return above to coordinate our efforts. If something were to go wrong, I want to be able to help remedy it.\n\nYou and Heem-Jas must dismantle the lures down here and rejoin us when you are finished. Good luck to you, outsider. And thank you.

It looked to me like the cultist used their amulet on the pedestal and opened a portal. Examine the pedestal and see if there's a place to fit the amulet.\n\nThese Dagonist fools think they've gotten the better of us. Let's prove them wrong.
