A ritual of this magnitude would take time to prepare. Tumma-Maxath would need to find a place to ready the necessary components and use the skull as a focal point. \n\nShould we find the ritual site, the skull will most certainly be there.

Perfect! Glad I picked the right person for the job! I would have liked to see the look on his face for myself, but I was busy replacing someone's bath soap with kwama lard.\n\nI trust <<1>> took it well?
As I understand it, the helm was a gift from the lord of Leyawiin in gratitude for Phalevon's many heroic deeds in Blackwood. The stories say it was fashioned in the shape of a roaring Dragon's face.

I want to take them back to Gideon and prove, once and for all, that my family's story is true. Fame, fortune, festivities await! \n\nBut if these relics—especially the Horn of Magnificence—are dangerous, perhaps I shouldn't bring them home.

You're right! Phalevon's magnificence deserves to be remembered far and wide. I'll take these historical relics to Gideon and prove the truth of my family's old legends.\n\nThank you for your encouragement!

You're right, of course. I will destroy the horn before its curse brings about a real tragedy.\n\nPatience, prudence, perspicacity. That's what I should learn from Phalevon. He pushed his luck once too often.
I shall! Prudence is my watch-word.\n\nGood luck with your future adventures. I have spent years chasing the ghost of a great hero, but it is an honor to have met one in person.

Don't worry about me. I shall set out at once, and I shall neither fear, fret, nor flinch from any dangers on my road. After all, I share the bloodline of a great hero!\n\nA few generations removed, anyway.

I don't like involving strangers in our affairs, but my daughter's gone. Not the first time—or even the fourth—that Annyce has run off, but … well, you've heard what befell the others.\n\nI'm worried she's in real danger.

A few days ago. I'd punished her for neglecting her chores, again. She must have snuck out in the night. I couldn't find hide nor hair of her in the morning. She hasn't been home since. She's a stubborn one, but normally she'd have come back by now.

I just want to know she's all right. I hate asking a stranger to do this, but no one else has the spine to leave the Nook right now and I can't go traipsing after that rapscallion like I used to.\n\nWill you find Annyce and bring her back to me?

She doesn't want to live here in Farmer's Nook, I can tell you that. That girl's been trying to get out of here since she was old enough to walk. She's still convinced she's going to travel to Abah's Landing and join some pirate crew.

Sailing is days of rope burns and sun burns. It's being tossed about the cabin while a storm rolls your ship. It's bad food, stale water, and wondering if you'll ever make it home.\n\nThat's not the life she's dreaming, although she won't listen.

It's not like I raised her to embrace a life of piracy! It's those books her father got her when she was young. Filled her head with ridiculous tales of far off lands, adventures, and riches.\n\nI sailed in my younger days. It's not so glamorous.

That's right. He'd gone to get supplies from Gideon. What should have been a couple of days turned into more than a week. I'd begun to fear that he'd been robbed and left for dead on the road, but he wandered back into town like nothing had happened.

Goblins? Oh those angry ones skulking around in here. I think since no one's been here since Leovic died, they must have … moved in? I mean, why not?\n\nI can't imagine they'll cause too much trouble for us.

Said he got lost. As if he hadn't walked that road a thousand times. I'd have accused him of gambling our money away on toad races, but he had every piece of gold he left with. How do you spend a week lost in the wood and not look worse for wear?

That's right. Even with that ink in the pool I could tell her body weren't there. I searched around the swimming hole too. Nothing. Not so much as a wet footprint or even more of that vile ink. Like she'd vanished.

In the far off land of Elsweyr, I was taken by Sea Elf privateers and sold into Imperial slavery. Bugtail had been a slave for many years when I arrived, like many Khajiit after Queen Euraxia invaded Elsweyr.\n\nWe bonded because we spoke so little.

You … may think me a spinner of tall tales, but I swear I speak no lies.\n\nBugtail and I were languishing under the hot sun, digging new metal for the Imperial queen, when a Dragon swooped out of the sky and scorched the land. In the chaos, we ran.

I hope those days have better prepared you for our troubles than I. \n\nTruthfully, I do not know what scared me more. Seeing that giant, fire-belching beast, or my quiet friend standing at my door like a phantom.

I will never forget the sound of those Euraxian soldiers screaming.\n\nTruthfully, I do not know what scared me more. Seeing that giant, fire-belching beast, or my quiet friend standing at my door like a phantom.

I didn't seek out the Golden Anvil for its material worth. I was in search of something touched by the Divine. To have endured so long in that tiny prison, he must truly have communed with Zenithar during his captivity.

What else would you call it? He stayed true to the teachings and carried the resolve of Zenithar in his heart to endure, even as everything around him crumbled to dust. Faith like that is worth far more than gold.\n\nWe can learn much from Gavos.

Sleepy little towns like Farmer's Nook are the most in need of an escape from the mundane. We came to offer them some mirth and mystery, but it appears we've been upstaged.\n\nWell, our troupe won't be outdone so easily. We have a reputation to uphold.
Help, of course. I've devoted my life to liberating people from their troubles—however briefly—and if I can't do that from a stage then I will take my talents where they are most needed.

They got what they were after, and now they're sending their forces to kill the rest of the councilors. With the other councilors dead, Vandacia will be the only person who knows the secret of the Longhouse Emperors.
I'm an assassin, not a soldier. I've done my part. Now go do yours.\n\nWhen I'm finished here, if Vandacia is still alive … well, then we'll see what we shall see.
And Vandacia will do everything in his power to get his hands on those documents.\n\nI suppose your course is clear. You need to return to Leyawiin Castle as quick as you can.

Vandacia? That … traitor! He tricked us. Lied to us. Had his own colleagues murdered. And all to get his hands on a few Daedric weapons?\n\nBut Lyranth the Dremora. She told me that the fate of the world was at stake. We need to reach the councilors.

Yes. The barracks connect to the rest of the castle. Since I dispatched the cultist guards, we can get to the councilors and the legates this way.\n\nLet's go but stay alert. We're not sure how many of those cracked acorns are waiting for us in there.
Yes, of course. The sanctuary. I suppose this proves the Dark Brotherhood wasn't involved in the plot to murder us.\n\nWhat else did you uncover while you were away?

No, though I imagine some will be. \n\nI happen to understand what it is like to be … impulsive, and overconfident at times. I see why he did it, and in my heart I know I can forgive him. Whether he can forgive himself is a different matter.

I am a prophet! Charged with carrying the words of the Dread Lady herself!\n\nCultist, however, is an insulting term. I am a true believer, a faithful servant of … well, of an entity I'd rather not mention in a public space. Makes the locals nervous.

That, I am not sure. But the fact that they put aside their grief and anger in order to help us in the ruins makes me believe that they understand better than I would have anticipated.\n\nI hope they forgive him, and that relations between us flourish.

In large part because of your efforts, we were able to find common ground and the desire to communicate. I have personally apologized for our responsibility for the bloodshed, and they have been gracious enough to accept my sincerity.

You have my enduring gratitude, traveler. Should your adventures ever bring you this way again, know that you may call us allies.\n\nI think Heem-Jas was looking for you. Be sure to say your farewells to him before you continue your journey.

Olik was trying to protect his people, and we understand that. But his actions cost lives on both sides, and for that, he must be punished. \n\nIt pains me, but it is necessary. Olik understands, and he will face his punishment bravely.

I've been asking about Quistley all over Leyawiin for days. An innkeeper told me that he'd fallen in with bored nobles who like to sneak off to the caves along the coast for some sort of revels. \n\nIt's the best lead that I've got.

The innkeeper told me that some of Leyawiin's upper-class folk like to dabble in dangerous stuff. He'd heard revelers talking about some sort of secret gatherings out here, daring each other to come.\n\nRich, young, and bored. Damned nonsense.

Skooma smuggling would be my guess. I haven't seen any obvious signs in the area, but caves like this are the perfect place for shady dealings. And the idea of trading in illicit goods would appeal to Quistley. \n\nUntil he had to actually work.

Keep your voice down! Not even her prophet is permitted to use the Dread Lady's name in casual conversation. You never know who might be listening!\n\nBut yes, that is one of the names used by my mistress. Now, please, tell me what she revealed to you!

The Dread Lady speaks to her prophet in dreams and visions. But for this task, she actually appeared to me in the flesh. She gave me that letter and bid me deliver her message to the person in my vision.\n\nWhat was that message, pray tell?

So that's how it's going to be, is it? All I get for my trouble is the thanks of the Dread Lady's chosen mortal? Very well. I can live with that. If I must.\n\nYou better get on with my mistress's business, then. I'd hate for you to disappoint her.
Can't say for certain. She only just returned and I can't say the girl and I were all that close. I'd just assume the worst if it's all the same to you.
I—I can't say. Just a feeling in my gut. Got to watch her a while yet to know for certain. If she's like Cylle the eyes'll tell. Mark my word.

Foolish! Witless! They wish to reach the Lady of Shadows and call her attention to this place of mud and dirt. Feh! They intend to channel the power from my Court to open a gate to her realm. But her power is not theirs to wield!

Crow Mother hatched us, She gave us wings so that we may fly! We are not meant to linger in one place, growing fat and dull.\n\nThe Court heard whispers of great treasures hidden in Blackwood. But the treasures here are strange. Not fit for crows.

Oh no, not me personally. I work for Leyawiin's Chamber of Legates. These days, I'm more of an administrator. Have been since the time of the Longhouse Emperors.\n\nSpeak to <<1>> or <<2>>. They hire adventurers for dangerous jobs on a daily basis.

A fair question. I'll hire anyone who looks like they know which end of a sword to hold.\n\nIt's my job to match up adventurers like yourself and big problems that need solving. Specifically, problems that require a group of adventurers to handle.
All kinds of things! I specialize in work that a single adventurer could accomplish, given enough mettle. Beyond that, it merely depends on what the people of Leyawiin ask of me.

Ah, I thought you might ask. These are the components for a traditional Argonian blessing. Gather and mix them together, then douse Leric with the concoction. Argonian niss'wo have been prescribing this to combat bad luck since the first egg hatched.

Several days ago, a huge Minotaur attacked a party of scholars examining old ruins near Fort Blueblood. Only one lived long enough to tell her tale to a passing traveler. She died with the monster's name on her lips: Bhrum-Koska.

That's right. The legates don't want to leave these problems to fester, and someone has to organize things.\n\nBack in the days of the Longhouse Emperors, I took up a sword and handled things myself. Nowadays, I do the paperwork and recruit help.

<<1>> represents business interests in Leyawiin that are willing to pay for an adventurer's help. These involve acquiring items or gathering components from specific locations.\n\nA single adventurer can usually handle these tasks.

Terrible monsters lurk in the wilds, threatening the good folk of Blackwood. They're too much for the Leyawiin Militia, so <<1>> is recruiting heroes to help.\n\nThese foes are tough. You will need a group of adventurers to defeat them.
Curiosity with a dash of prudence. Good qualities for an adventurer. Usually that means you'll live longer.\n\nAll right, what do you want to know?

A long-lost shrine that was once dedicated to the demigod Morihaus, the Man-Bull. It's said that Morihaus was the father of all Minotaurs, so I suppose I'm not surprised that people digging around in one of his old shrines angered Bhrum-Koska.

You know—the Reachman emperors. They ruled the Empire for decades. Old Moricar kept mercenaries like me busy. But I suppose their day's come and gone.\n\nI kept my job here because I knew where we kept the supplies. And hid some bodies.

What? No, I know exactly where I am. I'm just temporarily unsure of where I'm going. Seeks and I got separated when—well, he made a distraction so the Painted Eye wouldn't spot me, but I don't know where he ran off to. Can you help me find him?

Seeks would kill me if I told you about our job without him. But we really will rescue the hostages! I mean, we're already here and the commander is paying. Now we're not even trespassing!\n\nWe'll save those people in no time … once we find them.

Thieves? Who told you tha—Erilthel …!\n\nLook, I didn't ask why you're here on the job we're being paid for. And the hostages certainly don't care who actually frees them. So let's just forget about the matter of occupational titles, shall we?

It was a damned sight better than this! I had a castle, servants, suitors hanging off my every word … I had everything I ever wanted!\n\nYou don't know what it was like for us, growing up. We had nothing! We still have nothing.

Heseph? Heseph seems happy with his plow and his pigs. He's a grown man and more capable than I am at fending for himself. He doesn't need me anymore. And Cres was supposed to keep him company. We barely speak anymore as it is.
Dead? Oh, Heseph, I never wanted that ….\n\nI … I suppose I need to talk to him. Like we used to. He deserves that much.

It's an appellation of necessity. Teldundindo was a popular name in the Summerset Isles for my generation. There were five other Teldundindos in my class at the College of Sapiarchs alone. I can't have my work confused for any lesser Teldundindo's.
Wait? So this is real? The dream is gone? My treasure's gone? Why would you do that?
Pft. Heck of a way to go. Wait, is Cres dead then? Dammit. I guess there's no hope making another deal.
Why would he think I'm dead? That's not what Cres promised. They said they'd just be me. They even agreed to do my chores! Was that all a bunch of hogwash?
The sweetrolls! The most delicious, moist, warm, fragrant sweetrolls to ever leave a baker's oven!\n\nBugtail ate them often. Bugtail had them all!

So he could. If he were satisfied with iced rolls grown stale from weeks on the road. But when one offers the chance to have them at their freshest and most perfect, always and forever, why would Bugtail not take such a bargain?

Yes! What else would one dream about? Have you never known the ecstasy of sweet moon-sugar cream melting upon your tongue? This one has not tasted true sugar since he left Elsweyr. He has missed it so.

Yeah, I spotted her in the main hall.\n\nLook, I've been thinking. Since Farrul Lupus and Renna weren't totally honest with me, I might as well use an intermediary of my own. Plus, something's not right about all this. Will you talk to Renna for me?

Oh, Quistley's no child. He came to Leyawiin on his father's business. The Silvelles want Quistley to be responsible and take an interest in filling the family coffers.\n\nBut his main pastime is living well off his family's wealth.

I'm not from around here, but it's known as Deepscorn Hollow. The story I heard in Leyawiin is that a cult celebrated dark rites here long ago. Ever since, the place has had a bad name, but smugglers and other ne'er-do-wells use it from time to time.
She called herself Tenarei Vels. We were traveling in the same direction on the road out of Leyawiin and just sort of fell in together.

She said something about searching for an old smuggler's cave. But when I described Deepscorn Hollow, she said that wasn't the one she was looking for. We parted ways soon after.\n\nFrom the bump on my head, it seems she wasn't being entirely truthful.

Someone is. Smugglers would see the value of hiding in a place with an evil reputation. It keeps away the locals. Or bored nobles might be curious about the stories of dark powers and bloody sacrifices.\n\nEither way, I mean to take Quistley home.
I'm not sure, but I want to keep watch. I've had the feeling that someone's been following me since I arrived in Riften.\n\nI might be acting like a cracked acorn, but better safe than sorry, right?

Well, that led to an aqueduct, which led to an eyeless slaughterfish nesting pool, which led to me running, slipping, and falling down to you!\n\nI don't know what you and Seeks were doing down there, but I'm sure it was important too.

Yeah. Yeah. I guess we did. I don't think we're going to stick around to collect though. Commander Axius is going to have a lot of questions and I don't want to give him an excuse to keep us here.\n\nBetter Erilthel and I just get back to the Guild.

I saw the Dagonists use magic to temporarily disable the ward. Their power is limited however, and the ward reasserted itself before I could follow them.\n\nOnly power akin to the amulet can totally destroy the ward.
Concern? I am not concerned. I am curious. Secrets … intrigue me.\n\nIf anyone should be concerned, little mortal, it is you.

Mehrunes Dagon is one of the Daedric Princes, the lords of Oblivion. Specifically, he is the Prince of Destruction, Revolution, and Ambition. Natural disasters are his forte, though some consider him nothing more than a god of bloodshed and betrayal.

When a cult devoted to the God of Destruction performs mysterious deeds upon your doorstep, there's a good chance your home will soon be engulfed in fire, devoured by earthquakes, or submerged in a raging flood.\n\nAnd by your home, I mean Nirn.

Probably? Yes, yes I did. We were just idly talking on the road. It never occurred to me that someone else might be looking for that petulant brat.\n\nIt's not the first time I've been asked to get Quistley out of trouble.

I should try to hide it better, I suppose. We were raised together, more or less. Except he was the firstborn of a wealthy family and I was the foundling they took in. \n\nSomething which Quistley never quite let me forget.

No, not that I noticed. She said to keep an eye out for smugglers along the coast and departed soon after. \n\nShe likely just hung back and followed me the rest of the way. Foolish of me. I should have been more alert.

Well, it's the right thing to do. I mean, the Silvelles gave me shelter. Educated me alongside Quistley. Even hired a tutor for me when I showed some magical aptitude.\n\nI owe them. And if looking out for Quistley is how I pay them back, so be it.

The protective ward is deadly to Daedra. As a mortal, you are perfectly immune to any such dangers. The ward simply bars your way.\n\nBesides, the amulet can only be used by a mortal. That's part of the reason it can destroy the ward.
I knew I picked the right person for the job.\n\nI'm glad to see you survived the smell. How did <<1>> take it? He must have been embarrassed. But knowing him, I'm sure he took it in good spirits.
Oh, I should think so. I'm so glad you pulled it off. She's always pranking me, and is incredibly hard to get back at her. I knew I picked the right person for the job. \n\nHow did she react?

<<1>> is a talented dancer with a great sense of humor. I rigged my most recent contraption to release a potent stink when activated. While <<1>> is dancing, find his seat and place the prank kit under it!\n\nIt will smell awful. I hope someone faints!

As a mortal, you are immune to the harmful effects of the protective ward. As long as it is in place, however, it will prevent either of us from passing through the warded doorway.\n\nThat is its primary function, after all.

Yes. Now that I've studied the energy, I can detect it quite clearly. Getting through the initial ward must have expended a tremendous amount of power. I suspect the cultists haven't recovered enough as yet to replicate their earlier efforts.
If you cease your prattling and get on with it, yes. But do hurry.\n\nAnd remember, I cannot risk getting too close to these wards, so you'll need to deal with the Dagonists on your own.

I do not know. I only heard of it in passing as I escaped.\n\nI imagine something like that comes from a time when my people worshiped stone and had little reverence for the Hist. All I know is the Sul-Xan can use it to trap the spirits of the dead.

The target is my good friend, <<1>>. She also happens to be a carpenter with a little workbench that she's always huddled under. Set up the prank kit over her awning and the second she gets under it, blech! Slime catastrophe!

Enjoying my time on the road! This is my first sojourn abroad since joining the House of Reveries, and I'm quite taken with the life of a traveling performer. There's so much to see, and do, and drink! Oh, there's so many different things to drink.

What's not to like? I was obsessed even as a hatchling. There's nothing better than that moment of pure shock that comes from a successful prank. And you have to get creative with each one, really tailor it to the victim!\n\nOr, the target. Heh.

Quite well, thank you. The work of a master dancer never ends, and I hope this sojourn abroad will expose me to dances I've never encountered in Summerset. Did you know the Reachfolk have a complicated ritual dance that goes back centuries?

Well that would be grand, wouldn't it? Unfortunately, Alchemy believes that any overtures would be met with harsh words at best and unsheathed weapons at worst. Still, I hold out hope that I'll learn something new during our travels.

A shame. Boisterousness aside, he can be quite entertaining under the right circumstances. Still, it's good to see you well and still about your travels! I figured you'd have been eaten by a Dragon by now.\n\nI jest, of course. Don't give me that look!

We were scheduled to travel on, but our troupe never actually got to put on a show for the town. I think we'll stay in Farmer's Nook a few more days. These people have been through a harrowing experience. It might do everyone some good.

I almost hope they do. It's rare to land your dream role on the first audition, but a Hopeful won't let that discourage them. If Cres learned anything from these dress rehearsals, we might see them again. And never know it.

It's a place where they can lead many lives, travel the world, and wear any mask they like without question. I can't think of a better place for Cres to make their dreams a reality. Just not quite so literally.
That will be up to them. It's the least we can do to offer. Living their ideal fantasies is a hard act to follow, but the House of Reveries have never shied away from a tough crowd.

There's a more sinister mischief in Farmer's Nook than the sort the House of Reveries trades in. I hear of townsfolk disappearing, only to turn up and act oddly.\n\nWe only set camp recently, but the locals fear we've somehow caused their plight.

None. That farmer, Heseph, said his sister was among the afflicted, and she died recently. At least he thought she died, but she left no corpse.\n\nI must clear the troupe's name. With the locals wary as they are, though, I need help. And I can pay.

The Daughter of Sithis and her brother are in the Fane of Scorn. I don't know when she plans to grant Silvelle the Kiss of Sithis—someone else is to be sacrificed today.\n\nI've told you what you wanted to know. Can I go?

No, no! Quistley is Lalais's consort. You'll find them in the Fane of Scorn, I think the way there is back the way you came. Or … or maybe ahead? He's safe for now, though. They've got someone else to sacrifice today.\n\nPlease don't hurt me!

They caught a Dark Elf sneaking around. Even now she faces the Death of the Crystal Fangs in the ritual room just ahead, but Lalais isn't there. She and her brother are in the Fane, below. Your Quistley is with them, I think.

We follow Sithis, Serpent of Chaos, Unmaker, Bringer of Endings. The Daughter of Sithis claims this place has been sacred to the Unmaker for years uncounted.  \n\nOnly when all has been consumed in the jaws of the Void can the world be reborn!

War tears the Empire apart, Daedric sorcery scourges the land, chaos reigns. In times such as these, what power is greater than chaos?\n\nIt … seemed pretty exciting and different. Now, I'm not so sure. I didn't really expect all the killing.

Then I guess you've reached a dead end. Farrul never told me much. Just that he needed the book he sent Eveli to find. That he had to correct a terrible mistake.\n\nHe also mentioned that Leovic told him things, but he never got into specifics.

Once, I fashioned a thin, nearly invisible film made from dried cow spit and chitin.\n\nI put the film over my friend's privy late at night, knowing that first thing in the morning, he would need to … relieve himself.

It gets better. Or worse, depending on your perspective. Unknown to either of us, my friend's wife had eaten some bad fruit at a gathering earlier that evening. \n\nUnfortunately for her, she had to urgently use the privy in the middle of the night.

Indeed. It went exactly how you imagine it. There was much screaming, cursing, and an extensive cleaning that night. Much, much later, we had a good laugh.\n\nWhen the prank pranks the prankster, that's when you know it's special.

I should be able to climb up to those prisoners on the trellises. I'm more a tree climber, but close enough, I reckon. Don't see any of those Sul-Xan up there, so if you take care of the folk on the ground and keep them distracted, I'll be all right.
Well, I can tell you it's Ayleid in origin. It's … you know, it's quite lovely. And it lets you talk to ghosts!
Great! Soon as these folk are free we can figure out what to do about this overgrown creeper.\n\nI'll holler if I need you!

Oh, that's easy. You just sort of jiggle it. Or something.\n\nLook, I'm an impulse buyer! But I'm certain it will work. The Orc I bought it from is a very reputable dealer. The ghosts won't be able to resist its glow. You'll see!

Only the basics. My great-great grandmother lived in Gideon for a time before emigrating back to Sentinel, and she brought back all kinds of stories. Some joyful, but most tragic.\n\nI just wish I could have met her before she passed to the Far Shores.

Oh, you know. Star-crossed lovers, murder, betrayal, that sort of thing.\n\nBut like I said before, I'm done with those tired, old cliches. I want facts! That's why we're going straight to the source!

My great-great grandmother may have embellished a bit. What storyteller doesn't? But every tale she told had some seed of truth to it. And after speaking to the people here in Gideon, I'm certain I'm on to something.\n\nYou'll see! Just you wait.

Yes! Well, I fancy myself one at any rate. My novels receive … mixed reviews. But romance is a tough genre, you know? All those stuffy critics want is high-brow, "Elf in a parlor broods over losing his father's fortune" type stuff.\n\nWhat a snooze!

Because I'm a romantic, you silly!\n\nI mean, sure, I've never been in a really serious relationship. But let's be honest—tales of people settling into stable marriages and living happy, fulfilling lives don't sell. People want passion! Danger!

Of course. Makes sense you would want to know more. \n\nThe Four Winds have always wandered this region, defending villages from bandits and such. Ever since our ancestors erected the first hut, four warriors with unique skills have roamed the marsh.

Well, I already mentioned Elossi, the Sudden Gust. She glides upon her prey better than the quietest hackwing. \n\nThen there is Meer-Ta, the Zephyr Eternal. A practitioner of old Argonian magics. Not very sociable, so do not let him get to you.

No, no. When the Wind dies, the title passes to another of their choosing. There is a big celebration with drinks and dancing. And, a little bonding, if you understand.\n\nWe treasure the Four Winds. I do not know why they abandoned us.

Hmm … distressing news. It seems my great fear has come to pass.\n\nWhere then is Satul-Sa? She would never leave the villagers undefended. Even once we decided our time was at an end, she insisted on staying.

Of course I will. I was always going to. But I needed to see if you could fight by my side. Also, I wanted to finish my meal.\n\nI will meet you in the village center. Unless you need something more from me?

I see. You wish to bring us all back together.\n\nWell, a promise was made and I will keep it. Go southeast to find the dingy hovel where Meer-Ta resides. Look beneath the dirt and rock, and you'll find him. Just don't tell him I sent you.

Oh yes! Maybe too much!\n\nCastle Giovesse has a long, tragic history. You've read Carlovac Townway's 2920 series, right? If not, you absolutely must! If I could write something half as satisfying, it would be a dream come true!

Body? Ring? Reman on high! What's this about …?\n\nAloysius wrote this? And he's dead? This makes no sense. Howling? Chicken coops? It was just a mangy mutt. I don't even think it was rabid, let alone … oh no, Aloysius. You poor fool.
Well, why not? I've had absolutely no luck with the living and it's what he wanted.\n\nI'd rather die a widow than an old maid.

It's not like this is how I dreamed of getting married, but after being jilted so many times I may as well marry a man who can't change his mind.\n\nYou may not get it, but for your sake I hope you never have to.

That sounds like a whole bunch of not my business! Can't you see I am busy with my studies here? I don't have time to involve myself in the toils of others.\n\nSatul-Sa brought this on herself. Had she any sense of reason, she'd be alive.

Khah-khah-khah! You're seeking help from that drunken lout? You'd be better off on your own than with him. But if it gets you out of my scales, you can find him on the southwest edge of the forest, near the cliffside. I trust you'll be disappointed.
Was I not clear? Have nixads stolen my tongue? I said begone! \n\nWhatever their troubles are, I'm sure it looks much worse to you than it really is. My work, however, could change history. Go!

Not at the cost of his life. I'll figure out something—I always do.\n\nBut just in case, warn Tenarei that she'd better not try anything foolish when we get Quistley. She caught me off-guard once. It won't happen again.
That is no concern—wait. Did you say Larz-Tul?\n\nIs that why the Dark Elf's here? I've seen her in his headquarters. Oh dear. I may owe him some gold.
I can't believe they sent Bastian after me again. They treat me as if I were a wayward child. I am perfectly capable of managing my own affairs! I refuse to go.
… no knives … have you shouted … Satul-Sa ….
… no mud puddles for you, sir … ah, kaoc ….

Most certainly. Moments after the captain brought Councilor Lovidicus the news, the councilor summoned Teb and myself. He explained everything. \n\nHe should have done so sooner. Allowed us to help. But I know he thought he was doing the right thing.

Let me have your map. I'll mark where Councilors Faleria and Sophus were last seen. Go warn them. Convince them to take precautions.\n\nThen meet me at Councilor Jirich's manor in the city. Maybe we can find something to shed more light on this secret.

So Farrul Lupus hired me to retrieve a book from a retreat once used by the Longhouse Emperors. He never told me what it was, and he died before I could ask.\n\nThe book is … weird. It has weird pages and weird markings and I can't read a word of it.

Maybe? These long, gray years make it difficult to think.\n\nSeek out the chapel. You will find it to the west, amidst the ruins of the castle. If my armor keeps me in this sorry state, I beg you to find it. Without love, there is nothing for me here.

Oh, well they are very ripe. Pungent—er—potent, you might say. And after a few too many that porker becomes quite puissant. A veritable stench-breathing, drunken Dragon!\n\nBesides, the more you keep from him, the more Jad'zirri can mash for you!

Oh, yes, jaunter. Only those who have won the favor of the Jester Kings and Queen can stand as their champion against King Boar. You can't enter the arena without one. Or you aren't supposed to anyway. Rules are for fools, as they say!
Well, Jad'zirri supposes she could do something with even just one if it were particularly squishy—er—juicy, but she will take as many as you can carry. The more the merrier, this one assures you!

A briar that grows out this way might help. The seed is inedible, and it smells … awful. Especially to Argonians.\n\nIf we get a couple of those, the smell will overwhelm him and wake him up. If anything is going to work, that will.
The only plan I have next is gathering more seeds and shoving them right up his snout. He does not have a choice. Our village needs his help.

Perfect. Remind him he's too old to play the hero and I want to see him in Leyawiin Castle immediately if not sooner.\n\nThese brigadines will make sure I get to the city safely. Me and my records both. Gods speed, mercenary.

Perfect. I look forward to conferring with the remaining members of the old Elder Council.\n\nThese brigadines will make sure I get to the city safely. Me and my records both. I'll see you in Leyawiin, mercenary.

Yes. Arkay, forgive me!\n\nI wept over his body in this very chapel for three days without sleep or nourishment. My grief was ocean-deep. He was my only boy! So, I cast a simple spell. I tried to draw him back with promises of glory. I failed.

Really? Ugh. I think I spotted some on the way across the castle grounds. I knew that herbalism workshop would come in handy someday!\n\nIf we do manage to find the armor, be careful pulling it out of the tangle. Heartsbane's quite deadly.

No! My greatest friend—and I hoped, one day, my mate, if she would ever agree—dead? How can I bear such enormous tragedy as this?\n\nLay the facts onto the stones, stranger. Who has earned my unyielding, roiling anger?
Only one way to find out! Let's use the lantern again.\n\nI'm still carrying the ring. If he followed us here, maybe we're on to something!

A battle! Against murderers and thieves! These are the types of trials I live for. Or, at least, I used to.\n\nI imagine you and the blacksmith wish to join my struggle for freedom and revenge. Join me. I must celebrate my friend. And test your mettle.

Oh yes, I can sense that raging fire in your stout heart. I suspect you have slain many a foe in your travels. But if we are to go into battle together, I must put a fire in your belly as well.\n\nAnd so, we're going to do … a drinking contest!

Oh, I wondered about that too. House Vero mostly died out long ago, but they were certainly real enough. We can trace a relationship to Phalevon's line on my mother's side.\n\nThere is truth to my grandmother's tales. I'm certain of it.

The drinks are in front of me. You may choose what we drink.\n\nBe warned—mixing Argonian spirits can fell the stoutest outsider. If you do not believe yourself up to the task, you may leave now. I will call you many rude names as you flee, though.

No! No one outside my family remembers Phalevon. Almost all of the histories that recorded his deeds have been lost. Even his mausoleum vanished!\n\nBut now I'm close to the proof that Phalevon really existed. And was a great hero.
Well that sounds bad … obviously. What happened?

Stick close to them! You need to keep the Ambitions safe and out of Vandacia's clutches.\n\nWhile you're away, I'm going to continue helping Keshu's Black Fin Legion. And I want to be around when my cousins from Valenwood finally arrive. Good luck!
Oh! I knew there was a reason we plucked him out of Vandacia's fortress in the Deadlands. I mean, other than preventing a human sacrifice.\n\nSo who is this helpful person?
The Dremora of my clan have dwelt in the Deadlands for ages uncounted. This is the seat of my power, just as it is Mehrunes Dagon's.\n\nMy purposes, however, are my own.

I cannot say for certain. Their truths are their own, not mine.\n\nYet I know that they must walk this path. A mortal cannot become what they are meant to be without first understanding what they are. Much remains hidden from these two Ambitions.

Of course! I was always going to! This test was just to see if I would allow you to join me, or cut you down for waking me up.\n\nBut you passed! Let us link arms and bring the fight to those who slew my dear Satul-Sa.

Do not be fooled. He has a good soul, but his mood is as legendary as my strength. \n\nHere, take my banner, and place it on the cliff above my hut. He won't be able to stand knowing I'm going into a fight that he isn't. So don't worry. He'll be there.
Two of the three? Let me guess. Meer-Ta refused.
They're cultists, I think. They follow someone called the Daughter of Sithis, and they talk about sacrifices to the Unmaker. I was on the road to Gideon when they grabbed me.\n\nCan I go now?

Glad to hear you think so. But you saw what happened. He saw me as nothing more than an insect. And that's how he saw my uncle. And father. We're nothing to him.\n\nJust leave me. Go, please. Finish the deal. And free whoever still lives.
You would be, I suppose. Well, Phalevon the Magnificent had a golden helm. He wore armor of impervious mail. And he wielded a sword of exceptional sharpness.

I suppose Goblins aren't much of a surprise. They infest many caves in this region, although I'd hoped I wouldn't run into any.\n\nThe Minotaurs I didn't expect. None have been seen so close to Leyawiin in centuries!

That's because it was swallowed by the earth! One night seven hundred years ago, people living nearby heard a terrible sound. When they came to look in the morning, they found that the whole mausoleum had fallen into the caves underneath the hill.

That's the very question I was wondering about! Wherever they came from, these Minotaurs seem very hostile. Enraged, even. I've heard all kinds of fighting inside.\n\nI think they're angry at the Goblins. Do Minotaurs and Goblins get along?

Because the caves beneath this hill were the site of Phalevon's last and greatest battle. The mausoleum was a monument to his victory, as well as his tomb.\n\nUntil Undertow Cavern swallowed it up, anyway.
Well, it has been many hundreds of years. I suppose Phalevon's arms and armor might not be much to look at now. But in any condition they would be of immense historical value. I simply know it!

Surprised I actually have skill in something? In the village I'm something of a tinkerer. Fixing tools, crafting locks, even a little alchemy. Whatever someone needs.\n\nI guess I picked up a few useful tricks.
Yes. I knew each of them.\n\nThese cultists must pay.

It is in the mausoleum, beneath the great bridge—guarded by Calvus Vanin, first duke of Giovesse.\n\nRetrieve the sword and bring everything you've found to Tavia's Tower. If all goes as it should, we can reverse the spell and set both of us free.
Well, as Otumi-Ra carried me back to the village, we started discussing you. And how strong, courageous, and wise you are. And attractive, too. Did I mention that?

We hoped you might join their assault on the ruins. Help drive out Naxhosa and his dry-scaled thugs.\n\nThere needs to be a fourth Wind. That's what the legend tells us. If you join them with this, they cannot fail. Plus … I will pay you more.

Don't the actions of the Daedric Princes, when turned in this direction, always concern the fate of this particular ball of mud? The Longhouse Emperors have protected a secret for three generations. A secret that involves Mehrunes Dagon.

A secret guarded from mortals and Daedra alike that involves the Prince of Destruction? I do not think the threat could be any more clear if they painted us a picture.\n\nWhat form that threat will take, however, that is what I hope to ascertain.

Cracked acorns, you established adventurers don't understand. When you're starting out, it's hard to become recognized as a real hero. But that's what I want to be. Just like in the Investigator Vale and Green Hood stories!

Even deciphered, the journal didn't make much sense. Emperor Leovic wrote it. Lots of crazy talk about annexes around Tamriel where he hid caches related to something he called "the emperor's secret."\n\nI decided to investigate, so here I am.

She's got a kiosk in <<1>> that she uses to sell her wares. You shouldn't have any trouble finding her. \n\nShe'll look so funny covered in slime. It'll take forever to get out of her hair! You're in for a treat! Go on, get the kit and get going!

He's usually at his stall in <<1>>. Wait for a moment when he turns to hail customers. \n\nYou can probably sneak up and place the trick book on his table when he's distracted. It'll be great, I promise you! He's going to look like a torchbug!

Skurnd loves the bard in <<1>>. He's almost always dancing for the crowd, tiring himself out, and then sitting down for a swig of mead before getting up again.\n\nYou shouldn't have any trouble placing the kit under his seat while he's dancing. Easy!

You see those pulleys up there? They control the cell doors. I can cut them, but someone needs to open the grate in front of them. \n\nUnder the southwest tree, you'll find a crank. Turning it will open the grate. Then I can free them.
Ha, don't worry. This, I can manage. Just open the grate for me so I can work.

Why does anyone want to push anything over? To smash stuff, of course! You outsiders ask such ridiculous questions. I want the catapults below in splinters.\n\nSo, yes, I can push this most of the way. I just need your extra shove to finish the task.
I was hatched ready, you hilarious deek-beeko! Here we go!

Menthyx, an ancient rival. Challenging him was one of the last tasks Xynaa assigned to me as she trained me to control my power.\n\nTogether, we vanquished Menthyx and left his bones in the Spidernest.

Xynaa did something to Menthyx to chain his essence here forever. She kept him from coming back by trapping his power here, below her temple.\n\nThat's also why the skull contains energy. Energy I can use to recharge my own power.

She probably didn't want to have to deal with three Ambitions and you at the same time.\n\nShe needs our powers at their full strength for whatever she has planned. She reversed what I did. I can feel it. Calia and Destron's powers have been unleashed.

Eventually, but probably not before she completes whatever she has in mind.\n\nHurry, we need that skull. With it I can recharge my power and help the twins. Then, when they aren't in imminent danger of exploding, we can figure out the rest.
Oh, please. You knew I would show the moment you placed that banner. Did you really think I'd let Otumi-Ra revel in all the glory by himself? Rubbish. He knows that he's useless without me here.

I think I know how Naxhosa killed Satul-Sa. Do you see these weapons? Some mammal-licker enchanted them.\n\nWith these, a handful of limp-fins could fell the strongest of warriors. This is how they killed Satul-Sa, and mean to kill the other Winds.

We destroy them, of course! But I need the binding word for the enchantment. \n\nI refuse to leave these weapons alone, so you need to retrieve it. There's a library of sorts just to the east. Search through the books in there, and you should find it.
Ah, astute! There is hope for you yet. I'll make sure these weapons trouble us no more. Now we can land the final blow, and the Warlord won't have a counter.

Remove his symbol of authority. Walk into his chambers and pull down his banners. That way his troops will know he is broken. \n\nIf they don't outright turn on themselves, they'll likely steal what they can and flee. Hired hands are fickle.

Eveli's an adult. She doesn't need my permission to get into trouble. She's good at that. And she's good at getting out of it, too.\n\nDo I worry? Of course. But I can't tell her to go home. I did the exact same thing at her age. Plus, she's got you.

I suppose my stories influenced her. And the books. I brought her books from across Tamriel, especially tales of heroes. She loved those. Still does.\n\nAnyway, she's the best archer I've ever seen. As natural with a bow as bark on a tree.

Check the letter you found. It said something about a door located deeper inside the cave. And there was a strange line about death being the key, whatever that means.\n\nGo on. I'll follow along shortly.

Along with the clouded varla stones. Interesting. The censer might have prompted some kind of animus-inversion!\n\nUgh, the specifics can wait. Whatever happened, he's still aware of his surroundings. You might be able to fix this.

Renna's some kind of mage. She gave me the final instructions for my mission to the villa and handed over the gold. Well, the first payment. I'm promised more when I deliver the book.\n\nDon't worry. I'll make sure you get a fair share of the reward.

It's hard to describe. It's like carrying a weight, but not like a heavy pack or anything. More like a burden. A constant worry that never subsides.\n\nI've also had … dreams lately. Bad ones. But I don't want to talk about them. Not yet.

Not much. Xigira, the woman who hired us, was charming. I didn't buy her story that her expedition was for study, but she paid half our fee up front. I figured they were just treasure hunters looking for plunder. We had no idea they were a cult.
I can still hear the creeper fighting with that tree, for one, and the tree's losing. We've got to do something about the vines strangling its roots and kill the creeper.

Those two Dark Elves are Bevene's husband and son. She was still alive when we left her, but with her injuries she'll be as good as dead without help. Don't know if I can save her, but I can try.\n\nNow, head through there and rescue that tree for me.

Know a lot? I'd barely left the cradle when I erected my first arcane pylon. But if you're asking me to assist Revus in this buffoonery, I'd sooner put trousers on a vvardvark. It's just as fruitless, but infinitely more adorable.

Hmph. I suppose that's your attempt at being clever. Very well. I'll rise to the bait. The sooner we're done with this the better.\n\nKnow this, however—I'll not employ his silly, whack-a-hackwing methodology. Witness a true mage in action.

Those feelings weren't there at the beginning. Plus, I found that journal. I took it to my brother to decipher. By then I realized the Longhouse Emperors were hiding something. I wanted to know more.\n\nSo I went to Ne Salas, met you, and here we are.

We were trying to get back to the others … avoiding the soldiers as best we could. But we ran right into the cultists.\n\nThey wounded me, but I played dead. Watched their scholar-lady work her magic and break the ward. They headed inside, and .…
Hmph. It will take more than the prick of a Spiderkith's blade to fell Khud af-Hadajja.\n\nOnce this work is done, I'll seek out a healer in Gideon. But not before.

She's barely hanging on. Even my strongest medicine wouldn't do much for her. It'd take a miracle to—what's that?\n\nUh huh … oh, well that's great! This whole adventure was really bringing me down until now.

The Hist says the creeper's seeds could do the trick. Did you manage to get the pod? What's that? Oh, they did?\n\nWell, there you go. We can … ooooh but then that'd really be it for the creeper. No, that was rhetorical!

Discharging spells and jangling magic censers in front of an unstable well could prove explosive.\n\nBut, nothing is certain. Magic is more art than science! At least, that's what I tell myself in situations like this.

Yeah. Yeah, you're right. Even the tree knows that—what do you mean it's not for you to decide? What made you think I was qualified—oh, right, I should hurry.\n\nI'll mix up a medicine and hope for the best. We'll meet you outside with the others.

Right. Got to look at the bigger picture. I'm not just trading the life of the plant for the life of a woman. I'm trading all the potential benefits this ornery root can have for the whole ecology.\n\nI'll just have to make sure that's worth it.

A huge boar, a fox, and a pair of identical rams. Weird, huh?\n\nYou know, I'm attributing the dreams to the book, but it could be something I ate. My diet has been all over the place these past few weeks.

She's the reason any of us survived past the first few days here. She kept us sane. Devised a plan to escape. She gave us the hope we needed. She was like Mother Morrowind herself.\n\nI wish I'd been there for her.

You saw how they kept us. Isolated. There were few opportunities to attempt an escape. The best we could hope for was someone getting away to call for help. I knew it was dangerous, but I believed she'd come back to us. Foolish.

I'm wagering there is a greater lode of this clouded glass somewhere in the ruin—a stockpile or something that dwarfs these other varla stones in size, potency, or both.\n\nTiras should eventually find himself there.

Councilor Vandacia's cult? Yes, I read the reports sent from Leyawiin. I only met the man once. I didn't like him.\n\nI can't imagine what he wants with that old ruin, but you wouldn't be here if it wasn't important. Count us in.
We owe you a debt for your help with the Argonians. I'm grateful for the chance to pay it back. \n\nI'll gather my brigadines and head out at once. See you at Fort Redmane.

The harrada creeper! Never seen one myself, but then again most folks haven't. They only grow in the Deadlands, and even then they're persnickety. But when they do, they really do. Most variety of harrada root only get about Elf height though.

Oh, no, I came out here to learn about Hist trees. The Argonians hold them sacred as the Green, so I figure they're trees worth meeting. You don't find those in Valenwood! \n\nWas trying to get introduced to one when I heard about the Wild Elves.

The Toad-Tongues weren't much trouble until Zathmoz came along. Now they're attacking caravans and raiding homesteads. He's the problem.\n\nYou won't catch Zathmoz alone, by the way. He's got a small army of Toad-Tongues around him.

Zathmoz left her gnawed bones and a note by the road as a warning not to spy on the Toad-Tongues. But it seems she observed the Goblins for quite some time before they caught her.\n\nScholars. Not a lick of common sense.

We're not so different from your featherless courts, crow-friend. We gather, we plot. We have the fiercest knights and bravest vassals. We dispatch our foes with sharp talons and quick wit! And we are very cunning.\n \nWe also happen to be crows.

You have a name for these terrible things? Feh! Featherless schemes! Nothing of the sort exists in the Evergloam. My regal beak belongs on no other face, only mine! Who knows what that other grackle is planning?

Our crow-mother gave us wings so that we may fly! Not linger in any one place for long, growing fat and dull. The Court heeded whispers of great treasures hidden in Blackwood. But the treasures here are strange. They are not fit for crows.
I am a crow, of course. Why do you giants always ask such questions? Surely you have seen a crow before!

Yes, crow-friend! Smash them to bits! A fine plan. Those featherless cultists will rue the day they tried to control the Blackfeather Court! Rue! Their doom is nigh!\n\nCome, I will guide you through this wretched place!

Of course I, the Duke, know that now! I am quite clever! But I did not realize until I was already bewitched. The Court is ensnared by these … reflections.\n\nPerhaps if you destroyed these loathsome shinies, it would break the hold?

Don't shake any branches on my account … I just need a moment and then I'll sneak out of this place. Can't say the same about my mates, though.\n\nBut if you plan to help Eveli and do something about those cultists … you better get a move on ….

I can't imagine it will be pleasant. But with enough of the clouded glass in one place … we might be able to create a large enough resonance to restore Tiras's corporeal form—you using the phantasmal censer, and me using the attunement spell.

Xigira had us escorting her scholars around the area to place those so-called survey stones. Supposedly they would get the layout of this place in an instant. Bunch of guar dung, clearly.\n\nIt's sucking the life out of him!

Well, I suppose it could be poisonous … ohhh you mean, like, could it grow all over and make a mess of your garden like stranglers. Well, I bet it grows like crazy somewhere that isn't all ashpits and lava, but I'm going to keep mine in planters.

To cultivate, of course. Bet that's a plant with some good stories to tell! I read in one of Divayth Fyr's books that it's got wondrous properties for medicinal purposes, and that's a Mer who knows his salves from his sujamma. Eh?

That's right, a weed straight out of Oblivion! The likes of which no mortal has ever seen. But if there's a seed kept in these ruins, that could all change! This is the find to end all finds! And the trees never steered me wrong before.

I damn well plan to try. It'll be dangerous though. For Eolaf most of all. That ritual is already feeding off of him somehow. The sudden shock of destroying the stone might kill him.\n\nWe could try weakening the ritual before ending it entirely.

Uh, what's the word? Ayleids, I think, if you want to be proper. Used to be all over before the Empire wiped them out.\n\nBad blood between them, what with the Daedra worship and enslaving. But some good might come of it if they kept a seed here.

They're trouble. The tribe is large and fierce. They hate anybody who isn't Sul-Xan, even other Argonian tribes. Usually you don't see them west of Gideon, but small parties of Sul-Xan raiders pose a threat throughout Blackwood.

They're fanatical worshipers of chaos and death. My Argonian friends tell me that the Sul-Xan have a one-sided view of Argonian religion. They embrace the darkest, cruelest beliefs, and scorn the rest as weakness.

Argonian musicians prize singing frogs for use in their instruments. Specifically, a strange device called a vossa-satl. The frogs that live in the area around the Panther River are supposed to have a unique chirping call.

I very much doubt it. And even if it was, I don't think Argonians make a vossa-satl in Old Deathwart's size.\n\nIn all seriousness, don't underestimate Old Deathwart. A giant carnivorous frog is no joke.
An Argonian behemoth, to be precise. He's as big as an ogre, and not quite as smart. When Xeemhok gets bored, he attacks travelers and rampages through the countryside. Someone has to stop him.

It's a tribal tradition. Xeemhok is a vicious brute, but he respects the ways of his people. He demands that anyone challenging him must present a token that attests to their bravery.\n\nI think we're done playing by Xeemhok's rules, though.

I'm hoping that you'll prove stronger than those who have confronted the Harbinger already. We can't have a monster like that lurking in the area and feeding on souls.\n\nIf we can't save their lives, then at least we can free their spirits.

I asked the priests at Zenithar's temple about that. All you need to do is pour a little of the sanctifying oil I gave you over the body of a fallen warrior. And the priests said it wouldn't hurt to pray for the soul to be at peace.

Well, we can't just leave this nasty Oblivion weed with all these helpless greens. Let's dig it up. Maybe I can transplant it.\n\nAll we're finding out here are vines. I bet the heart of the harrada creeper took root near that tree.

Yeah! Or at least that's the impression I get. Tree-speaking ain't easy you know. Even Valenwood trees are all rhymie-whymie with their communication. I haven't quite got the Blackwood dialect down yet.\n\nGetting that creeper solves everything!

Harvesting. Chopping. Grinding some fiendish nettles into powder. They mix it into some concoction. Turns those brutes into monsters. More than they already are.\n\nWatched some tear each other to pieces. Don't think they felt any of it. Lucky them.
Right. She did, didn't she? Well, we'd better set them free before those Sul-Xan kill anyone else. The creeper's not going anywhere.

The cultists drain my Court's immense power while we are paralyzed. If my vassals and I were not so transfixed by the shinies, we could free ourselves!  \n\nBut until we remove the temptation, we cannot tear our gaze away!

I can tell you for sure that we will not fall for the same tricks again! We are too wise for that! A crow's memory is long. It is not easy to fool us twice.\n\nStill … perhaps we will leave this place, just to be safe. But only because we desire it!

Right to business? I wanted to ask if you'd tried the swamp eel in a blackberry wine sauce at the Egg and Hammer? I hear it's the specialty of the house!\n\nAnyway, Vandacia. I did some digging and I came up with this place. Amnis Manor.

Well, I got to thinking. A cult like the Waking Flame doesn't pay for itself. It needs wealthy donors, am I right? Of course I am!\n\nAnyway, Matus Amnis. He's a known supporter of Vandacia. And a closet Dagonist. Generous, too, I hear.

Hey, I can't do everything! Search the manor. Rumblings in the back alleys say that something big is about to happen. An event of some sort. And Vandacia's stink is all over it. Maybe something here will point you to it.

What? No, no, I'm extremely excited about it. My superiors in Tel Naga called it a product of minor interest. Believe me when I say that's as robust an endorsement as I'm ever likely to earn.\n\nIf the Telvanni Council thinks it's worthwhile, so do I!

In Morrowind? Ha! I wouldn't think of it! Silencing an ancestor is blasphemous, even if some of them deserve it.\n\nMy Aunt Sernsi can't let a visitation go by without complaining about her urn. We know you wanted purple. Get over it, already! Right?
That's a charitable way to put it.\n\nTechnically, I am Revus's student. But he's taught me very little beyond how to fumble aimlessly from one disaster to another. I can't wait for this to be over.

I often ask myself the same thing. The Telvanni Council insists that prodigies such as I leave Morrowind for a time to experience … whatever this is. It makes us more worldly, I suppose.\n\nAn insufferable waste of time if you ask me.

Yeah … that was before I saw it. The Sul-Xan have grown it so out of control that we'd never uproot the creeper intact. And we can't just leave it. I don't know what kind of weed killer would work on harrada, but just take all I've got and stop it.

The heart of the harrada creeper should be a big bulb with roots extending out. Reach in there and yank out its seed pod. Then pour those poisons all around the roots. That should kill it and keep any more from sprouting.\n\nI'll catch up to you soon!

I, uh, I … gosh. If it were the Green, wouldn't be a question. The plant comes first.\n\nThe Pact doesn't count here, but if I grow my own creeper … I can get more seeds and make more medicines. Looking at her now, though—I just don't know!

Difficulties? Pshh, no! Certainly not! I just place great emphasis on safety.\n\nSure, there have been a few bumps along the way, but like the old wizards say: in the mountains of magical praxis, one never climbs in vain!

Right. Sorry. The runes provide a stabilizing aura to prevent any real spectacular tonal reactions or spectral anomalies.\n\nI triple-checked every aspect of the experiment, but a mage can never be too careful! Especially if that mage is me.
Oh, yes.\n\nRevus knows where he stands with the Telvanni Council. On a precipice. And after today's nonsense, he will finally fall off.
Yeah, I thought of that. He took one look at the thing and handed it right back to me. Said it wasn't any language he ever saw and  wanted nothing to do with it.\n\nSome brother, right?
Hostile cultists? In Blackwood? That must not be allowed to go unchallenged.\n\nThe Three Winds will gladly fight by your side in defense of Fort Redmane.
An hour of great danger draws near, I can sense it. The Three Winds will not leave you to face this danger alone.

Crazed cultists? Retaking our garrison can wait. The brigadines of Borderwatch will stand with you. I do love returning a favor!\n\nI'll mobilize everyone I can spare and meet you at Fort Redmane. We'll fight these cultists together.

Don't mention it. Reports of Councilor Vandacia's villainy reached me, so I have some idea of what we're up against. I'm happy to lend our support to put an end to this Daedric cult!\n\nWe'll see you at Fort Redmane.

He'll be in for a surprise if he does. I may not have figured out how to teach Calia and Destron to control their powers, but I've been working with them on using their powers safely. We won't let anyone take us anywhere we don't want to go.
I know they're going to try. But will they succeed? And even if they do, at what cost?\n\nI'm not sure how comfortable I feel letting these soldiers put their lives on the line for me and my brother.

Sombren told me the same thing. \n\nI appreciate that the world outside my vault is a lot more dangerous and confusing than I imagined. But now that I'm here, I'll do my best to see it for what it is, not what I want it to be.

We assume that to be the case, but Vandacia attacked Leyawiin once before. I couldn't take a chance and leave the legates and the countess unprotected. Not to mention the common folk.\n\nI assure you. These are among the best brigadines in my service.

Positive. With the added brigadines the lieutenant brought us, we'll be able to hold the courtyard. It's the Ambitions that concern me now.\n\nGet to the guardhouse and stay with them. Enemies could emerge from portals at any moment.

The cultists seem to have moved away from Leyawiin. I don't think the legates are in any immediate danger. But they're also no longer trying too hard to hide their identity. They're gathering in great numbers and setting up a perimeter around Gideon.

I doubt it. If Amnis already left for the event, Vandacia probably did, too. Still, there are cultists here. Maybe we can learn where the event is taking place. It's like trying to put an arrow into a torchbug at a hundred paces, but I've made worse.
Information such as that is not part of the deal. I shall tell you if it becomes necessary, but that seems unlikely.\n\nIn the meantime, just focus on its acquisition.

Hmm … yes, that seems reasonable.\n\nThe lockbox's creator enchanted it with a ward that blocks access by Daedra such as I. In his hubris, he didn't think to ward against mortals. Assuming, I guess, they would never live to approach it.

Absolutely! Yes. Maybe. I don't know! But I have to try.\n\nWould I rather be poking around in a Dwarven ruin, unraveling the mysteries of tonal architecture? Yes. But no one ever said arcane practice always leads to excitement.

Really that important? Well, of course it is! I'm a member of House Telvanni for Vehk's sake!\n\nIf the Council drums me out, what would I do? Who would I share my theories with? No, once that door closes, it closes forever. It's unthinkable!

Hey! I may not be a seasoned adventurer like you, but I can do lots of stuff! And my experience with the cult counts for something. Plus, I sent word to Grahtwood. I have a lot of cousins who are good in a fight. You just watch out for the Ambitions.

He plans to seize the Ambitions and sacrifice them to Mehrunes Dagon! He murdered anyone who knew anything about them. Then he went looking for the vaults where Leovic hid them.\n\nWe have three of the Ambitions, but the fourth is still at-large.

Not a lot. We saw Destron obliterate the cultists that tried to grab him and his sister. And we heard what Vandacia said right before we stopped him from sacrificing Sombren.\n\nI guess you should try to find out exactly what the Ambitions can do.

Possibly—though it hardly matters. Even with a perfect alignment of arcane forces, Revus's device will still fail. We're really just delaying the inevitable.\n\nIt's not worth the trouble, in my opinion. We may as well stay here.
Honestly? In a lot of pain. I think that Baron Zaudrus monster did some real damage.\n\nBut it doesn't matter. Not really. I can push through it to find my father. So, let's go.

We? No, no, no. I've done enough damage. I'll come along—offer scholarly advice and such. But you're the only person I trust to see this through.\n\nThe first step is finding Tiras. His soul seems bound to the ruin. And these stones.

The Isle of Balfiera. Home of Clan Direnni.\n\nI apologize for the cramped accommodations. We pride ourselves on courtesy, but circumstances here have taken a turn for the bizarre. I needed to make sure you weren't a danger to yourself or others.

I have to. Without my attunement spell, the censer could banish Tiras for good. I can't hide from this forever.\n\nI am a mage. Hapless and clumsy perhaps, but a mage all the same! I owe it to Tiras, to you, and to myself to try.
Of course. I can't promise total transparency, but I'll be as forthcoming as I can.

We're bound for a place called the Keywright's Gallery. But first, I need to know you can defend yourself. Hurtling through the Aurbis and falling flat on your ear left you a bit scattered.\n\nFind a weapon and we'll work out the cobwebs. Fair?

To reach the Keywright's Gallery, we have to make it out of this ruin and across a wide field full of the golems I mentioned.\n\nWith any luck, we'll be able to slip past them. But I'm not all that lucky. So, I'm sorry in advance.

Well, it begins with a door—the first of many.\n\nThe only way to access the Gallery is through a mysterious gateway. Once we pass through that initial door, we'll step into a huge vault. This is the part that worries me most.
Unless you have a set of enchanting tools and a working knowledge of meteoric empowerment theory, no.\n\nThere's nothing for it. We need to find a replacement.
Of course. Let's not tarry too long, though.

Because of you!\n\nMatters in Tamriel are bleak. War rages in Cyrodiil, Daedric Princes conspire, Dragons ride the winds of Elsweyr …. The Second Era needs a savior. I believe the Gallery—perhaps even the Adamantine Tower itself—chose you.

What, me? No, I've got work to do! The Sinderill will want every bit of this place searched and studied. Since I did the discovering, I'll probably end up leading the effort!\n\nAdventure abroad sounds all well and good, but my place is here.

If the term leads us to the vault, so be it. All we can do is follow the clues we've been given.\n\nTalk to Keshu the Black Fin. If anyone can help us navigate the wilds of Blackwood, it's Governor Keshu.

As soon as I can, yes.\n\nThe censer was always a means to an end. Tiras's letter should give me the boost I need to continue my real work. Rare eggs, Dwarven machines, vegetable conjuring … all the bizarre obsessions that House Telvanni scorned.

Ha! No, no. I'm far too clumsy to evade the Telvanni Council's contempt for long. But we have to treasure the time we have, right?\n\nI'm sure I'll make some really worthy discoveries before they start nosing around in my work again.

Allegiances among Daedra are not as simple as they are in the mortal world. Let us just say that I do not wish to see Mehrunes Dagon succeed in this endeavor.\n\nThe Ambitions must not fall into his hands.
An anonymous letter asking us to come by ourselves to a creepy old manor? Nothing suspicious about that!\n\nWell, I don't suppose we have any better leads. I'll meet you there.
No. We were told our pasts weren't important. All that mattered was the moment and the future when our purpose would be revealed.

Well, uh, I don't want to risk those angry Argonians getting these creeper seeds again. So I reckon I better head to Gideon quick as I can. \n\nDon't think I want to take these seeds to the Green, either. Too dangerous. I'll set up shop in Gideon.
No, but I always assumed we were special. Meant for great things. I had no idea they only wanted to kill us. Like they were just fattening us up all those years for the inevitable slaughter.

She has a soft spot for people. Nothing makes her happier than bringing joy to others. When she sees people suffering, she just can't abide it. Her bleeding heart can be a bit of an inconvenience, but it makes her a good mentor. And friend.

She's made all sorts of acts of kindness on the road, big and small. Never for the praise. Alchemy may enjoy her accolades for her acting, but she's usually discreet with her charity. She even raised money for the orphanage in Leyawiin!

We heard rumors of Sul-Xan crawling through the marsh, but thought perhaps they might spare us. Foolish.\n\nThe attack was swift and ruthless. Our warriors held them off while some escaped and rallied at the city entrance.

So he made it to safety? Such sun-blessed news in a gloomy moment. Though, I expected him to send one of our allies.\n\nNo matter. You have come and that is what matters. At this point, I should appreciate any help we can get.

Rockgrove? You mean Krona-Konu. I forgot that the dryskin tongue enjoys placing its words where they do not belong.\n\nBefore this, only the breeze disturbed the grasses. Our tribe watched over the xanmeer and the walls kept us safe.

Guards, warriors, hunters—our tribe sees them as all the same role. But, yes, that is my duty. When I look around, it seems I may be the last one.\n\nI know the claws of my root-kin sunk deep into Sul-Xan scales. They fell to keep the tribe alive.
<You are about to enter a Group Trial. Are you ready to leave Blackwood?>

They went along with it, but I'm not completely certain it was their choice. Even true believers have to have some sense of self preservation, don't they?\n\nRegardless, it's clear that whatever Vandacia wants us for started at that moment.

Do we have any choice? I need to know everything, even if a part of me wishes we were still in our sanctum and you never found us.\n\nIf it helps us control our powers. If it keeps us alive. Well, I'm not ready to die. And neither is my brother.

You saw how they had us. Chained up, tending to that thing. Working my hands raw as its angry thorns raked at my skin. There was no escape from it. I could feel the vines slithering around my neck as I tried to sleep. Hungry.\n\nI … need to rest.

That's just some old handbill Annyce had been hanging onto. Months old. Some vessel seeking fresh-faced deck hands that's long since pulled up anchor. I pitched it to the hearth after our last argument.\n\nProbably why she left, but not where.

When Annyce was little, we couldn't keep her away from it. She'd grab it when we weren't looking and batter the walls and stairs, pretending it was her pirate sword. Drove my husband crazy.\n\nI've made due for so long I never bothered to replace it.

What's that doing out? Annyce's plan for a fort. My husband built it for her when she was about six. Must be a moldering wreck by now. Unless ….\n\nIf she hasn't run off to join that Elf circus, she might be there. It was east of here, in the hills.

Getting into character, you could say. Preparing for a part is all about understanding my role. How they think. How they feel. Anything and everything about who they are.\n\nI have always had a good head for details and it serves me well as an actress.
She's young, or at least young at heart. She's unhappy with her life, but she feels trapped. She has a dream to follow, but she's too scared to go it alone.\n\nOnly now, she's found help.

One place to sleep. Yet two mugs on the crate, both unfinished. And, of course, two sets of footprints heading south—into the marsh—dancing all the way.\n\nThe only way forward is to follow in their steps. Shall we dance too?
Oh, thank the Divines! These Argonians were going to flay me alive. They told me so!
I don't know what to say. I'd given up hope of being rescued from these fanatics.
Oh, thank goodness! You're a lifesaver, friend. Please untie me. And hurry!

What, had your head stuck in a swamp for the past few years? Durcorach was the Black Drake. A Reachman who stormed across Tamriel to take the throne and became Emperor!\n\nDead now, of course. Which, I guess, is how we can just walk into his home.

Nisswo Somarz oversees the Glenbridge shrine. The place is dedicated to Sithis and attracts Argonians from far and wide. Outsiders, too, for some reason.\n\nMaybe it's the xanmeer. There's one of those stone monstrosities close to the shrine.
What's to tell? Argonian curses are nothing to take lightly. Especially curses related to the ancient xanmeers. \n\nSo, as soon as I heard about it, I vacated the area with all due haste.

Oh, the kind my manservant Stibbons excels at, I assure you! I was studying the local xanmeer and once again assumed that Stibbons would prove to be at least somewhat helpful.\n\nInstead, the clumsy oaf managed to break an ancient Argonian relic.

The kind that comes with a terrible curse and has the locals all in a tither! Nisswo Somarz is very cross with me. She insists I return to the xanmeer and set things right. And Stibbons isn't any help. Not in his current state. Will you assist me?
No, nothing. She looks right as rain and I'd recognize that attitude anywhere.\n\nI know what you're driving at. You're saying I should be worried? Well, out with it.

Ritual? Feh, what nonsense has gotten into the girl's head now? Annyce doesn't know the first thing about magic, she's just got an overactive imagination and too much free time.\n\nWell, thank you for telling me. I'll mention it when I ground her.
Didn't mean to bite your head off. You've got good reason to worry.\n\nShe's certainly the picture of Annyce, but I'll talk to her and make certain nothing strange has come of her.

I believe so, but I'm not entirely certain we should. Right now the spell isn't doing any harm, but tampering with it could change that. I'd like to get a better idea how Annyce and the others came under this spell before I start striking it through.
Now that you've rehearsed your role, let's cast you as a pirate in her fantasy. See if you can reach Annyce within her dream and get her to wake up.
What did you—no, no, no! I'm Red Annyce, the Crimson Shrike, and I'll skewer any swab who says otherwise!

Belowdecks, of course, searching for a way to break this cursed calm. It's Prince Vaugr's work, have no doubt of that. Yet even his foul magics won't tame the crew of the Pale Spirit.\n\nThe Captain will find a way to put the wind back in our sails!

What can I say? I'm as fast as a leaf on the wind and silent as a shadow!\n\nI suggest we take different paths to that chamber, just in case. I'll meet you down there. Last one to put an arrow in a cultist is a sour gorapple!

So she's stepped right into the story that's inspired her since she was little. That explains the ritual with that book. How better to keep her under the spell than to put her in a prison she wouldn't want to escape? Insidious.

You're telling me this Cres didn't take her place, they traded for it? And not just her, but everyone here. What does Cres have to gain from these bargains? To infiltrate the town? What could a sleepy village offer someone who can create dreams?

The deal they made isn't so harmless as they might have believed. You've seen how frightened the villagers are. How many more need to vanish before Cres has whatever it is they want.\n\nThey won't like it, but we should wake them and end this farce.

Very little. It's a weapon, maybe? Or a device for summoning Daedric beasts?\n\nWe heard Spiderkith whispering about it—about how powerful it is and how it might aid Mephala in future schemes. They mentioned taking it back to the Skein in pieces.

Killed by Daedra.\n\nWe tried to learn all we could about the device, but traveled too far into the vault. A Spider Daedra discovered us as we tried to escape. I smashed the beast's head in, but not before a horde of spiders sucked Morgane bone-dry.

Yes. That's what we call them, anyway. They're magic trinkets that let us speak at a distance.\n\nWe found a pair of them in an Aldmer crypt back on Summerset Isle. I don't much care for magic, personally, but these stones are too useful to pass up.

Like I said, I'm no mage, but if you grip one of the stones in your palm, you can see the person who holds the other. What's more, you can see what's around them.\n\nIf you find Morgane's stone, I can help you investigate the vault.
I just want to live. Like you. I'm so tired of watching.\n\nI don't want to go back! Don't make me go back!

I kept getting it wrong. Being a person. Despite all I knew, I kept making mistakes. Bad, painful mistakes I couldn't undo. So, I had to try again. And again. Life is hard … but that makes it interesting!\n\nPlease, let me stay. Don't send me back.

To the unbound library of the One Who Knows. To record what was observed. That is our purpose. To watch your lives and ink the details down. Day in, day out. Always the same.\n\nThey know it too! The people here. That's why I offered an escape!
I'm not exactly clicking my heels, am I? But there's no sense in crying over spilled milk.\n\nWas nice having all that gold for a little while. Has me thinking I need to earn my fortune for real.

We're brothers. How do you think? We fight, and we curse, and we yell, but he's still my blood. To think, I spent weeks mourning the slob.\n\nStill, wouldn't want to see him burnt up in a bonfire. We'll tap a keg by the hearth next time.

Hah. Not as if the lout would make it anywhere else. He's got big dreams and little ambition.\n\nI told him I'd buy him a lute to entertain the customers if he actually does his work. The thought of being famous will keep him going a while.
Better. He's stopped staring at me, wondering if I'm real. I told him everything. I thought he might disown me for it, but he was just glad to hear me confide in him again.

We've made plans to travel—after the next harvest—but yes. It's not so bad here. I just … I need more than just the farm.\n\nWe'd like to meet some people in Leyawiin. It'd be nice to meet some new people. Maybe hire hands … or meet a suitor.

Suppose we will. Feels like it used to be, after our parents passed on. Just relieved. Finally able to live for ourselves. I didn't realize that it stopped being like that for her at some point.\n\nWe're gonna fix that. Together.
Yeah. Yeah, we finally do. I like it.\n\nMaybe I'll make her my first mate when I finally have my own ship!

What happened is my fault as much as it was hers. I've always been too harsh with her, too afraid to let her go off on her own. I remember how that made me feel when I was her age, now. Not good.\n\nIt's time I was more supportive.
