Ha! I wouldn't go that far, but if the girl wishes to know the sea I may as well be the one to show her the ropes. But don't think I'll indulge her whining when she gets a taste of real salt.\n\nIf she doesn't give up, maybe she'll make a fine pirate.
He endures. As we did under the yoke of Queen Euraxia. We are both well accustomed to surviving, but Bugtail has had his first taste of his desires. Having them ripped away has cut him deeply.

There is still sweetness in this world. He only needs to find it. That, I will help with. I have never been a baker, but the heat of an oven is little deterrent to those who have slaved in the desert. Now I will slave in the dessert. Haha! I'm sorry.

I don't think so. We found strange tools littered about—the kind of thing you'd find near a building site.\n\nOnce you get inside, we can get a better sense of what exactly is going on and how far they've gotten.
Mmm. Yes, I'm sure.\n\nTake care of yourself, comrade. And if anyone asks you what happened here, you tell them that Morgane and Khud af-Hadajja did their duty. Do that for me, all right?

You might not be so eager to escape once you hear what's going on. You arrived via a portal, along with a Daedric beast called Shyazzel. It seized control of our golems and unleashed them on the island.\n\nIf I free you, will you help me stop Shyazzel?
You went to the Deadlands? And you took the Ambitions with you? What were you thinking?

What did you expect was going to happen in the Deadlands? That's where Mehrunes Dagon keeps all his stuff!\n\nWell, at least everyone made it back. Now we just need to keep them safe from Vandacia and the Order of the Waking Flame.

To hear the Dark Elf tell it, some cult lured her and her ilk to an otherworldly ruin to sacrifice them in some unholy ritual. There's no evidence of that, so most likely it's a falling out between adventuring parties vying for claim of the ruin.

I'm here to keep watch on this newly discovered ruin. The Ivory Brigade has more important things to do than mediate disputes between vagabonds, despite what the Dark Elf might think. If it were up to her, the entire Chamber of Legates would be here.

It was definitely a Daedric ritual, but not your typical sacrifice. Offerings to the Princes are usually quick and brutal. This was much more purposeful. I don't know what they were trying to accomplish, but they were using Eolaf's soul to power it.

The s'wits didn't tell us much of their plans before stabbing us in the back, but I've got a rough idea where they were taking the other stones.\n\nIf we head out the other side of these corridors we should be on the right path.

He's a criminal. His primary interest is gold. This ring, for all its gaudiness, is worth plenty.\n\nLarz-Tul may not even sell it. He'll like the idea of wearing it around town. A lesson for those thinking of skipping out on their debts.

I'm not sure. I have a decent education and I'm good with figures. I could find a position that doesn't involve working in Leyawiin's seedy underbelly. Or maybe it's time I returned to Vvardenfell.\n\nIt's nice to have options again.

Do you assume I am without resources? That I do not have connections in both the Mundus and throughout the planes of Oblivion?\n\nI have given you the amulet and it will do its job. Nothing else matters, little mortal.
A Wood Elf slipped out of the shadows … but not one of my mates. Said her name was Eveli Sharp-Arrow.\n\nShe made sure I wasn't bleeding too badly and went in after the cultists.

I'm an author. Aspiring, really. I've penned a few romance novels, but they all lack … what's the word? Authenticity! Yes! So, I resolved to get out into the world and find my muse.\n\nNow, here's the exciting part: I found it in Castle Giovesse!

Yes! Well, not exactly. A tragic affair played out there years ago and lovestruck spirits still haunt the castle.\n\nI acquired a magic lantern that allows me to speak to the ghosts. But, you know … ghosts. I need you to ward off the angrier spirits!

You have a signet ring? Why, yes, this does appear to be Emperor Leovic's. At least, it's one of them. He certainly loved his jewelry!\n\nSo, first that journal that Eveli brought me and now this. What have you and my sister gotten into this time?

What? The creepy book with the weird writing? Nope. Not a thing.\n\nI took one look at it and gave it right back to her. It's … not good. I told her to find a deep hole to toss it into, but my sister has never been good at taking advice.

I deal in codes and ancient languages, not arcane tomes and Daedric artifacts. I'll tell you exactly what I told Eveli.\n\nI don't know what that book is and I don't want to know. If you have any sense, you'll tell her the same.

Right. I'm not an expert on Imperial politics, but I recognize Lovidicus's name. He was on the Elder Council before the Empire fell.\n\nI remember listening to a herald in Elden Root. They brought news that Lovidicus was alive and serving in Leyawiin.

Well, we know the Dark Brotherhood murdered Farrul Lupus, who turned out to be the emperor's steward. And we know that the Waking Flame are Dagonists seeking the Ambitions.\n\nIn Leovic's notes, the Ambitions were described as some sort of weapons.

I don't know! I usually just make things up along the way!\n\nI suppose I'll offer my assistance and see what happens. Once I make some contacts, I'll send word. If you're still interested in solving this mystery, you can meet me then.

Well, after all this muck and mire, I could use a nice, hot bath.\n\nAs for Stibbons … once he gets rid of the little balls of slime, I do believe he owes me a cup of tea. And some fish stew. I'm famished.

The many truths of Sithis cannot be contained within stone and walls. As a prison for the sorcerer, we valued the structure. But with that threat subdued, we shall just ignore the place and watch as it eventually crumbles to dust.

Sorcerer Rectavius? Yes, that's the name mentioned in the carvings. Actually, the entire tale is quite fascinating—if I'm understanding it correctly.\n\nThe ancient Jel language is nearly impossible for anyone who isn't Argonian to comprehend.

Only a rough translation, mind you. To cheat death, the sorcerer transferred his mind into … well, the literal translation is "death-mud." What we who know such things call a voriplasm.\n\nNot how I would choose to spend eternity, but I detest goo.

Unclear. When all else fails, I err on the side of excessive violence. I still have a section of the carving to translate, however. And I want to figure out what this Rectavius wants with Stibbons.\n\nIn the meantime, I have another task for you.

I only see one option. We're going to need to slay the sorcerer. Or destroy the blob of goo he occupies. And I'd like to accomplish that without killing my manservant.\n\nHmm. That reminds me. I think I understand the purpose of the duplicates now.

It's ingenious. As a ball of slime, the sorcerer can't break the seal or free himself. The Argonians made sure you needed hands for that. So he grabbed Stibbons and used him as a model for his mindless servants. Instant hands, as it were.

Not yet!\n\nI've heard some nasty rumors about howling ghosts that wander the castle grounds, attacking anyone who draws near. So, we have that to look forward to. Maybe we'll find someone else worth talking to. Hard to say.
I don't think so. We're basically offering the stage to any spirit who has something to say. There's no telling who might answer.\n\nI'd say it's worked out well so far!

Well, the lantern draws in spirits that yearn for connection—at least that's what the nice Orc who sold it to me said.\n\nThe ghosts that wander around Giovesse definitely aren't interested in talking.

Oh, I am surprised you do not know. You must come from the city. In our language, beek-ojel is something akin to … friendly outsider. Not quite a stranger.\n\nSaxhleel essentially is the same as Argonian, though the latter is an Imperial term.

Ah, forgive me. These things come easily to the tongue. In my language, beek-ojel is something akin to … friendly outsider. Someone who is not quite a stranger.\n\nSaxhleel essentially is the same as Argonian, though the latter is the Imperial term.

Yes. They activated as soon as the seal was broken. Though whether they're the xanmeer's or the sorcerer's, I have yet to determine.\n\nOh, and be aware that the duplicates are afraid of water. You'll need to figure out how to entice them across.

And people wonder why I consider myself the smartest person in the room.\n\nOnce across, command the duplicate to follow you to the floor plate, the one with the blue fire. Then tell him to wait there. Once he's on the plate, the doors should open.
The Keywright's Gallery is an ancient substructure of Balfiera Island, built long before my clan arrived.

Would it frustrate you to hear that I have no idea?\n\nWe Direnni are cautious by nature, so the Isle of Balfiera has many defenses. Magical stone guardians protect many of our sacred sites, but somehow this Daedra found a way to turn them against us.

Nothing irresponsible if that's what you're asking.\n\nI'm a member of Clan Direnni's intelligence guild, the Sinderill. More scholar than spy, I assure you. I was conducting some research in the Gallery, then … pop. You and that monster arrived.

I cast an incantation of the Steed, snatched you up, and fled as fast as my feet would carry me. I heard the Daedra cursing, followed by some kind of explosion, but I didn't look back.\n\nI hope the Gallery is still standing.

On account of all the doors.\n\nThe Gallery's full of ancient gates, each with some arcane connection to places in Tamriel and beyond. Once the gates came to life, rifts opened. You fell out of one of them. The Daedra, Shyazzel, emerged from another.

Such as? We know he's talented. It takes a great deal of magicka, applied with precision, to transfer one's essence into an alien form.\n\nHe's also quite insane. What's the point of living forever if you're nothing but a ball of ooze?
Of course! It's a show isn't it? And this way I don't notice if I stick myself!\n\nHah, you almost bought it, didn't you? I'm just a wee bit loose is all. Helps relax the gullet.
Welcome home.
Enter and be tested.

Planning to give it a try? Well, before you go turning yourself into a New Life roast pig, there's maybe a bit more to it than a bottle of Russafeld red. But if you ever make your way to Summerset, stop by the House of Reveries for a lesson.

She is fascinating, isn't she? If not for her, I'd not be a part of the House of Reveries, and as inconvenient as her bleeding heart may be, I couldn't imagine her without it. Her compassion makes her who she is, I think. And a stellar actress!

She'd shush me if she overheard, but she's quite the savior! She'll hog center stage all day and chew the scenery for applause, but never for her charity. We performed for orphans and she donated her proceeds to them, discreetly.
The only strange occurrence I've seen is a complete lack of interest in our show! You're the first person to show even the slightest interest.\n\nIt's been more than a little disheartening.

I've been greatly disappointed with how often I've gotten that question since we departed from Summerset. There's not a soul in the isles who hasn't heard of the Manor of Masques and its famed performers.\n\nBut, Tamriel will know it soon enough.

Theater, conservatory, circus, salon, temple! The House of Reveries wears as many guises as we do. It is the ancestral home of all the performing arts in Summerset, and the world if you believe some of the Sapiarchs.

I may seem a simple thespian to you, but I have had other roles in this life before I found my calling. While I may not count adventurer among them, I am certain that I am far better prepared to unravel this mystery than these unfortunate folk.
The two of us? Ha! It feels so odd having a partner.\n\nI have a lot of writing to do. Mathen, hopefully, will be able to enjoy an existence outside these old ruins. We have a lot to look forward to!

Are you joking? Of course I'm going to write about this! Tragedy, lies, murder, necromancy, intrigue … true love.\n\nThis will be a bestseller. Guaranteed. More importantly, it will help me remember Mathen.

Ha! No. I have Crown blood on my mother's side. The idea that a beloved ancestor who accomplished so much in Sentinel played a role in some salacious and deadly affair …? It would not go over well. At all.\n\nBetter to keep that to myself.

I did. At least, I think I did.\n\nI've never been one of those women who thinks about marriage and children. That's why I have my novels, right? To revel in the fun part of love. The only part I've ever really been interested in.

Ugh. Do I have to?\n\nIf I recall my studies correctly, I'd say it's a Harvester—a huge serpentine creature that feeds on souls and magicka. If it finds a way to consume the energies of the Gallery, we will be in very serious trouble.

The Gallery's always been a place of special interest for the guild, but we never quite cracked how it worked.\n\nDespite the dangers, this is our greatest breakthrough to date! The guildmaster will be ecstatic, provided we get it under control.

How remarkably narrow-minded you mortals can be. What is your definition of evil? Do I care for the lives of mortals? No. Do you care for the lives of ants that crawl beneath your feet? \n\nOur interests are aligned at this time. That should suffice.

As well as can be expected, last I checked. Bazrag has been doing a good job. He's working with the various clans to keep things going. It's hard, though. A lot of people liked and respected Kurog.\n\nEven after all he did, Kurog's still popular.

Nothing specific. But just like you, I felt it was time to move on. Time to take that next step, face that next challenge.\n\nSo here I am, digging into Emperor's Leovic's past at the behest of a wealthy benefactor.

Better. At least regarding Sombren allowing himself to be tricked and almost getting Destron and me killed. As far as my outlook beyond that … not so great.\n\nBesides that terrible vision of the future we witnessed, I still can't control my power.
For now, yes. But what happens tomorrow? Or the day after that? Or next week? Eventually, my power will build until it destroys me.\n\nAt least if that happens, the vision we saw won't come true.

Desperate. The coded message had that sort of air about it. But yes, he alluded to some end-of-the-world level stuff along with the rest of his crazy.\n\nI came here to see if there was any truth to the danger, to go along with his obvious delusions.

That's an odd question. I was hired to find another book at Black Drake Villa and came across the journal. I was curious and I had some time, so I had the journal deciphered.\n\nTurned out to be a lot of ramblings. Emperor Leovic was either crazy or—

Well, after everything we went through in Orsinium, I suppose that's not too much to ask. If you think the Daedra lady can help us, that's good enough for me.\n\nI'm going to keep an eye on her, though. You can't count your seeds before they sprout.

All right, if you say so. I suppose if she's willing to help, we have to give her the benefit of the doubt.\n\nI'm going to watch her like a hawk, though. You never count your seeds before they sprout, my Great Aunt Loral always said.

The fate of your world, little mortal, not mine. But do not fear. The mortal realm has always amused me. I will aid you as I can. Provided such efforts continue to benefit me as well.\n\nAlas, I cannot help decipher the emperor's code.

Really? She's told me all about you. You were all over her letters from Orsinium. And when she got back, she rarely said five words that didn't include some anecdote of your time together. You really made an impression.\n\nNice to finally meet you!
Didn't I? I guess the subject just never came up. Besides, we were pretty busy most of the time back in Orsinium. There weren't too many opportunities to tell you about my extended family.

Hey, you brought it up! And I have a perfectly fine amount of brothers and sisters. About the usual for a clan of Wood Elves from the deep forest.\n\nThere's twelve of us in the family, but I'm the youngest.

I can't say anything with certainty, but ridding the world of an otherworldly abomination can't hurt, right?\n\nIts influence might linger for a time, but the golems should return to normal before too long. Hopefully.
I believe Shyazzel, the Daedric creature that's causing all this mischief, may have nested itself in there. So be prepared to fight.

Ugh. I know it was the right thing to do. But Tava's feathers, that chest! I'll never meet another man like that as long as I live.\n\nI know, I know, he wasn't technically a man anymore, but you know what I mean!

Ha! Yes, I suppose that's possible. Though if Mathen ever makes his way to the Far Shores, I imagine Great Grandmother Alizinda will be waiting for him.\n\nHonestly, I just want him to be happy. He's kind, and honest, and good. He deserves it.

Wonderfully! We have more in common than I ever would have guessed. Did you know he was an author, too? Well, a writer at any rate. He dictates a sonnet to me every night. It's like a dream!\n\nWe are still working out a few things ….

Well … you know!\n\nIt's not as if I'm some—! It's fine. We just have to exercise some creativity. Would I like to feel his arm around me while I snuggle up with a good book? Of course. But every couple faces these little hardships, right? Right.

None. Yisara's smile is all the radiance I need, my friend.\n\nIn the end, that was what my mother understood least. I was born to wealth, yes, but I never aspired to more than being a worthy partner for my lady love. This is where I belong.

Then I will be glad for her.\n\nTrue love is not miserly. What we feel for each other is deep and true. In the end, all I wish for her is joy and fulfillment. If a day comes when she cannot find that with me? So be it.
A little, but he doesn't know if he can impart the same knowledge as he received from Xynaa. He's not sure he's that good of a teacher.

Can the actions of a fool be forgiven? I accept that he tried. That he allowed Xynaa to trick him and inadvertently put us in danger.\n\nBut he also showed us our past. And he has been helping, at least a little. I'm willing to keep going if he is.

I saw one in a vault just south of here a few days ago, but it was flanked by one of the island's more powerful golems.\n\nNormally, I'd say we should search for another option. But given the circumstances, I think we have to risk it.

Giant clusters of meteoric glass. They fall from Aetherius, charged with raw and very potent magicka.\n\nMages use skyshards in all kinds of rituals and experiments. We Direnni use them as a power source.
It's a monstrous sentinel called a gargoyle.\n\nI've never seen one fight, but by all accounts they are far more powerful than the golems we've faced thus far.

Yeah, not sure how I feel about the scary Daedra lady, but her ominous warning makes my leaves shudder. If Mehrunes Dagon has his sights set on Tamriel, we're in for all sorts of disasters. Whatever the Longhouse Emperors promised, it can't be good.

I can't be certain, but Deejos, Ghalor, and my little brother, Liam are still missing. We have to assume they've been captured and bound like the other two.\n\nWe need to stop these rituals, and not just for their sakes.

I did, didn't I? Why, that was much worse than this, with all those angry briarhearts and harpies and catapults flinging fireballs every which way.\n\nAnyway, let's get to it! Talk to Governor Keshu and see where she thinks we'll do the most good.
I think we have to. We've got three of the Four Ambitions. Now we just need to figure out what to do with them.

That goes without saying. Take Sombren to the Temple of Dibella in Gideon. That's where Keshu was going to hide the twins. Then meet me at the governor's mansion. I want to let Keshu know what happened.

Ah, that was Olik, a member of the tribe and a good friend. He is adamant that the Imperials are responsible for our missing people but does not think I should involve myself.\n\nHis opinion is shared by many, sadly.

No idea. But hopefully speaking with the lieutenant will shed some light on that. If his people are innocent, then he might help guide us to the real enemy.\n\nAnd if they are not, then I will strike them down with the power of a graht oak!

My heroic deeds have caused a few … mishaps, of late. In addition, everyone is convinced of the Imperial's guilt. \n\nBut an intelligent, seasoned adventurer such as myself is more skeptical. Mainly because we, er, have no evidence.

I should be honest—I don't really get hired that often. Usually I just wander about looking for an adventure. But not only did this sound exciting, also my biscuit bin was a bit low, if you know what I mean.\n\nI was happy for the gold.

Oh, you know me! Always on the hunt for more excitement. I traveled south a bit after I last saw you. Elsweyr was quite beautiful, if you haven't seen it. Did you know they have Dragons? Their heads are enormous!

That's the library I told you about. Stories claim it's a massive underground collection of books, scrolls, and artifacts that the Longhouse Emperors gathered over the years. Volumes of secrets and knowledge might lay right under our feet.

Ah, sorry about that. Based on the armor, I'd wager that was Kinras Ironeye. He led the Goblins that we saw earlier.\n\nI heard he was around this area, but didn't know he took over the villa. I guess some warning could have helped.

Both Governor Keshu and Councilor Lovidicus made that abundantly clear to me. \n\nThere's no finer general in Blackwood than the Black Fin. My brigadines stand ready to follow her orders to the letter. We'll keep the Ambitions safe.
General Keshu asked me to defend Fort Redmane's front gate from the battlements. I've posted a strong contingent of archers along the walls, and I intend to lead them personally.

Liam … hang in there, little brother. We'll find you.\n\nWe seem to be getting close to the heart of the cult's plot. Other than the ruins, the terrain here is unrecognizable from where we came from. I'd wager that's where we'll find him. And Xigira.

I think that mechanism must be connected to the gate, but that can't be the only thing stopping us or Xigira wouldn't be so confident. We should look around. There might be more of these Daedric objects involved in the barrier.
All right, but remember you already agreed to help me. It'd be rude to back out now.\n\nBut seriously, I need your help. Please don't change your mind.

They're still learning, but as long as I'm present to guide them, the risk isn't too great. I can devote my attention to shaping the power they release. And the strength of three Ambitions in concert will be difficult for any foe to overcome.
So far. Sombren has been showing us some techniques and they seem to be working for now.\n\nWe'll protect each other. After all, we're the only Ambitions we know.

I expect a two-pronged assault. The bulk of Vandacia's forces will attack the gate, while a smaller group uses portals to get inside. Portal magic is difficult. They could never move an entire army that way. Hence, we must defend from all directions.

Of course, Revus needs help balancing the delicate magical forces of his apparatus from someone that knows even less about what they're doing than he does.\n\nPlainly put: Watch the magicka pass between pylons. Whichever pylon doesn't get hit, attune.

About the time they said, don't kill her, we need her for the ritual. And while they were trying to subdue me. Probably saved my life though. I fought twice as hard knowing they were taking it easy on me.\n\nNo one else escaped, that I know of.

I mean stopping the ritual prematurely might kill her but there are fates worse than death. If her soul is drained entirely from her body, it won't be left to the mercy of the Divines. It'll probably wind up in the clutches of Oblivion.

I have a theory about the purpose of these rituals. The changes to the land, the sky, the blasted heat. I think this place is being overtaken by another plane. If I had to guess, I'd say it's becoming the Deadlands.
No. I don't care about that hooded viper. I just want my little brother back … but if she stands in our way, I'll gladly kick her fetching arse back to Oblivion.\n\nCome on. Liam needs me.

I need to make sure we hold the battlements. Deal with any other portals that open and see what support we can provide to Keshu and her legionnaires.\n\nNow go, mercenary. I hear more fighting inside.

My scouts tell me we closed the gate just in time. It appears the Waking Flame used magic to conceal their approach. The Black Fin Legion is holding them back, but you should make sure the Ambitions are safe.

I did! Quite fancy ones, in fact. Lighter than a baby jay's tail feathers.\n\nThe best part of these little excursions is finding all the stuff people leave behind. Sometimes it's a plate of old sweetrolls, but once in a while I find something handy.

Seems so! I assume a water enchantment of some kind. I've read about magic like that, but never really had too much interest in the stuff. Seems like cheating. \n\nSure helped us out in a jam, though.
Oh, I used the last one saving your hide. I'm not too troubled about it. You know how treasure can be—lightly come, lightly go.\n\nCome on, let's find that book!

I couldn't help myself. All these incredible volumes turning to ash—I just wanted to save something. This journal was resting on a desk as I ran past, so I picked it up.\n\nOf course, the one item I decide to save is completely illegible.

I know just the person who would love to dive head-first into solving this. He's a bit reclusive these days, but quite clever at figuring out puzzles.\n\nIt may come across as silly, but I just have to know what it says.

The casualness of the handwriting. All the little notes in the margins. Several tea stains on the pages. \n\nWhen you spend as much time reading books as I do, you recognize these things. Even with the words all jumbled around, I can tell.
Again, I'm just a scholar. But I'd encourage you to remember what we practiced before. Keep moving, strike true, and exploit any opening the creature gives you!
I was attacked … an assassin ….\n\nYou must warn the others … the councilors … Leovic's secret. It will be … the death … of us … all ….

I'm not sure, but they ran west. The inner bailey's in that direction. I wouldn't be surprised if Sombren plans to keep moving. Vandacia will have a hard time finding the Ambitions if they don't stand still.\n\nHmm. And so will we. That's awkward.

They are a tribe of locusts, swarming those who live peacefully within the marsh. Sul-Xan only wish to rend scale from spine. I hear stories of sacrifices to appease the chaos.\n\nI know little more of them, as I practice caution in their presence.

Ah. I offer my abdomen in forgiveness and welcome. Events have caused me to forget my training.\n\nCalling me Dust-on-Scales will be easiest. I serve as stone-talker for the Ca-Uxith—the Silent-Nest tribe. What remains of it.

I cannot explain it, but yes. Since the moment I hatched, I have witnessed the deaths of many egg-kin. Our souls return to the chaos, dispersing into the cycle once more.\n\nFor them to be removed in such a manner …. I must learn more.

Our small village of Krona-Konu lies close by. Though I understand the dryskins refer to it as Rockgrove. Outsiders rarely visit, so I see no need to quibble.\n\nThe Hist asked that we watch over this xanmeer and ensure that it stands. And so we have.
Oh, no one important, I assure you! I'm simply one of the councilor's aides. I help her with paperwork mostly. Run errands. That sort of thing.

A lot from our childhood, mostly. If our parents were around, they were deep in the skooma, so Cylle and I had to look out for each other. Not so much anymore. The years have been peaceful here. I suppose we'd grown distant, before she vanished.

No, no. Maybe. We'd sit down for meals together and tend the farm together, but there's not much to talk about in Farmer's Nook. Another field planted, another day gone by.\n\nWas she trying to tell me something? What was she trying to say …?

We were all a bit shaken by what happened with Igmund, but things were getting back to normal. Until Cylle went out to collect logs and didn't return.\n\nI begged the others to help me search for her, but they feared they'd vanish too.

Can a ghost take your hand? Make a meal? If she slept, I never saw it. I barely slept myself. The staring was the worst. Felt like she was always watching, smiling. When she'd blink it was like one eye was a hair shy of the other. Gave me chills.

Truth is, I didn't make it far myself. I thought I heard things in those woods. Even during the day it felt like something was watching. When she showed up at the house again, I nearly fainted. I should have been relieved, but I felt haunted.

Well, fate's sort of a clumsy way to put it. No offense!\n\nHonestly, we may never know why you were chosen. But I believe there was intention here. Something, whether it be the stars, the Gallery, or the Tower itself placed you here for a reason.

It is a bit overwhelming, isn't it? The whole of Tamriel stretched out before you.\n\nWe could start with the political considerations. Three great alliances vie for control of Cyrodiil. Does the fate of the Pact, Covenant, or Dominion interest you?
Excellent.\n\nYou can visit Stros M'Kai in Daggerfall Covenant territory, an island called Khenarthi's Roost that the Aldmeri Dominion set its eyes on, or the Ebonheart Pact's domain.
I don't blame you. Inter-provincial intrigue is the basis of my whole profession, and even I find it tiresome after a while.\n\nI suppose that widens the map a bit.
Hmph, like he didn't have a care in the world. He seemed to be enjoying even the usual drudgery. Never thought I'd miss his belly-aching over the chores, but he just didn't seem himself.

No. Things were as they usually are in Farmer's Nook: uneventful. It's exciting times when our little inn sees more than a couple travelers in a month. \n\nEver since Igmund got lost, things have been nothing but trouble.

Two others disappeared since Igmund, and all three were acting strange before they met untimely ends. If that's even what you could call it.\n\nNo one wanders from the village now. Some folk are sleeping at my inn just to stick close.

I would not have suspected anything amiss had I not known of what happened to Igmund and Cylle. There was nothing sinister in his look or manner. If anything, he regarded me more warmly than he had in years. Normally, he could go days without a word.

He seemed to want to reminisce about our more adventurous days, before we escaped to Farmer's Nook and settled down to raise horses. They were livelier times, but I would not trade them for what I have now.

Oh, I'm still trying to make a name for myself. I was green as a blade of grass when we met in Orsinium. Now I've got a few more adventures under my belt … but I've never dealt with anything quite like this.\n\nThis is a more than I bargained for.

The mark of the Dark Brotherhood, just like Farrul Lupus.\n\nRemember I said I was going to find Lovidicus? Well, I did. And turns out, he's the head of the city's Chamber of Legates! I just wish another person hadn't died because of this damn secret.

Let me have your map. This is where Councilors Faleria and Sophus were, last time I checked. Go warn them. Convince them the threat is real.\n\nThen meet me at Councilor Jirich's manor in the city. Maybe we can find something more about this secret.

The secret of the Longhouse Emperors. It has something to do with the Four Ambitions of Mehrunes Dagon. I think they're Daedric weapons, but that's all we know so far.\n\nRemember, I was working for Farrul Lupus. He sent me to find that strange tome.

While Countess Caro sits on Leyawiin's throne, it is the Chamber of Legates that governs the city. There are three legates—this one, Am-Halu, and Lovidicus.\n\nEach one has an equal voice. This one supposes Lovidicus's voice is slightly louder.

Lovidicus was the chief councilor of the Imperial Elder Council. Since the threat concerned his former colleagues, he decided to keep it to himself until he ascertained its veracity.\n\nHe did inform us as soon as the threat was deemed real.

I know his name is Lirar Droth, but the Fang-Furls make him lead a quiet life. To conceal his identity, I imagine. But all the muscle on their payroll visits him for late night liaisons. Very clandestine, the whole thing. But not to my keen eyes.

Scipion and I left Elsweyr to claim a gift left to us by our departed uncle, the Happy Averno Shipping Company. Formerly, it was one of Blackwood's main trade enterprises. We thought, with a little elbow grease, it might prove a profitable venture.

We discovered our uncle's affairs were more … precariously poised than described, for one. Many of his charters and contracts were voided by the Three Banners War. \n\nThe Fang-Furls did the rest. They came for everything they could steal.

You can learn a great deal from a business ledger. Where money comes from, where it goes, and then, all you need to do is apply a little pressure at a weak point. I don't know exactly what we'll find, but I do know whatever it is, I can exploit it.

While I have never laid eyes on one of the Xal-Krona, I know of their kind. Great warriors, massive in size, bestowed as gifts from the Hist.\n\nThey are not typically such a color. I suspect Bahsei may have … altered him somehow.

Not by myself, I didn't. You helped! What started as an historic mystery turned into a tale of murder, living Daedric weapons, and the end of the world. How do we follow that?\n\nOh, I know! With flagons of rotmeth and lots of roast paws on a stick!

You will be very impressed, I'm sure! I've had many adventures and victories since then … the Trial of Mud, the Great Fish Hook Escapade, the Toad's Overstuffed Belly, and many more! You will have to read some when things are not so dire.

Let's see … ah, it seems the Fang-Furls have their thumbs in some very dirty pies. I'm not one to talk, given where my hands have been.\n\nI have an idea. If we can draw out Pungent Adder himself, we can topple him and his gang.

My heart burned for more daring adventures! I have traveled far and wide, doing heroic deeds wherever I go. I came here a little over a month ago to offer my services to this tribe.\n\nAnd it is clear they have need of me!

The Imperials from Leyawiin have been expanding their territory eastward for some time. Now they creep like moss on the edges of what my tribe considers our land. At first, they were just a nuisance. We assumed the swamp would deal with them in time.

By gifting Pungent Adder some umbrage. Looking at this ledger, I see two morsels dangling before us.\n\nFirstly, according to this, the Fang-Furls use dead drops to issue and receive orders. If we steal those drops, we disrupt their operation.

We send Pungent Adder a more personal message. \n\nIt seems he has a barrel of Oleander Coast Reserve waiting at the docks. Let's say we … season it with something foul. Make it as pungent as the Adder himself?
The Imperials left us alone, but refused to leave the area. Eventually, tension turned to arguments. Shortly after, members of our tribe began to vanish.\n\nIt was like flame to a dry tree.

No, just the opposite! They wished to work with us to help expand their holdings and offered valuable goods and trade. \n\nBut my tribe turned their tails at them. Too many times our people have been pushed from our homes with fake promises.
Hang on to them, I suppose. They might be useful to peruse, after all is said and done—find out who's worth trusting, and who's happily squirming in bed with Adder.

The cask is at the docks, so I'm sure there will be something on hand. Pitch, bilge water, fish … anything will do. \n\nJust try not to get caught doing anything unseemly in public, hmm? No sense mixing business with pleasure.

That might very well be the case, though I have to wonder why she'd leave her pack behind if she had no intention to return.\n\nI don't like meddling in someone's family affairs, but let's confirm she's all right before we jump to any conclusions.

They're a good source of fuel for the working people of Leyawiin, of course! Once they realize how much energy and nourishment is in each grub, they'll forget about that privy-house scent!\n\nWhy not buy a skewer, stranger?
Wonderful! You won't regret it, I guarantee!\n\nOh, and speaking of regrets, don't eat these near any open flame. Enjoy!

The one at the top of Xal Irasotl? I am not surprised. Dismantling lures as powerful as this will require going inside the xanmeer. Unfortunately, as time abandoned Xal Irasotl, its depths filled with nightmarish horrors.

Of course! The Crow Mother taught us to speak, and since then we have talked and cawed with the utmost elegance! \n\nI have the honor of being named the Duke, for I am the loudest of my loyal vassals. My feathers are also the most resplendent!

The same to you, my Knight-Without-Feathers! \n\nThe Blackfeather Court is much richer indeed to count you as a crow-friend. Your loyalty is worth more than any shiny, no matter how big or bright it may be!

Wherever the wind takes us, crow-friend. Though, after this harrowing experience, we may return to Crow's Wood. \n\nI long for our skirmishes with the bats. Our gallant knights could use a fierce battle to forget this insult. A victory!

The Duke of Crows is the very definition of feathery cleverness! I used their own shinies against them! \n\nThe magic inside them does more than fascinate and drain energy from the Blackfeather Court, if you are as clever as I am.
I'm the son of Lord Martel Hallix … the traitor.

I suppose the story's not well known outside of court circles. My father was one of High King Emeric's most trusted advisors. But when I was only a toddler, he plotted to secretly murder Emeric and appoint himself regent. Or so I'm told.

He failed, of course. Others in my family were implicated in the plot. The high king stripped House Hallix of its titles and domains. My mother died of shame. I was far too young to have been a part of it, though, so the Silvelles took me in.

It is the realm of our Mistress! Our home, our place of creation, the cradle of shadow! The darkest realm of Oblivion, home to only those worthy. Worthy! The Blackfeather Court has dominion over the Crow's Wood within the Evergloam. It is our domain.

Now that this matter is settled, Scipion and I can begin restoring the Happy Averno Trading Company. My first priority is to find us somewhere else to live. \n\nI don't mind close quarters … but the two of us are accustomed to a certain lifestyle.

I found notes left behind by some unfortunate scholar. He'd apparently come here to make a survey of the ruins.\n\nI hope he had the good sense to retreat when he found fresh evidence of a cult presence. More likely, he came to a bad end.
I did. It's all the way down at the end of this maze, naturally. The scholar's notes hinted that it's an abandoned temple, once dedicated to Sithis.\n\nWell, probably not abandoned now.

That's … that's horrible! Are you sure? No, of course you're sure. No one would lie about something like that.\n\nI'll tell her brother what happened and send someone to tend to her body. Gods, what a day this has been!
Yes, that would be an elegant solution to my predicament. I'm afraid that I'm rather new to this … state of being. I haven't figured out that trick yet.
Just keep following the road. If you see a xanmeer, you're going in the right direction. And eventually you'll hear Lady Laurent. She's rather loud, as far as dryskins go.

You know, those great stone step pyramids that rise out of the Black Marsh swamps. Our misguided ancestors built them for some reason. The one near Glenbridge has always been a curiosity and was relatively safe to explore.\n\nUntil the curse, that is.

The mysteries of beyond are great. A creature capable of consuming so many souls must be enormously powerful.\n\nBut I have seen your skill in action. No one is better suited for this battle. May you stay moist and nimbly dance through the flames.

Someone she trusted enough to share a drink with. There's little doubt in my mind that she left with them voluntarily. \n\nThe question is, was this person really who they appeared to be. We won't know the answer to that until we catch up with them.

Oh ho, more than enough! These people feel a deep fire in their bellies. But someone needed to fan it until the flames shoot out their mouths! We have done this very thing.\n\nAnd with the addition of three Winds of Stonewastes, we are unbeatable!

You're right, he isn't here with us, but make no mistake—I spent many turns of the season at his side.\n\nHe's brash and filled with bees, but you'll find few with stronger character. He'll be here, if he isn't lurking around already.
Of course I am. How silly to even ask. The Winds of Stonewastes have stood up to much worse than a flimsy army and a paper mudcrab such as this warlord Naxhosa. This will be no trouble.
You know, you might not have made a bad member of the Winds yourself. We could use another.\n\nThink about it.

That is true. Perhaps you are right that I should not underestimate the danger that might be present behind those walls.\n\nBut by the same token, he should not have killed one of our own. If he sought to frighten the Winds, he failed.

I couldn't say. Dagon wants to kill us all, right? Grandee Bramia used to … used to tell me stories about great red siege craft dragged by giants with lava for blood.\n\nNever thought Mephala had an interest in conquest, but who knows?

It's Daedric in origin. Our employer claimed it was recently uncovered, but I have a hard time believing no one noticed until now. And despite its condition it doesn't seem that old. Barely any overgrowth at all.\n\nNone of it makes any sense.
Heh. No one ever makes just one of anything.\n\nI hope this was the last of these machines, but you … you need to keep your eyes fixed on this. Don't forget what you saw in there.

Morgane and I are … were … new to Blackwood. This was the only one we encountered, but people in Leyawiin insisted there are more—some craft of the Longhouse Emperors.\n\nIf more exist, I hope you do the same to them.

Like I said, the victim was one of the Dibellites high priests—a woman named Rolaine.\n\nThis was sixty years ago, mind, but my grandfather tells me the locals worshiped the ground she walked on. Thought she was a prophet, or something near to it.

These damned zealots rallied half the city. Gathered up torches and shovels and ran him and my father out of town with nothing but the clothes on their backs.\n\nEven outside of Gideon, the rumors followed him. We haven't had a moment's peace since.

Aye. My Granna Cerise was Rolaine's flower-bearer. Followed her everywhere she went. When a heap of treasure went missing and Rolaine vanished, Granna was the prime suspect.\n\nNo one could prove it, of course, since they never found her.
Bravil. Took an awful long time, what with the Three-Banners War and all. But I made it, and I'm not leaving till I settle this once and for all.

An apology? Ha! I'm not that naive.\n\nI'm a carpenter by trade. I'll settle for people not hiding my tools and splitting my saw horses six times a month. It's about respect. To Oblivion with the rest!

Might have happened yesterday for all these people care. Nobody holds a grudge like an Imperial.\n\nIf your name is Gemain, you're lower than dirt in their eyes. I just had a son a couple years back and he's already catching it on the chin! He's two!

I … well, not exactly.\n\nFor now, I can say I have good reason to think there's more to the story. I'll know more once we look around their makeshift Temple of Dibella, and I'll feel much better about doing that having you with me.

I don't know yet. I just know we have to look.\n\nTake this. It's a rare bit of magic called a memory stone. Granna Cerise gave it to Grandpa Lierre the night before she supposedly murdered Priestess Rolaine and fled. Maybe it'll show us something.

Ha! I'm a carpenter, not a mage. But according to this Dark Elf I showed it to, the mushroom wizards up in Morrowind use them to store their memories.\n\nThe catch is you have to stand where the memories occurred to wake up the magic in the stone.

Then you'll remember they hold their owner's memories inside them. I only learned about the stone's power a year ago, when a mage passed through Bravil and took an interest.\n\nHe said memory stones only awaken in the place where the memory occurred.

Aye, that's the hope. I know we face long odds on this. Magic stones and lost memories sound like storybook nonsense. But it's really all I've got to go on.\n\nHow about we start our search on the ground floor?
I followed you. I was glad to see Annyce back in town, but I knew deep down that wasn't my girl and watching her act the part made the worry in my gut so much worse. I had to see for myself.

As I understand it, memory stones soak up memories so you can revisit them later—like watching a play. But you have to be in the place where the memory occurred or it doesn't work.\n\nThe mage I met told me this one's worth a small fortune.

Good question. Granna Cerise didn't come from money. Grandpa Lierre told me Priestess Rolaine owned whole troves of baubles like this, though. Maybe it was hers.\n\nOf course that begs the question: why did Granna Cerise have Rolaine's stone? Curious.
Back at the Happy Crow. I told Bradon he could put whatever she liked on my tab if it kept her occupied.\n\nIf you wish to find the freeloader, that's where she'll be.

From what we have seen thus far, it seems as though these terrible rituals tear the souls from the victim. I believe the Sul-Xan found a way to transfer the stolen spirits into the idol in order to power it. It is dark magic, certainly.

Aye. Way Grandpa Lierre tells it, in the weeks before Rolaine vanished, a handful of novitiates went missing.\n\nNone of them were popular enough to raise an outcry. People said they must have just left—trying to get out from under Rolaine's shadow.

Granna Cerise helped all the novitiates—cleaning linens, tending to flowers, arranging sheet music. She knew everyone.\n\nThese people probably would have pinned the disappearances on her too, but the story took a dark turn after Rolaine's murder.

The Dibellites decided it must have been a conspiracy! The missing novitiates were all in on the plot. Now we see the truth of it.\n\nCan't be sure, but whoever murdered these novitiates might have murdered Rolaine, too! We should keep investigating.
She had an alibi. Grandpa Lierre said they were on holiday during the first two disappearances. They visited the Topal Bay every Midyear. Plenty of witnesses.\n\nIt wasn't her. I'm sure of it.

I did say that, didn't I? I suppose that even the charms of the Lady of Love can be too much for some folk. Not everyone can stand to bask in Dibella's glory for too long at a time.\n\nBut they were good people. I liked them all.

I heard them talking about a ruin north of Gideon. I know that particular place well. Let me mark its location on your map.\n\nWhen you can spare a moment, come back and enjoy one of our ceremonies. All should open their hearts to the secrets of love.

Rebuild, naturally. Nothing stands forever, even the great stone structures from our past. This impermanence is the truth of the world.\n\nI suppose I must train new apprentices as well. I cannot replace those I lost, but nor would I wish to.

Then, their death served a greater purpose after all. Courageous beyond the end, those two. I erect the spine of humility as their teacher.\n\nThank you for telling me this. Knowing they rejoin the one sets my heart at ease.
Alone. I suppose I am. I had not considered that. I will no longer be a part of the One, but something separate. It's unsettling, but also exciting.
I need a mortal pact to do anything more than create an illusion. I traded dreams because they are the neighbor of knowledge and within my reach. I don't have much else to offer a mortal in exchange.
Correct. The terms are not important, only the bargain matters. If I find someone willing to form a … less troublesome pact, then maybe I could stay?

Misguided as Cres was, I don't believe they acted in malice. There aren't many stories of compassionate Daedra, but it seems at least some of them might be true.\n\nThe question is, does this little Daedra's story have to end in tragedy?

What exactly are you implying, hmm? The fact that we share a certain degree of familiarity doesn't give you cause to be rude.\n\nStill, I see your point. Let's just say that where Stibbons is concerned, every day includes a modicum of trouble.
Trying to pitch me into Orkey's gnarled teeth—or Dagon's rather. Felt like all the air was sucked out of my lungs. Would have killed me if you hadn't come along.\n\nWas it always this hot in here?

Haven't felt this bad since I nearly drowned in the Sea of Ghosts, but I can feel my strength coming back. I—I think I'll be good enough to move once I've caught my breath.\n\nI'll be fine. Help the others while there's still time.

I'm just hired muscle. I don't meddle with magic. They—they were talking though. About positioning the other stones. They sent each of us as an escort. Split us up.\n\nIf they got the better of me, I'm sure the others are in just as much trouble now.

Oh! I thought I'd never see that again! Thank you. I have a great deal to add to it now. I think it's good to record all you can, good and bad. It forces you to think about what you've seen and done, makes you more mindful of how events shape you.

Among her followers she dropped the mask she'd been wearing. She's a Daedra. These cultists are the usual misguided fools dabbling with things they don't really understand. They're true believers. I'll never forget how they howled for her adulation.

Xigira was yelling at her followers about jeopardizing the foothold when I was trying to escape. I don't quite get what she meant, but I think they're turning this place into their stronghold.\n\nAnd, I saw Xigira when they caught me. The real Xigira.

Dark Elves have not been kind to my egg-kin, and I have not been kind to theirs in turn. I see I judged her too harshly. I should apologize to her … and her brother, if he still lives. He was taken prisoner by Xigira, personally.
To the heart of the vault, she said. Farther down this path. Where it leads, I cannot say. I don't even recognize this place anymore. I only know it dries my scales worse than Ebonheart.

Most assuredly! Safe means few dangers to deal with, and intact … well, intact ancient structures often contain the most remarkable treasures!\n\nIt was the perfect site to explore. Before my manservant went and bungled the basket, as it were.

Smash, smash! Destroy the mirror and my vassals will be free! \n\nNo longer will we be cowed and bound to these featherless masters. These fools will feel the sharpness of our beaks, the cutting wind of our feathers! Go, my tall soldier! Go!

Huh. I've heard of soul gems before, but not black soul gems. I thought mages just used them on rabbits and Goblins and such. These black ones can suck up the souls of men and mer? Eight preserve us.\n\nThe ledger said the killer traded them, right?

Hmm. I never told you how Priestess Rolaine died, did I? She left to visit Leyawiin in her carriage, along with her flower-bearer, Cerise … my grandmother. They never arrived.\n\nMaybe this map shows where they went! Let's see where it leads, eh?

Never heard of them. But then again, honest carpenters like me don't do much business with soul-stealing wizards.\n\nIt's all academic anyway. There's no way of knowing if the trade even took place. Unless that map you found contains a clue?

Grandpa said there'd been talk about how Granna Cerise and the other junior priestesses of Dibella were greedy. When news came that Priestess Rolaine had been murdered, none questioned they'd killed her.\n\nInstead, they burned Grandpa Lierre's home.

I don't see how it could be anything else. Sadly, I imagine the angry people who burned down our home and chased Grandpa Lierre away are dead now, so they're beyond justice.\n\nYet we can still clear my grandmother's name. We must, for Grandpa Lierre!

You're asking me? I figured you'd know!\n\nWhoever they are, I guess they like souls? The ledger said that the killer was bringing black soul gems to trade for a reward of some sort. Maybe they're part of the Waking Flame cult the killer mentioned?

By the Eight, I hope not! I can't imagine how horrifying it would be to die, but not die. To be trapped forever in one of those black soul gems. Just thinking about it makes me feel like I want to vomit.\n\nI'm so glad I have you to protect me.

So you do know about them. I figured. You seem to be taking this all so calmly, like you've seen all this horror and worse.\n\nSo these Waking Flame folks are still around? If our killer was one of them, that means they've been in Gideon for decades.

Grandmother told me the horn's note drove Minotaurs mad with fear and rage. But sometimes the horn called Minotaurs to battle even when no one sounded it.\n\nMaybe the Minotaurs are here because of the Horn of Magnificence.

Let me see. Yes! I've seen that seal too many times. See the flowers encircling the face? It's a symbol of Dibella. This is a high priestess' signet ring.\n\nIt can't be a coincidence. That skeleton is Priestess Rolaine. We found her!

So, Priestess Rolaine was transporting those? Why? Did Granna Cerise know about it? They left town together and vanished together. My grandmother's skeleton isn't here, so ….\n\nBy the Eight, could Priestess Rolaine be the killer?

Do you think …? No, it couldn't have been Granna. She wasn't in Gideon when the novitiates were killed! The Priestess had access to the treasury, had the ear of the people … it all makes sense, except how she died.\n\nWe just— Wait. Look there!

Bradon promised he'd get me a lute if I keep up the chores. A little practice and I'm sure the travelers will take notice. Once folk start coming around to see me play, maybe I'll take the act on the road. Like those Elves! That'd do.
Rhymes with bless? Yes! Alchemy helped me with my … outfit. Do you like it? I really like masks. Faces are hard. Um, expressions I mean. Acting.
Thank you! I can't wait to see it. Alchemy says I must try out. I imagine there will be lots of trying things. I can't wait!

It's wonderful. And scary. I'm … I'm me. No one expects me to behave in a certain way. I can just be. And when people ask me things about myself, I just make them up, and they laugh! Except Alchemy, she just rests her face in her hands usually.

I am betrothed! An arranged match, but a rather good one. \n\nI have a Silvelle heirloom—a ring—to present to my affianced. Or rather, I had it. While enjoying the end of my bachelorhood I, well, lost it gambling. I need that ring back.
Come on now. I suspect the knowledge of what I plan lurks within your strange but impressive belly.\n\nI will drink! We all will. For many, many nights. Then perhaps I will finally choose a student.

Feats of strength. Or, perhaps, I will test their knowledge of the most offensive words in Jel. No warrior can ignite their sinew without shouting something horrible!\n\nUntil then, I know the village is safe. This satisfies me.

The future? I know of no such thing. Today, I will help the village rebuild.\n\nI quite liked the hidden life out in the woods. But perhaps it was not the life I was meant to live. The shadows are an absence, where the light brings life.

Such an upstart bog dog. You know nothing of the journey of Meer-Ta. Yes, I did face death on a frequent basis. But you have seen my power. Nothing can stand tall before me.\n\nAlso … I had companionship back then. We fought for peace. It was good.

Without delay I will return to my studies. Now that I know the library within the ruins holds treasures, I expect to spend many days there.\n\nHowever, perhaps I should renew my bonds with the other Winds. And train someone new. The peace must be kept.

I lost it to a woman named Grenetta. She's with the bandits who hide out at Illessan Tower. If you and Bastian find her, you'll find the ring.\n\nIn return, I'll give him the old letter my father kept from him. It's from a Hallix family servant.

I had nothing to do with that—I just found the letter while searching for a little gold to buy back the ring. But if it motivates Bastian to help me out, then we both win. \n\nGo get the ring. I'll meet you nearby and give Bastian the letter then.

I've seen it a hundred times. All of the Silvelles have a way of warming up when they need me to do something for them.\n\nOffering something of value for my help, something about my mother? That's new.

He could, but he knows I would break his bloody nose. No, Quistley got himself into some new trouble, so he went looking for something he knew I'd want. And he's right, damn it. \n\nWhat has Lord Silvelle been keeping from me?

I know, I should have told you from the start. But I didn't want to scare you off—thinking I was crazy or something.\n\nIt started a month or so ago. A ghostly young woman rouses me from my bed every night and stares at me. Like she wants something.

I know it is! She just stared us both in the face and guided us to her remains, right? But what now?\n\nShe put an end to Rolaine's plot, but no one will believe me. The Gemains will keep getting stepped on. They'll say I faked the whole thing.

That … might actually work. Keshu the Black Fin and her Argonians couldn't give two croaks about Dibella and her flock. Keshu's war mage, Fire-From-Nowhere, knows local history. He might just listen.\n\nGranna Cerise gave us the proof. Let's use it!

That array by Eolaf seems to be the heart of the ritual, but the magic is being drawn to another focal point nearby. Destroying that might lighten the load on Eolaf, and the backlash of ending the ritual by force. It's the best chance of saving him.

Rolaine. Ah yes, the prophet-woman these smoothskins mourn. She has been dead for a very long time, but still they cry. It is very strange, but that is the Imperial way, I guess.\n\nWhat did you discover? Something to quiet their hearts, I hope?

Well then. That is not what I expected you to say.\n\nIf this is true, there will be a great wailing in the Dibellaseum. Disbelief, also. They curse the woman, Cerise Gemain, and all who hatch from her clutch. Your proof must be hard as stone.

I can tell you speak the truth.\n\nIn the name of Keshu, I claim the Breton, Faric Gemain, as my charge. I place my hand upon the Hist and swear—no harm will befall him here, and the truth of this will come to light, no matter how grim.

Honestly, I'm impressed she made it this far, but my gut tells me she's still here. I think we should keep looking for the rest of those sacrificial stones. Whoever's still bound up in the cult's rituals is in the greatest danger.

Not much, I'm afraid. I was very young.  But … I've always wondered why she left me with the Silvelles. They weren't related to her or my father. I never found a satisfactory answer as to how or why I ended up with them.

Only that I had no family left, and I should be grateful that they took me in. \n\nIn time, I learned that my father was the last of the Hallixes. My mother, though … I asked Lord Silvelle about her family a time or two, but he never said much.
Right. You're right. This isn't the time to lose it. There's still hope for the others.\n\nGhalor couldn't have wandered far like this. There must be another ritual site nearby. Let's go!

Maybe. I guess we'll never find out, will we?\n\nOne thing's for sure—love is much more complicated than I ever gave it credit for. That shouldn't really come as a surprise to someone who writes about it professionally, but here we are.

A hunch, mostly.\n\nWithout the power of the spirit lantern to illuminate him, Mathen should just be a whisper in the wind for most people. I think it actually makes it all even more romantic! Every moment together is a secret rendezvous. Marvelous!

Ha! I'm a romance novelist poking around a dingy castle in the swamp. Do I strike you as someone overly concerned with appearances?\n\nNo, it will all turn out. I doubt people will even be able to see Mathen.
Not in the slightest. The light of Aetherius pales before Yisara's smiling face. I have no regrets. Not anymore.
Hmph. In truth, I hardly care. I'm not so petty that I would wish some ill fate upon her, but I'm in no rush to see her again.\n\nWherever she went, she can stay there.

I don't know! He's my little brother, I have to try! If—if it comes to it … end the ritual prematurely. I'd rather send Liam into the arms of Mother Morrowind than let Oblivion have him.\n\nJust, try. Please?

I heard plenty about my father's treason. I think the Silvelles wanted me to understand how fortunate I was that they took me in. About my mother? The Silvelles only said she died of shame.\n\nOh, and I had an older sister. Who died too.

It may sound foolish, but I'd dearly like to know why my mother decided to send me to the Silvelles. We're not even related. And I want to know more about how she and my sister died. Shame usually isn't fatal.

I brought it. I wouldn't go back on my word—don't you make that face at me, Bastian!\n\nLook, I don't want to disappoint Mauriene, and I've promised my parents that I won't. This is the last time I wish to involve Bastian in my affairs.

None the worse for its travels. Thank the gods.\n\nBastian's letter is right there. I can't tell you why my father held onto it. So, Bastian, you should have no quarrel with me. I think this successfully concludes our business.

Oh, him? Yes, the blacksmith will be quite fine. Nuxul has never kept his head at our village parties. Always passes out from drink before the moon rises to the peak.\n\nHe is an excellent blacksmith, better than he believes. But a terrible drinker.

As a guess, I would say they are Lut-Eileel—Sharp-Eyed People. A petty tribe who revel in preying on other Argonians. They build nothing, but have no problem leeching off others to survive.\n\nMay their spirits never find dirt.

He is a vicious, cackling hyena. The first time I saw him, I swear his eyes were as black as a well.\n\nQuick with a blade, too. He made the first blow when Satul-Sa fell. I will never forget his laugh as she bled. Like I said, a total tzilnech.

Seems like a nice place, does it not? Far away from the noise and activity of the village. No one to bother me, unless the blacksmith comes knocking.\n\nI just wanted some place in the mud, where I can hear the frog-song at night. So here I am.
I see. Some minor errand, I assume?\n\nHmm. The house does not make a habit of employing imbeciles. You must have some talent. I take some comfort in that.

They're the ruling body of Leyawiin. When things fell apart in Cyrodiil, local officials stepped up. Although I wouldn't call Councilor Lovidicus a local official. He used to sit on the Elder Council.\n\nStrange times we live in, eh?

It's difficult to explain.\n\nMorgane and I expected to find Daedric halls and chambers, but there's much more. Vast caverns that look like they were pulled from Tamriel itself. And … I can't say for certain, but I think we entered another realm.

Yes. A canyon of fire and stone. If I didn't know any better, I'd say we entered the realm of Dagon himself.\n\nThis doomvault is … it's a place between places. I can't explain it. You'll see what I mean when you go inside.
I think I remember Inalieth. A little Wood Elf lady. She was kind to me.\n\nWhy would Lord Silvelle keep this from me? What became of my mother's jewels? Why was I not sent to my sister?

That's what I was told, but I don't understand. Clearly my sister was alive at the time my mother told Inalieth to take me to her. Did she die before we left Daggerfall?\n\nI need to go to Redfur Trading Post in Grahtwood. Inalieth might have answers.

Inalieth? You are several weeks too late. Poor thing. Vayzah was not here when it happened. Nellor the innkeeper found coins missing and blamed Inalieth.\n\nSent her off just like that, after Inalieth worked here for years! She would never steal!
She went into the woods. The Wood Elves, they love their trees, but Inalieth is not young anymore. This one worries.\n\nVayzah thinks she made camp somewhere south of the village?

Bastian? That little lad grown to such a big man! I have wondered and worried about him for so many years.\n\nLeaving him with the Silvelles never sat right with me. He should have been sent to his sister in Wayrest.

That wasn't true! Clairene married Count Auzin of Wayrest. Just last year I asked a traveler from Stormhaven about them. He told me the Auzins and their children were well.\n\nAre you saying that poor Bastian was never sent to her?

That was not what his lady mother wanted! Knowing that Bastian still had his sister was a comfort to her in her last days. And what of the jewels she provided? What did Lord Silvelle do with Bastian's fortune? \n\nDisgraceful! Why you poor lad!

The wilds can be dangerous in the best of times, but things have gotten worse of late. With all Blackwood's troubles, the Ivory Brigade can't spare many brigadines to keep the roads safe and the monsters in check.\n\nSo we hire mercenaries.

He did not introduce himself. He just gave me the letter and my instructions, along with a generous amount of gold.\n\nThe gentleman did ask if I knew of any establishments that serve mudcrab goulash, but that was the extent of our interaction.

Absolutely! I think I'm really cut out for it! You get to travel, meet interesting people, see ancient places. And you get to solve all sorts of riddles and mysteries.\n\nAnd sometimes people throw you a celebration party, too. A party with cake!

I feel … relieved, I suppose. And confused. It's strange. My mother made arrangements for me? I wasn't just forgotten. \n\nWhy did Lord Silvelle ignore her wishes? Was it simple greed, or did something else happen?

I want to meet her, of course. But I wonder if perhaps she didn't want a tie to our disgraced family. Or maybe she didn't want to be burdened with a child to raise.\n\nI need to think. I don't want to just appear on her doorstep, you know?

I wouldn't expect you to know about them. How many local cults are you familiar with? You seem so calm about all of this!\n\nSo these Waking Flame folks are still around? If our killer was one of them, that means they've been in Gideon for decades.

Because it doesn't matter what I believe. The legates heard her claim and I was ordered to keep watch on the ruin. Observe and report. That's all.\n\nAs to why I don't trust her, she's a little too fluent in the ways of Daedric cults for my liking.

She was a little too certain—a little too specific—in her knowledge when trying to convince the legates. \n\nNo upstanding, Divines-fearing folk would go into such lurid detail reporting a crime of this nature. She's not to be trusted at her word.

Why didn't you say so? Leyawiin's problems are legion, and now the Wood Elf archer's predictions seem to be coming true. Damn these old Imperial secrets! Councilor Jirich has disappeared and the Ivory Brigade is already spread too thin for my liking.

The Wood Elf, Eveli Sharp-Arrow. She brought news that the Dark Brotherhood was targeting members of the Elder Council. All because of some secret of the Longhouse Emperors.\n\nWe took her warning seriously, but Jirich refused brigadine protection.

With that guild of assassins, I'm not sure what to think. But Jirich is missing and I don't have enough brigadines at the ready to conduct a proper search. \n\nYou look capable. So, care to earn some gold and help us determine the councilor's fate?

A few. But we don't want to merely restore it to its original profitable status … my brother and I always strive for more. We rely on our ingenuity for success. \n\nOur dear uncle was rather kind-hearted when it came to debts. We'll change that.

It's not far. Pretty much dead center of the city. The place is called Armor and Fine Garments. Keshu suggested we should ask for a tailor by the name of Percius Loche. He's supposed to know his stuff.\n\nI'll meet you there!

A ruin? I wonder why they went there. Haven't those two had enough adventures after all they've been through?\n\nWe should go find the Ambitions or they'll miss the party. Did the priest say which ruin in particular?
Lead on, then! The party's going to start soon and we don't want to be late!\n\nI for one want to get a nice piece of cake! Or maybe a slice of pie? Oh, broken branches! I'll just have both!

She initially refused the captain's offer, but she received a letter that made her … uneasy.\n\nLast I saw, she was headed back to the city by way of the eastern gate. But she never returned to her manor, so I came to look for her. Please, find her!
Vinnus, h-he's dead? How? \n\nNo, he wouldn't want me to mourn when there is still work to be done. This letter mentions a stone. Hand it to me. Carefully!

When reports of the portals and the cultists started coming in, Vinnus packed his bags. He couldn't sit idly by and wait for more news, even after I asked him to.\n\nThis is the first I've heard from him since he left.

Unfortunately not. Or at least, we don't yet. More researchers have gone through the portals, maybe they'll be luckier than my Vinnus was.\n\nBetween their findings and this stone, we will be able to uncover what Dagon is planning. We have to.
Help you? I can indeed! It's good I decided to pack up and move to Leyawiin. I dread to think of anyone other than myself dressing you for a formal event.\n\nSo, how formal are we talking about here?

The Happy Averno Shipping Company was gifted to my brother and I by our dear departed uncle. Formerly, it was one of Blackwood's main trade enterprises. We thought, with a little elbow grease, it might prove a profitable venture.

An event thrown by a member of the former Elder Council? My word! That requires the utmost in formal attire. Unfortunately, such clothing carries a hefty price. There's only so much I can do, even for a friend, but perhaps we can arrange something.

We discovered our uncle's affairs were more … precariously poised than described, for one. Many of his charters and contracts were voided by the Three Banners War. \n\nThe Fang-Furls did the rest. They came for everything they could steal.

Sophus is dead? Damn! Was it the Dark Brotherhood? What am I saying, of course it was!\n\nI've torn this place apart, but so far I haven't found anything related to Imperial secrets or the Ambitions. Maybe you can spot something I missed.

Just line up your sights with a suitable anchor point, release the bolt, and get ready to fly.\n\nDon't worry, they're pretty much designed to do all the work. The worst you'll have to worry about is underestimating the pull and spraining your neck.

Some city official wants to curry favor with a local Argonian chief. We've been asked to find something … appropriate. And if we can remove a threat like Old Deathwart at the same time, so much the better.\n\nThe job pays well, anyway.

Calia's power is recharging faster than I anticipated. It will soon reach the point where I won't be able to help her. Then, she'll either release it and destroy everything around her, or it will consume her.\n\nEither way, people die. Including Calia.

A hundred years old, at most. I couldn't tell you who built it, or how it came to be demolished though. I didn't get much time to study it before those fetching cultists tried to throw a sack over my head and drag me off.

It's a big place. Xynaa taught me how to avoid notice there. And it's the last place Dagon's followers will think to look for us. As soon as Calia can control her power, we'll come back. I promise.\n\nThank you, my friend. For everything.

Use the Mysterium Xarxes to open a portal to the Deadlands. It's the only place I can think of where Calia will be safe. The realm naturally siphons off a portion of our power. That will give me time to teach Calia to control it on her own.
Murdered? Gods, keep your voice down. Do you want to start a panic?\n\nTell me what you found in the watchtower.

That explains some of it, but not all. We need to locate Talaise.\n\nSince you're already involved and working for Captain Rian, I want you to quietly try to find Talaise. Start by talking to the other servants in the kitchen and dining hall.

I've heard that the Ayleids bound Daedra to all sorts of tasks long ago. Perhaps the cultists who are summoning this thing found something the Ayleids left behind.\n\nFeel free to kill any cultists you see, by the way.

Hey, it wasn't my book! I was just keeping it safe for …. Well, as crazy as it sounds, I think I was meant to give it to Sombren. He certainly did more with it than I ever could.\n\nAnd I'm not about to miss the bad dreams and the waking visions.

We go to the party! It's taking place in the gardens behind the governor's mansion.\n\nTo think, this all started because I was curious about a coded journal I found in Emperor Leovic's old retreat. We figured out the secret and now we celebrate!
Well, as I said before, threats to Tamriel have grown like weeds practically everywhere.\n\nWould you prefer to spend time among my Elven kin, the Khajiit of Elsweyr, or men of the north and south?

According to our spies, the land of the catfolk is in sorry shape. Imperial holdouts sit upon the throne and a rage of Dragons spilled out of the Halls of Colossus, burning everything in their path.\n\nIf it's adventure you seek, you'll find it there.

If you take the gate to Vvardenfell, you can meet the Dark Elves and maybe even their god-king, Vivec.\n\nYou could also travel south to Summerset Isle—our ancestral home and the primary seat of power for the High Elves.

Certainly.\n\nOne of these gates appear to go to Western Skyrim—a hermitical kingdom of Nords led by King Svargrim. The other leads to Blackwood, at the southern tip of Cyrodiil. Imperial remnants rule there.

Always! Though the natives don't make it easy.\n\nHigh Elves of Summerset don't share the Direnni's pragmatism. They're often too proud to ask for help. But our agents reported some strange activity around the Crystal Tower. It's probably worth a look.

Squeezing information out of the Dark Elves is delicate business. To be honest, we know far less about what's going on in Morrowind than we should.\n\nI can tell you that Vivec put out a summons for heroes recently. That's worrying.

The Nords of Western Skyrim are … inhospitable. To put it lightly. Even so, we've been able to glean a few things.\n\nI've read reports about increased vampiric activity in the region. Never a good sign. They need stout adventurers to deal with it.

Our agents are investigating a handful of strange Daedric structures hidden away in the swamps near Gideon and Leyawiin.\n\nI honestly couldn't tell you how they got there, but the presence of Daedric anything in Tamriel is always cause for concern.

Perhaps it followed you to prevent you from reaching your … well, destiny sounds a bit too grandiose. Let's just say to stop you from reaching your potential.\n\nThen again, maybe the power of this place brought you here to stop Shyazzel.

Ha! An Elf can hope. Answering that question will probably keep me occupied for the next hundred years.\n\nIs the helix connected to the Adamantine Tower? How does it perceive distant corners of Tamriel? I may never understand it, but I'll do my best.
Probably not. But what's a life without unanswered questions? Right? Boring if you ask me.

It's … changing. More like it's two skies mixing together. It wasn't like that before.\n\nI'm not sure what exactly that means just yet, but I'd wager it's got something to do with the cultists' ritual.

Choosing exile to spare others from danger is a noble decision. I wish them well, even as I worry about Sombren and Calia out there on their own. \n\nEveryone else has gathered. Eat, drink. Talk to your friends. In time, I shall address the crowd.

Anyone you like. They have all come to show you their appreciation. And do not leave too swiftly. I intend to boast of your accomplishments soon!\n\nI see Eveli has arrived. Perhaps you should begin with her?

It's possible this is all just a side effect of the ritual, not its intent. Who knows, maybe their magic isn't just feeding on the souls of those they've captured, but everything here?\n\nAll the more reason to stop them quickly.

Yeah, these are definitely orders. It mentions Bloodrun Cave. That's northeast of Leyawiin, toward the edge of Blackwood territory.\n\nWell, as the spinners always say, the best way to find out what's happening in the clearing is to step into it.

Of course it does! Nothing has been easy since I found that strange book and started chasing down Leovic's secret.\n\nWell, are you still interested in solving the mystery of the Ambitions? Will you come with me to Bloodrun Cave?

I don't. I know she's about eighteen years older than I am—I was a late-in-life child. \n\nAccording to my mother's servant Inalieth, Clairene went off to marry Elmonde Auzin soon after I was born. Just before the fall of House Hallix.

I've heard his name a time or two, usually when Lord Silvelle and his visitors got to talking about court gossip. The Auzins are a minor house with lands in the countryside of Stormhaven. Elmonde Auzin is said to be respectable, at least.

That's the question, isn't it? Why did she send me to the Silvelles? Was her own situation too precarious? Did she not want the care of a child?\n\nOr perhaps she's dead. It's possible Inalieth is mistaken, and Lord Silvelle told me the truth.

I don't see why he wouldn't. The taint on the Hallix name makes other nobles uneasy, but that was many years ago now.\n\nOf course, if he didn't know about my mother's arrangements, he might be very surprised to learn he has a brother-in-law.

I don't know about that, but I certainly feel more experienced! And I have you to thank. Well, you and Captain Rian and Governor Keshu and poor Farrul Lupus …. Can you believe this all started because I couldn't leave Emperor Leovic's secret alone?

That's right! I almost forgot! And we should be ready to help Sombren and Calia when they return. I don't believe that Mehrunes Dagon and his followers are just going to leave them alone.\n\nI really thought the Ambitions were actual weapons, though.

She's been captured by slavers! Clairene was on her way to visit a friend near Koeglin when she was attacked. Luckily one of her guards managed to trail the slavers to Koeglin Mine.\n\nI must arrange a rescue at once. State your business—swiftly!

Bastian Hallix? That's him over there, isn't it? He looks just like his father.\n\nI don't know how to say this, but … Clairene believes he died as an infant. After her family's scandal, I thought it best to distance her from the Hallix name.

Interesting. She arrived a short time ago with a tale straight out of a mystery novel. She said that Emperor Leovic's former steward had been murdered by the Dark Brotherhood. Killed over some secret pertaining to the Longhouse Emperors.
