No, but Councilor Lovidicus has heard the term. Says it's a landmark in the Sul-Xan territory. The documents suggested it's a site connected to the Four Ambitions. Maybe where the weapons are stored?\n\nWe need to consult with an expert on that region.

Governor Keshu of Gideon! Councilor Lovidicus says she knows the swamps and bogs of Black Marsh like the back of her hand.\n\nSo, can I count on you? Will you come with me to Gideon to talk to Keshu the Black Fin?

Hey! Just because I got the shivers doesn't mean I'm not up to this. It's a purely natural reaction to something that includes both the word pit and the word outsider.\n\nI'll be right by your side every step of the way. Count on it!

I'm afraid so. And I told the Silvelles to let Bastian believe he had no family left. It was the safest course. Are the gods punishing me now for that choice? Is it my fault that Clairene—?\n\nWait! You and Hallix seem able. You can save her!

I … I suppose I can understand that. If the choice was telling a lie or risking the gallows for my sister, then Auzin made the right decision. It isn't cowardice to fear for someone you love.\n\nAnd it's clear that he fears for Clairene now.

I know the place. Bandits and outlaws often lair there.\n\nI'll sort out the rest of this later, after we make sure Clairene is safe. I couldn't bear it if I got so close to finding her, only to lose her now.

I doubt it. It's ironic that Quistley's fecklessness is the only reason I found out about all of … this.\n\nStrange. It feels like finding out I was never supposed to be left with strangers has lifted a burden I never knew I was carrying.

True. Hello, I thought you were dead? That might not be the best way to start a conversation. \n\nI've never been good at talking about my feelings. Maybe I should keep it simple and just say that I'd like to get to know her.

I've only just taken on my independence, so to speak. I like traveling with you. We're helping a lot of people.\n\nI'm just happy to learn that some of my family survived. I hope Clairene feels the same way. Beyond that? We'll see.
I think this ruin isn't actually part of Nirn. More like a piece of our world bottled up and the cult is trying to fill the bottle from another source.

We have to be, don't we? We've put our trust in your hands and we have to assume that you will keep us safe.\n\nThe Argonian seems intent on protecting us. If all else fails, Calia and I aren't defenseless. We shall be fine until you return.

Other than when we were moved from one sanctum to another, yes. I remember the caretakers telling us it was for our own good. That the sanctum protected us. I'm kind of nervous to be away from it. But it's kind of exciting, too.

Anything I can offer would be a guess. You and Eveli are much more familiar with the situation than I am. \n\nFor my part, I will gather the Black Fin Legion and make sure the twins are comfortable and safe. On that, you have my word.
No. I was waiting for you. Besides, they said they were supposed to deliver it to you specifically. Their instructions were very clear about that.

Leyawiin demands, does it? Very well.\n\nThis sanctuary belongs to the Dark Brotherhood. It has for a very long time. I've been given the joyous task of reopening it. I assure you, we're a business. We have no designs on Leyawiin or the councilors.

Obviously, some enemy of the councilors who wants to confuse you. Throw suspicion on the Dark Brotherhood. Keep you chasing after shadows while they accomplish whatever it is they hope to do.\n\nPerhaps we can work together to—what?

It makes sense that the count wanted to protect my sister. I could almost forgive that. But I suspect he was also interested in protecting his own good name.\n\nI can't help but wonder about the life I could have had if he'd chosen differently.

No. I was much better off than if I'd been left in an orphanage. But I wasn't family and I wasn't quite the help. If I hadn't met you, I would have spent the rest of my life looking after the Silvelles' interests without ever really belonging.

The Three Banners War. Let the alliances fight over the Ruby Throne, as long as they leave us in peace.\n\nI just wish I had more soldiers to spare for this new threat that Eveli Sharp-Arrow brought to our attention.

Indeed. Since the fall of the Empire, the Ivory Brigade had to redouble its efforts to replace the Imperial Legions. We maintain active defenses in the north to keep the ongoing war at bay, but we have our hands full with refugees, bandits, and such.

Something remarkable!\n\nYou appear to have absorbed the Aetherial energy stored in the shard. I've never seen that happen before. Come to think of it, are you all right? You're not dizzy or anything are you?

Thank the stars.\n\nIt's possible that if you find more skyshards during your travels, you might access some deeper connection to reality itself! Very exciting! Shards often split into three fragments. So, keep an eye out for two more, all right?

She apparently has been investigating this so-called Longhouse Emperor secret for a while now. She approached Councilor Lovidicus with news of the murder and evidence to suggest the rest of the Elder Council were in danger.

Ah, then you must be the associate she was waiting for. She'll be glad to hear that you've arrived.\n\nEveli presented her evidence to Councilor Lovidicus. That the members of the Elder Council were in danger. He decided the threat was credible.

Since the collapse of the Empire and the dissolution of the Elder Council, Leyawiin has become an independent city-state. Countess Caro sits on the throne, but the Chamber of Legates governs the city.

Councilor Jirich is a creature of habit. Her daily routine is to stroll along the river and stop to read near a cave across the way.\n\nWhile Eveli Sharp-Arrow examines spots the councilor frequents in the city, you should check these locations.

Did he? Oh, I'd prayed that one of the guards had managed to get through to him! Elmonde must have … that is ….\n\nI'm sorry, but your companion—who is he? He looks just like someone I knew a long time ago.
What? How is this … Bastian? My baby brother? I thought he was dead!\n\nBy the Eight, of course he looks familiar! He takes after our father. Oh, excuse me, please. I am quite overcome.
Look at him! He was so small when I left our home. Our parents were so excited to have another child, so late in their marriage.\n\nWhere has he been all this time? How did he come to find me now?

You do? Then he either torments us both or it's some spectral echo. A disembodied voice, sheared from his body like chitin from a kwama. Perfect. I came to silence ghosts and just made another one.\n\nThis is all my fault.

What's the point? It's not as if we can gather up screams and cobwebs and put him back together again. He was a person, not a teacup!\n\nIf you want to pursue that voice, feel free. I imagine you'll be safer without me. Tiras certainly was.

The clouded varla stones are sort of … thickening the magical fabric of this place. A soul like Tiras's would cause ripples.\n\nAllow me to make a small modification to the censer. There. If you use it now, it should illuminate Tiras's path.
Let's not get ahead of ourselves. Best to focus on navigating the ruin. I seriously doubt that Veyond's shown us all its nasty surprises.

My spymaster tells me that Councilor Vandacia still has eyes in the city. That even now we fear he is aware that we harbor the Ambitions. That he gathers his cultists to assault Gideon.\n\nThe presence of the Ambitions puts my people at risk.

Keep the Ambitions safe, but we need to find a better place to hide them.\n\nTalk to the Ambitions. Perhaps the third one you rescued. Sombren, was it? Eveli said he wasn't locked in a vault when the cult found him. Maybe he knows more than the twins.

I am! It might be a bit morbid, but all this dashing around and puzzle-solving—it's why I love being a wizard! I'd nearly forgotten that, with Tiras and House Telvanni pushing me around.\n\nWe all have to follow our bliss, right? Mine's in old ruins.

I guess someone hired them to eliminate everyone who knows about the secret. The question is, who?\n\nAnd I was told by a more-or-less friendly Dremora named Lyranth that the fate of our world was at stake. So of course I want to figure this all out!

Right! But it turned out, I wasn't the only one trying to learn more about the Ambitions. A group of cracked acorns called the Order of the Waking Flame. Fanatic Mehrunes Dagon cultists. Had to put arrows in more than one of those bastards.

No. The city is no place for a battle. When foes surround you, it is wise to put your back spines to a tree.\n\nWe will move the Ambitions to Fort Redmane. The Imperials abandoned it years ago, but my Black Fin Legion has been restoring its defenses.

No, I have another task for you. Summon what allies you can to Fort Redmane to help defend the Ambitions. I sent my legion ahead, but I fear we will need more warriors.\n\nBefore you go, tell the Ambitions what we are doing and why. They trust you.

Indeed. I confess, I was a little worried that she might not have much to say to me. After all, she's a countess, and we are strangers.\n\nClairene seems kind, though. I like her already. That feels rather good.

Which is something the Silvelles could never do. She has a good heart, I believe.\n\nIt's strange. I left the Silvelles because I wanted to find my own place in the world. Discovering a family I thought I lost? It roots you properly. So to speak.

Things were good when I left. King Bazrag had the clans well in hand.\n\nYou know, I kind of miss that old pain in the tusk. But after everything that happened, I had to strike out and try something new.
Very well. Step back and I'll summon another guardian.

I'd rather not know any more about this damn secret. It's cursed!\n\nBut did you see how they opened that portal? They used their amulet on the pedestal. You still have the one we found? Let's find another pedestal and see if we can follow them.

I knew you'd be a help, but I didn't expect you to just have the answer the moment you walked in. Good job!\n\nCouncilor Jirich's bedroom is upstairs. Let's see if we can find that hidden compartment.
I don't think Sombren means us harm. I think he actually wants to help us. I'm going to be wary of him for a time, but I'll stand by him.\n\nI don't think I have another choice. Not really.

Sombren is a fool. He allowed that Dremora to trick him. Almost got us killed in the process.\n\nI'll listen to what he has to say, but I won't blindly believe it. Not with what's at stake here. The fate of the entire world rests on what we do next.

I told you I had my own avenues of investigation. Why does it surprise you that I would be on hand for Vandacia's major announcement?\n\nBesides, the Dagonist who gave me this coin was only too happy to let me take it from her cold, dead hand.

As I understand it, he has been looking for them ever since Emperor Leovic's death.\n\nI suggest you take advantage of that disguise you're wearing and see what you can find out before Vandacia begins this extravaganza. I shall … remain close by.

Not exactly. I haven't been able to move about as freely as I would like. I don't want to reveal myself to Dagon's Dremora any sooner than I have to.\n\nBut some of these mortals believe that Vandacia has finally found one of the Ambitions.

I think I'll stick around the area for a while. Visit with my brother. Catch up with my cousins before they return to Valenwood. Maybe help round up any remaining cultists still hiding in the wilderness.\n\nAfter that, who knows?
So am I, and this is why we must do this.

He wanted to try something with the book. Away from other people, just in case.\n\nSombren thinks my only chance is if we return to the Deadlands. The nature of the realm naturally draws off my power, making it easier to control.

We must continue to remain vigilant. As long as the war rages to the north, there is always a danger it will spill into our territory.\n\nBeyond that, I plan to continue the work I started. There is still so much to be done!

As Arbitrator of the bazaar, he was responsible for the peacekeeping forces. Gavos and his soldiers were the only ones permitted to be armed, in the interest of preventing violent disputes. It didn't take long for him to abuse that power.

The rumors claimed that he used his office to enrich himself and drove this place to ruin through tax, tariff, and embezzlement. \n\nGavos was overthrown, eventually, but the anvil was never recovered and neither was the prosperity it provided.

Let me see that. A black hand print. The sign of the Dark Brotherhood. But where is the servant, Talaise? Is she involved in this fiasco? And how did she and the assassin get out of the watchtower? My brigadines never left their post.

I'm not sure. By the time we realized the distraction was nothing more than a ruse, the cultists had locked us out!\n\nIf the cultists harm Lovidicus, Vandacia, and the others, I won't rest until they pay.

What? Are you certain? Vandacia has served Blackwood and the Empire before that for more than fifty years. Enough! We need to get inside. Then we can determine the truth of all this.\n\nFind Eveli by the barracks and assist her.

No, probably not. But we're definitely getting stronger. You saw what I did in the sanctum. My power is lightning, but after seeing how Calia lost control, I'm hesitant to use it out here.\n\nI will, though, if I'm called upon to defend my sister.

Remember I told you about that strange book I found? The one with the Daedric writing that I can't read? I've been having bad dreams since I found it. And the dreams are becoming more frequent.\n\nThis time, it happened right while we were talking!

It was just a flash, but it was accompanied by a feeling. I felt a sense of overwhelming evil, all tied up in the figure I saw in my mind. \n\nLike someone held a portrait in front of my face for just a moment and then pulled it away.

As I said, I never heard the term. The Longhouse Emperors were enamored of secrets and code words, though. Perhaps I encountered it, but it was called something else?\n\nIf you think it might be important, ask the assassin when you interrogate him.

Oh, definitely! I learned a lot from that kwama business. Now, safety is my chief priority!\n\nThere might be some bumps along the way, of course. But like the old wizards say: in the mountains of magical praxis, one never climbs in vain!
Yes, yes, I know. I'm not accustomed to fumbling around in the dark like a Goblin. This is a churl's task. Nevertheless, I am the student.\n\nLet's get on with it.
That's because it is bad.\n\nLet's pick up the pace, all right?
I don't know! Look for a lever or a crank wheel or something. Maybe through that door over there? Let's go!

A good question. Perhaps the cost of that victory was too high. Or Gavos's desecration was too great for Zenithar to forgive. \n\nIf anyone was to have kept records of what actually transpired, it would be the trade-ministers.

The bazaar, of course, but this abbey also had a thriving port. And, despite its size, if you wished to conduct business in secret—like plot to overthrow a tyrant—you would need to do it somewhere secluded like the outer grounds.
Seven in ten? Give or take?\n\nYou've faced worse odds before, though. Right? Come on, hero. Let's do some hero-ing.

Have faith, laborer. It seems that the trade-ministers never trusted each other enough to combine these sigils and release the seal on the adytum. Even if that isn't the anvil's final resting place, it is likely Gavos Douar's. That may hold a clue.
Of course, this toil is ours to share. What is it you'd like help with?

It seems as though the new arbitrator was pressuring Ralos for bribes. His mention of the phrase "under the setting sun" seemed to spook Ralos. That must be a clue pointing to his hiding place, but I wouldn't take it literally. It must be a landmark.

He never got the opportunity to send it, it seems. He doesn't say as much, but this meeting spot he suggests to his contact might also be where he hid his sigil for safekeeping. Behind the forging fires could mean the smithy. Couldn't hurt to check.

Obviously somewhere with a fair vantage and out of the way. It's a hiding spot, after all. It might be close to a brewer or importer though, just not likely where the usual clientele would drink. The directory might help point the way.

They belonged to the three trade-ministers of the abbey. Their names were mentioned in some of the documents we uncovered. I'd compare them to the directory you took that rubbing from. It should tell you where they each did business. I'd start there.

Pray that Zenithar will grant me the strength to carry back to the Resolution in Leyawiin. Haha.\n\nNo, once I've confirmed the Golden Anvil lies here, I'll inform the Primate and the Knights of Iron will crusade to cleanse this abbey and recover it.

An order of templars who toil on behalf of the Resolutions. Zenithar prefers peace and prosperity, but he acknowledges that they must be earned. The farmer cannot tame the land while strife rules it, so a soldier's vocation is holy work as well.

Without you, the abbey's downfall would remain a cautionary tale with all the wrong lessons and poor Gavos its villain.\n\nZenithar shone a light on the truth through you, laborer. Your works honor us both.

If the Primate agrees, he might very well become one. Miracles aside, Arbitrator Gavos is a wealth of knowledge long thought lost and he has witnessed firsthand how even a holy temple of Zenithar can become corrupted by avarice. Lessons to remember.

I'm not sure. I only translated a small bit of the code before the assault began.\n\nIt mentioned a vault to protect them, which I assume to mean the Ambitions. It's hidden in the ojel-bak, but I'm not familiar with the term.

Argonian, perhaps? It sounds like it, but I'm not sure.\n\nI haven't reported to Councilor Lovidicus yet. Since it looks like he wants to talk to you now, please inform him of my findings. And tell him I apologize I wasn't able to decipher any more.

How could it not? When faced with even the slightest peril, I panicked. Rather than listening to my teacher, I cast a spell that turned my animus inside out! An experience like that would change anyone.\n\nThen there's the matter of my rescue.
I will try. Members of House Telvanni are stubborn. But true greatness comes from learning. This was a difficult, but necessary lesson.

Any other Telvanni wizard would have left me there without a moment's hesitation.\n\nHouse politics are cruel. But when faced with the prospect of death or professional ruin, Revus saved me anyway. I can guarantee you, I would not have done the same.

Oh, we have much to discuss. Find out how our experiences growing up are the same. And more importantly, how they might have been different.\n\nDon't worry. I just want us to get to know each other a little better.
Of course. We won't keep anything like that from you. I give you my word.\n\nNow, if you'll excuse us, I'd like to get to know the other Ambitions.

I did not know how dangerous this ancient magic truly was! I did not understand my actions were the cause of all this … not until I heard about the bodies you and Heem-Jas found. \n\nAnd once I realized, it was already too late.

Good question. As soon as you figure it out, let me know. I definitely want to have a chat with them myself.\n\nNow, it's been lovely seeing you again, but I really do need to get back to my daring escape. If you learn anything, I'll be in touch.

Evidence? I told the Speaker those calling cards would get us into trouble. It's not like we sign them or anything. Anyone can dip their palm in black ink and make a hand print.\n\nLook, there have been no contracts. I'm here on different business.

You're the one who took the job? Forgive my brusqueness. I should have known someone who looks as formidable as you would be here for work, not idle chatter.\n\nI do hope Deetum-Jas stressed to you the importance of discretion in this matter.

The Dark Elf Tenarei Vels. She's a traveler I met along the road. The cave is Deepscorn Hollow—the entrance is over by the dock.\n\nI'm here to retrieve a fellow named Quistley Silvelle. His family sent me to find him. I think he's in trouble.

Untie me, please. The Silvelles will pay well if you help me get Quistley out of whatever trouble he's in, and I could use someone to watch my back. Interested?\n\nOh, and check the shack. I think Tenarei dropped something during our struggle.

I cannot give you exact details. Most of it is so old, it's impossible to be certain anyway. Given the sensitive nature, I would guess you'll find communiques, reports, and the like. \n\nBut your task is to destroy the documents, not study them.
Pah. I am a politician, not a member of a criminal organization.\n\nWe have nothing more to discuss. Please, if you are interested in the job, do get on with it.

Always excuses with these Imperials. First they show up claiming to seek trade. When we ask that they leave, they camp near our borders and more arrive each day against our wishes.\n\nSuddenly our people go missing. This is no coincidence.

I wish I knew. There is a supposed peace between my people and the Imperials, Keshu the Black Fin ensures that. But that does not mean some do not still break rank. Especially if they want to lay claim on a new land.\n\nBut why not just attack us?

Heem-Jas is enthusiastic to a fault. He thinks himself a hero, but usually just ends up getting himself into more trouble. This is no different. If you insist on helping, then I suggest you drag him out of the northern swamps before he hurts himself.
Interesting. I don't think I like this cult. What did you call it?

An odd name for a band of religious fanatics. Ah, well.\n\nDon't worry about us. We're perfectly safe here. Go about your business while my sister and I talk with Sombren. I think we have much to share with each other.
Sacrificed! That's horrible!\n\nSo, you didn't find him in … what did you call our home? A vault?

The Deadlands? As in the Oblivion plane of Mehrunes Dagon? We learned about that in our studies. It's supposed to be a beautiful place, or so we were told.\n\nI'm glad you rescued him. Perhaps he knows more about who we are than we do.

The skull contains the trapped essence of a powerful Daedric lord. If Xynaa had simply killed her rival, he would have returned like Daedra do. So instead she trapped a portion of his energy to keep him from coming back.

You heard Xynaa. My power is of both Oblivion and Nirn. I can use a spark from the trapped essence of a Daedric lord to recharge my power.\n\nThat means Xynaa's old enemy will be freed to return someday. Not that I care about that any more.
I thank you for your service. Speak to <<1>>, he will have your reward. Our business is concluded.

Do you make a habit of asking intrusive questions of the people who pay you for work?\n\nMy reasons for wanting those documents destroyed are my own. You have my thanks for carrying this out, but I would appreciate it if you went on your way now.

It seems likely, yes. I was not about to ask him myself, of course. My clients' business is their own. It usually works out better for me that way. \n\nIf you feel like asking him, be my guest. Just … do not tell him I said any of this.

I've had some Mage training, so I'm pretty handy with a destruction staff. I'm also a decent sword and board man. You know, one-handed weapon and shield?\n\n<Placeholder. Will be replaced with RST 13317>

Thank you so much! This means a great deal to me. I've been in such a rut these last few weeks. Everything I try to write is as dull as an old blade.\n\nBut knowing the contents of that ruin will surely change that!

The tribe will flourish, now that we are no longer fighting with the Imperials.\n\nAs for me, I will continue performing heroic deeds across the coast. Great heroes like us never stay in one place too long!

Hah, I don't see how that's any of your affair, but if you must know I did cross paths with that unscrupulous Dark Elf and I'm worse for it.\n\nWhat's your interest in Irenni? I suppose she cheated you as well.

She came to me seeking information and—given our longstanding association—I entrusted her with it on the assurance that she would do me a simple favor in return.\n\nInstead she ran off and played me for a fool. No one makes a fool of me.

I mean, adventuring can be dirty business. My family is nothing but a bunch of no-good, tomb robbers depending on who you ask. But there's a big difference between digging through old ruins for treasure and outright stealing.
Let's hope so, but if we do wind up breaking the law, I could have a worse partner in crime. You're a good friend.

Do you have any idea how rare it is for a creation this ugly to survive on Summerset, let alone one made by the premier authority on sculpture? I even had the original assignment's written grade: barely-satisfactory! It's priceless.

Edvilda Stone-Stalker. She was probing my interest in Dwemer relics. I've no interest in it, but I knew Irenni has an unhealthy interest in them. She was camped near Steamfont last I heard. \n\nThat's all I can tell you, so our business is concluded.

This time. Death was the only thing that stopped my grandfather from chasing after that stupid trinket. I don't want it to be the same for her. You can only keep rolling the dice in this life for so long.
I hope so. Probably not, but I've weighed her down with enough guilt to hold her for a little while at least.\n\nEither way, sorry for dragging you into my family drama.

You must realize that the events surrounding Leovic's secret and the Four Ambitions have not yet reached their climax? When next Dagon and his followers emerge from the shadows, I will be waiting to see what they do.\n\nAnd then I'll send for you.

It's one of a kind! The first work of the current Sapiarch of Shape and Form when they were still a student! Irreplaceable.\n\nI never thought an Argonian would beat me at the cards, but the banker has more of a head for numbers than I expected.

I didn't! I just got so thoroughly thrashed at the table that I needed to offer collateral. Under-Root must have known what a singular treasure it is. Now that she has it in her greedy claws, she'll never let it go. Willingly anyway.

You are incredible! I can't wait to pore over what you came up with. But that can wait! I'm going to stay around here for a bit and soak up what I can from this location.\n\nYou should see Deetum-Jas for your reward! You've certainly earned it!

We lived there for a good few years when I was young. It was awkward at times—Argonians don't trust Dark Elves, for good reason. \n\nI like to think my parents showed them different, but not everyone warmed up to us.

Yeah, I suppose. I just feel foolish for taking our innocence for granted. If my ancestors weren't guiltless, I'll just have to be better than them. That's all there is to it.\n\nI can start by getting my mother to act more responsibly.

I know, I know. It just ashes my hide that a few rotten fetchers ruined it for the rest of us … but that's not quite the truth. It's easy to blame it all on House Dres and the Telvanni, but they weren't the only ones keeping slaves before the Pact.

I know, I know. It just ashes my hide that a few rotten fetchers ruined it for the rest of us … but that's not quite the truth. It's easy to blame it all on House Dres and the Telvanni, but they weren't the only ones keeping slaves before the Pact.

Everyone who helped ensure our victory. Brigadines, legionnaires, the allies you gathered. Not to mention dignitaries and nobles from all across Blackwood. It promises to be a grand event!\n\nI'll be personally escorting Countess Caro and the legates.

A great deal of boredom, I hope.\n\nI need to rebuild my forces. Do my best to make sure Blackwood remains safe and secure. And I plan to closely coordinate my efforts with Keshu's Black Fin Legion. We work well together. I want to see that continue.

We have no choice but to venture inside the xanmeer. But we do not have enough people to do so safely. We have lost too many of our warriors. \n\nYou are here as a mediator. Perhaps you could convince the Imperials to assist us in this matter?

Eveli brought word of a threat against the former members of the Imperial Elder Council, including Councilor Lovidicus. The threat seems to be related to a secret of the Longhouse Emperors. A secret concerning something called the Four Ambitions.

We don't actually know. We sent for an Imperial scribe to decipher the coded documents you found, but they have yet to arrive.\n\nIn the meantime, we've been doing everything we can to protect the councilors from Dark Brotherhood assassins.

Lovidicus, Faleria, and Vandacia are safely ensconced in Leyawiin Castle. Unfortunately, we couldn't save Jirich, Sophus, and Abor.\n\nYou found the Dark Brotherhood's calling card at every scene, yet the assassin you met claims they killed no one.

Oh, not that fetching thing again! Mom …! She's been chasing after my grandfather's Dwemer puzzle box for decades. Ever since the old Mer joined our ancestors at the tomb. It's her obsession.\n\nDon't tell me they got into a fight over it.

Great. Just great. So the shifty Nord met my mother out here and ran afoul of bandits? That explains what happened to Edvilda, but mom's not here, thank Vehk, but if she'd escaped we'd have heard from her, right?\n\nThey must have taken her captive.
You are not worthy.
You are not worthy.

It is just something I sense. \n\nI was drawn here by a purpose and a feeling. I wished to study Zenithar, and there is a temple here in Leyawiin. But I also feel as though something important has happened or will happen in this place.

What? No! Well, maybe just the little snacks coming by on the trays, but that's what you do at parties, right?\n\nSeeks and I just wanted to check in on you. He says maintaining good contacts is important in the business. Plus, you know, free food.

Indeed. I am intrigued by how differently his followers perceive him. There are those who consider him a source of gainful work, while others pray to him for wealth. Some believe he watches over trade. \n\nMost believe in some combination of these.

No, but I feel driven to continue reflecting on it. I feel as though I must do something, but I do not know what. It feels equally ominous and inevitable.\n\nAh, well, beeko. Perhaps it will become clear one day.
Have you not heard the story of how he saved Leyawiin? It's the greatest tale of all time! I actually came to Leyawiin to hear some firsthand accounts.\n\nHe just sounds so … heroic.

It was more than impressive! Can you imagine seeing something like that with your own eyes? I can't imagine the blood, the sheer carnage!\n\nAnd in the center of it all, Sai Sahan himself, radiating glory! I wish I could have been there.

Well, as the story goes, he led mercenaries here to free Leyawiin at Varen's request, but they turned traitor and started attacking him too! \n\nBut he fought his way into the city anyway, killing both mercenaries and Longhouse loyalists alike.
Trying to blend in. Badly. Just wanted to say farewell before we skip town. Figure we owe you that much after you salvaged that job for us.

Oh, I'm sure there'll be another adventure. And Stibbons goes where I go. I can't seem to get rid of him no matter how hard I try.\n\nNo, no, I jest. I wouldn't think of leaving him behind. Who else would carry all my packages? He's very good at that.

No, unless you count these tiny balls of goo that keep following me around.\n\nLady Laurent says she catches glimpses of other me's in the crowd, but I think that just her nerves. She can be quite tense and irritable if she skips her afternoon tea.
Yes, as a matter of fact! Tiras's letter was very well received in Tel Naga. The magisters want to see the Phantasmal Censer at work! Can you believe that?
The news is favorable. My letter to the magisters convinced them that the Phantasmal Censer is a worthy enterprise. I'm to carry on Revus's work.\n\nI believe my teacher is in good standing. For now.

Sorry, I don't mean to be such a bore on your big day. I was just thinking about how we all got caught up in this fetching mess. Events of this magnitude, people are bound to get swept away, but that doesn't take the sting out of losing them.

A great power runs beneath this old city. You have seen its side-effects—the geysers erupting all around us.\n\nAn acolyte of Mehrunes Dagon might channel such destructive energy to empower a ritual. I now suspect this was Bahsei's purpose.

Isn't that the truth. Of course, exciting for me is exploring an old ruin and hoping I find more treasures than traps, not battling the hordes of Mehrunes-fetching-Dagon over the fate of the world.\n\nI was not prepared for the latter.

I'm a little bit mad that Mirri didn't invite me to help you this time, but I won't pretend that I would have been any help at all. I barely got out of that scrape with the Waking Flame alive.\n\nJust, don't let her get a big head about it. All right?
A tribe that has lost their way. They worship violence and chaos above all. Their callousness brings unwanted strife and bloodshed to the marshes. \n\nThey are dangerous, particularly to outsiders.

Cruelty. Cunning. And likely powers I cannot predict. Based on what we have seen, it is clear the whispers of her loyalty to Mehrunes Dagon are true.\n\nShe will not yield, ojel. She must be sent back to the chaos.

They were each wiser than I, in different ways. Even as far from the egg as I am, I still learned much from them.\n\nKasa-Tah valued preparation for the nests to come. She believed we were too isolated, and that knitted branches held strongest.

The Nisswo and the Sul-Xan may both embrace impermanence, but they do so in drastically different ways.\n\nLikely the tome is something that should remain in the protection of the Clutch of Nisswo. Perhaps they killed him so they might keep it.

I have never seen it for myself. It is said to be a tome of shadow magic written by a dryskin man by the name of Azra Nightwielder.\n\nI have reason to believe it is highly dangerous, though I have heard the runes within cannot be read by mortal eyes.

Subdued at first. Those folks had been through so much, they weren't quite sure how to react. The House can handle the toughest audience, though, and we soon had them laughing and smiling again.\n\nWe seem to have stoked their interest in the arts.

The two are bound. Nisswo Nesh-Tei's soul cannot properly pass until the mission he pursued so fervently in life is resolved. His sense of purpose was so strong, it carries on. \n\nIf we finish his work, his death need not have been in vain.

Blessed as can be. The Resolutions have regarded Gavos, rightly, as living testament to the sanctity of pious labor. Of course, he's seen no rest since he left the abbey. My fellow clerics seek his knowledge night and day.

I am voh-vastei … an apprentice. All priests must first take on the role of voh-vastei before becoming a nisswo themselves. Nisswo Nesh-Tei was my mentor. \n\nSo you see why this matter is very important to me.

Plans? The same as they were before this trouble started. Work with Gideon to secure our borders and keep the war from impacting Blackwood directly. Make sure our communities stay safe and prosper. If not for you, none of that would even be possible.

Why? Shouldn't a leading Leyawiin business person attend a celebration for all of Blackwood?\n\nBesides, after I let word slip that you and Eveli had patronized my shop, business has been booming! Everyone just has to know which outfit you selected.

Though I am not yet a nisswo, as his apprentice, I feel it is my duty.\n\nIn life, this was Nesh-Tei's path to walk. Now he will walk with me. Through shadow and void. Through river and root. Through death and change.

Yes, I have! The relics we recovered from Undertow Cavern turned out to be exactly the sort of proof I needed to convince other scholars that someone important had been entombed there. \n\nI am veracious, victorious, and vindicated!
They are well. Thank you for asking. \n\nIt will take time for all of us to recover from the horrible things we witnessed, but you gave us that chance. We will never forget that.
Why so surprised? Where else would I be? It is impolite to not show up when the common folk hold a celebration in your honor. Is that not true among the featherless as well?
Wonderful. It's going smashingly! He's my muse, my inspiration, my reason for getting out of bed! And he's my … well.\n\nWe'll have to see, won't we?
Oh, I'll be all right. Eventually.\n\nTragic love stories are the things of legends aren't they? I'll be sure to compose a gripping story about him. It will be a tale for the ages!

Tentative, like a newly formed river emerging from two springs, but it flows. The water is muddy but will soon run fresh and clear, I am sure! \n\nNaheesh Nurwul and Lieutenant Viria have been working hard to ensure that our peace lasts, thanks to you.

After you left, we discussed moving on. But the Winds convinced us to stay. We fought for our home—leaving would hollow out our victory.\n\nSo, the rebuilding has begun. Feel welcome to visit should the marsh breeze ever blow you in our direction.
Your doubts do you credit, mortal. But in your heart, you know the truth.\n\nYour shadow grows long and dark. The shades of Evergloam dance at the edge of your sight. I am Ur-dra. I am Nocturnal.

I was here, honoring the Mistress as I do every night when Giovanni and Darene, some people I knew growing up in Leyawiin, stepped out of the shadows. They took my lady's relic! I tried to stop them, but I … I just couldn't.

No. Darene had a sword to my throat. I've never seen her so desperate.\n\nI don't know what's become of the sickle but Giovanni has a room in Leyawiin, around the corner from the bank. He might still be there.

Giovanni is a kind person and Darene is … abrasive, but she stood up for all of us when we were little. I know them, they aren't bad people.\n\nAnd if I'm right about Tumma-Maxath, no one deserves the fate he has in store for them.
Each feels that this land is theirs to tend. Yet, they don't actively fight over it. Words prevail here instead of war, for the most part. Of course, this was not always the case.

Imperials took it back. Then when the Longhouse Emperors ruled, they controlled the city until Sai Sahan, at Varen Aquilarios's request, liberated it.\n\nNow the city supports a harmonious mix of races. Argonians find this acceptable.

First, Argonians tended the land, allowing Khajiit to help. Then Nibenese settled here, causing the Khajiit to growl. After the Chapel of Zenithar was built, the Khajiiti wander-kings took it through blood-spilling. But that did not end the violence.

Dreamer is a marvel to behold. Fantastic and dreadful at the same time. A true idiot savant. They almost killed themselves practicing prat falls. Once informed that there is more technique than throwing themselves on their face, they learned quickly.

Wonderful! All of the Players have welcomed me among the troupe as if I've always been a part of it. Some even invented some back-stories for me that are way more interesting than anything I came up with!

You mean after helping you clean up this massive debacle? Oh, the usual, I guess. Try some more of the local cuisine. Collect my next contract. Complete my next contract. \n\nWhat can I say? I'm a creature of habit.
Oh, thank goodness that's over. Now that Nocturnal has the sickle, maybe she'll show me mercy.\n\nWhat about the necromancer Tumma-Maxath?

She's always been a worrier, even when we were kids. \n\nMillona's probably right, I only have to think about our employer and I break out into a cold sweat. When I'm done with this job, I'm going to become a carpenter. Fewer terrifying clients.

All right! No need to bring that shadowy hag into this. Look, Gio doesn't know this, but Tumma-Maxath said he'd turn us into his eternal slaves if we didn't help him. \n\nYou stop that necromancer and I'll find a more respectable occupation. Promise.

Hmm. I didn't think he would willingly part with a relic. Good. The Sickle should never be used in a necromancer's ritual. I'll make sure it's well-hidden next time. No thief will ever claim it again!\n\nSpeaking of which, are my friends all right?

Somehow, even if you did kill Tumma-Maxath, I would still be worried about him returning. As it is, he can't complete the ritual, not without the Shade Sickle. \n\nSpeaking of which, how are my friends?
That's a relief! Gio and Darene are good people, I know they are. Hopefully we can all put this behind us.
Oh, that makes sense. Gio was always the reasonable one. I'm glad he's going to try to turn over a new leaf.
See? Darene's stubborn, but she has some common sense. I'm glad she's agreed to turn over a new leaf, the life she wanted to live was going to get her killed.

I see. I wish this experience would be enough to let them see how dangerous their chosen path was. Still, they're adults and they can make their own decisions.\n\nI just wish they'd decided on a life that was less likely to get them killed.

Of course. The failure was mine. I earned whatever rebuke my lady had planned for me.\n\nFaith isn't a matter of convenience, my friend. My lady is unfathomable. Powerful. Eternal. I will follow her wisdom. Whatever the cost.

They said they were going to meet after delivering the sickle to Tumma-Maxath. Maybe you could follow Giovanni to this meeting?\n\nTumma-Maxath is a powerful necromancer. My friends are in more trouble than I am. Please help them. I'll pay you!

Keshu makes things happen. She is quite busy, of course, but she turns no one away. No matter who you are, if your need is great, she will use all her strength to find a way to help you. That is what makes her a great leader.

I am indeed. She has already accomplished much for many people. Her accomplishments are vast. From fighting against slavers to befriending King Jorunn, she has proven herself.\n\nIf you speak to her, you will understand why we place our hope in her.

I can tell you what I know, but it is only a glimpse into her greatness.\n\nKeshu is a war hero. She has traveled and learned much in her lifetime before coming to Gideon. Here, she hopes to build a more harmonious and modern Argonian society.

He is egg-brother to me, along with Keshu, Vos-Huruk, and Xocin. We grew up together in the village of Seekhat-Xol.\n\nIf you trust Keshu, you can trust Tee-Wan. But I should let him speak for himself once you meet with him.
Given what just happened here, with the captives and all, we decided on a new post. Normally I'd be on the wall, doing a walking patrol.
Simple enough. Our Hist tree wishes for us to help others however we can. Even though this currently presents a challenge, we will fulfill upon that wish.
Always. I am thankful that you thought to ask, friend. And now, I must continue my work. I suspect you have your own to do. Go with gratitude.

Indeed, the younger members of our tribe fear we give too much and note that we do suffer as a result. Our elders believe that as long as we fulfill the Hist's wishes, though, our suffering will not last long. It is a quandary with no easy answer.

It is a quiet place where secrets can safely be spoken aloud. But as spymaster, Tee-Wan could achieve the same secrecy in many places inside the city walls.\n\nIt is curious, but that is between you and Tee-Wan. The graveyard lies to the east.

Straight to it then. One of our own has gone missing. Xocin, one of our closest companions and Keshu's principal ambassador.\n\nMy informants tell me he was last seen speaking to a Dark Elf named Melyn Drad. That's where you come in.

He's staying at the Egg and Hammer Inn. The method of information extraction is up to you, and I will see you rewarded.\n\nAll I ask is that you be discreet. Too many prying eyes will ensure Xocin never opens up to us about whatever is going on.

Something's got him on edge, he won't talk to any of us. The members of the Black Fin Legion are easily recognizable in Gideon. \n\nI need someone he won't see coming. I want you to see if you can speak with him and learn what he and Xocin discussed.

Once it was the name of General Keshu's army. Over time, it has come to be synonymous with those who follow her. \n\nThose of us that have been members of the Black Fin Legion since its inception have been close since we hatched from our eggs.

Indeed. It includes Xocin, Vos-Huruk, Peek-Ereel and myself. We have followed Keshu the longest of anyone.\n\nHah. I still remember when Keshu had to rescue Xocin during our rites of maturity after he fell into a patch of quicksand.

Vos-Huruk. Likely the finest warrior in Gideon next to Keshu herself, and certainly the strongest of our ranks. She grew up with the rest of us in Seekhat-Xol and much like myself, has served the Black Fin for many years.

No, I have not informed her … yet. She is very busy, as you are no doubt aware. Her claws are full with the fallout from your encounter with those crazed Dagonists. \n\nI wish to keep her in the dark for the moment. She has enough to worry about.

Apologies. It's Keshu's nickname.\n\nVos was actually the one to witness the event that started it. During one of our trials, Keshu emerged from the dark waters of the swamp to kill three Naga … like a black fin on the prowl, Peek-Ereel wrote.

He is an odd one, but no villain. An accomplished mage, an expert on the planes of Oblivion. He put his conjuration skills to work in service of the Ebonheart Pact, though he's since retired to spend his days drinking and poring over old tomes.

Like most arrogant mages, he enjoys making sure others are aware of his superiority. He's a talker.\n\nMy mistake was not stopping Vos before she confronted him directly. He doesn't want trouble with the Black Fin Legion, so he's playing coy now.

I have great love for him, but we have always been opposites. When we were hatchlings, I was busy bloodying my scales while he was mixing tinctures. He is brave, and he is often too clever for his own good.\n\nI worry for him.

No clue. But Xocin is a master conjurer and a veteran of many battles, I have no doubt that whatever trouble he's gotten himself into, it will not get the better of him.\n\nStill, I believe he needs our help, whether he asks for it or not.

I'm not drunk. I'm retired! Do you know how long I served those ungrateful wretches of the Ebonheart Pact? And was my severance in accordance with my service? Ha!\n\nBut that's all changed now. Someone finally saw my value. I'm set for life!

He wanted a special ritual stone. I didn't have one, but I taught him the spells to make use of it, and we spoke of Doomvault Porcixid, a place that might contain such a relic.\n\nI told him to just summon a new servant. They're all the same. Pfft.

The very same! To think some consider him my equal in conjuration. Pah! Ridiculous.\n\nA true expert knows you never fall in love with your own conjured servants! I tried to talk him out of it, but he just kept raising his offer.

As if a novice could understand the inner workings of a runic conduit intrinsically linked by its very nature to the chaotic creation of Kyn! Ha!\n\nHonestly, talking to you is making me sober. You're worse than that giant lizard woman!

The damned fool! I told him to stick to Flame Atronachs. Sure, they can be nice to look at … but they're made of fire!\n\nHe preferred to summon Kyn, warriors from the Deadlands and beyond. Not my type, but who am I to judge when the coin is good?
Ugh. These vaults make my scales itch. There's a power to them. More tempting to mages than most, I suspect.\n\nDid Melyn say what Xocin's after?
Love? Oh, not this again.\n\nBy seed and spleen, I would bet anything that he's trying to reach Xyria.

They fell for each other on the battlefield. Then, Xyria died for him. Of course, that's what conjured servants do for their masters. But Xocin didn't see it that way. Not with her.\n\nWait. Here comes Tee-Wan.

It's a long story. \n\nBack when the Black Fin Legion went to war against the Akaviri alongside the Ebonheart Pact, Xocin summoned an entire cohort of Dremora warriors to help turn the tide. Xyria was among them, more loyal to Xocin than all the rest.

A ritual stone? I suppose that makes sense.\n\nI assume Vos told you that Xyria died fighting for Xocin some years back. When a Dremora dies, it reforms on its home plane, but it takes a considerable amount of time before it can be summoned again.

I need you to enter Doomvault Porcixid and find Xocin, make sure he's safe. He's clever, but there's no telling what kind of horrors await him in there. \n\nVos and I are needed here. Please, find our egg-brother for us.

My theory is that this ritual stone Xocin went to gather might be able circumvent the amount of time it would take to summon Xyria. \n\nLook, you've already done what I asked, but I could use your help for just a little longer.

Try to get him to listen to reason. He doesn't need to rush this. He should discuss it with Keshu and the rest of us.\n\nConjuration is dangerous to begin with. A ritual of this kind? I'm not even sure Xocin knows what could happen if it goes tail up.

It's dangerous, even for a seasoned mage like Xocin. Hostile Daedra roam the halls, and I've heard reports that the deeper you go, the stranger things get. Like it's a window into Oblivion.\n\nBe careful. We're not asking you to die for us.
I don't know much about love, but I do know warfare.\n\nAll I can say is when you put those two together on a battlefield, it's quite a sight to behold. Maybe that means something.

She's a Kyn. Dremora. Daedra. In my experience, they're only loyal when a conjurer has them bound nice and tight.\n\nI know she and Xocin bonded in battle. That doesn't mean I trust her. Likely never will.

I don't know much about conjuration either. I'd say Xocin can do just about anything in the right place with the right tools at his disposal.\n\nSo yes, he probably can. Though I'm not sure it's a great idea.

About ten years ago now. Defeated the invasion and helped form the Ebonheart Pact. Even commanded the Pact army during the start of the Three Banners War.\n\nThen one day she turned in her commission. Came back to serve as governor of Gideon.

Well, after we shut down the tunnel, the cultists tried to assassinate our entire garrison. While they did take out quite a few folk before we got them all, I have to wonder at the thinking there.\n\nNow, if you'll pardon me, I have a wall to watch.

Of late? Dragons. Though we also watch for odd activity on either side of the wall. We once had a cult of Nocturnal seek to build a tunnel beneath the wall for reasons they never shared.\n\nThat was one harrowing week.

South of Stonewastes, in the heart of Sul-Xan territory. I suggest caution and stealth. Try to avoid starting a war with the tribe if you can at all help it.\n\nBring whatever you find back here. Gideon will keep it safe, I assure you.

It is better to think of it as the tides of the sea, coming in and going out, yet the sea never empties of water.\n\nThis is flawed, of course, because unlike the sea, the Imperials never wish to retreat, which would cause harm to the natural balance.

Only what young Eveli was telling me before you arrived. I never heard of them before today.\n\nI will, however, get my best Black Fin Legionnaires to investigate them. Vandacia has lived in Gideon a long time. Someone here must know something.

You must have seen the stone structures in the swamp. The xanmeers? In the ancient past, my people created great wonders. A great civilization. Then, for some reason, they abandoned it for a simpler, less complicated life.

You have seen their cities, perhaps. Their wars? If you have not yet walked the bloodied soil around and within the Imperial City, you should. And that is what they seek to bring here. Placing all within stone cages to fight over.
Seek to control nature, certainly. Some also wish to destroy it, but it would be unwise of me to put an entire group in the same skin.\n\nI hope I have given you something to think about.

You perhaps know your cities. Your wars? If you have not yet walked the bloodied ground around and within the Imperial City, you should. And that is what Imperials seek to bring here. Placing all within stone cages to fight over.
I am no writer, so I could not say. I imagine the mystery of such a place would be intriguing to some. Mostly, Daedric ruins tend to inspire fear within me, but perhaps our dear poet is different.
And you as well, my friend. Thank you for continuing to assist my sister. I know she can handle herself, but that doesn't mean I don't worry about her.

Can you help … me? A famed warrior is asking if I need help? This is what I've always dreamed of! I, uh, don't have any dangerous things going on right now, but I'm sure I could find myself some trouble to get into if you'd want.

No, no, it's all right! Listen, what would you rather fight? A pack of lions? Perhaps a vicious troll? I'm sure I could find one nearby. Oh! It should be more than one. Let's give the bards a good song.\n\nHow does a dozen trolls sound?

You're right. Trolls aren't enough for a legendary hero! We need something bigger. More menacing. Oh! I heard about these weird cultists. The Order of the Waking Flame.\n\nYou can rescue me from the cultists! How exciting!
Hah! My friends are going to be so jealous. The fabled hero, come to rescue little ol' me from a vicious band of trolls. I can't wait!\n\nDon't take too long. The anticipation will kill me!

Oh it's nothing I couldn't handle. Took a bit of running. Dodged a few claws. Got stabbed by a few swords. But that's life for adventurers!\n\nI'm sure whatever you were doing was much more dangerous. I get it, really. But … I do have another idea.

Don't worry about it. It'll be easy! A little poison or something and you can swoop in with the antidote before I get too sick!\n\nThis is going to be amazing! My friends will never believe me. You'll need to let me take a souvenir for sure.

I won't wait! Black Marsh just has so many dangerous things. What do you think I should start with? Venomous plants? Carnivorous beasts? Oh! Maybe a hostile Argonian tribe.\n\nThis is so exciting! I'll see you soon!

Of course! I mean, how else will Tamriel know of your great deeds? You have to save someone in mortal danger or it doesn't qualify as a daring rescue.\n\nI heard there's some really dangerous stuff in Black Marsh.

Alas, my adventuring days are long past. I'm much more comfortable these days with a quill and ink instead of a sword and shield.\n\nI'll stick around and ask if Councilor Lovidicus requires any more of my services, though. As long as I'm here.

I imagine he didn't think I had time to decipher any of the coded passages. I barely had a moment to look at the documents when the portals opened and his cultists burst in.\n\nLuckily, I'm very familiar with that particular code. It was my specialty.

Isn't the family resemblance obvious? I was an adventurer myself back in the day. Before I became an Imperial scribe. I think that's where Eveli gets it. That and from all the books I've given her over the years.

I imagine he didn't think I had time to decipher any of the coded passages. I barely had a moment to look at the documents when the portals opened and his cultists burst in.\n\nLuckily, I'm very familiar with that particular code. It was my specialty.

Naheesh Nurwul is being lenient. A full exile would be fitting, but instead she has ordered me to hunt rare quarry.\n\nI cannot return until I procure the skin of an albino death hopper … a beast which has not been seen in more than a hist's age.

It is not an impossible task, just very difficult. I am exiled until I find my quarry, so I have no choice. It may take me many changes of the seasons, but that is what I deserve.\n\nI accept my punishment and will endeavor to see it through.

It is less of a concern now that we know they mean us no harm. But to ensure lasting peace, you are correct, we will need to negotiate. \n\nWe did as much to sully relations between our people, if not more. My tribe is prepared to make compromises.
Maybe it is time I hung up my adventurer's ruck and settled in with my worrywart of a husband. I just hate leaving things unfinished.

As surely as the colors of leaves change with the season. They are kinder than I ever would have thought. Perhaps not all are like them, but I will reserve judgment.\n\nLieutenant Viria in particular impresses me. I hope to see more of him.

Yes, I wonder who he is. Or she. Are they still trapped inside a vault? Or did they find a way to escape, like I did?\n\nI hate to think of them alone and unprotected, but maybe it's better if they remain hidden.

My commander asked me to be the official liaison between the Ivory Brigade and these Argonians. I hope to keep our alliance intact, and perhaps even turn it into a friendship.\n\nIt'll take some doing, but I'm confident we're off to a good start.

It was my father's prized possession. He spent decades trying to unravel its mysteries, until it was stolen from him. Then he spent the rest of his life trying to get it back. And most of mine after he died. I thought it might finally make him happy.

Opinions differ, but they are all honorable. They will hold up this alliance, even if they are still mourning those we lost. Time will heal that pain and even those who protest the loudest will see that peace is the right answer.

Right. I almost forgot about that. I need to figure out how to keep Calia from being consumed by her ever-increasing power. And them, too, once we find them.\n\nI suppose I have a lot to consider, and not a lot of time to do it.
Of course he did. I tried to spare him of this … I tried to spare all my egg-siblings, but things have gone awry. As I might have expected.\n\nYou know why I'm here then. You know about Xyria.

Wait. The Kynaz stone also suffered from my impatience. Expended like it is now, it's useless. It needs to be recharged, or this was all for nothing.\n\nTake it. Find trees like this one that still hold energy. It won't take much, I promise.

Yes, the Kynaz stone. And in my haste, I attempted to summon Xyria to my side immediately. A grave error.\n\nThese vaults are pure chaos. No place for a stable conjuring. The spell backfired. Sapped me of my magicka and nearly killed me.

Find more of these trees marked by runes. The ones next to us have been spent, the energy consumed by my botched attempt at the summoning ritual, but there are more not far from here.\n\nThe stone is already attuned. You just need to find the trees.

It may seem strange, but trees grow even in the realms of Oblivion. As on Nirn, they are blooming pathways teeming with the energy of their parent plane.\n\nThat force powers the stone. We'll need more of it if I'm to have any chance of saving Xyria.

It is difficult to explain. Conjuration requires a focus of two distinct points. Where the entity currently is, and where you wish it to appear. \n\nI underestimated the instability of these vaults. The swirling chaos clouded my vision and I failed.

It's more complicated than that. The chaotic energy of Oblivion is bleeding through into Nirn, but it's overlapping our reality without replacing what was … what is here. \n\nIn all my studies, I've never seen anything quite like it.

Well, I'm not just thinking of finally paying my respects. I can summon his ancestor spirit at the tomb. I'm hoping my grandfather can tell us something about his missing puzzle box that will help put this fetching fetcher fly hunt to rest.
Like I said, I don't think she's spoken with him since he died. Mom never talks about my grandfather. I get the impression that they weren't close.

He was obsessed with that puzzle box. When it was stolen, getting it back was all he could think about. I don't think mom gives two s'wits about the box, she just wants him to acknowledge her.\n\nMaybe I can convince him to free her from her duty.
Is that what Irenni has been doing all these years? Raising this whelp in the lap of luxury with that spineless Hlaalu boy while I molder in an early grave! Such ingratitude!

I was betrayed, by one whom I called friend. We whiled away many nights unlocking the secrets of that Dwarven puzzle, but on the cusp of the solution it vanished from my collection. When I came too close to the truth, my friend killed me.

Then perhaps this child is less a fool and ingrate than my own. No doubt you've been told I died in pursuit of my stolen puzzle box, but that is not the whole story. I was murdered. I came too close to the truth and I was silenced for it.

Ah, those foul things. I am glad Deetum-Jas was able to find someone interested. I do not know if the crows are still present inside the ruin, but I am sure if they are not, their eggs remain.\n\nYou must have questions. Please, ask away.

Crows are Nocturnal's servants, and they aid her in her dark deeds. It may seem like a small thing, but when given the opportunity to strip her of her power, we must. Destroying these eggs means there will be less crows to do her bidding.

Not sure, really. Could have been that weird ritual I was part of. Or that strange liquid I drank—some sort of venom now that I think about it. Lots of friendly … people!\n\nI did realize something on my way back here though.

I'm immortal now! At least, I think I am. So there's no need to worry. Besides, you're going to save me right as I'm on the brink of death.\n\nI wonder if the rumors of Dragons in Elsweyr are true? It's close enough to look into!

Saying that makes this even more exciting! You're an intrepid hero—as if you'd let me down. So I was thinking, what's the most daring thing you could tackle? Dragons. Rumor has it there are some in Elsweyr.\n\nThis is so exciting, I could squeal!
I'm always asking you to come save me, but I keep forgetting to tell you where I'm going! \n\nBefore I run off to this next adventure, remind me and I'll let you know.

As it turns out, I am. A shame really. Never did much with my life now that I think about it. But I did have some great adventures recently! Can't say I would have ever had those if I stay cooped up back home.\n\nI learned another valuable lesson, too!

Truth be told, I was afraid of the world. I didn't want to leave Bravil, my home. But then I'd read tales of adventure and heroes, like yourself.\n\nThey'd slay beasts. Save towns. Fall in love! I never thought I'd have something like that.

You've got to live your life. I mean, not just literally live it. Really experience it! Do things that make you uncomfortable. Things that make the hair on your arms stand straight up. \n\nFeel the thrill as a wamasu chases you through the swamp!

To find my courage. I knew if I thought you'd come along, I'd be brave enough to venture out. Even if I lied to myself. And I did it! I found my adventure.\n\nSo thank you. Thank you for finally letting me live the life I always dreamt about!

I experienced more in these past weeks then I have in my entire life! It was never really about being saved by you—it was about giving myself the courage to go out and do things myself. \n\nI'm not sure I ever really wanted you to save me.

It should come as no surprise that I intend to attempt to summon Xyria again. However, my egg-siblings are divided on whether this is the wisest course of action.\n\nI must admit I can be rash where Xyria is concerned. You bore witness to that.

I do not know. Xyria is alone in the Deadlands, newly reformed and already running for her life. I want to believe I can keep her safe here, even if it means we might attract more enemies to ourselves.\n\nWhat do you think I should do?

Tee-Wan and I believe Xyria would make for a powerful ally in the battles ahead. Having her here now could save lives.\n\nOn the other hand, Vos-Huruk is right to caution that Xyria is an outcast Kyn. She cut ties with her clan, and they will hunt her.

You have seen the dangers General Keshu and the rest of us face now. Vaults of Oblivion, cultists in service to Mehrunes Dagon, and tenuous alliances to meet them.\n\nNow is simply not the time to take unnecessary risks.

Against any other foe, yes. She is of the Deadlands, the home plane of the very enemies we've found on our doorstep. An outcast Dremora at our side may only serve to draw the full might of Dagon's armies down on our heads.\n\nThink on this.

I am, and not only for Xocin's sake. There's a storm coming, friend. If a war with Oblivion itself is in our future, I am not sure our Imperial allies will be enough to help us drive them back.\n\nWe're going to need all the help we can get.

I am the Black Fin's spymaster. I win battles by being better informed than my enemies. Xyria may know something of Dagon's plans, and even if not, she knows the tactics and weaknesses of Daedric forces.\n\nI think it is well worth the risk.
Were it not for you I would never have retrieved the stone, and this choice would not be before us now.\n\nI will respect your decision. Which do you think is the wiser course?

Having Xyria by my side once more will certainly outweigh any risk. So what if a few more Dremora come looking for a fight? We will banish them back to Oblivion. Together.\n\nThank you, my friend. I'll begin the summoning shortly.

What is that saying among Cyrods? Love is blind.\n\nPerhaps you are right. Just as I failed to see the wisdom in involving my egg-siblings in retrieving the stone, I may not be able to see the value of patience now. Very well. I will not summon Xyria.

You and Heseph have been our only visitors at the camp. If Annyce has only recently gone missing, there may still be a chance for us to find her before she becomes the latest victim in this ghost story. Do you have any leads?
You owe me no apology, friend. Had you not helped me retrieve the ritual stone, we would not be considering its use at all.\n\nPerhaps there is another way.
Yes, we've met. But she's not a person. That's Lyranth. She's a Dremora.\n\nDon't worry, she's friendly. Condescending and annoying, but friendly. Go on. See what she wants this time.

I dealt with one of the scouts. She will not bother anyone again. The other … may have slipped away while I was studying the vault's exterior.\n\nSo, I suggest you pick up the pace. The cultists could return in force at any moment.

Ah, yes. The scouts. One has been dealt with. The other … may have slipped away while I was admiring the vault's construction.\n\nSo, I suggest you pick up the pace. The scout could return with reinforcements at any moment.

What else could it be? The book seems very old, and it's written in a language we can't read. Just carrying it around … it feels heavy, oppressive. Like a burden I didn't know I had.\n\nBut Lupus sent me to find it. It must be important.

I don't know! I'm an archer, not a Daedric scholar or anything. I don't think I should let the Order of the Waking Flame get their hands on it, though.\n\nAnd maybe one of these visions—if I have any more—will actually help us figure this all out.

No, but that last vision I had was clearly a warning about the cult leader, whoever they are. They're powerful. And evil.\n\nSo, bad dreams or no bad dreams, I think I'll hang onto the book. Just in case.
Don't I know. I suppose I should be more grateful to mom and dad for letting me be my own person. I had no idea.\n\nIf my father talked to me that way, I'd have pushed him off a ledge myself.
Who told you that? Millona?\n\nI won't apologize for what happened the last time I saw her and you can tell her that yourself.
Who've you been talking to? Millona?\n\nShe went crazy after she found religion. Judging us when she worships Nocturnal. Pssh! Never could appreciate irony.

I'd like some, too. I'm curious to find out who has the gall to frame the Dark Brotherhood. And rather successfully, I might add. That's no small feat.\n\nWhoever it is, they managed to trick the lot of us. Crafty indeed.

Only so I can shove it up his ashes. This is important to my mother. I'm doing this for her. Not that old s'wit.\n\nLet's head to Vulkhel Guard. See if we can find this Onimiril. I may want to shake his hand.
Nothing substantial. You're the closest link we have to whoever this unknown enemy happens to be. \n\nNow that you're here, maybe you can—what?

Oh, wonderful! I implore you, you must find them and bring them to me. I know a place where they will be safe.\n\nNormally, I'd leave them be, but I've heard whispers of those who would rather see them destroyed. I want to prevent that from happening.

I'm an assassin. Nocturnal is dear to me, as she is to many of my profession. The crows are her children and servants, just as we are. They need to be respected.\n\nI'm quite busy myself, but I could not just sit by knowing they were in danger.

Like I didn't have nightmares before I knew that!\n\nIt's not talking to me. Not with words. But I can feel it. Like it's waking up. And while I've had similar sensations since I found it, the tingling really became intense when we entered this place.
East out of Gideon, where the Blackwood turns to muck. It's hard to miss, but you should prepare yourself if you intend to enter.\n\nThat's where Xocin was headed. Happy now?

Like woodsmoke in a wind storm. And without breathing a word to my Grandpa Lierre.\n\nWay Grandpa tells it, neither of them would so much as visit the loo without telling the other where they were headed. But the locals wouldn't listen.

It's all part of Mehrunes Dagon's master plan. He believes Nirn belongs to him. And he has long sought a way to combine his Oblivion realm with the mortal world. Hmm. Perhaps the Ambitions are another step in that direction.\n\nNow, open the door.

Might have happened yesterday for all these people care. Nobody holds a grudge like you Imperials. No offense.\n\nIf your name is Gemain, you're just lower than dirt. I had a son a couple years back and he's already catching it on the chin! He's two!
Ah, yes, Takaano is … was one of Onimiril's apprentices. Before he was, um, kicked out of the guild. It has left this one in a rather precarious predicament.\n\nPerhaps we could help one another?

This one might have turned Onimiril's other apprentice, Arelette, into a chicken. She has run off and should his new master discover Takaano's error he is certain to be expelled.\n\nIf you return poor, befowled Arelette, he will tell you of Onimiril.

Of course, of course! Onimiril was expelled from the guild not long ago, as you know, but he did not call the guild hall his home. He was very secretive and kept to a small, wilderness retreat northwest of Skywatch. Takaano was never invited to it.

Ah, not to speak ill of his former master, but Takaano thinks you should know that Onimiril was expelled from the guild for dabbling in forbidden magic. This one never saw it for himself, his master was always kind to him, but if true … be careful.

Last I saw, many crows gathered around Arpenia. Whether they remain is of no importance. There will still be many nests inside. \n\nLook for secluded or elevated places where the eggs would be safe from harm. You'll have no trouble finding them.

The crows gathered in Arpenia last I saw, so I imagine their nests are somewhere inside. \n\nAs for where the eggs are specifically, I would guess that they would be placed somewhere elevated for protection.

Wonderful. Give them to me and I will see to it that they are destroyed. Nocturnal will not have these servants. \n\nYou have helped cleanse the world of her influence, even in just a small amount. I thank you.
I hope you didn't run into too much trouble getting them. You have my thanks.\n\nQuickly, give the eggs to me and I'll take them to a place they will be safe to hatch when the time comes.

I get that, but I also get the impression that Onimiril's finding the answers he wants to find. Sometimes, a riddle is just a riddle.\n\nAt least his destination was clear enough. Hopefully the box is still in that Dwarven ruin.

I don't know. It's not like I've ever laid eyes on the thing. I just don't see how some hunk of Dwarven junk can be worth everything these two have sacrificed.\n\nIf we do find it, and I start going crazy, do me a favor and smash the fetching thing.
I'll send word to my mother to meet us in Othrenis. We will deliver it to my family's plot and hopefully she'll find some closure with my bull netch of a grandfather.

My granddad doesn't deserve mom's devotion, or forgiveness, but if it frees her of her guilt and obligations, she'll be safe and I'll be happy.\n\nCome on, let's not tempt fate by lingering with that thing.

Well, I was planning to grow it somewhere more convenient, for one, but I reckon the creeper is running wild around here and wreaking havoc on the native plants, which probably accounts for all the screaming.
Does the House Father heap gratitude upon his vassals for paying tributes left long overdue? I have been wronged. My forgiveness will not come so cheaply.

Grudges and curses are Dunmeri traditions dating back to the Anticipations. Just because they're old doesn't make them good.\n\nI'm happy to leave all that to rot with granddad and his stupid gold brick, but it looks like mom is willing to forgive.
I will not be lectured on the matters of my house by some uppity n'wah … oh, fine. I will be the bigger Mer. Let it not be said that I was never magnanimous.

She has nothing to regret. She did everything she could. That damn box was the last excuse that could be made for why they were estranged. If they still can't make up after this, granddad's just a fetching ashhole.\n\nEither way, she'll be fine.
We should keep searching for where the harrada creeper took root. Then we can figure out what to do with it.

This is only a very small part of my work. The fight against Nocturnal's shadowy presence is one that persists. I will continue the fight in whatever way I can. \n\nAfter I destroy these eggs, there is still much more to be done to keep her at bay.

Go back to work, I suppose. Paying people to brave dangerous ruins for crow eggs isn't my usual job, of course. This was merely a task of opportunity. \n\nI have contracts to fill and many places to travel. Perhaps we'll see each other again, though.

Good, I'm glad. I appreciate you taking up the job. I would have done it myself, but I know my limits.\n\nI gathered as much information as I could without being seen, but I wasn't foolish enough to try destroying their ritual tools myself.

For one, the Sul-Xan are crazy and worship chaos. I don't exactly know what the purpose of the sacrifices are, but it's clear the Sul-Xan use specific tools in order to carry them out. \n\nIf you can destroy those tools, it will slow them down.

Yes, both clients emphasized this. \n\nI do not know if all crows are servants of Nocturnal, but these in particular were of special interest. Something about Arpenia itself makes it so, but you would have to ask them for more specifics.
It's worse than that. Vandacia wrestled the documents you acquired from the other councilors away from the scribe. Once he translates them, he may know the location of all four of the Ambitions.

Ojel-bak? I've heard that term. It's Argonian. I believe it refers to a natural formation deep in the Blackwood marsh, but Vandacia was more familiar with that region than I.\n\nI know someone who can help us, though. I believe you already met her.

You ask to hear a long tale. One that I do not wish to tell. And may not have the right to tell.\n\nBe satisfied with this: A tree is not merely its trunk, or branches, or roots. It is also its seed. And so a tree without seeds is nothing at all.
Indeed. So it does. I may have failed it, but I cannot change the past.\n\nI can, however, change its future. With my weapons, I can fight this Naxhosa and defend the Stonewastes once more.

There were two other children once. And we used to have visitors. Teachers of all descriptions. And the emperor would come by. Emperor Moricar when we were very little. Emperor Leovic when we were older.\n\nBut we haven't seen anyone in years.

You did? That's astonishing! I'm … at a loss for words. I didn't expect anyone to take this job, much less accomplish it!\n\nThank you, friend. You did what I couldn't, and you saved lives. Please, go collect your reward from <<1>>!

I'll keep my eye on Xi-Tsei. The Sul-Xan will need to spend time recovering materials for their rituals, but I doubt they're done for good.\n\nI'll find <<1>> again if I figure out some other way to stop them. Maybe we'll cross paths again.

My foster brother—you've met him. The Silvelles took me in when I was young, and we were raised together … although I never really belonged to the family. Quistley is the Silvelles' son, no matter how many times he disappoints them.

We saved Quistley Silvelle from being sacrificed by the Daughter of Sithis in Deepscorn Hollow, near Leyawiin. The idiot thought he was in love with the leader of a death cult.\n\nCan you believe he was angry that we saved him?

I'm so glad! I really can't thank you enough for doing this. I would go myself but it really is quite dangerous. I care deeply for these insects, but I know I'd be no help to them dead.\n\nBut you look incredibly strong, I'm sure you can rescue them!
My father was Lord Martel Hallix. And he was a traitor to the crown.

The Undertow torchbugs themselves should be easy enough to catch! The real trouble is getting through the cavern itself, which I'm sure you're more than capable of handling.\n\nJust be gentle with the torchbugs, please! Take care when you handle them.

She was questioned rigorously, but the king's agents couldn't prove that she knew anything of my father's plot. Emeric spared her life. But the shame of the whole affair broke her heart, or so I've been told. She died shortly afterward.

He was a trusted advisor to High King Emeric. But when I was only two, he plotted to arrange the king's murder and assume power. My father was found out, though. The king had him executed, and stripped House Hallix of its lands and titles.

The king's officials thought Lady Clairene might be disloyal too. They commanded me to take young Bastian to the house of a minor lord and keep him there for a few months until they were sure she had nothing to do with Lord Hallix's treason.

That may be so, but I've learned that spirits are crafty. And calling on them is often necessary. As my mentor, ghost-hunting expert Claudina Illdene, would say—it's healthy to set boundaries in relationships. Especially with the dead.
Of course you do. To quote the famous ghost hunter Claudina Illdene—we mustn't shoulder the burdens of those who are gone. Their weight is light on the body, but heavy on the mind.
Lord Silvelle took them for safekeeping. He was supposed to send them with Bastian to Lady Clairene when the time came. But I don't know what happened after I was dismissed.

Someone in his court did. The Silvelles had a young lad of their own, they were close at hand, and there were no doubts about their loyalties. Lord Silvelle wasn't terribly happy about it, but he agreed to put up Bastian until things got sorted out.
