Lord Silvelle said that Bastian would be cared for and it wouldn't be my worry any longer. And he hinted that the king's officials had suspicions about some of us who served the Hallixes.\n\nI'm ashamed to say that I took his gold and ran for home.
I am not sure. If it is, I am sure it will not be for a good long while. But our bug enthusiast is much too concerned about the creatures inside to take that chance.

All insects are special, but these torchbugs happen to be very rare. You can't find this kind anywhere else. If the cavern floods, they'll die and become extinct! \n\nThat would be a great shame, since there's still so much we don't know about them.

What kind of question is that? Have you seen insects?\n\nI've cataloged one thousand two hundred sixty-three, each one more exciting than the last! They're all so unique. I caught a rare Habanoo caterpillar in Betnikh recently that had sixteen eyes!

Oh! You are a true hero! Thank you so much! I'm sure the torchbugs would thank you too, if they could. \n\nPlease, bring them to <<1>>, I gave him the proper storing materials to house them until I finish my work here. Thank you again, friend!

Not a great deal. They are comprised of Naga, who are generally meaner and more frightening than your average Argonian, much like myself. \n\nI hear they worship chaos and are incredibly violent … which is no great surprise.
No, but I reckon I can find it. Sounds like it's calling from deeper in the ruin. Thought I saw an entrance over that-away. Let's give it a try.
Yes, our people once used them as a means to gather food and resources. When the totem is active, creatures are drawn to its aura like a Kotu Gava to blood.

Well, I feel that my misdeeds have been exaggerated. But my father has made it clear that if I were to damage our new alliance with the Bouchend family through my youthful indiscretions, well … I have cousins who could inherit in my place.
Thank you, stranger. I promise to care for these until they are ready to hatch. No harm will come to them. \n\nGo speak to <<1>>, he'll give you your reward. I arranged everything with him.

What's there to think about? What reason is there to destroy life? Even if you do not follow Nocturnal, please do not take out your misgivings on these eggs. \n\nJust give them to me and we can be done with this. Then you can get your pay.

Thank you. Rest assured, I will destroy them immediately. \n\nThank you for your assistance in this matter. You have done a great deed today. Please, speak to <<1>> for your reward. I arranged everything with him.

Those eggs and the crows that hatch from them will bring nothing but grief and pain to the world. They are evil creatures, born for evil work!\n\nYou must give them to me so I can prevent them from harming anyone.

And risking my father's anger by meddling in business he did not want to come to light. If it weren't for me, Bastian would never even know that letter existed.\n\nLet's just say I'm being practical for once.

To be frank? It's an alliance. The Bouchends have their concerns, thanks to many baseless slanders about me. But the advantages to both families are significant.\n\nI am fond of Mauriene, though. I … want her to think well of me.

Bit of thorny trail we're on, yeah? But hostile Argonians making potions out of a plant from Oblivion seems like all the more reason to find that creeper and get it out of here.\n\nBesides, that poor tree's still begging for us for help.

Well, the next step is complicated. I need to identify the spiritual passenger you are dealing with. Have you been in any locations rife with death lately? A terrifying cave, or haunted ruin? A forsaken forest, perhaps?
The ghosts of civilization are almost always riddled with spirits stuck remembering their old lives. Some are malicious, some are amicable. Did you meet anything specific between the crumbling walls?

Plenty of creatures, both spectral and corporeal, roam the wilds. There are as many lost souls looking to take comfort in your mortal form as there are malicious entities who seek to take your life for themselves. Which did you run afoul of?

That makes sense. Subterranean places attract all manners of woeful entities. They reside within the crevasses, hide behind boulders, and wait beneath black pools. Did you encounter anything in the darkness?
I thought I sensed something savage about you. Your passenger covets a hunt. Death was not enough to sate their blood lust even though the hunt is over. Now on to you, how are you feeling?

Your passenger seeks the familiar to distract them from their plight. They hide in you to enjoy a dull likeness of the life they left behind. I'm afraid it will never be enough to satisfy their craving. Now tell me, how are you feeling?

I sense a strong, defiant, will. This entity relies on your ignorance to slowly overtake your thoughts and actions. If I'm correct, your passenger knows what they're doing and doesn't care about the danger you're in. Are you feeling all right?

You talked to <<1>>, haven't you? Look, so I'm having a few turns of bad fortune. Everybody does from time to time. \n\nSure, I lost the ring my father gave me. And my lover decided to run off with a House of Reveries performer. I'll bounce back.
No, he doesn't. But as much as I'd like to simply threaten Quistley until he gives it up, there's the question of the missing ring. However Quistley lost it, we should try to get it back.

Well, yes. The Bouchends are an influential Daggerfall family, just like the Silvelles. I've known Mauriene since we were children. I'm not surprised that a match was made.\n\nFunny. She always seemed to bring out the best in Quistley.

If Quistley is supposed to give it to Mauriene Bouchend, then yes.\n\nI don't want to see the Silvelles come to grief. A betrothal between two houses? It's important to a lot of people. And maybe it's what Quistley needs.

I believe you are afflicted with a Lurking-type spirit. These entities wait in lonely places for hosts and avoid detection by settling deep into the recesses of your mind. Shall I begin the cleansing rites?

Of course! You are afflicted with a Traveler-type spirit. These entities seek those with a passion for adventure. In extreme cases, their influence towards recklessness has been known to lead to their host's death. Shall I begin the cleansing rites?

Hmm, a spirit that seeks to avoid detection. Oh, oh no. There is a Possession-type spirit within you. If left untreated, it will infiltrate your mind, consuming all your thoughts until you have no identity left. Shall I begin the cleansing rites?

Very well. As Claudina would say—I admire the questioning nature of a skeptic, and look forward to continuing our discussions when next we meet.\n\nOf course, they're usually not alive for the second meeting, but maybe your fate will be different.
I doubt I know any more than you do, but sure. What's on your mind?
So they're still around? Sixty years on? Must be a tenacious bunch.\n\nYou don't … you don't think they're here now, do you? In Gideon, I mean?
Not yet? Ha! You've got ice water in those veins and no mistake!\n\nYou don't think this Waking Flame cult is still around, do you? This ledger's older than I am. They must be gone by now.

Can't say as I have. I'm playing investigator, sure, but I normally do my best to avoid situations like this. People like you who do this for a living? No offense, but I'll never understand it.\n\nHave you had a run-in with this Waking Flame before?

Like the ledger said, the murderer spent weeks lying about the novitiates being jealous, ferreting away gold from the treasury to make it look like they stole something, etcetera.\n\nWhen Granna Cerise vanished, they did what people always do. Assume.

By the Eight, I hope not! People stealing my lumber and dulling my saws is a damn sight better than being trapped in a gem for all eternity!\n\nLet's just assume that if they're here, they haven't noticed me. All right?

I know, I know. We'll find the proof we need with this map, I'm sure of it. If you're still suspicious, I don't blame you. But I just … I just have a feeling. I can't explain it.\n\nWe've almost cracked this. Just a little farther to go.

I also lost a lot of gold playing dice in the back alley. And I was fired from my job at the stables. And I stepped in a divot and twisted my knee. Not to mention I burned my tongue on the stew that so-called chef serves at the inn. It's been a week.
What do you mean? I don't have a problem. \n\nMy luck is going to change any moment now. I can practically taste it!
Well done. Head over to the well nearby. You will find a bucket you can use to mix the blessing solution.
Good, but what are you doing over here then? Go splash it on Leric before it loses its potency!
Barely any today. I hope you have better luck in Xi-Tsei than I'm having here. Nothing feels like biting, I suppose.

If what you and that vagabond say is true, I might be out of a job. I'll stick around for a little while, but if things get quiet enough, I may head off to Leyawiin or even Gideon. Always work for a man in my line.

Yes, I think so. Still feeling drained, but I'm beginning to get sensation back in my chest. Really odd feeling, let me tell you. I don't recommend it.\n\nMirri brought me along to have someone she could trust, but I just ended up being a liability.

My little brother and I answered a job posting seeking adventurers to help explore a newly discovered ruin, only once the expedition got underway—and we were all split up—our employers turned on us. I barely got away.

I never gave it much thought, to be honest. My father only said it was an obligation. And that Silvelles should live up to their obligations.\n\nI was angry about it, at times. Some days I resented Bastian's presence in our house.

Ah, yes. She told me about her plans to leave us. Can't say I blame her. When that total tzilnech of a warlord Naxhosa moved his people into our ruins, shadows crept upon us.\n\nAt one time, we had protectors to keep us safe. But no more.

That Bastian was not a Silvelle and never would be.\n\nMy parents saw to his needs, and when he was grown they gave him important work in looking after the family's business interests. I would expect more gratitude on his part, frankly.

Isn't it obvious? Bastian never got into trouble! When I didn't study, my parents would point at Bastian and ask why I couldn't be more like him.\n\nI thought they cared more for him than for me, until my father took me aside and explained things.

Those are them. The legendary Four Winds. They defended our village, until one day they had some big argument. After that, they disbanded.\n\nThree moved to the outskirts of the village and one stayed. She died during a raid by Naxhosa's people.

Lord Silvelle told me years ago that my older sister died. I assumed that she'd been caught up in my father's treason, or had fallen ill and passed away like my mother.\n\nI didn't learn I was wrong until a letter from an old Hallix servant turned up.

Inalieth, a Wood Elf. She wrote years ago, but Lord Silvelle hid the letter. When I finally saw it, I went to find her in Grahtwood.\n\nInalieth told me that Clairene was still alive. And that I should have been sent to her when my mother died.
<Zahsbi waits for his payment>
<Zahsbi waits for his payment>
<Zahsbi waits for his payment>
<Zahsbi waits for his payment>

Free my little brother and the others before something terrible befalls them. I don't know if I can do this on my own, but I have to try.\n\nCan I count on your help? Or were all the questions just morbid curiosity? I can pay if I have to.

There were five, in addition to me who got duped into this. My brother, Liam; Eolaf, a Nord warrior; Ardia, a High Elf researcher; Deejos, an Argonian scout; and Ghalor, a Wood Elf adventurer.\n\nOther than my brother, I don't know a lot about them.

Not much. Xigira, the woman who hired us, was charming. I didn't buy her story that her expedition was for study, but she paid half our fee up front. I figured they were just treasure hunters looking for plunder. We had no idea they were a cult.

About the time they said "don't kill her, we need her for the ritual" while trying to wrestle me to the ground. Probably saved my life though. I fought twice as hard knowing they were taking it easy on me.\n\nNo one else escaped, that I know of.

Otumi-Ra, the Unrelenting Gale. Stronger than an ox and tougher than a haj mota. Fun at parties, too. A much nimbler dancer than you would expect.\n\nThen there was Satul-Sa, the Steady Breath. The only one to stay here and protect us. But no more.

When those bandits first came to raid our village, she fought them off easily. We thought that was the end of it.\n\nBut soon they returned, and something had changed. They cut her down like a rotted tree. We have not been free of them since.

Well, I used to be the local blacksmith. I do good work, nothing special. But it keeps the village doors from falling off and the tools sharp.\n\nSince Naxhosa though, all I can do is patch up the injured after a raid. There is nothing left to smith.

Of course I have, ojel. Do you think I can see the wreckage of my village and not feel a fire in my gut?\n\nBut, I am no warrior. I am a smith. It is good to know who you are, even if it brings limitations.

Dead? Satul-Sa? She was the smartest and wisest of us all. This is impossible!\n\nAnd yet, since Nuxul brought you it must be true. The consequences of my selfish choice meant the death of my dear friend. Such a bitter lesson.

You shall have my aid, if you perform a simple task. When I … retired … I buried my blades deep in the ground.\n\nGo north to the ruins. Retrieve them for me so that I may avenge Satul-Sa. Be warned, as I made certain they are well-protected.

What else? Show me that you hold the same strong will that makes for the greatest of warriors! Oh, chum, we shall see if you can withstand the greatest of Argonian ales and wines.\n\nPlus, this should help numb the rodents gnawing in my head.

I was thinking the same thing. Could he have found the other two Ambitions? And are they people, too? Cracked acorns, mysteries make my head hurt!\n\nI'd much rather have a clear target so I can fill it full of arrows!
Lead the charge when you are ready, outsider. The Winds will be at your back.

Knew that would get your attention, I'm not the sort of woman who would lie you know. Can't tell you where it is, not with all these little ones running around. They don't want it to be too easy for you.\n\nI can give you a hint though.
There's a rock nearby. Look, I never said the hints would be helpful!
They say it's a place of buried ruins and lost hopes. And also stone arches. I've asked and there's nothing poetic about the arches. The squirrels say they're not even that good for climbing on.
It's hilly. What, you were expecting something more useful from a squirrel?

After Lord Hallix's treason, some of the king's counselors argued for executing the whole family to make sure no threat to the king remained. \n\nThe only way to survive was to convince the king's officials that the Hallix family no longer existed.
I'm tired of the squirrels' annoying chatter. Still, these little creatures have been my loyal companions for a long time, I'd like to see someone else grow to respect their usefulness like I have.

My gorgeous wife-to-be has commissioned a painter to capture our likenesses. She has taken it upon herself to organize all the details. Thankfully I only have one task, but I am worried that my eye is not as refined as she expects.

Yeah, I've read that somewhere. \n\nBut what about the calling cards. The black hand is definitely making a statement.

Right. Report to Commander Ortin on your way out. Tell him what happened. Then go check on Councilors Faleria and Vandacia. I need to return to Leyawiin and consult with Lovidicus.\n\nBut this? Between you and I? It isn't over. Remember that.

All right, but why keep it a secret from me? We were trying to prevent the councilors from being murdered, but four people had to die before you decided to mention your connection to the murderers! Oh, sorry, possible murderers!

Didn't matter? All right. I'll keep your secret. For now. But if the Dark Brotherhood turns out to be involved and you lied to me, I'll put an arrow between your eyes myself.\n\nI just hope I don't have another of those waking visions along the way.

Remember back at Fort Blueblood when we found the murdered servant? I had a vision of a shadowy figure. It was a robed and hooded cultist. Order of the Waking Flame, I think.\n\nIt was brief and powerful. Over in a moment. But the figure felt … evil.

What else could it be? It's written in an unknown language. Probably Daedric! Lupus sent me to find it, so it must be important.\n\nThe last vision was a warning. About the cultists. I can't let them get this book. I'll hang onto it. No matter what.

You really do know your Dark Brotherhood stuff. It sure would have been helpful if you mentioned any of this a lot earlier.\n\nAll right, assassin. Is that what I call you now? If you're so smart, go and open the door. I'll wait.

No. The orders suggested it was placed in the sanctuary after we abandoned it the first time. We hadn't finished reopening the place and I hadn't run across any hidden caches. Another mystery, I suppose.\n\nLet's keep looking.
I'm from Grahtwood! Have you met my people? It's all roasted this and roasted that. And even raw this and raw that, too!\n\nYou don't get to enjoy many pastries under Green Pact rules, you know.

Knowing that you helped people—and seeing how much they appreciate it—more than makes up for the dark times. You walk into town and people say, hey! It's Eveli!\n\nSoon the little kids around here will all have pig-tails in their hair. Count on it!

Her name is poison fumes spread by the wind. She shows great savagery, even for Sul-Xan. \n\nWhispers say Bahsei's magic no longer comes from the Hist. She abandoned the one to revere another—Mehrunes Dagon. And so earned her title of Flame-Herald.
As the Sul-Xan warriors charged us from the shadows, I saw her standing among them. She raised her arms and shouted that today they would take no prisoners. We were food to bring forth Xalvakka.

I do not know. And did not feel the need to ask. I sag my tail with regret knowing that now we have failed. \n\nOr perhaps this was its purpose? Nevertheless, I shall try my best to fulfill the will of the Hist.

Because she is a disappointment, as she has always been, s'wit. A Dunmer with her upbringing should have paid her respects to me a hundred times over.\n\nHer contempt for tradition is a blight on our house.

Of course not! She was intended to be betrothed to the House Father's first-born, not some tenth-rate House Cousin she fetched trinkets for. With a word she could have elevated our station to the Great Houses.\n\nI ask so little, and she delivers less.

Feh, close. We are family. Close has nothing to do with it. She was born and raised to carry on the legacy of our house. It was her duty to bring prestige and prosperity to our name as we have for generations, not run off with some feckless Hlaalu.

It was a singular find. The greatest in my career. A Dwemer puzzle box of such complexity and beauty that it could only truly be appreciated by a great mind. Onimiril understood that. We knew that this device hid answers to mysteries only they knew.

He was behind me at every turn. Studying the puzzle box. Commiserating its loss. Guiding me in searching for it. He was clever enough to keep my attention focused outward. Staying in my blindspot until the very moment he pushed me to my death.

Worth killing over, at least! I underestimated Onimiril's ambitions. I didn't think High Elves had the stomach for theft and murder. I should never have shared that box with anyone. It was meant for me and me alone!

Anyone who knew that device's true value would never let it go. He'd never part with it willingly, no matter how much its maddening design might thwart him. My only consolation is my certainty that the puzzle has tormented him ever since he stole it.

Well, you see, as Onimiril's apprentice this one was afforded certain privileges. His master was not so particular about the rules of the guild, so his banishment was not all that surprising, but his replacement is quite stern and this one has erred.
This one certainly hopes to get the opportunity to try, but that will not matter if Arelette is feathered and fried. Takaano will read up on transformations while you search. Just please find her.

Onimiril's former apprentices are on probation and his new instructor watches us like a hawk. It is only by some miracle that she did not witness Takaano's terrible error, but she will discover it if Arelette does not return soon.

Sombren doesn't think so. He says that's the last place they'd look for us.\n\nI'm still attuned to the realm from the trial in the Ashen Forest. Sombren believes he'll have enough time to teach me if I'm not in danger of imminently exploding.

Nocturnal, our Mighty Mistress. We are forever intertwined with her great forces. Each vassal of the Court is imbued with darkness! Shadows! \n\nThe cultists easily siphon such power while the Court is distracted.
The Waking Flame cultists lured me and Eveli out of the castle. Then they opened portals inside and attacked the remaining councilors and the Chamber of Legates.

Not quite. The scribe that Lovidicus sent for was able to decipher a portion of the code before Vandacia took the documents. That's the lead we want you to follow up on.\n\nFind Eveli at Leyawiin Castle. She knows more about the details than I do.
Mostly. You arrived and helped turn the tide. But not before Vandacia revealed himself to be the cult's high priest. He killed Councilor Faleria and stole the coded documents you recovered.

Home, I think. It turns out that there were some wealthy people in Leyawiin willing to pay to keep their relatives' involvement with the Cult of the Unmaker from coming to light.\n\nI made out like a bandit! Now I can pay off my family's debts, too.

They recently pillaged my temple without warning or provocation, taking the relics in our keeping and striking down anyone who tried to stop them. This behavior is nothing like the Knights of the Silver Rose that I know.
Of course you did, you're Undaunted! I don't care how many deadly Daedric artifacts a bunch of poncy knights possess, they'll never stand a chance against the likes of us.

We have come from the Battlespire to investigate the magical energies radiating from the Dread Cellar. This installation should be abandoned, but as you can see it isn't entirely empty.\n\nI'll turn a blind eye to any scavenging, if you assist us.
Dig up any good Imperial secrets while you were burying all those Daedra? Well, save them for the campfire. I've got no time for gossip and intrigue while there are still Pledges to be paid out.
<You are about to enter a Group Dungeon. Are you ready to leave your current Zone?>

I hoped a word with the knight commander would prove that the attack was the work of some overzealous recruits, but he's refused to see me or return the relics taken from my temple.\n\nI can offer more than blessings for their return.

If this ambush was any indication, we're going to face a fair amount of resistance searching these ruins. Help us clear out these Daedra and discover the source of the magical activity here and we'll compensate you for your service.

I know. It's in her nature to look after others. I'm glad she's got someone reliable to look after her when she needs it. She's liable to wind as tangled up in worry as her father and get an ulcer otherwise.\n\nBe a bad influence, like her mother.

Their goals hide among the worms they call friends. I know little of Sul-Xan desires, and had hoped never to learn.\n\nStories drift to me about brutal sacrifices. Bloodshed for the glory of chaos. But who can know the truth?

Ah, perhaps you have not traveled that far south. The old city is a sight to behold. The finest mud puddles in this region. And the stonework amazes any who visit.\n\nMost of us live in a village just outside so that we can keep an eye on the xanmeer.

It stands upon large vents of scalding steam that occasionally burst into large geysers. It's a rare occurrence, but they can threaten the structures of the xanmeer. Some of us work to keep it intact when an eruption damages the stone.

Another waking vision! Happened when I got here. I think that strange book is trying to tell me something.\n\nI saw these weird cubes with symbols on them. Symbols like the ones in the book I'm carrying. I'm not sure what it all means.

Didn't she tell you? We met before, after she first became aware of Leovic's secret.\n\nI believe the book she found is the Mysterium Xarxes, penned by Mehrunes Dagon himself. Or so they say. She must place it on the lectern to disable the wards.

I do hate leaving a story half-finished. One time I lost a book I was reading and it drove me crazy!\n\nBut yes, at some point we should find the fourth Ambition. And make sure none of them wind up sacrificed to Mehrunes Dagon.

When the Wood Elf and I crossed paths when she first learned of Leovic's secret, I sensed something unusual about her. It's the book she carries. It's an ancient and powerful tome of … questionable origin.

Curiosity, little mortal. How else am I to fill the endless days of immortality? I collect secrets, and I long to learn the truth of the Longhouse Emperors and their mysterious bargain with the Prince of Destruction.\n\nNow, go deal with those wards.

Need is such a specific word. I do not need anything, little mortal. I am quite content to find a new distraction and leave your pitiful world to the Prince of Destruction.\n\nHowever, if you do decide to open the vault, I shall aid you as I can.

He has grown distant lately. Meeting in secret with other mages, disappearing for days at a time. There is something troubling him that he does not want his egg-siblings to know about.\n\nBut I believe he might have told Melyn Drad.

As I told Eveli, a courier arrived shortly ahead of you. After you and your partner finalize your plans, make sure to talk to them.\n\nThey were quite insistent that they be allowed to deliver their message directly to you.

Yup. And Lyranth thinks they could arrive here at any moment. Let's look around.\n\nOh, hey, one more thing. The book sort of started to tingle the moment we entered the vault. Just thought you should know.

After we rebuild the village and I know we are truly safe, I may start selling my wares in other towns. Go north to dryskin lands. \n\nI want to be like the Winds, traveling around, taking in the sights. Living a better life.

I don't know it. I'm making an educated guess. Daedrology is my main field of study, though I tend to avoid getting caught up in their worship and rituals. Mostly I'm fascinated why anyone would join these fetching cults in the first place.

I took an interest in the Anticipations of the Tribunal and my ancestors' worship of them before the Three arose to godhood. \n\nDark Elves aren't the only ones who revere Daedra alongside Divines, but now's not the time for a philosophical discussion.

Not of this severity. We really only trained warriors out of tradition. Mostly they would hunt our food. A great sorrow that we have lost them all to the Sul-Xan.\n\nPerhaps if you manage to drive out these invaders, we shall know peace again.

The role of stone-talker involves communing with spirits and beasts who reside in the old city. Manasha truly reveled in speaking to these creatures. He wallowed in it as might a hog in mud.\n\nThe two of them meant a new era for Krona-Konu.

Not since we returned from the Deadlands. In fact, the book has been strangely silent. No tingles, no bad dreams, nothing. And I'm fine with that.\n\nGetting messages from a book supposedly written by Mehrunes Dagon is kind of unsettling.

We'll be getting back to the guild with our dues. I'm sure after this job I'll be a fully fledged thief—oops, full fledged thief! Then Lady Twilight will make her debut for real!\n\nWe should do another caper soon!

Seeks was afraid we'd get fleeced on the payment, but the old guy was totally fine with it being busted! He was relieved even! Said it's one less dangerous object in the world.\n\nTurns out he's got a vault full of cursed stuff! Weird thing to collect.

Back to give the guild its cut and report on Erilthel's progress, or lack there of.\n\nShe did manage to show some improvement this time, but she's not ready to leave the nest. Plus, I don't hate anyone at the guild enough to inflict her on them.

Surprisingly, yes. We got that hunk of junk to our buyer and they were thrilled to take it off our hands, even in its busted condition. I expected a High Elf collector to be more fussy.\n\nThings worked out for everybody but the Painted Eye.

You must complete a series of tasks in order to fully change the course of the river. \n\nSlay a fearsome enemy, find a striking locale, and speak with a city job broker. The order does not matter, all I care about is the completion.

No. I have no truth to speak. I simply listen. I hear the trees, the water, the people. You can learn a great deal about the world by listening. Consider me a storyteller. I just want to hear more stories of the world.\n\nYours included.

It is mine.\n\nThough I will return to the Hist upon my death, I want all the stories I have collected in this life to have their place … to be remembered. I carry this with me to add to it as I travel.

I merely want to hear all that I can. The world is too large for me to explore it all. I could spend a thousand lifetimes trying and still not learn all that it has to offer. So I seek those who change the water, who venture deeper than I ever will.

Yes. You must listen to the muttering of the rivers, the stillness of the ponds … each of them carry a thousand stories. I wish to hear them all. \n\nYou are someone who can help me with that, I have no doubt.

I simply wish to wade in the rivers that you will change. \n\nVenture through Blackwood. Triumph in a great hunt, see a place that was once forgotten, answer the call of petitioners! Report back once you have made the ripples, and I will reward you.

I knew it as soon as you approached. You are someone who will tell great stories.\n\nYou crave new experiences, and there is no doubt you will benefit from them. You will step into the river to change its course, like an errant stone.

No, I have followed her expedition for a time. She has not expressly forbade me from doing so, but she has not encouraged me either.\n\nBut I enjoy seeing the places she visits and hearing the stories people tell as they pass in and out of her tent.

Oh, just a lifetime of public service and bureaucracy. Mostly financial records, but also meeting notes, ledgers, those sorts of things.\n\nI oversaw budgets and finances, the collection of taxes, public works. And I kept immaculate records.

Gideon fares well. Many of those who secretly served Vandacia tried to creep back into their burrows after Fort Redmane. But my Black Fins are good at digging up mudcrabs of the two-legged sort.\n\nThey cannot escape justice by hiding.
The leader who would stand in front of her people must be ready to share their dangers. Where else do I belong, if not here? When do I stand and fight, if not now?

Blackwood is at peace. I can lay down my sword for a time and spend my days building something new instead of fighting to save what is already here.\n\nAlthough I think I will begin by building better walls in Gideon. Just in case.

We've had no more trouble with apocalyptic cults since the defeat of Vandacia and the Waking Flame. And between the Ivory Brigade and the Black Fin Legion, we've kept Blackwood safe.\n\nTruth be told, it's been rather boring.
Don't mistake my bravado for foolishness. Your ally Lyranth explained the stakes of the game to me. I'll see this through to victory, or die in the attempt. You can count on no less from me.

I fought for my home and my people. Any soldier would do as much. But you, my friend, had the courage to take up a cause that wasn't yours and face dangers beyond this world. And all for the sake of strangers.\n\nI salute you.

Rian and Keshu dealt with the Waking Flame adherents who revealed themselves in Blackwood. So I devoted myself to those who hoped to remain in the shadows.\n\nI must look after the Dark Brotherhood's good name, after all.

On the contrary, thank you. The destruction of Tamriel would have been bad for business. I'm grateful for the opportunity to have helped you avert that disaster.\n\nJust wish I had had a proper contract to go along with it.

Let me mark your map. Xynaa told me where to find these slivers of the Deadlands when I needed them. \n\nDagon cultists often enshrine these shards whenever they find them. You'd be surprised how often chunks of Oblivion make their way to Nirn.

No. You're not an Ambition. Besides, you've been to the Deadlands already and suffered no ill effects.\n\nIf the twins attempted that before we attune them, the plane would rip them apart. Our power, it's connected to Mehrunes Dagon in some way.

I'm not entirely sure. I just know that there's some element of Mehrunes Dagon inside us. And it wants to return whence it came. I think that's what Vandacia hoped to accomplish by killing me.\n\nAnyway, I'd rather not see that happen. To any of us.
I sense they are shells cracked open, just as I felt with Veeka-Gel. Their souls were not allowed to reenter the way of things. They were ripped—as if by a beast tearing flesh for a meal.
The keep maintains its vigil and the garrison's reputation stands strong despite that business with the Painted Eye, thanks to our victory at Fort Redmane.
The pleasure is ours. Too many nights of holding down a fort dulls a soldier's edge. We look forward to sharpening our blades on Dagon's horns.
If I were wise, I'd have left it behind long ago. I've been wed to the blade for so long now I wouldn't know what to do otherwise.\n\nSo long as I'm fool enough to keep fighting, you can call on me.

I bet knowing an outsider has saved the day will truly tug his tail. We often argued until the night-bugs slept about the risks of isolating the tribe.\n\nBut, I feel sun-blessed that he survived. I would not change a thing.

So my mud-soaked friend survived. The Ca-Uxith tribe will need him more than ever now. This incursion roiled the energies under Krona-Konu and only he can calm them.\n\nPlease, let him know that you spoke to us. Give him that kindness for me.

In every way! What was once just of Oblivion became mixed with Nirn. Now that energy is a part of both realms. And that is why Mehrunes Dagon wants it back. It will give him the connection to Nirn that he so greatly desires. A path to your world.

Yeah, we did, didn't we. All right, your secret's safe with me. But if the Dark Brotherhood turns out to be involved and you lied to me … well, let's assume that's not going to happen.\n\nI just hope I don't have another one of those waking visions.

And you as well. I arrived as quickly as I could, but even then I was too late to do more than glance at the coded documents. You should hurry, though. Vandacia went after Councilor Lovidicus and he had murder in his eyes.\n\nTake my sister and go!

Not only that, I'm the best scribe south of Skyrim! I arrived as quickly as I could, but I was too late to do more than glance at the coded documents. You should hurry, though. Vandacia went after Councilor Lovidicus and he had murder in his eyes.
My brother will fill us in after we save Councilor Lovidicus and whoever else is still alive in the castle.\n\nAnd don't worry about Beragon. He can take care of himself.

All week and twice on Fredas! He's also an excellent scribe and an accomplished adventurer. Which means he can take care of himself. The same can't be said of Councilor Lovidicus.\n\nBeragon will fill us in later. Let's go save the castle!

The trade is simple. I need silk from the bluewhisper moths for next season's line. Bring me a few bundles and I'll trade them for the attire you seek. They nest to the north, along the river bank.\n\nOr you can pay the gold … if you can afford it.

A pleasure doing business with you! \n\nNow, please. Take your time and select the outfit that most suits you. You want to look your best and also make a good impression when attending a formal event.

Excellent! The moth loves to nest in the brush to the north of Leyawiin, along the banks of the river. Bring me a few bundles of their silk and we'll call it even.\n\nDo be cautious while looking for the silk. Dangerous creatures abound in those hills!

I leave the specifics up to you. Consider who you have helped throughout Blackwood. Eveli might have some ideas.\n\nRemember, this is not a mission for just any courier or messenger. The cult has made the roads of Blackwood especially dangerous.

They are my brothers and sisters in arms. The finest Argonian warriors to ever emerge from Black Marsh.\n\nIt started as a mercenary band and was tempered in the Akaviri and alliance wars. Now they protect Gideon. And they will protect the Ambitions.

I believe the book to be the Mysterium Xarxes, a tome penned by Mehrunes Dagon himself. Or so they say. Whatever the truth of its origins, the tome is both powerful and dangerous.\n\nEveli must place it on the lectern to disable the wards.
That's great! My brother Beragon always told me that adventures turn on the favors we collect along the way.\n\nSo, who do you think we can count on?
Definitely go call in that debt! More brigadines would be very helpful when the Order of the Waking Flame attacks Fort Redmane.
The Borderwatch garrison of the Ivory Brigade! Great fighters, from what I've heard. You should absolutely ask the commander to send whatever support he can to Fort Redmane.

The legendary Argonian warriors? I read about them! You have to go ask them!\n\nI do hope they'll come. I really want to meet them. You'll ask them for me, right? We could use those kinds of skills at Fort Redmane.

Have you forgotten already? I may have abandoned joining the Sapiarchy, but I was still a top candidate among many a talented scholar and mage.\n\nI don't have your experience as an adventurer, but I'm more suited to unraveling this mystery than most.

Daedric rituals weren't on my curriculum in the College of Sapiarchs, but I've studied enough magic to puzzle this out.\n\nThere's a good chance Annyce will return to town, like the others. If she does, confront her about this.

The Merciless. Yes. We may have upset him when we made off with his entire cache of ancient jewels and three chestfuls of gold. Yet he will rue the day he challenged the crew of the Pale Spirit.\n\nSoon enough, we'll make an end of him. We always do.
I know that suffocating feeling far too well, and the desperation to escape it. I know what it's like to be blinded by the need for liberation. Cres and I both caused more pain than we ever intended.

It may fly in the face of common sense, but I think Cres might have the makings of a fine Player. They're a bit … unrefined, but taking on a new role seems to come naturally, and they'll never forget their lines.\n\nI could sponsor them to the House.

Misguided as Cres was, I don't believe they acted in malice. There aren't many stories of compassionate Daedra, but it seems at least some of them might be true.\n\nThe question is, does this little Daedra's story have to end in tragedy?

Do not fear. Since the triumph of the Winds over the bandits, many of our tribe have begun training with us. They see now that complacency cannot keep them hidden. I believe the village is safe in our absence.

Feh. You call that a battle? Merely pest removal. If you had witnessed my battle against Kasa-Eidu the Mud-Hearted, you would understand a true struggle of wits.\n\nAs you might expect, I returned to my studies. I cannot waste time before my time ends.

Elossi finally convinced us to take on students—replacements to carry the tradition of the Winds. They will need a great deal more training before they can match my … our greatness. But knowing they will be out there pleases me.

I was a massive, ancient tree fading from thirst. Then your arrival was a downpour, soaking me to my roots. I stand tall and filled with life once again.\n\nWhatever comes next, I am only prepared because you brought me back to the world.

How could the deeds of Otumi-Ra become any more legendary? My name is already known across all of Tamriel! What next, the moons? I receive my own stars? Actually … hmm …. \n\nNo. Just watching your great success pleases me enough.

Well, there was this one thing that stuck out. The cult Xigira was leading is much bigger than this group. Something about how this foothold would be vital to their ambitions. All rather typical cult drivel if you ask me.

Just what I overheard. It's not like Xigira gloated about her genius plans while I was bound up. She mostly just yelled at me for Mirri causing trouble and told me all the horrible things that would happen when they tossed my soul to Mehrunes Dagon.

Much improved since your arrival. Meer-Ta spends less time hidden away. I could sense his eagerness to join me in this battle, though he might deny it. And Otumi-Ra resists challenging every stranger he meets. These improvements encourage me.
Thank you for giving me a chance. I get to be anyone I want now. But most importantly, I get to be me.\n\nAnd don't worry, I am now totally aware that break a leg is merely a figurative expression.

Yes, yes, yes! I have gotten try out so many things since I became Alchemy's student! Like sticking a sword under my arm for a death scene and not stabbing myself in the chest. \n\nI'm not allowed to try sword swallowing yet, though.

Soon? Not in the least. Even this little scuffle we are about to enter does not worry me.\n\nBut eventually my scales shall turn gray, as all things must. The sheer volume of knowledge I desire to understand before then staggers me. And so I study.

Not soon, but eventually. In the meantime, it seems that Igmund wants to form a troupe of his own at the Happy Crow. And Annyce is already adapting Captain Wereshark for the stage.\n\nI'm happy we inspired them.
I think we both know that luck has little to do with it.\n\nMay your talents lead you to your dreams as well.

More than with most Hopefuls, certainly, but there's nothing more rewarding than nurturing a burgeoning talent. Mark my words, Dreamer will be a star. I might find myself next in line for Grand Maestro when all is said and done.
Fortunes shine upon you, blessed laborer. I will pray daily for your success.

Resting where we left it, awaiting the faithful to come and clear away the rot consuming the abbey. The Knights of Iron will soon launch a crusade against the vile beasts and Goblins inhabiting the place.
Indeed! I've got all sorts of ideas for a new book of ovamancy! Eggs with smaller eggs inside! Brilliant, right?\n\nDon't … just don't answer that.

Yes! Well, no. Sort of. I'm giving the censer to Tiras.\n\nAll the pomp, plotting, and vanity among the magisters … it's just not for me. I only made the censer to keep them off my back. This way, Tiras gets what he wants, and I get some peace.

The wise mage is the mage who can learn from their mistakes.\n\nI may not have underestimated Revus's skill, but I definitely underestimated his tenacity and faithfulness. I learned a great deal, and that is worth all the trauma.

Well, I'm the baby brother and Mirri takes her place as the eldest very seriously. She's more of a mother than our mother in some ways. Mom would call this a learning experience. Doesn't like to coddle.

Oh, no! No! Mom would have beaten Xigira to death with a cookpan if it came down to it, she'd just lecture us about needing to be able to get ourselves out of a pinch without her.\n\nYou know how adventurers are.
That's all a helpless baby brother can ask! At least until I can wrestle with four armed giants myself.\n\nHope to see you both again soon.
Yeah, well, fair. Mirri might even be more headstrong than mother.\n\nYou take care of my sister though. Our dad will get an ulcer if you two are always off to Vehk knows where in Oblivion.

You've done more than enough. Just keep fighting. It's all we can do. If nothing else, we know when push comes to shove, we can beat those fetchers.\n\nI think I'm going to just have a drink and a quiet moment to myself. Enjoy today. I'll be all right.
Not a chance, f'lah. Today I learned that's something I can do. And next time I'll be better prepared.\n\nBut try not to let that intimidate you.
One of our village guards. Though, now she may be our sole remaining defender.\n\nShe protected us as we ran from the initial attack. After we found safe haven, she sent me to call for aid.

Dust-On-Scales. The sinew and veins of our tribe. He serves as conduit between the Hist and Rockgrove's xanmeer.\n\nHe knows a great deal about the old city's secrets. You should seek out his guidance.

Hmm … how to explain? Great energies exist underground that bind our tribe's Hist and this xanmeer. At times, the flows are disturbed and erupt onto the surface. My role is to study these forces so we may better maintain the old temple.

Worse? I suppose that depends on your perspective.\n\nIt has been growing in intensity again. Back at the same level as when we first left the vault. Sombren is worried I don't have much time. That's why he's being so insistent.

Deeply concerning. Somehow Flame-Herald Bahsei has managed to tear the souls from my kin. They should naturally return to the Hist. Instead she collects them for some grave purpose.\n\nWe call this xul-vahat—a taboo death. It must be stopped.

Leyawiin has stood with Gideon more times than I can count. We will continue to work together to keep Blackwood secure.\n\nCaptain Rian and I were even discussing joint patrols. Imagine, brigadines and legionnaires walking side-by-side. It's inspiring!

The work to build a place where Saxhleel and dryskins can learn from each other in peace. Where all people can prosper while maintaining their own cultures.\n\nAnd I want to continue to study the ancient Argonians. To learn what they can teach us.

Blackwood? I was certain they said Blackfeather!\n\nWell, a party's a party. You helped us in our time of need, so we will help you celebrate your victory, too. It is the least we can do. The absolute least!

Please. I'm sure Stibbons is just dithering about somewhere in the xanmeer without a care in the world. Any excuse to get out of a day's work.\n\nHe is by far the laziest, most infuriating manservant in all of Tamriel!
That is what I want to hear. A little confidence like that around Stonewastes and perhaps Naxhosa would not have rolled over us like a boulder.\n\nWe should hurry before Elossi changes her mind.

I seem to remember a field of waking seeds grows to the east of here. Gather a handful, then come back. I will keep an eye on this hero of legends in the meantime.\n\nI should warn you. Some creatures are attracted to the smell. Keep your scales moist.

Who knows. He's been blistering my backside like an ornery shalk since I've been old enough to walk. I've got a thick skin for him, but that stupid trinket was like a deep splinter wedged between us. Now that it's plucked, maybe the rift will heal.

They are like my people, but harsher … crueler. Naga bear many similarities to the Saxhleel, but they are often taller, and their faces wider. They are drawn to war and violence. Both come easily to them.\n\nWhich is why this threat is so dire.

The order was sworn to protect Tamriel from the corruption of wicked Daedra. This stronghold is where they lock away dangerous items confiscated from harmful cults. I never expected them to turn their swords upon my temple.

I only know that the Knights of the Silver Rose have claimed many such items from Daedric cults in their time and that they keep them secured in Red Petal Bastion. We'll need to explore to discover where they are keeping the spoils of my temple.

I am Weylin, preacher of the Mother of the Rose. I live to profess Azura's love. She seeks to cradle and nurture all of our mortal souls. Those who rest upon her bosom know comfort like no other. Those who disturb that peace feel her thorns.

Helping. Is that so hard to believe? Not out of the goodness of my heart, of course. The priest was in possession of something I need until the Knights of the Silver Rose robbed it from him. We've come to a mutually beneficial arrangement.

You may call me Lyranth, little mortal. So long as you intend to help the priest and reclaim what was taken from him, I am your ally. If you so much as think about interfering in our arrangement you will live to regret it for generations to come.

Already forgotten our glorious adventure with the Thieves Guild? The vile Iron Wheel accosting me? The wondrous garb I made for the lavish wedding you attended?\n\nI even offered to make uniforms for the guild and Zeira laughed at me. Hmph. Their loss.

Ah yes, we worked together alongside the exquisite Bebbia Sleek-Fur. On her beautiful Khajiit tapestry. As much as I love weaving vivid imagery with my needlework, it doesn't pay the bills.\n\nNot that there was much gold in Senchal to begin with.

The laypeople who served the Silver Rose were growing more frightened of them by the day. They either fled or met with some more unfortunate fate some time ago. The last entries were long before the attack on my temple.
Putting myself in harm's way is hardly a comparison. What's costly to me is priceless to you, mortal. When your kind bargain with the lords of Oblivion, you always walk away poorer.

I'm sorry, no. I've never felt anything like this while communing with the Mother of the Rose. These energies are vast, but undirected. I couldn't begin to identify their source.\n\nThe only thing I'm certain of is that this can't be good.

Hmph. Much as I might like that, the agreement I have with Weylin is binding. We must recover all the items from his temple, at least so long as he's alive.\n\nTake good care of him and you'll continue to have my cooperation.

I will remain here for a time. There are many who pass through these parts. Perhaps others will be as generous as you were with their stories. \n\nThe waters will continue to change. I wish to drench myself.

Not so differently than one might conjure a Daedra. I merely called forth with my invocations and was answered. Instead of pulling something out of Oblivion, I pushed something through. Though I could not have done it without Azura's blessing.

Mortals who possess Daedric artifacts are often steered toward a Prince's desires through their use, but even locked away the insidious influence of all these items grew to be too much to contain. These dark desires crept into the knights' minds.
Persistence will not wear me down, mortal. If I deign to share my motives with you, it won't be for the sake of your idle curiosity.\n\nRemain useful and you may become part of my designs.

I'm not really sure. A Daedric relic a stranger dropped in my collection box. I can't for the life of me recall them. A trade for something borrowed, they said. I'm not sure what they meant, but I've held onto it ever since.
Returning Azura's hallowed objects to my temple comes first, but I will need to work quickly to make certain none of these other relics fall into the wrong hands now that the Silver Rose is no more.

It's not so much what I'm planning as what a troublesome Prince has in motion. Once I figure out where I—and this little trinket—fit in I'll be sure to seek your services.\n\nUntil then, you'll have to wait with bated breath.

I couldn't possibly explain it to you, admittedly because I don't know myself. What I do know is someone who shouldn't have it wants it very much and I'm very curious to know why this miniscule thing is of such great importance.

Simply put, a nymic is a Daedra's true name. Some of us have many, others only one. If another knows these secret names, they can wield great power and influence over the Daedra they belong to.\n\nMortals use them in their incantations to compel us.

Let me see the documents you found. \n\nI am familiar with nymics, but not with this egonymic. If it truly has the power to banish Mehrunes Dagon, then no wonder the Longhouse Emperors kept it hidden. And did you visit the doomvault mentioned here?

Interesting. And you found this in the vault? The one Moricar claimed belonged to his daughter? Then show it to the Anchorite. Perhaps she can remember something and ascertain its purpose.\n\nWe will need some advantage the next time we face Sombren.

We were tipped off that the Dread Cellar had become the source of intense magical activity from an unusual source: a Dremora named Lyranth. She warned that a group called the Waking Flame is at work here. That much has proven to be true.

The Dread Cellar was a prison for the worst enemies of the Empire. It was a highly protected secret until the Empire collapsed. It was abandoned not long after. There isn't much more I can say than that.

The principal stronghold of the Imperial Battlemages. The Spire's council continues to train and dispatch battlemages to preserve what remains of the Empire where we can.\n\nLucilla is a battlemage-in-training herself. This mission will be a good test.
Hmm. Do you have a name, child?
Well, I wouldn't sign it on this effigy, but I suppose it will have to do.\n\nNow, take it to one of the braziers nearby and douse it in the flames. That will imbue it with power from the Evergloam.
I'm Lucilla. That's Martus, my commanding officer. You probably could have guessed from our uniforms, but we are Imperial Battlemages. Well, he is. I am still a potential, in training.
Very little. Martus said our orders are simply to investigate the source of the magical disturbance that our informant spoke of. Anything else about this place is a state secret, apparently.

Hurts, but nothing a little magic won't patch up. I wish our retinue had fared as well. That ambush cut them down before they even knew what hit them.\n\nYou're ready to face the sort of enemy that can kill trained soldiers like that?

I had a vault? Yes, I remember something about a place where they put me when I was being trained by Sister Celdina.\n\nLet me see. Hmm. It does feel familiar. Like trying to remember a dream upon waking. Am I supposed to do something with this?

It could have simply been defective, or releasing the energy might have required it—like a child's clay bank—or it might have become overfull and burst. I've never seen anything quite like it. But I can feel more of this energy farther in.

Hmm. The obvious explanation would be that the creature feeds on these energy reserves, harvesting them as a honey bee might. I don't like obvious answers.\n\nAll these Daedra didn't come here to rear these things like cattle. There's a bigger picture.

My course has led through many corners of existence, mortal. There are few places I wished to avoid so much as … home, as it were.\n\nAnd you? Was it not enough to involve yourself in the affairs of Mehrunes Dagon? Now Molag Bal draws your interest?

I have a talent. That's not just some excuse to brag. I was selected because I have the potential to make a difference in this crazy world. It's my duty to use it to restore the stability of the Empire. A return to peace.
How fortunate for you. I shall enjoy observing how you go about accomplishing that particular miracle.

Isn't it obvious? The pendant contains an epiphany bloodruby. It tingles when it senses residual portal magic. Use it and it will lead you to Lyranth's lair.\n\nHow ironic. She chose you to assist her. Not her prophet, but you. A heathen adventurer.

A vast prison. In the middle of nowhere. Kept a highly guarded secret. Martus is right, I probably don't want to know what happened here.\n\nTo be brimming with so much of this awful power, it must have been horrific.

Pibiha tries everything at least once—especially if she knows it's a bad idea. When Merrunz' cult gained power in Fargrave, Pibiha was curious about them. She went to one of the cult's meetings with a friend. \n\nThey never came home.

Do you seek praise? You have done as I asked and been compensated. That is the mortal custom, is it not? You want more?\n\nVery well. You helped me unravel the Longhouse Emperors' secrets in Blackwood, where we discovered three of the four Ambitions.

A lot of crazy talk about conquest, Mehrunes Dagon, and staining the world with the blood of their enemies, but nothing more about the Ambitions.\n\nUgh, it's so frustrating! I definitively could tell that Emperor Leovic had certain records destroyed.

The closest I can compare it to is the way necromancy can harness connections between a soul and the intense emotions that can stir the undead. They are harvesting the residue of such emotions here. In disturbingly great quantities.

Yeah, sorry. I know Lyranth was counting on me to come up with some clue to follow. I thought I had a lead about one of their holdings, but I hit a dead end. It seems like the Longhouse Emperors took all the information with them to their graves.
The Dremnaken. It's hunting. It never stops.\n\nThe orb. It drains life—blood—for power. To find prey.
Sometimes it roars in the north. A tower.\n\nDon't follow. Just run. Only death.

Must I say it? That the great and powerful Lyranth had a lapse in judgment? That she failed to examine her surroundings before she opened the portal to her hidden lair?\n\nVery well. I erred, ever so slightly. And the Waking Flame took advantage.

Must I say it? That the Dremora you know and admire had a lapse in judgment? That she failed to take her surroundings into account when she opened her portal?\n\nVery well, little mortal. I erred. And the Waking Flame took advantage of the opportunity.

Quite the opposite. The blade carries a unique enchantment I've never encountered before. It paralyzed me. Gave them the time they needed to portal in others and ransack the place.\n\nQuickly, check my coffer. Make sure the velvet pouch is still safe.

The Order of the Waking Flame, to be precise. Fanatics devoted to Mehrunes Dagon, the Daedric Prince of Destruction.\n\nTwo of the cultists followed before the portal closed and surprised me. Incapacitated me with that enchanted blade.
Let me see that. Hmm.\n\nThis letter names the maggot I killed. Devastator Rullen. And it mentions Greenshade. I wonder what they're doing in that miserable place?

There isn't much to tell. I have yet to determine the relic's purpose or function. I was just preparing to study it when the cult invaded my lair.\n\nNo matter. The letter tells us where to find the Dagonists. I'll open a portal.
The note you discovered contains the answer. "Where umbrage creeps." It can only refer to one place in this region—Shadows Crawl.\n\nI have no doubt we'll find the Dagonists near there.
The Dagonists use portal magic. I can smell its residue on the air. The pendant that Rogatina gave you. It can be used to follow traces of portal magic in the area.

Ah, you must be another one of the Dread Lady's followers. I've had a number of pleasant conversations with her prophet, Rogatina. And I even got to meet the Dread Lady once. She mentioned she might have need of such a tincture, so I brewed one up.

No disrespect intended, but I was hoping she'd come to pick it up herself. I so looked forward to basking in her glorious presence again. Ah, well. Perhaps next time.\n\nHere you go. And don't bother about the cost. It's a gift for the Dread Lady.

Of course. Wheels within wheels and all that. After you drink the potion and disguise yourself as a Waking Flame cultist, I will pretend to be your prisoner.\n\nNot only are you returning with the portal key, you're bringing them a gift. Me.

I assume this cave serves as a base for the Waking Flame. Not very impressive, truth be told.\n\nCome, let us find whatever hole those cultists use to store their valuables. I want the relic back in my possession before the next clannfear caws.

That this Sister Celdina had the audacity to order the cultists to steal my relic. And she gave them the damn blade that incapacitated me.\n\nShe calls the relic a portal key. Claims it leads to some sort of base in Oblivion.

Now we need to leave this place. I shall open a portal to take us to a safe location. My minion, Rogatina, should already be there. I ordered her to make certain preparations.\n\nThere, we can study these items and devise a suitable plan of action.

Yes, from which they plan to unleash disasters upon your world. I suspect it has something to do with these schematics. A diagram for some sort of device they call the cataclyst.\n\nIt has some purpose regarding Daedric transformation. Intriguing.

Devastator Rullen, the worm who led the craven attack on my lair. He had the good fortune of dying by my hand before his associate incapacitated me with that damn blade.\n\nYou will pretend to be the cultist, and I shall pretend to be your prisoner.

No, not at all. I just doubt we're going to turn up anything useful. I got twenty years of memories restored in a few seconds. It may take more than a single ritual to sift through them all.\n\nBesides, there may not be any that can actually help us.

Maybe. So far, though, I've had no luck making sense of all the memories. They still feel like they belong to somebody else, you know?\n\nHey, have you noticed that Lyranth is more serious than usual. A little more scary? Probably nothing, right?

I was an interrogator here. Like Cyronin. Though I didn't enjoy the work the way he did. It was a necessary evil. The captives held here all posed existential threats to the Empire. Dangers to be contained. Intelligence to be extracted.

We trusted him to lead us and his priority has been to protect his secrets! Our escort might still be alive if we'd infiltrated using his knowledge instead of marching up the front gate!\n\nBut what's more blood on the hands of someone who worked here?

I wouldn't have expected you to. The inhabitants prefer their privacy. It's a realm without a prince, which gives them a modicum of freedom. And it's a crossroads of sorts. A way station between Nirn and the rest of Oblivion.

With no prince, the accords that make it harder for other realms to connect to Nirn do not apply. Once they learn the way, with relics such as the portal key, the Waking Flame can move through Fargrave with impunity to reach Nirn and the Deadlands.

Once you find your way to Fargrave, the paths through Oblivion become easier to navigate. Daedra and mortals alike can be found here, engaging in trade on a planar level.\n\nI begin to grasp why the Waking Flame have set up operations here.
Indeed! And the Fargrave cataclyst could use a new Daedric entity. For the next test, of course. I'll let you present her to Sister Celdina personally.

Right through that door. I'm sure Sister Celdina will want to hear all about your mission. And we've yet to attempt to use the cataclyst on a Daedra of Lyranth's caliber. I expect the results will be quite … informative.

A remarkable achievement, devastator. And fortunate, as well. We're about to perform another test with the Fargrave cataclyst, and Nokvroz is hesitant to provide me with any more of his precious Daedra.\n\nLyranth should do very nicely.

Yes, Celdina's blade. Pity she can't make enough of those for all of you. Might actually give you mortals the horns you need to rise from the mire of your pitiful existence.\n\nEnough. Present your prize to your leader, devastator.
Worthy? It is brilliant! Sentries, take the Dremora and place her in the cataclyst.\n\nDevastator, enter the cataclyst chamber when you're ready. Then the demonstration will begin!

The cataclyst initiative proceeds apace. Sister Celdina continues to make adjustments and improvements with every version of the device.\n\nI understand we're about to witness a new demonstration. I can't wait to see it perform as intended.

Our forces are in place. Soon Fargrave will belong to the Waking Flame. We will be able to operate openly and without concern. And Sister Celdina has made great strides in perfecting the cataclyst, no thanks to Valkynaz Nokvroz.

Does Sister Celdina not teach her devastators anything of import? Valkynaz Nokvroz is a favorite of Lord Dagon. Sent here to ensure Celdina doesn't mangle the cataclyst project.\n\nSuch endeavors are too vital to leave completely in mortal hands.

No. Never met him before. But I've heard of him. One of Dagon's fiercest generals. A soldier in his ongoing quest to satisfy his insatiable hunger for destruction. It appears he was ordered to work with Sister Celdina—and I don't think he likes it.

Like being in the eye of a storm. A deluge of raging infernos, devastating earthquakes, and apocalyptic floods. The energy would have transformed me had I not acted.\n\nI could feel the promise of power … and the strange sensation of change.

Some clue as to where we are and what the Order of the Waking Flame is doing here. I also think we need to determine if the cataclyst mentioned in Sister Celdina's letter is related to the device found at the Dread Cellar in Blackwood.

No, it will make you look like the dead cultist when he was still among the living. That's the intent, anyway. I am not much of an alchemist, but I believe I can make this work. Mortal flesh is much more malleable than you would imagine.

Those of my coven are always peering into the cauldron, scrying for signs of weal or woe. It is our way.\n\nWe sensed the encroachment of this entity as we listened to the whispers of the Evergloam. But we have yet to determine how it was summoned.
Yes. Creatures such as this are usually content to reside in the Evergloam, never turning their sights on Nirn.\n\nAnd it can be no coincidence that Nocturnal's Summoning Day has just passed ….

At one of the work areas nearby, use string to bundle the feathers together into the likeness of the Crowborne Horror. \n\nOnce you douse the effigy in a brazier, it will imbue it with energy from the Evergloam and lure the creature to us.
The effigy must be wrought by your own hands! You would make a frail old woman fight such a being? Pah!\n\nRun now to my bench! Pray your work is good enough to pass muster!
We are the seers. The sources of answers, the crafters of questions.\n\nWe scry for disturbances in the Evergloam and serve as caretakers in the time of Harvest.
That is ever-changing, my child. Unknown and unfathomable. Who can truly say?\n\nIf that answer does not satisfy you, you will not find me sympathetic.
You seek to quell my anger by suggesting we may still salvage something from this debacle? Very well. Show the memory vessel to Madam Whim. Let her tell us what it contains before I take my leave.

We have no clue as to how to find the last Ambition. The ritual was halted before it could fully sort the Anchorite's memories. Only one other avenue remains open—Sombren and Calia.\n\nThe likelihood that I can locate them is slim, but I must try.
Ah, this is a very early memory. The Anchorite as a babe, hearing her father's voice.\n\nI can use this, yes.

If you find the emperor, you can talk to him. Get the information you need, directly from Moricar himself. I sense he is imprisoned in the Deadlands, in the Brandfire Reformatory.\n\nTake the Anchorite's amulet. It will lead you to the emperor's soul.

Much of what I study is beyond the limits of your mortal comprehension, but I suppose you have earned some insight into my grand purpose.\n\nI plan to study the twisted rod you gave me. I also want to ask the Anchorite about the events at Fort Grief.

Certainly not. Nokvroz was attempting to figure out how to build his own cataclyst, you do recall? But we should strike at the Waking Flame while it is in disarray. Find their hidden stronghold, learn what I require, and then do what you must.

Did you not see that coming? I'm surprised they remained allies for as long as they did. Valkynaz Nokvroz obviously hated providing support to a mortal, and Sister Celdina clearly despised having Daedric oversight.

Twice now, something triggered a return of memory. First when the Collector examined my mask, and then when I disrupted the cataclyst. But I just see fragments. Nothing clear or precise.\n\nFunny, but I think the amulet has something to do with it.
Ah, I see your skill has improved. Very nice indeed.
Your fingers have the feel for it now. It's better. You've learned something. Not much. But something.\n\nYou know what to do now. Imbue the effigy in a nearby brazier.

I may be made to account for my role in this prison someday, but I won't bear the guilt of whatever madness Cyronin was party to long after I left.\n\nI will stop it, not because of misplaced guilt, but because that's my duty.

He helped train me at the Battlespire. I thought he picked me for this mission because he trusted me and my ability. Clearly he didn't, but now I see I'd never want to be the kind of person he'd trust his secrets to.\n\nI won't keep quiet for him.

As I said, fragments. Glimpses of clarity in a haze of forgotten moments. I feel loneliness. I see a dark, enclosed space. A flash of blinding light ….\n\nNothing very useful or definitive, I'm afraid. Maybe Lyranth can help me make sense of it?

Yes. Whatever I did to the cataclyst—and it was me, I'm certain of that, even if I don't understand how—it also charged the amulet. Like what happens to a lucent when you place it in a dynamus font. Except this energy draws out my memories.

I forced a cultist to tell me about Deadlight. It's a broken realm, apparently destroyed by Mehrunes Dagon eons ago. He gave it to the cult and they built a stronghold there.\n\nA clever hiding place, but the portal to the realm requires a special key.

We will search for more cultists. Here—the locations my scouts found in the Deadlands. I suggest you start in the Sever. Find a key and the portal, and we'll rendezvous before the assault begins. And take the daedrat with you. His smell offends me.

That … we have not yet determined. But I have a plan. You must follow one of the groups of cultists, trail them to the portal, and take their key.\n\nIf the portal key works like the keys to Fargrave, you'll also need the code to operate it.

We were the Kalmur. Good people who kept to ourselves. We weren't raiders or bandits. Just relied on our wits and strength to survive the wilderness of Wrothgar.\n\nThe Kalmur made good mead. Sold it to nearby towns and clans. Damn, I miss that mead.

Rynkyus is a kynreeve of the Bladebearers, a clan of nomadic Dremora who bow to no Prince. Like the rest of his clan, he is fierce, but values honor. He takes pride in his martial skills and the status of his Kyn. \n\nMortals hold no interest for him.

Friends? Hardly. That is a mortal concept. If I understand the idea, it implies affection. Vulnerability. That you would attribute such an affiliation to Dremora is amusing.\n\nBut I have known Rynkyus for a long time. We have never been at odds.

Very good. And I also assume that you heard Rynkyus? Sister Celdina warded this portal not just to prevent my entry, but any other Daedric entity as well.\n\nNeither I, nor Rynkyus, nor Arox will be able to step through this portal.

This one would call it light reading. Witchmothers do not bury their noses in books to acquire their knowledge, after all. But it helps to be knowledgeable of the world. Vanima wants to learn all she can.
Indeed. Do not act so surprised. The possibility certainly exists! But I suppose one such as yourself may not understand the subtle pathways of such a journey.

Did I say I was concerned? Just watch her. Neither we nor the Anchorite know what her memories will eventually reveal. Who she really is. None of us may like the answer.\n\nGo. We will wait here. Try not to destroy anything I may want to examine later.

Learn whatever you can about the cataclyst and Sister Celdina's plans. Then I suppose you will want to kill Celdina, for the sake of Fargrave and Nirn.\n\nJust keep an eye on the Anchorite. The events at Fort Grief have triggered an onset of memories.

You've seen this place. It's all about torture. I think they fused the souls of the emperors into that chunk of metal.\n\nSeems like a fitting punishment for anyone who incurred Mehrunes Dagon's wrath, but we need to free them to talk to them.

We need to ignite the furnace to melt the slag. I spotted two more discharge labrums. If we take that charged lucent and stick it in one, that might get us halfway there. \n\nWe'll need to find a second lucent, though.

So, not just magic. Blood magic. The type that steals memories from its victims. I know it. Utter cruelty.\n\nThe man, Kastav, said it's a Dremnaken. That's new to me. But, I don't care what it calls itself. It'll take the name I gave it.

I don't know. It's just a feeling. I'm getting those kinds of impressions all the time now. Like the dam has cracked and the memories are spilling out.\n\nI wonder what it will be like when the dam finally bursts ….

Nothing that will help us find Sister Celdina or another cataclyst, if that's what you're hoping. It's just a feeling.\n\nLet's keep moving. We should search for a way into the citadel. And let's try not to alert the entire fortress that we're here.

Daughter? You mean the weapon? Why have you brought her here? You cannot let her fall into the hands of Mehrunes Dagon! He reneged on his promise to us. I see no reason to keep our part of the bargain now.

An emperor never relies on a single strategy! We were promised power if we delivered the Ambitions at the appointed time. But Daedric Princes are not to be trusted. So I prepared Mairead as a weapon that could deal with Dagon should the need arise.

I am Leovic, last of the Longhouse Emperors. But who are you? You have the stink of the traitorous Varen about you. That snake! I knew he was coming. I knew I had to take action. Preserve the plan. Keep the secret. Salvage the contingency.

It started with my grandfather, but it was my father who passed the responsibility to me. It was all part of the bargain the Black Drake made with Mehrunes Dagon. We would prepare the Four Ambitions, and in return, our family would rule forever.

No Bladebearer would willingly enter a fortress loyal to Lord Dagon. I am in search of my clan members who disappeared, however. You say you found one of our swords at Burning Gyre Keep?\n\nTell me. What do you know of the Order of the Waking Flame?
That's just … did you have any idea? Well, I guess that makes it easy enough. Now we know where all the Ambitions are.\n\nDid you learn anything else before Sombren blasted them into nonexistence?

That's why the map didn't make sense. It wasn't a map of Tamriel—it's the Deadlands!\n\nAll right, my friend. Let's go see what we can find at the Isle of Joys. Mehrunes Dagon could move against us at any moment!

Wait a moment, I know that name!\n\nRemember Lyranth had me comb through the Longhouse Emperors' documents? That name was listed as one of their hunting retreats. But I couldn't find any other information. Do you know where it is?

Jynd is a Dremora Kynmarcher. She studies relics and devices. Zynoahz is Xivilai. He studies pain. \n\nThey are both subordinates of Valkynaz Nokvroz, who you say you encountered at Burning Gyre Keep.

If Dagon's servants struck down my Kyn to protect this device, I will punish them. But first they must be found.\n\nMy scouts followed rumors to Zynoahz's gaol and Jynd's foundry before they vanished. I will begin there. You may accompany me.

When Dagon's purposes interfere with our own, we gladly fight his minions. Prince Dagon knows this and welcomes it. We have met the valkynaz in battle before.\n\nThis business of mortal secrets and missing Dremora is new, however.

I have no interest in more of their lies. And neither should you. I gave the Longhouse Emperors exactly what they wanted—my power!\n\nBesides, they'll reform in this place eventually. I just couldn't allow them to corrupt the last Ambition.

I'm not sure how else to describe it. When we first arrived in the Deadlands, he insisted he could help me control my powers. That I could practice without fear of hurting anyone.\n\nBut lately he's been different, almost desperate.

You must remember. The book Eveli gave him. Lyranth called it the Mysterium Xarxes.\n\nHe's become obsessed with it. He's sure the answer to controlling our powers hides somewhere among its pages, and he pours over them at every opportunity.
Yes. Can you believe it? They think they can make more of those terrible Incarnates. And faster, too. But have they built this new device or do we still have time to stop them?

Right. A daughter. I suppose she'd be Emperor Leovic's half-sister. Have you heard of anyone coming forward with such a claim? I'm not totally current on happenings in Tamriel, but even in Fargrave we hear rumors.\n\nCome on, we should keep searching.
It is unusual for two high-ranking lieutenants of Valkynaz Nokvroz to suddenly concern themselves with mortals, yes. Nokvroz has nothing but contempt for your kind.\n\nIs that all? I grow impatient.

Kynmarcher Jynd oversees a foundry in the Sever, not far from Wretched Spire. Zynoahz is master of a gaol in the Burn. A place of suffering.\n\nMy scouts reported that both seek information about mortal dealings, each in their own way.

Bladebearers would not allow themselves to be seen by you, so do not waste your time looking for them. Search for information about the mortal device that drew my scouts to this site.\n \nI will look for my Kyn.

You exhaust me with all these questions. Are all mortals so … uncertain?\n\nThere is a scout's camp north of Zynoahz's gaol. I will await you there, but do not dawdle. My patience is extremely limited.

Look for strange devices or documents about mortal machines in Jynd's foundry. I will search for signs of my Bladebearers and question any churls I find.\n\nThere is a ritual site to the north. Meet me there when you finish searching the foundry.
Of course. Valkynaz Nokvroz refuses to accept that the mortal followers of Mehrunes Dagon can succeed where he has failed. A useful insight. What else did you find out?
That would be an inefficient use of my time and abilities.\n\nDo not expect me to guard you, mortal. But if you die, as mortals are prone to do, I shall inform Lyranth. At my convenience.

The Bladebearers are notoriously wary of outsiders. And they distrust Kyn who have more flexible views about honor and proper behavior than they do.\n\nI walk my own path. Some Dremora find that strange. Ask me if I care.

My Kyn learned little that we did not already know. They waited here, hoping to trail a Waking Flame messenger back to Sister Celdina. Since they are not here, it must have worked.\n\nWhich leaves us no closer to finding this mortal device. Or my Kyn.

No, but they confirmed what you told me at Wretched Spire. This device is a danger to all Dremora. How they found out, my Kyn did not say. But they were moving on to Kynmarcher Jynd's foundry.\n\nMeet me there, mortal.

Blind seer? That means nothing to me. Nor can I make sense of the drawing. The runic crux, however. The work seems poorly done. Zynoahz's methods have their limitations.\n\nI found something as well. A hidden message from my Bladebearers.
