Hmm, I guess if you'd found the key to a weapon that could banish Mehrunes Dagon in there, you would have told us about it.

Yeah, I noticed that straight away. Maybe they were part of a set and this one was Emperor Moricar's? And look, it has some weird runes etched into the surface. It might be important. Hold onto it.\n\nWhat about that journal?

Let me see … the egonymic is some sort of name? Says it has the power to banish Mehrunes Dagon! That's huge! But whatever we need to access it isn't here. It's in the Anchorite's vault. I still can't believe she's an Ambition.\n\nWhat about that map?
Really? You explored another vault? Without me? You trying to make me look bad?\n\nWhat did you find? Tell me there was something there that connects to all this. Did you get to search it all?
I think so! It's possible there might not be anything left to find, but that's the only place that map could be pointing to.\n\nIt has to be worth a visit! I'll mark its location on your map.
Because it took everything. My entire clan. My home. My future. All gone due to this … beast! \n\nI don't care if it speaks or reads. Or if it recites poetry—I will see it killed!

The Daedra of Wretched Spire prefer our unbound status. No masters, no summoners. We will stay under the protection this area provides. At any cost.\n\nTephilaz spoke for us with the city's leaders. Treaty negotiations. Influence over city operations.

Very smart that you recognize this. My answer is unsatisfying. Daedra do not want to change anything about Wretched Spire.\n\nThe protection's source remains unclear. The spire? The people? Until we understand more, all must stay the same.

Solitude. The constant disruptions of our existence by mortals anger us. An agreement would ensure we are left alone.\n\nYou should understand—the mortals believe they allow us to stay. They cannot conceive that we allow them to live.
A complicated place, even for a mortal town. It exists as a boil in the Deadlands. An infection that Mehrunes Dagon knows exists but cannot heal.\n\nIt goes unwitnessed. To my benefit.

Hrmph. Did Mehrunes Dagon's arrival on your plane go unnoticed? Was his tearing a city from its roots a common event on Nirn? I have never been there. So I do not know.\n\nA mortal summoned the Prince. He ripped up the spire and flung it here.

Good question. No one can say. I hear many theories. Protected by a different Prince. Saved for later. Dagon thinks it's funny. Nothing certain.\n\nWithout an answer, we must maintain stasis. Nothing can change. Otherwise, Dagon may take notice.

I refuse to have a master. I reject clans. No prince compels my allegiance while I stand within these walls. This arrangement suits me.\n\nWhen Tephilaz began negotiations with the mortals, I offered him protection. As you can see, I failed.

Limited mortal philosophy. Can he force me to kill you if I did not wish? No. Can he embed thoughts in my mind forcing me to worship him? No. Can he bring me to another plane against my will? Again, no.\n\nHe is no master. Only a useful tool.

Didn't you hear the voice? The shouts keep coming from higher up. And they wouldn't put so much protection around this if it didn't go somewhere important.\n\nNo, we're definitely on its trail. Before I leave this tower, I will destroy the Ravener.

Why would Valkynaz Nokvroz take the Anchorite? We saw that she had some power over the cataclyst, but what use of that would Nokvroz have. Unless … could he have succeeded in building his own cataclyst?
The daughter of a Longhouse Emperor and a powerful follower of Mehrunes Dagon? That's a recipe for, quite literally, disaster. But why did Nokvroz take the Anchorite?

The power I summoned to deal with the Riven Cataclyst. I think I can do that again.\n\nThe amulet reacted when I did that before, when I was focusing on the cataclyst. This time, I want to focus on the amulet. I think it will answer me.

By unlocking everything this mask has been keeping from me. \n\nI remember things that aren't here now—a totem in the stands, a starry globe, something in the mural. Watch closely when I concentrate on the amulet. I think you might see them, too.

News has a way of reaching the nexus city. Perhaps someone knows more about the cataclysts. Failing that, I intend to delve into the Anchorite's missing memories. Something about that doesn't sit right.\n\nShe obviously knows more than she recalls.

As much as you trust me. If his Bladebearers come to grief at the hands of the Dagonists or Valkynaz Nokvroz, then you share a common enemy. Remind him of that.\n\nA temporary alliance with the enemy of his enemy? That Rynkyus can understand.

Hmm. He's not on the same level as the writer of the Investigator Vale stories, but his writing isn't bad.\n\nInteresting. Does he know about the egonymic? It doesn't seem like it. He just says he thinks something important is inside that chest.

Then you know. Sister Celdina … is my mother. A consort of Emperor Moricar. Is that why I was hidden away? Raised in secret?\n\nGods. She raised me to destroy the world with an army of Incarnates. To kill so many innocent people!

How clear must I make it, little mortal? He has Calia and the Anchorite and is attempting to force them to go with him. He plans to present them all to the Prince of Destruction.\n\nWe must get to Annihilarch's Summit and stop him!

When I left to retrieve you, Sombren was attempting to wrestle power from each of the other Ambitions and take it for himself. He will turn that power over to Mehrunes Dagon unless we intervene. Quickly, through the portal. There is no time to waste!

It's all coming back. Elegian was ordered to make me a mask to protect me from my powers. But he secretly altered it to hide me from the Dagonists. From my mother.\n\nI have to confront her. If I can remember her now, then she can remember me, too.

No. I want her to see what I've become. The girl she tried to turn into a weapon is the same woman tearing down her wretched cult.\n\nThe power of the mask is broken. I'm Mairead, but I'm also the Anchorite. And I'm through hiding from my past!

For what purpose? Prince Dagon commanded Valkynaz Nokvroz and his subordinates to assist the mortals of his Waking Flame cult. Or so I heard.\n\nIf the mortals devised a tool for the Prince's use, why would the valkynaz need one of his own?

If neither Zynoahz nor Jynd have them, that is the obvious conclusion. Yet I do not know where this mortal Celdina and her Waking Flame cult are hiding. \n\nBah! I dislike the notion, but Lyranth may know where we should look next.

Yes. Kyn are not to be used by mortals. The very thought offends me. I must find signs of my missing clan mates.\n\nMeet me near the gaol of Zynoahz. The area features many deep ravines. Do not fall into one and die.
This reeks of mortal lies and trickery. Mortals do not enslave Kyn.\n\nAnd yet … I found signs left by my Bladebearers. Kyn of many clans gathered here before they were taken somewhere else.

You have to understand—as our totem, Atrozu is the clan. The bond between each Kalmur, our memories of the past … our hopes for the future. All of it melds to form him.\n\nOnce those bonds are gone, he dies. My clan is destroyed forever.

You are not a Bladebearer. You have no means to perceive the secret symbols of my Kyn. We are of Oblivion, made of its substance. It is a simple thing to leave an impression that others of our clan can sense.

Because that is where Sister Celdina is. The cult has ambitious plans for the demiplane. We delayed those plans, but we didn't stop them.\n\nI will find out what I can and then send for you. Assuming you still want to save your world, that is.

We are Bladebearers. All the Kyn of my clan are pact-bound, one to another. The clan-pact unites us in purpose, attunes us to each other. I know my Kyn and can see what they wish me to see. Others cannot.\n\nIt is a connection that can never be broken.

Why do mortals insist on receiving every detail, no matter how insignificant or profound, before they accomplish the task at hand?\n\nApocalyptic. Just what you might imagine where the Daedric Prince of Destruction is concerned.
No idea. That's not important. All that matters is that we pay it back. Destroy the creature for what it's done. Starve it into destruction.
Following the orders of the Dread Lady, of course. She sent me to her hidden lair to retrieve the body of this vile cultist. He deserved even worse for daring to raise a hand against my mistress!

You seek to understand the desires of the Dread Lady? Blasphemy! Ours is not to puzzle out the whys and wherefores of Lyranth the Dremora. Ours is but to do whatever she demands of us.\n\nWhatever. She. Demands.

Right! Exactly! I ask myself that very same question all the time. It even keeps me up at night. But in the end, the answer I come to is always the same.\n\nLyranth is perfect in every way and I can't fathom her reckonings.

Well, not by responding to a notice on a job board, if that's what you're asking.\n\nMy brother and I sought knowledge. A higher purpose. When Lyranth appeared to us and demanded we tell her where to find a sweetroll, we knew we found our calling.

She came seeking a relic in my care, one of the many stolen from my temple by the Knights of the Silver Rose. In exchange for her assistance returning the others to my possession, I will relinquish the relic she seeks to her.

Fortunately, what Lyranth desires is not sacred to Azura, but if that were the price of restoring my temple, it would be worth it.\n\nI'm afraid I have nothing similar to offer you, but I trust gold will make for adequate payment.

There were no official ties between my temple and their order, but I believed we were on good terms. Some of their knights even saw the Mother of the Rose as a patron deity and made offerings on behalf of their order. I don't know what changed.
That's between he and I. Nothing you need to concern yourself with, little mortal. So long as you don't stand in my way of acquiring it this can remain a pleasant reunion.

I seek a relic that was in the priest's possession until the Knights of the Silver Rose robbed it from him, along with the rest. I have agreed to help him recover his lost collection in exchange for that object. Simple. Don't complicate it.

Oh, I don't handle jobs. Think of me more as a scout for the organizations in the city who hire adventurers.\n\nSpeak to Luna Beriel or Vaveli Indavel. They hire mortals and Daedra for dangerous jobs on a daily basis.

Yes, I'm a member of House Hexos. Since you made it to Fargrave, I'll let you in on a little secret. My house gave up its claims in Tamriel centuries ago for a lucrative position in the Celestial Palanquin.\n\nBut even I'm not privy to all our secrets.

Luna Beriel represents the Gleaners, a group of … how do I put this? They're thieves. Oh, not the kind that robs from Fargrave. No, they retrieve items from elsewhere for interested parties in the city. They hire lone adventurers to help with that.

Vaveli Indavel represents the Saraathu Tong, a syndicate of outcast mages who control a lot of trade in the city.\n\nBetween their business dealings and research projects, they require groups to take on jobs too dangerous for single adventurers.
You're a wary one. I consider that a mark in your favor, considering some of the characters I've seen pass through Fargrave's many portals.\n\nAll right, what do you want to know?

Well, you don't get to be the foremost mortal family in a multidimensional Daedric city without being betrayed a few times over the centuries.\n\nWe thrive because my ancestors were cautious, and that's still a family trait to the current day.

Consider it a test. House Hexos serves as a bridge between Fargrave's mortals and Daedra. If you can't keep a minor secret, then we can't recommend you to other organizations. \n\nIt's a little out of line, but that's life on the edge of all reality.

We're a group of mortals and Daedra that do all sorts of things in Fargrave. We liberate items from across the planes for interested parties, explore hidden places, find treasure, vandalize. One thing I can say is that the work never bores me.

Mages who owe fealty to the Great House Hlaalu.\n\nWe transport wares and folks between Fargrave and Nirn. In a trade city like Fargrave, you can see how useful that is. Most merchants prefer working with us over … oh, I don't know. A cult.

Psh. Not everyone in the Tong spends their entire day working on the magics we've already discovered. The Tong supports artisans and scholars alike who tend to have projects suited for different … skill sets. That's where adventurers come in.

We leave them. And I keep Atrozu. I can weaken the orb enough so we can escape. And we'll have to run forever. But at least Atrozu would stay with me.\n\nPlease, help me choose. Save my own life, or do I keep my clan's memory alive?
The cataclyst's runic crux … the focus of its power. These Daedra wanted … to make their own. I didn't tell them everything ….\n\nTell Sister Celdina … I did not reveal the blind seer's final gift ….
I never met him … but he invented the cataclyst. We followed his schematics ….\n\nThe day of Lord Dagon's triumph draws near …. I hoped to see it …. Damn Nokvroz and his torturer ….
Next we need to … think Selveni think …. \n\nWe need to find the statues. There should be an altar in here that's used to locate statues in the Folly.

What? Oh, we'll use it to find the statues of Ordinator Nilera and Grandmother Sovisa. From what I heard in Wretched Spire, the altar is as a sort of dowsing rod. It helps Daedra find the statues they want to sneer at. \n\nThe Folly is very popular.

Sister Celdina's letter explained how to align the segments of the portal key. I shall set it accordingly and open a doorway to whatever realm the cult is using as a base.\n\nYou drink from the cauldron and step through. Then our charade begins.
Weak, but satisfied. I'm imagining the Ravener falling to pieces from hunger. Enraged that it can't find Atrozu.\n\nGo on through. I'll follow behind.
I hope not. The altar probably needs energy to work properly. So, we just place the stones and then pray to Mehrunes Dagon I guess. \n\nYou … may want to stand back after you place the stones.

The Blood Pit is a foul prison that I once oversaw. When I was cursed, I awoke there in this reduced form. Cast down with others who offended Mehrunes Dagon.\n\nThat's where I met Elegian. He was locked in a prison within the prison—the Durance Vile.
Gazmod the Collector's interest in my mask gave Lyranth an idea. Rather than try to remove it, she attempted to suppress its enchantment with her magic.

Master, I am not sure if Elegian knows who Elegian is or why he is there. You'll see. \n\nThe Blood Pit lies northwest of Burning Gyre Keep. I can guide you, but the presence of powerful Daedra not aligned with Prince Dagon will be noticed.

It was as if a curtain in my mind moved in the breeze for a moment. I saw Elegian—a sad old man with eyes that looked on things others don't see. And I remembered his name. \n\nI'm afraid that's all Lyranth could help me recall.

Now, you can't really kill those things, can you? They just keep coming back, whether you want them here or not. But, yes. I hear about everything that happens in Wretched Spire.\n\nOdd. I just spoke with him. Have you learned how he was killed?

No idea. However, Tephilaz seemed occupied with looking into a recent arrival to Wretched Spire. A shady character named Vontan.\n\nIf you're so interested, talk to that scoundrel. He squats over with the other dangerous trash in the Fleapits.

We know it's hunting prey. And it's falling apart without that. So we need to find and destroy that orb. Stop its ability to hunt and starve it to death. Perhaps I can watch it suffer.\n\nLead on. We're not leaving until the Ravener is dead.

I don't know. That vow claims the orb holds the spirits of my clan. I planned to destroy it so the Ravener couldn't hunt. But what happens to them if I do? And Atrozu?\n\nI need time to think. Let's just find the orb. I'll decide then.

Yeah, I thought so, too. But what if something in my past is terrible? What if that's why I can't, or won't, remember?\n\nAll right, let's do this. I think we can use lucent crystals, just like back at the bathhouse in the Shambles.

Lucents can be charged with energy and used to activate all sorts of things. Like opening that door, maybe.\n\nGather some lucents and look for a dynamus font to charge them. There's got to be one around here. Maybe on the balcony up above?
He mentioned spring. Could the elixir be related to a season? And he said something about pouring it on coals. There are braziers right beside him.
Look around for Elegian's elixir. I imagine the overseers would keep it close by in case they needed to talk to him.\n\nSomething in a bottle, related to spring. That's my guess.
Comment

That vile creation! Nokvroz was just here, asking about it. The Riven Cataclyst is my burden, my punishment, my greatest sorrow. I did not realize the purpose my designs would be turned to.\n\nWhy do you seek it?

Yes, I believe you speak true. Destroying it would be good. You can get to the cataclyst by going to Annihilarch's Summit.\n\nNokvroz speaks freely in my presence. He thinks me mad. That I hear nothing. Well, I am mad. And blind. But I'm not deaf.

You're right. I'm the final Kalmur. If I throw away my life, then all this was for nothing. Without the orb, the Ravener never completes its hunt. Let it starve.\n\nLet's do this together. I'll weaken the orb's power while you smash it.

I know Annihilarch's Summit. A high peak in the Sever, inhospitable to mortals. And Dremora, for that matter. Few go there. It would be a perfect place to hide the Riven Cataclyst.\n\nBut what's wrong with the Anchorite? Did Elegian recognize her?

Did he now? The cataclyst and the mask? This Elegian is clever, indeed. I am more determined than ever to examine the Riven Cataclyst in detail.\n\nWe must also keep the Waking Flame from misusing it, of course.
I'm not sure. Wouldn't a place like this leave scars you couldn't forget?

I don't know. And what does it matter? However we met, I just hope Elegian can tell me who I was before this mask was adhered to my face. \n\nIt would also be nice if he can tell us something useful about the Riven Cataclyst.

The seneschal did mention observing the knights training with several Daedric artifacts on one occasion before being barred from entering the fortress. They described the stonework quaking at the footfalls of one such knight clad in heavy boots.

He's confident my complaints to the Spire Council will amount to nothing. If he's to be believed, the Dread Cellar is something they're well aware of, if not responsible for themselves. Martus won't face justice for what he's done at the Battlespire.
Then I better remember what it is and how to use it, right?\n\nPut the relic on the table over there. Let me get a better look at it. Maybe something will come to me.

That seems unlikely. If Celdina already had such an army, she would deploy it at once. Remember, she is eager to conquer Fargrave and earn Prince Dagon's favor.\n\nStill, I do not think we have much time before that changes.

Possibly. But each time we delay the Waking Flame, we make it less likely that Elegian's mad vision becomes a reality.\n\nAlthough it might have been for the best if you had … removed … Elegian while you were in the Blood Pit.

Standing in the streets of Fargrave—I think I must have stepped through a portal. I stood there for a long time, trying to remember why I was there. \n\nI had a few pieces of gold in my pouch. Eventually I got hungry and bought a meal.
Так.

No. Nokvroz is no mage. He must have found some relic or forgotten curse to transform me into this daedrat body. And he must have caught me off-guard. Otherwise, I would have destroyed him the moment he struck at me.

I ran out of gold. I found myself hungry and homeless, sleeping in deserted buildings. At some point I wandered into the Shambles and was set upon by a street gang—the Errants.\n\nThat's when I discovered I knew how to fight.

Oh. You assumed I would provide more detail. You should have phrased your query differently. \n\nYes, I have been to the area. I found it uninviting. Building a secret retreat there would be difficult. I suppose we shall see.

You dare insinuate—! The master meant no offense. They're just a stupid mortal.\n\nNokvroz never dared display a hint of disloyalty, let alone challenge me for my place as Prince Dagon's champion. I would have crushed him into a paste. Can we go now?

Or—or we could free both, but then I'd be trapped. If I was better at magic, or even understood what Almalexia's Mother Stones did then ….\n\nBut no. There is no way to free both spirits and ensure my escape. I'm a failure.

If he could do it, I don't see why not. I just need to get a handle on these powers I suddenly have.\n\nI want to be careful, too. Sombren gave in to the dark part inside him. The part that belongs to Mehrunes Dagon. I don't want that to happen to me.
Dead? Another murder? And this time a mortal ….\n\nSo, the trail ends here.

Waking Flame? The mortal followers of Mehrunes Dagon? Here? Could they seek to disrupt our protections?\n\nWe must speak to Faven. He needs to know about this threat. And then we must purge the cult before they endanger our sanctity.

Yes. They refer to a location. A kind of encrypted map. But also a key. The Waking Flame's nearby camp. Indicates the cultists are about to make their move. I will try to rally the town, but I need you to go to the camp. Do what you can to stop them.

The inscriptions describe an entrance to the southwest. It may be hidden. Well-guarded. But you seem capable.\n\nFind what you can that explains these events. Do your best to hinder the cult. I will seek to rally the town's residents—all of them.

They're no less dangerous than they ever were, I don't have the power to destroy such things. The miasma of Daedric energy will accumulate again if these objects remain together, but this should stop the damage until they can be dealt with.

Most of Oblivion feasts on our mortal follies and darker natures. Its influence is often insidious. Convictions might spare us from worldly temptations, but they are not enough to keep power like this at bay.\n\nWe can't fight gods by will alone.

The order appears to have closed themselves off for a long time now. Given the hostility they demonstrated, I imagine no one will come to pay them a visit anytime soon. That may give me some time to relocate everything before the bastion is looted.

No, but I have no use for it. I'd forgotten I even had it until Lyranth asked about it. She at least seems to have some idea what it's for. I can't say if that's a good thing, but it's the price I paid to restore Azura's temple.
Please. I am nothing like my insipid older brother. Nothing at all.\n\nI am the Dread Lady's true prophet. Her voice resounding in the mortal realm. Her herald on the plane of Nirn.

Yes, I am aware of your relationship with my mistress. It may not be as intimate as mine, but she does seem to have a certain … fondness for you.\n\nStill, we must not use her name so casually. Enemies abound and mortals become skittish so easily.

That she is. Although gender isn't what you imagine when it comes to classifying Daedric entities.\n\nIt took a lot of effort to summon her to this plane, just to provide you with convenient transportation. My mistress insisted, however. So I complied.

My dimwitted brother claims to be many things. The Dread Lady and I allow him his delusions. Makes it easier to get him to accomplish the few tasks that aren't beyond his limited skill set.\n\nYou should feel honored that this time my mistress sent me.

Speaking the words of some higher power is the standard definition of a prophet. And there is no higher power than my mistress, no matter what the other temples or shrines may tell you.\n\nI do whatever the Dread Lady asks and am honored to do so.

The journal claims each hunt risks the Ravener's essence. He thought it looked weaker. This could be the answer—we starve it! Smash the orb. Stop it from finding prey. Kastav mentioned a tower to the north. And Atrozu has the trail again. Let's go.
Comment

In addition to the harsh conditions and the destructive wind? I expect you will face Daedra loyal to Valkynaz Nokvroz. Perhaps mortals devoted to the Dagon cult. Surely neither Nokvroz nor Sister Celdina would leave the Riven Cataclyst unguarded.

Given what we've seen of their interactions thus far, I'd say neither of them tells the other any more than necessary. Perhaps we can use that at some point. Widen the rift that already exists between them.\n\nNow hurry. We will see you at the summit.

The dangers of the Deadlands are numerous, mortal. Have you not determined that by now?\n\nValkynaz Nokvroz will have his minions out in force. He may have been ordered to assist Sister Celdina, but he will look for every opportunity to displace her.

Freshly spilled, master. A mortal died here, not long ago. We should look around and see what tale this place can tell us about those who ascend to the summit.\n\nTravelers can be careless. Especially when they are being killed.
Dead mortals pay little attention to where they leave their bodies or the things they carry. Very untidy. Selfish of them, really.\n\nDaedra avoid that by simply not dying. Usually.

A group of Dagonists known as the Order of the Waking Flame has been interfering in my mistress's activities of late. They are of no real concern to her, but I don't want to attract their attention.\n\nI suggest you take similar precautions.
Sweet Daffodil would never harm a fleshfly, let alone a favored curiosity of the Dread Lady.\n\nBut just to be on the safe side, I suggest not getting too close to her fiery bits.

Why would it? They were allies mere moments ago. I doubt he expects trouble from a group of mortals he despises.\n\nIt's possible the key already contains the coordinates to enter the fortress. I assume Sister Celdina visited the place many times.

It is one of the seven hundred and seventy-seven impregnable citadels that house Mehrunes Dagon's legions. Nokvroz commands the garrison, protected by a cabal of Dremora blood adepts.\n\nThat's why we need Arox once we get inside.

You think this one didn't ask her the same thing when Pibiha told her where she was going? Pibiha scoffed. Said that she didn't have anything to fear or gain from Merrunz. \n\nThen she called the Fire-Cat a kitten and laughed. She laughed!
Others call him Mehrunes Dagon, Khajiit know him as Merrunz, the kitten. He is … not feared by many Khajiit. This one is beginning to wonder if that is a mistake.
Zahsbi sees only good things in the future. Bright Moons ahead for you, my friend.
Your path is clouded and rocky, this one cannot tell what lies in store. \n\nIt may be wise not to eat fish until the future clears.
I cannot say what it was I saw, but know that it was under a Dark Moon. You are ill-fated, my friend. Keep a sharp eye out for danger.\n\nDo not be angry. Zahsbi does not control what he sees.
Tufeh should go back to Fargrave, as soon as she can. She didn't tell her family where she was going when Pibiha disappeared. They must be so worried.
Soon, you will visit a dark place of lava and fire. Keep your weapons and your wits sharp.\n\nDo not ask Zahsbi for more information. He cannot say.

I've never taken on a Daedric Prince before, so I can't say for sure. But I'd put my gold on us. If anyone can find a way to stop Mehrunes Dagon, it's you. You'll see this through.\n\nAnd I'll be right by your side when we face Sombren.
You, too? Ardent Hope is Valkynaz Nokvroz's seat of power, and it now appears that he is supreme among Mehrunes Dagon's vassals. \n\nI do not see why you all insist on making him your enemy.

Hmm. This key would allow me to open a portal directly into the fortress, which might give you a chance—no matter how slim. Very well.\n\nThere's an old portal dais in the Burn, south of Ardent Hope. Meet me there and I will attune your key.

And if he succeeds, I would be foolish to defy the new regime. Still, it would be irksome to live under the Prince of Destruction's authority. At least you have a slightly better idea than a frontal assault. The Bladebearers are fools to consider it.

I will open a portal to get us inside the walls of the city as Arox suggests. After that, our allies deal with the bulk of Solace's defenses while we try to intercept Sombren before he turns over his power to Mehrunes Dagon.
Optimism will serve us better than pessimism in this, mortal. But the sooner we begin the better.\n\nTake a moment to speak with your allies, if you want. Then let me know when you are ready.
Not at all, but the attempt will be glorious!\n\nI mean, of course, master. It will be difficult, but I will be there to assist you. Right up until the very end.

Great! It'll be easy. We'll just sneak right in and pop Sombren and Mehrunes Dagon right on the nose! It's just like that time when Investigator Vale … huh.\n\nYou know, I don't think Investigator Vale ever dealt with a Daedric Prince.

I don't know. It resembled a type of Daedra native to the Deadlands, but whatever this diabolical machine did to it made it unlike any Daedra I've ever seen.\n\nI have to wonder if it turned out as intended given the condition of this contraption now.

That will be up to the mages of the Spire Council. We don't have the resources to guard this place from further incursions. They may devise a means of cleansing the lingering energies here, or simply decide to blast it into dust. It won't be missed.

That will be up to her. I don't harbor any ill will toward her—or you—for any feelings you may have about my past. I don't expect either of you to understand. It's not something you can truly weigh against your conscience until you experience it.

Disappear for awhile. I'm sure the Spire won't appreciate my desertion, but I can't imagine they'll spend much effort looking for me. After that, find a cause worth fighting for. Something that will allow me to do real good.
I'm not the one he needs forgiveness from. If the Divines see fit to show him mercy, that's their prerogative. I intend to forget him.

You try to interpret Daedric actions through mortal understanding. I have seen the mortals of Wretched Spire do the same thing. It leads to all sorts of trouble.\n\nNokvroz will seek to discredit and undermine Celdina, even as he works to assist her.
Then the coward could have done it himself! \n\nIf he wanted to repent, he didn't have to wait for me to dirty my hands. Martus tainted everything he touched.

I always fought for the Daedra. They just want a home. They belong here as much as we do.\n\nThat group—they said they would help. Mortals on the side of Daedra. They said that if I poisoned Tephilaz, it would spur the Daedra to action.
I … I know. I've done horrible things. How do I even begin to atone?\n\nBut I'll go. No more running.

I am a member of the Witchmother coven. We venerate the Mistress of Shadows, Nocturnal, and do her bidding. \n\nBut who we are should be of no concern to you. I enlisted your aid to stop a force that threatens all of Nirn. Allegiances matter little.

Foolish question. Of course I do! I want a small sliver of its strength. I don't relish the idea of perishing along with the rest of Tamriel if it gets the chance to unleash that kind of power upon us. I am merely taking advantage of an opportunity.

Indeed, child. \n\nWhile we would not want to draw the Crowborne Horror here directly, using the effigy will allow me to control a small area of Evergloam for our purposes. Once the beast is lured in, it will have nowhere to turn.
Pibiha never gave into sorrow and neither will Tufeh.\n\nDon't worry, just because Tufeh is cautious doesn't mean that this one has not had her own adventures. She'll manage.

This one came to the Burn through the Plaza of Portals in Fargrave. With luck, she'll find the portal here still open when she retraces her steps. \n\nIt's no use solving a problem that may not exist. So, this one won't worry just yet.

For you, sweet mortal? Always. Let Lyranth and the others worry about these affairs and come back to Fargrave with me. Your life is short enough. Why risk it on this fool's errand?\n\nI can promise that our association would be mutually … satisfying.

Fighting for their lives, scattered to the far corners of this fortress, no doubt. You do not possibly have time to find them all. Mehrunes Dagon seeks to distract you from reaching Sombren. Do not lose sight of that goal. \n\nGood luck, little mortal.

What else would you call the Bladebearers' action? While they draw the attention of Nokvroz's forces, you must move quickly. You have until the last Bladebearer falls. Use that time wisely.\n\nAnd I do hope you survive. For aesthetics, if nothing else.

Oh, I was only having a bit of fun. You are so deliciously stoic. And correct, I must admit. Mehrunes Dagon has long coveted Fargrave's doors to the many realms. Do not let Nokvroz use our fair Anchorite to accomplish that.\n\nRemember, distraction.

Your needs are irrelevant and no longer my concern. Find your way through the fog. Perhaps you can gather your allies along the way.\n\nRemember, you must defeat Sombren and employ the egonymic against Mehrunes Dagon before he merges the worlds.

Oh, not in any romantic or mortal interpretation of the word. Not even in the way a child is fond of a puppy or kitten. Dremora aren't like us. You must have realized that by now. But my mistress finds you … interesting. Yes, that's the word.

If that portal leads to wherever the cataclyst waits, then Elegian spoke true. We will not know until we use it, however.\n\nI sense that the portal connects to Nirn. Moreover, it contains a ward meant specifically for me. I dare not step through.

Perhaps, but it would take time we do not have.\n\nYou must serve as my eyes, little mortal. Find the cataclyst. Examine it. Remember everything you see. Then do whatever you feel is necessary. Take the Anchorite. I'll send Rynkyus through shortly.

Why …? Do you know how I arrived in the Deadlands? Why I'm likely forced to live out my days surrounded by blight and storm? Are you so ignorant of the very place where you stand?\n\nMehrunes fetching Dagon flung me here with half the city!

Peace, feh. Daedra are single-minded creatures. They only strive for what their essence tells them to seek. They don't want peace with us. They only see a truce as a means to an end.\n\nWhat that end is remains mysterious. So they shall have no treaty.

Faven of House Indoril. Though, I don't know if that matters so much any more. I lead this castoff of a town.\n\nThe task was much easier when we arrived. We were mostly Dunmer. They knew their place. Now it's an assortment of adrift refuse.
I came with the spire. Crashed down after being ripped from my beloved Mournhold and flung into Oblivion.\n\nNever really understood how I, or any of us, survived, but I stopped thinking about it.

Tarvyn, yes. He introduced Tephilaz to me. A good son, but one who needs to learn his history.\n\nHe was born here and never saw Mournhold. He doesn't understand what the Daedra truly are. I hope that he never needs to.

Let me see. \n\nThis key is not familiar to me, but it might prove useful. A way into the Waking Flame lair, perhaps? Careless of them to let some weakling walk about with it. Or for Valkynaz Nokvroz to leave it behind. Unless he had no need of it.

We saw that Nokvroz directed his underlings, Jynd and Zynoahz, to question Waking Flame cultists about the cataclyst device. I believe this cultist met the same fate.\n\nBut seizing a captive on Sister Celdina's doorstep? Nokvroz grows bold.
As you wish, master. The day will come when I fall upon your enemies like a burning thunderbolt and lay a hundred blackened skulls at your feet!\n\nLet us see if the Bladebearer sneers at Arox then!

Part of the training to become a wise woman involves learning to hear Atrozu's voice. His thoughts come to me as images or moods. \n\nAll very mystical and weird. But he kept me company after everyone died, so I'm grateful.

I'll make my way back to Mournhold. I'll only tell everyone as much as you want me to, of course!\n\nSotha Sil, I'm honestly still a little scared about how things turned out here. But I know I can push through that, thanks to you.

I am guessing, but a guess is all I have. I believe that the twisted rod holds the key to breaking Arox's curse. The magic inside it, it's Arox's true form.\n\nIf I break the rod, Arox would be restored to his former glory—for a time.

If we want to save the Bladebearers and the Anchorite, yes. I will also need to stay behind. I can stave off the curse, but even that won't allow him to retain his true form for long. Take the rod and decide quickly, mortal. As I said, time is short.

Rynkyus and his Bladebearers will assault the front gate, drawing the attention of Valkynaz Nokvroz's forces. Meanwhile, we will infiltrate using the attuned portal key and attempt to remain undetected as we search the fortress for the Anchorite.

Let's just say I have an idea about how we may utilize it if worse comes to worse.\n\nJust keep Arox close. His knowledge of the fortress is essential if we're to make our way through the interior undetected.

We must prevent Nokvroz from using her blood to fuel his device. I admit I want to examine his so-called Perfected Cataclyst. This entire notion of changing the unchangeable … intrigues me. But I have no desire to face another of those Incarnates.

Hate is too weak a word for what I feel, master! I do not begrudge him for chafing under my rule. That is the Deadlands' way. It is natural to challenge those above you.\n\nBut Nokvroz chose the path of cowardice. He must answer for that.

I … I do not know. I would certainly be more worthy than Nokvroz. But Mehrunes Dagon allowed that worm to replace me through trickery and deceit. I gave Lord Dagon my unstinting loyalty, but where was his loyalty to me?\n\nBah! We should go, master.

Did Nokvroz face me in open battle? Did he strike me down with his own strength and fervor? No! He resorted to a trickster's curse.\n\nHis actions revealed his fear, not his power. He has not earned his place at the head of Lord Dagon's armies.

A mortal worry. We are Dremora. We do not die—we return. And Bladebearers do not fear pain. We exist for battle and glory.\n\nValkynaz Nokvroz has risen high among the Kyn, but we will prove stronger. It is our way.

The paths of Oblivion are dark and strange, mortal. None can say how long his reformation might take. But even if Nokvroz returns immediately, he will bear the dishonor of defeat. Who would serve a valkynaz too weak to defend his own fortress?

The stronger will fight for his position. The weaker will await the rise of a new leader.\n\nNokvroz commands obedience with his strength alone. None are proud to serve him. They know he won his place by making a staircase from his followers.

Because this one followed her. \n\nShe hoped to convince her flame-fried sister not to do anything stupid, but the cult moved quickly. Pibiha was shoved through a portal out of Fargrave and there wasn't time to think. Tufeh had to jump through too.

Quite the opposite. The blade carries a unique enchantment I've never encountered before. It paralyzed me. Gave them the time they needed to portal in others and ransack the place.\n\nQuickly, check my coffer. Make sure the velvet pouch is still safe.

The Order of the Waking Flame, to be precise. Followers of Mehrunes Dagon, the Daedric Prince of Destruction.\n\nTwo of the cultists followed me into the portal and surprised me. I wounded one, but the other incapacitated me with that enchanted blade.

As a matter of fact, it does. The velvet pouch contains the relic I acquired for services rendered.\n\nNow go, make sure the relic remains safe in its pouch. The Dagonists also sought it, so that's reason enough to want to keep it out of their hands.

Dremora are difficult to kill, and that's doubly true where I'm concerned. Besides, we don't actually die. Not as mortals do. Our essence simply returns to Oblivion and we are reconstituted. How long that takes varies.\n\nThe blade was more prudent.

Perhaps, but I have yet to establish a firm link between these activities and those related to the Longhouse Emperor's plots.\n\nRegardless, I have every indication that Dagon seeks to unleash destruction upon this plane of existence.

Mehrunes Dagon is a powerful Daedric Prince, ruler of the Deadlands and the so-called god of disaster and revolution. His mortal followers call themselves the Order of the Waking Flame. They are his devoted servants here on Nirn.

The Dagonists went to great lengths to forge a blade capable of trapping a Dremora inside its incapacitated body. Instead of simply slaying this form and risking I would return too quickly, they chose to entrap me.

I need to study the magic to be sure, but I don't think so. An enchantment of that magnitude is complex and requires a multitude of resources. I doubt they have other such blades just lying around and ready to use.\n\nI will be more cautious, however.

First thought? Someone in town is secretly a member of this Order of the Waking Flame. And possibly someone who Tephilaz was in contact with. Otherwise, they would not have gotten close enough to administer the poison.
Not yet, but in time. These type of runes, not my specialty. Also, I am cut off from a great deal of knowledge.\n\nThe price of freedom.

We tracked our first group of missing Bladebearers to Kynmarcher Jynd's foundry. When Nokvroz gave our Kyn to the Waking Flame mortals, we followed them to Annihilarch's Summit. That's where Nokvroz's blood adepts captured us.

Perhaps, but I think it unlikely. Faven protects the town. Claims it as his domain. Would never allow outsiders to take over. The mortal holds too much pride.\n\nAnd he hates Mehrunes Dagon. No sense to it.

Bother? You mean, anger? Upset? These aren't experiences that I have. My … moods are set. Fixed. I am who I am. Who I will always be.\n\nEven my search for freedom from mastery is eternal. Living here—just a temporary success.

I heard cultists talking. Apparently early versions of the cataclyst used a single Daedra and transformed them into some sort of living disaster. But this version, the Riven Cataclyst. It drains the essence from many Daedra, leaving nothing behind.

Not enough, unfortunately. He appeared recently, skulking around, trying to avoid being seen by decent people. He lives over in the Fleapits, where we relegate those who won't stay civil.\n\nI should really clear out the Fleapits.

Again, not death. Displacement? The proper word for their unique situation eludes me.\n\nTo answer your inquiry, no I did not see what occurred. I was actually headed into the Daedric district to meet with Tephilaz when I stumbled on the scene.

Tephilaz and I are friendly. As much as any Dremora has friends. I helped him gain the trust of the city council to begin treaty discussions.\n\nHe just met with my father, Faven, leader of the council. I wanted to know how the negotiations went.

Tell you what, you seem like a trustworthy friend. The secret is that my minstrels hail from places more exotic than anywhere on Nirn. You can't court these extraordinary performers with anything but the most exquisite treats and outstanding wine!

Really? All I know is that she's a Dremora who has an interest in the Dagon cult known as the Order of the Waking Flame.\n\nThis is where we were supposed to meet, but all I saw when I got here was that cultist and the votive rune he was casting.

What, poor Joset? She's one of my favorite regulars. At least she was, before the votives affected her. First she became belligerent. Then extremely melancholy. Now she's practically mindless.\n\nBut tell me, darling, what brings you to Madam Whim's?

The Anchorite promises to get me away from the cult in exchange for information. I hold up my end of the bargain and what do I get? Another fool seeking knowledge from poor Tilgo.\n\nThis is the last time, you hear? Make sure the Anchorite knows that.

Madam Whim didn't charge you, I hope. She usually lets you sample her wares for free the first time. After that it gets expensive.\n\nThe Shambles is a big place, but now we know more than we did when we started. Did you also make contact with Tilgo?

Because it's a big building, and big buildings always have multiple exits and entrances. Besides, we didn't come all this way to be defeated by a magical seal on a bathhouse door.\n\nLet's search the courtyard and find another way to get inside.

I spotted a lucent among the debris in this hall. It's a Daedric crystal that can absorb and store the background energy that pulses through all the realms of Oblivion.\n\nWe'll need that to get started.

The Anchorite? An unusual appellation, even for a mortal. \n\nAs for my absence, I heard a cultist mention that Sister Celdina had arrived at their headquarters in the Shambles. I could not let the opportunity to catch up with her slip away.

Yes, but she fled in haste. That means she probably left something behind. Let's search this bathhouse.\n\nBring me whatever you find. Sister Celdina's abandoned paraphernalia may be of use to me. And it may tell you more about the threat to Nirn.

As the name implies, I trade in eccentricities and capriciousness. I buy and sell as impulse dictates. My establishment carries indulgences from across Oblivion.\n\nAnd information, of course. Along with food, drinks, and an amenity for every appetite.

If we were talking about the Deadlands, no. But the Shambles is a different story. That section of Fargrave can't have too many places hot enough to make a devastator uncomfortable. The Anchorite will figure it out.

The Shambles can be a dangerous place, but it's also where the majority of Fargrave's mortals live.\n\nWarrens and dark alleys fill the area. There are three main paths through the Shambles. We can take any of them to reach the bathhouse.

Right here. Simply use the pendant and follow the trail of the residual magic. Then use it again once the trail turns cold. We must retrieve the relic they stole from me.\n\nI shall pursue my own investigation and meet you once we locate the cultists.

Hmm. Nor can I. And while your literacy may be in question, mine certainly is not.\n\nThis is no language, mortal or Daedric. It is written in code. One used by the Dagonists for their more guarded correspondence.

No. And neither could any lowly recruit we captured off the streets and tortured for information. This code is reserved for the order's elite.\n\nWe'll need to find someone who can decipher it. I'm sure Fargrave must have someone with those skills.
It invokes Madam Whim. Wants what belongs to Gazmod and Gazmod alone. It is presumptuous.\n\nLeave our gaze. Gazmod no longer wants to look upon it.
Do we have a choice? Look, I can take care of myself. Just find the Arox and get back here as quick as you can. I'll do my best to keep the Collector's attention focused on me and my mask.

There is more to the Anchorite than meets the eye. She survived the hazards of Fargrave before we arrived. I suspect she will continue to do so long after we have departed.\n\nLet us not waste the opportunity she has afforded us. Step inside.

While I have many, many talents, deciphering written codes concocted by fanatical mortals is not among them. Are you sure I can't interest you in something a little more … luscious? No? Pity.\n\nVery well. I may know someone who can help you.

We know of each other. Perhaps our paths have crossed over the millennia. Perhaps not. Whim has changed her name and appearance multiple times. Or so I've heard. I have no doubt she will do so again … when Fargrave no longer amuses her.

I've only just met her and I can already tell that Lyranth thinks very highly of herself. That's not an uncommon trait among the greater Daedra. And when two or more prominent Daedra come together, their every action becomes a battle for supremacy.

Oh, don't concern yourself with that, dearest one. I never ask for more than a client can afford. There's no profit in that.\n\nWhen you have time, come back and let Madam Whim show you some of the wares that have made her the talk of Oblivion.

Some things are private. Personal. You can't just walk up and demand I tell you my deepest, darkest secrets.\n\nAh, sorry. I agreed to talk about my name, my mask, everything. After you proved yourself. And you've certainly done that.

Where else was I to go? I assumed I awoke in Fargrave for a reason. I stayed to find that reason. And to see if whoever left me here would one day return.\n\nRegardless, the city and its people quickly captured my heart. Especially the mortals.

Certainly not! But if we do not do this, the Crowborne Horror's destruction will be inevitable. This path may pose some risk, but it's better than the alternative.\n\nIt must be drawn close enough to be accosted.

Question not this pitiable form, mortal. For within it beats the heart of the Terror of the Deadlands, the Sunderer of the Seven Skies, and the Warrior of the Floating Wastes! I am Arox the Mutilator!\n\nAnd, yes. I currently occupy this daedrat body.

The place isn't exactly a secret. At least not to those of us who wander the many realms of Oblivion. The reputation of the keep's warriors is such that other Princes often hire them out to accomplish impossible missions.

You've been wandering out here and you haven't run into them yet? They're everywhere!\n\nThe Waking Flame is Merrunz' newest mortal cult. They appeared in Fargrave a short while ago and already have a surprising amount of members.
That … is something Tufeh does not know. But since they follow Merrunz, this one is sure that whatever those sand-eating beetle feeders are up to, it will bring pain and suffering to the rest of us.

It might be a trick of the heat, but Tufeh thinks she sees the faces of prisoners on the cultists who walk out. \n\nIf this one's eyesight is true, then what goes on in the Reformatory makes her feel like beetles are crawling through her fur.
Word of this place came to Fargrave, our home, from the mouths of merchants. They say it's a maze where those the Waking Flame finds unworthy are left to rot. \n\nPibiha used to laugh about that.
No. None of the merchants know what happens inside. Anyone taken inside isn't seen again. \n\nAll Tufeh knows is that prisoners disappear inside the Reformatory and she only sees cultists leave.

Because this one's sister, despite her lack of self-preservation, is a fairly logical person. She said that no cult or Daedra would let their prisoners be wasted like that. They'd be sacrificed at the very least. \n\nNow the cult has Pibiha.
You don't know? It is Nocturnal's holy day, the 3rd of Hearth Fire. It is the day we are able to summon her to Nirn. \n\nPerhaps something else was brought along with the Night Mistress.

You ask too many questions! These braziers are blessed by Nocturnal, ruler of the Evergloam. The flames are fueled by her power. So, once you thrust the effigy into the fire, it will absorb the energy of the Evergloam that writhes within.\n\nSimple.

They are manifestations of the Evergloam. As the Crowborne Horror draws ever near, its energy builds in the form of dark feathers that grow upon creatures like an infection. \n\nThese feathers won't harm you, however. In case you have any reservations.
You don't know? \n\nIt is Nocturnal's realm. A place of shadows and darkness. It is inhabited by many, but ruled by only one.

And do not forget that Nirn is her ultimate target, little mortal. She plans to use Fargrave to sacrifice your realm to Dagon.\n\nBut Celdina figured out a way to change the very nature of a Daedra, truly change it—that bears further investigation.

Yeah, I heard. I may not remember who I am or where I came from, but I found a purpose in Fargrave. That's what keeps me going. Protecting the city and its people.\n\nI won't rest until we stop Sister Celdina and the Order of the Waking Flame.

This will be nothing compared to her trial within the Battlespire to attain the rank of Battlemage. She will be expected to survive traversing the planes of Oblivion. Killing the invading Daedra here is the perfect practice.

She's smart and ruthless. A powerful combination in a mortal. She commands the Dagonists here in Fargrave and oversaw the creation of the cataclyst. With that device, she plans to create an army of living disasters to unleash upon Nirn.

I hope your confidence is merited, for all our sakes. Martus is a veteran battlemage, and I'm far from helpless. But even with your help, storming this prison seems like a suicide mission.\n\nIf you decide at any point to turn back, I'll support you.

Has the Battlespire been forgotten already? There really won't be anything left of the Empire by the time the Three Banners War ends. We are, or were, the elite war mages of the Imperial Legions. I didn't join for the glory, but that's disappointing.

The fortress of all fortresses. Where the strongest mages in the Empire reside and train. It intersects with several planes of Oblivion, or so I'm told. My initiation trial will send me on a journey through them. If I survive, I'll be inducted.

Many don't. Which is why few of us ever get to attempt the trial. I'll have to prove myself capable many times over before I'm given my opportunity. If I can't pass the trial by the time I can take it, I didn't adequately prepare.

I know it's the power of the Empire that kept the provinces from this all-out war. The Battlespire, the Legions, all of it held Tamriel together. The Three Banners are just going to continue killing each other until that kind of might returns.

You could call it a hunch. I would call it experience. Daedra don't just arrive on the mortal realm by coincidence and they aren't here to just live off the land. They are doing this for a greater purpose. We just need to discover what and thwart it.

Is protecting Tamriel not a worthy enough interest?\n\nAh, too clever to believe that, are we? Fine. We plan to draw power from the Crowborne Horror once you lure it into the pocket realm. It is nothing that concerns you, child.

I have been waiting for so long to hear an adventurer say that! It's awful that those Daedra couldn't deliver the goods themselves, but I am looking forward to the number of favors I'll be able to secure with this haul.

Oh yes, what else would we do with it? Fargrave has a complicated financial system. Favors are often worth more than currency. And they last longer than the passing currency fads do. \n\nYou want to go far here? Learn how to trade in favors.
I'll go on with the mission, because those are my orders. Trusting him has nothing to do with it. I'm just not going to assume my welfare is his concern and neither should you.

An Elder Councilor's aid secretly spying on their correspondence. A guildmaster propping up a puppet governor. A Dibellan high priest who covertly commanded a cult of Mephala. A vampire who held an entire island in her thrall. Just to name a few.

I regret that I lacked the resolve for it. Had I still been an interrogator here, I might have uncovered something that would have prevented all this senseless slaughter. Or maybe I just would have become like Cyronin. Who's to know?

I extracted knowledge from them. Coercing cooperation however I could. Sometimes subterfuge was enough, usually it was not. Our methods were better left to the imagination. It left scars on them and I both. Eventually, I sought reassignment.

She can say whatever she likes in our debriefing. It will be a rude awakening for her though. Neither my history nor that of this prison is a mystery to our superiors. I was chosen for this mission for my knowledge and discretion. Sadly, she was not.
No, he doesn't. But that won't stop me from saying what needs to be said. Unless he thinks he can keep me quiet. And you too.\n\nIf you watch my back down here, I'll watch yours.

Never heard of him, but I do not trust him. I will watch him closely, master. Sniff out his intentions. I have a keen sense of smell in this otherwise pathetic form!\n\nI'd prefer to be huge and powerful again, of course, but this form has some uses.

Wonderful! \n\nWhen my shipment of goods got waylaid, I wasn't sure what I'd do. Daedra in Fargrave get a mite tetchy about selling their goods to mortals. If Vaveli couldn't find a willing adventurer, I was going to have to ask the Gleaners to help.

I've never gone up against the beast itself, but the Xivilai who have say not to let it touch you. That might've been a joke. \n\nBest advice I can think of? Don't underestimate this thing. It's a fearsome fetcher.

She did, did she? All true, but I hate to brag. She's an unusual mortal, though, isn't she? Our darling of the alleys. And clever. She sent you so as not to increase her tab at the House of Whims.\n\nAs a new customer, your first transaction is free.

Ah, two topics on the lips of many a Fargravian. The Dagonists are mortal rabble with a fetish for destruction. The votive runes are prayers to their Prince made manifest, spells that seem to affect only mortals. Like poor Joset here.

They don't tell lowly initiates all the details of their master plan, but I hear things. Sister Celdina wants to take over Fargrave. Make it an offering to Mehrunes Dagon. The votive runes play a part in that, but I don't know exactly how.

Sister Celdina leads the Fargrave cell. She has a grand vision for the Waking Flame. It starts with Fargrave, but it doesn't end there. She wants control of the portals. With them, she can hand Lord Dagon all of Oblivion. Even Nirn would be in reach.

The Deadlands belong to Mehrunes Dagon, but places exist where his minions rarely go. Wretched Spire stands as a refuge of sorts, a settlement where Dremora without clans and escaped mortal slaves can eke out a meager existence.\n\nHence the name.

As I said, the Bladebearers are nomads who do not pledge allegiance to Dagon. As such, they roost in places that aren't under the Prince's direct control. Wretched Spire is one such location.\n\nRynkyus's clan can usually be found there this cycle.

Damn it! No one is going to conquer Fargrave if I have any say in the matter! I suppose we need to investigate the old bathhouse. If we find Sister Celdina, maybe we'll find Lyranth, too.\n\nLet's meet in the Shambles. We can discuss our options there.

Mostly helping out around Leyawiin. And I did a couple of small tasks for Governor Keshu. Rounding up a few stray cultists, that sort of thing. Otherwise, it's been pretty quiet.\n\nUntil Lyranth contacted me, that is.
Excellent! I've been curious about the Unmaker for a while. Did you know that it has the fastest reformation cycle of any Daedra? Fascinating. Truly, unique—even among other Infernium!

Oh, don't worry about the stones. With all the experiments I've conducted before, the places where the stones go should be really obvious. \n\nAs for the Unmaker, don't let it hit you. Yeah, that's sound advice for facing any Infernium. Good luck!

My reasons are my own, little mortal. Suffice it to say that Sister Celdina commands an Order of the Waking Flame sect intent on seizing control of Fargrave. I want to determine how they plan to accomplish that.

Interesting. I noticed the Dagonic prayers and the effects they were having on mortals, but I still don't know their ultimate purpose.\n\nWhat I do know is that Sister Celdina plans to conquer Fargrave and use its many portals as a gateway to Nirn.

You need to find some lucents, preferably charged ones. Otherwise you need a dynamus font to charge them. Then place a charged lucent in the correct discharge labrum to release the energy and make something happen.

The furnace has two other discharge labrums connected to it. If we move the charged lucent you found to one of them, we'll need to find another lucent for the second. Once both are active, that should ignite the furnace.

That would accomplish nothing. The Dagonists are experts when it comes to disappearing into the shadows.\n\nSister Celdina will pay for her various insults soon enough. For now, see what she left behind when she fled.

What I seek still eludes my grasp, so our business is not yet concluded. You ought to be grateful. I can be a powerful ally—when the mood strikes me.\n\nI will meet you back in Fargrave. I'm sure the Anchorite knows someone who can decipher the code.

Sombren stole Calia's powers. The Anchorite stopped him from taking hers as well, but it has become clear that Sombren is now our enemy. As for Destron, I'm not sure. Was it his spirit or just a manifested memory?\n\nWe should discuss this elsewhere.

What do you think? Sombren betrayed us. He made poor Destron fight you! And he took Calia's powers! I can't believe he did this. And I can't believe we didn't stop him.  \n\nLet's just go. I want to make sure Calia and the Anchorite are safe.
I—I'm not sure. I just … shoved him. Somewhere. Away.\n\nCome on, let's get out of this place. Lyranth's portal looks extremely inviting right about now.
Yes, I can make it. I'll crawl if I have to. I want to get as far from this place as possible.

You wound me. I thought we were becoming friends.\n\nTalk to Gazmod the Collector. His villa on the west side of town contains quite the accumulation of Dagonic paraphernalia. Something in his collection should help—provided you can catch his eye.

The Bladebearers come to Wretched Spire every cycle. It provides a place to plot our next campaign against rival clans. When one of our war parties never arrived, I dispatched scouts to find it. They made one report. Then they, too, disappeared.

This is fantastic news! When I discovered that Daze found its way into mortal medicines, I just about rushed off to Vaveli with my shoes untied.\n\nGetting my hands on the Mantikora's venom will mean that we're one step closer to finding an antidote.

I wish I didn't. But it's my job to know about these sorts of things. And when Daze hit the market, I couldn't not study it. Apothecaries throughout Fargrave wanted to know if there was a cure. \n\nDaze led me to the Mantikora, which led me to you.

You did not know? The girl is one of the Four Ambitions of Mehrunes Dagon. But she's not like the other three. Oh no, I made a few modifications of my own to the high priest's ritual. She is not just an Ambition. She's my contingency.
Maybe. But familiar or not, they're still strangers. \n\nWe came here for answers, and while I learned something, it feels like all I got was more questions.

I've heard of the Collector. Has a villa on the west side of the city. Never met them personally, but I assume they're some sort of Daedra. Makes sense, considering their influence and where they live.\n\nI'll meet you there.
Sure. Let me know when you're ready to go.

Dagonic codes? Easy as ripping the ears off a Banekin! Arox is fluent in the many tongues of the Deadlands. No code can hide its meaning from the Mutilator's eyes!\n\nSpeaking of eyes, we should leave this place before the Collector looks this way.

I have already pledged to honor my debt to you. I will decipher every scroll in the tower of Lord Dagon's Viscount Scrivener if that is what you desire.\n\nI swear my fealty to you, mortal master. My life and my skills are yours to command.

You seem like you're more reliable than the last group that took this job. Honestly, adventurers these days are as spineless as they come. But I don't think you'll be the same. You have a different look about you.
They'll be the only thing in the area that doesn't look like they belong there. And they'll be glowing with magic, so very hard to miss.

How else would you refer to it? Lyranth summoned me and I responded. Now I hear her words and share them with the world!\n\nWell, clandestinely. Some people don't respond well to outright worship of Daedric entities.

Dislike? One must be familiar with something to dislike it. I am unfamiliar with your kind and not especially curious. You are simply … unimportant.\n\nI mean no insult. I am sure you are very important to you. As far as mortals are concerned.

I can't call a man like him comrade and I can't go back to an institution that would support all this. I can desert—he's injured,  he can't stop me—but then he'd never answer for his crimes. If—if I judged him myself, would you stand in my way?

Comfort is not a concept I give much thought to. It is something mortals seek, to protect them from fears and cares. Or so I have heard.\n\nDremora know little of fear, so the relative merits of being comfortable or uncomfortable are meaningless.

Xivilai are rarely bound to any clan. Sometimes they work together, but it never lasts. They are arrogant and do not like taking orders. Only the most powerful Daedric lords can compel their obedience.\n\nSuch as Prince Dagon.

You infer too much. I do not like or dislike Xivilai. They are difficult allies. Undisciplined. Quick to change course as their whims sway them. One cannot guess their goals, because they do not know themselves.\n\nMuch like mortals, it seems.

Our beautiful, beastly bards stand at the ready. All they need to launch into a mind-melting performance—which will be to die for—is the signal. \n\nCan you feel it? The anticipation of a grand time? The festivities that await us?

The only appropriate way to start boisterous music, of course, is with a clamorous note to kick things off. Now where is—ah! \n\nThat bell over there. That should do it. Ring the bell, stand back, and enjoy the show!

The clan-pact shapes us. It defines our essential nature. Bladebearer is not an allegiance. It is what I am. What I ever will be. \n\nShould this form be destroyed, I will respawn in a new body, but the clan-pact remains. We do not die, mortal.

The clan-pact shapes that which is us. It defines our essential nature. Bladebearer is not an allegiance. It is what I am, and ever will be. \n\nShould this form be destroyed—death, to you mortals—I respawn a new body, but the clan-pact remains.

Are you a Bladebearer? Then you have no means to perceive the secret symbols of my Kyn. We are of Oblivion, made of its substance. It is a simple thing to leave an … impression … that others like us can sense.

We are Bladebearers. All of the Kyn of my clan are pact-bound, one to another. The clan-pact unites us in purpose, attunes us to each other. I know my Kyn, and see what they wish me to see. Others do not.\n\nIt is a connection that cannot be broken.

Doubtful. Cyronin was an imaginative torturer, but not smart enough to contrive this whole scheme. He likely helped the Waking Flame tap into the torturous energy soaked into this prison, but conceiving of this machine would be beyond him.
No, but I suspect our Dremora informant may have more to say about that. I'll be sure to coax it out of her when she and I speak about what we uncovered here.
I'll need to meet with Lyranth. Martus promised to share what we learned about this place with her and I want to know just what she's gotten us involved in.
I—I don't know. It doesn't feel like I righted a wrong. I just feel worse.\n\nThe cruel bastard couldn't even die without hurting someone.

Didn't we explore all the vaults in Blackwood?\n\nWait a moment. I did read about one other vault. Doomvault Vulpinaz. It was cracked open and ransacked during Varen's revolution, so I assumed any Ambition inside it was long gone.
Well, we can't give up now! This is still worth looking into. Maybe this mark indicates a hidden portion of the vault that you didn't spot last time.\n\nWe have to at least try. I'll meet you there.

Those poor prisoners. They can't move. They must be terrified. Do you know that I recognized some of them? Members of our own are trapped there. \n\nThe only positive about this is that my teachers are pleased with me for finding the antidote.

The Dagonists probably wanted to do something nice for Taupezu Azzida. I saw them inject the prisoners with a potion that mimics the venom the Mantikora uses on its prey. \n\nKnowing what to look for made finding the quick cordial easier.
I can only imagine. Something to do, perhaps, with the changes among the people here. Those we've encountered who have been engorged or withered by it. That's not something I've seen before.
For a ward of this power? An enchanted source from which it must draw. Several, perhaps. Once those connections are severed, the spell should simply sputter out.

Hmm. If Elegian can create something as powerful as the Riven Cataclyst or as subtle as the Anchorite's mask, what else might he devise?\n\nOne never knows how a talent such as that might prove useful.

The Incarnates we encountered were indeed mindless engines of destruction. The Dremora within no longer thinks. All it knows is power and rage.\n\nSister Celdina directs these living weapons for now. But Valkynaz Nokvroz wants this power, too.

Volunteer? The very thought is repugnant. Do you not understand how we value what makes us who we are? To surrender to such a process is to be destroyed. The essence survives, but the mind, the purpose? Gone forever. Do you imagine they had a choice?

Oh, that. I was trying not to think too hard about it, thought it might spoil the celebration. Nothing puts a damper on a job well done like a Daedra who you sort of thought was your friend deciding to steal the powers of the Ambitions, huh?

As many as we can. Let's get everyone in the same place so we can all collectively catch our breath. Everything happened so fast after we kicked Dagon in his ugly face, we didn't really get a chance to talk.\n\nMaybe we could all meet in Leyawiin?

I don't know, and I'm not sure I want to know. I never really understood why she was helping us in the first place, but I didn't question it. Now, I have to wonder if this was her plan all along … and what she's going to do next.

That's true, but she's still a Daedra at the end of the day, isn't she? \n\nUgh. I hope you're right. She was with us every step of the way on our mission to stop Mehrunes Dagon. We couldn't have done it without her help. That has to mean something.

The few I have seen are foolish, weak, or mad. There is no alliance with such creatures that would benefit my clan. Some Dremora see value in studying the doings of your kind, but not I.\n\nI leave that to Lyranth the Foolkiller.

Lyranth's curiosity leads her down murky paths. Her unseemly interest in you has lessened her. No, that is unfair. It has made her different.\n\nShe is someone to be wary of. That is as true for mortals as it is for Dremora. Remember that.
Hey now, positive thoughts! Let's examine the chest. Maybe the ring will help? It got us into this hidden chamber. Who knows what else it can do?

I'd tell you to put up your feet but I know you better than that by now. You never sit still for long. \n\nSo I say we head to Fargrave and start by checking in with Calia and Madam Whim first. We don't even know if they've heard what happened yet.

Of course. I'd help you and Eveli hunt the others down, but I think I need to be alone for a bit. So much has happened and I feel like I still haven't caught up. \n\nWould you two be all right if I take some time for myself?

I can't imagine she's eager to run into us again after stealing the powers of the Ambitions. Though, that would be a normal reaction, and she doesn't exactly have a history of being predictable.\n\nI think it's impossible to say for sure.

I don't know if a Daedric Prince can ever be gone for good. They're immortal, that's their whole thing. \n\nBut at the very least, I think Fargrave will be safe from him for a long while. Nirn, too. We made sure of that.

I'm not really sure. What we learned from the Longhouse Emperors was that it would effectively banish him from Nirn. I would think he'd have turned up in the Deadlands, but it's possible he could be anywhere in Oblivion.
Hidden … safe …. Nokvroz envies us … hates Sister Celdina ….\n\nNokvroz fears that mortals will bring about Lord Dagon's triumph … not Dremora …. So he had me tortured. Help me ….

Sombren was able to take Calia's power. His summoning of Destron's spirit at the summit suggests he also has Destron's somehow, as well as his own. We need to do what he did and steal that power from him for ourselves.

Oh, not me, little mortal. The Anchorite. She's the Fourth Ambition.\n\nIf Sombren truly seeks Dagon, then he's heading for the Prince's capital, Destruction's Solace. We need someone who can lead us through that fortress so we can intercept him.

And while you track down Arox, I will gather what allies I can. We will need more than those of us here to breach the walls of Solace and take on Sombren.\n\nMeet me at Wretched Spire. Dagon's gaze never reaches that corner of the Deadlands.

There have been strange magical occurrences in the city. They started quite recently. And while I do not know for sure, I have a theory about these incidents. \n\nAfter hearing what transpired in Sundercliff, I believe they may be connected to Lyranth.

The little Wood Elf told us that Lyranth stole the power of the Ambitions. Even for someone as capable as Lyranth, all of that energy could be overwhelming. That kind of power is volatile, it may leak from her core until she manages to control it.

Hard to say. I think you'll probably have a better chance of getting her to open up than me. But will she actually tell us anything of substance? Lyranth isn't the type to show her acorns to anyone.\n\nI'll keep my fingers crossed, though.

Steal? Destron is dead, Sombren is dead, and Calia was already stripped of hers. I stole nothing. \n\nAs for the Anchorite, she is better off without them. She should thank me for removing that shackle to her past.

My plan? I started out looking to learn a secret. Where my search would lead, I had no clue. But yes, the more we uncovered, the more I grew interested in the Ambitions' power. The ability to shift destinies.\n\nWhat happens next? Not your concern.

Oh, but it does. Where I walk next, no mortal has even ventured. Possibly no Daedra, either, for that matter.\n\nI will not allow anyone to stand in my way. Not even you. It is time to let me go, little mortal.

Maybe that's for the best. Lyranth worked as hard as any of us to stop Mehrunes Dagon, but we all understood she wasn't doing it for Nirn's sake. \n\nI'm almost afraid to ask, but did she say why she took the power of the Ambitions?

Most of them are just happy to hear about Mehrunes Dagon's defeat. I think we should let them have that happiness without tainting it. \n\nLyranth may have put a fly in our blood pudding—doesn't mean we have to do the same to everyone else's.
I was thinking Castle Leyawiin would be a good spot. It's secure, and I'm sure the legates won't mind us being there.

Figures. Maybe it's silly, but I was hoping for a little reassurance that we didn't just unleash a new threat on the world directly after banishing another.\n\nI have a bad feeling about all of this. But there's not much we can do.

A little known plant, the fluster fume has a wide variety of alchemical applications. For our purposes, the root will suffice. That's where all the confusion-inspiring properties congregate.\n\nIt will help muddle the minds of those you encounter.

The Blood Pit imprisons disloyal Daedra with mystic wards. Lyranth and the Bladebearer would have to shatter those wards to enter. Mortals? Walls and locks are enough to bar your path.\n\nYour Dremora allies cannot come with us.
Consider it an enhancement for the potion I'll create. A strengthening agent, if you will. It provides the necessary layer of bewilderment that will reinforce your disguise.

An alchemist I know has a supply. Aurien. You can find her at the outpost south of Bramblebeach.\n\nTell her the tincture is for me and give her some of those yellow rocks you mortals are so fond of. Then return back to me.

You interest me, little mortal. I have ways to keep track of you. Does that surprise you?\n\nOr it might be that I simply decided there was nothing left to learn in Fargrave and came looking for you. Feel free to accept whichever answer suits you.

No. If the memory doesn't rise to the surface, the mask's protections are too powerful for my magic to overcome.\n\nPerhaps we can locate an expert and deal with that later. For now, talk to Arox and find out more about Elegian and the Blood Pit.

I have some amount of skill at magic that reveals secrets and hidden things. It wasn't too difficult to help the Anchorite make sense of the memory that welled up when the Collector examined her mask.

This creature is your pet? He killed the mortal of a very prominent Daedra. \n\nI am prepared to take him to our holding cells. If you want him released to your custody instead, you will have to compensate the Daedra.

You can count on your faithful servant. It will be my honor to fight alongside you once more!\n\nYou do remember that when mortals die, they usually don't come back, though, right? I have no such concerns for myself, but master, I worry about you.

You wish to challenge Mehrunes Dagon in his own city? A bold strategy, but I have come to expect nothing less from you, master.\n\nDestruction's Solace is a quiet, haunted place. Ghosts prowl the streets and Mehrunes Dagon basks in their agony.

The Anchorite? No, I've not heard that word. But I sense … my work. She wears my mask, doesn't she? I crafted that cursed item. It suppresses memories—both the wearer's and those who knew the wearer. Everyone forgets.\n\nSpeak quickly, stranger.

I cannot tell you who I made the mask for or why. The enchantment I devised does not simply abolish the wearer's memories. It erases the wearer from the memory of anyone who knew her. \n\nWhoever she was, that person is … forgotten.

Long ago I was a Moth Priest. I read from the Elder Scrolls and paid for the knowledge I gained with my sight. But while Moricar was still emperor, I was abducted by the servants of Mehrunes Dagon. They brought me to the Deadlands.

Dagon's servants … broke me. Drove me mad with torment and illusions until I no longer knew what was real and what was nightmare. The cataclyst design is but one product of my delirium … and by far the worst, I fear.
Of course not. The mask hides who she was, not who she is now.\n\nThink twice before you seek to unbind the mask from your friend. That curse was most likely put in place for her own protection.

An old Imperial prison. A battlemage I occasionally deal with investigated the place. Found Waking Flame cultists and a device called a cataclyst.\n\nIt was some sort of empowering machine, but I have yet to determine its ultimate purpose.

Ah, the battlemage. I dropped hints that the Waking Flame was up to something at the Dread Cellar. She, in turn, informed me of what you found.\n\nThat cataclyst was some sort of empowering device, but I have yet to determine its ultimate purpose.

Astute guess, little mortal. I learned that the cult is hunting quite aggressively for the relic that Weylin had in his possession—before the knights stole it—and I would very much like to see what has caught their interest in it.\n\nWouldn't you?

Not for any reason that won't give you nightmares, little mortal.\n\nNow let's find the cultists so you can present your prisoner. Then we shall learn what we can about the cult's plans and the true purpose of the cataclyst.
