What? The Dremora actually asked for help? Bah, I'll never understand the Grasp. \n\nAll right, before you do anything hasty, at least let me explain. This is a big misunderstanding. Or, I guess it's not, but we've got a good reason, I swear!

You saw Bakh? Is he safe? He must be, if he told you to come find me. I'm not sure why you're helping us, but I don't care. Thank you, stranger.\n\nWhat about Minwileth? Please tell me this wasteland hasn't taken her.

The Grasp interprets the Stricture, that which binds all Daedra in Fargrave. It keeps order by effectively turning the city into neutral ground.\n\nWe are the law, to put it in your terms. We make sure citizens adhere to the Strictures.

I cannot say. I must consider the balance of their crime of theft, their flight from the city and their voluntary surrender in accordance with the Strictures. \n\nI will deliver judgment once the measure of these events is fully comprehended.

I, uh, kind of had to figure that out on my own since an acolyte of Lord Vivec was called away before he could tell me. \n\nBut, I ran into someone familiar with this area in Wretched Spire. The altar is farther in the Folly. In a Daedric building.

Who else but Arox the Mutilator. The daedrat was once Mehrunes Dagon's most powerful general. He must have visited the city multiple times over the centuries.\n\nArox crawled off toward the Shambles when I told him I had no time to remove his curse.

I'm with you. She's still a Daedra, there's no telling what she has planned. Not much we can do about it now, anyway. Let's just hope it doesn't come back to bite us any time soon.\n\nWhatever her plans are, I hope she keeps them to herself.

Oh, very much so! Arox has been there many times!\n\nThe city walls are impenetrable, even by magical means. But I know of one specific location that would allow Lyranth to portal us through, if she is still a part of this.

I have this horrible feeling in my stomach. After everything we've done and everything we've lost to stop Mehrunes Dagon, it seems unfair for it to end this way. \n\nI would have trusted the Anchorite with that power. But Lyranth? I'm not so sure.

I arrived anticipating jolly conviviality. Imagine my disappointment when the only thing on offer was … this! \n\nHearing the same jokes repeatedly and watching people dance without music is sad. As an expert on merriment, this must not stand!

Just look around the city for sparkling balls of dancing light. I understand they can be quite beautiful. Or find my servant, Hezehk. I sent him to investigate. Either way, you'll run into Lyranth or not. She's stubborn, even for a Dremora.

Mortals. Always asking questions that do not require answers.\n\nBut I cannot discount your role in helping me achieve my goals, so I suppose I can try to satisfy your curiosity. Go ahead. Ask what you will.
To fulfill a promise made a long, long time ago, little mortal. And that is all I will speak of it.
We are no longer allies. I do not see the point. My part in this is finished and I am satisfied. There is nothing further I need from them. Or from you.

I am not a prophet, mortal. Seeing the future is not among my many abilities. But the whorls and eddies of existence carry us together and apart in their courses. None can truly know when we will meet again.

Ugh! Regular minstrels? This is the Jester's Festival! We can't praise the great Cheese Prince with a fool who strums in a tavern every other day!\n\nWe need something spectacular. I'd say this crowd deserves that, don't you?

I knew you were a kindred spirit.\n\nListen. Hear that? That's the sound of guests incorrectly thinking they're having a good time. Recruit our performers of mellifluous honor. Let's show these drunkards what they've been missing!

No idea. In time, I met Madam Whim. Found my place in Fargrave. I helped people, scavenged for scrap. I made allies—planar travelers, the people of the poorer districts. And when the Waking Flame arrived, I made enemies.

Has the Anchorite's mask affected you as well? If you insist.\n\nI summoned you to Fargrave to investigate the Waking Flame's Incarnates, living disasters created in cataclysts. We destroyed one at Burning Gyre Keep, but we didn't find a cataclyst.

Instead, we found evidence that the Bladebearer clan had been at the keep. Since I doubted the Bladebearers would ally with Dagon's cultists, we went to Wretched Spire to meet their kynreeve, Rynkyus. He told us some of his Kyn were missing.

No, but we discovered that Elegian, creator of the cataclyst, was being held by Valkynaz Nokvroz at the Blood Pit. He told you that the Riven Cataclyst could be found at Annihilarch's Summit.\n\nHe also admitted that he created the Anchorite's mask.

What can I tell you that you can't already guess? The Dread Lady is a powerful Dremora. Perhaps the strongest of her kind. She has served Daedric Princes but now walks her own path. She possesses a burning curiosity, forever seeking more knowledge.

Do not attempt to apply finite morality to an infinite being. Lyranth simply is, and right now she's interested in learning more about a danger that threatens all of Nirn. By helping her, you can save our world.\n\nNo pressure or anything.

There is no escape for me. Madness is my prison. Much more so than this cell. The elixir never lasts very long.\n\nBetter to leave me here. If you take me away, Dagon's servants will know we talked. They would be warned.

I reached an awful town called Wretched Spire. From there, I hitched a ride with a merchant caravan headed this way. \n\nI'm learning a lot about the people living beyond our home. Villages, families, communities exist in places I didn't expect.

Didn't want to come. Madam Whim promised a ward. Protection from summoning. Only temporary. Go back to the town soon.\n\nNirn is uncomfortable. Never been here before. Smells different. Too bright. Not clear why mortals like it.

Tufeh will spend some time with her family. She has learned not to take them for granted. \n\nAfter that? This one has given some thought to exploring Tamriel. There must be embers of the Waking Flame still lit. Tufeh would like to extinguish them.
Oh, well I'll return to Mournhold and tell the other members of the Tribunal what happened in the Folly. I'll leave out any details you ask of me, of course.
I … have yet to inform the elders in Mournhold that I resurrected Sovisa instead of the hallowed saint. I'm just … working on figuring out the best way to tell them, is all.

Though I am grieved to no longer travel at your side, I must return to the Celestial Palanquin. Madam Whim has agreed to assist me in searching for another way to release me from this cursed form. \n\nPerhaps it is too much to hope for, but I must try.

Good question. I have my memories back, no strange Ambition powers to speak of, and nothing riding on my shoulders. I could do anything.\n\nI think I'm going to stay close to Calia for a bit. Tamriel is new to both of us. We can navigate it together.

I grew up hidden away from the world, as did the Anchorite. We've decided to travel Tamriel together for the time being. \n\nI think of her as a sister, but one I don't know especially well. I'm looking forward to learning more about her.

Business, as always. Clients come and go, and come again. Oblivion will shudder for a time with the echo of Mehrunes Dagon's defeat, but it changes little for me.\n\nThe House of Whims will always provide for those who have need of it.

You called, we answered. Though I do not know if the mortals of Leyawiin approve of our presence. It came as quite a shock to those that witnessed our arrival.\n\nWe will return to Oblivion quickly after this is through, do not worry.

So I was told. The battlemages and I have exchanged information. Details concerning the cataclyst and its function were severely limited, however.\n\nSuffice it to say, I suspect the device plays into their plan to unleash disasters upon your realm.

Before we make use of the portal key, we must complete our own preparations. Then we can find the cult's base in Oblivion and determine their plans for the cataclyst.\n\nYou must acquire the root of a fluster fume plant and a tincture of befuddlement.

The relic opens a portal to Oblivion. Most likely the Deadlands. Regardless, we can't just stroll in and expect them to reveal their plans.\n\nI'll use those items to create a potion to fool them. It will make you appear to be the corpse lying here.

That was never going to happen. My bonds were illusory and it was a simple enough task to free myself once you activated the cataclyst. I observed long enough to grasp the workings of the machine. Then I made my escape.

I cannot say for certain, but if I am correct, it means Lyranth is somewhere in Fargrave. And it will only be a matter of time before she learns to wield that power without leaving a trail. This may be your last chance to speak with her.

We have no idea where we are or what we will find here. Trickery and deceit will serve us better than reckless violence.\n\nBesides, we need to learn the cult's plans and the purpose of the cataclyst. Such information will benefit us both.

It's unimportant. Whatever power it once held has been expended. The daedrat might sniff and paw at it, but if the rod had a purpose, Nokvroz would not have left it behind.\n\nCollect your pet. We should get to the summit.

They are a Dagonic cult of some reach and influence. Troublesome, but usually too busy squabbling within for power to pose a true threat.\n\nLyranth believes they are being driven by a more unified purpose these days. Not something to take lightly.
That should prove useful. Lyranth told us that these Dagonic cultists seem to be unified toward some greater purpose. We need to discover just what that is and put a stop to it.

A Dremora, if you can believe it. Called herself Lyranth. Most people wouldn't trust the word of a Daedra, and they'd be wise not to, but at the Battlespire we deal with the inhabitants of Oblivion more than most.\n\nMartus believed she was truthful.

Pardon me if I don't find that reassuring. It's a little convenient that one of Lyranth's associates shows up to help right after our escort was wiped out.\n\nNot that we can afford to refuse your help. Just … try not to justify my paranoia.

It's just … she's not forthright. She gave us this lead if we agreed to share our findings with her. So, I don't question Lyranth's information, I question her motives.\n\nAt any rate, she wasn't wrong about there being cult activity here.
That's my guess as well, though we haven't discovered evidence of that just yet. If the Cataclyst requires feeding off so much mortal suffering, its purpose must be truly frightening.
I'm familiar with the layout of this prison. I came prepared to assault it after all.\n\nOnce Lucilla and I have looked over this Cataclyst research we'll catch up with you.

That is how the cult refers to them and it's just as we believed. They are Daedric relics fashioned to soak up the residual negativity saturating this place.\n\nWhy they have those creatures feeding on that energy? I'm still not sure, but I can guess.
That seems like a safe assumption. Those creatures might just lead us to that infernal device.

An interrogator for the Dread Cellar, though that's a charitable descriptor. Torturer would be closer to the truth.\n\nI never knew what became of him after this place was abandoned. I tried my best to forget him.

That's what should have happened, though becoming entangled with a Daedra cult was a natural fit. He wouldn't have been able to continue indulging his dark impulses at the Spire.\n\nI'm only surprised he didn't wind up in service to Molag Bal.

When I learned the cult sought the relic, I acquired it first. Then they stole it from me and I employed your assistance to retrieve it. During that escapade, we learned that the relic was a portal key to a Waking Flame base in Oblivion.

My interests in these matters are strictly curiosity. I want to know more about their strange cataclyst device and its ultimate purpose. You, I assume, want to stop the cult from unleashing the disasters of Mehrunes Dagon upon the mortal realm.

No, but we can both get closer to our goals. We know that a cult leader called Sister Celdina is expecting our dead cultist to bring the portal key to her. And we know she plans to test the cataclyst.\n\nWe need to be there to witness that test.

You're a mortal, but do you have to be so naive? Sister Celdina has her place and she will keep it for as long as she proves worthy. When she no longer serves a meaningful purpose, Nokvroz will take action.\n\nUntil then, step carefully, devastator.

Is this some sort of test, devastator? The cataclyst is our great work. Our role in the larger purpose of the Order of the Waking Flame.\n\nWe will use the device to bless Daedra with the power of living disasters and then unleash them on Nirn.

The Ambitions? Another sect within the order is dealing with that. Our mission is to perfect the cataclysts and prepare incarnates to release onto Nirn. Daedra empowered with the energy of living disasters.\n\nThe destruction will be glorious!

Well, as I understand it, both the Ambitions and the cataclysts utilize the same magic and rituals. Lord Dagon never relies on a single path. Ours are just two of his plans for conquering Nirn.\n\nOnce the cataclyst is perfected, we'll be rewarded!

Ally, yes. Friend … not so sure. Like others of his kind, he considers himself the better of mortals such as ourselves. And he barely tolerates that Sister Celdina is in charge of this operation.\n\nSometimes I think he'd love to slaughter us all.

The weapons created by the Longhouse Emperors? I suppose they were created using the same techniques we've employed in the cataclyst, but our device is far superior.\n\nWhereas the Ambitions are four extremely powerful weapons, we can create an army!

You're right. Let's just hope it doesn't come back to bite us any time soon.\n\nCome on, we should get to Leyawiin. The others should be gathering, and I'll pick up any stragglers we missed on the way. Meet you there?

We learned that Sister Celdina's faction of the cult has a base in Fargrave. And they plan to conquer that obscure plane of Oblivion to use as some sort of staging ground for their nefarious machinations.

The power surging through the device carries the tinge of Mehrunes Dagon. It seems it is designed to imbue a Daedra with the energy of a single disaster and transform it into an Incarnate.\n\nThey plan to unleash these horrors on Nirn.

Perhaps. Nokvroz seemed to think so. I bought us time to consider, to plan. Sister Celdina can make more such devices, however. Eventually.\n\nBut did you see? Nokvroz despises Celdina. Perhaps we can use that.

We know that a portion of Mehrunes Dagon's energy was used to create the Ambitions. I could sense that same power surging through the cataclyst. I suspect the same magic and rituals were used in both, but applied differently.\n\nQuite ingenious.

How could I miss it? One moment he's walking along, the next he falls to the ground. His body shook a little, then nothing. I thought only a blade to the chest could kill them.\n\nNot that I care. You'll find no love for those things in my heart.

Seems to me that we should have handled it long ago. Daedra aren't meant to live among us. They have everywhere else they can go! Why do they insist on staying where I am forced to see their strange ways?\n\nI say, gather everyone and kick them out.

No, not a soul. Neither person nor creature around him when it happened. But he was coming from the spire and going toward where the Daedra stay.\n\nProbably getting up to foul business. You know how they are. I keep my eyes on them.

We have reached that point we knew was coming. The place where our paths diverge. You must deal with Sombren for the sake of your world, while I seek the knowledge I came here to acquire.\n\nI think I know what Dagon has planned, though.
Indeed. My relic. When I learned that the cult wanted it, I decided to acquire it before they could. I covered my tracks, but apparently not well enough.

Damn. I feared as much. \n\nI should have been more careful. The three of us have been stealing things since we were young and we always managed to come out on the other side just fine. But I was just so scared for Elisa, I wasn't thinking straight.

I won't stand by and watch someone suffer like that. Madam Whim and Lyranth seemed fine with it, of course. Maybe it's a mortal thing. Or just a me thing. \n\nEither way, Lyranth looks like she wants to tear my head off. But I don't regret it.

I'm not sure. She's acting strange.\n\nSomething is going on with her. Why does she care so much about Mehrunes Dagon and the Ambitions anyway? It has to be more than just her Daedric curiosity because she sure doesn't care what happens to Nirn.

Images … snatches of memory …. But it all happened too fast. Like a leaf caught in a river during a storm. Everything was rushing by … it was so violent. \n\nAsk Madam Whim if she can make any sense out of what you captured in the memory vessel.

Another early memory, but this time her father's voice is cold, commanding.\n\nThese fragments vibrate with emotional veracity. A signature of sorts. I can use that to scry the location of the Longhouse Emperor. Or, more accurately, his soul.

As I understand it, the amulet was a gift from father to daughter. Its connection to Moricar is strong. Use it in the reformatory and it will lead you to him. However, what state his soul will be in after decades of torture, I do not know.

Whomever builds the bridges sets the price of the crossing.\n\nOther groups in our position might not be as successful, but no one else has perfected transport across the planes. We're very specialized.

Has the mortal world already forgotten the name of Ducorach the Black Drake, first of the Longhouse Emperors? The plan was mine, mine! The blood of the Reach sings with fury in my veins. How dare Mehrunes Dagon betray my legacy!

Lies! You have the tongue of a liar and I will rip it from your mouth!\n\nI will not be swayed by your words. I won't let you betray me! The power promised by the pact is mine by right! You cannot have it. Away with you!

Many thanks. Their names are Elisa and Minwileth. We all split up once we got here but they shouldn't be far. \n\nI'll head to the portal now. I promise I'll explain everything once those two are safe.

Hold on, it's not safe here. Please, find my two friends and send them to the portal to Fargrave. It's where we planned to meet if we got separated.\n\nOnce we're together, I'll tell you the whole story. You can decide what to do with us from there.
Salvage physicality. Triangles examine interior hollows. Broken soul, limited cycle, grounded.\n\nNo more understanding. Ancient folding across rivers.
Detract yet written beyond his general. Forfeit linear pointed strangers. Recommended blush of new. Floating beneath and above and dissimilar plateaus.\n\nAt juncture perform exultation. Discreet.

First, I need this substance. Not to use. To examine. And … maybe to use. Depends on how events progress.\n\nMiksotet says he knows of it. On a fallen tree to the northwest. I would like you to collect some. Too dangerous for me.

I will ask around about this poison. See if someone peddles it. Perhaps someone moving for power.\n\nThen, I'll visit the last person Tephilaz spoke to. Faven Indoril. Meet me in the spire, center of town. Unlikely he reveals much without you there.

The Dread Lady requires a mortal's perspective. She finds the situation merely curious, but says it has apocalyptic consequences for our plane of existence.\n\nCongratulations, mortal. She has chosen you. And she promises compensation, if you survive.

Calm? I suppose. But I have faith in Lyranth, and she seems to have faith in you. I'll mark the destination on your map. Plus, I secured transportation—the regal Sweet Daffodil.\n\nOh, and take this pendant. You'll need it when you get there.

Please, you must find her. When we got here through the portal, we split up to keep the Grasp from tailing us. I took the east road, and she took the north one. \n\nIt's my fault we're all out here. I don't know what I'll do if she's hurt.

Vehk's head. Where to start?\n\nDaedra are heartier than a lot of mortals, and immortality can get boring. Daedra supplement their experiences with whatever they can find. Mantikora venom—Daze—is one of the supplements.

Oh, now that's a question. \n\nI don't really know. That's part of the reason why I need to study the poison. Daedra can have their fun, but mortals definitely won't have any on Daze. I'm just trying to see how we can stop innocents from being cooked.

For the same reason that mortals take Skooma. \n\nDaedra get bored with living. They need to add excitement to their lives. And they can withstand more than we can. Of course they're going to experiment with burning their stomachs.
That is some zzavfa I wish I didn't know! It raises the internal body temperature of the victim. Immobilizes them. And cooks them from the inside. I saw it happen once. That was enough for me.

No. Thank Vehk. Otherwise it'd be all over for us. Even Dremora can't withstand Mantikora stings. They char like the rest of us at those temperatures!\n\nIt seems like this particular venom is specific to Taupezu Azzida.

Not in the same way. I don't think he's having dreams or anything. Sombren's always been passionate. But since Destron died, his rage has been growing. And the frustration and desperation makes that rage harder, sharper.\n\nAnd what he just did ….

I scryed for it. Oh! That's a type of magic to help search for things. I started with small baubles. But once I got the hang of it, it was easy to move onto more abstract things. The possibilities are endless. \n\nI searched for a cure and I found it!

Right. Moricar said the answers were waiting at the Isle of Joys. I have no idea where that might be. \n\nLook, your friend Eveli wants to talk to you. And I need a moment to think this through. But don't worry. I'm with you to the end. I promise.
Well done. Beginning to understand why mortals summon Banekin. Very useful to have an assistant.\n\nA curious substance. If we find anyone else with it, we may have our target.
Speak to Faven. You're a mortal. He may respond better to you. Ask about his conversation with Tephilaz. Get a sense of his plans. \n\nImportant we delay a purge. At least until Tephilaz returns.
As you say, master. I remain in your debt and will do as you command. My nose will guide us, my rage will drive us, and my fury will freeze the cultists in their tracks!

I have heard of the location. A barren peak scoured by winds that flay flesh from bone. A good place to build a secret retreat, provided the walls can withstand the constant winds. \n\nSister Celdina has taken great care to hide the Riven Cataclyst.

Always. With Rynkyus and his Bladebearers beside us, we will fight our way to the Riven Cataclyst. When I have seen what I need to, you can destroy the device.\n\nMeet us at the base of Annihilarch's Summit, provided you want to be a part of this.

Yes, bound like Ogrim waiting for the torturer's lash. The mortal leader, Sister Celdina. Nokvroz stood beside her like a trained clannfear. They took our Kyn to the citadel, to their cataclyst device. They use our essence to fuel the infernal thing.
Angry that the Ravener put me in this position. But also comforted. Atrozu will stay by my side. I won't be completely alone in this world.

Corpse? Hmm. Can't say that I'm surprised. Mikget continues to be too uncoordinated for retrievals. He tries his best, but I fear it will be a few more millennia before he is able to move with grace or stealth.

I am under no obligation to explain that to you. We have no dealings, no contract or agreements. The only thing that ties us is that you returned what was lost. You are an admirable mortal, do not misunderstand me. But Madam Whim cannot favor you.
It won't be a lasting death. Maybe he will learn something from this that he did not from every death he has suffered before.\n\nYou said you have something from his possessions?

Telofasa is dead? Again? Zzavfa! It's been less than a century since the last time she died. With a short span like that, it will be hard to hire her again. \n\nYou said you found her in the False Martyrs' Folly?
Ha! Those slackwits ran as soon as they needed to fight something other than cultists. Worse off, they left the rods! Just left them where they were. In the lair of an intelligent mer-eating beast!

Did you not just hear me say it was intelligent? \n\nI don't know about Taupezu Azzida, but I've heard of Mantikora bartering with cultists. Bartering! Let's not be stupid enough to give it something it can gift to our enemies.

Oh, interested in the inner workings of the spell are you? Sorry, but that's classified Saraathu Tong knowledge.\n\nThe short, unclassified, explanation is that they anchor the spell. They secure one side of the portal to a place. Hence, liminal rods.

I am … not shocked by this news. Mortals do not always know when to back away. This makes them exceptional employees, but does decrease their already limited longevity. \n\nYou said you have the gem he was sent to retrieve?

Did your doombringer tell you nothing? The cataclyst enhances Daedra. Transforms them into incarnates of disasters.\n\nFirst we take control of this pitiful demiplane, then we launch our assault using Fargrave's connections to Nirn.
No one knows. Daedra have sought it for centuries. But with the treasure hidden away and Uxark's whole clan sent to float formlessly between the stars, there wasn't anyone who could talk about it.

Ah! A student of the Daedric studies? You probably know that Daedra don't die as Mortals do. They experience a cycle of death, existence, and reformation. A reformation cycle. \n\nThe Unmaker reforms fast and I plan to study it until I figure out why.

Mainly I've learned that Daedra—Dremora, Scamps, Ogrims, and one polite Skaafin—don't have any interest in assisting scientific inquiry. \n\nThe time of reformation does vary for the Unmaker. It's fast, but inconsistent even for an Infernium.

Inferniums are many-legged beasts with rows of teeth. They chase after their prey, screaming and spewing molten rock. \n\nI like to call them Lavapedes, but my apprentice, Barashana, says that's uncharacteristic of their morphology.

I—I'm not sure. The memory is only a fragment, and a jumbled one at that. Maybe if I retrace my steps, try to recreate my first few days in the city, maybe it will become clearer.\n\nAll I know is, whatever Gazmod did to me, it shook something loose.

You saw what they were like. Gazmod treated me as something to be studied. Never actually talked to me at all.\n\nOnly my mask interested them. When they examined it, a memory shifted into focus. Sort of. I think I'll be more help if I figure this out.

A construct of fire and iron. An instrument of terror and intimidation to pacify any unrest that threatened to compromise the Dread Cellar's security. The idea was its presence would be enough to instill obedience, but it's far more than a scarecrow.

No, and his erratic behavior worries me. Mortal minds were not meant to read the Mysterium Xarxes.\n\nI'm wary about him separating the Anchorite from us as well. We're going to need her once you determine the nature of this contingency plan.

Have you not realized after all this time that I have my ways, little mortal? I found Sombren and Calia once. I can do so again.\n\nIn the meantime, you and Eveli should search the Isle of Joys. We must discover this plan that Emperor Moricar spoke of.

My reaction is irrelevant. The Anchorite recently had her memories returned to her and has yet to make sense of them all. Now she discovers she's also an Ambition of Mehrunes Dagon and a tool of a father she didn't know. I understand her motivations.
As much as I want to, no. Someone has to investigate the Isle of Joys. We should stick together and take care of that.\n\nThe Anchorite, though. She'll be all right, right?

Good to hear. I barely know her, so I wasn't sure. Besides, Calia is with them. She'll keep Sombren from doing anything too crazy, I'm sure. \n\nWe just have to trust that the Anchorite knows what she's doing. Everything will be fine. Now let's go.

Yes, but not just any sort of thieves and spies. We're extraplanar thieves and spies!\n\nIn addition to utilizing Fargrave's public portals, we also have an arrangement with the mages of the Saraathu Tong. For when we need a special portal.

They're a group of Dark Elf mages that were cast out of Morrowind for some offense or another against the Tribunal. They came to Fargrave and use their expertise at portal magic to supply House Hlaalu with trade goods from across the multiverse.

Sometimes we need to go somewhere not readily connected to the portal plazas of Fargrave. Or we need to reach a specific location quickly and quietly. That's when we turn to the Saraathu mages.\n\nAnd when they require our expertise, we reciprocate.

How can they be allowed to paint their lies over Fargrave's walls? Do you see the damage that they're going to cause just by manipulating honest and good creatures? Daedra—no, even the Grasp—refuse to stop them!

Everyone in Fargrave is held accountable by the laws of the Stricture. The Grasp are there to enforce and interpret those laws. \n\nSince the cultists haven't killed anyone within the city, the Grasp says they can't ban them. I asked.

Some of our biggest clients are the movers and shakers of the city. And we tend to avoid pilfering in our own backyard. Plus, the Grasp don't care. As long as we keep a low profile and don't make a spectacle, the Daedric authorities leave us alone.

Ah, yes. This one thought about charging into the Reformatory to see if the information was true for himself, but—as tempting as gold and fortune is—Airlur's been told he looks better with his tail attached.

Hmm. Airlur does not have to answer. Though he will say that it was through a combination of hanging around the Shambles, luck, and collaboration with a Tong scryer.\n\n She is better looking than you.

Yes! I—uh, I was passing through there coming back from a different assignment and saw all the valuables, but I didn't have room in my bag to carry everything so ….\n\nBut I told Luna about what I'd seen the moment I got back to Fargrave!
I only went in there because I didn't know what it was like. Everything that's bad about the Sever? It's worse in there. And I was carrying so much at the time. I could have been struck by lightning!

I am not equipped to deal with all the ailments in Fargrave. So I'm always on the lookout for new curatives. \n\nWhen a young Gleaner came back from the Folly chattering about the plants there, I thought they could be useful.

Is there ever a guarantee of anything? I studied healing on Nirn and now look where I am. \n\nDiseases crop up between the planes that don't exist in any books. If there's a chance that this flower has some medicinal purpose, I need to know about it.

I'd handle dropping those off myself, but some overcautious desk Scamp thinks that sneaking around the Blood Pit is dangerous. As the founder of the Gleaners of Aurbis, they say it's irresponsible for me to take that risk.
The Blood Pit is a prison for Daedra. That alone should tell you what you need to know. \n\nPut another way, entering the Blood Pit is easy. It's the leaving that's impossible.

Is that what this is about? Look, I just saw shipments lying at the drop sites. No one touched them while I was there. \n\nNot sure if that's still the case, so if you plan to acquire them for the Gleaners, you better hurry.

They hired you and you don't know about the Shambles? It's not the safest place to visit in Fargrave, that's for sure. And it's full of rival gangs. If the Errants don't find those shipments, then the Vanquished or the Invisible Web sure will.

Great, the Spire must have assumed I was killed. Well, I was killed, but that's not the point. I'm trapped here. The spiritual enchantments of the prison's defenses are preventing my soul from leaving the Dread Cellar and lack of body isn't helping.
Very well. Just make sure you're prepared to face a tempest of blades or the Grim Warden will chop you to chowder in an instant.
I expect nothing less.\n\nI'm going to enjoy witnessing their attempts to overcome our security measures. Whenever that confrontation occurs, it will be enlightening.

I was trying to figure out how to restore the prison's arcane defense matrices. It should recognize me—or my soul rather—and allow me to make the adjustments needed to escape. It would also help you clear out these invaders more easily.

You've already begun the process just getting here. Light the braziers by the orange guardian stone and you'll have reactivated its arcane matrix. Once you've done that, I can revise the spell, but we'll get to that matter in a moment.

No sense standing on ceremony under the circumstances. You can call me Vitellia. I was the caretaker for the Dread Cellar. The prison's been abandoned for quite some time, so I was assigned to try to keep it from completely falling apart.

Those Waking Flame cultists and their Daedra happened to me. I managed to kill a few score of them, but they were too many and too willing to suicide charge through my destruction spells for me to fend off. So, here we are.
There was no need to sustain them with all the prisoners gone. Wouldn't have made sense to expend all the resources keeping an empty prison running a high alert.

I … really shouldn't get into the details, but prisoners who died in custody or who thought death might be an escape needed to be contained. At least until we could ensure they couldn't cause any harm.

Yes, some of the enchantments meant to contain any spiritual escapees are in place. I saw no harm in letting the enchantments run their course when I was still breathing. I'd prefer not waiting a hundred years for that to happen now that I'm not.

The process will be the same as what you've done so far. Find deactivated arcane matrices and restore them. Doing so will open another entrance to this nexus and you can attempt to subdue another guardian.

Well, who knows what the Waking Flame's done to the place since they've been here—I've heard them undertaking some enormous construction project. There will be one in the dungeons and another down in the pit. Keep an eye out for familiar signs.

At one time, a necromancer who abandoned their mortality as a lich. It was stubbornly difficult to keep dead, so it was brought here for imprisonment. Initially it was bound to serve as a sort of penance, but there's nothing left of its mortal soul.

Meaning it's merely the echo of a being who is long gone. It's driven only by instinct and the direction of the summoning spell to carry out its duties.\n\nYou won't be harming anyone by destroying it. Not that it ever deserved your mercy.
I'd sooner haunt this room the rest of my days than entrust my fate to that thing. That's not a way for a Divine fearing soul to go.

This prison had a propensity for hauntings, so the Undertaker helped shuffle deceased inmates to their final resting place. Though it was dangerous enough to act as a weapon against living threats as well.
Down in the Pit of Despair, but that's where the Waking Flame has done most of their construction. We'll just have to hope that they haven't damaged anything.

Originally, it guarded the tomb of a Ra Gada prince before being claimed as a trophy by Emperor Reman. Eventually, it was re-installed to serve as a guardian here. Once a tomb guardian, always a tomb guardian, I suppose.

Ancient Yokudan eternal guardians too mundane for you? Don't let any prior encounters color your opinion. This one was restored and empowered by some of the Battlespire's best mages. Underestimate it at your own peril.

Well, assuming I'm not just whisked away to whatever afterlife the Divines intended, I suppose I'll have to find my way back to the Battlespire. Or, perhaps, just to a priest of Arkay who can help a freshly lost soul.
To you as well. I hope the guardians help you kick those Daedra and their bootlicks all the way back to Oblivion. Painfully.

You do not need to concern yourself with my safety, little mortal. Besides, the Bladebearers who remain have a reputation that is well earned. We will be able to handle most anything that comes after us.

She believes that Mehrunes Dagon will destroy the world with fire in order to remake it. After suffering at the hands of the Reach, she took up with Emperor Moricar and joined the Waking Flame. \n\nLike she was trying to remake herself as well.
The Telvanni? Then it's as I suspected. Foiled by my own renown. Again. Intolerable.\n\nWell, there's no use dwelling on it. Did you find anything else?

The Ebony Blade? Well, that's uh … you know, not really my area of expertise. Daedric artifacts, I mean.\n\nThen again, there is a small errand that needs doing. A personal matter, you see. You help me with that, and my memory might improve.

If you know of any other group that's famous for making it out of dangerous locations without spilling a drop of blood, let me know. \n\nThe Waking Flame is full of spineless dung-mongers, but the people in the Brandfire Reformatory are victims too.

Ha! This is Fargrave! Everyone has connections to some Daedric Prince or another. Myself included.\n\nIf someone needs some fabric, then my door's open. But I don't abide by organizations who trick folks into joining a cult!

You didn't hear this from me, but some of the cultists come into my shop to get away from prying eyes. Oh, the things they say ….\n\nIf their doubts are ever discovered, the Reformatory is where they'd be taken for reeducation.

Well from what we learned at the Isle of Joys, we were supposed to find something at that spot in the vault. Hopefully it's got something to do with the egonymic. Maybe it is the egonymic! Show it to the Anchorite and see if it triggers any memories.

Airlur saw valuables and pretty things he wants to give to that scryer. If you're looking for information on what lies inside the Reformatory, get moving and see for yourself.\n\nThat was harsh. Be careful and you'll be fine. Airlur is sure of it.

Not by myself. I surprised him at Annihilarch's Summit. And he didn't have complete control of Calia's power yet.\n\nWe'll probably need to throw everything we have at him. Weaken him. Distract him. Then maybe—maybe—I'll have a chance.

It is an artifact of the dread teacher, Mephala. At first glance, it resembles a katana carved from obsidian. But, I assure you, it is far more than a simple sword.\n\nIt is the Lady's malice in physical form—a life-devouring instrument of murder.
Very well. Let me know when you are ready to proceed.
Hmm. Caution. I like that. \n\nThe Folly is damp and stormy. Keep your feet dry, your wits sharp, and your weapons at the ready. I do not want to see you back here bleeding on my floor.

You pay attention. That'll serve you well in the Pit. \n\nYes, I've visited the Pit many times—unofficially, of course. But don't forget who founded the Gleaners. There's no place I can't make my way out of.

Well, even if I did answer that, would you believe I wasn't lying? \n\nDon't think too much about me. And don't worry about killing anyone in the Blood Pit. Most of them can't die. At least not permanently.

And ruin their fun? No. They have to learn how to make their way out of every location in the planes. If they can't, they're not Gleaners material. Simple as that. \n\nKeep your eyes open and you'll figure it out. Just like I did centuries ago.

Look, I'm not a Gleaner. At best, I'm an occasional informant. So I don't have the protection of their organization to back me up.\n\nI may have let slip something I wasn't supposed to and the interested party may have heard. So, yeah, I'm hiding.

Because the Shambles is beyond the Grasp of the Grasp. The Stricture Guards rarely go there. Most business of the sort the Gleaners are involved in takes place in the Shambles.\n\nDanger is the price of doing business, right?

He spends most of his time reading that strange book, searching desperately for answers. He's obsessed with our power, trying so hard to understand it. But the more frustrated he gets, the more he pulls away. And now this.\n\nI'm worried about him.

An old associate of mine has gotten himself into a heap of trouble. Bad habit of his, but this time it looks like more than I can handle.\n\nI need to retrieve the items he was carrying—and rescue the fool if lady luck still has a shine on him.

If you ever need more sunshine, I'm sure some new band of beach-loving reprobates will settle on that island again. Of course, so will the yaghra I'm betting. Either way, it'll make a good vacation spot for Undaunted to tan more than their own hides.

I escaped a terrifying clan of Reachmen and Minotaurs that kidnapped me. They've been raiding villages and dragging away anyone they can.
No shortage of things crawling over the bones of that old shipyard, eh? Maybe now it can rest in peace. If not, I'm sure there are plenty of Undaunted willing to go make the ghosts shut up for a bit.

Some kind of diplomatic correspondence. A letter and a medallion. All I know is I'm being well paid to risk my neck for it, and you will be too. If you don't mind crossing these Ascendant Order troublemakers.\n\nSo, you in?
Please, save the others from their sorry fate!

Zzavfa! There's no need for that! I was … I was just joking!\n\nA couple of Skaafin showed up not long ago. Said they had to stow it away in the Hexos gallery vault. In the Shambles. Just don't tell anyone I told you, all right?

Eerily sharp, masterfully etched … and completely fake. This is a forgery. A brilliant one, I admit, but a forgery nonetheless.\n\nWhile I respect this forger's skill, I cannot abide a glut of fraudulent artifacts taking up my time and attention.
Ebony Blade, eh? That's the Mistress's heart-cutter. Somebody hammering out fakes? Clever.\n\nGot no idea where it comes from. Don't care. Tell Fyr he can find it himself.
A bauble I purchased before we set out for the Shambles. Keep it near to hand. It may prove useful.

No, it's an odd sensation, but not entirely unwelcome. Without them, Mehrunes Dagon will never have reason to hunt me. If Lyranth desires that burden, she's welcome to it. I'll finally have the peace I sought for so long.
Always! Whatever details you have to spare!\n\nDid you discover anything particularly noteworthy? Any unforgettable experiences? I'll add them to my notes.

I've never understood Lyranth's motivations. Sure, she was integral in helping us banish Dagon, but do any of us know why?\n\nI shudder to think about what she has planned for all that power. But I doubt we've seen the last of her.
I'm sure they'll all sort themselves out over time, but I'm not in a hurry. That chapter of my life is closed. I think it's time for new memories. Maybe even a new name, who knows?

A nap, first. After that? It's hard to say. Maybe I'll get a chance to explore the mortal world a bit. My part in world-ending prophecies and machinations is done. I'm just myself now, nothing more, nothing less. That's exciting.
Her curiosity about the mortal world will draw her back. She tries to hide it, but in her own way I think she is fond of us.

Ah, excellently! While you pursued Sombren, I helped the others hold back the forces of Mehrunes Dagon.\n\nI lost count of the foes I felled in your name! My whiskers tremble with the memory of their last moments!

Of course, master! The very foundations of this plane trembled with your might! A legion of Daedric eyes and ears bore witness to your victory! Dagon will never forget such a resounding defeat. It was my honor to be a part of something so monumental.

Just when I thought we might be overwhelmed, a great and sudden force seemed to freeze the Deadlands entirely. Our adversaries halted in their tracks, clearly shaken by the event.\n\nWe used the distraction to fall back, for we knew the fight was done!

Within this small body beats the massive heart of a titan! You have reminded me that my fight is not yet done and I can still be of use.\n\nI am finished feeling sorry for myself. And hope is not lost! Perhaps one day I can reclaim my true form!

Possible? You stormed the gates of Destruction's Solace and brought Mehrunes Dagon to his knees! And you brought your allies home safely. Nothing seems impossible after witnessing that. \n\nIf a cure for this curse exists, I will find it.

You banished Dagon to the depths of the Deadlands. It is as close to death as Daedra can conceive. You have done what many would consider impossible, but he will return eventually. \n\nEven I might have considered that impossible before meeting you.

Spoken like a true hero! I'll tell you, mate—that's exactly the sort of thing my readers want to know.\n\nI hope you had help. Oh, what am I saying? A warrior like you could probably kill a hundred of these things without breaking a sweat.
Oh, excellent! I toured around Alinor and that half-built Vivec City. Those buildings! They're no Fallinesti, but honestly, what is?\n\nThanks for the details, mate!

Oh, marvelous! The bugs in Valenwood are big, no question. But they're not that big!\n\nI heard those silt striders can survive anything—even Dark Elves digging around in their brains. That's really something, mate!
I am one of her assistants. Hezehk is another. We handle clients with less complicated problems so that she can focus her attention on more prestigious or troubling cases.

Madam Whim provides a service where she offers solutions to the problems of others. I would give specifics, but that is against our confidentiality agreement. All you need to know is that the service she performs for Fargrave is legendary.

Off the record, I hear they're all in a spot of trouble. Daedric mischief, you see? You didn't hear that from me.\n\nTo be honest, I don't have the first idea how someone would even get to half of these places, but they might not be around much longer!

You gave it to me to study. I studied it. It protects its secrets very well, but I have learned a few things while you were busy in Deadlight.\n\nIt is an old relic that contains an enchantment as twisted as its form. It is … disconcerting.

Well, look, I'm just a travel writer. Take all of this with a grain of salt, all right?\n\nI heard a trio of the worst sort of Daedra struck some kind of bargain. They mean to split Tamriel up like a guar-liver pie, starting with these locales.
You don't say? Well, let me put some of this down!\n\nSpit it out, mate! What have you heard?
You took on three Daedric Princes and survived? Z'en's price, that's amazing!\n\nWell, this little research project of ours should be over in the whip of a fox's tail!

Not exactly. Not yet. But Arox's essence is somehow tied to the relic. That could be why he was attracted to it.\n\nI will continue to examine it as time permits. Who knows? It may have a use we can exploit should the need arise.

I think we can both agree that a disaster like this festival is a singular affair. \n\nBut, no. I often add some merriment to many a celebration. Weddings can get particularly boisterous when I'm involved.

Mortal blood and Daedric essence perform similar functions. And blood tied to rituals make them more powerful. The cataclysts are basically rituals made manifest.\n\nRoyal blood flows through the Anchorite's veins. That makes it valuable indeed.
That's a complicated question. All of them, if you want to get technical about it. Everyone wants the best for their big day and many would say that I'm the best. \n\nThey're right, of course.
No. I care little for what she does with her prize. Neither you nor I have any use for the Ambitions' power. Why concern yourself needlessly?

An interesting question. Nokvroz is defeated. The Waking Flame is extinguished. And you, mortal, have dealt Mehrunes Dagon a humiliating blow that he will no doubt remember for eons to come. \n\nMy Kyn are avenged. I have many possibilities.

We have the same chance we always have. And we will find a way.\n\nWhat you told me raises questions about the Anchorite that I must have answers to. And you do not want Mehrunes Dagon's plans to succeed. So we shall deal with Nokvroz. Together.

Wait, was that why that huge rock over Vivec City went crackers for a while? It was, wasn't it?\n\nWell, top marks, mate. Would have been a shame to see that shiny new city blown to bits … even though some of those Ordinators sort of deserve it.

Sotha Sil? That Dark Elf wizard … er, god, or whatever? Y'ffre's bones, I thought he was dead. Or that he was made up. One or the other.\n\nI can't believe you met him! Should make this business a bit easier, eh? Friends in high places and all that.
Well, I understand about half of that. It sounds extremely heroic though. I'm assuming Nocturnal taking over that High Elf tower would have been trouble. So, thank you?

He's a Spiderkith, which is to say he's a treacherous, deceitful sneakthief.\n\nOur personal history is … contentious. Full of double-dealings and trickery. I've killed him more than once, but you know how these Daedra are. It rarely takes.
Nothing. Secrets of the Skein. You find out the secret, you die. Quiet. Alone in the dark.\n\nStill want to know how it works?
Signal line will show the way to the source. Of your fake Ebony Blade. Just follow the spider. Simple. Even for you mortals.\n\nYou feel like giving up, just say so. Got better things to do.

Surely you don't require a chaperone? Skrix, while clever, is hardly a match for a warrior of your skill. No, I'm quite certain you'll be fine without me.\n\nI have other lines of inquiry to explore. I won't be far behind, I assure you.

Gather a few lucent crystals. Preferably a charged lucent. Then we can activate that displacer so you can get up to the balcony.\n\nI'm pretty sure that if you place charged lucents in the discharge labrums above, that will open the cell door.
Then hopefully there are a few uncharged crystals lying about. In that case, we'll need a dynamus font to charge them. Why don't you search around?
More questions? No more questions … is it the season of blossoms yet? That was always my favorite.

All my ideas, gone. They poured them out and now I'm an empty bottle. So empty. Sometimes everything is right again. Usually not. But so many, many questions! I won't answer them unless … unless.\n\nDo you smell flowers? Flowers, cowers, showers!

An interesting question. Alas, I have no answer. But you're not the only newcomer to our fair city seeking such knowledge.\n\nMy eyes about town tell me that Lyranth the Dremora has come to Fargrave. She's in the Shambles, searching for Sister Celdina.

Hmm? Oh, the mortal on the floor? No, I don't believe so. The spell is quite potent. I suspect the votive runes have a darker purpose than simply elevating emotions and turning mortals into mindless husks.\n\nPity the Grasp refuses to investigate.

You came here without knowing, darling? How refreshing!\n\nLike an otherworldly conveyance, Fargrave personifies the existential concepts of transit or passage. It did start out as a strange, nomadic realm, after all. That's part of the city's allure.

A terrible place. I urge caution if you decide to venture there. It's a warren of alleys, tenements, and ruins hidden behind thick walls. Many mortals live there in the most appalling conditions, but it can also be a good place to conduct business.

An apt description, if somewhat inaccurate. They do enforce Fargrave's laws, but in ways that won't always be comprehensible to the limits of mortal understanding.\n\nTry not to commit any crimes in front of them and they won't harass you. Probably.

It means if you want to travel the myriad corridors of Oblivion, there's no better launching point than fabulous Fargrave. In addition to our famous Plaza of Portals, the entire realm is littered with dimensional accessways.\n\nPlus, we have no Prince.

A personal query? That will cost extra, my darling.\n\nI am a Mazken, what your kind commonly call a Dark Seducer. Unlike many of my brothers and sisters, I use my charms to beguile and entice for knowledge and profit. I have no interest in violence.

Without a Prince to set the laws and manipulate Fargrave's reality, we're free to shape this city as we choose. The freedom that affords us is sublime!\n\nPlus, no Prince means less chaos and violence in the streets, rogue cultists notwithstanding.

Darling of the alleys, fool of Fargrave, woman in the mask … ever since the Anchorite arrived in Fargrave, she's gone out of her way to help the mortals cast upon our shore. And she asks for nothing in return.\n\nPity I know so little else about her.

If Sister Celdina knew I was talking to you or the Anchorite, my life wouldn't be worth a scab on an Ogrim's elbow. I want out!\n\nLook, tell the Anchorite. She can find me at the Bearer's Rest in Fargrave when she's really ready to help an old friend.

The size, mostly.\n\nThese Hexos n'wahs are quite clever … by Imperial standards. They operate a number of warehouses in Fargrave, but only one of them is large enough to contain a vault of any appreciable size. I suppose we'll find out soon enough.

If I open a portal, it could alert Nokvroz to my presence. Better to take advantage of Fargrave's Plaza of Portals and use one of the permanent gateways between this plane and the Deadlands.\n\nThe portal to the Burn should get us close to the keep.

Yes. I know three ways to navigate the Shambles.\n\nWe need to be wary of the Vanquished if we cross the central plazas, and Boss Kezo's gang controls the western warrens. If we go east through Skein Row, try to avoid the Spiderkith that roost there.

Whatever the merchants were carrying when the Unmaker attacked.\n\nJewelry, armor, precious gems, magical items. The list goes on. We've recovered an innumerable number of goods from the Unmaker's hoard in the past.

Vares—obsessed oddball that he is—describes it as a giant insect, terrifyingly large, and with more teeth than you have bones in your body.\n\nPlus, it's almost always surrounded by flaming gigantic Daedra. Because, it needs that help.

Heard all that and you don't want to work for the Tong? Figures. \n\nHouse Hexos is the largest group, but there's also the Gleaners of Aurbis. You can talk to Hewlet Hexos or Luna Beriel if you're interested. But there are others too.

Mostly, higher ranking members will be the ones with jobs. Take Vares Dredayn for example. He's a high-ranking mage with a number of dangerous experiments underway. \n\nBut anyone can request the Tong assign an adventurer to their project.

Hexos is reliable and we've done enough business with the Gleaners to keep their thieving hands away from Tong property. But the Errant, that's what the others are called, are a selfish bunch. \n\nThey're pactless and that makes them desperate.

We all serve different purposes. Hexos deals in goods across the planes. We're more magically minded. The Gleaners are useful for all covert operations. And the Errant—disorganized though they may be—give mortals structure.\n\nFargrave's complex.

I don't presume to know the results of Vares's years of study or the extent of his eclectic knowledge. But I have noticed that the Unmaker reforms and returns to the Deadlands far more frequently than any other routinely killed Daedra.

This is the best news I have heard all day. I'll send my assistant down to the Unmaker's Den to collect the stones as soon as she returns from her last errand.\n\nThank you, the progress you've helped us achieve …. I left your payment with Vaveli.
Good thinking. Sera Indavel will prefer it if you haven't tampered with the merchandise.\n\nI'm still hoping there's something nice in those crates. Like an unlabeled elixir. Or a forgotten bestiary.

Ravam probably will go on and on about the scarcity of resources here, but I suspect the real reason he's so insistent in getting his hands on some Daedric armor and weaponry is that he's been trying to learn Daedric techniques for a while now.

Was it in good shape? No. Don't tell me, I'll just wrap up here and check with Vaveli myself. Go to her and collect your well-deserved reward my friend. \n\nBy Sotha Sil's grace I am going to learn something today!

That is not common knowledge. Why would Nass send someone as mortal as you to track it down? Hmm. This is a mystery. \n\nVery well, you've intrigued me. Why should I tell a Nirnling like you what Nass wants to know?

I suppose that's true. \n\nUxark went to Oblivion with a smile on her face knowing that the planestones would never be reunited. Now that they are, there's nothing stopping less reputable Daedra from soiling her treasure with their greasy hands.

Then I will uphold my part of our bargain. Let me mark the portal's location for you.\n\nYou've done me a free favor, mortal. When Uxark reforms, I'll know where the treasure is and we can storm Madam Whim's shop to reclaim it in bloody glory!

The Anchorite? An unusual appellation, even for a mortal.\n\nYou must be wondering why I summoned you and then failed to be on hand to greet you. When I heard that Sister Celdina had arrived at their headquarters in the Shambles, I had to act quickly.

You can plainly see that I did not. Finding this location took more time than I expected. And even then, getting inside has proven difficult.\n\nBut now that we're together, I suspect we can make short work of any obstacles and locate Sister Celdina.

My reasons are my own, little mortal. Suffice it to say, I want to determine how Sister Celdina plans to utilize the votive runes to seize control of Fargrave. She wants to use its many portals as a gateway between the Deadlands and Nirn.

Everything about Sotha Sil's pact is rumor and speculation, so that is what I hope to determine. And I want to examine the cataclyst.\n\nThe attack on Fargrave could begin at any moment. Shall we enter the next area and see what Celdina is up to?

Daedra empowered to unleash destruction upon the mortal realm and make it easier for Mehrunes Dagon to conquer Nirn. Did you know he's tried before? Dagon broke an agreement and the doors between the Deadlands and Nirn were sealed. He can't use them.

Mortals don't have the same issues with pride that Daedra do. \n\nWell, that might be a bit of an overstatement. What I'm getting at is that I send groups off to fight the Unmaker and they're usually successful. The Daedra like to face it alone.

Can't say, I'm not Vares. It feels like he requests another termination of this Infernium every few days. \n\nAs far as I know, that speed of return is unprecedented. It makes sense that Vares's studies have gotten a lot of backing from Dremora.

Oh, innocent mortal! The kind of business best engaged in where the Grasp of the Stricture doesn't reach. It's a perfect location to hide a Dagonist cult seeking to cause chaos and mayhem.\n\nI'm surprised our darling of the alleys didn't mention that.

We have scryers assess all locations before sending someone out. This lair has a few venom-charred bodies lying around. Taupezu Azzida's had some successful hunts.\n\nI almost wish I could be there for this fight. Mantikoras were always my favorite.

I've faced Mantikora before. They're aggressive fetchers. Their poison cooks their victims from the inside out. It does not smell good.\n\nNever had the pleasure of fighting this one though. Can't help you if you're looking for specific advice.
Then take the lucent to the dynamus font over there. That background energy I mentioned? The font absorbs it. Place the lucent on the font and it will fill it with the charged energy.

Finally, insert the charged lucent into the discharge labrum beside the door. That will release the energy from the crystal and disrupt the ward. That's the idea, anyway.\n\nI've seen the Daedra do all sorts of things using lucents, fonts, and labrums.

A magnificent battle awaits us within Destruction's Solace. Many will surely die. It is invigorating. \n\nYour allies stand by your side, honored to lay down their lives for you. Tell me, are you truly prepared for this?

Bah. I did not do it for you or the Anchorite, master. I did it because it offered my best chance for vengeance.\n\nHad I chosen the safe course, Nokvroz would have been beyond my reach by the time Lyranth found a way to break the curse permanently.

Just the sort of news I like to hear! \n\nI can't promise that an antidote will be forthcoming, but I know that we'll make one eventually. You also halted the production of Daze. All the apothecaries and healers in Fargrave will appreciate that.

Daedra spend centuries developing techniques. They'd teach the Scamps to sing before giving Ravam pointers.\n\nYes, he probably could use the materials, but I know Ravam, he'll study whatever you bring back too.

Good. You will need that conviction in order to emerge victorious. Do not let your stance waver, even for an instant. If you allow yourself even a shred of weakness, Mehrunes Dagon will exploit it. Of that, you can be certain.

If anyone had told me a tale of marching on Destruction's Solace with a band of mortals led by a daedrat calling itself Arox the Multilator, I would have laughed at the absurdity of their tale. Are you ready for this journey?
I will follow the orders Kynreeve Rynkyus issues, mortal. I fail to see why this is a concern for you.
Is there some benefit mortals derive from casual queries? Curious. I have heard that mortals ask questions even when they know the answer.\n\nRynkyus will be with you. That is enough.
I will never understand how you mortals face death with such confidence. A terrible battle awaits us within Destruction's Solace. Many will surely die. Yet your allies still stand by your side.
I know. I trust you. \n\nIt's hard, though. I still care for him. We were all each other had for a time. But I'm under no illusions. I know he's beyond saving. He's no longer the Sombren I once knew.
Pester Lyranth and Madam Whim until they devise a cure for my condition, of course. I may have patience, but that does not mean I care to remain a daedrat for one moment longer than necessary!

Lyranth has been a bad influence on me. I confess I am curious about your doings. Mortals, that is. I think I will follow you for a time and see what else befalls you in this realm.\n\nWho knows? You might find something else that can break my curse.

You do not know as much about Daedra as you think, master. We are patient, for time is on our side. In some century to come I will find another way to break this curse.\n\nBut even if I do not, our triumph over Valkynaz Nokvroz lives forever.

Many of my Kyn fell. Most of them, in fact. We were sorely outnumbered by Valkynaz Nokvroz's forces. But I do not grieve, mortal.\n\nThose whose bodies were destroyed in Ardent Hope will return soon enough. And every Bladebearer fell with honor.

Our feud with Nokvroz and his minions is over. Those of my Kyn who suffered at his hands have been avenged, and the tale of our wrath will be told far and wide.\n \nBut I shall be keeping an eye on Mehrunes Dagon's forces from now on. Just in case.

No Kyn goes willingly into the dark, mortal. We fight hard to stave it off, just as you would. And I will miss my clan-brothers and clan-sisters until they return. Some I will see again soon. Others I may not see again for a Prince's age.

Mehrunes Dagon juggles schemes within schemes. All Daedric Princes do. We may have put an end to Valkynaz Nokvroz's part in that, but what other plans does he have in mind for her? \n\nHe addressed her directly and by name, after all.

No, not that. The plan to turn Dremora into incarnations of destruction died with Sister Celdina and Valkynaz Nokvroz.\n\nBut the power the Anchorite demonstrated in Ardent Hope? That still exists. I suspect Dagon covets it for reasons of his own.
How like a mortal to ask a question like that.\n\nThe treasure itself is an enigma, it only retains its value when the contents are unknown. Once it's opened, the items inside become worthless.

Uxark made many treasure hoards. She conquered the armies of Shaeofasa Bloodletter and lived after fighting Molag Bal. \n\nUxark slew Koth twenty times with his own war axe and collected a treasury larger than any other from the ashes of Arms Reach.

I am not obligated to tell you that. Consider my place of work and extrapolate the answer from those lines of thought. \n\nDiscretion is a staple of Madam Whim's business, I will not give away the sources or avenues of my information that quickly.

Why wouldn't we want to possess such a powerful mystery?\n\nThe opportunity to recover Uxark's treasure presented itself, Skoedal is back from Oblivion, and it won't be long before the rest of Uxark's clan returns too. This is the moment.

I cannot discern the point of this question. \n\nI am a Bladebearer. My Kyn are of the Bladebearer clan. I presently serve Kynreeve Rynkyus. That is how it has always been. You ask such stupid questions.

If you offended me, I would challenge you. Wasting time on meaningless queries merely tries one's patience. I wouldn't waste a sword swing on such trivialities.\n\nThe kynreeve is waiting for you. Show some respect and move on.

Blood and coins, no. The Arms Reach treasure has been greatly cataloged. \n\nUxark only hinted at this one on her death bed. She said there was a plane within a plane where she hid the most resplendent treasure known to immortality.

It's the only teleportation spell that can be used reliably to transport goods and people to Fargrave from the other planes without the need of a portal key. \n\nOthers aren't reliable and you're likely to end up stuck between realms or missing an arm.

Good. \n\nI won't be ungrateful and say that you took too long, so I'll just settle with saying that you did a better job with this important task than that other group. I plan to make sure they never work again.

I've battled Mantikora before. I've seen them kill. They never take a life quickly. It ruins their fun.\n\nSince the drugged prisoners were left outside its lair, the Mantikora hasn't had the thrill of hunting them yet. Trust me, they're alive.

Thank Vehk! I was so worried about you and the prisoners. What if I sent you out there with the wrong antidote? But I don't have to worry about that now. Thank you. Oh! Don't forget to see Sera Indavel. I'd hate for you not to get paid for your work.

No, of course not. He'll squirm, and curse, and prevaricate until I banish him. But even a lying tongue tells some truths. He will give something away. He always does.\n\nI only wish the process wasn't so tiresome.

I thought we could trust Sombren, but he was hurting Calia. I had to make him stop. So I … sent him away.\n\nGetting these powers, it feels just like when my memories returned. I know they're mine, but they're not familiar.

Is that what it's called? He keeps it close. Never lets it go. He thinks the answers are in there. In there and with Mehrunes Dagon.\n\nNear the end, Sombren decided to just take our powers. I was too slow to stop him. Poor Calia.

Sombren wasn't making any sense. He kept trying to convince us to go with him. He's obsessed with the power and he thinks Mehrunes Dagon is the only one who can help us learn how to use it.\n\nHe kept quoting passages from that damn book.

I think so. He said we weren't worthy of them. When I said I wouldn't go with him, he got so angry, like I was the one betraying him. I don't think he wanted to hurt me. He kept saying he was doing this to protect me. But he's so angry, so obsessed.

How could it have been? Destron's dead. We both saw what happened to him. But even creating a copy … that was too cruel.\n\nI've already lost Destron once. I didn't need to see that again. And now I've lost Sombren. I just feel … empty.

Do I know the truth? Some things still remain hidden. I know who my mother and father were, yes. But I don't recall much about my childhood. I couldn't tell you where I grew up or who raised me.\n\nAnd I don't know what Mehrunes Dagon wants with me.

For now, I'll stay in Fargrave. There's work to do here—people who still need my help. And I think it's time that I got to know Mairead.\n\nShe's a part of me, even if I'm more comfortable as the Anchorite.

I can't rest yet. There are still pieces missing from the puzzle of who I am. I think I'd better find them before I face Mehrunes Dagon again. \n\nWhere will that take me? Who knows? No matter what, I'm still the Anchorite. I like who I've become.

For now. The Stricture should keep Dagon's Daedric servants from causing too much trouble, but I'm sure the Waking Flame cultists aren't the only mortals who do his bidding.\n\nWell, let them come. This is my city. And I'm not helpless.

You're right. Fargrave offers some protection, at least. Mehrunes Dagon's Daedric servants can't violate the Stricture. But I can't hide from the Prince of Destruction forever, and I don't really want to try.

You … are a tricky one. I don't care for a torchbug's admiration, but you show some Daedric qualities. \n\nAll right, child. Let's strike a bargain—like honorable Daedra. Bring me Vein Splitter, my sword, and I'll tell you what you want to know.

Child, is my blade sharp? Are my markings that of a warrior? Is there dirt from multiple planes stuck between my toes?\n\nI am Skoedal. My name and reputation are well known among the Daedra. None would dare doubt me.
Good, we have an agreement. \n\nNow I don't have to speak to your fresh face until you return with Vein Splitter.

You have served me well and I have a certain fondness for you, mortal, but do not presume that we are friends. Dremora have no need of such things. And I will not share my secrets with you. They are mine and mine alone.\n\nLet us talk of other things.

And they are both fools. Let me mark the portal's location for you.\n\nYou have done me a free favor, mortal. When Uxark reforms, I'll know where the treasure is. We can reclaim it in bloody glory. I can't wait to cut Madam Whim down!
You are not wrong in your summation, but we are not without avenues to explore.\n\nRemember the broken sword hilt you found at Burning Gyre Keep? It carries the mark of the Bladebearers clan.

No. The worth of Uxark's Hidden Treasure's is dependent on the mystery of what it is. Even speculating about what is in this container could lower its price. \n\nYou'd be wise to stop with that line of thought.

Danger is a matter of perspective. The price of a life is cheap when most return from Oblivion no worse for the trip.\n\nIf that bothers you … hopefully you'll never have cause to need my or Madam Whim's assistance.
Move onto my next assignment. I already have multiple Daedra and a few potentially qualified mortals lined up for retrievals.\n\nWe'll see if any of them are up to the task.

The Anchorite has demonstrated the ability to survive whatever hardships come her way. She will sort out her memories and come to terms with her parentage, eventually.\n\nAnd she should be safe here in Fargrave. The Stricture will see to that.

There are still sects of the Order of the Waking Flame active in the mortal world. In Blackwood, for instance. They have secrets that interest me, so that is where I will go next.\n\nAfter we have concluded our business here, of course.

The Bladebearers are a Dremora clan who forge their own path. They have no allegiance to Mehrunes Dagon, so I find it curious that their crest was found on a broken sword in the keep.\n\nI want to determine their involvement. With your aid, of course.

As a guess, it might be a stronger, more potent version of a nymic. If we gain access to it, we might be able to weaken Mehrunes Dagon. Perhaps even banish him to the darkest corner of the Deadlands, as the Longhouse Emperors intimated.

Besides the pompous name? Not much. Before this job I had never heard of them. They claim to be influential people from each alliance who oppose the Three Banners War, but membership is anonymous.\n\nThis is the first I've heard of them taking action.

There's not much more to tell than I already explained. I was hired to recover Jakarn and what he was carrying after he never arrived at his destination. I tracked him and his captors here. Now we're going to finish the job so I can get paid.

Kaleen. Captain Kaleen. Freebooter most days, privateer for the Daggerfall Covenant for the rest.\n\nAnd no, this isn't a mission for the Covenant, though it does seem to be related to the Alliance War.

Turning trouble into a profit and aiding the Daggerfall Covenant as best I can, as usual. And pulling that idiot Jakarn's arse out of the fire more often than I'd like. I'd leave him to roast, but that sweet talk of his does drum up good leads.
Yes and no. \n\nThere are strange wisps about, we have been following them. When I touched one, I saw an apparition of the Dremora.

Who said I killed them?\n\nIt was a group effort and the last beast took a chunk out of me that's still healing. Be on your guard when you face this one and hope your fellow adventurers are good at what they do.

It can be. Depends on which types of Daedra we're talking about. Thanks to the Stricture, most such negotiations here in Fargrave remain at the hypothetical level. A battle of words and posturing to determine dominance.\n\nIt's almost ritualistic.

Kind of. More like arbiters that maintain the peace among the Daedra. They have no love of mortals, however. Since we're not bound by the Stricture, they consider us with suspicion and even outright hostility. They're sure we're guilty of something.

It's a code of sorts. A magical covenant that binds the Daedra and allows them to operate in neutral territory without the need for a centralized leadership. When the bounds of the covenant slip, that's when the Grasp of the Stricture steps in.
Me? Ha! If I ever needed to send an adventurer out, I'd just go myself. \n\nIt wasn't too long ago when I was in your position, taking assignments from someone else.

I learned that walking away from an enemy doesn't mean that you don't lose too.\n\nThe planes are filled with the worst monsters and creatures the Princes can think of. Don't take these challenges lightly.

You didn't know? Taupezu Azzida got it in its head that its food should be cooked. So, its venom does just that. It cooks the victim from the inside out.\n\nI loved challenging intelligent beasts. They were always so interesting.

Since it was a Daedric caravan, I'm thinking that they weren't carrying mortal goods. Maybe they have skeins of Void Cloth. Ooh! It could be Xivilian steel!\n\nRaw materials are worth more in Fargrave, since most of our imports are finished products.

Aye. The sort of trouble you could probably lend a hand with, eh? Not that I'm telling you what to do, mind!\n\nAs long as you get around to my business eventually, you can cross swords with ancient evils all you like!
Ha! Does a shalk go mad on birckle moss? It … it does. Go on.
Is that right? Well, go on. I'm all ears!

I managed to squeeze through some cracks in the reef while you had the yaghra's attention. Nearly drowned twice, but I found a way under the perimeter. Good thing too. That door was barred from the other side.

I doubt the Ascendant Order would be keeping a prisoner close to the fighting. He'll be deeper in the ruins. Not sure where, but with any luck I can sniff him out. Jakarn wears his cologne like he bathes in it.
Of course! I'd love to hear all about it!
Me? Oh, I used to be a thief, but now I use my expertise to find talent and coordinate jobs for our clients.\n\nBesides, I love talking to adventurers. New arrivals and long-timer Fargravians alike.

Well, it's not something you can just apply for. Invitation only, you understand. And that invitation has to come from one of the higher-ups, such as our founder, Pieron Desant.\n\nBut the first step is to make a good impression.

Aren't they beautiful? One of our best features. No one is quite sure who or what they were, but legend has it they once carried the city from plane to plane—hence the allusion to a palanquin. Is it true? Well, the skeletons are real enough.

Hot? In the Shambles? Must be the old baths. The furnaces beneath the bathhouse have been burning forever.\n\nBut what was that about the votive runes? How does Sister Celdina plan to use them to conquer Fargrave?

From what I could devise, the votives elevated the emotions of mortals in the city, siphoning the energy generated into Sister Celdina's ritual. She planned to use that energy to destroy the Daedra, including the Grasp, leaving the city defenseless.

The Stricture recognizes the destruction of Daedric property as a crime, but since the only loss was a mortal life, a fine is considered acceptable recompense.\n\nIf you pay it, I will consider the matter finished.
You had to …? Before I could examine it? Did you at least take a close look at the device? Or bring back any of its component parts for me to study?
So we have nothing? Nothing I can investigate, no one I can interrogate? I am disappointed, mortal. Now I must start all over again.

Deadlight? That name is familiar. A lost realm somewhere in Oblivion. We need to return to Fargrave. Make inquiries. Locate this hidden place.\n\nMeet me at Madam Whim's, little mortal. Perhaps my investigations will yield answers after all.

Sending you to Master Rrvenk would be akin to farting downwind. I wouldn't inflict your odious odor on my worst enemy, let alone a Daedra of his esteem.\n\nWhatever your troubles, they'll be over soon. Your smelly existences are mercifully brief.

I just want to fish without your fetid meat-musk burning my nose. You can go pick apocalypse seeds from an End Times ash tree for all I care. Actually, that's perfect. Go get me a seed. I think there's one out in those burning wastes.
I want you to go away, but some shade would be nice—wait, stop that. I don't need to explain anything to you, fart wisp. Just blow away and vanish like the leaves of an End Times ash.

Ah, ha ha. You must be utterly baffled by the concept. Just sitting and waiting for something to occur with patience. As quickly as you expire the mere idea must appear ludicrous. How utterly pathetic.

What don't I have against you? You mortals are like an irritating itch. There long enough to be a nuisance, but nothing of any lasting consequence. The pointlessness of your existence offends me. Why any Daedra have an interest in you is beyond me.
Be warned. Physical injury is a certainty for mortals undergoing the Constrictions. You are warned, mortal.
Madam Whim does not permit me to administer the Constrictions of Moath on Nirnlings at too frequent an interval. Dead patrons offer her some value, but living ones offer her more.
I've seen the tide wash him up in worse shape. He'll be fine. I just wouldn't count on him to pull his weight. Not that he could to begin with.

That name belongs to an Elf who ran a fleet of ships for the Veiled Heritance. Heard all sorts of tall tales about how he terrorized the Aldmeri shipping lanes. Some claimed he used gryphons to swoop down and shred the sails of his victims.

All I know is my employer said it was imperative to deliver them to someone in Summerset, discreetly. No one was supposed to know I was even carrying them.\n\nI don't know who these Ascendant Order people even are, but they're well informed.
