One moment I was enjoying a leisurely voyage to Summerset on a cushy merchant vessel—courtesy of my employer—the next I'm being dragged through this ruin with a thundering headache.\n\nThere was this noise, I think, before it all went dark.

Fortunately, they needed to me to talk, so I've still got all my teeth. It would have been a real tragedy if they'd ruined this face, right?\n\nA beer, or three, and a good night sleep and I'll be right as rain.

When we first met, you asked about my name. Madam Whim gave it to me. I just arrived in Fargrave, and everything before that exact moment was … gone. All I had was this mask. I didn't know who I was or where I came from.\n\nStill don't.

Just one of Madam Whim's little jokes. Means I'm a recluse, a hermit. Living a life of seclusion behind a mask I can't remove.\n\nSometimes … sometimes it feels like memories are stirring deep inside my mind. When that happens, I need a distraction.

Because it feels like there's a war raging inside my skull. A war I can't win. Better to drink or … or whatever. Push them back down to stop the pain behind my eyes. That's my story, at least as much as I know.\n\nNow tell me what Madam Whim said.

Bits and pieces, but when the memories stir, the pain kicks in. If I try to focus on them, actually make sense of them, the mask … burns? It hurts me. Like it doesn't want me to remember.\n\nSomeday I'll look into those blank spaces, but not today.

Another label assigned by Madam Whim. Stay in her orbit long enough and you'll collect a dozen appellations. I can't stand to see anyone go hungry or be taken advantage of. I try to help and don't ask anything in return. Whim sees that as a weakness.

If we want a seed, we need it to sprout. That's impossible while it's dead, but I think we can encourage it to change if we provide it with the right catalysts.\n\nI'll try conjuring some elements. If I can manage that, you can apply them to the tree.

An audacious plan. Mehrunes Dagon has swallowed mortal realms before. Or at least a portion of them. Such as this settlement you see before you. You are fortunate that their plan failed.\n\nWhat brings you to the Deadlands now? Vengeance?

Strange. The Bladebearers I sent in search of the missing Kyn reported rumors of a dangerous mortal device of some sort. Then they disappeared as well. Perhaps they encountered the Waking Flame.\n\nTell me about these Incarnates.

We could, but I'm not quite to the point of risking my entire existence on blind experimentation. I believe Rrvenk is still my best hope of returning to a stable state. Provided we can convince Morah to help us find him.
Of course. Gold begets gold, living one. Unlike the madam, Nzerru provides no free samples—he will summon the prized substance from the most valuable of sources.
An apocalypse seed? How did you …? I honestly thought you'd wander off and die before the new seedlings took.\n\nAnd you just brought this to me? Why would you do that? I made no pact with you.

I suppose you demonstrated you aren't completely useless, and you muffled your overpowering stench. Fine, I'll help you to find Master Rrvenk.\n\nSeek out Shiro-dar in the Fleapits District of Wretched Spire. He was the last mortal to see the master.

Hey! No peeking! I was hired in confidence, for my discretion. My employer might be willing to forgive me if I can convince her that the only people who ever saw this letter won't be speaking about it ever again.
It asks me to betray the laws of commerce. Typical.\n\nA sale is a covenant between merchant and patron. If it wishes to learn the particulars, it should ask Divayth. That is my final word.

Living one, your interest is obvious, palpable. But the Golden Panacea writhing within you must be left unmolested to work out its euphoria. Were you to imbibe further, you would be quite overtaken by the brilliance, unto what you call death.

You … don't? That one, the ghost, she said the same—but Gilfrex has his tricks! His thugs hunt this one, like an animal. Shiro-dar does not know you, so he thought you among them.\n\nIf you are not with Gilfrex, what do you want with this one?

Oh, if you were to get Gilfrex off Shiro-dar's tail, that would make you much more agreeable in this one's book.\n\nShiro-dar is greatly in debt, but what Gilfrex asks for is beyond what this one can deliver. Perhaps you can remedy this?

Morah? The Daedra who is most rude? To hear it from her, this one's fragrance would befoul all the corners of Oblivion. Never has Shiro-dar been so insulted!\n\nSorry. Shiro-dar is too busy fleeing for his life to be of much help.
Great Vruxynbu is a magnanimous being, fellow mortal. But even so … even one so gracious as he must collect a tithe for the lustration, for the sake of the House of Whims.

It is with … it is with immense lament that Great Vruxynbu cannot accede to your request. It is the nature of our mortal spirits to wither if too well treated. Those that experience the lustrations of Great Vruxynbu must wait to experience it anon.

It is addressed to some despicable cur named Sister Celdina. A weak-sounding mortal name if ever I heard one! Why one of Mehrunes Dagon's most powerful warlords—not as powerful as Arox, mind you—would deign to aid a weak-named mortal baffles me.

Right to the chase? I hate that. I like to watch the needy squirm. Shiro-dar, for example. Big squirmer. You, not so much, I suppose. Is that why the cat sent you? As muscle? Raw deal. You'll never collect.\n\nEither way, I'm getting what I'm owed.

Yes, right. Ahem. "Troops stand ready at Burning Gyre Keep. Send word when Fargrave's defenses fall and the invasion will begin. Dremora blades will take the city, not your Incarnates."\n\nThat is every word, mortal master whose name is in no way weak.

The cat promised he could get me a little item called the Slave Choker from False Martyrs' Folly, but he was all talk. If I don't have that collar by the time I find the cat, I'll make one out of his tail.\n\nUnderstand?

When I get what I'm owed, the cat becomes your problem. Do what you will with him.\n\nFalse Martyrs' Folly is across the wastes to the east. Try not to get killed out there or we'll have to rename it after you.

It's not getting me any closer to the Slave Choker, that's for sure. Fine, I've wrung enough fear out of the cat these last few days to have my fill. It's overpowering the more subtle miseries I savor.\n\nHis debt is cleared. Now go.

The mangy cat's been trying to change his fortunes since he landed in Wretched Spire. Someone talked him into believing he could, so he came to me looking for a job. Then he backed out.\n\nFeh. Once a coward, always a coward.

Because it does what it sounds like it does, and it'd save me the trouble of chasing down debtors like your friend. See, I put it on someone and give them a task. Every day they fail to complete the task, the collar gets a little tighter.

Gryphon pedigrees, promissory notes, coded communications. Nothing relating to Jakarn's business. Our employer might have some idea how to make use of this information. So long as they're willing to pay for it.

Oh, it's nothing really. I need a crate picked up from the east side of town. Near the, uh … the Outlaws Refuge.\n\nI'd go get it myself, but some scallywags might recognize me. The sort of scallywags that like breaking auctioneers' kneecaps.

No! I'm just a lowly auctioneer. Sure, I hear things from time to time. But Daedric artifacts? That's the sort of thing we're all better off forgetting!\n\nThen again, there is that errand I mentioned. That might rattle something loose.

Zzavfa! There's no need for that! I was … I was just joking!\n\nA couple of Skaafin showed up not long ago. Said they had to stow it away in the Hexos gallery vault. In the Shambles. Just don't tell anyone I told you, all right?

So you have! And what do you know, a memory popped into my head just then!\n\nA couple Skaafin picked up the sword not long ago. Said they had to stow it away in the Hexos gallery vault. In the Shambles. Just don't tell anyone I told you, all right?

I just need a crate picked up from the east side of town. Near the, uh … the Outlaws Refuge.\n\nI'd go get it myself, but I owe some of those rascals quite a bit of gold. If I can't pay in coin, they'll take payment in broken bones, you see?
This collar sounds like some sort of Daedric relic with magical properties. I might be able narrow down its location. If I notice anything, I'll be sure to inform you.
Huh. You come in here with confidence, get right to business, make promises, and keep them. It just sucks all the fun out of extortion.\n\nMakes me wonder why I even bothered.
Oh, very well. Just leave the collar and get out of here. You're setting a bad example for my minions and drudges.\n\nFeh.
Gilfrex forgave it? Gilfrex never forgives anything. Perhaps Master Rrvenk was right. This one's fortunes can change for the better. Perhaps, next time, it will even be Shiro-dar who changes them.

This one will mark the place on your map. He is certain you will find the stubborn one and Master Rrvenk there!\n\nUnless Rrvenk has already convinced Hyxo and they have both moved on … no, no. Shiro-dar is sure you are meant to cross paths!

Well, you see, this one does not know the master's ever-shifting path, so he cannot say for sure. But he does know that Master Rrvenk planned to visit a new disciple … or disciple-to-be, rather. Hyxo, a skeptic of the master's ways.
The Grasp will release the daedrat once the offended party has been appeased. \n\nPerhaps if you grovel for forgiveness, Lucinia Portius will allow his release.

Master of lies! Rrvenk says even stone softens when needed. Nonsense. Things made strong are strong. Things made weak are weak.\n\nProve the strength of his words. Otherwise Rrvenk is nothing to me. And so are you.
You aren't … unless there is truth in Rrvenk's words. If there is proof to be found, you will find it near the Dremora outpost to the west.\n\nNow go. Die to the strong, maggots.

Ugh, how pitiful. I've had Scamps who could grovel better than that!\n\nFine. I have little patience for the Grasp and even less for this whole ordeal. You and your pet are quite lucky that I'm in a generous mood. Just take it and go.
Hmm. Hmm … it is as Rrvenk said. Strong becomes weak. Weak becomes strong. Change is inevitable.\n\nThese stones prove the strength of his words. I did not understand him. Now I do.
Rrvenk awaits you to the south.\n\nGrow, maggot. Into something strong.

A simple disagreement, really. But then the mortal insulted my honor. Called me vermin! The impertinence! I had to respond. That kind of insult cannot be ignored, not in a place like the Shambles. \n\nSuch conflicts happen quite often here.

Ah, well, taking the life of a mortal with ties to a prominent Daedra is not quite as common, unfortunately. The Grasp involves themselves in such matters.\n\nApparently, this particular mortal had a powerful master. My mistake.

This is Fargrave, a city in Oblivion with permanent and open connections to other realms. The cultists place those votive runes faster than I can destroy them, putting every mortal who lives here at risk. That's why I agreed to meet with the Dremora.

Lyranth the Dremora. She sent me a letter. Said the cult threatened Fargrave. Nirn, too. She wanted my help, but I can't deal with that now. The votive runes are clearly the immediate danger.\n\nWe should work together on this. I can pay.
I—I don't know. I'm stretched so thin. Just holding onto some semblance of reality all this time has been exhausting. I don't think I can go on fighting like this much longer.
If a master of the Eleventh Force can't fix this, what hope do I have? I can barely think straight anymore! If you have any brilliant ideas, I'm open to suggestions.

I'm afraid I don't remember much else from skimming through my guide to this realm. Not that it'd do me much good when my fingers would pass right through it.\n\nThis is a plane of natural disaster, but it may imitate life as we know it.

That's right. She came to me after she got word that the Jakarn's ship was attacked. She thought I could be trusted, since I have history with Jakarn. That much is true, even if she's otherwise a poor judge of character.

I'm close to everyone, just closer to some more than others. It's my gift of charisma—sometimes a curse when jealousy rears its ugly head. I saw this lady in need and did what I do best.\n\nNow she has more to be satisfied with than just my company.

Ordinator Nilera? She defended the Temple in Mournhold when Mehrunes Dagon attacked the city. I remember hearing the sounds of her battle.\n\nMany in Mournhold revere her as the greatest Ordinator to ever serve the Tribunal.

Didn't you hear me? Everyone thinks Ordinator Nilera was the greatest Ordinator to ever live? Not saving her? I'd fail in my mission. You—the other members of the Tribunal would despise me. Everyone in Mournhold would shun me!\n\nIt would be awful!

Oh, yes. I was—I was hiding in the temple while Mournhold burned. \n\nOrdinator Nilera was standing on the steps outside with her shoulders back and her head held high. It was a striking sight for the short time I saw it.

She was a priest at the temple. When Ordinator Nilera died fighting Mehrunes Dagon, she rushed outside and picked up Nilera's sword. \n\nShe—she wasn't very good at fighting. But she managed to hold the horde back until you and Almalexia arrived.

My family would shun me. My ancestors would desert me!\n\nAnd not just Grandmother Sovisa, all of them could leave me. That may not seem like much, but being out of favor with your own ancestors? I could lose everything!

Ahem … probably not. Mortals are delicate about such things.\n\nThe Blood Pit is a cruel place, master. Prince Dagon sends his enemies there to suffer. Mortal prisoners do not last long, unless they are valuable in some way.
Let us hunt, master!

Free just one of them? How could I even begin to make the decision between the two? I'd be saving one and dooming the other to an eternity of torture at the hands of Mehrunes Dagon!\n\nWait, would you make the decision?

I find it hard to believe a mortal such as yourself is ignorant of such a substance. Your kind are always scrabbling for it.\n\nRedmaiden is a drug. When regularly ingested, it can anchor a mortal to Fargrave just as a pact with a Daedra would do.

Redmaiden is a rare commodity, and difficult to produce. Mortals would tear each other apart for it if it was not strictly regulated. Not every mortal contracts the Drain. But many fear the very possibility, and will do anything to acquire the drug.

To prevent a sickness called the Drain. Your mortal minds are not meant for the complexities of Fargrave. Occasionally, mortals experience … decay. Some become violent, others begin to drool. Ultimately, they will succumb to it and die.
I am—I was—a member of the Undaunted. The last job my group accepted was from a fellow Wood Elf named Fingaenion. He hired us to rescue his wife from the Deadlands.

I … separated from the others in the chaos. Fingaenion's wife Gilraen rescued me before I had the opportunity to do her the same favor.\n\nShe's an impressive fighter with an even more impressive dagger.

You slew Dagon's champion, the Valkyn. Gilraen has an … object precious to the Prince of this domain. Among those trapped here and resentful of Dagon, the tale is well told.\n\nThe thing Gilraen took, Dagon wants it back.

Gilraen's not the only one who can make life-saving deals. But that shouldn't concern you. You are an ally and friend while at this camp.\n\nSo please, feel free to use my fire or let me give you a blessing before you continue your travels.
Then I'll make my way there. \n\nThank you, stranger. You can't know what this means to me.

Gods, no. This is all my fault. She only went along with the plan for my sake. I got the Drain, and now she's dead because of it. She lost her life trying to save mine. It's not fair. \n\nI need to see Bakh. Please, where is he?

I guess that's up to you, isn't it? You hold our fate in your hands. You were decent enough to hear us out, so we'll comply with whatever you decide. \n\nBesides, it's my decisions that got us all into this mess. I shouldn't be making any more.

This damn sickness, it's different for everyone. Some people get by for years with just headaches. For others, it takes them in a few days. \n\nI keep forgetting things. Sometimes I wake up and I don't even know my own name. It's getting worse.

What, really? I don't know what to say. I could kiss you, or cry, or scream … but I'll save us both the trouble and just say thank you.\n\nYou've given me a fighting chance. All of this won't have been in vain. Thank you, friend.
You found it? Then … no, I suppose I won't be able to change your mind. I don't deserve it anyway. It's my fault we got into this mess. I should be suffering. It's only fair.

The Redmaiden we stole … it would have given me time, at least. Bakh insisted we had to get our hands on some when we found out I was sick, but we didn't think we'd get caught. \n\nMinwileth had it when we came here. Gods know where it is now.

There isn't a good word to describe me. I'm a stranded soul. A wandering fool. \n\nWho I am, I suppose, is a traveler much like yourself. Trudging ever onward to complete a duty I suspect is impossible.

I made a deal with a Daedra of some great importance. I'm not allowed to say more about the exact nature of the deal. Asking for assistance, he said, would be cheating. \n\nNevertheless, I must roam the Deadlands until I fulfill my side of the bargain.
No one can, don't feel too badly about it.\n\nThank you for at least hearing us out. That's more than most would have done.

My compatriots and I were hired to help a man rescue his wife from the Deadlands. She ran into a portal to save her village. With a disposition like that, she could easily have been one of us. \n\nStill, we underestimated the danger of this realm.
I am not much of a mage, but this has given me much comfort and protection in my travels. I hope you will find yourself similarly bolstered.\n\nSafe travels to you, wanderer.
I'm not much of a mage, but I picked this up in my journeys. Hopefully it does you more good than it did me.\n\nSafe travels to you, wanderer.

Do I detect some suspicion in your voice?\n\nIf we recover the Ebony Blade, I will do what I do with all the dangerous relics I acquire—keep it safe. I assure you, there is no one better equipped to safeguard a terror like this.

I know it doesn't look like much, but it's the best tavern in the Shambles. People come from dimensions away just to drink here.\n\nOk. Well people that drink here do come from many dimensions away. It just might not be specifically their destination.

Doesn't matter. Probably talk, like he always does. Ask questions. I'll lie. He'll cast his banishing magic. Won't last. Will come back before long. Start all over again.\n\nOnly ends when Fyr dies. And he will. Nirnlings always do.

I am not much of a mage, but this blessing has served me well in my travels. When you court death with every footfall, any measure of assistance is helpful. \n\nOh, and you are welcome to use my fire as well. Warm yourself in friendship.

I assume you're being glib. As I said before, I am Divayth Fyr, House Telvanni's most eminent scholar and Tamriel's most powerful mage.\n\nI cannot fault your ignorance. I've not been home in some time. My work keeps me in Oblivion more often than not.
I am an explorer. Not in the conventional sense, of course. I do not seek unknown shores. I seek knowledge, or the means to acquire it. That often means coming here to Fargrave.

Truthfully? I'd compare Fargrave to an anthill built atop a silver mine. Hordes of small-minded beings frittering about with no understanding of their property's value.\n\nIt would be amusing if it wasn't so sad.

Ha! Rest is a luxury the ambitious cannot afford.\n\nMy business in the Clockwork City, while important, accounts for only a fraction of my grand design. I have interests in realms across the Aurbis. Including this one.
Yes. There's much left to do in Sil's domain, and time is not on our side. We should return as soon as possible. Or should I say, as soon as this business with the Ebony Blade is concluded.

On my person? No, I know better than to wander the streets of Fargrave with an artifact like that jangling around in my pocket. But it is quite safe.\n\nI gave Sil my word I would keep it out of the Daedra's hands. I always honor my agreements.

Yes, but Destron was killed during the battle with the Order of the Waking Flame's high priest. Still, we kept Sombren and Calia out of Mehrunes Dagon's hands. Now they wander the Deadlands with the Mysterium Xarxes, learning to control their powers.

So you do remember? Yes, in that Oblivion realm, we learned about the cataclysts and the process for creating Incarnates before you destroyed the devices. And we met the Anchorite, heir to the Longhouse bloodline. Dagon seemed very interested in her.
Tephilaz makes his own choices. He is unbound just as I am. If he wishes to walk without me, then so be it. I would not stop him. Though, obviously, it was foolish.

A long time ago, I stole a vial of ink off the desk of the Saraathu Tong's Leader. Figured out pretty quickly that the only ones who could see the ink were the ones who worked for me. \n\nTrust me. The glow is as strong as the storms over Apocrypha.

I always have a plan, mortal. We will require allies for this. Rynkyus and his Bladebearers. And a way to get inside. The Waking Flame portal key will do … if we can attune it properly.\n\nAnd we need Arox. He should be familiar with Ardent Hope.

Portal keys, when properly attuned, can open paths where none existed before. But we require an expert for this.\n\nTalk to Madam Whim, little mortal. She likes you. Convince her to help. If we have to assault the front gate, then we've already lost.

Whatever you can bring me.\n\nLike I said, we haven't had many opportunities to study the venom. As far as I can tell, the poison courses throughout the victim's blood. It'll be everywhere by the time the victim … cooks.

Although that would be both useful and edifying, Arox is correct. My presence would be immediately evident anywhere within the confines of the Blood Pit. \n\nI shall have to rely on your skills. Alas.

I'm sure you are capable of asking questions. But neither of you are Dremora, and your interrogation techniques are … limited. Most mortals are disinclined to robustly extract the needed information.\n\nNevertheless, I will rely on your skills.

Sister Celdina and the Waking Flame have attempted to neutralize me before. They warded this portal with a spell that will unravel my current body. Remember, I cannot die. Not like you. But I can be inconvenienced by the process of reformation.

This one has heard stories of the Daedric Princes her whole life. Zainan could not pass up an opportunity to finally see one, yes?\n\nWe have not seen Merrunz yet, but Skriliaa promises to get us close.
I'm—I'm on a pilgrimage. There was some trouble, you see, and—ah, I shan't bore you with the details.

Just my sworn duty. They needed a guide and recent circumstances put me in a situation where I was required to provide that service.\n\nThey wanted to see the Deadlands. I'm showing them the Deadlands.

Mages or scholars will tell you that Nirnborn cannot comprehend the magics and grandeur of Fargrave. But I think our minds know that we're not supposed to be in a half-way space. \n\nWithout a pact to anchor us, the Drain will claim us all.

They are. Most of us mortals are all right. There are organizations who have pacts with powerful Daedra. But plenty of pactless mortals resort to a substance called Redmaiden to keep their wits. \n\nAnyone who can't stay on Redmaiden … well.
I'm not exactly sure, but it helps stave off the effects of the Drain. All I know is, once you stop taking it the Drain comes back with a vengeance. \n\nIt's not a pretty sight.

That's true. But, I've seen what happens when the Drain sickness gets bad. The Drained forget to eat. I'm a cook. I feed people. So, I've been feeding them. When I can. \n\nSpend enough time with people and you'll be able to see their problems better.

I would much prefer to examine an intact cataclyst. If I cannot dispel the ward, I will simply travel to Nirn and find you. It will just take time.\n\nDeal with Sister Celdina and the Waking Flame as you must. But do not destroy the cataclyst.

Anything that stands out. Better if you can find notes or bring me a piece of the device. Whatever will help me understand how it somehow transforms Daedra who are supposed to be unchangeable, eternal.\n\nNow go.

There are things I still need to learn, mortal. If you feel you must destroy it, then do as I ask and examine it first. Tell me everything you see.\n\nBut if the danger is not immediate, leave it intact so I may study it directly.

A key? Yes, that might come in handy. Can I just say how refreshing it is to find competent allies? A rare luxury, I assure you.\n\nMake your way to the Shambles. There's a Hexos storehouse near the center of the district. Check there first.

Hrmph. Magic from a distance, then? I saw no scorching from fire. Cursed object maybe? No, pockets were empty. Let's hope Miksotet reveals more.\n\nWhy did he leave the Daedric area? He preferred not to upset the mortals.
He frequents the Wishbone—a tavern in the Shambles' northern alleys. Let's pay him a visit, shall we?

No, no. They're traders, not artisans. This is Daedric precision.\n\nI know a Spiderkith. Skrix. He's a small-time scoundrel who deals in stolen goods, counterfeit soul gems, that sort of thing. He might be able to point us in the right direction.
I served Flame and Destruction once, but that time is over. I would not exchange my current circumstances for anything. No matter how annoying those circumstances may be.

As a Dremora, I'm bound to a higher order. Some bow to the liege they serve. Others hold nothing higher than their own word. \n\nThese mortals … coerced me. I can't deviate from what I agreed to, no matter how badly they try my patience.

Another mortal under my wing? No, I don't think so. Besides, the Spike Pits and Scamp Breeding Grounds were chosen specifically for these two. So many options to choose from when survival isn't part of the contract.\n\nNow, we must be off!

You might know him as Mehrunes Dagon. A smoothskin name. Merrunz is his true nature. The fiery kitten of destruction and chaos!\n\nReligion has always fascinated this one. When the chance to visit the Deadlands presented itself, Zainan couldn't refuse.

Who raised you, Khajiit? A shaveskin? Everyone from Pellitine to Anequina knows that Merrunz is Mehrunes Dagon's true name!\n\nOur people tell so many legends about Fadomai's Litter. This one came to confirm what she can.

Meet? Well, Zainan would be happy if she only catches a glimpse of the majestic Merrunz. Think of the stories this one can tell her clan back home!\n\nBut, yes, a glimpse is more than enough to satisfy this one's curiosity.
Well, where else to submerge myself in the reality of the House of Troubles? I know my faith is strong enough to resist the flames of temptation, despite what those stupid Ordinators may think.

The Tribunal. The three Living Gods of the Dark Elves. And their unreasonable priest-soldiers, the Ordinators.\n\nIt wasn't my fault! I was … influenced by the forces of evil. With this pilgrimage, I'll show them all that I'm blameless. You'll see.
That's what the Tribunal calls the bad Daedra. Mehrunes Dagon is but one of the Four Corners, the Princes that constantly test the resolve of the faithful.

Precisely. I saw my friends fall and I lost confidence. I became daunted.\n\nStill, my tragedy does not concern you. All are welcome and safe at my fire. I can even give you a blessing to aid you in your journeys, if you wish.

Obviously not. I find it amusing when a mortal attempts to understand the workings of Oblivion.\n\nYou delayed this journey long enough. I plotted routes to more … thrilling locations. Locations that should test the limits of my enthusiastic charges.

For the usual reasons. Simple greed and fear of punishment.\n\nDaedra may not die, but the process of reconstitution is not pleasant. I can also make business difficult for him. For Skrix, losing wealth may cause more pain than losing his life.

No, but it feels familiar somehow ….\n\nForgive me, friend. I'm not ready to talk about Elegian yet. My heart breaks for the poor old owl and I need some time to think. You should tell Lyranth what we learned.

Threats, eh? With Fyr it's always threats. Skriddy Elf with big head and tiny wits.\n\nFine. Will cast a signal line for it. Finding ritual. Can find anything with it. After this, Fyr pays and you scuttle off. Final offer.
Calculations. Mostly. \n\nThere are some Dremnaken eyes that have gone missing. It's easier to convince Arns Farandas that something's missing if I show him where the numbers don't line up.
Smart.\n\nEnough talk. Put the sword on the table.
Then you're stupid.\n\nEnough talk. Put the sword on the table.
I pray you never have need to find out. Suffice it to say that it's insurance.\n\nEnough talk. Follow that spider. And don't take your eyes off Skrix. Not even for a moment.
Some people want to poison others and some people want to be unpoisoned. My teachers always said that a good poisoner could always undo their own work. \n\nPlus, I get double the business this way!

He might be able to explain how his Bladebearers came to be at Burning Gyre Keep. If Rynkyus knows more about the Waking Flame's activity in the Deadlands than we do, perhaps he can tell us where Sister Celdina and her device are hiding.

Then either Rynkyus knows about the involvement of his Kyn or he does not.\n\nIf he knows, then he is an enemy, and we may learn something by questioning him. If he does not know, then he is a potential ally—and a powerful one.

They'd leave their tortured undeath at the hands of the Prince of Chaos. But … I'd be stuck here. Alone. \n\nStill, I guess the spirits would be free and I'd have done my duty to them and the Tribunal. Is that what you want me to do?

Exactly what I'm doing now. Then I take the proof to the Tong leaders and let them deal with it. It's usually not a big deal. Most of the time goods go missing because Zirpar does the transmission spell drunk. \n\nNot much for an adventurer to do.

It happens more often than you think. \n\nI should just be handling the Saraathu Tong's finances. But, when you work for a group that transports items between the planes, those finances are tied to the goods. Missing goods mean missing funds.
Lose to a mortal? Me? Do you know how ignorant you sound asking questions like that? \n\nI am Erudolso, I haven't lost a battle since time began!
Time is of no consequence to immortals. If you're looking for a place to get blood on your blade, the Shambles are the place to go. When I see you there, we'll test your tongue against my steel.
My opponents would have to be alive for word to spread about my prowess. And my comrades in arms are too orderly to boast. Only those who are desperate to prove themselves boast.

That zzavfa happens all the time! I've taken my own antidotes so often that I voluntarily worked with a chef to improve the taste. My clients really enjoy that. \n\nI try to stay within earshot of one of the Tong guards though. It makes my day easier.

Not at all! Vares is an oddball, but he's pushed me to make so many new antidotes. Lavagild, Dagon's Choke, Miralis … and those are just the most recent ones. \n\nSome days, I'm convinced I have the best job on the Tong!

Trade or bartering usually works. Rayna Falas gives me a budget to use on my wares too, which is helpful. \n\nOh! And if Vares Dredayn is working on a new project, there's a good chance I'll be called in to help. His experiments tend to get wild!

As I say, it is a town covered in dirt and grime with little to recommend it. \n\nThe only quality in its favor is how Mehrunes Dagon completely ignores it. Never invades with his creatures or blasts it with a fireball. No idea why, but it is welcomed.

You will see once you enter town. Some time ago, Dagon caused havoc in my home of Mournhold. Ripped our temple right out of the ground and flung it here. And I came along with it.\n\nI miss the old city. Much nicer than here. Deadlands, indeed!

Ha! Well, there was one beautiful day when Vares tried to use magic to make a nail ….\n\nTo answer your question, other blacksmiths incorporate magic into their work, but smithing through magic? Daedric metalworkers can't even levitate a feather!

Wretched Spire hides Daedra. Can't get summoned while here. We like that. But mortals want us gone. That won't happen.\n\nTephilaz seeks a treaty. Removing him delays that. The mortals may try to purge Daedra in his absence. If so, they'll die.

She's right. Someone wants violence. I can't allow that. Don't know our protection's source. Chaos might end it. I need the mortals alive.\n\nProtect them. Speak to them for me. Learn what they know. And if lives don't interest you, I can pay coin.
Why does everyone ask that question like I did something bad? \n\nAll I did was change the color of the metal they were working on! The green armor looked dashing. Really.

I'm fairly certain they think I'm a lunatic! But I got into the Tong using my own skills and talent. They didn't. I'm doing something right. \n\nDon't worry, I have good memories of talking to the other Nirnborn smiths too.

I am still tenuously connected to this realm. I'm not even sure I'll be able to muster simple conjurations, but you and I are still relatively in phase. If all goes well, you can act as an intermediary and effect change on my behalf.
Arrived when the spire fell. Mehrunes Dagon flung him here. Hates Daedra now. Understandable.\n\nLeads the mortals' council. Opposes Daedra residence. Possible suspect.

Our existence can remain adversarial. Knives forever at our throats. Tension makes existence a burden, inefficient.\n\nOr, it can be beneficial. They provide a seat on the council. We offer protection from the Deadlands' many threats.
Tephilaz explained the situation. We will not leave. If the mortals attempt to force us, they will die. Simple.

Mortals. How did your kind make it into Fargrave when you don't know the rules? The Stricture? The Grasp? \n\nFine. The Stricture's the usual legal drivel. Don't damage Fargrave. Don't kill anyone who doesn't agree to it. That sort of thing.

Of course. The Stricture binds us—we're compelled to abide by it. You don't think any of us would be stupid enough to walk into a city without knowing the terms of entry? Even Ogrims mind their manners here.\n\nMortals, not so much.

Gaps. Loopholes. Places to foment discord. Dance a jig along the legal line. \n\nIt's easy for you mortals. You get to choose whether you abide by the Stricture. Daedra have to be a little more clever. And worry about the Grasp.

You got all the way here and you don't know who they are? They're the Dremora in charge of enforcing the Stricture. Closing the loopholes.\n\nIf you want to meet the Grasp, I have ideas. They'd make this city more … interesting.

I … don't know yet. I saw other mortals when I was in Wretched Spire, so there has to be other ways into this realm. I suppose I'll have to ask someone who's made the journey or find my own way back to Tamriel. It shouldn't be too hard. Right?

I'm not giving up on her. You and the others in the Tribunal tasked me with freeing two spirits from the Folly. I'm going to devote myself to figuring out how to save my grandmother. \n\nIt'll be hard. Maybe even impossible. But I have to try, right?

I'm not the brave one in my family. I'm not even competent and I'll likely have to adventure again, but I'm going to devote myself to figuring out how to save her.\n\nIt'll be hard. Maybe even impossible. But I have to try, right?
It's either that or get so scared that I can't move forward. Again.\n\nI just have to focus on making it back to Mournhold and stop being the s'wit that I am.
B'vek yes! I don't want to be here any longer than I have to. Did you see that six-legged creature back there? That thing was terrifying! I am leaving this realm as soon as I can.

I wanted to study the Eleventh Force, Change, within this realm of Oblivion. You see, Mehrunes Dagon is best known for his power of destruction, but that is merely a portion of his sphere of influence. All of his aspects are rooted in Change.

He is a well-known sage, though few besides his disciples have ever seen him. Rumors claim he's always in motion, which is fitting, but also makes tracking him down very difficult.\n\nMorah may be able to guide us to him though.
My feet are stilled for now. My path once led me where I was not welcomed. But I hope that the patron of all those blessed with dust on their boots still gazes fondly on me.

Who am I to know the will of the Divines? It is on me to show them my eternal devotion, but not to interpret their will. \n\nThere are worse places to make a life than Wretched Spire. I am hopeful for my future.

I wanted to see all the holy sites of the Divines, but there are those who take offense to visitors. I pray to Stendarr and the mercy he is known for that I will be able to resume my journey. If that is not his will, then so be it.

Apparently word spread faster than we thought. When I got here, there were already people gathered. Everyone knows what we did in Sundercliff. \n\nEveli's trying to muster the courage to say something to all of them, but she could use a little help.
Good, good. Now, let me prepare your way to the realms beyond Nirn.

Most likely it's where I left it. Seven Kynmarchers against one Xivilai usually has the odds in my favor. I beat them. Don't think I didn't. But they struck good blows.\n\nVein Splitter will be in their camp. It should be to the north of here.

It was Lyranth for certain, but only an echo of her. It must have something to do with the great power she is attempting to control. \n\nFollow the wisps, you'll understand what I mean. And keep me from having to face Madam Whim empty handed.

Everything I know about Deadlight is rumor and conjecture. It is a plane that suffered some great cataclysm in the ancient past. A realm forgotten and lost to time.\n\nI had hoped that Madam Whim would know more, but she claims the place is a mystery.

Interesting. The Bladebearer clan's scouts are indeed competent. Perhaps they can find the trail where we have thus far turned up nothing.\n\nVery well. Find Rynkyus and see what he has learned. Meanwhile, I have my own research to conduct.

My wish? Wretched Spire stays the same. Nothing changes. Nothing disrupted. Whatever power provides the protection for Daedra remains in place.\n\nWe cannot bring back the mortals. A complication, then. But I will work to fix that.

His father was leader. To keep the status quo, Tarvyn must take up the position. My people will not care. And we can appease any mortals who speak out.\n\nTarvyn will see the wisdom and agree, in time. Manipulable, that one.

What, you're investigating the death of a Dremora? Why bother? That creature will be back in a matter of days.\n\nHe came to push for the damned treaty of his. Wishes me to allow Daedra to reside here permanently. I refuse to allow it!

Newcomers tell me it was more than 600 years ago on Nirn. Only a few decades have passed for me. I can still remember the feeling of my stomach dropping as we lifted into the air.\n\nTime flows differently in Oblivion's embrace.

All of them, if the entire arcane defense matrix is to be restored, which it has to be if I'm going to free myself.\n\nLook, I know I'm asking a lot here, but you're my only hope. If you defeat the guardian, I'll make it so you can summon it yourself.

No sense standing on ceremony under the circumstances. You can call me Vitellia. I was the caretaker for the Dread Cellar. The prison's been abandoned for quite some time, so I was assigned to try to keep it from completely falling apart.

Those Waking Flame cultists and their Daedra happened to me. I managed to kill a few score of them, but they were too many and too willing to suicide charge through my destruction spells for me to fend off. So, here we are.

Tephilaz will be back! But then you showed up. I had to kill Vontan to protect myself. And my father wrote that decree. It would have been a war. The mortals, we would have all died! I couldn't let that happen. I didn't want to kill him but I had to!

Of course, it's my home. Or at least the closest thing I've ever had to one. But I'm excited to familiarize myself with Tamriel, there's so much I don't know.\n\nBesides, having Calia as a travel companion will be nice. We could both use the company.

Who knows? Maybe I'll find some new world-ending mess to get myself into. I've got a taste for it now!\n\nI'm going to miss you! But I'm sure our paths will cross again. The two of us never stay out of trouble for long.

There was a caravan moving through the Sever. We ended up in a city called, um, Fargrave. A group known as the Saraathu tong helped me get back to Tamriel from there. \n\nI said that you'd helped me in the Folly, I hope that was all right.
Oh, yes. I know. Obviously you're not the Magician. How could you be?\n\nBut, in the event that you are, your secret's safe with me. I promise.

Oh! I, uh. Selveni, of course Sotha Sil wants to know what you're doing here. \n\nMy lord, I was there when you saved Mournhold from Mehrunes Dagon. After I heard that you'd defeated him again, I wanted to congratulate you in person.

Ah. right. Of course. That would be silly. Why would a Living God come to help me in the Folly?\n\nYour secret is safe with me. I won't tell anyone that this is actually the second time you defeated Dagon.

Oh, I don't regret it for a second.\n\nI got to save my grandmother's spirit from torment. Sotha Sil himself helped me make the decision and I know I'm going to spend the rest of my life looking for way to free Nilera too.

Ah, right. Of course. That would be silly. Why would a Living God come to help me in the Folly?\n\nYour secret is safe with me. I won't tell anyone that this is actually the second time you defeated Dagon.
Uh, no. Not exactly. \n\nI was making my way back when I heard that you'd defeated Dagon, again. So I took a detour to join the celebration in your honor!

Is this a test? All … right. Ordinators are priest-warriors. They protect the temples of the Tribunal throughout Morrowind, including the great temple in Mournhold. It's their job to serve you and the rest of the Tribunal.

I don't know! We put the stones on the altar and then I prayed and a stone just exploded! \n\nIs Almalexia's power not compatible with the altar? Did Dagon figure out I'm not an evil cultist? Am I terrible at praying?

Originally, there were three stones. One to free Ordinator Nilera. One to free Grandmother Sovisa. And the last one was supposed to take me back to Mournhold. \n\nWithout that third stone, someone has to stay here—Sovisa, Nilera. Or … me.

Ordinator Nilera was the glaive of the Tribunal. And after Mehrunes Dagon's attack … well, I don't know anyone who'd say she wasn't the greatest Ordinator ever.\n\nFreeing her spirit from this … place, would bring peace to many.

Sovisa was … my grandmother. She was kind and smart. The sort of person who always pushed you toward compassion. \n\nShe was a priest at the Temple, not a warrior. But she saved so many from Mehrunes Dagon's horde when they attacked Mournhold.

I can't believe …. Is that what you—what the Tribunal wants from me? \n\nMaybe it's better than letting two spirits stay in eternal agony. But, Sotha Sil? I don't know if I can do that. Not even for Ordinator Nilera and Grandmother Sovisa.
You needn't worry. I'll be along soon enough.\n\nFair warning, the Shambles is a lawless slum—full of far worse things than mortal indigents. Prepare yourself.

What? To touch the sword? What exactly do you want me to say? The Ebony Blade is a Daedric artifact—a weapon of unspeakable horrors. It is decidedly not safe to touch. Nevertheless, we soldier on.\n\nNow, go on and pick it up.
I pay your salary.\n\nNow, enough stalling. Pick up the sword.

The long answer is that a mage of my caliber must always be cautious around items like this. If it bears a curse of arcane reversion, I could inadvertently kill both of us in a burst of magicka.\n\nI assume that's something you'd like to avoid.
I … well, I suppose I should be forthright considering your willingness to help me. I am Valsirenn of the Psijic Order. Let's not make a to-do about it, and kindly keep that tidbit to yourself.

Correct. Change is the most sacred of the Eleven Forces that govern reality. I thought observing it in such a pure state would provide insight into its influence over Mundus, but I underestimated its currents in the Deadlands. It's swept me away.

Are you suggesting I should have dragged half the order along on this expedition? Maybe held a symposium? I prefer to conduct my studies at my own pace, thank you.\n\nThough I did appear to underestimate how strong the Eleventh Force would be here.

That's a topic we could fill a symposium with, but suffice to say they're the Psijic's central beliefs, governing our understanding of the Eleven Forces of reality. Expanding our knowledge of those forces is what we devote our lives to.

A mystical, monastic society. We are devoted to the study of the Old Ways and mostly keep to ourselves these days. Those studies brought me here and led me into this current predicament. More exciting than another day in the library, at least.

Among other things. I'm out of sync with this realm, with myself. It seems that I've regained enough alignment to interact with you, but there's no telling how long I'll remain like this and I'd rather not become dispersed across time and space.
I suspected that might be the case. I have yet to meet a mortal who could curb their inquisitive nature.

Need? No, but it will make the attunement easier. Once a network of portal daises crisscrossed the Deadlands. The fortress was built around one of them.\n\nMost have been forgotten and are no longer utilized, but that doesn't mean the magic has faded.

I was not always the entrepreneurial Mazken who stands before you. Long ago, I played at amassing influence by pledging myself to the Daedric Princes. I learned many secrets during those dalliances, including ways into and out of secure locations.

Perhaps. But defeat does not mean the same thing to my Kyn as it does to you, mortal. Death is not the end for the Bladebearers—at least, not death in battle.\n\nFor what Nokvroz did to our clan mates, however, he must suffer.

Vengeance is an honorable goal. Besides, your best chance to rescue the Anchorite is for my clan to draw the attention of Ardent Hope. And ours requires you to deal Nokvroz a grievous blow.\n\nThis is how we tear down our foe, and I will see it done.

It is a vast fortress. Nokvroz does not personally oversee everything that goes on within its walls. But the Perfected Cataclyst, or the daughter of Emperor Moricar?\n\nThose are of vital interest to him. Nokvroz will guard them well.

We have the same chance we always have. And we will find a way.\n\nWhat you told me raises questions about the Anchorite that I must have answers to. And you do not want Mehrunes Dagon's plans to succeed. So we shall deal with Nokvroz. Together.
It is a very complicated place, beeko, but yes. Would you care to hear about the sights, or the culture?

They do? Oh, my … that somehow makes it even worse. There went the last vestiges of pity I held for you worthless creatures.\n\nAlas, I'll never be as cruel as whoever conceived of you reeking offal-bags.

I've observed her for some time now while trying to make contact. I think she's dissatisfied by more than just our presence. There's something more to this apocalypse seed business than she's willing to admit. It might help persuade her.

Morah mentioned End Times ash trees. I vaguely recall some trivial details from my travel preparations. I think I can identify one of those trees when I see it.\n\nMy present condition should actually make the search easier. I'll scout ahead.

I sent many individuals after many planestones. I would've been foolish not to. \n\nThe Deadlands are not …. civilized, for lack of a more accurate description. Even Daedra do not make it out of that realm intact.

I have no delusions about anyone's chances of survival out in the Deadlands, mortal or otherwise. Madam Whim only pays individuals for completed deliveries. There was no harm in letting a mortal attempt it.

I have suffered due to my own nature. I went to great lengths to ensure I wouldn't anymore. And, I will do everything it is possible to do in order to ensure I do not return to the state I was in before working for Madam Whim.

We are eternal and unchanging. After eons of experience, there is nothing new. I curb this plight with my involvement in Madam Whim's enterprise. My tasks are varied and my mind is kept busy by solving problems garnered throughout the realms.
It doesn't happen to everyone. Ogrims almost never experience the tortures of boredom. But, many Daedra do suffer from the stagnant nature of our existences.
She foolishly allowed her boredom to overrule her good sense and died because of it. That is not an uncommon occurrence among certain Daedra. Our boredom is often fatal.

I've heard it sounds a lot like waking up bleary-eyed in a misty morning. Or like a hangover. \n\nAll I can say is that being killed is an annoyance and an indignity that most Daedra would rather not undergo.
Existence. Death. Reformation. It continues from there. Reforming in Oblivion can take some time, but any Daedra who is killed will return to walk the planes.
Mortals' lives are finite. You expire and then that is all. Daedra follow different cycles.

They are heroes in Mournhold. They protected the innocent. Stood up for those who couldn't do it themselves. Fought a gigantic, four-armed Prince of Destruction. Sacrificed their lives for others. \n\nI can't live up to them!

Grandmother Sovisa died protecting me. Ordinator Nilera fought Mehrunes Dagon himself to keep me safe. The Tribunal—yourself included—sent me here to save their spirits!\n\nBut I am nothing like Sovisa and Nilera!

I—I am, aren't I? Are you saying that maybe it won't be that bad? \n\nI guess I have done a lot of things that I never thought I'd be able to do. Travel through the Deadlands. Go on a quest with a Living God. I can handle a little more time here.

Ordinator Nilera? She defended the Temple in Mournhold when Mehrunes Dagon attacked the city. I remember hearing the sounds of her battle.\n\nMany in Mournhold revere her as the greatest Ordinator to ever serve the Tribunal.

My grandmother served the Temple. When Ordinator Nilera died fighting Mehrunes Dagon, she rushed outside and picked up Nilera's sword. \n\nShe—she wasn't very good at fighting. But she managed to hold the horde back until you and Almalexia arrived.

A foolish group of mortals, nothing more. They have been in Fargrave for a few years, always skirting the lines of the Stricture and eluding the Grasp.\n\nThey are close friends and look out for one another. It makes them difficult to rein in.

No, they have never been so bold before. Perhaps they grew bored of petty theft and being a nuisance. I could not say. \n\nMany of their transgressions have been too small for the Grasp to interfere. Not this one.

Pynufax claims this shambling corpse is valid repayment for her debt to me.\n\nI told her I would accept a mortal as payment. The intent of my words was clear. I desired a living one. As much as one can desire something so crude.
Arbitrate? No, there will be no mealy-mouthed compromise. I summoned the Grasp to settle matters beyond protestation. They will rule in my favor.

Yes. The adjudicators of Fargrave's rules and customs. We derive these rules from the Stricture—a force few have dared to explore fully. The Grasp oversee all interpretation of the Stricture.\n\nAnd as I said, the Stricture is on my side.

Yes. And he is a fool to think so. Kaluzan made no mention of the mortal flesh's condition. His involving the Grasp doubly proves his weakness.\n\nHe demanded a mortal. He should count himself fortunate that I provided one that moves.

The Grasp do not respond gracefully to summons without merit. They will quickly rule in my favor and Kaluzan will be left to explain why he involved them in such a trifling matter.\n\nI am eager to see what punishment they apply.

Ah. You are mortal, so the distinction matters to you. No, it is not unfair.\n\nKaluzan needn't feed this mortal, or clothe it, or listen to its wretched sobbing about how it misses its family. He should be thanking me.

Dremora cannot shirk their debts. Unlike fragile mortals, the word of a Daedra binds for eternity. Nothing is more valuable or more viciously contested than an unpaid debt.\n\nKaluzan's accusation is a grave matter.
I will base my judgment on the flesh's utility. What tasks it can perform, what price its various organs might fetch in the marketplace, and so on.\n\nIt appears to be capable of movement.

I will determine the value of the payment based on the arcane intents of the Stricture.\n\nThe modest value of living mortals and dead mortals is clear. A dead mortal in this condition, however, is more difficult to appraise.

It possesses all its limbs. It appears to follow simple commands. Its smell is comparable to that of a living mortal.\n\nThen again, you mortals do place great value on your impoverished sense of self. Flesh deprived of this may be less valuable.
True. But its smell is only slightly more repellant than that of a living mortal. And it will not require disgusting mortal necessities, like food and warm clothing.\n\nSurely this is an improvement.

I turned my back for a moment and my bumbling servant wandered off. This mortal ran the creature through with a long-knife. Now, it is even less useful than it was before.\n\nI demand the Grasp find a suitable punishment for this crime.

This mortal has nothing of value. No connections—no favors to trade. And what meager debt can I extract from it? No, suffering is only suitable compensation for my inconvenience.\n\nI am sure the Stricture outlines an appropriate measure of torment.
A convenient excuse. The Grasp will show him no mercy.

Servant? It's a corpse, for Z'en's sake! It's not like it was polishing his silver and entertaining guests in the parlor. And it tried to eat me!\n\nI refuse to be punished for killing some feral creature that was already dead. How is this a crime?

Bah! The Grasp doesn't care about mortals. You think there are rules against killing a mortal in Fargrave? There aren't. And if they don't care about killing mortals, they definitely won't care about killing a zombie!\n\nThis is a waste of time.
Mortals killing other mortals is of little concern to the Grasp. But a Dremora's property was damaged. This demands retribution.
Correction for mortals is a delicate business given your fragility. So, the punishment must be something moderate. Slowly pulling the teeth from his skull one by one, for instance.
The Stricture demands compensation for the offended party. The punishment must fit the crime.
Cursed undead. The Stricture's demands on mortals past the point of expiration are not clearly delineated.\n\nNevertheless, Kaluzan's property remains destroyed. He had a servant. Now he does not.

Indeed. Stabbed him right in the back. Daedra cannot injure other Daedra in Fargrave. We are bound to comply by the Stricture. But your kind don't have to follow the same rules. This is the result.\n\nDelightful.

Now? We laugh at Kaluzan's misfortune and spread word of his failure far and wide. Imagine … falling prey to a Scamp-sized mortal. Pathetic.\n\nIf he does return, he will suffer such ridicule! I don't dare to hope he's that stupid.

Mortals can act outside the bounds of the Stricture, so this situation poses unique difficulties.\n\nFor instance, it is impossible for a Daedra to slay the husk of another Daedra in Fargrave. So there is little guidance on matters such as these.

Yes. But he will not.\n\nNo member of the Kyn would admit to being banished by a mortal—particularly a tiny one. Pynufax will spread word of Kaluzan's foolishness and frailty. Even the Varlets will mock him. Kaluzan's fate is sealed.
Difficult to say. The offended party is gone. Until Kaluzan reconstitutes and issues a summons of complaint, the Stricture makes no demands.

I don't understand. This is some sort of trick, isn't it? Are you even smart enough for tricks? Maybe you really did just bring it to me. Idiot mortal.\n\nWell, it's not like I'm just going to turn it away, but I'm not going to be in debt to a mortal.

I have no idea. He was an especially useless mortal as I recall. But Shiro-dar crossed paths with Master Rrvenk a few centuries more recently than I. That might help you find the master before you crumble to dust.

Yes, obviously. That's what I just said. You really are hopeless creatures, aren't you?\n\nBe proud, mortal. The tree I plant here will stand as a monument that even you managed to effect some lasting change in your brief existence.

He is under the impression that this one can retrieve some foul Daedric trinket from a most dangerous place. This one is much more skilled at fleeing and cowering. \n\nUnfortunately, Gilfrex will likely kill Shiro-dar for refusing.

Well, we usually have more work on hand than we have dedicated operatives. Besides, some missions involve dangers better suited to experienced adventurers instead of the specialized rogues who make up the core of the Gleaners.
What are you talking about?
Not likely.\n\nImagining things. Should get your head checked. Oblivion's no place for mortals. Scrapes your little brains raw.
Show me the strong stone that becomes soft. The hard stone that becomes brittle. The weak stone that becomes strong.\n\nShow me that you and Rrvenk are worth hearing. Then I might answer you.
Done what before?

Maybe so. Or maybe not. Maybe I already did.\n\nLike this game. Can see right through all that armor. Confused. Scared. Just how you ought to be. Can't do it all day, though. Check the sword. Can talk more after.
You sure? Look sick. Like you ate something rotten. Fargrave's not good for your kind. Makes you see things. Go mad.\n\nBetter lay down. Quiet the voices.
Indeed? I assume it went poorly the first time?

Then you used the sundial, yes? Excellent.\n\nSkrix has us at a disadvantage here. I assume this is his lair, which means it abides by his rules. You must be prepared to counter whatever trap he springs on us.
Ah, excellent. Spiderkith abhor fire. A single spark can set their entire world aflame.\n\nWait for an opportune moment, then apply the torch.
Spiderkith abhor fire. On account of their precious webs. If you're forced to use the sundial again, keep an eye out for anything flammable.
I cannot change her, but she can change herself. She seeks to master the Eleventh Force, but you do not master change. She must let go of this urge before the currents she fights against drown her.

The bat is born to fly, but still must learn to glide upon the wind. She cannot force the sky to carry her where she desires. She must learn to follow the winds of change before she can guide her course.
Yes. You're right. I'm a Psijic. I know myself better than anyone. If anyone is going to pull myself together, it should be me.
You're right. I'm letting fear and frustration get the better of me. This is no different than any of my other studies. I just need to focus my efforts and learn for myself.

Just give in? That's insane. My entire being would be scattered across infinite time and space! But … I suppose there was a positive reaction when others near us stopped resisting change.\n\nI … I'll have to trust in the Eleventh Force.

Indeed. They will find it much less forgiving than Fargrave. If they manage to survive the lightning and the tearing winds, they will need to contend with the wildlife. The Sever is not a gentle place. \n\nBe cautious when you venture there.

There wasn't time while we were in Fargrave, everything happened so fast. We agreed Minwileth would hold it and as soon as we were safe, we'd meet up again and I'd take it then. \n\nBut nothing worked out like we planned.

Exactly. Then, we ran here to escape punishment, but punishment is all we found in this wasteland.\n\nIf we stay out here, we'll end up like Minwileth. But if we go back, it's whatever the Grasp considers justice. And for Elisa, the Drain.
Don't be so insulting. Do you know how many enemies a town like ours faces? They will learn to fight—you will see. Once those mortals shape up and actually learn to kill each other, that is.
Yes. Of course. What a foolish question. \n\nUnder my tutelage and direction, anyone can be a worthy combatant—even these worthless mortals.

Think on your question, mortal. Has anyone in your squabbling history ever been prepared for an attack they weren't expecting? \n\nNo. That's why you train up your soldiers and make it so their ruthlessness overpowers that of your enemy.
All right. Uh, would you … grab the Mother Stones? I don't think I should touch them anymore.

You would be a fool to let your poor judgment keep me from my freedom, little mortal. Consider that I will find a way from this imprisonment, with or without you. What will become of  you and those who failed to help me, when that time comes?

Oh, right. You're in disguise. Sorry!\n\nYour disguise isn't bad. In fact it's flawless. You look nothing like yourself. But, no one else knew I was here. So when you appeared, I could just tell who you were. I hope that's all right.

I do not seek to relive the insult of how I arrived in this predicament. But rest assured, mortal, the powers I claimed from the Ambitions are safe — where only I can reach them. And reach them I will, when the time is right.\n\nNow — free me.
Why would I do that? Not respect you with your titles and name? I was raised by a Priest of the Temple! Even if I wanted to, I couldn't anger Grandmother Sovisa like that.

Being Ritemaster is half the reason why I'm here! I hardly have a moment to myself anymore. My study of the Old Ways has fallen to the wayside because of my usual duties.\n\nYour concerns are valid, of course. And noted.
Well, you're one to talk, aren't you? We're together now, so that's one problem solved already. Between the two of us we should have my synchroseisia resolved in no time.

No idea. The three of us had left the village so I could practice my rituals. I needed to summon Atrozu to mark the festival's end. But … I wasn't sure I could.\n\nAfter a few tries, he finally appeared. We heard screams soon after.

Pretty much. Attacked during a festival celebrating the first hunt of the warm season. Everyone drunk and tearing meat off a charred bear. I guess we didn't see it coming.\n\nOnly three of us survived. Me, Burzonash, and Uroga.
Atrozu ran from the Ravener. As the future wise woman, I needed to defend our totem, so I chased him. And my hunters followed me. We survived by fleeing.\n\nI refuse to make that mistake again.
Ran back, of course! We were met by heaps of torn flesh and pools of blood. And the Ravener. \n\nMouth covered in gore, stalking through town. It tore through our hunters. I swear it was grinning.

I was supposed to be my clan's next wise woman. We oversee the clan's health, both body and spirit.\n \nNow I'm all that's left. My two protectors died getting me across the Deadlands. Only Atrozu and I carry the memories of the Kalmur.
This citadel? Extremely little. I'm no scholar of Daedric lore. We barely made it here from Wrothgar.\n\nI heard some Dremora along the way call it Ardent Hope. Seems misnamed to me.
Our influence does not extend beyond the dunes of Fargrave. The Strictures are not concerned with the demesne of the Prince of Destruction. \n\nThey are now beyond my reach. But not yours.

Well I wasn't one yet. I needed more training. But Atrozu chose me to fill the role.\n\nThe Kalmur did things differently from other clans. Most wise women are just the chief's mother. But long ago we decided to let our clan's totem make the choice.

Madam Whim is a Dark Seducer who has her thumb on the pulse of Fargrave. Nothing happens here that she isn't keenly aware of.\n\nShe deals in favors and information, for a price. And the more you seek her help, the more expensive her services become.
Is it? I hadn't noticed.\n\nLook, we only just met. If you turn out to be trustworthy, I'll tell you the strange tale. If not … well, we'll deal with that if it becomes necessary.

Not a lot. She's apparently a Dremora, and she's interested in the activities of the Dagon cult known as the Order of the Waking Flame.\n\nThis is where we were supposed to meet, but all I saw was that cultist and the votive rune he was casting.

Madam Whim runs an establishment in Fargrave called the House of Whims. Just be careful. She enjoys getting her hooks in new arrivals.\n\nYou'll find Initiate Tilgo in the Deadlands, an area known as the Burn. The Plaza of Portals will take you there.

Initiate Tilgo's a member of the Order of the Waking Flame. He was my friend before the cult recruited him. \n\nTurns out, Tilgo's had a change of heart. He's been providing me with inside information about where the cult plans to strike next.
The Plaza of Portals is one of Fargrave's most important locations. A series of permanent gateways to other realms in Oblivion. \n\nOne of those realms is the Deadlands, the domain of Mehrunes Dagon.
Aww. Little mortal, are you curious? Do you want to know how I got myself tied up by a main road in Fargrave? Do you think you can solve my problems and set me free?
I found a loophole in the Stricture. And the Grasp, being the uptight order that they are, don't like it when someone does that.\n\nSo I'm being detained. Again.

Thinking of finding a loophole yourself, little mortal? \n\nThe Stricture is the code that's kept Fargrave running for centuries. The Grasp interprets the Stricture, and carries out judgment on anyone who … has their own interpretation.

That depends on whether the Grasp thinks I violated the Stricture and put their precious city at risk. \n\nThere's a chance they'll send me back to Oblivion—again. But that's never stopped my plans for long. I'll be back.

Oh. You are looking for your own then. \n\nThe Stricture prohibits the killing of any sentient creature. I didn't kill anything. I didn't even harm anything, I just made them wish I had. Apparently, my methods are under review.

As a crossroads, it's natural for people from everywhere to wind up here. I check on the mortals of the city on a regular basis. Help them as I can. That's why Whim calls me the fool of Fargrave, because I care. And it's why I abhor the Dagonists.
Perhaps. And maybe it's just a fashion statement.\n\nNow, go talk to Madam Whim and Initiate Tilgo while I make my rounds. I need to check on my charges around the city.

Is this a test? Are you checking if I know who I'll use the Mother Stones on?\n\nThey both died years ago. They protected the Temple from Mehrunes Dagon when he decimated Mournhold. I was there, hiding under a table. That was a day I won't forget.

We were visiting her at the Temple on the day of the attack a few years ago. When Nilera died, Sovisa rushed outside to take up her sword. She wasn't a warrior, but she managed to keep the horde from reaching the doors.\n\nI never got to say goodbye.

They're the guards of the Tribunal temples. Warriors who serve the Living Gods and protect their houses throughout Morrowind. \n\nI wanted to be one—like Ordinator Nilera was. But, I'm not a fighter. I've … seen my life's share of blood.

They won't work properly unless they're attuned. \n\nRight now, the stones couldn't return me to Morrowind. They need a lot of power to save Ordinator Nilera and Grandmother Sovisa. I mean, they're both dead and they've been trapped here for years.

I asked about that in Wretched Spire. There are these energy fonts that should be just the things we need. \n\nNo one in Wretched Spire could really tell me where the fonts were, but given their name, I think they won't be too hard to find.

You might have missed the explanation. You are busy.\n\nI got the Mother Stones from a Priest of Almalexia. She said that the Lady of Mercy created them. Once we attune them to the energy of the Sever, these stones will take her children home.
Maybe to gloat over them or use them as a warning to others. I'm not sure which. \n\nEither way, an entire garden filled with living statues of people I knew? That makes my skin crawl.

All I know is that most of the statues here are from the time when Dagon attacked Mournhold. They're just on display here. The fallen. On display. For all Daedra to see. Oh … I might lose my nerve again.

She was protecting the Temple from Mehrunes Dagon's attack a few years ago. I remember hearing her call him a Sar-shemand fetcher. It was the most heroic thing I've ever heard. \n\nI cried when her screams stopped.

They were both incredible women. Heroes in their own right who stood in the face of a great threat. I … I really look up to them both. I mean, one is possibly the greatest Ordinator to ever serve the Tribunal. And the other is my grandmother!

Six-hundred ….\n\nNo, this is a test. Almalexia's priest gave me the Mother Stones only a few weeks ago! I know how long I have been standing outside the Folly. Mehrunes Dagon's realm can't hold me captive. Not like the spirits I need to save.
The decimation of Mournhold? In 2920? The end of the first era? My lord, is there something terribly wrong with you? You—you were there. How could you forget?

Well, have you looked into the Folly? Lightning strikes happen all the time! Maybe I'm wrong, but I've always seen lightning strike the most in areas of high energy. \n\nIf we follow the storms, we should find the fonts. I hope.

My lord, forgive me. Have you been drinking greef? Any Dark Elf knows who they are.\n\nThey're the guards of the Tribunal temples. Warriors who serve you and all the Living Gods throughout Morrowind. I … wanted to be one when I was younger.

Yes, at length, with many hand gestures. Quite thrilling.\n\nI suppose congratulations are in order. But there will be time for that later. I am quite busy at the moment, and you are expected elsewhere.
True. Keep your eyes open. Among all these tomes must be something, anything.\n\nIf not, then I will throw myself at it with the rage of Clan Kalmur. Justice will be done.

No, I …. Look, you've brought Atrozu and me this far. We couldn't have made it without you. \n\nI just need to see this done, understand? And I can't do that alone. Once this ends, I'll be in your debt.

The Order of the Waking Flame. They appeared a few weeks ago. Proselytizing in the plazas. Then they started placing those votive runes. Some kind of prayer to Mehrunes Dagon, but it intensifies mortal emotions.\n\nThe runes are bad, I'm certain of it.

Then you know the cult is evil. They appeared recently. Proselytizing in the plazas. Then they started placing those votive runes. Some kind of prayer to Mehrunes Dagon, but it intensifies mortal emotions.\n\nThe runes are dangerous, I know it.

No. The votives mess with mortal emotions. Make everything more intense. Not sure why. Lyranth said the magic in her letter would allow her to recognize me. I think that's what the glow was.\n\nIf only I could get the Grasp to care about all this ….

Well, since mortals aren't bound to the Stricture, the Grasp pretty much ignores us. Unless we interfere with the Stricture in some way.\n\nAs long as the cult and its votive runes only threaten mortals, the Grasp simply doesn't care.

The Grasp of the Stricture. They're an order of Daedra—mostly Dremora—who serve as arbiters and interpreters of the Stricture, a magical covenant that allows Fargrave to serve as neutral ground for all Daedra.\n\nThey enforce the laws, to a point.

The mortal cultists inflicted no lasting harm upon me, as you set me free before they sent me into the cataclyst. The indignity of being imprisoned by mortals, however, is not one I shall soon forget.

The Grasp of the Stricture. They're an order of Daedra—mostly Dremora—who serve as arbiters and interpreters of the Stricture, a magical covenant that allows Fargrave to serve as neutral ground for all Daedra.\n\nThey enforce the laws, to a point.

No. The votives mess with mortal emotions. Make everything more intense. Not sure why. Lyranth said the magic in her letter would allow her to recognize me. I think that's what the glow was.\n\nIf only I could get the Grasp to care about all this ….

Well, since mortals aren't bound to the Stricture, the Grasp pretty much ignores us. Unless we interfere with the Stricture in some way.\n\nAs long as the cult and its votive runes only threaten mortals, the Grasp simply doesn't care.

Follow the orders of my kynreeve, of course. But if I must guess … I think Rynkyus will keep us in Fargrave for now. I am sure a few Waking Flame cultists still skulk around, hoping to escape punishment.\n\nThey should be disabused of that hope.

Trouble? Every day some mortal decides that their need—or their strength—entitles them to things that do not belong to them. It is the way things are.\n\nBut the conquest of Fargrave for Dagon? That sort of trouble, I am happy to avoid.

Some of the locals call it the Celestial Palanquin, but most know it simply as Fargrave. It's a city somewhere in Oblivion, sitting on a nexus of a multitude of realms. That's one of the reasons the place is so popular. It connects to everywhere!

I do not understand your question, mortal. I will continue to follow the orders of my kynreeve. I will challenge the enemies of my clan and measure myself against them.\n\nIt is not what I do. It is who I am. How could I be otherwise?

Bah! You mortals do not know what servitude is. A few decades and you're done with it, one way or another.\n\nStill, you have a point. If Dagon's legions had marched into Fargrave, things could have gotten worse for poor Hezehk. Much worse.

Fodder for his legions? Toil in his mines? Either I would spend eternity being cut down again and again in senseless battles, or breaking my back carrying rock out of some hole in the ground.\n\nNo, Hezehk would not like that.

The correct term is prophet, you heathen adventurer.\n\nBut yes, I still gladly and happily serve my mistress, the Dread Lady. And I have important tasks of my own to perform, if we're done here. Go on. Lyranth doesn't like to wait.

And there is your first mistake. Attempting to apply finite morality to an infinite being. Lyranth simply is. Right now, she wants to understand a danger that threatens Fargrave and Nirn. Help her and you can save two worlds. No pressure or anything.

How can I describe the beauty of the sun to a creature that has only known darkness? Lyranth is a powerful Dremora, perhaps the strongest of her kind. She possesses a burning curiosity, forever seeking more wisdom and knowledge.

Bringing the message of a higher power to lesser beings is the standard definition of the word prophet, yes. And Lyranth stands above all other higher powers!\n\nI do what the Dread Lady asks and am honored to do so.
I am the Dread Lady's true prophet. Her resounding voice in the mortal realm and her herald in the Celestial Palanquin.\n\nYou should feel honored that my mistress sent me to bring you her message.

The Grasp of the Stricture. They enforce law and order in Fargrave. The Stricture is a covenant that binds all Daedra and allows us to operate somewhat in concert.\n\nSince mortals aren't bound by the covenant, the Grasp tends to pay them no mind.

This one retraced her steps. The path to the portal was well worn by those ever-burning cultists. Tufeh even gathered the courage to free some of the cult's prisoners whenever she came across a group of the flame-cursed kidnappers.
It is. But Tufeh now knows the impact one skilled adventurer can have. She will train herself and set off when she can do some good.

Knowing her sister's fate changed Tufeh. She lacks combat skills, but she knows how to be quiet and where to cut. Tufeh won't bore you with the details, but she hopes to free every innocent person from the Waking Flame's clutches.

A very kind Nord woman in Wretched Spire said that there was a group here who could help me. I've been trying to find them, but I don't have much coin—\n\nOh, I'm sorry. But then I heard you defeated Dagon? Again?
I'm not confused—right. Right. You're in disguise too!\n\nI'll keep your secret here. I won't tell a soul, not even the Saraathu Tong when I find them. Your secret is safe with me, Magician.

I will! I just heard about Fargrave and your exploits and wanted to see everything for myself. 
I'll use the Mother Stone soon, and tell everyone about Ordinator Nilera's spirit.

I hope that's all right with you, Magician.
Oh! Right. You must be in disguise here too!\n\nI'll keep your secret here. I won't tell a soul, not even the Saraathu Tong when I find them. Your secret is safe with me, Magician.

I will! I just heard about Fargrave and your exploits and wanted to see everything for myself. I'll use the Mother Stone soon, and tell everyone about Grandmother Sovisa's spirit.\n\nI hope that's all right with you, Magician.
Oh! Right. You must be in disguise too!\n\nI'll keep your secret here. I won't tell a soul, not even the Saraathu Tong when I find them. Your secret is safe with me, Magician.

Broadly speaking, the innumerable lives within the reach of that unusual place would have been turned for the worse.\n\nSpeaking as a Psijic, the scale and scope of the forces at work were capable of drifting beyond our shared temporal experience.

I doubt Nokvroz had the imagination to use Fargrave's unique properties in such a way, but the potential for unintentional disruptions was within the realm of possibility.\n\nRegardless, you've changed things for the better. We all owe you our thanks.

The Dremora? She's practically all the order's old guard talk about these days. Seems she's been causing a lot of trouble for Sister Celdina. Interfering with her plans.\n\nSomething's about to happen. Tell the Anchorite. Fargrave's in danger.

What, you assume every Dagonist is a true believer willing to do whatever their superiors tell them? I joined up because they promised me a better life. A way to escape the Shambles.\n\nBut they lied. The Anchorite agreed to help me, for a price.

Despite everything, I think you're right. What's my life, if I'm all alone? I came here to honor my clan. Destroying them just to save myself would be a coward's choice.\n\nHere, take my blood and pour it on the orb. I'll use that to drain its power.

It's not getting me any closer to the Slave Choker, that's for sure. Fine, I've wrung enough fear out of the cat these last few days to have my fill. It's overpowering all the other subtle miseries.\n\nHis debt is cleared. Now get lost.

Just that it's mostly abandoned. Hasn't been used by anyone but squatters and vagrants for years. It's isolated at the northern end of the Shambles, easy to secure, and unbearably hot. The perfect location for the Dagonist leaders to plot and scheme.
