And I said I'd tell you … once I was sure I could trust you. Let's find out what's waiting for us at the bathhouse. Try to make contact with Lyranth the Dremora.\n\nAfter that, we'll see.

Let me see. Hmm. It contains a dormant enchantment of some sort. It feels … unpleasant. And the magic … it smells like your daedrat. I will keep the rod and study it as time permits.\n\nUnfortunately, I do not think it is related to Sister Celdina.

Depends on the time of day, who else has passed that way recently, or any of a dozen variables. It doesn't matter to me. We're going to run into trouble somewhere along the journey. This is the Shambles, after all.\n\nPick a direction and I'll follow.

The Spiderkith are a cruel Daedric spider people. Shaermeta and her clan, which she calls the Invisible Web, occupy the eastern section of the Shambles. Their territory is known as Skein Row.\n\nThey treat anyone who ventures there as prey.

Boss Kezo and his gang of street toughs control the western warrens in the Shambles. They call themselves the Errants, mortals who use threats of violence to get by.\n\nThey talk tough, but back off at the first sign of a real challenge.

A group of rogue Dremora that tend to hunt in the Shambles. Some legends say no Prince ever wanted them, others that they did something so awful their Prince abandoned them.\n\nEnzir leads the Vanquished from their hovels along the central plazas.

As I understand it, lucents form naturally in the void and occasionally rain down on the various realms. Some say they're actually crystallized bits of Oblivion. Who knows?\n\nI've seen Daedra gather them, charge them, and make use of their energy.

Well, as long as you have lucents, a dynamus font, and a discharge labrum, you can use the energy to open gates, ignite furnaces, operate torture devices. All sorts of things.\n\nWe're going to use it to overcharge the ward on that door and dispel it.

Look, I just observed how the Daedra use them. The dynamus font is sort of like a spring. Instead of water, energy wells up. Could be an atronach trapped in there. Or maybe it's the ambient dynamism that flows through the space between the realms.

Basically, when you plug a charged lucent into the labrum, it releases the energy stored in the crystal. Most of the labrums I've seen are integrated into some larger mechanism.\n\nI'm not sure what this one was originally used for.

I—I think I'm responding to the changes you're creating here. It's a miracle we've maintained a c—connection this long. I take it as—as a good sign that my synchroseisia is coming closer to alignment, even if it—it's unstable.

There's no more cause for concern. Once I was able to wrap my head around the concept, navigating the ever-shifting nature of this realm has become almost second nature.\n\nThough I must appear a flailing novice compared to Master Rrvenk.

I wandered alongside him for a time, observing. Master Rrvenk's a remarkable being. He seems to read the flow of the Eleventh Force so clearly he's practically precognitive, though he never once attempted to alter its course.

Only puzzling. I don't know whether Rrvenk can't affect the force of change or simply chooses not to. In our travels, he simply drifted along its currents like a cork in a river, pushed harmlessly aside by the ripples and rapids of turbulent events.

I'm not a Daedric scholar, all right! I just know what I know!\n\nDynamism. I heard the Dremora talking about it at Madam Whim's. It's what some call the energy of Oblivion. Or the energy in Oblivion? It's confusing, but it's energy that we can use.
You could, but you'd also get a destructive explosion. Better to control the release by using the labrum.\n\nBesides, the lucents can be used over and over again. But not if you shatter them.

Snakeskin! Then you aren't the volunteer I was sent to look for. We're trying to cure sniffles. Vares also sent me to get the chicken broth and toad eyelids he wanted. \n\nOh, the eyelids aren't for the experiment, Vares just thinks they're tasty.

Vares Dredayn? Oh, he's only the most exceptional sorcerer in the Saraathu Tong. He's even made a cure for hair loss that works on Ogrims. \n\nYou should really see the next exhibition he agrees to do, they're always fun and educational.
Oh, no! I'm just Vares's apprentice. But he's already taught me so much about spell-casting and magic, I know I'll be great with a bit more study.

You're really new here, aren't you? They're a group of mages and Dark Elves who have a pact with the fearsome Quath to study magics and portals within Fargrave. \n\nVares is pretty high up in the ranks because of his brilliance.

Oversized fiery Daedra. I'm not sure why these particular ones have taken to the Unmaker, but I hear that they are exceptionally ruthless. Also, they might be attempting to train the Unmaker? I can't imagine that's going well.

That would be true of most, but not you. Your relationship with the Eleventh Force is more like the moons and tides. Change doesn't pull you along its currents like the rest of us. It follows in your wake.

No, but he taught me to be more aware of the Eleventh Force. Feel its flow. When I sense its motions surrounding you, it doesn't so much push or pull as crash against you like an ocean crag.\n\nI'm obligated to study why. Hope you don't mind.

You saw what I saw when we first encountered Sister Celdina at the Waking Flame conclave. Her infernal device can transform Daedra into Incarnates—living disasters of immense power.\n\nThey threaten Nirn, so you should hope I learn everything I can.

Sister Celdina possesses the knowledge to create a device called a cataclyst. With it, she can transform any Daedra into a powerful Incarnate—a living disaster. She even tried to use the machine on me.\n\nThese Incarnates must be part of her plan.

They are persistent, if nothing else, these Dagonists. If they truly want to unleash their Incarnates on Nirn, using Fargrave's portals makes the most sense.\n\nThe hope, slender though it may be, is that the encoded note will tell us more.

We learned that Sister Celdina tried to use the votive runes to steal power from the mortals. Power she hoped would destroy the Daedra and allow her to conquer Fargrave. We stopped that plot, but this realm's many portals are too enticing to ignore.

The masked mortal has the right idea. Fargrave sits on the threshold to everywhere. If there exists a being who can decipher this code, we will find them here.\n\nI'd prefer it if we could find someone other than Madam Whim to deal with, however.

I have heard of the infamous Mazken who calls herself Madam Whim. I find her practice of turning gossip into profit to be loathsome, but even a filthy daedrat has its uses, I suppose.\n\nTake the note to her and pay whatever it costs for a translation.
What, to a fete like this? Of course not. Wading through all these social niceties is painful enough without dragging some squinty spider-lover along behind me.\n\nAlso, I already disposed of him.
Oh, don't be so dramatic. We both know he can't die.\n\nHe's swirling through the Spiral Skein's creatia … accreting, as they say. He'll be back to his old games soon enough.

I managed to extract some minor details about his forging methodology. Not enough to replicate the process, but something to build on at least.\n\nBeing able to create forgeries like the Ebony Blade we found would be quite the coup.
As always, my motives are pure. If they weren't, I suspect I'd have you to deal with. And neither of us would enjoy that, would we?\n\nEnjoy the party. Until next time.
I could trap would-be thieves and foolish treasure hunters. Barter for more valuable objects, and so on.\n\nEven the illusion of power is power of a sort. And power is the coin of every realm.

That surprises you? Oh the freedom to be as clueless as a stupid mortal! Yes, I'm bound to Madam Whim. In her service until I pay off the massive debt I accumulated at the House of Whims. When was that? Oh yes. Well before the Dwarves disappeared.
I'd rather not say. But Hezehk suggests you avoid the butterfly wing truffles at the House of Whims. Those intoxicating tidbits can be quite addictive!

While I may not like mortals, I've always found the events on Nirn to be fascinating. I loved getting summoned by mortal wizards. Oh, not because I like serving them. No, because I could often trick them and then wander off and explore for a time.

I do not know. Lord Dagon wasn't in the habit of explaining his commandments. I heard the entire town was dropped into the Deadlands from someplace else, but I was never curious enough to investigate further.\n\nSorry to have failed you, master.

Sotha Sil, one of the so-called Living Gods of the Dark Elves, supposedly made a pact with various Daedric Princes to protect Nirn. I don't know the details, but Dagon broke the pact.\n\nSotha Sil slammed the doors and closed off Dagon's connections.

A researcher. Specializes in the empty shells Daedra leave behind. Their composition. Uses alchemy and magic to reveal secrets.\n\nHe doesn't speak in the mortal tongue often. May confuse you. I'll need to interpret for him.

Specificity, chum. Specificity is the problem.\n\nI've wandered the streets of Shimmerene. I've explored the cantons of Vivec City. But there's a whole wide world outside the city walls. Danger! Excitement! Scenic splendor! That's what people want!

Why can't I—? Look at me! I'm like a malnourished ferret! You though ….\n\nHow about this: if you bring me some solid tales about the wilds of Summerset, Vvardenfell, Clockwork City, and Artaeum, I'll cut you in on my earnings. What do you say?

Fantastic! Actually, it's terrible. I'm just reflexively optimistic.\n\nMy travel guide's out of date. Things change so quickly in Tamriel, you know? Maybe you could assist me again. Explore Vvardenfell, Clockwork City, and Summerset like last time?

Excellent! I just need tales. Confront a foul creature, investigate an abyssal geyser, do some sightseeing in Vvardenfell … oh, or find some interesting handicraft in Clockwork City!\n\nI'll meet you at the nearest Impresario camp afterward.

Really? The Eleven Forces are only the basis for your entire studies as a Psijic. You should take some time from your practical studies to brush up on your theory.\n\nThe Eleventh, most sacred force is Change.
Everything, really. I underestimated Change's currents here in the Deadlands. When I reached out to dip my toes in, I got swept away. Parts of me, anyway.
Oh, I really couldn't say. Why don't you take a dip and see for yourself?
Meaning that the land is usually ripest for new growth in the wake of destruction. That might well hold true even here.

How do you think? It took a ride on someone's neck until they dropped dead out there. I guess it wasn't worth the bother of retrieving it from the dumb sod who was trying to run away.\n\nBut it's worth at least one dead cat to me.
I'd like to travel with Master Rrvenk for a bit, if he'll allow it. Despite appearances, I think he'll make an enlightening guide on this journey of mine.
There's always something more to learn. Unless you're a fool.\n\nToday I merely learned how to keep my head above water. Tomorrow, I practice swimming.

Banekin are not thoughtful by nature. Nor do Daedra change easily, even in a realm as turbulent as this one. To be so different from others of his kind? It proves just how far he's come on his own journey.\n\nHe's earned the title of master.
My words fall on deaf ears, but my thoughts find an open mind. I cannot send them far and wide, but when I am close to one who desires understanding, I will be heard.
No, no. Though it's possible all Banekin could do this. It's possible you could do this. Anything is possible. Reaching that possibility? Much less likely.

A complex course along the path of change can be a longer journey than most are willing or able to make. You yourself, mortal, are bound by the length of your life and must plot your course accordingly.

Practice.\n\nMost do not ever feel the flow of the Eleventh Force, but once you become aware of the motions of change around you, you need only feel them and observe. Eventually, they speak to you as they do to me.

I merely speak in terms you are familiar with, but these are new ways of thinking for me as well. I do not see everything through eleven lenses as your friend does. \n\nPerhaps I will peer through them for a while, and learn something new.

That is the name of her clan, so to me she is Lyranth the Foolkiller. Just as I am Rynkyus the Bladebearer. Do you not have clan names where you come from?\n\nLyranth concerns me. I cannot discern what she truly intends in these matters.

I like to get away from all those people from time to time. Sure, I understand it can get quite dangerous out here. But, if Ruldzara forces me to listen to any more inane gossip then I will scream.\n\nDeath by firestorm almost seems preferable.

Look, all Daedra seem odd to me. And they do not belong in Wretched Spire. But if I had to offer a preference, Noroth seems the most acceptable. He wants life to stay exactly the same, and I agree.\n\nDoes not speak all that much. Which I appreciate.

Normally, we cannot. But with our essence drained, nothing remains to return to Oblivion. Nothing to reform.\n\nYou need to know. They have another stronghold. A place called Deadlight. But if you seek the Riven Cataclyst, it's in the fort's citadel.

Mortals! You know nothing! They use the collected essences to create a single, powerful Incarnate. The essences overwhelm the recipient, erasing them, remaking them. They become a mindless force of destruction.\n\nMeanwhile, the drained ones … die.

Feh. Truly, I find Noroth's reliance on a mortal grotesque. \n\nI have nothing useful to offer you. I came upon Tephilaz twitching and seizing on the ground as though filled with insects. A shame it ended so quickly. He was quite amusing.

By smoke and light. Miksotet will call for a reagent. Find it, throw it on the ashes. He will explain what he sees. I will translate for you. His speaking needs practice.\n\nStart with the dead Banekin. We can go from there.

Makes sense. Would Faven attack him? Maybe. He resents all Daedra. But how? And why the delay?\n\nStill too many questions. Don't like it. Help Miksotet with the ritual. Claims the magic needs mortal hands. Promised me it won't hurt you.
Severed tongue, scattered sparks. Eternal flies withheld from knowing.\n\nNoroth knows.

Together we found a portal to the Deadlands. They protected me across this miserable land while Atrozu led us.\n\nSome Xivilai saw our fire. Stupid. They both died protecting me. Soon after that, I found this entrance. We were so close!

Makes sense. Kastav said the Ravener used him to power that orb it uses to hunt. And the Ravener shouted that its prey wasn't on Nirn. Blood magic could easily fuel a relic that can scry across planes.\n\nWhat about that claw?

Both Rynkyus and the Anchorite mentioned how she disrupted the cataclyst's power, giving you the opportunity to defeat the Incarnate and destroy the machine. She claims not to know how she accomplished that.\n\nPerhaps I can help her understand.
Hmm. He does, does he? Interesting. We have seen that the daedrat's senses are highly attuned. Perhaps there is more to the rod than I originally suspected. I will study it and see what I can learn.
Any tool can find a purpose in the correct hand. I sense dormant magic within the rod. And something about the energy reminds me of your daedrat.

I only want to hear her story. Ask her questions. She has indicated that when she tries to access her forgotten memories, the mask causes some amount of discomfort, but I will not personally inflict any harm upon her.\n\nDo you not trust me, mortal?
You unlocked her memories? Overcome the power of her mask? Interesting.\n\nAnd Nokvroz has a … what did you call it? A Perfected Cataclyst? Tell me, what did the Anchorite remember?

During the attack, it was a vicious animal—mindless and hungry. I was prepared to hunt it the same as I would a stag or a lion.\n\nBut if it speaks, then its attack wasn't mindless. It understood the pleas for help. It meant to cause suffering.
No.\n\nBefore, I was putting down a feral animal so it didn't kill again. Now I know the Ravener deserves punishment.
It would have been difficult even before you chose to break the twisted rod. Without the relic? The endeavor seems doomed to failure. I doubt it would be worth my effort to even try.

Gratitude is foreign to our natures. I understand the concept only because I know more about mortals than most of my kind. Bargains, though … should I acquire the means to restore Arox, he would pay any price for my aid. Hmm. I shall consider that.

He told me so. After the attack on my clan, once the screams faded, we returned. I needed to burn the bodies of my people, so that they could move on.\n\nAtrozu noticed a kind of energy, I suppose. From there he began following it. Like a scent.

Orc magic isn't the type you'll find in the High Elf fancy schools. Ours comes from the meat and bones of the physical world.\n\nAll wise women learn to use blood in their art. What better to power healing spells after brutal combat?

If we believe the daedrat, he was once a mighty Daedra in service to Mehrunes Dagon, as well as Nokvroz's superior. If that is true, then he must know how to navigate the fortress.\n\nIf we attempt a frontal attack, we'll never reach the Anchorite.
Let us make haste, master!
As you say, master!
As you command.
Our hunt continues!
Yes, master.
Let us depart, master.
With pleasure, mortal master!
At once, mortal master!

We have to catch Zenithar's attention so he can smile upon your task this day. It's my philosophy that when asking for a god's attention, you should offer thanks as well. It's only polite.\n\nBut if you feel uncomfortable, you're not required to pray.

Time, or the lack thereof, is the issue. If I had more of it, I could work out a permanent solution. But if we break the rod without removing the curse, it may restore Arox, at least until the curse reasserts itself. We could certainly use his power.

It was surprisingly simple for this one to find the portal back. Waking Flame cultists may be dangerous, but Tufeh suspects their charred skulls hold no room for genuine thought. They never even hid their tracks!

Well, this one has yet to show her family Pibiha's note. She needs to tell them what happened to her sister.\n\nAfter that? Tufeh has never been one to rush into a course of action she will regret. She will give herself time to think and grieve.
Oh, yes. Here, let me mark the location for you. I … may have obliterated one of the stones, but at least we have the information we need.

You really don't know anything about where you are, do you? That's the Brandfire Reformatory. Nothing good happens there! The Order of the Waking Flame cult takes people inside and they don't leave again. It makes this one's fur stand on end.

No. This one just saw the cultists force her sister, Pibiha, inside. If Tufeh could fight, those kyncursed cultists would be hanging above a lava flow by their ears! \n\nTufeh cannot help Pibiha now. Would you look for her? Tufeh can pay!

Ah … yes. I do that. I wasn't expecting anyone—oh! \n\nLord Sotha Sil, I'm doing what the Tribunal asked. I have the three Mother Stones and I know where the energy fonts are. I'll free the spirits from the False Martyrs' Folly, I swear!

No? Oh, you're in disguise. I'm glad you're here. Saving Ordinator Nilera and Grandmother—Priest Sovisa's—spirits from Mehrunes Dagon? I can't do that alone! \n\nBut I can give you tribute, um, payment? For the help of an … adventurer.

By entering the citadel they call Ardent Hope and hunting it down.\n\nOh, you mean how do we find the beast? My friend here, Atrozu, is … was my clan's totem spirit. He can track the Ravener. As for how to destroy it? I still need to figure that out.

Then you know I'm the last of my clan. A Xivilai patrol found us and they died to protect me. So I can't give up. But, if I go in there alone, it only ends one way.\n\nJoin me. Help me get justice for clan Kalmur. If we live, I can reward you.
It cost you nothing, mortal. As for what I paid, I'd rather not discuss it.

The memory … I saw glimpses of an old man. I know him … knew him … I think. And I saw other flashes. My first days in Fargrave. I think they're related in some way.\n\nI'm not sure if I want to thank the Collector or run a blade through them.

I was imprisoned there before I escaped. Only to be captured by the Collector, damn his many eyes!\n\nThey never were able to overcome my natural immunity to the wards. Something to do with my position before I was cursed, I imagine.

Perhaps. If time were not an issue. Besides, I can open my own portals to locations I am familiar with. I rarely use portal keys. We require an expert, and Madam Whim knows more about secret portals and byways than anyone in Fargrave. Including me.

We police High Isle. Ships that haven't arrived yet aren't our problem. Besides, we've got our hands full with these so-called Ascendant Order knights. They're stirring up trouble all across the island.

No, but perhaps one of my contacts in Fargrave has heard whispers of powerful mortals hiding in the Deadlands. We will turn our attention to locating the Ambitions after we talk to Eveli and see what she has learned.

You and the Wood Elf uncovered many documents in the Imperial vaults. We barely had time to examine them before other tasks drew our attention. Maybe they will reveal the location or the identity of the Fourth Ambition. One can only hope.

My curiosity is not yet sated. There are still things I wish to know about Mehrunes Dagon's plans and the creation of the Ambitions. \n\nI intend to learn these and other things. Since our goals align, why not continue to work together?

She gave me the highlights. Weird cataclyst devices, Sister Celdina, that evil Nokvroz guy. I'm sorry I wasn't there to help! I can't wait to meet the Anchorite, though. I always thought about getting a mask. Like the Green Hood or the Scarlet Judge!

She sent one of her creepy followers to bring me messages. That Rogatina woman. Letters, mostly, but Lyranth did stop by to give me final instructions on how to get to Fargrave. \n\nI got to use a portal key! That was exciting!

The humble apple. With a little work, it can be transformed from a common fruit into a glorious dish. What better dish is there to sanctify he who revels in the common folk?\n\nBaked apples, unassuming yet delicious. They're the offering we need!

Yeah. Strange doesn't even begin to cover how I felt when he addressed me directly at Ardent Hope.\n\nWell, go ahead and grab the memory vessel and let's get this started. Who knows? Maybe we'll get some answers after all.

If you have need of the recipe, there's a wonderfully friendly chef in the tavern just over there. She has the knowledge you seek.\n\nThe lord of commerce and trade smiles upon anyone willing to compensate others for their expertise.

I'll take the baked apples from you. Free up your hands for what comes next. \n\nIn my travels, I failed to bring my weaving supplies, but Zenithar always provides. I'd be much obliged if you gathered wood for my work.

Chopping wood, or trading for it, Zenithar equates such labor as the same as any heroic act.\n\nWe who serve Zenithar know that he respects the dirt under your fingernails as much as the offerings burnt in his name.

This lighthouse is special. It's blessed by Kynareth, the god of winds and sea. No fire serves as a beacon for nearby ships, but the divine light of Kynareth herself! But without the sacred idol, the light cannot shine.\n\nAlas, the idol was stolen.

Knights in unmarked livery broke in and stole the Kynareth idol! I watched the scoundrels flee to the west with the sacred edifice.\n\nPerhaps … dare I ask … would you be willing to recover the idol for the lighthouse so I may restore the beacon?

Ah yes. Zenithar is the patron of merchants and traders. \n\nThere are plenty of like-minded adventurers who congregate around here. I'm sure someone in one of the guilds would be happy to exchange goods with you.
They may wear the garb of knights, but the ruffians who assaulted me carry themselves like robbers and outlaws.\n\nWhoever they are, they're dangerous. Be wary of them and may the wind guide you.

Do I seem tense? Well, you and Eveli seem oddly calm for creatures whose very plane of existence is under threat. Do you enjoy it here in Fargrave? Shall this sand pit be your sanctuary once Mehrunes Dagon conquers your world?\n\nGo. Deal with Whim.

Hmm. Shortly after the lighthouse was pillaged, I spied three ships on the horizon. Then suddenly the clouds darkened and a terrible storm began to blow in. I lost sight of the ships after that.\n\nPerhaps they were simply blown off course?

The idol has little value outside the lighthouse. It's light does not shine in any other location. My order believes Kynareth's light blesses High Isle. Why steal the idol unless the knights meant to revoke her protection? A troubling thought indeed.

Amenos is notorious for its storms, but Kynareth generally blesses High Isle with fair weather.\n\nI wonder … the way this storm swept in seemed unnatural. And it happened so soon after Kynareth's idol was removed.
You can come across a barrel or perhaps a sack of apples quite easily. \n\nTrading with friends or merchants for goods will also surely please Zenithar greatly.

What a horrible notion! You don't think they plan to eat poor Privette? How could anyone look into those sweet eyes and consider such a deed. Privette isn't food. She's a friend.\n\nBut, I must agree. Very nasty behavior from my new neighbors.

Once, the building was the stronghold of the Knights of Death's Valor. The stories I could tell you about our lives ….\n\nBut Lord Leobert betrayed us, forged himself into a corruption of our very beliefs.

He performed tainted magic. Cleaved our bodies from mortality. But he didn't complete the ritual. His magic confined our bodies to the bounds of the keep. I couldn't allow Leobert to fix the spell, so I hid his ritual tools inside four sacred altars.

Leobert caught me and threw my body from the ramparts. Once I crossed over the wall, the magic binding my body together dissipated.\n\nHelp me. Kneel at the altars. Ensure Leobert will never leave. Do this and the treasures of the graveyard are yours.
In this case, I think it will ignite the furnace and open the door.\n\nThat's my best guess, anyway.

I took action! I moved the Ambitions to new vaults. Safe vaults. But before I could do more, the usurper murdered me. And how did Mehrunes Dagon reward me? By locking me away in a block of metal! And the secret of the Longhouse Emperors died with me.

My daughter, the Fourth Ambition. She's the key. Along with the other Ambitions, she can call forth the power to banish Mehrunes Dagon. That was my contingency. In case the Prince of Destruction lied and we needed to send him back to the Deadlands.

The Anchorite? Is that what you call Mairead? Bah! Use her. Her and the Ambitions. Bring my vengeance to the Prince who betrayed us! Go to the Isle of Joys, a retreat not far from here. All the details are there.\n\nAh, someone comes. My Ambitions!

Gonfalon Bay looks prosperous enough. Comfortable. Gold for all! Just the image the nobles want you to see. They've fattened their purses on the spoils of war. \n\nMeanwhile, common folk scrape to get by.

Aye. The Ascended, or something like that. They don't wear the colors of any house. Come from the mainland, I think. They've been recruiting here on High Isle.\n\nEven took some of us salvagers. Can't see why, though. We're not trained soldiers.

Things wash up here all the time. It only takes one good find to fill your belly for a week. Though even the Shallows are thin pickings of late. It's that new knightly order. Seems they can't even leave us the scraps.

Anything shiny! Look, this is the best spot. Aldbert used to have this spot, and now he's a knight! I bet he's eating meat pies and berry tarts right now.\n\nAll I need to do is find something they want!

The knights! They wear helms and carry no emblems, but their armor is knight armor. They asked Aldbert if he wanted to go with them. He's a knight now, too.\n\nJust need to find something they'll like. Something to show them I'm worthy.

Haven't seen anything sail by in the loch recently, and no new wreckage washed up today.\n\nBut I've been keeping my head down. Those robber-knights have been chasing off salvagers who won't promise to help them.

To a cave just down the beach, but I'd avoid it if I were you. Old Charbel nearly lost his head snooping around there.\n\nI don't know if they found what they were looking for, but I think they left a few knights behind to watch the Shallows.

They were recruiting, or at least offering the chance to earn a reward. They wanted people ready to haul in whatever came ashore.\n\nSeveral salvagers went with them. I wouldn't, though. What I find is mine.

A rogue band that calls itself the Ascendant Order. I thought they were only active on the mainland, but they're here on High Isle.\n\nRabble-rousers and troublemakers, if you ask me. And now I hear they're looting caravans outside the city walls.

Not specifically. But I saw some fancy-pants nobles giving the dockmaster grief. Missing ships could mean anything. Storms, pirates, poor winds, worthless navigators ….\n\nTry Sergeant Dayne over there. He's with the Systres Guard and knows a lot.

A sailor in Gonfalon Bay described them as creatures of molten rock. She said vulk'esh shed their outside layer of rock, like a snake. There's bound to be piles of scoria lying around for us to take. But Tarrinore went in on her own.

Tarrinore? Her mind turns around puzzles like a leaf floating on the breeze. It's hard not to be swept along. This isn't the first time that she's run into danger without a plan. It's just the first time she's done it without me.

We gather the materials our clients pay us for. I don't always know what use they have or why the clients want them. \n\nBut, since this scoria comes from living creatures, I'd guess it has some magical properties.

They're malcontents. They go on about how the high and mighty misuse their power by squabbling over the Ruby Throne.\n\nIt started out small enough—defying authority, inciting riots, petty sabotage. But now they're hurting people.

Darkened the beacon? The locals revere that light—who would dare offend Kynareth in such a way? Something is indeed wrong here. \n\nAt least our missing ships reached these waters, but this storm worries me. Tell me more about the rogue knights.

It's been my plan ever since I met Vinilsare. But the jobs we took never worked in its favor. There weren't enough goods to expand our clientele. All the rich artisans already had their own sources of rare materials.

I've tried. But he wants to protect me. He doesn't want to burden me with the weight he's carrying. I think he needs to work this out for himself. I just hope he can do that soon, before he lets that rage and frustration destroy him.

The Ascendant Order? Here? I heard rumors of knights troubling folk outside of town, but I had no idea they were the culprits. I've had dealings with the Order before. This doesn't bode well.\n\nTell me, did you learn anything at the Shallows?
Tarrinore's wounds need tending to and I could use something to calm me down.\n\nAfter that? Someone needs to sort the scoria, set up camp, and gather our provisions for the night.

The Ascendant Order models itself after other knightly orders, but they're nothing but terrorists. They claim to stand against those who would subjugate the nations of Tamriel under Imperial rule. But I suspect they plan to take power for themselves.
First thing, Privette needs a bath! She seems a little sad at the moment. But a long soak should fix that. Then I'll make us a meal. The simple pleasures.\n\nI just want her to feel safe again.

Valessea of the Mages Guild is a dear friend. We shared a few adventures when she was starting out, and I called upon her when I needed help with the conference.\n\nShe enchanted the invitation medallions the delegates require to attend the conference.

Those men were evil when they were alive. Do you think an existence of torture in the Deadlands would change that?\n\nThe last Ambition needs to learn from Calia and me. I sense that same power inside her that courses through us. We belong together.

Valessea you know. She created the invitation medallions. \n\nAs for Guild General Quentyn, I only met him when he arrived. Seems to have a good head on his shoulders, but the war has cost him dearly—he lost his wife in a raid.

A fantasy. We can't hope to stand against the Prince of Destruction.\n\nLook, I've learned a lot since last we spoke. Too much to explain and too little that you would understand. It's time for the Ambitions to take our destiny in our own hands.

Ah, yes. The curious mage and the stern warrior. They stopped by. When I mentioned that rogue knights had been making the countryside dangerous, they decided to investigate.\n\nI told them where I'd last seen the knights and they set out at once.

A clearing to the southwest. I'll mark the spot on your map. I saw a band of the knights gathering there the last time I went out to gather herbs. They forced me to retreat without them.\n\nI warned Valessea and Quentyn it might be dangerous.
Tarazka's associates learned of a group transporting a High Elf prisoner.\n\nWhile following them, this one realized the group was the Ascendant Order.

A tool for weavers of thread, reed, and wood. Zenithar gave it to the artisans of House Flonius. \n\nIt was entrusted to me so that the weavers in all the villages in Tamriel could experience the wonder of Zenithar.

Guild General Quentyn accompanied me to visit Druid Ryvana. When she told us about rogue knights in the area, Quentyn was eager to investigate.\n\nIt was the Ascendant Order! They overpowered Quentyn and knocked me senseless! They captured Quentyn!
Then perhaps you have more insight on why they are involved in such matters. Tarazka does not care about the details.\n\nStill, this one followed them, as Jakarn requested.
Inside there. Tarazka followed long enough to watch them disappear through an opening covered by vines. They did not come back out.\n\nThis one left something there to show you the way.

I don't think so—the Ascendant Order was definitely trying to take us alive. That's the only reason I had the opportunity to throw up a shroud spell and avoid being captured myself.\n\nDid you come out here to find us?

And Ryvana told you where to find us. Good.\n\nNow we must rescue Quentyn. I may have a way to find where the Ascendant Order took him, but we should get to safety first. Meet me back at Druid Ryvana's hut.

Zenithar looks favorably upon all who keep to their bargains and see their share of the work done. \n\nA word, before you set off to find the Greycloaks outside the town's limits. You may want to gather your fellow adventurers for this task.

I should have expected that. We ran into the Ascendant Order back at the Coral Aerie. They got their hands on the master medallion before we recovered it. Makes sense they'd go after the others. But why take Valessea? That's not their style.
Could be anything, really. Just keep your eyes open. And deal with anything that wants to stab, burn, or eat us.\n\nRemember, Tarazka said he left a lantern by a cave opening covered in vines.

I enchanted the invitation medallions that each delegate carries, so I can trace my own magic to locate Quentyn. Now let me see … they moved north and east, across the loch. I see a chapel, crypts. Maybe abandoned? \n\nNo question. Quentyn is there.

Lady Arabelle asked me to try as soon as we realized the ships were late. I wasn't able to make a connection with those medallions. Maybe they were too far away, or some other magic interfered with my scrying, but I wasn't able to detect anything.
The people of the Systres take pride in our knights, the same as anywhere in High Rock.\n\nThe Sapphire Tourney hosts three orders: the Iron Knot, the Oaken Order, and the Order of the Albatross.

No, we need to return to Lady Arabelle and share this information. Then we can mount a rescue for Guild General Quentyn.\n\nI'll meet you at Lady Arabelle's little pavilion. What she calls her field office, I believe.

I should have examined the medallions more closely after you recovered them. Someone has altered the enchantment. Trapped them to release a killing spell when worn.\n\nIt had to be the Ascendant Order. And they left them for you to find—oh no!

Smashing! This will be like that time I pulled General Gautier out of a Reach stronghold during the border raids of Five-Sixty-Six! Now that was an adventure!\n\nAnyway, it's too bad Valessea couldn't scry the locations of the other missing delegates.

I said you deserved the truth. Lord Bacaro invited the alliance leaders here for peace talks. He hopes to end the Three Banners War. If we find Quentyn with the Ascendant Order, we may find our missing royals. Meet me at the chapel north of the loch.

I suppose you've earned the truth, and you certainly deserve my complete confidence.\n\nThe three ships carried High King Emeric, Queen Ayrenn, and Prince Irnskar, son of Jorunn the Skald-King. I dare say I've misplaced the leaders of Tamriel.
I'm guessing it won't be that straightforward. But who knows?\n\nThere's a wayshrine near the coral river to the east. I'll meet you there, and we can make for the site of the trial.
Eight above help me … they're artists and sailors. Singers, bards, and pirates, all. \n\nBrave swashbuckling warriors that make you recite poetry. Ghastly stuff.

Oaken knights tend to be battlemages, conjurers, and support spellcasters. Their power stems from High Isle's strong tradition of druidic magic.\n\nOur trial will be to convince an elder to give us a staff, a symbol of their order.

No, thankfully. Our trial will be to reclaim the Gilded Lute of Captain Brenvale. The story goes that he went down into the castle crypts years ago, hoping to use song and steel to subdue a spirit. \n\nHe never returned. Hopefully we'll do better.

They're martial warriors and excellent ahorse. You might say the Iron Knot is the most traditional of the Sapphire Orders.\n\nOur trial will be to find the hilt from a lost sword called Redheart. It was the blade of the first Duke Dufort.

Somewhere on these lands, before they belonged to the Duforts. The hilt supposedly had a massive rough-cut ruby in it, should be easy to spot. \n\nMy last squire, Berjo, suggested we hit the castle library to get an idea of where to start looking.

Take this medallion and place it on my worktable in the camp. I'll create a dispelling powder that you can use to eliminate the danger and return the medallions to their original state.\n\nMeanwhile, I'll gather Delric's so I can cleanse it as well.

As we have discussed at length, friendship is an alien concept to my kind. I cannot comment on why mortals do the things they do. And I see little point in spending time agonizing over what could have been. Our time is better spent devising a plan.

Between his research and the knowledge Sombren already had that helped Calia control her power, he apparently figured out a way. Remember, he saw Vandacia absorb Destron's power. He may have extrapolated. Or he found something in that cursed book.

Let us solve one problem at a time, mortal. The relic first, then Sombren.\n\nHe has studied the Mysterium Xarxes and gained the power of two of the three remaining Ambitions. He will make his way to Mehrunes Dagon's side as soon as he is able.
Chase down Jakarn and use the dispelling powder on his two medallions before any more of the delegates are killed.\n\nMeanwhile, I'll restore the Guild medallions and contact Lady Arabelle.

Yes. My portal sent him to Windhelm. To deliver the Ebonheart Pact's invitation medallion to Jorunn the Skald-King. He's probably on his way to the Palace of Kings right now.\n\nTake the pouch of powder from the table and I'll open a portal for you.
So, we have a bit of a leg up on this one. The elder is a wizard named Erlibru. He's actually a friend of my father's. \n\nHeh, he used to tell me stories when I was young. Funny little man.
I would never! Stealing is … well … unknightly. Knowing Erlibru, the challenge will be more about thinking and reason than magic or subterfuge.

Complete the bargain made with the Longhouse Emperors. He will use Sombren to access Nirn, then take back the power of the Ambitions in order to merge your world with the Deadlands. It was his plan all along.\n\nI do hope you survive, mortal.

Do I expect it? No. But that doesn't mean we should let our guard down.\n\nThis venture wasn't a complete failure, though. We rescued the captains of our missing ships. We need to find out what happened at sea and what befell the alliance leaders.

Oh, the name comes from a book I'm rather fond of. I bought the manor to serve as my home in retirement, and I keep a few mementos of my career there.\n\nMeet me there, my dear, and we'll see what our rescued captains have to say about all this.

To Mandrake Manor, my home in Gonfalon Bay. I'll mark it on your map. \n\nJakarn, Valessea, and I have been using my townhouse as a base of operations. I'm confident that it is as safe from the Ascendant Order as any other location we might choose.

There's supposed to be a cavern farther down the bay, big enough to harbor ships. That's probably where the freebooters were dividing their loot and stashing their treasure. Whatever calamity befell their fleet probably occurred there, too.

Good question. Perhaps wait for Tephilaz to return. May take up pursuit of treaty. Tarvyn owes me. May be willing to sign. Covered up his actions. Mortals aren't aware. Maintained stability.\n\nEventually the protection will end. Then I'll move on.
Need to keep moving, you know? Maybe find another caravan. Head to more strange cities. Learn more than I could've ever thought.\n\nEventually I'll go back to Nirn. But not for a while.

I remember it like the ripples in my favorite pond. A storm blew up without warning. My ship was driven onto the rocks near Amenos and broke apart. All were cast into the sea. \n\nWhen we reached shore, those rogue knights grabbed us.

I did not see what became of him. He might have been trapped in the part of the ship that was swept away. Or maybe the currents carried him to a different part of the shore. \n\nOr … he might have drowned. I know that many of my crew did.

An armored mage and a gang of ruffians were waiting at the Shallows. They clubbed down all who made it ashore.\n\nDockmaster Arnauld showed up and I thought we were saved. But the mage—a Breton noble, by his voice—paid him to walk away and leave!

We were nearing landfall when a huge storm swept out of nowhere. I looked for the light at Gonfalon Head, but the lighthouse was dark. We were blown off course, crashed upon some rocks.\n\nI lost sight of High King Emeric, but somehow made it to shore.

Za'ji must admit he was sleeping in his cabin when the storm hit. He woke up when cold water climbed into bed with him. The next thing Za'ji knows, he is being fished out of the sea by strange knights.\n\nI'm saved, Za'ji thinks. Then they tied me up!

The annoying knights, yes. Za'ji heard a commander talking. The Lord, they called him. He was angry the alliance leaders did not wash ashore with Za'ji.\n\nZa'ji did not see the Lord's face, but he spoke like a Breton noble. Za'ji could hear it.

I just finished the invitation medallions for Lady Arabelle when the Ascendant Order burst into my workshop! They kidnapped me, took the medallions, tied me up, and left me here.\n\nThey never even asked any questions. I don't understand it.

I don't know for sure, but the group split up when we arrived. A few dragged me in here while the others went off deeper into the cave. They must have taken the medallions that way!\n\nThere are five medallions total. Please, you must find them.
Certainly. Since you're new to High Isle, I understand you may not be as familiar with the local area as I am. What do you wish to know?

Gonfalon Head Lighthouse, blessed by Kynareth herself, stands atop the hill just west of town. It offers an excellent vantage from which to watch the nearby waters.\n\nPerhaps the lighthouse keeper saw something that will help.

The currents of Loch Abhain are strong. Flotsam from the open sea often washes up along the shores of the waterway. Some of High Isle's poorer folk comb the beach, looking for salvage.\n\nLet's hope they haven't found any today.
The Ancient Anchor Inn sits just up the street near the city gate. It's one of the more popular places on the island. In my experience, inns are an excellent location to pick up rumors.

The gentleman beside me, Lord Bacaro Volorus, leads the Society of the Steadfast. They're a philanthropic fellowship that provides aid to people who have suffered in the Three Banners War. \n\nThe Society is sponsoring a conference here on the island.

That's not an option I care to contemplate. Not while there's still a chance to find them.\n\nForgive me for being evasive, but it's a rather sensitive topic to discuss in public. We've already faced adversity and the conference has yet to begin.

That's a well-guarded secret, my dear. Perhaps after you've proven yourself, I can bring you in on the details. For the moment, knowing any more won't help us find out what happened to my missing ships.

Yes, a sudden squall of unusual intensity. It died out just as quickly as it arose. I noticed it off to the northeast. Dark clouds filled that part of the horizon. Perhaps our ships were delayed by the shifting winds or decided to wait out the storm.
I'm afraid that's privileged information. \n\nSuffice it to say, the cargo coming in on those ships is vital to the conference the Society of the Steadfast is sponsoring.

Of course I do. But I learned long ago to have patience when it comes to such matters. Not every setback is a conspiracy, and not every delay is the act of a Daedric cult.\n\nThough if you do learn anything of imminent concern, please let us know.

Should I be? Lady Arabelle suspects some sort of foul play, but not on my docks! Not a chance. Gonfalon Bay is safe—everyone knows that. Trouble comes from the mainland, not from here.\n\nOf course, the waters to the northeast can be treacherous.

Like I said, storms close to Amenos aren't that unusual. I doubt the ships we're waiting for would have sailed that far north.\n\nJust in case, I sent people to look for signs of wreckage in the Shallows. I really don't expect them to find any, though.

The closer you get to Amenos, the more unpredictable the currents become. And storms constantly barrage the coast. Not to mention Sea Elf pirates.\n\nA good captain knows these things. None of that would keep Lady Arabelle's ships from reaching port.

Long story. It involves multiple maidens, a few princes, and one charming rogue who stole all their hearts. Then the authorities got involved.\n\nFortunately, Lady Arabelle agreed to take responsibility for my good behavior. Now I owe her.

You know me. Every day a new adventure. Had a good thing going for a while, smuggling spices out of Hegathe. Got married twice. No, wait. Three times. \n\nThe third one nearly got me hanged, but Lady Arabelle saved me from the gallows.

I try, but you know how it is. I prefer my independence, but Lady Arabelle isn't a bad boss. Not once you get to know her and get used to her tyrannical methods.\n\nMaybe you can put in a good word for me? Help clear my debt sooner rather than later.

Oh, nothing tawdry, my dear. We'll be too busy for romantic shenanigans before long, I expect. \n\nSome precious cargo was supposed to sail in on the morning tide, but it never arrived. I need someone not known around the island to be my eyes and ears.

While tales of my exploits credit me with all sorts of talents, I can't be in more than one place at a time. I could use a fresh face to mingle with the locals. Determine if anyone knows anything about my three missing ships … and their cargo.

Good, that will help us find the medallions once we get inside. Valessea said if you concentrate on it, the medallions will glow.\n\nI suspect the Ascendant Order won't make this easy for us. The bad guys never do.

No way to tell. But if we meet the Ascendant Champion, I owe her for tying up the beautiful Valessea. There's no call for that sort of rough stuff unless all parties agree.\n\nAnyway, remember—our priority is retrieving those five medallions.

Almost exactly! A wise old sage puts up a barrier around his home. He's trying to protect the little girl he's raising from a fearsome dark knight. \n\nShe grows up to be a mighty warrior. But the sage makes her figure a way out of the sacred grove.

I've seen it before … it's a druidic symbol for spriggans. In the tale, she befriended one that lived in the grove. She wore a spriggan's veil, a wreath of leaves they shed every year.\n\nHere, if you can find the items, I'll guard our spot.

Now, we get these medallions to Lady Arabelle. I can't wait to introduce you!\n\nShe's quite remarkable—a former Lion Guard officer, spy, agent for High King Emeric, and world-famous author! But don't mention that last part.

I keep an eye on the Systres for them. Make note of noteworthy people and events. Gather information. Exchange it with other eyes and ears around the isles. Folks beneath notice—Nari among them. The rewards far outweigh the risks. Usually.

Oh, she doesn't like to brag. In fact, she'll adamantly deny it if you ask. But she writes those wonderful Investigator Vale novels! At least, that's the word on the street.\n\nAnyway, we should get going before more of the Ascendant Order shows up.

This is risky business. Informants that get caught shouldn't expect a rescue, but I just can't leave her.\n\nThe truth of it is, Nari's my sister. Letting her be dragged off by the Sea Elves would make future family gatherings … awkward.

I am. Those stories Erlibru told me when I was little … they're a part of why I'm in the tourney today. \n\nAnd, I won't lie, it's nice to know he still cares about me. Strange, lovely man. Let's move on.

It's understandable, given the situation, but I can't say I appreciate her taking it out on me. I took care of the situation the best way I know how. All charging in after her would have accomplished is getting both of us captured, or worse.
Oh, he'll be fine. Probably bellyache for a bit. That's probably the worst he's had to suffer for one of these jobs of his.
Yeah, thanks. I'll have no shortage of scars from this, I think, but I'll be all right. This is the last time I help Titus with his deals though.

Pfft. I don't work for them. Neither does Titus. Not directly, anyway. He's a snitch. Whichever alliance is lining his pockets at the end of the day is the one he serves.\n\nEasy money, he said. Suppose that was mostly true, but today outweighs it all!

I'm a cursed soul. As are all who linger here. The Commodore of our fleet made a fool's bargain in a moment of desperation and damned us all to an eternity of restless undeath. A pox on his rotten bones.
Ah, from the Society of the Steadfast, right? Are you an associate of his? Well, you just missed him.\n\nHe delivered a medallion for the Skald-King and then went on his way.

Ha! Creature, that question would have held meaning an eon ago. I have been drawn so far from who and what I was as to have rendered such concepts meaningless.\n\nFor now, I am your benefactor and beneficiary both. Until Thras lies before me again.

Fresh waters. Distilled. Pure … and empty. Like nothing I've encountered before—and I have seen much. \n\nWhoever wove this spell intended it to last an eternity. It felt as such. But I am nearly free, thanks to you. Deliver me, creature.
I do not know. Memories of my capture have been … excised.\n\nThis place's architecture suggests Aldmer, but the magic tastes different from Summerset's dwellers, new and old.
Hmm, I recognize you. You helped Windhelm and the Skald-King before, so I'll trust you in this matter.\n\nCome with me. I'll show you to the medallion.

Hmm … very well. The Society of the Steadfast has never given me reason to doubt them before. I'll show you to the medallion, but if you make one move that threatens the Skald-King, I won't hesitate to cut you down. \n\nCome, let's get to it.

Your associate said the medallion was a gift from the Society of the Steadfast. Why would it pose a danger?\n\nI placed it in the study. I planned to present it to Jorunn once I had time to assess it.

We were cornered by a pursuing enemy. Outnumbered twenty-to-one. Doomed to die by the sword or the gallows. The Commodore performed some vile ritual of the deep druids to turn the tide in our favor. It did, in a way.
Good! Except for the make-up-a-poem-or-sing-a-song about it part coming up at the end of the tourney. That, I'm less excited about.\n\nLet's keep moving.

All that's left is to present the trophies. Everyone will be gathered at the tourney pavilion. I'm excited! \n\nAnd nervous. I get a bit … uncomfortable being the center of attention. Here, meet me on the jousting grounds. We'll head in together.

Ah, I believe you. But I think I'll still have our court mages take a look all the same.\n\nI thank you for the timely warning. Is your associate aware of the danger? He seemed eager to make his next delivery.

All that's left is to present the trophies. Everyone will be gathered at the tourney pavilion. I'm excited! \n\nAnd nervous. I get a bit … uncomfortable being the center of attention. Here, meet me on the jousting grounds. We'll head in together.

I am! I assumed the Iron Knot trial would be all about swordplay and martial skill. Maybe horse riding? Horses and I don't like each other much.\n\nAnyway, I'm actually quite pleased how we did. Let's move on.

We may be at war with Queen Ayrenn, but there's no honor in killing an enemy in this despicable manner.\n\nA boat's available at our docks if you need it. And I'll make sure the Skald-King receives this medallion from the Society of the Steadfast.

He said he was traveling to Auridon to meet with someone from Queen Ayrenn's court. You might check the docks in Skywatch.\n\nIf he intends to deliver another one of these medallions, you should hurry and intercept him.

It's that small island to the west of here. Not sure where the name comes from. I imagine something to do with whales.\n\nJailers play a game there with prisoners from the stockade. They let you loose and then send hunters after you.
Yes, yes, yes. I had hoped it would be her. She remembered the tale of Miriette la Courageuse, eh? \n\nSo nice you two could come out here. Usually it's just me and the forest spirits these days.
Of course not. Solve the puzzle, take the staff, that's the idea right? \n\nIt's out back, leaning against the cottage. Enjoy in good health, second!

I sure did. A couple names I even recognized. Wealthy merchants, both of them. Who would be a guest of a place like this? Well, voluntarily.\n\nStanding around in the open is no good. Where should we start looking for Anton?
Zenithar be praised! The awl's returned to the hands of a true and devout weaver. All is as it should be. \n\nWere my suspicions correct? Did the Greycloaks have the awl?
Yes. With the awl I just need to bend the wood … like so. And place this piece here. And then ….\n\nThere!
Our work for this task has come to an end. \n\nAll that's left is to set the basket and baked apples alight and offer them to Zenithar.

It's just a saying, dear.\n\nAs you're still on retainer, I'd like you to spearhead our rescue efforts. Jakarn will go with you to the island, then you'll split up to search for the royals. It's risky, but there's a lot of ground to cover.

Aboard a prison ship. They sail for Amenos regularly from the Dufort Docks. We'll be contracting the services of Captain Basrush. She's … a dear friend.\n\nJakarn and I will meet you there after I finish briefing Captain Kaleen and the others.

Captains Kaleen, Tsuzo, and Za'ji have been procuring ships for just that purpose. The waters around Amenos are treacherous, but I have faith in their skills. \n\nI wish I could send more agents to help you, but I'd prefer to keep a low profile.

The entire archipelago sits atop the bones of an ancient volcano. Sheer cliffs, jagged reefs, and dangerous currents make Amenos a perfect site for a prison. \n\nThe only safe landing on the isle is the dock at Amenos Station.

Sometimes I lose track of days myself, dear. Lord Bacaro hired me to provide security for the upcoming peace talks. I oversaw the arrangements to get the alliance leaders to High Isle safely.\n\nUnfortunately, the Ascendant Order uncovered those plans.

Draigh, I hope not. The idea of aspirants trying to directly sabotage each other doesn't sit well with me. And I see that look in your eye … no lockpicking.\n\nBut buff my plates, we still need that key.
Oh? And I suppose she's offering her usual pouch of gold and the promise of an evening's company at her manor? \n\nHa! She does know the way to this sailor's heart!

The gangs of prisoners who band together to survive in the jungle. They're all bad, but the Green Serpents are the worst.\n\nHere, for you and the pretty boy. Disguises. Put them on and try to look appropriately forlorn as you go aboard my ship.

If that's your port of call, who am I to argue? Just know the dangers before you step aboard my ship.\n\nIf they process you in the stockade, you'll never leave Amenos alive. If you head into the jungle, beware the beasts and the gangs of banished.
Yes, let's split up. I'll go speak to the castle stewards, and you head for the offices of the knight commander.\n\nWe can meet back here. Stendarr willing, one of us will have some luck.

What? Seriously? I'm glad I decided not to try on the medallions on my way here.\n\nHey, I already delivered the Ebonheart Pact medallion! We have to get back to Windhelm. I am not willing to add regicide to my growing list of bounties!

Oh! Good! Maybe start with that next time? \n\nAnyway, if you can dispel the evil magic, then don't let me keep you. You can fill me in on the details later. Just hurry before that pompous bureaucrat decides to try on the medallion.
Nah, do you? Maybe he stays away from the Amenos stockade on purpose. Only comes by to take more prisoners for his game.\n\nI wonder if he's even a jailer at all ….

No one would call the stockade a great place. But it's not so corrupt that the entire staff would do something like this. The jailers who took us to the island even warned me about it.\n\nI'm starting to think this Mannick keeps the whole thing secret.

Sure, the jungle is full of criminals. But they're not actively hunting us like on Whalefall. Well, some of them aren't, anyway. Maybe we'll meet others who just want to survive. Seems likely.\n\nHopefully Anton doesn't try to steal from them.

No, I'm … well. I'm hiding. I have a bit of a fear of spiders, you see.\n\nIn my defense, I made it past a bunch of the smaller ones … but I lost my nerve when a giant, red-eyed beastie leapt out at me.

Ah, the natural result of my poor survival skills. Though, I cannot imagine why you believe now is the proper moment for that story.\n\nRelease the bindings, please. Once we're safe, I'll tell you anything you want to know.

Just a moment! You won't get very far without the key to the deep crypts. Which I just happen to have! Hah!\n\nUm. I tell you what. When that thing surprised me, I may have dropped my sword. Return it to me and I'll slip you the key. What do you say?
While I ran and hid from the bloodthirsty murderers chasing me, I saw a bridge on the western side of the island. I think that would get us to the south side quickly.

We have a way to stay in contact, but she isn't answering my sendings. I was able to trace the magic of my medallion and it's headed toward an island off the coast of Daggerfall.\n\nSomehow, the Ascendant Order realized that we dispelled their magic.

Sword's Rest is an island off the coast of Daggerfall. High King Emeric uses it as a retreat. It makes perfect sense for her to meet him there.\n\nI need you and Jakarn to find a ship on the Skywatch docks and get to Sword's Rest as quickly as you can!

Because they came after me just before I delivered the restored medallion to the Fighters Guild. I think they may also be after Lady Arabelle! And I can't seem to open a portal to her location. That's very worrying to me.

Ah very good. You know, I've always said that Isobel was a fair hand.\n\nNever doubted you for a moment. Ahem. Here's your key. The door to the deep crypts should be off the main chamber east of here.
Yes, well, we're both sporting. Well done all around.\n\nHmm. And perhaps you won't mention this when telling the tale of your trial?

Oh! One of the other knights probably took it, or hid it. Cheating! Isobel will not like that.\n\nHmm. One of my mother's aides might have one. It's good she sent you to ask, though. Best she avoids the knight's wing for now.

She and I have been friends since we were very young. Knowing Izzy, she'll want to avoid even rumors she appealed to my mother for help.\n\nI'd start by asking Dame Hendra. Nilsmon might have a key as well.
A poem for me, who …? Oh. This is from Nilsmon, isn't it? \n\nEvery one of the tourney aspirants is after me, and I have a bookish Nord sending me poetry. This day is …. I've had better.

And I'm looking for a posting more interesting than pushing papers for Knight Commander Jourvel, or playing politics with snooty nobles!\n\nTell me, why should I give a key to the first peasant who comes wandering in off the lawn?
No, I'm sorry, that's not something I can give … wait. \n\nI take it back. I'll give you all the keys you want. Just … do me one small favor.

Ah! Gentle dove. She is an Aedra, come to Nirn. Her beauty is too much for we poor fools. I fancy myself a rather decent poet, you know. One day … one day ….\n\nWait. I was supposed to do something for you, wasn't I?
I'm trying to muster up the courage. We've been fighting quite a bit.\n\nI made Isobel promise not to say anything. I didn't want her jeopardizing her place in the tourney.
Apparently not. And here I am, working up the nerve. Mostly pacing. \n\nI know Isobel can win the tourney … but I just can't sit idly by, either. Ugh!

You must be new to High Isle. My mother is Dame Jourvel, Knight Commander! She has never, in all her illustrious career, gone back on her word. Not once.\n\nShe offered my hand in marriage. And by the gods, her honor means she won't unoffer it.
Gross. All right, since it's for Isobel. I'm sure it's yet another ode to my hair or face or something. \n\nTell him I blushed prettily and said I would read it later, when I'm alone. Good luck.

A bribe? How unexpected. Most people I have to deal with would rather get snippy and tell the commander about how rude I am. All because I can't be arsed to be obsequious.\n\nRefreshing! Here's a key. Try not to get killed down there.

Give this note to Lady Aurelia. Discreetly. It's my latest poetic offering, a treatise on her virtue. \n\nIt's crucial that you do not reveal who it's from. One day, I shall reveal myself as The Author. And she will finally see true love!

Yes, of course! Here you go. I shall remember your service to true love. Perhaps with a line in the epic romance I've been writing.\n\nThe heroine is named … Laurelia. Once it's completed, I'll have a bard perform it. And you shall be invited!

In rain or spotless skies, not a day goes by without toil and effort. If these things were not divine in themselves, why would so many have to work so hard? \n\nI pray that my road may be long and dusty so that I may serve Zenithar all my days.

If you want to continue your labors, speak with Fasaria. She has tasks more befitting of your talents.\n\nAnother way to praise Zenithar is by speaking to the merchants here. Zenithar blesses commerce and trade.

Zenithar's teachings and his approval—though worth seeking—is not paramount. Instead, those who serve him focus on their own satisfaction. \n\nI take pride in my offerings to Zenithar. Therefore, I know he approves of my efforts.
Our offering is complete, but the day's festivities continue. I'll speak to more pilgrims and organize offerings of their great crafts. There is more to do, if you feel your day is not yet finished.
Cross your heart ten times and seek a temple, lest you find a druid curse on you as well!  \n\nYou feel that rumbling? I wager this old cavern didn't care for that rotten magic either.

Plenty of other treasures tucked away in that cavern, I suppose. Hah, even without the ghosts that sounds like more trouble than it's worth.\n\nAh, I've got a good tale for the next Maul family reunion, in any case.

Asking for Zenithar's blessing and thanking him for the work we do is absolutely necessary. We can't expect him to always being watching.\n\nBut, if you'd really rather not pray to him, I understand. I'd be happy to offer a prayer in your stead.

You know the lady. She picks up strays wherever she goes. Helps with her work and she enjoys the company.\n\nThe first time we met, she was supposed to arrest me for smuggling. Instead, she turned me into an operative and we broke a much larger ring.

Let's see …. You're right, looks like the Duforts had a holdfast there, before they became nobles.\n\nOh, wait. I know this place! It's an old ruin off to the east. Aurelia and I used to pretend it was a witch's lair when we were young.
There aren't really roads back there. But I remember a nice wide path we can take. I'll mark your map.\n\nMaybe if we hurry we can beat Berjo and Langley to the ruin!
Langley's first and last thoughts every day are about himself. He'll have Berjo working on moving those trees … well. Until he gets bored.\n\nSo let's just go around.
Remember, Aurelia and I used to play up by the ruin. There's a path around the rise to the east. Let's go carefully, though.\n\nWe stopped playing up there when a faun warband moved in.

I hoped Valessea would sense our trouble. When the Ascendant Champion and her forces arrived by ship, they brought a powerful mage with them. Most of the island's defenses were rendered useless by his magic.\n\nBut what was that about the medallions?

Excellent. And I'll sprinkle this powder on the medallion along the way.\n\nRemember, we must stop the Ascendant Champion. If High King Emeric dies, any chance to proceed with the peace talks will be lost. We can't allow that to happen.

A dispelling powder? Very clever! Sorry to hear about poor Delric, but I assume you took care of the other medallions? Good.\n\nLast I checked, Emeric was safe in his private quarters. The wards there are still in place, but they won't hold forever.

We walk in, and the Tourney Herald announces us. I go forward and claim the trophies. As my second, you have the honor of displaying each of them as I call them out. \n\nOh, and most important: don't start laughing when I recite a poem.

It's tradition, Stendarr help me. The Order of the Albatross requires it.\n\nHaving you do this with me was more than helpful. You've been a calm and steady influence. A real partnership. Thank you. Let's just get through this last bit.

Before I engaged in two of my three favorite activities—eavesdropping and thievery—I heard the jailers talking about a bounty placed by the Green Serpents prison gang.\n\nThey're offering a reward for three nobles that washed ashore in the jungle.

What else could it be? Do you know of any other noble-born people who were lost at sea in the area? So head north and go through the big gate. That's your way into the jungle.\n\nMeanwhile, I'll see whether or not House Mornard is involved in all this.

Yes, I'm certain you do. Only an incurious fool wouldn't seek to know more.\n\nBut, it may surprise you to learn that I find being bound like this deeply unpleasant. Please, collect and extinguish the censer. I will answer every question once I'm free.

Typically I've stocked the room with so many creatures that a challenger must wade through them like mud. As those brutes came through, they had enough people to easily thin the swarm.\n\nNo matter. You weren't involved, so it's no harm to your honor.

The dockmaster ignored the wishes of the Ascendant Magus. Captain Kaleen saw Arnauld collect another payment at the loch. I suspect he got greedy. And once he proved he wouldn't stay bribed, well, he became a liability.

The Ascendant Order's throwing around a lot of coin on High Isle. If we follow the gold, we'll find someone with wealth and local influence behind this. Another clue that a High Isle noble is involved.\n\nHmm. Perhaps they want to keep the war going?

Profit, of course. That's what it always comes down to.\n\nLord Bacaro should be able to tell us which nobles stand to lose if the war ends. Go to Steadfast Manor, northwest of the city. I'll have Jakarn look for the dockmaster and then meet you there.

Almost certainly. As I said, we must be careful about whom we trust. \n\nIt is a concern, but it can also work to our advantage. Gold only buys loyalty for so long. And I suspect our adversaries are not as organized as they appear.

I doubt it. If Dockmaster Arnauld knew where the alliance leaders were, he would have happily sold that information to the Ascendant Magus in exchange for his freedom. \n\nWe know he didn't because the Order is still looking for them.

We know their opening move didn't go as planned. They were interrogating the captains to try to find the missing alliance leaders. Now they've taken the dockmaster, who would have been more useful to them where he was.\n\nThey don't trust each other.

They said that the archipelago belongs to nature. That they were carving a balance between the natural world and greedy mortals.\n\nThey brought us through the caves and up to the platforms above. Then they shoved us into cages.

The Eldertide … sacrificed my shipmates to it. Those druids need to suffer. The coral is inside the caves, just down that hill. Make them pay!\n\nI'll give up piracy if you do as I ask. Smash the coral. Free the others. Please.

Veslyn? She was whole when I escaped. I offered to help her, but she wouldn't leave the others and I had to run. I had to!\n\nI can't do anything. Not against the Eldertide Druids' power. But you—you can destroy their coral.

Just some old ruins, so far as I can tell. Not the worst place for a secluded hideout, if it weren't crawling with yaghra. Too far from any shipping lanes for pirates to bother with though.\n\nWhatever they're after, it's not plunder.
I understand. I'll ensure that Zenithar's eyes are turned toward you while you commit yourself to the task at hand.\n\nGo on dear-heart. I know your efforts will be met with success.

I've been a little busy, dear. Now go outside, get on your boat, and return to camp. I'll meet you there.\n\nI need to dispel the medallion. Then … well, situations like this tend to stress out the high king. I can help him with that. I have before.

You know Za'ji? And he's alive? That's good to hear. Now I can kill him for getting us wrecked as soon as I see him.\n\nWhen the storm hit, it was all I could do to hang onto some wreckage and make it to this beach. We're on Amenos, right?

The alliance leaders, right. I keep meaning to try to find Queen Ayrenn, but every time I get started, more of those prison mongrels rush out of the jungle and attack me.\n\nI love a good fight as much as the next sailor, but I'm exhausted!

Yes, I understand that you and Lady Arabelle have tangled with these brigands before. They claim to be knights, but they have no honor.\n\nWill you do as Lady Arabelle suggested and look for my retainers? I would consider it a personal favor.

Thank you, my friend. I'll confer with Lady Arabelle while we await your return. I'll tell her everything I know about the nobility of High Isle, if she really thinks that will help.\n\nI knew peace would be hard to achieve, but I never expected a war.

I sent Grenier and Danise to retrieve a shipment from the Navire docks, but I expected them back ages ago. They were traveling the road to the south. I just pray no evil befell them.\n\nThe supplies we can lose, but good people are irreplaceable.

Well, I believe a knight should not be measured by the worth of their weapon, but by the allies they keep. \n\nThe knights of High Isle pride ourselves on our courtesy. And I personally always wish to honor good people.
For acting as Dame Isobel's second during this year's Sapphire Tourney, I want to formally extend my thanks. \n\nAs both knight commander … and as a mother.

They're Daedra. Summoning Daedra is dangerous, but when placated with their favorite drink, these Daedra always behave. They've seen what happens if they don't. \n\nPlus—and this is important—our rejuvenated celebration is worth the risk. Trust me.

Grenier and Danise were helping arrange a banquet at Castle Navire. Then they were to collect the supplies and return here.\n\nWhat could they have seen that would cost them their lives? The banquet is just to welcome our royal guests to the island.

So Lady Arabelle informed me. I hesitate to accuse anyone, but perhaps you should join me at Castle Navire.\n\nAll the nobles of High Isle will be there. And if my retainers did see something at the castle, perhaps you can determine what that was.
The Ascendant Order, plundering Steadfast supplies and killing our retainers? Damn. It was brave of Grenier to try to fight back, but foolish. The supplies weren't worth their lives.

Duchess Elea wants to project confidence, especially in light of the current situation. Rumors travel swiftly in the archipelago. The people need to believe we have things under control.\n\nI expected to pay a ransom and have the delegates back by now.

Why not? I had the idea, the contacts, the plan. And I set the stage. \n\nBut you, you fought off hordes of monsters who eschewed our festivities. You gathered our talent. If anyone here should ring the bell, it is you, my friend.

Mostly they serve to keep errant magic inside Tor Draioch's boundaries. You know, the standard three-points-of-protection thing. \n\nUnfortunately, my spell kicked those wards in the teeth. They're not protecting anything now.

Next, you will encounter the Trial of Wits. Sailors must know how to think on their feet. No one writes a manual for everything you encounter on the high seas.\n\nNow, move quickly. Amunara continues her destruction of the fortress to bypass the wards.
All you have to do is place those crystals I gave you on the three protective wards. It'll be easy, I promise!

I am a simple connoisseur of all that is frivolous and fun!\n\nI've had a hand in many an outrageous gathering. Ball of the Skald King. The wake of the last Sibyl. Oh, the House of Dibella was livid when they remembered that one.

Stuffy celebrations can lose their patina after a while. Luckily, folk like you and I come along to help keep things interesting. \n\nOne day, you may understand just how much a compliment like that means coming from a person like me.

Rivals and partners. House Mornard built its wealth on trade. They rely on House Dufort ships to carry their goods. But the two families have long vied with each other for primacy.\n\nThe Mornards resent the fact that the Duforts rule High Isle.

My family has always believed that wealth is meant to foster good works. When the three alliances went to war, I made the decision to do whatever I could to help common folk caught in their violent wake.\n\nSo I started the Society of the Steadfast.

We're a small society that mostly works near the battlefields of Cyrodiil. I did turn a portion of my estate on High Isle into a healing center. We bring the badly wounded here to recuperate.\n\nThe peace talks naturally grew out of our other efforts.

And our missing guests of honor will no doubt be the main topic of discussion. This is a chance to listen as well as ask questions.\n\nMake sure you speak to Elea Dufort, Damard Dufort, and Jonne Mornard. They'll be the most important nobles present.

Until we know more, I suspect everybody. But if any of the nobles are funding the Ascendant Order, I think it likely that it's one of the grand families of High Isle. \n\nThat means House Dufort or House Mornard. Either way, we'll know more soon.

Not Jakarn. Waiter Phred. I'm in disguise! \n\nI told you about the chambermaid, right? She's one of the duchess's personal assistants. Well, she told me where the duchess keeps her sensitive documents—among other unmentionable items.

I'll lure the guards away from the doors. But I'll need your help. Talk to one of the musicians and ask them to play the tune Stagger and Sway. It's an old favorite of mine. \n\nI'll take care of the rest.

Nobles and the upper staff never pay attention to the common help. I easily filched a key from that stuck-up Steward Hercian. While I cause a distraction, you go take a look!\n\nDuchess Elea has a private study somewhere beyond the northeast door.

Er, I don't really take requests. Duchess Elea provided a list of approved songs she wanted performed. That one definitely isn't one of them.\n\nNot that she would notice. I don't think anyone is really listening to the music.

Well, there is a lady I'm interested in. Layla. Highborn, you know—out of my class. Normally I'd never even be in the same room as her.\n\nCould you give her this letter? Even if she hands it back, at least I'll know I told her how I feel.
It's good to see that someone appreciates the arts. All right, then. You'll have your song!

The most beautiful lady at the banquet! Hair like golden wheat, eyes as blue as the sea, pale skin like the beach at sunrise … and freckles! She even has freckles.\n\nAhem. Sorry. She's the one in the red dress with a flower in her hair.

Ah, Lady Arabelle. I knew she wouldn't leave us to rot in this jungle. But she only sent you? Not an army or a chivalry of knights? No matter. I welcome the company. Trouncing these Green Serpent bastards is amusing, but I'm starting to grow weary.

Ah yes. We were together for a time, but we argued and he rushed off in a huff. I believe I know where to find him, after we make some preparations for our rescue.\n\nYou can signal a ship, but I can help calm the storm that hugs the coast.

Oh very well, if you insist. You may not believe this, but Emeric and I do not always see eye to eye. He's as stubborn as his throne is uncomfortable. Why the Bretons insist their king must suffer every time he sits down, I'll never understand.

Lady Arabelle, you say? How is the dear woman? She and I have shared quite a few close calls over the years. But she only sent you? I assumed I merited at least a dozen knights or so.\n\nAh, well. I assume you have a way to get us off this damn island?

Ah, you've seen Ayrenn. And she's still alive? Good. \n\nDo you know I was looking for young Irnskar when these Serpents rushed out and tried to toss me in that cage? I showed them! But I think they may have captured our wayward Nord prince.

I half expected to find our young Nord prince sitting atop a pile of dead Serpents. But no such luck.\n\nLet's take a look around and see if we can find anything that points to where the Serpents might be holding Jorunn's pup.
