I'm aware of most things that happen on my isle. It's true we didn't connect reports of mysterious knights to the Ascendant Order until recently. But now that we know they are one and the same, we'll quickly bring them to heel.

Which is why I prefer to handle this discreetly.\n\nI suspect House Mornard is behind this. They profit greatly from the war, and they still hold a grudge against my house for overshadowing their own. Frankly, I put nothing past them.

I suggest that you and Lady Arabelle leave this matter in our hands. My knights have already pinpointed several sites where the Ascendant Order gathers. They are scouring High Isle for our missing guests even as we speak.

One should be careful when talking about one's neighbors. Still, Count Mornard's dislike of my family is well known. Years ago, his father backed King Ranser of Shornhelm in his dispute with High King Emeric.\n\nEmeric did not forget it.

My family builds ships. Our shipyards construct the finest vessels to ply the western seas.\n\nIn reward for our service, High King Emeric granted us the Duchy of Systres. We rule with care and compassion for all—even the Mornards.

The duchess explained everything to the court just before you arrived. If Lady Arabelle had consulted us, things would be different. We know what hazards await careless captains making the approach to High Isle.\n\nHer ships were simply unprepared.

Right. Mentions taking their captive noble to the coin fort. That has to be Prince Irnskar.\n\nAmenos used to be a stronghold for High Rock slave traders, but that was many years ago. There's a crumbling old ruin just west of here.

Elea gained her station by currying favor in High Rock. Then she made a show of backing Lord Bacaro's Steadfast Society.\n\nBut ruining the peace talks and getting heads of state killed? Blame must be placed, and she'd never fall on that sword herself.

Don't tell me you buy into this Ascendant Order nonsense! A shadowy order of knights working to undermine the governments all across Tamriel?\n\nIt's a ruse, my friend. A convenient fiction to protect the flawless name of House Dufort. Faugh.

I try to keep up on matters of state, but I confess. Elea told us all about you. I am Count Damard, the duchess's brother and court mage of House Dufort.\n\nTell me, has your investigation uncovered news regarding a sudden storm that appeared recently?

I don't think that storm was natural. The druids wield old magicks and consort with spirits. It is well within their abilities to summon such a tempest.\n\nThey mostly keep to themselves, but I suspect a ruse. Those are your culprits, mark my words.

A hypothesis that matches my own. While my sister chases bandit knights across the countryside, I wonder about the druids who make the wild parts of High Isle their home. \n\nThey have little love for civilized culture. They could be responsible.

We did indeed! There are songs sung about that weapon. Literally. Jorunn performed one of them the last time we shared company. We must return it to the prince when we find him.\n\nAnyway, our course seems clear. We make for the coin fort to the west!

A long time ago, yes. Not something the Covenant sanctions today. But you're missing the pertinent point.\n\nThe Green Serpent gang is using the old coin fort as a hideout, and they're holding Prince Irnskar there.

Didn't we cover this? I might be willing to do you a favor if you do something for me.\n\nDeliver that letter to Layla—the lady in the red dress with the flower in her hair. Do that for me and you'll get your song, all right?

He did? A letter? How charming! I wish he would just approach me directly, but of course he must worry about how that would look. My family wouldn't approve.\n\nI'll read his message in private. Oh, how exciting! Thank you.
Really? By Mara's grace, I hope she agrees to let me court her properly! I'll convince her father I'm worthy of her hand. \n\nAnyway, I believe I owe you a song. What was it again?
Nothing more suitable when love is in the air. All right. I'll get started right away!

I see. Hmm. Clearly Duchess Elea's investigation hasn't gotten very far. Perhaps we can make better use of the leads she's been developing.\n\nBut we have little time to waste. The Ascendant Magus demonstrated real power.

Among the other problems plaguing High Isle, lava vents have begun to open in random locations. Between the ground shaking and the storms, could the Magus have stirred the volcano?\n\nLet's return to my manor so we can study these items more closely.
Queen Ayrenn suggests subterfuge. They seek the nobles. Let's give them one.

So all three alliance delegates still live? Good.\n\nAs soon as I came ashore, I was set upon by the Serpents. I made the bastards pay, but even the son of Jorunn the Skald-King can't fight an entire prison gang on his own. There were too many of them.

Not a lot. Lady Arabelle, Lord Bacaro and some of his top aides, the three captains. Duchess Elea and a few nobles. And anyone the alliance leaders shared it with. \n\nIf there's one thing I learned about royal courts, they leak like a sinking ship.

We met briefly early on. Then we each sailed different, indirect routes to get here. I didn't rendezvous with the other ships until we were almost at the archipelago.\n\nAnyway, I guess this shows us how the Ascendant Order rewards its agents.

Look around. These traitors survived the storm and the shipwrecks and returned here, just like they were told to. And what did they get for their trouble? A blade to the heart for each of them.\n\nCome on. Let's get out of here and tell Lady Arabelle.

As I understand it, this grove was deemed sacred by the early druids, but it was also out of balance. They shaped Y'ffre's laws into a spirit and gave that spirit dominion over the grove.\n\nIt recognized that I was trying to help it and reached out.

The rune is a precaution, nothing more. These minstrels are a spirited bunch. It's not unlikely that they'll challenge you on sight. \n\nI prefer to keep my friends whole, especially when they're assisting me in such a noble pursuit!

Safe? This celebration is about to kill its own attendants with mediocrity! \n\nTrust me, friend. These minstrels won't attack while the rune of compulsion has a hold on them. And the specific vintages I've listed will calm them down.

Yes, but is that druid acting out of malice or ignorance? Either way, if the Evergrowth succumbs, then the corruption will increase and spread out of control.\n\nWe must take this news to the circle elders. Meet me in our village.

Lord Bacaro and I have a secure place. They'll be safe enough there.\n\nSo far we've been on the defensive, reacting to events. The time has come to take the fight to the Ascendant Order. And my plan starts with this meeting you heard about on Amenos.

And I think I know how to determine where this assemblage will take place. While you were away, I received reports of Ascendant Order activity at Mistmouth Cave.\n\nI propose we investigate. And, if luck is with us, catch ourselves a Lord and a Magus.

The far dock. That's not a House Dufort ship out there. Assuming Arnauld's a prisoner, that's where I'd stash him. \n\nIf we want to talk to him, we better act now. I don't think the good dockmaster is long for this world.
Let's just make our way to that ship and see if the dockmaster is aboard.

Normally House Dufort knights would be all over the place, but I haven't seen a one. Ascendant Order, though. That's a different story. They're guarding the docks between us and that ship.\n\nWhoever they paid to get rid of the knights hit the jackpot.

Hah! I could make a career of it, if I thought I had the patience. I'm still not sure how Jakarn got entangled with this whole affair, but you can be sure a pretty face is involved.\n\nLet's just hope the poor fool is still alive.

A rake. A rogue. A fool. I don't know how he got into this mess, but I can assure you a pretty face is involved. If he weren't so good at gaining the confidence of wealthy people, I'd have marooned him on some rock long ago.\n\nHope he's not dead.

You're right. I let the gold blind me! But look, I knew nothing about special cargo, or important passengers, or Amenos, or any of it.\n\nEven Lady Arabelle said the ships were just carrying supplies vital for Lord Bacaro's conference.

It's an island to the north. A jungle rock where they send prisoners to disappear. The Magus gave orders to look for someone on Amenos. Whoever he's searching for, he moved his knights from the Shallows to there.\n\nThat's all I know! Cut me free!

I gave the Ascendant Magus a list of names. Folks he could trust to keep quiet. Muscle to collect the goods when the ships ran aground.\n\nBut it was all a sham. They captured the captains, then gave orders to kill anyone else who washed ashore!

Worried about me? Oh, pish-posh! I was dealing with brigands, trolls, and threats to the realm since well before Ranser launched his ill-fated little war. There's nothing in this archipelago that I can't handle. \n\nBut thanks for your concern, dear.

Not as safe as they could be. Lord Bacaro, Valessea, and I arranged for the Mages Guild to protect the conference site on All Flags Islet with powerful defensive spells. \n\nI'll rest easier with the delegates safely behind those wards.

I know the feeling. I couldn't keep it all straight without my notebooks.\n\nThe Ascendant Order wants to kill the leaders of the three alliances. They sent a storm to sink the ships carrying them here for the peace conference.

Sergeant Brusic survived the wreck? The Sea Elves said he was as good as dead.\n\nThey regretted leaving him there as soon as those druids locked us all up. The sergeant and I take care of our prisoners.

That would be Chyrisnia. She offered to pick the lock on this cage, but I couldn't leave these two. Seeing the druids when they … killed Sunigil and the others, it broke their spirits. \n\nChyrisnia's many things, but she's not a liar.

Help me investigate. Search the village for any signs that a druid is involved in the corruption. Look in the huts, ask my fellow druids. Someone or something here will lead us to the source of the corruption. It has to.

She grasped my soul as though I were still a man of flesh, but lifted me like a child.\n\nAs you saw, Amunara's patience has run out. I underestimated her. She'll raze the whole fortress for the shield. The quicker you pass the final trial, the better.

We'll wait and see if it communicates with us again. If not, I have an idea. But let us try to find the druid responsible for this situation first. I want to determine if this was an accident … or a deliberate and reckless act.

Oh! I read that one, with the Windsorrow lady, right? What if my spell disturbed her and that's why the motes are acting up? That's … troubling. And also a problem for future Ember.\n\nLet's focus on one thing at a time. Or, two things, actually.

The traps are finished, but the livestock and Huldressa are still a problem. I want to figure out a way to return them all to their natural forms before the illusion does any damage.\n\nCould you set the traps while I do that?

I was too ambitious with the original spell—messing with things I shouldn't, adjusting bits without testing. Magic can be temperamental, but I know what I'm doing. So long as I stick to the basics, I can fix this. No more experimenting, promise.

No. He told me to present myself to a guild hall. But the idea of sitting in classrooms and having people blah blah blah at me all day? Not for this Khajiit.\n\nInstead, I showed up here. I think Magister Irin was amused more than anything.

I've been on my own for almost as long as I can remember. I have very few memories of my mother, but I know she spoke beautifully. Or at least, that's how I remember it.  \n\nBut she died when I was very young. The streets raised me after that.

I grew up in Skywatch but after that, I was doing odd jobs—working merchant caravans and so on. Magister Irin and I crossed paths and he saw me doing a bit of magic for one of my employers. He approached me and said I should be trained properly.

When you say it like that, you make it sound bad! I just took the opportunity to be a little more … daring. Magister Irin is great, but he's old fashioned. He wants me to learn things the right way—slowly, responsibly, and in a stuffy guild hall.

I just have no desire to sit around and learn from books when I could be learning by doing! I'm sure that's the way for some, but not for me. \n\nMagister Irin means well, and he's been a great teacher, but he wants me to be more restrained.

I lived there for most of my life. I have many happy memories there but a good deal of unhappy ones too. I used to have a crew there, a good one. Me and three others. We were just kids, but we did pretty well for ourselves.

I was not the only one with a difficult life, nor will I be the last. But it's all right, it was all I knew. I wasn't bemoaning my fate or lack of a permanent roof over my head all the time. I had a lot of freedom at least.

Nasty breed of deep-sea crustacean. They make dreugh seem like purring kittens. It's rare to find them on land, so it's just our luck that there's a whole brood foaming at the jaws to get into that ruin … but I suppose they're doing us a favor.

Ascendant Order. Abyssal Cabal. Maybe we can toss an Average Assembly in for good measure!\n\nLook, I don't know what that means and I don't think I want to. All that matters is Jakarn and what he was supposed to deliver.
I can grieve later. I'll hold up a flagon in her memory and sing one of those songs we learned together. \n\nAnd, of course, wear her ridiculous hat.
I know. We … we can talk about it later. Now then. Ahem.\n\nWe need to find the bloodmage and put an end to his murderous ways. Will you join me?

We're not sure yet. Based on everything that Lady Arabelle has told me, it's conceivable that the Ascendant Magus could be responsible for the disturbance here.\n\nRyvana is trying to locate its source. We could use your help.

Bloomingsong flowers grow in the copse of trees just north of here. You'll know them by their distinct blue and purple petals.\n\nAs for the torchbug, Ryvana told me they congregate near the lake at the heart of the grove. They are quite beautiful!

Ryvana's ritual is somewhat involved, and I'd like to help her prepare. Can you gather some reagents that we'll need?\n\nShe requires three bloomingsong flowers and an azure torchbug before we can begin.

I'll greet more newcomers to the festival. See if they're interested in earning the favor of our god. When that's done, I'll enjoy the festival myself.  Artisans and merchants are here from all over to share their goods, crafts, and cultures.
Amminus Varo and I will make for the nearest abbey and see if they have need of our services. After that, we'll go where we are sent. Providing our labor and skills where we can.

Me? I'm no one special, my dear. I've been an adventurer, a Lion Guard officer, a spy, a diplomat. People claim the Investigator Vale stories are about me. Or that I wrote them. Ridiculous. \n\nI'm retired now, but I still dabble from time to time.

All things are connected. Spirits of nature reside in the swaying trees, the blooming flowers, the glittering torchbugs.\n\nIt can be difficult to hear their songs, even for those of us who listen. But it's there. Can you hear it?

You come to the Trial of Constitution. How much pain can you endure, challenger? We shall soon find out.\n\nFind a way to unlock the exit without dying. None have passed this final room since before Lady Garick sailed.
I perform the ritual and we see where this trail leads.\n\nStand back. This will only take a moment.

The grove is in pain, projecting a sorrow that's felt by everything nearby.\n\nThis ritual will ask the rocks and the trees and the insects to simply share what they know. To lead us to the source of this disturbance. There, we might find answers.

My charming personality? When I was an agent for High King Emeric, I traveled widely and met many dignitaries—including Lord Bacaro.\n\nHe asked me to make sure everything went smoothly for his conference. So far, it's been anything but.
I'm overseeing security for the conference. A few months ago, Lord Bacaro approached me. Explained his grand plans and lured me out of retirement, you might say.
Wherever you think is best, my dear. But do get started soon. My intuition tells me that some sort of mischief is afoot, and my intuition is rarely wrong.

Nothing specific, I'm afraid. Just that the corrupted animals have made foraging in the grove dangerous. \n\nOh, this might interest you. I felt a disturbance emanate from the wards in the Undergrove recently. Like a surge of power went through them.

Ah, good. Then I can skip trying to convince you. But I promise to pay fairly should we succeed.\n\nI need to track down this affliction's source. Only patients at the manor seem affected. So I assume the cause must be nearby.
Let me see that again.\n\nHmm. Yes, the Ascendant Magus thinks he can draw on the volcano to lend power to his spells. The next target they attack, he'll have more control over his ritual.

Sadly, very little. The menders stay busy tending to the afflicted. And the patients don't quite trust me enough to talk freely.\n\nSo, I need you. If you track down the cause of this malady, perhaps the menders can do something about it.

Of course! It becomes quite clear when you put all the pieces together. The Duforts have interred their dead in the vaults beneath their castle for centuries. The Order must be meeting in the Navire Dungeons!\n\nI'll collect Jakarn and meet you there.

Below the Sleeping Knights? What could that mean? Statues? Or … bodies.\n\nI suspect we're looking for catacombs again, like the ones we found beneath Abhain Chapel. But I saw no Sleeping Knights there.

They are well funded and have a strong presence on the mainland. They proclaim a powerful message about greedy rulers and costly wars, but it's mostly rhetoric. Not that the commonfolk see that.\n\nOur conference makes a tempting target, I'm sure.

Not much, I'm afraid. He's an alchemist in Summerset. And he's interested in creating potions and powders that protect against fire.\n\nThat was all Tarrinore and I needed to know. We asked around about him, confirmed the job, and came here.

By using the summons we found in Mistmouth Cave, naturally. Take Jakarn with you and present the note if anyone tries to stop you. Once inside, confront the Ascendant Magus and disrupt whatever plan the Order has in motion.\n\nSimple as that, dear.

The archdruid sought to renew our bindings, but the ancient spells had already frayed. The part of us that is the Allwither tricked her. She spoke the wrong word. Now the Allwither is free to spread its corruption, and the entire grove is in danger.
Who does under the armor and hoods? I threw together some Ascendant Order outfits for the two of you. All you need to do is act like you belong there.\n\nHere, try them on.

The Allwither is a part of us, a spirit of nature called forth and made manifest by the ancient druids. At this sacred grove, the laws of nature are malleable. To strengthen those laws, the druids bound us here.\n\nBut nature consists of circles.

At one end, life. At the other, death. We are both life-nurturing growth and all-withering decay. That part of us is now free. And once the corruption fully takes hold, the Evergrowth will be gone. Only the Allwither will remain.\n\nWill you help us?

You need to recall the virtues you learned from the tablets after each Trial of Worth to answer each question, starting with this one:\n\nFaced with overwhelming odds, what must the bearer of the shield demonstrate?
Correct. Final question:\n\nThrough what quality will the bearer of the shield reach the pinnacle of their potential and ability?
Correct. Next question:\n\nWhat keeps the bearer of the shield stable and informs their choices?

We can, but only if you and this druid break the remaining wards that bind us to this place. That will allow us to recover enough of our power to restore the balance and return the Allwither to its proper location in the circle.

We are the spirit of the grove. We maintain the balance and keep the True Way. We know our duty and our responsibility. Trust us. Together we can end the corruption and return the grove to its natural state.\n\nBut decide quickly. We do not have long.

The entrance I am aware of is in the northern part of the grove. I will meet you there.\n\nI have never been in the Undergrove, my friend. I have no idea what we might encounter down there. So be on your guard and ready for anything.

That's not anything we need to worry about. The Ascendant Order promises a better life for the likes of you and I. They haven't lied to us yet. I trust them.\n\nThe nobles of High Isle are afraid to leave their estates. And they should be.

Know who he is? I should hope not! The Order has many enemies, and the anonymity of our leaders is a shield against them. \n\nWhy, everybody knows not to—ah, this is a test, isn't it? I shall reveal none of the Order's secrets, I assure you!

My father served King Ranser. He served his lord faithfully and defended Shornhelm with all his strength. For that, High King Emeric named him rebel, brigand, and murderer. Then they hanged him.\n\nTime for a new king. Or no king at all.
Let me see that. Hmm. That's the Ascendant Magus's seal, all right.\n\nVery well, you can go in. But enter quietly. You're quite late and the meeting has already started.
Incorrect, try again.\n\nFaced with overwhelming odds, what must the bearer of the shield demonstrate?
Incorrect, try again.\n\nFaced with overwhelming odds, what must the bearer of the shield demonstrate?
Incorrect, try again.\n\nWhat keeps the bearer of the shield stable and informs their choices?
Incorrect, try again.\n\nWhat keeps the bearer of the shield stable and informs their choices?
Incorrect, try again.\n\nThrough what quality will the bearer of the shield reach the pinnacle of their potential and ability?
Incorrect, try again.\n\nThrough what quality will the bearer of the shield reach the pinnacle of their potential and ability?
Terrible shame. Roslenn was one of our best healers. Incredibly talented. Her loss has really made things hard around here, but we're doing the best we can.\n\nWhat can I do to help?

Hard to argue with that. She is a talented healer, perhaps more than I am. \n\nVery well. If you think it may help, then take this key and have a look. Please do your utmost to keep things as they are.

Oh? Well, if you find yourself in need of work, we'd be delighted to offer you a position in the future. We can always use a skilled alchemist.\n\nHere's a key to the dispensary. Please be careful in there.

Look, I appreciate your concern. I really do. Roslenn's absence impedes our work here. Unfortunately, I can't simply allow anyone to just muck about in the dispensary. Especially an unknown adventurer.\n\nNow I must get back to work, thank you.

I'm afraid that's out of the question. I'm sure you have good intentions, but our dispensary is full of sensitive—even dangerous—materials. It's imperative nothing there be disturbed. Lives depend on it.

They are delegates too! <<1>> is very important Elf from Aldmeri Dominion. And <<2>> is noble Orc from Daggerfall Covenant who brings culture wherever he goes.\n\nI don't remember what we talked about. It must have been another diplomatic success!

A better quartermaster you won't find. He's meticulous—knows the whereabouts of every rope and biscuit that comes aboard. \n\nOblan always manages to get exactly what our crew needs. Even if their requirements are … less than accessible.

Can I see it? \n\nThis is Roslenn's, all right. Hmm … an illness related to vampirism? I might not have any more book-learning than you need to swing a sword, but I think I would've noticed a vampire hanging around. What's going on here?

Oh, you're with this … Nord?\n\nI'm not all that worried about what he left here. I'm worried about what he took—a night's worth of food, drink, and entertainment, all without paying! He and his friends skipped out on their bill.

Beware of the harpies. They can be vicious.\n\nI'd go with you, but I don't dare leave the patients alone with the menders—or with each other. Not if they're fighting off some kind of vampire-sickness.
I can see that. And look, here's something about harpy feathers. If Roslenn went looking for harpy nests, maybe we should too.\n\nShe says the nests are nearby. Shouldn't be hard to find.

Like I said, they ate and drank all night in a private room. When I noticed it was too quiet, I looked in and they were all gone.\n\nSomeone's got to settle up. Your friend left his scepter? It'll do as collateral until I get paid.
In the spirit of cultural bridge-building, I joined <<1>> and Rigurt for dinner. A routine exchange, but Rigurt ordered food and drinks all night long.\n\nWhy? What's going on?

Oh. I'm afraid I have no idea if I paid or not. I don't even remember leaving the inn. It's entirely possible that I forgot to contribute toward the bill in my condition.\n\nWhat in the world did I have to drink?

Rigurt! He got me into this mess. Last night after dinner we were talking about our favorite places in Wrothgar. He disappeared into the back and returned with a bag.\n\nHe said something about getting a dessert for me.

I left. On my way home this guard stopped me. I told him what I thought about that, so he frisked me. It turns out the bag was filled with skooma! I didn't know, I swear!\n\nCan you talk to <<1>>? I've got diplomatic immunity!

Back on my ship, preparing to make a quick escape once I have what I came for. Wouldn't do me much good if I brought the lot of them. They make better sailors than sneaks or soldiers. Hope you're more suited to this sort of caper.

Truly? I thought there was just one way to become a vampire, and it involved a bite to the neck. How do you know so much about vampirism? Well, no matter.\n\nThis mention of harpy nests might be a lead. Perhaps you should check it out?

I made something. I know it looks like a spoon but … well, technically it is a spoon. But I enchanted it, and I call it the Spoon of Undo!\n\nI just tested it on those chickens. It removes the illusions perfectly.

Normally I wouldn't bother, but illusions can be disorienting and cause terrible headaches. I don't want any of the animals suffering while I come up with my counterspell.\n\nOh, and Huldressa. I suppose I don't really want her suffering either.
Hah, it sounds cute when you say it. \n\nIt's a pretty simple reversing enchantment. It should counteract the magic from the motes and dispel the illusion. Basic stuff not even I can mess up.

Well, they're still animals. They might run around a bit, but I doubt they'll make it too difficult for you. They're not exactly geniuses.\n\nPersonally, if I was a sheep, and got turned into a human, I think I'd go off on an adventure.

I wasn't trying to turn animals into people, I swear. I had a theory about animating the inanimate. One of Magister Irin's texts gave me the idea. Hmm. That's probably why he locks so many of his books away, now that I think about it.

Well, I'm hoping to avoid that scenario. But if it does happen, I'm not sure. He's an odd one. I'm too old for him to punish and he's not really the type to dole out discipline anyway.\n\nI think he'd be disappointed. Which is so, so much worse.
I'm sure it's painfully obvious at this point that you've found me in this predicament. Perhaps you could help me out of it?
Look, this is embarrassing enough as it is. Perhaps you can help get me down by completing the Breton's task. I'll tell you all about it.
Where is that Breton? He said he'd be right back!

I have that singular fortune. My wife is away, entreating House Mornard for more sentries. She's better at handling Meryline. \n\nI don't agree with my daughter's actions, but her instinct to bring you here was good. I could use your skills.

They lost their ship? How'd they do that? Not as if it's a set of loose keys or a wayward dog. Doesn't matter. What matters is the food that cat stole from me!\n\nThe lads and I might be able to help find this ship, but not before you get me some tack!

You need me to—? Oh, you're one of those crazy people who gets their food from a merchant. Traders, putting their greedy little fingers all over your fish and potatoes …. It's disgusting! Isn't that right, lads?\n\nI get my food the right way!

And now my daughter is sharing our secrets.\n\nYes. The mine is in a state of disarray. Creatures known as Hadolids invaded the lower tunnels. Work's stopped. Sentries and prisoners are dead. I can barely hold the mine with the forces I have left.

Give me your map. The towers around the mine reported that a caravan laden with medical supplies was drawing near. They've yet to arrive. Find out what's keeping them.\n\nWe're desperately low on bandages. Don't dally.

A week's worth! Might seem like a day's worth to fat-fingered Tamsfolk like you, but I'm frugal. I make things last!\n\nI'll free the cat if you snatch up some vittles from the shore. I won't risk another run-in with those damn fish-elves!

That you did, that you did. Thank you.\n\nYour friend Jimila here's got a silver tongue. Talked me into cutting down her quartermaster before he passed out. He still passed out, though. For a bit. It was that boom what woke him up. What was that?
That, my friend, is a story I've not told in a long time. Six years on, the terror is still too close ….

Ha ha! You hear that, lads? Fish Elves blasted themselves to bits! To Oblivion with the lot of them, I say! Ha!\n\nOf course, their crewmates might have found some more. Dangerous stuff. That's troubling. Why don't you talk to Jimila. I need to think.
Traitors? This confirms our suspicions. But lodestones are powerful arcane focuses. What else did you discover, dear?

So the Ascendant Magus isn't infallible. That's good to know. And the evidence we've uncovered up to this point tells us the Order believes the alliance leaders are still alive. They're actively hunting for them.\n\nWe must find them first!

My ship! The Kamal's Bane! I thought I lost her forever! \n\nShe washed ashore on the Shoals, thank the Hist. It took me some time to reach this spot without being detected, but now that you're here we can see what remains of my vessel.
She will never sail again, but at least it will be good to see her one last time. And perhaps we can find some indication of what happened to my passenger, Prince Irnskar of Windhelm.

Roslenn? She tried to free me, but Viralaine returned and overpowered her.\n\nThis is his laboratory. He experiments on me, hoping he can use my blood to heal the wounded. It's madness. I'm afraid he drugged Roslenn … with my blood.

My blood, my strain of this curse, induces deep dreaming. When I bite someone, they later fall into a deep sleep … with horrific nightmares. A concentrated dose of my blood has the same effect. Immediately. \n\nI hate what my hunger does.

Viralaine? Surely you're joking! Why would—wait, it's coming back to me. \n\nI was looking for harpy feathers in the forest. But a bloodfiend attacked me! I fled into this cave, and I found Seraphyne here in a cage. But then … ooh, my head.

That's horrible! No wonder I noticed traces of vampirism! Yes, Vampire blood can speed recovery, but it's very risky. I know Viralaine thought our methods were slow, but still ….\n\nWe must confront him. Together, if Seraphyne's willing.

I won't lie—it's not easy. But there are alchemical methods that have proved effective in the past. It really comes down to the Vampire in question. Does she want to be cured?\n\nI think the answer in Seraphyne's case is yes.

If you're asking if I will fully recover, then … I don't know. I need to study the potion Viralaine fed us. I hope so.\n\nMentally? This betrayal stings. I trusted Alexis Viralaine. We both swore to heal the sick, not make them worse.

At least I finally did something good with this curse of mine. I hope she takes down that monster Viralaine and makes him pay for all this.\n\nI am so angry I could rip his throat out—no. That's my curse, not me. I need to end this. Somehow.
All right, I'll make my way there. \n\nSometimes Viralaine said that the mere sight of my eyes unnerved him. Well, he's seen nothing yet.
Of course I'll help. Anything to bring that monster down. Even if it means allowing others to see what I am.
It's no lie that the High Elves train gryphons for war, though I've never seen one attack a ship at sea. If this is the same Varallion, we'd be wise to keep an eye to the skies.

It was this unholy screeching, like the world's largest seagull was coming for my potato fritters. Might have been my imagination, or the knock on the head. I was out cold before I could even take a look.

They want to know who I was making the delivery to, so I guess they don't know everything. Lucky for me. I don't get the feeling they'd have kept me alive otherwise. What're a few lumps by comparison?

But still better than most, right? Luckily, they spared my face most of the punishment. Must be that High Elf appreciation for beauty. Heh.\n\nDon't worry your pretty little head over me. It'll take more than a few love taps to sink old Jakarn.

A very special lady. Very pretty. Very rich. That's all you need to know.\n\nThis debacle is going to blacken her adoring eye if I don't go above and beyond to save face. A little embellishment couldn't hurt. And a lot of flattery.

Exhausting. Jakarn's a handful at the best of times, but he's still trustworthy enough. In this cutthroat business, that makes him worth the trouble he causes. Most of the time.\n\nStill, I'll be glad to have him out of my hair for a while after this.

While you were helping my prisoners, I got my bearings out here. We're not that far from Brokerock Mine. I've made the run there a time or two in the past. \n\nWe can make it there and get the assistance we need to make it back to Amenos Station.

You have not heard of them? They are a group that opposes the Three Banners War. Their methods of protest are usually nonviolent, so this one finds it odd that they would be associated with a kidnapping. \n\nBut this is not Tarazka's affair.

The less Tarazka talks about that, the better. This one has known Jakarn a long time and has suffered his flippant attitude from the beginning. He is a thief with a silver tongue and a charming smile. There is no combination that is more obnoxious.
Tarazka is no hero. Jakarn asked for information, and this one has provided. And now that unclawed idiot owes Tarazka even more.
It was so close to the mine. What attacked them?\n\nIt looks like a beast tore them apart. But which one? Could—could it be the Hadolids?
It couldn't have been the prisoner gangs. They left a lot of supplies behind.\n\nIs this what adventuring is like? Seeing the people you grew up with … like this?
Oh? Well, that means he can't yell at you if he catches me out here. \n\nWhat did he ask you to do?

Bandits! Lazy vagabonds who survive off the work of others. They're a blight in Zenithar's palm! \n\nThe leaders of this village tell me the Greycloaks new leader—Stigthar— is a charming fellow with impeccable manners and a mean glint in his eye.

Would-be emperors have brought nothing but conflict and turmoil to Tamriel. Lord Bacaro is a fool to think peace can be won with gentle words. \n\nIt's time to throw down those who aspire to the Ruby Throne—and mete out justice with the sword.

You really don't know? I suppose even the legendary skills of Lady Arabelle Davaux were no match for the Ascendant Lord and his brilliant strategy.\n\nBut come now. You've worked beside the investigator. Surely you've learned something. Make a guess.

We will assume power and put an end to this wretched war. Strength can win the peace Lord Bacaro hopes for. Hard choices must be made, but one day the peoples of Tamriel will thank us.  \n\nA pity you are too blind to see this simple truth.

Adwig was telling us about a pirate cove to the north. Apparently, it's crawling with Sea Elves, but if the Prowler is still anchored here, that's where it will be. \n\nYou and I should go. The others can meet up with us once Oblan recovers.

Well done! Perhaps you are a worthy foe. Still, it's too late to stop me. If only Lady Arabelle were here to witness this.\n\nAh, but she is. My knights found her outside. She faces justice in the dungeons below. If you hurry, maybe you can save her.

Adwig promised not to hang Oblan upside down again, so there's that at least. He seems anxious to leave Amenos … and also anxious to stay. Difficult to say. I think he will help us, though.\n\nOnce they're ready, they'll find us near the cove.

Let me see. <<1>> didn't seem to be having fun so I bought her a special drink. And then <<2>> wanted dessert. I asked the man in the back for something sweet so my friends could have a good time.\n\nWe headed back to our own lodgings after that.

Damard Dufort! There was something familiar about that voice, but I couldn't place it. When he captured me, I no doubt became the perfect distraction to use against you. Sorry, about that, dear.\n\nStill, thank you for coming to my rescue.

I'm very observant, dear. Duchess Elea's new flagship is the largest vessel ever constructed by the Dufort Shipyards. The duchess planned to inspect her today, which gives us another reason to hurry. Who knows what Count Damard will do to his sister?

Where I just sent the delegates? Damn it!\n\nVery well. We're close to the Navire Docks. If Count Damard is launching a naval attack he'll want the Silver Swan, assuming she's seaworthy. If we hurry, we might catch him before he sets sail.
Ridiculous. You slander House Dufort at your own peril.\n\nI assure you, no one but House Dufort retainers are permitted in this area. Their loyalty is unquestioned.

I see no rogue knights here or hostile ships off our shore. Enough of this nonsense! The only threat here is you!\n\nThe duchess plans to sail with the tide. If I catch any of you sneaking around these docks, I will have you flogged. Away with you!

I came to inspect my new flagship. When I arrived, Steward Hercian led me to my cabin and locked the door! He said we were to set sail. That I would be kept safe until the Ascendant Order finished their work. I have no idea what he was talking about!

My brother is the Ascendant Magus? I assure you, I had no idea. I have nothing to do with those rogue knights! They are dangerous rebels and outlaws. Why, they even convinced my own steward to kidnap me!

Let me see. A contingency plan, eh?\n\nThe Ascendant Order expected the alliance leaders to drown in the shipwreck. But it seems they were prepared to launch a direct attack on All Flags Islet if all else failed. And now it has come to that.

Because if The Mirrored Way isn't with the rest of his things, it's probably locked away in his arcane library. The library he specifically forbids me from entering. \n\n The tome I need has to be in there. Without it, I can't make the counterspell.

Resonance crystals. The prisoners carry them to amplify the mine's sounds and help warn them of any collapses. But I used them to make my songs louder too.\n\nDid the glow scare the Hadolids off? No. It was the music!

Magister Irin has warned me not to enter his library a thousand times … but these are special circumstances.\n\nThere will probably be some magical traps inside meant to keep me out, so I'll need your help getting the book while I deal with them.

Let me take a look. Mmm … mhmm. No, not that, that would be bad. What about this?\n\nOh! Here it is. It's amahan'ist'exis, not gahan'amexis'ist! Good thing I checked. See? That's personal growth right there.

Two different arcane glyphs. They do entirely different things when written and pronounced aloud. The second one is what I need for my counterspell.\n\nNow, all that's left is to get to the old ritual circle and cast this. I'll need your help again.

I work for House Dufort. We coordinate the efforts of High Isle's knightly orders, local lords, merchants, and even friendly druids to handle unusual problems. I act as a broker, matching up adventurers like you with jobs that need doing.

That depends on who requests the work. Personally, I'm an employee of House Dufort. They more or less run things here on High Isle. But I represent merchants, knightly orders, and wealthy individuals who require help and have the gold to pay.

You misunderstand. I'm not the hirer, just an agent. More of an administrator, really. I make sure the job brokers are on the up and up.\n\nSpeak to <<1>>, <<2>>, or <<3>>. They hire adventurers on a daily basis.

I did indeed! There are important happenings going on right now. So important even I don't know all the details. But that means the guards and the knights are extremely busy. So the nobles sent me to oversee the job brokers and recruit help.

Common? I wouldn't say that. But much of the archipelago is wilderness. There are parts of High Isle that have never really been settled. Venture away from the city, and you'll find hostile druids, dangerous beasts, dark knights, and more!

<<1>> represents business interests in Gonfalon Bay. They're more than willing to pay for an adventurer's help to acquire items or gather components from specific locations.\n\nA single adventurer can usually handle these tasks on their own.

Sometimes the Systres Guard and the various knightly orders need a little help. Especially with the terrible monsters that lurk in the islands' wild places.\n\nParisse recruits adventurers for these tough jobs. You'll need a group to deal with these.
Curiosity with a dash of prudence. Good qualities for an adventurer. Means you'll live longer.\n\nAll right, who do you want me to tell you about?

That's not really in my sphere of influence. But the noble houses and the Society of the Steadfast are gathering delegates for some sort of meeting here on High Isle.\n\nWhatever's going on, it's got the guards and the knightly orders hopping.

Adwig knows a secret entrance into the cove, but it's risky. Not much cover. We're going to need a distraction, and that's where the kindlepitch comes in.\n\nYou don't mind taking on a dangerous mission do you? I mean, a more dangerous mission.

I'll tell her once she's calmed down. \n\nVinilsare's a lot better at finding clients than I am. We're a team. She figures out how to get jobs and I make sure we complete them. She doesn't like my methods, especially now, but it's worth the risk.

It won't be lumps of volcanic rock that do it. Those will just help expand our client list and make us some gold quickly. No, the boost this gives our reputation will change their minds. \n\nWhenever they want a rare material, they'll think of us!

I need you to lead Oblan to an overlook—it's got a perfect view of the Elves' flagship.\n\nNow, here's the tough part. You need to board the Sea Elf ship, place kindlepitch all over it, then signal Oblan to loose a fiery arrow onto the deck.

She'll live, but healing takes time. Who knows how long we'll stay here.\n\nI plan on getting on a ship back to Summerset as soon as possible. This archipelago is beautiful, but nothing compares to the shining isle.
I'll survive, not everyone was so lucky. We'll be digging graves tomorrow. Hopefully not for the Overseer. Or his daughter. \n\nPlease, follow her. I can't do much to help against the Hadolids now.

I don't know what I expected leaving her to her own devices here, even temporarily. Ember and trouble are old friends.\n\nI can still feel the repercussions of this spell gone … awry, as you say. Do I have you to thank for rectifying it?

I took her in because I knew I couldn't leave someone as skilled and impulsive as her to her own devices, but I have neither the time nor aptitude to teach her properly. It's my own failing.\n\nSpeak to her, would you? I must collect my thoughts.

Well, Jimila and I have been through a lot and she's never steered me wrong. We may have our differences now and again but I trust her with my life.\n\nAnd if she trusts you, I trust you. You're trustworthy, right?

Yes. You're going to lead me to the overlook above the cove so I can get a gull's eye view of the Sea Elves' ship. Once you plant the kindlepitch and give me the signal, I'll loose a fiery arrow onto the deck.\n\nThen … boom!
Go to the Sea Elves' flagship, place the kindlepitch, signal Oblan. Oh and don't forget the key I just told you about or we won't get very far!
From what Ennoc told me, it sounded like the attack just happened. \n\nMaybe if I'd been faster at the caravan, we could've rescued father.
Good. Tend to them as best you can. I'll see if the song works on the Hadolids. \n\nI think I know what happened before and how to recreate it.
I won't go far. If the Hadolids keep coming, I'll run to you and we'll make our stand. It'll be the two of us against … all of them.\n\nNo pressure, right?

Thorley and I know what we're doing. And that prisoner over there—Beletin—is spoiling for a fight. We'll be fine. \n\nBesides, if you two made it here, then I'm sure the way back outside is safe enough. We'll go there and reinforce the camp.

I didn't see him, no. But, we heard those monsters screaming in pain. Couldn't make sense of it until now. The overseer has a reputation for being fearsome in battle. \n\nThe sounds disappeared deeper into the mine.

I think <<1>> is staying at Steadfast Manor, a little way outside of town. She likes Lord Bacaro's gardens. <<2>> rented a small house in Gonfalon Bay near the west gate.\n\nHere. I'll be right behind you. When my head stops spinning.
Meryline saw all of that and she's still in here? No, why am I surprised? Of course she'd stay.\n\nI held off those foul beasts as long as I could. Do whatever you can to get them out of my mine.
They must have some reason to remain here. Kill them. Poison the tunnels. I don't care. \n\nI'm leaving and I'm taking my daughter and all my sentries with me. It's far too dangerous here.

Meryline still thinks the prisoners here are her friends! She never fully understood the dangers of Amenos and I wouldn't be a good father if I left her to discover it now.\n\nDon't leave these tunnels until they're safe.

Because losing sight of her while we're in a mine in Glenumbra is vastly different from her mad dash into this largely unexplored, lava-filled cave!\n\nShe's unarmed, distracted, and directionless. I have the only map we made!

Despite what father thinks, I know what I can do. My magic is useful. I can help.\n\nBesides, I wasn't going to let you go down there by yourself. I'm the reason you're in these tunnels. I won't abandon you.
Before today, I didn't even know that the resonance crystals—and my own magic—could keep monsters from attacking. Now look at where we are!
Chin up, friend! \n\nWe can't prepare for something we don't know about. Whatever happens deeper in the mines will happen. Let's deal with it then, yeah?
Have you lost your senses? Why in the name of Ruptga's starry britches do you want to go inside? There's nothing but murderers, cut-purses, and thieves in there. They'll eat you alive!

Only if it's still attached to a vulk'esh. Or, maybe if a crazed alchemist gets her hands on it. But I interview all our clients before we agree to work with them. We only work with artisans in good moral standing. We have a reputation to uphold.

No! Well, yes. A bit. But, no, it's the right decision. I took care of the lads for a long time. Built them a home, rigged traps, scraped old tack out of waterlogged barrels …. They've got all they need now.\n\nIt's time to say goodbye.

Of course I am! Adwig is strange, yes, but no stranger than other members of the crew. My boatswain wakes up twice a night screaming about sharks in the larder, and the purser can barely remember my name half the time.\n\nWe call this Prowler charm!
I'm sure the captain would appreciate that, but it's not really my forte. Trouble seems to find me, so I imagine I won't be able to avoid it.

As for finding a thief, I'd check the head jailer's office in the keep if I were you. You want to see if the thief you're looking for has been processed yet or not. The head jailer keeps a ledger with that information.

Just stories, really. Used to be a perfect, secluded place to weigh anchor before some terrible catastrophe made it impassible by sea, trapping countless ships. Heard a dozen tales claiming to tell how, but I only put stock in what my family says.

I do my research. Everyone in town says Jailer Omdil loves wine. They also say he's willing to look the other way in exchange for a free bottle every now and again.\n\nHe guards the back way into the stockade, which is perfect for your purposes.

Amenos Station is the only safe place on this damn rock. It consists of a port, a town, the prison stockade, and the jailers' keep. The rest of the island is a dangerous jungle full of ferocious beasts—and I don't just mean the prisoners!

North. House Mornard has a larger ship waiting for them. \n\nWe were tasked with taking the prisoners to the ship from Amenos Station. Their captain gave gold and her word that she wouldn't attack Mornard's ship in return for her crew's safe return.

It sprouted from the waves like some curse from nature. \n\nDozens of faces lost beneath the waves, prisoner and sentry alike. The lieutenant said the Sea Elves might act up, captain's bargain or no, But I've never seen one of them magic coral.

Piracy may be the work of scum, but it pays well. This lot was lucky to be caught. Most pirates go down with their ship. I suppose House Dufort felt charitable when their patrol ship captured this bunch.

One of the Breton noble houses. They govern Amenos Station and the prison stockade. The whole island is technically under their jurisdiction, but no one cares about the jungle. Well, except for the mines.

Stigthar is extremely dangerous. I wouldn't face him on my own.\n\nFind willing guild members, traveling adventurers passing through, or some other companionship to see you safely through this effort!

Valentyn, Valentyn … yeah, maybe I know such a person.\n\nYou seem the courageous sort. Let's make a trade. Help me get revenge on another inmate, and I'll point you in the right direction to find … what's-his-name.

Oh, nothing violent. A trusty named Yvara likes to make camp on the platform over there. All I need you to do is steal something from a jailer and place it in her bedroll. Simple as dirt.\n\nDo me this favor, and I'll tell you where to find Valentyn.

No need to get violent about it. Fine. I helped Valentyn sneak out of the stockade and into the caldera just before you got here. Said he needed to check something past the big tree and near where the waterfall plunges down.\n\nNow leave me be.

I was? What manner of unseemly laze-about was he? No, no, don't tell me, I don't want to spare a moment more of thought on him. Not when I can devote my attentions to the work ahead of me. \n\nWe have an offering to prepare.

No, not as such. Though there's one who's friendly with all the others. Chyrisnia. She got along with everyone and even thanked me a few times for their upkeep. \n\nDidn't think anything of the chatter before.
Our ship held fifteen, and ten sentries to keep watch over them.\n\nI only saw six prisoners and Veslyn flee the ship before it was too late. I was the last to make it off before it went under.

This lot seemed congenial enough, for pirates. Their captain paid well for their safe return. But taking a Sea Elf away from land? No, I can't believe they did this.\n\nPowerful Sea Elves make weather trouble. Not what we got. Not the coral.

I'm a sentry on a prison transport. I like the work all right. Sure, some prisoners give you trouble, but they quiet down after a few hits. Nothing bad ever happened prior to the shipwreck.\n\nThere's something sinister here. I know it.

Technically, other than the town, the entire island is a prison. They do something to the worst of the prisoners. Call it processing. Once done, they set them loose in the jungle and let them fend for themselves.\n\nIf they leave the jungle, they die.

Great! Listen carefully. Jailer Zalzay keeps his footlocker nearby and I happen to know he never locks it. Just reach in, grab something valuable, and stick it in Yvara's bedroll. She's got eyes like a hawk, though, so you might need to distract her.

That's one of the wonders of the archipelago, dear. The locals are very proud of their statue, even if few of them know the real story behind who it represents.\n\nI like it, as well. One of the reasons I bought the manor. Such a spectacular view.

In the tale, the symbols on the pillars held the key. Like the cat, there. A cat's paw is a pretty little flower that grows in shady forests.\n\nAnd that bird looks like a forest heron. I'd bet anything we need one of their feathers.
Oh my goodness! That's disgusting. No wonder I got sick!\n\nI promise I'll return to the inn and settle up soon. Now if you'll excuse me … all of the sudden I'm not feeling so good.

It was stolen. Now the weavers of this town feel slighted and their hands rest dejected. \n\nI fear Stigthar and his rowdy band of Greycloaks are behind this. Pah! Ruffians and thieves who steal the work of others. Their idle fingers besmirch the awl!

Bless another awl? When there is one within reach? The only thing that separates us from the awl is a bit of hard work. \n\nNo. I'll not even entertain the idea of praying for a replacement. The awl is whole. It has just been removed from my care.

While the awl was given to House Flonius, their duty is to share it with all the faithful. \n\nTrue devotees understand that Zenithar's blessings are meant to be spread, not hoarded. I fear I may be the reason the awl's gift was lost.
Excellent! My turn. I never renege on an agreement.\n\nValentyn arrived in the stockade earlier today. We got to talking and he asked me to help him slip into the caldera.

Valentyn said he needed to check something past the big tree, near where the waterfall plunges down. Head north out of the stockade until you see the river, then follow it toward the falls. My guess is you'll find him in the clearing to the west.
It's my job to guard the prisoners. I failed so many of them already, I'll not fail these, too. \n\nIf you open the door, I'm sure I'll be able to rally their spirits and get them out of here.

Marcelle? Why would she do that? She knew my plan was to get arrested and steal the Daybreak Gem. I let those jailers grab me on purpose!\n\nWell, at least it sounds like she has a better exit strategy than I devised.

I hoped the legend was wrong. That I'd only need the one key I already have. But alas, it requires three keys to open the vault. And now I know where to find them. \n\nHelp me survive the jungle and acquire the other keys, and I'll pay you handsomely.

Oh, yes! I am good diplomat, so I thought she would like something to remind her of home. After that, <<1>> kept asking for more drinks. We all laughed and had fun!\n\nWe said goodnight just outside. She got in her carriage and drove off for home.

If I had a gold coin for every criminal who tells me he's got friends in high places, I'd be a wealthy man. \n\nWord of warning, mainlander—make false statements to an officer of the law, and you'll be in front of the magistrate too.

Follow <<1>> and find where he keeps his contraband. I'll need you to bring me proof he's got skooma. We've tried to arrest him before, only to come up empty-handed.\n\nI saw Berjac in Gonfalon Square earlier. If you're in, start there.

They claim my ancestor sailed with one of the biggest fleets of freebooters in the Abecean. My family thinks they came here to divide the loot after a really big raid and turned on each other. It was a battle so big it closed off the bay.

When our pursuers cut us down, we rose up from the sea again and again. We couldn't be beaten, so we were buried. Bound here by that fool's pact until our bodies rotted and moldered away.\n\nPlease, you have to end it. Free us from this.
Let us make haste, master!

What happened here was out of our control. We'll make a report and get another ship to take the prisoners where they need to go. Mornard will see to the druids here. It might take some time, but the danger they pose won't be ignored.
Like I said, it's not too far. I've recovered my strength, Veslyn is none the worse for wear, and my prisoners will help us defend ourselves. Don't worry about us, we'll be fine.

Not sure. Usually, if we avoid them, the Eldertide Druids leave us alone. This was out of the ordinary. House Mornard will need to do something, but I don't know what.\n\nI'm just a sergeant, but I'll do what I can to put a stop to this.
She'll be angry, of that you can be certain. But the prisoners will tell her what happened. I suspect Chyrisnia will lead that charge.

I am so much more than a simple farmer. They only think of animals as a source of income. Or even, feh, food.\n\nNo, I am an animal steward! I serve each of the creatures under my care. Whatever their needs may be, I attend to them.

I regret that I didn't introduce myself when they arrived. Such a simple gesture from me could have prevented this crime.\n\nHadolids aren't soft like sheep. They're covered in hard shells with nasty spikes. Like overgrown mudcrabs. And the smell!

From the archipelago to the mainland, everything is war and fighting. But it doesn't have to be that way! I try to assume people have good intentions. And usually they do.\n\nMaybe this is all a misunderstanding. I can work that out later.

Not exactly. After that strange storm swept in and the ship hit the rocks, we were struggling to get to the small boats. A wave hit me and I thought that was the end.\n\nBut Prince Irnskar lifted me up, tossed me in a boat, and shoved it away.

The last I saw, he was alive and clinging to the part of the ship floating toward Amenos. Even through the storm, I could hear others in the water, but the winds were sending the wreckage in all directions.\n\nYou need to go find Prince Irnskar!

The Kamal's Bane started to break apart. The storm pushed us into the straits and the current was dragging most of the ship toward Amenos. \n\nI stayed in the small boat as long as I could, then I leaped into this piece of the wreckage and landed here.

Just that it's incredibly dangerous. The Dreadsails are some of the nastiest pirates we've ever seen and their pillaging has gotten out of control in recent months.\n\nIt's no wonder the admiral is out for blood.
Arrival confirmed. I'll make certain your pay is waiting for you when you return. One less worry to have on your mind before a large-scale battle.\n\nAre you ready to get started?
Dreadsail Reef, the Dreadsail pirate fleet's island hideaway. It's small, but the shallows are treacherous to navigate even without their Sea Mages meddling with the wind and tide.
<You are about to enter a Group Trial. Are you ready to leave your current Zone?>

Oh, if you've never had the misfortune of crossing a Maormer Sea Mage, you're in for an unpleasant surprise. I hear the Dreadsail leader is an especially powerful one.\n\nI've heard she's sunk countless ships with her storms.

Valessea crafted them from a master medallion. Lady Arabelle says they're crucial to the success of our mission, but I stopped listening when I realized they weren't worth any gold.\n\nThey're invitations of some sort, but she didn't tell me what for.

I asked the same thing! Lady Arabelle said, and I quote, "Don't be foolish, dear." She really knows how to wound with her words. \n\nIt has something to do with Valessea's enchantments. They permit the wearers to enter a protected location.

Valessea's a gorgeous young wizard making a name for herself in the Mages Guild. \n\nI've only met her twice, but she's wild for me. She probably stays up every night dreaming of this handsome face. I have that effect on people, you know.

Well, that corroborates what the dockmaster told you. If Prince Irnskar is still alive and made it to Amenos, perhaps the other alliance leaders did as well.\n\nOf course, that doesn't mean they're safe.

House Mornard controls Amenos, but they restrict their oversight to Amenos Station and the prison stockade. They leave the jungle to the prisoners.\n\nEither the royals washed ashore in the jungle, or the Mornards are keeping their arrival secret.

Only a small part of the island is hospitable, and Amenos Station is barely that. The rest of the island is an untamed jungle full of deadly plants, wild creatures, and gangs of prisoners. Not exactly a stroll in the park.

Exactly! First at one of those stuffy Society of the Steadfast events that Lady Arabelle forced me to attend. Then I saw her again after I recovered the master medallion and delivered it to her workshop.\n\nAll that matters is that we find her!

I'm not really supposed to say. I'd rather let Lady Arabelle give you the details. What I can tell you is that the medallions are invitations—I enchanted them to allow the wearers entry to a secret location at Lady Arabelle's request.

I believe we can hold All Flags Castle with a few warriors, but if we need to fight our way past the Ascendant Order forces, we'll never reach the alliance leaders in time.\n\nWe require a ship the Ascendant Magus won't suspect.

Remember Damard's letter to the steward? The Ascendant Order ship, Nereid's Song. It's waiting for the steward in a hidden cove. We just need to commandeer it and sail to All Flags like the rest of the ships in their fleet.\n\nCan I count on your help?

After we rescued Emeric, Ayrenn, and Irnskar from Amenos, Jakarn took them to the conference site on All Flags Islet. It seemed like the safest place. After all, Valessea and the Mages Guild personally set its wards, and the location was a secret.

Count Damard expects Steward Hercian to bring Nereid's Song to All Flags Islet. That makes her the perfect vessel to slip past whatever Ascendant Order forces are in the loch. \n\nAny other ship that encounters their fleet is likely to be attacked.

Today the small island is mostly abandoned, but long ago the All Flags Navy set sail against the Sload from that location. The ruins of an ancient memorial and a great castle are still in place there.\n\nIt seemed the perfect site for our peace talks.

He punished Avrippe Mornard by stripping him of his ducal title and granting it to my father instead. The Mornards remain counts, with holdings and estates throughout the isles.\n\nBut the Duforts are now the Dukes of the Systres.

No. They barely acknowledged my presence, despite the fact that they kidnapped me! And believe me, I was persistent!\n\nI don't know how they found out about the medallions in the first place, but their Ascendant Champion seemed very well informed.
You say lie, I say slight fabrication. Let's just agree to disagree.\n\nBut otherwise, yes. I always plan for the long game.

Share? Real thieves don't share, my sweet. Everything we do is selfish and self-serving. Valentyn knows that. It's part of the code. The treasure is mine. All of it.\n\nNow if you'll excuse me, I have minions to command and a vault to rob. Ta ta!

Cut the mooring lines. Start with the dock on the left and deal with any knights that get in your way. While they're busy with you, the rest of us will go around to the right and board Nereid's Song. We'll take care of the crew.

Once you've cut all three mooring lines, climb aboard. We'll do the rest.\n\nAnd don't pull your punches with those Ascendant Order bastards. I lost a lot of good sailors when the Spearhead went down in their storm.

You assume Marcelle knows about the Daybreak Gem, but I never mentioned it when I told her the legend of the vault. I always hold back a secret or two! \n\nMarcelle has no idea that the big, non-precious gem is really the key to a larger treasure!
Our keep stood as a bastion against the dark and beacon for the ill-fated for centuries. I remember the pride I felt being among the knights. The sense of purpose. All now lost.

Another relic of the All Flags Navy and the site of the peace talks. The Mages Guild cast protective wards around the hall to ensure the safety of the delegates. They should hold, for a time.\n\nTake this medallion. You can't enter the hall without it.

Defending the castle as best we can. We need to hold back the Ascendant Order as long as possible until Lord Bacaro arrives with help.\n\nIf the Magus gets past us, you must protect the alliance leaders. We'll buy you all the time we can.

I was Lord Leobert's confidant when we were but lowly pages. His father served as knight commander and had little time for Leobert. I should have seen what he was planning. Maybe I could have turned him from it.\n\nI failed us all.

The name reminded the knights to fight justly and well. We knew that death wasn't a thing to be beaten back or feared.\n\nStill, my demise wasn't honorable. And in death, I lie far from the brethren my negligence cursed.

Like Prince Irnskar, I had Captain Tsuzo commandeer a siege engine. That sent a few of their ships to the bottom. Then when the shaking stopped and the storm clouds parted, the remaining vessels fled.\n\nAfter you defeated the Magus, I suppose.

An excellent idea! Lord Bacaro knows it's vital to bring the delegates back to the table. After recent events, their faith in diplomacy might well be suspect. But a party, that's something they can all agree on.\n\nCan I impose on you again, dear?

Leave that to me, dear. I'll send Jakarn to round up our three brave captains and put them to work. It will be all hands on deck, as it were, but I think we can manage.\n\nYou just make sure the alliance leaders attend the party.

Tell the delegates Lord Bacaro dearly hopes they can attend a gathering at Gonfalon Palace. If anyone hesitates, use your charms to convince them to join us.\n\nMeanwhile, I'll throw something together. Meet me at Gonfalon Palace when you're done.

That's excellent news! My congratulations to you and Lady Arabelle! I'll still send the knights, but now their orders will be to shore up the castle's defenses, not rush into a war.\n\nBut pray tell, where are the delegates now?

Did they, now? I can't wait to hear the entire story. I am surprised they didn't make use of the wards protecting Memorial Hall, though. We prepared the site to keep the delegates safe throughout the peace talks.

Don't be modest, friend! From what I already know of your exploits, I can only imagine the heroics you demonstrated at All Flags Castle.\n\nInform Lady Arabelle. We'll gather at Gonfalon Palace to celebrate your courage and the safety of the delegates!

Like I said, there were four of us. We were all out on the streets for one reason or another. It's a tough life—most turn a blind eye to dirty, hungry-looking street urchins, so we learned to look out for each other. \n\nWe were inseparable.

A party? Just another excuse to get me and Emeric in the same room. Oh, very well. If we could face unprecedented danger together, we can probably survive sharing a few drinks and some food.\n\nAnd where will this gala event be held?

Well, that's a welcome bit of news! Even a party full of royals and nobles has got to be better than this place.\n\nWait. Will Emeric and Ayrenn be in attendance? If they declined the invitation, I probably should as well.

Hmm. Another royal function? I'm getting tired of those. Ghastly affairs, in most cases. I was just considering heading home. Queen Maraya must be missing me terribly.\n\nUnless … is the celebration in my honor? It's bad form to refuse such parties.

Heh. Most people were scared of Jhaka. He's a Pahmar, so everyone wrote him off as a big, dumb brute. But I've never met a kinder soul. He was always so generous, even though he didn't have a coin to his name. He was … spiritual, too.

That's probably for the best. It's close by. And All Flags Castle was quite a mess after the battle with the Ascendant Magus. It will take Lord Bacaro a considerable effort if he plans to make it ready for the conference again.

Then it seems I have no other choice. I will attend Lord Bacaro's celebration. And if the festivities evolve into more serious conversations … perhaps I will even listen.\n\nI'll see you there, my friend.

Ayrenn and Irnskar? Well, I can't allow them to attend and not show up myself. And I guess I do owe them something of a debt, too. They did help us on Amenos and at All Flags Castle.\n\nAll right, I'll attend Lord Bacaro's celebration.

We did not discuss peace, if that's what you're asking. We disagree on important issues … which is why diplomacy usually begins with social occasions. Banquets, balls, hunts, and the like.\n\nRarely do they involve fighting for your life, though.

Absolutely! He was an adventuring bard before he took the throne of Eastern Skyrim. He's not as ancient as Emeric, and that old lion enjoyed himself—when we weren't almost dying, at least.\n\nI'll send a report to my father. Tell him all about it.

I will need to treat that situation delicately. Until I can prove one way or another that Duchess Elea was truly ignorant of her brother's plot, I can't in good conscience reprimand the entire house.\n\nStill, I don't take treason lightly.

She's funny, that one. We called her Silverslip because she was always slipping in and out of the shadows. Like a knife, that girl. \n\nShe never talked much about her past, but I don't think it was pleasant.

Silverslip was all bared teeth and blood, even as a kid. Jhaka might have been the tallest, but Silverslip was definitely the muscle of our operation. \n\nShe could make a grown man piss himself in three words or less. Probably a survival tactic.

Eh, I don't really know. I don't subscribe to that stuff personally and he never pushed it on any of us. He just meditated a lot and always had something wise to say. Never got angry either, unless someone messed with me, Silverslip or Song, that is.

You simply don't understand, my friend. Marcelle and I are thieves! This is what thieves do. That doesn't change the fact that we love each other. We just love treasure and the competition a little bit more.\n\nBut have no fear. We've got a chisel!

You're really trying to get me into trouble, aren't you? And after all we've been through? All I've done for you?\n\nLady Arabelle writes those Investigator Vale novels. But she keeps that a secret. Doesn't want to be overrun by adoring admirers.

A passing merchant mentioned a Pahmar at the Gateway Inn in Sadrith Mora—a brawler fighting for entertainment. When I asked for details, he described Jhaka perfectly. Mild mannered, orange and black markings, three earrings in each ear. It's him.

The magic of the ritual will not let Leobert and his lackies leave the keep's walls. With the ritual items, their strength could grow. But since you took the tools from inside the keep, their cursed forms are trapped forever.

If the merchant is to be believed, Jhaka's there because he's a Telvanni slave. I don't know how long he's been in Vvardenfell, but I wouldn't be surprised if he was sold off as soon as he was snatched from Skywatch. The thought breaks my heart.

I am the only one who exited the keep. I believe the sight of my bones falling apart in the air frightened them. They'd never risk losing their mobility.\n\nI'll do my duty and watch over these items. I have a knack for long vigils now.
I hope so. I'd like not to rush into it, not while the others of my order pose a threat inside the keep. But one day, yes.\n\nWhen my time comes, I will smile. And that will be all.

Can you blame me? There's no reason besides tracking down Jhaka that I would willingly enter that land of hateful enslaving Dark Elves. \n\nIf I could, I'd send that meteor that floats in their sky into the Telvanni lands.

Ha! I'd like to see them try. I'll be on my best behavior because I want to find Jhaka, but if a Telvanni so much as touches me, I can't be held accountable for what I do. \n\nA lightning bolt through the skull might do some of them good anyway.

Not all of them. I just get mad thinking about the ones who kept Khajiit and Argonian slaves. I know not all Dark Elves are like that so I shouldn't be so distrustful … but the Telvanni definitely are. Arrogant bastards.

Just wanted you to know. I worked it out with Lady Arabelle. She considers my debt to her paid in full. I think she may have confused me with you, but I'll take it any way I can get it!\n\nSo, go in and enjoy the party. I'm sure I'll see you around.
I really am. But you know me. I lay low and some sort of trouble still finds me. I'm like one of those lodestones, I guess.

Definitely. If it had been Silverslip, I would have felt sorry for her opponents. But Jhaka is too sweet for that kind of violence. He's strong, but he hates violence.\n\nStill, back in the day, there was no one better to have in a tavern brawl.

I'll behave, don't worry. Once we find Jhaka, I plan to get him out of there as quietly as possible. Preferably in a manner that doesn't involve me shoving a dagger between Telvanni ribs.\n\nBut that's really up to them, isn't it?

Heh, not really. But we would start them pretty frequently. Once everyone was in on the action, Silverslip and I used to make good coin picking pockets among the mayhem. Easy money, beyond the occasional bruise or lump from flying fists or dishes.

Look, it's possible for me to loathe the history of your people and their treatment of mine and still accept that not all Dark Elves are inherently evil. You've been good to me. I wouldn't be traveling with you if I thought you rotten on the inside.

Definitely. If it had been Silverslip, I would have felt sorry for her opponents. But Jhaka is too sweet for that kind of violence. He's strong, but he hates violence.\n\nStill, back in the day, there was no one better to have in a tavern brawl.

I don't really give a daedrat's ass what the Telvanni think. \n\nAll I care about is figuring out if this Pahmar is really Jhaka and getting him out of there. Preferably in a manner that doesn't involve me shoving a dagger between Telvanni ribs.

Heh, not really. But we would start them pretty frequently. Once everyone was in on the action, Silverslip and I used to make good coin picking pockets among the mayhem. Easy money, beyond the occasional bruise or lump from flying fists or dishes.

I put on a few disguises, sure. And I'm glad everyone's safe. But all this hero stuff gives me a rash. I'm not supposed to attract so much attention!\n\nAnyway, Lady Arabelle wants a word with you before she starts the main event. She's waiting inside.
Pahmar? What do you want with one of them? Eh, I don't care. Go ask the inn owner. \n\nI'm just supposed to tempt customers with our delicious food.

Ah, Jara? Or was it Jhaka? You're referring to my has-been money maker, I assume. \n\nSadly, you're too late. I sold him a few weeks ago. He was getting slow, complained about being sick. People don't pay for a limp-fisted brawler.

That depends on how fast I can get workers out to rebuild All Flags Castle and restore Memorial Hall. And I need to send word to the Mages Guild. Valessea alone can't replace the wards. There's also a new Fighters Guild delegate to consider.

There's always a chance. As long as Lord Bacaro can finalize the necessary arrangements. We have an opportunity to put an end to terrible suffering. What sort of queen would I be if I did not do everything in my power to see this through?

Who knows? Will ice melt in the cookpot? That's a certainty. But the thoughts that run through the minds of the rulers of Tamriel? Those cannot be fathomed by even the most-brilliant sage.\n\nBut I will send word to my father. Ask for his advice.

What do I look like, a soothsayer? All I know is that peace has powerful enemies. Every day, people tell me that if we press harder, we can make good on the blood and treasure we've spent. Dictate terms from a position of strength.\n\nIt distresses me.

I was resting on that outcropping out there when the rock fell out from under me. Vinilsare will probably drag me to a healer. She's not going to stop talking about how she knew this cave was dangerous.\n\nIt's really annoying when she's right.
Thank you. Vinilsare trusts you. I'm putting the hope of our happiness in your hands. With any luck, the only thing I'm going to regret today is falling off that rock.

A jeweler by the name of Varvisi Uleni is selling a lovely bracelet that I wish to acquire for my wife. But she won't come down on the price.\n\nVarvisi sells outside Tel Naga most days. Get me that bracelet and I'll tell you what I know.

Sure I do. And I'll even tell you where—provided the brute is still alive. He had such weak lungs for a creature so big.\n\nBut first, you do something for me. My information does not come free of charge.

Good. I love my wife, but I knew—if we both came in here—she'd focus on my safety and ignore all the scoria we're supposed to collect. \n\nI really didn't want to have to sneak back in here after she dragged me out. Not with this hurt leg.

No rest for the weary, dear. I need to help Lord Bacaro restore All Flags Castle for the peace talks. Improve security. Figure out what other traitors beside Count Damard are lurking about.\n\nAnd, of course, I need to keep the delegates safe.

Here, take the Spoon of Undo. If you could run around and fix the livestock and Huldressa, that will give me a chance to finally whip up this counterspell. By the time you're finished, I'm sure I'll have something figured out!

As glorious as a fight to the death would be, I suppose I should try to survive. My subjects need me.\n\nBut the others went in search of their own battles. Prince Irnskar headed up to the battlements. Track him down while I clear a path to the hall.

Did you miss me, good-looking? I can't say I blame you. Most people find it hard to go long periods of time without gazing upon this impressive visage.\n\nI've been doing odd jobs, making myself available wherever they need a handsome face.

Not while we're all that stands between victory and death! If I abandon the battlements now, we'll be caught like wolves in a trap.\n\nI need you to deal with the vermin scaling the walls while I prepare the ballista to attack that approaching ship.
Plenty, but you'd never believe most of them. My memories of our adventures together always make me smile, though. You're a great companion, and easy on the eyes to boot!

You might not love this, but trust me, it'll be fun! I used to do this trick with Song and Silverslip whenever we needed some extra coin. \n\nI'm going to turn you into a monkey. Then, you run up to Varvisi and distract her so I can pinch the bracelet.

Hilarious, right? You'll be just enough of a distraction. Just rifle through her stuff. All eyes will be on you and no one will notice me slipping a hand into her pocket. It's perfect!\n\nBut the spell won't last forever, so we have to do this quick!

Exquisite! Am I correct in assuming your little friend back there did the deed? The cats who aren't properly trained to behave tend to be good little thieves.\n\nNow, I am a man of my word. I sold the sickly Pahmar to a group of bandits.

The gentleman I did business with told me that his band was headed to Pulk next. Here, I'll mark the location for you. \n\nThe man's name was Bralsa Inlador. And that, my friend, is all the information I have for you. Now kindly scurry off.
