Ugh. That red-eyed piece of guar dung just made us do his bidding for no other reason than to make sure we know how superior the Telvanni are. \n\nTurning you into a monkey was fun, but now all l can think about is wringing that bastard's neck.

You're right. Thanks. I needed that.\n\nI have to remember that we're here for Jhaka. I can suffer anything if it means finding him in the end. And I know someday, the debt that the Telvanni have incurred will come due. I hope I'm around to see it.

As quickly and efficiently as possible. If Jhaka is in there, I don't want him suffering any longer than he has to. I've already made him suffer long enough. And if we get to knock some heads along the way, all the better.\n\nCome on, let's get inside.

Once, Jhaka wondered if Ember had orchestrated some part of our family's fate. But that thought passed as quickly as it came. The little girl with the ember eyes—she would never harm us.\n\nShe … <cough> was … <cough>

Yes, of course. Thank you. This one had hoped not to die in this wet, dark place but had resigned myself to it all the same. This is a welcome change. \n\nJhaka will follow you to safety. Lead the way.

It was all very sudden. It was a group of mercenaries, though not any faction this one was familiar with. They descended quickly and incapacitated me. Then, they went for Silverslip and Song. \n\nThere was one strange thing ….

It was Silverslip's expression. She looked scared as they took her and Song away. You must understand, Silverslip was never scared. Even when truly afraid, it manifested as anger. It was odd, as if she knew something in that moment we did not.
I knew it! Thank you, mainlander. We've been trying for months to catch <<1>> with incriminating evidence, but he can smell a guard from a block away. He hides it all before we get anywhere near him.

I'm true to my word. I'm after the smuggler who's bringing skooma into my town, not some drunken fool who ends up with a vial in his pocket. \n\nBut tell your friend if I see him anywhere near moon-sugar again, I'll arrest him on the spot.

No one paid the innkeeper? I don't understand. We ate and drank quite a lot last night, but Rigurt said he'd taken care of it. I would never skip out on a bill!\n\nWe have to make this right. What do you need me to do?
Gladly. I'll head back to my rooms and clean myself up. As soon as I can feel my fingers again, I'll meet you back at the inn with the coin for my share.\n\nIt's the least I can do.

He did small jobs for them sometimes, if the pay was all right and the work wasn't too unsavory. I think before we met up, he may have been with one group or another. Not much to his liking, I think. He never fit in with that type—too soft-hearted.

I've always wondered … what if it was one of our pasts that caught up to us that day, and that's why my friends were taken? What if it was my past? I mean, it doesn't make any sense but in the absence of any other information, it kind of haunts me.

Look, people end up living on the streets for a lot of reasons. You don't pry. Sometimes you learn something in passing, but if the person has your back in tough spots, their past isn't that important.\n\nThough, I wonder if that was wise.

Indeed. They were called Kestrin's Blades. Curiously, they disbanded sometime not long after we were accosted by them in Skywatch. \n\nThough they no longer operate, this one found the name of one of their captains, Guruz.

Not very much, sadly. But this one does know he currently lives near Stonetooth Fortress, in Betnikh. If he was a captain of the Kestrin Blades, he may know where they took Silverslip and Song. And why. \n\nThis one is hopeful.

Yeah, yeah—more like Kestrin's Farts! That band was doomed from the day we joined up together. Pah!\n\nI know it well, stranger. I was one of the captains, but what of it? I told you, I'm retired! Blissfully retired and drunk.

Yeah, I remember now. I wasn't thrilled with the contract. It came from some secretive group but the pay was too good to pass up. It seemed easy enough on the surface—grab a Redguard lass and if her friends were with her, they were fair game.

And now you've found me. Shall I recount the tale for her? The one where I'm a gullible, foolish child who thought Song's family really missed her, and that I could help reunite them?\n\nI should have burned that letter. That's how they found us.
Convo A

Eh? A Pahmar and … oh, well that does sound a bit familiar. My head is too fuzzy. You expect me to remember something that far back when I've been drinking all day?\n\nPiss off, you and your three friends back there.

Naw, they didn't really say and the Blades knew better than to ask. Besides, we got a Pahmar and a Wood Elf out of the deal. The Pahmar sold for a good bit of coin. The Wood Elf though … she was trouble. Still feel bad about her.

Hmm, you might be right. I never looked into it because I thought it was better if everyone assumed I was dead. Then, I wouldn't ever have to face the truth.\n\nBut deep down, I always knew this day would come. Now that it's here … I want to help.
Info 2

Unlike some people in this room, I remember to pay my debts when they're due. These three ninnies came back and paid what they owed, so here's the scepter.\n\nYou should tell your friends to use more common sense in the future.

Diplomacy is hard work. I bought special drinks for <<1>>, but they made her sick. I ordered dessert for <<2>> and tried to pay for dinner. <<2>> got arrested and the innkeeper kept my scepter!\n\nNow I am even more confused.

Hmm. I have spent all my advance for travel expenses and diplomatic entertaining. No matter! I am happy to diplomacize High Isle for free.\n\nWhatever else happens, they are sure to remember Rigurt the Brash!

Mount Firesong is the volcano that rises above the island of Y'ffelon. You can see it in the distance. It's always been restless, and its vents and hot springs stretch throughout the archipelago. \n\nI didn't think too much about the initial rumbles.

I love the man like a brother, but Anton can sometimes act flashier than he should. He likes to show off his sleight of hand skills.\n\nAfter we got thrown in the stockade, Anton decided to make friends with a jailer. Olivya was her name.
I know I'm not a great person. I've lied, stolen, manipulated, cheated, harassed, and once committed arson. \n\nBut I've never killed anyone. And I won't start today.

There are cakes, sweet-beetle pies, and all sorts of delicious smelling foods I can't even name. How could I resist? \n\nI didn't even realize that this was a festival for Zenithar until I arrived and talked to the concessions seller over there.

No idea, we peeled off from Kestrin's Blades before we ever made the trade. Things started falling apart after that job.\n\nBut if you want to find the Wood Elf, try the Shrine of the Black Maw. Bloodsuckers are still crawling all over that place.

The others at House Ravenwatch do their best, but they're struggling to accept Verandis's absence. So, I'm surprising them with some gifts. \n\nThis festival seemed like the perfect place to peruse craftsmen's wares.

Your friend Rigurt happened. First he bought the High Elf rotmeth, thinking it was a taste of home for her. After that he tried to get a sugary dessert for the Orc and mistook a skooma dealer in the back room for one of my staff.

The skooma dealer gave Rigurt something for his friend the Orc, all right. Rigurt decided that settled the bill. He came back and told the others he'd taken care of it. They were both far too drunk to sort it out.\n\nNinnies, all of them.

Look, it's embarrassing enough without you rubbing it in. \n\nWe drank far too much. Rigurt bought me rotmeth, thinking it was a taste of home and not some nasty Wood Elf swill. And I downed it without even looking to see what it was!

Because Rigurt kept buying them! It's the first rule of diplomacy: Don't embarrass your host by refusing what they give you. But the second rule is don't make your guests drink like a Wood Elf pirate.\n\nEvidently Rigurt didn't know that.

I didn't even want dessert! We'd been eating and drinking all night. But since we'd been talking about cakes earlier in the evening, Rigurt must have thought I had a sweet tooth.\n\nI was even more surprised than the guard when he found the skooma.
It wasn't my finest hour. I … may have relieved myself against a building along the way. And when the guard spoke sharply to me about that, I argued back at him.\n\nYou know the rest of the tale.

I don't know what High Elves like to drink. And I'm not sure why that man gave me a bag of skooma when I wanted something for my friend <<1>>. I only wanted him to have good time!\n\nI am stumpled. Did <<2>> have my scepter of office?

Hmm. I was hoping father needed us to battle the Hadolids. Recovering bandages and poultices is just as important. Right? \n\nOoh! Maybe there'll be resonance crystals. I haven't sung into one of those for a while.

Oh, take them down with as much violence as possible. That goes without saying. But try not to take on the entire Order by yourselves. Good help is hard to find.\n\nIf you can expose the Lord or Magus's identities, that might be enough to defeat them.

I'm not going to leave without singing a song to honor my friends! These crystals will project my voice to the other carts.\n\nWould you check for the supplies while I sing? I see the other carts to the left.
I think so. Or it calmed them enough that they left peacefully?\n\nPox! I never finished the song! I'll have to start from the beginning now.

In a sense. The young woman you seek is the heiress of a family that runs a very powerful and dangerous organization called the Emerald Eye. The king seeks to put down the Emerald Eye for the betterment of Alik'r, but has been unsuccessful thus far.

We both seek the same woman, albeit for different reasons. But you have an advantage that we do not. You are not agents of the king.\n\nWe know of an estranged uncle from said family living in Alik'r. But he refuses to speak with us.

No, I am fine, just tired. Thank you. But I must know … how did you find me? After all this time?\n\nThe last time I saw Ember was the day the mercenaries took me, Silverslip and Jhaka. I feared I would never see them again, much less here.

Truly? I had all but drowned in grief thinking that my family hurt them to get to me. \n\nI cherished Ember, Silverslip and Jhaka more than anything. I tried to escape many times over the years in hopes that I might find them.

Indeed. His name is Azamel. As far as we can tell, he's been cut off from the family business, but likely still has valuable information. \n\nGo to Sentinel and convince him to speak with you. He's likely hanging around an inn. Just be cautious.

I'm not sure. They sound like bad news. And what sort of family kidnaps their own child? Song must have had a reason for running away from them. \n\nBut what if I'm wrong? What if she really is a willing participant and she's not the person I remember?
I … don't know. I need to think. None of this makes any sense to me. I just want to find her. I'll deal with everything else later.\n\nLet's talk to Azamel in Sentinel and learn what we can.

Allow me to explain. The Emerald Eye came to power after our ancestors discovered an ancient relic in the desert. The relic gives the women of our family powerful visions. These visions are the key to the wealth and influence of the organization.

I don't know for sure. The Emerald Eye moves often to avoid being tracked. But I have the location of their last known camp, at the Easterly Aerie. Here, I'll mark it on your map for you. If the Eye has moved on, there might still be a clue there.

I'm a selfish man, what can I say? I value my life. Song became the Emerald Eye's most sacred possession, save the relic, as soon as she was returned to them. Trying to prise her free from their grasp by myself would have been a death sentence.

I would not have spoken to you if I thought otherwise. You clearly seem capable enough, and when Song spoke of her friend Ember, she complimented her resourcefulness. I have no doubt that the two of you will be more successful than I.

I hope they try. I couldn't save Jhaka from being forced to fight and I couldn't save Silverslip from being turned into a vampire … but I'll be damned if I don't save Song from her fate.\n\nWe need to get to that Emerald Eye camp. Now.
Let me see. Oh good, there's a map.\n\nNever heard of the place, but necropolis sounds bad. Looks like we need to spot a tomb door that's different from the others?
I say we go to the Motalion Necropolis, bust in there, make those Emerald Eye bastards wish they were dead, and rescue Song. That's my rough plan, anyway.\n\nSound good? Good. Let's get to it.

No, absolutely not. Whatever is going on with her and her family doesn't change my feelings. She was my friend. I care about her. I know Jhaka and Silverslip do too.\n\nBesides, I'm still having a hard time believing Song could be dangerous.

Song had a gentle soul. The rest of us knew how to survive better, but it made us hard. Tough.\n\nSong was different. She wasn't weak by any means, but we all watched out for her. She was fiercely independent but didn't have that … darkness to her.

At length. Her father would punish her for speaking of them, but while I was still in the family's good graces, I listened. I heard all about gentle Jhaka, and pugnacious Silverslip. It seems they treated her better than her own family ever did.

Not even close! I am Count Damard Dufort and you are too late to stop me. If only Lady Arabelle were here to see this. \n\nAh, but she is! My knights found her outside. She now faces justice in the dungeons below. If you hurry, maybe you can save her.

The steward? You are not as clever as I thought. I am Count Damard Dufort! If only Lady Arabelle were here to see this.\n\nAh, but she is. My knights found her outside. She faces justice in the dungeons below. If you hurry, maybe you can save her.
No. I don't have your experience, but I am not going to twiddle my thumbs while father's fate is decided!\n\nAnd if you don't think I can do this, I'll prove myself to both you and father!
I explored the tunnels a lot when I was younger. At night, of course. I didn't want to be caught. \n\nUnless they dug new tunnels, I'll know where we are.
No idea who you are or what you are talking about. Leave me be!\n\nBack off, then follow me. Discreetly.

Well, no. I saw Damard earlier, but when he learned the Swan wasn't ready to sail, he said he made other arrangements. He spoke with Steward Hercian, gave him a letter, and departed. \n\nWait, the steward left the letter behind in his rush, I'm sure!

The Emerald Eye was found ages ago. It brought our family wealth and power in the form of visions. But only the women of the family could see such visions, and only by communing with the Eye.\n\nThen, the Eye took and took until nothing was left.

Yes. I fled when I learned the truth and watched my mother succumb to the Eye. It was horrible to watch her deteriorate. I did not want any part of it, but my family insisted.\n\nSo I ran. I was lucky to find my friends, if only for a short time.

No! I'm just … thinking. I have carried this guilt and fear for a long time. Finally putting it down feels strange. Good, but strange. \n\nI think I needed to settle my past in order to move forward. I feel like a fog has been lifted.

It's a place where banished prisoners work in exchange for warm meals, clean water, and a little protection. They unearth ammonites for House Mornard.\n\nFather never let me leave the camp. He said Amenos was no place for a child.
You want to know about those boring old shells? They don't look like much to me. Father says mages use them to store magic … somehow. \n\nI never listened when father talked about the ammonites.

Who else would do it? They're the only ones here! Prison labor is plentiful and cheap. The mine offers them short contracts. Agree to work for three months, get room and board. A lot request to stay on longer, or leave and return later.

You know that the banished prisoners can never leave the jungle, right? Well, the jungle is dangerous. The mine gives them a place to work in exchange for a little bit of safety. \n\nFather employs a lot of sentries at the mine to ensure that safety.
My magic can help people. But if father had his way, I'd be stuck conjuring butterflies for nobility my whole life.\n\nFather never even let me leave the mine camp without three bodyguards!

I've been away from Amenos for a while. Father allowed me to get a better education. \n\nMagic. Music. No one masters those things without teachers. I was lucky to find mentors from both the Bards College and the Mages Guild.

Most mages cast a spell with some arcane gestures and their innate mental power. That's how a friend explained it. I don't—well, I can't. My music focuses my magic. I had to train with many renowned mages and bards to get where I am now.

Father never let me get close to one, so I've only seen them from a distance. They're covered in thick shells and have beady eyes. They seem to really like the shoreline and tide pools.\n\nHonestly, they don't frighten me.
I asked mother the same thing when I saw her! \n\nShe didn't have an answer for me. The Hadolids weren't in the mine one day. Then they were in the tunnels, attacking everyone who came near.

If my wife was successful in her negotiations with House Mornard, she'll return with enough sentries to replace the ones we lost. With the Hadolids calmer due to Meryline's song, my sentries will be able to fight them off in due course.
If they do, we'll be ready for them. \n\nI'll come up with a strategy to further deal with the infestation tonight and speak with the sentries. No one will be caught unaware again.
The future? It's what I want to do now! \n\nLook at all the good we did here. We saved the mine!

Somewhere where no one knows who I am or who my father is. When I leave, I don't want to feel like I'm still proving myself to him. I'll be an adventurer in my own right.\n\nMaybe Khefrem or—or Summerset? Ships sail to those shores all the time.

I hope it doesn't come to that. We'll talk. Work through our disagreements. But if he goes back to being a stubborn mule, then I'll have no choice but to leave anyway.\n\nThe world needs my skills. I'm not going to be content here.

Not really. My first job for Lady Arabelle was to track down the master medallion, the template used to make the others. I don't know the finer details. Or care to.\n\nI was supposed to get the medallions from Valessea, but they were missing, too.

No, that was the master medallion. It was the template used to make the others. So we secured that one, at least. Good on us!\n\nThe medallions I was supposed to pick up from Valessea are the actual invitations, but they were missing, too.

Damard Dufort? Astonishing! I was certain the Magus was going to turn out to be one of the Mornards.\n\nTell me, what of this mysterious Ascendant Lord you encountered beneath Castle Navire? Did you learn anything about him?

These royals are a stubborn lot, or hadn't you noticed? I can never predict what they will do from one moment to the next.\n\nRemind them these peace talks are imperative. If that doesn't work, tell them the other two accepted your invitation.

Sometimes a few untruths are required to grease the wheels of diplomacy. The royals will see right through the ruse, of course, but they'll play along. All they need is a reason to believe that this isn't a waste of their time.

I—I think so? The Commodore said so long as they're protected, his fleet will never die.\n\nYou go and destroy the idols. I'll convince my ancestor to share what she knows and we'll meet you at the old tome to break the curse.

As long as nothing else out of the ordinary happens, I'll stay. At least for awhile. The weather here on High Isle is so much nicer than what we have in Windhelm.\n\nI can do without the cold and the snow for a little longer.

Just that she was clearly in charge of this operation. All of the so-called knights that manhandled me acquiesced to her every command.\n\nShe went off deeper into the cave with the group that I presume took the medallions.

Listen friend, Stros is one of the busiest ports this side of Hew's Bane. Lots of folks come through here.\n\nBut yeah, I saw Kiv Lindres. Seems the sly bastard has gone legit. He booked passage on a ship, working a job for Veloise Mercantile.
Sure. He was on Daidezi's ship, the Senche's Heart. They sailed for Seyda Neen.\n\nDavak Hlaren over there can get you to Seyda Neen, if you have coin.

I feel like we have to. He's already used the signet to buy a passage on a boat.\n\nMy parents' business is built on their excellent reputation. What if he uses that ring to withdraw funds, or cheat one of our trade partners?

Thank you, my friend. On top of what this could mean to my family, I'm just so annoyed with Aurelia! \n\nI cared … when I gave her the ring, all those years ago, it meant a great deal. I can't believe she let this happen.
Oh yeah, I know Kiv. Men like him, they're a lot of fun … until they drag you into some scheme of theirs and you lose your job.\n\nSlimy fetcher has already moved on. What did he do now?

We regaled each other with tales of how we survived the shipwrecks and our adventures on Amenos.\n\nI believed Emeric was past his prime, no longer the great hero. And Irnskar struck me as young and brash. I now have a different perspective.

Not shocking, flah. He's a schemer. Left some stuff behind in the tavern and left in a flash.\n\nI vouched for him, so I lost my job. Feel free to look through his pack. I think he was headed for Wayrest.

No, but we didn't exterminate all of those Order bastards. And their so-called Ascendant Lord is still loose. I have no doubt his rogue knights will rise against us again.\n\nI'll withhold judgment on the Duforts until my Daggers investigate, though.

Yes. The Abbey's rise from poverty is a miracle that can only be attributed to Zenithar's favor. Gavos longed to see beyond the Abbey's walls and so, we are here. To tell the other devotees of Zenithar what happened and to enjoy his lessons.

Cowards like that let others do the fighting for them. I imagine he's in hiding, fearing exposure and seeking a way to rebuild his forces. I suspect the Lord will remain in the shadows for now.\n\nStay vigilant. Inform me if you learn anything more.

He longed for company and to see the Abbey restored. With each passing day, I believe the work we do uplifts him. After so many years in silence and isolation, he is among friends. \n\nI hope that many will listen to his story.

It prospers, though only through time and effort will it be fully restored. The Golden Anvil's constant glow renews our faith in Zenithar. And, in telling of its incredible return to our care, the anvil supplies the Abbey with hopeful supplicants.
Let me see.\n\nThere's that Ascendant Champion again. Lady Arabelle will want to hear about this. But I know this place, Sareloth Grotto.
It's in Vvardenfell, but they neglected to say exactly where inside the grotto they took the medallions.\n\nHmm. I think I have something that may help with that. Here. Take this shell.

It's not just a shell. I enchanted it with the same magic I used on the medallions. If you focus on the shell, the medallions will glow for a short time.\n\nHere, I'll mark the grotto on your map. And the boats mentioned in the scroll should be nearby.
The reconstructions are well underway. With our work and Zenithar's favor, it'll be restored. The anvil hasn't lost its glow, I pray that our labors please Zenithar.

Penance for my mistakes. I am to spread the word of the Abbey and the Golden Anvil's restoration. \n\nDaluion and the rest of the Resolutions believe that the festival will lighten my spirits. Remind me of the joys that toil brings.

Watching these artisans interact reminds me of the golden days in Zenithar's delight. But happy memories are accompanied by sad ones. After so many years in the darkness, this is almost too much to bear.\n\nI will not waste this opportunity.

Aye. Bugbears and bogeys often whispered of by sailors around the Systres. Folk said to worship and commune with the unknowable things that call the vast, lightless abyss beneath the waves home. A myth even in my time, but they were real.

I will … eventually. Seems in poor taste to bring it up right off the gangway, even without all this curse business. She'll help us—I'm certain—but it's only fair we do her a turn first.\n\nLet's go find those ship logs she mentioned.

I'm not hurt, no. Izzy must have told you what happened. I came here with a painter friend, Kiv Lindres, and I thought our rooms were burgled a few days ago.\n\nWell, it turns out … Kiv was the thief. He'd been after my jewelry from the start.

Something just felt off. I asked a waitress about him, and she said Kiv was well known as a swindler.\n\nI went to his room to confront him and we tussled. In fact, I tore his travel bag and one of my earrings fell out! Then he took off running.

Ah, apologies. I'm Marso, a captain under the Veloise Mercantile banner. I work for Isobel's folks. \n\nThank Sai I got thirsty. I came here to the inn for a drink, and saw Lady Aurelia bawling her eyes out at the bar.

I've worked for Isobel's parents for many years, yes. I've known both women since they were young. Though I must admit, it's been some time since I've seen Lady Aurelia. \n\nAh, I just regret I wasn't of any assistance to her.

Look around, friend, Stros isn't exactly a bastion of philanthropic do-gooders.\n\nGood luck in your search. I'll stay with Lady Aurelia, ensure she stays safe. If the thief is gone … well. Isobel will need to tell her parents about the missing ring.

Some philanthropic organization that Lady Arabelle works for. They provide aid to those displaced or wounded by the ongoing war in Cyrodiil, among other charitable works.\n\nNow, can we go find Valessea, please?

I should have expected that. I ran into them during my first job for Lady Arabelle. They got their hands on the master medallion before I stole it back. Makes sense they'd go after the others. But why take Valessea? That's not their style.

Good old Tarazka, always thinking. All right. Let's go find that lantern. And if the Ascendant Order has harmed one beautiful hair on Valessea's beautiful head … well, we'll find some way to make them regret that. Mark my words!
Body? I'm sorry to hear that. He was never very sneaky. Always stumbling around in the dark. His night vision was horrible, unusual for a Khajiit.

I'd tell you to mind your business, but you've done me a good turn.\n\nI wasn't always such an upstanding citizen. I got involved with some unscrupulous things around Port Hunding. It caught up with me and I found myself on Amenos soon enough.

Ferone's dead? I can hardly believe it. That Dark Elf was a seasoned marine for the Pact once. Guess the wilds are growing more treacherous ….\n\nGlad you were more fortunate. I'll take that fragment off your hands for a fair sum.

He was one of the most capable people I knew. I wouldn't have trusted just anyone … but you actually did it. I owe you for that.\n\nI'll take that map fragment off your hands. For a reward, of course.

The old pirate claimed to have taken a number of trophies from his raids around Sentinel's shores. Items chosen to insult the crown, not for their monetary worth. He said if I returned those to King Fahara'jad I might be pardoned from my exile.
Expected? No, I'm just not very surprised. I warned him there was risk, but he was eager and needed the work.\n\nLooks like you'll be collecting instead. I'll gladly pay you for his piece of the map.

Theories aren't part of my repertoire. But I can smell trouble when it's brewing. The Ascendant Order is planning something big, and I don't like it.\n\nCome on, let's find Valessea. More rescuing, less speculating.

If I knew where my daughter was, I would not have written to Isobel. Aurelia left a note saying she's gone adventuring to fix a problem she created, and not to worry.\n\nAs if telling me not to worry will make everything fine.
I know, right? \n\nLet's see … if I'm reading these scribbles right he went down to Gonfalon Bay.
Yes. I immediately thought of Isobel, of course. As a knight on errantry, she is free to do as she wishes. This is not an order. \n\nIt's a heartfelt request from a mother concerned for her daughter.

These bottles here are All Flags rum. It's foul stuff, proudly made right near the harbor. They serve it at the Ancient Anchor, just south of the main gate.\n\nNilsmon, you'd better be down there. I swear to Stendarr ….

Ah, yes. I am a traveling priest, seeking to inspire the minds of both young and old. To live a fulfilling life by learning skills and trades for self-sufficiency. Hard work and perseverance enrich the mind, the body, and the soul.

We present offerings that reflect our skills to honor his wisdom. \n\nOne of my skills is basket-weaving, and this season I want to weave a basket worthy of my god. I could use some help gathering what I need to create it. Might you assist me?

We met a couple of times. He wouldn't have been memorable at all if he had not been so determined to get my attention. His advances were harmless, of course, but quite persistent. \n\nStill, I'm not sad to see him. I'm grateful for the rescue.

You tease me, my little vixen! You know I am a captain in the magnificent All Flags Navy. Perhaps the best in the entire fleet! Oh, but I do enjoy our little amusements.\n\nWhat game are we playing this time, pray tell?
Arrgh! Get. Out. Of. My. Head!

Alas, that is the nature of war, my dearest. Those Sload are terrible creatures.\n\nBut know this. Every time I set sail, I do it for you. I cannot abide another day with my love in dire peril from the threat of Thras's monsters.

I remember that he was a cad and a coward! A sorry excuse for a man!\n\nHe was my beloved's brother. And the master builder of the All Flags memorials. He carved the names into the garden plaque personally. But not my captain's. Not my love!

The All Flags? Yes, yes, I think that's right. That's what it says on these old plaques. Oh, I wish I could remember more. It's the curse, I fear. Gets into everything and muddies the water. Been that way ever since … ever since ….\n\nDamn it!
Fix the boat! I can't rest.

That is what Za'ji said, was it not? It was like they sought vengeance on Khajiit for sharpening our claws on too many of their kin! The woods had nasty, twiggy claws of their own that Za'ji did not wish to have sharpened on him.

Have faith, walker! Caska would never succumb to those brambles and branches. She is merely lost in the fog and will be greatly relieved to see she has once again kept her captain safe once we find her!

She pounced upon the angry lumber like a kitten eager for play when last he saw her, so Za'ji made great use of the distraction, as he is sure she would have wanted.\n\nHe expected she would come signal to Za'ji when it was safe to come out, but ….

Amminus Varo and I belong to the Resolution of Zenithar. A temple devoted to the anvil and the god it represents.\n \nWhile the glorious vendors and crafters ply their goods, we ensure they all receive Zenithar's blessing.

He's a thief, of course, and a charmer. That's how he gets you. I first met him in Ebonheart. I had nothing valuable, so I wasn't a mark. \n\nI only work in places like this to pay for my alchemy studies.

He showed back up in town flashing some merchant house signet ring. He said he'd gone straight. Spent big, charging everything to the house.\n\nChow-Chow, the cook, knew something was fishy and got the owner involved. Kiv bolted, and I got fired.

I'd known him for a while, casual, before we started up our thing. He treats a person nice when he just wants to have fun. Got a good sense of him.\n\nBut live and learn and Dumac take my pride, I suppose. I'll be fine. Lesson learned.

What I should do is move on, find another job, continue my studies. But part of me wouldn't mind seeing Kiv get some payback.\n\nMaybe I'll take a page from your book, serjo. Track him down in Wayrest and pay him back.
Just so! That scoundrel is an ancient spellcaster, a cruel bastard that's clung to life in this old tower for centuries. \n\nThat reign of terror will end today, if I have anything to say about it.

Kiv! What? Have you found him? Is he all right?\n\nSteady on, Julles. You're better than this. Let me start again. I know Kiv. Very well. I believe he made off with several items of value. In fact, I handed one to him personally.

I poked through his things when he was bathing. I found a note from someone named Goldleaf about a meeting in Belkarth. The note seemed as much … personal as business.\n\nI confronted him, and now he's gone. I've half a mind to warn this Goldleaf.
Fix the boat! I can't rest.
I'm here with my captain and I have no patience for the advances of his foolish younger brother. Away with you, foul sir!

I'll mark the location of her camp on your map. It's safer if we split up, so I'll meet you there.\n\nYou hang onto the medallions for now. It pains me to admit it, but I think you can protect them better than I can. I'm more of a lover than a fighter.

Does he now? I'm not surprised. Jakarn is the kind of person who thinks everyone is enchanted by every breath he takes. And I'm sure some are. I'm just not one of them.\n\nHe's amusing, at least. Just shy of insufferable.
Why, just the finest warship ever to set sail from High Rock! Surely you remember the name of … of …?

Why, yes, of course—the Pristine Halberd! The pride of the Breton fleet! We've helped protect this rock during the long years of build up. Now we're ready to be the instrument of vengeance, just as you planned.

Barkskinned beasts and spriggans. They ambushed us near the old mill and now the woods are thick with them. Tough, but they die like anything else if you claw enough.\n\nYou ready to snap these twigs and get on with this treasure hunt?
Fix the boat! I can't rest.
Stibbons? What a ridiculous name! \n\nI'm Tobin Moorcroft. Master Builder of the All Flags Navy monuments. My work, unlike my brother's, will be remembered forever!
Everything on Monument Islet! Well, I had help. Apprentices, assistants, laborers. But the design and the fine detail work? That's all mine.
Let's hope you're not all talk, like a certain captain I know.
I missed your courage and your competence. Let's go cut some timber.

I act as a humble guide for those interested in devoting themselves to larger tasks in exchange for greater rewards. \n\nWhile Zenithar smiles upon daily tasks, he recognizes the brilliance of working toward a larger goal.
How do I feel? Like some virile man was stomping around inside my body with his oversized boots and manly urges. It was unsettling.\n\nAnd, if I'm being totally honest, somewhat arousing.
Oh, never mind that. My manservant wants a word with you. But please hurry. I have a task for Stibbons that needs to be dealt with post haste.

You can't, not really. But you can absolutely trust that I want to walk away from this with my hide intact.\n\nI'm betting you're more willing to chat than the stabby sword lady here, and I've got to tell you where the ring is.
I hid it, but I'll tell you where it is. You found me once, I'm sure you can find me again.\n\nJust let me leave with my beautiful face on my perfect body. All right?

Bloodmage Cassel has been a scourge across the isles, and of late his raids have become too much to bear. His minions have collected piles of booty for his dark vault. \n\nThe head of my order himself charged us with ending this fiend's life.

That bastard is more dangerous than I expected. I'll keep him busy while you two even our odds.\n\nRayan holds the key, he was the one that came up with the plan for our assault. He'll be a tremendous knight one day! Stendarr guide your arm!

No. We came upon them just as they were finishing an attack on a caravan. But I assume they recognized us or decided our station warranted capture rather than elimination.\n\nBut you came with a warning, didn't you? What did you find out?

I've remained at Lady Arabelle's side since we delivered the invitation medallions to the delegates. I hoped to help make sure their journey to High Isle proceeded smoothly.\n\nIt seems the Ascendant Order is not so easily avoided.

Whatever the situation, I won't abandon Quentyn to his fate. Oh, that's good. Let me write that down.\n\nBesides, we have to risk it. Both to save Quentyn and to see if we can learn anything about the missing alliance leaders.

The tower itself is a conduit for the bloodmage's power. \n\nThe heart of the tower is his dark phylactery. He's invested his soul within this mystical construct, so violence to his physical body will not be enough to end his dark reign.

Hah, I can see you are no stranger to inexplicable arcane phenomenon!\n\nTogether, we will construct a symbolic weapon that we can use to smash the phylactery. Normal weapons, like hammers, wouldn't make a dent in this thing.

First we gather materials from the tower grounds. They'll be sympathetic foci for the dark power Bloodmage Cassel wields. \n\nOnce we have the materials, we imbue them with gore from the heart. Then … well. Smashy smashy.

Not exactly traditional, I know. But these objects are soaked in the dark aura of this place. They should prove able vessels for the tower's power. \n\nAnd they'll smash the heart without fail. That's important, too.

Aside from releasing some strongly worded condemnations, the order hasn't really done anything. Does intercepting Jakarn signal them switching from talk to action, or is this just the first we noticed?\n\nThey might be setting this place up as a base.

We had a long conversation about her misadventure on Stros M'Kai. About what that signet ring means to Isobel's family, how much damage that conman might have done.\n\nShe seemed quite … sobered by the discussion.
Yes. I'd hoped her brush with misfortune would convince her to buckle down, figure out what she wants out of life.\n\nRunning off at the drop of a hat is hardly the response I expected.
Oh, away. On a ship. You know. Woosh. How can she like that Captain Marso so much?\n\nHe just has a boat. He doesn't even write poetry!
Huh. Well that's not exactly the kind of information I just hand out on a whim, is it? \n\nWhy are you looking for Marso? We've never had trouble with Veloise Mercantile. And Marso is a good 'un.
Oh yes! Give it … ow!\n\nYou have the seathorn? Give it here to Halz, please. And thank you.

She what? She told me … damn her incredible eyes. Aurelia showed up at the port and asked me for help.\n\nShe had people looking into Kiv Lindres, the thief who stole Isobel's ring. She was worried about what he could have done with that signet.
So many questions! I can't keep up with the four of you. I don't know where their ship went. \n\nAsk a shipping perk. No, snipper clerk. Shipping. Clerk. Talk to them.
Oh, a lost lamb! Tugs at my heartstrings, it does.\n\nI tell you what, let's do a trade. You help me with a problem, and I'll tell you where your little lamb has got to. What do you say?
Khajiit stole nothing! It is possible a few bottles of fine wine ended up in this one's pack at the end of card night.\n\nBut ugh … no time for banter. Here is the fine wine from Skyrim.
I'm not sure. We didn't even make it to the village. Maybe they're Kiv's business partners? We can search the bodies later when Aurelia's safe.
Oh, the poet? Yeah, sure. He's been in here a lot recently. He sits in the corner nursing his rum and writing.\n\nHe's not here now, but I think he left some of his work in the back.
You run in interesting circles, friend. No, not that I know of. The Anchor's a bit low brow for her sort, isn't it?\n\nAnything else I can help with?

You have any idea how long I've been in this cage getting nipped at by reef vipers while Titus found you? I bet he was more concerned about those stupid papers than his own sister.\n\nCan you open the cage? I want to get out of here.
A cheating no-good son of a horker named Halz stole a couple of bottles of wine I'd procured for a client.\n\nWhen I confronted him he said, Khajiit stole nothing! Crabby old cat.
Ah, success! You've saved me an awkward discussion with my client, friend.\n\nI thought you'd come through, so I looked up their course. Captain Marso sailed for Rivenspire.

He was to put in at Northpoint, but Marso mentioned they were headed for a little village just outside the city. Some backwater called Northsalt. \n\nBe careful in Rivenspire, swabbie. I've heard dark shadows hang over that part of the world.

Well, I'm far from an expert in such matters, but it started as soon as m'lady opened that old chest. Lady Laurent immediately changed and started acting like an ancient sea captain!\n\nShe's certainly not her usual, demanding self.

So Jakarn mentioned. Well done! I'm not sure how the Ascendant Order ascertained our plans, but at least you recovered the invitation medallions. They're the key, after all. Figuratively and literally.\n\nOh, that's good. I should write that down.

I remember my ship, a proud vessel. And my valiant crew. There was a storm, I think, but I can't remember my name.\n\nHmm. Interesting. My body didn't have quite this many tempting curves the last time I checked.

Why, I'm Captain … Captain …. Hmm. Kynareth's arse, it's right on the tip of my tongue ….\n\nWell, never mind that. Come Janne, we must hither to the big tree! I promised to meet you there and now that I have a body, nothing can stop me!

Hmm. I suppose you've earned that information. The Society of the Steadfast has decided to sponsor peace talks to end the Three Banners War. The medallions will allow the chosen delegates to enter the hidden location where the talks will be held.

That, my dear, is precisely what I plan to figure out. These talks are too important to allow anything to interfere with them. We must determine what the Ascendant Order wants, and we must do so quickly.\n\nBut first, may I have the medallions?

Precisely! These bandit knights tried to kill High King Emeric, Queen Ayrenn, and Prince Irnskar, but the Magus lost control of his spell. \n\nThanks to you, we now believe the leaders are on the island of Amenos. We're going to rescue them, my dear.

That's for smarter minds to figure out. I'm a thief. My skills don't lend themselves to uncovering mysteries and determining motives. Want me to steal something, find something, or seduce someone? I'm your man. Otherwise, I just go where I'm told.

I suppose you can call it that. It serves the nearby prison stockade, though the worst offenders are banished to the jungle.\n\nThe Empire used to send prisoners to Amenos, and it still is a dumping ground for people the authorities want to disappear.

House Mornard runs the prison stockade for the Daggerfall crown. They profit off the prisoner exchanges, the mines in the jungle, other prisoner labor.\n\nAnd they maintain Amenos Station, the only true civilization on the entire island.
Za'ji has a few talents. Sniffing out treasure is one of them. For all the fools errands he's lead me on, there's been a payout worth the risk.
Well, binding the parts together won't be a problem. The real question is, how do we imbue it with the heart's power?\n\nMy research indicates the tower's energies flow into the watercourse nearby.

I want to tell you it's just a feeling, but it's more than that. This is the high king's retreat, and none of his soldiers are here to meet us. Plus, see that ship over there? It's not flying any colors. I bet the Ascendant Order arrived on that.

First find the leaders. If you can't do that, find the Serpents. One of them is bound to know something. I hear they have a camp northeast of the jungle gate.\n\nAnd take this flare. The three captains are circling the island, waiting for your signal.
Arkay only knows, but my weary soul feels freer already. I just hope to look upon the open sea one last time before he sweeps me away.
They are still here, so there is still a chance! We mustn't let them escape with the prize!
Za'ji appreciates your plucky spirit. The Pounce could use more volunteers like yourself!
Whether it's Dragons or plunder, Za'ji really likes your okay-fine-I'll-do-it attitude, walker. You're a good one.

The magic of this place permeates everything. As you saw, the water here has taken on aspects of the bloodmage's power. \n\nNow that we have a hammer made of the pain and death in this place, we just have to—for lack of a better term—forge it.
Isn't magic strange? I believe if we dip the weapon into a trough of this churning water, it should have all the properties we need to destroy the heart.

I do. With enough time he might be able to recreate his phylactery, even limited as he would be in his hemomorphic spiritual form.\n\nWe won't give him the chance. You, Dame Madach, and I will put an end to him. Once and for all.
Haha. They … They don't feel good either. I'm afraid this is as far as I go.\n\nYou and Sir Rayan will need to finish our quest. Dash it all.
You're so close to victory. And … there will be a spot in the Order when I'm gone. \n\nHe becomes a full-fledged knight today. I'm glad I could play a part.

Aye, I took on this quest knowing it would be my end. I have … only a few months to live. \n\nA wasting disease. So terribly cliche. I couldn't stomach the thought of my last tale ending in a sickbed somewhere.

You got big ears, new meat.\n\nIf you must know, word around the stockade is that the Green Serpents are offering a way off this rock. Something about friends in high places. You just need to find a trio of nobles supposedly wandering the jungle.

I am not—ugh! There may be a chance that Vinilsare is right. But, our life together hinges on this job. The, uh, lack of coins in our purses is already damaging our marriage. \n\nPlease. Say you'll get those scoria.

I know, I acted quickly. But listen, I have so much to say. \n\nAfter the … problems with Kiv, I had a long conversation with mother. She really helped me to understand how badly someone could bungle things with that signet.

I did! You don't spend your life as the knight commander's daughter without learning the value of a good scribe. \n\nI managed to stop most of Kiv's schemes with a few letters, but he withdrew some money from an account in Northpoint.

First I've heard of the place. But if it's really High King Emeric's personal retreat, we can expect it to be heavily guarded. \n\nHopefully, the Lion Guard can hold off the Ascendant Order until we get there to help them.
I did. And … agh. I can't believe it. She's been impulsive before, but this? Running around pretending she's Investigator draighing Vale?

Yeah, I noticed that, too. Let's head there. We can't just wander the island calling his name. At least this gives us a direction.\n\nAnton knows enough to hide. But I doubt he'd last long. Usually he's the one people notice while I lift their gold.
We recently gained access to Alkosh's Void. We wanted to collect data so I sent the initiate in to do some research.
Excellent! Hopefully we have enough information now.
Ah, yes. Remarkable craftsmanship. Valessea has come a long way since she was my apprentice.\n\nI created the master. It was no small feat! Intricate work making enchantments of such power.

Once I slip the chain over my head, the medallion will be linked to me until the peace talks are concluded.\n\nAnd is that second medallion for the Fighters Guild? I suggest you get it to them as soon as you can.
Sure. Two noses are better than one. If we can pick up Queen Ayrenn's scent, I can track her. That's sort of my specialty. The nose knows, as the kittens say.\n\nStay close and follow me.

Peace conference? Is that what this is all about? Za'ji received orders from the crown. I guess we were conscripted. Once I learned that our passenger was Queen Ayrenn, I was dumbfounded that she chose the Perfect Pounce.\n\nProud, but dumbfounded.

Za'ji's alive! That's good to know. Now I can kill him for getting us wrecked as soon as I see him.\n\nWhen the storm hit, it was all I could do to hang onto some wreckage and make it to this beach. We're on Amenos, right?
Sure. Two noses are better than one. If we can pick up Queen Ayrenn's scent, I can track her. That's sort of my specialty. The nose knows, as the kittens say.\n\nStay close and follow me.
Peace conference? Is that what this is all about? \n\nZa'ji received orders from the crown. Probably because of our reputation as Dragon slayers. And smugglers. We're good at that, too.

She's been keeping me abreast of her investigation. The princess detective, I've taken to calling her. \n\nAurelia still believes she can retrieve the money stolen from Isobel's family. She feels quite guilty about it.

Apparently quite well, Aurelia's last message was all smiles. It's on the table, there. Please, take it with you. She and Marso would visit soon, she said, back home to give Isobel the good news. \n\nWill you return to Rivenspire? See how she's doing?
Hmm, you know me all too well, my friend. Some of this hurts to read. Why didn't Aurelia tell me she blamed herself? And enough that she feared speaking with me?\n\nThat girl, I swear to Stendarr ….
Yes … it's … Draigh! I'm finally a good influence on her, and she might be missing?\n\nLet's head to Fell's Run. We're not going to learn anything standing here smelling the rum fumes.

I'm fine, I'm fine. \n\nCaptain Marso and I were following up on that criminal conspiracy we uncovered in Northpoint. You remember, Kiv Lindres stole Isobel's signet ring, and managed to cause her family some trouble.

Yes! Kiv owed money to someone named Vetitia Marcott. She's part of a minor noble family here in Rivenspire. Apparently they were a part of King Ranser's traitorous army during that terrible civil war.
Of course, ask me anything. I'll help however I can.

I think we did … well. Too good a job. We set out to discover what happened to the money stolen from Isobel's family. \n\nMarso and I found a number of leads, which took us practically to the Marcott family front door.
Just west of Lorkrata Ruins. The Scar is home to a group of orcs called the Oathbound. \n\nFrom the description of his attackers, it sounds like Vetitia is paying them to hold Marso. For the moment.
Just getting out into the fresh air is an improvement. That place was a nightmare. \n\nBrigands, Daedra, rats … I wasn't sure if I'd end up with a knife in my gut or eaten by Ogrim.

Ahh … I tell you what, my friend. That woman is like the sea. She'd come roaring in and smash aside those in her path. Heh. \n\nHere, I can get back to the Fell's Run on my own. You two go ahead and let Aurelia know I'm safe.
The child said Aurelia called the brigand Vetitia? Isn't she the one that kidnapped Marso?\n\nShe went north, toward the old Ayleid ruin northeast of town. I'd bet that Vetitia took her there!
I'm tired but … happy. My life has changed so quickly it made my head spin. \n\nAnd the part that twisted me up the most was my changing feelings. Heh, and my changing friendship.

I'm not the little girl who gave her friend a ring. And she's not some entitled princess. I think she truly cares for Marso. You can see it in every word, every gesture ….\n\nDivines help me, I've read too many romance novels.

He'll have to. No one else is desperate enough to come here and collect vulk'esh scoria. \n\nBesides, our health matters more than his good opinion of us. We'll wait for Tarrinore to recover before we head out.
With a plan, my dear. Head up to the courtyard and confront the Ascendant Champion. In the meantime, Jakarn and I will make our way around the back and surprise her mage from behind.

Ah. Yes. I have heard that sentiment before. It was my use of expensive words, wasn't it?\n\nDame Madach has been an able teacher, and I'm a fair hand with a blade. But my mouth and my mind are my greatest weapons.

As sure as the light of Magnus rises upon the face of Nirn each morning. \n\nI've wanted to join the knightly orders since I was a child at my father's knee. Dame Madach was good enough to take me into her service. I'll do her proud. You'll see.

Haha! You think Vinilsare will let me walk out of here on my own? She probably won't let me fetch water by myself for the rest of my life! \n\nDon't worry about me. I'm going to be smothered in scolding conversations and healing teas.

I was looking over that outcropping above us when it crumbled underneath me. I banged myself up pretty good on the way down. I'm going to get such a lecture about how Vinilsare knew this cave was dangerous.\n\nIt's really annoying when she's right.

An excellent question! We stand before the Spire of the Crimson Coin. A relic of a bygone era, the time of the Breton coin-barons. \n\nThe Systres have been owned by many groups over the years, sold and resold by Tamsfolk on the continent.

I have only an educated guess … but my guesses are usually pretty good. I believe the spire's ruler is none other than Jacquard Cassel, archmagus in service to House Guimard some thousand years ago. \n\nFascinating, isn't it?

Apologies! My name is Isobel Veloise. I'm an aspirant in the Sapphire Tourney, a proving ground for squires looking to join the knightly orders.\n\nAurelia's mother is Knight Commander, and umm … brashly offered her daughter's hand as a prize.

Well, normally aspirants only compete in one of the trials. If I can win all three, the Knight Commander will be compelled to grant a boon of my choosing. I can free Aurelia from her mother's promise! \n\nWhat do you say? Will you be my second?
Most of my life, really. I've been her squire since I was first able to hold my own sword. \n\nIt was an inspiration to see her in fighting form, wasn't it?

She was ill for some time, just a short while ago. Past it now, I'm sure. But she's such a vibrant force, on the battlefield or the stage.\n\nIt was a blow to see her barely able to swing a blade. Not like today, hah!

I've learned a lot from Dame Madach's … erm … unorthodox leadership approach. She firmly believes in pushing squires to better themselves. \n\nAs she likes to say, I'm not your captain, kid. Figure it out!
I didn't, but I suspected. She's been a bit quieter, the last few months. \n\nShe'd never make people worry about her. Those of us closest to her would be the last she'd want to know.

She was trying, sometimes insufferable, our Dame Madach. I mean, look at this hat.\n\nBut she was also the most generous, kind person I've ever known. And her example is one I shall follow to the end of my days.

Each of the captains have their own view on how to earn honor. I've heard stories that the Iron Knot's captain, Orlfeth, has slain trolls twice her size!\n\nSo just swinging a sword won't impress her. She wants warriors that can think as well as fight.

Hah, that's a funny thought. I don't think so? But we can ask her. \n\nThe hilt itself is classic Iron Knot. A historic trophy from a mighty warrior who fell in single combat at a crucial battle. And changed history with his blade.
Ugh. Langley is a bore, Brelannal cares only for coin, and Snegh is an oaf.\n\nAnd then there's the milksop, moribund Mortens. The less said about him, the better.

That's a complicated question. The easy response is that Commander Jourvel never goes back on her word.\n\nBut it's more than that. The tourney means the world to her, and in recent years we've had fewer entrants.
I am. I founded our alliance right after I accepted my dead father's crown. Anything else you want to know? We are still lost in a hostile jungle, in case you haven't noticed.

Royal duties in Elden Root are as frustrating as ever, but the Dominion holds strong. \n\nThere's been so much strife just in the few years I've been queen. Is it wrong to hope peace might one day surround the eagle banner?

Well, vulk'esh are creatures of lava, right? The scoria is what happens when the lava meets the air and cools down. \n\nIt's not good for crafting, but skilled alchemists and scholars are very interested in it. Which is how we got this job.

Right now I should say those trees that are blocking the path!\n\nI, Langley LeTarte, arrived here first. My faithful second shall aid me in removing the trees. Then we shall proceed into the woods. You two will just have to wait.
I'm glad you're helping her out. She's a nice lady and I felt bad leaving her in the lurch.\n\nBut Langley was very persuasive, and I really have to become a squire. So ….

Thank you. Some days I fear all this death and pain will be for nothing. But in times like these, times that challenge every belief we have, we must stand together. \n\nThat's why the Dominion was founded. And why we will claim victory in the end.

Well that is a shame. But, the Knight Commander herself offered Aurelia's hand! She is honor bound to keep that promise. \n\nI don't want to boast, but I will be an exceptional knight. With Lady Aurelia's connections, we would be … perfection.

I was here first, I should note! Look at me! I am large. I am muscular and well-trained.\n\nIf Isobel and I were to come to blows, I'd likely trounce her. That would upset my lovely-bride-to-be, Lady Aurelia.

I did! But just look at Langley. He already acts like a knight. When he joins the Order of the Iron Knot, he'll be the most knightly … uh, knight … in the order!\n\nMy father was very clear, no excuses. So here I am. Chopping this tree.

The old ways are gone. The High Elves, the Khajiit, and the Wood Elves have the strength of will and character to unify Tamriel.\n\nI know we may not see eye to eye, but the war has only served to forge my resolve. I believe it with all my heart.

It was a well-planned and dastardly attack. I could sense the magical nature of the summoned storm, and none of my own arcane protections functioned. They blocked them somehow.\n\nIf the storm hadn't raged out of control, I'd be dead now.

Plans, of a sort. Diagrams. Techniques for outfitting a ship that have been lost to time! But not forever, Za'ji hopes such important things would be preserved against the weather when one's trade involves the sea.

Truthfully, walker, Za'ji came here with his trusty first mate, Caska, but a monster ambushed us at the old mill and we were separated in this soupy fog!\n\nZa'ji was waiting for Caska to find him when you arrived. Now we need wait no longer!

Oh, there are many legends about Shipwright's Regret, walker. Za'ji's favorite is that they built a ship so large it sunk the yard when they dropped it into the sea, though what he is most interested in are the tales of the First Era.
Crisp air winds its way through the town and another season turns. Ah, it's time to create another magnificent offering to Zenithar!
Why not? For old times' sake. You have a gift! These apples won't just bake themselves, you know.

Correct. Which brings us to our present situation. We need to steal an Order ship and use it to sail past their fleet to All Flags Castle. We can't aid the alliance leaders if we never make it to the islet. Go talk to Kaleen and let's find this cove.

I wish I knew. Duchess Elea was aware of the site, of course, but not of our plan to move the leaders there so soon. Now that we know the Ascendant Magus is actually Count Damard, it's possible he overheard or saw something in his sister's court.
I should bloody well hope so, after all this.\n\nThank you, adventurer. Now … let me talk to my squire one last time.

We knew the Order had resources. Count Damard's rich and his family owns a shipyard. I imagine he quietly ordered some extra construction or even commandeered vessels from his own shipyards.\n\nI suspect he's been planning this for quite some time.

Properly garrisoned, All Flags Castle could hold off any fleet. But we don't have the forces at present to defend the ramparts. \n\nMagical wards protect Memorial Hall, however. I hope we'll find our delegates safely behind those wards when we arrive.

I mean, they're not real pirates. They're knights who ride the waves instead of horses. And sing. By the gods do they sing.\n\nThere's an old joke around the castle that they're called the Order of the Albatross because they're so damned loud.

Yes, a golden lute. The story goes that some years back the head of the order, Sir Brenvale, went down to clear the catacombs of a mad spirit. \n\nI think it was some Dufort noble? I'm not sure who. But Sir Brenvale never returned.

I'll be honest, this is one order I'm not likely to join. They're an odd group. \n\nBut it kind of makes sense. Just think of them as something like chivalric bards. They're constantly on the hunt for new adventures, new tales to tell.

Not much to tell. Archdruid Agathie oversees our community here. A number of the village elders serve as her advisors and help train the younger aspirants and initiates in the True Way.\n\nI'll introduce you to them once we get to the village.
Right now? But—all right. \n\nIf knowing more about them will help you save the others, I guess I can stay in this place for a bit longer.

Za'ji heard tales that this sodden shipyard outfitted a hodgepodge of provincial fleets into the swiftest, strongest armada to ever sail the seas! The shipwrights could turn an incredible ship into an invincible one, and Za'ji has an incredible ship.

They're the ones who should be locked up in the Amenos stockade! They're not even supposed to be here! They corrupt nature. Even their magic does horrible things. It hurts too. The way Sunigil screamed ….

Does there have to be a reason? Eldertide Druids can corrupt other sea creatures, too. Urchins, sea stars, fish, crabs, that sort of thing. But the coral they corrupted here? It looks like the coral that wrecked the ship. \n\nThey planned this.
I passed by one a little while back. It should be down that way. \n\nThe other corals are probably inside the caves. We could still hear our shipmates' screams from the cages we were locked in.
They changed the coral into something unnatural. It stinks of druid magic and … blood. \n\nIt'll look different too, if there's light enough to see. I'm not going to let them turn me into that.
Oh, the fiercest of Khajiit, walker. When Za'ji's guile and charisma cannot solve his troubles—which is rare—then Caska's muscles often do.\n\nShe is surely safe in his absence.
Of course, walker! She is as much a fixture of the Perfect Pounce as Za'ji himself!\n\nHe is certain Caska must still be searching for him somewhere. If we are thorough, we will surely cross paths!
Za'ji believes so, yes. At least, he has ruled out nearly every other shipyard it could be. Of course, it would be the most dangerous, but nothing ventured, nothing gained!

The greatest fleet in the history of Tamriel sailed to war with the Sload. Ships from every province and navy banded together as one armada!\n\nZa'ji heard rumors that all those mighty vessels were outfitted by the greatest shipyard in High Rock.
I found a lantern, I have my sword. I shall be perfectly fine. \n\nGood luck with the spiders, and the ghosts, and whatnot out there.

I suppose in the stories knights are usually all swords and glory. But the druids have been here forever, practically.\n\nEvery kid in the Systres grows up knowing a little bit about runes, and nature, and the True Way.
I think they used to be? But no, these days anyone can join. Even non-mages who want to learn the ways of Y'ffre.\n\nJust another little quirk of life on High Isle.

She knows how to guide those new to Zenithar's teachings along the path to his wisdom. \n\nShe'll ask you to craft, trade, gather, and toil. I am but a novice in the light of her experience. Truly, she shines with Zenithar's favor.

The Covenant remains strong. Or so I tell myself from atop the lumpy pillow on my unbearably uncomfortable throne.\n\nLook, we've accomplished quite a bit in these past few years. I mean, you tell me. Is it madness to hope for peace in our time?

What does a high king do? Everything and nothing, or so it seems some days. I lead the Daggerfall Covenant, I rule over High Rock, and I attend meetings. So many meetings!\n\nAny other questions before more of these Serpents show up?
Oh no, no, no. That would be wildly inappropriate.\n\nI pulled this challenge directly from the pages of one of my favorite books. Who can blame me? I'm a daffy old wizard. Hehe!

I was her student for a time. I spent years with her, working by her side on a daily basis. Now that I've advanced to a more learned position, I am in awe of how effortless she made teaching me seem. \n\nHer devotion to Zenithar is an inspiration.

Indeed. The people of High Rock, Hammerfell, and Wrothgar seek to build a future together. A process you've been a part of.\n\nSomeday, the Covenant will be victorious. In my heart, I believe that. But if we can achieve peace sooner, why not try?
That's a good question. Jorunn the Skald-King was invited, of course, but the official response we got out of Mournhold was short and sweet—his son would negotiate on the Pact's behalf.

When Ranser challenged my rule, an alliance seemed a prudent course for a quick resolution. Luckily, it was still in place when the Empire collapsed.\n\nThe Covenant represents a return to the ideals of the past and, I believe, our best hope for peace.
Something else, friend?

I can use something as simple as a thin blade to strip the bark from the wood. Then I can turn the wood into strips. One has to separate the pieces by their natural growth rings. It's laborious, but fulfilling work.
Check the trees around Belkarth's perimeter, just beyond this square.
Just passing through. You'd be surprised at just how useful random information about small towns or crafting techniques can be in my line of work.

Knowing Naryu is … like walking on warm sand. Sometimes it is nice between the toes, and sometimes there are stabbing pains. \n\nThe last time Raz saw Naryu, he threw an iced sweetroll at her. It is only a matter of time before his feet burn.

In a word, yes. Pretend Emeric is your prisoner, escort him to the front gate, and wait for them to let you in.\n\nMeanwhile, the queen and I will await your signal. After we free Irnskar, we'll find a place to signal the rescue ship.

That's the only thing that makes any sense. Why else place deadly spells upon the medallions if they didn't want us to retrieve and deliver them?\n\nAnd why leave me in that cave for you to find? They wanted us to do their dirty work for them.
Chyrisnia? She decided to stay with me and Veslyn. Become a transport sentry.

No, but that was all part of the ruse. The Ascendant Champion sacrificed her own people to convince us that nothing was wrong. She must be a heartless monster!\n\nDelric died to show us the truth. Let's not waste this opportunity to make things right.

A sailor I admire said the druids are experimenting. Enchanting some creatures the likes of which no one's seen or heard of before. \n\nNow don't go asking me where, I don't know. Just be on your guard. It is a strange world we live in.

Oh, they always knew about the druids. We're just the first survivors. \n\nTurns out those zealots aren't just messing with sea life. There are rumors of vines bursting from the coast, ground splitting, and one so ridiculous I can hardly believe it.

The spell I created has my magical … mark on it, if that makes sense. There are certain types of magic that can be affected by their creator, intentionally or not. \n\nMessing with forces already attuned to you can have unpredictable results.

Mostly trying to keep anything with ill intent away from you.\n\nMy errant spell seems to be affecting the creatures around Tor Draioch in all kinds of ways. Things that were once docile might be a little … grumpy right now.

Exactly. Magic is powerful and great and all that, but it can be pretty sensitive. Fussy, Magister Irin likes to say. \n\nAnd since my spell is already wreaking havoc across Tor Draioch, I'd rather not take any unnecessary risks while fixing it.
Sergeant Brusic says we're getting a break from our regular duties by delivering supplies around the city. \n\nI'm not sure what he was told, but this feels more like a punishment than a break.

I bet the city does, but that's not our job. We're meant to be traveling back and forth to Amenos. Making sure the prisoners are transported safe and orderly. They're our responsibility.\n\nWho knows who's watching them now?

Not every sentry cares to know why the prisoners are being taken there. They're not all dangerous. Take Chyrisnia. She'd never hurt us. Steal some coins, maybe, but draw blood? No.\n\nBut some sentries treat them all like murderers.
She volunteered to work for House Mornard. We hired her on a probationary period. \n\nSergeant Brusic and I are training her!

Heh, not being killed for some druid's evil plan or slaving in a mine will do that to you. Turns out not making extra work for the people just trying to keep you alive is a good idea.\n\nI'll have to remember that. Seems like it'll be useful later.

It wasn't always. It used to be one of the safest locations on the island. In fact, my ancestors deemed the grove sacred when they first arrived.\n\nNow the corrupted wildlife attacks for no reason, and some of my fellow druids have been afflicted.

Not much, unfortunately. I noticed its affects a short time ago. Usually docile creatures turning aggressive. A strange blight spreading through the plants and trees.\n\nI brought my concerns to the archdruid, who initially thought I was overreacting.

Not to be confused with our ritual circles, I mean the druids of the archipelago all belong to one of three distinct subgroups. You would probably call it a sect. Those who hold to the same circle share common beliefs and approaches to Y'ffre's will.

Just that. They have become as hostile as the rest of the afflicted wildlife. We may have to deal with any corrupted druids we meet.\n\nBut with your help and the blessing of the True Way, we'll soon have a solution to present to the circle elders.

Well, I've been thinking. I'm grateful to Magister Irin, but sitting and reading about magic has little appeal to me. This whole thing just proved to me that I'm too restless here. I want to do magic, not just study it! Go on adventures! See things!

I think it's time. I've been given good training here, but I still have a lot to learn.\n\nFor me, the best teachers are curiosity and experience. I learn best by doing, so I need to get out in the world and continue my training.

Nothing truly valuable, but Isobel gave me that ring with her family crest all those years ago. \n\nI know it's important to her, and I really wanted to get it back. When I went to the town guard, they just laughed at me!
And we will—after we deal with the Ascendant Order leaders! Emeric would agree. And so would Ayrenn.\n\nCome, friend, we can deal with these traitors in one fell swoop!

Suungir, Axe of the Skald-King! It feels good to cradle you in my arms again, you powerful blade!\n\nBut we can't go yet. The Serpents said that something called the Ascendant Order is behind this. Their leaders, the Lord and Magus are here!
Unfortunately no. The wards are just to keep the unstable magic inside the bounds of Tor Draioch. That way, I can work on a counterspell without worrying about the original spell spreading.

Magister Irin made sure I knew what they were and what purpose they served as soon as he took me on as an apprentice. He wanted me to be familiar with as much of Tor Draioch as possible. Or, at least the parts that keep it safe.

No. I was a pirate, but where did that get me? In line to be a lump of sea rock. I'll try my hand as a prisoner transport sentry. We'll see how that works out. \n\nBut for now, I've got a deck to clean.

Oh, pish-posh. Do these look like the ink-stained fingers of a writer of overly imaginative and lurid tales to you?\n\nI am rather fond of the bawdy investigator and her adventures, though. They remind me of my younger days.

Excellent! I hope you're knowledgeable. The other devotees of Zenithar at my Abbey detest my quiz. Apparently it's difficult and arduous. But the gift of Zenithar cannot be given for free. \n\nAre you certain you're prepared for this?

Never heard of High Isle? I'm not surprised. It's sort of a get-away spot for nobles and royalty. It's the largest island in the Systres Archipelago, in the Abecean Sea.\n\nTechnically it's a Breton territory, but most treat it as neutral ground.

Did he now? And what other secrets has he revealed, I wonder. Well, let me sate your curiosity. \n\nI've been many things in my long career. Mercenary, Lion Guard officer, spy, and agent of the High King, to name a few. I have many talents, my dear.

So long as the gold keeps flowing, sure. I'm a man who lets the potential rewards dictate where I go and what I do. But I will admit to being slightly invested in this whole ordeal now. The Ascendant Order got under my skin. So now it's personal.
What is Zenithar the god of?
Zenithar is both a warrior and a god of peace. What symbol is associated with him?
Zenithar does not ask much of his worshipers, only that we see the value in our actions. That being said, what is something that would offend him?
Many devotees will talk about the Resolutions of Zenithar. What is it?
That's correct! But, I wonder if you'd be so knowledgeable when it comes to the application of all Zenithar's taught us? Are you ready for another question?

That's not quite correct. There's a festival taking place in Belkarth. Perhaps you should inquire about the Lord of Labor there.\n\nOf course, you're more than welcome to think a moment and try my questions again.

Yes, my dear. It's really quite beautiful. I have a manor there. For those brief periods when I'm not working on one thing or another.\n\nThe Society of the Steadfast selected it specifically for the peace talks. I can't wait for them to get underway.

I'm not sure. The motes aren't new, they're always hanging around Tor Draioch. I think they're drawn to places like this.\n\nBut there was nothing in my spell that should have made them act malevolent. And there are a lot more around than usual.

Yes. I can make traps to contain them, but I'm still worried about their behavior. While I work on the traps, could you head into the tower and look through Magister Irin's things? He might have a book with more information about the motes.

Never believe what you read in the chronicles. Do these look like the ink-stained fingers of a scrivener to you? \n\nI am rather fond of the bawdy investigator and her exploits, though. They remind me of my younger, carefree days of adventure.

Just that they're little more than well-armed bandits. They've been recruiting the poor to bolster their numbers. Now they're robbing caravans while claiming they fight for justice.\n\nBah. Honest folk don't hide their faces behind helmets and masks.

Yes! You answered my questions correctly! You've earned your reward. Here I'll bestow you with Zenithar's Blessing.\n\nMay Zenithar watch over you and help you to see opportunities for work and growth wherever they present themselves.
Your child comes of age and asks for guidance on what path she should follow in her life to please Zenithar. What advice do you give?

That's not quite correct. There's a festival taking place in Belkarth. Perhaps you should inquire about the Lord of Labor there.\n\nOf course, you're more than welcome to think a moment and try my questions again.
Before you lies a coin purse filled with gleaming coins, the mallet you whittled by hand last winter, and a tome given to you by a traveling mage. Which would make the most appropriate offering?

Zenithar comes to you on your deathbed and asks what accomplishment you're the most proud of completing in your lifetime. What is your answer?\n\nThe integrity of your family name, the wealth growing in your coffer, or the land you amassed?
You catch a thief robbing from a merchant in the marketplace. How would you ensure Zenithar's justice is carried out?

That's not quite correct. There's a festival taking place in Belkarth. Perhaps you should inquire about the Lord of Labor there.\n\nOf course, you're more than welcome to think a moment and try my questions again.

That's not quite correct. There's a festival taking place in Belkarth. Perhaps you should inquire about the Lord of Labor there.\n\nOf course, you're more than welcome to think a moment and try my questions again.

One of those motes got to her. Thankfully it was just one of the mischievous ones. It turned her into a guar.\n\nDon't worry, it's just an illusion. She'll be disoriented, but unharmed. In fact, I think some time as a reptile might be good for her.

To be fair, she didn't like me first. When Magister Irin took me in, Huldressa didn't waste any time deciding I was a no-good street urchin who's too impulsive for her own good. She's not entirely wrong, but she never even gave me a chance!

I think so. I'm using a variation of something I was already working on. I enchanted a bit of silver for each of them.\n\nIt's simple, when a mote gets near one of the traps, it should suck it up. Like … pffffft!

The original idea was an olive branch for Huldressa—a spell that cleans up dust. My magicka practice kicks up a lot of the stuff, so I wanted to make something that would help her out a bit. \n\nI'll make the traps using the same design.

Magister Irin knows what he signed up for. Taking me on … I'll admit, it's no small feat. But he's never judged me for being the way I am. Which is why I don't want to disappoint him by ruining his tower with unhinged magic. \n\nHe does a lot for me.

Darkened the beacon? The locals revere that light—who would dare offend Kynareth in such a way? Something is indeed wrong here. \n\nAt least our missing ships reached these waters, but this storm worries me. Tell me more about the rogue knights.

The Ascendant Order? Of course. I thought the rumors about rogue knights troubling folk outside of town had a familiar ring. But I hoped we'd seen the last of the Order at Sword's Rest.\n\nTell me, did you learn anything at the Shallows?

To disrupt the peace talks? It would be a grand stage for the Ascendant Order's message. Or … they might plan to strike at the delegations. Influential voices from all three alliances will be here soon.\n\nA tempting target.

The Ascendant Champion's superior. When we defeated the Champion at Sword's Rest Isle, we only defeated one of the Order's leaders.\n\nI've heard whispers about an Ascendant Lord, too. I can't imagine there are too many more of them after that.

Then you have come to the right place!\n\nTales of Tribute is a game of stories—some fantastical, and others all too real. Two players share their tales with decks of cards. The game is elegant and easy to learn, but it takes great effort to master.

First, you will need two decks. Each deck represents a different story—a different strategy. Your opponent brings two decks as well. Once you and your adversary combine your decks, the game can begin.\n\nA shared pool, you see? A level field of play.

It seems the Ascendant Order knew the ships would be wrecked, and they helped make sure by extinguishing the lighthouse beacon. They knew my cargo was coming to High Isle!\n\nThis means the Fighters Guild and Mages Guild delegates are in danger, too.
