It seems the Ascendant Order knew the ships would be wrecked, and they helped make sure by extinguishing the lighthouse beacon. They knew my cargo was coming to High Isle!\n\nThis means the Fighters Guild and Mages Guild delegates are in danger, too.
Buried at the base of a twin-spire rock. It's just north of Ogondar's Winery.\n\nHey. Uh, no offense, but I hope we never meet again.

I only met Guild General Quentyn when he arrived. He seems to have a good head on his shoulders, but the war has cost him dearly—he lost his wife in a raid.  \n\nI understand why the Fighters Guild chose to send him to the conference.

Her name is Ryvana. She's something of a local apothecary. She uses her skill with herbs and healing to help the folk of High Isle.\n\nWith the conference delayed, Valessea was curious about druidic magic so off she went. Quentyn decided to tag along.

Make your way to the beginner's lounge and find my associate, Brahgas. Tell him Razhamad approved an initiation match. He will lend you a pair of decks and teach you the basics.\n\nComplete this trial, then return to me for your reward!

Yes, of course!\n\nAs Brahgas no doubt told you, I am Razhamad. I hold many roles and offices—Tribute master, game-baron, and proprietor of this hall. I also lead our regional Roister's Club chapter—the Gonfalon Chapter.

Brahgas … yes, he loves the game in his way. I wish he exercised more caution. He often forgets how much he has to lose.\n\nBut he's a bright lad. Full of youthful energy and hope. That is more than I can say about most people in this world.

Oh, did he? Oh, I love it when we bring new players into the fold! Gets boring playing the same old salts day after day. We need new blood in here!\n\nNow, before we begin, you'll need these. Two Tribute decks you can borrow for educational purposes!

You try to defeat me, of course! First to forty prestige, or winning the favor of all the patrons, is the victor. Don't worry, chum. I'll explain that as we go along.\n\nAnd loosen up, eh? You'll do fine. I'll go easy on you!
Sure. Talking's a big part of the job, after all. The part that doesn't pay anything.\n\nWhat do you want to know?

Yeah. Read up. We keep an official Roister's Club rules guide right there on the bar. Have a look any time you like.\n\nOh, and try not to spill your ale on it. Damn sea-legged locals don't appreciate a good leather-bound book.

Eh. I dabble.\n\nI like to think of myself as more of an observer. I love the game, its rules, the art—all of that. But I just don't have the time to play it. Too busy taking care of the hall. This place'd be a dump without me!

Well, there's Brahgas. Kid's got a good heart but keeps his purse-strings looser than an ogre's trousers. Heard he's been betting on Tribute matches recently. Lots of coin changing hands.\n\nLad's going to end up in a cell or a ditch if he keeps it up.

Now, you claim membership in the Gonfalon Chapter of the Roister's Club—a fraternity of Tribute players committed to fair play and stiff competition.\n\nAs an official Roister, you will gain access to a host of opponents and decks of your very own!

Oh, countless rewards! With each victory, you will rise higher in the club rankings. Do well enough and you may even earn the right to challenge the club's founders—the creators of the game itself!\n\nSo, what do you say? Will you join us?
Oh, you'll find druids throughout the Systres Archipelago. Not too many on the mainland, though. Long ago, we druids left Tamriel and its troubles behind us. But here, our ancient ways survived.
Our forebears among the Bretons believed civilization should live alongside nature, not tame it. In the early years of the Direnni Hegemony, they struggled for the soul of High Rock.

We follow the old ways. Some call us priests of Y'ffre, but that is only part of our truth. We are children of the land, like the wyrd. Guides and teachers to those who live in harmony with nature. People were not meant to bow before crowns of metal.

No, friend. We know the wyrd and we respect their beliefs—druids and wyresses are two branches that grow from the same tree. But we are called to be in this world, not to withdraw from it.\n\nSome circles see it differently, of course.

Circles are fellowships of like-minded druids. Each interprets Y'ffre's will differently, but druids of the same circle share common traditions. And goals.\n\nI belong to the Stonelore Circle. We seek to teach others by the example of our work.

Yes. Travel far enough in the archipelago and you may meet druids of the Eldertide or Firesong circles. Although the Firesong rarely leave their island, and you should be wary of the Eldertide. They do not like city folk or mainlanders.

They lost. Driven into exile, the druids left to seek a place where they could live according to their beliefs. Their wanderings brought them to the Systres. \n\nThe followers of the Wyrd remained behind. They walked a different path than the druids.
An offering? Like food? Do the gods even eat? \n\nOh! I have a little gold. It's not much. I turned to the God of Coin for a reason. But still, give a little to get a lot? That makes sense.
All right. I'll try anything at this point. My situation can't get any worse. \n\nHere goes nothing. I hope Zenithar approves.
Oh, look. They have little anvils on them, like the shrines to Zenithar do. He has to approve of me using these.\n\nAll right, I'll give this a try.

Woah! I've never seen a vegetable this big before. If the gods can eat, I hope they like radishes. This one could feed at least four gods, I'm sure of it!\n\nAll right, time to give it to the Trader God.

Well, we can't just barge in. We're not blue enough or ugly enough to pass for Sea Elves, so disguise isn't an option. Hmm.\n\nLet's keep moving along the ridge. Adwig said he'd try to meet us on the far side of the cove. I might have a plan.

Of course I do! No offense, but I treasure every moment I get to be alone. Privacy is not something we sea captains have in great supply.\n\nAnyway, you're the one who's going to be carrying sacks of exploding powder, right? My job's easy!

You won't like it. Well, maybe you will. You have a bit of a wild streak, yes?\n\nYou said the Sea Elves were gathering kindlepitch back on the shoals. See if you can find any and bring it along. I'll go ahead and try to find Oblan and Adwig.

Well … there's a bit of selfishness there. Our Tribute chapter—the Gonfalon Chapter—needs some new blood. But we make it worth your while!\n\nWe handle all the registration fees, membership dues, and so on. It's a win-win!

Sorinne, right? She definitely has an eye for talent!\n\nYes, I can tell you all about Tribute! It's a card game, a scavenger hunt … Z'en's price, it's practically a religion for some folk. You want fame? Gold? It's all there for the taking!

Ha! A fresh player! Excellent!\n\nFirst things first. You need to learn the rules of the game. And you'll need a couple decks of Tribute cards, of course. Find Razhamad in the Gonfalon Gaming Hall. Tell him Brahgas sent you. He'll get you sorted.

If they recognized us as delegates, there's all sorts of ways they could hold that over the conference. If they just assumed we were rich nobles, ransom is always an option.\n\nBut who can really say what those helmeted bastards are thinking?

Wrecked the ships? How in Oblivion could they coordinate such a thing?\n\nClearly the Ascendant Order is aware of the plans for Lord Bacaro's conference. They're here in force and causing more trouble than we anticipated!

Lady Arabelle and I had dealt with them on the mainland. The Order tried to stop the conference by striking at delegates before they even left Tamriel.\n\nWe stopped them. But not before the previous guild delegate was killed. Then they appointed me.

I came to talk to Ryvana about arcane and related topics, and Quentyn decided to tag along.\n\nWhen Ryvana told us about rogue knights, I feared it might be the Ascendant Order. Quentyn wanted to investigate. Turned out I was right.

I came to talk to Ryvana about arcana and related topics, and Quentyn decided to tag along.\n\nWhen Ryvana told us about rogue knights, I feared it might be the Ascendant Order. Quentyn wanted to investigate. Turned out I was right.

Ah, that part comes later. The darling Valessea has disappeared, so that takes precedence. \n\nI was hired by Lady Arabelle to pick up some medallions from Valessea. But when I got to her workshop, I found the place ransacked and she was gone.

People in my line of work tend to acquire various contacts. I put the word out and finally got one of mine to bite. I'm off to meet up with Tarazka now. \n\nSo, want to help me find Valessea and talk to my contact? You'll be paid, naturally.

The Allwither is a part of us, just as death is a part of life. Two parts of the same circle.  They are back where they belong, in the natural order. And we are where we are needed, maintaining the balance of this sacred grove.

Our people—the Breton people—went astray when they forgot the ways of nature. Stone walls and empty titles separate folk from the True Way. We help them remember what their ancestors once knew.\n\nSome circles see it differently, of course.

We know their medallions aren't there, but they could have lost them at sea. Regardless, if the Ascendant Order uses the chapel as a hideout, we may learn something about their plans. Or a clue as to where to search for the alliance leaders, perhaps.

Yes! And what fragrant challenges they are! Each day, Kishka creates new tasks for rank and renown.\n\nOne will pit you against the common folk of Tamriel. The other will set you against card-playing adventurers like yourself.

Ha! You would fill your purse with heaps of tiny baubles? No, walker! As this one said, you can win one match for a tiny reward or keep playing for a bigger prize!\n\nSimple, yes? The more you play, the sweeter the reward!

It is Kishka's pleasure. Come back soon, yes? This one's grand challenges will be waiting!\n\nNow, you should go find Brahgas. He is out on the seaside patio, most likely. Kishka is very busy doing … something. What was Kishka doing again? Ziss'vo.
All right? All right? She made me look like a guar! What do you think?\n\nI told Magister Irin that Ember was trouble the moment she showed up. Trouble, I said. But did he listen?

There wouldn't be anything to work out if that careless Khajiit would listen more and mind her elders. She's brash and often quite rude.\n\nWhy am I standing here talking to you? I'm going back to my kitchen and I may just have a glass of brandy.

You know me. Every day a new adventure. Had a good thing going for a while, smuggling spices out of Hegathe. Got married twice. No, wait. Three times. \n\nThe third one nearly got me hanged, but Lady Arabelle saved me from the gallows.

Well, I used to. Then Lady Arabelle put me to work chasing stolen medallions and rogue knights all over Tamriel.\n\nI guess she's not so bad once you get to know her. Maybe I'll be my own boss again when this is all over.

It may be unrelated, but my aide Nilsmon has not been seen in days. He is quite fond of Aurelia, and may know more than I do.\n\nYou have my permission to search his bunk, over in the barracks. Down the hall on the left.
Valessea? Poor girl's smitten with me. She can't help it. And who am I to break her heart?\n\nSo I flirt a little, just in case she's looking for an excuse to finally agree to my advances.

I can see why you'd have that opinion. Valessea hides her true feelings well. And she's hesitant to start a romance with a colleague. But she'll come around.\n\nIf not, I can take no for an answer. It's just … that hasn't happened before.

I would be happy to!\n\nThe tournaments started informally. Premiere players like myself and Teliv Fels gathered in major cities to match wits and sharpen our game. The Roister's Club leadership caught wind of it and began sponsoring official events.

Well, many of the players who participated in those early matches went on to form teams which, in the fullness of time, became club-sponsored chapters. Now, those chapters compete against one another in groups.\n\nIt is better to share a victory, yes?

No, my friend. I have achieved all that I set out to achieve at the tournament level. Now, I prefer to observe, teach, and celebrate my pupils' victories! Mostly the celebrating part.\n\nWith luck and determination, we may raise a glass to you someday!

A grand prize, yes! The Roister's Club and city governments all contribute to a weighty purse.\n\nBut, in truth, the greatest Tribute players compete for pride and glory, not coin. And the revels of course. The Gonfalon Chapter loves to celebrate!

Not sure. I picked the lock on the place as soon as I figured out he didn't want me getting in there. He's since put up protections and told me to stay out unless I have his permission. \n\nI'm sure he's got some kind of ward or barrier set up.

Correct. Since you've passed all the trials, you've learned the pass phrase that will let you walk where none have walked for centuries. Just keep following these corridors until you reach the Shield Hall. I'll await you there.

Necessity. I wasn't exactly raised in the lap of luxury. Not even in the lap of genteel poverty, for that matter. \n\nYou get good at things like that if you don't want to be hungry. Or caught by guards or angry merchants.

It wasn't hard. Mages like Magister Irin tend to think in very … magical ways. They'll put magicked reinforcements over every inch of a place, but forget a few pins and a good ear can foil them.\n\nAnd to be fair to him, I'm a very good lockpick.

I worked out a trade. He's got a bad back, and wants to make a seathorn poultice.\n\nShould be some growing along the water east of town. Grab some, then go looking for that thief in the Outlaws Refuge. He'll give you the wine.

Ahhh, thank you new friend. Halz will take this and make a most potent poultice, as taught by his dear sweet Mimi-dra.\n\nTell that Orc next time we play cards, she is the one to be buying the drinks.

Yeah, of course! We should start with rankings.\n\nLook around. Every player you see has a place in the Roister's Club rankings based on their experience. That rank determines who they can and can't challenge. It's banded, see? Like a … layer cake!
With that final and correct answer, I will dispel the wards and grant you access to the Sacred Shield. Congratulations, champion.

The old ritual circle is a place of power and I'm going to need all the help I can get. I plan to draw on the magic there to help strengthen my counterspell. Magister Irin told me about it. This probably isn't how he wanted to implement the lesson.

You're just starting out, so you're at the novice rank. As a novice you can take on other novices, but not higher tier players. Oh don't fret! You'll square off against a game-baron soon enough!\n\nRising in the rankings is just a matter of experience.

Just challenge another novice here in the gaming hall. Get a real game under your belt. Not just a bib and diaper match where Brahgas lets you win. Oh! Not that that's what happened with you!\n\nOh dear. Just go play a game and let me know how it went.

I wish you could, but since this is my spell, I think it's safer if I'm the only one who messes with it. But I appreciate the thought.\n\nBelieve me, I'm still going to need your help when we get to the ritual site. No idle hands for you!

Maybe? Old tales and myths always start from some truth, at some point in time. The motes around here seem to be affected by more than my spell, is all I'm saying.  \n\nI always expect the worst. I find it helpful.

If luck is with us, maybe just some irritated wildlife we can deal with as we've done before. Or some of the bolder motes.\n\nBut if there is some truth to the ancient tales, then maybe we find some sort of really cranky wind spirit.

We should have a word about decks, I guess. Those decks Razhamad gave you are just the beginning. Fresh decks pop up all over Tamriel, and each of them offers a unique style of play.\n\nYou can even find upgrades to the cards you already own.

I've earned a fair amount from just playing Tribute. Kishka offers them in her daily challenges sometimes, especially if you hit those win streaks!\n\nI've even heard rumors that adventurers find them out in the wild!

Well, between you, me, and old Bendu there, I've heard they might offer some new decks as prizes in the upcoming tournaments. Beyond that? It's a mystery.\n\nJust keep working on raising that rank by playing matches. That's the best path to success!

I'm not sure. I didn't see any of the royals when I waded ashore, and I was the last one from my ship to make it to the beach. The tide turned as I swam in and no one was washed up after me.\n\nI'm afraid you won't find the high king at the Shallows.
There is much to say and not much time to say it in. Here, give me those bones, perhaps he can help answer some of your questions.
What? No! No, it'll work fine, probably! And boy am I excited to see those dirty Fish Elves go up in smoke! I wish the lads were here to see this.\n\nAh well, I'll tell them the story soon enough!

I remember when I was this naive. You probably thought I was just some crazy old man talking to ghosts, well that still very well may be true, but maybe I wasn't as crazy as you suspected. Ready to talk to a ghost?
Whatever the Magus is planning next, it's going to be big. Not even all the kings and queens of Tamriel can stop us now. \n\nYou'll see.

Za'ji lost Queen Ayrenn! And First Mate Caska, too. The wind and the waves must have carried them somewhere else. \n\nThe Lord and the Magus, the Order's leaders—they swore to comb every beach until they found her. And the others too, Za'ji supposes.

It is a fairly simple plan, but all right.\n\nTry to find vulnerable points on the ship. Under the main mast, the captain's quarters, the quarterdeck near the wheel, and so on. Sea Elf ships are very swift, but not so sturdy.

Of course, walker. What else could they have come to these soggy, sopping ruins for? Nothing but rotten wrecks and crumbling masonry as far as the eye can see. Which, Za'ji admits, isn't far under the circumstances.
That is what the old mill's map shows, provided it hasn't been washed away by centuries of storm and tide. No, no, no! Now's not the time for doubt! Let us cross and claim what's mine—ours. Ours!

Everyone will compete, save Kishka and I.\n\nKishka has no interest in tournaments. A bit too much structure for her tastes. And as I may have mentioned, I prefer to observe. That leaves Brahgas, Sorinne, and you—our prize protege!

Not unless you all make it to the finals. Ha! What a blessed result that would be! The chances of such success are slim, however. I would not worry.\n\nFor now, focus on opponents from the opposing chapters. And enjoy yourself!

Who, me? Yeah! I just get … you know, a little anxious before tournament play. Nothing serious.\n\nThere are plenty of different opponents out there. I mean, we could get paired with anyone, right? And there are some chapters we won't see at all!

Yup. It's simple. To advance to the next round of the tournament, we have to battle our way through a series of chapter opponents. Beat them all, and you'll face off against their chief novice. Whoever that is.\n\nJust try to relax. You'll do great.

Yeah. I spent some time in Elsweyr. In my youth. Got into trouble and made a lot of terrible mistakes. In the end, it almost cost me everything.\n\nBut that's hardly game-day conversation. We have a much healthier addiction to feed! Be ready!

This priest of Z'en blessed me when I got his questions right. And then, while I was walking around, I saw a ray of light hit this dirt mound.\n\nSo I did the only thing I could think of. I dug around in the dirt. Guess what? I found treasure!

Oof! An atrocious name. And don't you worry. You'll witness our glorious victory firsthand—through the tearful eyes of a soundly beaten loser!\n\nNow, since you're his stand-in, I assume Razhamad told you the rules?

Just so. You'd face me in Wayrest … in much the same way that a chicken faces a farmer's axe.\n\nI almost wish you could face me. Pity. Our chapter is bound for far better things and you are mere stepping stones. Be seeing you, Gonfalon.

My family owns the mineral rights to a remote site on Amenos. A few months back, I hired a scryer to study its mining potential. She sensed strange stones there that seemed to amplify earth-magic. But the Eldertide Circle was watching us.

Two Eldertide theurges moved in. They claimed the isle's geodes rightly belonged to druids, and started reshaping the land with their magic to bring them up.\n\nThey drove off my people. And they've killed anyone trespassing on the site since.

If I must. As you can see from the tournament lists posted by the hall there, you must defeat my pupils—Fabermund in Daggerfall, and Cecile in Shornhelm.\n\nIf, by some miracle, you managed to defeat them—and it would be a miracle—well ….

That's true. The ground rumbled when he summoned a storm at the castle. And the volcanic vents became active after he conjured the storm that wrecked the alliance ships.\n\nThere was no storm this time, though.
Here, take it! Just don't hurt me!

He has good timing too. My coin purse is nearly empty. And there's a whole festival to enjoy!\n\nIf you don't know much about Z'en, best study up before you find the priest. I'd like you to share in my good fortune.

You mean this treasure is yours? Oh. Well, then here you go. \n\nThe Provider of Our Ease does like seeing lost items returned to their rightful owners. Maybe my role in all this was to make sure that happened. Hopefully, this pleases Z'en.

Anything that points us to the Order's upcoming meeting. If the Ascendant Magus sent out a summons, someone here should know about it. \n\nAnd keep watch for anything else of importance. You never know what clue will be the one to solve the mystery.

Absolutely nothing, dear. But Mount Firesong hasn't erupted in centuries. The druids maintain its slumber. Let's hope they can keep it calm until we stop the Magus from drawing more power.\n\nIn the meantime, let's look inside Mistmouth Cave, shall we?
Ooh, so stoic. It's the stoic ones who always weep the loudest.\n\nLast chance to weasel out of this. No one will think any less of you. It's impossible to think any less of you! Ha!

Yes, indeed! The players of Gonfalon Bay have all officially advanced to intermediate-tier play! Putting that Breton in his place felt good, but things are going to get much tougher from here.\n\nBut now's not the time for fretting. It's time to revel!

It means that after Razhamad approves your promotion, you'll be able to challenge mid-tier Tribute players all across Tamriel! And it also means I can start paying off some of my debts.\n\nYou don't even realize how close I was to disaster.

Just a little predicament I got myself into. I made a few side bets, you see? Big ones. Another month of missed payments and … well, I'd rather not think about it.\n\nAnyway, if we keep this up I'll have nothing to worry about! Now, go see Razhamad!
All roads are made of the same dirt. One is not more generous than another. \n\nMore travelers could lead to more travelers looking past my curved tail. Chewing rocks has more appeal.

She always did. You know, as bad as Nilsmon's poetry was? I … sort of … understood it. She made me feel that way once, too.\n\nAll right. She's a woman grown. If she wants to stay in Rivenspire, I'm not going to drag her home like an unruly child.

According to legend, a necromancer conjured the armor to help her in battle. She died shortly after the spell was complete, leaving the Sable Knight unshackled and uncontrolled. Ever since, it's wandered the land, spreading dark magic.

Well, in that regard, we are two flowers from the same root. \n\nStill, you did not ignore me. I hope your stomach growls quietly and that your feet encounter no stones on this road. Good day, traveler.
Thank you! I will eat well and sleep happily tonight.

Breton nobles? Yes, we heard that as well when the Ascendant Lord and the Magus were speaking in the crypts. That's something to go on.\n\nAnd if the alliance leaders didn't wind up in the Shallows, we'll need to look elsewhere. What else, dear?

Well, that's a lead we can investigate! I'd like to have a chat with Dockmaster Arnauld about that and a great many other things. I detest being lied to, and he did it with such conviction.\n\nYou're still on retainer, dear. Would you care to join me?

The Colossus of Gonfalon Bay is Baron-Admiral Bendu Olo, though most on the mainland would know him as the Colovian King of Anvil. He formed the All Flags Navy around 2260 in the First Era to gain vengeance against the Sload for the Thrassian Plague.
Attack? No! My claws are dull, see! \n\nI've been told that one with scales like mine is threatening travelers near here. That may be why they walk by and do not hear my cries for aid.

I warned them it was dangerous to venture into Wildhorn's vale. Hunters have gone missing in that area before. But my clients had heard about a valley full of game, and they insisted.\n\nWildhorn trapped us like lambs. Closed the path behind us.

Marso went to meet an informant, to gather one final piece of evidence, and some brigands working for Vetitia snapped him up.\n\nThat … witch sent me a letter demanding I leave Rivenspire and abandon the investigation, or Marso would die.

I'm not sure, but I believe her family has some kind of political aspiration. Maybe she's reluctant to kill him outright?\n\nMy hope is, that means Marso is safe … right up until she has no use for him anymore.

Well, um. Neither of us have done this before? So we weren't as subtle about our investigation as we probably should have been.\n\nIt wouldn't have been hard at all for Vetitia to learn who was asking about her family.
Your knowledge of the strange and dangerous locales of Tamriel is truly breathtaking. I know why Isobel likes spending time with you.\n\nWhat happened the last time you were there?
Hmm. Sounds like that rescue attempt didn't go so well. \n\nWell, at least you know the lay of the land. Hopefully that will help you find Marso.

Are you pulling my leg? Look at all we've done together. We dominated the Sapphire Tournament and freed my childhood crush from a stupid promise. \n\nWe recovered a lost signet ring that could have cost my family dearly.

I am one of the guild's foremost experts on fire magic. This research is vital to the further refinement of fire spells of all sorts.\n\nThe reagents have been ensorcelled to gather fundamental information from the molten rock and send it back to me.

Just what you'd expect. Expand the knowledge of the Mages Guild! My research will make fire spells more powerful and of longer duration. Perhaps even help me discover new spells or new applications of existing spells.\n\nThe possibilities are endless!

Oh, there's no time to give you a lesson on the arcane dynamics of living, burning rock. Just know that the vents in the Firepot have a primordial nature that can reveal untold mysteries. My ensorcelled reagents should last long enough for the task.

Lord Bacaro needs to hear about our victory at All Flags. He can stop mustering a counter force, at least for now.\n\nThanks to you, Count Damard's plan to decapitate the alliances has failed. The leaders are safe and back to their usual bickering

Count Damard's defeat cost the Ascendant Order most dearly. It will take time for them to recover—which gives us a chance to salvage the peace talks.\n\nBring the news to Lord Bacaro, then meet me back here at the manor.

Well, I'm not quite sure. I've never been good about keeping a clear account of such things.\n\nAs soon as we're all done, I'll bring the matter up with Lady Arabelle. She must have a record in one of those journals she's constantly writing in.
Ah! That's excellent news! It was dreadful sitting around back at the castle.\n\nEveryone was giving me these pitying looks, and I just can't get into another shouting match with mother.

Isn't that the question of the hour. I thought we'd settled this idea of her arranging something for me years ago. But … well. She cares about me, dearly.\n\nI want to believe this is a combination of her heroic bravado and her affection for me.

There are many aspirants on the island that might release me from my mother's promise … but none in the tourney this year. \n\nBrelannal, Mortens, and Langley all see me as too great a prize to give up.

Langley is as shallow as a tidepool. He just values me for my looks. Brelannal doesn't see a woman when she looks at me, just a big stack of coins.\n\nAnd Mortens, my goodness. That man needs to be handed a partner on a platter.

Had being the operative word. Clearly, her best days are behind her. I cannot fathom her methods. The delegates are lost, so what's the point of distressing the duchess's guests with incessant questions?\n\nBesides, we have the situation well in hand.

I have instructed our house knights to question known malcontents all over the island and offer hefty sums of gold for information. Criminals are quick to turn on their own for a small handout.\n\nThis so-called Ascendant Order can't hide forever.

Magic is the legacy and heritage of the Breton people. Oh, I spent my time mastering the sword and knightly pursuits in my youth. But I believe that a true Breton must study both halves of our nature.\n\nAnd perhaps the ways of the druids, too.

No. Some have forgotten our traditions. Were it not for my talent, I doubt my sister would bother with a court mage. She sends me to look after Dufort interests in ports across Tamriel, rather than making full use of my arcane skills.\n\nA pity.

My friends are all around us right now, even if you can't see them. And, while I may be nice and calm right now, I can assure you that they are not. \n\nThey like to take what they want. But me? I ask politely. And then not so politely.

I just want to help. My friends won't attack you if you bear my mark of protection. Unfortunately, Zenithar only blesses an exchange of coin. So purchase one of my marks of protection and I guarantee my friends will leave you alone. How's that sound?
Well, you might. Let me see. \n\nYes, exactly as I thought. I don't have to give you a new mark entirely, which is good. That would've cost you extra. But this thing here is running out of time.
It's been so nice doing business with you. Enjoy your time at the festival!
Suit yourself. But don't say I didn't warn you.
Guildmates? You mean they're with you? Oh. I suppose they might be able to fight off my friends. How about this? Let's go our separate ways? Yeah, that's what we'll do.
Hmmm. I don't think you will. But, I'd love to see you try.
Those well armed warriors are with you? Well they, uh, they look quite capable. Tell you what? Take some of these coins and we'll call it even. No hard feelings.

I suppose you would call it our doctrine, our religion. The True Way represents a life guided by natural principles and the value and willfulness of nature. All of nature comes from Y'ffre, and the druids are the arbiters of Y'ffre's will.

I'm not sure anyone has ever convinced Archdruid Agathie of anything. But she couldn't deny that something strange was happening in the grove. She ordered me to look into it and bring my findings back to the circle elders.

The druids of this grove belong to the Stonelore Circle. We revere nature, but believe that all cultures have a place here. Some of the High Isle folk refer to us as the friendly druids. We rarely evangelize, letting our work speak for itself.

You'll probably encounter the Eldertide Circle in your wanderings. Be careful. They are overtly hostile to the civilized residents of High Isle. As for the Firesong Circle, even I don't know much about them. They never leave the island of Y'ffelon.

Have you never heard of Y'ffre where you come from? The Storyteller? The God of Song and Forest? The Spirit of the Now?\n\nY'ffre formed the frame upon which nature was woven. He gave rise to the rules of life on Nirn. His way is the True Way.

I am a druid of the Stonelore Circle. I am a teacher, a healer, a counselor—as well as a steward of the natural world.\n\nI hear the voice of Y'ffre and his Earthbones, and I do my best to be his advocate. Natural principles guide my every action.

Things so clever that Za'ji thinks this master shipbuilder must have been a Khajiit! For instance, this one, a hull cladding to make the vessel sturdier than a boulder, but still swift as a gale!\n\nThough Za'ji sees his journey is not finished here.

Just so, walker! Though they are only made reference to. Za'ji did not see designs regarding them directly. He imagines the Sea Elves kept them together.\n\nThey do seem to be tied to navigation, though he doubts a simple compass is involved.

Za'ji can sniff out a scheme when he smells one. These Dreadsails and their lodestones are up to something, and something is always sinister when it comes to Sea Elves. It would be better for such things to stay in Za'ji's care, wouldn't you agree?

Za'ji will need to find shipwrights of some skill to put these plans to use, and the materials from which to build them. The All Flags Navy took many a fortune to create!\n\nThis will be a costly affair, but Za'ji's Perfect Pounce is worth every drake!

My family ruled the archipelago for generations, but the Duforts were never happy in our shadow. They spent years poisoning the court against us. And when my Uncle Avrippe quietly supported King Ranser a few years back, it paid off for them.

The High King stripped my uncle of the ducal title and gave it to the Duforts. It was an outrage, really. We took no part in Ranser's War.\n\nAt least the Duforts didn't get everything they wanted. We kept most of our holdings, and it eats at them.

What gave it away? The fact that no one gets off this rock or that the Serpents have friends in high places? Or maybe how ridiculous it is to imagine nobles lost in the jungle.\n\nI'll tell you what I told Rassa. Going into the jungle is crazy.

Good, good. Those poor souls have been unattended for far too long. Terrible shame what happened to them and their order.\n\nI'm too old to brave that damned keep, but it warms my heart to know that someone has taken up my cause.

When my brother fixed his mind on a goal, he did not allow anything—or anyone—to get in his way. We were never close, but our relationship only worsened after I accepted our father's title.\n\nAnd now he's left our house on the brink of ruin.

I'm no diplomat. Up to now, it's been my task to support Lord Bacaro and Lady Arabelle with my magic. I understood what they needed and how to craft it for them. But I know nothing about negotiating.\n\nI don't understand why the Guild sent me.

What? No, no, no … nope. I'm good here. I tried to introduce myself to High King Emeric when the commander spoke to him, and I … kind of forgot my own name.\n\nSo. If I try that again I think I'll die of shame.

The alliance leaders, right. I keep meaning to try to find Queen Ayrenn, but every time I get started, more of those prison mongrels rush out of the jungle and attack me.\n\nI love a good fight as much as the next sailor, but I'm exhausted!

Sort of? My music is the spell. Once, as a child, I sang a little ditty and turned the cooking fire green!\n\nOne of my more eccentric tutors liked to babble about tonal architecture, but even he didn't understand it. I'm sure my songs are easier.

Chizbari, Sidura and the rest stayed behind in Senchal. Because of the secrecy, they gave us royal agents to crew the Pounce.\n\nI'm not sure there are any other survivors to find. I didn't see anyone else make it to shore.

They control the whole island. \n\nFather says the aristocrats on the other islands don't know anything about Amenos. But there are lots of House Mornard representatives at Amenos Station. Mother reports to them once a season.
Hah, thank you! Take the credit you're due. You kept me focused, gave me a sounding board. And most importantly, I knew whatever happened, I wasn't alone. \n\nI can't tell you what that meant to me.

I still can't get used to it. Dame Isobel Veloise. I dreamed about wearing shining armor, riding a valiant steed. So far it's been crypts, creatures, and a lot of running around.\n\nHah! I've loved every moment. Except maybe the poetry part.

Just the skulls will do. With those, the priests can perform their rites and we can lay them to rest.\n\nAs for the keep, rumors persist that all manner of undead haunt the place. No one knows what happened there, but the order never recovered.

Every knight deserves a proper burial. When I learned that their remains were still trapped inside that old keep, I decided to do what I could. I'm too old to deal with whatever horrors stalk those ruins, but I have gold. That counts for something.

The ground shook and a terrible storm struck with no warning. It was the same magic I sensed at the druid circle. Then warships full of Ascendant Order knights appeared and began to land their forces. They'd used the storm to conceal their approach.

Omdil? What in the name of Count Mornard's big toe do you want with him?\n\nNo. Never mind. None of my business. But if you're looking for Jailer Omdil you can probably find him at the rear gate. He loves that post.

I urged them to withdraw to Memorial Hall, but they did not want to abandon the fight. High King Emeric and Prince Irnskar went to defend the walls, while Queen Ayrenn took charge here.\n\nBut our foes were already inside the castle.
The ground shook again just moments ago. Fiery monsters broke through the floor of the museum. Queen Ayrenn ran downstairs to confront them. \n\nShe left me here to defend the door.
Omdil? That drunkard! If he isn't under a table somewhere sleeping off last night's wine, you can probably find him at the rear gate. He volunteers for that particular station every chance he gets.

By myself? No, I was waiting for you.\n\nI wouldn't have even noticed the entrance if I wasn't looking for it. Probably why the Ascendant Order chose it. That's the thing about islands and ships—you can always find the rats.
Not alone you won't. For all we know, the whole damned Order is meeting inside!\n\nWith any luck, I'll get a chance to pound the bastards that wrecked the Spearhead. Let's go.

A review of the evidence. Excellent idea! Lord Bacaro is sponsoring peace talks here on High Isle, but the ships carrying High King Emeric, Queen Ayrenn, and Prince Irnskar never arrived.\n\nWe suspect the Ascendant Order is somehow responsible.

Precisely! Since we also know that the Ascendant Order is still looking for the missing royals, we'll use them to point us in the right direction.\n\nInvestigate the three sites on the map and learn everything you can, my dear. Leave no stone unturned!

Never heard about my time with the Sea Elf pirates? They taught me some weather magic.\n\nCould you get what I need for the ritual? A claw from a volcanic beast, a feather, and the bones of a drowned sailor. Sadly, these beaches are thick with those.

Find Irnskar. Then look for Emeric. He said something about dealing with the storm.\n\nWe will gather at Memorial Hall, but understand this. I have no intention of hiding behind wards while others die to protect me. This queen fights her own battles!

They say these are the times that try a mer's soul, but I want to believe I've risen to the occasion. Our first adventure together feels like a lifetime ago, though, doesn't it?\n\nIf I'm to be stuck on a jungle island with anyone, I'm glad it's you.

I was as well! That business was ghastly, and I thank you for your help.\n\nMeanwhile, I was stuck in yet another interminable meeting at Elden Root. I can assure you, Daedric Princes or no, you were having more fun than I was.

I swear, that Eye of mine. He gets friskier and friskier with each passing day. \n\nOur last conversation was not about matters of state, or threats to my security, but about the meritorious backside of a Grahtwood emissary. Riveting!

Ha, what have you heard? I adventured for a time, but the tales of my exploits have been greatly exaggerated. Except the story about the bear. Or the kite. Or the trolls. \n\nI miss adventuring. That's where I met Caska. In Elsweyr during my travels.

When my father died, I took up his throne. It was a … difficult transition.\n\nBut I believe my experience has prepared me, honed me, to be the ruler the Dominion needs. The ruler Tamriel needs, if I may be so bold.

I'm sorry. You met Alwinarwe at a very difficult time. She's actually a lovely person, and she has a brilliant mind. \n\nI desperately wish I could have been there to lend my aid. And my sword arm. I don't get to unsheathe my sword nearly enough.

I sent him on ahead to prepare the way, but who knows where that cat has gotten to. I promised there would be no trouble. That all the secrecy and careful planning would make the voyage uneventful.\n\nStars above, I'll never hear the end of it now.

Well, the staff is obviously connected to Breton magecraft. Definitely not the implement of a druid. \n\nA cracked staff is a bad sign. Whatever they were trying to do here, they probably didn't get the result they were hoping for.

I've used such stones before. They help focus magicka over a distance. They come in pairs, you see, forming a sympathetic link between two points.\n\nSo this spell, whatever it was, was aimed at a point outside this circle.

Not with certainty, but I can make an educated guess.\n\nIf the Ascendant Magus used this site to summon the storm that wrecked the alliance ships, then obviously he lost control. The result wasn't what he expected and now the Order is scrambling.

I sent Tsuzo and Za'ji to search along the northern shores for signs of their wrecked ships or the alliance leaders. Tsuzo's message was short but direct: He found something and needed help. \n\nYou're the first to return, so you get the job.
Well, sounds like we were right, for all the good it does us. A noble is backing the Ascendant Order. It's got to be someone from House Mornard or House Dufort, right? \n\nThe question is—who?
You go on ahead. I want to make sure we didn't miss anything.\n\nOh, wait. When you saw Valessea did she … say anything about me? You know what, tell me later. I'll see you back at the manor.
Now that's information we can use. Though, if the leaders did end up on Amenos ….\n\nI'm going to go ahead and pre-emptively call not it? Royals or no, that place is a death trap.
She said what now? Rotmeth? Hemgruuf smells bad, but not that bad!\n\nTime to deliver the ouchy-ouchies! Out of my way, friend!
Don't know him. Someone came through here in a hurry, though.\n\nThought about killing him too. Quick-like, dagger in the back. Didn't. Someday maybe.
Probably. Ask Aydrah. I have … other things to think about.

Very well, thanks for asking. It feels like forever and a day since you acted with my authority on the Covenant's behalf, doesn't it?\n\nI must say, shipwrecked or not, it's a pleasure to have you by my side again!

I can give a firsthand report. The first symptom is the nightmares. I'm familiar with dreams of war, but these were somehow more horrible.\n\nI remember eyes around me, peering from darkness. And screaming. Constant screaming.

Absolutely. Tamriel is changing and her leaders must adapt. The situation in Cyrodiil right now, I can't see a way forward.\n\nPerhaps these talks represent a solution. I'm always in favor of people sitting down to have an earnest conversation.

Of course. I'm not an archmage, but I know my way around a spell or two. They must have had agents aboard as well, because I sensed a pulse of magicka before the storm hit.\n\nWhatever it was, the bastards rendered every enchanted item we had useless.
I did. The reports were terrible. After everything that's happened, you'd think one more Daedric Prince trying to take over the world wouldn't shock me. \n\nAnd yet ….

Well, we've had him by the palace a few times. He brings along a barrel of Kurog's favorite ale and we toast the memory of dead warriors.\n\nStrong alliances have been forged on less than that, don't you know?

Kurog. He was … complicated. Quite literally saved my life, you know. \n\nYour role in his death and Bazrag's rise to power. All very understandable, given the situation. But I'd be lying if I said it wasn't a somber day when I heard the news.
It's not as if the Longhouse Emperors were known for their temperance. But yes, it's disgusting.\n\nIncredibly impressive, your actions in Blackwood.

Not for me. I have heard that Irnskar is something of a royal pain in the arse, but aren't we all to some extent?\n\nPerhaps Jorunn is using this as a training exercise. If Irnskar doesn't make matters worse, maybe he'll learn something.

I have! I would have said anyone was better than that terrible Tharn woman, but Khamira is a stars-blessed delight. She's so brave. The idea of the two of you facing down Dragons!\n\nThat's another battle I could only read about in an Eye's report.

I think so as well. Core to the Dominion is self-governance and respect for every culture.\n\nBut if we can see a unified Anequina and Pellitine, if the Khajiiti people can rally behind a single voice, it would certainly make my life easier.

Don't you see? The Ascendant Order altered the medallions. They wanted us to recover them. And now Jakarn and Lady Arabelle are on their way to deliver them. They must be stopped before the other medallions are activated and the delegates are killed!

Actually, I have a question for you. The head of my intelligence ring, Copper Dariah? She's an ogrim! Scares me half to death, but she's terribly effective.\n\nShe mentioned your name in connection to the Thieves Guild, of all things. Care to explain?

Ha! Good answer. I'll let you in on a little secret the other alliance leaders won't tell you. Commerce in Tamriel won't work without outlaws.\n\nWhy else do you think we let them place those ostentatious little hidey holes and refuges everywhere?

One is clearly the Dufort Shipyards, where the house constructs new vessels. Another is near Stonelore Grove, home to a circle of friendly druids. The third appears to be a cave near Tor Draioch.\n\nHmm. A strange set of disparate locations indeed.

I'll leave that to you. Investigate all three and report back here.\n\nI'll send Jakarn to the docks, Captain Kaleen to the cave, and Valessea to the grove. Rendezvous with them at each location and see what you can uncover about our rogue knights.

Here, I'll mark your map. It was just north of here. I wonder how excited you'll be when the Eagle and the Lion are back together again. We tend to argue. A lot.\n\nI'll catch up after I prepare the items you brought me for the ritual.
Perhaps. I also understand that Amenos has protections in place to discourage scrying and portal spells. \n\nBetween the two, it's no wonder the Mages Guild couldn't trace our medallions.

Over my strenuous objections, honestly. I was Earl of Cumberland before King Gardner died. He dropped dead of the Knahaten Flu and suddenly I was crowned King of Wayrest.\n\nHaven't had a decent night's sleep since.

Being the eldest son of a noble house, I was trained to lead, though not necessarily to be a king. \n\nMy father sent me to the best teachers. I particularly remember studying under Count Ravenwatch. A brilliant man and still a good friend.

Like the others, I fought for my king—until I caught a spear in the gut. I laid in the mud for hours before an Orc shaman found me. She dragged me back to camp.\n\nI ended up in a Breton infirmary. That's when I got the offer.

A representative of the Society came to my bedside. Told me about a noble plan to foster peace in Tamriel. She described how I'd recover alongside my enemies. I thought it sounded overly optimistic, but who turns down a stay by the ocean?

Oh, I dream of peace, friend. I've seen too many friends killed and too much blood spilled to wish otherwise.\n\nBut I also know that the powerful crave more power. And they don't seem to do much of the fighting or bleeding for it.

The manor belongs to Lord Bacaro Volorus. He formed the Society of the Steadfast to work for an end to the Three Banners War. The Society brings wounded soldiers from all sides here to recover.\n\nThey hope we'll find common ground with our enemies.
That's our hope, now that the alliance leaders are here and safe. They just need a little time to recover from their ordeal.\n\nAnd we need to make sure the Ascendant Order no longer poses a threat.

I guess I'm the guard. Usually the patients mind their manners—or they're in too much pain to cause trouble. But we're all soldiers.\n\nWhen fights break out, I settle them. Which means the other patients don't really open up to me.
Fortunately, no. I'm lucky … though I dread the day when it comes for me.\n\nThe malady doesn't seem to strike the same way twice. That's one of the factors that has confused the healers here.

It must seem strange to you. When I first traveled here, I found their Stonelore Circle's work intriguing. I began to believe that Y'ffre is but a shepherd of Sithis's will. Change adheres to natural laws, after all. Trees fall down, not up, yes?

There are three distinct circles around the Systres Isles. I'm a member of the Stonelore Circle. We are a friendly sort and tend to get along well with the other residents of High Isle. Not so with the Eldertide Circle. They are small, but hostile.

I mentioned you're going to need a group. This is a big job, much too large for just one person. \n\nYou need to get to the vent and do whatever you can to defeat the druids encouraging it to erupt. Any forces they have at play must be destroyed.

They did not turn me away. Acceptance is not the core of my interest, at any rate. I consider myself a druid, but there may be some who disagree. \n\nRegardless, they have allowed me to seek help for the vents on their behalf, so here I am.

I am. Many years ago, I was only a warden working at Amenos Station. House Mornard took note of my work and gave me leave to oversee Brokerock Mine. They treat my family and I well. In return, the mine supplies them with precious ammonites.

Prisoners swing the pickaxes while sentries keep an eye on things and organize work in the tunnels. \n\nDon't be fooled by misplaced compassion. The prisoners deserve their sentences and my mine provides them with protection, food, and pay.

The Hadolid's origins are a mystery and not my concern. Dealing with their infestation is my priority. Nothing holds them at bay. \n\nEnough talk, our tasks require attention. Go. Find my missing supplies.

Unless I catch some foulness from these fetid waters, only my pride has suffered. I would have liked to have batted that Sea Elf around like a frightened jerboa, but I'll settle for seeing him beaten and face down in a puddle.

Time will be the judge of that, but I trust Za'ji to find use for these designs, or profit if nothing else. I'll do my best to keep him going overboard outfitting the Pounce, lest we find ourselves overladen with dubious doodads.

Interesting. Well, he's a good man. If he thinks you can help, then you can stay. But if you start hearing voices or seeing strange things, tell me straight away.\n\nA shame that Mender Roslenn's not here to speak with you. We truly need her.

Eh, someone was going to ask that eventually.\n\nPublicly, Jorunn wants me to step up. The Pact is a sprawling alliance facing threats from all sides. The Skald-King has many responsibilities. This is his way to finally allow me to share his burdens.

Privately? The old goat has someone warming his bed at night and refuses to stray too far from home.\n\nShe's a lovely Riften lass. Brunhilde. My father's never been happier. He was only too eager to let me travel in his stead and represent the Pact.

Hope is for poets, like my father. I am a warrior. One does not shy from battle at the first sign of danger.\n\nEven if nothing is gained from these conversations, Emeric, Ayrenn, and I shall be the ones who decide when to quit the field.
The Ebonheart Pact is as strong as ever, thanks in part to warriors like you.\n\nTell me, are you still having fun? Does your heart still leap at the sight of the Dragon banner?

Haha, good! At first, I had my doubts about this alliance. But fighting alongside the Dark Elves and the Argonians, I have learned we are stronger together.\n\nThis is why the Pact was forged. Why one day our banner will fly across all of Tamriel!

Affliction? A good word for it. I can feel it wearing away at my mind. After days without sleep, my thoughts are cloudy. I'm … I'm a shell of myself.\n\nMender Roslenn's tonics helped some. She knows what she's doing … unlike some here.
Curious about the Prince of Windhelm, are you?\n\nWhat do you want to know? I have nothing to hide.

You don't know the story? How our three disparate peoples came together to repel the Akaviri invaders? \n\nI haven't always thought so, but I believe the Nords, the Dark Elves, and the Argonians are truly stronger together. I've seen it firsthand.

My role? I've been a prince my entire life. My youth was not unlike yours, I imagine. I hunted, I fought, and I learned my lessons. I bathed in the frigid waterfalls that crash from the high peaks and wrestled with wolves for sport.\n\nThe usual.

Hmm, a personal question. My relationship with the Skald-King is complex. He loves the chance to teach lessons, to pass on his tales. \n\nBut he is still disappointed that I can't sing, forever denying him that father-son duet he's always dreamed of.

You mean aside from being half-drowned and captured by a prison gang?\n\nI've fought in many battles, worked at my father's side. And I have started knitting. One of the grans at the castle has been teaching me. Says it's good for my temperament.
Nor I, my friend. Vampires and a mad jarl, now that's the stuff my father loves to sing about!\n\nAnd that Svana is … well. She's a commanding presence. She's changed so much since we were children.

Truly? Apologies for my levity, friend. Ask a Nord warband if they would die for their fellows and you will see a forest of raised fists.\n\nYet another thing my people and the warriors of Black Marsh have in common, I suppose.

I can only imagine. Father introduced me to the Tribunal. When Lord Vivec spoke, it was like the chimes of the universe sounding in my ears. And Sotha Sil … I'm not so sure about that one. Almalexia is all right, though. Intense, but all right.

If you put a blade to my neck and asked me to explain almviss … alsav … the Tribunal … I'd probably go down in a spray of blood. I read in the reports you were there.\n\nSaved a god, stopped a rock from the heavens. Standard fare for you.

Your adventure in … oh! Yes, something about a big sack of amber, right? As brave as the Argonians can be, the Hist makes as much sense to me as a High Elf at Hrothgar.\n\nDid you … stop some kind of threat? Or save someone's life?
What? No! What an impertinent question. You are lucky you are the savior of Western Skyrim. Bah! Fancy Svana, I could never ….\n\nAhem, what were we talking about again?

Master Healer Viralaine only manages the symptoms. He sedates us, or just offers comforting words. But he won't seek out the root cause.\n\nRoslenn studied this affliction. She believes it's a curse of the humors. But she needs more research.

This one believes so. Milagi was beginning to feel strong. He planned to return to his family in Rimmen.\n\nThen at dinner one evening, Milagi could not catch his breath. His heart pounded, his vision darkened. Only Mender Roslenn could calm him.

Mender Roslenn is a master of alchemical remedies. She mixed a powder into Milagi's tea that calmed the storm.\n\nYesterday Roslenn told this one she might have a cure for his sickness. A new potion that looked promising. But she has disappeared.

Why don't we set this aside for now. We both have places to be and time is short. If you want to discuss rumors and innuendos, we can talk later. Perhaps over a meal and an expensive bottle of wine?\n\nFor now, just deliver your medallions, dear.

Hilgrim and I are always experimenting with different flavors and ingredients. Not all of them are successful, of course, but this combination in particular was exceedingly delicious. We stumbled upon something revolutionary, I'm sure of it!

Once Hilgrim gets back on his feet, we'll start making a larger batch that we can eventually sell. Then we'll take our stock to the docks, the taverns, the streets—wherever there might be thirsty rich people looking for something delicious.

The fleshfly wings add a bit of bitterness and body to the drink. The Systres passion flower gives it a lovely floral aftertaste and a lovely color. And that particular type of mushroom infuses a great deal of sweetness and heaviness to the mix.

Ha! Now, that I'm prepared for! I'll be able to plan for it. First, there'll be no more taste testing for Hilgrim—his privileges are officially revoked. Second, I intend to hide our stock in a secure location. Third, I'll kill him if he tries it.
The rift before you leads to the final lock upon my prison. Compared to the wards and guardians you've already defeated, it will be a trivial task, but necessary for my release.

Do you believe anyone should languish as I have? Have I not shown you my gratitude and aided your own plight? Perhaps I was too trusting, to grant you my power before my release.\n\nWill you really turn your back on me when you have everything to gain?

Oh, not that again. You don't realize how tedious that question has become. And all because of a nosy chronicler and her unfounded accusations.\n\nListen, my dear. You and I will get along much better if you never ask me about Investigator Vale again.

I always do, friend, I always do. Now, don't be a stranger. There's no one I'd rather have at my side when danger rears its ugly head. Or in a crowded wagon or a tiny boat. You're not bad as far as company in tight quarters is concerned, either.

It's remarkable. The legend of the Systres Sisters! Famaza, Finimi, and Fera—a trio of pirates who amassed untold treasure from their raids along High Rock's coast.\n\nAccording to the story, they chose Amenos as the site to build their hidden vault.

That's correct, dear. And while you were rescuing Prince Irnskar, you overheard the Ascendant Lord tell the Magus to summon the Order to a meeting on High Isle. We're going to follow up on that and figure out where this meeting will take place.

There's Sorinne. Energetic girl. Used to be caught up in a worse mess than Brahgas. Set her life right, though. Now she's just addicted to playing Tribute. And being cheerful. Hmph.\n\nKishka—that Khajiit in the next room—is another member.

He's a former Tribute champion and the leader of our chapter. He keeps us all out of trouble … as best he can. Without him this place wouldn't exist.\n\nHe's one of the only tuskless people I trust. A good man, through and through.

Yeah, Kishka's our broker. Takes care of the chapter's daily challenges with her brother, Marunji. Damn good Tribute player too, but she never leaves her spot. Too busy being … well, being Kishka. She's one of a kind.\n\nThen there's Razhamad.
I'll find more resonance crystals. Their power and my song will keep me safe. And I'm going to honor my friends, monsters or not!\n\nYou should go back to the camp. Tell father what happened here.
That one mentioned something of lodestones, but they must refer to something more than simple compasses. Perhaps there is something among the designs Za'ji found to make sense of it.

Yes, yes. Of course. I may not be an optimistic fool like Meryline, but I was once a capable warrior in my own right. I can handle a few beef-witted beasts, even in my condition.\n\nMeryline … I won't be able to keep her safe, will I?

Very well. I hope you understand the weight of responsibility you've undertaken. My wife expects Meryline to be here when she returns. If she were to hear—if I had to tell her terrible news …. \n\nDo not fail me, adventurer.
Meryline's little songs actually do that? I thought she could only cast illusions. Well, she still needs someone to watch over her.\n\nI'm trusting you to bring my daughter back to me.

The Stonelore Druids administer to the vents here on High Isle, but the Firesong Circle controls Y'ffelon. Outsiders aren't welcome there, and I've never seen one of their druids.\n\nThey say the Firesongs work to keep the volcano appeased.

After we saved the mine from those Hadolids, father relented and admitted that I was more capable than he thought. \n\nI thought he understood. But, he only agreed to let me help around the mine. He wanted to use my voice to shift rubble and stones.

I argued with him. Of course. I thought I could make him see that I wanted to spend my life on the road. Help people.\n\nBut, he said he'd let me do that if I took one of his sentries with me as a guardian. A guardian? Can you believe him?

I left without one. I love father, but he doesn't get to order me about my whole life. I need to do this, and I need to do it without being coddled!\n\nI started small on my way here. Helping anyone who needed it.

Living the life I dreamed I'd have! I'm helping people. Figuring out how my magic can be used to solve actual problems. \n\nAnd I'm doing it without having to sit in the feast hall conjuring flowers for the noblewomen!

Eventually. But right now there are people who want my help. No, they need it. I won't leave them to their distresses.\n\nI'll go when it's the right time for me, but right now I'm just enjoying being useful!
I can calm the Hadolids with my magic! With the resonance crystals amplifying the song, we can get more of the Hadolids to stop attacking us! \n\nBut, I think I can get them to do something else too.
My plan? I'm going to change the nature of the spell! Make it so the Hadolids aren't just calmer, but they don't want to be in the mine at all. \n\nI'm sure I can convince some of them to leave!

I'm a thaumavocalist, remember? My music casts magic. If I can change my lyrics, I can get the spell to change, too! \n\nWe'd need to place a lot of resonance crystals. I know just the spots! And we'll need to find the entrance the Hadolids use.

Indeed! The Hadolids that reside in Breakwater Cave on the southern coast of the island have a habit of attacking House Dufort supply wagons. They drag crates of supplies into their lair for gods know what purpose.

Everyone respects Mender Roslenn. She's got a rare combination of kindness and skill. And, between you and me, she plays a strong game of cards.\n\nNow that I think about it, I haven't seen her in a while. Where could she be?

You saw that? It's nothing, really. Brahgas just gets a bit of swagger when he hits a hot streak.\n\nHe's been winning a lot recently, so he offered to get me in at the ground floor—tip me off to sure things so I can make a bet and such.

Ha! Perceptive. Listen, your focus should be on the fun of Tribute! I'm not going to drag you through the details of my sordid past. We'd be here all day!\n\nJust get out there and have some fun, all right?

Are you kidding? He hates it! He tries his best to curb Brahgas's antics, but we're getting to the point where he's ready to let that Elf learn his lessons the hard way.\n\nSometimes you have to hit the bottom before you can rise back up to the top.

Hmm. Strange that this affliction shows up at the same time people start disappearing. I don't believe in coincidences.\n\nWhy didn't Viralaine tell me about this? Sure, I'm not a member of the Society, but still …. Anything else?

Then we need to get into the dispensary. That's where Roslenn worked. \n\nHmm … Viralaine has a key. And so does Mender Aldvar. Get the dispensary key from one of them, and go take a look around. I'll keep watch while you're inside.
Try flattery, if you're good with words. If you can impress him with some alchemy, he might trust you. Or maybe mention you're searching for Mender Roslenn. Those two are close.
Well, I've never seen a lazier mender. I bet you can find him asleep on the docks. Now, I'd never suggest you steal the key from his pack. But, if it fell out and you picked it up ….

I guess you could pick the lock. But you didn't hear me suggest that. Supposedly I'm the security here.\n\nThis affliction keeps the menders busy, so I doubt you'll be noticed. Just don't break the door. We can't let patients take what they want.

Precisely. Gods know what sorts of maladies those sea creatures carry. The supplies are ruined, we're sure of it. Better to destroy the crates and deny the Hadolids their contents.\n\nWithout the supplies, maybe the creatures will move on.
Of course. But other matters across High Isle have them occupied right now. Besides, I assumed that an adventurer such as yourself would appreciate the gold we have provided to see this job done.

I offer only two challenges per day, but you can earn sweeter prizes by winning multiple matches. Small rewards for a single win, fine prizes for two, and a grand bounty for three!\n\nKishka will also make sure your rank soars if you participate.

She's the moony Khajiit downstairs. Kishka and her brother create daily challenges for the chapter to keep us sharp. It's great practice and you can win some fine rewards, too!\n\nKeeping her attention's no small feat, but when she focuses, look out!

Are you serious? He didn't trust me. I never got a real name or saw his face. But he's rich, I can tell you that much.\n\nLike, nobility rich. Royal rich. You can smell it on them, you know? All the perfumes and soaps and fancy clothes.

You go on ahead. I want to make sure we didn't miss anything. Oh, wait. When you see Valessea make sure to tell her I say … hey. \n\nActually, you know what? Never mind. I'll see you back at the manor.

Vinsha is a fanatical priestess, driven by visions of the Serpent God of Satakal. When my circle discovered what she was doing to the shy serpents under her control, we confronted her.\n\nBut she turned them against us and drove us away.

Amenos! I suppose it's possible the leaders washed onto that gods-forsaken island.\n\nWhile I determine our best approach to that place, I need you to go to Shipwreck Shoals and aid Captain Tsuzo. I received an urgent message right before you arrived.

Like I said, it's in that hulk at the center of the shoals.\n\nI was picking the bones of that beauty, then the fish elves came snooping around with their swords and bad breath! I had to scramble out of there triple-quick. Lost my pack in the process.

Ah, ah, I said as if encouraged by an outside force! It could be nothing more than the ramblings of an old druid. I just know that this activity is strange … but much of nature is, thanks to Y'ffre and his Earthbones.

It's hard to put into words. Butterflies are fickle creatures naturally, and even more so when distressed. But it at least communicated to me that the disturbance in the natural order happened quite recently. Curious.
Yes, though neither the spirit nor I are able to determine the source. But abundant magicka in any place that it doesn't belong is a problem.\n\nAnother part of the puzzle.

As I suspected, the new activity here is far from natural in origin. That, and we are running out of time to halt imminent disaster. \n\nI think I've learned all I can from the spirits here. Now, it is time for action.

I'm afraid not, and that worries me. You see, Roslenn isn't one to abandon her duties. And some patients have vanished as well. Just gone from their beds when we check on them.\n\nI shouldn't talk about this. People are upset already.

Thank you. I … I need a moment to recover my strength. Viralaine's notes are in the laboratory, if you need help with the antidote.\n\nI'll meet you at Roslenn's side. I haven't fed in a long time, and I shouldn't be alone with her.
She sleeps in the next chamber, but soon she'll awake with my curse.\n\nThere's a vial of my blood in the laboratory across the hall. We can use it to create an antidote. Release me. Please?
Thank you—my mind is a little foggy yet.\n\nWe should head back immediately. I have to check on my patients … and perhaps add Seraphyne to them. I think I can cure her, if that's what she wants.
Such smugness! You may get rid of me, but doing so will spell doom for dozens of those poor souls out there. My methods were unconventional, yes, but they would have worked!

In time I would have perfected it! In time, it would have been safe! Sometimes we have to make hard choices. How can you not understand that?\n\nI'm done talking. Do what you will with me, but I'll be proven right. You'll see.

The regrettable means to a greater end. The vampire will live forever, but those people outside won't. If one suffers so that many more can go on to lead full lives, what of it?\n\nI could have saved hundreds—no, thousands—more!

Excellent! I will add your name to the lists and pay the sponsorship fees so you can focus on the important part—winning!\n\nI admit that our chapter has suffered … a dry season. But Zeht rewards those who endure!

You will play several matches. If you defeat enough of the opposing chapter's players, you may face off against their chief novice. A worthy opponent, to be sure.\n\nNow, gather with the others in the beginner's lounge. The first game draws near!

Me? I'm calm as a slug on Sundas! I don't let these things get to me. Tribute is meant to be fun! My days in Elsweyr taught me that there's far worse things to get upset over. Far, far worse.\n\nJust enjoy yourself! Let Brahgas handle the stress.

Yes! Anyone but the Mournhold Chapter!\n\nNo, uh … no specific reason! It's just… they're really good. That's all. But I wouldn't worry. I doubt they even sponsor a novice-tier team. They're a top-tier operation. Yeah, there's no way it's them.
If he's not in the library writing verse to annoy fair maidens, he's usually toiling away in Commander Jourvel's offices.\n\nWhy, what has he done now?

If anyone will know where the fair flower of Castle Navire currently sits upon her set-upon, it will be Nilsmon. Good luck with that, I suppose. \n\nMeanwhile, I am readying for my first quest as a knight of the Iron Knot.

Despite Dame Isobel's questionable behavior and dubious win during the Sapphire Tourney, the order of the Iron Knot was eager to see me join their ranks.\n\nThey know a true knight and valiant warrior when they see one.
Since I opted to travel with you, I'm considered a Knight-Errant. A wanderer, basically. \n\nJust trying to make the world a better place one act at a time. Like you.
Draigh, no! I never thought my knighthood would be quite like this, true. \n\nBut we've righted so many wrongs together. I wouldn't change my decision for all the treasure in Gonfalon Bay.

That's entirely up to the head of the order. Knights might be assigned to a town, or asked to go on a quest, or even just patrol the isle.\n\nI know it was hard to tell during the tourney, but the orders are meant to serve the community.

Ah, my trusty hammer and chisel! Saved my arse on more than one occasion!\n\nNow let's go find that gem and get to the extraction point before Marcelle. If we hurry, we can still turn the tide on the love of my life.

Not a clue. I'm still in the information-gathering stage of the heist. Legends require a lot of research and study to fully uncover. But one day!\n\nI will need to hide the gem, though. I don't want Marcelle to get too curious when she gets back.

I do. He's one of the good ones, always was. He never treated us like the strays we were—he had a smile and a fresh baked something to give us every morning.\n\nHe wouldn't contact me for a hunch. He's got something real, I know it.

Song was the best of us. She was quiet and kind—our moral compass. Balanced the rest of us out, y'know? She never told us where she came from, but I think it had to be somewhere nice. She had manners and knew how to charm people. Useful, that.

Something like that. She had nice clothes when we found her and just generally acted … different. But she never complained about sleeping on the streets or sharing a moldy heel of bread between four people. She just seemed happy to be with us.

Well, I went out to find us a meal like usual. But when I got back to our base, they were gone. I sat around for a while like an idiot, figuring they were just off doing something.\n\nThen, I noticed signs of a struggle in the dirt.

No idea. Nothing good, I'll tell you that. I asked around for months, trying to find someone who saw anything, heard anything. \n\nWhatever happened to them happened real quiet. Maybe because someone didn't want anyone finding out.

Every so often. If a caravan that hired me passed by, I'd sneak back in and talk to people. But I was always worried that someone might be looking for me. I had no idea who took the others, so my imagination ran a little wild. Mostly, I stayed away.

If Brahgas started acting peculiar, I would have a hundred theories. But Sorinne shines brighter than the sun over the Alik'r. She has no enemies to speak of, so far as I know.\n\nShe did have some trouble in Elsweyr before coming to High Isle, though.

Sorinne rarely speaks about her past. When I try to learn more, she becomes evasive. Nervous. I do not wish to pry, but we all adore her and would try to ease her burdens if given the chance.\n\nI only know that the trouble had to do with skooma.
Were I a betting man, I would say yes. But we cannot help her if we do not know for sure.\n\nFind her. Speak with her. I only hope she speaks more candidly with you than she does with me.

Of course. Draigh, I'm sorry. I bet I came on a little strong. I've spent months preparing for the tourney. \n\nAnd now the commander's pronouncement has set me adrift. I'll be all right. What would you like to know?

No, no. She … she just wants me to be happy. It's expected of noble ladies on High Isle to marry for advantage. Advantage to the ladies, mind.\n\nShe thinks I'm afraid to take that step, and wanted to give me … well, a push.

I'll be better once we find Jhaka. It's just … if I'd gotten back a little faster that day, maybe I could have stopped him and the others from being taken. He's suffered this whole time because I wasn't quick enough. Because I wasn't there.

Thanks for saying that. I don't know if I believe you, but it's nice to hear, anyway.\n\nI'm not helping Jhaka, or any of them, by sitting here whining. It's just something that's been weighing on me, y'know? So thanks for listening. Let's go.

You're right! I'm not doing him any favors by sitting here feeling sorry for myself. I may not have been able to help him then, but I'll be damned if I can't help him now.\n\nThanks for that. Honestly. Now come on, let's go.

This one remembers very clearly an insignia on the mercenaries' armor. It is burned into my mind, but for all these years, I have not been free to investigate it. \n\nNow that I am safe, I will focus on getting well and hunt down that symbol.

I'm not a knight just yet. That's why I'm in the tourney! I was a squire for years before I 'came an aspirant. \n\nYou don't want to know how many stalls I've cleaned. The tourney gives me a chance to prove my worth to the orders, you see.

Nope! The tourney is only called every few years, as schedule and aspirants allow. The commander wants to make sure there are enough people in the mix to make it a challenge. \n\nAnd the orders are only so large on High Isle, as you might imagine.

Hah, sorry. It's a curse I picked up from my dad. A word from the old druid tongue that's been co-opted for common folk. \n\nI sort of grew up here at the castle and it's a little more acceptable than the curses the dockhands use. So I use it.

As an advocate for the Society of the Steadfast, I provide legal counsel to the poor and unfortunate. Currently, I am involved in a long-term effort to improve conditions on the prison island of Amenos.

That's a handsome question. I wish I had an answer for you. I can see ways that I'd be a good fit for either the Oaken Order or the Iron Knot … maybe even the Order of the Albatross!\n\nThat's a problem for day's end Isobel to face. Heh.

I'm not sure how tamsfolk tourneys work, but here each order sets a challenge. Attempting the challenge for an order marks you in good standing, and each order only chooses one or two aspirants for knighthood.\n\nIt's fairly competitive, as a result.

Because many of the prisoners I was helping have disappeared and the jailers have no record of what happened. My sources tell me they were sent to Whalefall to die.\n\nDetermine the truth of this and bring back anything to identify the prisoners.

Look for the prisoners. Hopefully they are alive, but if you find their remains, they should be carrying documents that identify them, list their crimes, and detail their sentences.\n\nBring those documents to Wayllod and he will return them to me.

You're going after them? I hope you're prepared. The Executioner and Harrower imprisoned me and my friends when we refused to join them. I … I hope my friends are still alive. Although they might not be the same after what's been done to them.

Sorinne? She's been a little sullen the last couple of days. Something about a letter, I think? I saw her head upstairs earlier. Couldn't tell you if she's still up there or not.\n\nIs something wrong?

Maybe? What's that supposed to mean? She's going to play, right? Right?\n\nZ'en's price, she's not going to play, is she? Damn it! She's worked so hard. We all have! Did someone threaten her? Just give me a name! Let me at them!

Think Brahgas think! She might have been … yeah, she was definitely talking to some Khajiit lady. It wasn't that long ago. The cat's probably still here in the Gaming Hall.\n\nJust hurry. We've got some time before our opponents arrive, but not much!

We were passing through Shadowfen and ran afoul of some vampires. Our leader bargained for peaceful passage and gave her to them as payment. Not far from the Shrine of the Black Maw.\n\nWasn't my choice, but I went along with it.

That Silverslip is dead, or turned into a vampire, or ran away and ended up somewhere worse … I can't stop thinking about it. Seeing what Jhaka went through after the mercenaries picked him up was bad enough. Now this?\n\nI feel like a failure.

You know, when you say it like that, I really believe you. I feel like when I've got you at my side, all of this doesn't seem so impossible. We found Jhaka together, didn't we? We'll find the others too.\n\nNow, enough mushy stuff. Let's get a move on.

Damned fish biscuits … I hope you're right. I mean, knowing Silverslip, I wouldn't be surprised if she took on an entire vampire coven by herself and is now sitting at the Black Maw shrine like a queen. \n\nWe'll just have to pray that's the case.

My life hasn't been rosy by any means, but at least I wasn't enslaved or taken captive by vampires! It hurts to know my friends suffered and that I didn't do anything to stop it. \n\nAnd I still don't even know why they were taken in the first place.
Sorinne? Yes, Sorinne is an old friend of Raenobi's! This one was just catching up with her, yes? We have not seen each other for a long, long time.\n\nThis one missed her dearly.
