A gift, walker. Just a small reminder of where she came from and what she left behind. This one hopes she found a quiet corner where she could enjoy it. It always did help her game.\n\nNow, if there isn't anything else? Good luck in the tournament.

Well, Raenobi heard her old friend made it to the second round of the Tribute tournament! A proud moment for this one, truly. Raenobi introduced Sorinne to the game, you see? \n\nSo, this one just came to wish her luck and give her a tiny sweet, yes?

Nothing to worry about, I've felt worse after a bad storm out at sea. My first mate will recover as well, though he'll need to take it easy for a few days. \n\nI cannot thank you enough for finding Aurelia so quickly.

So, now I'm dragging Razhamad into this too? Mara's mercy.\n\nI got a letter from an old friend. She and I were very close, but … I hated the person I was around her. I had to leave Elsweyr—to leave her. And now, suddenly, she's back in my life.

Indeed, a letter supposedly from Song's heartbroken mother. I read it because I'm an idiot, but I remember a drawing on the parchment. A strange eye. It must have been magic, a glyph maybe? I'm almost certain it's how they tracked us down.

Because I was stupid, all right? I was a dumb, naive kid who thought she knew the world better than everyone else. I never thought it was that big of a deal. I just wanted to help Song, and I didn't think I needed anyone's help. Lot of good that did.

I will. Aurelia has a caring heart. She was so ashamed after that day on Stros M'Kai. She acted the fool, even if she's too proud to say as much.\n\nShe is bound and determined to right the wrong she created, and I am honored to help.

Noticed that, did you? That's a keen eye you have. \n\nBut yes, I am. It wasn't exactly my choice, but I've learned to accept it. I have people that look out for me now, almost like the old days. It's not unbearable or anything.

I never stopped wanting it. Even now, talking to you, knowing what I know about what this does to people, I still want a taste.\n\nI just need a moment to think. Thanks for checking on me. Can't say for sure, but I think you just saved my life.

The usual. Little stories. Inside jokes. They tore down our favorite tavern, apparently. Our favorite from back when I was using, I mean.\n\nIt just … it all came flooding back. Everything I tried to escape. It's like I'm right back where I started.

Maybe not, but I should have been smarter.\n\nI just wanted Song to have a family who loved her. I wanted a family, a real one, my whole life, and there was one practically begging her to come back. I thought I was doing the right thing.

That depends if she is a willing participant in their schemes. However, the information we've been able to glean thus far makes that seem unlikely. If she's not a willing participant, the king will protect her. You have my word on that.

Then I should hope we could talk in a civilized manner until both parties are satisfied. But all that is moot if we cannot find the woman. \n\nYour friends Jhaka and Silverslip were not equipped to do so. You, however, are of a different breed.

I don't know much else, only that he has a sort of animalistic presence. Nothing obvious, but hunters recognize the way he stalks through the markets. \n\nDon't underestimate him. Zenithar smiles on those whose work is well-reasoned.

Oh, is that what you've come to me for? I suspect it might be possible to extract a potent stimulant from Hadolid tissues, but the brine glands are usually irretrievable.\n\nWhen their shells are soft, however, the glands can be harvested intact.

Most are willing participants, but Song is forced to commune with the relic. The visions drain the life force of the vessel no matter what, but those who resist suffer greatly. \n\nThe family profits off her agony and keeps her prisoner to ensure it.

Raenobi has her claws in many sugar jars. Can a businesswoman not enjoy herself from time to time?\n\nAnd business can be pleasure also, yes? Many Tribute players want what Raenobi sells. Skooma makes us sharper. Sleeker. You should try it someday.

Sabotage? Do you think this game means so much to Raenobi? No, walker. This one misses her friend. Sorinne is wasted in this dungy place. She belongs with Raenobi. She only needs reminding, yes?\n\nBut ziss'vo! So serious. We have a game to play, yes?

Of course! Though, it will be difficult with only you and your little acorn-Elf, yes?\n\nLentondil will face you at Skywatch Market in Auridon. Then Malilen in the city of Marbruk in Greenshade. This one lounges in Elden Root. See you soon, sweetmeat!

No. You ensured the terrible legacy of the Emerald Eye will fizzle out. Without their precious relic, my family has no need of me.\n\nI am free to pursue my own life and reunite with my friends. I am sure there is much for us to talk about.

I knew you were special when I met you at Tor Draioch, but I never could have guessed you'd be the one to help me stitch the pieces of my past back together. \n\nYou've reunited me with my friends and become someone I trust—no small thing. Thank you.
Well, in my defense, I didn't know it was owned by the Duforts when we played there as kids.\n\nWe also didn't go looking for knightly relics! Which, now I wish we had.

We've been having issues with lava fissures recently. They appear in various places, spew molten rock and strange creatures, and create a danger for the area.\n\nDruid Peeska can tell you more. I recommend you form a group to deal with these threats.

Without the relic, my family will struggle and scrounge to maintain their power. Over time, their wealth will dwindle and they will be lost, I'm sure. \n\nWith my father gone, there is no one to lead the Emerald Eye. I imagine it will dissolve in time.

My father feared as much. But now that the Emerald Eye's source of power is gone, I doubt the king will maintain his interest in my family. As for me, I will speak to him myself if he seeks me out and assure him that the Emerald Eye is no more.

I … do not know. Freedom was just a forgotten dream to me before this moment. Now, there are possibilities. And thanks to you, I have my friends here to help. Maybe it's silly, but what I want most is to just be near them. I don't care where we go.

Uhh, must think again … no. We parted ways with great enthusiasm in street just outside Ancient Anchor. I went back inside and I had it with me then.\n\nI need my scepter of office. I can't lose another one, or they'll dock my pay.

I was sent weeks ago to party in advance. No, that is not quite right. To be part of advance party. When diplomats meet for talks, their helpers usually gather ahead of time to begin making friends. And drink. \n\nI am good at that!

Feh! Raenobi learned from the best. While you supped from boozy Razhamad's baby bottle, this one sat at the paws of true masters. You have no chance, walker. None.\n\nBut, you are right. Why speak when you can show, yes? Shuffle your deck, walker!

Really? I suppose the king was bound to investigate the Emerald Eye's activities at some point. I'm grateful for his offer. I don't think it's necessary, but perhaps I could still speak with him about routing out the last bits of the organization.

Yeah, actually. I am. After our talk earlier, I know I can do this.\n\nI spent so many years being the woman Raenobi thought I was—I never thought about the woman I wanted to be. I see that woman now, thanks to you.

Oh, luck will have nothing to do with it, my friend. This is a thrashing that's a been a decade in the making.\n\nNow, you go on. Get back to the gaming hall and enjoy your victory! I'll join you directly.

My ancestor was real enough, and if her treasure's here it might be my means to a ship of my own. I don't know about you, but I won't be finding my fortune working as a deck hand the rest of my life. Nothing ventured, nothing gained.

After our adventure in the Deadlands, I wanted to enjoy myself. So, I stopped paying too much attention to anyone religious or in robes. \n\nAs much fun as throwing parties in your honor—or being praised myself—was, it's nice to just have fun!

Nothing that bad. We were sitting at a table with my parents, eating the food I grew up on. Calia tried not to look sick when I explained what was in each dish. It was a good dream!\n\nWherever those two are, I think they're having a good time.

Oh, I haven't faced anything like Mehrunes Dagon or the Incarnates, but my curiosity got me in more than a few dangerous situations since the last time I saw you. \n\nSpeaking of which, I dreamed about Calia and the Anchorite recently.

They wanted to explore a new world and I bet they're having a great time of it too!\n\nIt's time I did the same. This festival only happens once a year, I'm not going to leave until I figure out what a horker pie is.
Yes, yes! I mean, we sort of put her in the carriage, because she couldn't stand by then. And we told the driver where to take her, because she wouldn't stop singing.\n\nBut that is about right.

I did not really keep count. Four tankards? Five? Everybody knows that Wood Elves love rotmeth—\n\nOh. <<1>> is a High Elf, isn't she? I might have forgot differences between Elves. But I am sure she will be fine!

I speak of the compassion you showed for Sorinne.\n\nNo matter the outcome of her match with Raenobi, she cast off a pair of heavy shackles today. There will be other difficult days, but with your help, she's better prepared to weather them.

Only they could say for certain, but I'd wager so. One might find an oddity or two washed up on the shores in their lifetime that may have belonged to the deep druids. Sea Haven Bay was festooned with them … before we plundered it.

They left things behind. Things bought and sold as curios or dabbled with by fools like the Commodore who damned us all to this damp tomb.\n\nTheir idols and objects of worship were plentiful around Sea Haven Bay, before we claimed it for ourselves.
If it's treasure that brought you here, I have my share to give. But I paid dearly for it, as you can see, so I won't part with it so easily.\n\nBreak this curse on my soul and you'll get your due.
Ilyes knows where I kept what I claimed for my own. If he wavers giving you a fair share, just tell him I'll haunt him until the debt is paid.

Nothing. I haven't gone back yet. Until I determine if the corruption can be cleansed and find the source, I don't actually have anything new to report.\n\nWell, except that now the corruption has spread to some of my fellow druids.

Of course. The three alliances have been sending supply ships to High Isle for weeks now. All in anticipation of some unrevealed business.\n\nAnyway, they hired the Fighters Guild to serve as an agent for all of them, and the hall steward assigned me.

The waters between High Isle and Amenos are particularly treacherous. Ships run aground or get smashed by storms on a regular basis. These ships, however, were carrying uniforms for the three alliances.\n\nIf those fall into the wrong hands ….

Because we know the Dreadsail pirates use the place as a port of call. Get in there, find the crates, and burn them to ash.\n\nImagine the kind of havoc those Sea Elves could cause if they can disguise themselves as alliance sailors and soldiers.

Oh, yes! I am good diplomat, so I thought she would like something to remind her of home. After that, <<1>> kept asking for more drinks. We all laughed and had fun!\n\nWe said goodnight just outside. She got in her carriage and drove off for home.

Oh, that was early in the First Era. After struggling against the Direnni Hegemony, our ancestors came to this archipelago because of its connection to Y'ffre. When they arrived, our druidic circle deemed Stonelore Grove to be a sacred site.
Yes, yes! I mean, we sort of put her in the carriage, because she couldn't stand by then. And we told the driver where to take her, because she wouldn't stop singing.\n\nBut that is about right.

We might have been arguing about where to get the best cake in Wrothgar. That made us want cake. But the man in the back room said he did not have any cake.\n\nSo I asked him to give me whatever he had. For <<1>>!

We might have been arguing about where to get the best cake in Wrothgar. That made us want cake. But the man in the back room said he did not have any cake.\n\nSo I asked him to give me whatever he had. For <<1>>!

I don't know. But it must have been very special. He told me not to let anyone else open the bag except my friend.\n\nI hoped <<1>> would look inside so I could see the surprise. But he just said he'd take it home and eat it later.

That name is familiar … yes! That was it. I thought he worked for the inn, so I asked him for something for my friend. Dessert seemed very expensive!\n\nWhen I asked him what else we owed him for dinner, he said he was good. So we left.

I don't know. But it must have been very special. He told me not to let anyone else open the bag except my friend.\n\nI hoped <<1>> would look inside so I could see the surprise. But he just said he'd take it home and eat it later.

Yes, I'm Lady Laurent. And enough with the sweet nothings.\n\nYou! Talk to Janne and see if you can determine how this curse started. Maybe then we can figure out how to end it. I'm having my own problems, as you can plainly see.
I … I hesitate to say. If I tell you, do you swear on your honor that you will share this with no one? Particularly not Isobel or Aurelia?
Now that I'm no longer looking at a bleak future as some dreary knight's bride?\n\nI haven't quite decided yet. With Isobel leaving High Isle, I think perhaps it's time I did the same myself.

When Aurelia was very young, her father passed away. She barely remembers him, dear man that he was. \n\nI spoke to a druid, an old woman in the woods, and asked for her blessing so that Aurelia would have a good, easy life.

The witch in the wood made me promise that Aurelia would win favor as a knight, or win a knight's favor, by the time she reached my age. \n\nAs you can tell, Aurelia is hardly knightly material. And that deadline is quickly approaching.

I did. And thank the Divines, she won the favor of a knight. I saw the witch at Isobel's knighting ceremony, and she gave me a sly wink. Our bargain is met. And my daughter is safe. \n\nThanks to you, second. And Dame Veloise.

Well, Isobel keeps encouraging me to pick up a trade or a hobby to get me out of my chambers here at the castle.\n\nI've never quite considered what that might be … but now the whole world seems full of promise. Who knows what tomorrow will bring?

The island's volcanic vents create all sorts of underground spaces. The large cavern beneath us is the Undergrove. No one's allowed down there. Not without the archdruid's permission.\n\nThe wards have something to do with the spirit of the grove.

Await word from Lord Bacaro, I imagine. I came all this way and endured much. It would be a shame to just walk away now. \n\nI must send word back to my court. Assure them that I am alive and well. After that … we shall see.

Adusa-daro took on almost all of Verandis's duties—I don't envy her for that. Fennorian and I do as much as we can. \n\nFennorian's had the hardest time of it. He still volunteers to investigate every rumor of evil that reaches us.

As a whole, they don't take issue with the members of House Ravenwatch. Individually? Who can say. \n\nIt'll take me all festival to find enough gifts. Let's make a habit of these outdoor meetings, they smell better than the alternative.

We didn't think there would be an issue with my presence. But, it's better to stay safe. \n\nOne vampire could raise their suspicions, but two or more? If they were the torch wielding type, that'd be the end of the festival. No gifts for anyone then.
For now. Provided Emeric and Jorunn's cub agree to remain. We were able to put aside our differences and deal with the Ascendant Magus. Perhaps that indicates a measure of hope for peace, after all.

I'm not quite certain. Lord Bacaro's plans are in disarray. We were stranded on Amenos and assaulted in his supposedly secure facility. Makes one wonder if all this talk of peace is actually worth the effort.

Ending a war is a complicated business. If the others agree to remain, I don't see how I can get out of it.\n\nIf nothing else, this little adventure has proven that we can work together when the need arises. And it was a memorable battle, truly!

Next? What makes you think I know? My father's instructions didn't cover anything like this.\n\nI'm just happy to still be alive, and not dead on the battlements or roasting in the belly of a lava-beast.

We just escaped death and you're asking me about politics? I suppose I should get used to it, but not without a great deal of mead. I think I understand why the Skald-King drinks so much now.\n\nIf the other leaders agree, I will stay to talk.

They might, but I've never been good at listening to what the Mehras say. I like playing the s'wit. It means I can surprise them later. \n\nI never know where I'll be called to go. And I'd rather not become one of the Tribunal's toys.

Such suspicion. Are you going to search me for weapons? You'll find some. But I doubt even you would confiscate all the knives I'm carrying. \n\nIt may come as a shock to you, but I can do more than sneak around in the shadows.

Very soon, but our delegates have been through an unimaginable ordeal. They might not admit it, but they need to rest.\n\nWe'll move them to a secure location and give them time to recover. Then we'll proceed with the talks.

Exactly. Which is one of the reasons I'm laying low and talking to all the wonderfully boring people here. I'll be in Mournhold again soon, but I want to give the Living Gods a chance to find new hobbies.

The Order still poses a threat, of course, but I trust Lady Arabelle to handle our security. I'm counting on her to deal with the Order while I prepare for the conference.\n\nThe Ascendant Lord and his Magus surprised us once. They won't do so again.

While the conference site is repaired, I'll secure them in Gonfalon Bay. The captains and Caska can watch over the royals and Valessea, and we'll have time to send for a new Fighters Guild delegate.\n\nI'm surprised this turned out as well as it did.

I didn't notice how powerful the Ascendant Order had become. And I should have sniffed out Count Damard's treachery. The clues were there—wealth, grievances, arcane skill.\n\nThanks to you, we salvaged the situation. And I can learn from my mistakes.

He received word that she hadn't been in a fight in a long while. Combat is one of the few things Raz knows can put a genuine smile on Naryu's face. \n\nSo this one took it upon himself to remind her of a good one.
No, this one was very careful not to be seen. But he is taking every precaution to ensure Naryu does not spot him. At least for a while. \n\nHe doesn't want to draw attention to himself.
The fight Raz chose was when we were ambushed at the Sweetroll Killer's farm house.
The problem is, Raz is not sure why Naryu is at this festival. Is there something interesting happening? \n\nHe will have to stay for a while, keep out of Naryu's sight, and wait for trouble.

Tell the druids what we have said. They summoned and bound us in the past. They must be able to do so again.\n\nBut urge them to hurry. The corruption … consumes us. Soon, we shall not be able to stave off the Allwither.

Oh, that's hurtful. And here I thought we were friends.\n\nBut let me think. Oh, there's a coin fort on the far side of the island. Steer clear of that unless you run out of other options. It's controlled by the Serpents and they're stone-cold killers.

And I'll start digging around out here. Oh, and if you were wondering, I'll hop a ship back to High Isle when I'm finished. Easy enough out here in Amenos Station—as long as you don't look like one of the prisoners.

I haven't seen any signs of the Order here on Amenos. Yet. But there must be a connection, right? \n\nHow else would the Serpents know about the alliance leaders if the Ascendant Order didn't tip them off?

If I am asked to verify it or to add in my involvement, I will not hesitate. But this is Gavos' tale. All I can offer him, is my support while he labors in memory. \n\nI know his words will serve the Abbey well.

The Mirrored Way has a bunch of references for arcane glyphs. For some spells, arcane glyphs provide the framework to make everything work smoothly. They're pretty powerful. But if you're even the slightest bit off, it won't be successful.

Exactly. Considering how my first spell went today, I think it's probably wise to be a little cautious. I'm almost sad Magister Irin won't get to see this. He'd be proud of me taking the time to look before I leap.\n\nEven if it is a little late.

There may still be corrupted wildlife lingering about, but the druids can deal with that. Otherwise, know that the danger has passed.\n\nAnd know that we are grateful, mortal. For everything. May your harvest never falter.

I see. As trying as she can be, she truly is a talented mage. She can be impatient, but given her natural inclination to magic, it's understandable. I always knew I was perhaps not the best teacher for her.

We might have been arguing about where to get the best cake in Wrothgar. That made us want cake. But the man in the back room said he did not have cake.\n\nSo I asked him to give me whatever he had. For <<1>>!

Oh, yes! I am good diplomat, so I thought she would like something to remind her of home. After that, <<1>> kept asking for more drinks. We all laughed and had fun!\n\nWe said goodnight just outside. She got in her carriage and drove off for home.

I don't mean to give the impression that Ember is incapable of learning, that's not the case. She's a bright mage—one of the brightest I've ever seen. Everything I've taught her, she's taken to like flame to parchment. But therein lies the problem.

Exactly right. Ember needs someone who can keep up with her, someone who thrusts themselves headlong into adventure so that she may temper herself and her magic beside them. Perhaps when I was younger, I could have been that for her. But not now.

Just like a flame, Ember wants to devour everything around her. Her appetite for knowledge is ceaseless. That's a good quality in a mage, but not necessarily one I'm equipped to deal with. By my own admission, I am methodical. Cautious. By the books.

Coral Cliffs is a rocky cove on the northern side of Amenos. You know, the so-called prison island. I need you to go there and gather some of the components the druids use in their rituals. I'm studying their approach to magic for the Mages Guild.

Unfortunately, no. Even the friendly druids of the Stonelore Circle refuse to give away their secrets. But I really want to study the magic of the Eldertide Druids. It's very … volatile! With enough components to study, there's so much I can learn.

Well, I'm fascinated by the magic that the druids of the Eldertide Circle cast, and I have it on good authority that Coral Cliffs is one of their strongholds. I do urge caution, however.\n\nThe Eldertide are what you might call hostile druids.
Now I know you jest, my sweet! To my crew, I am captain! But to you, I am—Ouch! Ouch, ouch, ouch!
Of course they did. Good chaps. And of course, I was one of the order's most renowned composers. \n\nThey no doubt wish to put my beautiful gilded lute in a place of honor.

Of course, of course! I commend your efforts. Please let the rest of the order know that I, Sir Brenvale the Golden, shall now depart this plane at last.\n\nMy next performance will be in the great theatres of Aetherius! Adieu!

Ah yes, I'm sure when I did not return there was many a fair damsel who wept inconsolable tears. \n\nAfter all, once you hear my voice raised in song … to know the voice of Sir Brenvale the Golden was silenced. A tragedy.

Hmm. He could have prolonged his life any number of ways. My best guess is some form of mystical prolongation, commonly called lichdom. My research indicates he has invested his soul in a powerful phylactery.\n\nFurther study is obviously indicated!
Oh, some locals said they'd seen the vulk'esh emerging from some lava vents. The vents can scrape at the vulk'esh's outer layers. Help pry the scoria off.
As a matter of fact, I noticed animals in the grove suffering from an affliction. I mentioned it to Archdruid Agathie and she said she would look into it.

Definitely a druidic ritual fetish. I use such accoutrements when conducting my own rituals. But this one bears the taint that afflicts the grove.\n\nThis fetish must have been used in the ritual that released the corruption.

Tobin? Yes! I refused that snake's advances! I was grieving, in shock and in pain. And he demanded I betray my love for another man. How could I? It was too soon.\n\nYou must help. I think … it started at the inn. End this curse so I can remember!

Emeric is nothing if not reliable. Look at the way the dead Serpents are laid out. Isn't it obvious? He left a trail to follow. It leads directly into the cave just up the path.\n\nGo ahead and look for him.

I'll be along shortly. The poultices should have done their job by now, so I want to go back and retrieve Caska.\n\nWe will want her strength at our side before this is over. And she needs to be nearby when you signal for the rescue ship.

Ugh. I should never have kept all this from him. I know he likely put you up to speaking with me, but the fact that you followed through—that you listened—made all the difference in the world.\n\nI'm not alone anymore. You reminded me of that.

I intend to determine the cause of this new volcanic activity to the best of my ability. Thanks to you, I'm no longer in danger of drowning in a molten wave of Y'ffre's wrath. Now, I can take my time with my investigation.
Now? We train harder than ever!\n\nWe're headed into the final matches. Whoever we end up playing will have crisp cards and masterclass technique. We have to be ready!

With facing each other, you mean? Yes, of course.\n\nDefeating a friend can ruffle some feathers, it is true. But, in the end, it is only a game, right? Plus, haven't you always secretly wondered who is the best player in Gonfalon Bay?

Ha! Yes, that goes without saying.\n\nTruthfully, I cannot think of anything that could lure me out of retirement now. And to be the greatest, you have to play. Is it not so? No, the reign of Razhamad is over. One of you must claim my place.

So soon? Funny how it feels like an eternity between rounds, then it's a sprint once things start! Honestly, I never thought I'd make it this far.\n\nMara's mercy. The final round. Did Razhamad tell you the rules? Everyone for themselves and all that?

There are places on top of this mountain where you can look down into the Firepot. Hunters usually stay clear of these windows, but a few brave ones helped us prepare for this foray into the cave. \n\nNow it's up to us to get the scoria.

I saw him scuttling down an alley near the docks. Knowing him, he's off making some ill-advised bet. Gods, I hope I'm wrong. He's got a real chance at greatness here! He can't muck it up!\n\nOh well. Hopefully I'll see you both at the gaming hall soon!

Whatever happens, I'm rooting for you and Brahgas. But mostly for myself, of course! \n\nI'll tell you, standing here within spitting distance of the championship … it's really something. Sorinne the Tribute Champion has a nice ring, doesn't it?

Well enough.\n\nOnce that initial rush of victory wore off, I remembered how far I still have to go, you know? Once skooma has its hooks in you … it's not something you can just shrug off with a game of cards. But I did open up to Razhamad.
The captain? Why, I am the captain!
Renwic Moorcroft, captain of the Pristine Halberd and proud member of the All Flags Navy!
My name? Why, I'm … I'm ….

Yeah? What? And who's going to beat me? Sorinne? You? Listen, you're a talented Tribute player, but I've been playing cards for years. I taught you how to play, remember?\n\nZ'en's price, I'm sorry. I didn't mean to …. I just really need this gold.

Razhamad's already bailed me out twice. Sorinne poured out a month's wages to pay off a Sea Elf I owed. I can't keep hiding behind my friends. I have to settle this on my own.\n\nIf I pull off this one last bet, it'll settle my debts and then some!

It's a bit late for that, chum. I'm eyeball-deep in it now. Only way out of this is a glorious triumph … or, well, let's not think about that.\n\nCome on. Let's head back to the gaming hall. Our opponents might already be there waiting for us.

That's the spirit! I've had it up to my acorns with all the pity. Poor, pathetic Brahgas! Sure, I've stumbled in the past, but this is my ticket to a clean slate!\n\nCome on. Let's head back to the gaming hall and meet our soon-to-be-defeated foes!
Out, you vile creature! \n\nNever fear. I'm myself again. And better yet, I know where this Tobin hid his tools. I saw it while he was inside my head. To the graveyard, my friend!
Storm and fire? I am troubled.\n\nIf the Ascendant Magus can use powerful storm magic against his enemies, does he also command the tremors and volcanic fissures? It is maddening to even contemplate!

Za'ji is right to worry, then. The loss of a monument might be the least of our concerns if the Ascendant Order can rouse the volcano.\n\nLady Arabelle is inside, friend. Perhaps she'll know what to do.

Oh, yes. Of course, the effects may linger for a time, but the worst of it is over. And we righted a wrong of history. Captain Renwic Moorcroft's role in the All Flags Navy has been restored. \n\nBut how is Lady Laurent? Is she all right?

When the first druids of Stonelore discovered this sacred grove, the place had no spirit to nurture and protect it. So they prayed to Y'ffre and shaped his will to call forth the Evergrowth.\n\nThey bound it to the grove to preserve its balance.
Mostly what you would expect. I oversee the druids that care for this grove and help train the novices in the True Way. Elders Karic and Warrane advise me on matters related to my work.
I do not know much, since I have never been allowed down here before. They say the spirit of the Evergrowth resides in this place, as well as the wards that bind it to the grove.

Oh … it's a simple matter. Nature is home to all. But many city dwellers and merchants don't see that as truth. \n\nMy sister feels slighted by the nobles of Gonfalon Bay. But I know the value of patience. All things change with time.

Do you expect me to dance and sing while those blasted nobles use our forests for sport? When peasants tear down all the animal's homes to make useless fences for their farms? Something has to be done, or we'll lose everything of worth that's here!

Such a prying question from someone whose standing is unclear. We're celebrating. My companion's enjoying a well-earned vacation and I'm drinking for the sake of drinking. Would you care to join us? No … you're no noble. \n\nWould you like to serve?

If you looked carefully, I'm sure you'd find many small circles communing with nature. But most align to either my circle, or my sister's. \n\nStill, there is a third. But it's bad luck talking about them. I have enough to deal with here.

No. We Stonelore Druids know that we can't force our beliefs on anyone. We strive to do our best and practice the way we see fit. We welcome all who want to join, of course.\n\nBut my sister and the Eldertide want change regardless of its price.

They are if they have sense! I'm not one of those spineless Stonelores like my brother. \n\nDrastic change requires action. And if you think I've gone too far, then pray you never meet members of the other circle.

Look, I may have exaggerated my distress when we met, but everything I told you is true. They grabbed Valentyn for no reason. And if we don't get him out, he'll be lost forever.\n\nIt's not just the dangerous currents that make Amenos a prison.

Look, Valentyn and I are thieves, and we're damn good ones! Getting into and out of impossible situations is what we do. In my case, I've had time to plan and prepare. Valentyn didn't get the chance. That's why you need to go in there and help him.

They do something when they process the prisoners. Magic or alchemy, I don't know the details. But anyone banished to the jungle, they can't survive anywhere but on this accursed rock. It's a perfect prison … and totally inhumane.

It's simple! You find my husband before they process him, escort him to the location I marked on your map, and we all get away before the jailers notice a thing.\n\nTrust me. Valentyn and I have been doing stuff like this since the moment we met.

The jungle's as bad as the darkest pit of Oblivion. Wild beasts, monsters, and banished marauders roam freely. Valentyn wouldn't last two shakes of a guar's stubby tail out there. And if they process him, he'll be trapped—until something kills him.

There's no need. Getting to Amenos isn't hard. Getting off the island? That's another matter. Besides, between the gangs, the creatures, and whatever the jailers do to process the prisoners, only the toughest survive. And they have nowhere to go.

Funny story. Mabzin hired us separately to pull off the same job. She hoped we'd kill each other. To eliminate the competition, you understand.\n\nThe look on her face when she found us, arm in arm, waiting in her chamber two nights later—priceless!

When she accidentally separated the Allwither from the Evergrowth, I suppose her fate was sealed. The circle will assign a new archdruid to the grove. In the meantime, the elders will keep us on track.\n\nI guess that's me, now. Elder and mediator.

That remains to be seen. She and the other druids who were afflicted with the corruption … we need to see if we can restore them. We'll get our best healers involved. And I'll consult with the Evergrowth.\n\nI guess that's my job now, as mediator.

Not just any prisoner. Yvara. That viper used something I found to earn her status as a trusty. I should be the one getting three meals a day, a spot on the platform, and a guarantee I won't be processed. Help me teach her a lesson and I'll help you.

He went down to the courtyard to deal with the Eldertide Druids. Can you believe they allied with the Ascendant Order? They're feeding this storm. \n\nYou should help him—after you help me. All I need is a moment to clearly align the ballista!
That's what the jailer's call the area between their keep and the gates that lead into the jungle. Not the safest place to go wandering, in my opinion, but Valentyn insisted.

Good. Then I can use this ballista to destroy that ship! Just get down to the dock and keep these rats at bay long enough for me to smash those reinforcements out of the water!\n\nThen we can fall back to the hall.

Ah, yes. The protected hall. I thought Lady Arabelle's arrangements were overly cautious. Events, however, reveal the wisdom of her actions. As much as I dislike hiding, we must deny our enemies an easy victory.\n\nDo you have an invitation medallion?

Then we should make use of the defenses she prepared. I'm sure she plans to launch a counterattack, just like she did during Ranser's siege of Wayrest. Why, she—ah. Never mind. A tale for another time.\n\nThe door to the hall is on the south wall.

There may still be corrupted wildlife about, but the druids can deal with that. Otherwise, know that the danger has passed.\n\nWe mourn the loss of the archdruid, but we are grateful for everything you did, mortal. May your harvest never falter.
Just so.\n\nYou and your compatriots will face my associates here. The winners of those contests will then play each other to determine who will have the honor of facing the reigning champion. Me.

Long enough to know that one should never underestimate an opponent or leave anything to chance. Your leader, Razhamad, taught me that lesson. It's one of the reasons I hold him in such high esteem.\n\nUnlike others in your coterie.

Indeed. To think that he lives in the company of such a great man and still learns nothing. Heartbreaking.\n\nWell, when this is all over, I expect Brahgas won't trouble anyone else … beside the slavemasters of House Dres, of course.
The Sapphire Tourney is underway, of course!\n\nDuchess Dufort and Knight Commander Jourvel have entrusted me with the very important role of overseeing the festivities!

The Duchess herself asked me to organize and execute this tremendously popular affair. \n\nI mean, who else could do it? I am a man of many connections! I've managed tourneys, fairs, banquets, investitures, weddings and, of course, funerals.

More than you can count with two hands! We have a whole troupe of performers, several cookmasters preparing different delicacies from across the seas. \n\nAnd it would hardly be a proper tourney without the joust, now would it?

The understatement of the year. And once this tourney is completed and the grounds restored and the staff paid, we start planning all over again. The next one is just a few years away, you know. \n\nI love my job.

I prefer to be carried—it's less disrespectful—but I suspect you'll need your hands free for the trials ahead.\n\nHonor demands that I accompany you on this quest. More importantly, my presence will be necessary inside Death's Valor Keep.

She's the scourge of the Systres Archipelago, one of the Sea Elves' most powerful conjurers—a Sea Mage. Her storms have sunk many a warship in pursuit of her fleet, but we hope cornering her on land may tip the scales in our favor.

We've only spied it from afar. It's a craggy rock full of tunnels that these wharf rats have turned into a warren. \n\nWe'll get you as close as we can, but the shallows are full of jagged rocks and coral waiting to take a bite of our hull.

They've been a nuisance for years, but the losses suffered going after them always outweighed the benefits of victory. That changed in recent months. The Dreadsails have been striking waterways all over the Systres in small, well-coordinated groups.

I captured the slipperiest pirate this archipelago has ever seen. Minasi eluded my grasp seven times. But—at last—I've managed to put her reign of terror to an end. This time, she won't be released to wreak her havoc on the unsuspecting.
She what—not again! Minasi! Please stop! In the name of the Divines!

Ordinary bandits, the Systres Guard can handle. But when we send enough guards to meet a company of Ascendant Order ravagers, these faceless knights just melt away. And if we don't send enough guards?\n\nThen our guards don't come back.

Might as well be. Most knights proudly display their emblems. They wear the colors of their house and paint family crests on their shields.\n\nThese Ascendant Order knights never remove their helms and bear no devices. They could be anybody.

Who, me? Ha! No, no. That Mournhold bully over there eliminated me in the first round. You know what, though? It's fine. I had a grand time and there's always the next tournament.\n\nNow, I get to relax and cheer you and Brahgas on!

I really was looking forward to watching you beat the flin out of this Elf. Ah well.\n\nAfter your match, I'll head back to Gonfalon Bay and do some investigating. Meet me at the gaming hall when you finish up here. I'm rooting for you!

Nothing yet, but I'm hopeful. Honestly, I've been trying not to think about it. He's in it deep this time. The bets he's making … I don't know the specifics, but I know it's much, much more than he can cover.\n\nI should probably check on him.
Just like that? Are you sure you don't want to make any outrageous bets beforehand? Isn't that the custom among certain members of your chapter?

Yes, of course.\n\nQuite the cautionary tale, that one. I haven't seen him yet. So, he's either vainly soldiering on against one of my companions, or already someone's property. Are you sure you don't want to place a bet too?
Brahgas defeated Teliv's associate. Only one opponent stands between him and the final match.

Brahgas's debts are … no longer in Brahgas's hands. There is hope still, but you must defeat Teliv in order for my plan to work. And to defeat Teliv, you must beat Brahgas here. Now.\n\nHe's upstairs waiting. HoonDing give you strength.

If Brahgas faces off against Teliv, he will lose. Brahgas mirrors my tournament style. Against a lesser opponent, that might be enough. But Teliv has studied my strategies in detail. He knows every counter.\n\nBrahgas cannot defeat Teliv. But you can.

Worried? Chum, I've been worried all my life. Running from gangsters, hiding in fish barrels, scraping for loose coins on filthy tavern floors. I'm done with that. All of it.\n\nIt's win or die now. No tricks. No excuses. Just us and the cards.
Then … I face the consequences. Come what may.\n\nI wouldn't worry about it, though. I'm going to win this match, friend. I've come too far. Now, enough talk.

Well, this was before Amenos Station and the prison stockade. The sisters built their vault and hid their treasure. While the vault was under construction, Famaza fell in love with a local named Altinwe. That's when everything started to fall apart.

Right behind this rocky cliff side. The locks are hidden in the boulder I was examining. Ingenious design, but it definitely requires all three keys.\n\nYou know, I was hoping the legend was wrong about that. Ah, well.

This isn't just any gem! The Daybreak Gem has a rich history. And it's part of a different legend. \n\nI'll let you in on another secret—with the Daybreak Gem, I can find an even more legendary vault that contains an even greater treasure!

Razhamad didn't want me to tell you, but you need to know. He struck a new deal with Teliv to settle Brahgas's debts. A big one.\n\nIf Razhamad loses this bet … he's signing over the entire gaming hall to the Mournhold Chapter.

Yeah. Building, staff, licenses, the whole thing. Who knows what Teliv has planned for it?\n\nBut there's still a chance. Razhamad bet that a member of the Gonfalon Chapter would win the tournament. It didn't matter who—just one of us.

As if you needed more pressure, right? That's why Razhamad didn't want to tell you.\n\nYou can do this, though. I believe in you. Razhamad believes in you. The entire chapter is behind you. Now, go to Mournhold and show Teliv what Gonfalon's made of!

Nothing good. The Systres Sisters died fighting each other, leaving Altinwe with one key and the secret of the vault. He bragged of it in a tavern, which is how the legend got started.\n\nHe met his end searching the jungle for the other two keys.

Altinwe convinced Famaza to betray her sisters so they could keep the treasure for themselves. Her sisters learned of the plan and hid their keys before any confrontation could occur.\n\nYou see, all three keys were needed to open the vault.

Dangerous? Sure, but nothing you can't handle. We haven't been processed yet, so we can come and go from the jungle as we please. Just make sure none of the jailers notice. They usually don't pay much attention outside the stockade, though.

Precisely! Now you see why I was willing to risk banishment to obtain the Daybreak Gem. I'm just glad Marcelle found you and sent you to help. She really is a terrific partner!\n\nNow, let's go get those keys!

A lot of research went into determining which rare book mentioned the keys. Then more to find out there was a copy in the prison. After I obtained Famaza's key from a far-too-trusting descendant, I came here.\n\nAnyway, we'll soon have the other keys!

It is marvelous, is it not? This is actually the second beacon to stand atop Gonfalon Head. It dates back to the early first century. When I assumed my duties here, the tower was in poor repair. Dangerous, even.

When Duchess Elea Dufort assumed her father's duties a few years ago, she ordered a complete renovation of the structure. I'm sure she wanted to protect trade in Gonfalon Bay, but she spared no expense in rebuilding the lighthouse.

Horrible monsters, whose very skin oozed molten rock. Or perhaps you'd prefer the melancholy tale of the undead looking for a way to escape the walls of a keep. Hmm I can tell you'd prefer the mystery of a hospital where the patients get sicker.

Ah yes, there's a cave on High Isle which is filled with roving packs of vulk'esh. The creatures are so great that their footsteps shake the earth. \n\nI stood atop the mountain and felt the blistering heat on my face. No mortal could survive there.

Ruins of former knightly orders litter the archipelago. But this particular knightly order didn't die with their bodies. \n\nI journeyed to the keep and heard voices of the dead emanating from the very ground. They sounded lively for ones so long gone.

When Lord Bacaro accepted soldiers from every alliance in his hospital, I thought it was for the best. But that was before the soldiers lost their minds. \n\nI was in there but for a few hours before I felt I was losing the very essence of myself.
Oh, so you've heard of it?\n\nWell—well then you must be suitably impressed at my bravery. I stood closer to those rivers of flame than any other.

Do you recall the invitation medallions I enchanted? Each delegate carries one, so I can trace my own magic to locate Quentyn. Now, let me see. They moved northeast, across the loch. I see an abandoned chapel, crypts. \n\nNo question. Quentyn is there.

Lady Arabelle asked me to try as soon as we realized the ships were late. I wasn't able to make a connection with those medallions. Maybe they were too far away, or some other magic interfered with my scrying, but I wasn't able to detect anything.

No, we need to return to Lady Arabelle and share this information. Then we can mount a rescue for Guild General Quentyn.\n\nI'll meet you at Lady Arabelle's little pavilion. What she calls her field office, I believe.

Not a student of politics, my dear? I understand completely.\n\nThey're the leaders of the alliances vying for the Ruby Throne. Well, Ayrenn and Emeric lead two of the alliances. Irnskar is the son of Jorunn the Skald-King, who leads the third.

It's … complicated. The Ruby Throne sits vacant, and the Tamrielic Empire lacks an Emperor. None of the alliances can stomach the idea that one of the others might win the throne.\n\nIt's a wonder Bacaro and I got them to agree to these peace talks.

You poor dear. You must pay more attention to current events.\n\nQueen Ayrenn leads the Aldmeri Dominion. High King Emeric, the Daggerfall Covenant. And Prince Irnskar represents the Ebonheart Pact. The opponents in the aptly named Three Banners War.
Quite confident. I double checked her binds myself. This time I finally have her. She's just—not again! Stop in the name of the law!

Find a weak spot and knock on the wall. You'd be surprised what you can do with a good hammer and chisel.\n\nI'd do it, but I'm more about the strategy and tactics than the physical labor. Not really built for that sort of thing, you know.

Absolutely! In many ways I take care of every creature on High Isle. Those that cannot speak for themselves, anyway.\n\nMany animals find their way to my home that deserve special attention. Privette was just such a sheep.

I woke one morning and instantly knew someone needed my care. I leapt from bed and ran to my door! And, just out front, there she was.\n\nOh, Privette was quite the beauty! From the moment I laid eyes on her, I knew I had to serve her.

Like rotten meat floating in dirty sea water. They usually live far below the water, so I shouldn't judge. Maybe my scent of fine lanolin and fresh hay offends them!\n\nListen to me gossiping like a child. This happens when I get emotional.

Yes. If you win, I will release Brahgas, debt free. More importantly, Razhamad will retain control of his gaming hall.\n\nYour friend's freedom and your teacher's livelihood … both reliant on a game of cards. I hope you play well under pressure.

We know Privette came through here, because we found her sash. But since we didn't see any sheep bones, they must have moved her.\n\nLet's search the caves over to the west. I know it's rude to rummage around someone's home. But they started it.

You were quite stern with them. Maybe the Hadolids got the message not to bother their neighbors.\n\nIf I see them lurking around again, I will just tell them they're not welcome! I can be quite stern as well when I need to be.
You think so? I suppose. We do have a healthy competitive streak, but it adds spice to our marriage. We really do love each other.

Well, first I need to get off this damn island. Then that research I mentioned. And some relaxation. Always good to take time, especially after a successful heist.\n\nI also want to plan something nice for when Marcelle gets home. Something romantic.

The altars inside served as the final test of a squire's worthiness. The chests won't open unless the order's creed is said in earnest.\n\nMy presence ensures that kneeling at the altars will unlock the chests.

The Eldertide Circle refuses to recognize the authority of any lord who doesn't embrace druid ways. And they simply hate mainlanders. I don't know what the theurges want with the stones under Lord Felipe's lands, but it can't be good.

It's not really my area of expertise, but I presume you just hit it until it stops moving. And given the fact that the Sable Knight animates the bodies of its victims with necromantic power, I'd appreciate it if you didn't join its little army.

Ever have soft-shelled mudcrab with a side of melted butter? Hadolids are like that after they molt, but without the butter. So a big, strong, bad-tempered Hadolid that isn't molting guards the others while they've vulnerable.\n\nThat's the matron.
Well, if not, you're close!\n\nGo talk to Razhamad and let him know you introduced yourself to the chapter's premiere players. He'll be glad to hear it.
Then show me, Gonfalon. It's time to find out who will be crowned the next Tribute champion!
A traveler buried me here, but left my head on the gravestone—a warning to all who journeyed on this road. My presence ensured that no one disturbed the keep or unleashed the horrors within.

The ritual requires an attuned torchbug. I always carry a few on my person—here, take him. Gently.\n\nI'll need you to toss the bright-bummed lad into the largest volcanic vent, it's just to the north. Don't worry! No harm will come to the torchbug!

The spirits noticed an abundance of magic—both at the vents and within the volcano itself. My people are the only ones who can claim power over volcanic forces, but that doesn't make any sense. Why would anyone want to usher a volcano along?

Not forever, but now that I know the nature of the activity, I can conduct a ritual to calm the vents. That way, they won't be a danger to anyone, at least not for a while.\n\nBut to do so, I need your young legs again. How do you feel about torchbugs?

Fauns are … fickle. They're protectors of nature, but usually they aren't vicious. Wise hunters steer clear of their lands, but Wildhorn is more aggressive than most.\n\nBe careful. A faun lord can turn the forest itself against intruders.

I couldn't say for sure. But Sea Elves have an affinity for serpents and breed them for war, or so I hear. And they hate pretty much everyone else. \n\nPerhaps Vinsha is looking for new weapons to unleash against the people of the Systres.

The Ascendant Order is hungry for recruits. I suspect it's a join-us-or-die sort of thing, but these two don't just kill the ones who refuse. They use prisons of shadow magic to drain their power first.\n\nBy now, they must be very strong indeed.

I honestly don't remember much about last night. Genalda and I always taste test our new creations, but I must have gotten a little carried away. Clearly, we did an excellent job crafting a delicious drink. \n\nMaybe too delicious, heh.

What? No! You think Genalda would put up with me if I made a habit out of drinking our livelihoods away? She's a patient woman, but not that patient.\n\nNo, I think our newest concoction was just particularly tempting. Or potent. Or both.

Well, the welts and bruises will take a few weeks to heal. Feels like I fell off a horse … as it was falling off a cliff.\n\nBut, a few bumps and scratches are the least of it. The real consequences hurt a lot worse.
Ah, enough of all the mushy stuff. You should head upstairs and talk to Razhamad. He's got a reward for you. Go claim it, champ!\n\nAs for me? I'm going to have a bit more of this delicious medicine.

Razhamad revoked my chapter sponsorship and suspended my Roister's Club membership—we've barely spoken since we got back.\n\nLooks like my days on the Tribute circuit are over. After what I put Razhamad through, I can hardly blame him.

I'm divine, my blurry friend. Just fine! Genalda and I are going to sell our incredible drink to the rich and become famous! I've always wanted to be famous. Hilgrim and Genalda the innovators! The saviors of taste! The—hic— heroes of liquid.

I befriended another exile from Hammerfell. An old pirate who captained the Scourge of Sentinel. He terrorized the crown for years before disappearing. He told me he split a map of his treasure among his crew, but they never claimed it.

The old pirate gave me his fragment before he passed to the Far Shores and told me the rest of his crew were still in the Systres, so I tried to track them down. None of them seem to still be alive, but following their trails seems to have paid off.

No, thank you.\n\nThis was supposed to be a simple tournament, and to many it was.  But not us. Not you. You reclaimed our chapter's honor. Saved property … lives. Whatever the future brings, Razhamad and the players of Gonfalon Bay are in your debt.

Now, we should discuss the matter of the tournament itself!\n\nI watched you grow from a novice to a veteran. Through dutiful card-collection and countless matches, you stand before me … a Tales of Tribute champion!

Because as soon as she opened the old chest, her posture changed. She started to swear like a sailor! Claimed she was the captain of a great sailing vessel and ordered me around like a lowly deckhand.\n\nIt was even more degrading than usual.

Just that. I noticed a lot of historical plaques scattered about. They talk about the All Flags Navy, which I think was rather famous in its day.\n\nThe Society of the Steadfast hired Lady Laurent to preserve the site prior to their big meeting.

And you as well, my friend. I just wish that one of your visits didn't involve the imminent demise of either me or my honored employer.\n\nLady Laurent will be happy to see you … especially if you manage to remove the captain's spirit from her body.

You've never heard of the famous historian and treasure hunter, Lady Clarisse Laurent? Some of the most important discoveries of the age can be directly attributed to m'lady.\n\nAs for me, I'm just her humble manservant. Now about that sea captain ….

You know me. Every day a new adventure. Had a good thing going for a while, smuggling spices out of Hegathe. Got married twice. No, wait. Three times. \n\nThe third one nearly got me hanged, but Lady Arabelle saved me from the gallows.

Gotta keep things interesting.\n\nDidn't really want to work for anybody, to be honest. But Lady Arabelle's not so bad once you get to know her. Maybe if you put in a good word for me I'll be a free man again when all this is done.
How could you know that? Do you mean to tell me that you've been to Death's Valor Keep and spoken to the skull yourself?

How could you know that? Unless … you're the one who put a stop to it. I heard the soldiers were beginning to recover from their harrowing ordeals. \n\nIf that's the case, then I must concede to your expertise. You're more the knight than I.

Mostly because the sea captain rambled about the curse of the islet and the curse that binds his spirit, etcetera, etcetera. Made the hair on my neck stand on end.\n\nTo think there's someone in there with m'lady … it's very troublesome!

As I said, three trials await you. Perseverance, Wits, and Constitution. They each test a virtue that Lady Garick sought in those she sailed with.\n\nI will meet you before each one to explain your goal and offer guidance. After that, it's up to you.

I mean … like over drinks? Ha! Only kidding!\n\nWhat's the newest Tribute Master want to talk about? Strategies? Rare cards? The ingredients of Gelekh's eel pudding?  Actually, let's avoid that last one.

For you, my friend? Of course! You saved my hide!\n\nIn fact you got any jobs that need doing? Need a horse groomed? Garden weeded? As long as it doesn't involve betting, I'm game! You would need to teach me about horses and gardens, though.

Were it not for the excess of magic, I would think it nothing more than an example of Y'ffre's uncompromising and intractable will. But there is more to this.\n\nDread brews in my stomach like a terrible storm. Or perhaps that's just gas. Who can say?
I am. The two of us would not be having such a friendly conversation were I part of the Eldertide Circle, heh. Lucky you! Can't say much about the Firesong Circle, however, and I don't care to.

Easily! I may be old, but I'm still a druid. I am an arbiter of Y'ffre's will and therefore my magic helps me take care of and communicate with nature. I can make flowers grow beneath your feet if I wish, and I can summon spirits.

Ah, it is good for Jhaka to even think of this. Many days were full of despair and I did not wish to think of the future. \n\nFirst, I will get far away from this place. I will get healthy again and I will help Ember. We will find lost friends.
You are kind, friend of Ember. I am at ease now that I see Ember and now that I have my freedom back. \n\nJhaka will recover and see what other adventures Jone and Jode have in store.

I saw both of my friends accosted, then it went dark. When I came to, I could hear Song weeping.\n\nAfter that, there was magic sleep, I think. When it wore off, I was in the belly of a stinking Dark Elf boat.

Oh, by all the stars! Why must that ghost make this difficult? Amunara didn't even know he'd be here! Who sticks around after they die to give people tests?\n\nThis one sympathizes, but when Amunara leaves, the shield goes with her.

Amunara supposes that's fair to tell you. There's a story about Lady Garick's famous shield. Arkay himself anointed it with his blood. Allegedly.\n\nAn ambitious young necromancer could use such an artifact. Draw out its power to become stronger.

Lady Laurent was hired to preserve any items and structures of historical import and make the islet safe for the upcoming meeting. They knew they had a problem with undead, but they never mentioned anything about an ancient curse!

Oh, I'm just a meager, put upon manservant. I wouldn't know anything about such monumental events. Well, I may have heard a mention or two. So, yes, I suppose ending the Three Banners War is the purpose of the big meeting.\n\nConfidentially speaking.

I couldn't say. I'm just a meager, put upon manservant after all. I may have heard a mention or two about influential visitors and an important discussion, but I didn't really pay much mind.\n\nLady Laurent keeps me very busy, you understand.

Not very much, I'm afraid. He's boisterous, confident, and rather bawdy, if I'm being honest. I detest him. And I can't abide such a depraved individual taking up residence in my mistress. It's … unseemly!\n\nCome along and you'll see for yourself.
Oh? I knew you looked like the helpful sort. You have my thanks for assisting them. It's comforting to know you're a friend to my people. There are many who view druids with suspicion … or worse.

A minor setback, I assure you. We were going to stop a hoard of bandits and elevate our names, but then a traveling druid told me about a Dragon and I confess my excitement got the better of me. No matter, we'll find some great villainy soon.
It's quite exciting! Legends say Lady Garick's shield contains the power of Arkay. It preserved her life as long as she held it, yes?\n\nIf Amunara can absorb that power, think of the possibilities!

Yeah, she's here. And she came bearing gifts. Skooma.\n\nAfter all this time, you'd think I could just say no, but I plucked it right out of her hand. No hesitation. I told myself I would bring it down here and pour it out in the harbor. But now ….
Does it matter? Evil must be defeated wherever it is found. Otherwise it festers like a … like a … festering thing. \n\nMy squire would have a good metaphor.

She's angry with me. She feels that I failed to collect rations for this journey. Rations? Who needs food when adventures lie ahead?\n\nHer skills are commendable, but she still has much to learn. Which is why she is the squire and I am the knight.

He won't do anything to help people! We've let three villages suffer because their problems weren't grandiose enough.\n\nI'm half tempted to invent some great villain just so he'll find the motivation to fight!

An evil knight you say? You know, that just might be odd enough to work. My knight master will probably spend the entire trip challenging the other knights we meet along the road. But, what else is new?\n\nI'll tell him about this villain right away.

Pirates? Yes, he'd definitely believe that. Plus, I'm sure we will be able to spot some pirates along any coast these days. And having some merchants indebted to me—I mean us—wouldn't be a bad thing. \n\nAll right, I can use this!

No fighting and the journey ends up profitable. Now, that's the kind of adventure I could go for. Hopefully some of that treasure contains a few relics or something I can throw his way to keep him placated.
We should probably check out the local Outlaws Refuge. He's probably laying low, just in case. People like me and Jhaka tend to feel safer in places like that.
I mean, I wouldn't exactly call us outlaws, but my friends and I were never fussy about how or where we got our food and coin. Outlaws Refuges tend to attract people with similar mindsets, is all.

No. Even after all this time, this one still remembers how to sneak about and move unnoticed. I traveled in darkness and with the gold Ember provided, eventually bought passage on a boat to Skywatch.\n\nI found Brisha and eventually, he sent me here.

Without the others, Skywatch did not feel the same to Jhaka. Bad memories, perhaps. But with coin and some easy work, I can stay warm and eat regularly here.\n\nI had time to search for information about the mercenaries. This one hopes it is helpful.

Magister Irin taught me this one, believe it or not. It's technically alchemy, but that's just another form of magic to me. \n\nSour algae smells and tastes terrible, but if you mix it right, it makes even the drunkest toffs clearheaded.
Two handfuls of the stuff should do it. We don't need much. Trust me, once you smell it, you'll understand why.\n\nIt'll be alongside the shore. Come on, let's go.

I knew it! That explains why we haven't been able to find any of their knights around Gonfalon Bay. The Ascendant Magus must have gathered all of his forces to participate in the attack.\n\nWhat do you need us to do?
Here, I'll mark the cove's location on your map. As for a crew, well, you're looking at your captain.\n\nAs for the rest, I'll see who I can drum up.

Hmm. The best place to hide a vessel on that part of the island is Jheury's Cove, north of the Navire Docks.\n\nLet me guess. Nereid's Song is an Ascendant Order ship. You want to use it to slip past their fleet and rescue the alliance leaders.
Now I do a bit of this, a bit of that, and try not to gag while I work. Just give me a moment to whip up the tonic.
Ha! Why didn't you just say so? Give it here!

Did you notice how the ground shook when he unleashed his storm? That's not a magic I've seen before. Somehow his storm magic is causing earthquakes.\n\nAt least he hasn't recovered the alliance leaders yet. We still have time.

Silverslip made a mistake when she was a kid. Who among us is immune from that? I'm not angry with her at all. I was a little … thrown by seeing her as a vampire, but ultimately I'm just happy she's here, and that we're reunited.

True! It seems like seeing me is giving her the kick she needs. She's been feeling guilty for so long, but now she has a chance to make it up to herself. \n\nAnd she even has a clue to lead us to Song! This worked out all around!

I was born of noble blood and ruffian tastes. When my days of piracy ended in capture by the authorities, my family pleaded for clemency. So I was spared imprisonment along with my peers but only if I never returned home. Even after I mended my ways.

I'm a Dark Elf. We are not in the habit of making threats. We only state matters as they are. Brahgas has every reason to worry.\n\nBut enough of that. We have games to play! The tournament lists are there in front of the gaming hall. Be seeing you.

I am Fillia. Or I was. It hardly matters.\n\nIn life, I was a master of games! Games of all sorts. Cards, dice, parlor games … I loved them all. Alas, I ran afoul of a drunk who'd grown sick of me winning all the time. So, he put a knife in me.

In part? Truthfully, I think other forces keep me here.\n\nBefore I died, I helped the Roister's Club craft their game. I played countless matches, but always won. To truly know a game, you must lose. Perhaps if I'm defeated, my spirit will move on.

Tempting. But I sense that you are not ready. Only a master can defeat me.\n\nGo and hone your craft. Challenge others and improve. When you reach the summit, return to me. I would relish a challenge.

Hmm. Yes, I can sense your confidence. I gaze into your eyes and see victories beyond counting. Yes! You will be the one to put me to rest.\n\nBut be warned: I will not hold back. Only a true victory will set me free.

I listen. I feel. After a life spent gazing into the future, perceiving the mundane is not so difficult. These Ternions understand. That is why I came here.\n\nBut you didn't come for philosophy. You seek the thrill of competition. Is it not so?

Ha! People will say it is witchcraft, or that I am not so blind as I seem. But it is nothing mystical, and I do not lie. I can play because I know these cards better than sparrow knows the wind.\n\nI made the cards, you see?

I'm sorry, but at my age, I mainly play for variety. I wish to feel an array of cuts and styles—cards made in different ways at different times.\n\nIf you assemble a grander collection, I will accept your challenge. But not before. Divines guide you.
I smell … yes, you have quite an array of unique cards. A true collector! I accept your challenge, traveler. To hear such a deck shuffled—it's music to my ears.\n\nLet's begin.

I am. One of the first. I know the cut, the weight, and the smell of every card. My fingertips greet each deck like a mother greets her children. Truly, they are my greatest joy.\n\nI'm glad to see people of quality have taken to the game.

Well, that's great news! People in my condition struggle to find opponents. Most of the tournaments take place during the day. And Verandis's band of orphans? Well, they all stink.\n\nI helped craft the damned game, but I barely get a chance to play!

Eh. On second thought? No. I'm tired of bleeding novices dry. I'm sure you're a fine player. But, I need a real challenge. And as you can see, I've got nothing but time.\n\nCome back when you've got a title under your belt.

Yeah. I'm Murzaga. I help the club with acquisitions. Inks, stock, that sort of thing. Better keep that to yourself, though. We Founders value discretion.\n\nSince you're here, though, I could really use a tough match. Bare-knuckles! Nothing held back!

Well, I can't help but respect a player who's willing to kick down the doors of a haunted castle and challenge someone six times their age.\n\nYou carry yourself like a Tribute master. Bet you taste like one too. Let's see if your skills measure up!

I'm doing what I do best, breathing new life into long forgotten games. I freely admit it's an obsession. A lucrative one!\n\nAncient Yokudan games have a charming asymmetry to them. Perhaps they'll inspire a Tales of Tribute deck some day!

Hmm. No, I think not. You carry yourself well, but I've not heard of you before. I have too much work to do to fritter away the hours with a journeyman player.\n\nGain some more experience. We'll play when you've got something to teach me.

I'm a Roister's Club Founder, so yes—I'm a creator … of a sort. I consult on strategy, deck composition, and the like.\n\nDo you play? I'm curious about the current dominant strategies. And I do mean dominant. I've no interest in the uninspired.

Hmm. You do strike me as the worldly sort. There's an ease to the way you handle the cards. Yes, you're a master all right.\n\nLet's get to it, then! Show me what strategies Tamriel's finest have cooked up!

I kept busy, if that's what you're asking.\n\nWe made our way around the fort and kept the bulk of the Serpent's forces occupied. Caska was a real champion. She cut down three ruffians for every one that Ayrenn or I dealt with.

For all their rhetoric, it's clear that the Ascendant Order doesn't want the war in Cyrodiil to end. At least not with one of us on the throne.\n\nThey're the worst kind of evil. A malicious greed masquerading as a benevolent purpose.

Between Emeric and I, the Green Serpents scattered like leaves in a strong breeze. And thanks to Caska's formidable presence, the rest were quick to abandon their posts. \n\nI made sure to hold off on the ritual until I saw the signal flare.
Of course. But you must tell her what I learned while I was a captive. The Ascendant Order is behind all this, and they are led by the Ascendant Lord and his Magus.

As sure as we made it onto this ship alive. They want to make a show of it.\n\nYou could hear it in their voices. This Magus, this Lord, they hunger for power. And the death of three alliance leaders would be quite a start to their feast.

Truly? Well, you did not know that they were planning a big meeting on High Isle until we heard the Ascendant Lord say it. So that's something.\n\nAnd did you know the Lord planned to kill us as soon as the Green Serpents delivered us to him?

You may call me the Author.\n\nTales of Tribute is many things to many different people. For some, as I said, it is simply a means to revelry. But for the dreamers and truth-seekers, it provides so much more. Each deck tells a story. A timeless fable.

No. There are many challenges you must overcome before I would even consider it. At bare minimum, you must attain mastery of the game and defeat some of my fellow Founders.\n\nDo this, and I will give it thought.

Stories I tell—along with my fellow Founders. The Roister's Club has goals that extend far beyond simple amusements. We seek to challenge. To hone. To teach. To improve.\n\nEvery rule … every stroke of the brush serves this goal.
Yes, I see something in you. A spark of … wisdom. At last.\n\nHave a seat. You have reached the summit, traveler, and the deepest truths of Tribute are within your grasp. Defeat me. If you can.

Every day. Alas, no one can compete. To my great disappointment, players play the game, but they do not know the game. Not in the way it must be known to defeat me.\n\nI fear I will never meet another person who truly understands what we seek to do.

You.\n\nBrahgas has never come this close to a title. His life depends on defeating Teliv and winning the tournament. His game has never been stronger. He plays with fierce determination. And that is why he cannot win this match.

We're here to remind the hard working folk of Tamriel that Zenithar sees their toils. He blesses them for their devotion to daily tasks. \n\nWith every season that passes, it's easy to lose sight of the divine in a hard day's work.

The Lord of the Anvil asks only that we earn new skills. Achieve great feats. Recover antiquities or treasure chests long thought lost. Or—barring all else—trade with vendors. \n\nHe does not ask more of us than we can give. Not even prayer.

I've had the misfortune of clashing with her fleet on many occasions. We've lost more ships to her waves and gales than to honest warfare. The only way this attack stands any chance of success is if you stop her.

Amminus is a master weaver. His blankets are warm and his baskets sturdy. He's proud of what his hands create. \n\nI, however, am known for assisting in gardens. My nimble fingers can still pluck weeds.

The serpents Vinsha corrupts are rather rare—each egg is precious. They must be retrieved and cleansed of her unnatural influence, if it is possible. I'll tend to that once you return the eggs to the broker.

Aye. Taleria has split her fleet into small attack groups to hit as many shipping lanes as she can. We've tried to catch them out in smaller numbers, but their groups maneuver in perfect concert with each other.

Our flotilla will do its best to draw the Sea Elves' attention, but you should expect scores of pirates to stand between you and the Fleet Queen. They'll also have trained sea beasts at their beck and call. Victory will be hard won.

Yes, well … they're quite large and rather dangerous. Otherwise I would simply go collect a sample for myself. But I've been told there are plenty of adventurers on High Isle willing to assist my research by facing angry Hadolids for coin.
Of course. It's been a pleasure to travel with you since that day at the tourney, but we haven't had much of a chance to chat about my past. \n\nWhat would you like to know?

As much as I can, but they're often out of town on business trips. We're always together for holidays like New Life, though.\n\nThey were in Summerset when we won the tourney. That's why they weren't at my knighting ceremony.

Since I was old enough to hold a branch and pretend to fight Daedra? My parents supported me all the way and set about making sure I got what I needed.\n\nSo that's why Aurelia and I grew up together. As almost-but-very-much-not sisters.

You want me to say, "Oh yeah! Of course!" and all that, but the truth is, I just don't know. I've got a problem, chum. A big one. I want to stop. I need to stop, obviously. But I don't think I can do it alone.\n\nI'll find the help I need. Promise.

No idea. But I could see her inside you while the captain was … at the helm, as it were. She was giving me … him … the puppy-dog eyes. Very disconcerting.\n\nAnyway, to the lighthouse! It's clear this is somehow tied to the All Flags Navy.

The runic prison they put me in failed, and I wriggled out when they weren't looking. It's awful—the runes siphon life force from the victims. The pain is excruciating.\n\nI tried to get my friends out, but I couldn't. So I went for help.

The gaming hall provides a wealth of opportunities for Roisters Club members. Why not look around and familiarize yourself with them?\n\nBrahgas can make the proper introductions. Speak with Sorinne, too. She's another protege of mine.

As in all things, the best way to improve is through doing! Set out and find new opponents. Win or lose, your skills will grow and your strategies will sharpen.\n\nOnce you establish yourself in the beginner's circuit, return to me for a reward!
What I do with my daughter is none of your concern. \n\nThat being said, she did defeat the Hadolids. There may be a place for her here in Brokerock. I'll speak to her.

Now that we've met Julles and Galedra, I think he acted out of character with Aurelia. He must have wanted the signet ring badly. \n\nHe's nervous, maybe not as careful? I … I truly wish I hadn't given that thing to Aurelia.

I never said that. But if that's what she wants … we'll talk. As a family. Until my wife returns, Meryline and I will just be happy we're alive.\n\nI give you my word that I'll hear her out. I won't break an oath like that.

Well, when I gave it to her my feelings towards her were very different. I thought … I thought I loved her. \n\nI assumed Aurelia would realize what the ring meant to me … and so in turn she'd understand what she meant to me.
That's my job.\n\nMeryline is excited to talk to you. I suggest you say your farewells before you head back out to your … adventuring.
Oh, Guiffa? Just a lover's spat. She loves making fun of my nose ring and I love losing money to her … apparently. Match made in Aetherius.

It has to be. A priest of Z'en blessed me. It's the festival of Z'en's generosity. And now I find a ray of light pointing out where some amazing treasure is hidden? \n\nThis has to be a sign of Z'en's favor. What else could it be?

Usually? No, no. Most players are in it for the joy of competition. But you know what they say—if there's an uncertain outcome, someone's got gold on it.\n\nI play a lot of unsanctioned matches. Putting skin in the game keeps things fresh.

Aye. That big building there.\n\nUsed to be a House Mornard villa, believe it or not. House Dufort seized it during the transition of the duchy, but got tired of paying for the upkeep. The Duchess sold the place to Razhamad about a year ago.
Yeah. A chapter is like a team of sorts. The Gonfalon Chapter meets here.\n\nBut we're wandering into the weeds a bit. Focus on the game, first. We'll discuss the rest later.

Well, we drink in there too.\n\nPeople need a place to relax, chum. The Ancient Anchor's fine for sailors on shore leave, but people looking for a really good time always come here. Plus, it serves as our Tribute chapter seat.
Ha! Y'ffre's bones, an introduction would be nice, wouldn't it?\n\nCall me Brahgas. Professional gambler and semi-professional everything else. Aside from sailor, of course. I hate the water.
The suggestion to give the festival a chance was more than enough aid for me. I hope there are always beetles in the dirt under your feet.

I've heard of the festivals taking place. But would a festival for Zenithar be welcoming toward beggars? Or will the merchants there be generous? \n\nYes. I think I will try. If nothing else, I can always follow another road out of the city.
I tried cities. They did not suit me. My scales need the wind of the countryside. \n\nSo I wander. My scales are happy. My feet are tired. Only my stomach longs for more.

The better question would be, "What made you leave Valenwood?" The answer, my friend, is debt collectors. Vigorous ones.\n\nOnce I save up enough I might go back. But I'm in no hurry. When a stiff breeze comes through, the Systres are really beautiful.

Yes, the Roister's Club.\n\nIt is a far-reaching organization that administrates all aspects of Tales of Tribute. They organize tournaments, publish new rules, sponsor chapters, and most importantly, they manufacture the cards themselves.
Anyone with a pair of Tribute decks, a game-baron sponsorship, and a thirst for competition, yes!\n\nComplete your training, and it will be my honor to welcome you into the club.
Kiv and I have kinda been … flirting with the idea of doing business for a while. And then I get a letter from him saying he's working with the Veloise Mercantile. So I say, sign me up!
Moving High Isle silks over here on the continent. Very desirable among some of my clientele. But from what I'm hearing now, this was all just a con.

Ah, that's the pits. Look, I have me own family's good name to protect. I was gonna meet him in the basement here. Entrance is around the side.\n\nWhy don't you and your—oof—imposing friend here go chat with him?
Each story will mention a cardinal direction. Use those, along with the order of the tablets, to help you succeed.
