We must warn Lord Bacaro of the danger. If we can't trust House Dufort's knights, we'll need whatever troops House Volorus and the Society of the Steadfast can scrape up.\n\nLord Bacaro is supposed to meet me at Mandrake Manor. I'll see you there.

Well, I had to stop studying alchemy because I lost my job. What better way to punish him than to try out one of my concoctions?\n\nIt's a transformative admixture that … should turn him into a skeever for a few days.

I'm sure I did the measurements right. It'll last for a week at most. Maybe a month. \n\nLook, it's a bit experimental but my instructor was really pleased. And best of all, it's applied to the skin. So it has more uses than a drinkable concoction.

Well, Kiv made me feel quite foolish. But I'm not actually angry with him. I want to cherish the time I had with the rogue. \n\nMara protect a loving heart from such mistakes. I propose to make arrangements to have Kiv taken to a remote monastery.

Oh, the Brothers of the Bond are a strict order. Kiv won't be able to leave for one full year. It's my hope that he will learn from their philosophy. \n\nAlso they are a strictly celibate group. I believe that will help him clear his mind.
Normally, that'd be great. But talking to the other two, it sounds like Kiv would just talk his way outta jail.
Listen, Galedra there is a hardcore cynic. You can tell from just a few moments talking to her. And even she fell for him. \n\nAs for me and Julles, we're just emotional men. What can I say?

Just looking at it … my emotions have me all tangled up. Aurelia knew me better than anyone in the whole world when I gave her this ring. \n\nBut she didn't know what the ring meant. She never really understood it. Or me.
The only thing I want in the whole of Tamriel right now is to see my parents.\n\nI need to tell them what happened. Leave this with them for safekeeping. Maybe get a hug from my mom.

Aye. Her magic is the only explanation I can muster for how well coordinated her fleet has been over great distances. How she came to acquire such a power is anyone's guess, but it must have been a recent development.

It would make patrolling the Systres much easier if they could, but I doubt there are any among them with a fraction of Taleria's power.\n\nStill, once we've claimed this island and conducted a search, maybe we'll learn a few of her tricks.

I aim to sink as many as I can, but I imagine those who manage to escape will sail home to Pyandonea, or search for safer waters to prey upon. Either way, the Dreadsail fleet will be a thing of the past.

The land the Sea Elves occupy when they aren't plaguing ours. Never seen it myself. No sailor has, except the Sea Elves themselves. Maybe one day there'll be a navy up to the task of taking the fight to them for a change. Not mine though.

A soldier of the Daggerfall Covenant. A bit gruff, as you'd expect from a veteran. But I've seen how tenacious he is. I doubt he'll sleep until he learns the cause of the malady.\n\nJust don't take his tone personally. He's like that to everyone.

Brahgas should be returning any minute, but I know he'll be ready. Sorinne though? Possibly less so.\n\nI hate to think that she'd withdraw at this point. Advancing in the tournament is hard enough as it is. Without her, it's unlikely.

Yesterday a letter arrived addressed to her. Upon reading it, she seemed troubled and would not say why. The fact that it arrived the day before the tournament is suspicious enough.\n\nPerhaps you could speak to her? Sorinne clearly likes you.
Oh, I know. He told me. Repeatedly! We're lucky to know him. All of us.

Difficult, at first. But I adore Razhamad. Even when I told him the really difficult stories—the lowest lows—he never once sneered, or laughed, or judged.\n\nI know I can rely on him in the future when the stars aren't quite so bright.

Some backwater called Northsalt. Never heard of it before. These merchants blow where the winds take them, you know?\n\nHey, be careful in Rivenspire. I've heard dark shadows hang over that part of the world.

Well, well. No fussing about, I like it. That gold will take care of my problem quick enough.\n\nCaptain Marso sailed for Rivenspire. He was putting in at Northpoint, but he mentioned they were headed for a little village just outside the city.

No, but I'm not surprised. He and the Steadfast don't have a standing army. I imagine he's still at his manor, sending missives across High Isle in an attempt to recruit knights willing to aid us.\n\nGo tell him he can stop. The threat is over for now.
Two rooms with locked exits. Each room swarms with hideous creatures ready to destroy you.\n\nFight through the hordes, then pull the levers to unlock the doors. Only then may you escape.

That's a good question. Lots. And also, not enough. \n\nI'm on vacation, me. Got through three … four … five? Five drinks. If you don't count the flask of wine from that wine shop. But it was a sample. Terrible sweet it was.

Of course. All Flags Castle must be half in ruins after what I can only imagine was a fierce and costly battle. I'll get with Lady Arabelle and we'll thank the delegates for their patience. \n\nI do believe another celebration is in order, though.

There can only be one winner in this tournament.\n\nPrevious matches allowed Brahgas, Sorinne, and yourself to advance as club members. The final challenges in this tournament can only crown one winner. Everyone will be aiming for the title.

If our opponents of the rival chapter are defeated, you will have to face any remaining player who has yet to be eliminated. Gonfalon Chapter members included.\n\nWith how well you three have played thus far … I just hope you're prepared.

Yes, I have watched them tearing down walls across the fortress. She was not exaggerating about her plans to gain the shield.\n\nThe only way to honorably defeat her is to pass the Trials of Worth. So hurry! Our time slips away.

The name's Ember. Well, technically it's a nickname, but it's all I use. I'm Magister Irin's apprentice. I think he regrets taking me on sometimes, but he's got a big heart. He saw that I had no formal training and told me to come here to learn.

This is Tor Draioch. There's a big wizard's tower, you can't miss it. I've been living there with Magister Irin plus a few people who keep up the grounds and the tower itself. All of whom have been affected by my spell, I'd guess.
I made it clear to her that I would not bend to her demands. I can make it clear again if I need to.
Yes, my friend! I … I caught that. Hoo, what a day.\n\nYou know what, I joke? But I'm glad they're going home. Marso is a good man. And I imagine they'll want to talk to the Knight Commander.

Sadly, no. She will never sail again. But several Ascendant Order vessels were abandoned after the fight at All Flags Islet. Since the Order wrecked my ship, I hope to claim one of theirs for compensation.
I'm not going anywhere until High King Emeric finishes up what he came here to do. That's fine with me, though. It'll give me time to sign on a crew and put Nereid's Song in proper shape.

Long sunny days and tender nights filled with song, drink, and love, or so Za'ji hopes! Since Queen Ayrenn has no one else to look after her in these islands, Za'ji hereby appoints himself the task of catering to her every need.

That depends on Queen Ayrenn. We're staying in Gonfalon Bay as long as she is, but that suits me fine. We've got a new ship and a new crew to break in. \n\nAnd I'll be keeping an eye on Za'ji. As always.

If you don't mind, I'd rather not recall that dreadful experience. You have no idea what it's like to have a foul-mouthed, libidinous sea captain inside your head.\n\nAlthough, I must say the feelings he left me with were rather … enticing.

What! Well, yes. Everyone does. She's a fine and noble woman! Quite personable … when she isn't calling for tea or ordering me to do some fool thing or other.\n\nBut I do not appreciate what you are implying, my friend.
I do. Let's go see those crazy kids in Gonfalon Bay. Our friendship has withstood some rocky seas, the last few days. \n\nBut it will make me happy to see her finally at ease.
Where better to find a ship then in Gonfalon Bay? I'll get passage on one of them. Until then, I'm helping people.

Exceedingly well. With the trials out of the way, the jousting and revelry has been some of the best we've ever seen. \n\nI rarely get a chance to enjoy much of it, but Aurelia has encouraged me to live a little.
Oh, very good! Tanillin and Ulgonash said my diplomacy was so strong they didn't need to be diplomacized any more. They told me I could go commit diplomacy on new people and make more friends!

Wherever I please! That's the joy of the sailing life. We have a few jobs lined up. Sailors must eat, after all. But I think we can afford some shore leave.\n\nAnd Queen Ayrenn asked to talk later. I sense more dangerous cargo in the near future.

Returning to normal, thanks to you. The symptoms of Viralaine's experiments have faded from our patients. Now they can focus on the conditions that originally brought them to me.\n\nThat will be its own struggle. But one we're trained for.

More or less. Nature has a way of doing the unexpected, but that's part of its grandeur. The spirit of the grove has become more of a partner than a tool, and I am glad of that. You helped make that possible. The circle will never forget that.

Of course! Some people seem skeptical that the same person who rescued the alliance leaders and killed the Ascendant Magus also chased down sheep magicked to look like people. But that's part of the fun!\n\nNow go celebrate! You've earned it.
I did. The Order of the Albatross welcomed her home. She's been interred in a crypt reserved for knights that died on errantry. \n\nI've visited her a few times. She … she has a nice spot.

I previously refrained from asking you to attack Amunara. It seemed that defeating her by the Trials of Worth was the more honorable path.\n\nBut she's bound me, torn at my home, and now summoned me like a common specter. I shall refrain no longer.

Who knows what dangers lurk in this old ruin? And Amunara refuses to deal with this trial nonsense. The mercenaries will help me break through into the Shield Hall.\n\nLook, be reasonable. Move on and no one will know. Now, this one has work to do.

Yes, but not in some plain manner. We can use Amunara's own censer to bind her. As you carried it, the device will have reattuned for living energies. \n\nNext time we meet her, light the incense then toss it at her. It will bind her as she trapped me.

In her recklessness, Amunara buried the door to the third trial under rubble. But I know a hidden route.\n\nFirst, you'll need the key. I can mark on your map where to find it in the library. We'll reconvene there. After I've pulled myself together.

The Trial of Constitution will test your hardiness in one of the castle's old training grounds. You can expect to be assailed by dangerous traps and snares.\n\nNo challenger has completed this trial since I walked among the living.

Oh. May I see? Ah, yes. It's … from Lady Garick. The love of my life. She had to leave to fight a war. Said I could not join her in that war because I was the only one she trusted to guard the shield. \n\nThis … should have stayed under the rug.
Similar to the Trial of Perseverance, the door to the exit is locked, but a device exists to open it. Reaching both the device and the door is where the difficulty lies.

A magnificent knight. An incredible sailor. She was unrelenting, intelligent, and kind. Serving under her in the Order of the Sacred Shield, even for a millennium, would be an unsatisfying amount of time.
I'm sure that censer won't hold her forever. Once she's free, she'll likely be quite angry. I suggest you leave this place before that happens, champion.

Marso and I have been talking with mother. We also paid a visit to Lord and Lady Veloise. \n\nDon't give me that look over their shoulder, Izzy. Yes, I've been talking to your parents. It's all settled.

I owned up to my folly with the signet ring. Izzy's parents were very kind, especially after we explained all we did to resolve things.\n\nWe also wanted their permission. Marso insisted if I was to sail with him, they had to know.

Yes. I saw his power firsthand at Castle Navire. And Valessea explained that he somehow drew power from the volcanic vents that permeate the islands. A reckless use of magic, with little regard for consequences.\n\nWhere did he learn that, I wonder.

No. The reagents can't stand up to the heat for very long. Each application provides only an infinitesimal amount of details.\n\nI will need someone to repeat the procedure every few days until the available knowledge has been exhausted.

Yes! And what fragrant challenges they are! Each day, Kishka sets new tasks for rank and renown.\n\nOne will pit you against the common folk of Tamriel. The other will set you against card-playing adventurers like yourself.

Ha! You would fill your purse with heaps of tiny baubles? No, walker! As this one said, you can win one match for a tiny reward or keep playing for a bigger prize!\n\nSimple, yes? The more you play, the sweeter the reward!

I offer only two challenges per day, but you can earn sweeter prizes by winning multiple matches. Small rewards for a single win, fine prizes for two, and a grand bounty for three!\n\nKishka will also make sure your rank soars if you participate.

Well, when you possess an intellect like mine, the outcomes are always crystal clear. Victory is a simple matter of planning and tactical precision. Not that a protege of Razhamad would know anything about that.
I was unfairly exiled by others of my class. They stripped me of my wealth, my business, everything! I must return and exact my revenge!\n\nIf only this oaf would get out of my way!

We safely traversed the ocean on a seaworthy vessel on the way to Amenos. I see no reason why we can't leave via the same method. \n\nAnd better yet, it's safer than the foolhardy plan my companion is stubbornly arguing for!

No, I love it here. I'm going to spend the rest of my life basking in the paradise that is Amenos. \n\nOf course I want off this inhospitable sand bar! I don't deserve this! And I don't deserve to suffer this fool. He thinks we can sail to freedom!

I'm trying to understand this device the Dreadsails looted. It's full of latent energy, but I can't tune it properly. Too much interference around the island.\n\nIt's the Fleet Queen's runes. I'd like you to find and destroy them.

Of course I disagree! I suggested that we just capture one of their ships, sneak aboard as guards or something, but no. Apparently, that is stupid and would never work. \n\nSo we should just build our own raft instead! That will work.

In the adjacent caverns. I'm not sure where—precisely—but, I assure you they are there.\n\nI'm sorry I can't be more help in this regard. Our hosts don't allow us free reign of their home. For good reason.

I am the mage-navigator of the Fickle Maiden, and a man with an eye for less mundane treasures. I was intrigued by the Fleet Queen's invitation, because she claims to have a secret weapon that will make her the uncontested ruler of the Systres.

It appears Dwarven and unusually simple for their work. It seems to react to magical energies, but the interference from Taleria's runes make its output too chaotic for me to understand.\n\nThose runes must be destroyed if I'm to learn more.

I already located and destroyed two. When I did, the tonal output of this device increased, but I sense the presence of more interference coming from outside this chamber. I'd wager there are about five more runes, if they are of similar potency.
I don't know! That's what's so interesting!\n\nI'm sure it's perfectly safe. Dwarves are meticulous artisans.

Then who would record the results? You? I have a very specific process. Better I observe.\n\nLook, I'm sure I could convince one of these drunken louts to stand in, but we've come this far together. Why not be a part of the discovery?

Other patients have fevers and fits of shaking. Some become confused, believing themselves back on the battlefield. I had to subdue a Dark Elf who turned on a mender.\n\nSeeing the others like that? I hope that's not where I'm headed.

Of course.\n\nThe Roister's Club ranking lists allow players to track their mastery of the game and find players of comparable skill. As always, stiff competition and fair play are the club's greatest priorities!

By playing Tribute, of course! You can challenge other adventurers like yourself, or face off against less-dangerous players in taverns and clubs the world over. \n\nKishka's challenges provide rank bonuses as well, so don't pass them up!

Ah, that is where the tournaments come in.\n\nOnce you reach the highest echelons of your current rank, you can compete in that tier's tournament to advance to the next level. Luckily, the Novice Tournament will begin soon. So, start winning matches!

No, but that's why I invited the Khajiit on our venture. He was a sailor, I think. I might be confused on that front. I thought he'd weigh in on my side, but he's been almost silent. \n\nStill, I know I'm right. My plan is more feasible than hers.

I don't know if we'll ever agree. But I can't put my plan into action on my own. Of course it's my luck that the only people who listen to me have wool for brains. \n\nStill, I'm not dying here. I will leave Amenos, even if I have to do it alone.

Don't get me wrong. Lady A is great and she pays well. But I need to draw the line at acting respectable. Of being all heroic.\n\nI'm a thief! I've got an image to think of! But I'll never say never. Do that and fate intervenes.

I'm certainly going to try. We've all accomplished too much to let the talks just fade away like mist in the morning sun. You showed them they can work together. We can build upon that. Provided I can get them to stay until we're ready to begin.

I must assume so. Why else would they be here? They are honorable leaders, despite our differences and the terrible war we're engaged in. \n\nI believe they want what is best for their realms as well as mine. Beyond that, we shall have to wait and see.

Mostly. But he wasn't with us on Amenos or at All Flags Castle. He didn't fight side-by-side with the Lion and the Eagle. My father doesn't expect much from these talks. I'm not so sure.


If the talks do take place, I'd love to surprise him.
It's a particularly treacherous route through the Systres Archipelago. Anything larger than a skiff that gets pulled in by the currents usually winds up running aground on the shoals. Violently.

I'm afraid I do. If I decide to ignore them and hold my ground, there's no promise Ayrenn and Jorunn can do the same. Peace is only possible when everyone sees there's no more to be gained from war.\n\nStill, if the others are willing to try, so am I.

The high king says he does not hold me responsible for Damard's misdeeds. But the ships that attacked All Flags Castle were built in Dufort yards, and many of our knights fought under Ascendant helms.\n\nOur honor is irreparably stained.

No! That's impossible! You must have hidden some cards or … is there a mirror behind me? You're up to something. You have to be! I can't lose. I cannot!\n\nDo you know how many times I've won with these strategies? A hundred times. A thousand times!
I …. Get out of my sight! I have a long and damning letter to write!\n\nThe Roister's Club will … you'll be hearing from them soon! Now, begone!
The dungy Sea Elves locked the Prowler's wheel. Tough to tell at this distance, but the chain links seem too thick to break. We need a key.
The Sea Elf captain's quarters is my best guess. Check there. Before you blow up the ship—in case that part was not obvious.\n\nI have to get back to Adwig. Good luck!
Everybody in town! Sailors, merchants, fishmongers, dockworkers, beggars, anyone I could catch! People like you when you buy them drinks. Although I'm not really sure how that helps Ebonheart Pact.

My work here is just beginning. My body's been healed for some time now, I guess. But now I think something in my spirit needed to be here too, helping others. \n\nIs it strange to say I don't really want to leave?

I must administer more of your antidote to everyone suffering from Viralaine's so-called treatments. And once his evil work is undone, well … there are still the wounds of war to deal with.\n\nI hope to help our patients with those, too.

I pray that Roslenn can help me find a cure for my disease. I'm willing to stay as long as it takes and endure any treatment. Surely it can't be worse than what I've already survived.\n\nAt the end of it, I will finally be free.

Continue to challenge others. Complete Kishka's challenges, and more importantly see if you can find Tribute cards to improve your own.\n\nYou're an intermediate player now — challenge some others of the same rank. You might learn a thing or two.

Thanks to you, it is! Last time, you helped make the Cultural Exchange glorious success. So much success, King Jorunn said we didn't need to send culture to High Isle.\n\nThen I told him you might be here to help again. He said I could come!
Rigurt leads Glorious Expedition of Nord Cultural Exchange. I travel to many lands to explain excellence of Nord culture with great forcefulness!

Hire a crew and refit here in Gonfalon Bay. I do not know how long Prince Irnskar plans to stay, but it would be my honor to return him safely home when the time comes.\n\nUntil then, I promised Lady Arabelle I would help protect all the delegates.
Must I spell it out?\n\nBrahgas owes Master Fels a magister's ransom in gold. We've given him ample opportunities to repay his debt, but the hole he digs grows deeper still.

Lady Arabelle insisted and the duchess doesn't seem opposed. Still haven't decided whether to rename her. There's a lot of luck tied up in a ship's name.\n\nOh, and while I'm here I agreed to protect the delegates. I could use the extra gold.

That is a task better left in Caska's claws. Who will look after Queen Ayrenn, if not Za'ji? And Lady Arabelle insisted we help guard the delegates anyway. So what is this one to do?\n\nZa'ji can only hope his devotion is rewarded!
Oh, it's not a matter of if he pays. It's a matter of when he pays, and with what.\n\nAnd if he refuses? Well, we have ways of dealing with those who neglect their obligations.

Sure—you're helping me track down my friends that I had growing up in Skywatch. They all disappeared one day and I had no idea what happened to them until you and I found Jhaka. But Silverslip and Song are still out there somewhere.

He said that a mercenary group grabbed him and the others, and he remembered the symbol on their armor. That's how he tracked down our next lead. He also said something about remembering Silverslip acting strange, but wasn't sure why.

There are other mages with more experience, such as Vanus Galerion or … anyone! They would be better negotiators. \n\nAh. That's the point, isn't it? My role here isn't to negotiate. It's to speak honestly and keep an open mind. That I can do.

Not right now. The captains and Caska have agreed to help guard the delegates, but the rest is all paperwork and supervision. When the peace talks get underway, I'll send for you. If you're still interested in helping, of course.\n\nNo pressure, dear.

Yeah. And that overconfidence is going to be what puts him in the losers' circle.\n\nI'm going to win. Have you seen how well I've been playing? I'm on the roll of the era. I'm going to win, and all my problems? Gone. Poof. Like smoke on the wind.
That's not going to happen!\n\nJust … just worry about yourself, all right?

I still have a few last things to take care of on All Flags Islet before the peace talks can proceed. After that, who can say? I go where I'm needed, and Stibbons follows faithfully in my wake. Someone must carry my personals, after all.

That goes without saying. I am Tamriel's most celebrated treasure hunter and author, after all.\n\nI may stick around for the peace talks. Or I heard about some strange happenings in the Telvanni Peninsula. Or Hammerfell. I haven't been there in ages.

Nothing too exciting. I have lists to make, crates to pack … and Lady Laurent's collection of combs, brushes, and Reach fetishes won't sort themselves.\n\nI'm sure we'll see you again. M'lady appreciates your help, even if she doesn't say so.

After the … you saw—? Well, nothing happened. Not really. Nothing I want to discuss, anyway. Lady Laurent wasn't herself. She was still caught up in the stifled emotions of a sea captain who had been alone for—\n\nMust we talk about this?

No, not yet. It's like the very rock refuses to talk to us, and we're the Stonelore Druids! I've been busy getting the grove settled, but I think I'll offer to help with the investigation into the lava vents and the volcano. It's the least I can do.

Don't worry about that. I need you to focus on beating Brahgas. Lose against him and this plan falls apart regardless.\n\nI trust you. You're the best the chapter has to offer. Do what you know how to do and win. I'll handle the rest.

I know we will. Well, you will. This burden is on your shoulders.\n\nThe fact is, you've helped each and every one of us. Especially me. Just … regardless of what happens, it won't be your fault, all right? Do your best. That's enough.

Me? I'm going to enjoy myself. Maybe try some new foods. It's nice being at a party and not having to worry about being called on to perform.\n\nAfter that? I'm going to battle monsters. Solve real problems. Like you.

Yes! I started by singing rats off of a galley. It's a small start, but now folks are coming to me with their problems!\n\nI'm making a name for myself. It might not be much—yet—but I crafted it myself. And it's my name, not my father's.
I'm waiting for my squire to orient me and point me in the direction of more adventure. \n\nOh, I can regale you with the tales of my travels while we wait!

My master will believe anyone who says they have a quest for him. I know, I've seen it happen more than once. I just didn't want to be the person to lie to him. \n\nIt worked though, we raced off to find our … ugh, glory.
See? That there's that swagger I saw during our first match. You've got this well in hand.\n\nKeep that confidence and don't hold back. Use everything you've learned and beat this bastard.

You are right. And for that, you have my deepest apologies. In my rush to rescue one of my students, I left another exposed to … well, all of this.\n\nYou have done nothing but good since you joined the chapter. You deserve better.

I hand over the keys to my gaming hall to Teliv, along with all the hall's assets. He would dissolve the chapter, no doubt. The revels would come to an end.\n\nI hope that the regulars and the staff would still be well-served, but nothing is certain.

Brahgas would become a member of Teliv's house. Against his will.\n\nRegardless of their agreements with the Argonians, the Dark Elves have never been self-conscious about slavery. Service in chains … that's what Brahgas is bound for.

Of course!\n\nThe tournaments provided the lift you needed to reach master status, but you are still far from the summit. Searching for new cards, playing ranked matches with high-level players … maybe even seeking the Founders.

Yes. The creators of the game and founding members of the Roister's Club.\n\nThey keep their identities hidden. Even we masters know precious little about how Tales of Tribute came to be. No one I know has ever met a Founder, but we know they exist.

You may already be familiar with them, but many adventurers, like yourself, have begun challenging each other for rank and renown. These matches lack the structure of our recent tournaments, but the rewards seem well-worth the effort!

I believe it is time to upgrade the gaming hall, don't you? With one of our members being the newest Tribute Champion, players have started flocking to our club.\n\nThis means coin. So much coin! We can finally afford some assistants for Gelekh!

I received an unsigned letter months ago. It stated, "They walk in the city of light amid the horrors of azure doom." It refers to a Founder, I think, but I am quite comfortable here—far from any doom, azure or otherwise.\n\nI hope that is helpful.

Well, according to some of the highest tier players, if you manage to find a Founder, you can challenge them to a game of Tribute. Those who win gain a fabulous prize.\n\nI cannot say for sure if that part is true, but it could be worth investigating.

When you play games of luck and skill, you meet many people. Some are prudent. Some are not. Unfortunately, the imprudent players tend to remain that way. Unless they seek help.\n\nIf Brahgas finds help, he may turn things around. I hope he does.

That is up to them. Well, except for Brahgas. I imagine you spoke with him.\n\nI remain … cross, but he is still my friend. I hope that revoking his membership will finally set him on the right path. I wish I were more optimistic.

No rest for me! It's right back to ranked matches!\n\nMight try out a new deck—test some unconventional strategies I've been cooking up. I did well in the tournaments, no question. But I know I can do better.

A mutual friend reached out a while ago. She said Raenobi doubled down on her skooma operation after losing to us … to me. Apparently a deal went poorly and she just vanished. No one's heard from her.\n\nPart of me wants to look for her. Even now.

A Founder? No, never. I did hear a crazy story about a card-playing ghost, though.\n\nProbably guar dung, honestly, but given the state of the world nowadays, I'd believe just about any crazy story you told me.

Razhamad did the right thing. A big part of overcoming an issue like Brahgas's is managing access to the games. At least, that's what I've heard.\n\nI started talking to a scholar about addiction. Priests too. I'm learning a lot!

I absolutely have. And I have all of you to thank. You, Brahgas, Razhamad …. You're my family now. No more mind games or temptations—just honest friendship.\n\nI know I've said it a million times, but thank you. Seriously.

Don't be. Raenobi was … honestly, I don't know what she was to me. A friend. An enemy. A lover. An abuser. It's just … I don't think I'll ever really untangle it.\n\nWhatever the case, I'm better without her. It's a hard lesson I'm still learning.

I heard she haunts some cabin in the deepest groves of Grahtwood.\n\nI've never had a chance to explore those woods, but if I do? You bet your last drake I'm going to find this ghost and wreck her deck!

According to the rumor, this ghost has a full set of Tribute cards. And she plays like … like some kind of fortune teller-wizard.\n\nI've thought about trying to find her more than once, but knowing my luck, she'd probably possess me or something.

Possibly. When ships fail to make port, it's only natural to wonder if they were damaged or blown off course by a storm. The lighthouse keeper has a perfect view of the approach to Gonfalon Bay. If my ships were out there, she might have seen them.

Eh. Been better. Been worse, too. The important thing is that I'm free. Broke. Very broke, in fact. But free all the same!\n\nGelekh offered me room and board as long as I pitch in. Sweeping up. Washing the dishes, that sort of thing. It's been nice.
Not a peep. I don't usually stand for threats, but when Teliv learned about how you make your livelihood, well, I think that closed the book on his quarrels with me.\n\nSo, again, thanks for that.

Founders? Really leaping into this master thing with both feet, eh?\n\nCan't say for sure, but I think I might have met one a few months back—up in Rivenspire. She was an Orc, but a real spooky sort. Gray skin. Red eyes. See a lot of that out there.

Stranger things have happened. My uncle used to dance naked through the grahts hunting shalks with a deer-antler. Now he sells pottery in Pellitine. Things change.\n\nAs much as I complain about it, I do love this city. So, yeah. It might just stick.

Oh sure! My grandmother taught me all the family recipes. It's just been so long, I guess I just forgot about it.\n\nHey! I like this idea! I'll put together a new menu for the club. Ha! I can't wait to see Gelekh's face when I share the news!

Just between you and me? Not enough! I mean, don't get me wrong, Gelekh runs a tight ship, but the food here is just …. There are opportunities for improvement, let's put it that way.\n\nCome to think of it, I'm something of a chef myself ….
We'll see him at competitions. Well, maybe you will. But I think he's smart enough to avoid another bet against the Gonfalon Chapter!

Like a three-legged mule! She gave me the worst thrashing of my life.\n\nWhen we parted company, she mentioned something about meeting her friends at a castle nearby. Can't remember the name … I think it had a bird in it? Sorry, that's all I've got.

I know she was!\n\nWe met on the road, late at night. I thought she meant to eat me at first, but then I noticed a pair of Tribute decks peeking out of her bodice. Naturally, I challenged her to a match. Went about as well as you might expect.
Founders? You may have noticed we don't serve a lot of elite clientele here. If a Founder came rambling through, I think they'd stick out like a broken tusk.\n\nI do hear rumors now and then, though.

Oh sure. Heard one about the Duchess that'll knock you flat on your—oh, you mean about more Founders.\n\nSome Nord told me about a blind Tribute player in Eastmarch. Said he tried to cheat, but the guy knew somehow. Witchcraft, I wager. Be careful.

An Imperial swung through a few weeks back. One of those sandy types who like digging for old teacups and such. He told me about a card-playing scholar he met in Craglorn—weird lady rooting around in ruins for ancient games.\n\nMight be worth a look.

My apologies, it was never my intention to threaten. I merely wanted to stress the imminent danger you and your friends were putting yourselves in by getting closer to the Emerald Eye. People who cross this family die.
Are you going to lecture me, Langley LeTarte, about knightly behavior? I think not!\n\nI hold no grudge towards Isobel, but this is a competition, not a garden party. My second and I were here first.

If you look at it from a certain perspective, I suppose so. It was required until the spirit bonded with the land. And once that occurred, there was no reason to eliminate the bindings.\n\nBut if the Evergrowth suffers, so does the grove.

I would lose the advantage of having gotten here first. I see no reason to hinder my trial just because you think it would be nice of me to do so. Now run along, I've work to do. \n\nBerjo, put some muscle behind that swing!

We know frustratingly little about the organization itself. They're powerful, wealthy, and they have a hand in a great many illicit activities. There are many rumors about how they came to power, but most prevalent among them revolves around a relic.

Yes, one possibly magical in nature. That's what concerns the king the most. Not only do they have a great deal of unchecked power, but if the means by which they accumulated it is based in rituals and dark magicks, then they may be harder to quell.

Yes, yes! One day Rigurt was drinking in the Skald-King's hall and loudly explaining all the good things people don't know about Nords. King Jorunn said he knew that already and I should go tell somebody else.\n\nSo I did!

I actually requested the honor. Rayan and I belong to the Order of the Albatross. Every knight bearing our crest has a song in their heart and a story on their lips.\n\nBut a true knight is not content to retell the tales of others.

I have the utmost faith in young Audrine. What I do not trust is the word of a capricious nature spirit.\n\nGo with Audrine. Get us proof that a druid is responsible for the corruption. Then we will take every action necessary to solve the problem.

Only rumors. Some told me all the prisoners brought here have to fight each other. The jailers promise the last one standing will go free. But they bring people over all the time, so no one ever wins.\n\nI also heard a stranger story.
I met a Dark Elf in the stockade who claimed to have once served a fancy Breton family. After I gave him half my bread, he told me that his master often mentioned going on hunting trips to Whalefall.
Maybe the game at Whalefall isn't for the prisoners. Maybe it's for rich highborn monsters to hunt down desperate people.\n\nWhen you have enough gold, you can do pretty much whatever you want.
I am. Sir Le Fleury was very impressed with my tale. As he put it, who am I to stand in the way of the unstoppable Dame Madach?\n\nI'm still not used to the title, but I'll get there.

I think I'll spend some time working with the knights at Castle Navire. Get my sea legs under me, so to speak. The knight commander is already muttering about having me take on a squire. \n\nSo, I expect it'll be back into the breach soon enough!

There are strange texts about its origin passed down through generations, but even still, it's hard to know anything for sure. All I know is that it killed my sister, and our mother before her, and it will eventually kill Song if you don't save her.

It's just too much for their bodies to handle. Those who are willing, like my sister, can withstand the rituals for years before succumbing. But the end result is always the same. The visions rob them of their light and vitality until they are spent.

There is a ritual. I've never seen one take place, but I've heard that the relic has enough power to take over the body of the vessel. During that process, a vision is given to the vessel.\n\nMy sister made me a very rich man with such visions.

I don't know all the details, but from what I've been taught, the Evergrowth resides in the Undergrove. The wards connect it to the grove but also bind it. \n\nWe need to talk to the archdruid. She's usually in the northern grove this time of day.

Whoever scrawled this did so in haste. They made an obvious mistake in the middle verse. It should say restore, but the author wrote down remove.\n\nThat alone would have disastrous effects when the ritual was performed.

Hmm. I'll free <<1>> if we catch the criminal who refined the moon-sugar. There's a smuggler named <<2>> who hangs around the Ancient Anchor. We're sure he deals in skooma, but we haven't been able to prove it.\n\nHe's the criminal I really want.

The Allwither moves quickly. Already we can feel ourselves weakening, losing cohesion. The remaining shreds of our bindings have been corrupted and add to our pain.\n\nIf you set us free, we can pull energy from the uncorrupted grove and aid you.

So they told us. But, I've spent my entire life around criminals, thugs, and related scum. And never once have I met someone who said they got set free from Whalefall.\n\nYou'd think I'd have run into someone if it were true.

Oh, like I said, he and I are the swindlers. A little distraction over here, and suddenly your purse is gone. Nothing too bad, you know? But it's not like anyone here on Amenos is the innocent type.\n\nSeems we marked the wrong target this time.

Anton was playing her, of course. I don't even think he wanted something from her. Just a way to pass the time.\n\nBut she actually fell for the old charmer. Once she saw the ruse, Anton's name ends up on the list for Whalefall.

Slipping in and out of the stockade isn't that difficult. And they really don't seem to mind if the prisoners wander off into the jungle.\n\nAs soon as the jailer dragged Anton away, I knew he wouldn't last. I left the stockade to go after him.

Made it with my own two hands! Quite proud of it. I knew I'd never survive the swim, so I scavenged anything that floats. The tides around here tear everything to shreds. So I had plenty of debris to choose from.\n\nI just hope it holds together.

Eh, there was some hue and cry, then finally they caught us. Not the first time Anton and I got arrested. But I guess the lord wanted to make an example.\n\nHe shipped us to Amenos as a message. Don't mess with even the stupid nobles, it says.

Some noble in High Rock. Lord Featherbuns or whatever. They're all the same to me.\n\nWe tried the old pig-in-a-poke on him. Was going fine until his servant called for an appraiser. He was upset to hear the ancient magic orb was a painted goose egg.

Some creatures naturally inhabit underground spaces such as this. As for my corrupted brethren, I suppose the Allwither summoned them to defend it. Much as the Evergrowth has called on us for aid.\n\nNow let us finish this, my friend.

Oh, yes, we mustn't impugn the honor of the great Razhamad! Feh!\n\nI've studied that drunken Redguard's matches. His strategy was slipshod buffoonery, devoid of craft or subtlety. He owes his victories to simple luck more than anything else.

Indeed we will. Or, to be more precise, you will. As I said, I doubt we'll have the pleasure since my companions are more than capable of defeating you themselves.\n\nFarewell, Gonfalon. Enjoy your time as a novice. It won't be ending any time soon.

Just the rumors I've heard in the stockade. No one knows which jailer runs the game. If he chooses you, then it's off to Whalefall. You get set loose and he hunts you down.\n\nApparently he promises freedom if you survive. But I doubt that.

So many years, yes. I know every tree and rock. I've seen every type of person arrive on Amenos thinking they can outsmart it. And do you know what I've learned?\n\nThere's no way off. They all died trying.

The two of us work together to convince people to give us their gold. We're not really the fighting types. I can't see Anton lasting too long alone against hunters.\n\nHow about you come with me? I need an escort. And I'll give you the coin I have.

Ugh, I'm so tired of telling that story. The first thing anyone asks on a prison island is always how did I get here? I'm more than the crime I committed a lifetime ago!\n\nAnyway, I turned an entire Breton town into skeevers. Not a big deal.

Sadly, no. That's the sort of thing I'd learn in a friendly conversation.\n\nI've heard rumors about Hadolid attacks on other islands around here. In the past, I assumed that was just bigotry. Now, I'm not so sure.

Of course you do! I could go on for an eternity about her. I already mentioned her beauty. But she's also so considerate. \n\nOne time, I caught her chewing on a shirt. I felt very cross until I realized she'd done me a favor!

It was my old, worn gardening shirt. I like to give used cloth to the seamstress in town. She makes patches. But she's old and it hurts her to cut cloth. So, I cut it before donating.\n\nPrivette saved me the trouble. She's great!

I command few troops, my friend. I have some household guards at Steadfast Manor, but they wouldn't do much against an Ascendant Order fleet. And the Society of the Steadfast is a humanitarian group, though I'm sure I can muster a few volunteers.

A number of knightly orders have a presence here in the archipelago. How long it will take them to answer my summons—provided they care to—I cannot say.\n\nIf you feel you must rush off, know that I will send help as soon as I can.

I was experimenting with a spell while my mentor, Magister Irin, was away. But the magic went … awry. If it doesn't get dealt with, it's going to spread beyond this area and harm a bunch of innocent people. I can't fix it on my own, so I need help.

Catching the creatures requires a swift hand. But I also need a bit of your own energy to do the ritual. Once you catch something, you'll need to release it toward me so I can draw on both your power and the creature's to communicate with the spirit.

I need to develop a counterspell. But first, the protective wards around the area need to be restored by someone other than myself so I don't taint the magic.\n\nThat's where you come in. Like I said, if you help, I can pay!

I do. But it warms my heart to know she's getting a chance to see the world as your companion. I've known her for almost her whole life, you know. \n\nThe smile she wore the day she won the tourney was a rare treat.

Other than putting my boot squarely in my mouth, you mean? Yes, I'm having a lovely time. Have you had any of those little finger sandwiches? \n\nAnd Jakarn has tried to hit on me no less than three times. I don't have the heart to tell him.
I said I'm tired of talking about it. \n\nBreton town. I show up. Skeevers. Then, Amenos. That's all you really need to know.

Back when I arrived, the Amenos jailers used it as a training ground. It's a nice, isolated place to learn about subduing prisoners.\n\nSometime after they processed me and I was banished to the jungle, rumors started about a game on the island.

I don't know much to tell. No one I've met has ever come back to talk about it.\n\nPrisoners get recruited from Amenos Station with the promised reward of freedom. If you survive their hunt, you win. Survive for how long, though? They don't say.

Other than her delusions of escape? She must be new. I've never seen her before now. And I make it my business to know everyone in the Amenos jungle.\n\nShe's a swindler—someone good at tricking people into giving away gold. Be careful with her.

I suppose I'll talk to the Evergrowth. Get it to help us restore the grove and finish removing the last of the corruption.\n\nI just wish the archdruid were here to see this. She was tough, but I know she wanted me to go far in the circle.

I suppose I'll talk to the Evergrowth. Get it to help us renew the grove and finish removing the last of the corruption.\n\nAnd if we can save the corrupted druids and the archdruid, so much the better. I'll do whatever I can to help them.

Whoever cast this ritual obviously attempted to tap into the deep magic of High Isle. The power beneath the surface here is very … seductive. \n\nBut as I am sure Ryvana would tell you, using it and controlling it are not the same thing.

Oh? Fascinating. That makes sense. These lodestones can also be used to focus navigation spells. \n\nThis is the truth of magic, after all. It is not inherently good or evil. It merely reflects what's in the heart of the caster.
I need to recover Madach's body. I'll see her brought back to the Order, and make sure she gets proper honors for her deeds.

I shall return to the tower and slay the bloodmage. With his phylactery destroyed, he will be well and truly dead.\n\nAlso … I need to recover Madach's body. I'll see her brought back to the Order, and make sure she gets proper honors for her deeds.

I don't know. It depends. Some prisoners undergo processing within days. Others get to remain in the stockade indefinitely, as a reward for some service or another. The jailers call them trusties.\n\nI'd use a different word.

Nothing illegal, if that's what you're asking. Well, nothing overtly illegal. We were watching the ships come and go. Looking for a suitable crew and cargo we could take advantage of.\n\nWe're thieves, all right! Maybe the jailers recognized Valentyn.

You would think that, wouldn't you? That is because you do not know her like Raenobi does. Sorinne has walked this path before—all pride and preening. But given enough time, she always comes back to Raenobi. Always.

Bah. This one doubts Sorinne will even make it to the final match.\n\nLentondil is the pride of Auridon—as sleek a player as this one has ever seen. And Malilen shows fierce focus. Every player in Marbruk quivers at her approach!

The truth is that she is no different than Raenobi. No better than Raenobi. She hates this, but better to be honest scum than a lying snob, yes?\n\nYou barely know Sorinne. So, trust Raenobi. All of this moralizing? It is an act. And it ends soon.

Then, Raenobi will use every trick she knows. Every devious feint—every mind game and threat. This one will catch Sorinne's ear and whisper every vile secret that she buried here in Gonfalon Bay until she remembers the truth.

Oh, Basrush is delightful! You'll get along with her smashingly! We met when she was a smuggler operating along the Sentinel coast. Now she runs under a charter from House Mornard, ferrying prisoners and supplies to Amenos Station.

Goodness, no. It served as a haven for pirates and smugglers once. Before the Empire decided it was the perfect place to dump its undesirables. Political prisoners, prisoners of war, rival nobles.\n\nEmeric continues the practice to the current day.

She must be! Anything else is too painful to contemplate!\n\nBut Za'ji knows Caska is still alive. She is far too stubborn to let the ocean take her. And she would do anything to keep the queen safe. Still, lost in a jungle with violent criminals ….

Who is Caska? Only the finest first mate and best friend a Khajiit ever had! She is a Senche-raht. A mighty warrior. She must be on Amenos. Anything else is unthinkable.\n\nStill, lost in a jungle with violent criminals … Za'ji needs another drink!

Depends on your intentions. If you just want a word or two with the thief, the head jailer keeps records of which prisoners are in the stockade and which have been sent to the jungle.\n\nOn the other hand, processing means a lot more if ….

What? Do I look like some fancy robe from the Mages Guild? The process is magical, I think. Or maybe alchemical? Anyway, a processed prisoner can only survive in the wilds of Amenos—if you can call living in that jungle surviving.\n\nNow go away.

If you're planning a rescue. But I don't want to know nothing about that.\n\nIf the thief has been processed, then he's already been banished. Or he's about to be. And once that happens, there's no leaving this island. At least not alive.

From the prison? What ever gave you that idea? No, I needed to get into the prison to examine a book I knew was inside the jailers' keep. Secrets of Amenos. A rare tome full of secrets I require to access the old vault.

This one cannot do that. This one was processed, so she cannot live anywhere but within this dung-infested jungle. You are prisoners and do not know this?\n\nOnce you are banished to the jungle, leaving it will kill you dead, dead, dead.

No, no lie. This one saw it with her own eyes. Poor Humdo did just that. Turned to dust before he had gotten more than a few steps through the gate.\n\nThe jungle is bad, but turning to dust? This one thinks that would be much worse.

Most certainly! I learned a long time ago that some fine wine, a box of sweets, and a little romance take the edge off. Helps soothe Marcelle's murderous impulses after I win one of our competitions.\n\nThat's the secret to a happy marriage, my friend!
I know. And whatever the outcome, I am grateful for everything.

Hmm. Gelekh, perhaps? As a barkeep, she meets scores of people every day. One of them might have dropped some hints on where to find a Founder.\n\nIt might be worth asking the others as well—Sorinne and Brahgas. They both have keen ears for rumors.

It's a tempting route for clandestine maneuvers. That makes it a favorite of pirates, and alliance warships, seeking to avoid a lot of attention. I suspect the Dreadsail's presence explains why so many ships have been lost lately.
I fear I cannot tell you much. The curse has something to do with forgetfulness and plays havoc with the memories of all it touches … including me.
I think so? Oh, why is it so hard to remember anything? Damn this curse! It puts me all out of sorts.\n\nPlease, I don't want to talk about this any more. It upsets me so.
I remember a little. My name is Janne Emarie. I know I've been waiting a very long time for my love to return to me. That sounded like him, inside that noble lady.

Is that—what a ridiculous question!\n\nWait! I know you. Stibbons found you? Finally did something right for a change. Good. You can help me break the curse. I seem to have unleashed it when I opened this chest.

Is that—what a ridiculous question!\n\nWait, who are you? Did my hapless manservant actually manage to find someone willing to help? Good. I seem to have unleashed some sort of curse when I opened this chest.

It's the sea captain. Stibbons and I were exploring when I spotted this hope chest partially buried in the sand. I usually let my manservant deal with such things, but for some reason I felt compelled to open it.\n\nThat's when … when ….

Arrgh! Get. Out!\n\nYes, it's me. At least for the moment. Take my useless manservant and go to the lighthouse. The plaques there tell the story of the All Flags Navy. Maybe they contain a clue as to how to break this damn curse!
I know he is.\n\nAnd just because he's not a member of the chapter doesn't mean we'll cast him out like a flu-wracked beggar. He's our friend. He won't do this alone.

You do realize it's taking everything I have to keep that foul-mouthed, lascivious sea captain at bay? Go read the plaques and learn the history for yourself.\n\nOr maybe you can get that ghost inside you to help. I'll be along shortly.

I remember only glimpses, like a shadow moving across a wall. He was a sea captain. Tall, strong, proud. He called me his little turtle dove. His safe port in a storm.\n\nOh, I wish I could remember his name, or his touch, or his face!
You misunderstand me. This quest is not about glory but about… a lasting legacy. For myself, another tale in a long and storied career.\n\nAnd for Rayan, his first chapter as a knight.
Arrrh! Out!\n\nNo, I'm Lady Laurent. He's Captain Renwic! But why haven't you broken this curse yet? I'm not sure how much longer I can fight off the captain. Talk to Stibbons and end this already!
The finest hammer and chisel in the world! I paid a small fortune for the enchantments, but you'll never discover where I hid—Ugh!

Well, if it concerns High Isle, House Dufort usually foots the bill. If there's trouble on Amenos, that's mostly a concern for House Mornard. And the druids of the Stonelore Circle have thrown in the gold for the lava fissure problem.

We proudly sail for the Aldmeri Dominion during a time of war, yes? And I would never allow the Prowler's crew to betray our allies.\n\nBut, sometimes, only some strong bottles of Black-Briar Mead will lift morale. And Oblan will know how to get them.

I never ask. And he knows better than to tell me. I've learned when to look the other way. If a bottle of Nord mead or a Dark Elf card game gets me a happier crew, what's the harm?\n\nNow if I could only find a way to cheer up Oblan ….

Surely my reputation precedes me? The great captain of the famed Prowler?\n\nI kid. Sure, I may have sailed all across Tamriel. Delivered supplies that turned the tides of battle. Saved the lives of heroes! But, there's no reason you should know me.

No, no. He just enjoys acting surly. I doubt he feels happier than when he's growling at a young sailor for losing a fork or something.\n\nBut I'd give anything to see him smile one day. Even for just a moment.

The Prowler takes on many tasks. These days, yes, we do a great deal of shipping for the war effort. But we'll take on passengers or even livestock.\n\nAnything to keep the crew fed and the ship afloat.
Ah. Hmm. Oh, the usual. Just picking up supplies for our journey to the Summerset Isles. Nothing really notable at all.

The usual kind. Ropes … hammers … crabs ….\n\nNo, I shouldn't lie to someone who offers me help. But also I can't tell you the truth. All I will admit is sometimes the Prowler takes items where they aren't supposed to go.

Amenos has earned a reputation for destroying most ships that approach it. The water here stays forever angry, and the shore's rocks chew through most hulls. The name Skulltooth Coast is rightfully earned.\n\nUnless one is a brilliant captain.

We often use this beach as a transfer station for these items. Not many people can sail here, which makes it perfect for hiding.\n\nSo, when hired for such a job, we make the pick up here away from prying eyes.

Ah. He wouldn't have wanted me to mention that. So, when we find him, keep it to yourself, hmm?\n\nBefore he joined the honest privateering trade, Oblan was a full-time smuggler. That's where he learned these marks.

That I honestly don't know. That scruffy sea cat has led many lives. He keeps them all to himself. I respect his privacy.\n\nIt's not like he left the smuggling game entirely. When a bottle of High Rock Port appears on my desk, I know how it got there.

Any smuggler worth their salt knows how to read them. They give simple directions or warnings. \n\nIf you're not taught properly, they only look like random scratches. Hiding in plain sight works well for that career.

Before Leobert tarnished the name of Death's Valor, the altars stood as a test of squires' worthiness. Kneeling at the altars—and praying to the ideals we held dear—disengaged the locks holding the chests next to the altars shut.

Items sacred to us. The burial shroud of Lucette Suriel. A black candle. A sack of grave dirt. Dried petals. \n\nI desecrated the chests, but there wasn't much time. Leobert had to be stopped. The chests were the only option.

That may be the only light in this dark situation. The power of the altars only reveals itself to those who are worthy. \n\nLord Leobert, in his arrogance, shunned our order. Our very creed! He's no more worthy than an ant!

Oh, I asked that sour cat to come and thank you. But, he turned me down. Something about needing to count the crates another time. He never stops working, that one.\n\nBut I know for a certainty that he's grateful for everything you've done.
The Firesong Circle. They are the oldest of the circles but I … I do not wish to speak of them.

Quite majestic, isn't it? The pride of Lord Bacaro Volorus. He's shown such generosity by opening his doors to the wounded.\n\nI don't know much about the building itself. But I can't imagine a more beautiful place to work.

Oh, that's the Render of the Loch himself! Sixty years ago he swam into Loch Abhain from the open sea. He went after anyone who dared to wade in past their knees. Killed a dozen people between here and All Flags.\n\nAnyway, he owns the place.

The way I heard it, Captain Maciana liked to boast that anyone who beat her in a fair fight could have the inn. When the shark got her, the townsfolk honored her wish. To this day, the Render remains the official owner of the Ancient Anchor.

Sure! One of his victims was the proprietor of the Ancient Anchor, Maciana Stormspray. She was a captain—half a pirate, really—who retired to Gonfalon Bay and bought the Anchor. But she got bored and decided to hunt down the Render.
Oh, of course! As long as this horrible war rages, I will help heal the injured. And I believe in Lord Bacaro's dream. Learning about the lives of our enemies offers the best path to peace.
That's Mount Firesong. It's a restless sleeper. Snoring, belching, twisting and turning constantly. And High Isle shivers every time it does.
Stop? That's no fun. But the headache tomorrow will be no fun, too. \n\nI suppose I could stop. Help the missus figure out where we are.
You're right! I got cause to celebrate. Let's find another! More liquor for me!

You're very helpful stranger. I'll be sure to recommend your advice to others back home. \n\nNone of them thought we'd have any success on this little escapade of ours but look! We're happily intoxicated and being assisted by someone of your finery!

That's a shame. Because I'm almost out of drink! Perhaps there's a tavern nearby. That would be wonderful. A tavern, a place to sit that doesn't get my clothes all mussed. \n\nDo you know of a tavern?

You can't, not from Gonfalon Bay. Mount Firesong is on Y'ffelon, the island to the northwest, but its roots run all through the Systres. \n\nY'ffelon's bad dreams can rattle windows and shake shelves here, all the way over here on High Isle.

No, it's not. I've never seen it this bad. The Colossus stood guard over Gonfalon Bay for nine centuries. Now it's gone.\n\nI think I'll go over to the temple later, and ask the Divines to protect us. It couldn't hurt.
No, my friend. You've done so much already. \n\nI am … was … her squire. This is for me to do alone.
I'd like that very much. Best of luck on your adventures here on High Isle. \n\nI'll ensure that your name is sung alongside Dame Madach's in the Tale of the Crimson Spire.
I'd like that very much. Best of luck on your adventures here on High Isle. \n\nI'll ensure that your name is sung alongside Dame Madach's in the Tale of the Crimson Spire.
No, my friend. You've done so much already. \n\nI am … was … her squire. This is for me to do alone.

Absolutely. They raised a storm and sank three ships to try to kill us. As long as their leaders live, there's no reason to expect them to just surrender.\n\nAt least Emeric, Irnskar, and I still draw breath. Thanks to you.

Lord Bacaro believes, and I agree, that living alongside the enemy dulls hatreds. These soldiers share stories, heal together, eat at the same table.\n\nHopefully our hospice plants seeds that will someday bloom into peace.

Lord Bacaro leads the Society of the Steadfast. They're a philanthropic group that wants to bring the Three Banners War to an end. While they work toward peace, they try to ease the suffering it causes.\n\nOur work at the manor is part of that.

Well, you wouldn't know it by looking at him right now, but he's actually a very charming, intelligent, and passionate man. We fell in love over a bottle of Alto wine years ago and discovered we both had a gift for concocting delicious libations.

He makes me want to tear out my own hair most days, but yes, we are. As much as he vexes me, he makes me laugh too. And he has incredible ideas—it was his notion to use the fleshflies to add a hint of bitterness to the drink. Just brilliant.

Ha! Got you, didn't I?\n\nLook at these ramparts. No pirate ship's ventured within sight of the Gonfalon Colossus in twenty years or more. And if any pirates did set foot on High Isle, there are at least three knightly orders ready to thrash 'em.

Yes, the Evergrowth. I'm surprised you know that ancient designation.\n\nI believe the wards reinforce the spirit's connection to the grove, but I'm not an expert on that. I can sense them, though. I have an affinity for such things.

Yes! This place brings in rich nobles by the bucketful—or at least it used to before those delegates came around. But there are still enough gadabouts to take advantage of. People who will pay almost anything for a taste of something different.

It impresses Tamsfolk fresh off the boat. They like to pretend the Systres are made up of lawless ports and wild islands. So I sell 'em good steel for protection. Against pirates. Ha!\n\nMind you, the steel's good. That's no stretch of the truth.

You might have a point there. I talk up pirates to impress mainlanders fresh off the boat. Sell 'em good steel for protection. But maybe that's not as much of a stretch these days.\n\nMind you, the steel's good. I wouldn't exaggerate that!
You ventured inside the Firepot cave? And collected cast off rock from the vulk'esh? \n\nI—I must bow to your tale. It's far superior to mine.

Someone or something disturbed the wards in the Undergrove. Probably when the ritual was performed. And it appears the archdruid knew about the corruption before I mentioned it, but she acted like she knew nothing.
You did all that? \n\nI must confess I was not so brave as to step within the walls. Seeing one undead knight—even if it was just his skull—was enough for me. I wish I had your courage, my friend.

We find the corrupted wards. I cleanse them and you break them, much as we did in the grove.\n\nAfter we deal with the initial wards, the Undergrove's central chamber should open, allowing us to destroy the last binding ward and set the spirit free.
I'm not sure, she didn't say. If I had to guess, she met a pretty face and decided to follow him to the island.\n\nHalf of Aurelia's stories sound like the beginning to a romance novel.
I would never … yes, of course I'm a fan of romance novels. What woman in the Knightly Orders is not? \n\nHave you read "Desires of the Sword?" But, wait. That's not important right now.

It's not made of gold or studded with gems, no. But signet rings allow banks and trading partners to know if one of the family's agents are negotiating in good faith.\n\nSomeone could cause no end of trouble for my parents with that ring.
That … ah. That is a very good question. It … it seemed like a good idea at the time?\n\nBecause. Well, that's not important right now. Let's just focus on the here and now, all right?

My father and the late Lord Jourvel were friends. When it came time to see to my education, the Knight Commander offered me a place in her household.\n\nIt was a kindness I still thank her for to this day.

We've only just met, lovely stranger! I can't go giving you all our secrets just yet. Hilgrim and I have a special technique when it comes to the blending. But truthfully, we can't take all the credit. The local ingredients play a major role.

Yes! In both drink making and in life! Isn't she lovely? The way the light reflects off her hair, her perfect frown, the way she … narrowing her eyes at me now—I don't know what she sees in me, but I'm grateful. And perhaps a little drunk.

It's a wonderful story! A mutual enthusiasm for libations, two brilliant minds, two fates intertwined, a love so passionate it threatens to engulf all of Tamriel as we bring drinks to the thirsty and curious! It's … wait, what are we talking about?

Draigh, no. She's still my best friend, but we've taken such different paths in our lives. It never would have worked out.\n\nIf you're still game, let's head for Craglorn. Seems we'll have lots of company in Belkarth.

Yes. The Sable Knight does not speak. It is entirely possible that it does not even think. But it seems drawn to attack servants of the Divines and despoil their sacred places.\n\nA remnant of the dark will of its creator, perhaps.

Well, yes, but we're trying to keep the details under wraps. Only a handful of people know the true purpose of the conference.\n\nYou were brought in on the secret during our last run-in with the Ascendant Order, but please keep it to yourself.

I am .. well enough. Since our last encounter, my travels have taken me across the length and breadth of Tamriel. \n\nMy mortal need for rest always gives my prey the advantage. Still, I try my best.

Stowed away on one of the galleys that comes through Amenos Station to pick up what the prisoners bring in. I just grabbed a sack and started unloading as soon as we entered port. \n\nWhen I walked off into the wilderness, nobody made to stop me.

Ah, heh, I didn't think that far ahead. Way I see it, if I find my ancestor's treasure I can probably bribe my way out … and if I don't, I've got bigger troubles.\n\nI'll sink that schooner when it comes 'round.

Like a Pellitine fire blossom! One of the really big ones! Once your work is done, run to the Prowler. We will meet you on board. Hopefully.\n\nDon't worry! This plan will work. And if it doesn't, we'll all be too dead to argue about it.

During centuries of death, one finds many opportunities for study. You'll see how large the library of Garick's Rest is. I grew curious about my nature and did some reading.\n\nTurns out that spiritual energy manipulation is fairly simple.
This is what Adwig tells me. He brought a bow for Oblan fashioned from old planks and fishing twine. The crazy Breton smells terrible, but he is very resourceful.

I won't claim to be a full-fledged necromancer. But Amunara's device looks fairly standard issue to me.\n\nThe incense is energy-receptive. It passively attunes to dominant existential energy nearby. Once triggered, the trap seeks similar energy.
As I said—many centuries, my friend.

Most of the parts are common. You'll find the censer itself in any temple. Assuming temples still exist in this era.\n\nI can't say where to find the energy-receptive incense though. All my sources are out of date by more than a thousand years.
Bah! Once a sailor, always a sailor!\n\nIt's like Watkins always says: "What happened to my legs? Where did my legs go? I guess I left them at sea!"

Well, I'm sure none of them snivel like Donel or grouse about the weather like Watkins. I love meeting new people! Love it!\n\nI'm only wondering what job Jimila has planned for me. I'm a damn fine coxswain! Or I was, at least.

High Isle is the primary island in the Systres Archipelago. Technically, we're a Breton holding, but we try to behave as a neutral port. People from all over Tamriel come to experience the natural beauty of the island. \n\nWell, nobles, mostly.

Mostly political prisoners from the Empire at first. Later, rival nobles, pirates, murderers. The worst of the worst. Today it also includes war criminals and certain prisoners of war.\n\nAmenos Station is friendly enough, but the jungle is deadly.

Parts of it. But we have a rich history and the same sorts of dangers you'd experience on the mainland. Bandits, pirates, wild beasts. \n\nAnd you might want to avoid our sister island, Amenos. It's a harsh jungle that has long served as a prison.

The wyrd are Breton witches. They follow teachings and practices that share a common ancestry with the druids. Whereas we left the mainland, they remained behind to safeguard the forests of High Rock.

We have more in common than we have differences. The biggest that you would notice is that the wyrds are all female, while we druids accept all genders in our ranks. And we organize in circles of common beliefs, while the wyrd sisters form covens.

I warned them of the danger, and we took such elaborate precautions. Obviously they weren't enough.\n\nIf we find Quentyn with the Ascendant Order, we may find our missing royals. Let's meet at the chapel north of the loch and see what awaits us.

Nothing, my dear, but you asked.\n\nLord Bacaro selected High Isle for the peace talks because of that history, though. The All Flags Navy recalls a time when disparate people united in common cause. He hopes to inspire the delegates to do the same.

Lord Bacaro worked diligently to bring the peace talks to High Isle. Not everyone thought that was a good idea. I'm curious as to who opposed him and why.\n\nBetter yet, he won't voice suspicions without good cause. We can rely on his discretion.

I suspect the Order wants power, not peace. When the throne is vacant, your prospects of becoming emperor suddenly seem a good deal more promising. \n\nThat sort of prize might tempt a noble with just the right mix of ambition, gold, and imagination.

Elea is the duchess of House Dufort and nominal ruler of High Isle. Damard is her brother and a count. Jonne Mornard is the highest-ranking noble of House Mornard currently on High Isle. He's Count Leonard's cousin, representing house interests here.

We Bretons trace our ancestry to Nedes and Elves who intermingled during the early history of High Rock. Therefore, spellcraft is in our blood and we all at least have some talent with magic.\n\nI find the subject fascinating and decided to embrace it.

Because the Ascendant Magus has made a show of wanting us to fear him. Why would he care if he had what he wanted and couldn't be stopped? No, the royals elude him. Somehow.\n\nBut his magic … I wonder ….

I … did. I arrived just in time to see part of it collapse. As much as it saddens me to see the proud baron-admiral fall, we have more pressing problems to deal with.\n\nI'll mourn the Colossus of Gonfalon Bay—after the alliance leaders are safe.

It's a closely guarded secret, I'm afraid. When prisoners are selected for banishment, they undergo some sort of magical or alchemical treatment. After that, they can only survive in the jungle.\n\nIs it true? Does it matter? The prisoners believe it.

Amunara doesn't like to talk about herself. This one is just a simple Khajiit bone-raiser trying to make her way in the world.\n\nLook, Amunara just met you. Perhaps next time we can swap stories. For now, this one has a shield to acquire.

Out in the Abecean lies a spot shrouded in mystery. Old pirates love to scare themselves by swapping tales about it. Any ships that enter those waters, they never come out.\n\nSome think a giant whale swallows them. Others say it's a pit to Oblivion.

The Harrowstorms are necrotic tempests of incredible power. They scour life from the land and make following the trail my quarry has left behind quite … difficult.\n\nIf we are going to locate the blood leech I seek, we must destroy one. Together.
Your bravery is an encouraging mixture of steel and ignorance. I respect it.\n\nSeek out a storm. I will join you. And perhaps finally my blade's thirst will be slaked.
No, no. She's keeping that secret close to her vest, but I heard some of her sailors mention lodestones in an … unusual context. I think her plans must involve whatever those are.

They fell for her charms, obviously! Who wouldn't want my sweet Privette living with them? She brightens every room—even a moldy cave.\n\nMaybe those Hadolids never intended to eat her. Yes, that must be it. She was never in danger.

Oh, not about the whole Ascendant Lord and murder thing. But about finding someone other than one of us to sit on the throne? I can't imagine Ayrenn or Jorunn agreeing to bow down to me willingly. And I feel the same way.\n\nWe'll just have to see.

More druidic traitors? I really must have a talk with their elders. And they were working with Sea Elves? That's not an alliance I would have predicted. But what about the Ascendant Order? Any sign of them or their lord?

No. Lord Bacaro wants the peace talks to occur under controlled conditions. He's worried that if left to our own devices, we'd start another war. And I can't say he's wrong. We're all a bit hot-headed and stubborn, if you hadn't noticed.

Aha, Arabelle. She's never failed me yet! Give her whatever help she requires.\n\nI haven't spoken to Ayrenn or Irnskar since the celebration. I think I actually miss them. The guards are overly protective of us, and we've had practically no contact.
Well, that's something, at least. I swear, though, if something doesn't change soon, I'm going to call for Captain Za'ji and return to my own domain. I've been absent long enough as it is.

Locked away for my safety is not what I had imagined when I agreed to attend this conference. I'll abide a little longer. But my royal patience is growing quite thin. \n\nGo, my friend. End the threat so we can get to the business that brought us here.
Druids and Sea Elves? Impressive, as always. And have you learned anything more about the Ascendant Order and its mysterious lord?

Yes, yes. For a Breton noble, Lady Arabelle seems quite competent. I know my father trusts her, despite her ties to Emeric and the Covenant. \n\nWell, get to it! I can't wait to get out of this room so we can finally start talking!

Mainlanders rave about our local cuisine! Some of the finest seafood in the world swims in the waters around the archipelago. Try the dishes I've had prepared here in the hall.\n\nI look forward to your opinion, as seafood makes me terribly ill.
I'm listening. What's on your mind?

She sleeps in the next chamber, but soon she'll awake with my curse.\n\nThere's a vial of my blood in the laboratory across the hall. We can use it to create an antidote. Release me. Please?
And? As I said, seafood makes me ill, so I haven't been able to taste any of the dishes myself.\n\nWere they good? Did you like any of them in particular? Please, tell me your thoughts.

I'll sell tours of the islands to wealthy visitors. Wine them, dine them, and show them the sights. They'll tell their friends all about us when they return home!\n\nWith an enterprise such as this, we'll soon be rolling in gold!

By advertising, of course! I'm drafting a pamphlet describing the tours of the isles. Publish it in cities across Tamriel to attract visitors. \n\nWhat I need at the moment is someone to test my suggested itinerary. Interested? I'll pay for your time.

I'm a historian in the Stonelore Circle. The Firesong and the Eldertide Druids look down on us for accepting outsiders, but they've never been violent before.\n\nThese Stonelore Druids treated me like family. I thought the Firesong were family, too.

There was, centuries ago. He led the druids of old to the Systres Archipelago. \n\nBut he foresaw something. The stories make it sound terrible. He's the reason the druids split into three circles. And he gave us our sacred seeds.

His village housed me on Y'ffelon, the Firesong's island. It contains some of the most intact records about the Druid King's life. Archdruid Devyric was never friendly, but almost no one was.\n\nThe Firesong respect him. He is an archdruid, after all.

Each circle has many archdruids. I'm not sure how many the Firesong have. And they rarely leave their island. \n\nWe thought Archdruid Devyric was here to learn. But now he's going toward the Dais of Stonesight.

They do … but we're not really widely known outside of a few noble and merchant circles. And many visitors never even leave the comforts of Gonfalon Bay.\n\nI want to share the beauty of the entire archipelago with my guests and reap in the profits!

That's part of it. But I really do want to show our guests everything our islands have to offer. And I want to build something of my own. A business beyond what the Visour family already stands for.\n\nAnd with your help, my tours will be magnificent!

A gift from the last Druid King. He gave the leaders of each of the circles a seed, to care for until such time as the seeds would be needed. \n\nThat's a very literal translation of the prophecy. I came here to learn more about the Stonelore seed.

Our records of the Druid King's last days are limited. I've studied them—potentially more than anyone else—and even I don't know. \n\nBut, if Archdruid Devyric is willing to kill to get the Stonelore seed, then we can't let him have it.

They support the Deeproot and protect the spirit inside from collapses. Archdruid Devyric did something ….\n\nHe tied the magic of these barriers into the sap of the sentinels. I can't open the way through while the sentinels live.
The Dais of Rootspeak grants knowledge through the Spirit of Root. It allows druids to hear the realm through interconnected roots of all plants.

The seed isn't in the Deeproot, but he doesn't know that.\n\nHe's probably corrupting the Spirit of Root as we speak. I don't know if we can stop him, but a corrupted Spirit of Root will twist us in vines and buy that unrelenting parasite more time.

To the Dais of Skytremor, if they can make it through the Path of the Salt Wind. I never go out there. The spirit is too loud and the cliffs … it feels like one strong gust could push me off the rocks.\n\nI stay underground, where I know my footing.

I'm a druid of the Stonelore Circle, from Galen. One of the islands in the Systres Archipelago. I've studied the Druid King all my life. I suppose you could call me an expert, but so much of our history was lost over the centuries.

I'm a druid. The Druid King's path reveals the origin of my people. Why we departed High Rock, how we found the archipelago, what divided us into the three circles—it's all connected. So much of our history was lost over the generations.

I'm not actually sure they are. Dhulef just said he noticed them while he was conducting his investigation. The last time I ran into them those path-traitors attacked the Earthen Root Enclave and killed people I cared about. That won't happen again.
