I'll take it to Galen. It's our duty to keep this seed safe, and it's not safe here—not after what happened. What we do with it, that's the archdruid's decision. But I'm sure it will be secreted away again.

All he said was that his leader made him one of Y'ffre's chosen. But Y'ffre would never select that foul-smelling sack of root rot for anything.\n\nStill, I wonder why he cared about this seed. If he wanted to study it, the Firesong have their own.

Not me, unfortunately. I only came here to study the sacred seed. If I tried to help, I'd be more likely to pluck the flowers than the weeds.\n\nNo, the enclave's keepers will restore this place. They'll care for the spirits now.

I need to ask our archdruids, but it may be useful to reach out to the Eldertide Circle. They could have information and insight. \n\nWith what just happened, I doubt we'll talk to the Firesong. But the Draoife will hear of this. I'll make sure of it.

An ancient tablet. The carving's as old as Tu'whacca's tail, but the symbol at the top represents the Druid King! And the pattern suggests some sort of ritual. But I'm not sure about the other three symbols. Wyrds, maybe? No idea.

Earlier, I met with a Beldama wyress. Thought she might know something about why the Druid King visited the wyrds before leading the druids to the Systres. She needed time to recall the stories, but remembered this tablet and sent me to examine it.

No idea. That's why I made this rubbing. Why don't you take it to the Beldama camp near the Wyrd Tree and show it to Wyress Tola. Maybe it will help her recall any stories about wyrds and the Druid King.\n\nDruid Laurel and I will meet you there.
The Firesong leader, Archdruid Michiel, demanded that Wyress Tola come with him to open the—how did he phrase it—the Druid King's ritual site?\n\nWhen she refused, they attacked. They took her away!

Hag Fen? The marsh to the northeast? Well, if the Firesong marked a location on their map, it must be important. We need to head there and fast! I don't trust that path-traitor Archdruid Michiel to not hurt the wyress.\n\nDid you find anything else?

Orders? Let me see that. Hmm. Archdruid Orlaith is one of the most respected elders in the Firesong Circle. But why did she send Michiel here to get a nature spirit? We have plenty of our own in the archipelago.\n\nAnyway, is that everything?

After consulting with my fellow elders and listening to the Firesong druid prattle on, yes. In one story, the Beldama Wyrds worked with Druid King Kasorayn long ago to consecrate this place for a ritual.\n\nDid Dhulef find the tablet I pointed him to?

I believe it's the ritual depicted on the tablet, but in reverse. It shows the Druid King and the wyrds consecrating a place for a nature spirit. The archdruid's ritual desecrated this site. Now he's off to do the same thing at the second site.

As sure as Rain's Hand's showers give rise to Second Seed's flowers! Let's hurry to Bangkorai and find that Glenmoril camp the wyress told you about.\n\nWe need to keep Archdruid Michiel from desecrating the second ritual site.
Odd. I wasn't aware there were such distinctions. But if you're not with these Firesong, then why are you here?
Yes, Frii! Keeper, nourisher, the flower grown and given form. Dreamed by the Green long ago. I … am. The king spoke, the wyrds sang, and Frii … became Frii.\n\nBright. Too bright.

Purpose? Frii has a purpose, but the memories are … unclear. I am the tender, the nourisher. Gentle hands mend the ground. Awake now. But where … who? Blood warm in the soil. \n\nAway. Sunlight on leaves. Please.
Surely something will occur to you! Perhaps they can be driven away by a staged accident? Or perhaps you can find someone else to deal with them?\n\nThat's what Raz did.

Too many ears listen here, friend. Raz arrived in advance, as Queen Ayrenn Arana Aldmeri made ready to travel to High Isle.\n\nThen … Raz caught a whiff of something bad. And this one was given leave to follow his nose.
A scent he has not detected in a long, long time. From one of his earliest missions as an Eye of the Queen. \n\nWe can talk more of this stench when not so many listen in, yes?
As sleek and fragrant as ever, five-claw. Raz must say, he could get used to the salt air and delicious food of the archipelago. \n\nThe drinks taste of bilge-water, though. Such a pity.

Oh, politics as usual. Raz would have stuck around to help with the cleanup … he was just getting friendly with the Proxy Queen! \n\nBut alas, duty called and he had to leave those beautiful beaches behind. You know how it is.
Ah yes, our adventure with the lovely Naryu! Seems like so long ago, now. Do … do you think she remembers Raz, hmm?\n\nSurely … no. But perhaps? But … no. But … perhaps ….

The Mane? She is a treasure. One of the reasons Queen Ayrenn felt it safe to travel. The Dominion is a fragile thing, you know. \n\nSome days Raz thinks he can feel its heartbeat in his paw. But heroes like the Mane make the world just a bit safer.
By all means, five-claw. Ask away.

Oh, well. Let's see. We have a variety of fish stews, those are always popular when Angler's Day comes around. Fruit pastries, the nobles love those. \n\nAnd then we have some druid fare, like Y'ffelon Surprise.

My friend Druid Laurel enjoys digging up ancient histories. These days she's fascinated by someone called Druid King Kasorayn.\n\nLong ago, he led his people to the Systres islands. Laurel gave me a logbook from his trip, but it's incomplete.

It's a druid … delicacy. A sheep's bladder filled with milk and curdled with sacred herbs. Then we split the bladder, stuff the curds with fish, sew it back up again, and leave it to ferment.\n\nDelicious! If you can get past the odor.

I'd be happy to, but chef has asked that we not serve it unless the customer is a true gourmand. Someone who knows food inside and out. \n\nWe've …. had a few angry customers. You understand. The smell really is quite … powerful.
I really can't tell you that. The secret is the only thing that's currently protecting the seed from Archdruid Devyric. If he found it ….\n\nLet's just stop him before that happens.

Where the Druid King launched from when he led the druids out of High Rock. She's tracing his path from Tamriel to Y'ffelon, but hit a wall. If I can find anything to advance her research, she'd appreciate it.\n\nI admit I don't know much about this.

Looks like you and I have found what's inside the infamous Graven Deep. Can't say that this small island lives up to the legend. The speed of that storm that hit us, though, that surely does.\n\nI'd wager we'll learn more once we climb those cliffs.

It crashed upon us with a hunger, didn't it? I can't say it was the roughest storm I've endured. But it was most certainly the fastest.\n\nLook around though. The beach debris didn't only come from us. This has happened many times before.

A tavern brawl, of course! A fracas, a melee, a clash between two wretched souls sodden with drink. \n\nWhen I first heard of this establishment, I was expecting violence enough to make a Kvatch arena fighter blush!
Oh … well. I couldn't possibly. I mean, I'm a proud son of Summerset! Trained in the fencing arts by a retired Welkynar!\n\nI might do mortal harm to any mere bar-fighter.

Truly? Hmm. I suppose I have come all this way. It would be silly to leave without getting the full experience. \n\nVery well! Just point me to these friends of yours and I shall issue a challenge forthwith!

The Spirit of Air can repeat anything that's spoken aloud. All Archdruid Devyric has to do is focus the spirit on Druid Laurel and it will know where the seed is. \n\nIf they make it there, all of this death and sacrifice will be for nothing.
They only want to hear the old standards. I, however, only play original compositions. \n\nThe uninformed may call them screeching and cacophonous, but that's only because I'm not famous yet!
Hah! I'd be happy to. Always nice to meet an appreciator of true art.\n\nNow, there's just the matter of my payment ….
Did this one give you the impression he could? \n\nContinue to help the Queen's Eye, and you will be paid handsomely. As handsome as Raz!

Just so. The Aquilarios Bequest. A ludicrous fortune sent by ship, to Galen, during the final years of Emperor Varen's reign.\n\nIt was thought lost at sea. But somehow, Redblade has learned its true location.

As far as Raz can tell, no. We must find the bequest first. Luckily, this one has a place to start. Another Eye, years ago, sought to recover the bequest … and we have her notes.\n\nWhat do you say? Help Raz claim this prize and save the day?

A circle of druids that usually stick to their own island. Lately, however, they've been turning up all over and attacking people. I hoped I was done with them after Earthen Root Enclave, but Dhulef spotted them while investigating a lead.

I'm a historian. Dhulef's helping me trace the movements of the Druids of Galen after they left High Rock in ages past. I'm not familiar with this land, so Dhulef went on ahead. Now he's in trouble. Can you help? I'll find a way to reward you.

Aye. Dwarves, without a doubt. I'm no expert, but their buildings have a signature look. And like everything Dwarven, this place seems abandoned.\n\nBut why in the middle of the sea? What were they hiding here? The questions are many and much.

I'd like to sift through these documents. Maybe some lost sailor found the secret to Graven Deep.\n\nAnd who knows? Perhaps information about the Druid King will float to the surface. A long bet, I know. But I feel in my bones that something's here.

See if you can find any more documents or any survivors. Scout ahead for possible danger as well. Those Hadolids could have set up homes in here, too.\n\nI've heard stories of Dwarven traps in places like this. Careful not to lose a limb.

Yes, but that's beyond the scope of my original contract. I hate it when the client defines the job one way, then the whole thing takes a left turn. Typical.\n\nPerhaps I'll add a life-threatening-danger clause to future contracts.

When you sail the waters as long as I have, you see the wildest things. Creatures longer than ships slithering under the waves. A man entirely made of coral. Fish that fly through the air.\n\nUsing magic to summon storms is a basic application.

If the pipes draw magicka in and funnel it downward, they must feed into something. Knowing the Dwarves, it's likely a huge machine of some kind. The Mages Guild library contains many tales of that sort of thing.\n\nI suppose we'll know soon enough.

According to the reports I received, you were there, my dear. You saw firsthand the destruction at Vastyr, the rumblings from Y'ffelon. The Society of the Steadfast is sending aid to the islands as quickly as their ships can make the journey.

Lord Bacaro Volorus, philanthropist and founder of the Society of the Steadfast. He and his organization have gone to great lengths to assist those impacted by the Three Banners War and other catastrophes, such as what's happening on Galen.

I had to put them somewhere, dear, and Mandrake Manor isn't large enough to keep them comfortable and adequately separated. There's more than enough room in the palace to make sure they don't engage in any unchaperoned squabbling.

That would never work. It took untold hours of planning and preparation to get them here in the first place. And then we nearly lost them on multiple occasions.\n\nNo, this is our one chance for peace. We won't get another if they leave.

The Ascendant Lord and his minions are still out there somewhere. Lord Bacaro is hesitant to proceed when an attack could occur at any moment, but I can't keep the alliance leaders here much longer. Their patience with the situation grows thin.

They are a proud and fickle lot, but they have one thing in common, dear. They respect you.\n\nGo to the city palace and talk to them. Ask them to remain patient. Then speak to Lord Bacaro. See if you can convince him to let me get things started.

Lady Arabelle uses every weapon in her arsenal. I suppose that's why I hired her.\n\nBut the timing isn't right, my friend. There's too much at stake to risk another setback. Once the most recent threats have been eliminated, then we may begin.

If you're still working with Arabelle, then you can look into the validity of this threat. Discover what became of my messenger at the Dufort Shipyards.\n\nThat would ease my mind while I aid Vastyr and get us closer to starting the peace talks.

I was about to send word to Lady Arabelle. My scouts reported new Ascendant Order activity at the Dufort Shipyards. I sent a messenger there to confirm these reports but they have yet to return.\n\nI fear Duchess Elea has fooled us all.

After you discovered that her brother was the Ascendant Magus and killed him, Duchess Elea claimed no involvement. She was stoic in her grief and assured me her brother acted without her permission or foreknowledge.\n\nHmm. Since you're here ….

Raz knows who the thugs work for. The tailed tail used a member's-only entrance to the local Outlaws Refuge.\n\nJust inside the refuge is a gambling parlor owned by a local crime boss called Yves Grandvache.
If Grandvache is backing Redblade, the sharp claws of knowledge will undo them. This one has dealt with Grandvache before. \n\nRaz will have to wear a disguise, but that is a small price to pay.

Raz mentioned another Eye, who fell tracking the bequest? A skilled agent named Roneiia. Raz always believed Grandvache was behind her death, but could not prove it.\n\nHer ciphered notes were never recovered. Grandvache must have finally cracked them.

First things first, five-claw. We must learn what our enemies already know. That means tailing those two back to their boss.\n\nTrust Raz. This is his bread and butter … or cake and jam, which Raz likes better.

When we were both younger, and Yves had yet to set up his little empire. \n\nThe tale features a sea serpent, an Argonian opera singer, and a relic called Auri-El's Lute. Ask Raz about it sometime. It's a good one.
Roneiia was one of the very first Eyes of the Queen.\n\nRaz only knew her for a few moons. She was a legend, an example for us all. Many of her missions are still kept secret to this day.

Well, they didn't ask me directly. They hired a person who contracted someone else. That person contracted a third party. Then, she hired me.\n\nNow that I've employed you, I'm finally no longer the last link in the chain.

The rich always want to expand their holdings. Mines run dry, you see. Just part of the trade. So, if the house wants to maintain their wealth, they need to find new sources.\n\nAt least, I assume that's the thinking. Maybe they're just greedy.

Poison, I should think. It has all the usual signs.\n\nRight after you left, I received a package. My favorite wine and a note of congratulations for saving the alliance leaders. I should have known better than to pour a glass … but here we are.

How can that be? Duchess Elea assured me she had retaken control of her shipyards.\n\nWe'll deal with that later. Right now, I need you to figure out where that package came from. Determine who wants me out of the way. Nothing has been touched ….

The note was suspiciously vague about that. If I hadn't been tired and thinking about twelve dozen other things, that should have set off a warning bell. Instead ….\n\nNo matter. Tell me, is Lord Bacaro ready to start the peace talks?

More often than you might expect, actually. Comes with the territory. I am rather famous, dear.\n\nStill, I should have been more careful. I can't afford to make a mistake like that again. People who send expensive gifts usually want to take credit.

Just guesses. I suspected the Ascendant Lord, but your news about the Dufort Shipyards concerns me. Did we misjudge Duchess Elea? Was she working with her brother? Is she part of the Ascendant Order?\n\nWe need evidence before we make an accusation.

This poison smells slightly of garlic and has all the earmarks of a druidic compound, but its effects remind me of much older recipes. No healer without druidic training would have even recognized some of the ingredients that make up the poison.

Just what Lady Arabelle asked. Discover where the poisoned wine came from and who sent it. I'll leave more of my tincture with Za'ji and give him exact instructions. Then I need to go do research of my own.\n\nMeet me at my workshop as soon as you can.

Let me guess. The 571 vintage. I'd be hard pressed to refuse such an exquisite wine.\n\nAshcroft's Fine Goods and Imports. Only place on the island that might have any bottles available. Other than the duchess's private stores. Go talk to them, dear.

Ask for Philian Ashcroft, the proprietor. He knows me well and keeps a spot in Bayside Artisans here in town.\n\nAnd while Ryvana works on an antidote, I'll send Za'ji to make sure the alliance leaders don't accept any mysterious gifts.

Hmm, let me see. Yes, a fine vintage. Very fine indeed. I may have sold a bottle or two recently, but I don't make a habit of discussing my client's orders.\n\nWhat is this about, if I may be so bold?

What? I had no idea! Lady Arabelle is one of my best customers!\n\nI swear on my reputation, that wine left this shop unaltered. In fact, I only made one sale that included this particular vintage recently. It was a rather large order, in fact.

Oh, this is awkward. Castle Navire's seneschal placed the order. Claimed he needed to replenish the cellars for Duchess Elea and demanded I sell back the wine I had purchased from them. That exact vintage to be precise.\n\nYou'll want to talk to them.

Ashcroft's? No. Some hooded figures hired me to take some crates to an isolated spot up north. That's where I met another hooded figure. He helped unload my wagon, gave me the crates for Castle Navire, and told me to make the delivery.

Right below the cliffs of Garick's Rest. Look, I know how all this sounds. But I needed this job. Courier work has been hard to come by since the trouble here and on Galen. All I know is I delivered one set of crates and received another for Navire.

No names. Just enough gold to make me not want to ask any questions. You did hear me say we were in an isolated location, right?\n\nBut if it helps, they were definitely wearing armor under their hooded cloaks. Knight armor.
That's just it. I identified the various plants—root, stem, and leaf! But they aren't those plants. Not exactly.

Neither did I, at least not at first. But after careful study, I can see that someone with extensive agricultural knowledge created new and more potent versions of the rare plants used to prepare the poison.\n\nOh, did you discover who sent the wine?

Garick's Rest? Strange magic saturates the wildlife around those ruins. If that's the source of the poison, I'll need samples to craft an antidote. Meet me there.\n\nI fear we could be dealing with another rogue druid—and a powerful one at that!

We know that the Ascendant Lord allied with factions of the Eldertide and Firesong Circles, but to actively promote a sacred druidic prophecy to gain followers to his cause ….\n\nWhat about those crates we found?

And I assume the key we found will grant us access to this alchemical garden. Then I can craft an antidote for Lady Arabelle.\n\nShe and Lord Bacaro will know how to best handle this situation once she recovers from the poison.

Armor that the Ascendant Order can use to impersonate Steadfast knights. I know Captain Marguerite by reputation. We must talk to her about the shipments.\n\nBut first, I still need to gather samples of the plants used to make the poison.
Yes, so I better get started. Luckily, I made some notes while we were hunting for those crystals. I know right where to go to get the results that will please House Mornard.

That's a Shard of the Green. I've never seen an intact one before. Long ago, druids used them to protect sacred locations. The practice withered like leaves on a dying vine, mostly because they were so hard to come by.\n\nHang on to that for now.

The high-roller suite, they call it the patrician suite, is for game winners only. This is where you come in. Raz has an idea. \n\nOne of the games they play is Tales of Tribute. Are you familiar with this card game?

Now? Now we do exactly what Lady Arabelle would want us to. We follow the clues.\n\nHead to Steadfast Manor. We need to talk to Captain Marguerite. I'll meet you there after I start the preparations for the antidote.

Excellent! Raz cannot risk being recognized. So you must play in his place. Here, take these chips. Do not ask where he got them.\n\nAfter you win, head up to the patrician's suite. And do not worry! Raz will be close behind.
Apologies, five-claw. This one is far better at dice than card games. \n\nJust ask the queen if Razum-dar is safe to challenge in dice. Her answer will be pointed and memorable.

I'm not sure. Most Sea Elves are pirates—easy plunder is what they're usually after. But the Dreadsails are more determined than any Maormer I've seen before.\n\nWhatever their goal, we must push them back.

Not as ready as I would like, friend. We don't have enough knights to protect the whole island. But I need information even more than I need soldiers.\n\nFind out what the Dreadsails really want, if you can. And where they plan to strike next.

Hand me your map. I've received reports of Dreadsails near Windwrack Fort, the village of Tuinh, and Suncleft Cove. I need you to investigate these sightings and chase off any Sea Elves you find. Let them know Galen won't go down without a fight.
As the guest wishes, of course. Present your decks and we shall play.

Sir Stefan's a dear friend of mine, and practically a druid himself! We studied together under Archdruid Rahval when we were younger.\n\nIt's not unlike him to worry about the druids—even the Eldertide.

That's strange. It makes me wonder what the Sea Elves really hope to gain by these attacks.\n\nLet's look around. Watch for anything that looks interesting or out of place. With any luck, we can figure out why the Sea Elves attacked Tuinh.
No, Archdruid Devyric did something to it—changed it, made it aggressive. The Spirit of Stone was gentle and patient. It barely even moved.

Somewhere beneath Steadfast Manor. But if you're asking what purpose it serves, that's an ancient druid circle.\n\nIt's a place of power and meditation from long ago. As far as I know, the Stonelore Circle isn't aware this location even exists.
More often than not, places such as this are forgotten for a reason. Let's see what else we can learn and depart this ancient hall as soon as we can.

I'm not sure. But stones as old as these, they hold memories, emotions from ages past. Some believe they can tap into that power. Use it for their own purposes.\n\nThere may be a perfectly benign reason to keep such a place secret.
What? But Lord Bacaro is a man of peace. Why secretly control the very order of rogue knights that are actively trying to destroy everything he's worked for? I don't understand.

Let me see that. Could this be accurate? Could Lord Bacaro be a direct descendant of Druid King Kasorayn?\n\nOh no. The carvings. I think I know why this place is important to Lord Bacaro. Examine the carvings. I'll explain what I see in them.

So he helped foster the conflicts on Galen, then stepped in to help with the Steadfast after the dust settled. All while making alliances with the victors. But his plans failed. No new Druid King has been crowned.

The poison must have affected my hearing. Did you say Lord Bacaro is the Ascendant Lord?\n\nHow can that be? He sponsored the peace talks. He started the Society of the Steadfast, which has done nothing but good for the archipelago and the mainland.

Looking at things from this perspective puts the delays and how the Ascendant Order has managed to stay one step ahead of us in a very different light.\n\nBut why go to all this trouble? What is Lord Bacaro actually planning?

Ah, I feel better already. Well done, dear Ryvana!\n\nAs for this business about the Druid King, I read the reports from Galen. Some druids truly believe that the Ivy Throne would be an improvement over the ruby one. But all this chaos and murder ….

It's an initiative this one began to properly train fighters to face down the Dragons plaguing Elsweyr. Without leaving behind heaps of charred bodies, of course.\n\nYou'd be surprised how poorly some of the recent battles have gone.

Just last month, this one saw a spirited Argonian leap into the fray clutching a rusty frying pan for a weapon.\n\nIt has been … trying. However, since our training sessions began, this one has seen improvements. And far less frying pans.

As far as administrative members, it is just myself and Apprentice Taz for the moment. But all over Elsweyr there are fighters who have benefited from our specialized training. \n\nWe hope to expand our efforts to other parts of Tamriel soon.

I spotted more Sea Elf warships brimming with reinforcements. Luckily, the fort's ballistas are intact. Get to the ballistas and stop those ships.\n\nThat will give us time to deal with the enemies who already made it to shore.

Of course! First, the trial of knowledge! We suspect there are buried tablets in the canyon surrounding the Stitches that contain ancient Dragon-slaying secrets.\n\nThe only mandatory part of your task is to locate one and bring it to me there.

I'll see if I can rally the knights and get the wounded back on their feet. We'll need them to hold the fort once you stop the reinforcements from reaching the shore.\n\nMeet me on the bluffs north of the fort when you're done.

The Sea Elves? Haven't spent much time in these waters, eh? The technical term is Maormer, but nobody actually calls them that. They're bloodthirsty raiders from the great isle of Pyandonea. We usually see a ship or two, but this bunch have a fleet!

You've done your part. We can deal with the stragglers around Windwrack Fort, now that they've got no reinforcements coming to support them.\n\nYour work's just beginning though, mate. I fear the seas ahead will be rough for all of us.

Word is the Sea Elves struck there as well. It's just up the coast to the north. I believe Druid Laurel of the Stonelore Circle is there, looking into things.\n\nI'd appreciate it if you kept an eye on her, mate. Laurel is like kin to me.

Aye, I heard that, too. Something about Sea Elves taking prisoners into a cave near the cove. Strange. If the Dreadsails took captives, why haven't they tried to ransom them yet?\n\nBanneret Corrick went to investigate. Help him if you can.

Well done, mate! Then set your course for Vastyr and report to Stefan. I know he's got a whole island to look after, but he needs to know what the Dreadsails have been doing around here.\n\nHe should be back at Castle Mornard by now.

Archdruid Rahval is dead? I … I knew something had gone wrong. The spirits of nature that surround Glimmertarn were acting so strangely.\n\nBut if the archdruids are dead, what happened to the sacred seeds?

The relic the Dreadsails sought is the sacred seed of the Eldertide. A gift of the last Druid King. Each circle was granted one. That's what Archdruid Orlaith meant by gathering seeds.\n\nCould she be the druid mentioned in the Dreadsails orders?

A council of druids, elders from all three circles. Archdruid Rahval of the Stonelore has summoned the Draoife to address grievances against the Firesong, but up till now Orlaith ignored him.\n\nTell Stefan about this. Pirates aren't his only problem.

We need to return to the Glenmoril Wyrd camp and let them know what happened here. They deserve to hear about Wyress Sorcha from us, as well as about the fate of Archdruid Michiel. We can discuss our next steps back there after we give them the news.

The trial of bravery. The most harrowing, but necessary test!\n\nKnowledge and skill mean nothing without the mettle to face your foe. Slay a Dragon and bring Captain Samara its heart to prove your courage.

If you so choose, I have a few of my Draconic themed questions for you. A small exam, if you will. Such fun! \n\nNext, the trial of endurance. You must battle to the depths of a dungeon within Elsweyr and claim the Defense Force standard placed inside.

Wonderful, anytime! I'm happy to be of service! Please let me know if you need further assistance.\n\nMany have approached the trials with hope and determination. Not all have the strength to see them through. But I have a good feeling about you!

Then we must assume that Count Stefan and Druid Laurel are in danger. If Lord Bacaro truly believes he's the heir to the Ivy Throne of the druids, he'll stop at nothing to get his way.\n\nWe must go to Galen and defend the remaining regalia.
Master Grandvache? He often fraternizes with the elite guests in the patrician suite. \n\nIf you wish to discuss a matter with the master, the guest would do well to look there.

Druid Ryvana and I will get Za'ji to sail us to Galen. While we collect the staff from the Stonelore Circle, I want you to go to Count Stefan and protect the Druid King's crown.\n\nWe'll meet you at Castle Mornard as soon as we can.

Because we don't know how far-reaching Bacaro's conspiracy is. The alliance leaders are safe inside the palace, with their loyal captains watching over them.\n\nAnd we don't want them to hear of this betrayal yet. It would end the talks in a flash.

A Breton. Or, at least I was. Now I look for my legs and all I see are wisps of blue … essence. I think I'm round-ish. An orb? And I feel small. Fenas, the druid over there, laughed when he saw me. I must look ridiculous.\n\nAm I a sprite? A wisp?

Octin's always been the thinker. I'm the impulsive one. So, when the tablet broke and Octin disappeared into a ball of energy, I thought he got vaporized. I went to pick up the broken pieces of stone before I even realized what I was doing.

I don't really know. I'm not an expert on druidic law and prophecy. According to what you and Ryvana discovered, Bacaro believes he's a direct descendant of Kasorayn, the last Druid King. If he gains the regalia, he could make a claim for the title.

I never underestimate anything when it comes to religious fervor.\n\nIf nothing else, his connection to this legacy gives him a legitimate claim to power through his mother's bloodline. And many might see the Ivy Throne as preferable to the Ruby one.

Sure! I mean, I think so? The trees all look the same, so the sap must be the same too, right? Try that one over there. With those fancy hands of yours, it should be easy to acquire.\n\nAt least, if the forest wraiths don't try to kill you.

My knights tracked a band of Dreadsails to the cave here at Suncleft Cove. As they tell it, however, a single Sea Elf tore through them before they could search inside. Didn't even bother to kill them. Just knocked them senseless and left them here.
What makes sap sacred, I wonder. Druids are so funny. \n\nOh no! Joslin! I just remembered! She's turning into a tree! We need to get back to Druid Fenas. He's going to save her. And maybe me!

Right. That was in my report. Since Sir Stefan sent you, I could use your help. Scout the cave. We have to find the prisoners and free them.\n\nI'll follow once my knights recover. Just watch out. The Sea Elf who beat them is somewhere inside.

With the freezing spell the druid gave me. Be careful, there's just the one.\n\nLook, I'm not getting close to the lava. Not like this. So you take the spell. It will cool down the fire shard without extinguishing it. Make it safe to carry. For awhile.

Captain Siravaen of the Gilded Blades. You'd call me a pirate, I suppose. But I'm not one of Sealord Nalos's traitors, and I'm not involved in all this druid foolishness.\n\nYou look confused. Must be from the continent. Yes, I'm a Maormer.

Well, they're not captives anymore. And you and I need not be enemies. Sealord Nalos is my quarry, for reasons of my own. But I'll tell you this much, mercenary. Nalos seeks some sort of druid relic. Calls it a sacred seed.

I'm not sure. That slimy eel escaped and he took one of the druids with him. Probably thinks she can take him to that seed. No matter, I'll find him.\n\nWarn your allies about the sealord, mercenary. Galen isn't safe while he lives.

It seems that way. This one supposes he should not be surprised. A spy faking their own death happens more often than you may think.\n\nBut why? What of the treasure, this Redblade persona? Raz smells a rotten tale lurking beneath his whiskers.
They … can be. Everything Archdruid Devyric plants grows pain and death. First he attacks fellow druids and now he corrupts nature itself?\n\nHe has to be stopped.

I've heard of magic twisting nature spirits, but it's never happened to the ones here. They're old and powerful, dating back to when the first druids landed here. Corrupting them … I don't know how Archdruid Devyric managed it.

It's a cavernous place where the voices of the roots can be heard. Some druids like to sit with the mushrooms and the pools of water and listen to the songs of the plants. \n\nI learned the darkness down there holds no comfort for me.

No. Not a bit. Roneiia, Redblade, whatever she calls herself now. Her goal is still the same. To find the Bequest, form a pirate fleet, and plunder the ports of Tamriel.\n\nWe have to stop her from finding the treasure.
Ah, but during our daring escape, Raz helped himself to a few letters. It seems our friend was a prodigious scrivener.\n\nThe letters may have the answers we seek.

Roneiia was a legend among the Eyes of the Queen, five-claw. If she does not want to be found, we have a better chance of sniffing out a sweetroll in a tannery.\n\nLet's look through Grandvache's documents. They may give us a place to start.

Plants talk to one another. The Spirit of Root speaks with all those plant voices. Spend enough time down there and you might start to hear the rootsong yourself.\n\nI don't want to hear what it sounds like after Archdruid Devyric corrupts it.

This enclave hosts the spirts of Stone, Root, and Air. At their daises, druids can commune with the spirits and experience nature as they do. \n\nGaining Stonesight would allow Archdruid Devyric to see all that rests in the rock here.
Maybe that path-traitor thinks it's planted in the ground.\n\nThe spirit won't help him anyway—not when the blood he's spilled still drips into the earth. Sky and dirt have long memories.

Frii was asleep for so long, they need time to adjust and remember who they are. And to figure out the purpose that the Druid King and the ancient wyrd had in mind when they summoned them.\n\nOn Galen, they'll be safe among the Stonelore Druids.

For a bit. I'm sure as sand certain they'll be interested to hear what the Firesong have been up to. But I'll make my way to Galen eventually. So long as Druid Laurel needs my help with this, I'll be there for her.
Question, kindness … curiosity? Awake and asked, plucked and guided.\n\nGalen will tend. Will prompt. Frii was made for druids. The nourisher goes where they need them.

Good thing I sent you to Tuinh, then. The Eldertide rarely need or want our help, but I'm glad we could provide it.\n\nStill, why would the Dreadsails take prisoners to the cove? When Sea Elves take captives, they usually sail off and demand ransom.

The Dreadsails are working with a druid of the Firesong Circle? The Firesong usually have nothing to do with outsiders, let alone Sea Elf pirates.\n\nNow I understand why Laurel seemed so worried … and why the Draoife has been summoned.

What madness! A war among the circles is the last thing Galen needs right now.\n\nI've been invited to observe the Draoife. I'd like you to tag along. Find Laurel in the Vine District here in the city. If she agrees, you can join us.

I may be the son of Count Mornard, but I studied for years with the Stonelore Circle. I hold druid beliefs in high regard. In fact, I share many of them, which is unusual for those not dedicated to their ranks.\n\nIn return, the druids trust me.

The Eldertide Circle has no love of outsiders. If they had their way, we'd get back into our ships and return to High Rock. The circle here on Galen is more forgiving than the Eldertide on High Isle, but they still don't fully trust us.

My father's knights protect the city and the harbor is well fortified. Besides, I think you chased away the Dreadsails for now. Our scouts report they're nowhere to be seen.\n\nBut if you're concerned for my safety, don't be. I can fend for myself.

You know, that's not a bad idea. Few outsiders are permitted to attend the council meetings, but you can attest to what we saw at Tuinh. The Firesong Circle is willing to use force to gather the three sacred seeds, and that's just wrong.

Hmm. Meet me at the Telling Stone, the landmark near the center of the island. It would be easier to simply show you the prophecy, and it's close to Draoife Dell.\n\nBesides, there's someone at the stone you should meet.

A contingent of knights from the Society of the Steadfast entered the castle. Not in and of itself a concern. We are allies, after all. But we weren't informed of a visit. When one of my knights saw them go into the library, she went to investigate.

We must get dramatic! We collapse the cavern, bury the ship, and deny the world the Aquilarios Bequest.\n\nThere's enough stone in this cavern to ensure this treasure is never, ever found. What do you think?
The Ascendant Order? The rogue knights that gave you trouble back on High Isle? What would they be seeking in my castle?

She discovered them ransacking the library. They attacked her, but she was able to fend them off and summon help. My knights routed the villains, but we're unsure if anything was stolen or if there are more of them hiding elsewhere in the castle.

Yves didn't exactly impress Raz with the quality of his operation. Who knows how many people are aware of this place?\n\nAnd if the Covenant, the Pact, or even the Dominion found out? Galen could become a new front in the Three Banners War.

I assumed it would be safe enough locked in a case in the library until I could make other arrangements. We had no reason to believe the relics were in danger.\n\nBesides, I only returned to the castle a moment before you arrived.

Raz hung back in Vastyr to get these. Some alchemical charges. He had them made specially by a Vinedusk Ranger for an operation that never happened. \n\nLook for the pillars holding up the ceiling. Place one on each. And when we're ready … boom.
Next, I head back to the druid and Fauns' Thicket while you go north and meet Octin.\n\nHe can point out the sacred tree where you need to gather the sap from.

At the docks preparing to receive Lord Bacaro's ship and the relief supplies he promised. It never arrived. I suppose that was all part of the ruse, based on what you just told me.\n\nNow let's go make sure the crown is still safely locked away.

Some of the most beloved places on our islands include secluded fishing holes and scenic vistas. The problem is that visitors currently must find such locations on their own, or hire expensive and often dubious guides to reach them.

Visit and survey the sites. Make sure they're safe. We wouldn't want to take our guests into danger!\n\nYou'll find some sites here on High Isle, and others on Amenos. There's a boat that can take you there when you're ready to go to the prison island.

What's it feel like? Like I'm turning into a tree!\n\nMy bones are stretching. My skin has turned to bark. My feet are growing roots. If I stand still too long, I'm afraid I'm going to become planted! The druid has to break the curse. He has to!

To achieve absolute victory in the knowledge trial, the challenge is simple.\n\nYou must answer all of my questions regarding Dragon lore correctly. Surely you'll have no trouble. Do you accept the challenge?
Correct! Next question.\n\nWhat is the name of the Dragon God of Time?
Sorry to say, that's incorrect.\n\nPerhaps you're not yet ready for this test.
Not quite correct, I'm sorry.\n\nPerhaps you need to brush up on your Dragon knowledge, my friend.

If you go back far enough, most Bretons have a druid hiding somewhere in their bloodline, but so many records have been lost. How could he be certain?\n\nRegardless, why the ruse with the peace talks and the Ascendant Order?

Orlaith may have believed in a new age, but Bacaro is leading us toward the Green Scourge! King Kasorayn's prophecy of the return of the Druid King, it predicts two possibilities. Either an era of peace and harmony, or a time of nature run amok.
So Bacaro was behind it all? The attempts on the lives of the alliance leaders, the death of the archdruids? Of Rahval and my father?\n\nWait, Druid Laurel! The staff! Laurel and Frii are in danger!

Siravaen is a mercenary, but she and her Gilded Blade proved themselves trustworthy against the Dreadsails and the Firesong. Since then, we've been paying her to help with the relief efforts. We needed every ship we could hire.
I won't know until I ask. And if she refuses, you'll still have House Mornard at your side in the battle to come.\n\nNow, hurry, my friend. Go make sure the staff and Druid Laurel are safe.

That's … that's so unfair! I don't want to be a tree!\n\nWell, if only one of us can have our life back, I want you to choose Octin. He's too smart to let his mind turn to mush. Or light. Or whatever. Just don't tell him … I'm scared.

Only one? One what? Oh. Oh! That's not fair. I'm pretty sure neither of us wants to stay cursed.\n\nWell, if you can only choose one, you have to choose Joslin. She doesn't deserve to suffer because I made a mistake. Besides, this isn't so bad ….
Somewhat close … but still incorrect.\n\nA good attempt, however!
Oh, interesting. I don't recall any tales of Alessia being a Dragon.\n\nI'm sorry, that's incorrect. But quite intriguing.
Very creative, but no, unfortunately that is incorrect.
Correct again!\n\nTruly, you are a learned scholar of Dragon lore. I will let Captain Samara know you've proven yourself twice over in the trial of knowledge. Well done!
Now that would be a sight.\n\nMy apologies, but that is incorrect.
Yes! Perhaps the most well-known Dragon. It carries quite a power, doesn't it?\n\nAnd finally, what manner of creature typically accompanies a Dragon in battle?

I'm a sprite? Oh yeah, I forgot about that! It's not as bad as I imagined. It feels like a great weight has been lifted off of me, but that could just be that I'm so much lighter now. No flesh or bones, see?\n\nBut poor Joslin. She looks awfully sad.

Druids try to follow Y'ffre's True Way. But when one of us does something like this … betrays the path to the True Way, well, that druid gets shunned. It's difficult to deviate so far from the True Way, but Y'ffre wouldn't want this.

Druids follow Y'ffre's teachings. We strive to find the True Way and live harmoniously with nature. Or, at least that's what I thought we did. This? This would disgust Y'ffre.\n\nArchdruid Devyric and his ilk aren't on the path to the True Way.

Just speculation really. Y'ffre's Path is a sacred place, and such locations contain power if you know how to draw upon it. Bacaro is going to need all the power he can get if he wants to press his claim as the Druid King.

A fair question. Dhulef likes to tease me about it. Says I love an unsolvable mystery. So much of Druid King Kasorayn's story and the origin of the druids is more legend than fact. I want to learn the truth about who we are and where we came from.

What can I say? A pirate washed ashore near my home and me and some other druids nursed him back to health. He fascinated me, and he seemed equally intrigued with us.\n\nWe shared all sorts of stories and he even showed me how to use his cutlass.

I wanted to hear all about pirating, and he asked about druids. After he recovered, he decided to give up his old life and study magic with the Mages Guild.\n\nDhulef's tough as bark. I've known him for ten seasons and love him like an uncle.

She's definitely on the mend, but she should be resting. Running after the so-called Ascendant Lord can be hazardous to her condition in a number of ways.\n\nGo after her, my friend. Keep her safe and deal with Bacaro before things get worse.

Lord Bacaro and a contingent of Steadfast knights arrived with their usual crates of supplies. He took me aside. Warned me that the Ascendant Order was after the Druid King's regalia. He wanted to make sure the staff was still safe.

We tried to resist, but we were no match for his knights. Then Bacaro displayed the regalia, proclaimed himself the Druid King, and commanded Frii to follow him. And they did! That's when Lady Arabelle arrived.\n\nWait, Stefan! Is he all right?

Blight it all, but I did just what you'd expect. He's our ally! Or I thought he was.\n\nI showed him that the staff was safe and he grabbed it. Ordered his knights to hold us back. He has all three of the regalia, friend. All three!

How should I know how that blighter thinks? Lady Arabelle told me that he's the Ascendant Lord. Which now makes sense. As soon as he revealed his treachery, his knights threw off their cloaks and revealed themselves to be the Ascendant Order.

In every way! Everything I know tells me the Druid King can command nature. Wield it like a tool or a weapon. If the title is taken by force, the prophecy tells us it begins an age of destruction.\n\nThe Green Scourge.

I'm not sure. Other than Orlaith, no one else has ever attempted to claim the title. At least not to my knowledge. Is it enough to just possess the regalia? Is that why he needs Frii, to legitimize his claim? I'm not sure.\n\nStill, this is bad.

Bad timing. He arrived before I did, so he left me a letter and went on ahead. When he mentioned spotting the Firesong, I couldn't help but worry about him.\n\nNow that you're here, we can go to the meeting place and make sure Dhulef's all right.

I'm not entirely sure. When I asked her about stories concerning the Druid King and the wyrds, it was the first thing she remembered. Like the druids, they mostly keep an oral history, so this tablet must have special meaning.

A council of some of the most influential druids from each circle. They settle disputes and handle concerns across all three circles. I'll bring this to their attention and let them decide what to do about Archdruid Devyric and the Firesong.

Ha! By sand and seas, if they are, they've been looking in the wrong place! After I wrote to Laurel and gave them the slip, I haven't seen them since. But they're still out there. I can feel them in the wind.

I discovered a logbook covering a portion of the druids' journey to Galen. It's strange. Why only document part of the route? I asked Dhulef if he could investigate.\n\nI hope he's off on an adventure. I certainly miss his company and stories now.

We might look an odd pair, but Laurel and I go way back. She pulled my carcass out of the sea after I shipwrecked off the coast of Galen … had the Stonelore Druids take care of me. After that I stopped being a pirate and charted a new course.

I owe her more than just investigating the path of the Druid King, but she's my friend. She showed me that there was more to the world. More to me. \n\nAnd after what happened at the enclave … Firesong dogs! Them being here can't be a coincidence.

That's unfortunate. I know Amenos is dangerous, of course, but I hoped the sites were safe. Still, wouldn't want to lose any paying customers. Incidents like that can positively ruin a business.\n\nHere. Mark the sites we shouldn't include on this map.

Only recently. We were curious at first, not concerned. Frankly, most of my sisters thought druids were just myths. I certainly never met one. When they started setting up camps, we just wanted to keep an eye on them. \n\nMaybe that was naive.

Tablet? No, I've never seen this before. The symbol in the middle, that's similar to one we use to represent nature … and the one on the bottom left looks like a version of the Beldama symbol.\n\nAs for the other two … I don't know what they mean.

Yes. Wyress Tola spoke fondly of your friend. He asked if she knew any stories about the Druid King meeting the wyrds long ago. She seemed to know something, but she wanted to consult the other elders. Maybe that's why the Firesong took her?

Me? I come from a long line of swordmasters that go all the way back to Yokuda.\n\nIn Hammerfell, my father always complained that my blade skills paled in comparison to those of my six brothers. Recently, he decided to send me to Elsweyr to train.

Not anytime soon. In a way, being sent away was the best thing that ever happened to me.\n\nNow, I am a skilled fighter, I have a mentor who values me, and a land worth protecting. I am, as my father would say, a blade that has found its sheath.

Ha! Compared to my father's disappointed scowl, a Dragon's flame is tame as a warm breeze.\n\nI've actually grown quite fond of this land. And I've learned a great deal! I wager I could take on all six of my brothers at once, now.
This one was born here in Elsweyr, but spent many years traveling Tamriel as a mercenary. When I received word about Dragons terrorizing my home, I could not sit idly by. This one had to return.

Let me have your map. The archdruid asked about an ancient ritual site, one we only know through legends. It lies somewhere deep within the Sunken Road. I marked the entrance on your map.\n\nIf you truly want to help, hurry and save Wyress Sorcha.

Any minerals and ores are worth a lot to the people who want them. I make my gold on that fact. People hire me in the hopes I discover something they need.\n\nI search the chosen location and report my findings. The rest is up to them.

Right. All I need is for this cave not to fill up with lava. At least not until I finish my survey. What happens after that, I don't care.\n\nWhen the druids chased me, I saw at least three more crystals on my way back out. We should get rid of them.
That's what I hired you for! To figure out these kinds of things.\n\nMaybe if you tried smashing it? Breaking stuff always fixes something, at least in my experience.

Oh, that doesn't matter. As long as I bring them proof that it's worth their effort to establish a new mine, then everyone will be happy.\n\nAnd then maybe next time, House Mornard will hire me directly instead of going through agents and brokers.

A pressure plate, I think. Some sort of trap put here who knows when and by who knows who.\n\nThat can wait, though. I followed Lord Bacaro in here. He met with a group of druids. Firesong, I think. He promised them vengeance against the Stonelore.

The nature spirit? Yes, they were here. I couldn't quite tell if they were a prisoner or not. Bacaro did say he needed them to talk to Y'ffre's Path, whatever that means.\n\nYou need to go after them, my dear.

Better. I'm afraid you saw a pretty vulnerable side of me at Earthen Root Enclave. The Firesong tore me from the ground and tossed me aside like a blighted weed. Honestly, I'm still recovering. Dhulef's been a big part of that.

By taking my mind off those terrible events. Keeping me focused on my research and helping me learn more about Druid King Kasorayn. \n\nHis friendship is also a comfort. The Mages Guild hasn't changed him. He's still a bolt of lightning on a clear day.

Dhulef is no water lily, but you've seen what the Firesong are capable of.\n\nIf the Firesong and him wind up crossing paths … well, I don't want to leave him on his own for any longer than we have to.

At first, I did not. This one thought they were just mindless beasts loosed upon Tamriel. Samara has since learned that they are quite intelligent.\n\nTo knowingly wreak such havoc, they must be truly wicked. They have earned my hatred.

No one ever said as much. But sure, maybe that's why I've always been so interested. And why not me? I've already learned so much. I need to see where this search takes me.\n\nAnd I won't be intimidated by the Firesongs into abandoning my research.

Confused? Not that I'm aware of.\n\nOh, you mean the forgetting and the rambling and the weird dreams. I have become a glowing ball of light, you know. This could be perfectly natural for someone in my condition. I deserve it. It's my fault, after all.

Octin's usually really level-headed and focused. You may not believe it, but he's the brains behind all our exploits.\n\nSomething happened to him though. More than becoming a sprite. It's like he can't think straight for more than a few moments.

Some of them. But when Dhulef wrote that he spotted more of them here on the mainland ….\n\nI don't know what changed, but the Firesongs went from the most isolated circle to the most violent faster than a tree sheds leaves in the autumn chill.

Up until now, you'd rarely see them outside of Y'ffelon. The Eldertide Druids aren't quite as engaged with the world as my circle, but they don't actively obscure themselves. The Firesong were truly reclusive. Which is why this shift is so odd.

I've been busy! Druid Laurel runs a tight ship, but I'm always happy to help. \n\nSpeaking of help, thanks again for assisting me at Graven Deep. Never would have found that old logbook—not to mention getting out of there alive—without you.

I study the Druid King. I used to think that understanding the shared past of our circles would resolve our differences, but the mystery is what calls to me now.\n\nTruthfully? I wish I was still unaware of all this. Then I'd still have hope.

No amount of magic can make a tree forget its roots. Spirits can be pushed into imbalance, but their nature is not erased. All I have to do is remind it of what it once was. \n\nThis is the art of studying Y'ffre's True Way.

My apologies. In all the excitement, I forgot to introduce myself. I am Sir Stefan Mornard. And this is my father, Count Leonard Mornard. Our house has the honor of governing the isle of Galen for our liege, High King Emeric.

Galen may claim to be a Breton holding, but the druids have lived here for centuries. Some of them don't like city folk, but they certainly defend the coast from pirates.\n\nEspecially the Eldertide Circle. It's not like them to avoid a fight.

One of the three circles of druids in the archipelago. The Eldertide live by the coast and dislike outsiders. The Firesong are recluses, keeping to old places of power. Then there's the Stonelore. I studied with them when I was young.
Time is pressing, but I suppose it's only prudent to find out something about what you're getting into. Which location are you curious about?

It's an old fort, built on Windwrack Point centuries ago to protect Vastyr against attacks from the east. It's not in good repair, but we garrison it as strongly as we can. Yet perhaps not strongly enough.\n\nAnything else?

Tuinh? It's an Eldertide settlement. They have little love for House Mornard, but they like Sea Elves even less. I expected them to put up a stout defense against the Dreadsails, but we haven't heard from them in quite some time.\n\nAny more questions?

Until today, I would have said Suncleft Cove wasn't important at all. It's a pretty enough spot, but there are certainly better places for the Dreadsails to land raiders. I can't imagine what the Sea Elves want there.\n\nIs that all?

I leave that to you. With luck, you'll find allies at the fort or village. But whatever you do, go swiftly. If we fail to meet the Sea Elf threat now, it's only a matter of time before we see them at the walls of Vastyr.

After our last adventure together, I wanted to do more to help Druid Laurel with her exploration of druid history. I came back here to dust off some old books. Ask a few questions. After all, Galen's like a second home to me.

A huge one! Call themselves the Dreadsails. They're a vicious band of pirates that have been causing trouble in the archipelago for some time, but no one realized how large their fleet was. Now they seem more intent on conquest than pillaging.
Just what I said! Whatever happened to his mind when the curse started, it's getting worse. Right now, I'm worried he couldn't remember his own name if his life depended on it.\n\nI miss my cousin.
I started to turn into a tree and I panicked!\n\nI suppose Octin took the brunt of the curse since he transformed immediately. I'm changing slowly. Maybe that means the tablet blames me more.

Not so much as a torchbug trusts a spider! But no one listened. Wyress Tola had us keep an eye on the camps, but that was all. I said we needed to protect ourselves, determine their intentions. Then they showed us.\n\nI wish I wasn't always so right!

He seemed very … impatient. Wyress Tola tried to calm him down, but he didn't listen. He said he needed a wyress to open the path to some ritual site. That the rest of us were expendable. I don't think he cared which of us went with him.

I don't know. Before the druids arrived, Wyress Tola and a few of the other elders were reciting our oral histories. Stories involving druids or the Druid King.\n\nShe never mentioned any ritual site or path like the archdruid asked about, though.

We have some stories about the spirit that sleeps beneath the Sunken Road. They mostly revere and venerate the spirit, which the stories call Frii.\n\nInteresting. I just remembered a verse. "Awake, Frii, when the barons in ivy robes need you most."

No. To be honest, we hardly even think about druids. They've been absent from High Rock for centuries. Our stories talk about a singular entity, the druids of Galen. I suppose I should have realized they'd form subgroups. The wyrds certainly have.

I thought Devyric and Michiel were Firesong renegades, acting of their own accord. But the orders we found, and what Orlaith just said. The Firesong want all the sacred seeds.\n\nArchdruid Orlaith leads the Firesong. This is her doing.

Not as far as I know. The seeds are mentioned in the Dream of Kasorayn—the prophecy of the last Druid King. The Firesong seem to believe its time has come. The other circles, not so much.\n\nPerhaps the Draoife can make sense of all this.

That's a good question. We work with nature spirits all the time, but Frii is unique. They're connected to our past in ways I can only guess.\n\nI'll do my best to make sure my people help Frii in any way we can.

It's not really my place to say, is it? I think Frii would be safe with the Mages Guild, but this is really more of a druid issue than mine. If Druid Laurel thinks Galen is the place for Frii, then I trust her judgment.

Me? I'm a mercenary, mate. A Mages Guild staff-for-hire. When all this trouble started to brew up in Galen, Count Mornard sent word to the guild that he needed a court mage. I was here already, so I got the job.

I wish I knew. Before joining the guild, I spent my days hunting treasure and roaming where the winds took me, not rubbing elbows with nobility. I advise Count Mornard as best I can. Help out where I'm needed and get my hands dirty when I have to.

Why don't you track down Umindior? If I find him, I'll be very cross that he left me alone. And shouting won't help anything.\n\nAlso, not to offend, but I haven't seen you in action yet. I trust myself to scout around without being noticed.

It's a beautiful island in the Systres Archipelago. Galen may be less tame than High Isle, but I like it. House Mornard oversees the main city of Vastyr, but the rest of the island is wild and free. In that wilderness, the Stonelore make their home.

Hmm. I assume this was at least in part a test of sorts. To see if he could actually call forth a spirit and command it. Plus, he wanted to prove to his followers that he is worthy of the Druid King's regalia.

Forest wraiths! Where? No, I'm not floating a lichen's width farther. You can fight those horrible forest spirits on your own. You've still got all your limbs, after all. \n\nThe sap tree is just over there, in that cave. Don't get squashed like a bug!

I dropped the tablet. Slipped right through the fingers I no longer have. I broke it. And if Joslin hadn't tried to help me, I'd be the only one cursed. \n\nBut maybe Druid Fenas will save us. Druid Fenas … and you. Let's head back to Fauns' Thicket.
Are you suggesting that the Eldertide have anything to do with the treachery of the Firesong, outsider?

The keep is built over an old Eldertide village. A cave at the foot of the bluffs leads to the castle's dungeons. I think they're holding Druid Niraya there, as well as Sir Stefan. And … I had Niraya hide our seed there before the place was seized.

Hmm. One of our druids was captured in the attack on Tuinh. I've had scouts searching all over for her, and they tracked the Dreadsails to Castle Tonnere. It's a ruined keep on Galen's northwest shore.

An effective course on Dragon slaying, courtesy of the Elsweyr Dragon Defense Force. \n\nAs of late, the scaly beasts have caused far too many deaths. To combat this, this one put together a proper training program for both amateurs and veterans alike!
We shall see if you're up to the task.\n\nSpeak to this one's apprentice, Taz, for more details. He can say more about each of the trials themselves.

Three trials. First, you must retrieve a piece of vital Draconic knowledge. Second, test your combat prowess by securing a Defense Force standard from the depths of a dungeon. Finally, you must present to me a fresh Dragon heart.\n\nAre you interested?
Excellent. Samara had a feeling.\n\nSince your last training, the Dragons have no doubt become stronger. A refresher course is always useful. Tell me, do you remember the trials?

Indeed. You must recover a piece of lost knowledge, claim a Defense Force banner left in one of Elsweyr's dungeons and bring me back a fresh Dragon heart. \n\nAre you ready to show what an Elsweyr Dragon Defense Force veteran is made of?
Good luck to you then. This one eagerly awaits your results.

Like most nobles, my father pays little attention to the druids. When he must speak with the circles, he summons emissaries to Vastyr.\n\nThe Draoife is a meeting of druid leaders. Outsiders are rarely permitted, but they consider me almost a druid.

Somewhere he can further strengthen and consolidate his power, especially since he knows we're on to him.\n\nDruid Laurel is examining the stone carvings. Perhaps they can tell us something. Take a look and talk to her, dear.

The trust of the Eldertide isn't easy to earn. Ellic would not reveal the hiding place of their seed unless he truly thought you might find Stefan in the castle.\n\nSo, will you truly attempt to rescue Sir Stefan and recover the Eldertide seed?

Like so much of the ancient knowledge that remains, these carvings are open to interpretation.\n\nObviously we can see the spirits of the Green, forces of nature in the bosom of Y'ffre. Then we see a spirit slumbering beneath Mount Firesong.

Sealord Nalos locked up three of my crew. I'm going to free them and kill the bastard. Unfortunately, the Dreadsails are here in greater numbers than I anticipated. Which makes me wonder how you plan to rescue the lordling they have in there.

The last Druid King gave one seed to each circle long ago. He also gave us a prophecy, the Dream of Kasorayn. Some druids consider it a warning, but Archdruid Orlaith and others believe it's a call to action.

I saw Nalos and some Firesong Druids arrive with a captive noble in Mornard colors. The druids left shortly after, but their prisoner stayed behind. Now you're here. Not hard to put wind and wave together.\n\nSo what's your plan?

A foolhardy rescue attempt? Perfect! Just the diversion I need. That should give me the chance to find my crewmates and confront Sealord Nalos.\n\nTake your secret path—I'll find another way in. We'll hit them from two directions.

He's a traitor and a murderer. The Gilded Blades used to lead the Dreadsails Fleet. We were loyal to King Orgnum and the Pyandonean Armada. But Nalos was not satisfied with that. He challenged my brother Siraesar for leadership.

Very much so. And the spirit must be extremely powerful, due to how sacred Mount Firesong is.\n\nI think that's what the final carving tells us. Let the sleeping spirit lie. For generations, that's been one of the Firesong's primary purposes.

No, not like you mean. We have enclaves, small communities of druids working together to keep the True Way.\n\nWe have a larger camp which should serve as a safe haven for Frii—at least until we know what Frii wants to do next.

Even the fish bisquits? That's excellent news! You don't know how much I appreciate you trying them for me. Even a bite of any of those dishes would make me ill for a week!\n\nNow, what did you think about the fishing holes and scenic viewpoints?

I suspected you'd like that dish. It's a local favorite! As for the others, I was hoping to include them. Ah, well. I'll find something better to replace them with.\n\nWhat about the fishing holes and scenic viewpoints? Are they all safe for tourists?

That's … disappointing. Still, better to know that now than find out when my customers complain about the quality of our supposedly excellent cuisine. I'll need to find a better chef. I know we have good food on the islands.\n\nWhat about the sites?

Joslin has never been fond of nature. She prefers the indoors to outside. Hates the bugs and the dirt and the weather. I wonder if we could plant her in a building. That might make this more bearable for her.\n\nIf we can't break the curse, that is.

Octin's a ball of light! How do you expect he's doing? He's getting more confused with every passing moment. I suppose I'd find it hard to think if all I had for a head was a pulsating sparkle.\n\nHey, could we get on with the curse breaking now?

Someday a new Druid King will appear to take the Ivy Throne. Kasorayn led our withdrawal from the mainland, but he also saw a day when druids would once again take their place in Tamriel.\n\nFor good or ill.

The dream is a promise and a warning. Some druids believe we're destined to bring a Green Renewal to Tamriel. To teach everyone to live in harmony with nature.\n\nOthers fear a Green Scourge, when nature runs amok and the tyranny of druids takes hold.

Kasorayn was the last of the druid kings. In an age long past, he led our people from High Rock to Galen. They hoped to find a land where druids could live in peace and follow Y'ffre's teachings as they understood them.

He chose no successor before he died. Instead, Kasorayn recognized the three circles and told them to govern themselves. Together, in peace. And so the Draoife, the council of druids, came into existence.\n\nThe Draoife has guided us ever since.

The sacred seeds were given into the care of the three Druid Circles by Druid King Kasorayn, to keep and guard until the time they would be needed. That's what the prophecy says, but the actual meaning has been debated for centuries.

The Dream of Kasorayn. I've been fascinated by the stories of the Druid King since I read the prophecy inscribed on the Telling Stone. Of course, each of the circles interprets its meaning differently.\n\nJust one of the many things we disagree about.

Who knows why those foul sacks of root rot do anything? Obviously, they wanted to take possession of the Stonelore sacred seed. But why they want to acquire a nature spirit from the mainland … I have no idea.\n\nMaybe we're all just chasing legends.

Let's see. Fascinating! This is certainly worthy of the trial of knowledge. Well done! I'll see to it that this information is passed into the records of the Elsweyr Defense Force. \n\nAre you interested in the additional challenge?
Excellent!\n\nFirst, what is a Dragon's main form of conveyance? How do they most often get around, so to speak?

Dreadsail interrogation tactics aren't subtle. They pressed me for information about Vastyr—defenses, weaknesses, those sorts of things. Sealord Nalos obviously has ambitions in Galen beyond the bargain he made with the Firesong Circle.
He might, or it might be stored somewhere in his chambers. Get the key however you can … but I'll shed no tears if you dispatch Goriadh.

Not easily. This lock has some sort of arcane reinforcement—you won't be able to pick it. We need the gaoler's key.\n\nHe's a fearsome brute called Goriadh. His chambers are across the hall to the east. That's how he comes and goes, at least.

The Sea Elf that hunts others of her kind? Banneret Corrick told me about Suncleft Cove. An unlikely ally.\n\nI don't mean to complicate things, but there's another prisoner. An Eldertide druid named Niraya. We must rescue her as well.
Then we must rescue Niraya and get her to tell us how to find the seed. We need to retrieve it before Sealord Nalos.\n\nCome, friend. The interrogation chamber is through the door to the north.

The archdruid sent you? Then perhaps there's still hope. I hid the seed in an ancient Eldertide shrine below the castle. But Sealord Nalos forced me to tell him how to find it.\n\nIf only I'd been a little stronger.

There's an ancient tree in the castle's upper courtyard. The door to the shrine lies hidden within its roots. Captain Uldiss heads there as we speak.\n\nPlease. Don't let the Sea Elves take the sacred seed.

Nothing more to tell. He's got a massive fleet and it's going to sail straight for Vastyr. He's just waiting for the Firesong to provide their support. That won't come until they get the Stonelore relic. At least, that's what Nalos indicated.

Gather more of the Gilded Blades from wherever Nalos stashed them. Then wait for another chance to kill the bastard. Who knows? Maybe I'll come to Vastyr, since I know Nalos will be there.\n\nAs long as we share an enemy, I'm on your side.

I … I can hardly believe it. Too many Eldertide fell to Firesong treachery and Dreadsails blades. I was sure we had lost our sacred seed as well.\n\nI'll hold onto this for now. If Archdruid Orlaith wants the seed, she can pry it from my dead hands.

Then we'll give them a fight. The Breton lords and I have our differences, but they build mighty walls. The Eldertide will help defend them. You have my word.\n\nOh, young Sir Stefan wants to speak with you. He said to find him at Castle Mornard.
Quen? Job? That can wait, lovely.\n\nI'm quite thirsty. Could you bring the water bucket? You wore me out.
Damn it all to Oblivion! At least Laurel is all right.\n\nI've assembled what knights I can spare, but we could really use Siravaen and the Gilded Blades. Maybe you can convince her to help.

I'd appreciate it. I've been banging my head against that particular wall for hours now.\n\nRemind her that if Lord Bacaro takes control of the archipelago, any safe ports she has on Galen will evaporate like a drop of water in a hot skillet.

And that concerns me how exactly? \n\nIf druids want a king or not, that's their business, not mine. Sealord Nalos was my problem, and I took care of it. What happens on Galen next doesn't matter to me.

That … is certainly something I hadn't considered. I do like the safe haven that the lordling has provided us with.\n\nAnd what was that about allies? Bacaro is working with the Firesong? All right, you convinced me. My ship is yours—for now.

Just because our purposes aligned once, doesn't mean we'll sail side-by-side forever, mercenary. We both wanted Nalos dead and now he is. That was a win for both of us.\n\nI'd need a more compelling reason to risk my crew again.
The waterfalls? I'd rather not discuss the waterfalls. That area is very … private. Not a place for those outside our circle.\n\nStill, if that's where the Firesong Druid went, we need to check.
There were a lot of them in the raiding party. They must be somewhere. Come on, the waterfall's on the north wall of the valley. Let's keep looking.

Sleight of hand, my dear. Count Stefan and Captain Siravaen landed farther up the beach. While our allies draw their attention at the main entrance, you and I will follow in their wake and find another way into the mountain.
Laurel wasn't sure, but she thinks she remembers a cave to the right of the main entrance. Let's search around. If nothing else presents itself, we'll see where that cave leads.

That's … unexpected. We normally don't get involved with wars and politics. But the Firesong started this, so I guess that makes it a druid problem.\n\nLook, we're practically surrounded by the Firesong and Dreadsails out here. I could use your help.

The blessing I bestowed upon us before we set out must be keeping the motes at bay. Given the power we just saw, I'm not sure how much longer that protection will last.\n\nI suppose you'll need to accompany me into the tunnels.

Let me see. Right. It's coming back. I heard Neri guarded it. The relic. I followed her. We came here.\n\nShe grumbled about this. Said two idiots went where they didn't belong. Activated it. Her anger made things more fun.

The Dreadsails have a beachhead at Broken Oar Cove, just northeast of here on the shore. Retrieve the everflame torch and meet me at Veil's Bluff to the west. That's where we need to go to light the beacon.

We need to light the beacon that will gather every Stonelore druid on Galen to Glimmertarn. However, the Dreadsails grabbed the everflame torch in a recent raid on the village. We need that enchanted torch to ignite the beacon.

No. But hey—now we know two people who can tell us. Minahel locked them in a cell on the beach. Maybe they're mad about that? Let's see if they'll tell us something.\n\nI'm pulling it together, but I still need a moment. I'll meet you at the cell.

Oh, I learned a great deal. Wait, you mean about the job. I've told you what I remember. Neri's a guard. Two idiots. An activated relic, whatever that means.\n\nThe Sea Elves are typically private types. Hard to read and keep to themselves.
It is a sacred place, outsider. The tunnels lead to ritual chambers, the muse-mouth plants … and to the Spirit of the Path, the Chronicle.\n\nHopefully, my Gwenaelle is also somewhere inside.
You do not hear their song? I hear it. Yes, I can guide you to the seeds. They are my purpose. I cannot be kept from my purpose. Bound, yet there is choice.\n\nWhat is your purpose?

Frii senses the seeds within the vale. After all the trouble Orlaith caused to get them, she won't let them out of her sight.\n\nThere's a door at the heart of Ivyhame. A place of the Druid King. It hasn't been opened in centuries. Maybe she's there?
Long ago, mortal hands taught the stones of this place a song. A promise. A greeting. Not a song for mortals. A song for … me. \n\nI must look upon the door in the hillside.

Yes, the song is louder in here. More … insistent. It wants to fulfill its purpose. Like me. Like the seeds.\n\nThe song is from King Kasorayn's season, but it is not from the Druid King. Not exactly ….

Though I slumbered, I learned much from my time with the wyrds. They would drink the elixir and commune with me. Teach. Talk. Listen.\n\nGather herbs from each part of the garden and I will create the elixir.
Has it been so long since you served as my apprentice, Aiven? Have you forgotten the Temple of Y'ffelon? \n\nOur misguided brothers and sisters defile this most hallowed place with their violence.

Remember everything you see, Aiven. When the prophecy is fulfilled and a new king arises, the seeds must be brought here and blessed by the Sower I spoke of in my Dream. You must preserve this moment to instruct the Sower.\n\nNow, go help Verline.
Gather the sacred seeds. Help me summon Urdiir the Guardian. A powerful ally for the Sower … a protector to ensure that only a worthy king regrows the seeds. Then ….
Wild and fierce. A spirit called from the Green, like I was. \n\nIt is bound to protect crown, staff, and gauntlet. The Firesong risk much to awaken its anger.
I no longer sense Druid Laurel nearby. If the Firesong took her, they would go to Archdruid Orlaith. To Y'ffelon.\n\nA ploy, I think. To capture me.
Perhaps, if the balance is restored. A new spirit must fill the void in Mount Firesong's heart.\n\nI will be that spirit.

Frii was able to contain all that power? They saved the archipelago, the alliance leaders … all of us.\n\nBut where's Frii now? Why didn't they return with you? You said they took the place of the spirit. What does that mean?

It's just as well. As long as the druids remain divided, they aren't ready for a new king. And I'm not sure how Emeric and the others would react to another royal in their midst.\n\nWell, talk to our friends, dear. Then we should return to Vastyr.
I've helped the worst of the wounded. Most of them are more shaken than they are hurt. But I doubt they would have survived if they hadn't made it to Glimmertarn.
It was an accident. No idea what went wrong. One moment I could see, the next? No eyes at all.\n\nDon't ask me how I know you're there. I have no idea.

Ah. Heh. The sea witches found a druid shrine inside a buried cavern. They think it's dedicated to, hmm, passion.\n\nThe relic was inside. Laniwys and I heard that people felt warm and excited when they got close. It intrigued us.

The beacon is used in times of danger to alert the Stonelore Druids spread across the island and summon them back to Glimmertarn. The enchantment contained in the everflame torch allows the beacon's light to be seen from anywhere on Galen.

I'd like you and Druid Laurel to make sure the seed and Frii are all right. Laurel believes Frii took it to Clohaigh—an old cave they've visited often since coming here. We had mostly forgotten about the cave, but Frii seems drawn to the place.

By Y'ffre and the Green, I can rally my people and the Eldertide who seek refuge here. I need you and Laurel to check on Frii and the seed. With the Dreadsails and Firesong scouring the area, it's only a matter of time before they're discovered.

Hmm. Stefan needs to bolster his army and wants to do so with the Stonelore and Eldertide? I suppose that makes some sense. We can defend ourselves, and it is our third circle that has gone rogue.\n\nI can pledge the Stonelore to this cause.
Let me talk to Ellic. If anyone can convince him to bring his people to the city to help defend its walls, it's another archdruid.\n\nInstead, I want to send you to Glimmertarn.

Of course. Why else surround us? Why else steal the everflame torch?\n\nAt least they haven't made it to the beacon. It's ready. It will call the Stonelore to Glimmertarn like a songbird guiding them home. Did you get the torch?
Good. Then go ahead and ignite the beacon. Hurry, before any of those Dreadsails spot us.

Not that I'm aware of. There are some druid carvings and such, but I haven't had a chance to study them. The whole place is overgrown with vegetation.\n\nThe cave did fascinate Frii though. Something kept drawing them back here.

A few times, yes. I'd try to clean up a little while Frii looked around. Sometimes they'd sit and meditate for long stretches. When we find them, this time I'm going to ask what that was all about.\n\nNow let's go help Frii!

Frii is Frii. Place made by Druid King. Sang to me. The walls, taught me. Told me who I am. The Sower of the sacred seeds, curator of the regalia. When season is right, I will grow them from the seeds.\n\nExpected the seed to be safe here. It was not.

Good. I am … thinned. Tired. Wilting. I have grown too tall. Take the seed to Archdruid Rahval. His to nourish now, to protect. Slip within the walls, face the storm. \n\nClaim the seed and let us leave this place.

Despite the efforts of the Firesong and their Sea Elf allies, we still possess our sacred seed. I fear this means that the assault on Vastyr will begin soon.\n\nNow—oh, Sir Stefan. Here? That bodes ill. Perhaps you should speak to him, druid-kin?
