Good. Once we hear Stefan's news, I'll order our druids to head for the city. I think Druid Laurel and Frii should remain here, however. To guide any stragglers. And to keep the nature spirit hidden from Archdruid Orlaith.\n\nThank you again, friend.

Dhulef was following the Druid King's path when he found an ancient logbook. It was from one of the druid ships that never made it to the Systres. The logbook contained an entry that indicated the Druid King met with the wyrds before setting sail.

I don't know! Maybe because I didn't stop Octin from breaking it? Or that we … procured it without asking permission? I don't know how any druid magic works!\n\nThat's why we asked Fenas to help. He's a druid. He knows about this stuff!
Squawk! No prey! Prey!\n\nThis half sleeps beneath the shade, in tangled roots of tunneled glade. A stream of fire cuts the trees, yet south of home for he who sees.
Fauns' Thicket. Some druid went there to study the Fauns and left all her things behind. It's a little old and outdated, but our fence said we could get a good price for whatever we brought him.

Not stealing, procuring. That old place is abandoned. The druids are content to just let nature claim it. But there's someone on this island who will pay a lot of gold for some dusty journals and stuff.\n\nWe couldn't pass up the opportunity.

Oh. Remember Veshin, the Sea Elf when you found me? That explains his advances. Hmm, I have mixed feelings about that.\n\nWe can't take the relic from Llanshara while it's still affecting people. But, I know how to learn the Sea Elves' plan for it.

I'll ask Veshin join me for a picnic. Get him relaxed. You bring some delicacies while I turn on the charm.\n\nI saw some blue-backed siltcrabs in the tide pools. Grab some and meet me at that nice grotto to the east. I'll entice Veshin to join me.
I skulked around as many Sea Elf homes as I could while you found Umindior. Looking for the relic, of course. But don't blame me if I picked up a little extra.
I'm not a druid. How should I know how long the stupid spell will last? Just be quick and everything should be fine.\n\nI'll wait right here.

The Chronicle's always been more emotional than other nature spirits. It comprehends the experience of mortals and feels our emotions vicariously through the stories it shares.\n\nI've felt its calm, its joy, and even its grief. But this ….
Pay! Pay!\n\nThe second piece is within reach, between vaster shores and wind-wracked beach! Craft approach with spade in hand, eye the cauldron and turn the sand! Squawk! Sand!
Key! Key! Time for riddle three! \n\nThe sun-warmed side of Singer's path is where you'll find your prize. Hang Gloomlantern upon your ship to shroud her from all eyes!

Thanks to you and Dhulef, I wasn't harmed. My fellow archdruids … weren't so fortunate.\n\nStill, we moved our sacred seed to a new location, known only to a few of the Stonelore. And I'm sending Laurel to keep Frii safe. I pray it's enough.

Archdruid Orlaith believes in a literal interpretation of the Dream of Kasorayn. She sees the signs of the season as proof that the prophecy is upon us.\n\nThat's why she seeks to gather all three sacred seeds. And why she wants Frii.

Mount Firesong rises above Y'ffelon, but its roots extend throughout the archipelago. It gives the islands their hot springs and steam vents. Usually these are curiosities, not particularly dangerous. But this recent activity is concerning.

Seen? No. But I've overheard some of the sentries talking about a druid they're holding somewhere in the castle. Maybe even the same one Nalos took from Suncleft Grotto.\n\nAha. You think that relic he's looking for might be here, too?

Keep your little secrets, then. I don't have any interest in druids or their sacred relics. But if I find something that belongs to them, I'll be happy to turn it over. For a suitable finder's fee, of course.

It's an old saying. The druids we knew embraced so-called civilization. They were as bad as the city-dwellers. Wyrds seek the beauty of unmarred nature, isolation. The stories give the impression that the druids of old found our ways … unsavory.

As much as I want to confront Archdruid Orlaith at your side, I have responsibilities. I'm heir to my father's title. And his duties. From this day forth, I must think of the people of Galen first. \n\nThey need to see that House Mornard still stands.

Is there anywhere I can guarantee Frii's safety? Archdruid Orlaith laid siege to Vastyr to get the sacred seeds. She will come for Frii. I trust Laurel to make sure Frii isn't easy to find. But that puts Laurel in danger, too.

I … I don't know. And our other archdruids died in the attack on the Draoife. At some point I'll need to send for an elder or archdruid from High Isle, but for now we're on our own. In the meantime, I'll do my best to lead the way Rahval taught me.

No, that doesn't feel right. I think we should bring Frii along. If Frii can sense where the seeds are, they can lead us straight to them. Or tell us if Archdruid Orlaith takes the seeds somewhere else.\n\nThere's another reason, too.

For all my time studying the history of Druid King Kasorayn, that's been one of my primary questions. Is the Ivy Throne a metaphor? Is there an actual throne, like the one High King Emeric sits upon? We just don't know for sure.

Kasorayn, the last Druid King, didn't reign from a fine palace or grand keep. Instead he set the Ivy Throne in a sacred vale, Ivyhame. It was the heart of the druid realm in the early days of Galen. It fell into ruin after Kasorayn's death.
No. Before they were … distant. Quiet. Whispers and dreams. Now that the seeds are together, they stir again. They are finding their voices. Remembering what they are. Calling out to me.
If this is the appointed season, the seeds will grow. If it is not, no power can make them act against their nature.

The Dreadsails are a spent storm. Leaderless. I don't think they could muster another major attack. And the Firesong got what they wanted—Archdruid Orlaith has the sacred seeds. But I think we're a long way from safe.

I sense spirits called from the Green. Bound into the shapes of fauns and darker forms to defend this place.\n\nThey … may not know me. They have waited a very long time. Forgotten themselves and grown wild. Be careful, Laurel-friend.

Spirits are bound to purpose. We do not change. But the purpose King Kasorayn gave me was to make a choice for him. He could not know how to make the choice, so he did not bind me. I can grow. Learn. Decide.

Druid Laurel talked about it. It stands on the island of Y'ffelon. A cathedral of the Green, long ago. Still sacred. Now we know Urdiir waits there.\n\nI have never been in that place. But I remembered it in the elder's memory.

From seeds were the crown, staff, and gauntlet called forth. To seeds we must return them. \n\nYou have heard my dream, Aiven. How the Sower will one day awaken, once the schism that divides our people is finally mended.

These troubled times confuse even me, my friend.\n\nVerline is my closest counselor. A loyal Firesong, all too familiar with the threat posed by those sworn to the Allwither. He is in danger, too, from those who call him a traitor to their cause.

Laurel, captured? Is there no end to this outrage? Our own forces are still recovering from the siege of Vastyr, but even at full strength we'd be hard pressed to assault the Firesong on their island.\n\nWhat of Frii? Did the spirit return with you?

If we must do this … then yes, we need the light of Mara's Tear and Shandar's Sorrow.\n\nOn each side of the balcony stands a druid stone. Turn them both to face the sacred pool. That will call the light of the moons to sanctify this place.

Touch the mote to begin the summoning … I will do the rest. Urdiir is a spirit from the Green. It will protect this place until a new Druid King arises. \n\nUrdiir will keep its vigil until the Sower decides the season of the seeds has come again.

That task I leave in your hands. Rally the circles against those who follow the Allwither.\n\nDefeat them. Bind them in the mountain. Then … let them be forgotten. There can be no healing while druids seek power and harm one another.
He didn't go into detail about what happened to him, but he keeps complaining about how sore he is. He doesn't seem all that reliable.\n\nHonestly, I'm not so sure how good a thief he even is.
Y'ffre is the Singer, right? And sun-warmed could mean the south. The south side of Y'ffre's Path, on the north side of Galen!\n\n… Right?

Legends tell us that the Green and its spirits can summon forest wraiths to protect themselves. The Chronicle felt threatened, so it did the same.\n\nI'm not sure if this is how all forest wraiths are created, but we saw what the Chronicle did.
Sounds fun. But, also, distracting. Imagine the effects of carrying it through Vastyr. Heh. Hmm.\n\nNo, eventually we need to get paid. There must be a way to stop it.

Why sail into danger no one returns from? For the fun, of course.\n\nMore so, I'm tracing the path of a legend from history—the Druid King. As he traveled to the Systres Archipelago, he went through Graven Deep. I'd like to know what happened there.

Some might say I used to be, but in my heart I never ceased. I once cut through the waves of the Abecean with vigor. However, some days back I put that aside and joined the Mages Guild.\n\nThe chance to sail into danger once more makes me quite joyful.

While the Firesong call Y'ffelon home, I suspect Orlaith will keep him close until she acquires the seeds from the other druid circles. He could be on a Dreadsails ship, but I doubt the Firesong would trust their allies with such precious cargo.

A hard question … but a fair one. My house has always found it wiser to let the druids take care of their own affairs. Most of them dislike us as it is. Imagine their resentment if Mornards took sides in all their petty disputes.

I blame his mother. Viselle took an interest in druid teachings when she came to Galen. She shared that interest with our son. \n\nWhen Viselle died … well, I could not forbid something Stefan had shared with his mother.

Yes, we're members of the Eldertide Circle.\n\nYou're fortunate that I need your assistance. Outsiders aren't usually permitted to set foot in our sacred sites. But Y'ffre sent you, so who am I to question that?
Do tell? Well, go ahead. After everything you've done for the people of the archipelago, you've earned the right to be direct with me.

Again? I thought my knights ran them off after that terrible business with my brother. Thank you for bringing me the news. I'll send a battalion to deal with them right away.\n\nI know how this must look, but I am not in league with those malcontents.

Lady Arabelle poisoned? Is she all right? But what was that about wine? I haven't placed any orders recently, not while the castle is still in disrepair. And I haven't appointed a new seneschal since that trouble with Steward Hercian.

Did he? Well, I want the Ascendant Lord brought to justice, the same as you.\n\nThat wine that poisoned Lady Arabelle. Was it a Dufort Singular Amber, vintage 571? I received a similar gift this morning. It's in the knight-commander's private chamber.
I heard that story many and many times in my youth. I've no idea the truth of it. But, I always deemed it wise to take the warning.\n\nOne way or another, I suppose I'll find out.

Perhaps, but there's a depth to this emotion I've never felt before. It unnerves me. \n\nLet's hurry. My Gwenaelle is in here somewhere and my fear for her safety grows with every passing moment. The door is just over there.

Blue-back siltcrabs! Isn't she a delight, remembering my love for them. Now I have two delicious creatures before me.\n\nYou know I'm a sea witch? Quite a powerful one. Would you like to see my power? I think I'll soon be stronger than Minahel.

We have a chamber of study up along the cliffside. It allows us to watch the other Dreadsails from above. The view is quite beautiful.\n\nPerhaps you two could join me. I impressed Minahel so much, she honored me with a key to our inner caves.

We assign tasks, perform rites, do some healing. I focus on defending Llanshara from intruders. No one escapes my notice.\n\nI just told our lovely friend about a relic we found. It has affected some of our weaker crew. Not me. I'm too strong-minded.

Minahel found a solution. Naturally, I'm the one who inspired her.\n\nWe infused a ship's sail cloth with a counter-magic spell. It's quite complicated, but covering the relic should muffle the effect. Then our brethren can return to their labors.

As we discussed and you no doubt noticed, the letter was unsigned. My knight commander insisted on having someone else taste the wine before she would allow any to pass my lips.\n\nI'm just glad you arrived before that happened.

Possibly? The Chronicle transformed  Gwenaelle into one of those things. It should be able to turn her back and return her to me.\n\nI know I've asked a lot of you, but please come with me. We need to talk to the Chronicle. Convince it to release her.

Then your answer may be right outside. I told the sentry to have them wait by the jousting tents until I was ready to deal with the mix up.\n\nTalk to the courier and find out who hired them to deliver the incriminating bottles of wine to my castle.

To sow confusion and weaken House Dufort, of course. And to further delay the peace talks. Perhaps even scuttle them completely. I have political rivals, but none who would stoop to murder.\n\nIf I had to guess? This is the work of the Ascendant Order.

I fear we'll find the Ascendant Lord's hand on the tiller of most of the recent events that have plagued the archipelago. Call it a feeling deep in my bones.\n\nIn the meantime, talk to this courier and see what they reveal about whoever hired them.

A rare silver flower that's considered a delicacy by the Sea Elves. Grows on certain trees near the beaches in this part of the island. \n\nLucky for us, I saw some just southwest of here, up the hill a bit. I took note of it while scouting.
I heard. If we can get him to tell us how to contain the relic, we can sneak into the caves and grab it.\n\nGo get the silverbloom. I'll keep him talking. Talking with those wet, blue lips of his.

Ha, a fair question. Before the Mages Guild, I sailed all across the Abecean Sea. I dare claim that no one knows these waters like I do.\n\nLaurel wanted to trace the Druid King's voyage and fortunately, this old pirate owed her a favor.

Start near the Dreadsail ships to the east. Look for anyone weaving cloth into a covering of some sort.\n\nI'll scout the upper cliffs to find the sea witch caves. We'll use the key to slip inside and grab the relic.

Ha! This one knew you had the look of a Dragon slayer! There's a fierceness in your eyes that only those who have faced such a foe can boast.\n\nWorry not. The Elsweyr Defense Force's program is not just for those fresh to the field.

Killing Dragons is a talent that can be honed just like any other. These trials serve not only to teach newcomers, but to improve upon that which skilled fighters already have. And you will no doubt inspire others around you.

Then we're ready. Let's sneak in, grab the relic, then leave. The Dreadsails are still distracted, so as long as we don't cause a ruckus, we should be fine. We've already drawn enough attention to ourselves as it is.

I suppose we must. But only once we have the relic in hand. The buffoon has almost ruined this job a dozen times now. I bet two gold that he's exactly where you found him the last time.\n\nAll right, ready? Let's go.

I sure do. That's Umindior's medallion. He was very proud of it. Earned it in a Tribute tournament or something.\n\nSeems he followed his—well, not his heart—right into trouble. Let's hurry before those sea witches kill him.

In whatever way this one could, yes. Samara came to realize that her time spent as a mercenary could be useful to others. This one learned much throughout my journeys— if I could share that and save lives? There was no question in my mind.

Yes, friend of Laurel. Powerful magic anchored by druid stones. I hear them. They are not far.\n\nFind the stones and awaken them. Two north, one west. Let them know I am here. Then the door will open for me.

Hmm. That sounds like the Ascendant Order. But only a skilled druid could alter plants and create this vile poison. We know they worked with the Eldertide Circle before. Maybe they still have some druid allies assisting them.

The tincture I provided will slow the poison's spread, but it won't hold off the inevitable forever. She should be all right for a while longer, but I do recommend we hurry.\n\nOnce I have a sample of the plants, I know I can craft an antidote.

Interesting. I was informed that those crates were lost at sea, but I suspected there was more going on than a simple accident. Add to that the minor thefts and intruders my knights keep running off … it seems the Ascendant Order has targeted us.

You say you found this with the Ascendant Order? That's one of Lord Bacaro's most prized possessions. He usually keeps it down in the cellars with his collection of trinkets from his adventuring days.\n\nThose thieves were bolder than I thought.

Claiming? The society provides aid to those in need. But it's evident that the Ascendant Order stole from us.\n\nYou're Lady Arabelle's investigator. Would you check the cellars and help me determine how those thieves got past our security?

No, I oversee their dispersal. Lady Juline and the druids Gastoc and Aishabeh can tell you about specific jobs that are available.\n\nEach tend the wilds in their own way, but they all benefit Galen and have been approved by House Mornard.

Indeed. It's been an honor serving House Mornard. First as a scout and soldier, and now as a recruiter finding adventurers like yourself for dangerous assignments. \n\nThe work we do here benefits Galen and all its people.

She's a curious one. Lady Juline wants to make a tour of the island's sights. She needs lone explorers to secure the route.\n\nI think she underestimates the dangers, but if she wants to spend coin to make the wilds safer I won't stop her.

Druid Gastoc represents the Stonelore Circle. He's got a mean look and meaner tasks, but he's a nice fellow once you get to know him.\n\nIf his stories about terrible foes are true, you'll want to bring along a capable party.
Getting the lay of the land before starting a campaign? I can respect that.\n\nWhat would you like to know?

Of course I am. Some may find fault with the house's recent history, but I wholeheartedly believe the count will steer us into a new age of prosperity.\n\nAnd the aid of adventurers such as you will secure this future.
Umindior and I will deliver it. Together. I can't let him take a mote of credit. Maybe I can get his cut of the pay, too.\n\nSpeaking of which—um, the relic, please?
Very well. As they say in adventure novels for the indolent, would you like the long version or the short?

Yes, well … in truth my campaign is a stain on the Adrys family honor. I tried, as best I could, to maintain a respectful distance.\n\nUnfortunately, my nephew Niras became aware of my quest. Veloth forgive me, he chose to follow in my footsteps.
You should know, my family is of no great import. Some minor nobles in a Deshaan village. A cousin in the Fighters Guild. \n\nThat is the extent of our legacy, a ripple in the ocean of time.

You are correct. He fell prey to the blood years ago. I tried to track him. To end him. But for years I heard nothing but silence.\n\nThen, news. The dark knowledge that Niras had … transformed. Metastasized.

Yes. Here, I shall mark your map with the location of his most recent feeding. I will meet you there.\n\nThank you, hunter. Know that when the Worm is ash, some small amount of my pain will be healed.

If you must, but don't let him sway you. I want Octin to go back to the way he was. No one should have to lose their mind and turn into a ball of light. Especially not someone as brilliant as my cousin. Whatever the two of you talk about, choose him.
Joslin? Is my cousin here, too? Did I tell you she hates nature? Abhors it. And trees and flowers make her sneeze.\n\nDon't let her become a tree, friend. Please choose her.
Why not? We restored me. And I'll make it up to Druid Fenas. Give back everything we procured and make amends. He has to help me lift the curse from Joslin if I do all that, right?

Heat to prepare the sap, and sap to bind the stone. The inscription mentions those two ingredients at length. I'll send Joslin to an area outside of Embervine. The lava pools there create fire shards—rocks that retain extreme heat.

Thanks. In the meantime, I'll get Druid Fenas to show me how to care for Joslin. Prune her leaves, water her roots, whatever a tree needs to stay healthy and happy.\n\nThings will work out. I just know they will.

Not on my own. I'm not a scholar or a mage. But with Druid Fenas to help me, we'll find a way to restore my cousin to his rightful form.\n\nLook, I know you were put into an impossible situation. Thanks again for making me not a tree.

Luck won't be a factor. This is a job for skill. My skill as a … procurer of things that aren't mine. And Druid Fenas's skill as a … well, as a druid.\n\nI owe my cousin everything. This is my responsibility now, and I mean to live up to it.

Meet Joslin near Embervine. I'll give her a spell to retrieve a fire shard, but she shouldn't touch them herself. Even with the spell, she's too flammable in her current state.\n\nAfter that, meet Octin near the sacred tree to the north to get the sap.

It's in an obscure druidic script. Luckily, I've made a study of such writing. This one, however, is different. I have no idea what it was doing with Druid Madena's things.\n\nIt would be a lot easier if they hadn't cracked the tablet, I assure you.

The tablet. The part I couldn't translate. Now that the tablet is whole, I see it. "In fire and foliage born, what is broken, only one to restore." It rhymes better in old druidic. \n\nDon't you see. We can lift the curse—but only for one of them.

Y'ffre's Path is a sacred place, with a small community of druids to look after it.\n\nY'ffre set the spirit here, the one we call the Chronicle. It shares stories with us, shows us events that happened long ago.
Besides the Firesong Druids, the very air is thick with spirit motes. You'll see them once we enter the valley.\n\nThe worst are the animals though. They frighten me.

They're dark creatures, filled with rage and longing. Usually they inhabit the deepest wilderness where no druid dares to tread. I've never seen one in these tunnels. They have no purpose here. \n\nThey're dangerous, be wary.

Yes, I saw it, too. The Firesong druid said something about accessing the Chronicle. Could that be what this is all about?\n\nBut something we saw plagues me. The orb. That was the Chronicle, but the spirit has never appeared in a vision before.

There is always a chance, my friend. Anything is possible, as long as we have faith.\n\nI'll do what I can. Study the tablet some more. Consult with the Stonelore elders and archdruids. We may find a way to help Octin. Eventually.

Curses are complicated, but anything is possible. All we need is faith, right, my friend?\n\nI'll show Octin how to care for the Joslin tree while I study the tablet and consult with the Stonelore elders and archdruids. We may find a way. Eventually.

We saw her in the Chronicle's vision, didn't we? And we've yet to find any evidence that she's injured. \n\nStill, this situation is more dangerous than I anticipated. Whatever caused the Chronicle to turn so dark can't be good.

The newly created wraiths went farther into the tunnels. We keep moving and I'm sure we'll meet up with them shortly.\n\nAs for recognizing my wife, she may be a creature of darkness now, but I know I'll be able to identify her when I see her.

The Chronicle defends itself. Not many creatures can withstand this many spores. The only chance of defeating these bloated muse-mouth plants is with Y'ffre's Rain. \n\nWhy the Chronicle grew this many, I cannot fathom. This is more than necessary.

We'll rebuild. Ask more Eldertide to join us. For too long, we relied on the Chronicle to show us our past. To tell us our stories. It's time for us to take responsibility for our own memories, I think.

Fast, confusing, but then it was simple. I had a purpose. There wasn't room for fear.\n\nI'm no more murderous now than I was before. But still, it was odd. If Pitof came any closer, I might have hurt him. That will be difficult to forget.

Ah, no wonder Tava's winds brought us together. Over the years, I've come to rely on Laurel's judgment of character. If she trusted your help, so can I.\n\nTell me, what did you think of the enclave? When I visited it, I found it quite serene.
What? The enclave is gone? Those Firesong dogs and sons of dogs!\n\nPlease tell me—Laurel, how is she? Did they hurt her?

Good, good. I haven't spoken to Laurel in some time. My preparations for this trip kept me too busy.\n\nThank you for telling me. It seems I already owe you a debt. Now that I know she's safe, I can focus on the task at hand.

Don't be surprised when I say this isn't my first shipwreck. A long while back, I washed up near Druid Laurel's home on Galen. She found me, full of seawater and mostly dead.\n\nLaurel didn't care that I was a stranger. She worked fast to save my life.

I prayed for Tu'whacca's mercy as darkness crawled over my eyes. But then, it felt like my chest might explode.\n\nThat brilliant girl cast a spell that forced air right into my lungs. I couldn't stop thanking her as I coughed and spit up briny water.

She called to others from her circle and they carried me to their home. Over several weeks, the druids nurtured me back to health.\n\nLaurel and her people changed my life. I quit being a pirate, began studying magic, and joined the Mages Guild.

Perhaps not so much a legend as a warning. Graven Deep is a blank spot on every pirate's map of the Abecean. Don't dare enter it, they'll tell you, or you'll vanish from the sea. Like the morning fog burned away by the sun.

Perhaps, in a way. I've heard the warning of Graven Deep told by many and many since childhood. It became its own truth over time.\n\nHa, and if I tried convincing a crew to come here, they'd keelhaul me in an instant.

Ha, the sea would wash this island away before I could tell you my whole story. These days I'm a member of the Mages Guild.\n\nBefore that, most would call me a pirate. And I can't deny that it fairly describes my work back then.

Like most Redguard, I grew up skeptical of magic. But about ten years back, I had a close brush with death. In that moment, I realized I wasn't yet ready for Tu'whacca's journey.\n\nI prayed for more time, and it was magic that brought me back to life.
My friend Druid Laurel found me on the beach. She used her magic to heal me.\n\nI didn't fail to heed Tu'whacca's lesson. Once my strength returned, I sought out the Mages Guild.

Oh, when one's a pirate, I don't think they ever fully give it up. The seawater stays in your blood.\n\nBy the time I began studying magic, I'd done everything a pirate could possibly do. Stormed ships, fought sea monsters, and looted treasure galore.

Right. Dhulef mentioned you helped him at Graven Deep. It was sheer luck that he found that old logbook at all. It contained an entry indicating the Druid King met with the wyrds before departing High Rock. Dhulef went on ahead to meet with a wyress.

We may share the same roots, but back then wyrds and druids wanted nothing to do with each other. Our oral history contains no stories about such a meeting, so of course I was intrigued.\n\nHopefully, the wyrds remember something the druids forgot.

Not too much. I know they existed long before us, then vanished. But every child in Tamriel hears that story. Surely you've seen their remnants scattered all over the land.\n\nPerhaps when I return home, I can read more about them.

On the sea I rarely had use for Dwarves. Other than raiding a ship or two for, well, acquiring their artifacts from other traders. Heh.\n\nWhen I began studying magic, I focused more on defensive spells. Ancient research never appealed to me.

There are three distinct circles of druids that live throughout the Systres Archipelago. The Stonelore Circle Druids, the circle I come from, have enclaves on High Isle and Galen. The Eldertide mainly stick to Galen, but they're not isolationists.

Dhulef was following the Druid King's path when he found an ancient logbook. It was from one of the druid ships that never made it to the Systres. The logbook contained an entry that indicated the Druid King met with the wyrds before setting sail.

Right. Dhulef mentioned you helped him at Graven Deep. It was sheer luck that he found that old logbook at all. It contained an entry indicating the Druid King met with the wyrds before departing High Rock. Dhulef went on ahead to meet with a wyress.

We didn't fight these crusty brutes for nothing! Next, we go into that hatch. Search around for the storm's explanation. And hopefully find some information for Laurel.\n\nMate, I believe our fun together has only begun.

We may share the same roots, but back then wyrds and druids wanted nothing to do with each other. Our oral history contains no stories about such a meeting, so of course I was intrigued.\n\nHopefully, the wyrds remember something the druids forgot.

Three distinct druidic circles live on the Systres islands. The Stonelore and Eldertide have enclaves on High Isle and Galen, while the Firesong occupy Y'ffelon. The Firesong never leave their island. They're reclusive. At least, they used to be.

In and of themselves, the regalia have no innate power. They're symbols, nothing more.\n\nHowever, the very fact that the sacred seeds have been regrown into the crown, staff, and gauntlet give credence to the prophecy of the Druid King.

The Dream of Kasorayn. The druids of the archipelago have debated its meaning since it was first uttered so long ago. With the regalia, Lord Bacaro can proclaim that the conditions of the prophecy have been met and that he's the new Druid King.

Captain Marguerite's reputation is impeccable and she seemed unaware of all this. But the same could be said about Lord Bacaro.\n\nUntil we determine how far this corruption has spread into the Society of the Steadfast, we keep this to ourselves.

No. But if you really want to help, find Wyress Tola and bring her back safely.\n\nDruids haven't been seen in High Rock since the Wyrd Tree was just a shrub, so when they appeared, we took interest. I'll mark the locations of their camps on your map.

Obviously it had something to do with the quake we experienced, but why only one structure fell … I just don't know. It does show that the volcano is becoming more dangerous.\n\nRahval said it was because the Firesong were neglecting their duties.

Until recently, Firesong Druids rarely left Y'ffelon. They communed with Mount Firesong's spirit. Singing it back to sleep when it grew restless. Or so I was taught by the Stonelore.\n\nThey've always been secretive about their vigil on Y'ffelon.

Mount Firesong has rumbled my entire life. I wonder if it was the stirring of the volcano that woke Orlaith instead. The Dream of Kasorayn mentions the mountain. Perhaps it was the sign she was waiting for.

Yes, of course. Laurel is … a close friend. \n\nI doubt Orlaith would harm Frii. She thinks she needs the spirit. But we saw how Orlaith deals with anyone who interferes with her ambitions. I don't want to see Laurel share Rahval's fate.

At least something good has come of all this. But poor Stefan. His father wasn't a friend to the druids, but he mostly left us alone … unlike some of his predecessors.\n\nFrii said they felt the seeds calling. Maybe they can help us track them down.

Blight and damnation! Frii told me they sensed the seeds stirring. Moving. I couldn't think of any good reason to account for that, and neither could Frii.\n\nBut what about Vastyr? Does the city still stand?

Lady Juline is a few arrows short of a full quiver, if you ask me. But yeah, I ran into those murderous Sea Elves while rounding the northeast point of Galen. Dreadsails pirates.\n\nThe old druid settlement of Llanshara belongs to them now.
Through the blessing of the spirit motes. Y'ffre is the Storyteller. All of nature comes from Y'ffre, but so do our tales and songs. The Chronicle utilizes both aspects of its creator.

Particles released by the Chronicle. Normally, we breathe in the gift of the spirit and experience the story it wishes us to see. A vision, you might call it. Perfectly safe.\n\nExcept I've never seen such large clouds of spirit motes before.

I've been searching the perimeter of the path since the attack and I've seen no one else. I can't believe I left without her. If I'd only stopped to see if she followed, she'd be safe.\n\nIf she dies, I'll never forgive myself.

You're not a druid. You don't belong on the Systres Archipelago. \n\nStill, I'll set aside my animosities for Gwenaelle. She's my bubbling spring. She soothes the burns of life and cools my harsh temper. We need to save her.

Crocodiles, wolves, ursauks, among others. The animals in the path are usually docile. We feed them, care for them. Now they attack without provocation. For things to be so out of balance … it goes against my understanding of nature.

It started after their attack, but I've never seen a druid who could control the spirit motes before. Only the Chronicle commands them. Chooses when to release them and what story they carry. I have no clue what's happening here.

In the direction of the rising sun. The point on the isle where that first happens. \n\nI will help you find the seeds and keep them. Safe. Until crown, staff, and gauntlet must flower. That time is soon. It is not for me to tell seeds not to grow.

Are you serious? You know each and every Dreadsail in Llanshara already has a job, right? It's called piracy, and they're damn good at it!\n\nPeople think Wood Elves are bloody-handed. We can't hold a torchbug to those sea-wolves.

Who are you? The port authority? I have my reasons. Let's just say those Dreadsails view anyone who wanders too close as fair game. That includes you, too.\n\nThe real question is why does that silly Breton lady care?

The Ivy Throne, or so the legends say. Where the last Druid King held court. If she really seeks to become the new king, that's a good place to start.\n\nYou and Frii check out the door while I scout the rest of the vale. I'll catch up with you later.

The Faun herd has lived in this location since before druids settled on Galen. Even Druid Madena chose this thicket to study them. \n\nBesides, I adore them. They're smart and playful. Like little Mohair here. Watch out. He might try to eat your pack.

Yes. The sealed door that Laurel spoke of. The door the Firesong archdruid could not open. At the top of these steps.\n\nThe song of this place calls to me. There must be a way inside. Let us find it.

Nobles get all kinds of ideas in their heads about rare ingredients with properties that give them a … different meaning of the word stamina than you are probably used to.\n\nIf I can accommodate these requests, I try not to ask too many questions.

Vastyr and all its inhabitants are part of this once untamed island, for better or worse. We Stonelore Druids seek harmony through common ground with one another, but the same can't be said of the other circles.

Have you ever used an axe to fell a tree? Used that wood to craft armor, maybe a weapon itself?\n\nImagine if, upon your first stroke of the axe, the tree you were aiming for struck back. That is what forest wraiths are.

The song is not for Archdruid Orlaith. It is for me. The door will not open for anyone. It is waiting for me.\n\nCome, Laurel-friend. Help Frii awaken the druid stones. Then we can see what else the song wants to tell me.

Interesting. We druids use totems and fetishes in our rituals. Does this serve a similar purpose? And what's this word inscribed here? Frii? Never heard of it.\n\nWe have no other choice. We need to see if the Firesong took Wyress Tola to Hag Fen.

It all happened so fast! He said something about needing a wyress to open the path. And I know he mentioned the Druid King and a ritual site—things I'd never heard of until the mage arrived and asked Wyress Tola about them.
Will fire ever create instead of destroy? Will the tides ever change their rhythm? Mountains may flatten waiting for such a change. \n\nBut it is not impossible, my friend. Nothing ever is.

When needs call for it, spirits of the forest can facilitate druid magic to meld man and tree. Some among us willingly submit to such an honor.\n\nWhat results is a twisted guardian that has the strength and spirit of both, but the wisdom of neither.

Understanding. I was summoned to quicken the seeds. Crown, staff, and gauntlet. But I do not know why King Kasorayn made them sleep. So how can I know when to wake them?\n\nWe should explore. Learn. I will follow you.

The Firesong found my bower. They tore me from my slumber with words of binding. Compulsion. I was young. I could not refuse.\n\nBut Druid Laurel stopped them. They did not bind me. I can still choose. She brought me to Galen. Let me grow.

Understanding. I was summoned to quicken the seeds. Crown, staff, and gauntlet. But I do not know why King Kasorayn made them sleep. So how can I know when to wake them?\n\nWe should explore. Learn. I will follow you.

Ah, just as I remembered. The pattern depicts a ritual, though one I am unfamiliar with. The symbols represent the Druid King, the Beldama Wyrd, and the Glenmoril Wyrd. And the one in the center, I believe that's the spirit Archdruid Michiel seeks.

Not specifically, but if the Glenmoril Wyrds assisted the Druid King there, then it must be somewhere in Bangkorai. The archdruid will require another wyress to access the ritual site. Then if he completes his spell, he can summon the nature spirit.

It will show us what the elder wants us to see. We will become a dream. A memory. And in that way, we will remember.\n\nBut it is you who must drink. Only a mortal vessel can understand a mortal memory. I will see, too. Through you.

Dangerous? Hares and lizards and rats? No! Do you think a critter did this to me?\n\nIt's the monsters roaming all around the place that are dangerous! Oh, it will be easy, she said. Just nab a couple of those cute critters, she said!

What kind of monsters weren't in there? Zeht's tears, even the plants were trying to eat me!\n\nI barely managed to scoop up a couple of critters for that daft Juline before a faun chased me out. I wouldn't go back without a company of knights!

Does she now? And what role would a minor count play in discussions concerning the greater fate of all of Tamriel?\n\nNo, forgive me, friend. It's just been a lot lately. Of course I'll attend. Is there anything Lady Arabelle needs of me?

Ah, yes. After all this trouble, such a request isn't all that surprising.\n\nVery well, tell Lady Arabelle. Count Stefan shall attend the peace talks with a contingent of his finest knights at his side. Will that do?

Well, sweetling, Dreadsails don't survive for long if they can't deal with some rough treatment now and again. But, Minahel had to ruin our fun. I want to go again.\n\nLaniwys and I did nothing dangerous. Minahel can go rot in the sun.

The Beldama sent you? Well, you're too late. The druids took Wyress Sorcha with them.\n\nIf you really want to help, I'll tell you what I know. The druids seek a nature spirit. A very special one that has been asleep for a very long time.
Oh please. I know what he was affected by.\n\nShe's a Dreadsail pirate. They're dangerous! He's lucky she didn't just kill him. And now he runs right back into danger? Typical!
Yes, I think so. Abandoning a partner looks just as bad as not completing a job. Umindior found this job, so I might not even get paid without him.\n\nBut I really want to leave the loaf. I truly do.

Really. After you just saw my negotiating skills in action? Wait, you're serious?\n\nWell, why not? I definitely want what's best for my people. And maybe I can learn something watching the alliance leaders. I'll be happy to attend.

I was on a hunt, when I received word that the Gray Host had overrun these lands.\n\nAn army of parasites from out of the past. Even the dregs have proven to be a worthy challenge. But a true hunter does not shrink from danger.

Not that I saw, but everything happened so quickly. We were running and there was so much chaos. Rahval is quick, though. He wouldn't be brought low so easily. He must have gotten away unscathed. I just don't know how long he can continue to do so.

I don't know. We got separated. But they're going after Rahval as well. You have to find him! We cannot let the Firesong lay claim to all three of the sacred seeds. There's no telling what would happen!

Most of them were scattered throughout the city once the attack began. Many are helping the House Mornard knights defend against the Dreadsails. I'll gather everyone I can who isn't fighting on my way to the cathedral.
Well, they've barricaded the main streets, but there's a short cut to the west and up the stairs. Head that way and see if you can find him.\n\nAnd may Y'ffre protect you, outsider.
The house of the city gods? Yes, of course. I'll head there immediately. The walls should offer adequate protection.\n\nNow, go. Help Archdruid Rahval.

I'm tracking several scions of the Host, in hopes to find one vampire in particular. They will all be ash when I am through.\n\nWill you join the hunt? I've had a few close calls. I wouldn't turn away an able adventurer such as yourself.

Za'ji and Caska are invited? Well, as expected, of course! After all Za'ji has done, it is only natural to want him there to observe. And to keep the queen and the others safe.\n\nBut Caska, too? Really? Oh very well. If Lady Arabelle insists.
Urdiir waits, as I did. The Firesong must return the seeds to the place we saw in the then. The Temple of Y'ffelon.\n\nI know how to call Urdiir. A song of defense. It is my choice.

Perhaps. She may think she can bind Urdiir. Command it with crown, staff, and gauntlet. But King Kasorayn told some spirits to make their own choices. I am one. Urdiir is another.\n\nWe should find Druid Laurel. She will know what to do next.

Yes. The Chronicle grows plants, called muse-mouths, which release a small amount of spirit motes when we commune with it. The motes show us the stories. They've never threatened or harmed us before. And they never appeared as great clouds, either.
I have grown much since my awakening. Blossomed. Made friends. Druid Laurel is my friend.\n\nWhat can I do to help?
Then we still attempt to rescue the captives from Archdruid Orlaith. If Frii isn't willing to help, I won't try to force them. We'll do our best without the distraction Frii would provide.

Just climb aboard the skiff when you're ready and it will ferry you to the Mad Maiden. Then it's off to Y'ffelon as quick as the wind will take us.\n\nBear this in mind. On the Mad Maiden, I'm the captain. If I tell you to do something, do it.

Good. Tell Captain Siravaen when you're ready to sail while I gather a few of my knights. With luck, the Mad Maiden can slip us into Y'ffelon without anyone noticing. We can land at Cinderwash Point. We think they're holding the captives there.
Your work here is done, mercenary. Head below and rest up for the fight on Y'ffelon—the real battle is still ahead of you.\n\nMy crew can take care of that Firesong scow burning alongside us.

We need to split up and find Laurel and the other captives. My knights are already ashore. Head east along the beach and join them. Free any townsfolk you find. Send them to the Mad Maiden.\n\nI'll head toward the temple. Meet me there when you can.

Then the first part of our mission has been a success. We still need to save Laurel and Frii, and find a way to stop Archdruid Orlaith.\n\nI've had little luck so far. I scouted the temple's outer passages, but too many Firesong guard the way ahead.
I do not know. It is not the place of a spirit of the Green to decide for mortals. It is a question for the Draoife, I think. Like intertwined roots, wisdom must come from counsel taken together.

House Mornard's knights stand ready. The druids will bolster our defenses, but you must bring the Gilded Blades to aid us. Whatever the Firesong promised them, the Sea Elves are committed.\n\nMy scouts spotted an armada sailing toward the city.

Her message was brief, but she indicated that most of her crew was missing as well. Scattered or captured, she'll need them back to sail her ship. And we need all of the Gilded Blades to help defend the city.\n\nDo whatever you can to make that happen.

Well, truth be told, she contacted me. Easier to get a message to Castle Mornard than to find a Sea Elf hiding in the wilderness.\n\nWhen Sealord Nalos rejected King Orgnum's orders, he seized Siravaen's ship and scattered her crew. She needs our help.

Specifically, she requested I send you to help her. She'll meet you on the Castle Tonnere docks, on the western shore. Do whatever you need to, but make sure she recovers her ship. We need the Gilded Blades when the assault on Vastyr begins.

That's right. See it down there? Those bastards chained the Mad Maiden to the dock and placed my crew under guard.\n\nThe Dreadsails have already set sail for Vastyr. If you want my help in the battle, I need both my ship and my crew.

Someone's got to defend the home port. Even a slime like Sealord Nalos knows that. They're more of the lowly scum who spit in the face of King Orgnum. \n\nThey'll put up a fight, though, same as the ones you faced in Castle Tonnere.

When Sealord Nalos rejected the orders I brought from King Orgnum, he didn't have the decency to kill me. He seized my ship and scattered my crew so I couldn't do a damn thing about it. Some were sent to serve on other ships, but most were locked up.

Ha, I knew you had saltwater in your blood! Cut the four moorings binding my ship, then head to the far dock to release the harbor chain so we can sail to Vastyr.\n\nYou'll have to take the platforms to get down there. Go on.

We need to work in tandem. I'll get my crew while you free the Mad Maiden. Cut the mooring lines and drop the harbor chain so we're ready to set sail the moment my crew is free.\n\nThey left some slimy eels on guard. Think you're up for it?

The Mad Maiden is faster than any ship in the Dreadsails armada. We'll get there in time. And then Sealord Nalos and I will have words. Sharp, bloody words. Wait below deck until we dock.\n\nThe rest of you, weigh anchor! Set sail for Vastyr!

That's an old wyrd totem. We don't use those very often in our rituals and ceremonies anymore, but they used to be more prevalent. Hmm, that word inscribed there. Frii. Sounds like ancient Breton to me, but I have no idea what it may mean.

Into their damn prison stockade! And it won't be long before they finish processing him. Then they'll banish poor Valentyn into the jungle … and I'll never see my beloved again.\n\nHelp me save my husband, stranger. I'll pay you handsomely. Please!

We saw the same memory. The choices that led the Druid King and Elder Verline to the temple are forgotten now. But I know the Allwither. It is of the Green, yet it hates what it is. It hungers for what it is not.

On the prison island of Amenos? Hardly! Besides, there's no time. Here. Take this bottle of Dufort Red. It's a rare vintage that Jailer Omdil absolutely adores. Give him that and he'll let you inside.\n\nThen find my Valentyn and get him out of there!

Some betrayed. Not all. Only those in the grip of the Allwither. Those are the ones that were stricken. Forgotten. The rest were … forgiven.\n\nI think Orlaith remembers. Knows what others forgot. And so sees the Dream differently. A path to power.
Oh, just the usual hemming and hawing. I just applied my natural charisma and threatened them with bodily harm.\n\nThe leaders do want a word with you, though, if you're willing to indulge them.

If it wasn't one of the Sea Elves' primary targets, yes. But the cathedral has stout walls and strong doors. And few enemies will risk angering the gods by attacking a holy place.\n\nTrust me. It's the safest place for the injured and noncombatants.
No point in me telling you that. I suspect you'll underestimate Minahel and get yourself captured. The less you can tell her, the better the chance my beloved and I can make it safely away from here.

Not long. We're holding our own, but the city wasn't built to withstand an armada of this magnitude. The castle and cathedral will endure, at least. The rest? I fear we'll be looking at rubble before long if we don't turn back the invaders.
I would like to see the city of stone. Find Laurel-friend Stefan. He can help us. Laurel trusts him. Likes him.\n\nI will meet you in Vastyr, Laurel-friend.
Embervine? A perfect encapsulation of Galen's volcanic nature. Lush and fertile, teeming with life, yet seething with seismic danger. Not unlike my homeland of Vvardenfell.\n\nWhy do you ask?

Oh, that girl. She asked the same of me. I had to convince her that my interest in the locale is more academic than artistic.\n\nI fear she does not quite respect the complex nature of Embervine's caverns and vales.

The region's volcanic hazards and dangerous wildlife are nothing for unprepared sightseers to trifle with. Yet she still sends her little adventurers there to draw her pictures.\n\nNo offense, of course. I do wish you luck.

I saw him follow a woman through a door right here. And here's our camp. We can meet there after you find him.\n\nTry to stay out of sight. If a guard sees you, look for a hiding spot. I'd rather not alert the whole settlement.

I plan to hire Captain Siravaen's ship. The Mad Maiden is anchored just outside Vastyr's walls, and she has no love for the Firesong Druids. \n\nHer ship and crew are battle tested. They'll be perfect for what we need to do.

Urdiir, the spirit we saw in the vision. Their purpose is to protect. The seeds. The temple. Perhaps even me.\n\nWhen the moment comes, I think I can wake the guardian. Will that be enough to stop the archdruid? I do not know.
Yes. They are together, but distant. Far away. At the Temple of Y'ffelon.\n\nThey stir. Become restless. Soon they must grow. Sing.

Urdiir's task was to guard this place until a new Druid King claimed crown, staff, and gauntlet. The seeds are regrown, but there is no king yet. Urdiir's purpose is now … cloudy. Unclear. Rootless.\n\nAs is mine.

We saw Elder Aiven give the Firesong a seed in the ancient then. They overcame the blight of the Allwither. In the now, they will overcome Orlaith's darkness.\n\nThey must if the druids are to be made whole.

My part's simple enough. Get you, the lordling, and his knights over to Y'ffelon island. Then bring anyone you rescue back to Galen.\n\nI suppose sailing away and offering them for ransom would be in poor form.

Wind and wave I can master. But that volcano has been belching out clouds of ash and steam. This is no ordinary sea-fog around us. If it were, I would've run circles around a bunch of druids in stolen ships.

It's a great hall built into the natural caverns and old lava tubes beneath Mount Firesong. The druids constructed it after King Kasorayn led them to these islands. Archdruid Rahval took me there once.

Followers of the Allwither among the Firesong Circle. While most of that circle serve the cycle of creation, those who revere the Allwither worship only death and decay.\n\nThey seek to seize the Ivy Throne. To lead us into an age of unending darkness.

I must return my regalia—crown, staff, and gauntlet—to Y'ffre. The season of the Druid King must end. For now.\n\nMeanwhile, we need to make preparations so my dream comes to pass. Escort me to Elder Verline in the ritual chamber. This ends today.

You're sure you're all right, Aiven? The Dream is my prophecy of two futures—one good, one bad. The Sower is the key, a spirit I called from the Green and left in the care of the wyrds. Frii.\n\nYou must prepare the message for them, as we discussed.

I've been lucky enough to never encounter one face to face … to face, to face. Much like certain druidic circles I could mention, chimera are fiercely territorial. But that's simply how they were created.

All chimera that roam the land today were created by the Druid King himself. They guard and protect sacred places or important relics.\n\nWhile we Stonelore revere them and their purpose, it's clear that the world is outgrowing them.

I wanted … damn, this went better in my head. I've never been as good at speaking my mind as my father was. Or Archdruid Rahval. Now he was an orator!\n\nSorry. I'm babbling. Let me start over. Thank you for everything, my friend.

Northern Galen has plenty of trees. Big ones! Sounds like it's buried under one of those, near some sort of … river of fire? Lava, maybe? \n\nHe who sees … I've no idea. Whatever that is, it sounds dangerous.

Give one seed to each druid circle to guard … to keep. Oak to Eldertide. Rowan to Stonelore. Ash … for the Firesong untainted by the Allwither.\n\nOne last thing … go to the Ivy Throne. Seal it. No one must enter until the Sower awakens.

No, but the others all lived in our community. And from the looks of it, they were killed by the Firesong attackers. They must have been surprised. There are no Firesong Druids among the dead.\n\nBut there's also no sign of my wife.

Just what I saw. It floated above a wide fissure in the rock. Streams of energy flowed from the lava into the crystal as the druids chanted.\n\nOh, I just want the druids gone. Or at least make them stop what they're doing so I can complete my survey.

Well, not all of them, but the crystals do seem to be related to the lava.\n\nIn my field, cause and effect is easy to spot. Hit the rock with a pickaxe, uncover a vein of ore. Same here, right? Smash a floating druid crystal, disrupt the druid magic.

A temporal distortion swirls through Bal Sunnar. I wanted to find the source before it affected causality. But I'm too late. Somehow, these Telvanni met us already. Events have occurred out of order for them.\n\nWhy did they call us a scourge, though?

Who can trust anyone that wants to play around with time? We've got enough to deal with here and now.\n\nI don't even think about the past! Once I've made a decision, there's no looking back. And Undaunted don't worry about the future.
<You are about to enter a Group Dungeon. Are you ready to leave your current Zone?>

Go in there and contain the source. But these are Telvanni. They guard their secrets jealously.\n\nI'd like your help. For pay, of course. And, since they know us already, it seems we're predestined to work together anyway.

It will be, once the spirit motes disperse and the remaining Firesong are driven off. Without a spirit, Gwen and I will become the chroniclers. We'll remember and record our stories and our history. Share it with all who wish to hear.

My understanding of nature spirits has changed. I don't know if I can treat them with the same respect I did before. \n\nI'll give myself some time to recover and reflect. The shock of everything that happened could be clouding my judgment. We'll see.

With the Chronicle influencing my mind? In an instant.\n\nThat feeling will stay with me for the rest of my days. Part of me is glad the Chronicle is gone. For all its insight, it didn't understand mortals. I hope I can still be a druid after this.

My poor boy. He set off days ago to forage the woods to the northeast. Damn! The druids warned them about the wraith there!\n\nI guess I should just be grateful that Druid Gastoc was able to find a rescuer.

You haven't heard of her? She inspired me to become a druid! She's an elder now, but in her youth, she came here to study the Fauns. She learned so much about them, how they interact and how clever they are. Her love of Fauns became mine.
There was an incident with his herd. The guards outside Vastyr thought that the local Fauns were attacking them. They weren't. \n\nStill, Mohair was the only survivor.

The wolf pack's usual prey was decimated by a blight last season, so they came here to hunt. They're starting with smaller prey, but it's only natural for them to hunt the Fauns next. I want to keep that from happening.

Not long, but he didn't collect much on his first couple expeditions. I expect that's why he ventured where he shouldn't have.\n\nThis work is too dangerous for what these hirelings get paid, I tell you! Especially on Galen!

You know how these young folks are. They only listen to one another!\n\nHis friends convinced him to seek hireling work under House Mornard. I'd have been content with him washing dishes at the Jaded Ornaug! At least then he'd be safe ….

Hey, I'm a druid. Knowing this kind of nature stuff is sort of part of the job description!\n\nThose seeds grow exceedingly fast and produce berries that Mohair loves. Wolves, on the other hand, hate the way they smell. Just a whiff makes them run!
I suppose it may be too much to ask that they left the blasted relic where they found it. We could grab it, get out of here, then be done with this whole thing.\n\nUgh. I wish I could think straight.
The one where they frolicked so hard that they spread good feelings to every Sea Elf in Llanshara? Incredible.\n\nHonestly, I feel grateful. Because of them, I had a delightful romp.

The truth is, until she came here, no one knew much about Fauns. They were mainly seen as cunning pests. She was the first druid to really delve into how the herds worked. I believe her efforts resulted in fewer Faun deaths and deeper understanding.

Vaster, wind-wracked shores … that sounds like Vastyr and Windwrack Fort to me. And the riddle makes mention of the distant cauldron.\n\nMaybe … somewhere on the shore between Vastyr and Windwrack Fort, within sight of Y'ffelon?

Curious. You're the second person to ask me about that overgrown glen. We must share a common acquaintance in Lady Juline.\n\nI'm surprised. I was sure she would only remember one thing from our chat, and I didn't expect it to be my name.

While everyone slept, we snuck in. Standing near the relic felt so incredible. We decided to have a little passion of our own.\n\nAfter, we noticed the relic glowing. That's when Minahel stormed in and dragged us out. We just wanted to have some fun.

Faun herds are close knit families. They wouldn't just accept an outsider. Especially not one who's small or weak.\n\nStill, Mohair helps me convince stubborn outsiders that Fauns aren't terrible creatures. He's like an ambassador to man and mer.

I'm probably more like a bossy sister. We get along, but he still tries to irk me when he's bored. I keep him out of danger, but I can't control him. \n\nEspecially at this age. He's more rebellious than I was in my youth.

Druid decorum requires that I fully disclose the potential dangers—no matter how unlikely—to any non-druids taking part in a complex and somewhat lethal ritual.\n\nSo, you must do exactly as I say. One wrong move and ….

And we could be afflicted with the same curse that has befallen Joslin and Octin. The odds of that happening are infinitesimal, but I feel obliged to warn you just the same.\n\nNow, are you ready to begin?

Everything in my power. We've never faced an invasion of this scale before, but Vastyr isn't defenseless. We have knights, walls, and the advantage of foresight. We can set barricades, prepare traps, and get noncombatants to safety.
That's an intriguing idea. She does seem to be willing to assist us. It was her warning that alerted us to this impending attack.\n\nI doubt she'd help us out of the goodness of her heart, however.

We can only ask for their aid and hope, my friend. Druids may not be warriors by tradition, but I know they aren't cowards. And they can fight. I've seen what the Eldertide can do, and I know the Stonelore will protect themselves when necessary.

Kingsblood. She asked you to get some for her, didn't she? As soon as I described the plant's beauty, she had ears for nothing else.\n\nI hope she also mentioned the man-eating plants, murderous fauns, and ancient druidic magic?

Ah, well. Let my words be a warning then. I tried to dissuade Juline from these tourism ventures, but yet here you are. It seems my guidance fell on deaf ears.\n\nTake care if you venture into the glen. I pray you come to no harm.

Me? I won't dare assume anything about Dwarven machinery. Without the map I'd have no clue how to find this core. Or that there's even a core to find. This logbook suggests the Dwarves experimented with weather control here. Weather like huge storms.

Hmm. That's worth exploring. We saw many undead in this station's halls. Perhaps the lich wrecked ships to build an army. Or consume souls of sailors. The ways of such creatures are dark and awful.\n\nI'll ask a Guild colleague to look into it for me.

An interesting bunch. They live in the High Rock forests, worshiping trees. I've met a few in my day, and I'm on good terms with a Beldama wyress.\n\nI'm not sure the exact difference between wyrds and druids, but don't tell Druid Laurel I said that.

That's a question for Laurel. The logbook's author seems surprised that they met, but may the sea take me if I know why. She'll have to tell me the significance of such a meeting when I deliver the book to her.

Way ahead of you, mate. You saw the raft I built on the beach? I promise you it's sturdy. I've crafted many such transports over the years. Saved my life on more than one occasion, too.\n\nThis portal will return us there. Then we float back home.
Do you have to ask it like that? I know I don't look good, but spare me an ounce of vanity, please. I don't know if I'll make it to the day's end!

Perfectly. I gave it to Frii for safekeeping. As a spirit forged from Y'ffre's will, who better to protect something so sacred? They've been quite curious about it. Said they felt a connection and wanted to study the seed.

The request came from Stefan, and my circle loves him as one of our own. Plus, the Firesong attacked us, as well, and we feel a responsibility for our misguided brethren. Besides, I am their archdruid and I have already agreed. The matter is settled.

A chimera?! By the eight! Is that what that was? When the other Stonelore mentioned them, I thought they were hazing me as a new initiate! \n\nI was sure it was just a gryphon! That was surprise enough for me.

I suppose they must have been. That certainly explains why I heard the others screaming when I felt a giant beak trying to cut me a new hole. \n\nThree heads! And I met the most vicious one, I have no doubt. Just my luck. You'll avenge me, won't you?
Wait! I stand by what I said before. \n\nMake. That. Beast. Suffer! Three times more than what you were planning before!
Then what are you still doing here? Go! Quick! You have no idea the pain I'm in right now!

Mount Firesong is as indifferent to the life on this peninsula as … well, the Firesong Druids are. \n\nBut where the Firesong seem incapable of listening, the shrines allow communion with earth spirits to keep Vastyr safe from the volcano's wrath.
Ahh, yes. Lady Juline. At least she had enough sense to send someone else on her fool's errand. Trust me, friend. Y'ffre's Path is no place for a tour, let alone one meant for soft-footed nobles.
Some among us do. Or they would, if not for the rampaging chimera. That makes things difficult, as you can probably imagine.

Hmm. It seems my stern warnings weren't enough to dissuade Lady Juline.\n\nThe Eldertide Circle has never taken kindly to strangers traipsing about in the sacred site. Now the path is more dangerous than ever, thanks to recent events.

Something's turned rotten in Y'ffre's Path. Corrupt. The beasts there turn on anyone who sets foot in the place. And the very air is thick with strange spores.\n\nIf you must go, stay on the main paths. And hold your breath.

We heard some of their war bands talking. Something about finding the druid relics. I'm glad for the warriors, but did they have to bring their damn religion into my city, too?\n\nAnyway, I need you to find Archdruids Rahval and Ellic. Keep them safe.

I resolved to help them before I even knew how this tablet came into their possession. This curse is druidic in nature, so it must be a druid who undoes it. Whatever Joslin and Octin's past intentions, they don't deserve this fate.

Others would come to harm? Because of me? No, that is not my purpose. That is wrong.\n\nBut the archdruid needs me to grow the seeds. To reforge the regalia. To make her the Druid King. That is wrong, too.

Ah. Understanding cuts like the sun through clouds. Deception.\n\nArchdruid Orlaith will try to compel me. Force me to do as she wants, not as King Kasorayn intended. But Urdiir the Guardian is there. They will help me. So I will help you.
As safe as anything that lives in the wild can be.\n\nMohair and I will come check on the herd every now and then to see how they're getting along. Plant a few more berries if necessary.

The writing on the tablet is in an ancient druidic script. It would take a Mages Guild wizard too much time to decipher it and understand the process needed to break the curse. \n\nOctin and Joslin don't have long before the change becomes permanent.

I'm not sure about Rahval, but I saw Archdruid Ellic heading for the old druid tunnels. Follow those and you should find him.\n\nLord Bacaro and I are taking people to the cathedral. Besides the castle, it's the most defensible place in the city.

No. The Fauns and wolves need some time to settle in. If we stayed and observed, then I'd be more likely to intervene too early. We'll stay in the area, but I won't check on the herd for a while.\n\nMohair will let me know if something goes wrong.

We were thinking about heading toward Vastyr. There's always newcomers there to educate about Fauns. Besides, it's been a while since we visited the Vine District and there are some folks who'd love to see how big Mohair's getting.

He let me know when the herd was frightened of the wolves. I don't know if he caught a scent or if he heard the Fauns' call from far away.\n\nFauns are miraculous creatures. Did you know they have magic? I learn something new about them every day.

If you hear its scream, ready your weapon at once. After that, beware of shifting ground and deceptive magic. \n\nOnce a wraith has identified you as a threat, there is no convincing the angry spirit that pilots these beings otherwise.

Druid Gastoc is a friend of mine, but I'm afraid I don't know what job you're referring to. \n\nOh dear. Did I forget to shadow a group of initiates again? Don't tell me there's been another chimera attack ….

He really did that just for me? He's too sweet!\n\nI hope you make it back in one piece. The regenerative properties of the moths are strictly theoretical at this point. I'd hate for you to die and Gastoc to think he failed me.

I was hoping to study them for possible regenerative properties. But I'd heard northern Galen was too dangerous, on account of the forest wraith in the Valley of the Watcher.\n\nDid Gastoc hire you to gather some for me?

A nature spirit, called from the Green by King Kasorayn and hidden with the wyrd in High Rock. They slept since the time of the last Druid King until the Firesong Circle sent an archdruid to find Frii and awaken them.

You saw what Archdruid Michiel did to the wyrds. Druids who are ready to hurt others like that shouldn't get what they want. So I've been keeping Frii safe and helping them learn about people.\n\nThey grow more every day. It's … incredible.
A song of hate blows through the branches. Harm drips like sap. It soaks the ground.\n\nAwakened to fire. Tremors, volcano. Deadwood, blood in the shadows. I am troubled.

Fascinating things. An adventurer brought me a few samples. Told me the cores were just lying about in Embervine. I can hardly go gather them myself, so I asked Lady Juline to find someone who could bring me more.\n\nFoolish of me.

I tell her about the potential of these cores, and she decides they would make nice paperweights! She is just a coin-blinded fool trying to bring gadabouts to Galen.\n\nBah! Let the tourists stay in Gonfalon Bay.

The radiant cores seem to absorb energy from volcanic sites such as the ones in Embervine. If we can tap into this power, we could use it to fire our forges. But I won't know for certain until I get more cores to study.
I suppose it could be worse. I could be a netch.\n\nAll those limbs? No thank you!

He grumbled something about his responsibilities as a Stonelore druid. If you ask me, I think he's hoping to convince us to give back all the equipment we took. Procured.\n\nHe probably knows the druid it belongs to. But she left it to rot!

No idea. Seems fairly irresponsible to me. Anyone could just pick it up, break it, and get cursed. Maybe she wanted to keep people like Octin and me from stealing her research? \n\nDruid Fenas said he might be able to help, so we're letting him.

I need to continue to work on the translation.\n\nThere's something about this text. A word I can't translate. From the way the sentence lines up, it's nothing good. This curse is already potent enough. I'm worried about what else it might do.
Of course, of course! You would think Raz was going to curl up and fall asleep right here at your feet!\n\nHmm … actually that is not a bad idea.
I know. It's my sincere hope that they'll return the tablet—and anything else they stole—once this ordeal is over.\n\nAnd hopefully, this will teach them to avoid druidic sites in the future.

An elder in the Stonelore Circle. She used to study the Fauns, but one day she decided she was finished. Left all her equipment behind. These two tried to help themselves to it and look what happened.\n\nBut I'll figure out how to break this curse.

Dhulef will deliver Frii to the Temple of Y'ffelon. Hopefully by the time we arrive, everyone will be too focused on Frii and whatever the archdruid is doing to pay any attention to us.\n\nBut be ready, friend. I have no doubt we're in for a fight.

The Firesong Circle sailed off with at least three good Dreadsail warships. I doubt those oyster-shuckers know how to handle them, but they're out there somewhere. Plus whatever scows they use to get from island to island.\n\nMight be rough seas ahead.

Not far. I'll show you. We need to go to the spot where they found the tablet. Once we return it, we can set about restoring it. \n\nThe ritual won't be easy. Nothing about curses ever is. Just one more detail and we can get on with this.

Count Stefan will be at Castle Mornard and Druid Laurel should be in the Vines District in Vastyr. Za'ji's likely at the docks here in Gonfalon Bay. And Druid Ryvana is at her workshop here on High Isle, just west of the city.

The items for the ritual. Give them to me. Then I need you to go on ahead and clear a safe path to the spot I marked on your map.\n\nI'll follow with Joslin and Octin when the way is clear and prepare the site for the ritual.

Sir Stefan paid me. With the trouble on Galen, there aren't many pickings left for a pirate. But mercenary work? That's looking up.\n\nBesides, I could use a port where folk think well of the Gilded Blades. Most places they try to kill us on sight.

No, you're wrong! You must be! Stand there if you like, but I won't abandon them! I refuse to leave them! My father … Archdruid Rahval … even Archdruid Ellic. All … gone.\n\nThis can't be. How could this happen?

Small comfort to the survivors … and to the dead. Ah, apologies, my friend. I need a moment to … to collect myself. \n\nThere are things to do, but …. I saw Siravaen go toward the gate. Find her before she vanishes. We could still use her help.

My contract with the Society of the Steadfast doesn't end until the peace talks conclude, and who knows how long the alliance leaders will yell at each other now that they've finally started. After that? Some travel, some writing. Some time to relax.

Story unclear. Tell again. Druids of the path attacked. Killed. Chronicle shocked, angry. Spirit motes released. Cannot hold back the wind.\n\nCreated wraiths to defend the path. Lost control. Cannot stop. Sorry. So sorry.

The lordling hired me to get him and his knights to Y'ffelon, and that's what I'm going to do. \n\nWe've accounted for the Dreadsail ships the Firesong took from Vastyr. But there might be others around. The sooner we're on our way, the better.

We stumbled into this Firesong scow while I was in my cabin checking charts. By the time my deck watch spotted the enemy, they were too close to avoid. \n\nJust bad luck. I think the Firesong were as surprised as we were.

All I know is the legend. How after the Druid King died, they decided to bury him in the temple's shrine. Then they sealed the place and it's been closed off ever since. Well, until now.\n\nOrlaith has Frii and is forcing them to regrow the seeds.

I was scouting the vale when I ran into too many Firesong to deal with. They overpowered me, dragged me here, and presented me to Archdruid Orlaith. She threatened to hurt me if Frii didn't cooperate, then locked me in here.\n\nHey, is that my staff?

By the Green, I hope so. The Stonelore and Eldertide Druids. They're in as much danger as we are. Perhaps more so because the Firesong want their sacred seeds. We need them to help us defend the city.\n\nAnd that's where you come in.

While I help my father prepare the city's defenses, I want you to find the archdruids and secure their assistance. In exchange, they'll gain a place to protect their wounded and their seeds. Start with Archdruid Rahval of the Stonelore Circle.

Yet the three circles still live. Eldertide, Stonelore, Firesong. From their surviving elders, a new Draoife can be called. They can decide whether the season of a new Druid King is truly upon us or not.

I will carry the crown, staff, and gauntlet until the druids decide what to do. But not here. This place has served its purpose.\n\nWe should leave this place, friend of Laurel. Urdiir the Guardian is ill at ease with so many trespassing in the tomb.

Archdruid Orlaith never intended the Draoife to judge her actions. Root and rot! She only agreed to come so she could have the Dreadsails kill the archdruids!\n\nShe meant to leave the Stonelore and the Eldertide crippled and without their leaders!

All this trouble over druidic nonsense? And it led to the deaths of four archdruids? Unbelievable!\n\nBut I wouldn't expect Sea Elf pirates to bother with an alliance that doesn't pay in plunder. What does Sealord Nalos get out of all this?

Oh, just the next big thing to come to Galen! Perhaps the biggest thing to come to all of the Systres Archipelago!\n\nGonfalon Bay on High Isle attracts all the well-to-do from Tamriel. Well, my tour is going to change that!

Savage Systres Tours will combine the grandeur of High Isle with the … well, savageness … of Galen. We'll attract the most intrepid and adventurous tourists from across Tamriel!\n\nAnd you can be a part of it!

Exactly so! I need scouts to find the best spots for our patrons to explore. And since I'm so busy here in Vastyr, that means I need heroes like you to help out.\n\nTogether, we'll put Galen on the map!

Ah, thank you. We're shorthanded and I haven't had anyone to send for these. As you can see, the fighting on Galen has caused no end of suffering. And most of the victims are simple farmers and townsfolk, not soldiers.\n\nDamn those Sea Elf pirates!

For the most part. There have been some incidents among the druid circles, too. But the Sea Elves are definitely the biggest threat. Talk to Sir Stefan Mornard. I'm sure he can find a use for someone with your obvious talents.

No. I came to these lands as a child, orphaned and alone. The Stonelore Druids took me in when I had nowhere else to go. They've always accepted me, and they are the only family I've ever known. I consider myself as much of a Stonelore as any.

I'm not sure. Some of us have our suspicions, but no one has any proof. There are those who believe the Firesong's treachery and their refusal of Y'ffre's True Way has upset the balance. Others think there may be something more sinister at play.
Like … the Firesong Circle might be doing something intentionally to stoke the volcano's wrath, putting all of Galen in danger. Of course, no one knows anything for sure. All we have are suspicions.

As I said, you'll need a few other adventurers to help. That's not a suggestion you should take lightly. This is a big job, and it will be a tough fight. You'll need to deal with everything at the vent before it can be sealed, so be prepared.

Remember how I mentioned that shipwreck years ago. When the Stonelore Druids rescued me and took me in. Taught me to see the world in a new way. That was here on Galen.\n\nI set aside my cutlass for magic, but lately I've needed both blade and staff.

Count Mornard sent word to the Mages Guild that he wanted to hire a battlemage. I was already here, so the guild sent me. Not the first time I've sold my sword. Or my staff.\n\nI advise the count and get my hands dirty when I need to.

We've never faced such a test, but Vastyr's walls are built to withstand punishment. I believe they'll hold and give us the time we need to drive off the invaders. But even the strongest stone can be chipped away at with enough effort.

I'm not going anywhere while Sealord Nalos still lives. I could never return to King Orgnum while he draws breath. I don't care how many Sea Elves that beast has lured to his side. He dies by my hand.

Aye! I used to be a pirate. But years ago I was shipwrecked off Galen. The Stonelore Druids saved my life. They taught me to see the world in a different way.\n\nI took up magic. Then I started hunting knowledge instead of gold.

The druids of the Systres Archipelago are divided into three circles. The Stonelore, the Eldertide, and the Firesong. Usually they get along … or at least leave each other in peace. Lately? Not so much.
No. That's why we need the druids to help defend the walls. Vastyr cannot fall to the Dreadsails.

And House Mornard would be willing to hire her services. We're not above employing mercenaries, as you well know.\n\nThe point may be moot, however. We don't know how to get a message to her, or even where she's hiding.

There have been disagreements. Some of them violent. Firesong attacked Earthen Root, a Stonelore enclave. Claimed they were keeping a sacred seed from them. And some Eldertide on High Isle are causing trouble, working with the Ascendant Order.

Evil? It's not that simple, mate. The Eldertide don't like outsiders, and they'll fight anyone who threatens druid customs. And the Firesong are reclusive. They protect their sacred places and mostly ignore the outside world.
I know, mate. I was there. The Firesong say they don't know anything about Archdruid Michiel's travels and didn't approve his actions. I don't believe them. Neither do the Stonelore or the Eldertide.

Aye, they've been spending time at Glimmertarn, a Stonelore village to the north.\n\nLaurel has also been scouting for Sea Elf incursions. Frii rarely leaves her side. You wouldn't believe how Frii has grown. Matured? Not sure how to describe it.
