Aye. Druid Laurel told me about that. The Stonelore were shocked. Down through the years there have been arguments that turned violent, but nothing like a full-fledged war among the circles.\n\nAt least you stopped them from getting the Stonelore seed.

The Eldertide resent the Breton noble houses. All outsiders, really. They believe islands belong to the druids and some of them act on that belief. But we've got something of a truce with them on Galen.\n\nTurns out, Sea Elves are everyone's problem.

Hidden it somewhere, or so Laurel tells me. But she and the rest of the Stonelore are baffled. The seeds are just symbols. They don't know why Archdruid Devyric was ready to kill to get his hands on it.

Druid Laurel thinks it's got something to do with an old prophecy. The Eldertide blame the Sea Elves. And the Firesong … refuse to explain themselves to anyone.\n\nSo, your guess is as good as anyone's, mate.

You'll have to ask Frii yourself. I returned to Vastyr right after delivering the seed.\n\nThe way Frii communicates is still … perplexing. I believe we learn more about one another with every passing day, but many mysteries remain.

That would be Sealord Nalos. He recruits Sea Elf captains and offers them a place in the Dreadsails fleet. If I didn't know better, I'd say he was trying to create his own Sea Elf kingdom far from Pyandonea.\n\nCould explain our current problems.

Many, many seasons ago. I was so young I barely remember it. I recall being scared. There was some sort of rabid creature roaming the northern half of the island.\n\nAnyway, it's rarely used and only in extreme emergencies. I think this counts.

One of my guards noticed a group of Society of the Steadfast knights enter the library. Since we weren't expecting them, she went to check and found them ransacking the place!\n\nWe routed them, but now we're scouring the entire castle just in case.

Ah, very good. Look about you, friend. As you can see, the troubles on Galen cause no end of suffering. And many of the victims are simple farmers and townsfolk, not soldiers.\n\nDamn those Sea Elf pirates!

For the most part. There have been some incidents among the druid circles, too. But the Sea Elves are definitely the biggest threat. Talk to Sir Stefan Mornard. I'm sure he can find a use for someone with your obvious talents.

Yes, I'm aware. Probably has more to do with how developed High Isle has become as compared to Galen. Here, we mainly stick to our corner of the island and give the druids free rein over the rest of it.
Jonne is my cousin. He holds title to the Mornard estates on High Isle for my father, and manages many of our mercantile concerns there. But my father, the count, is the patriarch of House Mornard.

It might be more accurate to say he governs Vastyr and the lands surrounding the city. The northern half of Galen is mostly wilderness. Quite a few druids live there, but they look after their own affairs.
I leave that to you. I must keep the power of the ritual flowing until a choice is made.\n\nTalk to both of them, then decide. Will we restore Joslin or Octin to their original forms?

Aye, they're part of the same fleet, though they seem to be made up of many pirate bands, each with a ship or two of their own. It takes a strong leader to hold a fleet like the Dreadsails together and make them work toward a common purpose.

Laurel found me half-drowned after a shipwreck ten years back. She was just a girl then, but she had the sense to fetch help. Which is how I came to know the Stonelore Druids. She's been a friend ever since.
A key! But to what?\n\nShow it to Kiko. Maybe he's got another riddle for us. Morwha's four hands, I really didn't think we'd get this far! I'm glad you came along when you did.

Of course. After everything you've done for us, I still forget sometimes that you're not a druid.\n\nFrii had a special connection to the sacred seeds. They used their power as a nature spirit, as the Sower, to put some of that magic into the soil.

Druids choose their own paths. The Eldertide of High Isle are bitter, resentful. But as long as the Mornards don't push into druid territory, the Eldertide of Galen are content to live in peace.\n\nIt was foolish of the Dreadsails to provoke them.

Za'ji decided to … to … to wait out here for you, five-claw! Yes, yes, Za'ji waited to direct you. It is easy to get lost in such places, yes?\n\nLady Arabelle followed the Ascendant Lord—should Za'ji call him that now?
Oh, thank you, five-claw! Za'ji will go back to the druid village and wait for you there.\n\nLook for Caska. She is a great tracker. If she hasn't found Bacaro yet, she will shortly.

This isn't the first blood the Firesong have spilled. A group tried to take the Stonelore seed from a shrine on High Isle. Others attacked wyrds on the mainland. Now signs of them here at Tuinh?\n\nThey've turned against the other circles.

I thought Archdruid Devyric and his followers were renegades—a splinter group. But those orders we found, and what Orlaith just said—the Firesong want all three sacred seeds.\n\nArchdruid Orlaith is the leader of the circle. This is her doing.

Maybe? I'm not sure why they wanted to wake Frii, but other Firesong tried to take the Stonelore seed right around the same time. And now this.\n\nArchdruid Orlaith mentioned the Druid King's prophecy. Could that be what this is all about?
The relic? Ugh, my head. I can't remember. Sea Elf wine—so strong, so sweet.\n\nWait. Yes. I heard Neri had information. She found me when I followed her. Oops, hold on, still tipsy.
They headed west and followed Bacaro into Y'ffre's Path. Bacaro left some knights behind to slow us down, but I took care of them. \n\nDid you happen to see Za'ji on your way here?

It means that the sacred seeds aren't gone. That the Druid King's regalia will return … some day.\n\nUntil that time, we'll need to protect this tree. Nurture it. I'll make sure that all the circles know. We'll find a way to do it together.

Yes, dear, I am. Captain Marguerite's reputation is impeccable, and I've begun to study their ledgers. Nothing is amiss. I'll get someone I trust to perform a thorough investigation, but the society has done too much good to shut it down now.

Just about. Preparations are underway at All Flags Islet, but I have a task for you. I'd like you to invite Count Stefan, Druid Laurel, and Druid Ryvana for the talks. They deserve to have a voice in the proceedings.\n\nCaptain Za'ji and Caska, too.

The Stonelore are content to live alongside people who don't share their beliefs. They hope to set an example for others to follow, but they make no demands.\n\nAs for the Firesong, they're reclusive. They usually stick to their isle and ignore us.

Hmm. Meet me at the Telling Stone, the landmark near the center of the island. It would be easier to simply show you the prophecy, and it's close to Draoife Dell.\n\nBesides, Frii might be there. They will want to see you again.

I think the dream is a metaphor. Kasorayn was reminding us of where we came from. The day he describes will never come, but we should lead our lives as if it's close at hand. Make the right choices. Do the right things.\n\nThat's how I see it.

So much has been lost, so I can only guess. Maybe Archdruid Orlaith believes the seeds must be united to make the prophecy come true? Until they end their violent ways, though, I plan to keep Frii a secret.\n\nLet's go see what happens at the Draoife.

I probably know more about the Druid King than any other druid alive, but so much remains a mystery.\n\nThe Dream of Kasorayn describes a mountain shaking and a Sower awakening. I think it's talking about Mount Firesong and Frii.
Rock. Root. Leaf. Brook. All dreams of the Green. My kin, spirits given form. We are … purpose. Meaning. \n\nNow, a new purpose grows. Unwelcome change.

So much has been lost, so I can only guess. Maybe Archdruid Orlaith believes the seeds must be united to make the prophecy come true? Until they end their violent ways, though, I plan to keep Frii a secret.\n\nLet's go see what happens at the Draoife.

I probably know more about the Druid King than any other druid alive, but so much remains a mystery.\n\nThe Dream of Kasorayn describes a mountain shaking and a Sower awakening. I think it's talking about Mount Firesong and Frii.

Oh, I agree. But that's not going to be done quickly. And as long as I remain in place, we're all perfectly safe.\n\nYou go on ahead. Druid Laurel can stay here and help me disarm this insidious contraption.

The Druid King called Frii from the Green. Bound us to one day reforge the regalia. Sow the seeds when three circles become one. That is my purpose. A tender to the garden.\n\nBut events are uncertain. The seed is not safe, even here. What can we do?
King Kasorayn called me from the Green, a choice to be made. A moment, waiting. Needed.\n\nMy purpose is … to be. Wait. Listen. Roots must find water before they drink.

House Mornard put out a bounty on three gang members, each of them dangerous in their own twisted way.\n\nJust my luck that they've split up across Galen. But I suppose it's easier to break them one by one than face them bundled together.

The Stonelore reported glimpses of someone fitting his description lurking near Glimmertarn on the north side of Galen.\n\nHe's sneaky enough to not be seen, but he feeds off of fear. Best take care of him before he decides to kill again.
Yes, long ago. It was a … sanctuary. Lost to time. But it held answers, the truths of me. The longer I stayed, the more I learned … remembered. \n\nMy hands alone can ordain. I grow the seeds.

I … studied. The Stonelore Druids helped. Talked. They were patient, kind. The longer I spend with them, sun on leaves, wide smiles, soft hands, laughter like babbling streams. It gets easier to speak the mortal words. To be.

I don't know, but Count Mornard will be furious.\n\nArchdruid Orlaith might demand the sacred seeds in exchange for Stefan. Or she could make House Mornard stand down until her allies collect the seeds for her. This … is bad.
So I see. Thank you. That was more good than I could do. I chased after Orlaith and ran directly into her hands. Worse yet, I brought Stefan right to her.\n\nNow the Firesong Circle has a hostage.

We've been trying to get the leaders of all three alliances to the table since this whole affair began. It's being sponsored by the Society of the Steadfast. There are no guarantees, but this is our best chance to end the Three Banners War.

Typical. A druid who doesn't believe in property generously giving away something that doesn't belong to her. When last I looked, I ruled Galen.\n\nDid Archdruid Orlaith say what she wants from me as her price for keeping my son alive?

I … do not know. I just know that I alone can grow the seeds.\n\nA ritual. Hallowed ground. Three sacred seeds, three powerful symbols. They will sprout a crown, a staff, and a gauntlet. The Druid King's regalia, perhaps for a new king to wield?

You've been up to your eyes in heroics, as I hear it. The Dreadsails have been nothing but trouble for Galen. Unfortunately, it's not as simple as just a bunch of ornery Sea Elf pirates raiding the countryside. The druids are mixed up in this, too.

Right, the prophecy of the last Druid King. The Firesong want the sacred seeds that rightly belong to the other circles, while the Dreadsails just want Vastyr. This all has more knots than a tangled rope, mate.\n\nGood thing you're here to help.

Well, the three circles have been arguing, and that came to a head when the Firesong attacked and killed most of the Stonelore and Eldertide archdruids. That's how we learned they were working with the Dreadsails.\n\nAll because of some prophecy.
Not a great deal, unfortunately. It may have had some significance in the past, but now it's just an abandoned, overgrown cave. No one paid it much mind until Frii arrived at the village.

The Pale Worm is my nephew. A man once known in life as Niras Adrys. He was the light of my sister's life. And now his foul existence will end as ash and embers. Just like so very, very many others.\n\nI will mark your map, hunter. Let us end this.

I'll have to think about how to phrase it. I don't think I need to go into every detail, about how I should have really pressed Umindior more about this job before we arrived. \n\nAnd maybe I'll keep my flirtation with Veshin to myself.
You know, I never had the opportunity to ask. Frii did love to explore the place though. Took Druid Laurel along a few times, I believe. Perhaps she can tell you more.

Oh. Um. Am I blushing? \n\nI mean, he's interesting and very different. You know, even if it was just the influence of that stupid relic, I had fun talking to him. Usually I feel all awkward and don't really try to assert myself. Romantically, I mean.

The beacon has been ignited. I must give our druids time to make the trek from all points on the island. Plus, we have weapons to gather, supplies to pack.\n\nDon't worry. We'll get to the city before the attack begins in earnest.

This is Stonelore territory. My people know paths and trails that should allow them to avoid most of our enemies. And if all else fails, they know how to fight. That's why Stefan asked for our assistance in the coming battle.

Galen is no stranger to volcanic activity. Lava vents across the island are spewing forth molten rock and savage creatures.\n\nDruid Aishabeh knows more. She advises forming a group to tackle these vents.

I think Bacaro plans to call forth the spirit of Mount Firesong with the Druid King's regalia. With a spirit of that magnitude, the armies of Tamriel won't stand a chance.\n\nGo to Vastyr and tell Stefan to prepare his ships. We must go to Y'ffelon.

I founded the society to alleviate the suffering caused by the war in Tamriel, but now we go wherever we are needed. We provide healing, food, and shelter to those afflicted by strife or natural disaster. Our healing pavilions are well known.

We happened to be holding a conference on High Isle when Count Mornard sent word of the Sea Elf attacks. I mobilized the society here in the archipelago and came as soon as we could.\n\nWe'll draw resources from the mainland, but that will take time.
The Mornards are neighbors, so to speak. Count Leonard sent word to me about Galen's troubles with the Sea Elves. I have many responsibilities on High Isle, but still … I had to help an old friend.

I am trying to be in two places at the same time as best I can. It involves frequent voyages from Vastyr to Gonfalon Bay. Fortunately, I can trust Lady Arabelle to look after the alliance leaders when I must be absent.

I travel about, visit caves and quarries to identify the potential presence of valuable ores and minerals. My previous job was much safer than this one. No real risks whatsoever.\n\nI can't believe I almost died so early in my career.

Well, just the one. That's why I'm so affordable. I want to make a name for myself in the trade and I need the work. Maybe my employers will tell House Mornard how talented I am.\n\nHopefully on my next job I'll remember to ask about volcanoes.

That was what the Druid King told me. What the Dream tells us all. When the druids are ready to be … whole. Streams pouring into one river. Not fractured, not grasping for seeds with bloody fingers.\n\nI am awake, but the season is … wrong.

Magic? No, not like you're thinking. Symbols of office, authority. Only I can grow. Only I can sow the seeds. The Sower. Still ….\n\nWe must keep the seeds safe. Archdruid Orlaith must not claim them. Just in case I am wrong.

Visions and prophecies! That's what started this chaos! If Orlaith can't get the Sower, she'll use the blood of Laurel and my people to make herself the Druid King.\n\nTell me you found something. Give me a reason to hope. I am in sore need of it.

Respect? Perhaps not. But I left them mostly alone to practice their ancient religion. My biggest problem with them, before the current crisis, was their insistence to hold onto the past. Bretons need to embrace modern ways if we're going to thrive.

Legends call it the Gloomlantern. Some artifact stolen by pirates from the deep druids. It's said to shroud any ship in a thick veil of fog, hiding them from enemies. \n\nSounds perfect for getting bloody revenge on the Dreadsails, doesn't it?

Kiko apparently belonged to some commodore whose fleet made berth in the Systres. Legend says this commodore meddled in some druid ritual and cursed his fleet to undeath, including his stupid bird here.

He's sponsoring them, dear. And he's paying our salaries, so keep that in mind when you go to talk with him.\n\nGet Lord Bacaro to agree to let me begin the peace talks and then we can get High King Emeric and the others to the table.

Mount Firesong has certainly grown more active recently. But Frii only awakened due to the actions of the Firesong. Can one force a prophecy to come to pass? Still, I have a terrible feeling that Orlaith knows something we don't and that concerns me.

The volcano is erupting already. Lava vents long dormant on Galen and High Isle now flow with molten magma. The last time the volcano erupted, it caused terrible damage to the islands. Thousands of lives were lost. I pray it doesn't reach that level.

Don't worry about us, we'll be fine. We'll make sure any stragglers and the remaining wounded Eldertide get to Vastyr safely. And those who don't make it in time before the attack gets underway we'll keep safe here.
I … do not know. I did not have a chance to speak with her after she returned from Castle Tonnere. And then our village was attacked.\n\nI know Niraya, though. She did as I asked, I am sure of it.

The sacred seed. It's the relic they seek. I know how you helped the druids at our village.\n\nNiraya will resist, but Sealord Nalos will break her eventually. I would join you, mainlander, but my injuries will only slow you down.
Ages ago, a Breton coin-baron decided he liked the spot. He built his keep on top of an ancient Eldertide village. My folk lacked the strength to stop him. But we never forgot the insult.

A few seasons later, an Eldertide druid found the cave passage I told you about. He killed the coin-baron in his bedchamber. The same thing happened to the next lord who claimed the castle. The place was eventually abandoned, and it fell into ruin.

Certainly. The two of us can handle anything that crosses our path. I doubt either the Firesong or the Dreadsails know the seed exchanged hands yet, so we shouldn't attract too much attention. Regardless, I have no fear with Stefan by my side.

Many of the crews I've seen around here are new to the Dreadsails fleet. I think Sealord Nalos is hiring on every band of murderous scum with an itch for plunder he can find. I wonder what he's offering them.

Pirates don't gather in massive fleets unless the sealord plans to descend on a large, well-defended port. The only one on Galen is Vastyr. It's just a question of when and how Nalos chooses to launch his attack.

Now that you say that, I think she was wrong about a lot of things. Sailing into a hurricane is never a good idea, even if you are running from Dreadsails. \n\nDoes this mean I still have to avenge her?
My captain always said I didn't have a mind for such things. My crew never argued with her, so I just thought it was true.

The archipelago is too large for me to investigate by myself. We have to drive the Ascendant Lord out of hiding and put an end to him and his Ascendant Order. Since you know the movers and shakers on Galen, I'd like to send you there in my stead.

Possibly. But more to the point, I want you to warn Count Stefan and secure the aid of House Mornard. Sail to Vastyr and meet with the count. Let him know what transpired here and get him to agree to aid us when the order appears again.

Nalos won … by using a poisoned blade. Then he promised the Dreadsails vast riches if they forswore their oaths to King Orgnum and followed him into exile. A coward and a traitor.\n\nI will see him dead at my feet. I swear it!

The Ascendant Order? The rogue knights that caused trouble on High Isle? I haven't seen any indication that those rebels are on Galen, but I'll make sure the druids and my knights remain vigilant.\n\nI assume this has to do with the peace talks?

I certainly hope not. We're still recovering from the Dreadsails raid, not to mention Archdruid Orlaith's attempt to become a new druid king. Lord Bacaro sent the Society of the Steadfast to provide aid and support, and we appreciate the help.
Of course. After I accepted the countship, Lord Bacaro told me all about the plan to get the alliance leaders to sit down and discuss peace.\n\nHouse Mornard stands ready to help in any way we can.
Not usually, and never when the spirit has a story to share. I don't sense any danger, but I'll be right here in case you need help.\n\nNow, examine the plant and find out what it wants to show us.

Nature spirits, especially ones as strong as the Chronicle, are known among the circles. While the Firesong rarely leave Y'ffelon, they've always been aware of our spirit. Some even traveled here to partake of its stories.

Of course. That explains much. Sealord Nalos wants to get the seed for the Firesong. Obviously, we can't let him have it. Nor can we leave Niraya to the cruelty of the Dreadsails.\n\nThey've been interrogating her for hours.

This old keep stands above a pristine cavern, forgotten by all but the druids of my circle. After the lords of Tonnere abandoned their castle, we reclaimed our ancient shrine. It serves as a secret meeting place and refuge when the need arises.

Yes. There are Sea Elves held in the castle above. Traitors or outcasts among their own kind, I guess. I saw them once or twice when I was taken for questioning, but I didn't get a chance to speak with them.
Sealord Nalos kept me in the dungeons. I'm sure he isn't holding any Sea Elf prisoners down here, so they must be elsewhere in the castle. One of the old towers, perhaps.

When Archdruid Orlaith demanded our seed, we decided it was no longer safe in Tuinh. Ellic told me to take the seed and hide it. This was the most secret place I could think of.\n\nI didn't know the Dreadsails were coming, though.

The Eldertide, maybe? You know how vague legends can be. It was stolen from druids and hidden away when they fought back.\n\nSomeone must have taught Kiko the riddles so they could find the Gloomlantern again, but I guess they never got around to it.

And why shouldn't I? Captain always told the crew that Kiko and I were equals on account of how brainless we both were. \n\nBut I never promised to lead anyone to treasure, so you can guess which one of us got the better treatment.

Did you? Suppose that'd mean Kiko's mortal again. Well, I'll be a Goblin's aunt.\n\nI'll be sure not to kick him around the way the captain used to. And I suppose we ought to listen to his riddles before I decide to pluck him and make a pillow.
A meal's only as fine as its ingredients! And locally sourced and rare ingredients are all the better!\n\nWhat would you like to know?

They want our sacred seed? Whatever for?\n\nIt doesn't matter. If they wanted to learn more about the sacred seeds, then the Chronicle would be a good entity to ask. It must have stories from the age of the last Druid King.

Obviously the Chronicle is capable of more than we ever gave it credit for. Recording and showing recent events, influencing the minds of people and animals. But why druids would want access to that kind of power, I can barely speculate.

Do I look worried? He's a coward and a traitor, as are those who follow him. I'm not afraid of him. He should fear me! It doesn't matter how many blades he surrounds himself with—once I have the Mad Maiden back, I'll see him dead.
The Spirit of the Path. It calls to us. We must go. Defend it. Protect it.
As I said, I don't sell my vintage to just …. Wait. Chef Rhazeez? The Chef Rhazeez? \n\nA friend in Shornhelm said he paved life's roads with flavor. And now he's here in Galen?
Attacked. Frightened. It needs us. It must be defended!
I'm counting on it. This is one opportunity I can't afford to miss. \n\nNow make your way back to Chef, put in a good word. And be careful with that bottle!

Hmph! Fine. I'll have to figure out how to make the introduction on my own. I suppose I'll have to rub elbows with the common folk and see this demonstration for myself.\n\nWell, you have what you came for. Be off with you!
It means I will calm the volcano before it destroys the archipelago. Attempt to contain most of the damage to Y'ffelon.\n\nBut I will need your help, friend of Laurel. Friend of Frii.

Place the regalia to form a circle around me. Then command me to bind myself to the mountain. You are not the Druid King, but with the regalia and my willingness, the binding should hold.\n\nThen I will do what I can to quiet the volcano.

I will remain, but I will be different. As the seed becomes a tree, I shall become the spirit of the mountain. And I will slumber, as will Mount Firesong.\n\nNow take the crown and the gauntlet and place them around me.

First and foremost, we want to practice safe food handling. So be sure you don't let that smoldering cut set you ablaze!\n\nSure, it's extra work to harvest from a creature born in magma. But I'm certain it's got a unique flavor that can't be beat!

Hotter than Dragon's breath, and about as hard to find. They grow in ashes warmed by fresh lava flows. So where you find those peppers, you can bet there's probably a vulk'esh or two nearby.\n\nI can't wait to dice some up and try them raw!

I've heard great things about a brandy being made right here on Galen. Talk to Foucault Pierrane at the Jaded Ornaug.\n\nIt's a little hard to get a hold of, but supposedly it's the best. And who would I be to deny my dish the very best?

Oh, Tava's mercy, forgive me. Once I've got a dish on my mind, it's hard to think about anything else!\n\nI am Rhazeez! Chef of counts, saucier of servants, baker extraordinaire, and all-around purveyor of local delicacies. At your humble service.

To travel the world and craft the most exotic eats known to man and mer! I strive to make food that would be the envy of the Divines, the lamentation of the Daedra.\n\nA lofty goal, sure, but what brings us mortals together more than food?

Of course! How could I not come after hearing so much of the beautiful Systres? And with your help, my dish today will impart the blazing power and heat of Mount Firesong. \n\nOh, I can taste it already.

Frii isn't gone, friend. They've just become something … more. As a tree grows from seed to sapling to massive oak, so too has Frii transformed.\n\nThey're still with us, asleep in Mount Firesong, keeping us safe from the power of the volcano.

The Gilded Blades handled themselves well, as always. And when Lady Arabelle sounded the warning, we headed to the nearest ship and set sail. For me, that happened to be this one.\n\nAnd your spirit friend decided to stay behind? Is that true?

That's … intense. Can't say I'd have done the same, but I can respect someone willing to give up their life to save others. It isn't particularly the Sea Elf way, but still ….\n\nI think I'll drink to Frii whenever I sail past the mountain.

Whenever you want to see Frii, just look toward Mount Firesong. They're a part of it now. The spirit of the mountain.\n\nI need to tell the druids what happened here. Let them learn the last lesson the Sower had to teach us. Sacrifice.

All this death and destruction because Bacaro wanted to dig up some ancient Breton legacy.\n\nIf I learned anything from my time with the druids, it's that they don't need a king or a prophecy to make the world a better place. They just need to do it.

Don't be silly. Of course I do. But that legacy isn't crowns and gauntlets. It's people, born of humans and Elves to become something altogether new. It's magic, druids, and knightly orders. That's the Breton legacy I believe in. It's the best of us.

Despite Lord Bacaro's betrayal, the society has done good work here in the Systres and back in Tamriel. I'd hate to lose that, but you're quite correct. I need to determine if the society is trustworthy.

I'll start by meeting with Captain Marguerite. The society attracted many good people who have done a lot of good work. I won't see that die with Bacaro.\n\nI want the organization to continue, if at all possible.

It's the richest port on Galen, overflowing with plunder. Any pirate lord would gladly sack it if they thought they stood a chance. With the power of the Firesong at his side, Sealord Nalos believes he can succeed.\n\nHe also has a higher ambition.

What, you think I need more than these two? Well, you're not wrong. These are two of my officers. Veloran, first mate of the Mad Maiden, and Kovax, our quartermaster. Sealord Nalos imprisoned them because they were loyal to me.

Nalos wants to be king. Once he captures Vastyr, he plans to make it his throne. A large port with stout defenses would give him an island-kingdom to call his own. And the power to defy King Orgnum and all the fleets of Pyandonea.

Because he's a disloyal bastard. The warships and warriors Sealord Nalos plans to use to further his own ambitions belong to King Orgnum. They're not his to command. Nor is Galen his to rule.\n\nI'm here to deliver the king's justice.

They're scattered throughout the Dreadsails fleet, forced to obey Nalos because they think I abandoned them. But once word gets around that I'm ready to challenge Sealord Nalos, they'll return to my side.\n\nThen the Mad Maiden will sail again.

The muse-mouth plants in the room ahead are bloated, spewing out huge clouds of spirit motes. I can remove the vines that block the door, but I'm too old to withstand the motes in such concentrations.\n\nLuckily, I have a few vials of Y'ffre's rain.

Purified water from a sacred waterfall. Gwenaelle uses it to awaken those who sometimes get lost in the visions.\n\nThe water causes muse-mouth plants to shrink and close up for a time. Even ones bloated as much as these should react the same way.
Roots corrupted by blood, anger. Bindings tainted. Spirit … unwell. The Chronicle must … end.\n\nUse Y'ffre's rain on roots. Break bindings. Cleanse corruption. End … the story.
It is the only way. Pour the sacred water. Close the current book. End the anger, the sorrow … the mistakes.\n\nThis is what the Chronicle wants. What the story needs. Please.

Tava's mercy, no! To master your craft, you have to push your boundaries! Make mistakes! Lose a finger or two! How else would we ever learn anything?\n\nThe next attempt will be better! And the next after that more so!

It'd be a waste not to! I only used a sample from the ingredients you brought me. I've got plenty here to refine the recipe and try again. \n\nChef Rhazeez doesn't back down from a challenge, you know!

Aye. It's hard to believe, isn't it?\n\nThings seemed simple enough. Sea Elf pirates calling themselves the Dreadsails, harrying Galen. You turned back their attack at Windwrack Fort. But then we learned the Dreadsails had allies ashore.

Archdruid Orlaith demanded the other circles give her their sacred seeds. Said it was time to choose a new Druid King. When they refused, her Sea Elf allies attacked.\n\nWe fought them off and save two of the archdruids, but Sir Stefan was captured.
Aye, Archdruid Orlaith made a bargain with Sealord Nalos. Promised him a stronghold on Galen. In return, he was to get the Eldertide Circle's sacred seed for her.\n\nAnd eliminate the Draoife.

Wishing I was with you, most likely.\n\nI've got no head for strategy or court politics. But with Sir Stefan missing, Count Mornard's going to need my help with Vastyr's defenses. My place is here in the castle, like it or not.
You could say that. We studied together under Archdruid Rahval when we were both young. He remains a dear friend.

I have no family to speak of. To a great house, I'm little better than a vagabond. Poor and common, as nobles measure such things. Stefan's father would never allow us to marry. So I broke it off.\n\nA kindness for both of us in the end.

You … you see through me. There was a time when we were more than friends. Those feelings never truly leave you. But Stefan is the son of Count Mornard. There could never be anything more than daydreams for us.

Because Archdruid Orlaith demanded the nature spirit along with the sacred seeds. She thinks Frii is mentioned in the prophecy, the Dream of Kasorayn. That Frii is the Sower.\n\nI don't think they could hurt Frii, but we don't want them taken, either.

I'm not sure what I think. I know Frii has no desire to wield power and wouldn't harm a fleshfly. Frii doesn't understand such impulses. They're not a child or a fool, but they are naive to the ways of the mortal world and could be easily misled.

Yes, uh, you have the gold and I have the knife. So if you don't mind just, uh, handing it over then we can both go our separate ways and I won't have to stab you in any of your bits. That sounds very nice now doesn't it?

Wait— really? \n\nHah! I did it. Thank you so much. Now I can plunder and pillage. I can raze the coastline and scrape barnacles off the hull. My captain will let me back aboard. I can be a real pirate!

Is that a threat? Because it's very convincing. You're not going to punch me, are you?\n\nYou know what? How about I just leave you alone? Yes, yes, I'll just go off this way and you can leave me alone? That sounds good. Let's do that.
I have … ambitions. I think a few more jobs like this and I'm ready to become a professional. I think it suits me.\n\nI won't say more than that. But, trust me, I have plans.

I've heard that some people do this sort of thing for a living. As part of an organization. But I really don't know if I should talk about that.\n\nYou have real skills. We could do this again. If that interests you, find me in an Outlaws Refuge.

I don't trust Archdruid Orlaith to spare my son, even if she gets everything she wants. I will instruct my knights to stand down. Let her think I am paralyzed by this threat. Meanwhile, we secretly work to save Stefan from the Firesong.

While Archdruid Orlaith sees my knights doing what she demanded—nothing!—I want you to find Stefan and set him free. Dhulef says the Stonelore and Eldertide archdruids are here in the city. Get them to tell you where Stefan is being held.

Three. Eldertide, Stonelore, and Firesong. Stonelore are adequate druids, but they stay close to betraying the True Way. Accepting outsiders? Pah!\n\nThe Firesong are reclusive, but they never attacked other druids before.
What aren't I sketching may be a more apt question. Every direction I look is inspiring. Every ray of light a muse uncovering this land's natural beauty.

I think so, but I lost track of Frii when the Eldertide started pouring into the village. I'm sure they found somewhere safe to hold up. \n\nLet's trust in Frii. We can check on them after we light the beacon.
I don't think I was! Not really. No, this is very genuine. And I feel confident it was real for Neri as well. \n\nShe was something else. So different, so exotic. So strong.

What? Oh, yes. Of course. I'll be fine. Just got a bit caught up in the moment. Moments. Lots of moments. \n\nQuen seems a bit, ah, disappointed in this particular heist. But I'll remember it forever. She's probably just a little jealous.

Funny, Abah's feels like my home now. I'll head back there, of course, but I like being sent out like this. Seeing the world is fun. I think Zeira has some good ideas about making connections. \n\nDon't tell Velsa I complimented Zeira!
It could be anything. A legend. A story from the past. Maybe a bit of history. Y'ffre is the master of every story, both real and imagined. And through the Chronicle, we have access to them all.

While the location rightly belongs to all druids, it was abandoned long ago. The Ivy Throne was sealed away after the Druid King died, but druids of all circles once wandered the vale and dreamed of the past.\n\nThat is, until recently ….

Ivyhame has always been a symbol. The Firesong took control of the vale when Archdruid Orlaith began to demand the sacred seeds.\n\nIn hindsight, we should have seen that as the first sign of trouble.

What a relief. I can't bear to think of him trapped in such a state for all these years, suffering. I'm glad to know he's all right. \n\nI've heard stories of those who die upon the sea and remain in agony forever. Did he say anything else?

I hardly believe it myself. As Archdruid Orlaith was murdering Archdruid Rahval, suddenly the entire island began to shake. Then the cathedral shook apart, burying all the injured and innocents sheltering there under rubble—including Count Mornard.
I can rest easy tonight knowing he feels peace. I can only hope that your selfless deed will let him rest as well.

By utilizing my network of informants, of course! You aren't the only horse in my stable, dear. I have handmaidens, shopkeeps, dockworkers, and beggars throughout the island serving as my eyes and ears.\n\nIt costs a bit, but saves me time and effort.

Those silly things? Let's just say the author is a very dear friend of mine. I know her as well as I know myself, and I will admit to sharing a tale or two with her over the years.\n\nBut enough of that. You have a count to go talk to!

My notes. I make a record of all my cases. A habit I acquired working as a Dagger for High King Emeric. He was insistent on receiving complete reports.\n\nBetween you and me, dear, some of my adventures would make excellent novels!

Besides finishing this drink? Not a clue, my friend. Just spent the last of my ill-gotten gold, so securing a vessel would be our first point of order.\n\nAnd we may have to get … creative with how we do that.

We were at war with the Dreadsails. A lot of people died. The count, Archdruids Rahval and Ellic, lots of knights and druids …. It was a bloodbath.\n\nAll because Sealord Nalos wanted to claim Vastyr as the capital of a new Sea Elf realm.

The Firesong Circle and Archdruid Orlaith. They think the time of the druid prophecy is upon us. She wants to be the new Druid King and allied with the Dreadsails against the other circles.\n\nYou stopped her twice, but now she's got all three seeds.
Really? I appreciate the lead. First mate! That'd be quite the step up.\n\nYou hear that, Kiko? We'll make our names as honest pirates after all!
I've a feeling you're right. The fleet's just about done for, isn't it? \n\nI would've liked to get in on the action, but I suppose it's one less thing for us to worry about.
You know, if it was us that got killed instead of them, they wouldn't have batted an eye. Would they have, Kiko?\n\nRevenge can find me, if it wants to. The only thing I'm looking for now is a ship.

I saw Firesong Druids sail off with Dreadsails ships after Archdruid Orlaith buried allies and enemies alike. They had scores of captives aboard—people the Sea Elves captured during the attack.\n\nI can't help but wonder why Orlaith needs them.

We'll find a ship that deserves us, then use the Gloomlantern to pirate and plunder to our heart's content. It's the life I've always dreamed of!\n\nMaybe we'll see you out there on the high seas. We'll see you, but you won't see us. Cheers, mate!

I hoped I could count on Archdruid Rahval, but it's good to hear those words. Even with the secret paths, though, it was difficult avoiding our enemies. The wilderness is thick with Dreadsails and Firesong.\n\nI assume you helped settle things here?

I don't think I'm anybody, now. Once, I was known as Jocien Rane. I was a sailor in Duke Mornard's shipping fleet. We went from Vastyr, to Gonfalon, to Daggerfall, to Wayrest, and back again.\n\nIt was a safe enough route. Until this damn war.

Three Banners War? I've heard of no such thing. I'm talking about Ranser's War, of course. Emeric seemed a decent sort, but his sleight can't be so easily forgotten.\n\nHis privateers sank us off our very own shores.

Heh, a good jest, stranger. Next you'll tell me a Daedric Prince sits in the White-Gold Tower. No, my friend. As bitter as it is fighting our kin, this war will end only one way.\n\nWith Ranser on the throne and House Mornard properly elevated.
Trees that grow crumble into mulch. Rivers turn to streams, to brooks, to nothing. The fungi, they claim all. \n\nMy head, it aches so.

I … I do not rightly know, stranger. In life, I had saltwater in my veins. Perhaps I need to be near it in death. \n\nThe sea has some claim over me. Watching the tides go in and out brings me a sort of peace, melancholy as it is.
This squirrel is accusing me of robbing her out of house and home! Can you imagine the gall? Accusing me, after all I've done for her?

It is my duty as a scholar to transcribe the wilds of this forbidden island so the rest of Tamriel may imagine its savageries from the comfort of their studies. It has bested me once before, but by the Divines I won't fail again.
I can't recall … no, wait, I'm certain I haven't. I've only just arrived here, after all. I don't feel ready.\n\nPerhaps when my bones turn to salt and sand, I'll take a walk. Perhaps then.

Yes, but if I had known how much endless prattling I'd have to endure, I'd never have taken the contract. No amount of coin is worth this dolt's interpretations of rock carvings and moss readings. I'm at my wits end.

Archdruid Orlaith has demonstrated a talent for getting what she most desires. She found the Stonelore and Eldertide seeds. Multiple times, in fact. To protect Frii, to keep them safe, we need to keep them with us.
Plundering, of course. My guess is he's been passed from ship to ship for some time on account of the curse keeping him alive. \n\nAlmost makes you feel kind of bad for him. Almost.

My crew? Of course! Been a pirate all my life, and they were the only people I had in the world. They were like family to me. Isn't this what you do for family?\n\nAnd Kiko keeps squawking out these riddles, so I can only guess he agrees.
Seeds cannot un-sprout, even if I ask them nicely.\n\nThe seeds are together. I do not think they will want to part again. Not before crown, staff, and gauntlet are regrown.

Ah, well … I suppose that's my fault. When we took our last prize, I was reading through the ship logs, as I like to do, and that's when I found Kiko's passphrase.\n\nThe captain smelled treasure, and that was it. We were bound for the Systres.

It would be wrong for Orlaith to take crown, staff, and gauntlet. Bad. But it is also wrong to deny growth when the season is upon them. How can I choose between wrongs?\n\nI have not learned to do that.
Looks like a … key? Or half of one, maybe? Never seen anything like it. \n\nMaybe we'll dig up the other half next.
Tall Papa's breeches, I hope not! Though I'll admit it's a blessing having you here to help.\n\nKiko must think so, too. Look at him, he seems happier than I've seen him in ages.

Because so many of our records have been lost. The druids were almost wiped out a number of times in our history. And the Druid King's sanctum in Ivyhame has been sealed since his death. No one has passed through that door in countless seasons.

We're better off than we would have been if we'd been surprised. And the extra warriors help. The bastards would have taken Vastyr quickly without them.\n\nWe had defenders and a bit of foresight. That at least gave us a fighting chance.

We need the light of the moons to shine upon the sacred pools in this chamber. Mara's Tear and Shandar's Sorrow must witness and sanctify our deeds this night.\n\nElder Verline can tell you what to do. I must prepare myself.

You need to know more than that they are here and desire our deaths?\n\nAh, forgive me. I share your confusion. We did not guess how prevalent the Allwither's influence had become. Many powerful Firesong Druids have fallen under its dark influence.

A difficult question. Firesong Druids revere the great cycle of creation and destruction. Death and rebirth. But those who give themselves to the Allwither see only half of this endless wheel. The dark half.\n\nThey must not gain the Ivy Throne.

Tradition demands that together they acknowledge a new druid king. Since no druid is ready to make that claim, better that Laurel, Bacaro, and I keep them safe.\n\nGalen is at peace. The Dreadsails have dispersed, the druid war has ended. Now ….
I suppose we did. I am not accustomed to working alongside a partner. But your presence made this dark journey through these unhallowed lands … just a little bit easier.\n\nThank you.
To know the worthy. I am the Sower. But I can choose when to quicken the seeds … and for whom.

I know what you're thinking. How did a Wood Elf become a Stonelore druid? I wasn't satisfied with just following the Green Pact. It wasn't enough. So I came to Galen to find myself. Turns out, I fell right in with the Stonelore Circle.

First bounty's on a Bosmer called Urredhel. Always had a hunch he'd try to make it to Amenos one day. It's a prime hunting ground for someone as twisted as him. \n\nBut it seems he's decided to whet his appetite for murder on Galen first.

Elissa Marcellinus, Imperial sorcerer. Suspected of murder even before she fell in with the Ascendant Order.\n\nHer societal connections protected her back on the mainland, but House Mornard isn't willing to give safe harbor to her blood lust.

A Khajiit by the name of Sabashur. Assassin for hire who crossed the wrong person and fell in with this crowd. Now his name has made it to the top of my bounty list.\n\nPity. Got a feeling he was the most principled of the bunch, at least.

They were the only ones who would talk to me at first. The other circles don't like outsiders. Even now,  they struggle to accept that I'm one of them. Still, I've gotten good at convincing the Eldertide not to attack me. And having Mohair helps.

Haven't you heard? You are what you eat. After a few meals, the Fauns will smell like the berries.\n\nPlus, I had these seeds infused with magic. They'll sprout when you plant them! The Fauns will have plenty to eat and the wolves will leave them be.

I'm neither an elder nor an archdruid. Shouldn't Lady Arabelle invite one of them?\n\nHmm. Most of the surviving senior members of the circle are deep in discussions about the Draoife. Very well. Tell her I'll attend the talks.
That's really it, isn't it? Just like the legends said. I can't believe it!\n\nWell, that's it. I owe you a drink, at the very least.

She's somewhere on the east side of Galen, near what the locals call the Embervine. \n\nShe may try to integrate with the druids, but more likely she's using the hotspot there as a convenient smokescreen for her experiments with Daedric sorcery.

South side of Galen, near Windwrack Fort. Loves his work, hates not keeping busy. Got a feeling he's waiting for the right moment to stow away and get back to it. \n\nWe'll see if me and my sword can persuade him to take an extended leave.

Frii is our secret weapon. Dhulef will take Frii to the Temple of Y'ffelon, just as Archdruid Orlaith demanded. Then, while Frii stalls her with this guardian you told me about, you and I rescue the captives from the Firesong. Including Laurel.

We land on the far side of the island with my knights and free my people while Orlaith conducts her ritual.\n\nI'll arrange passage to Y'ffelon. Find Frii and get them to agree to the plan, then meet me at the docks. You'll be well rewarded, friend.

We'll continue our respite until we're called back to our duties in Hammerfell. Worry not, I won't let Unu out of my sight so long as we remain here. \n\nI've come to quite like this island, and Unu seems fond of the taste of salt water.

He may not look it, but Unu is a key component to our business endeavors. None would dare pull one over on me with the looming threat of third-degree burns nipping at their heels. \n\nAnd, well … it doesn't hurt that he's quite adorable.

Hmm. I have my suspicions. Unu and his kind are native to Hammerfell. He may be the first dragon frog to set foot on Galen! \n\nAnd, I mean, look at him! It's no surprise that he's caught an envious eye or two.

Aye. Never hurts to take stock of what we know.\n\nArchdruid Orlaith captured Druid Laurel while you and Frii were exploring the ruins of Ivyhame. Worse yet, Orlaith finally got her hands on the sacred seeds of the other druid circles.

I could put him in a carrier cage, though I can't imagine he'd enjoy that. \n\nPerhaps I should enroll him in a training program. Ensure that he'll be prepared in an emergency situation. A program led by me, of course. What do you think, Unu?

Captain Siravaen strikes me as someone who pays her debts. Without your help, her ship and crew would still be in the Dreadsails' hands and Sealord Nalos would be alive. I might remind her of that.\n\nAnd my generous offer of gold should also help.

She allied her circle with the Dreadsails, broke the truce of the Draoife, and murdered Archdruid Rahval. It's clear Orlaith will hurt or kill to get what she wants. Which is why I'm worried for Druid Laurel.
Ha! As if you didn't know. You're here to face a reclusive master of Tales of Tribute. \n\nYou weathered the island's hazards, all in the hopes of playing cards against the legend that is … me!
A druid that plays—root and stone, I'm Braigh, sandpiper! The Braigh! Braigh the Deck-Breaker! \n\nI wield the power of the Druid King's Tale! My deck conquers all!

Poor tamsfolk. You came all this way to play cards against a master. For what? To learn my secrets? To glean my wisdom? \n\nLet's play. But the only thing you'll learn is how a loss to Braigh burns like druid fire! Yes, indeed!

Once again you've asked me such a daunting question. Perhaps it's the massive trees that have stood east of Galen for thousands of years. Or maybe the druidic stones with their delicate carvings. Beauties both man made and natural abound.
Wherever my muse takes me. Along the riverbed, through the glen, atop the mountains. There are wonders great and small here. Though, I certainly wish I brought more parchment.

It is difficult with the visions and whispers floating in my mind. I fear what they tell me though I know I'll not be a witness to their terrible events. \n\nStill, I should rest and drink water. I have not done so in longer than I can remember.

Not happened. Will happen. Or might. The tides of time are difficult to chart. So many swirling waters and undertows. You could get lost out here in the expanse. Float away before the end and the whispers sweep up to shore. \n\nMy stomach growls.

I had a good feeling about young Stefan. He's nothing like his father, gods rest his soul. \n\nNow we can get back to the matter at hand. It's time to move forward with Lord Bacaro's peace talks. I just wish I knew what the Ascendant Order was up to.

They are a proud and fickle lot, but they have one thing in common, dear. They respect you.\n\nGo to the city palace and talk to them. Ask them to remain patient. Then speak to Lord Bacaro. See if you can convince him to let me get things started.

The Ascendant Lord and his minions are still out there somewhere. Lord Bacaro is hesitant to proceed when an attack could occur at any moment, but I can't keep the alliance leaders here much longer. Their patience with the situation grows thin.
Perhaps. Perhaps not. For good or ill, the season of their awakening draws close.\n\nAnd if Archdruid Orlaith hurts others to compel me … I do not want to see blood spilled because of me.
Think of it more as pruning than killing. There's no campaign against the creatures, but they have outlived their original purpose and lived too long in a fraught existence.
Hah! Or your Three Banners!\n\nAll I know is that having three heads seems like it would be a tormenting existence. I've only got one, and I can barely keep it on straight!
Of sorts. The way I see it, chimera are a living reminder that while there is power in unity, there is not always harmony.

A personal question? Hmm. Well, I suppose you earned that right. To tell the truth, I never wanted to replace my father. He was more suited to politics and budgets than I'll ever be.\n\nI'm coping. And I'm trying to do my best for Galen and its people.

We've exchanged letters, but I've been busy here in Vastyr, and Laurel has her hands full helping the druids recover. The deaths of the archdruids hit both of us hard, especially Archdruid Rahval.\n\nAs for Frii ….

Eyfi? Protect me? Preposterous! No no, she's here to assist with menial tasks that could otherwise impede my research. Speaking of which, I must be off soon. This has been a lovely reprieve, but there is much left to record!
A simple misunderstanding between myself and the local druids. They mistook my gestures for rudeness and, well— we shouldn't dwell on the past. I'm sure all has been forgiven by now. Probably.

Laurel says Frii is unsure what to do next. Their purpose revolved around the sacred seeds and restoring the Druid King's regalia. Now they're waiting for a new Draoife to be formed so that the druids can decide how to move forward.

He was always full of adventure, that was what made me fall in love with him. Everything was exciting to him. He greeted each day like that specific one had the possibility to make all his dreams come true.\n\nI loved his laugh more than anything.

I have eyes that see, yes. And someday, you and I may come to blows.\n\nBut tales of your adventures precede you. And recent acquaintances have taught me that perhaps some of your kind can tame their thirst. Let us see what tomorrow brings.

Every vampire leaves a trail of blood and sorrow in its wake. Some more than others.\n\nThere is a beast nestled somewhere in the belly of Western Skyrim. I will find him, and pull him wriggling into the purifying light of day.
Every hunt is personal. But yes, the end to this pursuit will manifest a deep satisfaction within my very soul.

I'm sure that's what Jocien would want for me, but … I don't know. I miss him, of course, but I don't feel lonely. \n\nAll these years, I've felt him in the sea air, seen him in the sun on the waves. And now, having his ring, I'm content. Truly.

Aye. The Firesong dragged her to the temple along with Frii. Orlaith made some ugly threats, but Laurel was unharmed when last I saw her.\n\nShe'd better stay that way or the Firesong will have to answer to me. And to Stefan as well.

My people are like a pack of wild dogs. With a strong leader to guide us, we'll fight to our last breath. But without one, our fury … dissipates.\n\nOnce Sealord Nalos fell and the Firesongs abandoned them, the remaining Dreadsails fled.
I'm afraid not. But hey, if there's anything else you need, just let me know!
A break-in. To go where we are not wanted. Brings Raz back to his days as a kitten. \n\nHe was endlessly causing trouble for his mother. Ah, simpler times.
Exactly! Plan A did not work, which is fine! Plan B is just as good.\n\nRaz will stay here, in the parlor. You head back out into the city. After a moment, Raz will cause a distraction.

Do not get this one started. Young Raz was a rapscallion. He gave poor Kideya fits, always sneaking sweetrolls and moon-sugar pies from her kitchen when her back was turned. \n\nNot important. Head outside and look for a way into the suite, yes?
Jocien? Oh, by the Eight. He went missing so long ago, I feared the worst. I didn't want to believe it. \n\nBut how did you happen upon his ring? And … how did you know where to find me?
His ghost! Oh, my poor Jocien. \n\nI can scarcely believe it, but there's no denying this is his ring. And I know my Jocien, he would have wanted me to have it. Even in death.

No, and Queen Ayrenn grows more annoyed with every rise and fall of the sun. Inactivity pains her.\n\nLord Bacaro keeps delaying, and Lady Arabelle isn't sure what to do. But these are details that Za'ji isn't aware of. You should talk to her.

Feh- the gold be damned now. It was the allure of getting out of Skyrim. But now… well. I just have to make sure he doesn't end up entangled by one of those druids or a chew toy to one of these beasts.
I've been sorely tempted, believe me. But— my honor and my conscience tells me leaving this fool to his own devices would be a death sentence. One he doesn't entirely deserve. Well, not yet anyway.
Right. All the best to you. Eyfi, my loyal companion, on your feet. Time to continue on our journey of exploration!
Very well, but don't dawdle too much. There's scholarly pursuits to be done!

Willing! Hah! Please.\n\nNot every request from House Mornard calls for threat of life and limb. But we try to respect even the more frivolous ones for the sake of diplomacy. Even if just to spare the lives of some poor, defenseless hirelings.

Orlaith murdered Archdruid Rahval during the Dreadsails attack on Vastyr. And Count Mornard and Archdruid Ellic were buried under the city's cathedral when it collapsed.\n\nAt least you killed Sealord Nalos. The Dreadsails aren't a threat anymore.

She's trying to make the prophecy—the Dream of Kasorayn—come true. With herself as the new Druid King! To do this, she thinks she needs the sacred seeds. And Frii, the Sower named in the prophecy.\n\nThat help, mate?

Frii said they spent a long time preparing it. That it was a part of them, a part of Galen. A part of the druids. I don't know if they meant that literally or figuratively. It wasn't always easy to understand Frii and the ways of a nature spirit.

Frii enjoyed sitting under it. I think they felt a connection to it, but I'm not really sure. The ways of nature spirits are very different from the things we know.\n\nThey said to sprinkle the soil, and I think that's the perfect place to do it.

That is unclear. He lost a father today, as well as a mentor that was just as precious to him. We may have won this battle, but Archdruid Orlaith has all three sacred seeds.\n\nSpeak with Stefan, Count Mornard now. He must decide how we move forward.

To get to Frii. The spirit is fond of Laurel. They spent a lot of time together after Laurel brought Frii to Galen. Orlaith can bend Frii to her purpose by threatening Laurel.\n\nTu'whacca knows Orlaith doesn't make empty threats.

Frii made their decision. Without their sacrifice, none of us would have survived the volcano's eruption.\n\nI'll find time to go to Mount Firesong. To commune with the new spirit of the volcano. Sometimes bound spirits respond. Sometimes they don't.

No, it's not all that bad. Stressful, yes, but rewarding in its own way.\n\nYou know, I really do like making decisions that help people. And I've even gotten the nobles and druids to sit down together. Once. Maybe my plans will work out after all.
What? Did Stefan say something? What are you asking?\n\nCount Stefan and I are getting along fine. Never better. And I'd rather not talk about this at the moment, if that's all the same to you.

Perhaps one day, but I'm much too young to be called an elder, don't you agree?\n\nAs for archdruid, one doesn't just receive that accolade. Only druids of immense presence and power ever achieve such a rank. Will I someday? We shall see.

There is always a chance, five-claw. It may be very, very small. So small that you cannot see it with the naked eye. But it is there nonetheless.\n\nThis one does hope it works out though. War is a terrible business indeed.

Yes, but according to Za'ji, the queen's in a terrible mood. He thinks she'll raise anchor and leave the proceedings the first time something stupid comes out of Emeric or Irnskar's mouth.\n\nHence, our sudden burst of activity.

I will go with friend-Dhulef. Give myself to Archdruid Orlaith. Then I will wake Urdiir the Guardian. Call them to fulfill their ancient duty.\n\nPlease. Find Druid Laurel. Save her. Too much blood has watered these lands already.

Years ago, when I was studying with the Stonelore. Back then the Firesong were more connected to the other circles. We only visited the outer chambers. The central area was sealed off long ago, after it became the tomb of the last Druid King.

The Society of the Steadfast's primary charter involves providing relief to those unfortunate enough to be caught up in war or disaster. Galen was recently rocked by both brutal assaults and volcanic activity. We're sending supplies and healers.

You misunderstand. I don't plan to lord over the druids. Instead, I want to welcome the druid circles as friends and neighbors. Give them a voice in the governing of the island if they want it.\n\nMy time with the druids … I understand them.

Something I like? I … I like being with Druid Laurel. I like to walk in the woods and listen to songs as old as the world. To care for the gentle creatures of the forest. Tend seedlings that fall on hard soil.

I haven't spoken with our surviving elders and archdruids about that yet. I did briefly consider asking to be part of the new Draoife, but I'm not sure that's a good idea. I'm a much better historian than I am a councilor.\n\nBut if I'm asked, I will.

For now. The Mad Maiden needs repairs. We took some damage in that broadside with the Firesong Druids. It's nice to have a friendly port where we can tend to that work.\n\nAnd I have grown fond of the food they serve here in the castle.
The council of druid leaders? Oh of course, but how long will it take them to sort that out?\n\nNo, no. I was speaking in the abstract. It is an interesting puzzle to consider, don't you think?

I imagine I'll set sail sooner or later. I'm a treasure-hunter at heart, not a court mage. But I'm in no hurry. Count Stefan is going to need some help putting the island back together.\n\nI'm not about to leave him in a bind.
Plan A will not work, then! No worries, Plan B is just as good.\n\nRaz will stay here, in the parlor. You head back out into the city. After a moment, Raz will cause a distraction.

The parlor is below ground, yes? But the patrician suite is above the parlor. The suite should have a view of Vastyr.\n\nWhile Raz keeps the thugs focused down here, find a way inside. Perhaps a ramp or ladder? Get creative.
Take the path to the west and follow it toward the mountain. You'll come to a door that leads to the temple.\n\nI'll … need a moment. The Firesong were none too gentle with me.

That was my thought. The tomb is said to lie at the heart of the old temple. Where else would Orlaith perform the ritual to claim the regalia and name herself the new Druid King?\n\nLet's go get back our friends and put an end to that ritual.

King Kasorayn saw much in his Dream, yet I do not think he saw this. I quickened the sacred seeds as foretold. The task is done, yet I'm still here. Unbound. Free to choose.\n\nI must find a new purpose. A new choice.

I face a new challenge, more intimidating than a thousand foes. I must take my father's place as count, leader of my house, Steward of Galen, and loyal vassal of High King Emeric.\n\nThere are wounds to heal. Things to tear down and build anew.

Not in the least. That's just between the Gilded Blades and Galen. Maormer don't have friends—we have prey. But it might be useful to have a neutral port where we can talk or trade.\n\nI'll mention it to King Orgnum next time I see him.

Oh, a chef's work is never done while the world still hungers! I'll just have to see what's on the menu for adventure tomorrow!\n\nPerhaps I'll dazzle some sailors with a coral crab confection, or see what dishes the local druids might inspire!

No surviving Stonelore was as close to Archdruid Rahval as Laurel was. She would be a strong and passionate voice for her circle here at court. An excellent idea, friend!\n\nOh. That's not what you were asking, is it? Well, let's leave it at that.

Then I will do that. Listen, tend, learn. I am old in seasons, but young in understanding. Perhaps I will come to understand more of this world with the passing seasons.\n\nThank you, Laurel-friend. I am glad our roots intertwined.

Oh, most certainly! The Steadfast knights will keep it safe. But I need to return to High Isle. The attacks, the damage to the city, and the ongoing activity from Mount Firesong have devastated Galen. The island needs all the aid I can give it.

Frii will always have a place among the Stonelore, but without a purpose, I'm not sure what they'll decide to do. Most nature spirits are bound to a particular location. Not Frii. They can come and go as they please.\n\nBut I hope they decide to stay.

It was terrible. The building started to shake and the stones above trembled. I yelled for everyone to run for the doors. I threw them open … then the floor fell away.\n\nI must have blacked out. When my head cleared, I was outside … alone ….

That's some good news. Focusing on what we've won rather than what we've lost is the only way to not fall into despair. Vastyr still stands, safe because of our efforts. And though we've been dealt a terrible blow, all hope is not lost.

Look, I wasn't going to actually hurt the bird. Really, I couldn't. I'm a pirate, I've slit a few throats, but Kiko? He's never hurt anybody.\n\nOur captain would say I'm weak, but I just can't find it in me to treat Kiko the same way she did.

You've bigger things to worry about than my intentions. But the lordling is right. You do need me.\n\nLook, you helped recover my ship and crew. Helped me kill Nalos. Why don't you head to the castle? Check on the lordling. I'm not going anywhere.
Barnacles! You're right. What are we waiting for? Let's go claim our prize!

Don't think I've forgotten that. I'm a pirate, but I'm not the type to go back on my word!\n\nI just need to … secure some funds, that's all. Maybe Kiko can help with that. You hold on to the Gloomlantern for now and meet me at the tavern in Vastyr.

Ah, fair enough. I'm a member of the Psijic Order, though my affiliation sometimes feels thin. I tend to work alone.\n\nI have the responsibility of oversight in this region. A role that I assigned myself, in all honesty.

Hmm … no quick way to answer that. We're mages who dedicate ourselves to the Old Ways—methods of controlling reality that are much too powerful for most.\n\nTime magic, for example. Not something we like to see wielded belligerently.
Picture time as a river. Trite, perhaps, but a useful concept. An eddy swirls within Bal Sunnar's temporal flow. Not too large, yet. I'd like to find the source before it grows.

Not yet. An event like this can arise for all sorts of reasons—powerful spells, activated relics, Daedric trickery. Sometimes they just happen.\n\nThe source should be obvious when you see it. Time distortions require a great deal of power.
Depends. I've studied events like these for a long time. If the source is something common, then I'm prepared. If not, well, I'll have to figure it out.
To King Orgnum, yes. And to my brother. I hope Nalos saw my brother's face as we cut him down.\n\nNow go take care of your own, mercenary. I'm sure the lordling could use a friend right now.

When the temporal knot resisted containment, I lost control. It exploded with energy. And now we're here.\n\nThis vaguely looks like the tower, but different. Newer. We should go outside to investigate.

Zalar-do … ahh yes. The vampire lord in Hrota Cave. After I cleansed my blade, I returned home to the ashlands of Morrowind. My father passed away, joining our ancestors in our ancestral crypt. \n\nIt was a long journey, escorting him to Necrom.

Hold your sympathies. Do I seem as though I had a happy childhood?\n\nMy father was a tyrant. His passing meant little to me, beyond a tiresome task and a long journey through the lands of the Telvanni.

Now that you're here, I'll head back, too. I could be more helpful at the druid village than in a cramped cavern. You might not believe this, but sometimes my size can be a hindrance.\n\nJust make sure to bite Bacaro a few times for me.
I feel emptied. This attempt at containing the distortion took all I had. And yet, it wasn't enough.\n\nI have to consider my next approach. Perhaps it can't be contained at all.
Seems pretty similar, right? I can only surmise, based on what happened in the tower, that we've jumped in time again. The question now is when?\n\nI don't recall this lava in the past.
I owe my family an explanation. I will return to the ash and sullen skies of my homeland. Perhaps my words will help. \n\nThe knowledge that Niras is laid to rest will ease the suffering I've caused.
Yes. You already know it. Or you will. Your path is more difficult to see. Blurrier. Like seawater.\n\nIf you do not know, it is not my place to say. Do not ask again.

I fragmented. Shattered across time. Something … collected me. Rebound back into this form.\n\nNow, I am with you. But, also, watching an emperor rise. A nation cut in twain. A people vanish. I see all of these.
Yes. And no. It was the same will that tied the temporal knot. Cold. Silent.\n\nI choose not to investigate further.

They were distinctly Firesong, that much I know. As I sailed to Galen, I read about druids. Fascinating folk. I recognized the symbols on their clothing.\n\nBeyond that, the guidebook was short on details, other than they usually stay on Y'ffelon.

On the street, like some common vagrant? Oh, that won't do! \n\nI heard Queen Maraya hosted him when he came through Wayrest! He's the most innovative chef in all of Tamriel, and he's sending some shabby hireling to beg for my fine vintage?
Tell you what. I'll sell you the bottle you're asking for. \n\nBut, if you can convince Chef Rhazeez to cook a private, high-class dinner at my estate, I'll give it to you for free.

By utilizing my network of informants, of course! You aren't the only horse in my stable, dear. I have handmaidens, shopkeeps, dockworkers, and beggars throughout the island serving as my eyes and ears.\n\nIt costs a bit, but saves me time and effort.

Those silly things? Let's just say the author is a very dear friend of mine. I know her as well as I know myself, and I will admit to sharing a tale or two with her over the years.\n\nBut enough of that. You have a count to go talk to!

My notes. I make a record of all my cases. A habit I acquired working as a Dagger for High King Emeric. He was insistent on receiving complete reports.\n\nBetween you and me, dear, some of my adventures would make excellent novels!
Famous? That's a matter of opinion! The more places I visit, the more chance I have of becoming a household name, I suppose.\n\nBut I don't care about that as much as I do about my mission!

That's hard to say—the Ascendant knights hide their faces. They talk about standing up against unjust rulers, but they rob and pillage as they please. They've been active over on High Isle. Haven't seen them on Galen yet, though.

Who's to say they haven't? \n\nWhat we do know is that the wraiths are not attacking these Firesong. And for that I have no explanation. Perhaps it has something to do with the motes we see clouding their minds.

Not officially, no. But Lord Bacaro tells me everything. I handle the day-to-day workings of the Society of the Steadfast and command our small contingent of knights. When Lord Bacaro travels, I oversee operations at Steadfast Manor.

They're one of the Breton houses that keeps my trade well-funded. They deal in ore and minerals, both extraction as well as commerce.\n\nThey grew quite wealthy from this business. You can understand why I'm eager for them to learn my name.

Druids! They mostly keep to themselves, refuse to participate in politics or significant trade, and look down upon the great works of House Mornard and the Breton people. They contribute practically nothing to Galen's strength or prosperity!

As the duly appointed count of Galen, I oversee the regional authority of Vastyr and the rest of the island. We learned long ago that nothing good came of making druids pay taxes. Better to leave them alone.\n\nA lesson my son would be wise to heed.

A leader who takes foolish risks doesn't last long. I serve my people best by commanding from here, not fighting in the field. If the need arises, I won't hesitate to ride with my knights.\n\nUntil then, I trust Stefan to see my will done.

I started leaving out seeds and nuts for her after she lost her mate in an owl attack. \n\nBut it's been months now, and I never once got a thank you, so I stopped, and now her tail's all in a puff. To her, I guess that counts as stealing!
Talk? I can barely get a word in to defend myself! Then again, she's never been a very good listener. I don't know why I'm surprised.

The Dreadsails happened, but it makes no sense. The Eldertide have no riches—druids don't care about such things. And they command formidable magic.\n\nWhat pirate attacks a target that can fight back for no obvious profit?

Nothing good, that's for certain. They're pirates, slavers, murderers, and thieves. In my experience, the only good Sea Elf is a dead Sea Elf.\n\nThese Dreadsails, though. They're the worst of their kind.

Corrick's the name, banneret in the service of House Mornard. My family has proudly served the lords of Galen for generations. I'll bring these murderous Sea Elves to battle and defeat them. Or die in attempt.

Nothing like this. Isolated raids, some pillaging. They were pirates before, but now they act like a conquering army.\n\nWatch out for the one that knocked my knights senseless. She must be quite a fighter to defeat them without spilling any blood.
And you lived to tell the tale? I'm impressed. You might be able to teach my knights a thing or two. Maybe Sir Stefan will lend you to me as a training officer when this is all over.

Oh, not familiar with knightly ranks? Do they do things differently on the mainland? A banneret is the equivalent of a captain in my order—a knight who commands other knights.\n\nLooks like I've got some work to do with these louts, though.

Zeira asked me to seek out the Thieves Guild here in the Systres. I think she has plans to connect with some of the different guild halls around Tamriel and these islands. \n\nMet Umindior and agreed to work with him. Now he's missing.

Beautiful, isn't it? If this wasn't a job, I'd like to take in the sights. It was an old druid settlement. Since they don't keep records, no one knows what they used it for.\n\nAt some point the Sea Elves moved in. Now they live here enjoying the sun.

Ah, such a nice change of pace. Usually this one cannot walk through a seedy tavern without half the room trying to catch his eye or admire his sleek fur.\n\nThis one is called Razum-dar, and it is a great pleasure to make your acquaintance.

Hard not to in this line of work. And once you get near an oozing vent, you never forget the smell.\n\nI don't know why anyone would want to intentionally bring lava to the surface. That stench lingers on your clothes for days.

He will tell you, but you must keep this a secret between us. Raz is a spy for the Aldmeri Dominion. One of the Eyes of the Queen. \n\nRaz serves her majesty across the length and breadth of Tamriel. And he likes to think he's quite good at it.

No. But I have given Lady Arabelle a tincture that will keep her stable and slow down the poison's most deadly effects. I need to return to my workshop. Analyze the components and consult my ancient herbal apothecary. I'm sure I've seen this before.

Not what I expected, truth be told. She dragged me in here. Now I'm very, very sore.\n\nOh! The note. Someone delivered it. After. Neri cursed and ran out. It's on the table. Maybe read it? I can't. My eyes are blurry.

This one is normally happy to chit and chat, but some things must remain secret for the safety of all. \n\nSuffice to say, the queen's arrival in the archipelago may signal a new chapter in the story of the world. Fingers crossed and tail in knots.

The queen is well, thanks to you! This one heard all the details. The Ascendant Order, the talks, a daring escape from a moldering old fort. \n\nRaz will not soon let her forget what happened when he was not at her side.

Not yet begun, from what this one has heard. Knowing the players, this is a card game that will take many hands to play out. \n\nBetween you and Raz? Great things may come of these talks. But we must all be patient. And try not to get our hopes up.

Hah, you remembered! The queen had one made for her Eye. It was a touching gift. Raz will not lie, he may have shed a tear.\n\nNow he can ride without his sleek tail getting pulled. Truly, it is the little things that matter.

She caught me hiding behind some rocks. We locked eyes. As she approached, I knew I should run. But something about her look. It kept me still.\n\nWhen she grabbed my collar I thought I was dead. Until she kissed me. Hard. Then we came here.

I wouldn't call myself unlucky in such affairs. But, no, not typically. I don't know why. Look at me.\n\nMaybe I'm just too intimidating. Yes. That must be why I attracted Neri. She is so very strong.

I think they're Sea Elf religious figures. Or magic leaders? Honestly, I can only guess. I didn't think I needed to read up on them before I came here.\n\nMaybe Neri can tell me more. When we're together again. If we have time.
Old druid settlement, I think. Makes sense based on the name. Though, this whole island was druids.\n\nNow, the Dreadsails are here. I wonder what their plans are?

Hmm. Sure, I'm a little drunk on strong wine. And an even stronger woman. But not so much to tell a stranger my secrets. You should know—on this kind of job, we keep to ourselves.\n\nPlus, you got me all wet! Not even sure I even I like you.

Could you track down Umindior? I've seen your talent at scouting on the sly. No question you could search Llanshara alone.\n\nBut if I find that slouch alive, I'll get angry that he left me alone. I'll probably start yelling, which we don't want.

He followed a woman through a door right here. Oh, and I'll mark where we made camp. We can meet there once you find him.\n\nWe've done this before, partner. Stay out of sight. Find a hiding spot if someone sees you. You know, the usual.

We have no secrets here, friend. The courier claims a large shipment for Duchess Elea, but I have no record of any impending deliveries. I'm sure it's just some confusion since the loss of our castle steward. The duchess will deal with it eventually.

What madness! A war among the circles is the last thing Galen needs right now.\n\nI've been invited to observe the Draoife. I'd like you to tag along. Find Laurel in the Vine District here in the city. If she agrees, you can join us.

The sea witches threw us in here to punish us. So, as far as I know, the relic is still in the cavern. You can find it up on the cliffs.\n\nBut now that incredible feeling has spread to all the Dreadsails. I don't see why they're angry.

There's not much to say. It arrived without fanfare, with an anonymous note. The vintage was my father's favorite. He was still new to his role as duke when the vineyard turned out those precious bottles.

Ugh. They're a bunch of sticks in the sand. Just some Elves who think they're above the rest of us because of their connection to the sea.\n\nMinahel's the worst of them. So strict. We're the Dreadsails! No masters! Well, unless you want one.

We depleted our own stores of that vintage a long time ago, but everyone at court knows I was fond of that wine. We opened a bottle once a year to celebrate my father and the elevation of House Dufort.\n\nI was quite sad when we uncorked the last one.

Not much. Seems like you had all the luck. A lot of Dreadsail stuff doesn't seem that valuable.\n\nI did accidentally see a lot of Sea Elves, um, together. I thought it strange that so many of them seemed … busy. Now I understand.
