Hold on! Earlier, you mentioned that the shopkeep claimed that my seneschal placed an order for a large amount of wine. While we did no such thing, one of my sentries informed me that a courier had arrived with an unscheduled delivery.

Yes. They're over by the tournament tents, waiting for an audience with the duchess. I still find it strange that we wouldn't have a record of a shipment as large as the one they're trying to deliver.
Not much to tell. I'm new to this whole, um, thing. The, uh, procurement world. Just trying it on for size, I suppose.\n\nOf course, being spotted by that Sea Elf isn't an auspicious start.
Sea Elves typically stay private. Aggressively so. These Dreadsails are different. They just … do whatever they want.\n\nLook at this place. Wouldn't you move in if you could?

Vastyr was built atop an old druid settlement. The tunnels that extend below the foundations of the city are all that remain of it. Some of them have collapsed over time, but many are still passable. There's an entrance just up ahead to the east.
You'd do that? You'd help me out? Yes! I mean, sure if you think you can.\n\nHow was that?
Is it that obvious?\n\nWell, it doesn't matter, I'm the one who's armed here. So … give me your jewels.
My captain marooned me here. Said I couldn't return to the ship until I proved I could earn my keep. So here I am. Uh, earning—trying to earn …..\n\nWill you please just hand me your valuables?

My—my toes? No, you can't have them.\n\nI'm just going to … leave. Yes. You can have this spot and I'll go back to my ship and beg my captain for my place back. There's more to being a pirate than this.
Better? Like more aggressive? I'm not an aggressive person. Hmm.\n\nHalt. Give me your jewels or I'll kick you in them!
How's this?\n\nHand over your coins right this second. I mean it!

Creative? Threatening people into giving up their gold is harder than I thought. All right. \n\nGive me all you own or I'll cut you into tiny pieces with my tiny knife and feed you to the fish as an appetizer.

Yes, but we used to control so much more. My father was the Duke of the Systres. When he supported King Ranser in his war against the high king, Emeric took the ducal title and awarded it to House Dufort.\n\nAn unjust and harsh penalty, in my opinion.

Hmm. An intriguing question. Unfortunately, as far as I know, the Firesong don't have any strongholds on Galen … unless …. Perhaps they've occupied one of the ancient druidic sites?\n\nMaybe Archdruid Ellic of the Eldertide can tell you more.

Thanks to you and Dhulef, I wasn't harmed. My fellow archdruids … weren't so fortunate.\n\nStill, we moved our sacred seed to a new location, known only to a few of the Stonelore. And I'm sending Laurel to keep Frii safe. I pray it's enough.

The island is sacred to all druids, but yes, the Firesong call it home.\n\nThe circle's ancient duty is to calm the spirit of the volcano when it grows restless. Yet the mountain grows angrier. I wonder if the Firesong can contain it—or want to.

All seeds are a promise, mainlander. A potential still to come. This seed was a gift from the last Druid King, entrusted to the Eldertide Circle countless ages ago. As long as we guard it, the Dream of Kasorayn lives.\n\nI will not let Orlaith take it.

Can you tear down a castle with this seed? No. But symbols have the power we give them. With our seed, the Firesong could destroy the Dream of Kasorayn. Show me the spell or sword that can slay an idea, then we can talk.
We will gather our strength within these great stone walls and prepare for the battle to come. My brothers and sisters are scattered, but we will not bow down to the Firesong or their Sea Elf allies.

Were you not paying attention? To stop a pirate! Redblade is gathering crew and ships to build an armada. They would threaten every port from Alinor to Balmora! \n\nTheir plan hinges on a secret—a trove thought lost and forgotten.

That is Raz's best guess. The only way we can be sure is to get in there and find out. Go, enter the Outlaws Refuge and make your way to the gambling parlor. \n\nThis one will meet you inside, once he has donned the perfect disguise.

I don't want to leave Glimmertarn totally defenseless. There will undoubtedly be more druids arriving, delayed by something or other. That, and I'd rather not have Frii in the middle of a battle. They're capable, but far too valuable to be lost.
Druid Laurel wishes it. Battle is too sharp. Loud. The city soil … harsh, full of salt, no place for a nourisher. \n\nI am better here. Protector. In defense of Glimmertarn. Strength here, too.

Glyphics are creations of Hermaeus Mora. Each one contains knowledge or a memory. With the proper coaxing, they can be urged to transform into a tangible version of the concept within. You need the contents of three glyphics to assist Hermaeus Mora.

The tome is one of Hermaeus Mora's Books of Forbidden Secrets. He provided it to lead you to the vault that houses the Emerald Glyphic.\n\nRead the book after you step through one of the portals and it shall guide you to the hidden location.

Glyphics are creations of Hermaeus Mora. Each one contains knowledge or a memory. With the proper coaxing, they can be urged to transform into a tangible version of the concept within. You need the contents of three glyphics to assist Hermaeus Mora.

I can't leave Vastyr. Someone has to pick up the pieces, and that responsibility now falls on me. \n\nFind Druid Laurel. She needs to know that Archdruids Rahval and Ellic are dead. That Orlaith and the Firesong have the sacred seeds.

She told us as the cathedral collapsed. She's going to proclaim herself the new Druid King. But while she has the seeds, she still needs the Sower.\n\nFrii has a part to play in all this, but they'll need your help. Find them, friend. Keep them safe.

Druid Ryvana's elixir has done wonders. I feel stronger already. Still, I was weak from the poison for a long time. I expect my recovery will be slow but persistent.\n\nDon't worry, dear. I'll leave the dangerous work to you and Ryvana for now.

The parlor is below ground, yes? But the patrician suite is above the parlor. The suite should have a view of Vastyr.\n\nWhile Raz keeps the thugs focused down here, find a way inside. Perhaps a ramp or ladder? Get creative.

This one barely had time to hide the Itinerant Staff before she took the scribes from me. She's crafty and convinced the scribes Keshargo failed his obligation to Hermorah. She said the scribes had to interfere against the atrocities of the realms.

I'm suspicious of any Daedra worshiping cult who says they're pacifists. \n\nPacifists, soldiers, they all die the same way. And I know the moment the Scribes of Mora deal with another hostile takeover you'll be there to stop them, ey?

A means of safe return from all the planes of Oblivion and the symbol of leadership for the scribes. Recovering the Itinerant Staff would rip the scribes from Valinna's grasp. If you help Keshargo, you'll be rewarded.

Krin Ren-dro? Krin … oh, moon-sugar biscuits, him? What an oaf. Cariel told Raz all about your adventure at Pa'alat.\n\nYes, just like Krin. Former spies become claws in the side. A saying too real by half these days.
Now, now, now. Sometimes, little kitten, Raz must do things he does not like. Up to and including making his friends think he has died.\n\nIt was just the one time, Raz thinks. Is that right?

We receive many visions from the Great Eye. It's how he makes his will known to the faithful. I am Dralys, a devotee of the Sodality of the Eye. We were told to protect the glyphic until you arrived to claim it.\n\nI also acquired this letter.

A protective shield placed by a powerful priest of the Sodality. It has stymied the vampire mercenaries so far, as only fate's chosen may pass through it and take the glyphic. I suggest you do so with all due haste, friend.
We're still trying to determine that. Everything happened so fast. I just find it hard to believe they were actually Steadfast knights. We've never had any trouble with the society before.
To this place and it's twice cursed proprietor.\n\nHe took my gold and offered me more. Now my claws are his. I'd kill him if I could, but so far the opportunity hasn't presented itself.

I don't want to kill Yves, I want to hurt him. I want him to suffer and know it was me. But I shouldn't be talking about this.\n\nJust know that he'll get what he deserves, I'll make sure of it. And If I have to protect him until then? So be it.

Curiosity is a dangerous quality in this place. Most are content to avert their eyes before opening their mouths. If you want to stay here, you best learn that too. \n\nMy gripes and troubles are my own. I can fix my own problems.

Raz hopes so, five-claw. Most folk believe the treasure was just a story, anyway. And if anyone follows hints from Vastyr to the caves, well. They'll have to dig out a mountainside for even a handful of coins.\n\nIn this one's opinion, a job well done.

Not great, kitten. Not great. Raz wishes he could say he was even surprised. But he is not.\n\nThis war … Raz knows in his heart the Dominion is on the right side of things. But it has gone on so long. And so things like this will continue to happen.

Enemy forces move against the One Who Knows, just as he anticipated. I mourn for the deaths of Hermaeus Mora's faithful, but grief must not slow our progress.\n\nStill, I wish we knew more about this enemy.

Yes, the one you carry and the two in my possession. We can use them at the shrine to formalize your arrangement with Hermaeus Mora.\n\nUnfortunately, I am not one of the faithful. Only his followers know the locations.

As if you didn't know. Yes, yes. You've found me. Druid Braigh. He who introduced Tales of Tribute to the three druid circles. The Ivy Prodigy of Galen.\n\nI suppose you want to challenge me to a game?

Look around you, outsider. Firesong reavers on our doorstep! Raging furnaces beneath our feet.\n\nI'm not exactly in the mood to roll up my sleeves and play a friendly hand or two. Come find me again when things have settled, aye?

It's from the Dream of Kasorayn, the prophecy of the Druid King. "One choice, one will, one binding word, shall bless or scourge all lands."\n\nSince those lines were carved into the Telling Stone, they've become the basis for our two possible futures.

Hard to say. So much is open to interpretation. I think it warns of a usurper who claims the kingship by force and treachery. It may be related to the end of Kasorayn's rule. I found one reference to an Allwither death cult active at that time.

The blessing of the Green Reward or the curse of the Green Scourge. One ushers in an age of harmony with nature. The other predicts a world under siege by an angry and vengeful wilderness.\n\nTwo possibilities, one Druid King.

The druids have argued about that for generations. From what you found at Ivyhame, it's clear Kasorayn believed the Reward would come when the circles reunited and selected a new king, while a usurper would summon the Scourge. A tyrant like Bacaro.

No, the One Who Knows rarely gets that involved in determining the course of fate. This was the work of a traitor, one who claims devotion to Hermaeus Mora but works to advance the threat we have been tasked to stop.

Hermaeus Mora told me that adversaries were gathering against him. I wondered why he never told me who they were. Perhaps he doesn't know. But how is that possible? The One Who Knows … knows everything.\n\nAs for the glyphics, we will keep them safe.

We must reach Bassian before this betrayer gets to him. Learn the location of the Shrine of the Golden Eye. \n\nThe best way to keep the glyphics safe is to get to the shrine and use them as Hermaeus Mora instructed.

The Stonelore Circle at least will never accept his claim. Not unless forced to. Not to mention the three alliances. Bacaro is going to need more than the regalia and his small army of knights to accomplish his ultimate goal—to rule all of Tamriel.

If only I could, chosen. Our master demands the utmost secrecy, and we must be careful around nonbelievers. Many would injure me or worse if they suspected I consorted with Daedra.\n\nWhenever I go to worship, I am blindfolded and led there by others.

Prophecy and faith are powerful things, outsider. And Orlaith told very convincing stories with her words.\n\nBy the time I saw the truth of where she was leading us, there was no way to oppose her. Orlaith was just too powerful.
Naraheida always takes me to the shrine. I'll mark her camp on your map.\n\nMay the Golden Eye lead you to the knowledge you seek, chosen.

It's true that a small number of Firesong cling to Orlaith's lies. But the rest of us … we want to make amends. Work with the other circles and see what comes of Count Stefan's overtures.\n\nWe'd like to be part of the future of the archipelago.

I'm not at liberty to divulge the secrets of my order, but I can tell you that Leramil plans to use the glyphics to betray the Great Eye. And Naraheida whispered, "Leramil is the doom of Apocrypha" with her dying breath.\n\nWhat more proof do you need?

I can help you with that. The faithful in this region tell a riddle. "Where claw meets prey, beneath open air in stone shows the way." I believe it refers to the location I marked on your map.\n\nJust remember, stay alert around Leramil.

I'm not hiding it, Hircine's Curse courses through my veins.\n\nYves thought to control me through my condition—as he does with everything else—but I refuse to give him that power. I announced what I am the moment I realized what he was doing.

How can I not? It plagues my dreams with all that I've done under the burden of my debt. My past and all the mistakes therein follow me even into the safe embrace of slumber. \n\nThere is no escape for me.

Right now, I cannot afford to lose it, but as soon as Yves no longer controls my fate I'll rid myself of my condition. I have tasted the blood-lust of the hunt, it lacks the flavor of my current quarry.
All the job broker said was that the Sea Elves recently found it. He told us the relic was in Llanshara, but that's it. Not even a description. Maybe we'll learn more as we search the settlement.

Zeira had little information about it. Apparently, the Sea Elves only recently found it. The buyer told her it was in Llanshara and how to get here.\n\nThey didn't even describe the thing. But Umindior knows something. That's why we need to find him.

Oh, poor Frii. Their sacrifice saved us all. I'll remember them fondly for that.\n\nAnd you're sure Lord Bacaro is defeated? Without their leader, his Ascendant Order should fade away. But what happened to the Druid King's regalia, dear?

I found a broker who handles this kind of work. He gave me the details after some convincing. They don't trust new people right away.\n\nDidn't help that I embarrassed myself at first. I tried sounding shady. But that's not really how they talk.
The broker liked my drive, but not my lack of experience. So, he teamed me up with Umindior.\n\nI hope I don't let him down by losing my partner. That's bad for a reputation.

He wouldn't stop complimenting me. My looks, my personality—I'd barely said a word to him.\n\nUsually I appreciate such kind words, but it's strange when a Sea Elf does it. He was just a little too friendly.
Sea Elves aren't known for their warmth. He'd just caught me spying on his settlement. I thought I had a fight on my hands.\n\nInstead he flattered me, then ran off. I hope this doesn't ruin the job.

Perfect. I love when others do the work. We can lift whatever Minahel has made, then use it to safely carry the relic.\n\nWe have a camp outside Llanshara to the northwest. Let's head there. If Quen's back, she might have thoughts on how to proceed.

I can always take care of myself, but … I don't think he'll be angry. Maybe confused, but I'll reassure him. \n\nOh! I've got it. I'll say one of my friends must have played a trick on me and put something in my wine.
I think I do. I think Veshin will, um … know what he's doing as well. I hope.\n\nHe really is good looking. All that salty sea air and working the ropes and sails of a big ship, I guess.
How interesting. So few of us make it out to the Systres.\n\nIn fact, I've had the offerings of Galen to myself for so long, I've quite forgotten how to share.

At my age, my palate is refined to the wholesome offerings of Galen. And when I desire dining with a bit with more richness, I charter a ship to High Isle for a fortnight.\n\nBut then, I suppose it'd be poor manners to simply suggest that you starve.

Oh, come now. I don't wish to quarrel. It's just that my methods are highly efficient. I've managed to blend in quite well here, for many years, all on my own. \n\nCouldn't you sail over to Amenos and sate yourself on the wretches there?

I shall share with you, then. I'd rather no bad blood come between us. We'll hunt as two shadows, passing in the night.\n\nEnjoy yourself, but do be courteous. It'd be equally poor manners for you to gorge yourself on the local fare.

Perhaps I'm a lonely widow. Or a noble in an estranged marriage, with surprisingly deep pockets.\n\nI can be whatever interests you, my dear. I'm only looking for company. A companion with whom I might share a meal.

What can I say? They both taught me so much. My father was a hard man, but fair. He wanted the best for me. And he demanded the best in return. Archdruid Rahval was a mentor and a good friend. \n\nTogether, they showed me what it means to be a Breton.
Nothing, my dear. Nothing. \n\nRun along, now. Forget that we even spoke. I may think of you often hereafter, but you'd do well to forget me.
That was my intention, but the more I look at you, I think you might come on a little … strong for my taste. An indulgence, to be sure, but a dangerous one. One I might not survive.

I believe I have. Why limit ourselves to one aspect of the Breton legacy? There's room for it all in our hearts. That's why I'll include the druids in Galen's government somehow.\n\nWho knows? I may even become something new. A druid-knight, perhaps?

I know a great many things, mortal. What may be, what will be, what will never come to pass. It is … my nature.\n\nI saw that you would reveal the reason for Dralys's betrayal, but I only caught a glimpse of our true enemy.

First, we must enter into an agreement. A contract that binds us for the duration of this threat. It also guarantees that I will do nothing to harm you, your interests, or the mortal realm.\n\nYou are the chosen of fate. Now bring forth the glyphics.

Nothing too out of the ordinary. Just a meeting of the society and local leaders, looking for more ways the society can be of use to all the people of Tamriel.\n\nSpeaking of use, I should get back to it. Talk to Sir Stefan if you want to lend a hand.

With the druids and with a knightly order. I suppose you could say I had a well-rounded Systres education!\n\nIf you're interested, I'll tell you more about it later. Right now, I need you to check out those locations.

While we examined the letter that Dralys gave you, Bassian remembered another follower who may know the location of the shrine. Naraheida. Let me mark her camp on your map.\n\nWe must reach the shrine and use the glyphics as Hermaeus Mora instructed.
Mildanor always takes me to the shrine. Ah, I see his home is already marked on your map.\n\nMay the Golden Eye lead you to the knowledge you seek, chosen.

Druid Ryvana wants you to come to her workshop right away. Do you know where it is? Just west of Gonfalon Bay and north of Druid's Gate.\n\nWhen you see her, remind her that Lady Arabelle still needs the antidote.

That makes Za'ji feel much better. It was good to get out of the manor and do something! All this waiting makes Za'ji's ears itch.\n\nThis one will head back to the manor and make sure Lady Arabelle is taking her tincture.

A bit of alteration magic. I've been studying with the druids of Glimmertarn, and their work with plants inspired me to see if I could increase or decrease the size of people, too. So far, it's working!
Exactly! You catch on fast. So, interested? I can, for a few seconds, change you into a smaller or larger version of yourself.
Excellent! Oh, you won't regret this. And enjoy the slightly elevated view while you can!
Interesting choice! I'm sure you'll gain a new perspective while transformed. And thank you for helping me out this way.
Hmmm … this should be fun for you. Oh, I can't wait to tell the folks at the Mages Guild how these spells turned out. Thank you for letting me do this!

That they weren't coming back. Frii gave me a pouch of soil. They said it was special. That they prepared it as part of their purpose. You remember how Frii would go on and on about that.\n\nAnyway, they asked me to do something after they were gone.

They asked me to go to the overlook north of Glimmertarn. To sprinkle the soil from the pouch there.\n\nI made a promise and I'd like you to fulfill it with me. I think Frii would want you to be a part of this. Will you help me, friend?
The Llanshara job got a bit … weird. I worried you might not partner with me again. Oh, I mean, on the job. Work together.\n\nNow I realize I should've asked you from the start.
Well, I paid for a ship in advance. I didn't realize how far I'd have to look to find a suitable partner. For the job, I mean.\n\nBut we can talk about this at the docks!
Well, I paid for a ship in advance. I didn't realize how far I'd have to look to find a suitable partner. For the job, I mean.\n\nBut we can talk about this at the docks!
Well, I paid for a ship in advance. I didn't realize how far I'd have to look to find a suitable partner. For the job, I mean.\n\nBut we can talk about this at the docks!
No way to understand a job until you're truly in it. We both know that. \n\nAt least this time Umindior isn't here to muck things up.
A few, here and there. Nothing this size. My job broker still sees me as green.\n\nThis time I did proper research, hired transportation, and found the perfect partner. All on my own. I'm ready.

I'm the court magician, remember? I still don't know what that exactly entails, but I know how to fight a war. I've prepared a number of surprises for the enemy, so I need to be close by to make sure they trigger when they'll do the most damage.
When we first met, I brought you into the job. I enjoyed working alongside you. Now, <<1>> wants me to follow your lead.\n\nI'm trying to say, it feels weird to hear this. I hope you understand.
We've gone through a lot, you and I. Maybe we can discuss this some other time. After all this.\n\nFor now, we should focus on clearing our names. Sound good?

We shouldn't take any chances. Orlaith has accomplished things we never expected. If she made her way to the Ivy Throne—or whatever waits behind that door—we need to find out.\n\nAnd Frii might sense something, like they did at Clohaigh.

I suppose it's the least I can do to return the favor. I'll seek him out, then!\n\nI still have plenty of ingredients left to refine my Galen-style steak. Do you think he'll appreciate being served such an explosive combination?
Well said! Everyone deserves a little entertainment with their sustenance, I always say!\n\nMay our paths cross so I can cook for you again someday, my friend!

A little. His voice calling me from the Green. The song of his magic, strong and good. He gave me into the care of the wyrds before my eyes ever opened to the light of this world. They tended me while I dreamed.\n\nUntil the Firesong woke me.

Dralys? Yes, I believe our paths have crossed before. \n\nHmm. This document is written in an obscure code. I shall endeavor to decipher it while you find the Shrine of the Golden Eye. That is where we must bring the glyphic and its counterparts.

Research is one of my passions, proxy. I was a scholar long before I entered into my arrangement with the One Who Knows, and I have learned more about uncovering truths and revealing secrets in the years since.

I am a seeker of knowledge, a chaser of wisdom, and a delver of secrets. Long ago, I made a bargain with the Prince of Fate. In exchange for glimpses into Apocrypha's forbidden tomes, I undertake missions such as this from time to time.

These are the situations that make us flinch at every shadow, proxy. If Dralys also suspects a traitor, that means we follow the same trail. His only mistake is assuming it was me.\n\nI seek to assist you and save two worlds, nothing more.

You did what it asked of you. What you had to do. But don't despair. I felt its anger slip away. Its intentions were pure, outsider. Things just got out of hand.\n\nIt was the actions of the Firesong that tainted the spirit. Corrupted it.

It used its motes to try to stop the Firesong. Created the wraiths to protect our home. But it knew it went too far. Like a bee whose sting causes its own death, it reacted in desperation. \n\nI hope it finds peace now. Back in the Green.

Thanks. You don't realize how much you rely on something until it's gone.\n\nWe need to get into the tomb, but it isn't going to be easy. Orlaith's got an army in there. Frii said something about waking the guardian, but they didn't explain further.

Healers, supplies—everything the Society of the Steadfast is known for. I need to coordinate efforts and stock the ships, but our pavilions will spring up before you know it.\n\nAnd when I return, I look forward to working closely with Count Stefan.

Just that I learned the ways of the druids, as well as the ways of a knight and Breton noble. Too long have the druids and House Mornard sought the glory of the past. This is an opportunity to find a new path that combines the best of our legacies.

We are blessed with a dual nature. Part Elf, part human. Our legacy on one hand encompasses nobility and knighthood, while on the other it embraces magic and the natural world.\n\nI think I've been trying to reconcile this duality my entire life.
Other than the thick concentration, I'm not sure. Druid Senna mentioned that the Firesong caught in the fog lowered their weapons and then marched off as if in a trance.\n\nThis is very strange.

Trust has to start somewhere. But we still need to gather the elders and form a new Draoife. After that, I'll broach the subject.\n\nIn the meantime, I'll commune with the tree. With the growing seeds. And I'll be here when they finally blossom.

Oh, Frii will commune with me if they're able, but every spirit binding is different. Some can communicate freely. Others can only share impressions. And then there are the ones that more or less slumber, as Frii did before they were awakened.

I won't keep that a secret from High King Emeric and the others. But I will urge them to see the talks through, despite their less-than-honorable beginnings.\n\nThis is a real chance for a lasting peace, and I damn well plan to make that happen.

As well as can be expected. Pitof and I are figuring out what it means to be chroniclers. I mean, without the help of a nature spirit.\n\nAnd we talked with Druid Laurel. I think we're going to allow druids from the other circles to come help us.

We left the path in the care of the animals who roam it. I have no doubt that they'll be able to deter outsiders from wandering too far into our sacred site. Other druids will join us there soon and we will rebuild our halls of memory.

What choice do we have? Our stories and history are important, perhaps now more than ever. If my understanding of recent events is true, then you know the dangers of burying or misinterpreting the past.\n\nHistory should be learned from, not repeated.

Not so far, but I have hope. Druid Fenas is consulting with the best minds in the three druid circles. Someone is bound to come up with a solution eventually.\n\nAnd in the meantime, Joslin's leaves are growing in nicely.

Not yet, but I think we're getting closer. Druid Fenas isn't giving up and neither am I. He's been talking to druids from all the circles. Sooner or later, someone will think of something.\n\nIn the meantime, I'm saving a lot of gold on candles.

This one is called Shadeya. She and her mercenaries are here only to protect the caravan for coin. This one dislikes this place and will remain no longer than she must.\n\nYou have questions? Talk to the elder. This one knows nothing.

Ah … no. We Baandari are used to scrutiny, but rarely from such a distance. The Dark Elves in these lands seem colder than most.\n\nThis is no matter. This one extends his warmest welcomes to you, instead.

The shrine … Oh! That shrine. It is a place holy to Dark Elves, yes? Of little interest to us Khajiit.\n\nThis one is late in his years, and does not remember, but he may have accidentally wandered through. Yes! That was probably so.

I fear the Lark might leave a note for me at the shrine, if he hasn't already. Aggravating little habit of his. \n\nKeep it hidden from the high priest, if you can. He already thinks little of me for how I've handled the Khajiit camp.

I've got a plan of my own already in motion. Crucial pieces of it need tending to.\n\nBut I can tell you more about that when we meet up later. Unless you have more questions, I suggest you be on your way.

Shh, not so loud! This is a very delicate situation. We need to ensure that what few pilgrims we have aren't scared off by any of this. \n\nRilasi hasn't exactly kept us apprised of her plans. What did she send you to do?

Of course she did. That's it, I'm sending a priest to shadow her.\n\nAfter Rilasi came through to examine the talisman, I've had to stand watch. I've made sure not to let anyone get too close, especially not any outsiders. It's been exhausting!
Surprised are you? Do you expect to find me in random places? I'm flattered, truly.\n\nOr, were you looking for me? It would be your turn to play the messenger.

I was setting up protective runes in the crypts when some s'wit priest came bumbling in after me and set them off!\n\nWe were forced to flee when the spirits of the interred attacked us. And then the Lark of Rosgard managed to slither into the crypts!

It's routine really. Whenever the Consortium believes a mine is operating below standards, they send along an auditor to run an inspection. This usually entails the overseer providing a comprehensive tour of the kwama pens and the mine's queen.
Oh yes, a healthy Kwama queen is as good as gold around here. Their eggs are a staple food for Dark Elves. The Consortium outfits these mines with the best tools and workers money can buy.

Ah, both here of our own volition. Good. I'd hate to have someone else's whims meddling in this affair. \n\nI suppose since we are catching up, have you had more dealings with Naryu or are you here for yet another of your heroic deeds?
All you need to know is that I'm an agent of the Morag Tong.
You see the blades, do you not? I grant the fool unfortunate enough to become my target the long sleep.\n\nAnd before you ask, the Morag Tong aren't affiliated with the Camonna Tong.

Even in our dwindled state, we hoped our name still held power. Alas.\n\nThe Remnants are the sword and shield of Hermaeus Mora. We stand between his infinite knowledge and those who seek to plunder it. That is, we did once.

The Apogee is a vault for items of arcane interest. At its center lies the shrine of The Tormenting Eye, one of Hermaeus Mora's famed Black Books. It is currently off serving his divine purpose.\n\nOnce, many considered this place to be impenetrable.

The Mind Who Grasps, Lord Hermaeus Mora himself, bestowed these gifts to the Remnants. A pact made centuries ago gave us strength in exchange for service.\n\nOdd that you'd possess such powers. But even we won't claim to understand our lord's plans.

Currently dealing with. I'm activating the Dwarven constructs. They're highly effective at frightening off any hostiles who come here. Really, this is standard procedure. I'm not even sure what that dithering fool was worried about.

No reason to wet my blade with the blood of the unworthy. And I don't kill for money or superstitions like the Dark Brotherhood. Writs are issued to us by the Grandmaster and sanctioned by the Great Houses.
Have you faced animunculi?\n\nWhatever the Painted Eye are after, I doubt it's valuable enough to drive them to such bravery. Not when murderous Dwarven machines spring from every wall.

Dreaming … burnt fields. Rust. Apostle Nilphas Drethan Override. Doors: Unlocked. Painted Eye Hostiles. Outer Laboratory: Compromised.\n\nError. Dreaming: Incomplete. Diagnostic Test: Failed. Protus Model: Critical Components Missing.
Scanning for Components. Percipience Cortex: West Wing. Cognition Cluster: West Wing. \n\nSelf-repair Protocols: Accessible. Components Required.

The high priest refused my order to take the relic off display. He thinks it's safe as long as he's watching it.\n\nBut the Lark could steal stripes off a cat. If I couldn't stop his heist, I thought I could at least trick him into taking a replica.

A story. Great. What reason would this elder have to visit the …? Wait. Did you read this? His legend says the relic holds this Eye of Baan Dar. \n\nFetch it all. I need you to get back to the camp quickly, before the high priest intervenes.

Shadeya? Why did he tell her? That old cat is too quick to assume the good in everyone.\n\nAnd perhaps I'm about to make the same mistake. But I'll ask it plainly: can I count on your help in rescuing my client and his family, or not?

Stealing is so inelegant a word for what I do. I prefer to think of it as reacquisition. And the simple answer is that some things are much better earned than bought. \n\nTrust, for example. If I give you the talisman, will I have earned yours?

Percipience Cortex: Functional. Cognitive Cluster: Restored. Corporeal System Repair: Complete.\n\nHello. I am Protus, Kemel-Ze Security Oversight Construct. I ensure that the inner laboratory is not disturbed until the Creator—Lord Seht—returns.

Another of Lord Seht's early projects. Later, he stored his memories in the stars, but in Kemel-Ze he was more grounded. They can connect information to the inner workings of the laboratory. \n\nImportantly, they are compatible with my form.

My form is fully functional, but my memory and connection to the systems here remain fractured. \n\nNilphas Drethan removed the Mnemonic Fragments which facilitated that connection. We will need to install new ones.

All that and more, mortal. I see all that is, was, and will ever be. And in so doing I saw hidden rivals that threaten Apocrypha and all of reality. They must not succeed.\n\nThe time has come to honor your agreement.
Affirmative. These are the locations of the major Mnemonic Fragments. \n\nFind them and my systems will be fully restored.

I am the Golden Eye of Fate and the Keeper of Whispers! I foretold that a mortal was needed to preserve reality. You are that mortal, and we signed a contract that binds us for the duration of this threat.\n\nApocrypha is in danger. Now you must act.

Let Leramil guide you. She can perceive the threads of fate and lead you to the three tasks that will reveal my hidden adversaries. Meet her in the Necrom Bindery, in the mortal city of the same name.\n\nYour journey to preserve reality begins there.

And so I shall. The One Who Knows traced three crucial events to this area. Investigate each and he believes we can expose the conspirators moving against Apocrypha.\n\nWe may even stop them before the ultimate threat takes shape.

I do not know. I was only presented with what was required to bring you to the right place at the right moment.\n\nYou must determine why fate needs you in each location. Then take the appropriate action.

One or more of Hermaeus Mora's rival Princes, although they have yet to reveal themselves. They work through agents … such as whoever sought the glyphics when we first met. \n\nA spider lurks at the center of this web. I am sure of it.

Have you never heard of the Daedric Prince of Forbidden Knowledge? The Lord of Fate? The Riddle Unsolvable? Hmm. Hermaeus Mora knows everything. He is the wisest of the Daedra. Every secret and all knowledge finds its way to Apocrypha in time.

I am Leramil. Sometimes called the Wise, although that is not a sobriquet I care for. I seek to comprehend the emergent truths elicited by—ah, never mind that. I am a scholar. A century ago, I struck a bargain with Hermaeus Mora.

Do you know so little, mortal? Apocrypha is my domain. A plane of Oblivion I have shaped to my needs. And this plane—the mortal realm—some refer to it as Nirn.\n\nAs for the connection, just know that if Apocrypha falls, Nirn will cease to exist.
Precious little. They are shadows that vanish under my scrutiny. Obscure figures that somehow hide from my gaze.\n\nIt is … disconcerting. Never have I been so blind.

That is why I agreed to bind myself to you with a powerful contract. I cannot act against you or your interests, so long as you adhere to your part of the bargain.\n\nOur enemies have no such constraints, so proceed with caution.

A reasonable and prudent request. I shall provide what details I can, but I know little more than you do. Local history and politics are not my usual area of study.\n\nWhich location would you like to know more about?

Necrom serves as a center for the ancient Dunmer practice of ancestor worship. A strange custom.\n\nThe monks of the Necropolis, called the Keepers of the Dead, tend the catacombs beneath the city. They guide the faithful in venerating their forebears.

Tel Rendys is one of the many mushroom towers that dot this land. They usually serve as domiciles of Telvanni wizards who wield formidable magic, but this tower is abandoned.\n\nInteresting. Fate dictates that when you go there, I shall accompany you.

Alavelis is a minor settlement whose only claim to fame is its malachite quarry. A glass mine, as the Dunmer refer to it. That thread of fate vibrates with particular intensity.\n\nWhat you shall find there, I cannot say, but I urge caution, proxy.

An old bookbinder's shop. Our temporary base of operations in this region. I secured it so we could travel to and from Apocrypha without causing undue panic. I doubt Necrom's authorities would approve of portals to an Oblivion realm in their city.

She wouldn't. The only person Rilasi wants to suffer for this crime is me. And she still needs to catch me.\n\nBesides, if the high priest knew about her little stunt with the replica talisman, she'd be finished. We've got that we can hold over her.

No, no. See, the important thing here is that Rilasi didn't catch me.\n\nIn fact, you looking like you caught me works in my favor. Trust me, she needs the encouragement. It'll keep her from giving up.

Rilasi has made things hard for herself, remaining a decent person in her line of work. Even her making that replica was done with the best of intentions.\n\nChasing someone for so long with little to no headway can't be easy. She deserves a win.
Plague? That's not a word to toss around lightly. What proof do you have?

No, I wouldn't want that. All right. If you're careful and don't touch anything, you can go aboard and take a look around.\n\nBut if you find anything to verify your claim, I want you to bring it to me immediately.

Sorry, I can't let you wander around unattended on a ship under my watch. And since my assistant Randas never showed up for work today, I have no one available to escort you.\n\nWithout Port Agent Randas or more substantial proof, I can't help you.

It's changed, somehow. The gem inside seems to have a different sort of luster.\n\nI rather wonder if your forceful expression of will in seeing its safe return has somehow tapped into its hidden power! It's an exciting development, to say the least.
I'll send a report to my superiors. I'll remain in Sailenmora for a few days, just to make sure it's safe.\n\nAnd then I'll likely be back on the trail of the Lark of Rosgard.

Ah. So the fate of the Eye of Baan Dar falls to you!\n\nWhichever way you choose, walker, this one asks only that you do not use what you learned today about the Eye to challenge the faith of those who serve at the shrine.
Well enough to go fishing, but too sick to work? A likely story! \n\nI should drop everything and go catch him in his lie. Then I'd have a reason to dismiss him and hire a competent assistant.

Shor's bones! I ask for aid and they send an auditor? At this rate there won't be a mine left to audit! I'm Overseer Ulfengar. The egg tenders behind me are Malsa and Barluk. \n\nWe barely managed to escape the kwama, let alone those damned cultists.

Yes! I sent word days ago asking for more guards. We first saw them sneaking around the mine, but now they've broken in somewhere near the hatchery. They've whipped the kwama into a frenzy and I'm worried they're trying to poison the clutch.
You know which organization I belong to and what I do for them. Surely the answer to your question is obvious.\n\nI don't know the specifics yet, but I'll find more details once I'm there.
Keshargo's former protégé. Her mind is sharp, orderly, and her magical capacity well exceeds this one's. Still, she grew discontented with the scribe's creed of passive observance.

Not long ago. It took some time for Keshargo to journey to this place and he moved cautiously so as not to be followed. Valinna is unaware that the hall has a secondary entrance. Once we step through, we improve our chances of remaining undetected.

She brought in other mages and warriors. She even convinced many formerly loyal scribes that by only observing, we were complicit in the crimes we saw happen.\n\nShe staged a coup and took the mantle of Magnastylus from this one.

An organization of librarians and scribes this one dedicated his whole life to.\n\nFor centuries now, we've documented all observable things. Down in the Scrivener's Hall, the fruits of our efforts are collected for Hermorah's perusal.

Anything it is possible to record. There are unstable rifts below the rock here. The scribes carved out this library and live amongst these pages.\n\nWe use minor magicks to stay hidden, to observe. Now, Valinna shatters that creed.
Now why in Oblivion are you worried about them? They're soldiers. They know how to fend for themselves and how to find their commanders. I'm sure they'll be fine.

We did our part and freed them from the Camonna Tong's grasp. The root of the problem has been solved. If they talk about either of us, then this nuisance may become a much larger mess. And as of right now, it's a mess that I do not have to clean.
All of Apocrypha once knew of us. We guarded Hermaeus Mora's most treasured secrets. Even explored the mortal realm.\n\nWe were a force unmatched.
We head to the courtyard. If the Dreamcarvers wish to breach the Crux, they must go there to do it.\n\nThe passage to the east will take us to a balcony. We can assess their progress from there.

The walls of the Crux cannot break. We connected the locks to the Remnants' mental web. Only we may enter unscathed.\n\nUxunath's ritual siphons Remnant minds. She blends their psychic energy with her own essence.
One of my favorite topics. As the owner of Plokun's Inquisitive Menagerie, I bow to no Prince or master. I call no plane my home. My vocation takes me wherever the desire to see my creatures exists.
Perhaps. No one has entered for countless eons. The Remnants have keys to the Crux, but we have never needed them. Until now.
We need the Journal of the First Remnant. It will tell us which relics we need to place around the circle to open the door.\n\nThere is little time. We must go, now.

Our situation grows dire. Very few of us still stand, and we can no longer hear those who do. The Dreamcarvers must not reach the Crux, but we cannot stop them in our weakened state.\n\nYou, however, are an unexpected development.

The shrine protected our wares. The unified strength of the Remnants kept it alive. Perhaps, as we waned, so did the protective wards.\n\nWe may need to concentrate our efforts in one location. Much easier to watch for thieves that way.

We assume you refer to the Hushed. Unfortunate creatures who arrive from your realm.\n\nThe mortal mind was not meant to hold the blessings of Lord Hermaeus Mora. They transform into the beings you saw. A cautionary tale.

An imposter? Let me see what you found.\n\nI knew there was something wrong the moment I saw the prelate, or I suppose I should call him Blightcrown. What kind of name is that? And what does a devotee of Peryite want in the Necropolis?

All sorts of relics and heirlooms are stored in the catacombs with the ancestors. And with Peryite cultists loose inside, Abbot Ilvel and the keepers are in terrible danger!\n\nWe need to get into the Necropolis, but how? The main door is locked!

It failed the moment those Consortium horkers chose to ignore my letters!\n\nDoes Cindieth really think a queen's gland and some elbow grease will be enough to put that place to rights? You saw what those cultists were doing. It's blighted! Finished!

Hmph. Well, I guess we'll find out.\n\nLet me see this gland. And tell Cindieth we'll stay on if the Consortium provides all the staff and resources I need. The moment they hedge, I'm leaving and taking Malsa and Barluk with me. Necrom be damned.

The Anchre colony was special. Just makes me wonder, what really killed it? Those cultists' spells or the Consortium's indifference. Bah. Doesn't matter.\n\nMalsa and Barluk are tough as horkers. We'll find work elsewhere. Thanks for the nudge, friend.

So, it's my burden, then? Shor's bones, those bastards are just greedy enough to risk it, aren't they?\n\nWith a fresh queen's gland …. Bah! No, we'd need an army of egg-hands, alchemists, a staffed garrison. The Consortium would never agree to it.

Further, where does our power come from? We cannot say.\n\nNow, we must decide. Do we tell the Remnants of our discovery? It would surely destroy us. Or, do we use the victory to reinvigorate the clan? Show that Apocrypha still needs our defense.

Once we learned of the emptiness at our core, it became clear that the Remnants have ended. We can let it fade from memory. Our … my future lies somewhere else.\n\nI feel unburdened. Fighting against the tide took great effort. Now I can be free.

An excellent point. Our goals do not need to come from some external source. We can reinvest in our purpose on our own.\n\nPerhaps others will join out of a desire to gather knowledge, instead of to serve another.

I suppose much depends on the results of the peace talks. We've always been Breton on one hand and neutral on the other. I'd like that to continue. We just need to show that the islands are safe once more. And thanks to you, that's true.\n\nMostly.

Well, aren't you demanding. \n\nShe's an enterprising member of the Camonna Tong—a group of Dark Elf lowlifes. They believe in a lot of nonsense: the competitiveness of their smuggling prices, Dark Elf superiority … the security of Camonnaruhn.
It was her idea to capture the soldiers and threaten the entire Ebonheart Pact. Of course she's the one I've been contracted to kill.

Think about it. How would you react if one of your allies held your soldiers hostage?\n\nThat's why I incorporated releasing the prisoners into my plan. Is it a little more work? Yes. But in this instance, it's worth the effort.

He's the Prince of Forbidden Knowledge, Master of the Tides of Fate, the One Who Knows. His reach is long and his eyes plentiful. Everything the scribes record is done in his name. His library is vast and we are but one order who seeks to add to it.

It'll take some time before the mine can be reopened. We'll need to clear it out. Find a new queen. Hire on replacements. \n\nIf they keep me on as overseer, I can see it reopening within a few months. But it's up to the Consortium now.

Zilipif? They're a friend, of sorts. Zilipif is bound to observe and gain knowledge through experience. Keshargo's purpose is to record the ever-changing landscapes of the realms. We help each other, but the arrangement is … unique.

This one created many detailed and accurate maps using Zilipif's ability to fly. And Keshargo's place among the Scribes of Mora gave Zilipif access to every open rift. The two of us traveled across the planes making maps and hunting for knowledge.

There are rifts to many of the planes of Oblivion here. Most are shut and it's unknown when they will reopen. There are no records from the scribes that came before on when the rifts first appeared, just that the hall was constructed around them.

You think I trust anyone from the Consortium to do it? No.\n\nWe'll need to find better positions for Malsa and Barluk, too. They're young, but they know their stuff. And they deserve the promotion after all that's happened to them.
Until recently, the Scribes of Mora refused to interfere with any of the realms. No. Instead, we documented what was available to us and left dominion over the planes to the Princes—as it should be.

Then anyone inside is unfortunately trapped in that plane. At least until they find another path back. This is why the Itinerant Staff is so important. It can transport the wielder back to Scrivener's Hall.

Veteran scribes hold no fear. We know the timings and cycles of the rifts. Still, fear cannot overcome the hunt for knowledge. Plenty of non-scribes journey between the planes without assurances of returning to Nirn.

It's tough to say. Wringing anything out of the Consortium is like squeezing water from a stone. But she seems confident enough.\n\nTimid ones like her are always more dangerous behind a desk, anyway. Some warriors prefer pens to swords.

Who knows. Used to admire that the Three Banners never touched Telvanni shores. But there's work in war. Razed towns and broken forts need repairs, after all.\n\nWe'll make do, somehow. I'm sure of it.

I used to think egg mining was safe! At least with a war, I know what I'm getting into.\n\nI just wish this Consortium could hear that from us. Learn something from it. But that's a lot to ask from the Telvanni, I know.

I'll do everything in my power to try. The Consortium is obligated to serve the needs of the citizens of the peninsula, and that includes its miners.\n\nI may not be much use in a mine, but bureaucracy I can handle.

Funny how anxious I used to be about such things. Ulfengar put his life on the line for his workers! The least I can do is pressure the Consortium.\n\nThis is my battlefield, after all. It might surprise you what a few strongly-worded letters can do.

Fomesa went looking for survivors down the southern ramp, and egg tender Gine left to scout the southeastern passageways for a way out.\n\nI ended up here with Malsa and Barluk. If there are others alive out there, you'd know better than me.
Ysmir's beard, the both of them? Those cultists need to pay for what they've done!\n\nI imagine if you hadn't shown up when you did, the three of us would have surely joined them.

Oh, Fomesa …. She was hard as steel and twice as sharp. If she didn't make it, that doesn't bode well for the rest of us.\n\nCan you find Gine? He made his way towards the mess cavern not too far from here.

Gine, dead? That man loved these kwama like they were his own kin. I can't imagine how he felt having to face them like this.\n\nLast I saw Fomesa she was heading south on the ramps looking for survivors. Perhaps she made it out?

Maybe that's a good sign? I was beginning to doubt any of us had a chance of escaping.\n\nMight be worth checking the southern ramp for Fomesa, and the mess cavern for Gine. They might still be around.

The Kwama Consortium of Necrom oversees the care and husbandry of egg mines on the peninsula. Their export of eggs is second to none, but even one mine operating below expectations can lead to grumbles among shareholders.
You mean you don't know? Why come out here then? Very well, it's a smuggler's den of the usual unsavory dreck. Are you familiar with the Camonna Tong?

They're criminals who hold on to … archaic ideals. It's no coincidence they devised a plan to capture Argonians. Dark Elves have a sordid history with certain races and the Camonna Tong find pride where others see vile history.
Quick to the draw, aren't you? They have foolishly short memories if they think the old ways were best.

All I've been able to gather is that the prisoners are separated and probably in different buildings around Camonnaruhn. They may even be guarded. Try to make as much noise as possible. You are creating a diversion after all.

I was right, she is here. I suspected as much. Her presence causes quite the stir, I've grown accustomed to sensing when we're sent to the same area. \n\nDo you know of her writ? Does it sound more impressive than mine?
I have evidence to suggest that Naryu's in the area. I received a strongly worded note by way of some smitten fool warning me to stay out of one particular city at a certain time.
Of course, but I'm not about to tell you. If you find her, it'll be without my betraying the Morag Tong. Her work is protected by secrecy. I'm refraining from shadowing her and studying her methods.
I've studied her movements and manners enough to be familiar with her handwriting. And we collaborated on a few writs, you remember.

With the Telvanni Council? Well that certainly sounds … interesting. If I had the time, I might have gone to see what her methods would be there. But, it's better that I left her alone. Dealing with the Great Houses puts her in a sour mood.

The Lark of Rosgard is a slippery, pompous, no-good brigand. He plots his exploits and picks his marks to sow misery, reap notoriety, and make my life difficult.\n\nI know … very little about the relic. You might ask about it up at the shrine.

We met our contact after leaving Llanshara. I thought Umindior would take credit, but he didn't care. All he could think about was that Neri woman.\n\nThe pay was good, but the experience was more important. I really think this is the life for me.

Money and adventure aren't the only reason I got into this life. I have something important I need to do. Someone I need to find.\n\nI don't really want to get into it now. But if you ever land in Abah's Landing, maybe we can work together again.

Zeira keeps me busy. Grab a relic here, some accounting ledgers there. Honestly, it's great. I get to see all of Tamriel, then return to my new home in Abah's Landing.\n\nIf you ever hear of some fancy jewels going missing, think of me.

Feud? Any animosity between our houses died with my brother and Count Stefan's father. I'm sure we'll work hand-in-hand for the betterment of the archipelago.\n\nPerhaps we can even find some way to forge a more lasting alliance.
Hermaeus Mora? The Keepers of the Dead have nothing to do with the Lord of Secrets! And I never heard of anything called the Fulcrum Obscura—wait!\n\nHow do you know all this? Are you a cultist, too?

Hmm. Prior Durdryn founded the Necropolis and our order. Abbot Ilvel idolized him. Told me the prior was obsessed with Necrom's history and had received a special charge from Lord Vivec.\n\nThere's a key to the catacombs in the desk. Hurry, friend.

Where better to hide Oblivion portals than inside a ruined bookshop? This is just one of many studies I utilize across Tamriel. I even have a site in Apocrypha from which I can conduct my research. In Cipher's Midden, to be exact.

Daedric cultists that regard themselves as part-time rivals and full-time enemies would only band together under direct orders from their Princes. Obviously, their cooperation relates directly to the threat the One Who Knows has foreseen.

The Ciphers of the Eye established the site as a headquarters of sorts. These mortals have come to Apocrypha at the invitation of Hermaeus Mora. They maintain and study the many libraries of the realm.\n\nIt is both a refuge and a place of learning.

Oh, me? I'm just your run of the mill planar adventurer. A Gleaner of Aurbis operating out of Fargrave. Proud to say I've traveled all over creation.\n\nFrom Mundus to the realms of Oblivion and all the squiggly bits in-between.

Ah! A kindred spirit! Though I suppose I shouldn't be too surprised. It's not every day you run into someone strolling through Apocrypha like it's a walk in a park.\n\nHope my colleagues left a good impression! We can be an eccentric bunch.

Just a band of like-minded travelers performing odd jobs across the planes. You know. A little light exploring, a bit of harmless smuggling, a pinch of heisting ….\n\nA bunch of busybodies if you ask me. Or, at least I am.

If Vorm had lips right now he'd talk your ear off. He's an archivist here and it's a library of sorts. Well, this whole realm is a library, but this place was always a bit more eerie.\n\nOh, I can hear him now, "Ysgild, you're being reductive."

I haven't a clue. I hadn't heard from Vorm in a while which is odd for the Nord. He does enjoy scolding and chastising his sister over inter-planar mail.\n\nSo, I thought I'd hop on over to his favorite haunt and this is how I found him.

Vorm once told me that this study breathes life into his books. That inked words hummed with magic and nearly leapt from the page. I thought he was being flowery with his prose, but perhaps I was wrong.\n\nI suppose we'll have to see for ourselves.

Vorm's always been the sentimental type. Knowing him, he's cataloged every book he and I have ever touched. So, yes. Trust me.\n\nHis natural philosophy books, Mother's history books, my favorite adventure series. They'll be in there.

Well, not completely. There are still mysteries to solve, secrets to learn. But I also need to concern myself with the present, the future. What's next for the Stonelore and the druid circles? How do we move forward from here?\n\nI do love a challenge!

Frii isn't gone, they just found a new purpose. And by their actions, they calmed the volcano and saved us all. I'll go to Y'ffelon, try to commune with Frii. Sometimes bound spirits respond, sometimes not. But they'll know I remember. That I care.

The remaining elders and archdruids are talking. They'll call a Draoife soon. Then … we'll see. We have to make sure the Firesong return to the true path. And we have to learn to trust them—to trust each other—again. Y'ffre will guide us.

Stefan suffered some great losses. We all did. But he's strong. He'll make a good leader for Galen. And the druids are already responding to his overtures.\n\nOh. You mean …. That's rather personal. Even for us. But Stefan and I … we'll see.

Now don't start with that sort of nonsense. Of course I need to thank you! You saved us all! What kind of count would I be … what sort of friend … if I didn't let you know how much what you've done for us means to me.

All right, I've taken up enough of your time. I know how eager Lady Arabelle is to get the peace talks underway.\n\nWe'll talk later. Now go speak to Lady Arabelle and let her know everything is ready for her to begin.

Astounding. Mortal, I'll speak plainly. I am the Morbid Observer, an overseer that presides over the Cloisters. I'm afraid you've stumbled upon a trap in motion. Both myself, and all those within the Cloisters, are stuck in a never-ending cycle.

I assure you that a trap set by Mora himself won't be easy to undo. My best guess is to find the root of its cause. The crime that Meenai-Shai participated in, though he doesn't seem to remember. But enough talk, the Argonian returns.

Yes, though soon he'll return. Just know that when he does, he will not be able to see me. I've been kept separate from the others. Unseen and unheard. I believe someone tried to steal from the Cloisters and this triggered a magical countermeasure.

No. Both my father and Archdruid Rahval taught me better than that. It is tempting, though. To pick a direction and just … go. But there are challenges to take on right here in the archipelago. I think I'm actually looking forward to them.

Interesting. I know Prior Durdryn cavorted with Daedra, but there was no mention of Peryite in any of the chronicles.\n\nAt least I see that you recovered the rest of the relic. I have no idea what they think it can do or if it even still functions.

Oh, hold onto it, of course. Gadayn said that fate led you to us. I can only assume it was because of the Fulcrum Obscura. It must have a role in whatever trials you must face to save Nirn.\n\nYes, my young charge told me everything. He does that.

I admit the particulars of their plan currently elude me. Clearly, they believe the relic—this Fulcrum Obscura—and the rite are key to remembering the dream they seek.\n\nTo stop them, we must learn more about the dream and the secret it holds.
Naturally. One must always stay working. Maximizing effort means increased income and respect.\n\nI should offer my services to all the assembled dignitaries. That's how I get my name out there.

We go to Apocrypha. The stacks of Cipher's Midden contain the most extensive collections of tomes and treatises in all the known realms. If answers to our questions exist, we will find them there.\n\nWill you continue to aid me in this endeavor?

Safely and productively, thanks to you. I found a rich vein of ebony that quite pleased House Mornard. I assume they'll start mining right away.\n\nIf only I could receive a cut of those profits. But I know they'll spread my name to new clients.

When you travel through the planes as much as we do, you figure out a few tricks! A brother who lives in Apocrypha, a mother from Fargrave, some crazy uncles on Nirn, and each one of us nosier than the last.\n\nCan't gossip if you don't keep in touch.

Well, he responds to his name, for a start! That must mean something. Of course, the family's pet bantam guar did too and that had a brick for a brain.\n\nThis thing is definitely as annoying as my brother, so let's just call it a twin's intuition?

This is the Necropolis of Necrom, perhaps the largest and oldest necropolis in all of Morrowind. For thousands of years, families have interred their revered ancestors in these catacombs.\n\nIt's my honor to serve as one of the Keepers of the Dead.

Dual heritages? Do you refer to Bretons being half Elf or are you talking about my noble versus druid upbringing? Either way, there's nothing to reconcile. All of that is a part of me. It makes me who I am. If anything, I want to make use of it all!

I think I have more than enough on my plate with Galen and building better relations with the druids. But I don't believe in the feud that has plagued the noble houses of the Systres for years. If High Isle needs help, House Mornard will provide it.

After all that has happened, I suppose I can confide in you. I'm going to ask Druid Laurel to stay in Vastyr. Help me as a liaison between the city and the druid circles. And if we also find time to renew a friendship of old … well, we shall see.

Truthfully? I'm not sure. I hope Emeric and the others can work something out. There's been more than enough blood spilled over the Ruby Throne for my taste. Alas, things like this aren't up to me. I do think there's a chance, though, thanks to you.

I rarely have to look, dear. They seek me out. I would like a little time to recover from this ordeal, though. My old bones don't spring back like they once did. And I really want to find someone to … let's say share a bottle or two with, yes?

These accusations that I'm some clandestine writer of tawdry thrillers are beginning to rankle, dear. I understand that the next Vale novel will feature an unlikely location, a new romantic interest, and a villain of epic proportions. Or so I heard.

Somehow my know-it-all twin found a way to become even more pretentious. At least, I'm pretty sure it's him. Hmm. No, no, it's definitely him.\n\nI think he wants me to enter the study to find a way to fix him. Care to join? It'll be fun!

Before you came along Vorm spat this note at me. "The family's favorites, V." Short and vague, but can't imagine it was easy writing this given his current situation. \n\nMy best guess? We go into the library and check out some books. How terrestrial.

I'm sure it would have already, but yet you still stand. You don't happen to have a pact with the fathomless Prince, do you? Regardless, return the book to its proper spot. 'Portents of Celestial Bodies' should sit right over there.

For as long as I've known him, Vorm has kept his secrets and sentiments tucked away between the pages of a book. Wouldn't put it past him to put the juiciest tidbits of knowledge he's collected inside tomes with sentimental value.

Anything and everything! I once found proof of our cousin's affair inside a Dwemer telescope manual. Vorm fancies himself a scholar, but what he's best at is interplanar gossip.\n\nSo, if there's a fix for his affliction, it'll be in a book.
I can't tell you specifics, but I'll share what I can! Whose favorites would you like to know about?

Oh, easy! The Curse of Blackscale Island is easily my favorite adventure book! There's one part, after the treasure gets stolen, when Captain Gold-Smirk comes face to face with the ghost of Laryssa Blackscale and—\n\nYou know what, I won't spoil it.

Have you ever seen one of those heavy old tomes with text smaller than dust and the only pictures are boring shapes with numbers and labels on them? Yeah, Vorm likes those.\n\nFind the most boring section of the library and you'll find his favorite.

Ah, that might be tougher. Mother was a historian and she loved nothing more than diving into events of the past. And recounting these stories to Vorm and me, of course.\n\nIt's been so long, but I'll know her favorite when I see it, I'm certain.

Abandoned, yes, but not without its defenses. Tel Rendys is a dangerous place, f'lah. I advise you not to interfere with the Dusksabers. And it seems Meln the Mouthless left Tel Rendys well protected, as my mercenaries can testify.

Oh, the Telvanni magister who owned this place. He's been missing for decades. The old fool possessed a book that I very much want to add to my library. Scavenge if you will, as long as you understand the book is mine.\n\nNow, why are you really here?

Indeed? You don't look like a Daedric cultist. Running errands for Daedra is frowned upon in most lands, but I appreciate your honesty.\n\nMy Dusksabers are stymied. And Meln warded his tower against other Telvanni such as myself. Perhaps you can help.
Indeed. Whether that book is tied to the threads that brought us here or not has yet to be determined.\n\nLet us make our way to the tower and see what fate shall reveal to us.
This is … a lot to take in. Am I to do as my father says and condemn him to this place?
We were caught in a powerful storm and the sky shone a sickening hue. I had my sea legs, but the incessant waves drove me to my knees. I heard my father … shouting?
I'm sorry, traveler, but I do not understand the question. I know the Cloisters can be quite distracting, but the sooner we return these books the better. Come now, I'd hate to disappoint my Prince.

A strange cipher bearing an unrecognizable pendant and fabric that does not match the robes of the Cloisters? This cipher fooled Meenai-Shai into unsealing protected tomes and we've been paying the price this whole time. I'm certain of it.
A new cipher? It isn't often someone joins our ranks, but I must say, those that do are often strange in their own ways. Perhaps when we're done here I can help you find who you're looking for.
Yes, yes. Some say it is like a dream-world where the minds of all in the Chorus can wander freely. Interacting with one another while the Great Eye studies them.\n\nWhat else did you learn?

The Chorus? It's the whole reason this place exists! The Rectory, I mean, not Apocrypha.\n\nBut what is it? Hmm. How to explain. It is the combined output of all the Rectory's vessels—a powerful, decentralized entity.
Well, danger comes in many forms, yes? Depending on the severity of the leaks, we may face arcane anomalies, bursts of raw magicka, or even structural instability.\n\nThen, there's the arcanovores.

Nalia tried to push through the ward on that door. The note over there suggests that something in this room disarms the trap. Clearly, she guessed wrong.\n\nI think this strange lens is part of the puzzle. We found it by the note.
Here, you take it. We obviously weren't able to figure it out. I'll be damned if I try to use it again.\n\nIf Shelreni sent you, by all means be my guest. I'm just going to stand back here ….

At least that narrows the scope of our research. The disturbance must originate from within the Rectory, or even the Chorus itself!\n\nPress on to the Esoterica Corporea to the north. It houses our preparatory instruments and an auxiliary somnambulum.

So you experienced something similar? As though the stacks were actively trying to keep the information hidden?\n\nStill, you managed to save some of the research. A reflection of your role as fate's proxy, perhaps? Let me peruse these pages ….

Hmm. This implies the relic was specifically created to reveal hidden secrets. Do these secrets pertain to the ancient cipher's report regarding the dream of a lost memory? And this last one ….\n\nCould the enemy be seeking the Infinite Panopticon?

Only one of Hermaeus Mora's most secure repositories of secret knowledge. It exists within a pocket realm of Apocrypha, but the entrance constantly shifts locations.\n\nOf course! They must be using the Fulcrum Obscura to reach the Panopticon.

A charm that will provide Gadayn with some measure of safety as you travel through Apocrypha. Please keep him safe, proxy. Even with the charm, he seems overly … fragile.\n\nEach cairn should glow after the successful application of dust and relic.

Research is often a series of trials and errors, but yes, this should work. In addition to its normal properties, the relic should also seek out its other half.\n\nAfter you activate the three cairns, return here. Then I shall complete the ritual.
The Esoterica Corporea acts as the entry point for newly interred minds joining our Chorus. An important process where any slight mistake could irrevocably harm one's mind.

It depends entirely on their contract. Some may spend their entire lives as part of the Chorus in exchange for a promised fortune or magical knowledge. Others may only spend a few winters. But I assure you each mind is as important as the last.

The ritual directed me to the desolate, northwest reaches of the Chroma Incognito.\n\nI sensed the entrance we seek there, as well as the other half of the Fulcrum Obscura. Our enemy must have also located the entrance—or is close to doing so.
Let me mark the location on your map. Go quickly, proxy. I shall follow and meet you there after I make sure Curate Gadayn gets back to Nirn safely.

My father has captained the Opulent Gale since I was a boy. He built the ship with his own two hands. I may never be the captain he hoped I'd be, but I'll never forget how alive I felt knowing he was at the wheel.
In truth, Traveler, I do not. It is a great crime to have removed books without the master's blessing. I can't bear the thought of letting my Prince down.

Yes—a troublemaker, disconnected from the Chorus. It keeps trying to escape through a connected body, but the attempts prove fatal every time.\n\nOut here in Apocrypha, we have no hope of isolating it. But if one of us entered the Chorus ….
We must rush the process, so I am sorry to say you won't feel the chorus' warm embrace.\n\nYou will likely arrive on the lowest level of the Chorus—what we call the cognitive substrate.

Never! This is wholly unprecedented.\n\nI almost wish I had more time to study it. The fortitude necessary for a mind to break free from its body? To travel through the Rectory's magicka flows unimpeded? It's as astounding as it is terrifying.

Ah, yes! Wisdom and bravery. You are a true child of Mora!\n\nLet's proceed to the next room. The auxiliary somnambulum is there. It will allow you to enter the Chorus, but you will not travel alone. Huzmargo will guide you from here.

Well, you. Obviously. Huzmargo must oversee the procedure and monitor the apparatus, yes?\n\nI would not suggest it if we had any other way of finding the rogue mind. But every moment we delay puts another vessel at risk! So, will you do it?

In order to access the Divinatory Forums, a cipher must tap into the sigil magic that pulses through the Cloisters. You'll have to trace the Sigil of the Great Eye and pray that my presence, however tenuous, still allows us access to its halls.

I know not which of our enemies have entered the Panopticon, but the ritual latched onto both the hidden entrance and the other half of the Fulcrum Obscura. They must have used the relic to find this place, not unlike how we did it.

Why does a Telvanni do anything? Ambition. Power. Greed.\n\nTwenty years ago I stood in Shelreni's path. An obstacle to the higher rank she craved. She requested a meeting. Instead of negotiating, she killed me and tried to steal my prized possession.

Legends say the Panopticon is an endless labyrinth of rooms and passages, but nothing inside conforms to reality as we know it. It protects some of Hermaeus Mora's most precious secrets, and powerful guardians roam its lengths.\n\nShall we proceed?

The Tormenting Eye. A tome of forbidden secrets. I see Hermaeus Mora's mark on you and your companion. If you don't know about the Black Books, she can tell you more.\n\nShelreni Baro is careless in her pursuit of power. She must not possess my book.
Well, make it quick, before more of those mercenaries decide to show up.\n\nI just can't figure out where I slipped up. Reynila shouldn't know I was after her. My catches never do.
I think so? I don't know. I was handed the job by my job broker. \n\nHe let slip that Reynila used to work for the client, but I didn't stick around to hear much else.

We know they seek details concerning a lost dream, and they plan to use a rite from a Black Book to recover it. But first they must determine where it is stored. I assume that is what they hope to learn in the Panopticon, the dream's location.

They believe so. And with the Fulcrum Obscura, they can sift through the infinite secrets locked within until they find the exact one they require.\n\nWe must get inside and prevent them from accomplishing that.
Reynila Treviri. Really. \n\nI may know something about her. Perhaps you can enlighten me on why it is you're seeking her.

Brelynn Ardas and Menredius Cortin will be my recipients. Brelynn likes to shoot dice outside the palace. Cortin should be hawking his wares by the fountain.\n\nMeet me at the tavern when you're done, and I'll tell you where you might find Reynila.
Keep your voice down, all right?\n\nReynila was through recently. She sought out Deredrien, a fence who specializes in moving specialty items.
For me? You charmer. What's the occasion? If you're in such a generous mood, the evening could be ours to spend however we choose.

Great. Well, maybe they patched things up and Deredrien went to go help her. \n\nThough that doesn't explain why she'd leave behind a note that says exactly where she's gone. Especially if she's trying to hide from this Reformer that Reynila mentioned.

I already told you most everything I know. \n\nI came to in Valenwood. Middle of nowhere. Blood on my claws. Someone was screaming. Didn't see who. My head felt like it was split in half, so they got away.

I woke up a few years back in the middle of Valenwood with a nasty headache and no memory except my name.\n\nBut that doesn't have anything to do with the job. Let's get to that campsite. I'll scout ahead and see if we can take Reynila by surprise.

Well, I was in the middle of the forest. Had to hunt and track so I didn't starve to death.\n\nAt one point, I started heading towards this huge tree in the distance. Elden Root. Civilization. Sometimes I wonder if I should've just stayed in the woods.
I figured you would.\n\nI hate Sadrith Mora, so I'm not in any hurry to get there. Ask away.

Track him down? What, to kill him? Oh. I suppose someone has to. You really think you can?\n\nListen. I had plans to blackmail the Reformer before I realized how stupid that would be. The cache of information can be yours and Sharp's, for a price.

It's probably not going to be much. He gave up on using it as blackmail, after all.\n\nHe's clearly scared for his life. Maybe helping him isn't the worst thing. But I say we don't go out of our way to set him up for a life of luxury.

To recover Meln and his Black Book, you must find Master Shelreni. And the letter you discovered explains how to do that.\n\nGo to the Assembly of Masters at Ald Isra and question Shelreni's mouth, Vabdru. He shall know how to reach her.

Then you shouldn't be surprised that they took Argonians captive.\n\nCaptives aside, I expected this writ a while ago. It feels almost like the Great Houses were waiting for an excuse to send one of us here to Camonnaruhn.
This writ bores me. I'm used to sneaking through entire armies or into well-guarded houses. Thugs pose no threats. \n\nWith you in the mix this writ could be interesting.

Of course. It's a means of keeping the Houses in check, if you will. The existence of the Morag Tong ensures peace is maintained. A writ is sanctioned and we act. We do not get to choose. So the Grandmaster decrees, so it will be done.

The Talisman of Saint Vorys is exactly what you'd expect. It's gaudy and ancient and the high priest will no doubt be thrilled to enlighten you on its history.\n\nThose details don't help me in stopping the Lark, which is my primary concern.
That is what plagues me. I would have never chosen such a thing! He was everything to me, and now I bear the guilt of the sacrifice he made. How can I face my mother after this?
I wish there were. Dealing with the Daedra is perilous in the first place.

An elder Khajiit came by and showed more genuine curiosity for Saint Vorys than any Telvanni that visited this shrine in years.\n\nI'm not worried about him, sera. I've heard the dangerous ones travel in groups, like that caravan nearby. Mind yourself.

Master Shelreni never comes to Ald Isra. Telvanni masters rarely do. I expect she is at her tower, Tel Baro. But I would be a poor mouth indeed if I let you pester her at home without asking what business you have with her.

For starters, I'm actually a Nord and not a floating book. I work as an archivist in service to Hermaeus Mora, though the Lord of Knowledge affords us some freedom on how to conduct our business.\n\nHence my private little library.

Naturally! The Guardian of the Unseen may be inscrutable at times, but my Prince will surely sort out the bedlam in his halls of erudition before too long. His loyal servants will need to return to make order of the disorder, and I will do my part.

Well, as I like to say, there's no one way to read a book. My family's unconventional upbringing gave me a rather unique perspective and that attracted the Prince's attention. \n\nI get my own space to study as long as I share my findings.

Oh, just hubris and folly, I'm afraid. Though I'm skilled in many arts, confronting beasts and skulking through labyrinths was always my sister's specialty. I'm not ashamed to admit that when chaos began to befall the study I panicked.

My mind wandered while attempting to portal out of the study. I imagined hiding within the pages of a book and, in my haste, the spell went awry. I was left a tawdry tome with no hope of returning to normal.\n\nUntil my sister arrived of course.
