In truth, I didn't know for sure. But one's sense of self stems from the moments and events that shape us. I was willing to bet my connection to these written words, paired with my family's bond, would help return me to normal.

Good question! Well, seeing as the study is a bit, occupied, Vorm is going to need a place to stay. And as I have no place for him to stay, that means he'll need to accompany me on the proverbial road!\n\nIs it too late to turn him back into a book?

He may be bookish, but my brother really is made of tougher stuff than it seems. This ordeal proves it. He'll do just fine by my side until his precious study is back to normal!\n\nWho knows, he may even grow to enjoy a bit of adventure?

Sharp-as-Night? I like that lizard. And I hear I'm not the only one. \n\nThat's useful information, f'lah. I'll tell you what you want to know. Reynila was through recently. She sought out Deredrien, a fence who specializes in moving specialty items.

She keeps a room at the Palace View Apartments, just around the corner.\n\nBut do be careful. Deredrien and Reynila fell out some time ago, and they might not appreciate you dredging that bad blood between them.

I believe so. He has somehow combined the power of dream with the power of pestilence to shift between the layers of this reality. They are here but not here, effectively hidden from the all-seeing gaze of Hermaeus Mora.
I shall concentrate the residual power of my ritual into a final tracking spell. Follow where the energy leads.

Many mortals find their way to Apocrypha, but few find their way home again. The secrets and insights of the Great Eye's realm fill the mind, crowding out that which makes us … us.\n\nWe call it the Hush. And those it takes, the Hushed.

We are mortals who have earned the privilege of serving Hermaeus Mora in Apocrypha. We devote our lives to tending his great library. All things known in both Nirn and Oblivion are somewhere in these stacks.

Many of the books you see in Apocrypha are echoes of books that exist elsewhere. But scriptoriums such as Quires Wind are where the Great Eye's Daedric servants—Seekers, usually—write down forbidden things. Black Books, for example.

The First Servant? I thought he was a myth. One of those stories of Apocrypha ciphers sometimes tell each other. But if he's real, his ambitions might lead him to seek out a disaffected cipher in Quires Wind.\n\nSuch as Sabinius.
Assuming things return to normal in Quires Wind, I'll resume my work assembling the materials needed by the Great Eye's Daedric scribes. And one day, perhaps, I'll be chosen for the ultimate honor.
I am. I made my choice the moment my son was swept overboard. Herm'us Mora honored his side of the deal. I will honor mine.
My father put everything on the line to save me. But I cannot let him die, not if there is a better alternative.
I heard him yelling. At me? At the crew? A huge wave struck the ship and I fell into the churning sea.  I can still taste the salt water. My lungs felt so heavy. I was choking on it.
But if I drowned, then how did I awaken here? What happened to the rest of the crew? What became of my father? Why was I spared?
And I should have a son forget his father? I would rather perish, literally. Let me honor the original promise I made. My son is stubborn, but he offers too much. Give me the logbook.
Should I hesitate where my father made the same choice? This isn't what I wanted, but my memories seem a small price to pay for his life. Give me the book.

Missive? I don't know anything about a missive, but I could use your help. I seem to have in my possession three of my master's tomes with no memory of having taken them. I can't understate the trouble I could be in if he finds they're missing.

Oh, certainly. It has been a privilege to work within these halls. And besides, it's been a while since I've been able to properly conduct my role as a cipher. Imagine all the predictions that have piled up while we were trapped!
I haven't seen it firsthand. Prelate Faram says the monks are delirious with fever. Now I'm stuck out here, turning pilgrims away, while everyone else is quarantined inside.

It might sound strange, but I think I'd like to read. I was surprised by how torturous it was to be surrounded by this knowledge and be unable to access it.\n\nYes. That's what I will do. I'll sit down and read. How … comforting.

Yes. We're a monastic order. We keep the crypts in good repair. We help families make funerary arrangements. And we guide those pilgrims who come to visit their ancestors. We never turned anyone away—until now.

The Lord of Secrets? I hope not! I mean, I suppose Hermaeus Mora isn't bad as far as Daedric Princes go—he's not part of the House of Troubles, after all. But trafficking with any Daedra is dangerous business.\n\nEveryone knows that.
For me? Is it from …?\n\nOh no!

My spirit is bound to the soul gem Shelreni used to capture me. Disentangling the connection will require more time and expertise than you have, so simply take the gem and leave.\n\nWithout me, she may never be able to unlock my Black Book.

Shelreni took the Black Book with her. But without my help, she'll have to unriddle it page by page. The labor of days or weeks, not hours. If she can even accomplish it.\n\nShe's too fond of the easy path to power. It will be her undoing someday.

I don't, f'lah. Not really. But I don't do anything for free. Can you imagine the damage that would do to my reputation?\n\nYou want something from me. I want to have some fun. This way, we both end up happy.

I do love your little questions, but if we keep going on like this, those flowers will wilt before they reach their intended recipients.\n\nLet's just say they serve as a reminder that I have them in my thoughts. Now, run along, will you?

Is that what Hermaeus Mora and his High Elf lackey told you? Can you imagine any revelation that possesses such power?\n\nNo, this is about keeping secrets. Hoarding knowledge. Stealing memories. Hermaeus Mora, the great miser of Oblivion!

I will continue my search. You, however, should turn back. Wandering the memories of a Daedric Prince is dangerous for one such as I. For you, such a journey will most likely prove fatal.\n\nI would hate to see fate's chosen reach such an ignoble end.

All I have is fragments of a dream. Even Vaermina could not help me recall it. But we remembered enough to get us this far. Hermaeus Mora stole this knowledge from us.\n\nI do not wish to harm you, mortal. To harm anyone. But I will learn the truth.

Torvesard spoke true. Forbidden knowledge and secrets are my prime concern. Much of what I hoard serves to protect all the realms of existence.\n\nThis particular secret, however, must stay forgotten. Even this slight recollection threatens reality.

Torvesard found a way to slip past the eyes that see all and entered a memory he should have had no ability to access. And yet here we are. He restored that which I destroyed and now this recollection is no longer forgotten.

The threads fray, but have not yet snapped. Torvesard and my enemies recall a fraction of the memory, but the most devastating secret remains locked away.\n\nReturn to your allies. The situation can still be salvaged, if you and Leramil work together.

I thought about that on the way over, too. If Reynila could afford to hire mercenaries, she wouldn't be desperate for Deredrien's help, like she was in that note we found. Right?\n\nSomething else is going on here.

That campsite is the only lead we have on finding Reynila. If we can get there, maybe we can find something to keep us on her trail.\n\nI'm not used to looking out for others. Can you handle yourself if we run into trouble?

Right. She threw in with the Reformer … who told her to prioritize my capture over Reynila's? What?\n\nAnd he's the one who hired me? Without knowing it? This is the last time I ever find work through a job broker.

The Reformer uses experimental magic on his slaves. Reynila didn't understand the process, and when she excised it from Sharp to free him, it tore something from him. His memories, she thought.\n\nReynila never forgave herself for what happened.
I can spare a moment to tell you what I know—but after, we really should get moving to Gorne.
This is far beyond what I hired you for. Isn't it?\n\nMaybe you're like me, and you never pass up a payday. But I probably wouldn't even have stopped to help someone like me in the first place.

No, but we can piece it together. The fence moving specialty items. The two-lantern signal. The list of operatives. This person called Dim who the Reformer wants back alive.\n\nReynila isn't traveling alone with some trinket. She's freeing a slave.

She is my wife. Sharp is the reason we met, actually—she needed forged documents for his new identity. I'd never done anything like that before, but she convinced me.\n\nPity he didn't get to use the forgeries, but some good came of it, at least.

Gorne is packed to the brim with mad wizards. Doesn't make it too different from rest of the peninsula, but I've heard worse things have moved in recently.\n\nI guess what I'm saying is I'll watch your back in there so long as you're watching mine.
He's so slippery, there's no guarantee they'll even slow him down.\n\nQuickly, please—if you can help deter the spirits, I'm sure we can corner him and stop this once and for all!

If someone somewhere cares I'm gone, they're keeping awfully quiet about it. Either nobody misses me enough to go looking for me, or I was a loner before, just like I'm a loner now.\n\nI'm not trying to find answers on my past. You shouldn't either.
Sure. A bit.\n\nLook, I didn't know if I'd killed someone, or someone had tried to kill me. I kept my head down. Took any job to get by. And now I guess I'm here.

That arrogant s'wit! And if that foolish priest hadn't prematurely set off my runes, I'd have clipped the Lark's wings and had him dead to rights.\n\nTell me this isn't over. Tell me you found something useful. Something at the Khajiit camp, maybe?
I must either lie about our whereabouts and say that we were lost. Or, tell the truth and become embroiled in potential political machinations. Neither is appealing.

We weren't captured, we were kidnapped. Those dryscales came into our camp, stamped out our fire, and brought us here under the cover of night. They're cowards. They planned to ransom us. I'm not surprised an assassin was sent to deal with them.

You'd have to ask him that. \n\nI'll have plenty of time to think about his request. Those dryscales may have kept us bound, but no one ties our tongues against our will. Whatever my report, it'll be what we want not what Ashur decrees.

So that's the assassin's name. No, we had no idea anyone was sent, but I knew those thugs' plan would attract the Pact leaders' anger. \n\nI'm sure some of the Great Houses know what happened here, but Ashur asked me not to include it in my report.
You think the Baandari are paying me? They could barely afford to pay their mercenaries. \n\nThe Lark of Rosgard never leaves a job unfinished. Simple as that.

Valinna thinks Keshargo is an old fool. She would never consider that he would go to a different plane. \n\nNeither of the rifts will close for a while, but Valinna favors the second one. So we turned to the Deadlands to keep the staff safe.

When we get to the ruins, I need you to barter with Shadeya. Do whatever you can to keep her occupied with the talisman.\n\nWhile you do that, I'll do what I do best. It's a gamble, but I think we can pull it off.

Hmm. First you shout plague, then I hear that several of the dock workers who unloaded the Stormwing took ill. Now Randas?\n\nAll right. Go investigate the Stormwing. If you find anything incriminating, I want to hear about it!

Mazandi's notes are meticulous, her maps are detailed, and her mind is sharp. This one fostered her skills when Valinna's loyalty soured.\n\nIf Keshargo knew how to get a message to her before coming here, he would have.

Valinna punished Mazandi's loyalty by making her a rift guard. Instead of exploring the planes, Mazandi was forced to watch at the edge of the Deadlands. This is an insulting task for one of her skills.

Because that's what I do best. You have the pleasure of speaking with the Daggerfall Devil. The Bane of Glenumbra. I struck fear into all who crossed my path. And I won't hesitate to show you exactly what I'm capable of.

Mora understands that what I do is an art worth studying. And I'll admit that time wracked my bones and addled my joints. So how could I turn down a chance at finding a new, younger body to continue my life's work.
In fact, perhaps your body would be the perfect vessel for my great return. Oh, I can hear their screams now. Beautiful. Perfect.\n\nNo one will stop me. Not even you.

Nathyn's protective wards. You know—Sathile's magic barriers that kept Nathyn's half of the tower in isolation. I couldn't cross them at all. They certainly made tidying up a bit of a trial.\n\nI mentioned the wards before, didn't I?

She told us Keshargo died. She was his successor, I never thought she'd lie!\n\nWell, it seemed better to be a Scribe of Mora than no scribe at all. So, I did what scribes should do. I kept quiet and didn't interfere.

Then you'll have honored the Tribunal and saved the Shrine of Saint Vorys from a fate of worshiping a worthless trinket with no real mystical properties for time immemorial.\n\nOr … perhaps they'd be doing that either way. Who can say?

As far as Rilasi knows, you only have the original talisman. \n\nIf you give the original to Eilirsu-dro and the replica to Rilasi, she'll have to pretend it's the real thing—or get herself in a whole world of trouble by admitting how she lost it.
This place? I don't know where we are. There was a storm and a great wave and my father shouting. Yes, he was shouting at the storm.

Hermaeus Mora? High Elves don't deal with Daedra, but he's known among the sailors as Herm'us Mora, the Tide King. He carries many names, but he lives deep beneath the waves. Could my father have angered him somehow?

I don't—wait! When I wanted to slip out after curfew, I used the cellar that connects to the city's underways. I doubt Blightcrown or his attendants know about it. Meet me in the tunnel behind the Necropolis. I think I can get us inside from there.

Not a terrible lot. I'm not an expert on Daedric studies or anything.\n\nI know he's the Daedric Prince of Pestilence, the Blighted Lord, the Master of Tasks. Some believe he isn't a very important Prince, but people get sick all the time.

I was orphaned at a young age. No other family. Abbot Ilvel took me in and raised me. He … he's the father I never had. A kind and devout servant of the Necropolis, but maybe too trusting.\n\nIt never occurred to him to question Blightcrown's story.

Safe from immediate danger, yes. But stress levels among the vessels are still far too high. I must inspect each mind and vessel to ensure their well-being.\n\nYou have a strong mind! If you have the time, I would certainly enjoy studying it.

Huzmargo supposes a fair amount of cleaning and vessel repair. But don't worry, It won't be long before Ciphers hear of your success and return to the Rectory. Once I have a team together I'll be sure to tend to our surviving minds.

Portals. Fascinating fissures in space. They open to other places, other times. Even other realms. Ah, what was the question? Oh, which portal ….\n\nWhichever appeals, proxy. They lead to the Hoarvor Pit, Rootwater Grove, and the Ondil Outskirts.

Of course, of course. Huzmargo is sure our Prince has plans for you beyond the Rectory Corporea. But, do keep the offer in mind!\n\nYou did a great service for us, friend. I suppose the time has come for payment, yes?

It's a suspicion, nothing more. The Sodality of the Eye recently learned that some who profess to have the Great Eye's best interests at heart are actually working to undermine Apocrypha. Is Leramil among them? I can't prove that … not yet.

Hermaeus Mora answers to many names. More than the blades of grass in these fields. I belong to the Sodality of the Eye, and we revere the Great Eye.\n\nThe Golden Eye is a different sect. We are not so many, however, that we are unaware of each other.

Orders for the Dusksabers, vampire mercenaries from the Telvanni Peninsula. They were hired to steal the Emerald Glyphic and take it to the Shrine of the Golden Eye.\n\nIt also contained a riddle to direct them to the shrine's location.

Dralys, hmm? The coded riddle was slightly different. "Where claw meets prey, the farthest corner in the largest hall shows the way."\n\nI suppose the shrine could have two entrances. I shall mark your map and let you determine the proper path.
Does the term offend in some way? It is a perfectly appropriate word for one who acts in the place of another.\n\nHermaeus Mora has chosen you to act as their agent in this matter. Hence, proxy.

Yes, a nosy walker came to spy and ask foolish questions! And Shadeya was the only one bothered by this!\n\nThen again, the elder and his family are Baandari. They are used to being treated like criminals. Anything else, nosy walker?
This one is not in the habit of paying tithes to foreign saints. The elder may have gone, but he insisted others stay at the camp.\n\nFine by this one, so long as she gets paid.

Ask Shadeya. This one thought it sensible to hire protection while crossing a land rife with slavers, and her sharp eyes miss nothing!\n\nAnd you are welcome to ask around our camp, walker. Make yourself at home among the Baandari.

Torvesard and Blightcrown could be anywhere, but Master Shelreni has roots in the Telvanni Peninsula. If anyone can help you navigate the complexities of the Dunmer Great Houses, it is Curate Gadayn.\n\nInvestigating Shelreni is our best option.
Spores nearly killed me. Barely, barely exposed. Natural immunity. I will live.\n\nHeard shouting. Then screaming. Everyone came running. Big mistake. Subject's spores … too strong. Wanted to escape.
Though only one chases the other. \n\nAll right. It's obvious Folsi sent you. And she gave you the code of a courier. That tells me you have something for me. Go on, then. Hand it over.

A cult composed of followers of Vaermina and Peryite, Princes that usually work against each other, may be easier to uncover. I shall see what I can learn from my contacts among Hermaeus Mora's faithful.\n\nWe will succeed, proxy. We have to.

Perhaps. That is one of the possibilities I plan to explore. However, Torvesard demonstrated powers unheard of for a typical Dremora. He may have other abilities. I need to proceed with caution.\n\nAnd Blightcrown serves Peryite. Another obstacle.
So what if I did? They'd both do well to believe it. They can never be together, do you hear me? Never!\n\nLeave this place! Forget all that you've seen, or you'll end up worse than Tun-Shei.
Wait. I remember you from Ald Isra. You stopped Shelreni. You saved us all.\n\nBut you cannot help here. You will find only monsters ahead. Leave, while you still can.
Let me see …. No, I'd never write such a thing! Did Sathile write this? Does she really think this sounds like me?\n\nWhat did the research notes say?
I know, but …! Fetch it all, I just wish I could remember where I've heard it before.\n\nDelmon, Delmon ….

I don't know. Has she gone mad? Was she always this way?\n\nIf so, she's been hiding it—and I can't blame her. If she were carted off to Gorne, she'd be parted from Nathyn. The thought of it probably only made things worse for her.

Blightcrown and Shelreni concocted the dream affliction with the help of Vaermina and Peryite. It allowed them to avoid detection by shifting into alternate layers of reality. It even affected Mora's guardians.\n\nAnd we know they plan to improve it.

Folsi can fend for herself. Right now, I need to see if she learned anything to point me to the true identity of my target. Tredecim, the name on the writ, is an alias.\n\nInteresting. According to Folsi, House Dres established a camp to the south.

Folsi seems to think so. Since you want to get paid, how about you help me out? I need to assassinate a spy in Tel Huulen. But to do that, I need to figure out who actually deserves my blade.\n\nIt's quite legal. I have a Morag Tong writ of execution.

Almost no one does. Hermorah is the lord of secrets and as such, this entrance is known only to a select few. It's a way to ensure the safety of all we record.\n\nValinna and the scribes will not expect us.

Endangers Nirn? I'm just a minor curate working in the Necropolis! Feuds between Daedric Princes are beyond me. Still … I want to help.\n\nFinding anything in the catacombs will take time. We might be able to catch up with Blightcrown if we hurry.
Prior Durdryn established the Keepers of the Dead as a religious order and built this abbey over the ancient necropolis. He lived and died here centuries ago.

Since the founding of Morrowind, Dark Elves have interred their dead in necropolises. Necrom is one of the oldest. Maybe the oldest.\n\nHere our people can visit their revered ancestors. Seek their guidance. Remind them they haven't been forgotten.

Rescue? Then she really does love me? There was this note, you see—I was certain it was fake, but then I saw you and … well, I started to wonder.\n\nBut I cannot leave. If you came through the caverns, you must have seen what I'm capable of.

Delmon and I were trying to save the world. A promising fungal spore sample was on its way from Black Marsh when Delmon caught the very thing we were trying to cure. And I lost him.\n\nI had to know if the spores would have saved him. And now I know.

Leaving for good is no option for me. My heart is Nathyn's, and his is mine.\n\nIf I don't give up my freedom, I can help Sathile find a cure. I'd get to see the world like I always wanted … but I'd be in her service. And I'd be alone.

The ancestors watch over us. I have faith that in moments of need, my prayers will be answered. Although it certainly helps that the censers were destroyed and that foul miasma is dissipating.\n\nI'll do what I can while you deal with the imposter.

It depends what you mean by relic. Many families choose to honor their dead by entombing them with trophies or keepsakes. Some of those might be valuable … or dangerous. But no Dark Elf would think of stealing from their ancestors.

It's complicated. The Assembly of Masters consists of just their mouths. The actual masters rarely leave their towers, and never to meet with their rivals. A conclave, however, is a different story. The masters themselves are compelled to attend.

At Tel Huulen, the tower hall in Ald Isra. As a curate, I think I can get us into the conclave by claiming official Necrom business. House Telvanni prefers to stay on our good side, so they rarely ask too many questions of the Keepers of the Dead.

Of course! Wasn't I the greatest magister of my time? If not for my desire for solitude, I would have been the archmagister!\n\nUnfortunately, my spectral body isn't good for anything these days. You'll need to serve as my hands for this to work.

It started when a stranger came to town. A Telvanni master. She offered to purchase the old glass mine. I thought it was too good to be true. The mine closed years ago. But she offered us a chest full of gold and the village elders accepted it.

I don't know. But listen, the overseer and his workers—they're Daedra worshipers! They rounded up the villagers and took them away. I … I hid.\n\nCheck the Green Glass Inn. The cultists commandeered it. Now, please, I need to get out of here.

Everyone in the village was given a job in the mine. Then others came. Masons and additional laborers, we thought. Then the dreams started. Nightmares. Toiling in the darkness. Working to cut malachite and stone for an arch and a statue.
You and me both.\n\nWell, go ahead. Guess it's the least I can do, since this is a bit beyond what I initially hired you for.

Who cares? He was a trusted associate, and now he's in the pocket of this … Reformer. Whoever that is.\n\nNo point in figuring out why or what happened. Not like we can patch things up after this, anyway.
No idea. Obviously.\n\nBut my gut starts churning whenever I think about it. Maybe we should just get moving.
Certainly. \n\nYou know, it's been so long since I spoke to another outsider. I didn't think I'd miss it so much.

It is. She told me he had ambitious ideals that challenged the traditions of house Telvanni.\n\nBut when she witnessed the cost of those ideals firsthand, she had a change of heart. Breaking ties wasn't enough. She started freeing his slaves.

Reynila can tell you more when we find her. The way she speaks of him, it's like she's worrying after an old friend.\n\nShe liked to imagine that he ended up living a peaceful life as a fisherman somewhere.

He's a rich and powerful Telvanni magister who hides behind his moniker and keeps the particulars of his research close to his chest.\n\nHe practices horrible experiments on his slaves. Somehow, he thinks his work is going to end slavery in Tamriel.
Reynila says he uses some experimental metal to create a sort of link between him and his subjects. \n\nI've blocked out most of the details. But I do know that Sharp was the Reformer's favorite.

He was feral when she excised him from the Reformer's control. She had no choice but to subdue him.\n\nShe delivered him to Deredrien at an old safe site in Valenwood. He was supposed to go to Black Marsh from there, but things didn't go as planned.

Just this. I am in no condition to help you recover the relic. None of the keepers are. Well, none except Gadayn. I will send our young curate with you.\n\nSearch out these villains, put a stop to their scheme, and recover the Fulcrum Obscura.

Too late for me. Deredrien and those mercenaries made sure of that.\n\nI never wanted my Mevei to get caught up in all this. To have to run forever from the Reformer. And the others. He'll never stop until Sharp is his again.
Kaj-kujei. Elder brother. It's what I always called him. \n\nReynila didn't know how to properly excise him from the Reformer's attunement back then. Like the others. Like me.

Deek-nujei. His little sister. I don't think we had the same parents, but that was what he called me. He was there from the day I hatched.\n\nHe always said he would come back for me. Help me escape. I'd given up all hope.
I don't feel any memories stirring when I look at her, either. Just … nothing.\n\nI gave up on finding answers about my past a long time ago. I don't understand why this had to happen now.

Help her? I'm a mercenary. I don't know how to look out for someone like her.\n\nAnd if this Reformer is as powerful and dangerous as everyone's said, there's not a place in Tamriel that is going to be safe for her anyway.

The staff facilitates a return to the study from anywhere in Oblivion.\n\nMore importantly, it is a symbol of leadership. Without the staff, Valinna doesn't believe in her own command. She only thinks of truth and lies, never of what exists between.
Dreynis's notes didn't do it justice. The power this prism radiates is palpable. And to think a Daedric Prince wasted such an artifact on an old fool. Did he tell you how to use it?

I haven't the faintest idea. I was only sent along to conduct an audit, though the Consortium did seem rather on edge. They said I should expect to hear all sorts of excuses, from cave-ins to cultists. Laughable, I know, but it's part of the job.

Ulfengar? I've met him once before, back when the mine was first opened. Nord fellow. Tough as rocks and sweet as salt, but a hard worker. You want that in an overseer.\n\nTo be honest, I'm surprised he's late. It's definitely out of the ordinary.

I shouldn't jump to conclusions, especially when I haven't had the chance to assess anything yet.\n\nBut yes, my employers certainly seem to think so. After all, not every worker keeps their company's best interests in mind.

Well, last week, the head steward assigned me to Master Sulis's quarters. He's friendly in public, but exceedingly mean behind closed doors.\n\nI heard him talking with Masters Foves and Thilse about a secret project, but I didn't get any details.

Myself and others like me, yes. Auditors. Adjusters, if you will. We assess the egg mines to ensure they continue to meet the Consortium's production standards. Though, that's certainly not to say I'm irreplaceable.

Anchre Egg is a particularly important mine. It may seem dramatic, but I'm convinced any failure here will result in my dismissal. It isn't easy for an outsider like myself to be accepted into a Telvanni business so, yes. I'm a bit worried.

You brought me a jar? Ugh, it reeks like Ashur's undergarments!\n\nWhy in the world would a servant need a jar of kagouti musk? I can't think of a single useful purpose other than to stink up the place. Did Aki-go have any useful information?

You can call me Ogle. I'm a Watchling in service to Hermaeus Mora. I aid in the designation or disintegration of failed fates. It's a coveted role, I might add. And one that I don't wish to risk losing.

A fated glyphic is the physical manifestation of a potential fate. A stone that holds a transcription of a possible future. They are a powerful and precious source of knowledge.\n\nThis particular glyphic is one of my master's favorites.

Fated glyphics whose futures do not come to pass can latch onto our own reality and cause havoc. These intrusions are, well, wasteful. Underweave is the place where these failed fates are unwoven. Recycled.

Nathyn came from me. I am enough of him that the fungal symbiote does not register me as a separate entity, and therefore not a threat to its host.\n\nThat is when I named it. Delmon Mycota. The cure, like love, that would be with us always.

Clearly, the cult used the mine to construct a portal to Apocrypha for the express purposes of invading my master's realm. They also sent stone to restore a Daedric shrine, most likely one devoted to Peryite or Vaermina.\n\nBut who's Master Shelreni?

Life offers no guarantee of love either, but I found that, didn't I?\n\nI don't see it as giving up my freedom. I see it as a choice of how I get to show my love. But … my heart is split. If you were in my place, which would you choose?

Remarkable! Even at a glance I can see these are more comprehensive than the scribbles you found strewn about the island. Oh, it's a pity Dreynis became so … confused. There's a shadow of his genius in these pages.\n\nWhat of the prism?

Searching for the staff, mostly. And then watching the Deadlands rift. Valinna hates me since I won't do what she wants. But scribes do not meddle in the affairs of Oblivion.\n\nOh, it's all right that she hates me. I don't like her much, either.

Well, that narrows down the list of suspects. And it also tells us how they exchange information with their contact. They're using the kagouti nests to the north as a pick up spot.\n\nDid you find anything else?
Not quite yet. This could just be another diversion. Let's not jump to too many conclusions just yet.
Mevei? The one who made it clear I was a dangerous liability because I was choosing to go after the Reformer? The one who likely blames me for the death of her wife? That Mevei?\n\nNo. I haven't.
Why not? It's probably how I'd feel, if it were me.\n\nI can't replace Reynila. But I can try and fix things my way. Our way, if you're still with me.

I don't know how to find her, and she couldn't find me if she tried.\n\nProbably for the best that it stays that way. You saw how disappointed she was when she realized I wasn't her kaj-kujei. The brother she knew from before.

Please. Like I care.\n\nBut I owe him for not giving me up when he could have. I'll leave the selecting to you, since you clearly have more particular tastes than I do. Federo will probably appreciate your judgment better than mine.

It wouldn't have been my first place to look either. But I guess a truly skilled forger could hide in plain sight.\n\nIf that's what Federo heard, let's follow his lead. He's been here longer than we have, I suppose. It's the clothes I'm worried about.

This is really the best you could do? I'm a courier for the Antiquarian Circle? This document makes it sound awfully dangerous.\n\nWhat's that smell? Don't tell me that's coming from the clothes. You did remember to bring me clothes, didn't you?

No! I'll take it. Sharp was always my best man for the job. If he says this was the most you could do, I believe it.\n\nI guess being a courier isn't so bad. But the smell on these clothes—oh, never mind. It's nothing a good wash can't fix.

That fetching thief has been a thorn in my side for far too long!\n\nHe's planning to rob the shrine at Sailenmora of the sacred relic of Saint Vorys. I need extra hands if I'm to stop him. Yours could do. Are you looking for work?

Stand in for me at the shrine and the Khajiit caravan nearby. Ask questions, search for any clues or suspicious activity, and assure the high priest that I have everything under control.\n\nHelp me, and I'll make sure you're compensated for your time.

The master's fated glyphic could be anywhere! It may have even been fed into one of the nemesis looms already!\n\nThis is it for me, mortal. Cherish the moments you shared with Ogle, because I am not long for this plane.

I think I'll take one more walk around the grounds before I join Nathyn.\n\nIt'll be my last moment alone for quite some time, and I want to spare some thoughts for my family. I think they'd be happy I found my true love.

I expect I'll get straight to work for Sathile—I mean, Mistress Dreloth.\n\nIf I can spare a moment alone with Nathyn, I'll take it. But I don't want to waste any more time when I could be searching for a cure for him.
By the Three, she's going to be here! In here! With me! I've never had that before! \n\nWhat do I do? I need to tidy up! Look presentable! Make sure she's going to be comfortable …. So much to do!
I'll ask my mother to order me songbooks. And then I'll learn and practice every song I can. When Dacia returns, I'll play, and she'll sing, and it'll be just like when we first met.

I'll say goodbye to Nathyn. His affliction doesn't affect me because of our shared blood, but I don't have the same connection with Dacia. Her spores would kill me.\n\nI'll inoculate Dacia, and return to my work.

It'll put a stall in my research, but I think Dacia deserves a break. I've put her through quite a lot.\n\nLetting her be with Nathyn—as much as she can be, with him behind these wards—will be a good reminder for why she chose the way she did.

They seem to be servants of other Daedric Princes. Rivals to the One Who Knows. The threads of fate that converge in this region should reveal more. That is the hope, at least.\n\nAnd we are not dealing with just simple cultists. There are … others.
Good. I can't stand them. So excited about changing the world, but not willing to deal with the real problem here. \n\nThose skittering Cartoklepts keep finding their way into the vault!
We cannot thank you enough for what you have done today. We will gather supplies and do as you suggest.
Once we have these doors open we will gather our supplies and escape. We cannot thank you enough for what you have done here today. We will tell our story to all who will listen.
Immense gratitude, strangers. We will take what we can and do as you suggest.

Vermin. Pests. Thieves! I keep blocking their holes but it's no use. They take the keys, the books, the scrolls. And they don't sign anything out. \n\nIf you see them anywhere, slaughter them. Bring back some proof and I'll let you into the vault.

It's an index of sorts. Whatever the Hidden Kindred seek in Apocrypha, they must not know where to find it. So they've come to the Catalog to get an exact location.\n\nThe Pool of Inquiry contains such information—if they know how to retrieve it.

Ah, of course. A few too many syllables, I suppose. How about rise instead?\n\nImagine a ladder. As a Telvanni spellwright, I must prove my skill and expertise each time I wish to go up a proverbial rung. I hope to speed my climb.
I am the keeper of the vault. The curator of the scribes. I know all that is recorded in the Scrivener's Hall and keep its secrets from prying eyes … light fingers too.
Master Foves's aide? Interesting. Once House Dres heard about the writ, they must have panicked.

At his peak, Dreynis was a Telvanni master unmatched in portal magic. It's been ages since he's published any of his research, but he must still be tinkering away. I'm certain we can find a few pages lying about the island.

He chugged a bottle of that elixir, then took a run at the first giant we came across. Never seen a body fly like that before.\n\nBuram told me to get rid of the man's belongings at the inn, but the armorers won't take his clothes.

Even with a good wash, it all still smells like that strange elixir of his. Like columbine flower, spoiled cabbage, and burnt hair.\n\nCan't decide whether to burn the clothes or bury them. You're welcome to take them off my hands.
Then let's go get Guitot. We'll meet back in Ald Isra, at Tel Huulen. Then I'll complete the writ.\n\nAfter that? A hot bath with a strong soap to wipe away the stink.
Ugh! What's that on the letter? Are you sure that's just mud?\n\nWhy don't you just read it to me from over there.
If Guitot and the Dres used this site often, they could have left behind other information.\n\nKeep looking around for anything not kagouti related.
Not so fast, hero. Have we found everything here at the kagouti nests? There might be more clues scattered around this Dres message relay.

The nemesis looms unmake everything! By now the glyphic's been reduced to unwoven strands. Sputtering fragments of a former fate. I just know it!\n\nThere are too many paths to follow. I need a moment to think, mortal. This is all too much.

Recording? Yes. Sharing? No. Our lord Hermaeus Mora taught us that there's power in secrets. I don't let Scrivener's Hall divulge the knowledge and treasures of the realms to just anyone. Not even the Magnastylus can waltz in here.

I'm the only one who holds the key to this gate. This is why the Cartoklepts are the greatest threat to our hall. They do more than just break into the vault, they steal from it. They must be stopped!

Valinna? That newcomer? She came by here once asking for some staff or other. Didn't even want to hear about the genuine threats the Cartoklepts pose!\n\nShe said she's our new leader, but at least Keshargo helped me deal with those impish thieves!

Hmmm. Treasures. Objects of power and riches beyond your imagination. You won't be allowed near those. \n\nThere are chests though. Sometimes the Cartoklepts steal the keys, if you find a key, you're welcome to open the chest.

My next step is quite clear—I kill Guitot. The writ covers Tredecim and just Tredecim. Anything you want to do beyond that is up to you, hero.\n\nLet's return to Tel Huulen. Hopefully Guitot is there so I can wrap this up.

Gnisis? Well, that's not too far. Let's see. Bridge, Dwemer ruins … I think I know the place. No hope of pronouncing it, though. I'll mark it on your map, and we can skulk around for a way inside.\n\nAnything worthwhile in the other notes?
Reynila? Let me see. \n\nHm. I think you're right. She was the reason that Federo had somewhere safe to go when he needed to run. He protected me because she gave him a way to do so.

The Reformer had hold of me through that metal, somehow. Like he was trying to reunite me with a piece of myself that was trapped inside. It was a glimpse of my forgotten life. My memories.\n\nI'm not making any sense, am I?

Sondivel felt him, right? Sharp was never properly de-attuned from the soul magic—his memories still resonate, living collectively inside tyranite calx.\n\nBut I'm no longer attuned, and you've never been attuned. See? It's brilliant!
I'll be fine. I just need to shake it off. Wasn't expecting him to just grab me like that.\n\nThat journal you found. Was it more of what we found in the letter?

Hmm. Nice try, Foves, but not good enough. I appreciate the effort, but he loses again. Just as he always does.\n\nThank you for this. This evidence is all I need to bury him. Or worse, make him indebted to me.
Maybe I could answer them over drinks? I've grown quite partial to the sweet mead they drink here—\n\nOh, never mind. Sharp's giving me a look. Ask and be on your way, then.

It wasn't my choice. I'd been getting these letters for some time—pleading with me to defect, stop working for House Telvanni, telling me how I was complicit ….\n\nWhen I finally did leave, of course, it was too late.

That I'd decided to leave a cult and was laying low until its members forgot about me.\n\nCommon enough, and doesn't prompt a lot of questions. Most of the Nords who asked just nodded knowingly and offered me a drink. Maybe I'll keep the story.

Isn't it obvious? If I publish the findings in my own name, the finest minds on the peninsula will flock to me. Oh, they'll be eager to bask in the genius of Garalo Givyn, portal master!\n\nI can feel their adoration already.

Excellent! Let's take a look. Hmm. This can't be right. It's little more than a personal journal. There's barely anything worth publishing. And what's this about a prism?\n\nOh. How interesting. I've got an idea, adventurer.

Dreynis writes that he turned the manor's rotunda into a magical conduit. That would make this room the center of his work with portals. Yet there's no sign of this prism. If he hid it, then it must be important.

If I were a master of teleportation, I'd hide my secrets in a place only I could reach. That's it! The magical foci on the balcony above us. If we activate them, we may open a portal to Dreynis's little hiding place.\n\nOh, I'm a genius!

Before all this, he was a pampered Telvanni rank-climber. That is not an illness you recover from overnight.\n\nWe handled Reynila's unfinished business with him, and now we're on to more important things. It's up to him how he moves forward now.

I do? Well, we mustn't waste the opportunity. I beg you, don't give the prism to your mage associate. It warps you. Twists you until you can understand what it shows you.\n\nI thought it a gift from Sheogorath. But what it revealed ….

I haven't decided. It might be too dangerous, you know? Probably safer for him to make a clean break from all this.\n\nBut saying that makes me wonder if Reynila thought the same about me. If that's why she didn't try harder to find me.

The scholars and mystics of your world call me a Daedric Prince. What you see is only an aspect of my true self, for the mortal mind cannot contain the whole of me. This form suffices.\n\nYour mind must remain intact for you to be of use to fate.

What all good Telvanni masters do. Carefully consider my options and then take the course that gets me more of influence, prestige, and power.\n\nMaster Foves will need to be punished for dealing with House Dres, but beyond that? I need to think on it.

It is a time-sensitive job, and I was told to stop Reynila at any cost. Thought it'd be better to get on her trail sooner rather than later.\n\nI don't need to know all the fancy details and motivations. I just need to know enough to get paid.

Many possible futures branch from every mortal choice. If we know the consequences of our choices, it changes the outcome. Therefore, Hermaeus Mora tells us only what he must.\n\nAs fate's chosen, the rest is up to you.

Just information? No risk to scale or tail? Very well.\n\nI don't know about a spy, but a servant leaves the quarters late every Sundas and Middas night, then returns early the next morning. No idea who. But there's always a strange smell the next day.

You wouldn't! You would? Fine! Working for House Telvanni is just one terrible moment after another. Here, but I don't want to know anything about what you do in there.\n\nJust leave the key in the lock. I'll grab it once you leave.

Oh. I didn't expect you to be reasonable. That's refreshing.\n\nI can't give you the key to our quarters. My masters beat me enough as it is. But I happen to know that Garnse leaves his key on a table in the courtyard when he's working. Now go away.

I've got this little tracking spell I've been working on in my free time. Should be able to pick up on the trail we're looking for.\n\nI'll need to concentrate on Federo's letter as I'm casting the spell. You'll watch my back while I do that, right?

One concerned the Pact Primordial. Could they be seeking a way to subvert that ancient restriction? The second mentioned lost dreams, such as the one Torvesard seeks to recover. It told of a place in Apocrypha to find such misplaced memories.

The pact refers to ancient laws that bind the Daedric Princes. No Prince may physically intrude in another's realm. Everyone knows that. Well, perhaps not mortals.\n\nThat they sought out the tome tells us something important.

Mortals are quite skilled at picking up garbage, aren't they? Anyway. This fabric tore off a Voidprowler's tunic. I grabbed for it as I fell. We'll use this to track the thieves.\n\nThis notebook … I knew it! They did follow me from Fargrave.

The mortal knows very little about Skaafin, yes? My mirror shows me other places in Oblivion. Usually places I've already been to.\n\nThis time, I used that junk you found as an anchor to the Voidprowlers. That lets the mirror show me where they went.

They're a Dremora clan. Ignore the exciting name; no one sees them as more than petty brutes.\n\nSince anyone in Apocrypha probably has a secret or two, the Voidprowlers can easily steal them from the unsuspecting.
Our leader. Pushed us to raid the Forum. Quite the bounty, he thought.\n\nI told him—the Darkreaves live in there. They'll tear us up. Now look.
Not personal. He works for Whim. She has the juicy stuff. Valuable.\n\nWith that and the score here, maybe we'd get our own fortress.
Vicious guards. Crazed. Attack on sight. Unless you're a book.\n\nYou're with the runt. Zavaal's still in there. If you go after him? You'll die, too.
Pfft … mortals. It was a joke. We don't die.\n\nThis just hurts. I'm ready for a new body.
The longer we wander aimlessly, the more likely a swarm of Darkreaves tears us apart. This is impossible. I suppose I'll prepare myself for another thousand years of serving Madam Whim.

Now you're giving me orders, can Hezehk ever make a decision of his own? Yes, of course, let me do as you wish. \n\nHmm … it does appear the leader was here recently and we might find him in that large room below us.

You don't understand. Secrets want to hide. They change appearance to blend in. Hezehk bets this one looks like a book now, because, look around!\n\nWe can't find one secret among all these tomes. No, I'll just have to go back to Fargrave.

No, all I see in it is my pitiful face. Just how Madam Whim must see me. Wait. Hold on. Lost items.\n\nYes! How could Hezehk forget? I know a spell. It reveals anything that's lost. It's … it's how I met Madam Whim. But I need reagents.

Yes, that's right. And I need to do this. To reduce my debt, of course.\n\nI'll need perfect concentration, so don't bother me! Head down into the hall. When I've located the secret, you should collect it.

While Hezehk knows what he's doing, I might not get this right the first time, so you'll need to be patient. \n\nI'll call out the location of where I think it is and you go there and look for it. When you see it, collect it for me!
No, you hold on to it. That thing has caused me enough trouble. If the Darkreaves attack us on the way back, Hezehk might lose it again.

Madam Whim wants me to deposit that secret at the Intake Maw. That will purchase her a Boon of Mora.\n\nI need a moment to recover. Go back to the intake room and drop this secret into the Intake Maw. I'll be right behind you.

Mortal, you and I are different. Madam Whim, me, probably most Daedra, we like our secrets. It's what we're comfortable with.\n\nYou can go tell your feelings to whoever you want. Hezehk wants no part of that.

That big insect-like Daedra. Don't underestimate them. Inferniums are really smart. We have a book about them back in the hall. If I remember correctly, they managed to take down one of the Xivilai clans back in the First Era. Caused quite a fuss.

It's not. And I couldn't care less about the Telvanni. House full of arrogant arses. I'd put each of them to the blade if I had the writs for it.\n\nThis is strictly business. The assembly took out a writ. I'm here to enforce it.

My calculations could contain errors. I am a purveyor of entertainment, not a mage by trade. Impromptu spells aren't my strong suit.\n\nIt's possible that as I open portals to send my creatures to Fargrave, anomalies may arise.

Did she? Not the first time the port master sent someone to fetch me. \n\nBut you can tell her I won't be much help today. I fell ill after inspecting the Stormwing when it arrived in port the other day.

Shadeya kept pushing to leave. Eilirsu-dro insisted we stay.\n\nAnd then he told her everything. The relic. The thief. Secrets we swore to keep. He spoke on the Eye's value to the Baandari. But she heard only the promise of coin.

Intrinsic forces govern events on Nirn. Some are constant—like the force which compels objects to fall to the ground—while others defy prediction and categorization. The Probabilis allows for willful manipulation of such forces.

The Painted Eye breached the door to the inner laboratory. They are close to the Clockwork Probabilis, and Apostle Nilphas Drethan is with them. \n\nI will use the security measures to hinder them, but we must protect the Probabilis.

It is a prototype. A precursor to Lord Seht's great work: the Throne Aligned. If Apostle Nilphas Drethan activates the Probabilis, Nirn will suffer destabilization. Loss of life will far exceed acceptable thresholds.\n\nSafeguards breached ….

Cottages. Taverns. Sign posts. \n\nThe only time I've ever been caught on a job was by a Khajiit house slave. We didn't speak. He pointed to the two lamps in the window. I showed him my two axes. He left me alone. Guess I wasn't who he was waiting for.

After losing my memories, the place I came to in Valenwood is crystal clear in my mind. There was a campsite. Small fire, provisions, one cot. Two lanterns.\n\nThinking back, I've seen them other places, too.

He wouldn't. At least, I thought he wouldn't.\n\nBut you saw that note on that body. Three times promised pay just to bring me in. I guess I can't blame him for selling me out, if that's what he's done.

I don't want to think about that right now.\n\nThis can't be all there is. There has to be someone who can give us answers. There was another name I saw—Mevei. In Ald Isra, right? That's not far. If we can find her, maybe she can tell us more.
Sharp's resistance always captivated the Reformer. It was as if perfecting that link and conquering Sharp's will was his greatest trial.

Gorne belongs to House Indoril, as you'll see when we reach their sprawling estate. I've heard they formerly used the island to house the mentally unstable and magically insane. But I don't know whether it's still in use.
You should know that you're talking yourself out of my memoir. Imagine the prestige you could gain in Telvanni lands for being the loyal and capable servant to an esteemed mage.

Steal is so vulgar. I much prefer material sourcing. And I'll have you know I did plenty of research. For example, the going rate for capable mercenaries such as yourself. A tidy sum well worth your time and effort.

The Itinerant Staff is powerful and power is corrupting. So we will limit what it can do. \n\nThe staff can remain the symbol of leadership. But, from now on any scribe who crosses a rift is responsible for their own safe return.

The Umber Glyphic gave us much security. But, recent events have shown that it cannot be trusted with the scribes. \n\nThe glyphic shall remain a mystery to scribe and spider. As his last act as Magnastylus, Keshargo will send it away for safe keeping.

I thought I could set it aside whenever I wanted. But the damage is done. I can't return to the way I was before, even if I wanted to. There's … not much of me left.\n\nGaralo Givyn may be a fool, but he doesn't deserve this. Warn him. Please.

It showed me the sinews of the planes. The strings of magic threading together all existence. Oh, it showed me how to open portals to any corner of reality. But it brought me never-ending unease. Maddening curiosity.

She's the pinnacle of a Scribe of Mora and staunchly upholds our duty to Apocrypha. \n\nMore importantly, she's experienced one of the worst calamities to ever befall the scribes. She'll know how to avoid this situation in the future.

I don't know her. She was the last one Reynila freed from the Reformer before she died. \n\nWe were enslaved under the Reformer together. The way she tells it, I was like a brother to her. But I don't remember any of that.

The thought of reliving the memories I have of Sondivel already has me digging my heels in the mud. But you'll have to suffer through them, too.\n\nThere's no one else I'd trust more with this, but you need to tell me if it's too much to ask of you.

If Sharp's mind is a blank scroll, and his memories are like ink, touching tyranite calx directly would be like upending the bottle—a mess.\n\nYou will act as the quill. His memories will flow through you as we transcribe what once was written.
We have to go after her, but that's exactly what he wants. He knows I can find him, because it's what I'm best at.\n\nIf we want to save her, we're playing right into his hands.

Not anymore. Don't see the point.\n\nI used to make up stupid stories about where I came from just to, I don't know, entertain myself. Chase off loneliness. Want to guess how many involved me being a slave? None. Not a single one.
What? Where did you—?\n\nIt does not matter. Give it to Shadeya, now!

Keshargo will offer his assistance as an advisor. There are many secrets she must learn—the entrance where we met being only one of them.\n\nMany qualities of a leader can be taught. Mazandi's shelves are filled with the ones that cannot.

I am. Keshargo has been my Magnastylus ever since I joined the scribes. To think that he'd give it up … to me? I'm happy, of course, but also this is an enormous responsibility. I don't know if I'll be able to perform the duties correctly.
What was that? No! Curse you, thief!
With so many hands grasping for it, someone must pay well for it, yes?\n\nShadeya is losing patience. Toss it over, now!

Keshargo mentioned the Umber Glyphic? If it's as dangerous as he said, Zilipif will be the one to transport it to safety. The Itinerant Staff's an incredible tool, but its power does not define the Magnastylus. I'll make my way without it.

I suppose I'll have to learn how to lead the Scribes of Mora. I know which duties Keshargo performed, which responsibilities I saw him take. I guess I'll start there. But I won't be able to do it alone. I'll need Keshargo's help. And Zilipif's too.

The compass is the answer. If anomalies appear while I'm casting, you must use the compass to repair them. Since I'm linked to the compass, it can redirect any stray energy back to me.\n\nSimply hold the compass to each anomaly so I can repair it.
Then let's get started. Stay close. Portal magic is either perfectly straight forward or extremely complicated. Depends on the mood of the universe, I suppose.

The Telvanni are one of the great Dunmer houses. They focus on magic and the arcane arts, and they consider power, ruthlessness, and ambition to be paramount. We must be careful in our dealings with them, for they are nothing if not dangerous.

Yes, but I could not learn much. Just that he owns this tower but has not been seen in some time. The place is considered abandoned.\n\nHe was a Telvanni magister, the highest rank in the house, second only to the archmagister.

Even as a Mnemonic Fabrication, I know that many will take issue with my work. Nilphas Drethan tried to reconcile his beliefs with reality and his answers fell short. He leapt to false conclusions, as he was always going to.

Mnemonic Fragments store memories. I sought to use the memories to create an artificial animus. Alas, all I was able to achieve was the appearance of a fully developed soul. I am a convincing lie—artificial, perhaps more than Protus.

I could not. Just as he could not stop himself from committing this act. Cause and effect are matters of fact.\n\nNow that the Drethan event is concluded, Protus will receive new safeguard directives. When we are through, speak to Protus.
It sounds like she's settling in well to her new life. She's found her people, and I've got you.\n\nI could try. I just don't want to disappoint her.

Ah, this again. You may not have met me yet, but I've met you. I am quite familiar with you and your meddling antics. Now let's focus on the matter at hand.\n\nIt's very important that I don't miss my chance to access Mora's fated glyphic.

Well, I didn't know that. This friendship thing is still new to me.\n\nAfter it's done, I might need some time to process everything. You might look at me different. I might feel different. But I don't want anything to change between us. All right?

Hmm. I collect arcane relics, f'lah. It's something of an obsession of mine. I send the Dusksabers to recover a great many things.\n\nA glyphic, you say? I'd have to check my ledger. There are so many items on my list.

An appeal to my vanity? How charming. And clever. We Telvanni think highly of ourselves and enjoy sharing.\n\nI'm an accomplished mage, as you might guess. And I have more than earned the right to wear a master's hood. In fact, I should be a magister.
The next rank up in the house, which will allow me to challenge the archmagister. I expect to be awarded the rank soon enough.\n\nNow, don't you have a tower to break into?

Forces beyond your understanding ordained that I must come into possession of this glyphic. Since Hermaeus Mora rarely lets such a valuable object leave his personal collection, I simply charmed the Watchling into misplacing it.

Of that much I'm certain. I'm sure his notes will show me how to make use of it. Remarkable. It seems we've stumbled upon Gorne's true treasure, adventurer. I don't suppose you'd let me test it on you?

Pity. The rigors of magical academia aren't for everyone, I suppose. I've grown quite fond of you. We could have had a wonderful career together as magister and quill fluffer. Or paper fetcher? I had a list of fun titles prepared, mind you.

Yes, yes, I deceived the Watchling. How morally gray of me.\n\nListen closely. You need me to locate the glyphic for your Daedric friend. However, the nemesis looms make my presence here tenuous. If you can shut them off, you'll help everyone.

Corrupts its owner? Oh. Was this the cause of Dreynis's deterioration?\n\nI suppose his research notes alone would serve for publication. It might be rash to expose a mind as important as mine to the prism's affliction.

I've spent years hoping for the chance to study an artifact such as this. Now? I'm not so sure.\n\nI certainly can't leave the prism here. Someone else might claim it, and my place in House Telvanni. So perhaps I lock it away. Or destroy it?

Thaddeus Cosma. A traveler on tides of time and reality, but it really isn't important.\n\nThat's not to say I'm not important. I am, but that's neither now nor when. All you need to know is that when our paths cross, reality itself may be at stake.

Sorry. I guess I've been here so long, it's become normal to me.\n\nSathile said the outside world would kill Nathyn, and she was working on a cure. But as far as I know, she and her husband were trying to cure the Knahaten Flu.

He died years ago, when Nathyn was just a baby. From the disease they were trying to cure.\n\nSathile must be sheltering Nathyn for fear of losing him, too. She's doing it out of love. That I can understand. But that doesn't make it right.

Spores? The researchers spoke of those. Little seeds on the air, invisible to the eye—like flu or fever. I think that's how molds and mushrooms make more of themselves.\n\n"Delmon Spore Sample." Delmon, Delmon. What is that? It sounds like a name.

It sounds familiar, I just can't place where I've heard it before.\n\nShe mentions these toxic spores interfering with wards. Does that mean Nathyn's wards? If these spores reach the isolation tower, he could be in danger.
Mistress Dreloth. She coaxed him back to isolation.\n\nDelmon … too strong. Stronger than I've ever seen.
That must mean the isolation tower. Where Nathyn is.\n\nLet's keep going. I don't know what we're going to do, but Sathile needs to be stopped.

No, that's just the trouble—if Nathyn had said or written it, I'd probably remember it exactly. Delmon, Delmon. It's on the tip of my tongue.\n\nWhere did Tun-Shei say Sathile took the subject, again?
Delmon? \n\nWhere did you hear this name, Delmon?
If you mean to heed Sathile's words and leave, then I'll have to go on alone. \n\nNathyn is my whole world. I'm not leaving without him.

My father, yes. The affliction my mother gave me. She named it after him. \n\nI didn't know until I tried escaping—the wards were never for my protection. They kept others safe from me. If I had left with Dacia when we planned, she'd be dead!

Then she can make herself useful and help me find a cure.\n\nI'll hire her on again. I need someone dependable to procure rare ingredients to keep testing possible cures for Delmon Mycota. Perhaps someday she can be one of my researchers.
A platitude, but still you are correct. I followed my only course of action.

The progression of time is linear. It expands in both directions at a fixed rate. Nilphas Drethan activated the Probabilis, therefore it must be functional so that it could be activated.\n\nDo you think leaving it the way I did was irresponsible?
There are no cultists here. Only my Dusksabers and the defenders Meln the Mouthless left behind. But I am curious about how you are acquainted with Torvesard. Where did you encounter him?
Of course.\n\nI cannot promise you satisfaction, only that I will answer as truthfully as I am able.

In some quarters it's impolite to ask about such things. I'm a Telvanni master—I know many Dremora. My dealings with them are not your concern. But if you must know, I had no part in whatever happened in Necrom.

He is mortal. Mortals can be swayed to endanger the security of Kemel-Ze. I'm sure Thoryn Armas will quickly be assigned to another sacred site. Do not fear for Thoryn Armas. \n\nI will maintain this laboratory on my own. It is my duty.

Without Nilphas Drethan to guide them, the Painted Eye's presence here will dwindle until the halls are quiet once more. \n\nI will work with the security systems in order to drive the Painted Eye out.

Find a way into the tower and breach Meln's defenses so I can recover the book I seek. You can then attend to your business … with the gratitude of a Telvanni master.\n\nSo what do you say? Do we have an agreement?

Hmm. A capable adventurer might be just what I need. The wards of Tel Rendys are intended to keep out other Telvanni wizards, myself included. And since my Dusksabers are stymied, I have a proposition for you.

I'm so glad you asked!\n\nThis shrine has stood since the dawn of the Second Era in honor of Saint Vorys the Immolant, patron saint of House Telvanni. I am the high priest, and I oversee the care of our most valued relic, the Talisman of Saint Vorys.

Saint Vorys believed that we honor our ancestors through the forceful expression of will over others.\n\nThe gem within the relic exemplifies this belief. It was claimed in conquest during his march across Elsweyr.
Stand a bit closer and find out. This one is quick with her blade and does not hesitate to stick it in those who ask for it. Pray that won't be you.
Bother someone else if you're looking for a job, walker. This one's band has no room to cut in another share. These pedlars can barely afford us as it is.

I took steps to prepare for this possibility. The benefit of shutting down the nemesis looms was twofold. It allowed me to maintain a more stable presence in this realm. And it unhindered my spellcasting abilities.

We'll take the glyphic's remains to the Heart of Underweave. There, I should be able to siphon enough energy to restore it. But be prepared—the Heart may be heavily guarded.\n\nBring what's left of the glyphic and meet me there, meddler.

We assist Hermaeus Mora's Daedric servants in the creation of books holding secrets. The Seekers compose the texts. Mortals help prepare the materials. Sometimes, after decades, a mortal is allowed to work as a copyist in the scriptorium itself.
That's what I like to hear. Leave no stone unturned and all that.\n\nCome back out here when you're through.
Have you finished searching the Dres camp? I hate to send you back in there, but I really do need every possible bit of information.\n\nIf you think there's anything else to find, go grab it.
Good. We're getting close. I'll be able to wrap up this writ in no time, thanks to your help, hero.
The Lark gave them to you, did he? Why? Everything he's done today has questioned what I thought I knew about him. Including putting this choice in your hands.

Head back to Ald Isra and talk to Aki-go at the servants quarters. Find out what the servants know. He and I worked together before, so I know he hears a lot. \n\nDon't let him turn you down, though. His nerves get to him sometimes.

So it appears that an aide or servant leaves messages for House Dres at the kagouti nests to the north, using the musk to keep from being attacked.\n\nFirst, go to Tel Huulen and update Master Sulis. Then we'll check on those nests.

We assist Hermaeus Mora's Daedric servants in the creation of books holding secrets. The Seekers compose the texts. Mortals help prepare the materials. Sometimes, after decades, a mortal is allowed to work as a copyist in the scriptorium itself.
Well, better get to it. I need to get back to Tel Huulen and see if I can spot anything out of the ordinary going on with the mouths or masters.\n\nSee you soon, hero.

Now that's interesting. Certainly worthy of the efforts of a spy, depending on the nature of the project.\n\nLet's you and I keep this to ourselves for now. See what else we can learn about this secret project.

The Daedra attacking Vanton exists only in nightmare. But Vanton's power might be enough to bring it fully into this plane.\n\nWarlock Vanton was studying the Dreamstone. If there is anywhere a nightmare creature can hide, it's in that relic.
He's being plagued by a creature of nightmare called Ansuul the Tormentor. Vanton's as stubborn as a foot fungus, but even he can't hold on much longer.\n\nThe things I've heard about Ansuul ….

Mostly, we'll do our best to keep Ansuul's influence from spreading. If Vanton starts to fall, Ansuul may be able to reach out into our minds.\n\nThe hope is that you can beat Ansuul back and we can return her to the Dreamstone without anyone dying.

Unequivocally. Ansuul the Tormentor is a master of mental manipulation and feeds on anguish. Vanton's mind is her domain now. She'll be extremely powerful in there.\n\nIf Vanton falls, she can use his magical power to escape into our realm.

They're friends, but Vanton can be reckless. He's lucky Twelvane has been keeping an eye on him. Studying the Dreamstone without wards? What was he thinking?\n\nTwelvane is the only reason we got here before Ansuul destroyed him.
<You are about to enter a Trial. Are you ready to leave your current Zone?>

We're worried about what would happen if the Daedra's plan succeeds and it enters this plane. If the thing plaguing Vanton infects anyone else …. It's better if we send someone else to help Vanton. \n\nSomeone whose mind isn't at risk.

Destroy it? Without knowing the magic it possesses? Without fully comprehending the power it holds? No. \n\nI agree the relic is dangerous. But that's why only the most accomplished Mages Guild members should deal with it.

He asked to study it. None of us thought he'd be foolish enough to do so without setting protective wards first.\n\nI don't know Vanton very well, but Wizard Twelvane speaks highly of him. I hope this doesn't destroy his mind entirely.
I … don't know. \n\nWe will do our best to shield you from Ansuul's control. But you could be trapped inside Vanton's mind. Stuck in a nightmare reality forever. Or—you could die.

That's the thing. We don't know. \n\nAnsuul's a powerful Daedra. Apart from linking her victims to the Dreamstone, we don't have any records of how she gets into her target's dreams. We're going to be overly cautious and not repeat Vanton's mistake.

Ansuul is a creature of nightmare who serves Vaermina—mistress of the sleeping realm. Neither care much for mortals, aside from using our fear for their own purposes. We believe Ansuul is trying to enter Mundus. No one wants that.
I had hoped to see some change in its nature from your own forceful expression of will in returning it to us.\n\nBut you handled it so well—perhaps its retrieval was not as forceful as I thought.

I get it. Tredecim uses the kagouti musk to help get close enough to the nests to the north without raising the ire of the beasts. We need to take a look at those nests.\n\nFirst, though, we need to update the masters. Go tell Sulis what we learned.
We shall mourn those we lost and leave the lands of the Telvanni. \n\nWe hope to come across another caravan of Baandari soon and trade for supplies, as we have run rather low.

This one wishes to mourn those lost. But we must make haste from the lands of the Telvanni.\n\nEilirsu-dro is ready to leave the Eye's obsession to the Dark Elves. It has cost this one and his family too much to reclaim.

Not much. I remember that note we found in the Reformer's old lab saying he'd only ever tested tyranite calx on Argonians before.\n\nBased on the location of her hideout, I'm guessing this Starflower is setting up to go after Khajiit next.
He does? Let me see. That's a relief.\n\nThis Starflower might have thanked us for sparing her the obligation of answering the summons of this spineless flat-head.

Assembling metaphor. Dreaming … steaming kettle. Sunrise. Metaphor complete.\n\nThink of Kemel-Ze as a clock. The fragments are the gears which keep the clock running. As with a clock, the fragments are connected to the whole and to each other.

Surprised you remember that. This time, I'm going to use the essence of the tyranite calx and follow its natural resonance to find more nearby.\n\nI figure where there's more, that's where we'll find Sondivel.

I stopped caring about my memories the moment he took Dimik-ei. What use is remembering our past if she can't be part of my future?\n\nAnd the Reformer doesn't get to live on in my memories. That's enough for me.
Dimik-ei has found a place with her tribe. I think I might want that for myself someday.\n\nBut not today. Probably not anytime soon. So I guess your question should be—what's next for us?
Response

You saw that memory of mine. I have been ready for longer than I can even remember.\n\nHe needs to die. But as far as priorities go, saving Dimik-ei and any other slaves under Sondivel—that's more important.
Spotted a fragment at Elistrenne's place. Didn't touch it. Kept it wrapped. Figured it might be useful to have.\n\nTake it, and set it down in the ritual circle when I tell you to.

I don't know if she'll ever know me the way that you know me, but it's worth trying.\n\nShe's a piece of my past. I was too focused on finding the Reformer to realize that. And now that he's gone, I have my whole life ahead of me.
I'll trust you to make that decision. You already know I'll follow you to Oblivion and back.\n\nBut I think we've earned a break. I wouldn't say no to a little fishing.
Response

Dreaming … sunrise. Netches suspended in air. Insufficient knowledge, Apostle Nilphas Drethan's motivations are hidden, never shared. \n\nPerhaps the recorded journals he kept will shed more light on this line of inquiry.

The Clockwork Probabilis simulates control over formative rules of existence. It is a prototype. Unfinished.\n\nStill, manipulating it will produce effects. And improving it beyond the bounds of Lord Seht's work? That could have untold consequences.
Interested, are we? Of course you are. No one can spend an hour in my company and come away without an appreciation for my intellect. Well, I'm awash with brilliant ideas!

Recording? Yes. Sharing? No. Our lord Hermaeus Mora taught us that there's power in secrets. I don't let Scrivener's Hall divulge the knowledge and treasures of the realms to just anyone. Not even the Magnastylus can waltz in here.
I am the keeper of the vault. The curator of the scribes. I know all that is recorded in the Scrivener's Hall and keep its secrets from prying eyes … light fingers too.

I'm the only one who holds the key to this gate. This is why the Cartoklepts are the greatest threat to our hall. They do more than just break into the vault, they steal from it. They must be stopped!

Valinna? That newcomer? She came by here once asking for some staff or other. Didn't even want to hear about the genuine threats the Cartoklepts pose!\n\nShe said she's our new leader, but at least Keshargo helped me deal with those impish thieves!

Return to Tel Rendys. Around my tower, you'll find the components necessary to assemble a passable cloak of omission. Look for dried hoax-wort, a lamia-scale shawl, and an illusion tincture of my own creation.\n\nI'll tell you more when we get there.

As Baandari, our travels take us wherever the roads may lead us.\n\nThe roads happened to lead us here, to this Sailenmora. We sought to stay at the grand outpost east of here, but it seems to be in ruins.

Of course not! I buried the components we need in separate caches on the tower grounds. I just can't remember exactly where I put them.\n\nNo matter. With your assistance, I'm sure we can find the right spots.

It may have pointed me in the right direction. I hope to present my findings to representatives of House Telvanni back in Necrom. They'll be eating out of my hands! I'll have to choose between all the offers and titles.
Shhhh! Don't speak of it so loudly. It's marvelous, truly marvelous, but no one else can know that it exists! I must leave no opportunity for it to be taken from my care.

If they ask, I'll simply say "But of course, my magister." If that old loon got results, then so can I. Soon enough, you'll hear my name from lips of strangers. I'll be remembered every time a portal is opened!

It's … strange. Wondrous. Almost ethereal. Already it seems to be revealing itself to me. I keep glimpsing tendrils of magic, just out of the corner of my eye. A remarkable artifact, truly. One that I can't wait to pore over.

She gave me lodging and fair wages, too. She was kind to me, in her way.\n\nI used to think it was out of some goodness of her heart that she took me in. After she dismissed me, I was left wondering if she even has a heart.

I used to ask myself that question every day. It all happened so fast.\n\nI had a big family in Cropsford. We fled east from Cyrodiil when the Three Banners War began. By the time I made it here, I'd lost everyone. I was on my own.

As in how we met? It's a bit of a silly story. I have a habit of whistling while I work. Songs from back home, to keep my mind busy.\n\nOne day, when I was working in the garden, I heard it—chords of Chim-El Adabal, coming from the balcony above me!

Nathyn started dropping notes for me in the garden. He folded them so beautifully to look like flowers.\n\nHe'd make up excuses to send for me. We'd stay up all night talking or reading. It took a long time for either of us to admit our feelings.

He'd never even heard it before. He learned it on the lute just from listening to me!\n\nHe would play, and I began to sing again. It was like Nathyn gave me my voice back. And I could think of home again in a way that felt like healing.

I placed sigils at the spots, but on a different layer of reality. Use my ghost sight and you should be able to see them. The caches are buried beneath those locations.\n\nWhen you get close to a spot I recognize, I'll tell you to activate my sight.

Use my ghost sight. It will reveal the hiding places. Remember, Tel Rendys is my place of power, despite Shelreni's attempts to make it her own. Here, I can easily use my magic through you. \n\nAs long as you're willing.

Did I? I don't recall. But if you're asking about the cloak of omission, it can only shield you from so many scrying attempts. Eventually, someone will notice you. But the enchantment should last long enough for us to get our hands on Shelreni.

Now that you mention it, yes. Gadayn can get you on the access list, but you must play your part. Dunmer laws are labyrinthine, Telvanni especially. You need to invoke the proper statute to avoid suspicion.

Just say the following to the sentry at the door. "I hereby invoke the twenty-sixth statute of the Necrom Agreement," and then demand entry to the conclave. Can you remember that?\n\nOnce we get inside, we can meet up with Curate Gadayn.

Necrom, hmm? Let me see … ah, yes. You're listed as Curate Gadayn's attending clerk. Very good. You may go inside.\n\nI expect you'll find the curate in the assembly antechamber as the attending magister declared the conclave for masters only.

Ah, and now we come to the problem. Magister Gothren arrived from Sadrith Mora to oversee the Masters Conclave. He immediately expelled all but the Telvanni masters and placed a ward on the door. There's no way to get into the assembly hall.
Sadly, disabling a ward placed by a magister is beyond my capabilities. If you have any ideas, please share them. Otherwise, I fear the masters are on their own in there.

You probably shouldn't, but that doesn't mean I'm lying.\n\nI admired Shelreni for her skill and power. Thought she would help me rise in the ranks. But her ambition and contempt for her fellow Telvanni will doom us all.

Master Shelreni made a deal with not one but two Daedric Princes! She plans to use their help to eliminate all who oppose her so she can become archmagister.\n\nThe masters won't listen to me. They don't understand the danger.

I'm not sure. Master Shelreni stopped confiding in me. But I know how she thinks. She has no respect for the masters or this conclave. When they move to reprimand her, she's going to show them just how powerful she's become.\n\nIt will be a bloodbath!

We are holy guards and warrior-priests, dedicated to serving the Tribunal Temple and the Living Gods worshiped therein. \n\nHere in Necrom, we tend to our flock in the Telvanni Peninsula and keep a wary eye on the portals to Apocrypha.
That depends entirely on what the High Ordinator deems necessary. But, there are more jobs than capable hands. If you survive, then I'm sure we will continue to have work for you.

Yes. Beyond their financial value, we ship these eggs throughout Tamriel under the Temple's holy seal.\n\nProviding a delicacy as delicious as kwama eggs to Dark Elves abroad reminds them of the generosity of the Tribunal and the bounty of Morrowind.

I am certain.\n\nThere was a time when the Camonna Tong prized subtlety, but this new generation of gangsters are little more than silk-clad street toughs. With the war raging in Cyrodiil, they just don't have to be as cautious. Or so they believe.
