I am … puzzled. Few beings detest the Daedra more than my lord, Seht. Yet he still seeks out their work. Sotha Sil is the Light of Knowledge. What would he need from the Daedric Lord of Secrets?\n\nIt is not for me to ask, of course.

We do not just publish ancient texts at random. Our libraries are full of epistles, saintly accounts, lost codices—some in line with orthodoxy, and some not.\n\nIn the wrong hands, these texts could sow doubt and apostasy. So, we exercise discretion.

Exceedingly. They're Daedric beasts with long claws, rows upon rows of gnashing teeth, and enough muscle to make a bull kagouti whimper. \n\nThere's a reason why we're paying someone else to gather their teeth.

Fathoms Drift is a ships' graveyard in Apocrypha. I've heard that some of the wrecks are floating in air, impaled on rock spires, or listing noiselessly on silent seas. It's unnerving, from the reports I've heard.

It is the realm ruled by Hermaeus Mora, and as such is a threat to the Living Gods and to us. In these lands, though, the veil between our plane and his is thin and easily pierced. We know of several ways to reach Apocrypha.

Hermaeus Mora is no friend of the Dark Elves, but we have sent agents into the Prince of Fate's domain, hoping to uncover hidden knowledge. We cannot go ourselves, so we employ paid agents, like you, to discover what lies beyond the veil.

Settling mine crises and labor disputes is the business of the Kwama Consortium, not the Temple. If the situation deteriorates to the point where Ordinators must intervene … well. Neither the miners nor the Consortium will enjoy it.
I doubt those Camonna thugs took the time to unload the parcels or scrape the labels. Look for crates marked with the Necrom merchants' insignia.\n\nMay the Three speed you in your search!

Do I think he would debase himself by wielding the artifice of the Daedra? Ha! No, I do not.\n\nRegardless, I would never question my god's plans. We are the instruments of his will. Secure these items and return. You will be well rewarded.

Beyond their threat to doctrinal purity? No. Not to one such as you, at any rate.\n\nTribunal sages enchant our more controversial tomes with scrambling runes. They inflict severe headaches on the reader, so I advise you don't look too closely.
Hidden knowledge is the currency of the Keeper of Secrets. The apostate sought to gain favor and status in his new faith by revealing our texts.

You won't have to fight the Dremnaken to get their teeth. \n\nDremnaken teeth grow and fall out from use. Most are broken from teething on old hardcovers. You should find some perfect, unbroken teeth lying around, if you hunt for them.

It's a place beyond the power of our Living Gods. It is filled with the spirits of drowned sailors and lost souls. It is a domain of the damned.\n\nBut do not worry. Your reward will be proportionate to the dangers of the task.

Last I heard Magnate Feina-Darak was still in charge of that little town. I suppose she figured out how to lead without relying on her family's lie. \n\nIf more people were like her, then I'd have less work.
I do what I can to avoid stepping into Vvardenfell these days. That business with Veya really mucked things up. Not that I had anything to do with that. Have you since met up with Naryu?
I have some answers, but let's not go on too long. As much as I'd welcome seeing Rilasi, I think it's best if we keep ahead of her for the moment.

She was on duty guarding the Library of Vivec when she almost caught me reacquiring a rare first edition on behalf of the original author.\n\nShe took it very personally, and she's been obsessed with catching me ever since.

I say this with love, but Nathyn's not a fighter. He's lived a sheltered life, and Sathile is a very skilled mage.\n\nBut he wouldn't fight his mother anyway. Until he met me, he seemed content with heeding Sathile's every word.

I'll see to High Priest Trilam. I'll assure him that you're in pursuit of our thief, and everything is going as planned.\n\nIf you don't manage to recover the talisman … well, we'll cross that bridge when we get to it.
Good question. I've never known her to be particularly combative. But if Nathyn's wards were any indication, she does wield very powerful magic.\n\nWhich she may use to … escort us out.
There are quite a few of us. \n\nYou likely encountered our prickly Madam Virian. I hope she wasn't drunk, she has a fondness for the wine within Necrom in particular.
You really think they'd have packed up all those tents and left in the time it took us to get through the crypts?\n\nNobody's that fast. Not even the Lark of Rosgard.
Happy to see me? That's not usually the reaction I receive. You're a delightfully odd one.
Conclusion: Affirmative. Imperative: Stop Apostle Nilphas Drethan. Protus Security Oversight: Error. \n\nProtus Assistance: Repair Required. Critical Components Missing.

Nathyn's well-being is a family affair, and the researchers are far more focused on their work. \n\nThey're tasked with observing their subjects for the slightest changes, so they won't keep their eyes on us for long, anyway.

No. And that's exactly what worries me—she's tested no cures on him because there's nothing to cure! He's not sick. She just wants control.\n\nPoor Nathyn. His mother loves him, but it's almost like she's the one with the sickness.

Test subjects for her experiments. Animals, as far as I know. Some of the experiments are rather grisly. I kept away from the lab for that exact reason.\n\nI've heard some of these Telvanni use slaves for such things, but Sathile's not like that.

Hmm. She writes about how Torvesard came to her, indoctrinated her into Vaermina's service. How he was consumed with restoring something that was either stolen or lost. And how he insisted they find this ancient shrine. Interesting.

This must be where that original memory took place. Where Vaermina and Peryite think Hermaeus Mora wronged them and stole whatever it is they now seek.\n\nLet's keep going. That restored statue and Master Shelreni must be somewhere in this old ruin.

So they sent the malachite mined from the Alavelis quarry here. And she discusses how the Hidden Kindred were formed to provide the workers needed to accomplish the restoration.\n\nSomehow, rebuilding a Vaermina statue is the key to Torvesard's goal.

I'd have been here sooner, but High Priest Trilam kept badgering me with questions. \n\nHe hasn't even realized his precious relic was replaced with a fake! When I got there, he'd taken it off the pedestal and was clutching it to his chest!
While there are lives at stake? I couldn't give a nix.\n\nIf you can go after them, I'll escort the elder here safely out of the caverns. Can I still count on you?
This one … misplaced his trust, and now pays dearly for it. Those who tried to fight back were killed.\n\nPlease, walker. None of this was worth the lives of my family. Save who you can!
Oh, I assigned myself this job. I often work separately from the others.\n\nThis region of Tamriel worries me. So, I took responsibility for keeping an eye on it.
Ah, of course. Apologies, cohort. We rarely have a chance to catch up.\n\nYour adventures are as stimulating as they are manifold. You certainly stay busy.

Well, I started with a simple question. How can we sew up the threads my experiment has frayed?\n\nThat led me to a metaphor. What if we could create a sort of mystic spool we could attach to the Key? Something to help in reweaving my fateline?

Spool is a terrible word. Let's not call it that. Perhaps … a bobbin? Azandar's arcane bobbin? Ugh. We'll keep working on it. \n\nPeerless observation though. Yes, we create a simple arcanomystical focus we can use to anchor the threads of fate.

Within loyal Gubbins, my most recent atronach, lies the nascent form of the bobbin. Just need to get it out of there.\n\nI've prepped an arcane stencil for you. Retrieve it from the rummage bin and imbue it with magicka from the font, please.

There was a time when any who walked through Apocrypha knew of us. We patrolled this realm for the thieves of secrets. Our reach extended to the mortal world, where we gathered any wisdom that deserved protection.\n\nWe were a force unmatched.

We only know a little. The Dreamcarvers caught us by surprise. They made no sound—no shouting, no crash of shields. Just a sharp feeling of loss as we fell, one by one.\n\nA call came to flee and rally nearby. We did not bother to stop running.

This mine is critical to the people of Necrom! Anchre's proximity makes it a boon to the city's markets. And we're not just talking about the food produced here. Every broken shell, every kwama gland, every shard of chitin has value.

Exceptional! Now to simply attach it to the Fateweaver Key … and there we are! Dear Martina's methods distilled down and improved by yours truly.\n\nLet's find a new round of frayed fates and put theory into practice!

Of course! Having experts who know the mine well will be essential for bringing the operation back up to speed, particularly given the cultists' mischief. Ulfengar saw those skeevers in action and can describe it to our alchemists firsthand.
Yes, of course! You are taking the lead down here, after all. Which part of the audit do you wish to know more about?

The scrying ritual highlighted the village of Kozanset, in the hinterlands of the Alik'r desert. It … ah. This is somewhat embarrassing. \n\nThat tiny hamlet is my home town. Where the impressive arcanist before you got his humble start.

The egg-hands use the pens to efficiently track and corral the workers and scribs to cut down on overcrowding and the dangers that come with it.\n\nIn fact, most production errors originate with the pens, so it's always a good place to check.

Naturally the overseer must, in triplicate, sign off on the state of the mine and provide records as to its upkeep and production goals. The Consortium will then review his records with my findings to root out any inconsistencies.

The importance? The queen is the mine. The workers tend her, the warriors defend her, and the egg-hands harvest her eggs and other byproducts for the people of the peninsula.\n\nKnowing her health is critical information for the Consortium.

The Telvanni Assembly of Masters meets there. Well, their representatives do. The masters themselves rarely bother to make an appearance. That is what they have mouths for.\n\nYou want to go to Tel Vara. The mouths work out of that tower in Ald Isra.

The masters leave day-to-day concerns to their mouths. Their own arcane studies are far more important to them. And they try to avoid direct interaction with their rivals whenever possible.\n\nThe fate that befell Meln is not an uncommon one.

Yes and no. My brother and his family still live nearby. But I haven't spoken to them since I left. I was determined to have conversations about anything other than what to feed the camels.\n\nIt's always some kind of grass, by the by.

No. Here our paths diverge. I leave Mouth Vabdru and Meln in your hands. While you pursue the spirit, I shall research the Black Book and contemplate the other threads of fate.\n\nI must determine how this factors into the threat against Apocrypha.

They are meant to deal with any thieves that should find their way inside. We store many of Hermaeus Mora's treasured secrets here, after all.\n\nWhen active, their power floods the entire Cenotaph. But that will take time.
I haven't the faintest clue, but whatever it was has done incalculable damage to the mine.
She was kind to me during my last visit. Workers aren't too keen on Consortium auditors, but she … well, she learned my name and I learned hers.
No, but he had a smile almost as glowing as his recommendations. Felt like he lit up the room when he came by the Consortium to turn in his paperwork.

This is the first I've heard anything about cultists. I've never known Ulfengar to exaggerate, so if he asked the Consortium for guards I believe him. As to why the Consortium wouldn't supply them, let alone give me a warning? It's troubling.

What does it matter, if she and Nathyn are able to live out their days together?\n\nI'd only prioritize curing her. But I am a researcher. I am not above recognizing the benefit of additional subjects with which to compare results.

My researchers signed on with me because of my area of study. They knew the dangers of Delmon Mycota, as well as its potential. All that space in the labs was necessary for safe experimentation.\n\nI regret their loss, but they knew the risks.

Or if I had time to think of a more believable lie to tell the both of them.\n\nI knew they had been meeting for quite some time. When I overheard their plans to run away together, I had to act quickly—or else risk Dacia's certain death.

I've been studying Delmon Mycota for over twenty years. If anyone can find a cure, it's me.\n\nI'm not about to abandon my life's most important work. There has to be something that can eradicate the fungus once it's disposed of the Knahaten Flu.

With it we may be able to calm the frenzied kwama. Keep them docile and working until we can find a new queen to bond them to or until they die off naturally. It's not a guarantee, but the start of a solution.

Master Shelreni never returns anything she takes. But if you're willing to scratch behind my ear, I'll scratch behind yours.\n\nServing Master Shelreni has become … difficult. I would prefer to find another role in Ald Isra.

Oh, I already have the perfect position in mind. I just need to show them I'm the best candidate.\n\nYour part is simple. Gather some papers from the servants quarters. Bring them back here and leave them on Mouth Delvi's desk. Discreetly, of course.

Ah. Master Shelreni doesn't discuss her work with me. Very well.\n\nTake the Tel Baro insignia from my office. You'll need it to unlock the wards, otherwise you'll never get through the cavern to reach the tower. She takes security quite seriously.

We tend to the affairs of the assembly on behalf of the masters we represent. Master Shelreni is far too important to waste her time in matters of house business. All the masters are.\n\nSo we mouths make sure routine matters never trouble them.

A better question is, do I think you're an assassin? Or do I even care?\n\nIf you aren't, there's no danger. If you are, well, Master Shelreni can protect herself. Beyond that, I'm not sure my master and I are still on the same path.
It's me! Or, well. A frayed version of myself. \n\nA version so malevolent and willful that it's thrown everything I thought I knew about this magic into the abyssal seas.
Back in the first era, before the Tribunal ascended to godliness, King Nerevar brokered an alliance with the Dwarves. Dumac Dwarfking gifted Sotha Sil a wing of Kemel-Ze as a sign of that alliance.

Magicks that are far beyond the scope of my understanding. Sometimes, the Telvanni masters try to access the wing to see what Sotha Sil studied, but we have defensive measures in place to keep them from seeing too much of his research.

Oh no. He's much too busy. \n\nNow, most of Kemel-Ze belongs to the remaining Dwarven machines. Nilphas and I care for Sotha Sil's wing. Nilphas oversees Sotha Sil's experiments, and I keep thieves and miscreants from the doors. This is my fault.

Remember, I was a Telvanni magister. Still am, as a matter of fact. One of the most powerful mages in the peninsula. And I've dealt with Hermaeus Mora before. And Shelreni. Don't you think my counsel will be worth listening to?\n\nWell, it is.

A violent group. They take what they want and do what they want with what they take. I don't know why they stormed Kemel-Ze or even how they found out about it, but they started looting the outer laboratory as soon as they broke through the door.

I'm not sure. I don't even think they knew. Usually organized violence has someone there to oversee it, right? When I fled the underground, I didn't notice anyone who was in charge. Seems strange to me.

Let's focus, cohort. Perhaps later we'll have a dram of gormapple schnapps together and toast the old homestead.\n\nFor now, we need to find those frayed fates and sew them back into the fabric of reality.

How could you possibly think I'd know something like that?\n\nNow, if you'll excuse me, I have sacred items to collect. Best not let any Painted Eye stragglers find Lord Seht's world-altering projects. Give my regards to Thoryn.

Written? No, that work is reserved for the Seekers. Mortal scribes in the Wind simply prepare materials. Rare ink, special parchment and leather, alchemical glue. I've spent years brewing the ink for a single page of a book I will never read.

Yes. Each one contains a secret Hermaeus Mora has chosen to tempt or test mortals, as well as a doorway to Apocrypha. Those who study a Black Book learn something few others know. And they gain access to the Great Eye's domain.

Yes. The secrets they take into their minds change them. Their bodies mold themselves to follow. They become warped.\n\nMost Hushed go about in silence, lost in their own delusions. But others can lash out in unprovoked violence at any time.

That mystic phenomenon I was struggling with? I'm calling them frayed fates. They're echoes from a choice I once made. \n\nMy work to create the Fateweaver Key has snarled them up. So untidy. If I'm ever to perfect the key, I'll need to unfray my fate.

A good question! I need to … reset. Return to the roots of my research to unravel this issue.\n\nThat's why I'm hoping to find my old colleague. Their name was Martina Abor, a talented researcher … though we've since parted ways.

My hope is that a Daedric consultant, a Watcher named Tem, will know where they are. The book will lead us to Tem, you see.\n\nThankfully the Ciphers of the Eye have given me access to their stacks! Hah!

Here's the ritual to summon Tem. Easy enough, just a question of the appropriate summoning materials.\n\nWe'll need expunged tomedust, the talon of a Seeker, and black ichor from the spumy pools of Apocrypha.

Let me mark your map. Seekers tend the flora of the region. Their talons often break off in the resin. \n\nAnd there should be plenty of tomedust scraped from parchment in the Cipher's Midden expungatory. Try to get some from a Daedric incantation.

She did! That waif of an Elf may have been a shivering mess in the mine, but with a quill in her hand she is as fierce as any warrior.\n\nBy the time she was done writing up her account of the mine Consortium officials were begging us to stay on!

The good captain here will lead the assault to clear out the tunnels. In the meantime I have Malsa and Barluk recruiting new egg-hands and sourcing a replacement queen.\n\nThere's a long road ahead of us, but for once we have all that we need.

All that and a cask of Riften rye if I asked for it, hah! They promoted the two scribs back there which is good because I'll need their help.\n\nAnd Cindieth even has the Consortium compensating the families of those lost. That's a kind gesture.

You're observant, my friend. We keep an eye on the Telvanni Peninsula and now Apocrypha as well for the Temple. It's more than anyone can handle alone. We've many dangerous, well-paying jobs available for teams of talented adventurers like yourself.

He is one of Hermaeus Mora's strongest servants who lurks in a cavern in Apocrypha.\n\nHe tested Lord Vivec's mettle ages ago. Of course, our lord prevailed, but Vro-Kuul-Sha forgets nothing. Now, he's unleashed eons of hatred on these Armigers.
It's a powerful minion of Vaermina, Daedric Prince of Dreams. It's made of warped dreams incarnate, with insect-like legs and an eyeless skull. We need to know more about it.
Dek is a high-ranked leader among the Dreamcarver Clan. He's set up a base of operations in Apocrypha with a host of his less-powered Dremora. Efforts to discover what he is up to have so far failed.

The Prime Cataloger is a particularly obsessive Seeker that hoards forbidden knowledge—hiding secrets from everyone, even its fellow Daedra.\n\nOver the ages, it has grown in size, cunning, and power, making it a particularly dangerous foe.

Regrettably, we don't know much about Xiomara. He wields power unlike any we have seen. Not only of souls and magicka, but of knowledge. Without access to his tomes and codices, we are left to wonder.\n\nSuch blind spots are unacceptable.
Corlys the Chainmaker is a showman who runs a fighting club of sorts. He imports rare and dangerous creatures. Would-be warriors pay him to fight them.
I didn't think anyone would save us! The horrors! I'll never forget them! Thank you.
I'm at a loss. I'd given up hope of being rescued.
The things he made me see … I need to get as far away as I can.

This was before Vivec's apotheosis, when he still labored under the burdens of mortality. The stories say it was a brutal fight, and Vro-Kuul-Sha almost bested him. But in the end, even a mortal Vivec was unbeatable.

Rathas Favel, a young scholar that had recently joined our ranks. He was a headstrong youth, and I think he was just a bit too eager. I hope he was able to make some decent observations before he met his untimely end.

The Dreamcarver Clan swears allegiance to Vaermina, Prince of Dreams and Nightmares, one of Hermaeus Mora's rivals. Why would Hermaeus Mora allow these minions within his domain? Our people could not find out.

Lord Vivec wishes to understand all potential threats to the Tribunal Temple and its people. The power this new arcanist wields is such a threat, and it must be dealt with now. Before it gains purchase in Tamriel.

True servants of the Temple take all threats to the Three and their people seriously, including the Daedric Lord of Secrets. But our need is your gain, my friend. We pay well for others to take care of these issues.

No doubt! Ulfengar and Cindieth have been true to their words, Barluk's back on his feet, and the Consortium saw fit to give us a raise once the mine opens back up!\n\nIt's nerve wracking, but in a good way, yeah?

Well, yes and no. I might never be able to look at a kwama the same way again, but Anchre holds good memories too. I'll be more relieved than anything to hear that it is cleared out and that we can step foot in it again.

Good! Cindieth made sure I was looked after by the best healers the moment we got back to Necrom. The city can be a bit creepy with the death fixation, but their healers know their craft.\n\nAnd guess what? Ulfengar is making me head of the pens!
Ah, that? Nah. The thing about working with animals is to know they're animals. Can't fault them for lashing out when those cultists broke in. They were likely just as scared as we were!

No longer overseer, but yes. After the way the Consortium treated us, the dead, and Cindieth, I'm glad to turn my back on them.\n\nAt least the latter has decided to join us. Smart as a whip she is, and the Consortium would have ground her down.

You're as surprised as I was. After seeing the true bloodsucking nature of the Consortium, she decided her skills were better suited elsewhere. She'll help negotiate contracts, write up deals, handle finances. She even sounds excited about it.

Ah, no. After the fiasco at Anchre and the Consortium's inability to do what was decent for the survivors and those lost, I decided to part ways. Let's call it ideological differences?\n\nFortunately, the good overseer offered me a job!

Traveling the world is my hope! Ulfengar is confident my talents will be put to good use, though. Negotiating contracts and making deals and the like.\n\nI'm nervous, but also exhilarated! Working alongside honest friends will be a change!

Not too bad, friend. Ulfengar knew a healer in town and they were able to help fix me right up. Which is good because I'm already starting to get the itch to get back to work. Not in Anchre of course.

I won't lie and say I won't miss my little bugs but I could do a lot worse than have Ulfengar as a leader and mentor.\n\nMalsa and I are in good hands, and even Cindieth is tagging along! I think there's nothing but good in store for us.

Dangerous? In the wrong hands, perhaps. But each Black Book is a secret Hermaeus Mora has chosen to give to mortals. A tool that can be used for great change. The Lord of Knowledge has a purpose for every one he directs his Seekers to create.

To work as a copyist or embellisher in the scriptorium. Only a handful of mortals are ever chosen to put quill to parchment in the Great Eye's forbidden tomes. Perhaps I might even earn a glimpse of a Black Book.

A mortal who lived in the days when Dragons were worshiped as gods, or so it's said. Hermaeus Mora opened Apocrypha to the First Servant, and he's been here ever since. Spinning plots and gathering power. Sabinius must have fallen into his web.

Nothing. By tampering with Quires Wind, the First Servant set himself against the Great Eye. If Hermaeus Mora still has a purpose for the First Servant, he'll spare him. If not, he'll destroy him.\n\nIt's out of our hands.

I used to have to go to Federo's place to get paid before I convinced him to start utilizing dead drops.\n\nTried to teach him how to fish once or twice. It didn't take. He always tried to get me to go drinking with him instead. Can't imagine why.

Well, I'm not working for him anymore, am I? I keep a low profile when I'm not spending time with you.\n\nMaybe he's set up a trap for me at his place. Or maybe the Reformer made him disappear. I don't know. Guess we'll find out.

How should I know? We weren't close. He was just someone I worked for.\n\nSo there's no reason to hold back if we need to shake him down for information when we find him. Especially if it's clear he's decided to keep working for the Reformer.

He'd be stupid not to. You remember the Reformer was offering three times the promised rate to his mercenaries for my capture, right?\n\nAll Federo ever wanted was to get rich and climb ranks within House Telvanni. Turning me over would get him both.

Peerless work! Let's see … here's the ichor. Unpleasant to gather, but I've done worse in my day. \n\nNow then. I'll light the fonts and begin the incantation. As we go, I'll need you to offer up the tomedust, talon, and ichor. In that order.
Just so. With any luck this Tem can tell us where the whims of fate have led Martina. \n\nIf this doesn't work … well. I'm sure I'll think of something. But let's hope it works eh? Onward!
Hah, that's the mark of a valuable partnership! When researchers are so closely aligned in thought they're able to finish each other's … erm.

Well, as we learned in Kozanset, frayed fates are most likely to appear at locales where I spent a considerable amount of time. That said, I'm not quite sure what I … did in … Stonefalls. \n\nOh, Mora's many eyes. Damn it!

Ahh. Nothing wrong per se. But I just remembered what I did in Stonefalls that might have resulted in weighty choices made.\n\nI was just starting out as a field researcher, still coming into my power as an arcanist. My inquiries were … misguided.

I chugged half a firkin of moon sugar and stayed awake for four days reading the Sermons of Vivec. At the time I hoped to gain some new insights into ancient magics.\n\nIn any case! We know where to go. Onward and upward. To Ebonheart!

Well, I should hope so! I've been coming here for years. Fascinating place!\n\nYou can learn the ways of the arcanist back home, of course, but to truly understand the forces of fate, tides, and the abyssal sea … there's nowhere else like it.
Oh here and there, you know. You've seen one post-feudal city-state you've seen them all. Am I right?\n\nMy family hails from Hammerfell. Born and raised in Tall Papa's shadow.

I'm no youngster, obviously. My parents now dwell within Aetherius and the rest of the family politely pretends I don't exist. Best for all involved.\n\nNow then! We have a Daedra to summon, knowledge to gain!

Full disclosure, cohort, no. I'm trying hard to maintain my sunny disposition and halcyon personality. \n\nI swear I can feel Dreugh pedipalps upon my skin. And my adversary … what is his plan? It's vexing.

As I said, divergences in the threads of fate call to me. My purpose is to correct those digressions, examine the contradictions and rectify them. I can't leave until I succeed.\n\nDon't ask me why. There is no why. It simply is.
It's … is it a show of strength? No. He's me. This has some purpose. He's gathering power. But to what end?\n\nMy initial enthusiasm for experimental results seems increasingly inappropriate.

Let's away to Malabal Tor, the Ayleid ruins of Ilayas. I spent some time there, years ago.\n\nBoring though it was, it's likely the location of my frayed fate. Hopefully we'll find some clue to the adversary's plan.

Do you mock me? I detect a note of mockery. I should reduce your brain to rotten cheese for your temerity. Eh, but what's the point? What's the point of anything, really? Just know that I can summon a mighty strike when fate requires it. Very mighty.

Alavelis? Or this tedious mortal plane? No, don't tell me. My answer's the same in either case. It's a dust mote, populated by delusional insects whose meaningless lives seem important to them.\n\nI can't bring myself to care.

Something special about a mortal settlement? Hardly. Alavelis fails to stand out from the sheer mediocrity of a thousand similar places in this world. Until the followers of a Daedric Prince seized control of it, anyway.\n\nWhich may be something ….

Not what I want, but what I need: a new life. New name, new identity, new clothes! \n\nI heard there's a document forger in the Adept's Retreat in Windhelm. Work out a deal, then meet me in the Outlaws Refuge. I'll tell you where I buried the cache.
The parasitic tomeshells feed off the Prime Cataloger and gain some of its knowledge. When these tomeshells shed their skins, these papery husks reveal that knowledge.
No, but he sometimes turns his creatures loose on the countryside to drum up business. We want him stopped, and we want to know who his suppliers are.

You mean besides the dead devotee of Hermaeus Mora? Hmm. They call themselves the Hidden Kindred. Since I could see them, the nomenclature must be ironic.\n\nI also noticed some Daedra. Dremora of Clan Dreamcarver, sworn to serve Prince Vaermina.

A rhetorical question? Must be. Very well. Vaermina is the Daedric Prince of Dreams and Nightmares.\n\nI also noticed Peryite followers among the Hidden Kindred. Before you ask, he's the Prince of Pestilence. Never heard of such an alliance before.

Of course he did. Mortals always get the special titles. But who winds up doing all the work? Usually, that's me. Well, as long as we're both here, we might as well work together. What's the worst that could happen?\n\nNever mind. I already know.

Peryite and Vaermina, working together? That could be the source of the disturbance in fate. The mortal who summoned me spoke of nightmares before he died. I was just about to start my inquiries when you arrived.\n\nPity you don't have more tentacles.

The mortal who summoned me complained of terrible nightmares before he died. Beyond that, I was just about to begin my long and grueling investigation when you arrived.\n\nIf only you had more tentacles. It would make the work go faster.
Uxunath steals our defining feature. The thing that makes us Remnants.\n\nOur mental web, the connection that binds us. We believe it is more than a means of sharing knowledge. It amplifies us.

The Remnants keep watch on many of the other clans. Our calling is the defense of Apocrypha, after all.\n\nWe once had agents across more realms that a mortal's mind can hold. Perhaps we can regain that reach once more.

I am Scruut! A powerful servant of the Great Eye. Creatures of my Daedric order call ourselves … it doesn't matter. Everyone else calls us Watchlings.\n\nAn insulting diminutive, but I expect nothing more.

I have no clue. When my master exerts his power in this plane, the consequences linger. Footprints in the malleable clay of fate that harden to stone with the passing ages.\n\nI sense that events here run counter to something my master did long ago.
You know her? Master Shelreni didn't stay long, but she sent an overseer who started hiring workers immediately. Master Shelreni said she wanted the mine reopened as quickly as possible.

In the dream, they were building an arch in the mine while we dug out the glass and stone. What wasn't used for the arch was sent to restore a statue, at least that's what the overseer said.\n\nWe woke each morning exhausted, hands bloody.

Hmm. Am I? No, not particularly. Daedra are strange beasts, you know. Their concept of mortality, time, and danger are very different from our own. \n\nClearly there have been some unintended consequences, but nothing the two of us can't handle!

We were excellent collaborators. Together we gathered power from across the Daedric realms! But in the end she had very different goals than I do.\n\nIf nothing else, damn it. I want to have some fun! Hah!

You must understand. I have been studying arcane ephemera for decades now. The Underweave is just so … obvious. And I try very hard not to be boring.\n\nPlus it's extremely dangerous in there. Fate shifts like the tides of the abyssal sea.
The Fateweaver Key is palpitating, pulling me … off to the east? Fascinating. Something in Martina's sanctum must be synergizing with the relic.\n\nLet's find that laboratory!

I prefer to keep an eye on House Telvanni. They worry me. That's how I recognized when they disturbed the temporal flow around Bal Sunnar.\n\nTypically, my order doesn't interfere directly. Something like this requires a little more.

Stone's Blessing. That's what the name means. The Dark Elves constructed it centuries ago. Placing it here with the surrounding mountains keeps them hidden away.\n\nRarely do people come in and out of this town. It's quite a strange mystery.

Even among the paranoid houses of Dark Elves, the Telvanni excel at secrets. I've seen them act with keen savagery.\n\nThey have a reputation as masters of the arcane. But this knowledge comes from cruelty, not calm study.
It's time to put my failure behind me! So far, the fates have come to me. \n\nWith Martina's research we can scry for one, find it, and shut it down! What do you think of that?

Are you not acquainted with the concept of the Daedric Princes? The most vast and powerful of all the Daedra and the rulers of the realms of Oblivion?\n\nHermaeus Mora is the Prince of Fate and the master of Apocrypha. He sees and knows … everything.

No one of consequence. Just a simple scholar who made a bargain with a Prince more than a century ago. In exchange for glimpses of forbidden knowledge, I occasionally undertake missions for Hermaeus Mora.\n\nNow hurry. Forces gather while you tarry.

A curious fetish, is it not? Legend has it that this petrified, rune-covered tentacle was a gift given to a priest of the One Who Knows, sliced from his own body.\n\nAcquire the glyphic, then use the talisman. It will open a portal to return you to me.

Doors in Apocrypha lead to secrets and knowledge. Something this Torvesard saw in a dream? Is that why Vaermina is involved? I suppose we should investigate the mine next. Just make sure I don't get mutilated.\n\nReconstitution is so unpleasant.

Hmm. Black Books open doors to Apocrypha, so why do they need a gate? Still, Telvanni masters are powerful. That makes her dangerous and important to the Hidden Kindred.\n\nBut why go to all this trouble? It's impossible to sneak past my master's gaze.
Hoarvor Pit is a cave in central Malabal Tor teeming with hoarvors. Many adventurers have fallen to these blood-sucking creatures.\n\nAn entrance to the vault waits somewhere in its depths.

Rootwater Grove is a bog in western Greenshade that conceals a library of secret knowledge. A cult that calls itself the Wooded Eye maintains the site. One of the entrances to the glyphic vault can be found there.
Ondil is an ancient Aldmeri ruin in central Auridon. Plague-infested peasants patrol the outskirts surrounding the ruin. Be wary if you decide to use the vault entrance located there.

Doors in Apocrypha lead to secrets and knowledge. Something this Torvesard saw in a dream? Is that why Vaermina is involved? I suppose we should investigate the mine next. Just make sure I don't get mutilated.\n\nReconstitution is so unpleasant.
Excellent, proxy. Hermaeus Mora chose well when he selected you for this delicate and important task.\n\nNow go. The fates of multitudes, both in this world and beyond, hang in the balance.

The Remnants have acquired these relics while gathering secrets for Hermaeus Mora. They either made our jobs easier or could not be left for anyone to find. So we gathered and stored them to keep them safe.

I'll mark the location on your map. It's not far from here.\n\nYou're really going after the Reformer, aren't you? I'd wish you luck, but I think Sharp's used up all that in finding you. I'm going to need luck more than you two. Courier! Psh.

We shall stitch together the unraveled threads of my fate. Mistakes made in forging the Fateweaver Key will recede into the past.\n\nTogether, we will reap the rewards of knowledge, insight, and scholarship. Just as Martina would have wanted.

Are you not acquainted with the concept of the Daedric Princes? The most vast and powerful of all the Daedra and the rulers of the realms of Oblivion?\n\nHermaeus Mora is the Prince of Fate and the master of Apocrypha. He sees and knows … everything.
Hello, Sondivel Ulres. Let's see what a piece of work you are ….

Fine. He's a crazy Telvanni, but we knew that. Right?\n\nWell, we have the approximate location of this lab of his and a key to get inside. Sondivel wants to meet in person so badly. Let's see if he's there.

I have no idea. I took it from one of the vampires, but it's written in some sort of code.\n\nYou're working with Leramil the Wise, aren't you? One of the Great Eye's favored mortals … despite her lack of faith. She might be able to decipher it.

The Sodality of the Eye is a small fellowship devoted to the Great Eye. Who you call Hermaeus Mora. He directed us to guard this vault until you arrived, and we have fulfilled our mandate—despite the deaths of so many of the devoted.

The Dusksabers are mercenaries from the Telvanni Peninsula. Someone hired them to reach the Emerald Glyphic and acquire it before fate's chosen could do the same.\n\nI don't know who they work for, but the letter I gave you may hold the answer.
It's entirely possible some dangerous artifacts are still kicking around in there. Most don't know how to use them. \n\nBut I do. Which, in all likelihood, probably means ….

If he's here to expand on my Fateweaver research, I imagine we'll find him in the Ametric Interval Chamber. It's at the heart of the ruins.\n\nBe ready for a scrap. I took pains to keep a low profile but together we'll likely attract attention.
Yes! I mean, would I prefer this adversary enjoy a strenuous argument over a pot of tea? Without a doubt.\n\nBut you have to understand, I believed the Fateweaver experiment was an abject failure.

Indubitably! And mark me well, this discovery would not have been possible without your insights and abettance. We make a superlative research duo, you and I.\n\nI haven't had a competent cohort in some time.

To erase me, replace me, and inflict the power of his dark Fateweaver upon our world. \n\nCohort, knowledge was the gift that allowed me to strike out on my own, to travel Nirn and beyond. To see it twisted like this is sickening.

If they escape before we catch up to them, then we do what they did. Use the Pool of Inquiry to find them. The waters contain a record of everything in Apocrypha—which now includes these enemies of the Great Eye.

Just a band of like-minded travelers performing odd jobs across the planes. You know. A little light exploring, a bit of harmless smuggling, a pinch of heisting ….\n\nA bunch of busybodies if you ask me. Or, at least I am.
Think of it as a small bundle of twigs nestled into the branches of Oblivion. A lovely little nest of connections and pathways into, and out of, other realms frequented by Daedra and mortals alike.

A time existed when the Remnants had no home. We served as wandering knights for our lord.\n\nThen, as if flung through the void, this castle landed within Apocrypha. We took this as a gift and soon occupied it.

I believe you are familiar with the Onyx and Umber Glyphics. Currently, I carry them. We need them at the shrine to formalize your arrangement with Hermaeus Mora.\n\nUnfortunately, I am not one of the faithful. Only his followers know the location.

I leave the supplication and exaltation of the One Who Knows to Dralys, Bassian, and their ilk. My association with Mora is strictly professional.\n\nNow come, proxy. Time is a precious commodity when the fate of two realms hangs in the balance.
Precisely! We have worked together long enough now that I feel quite sustained by our companionship.\n\nI do my best work at your side, these days. Exemplary work, if I do say so myself.
Um, not my intention. But certainly!\n\nI'm partial to a nice shakshuka or some of those Wayrest crepes, if you want to get some food later.

As I conducted my own investigation of Leramil's treachery, I discovered that someone was hunting the Prince of Forbidden Knowledge's faithful. Naraheida is … was … a friend. \n\nI wish I had gotten here sooner.

Is that where his investigation has led him? To a conclusion as inaccurate as it is absurd? What do they teach the followers of the Prince of Secrets these days?\n\nMy interests lie in accumulating knowledge and saving two realms. Nothing more.

It is said to be the Prince of Fate's scriptorium and bindery. Here his minions toil eternally to craft perfect volumes for their lord. Only those without flaw are brought to him, and he imbues them with power. Those volumes become the Black Books.
We cannot stand being alone. Dreamcarver magic squirms through our mind. It wants our secrets. It wants inside.

The invaders found a way to enter Apocrypha undetected. Perhaps they hope to open a path for one or more of the rival Princes? That would be disastrous!\n\nThere's nothing more we can do here. It's time to exit the Tranquil Catalog.
We no longer feel their presence in our mental connection. The Dreamcarvers have learned a way to isolate us. Severing us from ourselves.\n\nSuch a process, it seems, drives us to madness.

The vampires? No, they are merely hired blades working for another ambitious mortal. I refer to the new patrons that Dralys chose over me. The Daedric Princes he pledged himself to. He died before I could pull their identities from his mind.

Because this shrine is one of the few places on Nirn where I may manifest. Where I may communicate freely for a short while.\n\nAs Leramil explained, I require your assistance. Help save Apocrypha and you will also preserve Nirn.

Know that the Prince of Secrets addresses you, chosen of fate. I can observe through my Watchlings' eyes, speak through them. Even act through them when necessary.\n\nYou and Scruut uncovered a threat before even I became aware of it. That concerns me.

Right. It's a connection that goes both ways.\n\nIf we can find more of that metal—that tyranite calx—there may be a way we can exploit it. That's it! If we find more, we can use it to track down Sondivel. Somehow.
I'm Naanurrel, captain of the Opulent Gale. My son's been restored to me! We must complete the pact before this gift is taken back!
These all belong to my father—the locket, the spyglass, and the logbook.
Not my fault you can't understand. I got lost in the books. Now my words are scrambled. Like Kwama eggs!\n\nKnowledge, truth, facts, they're not what you think they are. Don't go looking for them.
I watched my son swept overboard. He would drown in the storm. I appealed to a greater power, but didn't complete the ritual. We must finish the task lest he perish again!
You must sacrifice three tokens from my past—logbook, spyglass, and locket, at the Unquenchable Brazier near the entrance to the sea caves, to seal the pact. Do this for us.

That's an aspect of our beliefs, but not the primary component. And it's different when you visit the catacombs and a spirit appears before you.\n\nI suppose if Shelreni decides to speak to us, that shouldn't violate the codex too badly.

Indeed. The recently departed are often confused. And that confusion can turn violent.\n\nI much prefer to deal with the spirits of our ancient ancestors. They may be cantankerous, but they've had enough time to reconcile to their undead existence.

Aetherius is the Immortal Plane. When a person dies, their spirit moves on to that realm unless something prevents that from happening. A violent death, perhaps, or because the spirit still has tasks left undone.\n\nShelreni fits both categories.

What Hermaeus Mora foresaw was always about an assault on Apocrypha. Vaermina and her allies want to recover the memory that was stolen from them. But the way she is going about it will doom us all.\n\nWe need to determine her destination and stop her.

You know how you can feel the warmth and know the sun is above you, even if you never look up? That is what Scruut experiences every day in the service of her master. And what I sense when I commune with the One Who Knows.\n\nNow it just feels empty.
Forgive me. What I had managed to do for my son came at a great cost. The others … did not make it, I'm afraid.
To be honest, I'm not sure.
Where isn't she? The ciphers have eyes everywhere. They watch us. All the time. \n\nWe should go to Frielvi's study. It's through this door and if we don't wander off, we'll be there in no time!

You have seen the wandering souls shambling on these shores. I have been charged with guiding them home. But I must seal the pact, lest Herm'us Mora take back my son! Take my belongings and burn them at the brazier!

Oh, this. I got too chummy with a certain Argonian associate of mine. All I did was put a hand on his shoulder to get his attention.\n\nApparently, it was the wrong move. He let me know with a nasty swipe of his claws.

No, just thank him. This scar gives me a subtle air of menace that has done wonders for my business.\n\nI don't hold it against him, but the same can't be said for my bodyguards—so I suppose it's for the best that he keeps his distance.
I suppose you're right. Still, I am left to mourn a loss that did not have to be.
Odd. Things feel familiar but distant. I remember you, and almost drowning, and washing up on shore. But there's something else. Something deeply important that I've lost track of.

He always thinks that. My plan was to stop the Dreamcarvers before they got to the Forbidden Exhibits, but you can see how well that went. Those bastards—so many unique creatures … gone. \n\nWhat do they want? The Known Thing?

The barrier. Right. The truth is, it's weak in the Forbidden Exhibit—which is why the Cephaliarch placed Seeker sentinels there.\n\nHermaeus Mora wants Morian trapped, he never indicated that he wants Morian dead. Help him. He doesn't deserve to die.

Seekers defend the more permeable parts of the barrier, but they're distracted by the Dreamcarvers attack. You might be able to get around them. Not sure about the Keeper of the Box.\n\nThis is his best chance. Don't waste it.

Now why in the name of my despicable ancestors would I even consider such a notion? You're my enemy! I'm content to sit back and watch as Vaermina and Peryite steal back whatever they think Hermaeus Mora took from them.

I decrypted Meln's Black Book, perfected Blightcrown's subterfuge concoction, and performed the rite that gave Vaermina access to Apocrypha. And all for a simple favor—eliminate my competition and elevate me to the rank of archmagister!

You know nothing of the Telvanni, outsider! Or of me. But I will admit that I hate it when a greater power reneges on a mutually advantageous agreement. Frankly, my role in all this was more difficult than what I requested of the Princes.

The Infinite Panopticon? First they sought a memory to alter, now they seek … what? Another memory? And can they even find the entrance again?\n\nWell, we have a destination. Now all we need is a plan.

What research I was able to accomplish tells me that Vaermina will be a formidable opponent. But in order to enter Apocrypha without Mora's consent, she requires an anchor and a shield. In this case, Master Shelreni's body.\n\nThat will be her undoing.

Shelreni's body is mortal. If we destroy it, I do not believe that even Blightcrown's concoction will hide Vaermina from the One Who Knows.\n\nOf course, there is also the matter of Apocrypha gone amok, but one problem at a time, I think.
The spyglass is my father's. He would let no one else use it, and took meticulous care of it. These cracks are new. They radiate from a single point, as if it witnessed something truly horrid.
This is my father's log, from the Opulent Gale. It's where he'd track our voyages, noting the weather and the navigational heading. Except for these last few entries. They're … odd.
Yes, the locket! This engraving is of myself as a boy and my mother. He rarely let this out of his sight. But this, this symbol on the back. It wasn't here before.

This hardy thing has seen more years of use than I've been alive, and never had a single scratch.  For it to not be simply scratched, but cracked like spiderweb—no, what he saw was unfit for mortal eyes.
Yes. I've seen it on charms the other sailors carry. It's Herm'us Mora's sigil. But why is it scorched onto my father's locket?
The Forbidden Exhibits. I always knew I was going to get in there.

I was going to go ask the Known Thing if it wanted to help me escape, but there are Seekers. They make … noises. \n\nThe entrance is southwest of us now. If we pretend to be sneaky mice, maybe the Seekers won't notice us. Can you be a mouse?
It's all strange symbols and personal entries at the end. And there is something else, written by someone else. The last note is addressed … directly to me.

Plan? I don't plan. I jump before looking and hit the ground whenever it wants to meet me again.\n\nHmm. Known Things turn Seeker minds into runny-nose soup. If we open it and point it at the Seekers, then they'd be the toad brains. Oh this is perfect!

If you're worried about dying or losing your mind you'll never learn anything useful! I survived a Known Thing and look at me.\n\nSo, what do you say? Are you ready for a lesson? It'll be the most important of your life.
Yes. Listen. "I cannot condemn you to the depths, my son. I must do the unthinkable. I am sorry." He was afraid I would die. And I remember being swept off the ship. I'm not … dead, am I?
Right. Then why did he apologize? And this other writing—whose words are these? "The pact is made." Father, what did you do? What deal did you make?

I have no clue which memory of Hermaeus Mora this particular eye contains. But we should go in and do what we came here to do. Find Vaermina and destroy Master Shelreni's body. Without the protection it provides, Mora should be able to pinpoint her.

He's one of Necrom's only crime lords. Big fish in a small pond. And he knows everybody, so I'm certain he knows Reynila. \n\nI've worked for him before. We're not on bad terms. But I wouldn't go to him if I had any other choice.
What? My story? I tell you to make it quick, and that's what you decide to ask me?\n\nTry again, or get moving.

You're right, I don't hear the Great Eye. I think that has something to do with Vaermina's presence, Blightcrown's corruption, and the rite they completed to enter the realm.\n\nIt's just a guess, but if we solve one problem, it should help.
Its significance is that Harn Orenvi is a double-dealing, dishonest, conniving s'wit!\n\nI'll give him what he's asking for. And a piece of my mind with it!
I'm not stupid enough to get myself into debt to Harn Orenvi, you fetcher. He's blackmailing me for—\n\nNever mind what it's for! Get out of my face, now!

Please. The Lark of Rosgard, enlist an accomplice? That fetching glory-hound would never.\n\nThat "fetching" wasn't in regards to his looks, by the way. His mask prevents me from making any objective assessment. What else did you want to know?

Shh! It's a secret. No one can know. I can't even know! I hid it from myself and now I couldn't find it even if I tried. It burned, you know? Felt like a star was falling through me, changing everything. \n\nI wonder what this one will be like!

I'm Rilasi. I'm a Buoyant Armiger, and I serve the will of the Tribunal. I'm fully aware that I may be more straight-laced than other Armigers you've met. No need to remark on it.\n\nMy standing orders are to apprehend the Lark. That's why I'm here.

I can detail the charges of his past exploits once we've caught him. Arrogant fetcher might even tell you himself.\n\nSee, he has to evade me every time. I only have to capture him once. By Vivec, and with your help, today's going to be the day.

I know a Known Thing. It made my eyes bleed and gave me an extra toe. Knowledge is power. Power is dangerous. \n\nMy advice? Eat your vegetables, read books, and don't listen to the whispers in your head.

Many things. Planes-walker, prisoner, teacher, student, friend, enemy. The multitudes in me contain smaller multitudes. I hear them sometimes, the multitudes. They whisper. I wish they'd stop, but you can't tell what isn't there to stop talking.

In short, I haven't. They're Baandari Pedlars—a group of nomads with a bit of an unsavory reputation for theft.\n\nHigh Priest Trilam thinks they have something to do with the intended theft of the Talisman of Saint Vorys. I'm not convinced.

Aside from you? There was one other. An elder Khajiit who asked many questions. Without, I might add, the judgmental sneering typical of most outsiders.\n\nI cannot recall his name, but he was alone. I've heard the dangerous ones only travel in groups.

You think we've reached that point in our relationship where I smile, wink, and divulge all my deepest, darkest secrets? Hero, you couldn't handle that sort of revelation.\n\nJust do the job, get paid, and you never have to see me again.
Vaermina hasn't been in here very long. She didn't have time to craft a perfect dreamscape to hide within. Look for flaws in the illusion. The cracks in the facade.

Good idea. If you can find the weak points, I can break them open and expose the true memory beneath.\n\nOf course, knowing what the Great Eye values, that will probably drive us insane. Took me centuries to recover the last time that happened.

Testing one's will on the talisman serves as a humbling reminder that forceful expression of one's will is an unending journey.\n\nSailenmora used to be a haven for aspiring Telvanni, pilgrims eager to test their mettle. But alas, those days are gone.

Not stole—claimed in conquest.\n\nThe shrine is dedicated to exercising our forceful expression of will. We hope to someday unravel the hidden mystical properties held by the gem that eluded even the great Saint Vorys until his death.

Most come to visit the crypts. Few stay to properly observe the majesty of the relic. I cannot understand why.\n\nAdmittedly, we have had an influx of visitors since this Lark character announced his intentions to steal the talisman.

Not just any glyphic. One of three primordial glyphics that in total contain the entirety of the memory I made everyone forget. A memory that, if restored, will destroy reality.\n\nEnter the vault. Check on the glyphic.

That which I cannot see. The corruption coursing through Apocrypha continues to weaken me. I must do everything I can to maintain a connection to my realm. Enter and examine the glyphic. I give you permission to gaze upon this portion of the memory.

Examine the Glyphic of Hidden Paths. It will reveal its portion of the secret to you.\n\nRegrettably, there is no other way to determine if the glyphic remains intact. But fate will survive a slight fraying of its fabric. It has to. Now go.

No, no. Just thinking out loud. I need to see this through. I promised to recover the other half of the Fulcrum Obscura, and I really want to help Leramil. Oh, and you, too, friend.\n\nThe end of reality as we know it is not something to take lightly.
Find Blightcrown and beat him with a stick? \n\nHow should I know? I'm an auditor of fate, not a Watchling of action. That's for you and Leramil to figure out.

The Sidereal Cloisters chart the stars to predict our futures. Through orreries and century spanning studies, the ciphers here weave starlight itself into the fabrics of fate. And because of this, the information in these walls is fiercely protected.

I'll admit to slightly embellishing. One can't walk into the Cloisters and leave with their fates revealed. No. Years of study are required. But should one want the secrets of the stars? Their paths and predictions? Well, that must be protected.
The pact was with Herm'us Mora, who sleeps with his secrets in the depths. I had learned an incantation to entreat with him from an ancient sailor, and inscribed the summoning into my logbook.

Aren't we all? The lord of eyeballs watches us all and lets us stay here in Apocrypha, in the gallery … in our own minds. I've been locked in my mind so long that I can't find my way out.\n\nI used to be something, you know? But now I'm different.

She knows where mine is, it's only fair. Her study is all right, but it's worse than my enclosure. I, at least, know I'm trapped.\n\nThe powerful wiggly one told me that I'd never leave. My ears were still ringing from the Known Thing, but I heard him.

The Cloisters represent centuries of fate-scribing perfected. The magics at play here translate the very stars above us. Primordial predictions that, should they be misinterpreted, could cause dire consequences across all the planes.

I ensure that no tome leaves the Cloisters without my master's permission and that the ciphers are able to continue their work unimpeded. An interruption such as this is troubling to say the least. Being unable to act does not suit me.

Our last adventure helped to focus my efforts. I believe the adversary is anchored to my fateline by defining moments in my life.\n\nThat's what led me to the Unraveling Palimpsest. Bit of a cheat, but it wouldn't be the first time. Heh.

Just skimming past some nonsense about my inner self. Serenity, inner peace. Ah, here!\n\nMy research was correct. It seems the adversary is anchored to my fateline by specific moments, particular choices. We can use those anchors against him.

It will require an uncomfortable delve into my past. Prepare yourself. We'll have to acquire a trio of artifacts that represent hinge points in my life.\n\nThe first is a bloodstone to represent my time with dear old Spellwright Nilvon, in Balmora.

An Aetherial Rubric. I made one studying with the Star-Gazers. Nonsense I left behind near Belkarth. \n\nWe'll also need … Nathriin's Commentaries. A rebuttal of a treatise I wrote during my time at Shad Astula. Not looking forward to that.
Of course! They're all, well. Personal representations of my past. Totems.\n\nEffigies of past failures, you might call them? What would you like to know?

It's technically a calx of Alessian solvents, but no one calls it that. The Balmoran alchemist I studied with, Nilvon, is one of a handful in the world who know how to make them.\n\nIt's the perfect representation of my studies, and failures, with him.

It's an instrument. The Star-Gazers believe it can allow them to interact directly with the Celestials. Codswallop, of course!\n\nBut the underlying magical principals in their work have been instrumental in my own research.

Elydrina Nathriin, one of my tutors at Shad Astula. During my time there I wrote a treatise called "The Fate Dialectical." She took umbrage with my assertions, and wrote an extensive rebuttal. \n\nI thought it was drivel. Now … it's key to our plan.

Of course you are. It's always about what he needs. Or, rather, what he wants … what that man needs is a different thing entirely.\n\nWait … I'm sorry. I'm not being fair to you. My professional relationship with Azandar was brief, but intense.

Much the same as you, unless I'm mistaken. He's … well. He's brilliant. And that brilliance draws people in, like a moth to a flame. Just as blinding.\n\nBut I digress. You said you needed a bloodstone?

No, and it vexes me to no end. Being forced to observe Meenai-Shai's endless stumbling is a torture more potent than I could imagine. Perhaps with your help I'll finally be freed from this blasted cycle.

Perhaps you have come across our kind in your travels before?\n\nNo matter. We are traveling merchants, seeking to sell our wares in all corners of the land. This one was born on the road, and has traveled with this caravan all of his days.

Shadeya and her mercenaries are not, though they would be welcome among us if they desired to be.\n\nOur clan opens its arms to those who wish to follow the way of the Baandari. Very different from what this one has seen of these Telvanni, yes?

This one has seen many years pass, and wearies more easily of travel. He thinks just this one more night will do well for his aching bones.\n\nYou are welcome to join us, walker. We have food and tents to spare for those who share our company.

To protect the planes? Or, to covet the knowledge for himself? It makes no difference. Though, I am certain there is a way to release us. After all, even Mora wouldn't want to lose the Cloisters to an endless loop. It'd be a waste.

Hm? Died? I don't know that I did. After all, here I stand in one piece. Though I suppose death can encompass a great many things. A change in self, a departure from the old. Perhaps we can compare notes after we are finished, hm?

You mean other than the fact that I have a writ for someone named Tredecim who apparently doesn't exist, that House Dres has a nearby camp, or that I want you to question a servant named Aki-go?\n\nWhich of those would you like me to spell out for you?

A truth so powerful it can melt the mind of anyone who's exposed to it. Morian's the only mortal I've heard of who survived a Known Thing.\n\nIf they find out, the Dreamcarvers might see Morian as more of a threat than the other exhibits.

Well, I am carrying a satchel of magical odds and ends that may not react well to frost or fire. And Vorm doesn't have the tendril muscle mass to lift an egg, much less a book. So, that leaves us with you. A very capable and friendly adventurer.

You've been down there! Half the projects I've got cooking could level this city!\n\nPlus, I'd bet a sackful of glyphics that plonker is hoping to do to me what we're trying to do to him. He means to overwrite my fateline with his.

Hey now, I wouldn't put you directly in harm's way! It may make a blizzard feel like a warm kiss, but when it comes to avoiding scorching flames and volatile magic, it can't be beat. So long as you make it quick, of course.

Ever hear of Takubar? Absolutely dreadful place. Colder than a scorned shield maiden and twice as bitter. Place is abundant with these shards. Damn useful, really. Keeps the canteen cold. Just, don't let it touch your skin.

We can, but it would take time we don't have. By that point, Skywatch could be a smoldering ruin.\n\nWait. If I were doing this, I'd focus the runic threshold at a single point. We might be able to slip under his shielding at another location.

Exceptional inquiry, cohort. The ruins beneath the city extend out into the countryside. There's a side entrance to those ruins in a cave called Entila's Folly. \n\nIf we can reach that passage, we can enter the sanctum.

All tomes kept within the Cloisters hold significance to our master. I cannot yet glean the connection between these, but they appear to revolve around the forecasting of the future or the interpretation of omens. Perhaps you're onto something.
My master revels in the search for knowledge. It befits him that undoing this trap would slowly reveal what tripped it. We should investigate this vision and see what we can learn from it.

I'm so certain, it would make a Sapiarch blush. You know, it's funny cohort.\n\nI reached out to you because I firmly believed that I'd failed. In truth … the Fateweaver experiment was a smashing success!

The key was the final anchor to my fateline. With the runeform applied and the Fateweaver Key destroyed, the adversary has been banished to … well.\n\nHonestly I'm not quite sure? But I feel confident wherever he is it's deeply unpleasant.

Because I'm an Armiger. I should delight in such a grand and poetic experience. But no matter how clever or prepared I am, every chapter against the Lark ends with me playing the fool.\n\nThis refrain only ends when I beat him for good.

The replica, you mean? I know what the Lark said, but I actually have principles. A code I try to live by.\n\nI can downplay the caravan's involvement, but I'd have to tell the truth about my actions. I've caused enough trouble already.

He must be, otherwise I would have never made it out. If I had to guess, there's a lot going on between the eyeballs right now. Why worry about me?\n\nIf I am being watched, it's because I'm more entertaining out here than I was living in there.
Become a secret even from the secret keeper. Keep changing and never swim in the sea of fate. Read not to learn but to alter. \n\nExist everywhere and nowhere and never climb on the bookcases.
Without reading every book? Ha!
Old habits are dead but I'm an idea necromancer. \n\nThis new exhibit of mine is bigger and has more books— I think I'll enjoy being trapped here.
I've always known Meenai-Shai to be a dedicated cipher, but he isn't without his faults. For instance, it seems he is extremely gullible.

The people working for the spy. That's my assumption, at least. When a dagger flew past my head, I took off.\n\nLook, you don't want to know any more about this. You don't need details to deliver a letter, and the more you know, the greater the danger.

It's just another Telvanni town. It's claim to fame is that the Assembly of Masters congregates there.\n\nLook, I'm from the other side of Morrowind. I just had orders to meet my contact here and deliver that letter. Want to know more? Ask a local.

We don't have time for this! Look, the name is misleading. Telvanni masters never assemble. Instead, they send their assistants—the mouths—to represent them. So, it's really the Assembly of Mouths, but no one wants to call it that.\n\nCan I go now?
Took them to the ruins. The relic is the price of their lives.\n\nToo late for me, walker. Please … find the Lark. Save the others!

Just as Gadayn told me, then. The Fulcrum Obscura. The Hidden Kindred are well named. Although I understand you prevented them from escaping with the complete relic.\n\nLet us move on. What happened after we parted ways at Tel Rendys?

Ah, I believe I see. The relic must be the key. The secret Vaermina's servants sought in Apocrypha is the location of the dream. And the Black Book is needed for the rite they plan. Clever.\n\nSomeone put them up to this. But who?

Oh, sure. Within kissing distance every time we've met. The only reason she hasn't yet is luck, plain and simple.\n\nBut you'll never see me admitting that to her. Better to leave her thinking I'm at least one step ahead.

I met Eilirsu-dro with a bounty on my head. He could have turned me in for the payout. Instead, he welcomed me into the caravan.\n\nAnd that story of his ancestor tricking Saint Vorys into coveting the Eye of Baan Dar always stuck with me.

The Baandari believe that favors should be passed on, not repaid. The Lark of Rosgard was born from that idea.\n\nStill, we both always wanted to reclaim the Eye of Baan Dar. So we planned it, with some trickery of our own.
Reacquire. Not steal. \n\nAnd no. The only things I keep are memories and my notorious name.

Leave that to the customs of the Baandari. His family wanted to reclaim the Eye just as much as him. Going alone was never an option.\n\nStill—the camp was vital to misdirect investigation, just as the Lark of Rosgard serves to misdirect motive.
I keep telling her we should run away together. That's probably what she tells herself to keep from saying yes.
She's obsessed with my every movement, but I'm the flirty one. Sure.\n\nOoh. I wonder if she'll be jealous when she finds out we've been working together.

Yes. I am overseeing the Temple's efforts in the peninsula and the dread lands of Apocrypha. It falls to my subordinates, Ordinator Tandasea, Ordinator Tilena, and Ordinator Nelyn, to assign the available work to those that are capable and willing.
It is the prudent warrior that trusts in the guidance of the Three, yet still seeks to know the face of their challenges. What do you need to know?

Ordinator Tilena focuses on infiltration and reconnaissance. She makes use of single operatives to perform missions for the Temple where larger forces might be unwieldy. She is dedicated to the Three and encourages others to be devout as well.

Ordinator Nelyn oversees the logistics of larger operations. The Temple relies on him to manage assignments that require groups of operatives working together. He is very aware that heroism often costs, and pays accordingly.

I serve the Tribunal Temple. The labor I perform is done in service to the Living Gods, not personal gain.\n\nI don't expect my fervency to be shared by all, nor do I expect others to take up arms for the Temple freely. But I do so, gladly.

Nonsense. I appreciate your aid, Traveler, but it is my duty to see this book returned. To think I played any role in removing them is pain enough. I won't shirk my duties onto a stranger. No offense.

Such is the nature of this place. To contain knowledge and keep it out of the reach of those who may try to steal it. A pity though. The Sidereal Cloisters are a work of beauty. \n\nIf only you could experience it free from this cycle.

It concerns beginnings and endings, secrets too dangerous to reveal, and the stability of the threads of fate. Hidden rivals threaten my realm, and thereby threaten all of reality.\n\nIf they succeed, fate will unravel and doom both our worlds.

I am the Golden Eye of Fate and the Keeper of Whispers! Knowledge and memory are my domains! How this threat eludes me, I do not know.\n\nBut you are the key to preserving Apocrypha. I have foreseen it. And in doing so, you shall save the mortal realm.

It is for your peace of mind, mortal. I offer to bind myself. To give you the power to constrain my actions so that you may trust me. The contract also marks you as my proxy. That could prove beneficial in some places you must travel.
Now I complete my writ. I figured you'd want to witness a professional at work. After all your help, you've earned that right.
Yes, I am. Along with the mysterious cipher whose echo we've been chasing. At least the final book revealed who we can blame for this mess.
Show Master Sulis the evidence if you like. Guitot won't go anywhere without my notice. I'll wait here until you're done.

The rules are quite explicit. I can only terminate the person or persons listed on my writ, and this writ only covers Tredecim. We know that's Guitot, so he's my only target. \n\nA Telvanni master may be guilty of scheming, but that's nothing new.

Someone sent the Dusksaber Company to seize relics belonging to Hermaeus Mora from their hiding places in Tamriel. Elite vampire mercenaries commonly employed by Telvanni mages.\n\nI expected the cultists. The Dusksabers were an unwelcome surprise.

Glyphics. Think of them as crystallized memories. Condensations of notional—ah. I explain too much.\n\nI managed to protect Mora's glyphics, with some help. But our adversaries once again move against us.

No. The Onyx, Umbral, and Emerald Glyphics are out of their reach. We stopped our unseen foes from seizing them. Now they have been forced to change their tactics.\n\nBut they have not abandoned their grander scheme and fate remains in danger.

Way ahead of you. While you were saving the hostages, I doubled back and managed to steal Rilasi's replica off the high priest personally.\n\nServes him right for not listening to my favorite armiger in the first place.

So I could give it to you.\n\nWill you honor the patron saint of House Telvanni by restoring his shrine's most beloved spoil of war? Or will you don the mask of the Pariah and deliver them the replica? The choice is now yours.
For everyone involved to keep their desired reputations, there is no one else I can trust with this decision. It has to be you.\n\nI mean, I know what I'd do. But it's in your hands now.

My reputation wouldn't be half of what it is today without Rilasi making me notorious. That's a valuable thing to have in a long-term adversary.\n\nAnd she keeps me on my toes. That's useful—even if I'd much rather she have me on my back.

Rilasi follows a code. As did Saint Vorys, as do the Baandari. As I do, and I'm sure you do, too.\n\nOur codes clash and harmonize. Most of the time, they pass in quiet opposition. I'm holding out hope that Rilasi and I will harmonize again someday.
That question, my friend, would be best asked of Eilirsu-dro. \n\nThough if you've heard the tale of his Little Ancestor, you may have some understanding of it already.

What they don't know won't hurt them.\n\nThe Eye of Baan Dar has been lost for generations, and yet the Baandari kept its legend alive through stories. Is the faith in Saint Vorys so fragile that the loss of one relic would send it crumbling?

At a cost. My son was saved, but I am fated to serve as Herm'us Mora's guide in this land of lost souls. You must burn the relics of my past, so I exist only in memory. Sacrifice the spyglass, logbook, and locket in the brazier!
When I saw my child swept away in the storm, I knew he would perish, and I invoked the pact. Herm'us Mora heard my prayers and answered.

Yes and no. These are the same forces that hired the Dusksaber mercenaries and colluded with Dralys Athren to seize the Emerald Glyphic. Since you put a stop to that, they have changed tactics. But they have not abandoned their scheme.

Yes and no. We face the same foe who sought the Onyx and Umbral Glyphics, and colluded with Dralys Athren to seize the Emerald Glyphic.\n\nYou forced them to change tactics when you stopped them. But they have not abandoned their grander scheme.

I do not worship him, if that is your question. The Prince of Knowledge is an ally and patron. Mora provides me with access to rare and esoteric lore. In return, I undertake various tasks for him.\n\nA mutually beneficial arrangement.
I delivered them to Apocrypha. They are in Hermaeus Mora's possession now. I foresee they have one more part to play in these unfolding events … but you shall learn that soon enough.

If Hermaeus Mora thinks for even a moment that one of his ciphers is trying to steal knowledge from him he'd unwrite my very existence without a second thought! Please, the Cloisters run amok with danger. Will you help me return these books?

This one grew up hearing the story of his Little Ancestor sparing the life of her caravan by tricking the Fiery One into his obsession with the Eye. Now, this one followed his own obsession—and lost many.\n\nAsk what you will. This one will answer.

You mean that the Eye of Baan Dar inside the relic has no hidden magic at all?\n\nBy the code of the Baandari, such words would be unwelcome in the ears of those who follow Saint Vorys. They would cause harm. And so, we discourage them.

Ah. By all appearances, it is a simple gem trapped within a gilded talisman, yes?\n\nThe Eye of Baan Dar is a relic traded between clans of Baandari. The holder may ask for any item, any favor within means, and the receiver must provide.

Should you break it free from the talisman, you would see: it is moonstone. Worth very little coin, yes?\n\nAnd yet it is rubbed smooth and small from passing between the hands of my people. A symbol of indulgence and trading in good faith.
Walker—this one is at a loss for words!\n\nOur caravan will pay forward your generosity a thousand times. But … what will become of the Shrine of Saint Vorys?

This one cannot say, walker. This one only has the code of the Baandari—to indulge the beliefs of others.\n\nBesides, to wield the truth in such a way would ruin the most fragrant mischief of the story of Little Ancestor, yes?

Black Books are relics of Apocrypha. Each holds a different secret. Most are kept in the vast libraries of Hermaeus Mora's realm, but he sometimes gifts one to a mortal.\n\nIn addition to forbidden knowledge, each serves as a portal to Apocrypha.

I am astonished how little the mortals of our tiny world comprehend. Apocrypha is the realm of Hermaeus Mora. His home and seat of power, one of the countless realms that drift through Oblivion.\n\nPlease, do not ask me about Oblivion.

Indubitably! I knew I was right about you. Now, an esteemed elder within the Ciphers once summoned forth this Daedra.\n\nIf we can find the notes from this elder, you and I can summon Tem and engage in parley.

You've never been to the Library of Dusk, I take it. Or the forbidden section of Gwilym University.\n\nDedicated scholars must develop their own search magics. I'll begin the incantation, just be ready for anything. Apocrypha is full of surprises!

The Ciphers of the Eye offer hospitality and refuge to mortals who arrive in Apocrypha, whether purposefully or by accident. However, I am reluctant to involve them in this endeavor.\n\nFortunately, I have my own methods for conducting research.

All research requires parameters. This spell should locate information pertaining to the Fulcrum Obscura, the rite, and Torvesard's lost dream.\n\nUse the scroll's enchantment to aid your search. Then return here and we shall compare notes.

The contents of these stacks change from moment to moment. Such is the nature of this realm's thirst for knowledge.\n\nI can prepare a spell scroll for each of us. As you search, it will dredge up anything related to the parameters I set for the spell.

That is the reason fate chose you. Your instinctual ability to succeed no matter the obstacles placed before you, no matter the odds.\n\nFollow the threads I selected for Leramil. See where they lead. That is the key to saving both our realms.

As I explained on the mortal plane, I am tasked with aligning wrinkles in the annals of fate. How I accomplish that is totally up to me. But when something alters fate's prescribed path, it makes ripples.\n\nJust like the one I followed here.

I was afraid of that. Whatever you're involved in may be beyond my jurisdiction. I suspect the secrets you hope to uncover fall under the direct protection of Apocrypha itself. The Great Eye has put precautions in place to keep them hidden.
Interesting. It would be good to know more about what the agents of Vaermina and Peryite seek in my master's realm.\n\nDid anything out of the ordinary occur while you were conducting your search?

Only if you desire to do so. The threads of fate Hermaeus Mora asks you to investigate begin here in the Telvanni Peninsula. Where they shall lead us, I cannot say. \n\nBut with the threat directed at Apocrypha, I thought quick access was prudent.

Can you feel it? I sense an eddy in the temporal flow through Bal Sunnar. I came here to find its source. You know how these things can affect causality.\n\nIf these Telvanni have met us somehow, then I'm too late.
