I'll find and contain the distortion's source. But the Telvanni will give resistance. If you could help a fellow monk, I'd feel grateful. I can pay for your time.\n\nSince they recognized us, it seems we're predestined to work together anyway.

He admitted as much when he took the glyphics. He rambled on about his new patrons, but never revealed who they were or who else is involved in this plot against Apocrypha.\n\nNow prepare yourself, proxy. I sense the One Who Knows approaching.

Did you forget who you're talking to? It's not my place to challenge the faith in any of the patron saints of the Great Houses.\n\nAnd even if it was—do you really think that stubborn high priest would give the story any credibility? I don't.

You mean the third-hand account that directly challenges the religious importance of the most sacred relic in the shrine of this peninsula's most influential patron saint?\n\nI wasn't planning on it, no.

Black Books serve as doorways into Apocrypha. A master such as Shelreni Baro likely has other ways to reach Hermaeus Mora's domain, so why is this particular book so important to her?\n\nHmm. What did you find in Alavelis?

I've heard nothing. But of course, no one knows the talisman as intimately as I do.\n\nOur relic being threatened as it was has to mean we'll have an influx of pilgrims soon. Perhaps others will be able to provoke it further!

This one does not plan to hold it for long. Perhaps he will trade for supplies, or perhaps he will trade it for a simple song.\n\nBut he is blessed to see the Eye returned to his people in his lifetime. Luck be with you always, walker.
Did I? I don't think so. Hezehk didn't know mortals were prone to hear things that were never said. That I certainly never said. And if I had said it, I wouldn't tell you anyway.

Long ago, before I worked for Madam Whim, I found things. It was my whole existence. Lose something? I'd find it. Mortals summoned me just because they needed stuff found.\n\nThis spell helped me do that. It's been a while, but I'll remember it.

Oh, I've always had an eye for that sort of thing. The sacred gem looked enough like moonstone that I made it work in a pinch. A little bit of weathering using some basic spells, and that's it.\n\nSometimes I wonder if I got in the wrong line of work.

No, no, no. I get enough teasing about how good a thief I'd be from the Lark of Rosgard. I don't need it from you, too.\n\nNow run along, before I decide to change my mind about not taking anyone into custody for this case.

It's just being furtive and aware of your surroundings. I suppose I have some sort of intuition I've picked up from my work on ….\n\nYou know what, I'm going to stop this line of questioning right here.
I was … indisposed for a moment off the side of the road when I thought I heard a snake. \n\nNot ideal when you have your pants around your ankles. You can probably imagine the rest.

Her name was Uveyna Nrayn. As an Ordinator, she served the Ministry of Justice with distinction for many years. \n\nShe served until she was too old to don armor and hold her shield. They hung it in the Hall of Justice in Vivec City in her honor.

The shield will burn here with her remains. Then the Keepers of the Dead will shepherd the ashes to our family's niche in the catacombs.\n\nThere, Aunt Uveyna will find lasting peace with the rest of the Nrayn family. Thanks to you, courier.

Sharpening my blades. You never know how soon I'll need to draw them again.\n\nThen a trip to Necrom, I think. I should pay my respects at the Necropolis while I'm in the area. I put a lot of ancestors in those catacombs!
The high priest doesn't need to know the full details of our … investigation.\n\nBut I need something to return to him. You have something, don't you?

If I do, I'll most certainly be stripped of my title as a Buoyant Armiger. I'd be severely limited in my capacity to stay on the trail of the Lark of Rosgard. \n\nAnd who else is going to apprehend him if not me?

For the assembly? Master Sulis rises in power and Master Foves falls a few steps back. At least for the time being. It's like a game to the Telvanni masters.\n\nAs for me, I think I'll head to Necrom and find a spot in a crowded tavern. I need a drink.

While I wish we hadn't had any information passed to House Dres, we caught the spy and Foves is in my debt. So, things couldn't have gone much better for me.\n\nI'll remove him from the project though. Which, frankly, will be an improvement.

I am the mystery at the end of existence. The first secret whispered at the dawn of creation. I am the guardian of the unseen and the question unanswerable. I hold the knowledge forbidden and untangle the threads of fate.\n\nI am … the One Who Knows.

Ah, the event that began this cavalcade of fate. Of course, such drastic measures must have been taken for good reason. The One Who Knows keeps referring to the unraveling of reality if we fail in our efforts.\n\nWhat else did you experience?

Our most dangerous fates are magically tagged. Their presence leaves markers we can follow. We don't want to lose track of a particularly minacious anomaly, after all!\n\nMy Watchling's Sight makes it so you can see these markers.

Absolutely! I've tuned my sight to your mortal senses. You can only see the magical traces specific to my master's glyphic. They should look like blue vapors and smell like a mortal child's tears.\n\nCan we get going now?

With that level of power, Torvesard is clearly more than your average Dremora. Much more ….\n\nDoes that mean the secret has been remembered? Have we failed? Shall reality begin unraveling all around us?

You did? I … I am unsure how I feel about that. I want to ask you a thousand questions, but the corruption plaguing Apocrypha grows worse with every passing moment and Vaermina still roams free. I am torn as to what to do.

Hmm. An opportunity, perhaps? It shall take Vaermina time to locate the remaining glyphics. That gives us a chance to end the corruption and restore Hermaeus Mora's power.\n\nAre you willing to hunt down Blightcrown while I try to locate Vaermina?

I don't know the full story, but Zilipif used to work for Mephala. As a Watcher, they would separate the lies from the truth and add to Mephala's powers of deception. They had a change of … well not heart exactly, but Zilipif changed their mind.

It's true that most of Mephala's Daedric followers are Spiderkith, or other arachnid Daedra.\n\nAs a Daedric Prince of secrets, lies, and deception, she has to have eyes watching the threads of mortal affairs. They can't all be spiders.
Not easily, and most don't even bother. But, Zilipif did. \n\nKeshargo once told me that Zilipif takes a lot of care to avoid even the smallest of spiderwebs.
Saddened. You were right to give him the book, but I'm left to mourn a loss that did not have to be. Even now, I cannot shake the feeling I could still free him.
He does not. When I tell him, he doesn't hear. Such is the power of Herm'us Mora's sorcery.
Odd. Things feel familiar but distant. I remember you, and almost drowning, and washing up at Fathoms Drift. But there's something else. Something deeply important that I've lost track of.

Did I use the wrong words, mortal? My investigation is incomplete. To find out what the Hidden Kindred seek in my master's realm, I must follow them. And since you agreed to assist me, you must follow me.\n\nI like it less than you, believe me.

My favorite one was something about my parents not wanting to give me up to be a Shadowscale. So we lived on the run from the Dark Brotherhood trying to track us down and make me one of their assassins.\n\nI told you it was stupid.

Have I ever told the fanciful children's tale of my secret imaginary past to anyone else? Come on.\n\nAnd it really is like a children's tale, so if you enjoyed it, just think about what that says about you.

Oh, my parents begged some Spinner to rewrite my destiny at the cost of our memories of each other. Explains why I woke up in Valenwood. And despite everything, I became a merc anyway.\n\nThe irony and continuity were very important to me at the time.

Who can guess with the Princes? Perhaps he valued my son's memories as highly as my life. He is a master of knowledge, after all. Still, I will take care of my son as best I can. Perhaps we will voyage together again.

Well, no. But that's why we'll test it out first. Just one memory, before his entire lifetime.\n\nMevei said you wanted a sample of tyranite calx anyway, right? Even if you don't want to do my plan, you'll find some across the water in Broken Tusk.

That's what she said. I knew Valinna was spending time in the Spiral Skein. Was she talking to Mephala? \n\nMephala is the Daedric Prince of secrets, like Hermaeus Mora. But she doesn't care about the truth, only what she can use against others.

Yes, we know. So few survived that assault. Eventually the vestiges who the Dreamcarvers cut down will reform and return to Apocrypha. Until that time, our gifts remain weak.\n\nIn any event, we are grateful for your effort.

As it stands, our research just adds to the library of Apocrypha. The chances of dangerous information being read by anyone's eyes is fairly low. \n\nBut if the scribes were motivated to seek out the secrets Mephala deals in? It could be disastrous.

My business is my own, but if you must know, I recently purchased a shuttered malachite mine there and put it back into operation. I'm not surprised you found some of my correspondence. I regularly exchanged letters with the overseer I hired.

Are you sure it was the Dusksabers? In my experience, it's hard to tell one vampire from another. It's why I insist that Captain Zenfis wear a name tag.\n\nI never tell the Dusksabers how to do a job I hire them for. Mercenaries—what can you do?

I instructed my work crew to set up an arcane experiment. Nothing dangerous. If the overseer I hired employed Daedric cultists, it was without my knowledge or consent. And I rarely order my hirelings to commit violence, let alone kill anyone.

My business is my own, but if you must know, I recently purchased a shuttered malachite mine there and put it back into operation. I'm not surprised you found some of my correspondence. I regularly exchanged letters with the overseer I hired.

I instructed my work crew to set up an arcane experiment. Nothing dangerous. If the overseer I hired employed Daedric cultists, it was without my knowledge or consent. And I rarely order my hirelings to commit violence, let alone kill anyone.

In some quarters it's impolite to ask about such things. I'm a Telvanni master—I know many Dremora. My dealings with them are not your concern. But if you must know, I had no part in whatever happened in Necrom.\n\nNow, assist me or leave this place.

The Necropolis? My favorite ancestor is buried there. That reminds me. I owe her a visit. As for Alavelis, I recently bought the glass mine there. I'm trying to get it operational, but it may be a lost cause.\n\nYou ask the strangest questions, f'lah.

Well done. Hmm. Yes, just needs a bit of finessing. Brilliant. Should be all ready now to give to Oathman Llaro.\n\nMay I ask one more favor? Could you give it to him in my stead? Last I saw him, he was meeting with Spellwright Varsva.

What? In large doses perhaps, but ….\n\nOh, all right. It's poison. But understand, Llaro is dreadful! A violent bully, totally unfit for his station! You'd be doing a favor to all House Telvanni. It is up to you, but please, deliver the tincture.
Poison you say? Ha! I didn't expect that worm, Balver, to have such a murderous disposition. You did well to inform me. I'll see to it that he's dealt with accordingly.
Not yet. There's an old man here who's been looking after me. He's been very kind. He's a captain, and talking about building a new ship. I think I'll help him. That would be good for me.
Edril Athren. I serve Retainer Balver. But that's not important. Like I said, Balver is up to something. Stinks. Maybe some coin will help me remember what it was.
My book on … oh no. I'm guilty of authoring that nonsense, yes. \n\nA journeyman effort from several centuries ago. If you have it, please take it with you. It is trash.

This is the Expungatory, an important hub in our settlement. Here, palimpsests are recycled for re-use.\n\nScrolls are scraped clean of old sigils, ready to be used again in a new and potent arcane working.
Mhm, yes. Coins jog the memory a bit. I remember seeing Balver's journal. He keeps it in the basement of the Retainers' Billet. Read it and I'm sure you'll find out what he's really up to.

Point taken. Well, if it can't be done easy, at least we can try and get it done quick.\n\nIf you ever think of a way for me to make all this up to you, let me know. I don't want this to change things between us for the worse.

I—I don't know. But the pain and the blindness … is this what caused the Great Eye to disconnect from his realm? To allow Vaermina's dream to envelop him in order to escape the suffering?\n\nYou don't suppose she has a dream for me, do you?

Invaders forced their way into the Tranquil Catalog. I think they were devotees of Peryite and Vaermina, but how could that be? And Dreamcarver Dremora accompanied them! They killed or drove off my fellow ciphers.

I am a humble cipher, a mortal scribe in service to the Great Eye. This is the Tranquil Catalog, a register and index of the contents of Apocrypha. Hermaeus Mora's enemies could wreak havoc with the information stored here!

Ah. Balver Bemis sent word that he had made a tincture for me. Given the quality of Balver's other servants, I'm surprised you managed the trip without wandering off into the wilderness. \n\nDamn these headaches!
Fine, fine! Balver is always up late writing. His journal will have the answers. It is in the basement of the Retainer's Billet. Now, leave me be!

It was an alliance of necessity. I needed their assistance to recover that which was taken from us in ancient times. Hermaeus Mora did what he thought right, as have I. I have no desire to punish him for following his nature.

I know where to find Blightcrown so that you can stop him before he does irreparable damage to this realm. And I can show you where Vaermina has gone. I no longer care to share the ancient memory with her or Peryite.

Because I also require help. I offer a trade. An end to this assault on Apocrypha for the assistance of fate's chosen.\n\nDecide, mortal. Blightcrown even now works his way toward the core of this realm. Soon it will be too late to reverse the damage.

Are you a spy for one of my rivals? Or perhaps you're really working for one of those tiresome Temple Ordinators? Regardless, I don't need to explain myself to you.\n\nNow, either assist me with gaining entry to Tel Rendys or leave this place at once.
At least I still remember him. I should thank you for helping me find out what happened to him. And for letting me keep my memories.
I do certainly feel out of my depth but this seems apropos for one that seeks insight into Herm'us Mora's mind as I do.

Telvanni masters and magisters avoid undue socializing, fearing threats from all directions. So they appoint agents to represent them. Mouths. Meln eschewed the practice, hence they called him mouthless.\n\nI expect his tower to be a fortress.
At least I will still remember him. I should thank you for helping me find out what happened to him. And to me.

Three glyphics contain the concepts that, once released, shall solidify your association with Hermaeus Mora for the length of this crisis.\n\nI have already acquired two of the glyphics. You shall obtain the third.

These three specific glyphics contain the concepts that, once released, shall solidify your association with Hermaeus Mora for the length of this crisis.\n\nI have already acquired two of the glyphics. You shall obtain the third.
I'm not sure. This old man. He seems … familiar. I think he's a captain. Perhaps I will go to sea again. Yes, that would be good for me.

In truth, I haven't a clue. What in all the planes am I supposed to say no to? A mystery to be sure, but I have Apocrypha's extensive libraries right at my fingertips. Can you imagine a better place to find an answer?

I will not need to access the memory storage component of the fragments, only their connection to Kemel-Ze as a whole.\n\nOur interfering with the fragments may cause their stored memories to reveal themselves, but they will remain intact within me.

A great mage. Perhaps even a Telvanni master. Though if you go too long without proving your magical prowess, people start to question whether you still deserve the title.\n\nAnd Dreynis has spent a very long time here on Gorne.

After being a tentacle's touch away from facing the business end of a nemesis loom? I'll return to my duties, thank you very much. After I see my master's glyphic returned to its proper place, of course.

What else? We all have our place in my master's plan. Just as you do. I certainly won't be looking for another—what would you call this, an adventure?—any time soon.\n\nNotarizing and disseminating is exciting enough for me.

The Dreamcarver invasion proves that our clan has grown weak. If we cannot defend our home, how can we serve the Great Eye?\n\nA rift threatens the Remnants. Do we attempt to regrow or disband entirely?
Through the door Apostle Nilphas Drethan used when we first met. It will open for you now.

The rooms are named after their contents, for precise documentation purposes. They are the Fauna Study, the Floral Atelier, and the Laboratory of Sparks. Each represents a different avenue of Lord Seht's research.

No, no! I would never—\n\nWell, yes, I would. But please, just give him the poison—I mean the tincture. I'll take blame if you get caught. Just deliver it to him. He's truly awful. Bullying, boorish, with bad taste in clothes. Need I go on?

We will find them north of here. They will require both of our efforts to set. You must hold the trigger while we funnel energy into it.\n\nOnce set, the wards will drive most of the Dreamcarvers from the Cenotaph.

Magic has long known the mechanics of the body and its repair. But Lord Seht wasn't satisfied with repair. He sought improvement. Of rabbits, guars. All things.\n\nHe quickly settled on metal enhancements and began their exploration here.
What is a world without plants?\n\nLord Seht thought it was no world at all. Even the driest of deserts contain floral life. It is everywhere and so it must exist in the Clockwork City.

It hails from one of his more energetic moments. He had a revelation, early in his project, to focus on metal as the medium for his new world. While flesh decays and bark rots, metal can be preserved.\n\nThis laboratory is his spark.

Because you're not a Telvanni. That particular statute relates to the agreement between House Telvanni and the Keepers of the Dead. If you present it with authority, the sentry will probably grant you access.

And tell them what? If you even imply that any Telvanni would require the help of an outsider, you'd insult them at best or get arrested, if not immediately challenged to a duel of spells.\n\nBelieve me, any of those would be counterproductive.

Two things protect my book. The spell of illegibility I cast upon it and the fact that without my aid, it will take her time to break the spell on her own.\n\nStill, I'd rather she never gets her hands on it. Stop her and I'll find a way to reward you.

Perhaps not the first to look, but I intend to be the first to succeed. Once we have that research, we can leave Dreynis to his fungal teas.\n\nSearch the perimeter of the estate. I'll head for the manor house in the middle. We'll meet there.

Your master has delayed these proceedings long enough. Master Shelreni reached above her station and must be dealt with. Anything that postpones that and increases the time I must spend in the company of my so-called peers will not be tolerated.

Murder, you say. That is serious. I suppose anything can be expected from a master who makes pacts with Daedra. We really need to strip her of her rank and exile her.\n\nWell, if you must see her, she's being held in a meeting room down the east hall.
Meln may have confused Magister Gothren, but there's no provision for a dead Telvanni participating in a conclave. It's just not done!

The Prince of Fate, the Guardian of the Unseen, the Lord of Secrets. Perhaps you know him as Hermaeus Mora, the Daedric Prince of Knowledge and Memory.\n\nHe has seen many paths forward, but only one where both Nirn and Apocrypha survive.

I want you to help preserve the realm of Apocrypha to keep the reality of Nirn from unraveling. At this particular moment, in this specific instance, the fates of both realms are inextricably linked. Will you do as the Prince asks and assist me?

Well, they're vital to the recipe. I don't want to bore you with the details, but the stinkhorn provides a binding catalyst, while the bull netch musk gland balances the humors. They're very important. Yes, definitely.
I'm just a servant, doing their tasks around Ald Isra. A servant with the House's best interests in mind, you see.

To be honest, I try to keep a good distance from Oathman Llaro. I do some apothecary work for him and gather any ingredients he needs for his own work. But best not to get underfoot. He's a yeller, you know.

What has occurred is what was meant to be. All the potential futures, coalesced into a single point in time to render a moment in fate absolute.\n\nIt was inevitable. Torvesard has the ability to avoid detection—even from my all-seeing gaze.
For one who knows everything, I can only speculate. Odd, I find that refreshing. It relates to the forgotten memory, but unless I look into the glyphics, those details are lost … even to me.

Now I must restore my realm. The Hidden Kindred linger, but without leaders they are merely a nuisance.\n\nYou, however, are still fate's chosen. Return to your allies in Cipher's Midden. When the time comes, you will find Torvesard and deal with him.
Poison? Of course. There are attempts to climb up the ranks all the time. Some fail. Some succeed. The price for failure is steep. Had Balver Bemis failed in his attempt, he wouldn't be so merry.

Fate selected you to save Apocrypha and preserve reality. You have accomplished all that and more. Destiny followed the exact path that I foretold.\n\nBut we are not yet done. You have more to do before our contract is fulfilled.
You know, I hadn't thought about it. Frankly, I didn't expect to get this far. I'll have to think about my next moves.\n\nYes, I'll be making moves. I feel a change coming. A big one!

Often enough. Though assassination attempts are seldom this clumsy. So it goes.\n\nOathman Llaro will make Balver an example to others. Well done. Or, my condolences. I don't know. Honestly, I can't bring myself to care about any of this.
Now? Now, I deal with this poltroon and get back to business. Being an Oathman is such a headache.

Of course. He needed you to lead him to Vaermina. Guide him to where she was lurking because she was hidden inside the body of Master Shelreni.\n\nAnd what of the second glyphic? Is the secret memory secure?

The less said, the better for both of us. Suffice it to say, you helped me secure a new position in accordance with the time-honored traditions of House Telvanni.\n\nWith my business behind us, we can see to yours.

Take the Tel Baro insignia from my office. You'll need it to unlock the wards, otherwise you'll never get through the cavern to reach the tower. Master Shelreni takes security quite seriously.\n\nNow if you'll excuse me, a mouth's work is never done.

Tlaxalt is dead? That is … unfortunate. She was a promising cipher. I looked forward to many profitable discourses with her, but Apocrypha holds many dangers for mortals. What kind of situation could she have gotten herself into?

That is … unclear. No mortal has read a volume of the Numinous Grimoire and survived with their mind intact. We think it deals with transformations. Immortality. Or so the Daedra familiar with the book tell us.\n\nThey could be lying.

Dreyla dead? I feared he might come to harm here. He was naive, yet full of ambition—a dangerous combination in Apocrypha. The path of the cipher is not for everyone.\n\nYou found him with this book, you say?

I feared the worst when Nelfynn dropped out of sight. Strange things have been going on around here. It seems I was right to be worried.\n\nYou mentioned a strange book. Was it the Numinous Grimoire, Volume 3?

I'm not sure I can. No mortal can read the Numinous Grimoire without losing their mind, so all we have to go on are the ravings of the mad. But when I began to suspect Akacirn, I asked around about his recent research and interests.

I pored through every description of the Numinous Grimoire and its contents I could find. In so doing, I learned about a long-dead cipher who nearly completed the Numinous Rite before madness took her. Akacirn must have come across her notes.

Ahh, the self-proclaimed "Akacirn the Deathless." Many mortals hold inflated opinions of themselves, but he appears to be a special case. I have met few of your kind more disagreeable. What is your business with him?

If it gets you to leave, then I shall oblige. Mortal souls are not fettered to this existence as Daedra are. The Numinous Grimoire explores a path to decoupling the soul from the body. To becoming a thing sustained by spirit, not matter.

In my studies of mortal heresies, I occasionally find it useful to help mortals advance their ambitions. It gives me perspective. Why do mortals thirst so much for that which is forbidden to them? It is … intriguing.
That makes two of us. There must be a connection between these ciphers. Something they have in common … but I do not know what it is.\n\nWhich missing cipher do you want to know about?

Why, this is the first volume of the Numinous Grimoire! It's one of the tomes that went missing from our collection. A dangerous book of forbidden knowledge. It destroys the mind of any mortal who reads it.\n\nI'd better take that.

Because ciphers are dead. The note you found makes it clear someone used my colleagues to get their hands on the Grimoire. Then this instigator repaid a cipher's help with death.\n\nNone of us are safe until this mystery is solved.

Cipher Akacirn is a very old man. He spoke bitterly to other ciphers about how little time he had left to finish his studies. And he was jealous of the Daedra, too. He seemed to think they were keeping the secret of immortality from us.

The Numinous Grimoire is said to hold secrets of immortality. Magic dealing with the mortal soul exacts a great price, but Cipher Akacirn is desperate. I worry that he plans to do whatever he must to escape death. Even hurt others.

I sent Akacirn to a ritual site within the Apogee of the Tormenting Eye. Here, I will mark the location for you.\n\nThe ritual requires time to take hold—time during which he must lie dead in truth. Destroy his body, and his rite will fail.

Yes, the Numinous Rite. He asked about it.\n\nVery well. I did not ask to become embroiled in a mortal's quest for power. If you want to stop Akacirn, there may still be time. And I need nothing more than to know I contributed to his failure.

Ahh, that was clever. Akacirn had others read it for him, and then consumed the contents of their minds. Learning how to do that took him decades of study, or so he told me.\n\nI suppose he is already the thing he hopes to become. How ironic.

I won't destroy it, if that's what you are suggesting. Ciphers exist to preserve knowledge. But I will lock it away someplace where no cipher will come across it for a very long time. And Akacirn's research, as well.\n\nLet it be buried.

I knew ciphers who asked Nelfynn to do things they didn't want to do themselves. Fetch books from dangerous spots, or ask favors of prickly Daedra. She was eager to please. And far too trusting.\n\nWhat else would you like to know?

Nelfynn was new here. A Nord, cheerful and trusting. Many of us ciphers are absorbed in our own interests. Unwilling to concern ourselves with others' troubles. Yet Nelfynn was happy to help with any chore. Some took advantage of that.

It might. I can think of a few entities who might use that monogram—some mortal, some Daedra. I need to make some inquiries … discreetly. If I ask the wrong question of the wrong person, I might put myself at risk.

The Ciphers of the Eye have no ranks. But some of us have been here longer than others. Senior ciphers enjoy access to collections we do not share with new arrivals. Dreyla did not want to wait.\n\nWhat else do you wish to know?
He is—was—a Dark Elf. Young for a Cipher. It takes decades of study for most of us to find our way to Apocrypha, but Dreyla was a brilliant student. Clever and ambitious, but impatient.

It might have. Tlaxalt sometimes made strange bargains with those she wanted to learn from. Dealt with entities few other ciphers know. Knowledge has a price … especially in Apocrypha.\n\nWhat else can I tell you?

Tlaxalt? An Argonian scholar who didn't always fit in here. A free spirit of sorts. She valued knowledge in many forms—songs, art, handicrafts. Tlaxalt rarely bothered with books. When she wanted to know something, she sought instruction.
We use the gathered relics. Once placed, our power shall bind them together. They will connect to what remains of the Remnants' mental web. The resulting mesh will open the Crux.

I created and rule over Apocrypha, my endless repository of knowledge in the vastness of Oblivion. Every secret known to mortal and immortal resides here, as well as many known only to me. It is a realm of fate, time, and wisdom.

Many realms of Oblivion have a relationship to the mortal world. Some believe that Nirn is a reflection of the Daedric realms, or that the Daedric realms are an echo of Nirn.\n\nRegardless, Apocrypha and Nirn share a powerful connection.

Exactly what Leramil told you. You shall render what aid is required to preserve the course of fate and keep Apocrypha safe, thereby protecting Nirn.\n\nMoreover, the contract specifies that I will not force you to act against your own best interests.

If my enemies succeed and damage or destroy Apocrypha, the resulting ripples of fate will unravel the mortal world.\n\nIn short, Nirn will cease to exist. You must help me to prevent that fate from coming to fruition.

Go about your usual business and await my summons. The threads of fate tell me that we must separate for a time, but we shall come together again when the moment is right.\n\nUntil then, stay safe, proxy.

We must free Meln the Mouthless from Master Shelreni's grasp and retrieve the Black Book. But to do that, we need more information.\n\nLook around, proxy. If Meln was indeed murdered here, there might be proof of Shelreni's villainy.

Per the courier's oath, "Your job isn't to know, it's to take the parcel and go." All I was told was that it's very important.\n\nBetween you and me, they say that for all deliveries to members of House Hlaalu. But the less I know, the better.

No point now. I've been waiting for so long that even if my boots were broken in, I'd still never make it in time.\n\nFunny thing is, I bought this ensemble to treat myself for landing this position with House Hlaalu. Should've just saved my gold.

You didn't look like a Elouan Genin to me, but I wasn't going to say anything. What matters is that Elouan made sure that you could get the job done, whoever you are.\n\nNow, I'd like to tend to my aunt's pyre in peace. Safe travels to you.

You're Elouan Genin, are you not? The House said they were sending one of their best, and you did not disappoint. I will send along my gratitude.\n\nNow, I'd like to tend to my aunt's pyre in peace. Safe travels, courier.
The choices of Azandar al-Cybiades hang heavy about him, reeking from stains on his hands and his soul. \n\nAlso, he speaks with a distinct lack of respect for Tem, the Omen of Destiny.

Martina Abor, arcanist of the abyssal sea and illuminatus of the threads of fate. Retreated to their sanctum nine hundred and twenty days ago. Seek them within the subrealm known as the Underweave, at a place called the Heart.\n\nBut beware, mortal.
Fearless is as fearless does. Everyone is afraid of something, but you having fears and fears having you are two different things.
Really? Then you are better equipped for the Witches Festival than most. Farewell.
Targets. Bounties. Got fishing on the mind, I suppose. I was planning a trip when I got put on this job. High priority, and the pay was nothing I could pass up. \n\nLucky for the fish.

Fault is a strong word. I operate Oblivion's premiere traveling creature exhibit. Notable entities across the planes line up to see my show.\n\nBut my portal spell went awry and I crashed here. My creatures fled, leaving me alone in this strange land.

No. My portal spell needs retuning. But my creatures. Their majesty is wasted here, and I can't deprive Fargrave of my show. Also, they tend to be rather destructive.\n\nMortal, retrieve my five creatures and I can provide you with treats.

Hmm … Martina says here she could somehow scry for the fates frayed from her timeline? Fascinating.\n\nShe experimented with several different methods … ugh, including using her own blood? Messy. Dangerous. But perhaps effective.

Yes … Yes I believe so. I have some thoughts that need to… germinate. And I'd like to dispel this ward, take care of Martina. Ahem.\n\nLet's retire to my rooms at Cipher's Midden, near the wayshrine. I'll see you there, my canny colleague.

Research, of course. Always research. Just like in the old days. Martina and I were excellent collaborators. \n\nI was the gab, the talker, the trader. Martina was the silent strength, astute observations after lengthy contemplation.

I'm an arse. It seems wrong to coat the truth in moon-sugar, standing over Martina's final work. I can be challenging to know, and worse to work with. \n\nMartina put up with me for the better part of five years. Longer than anyone else.
I'm not quite sure. I think, perhaps, she was trying to manipulate fate itself. But I'd have to examine Martina's notes to fully understand what happened here.

It's a sinkhole in reality, a graveyard for ships from across the realms. Hermaeus Mora is the Tide King, after all. \n\nIn his role as master of the seas and One-Whose-Tentacles-Rise-From-the-Deep, he claims sunken vessels to add to his trove.

We know it is a vile combination of dream and disease developed by Blightcrown from concepts provided by Vaermina and Peryite. Master Shelreni helped to perfect it and her rite increased its strength.\n\nIt hides Vaermina and weakens Hermaeus Mora.

As we have seen, it drives the inhabitants of Apocrypha mad and turns even allied Daedra violent. Scruut could sense the agony of the realm back on Nirn. Here, I fear she may eventually succumb as the other natives have.\n\nEven I am not immune.

Are they really? Well, aren't you a clever one.\n\nSince you've made yourself useful, I'll tell you that Reynila came through recently seeking Deredrien, a fence who specializes in moving specialty items.

The other mortal? Oh, to have my fate rest in such fragile hands! Really, you should go. Apocrypha is no longer safe. And I don't want to hurt you.\n\nWait. A barely perceptible ripple in the threads. Someone approaches!
Can't say I blame him. I've attacked people for far less.\n\nI haven't seen this associate of mine for quite some time. Pity. I'd like to thank him properly for what he did.
Really? Then it seems my prayers on your behalf were answered. Excellent! Farewell.
Let me petition Arkay for courage on your behalf. What horrors of the night trouble you most?
Then it seems my prayers on your behalf have not yet been answered. Perhaps you need more faith.\n\nWhat is it that you fear again?

Once, long ago, I was her mentor. But I recognized a darkness in her. And not the usual Telvanni traits. She was reckless. Dangerous. I refused to sponsor her advancement beyond the rank of master. And she coveted my Black Book.\n\nSo, she killed me.

I don't know, all right? And I don't remember. And I don't want to think about what it means if I'm ….\n\nLook. Let's not form any solid theories until we find this Mevei, all right? Let's just get some answers first.

No one will enter, except Lord Seht. I have eons of experience dissuading the strongest of Telvanni mages from these halls. No one will come here again without my permission.\n\nI appreciate your help. Without you, these halls would never be safe.

I cannot say. It may only take a few hours, or it could take a season. It depends on how stubborn they are. But after they are gone, I will begin the locking sequence. Like my creator before me, I will shun the world of mortals.

She put herself on assignment. She's freeing another from the Reformer. I haven't heard from her, but that's how these things often go.\n\nForgive me, it's only just occurred to me, but if Sharp has no memories of Reynila … how did you find me?

What? Deredrien … No! Reynila needed her help to find the smuggler's tunnels in Gorne. She'd arranged for a boat to take them to safety.\n\nIf it's just the two of them in those tunnels—I need to get to her. Please, can you help?

Ah yes, Vampires. A spreading plague of blood and fangs. A justifiable fear, but one that must be faced in these dark times.\n\nMay Arkay grant you courage in your dealings with them. Be safe, wanderer.

Werewolves. Of course. Prowlers with the cunning of warriors and the savagery of beasts. A justifiable fear, but one that you must surely face in these dark times.\n\nMay Arkay grant you courage in your dealings with them. Be safe, wanderer.

I sympathize. Fleshless, clacking skeletons defy Arkay's will. A justifiable fear, but one that I am sure you will face in these dark times.\n\nMay Arkay grant you courage in your dealings with them. Be safe, wanderer.

Right. But who? And why Eastmarch, of all places? \n\nFedero wasn't stupid—he'd know I'd see through a cover story as fake as this wine-drinker being his betrothed. And he knows how good a tracker I am. Why leave such an obvious loose end?

I suppose he'd be in trouble if he didn't make every effort to hand me over to the Reformer. I just can't imagine why he'd do that for me.\n\nThe place the Elf mentioned is west of Cragwallow. Right on the hot springs. Ugh.

As the curate can tell you, Necrom forbids summoning the dead. But there's no regulation against the dead choosing to speak to you. \n\nWe don't have to summon Shelreni's spirit. We can go to her and simply request an audience.

Same place you found me. In her tower, of course! We must go to Tel Baro and search her sanctum. If her spirit lingers, she'll haunt there.\n\nOh, and better take Gadayn with us. If she's become a vengeful spirit, his expertise might be required.

Oh … oh, he's … dead, I'm afraid. Killed by some mercenary called Sharp-as-Knife. Just brutal.\n\nNasty business. Tragic, really. I'm heartbroken. We were going to get married, you know. But he told me that since he's dead, I can keep the house.

Huh. Good question.\n\nLook, Federo just told me to say that to anyone who came asking after him. He's a good guy, really. Said he was meeting someone who was going to keep him safe. You're not trying to hurt him, are you?

I don't mind endless tracts of ice and snow, but Eastmarch has that rotten egg smell from all the hot springs. Makes me want to gag.\n\nBesides that, the Nords of Windhelm are a bit chipper for my taste. Otherwise, no strong opinions.

I'd be surprised if he were. Like you said, he was meeting someone. If we have to do more tracking, that's fine by me. I'm good at that.\n\nI can't picture him staying in the wilds of Skyrim for long, though. He's what I'd call an indoor Elf.
When I say he asked me to drink with him once or twice, I might have agreed. Once or twice.\n\nEasier to think of him not as a friend, if he happened to sell me out to the Reformer.
I did. But I'm beginning to rethink that theory. I'm not going to say I was wrong until I actually am. And probably not even then.\n\nAre you done with the questions? We have an armpit to get to.

Precisely. After that happened to Sharp, Reynila studied the vile process and learned how to safely de-attune those freed after him.\n\nShe'll be thrilled to see him again. I just know it. She might even know how to restore his memories!

She has an informal web of operatives across Tamriel focused on freeing slaves.\n\nShe relies heavily on favors and appealing to people's better nature. It's a struggle, to be sure. I think Reynila takes on a lot more than she can bear.

Deredrien put a hand on Sharp to shake him awake, and he nearly clawed her face off. She said she barely escaped with her life.\n\nI can't blame Sharp, and Reynila felt the same. He must have reacted in fear, that's all.

No. Deredrien was furious. Reynila didn't know such a thing would happen, but that didn't seem to matter to Deredrien. She had complained that Reynila wasn't paying her enough, anyway.\n\nI'm just sad it ended this way for her.

It started with Torvesard and his dream of something lost long ago.\n\nHe needed someone to acquire Meln's Black Book and perform the rite. In return, he would help me achieve my dream of becoming archmagister, as long as I pledged myself to Vaermina.

Reynila worked hard to bring light to all corners of the world. Now that she's gone, everything feels cast in shadow. Like I've lost my purpose.\n\nBut forgery is something I know. Something I did for her. This new identity—is it for Sharp?

Reynila's work, then—it wasn't for nothing. A spark still remains. Her mission didn't have to die with her.\n\nI'll draft up a plausible identity. Something that will allow Federo unrestricted travel, wherever he might wish to go.

I know that name. Reynila used to keep tabs on him. She wrote him, pleading for him to defect as an abolitionist.\n\nI was convinced he was a lost cause. But Reynila didn't believe in lost causes. He's really had a change of heart, has he?

First, we enter the drift and find the darned thing. The Fateweaver Key, in your able hands, will lead us where we need to go.\n\nNow properly attuned, it should allow you to tug on the threads that bind my fate to me.

We use the Fateweaver Key itself to bind this frayed fate back into the fabric of the universe. I'm not … well to be totally honest I'm not exactly sure what that will look like.\n\nBut we're armed with a dead friend's knowledge. We'll see it done.
Of course! Just processing. Tem, it seems, was telling the truth. A frayed fate has grown in strength somehow. Become … adversarial.

Allow me to take back the Fateweaver Key. Hmm. I'll need to consider this new information. \n\nThe introduction of this … adversary into the experiment was unforeseen. Let's reconvene in my room at Cipher's Midden.

I don't know. She said something about a safe house in Silent Mire, but our final destination was somewhere deep in Black Marsh. \n\nWe barely escaped Deredrien. And now, Reynila's gone. I don't know what I'm going to do.

He's more than after me. He's obsessed with me. But that I can do something about. If I could just track him down ….\n\nThat's what I have to do. Find the Reformer, and be his end. But you heard Reynila. If I try to do it alone, I'll end up like her.
Troubled? What mortal is not? Death comes for every one of us in the end. And yet we pretend otherwise!
Maybe. Your words sound true, but I don't know.\n\nWell, thank you for trying to help. It's appreciated.
You mean? Oh! Oh please, no! I'm not ready! I'm not ready!
Nonsense. It's the end of life! The Skaldolf family have always been metal smiths. All are gone save me. They toiled and slaved, but could take nothing with them in the end.

Really? My grandfather's grandfather was a silversmith. I was named after him. This must be his work!\n\nI—I see now. My ancestors live on through their work. If I commit to my craft, perhaps I can as well! Thank you, friend!

I don't know, but I don't think this is his plan. A cipher would never betray the Great Eye, and Sabinius has never shown any hints of madness or dangerous ambitions. Either he made a terrible mistake, or someone else put him up to it.

I don't know, but I don't think this is his plan. A cipher would never betray the Great Eye, and Sabinius has never shown any hints of madness or dangerous ambitions. Either he made a terrible mistake, or someone else put him up to it.
Well, sure. But mainly I bring him for protection. You can never be too careful, especially this time of year, what with all the witches lurking about.

Absolutely. She claimed it was a ward against evil. Which goes to show you how crafty witches can be! But I saw through her deceit and <<1>> dealt with her.\n\nLet that be a lesson to you. Be careful out there!
This is … where did you find this?\n\nNo. No, no—it's him! He's found me! You led him to me!

Oh, yes! At my own home, no less! There was this strange woman who lived nearby. She kept a lot of cats and always smelled a bit off. She tried to give me a cursed cat-shaped figurine! I set <<1>> on her and he put a quick end to her.
Ma'nna was curious about the world. She loved to come with me when I traveled. One day when I was distracted, she ran off. I heard a scream. \n\nI—I'm sorry, it is still too much to bear.
I know. Just—not yet. Not yet.

Petal! You found Petal! This was Ma'nna's favorite traveling companion. Oh, so many memories.\n\nI'm going to make dolls for my other children. I cannot let my fears drive them away. Thank you for giving me this, stranger.

Yes. I'm just glad the other children were too young at the time. They often pleaded with me to come along on trips like this, but I cannot bear the thought of losing them like poor Ma'nna. They're safer at home with my husband.

You could say that. But what better time for it? A mask would normally give me away, but with all the other revelers celebrating the festival, I fit right in.\n\nI'd give you a deal on something, but these trinkets are for my personal collection.
With all the masks, you're never sure who you are talking to. Feel free to tell others of our little chat. This time of year, I'm sure no one would be surprised.\n\nTake care. I'll be seeing you.

Yes, that's mine. A lot of my things end up on Nirn around this time. I'll have that back now.\n\nI should be unhappy with you. The fork and the doll are rightfully mine. Still, that cat-shaped ward did track down that murderer. So call us even.

I do indeed. But for me, sentimental value is the measure of something's true worth.\n\nI have quite the collection of macabre items, mementos of a festival that has treated me oh-so well. You'd be impressed.

They serve the Daedric Princes Vaermina and Peryite. I know that dangerous champions lead the attack. But the real threat is the master of the Seeker heralds. It has subverted Bastion Nymic's defenses. Mora's own Daedra will try to stop you.

No. But we must sometimes forge strange alliances. Our people have a long history with the Daedra, you'll recall. I have an understanding with Mora. We help each other, from time to time.\n\nEspecially when his affairs spill over into our world.

One of Sotha Sil's Clockwork Apostles. He's a little arrogant, but I think our time together has endeared me to him in his own way. He's stopped looking down on me and instead began talking to me through notes and letters!\n\nStill, he's an odd one.
I don't want to say anything out of turn. I'm sure he has his reasons as well. \n\nBut, the things Nilphas says seem … overzealous, even for an Apostle.
You didn't sate your curiosity the last time we spoke?\n\nVery well, ask your questions. I'll answer you truthfully, though I cannot promise that you'll find my answers more satisfactory this time.

Entry 1. I spent so many years idolizing Seht's perfect creations, but he is a fool. When one machine doesn't work, you don't leave it incomplete. You destroy it and build anew. So why is this imperfect world still standing? Why does Nirn exist?

Entry 279. Those Painted Eye fools care only for profit and their leaders are far too simple-minded to double cross me. While they deal with Thoryn and the Laboratory's security, I'll disable Protus.\n\nWith the Probabilis, I will make things right.

Entry 228. Still no documents on why Seht continues to allow a flawed plane to exist. Why allow this broken place to continue? There may be answers within the Probabilis, but Protus refuses to open the doors. Obstinate machine.\n\nI will have answers.

What an absurd accusation! I've done nothing but go out of my way to assist fate's chosen, and this is the thanks I receive?\n\nBelieve what you will. I've told you how to find the shrine. Do as you see fit, chosen.

Tides no! Most fates don't rise to this level of importance. Only potent fates, those with the chance to alter the very course of the planes, can be found etched into these glyphics.\n\nThis makes every fated glyphic a powerful and coveted object.

Yes. That's why Hermaeus Mora requires outside help to deal with this threat. He can't rely on his own Daedra in Bastion Nymic. \n\nYou can expect no mercy from Mora's former servants. Give them none in return. Eradicate them all.

Let's just say they choose not to examine my methods too closely. The Lord of Secrets provides me with eyes and ears in many places. That can be very useful in my work. I repay that favor when he asks for help. Such as now.

Just a suspicion. The Telvanni have always concerned me. Their hunger for power leads them in unwise directions, such as disturbing the temporal flow.\n\nI know we're not supposed to interfere. But I feel it's required.

Indeed. A mystery only a Cosma could solve! This glimpse of fate wasn't a warning. It was a clue. A piece of an exciting new puzzle I've already started on.\n\nMora will regret not smashing this fate into dust. Farewell, meddler.
It's a gallery! Of special beasties and other things. Secretly special, no one knows why. Except for Hermaeus Mora. But he knows everything, so that's cheating.

Who knows. Maybe he likes it. Maybe he keeps dangerous creatures here. Maybe he doesn't have a reason. \n\nThe ciphers spent a long time trying to figure it out. Wrote their theories down in books in the study.

I see her slipping away over and over. We're leaving each other.\n\nPeople, faces, names, paragraphs, they escape through holes in my mind. All the Ciphers are dead or dying. If I can't hold onto her, who's going to remember Frielvi?
That's right. They also taste of raspberries.

Minds rely on what they think they know. But truth doesn't care about you or what you think.\n\nLooking into a Known Thing, trying to comprehend the impossibilities of them, does funny things to you. Like make you grow an extra toe.
He posed no danger to me. But I am finished with Akacirn now—I have learned what I needed to from his dark ambitions. If he has wronged you or others, do as you will with him.

The expunged spells are still quite potent, so we hold them for a time to allow their energies to dissipate naturally. \n\nIf you must, feel free to search the rune piles for your summoning ritual. And let me return to my work.

Only recently. That was Nathyn's idea.\n\nAfter losing my family, I sought safety and found it in Tel Dreloth. But over time, we both realized life is too short, too precious to spend it stuck in just one place. We decided we wanted to see the world.
The book invokes the pact I made. I transcribed the spell into it. When I spoke the words aloud, Herm'us Mora's writing appeared beneath it, agreeing to the deal.
Burning the book and the other items finalizes my agreement. Unless it is fed to the brazier, there is still a chance Herm'us Mora would return my son to the depths and let him drown.
Ah, that is a treasured totem of my past life, of my lovely wife and devoted son. It is marked by the hand of Herm'us Mora when he agreed to spare my son's life.
With this glass I beheld Herm'us Mora rising from the sea in response to my evocation.
It nearly shattered my mind, so horrid was its visage.
Uh. Well, yes. It should be. You know, frightening. Isn't it?
Good. My arm was starting to cramp from all the cursing today. Thank you, and good luck out there with the witches!

Oh, right. Tremble at the sight of my greatness! My power is not to be trifled with! My curse is deadly! But you can be spared, for the right price.\n\nI'm even running a Witches Festival discount—ten percent off all curse-free encounters!
Oh, I will, foolish one. I will. Receive my curse!
Oh. Both of us? Right. Y-you know, that sounds like a good idea. Let's do that.
M-my soul? Yes, of course—take it. No, no, no! Not my soul. I mean the gold! The gold! Here, take it!
You will? I mean, of course you will! Being cursed is no fun for anyone. Well, goodbye then.

Nervous? Me? Darkness incarnate? A little. B-but only because I'm afraid of what my curse might do to you!\n\nThat said, I like you. S-so I can let you walk away for much less than I usually charge. What do you think?

From what I understand, she's trying to cure the Knahaten Flu. It took the life of her husband many years ago, when Nathyn was just a baby.\n\nI'm sure that's why she's so protective of her son, but it's no way to let him live.

Hmm. Never heard of him. The letter we found claims he's an unaligned Dremora working with Vaermina and Peryite. And with Master Shelreni, too. It's highly unusual for a Dremora not to be dedicated to a clan or a Prince.\n\nThat mention of a dream ….

Would it matter? Nathyn deserves to make his own choices, regardless of his mother's wishes.\n\nAnd if she really felt that way, why wouldn't she just make her feelings known instead of throwing me out? I wasn't trying to steal him from her.

I wish I knew. If she were any other Telvanni master, I'd guess she didn't want her son settling for some lowborn servant girl.\n\nBut nothing like that ever seemed to matter to Sathile. She was far more focused on her research than her rank, anyway.
Um, well, now that you mention it—do we really need to talk about this? I don't think we should talk about this.\n\nUm, aren't you supposed to be talking to Scruut right now?

Hmm. Apocrypha can be overwhelming for mortals. You may find power or despair, knowledge or madness. Still, you bear the mark of Hermaeus Mora. I think you're meant to go there. And, damn it all, I think I'm meant to go with you.
No, it's not you. It's the Witches Festival. This time of year always puts me on edge.
It's … it's him. You know, him. He-he appears to me. Do you understand?\n\nI'm not crazy. So many people think I am. So many people. Too many people!

It happens when there are people around. One of them approaches and w-whispers unspeakable things to me. And I know it's him.\n\nNo one sees. No one helps. He tells me they're all in on it. He tells me everyone will h-hurt me if he tells them to.

Well, yes. Let me be honest—I'm afraid of crowds. It's always difficult for me, but it's unbearable around the time of the festival. So many people! So many masks!\n\nSo I come out here to wait it out. <<1>>, here,  is a calming influence on me.

And I see him in his true form. H-His teeth are long like fingers. His fingers are sharp like teeth. His breath smells like rot and death.\n\nWhatever you do, don't let him talk to you. Once you do, he'll come back. Now please, go. And be careful!

The memories released from the two glyphics are accurate and true. Ithelia. The Prince of Paths, the Mistress of the Untraveled Road, the Unseen. Her ability to alter fate, to shape destiny to her liking was a threat to all reality. \n\nIt still is.

I gathered my fellow Princes and revealed the danger I foresaw. Most agreed to aid me, some refused. In the end, it did not matter. I erased Ithelia from history. But I could not erase my own memories. Those I sealed in the three primordial glyphics.

What mortal could? The Fate-Changer is an arbiter of chaos who can unravel the strands of fate and rearrange them to suit her every whim. Her very existence endangers everything.\n\nI saw no other way to preserve reality than to do what I did.

Just one of the skills I've picked up. I can manifest my image in your mind from a distance. It takes a great deal of concentration, so maintaining it is difficult.\n\nI'll use this projection to keep you apprised of my progress. And check in on yours.

Surely you've experienced this before. I will insert my image into your mind when I need to speak to you. It will be temporary due to how much I'll need to concentrate.\n\nI can observe your progress this way, and inform you of mine.

Able to invade Apocrypha unnoticed and break into the realm's master index? Our enemies are bold and capable it seems.\n\nThree different locations and three different schemes. They must be connected, but how? What are Mora's foes trying to do?
Very little, actually. It's not what she said, rather ….\n\nWhile packing, I found a note in my belongings signed by Nathyn, full of hurtful things. Things I know he would never say to me.
I'm certain of it.\n\nI know Nathyn's handwriting, and more than that, I know his heart. He'd never say such cruel things to me. And the fact that Sathile made up those lies hurts me even more.

Leramil and I spoke with a few of the ciphers and we're all in agreement. We want to add your story to the Chronicle of Apocrypha. Only the most momentous events make it into that sacred volume.\n\nI also wanted to say, you expanded my outlook.

I always saw fate as black and white. Set in stone. Unchangeable. But now I see that not every aberration is a disaster, not every surprise a mistake. Thanks for that.\n\nNow, let's inscribe you in the Chronicle. Then Curate Gadayn wants to see you.

Imagine time as a woven fabric with threads that cross and stitch together. That distortion bound the threads unnaturally.\n\nA crude analogy. Time isn't made of physical strands, of course. But it's the best way I could think of to describe it.

They scattered once they broke into the Catalog. But two headed toward the Pool of Inquiry—a Dreamcarver kynreeve and a second Dremora with markings the likes of which I've never seen.\n\nPlease. You bear the Great Eye's mark. Stop them.

Delmon. Mistress Dreloth's greatest experiment. The cure, the affliction. Delmon did this. \n\nTrouble breathing. Barely survived. The other researchers, not so lucky. Too late for them. Go no further. You could be killed!
Ah. I see. So your half-informed mind proves far more dangerous than an uninformed one.\n\nYou cannot help. Leave this place, or I will do everything in my remaining power to stop you.

That's good. That's very good. I appreciate it. Besides, I want to let the abbot know what you did. You preserved Nirn as well as Apocrypha through your actions.\n\nBy the way, did you find Torvesard? Leramil has been dying to know what happened.

A living cure, a symbiote that protects its host with toxic spores. I would not be alive without it, and it would not thrive without me.\n\nAll these years, she really has been trying to cure me so I might live a normal life. Why did I ever doubt her?

I have returned to Artaeum. I am locked in a cage of warded glass for observation. I sit on a rooftop in a city between places, watching. I feel the bite of an arrow piercing my shoulder. I dance in a warm rain.\n\nI die in bed as my son holds my hand.

He's helping us. Like me, he's had trouble putting his old life behind him. He helped me track down an old contact of his who's working directly with Sondivel Ulres.\n\nApparently, she's established a lab and slaving operation nearby.

Nonsense! My enormous intellect certainly came in handy, but you're fate's chosen. You would have found a way, with or without me.\n\nBut I'm glad you rescued me from Shelreni. That you took me on this adventure. If I never escape this soul gem ….

Elistrenne Starflower. She's in Senalana, an Ayleid ruin north of here. Our source said to look for a door with her namesake growing nearby.\n\nShe may have information on Sondivel, but she won't give it up easily. Dispose of her how you see fit.

Maybe. I'm in no rush. Adventuring is a new experience for me. I'm content to follow along for now. I'm going to rest for a while. Remember, as long as you have my gem, if you ever need me, just call.\n\nNow, talk to Scruut about the Chronicle.

The truth is a poor cure for love. I did not want Dacia to share my fate of being shackled to Tel Dreloth by her own heartstrings. So I tried to drive her away.\n\nBut since hers is a love that clearly cannot be cured, I have devised a choice for her.

Of course I did. I was glad for it at first. Dacia brought Nathyn happiness. If only they could have remained content being in love with the wards up between them.\n\nIt was only when they doubted me that things got dangerous. And now, here we are.
They provide a nutty, hay-like flavor. Covers up the bitterness of the brew, you see.

I suppose my research notes wouldn't give you the whole picture, would they?\n\nTun-Shei, one of my most devoted researchers, discovered it in a pool of brackish water deep within Black Marsh. Its capture and transport was quite the undertaking.

When bonded inside the lungs of its host, Delmon Mycota passively produces spores toxic to almost all non-fungal life, as you saw in the caverns.\n\nIt seems to eradicate anything that might threaten the life of its host—including the Knahaten Flu.

Correct. Somehow, Delmon Mycota recognizes itself, and of course doesn't see itself as a threat.\n\nArgonians like Tun-Shei are a different case, but only barely. Their natural resistance to toxins very nearly meets its match with Delmon Mycota.

It is sensitive to smoke, a herald of fire, which causes it to release reproducing spores in anticipation of finding a new host.\n\nThese are the spores we would use to inoculate Dacia, if that is what she chooses.

I'll have to, won't I? And Tun-Shei will help me, as he's always done.\n\nI pay well, and the world is in no shortage of those who lost loved ones to the Knahaten Flu. I don't anticipate any trouble in finding more help.

I'll have to, won't I? And Tun-Shei will help me, as he's always done.\n\nI pay well, and the world is in no shortage of those who lost loved ones to the Knahaten Flu. I don't anticipate any trouble in finding more help.

I'm always suspicious of good fortune. But any day I get to gut a slaver is a good day.\n\nI guess I shouldn't credit all our progress on luck. Really, it's you. What made you stop that day in Necrom to help me?

Sharp wrote me for help if you can believe it.\n\nAll I could think of was if he's writing Belvis Salavel, courier for the Antiquarian Circle for help, it must be really serious. Of course, he did also write Mevei and she tracked me down. Now I'm here.
We used to know the same people, once upon a time when I was richer and better dressed. \n\nUnlike Sharp, I had plenty of friends in my old life. Looks like the two of us are evening out these days.

They capture us to work, but also to study. Experiments of our mind.\n\nIf we solve the puzzle, we can go free. So they say. It cruelly mocks us. I believe they change the solution in secret. That way we never succeed.
To build their homes. For entertainment. To experiment on. Take your pick.\n\nThe man you slew was brutal. He enjoyed watching us fight. I will not mourn him.

We work day and night to build their homes. They have found something deep below ground. Now they want to expand the settlement.\n\nMore and more of us arrived every day. But with you here, we can go home.

I wanted to know everything. I found what I wanted—which is different from what I was looking for. I know that which shouldn't be known.\n\nDiscovering the secrets of the secret keeper has its consequences. Confined. Stuck! Like me!

Why would I want to do that?\n\nOh I may have been different in the past, clearer, purposeful. But that person learned all he could to share it across the darkness. I learn because I enjoy it. Not selfish. Pure. This is my purpose.

I was a poor guest in his realm, but he did invite me. He sees too much and I hear the same amount.\n\nHis attention wandered. I don't feel the light of his eyes on me all the time. I can move in the shadows now.
Servant, retainer, oathman, spellwright. Regardless of station, we all do what we must to get by.

The pact refers to ancient laws that bind the Daedric Princes. No Prince may physically intrude in another's realm. Everyone knows that. Well, perhaps not mortals.\n\nThat they sought out that tome tells us something important.
Well, then we'll have to be sneaky mortals and try it anyway.\n\nI'll join you outside. I'd like to say goodbye and hello to Frielvi.

But you and Scruut were not fooled. For that, I give you a gift. So that I may better aid you against this ongoing threat to my realm and yours, I will make this Watchling available to you for the duration of our agreement.\n\nNow, Leramil comes.
Forgotten Crypts—that's in Deshaan. In the heart of Pact territory. Of course, who's going to focus on slave operations when there's wars and plagues ravaging the region?\n\nAny word of Dimik-ei?
Federo and I will wait for you and the others nearby in Narsis.\n\nYou're really doing this, aren't you? I only wish Reynila was here to see it, too. Good luck, my friend. Stay safe.

Just think, what could you learn by looking beyond your own life? At the paths unwalked? What kernels of truth could you hull with such a tool?\n\nI hoped to gain knowledge about myself, about the universe, why … about the very nature of mortality.

An excellent question. I'm a scholar of esoterica, eldritch secrets, and things mortals were not meant to know. \n\nI'm an arcanist of the highest order, proud to say. Wresting the power of Apocrypha into my quill-gnarled hands. As you do.

It's not my fault! I mean … ahem. I was attempting to peer beyond the veil of our reality, much as Hermaeus Mora does. To gaze upon other fatelines. \n\nIt would have been brilliant. Should have spent more time developing my infralux notation.

Hmm. A simplistic example. Not all choices are equal. But if the choice to have oatmeal instead of eggs changed the course of your life …. \n\nThink of them like divergence points. And everything you could learn seeing the might-have-beens play out.

Arcanist is a broad brush, to be sure. But we're all devotees to abstruse arcanum, individual proclivities aside. From mad hermits raving about tentacles to precision runecrafters. \n\nI consider myself a scholar, first and foremost.

Ahh! A fellow seeker of knowledge! Do you hold more to the tentacular school of thought, or are you more of a rune-carver? You're not one of those tiresome paddlers in the fathomless seas, are you?\n\nApologies, we can compare notes later.

I'll procure that, worry not. Don't want you to think I'm taking advantage of your assistance.\n\nOnce you have the dust and talon, we'll meet back up at the ritual site I've marked on your map. What do you say?

Trade them for something they want. I see them in Fargrave sometimes. Always pushing people around. Sometimes they even do business with Madam Whim.\n\nAh, that's how they knew poor Hezehk carried a secret. Probably tracked me the whole time.

Wasn't my choice. Madam Whim wants a boon from the big Eye-in-the-Sky. Wait, I should probably be respectful while I'm here.\n\nAnyway, the Ravening Morass is where they built the Obscured Forum. And that's where I can get the boon. So, here I am.
No! I never said that. Why would you think such a thing?\n\nMortals talk too much. Leave Hezehk be and find the mirror.
It's nothing. Not every piece of detritus you see on the ground is about you.

You don't give Hezehk orders! But, yes, I'll use this cloth and notebook to locate them.\n\nHmm, should have guessed. They went to the Obscured Forum. Right where I was headed. I bet they plan to trade the secret for their own boon. That's my job!
Let's see. What's useful in a book store? Get me a tomeshell feather, a glob of mold—red, not green—and, oh right, a quill. Hezehk has never had a great memory, but that should do it.

Oh my. I hadn't dared to hope, but it seems this prism is a Daedric artifact. And a powerful one at that! This prism could accelerate my studies beyond imagining.\n\nI can't imagine Dreynis was happy about parting with it.

You didn't know her for long, but you might remember her longer than my mind will allow. Thank you. \n\nNow, let's find the Forbidden Exhibit so we can both get out of here. Cipher Frielvi's memory will only live as long as we do.

Paper memories? Of course! Records and histories live longer than mortals. With all the books and thoughts here, no one gets lost for too long. Not even to time. \n\nMaybe I'll run into Cipher Frielvi in the shelves. Then I can remember her again.

Giving Vaermina access to Apocrypha and a host to work through. They must know where to find the memory they seek. Or they have a good idea where to look.\n\nApocrypha is infinite. Without fate to guide us, we are lost in the dark without a candle.

Blightcrown and Torvesard have ways to avoid detection. Only one viable option presents itself. We must ask Master Shelreni where Vaermina has taken her body.\n\nWill you see this through, proxy? Before the disaster Mora foresaw comes to pass?

Frielvi calls it the Feral Gallery. It's a good name. This is an untamed catalog of monsters and creatures. \n\nThe ciphers kept the peace—made sure no one wanted for food or fun. Some creatures roared, others tweeted—I spoke!

Oh yes. I'm not a cipher, they're the caretakers here. I'm an animal.\n\nThere was a time when I had powerful enemies. My staying here appeased them and it gave me some safety—and books. But now it's dangerous.
I'm not dead, so maybe they don't hate me enough to kill me. But, I am trapped. \n\nNot in the gallery, I wanted to be here. The ciphers also don't make me wear socks. Life is better here.

Those Daedric bullies think they can bring pain and suffering into this library? It's quiet here!\n\nBesides, pain and sickness aren't scary. They should really look into the terrifying experience of finding out your book's missing the last chapter.

She runs the gallery, leads the other ciphers, and takes care of us all.\n\nThe ciphers serve the One Fate of Tides. No, that's not right. They serve … Moron Hermes. I'll get this eventually. Hermaeus Mora.

They wanted to? Or someone wanted them to. \n\nI know they killed the ciphers. I just hope Frielvi isn't dead yet. I don't want to be stuck here if nightmares control the gallery—it's nightmarish enough with the gallery as broken up as it is.
I made a deal. Join the gallery and stay in one place in exchange for all the books I could read. \n\nI should've negotiated for all the books I wanted.

I walked. And then did some magic that makes my brain hurt. I think I went to other planes first. But if I try to remember, the voices come back and I don't like them. They ask questions. \n\nYou're also here. You know what I'm talking about.
The arcanist you travel with sought to view the paths unwalked, but failed to see where those paths led. In his hubris, he has allowed a thing that should not be, to be. \n\nTem has spoken.

Not yet. One thread in the tapestry snapped, but two more remain. If you can keep my enemies from unsealing the final two glyphics, there is still a chance to preserve Apocrypha and the rest of reality.\n\nYou saw how this began. The Great Omission.

Do as you have done. Follow your heart. Return to Leramil. Consult with her. Defeat those who oppose us. You will know the best course of action when fate requires it.


Now, I must conserve my strength. Apocrypha is under attack and I feel its pain.
I'd be more concerned if Federo had written acting like nothing was wrong. Asking to put me on another job or something. It's not like him to not write.\n\nIt's the other stuff that worries me more.

It's not the threat of danger so much. I know we can handle whatever comes our way.\n\nIt's the Reformer, I suppose. The note we found where he mentioned me by name. I try not to think about the way he talked about me. How unsettling it was.
Some part of me wonders if I'd be better off not knowing the answers. But I guess we'll have to see.

Me, of all people. Guess that's how we know he's crazy.\n\nI guess that's what has me so unnerved. I mean, I've done awful things for money, but what's he doing them for? And what do I have to do with any of it?

Oh, information? Seems harmless enough to me.\n\nHe had me seek passage to Eastmarch for him. Paid me in wine to do it. Let slip he was headed to Tonker … Twinkler … Tinkerer Tobin's workshop, I think. Does that help?

What a curious query. Where else would I research and ponder the knowledge that the One Who Knows deigns to share? It is a humble refuge, nothing more.\n\nNow, we really must see what information we can draw from the stacks of Cipher's Midden.

I was with Abbot Ilvel when Prelate Faram arrived. I was barely introduced when the abbot sent me to get tea from the market.\n\nI'm worried about the abbot. He's always been kind to me. He and the monks raised me after … well, I had no other family.

I think he brought this sickness to the Necropolis, yes. Perhaps he picked it up on the voyage to Necrom … although neither he nor his aides appear sick.\n\nI wish I could ask Abbot Ilvel about it. But Prelate Faram won't let me inside to see him.
Maybe? But if it isn't spreading to the prelate or his aides, is it really that dangerous? I have no idea.

A powerful Watcher that protects the Known Thing and all the creatures down in the Forbidden Exhibit. You may not always see it, but it sees you. It might ambush you if it thinks you're a threat. \n\nI hope that doesn't happen.
There's a barrier. It keeps the exhibits inside. We can't leave the gallery. Those Daedric Dreamcarvers mucked everything up. Now there's no one alive to bring me books! We had a deal!

Simple! Cipher Frielvi. She'll know a way, and she might be alive. But, she won't be easy to find. No! The bristleback lords won't let us through. And Dreamcarvers! Yech!\n\nIt'll be worth it, though! Help me find Frielvi. She'll give you a treat.
Don't speak his name! I'm sorry. I—I need some space. Please go.

Vaermina, the Daedric Prince of Dreams, and Peryite, the Daedric Prince of Pestilence. They set aside their animosities to challenge Hermaeus Mora, the Prince of Fate. They pursue a secret they believe is connected to whatever offense Mora committed.

Hermaeus Mora selected you to help preserve reality from a threat he foresaw. Your ability to alter destiny and fate makes you instrumental in the struggle ahead.\n\nWe learned that a secret Vaermina and Peryite seek threatens both Apocrypha and Nirn.

Torvesard is a Dremora without a clan. He seems to be the linchpin that negotiated the alliance between Vaermina and Peryite, all because he believes his lost dream concerns some wrong they think the One Who Knows perpetrated against them.

You and Gadayn recovered a portion of the relic, the Fulcrum Obscura, from the catacombs of Necrom. The rite appears to be related to a Black Book once in the possession of Magister Meln. \n\nBoth seem to be essential to the enemy's search for a dream.

Apocrypha contains all secrets and knowledge. Whether they be dreams or memories or tomes, they all wind up here.\n\nWe know that Torvesard learned something at the Tranquil Catalog. We need to conduct our own research now and try to get ahead of them.
The Nords and others who frequent the Tinkerer's camp seemed affable enough, but I got rid of any identifying information, just in case they started to doubt my story.

I don't know, he seemed nice! He had these grand new ideas, powerful connections. Things that mattered to me. \n\nJust goes to show: first impressions aren't everything. But you know that—you're friends with Sharp.

Whoever wrote me said I could go to Tobin's as a sort of safe house—they would know somehow that I'd made it there, and they'd be along to set me up right with a new life, new identity.\n\nBut nobody showed up. Until you and Sharp did, anyway.

The one in Adept's Retreat? Small world. I hope you gave her my thanks.\n\nAnd I hope we see each other again. Remember, the world isn't against you—it just seems that way when you're up against a rich and powerful Telvanni magister.

Reynila? Not the one the Reformer was after? I didn't know she was freeing his slaves until it was too late. No wonder she didn't come for me. She's dead, isn't she? \n\nWho is Mevei? Someone dear to Reynila, I imagine?

I haven't the faintest idea. And hopefully, I'll never have to think about such things again.\n\nI'm glad to get away from all this. The Reformer really is unhinged. You'll see what I mean when you find that cache.

He had it in his head that he could eliminate the need for slavery in all of Morrowind, if you can believe it.\n\nHe was very protective of his methods, of course. Typical Telvanni. But he said the slaves he had were a necessity to perfect the process.

Now that you mention it, the air in the lower holds smelled … unhealthy. And the passengers kind of gave me a bad feeling, though I can't rightly say why. \n\nLook, tell the port master I'm sick and can't work today. For once, that's the truth.

Look, illness is a part of life when you work with the dead. I'm surprised the Keepers of the Dead aren't sick more often.\n\nPlague can be serious, but I'd need more than your word to shut down the port or quarantine the city.
You were there along with the many multitudes of me. Didn't you see the light of darkness? Fly in the weight of truth? Slurp the dredges of your mind through a cup?

Of course not. Why would you? You're only mortal.\n\nYou were selected to help Hermaeus Mora save Apocrypha and Nirn. To do that, you must uncover the very secrets the Great Eye's enemies pursue—secrets that can unravel reality as we know it!

I don't know. All that raspberry smell made me close my eyes.\n\nEither it's in the box, or it isn't. The moment you go back and check, it'll decide where it is regardless of which answer you like better. Best not to wonder and let it be both.

For me to complete my task, you must succeed in yours. Which is clearly impossible, since you can't overcome Apocrypha's protections. Which means you won't be able to save fate, so I suppose it doesn't really matter. Reality will unravel soon enough.

Obviously. Everything of Apocrypha is of Hermaeus Mora. Only through the Great Eye's will could the sacred tomes be destroyed.\n\nYou were chosen. And then I was unlucky enough to become involved. For good or ill, our fates have become tangled.

You and Gadayn must use the part of the relic you possess to do the same as the enemy—locate the entrance to the Panopticon. There are cairns throughout the realm. Sprinkle this dust of conjunction on three of them, then let Gadayn apply the relic.

Only what I read. It exists outside the time and space of Apocrypha, hidden from all. It supposedly contains many of Hermaeus Mora's most closely guarded secrets.\n\nThe interior is said to be so bizarre that the very sight drives mortal minds insane.

Do not fear. My decades of study have made me mostly impervious to the horrors of forbidden knowledge. And you are fate's proxy. You should be able to survive a visit to the pocket dimension.\n\nBesides, to save both realms, we have no other choice.
