People worship all sorts of things. Peryite's followers see disease as a blessing. They revel in suffering and spreading plagues.\n\nBlightcrown's attendants have pox scars. I should have suspected something when I first met them.
He does seem the type to get lonely very easily. And he acts all put-upon when he does.\n\nMaybe I will, then. For his sake. And only because you suggested it.

I only have Blightcrown's word about that. I'm not even sure if the abbot and the keepers are really sick. When I returned, the place was already locked tight and I was ordered to stay at the door and turn pilgrims away.

As Prelate Faram, Blightcrown has the authority of the Temple. The Necrom Guard would never make a move against a Temple prelate or the orders of the abbot. No, we need to get inside and find the abbot ourselves. Before it's too late.

You did? Prelate Faram—I mean Blightcrown—spoke privately with Abbot Ilvel when he first arrived. His attendants didn't speak at all. I wonder what they could be seeking in the Necropolis.\n\nWhat was the Hidden Kindred doing in Alavelis?

Apocrypha? By the ancestors, what does our Necropolis have to do with Daedric Princes and Oblivion realms?\n\nStill, there are all sorts of treasures in the catacombs. I'm not sure if the keepers even have a complete record of everything down there.
What name would you have given it? I briefly considered calling it Piffle. \n\nBut Martina used to call magical instruments gubbins, and I was feeling sentimental.
Yes, well. I thought I could steward a new arcanist and it … did not go well. \n\nThey failed to have either the zeal or intellectual curiosity you do, cohort.

Oh. It acts as reliable help down here. The way things are with the Mages Guild, I try to keep entry and exit to a minimum.\n\nBesides, I don't want someone messing up my papers. Or having them quit on short notice just because something exploded.

Just so. With the improved key as a focus, this scrying ritual should be even more effective. It was a stroke of luck I recognized Fathoms Drift, last time around.\n\nLet's away to my Inner Sanctum and scry. Onward and upward.

Hmm. I don't remember that coming up in any of the abbot's lectures. But Prior Durdryn possessed many talents. Legend has it he could command powerful Daedra and resist their lures. And he was given some sort of charge by Lord Vivec personally.

I only visited it once, with Abbot Ilvel when I was very young. It's somewhere in the lower catacombs, at the very deepest point in the Necropolis.\n\nRemember, Blightcrown brought the Hidden Kindred with him. You might have to fight to get there.

Before I met you? I used to pass through Stormhold every now and again. As far as cities go, it's not so bad.\n\nBefore that? No idea. Could be that I hatched in Shadowfen before the Reformer's slavers took me. But who knows.

It's a mysterious artifact that amplifies dreams. Vanton hoped to study how the subconscious informs a mage's arcane talents. There were whispers that a sinister presence lurked in the stone, but we had no idea Ansuul was a powerful Daedra.

Well, I introduce myself as "Azandar al-Cybiades." Which to another son or daughter of Ruptga means I hail from an island off the coast. \n\nIt's all a bit of braggadocio, though. Part of the mystique! Ahem.
Sure! Anything. What do you want to know?
Yes … yes. I'm even more brilliant than I imagined! The bobbin is rattling against the key, straining at its runic bonds. It now acts as a passive frayed fate detector. \n\nIncredible! Phenomenal!

Have you heard the way he talks to me? He thinks he's better than I am because he's bringing homemade goods to Necrom. I don't have the skills to make the offerings my ancestors want. Is it so bad that I buy them instead?

I burned up any hope of finding my forgotten past a long time ago. I decided to move forward, and I haven't stopped since.\n\nWhat if the Sharp I was hates the Sharp I've become? What if Dimik-ei is only doing this because she misses her kaj-kujei?

She did little more than purchase them from a merchant. There's nothing that ties her family to the offerings except an exchange of gold. If I were her ancestor, I'd feel snubbed, deprived of a connection to the lifework of my family. Forgotten even.
A thing can be both dangerous and boring. The universe contains multitudes. \n\nI truly believed I would be able to master fate itself without entering its walls. Vexing to have been proven wrong.

Yes. Of that I have no doubt. Martina is a consummate professional. \n\nJust don't get her started on the transliminal properties of exogenic materials or the writings of Denogorath the Dread Archivist. We'll be there all day.

I guess she probably wants that as much as I do.\n\nThere's other things for me to consider. Other things I'd remember. Less pleasant things like the Reformer, and the years, and years, and years under his control.

I'm not used to looking at the world that way.\n\nYou're right. There's no way to value my past when I don't know exactly what I've lost. And if Dimik-ei can shoulder everything she's been through, then I should be strong enough, too.

I'm glad I have you to understand me.\n\nI suppose we have to give Dimik-ei credit. She and I have lived nearly the same life, and she remembers all of it. I have to be as strong as her. I have to try. It's the only way we have of moving forward.

Mevei had all of Reynila's notes on what the Reformer was up to.\n\nShe was going to destroy them. The grief of losing Reynila—she wasn't thinking straight. I convinced her to leave the notes with me. They're here, if you want to read them.

My tribal elder Nuetepa said it best—I'm a seed that's finally been allowed to grow.\n\nSharp taught me plenty about survival. Those skills are useful, but what I've found with my new tribe isn't just surviving, it's actually living.

Horrible things about tyranite calx. And that de-attunement can be accomplished with soul magic.\n\nI'm interested in exploring defensive or preventative applications of soul magic, if such a thing exists. I'm still learning how it all works, exactly.
Superb supposition. The key is indicating … hmm. North and east, out of town. Perhaps the old ruins?\n\nHere, take the key. Let's move!

Small freedoms keep slaves in line better than total subjugation. \n\nBut for Sharp, it was his last piece of home. His tribe of fishermen. Tugs on the end of a line saying they were still with him. It's the only time I've ever seen him truly at peace.

Well, he hatched under the sign of the Thief, if that tells you anything. He's sly and stubborn and his thoughts run a lot deeper than he lets on.\n\nI knew Sharp from the moment I hatched. He named me, taught me some Jel, and showed me how to fish.

A specific one. Portals and Pustules: Maladies of Inter-planar Travel. It's just the source I need to prove my theory about the effects of traveling between Mundus and Apocrypha.\n\nI was taking it to my desk, but it disappeared on me!

Even if that were possible, I found this book at the bottom of a pile. It can't go back. For a variety of reasons. Including that books cannot move on their own! \n\nI appreciate your attempt to help. Maybe I just have to retrace my steps.
You question my memory? I could kill you for even thinking that I might be wrong. \n\nI know exactly which book we've been sent to retrieve. Wolfhound and Sea Breeze is a classic.

My associate and I are book hunters, we seek the tomes that are too well hidden for others to find and return them to their rightful places. Or we would if Nassophra didn't keep forgetting which books we seek.

In a way, yes. I'm working my way through the Telvanni rankings and the only thing standing between me and the next title is this obstinate fool. He thinks his magic is stronger than mine. Ha! I'll crush him.

An exam. We're going to cast our best spells and see which one of us is fit to join House Telvanni. I'll win, of course, but I just have to figure out the best way. Stopping my opponent from casting anything would be ideal, or course.

Necrom. A nook there awaits my urn. A shelf that, once I arrive, I can never leave. So I spend my days wandering nearby, waiting until my time comes to make the final journey.\n\nAre you familiar with the Necropolis?

No way! Our work is dangerous, and you know what he's like. He'd just get in the way. Or killed. Or hurt. And then we'd never hear the end of it.\n\nBetter if he just settles into some cushy little life somewhere. Not that it'll stop him complaining.
I guess our finding her in Windhelm inspired her to pick up Reynila's work where it left off.\n\nSounds like a lot of work for her to take on alone. Hate to see her make the same mistake Reynila did.

Precisely. Each time, our expertise with this particular bit of metamagic improves. The connection between the Fateweaver key and choices along my fateline grows stronger.\n\nMy hope is to find multiple fate sites, this go around.
The Daedric Prince has many faces and is known by many names. To the Khajiit, Hermorah. Herma-Mora to the mer. Among seafarers, he is called Herm'us Mora, he who resides in the darkest depths.

Do you honestly think my people need a legitimate reason? Well, how about impersonating a Necrom official? Or infiltrating a meeting of the Masters Conclave? Not to mention acting in the service of a Daedric Prince?\n\nWe can't risk it.

Ah, so I received word to let the bedlam in the study run its course. I'm beginning to think it may have been a purposeful test for reasons I can't guess.\n\nAlas, this is an occupational hazard for serving the ever-enigmatic Prince of Apocrypha.

Are we who we are only because of what we remember? Or are there some parts of us that can't be stolen?\n\nHe doesn't seem too different from the Sharp I knew. If he's still a big baby when it comes to bad smells, he's practically the same.

The Three Waters tribe. Sondivel always said I'd be lost if I ever returned to Black Marsh, but he was wrong. There are others like me and Sharp, either hatched in slavery or with no tribes to return to. We're not lost or alone. We have each other.

According to Reynila's notes, it will be as if you are Sharp himself.\n\nI'll be channeling the magic. It won't be an easy process, which is why we're starting small—just one memory, whatever surfaces first, to see if this even works. Are you ready?

So long as her predilection for jumping into danger remains ever so constant I'll never frown at the quiet moments like this one. As if she can be very quiet.\n\nBut I jest. Traveling with my sister is an adventure, but one I'll always enjoy.

I can't complain, and I'm normally quite an expert at that! It's been nice having Vorm around. It's usually so hard to drag him away from his books that it's funny it took him becoming one to get him out here!\n\nIf only mother could have seen him ….

Oh, she's off on the next big adventure you could say. And don't feel sorry! We don't. Our dear old mom did more in her life and saw more wondrous things than any ten other folks combined, and that's a fact!\n\nAnd now her kids are off doing the same!
I lost my memories years ago. The Sharp that Dimik-ei knew might be gone for good. His replacement isn't a ray of sunshine. I don't want to hurt her more. She's been through enough.

Because with a piece of tyranite calx, we can act as a conduit for Sharp's memories!\n\nThere must be something in his past that would help you track down Sondivel. He was so sure Sharp would be his forever. He told Sharp everything.

This is why you make a good collaborator. Your focus. I place in your hands the Fateweaver Key. Still flawed, unfortunately, but newly modified thanks to Martina's notes. \n\nFollow along with me and we'll seek out a frayed fate!
Truly? I have no Aurbisal idea why a path unwalked would lead me there.\n\nBut Martina was shrewd, clever, and other complimentary words. We can trust their work.
Truly? I have no Aurbisal idea why a path unwalked would lead me there.\n\nBut Martina was shrewd, clever, and other complimentary words. We can trust their work.

Martina was as nimble-witted as anyone I've ever met. And stubborn as the abyssal sea. If she thought they could twist fate itself, nothing would slow them down.\n\nChanging the fatelines is something not even Hermaeus Mora himself can do.

Fine. I belong to the finest league of assassins in Tamriel. In Morrowind, we're part of the legal establishment. Instead of going to war, the leaders of the Great Houses employ us to settle scores and keep the peace.

I must! My fate is still frayed, after all. It must be restored, and this dark being dealt with.\n\nBut now, a question for you! Would you be willing, if you have the time and inclination, to continue our collaboration?

Vanton will wake when he's ready. Twelvane doesn't know the extent of the damage Ansuul left behind, but she will help him however she can.\n\nIt may be a long time before Vanton can return to his duties.

Does he seem like an arrogant and powerful mage to you? Even in his own mind, he second-guesses himself. \n \nWith Ansuul gone we can work on strengthening his resolve. But for Vanton, it may be a long time until the nightmare is over.

There are healers of the mind. We'll send for one as soon as he awakens. The mind can be a surprisingly resilient thing.\n\nFor now, we'll support Vanton and do everything the healers say to help him get well. No matter how long that takes.

She's gone. This one doesn't know if you killed her or if she just retreated from Vanton's mind.\n\nAnsuul will return if she can, but Twelvane will ensure the Dreamstone is carefully guarded. Ansuul won't surprise us again.

Ah. Yes. The second volume of the Numinous Grimoire. A very dangerous book—any mortal who dares to read it is driven mad. It went missing from our collection recently … and now we know who took it.\n\nI'd better put it somewhere safe.

The Numinous Grimoire is dangerous. At a casual glance, it's illegible. But if you study it long enough, its meaning becomes clear—and you go mad. Nelfynn should have known that.\n\nLeave the book with me, and I'll put it away. Safely, this time.

We are scholars. Scribes. Seekers of knowledge. Mortals drawn to Apocrypha from all corners of Tamriel. Here we help tend Hermaeus Mora's infinite library. In return, the Great Eye grants us access to its contents—infinite knowledge.

Apocrypha can be dangerous for mortals. Cipher's Midden serves as a refuge of sorts. Here, those who follow the cipher philosophy come together for protection. Creature comforts. Fellowship, after a fashion.\n\nIt's not much, but now it's home.

Hardly. Most mortals visit Apocrypha in solitude, seeking answers to questions important to them. But some of us come to realize that no ambition in the mortal world compares to what surrounds us here. We choose to stay in Cipher's Midden.
For once, I have no stars to guide me. I cannot simply return home to my wife. I cannot tell her Landolvel thinks me to be a stranger.

Bodies? What are you—? Oh. You mean the vessels. I forget that non-ciphers get a little confused when they come here.\n\nLet me take a few steps back. Welcome to the Rectory Corporea—Hermaeus Mora's library of minds.

Yes. Well, mostly. It's not the most exact metaphor. But the broad strokes are apt.\n\nThe vessels have their minds joined together in service to Hermaeus Mora. Their combined psyche—the Chorus—thinks and dreams and my master listens.

What? No. No, no, no. Every vessel here willingly entered a pact with Hermaeus Mora. They surrendered their bodies and minds to the Rectory for a fixed period of time. In the end, they will receive … well, whatever it is they wanted from the Eye.

Normally they just lie there! The Rectory's magic keeps the vessels healthy while their minds serve the Chorus. They—they don't just get up and say scary things before keeling over!\n\nWait. This vessel is dead? Oh no!

They never try to break free! But if they did … I suppose it is possible. Even the gradual extraction can cause stress. Nosebleeds. Seizures.\n\nBut something the vessel said—"another failed body." Those were its words, remember?

Precisely. This worries Huzmargo the most. Something may be toying with the vessels in the Rectory and killing them in the process. But Huzmargo doesn't know what could do such a thing.\n\nWe should check the Rectory Archives. They are just next door.

Hired by a client of his, I think. Didn't sound too happy with him. And they weren't too happy with me after I hurled all over the one holding me.\n\nLot easier to lie when you're sober, but where's the fun in that?

Oh, we're just friends. Drinking buddies, really. I think he always had a thing for one of his mercenaries. Told me about him once, but I forget.\n\nI'll set you up with him, if you like. He's a great guy, really. Gave me his house!

No cipher has authority over another. The only law in Cipher's Midden is that of Hermaeus Mora, and he takes no interest in our dealings with each other. Our society survives because we choose to follow the customs of this place.
It is … unprecedented. I believe I can convince my fellows to expel or punish a murderer for our own collective protection. But I do not think we have the time I need to build that consensus.

Oh, that. I thought it'd make Sharp seem dangerous and unpredictable. I thought it'd throw the Reformer off his scent, and mine. \n\nAnd I thought maybe the Reformer would be afraid that Sharp was coming for him next. And look, now he is.

Turn over my best mercenary? I couldn't live with myself if I did that! Only got as far as I did on the peninsula because of Sharp. I might have called him my friend, if he were the type to make friends.\n\nSpeaking of, who are you, exactly?
Of course he did. Gold, power, prestige. He practically sounded like a game of Tribute. \n\nIt'd have been so easy. And I'd be living like a king right now if I had!
A fair question. When I first left home I was desperate to shake the metaphorical sand from my boots.\n\nWhen someone asked my name in a Sentinel marketplace, I couldn't bear to tell the truth.

I catalog mortal delusions. Misapprehensions, follies, and fallacies, especially as they pertain to the nature of realms and beings beyond their own small world. A fruitful and ever-growing field of study.
Knowing is its own reward, mortal. Besides, I serve Hermaeus Mora, the Prince of Forbidden Knowledge. What is a heresy, if not a forbidden thought?

B'vek, never! I could never …. He would strike me dead for speaking out of turn. With spells and such!\n\nI mostly keep my head down and stay out of his way whenever possible. That's why you should deliver the tincture, not me.
You wouldn't! Would you? No, please. If you did it would be very dire for me. And maybe you too. I wouldn't recommend that option. In fact, perish the thought of it all together!

A ghost is dead, but the Numinous Rite unmoors a living soul. Like any mortal thing, it must sustain itself by consuming something. The souls of others, in this case. One can see why the book's author made it difficult for mortals to read.

I'm not here on business, if that's what you're asking.\n\nI don't get to see all these mages and pilgrims in my line of work. While I won't say that it's nice to be among them, it is a change from my usual routine.
How strange. As no one but masters are allowed inside, Master Norvora explicitly told me to wait out here until after the conclave concluded its business.
I know. We meet up when we're in the same area. It gives us an opportunity to compare notes.

I've wandered the streets and marveled at the architecture, yes. Being welcomed into buildings of import and wealth is unusual for me.\n\nAlmost as strange as encountering a competent adventurer. No offense.
Well currently, I'm taking advantage of our host's hospitality. \n\nPowerful figures rarely go to the effort of providing food and drink when I show up at their door.
The Morag Tong aren't a small organization, but our work isolates us. And there are very few of our number that I find tolerable.\n\nNaryu is … usually one of them.

Wait until I'm issued another writ. Keep my skills honed and do my best to avoid feeling aimless.\n\nI think the grandmaster wanted me on hand in case the Telvanni couldn't deal with Master Shelreni's threat, but you handled that. Thanks. I guess.
Well, obviously Master Norvora needs her spell book. No master should ever meet her peers without being totally prepared. I'll go and fetch it at once.
How rude! The Ald Isra Committee of Social Decorum will hear about this insult. Of that, you can be sure.

This is the Telvanni Peninsula. What other options do I have?\n\nIf I just make him sick, he'll blame me for it. If I do nothing, I'll just continue to be bullied. Please, take the tincture, but just don't tell him. That's all I ask.
Oh, you know. The usual. Cleaning this, tossing that. Busy, busy!\n\nI also, uh … I need to avoid the mushrooms. Yes, that's it—the mushrooms. All those spores in that area are murder on the sinuses!

By the Three, no! I'll leave that to you and Sharp.\n\nI'm helping Mevei to relocate whoever it is you're freeing. Guide them from lamp to lamp until they're safe. Easy to do when you're a courier of the Antiquarian Circle.
Nagging? How rude. I hope I don't really nag.\n\nDid you feel anything else? I need to know if subconscious desires interfere with what I'm issuing as conscious directives.

To enter the chorus, every vessel signs a pact. You think of flimsy parchment contracts, yes? Not so in Apocrypha! It is an anchor that binds the vessel's mind.\n\nNo one can travel far from their pact, and Huzmargo has a spell that can sniff it out.

At the very least, it will tell us who the mind belongs to.\n\nI do not know what shape the spell will take inside the chorus. Each vessel's perception of the space is unique. But it should be easy enough to manipulate and follow.

Yes? Yes! But dealing with him means killing him—a task that is a little more difficult than just stabbing his choral manifestation. Huzmargo would need to make sure the Daggerfall Devil couldn't flee to another body and hide.

Huzmargo thinks so. But we will need to act at the same time. Like two claws pinching a well-oiled grape.\n\nHuzmargo will need to leave you to find the body while you find the mind. The pact, thankfully, provides us with some inkling of where to look.

Leaping into other people's bodies may have caused some mnemonic bleed. Elements of his psyche—memories—could have broken loose.\n\nI'll tune the spell to seek out his memories. If you can find enough of them, it should lead us to his mind's core.
Looking for other necromancers. This may be the Mages Guild of Necrom, but we don't practice that magic here. \n\nIt's disrespectful!

Or anyone else's. \n\nWe have very strict rules about this sort of thing. Our ancestors deserve our veneration and respect, if you disturb even one of them, you call down the wrath of every Dark Elf in this city.

Very funny. No Dark Elf will ever show you there, let alone leave you to your own devices. The dead here are protected and you will not interfere with them. \n\nSomeone from the Mages Guild will be watching you while you're in our city—just in case.

I don't know how you can even practice the magic you do. Raising the dead … do you want your afterlife to be filled with torment? Or worse, have no afterlife at all?\n\nYou've made a very terrible mistake. I hope it doesn't send your body to Necrom.
I didn't. I just hoped you wouldn't do it and it seems as though I was right. I shudder to think what might have happened had you sold me out.

Wait, you didn't know? I thought for sure I had bungled it. Huh. I'm a better liar than I thought!\n\nHonestly, I had no fallback. It was a crime of passion. I just hoped you'd show me some sympathy. And it all worked out! Well, except for Llaro.
And Magister Meln thought us so ineffective that he had to swoop in and save the day? How presumptuous of him.\n\nDo you really think one rogue master is a match for this assembly?

Enough of this nonsense! I listened to the concerns of your magister and heard his allegation. Now we are finished. \n\nMeln may stay if he wishes. That is his right. But you and the curate should go and leave us to our work.

So I heard. Hence the reason I decided to leave my comfortable tower and come all this way to personally take charge of this conclave. The masters will hear the charges, question the subject, and render swift judgment.

Don't mind if I do. Balver Bemis sent word that he had made a tincture for me. Glad you managed not to get lost. Damn these headaches! Makes it hard to concentrate and deal with my indolent and incompetent retainers.

Yes, quite a display. She used the conclave to formally announce her intentions. Her spell would have killed everyone and positioned her to challenge the archmagister for rulership of the house. Luckily, I was on hand to save the local masters.

Really now, who do you think Meln consulted when he first invented his cloak of omission? I see the mark of Mora upon you. House Telvanni wants no part in the machinations of Daedric Princes.\n\nJust make sure to kill Shelreni when you find her.

Shelreni may be a powerful master, but I am a magister of the Telvanni Council. It was a simple matter to deflect her attack while the conclave dispersed. Then I stabilized the portal she fled through, assuming you would want to follow her.
Good. I have no patience for that sort of thing.\n\nDid either of them happen to say anything incriminating? I haven't eliminated a Telvanni master in quite some time.

No. But if anything happens, I know you've got my back.\n\nAnd if it alerts Sondivel that we're coming—good. I'd like to see him run. Let him feel like the prey for once. And more than that, I'd like to save Dimik-ei.

Why would you? You are merely mortal. But I have wandered the planes of Oblivion for eons, an outcast with no clan.\n\nI believed I was formed that way. A forgotten scrap of creation. Until the dream began to haunt me. A fragment of an ancient memory.

All of my years wandering the world on my own, I'd never met anyone who genuinely just wanted to help me before.\n\nI guess I want to say thanks. For helping me figure out … not who I was. But who I am. Who I want to be.

Heh. Guess we're more alike than either of us care to admit.\n\nThen I'll just say … thanks. For helping me push this far, helping me end this, and letting me figure out who I really am along the way.

The unraveling of reality, Hermaeus Mora called it. All because Vaermina, Peryite, and Torvesard seek to find a dream remembered only in Apocrypha. We must ferret out why.\n\nHopefully the knowledge stored in Cipher's Midden will aid our investigation.

We shall rebuild. Our order may have seemingly collapsed, but perhaps we can rebuild stronger. We will create a more solid foundation.\n\nWe still believe in serving Hermaeus Mora. The task is still worthwhile. We feel rededicated.
I am not superstitious. But my father, on the other hand, would mutter some prayers into his locket each time we set sail.

Among seasoned sailors, Herm'us Mora is both a blessing and a warning. Speak his name with dignity and one may cross the most vicious seas with little more than slightly damp boots. Ignore him and you risk his wrath.

Not enough. Dralys could be counted among their number, along with the arcanists who fought beside him when you defeated them. They are Daedric cultists devoted to rival Princes. Their cooperation relates directly to the threat Mora has foreseen.

The unraveling of reality, Hermaeus Mora called it. All because Vaermina, Peryite, and Torvesard seek to find a dream remembered only in Apocrypha. We must ferret out why.\n\nHopefully the knowledge stored in Cipher's Midden will aid our investigation.

Unclear. No matter what comes, I must secure the collections inside the Cenotaph. Pact or not, they hold dangerous power.\n\nAfter that, I would like to learn what happened here. Perhaps I go on my own journey to seek knowledge. Alone.
It pains me, but he chose to save me, at the cost of his memory. I'm unsure what happens next, but I will watch over him, in hopes that one day we might journey together.
I will remain until I find a new path. Perhaps I may guide him a bit longer. No longer as father, but as companion. There is a settlement southeast of here, I understand. I shall lead him to safety.

Let Leramil guide you, as she can perceive the threads of fate without undue mental anguish. They converge in three locations, places of revelation. Meet her in the Necrom Bindery, in the mortal city of the same name.\n\nNow let us seal our covenant.

The most devout of Sotha Sil's worshipers. They live almost exclusively in the Clockwork City. I heard they even cut off their own body parts and replace them with mechanisms—didn't believe that until I met Nilphas Drethan.

Only the greatest achievement since the creation of all life! The Magician's mechanical world. It's a marvel, a wonder!\n\nI've never actually been there or seen it, Truthfully, the city is hidden away and none but the Apostles know where it is.

Do I look like a Cipher of the Eye to you? A simple scribe or archivist toiling away in the endless stacks of Apocrypha?\n\nOh very well. Those are the clues you uncovered for the Great Eye during your investigations in the Telvanni Peninsula.

The Great Eye says that without your help, reality will unravel, starting in Apocrypha and then spreading everywhere—including your mortal realm of Nirn.\n\nNow, this is just a guess, mind you, but I assume that happens if they recover the dream.

The message, mortal? The one I just delivered? Leramil is ready to get on with the research.\n\nYou know that the relic is called the Fulcrum Obscura. And you think the dream is locked away somewhere in Apocrypha. If the Hidden Kindred find it ….

Oh, I am! I sail for a small temple tomorrow. \n\nIt won't be as grand as Kemel-Ze, but it will be quieter. The Temple must be pleased with my diplomatic exploits. They're sending me to a place where I'll have to interact with more miscreants.

No, and I doubt I ever will. It seems like doors to Sotha Sil's laboratory are sliding shut forever. Protus will be all right. As far as I know Factotums don't experience loneliness.\n\nSotha Sil, in his infinite wisdom, gave them that comfort.
I can't say. Sacred temple secrets to uphold. \n\nI thought my betters were going to be furious that I even told you about Kemel-Ze, but apparently I made the correct decision.
I have to hope so. But if it doesn't, we have to consider every option.\n\nThe Reformer made me an offer, if you remember. Turn myself in, and all his slaves go free.
It better not. I haven't caught nearly enough trophy fish to consider myself a respectable angler yet.\n\nAnd they always seem to bite more often when you're around.
If I can't kill the Reformer, he'll hunt me forever.\n\nBetter that I alone satisfy his obsession, if it means Dimik-ei and the others can be free of him.
I truly do not have the time for this. \n\nFine. If it means you're less likely to poke your nose in matters where it doesn't belong, then I'll listen to your queries.

I didn't replace my flesh out of curiosity.\n\nIf you're wondering what one of Seht's most devoted followers is doing here, I came to study his greatest machine and keep it protected. Which is what you're keeping me from.

That mechanism there. They were built to maintain the Clockwork City. Usually they stick to singular tasks—sweeping, maintenance, that sort of thing.\n\nThis one is a prototype. One of the earlier models, which explains its poor condition.

In addition to the three to take you to the locations you must investigate, I summoned two gateways to Apocrypha.\n\nOne leads to the Endless Library, a place of books as numberless as the stars. The other to Chroma Incognito, where lost fates linger.

That is what we must determine. The various repositories of Apocrypha are infinite. Books, glyphics, vaults. We have ascertained that if this particular secret is uncovered, it has the potential to destroy reality as we know it. That must not happen.

Flesh is flawed. Why else would Seht create a world of mechanical permanence?\n\nIn the Clockwork City, my arms allowed me to access more research and study more mechanisms than you'll ever encounter.
It's broken. \n\nIf I had to guess, the damage occurred during the Painted Eye's attack.

A world set apart from our own. Seht—Sotha Sil, whatever name you call him by—created it. It's a place of machines where everything runs routinely and very little changes.\n\nI'd be surprised if you ever laid eyes on it.
Then why did you ask me what it was?\n\nYou've wasted my time when Seht's greatest works could be under siege.

While Vaermina hides from me, I glimpsed Peryite's lapdog break into the Mythos before my sight faded. He spreads corruption into the realm's foundation. As Apocrypha succumbs, the realm will crumble. Such destruction will ripple throughout reality.
The Unquenchable Brazier is a kind of a beacon for the blighted souls that are damned at sea. Herm'us Mora calls to them.

Zemzo is Master Thilse's servant. She requested this one to observe the meeting and report back. Though she is quite concerned about the situation, her many responsibilities demand she focus her attention elsewhere.

Of course not. There is something unusual about that Dremora. Not the least of which is the fact that the One Who Knows cannot detect his presence.\n\nBut Torvesard obviously requires something from you. Use that to your advantage.
What choice do I have, mortal? The Great Eye commands and I obey.\n\nBesides, whatever Torvesard did to me, it seems to be holding back the worst effects of the corruption. At least for now.

Truthfully, I have no idea. I've seen you accomplish some amazing feats. And Hermaeus Mora has faith in you. But this is the Mythos we're going into. To face the champions of two enemy Princes. Maybe even the Princes themselves.\n\nNot my usual fare.
Are you offering me a way out? Thank you, friend, but I'll pass. I promised the abbot I'd recover the Fulcrum Obscura, and Torvesard assured me Blightcrown has the relic.
It's as you say. For our purposes, it's a direct connection to Herm'us Mora himself. There we'll offer the sacrifices of my past so that I may guarantee my son's survival.
If you have to ask, then you don't need to know. Or deserve to.\n\nSuffice it to say that Master Foves requires an urgent matter dealt with. However, the help doesn't appear especially motivated.

To end him. But that's easier said than done. With the strength he's gained now … who knows what my adversary is capable of.\n\nI will throw myself into this research with the full force of my faculties, cohort. You have my word.

Entry 239. There are no answers. No resolutions. No recorded thoughts or explanations. Nothing!\n\nThe Clockwork City exists, as does the Probabilis … maybe this is what I am here to achieve. If Nirn can be fixed, it will be with the Probabilis.
Privacy! Supplies. And erm … materials. You'll see when we get there. I'm quite proud of the place.
That is a long and mildly scandalous story. The short version is that Telenger the Artificer, gloryhound of the Mages Guild, lost a wager. Badly.\n\nI'm afraid he doesn't like me very much anymore.

It is simultaneously vexing and alluring in equal measure. I'm still unsure what I did quote unquote wrong in making the Key. \n\nBut with Martina's notes and some hands-on experimentation during our first adventure, I have had much to go on.
Me? Question the Prince of Fate? I would never! No, no. That's laughable. I have journaled about it though.
Meenai-Shai and I are tending to the Cloisters. There is a great deal of upkeep that we must catch up on now that the cycle has been broken.

We still … uh-ah, I apologize. The transition is challenging.\n\nI still wish to serve Hermaeus Mora in some capacity. Perhaps I will become a wandering knight and roam across the realms in his name. I suppose the choice is mine now.

I am hiding. Didn't you hear me? I did the invisibility dance. I'm even crouching tactically behind this crate! You can only see me because you helped me before. We're tied now. \n\nJust don't betray me to the eyes and their shadows.

Yes! So pleased that she knocked a century off my debt. That's not a lot compared to the full amount, but Hezehk still appreciated it.\n\nI, uh, didn't mention your help. Hope you don't mind. Maybe it could be our little secret?
Well said! And you can count on me for every one.
Well enough. It feels like a part of me is missing. But I want to thank you for everything you've done, for me and for our peoples.
It is, occasionally. I'm trying to keep a positive outlook though. We've been reunited and for that I'm thankful for what you've done.
I'd say that risk will always be there, yes. But if it happens again, I'll be prepared. Thanks to you!

He's chatty. Too friendly for my taste. Lures people in just so he can get them under his thumb and in his debt.\n\nLast time we did business, we … didn't see eye to eye on something. Let's leave it at that.
I know because the Sotha Sil who made me knew.\n\nKnowledge, foresight—whatever name you give it, it is my burden.

The pompous mortal riddled with disease? The memory rejected him. We entered together but I stand here, alone. Except for you.\n\nBut worry not for Peryite's priest. Blightcrown has skills. It should be a simple matter for him to return to Nirn.

Such is the duality of my mind. I know I am not the true Sotha Sil, but my memories are his. My thoughts mirror his.\n\nI speak like him, because the memories allow for only one way of speaking. I exist only for the sake of this conversation.

You seem resolute in that. \n\nThe truth—which is what I promised—is that this wasn't your decision to make. It was mine. I did what I had to as you would have done in my position, regardless of the outcome.

Protus will preserve the Mnemonic Fragments so I will not fall to ruin, but I will not grow or develop either. I will be stuck in stasis until such time as circumstance alters my course. I hope my original does not face the same fate.

I could offer you a convincing lie, but I did promise the truth.\n\nKnowing and understanding are entirely different. I knew what I needed to create down to every gear and wire. But still, I did not understand a single piece.

My laboratories here in Kemel-Ze were the beginning of a much larger project. I knew where my experiments and tinkering would lead, but without starting here, those goals would never be achieved. Because I knew my success, I also knew my course.
Is it safe to go back?\n\nWhat happened?
What? A Clockwork Apostle wouldn't do that! But, you did say you knew Protus. And if you met Protus then I don't have any other choice. \n\nWait what do you mean Protus will be the only caretaker?
There are temples all over Tamriel. I'll travel to the nearest one and go from there. Maybe I'll be assigned somewhere new, I haven't been outside Morrowind yet!

Then only some of the lost memory has been restored. The most dangerous portion of the secret must still be hidden.\n\nVery well. If you plan to honor your contract and still want to help save Apocrypha and Nirn, I shall assist you as best I can.

She keeps a room in town. I'll mark it on your map.\n\nCareful, though—Deredrien and Reynila were old friends, but they fell out some time ago. Asking after one might cause the other to be very … sharp with her answers.

All right, don't get so touchy, f'lah.\n\nReynila was through recently. I can tell you what I know, but not without a favor in return. Why don't you deliver these red flowers I just gathered to some dear friends of mine?

Maybe. My job broker told me to track down Reynila and take back what she stole for an important client.\n\nHe didn't give other details, and that's usually fine with me. No memory of my past makes no answers an easy pill for me to swallow.
When she lets me. I'm skilled in forgeries and logistics, but I've never done field work. Not like her.\n\nIt's dangerous work, and … well … she's always been very protective of me.

We have thought about that for a long while. Those who left claimed to lose faith in our lord, the Eye that Wanders. This confused us, but we accepted it.\n\nPerhaps if we pushed harder for their return, some of our clan would not call us a dead order.

We faded. It started slowly. Our numbers dropped subtly. We noticed our strength waning as our clan dwindled. The more who left, the weaker we became.\n\nA cycle of withering began. Weakness bred deserters, which led to more weakness.
Your question confuses us. We told you, we are the Remnants. Should we feel concerned that you weren't listening?

Ah, now the problem becomes clear. The Remnants are a whole. Our minds, linked. Our experiences, shared. We do not distinguish individual parts the way mortals do.\n\nSpeaking in your tongue, the best word to describe us is we.

Do you recall Tem, the Omen of Fate? I'm loathe to say it, but that Daedra's skill with fateweaving outstrips even my own. \n\nIf I offer him a contract, I believe he can quickly and efficiently transform our anchors into a Runeform of Unmaking.

The flow of magicka through every hall is different. Each resonates with a unique arcanic potential. It's all in the subtleties, you know.\n\nAlso, I stole the key to the ritual room at the Riften hall several years ago and they still haven't noticed.

Hmm. Your fingers—do they not form your hand? And your hand, it is part of your body, yes? As is your foot, your legs—these are you.\n\nSuch it is with us. The Remnants are a body. To perceive the parts as separate misunderstands our nature.
Right. Won't take but a moment.

The rules are quite explicit. Only the name of the writ is my target, and that's just Tredecim. Guitot is the spy and he's my target. Anything more is up to you.\n\nDo you want to tell Master Sulis about Master Foves' plan to set him up?

He's the Magician, the Clockwork God. He, along with Vivec and Almalexia, make up the Tribunal—the Living Gods.\n\nAs a member of their temple, I worship them all and carry out their will. Letting mercenaries into Kemel-Ze is a failure of my duties.

Not much to tell. I just arrived myself. This mortal served the Great Eye, but he died before he could tell me about the other Daedric cultists that scamper about.\n\nThey're creating an intolerable contradiction in reality. Makes my tentacles ache.

He's not alone. Kemel-Ze is filled with Dwarven machines, Fabricants, and there's even a Factotum who oversees all the security measures. \n\nBetween the Dwarven constructs and Sotha Sil's own mechanical creations, the Painted Eye should slow down.

Oh, yes of course. \n\nFabricants are beings created by Sotha Sil of both metal and flesh. They're works of genius who populate the Clockwork City. Factotums are entirely mechanical and resemble large suits of armor. They talk too!

Something here undermines a fate recorded by Hermaeus Mora. Likely foolish mortals trying to change what has already been written. To fix this, I could use some help.\n\nHmm. It's common knowledge that mortals prize gold. Aid me and I'll give you some.

You stand before none other than Armiger Bolm, the Paramount. I abide in this place, awaiting challengers that will further my legend and renown … or see it ended. \n\nI seek to duel those willing to fall to my Tribute deck.

You stand before none other than Armiger Bolm, the Paramount. I abide in this place, awaiting challengers that will further my legend and renown … or see it ended. \n\nI seek to duel those willing to fall to my Tribute deck.

Forsooth! To fell a foe with my axe's blades is no challenge at all. It has been years since I faced a contest, a struggle, in a test of arms.\n\nTherefore, let these cards be my weapons. This deck is blessed by Mother Morrowind herself!

I am as the apex kagouti, coiled to strike. Are you the gentle guar, bearing your throat to my jaws? Or are you the cliff racer, come to pluck my eyes from my skull and feast on my carcass?\n\nDraw your cards. Chance and skill will guide us now.

In time, but for the moment I must perfect the forty-seventh canto of my dirge-oath. Forty-six times I stood on the precipice of death. And forty-six times I have danced in secret ways to avoid it. As my gods have taught me.\n\nReturn anon, traveler.
Precisely. I suppose you could say that I worked backwards and in doing so found more answers than I thought I had questions.

This is somewhat embarrassing. He was a big talker, lots of energy, a fun person to talk to. I had a bit of a crush on him. \n\nI'm not sure he ever noticed, to be honest. He was more interested in arguing with the senior members than me.

That was a long time ago, I have to imagine he's become less … impetuous since then. And I'm married, thank the stars!\n\nYou're welcome to look for the rubric. I'd try chests and coffers first, it has to be around here somewhere.
Right. What's in my heart. Helpful to the end, that's you. Well, I might as well get this over with.\n\nOh, while I pull my thoughts together, Leramil wants to talk to you.

That is good to hear. Even though the assembly enacted the writ, I know that Naryu is under no obligation to keep us informed. I appreciate it.\n\nI know better than to ask for specific details. The Morag Tong prefers to work unhindered. Anything else?

You did, did you? Interesting. Yes, I'm working on something with Masters Foves and Thilse. We've been meeting frequently until fairly recently. Then Foves stopped attending. He's worried about the spy. His aide delivers him notes after each meeting.

I totally understand. What some call paranoia, I call prudent caution. This spy could cause irreparable damage to the assembly, if not to House Telvanni itself.\n\nTell me, what did you and Master Sulis talk about just now?

If they can perfect their formula, what better way to steal the most dangerous secret in Apocrypha than from under the gaze of the One Who Knows?\n\nBut if we can stop Master Shelreni and they cannot find the secret they seek, it shall not matter.
Don't you see? When they convene the Masters Conclave, Shelreni must be on hand to contest the charges. So, we know where we can find her and when!

Oh really? If I recall clearly, and I do, he read the first two paragraphs when I presented it to him. \n\nThen insulted me using several words I'd never heard before, and threw the document in the fire.

You don't think I'd give my only copy of a written piece into his hands, do you? I have another.\n\nHowever, my assistance comes with a price. I always liked Azandar, despite himself, but he insulted me that day. Truly.
You have to understand, cohort, at the time I thought it was merely a scholarly disagreement! \n\nI'd spent months on my dialectics. And I felt I was being dismissed as unimportant, unoriginal.

I mean. Yes. You're quite right. I just remember how angry I was … but in truth. Her arguments were well-thought out. Insightful, even.\n\nThrowing her work into the flames, in front of her no less, was a childish act. Very well ….
The Dusksabers? They're mercenaries, f'lah. Efficient, capable, and rather expensive, but I believe in hiring the very best.\n\nNo need to worry. They won't bite anyone unless I pay them to.

Just what are you implying, outsider? That Mouth Elar isn't totally loyal to his master? What a ridiculous assertion!\n\nMaster Norvora must require her assembly log book. I shall attend to that at once.

Apocrypha is quite resilient. And since the burning sensation in my tentacles and the pain behind my orbs have mostly faded, I'd say yes.\n\nBesides, I can hear the melodious hum of the Great Eye resonating all around me, so that's a good sign.
Of course. Didn't you hear me? They know more than you think. \n\nJust because you can't understand them doesn't mean they're not wise.
Intuition? Context clues? Gestures? Motions? There are so many ways to understand the unintelligible. \n\nYou'd be surprised at how good spiders are at silent charades.

When Prelate Faram and his aides arrived, my fellow Keepers of the Dead were plagued with a strange malady. I was away when the disease struck and I haven't been allowed back inside since.\n\nThe prelate said the abbot ordered the closure, but ….

Prelate Faram arrived from the Temple and suddenly my fellow monks fell ill. We were never notified of a visit and besides, Faram isn't our usual prelate. Never even heard of him.\n\nIf you can help, I can make sure you're compensated. I think.

That has yet to be determined. One of the strands of fate revealed to me converges at this location. More than that, Hermaeus Mora expects us to learn for ourselves.\n\nOf the three sites, this one requires that I be on hand to assist you.

I never said it was more important. Just that fate requires both of us here. More than that, we shall need to determine.\n\nI do sense a lingering presence. A connection to Apocrypha. Help me investigate this place and Hermaeus Mora will reward you.
Since our purge of the Dreamcarvers, the Remnants feel renewed. We have dedicated ourselves to regaining everything that we lost.
I know. I miss him. But he honored his promises and remained true to his word. I respect him for that.

Their sensibilities don't extend as far as my fingertips. Whiskers and ears and a nose that wrinkles? Experimentation is very disjointed.\n\nWait for me outside? I don't want Frielvi to go into the dark alone.
One of the hunt! That changes everything. A hunter and hunted working together? We will rip our escape route from the Seeker's grip!\n\nGive me one moment with Frielvi. I'll meet you outside.

The thought had crossed my mind. But it would hardly be sporting, making an arrest and taking attention off your good deeds.\n\nI'm here to tell you that you're an inspiration. Your heroism across the peninsula has given me something to aspire to.

At this gathering to reopen the Necropolis? I couldn't possibly. As much as I might want to take him by surprise. \n\nBut no. It wouldn't be proper. We're here to celebrate, and that's precisely what I'm doing.
No more than usual.\n\nBesides, maybe I want her to see me. Maybe I've been standing here, waiting for her to look my way.
Excellent. We'll search for crumbs and keep out of sight. The barrier may keep the exhibits inside the gallery, but not two mice!\n\nI'll meet you on outside. I can't leave until Frielvi's gone.
Too busy! And that spellwright, Varsva, is just painful to work with. Perhaps I can make a tincture for her, eh?
Oh, we shan't be hearing from Balver Bemis any time soon. Of course, I still need to find a proper replacement.

She doesn't need it at all. She's in league with a Dremora, Torvesard, and a pair of Daedric Princes. There's apparently a rite contained within the book they want her to cast. In return, they'll give her what she wants—control of House Telvanni.

History. That's one way to put it.\n\nThe others in my order seem to delight in romanticizing this cat-and-mouse dynamic the Lark plays up between us. I tell you, there's nothing poetic about persistently playing the fool in someone else's story.
Haven't been to many. I suspect they're not really my thing.\n\nI hoped there'd be fewer people. And more food and drinks. But you're here, so it's not a complete waste of time.

A caravan of alleged pickpockets taking blame for the Lark's grand larceny? That's preposterous. And worse, it's unjust.\n\nQuestioning from an Armiger seems unnecessarily hostile. I'm glad to send you in my stead.
I appreciate your concern, friend, but I'm fine. More than fine! The knowledge I've gained is worth every twitch and spasm!
You were quite right to warn me. Even so, sometimes late at night, it's like I hear it whispering to me.
Worried? Hah, hardly! The only things to worry about in Kozanset are getting stung by a scorpion or your lips drying out. \n\nLet's make haste, cohort. These fates won't unfray themselves, you know?
It's an improvement on the ocular lens you used in my tower. I created a spell to produce the same effect without any need of a crude focus. Turns out, it works even better now that I'm dead.

Is that why you're here? To add another charge to Shelreni's list of crimes? Then so noted.\n\nPerhaps that's why she turned herself over without any fuss or bother. So that she can plead for mercy. Perhaps I'll be lenient. Perhaps not.

My Black Book, The Tormenting Eye contains many secrets. Ghost sight was one of them. With it, I can expand your senses. Allow you to see the hidden, the imperceivable, the unseen.\n\nI have no doubt it will prove important in the tasks ahead of us.

Is that a threat? Master Marena led Shelreni through the east door for making similar pronouncements only a few moments ago. If that can happen to a master, imagine what's in store for a lowly mouth like you.

I think I deserve some time off. A woman can only slit so many throats and stab so many backs before she needs a hot bath and a bottle of wine. Make that two bottles.\n\nAnd if I can find some company to share it with, all the better.

Don't worry. I haven't gotten caught in such a long time.\n\nNo, I'll stay here until the eyes swim from these shores and make a wake for me to follow. It's so much easier than fighting the current, don't you think?
Same as everyone else. I followed the spiders. \n\nI couldn't miss this. Imagine if I had to read about your celebration between the covers of a history report?

It's been quiet so far. She and Tun-Shei are still trying to find more researchers, but I'm sure they'll get back to it soon.\n\nNathyn thinks we'll be free before the year is out. He seems restless! I don't blame him. But me? I can wait.

I'll start at the Library of Vivec, then head over to Winterhold … Sathile and I have the whole route planned.\n\nAnd since she taught Nathyn how to project his image, it's like he's here with me! Sort of. He's still getting the hang of it.

Easy enough. Just a fair warning, friend. If Azandar offers to pay you back? He probably won't. The man has a hole in his coin purse as deep as Apocrypha.\n\nI'll summon the stone. Take it. And good luck to you.

I do, Azandar and I made it together years ago. It's hidden away in a cache of supplies. I'd even be willing to summon it here for you. \n\nIf the price is right. Those things are expensive to make, you know.

Blissful. Strangely so. I'm so happy, I'm afraid to trust it. Like it's a dream I'm going to wake up from.\n\nIt's odd having my mother on the other side of the wards. I suppose it's how most young adults must feel leaving home for the first time!

Missing Dacia, of course—but my mother's been teaching me how to project my image with magic. \n\nIsn't it brilliant? Anywhere she goes, I go too! Sort of. The image on this side isn't very … well, it's better than nothing!

When we've just started having fun? No, no. The Lark's got plenty of work to do, believe me.\n\nAnd if I wind up playing the fool in Rilasi's story more often, I think that's something I can live with.
Oh trust me, lesson learned. Especially after having to deal with that Imperial. He was exceedingly strange!
I can tell you that it won't involve time travel. I won't go near the stuff, not for a long time.\n\nWait, is that a paradox?
We were thinking of visiting another plane of Oblivion! Maybe the Realms of Boethia, or perhaps the Myriad Realms of Revelry? I hear those can be nice!

Without a doubt. I've realized that the experiment was just a shortcut to the acquisition of knowledge. Instead, I'll have to acquire erudition the old-fashioned way. \n\nTraveling with you, cohort? That will take no time at all.
Believe me, I don't plan on it. Being a book felt very … stiff.

No, I don't think so. My fateline has been shaped by our time together. Our imbroglios and carousals are far too entertaining.\n\nAnd as is the nature of fate, I'm a different person than I was before I made the Key. That time in my life has passed.

Oh, a very long time. While the core idea blossomed in the depths of that Dwemer complex, the twisting nature of fate has been on my mind since I was a child.\n\nThe Fateweaver Key was my magnum opus, the summation of my time as an arcanist.
Very well! Things at the mine are so much better since you came along.
Not well, I'm afraid. They are too afraid of the profits they stand to lose. I won't give up, though.
It's hard work, but we wouldn't have it any other way. And I do enjoy the antics of the scrib!
We took a vote and most of the team opted to head to Vvardenfell. We heard there are more opportunities out that way. So that's where we're going!

We decided to restore its glory rather than abandon it. Some of the knowledge was one of a kind and is lost for now. Everything still exists in the Great Eye's marvelous mind, of course. He'll replace the missing knowledge when he sees fit.
Our Cenotaph still requires clean up. We will stay together until our relics and tomes are secure.\n\nAfter that, we must perform a severing. It will be unpleasant. But necessary.
Our judgment was flawed. We saw an end where only a challenge stood. Now the Remnants find renewed purpose. We shall lift the sword and shield once again.
That can't be good. We better hurry to the masters private hall. It's through the north corridor.

This one was eager to pass it to the next generation of Baandari. He traded it to his nephew for a sweetroll. To feel it pass from this one's hands … there are no words, walker. It felt right.\n\nMay luck be with you all of your days.

Elsweyr. This one is old, many years past his prime, and his journey may end soon.\n\nHe wishes to see the desert one more time, and give the story of the Little Ancestor to any who would hear it along the way.
What? Why? You don't think that thief would return … oh, no. I never should have left! \n\nI just came to ask—but it hardly matters, does it? I could have just made something up!

In all honesty, no. In case you haven't noticed, we of House Telvanni are a superior lot. Sentiment and mercy rarely factor into our actions.\n\nNow, step lively. That portal will close as soon as my attention wavers, and I feel a yawn coming on ….

I'll keep the Stormwing quarantined until I can get it properly fumigated. Sooner or later, the ship's owners will send a new captain and crew from Vivec City. \n\nIf they can find anyone willing to serve on her, that is.

Ah. You wonder if there's a place for Master Shelreni's mouth in Ald Isra after all the things she did. \n\nDo not worry for me. There are a number of vacancies in the Assembly of Masters. I could be very useful to a newly promoted master.

I've ventured inside twice now. The corrupting influence of the scrolls is gone and I was in no danger of succumbing to the Hush. But madness still grips the Daedra and my fellow ciphers. I'm afraid Quires Wind isn't yet safe.

I decided it would be better to find a Daedric guardian for the grimoire. It's unfair to hide knowledge from those who seek it, but some books are simply too dangerous for mortals.\n\nNo more ciphers will lose their minds in the Numinous Grimoire.

An astute observation. The Fateweaver Key was created simply to observe the might-have-beens. This absolutely, categorically, should not be happening.\n\nIf not for you, it might already have killed me. A distressing notion, I must admit.

Research. Surely something back at the sanctum …. Or perhaps a tome we find in our travels? Either way, I have yet to find a question to which sufficient research does not hold the answer.\n\nBesides, I need to stitch Gubbins back together.

I'd hate to think that spectacle was the only thing calling pilgrims to the shrine anymore.\n\nAnd if the Lark succeeds, there won't be anything here worth visiting for at all! Please, make sure Rilasi stops him, will you?

Everyone in the village was given a job in the mine. Then others came. Masons and additional laborers, we thought. Then the dreams started. Nightmares. Toiling in the darkness. Working to cut malachite and stone for an arch and a statue.

You really don't trust me, do you?\n\nIf you must know, I was waiting until you ran off to try and catch a moment alone with Rilasi. If I had known what happened with Shadeya, I would have come straight here.

Nothing. All the times we met before, there was this fire in her eyes when she pursued me. Now it's … gone. I think I pushed her too far this time.\n\nI thought making my presence known would have just made things worse. So I left her alone.

Yes, the skeptics and faithless among us throw that line at me often. How original.\n\nYou really think because you could not reveal its secrets that it cannot be done? What a helpless world you must live in. I'll pray for you, sera.

Ah! Our partnership is the fulcrum we will use to topple this mystery. The adversary is me, after a fashion, right?\n\nBut he does not have access to our intellectual rapport. Nor our experience at surviving fierce battles. And so … we shall prevail!
I'm listening. What's on your mind?

Perhaps. We know Blightcrown used a corrupting combination of pestilence and dream to avoid detection in the Panopticon. And he was trying to increase its potency.\n\nMaybe the rite did more than open a path. Maybe it cut Mora off from his own realm.

This one has two answers. First, it would be much better to stop Ansuul before she gains access to all of Vanton's power. After all, it's easier to keep a star in the sky than return it to its place after it's already fallen.

Because Ansuul needs to break Vanton to gain control. She's showing him horrors which have driven countless others to madness. Turning his own mind against him. Torturing him.\n\nNo one deserves that fate.
