Well, you know how receptive she is to ideas that aren't her own.\n\nI'm so glad I got to see you once more before I left! Thanks for helping me make the right choice. You're traveling, too, right? Maybe we'll see you around!

And you! I just wanted to thank you. Dacia's traveling the world! She's radiant! I've never seen her so happy.\n\nI really think she's going to find this cure for me. I'm looking forward to the day when I can shake your hand in person!

Oh, no. Even if we did, we have the whole isolation tower to ourselves now. Plenty of space, and all manner of diversions.\n\nAnd I do hold out hope that my mother is on the verge of a breakthrough. Maybe we'll be out sooner than we think!

I still want to, sure! But for the first time in my life, I'm safe, provided for, and loved. So loved. I've never known such peace and happiness.\n\nSathile was right. I want for nothing. Thanks for helping me make this choice, stranger.

All the pilgrims care about is hearing how you and Rilasi stopped the Lark of Rosgard. But I don't know very much about you ….\n\nI'll just ask the others here about your exploits. Then I'm headed straight back to the shrine!
Certainly. It's made me realize that story with the Lark can be one of many in my service as an Armiger.\n\nThat story will still end with me catching him, though. Mark my words.

Blightcrown sounds unpleasant, but doors in Apocrypha lead to secrets. Something this Torvesard saw in a dream? Is that why Vaermina is interested? I suppose we should check the mine next.\n\nI hope I don't get hacked up. Reconstitution is irritating.

Reality. The place where we keep all our stuff! When Vaermina entered Apocrypha without permission—which should be impossible, I might add—reality went askew. My connection to the realm radiates with torment.\n\nBut the silence is worse.

I no longer hear the melodious decrees of my master! Hermaeus Mora is just … gone. And that shouldn't be possible, either!\n\nFind a way to fix this mortal, or I fear Apocrypha will just be the first realm to suffer.

I have no idea. Maybe I was limber. Maybe it liked me. Maybe I didn't survive it? Leave the arguing to the philosophers and the mountains. Hypotheticals mean nothing to truth. \n\nDon't worry. If this one kills us, we won't know.

You spoke to the Magus? One of the Three knows about this? He might know who I am!\n\nWell, if Sotha Sil is behind all of this, then maybe there's a different plan for me. Some other temple that needs attention. That must be it!

Torvesard behaves like a broker, bringing disparate parties together for mutual benefit. In truth, I now believe this is all about Torvesard. He has his own agenda.\n\nAnyway, he convinced the Princes to set aside their differences and work together.

Truth be told, I never much cared. All I wanted was to do what was asked of me and get my reward. Instead, I got a dagger in the back from that disgusting Blightcrown.\n\nThey believe Hermaeus Mora stole something from them. From all of us, really.
Silent, you say? Then my enhanced subterfuge concoction worked? Hehe, I told Blightcrown I could do it!

It involves Torvesard's dream. He had vague visions of a Vaermina shrine. Believed it was important. So he asked Vaermina to help him recall the entire dream. When she failed, he expanded his list of allies.\n\nThat's where the Hidden Kindred came in.

I took Blightcrown's mix of disease and dream and, with a few adjustments to the rite, enhanced its ability to hide them a thousandfold! If Mora has gone silent, it means it affected him, too. Cut him off from his own realm!\n\nAm I a genius or what?

Oh, fear not. You can't separate a Daedric Prince from their realm for very long. Should last just long enough for Vaermina to get whatever she's after.\n\nOf course, who can say what will happen when a realm and its Prince are sundered, even briefly?

I am not certain. The ritual I utilized earlier is not something I dare to perform again so soon. But there is another option. One I have only read about but never attempted myself.\n\nLet us forge ahead and see what fate has in store for us.

I did. I'd suggested that Sathile was being a little overprotective of him. \n\nWe were almost arguing about it when I just admitted that I'd fallen in love with him. But I didn't know if I wanted to stay at Tel Dreloth forever like Sathile.

I heard Sathile used to keep test subjects in the isolation tower. If she's keeping him anywhere, I imagine it has to be there.\n\nHe spends most of his time on the balcony of the main tower. But he hasn't been out there at all since I left!

Quires Wind is a scriptorium. Here the Great Eye's Daedra bind secrets into tomes. Ciphers like me help with this sacred task, preparing materials. Ink, blank pages, bindings. But the new scrolls Cipher Sabinius brought to the Wind are corrupt!

The scrolls give off a maddening aura. Sabinius left several hidden in the Wind. We need to destroy them, and make sure Sabinius has no more.\n\nThe Hush will take me if I go back. But an outsider like you should be able to resist. Can you help me?

One of the egg-hands, Gine, noticed young kwama returning to their pens with green slime. A few days later we started spotting cultists skulking about. What better way to poison a clutch than to taint the young ones. But there has to be more to it.

There are plenty other mines across the peninsula. Killing this brood would only be an inconvenience to the Consortium, but yet the cultists are here in full force. I'm certain there must be more to their plan, but I have to look out for the miners.
Just something from very long ago. Something I did not expect to encounter ever again. It is not important. Not yet.\n\nRight now fate requires a champion, mortal.

I'm a mercenary. Bounty hunter. Assassin. Whatever gets me paid.\n\nReynila stole something. Was told I'd know it when I saw it. Research notes to try and gain favor with some rival Telvanni magister, maybe. Tale as old as time in these parts.

No. Despite your status as fate's proxy, you seem resistant. Now explore Cipher's Midden and try to track down Blightcrown or determine how the affliction spreads. I shall attempt to locate Vaermina.\n\nRemember, they used censers in the Panopticon.
As have you and I, proxy. That is only natural when allies face unimaginable danger at each other's side.\n\nBeyond that, I would prefer if we did not mention this again.

The Chronicle can wait. This is more important! Why else would I have even mentioned anything, mortal? It's like no one ever listens to a word I say.\n\nAnyway, I noticed an anomalous thread not far from here. At the Prismatic Iris Shore.

A fate anomaly. The sacred task appointed to me? My job is to spot and correct them. It's really important, but you don't care.\n\nI think it's the stolen glyphic. Removing it from the Mythos triggered the irregularity. Luckily I happened to spot it.

I will mark a location on your map. Here we can open a path to the place Hermaeus Mora calls the Mythos. Not to a memory this time, but to the here and now.\n\nThen you can stop Blightcrown before the corruption becomes irreversible.
Good. Once inside, you will be my eyes. I will not be able to assist you directly, nor show you where to find the invaders.

Did he now? Well, most Telvanni try to steal from the best. But Garalo erred in coming to Gorne. Don't you know the nursery rhyme? "Two bantam guars in an alit's den, each came in one piece and left in ten."\n\nYou'd better turn around now.

You're welcome to my notes. They're scattered around. If you want to round them up, look for a glow. A little spell to help in case I needed to find them again. And ever so pretty!\n\nBut my new friends from the Shivering Isles might not like it.

My gift for teleportation magic is just that. A gift, from a Daedra of Sheogorath's realm named Straath. In exchange, I let him and a few legions of his friends come here to revel in the madness of the asylum's insane mages.

Torvesard? Of course. The Unseen. I cannot sense his presence.\n\nThe Black Book you carry. Use it if you need my strength. Just do not look directly into the pages. Even fate's chosen can be harmed by the briefest of exposures to forbidden knowledge.

Not much of a listener, are you? Adorable. \n\nGorne is an asylum for the mentally infirm—if you're a mortal. If you're a Daedra sworn to the Prince of Madness, it's a buffet. An opulent feast ripe for the taking!

You know how it is with eternal beings. "He stole my prisoner." "She gutted my vassal." "He's an embodiment of my sovereign's mania." "She's an avatar for Sheogorath's dementia." And then the blades come out.\n\nRather tiresome, I must admit.

Feasting, bathing, however you like to think of it. But yes, they slake their appetites with the inmates here. And me, too. Straath saw to that! \n\nNot all of them have the best table manners, of course. They're feuding with one another.

My patron! The little finger of the right hand of Sheogorath, the Prince of Madness himself!\n\nAll my facility with teleportation magic, I owe to Straath. He taught me how to break my brain in all the right ways.

Oh, no. The research I did in teleportation was all my own. He only set me on the right path. Gave me a little trinket to help light the way.\n\nBut I shouldn't go on about Straath's secrets. If you wish to know more, just read my notes!

I didn't say that. The fate of reality hangs in the balance. That's not something to walk away from. Not if we have the slightest chance of preserving existence.\n\nNo, I'll help you as I can. The spirit of a Telvanni magister and his surrogate body.

Just what Mora told you. Use it when you need to call on his strength. Do not look too deeply into the pages, though. I know from experience what gazing upon such knowledge can do to a mortal mind.\n\nI just wish Gadayn did not insist on going with us.

That's an excellent question. I had to employ numerous wards to barely study the thing without being whisked away to Apocrypha.\n\nBut if the Prince of Fate says you can use it to aid your mission, take him at his word. He has no reason to lie to you.
The Prince of Fate has his secrets and I have mine.\n\nThe truth is, however, I do not know. That is one of the things I hope to learn when I recover the stolen memory from the ancient past.

I believe the lost memory concerns us all. But yes, I think it holds a special significance for myself. What that is, I can only imagine. Not knowing, though … it drives me to reveal what was hidden. No matter the cost.

Practicing my evocation, of course. I know it must look odd, but I'm just embarking on my own studies. I came to Grandmother's shrine to ask for a little help. She was a Telvanni spellwright in her time!

Often? No. Still, I was hoping she'd provide me with a little insight into this puzzling tome. She always had a knack for making even the most difficult concepts simple.\n\nBut I think she wants me to work things out for myself today.

Oh, yes! Grandmother Faras served in Ald Isra for more than a century. She could have claimed a master's hood if she'd wanted, but she had no interest in politics and rivalries. She devoted herself to her family instead.

Perhaps. But the One Who Knows seems to think something more is at play, and I agree. Torvesard requires further investigation. But later, when reality is no longer in imminent danger.\n\nRemember what Hermaeus Mora told you. Remember the Black Book.

Danger exists in every corner of fate, chosen. Such is the nature of existence. But the entirety of what was hidden in the distant past remains sealed away. The threads it connects to have frayed, but they have not broken. Reality can still be saved.
The Prince of Fate does not lie!\n\nTwo beings now remember a small part of a greater whole. There is still time and opportunity to correct this before the memory spreads.

Unfortunate but not unrecoverable. Now that Hermaeus Mora is restored, he can locate Torvesard and deal with him once and for all—unless ….\n\nDoes Torvesard still have some way to elude the One Who Knows? Even without Blightcrown's corruption?
No! The dream that will end it! That will finally restore all that was lost. Hermaeus Mora caused all this with his greed and selfishness. He made us all forget. He made me forget!

No Prince of Oblivion can truly be destroyed. The final glyphic contains that secret. How to find them and restore them to their rightful place. And then, Mora will answer for his crimes.\n\nSee for yourself. I leave the glyphic for you to examine.

Torvesard. Something I did not foresee. An agent of Ithelia, hidden for all these eons. Her contingency plan. Her revenge.\n\nAt least the final glyphic is secure. Until it is found and opened, reality remains safe. For now, return to Cipher's Midden.

All right, all right. Not imminent is better than imminent … if the Prince of Fate needs you, he can find you on Nirn as easily as here in Apocrypha.\n\nI'm sure there's more to it, but that's your business. I'll leave it to you and Leramil.
No. I really did come for the celebration. And I think the same can be said for her being here, too.\n\nWell done helping out the peninsula. I hope our paths cross again soon. But not too soon.

Inordinately. But once we make use of the tome, well … we cannot do so again. I've been keeping it in my proverbial back pocket. \n\nA lever to shift a problem I cannot solve any other way. I feel the adversary rises to that level.

The tome is a supernatural phenomenon, created in reaction to the vast oceans of knowledge in Mora's realm. \n\nThe reader can learn any secret, any truth, as long as it pertains to their life. It "unravels" the secrets of the reader's fateline.

I've been searching for power and knowledge since I was old enough to draw runes in the sands outside Kozanset. I've realized, in some ways I never looked up from those sands. \n\nTogether, cohort. You and I? We can set this thing right.
I promised you a convivial attitude when we first began working together, and I hope I've delivered on that promise.\n\nBut our time together has … well. Clarified a few things for me.

I've checked, this is the only one on the topic. It's not like a lot of mortals cross the sands of Oblivion enough times to get sick from it. And Daedra are more resilient to disease. \n\nNo, I'll just have to keep looking. My book is here somewhere!

Over there. I was just going to rest my feet, but now it's gone!\n\nIt's the only printed edition. Not just in Apocrypha, everywhere. I spent too long tracking it down. That's what I get for looking up obscure tomes.

Yes! I haven't been here long enough to lose my faculties. I was sitting right over there and now my book is gone. \n\nMaybe it got buried or something. Stranger things have happened. I just have to keep looking.

Every possible fate unfolds before me. They all lead to an event I thought erased from chance eons ago. If this course isn't altered, Apocrypha falls, reality unravels, and Nirn is destroyed.\n\nThis enemy eludes me, but you are my secret advantage.
She isn't. \n\nBut you don't know, maybe I'm testing her. And, if I am and her insistence on that dreadful tome is correct, then we will be praised and none will be the wiser.

Me? Be led around by that mortal? Never. \n\nThat being said, I may allow her to retrieve that butterfly book. Maybe the humiliation of being wrong in front of all the other ciphers will teach her a lesson.
I … of course. I've never heard of that other book in all my years in Apocrypha.

Of course. I've recovered a sizable number of the books here. If it weren't for the mortals moving them or misplacing them, I'd have organized a large portion of the realm. Your kind's memory is too fickle to keep track of these priceless tomes.

Finally, a mortal who knows not to question my mind. If only my companion were so aware of my superior intelligence. She doesn't even know that I recovered that book a few centuries ago. It's not lost, It's where I left it.
I didn't have time. There's so much I could have done. I just couldn't do it on my own.\n\nSharp looks strong. Healthy. I'm sorry … so sorry …. But glad to see him one last time.

Because I wrote it down! I'm not the first partner Nassophra's had. I was warned about this, but I didn't think it'd be so annoying. \n\nUgh. I just have to play along until I can introduce the paper as evidence and catch Nass off guard.

Temperament aside, she's the best book hunter in Apocrypha. She knows this realm better than anyone else. We've never searched more than a few days before finding the tome we're looking for.\n\nI want to learn even a fraction of what she knows.

Have you talked to her? She doesn't take being contradicted well. I don't want to have to deal with an angry Dremora. Not here in the wilds. \n\nNo, I'll bide my time. It's smarter and safer that way. But I don't have to like this treatment either.

Help her find a book we're not supposed to be looking for?\n\nHonestly, I've never tried that. It could work, at least it'd be different from rehashing this same argument over and over again. It may be worth it.
I know everything. You have come to my shrine because the stars have fallen to Tamriel. You want to know how to defeat them.
I hunger for lost bits of lore. I thirst for new knowledge to add to my coffers. Bring your offerings to me. If I find them acceptable, I will return their worth in the knowledge you seek.

Then listen closely, as I will not repeat myself. The Celestial Warrior's army of Anka-Ra was created centuries ago by the Yokudan general, Tarish-Zi. \n\nHe came to me to learn how to bind his army to him—even in death. I granted his wish.

I can. But knowledge must never be given freely. A price must be paid.\n\nPart of the cost was bringing my servant Ibrula back to me. But you will pay much more if you want to learn all that I know about the Celestials.

His offering pleased me. He built the temple above this shrine and promised that his army would defend it.\n\nThe Anka-Ra have risen, which means Tarish-Zi has risen as well. They are bound to him. To defeat them, you must defeat him.
All I have told you is all you have earned.\n\nIf you wish to know more, you must become my eyes and ears in Craglorn. You must bring me fresh knowledge to feast upon.
I'll have to wait it out. I believe the damage Cipher Sabinius caused is slowly fading. In time, the denizens of Quires Wind will remember themselves and get back to the Great Eye's work.
Honored with the trappings of wealth instead of the comfort of familial affection? Psh. Never. \n\nWhat would you know about this anyway, n'wah? You're no dark elf. Don't assume you know our ways.

Incense formed by the deft hands of my daughter. Fragrant bread baked by my son. Fruit picked by my wife. And the yarn I spun myself. My great grandmother's spirit will be placated with the knowledge that her family remembers her well.

They do. They speak to us and demand our respect. The walls of Necrom are filled with the spirits of the deceased. \n\nIt's an honor to make the pilgrimage there to give our gifts to those who wait beyond life.

Wanting gifts of gold? I've never heard of such a thing. Most want to feel close to life. They want to be remembered fondly by their decedents. Respected even. To pay off your ancestors with gifts bought by gold is …. I wouldn't do it.
That's my position, but apparently appeasing the ancestors is about more than giving them exactly what they ask for.\n\nThe keepers in Necrom wouldn't allow these goods in if they weren't sufficient.

Is it so terrible that I purchase my offerings from those who make them better? I'm not an artisan. I don't own land. My skills over the cook-fire extend only so far as my own survival. \n\nBesides, I'm not the only one who buys their offerings!

That's what a mouth does. I loyally represented my master's interests against all opposition. And I demonstrated the discretion to put House Telvanni's interests first when Master Shelreni became a threat.\n\nI shall find new employment quite soon.

Do what you want with your own ancestral offerings and leave me to do the same. \n\nStill, maybe I could learn to cook. Or work silver. Something useful I could incorporate into my life and not just give to the dead.
Finally, someone who can see reason. \n\nIf my ancestors are happy, then there's nothing wrong with what I give them. No one else should be judging me.

Ah, that's not surprising. It is the city of the dead. A wonderful location of respect, duty, and life. Yes, life. \n\nBetween the keepers and the pilgrims, Necrom is a wonderfully lively place. I had such fun there during my early years.

Oh, thank the Three I am not. The next time I visit Necrom shall be an eternal one. I don't want to rush there. Besides, I don't go anywhere quickly these days. May as well enjoy the scenery while I can.

An outsider knows of our ways? It is becoming more common, though in my youth I never once came across any one of your kind who did. \n\nPersonally, I'm pleased by Necrom's expansion. We all benefit from sharing our cultures with one another.
Good to know our ways still thrive.\n\nWhen I was your age, I made a pilgrimage to give my offerings to the ancestors. Curiously, they never spoke to me. I hope you don't share my luck.

Yes. Well, there is something new to see everywhere you go. I used to hate the repetitiveness of travel, until I truly traveled. Now I see new delights in every rock. \n\nTake your time and enjoy where you are. There's nowhere else quite like it.
Toby's … No, that's not right. Tinkerer Tobin's Workshop. Eastmarch.\n\nOh, bundle up, if that's where you're headed! I hear it's cold there this time of year. Or every time of year, I suppose.

Yes, thank the ancestors! Although some of our brethren nearly became permanent residents of the Necropolis before we were able to nurse them back to health.\n\nThings would have been much worse if Gadayn hadn't acted … and teamed up with you.

Huh. Well, good you came along, or we'd both probably be a lot worse off.\n\nYou know the Reformer is obsessed with Sharp, right? He won't kill Sharp, but I'm sure he'll cut down anyone else who stands in his way. Just be careful.
Herm'us Mora has changed the bargain. It now reads "Let Naanurrel, OR THE MEMORY OF HIM, become my guide for the drowned dead." The words "or the memory of him" are new. What does this mean?

We resume our sacred task—helping our people stay close to the ancestors who have gone before them.\n\nIn time, I will join those who sleep below. Who knows? Perhaps Gadayn will be ready to take up my responsibilities when that day comes.

First of all, the active nemesis looms muddied my sight. I had no way to know where the glyphic was. Secondly, there's no use in crying over spilled fates.\n\nThe sooner we get to the Heart, the sooner we can put this all behind us.

It's a simple matter of temporal reversal. With the looms no longer operating, I'll be able to draw on the full power of the Underweave. In fact, do you have any wine you'd like rapidly aged?\n\nI kid, of course. Let's get moving.

My place is in Apocrypha. Yours is in your own little world … although I'm sure it's very important to you. Sooner or later, fate will lead you back to the mortal realm. And I'll return to the unbearable ennui of my existence.

I wouldn't expect gratitude from the Great Eye, mortal. But sometimes he's satisfied with how things turn out. If I was useful in resolving this contradiction, he'll find opportunities for me to be useful again.\n\nWhich is … something.

Oh, Hermaeus Mora is going to remember. He doesn't want what happened here to happen again because he forgot to keep a proper watch.\n\nJust never mention any of this to him or anyone else. I'd hate for the Great Eye to obliterate you or something.

Right. Preserving reality and all that. But what does forgetting all this actually mean? Will I still remember you and Leramil? Will I recall at least the core of the experiences that helped me grow?\n\nI don't want to forget Leramil. Or you, either.

I've been as busy as usual at the Necropolis. Busier! Abbot Ivel has given me more responsibilities. He trusts me now more than ever after we recovered the Fulcrum Obscura.\n\nHe did grant me leave for this trip. And for a sabbatical to follow.
You mean to suggest Herm'us Mora wants me to forget my own father? Forget our time together?
He's a very … demanding individual, even at the best of times. Commands with an iron fist, you know? And when these headaches strike, he is positively tyrannical.
I see. Are you at liberty to tell me what the glyphic contained?
Yes, yes. I think it will address his malady fully. I mean, I hope so. He's terrible when he's like this.
A forgotten Daedric Prince? Only the One Who Knows could keep such a fact secret for so long.\n\nIs there anything else I should know, proxy?

Then I am sure Hermaeus Mora shall call upon us again when the time is right. You are still fate's chosen, and I am your guide. But reality seems to be holding together for now.\n\nI think we have time to rest. To reflect. And to listen to Gadayn.

The Observatory just above Belkarth was where I spent most of my time. The Star-Gazers are an odd group, and I'm not sure who among their order will still be around after all these years. \n\nWe'll just have to hope someone remembers me.

Nathriin will be in the Shad Astula main building, likely the Arch Mage's offices. She was already a prominent scholar, and no doubt has continued to rise since my departure.\n\nI'm just hopeful she's mellowed in the intervening years.

He has an alchemical studitorium, of course, but as I recall he enjoyed studying with the background drone of conversation and libation. \n\nWe should check the inn at Balmora, a quaint little place with the ever-so-droll name of The Randy Netch.
I am helping! We're helping.\n\nKilling the Reformer, cutting things off at the head—it's the only way I know how to help. And it'll help me sleep at night, knowing he's dead.
He wrote a while back. Plenty of griping, which I expected. \n\nAsked if there was anything else he could do to help us, which I did not expect. Even offered to tag along. Can you believe that?
Obviously. Can't you feel the power behind the spell I'm casting? It's going to be enormous. After this, everyone will fear the power of my shattering megamagic!

Hmm. Large, grandiose spells are more to my liking, but you're right. I shouldn't waste my grandest spell on this cretin. No, I'll just knock him out. Save the real power for the next fool who stands in my way.
Surely I would never …. No, I will do it. If it means my father will return to the mortal plane, I will do whatever it takes.
Herm'us Mora will trade my memories for my father's life. I would forget him, but he would live. Yes! Give me the book!

I want a sincere apology. As sincere as Azandar can make it, I suppose.\n\nI can see over your shoulder he looks quite guilty, and he certainly seems more mature. But to dismiss and denigrate the efforts of his peers was wrong.

Introducing a new queen to an ailing colony is a delicate affair. The few healthy kwama that remain are still loyal to the dead queen and they won't hesitate to kill a new one unless egg handlers use the gland to mask her scent.

Yes! His familiarity with this colony, his years of experience … the Consortium hired him for a reason.\n\nWe only get one chance to re-queen, and I fear that a new overseer will botch the job. Then we really will have to shutter the mine for good.
With Ulfengar's help? Yes.\n\nWithout it, though? Well, it will be slow going, for sure.

With the nemesis looms deactivated, there's a surplus of power sitting idle within the Underweave's heart. Tapping into this reservoir will give me just the oomph I need to create a bubble of reverse time, repairing our glyphic instantly.

Meddling with time is always dangerous. Not to mention utilizing unfiltered magic from the heart of an Apocryphal refinery. Or trying to repair a fragment of a fated future.\n\nBut, as they say, the planes weren't shaped by idle hands.

The Heart pumps magicka throughout all of Underweave. Not only does it power the nemesis looms, it also stores the magicka released from the destroyed glyphics. The power concentrated here boggles the mind!

Knowledge is finite. Every book or letter or glyphic is a bucket of water from a well that may one day dry up. The Underweave is how my master refills that well.\n\nYou probably shouldn't press any further. Some things must remain unknowable.
Curious. I've handled my fair share of fated glyphics, but something about this one seems almost familiar. Like a tone ringing at the edge my memory. A song perhaps. A lullaby?\n\nHow very strange.

I believe it does. Whether it's one fate of many, or a singular inevitable fate, I won't know until I activate it.\n\nFunny. After all this, I find myself hesitating. Give me a moment, meddler. Perhaps take this time to calm your Watchling friend.

It's no secret my travels take me far and wide. I go to places far beyond what a simple compass or map might show. And in my travels, I heard an interesting rumor. That the Prince of Knowledge had found a special fate. My fate, in fact.
Of course! A spell to restrain him and stop his spell from completing. Oh, that's genius! Give me a moment.
I could wax poetic about Trinni all day. But, long story short, she's wonderful. Nobody has ever complained about motion sickness while getting to their destination.\n\nWhich is Ald Isra, by the way.
Oh, of course! Yes, Bittersweet here has taken the path between Ald Isra and Necrom for more years than I can remember. Nothing stops her from reaching her destination.

Tandasea walks a narrow and perilous path but sees much that I do not. The Temple values her mastery of hidden matters—matters … adjacent to our holy mandate.\n\nI take such flirtations with heresy seriously, but her results are undeniable.

The Golden Eye called it a logonymic ward. A power of the bastion the Herald uses to defend itself. But the champions of Vaermina, Peryite, and Hermaeus Mora each hold part of the logonymic. You must release them to breach the barrier.

Each one occupies an outlying district of the bastion. Vhogor the Pestilent is Peryite's champion. Kynmarcher Strix serves Vaermina. And the Eater of Secrets served Hermaeus Mora, until the invading princes subverted it.
I think you're strong enough that you could do that, if that's what you really wanted. I haven't perfected the process. You say you want to kill me, and yet I'm still here.

Dim. That's right. Your sister. Of course. That's who I feel. The way she missed you. She wants to make you remember! Just like me.\n\nAnd there's another. Masking your resonance from me. Who are you, I wonder?

The metal Sondivel uses to experiment on his slaves. Mevei told me you and Sharp found some in one of Sondivel's abandoned laboratories.\n\nWhen Reynila helped Sharp escape, his bond to tyranite calx is what tore his memories from him.

Oh, a fairly standard parley. Daedra are immortal, you know, so they're always looking to trade favors.\n\nThat is what I shall do with Tem. A favor owed in exchange for his assistance today. Don't worry, cohort. Perfectly safe.

I set out to learn about the paths unwalked, the might-have-beens. And that's exactly what the Fateweaver Key showed us. \n\nThe adversary was a lesson unto himself! Point taken, reality. Let it never be said Azandar al-Cybiades does not listen.
Kill them, of course. The logonymics are bound up in their very beings somehow—Daedric names are strange things.\n\nSimple, right?

Oh, books of this sort should not leave the Cloisters!\n\nIn the Cloisters, all futures—both possible and impossible—stretch out like a great and terrifying ocean. Foolish people would try to use these books to catch a glimpse of their own fate.

Well, they would go mad, of course. Even I fear to look at them outside the Sidereal halls.\n\nThese books, like many books, are too dangerous to leave unguarded. I still don't understand why they— Never mind. Let's just return them!

We are bound together by a common danger. Enemies of Hermaeus Mora threaten his realm of Oblivion—and in so doing, pose a threat to the mortal world as well.\n\nTherefore Mora sent me to meet you here and secure your cooperation.

Only a mortal proxy can deal with the threat and save both Apocrypha and Nirn. The fates of both realms are linked, and you are the key to preserving reality. Without you, everything unravels.\n\nHelp avert this disaster and Mora will reward you.

Given the focus of our research, it makes perfect sense. Fate itself pulses through the corridors of the Underweave. \n\nAnd it's tradition for powerful arcanists to establish a sanctum. I have one myself, you know. Quite proud of it.

We need to send someone into Vanton's nightmare to confront Ansuul.\n\nWizard Twelvane is in charge of the spell that will take you into Vanton's mind. She'll know what she needs … and she'll want to meet you first. We can't underestimate Ansuul.
That's an excellent idea! And the best thing about it, is that my opponent will never suspect something so simple as a sleeping spell. He won't have any guards up. It's bound to work!

Somnambulum. One of the devices that grants entry to the Chorus, sustains the vessel, and so on.\n\nExamining one might provide us with some clues without disturbing the other vessels. Or, without disturbing them more, at any rate. I'll meet you there.

That is likely, yes. But look on the bright side! Not only are you saving the vessels—you're also testing the tolerance levels of the Chorus' immune system. Fascinating, yes? No? Yes!\n\nJust be ready to defend yourself.

The substrate? It is like a mental cistern full of subconscious impulses, suppressed urges, and so on. Very dangerous! Rectory mind-sentinels patrol it for anomalies, though, so it is not too scary.\n\nOf course, you are sort of anomalous.
When required. I don't have much choice. Hezehk's debt to Madam Whim is long. And only getting longer.\n\nSo, yes, I carry secrets. Fetch people. Do her shopping. Whatever she asks.

She owns the House of Whims in Fargrave. It's a shop that trades in … well, all of it. Think of something. Yeah, she can get that.\n\nMost people go to her because she's discreet. That's probably how she got this secret in the first place.
After some misunderstandings, she made me choose: a debt of service to her or traded to Peryite. Easy decision.\n\nThat was, oh, about a thousand years ago. But the interest keeps accumulating.

No matter how often I deal with them, mortal ignorance always surprises me.\n\nFargrave is a place between places. It connects spots in Oblivion to make getting around easier. No prince owns it, which makes life there a bit of a free-for-all.

Pfft, physical item. What's physical? Am I physical? I made this meat heap you see out of energies from Oblivion. So what am I—physical or energy?\n\nMortals have souls, yes? Ah, well, are you meat or a soul? Both, right? There you go.

That's an odd question. How do you carry anything? You put it in your pocket. Or maybe your pack if it's a big secret. Several hundred years ago, I hired an imp-drawn cart to convey a particularly large secret for Madam Whim.

First, I didn't lose it. It was stolen.\n\nAnyway, it looks like a … what do mortals call it? Thing you use to eat? A fork! Yeah. Couldn't tell you why it chose to look like that, though. Secrets aren't known for explaining themselves.

Oh, just all the contingencies I had in place. With my last breath, I banished her from the tower and set all the wards and defenses. They held perfectly well … until you mucked everything up.\n\nShe'll have no trouble stealing my Black Book now.

That is a secret the One Who Knows has not yet shared with me. I can count the number of Black Books I know about on one hand. And each is unique. Only one copy of each book exists.\n\nThis is the first I have heard of one titled The Tormenting Eye.

Busy. People always need something from her. The House of Whims gets so full that I need a side entrance just to get in.\n\nOf course, when she's busy that means I run all over Oblivion with menial tasks.

We ask ourselves that very question. Some broke off due to a lack of faith. As they left, our powers waned. That weakening led to others leaving as well.\n\nWhat caused the initial shift, we cannot say.

Dremnaken are pests. They have tested our defenses since the Apogee's construction. If one discovered a faded ward or a crack in our dimensional shielding, it would slip in. Others could follow, further widening the breach.
It dreams of things. Teaches us things. Honestly, it will be easier to explain once you see how it works.\n\nYou have questions, I know. But trust Huzmargo, it will all make sense soon.
Well, whatever they're doing, Huzmargo is certain it is not helping matters.

Yes, yes. Beasts that consume magicka. Surely you have these on Nirni? Dremnaken? Irksome little tomeshells? No? Yes? Ziss'vo. They are so annoying!\n\nAnyway, many of these beasts stalk the grounds now. Gnawing on things. Growling. Very scary!

Who, Huzmargo? I am just one of the Tide-King's many, many servants. I oversee the Rectory's facilities, monitor the vessels, clean the instruments, and so on.\n\nLots to do. Busy, busy! Until something like this happens.

The same as you, I expect. Huzmargo read many, many books. The sermons of Amun-dro, of course. But also the Rites of Sangiin, Noctra's Hissing Codex, that sort of thing.\n\nWhat can Huzmargo say? He is a book worm, yes?
Huzmargo does not like this word, cultist. But yes, it did not take long before I became a cipher. And I've seldom had cause to regret it!

Yes. Hermorah's Tome of Tides. Huzmargo can still see the cover when he closes his eyes. Moist. Supple. Constantly leaking ink and foam. A beautiful thing.\n\nA few nightmares, hallucinations, extra limbs, var var var. You know how these things go.

Yensa is concerned that the three relics will not be enough to dull this curse. She recommends we source an ancient phylactery hidden away in Apocrypha by Magister Nisfarik. If you can acquire it, we can use its stored energy to power this ritual.
Me? I run another market stall. I'm just checking out the competition. Poor sods.
Bah! Not worth the prices they're charging. I get better vegetables from Ald Isra. Not losing any sleep, I'll tell you that!

Yensa believes Nisfarik stored his most potent phylactery within Bastion Nymic. We'd go to retrieve it ourselves, but we must stay and begin preparations. I worry I've already asked too much of you, but please, traveler. There isn't much time.
Thank you. Yensa and I will prepare the ritual. When you return we can begin immediately.

Yes, but it's usually easy enough to nudge a mortal follower of Hermaeus Mora to summon me when the ripples of fate draw me here.\n\nIt's not my fault the fragile mortal got himself killed. Well, maybe it is. Who can say? Fate works in mysterious ways.

Yes! They'll drift away to the land of dreams. Good dreams, though—not Dreamcarver bad ones! There, they'll drink in the halls of their noble fore-boarers! I know because I've had pig dreams. They're sublime!\n\nOnce they're asleep, we'll slip past!

From the skyway there.\n\nLet the potions fall on them and the gas will do the work. The lords will try to intimidate you, cajole you … cuddle you with their great stinking arms. If any of them tries to lure you to their side, ignore them! Resist!

Their crimes are too horrible to name, their passions too lustful to speak of politely. They are the conundrum of mortality, friend—imbued with the grace of gods and the frailties of flesh.\n\nWhich is their true nature? Ah ha! A riddle!

Another contradiction in a flood of discrepancies. Daedra don't normally dream. Not like mortals, at any rate. Not even the Dremora, who consider themselves above the rest of us.\n\nI may need to look into this Torvesard when I return to Apocrypha.

No, but we have to assume Torvesard learned the location before the text faded away. The final book referred to one of Hermaeus Mora's most infamous Black Books—The Tormenting Eye. It said it contains a rite for unlocking dangerous secrets.

Because Hermaeus Mora has foreseen that if they reveal this secret, reality itself will unravel, destroying not only the realm of fate but our world as well. That would be regrettable.\n\nThis appears to be related to Torvesard's lost dream.

It's who I am. The book-loving introvert from Kozanset, the young man drawing runes in the sand and dreaming of a wider world … well, I won't be so dramatic to say he's dead. \n\nBut he and I have very little in common.

Indeed. Malabal Tor, most likely, will see us going to the Ayleid ruins of Ilayas. I spent a stultifying season there studying the wells that typify such locales.\n\nI'm less sure about the Dwemer ruin. I've studied dozens of their constructs.

Well, anywhere as defined by the ancestral homeland of the Deep Elves. The region called Morrowind. Or anywhere along the north-northwest arm of their post First Council diaspora ….\n\nAh, but you were speaking colloquially. Apologies.

Not that it's any of your concern, but I proudly serve Master Foves as his chief scribe and valet. Some find him distasteful, even caustic, but I feel honored to work for him. His candor is refreshing in this nest of alits, and he treats me well.

Ah, Master Sulis. He tries to appear kindhearted, but he's as conniving as all the Telvanni masters. That's why I respect Master Foves. He makes no attempt to hide who he is.\n\nHmph. I shouldn't gossip with strangers about this.

By eliminating anyone who threatens the stability of the system. The Great Houses of the Dark Elves exist in a precarious balance. Without us, violence between them would spill into the open rather than staying behind closed doors and false smiles.

It was part of the writ. Provided by whichever scribe the masters had contact the Morag Tong. But since no one here knows anyone with that name, it must be an alias.\n\nBelieve me, when I figure out who took out the writ, I plan to ask them about that.

Ah, hero. If we had a bottle of wine and all the time in the world, the stories I could tell you!\n\nBut I really want to complete this writ and then wash the stink of the Telvanni out of my hair. Can we catch up later, please?
Because he's me. He's the Azandar I see in the mirror on my worst days. \n\nThe arse I struggle with in the darkest parts of the night when research, travel, and tea can't distract me.

The power of the ritual we used to locate the Panopticon lingers. We can use it to focus on the portion of the Fulcrum Obscura that Torvesard and Blightcrown carry. We can follow its trail directly to them.
A trifle! We shall borrow a summoning circle from the Mages Guild. At your earliest convenience, cohort, we should make for the city of Riften. \n\nIn … the Rift. Ach, Nords.

Categorically. The arcane adventure we set out upon back at Cipher's Midden is complete.\n\nThat said … if it's all right, cohort … I'd like to continue to travel at your side. The opportunities for research as your companion are endless!

Because Folsi thought me knowing about it was important enough to involve you.\n\nHouse Dres controls the land far to the south, near the Black Marsh border. Them setting up a camp near here could be coincidence, but it's worth checking out.

Aki-go is a contact I cultivated the last time business brought me out this way. For a minor servant, he excels at avoiding notice and absorbing everything that happens in town. He'll only help if it's safe. He knows what the Telvanni do to traitors.

Are you sure? Don't want to ask about my favorite beverage, how I look so good without any effort, or which scrib I favor in tonight's race?\n\nGood. Then let's get to work, hero. We have a spy to identify.
Another significant event in the annals of fate and I missed it? But Master Shelreni is dead? And Vaermina did what?\n\nStart from the beginning, proxy. What happened at the Masters Conclave?
So that was Shelreni's plan. Use whatever power the Princes provided to eliminate her rivals and move up in rank.\n\nI am glad she failed, but what happened after that?

And Blightcrown decided to complete the rite anyway by sacrificing Shelreni instead. Ruthless, but in keeping with a follower of Peryite.\n\nAnd you say this allowed Vaermina to possess Shelreni's corpse? What happened next, proxy?

Foves is a typical Telvanni master. Full of himself and twice as annoying. Sulis is reasonable, but he's hiding something. Then there's the servant Zemzo.\n\nI expected to deal mostly with servants and mouths. Surprised to find this many masters here.

Information discussed during the meetings of the Assembly of Masters has gotten out. One of the mouths accused this Tredecim and the masters applied for the writ.\n\nUnfortunately, no one here is named Tredecim. Means we actually need to do some work.

Just that lick spittle, Alam Guitot. He's Foves's aide. Made a good show of subservience, didn't he? Like all Telvanni servants, I assume he's quietly vying for power in some way.\n\nThe sooner we're done and I can leave, the better I'll feel.

Not much, in my opinion. They're all just interested in gaining power, stabbing each other in the back, and earning higher ranks in the house.\n\nMouths serve their masters, representing them so the masters don't have to leave their towers.

Look, maybe Mora stole Torvesard's favorite sweetroll recipe. I wouldn't put it past the Prince of Fate. He collects knowledge like House Hlaalu hoards gold.\n\nAll I know is Vaermina and Peryite want the memory back. But Torvesard wants it more.

What's there to know? Look around. It's a morass. I don't really know what a ravening is, but I'm sure it's that, too.\n\nI guess it's not the worst place in Oblivion. Coldharbour? Now, that's awful. Or Nirn! So boring. Ever been? Oh, uh, never mind.

If I get it back, then yes. Inside the Forum is a thing called the Intake Maw. You can deposit some knowledge into it. It's sufficiently powerful, the Maw delivers a boon from Hermaeus Mora.\n\nI suppose Madam Whim thinks this secret has enough power.
I guess you'd understand the Forum as a big marketplace, but instead of buying things mortals use, you trade knowledge. It has any kind—truths, fantasies, wisdom, whatever you need.
No? It's a secret.\n\nSecrets rapidly lose value the more people know it. If it becomes worthless and Hezehk can't trade it for a boon, Madam Whim will just add even more to my debt.
I suppose you can. It's not like we need to catch up with escaping thieves or anything.\n\nHonestly, I'm happy to talk about anything other than this place.

We're inside one of the Great Eye's secret memories. That's just an echo of him, part of the memory. Like I said, Vaermina's overlay of dreamstuff isn't perfect. And we can take advantage of that.\n\nLet's see if we can spot any flaws we can exploit.
Ah, expertly done. Now then, a choice. Who do you want to benefit from your efforts, hmm?\n\nYensa or Tralise?

Well, more perambulations with you, I expect. I'm taking copious notes. Part travel diary, part research treatise.\n\nI'm sure one day soon these old bones will be too frail to continue our escapades. Then … hah! The papers I shall write.

I have given that a great deal of thought. The adversary was a dark and twisted mirror. I'm forced to face the truth that … well. \n\nThere but for the grace of Mora go I. The bitterness in his heart dwells within me as well.

You recall the three anchors we destroyed to create the Rune of Unmaking? They were representative of moments in my life tied to him. \n\nImagine if Nilvon's bitterness had infected me. Or if I'd grown hateful after Shad Astula?

I assumed my intentions were quite clear. I seek to restore that which was wiped from existence in the ancient past by Hermaeus Mora. The memories that I only suspected were real because of the dream that haunted me.

Because Daedra do not normally dream. And this one was relentless. Recurring night after night. A vision of a statue of Vaermina and the ever present gaze of Hermaeus Mora.\n\nI originally sought out the Prince of Dreams' help to make sense of it all.

Obviously. But all Vaermina was able to do was determine that she and Peryite shared the barest recollection of the same memory. That knowledge bound us together. We pooled our resources and planned to recover the stolen memory from Apocrypha.
Now is not the time, hero. Distractions can lead to a blade in your back. Or worse, to one in mine.\n\nConcentrate on the mission. Let me do my job, then we can talk.
We shall open a door like any other. You will have no problem entering. \n\nThat said, once inside we must close the door behind us. Otherwise, we risk a swarm of Dreamcarvers joining us within.

I cannot answer those questions. I have no memory of life before I lost my clan. I don't even know where I originally came from. A part of my past is missing. A part of me. And I won't rest until I recover it.\n\n Some memory returns, but not enough.

It's time we finally talk about what happened. As much as it pains me to revisit the events of the past and of … Veya … we need to do this. I … need to do this.\n\nFind me in Necrom's tavern. There are too many prying ears here.
Well, how can I turn my back on saving reality? Or abandon Leramil? As long as the corruption threatens her, she's going to need someone to lean on.\n\nWait a moment … what are you implying?

I am concerned about all my allies, but … yes, Gadayn's safety worries me. I fear that his heart is too pure, too inexperienced, to survive what we shall experience in the Mythos.\n\nIf I falter, keep him safe, proxy. Please.

Razum-dar gave me his version of the story. I'm fairly certain he didn't ride into a Daedric realm on the back of a griffon, though, did he?\n\nRegardless, I know what transpired. I can't help but think Veya's actions were because of my failures.

Oh, I lied to a lot of people. Yet I remember it was you who told me to put the blade to her throat. It was clear that your mind was made up.\n\nYou were right, though. I should have put an end to her suffering. It took me a while to realize that.

And yet all she saw was her only friend pushing her away. I don't get emotional, hero, but even I would have been resentful in her place.\n\nTruth was, I didn't know what to do. So I shrugged her off on someone else. Or tried to anyway.

Veya wrote me when she arrived in Summerset. Detailed the pain she suffered. The pain she planned to inflict on others. That sweet young woman I once knew died that day in Balmora.\n\nYou saw what I couldn't—or wouldn't—see.

Veya wrote me when she arrived in Summerset. She made it clear that sending her away was what I thought best for me. Not for her.\n\nAlone with nothing but her thoughts—thoughts of anger, sadness, abandonment. Can I blame her? But what it led to ….

And a path I should have ended when I had the chance. Instead I did what I always do. I focused on my work. The here and now. It's too dangerous to ever get distracted. That's what I told myself, anyway.\n\nAnd you got pulled in. Again.

Now I need a drink and to gather my thoughts. Get my next job and get out of this damned peninsula. Maybe the next time we run into each other, we can put this behind us and have a more pleasant encounter. Just don't turn up on one of my writs, hero.
And from what I hear, it cost a great deal of lives. But you did what I couldn't. As always you were the hero, hero.\n\nI'll only say this once, so don't get used to it. I'm sorry.

Hermaeus Mora believes you can save Apocrypha and I have no reason to doubt him. Besides, I have seen you accomplish amazing things. And you carry the Black Book.\n\nJust remember, you must destroy the shell she wears to remove her protective spells.

Magister Meln. I had almost forgotten about him.\n\nNo, keep the soul gem with you. While the rest of us might not be in any condition to assist you, having the power of a Telvanni magister in your pocket could be the edge you need to defeat Vaermina.

As tempting as that sounds, no. I'll see this through. You're going to need the skill of a Telvanni magister to win this battle. And you're carrying my Black Book. If you need to use it, I can help with that. \n\nFace it. You're stuck with me.

Are you asking me about my current state of existence? No one has ever done that before. Interesting.\n\nLeramil and I will continue to feel weak and tired until the corruption fully dissipates. With the manufactories destroyed, we'll recover in time.

Nothing springs immediately to mind. But I can feel the fabric of fate churning like a storm-wracked sea. Something major will be decided here. Something … significant.\n\nTry not to muck it up, mortal.

That's my best guess. The nature of fate is such that it's impossible to tell. But he was me. And I am him. Let my adversary be a lesson to us both. That our choices define us, eh? \n\nHere's hoping we both make choices that shape us for the better.

Torvesard's nature, he is unlike any Dremora I have ever encountered. He helped us to help himself, but I believe him when he said he meant no harm. He just does not realize the danger this memory poses.\n\nI suppose that means we need to find him.

Oh, the usual. Various denizens of Apocrypha, the stray Hidden Kindred or Dreamcarver loitering about … but you might need Meln's ghost sight to follow the trail of the glyphic. I barely noticed it, so it must still be in Torvesard's possession.
What? No. It's locked for a reason. We servants don't have that much. I won't let a stranger in to go through our meager belongings.\n\nNo, this key stays right here with me.

There was another Daedric Prince! My Prince! A Prince that saved me and preserved just enough of my memory so that I could one day save them in return. A Prince whose jealous, craven siblings cast them down and wiped them from the annals of history.

Yes, she's being quite insistent on … wait a moment, are you having a jest with me?\n\nLeramil is a special person—as I'm sure you already know! We're just friends. I think. Oh, I don't know what I'm saying. We'll meet you back in Necrom.
Not nearly friendly enough, proxy. Talking to Gadayn is like conversing with a hungry ogrim. They both pay rapt attention but still fail to understand a single word you say.

An interesting offer, but I think I'll pass. I was thinking more of something casual and meaningless. Someone or someones I won't mind gutting once I've had my fun.\n\nI'd rather not put any more holes in you than you already have.

What? Did Leramil say something? Was I too forward? Not forward enough? Oh, I am so not good at this!\n\nHow could I keep a secret from you? Leramil has agreed to stay in Necrom. At least for a while.

You … you really think so? Thank you, my friend. It means a lot for you to say that.\n\nAnd I meant what I said. If you ever need my help or a place to stay or anything, don't hesitate to call on me. I … I learned so much at your side.

Leramil has expectations? What sorts of—oh!\n\nI see. Yes, I shall endeavor to monitor not only her words but her gestures. I must seem like a country bumpkin to someone as sophisticated and traveled as Leramil. Oh, what's the use! I am a bumpkin!

Grow up, proxy. I am well over a century old. Young for an Altmer, but not without my share of romantic experiences. I find the curate to be … intriguing. I wish to take the time we have to get to know him better. To see where things may lead.

I have and I wish they'd do it quietly. I won't tell the head steward, but they could repay my discretion by not disturbing my sleep.\n\nAnd, no, I don't know who it is. Staying ignorant means I don't need to lie when someone asks.

I expect so. As does the One Who Knows. Which is why you are still bound by his contract and I am still on call to aid you. But that is tomorrow's concern. I shall send word when the threads of fate that bind us once again converge.\n\nBe well, proxy.

Yes, but he no longer has the resources of Vaermina and Peryite at his command. He used them and they shall not soon forget that. So, even with his many abilities, he will need time to plan before he can attempt another assault on Apocrypha.

That's hard to miss. It's like a barn that hasn't been cleaned in a while. You'd think a servant could wash up occasionally.\n\nStrange, the smell began when that person started leaving at night. Probably a coincidence.

Yes, and it's right in front of me. Have you been wrestling in the swine pond? Probably with the servant that sneaks out late at night, I imagine.\n\nPlease, take that smell and leave. We've been trying to air out this place for weeks.

Indeed! Leramil and I are going to tour the continent. Spend some time together. Just the two of us. \n\nShe's been locked away in the libraries of Apocrypha for so long that she's scarcely seen Nirn. And I've barely traveled myself. It will be fun!
That's the smell! You found it in our quarters? I'll finally be able to breathe in there.\n\nI have no idea who it belongs to or why they'd have it. But good riddance.

The masters send representatives to the assembly. Our mouths. They have the authority to speak in our names. Some sessions require a master or two to attend, as well as any aides and servants.\n\nScribes take notes so every master can stay informed.

Did he, now? How easily he lets slip confidential information to a stranger.\n\nI know others find me grating, but I've spent my life making House Telvanni stronger. This spy threatens our stability. I need you to find them. Eliminate this threat.

Of course. After all, in these lands your family standing determines your worth. Sorry, that's not a judgment on you.\n\nIt's just the three of us. After Mother's passing, Father dedicated himself to his research. Which, as you can see, led us here.
I would be concerned if you didn't. This is certainly no simple task, otherwise I would've hired a squire, or a trained scrib of some sort. Ask away.

Is this your first dealing with House Telvanni?\n\nGlibness aside, Master Faras and his daughters were right. The secrets held within this tome would elevate their family beyond even their late mother's standing. You'd be doing them a great favor.

Then how fortunate for the peninsula that Master Faras and his exceptional daughters were able to contain such horrid and deadly Daedric magic.\n\nThat's the essence of a Telvanni, my dear outlander. Every situation can be turned to one's benefit.

It should come as no surprise that magic pages have a curious ability to wind up in the strangest of places. Beneath the hooves of a beast or caught in a farmer's bundle of hay. To put it simply, you should look everywhere.

So you do understand.\n\nI was their mother's Mouth before she left me saddled with Master Faras. I've been torn as to which daughter would rise to take their mother's place, but with these pages, it doesn't have to be left to chance.

A terrible illness took her from us when we were children. She was an extraordinarily gifted mage, and her loss lessened our family's esteem greatly.\n\nIt was Father's hope that a discovery of immense value would make up for his—our loss.

He's always obsessed over the founding members of House Telvanni and has long believed that they took their most powerful secrets to the urn. When he caught wind of a lost journal kept in an Apocryphal vault, well, he couldn't resist.

Well, I'd say you found the source of the smell. But why go out on specific nights just to return with a jar of stink?\n\nCould it be some sort of weird romantic rendezvous? That's no courting ritual that I'm familiar with. Anything else?

Remember how the Dres agent checks the kagouti nests on Morndas and Turdas? This servant leaves the night before every time. I'd bet you my Tribute winnings that's a jar of kagouti musk.\n\nFeeling quite good about this. Anything else?
Not a bad play. Not sure it totally rules out Master Sulis as a part of the conspiracy, but it's a start.\n\nHeh. Using false names to identify the masters. Clever, and demonstrates a sense of humor.

Add all this to that jar of kagouti musk you found in the servants quarters and I think we're getting close to catching our spy.\n\nHeh. Using false names to identify the masters. Clever, and demonstrates a sense of humor.
Not a bad time to review the evidence. Though I strongly advise that you not mention any of this to the mouths and masters at Tel Huulen.\n\nWhere would you like to start?

The Dres call the spy Tredecim. They're a servant, but more than that, a personal aide to one of the Telvanni masters.\n\nWe also know that Tredecim passes information to the camp House Dres established outside Ald Isra.

They resemble the contents of the text itself. Most of the books here in the archive are historical accounts.\n\nThey seem differently tempered as well. Some are peaceful, many hostile, and almost all have different skills and strengths.

Think about it this way. A book can discuss a king as a vicious conqueror or a benevolent philanthropist. Both of these descriptions could be true, but a text must choose one.\n\nAs for the differences in strengths, not all authors are equally skilled.

The Infinite Archive holds written records of events that were or that could be. \n\nThere were others who called this place home, but they're dead to the archive. I didn't think that was possible. The infinite challenges many of my assumptions.

You'll see evidence of them as you travel. I know of a few who aren't dead to the archive, but I'm not sure if they encountered the maligraphies yet. I'll do my best to steer you toward them when I can. They could help you.

An excellent question. We felt our power wane long before the Dreamcarvers attacked. And now, we can hear so few of our minds. That which connects the Remnants grows silent.\n\nWhen you reach Tyss outside the Cenotaph, ask her why this has come to be.
Ah, yes. Mortals.\n\nWe do not have a yourself. The Remnants are a whole. What we are, what we know, it is all unified. The best descriptor we can use in your language is we.

We see how the distinction may challenge you. A metaphor of the body often helps the confused.\n\nMortals have a left and right foot. If we point to one, you could say its name. Yet, they both are part of your body. Such is the case with the Remnants.

Although our power sputters and dims, we still emit a small glow. The Remnants are the sword and shield of the Eye-Who-Sees-All. No greater honor exists in Oblivion.\n\nOur pact with Hermaeus Mora still holds, so we must defend it.
We search the grounds. Find other ritual foci and destroy them.\n\nSteel yourself. Dreamcarvers roam everywhere.
What it means, mortal, is she has crafted a key to the Crux. Once she blends enough Remnant minds with her own vestige, she will appear as one of us.\n\nThe Crux will open. The pact will be exposed.

Think of the power nodes we charged. Our pact with Lord Mora is the kernel from which the Remnants' gifts emerge.\n\nOur mental web amplifies those gifts. The more who are connected, the stronger we become. To isolate us from it is savagery.

We deduced that Tredecim leaves their quarters late at night to drop information off at the northern kagouti nests. They use musk to keep the beasts from attacking.\n\nThe next day, Dres agents recover the information.

Only speculation. It probably has something to do with that secret project the servant mentioned. Something that Masters Sulis, Foves, and Thilse are working on.\n\nBeyond that, it could be anything. A lot of important business happens in Tel Huulen.

Hmm, hard to say with confidence. Tredecim sent a letter requesting a transfer of gold into Master Sulis's bank account.\n\nWe could interpret that as evidence of his involvement. But it could just be a diversion. Let's not draw the wrong conclusion.

Good, because we still have a lot to do. Head back to Tel Huulen and update Master Sulis. Placate him, but don't give him any more information than necessary. We're still not sure if he's involved. \n\nThen meet me at those kagouti nests to the north.
Not especially. I suggest we change topics.

To a Telvanni master such as myself, everyone is a spy and a threat. It's something of our way of life. Hence the need for you and the Morag Tong assassin. A fresh set of eyes and a dagger to get the job done.\n\nI suggest you get back to it.

Only in the sense that it involves both you and I. No, a perfectly common day in Ald Isra usually includes a spy and assassination attempts. Don't unnecessarily draw connections just because of the timing.\n\nIf you do find a connection, let me know.
I'm suspicious of everyone. Especially my peers and rivals. You have to be, in my position.\n\nSulis, though. He's changed. I don't like it.
What? No, of course not. What part of the word secret are you unfamiliar with?\n\nNo, I cannot discuss our project. Sulis should never have mentioned it to begin with.

He has a new urgency about him. Always wants to talk about some new idea or another. For example, Sulis mentioned our secret project, yes? He insists that we meet in person. And with a spy and possible assassin roaming this tower? Ridiculous!

Hmm? Oh, Alam Guitot? Yes, he's been my loyal assistant for a number of years. Maybe I've been working him too hard. Seems like he has no time to keep up his appearance. And the smell! Perhaps I should get him a room outside the servants quarters.

This spy part of Master Shelreni's treachery? I hadn't even considered that! I was trying very hard to put that entire incident out of my mind. I almost died, you know!\n\nNo, this is just typical Ald Isra cloaks and daggers. It has to be.

If Master Foves feels that worried about Tredecim, we can assume he's not involved. Unless it's a bluff. Gods, I hate Telvanni machinations!\n\nWhat was that about Alam Guitot? He smells? Well, that's something we should check on when we return.

Code names, no doubt. Guitot received help from someone else, but who? Without the key, we stay in the dark.\n\nI suppose it doesn't matter that much. The writ is for Tredecim and we now know who that is.

Some sort of Telvanni secret project? Hmm. Guitot is playing a very dangerous game by passing along that kind of information.\n\nWell, dangerous enough for someone to hire the Morag Tong. Anything else?
Ah, probably that secret project the servant mentioned. Foves is part of the project, so as his trusted aide Guitot gains access to the details. May have even taken the notes himself.\n\nWhat else?

Bristleback … Sparrow …. That letter from the Dres Camp explained these code names. This means Master Foves worked with Guitot this whole time. They even tried to frame Master Sulis as the spy.\n\nCan't say I'm overly surprised.

I'll return to Tel Huulen. If Guitot is there, we can wrap this up.\n\nYou should join me. But I don't recommend bringing up what else we know. There's too many holes and you'd just mark us for a blade in the belly.
What? What's that supposed to mean? I am not fond of assassins, outsider. Or their sharp knives!\n\nOh, I wish this terrible business was just finished already!

A binding document that gives me the authority to eliminate the name on the writ.\n\nWe figure out who Tredecim actually is, I finish the job, you get paid, and we go home. Not together, necessarily. Depends on my mood. So, what do you say?

Why would she not? Zemzo is an excellent servant! This one takes great pride that Master Thilse trusts him with such important tasks.\n\nOne day Zemzo will be promoted to hireling! Then he will work his way up and become Master Thilse's mouth, yes?

There will be a place somewhere within the archive where Tho'at Replicanum's presence is strongest. If I use the full nymic there, the natural pull of Tho'at's presence will help draw her to the exact location we want.

I don't even know if it exists. Isn't research delightful?\n\nStill, the logic makes sense. Tho'at is an infection and those always are nebulous. Some places will be more concentrated than others. The trick is finding the right spot.

Knowing what army a soldier belongs to is not the same as knowing their name. To continue the military metaphor, you just fought a general. \n\nAs the foremost expert on maligraphies, I know next to nothing.

Since Tho'at summons the maligraphies, perhaps they retain a piece of her? Her magic could require a portion of her nymic. There's also a possibility that Tho'at is less in control of the maligraphies than we think.\n\nOh bother. I'm hypothesizing.

There's still so much we don't know. But I doubt any Daedra would willingly divulge a piece of their nymic. I can only conclude that this fragment wasn't freely given.\n\nWhich means the nymics are an inherent part of these maligraphies.

Knowledge? Power? To cause mayhem? Who knows. Why would anyone want to destroy a well-organized archive?\n\nThis runs counter to all of my instincts, but let's focus on getting rid of Tho'at Replicanum before we delve into her motives.

We knew that Tho'at could manifest creatures of ink. That's what the maligraphies are. To think that Tho'at became vivified ink herself, animated ink, it's a leap … unless I misconjugated.\n\nNo, she became living ink. She wasn't always like this.

It all comes back to ink. The maligraphies are made out of the book. And I've seen Tho'at Replicanum scribbled across the margins of many pages here.\n\nI'm practiced enough at research to know when I'm on the cusp of discovery.

She's a Daedra who can manifest creatures out of ink. She's also a being of living ink. If I were in her position, I'd figure out how to create copies of myself. It explains why I keep finding her name in my books.\n\nOh. Fantastic.

Tho'at Replicanum is a creature of ink. She created everything you fought so far out of that ink. Which makes her all the maligraphies, to some extent. That's why they have fragments of her nymic. You've been fighting her the whole time!

Well, it's unlikely that Tho'at will talk to us, reveal her master plan, and agree to leave our Infinite Archive peacefully. \n\nShe's probably going to run in and try to kill you. Same as just about everything else here.
Tho'at made all the maligraphies. How many of them have wanted to chat so far?\n\nI hope we'll get some answers out of her, but I don't think we can stop her peacefully.
We did. And yet, we very much did not. It's a paradox. I love those. \n\nThat nymic we recovered from the maligraphies allowed me to summon a version of Tho'at Replicanum. That's who you defeated.

While Verses are more powerful, they don't last very long. Conversely, the same is the true about Visions. Their augments are less impactful, but they'll last for as long as you're in the archive.\n\nReceiving an offering of Visions is … impressive.

After we fled from the initial assault, we did not heed the call to rally. As our connected minds fell quiet, fear and guilt crept in.\n\nWe decided to return and survey our fortress. The Dreamcarvers have only entrenched further.

That is a mystery. When we entered, our voices silenced. Perhaps that knowledge stays locked within the Crux.\n\nOr, perhaps our Lord Mora does not wish that knowledge to spread. Who are we to question such a judgment?

Mortals have libraries, right? Master Malkhest mentioned that yours pale in comparison. Which isn't surprising since ours are quite dark. \n\nThe Infinite Archive is large though. There's a lot for us filers to do.

The archive is in some danger right now, but you don't seem like a weakling. \n\nI mean, mortals are strong. You're capable, and bright …. Can I give you a reward for coming all this way and we forget about my calling you a weakling?

Dangerous … oh, you mean deadly? Right, you mortals have to worry about dying. Usually, it's not dangerous at all if you can fly. But these aren't usual times.\n\nIf you have an ally, a sword, or even a good stick, I'd recommend bringing it.

The source of our troubles is Tho'at Replicanum. She's summoning maligraphies—creatures of ink—and they're making the archive unsafe. \n\nI have a plan, but I'm a researcher and not well equipped to deal with the dangers.

Daedra can be commanded by nymics, their true names. If you can find Tho'at Replicanum's nymic, we can summon her and defeat her.\n\nThis will be treacherous, so I'm prepared to offer you a reward to compensate for the dangers you'll encounter.
[Stares even more intently.]
I can usually tell after they attack. \n\nMost of the maligraphies will fight you. But that doesn't mean that all of them will. Just keep an eye out for any that behave violently.

Then you underestimate the power of the written word. Remember that these characters, as you called them, aren't in their books anymore. A sword made out of ink is still a sword. I have the scars to prove it.

The archive is unique in that the locations which form the sprawling archival wings are not actually connected. Portals are the only way to travel.\n\nDon't worry about getting lost. I'll make sure to create a portal to where we first met in each wing.
Oh, that's simple. We use the Index.

I remember when the concept felt foreign to me as well. \n\nThere might have been land at one point, but it's gone and left very disparate locations a great distance from one another. The books we must have lost when that occurred ….

The giant orb in the room where we met. It's connected to everything in the archive—you, the filers, the books, the maligraphies, everything. It's a safeguard against all manner of danger, too. Get hurt enough times and you'll appreciate the Index.

I tried that. Unfortunately, nothing happened.\n\nThese versions of Tho'at Replicanum are technically separate entities. I'm not sure how much they differ, but they must have unique experiences. Regardless, they don't share the exact same true name.

Last time, the larger maligraphies carried the fragments of the nymic. That's where I suggest we start. Who knows? Maybe Tho'at Replicanum will be too wrapped up in whatever it is she's looking for to hide the fragments better. We can always hope.
This maligraphy seemed more powerful. However Tho'at creates maligraphies, this one probably took more energy to manifest. That sort of magical effort takes its toll.

One thing I can guarantee you about this place—anything is possible. \n\nI read about incredible figures such as the Imperfect, Prior Thierric, and Cynhamoth. Any number of deadly enemies are contained within the archive's tomes.
This construct is where my path to the Fateweaver Key finally came into focus. The ancient lore of the Dwemer commingled with my incandescent research.

Oh no, not directly. But Dwemeric tonal architecture was the final inspiration I needed to crack the problem. \n\nIt led directly to my understanding of fateweaving. And thus, to our current situation.

This is an archive for books, not unbound sheaves. If you have doubts or are fluent in the ancient languages of the Reachfolk, perhaps you could read the pages as they are. If not, you'll have to wait for the translation.
It's an important tome of ancient Reachfolk lore.\n\nBesides, translation's an aspect of my duties here. My work preserves knowledge contained within the books.

Almost none. I can read infinitely more than I speak. Understanding the meaning of written Jel is so vastly different than hearing the sounds and making sense of them.\n\nWritten translation is as far as my skills go, I'm afraid.
This room, this archive, it's so … scattered. Are we following authors? Eras? Geographical locations? Subject matter? Binding materials? Ink types?
The only time it's bearable is when I'm reading or working. Otherwise I just want to tear all the books from their shelves and restock them correctly!

What if I organize them by the wrong category? Have you seen an archive organized by spine color? Or by date written? No. \n\nBesides, this is Hermaeus Mora's archive. I don't want to inadvertently upset the Prince of Knowledge.

She keeps a room in town. I'll mark it on your map.\n\nCareful, though—Deredrien and Reynila were old friends, but they fell out some time ago. Asking after one might cause the other to be very … sharp with her answers.

A creature of living ink. She created all the maligraphies you fought in here. Nasty attitude as well, if Malkhest's account is true. The text you found said she became vivified ink. So, I suppose she wasn't always like this.
