Help me put a stop to the Albus family. That's the only way we can ensure that no one else will get kidnapped. If we stop them, we also end whatever nefarious scheme they have brewing that requires soldiers.

You know about Orpheon? Impressive. This war's gone on so long, I thought everyone ignored the temporary emperors. \n\nOrpheon made up his mind on what our Elder Scroll contains. He's wrong, but that won't stop him from ransacking this island.

The Undaunted respect anyone who is triumphant and courageous. Just from what I heard about Orpheon the Tactician, he was neither of those things. But I don't need to speculate on Orpheon's accomplishments, I just need to know if he's dead.\n\nSo?
<You are about to enter a Group Dungeon. Are you ready to leave your current Zone?>

A prophecy that will legitimize his claim to the Ruby Throne. He didn't like it when I told him that the prophecy wasn't about the empire. I guess he expected I would kneel and hand it over. Fool.\n\nThe Hel Netu monks are wealthy. Will you help us?

I admire your curiosity, zha'al. Most consider it bad luck to speak of the work of my necromantic order.\n\nOur path ventures through the dark, yes. But we do not enslave the dead. Through Azurah, we open doors to redemption in service to the living.

Defend yourself. When you defeat dro-m'Athra they retreat to the Void, Namiira's plane of darkness.\n\nIf you had a Twilight Cantor with you, we could banish their spirits permanently. But as much as I would like to accompany you, I am forbidden.

With those large, friendly eyes and the cutest little whiskers? No. Dark spirits like dro-m'Athra take a different shape and have for thousands of years. This is no trick of Namiira.\n\nFind the spirit and determine what must be done.

Spirits of fallen Khajiit follow many paths to Azurah's Crossing. Those with darkness in their hearts can better find their way through the path of redemption.\n\nWhen I use necromancy, I invite forth their spirits and show them the way.

Ah. A simple perspective to have so long as your soul is not the one being pressed into service, eh?\n\nIf we see combat together, I will demonstrate how you can invite forth spirits that wish to be used so. There is no need for force. You will see.

Then we are not so different in our methods. That is good to hear.\n\nAll can benefit from such practice. Spirits wish to walk Nirni again and redeem themselves for misdeeds committed in life. We can give them a chance to do that.

You commune with the dead as well? You are brave to admit it. I confess, it is a relief to meet someone who will not be disturbed by my calling.\n\nBut tell me, how do you use these spirits you call forth? Do you summon them by force?

The Moonlight Blade? I have only heard about such a thing in legends.\n\nYour story …. I am not sure I can believe it just yet. But if you did this, I owe you thanks. On behalf of all of the Hidden Moon.

Arum-Khal? I do not know this name. Perhaps he came after my time, but … forgive me. I do not wish to question your account, but I cannot believe that this is how my order met its end. At the hands of a lich.\n\nHow did you deal with this lich?
My eyes see many things in shadow, tamiit. I can tell you what I see as I see it.

Fighting their leader is how I met my end. The inscription on my tomb said they disappeared from this world when I died.\n\nThey have returned, and I believe Azurah herself sent me back to dispatch them. We only need to find them.

They prey on those with music in their hearts, whose power can be twisted to strengthen their ranks.\n\nYou and I can stop them. As we did in Claw's Strike and the Vile Manse. With your might and the tools of my order, we can redeem their fallen souls.

As much as I can stomach. The moonlight these fanatics worship is sterile. They follow lifeless teachings of some false prophet. \n\nTheir world is flat and colorless. Those who are not ignorant of my order look upon it with revulsion. I pity them.

I have a low opinion of this high cantor. But, then again, perhaps this is unfair. I hardly know her.\n\nShe is loyal to those Inquisitors of the new faith of Elsweyr, yes? This Riddle'Thar that brands me a heretic.

The memory returns, though I do not wish to recount it just yet. I did not expect to survive.\n\nIt seems my efforts were not in vain. If you have not heard of a Rajaska, then the tablet speaks true. It is a blessing that they prowl Nirni no longer.
Hmm. This only confirms my suspicions. They're Daedric. Handcrafted by Ayleids, most likely. The make reminds me of the lost Ayleid worship idols the Dawnway keep in Vashabar.
No, never. To follow the Dawnway is to see the forest for the trees. Plucking a berry, harvesting fallen wood. Not worshiping Daedra.\n\nAt least from what I know.

From my research, many Ayleids migrated from the Summerset Isles. These idols might have been made by them, and were either lost or tossed away on their travels to avoid suspicion from strangers.\n\nI hope no one in the Dawnway secretly has these.

Ziss! I need to get back. I am beholden to the Torval Curiata, and they are mobilizing for some sort of attack.\n\nI will try to find you in Rawl'kha if I can slip away again. Good luck, walker. And stay safe.

Some are aware of the ties our ancestors have to the Daedra, but ignore them. I used to believe they were lies. But we must accept it, and only follow the good practices the Ayleids showed to the Green. It's all we can do.
Hmm, this refers to the Ayleid Diaspora. But King Nantharion never spoke about Ayleid Daedric Kingdoms in our culture.\n\nIt says they tortured slaves to summon armies of Daedra. How cruel.

The thought had sprouted, yes. But would it make a difference? I joined the Dawnway out of love for the Green. Who the Ayleids were doesn't change that.\n\nBut Dawnway followers need to be aware of the connections the Ayleids had with the Daedra.

That's where the book comes in. But I hope it helps them accept this dark part of our history.\n\nAs for me, I feel like I've grown into a strong, graht-oak tree! I'll plant one in your name. For good luck.

My moonclaw guides me. Though weak, I can feel its pull. Somewhere east of here. At the Shrine of the Consummate S'rendarr, I believe.\n\nI must now humbly ask for your aid. The last time I faced a Rajaska alone, it cost me my life. Will you help me?

Dro-m'Athra are what happens when Namiira possesses the heart of any Khajiit. They are creatures of darkness and violence.\n\nRajaska are what happens when that darkness ensnares a moon-singer. You still have moon-singers in this age, yes?

They are storytellers, but this is a woefully simple explanation. In my time, the strongest singers wove stories into song, casting powerful spells in Azurah's name.\n\nThe boldest among those singers often aided the Hidden Moon.

Then you know of what I speak. In my time, the strongest of the moon-singers wove stories into song, casting powerful spells in Azurah's name.\n\nThe boldest among these singers often aided the Hidden Moon.

We did not have Twilight Cantors in my time. But the name suggests an allegiance with Azurah.\n\nPerhaps they are not so different from the moon-singers of old. I would like to meet one and learn more.

It is their songs. A once-joyous litany with the power to drive back the darkness becomes a shadowy dirge, a phantasmal chorus that grows in strength and beckons the drums of the Bent Dance.\n\nThe stronger the moon-singer, the stronger the Rajaska.

I did not pull it from the bones of my fallen brothers and sisters, if that is your concern. I found a cache of supplies and saw fit to equip myself.\n\nBut I do not wish to stick out like a broken claw in my travels. What do you think of it?
Inquisitor for the Torval … what?\n\nI do not know what you speak of, but Inquisitors do not sound friendly. Are these Inquisitors like the Twilight Cantors you spoke of?
Well, blessings from Azurah that you found me then, and not these Inquisitors.\n\nNo matter. We must deal with this Rajaska threat before we concern ourselves with this Torval … whatever it was.

Var, var! Such kind words. Function is more important, of course, but what Khajiit does not like to present a sleek and pleasing form?\n\nThis is not quite what we wore during my order's time, but it will do well enough to protect me.

Ah, I was afraid you would say that. I suppose it must appear antiquated. But it will serve well enough for now.\n\nWhen we find the time, perhaps you can assist me in finding armor more appropriate to this era.

The Archmagister asked that I not say too much in earshot of my guildmates.\n\nLet's just say it's a magical anomaly. Untamed power from an unknown source. Plenty to catch a mage's interest, but that's just the trouble. It could be highly dangerous.

For now. Power draws mages like moths to a flame, we're a little hopeless that way. \n\nVotary Nahlia, a knight from the Order of the Lamp, is on the scene. She needs someone to help her explore this anomaly and assess the danger. What do you say?
Let us venture down these cliffs. The temple ruins seem to have been left where they fell.\n\nPerhaps if we sift through the remains, we can still find something carrying the Dark Moon's blessing.

Ah. My constant companion. I hope he lived a long and happy life after I passed.\n\nI found him yowling for help on the streets of Corinthe. I took pity, cleaned him up, and replaced his missing eye with a bit of moonstone. You can hardly tell now.

The Dark Moon is the true spirit of Lorkhaj. Redeemed and made protector of the Lunar Lattice by Azurah's grace.\n\nThrough him, we of the Hidden Moon find our way through darkness to lead Azurah's children to her Crossing.

Kra! Do not ask me about that. We have only just met. I want you to think well of me.\n\nIn all seriousness, it is … regret. I have no bent tail, but I walked a bent path. In the end, my misdeeds cost me dearly.

It is … not much of a proper name at all. A shortening of ja'khajiit. Kitten, I think you would say. With how sharply the sounds roll off the tongue, it means he is small but tough. A tough little guy.

Just so. At the height of our training, hadaliit of the Hidden Moon steep ourselves in darkness so we cannot fall to the Bent Dance and become dro-m'Athra.\n\nWe train to walk through Namiira's dark without Azurah's light.

She wouldn't. But she was supposed to meet us here. And the place is a mess ….\n\nOh no. What if we're too late? What if the Ceythalmor got here ahead of us? Hurry, look around! Maybe they didn't find her research.

It aids in navigating lunar byways to guide souls. A most ancient purpose given to my order by Azurah herself.\n\nAs such, it must be empowered by something related to the Dark Moon. Something that we search for now.

Ha, no. I was a knave and a jeek long before I heard Azurah's calling. And long after.\n\nNow, it seems I have been given a second chance. Perhaps things will be different this time. It is all still so hard to believe.

When I was still a young student with much to learn.\n\nIt was the practice of the Hidden Moon to partner their adepts with Moon-Singers. Talbira was mine until she was late in her years. Others were chosen for me, but none lasted. Not until Ravith.

Few can bear to walk the path of the Hidden Moon, where we have little comfort aside from faith. Ravith came from nothing. Feared nothing. Her faith in Azurah filled her with the same fire that filled me.\n\nWhen you are ready, let us move on.

Ecstatic. And for two reasons. First, you remember the boat? Back on the beach? Through my deep magic I can sense the connection between people and objects. \n\nAnd I sense Snapdragon all over this piece of paper. She cared about this sheet.

There's a Bluemoth flower near the door. Grab some petals and … oh, there's some oil on that bookcase. You can grind the petals and combine them with the oil at her alchemy workbench.\n\nHere, I'll put the sheet of paper back on the table.

Of course. We were so filled with love, with music, that I feared losing her. Just as she feared losing me. But while my training armored my soul, it could not save Ravith.\n\nNamiira coaxed her into the dark, taking her heart one piece at a time.

She convinced Ravith that if Azurah knew we loved each other more than we loved her, she would never let us be together.\n\nI prayed for help. Begged. But there was nothing to be done. Azurah cannot help those that do not want to be saved.
I will show you. And Krin'ze. This is the part that may be the most difficult for her to see. And for me.\n\nAre you ready?
Then, as Jone follows Jode, we move as one. A bond of fellowship, of two souls made better by one another.\n\nMay that bond see us through to the other side of this darkness. Together.

In my time, it was a word of partnership. If we travel together, our souls will move as twin moons. Strengthened by our bond. \n\nYou see, the world has changed much since my time. There is much for me to explore and learn. I am eager to see it all.

As I understand it they tie all the living creatures and books here to the Index. I suppose the threads act as security against the dangers of the archive. \n\nDying severs a thread. Lose too many and you're returned to this chamber.

The principles of what the Ayleids founded are what led me to the Dawnway. Planting a tree, reaping what the Green gave us. This is what it means to be a Dawnway follower.\n\nBut I believe we've been misled.

Master Malkhest and the filers are too busy with the other troubles in the archive to look into what happened. But that is not what bothers me.\n\nI am not upset about the Index's lapse. I am furious at the creatures who severed my threads.

You helped her in Black Heights, didn't you? I am glad you were there to help her see Vijari's soul pass on in peace.\n\nOur Chief Crier is on holy sabbatical, by Azurah's blessing. Viti endeavors to serve as a sort of leader in her stead.

You were at the Temple of Seven Riddles? Bright moons! We still sing odes to you and the others who took up arms.\n\nOur Chief Crier is on holy sabbatical, by Azurah's blessing. Viti endeavors to serve as a sort of leader in her stead.

I'm not sure. It usually took exploring a few different archival wings to find one.\n\nThose bastards are probably waiting to see how much of a threat you are before revealing themselves. They see the archive as a challenge or something.
Me? Oh, I'm only a Wood Elf who preferred a quill to an arrow. I was never as nimble as most of the others. Certainly could never be a jaqspur. I think I nearly took out someone's eye once.

I hope we go back to our regular duties—wandering Elsweyr, answering summons, practicing songs, and tending to exorcisms.\n\nBut this business with the Rajaska and the Inquisitors … it feels like it has just begun.
Of course. If I learn something from the Inquisitors about the Rajaska, I will find a way to contact you and Zerith.\n\nAnd I will try to research more on the Rajaska. Wish me luck.

If they press me, I will have no choice.\n\nDo not worry. I won't tell them anything else about you and Zerith-var. I think I can convince the others you saved to do the same. Viti … is being unreasonable. I am sorry about that.

Exactly. For now, most of what I've written is about Ayleid history and references to their worship of the Daedra. All I have left are the remnant chapters. We'll study each remnant like reading tea leaves, except it's about the past.

No, the pain only lasted a moment and then it passed. But I do feel strange. Like remembering something I never knew I forgot.\n\nLike the song. Talbira's song. I know it! Bright moons, I can hear it!
Moon-Singer Talbira taught it to me. Or rather, she does not need to. She is here! She has always been here. She ….\n\nWait. Do you feel that? Something is coming.
Inscriptions, toils lost to time. Even a crack in a remnant can tell us so much about the Ayleid hands that crafted it. If they were devoted to the Daedra, we'll find something.

They usually take a little bit of time before they make an appearance in the archival wings. I thought it was because they were intimidated by my skills, but now I know better. \n\nThey're stronger than you expect. Don't underestimate them.
Partly that, and for genuine curiosity about our ancestors. I once revered the Ayleids. Now it almost feels like I knew nothing about them. I want answers. And I know others will, too.

Many in the Dawnway tend to praise the Ayleids. But the loose ties they had with the Daedra were kept hidden from us. I only found out after pursuing my book. Stung me like a prickly vine when I did, too.

I did. But something always felt missing. I had written untold stories about other cultures, and yet knew little about my own roots. I thought the Dawnway would give me answers. But I was only left with more questions.

Mostly strolling while others leapt branch to branch. But I believe that's where the seed was planted. I spent a lot of time observing the Green, pondering about it and the world outside. I wanted to know more.

Right, but how did anyone know about her research? Or that it was stored here? Something's terribly wrong. \n\nFriend, we've got two very different letters from Hyacinth. Obviously, he didn't send one of them! We have to get to him and Snapdragon!

It's a big tree in Grahtwood, near the Bone Orchard. We used to have meetings there to exchange information, back when I first joined the Ring.\n\nI'll mark it on your map. We've got to get over there as fast as we can!

One masked brigand and the pack of horrid beasts she commanded! Fralgatha did everything she could to protect me, bless her heart, but the thief made off with my entire dowry. Now I haven't a napkin ring to present to my future bride.

She disappeared into the nearby Fyrelight Cave. Adventurer, if you can recover my four dowry bundles, I promise to make it worth your while. Every scrap of silk and muddied jewel could save me from becoming the laughingstock of Skingrad.

Zerith knows about the Rajaska. Well, Zerith and perhaps the inquisitors. I do not need to tell you that they will not help us. \n\nIf only we could find Ravith-morna. Then maybe Zerith could save the cantors bent by her song.
Most certainly. Seeking knowledge keeps our minds as sharp as our blades. What would you like to know?

The power of Azurah echoes in their canticles, yes. But it is an imitation of old traditions. The Riddle'Thar has done much to rob their songs of strength and meaning.\n\nBut Krin'ze now harbors the soul of Moon-Singer Talbira, so that may change.

Hrm. You keep me honest, tamiit.\n\nYou recall that I had to stop the ritual of memory when Talbira asked me to raise my blade against Ravith-morna. Reliving that pain was physical, somehow. It is that same pain that halts me now.

She said forgiveness cannot abide while truth festers in shadow.\n\nI suspect I know what truth she speaks of. But finding the words to tell this truth to the one who needs to hear it is no small task.

Pa'alat? The town just west of here?\n\nListen. Inquisitors are not known for their subtlety. If this meeting is really a trap, their presence would not be difficult to spot. I suggest you ask around Pa'alat and see what people are talking about.

Just so. She is not used to others standing up to her like that. I would have myself, but I never had reason to. Until Zerith came along.\n\nViti has a good heart, walker. It saddens me to see her led astray by the Inquisitors.

Talbira's spirit? I see. You mean as a replacement mentor for Krin'ze. I had not thought about such a possibility. Her spirit now resides in Krin'ze, which I still find hard to believe.\n\nAnd I never saw the dead as much consolation for the living.
I'll tell you nothing. Our agent played the Garland Ring masterfully. From that Gardener of yours to this bar crawler here. We have nothing to fear from any of you.

No idea. We have boltholes like this one all across the Dominion. We shift between them all the time, even I don't know where the next muster point will be.\n\nYour Hyacinth is gone. And I have no idea where.

A dark event in Ayleid history, but one that led them to Valenwood. The Ayleids once enslaved the Nedes. Eventually, they targeted the Ayleids and fought back.\n\nBut this confirms there were Ayleid Daedric kingdoms, hmm.
I've never spoken to our agent. No idea who they are. All I know is that they've been embedded in your group for years now.\n\nThat's everything. Please. I can't bear the pain anymore.
Oh, I'm still strong as a stump. I knew our ancestors had a complicated past. But so much has been hidden from us.\n\nWe need to keep searching.

This one's fear of necromancy blinded her to the Hidden Moon's true calling. Viti now wishes to see Zerith-var's powers of redemption with her own eyes.\n\nIn exchange for this service, Viti is prepared to offer information of value to you.

This one will share everything the Inquisition knows about the Rajaska. You seek their leader, Ravith-morna, yes? Viti knows the den where she lairs.\n\nIf you agree to this, let us meet in Orcrest, in Northern Elsweyr.

I know, and I'm absolutely nauseous about it. The Garland Ring isn't that big. Poor Snap is dead, Hyacinth is innocent but captured. That only leaves …. \n\nLet's focus. We need to get to Crimson Cove and save Hyacinth. Again.

It's a cave on the north shore of Malabal Tor. On a good day, it's dangerous. If the Ceythalmor are there, we're in for a tough time. \n\nDoesn't matter. We need to get in there. I'm not letting another friend die today.

Typical of this day and age, I am sad to say. But Viti was adamant we go to Orcrest to demonstrate the Hidden Moon's power. \n\nWe will need to do our best to keep her safe there, whatever the situation.

In my age, the city's bazaar was a jewel in the Scar of Anequina. Streets packed with caravans that spilled into the desert. In this time, I anticipate the worst.\n\nViti insisted she witness my powers there. Whatever the reason, we must be vigilant.

More than I want to think about. I fought three before the fourth severed my thread. \n\nThey like to rudely invite themselves in your perfectly civilized fights and wreck any sort of plans you may have on the battlefield. Bastards.

Keep your eyes open and never be complacent in there. Marauders will join your enemies the moment you let your guard down. \n\nDon't let them get behind you. Don't let them hit you. And for the light of the Eight, don't let them kill you.

Not much to tell. We're a small town full of hard-working people. Most everyone is employed by the Carvain Ranch or the Raxalee Quarry. Baron Carvain and Lady Raxalee have always had a sort of friendly rivalry, but lately it seems … less cordial.

It's the illness affecting the workers. Took Constable Ulbren, too. We saw the first signs of it a few months back. It started innocently enough. Most thought everyone was working too hard. \n\nBut then those with the illness started dying.

He was? That's a good question. I suppose maybe it was a little strange that only people who worked at the ranch or the quarry were getting sick. Until that is Healer Nevama and Ulbren got ill. The disease came upon them and they died very quickly.

The ranch makes a substantial profit providing food for the town and the region. While the quarry has had some success, since the war for the throne heated up it's begun to challenge the baron's status and put a strain on their relationship.

This one was away when the plague struck. Eifa sought dark magic to resurrect those we lost. It was a desperate bargain. From that desperation came the pull of the Bent Dance.\n\nBy the time this one returned, it was too late for her songs to save her.

No. Viti killed her before she fully turned. Otherwise, the song of banishment would see her soul lost forever. Viti thought it was a mercy. Done out of love. But after all these years, this one knows Eifa is lost, unable to reach Azurah's Crossing.

Zerith's methods cleanse and purify. They do not destroy. This one asks that he invite forth Eifa's spirit. Let this one try to make amends … for her sake as much as mine.\n\nThis is how his gift from Azurah works, yes? Will he help Viti?

Within a shrine to Namiira deep in the wilds of Northern Elsweyr. A defiled place called Predator Mesa.\n\nRavith-morna leads her fallen cantors in lamentation. Dark songs of unknown purpose. Can you silence her?

Spirits who seek Azurah's Crossing. We hear the songs of Ravith's Chorus echo from Nirni. The rising song of those bent to join her dirge. We lose our way. And even in death, the Void calls.\n\nRavith's songs, they are a summoning.

Ravith calls forth a hunter. A moon beast to prey upon spirits on the paths to the Crossing. It will hunt them, pull them screaming into the Void.\n\nNo songs can reach them there. If she succeeds, no one thereafter will ever enter Azurah's embrace.

The Sands Behind the Stars … I can feel them calling to me now. Azurah opens her arms to me. I have never felt such peace.\n\nViti bid you save my soul, walker. Now I beg that you keep the Crossing open so that hers can reach it one day.

Ah, but I forget my blessings, tamiit. It is because of Cantor Krin'ze's curiosity and devotion to Azurah that she found you. And you found me.\n\nAzurah wished our paths to cross. Now we walk one path together. Perhaps Krin'ze will join us in time.
Thanks to us, the Inquisitors are leaderless. Without the Grand Inquisitor, I suspect their efforts will be much less coordinated from this point forward.\n\nThat is my hope, anyway.

The enforcers of faith have a very specific definition of heresy. I am more concerned about cantors becoming dro-m'Athra than I am about changing minds.\n\nCan you ask around about Izalgo? Perhaps someone here in the trading post saw where he went.

Want it? I need it. I live for it … in a matter of speaking. \n\nThe enemies in the archive, the ones that severed all my threads of fate, I know they are copies. Killing one, two, or even a hundred of them will not satisfy me.
My vengeance comes from knowing those bastards are suffering and dying in the archives. \n\nDon't worry, warrior. As much as this existence irks me, it is tolerable.

Have you ever had a melody stuck in your head? That experience would not be too far from what death is like now. \n\nAt times it's comforting to have something to think about. Other times it is the most aggravating experience in all of existence.

Why? For the same reason Viti killed her sister. I was afraid of losing Ravith forever.\n\nIf she refused Azurah's redemption, our souls would never meet at the Crossing. I was not strong enough to accept that. Not then. So I struck at Talbira instead.

Ravith-morna escaped. Everyone believed she had killed Talbira. I could not admit my guilt, so I remained silent.\n\nI never was able to compel Ravith back from the shadows. I died at her hands. According to that tablet, she met her end that day, too.

Yeah. Snap has her all over Greenshade. Along the coast, near the ruins of Labyrinth, and somewhere called Echo Pond. What were you up to, Wisteria?\n\nHow do you feel about taking another little trip, friend?
You did. But, I think you underestimate the depths of my anger.\n\nMaligraphies aren't real creatures. I died and my opponents didn't even have the decency to exist!
They're real enough to injure, maim, and kill. But do not mistake them for being unique or original. Killing one does not end their line. Another can be summoned from the same script.

Daedra at least have the decency to disappear for a while after they're killed. Killing a Fabled does nothing. They manifest again with no interruption!\n\nI'll never have my revenge in the way that I long for. But, I refuse to give up.
You did. But, can you fathom just how many Marauders there are in the archive? How many copies of the same Marauder?\n\nThis fight is not over. It will never be.

Why do I have to choose between the two options? We get the glorious opportunity to make all versions of the Marauder feel the same pain that I felt.\n\nJust think of all the Marauders you can kill. Think of the agony you can introduce to their lives.
I can't force you. But don't think for one moment that those bastards will show you mercy. They'll be more than happy to tear you apart and feast on your pain.
Do you think you could? Perhaps that will be possible one day—if Master Malkhest's plan to fix the archive ever works. \n\nBut no. I just want the Marauders to suffer.
Unequivocally. \n\nI would die again if it meant I could send warriors like you after the fabled.

Normally, we cantors are a nomadic and solitary bunch. Easy prey for a Rajaska.\n\nWe correspond with each other often, trading songs and stories of our travels. But some of the other cantors have fallen silent. I fear the worst.

Viti says they are, in their own way. They are intent on attacking the Rajaska, instead of defending those they prey upon.\n\nI am sure they would get that done faster if they worked with you and Zerith. But nobody pays attention to my suggestions.

It is hard to get word to every member of a group as scattered as ours. Besides, we cannot pause in our duties. \n\nWe exorcise dark spirits, but we cannot cleanse bent souls the way Zerith can. Namiira never sleeps.

Plenty of field work, actually. Not all exorcisms. Tending to those in need, writing songs, singing whatever I wanted whenever I wished to.\n\nQuite the change of pace from what I had been doing before all this.

You mean strictly my opinion? Let's say some Ayleids worshiped a secret deity. Or a person. Someone who was eventually taken away from them and the world, forever.\n\nThat's what I'd like to say. But we're here to dig for facts, not fiction.

The jagged handwriting and carvings.The last inscription talks about setting someone free. A slave? The deity they worshiped? It's too vague for an objective theory. This can't go in the book, not until I'm sure what it means.

Viti is an exceptional mentor. But I could not remain with someone who ignored such an obvious sign from Azurah. \n\nBut she is not an Inquisitor. She may yet come around. I just hope that happens sooner rather than later.

Before that, even. I was sahida under High Cantor Viti. Her protege. We had a falling out. She refuses to see the good in what you and Zerith can do. \n\nI am free to wander on my own now. Despite the risks, I plan to make the most of it.

Izalgo is a little scatterbrained. I swear, he would lose his tail if it were not attached to his arse! And yet he always manages to keep track of that journal of his.\n\nHe has the most beautiful voice. I hope you get the chance to hear him sing.

Well enough to know that if he has not replied to one of my letters, it means something is wrong. \n\nWe are more than just fellow cantors. I sang at his nephew's name-day. I really hope you can find him.

As it happens, she dropped the message the courier gave her. Seems like the cantor ran afoul of the Inquisition. Which explains her anger. The Inquisition has methods that will make your tail hairs bristle.\n\nSee for yourself. Just leave me out of it.

Thankfully, she wasn't here to perform an exorcism. Said she was meeting someone, but expected interference. Told me to wash away any lingering darkness and dropped this scroll before she ran off.\n\nI never had a head for letters, so you can have it.

The Bent Dance is a rhythm felt in the soul when one has strayed too far from the joy of life by circumstance. Khajiit hear it as part of the duality of our nature.\n\nYou have fought your share of dro-m'Athra by now. They are the end result.

Songs of the Twilight Cantors can help those who hear the Bent Dance reject it, if we are quick enough. But a living soul that listens to the Bent Dance for too long falls beyond our reach.\n\nZerith claims the fallen are not lost to him. We shall see.

Think of the moons. They have faces that are light, and faces that are shadowed.\n\nKhajiit also have two faces. Most only ever wear their face of light. But with rage or anguish, a rhythm calls us to wear our shadowed face. That is the Bent Dance.

Sort of. But this was all me. Me and my magic. I think it was Wisteria's memory. I reached out through the connection we share and manifested a moment that happened, right there in that tent. \n\nWait. Do you think I could do it again?

Exactly! Where were those other two places Snap wrote down? I think the next one was over near the Labyrinth? We head over, find another object connected to Wisteria. And this time I really focus.\n\nWho knows what we might see?
Never heard of the place. We tried to find the Ceythalmor's primary base for ages. But you can't throw a rock in Summerset without hitting a ruin. Any one of them could be a secret lair.
Tanlorin Response

We have one more location to check. Echo Pond. I say we head there and see what other memories I can manifest. We might learn more about their big plan or the location of Dusk Keep. It's obviously the staging ground.

We don't know where it is, but we do know Wisteria will be there. Gods help me, I have an idea. I pulled on our connection to see memories of her past, right? \n\nWhat if I try to push on that connection and use it to open a portal straight to her?

That's a reasonable question. Won't know until I try! But first, let's go to the greenhouse. Hyacinth and the Gardener have connections to Wisteria, too. \n\nIf I can tangle us all together and really push, maybe I can get us directly into Dusk Keep.

I do not trust my tongue to recount this sad tale, but there is a ritual I could perform. It allows us to walk the path of my memories. But I must perform it in a specific place.\n\nTry to keep an open mind. What you and Krin'ze see may trouble you.

Zerith can invite forward the dead, yes? If he calls forth Moon-Singer Talbira, she could share her song with me. A song that can hold fast even the first Rajaska.\n\nWe have to do something to save the other Twilight Cantors. This could be it.

He loved her, walker. I imagine he tried. But no amount of love can force someone to seek redemption. You must want it for yourself.\n\nRavith prayed for power, sought it from whoever was listening. It seems Namiira answered her call.

You know me, yes? You need to trust me right now. I am an exorcist. I know the signs of dark spirits. \n\nThe things the Void whispers, tempting us into darkness. I sense nothing like that from Talbira.

It's hard for her to show me anything right now. And yet I can't shake the feeling that our souls are deeply connected.\n\nI'll have to go looking for myself. Remembering things from a life I didn't know I lived is … very strange.

I am a bit overwhelmed. But with your help we have found a song that can stop Ravith-morna. \n\nAnd I've made a deep connection with one of my ancient sisters. I am awed by the grace of Azurah. And ready to sing.
Forgiveness cannot abide while truth festers in shadow.\n\nMysterious, isn't it? There must be some reason for shrouding her exact meaning from me. I'm eager to discover it for myself!

It certainly seems … feels? As if it has something to do with Zerith and Ravith-morna.\n\nHe works to forgive and redeem fallen souls. Perhaps some truth must still be revealed before he can forgive her for what she's done.
This is all very new to me! I still have much to discover. Azurah teaches us that living Khajiit are unbound by fate. \n\nWe find our own paths, walker. As I will find mine with Talbira.

I know Talbira's song. Now I need to practice. I'll also see if I can teach it to other Twilight Cantors. \n\nI just hope nobody asks too many questions about how I learned it. Especially the Inquisitors.
That I wrote the song myself. If Talbira's soul has been reborn in me … well. That's not really a lie, is it?\n\nI won't mention you and Zerith, don't worry.

The ritual caused me a great deal of pain, tamiit. Speaking about it only opens wounds I would rather remain closed.\n\nLet us invite forward the spirit of Moon-Singer Talbira, as Krin'ze suggests. Through her, everything will be brought to light.

Manifested a memory? No. Never. My deep magic, it's not something I really like to use. But that time? It felt natural. Like breathing.\n\nI focused on how badly I wanted to see Wisteria. And it's like I just pulled part of her right to me.

I think, I think I may be on her mind. I once found her drinking a bottle before a mission. She was embarrassed. Told me that it reminded her of home.\n\nI said it was a bad habit that would be a little less bad if we shared it.

Haha. Not even a little. Hyacinth was so mad.\n\nFriend, I think she's scared. I mean, I clearly don't know everything about her. But if she's drinking this, she's worried. Worried that our—that her fight might cost her everything.

The captain! Our squad captain might know. His quarters are just in the next room. No guarantees. We cover our tracks, even from each other. Something the lot of you could take notes on.\n\nBut there may be something there ….
I've been aware of Lord Hollowjack's power for a long time now. I know when he casts his victims back into our world.

You have seen how the moonclaw works. Not only does it focus my power, it senses the presence of creatures of darkness, like the Rajaska. But Azurah has also used it on occasion to lead me to where I am needed.\n\nAt least, that is what I believe.

Detritus? It's a ghastly place, a half-world filled with horrors. Lord Hollowjack sups on the fears of mortals there. During this time of year, portals open between that demiplane and this, and he works his dark desires on the living.
I do. I'm sorry. The shame I feel goes beyond mere words. When you are trapped as long as I was, you will make any excuse, justify any injustice, for a promise of escape.
I know. No words will ever make this right. I can only hope that my actions to atone for what I did, not just to the Haunted you rescued, but to you, will some day be enough.

I pray you never have to find out. I've missed so much in the time I was gone. The Witchmothers have given me shelter for now, to teach me about what I've lost. And perhaps this poor old priest can find forgiveness someday.

Whatever we discover in Pa'alat, we must do what we can to mend the rift between Krin'ze and Viti.\n\nForgiveness. That is the business of my order. If it were easy, the world would never have needed the Hidden Moon.

These scrolls were penned by those who understood the teachings of the Hidden Moon. The lessons inscribed are meant to take precedence over the whims of the heart.\n\nMy struggle with such matters is why we are here now.

You are right. It is for Azurah to determine if I am worthy to carry forward the teachings of the Hidden Moon into this age. To embody them and apply them. And to know that it is never too late to remember a forgotten creed. \n\nThank you, tamiit.

I cannot deny this. An imperfect vessel is better than no vessel at all. Azurah still has need of me. Why else would she have sent me back? And through her, I may yet see myself repaired.\n\nThank you, tamiit.

Not the perfect implement of Azurah that I once held myself to be. But to say I was ill-made by the Mother of Twilight … I would not hiss in her face so.\n\nI am flawed by my own actions. My choices in life.

Vandorallen told us stories of his family's glorious past. They served as advisors and confidants to important figures. \n\nHe always seemed upset that they fell to minor nobility, which makes their absence from the noble circles worth note.

It was a while ago. I remember being glad that I wouldn't have to spar with him again. \n\nVandorallen kept his own counsel, but I know being pulled from training upset him. He sobbed as he passed through the gates.

Most nobles, especially the ones looking to gather more power and rebuild the glory of their ancestors, tend to sponsor a festival every now and again. \n\nBut the Albuses haven't done that since Vandorallen left the Spire.

A lot of scouting, thinking, and more sneaking behind soldiers than a trained Battlemage wants to admit. I knew if I followed one squad stationed in Cyrodiil for long enough, then something would happen. \n\nI was right.

I suppose the heart of the Hidden Moon is redemption through service. No one is ever so lost that they cannot find their way back into Azurah's embrace.\n\nWe serve Azurah in our actions now. Thank you for reminding me, tamiit.

I see the wisdom of your words. And in times so dire, none of us have the luxury of self-pity while so much is at stake. Myself least of all.\n\nI will have to think on this concept of redefinition. I thank you for talking me through this, tamiit.
I started training for missions like this when I was ten. I'm more than prepared.\n\nBesides, the Albus scouts were very focused on their targets. I don't think they even knew I was nearby.

Knowledge of the Empire really is fading. \n\nIt's a fortress where the Imperial Battlemages live and train. Our number is dwindling. Most potentials would rather join a guild or fight for their alliance than face initiation.
I still have to complete several missions before they'll consider letting me take the initiation trial. \n\nDon't worry about me. Even if I'm not a full-fledged Battlemage, I can handle myself.
Many potentials don't survive it. I hope that solving this mystery will prove that I am ready to take the trial, but we'll see.

The parable posits that those of the Hidden Moon who eschew the outside world can never truly help their fellow cats. We are meant to know the heights of joy, the depths of sorrow, and everything in between.\n\nWhat could Izalgo mean by quoting it now?
Hrrm. You are right. And not just my life before. But here, now. In my life with you.\n\nFinding my way out of darkness may serve to honor Azurah. I will meditate on this. Thank you, tamiit.

Guilt is strong enough to build walls around our souls. Trapped by such dejection, one may forget to touch other lives for the better. To truly live as Azurah wants us to.\n\nA hard truth, tamiit. But one I needed to hear. Thank you.

Finding a new cause to fight for. The Spire used to be that for me, but I will never blindly follow an organization again. \n\nI have the skills to create change, but I have to ensure that change is for the better.

No. And if the Divines favor me, I never will. He wrote to me a few times and I burned the letters. Martus betrayed the Spire, he betrayed our cause, and he betrayed me. \n\nI didn't kill him in the Dread Cellar, thanks to you. But I still want to.

Trusting someone to guard your back isn't easy with all we experienced. Martus and the Dread Cellar affected me more than I thought they would. \n\nStill, I trust you enough to join me for this mission.

He's not daft enough to tell the nobles that he's behind these deaths. \n\nSoldiers disappear all the time. Perhaps the alliances say that these soldiers died in battle. Then Cato steps in and gives their families a cause to fight for.

He must be better at it than we think. Look around. There are more guards here than one noble family can employ. \n\nWe have to press on. If Cato thinks he's avenging his son, he will never stop on his own.
I opened every occupied cage I could find. They should all be on their way out of the redoubt and back to their respective armies as we speak. I have their word that they won't attack each other.

The soldiers thought there was a strict timeline to these events. To what end? I do not know. Cato Albus is eccentric, but he has his reasons for all of this. We just need to figure out what they are.
