Better than he knew me. We were in the same training groups at the Battlespire so I had to duel, study, and eat next to him for years.\n\nI cheered when he left the Spire.

Of course, but let me take another look.\n\nThe townsfolk said she was upset at the courier. I can see why. This summons is less of an inquiry and more of an accusation. I have little sympathy for Viti, but this missive makes even my fur rise.
I didn't mark the day in my journal. Most potentials remove themselves from the Spire, but I remember hearing that his uncle demanded he return home. \n\nThat must've been when Cato's son died.

I don't know. Maybe Caecilius didn't have the magical aptitude necessary to train there? \n\nI heard that Cato Albus is as powerful a mage as Vandorallen was. Perhaps their magical talent drew them together after Caecilius's tragic demise.

Not just High Cantor Viti. The Inquisitors only tolerate worship of Azurah so long as it suits their own needs, yes? They consider the Twilight Cantors to be tools, nothing more.\n\nAnd when tools no longer serve a purpose? You dispose of them.

It refers to us both as heretics, tamiit. We should be used to such insults by now.\n\nBut they blame the Twilight Cantors for failing to stop the spread of Rajaska. Charging those most at risk with failure to protect others? Pathetic.
It is … a personal matter. This one has history in Orcrest.\n\nIt is something that has weighed heavy upon Viti's soul for some time now. We will talk more about it once we reach our destination.

Great danger. This once-proud city is overrun with plague and monsters. The Twilight Cantors know of no songs that might help.\n\nBut Krin'ze tells Viti this is no concern for you and Zerith-var. This one hopes my sahida is not wrong about that.

Viti is aware. A different sort of danger than Inquisitors or Rajaska, yes? And this one knows of no songs to drive off sickness and disease.\n\nBut Krin'ze tells me this is no concern for you and Zerith-var. This one hopes she is not wrong about that.

I'm not upset with myself. I'm furious with Cato. He caused so much suffering and death, but didn't live long enough to give any of the other families he harmed some closure.\n\nI can set my feelings aside. We stopped the Albuses. That's what matters.

The noble families Cato Albus targeted deserve to know what happened to their loved ones. \n\nI'll write to them and explain this whole ordeal. Perhaps knowing the cause of their grief will ensure this never happens again.

They only lent their support because Cato convinced them that the Three Banners War killed their loved ones. Noble houses don't like to be duped. The only solace we can offer them now is that Cato is dead, as is anyone else involved in the plot.

Return to the Battlespire. The battlemages hold some influence among the noble houses. There's going to be an uproar once the leading families discover what the Albuses did. It will be a nightmare, but one you and I don't have to solve.

Even without the connections of the Battlespire, I'm beginning to make a name for myself. Work finds its way to me as often as I go looking for it. So it's onto the next place where I can make a difference.
Why did he only appear now? If he intervened before, a lot of soldiers wouldn't have died. He could have stopped this, but he didn't.

That makes some sense. Caecilius seemed to want to end this entire affair peacefully, which aligns with how Cato spoke of him. Thankfully, it looks like Caecilius managed to calm his father. I'm sure I can get him to stand trial now.

Of course. He wronged so many for so long, I can't allow him to go unpunished no matter the reason behind his actions.\n\nHe doesn't look like he'll fight me anymore and now that we have him secured, I can monitor his magic. He won't surprise me.

I left Krin'ze to heal at Khenarthi's Rise and decided to gather my fellow Twilight Cantors. I planned to bring them there as well, but with the disappearance of the grand inquisitor, the Inquisitors ordered us to aid them.

I did not ask. They had a location and a plan of attack. They just needed the Twilight Cantors to assist them.\n\nAs ever, the Rajaska were too much for the Inquisitors. Their faith was not strong enough. But without their swords, neither are we.
Of course you are. Thank the moons and all their forms for this mercy. Is there a clear path to safety?
Hah! High time the high cantor was bestowed the gift of common sense.\n\nWe can hold this position no longer. Is there a way to safety?
Oh! Blessed mother of the dusk and dawn, who sends such warriors to protect her devoted! \n\nWhen the Inquisitors fell, we feared all was lost. Is there a path to safety?

A shortcut. A doorway across planes. Where the void in my own heart was born.\n\nRavith-morna will use this bypass to send her moon beast to the Crossing. To let it prey on the souls of all Khajiit and make real the dark dream of every dro-m'Athra.

I feel the truth of what Krin'ze said back in Khenarthi's Rise. My guilt holds open this door to the Void.\n\nI am ready now, thanks to you. To embrace forgiveness and close this breach. But I cannot face Ravith-morna or her moon beast alone.

Talbira and Krin'ze share a soul now. She taught Krin'ze her song. I thought perhaps she made other things known as well.\n\nI have no further excuse beyond cowardice, tamiit. If this was a test from Azurah, I have surely failed. I am sorry.
Go on then, tamiit. I have nothing left to hide.

It was easy enough to convince myself that it was. I had not the strength to kill Ravith-morna, so Talbira would have fallen to the might of her song regardless.\n\nThe difference is that I would have died as well. Perhaps I would have deserved it.

What haunts me is that I did not even have to lie. Like our Twilight Cantors, moon-singers were prey to Rajaska.\n\nI was not the only hadaliit of the order to turn a blade of mercy on a singer in the throes of falling to the Bent Dance.

It was not a lie, tamiit. I thought myself beyond Azurah's redemption. My soul would have bent if not for the training of my order.\n\nBut as hopeless as I was, in those final moments, I could not bring myself to denounce my faith in Azurah.

I remember Ravith's anger. Not like the Void. Like the dawn's fire she had before the darkness took her. I felt her blade. And then … nothing.\n\nWhatever happened, I must have taken her down with me. She came back in this age, and so did I.

The Hidden Moon contended with the Rajaska for years after Talbira's death. At some point, the weight of my guilt became too much for me. I sought out Ravith-morna. Told her I was ready to join her in the Void.

I think for the same reason I could not turn my blade on her. Even shrouded in darkness, I know her heart. \n\nI wanted to coax her to the Crossing. She wished to call me to the Void. In death, we would lose each other forever.

I felt the eyes of other hadaliit. Some of them must have guessed the truth.\n\nBut, no. I did not correct the assumptions made. As Talbira warned through Krin'ze, I let the truth fester in shadow. Then and now.

You saw the tablet in my tomb. I lingered in undeath, body preserved, spirit wandering. Perhaps my transgressions weigh so great that I am beyond Azurah's redemption, that I will never find my way to the Crossing. But I refuse to give in to the Void.

To redeem my actions and see an end to Ravith-morna, of course. Otherwise, I would have passed to the other side of Azurah's Crossing. The Lunar Lattice. The Sands Behind the Stars.\n\nI can think of no other reason for me to be here.

That is true. And despite everything, you are here with me.\n\nI suppose some lessons are only learned through action and ritual. If you are willing to help me, perhaps we can learn together. Let us explore this place and see what we can do.

Strange. Time passed differently with the spirits, but she should have returned by now. Did something happen? No, I will not give in to fear by speculating. I am renewed.\n\nI need to be to stand with you twin moons and see the end of Ravith-morna.

Yes, Viti helped get us here. Then, with Talbira's assistance, I started to commune with the spirits that fill this place. Viti left to gather the Twilight Cantors. To bring them here for safety.\n\nYou did not happen to see her when you arrived?

Love is a willing bond between two souls. I can think of no stronger connection. Ravith and Zerith were both devotees of Azurah. Love is all she teaches.\n\nWell, that and forgiveness. So now Zerith needs to be reminded of the latter.

How do you think she felt? To ask her partner to kill the one he loved? After all, she introduced them.\n\nZerith's heart is not the only one wounded by guilt. But he is the only one whose heart was so tightly lashed to Ravith.

Scattered throughout the ruins below.\n\nYou remember Eifa's warning, yes? Of the moon beast Ravith-morna is summoning? I hear it growling. It stirs from the call of her chorus. Pray we are not too late to stop its waking.

And why should it stop there? If we survive, I will spread more of Azurah's teachings of love and forgiveness. This era is definitely in dire need.\n\nYour words lead me to illuminated paths of clarity, tamiit. I am ready to face Ravith-morna.

Yes. You are right. Azurah forgives all who seek forgiveness. Why should I think myself the exception? Pride makes me stumble on this path. Thank you, tamiit, for guiding me to more stable footing.\n\nI am ready, then. To face Ravith-morna once more.

For all the plans and tactics involved, war is messy. Spies are everywhere provided your opponent has gold and means. It's natural for soldiers to be suspicious.\n\nNot that explanations have any effect on grief.

When you have walked the world as I have, you see how often trust is rewarded.\n\nStay away from my sahida. She may not understand, but I know nothing good comes from abiding necromancy. Even if it is well-intended.
My sahida? Disobey my direct orders? You and that charlatan necromancer have influenced her with your dark thoughts. \n\nAnd in so short a time! What business could she have with you?

Ah yes. The Rajaska. How convenient that they appeared at the same time as your friend.\n\nThis one looked into his Order of the Hidden Moon. A once-noble clan brought to ruin by corruption from within. And this is who you choose to travel with?

When the vulture eats the asp, it does not do so out of virtue. It does so to slake its appetite for flesh.\n\nYou may hunt the shadows. This one has seen as much. But there is a darkness in your friend where his heart should be. Viti can sense it.

Amazing! Let's see … river lilies should be easy enough to find along the stream near Phaer.\n\nOh, and ask my friend Chirrabi in Mathiisen to sell you the silver dust. Tell her "buttercups aren't weeds" and she'll know you're with me.

We suffered a lot of tragedies in the Spire. I know the feeling. There are times when the pain barely affects you and others ….\n\nI don't know if I understand Cato. But I know that a death can be more than the loss of one life.
I see. Well, don't let me overwhelm you with our problems. \n\nTan, do you need some help with that lock? Maybe your friend will have better luck with it.

I've gotten into worse scrapes. Tan and I can tend to my wounds, and I'll make for one of the greenhouses.\n\nI appreciate the concern though. I'm not one to turn down a little attention. Especially from Tanlorin, when I can get them to focus.

Ravith gave in to Namiira and became the first Rajaska. She stalked the other moon-singers at Star Haven Adeptorium, bent them to join her chorus. Any of the Hidden Moon that opposed her, she slaughtered them.\n\nAll but Moon-Singer Talbira and me.

My former partner was strong. With Azurah's aid, she created a song to ensnare even a Rajaska. She ordered me to take up my sword. And I ….\n\nThe pain. I can speak of this no more! Please, tamiit! Abandon this ritual.

If you get a clear answer, make sure to tell me. Tan has a tendency to exaggerate. \n\nDid they tell you the one about the Whiterun Jarl's daughter? It's better when I tell it. I don't leave out the ice troll that threw Tanlorin into the lake.

The Ring has boltholes we call greenhouses scattered across the Dominion. Hyacinth's is in Greenshade. I want to check that he's safe and get his take on all this.\n\nIf you decide to walk away, I won't blame you. But I sure would love some company.

Forgiveness cannot abide when truth festers in shadow? Yes. I am certain I understand Talbira's message.\n\nBut Krin'ze does not. Strange. Perhaps the Moon-Singer still has things to teach our cantor. She will understand soon enough.

I am still getting used to such a formal title for her. I am her sahida. Her protege.\n\nIn Viti, Azurah's love and devotion takes a much more … rigid form than other Twilight Cantors you may have met. But I value her guidance all the same.

I tried to get on his good side, walker. I really did. He does not seem to have one.\n\nHe is an Inquisitor of the Torval Curiata. The militant arm of those who uphold the Riddle'Thar epiphany. As far as I can tell, he is very good at his job.

Refuse those who require our songs? Kes kridesi! It is unthinkable.\n\nYes, they force us into these uniforms and bestow our elders with fancy, high-ranking titles. And they keep us from wandering where we like. Still, they need our help.

Too long, it feels like.\n\nThe Inquisitors only recently pressed us into service. They have need of our songs or would hardly bother with us otherwise. Our worship of Azurah does not fit in their neat little box of what constitutes proper faith.

Outsiders sometimes think of us as acolytes of Azurah. Our devotion to her allows us to exorcise dark spirits through the art of song.\n\nWhen not on a mission, we wander where we like. Or we used to.

I'm not naive. I know we can't change the world overnight. But all you need is one spark to start a fire, right? To start burning away the corruption that eats at my homeland.\n\nOut of idle curiosity. Does that sound at all fun to you?
A tenet of faith that reveres the moon spirits, Jone and Jode. \n\nWe cantors, instead, are permitted to serve and follow Azurah. Our songs are too valuable for us to be excluded from the faith.

The beating of the dark heart of Lorkhaj. If one listens for the whispers of Namiira, the Lady of Decay, the drums of the Bent Dance are sure to follow.\n\nTo speak too much of these evil things only serves to invite them in. Be wary.

It could prove a fortuitous partnership, should these Daedra-worshiping singers overcome their impudence and lack of discipline.\n\nThe high cantor here serves as an example for all to follow. In the Riddle'Thar's name.

We have orders from the Inquisitors of the Torval Curiata.\n\nOur mission involves something dire and immediate. We need the voice of every cantor we can get. As soon as the rest of our cohort arrives, we must go. But Azurah provides and sent us you.

The beating of the dark heart of Lorkhaj. A haunting and discordant song.\n\nHearing it creates cracks in the soul. And once the Void seeps in, it fills its vessel. Turning the poor Khajiit into a mindless puppet of the Void. A dro-m'Athra.
The fate of my order? When you say it like that ….\n\nYou mean to tell me it no longer exists? I do not believe you. How could such a thing even happen?

We are Azurah's most faithful. I follow her calling. I devote my life to her message of love and redemption.\n\nBut my duty is not in conflict with the other spirits known and worshiped across the sixteen kingdoms.

The Temple of the Hidden Moon lies deep in the Ashen Scar in Northern Elsweyr. Carved into the long shadows of a desert canyon.\n\nBut we have shrines hidden in other places, too. Such as the one we head to now. You will see.

It is a most holy totem. Azurah's grasp laid over my own.\n\nWith her strength and my faith, it allows me to invite forth the souls of Khajiit who need guidance to the afterlife. It also allows me to create doors to cross Nirni with great speed.

At its full power, certainly. Now? I must be careful. The magic has leaked from it during the years I was interred.\n\nI apologize, zha'al. This all still feels like a bad dream. I am left to wonder why I am here. Perhaps we can find out together.

Revenge happened! We misjudged the guildmaster's skill. And his anger. \n\nHe let me live when I renounced the Order of the Black Worm. What you call the Worm Cult. Made me swear to tell Prince Azah everything I know.

All right, you bastards! I'm done with all this anyway. No promise of power is worth dying for. \n\nThe Order of the Black Worm has returned to take vengeance. On the Fighters Guild, the Mages Guild, and all of Tamriel.
I don't think so. Not quite yet.\n\nMy pain is great. Get me something to ease my suffering. Then, I'll share what I know.
To the undercroft beneath the Vile Manse. If my fellow Twilight Cantors are not dro-m'Athra already, they will be soon. And then they will be lost for good.\n\nThere is nothing that can be done.

When Khajiit die, love and forgiveness set their souls upon a path toward blissful light. But sometimes guilt and misdeeds cloud that path.\n\nAzurah commands those lost in the dark must not be left to suffer forever. It was my duty to retrieve them.

Necromancy. Adepts of the Hidden Moon call to the Void and invite a willing soul back to inhabit a physical form. These dead followed us into battle. Fought and fell alongside us.\n\nIn service and sacrifice, they see their souls purified.

Honestly, every time I go to Vulkwasten, I end up … well. Let's say I don't have any clear memories of the area. But I think there's a little island near Belarata. \n\nBut what sort of ring can you grow? Let's head there and find out!

Not a clue. Oleander and I did try to figure it out once, but we didn't get very far.\n\nThe only thing we know for certain is that he has access to coin—heaps of it! Our gear, our weapons, the greenhouses, the Gardener provides them all.

I'll tell you what I can, but he's a bit of a mystery to me. I've only met him a handful of times. \n\nStrong scent of perfume, fancy clothes. And like I said, he loves riddles. He's the one that picks our flowery code names, so Bogcup is his fault.

Hard to say. As the Gardener says, he's always growing something. I think he opens and closes them to maintain secrecy. \n\nI spend most of my time at Hyacinth's greenhouse, in Greenshade, but others are scattered all across the Aldmeri Dominion.

Why wouldn't I wait? I've enjoyed traveling with you so far … I mean, other than what happened to Oleander. Not sure I would have gotten through all that without you.\n\nBesides, the invitation specifically said to bring a friend, so here we are!

Not at all. Hyacinth's greenhouse is unique. It reflects his personality, what with all the constructs and magical gear.\n\nMost are just warehouses. Hideouts to spend the night or weather a storm. I've got wine stashed in a few of them, just in case!

Grief is a strange and powerful motivator. No two people suffer the same pains, but it can be a powerful uniting force. \n\nI don't doubt that the Albuses can garner favor, sympathy, and convince other nobles to join their cause this way.

I supposed as much. Their leader can turn other Khajiit into dro-m'Athra with a swiftness unlike anything I have ever seen!\n\nBut with cantors, we become like her. Our voices turned into dark weapons. I never thought we could be twisted in such a way.

I want to tell people he can be trusted. That he truly was sent by Azurah. But it may take some convincing. And saying as much could get me in trouble with the Torval Curiata.\n\nI will have to be careful with what I say, and I who I say it to.

I will certainly try. I would leave it to the high cantor, but I overheard her say she does not wish to cause my brothers and sisters to panic and neglect their duties.\n\nBut the cantors need to know!

Smart. And I'm in too much pain to argue. Merric spared my life when I told him that the Order of the Black Worm, what you call the Worm Cult, has returned to take vengeance on first the Fighters Guild, then the Mages Guild, then all of Tamriel.

Yes, Lirinisse! Are you friends of hers? She was as starched as the archmagister's robes, but she knew her spellcraft. \n\nIt was eerie, she was so calm when they dragged her out of her office. Almost like she was expecting them. Strange.

I made it a point to avert my eyes and look away. But Reeve Nardarmor has an office in Skywatch Manor. If anyone knows where they took Lirinisse, it would be someone there.\n\nJust don't mention you talked to us. We don't want to end up on his list.
I am hurt that she would speak with such venom. And angered that she would seek to turn you against me.\n\nBut … she is not wrong about me. Darkness gathers in my soul, like in any Khajiit.

My training with the Hidden Moon armors my soul. Unless I abandon my faith in Azurah, it will keep me from bending to the dark. \n\nHigh Cantor Viti does not know this. Could not know this. But in my life before, I passed far greater tests than these.
Ha. Surviving them is one thing. Recounting them another.\n\nSoon, tamiit. But we should not keep Krin'ze waiting.
Oh this? Just an average day for me. But say … if you help me out of this ice, I'll tell you all about it. \n\nI'll happily pass some coin your way, too. For the inconvenience. Please?

I am sorry about the Inquisitors, but my concern is for Izalgo. Let me see. Oh. Were the other cantors lured with dreams such as this? We have no defense against such darkness. No song that can cure such a summons. \n\nWe must stop this Ravith-morna.

We must attack with everything we have.\n\nSummoning a moon beast from Namiira's Void takes time, but we have no idea how close Ravith-morna is to succeeding. She only grows stronger and bends more to join her dark chorus while we delay.

Krin'ze knows the song of Moon-Singer Talbira, which will bind Ravith-morna. And Viti insisted on coming. She can protect Krin'ze while you and I silence Ravith's chorus.\n\nThis is the chance to finally redeem myself. Are you ready, tamiit?
Mistscrub grows around here. Low bushes with red, jagged leaves. Chewing the leaves dulls pain. \n\nBring me some mistscrub leaves and I'll tell you everything I told Merric.

I never worry about the inevitable. Our paths will cross again, and soon.\n\nI know how to stop Rajaska. Their presence here explains mine. But I do not know how to navigate this new faith, these Inquisitors. Thank Azurah that you are here to help me.

Some part of me always will be. But it is clear I am needed here now. With you.\n\nI am immensely grateful for this second pounce, tamiit. Knowing it is for a reason and a purpose makes it easier to appreciate the wonders of this age.

There are more things now that unite than divide. Guilds, factions, parties of adventurers all working toward common goals. Friendships forged like the bonds of family. Distance is not the obstacle it was back in my day. It is inspiring to see.

Talbira's song was powerful enough to hold Ravith-morna, to drown out her voice. Ravith has forsaken Azurah. But perhaps we might yet persuade her to return to the light. \n\nOf course, Krin'ze will need time to practice before that day comes.

I tried, tamiit. I truly did. With you at my side, I thought I was ready to confront my past. But the pain … I was wrong. I am sorry.\n\nBut Azurah has given us a path forward. Talbira is here, lending us her song. So it was not for nothing.

Excellent. Lady Lirinisse was very specific. I have the document right here. A vault to be held in trust. To be accessed only in the event of her demise. Very pragmatic.\n\nIn this case, to be made available to one Tanlorin of Rellenthil. And friend.

Here is the key. The vault is on the table behind me. She only purchased a small one. The contents now belong to you and your friend.\n\nIf Tanlorin wishes to retain the vault afterward, they'll need to sign a new contract. At a reasonable rate.

Snapdragon didn't have a chance to follow up. These could be mustering outposts, with all kinds of notes about what the Ceythalmor are really up to.\n\nBest case, we figure out Wisteria's plan. Worst case, we cause the Ceythalmor some trouble. Heh.

I will put aside the title of high cantor. It was a construct of the Torval Curiata, used to control the Twilight Cantors.\n\nI thought at one time that taking on the role would spare my brothers and sisters from the purges of faith. No longer.

There are so many things I am and am not. Am I whole? No. But perhaps no one truly is. Making peace with that truth is my challenge now.\n\nI am able to step forward. It is easier to do so with you at my side, tamiit.

She was the love of one life, yes. But when we were parted and met again, we were much changed from each other. For the better, I think.\n\nI have a new life, now. I am a moon in a new phase. Let us see where that takes me.

Somewhere in Cantor Krin'ze's soul is the song that Moon-singer Talbira used to bind Ravith-morna. \n\nIf Krin'ze can hold Ravith-morna in place, perhaps … after all these years … I can persuade her to return to Azurah's embrace.
How can that …? We eradicated them, didn't we?\n\nA threat of this magnitude must be crushed swiftly. The mages and Merric can use our help. Can I count on you to join the fight?

No. It should have been impossible. Wards throughout the underground chambers should protect against incursions. The underground library, doubly so. It's where we have all our secure meetings. But let's figure it out after we stop the attack.

Gladiolus and Snapdragon were on a simple mission. Follow and observe. Easy. They were attacked. Got separated. When she found him, Gladiolus was dead. Frozen. A look of fear on his face. \n\nThis traitor, they've taken so much from us. It has to end.

We know that now, but back then? We've always been a small group. Tight knit. Like a family. The Gardener said he trusted every one of us. That we couldn't start pointing fingers.\n\nWithout solid proof, it would have destroyed us.

We learned about the traitor from Snapdragon, a former member of the Ring. We helped her escape from a secret prison, after she was captured by the Ceythalmor. \n\nThe most daring prison break I've seen since that Hidden Armiger we—uh—never mind!

No, and I doubt she ever will. But if I know Snapdragon, that won't matter. Not until we find the traitor that imprisoned her. That got her husband killed.\n\nI just hope I get a chance to say goodbye before she leaves us again.

I don't even want to think about it. You've seen how we operate. We're a circle of trust, handpicked by the Gardener to get the job done.\n\nWhoever has turned against us, I know them. Probably very well. It hurts my stomach to even imagine.

What's not to love? We're cracking skulls and earning gold. The work I did for the Garland Ring was fulfilling, don't get me wrong. But it doesn't pay for drinks. No, to do that, I had to get creative.\n\nGot real good at bar tricks.

I'm not worried. Not really. Not when I'm by your side. We've done so much together already. Whoever the traitor is, we'll find them. \n\nWe have to, for Oleander. For Gladiolus. They deserve justice.

Miss what? Shoving gold coins up my nose? Oh, you mean the Garland Ring. Yes and no. It all has this weight to it now.\n\nHonestly, I'm trying to stay focused here with you. The traitor is a friend, right? Or, at least, I thought they were.

Don't, please. I know what you're saying. But if it's her ….\n\nIf we walk in that cave and Wisteria turns out to be the traitor … I don't know what I'll do. I can't run from this. But I can't talk about it right now, either.

We both heard the words of Eifa's spirit. Ravith-morna is attempting to summon a moon beast from the Void. A monster to hunt the souls seeking paths to Azurah's Crossing.\n\nShe uses the dark songs of her chorus to call this terrible beast forth.

Eifa said it best. The souls of Khajiit would never be safe to find their paths to Azurah. Even my Hidden Moon method of deliverance would not guarantee a secure journey.\n\nThe spirits of my people would never see the Sands Behind the Stars again.

Upon death, the spirits of Khajiit wander on paths to the Crossing, lit or dimmed by our deeds in life.\n\nThere, we find Azurah's embrace as she lifts our souls to the Lunar Lattice. A liminal place. The final destination before eternal paradise.

Talbira taught Cantor Krin'ze a song that can trap a Rajaska. Once Krin'ze learns it fully, we will find the den of the Rajaska and use the song to end them. And Ravith-morna, my heart from another life. Their leader.\n\nThis justice is long overdue.

Sure, but I let myself get captured. Let Mezamma use her illusion magic on me. You saw how she pretended to be me to capture Vanus. My guess is she's using the same trick here to infiltrate the Earth Forge.

Not only do I lead the Mages Guild, but I founded the organization! Some call me the greatest living mage, but that hardly does justice to my prestige.\n\nNeedless to say, I take particular offense to attacks against the guild and its member mages.

I can still feel her. The connection is fading, but still there. When we first arrived, she was like a storm beating against the inside of my skull. Anger. Frustration. Fear. Now, she's a breeze. A whisper in my ear.\n\nAnd now, she's gone.

I'm not going to waste time wondering what might have been. If this is how she wanted to change the world, we never had a future to begin with.\n\nFriend, hey, look. We won. The Proxy Queen is alive. Let's try to take joy in that.

Yes, Gabrielle called Mezamma snake-like. My extensive knowledge of Daedra tells me that she's likely a Harvester. Known for their illusion magic. I suspect that's how she got into our sanctum undetected.\n\nTell me, how did Merric die?

Merric was a great warrior, but also reckless. Attacking an unknown arcane device? Clearly a miscalculation. An intact soul reaper would have revealed more than the shards we recovered.\n\nHad he waited for you to intervene, he might still be alive.

Guild scout, bruiser, and general pain in the arse. At least, that's what Merric calls me.\n\nWhile most of the guild settled in to defend the remaining guildhalls, I volunteered to stay in the field.
You want us to waste time getting approval? No. I don't think so. I'm tired of waiting to be told what to do and when to do it.\n\nWe can handle this without them.

When have we ever needed assistance? We've been fine on our own, right? If anyone's going to stop Wisteria, it's going to be us. It has to be us. Hyacinth will just try to talk me out of it. Take things slow. Play it safe.\n\nNot today. Today we act.

When I was younger, before my tattoos, my magic would flare up when things got too emotional. And not just me, people around me. Their anger, or fear, or joy. I could feel it, physically feel it.\n\nI used to hate it, but this was kind of beautiful.

When I joined the Garland Ring, she accepted me, faults and all. Taught me how to use magic despite the dampening my tattoos projected. How to fight. Be confident. \n\nHow could I not fall in love? And now, that love might be just what we need.
All right, as long as we're quick. The Proxy Queen! I still can't believe Wisteria plans to kill her.

Hehe. She was trying, in her own Wisteria way, to say that I had to fight for what I wanted. That I was oustered for not being strong enough. That I still needed to grow up.\n\nI spent every day after that trying to keep up with her. Until I met you.

When I was oustered, my friends tried to be supportive. They said that I was strong. That I'd survive without my family. Find joy despite them.\n\nBut not Wisteria. She called my dream of changing the world childish. She was nothing if not honest.
As always, we are steadfast in contending with threats to the Khajiiti people. The specifics of our mission are not for wanderers to inquire.\n\nThis one suggests you be on your way.

I have contended with the Worm Cult longer than anyone. Based on previous encounters, they usually seek something disastrous. The more information we learn down here the better.\n\nI sense illusion magic nearby. Let's search this room for its source.

Our goal is to apply pressure to those well-placed individuals. Sometimes these … what to call them? These wartime profiteers?\n\nThey often have secrets. Adulterous affairs, fraudulent treasuries, gambling debts. That sort of thing.
Ha! Not everyone considers our work to be for the greater good. \n\nBut if I let a few frozen toes stop me from doing what I love, I'd never have met a stunning adventurer such as yourself.

If I tell you about the Ring, I'd have to stick a dagger in your gut. I'm joking! Mostly. \n\nHow do I put this? The High Elf colleges make decisions that effect the people of Tamriel. And some in those colleges use their positions to turn a profit.

I'm no one special. Just a lover of heists, princesses, and social politics. Which is exactly why I'm part of the Garland Ring!\n\nI adore the work! Even if it involves the occasional trap, daring escape, or the sharp end of a battle axe.
Sure. I was wondering when you'd ask. Not exactly subtle, are they? My family convinced me to get them. \n\nThey're magical. Something to keep me a little more, um, contained?

My family members are renowned mages, every one of them. But growing up, my relationship with magic was always a little more wild. Unstable.\n\nThese tattoos are meant to keep the magic, to keep me, under control.

No, no. It doesn't really hurt to talk about it anymore. Thanks to Wisteria, actually. \n\nShe really helped me get my magic under control. Mostly. Together we even discovered a few things. Maybe I'll show you later. If you play your cards right.
Forward, aren't you? I'm Tanlorin's mentor. I've trained them in combat, infiltration, and how to channel magicka—despite those damned tattoos.\n\nBeyond that? Well. Depends on the season, I suppose.

Oh, I like you. Listen, the Ring will lay low for a bit. Try to figure out how they learned about our mission. I'm going to have some time on my hands.\n\nI'd love to travel with you. I promise not to get you into trouble. Not too much, anyway.

A rest, I think. We Twilight Cantors are not used to all this excitement.\n\nSome quiet, far-off place where I can give my voice respite. And when I return? I will work with the other Twilight Cantors to learn more about the Hidden Moon.

She is still with me, of course. She is at peace now, seeing Ravith and Zerith made whole again. But her life was cut short. I do not mind sharing mine with her. Perhaps she has more to teach me.\n\nThank you, walker. For everything you did.

Certainly. No agent should head out unprepared.\n\nI know we might seem odd, with all the flowery names and subterfuge, but the Garland Ring stands for something important. I'm extremely proud of what we've accomplished.

They were to observe a high-ranking noble, a sponsor for the College of Aldmeri Propriety. Instead, they were set upon by assassins, agents I now believe were members of the Ceythalmor.\n\nShe resigned from the group, convinced they had been betrayed.

Snapdragon and I never quite saw eye to eye. Two strong wills clashing over everything. We managed to remain professional … until she lost faith in us, in our work. \n\nHer husband, Gladiolus, he died on a mission.

Well enough. And nothing in the greenhouse was permanently damaged. There are a few experiments I'll have to start again, but such is life. \n\nI understand the Ceythalmor's goal was to capture me. But why disturb my collections? Infuriating.

My wounds? You were asking after my health. Ah. I am completely healed, thanks to restorative magics.\n\nI considered fashioning a back brace from brassilisk parts. Unfortunately, by the time I worked out the design, I no longer needed the contraption.

We never went on any missions together, but she made quite an impression. Commanded the room, you know? And she liked me. I think. \n\nShe always teased me about something. In my experience, that's a good indication that someone doesn't hate you.

By doing something reckless. We must split up. I suspect time is of the essence, and I won't see another member of the Fighters Guild fall this day.\n\nTake the eastern hallway. And be careful. Illusions abound in this place.

Very much so. How did she say it? She knew what she was about. Composed when she needed to be, but otherwise she took up the space she felt she deserved. How could I not admire her?\n\nNow let's go make sure she's all right!

No. And I don't want to think about it right now. The best thing we can give Snapdragon and the Gardener is time to figure things out. \n\nIf I know Snapdragon, she won't have stopped her research just because she left the Garland Ring.

I think if she knew who the mole is, she would've tried to gut them by now. No, we just need to let them work. They'll reach out when they have a plan.\n\nThat leaves us with time to do some good old fashioned adventuring.
If I haven't gotten too turned around, this exit leads to one of the main thoroughfares.\n\nIt better not be too destroyed. A lot of people live up there.

It was a long time ago. When my studies of the Elder Scrolls advanced enough that I began to read them. \n\nIt was an odd process. Each time I read a scroll, it felt like my mind expanded as my world shrank. I've made worse trades in my life.

I heard wheels when Khafdeed led me through the tunnels. It seemed odd at the time, but I think Orpheon's army brought siege weapons with them. \n\nThese homes are old. They were built to weather storms, not catapults.

Live through this ordeal and you may find out. \n\nElder Scroll prophecies are hard to explain. What I saw proved that the scrolls are an important part of our past and future. They should be protected.
I can't. Not right now. I can't stop to talk about this while Snapdragon lies there and Hyacinth gets away!\n\nI—. Do you really think Hyacinth did this? That he's really the traitor?
Right. Just more words. And that scares me. \n\nLet's push forward. Find Hyacinth. Then, for Snapdragon's sake, I'm prepared to do what needs to be done.

Remember when I was stuck in that ice? I kept thinking, Wisteria will save me. \n\nShe'd come strolling down the path from Vulkhel Guard, smiling that sharp smile of hers. I'd crack jokes while she chipped me free.

The Wisteria I know. Well, the one I knew. She could face down a minotaur and not break a sweat. \n\nBut one look at you and the veins in her neck pop! I think she's scared of you. Scared of what we can do together. And that gives me hope.

And look how far we've come. Actually, maybe that's why she hates you so much. She seems to really hate you, by the way. In case you hadn't noticed. \n\nIf she hates you, the best adventuring partner I've ever had, clearly I'm doing something right.

A lucky guess? I owe you better than that. My relationship with Wisteria is complicated. We've had these intense, lengthy chats and I know so much about her, but … sorry. \n\nWe can talk about this more later. After we find her and Oleander.

We still have no idea what her actual plan is. I mean, some of our missions against the Ceythalmor actually succeeded! Were those just shams? Her letting us think we won?\n\nAnother thing. That day in Auridon. The ice trap. Why me? Why not Oleander?

After everything that happened? You've been a boon. I can't imagine what sort of trouble I'd have gotten into without you. The Divines know I needed a distraction.\n\nWithout you, I'd probably be three bottles deep before midday.

Is it any easier to know that she was lying to us from the beginning? That she's been undermining our efforts since the moment she joined the Garland Ring? No.\n\nAnd the more I think about it, the more confused I am.

Ha! Don't tempt me!\n\nYou're a good friend. Gallivanting aside, you've shown me kindness. And that's a rare thing in this world. More rare than you might realize. I appreciate it, and I appreciate you.

Instead of trying to protect me, she could have treated me like an equal! Told me the truth! If she had, maybe I could have changed her mind. Or she could have changed mine. \n\nI don't mean that. I just wish a lot of things had gone differently.

Enough to know they're alive, but that's about it. I'm not surprised. Those two love to sit in dark rooms and map out every move the Ring makes ahead of time. \n\nIn the early days, I couldn't so much as kick down a door without consulting Hyacinth.

Wisteria started running the missions. She let me make my own decisions. Let me make mistakes. \n\nIt was a big change from when I was growing up. Back then, every moment was calculated, controlled. And when that didn't work, I got these tattoos.

For a long time, I couldn't look at them without feeling a sense of failure, of disappointment. But the way you and Wisteria look at me? Look at them?\n\nThey've grown on me. They make me feel kind of special, actually.

Let me see … oh. Heh. I remember that night. I wanted to warm my hands by the fire, but I didn't want Wisteria to see me shaking. I really wanted her to like me. I was so nervous.\n\nShe's usually so perceptive, but she completely misread me.

Queen Ayrenn leads the Dominion, of course. And personally, I think she's amazing. \n\nBut understand, for Summerset, the Proxy Queen is a far more public royal face. If she's killed, and the Ceythalmor have someone lined up to take her place ….

If the Ceythalmor truly want to change the world, an Aldmeri Dominion civil war would be a great place to start. \n\nThe Eyes of the Queen fighting Ceythalmor in the streets of Alinor. Cyrodiil forces under the eagle banner struck from behind? Ugh.

I promised my niece I'd return to Alinor, to debrief her and the court. Make no mistake. Elements of the Ceythalmor still threaten the heart and soul of the Dominion. \n\nI'm under no illusion that we defeated them completely. More's the pity.

If not the Ceythalmor, then another banner will rise some day. The people of Summerset struggle with an idea, you understand. The corrupting belief that High Elves are destined to rule.\n\nFighting that idea is the singular challenge of my people.

It appears I have some spare time. No doubt the Gardener will call me back to my workshop soon enough. But not today.\n\nPerhaps I will do some traveling. You and Tanlorin seem to enjoy that lifestyle. Perhaps it would suit me, as well.

It has been some time since I did a thorough scavenging run into a Dwemer construct. Or perhaps I will once again try to find the entrance to the fabled Clockwork City. \n\nI have learned so much from the scraps. Imagine what I could learn firsthand.
Maybe. Probably. I've made incredible memories with the Ring. And drowned away an equal number of sorrows drinking with them. \n\nTraitorous lovers and assassinations aside, I think we did some good.

I'm going to work on my brooding. Maybe flirt around. Most of all, I want to keep adventuring with you. See the rest of what Tamriel has to offer. \n\nCheck out all those Daedric realms. Maybe even an Aedric one, if you're up to it. Just say the word.
All right, spit it out. I'll tell you what I know, for whatever that's worth. The day is moving kind of quickly.

The Eyes of the …? No. Very, very much no. Everyone in the Garland Ring is like me, just a regular person who hopes to make tomorrow a little bit better than today. \n\nI've heard stories about the Eyes. Honestly, they scare me.

So don't be alarmed. But they're the ruling bureaucracy of the Aldmeri Dominion.\n\nThe Thalmor consists of … well. Exactly who you'd expect. Canonreeves, merchants, and nobles. All, theoretically, advising Queen Ayrenn on how to run the alliance.

It's not much of a story. I have a complicated relationship with my family. I'm technically oustered, if you know what that means. \n\nAnyway, I'm pretty good with my hands. You saw how I handled that lock. I took to thieving to make ends meet.

You're full of surprises, my friend! I'm guessing you had a hand in what happened to them. Thank you, honestly. \n\nI lost a cousin to the poison the Heritance was spreading. And you're right, they were connected to some powerful people.

More than any citizen of the Dominion should be comfortable with, if they bother to think about it. Have you ever heard of those Veiled Heritance idiots? \n\nXenophobic racists, the lot of them. Rumor is they have support in the Thalmor. Disgusting.

Auri-El must be looking out for me today. She sent me someone that's worked with the Eyes of the Queen! \n\nI imagine we seem small in comparison. But I promise you, we make up for size in charisma, enthusiasm, and winning personalities.

I thought he was going to turn me in to the city guard. But he wanted to compliment me! Said he was impressed, and offered me a … how did he put it? A job that would make frequent use of my skills.\n\nAnd here we are today.

I'm in the Garland Ring because I'm a thief. I was snatching rings and coins off some rich nobles in Skywatch when I looked behind me and realized one of my marks was following me. A strange-looking man in a frankly shocking outfit.

Precisely! And we've got the papers to prove it. The name alone … in old Ayleidoon cey means shadow. So literally, the Shadow Thalmor. \n\nIt's exactly the kind of pompous affectation a Thalmor official would find appealing.

In the eyes of my family and Summerset society, I'm banished. It's ceremonial, of course, but still. \n\nMy family had expectations of me I couldn't fulfill. My tattoos are a memento of all that. I just don't fit in.

That's not an easy question to answer.\n\nWhat I can tell you is that the Elder Scroll is not currently related to Orpheon, but prophecies are fickle things. It could change, or his reading of it could push him to do something drastic.

I belong to the Order of the Ancestor Moth. Everyone calls us Moth Priests. We care for Elder Scrolls and we have the privilege of reading them. Reading the scrolls blinds us—but it is important work.

I am a Moth Priest. There weren't many of us on this island, but there aren't many of us anywhere these days. \n\nStill, if you know about us, then you know how important this Elder Scroll is. I swore to take care of it.

Fate is more fluid than you think. It doesn't happen often, but sometimes reading a prophecy alters it.\n\nOrpheon invaded an entire island for the scroll. Even if it's a small possibility, I don't want him to find what he's looking for.

They're proud Redguards and very dedicated to remaining undetected and practicing quietly. \n\nThat's the reason my predecessors chose to come here with our Elder Scroll after the Empire fell. Because the Hel Netu could keep us safely hidden.

Orpheon's army consists of soldiers who deserted from every other army in Tamriel. They're battle hardened merciless cutthroats who chose to follow Orpheon instead of becoming bandits or mercenaries.\n\nThat tells you enough about Orpheon.
The Hel Netu know how to defend themselves, but Orpheon's army controlled every keep outside the Imperial City. \n\nThe monastery didn't stand a chance.

Not nearly as large as one of the alliance armies, but sizable enough to overrun this island. \n\nThey have many animals and creatures with them. I remember hearing a lot of noises as Khafdeed led me through some hidden passages.

There is day and there is night. Sand and shore. Sword-singers and Hel Netu.\n\nThe best way to avoid the desert heat is to live in the ocean. We win every fight that never was. But we know how to best the Sword-singers, too.

Careful footwork, mastery in a variety of weapons, and a sturdy understanding of how to redirect their power.\n\nStill, we are too few to withstand Orpheon's forces. Our expertise crumbled under their boots.

You have the face of my ancestors—and their bladed enemies. Why should I tell you? \n\nKnow that our skills and techniques can keep the Sword-singers at bay, but we were too few to withstand Orpheon's forces. Our expertise crumbled under their boots.

We have for my entire life and we think of this island as our ancestral home. But in honesty, this is not the truth. We are from somewhere far over the sand dunes. \n\nThe sea breeze suits me. I do not long for the desert or what it holds.
Depends on which door you open. I assume Mentor Huzbedad will take several that climb the rocky cliff faces and avoid detection that way. \n\nWe will take a more well-known path to the monastery.

To keep us safe when the sea swells or the sun beats down too hotly. They protect us and keep us hidden.\n\nI hope my family and friends took shelter when the attack began. When this is over, we will have to search each crevice for wounded.

No. I do not often interact with the Moth Priests. But Mentor Huzbedad tasked me with her safety. I will not fail. \n\nI just wish I could fight for my home. Ignoring the sounds of destruction was one of the hardest things I had to do.

Only Moth Priests such as Sister Chana know how to handle the scrolls with care. I can't risk damaging it or altering the prophecy.\n\nNo, I'll stand guard until it's safe enough for Sister Chana to come retrieve the scroll herself.

And expose her to risk? If Orpheon claims both Sister Chana and the scroll, then everything my people suffered will be meaningless.\n\nWork with Khafdeed to keep her safe and leave the scroll to me. I will defend it with my life.
Snapdragon no longer uses her code name. Now she's Lirinisse, mentoring Mages Guild adepts in Skywatch. I suggest you start your search there.

Change for a better tomorrow. The Thalmor, the Ceythalmor, they're all the same. Powerful people using their resources to ensure wealth and longevity for the few and the privileged.\n\nThat's where the Garland Ring steps in. To balance the scales.

Yes. Paranoia, I believed then. I personally handpick every member of the Ring, you understand. But so much has happened. And now she might be missing. \n\nPerhaps her accusations were not just anger and the baseless speculation I believed them to be.

Hmm. All I will say is that I have access to family wealth. Terrible, selfish, exorbitant wealth. \n\nStars willing, through the actions of the Garland Ring, I can begin to repair the damage done by centuries of entitled and simply awful behavior.

Not much, I'm afraid. We have to keep some secrets in this line of work, you understand. \n\nI founded this organization and personally fund all our activities. We undertake missions of a charitable and humanitarian nature, at my sole discretion.

You're a worldly person. You've no doubt seen talented, intelligent people in roles that don't make use of their abilities. That don't give them the chance to truly make a difference.\n\nTo me, that is the Ring. Talent and skill, harnessed for change.

Tanlorin's not a flower. It's my real name. I … I don't like the codename they gave me. I mean, would you want people to call you Bogcup? I don't think so.\n\nI just hope that group we've been worried about isn't involved in all this.

Perhaps. Perhaps not. Who can know the mind of a man like Emeric? In any case, it's not up to me. I shall bring your argument to my superiors in Daggerfall—and it was a very convincing argument to be sure!—and let them decide.

Not exactly. Prince Azah and I were able to get the alliances to send ambassadors to Stirk, the same island where Vanus forged the agreement to attack Coldharbour. But we're far from reaching such an agreement again.\n\nFrankly, we could use your help.

Everything is connected. People, objects, the sea. Despite the best efforts of their close-minded relatives, Bogcup's affinity to soul magic is quite exceptional. \n\nThe spell will enhance these connections to speed your voyage and hide you at sea.

If you must. I try not to dwell on that too much. Hyacinth always tells me to utilize my inner talent. His words, not mine. My magic is all muddled up with my family, my tattoos. I'll tell you what I feel comfortable talking about. But beyond that ….

My family never understood me or my magic. You could only be a mage if you performed magic the way the Sapiarchs taught it. My mother said I was lying about my abilities, even after I showed her what I could do.\n\nThat's all I want to say about this.

Slinging around fire or soul stuff in a fight, I don't mind that at all. I even think I'm pretty good at it. I hope I've been useful in our scraps so far.\n\nNo, I don't like to use my … I don't know what to call it. My deep magic.
The tattoos were my family's attempt to control me. To stop me from sensing stuff, talking about things I shouldn't know. Generally, to keep me from being me.\n\nAs you can tell, it didn't work. Heh.

The note you found described the Worm Nest as a gathering place for Worm Cult remnants from around Tamriel, so we could face lots of opposition.\n\nI hope that it holds information about the soul reapers. Prince Azah thinks we'll find Mezamma there.

Ever since I was very young, I could sense connections between me and other people. Between people and objects. And sometimes, like just now, if I focus I can strengthen that connection. Almost reach out and touch it.\n\nAnyway, we should get going.

Because they're cruel. Because they work for greedy, callous puppet-masters who can't abide when their status quo is challenged.\n\nLook, where his neck meets his shoulder. That's frostbite. Gods, they tortured him the same way they trapped me.
We need to find her. Now.

Mezamma teleported me and locked me in a cell. Reminds me of Coldharbour, but also it doesn't. A problem for later.\n\nListen. The soul reapers are just the start. The Worm Cult has a hidden nest. It's amassing forces to launch a devastating attack.

My guards mentioned an isolated island called Solstice. If I learn more, I'll contact you again, but you must convince the alliances. They must join with the guilds again to stop this threat. If not, the Worm Cult will bring death to all of Nirn.

I'm not sure. I'd like to stay here, if the Hel Netu will still have me and the Elder Scroll. So much of our past is tied together. I shudder at the thought of our futures continuing separately.\n\nMaybe they'll accept my help in rebuilding.
Despite what happened today, the Hel Netu have kept this scroll shrouded with secrecy for a long time. Longer than I think anyone else could manage. \n\nIt could be safe here again.

Put out the fires and take stock of what remains. Look for more survivors as we work.\n\nDepending on what we find, we'll mourn and rebuild. We may not stay on Lep Seclusa, but the Hel Netu are not finished.

If this island were uninhabitable? Yes. It will be difficult, but my people have trekked across the desert sands before. We will find a new place to make our home. \n\nWe will not be too hasty, though. Making a decision like that will take time.

I won't shackle Sister Chana to a wounded lion. If she wants to take her scroll somewhere with more defenses and greater protection, we will part on good terms. But I'd like it if she stayed. \n\nWe'll talk it through.

I wanted to talk to you first because Bogcup seems to trust you … and because you weren't here when my husband was killed. I can be almost absolutely certain that the traitor isn't you.\n\nBut time is short. The Ceythalmor could arrive at any moment.

I am close to getting Talbira's song just right. She feels like a part of me I never knew was there. But the Inquisitors keep us busy. Be glad you have not been pressed into service!\n\nStill, I wish I could tell Viti about it. I miss her guidance.

Because Snapdragon taught me how to hide messages in plain sight! You use an ink wash, almost like a watercolor. We just need to make a pigmented oil. Easy!\n\nKnowing Snap, we can find everything we need somewhere in the cottage.

Heh. That's why you always search a Garland Ring agent. He must still have some of his constructs on him. Most aren't very large.\n\nI'm not sure how it works, but it imprints events that can be reviewed later. Like we just saw.

Sick to my stomach, but I guess I'm less angry. I'm trying not to lose sight of Snapdragon's death. Even if I'm incredibly relieved Hyacinth isn't the traitor.\n\nGods, she went to her grave thinking her friend had betrayed her. I hate these people.
Always. When I thought Hyacinth had turned against us. Gods. What his mind might do working for the Ceythalmor. \n\nVery glad that's not something we'll have to deal with.

The events at Namiira's shrine scatter my thoughts like sand in a strong wind. But this feels right. Something there will aid us in our quest to stop Ravith-morna. Some sort of lesson, perhaps, or a revelation from Azurah.\n\nOne can only hope.

I visited the place early in my journey to walk the path of the Hidden Moon. Ma'hadaliit, new adepts, were brought there to study the arts and prayers of the order.\n\nIn my time, it was an ancient place of learning.

Not since we parted ways at the Namiira shrine. The revelation of my actions, what I did to Moon-Singer Talbira, it sent poor Krin'ze into darkness. Toward the Bent Dance.\n\nThe High Cantor said to wait until she sent for me. So far, no word.

Must I say it again, tamiit? Ravith-morna revealed the truth from my past that I had kept hidden. That when Talbira commanded me to strike at Ravith, I instead turned the blade on her.\n\nKrin'ze was devastated, the song faltered, and Ravith escaped.
We had Ravith-morna's location and we had Moon-Singer Talbira's song. I thought we had everything we needed to end the Rajaska threat, but I was wrong.

We cannot defeat Ravith-morna and her chorus of Rajaska without the song known to Cantor Krin'ze or something else that will give us an advantage. \n\nThat is what I hope awaits us at Khenarthi's Rise.

Then every Khajiiti soul in search of Azurah's Crossing will be hunted down and dragged into the Void. They would never know the peace of the Sands Behind the Stars.\n\nEven now, Ravith-morna's chorus sings to summon the beast. We must silence them.

Perhaps. But without a permanent solution, the Void would simply send her back at some future time and the danger would rise again. No, we need to stop Ravith completely. The threat to all Khajiiti souls posed by this moon beast is just too great.
What, and rule the Summerset Isles as pawns of the Ceythalmor? Not even a little bit.\n\nShe's been one step ahead of us at every turn. We don't even know what this plan of hers is really about.
There are more workshops and eating halls there. But most of it is dedicated to the needs of the Moth Priests.\n\nWhen the water rises and the sea splashes, the upper monastery is dry and stable.

Of course. Sister Chana couldn't do everything on her own. They were fewer than the number of logs in a hearth, but they kept the monastery lit. \n\nOrpheon changed that. I hope Sister Chana is prepared to be the only star in the sky.

Hah! Sorry. This is so exhilarating! Like the smell after it rains. Have I been able to do this all along? Not important right now. \n\nWhat if we go to other places she's been? I can manifest her image again. And maybe use this to learn their plan!

Yeah. My parents brought in a Sapiarch to examine me. Said it was undisciplined soul magic. And when I couldn't hide the flares? Tattoos. \n\nAfter that, the flares were much easier to control. But that feeling of connection never quite went away.

Proxy Queen Alwinarwe? She stands in for Queen Ayrenn at the Summerset court in Alinor. It's an open secret the Queen hates politics, so she recruited her cousin to do her dirty work.\n\nSo, a person we absolutely cannot let get assassinated.

That's a casual way to drop that into the conversation. You have some history with Proxy Queen Alwinarwe? Friend, you are a never ending fountain of surprises.\n\nIf you know her, then you know how much we absolutely cannot let her get assassinated!
The Garland Ring? How curious. You do get around, it would seem. We suppose that makes sense, given your affiliation with that … cat.

A lovely sentiment. And one that we share. We will have to make a formal inquiry. Most likely alert our cousin, Queen Ayrenn. But it is not every day an attempt is made on our life. Even rarer that we are so … unsettled.\n\nThank you. Both of you.
Ah, yes. We have heard of this Ceythalmor organization. It is clear we underestimated the threat they posed.\n\nIt seems we owe our lives to you once again, adventurer. To you and this Garland Ring.

We lost so much to the Ceythalmor. Only a handful of us remain. When I return to Alinor, I shall propose to my niece that we fold the Ring into the Proxy Queen's court. \n\nWe will continue the fight for the Dominion's soul from within.
There is no journal. All our deepest secrets, those are all in my head. \n\nRegardless, you need to confront Wisteria. Stop her. For Bogcup.

With extreme prejudice. Kill every Worm Cultist that crosses our path. Destroy those damn soul reapers. And then find Mezamma and send her back to whatever Oblivion pit she crawled out of! Let's get moving!

What haven't I been up to? I am Tamriel's greatest living mage after all. I had just started to get inclinations that the Worm Cult might not be as finished as we thought when word reached me about the attacks on the guildhalls. I am beyond annoyed.

Isn't it obvious? With Merric dead, someone needs to take the reins of the Fighters Guild until their ponderously slow council can select a new guildmaster. Since they're in the thick of it, Skordo and Prince Azah are the most likely candidates.

I have no idea who that might be. One moment I was about to board a coach to Shornhelm when a strange woman stopped me and looked deeply into my eyes. The next, I was waking up here, feeling awful and very much put out.

That was the second interruption! Merric spouted nonsense about the Worm Cult even as my apprentice spouted nonsense about seeing me board the coach to Shornhelm while he was carrying me here.\n\nMerric ran off, chasing after the coach, I presume.
That's a strange story. And the woman, it could have been Mezamma.\n\nDid the magister say anything about Guildmaster Merric?

It's not a very pleasant prophecy. Fires and rubble. Shadowy figures in the ruins of a city I've never heard of.\n\nWhatever future this scroll paints, it's not one Orpheon could use to gain power. That's what I tried to tell him.

Those tusking bastards! I came back here to rally the troops, but I should have gone down there with you. I could have saved Merric, damn it!\n\nThis is bad. What's the guild going to do without its guildmaster? And at a time like this?

Oh. Right, of course. Merric loved these. They were family heirlooms. He was proud to wield them in service to the greater good. He was always spouting nonsense like that.\n\nAll right. Tell me that you and the prince have a plan to make someone pay.
By now you should know just how many paths there are in this island. \n\nThe main gate is not navigable, but that door behind us will lead where we need to go.

The note we discovered in the Mages Guild sanctum talked about a Worm Nest on the northern coast of Rivenspire. We must gather our forces, storm their lair, and deal with the Worm Cult leader, Mezamma.

We can destroy the soul reapers without unleashing a killing explosion? That's excellent news! I can't wait to hear the details.\n\nBut what do they actually do? And by the swords of my forefathers, tell me what happened to Vanus!

An ancient Dwarven forge now controlled by the Fighters Guild. It creates items of immense power. Merric used it to craft a weapon strong enough to destroy a Daedric artifact.\n\nAs Skordo, Mezamma will walk right in. We need to get there now!

Merric is many things, but mage is not one of them. I trust the scouts, but he could not be in three distant places at the same time. I need you to make your best guess. Pick a location and see if you can find our missing guildmaster.

So far, distinctive clues elude us and no one has claimed credit for the attacks.\n\nAt this rate, they could destroy the guild before we learn anything. It's the biggest crisis since the Planemeld, but without Merric, I'm not sure how to proceed.

Yes. Merric was supposed to meet me here, but he never arrived. While most of the guild secures the remaining guildhalls, I could use some outside help to track down our guildmaster. Then together we can stop these attacks.\n\nCan I hire you, wayfarer?

No one has claimed credit for the attacks and evidence has been lacking. It makes no sense.\n\nStill, I expect more and more attacks at any time. Without Master Merric, our guild could fall. It's our biggest crisis since the Planemeld.

Just that. I was supposed to meet him here, but he never arrived. Most of the guild is securing the remaining halls, but with you here we can track down the guildmaster and stop these attacks. \n\nThe guild needs you, comrade. Will you answer the call?
Later. After this fellow spills his guts. I want to be perfectly sure before I jump to really terrible conclusions.
The Order of the Black Worm. Scourge of Tamriel. Fist of Molag Bal. I'm done with that, but I hurt too much to talk about it. Ask your friend. He was there. But get me those leaves!

Let me see. A Worm Cult nest on Rivenspire's northern coast? Stendarr blesses us with another foolish enemy, quick to put their plans to paper.\n\nFirst, however, we must go to the Fighters Guildhall in Shornhelm. Tell Skordo what befell Merric.

The Worm Cult? Oh, not that old specter again! We defeated them soundly during the Planemeld crisis. Their threat has faded from Tamriel like dew in the morning sun. You waste my time with rumors and speculation!
Merric and Vanus …. That shines a very different light on the subject. I can see why Prince Azah and Gabrielle seem so worried. I'll bring this information to my superiors right away.
Are you certain it's a resurrected Worm Cult and not just the work of an insignificant handful of fanatics who refused to accept defeat? Surely, they can't be a threat to the mighty Aldmeri Dominion?
I see. Yes, I can see why Gabrielle and Prince Azah seem so concerned. I'll bring this information to my superiors straight away.
Are you certain it's a resurrected Worm Cult and not just the work of an insignificant handful of fanatics who refused to accept defeat? Surely, they can't be a threat to the powerful Ebonheart Pact?
That explains the obvious concern displayed by Prince Azah and Gabrielle. Perhaps this threat is more dire than I anticipated. I'll bring this information to my superiors right away.

That's not up to me or Vanus. That's for the guild council to decide. Merric just died and nobody wants to replace him. But someone needs to have their hand on the tiller. Might as well be Azah.\n\nMerric trusted him, so that's good enough for me.

What, do I look like a mind reader to you? If I had to guess, he got word of this latest plot and he's been following it nonstop. No time to call for help when the Worm Cult apparently has a new weapon and plans to take revenge against the guilds.

Vanus's staff is a powerful arcane tool. He may not have wanted it to fall into the Worm Cult's hands. Or he had some other reason to make sure it ended up with us and not the enemy.\n\nWe have to trust Vanus. He never does anything without purpose.

It's an island off the coast of Hew's Bane. It's considered neutral ground by all the alliances. They met for talks there once before, the last time the Worm Cult and Molag Bal threatened Tamriel. \n\nIt's the best place for our purposes.
Of course I'm worried, but Vanus is a powerful mage. Perhaps the most powerful. He can handle himself. I just wish he told us more about Solstice.

Not a damn thing. It could be an island paradise, for all I know. Or it could be a carnal pit crawling with worms and Daedra. Probably a little bit of both.\n\nAs long as there's something there for me to punch, all good.

We set aside our differences once to defeat the Worm Cult. It may take some convincing, but I am certain the Aldermi Dominion will contribute. At least a champion or two. Perhaps a few knights. At least until we know the true extent of the threat.

Jorunn brought the Dark Elves and Argonians together to defeat the Akaviri. And he set aside hostilities to defeat the Worm Cult once before. I can't say with any certainty, but I believe the Ebonheart Pact will do the right thing.

A guild scout talked to hunters who said they spotted Merric near Vulkwasten. That area contains many nooks and crannies among the rocks to hide in, and Daedra roam the vicinity as well.\n\nDo you think Merric could be searching there?

Both Merric and I know the desert well, but I have no idea why he would go there. Still, a guild scout claims to have spotted him in Sentinel's outskirts. If you decide this is the spot, I suggest you search for him among the cliffs there.

A guild scout says Merric was spotted outside Windhelm. A place of snow and ice, and Merric hates the cold. Still, if some clue pointed here, he wouldn't let a little weather stop him.\n\nDo you think Merric searches for our enemy in Eastmarch?
I would be surprised if you didn't, comrade. What can I tell you, bearing in mind that our understanding of the facts is incomplete at best?

There is not much to tell. I suppose it's fair to say that I am a prince. The son and heir of King Fahara'jad of Hammerfell. After the events of the Planemeld, my father suggested I learn more about the wider world. So I joined the Fighters Guild.

I respect Guildmaster Merric and care about all my guild comrades. Merric is a hard taskmaster, but he is fair and honorable. He's taught me many and many things.\n\nIt did not feel right to leave him, but he gave me a task and I had to complete it.

After the events in the Alik'r Desert and the Planemeld crisis, my father, King Fahara'jad, thought I should learn more about the wider world. Preparation for one day ruling in his stead, I suppose. So I joined the Fighters Guild.

Merric's an excellent fighter—smart, brave, and quick. A true follower of Stendarr. And he's a good mentor.\n\nSince becoming guildmaster, he hasn't stopped leading from the front of the charge. It inspires the guild but puts him in constant peril.

That's a tale from before I joined. It happened during the Planemeld crisis. The prior guildmaster, Sees-All-Colors, betrayed the guild. She killed her predecessor to earn her rank.\n\nWhen the council found out, they removed her and promoted Merric.

As I understand it, he hasn't changed much since becoming guildmaster. I know he has mixed feelings about how he got the position, but he's been a shining example for the guild. There's no one I'd rather serve. No one I'd rather learn from.

We were following up on the attacks but not getting very far. He sent me to file a report with the guild. Then I was supposed to meet him here. He never arrived. When I informed the guild of the situation, the scouting reports started coming in.

Devastatingly brutal affairs. And thorough. Not a single survivor. And we only found the remains of guild members. The attackers must take their dead or they strike so fast that no one can react.\n\nBut how were they able to get past the defenses?

Guildmaster Merric and I were trying to figure that out. I can only assume that he discovered something and followed after it, which is why he isn't here. Something so urgent he could leave no note. \n\nWe need to find Merric and get some answers.

Guildhalls are well defended. They're filled with some of the best fighters in all of Tamriel. Assaults at the entrances would create damage, but there's no evidence of such.\n\nIt's like they walked right in and suddenly attacked from deep inside.

A disgusting group of necromancers. They attacked Tamriel a while back and caused all kinds of trouble.\n\nLet's hurry and get those leaves. I want to stay on Merric's trail. I'll tell you what I think about the worms after that.
Thank you. Once the pain subsides, I'll limp into town.\n\nNo more cults for me. Or religion of any kind, for that matter. I'm done with it all.

The damn Worm Cult is really back. I thought they scattered after we stopped the Planemeld. You'd hear about a few remnants, but nothing significant. Not like this.\n\nAnd he said they had a new weapon. What the tusk is a soul reaper anyway?

That's over in Vulkwasten. They built it inside a big tree on the western side of town.\n\nHow about you find this magister? Figure out what business she has with Mezamma and if she's seen Merric. I'll collect Wimi and wait for you outside the tavern.

I think that's in Sentinel, elaborate building on the northwest side of town.\n\nHow about you find this magister? Figure out what business she has with Mezamma and if she's seen Merric. I'll collect Wimi and wait for you outside the inn.

That's in Windhelm. The stone building right by the southern stables.\n\nHow about you find this magister? Find out what business she has with Mezamma and if she's seen Merric. I'll collect Wimi and wait for you outside the inn.

They call themselves the Order of the Black Worm. Followers of an evil bastard named Mannimarco, a necromancer who worked for Molag Bal.\n\nThey tried to drag Nirn into Coldharbour with giant anchors from the sky. Called it the Planemeld. Crazy time.

The three alliances teamed up with the Fighters and Mages Guilds to fight Molag Bal. Some heroes ended Mannimarco, but I don't know the full story.\n\nIn the end, we stormed Coldharbour, broke the Great Anchor, and kicked the dung out of them.

We all thought they scattered. Without Mannimarco, the remnants didn't pose any significant threat. Or so we thought.\n\nWe thought we squished those worms, but I guess we drove them underground. Not a mistake I plan to make twice.

I thought so, pal! They were leaderless after you and the Companions beat that evil bastard Mannimarco. When our little trip to Coldharbour stopped Molag Bal's Planemeld, the Worm Cult should've died.
I guess we forced them underground, but didn't squish them hard enough.\n\nLet's catch up with Merric so we can do just that.

She stepped out of the shadows and blocked my path as I walked to the coach. I remember her unsettling eyes as she stared at me. After that, I awoke in here.\n\nIf she used some spell to take my form, she must be a powerful mage indeed.

And we need to go and help him! Sure, Merric got the drop on a small camp of Worm Cultists, but they've already destroyed four of our guildhalls. He's a great fighter, but whatever they have planned for Shornhelm might be too much even for him.

The magisters were meeting to interpret the dark divinations of various guild mages. They asked me to attend because of my experience fighting Molag Bal during the Planemeld.\n\nTo be honest, I prefer digging up antiquities for the Antiquarian Circle.
What? No! Please, my suffering is great. Merric told me to share what I know and I will. But I need those leaves to ease my pain.

Not a prince, but a jester? You do make a good point, though. Life in the order involves lies and dark secrets. I no longer wish to walk that path.\n\nBut I still need something for this pain. The information I possess must be worth at least that.
You bastard. The pain is too great. I'll pass out or die before I can tell you everything I know. And then where will you be?\n\nPlease, help me and we'll both get what we want.

You're right. No better time to change than now. The Order of the Black Worm has risen from the ashes of defeat to take vengeance. First on the Fighters Guild, then the Mages Guild, then all of Tamriel.

Not enough. We have guild sages studying what remained of the device. It involves soul magic, but we don't know its specific purpose yet.\n\nWe have heard the devices are appearing in multiple places. We're investigating, but it's still early.

Vanus Galerion. Founder and guildmaster of the Mages Guild. He can be difficult to track down sometimes. But after what happened with our magisters, I feel certain he'll want to help.\n\nAnd I won't lie. We could use someone with his power.

Perhaps so. Maybe further study will reveal that he saved lives as well. But with a threat of this magnitude, we need every means at our disposal to gain the upper hand. \n\nI've heard enough. Where is this Worm Cult nest you learned of?

That's … fair. I do appreciate the help. And perhaps more would have died if Merric hadn't destroyed the soul reaper.\n\nThank you for your recounting of what you saw. Now, where can we find the Worm Cult nest you uncovered?

Compassion has no place in events of this magnitude. How does a single life compare to the hundreds, nay thousands, at stake from the Worm Cult machinations?\n\nI mourn Merric's loss, but the facts remain the same. Now, where is the Worm Cult nest?

Yeah, but I think she's planning more than that. Did you hear what she said about the Fighters' heart?  But what do I know? I can't even keep my friends safe!\n\nIt's all falling apart, pal. I don't think we're going to beat the worms this time.

Yeah, of course we do. At least we need to go down fighting, right? But we need to get out of this stinking pit. Clear my head from Mezamma's spell. Then figure out what to do next.\n\nLet's ask Gabrielle to make us a portal. She loves doing that.

Can't even let me have a moment, huh, pal? But, yeah, I'm still better at punching people than anyone I know. Present company excluded.\n\nAll right. Let's get the tusk of out of here. Maybe Gabrielle can portal us somewhere and we can make a plan.

Just the basics. I was on assignment when the attacks occurred. Since then, I've been trying to dig up anything to point us at the perpetrators. Then I got word that Merric had disappeared.\n\nI hope he's onto something and not another victim.

Thank you. Any amount of assistance is much appreciated.
A little on the dark side, but I totally understand the sentiment. I've dealt with the Worm Cult before myself.

Introductions later. Right now you have to get below and stop the attack on the Mages Guild. You're with Skordo and Prince Azah, so I trust that you'll be useful in the fight. So, please, get down there and do what you can.

Not exactly to the Daedric Prince of Domination, but the omens certainly had the taint of Coldharbour about them. We were hoping to determine more when the Worm Cult attacked. If not for Merric and my tardiness, I might be among the dead.

I see what you're doing. Using absurdity to make me clear my mind and remember my duty. I must focus on everything my father, King Fahara'jad, taught me. Everything I learned from Guildmaster Merric. Only then can we defeat the Worm Cult.

You dare speak to a prince of the realm like that? Using harsh words to ignite the fires of anger … and burn away the depression that was dampening my resolve. Well done.\n\nWe may have lost Merric, but we're not done yet. Thank you for reminding me.

Perhaps, but I don't think so. Everything happened quickly after Merric destroyed the soul reaper and Mezamma retreated.\n\nThe job I hired you for ended when we found Merric, but I'd like to extend your employment. Help us assault the Worm Cult nest.

Consider it the equivalent of a field promotion. I've trained under Guildmaster Merric since I joined the guild. And I've been groomed to be a king. The guild will follow me in this time of crisis. Then the council can select a suitable replacement.

Yeah, optimism. I suppose we need that right about now. Prince Azah is going to want an intact Fighters Guild to lead after Gabrielle and him convince the Three Alliances to join forces. That means it's up to us to save whoever's still alive here.

Take my portal to Stirk and talk to your alliance's ambassador. Convince them that the Worm Cult threat is real and we need to work together to stop it.\n\nPrince Azah and I will lean on the other two and do the same.
No. I'm barely sure I've even read about the place. But I plan to do some research while we wait for Vanus's next message.

For the duration of this crisis and until the council can formally select a replacement for Merric, certainly.\n\nI give him a hard time, but Prince Azah is a good man. And a good warrior. He'll make Merric proud, just you watch.

Our way forward is blocked by three primary obstacles. The Stirk Fellowship must still be organized, we don't know where the island of Solstice hides in the vast seas, and we have only the barest idea where Vanus is imprisoned.

While the guilds and the three alliances have agreed to work together to combat the Worm Cult in principal, there are still treaties to be signed, logistics to work out, and plans to be finalized. That will fill mine and Gabrielle's days for a time.
That task will most likely fall upon the Mages Guild and the scholars and sages of the alliances. If there is even the merest mention of Solstice in an old scroll or text, we will find it.

The rescue of Vanus is crucial, but stopping the threat posed by the Worm Cult and their soul reapers must be our first priority. And to do that, we need to locate Solstice and transport our forces there.\n\nWe'll save Vanus as well. This I swear.

Coordinating the forces of two guilds and three alliances? That's not a job I envy!\n\nAs for Vanus, he got captured trying to rescue me. Least I can do is return the favor. Soon as we stop the Worm Cult from bringing death to all Nirn, I'm on it!
